records.english: Good morning, Mom!

records.english: Good night, Grandpa, and sleep well.

records.english: I'm a little tired this morning.

records.english: It's a beautiful morning, isn't it?

records.english: Hello, Sarah, how was school today?

records.english: We say good evening when the sun goes down.

records.english: Good morning, class, please sit down.

records.english: Are you awake yet?
records.zomi: Na khanglo khin hiam?

records.english: Have a nice afternoon!

records.english: Hi, Grandma, did you eat breakfast?
records.zomi: Hello Pi, zingsang an na ne khin hiam?

records.english: Good night, see you tomorrow.
records.zomi: Zanpha, zingciang kimu kik ni.

records.english: My little brother waves to me every morning.
records.zomi: Ka nau pasal in zingsang simin khut hong lap hi.

records.english: Is it too late to say good afternoon?
records.zomi: “Sunpha” ci dingin a zekai khin hiam?

records.english: Please greet our guests at the door.
records.zomi: Kongkhak ah i zinte hopih in.

records.english: Morning, David, the coffee is ready.
records.zomi: David, zingpha, kawfi a kizo khin hi.

records.english: She said good evening to the neighbors.
records.zomi: Amah in a inn vengte “Nitakpha” ci-in a hopih hi.

records.english: Let's say good night to Dad.
records.zomi: Pa kiangah “Zanpha” ci ni.

records.english: Whenever I walk into the kitchen, my mother greets me with a cup of hot tea.
records.zomi: Anbuk sungah ka lut simin ka nu in niangtui lum khat tawh hong hopih hi.

records.english: You should say "good afternoon" instead of "good morning" after twelve o'clock.
records.zomi: Sun nai sawm leh nih khit ciangin “Zingpha” ci sangin “Sunpha” na ci ding hi.

records.english: Sorry I didn't say hello this morning; I was running late for the bus.
records.zomi: Tu zingsangin “Hello” ka ci lo hangin hong maisak in; bus tuan dingin ka zekai hi.

records.english: In our family, the children greet their grandparents first when they come home in the evening.
records.zomi: Ka innkuanah nitakin inn a tun ciangun, naupangte in a pu leh a pite uh a masa penin a hopih uh hi.

records.english: Could you tell me whether people here say "good evening" or just "hi" at dinner?
records.zomi: Hih munah nitak an nek ciangin mite in “Nitakpha” a ci uh hiam, “Hello” bek a ci uh hiam, hong gen thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: The shopkeeper greeted me warmly, even though it was already late in the afternoon.
records.zomi: Sun nunglam a hi khin napi, dawlngak pa in lungdam takin hong hopih hi.

records.english: If you get up early, don't forget to wish Grandpa a good morning before you leave.
records.zomi: Zingsang tuungin na thoh leh, na pai ma-in Pu kiangah “Zingpha” ci ding mangngilh kei in.

records.english: What do you usually say when you meet your neighbors in the evening?
records.zomi: Nitakin na inn vengte na kimuh ciangin bang na ci ngei hiam?

records.english: My roommate isn't a morning person, so she just nods instead of saying hello.
records.zomi: Ka inn tenpih in zingsang a lungnuam mi a hi kei ahih manin, “Hello” ci lo-in a lu bek a ngun hi.

records.english: We were greeted by the whole family as soon as we arrived for Sunday lunch.
records.zomi: Nipini sun an ne dingin ka tun pakun innkuan khempeuh in hong hopih uh hi.

records.english: I've been trying to say good morning to the bus driver every day this week.
records.zomi: Tu kal sungin bus mawngtu kiangah ni simin “Zingpha” ci dingin ka hanciam hi.

records.english: Would you like to come in for some tea, since it's such a cold evening?
records.zomi: Nitak vot mahmah ahih manin, niangtui dawn dingin hong lut nuam hiam?

records.english: After a long day at work, Joseph loves hearing his kids shout "Welcome home!"
records.zomi: Ni khat sung nasep a sep khit ciangin, Joseph in a tate in “Inn ah na hong tun kik lungdam hi!” a ci-a a kikoukouna uh a zak a nuam mahmah hi.

records.english: Why didn't you say good night before you went to bed?
records.zomi: Na lup ma-in bang hangin “Zanpha” na ci lo hiam?

records.english: When my aunt calls in the afternoon, she always asks if we've eaten yet.
records.zomi: Ka ni in sun lamin hong sam ciangin, an na ne khin uh hiam ci-in a dong tawntung hi.

records.english: Let me introduce myself properly, since I only said a quick good morning earlier.
records.zomi: Tua ma-in “Zingpha” bek ka ci zawh ahih manin, kei hong kiphawksak hoih ning.

records.english: My grandparents get up before sunrise and greet each other with a short prayer.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh ka pi in ni a suah ma-in tho-in, thungetna tomno tawh kihopih uh hi.

records.english: If it's after six, I usually say "good evening" when I answer the phone at work.
records.zomi: Nai guk khit a hih leh, nasepna munah phone ka dawn ciangin “Nitakpha” ka ci ngei hi.

records.english: Don't just mumble "morning" at people; look at them and smile when you greet them.
records.zomi: Mite kiangah “Zingpha” ci-in na kam sungah bek gen kei in; na hopih ciangin amaute en inla nuihmai in.

records.english: How was your afternoon, and did the meeting go well?
records.zomi: Na sun hun bangci om hiam, kikhopna zong hoih takin bei hiam?

records.english: The new teacher greeted each student by name as they came in.
records.zomi: Sia thak in a hong lut sangnaupang khatciat a min tawh a hopih hi.

records.english: I'm sorry for calling so early, and I hope I didn't wake you.
records.zomi: Zingsang tuung mahmah hong sam ka hih manin hong maisak in, na ihmutna ka hong phawng lo ding ka lamen hi.

records.english: Our neighbor across the street waves at us every evening while she waters her plants.
records.zomi: Lampi galkhat a om ka inn veng nu in nitak simin a pakte tui a buak laitakin hong khut lap hi.

records.english: You can greet older relatives a little more formally than your friends.
records.zomi: Na upa sanggamte na lawmte sangin zahtak deuhin na hopih thei hi.

records.english: Although "good night" sounds like a greeting, people actually use it when they are leaving or going to bed.
records.zomi: “Zanpha” cih pen kihopihna bang a hi napi, mite in a pai ciang uh hiam, ihmu dingin a lup ciang uh hiam a zang uh hi.

records.english: Had I known you were already awake, I would have come downstairs to say good morning sooner.
records.zomi: Na khanglo khin hi cih ka theih nak leh, “Zingpha” ci dingin a masa zawin ka hong kumsuk ding hi.

records.english: Even on the busiest mornings, my father insists that everyone at the table greet one another before eating.
records.zomi: Zingsang buai pen hi zongin, ka pa in an a nek ma-un dawhkan kiim a om mi khempeuh kihopih ciat dingin a ngen ngiat hi.

records.english: What many visitors notice is how warmly older people greet the children in the evening, as if they hadn't seen them in weeks.
records.zomi: Mikhual tampi in a muh uh khat pen, nitakin upate in naupangte kal tampi sung a mu lo bangin lungdam mahmah-in a hopih uh hi.

records.english: Rather than simply saying hello, Mary tends to ask how everyone slept, which makes the morning feel more personal.
records.zomi: “Hello” ci bek sangin, Mary in mi khempeuh bangci ihmu uh hiam a dong ngei ahih manin, zingsang hun a nuam zaw hi.

records.english: If you're unsure whether it's afternoon or evening, a simple "hello" is never the wrong choice.
records.zomi: Sun hiam nitak hiam na theih ciang kei leh, “Hello” cih pen a khial ngei lo hi.

records.english: It took me a while to realize that my colleague's cheerful "Morning!" was her way of being friendly rather than formal.
records.zomi: Ka nasep pih nu' lungnuam taka “Zingpha!” a cih pen zahtakna hi lo-in lawm bang a kizopna ahi hi, ci ka theih dingin hun sawtpi la hi.

records.english: Not until I moved abroad did I appreciate how much those quiet morning greetings at home had meant to me.
records.zomi: Gamdang ah ka pai khit ciang bekin, inn ah zingsang dai taka kihopihnate in keima' adingin bang zah thupi hiam ka thei hi.

records.english: Would you mind greeting the guests on my behalf this evening, since I won't be back until after dinner?
records.zomi: Nitak an khit ma-in ka tung kik kei ding ahih manin, tu nitakin keimah aiawhin zinte na hopih thei ding hiam?

records.english: In the Zomi families I grew up around, younger members made a point of greeting their elders respectfully when everyone gathered in the evening.
records.zomi: Ka hong khanglianna Zomi innkuante lakah, nitakin mi khempeuh a kikhop ciangin a naupang zawte in a upate uh zahtak takin a hopih ciat uh hi.

records.english: Having worked night shifts for years, my uncle still says "good morning" when he wakes up at three in the afternoon.
records.zomi: Kum tampi sung zan nasep a sep ahih manin, ka pa neu in sun nai thum ciangin a khanglo ciangin “Zingpha” a ci lai hi.

records.english: A warm greeting at the start of the day can set the tone for how the whole family gets along.
records.zomi: Ni kipatna ah lungdam taka kihopihna in innkuan khempeuh bangci kipawl ding uh hiam a lamlak thei hi.

records.english: Good morning, sweetheart, it's time to get up.
records.zomi: Ka it, zingpha, thoh ding hun a cing ta hi.

records.english: Morning, Dad, is there any toast left?
records.zomi: Pa, zingpha, toast a om lai hiam?

records.english: Good evening, Auntie, come in and sit down.

records.english: Hi, Grandpa, how was your nap?

records.english: My sister says good morning to her cat first.

records.english: Wake up, sleepyhead, the sun is out!
records.zomi: Khanglo in, ihmungai, ni a suak khin hi!

records.english: Good afternoon, Uncle Pau, are you busy?
records.zomi: Pu Pau, sunpha, na buai hiam?

records.english: Did Mom say good night to you?
records.zomi: Nu in nang kiangah “Zanpha” a ci hiam?

records.english: We kiss our grandmother good night every evening.
records.zomi: Nitak simin ka pi uh “Zanpha” ci-in ka tawp uh hi.

records.english: Please say good morning to Grandma when she comes downstairs.
records.zomi: Pi a hong kumsuk ciangin “Zingpha” ci in.

records.english: Good evening, honey, how was work?
records.zomi: Ka it, nitakpha, na nasep bangci om hiam?

records.english: My baby brother smiles at everyone in the morning.
records.zomi: Ka nau pasal naungek in zingsangin mi khempeuh nuihmai tawh a en hi.

records.english: Let's go say hello to Dad; he just got home.
records.zomi: Pa “Hello” ci dingin pai ni; amah tu-in inn a tung hi.

records.english: Good morning, Mom, you're up early today!
records.zomi: Nu, zingpha, tuni a tuungin na tho hi!

records.english: I always hug my kids when I get home in the afternoon.
records.zomi: Sun lamin inn ka tun ciangin ka tate ka kawi tawntung hi.

records.english: Night, Mom, I love you.
records.zomi: Zanpha, Nu, kong it hi.

records.english: Can you say good afternoon to your cousins?
records.zomi: Na sanggamte kiangah “Sunpha” na ci thei ding hiam?

records.english: My husband brings me tea and says good morning.
records.zomi: Ka pasal in niangtui hong lak-in “Zingpha” hong ci hi.

records.english: Good evening, Grandma, did you have a nice day?
records.zomi: Pi, nitakpha, tuni na nuam hiam?

records.english: Our dog barks hello every evening when we come home.
records.zomi: Nitak simin inn ka tun ciang uh, ka ui uh in hong hopih bangin hong ham hi.

records.english: Sleep tight, little one.
records.zomi: Ka naupang neu, nuam takin ihmu in.

records.english: Good morning, Niang, did the baby sleep through the night?
records.zomi: Niang, zingpha, naungek zan bup ihmu hiam?

records.english: Welcome back, Tom, how was your afternoon at Grandpa's?
records.zomi: Tom, na hong tun kik lungdam hi, Pu' innah sun hun bangci om hiam?

records.english: Don't forget to say good night to your father.
records.zomi: Na pa kiangah “Zanpha” ci ding mangngilh kei in.

records.english: When I came downstairs this morning, my grandmother was already waiting with a warm smile.
records.zomi: Tu zingsang ka hong kumsuk ciangin, ka pi in nuihmai lum tawh hong ngak khin hi.

records.english: Have you said good morning to your aunt yet, or is she still asleep?
records.zomi: Na ni kiangah “Zingpha” na ci khin hiam, a hih kei leh amah a ihmu lai hiam?

records.english: My daughter has started saying "good afternoon" in a funny deep voice to make us laugh.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in hong nuihsak dingin aw thuk nuihzak tawh “Sunpha” a ci pan hi.

records.english: Every evening, my parents greet each other with a kiss at the front door.
records.zomi: Nitak simin ka nu leh ka pa in inn mai kongkhak ah kitawp-in kihopih uh hi.

records.english: I'm sorry I was grumpy this morning; I didn't mean to ignore your greeting.
records.zomi: Tu zingsangin ka lungsim a nuam lo ahih manin hong maisak in; na hong hopihna ka limsak lo ding ka ut lo hi.

records.english: You should knock on Grandpa's door and wish him good morning before breakfast.
records.zomi: Zingsang an ma-in Pu' kongkhak kiu inla, “Zingpha” ci in.

records.english: Why does Uncle Sam always say "good evening" so formally, even to his own kids?
records.zomi: Pu Sam in a tate kiangah zong bang hangin “Nitakpha” zahtak takin a ci tawntung hiam?

records.english: If you call Grandma this afternoon, start by wishing her a good afternoon before asking for anything.
records.zomi: Tu sunin Pi na sam leh, bangmah na nget ma-in “Sunpha” ci-in kipan masa in.

records.english: Would you like me to wake the children so they can greet their grandparents?
records.zomi: Naupangte in a pu a pite uh a hopih theih nadingun ka phawng sak ding na deih hiam?

records.english: My brother and I used to race downstairs to be the first to say good morning to Dad.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal leh kei in Pa kiangah “Zingpha” ci masa pen dingin a nuai ah kitai-in ka kumsuk ngei uh hi.

records.english: Whenever my mother-in-law visits, she greets each grandchild by their full name.
records.zomi: Ka sungnu in hong veh ciangin a tute khatciat a min bup tawh a hopih hi.

records.english: Could you say hello to Aunt Cing for me when you see her this evening?
records.zomi: Tu nitakin Ni Cing na muh ciangin, keima' adingin “Hello” hong ci sak thei ding na hiam?

records.english: My teenage son only grunts at us in the morning, but by evening he's happy to chat.
records.zomi: Ka tapa khangno in zingsangin hong ngoih bek hi, ahi zongin nitak ciangin kiho dingin a lungdam hi.

records.english: We were greeted by the smell of pancakes when we woke up on Saturday morning.
records.zomi: Kiginni zingsang ka khanglo uh ciangin pancake gim ka nam uh hi.

records.english: How did you greet your grandparents when you were growing up?
records.zomi: Na khanglai in na pu leh na pite bangci na hopih ngei hiam?

records.english: Let's video call Grandma this evening and say good night to her together.
records.zomi: Tu nitakin Pi video call tawh sam khawm ni-in, “Zanpha” ci khawm ni.

records.english: Before heading to work, Hannah peeks into the nursery to whisper good morning to her sleeping twins.
records.zomi: Nasem dinga a pai ma-in, Hannah in a ihmu lai a ta apengte uh “Zingpha” ci-in a bil uah a hopih ciauciau dingin naungek khan ah a en hi.

records.english: My father greets the whole family with the same silly joke every Sunday afternoon.
records.zomi: Ka pa in Nipini sun simin ciamnuihna khat mah tawh innkuan khempeuh a hopih hi.

records.english: I'll be home late tonight, so please say good night to the kids for me.
records.zomi: Tu zanin zekai takin inn ka tung ding ahih manin, keima' adingin naupangte kiangah “Zanpha” hong ci sak in.

records.english: Has anyone wished Grandpa a good afternoon since he got back from the hospital?
records.zomi: Pu zato pan a hong tun kik nung, kuamah in “Sunpha” a ci khin hiam?

records.english: Our family usually shares a short prayer before everyone says good night and goes to bed.
records.zomi: I innkuan in mi khempeuh in “Zanpha” ci-in a lup ma-un thungetna tomno i nei ngei uh hi.

records.english: When my cousins arrived in the afternoon, we all rushed to the gate to welcome them.
records.zomi: Ka sanggamte sun lamin a hong tun ciangun, amaute hong muak dingin kongpi ah ka tai khawm uh hi.

records.english: You don't need to wake your mom just to say good morning; let her sleep in today.
records.zomi: “Zingpha” ci dingin na nu phawng sak kei in; tuni a ihmut sawt deuh hen.

records.english: I was so happy when my son said "Good morning, Daddy" for the first time.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in a masa pen in “Pa, zingpha” a cih ciangin ka lungdam mahmah hi.

records.english: Ever since Grandma moved in with us, our mornings have started with her calling each of us by name from the kitchen.
records.zomi: Pi i kiang ah a hong teen pan nungin, i zingsang hunte anbuk sung pan Pi in khat ciat i min tawh hong sap tawh kipan hi.

records.english: Had my daughter not left a "good morning" note on the fridge, I would have started the day in a terrible mood.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in vot bawlna ah “Zingpha” lai a nusia kei nak leh, lungsim siatna tawh ni ka kipan ding hi.

records.english: What I miss most about living at home is hearing my father hum while he greeted us at breakfast.
records.zomi: Inn ah ka om lai a ka ngaihsun pen in, zingsang an nek laitakin ka pa in la nuam takin hong hopih na a ka zak ahi hi.

records.english: Although my parents live far away, they insist on a quick evening phone call just to say good night to the grandchildren.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa gamla takah a om uh hangin, a tute uh “Zanpha” ci dingin nitakin phone tomno a sam ngiat uh hi.

records.english: Little did I know that my stepfather's awkward "good afternoon" was his way of trying to connect with me.
records.zomi: Ka pakik' “Sunpha” a cih lungzaw dan pen keimah tawh kizop nopna ahi hi, ci ka thei lo hi.

records.english: If you'd told me years ago that I'd miss my brothers' noisy morning greetings, I wouldn't have believed you.
records.zomi: Kum tampi a bei ma-in ka sanggam pasalte' zingsang kihopihna ging buaibuai ka ngaihsun ding hi, na hong ci leh, ka um kei ding hi.

records.english: No matter how tired she is after her shift, my mother never goes to bed without saying good night to each of us.
records.zomi: A nasep khit ciangin bangzah gim zongin, ka nu in khat ciat “Zanpha” hong ci lo-in lup ngei lo hi.

records.english: Not only did my nephew greet every relative at the afternoon reunion, but he also remembered what each of them had been up to.
records.zomi: Ka tanau in sun lam kikhopna ah a beh leh phung khempeuh a hopih bek thamlo-in, amaute khat ciat bang na a sem uh hiam zong a phawk hi.

records.english: Do you think my in-laws would be offended if I greeted them with a casual "hey" rather than a proper "good evening" at dinner?
records.zomi: Nitak an nek ciangin “Nitakpha” ci lo-in “Hey” bek tawh ka hopih leh, ka sungte in a lungkia ding uh na ci hiam?

records.english: As in many Zomi homes I have visited, my aunt expects the children to greet any visiting relatives before they run off to play.
records.zomi: Zomi inn tampi ka zuat bangin, ka ni in naupangte in a kimawl dinga a tai ma-un a hong zin beh leh phungte a hopih masa ding a deih hi.

records.english: Having been away at college all semester, Grace found herself tearing up when her little sister ran to greet her one winter evening.
records.zomi: Semester khat sung sangpi ah a om khit ciangin, phalbi nitak khat ah a nau numei in a hopih dinga a hong tai ciangin Grace in a mittui luang hi.

records.english: The way a family greets one another in the morning often says more about their relationship than anything they discuss at dinner.
records.zomi: Innkuan khat in zingsangin a kihopih dan in nitak an nek laitakin a kikupna uh khatpeuh sangin a kizopna uh a lak zaw ngei hi.

records.english: If you have a complaint about noise, you can contact the city's community services department.

records.english: What frustrates me most is that the charging port on this phone is so easy to damage.
records.zomi: Ka lungkia pen hih phone a charge na kongkhak a siat baih mahmah ahi hi.

records.english: It's worth remembering that a faster processor won't help much if the computer doesn't have enough memory.
records.zomi: Computer in memory a cin kei leh processor a manlang zaw in tampi a huh kei ding hi, ci phawk ding a hoih hi.

records.english: Before handing down his old laptop to his niece, Joseph wiped the hard drive and installed a new battery.
records.zomi: A laptop lui a tunu tungah a piak ma-in, Joseph in hard drive a phiat siang a, battery thak a koih hi.

records.english: My grandmother is proud to be Zomi.
records.zomi: Ka pi in Zomi ahih lam a kisaktheih hi.

records.english: Are you Zomi too?
records.zomi: Nang zong Zomi na hi hiam?

records.english: We speak Zomi at home.
records.zomi: Inn ah Zomi pau i zang hi.

records.english: My dad tells us stories about our village.
records.zomi: Ka pa in i khua thu hong gen hi.

records.english: Please tell me about your family.
records.zomi: Na innkuan thu hong gen in.

records.english: Lian is learning to write in her own language.
records.zomi: Lian in amah' pau tawh lai gelh a sin hi.

records.english: Our church has a Zomi service on Sunday.
records.zomi: I pawlpi in Nipini ah Zomi pau tawh biakna a nei hi.

records.english: Do your children speak Zomi?
records.zomi: Na tate in Zomi pau a zang uh hiam?

records.english: I feel happy when I hear my language in a new city.
records.zomi: Khuapi thak khat ah ka pau ka zak ciangin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: Mang wears a traditional shawl on special days.
records.zomi: Mang in ni thupi teng ah Zomi puan a sil hi.

records.english: Where is your family from?
records.zomi: Na innkuan uh koi pan hi hiam?

records.english: My family is from Chin State in Myanmar.
records.zomi: Ka innkuan Myanmar gam Chin State pan hi.

records.english: We eat together after the community meeting.
records.zomi: Mipi kikhopna khit ciangin an ne khawm uh hi.

records.english: Let's sing a Zomi song tonight.
records.zomi: Tu zanin Zomi la khat sa ni.

records.english: My mother cooks food from our home village.
records.zomi: Ka nu in i khua neu an a huan hi.

records.english: Thank you for asking about my culture.
records.zomi: Ka ngeina thu hong dot ahih manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: Is this shawl from your grandmother?
records.zomi: Hih puan na pi' hi hiam?

records.english: Many Zomi families live far from their homeland now.
records.zomi: Zomi innkuan tampi tu-in a gam uh pan gamla takah a teeng uh hi.

records.english: I want to visit my parents' village one day.
records.zomi: Ni khat ni-in ka nu leh pa' khua ka va en nuam hi.

records.english: Niang teaches small children Zomi words.
records.zomi: Niang in naupang neute Zomi kammal a hilh hi.

records.english: Say hello to the elders first.
records.zomi: Upate “Hello” ci-in hopih masa in.

records.english: My name has a special meaning in my family.
records.zomi: Ka min in ka innkuan ah khiatna tuam a nei hi.

records.english: We met another Zomi family at the park.
records.zomi: Park ah Zomi innkuan dang khat i kimu hi.

records.english: Don't forget to call your grandfather this weekend.
records.zomi: Tu kal bei-in na pu sam ding mangngilh kei in.

records.english: When people ask where I'm from, I usually say I'm Zomi before anything else.
records.zomi: Mite in koi pan hi na hiam hong dot ciangun, a masa penin Zomi ka hi hi, ka ci ngei hi.

records.english: Could you help me explain the word "Zomi" to my classmates?
records.zomi: “Zomi” kammal ka sang lawmte kiangah ka hilh nadingin hong huh thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: My cousin was born in the United States, but she still calls herself Zomi.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu United States ah a suak hangin, amah le amah Zomi a ci lai hi.

records.english: If you want to understand our community, you should come to one of our gatherings.
records.zomi: I mipi na theih nop leh, i kikhopna khat ah hong pai ding na hi hi.

records.english: We've been meeting every Saturday so the kids can practice reading in Zomi.
records.zomi: Naupangte in Zomi lai sim a sin thei nadingun Kiginni simin i kikhawm hi.

records.english: Why do some older people prefer a different name for our community?
records.zomi: Bang hangin upa pawlkhat in i mipi adingin min dang a deih zaw uh hiam?

records.english: I didn't realize how much my language meant to me until I moved away.
records.zomi: Ka pai khit ciang bekin ka pau in kei adingin bangzah thupi hiam ka thei hi.

records.english: My grandmother always reminds us that family comes first.
records.zomi: Ka pi in innkuan pen masa ding hi, ci-in hong phawksak tawntung hi.

records.english: You should ask the elders before you post photos of the ceremony online.
records.zomi: Poai limlakte online ah na koih ma-in upate na dong ding hi.

records.english: Thang feels more connected to his roots when he wears his traditional clothes.
records.zomi: Thang in a ngeina puan a silh ciangin a bulpi tawh a kizom zaw bang a kisa hi.

records.english: Our youth group is planning a cultural night to share Zomi songs and dances with our neighbors.
records.zomi: I khangno pawl in i inn vengte tawh Zomi la leh lam a kihawm nadingin ngeina zan khat a bawl ding uh hi.

records.english: I'm sorry I mispronounced your name, so could you say it again slowly?
records.zomi: Na min ka gen khial ahih manin hong maisak in, zawlzawl in gen kik thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Even though we live in different countries, we still share the same identity.
records.zomi: Gam tuamtuam ah i teen hangin, i kilatna khat mah i nei lai hi.

records.english: Have you ever been to a Zomi festival in your city?
records.zomi: Na khuapi ah Zomi pawi khat ah na pai ngei hiam?

records.english: My parents taught me to greet older people respectfully, no matter where we are.
records.zomi: Koi ah i om zongin, ka nu leh pa in upate zahtak takin hopih dingin hong hilh hi.

records.english: What does being Zomi mean to you personally?
records.zomi: Zomi na hihna in nang adingin bang khiatna a nei hiam?

records.english: Kim is writing a school report about her family's journey and her Zomi heritage.
records.zomi: Kim in a innkuan' khualzinna leh a Zomi ngeina thu sang lai khat a gelh hi.

records.english: We often switch between English and Zomi when we talk at dinner.
records.zomi: Nitak an nek laitakin English leh Zomi pau i kilaih ngei hi.

records.english: I'd love to learn more about the patterns woven into these shawls.
records.zomi: Hih puante sunga kiphuan limte thu ka sin zaw nuam mahmah hi.

records.english: The pastor encouraged young people to keep their language alive.
records.zomi: Pastor in khangnote in a pau uh a hing den nadingin a hanthawn hi.

records.english: Some kids at school had never heard of the Zomi people before I told them.
records.zomi: Sang a naupang pawlkhat in ka hilh ma-in Zomi mite thu za ngei lo uh hi.

records.english: Would you like to join us for a meal at our community center?
records.zomi: I mipi inn ah an ne khawm dingin hong pai nuam hiam?

records.english: My little brother gets confused when people think we're from another country.
records.zomi: Mite in gam dang pan hi uh hi, a ci ciangun ka nau pasal a lungbuai hi.

records.english: After the service, the women usually share news from relatives back home.
records.zomi: Biakna khit ciangin numeite in inn a om beh leh phungte thu a kihawm ngei uh hi.

records.english: Growing up between two cultures, I've learned that being Zomi isn't something I have to prove to anyone.
records.zomi: Ngeina nih kikal ah ka khan manin, Zomi ka hihna kuamah kiangah ka lak kul kei hi, ci ka thei hi.

records.english: Although our community is scattered across many countries, social media has made it easier to stay in touch.
records.zomi: I mipi gam tampi ah kitheh hangin, social media in kizom den theih nadingin a baihsak hi.

records.english: If my children forget the language, I worry they'll lose part of what connects them to their grandparents.
records.zomi: Ka tate in pau a mangngilh uh leh, a pu a pite uh tawh a kizopna uh a mansuah ding uh, ci-in ka lungkham hi.

records.english: What struck me most at the gathering was how quickly strangers became like family once they realized they were all Zomi.
records.zomi: Kikhopna ah lamdang ka sak pen in, Zomi ahih lam uh a theih ciangun mikhualte innkuan bangin a manlang takin a kipawl uh ahi hi.

records.english: Rather than choosing one identity over another, Esther has decided to embrace being both Zomi and Australian.
records.zomi: Kilatna khat teel sangin, Esther in Zomi leh Australian a hihna nih tengteng a pom hi.

records.english: Had my father not insisted on speaking Zomi at home, I probably wouldn't understand my grandmother's stories today.
records.zomi: Ka pa in inn ah Zomi pau zang dingin hong ngen ngiat kei nak leh, tu-in ka pi' tangthute ka theih kei kha ding hi.

records.english: It's worth remembering that people may use different names for their community, so it's best to ask how they prefer to be identified.
records.zomi: Mite in a mipi uh adingin min tuamtuam a zang thei uh ahih manin, amaute bangci sap a deih uh hiam dong masak ding a hoih hi.

records.english: The older generation often sees language as the heart of identity, whereas younger people may emphasize shared values and community ties.
records.zomi: Upate in pau pen kilatna' lungtang ahi hi, a ci ngei uh hi; khangnote in i kibatna ngaihsutna leh mipi kizopna a thupi sak zaw uh hi.

records.english: Whenever I fill out a form that doesn't list my ethnicity, I'm reminded how invisible small communities can feel.
records.zomi: Ka phung min a om lo form khat ka dim ciangin, mipi neute bangzah kimu lo bang hiam ka phawk hi.

records.english: Not only did the cultural night raise money for the youth program, but it also gave second-generation kids a chance to feel proud of who they are.
records.zomi: Ngeina zan in khangno nasep adingin sum a ngah bek thamlo-in, khangthak naupangte in amaute a hihna uh a kisaktheih nadingin hun a pia hi.

records.english: I'd recommend that newcomers find a local Zomi church or association, since it can make settling into a new city much less lonely.
records.zomi: Khuapi thak khat ah a teng thak mite' lungkhamna a kiam nadingin Zomi pawlpi hiam pawl hiam zong dingin ka deih hi.

records.english: My sister and I wear our Zomi clothes for family photos.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu leh kei innkuan limlak ah Zomi puan ka silh uh hi.

records.english: My grandmother tells us stories about Jesus every night.
records.zomi: Ka pi in zan simin Jesu thu hong gen hi.

records.english: According to the Gospels, Jesus was born in Bethlehem.
records.zomi: Lungdamna Thu bangin, Jesu pen Bethlehem ah suak hi.

records.english: Do you know the story of Jesus feeding a big crowd?
records.zomi: Jesu in mi tampi an a vak tangthu na thei hiam?

records.english: Please read the next verse aloud.
records.zomi: A zom Laisiangtho cang aw ngaih takin sim in.

records.english: In the Gospels, Jesus has twelve disciples.
records.zomi: Lungdamna Thu sungah Jesu in nungzui sawm leh nih a nei hi.

records.english: Our Sunday school class is learning about Jesus this month.
records.zomi: I Nipini sang pawl in tu kha sungin Jesu thu a sin hi.

records.english: Who did Jesus call to follow him first?
records.zomi: Jesu in a nungzui dingin kua a sam masa hiam?

records.english: In the Gospels, Jesus often teaches with short stories.
records.zomi: Lungdamna Thu sungah Jesu in thugentehna tomte tawh a hilh ngei hi.

records.english: Let's draw a picture of Jesus calming the storm.
records.zomi: Jesu in huihpi a nemsak lim gelh ni.

records.english: I really like the story about the lost sheep.
records.zomi: Tuu mangthang tangthu ka deih mahmah hi.

records.english: Where did Jesus grow up?
records.zomi: Jesu koi ah khang hiam?

records.english: The Gospels say that Jesus grew up in Nazareth.
records.zomi: Lungdamna Thu in Jesu pen Nazareth ah khang hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Is this the story where Jesus walks on water?
records.zomi: Hih pen Jesu tui tungah a pai tangthu hi hiam?

records.english: My little brother asked me why Jesus went into the desert.
records.zomi: Ka nau pasal in bang hangin Jesu gam lak ah pai hiam hong dong hi.

records.english: Open your Bibles to the Gospel of Mark, please.
records.zomi: Na Laisiangtho uh Marka Lungdamna Thu ah hong un.

records.english: Jesus is kind to children in the stories we read.
records.zomi: I sim tangthute sungah Jesu in naupangte tungah a hehpih hi.

records.english: We sang a song about Jesus at church today.
records.zomi: Tuni biakinn ah Jesu thu la khat i sa hi.

records.english: Can you tell me about the Last Supper?
records.zomi: Nitak An Nunung thu hong gen thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: The Gospels tell us that Jesus was baptized in the Jordan River.
records.zomi: Lungdamna Thu in Jesu Jordan Lui ah kibaptaiz hi, hong ci hi.

records.english: Don't forget to bring your Bible to class tomorrow.
records.zomi: Zingciang class ah na Laisiangtho tawi ding mangngilh kei in.

records.english: What a beautiful story that is!
records.zomi: Tua tangthu a hoih mahmah hi ve!

records.english: Mom read us the story of the wedding at Cana.
records.zomi: Nu in Kana khua a kiteenna tangthu hong sim sak hi.

records.english: Did Jesus have brothers and sisters?
records.zomi: Jesu in sanggam pasal leh numeite a nei hiam?

records.english: Jesus heals many sick people in the Gospel stories.
records.zomi: Lungdamna Thu tangthute sungah Jesu in mi dam lo tampi a damsak hi.

records.english: When I was a child, my father used to explain the parables to us after dinner.
records.zomi: Ka naupan lai-in ka pa in nitak an khit ciangin thugentehnate hong hilhcian ngei hi.

records.english: Our pastor said that Jesus spent a lot of time with people others ignored.
records.zomi: I pastor in Jesu pen mi dangte in a lim loh mite tawh hun tampi a zang hi, a ci hi.

records.english: If you're new to the Bible, I'd suggest starting with the Gospel of Luke.
records.zomi: Laisiangtho na sim thak leh, Luka Lungdamna Thu tawh kipan dingin ka hilh ding hi.

records.english: Could you explain why Jesus spoke in parables instead of giving direct answers?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Jesu in a dawnna tangtak a piak sangin thugentehna tawh a gen hiam hong hilhcian thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Christians believe that Jesus was baptized by John before beginning his public ministry.
records.zomi: Christian te in Jesu pen mipi lakah a nasep a kipat ma-in Johan in a baptaiz hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: We've been reading one chapter of Matthew every evening as a family.
records.zomi: Innkuan khat bangin nitak simin Matthai cangpi khat i sim uh hi.

records.english: The kids were surprised to learn that Jesus washed his disciples' feet.
records.zomi: Jesu in a nungzuite' khe a sil cih a theih ciangun naupangte lamdang a sa uh hi.

records.english: Have you ever wondered what Jesus did during his years in Nazareth?
records.zomi: Jesu in Nazareth ah a om kumte sungin bang a sem hiam, ci-in na ngaihsun ngei hiam?

records.english: While we were cooking, Grace kept asking questions about the Sermon on the Mount.
records.zomi: An i huan laitakin, Grace in Mual Tung Thugen thu a dong tawntung hi.

records.english: You should try reading the story of the Good Samaritan from the point of view of the injured man.
records.zomi: Samari mi hoih tangthu pen a liamna pa' et dan tawh sim dingin na hanciam ding hi.

records.english: I'm sorry I missed Bible study, because I heard you talked about the feeding of the five thousand.
records.zomi: Mi tul nga an a vakna thu na kikum uh hi, ka za a, Laisiangtho sinna ah ka pai kei ahih manin hong maisak in.

records.english: In our village church, the elders often retell the story of the prodigal son during harvest season.
records.zomi: I khua neu pawlpi ah, upate in buh lak hun ciangin tapa mangthang tangthu a gen kik ngei uh hi.

records.english: My niece was amazed that Jesus took time to talk with a woman at a well.
records.zomi: Ka tunu in Jesu in tuikhuk kiangah numei khat tawh kiho dingin hun a piak cih ah lamdang a sa hi.

records.english: Why do you think Jesus chose ordinary fishermen as his followers?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Jesu in nga man mi pangai mite a nungzui dingin a teel hiam na ci hiam?

records.english: Would you like to join us for a short study on the miracles of Jesus?
records.zomi: Jesu' na lamdang bawlte i sinna tomno ah hong kihel nuam hiam?

records.english: The story of Zacchaeus climbing a tree always makes my students laugh.
records.zomi: Zakkhias in singkung tung a kah tangthu in ka sangnaupangte a nuihsak tawntung hi.

records.english: According to the Gospels, Jesus often went off alone early in the morning to pray.
records.zomi: Lungdamna Thu bangin, Jesu in thu ngen dingin zingsang tuungin amah bek a pai ngei hi.

records.english: Let's act out the parable of the sower for the children's program next Sunday.
records.zomi: Nipini a zom naupangte program adingin khaici vawhpa thugentehna lim lak ni.

records.english: I didn't understand the story of the talents until my teacher explained it simply.
records.zomi: Ka sia in baih takin a hilhcian dong telen tangthu ka thei kei hi.

records.english: Many Christians read about the life of Jesus during the weeks before Easter.
records.zomi: Christian tampi in Easter ma-a kalte sungin Jesu' nuntakna thu a sim uh hi.

records.english: Before the meal, Uncle Thang reminded everyone how Jesus gave thanks before breaking bread.
records.zomi: An nek ma-in, Pu Thang in Jesu in moh a phel ma-in lungdam a ko hi, ci-in mi khempeuh a phawksak hi.

records.english: Make sure each group reads a different miracle story and shares it with the class.
records.zomi: Lom khat ciat in na lamdang tangthu tuamtuam sim unla, class tawh kihawm un.

records.english: Jesus is remembered for welcoming children when his disciples tried to send them away.
records.zomi: A nungzuite in naupangte a nawlkhiat sawm ciangun Jesu in naupangte a muak hi, ci-in kiphawk hi.

records.english: I've always found the story of Jesus weeping at his friend's tomb very moving.
records.zomi: Jesu in a lawm' han kiangah a kah tangthu in ka lungsim a tawng mahmah tawntung hi.

records.english: Although the parables seem simple at first, my Sunday school students often find that they raise surprisingly difficult questions.
records.zomi: Thugentehnate a masa-in baih bang hi napi, ka Nipini sangnaupangte in dotna haksa a piangsak hi, ci a thei ngei uh hi.

records.english: Had I read the Gospels more carefully as a teenager, I might have noticed how often Jesus ate with people considered outsiders.
records.zomi: Khangno ka hih lai-in Lungdamna Thu cingtak zawin ka sim nak leh, Jesu in polam mite tawh bangzah vei an a ne hiam ka thei kha ding hi.

records.english: Christians traditionally interpret the temptation in the wilderness as showing that Jesus faced real struggles while remaining faithful.
records.zomi: Christian te in gam lak ah a kizetna pen Jesu in a muanhuai den laitakin haksatna taktak a thuak hi, a lakna hi, ci-in a theih ngei uh hi.

records.english: What strikes me most about the ministry of Jesus is how much of it took place in ordinary homes, fields, and roadsides.
records.zomi: Jesu' nasepna ah lamdang ka sak pen in, a tampi zaw pen inn pangai, lo leh lampi gei ah a piang hi.

records.english: It wasn't until our youth group compared all four Gospels that we realized each writer tells the story with a slightly different emphasis.
records.zomi: I khangno pawl in Lungdamna Thu li tengteng a kiteh ciang bekin, a gelhtu khat ciat in tangthu tawm khat a tuam deuh-in a gen uh hi, ci i thei hi.

records.english: Rather than memorizing the miracles as a list, try asking what each one reveals about the people Jesus met.
records.zomi: Na lamdangte list bangin ciamteh sangin, khat ciat in Jesu' a muh mite thu bang a lak hiam, dong dingin hanciam in.

records.english: If our grandparents hadn't kept reading the Bible aloud at home, many of us would never have learned the stories of Jesus' ministry.
records.zomi: I pu i pite in inn ah Laisiangtho aw ngaih takin a sim den kei nak uh leh, i lak pan mi tampi in Jesu' nasepna tangthute i sin ngei kei kha ding hi.

records.english: Many believers say that the way Jesus treated the poor challenges them to rethink how they spend their own money and time.
records.zomi: Upmi tampi in Jesu in mi zawngte a et dan in amau' sum leh hun zat dan a ngaihsun kik sak hi, a ci uh hi.

records.english: Whenever my daughter asks why Jesus didn't simply avoid the people who opposed him, I try to give her an honest, age-appropriate answer.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in bang hangin Jesu in a langpangte a pelh lo hiam, hong dot ciangin, a kum tawh kituak dawnna tangtak pia dingin ka hanciam hi.

records.english: Would it be possible for you to lead a discussion on how the healing stories might have been understood by the people who first heard them?
records.zomi: Damsakna tangthute a za masa mite in bangci a theih kha uh hiam cih kikupna khat na makai thei ding hiam?

records.english: The more I study the Gospels, the more I notice how patiently Jesus responded to his disciples' misunderstandings.
records.zomi: Lungdamna Thu ka sin semsem ciangin, Jesu in a nungzuite' a theih khialhnate bangzah thuakzawh takin a dawng hiam ka mu semsem hi.

records.english: In many Christian homes, telling the story of the nativity has become a way for parents to pass on both faith and family tradition.
records.zomi: Christian inn tampi ah, Jesu suahna tangthu gen pen nu leh pate in upna leh innkuan ngeina a tate tungah a piak nading lampi khat suak hi.

records.english: Our office cleaner says good evening to everyone in three languages.
records.zomi: I office siangsaktu in mi khempeuh pau thum tawh “Nitakpha” a ci hi.

records.english: The night nurses say good morning to the day nurses at seven o'clock.
records.zomi: Zan nurse te in nai sagih ciangin sun nurse te kiangah “Zingpha” a ci uh hi.

records.english: The principal had the older students welcome the new children on the first morning of term.
records.zomi: Sang makaipa in kum lian zaw sangnaupangte in sang kipat zingsang masa pen ah naupang thakte a muak sak hi.

records.english: Morning, Pau!
records.zomi: Pau, zingpha!

records.english: Good morning, Director Pau.
records.zomi: Director Pau, zingpha.

records.english: Nobody may leave the hall until the headmaster has finished his morning greeting.
records.zomi: Sang makaipa in a zingpha kihopihna a zawh ma-in kuamah inn lianpi pan pai khia thei lo hi.

records.english: Please say good morning to the visiting inspectors on behalf of the whole staff.
records.zomi: Nasemte khempeuh aiawhin hong veh enkaktu te kiangah “Zingpha” ci in.

records.english: The boss might greet us in person this evening, or she might just send a video message.
records.zomi: Tu nitakin a ukpa nu in amah mah in hong hopih kha ding hi, ahih kei leh video thu khat bek a khak kha ding hi.

records.english: If the receptionist greeted visitors more warmly, fewer of them would complain about the long wait.
records.zomi: Mai lam ngaktu in mikhualte lungdam zawin a hopih leh, ngak sawtna thu a phun mi a tawm zaw ding uh hi.

records.english: Good evening — sorry I'm late for the night class.
records.zomi: Nitakpha — zan class ah ka zekai ahih manin hong maisak un.

records.english: We arrive ten minutes early so that we can greet our students at the door.
records.zomi: I sangnaupangte kongkhak ah i hopih theih nadingin minit sawm a masa-in i tung hi.

records.english: What surprised me on my first day of teaching was that the students greeted me before I could greet them.
records.zomi: Sia ka sep ni masa pen ah lamdang ka sak pen in, ka hopih ma-un sangnaupangte in hong hopih masa uh hi.

records.english: How long have you been greeting customers at this bank?
records.zomi: Hih bank ah bangzah sawt mite na hopih khin hiam?

records.english: I've been doing it for about six years, ever since this branch opened.
records.zomi: Hih branch a kihon pan kipan kum guk bang ka sem khin hi.

records.english: Good evening, everyone, and welcome to tonight's parent-teacher meeting.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh nitakpha, tu zan nu leh pate leh sia kikhopna ah na hong tun uh lungdam hi.

records.english: Did you say good afternoon to the new cook?
records.zomi: An huan thak kiangah “Sunpha” na ci hiam?

records.english: Lian greets the cleaning staff every evening before she leaves the office.
records.zomi: Lian in office a paisan ma-in nitak simin siangsaktu nasemte a hopih hi.

records.english: Good morning, class — please take your seats.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte zingpha — na tutna uah tu un.

records.english: The team members greet one another before the morning meeting.
records.zomi: Zingsang kikhopna ma-in pawl mite kihopih uh hi.

records.english: Good morning, Doctor.
records.zomi: Siavuan, zingpha.

records.english: May I say good morning to the whole team over the loudspeaker?
records.zomi: Loudspeaker tungtawnin pawl khempeuh kiangah “Zingpha” ka ci thei ding hiam?

records.english: The headmistress insisted that every teacher be standing at the classroom door when the morning bell rang.
records.zomi: Sang makai nu in zingsang kalai a ging ciangin sia khempeuh class kongkhak ah ding ding hi, ci-in a ngen ngiat hi.

records.english: Good night, everyone — see you at work tomorrow.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh zanpha — zingciang nasepna ah kimu kik ni.

records.english: Our teacher makes us stand up and say good morning together at the start of every lesson.
records.zomi: I sia in sinna kipat simin hong dingsak a, “Zingpha” i ci khawm uh hi.

records.english: It was only after she had greeted every employee personally that the director began her speech.
records.zomi: Nasem khempeuh amah mah in a hopih khit ciang bekin director in a thugen a kipan hi.

records.english: Children may greet their teachers with either a bow or a handshake.
records.zomi: Naupangte in a siate uh kun-in hiam, khut kiman-in hiam a hopih thei uh hi.

records.english: Can I leave early tonight if I say good evening to the manager first?
records.zomi: Ukpa kiangah “Nitakpha” ka ci masak leh tu zanin ka pai masa thei ding hiam?

records.english: I've been working here for three weeks, and the receptionist still greets me by the wrong name.
records.zomi: Hih munah kal thum ka sem khin a, mai lam ngaktu in min khial tawh hong hopih lai hi.

records.english: The principal had her morning greeting recorded so that teachers who missed the assembly could listen to it later.
records.zomi: Kikhopna ah a kihel lo siate in a nung ciangin a ngaih theih nadingun sang makai nu in a zingpha kihopihna a gelh sak hi.

records.english: The security guard greets every worker at the factory gate at six o'clock.
records.zomi: Ngaktu in nai guk ciangin factory kongpi ah nasem khempeuh a hopih hi.

records.english: The cafeteria workers greet the children with a song each morning.
records.zomi: Anneekna nasemte in zingsang simin la tawh naupangte a hopih uh hi.

records.english: Our coach said we were not allowed to skip the morning greeting before practice.
records.zomi: I coach in sinna ma-a zingpha kihopihna i nusia thei kei hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Mr. Pau told us that he had been greeting students at the school gate for twenty years.
records.zomi: Pu Pau in kum sawmnih sung sang kongpi ah sangnaupangte a hopih khin hi, hong ci hi.

records.english: Good morning — is this the staff room?
records.zomi: Zingpha — hih pen siate' khan hi hiam?

records.english: Remember to greet the guard when you walk through the gate.
records.zomi: Kongpi na pai pelh ciangin ngaktu hopih ding phawk in.

records.english: Our manager asked us to greet customers within ten seconds of their arrival.
records.zomi: I ukpa in mite a hong tun pan second sawm sungin hopih dingin hong ngen hi.

records.english: Greeting a room full of tired evening students is harder than it sounds, especially when many of them have come straight from work.
records.zomi: Gim nitak sangnaupang a dim khan khat hopih pen a kigen sangin a haksa zaw hi, a diakin amau lak pan tampi nasepna pan a hong pai pah uh ahih manin.

records.english: At this school, do the teachers say good morning first, or do the students?
records.zomi: Hih sang ah, siate in “Zingpha” a ci masa uh hiam, sangnaupangte in hiam?

records.english: A sincere good morning from a supervisor can change how a nervous trainee feels about the whole day.
records.zomi: Ukpa khat' lungsim taktak tawh “Zingpha” a cih in lau sinna mi khat' ni bup a lungsim a laih thei hi.

records.english: Thang wondered whether greeting his boss with "good afternoon" at eleven-thirty would seem careless or simply relaxed.
records.zomi: Thang in nai sawm leh khat leh a lang ciangin a ukpa “Sunpha” tawh a hopih leh limlo bang hiam, nopsakna bang hiam a kisa ding, ci-in a ngaihsun hi.

records.english: The teacher wished the class a good afternoon and let them go home.
records.zomi: Sia in class kiangah “Sunpha” a ci a, inn ah a paisak hi.

records.english: The factory owner, who rarely visits the floor, surprised the workers one afternoon by greeting each of them by name.
records.zomi: Factory sung a hong pai ngei lo factory neipa in sun khat ciangin nasem khat ciat a min tawh a hopih ciangin nasemte lamdang a sa uh hi.

records.english: To make new staff feel welcome, our team leader greets each of them personally on their first morning.
records.zomi: Nasem thakte in lungdamna a ngah nadingun, i pawl makaipa in amaute zingsang masa pen ah khat ciat a hopih hi.

records.english: Good afternoon, Professor Lian.
records.zomi: Professor Lian, sunpha.

records.english: Students are not allowed to shout greetings in the hallways during exams.
records.zomi: Sitna hun sungin sangnaupangte in inn sung lampi ah kikou-in kihopih thei lo uh hi.

records.english: By the time the night shift begins at ten, the cleaners will have greeted every guard coming on duty.
records.zomi: Nai sawm ciangin zan nasep a kipat ma-in, siangsaktute in nasep a hong lut ngaktu khempeuh a hopih khin ding uh hi.

records.english: Mrs. Niang has taught for thirty years, yet she still feels nervous before greeting a new class on the first morning of the school year.
records.zomi: Niang nu in kum sawmthum sung sia a sem khin hangin, sang kum kipatna zingsang masa pen ah class thak a hopih ma-in a lau lai hi.

records.english: Good evening, students — tonight's class will end at nine.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte nitakpha — tu zan class nai kua ciangin bei ding hi.

records.english: Could you greet the visitors in the lobby for me while I finish this call?
records.zomi: Hih phone ka sam zawh ma-in, lobby ah mikhualte keima' aiawhin na hopih thei ding hiam?

records.english: Thank you for greeting my parents at the school gate this afternoon.
records.zomi: Tu sun sang kongpi ah ka nu leh pa na hopih ahih manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: Every morning, our supervisor shakes our hands and asks whether we slept well.
records.zomi: Zingsang simin i ukpa in i khut hong man a, i ihmut a nuam hiam hong dong hi.

records.english: We greet our boss with a smile every morning.
records.zomi: Zingsang simin nuihmai tawh i ukpa i hopih hi.

records.english: Kim says the new manager greets everyone warmly in the morning but hardly speaks to anyone after lunch.
records.zomi: Kim in ukpa thak in zingsangin mi khempeuh lungdam takin a hopih hi, ahi zongin sun an khit ciangin kuamah tawh a kiho tawm mahmah hi, a ci hi.

records.english: I'll greet the new teacher for you, since you have a class at eight.
records.zomi: Nai giat ciangin na class a om ahih manin, nang aiawhin sia thak ka hopih ding hi.

records.english: Good afternoon, sir — how may I help you?
records.zomi: Pu, sunpha — bangci kong huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: You may not answer your phone while you are greeting a client.
records.zomi: Mi khat na hopih laitakin na phone na dawng thei kei hi.

records.english: Good morning, Thang — did you finish your report?
records.zomi: Thang zingpha — na report na zo khin hiam?

records.english: The trainer spent the first fifteen minutes of the workshop greeting participants and learning their names.
records.zomi: Sinsaktu in workshop' minit sawm leh nga masa pen mite hopih leh a min uh sin-in a zang hi.

records.english: When the new intern arrived, nobody greeted her, so she sat alone until lunch.
records.zomi: Intern thak a hong tun ciangin kuamah in a hopih kei uh ahih manin, sun an dong amah bek a tu hi.

records.english: Is it rude to say "hi" to the principal instead of "good morning"?
records.zomi: Sang makaipa kiangah “Zingpha” ci lo-in “Hi” ci pen zahtak lohna hi hiam?

records.english: How was your afternoon at the river?
records.zomi: Lui ah na sun hun bangci om hiam?

records.english: It was wonderful; we swam for two hours and caught three fish.
records.zomi: A nuam mahmah hi; nai nih sung tui ka peek uh a, nga thum ka man uh hi.

records.english: How long did you chat with Mr. Thang after you greeted him this evening?
records.zomi: Tu nitakin Pu Thang na hopih khit ciangin bangzah sawt na kiho uh hiam?

records.english: We talked for nearly an hour on his front porch.
records.zomi: A inn mai ah nai khat bang ka kiho uh hi.

records.english: Isn't it a bit early to say good night?
records.zomi: “Zanpha” ci dingin a tuung deuh lo hiam?

records.english: It is early, but I have to catch the first bus tomorrow morning.
records.zomi: A tuung hi, ahi zongin zingciang zingsang bus masa pen ka tuan ding hi.

records.english: Asked why she greets every passerby before sunrise, the old baker replied that a kind word is the best way to begin anyone's day.
records.zomi: Bang hangin ni a suah ma-in a pai khia mi khempeuh a hopih hiam, a kidot ciangin, moh bawl pi in kammal hoih khat pen mi khatpeuh' ni kipat nading lampi hoih pen ahi hi, ci-in a dawng hi.

records.english: Has the sun come up yet?
records.zomi: Ni a suak khin hiam?

records.english: Not yet, but the birds are already singing outside.
records.zomi: Suak nai lo hi, ahi zongin a polam ah vasate a sa khin uh hi.

records.english: Can I say good morning at eleven o'clock?
records.zomi: Nai sawm leh khat ciangin “Zingpha” ka ci thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, you can say good morning until noon.
records.zomi: Thei hi, sun laitak dong “Zingpha” na ci thei hi.

records.english: What do you say to the bus driver when you get on in the afternoon?
records.zomi: Sun lamin bus na tuan ciangin bus mawngtu kiangah bang na ci ngei hiam?

records.english: I usually just say good afternoon, and then I thank him when I get off.
records.zomi: “Sunpha” bek ka ci ngei a, ka tum ciangin lungdam ka ko hi.

records.english: Is it considered impolite to greet an elderly neighbor with a simple wave instead of actually saying good morning?
records.zomi: Upa inn veng khat “Zingpha” ci lo-in khut lap bek tawh hopih pen zahtak lohna a kisa hiam?

records.english: Most of our older neighbors appreciate hearing the words, but a warm wave from across the street is rarely taken as rude.
records.zomi: I inn veng upate in kammal a zak uh a deih zaw uh hi, ahi zongin lampi galkhat pan lungdam taka khut lap pen zahtak lohna-in a ngaihsun tawm hi.

records.english: Whose dog barks at everyone who says good morning on this street?
records.zomi: Hih lampi ah “Zingpha” a ci mi khempeuh a hamsak ui pen kua' ui hiam?

records.english: That noisy brown dog is Mrs. Niang's, but it is really very friendly.
records.zomi: Tua ui sangdup ging buai pen Niang nu' ui ahi hi, ahi zongin a lawmsiam mahmah hi.

records.english: This morning, Pau knocked on his neighbor's door.
records.zomi: Tu zingsangin Pau in a inn veng' kongkhak a kiu hi.

records.english: When the old man opened it, Pau greeted him and asked how he had slept.
records.zomi: Pu upa in a hon ciangin, Pau in a hopih a, a ihmut a nuam hiam a dong hi.

records.english: The neighbor answered that he had slept badly because of the storm during the night.
records.zomi: Zan in huihpi hangin a ihmut a nuam kei hi, ci-in a inn veng in a dawng hi.

records.english: Did my loud good morning wake you?
records.zomi: Ka “Zingpha” ging khauh in hong phawng hiam?

records.english: No, the rooster woke me long before you came in.
records.zomi: Hong phawng kei hi, na hong lut ma-in akpi in hong phawng khin hi.

records.english: How did you say good morning to your aunt when she lives so far away?
records.zomi: Na ni gamla takah a om ciangin bangci “Zingpha” na ci hiam?

records.english: I sent her a short voice message with my phone.
records.zomi: Ka phone tawh aw thu tomno khat ka khak hi.

records.english: At sunset, the tired travelers reached a small village.
records.zomi: Ni a tum ciangin, khualzin gimte khua neu khat ah a tung uh hi.

records.english: An old woman sitting outside her house greeted them and offered them water.
records.zomi: A inn polam a tu numei upa khat in a hopih a, tui a pia hi.

records.english: Grateful for her kindness, they stayed and talked with her until long after dark.
records.zomi: A hehpihna lungdam a sak manun, khua a mial khit sawtpi dong amah tawh a kiho uh hi.

records.english: Good morning, Mrs. Cing — how is your knee today?
records.zomi: Cing nu, zingpha — tuni na khuk bangci om hiam?

records.english: Good morning — it's much better, thank you for asking.
records.zomi: Zingpha — a hoih zaw mahmah hi, hong dot ka lungdam hi.

records.english: When do people here stop saying good afternoon and start saying good evening?
records.zomi: Hih munah mite in bang hun ciangin “Sunpha” ci tawp-in “Nitakpha” a ci kipan uh hiam?

records.english: After about six o'clock, most people here switch to good evening.
records.zomi: Nai guk khit ciangin hih munah mi tampi in “Nitakpha” a ci uh hi.

records.english: Would you mind telling me whether people in your town still greet strangers on the road in the early morning?
records.zomi: Na khua ah zingsang tuungin lampi ah mikhualte a hopih lai uh hiam, hong gen thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Many of the older people still do, but the younger ones mostly keep their eyes on their phones.
records.zomi: Upa tampi in a hopih lai uh hi, ahi zongin khangnote in a phone uh bek a en uh hi.

records.english: Are you awake, Grandpa?
records.zomi: Pu, na khanglo khin hiam?

records.english: Yes, I am awake — good morning, my dear.
records.zomi: Ka khanglo khin hi — zingpha, ka it.

records.english: When it's evening here and morning where your brother lives, which greeting do you use on a video call?
records.zomi: Hih munah nitak a hih laitakin na sanggam pasal' omna ah zingsang a hih leh, video call ah bang kihopihna na zang hiam?

records.english: I usually say good morning, since his day is the one that's just beginning.
records.zomi: Amah' ni a kipan pan ahih manin “Zingpha” ka ci ngei hi.

records.english: What's the proper way to greet a pastor on Sunday evening?
records.zomi: Nipini nitakin pastor bangci hopih ding a kilawm hiam?

records.english: A respectful nod and a quiet good evening are usually enough.
records.zomi: Zahtak takin lu ngun leh dai takin “Nitakpha” cih a cin ngei hi.

records.english: Who rang the doorbell this morning?
records.zomi: Tu zingsangin kongkhak daak kua in a kiat hiam?

records.english: The mail carrier rang it to hand us a package, and she wished us good morning too.
records.zomi: Lai puaktu nu in thuamhual khat hong piak nadingin a kiat a, “Zingpha” zong hong ci hi.

records.english: How long had the visitors been waiting in the cold before anyone came out to greet them?
records.zomi: Kuamah in a hopih dingin a polam a pai ma-in mikhualte vot lak ah bangzah sawt ngak uh hiam?

records.english: They had been standing by the gate for about twenty minutes, so we apologized and invited them in.
records.zomi: Kongpi kiangah minit sawmnih bang a ding uh ahih manin, hong maisak un ci-in a sung ah ka sam uh hi.

records.english: With a flashlight in one hand, the night guard waved good evening to us with the other.
records.zomi: Zan ngaktu in khut khat ah meivak tawi-in, khut khatlam tawh “Nitakpha” ci-in hong khut lap hi.

records.english: Who was the first person to greet you this morning?
records.zomi: Tu zingsangin kua in hong hopih masa hiam?

records.english: My little sister was, because she climbed onto my bed and shouted good morning in my ear.
records.zomi: Ka nau numei in hong hopih masa hi, ka lupna tungah kah-in ka bil ah “Zingpha” a kikou hi.

records.english: Did the baby wake up before sunrise again?
records.zomi: Naungek ni a suah ma-in a khanglo kik hiam?

records.english: She did wake up early, but she smiled at me when I said good morning.
records.zomi: A khanglo tuung hi, ahi zongin “Zingpha” ka cih ciangin hong nuihmai hi.

records.english: Good evening, everyone — have you all eaten dinner?
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh nitakpha — nitak an na ne khin uh hiam?

records.english: Yes, we have, and we saved a plate for you.
records.zomi: Ka ne khin uh hi, nang adingin kuang khat ka koih uh hi.

records.english: Why do you suppose the hotel staff greeted us with good evening even though it was barely four o'clock?
records.zomi: Nai li pha nai lo napi zinbuuk nasemte in bang hangin “Nitakpha” tawh hong hopih uh hiam na ci hiam?

records.english: They were probably following a rule that the evening greeting begins once the afternoon shift takes over.
records.zomi: Sun nasep pawl in a laih ciangin nitak kihopihna kipan hi, cih thukham a zui uh kha ding hi.

records.english: How do people greet each other in the evening at the market?
records.zomi: Zuakna mun ah nitakin mite bangci kihopih uh hiam?

records.english: Most sellers just call out good evening and ask what you need.
records.zomi: Zuaktu tampi in “Nitakpha” ci-in na kisapna a dong uh hi.

records.english: Why are you up so early, Lian?
records.zomi: Lian, bang hangin tuung mahmah in na tho hiam?

records.english: I got up early to watch the sunrise from the hill.
records.zomi: Mual tung pan ni suah en dingin ka tho tuung hi.

records.english: Did Pau come over just to say good evening?
records.zomi: Pau “Nitakpha” ci dingin bek a hong pai hiam?

records.english: He came over to return my ladder and to wish us a pleasant evening.
records.zomi: Ka kahlei hong ap kik dingin leh nitak nuam takin om dingin hong ci dingin a hong pai hi.

records.english: Do you greet your neighbors in the morning?
records.zomi: Zingsangin na inn vengte na hopih hiam?

records.english: Yes, I do, and they always greet me back.
records.zomi: Ka hopih hi, amaute in zong hong hopih kik tawntung uh hi.

records.english: Who are these flowers for?
records.zomi: Hih pakte kua adingin hiam?

records.english: They're for my mother, because today is her birthday.
records.zomi: Ka nu adingin ahi hi, tuni a pianni ahih manin.

records.english: Who is your favorite aunt?
records.zomi: Na ni lak pan kua na it pen hiam?

records.english: Aunt Dim is my favorite because she always makes me laugh.
records.zomi: Ni Dim in hong nuihsak tawntung ahih manin ka it pen hi.

records.english: Who would have guessed that my shy younger brother would end up becoming a teacher?
records.zomi: Ka nau pasal maizum in sia hong suak ding hi, ci kua in a ngaihsun ding hiam?

records.english: Who is responsible for making sure Grandpa takes his medicine every day?
records.zomi: Pu in ni simin a zatui a zat nadingin kua in a mawhpuak hiam?

records.english: My cousin Niang stops by every morning to make sure he takes it.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam Niang in a zat nadingin zingsang simin a hong pai hi.

records.english: Who would you want to raise your children if something happened to you and your husband?
records.zomi: Nang leh na pasal tungah bangzah hiam a tun leh, na tate kua in a khoi ding na deih hiam?

records.english: We would want my sister Cing to raise them, since the kids already adore her.
records.zomi: Naupangte in a it khin mahmah uh ahih manin, ka sanggam nu Cing in a khoi ding ka deih uh hi.

records.english: The relative I feel closest to is my great-uncle, who raised me while my parents were working in the city.
records.zomi: Ka naih pen beh leh phung pen ka nu leh pa khuapi ah a sep laitakun hong khoi ka pu ahi hi.

records.english: Nobody in the family remembers who planted the mango tree behind the house.
records.zomi: Inn nunglam a om haigah kung kua in a suan hiam innkuan sungah kuamah in a phawk kei uh hi.

records.english: Who in your family has lived abroad the longest?
records.zomi: Na innkuan sungah gamdang ah kua a om sawt pen hiam?

records.english: My uncle has been working in Malaysia for over fifteen years.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in Malaysia ah kum sawm leh nga val na a sem khin hi.

records.english: Who said we couldn't keep a dog?
records.zomi: Ui i khawi thei lo ding hi, kua in a ci hiam?

records.english: Dad said that dogs aren't allowed in our apartment building.
records.zomi: I teenna inn ah ui khawi phal lo hi, Pa in a ci hi.

records.english: Who made you cry?
records.zomi: Kua in hong kapsak hiam?

records.english: Nobody made me cry; I just miss my mom.
records.zomi: Kuamah in hong kapsak kei hi; ka nu ka ngaih bek hi.

records.english: Who should the school contact in case of an emergency?
records.zomi: Thu haksa a tun ciangin sang in kua a sam ding hiam?

records.english: You need to call my husband first, and then me.
records.zomi: Ka pasal na sam masa ding a, tua khit ciangin kei hong sam in.

records.english: Who did your sister marry?
records.zomi: Na sanggam nu in kua a teenpih hiam?

records.english: She married a nurse named Lian from the next village.
records.zomi: A zom khua pan nurse Lian a kici khat a teenpih hi.

records.english: Who taught you to ride a bicycle?
records.zomi: Siiksakol tuan kua in hong hilh hiam?

records.english: My cousin Pau taught me when I was seven.
records.zomi: Ka kum sagih lai-in ka sanggam Pau in hong hilh hi.

records.english: Who needs to sign my permission slip, Mom or Dad?
records.zomi: Ka phalna lai kua in min a gelh ding hiam, Nu hiam Pa hiam?

records.english: Either of us can sign it, but it has to be returned by Friday.
records.zomi: Kua in zong min a gelh thei hi, ahi zongin Laithai ni ma-in ap kik ding hi.

records.english: Who are you to tell me how to raise my own children?
records.zomi: Ka tate bangci ka khoi ding hiam hong hilh dingin nang kua na hi hiam?

records.english: Do you know who my father worked for before he started his own business?
records.zomi: Ka pa in amah' sumbawlna a kipat ma-in kua adingin na a sem hiam na thei hiam?

records.english: Who is the oldest of your brothers?
records.zomi: Na sanggam pasalte lakah kua a upa pen hiam?

records.english: Thang is the oldest, and he just turned twenty-five.
records.zomi: Thang a upa pen a, kum sawmnih leh nga a pha thak hi.

records.english: Who chose your name?
records.zomi: Na min kua in a teel hiam?

records.english: My grandfather chose it before I was born.
records.zomi: Ka suah ma-in ka pu in a teel hi.

records.english: Who should we ask to be the baby's godmother?
records.zomi: Naungek' pasian nu dingin kua i ngen ding hiam?

records.english: I think we should ask your cousin Mary, since she has stood by us through every hardship.
records.zomi: Haksatna khempeuh ah hong pang den ahih manin, na sanggam nu Mary i ngen ding hi, ci-in ka ngaihsun hi.

records.english: Who is the baby in this photo?
records.zomi: Hih limlak sung naungek pen kua hiam?

records.english: That's me, a few days after I was born.
records.zomi: Tua pen kei ka hi hi, ka suah khit ni tawmno.

records.english: Who let the kids stay up so late?
records.zomi: Naupangte bangzah zanin om sak kua in a phal hiam?

records.english: Their grandfather let them watch a movie until midnight.
records.zomi: A pu uh in zan laitak dong movie et a phal hi.

records.english: Tell me who you were with last night.
records.zomi: Zan in kua tawh na om hiam hong gen in.

records.english: Who was it that convinced you to move back home?
records.zomi: Inn ah a pem kik dingin kua in hong ciam sak hiam?

records.english: It was my mother; she told me she missed having me around.
records.zomi: Ka nu ahi hi; ka om nawn loh a ngaih hi, hong ci hi.

records.english: Who gets to sit in the front seat?
records.zomi: Mai lam tutna ah kua a tu ding hiam?

records.english: Grandma always sits in front because of her bad knee.
records.zomi: A khuk a nat manin Pi mai lam ah a tu tawntung hi.

records.english: Who do you live with?
records.zomi: Kua tawh na teeng hiam?

records.english: I live with my parents and my two younger sisters.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh pa leh ka nau numei nihte tawh ka teeng hi.

records.english: Who isn't allowed to eat peanuts in your family?
records.zomi: Na innkuan sungah kua in bekang ne thei lo hiam?

records.english: My youngest son can't have them because he's allergic.
records.zomi: Ka tapa neu pen in a ne thei kei hi, a tak tawh kituak lo ahih manin.

records.english: Who are you saving all this money for?
records.zomi: Hih sum khempeuh kua adingin na khol hiam?

records.english: I'm putting it aside so that my daughter won't have to borrow money for college.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in sangpi adingin sum a leitawi kul loh nadingin ka khol hi.

records.english: Who is going to watch the children while you're at the hospital?
records.zomi: Zato ah na om sungin naupangte kua in a ma ding hiam?

records.english: My mother-in-law is coming to our house to take care of them.
records.zomi: Ka sungnu in a ma dingin i inn ah a hong pai ding hi.

records.english: Who wants to visit Grandpa this weekend?
records.zomi: Tu kal bei-in kua in Pu a va veh nuam hiam?

records.english: I want to come, but I have an exam on Saturday morning.
records.zomi: Ka pai nuam hi, ahi zongin Kiginni zingsang sitna ka nei hi.

records.english: Who had the family car fixed?
records.zomi: Innkuan mawtaw kua in a phuah sak hiam?

records.english: Uncle Khai had it repaired at a garage near his office.
records.zomi: Pu Khai in a office kiang mawtaw phuahna ah a phuah sak hi.

records.english: Ask your father who is allowed to use his tools.
records.zomi: Na pa' nasepna vante kua in a zang thei hiam, na pa dong in.

records.english: I've never known who my great-grandparents were, but I'd love to trace our family history someday.
records.zomi: Ka pu ka pite' nu leh pate kua hi uh hiam ka thei ngei kei a, ni khat ni-in i innkuan tangthu ka zong nuam mahmah hi.

records.english: Who told Grandma that I had lost my job?
records.zomi: Ka nasepna ka mansuah hi, ci-in Pi kiangah kua in a gen hiam?

records.english: Your brother mentioned it when he called her last night.
records.zomi: Zan in na sanggam pasal in a sam ciangin a gen hi.

records.english: Who has your grandmother been living with since your grandfather passed away?
records.zomi: Na pu a sih khit nungin na pi kua tawh a teeng hiam?

records.english: She has been living with my aunt Cing for almost three years.
records.zomi: Kum thum bang sung ka ni Cing tawh a teeng khin hi.

records.english: I left my glasses at home, so I can't read the board.
records.zomi: Ka mitlimlang inn ah ka nusia ahih manin suanglaipi tung ka sim thei kei hi.

records.english: Give this letter to your father.
records.zomi: Hih lai na pa pia in.

records.english: Your grandmother may come and talk to the class next week if she has time.
records.zomi: Na pi in hun a neih leh kal zom ciangin class tawh hong kiho thei hi.

records.english: Wait here until your mom comes.
records.zomi: Na nu a hong tun dong hih munah ngak in.

records.english: Pau, you can go home early because your father is here.
records.zomi: Pau, na pa hih munah a om ahih manin na pai masa thei hi.

records.english: Can I call my dad?
records.zomi: Ka pa ka sam thei ding hiam?

records.english: The teacher had my older brother carry the books to the library.
records.zomi: Sia in ka u pasal laibu inn ah laibute a puaksak hi.

records.english: My mom wants to know whether I can do the project with my cousin.
records.zomi: Ka nu in ka sanggam tawh project ka sem thei ding hiam a theih nuam hi.

records.english: Each of you is to have a parent or guardian check your spelling list before it is handed in.
records.zomi: Na khat ciat in na laimal gawmna list na ap ma-un na nu hiam na pa hiam, na khoitu hiam in a en ding hi.

records.english: Anyone who would like their project returned to their family at the end of the year should write a home address on the back.
records.zomi: Kum bei ciangin a project uh a innkuan uh kiangah ap kik ding a deih mi khempeuh in a nunglam ah a inn mun a gelh ding uh hi.

records.english: The teacher told me to practice reading aloud to my grandparents for twenty minutes every evening.
records.zomi: Sia in nitak simin minit sawmnih sung ka pu leh ka pi kiangah aw ngaih takin lai sim dingin hong hilh hi.

records.english: Is your homework finished?
records.zomi: Na innlai na zo khin hiam?

records.english: Write three sentences about your favorite family meal.
records.zomi: Na innkuan an nek na deih pen thu thugelh thum gelh in.

records.english: Mrs. Hau asked us whether we had been copying answers from our older siblings' notebooks.
records.zomi: Hau nu in na u leh nau te' laibu pan dawnnate na gelh kik uh hiam, hong dong hi.

records.english: Draw your family tree on this sheet, starting with your grandparents.
records.zomi: Na pu leh na pite tawh kipan-in hih lai tungah na innkuan sing lim gelh in.

records.english: I'm sorry I'm late; I had to walk my little sister to her school first.
records.zomi: Ka zekai ahih manin hong maisak in; ka nau numei a sang ah ka paipih masa hi.

records.english: Did your parents check your math answers last night?
records.zomi: Zan in na nu leh pa in na kisim dawnnate a en uh hiam?

records.english: Thank you, Mrs. Kim, for letting me sit at the front because of my eyes.
records.zomi: Kim nu, ka mit hangin mai lam ah hong tu sak ahih manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: If it weren't for your uncle's help, would you have been able to finish the model on time?
records.zomi: Na pa neu' huhna a om kei leh, model na bawl hun takah na zo thei ding hiam?

records.english: You can bring your sister to the class party.
records.zomi: Na sanggam nu class poai ah na paipih thei hi.

records.english: You can't bring your sister to the class party.
records.zomi: Na sanggam nu class poai ah na paipih thei kei hi.

records.english: Remind your parents that the school trip costs five dollars.
records.zomi: Sang khualzinna man dollar nga ahi hi, ci-in na nu leh pa phawksak in.

records.english: The more your parents read with you at home, the easier these lessons will become.
records.zomi: Na nu leh pa in inn ah nang tawh lai a sim tam semsem leh, hih sinnate a baih semsem ding hi.

records.english: I forgot my lunch at home.
records.zomi: Ka sun an inn ah ka mangngilh hi.

records.english: Whoever is collecting you today must sign the pickup sheet at the front desk.
records.zomi: Tuni hong la ding mi in mai lam dawhkan ah lakna lai ah min a gelh ding hi.

records.english: The note your mother sent says you have been excused from sports this week because of your sprained ankle.
records.zomi: Na nu' khak lai in, na siakmit a kitawl hangin tu kal sungin kimawlna pan kikhah hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Say thank you to your grandmother for the cookies she baked for our class.
records.zomi: I class adingin a bawl moh neute hangin na pi kiangah lungdam ko in.

records.english: Mom, the teacher said we have to bring an empty shoebox tomorrow.
records.zomi: Nu, zingciang khedap kuang awng khat tawi ding hi, sia in a ci hi.

records.english: Mom, please help me finish my poster tonight.
records.zomi: Nu, tu zanin ka poster zo dingin hong huh in.

records.english: My twin brother and I are in the same class, but the teacher makes us sit apart.
records.zomi: Ka apeng pasal leh kei class khat mah ah ka om uh hi, ahi zongin sia in hong kikhen tusak hi.

records.english: My dad helped me with the fractions, but I wrote all the answers myself.
records.zomi: Ka pa in fraction te ah hong huh a, ahi zongin dawnna khempeuh keimah mah in ka gelh hi.

records.english: Niang, have your parents fill in this form and return it by Monday.
records.zomi: Niang, na nu leh pa in hih form dim uh henla, Pizing ni ma-in ap kik in.

records.english: Who signed your homework?
records.zomi: Na innlai kua in min a gelh hiam?

records.english: My grandfather signed it last night.
records.zomi: Zan in ka pu in min a gelh hi.

records.english: Read this book with your parents over the weekend.
records.zomi: Kal bei-in na nu leh pa tawh hih laibu sim in.

records.english: Whatever you choose to write about, make sure it is something your family actually does together.
records.zomi: Bang thu gelh dingin na teel zongin, na innkuan in a sem khawm taktak uh na ahih ding phawk in.

records.english: Keep your report card in this envelope so that it doesn't get dirty on the way home.
records.zomi: Inn na ciah laitakin a nin loh nadingin na report card hih lai ip sungah koih in.

records.english: Spend half an hour each evening this week helping a family member with a chore, and write down what you learned.
records.zomi: Tu kal sungin nitak simin innkuan mi khat a nasep ah nai lang khat sung huh inla, bang na sin hiam gelh in.

records.english: Please show this note to your parents tonight.
records.zomi: Tu zanin hih lai na nu leh pa lak in.

records.english: Why does the teacher want us to ask our parents about their childhood?
records.zomi: Bang hangin sia in i nu leh pa uh' naupan lai thu dong dingin hong ngen hiam?

records.english: My aunt is picking me up today, so I might have to leave a few minutes early.
records.zomi: Tuni ka ni in hong la ding ahih manin, minit tawmno a masa-in ka pai kul kha ding hi.

records.english: Lian, could you take this worksheet to your brother, since he's home sick today?
records.zomi: Lian, na sanggam pasal tuni inn ah a dam lo ahih manin, hih lai amah kiangah na tawi thei ding hiam?

records.english: So that no one feels left out, you may write about any adult who looks after you, not just your parents.
records.zomi: Kuamah a kinusia bang a kisak loh nadingin, na nu leh pa bek hi lo-in nangma hong khoi upa khatpeuh thu na gelh thei hi.

records.english: Interview someone in your family for at least fifteen minutes about their first day of school.
records.zomi: Na innkuan mi khat sang kah ni masa pen thu minit sawm leh nga val sung dong in.

records.english: Can my cousin borrow my old textbook?
records.zomi: Ka sanggam in ka laibu lui a leitawi thei ding hiam?

records.english: By the time your parents arrive for the open day, every poster should have been hung on the wall.
records.zomi: Na nu leh pa open day ah a hong tun ma-un poster khempeuh bang ah kikhai khin ding hi.

records.english: Who is picking you up after school?
records.zomi: Sang a khak ciangin kua in hong la ding hiam?

records.english: Your father mentioned that you've been staying up late to finish your homework, so tell me if the workload is too heavy.
records.zomi: Na innlai na zawh nadingin zan sawt takin na om hi, na pa in a gen hi; nasep a tam lua leh hong gen in.

records.english: Bring a photo of your family for tomorrow's lesson.
records.zomi: Zingciang sinna adingin na innkuan limlak khat tawi in.

records.english: It isn't that I mind you bringing your baby sister to class; it's just that she might distract the others.
records.zomi: Na nau naungek class ah na paipih ka lungkia kei hi; mi dangte a buaisak kha ding cih bek ahi hi.
