records.english: Students are not allowed to bring younger siblings into the exam room.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte in sitna khan sungah a nau neute uh paipih thei lo uh hi.

records.english: No pets are allowed in the classroom, even for show and tell.
records.zomi: Show and tell adingin zong, class sungah inn ganhing paipih phal lo hi.

records.english: May I see the school nurse, please?
records.zomi: Sang nurse ka va mu thei ding hiam?

records.english: Our teacher made us rewrite the paragraph twice.
records.zomi: I sia in laigual nihvei hong gelh kik sak hi.

records.english: My mother is our class helper today.
records.zomi: Tuni ka nu pen i class huhtu ahi hi.

records.english: Sit next to your cousin.
records.zomi: Na sanggam kiangah tu in.

records.english: Ask your grandfather to tell you a story about his school days, and write it down in your own words.
records.zomi: Na pu kiangah a sang kah lai tangthu khat gen dingin ngen inla, na kammal tawh gelh in.

records.english: Tell your parents that school starts an hour late on Wednesday.
records.zomi: Nilai ni ciangin sang nai khat zekai-in kipan ding hi, ci-in na nu leh pa gen in.

records.english: You are welcome to invite your parents to watch your presentation on Friday afternoon.
records.zomi: Laithai ni sun ciangin na thugen en dingin na nu leh pa na sam thei hi.

records.english: It would help me if you could speak a bit more slowly, because we don't speak English at home.
records.zomi: Inn ah English pau i zang kei uh ahih manin, zawlzawl deuhin na gen thei leh hong huh ding hi.

records.english: Having lost his own father young, my dad made sure he spent every evening with us.
records.zomi: Amah' pa a naupan lai-in a sih manin, ka pa in nitak simin keimaute tawh a om tawntung hi.

records.english: Who in your family told the best bedtime stories?
records.zomi: Na innkuan sungah lup ma-a tangthu kua in a gen hoih pen hiam?

records.english: My cousins and I were forbidden to climb onto the roof of the barn.
records.zomi: Ka sanggamte leh kei buh inn tungah kah ding ki-khaksak uh hi.

records.english: Do you think our kids will remember these years the way we remember our own childhood?
records.zomi: I tate in i naupan lai i phawk bangin hih kumte a phawk ding uh na ci hiam?

records.english: I will never forget the day my baby brother was born.
records.zomi: Ka nau pasal a suah ni ka mangngilh ngei kei ding hi.

records.english: Our old dog slept by the front door for hours every afternoon.
records.zomi: I ui lui in sun simin mai lam kongkhak kiangah nai tampi sung a ihmu hi.

records.english: My big brother held my hand so tightly on the way to school that it hurt.
records.zomi: Sang ka pai laitakin ka u pasal in ka khut a nat dongin a man khauh hi.

records.english: The flood washed away our family's vegetable garden when I was seven.
records.zomi: Ka kum sagih lai-in tuikhang in i innkuan anteh huan a tai mang hi.

records.english: Dad promised that he would build us a treehouse, and one summer he finally did.
records.zomi: Pa in singkung tungah inn neu khat hong lam ding a ciam a, khuakhal khat ciangin a lam taktak hi.

records.english: Thank you for keeping all the letters I wrote you when I was little.
records.zomi: Ka naupan lai-a ka khak laite khempeuh na kem ahih manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: We weren't allowed to touch Grandpa's radio.
records.zomi: Pu' radio i khoih thei kei uh hi.

records.english: Ironically, my grandfather, who had been told by his doctor to avoid sweets, was the one who secretly slipped us candy after dinner.
records.zomi: Lamdang takin, siavuan in a tui-namtui nek dingin a khaksak ka pu mah in nitak an khit ciangin hong guk piak ngei hi.

records.english: My family moved three times before I turned eight.
records.zomi: Ka kum giat a pha ma-in ka innkuan uh thumvei a pem uh hi.

records.english: The quilt that my great-grandmother stitched for my mother's wedding became the blanket under which all of us children slept in winter.
records.zomi: Ka pi' nu in ka nu' kiteenna adingin a khui puanpi pen phalbi ciangin naupangte khempeuh i lup nuai a puan suak hi.

records.english: I wish you could have met my grandfather.
records.zomi: Ka pu na muh theih nak leh ka ut hi.

records.english: Is it true that you once ran away from home?
records.zomi: Na naupan lai-in inn pan na tai khia ngei, cih a dik hiam?

records.english: Yes, but I only got as far as the end of the street before I got hungry and came home.
records.zomi: Dik hi, ahi zongin lampi tawp dong bek ka pai a, ka gil a kial ciangin inn ah ka ciah kik hi.

records.english: By the time I turned ten, I had already been looking after my two younger sisters for three years.
records.zomi: Ka kum sawm a phak ciangin, ka nau numei nihte kum thum sung ka ma khin hi.

records.english: My grandmother wrapped my sore ankle with a strip of cloth soaked in warm water.
records.zomi: Ka pi in ka siakmit a nat pen tui lum a kidiah puan tawh a tuam hi.

records.english: Were you closer to your mother or your father?
records.zomi: Na nu tawh na kinai zaw hiam, na pa tawh hiam?

records.english: The baby chicks hatched while we watched.
records.zomi: I et laitakin akno-te a suak uh hi.

records.english: Even though she had never gone to school herself, my mother sat beside us every evening to make sure we finished our homework.
records.zomi: Amah sang kah ngei lo napi, ka nu in i innlai i zawh nadingin nitak simin i kiangah a tu hi.

records.english: My little sister cried for two hours when Dad sold our old car.
records.zomi: Pa in i mawtaw lui a zuak ciangin ka nau numei nai nih sung a kap hi.

records.english: My mother sold vegetables at the market to pay our school fees.
records.zomi: Ka nu in sang man pia dingin zuakna mun ah anteh a zuak hi.

records.english: If Grandpa hadn't been so patient with me, I would never have learned to play the guitar.
records.zomi: Pu in hong thuakzawh kei nak leh, guitar tum ka sin ngei kei ding hi.

records.english: My uncle carried me on his shoulders so that I could see the parade.
records.zomi: Lamlakna ka muh theih nadingin ka pa neu in a liang tungah hong pua hi.

records.english: My parents spent weeks arguing about whether to send me to boarding school, which I only found out years later.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh pa in boarding school ah hong khak ding hiam cih kal tampi sung a kinial uh hi, kum tampi nung ciang bekin ka thei hi.

records.english: Tell me what your parents were like when you were small.
records.zomi: Na neu lai-in na nu leh pa bangci mi hi uh hiam hong gen in.

records.english: Grandma knitted a red sweater for each of her grandchildren.
records.zomi: Pi in a tute khat ciat adingin sweater san khat a khui hi.

records.english: My little brother often fell asleep at the dinner table.
records.zomi: Ka nau pasal in nitak an dawhkan ah a ihmu ngei hi.

records.english: My mother sewed my school uniform by hand every year.
records.zomi: Kum simin ka nu in ka sang puan a khut tawh a khui hi.

records.english: My sister once asked me whether I thought our parents loved her less than me.
records.zomi: Ka nau numei in i nu leh pa in amah sangin kei hong it zaw uh na ci hiam, hong dong ngei hi.

records.english: The storm broke our kitchen window, and pieces of glass flew everywhere.
records.zomi: Huihpi in i anbuk tawhkhawng a kitan sak a, khuang-meeng tawm a lengla hi.

records.english: My older sister saved her pocket money to buy me a birthday present.
records.zomi: Ka u numei in ka pianni letsong lei dingin a sum neute a khol hi.

records.english: My grandfather made me a whistle out of bamboo.
records.zomi: Ka pu in ka adingin gua tawh phit hong bawl hi.

records.english: Grandma kept a jar of honey on the top shelf, where none of us could reach it.
records.zomi: Pi in khuai tui um khat dawh tung pen ah a koih a, kuamah in i tun theih kei hi.

records.english: My aunt says I was the noisiest baby in the whole family.
records.zomi: Ka ni in innkuan bup sungah kei naungek ging buai pen ka hi hi, a ci hi.

records.english: My father cut my hair with old scissors in the kitchen.
records.zomi: Ka pa in anbuk sungah temteh lui tawh ka sam a met hi.

records.english: I'm sorry I broke your favorite cup when we were kids.
records.zomi: I naupan lai-in na khuat na deih pen ka kitan sak ahih manin hong maisak in.

records.english: The sweater my aunt knitted for me shrank the first time it was washed.
records.zomi: Ka ni in hong khui sweater a sawp masak pen ciangin a tom hi.

records.english: Long after my father had stopped riding it, his old bicycle stood rusting in the shed, as if waiting for him to come back.
records.zomi: Ka pa in a tuan nawn loh sawtpi nungin, a siiksakol lui pen inn neu sungah a hong ciah kik ding ngak bangin a ngal hi.

records.english: Looking at these photos, I can hardly believe how small our first house was.
records.zomi: Hih limlakte ka et ciangin i inn masa pen bangzah neu hiam ka um zo kei hi.

records.english: My brother accidentally burned my favorite storybook.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in a theih loh-in ka tangthu laibu ka deih pen a hal hi.

records.english: At family picnics, we used banana leaves as plates.
records.zomi: Innkuan picnic ciangin banana nah ankuang bangin i zang uh hi.

records.english: My mother would often say that a family that eats together stays together.
records.zomi: An a ne khawm innkuan in kipawl den hi, ci-in ka nu in a gen ngei hi.

records.english: Dad used a stick to draw maps in the dirt and teach us the names of nearby villages.
records.zomi: Pa in sing tawh lei tungah map a gelh a, i kiim khuate min hong hilh hi.

records.english: My father seldom talked about his own childhood, but when he did, all of us fell silent and listened.
records.zomi: Ka pa in amah' naupan lai thu a gen tawm hi, ahi zongin a gen ciangin i khempeuh dai-in i ngai uh hi.

records.english: My twin sister and I wore matching clothes until we were twelve.
records.zomi: Ka apeng numei leh kei kum sawm leh nih dong puan kibang ka silh uh hi.

records.english: Mom, could you tell us again about the night I was born?
records.zomi: Nu, ka suah zan thu hong gen kik thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Mom kept our baby teeth in a little tin box.
records.zomi: Nu in i naungek ha-te dangka kuang neu khat sungah a koih hi.

records.english: Did your parents ever punish you for coming home late?
records.zomi: Zekai-in inn na tun manin na nu leh pa in hong bawlsiat ngei hiam?

records.english: It was my grandmother, not my parents, who decided what we children would wear to weddings.
records.zomi: Kiteenna ah naupangte in bang i silh ding hiam a khensat pen ka nu leh pa hi lo-in ka pi ahi hi.

records.english: Our grandmother insisted that every grandchild learn to cook at least one dish before leaving home.
records.zomi: I pi in tu khempeuh in inn a paisan ma-un an namkhat bek zong a huan theih ding uh a ngen ngiat hi.

records.english: How long did you live with your grandparents?
records.zomi: Na pu leh na pite tawh bangzah sawt na teeng hiam?

records.english: I lived with them for five years while my parents worked in another city.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh pa in khuapi dang ah na a sep laitakun kum nga sung amaute tawh ka teeng hi.

records.english: I miss the way my mother hummed while she cooked.
records.zomi: Ka nu in an a huan laitakin la nuam taka a sak ka ngaih hi.

records.english: Nobody was allowed to eat until Grandmother had said grace.
records.zomi: Pi in an thu a nget ma-in kuamah an ne thei lo hi.

records.english: I got up early on Saturdays to help my father in his shop.
records.zomi: Ka pa' dawl ah ka huh nadingin Kiginni simin ka tho tuung hi.

records.english: Mom told us never to swim in the river without an adult.
records.zomi: Nu in upa om lo-in lui ah tui peek ngei kei dingin hong hilh hi.

records.english: The candle melted while we waited for the power to come back.
records.zomi: Meivak a hong om kik dong i ngak laitakin khawimeivaak a vui hi.

records.english: Thang's wife made him call the clinic after he described the chest pain as a heavy weight sitting on his ribs.
records.zomi: Thang in a awm natna a guh tung a tu a gik bang hi, ci-in a gen ciangin, a zi in clinic a samsak hi.

records.english: Throughout the night, Grandma's breathing was so shallow and irregular that none of us dared to fall asleep.
records.zomi: Zan bup sungin Pi' hai dan a tom leh a kitel lo ahih manin, i lak pan kuamah ihmu ngam lo hi.

records.english: Whether it's the new pillow or just old age, Grandpa wakes up every morning with a stabbing pain between his shoulder blades.
records.zomi: Lukhum thak hang hiam, kum upa hang hiam, Pu in zingsang simin a liang kikal ah sun bang a natna tawh a khanglo hi.

records.english: My son has a bump on his head.
records.zomi: Ka tapa' lu tungah a bawk khat a om hi.

records.english: Is anyone else in your family sick?
records.zomi: Na innkuan sungah dam lo dang a om hiam?

records.english: When did your mother start feeling short of breath?
records.zomi: Na nu bang ciang pan a hai a tom pan hiam?

records.english: I have a pain in my side.
records.zomi: Ka nai lam a na hi.

records.english: I'm calling for my mother because she has lost her voice.
records.zomi: Ka nu' aw a mang ahih manin amah aiawhin ka sam hi.

records.english: Mom, I feel hot.
records.zomi: Nu, ka sa hi.

records.english: For the sake of our elderly neighbor, who lives alone, my wife checks in every evening to ask whether her chest pains have returned.
records.zomi: Amah bek a teeng i inn veng upa adingin, ka zi in a awm natna a hong pai kik hiam nitak simin a va dong hi.

records.english: My eyes hurt from the smoke.
records.zomi: Meikhu hangin ka mit a na hi.

records.english: Dim suspected that her son's constant ear-pulling meant more than teething, so she booked him an appointment for the next morning.
records.zomi: Dim in a tapa in a bil a lai tawntung pen ha suak hang bek hi lo ding hi, ci-in zingciang zingsang adingin siavuan a hun a khen sak hi.

records.english: My daughter has chickenpox.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in khuaphiat a vei hi.

records.english: My sister has a toothache.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu' ha a na hi.

records.english: You're not allowed to scratch those bites, Sui, or they'll start bleeding again.
records.zomi: Sui, tua a ciksate kok kei in, si a luang kik ding hi.

records.english: I feel better today, Mom.
records.zomi: Nu, tuni ka hoih zaw hi.

records.english: I made my brother sit down because he looked pale and was sweating.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal a maai a kang a, a guai a luang ahih manin ka tusak hi.

records.english: On Saturday evening, Mang said his throat felt raw.
records.zomi: Kiginni nitakin Mang in a gawl a na hi, a ci hi.

records.english: By Sunday morning, he had almost lost his voice and was burning with fever.
records.zomi: Nipini zingsang ciangin a aw mang dek a, a cisa nasia hi.

records.english: His wife drove him to the clinic before lunch so that a nurse could examine his throat.
records.zomi: Nurse in a gawl a et theih nadingin a zi in sun an ma-in clinic ah a paipih hi.

records.english: Cing told her husband, "I can barely lift my arm this morning."
records.zomi: Cing in a pasal kiangah, “Tu zingsangin ka ban ka liap zo khol kei hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: I'm writing down my father's symptoms so the doctor can see the whole picture.
records.zomi: Siavuan in a bup a muh theih nadingin ka pa' natna limte ka gelh hi.

records.english: Not wanting to worry his parents, Lian downplayed the stomach cramps that had kept him awake for most of the night.
records.zomi: A nu leh pa a lungkham loh nadingun, Lian in zan bup a ihmut hong phawng gil natna a gen neu hi.

records.english: If my sister hadn't insisted on checking my temperature, I would have gone to work with a fever and probably made everyone sick.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu in ka sa lum en ding a ngen ngiat kei nak leh, cisa tawh nasepna ah ka pai a, mi khempeuh ka natsak kha ding hi.

records.english: Pau's daughter said, "It feels like ants are crawling on my leg."
records.zomi: Pau' tanu in, “Ka khe tungah sikte a pai bang a kisa hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: My eye is puffy and red.
records.zomi: Ka mit a vung a, a san hi.

records.english: Kim, please tell the doctor how many days your son has had diarrhea.
records.zomi: Kim, na tapa' gilphawl ni bangzah a vei hiam siavuan kiangah gen in.

records.english: My wife feels sick in the mornings.
records.zomi: Ka zi in zingsang ciangin a lungsim a hoih kei hi.

records.english: My dad's back hurts after work.
records.zomi: Nasep khit ciangin ka pa' nungzang a na hi.

records.english: My husband keeps waking up with cramps in his legs.
records.zomi: Ka pasal in a khe zawlna tawh a khanglo tawntung hi.

records.english: Are you okay, Grandma?
records.zomi: Pi, na dam hiam?

records.english: Does your daughter itch more after she takes a bath?
records.zomi: Na tanu in a kisil khit ciangin a thak zaw hiam?

records.english: Everyone in our house has a cough.
records.zomi: I inn sung mi khempeuh in khuh a nei uh hi.

records.english: I'd been brushing off my sister's complaints of tiredness as stress, so I felt terrible when she finally admitted she'd been fainting at work.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu' gimna thu pen lungkhamna hang hi, ci-in ka limsak kei a, nasepna ah a lipkhia ngei hi, a gen ciangin ka lungsim a na mahmah hi.

records.english: So that the doctor would understand how quickly the swelling had spread, Thang took photos of his son's arm every few hours.
records.zomi: A vunna bangzah manlang takin a zel hiam siavuan in a theih nadingin, Thang in nai tawmno ciat ah a tapa' ban limlak a la hi.

records.english: The hardest part of caring for my father is that he insists he feels fine even when he's clearly struggling to catch his breath.
records.zomi: Ka pa' ka ma ah a haksa pen in, a hai haksa taktak napi, ka dam hi, ci-in a gen tawntung ahi hi.

records.english: Does your baby still have a fever?
records.zomi: Na naungek a cisa lai hiam?

records.english: My aunt told me she has had a ringing in her ears for almost a month.
records.zomi: Ka ni in kha khat bang sung a bil ah a ging hi, hong ci hi.

records.english: Nobody should give Grandpa anything to eat until the nurse finds out why he keeps choking.
records.zomi: Bang hangin a kiak tawntung hiam nurse in a theih ma-in kuamah in Pu an pia kei hen.

records.english: My grandpa's hands shake.
records.zomi: Ka pu' khut a ling hi.

records.english: The nurse asked whether my father had felt any pain in his jaw.
records.zomi: Ka pa' khagong ah natna a om hiam, nurse in a dong hi.

records.english: Please don't let Grandma carry the water bucket; her back has been hurting since Sunday.
records.zomi: Pi tui bawm puak sak kei un; Nipini pan a nungzang a na hi.

records.english: Your forehead feels warm, Niang.
records.zomi: Niang, na taltang a lum hi.

records.english: My feet are cold all the time.
records.zomi: Ka khe a vot tawntung hi.

records.english: Last week Hau's mother told us she had been seeing flashes of light in one eye.
records.zomi: Kal bei-in Hau' nu in a mit khat ah khuavak tangtang a mu hi, hong ci hi.

records.english: Could you watch the kids so I can take my wife to the clinic?
records.zomi: Ka zi clinic ah ka paipih theih nadingin naupangte na ma thei ding hiam?

records.english: Uncle Pau coughs a lot at night.
records.zomi: Pu Pau zanin a khuh tam hi.

records.english: The doctor had my mother keep a diary of her dizzy spells, noting the time, how long each one lasted, and what she had been doing.
records.zomi: Siavuan in ka nu' lung a am hun ciat, a hun, a sawtna leh bang a sem laitak hiam gelh dingin a ngen hi.

records.english: My parents won't let me play outside until my cough goes away.
records.zomi: Ka khuh a dam ma-in ka nu leh pa in a polam ah hong kimawl sak kei uh hi.

records.english: Does your ear still hurt, Joseph?
records.zomi: Joseph, na bil a na lai hiam?

records.english: The baby won't eat today.
records.zomi: Tuni naungek in an a ne nuam kei hi.

records.english: Hold my hand, Mom — my stomach hurts a lot.
records.zomi: Nu, ka khut hong man in — ka gil a na mahmah hi.

records.english: Since our toddler can't explain what hurts, we watch for signs like fussing, pulling at his ears, or refusing food.
records.zomi: I naupang neu in bang a nat hiam a gen thei kei ahih manin, a kap buaibuai, a bil a lai, an a ne nuam lo bang limte i en hi.

records.english: How long has your husband had that pain in his chest?
records.zomi: Na pasal' awm ah tua natna bangzah sawt a nei khin hiam?

records.english: Niang asked me to describe her son's symptoms to the nurse because she was too upset to talk.
records.zomi: Niang a lungkham lua manin kiho thei lo ahih manin, a tapa' natna limte nurse kiangah gen dingin hong ngen hi.

records.english: Our daughter has had a rash on her neck for four days.
records.zomi: I tanu' ngawng ah ni li sung vun san a om khin hi.

records.english: It wasn't until my grandfather stumbled twice in one afternoon that we realized his numb feet were more serious than he had let on.
records.zomi: Ka pu sun khat sungin nihvei a puk khit ciang bekin, a khe a zap pen a gen sangin a nasia zaw hi, ci i thei hi.

records.english: My brother's nose is bleeding.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal' naak pan si a luang hi.

records.english: Dad, my tummy hurts again.
records.zomi: Pa, ka gil a na kik hi.

records.english: Grandpa says his knees ache more on rainy days.
records.zomi: Guah zuk ni ciangin a khuk a na zaw hi, Pu in a ci hi.

records.english: Cing's grandfather served as village headman for twenty years.
records.zomi: Cing' pu in kum sawmnih sung khua ukpa a sem hi.

records.english: I hope my daughter becomes mayor someday.
records.zomi: Ka tanu ni khat ni-in khuapi ukpa a suak ding ka lamen hi.

records.english: Grandpa, you must not burn trash in the backyard — it's against the town rules.
records.zomi: Pu, inn nunglam ah nawi na hal ding hi lo hi — khua thukham tawh a kituak kei hi.

records.english: We need a permit before we can add a room to our house.
records.zomi: I inn ah khan behlap ma-in phalna lai i kisam hi.

records.english: Be careful at the town office on Fridays, because they close the line early.
records.zomi: Laithai ni ciangin khua office ah pilvang un, kigualna a khak tuung uh hi.

records.english: So many parents complained about the bus schedule that the council finally added an early morning route.
records.zomi: Bus hun ciamteh thu nu leh pa tampi in a phun manun, council in zingsang tuung bus lampi khat a behlap hi.

records.english: Grandpa keeps every letter he has ever received from the town office.
records.zomi: Pu in khua office pan a ngah lai khempeuh a kem hi.

records.english: My grandparents insisted that I vote in every local election, no matter how small.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh ka pi in khua teelna bangzah neu zongin khempeuh ah vote khia dingin hong ngen ngiat uh hi.

records.english: Thanks for helping my daughter with her petition to the council.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in council kiangah ngetna lai a khak ciangin na huh ahih manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: The local government is planning to build a playground right next to our home.
records.zomi: Khua ukna in i inn kiang tak ah naupang kimawlna mun lam a ngaihsun hi.

records.english: Our family has lived in this ward for three generations.
records.zomi: I innkuan in hih ward sungah suan thum sung a teeng khin hi.

records.english: The mayor is my mother's cousin, but she has never asked him for any favors.
records.zomi: Khuapi ukpa pen ka nu' sanggam ahi hi, ahi zongin bangmah a ngen ngei kei hi.

records.english: Once the deadline passes, the housing office will stop accepting applications, so please get your aunt's forms in this week.
records.zomi: Hun ciamteh a bei ciangin inn office in ngetna lai a sang nawn kei ding a, tu kal sungin na ni' form te hong khak in.

records.english: Is the mayor related to your family?
records.zomi: Khuapi ukpa na innkuan uh tawh kizom hiam?

records.english: I really do want to help the town plan the summer festival.
records.zomi: Khuakhal pawi bawl ding ah khua ka huh nuam taktak hi.

records.english: It was my older sister who convinced the mayor to keep the clinic open.
records.zomi: Clinic a kihon den nadingin khuapi ukpa a ciam sak pen ka u numei ahi hi.

records.english: Our city allows families to keep chickens in their backyards.
records.zomi: I khuapi in innkuante in inn nunglam ah aak a khawi thei dingin a phal hi.

records.english: Our city does not allow families to keep chickens in their backyards.
records.zomi: I khuapi in innkuante in inn nunglam ah aak a khawi thei dingin a phal kei hi.

records.english: My wife works part-time at the water department.
records.zomi: Ka zi in tui department ah nai tawm na a sem hi.

records.english: My husband and I registered our marriage at the town hall yesterday.
records.zomi: Zan in ka pasal leh kei khua ukna inn ah i kiteenna ka gelh uh hi.

records.english: Can we bring our kids to the council meeting?
records.zomi: Council kikhopna ah i tate i paipih thei ding hiam?

records.english: The town council should do more for families with young children.
records.zomi: Khua council in naupang neu a nei innkuante adingin tam zaw a sem ding hi.

records.english: Children are not allowed to swim in the city reservoir.
records.zomi: Khuapi tui kholna ah naupangte tui peek phal lo hi.

records.english: If my brother had registered his business on time, he wouldn't have had to pay a fine.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in a sumbawlna hun takah a gelh nak leh, sum gawtna a pia kul kei ding hi.

records.english: Our family's land records are kept at the county office.
records.zomi: I innkuan' gam lai pen county office ah kikoih hi.

records.english: Would you like to come with me to the neighborhood meeting tonight?
records.zomi: Tu zanin inn veng kikhopna ah hong pai khawm nuam hiam?

records.english: Ask your uncle, because he used to work at the township office.
records.zomi: Na pa neu dong in, amah township office ah na a sem ngei hi.

records.english: Thang wants to run for the village council next year.
records.zomi: Thang in kum zom ciangin khua council ah kiteel a sawm hi.

records.english: We have to renew our family's residence registration every two years.
records.zomi: Kum nih simin i innkuan' teenna min gelhna i thak sak ding hi.

records.english: It is essential that every household register with the local office within a month of moving.
records.zomi: Innkuan khempeuh in a pem khit kha khat sungin khua office ah a min uh a gelh ding thupi mahmah hi.

records.english: Grandma's request to have the bus stop moved closer to her apartment was finally approved by the transit committee.
records.zomi: Pi in bus khawlna a inn kiang naih zawin suan dinga a ngetna transit committee in a pom tawp hi.

records.english: Families are not permitted to bury relatives on private land without approval from the local authorities.
records.zomi: Khua ukte' phalna om lo-in innkuante in a beh leh phungte mimal gam sungah a vui thei kei uh hi.

records.english: Happy retirement, Mr. Kim — thank you for thirty years of service to our town.
records.zomi: Pu Kim, na nasep tawpna nuam takin zang in — i khua adingin kum sawmthum na sep ahih manin ka lungdam uh hi.

records.english: Niang went to the council meeting to ask for a crosswalk near her children's school.
records.zomi: Niang in a tate' sang kiangah lampi galkahna ngen dingin council kikhopna ah a pai hi.

records.english: Could you help my grandfather fill out his property tax form?
records.zomi: Ka pu in a gam siah form a dim nadingin na huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: My dad is going to the city office to get my birth certificate.
records.zomi: Ka pa in ka pianna lai la dingin khuapi office ah a pai ding hi.

records.english: As a single parent, Esther relies on the city's after-school program to look after her children until she finishes work.
records.zomi: Nu khat bek in naupang a khoi ahih manin, Esther in a nasep a zawh dong a tate a ma nadingin khuapi' sang khit program a muang hi.

records.english: I'm going to ask the council to build a ramp so that my father can enter the library in his wheelchair.
records.zomi: Ka pa in a wheelchair tawh laibu inn a lut theih nadingin council kiangah lampi khiahna lam dingin ka ngen ding hi.

records.english: The village leader gave a short speech at my cousin's wedding.
records.zomi: Khua makaipa in ka sanggam' kiteenna ah thu tomno a gen hi.

records.english: The city gave my mom a small grant to repair our roof.
records.zomi: Khuapi in i innkhum a phuah nadingin ka nu sum neu khat a pia hi.

records.english: Mary has been waiting three weeks for the city to answer her letter about the flooding.
records.zomi: Mary in tuikhang thu a laikhak khuapi in a dawn ding kal thum sung a ngak khin hi.

records.english: The town offers a discount on water bills for families with elderly members.
records.zomi: Khua in upa a nei innkuante adingin tui man a kiamsak hi.

records.english: Which office handles adoption papers in this city?
records.zomi: Hih khuapi ah ta kila lai kua office in a bawl hiam?

records.english: My cousin has been volunteering at the community center since she was sixteen.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu in kum sawm leh guk a pha pan mipi inn ah thalawp takin a sem hi.

records.english: Sorry, Mom — I forgot to pay the garbage fee again.
records.zomi: Nu, hong maisak in — nawi man pia ding ka mangngilh kik hi.

records.english: Without the town's help after the fire, our family would have had nowhere to stay.
records.zomi: Mei kang khit ciangin khua' huhna a om kei leh, i innkuan omna ding nei lo ding hi.

records.english: Because my grandfather couldn't read the notice, I translated it for him.
records.zomi: Ka pu in thuzakna lai a sim thei kei ahih manin, amah adingin ka let sak hi.

records.english: The more the city raises property taxes, the harder it becomes for young couples like us to buy a home.
records.zomi: Khuapi in gam siah a khangsak semsem leh, kote bang kiteeng thak nupate adingin inn lei a haksa semsem hi.

records.english: Pau said, "I'll take you to the township office after lunch."
records.zomi: Pau in, “Sun an khit ciangin township office ah kong paipih ding hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: Does your sister still work at the town library?
records.zomi: Na sanggam nu khua laibu inn ah na a sem lai hiam?

records.english: "Please fix our streetlight," my son told the mayor at the fair.
records.zomi: “I lampi meivak hong phuah sak in,” ci-in ka tapa in poai ah khuapi ukpa a gen hi.

records.english: Is it true that the city will pay for your mother's hearing aids?
records.zomi: Khuapi in na nu' bil-ngaihna man a pia ding, cih a dik hiam?

records.english: My parents met at a village council meeting forty years ago.
records.zomi: Kum sawmli lai-in khua council kikhopna ah ka nu leh pa a kimu uh hi.

records.english: The council voted to rename the park after my late grandfather, who planted most of its trees.
records.zomi: Council in park pen a singkung tampi a suan ka pu sisa' min tawh sap dingin vote a khia uh hi.

records.english: My son asked me, "Why does the mayor have such a big car?"
records.zomi: Ka tapa in, “Bang hangin khuapi ukpa in mawtaw lianpi a nei hiam?” hong ci hi.

records.english: My father, who was the town treasurer for years, still reads the budget report every spring.
records.zomi: Kum tampi khua sum kemtu a sem ka pa in spring simin sum zat ding report a sim lai hi.

records.english: How long did it take to get your building permit?
records.zomi: Na inn lam phalna lai ngah dingin bangzah sawt hiam?

records.english: Our street committee meets at my aunt's house once a month.
records.zomi: I lampi committee in kha simin vei khat ka ni' inn ah a kikhawm uh hi.

records.english: Who should I call if my neighbor's dog keeps running into the street?
records.zomi: Ka inn veng' ui lampi ah a tai tawntung leh kua ka sam ding hiam?

records.english: My brother-in-law is a police officer for the city.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu' pasal in khuapi adingin police a sem hi.

records.english: Who spilled juice on Dad's keyboard?
records.zomi: Pa' keyboard tungah juice kua in a buak hiam?

records.english: I keep a small brush next to the computer for cleaning dust out of the keyboard.
records.zomi: Keyboard sung leivui phiat nadingin computer kiangah brush neu khat ka koih hi.

records.english: My son has wanted a gaming computer with a powerful graphics card for years.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in kum tampi sung graphics card hat a nei gaming computer a deih hi.

records.english: Are these earbuds yours or your sister's?
records.zomi: Hih earbud te nang' hi hiam, na sanggam nu' hi hiam?

records.english: Could you help me clean the fan in my grandmother's laptop this weekend?
records.zomi: Tu kal bei-in ka pi' laptop fan nul siang dingin hong huh thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Grandpa wants a mouse with bigger buttons.
records.zomi: Pu in button lian zaw a nei mouse a deih hi.

records.english: It was my grandmother, not my uncle, who noticed that the speaker cable had come loose.
records.zomi: Speaker cable a kiphel cih a mu pen ka pa neu hi lo-in ka pi ahi hi.

records.english: Wait until the laptop cools down before you take out the battery.
records.zomi: Battery na lak ma-in laptop a vot dong ngak in.

records.english: My cousin built his own computer from parts he bought online.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam in online pan a lei parts te tawh amah' computer a bawl hi.

records.english: Grandpa, press this button to turn on the screen.
records.zomi: Pu, screen hon dingin hih button nen in.

records.english: Thank you for fixing my headphones, Grandpa!
records.zomi: Pu, ka headphone hong phuah sak ahih manin ka lungdam hi!

records.english: You kids must not open the computer case unless I'm with you.
records.zomi: Naupangte, ka om lohna ah computer case na hong thei kei uh hi.

records.english: Do your kids each have their own laptop, or do they share one?
records.zomi: Na tate in laptop khat ciat a nei uh hiam, khat a zang khawm uh hiam?

records.english: Our family has relied on the same desktop computer ever since my youngest brother was born, replacing only the keyboard and mouse along the way.
records.zomi: Ka nau pasal neu pen a suah pan i innkuan in desktop computer khat mah i zang den hi, keyboard leh mouse bek i laih hi.

records.english: Uncle Kham replaced the cracked screen on my phone for free.
records.zomi: Pu Kham in ka phone screen a kitan a man om lo-in a laih sak hi.

records.english: Unless the motherboard has a free slot, we won't be able to add more memory to my daughter's computer.
records.zomi: Motherboard ah slot awng a om kei leh, ka tanu' computer ah memory i behlap thei kei ding hi.

records.english: Whoever used my laptop last forgot to put the USB drive back in the drawer.
records.zomi: Ka laptop a zang nunung pen in USB drive dawhkan sungah koih kik ding a mangngilh hi.

records.english: Mang's daughter uses a stylus and a drawing tablet to finish her art homework.
records.zomi: Mang' tanu in a lim gelh innlai a zawh nadingin stylus leh drawing tablet a zang hi.

records.english: My brother taught our grandmother how to use the touchpad.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in i pi touchpad zat dan a hilh hi.

records.english: Please charge my phone for me while I'm in the shower.
records.zomi: Ka kisil laitakin ka phone hong charge sak in.

records.english: Should we buy Grandma a wireless keyboard so that she doesn't trip over the cable?
records.zomi: Pi in cable a pal loh nadingin wireless keyboard khat i lei sak ding hiam?

records.english: Lian printed the photos for her grandparents on the new printer.
records.zomi: Lian in a pu leh pite adingin printer thak tawh limlakte a print hi.

records.english: Our dog chewed through the charger cable last night.
records.zomi: Zan in i ui in charger cable a ngoih tan hi.

records.english: Both of you can use the headphones, but you'll have to take turns.
records.zomi: Note nih in headphone na zang thei uh hi, ahi zongin na kilaih ding uh hi.

records.english: Is this your brother's charger?
records.zomi: Hih pen na sanggam pasal' charger hi hiam?

records.english: Rather than throwing away her late husband's computer, Mary had its hard drive copied so that the family photos would be kept safe.
records.zomi: A pasal sisa' computer paikhiat sangin, innkuan limlakte a kem nadingin Mary in hard drive a copy sak hi.

records.english: The more programs my teenage son leaves open, the louder the cooling fan gets.
records.zomi: Ka tapa khangno in program tampi a honsak semsem leh, cooling fan a ging semsem hi.

records.english: My parents' printer ran out of ink the night before my brother's science project was due, so we had to drive to my uncle's house to print it.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal' science project ap ni zan ma-in ka nu leh pa' printer ink a bei ahih manin, print dingin ka pa neu' inn ah mawtaw tawh ka pai uh hi.

records.english: This memory card holds all the pictures from my sister's wedding.
records.zomi: Hih memory card in ka sanggam nu' kiteenna limlak khempeuh a nei hi.

records.english: The hard drive might be full of my son's games.
records.zomi: Hard drive pen ka tapa' game te tawh a dim kha ding hi.

records.english: If my father had kept the receipt, the shop would have replaced the broken power supply for free.
records.zomi: Ka pa in receipt a kem nak leh, dawl in power supply siat pen a man om lo-in a laih sak ding hi.

records.english: Boys, stop fighting over the game controller!
records.zomi: Tapate, game controller kilak kei un!

records.english: Cing bought a new keyboard for her father's birthday.
records.zomi: Cing in a pa' pianni adingin keyboard thak khat a lei hi.

records.english: We saved money for six months to buy our first family computer.
records.zomi: I innkuan computer masa pen lei dingin kha guk sung sum i khol uh hi.

records.english: The speakers are too loud for the baby.
records.zomi: Naungek adingin speaker te a ging lua hi.

records.english: I'll install an extra fan in your computer to keep it cool, Sui.
records.zomi: Sui, na computer a vot nadingin fan khat ka behlap ding hi.

records.english: I'm sorry I dropped your tablet, Mom.
records.zomi: Nu, na tablet ka kiak sak ahih manin hong maisak in.

records.english: Can I borrow your mouse until Friday?
records.zomi: Laithai ni dong na mouse ka leitawi thei ding hiam?

records.english: Dad used a small screwdriver to remove the back cover of the laptop.
records.zomi: Pa in laptop nunglam khuhna phel dingin screwdriver neu khat a zang hi.

records.english: Niang unplugged the old monitor from her grandmother's computer.
records.zomi: Niang in a pi' computer pan monitor lui a phawi hi.

records.english: Then she connected the new monitor with an HDMI cable.
records.zomi: Tua khit ciangin HDMI cable tawh monitor thak a kizom sak hi.

records.english: Finally, she made the text larger so that her grandmother could read it easily.
records.zomi: A tawpna-ah, a pi in baih takin a sim theih nadingin laimalte a lian sak hi.

records.english: We'll need a longer HDMI cable to connect the laptop to the living room TV.
records.zomi: Laptop pen innsung TV tawh kizom sak dingin HDMI cable a sau zaw khat i kisam ding hi.

records.english: The laptop my brother handed down to me, whose keyboard is missing two keys, still works well enough for schoolwork.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in hong piak laptop, a keyboard tungah key nih a om lo, sang nasep adingin a hoih lai hi.

records.english: This old monitor belonged to my grandfather.
records.zomi: Hih monitor lui pen ka pu' a hi hi.

records.english: Thang has been fixing his uncle's laptop for three hours.
records.zomi: Thang in a pa neu' laptop nai thum sung a phuah khin hi.

records.english: How long does the battery on your new laptop last?
records.zomi: Na laptop thak battery bangzah sawt a om hiam?

records.english: About eight hours, so I can use it all day at my aunt's house.
records.zomi: Nai giat bang, tua ahih manin ka ni' inn ah ni bup ka zang thei hi.

records.english: Please, all of you, keep your drinks away from the computer desk.
records.zomi: Na khempeuh uh, na dawn ding uh computer dawhkan pan gamla takah koih un.

records.english: Is the microphone built into the laptop, or do I need to plug one in for the family call?
records.zomi: Microphone pen laptop sungah a om hiam, innkuan sap adingin khat ka ciktan ding hiam?

records.english: My wife's laptop doesn't have a DVD drive, so we can't watch our old wedding videos on it.
records.zomi: Ka zi' laptop in DVD drive a nei kei ahih manin, i kiteenna video luite tua tungah i en thei kei hi.

records.english: My dad's computer has two monitors.
records.zomi: Ka pa' computer in monitor nih a nei hi.

records.english: The children are not allowed to use the printer without asking first.
records.zomi: Naupangte in a dong masa lo-in printer a zang thei kei uh hi.

records.english: Never put a laptop on a soft bed while it is charging.
records.zomi: Laptop a charge laitakin lupna nem tungah koih ngei kei in.

records.english: Even if we upgrade the processor, Dad's ten-year-old computer may still struggle with video calls.
records.zomi: Processor i hoihsak zongin, Pa' kum sawm a cing computer in video call a zawh haksa lai kha ding hi.

records.english: Aunt Dim, who worked as an electronics technician for thirty years, can name every part on a motherboard at a glance.
records.zomi: Kum sawmthum sung electronics technician a sem Ni Dim in motherboard tung a om parts khempeuh a muh pakin a min a gen thei hi.

records.english: My aunt's laptop battery lasts only two hours now.
records.zomi: Ka ni' laptop battery tu-in nai nih bek a om hi.

records.english: By the time the technician arrived, my father had already replaced the faulty memory himself.
records.zomi: Technician a hong tun ma-in, ka pa in memory siat pen amah mah in a laih khin hi.

records.english: The only reason Grandma agreed to try the computer was that the keyboard had large, glowing letters.
records.zomi: Pi in computer zat sin dingin a lungkim hang bek pen keyboard in laimal lian a tang a nei ahih manin ahi hi.

records.english: If the fan stops spinning, the processor could overheat.
records.zomi: Fan a kizang nawn kei leh, processor a sa lua kha ding hi.

records.english: Cing's parents had her birth certificate translated so the school could enroll her.
records.zomi: Cing' nu leh pa in sang in a lak theih nadingin a pianna lai a let sak uh hi.

records.english: My son might want to learn Zomi when he is older.
records.zomi: Ka tapa a upat ciangin Zomi pau a sin nuam kha ding hi.

records.english: Who chose your name, your father or your grandmother?
records.zomi: Na min kua in a teel hiam, na pa hiam, na pi hiam?

records.english: My grandmother chose it.
records.zomi: Ka pi in a teel hi.

records.english: Our baby will wear her grandmother's shawl at the dedication service.
records.zomi: I naungek in a pi' puan Pasian tungah apna biakna ah a silh ding hi.

records.english: Come and eat, Grandma.
records.zomi: Pi, an hong ne in.

records.english: Grandma, would you please come and eat with us?
records.zomi: Pi, ko tawh an hong ne khawm thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: The more time I spend with my aunts, the more Zomi I feel.
records.zomi: Ka nite tawh hun ka zat tam semsem leh, Zomi ka hihna ka kisa semsem hi.

records.english: We saved money for years to take our kids to see where their grandparents grew up.
records.zomi: I tate in a pu a pite uh' khanna mun a muh nadingun kum tampi sung sum i khol hi.

records.english: We are a big family, and every cousin is like a brother or sister to me.
records.zomi: Innkuan lian i hi a, sanggam khempeuh kei adingin u leh nau bang ahi hi.

records.english: I miss my grandparents' house.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh ka pi' inn ka ngaih hi.

records.english: Each of us wrote a letter to explain what our heritage means to us.
records.zomi: I khat ciat in i ngeina in kote adingin bang khiatna a nei hiam hilh dingin lai khat ka gelh uh hi.

records.english: Grandma, thank you for keeping our family stories alive.
records.zomi: Pi, i innkuan tangthute a hing den nadingin na kem ahih manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: You must not call your elders by their first names in our house.
records.zomi: I inn ah upate a min tawh na sam thei kei hi.

records.english: My grandfather made us repeat our family line until we knew it by heart.
records.zomi: Ka pu in i innkuan khangthu a lungsim tawh i theih dong hong gen kik sak hi.

records.english: Grandma always said, "Never forget whose child you are."
records.zomi: Pi in, “Kua' ta na hi hiam mangngilh ngei kei in,” a ci tawntung hi.

records.english: It was my grandmother who taught me what it means to be Zomi.
records.zomi: Zomi hihna in bang khiatna a nei hiam hong hilh pen ka pi ahi hi.

records.english: Not knowing our language well, my daughter sometimes feels left out when relatives tell jokes.
records.zomi: I pau a theih hoih loh manin, beh leh phungte in ciamnuihna a gen ciangun ka tanu a kinusia bang a kisa ngei hi.

records.english: If I had listened more carefully to my grandfather, I would know our family history better now.
records.zomi: Ka pu thu cingtak zawin ka ngai nak leh, tu-in i innkuan tangthu ka thei hoih zaw ding hi.

records.english: Whose family photo is this?
records.zomi: Hih innkuan limlak kua' innkuan hi hiam?

records.english: My aunt has been teaching me our family songs for three years.
records.zomi: Ka ni in kum thum sung i innkuan lasate hong hilh khin hi.

records.english: My nephew asked me, "Am I still Zomi if I can't speak Zomi?"
records.zomi: Ka tanau in, “Zomi pau ka zang thei kei leh Zomi ka hi lai hiam?” hong ci hi.

records.english: You are definitely Zomi, even if you are still learning the language.
records.zomi: Pau na sin lai zongin Zomi na hi taktak hi.

records.english: We visit my grandparents every Christmas.
records.zomi: Christmas simin ka pu leh ka pi i va veh uh hi.

records.english: By the time my son finishes school, he will have spent ten summers with his grandparents.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in sang a zawh ciangin, a pu leh a pite tawh khuakhal sawm a zang khin ding hi.

records.english: I don't want my kids to feel ashamed of their roots.
records.zomi: Ka tate in a bulpi uh a zahpih ding uh ka deih kei hi.

records.english: My parents worked hard so that we could have a better life without forgetting who we are.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh pa in kua i hi hiam i mangngilh lo-in nuntakna hoih zaw i neih nadingin haksa takin a sem uh hi.

records.english: My aunt might know more about our clan's history than anyone else.
records.zomi: Ka ni in i phung tangthu mi dang khempeuh sangin a thei zaw kha ding hi.

records.english: Whatever language my children end up speaking, I want them to feel at home among their relatives.
records.zomi: Ka tate in bang pau a zang ding uh hiam a hih zongin, a beh leh phungte lakah inn bangin a kisak ding uh ka deih hi.

records.english: At our family reunions, the older relatives make every child introduce themselves with their father's and grandfather's names.
records.zomi: I innkuan kikhopna ciangin upate in naupang khempeuh in a pa uh leh a pu uh min tawh amau le amau a kiphawksak sak uh hi.

records.english: Mang's family welcomed my husband as if he had always been one of them.
records.zomi: Mang' innkuan in ka pasal amaute mi khat ahi den bangin a muak uh hi.

records.english: I'm writing down my grandfather's stories so that my children can read them someday.
records.zomi: Ka tate in ni khat ni-in a sim theih nadingun ka pu' tangthute ka gelh hi.

records.english: I do feel Zomi, even though I was born in another country.
records.zomi: Gam dang ah ka suak hangin Zomi bangin ka kisa taktak hi.

records.english: Thang told his daughter, "Your name carries your grandmother's memory."
records.zomi: Thang in a tanu kiangah, “Na min in na pi' phawkna a pua hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: Lian's grandmother had her wear a traditional skirt to her graduation party.
records.zomi: Lian' pi in a sang zawhna poai ah ngeina puandum a silhsak hi.

records.english: My father was named by the village elders.
records.zomi: Ka pa pen khua upate in min a phuah hi.

records.english: Does your family still keep the old recipes?
records.zomi: Na innkuan in an huan dan luite a kem lai uh hiam?

records.english: My wife is not Zomi, but she sings our hymns better than I do.
records.zomi: Ka zi Zomi hi lo napi, i la-te kei sangin a sa hoih zaw hi.

records.english: Please wait until Grandpa starts eating.
records.zomi: Pu in an a nek kipat dong ngak un.

records.english: My grandmother has lived with us since my grandfather passed away.
records.zomi: Ka pu a sih khit nungin ka pi i kiangah a teeng hi.

records.english: My husband's family may speak a different dialect, so we sometimes switch to English to avoid confusion.
records.zomi: Ka pasal' innkuan in pau tuam deuh a zang kha ding uh ahih manin, kituak lohna a om loh nadingin English pau i zang ngei hi.

records.english: Phones are not allowed at the table during our family prayers.
records.zomi: I innkuan thungetna hun sungin dawhkan ah phone phal lo hi.

records.english: Being the eldest daughter, Cing is expected to look after her younger siblings and keep the family traditions.
records.zomi: Ta numei upa pen ahih manin, Cing in a nau te ma-in innkuan ngeinate a kem ding a kilamen hi.

records.english: Sometimes I wonder whether my grandchildren will still call themselves Zomi.
records.zomi: Ka tute in Zomi kici-in a kisam lai ding uh hiam, ci-in ka ngaihsun ngei hi.

records.english: Our family tree was drawn by my uncle on a large sheet of paper.
records.zomi: I innkuan sing lim pen ka pa neu in lai lianpi tungah a gelh hi.

records.english: Can you teach my son a few Zomi words?
records.zomi: Ka tapa Zomi kammal tawmno na hilh thei ding hiam?

records.english: It is possible that our great-grandparents spoke a slightly different dialect from ours.
records.zomi: I pu i pite' nu leh pate in i pau tawh a kibang lo deuh pau a zang uh kha ding hi.

records.english: Grandpa Pau gave me my Zomi name when I was a baby.
records.zomi: Ka naungek lai-in Pu Pau in Zomi min hong phuah hi.

records.english: This shawl was woven by my great-grandmother.
records.zomi: Hih puan pen ka pi' nu in a khui hi.

records.english: How long have your parents lived abroad?
records.zomi: Na nu leh pa gamdang ah bangzah sawt a teeng khin uh hiam?

records.english: They have lived abroad for twenty years.
records.zomi: Kum sawmnih sung gamdang ah a teeng khin uh hi.

records.english: Is your father's village near the mountains?
records.zomi: Na pa' khua mualte kiangah a om hiam?

records.english: I can say a short prayer in Zomi.
records.zomi: Zomi pau tawh thungetna tomno ka nei thei hi.

records.english: Grandma doesn't allow anyone to leave the table before the elders have finished eating.
records.zomi: Upate in an a nek zawh ma-un Pi in kuamah dawhkan pan a dinsak kei hi.

records.english: Having grown up far from my parents' homeland, I learned about it mostly through my mother's cooking.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh pa' gam pan gamla takah ka khan manin, ka nu' an huan tawh a tam zaw ka thei hi.

records.english: I am Zomi, and my children are Zomi too.
records.zomi: Zomi ka hi a, ka tate zong Zomi ahi uh hi.

records.english: In our family, the clan name is passed down from father to son.
records.zomi: I innkuan ah phung min pen pa pan tapa tungah kipia hi.

records.english: My parents never pressured me to marry within the community, yet I find myself drawn to someone who understands where I come from.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh pa in mipi sung bek ah kiteeng dingin hong khauhsak ngei kei uh hi, ahi zongin ka hong pai na mun a thei mi khat ka it hi.

records.english: Niang does speak Zomi; she is just shy around strangers.
records.zomi: Niang in Zomi pau a zang taktak hi; mikhualte kiangah a maizum bek hi.

records.english: Grandpa, can you tell me about your childhood again?
records.zomi: Pu, na naupan lai thu hong gen kik thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Who are we waiting for before the meeting can begin?
records.zomi: Kikhopna a kipat ma-in kua i ngak hiam?

records.english: We're still waiting for the director, who is stuck in traffic.
records.zomi: Mawtaw buai hangin a om director i ngak lai uh hi.

records.english: Who's presenting our group project on Friday?
records.zomi: Laithai ni ciangin i lom project kua in a lak ding hiam?

records.english: Who's on the night shift this weekend?
records.zomi: Tu kal bei-in zan nasep ah kua a om hiam?

records.english: To find out who your adviser is, check the email the department sent last week.
records.zomi: Na hilhtu kua hiam na theih nadingin, department in kal bei-a a khak email en in.

records.english: Who signed for the package that came this morning?
records.zomi: Tu zingsang a hong tung thuamhual kua in min a gelh hiam?

records.english: The receptionist signed for it before she went to lunch.
records.zomi: Mai lam ngaktu in sun an nek dinga a pai ma-in min a gelh hi.

records.english: Who's picking up the lunch order for the staff meeting?
records.zomi: Nasemte kikhopna adingin sun an kua in a va la ding hiam?

records.english: I wonder who will take over the class after Mr. Pau retires.
records.zomi: Pu Pau in a nasep a tawp khit ciangin class kua in a hilh ding hiam, ci-in ka ngaihsun hi.

records.english: You aren't allowed to tell anyone who scored highest until the results are official.
records.zomi: Thu a kiphuan ma-in kua in a sang pen hiam kuamah na gen thei kei hi.

records.english: Who, in your opinion, has done the most to improve the way this school is run?
records.zomi: Na ngaihsutna ah, hih sang ukna hoihsak dingin kua in a sem tam pen hiam?

records.english: Who would be the better person to write my recommendation letter, my professor or my former boss?
records.zomi: Ka thu theihpihna lai kua in gelh leh hoih zaw ding hiam, ka professor hiam, ka ukpa lui hiam?

records.english: Who do I talk to about changing my class schedule?
records.zomi: Ka class hun ciamteh laih nading kua tawh ka kiho ding hiam?

records.english: You can speak with Ms. Cing in the registrar's office on the second floor.
records.zomi: Inn dawl nihna a om registrar office ah Ms. Cing tawh na kiho thei hi.

records.english: Who left the copier jammed again?
records.zomi: Copier kua in a buaisak kik hiam?

records.english: I asked around to find out who had been taking supplies from the storage room, but no one would admit to it.
records.zomi: Vante koihna khan pan kua in vante a la hiam ka dong kawikawi hi, ahi zongin kuamah in a pom kei uh hi.

records.english: Who isn't here today?
records.zomi: Tuni kua a om kei hiam?

records.english: Who will be held accountable if the shipment arrives late?
records.zomi: Vante a zekai-a a tun leh kua in a mawhpuak ding hiam?

records.english: Who is your new manager at the warehouse?
records.zomi: Vante kholna inn ah na ukpa thak kua hiam?

records.english: It's hard to say who deserves the award more, since both teachers worked incredibly hard this year.
records.zomi: Sia nihte in tu kum haksa mahmah-in a sem uh ahih manin, kua in letsong a ngah zaw ding hiam gen haksa hi.

records.english: Who is expected to take over your duties while you're on vacation, and have you briefed them yet?
records.zomi: Na khawl laitakin na nasep kua in a sem ding hiam, amah na hilh khin hiam?

records.english: Who should I ask if I need a day off?
records.zomi: Ni khat ka khawl nuam leh kua ka dong ding hiam?

records.english: Whoever gets to the office first is expected to unlock the front gate.
records.zomi: Office a tung masa pen in mai lam kongpi a hong ding hi.

records.english: Who wrote "See me after class" on my test?
records.zomi: Ka sitna tungah “Class khit ciangin hong mu in” kua in a gelh hiam?

records.english: "Who's in charge here?" the inspector asked as soon as he walked into the factory.
records.zomi: “Hih munah kua in a uk hiam?” ci-in enkaktu in factory a lut pakin a dong hi.

records.english: Who in your office would you trust to cover for you in an emergency?
records.zomi: Thu haksa a tun ciangin na office sungah kua na muang ding hiam?

records.english: Who's the quiet boy sitting at the back of the classroom?
records.zomi: Class nunglam ah a tu tapa dai pen kua hiam?

records.english: That's Mung, and he just transferred here from another school.
records.zomi: Tua pen Mung ahi a, sang dang pan a hong pem thak hi.

records.english: Who chose the topic for your final essay — you or your teacher?
records.zomi: Na lai gelh nunung pen' thu kua in a teel hiam — nang hiam, na sia hiam?

records.english: Who is ultimately responsible for making sure the lab is locked and the gas valves are shut at the end of the day?
records.zomi: Ni bei ciangin lab kalh-in gas kongte khak ding kua in a mawhpuak pen hiam?

records.english: Who broke the window in the science room?
records.zomi: Science khan tawhkhawng kua in a kitan sak hiam?

records.english: The science room window got broken during last night's storm, so nobody is to blame.
records.zomi: Zan a huihpi in science khan tawhkhawng a kitan sak ahih manin kuamah mawh kei hi.

records.english: Who wants to read the next paragraph aloud?
records.zomi: A zom laigual aw ngaih takin kua in a sim nuam hiam?

records.english: I do want to read it, but my voice is a little hoarse today.
records.zomi: Ka sim nuam taktak hi, ahi zongin tuni ka aw a ek deuh hi.

records.english: The committee has yet to announce who will receive this year's scholarship.
records.zomi: Tu kum scholarship kua in a ngah ding hiam committee in a gen nai kei hi.

records.english: Who had the idea of starting a reading club for the younger students?
records.zomi: Sangnaupang neute adingin lai sim pawl khat kipat ding ngaihsutna kua in a nei hiam?

records.english: Please tell the front office who is picking you up so that they can let your ride through the gate.
records.zomi: Kongpi pan na tuanna a lut theih nadingin, kua in hong la ding hiam mai lam office gen in.

records.english: Whoever designed this schedule clearly never had to take three exams in one day.
records.zomi: Hih hun ciamteh a bawl mi in ni khat sungin sitna thum a et kul ngei lo hi.

records.english: Who has the key to the supply cabinet?
records.zomi: Vante koihna bawm tawhtang kua in a len hiam?

records.english: Do you happen to know who is giving the lecture in Hall B this afternoon?
records.zomi: Tu sun Hall B ah kua in thu a gen ding hiam na thei hiam?

records.english: Students must not leave campus without telling the teacher who is on duty.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte in ngak a om sia gen lo-in sang huang pan a pai khia thei kei uh hi.

records.english: Who do you report to at your new job?
records.zomi: Na nasep thak ah kua kiangah na gen hiam?

records.english: I report directly to the head of the engineering department.
records.zomi: Engineering department makaipa kiangah ka gen pah hi.

records.english: Nobody knows yet who will be promoted to supervisor.
records.zomi: Kua in supervisor a suak ding hiam kuamah in a thei nai kei uh hi.

records.english: Who are you working with on the history assignment?
records.zomi: Tangthu nasep ah kua tawh na sem khawm hiam?

records.english: Who will be our substitute teacher while Mrs. Lun is on maternity leave?
records.zomi: Lun nu a nau neih khawl laitakin i sia aiawhtu kua ding hiam?

records.english: Who gave you permission to leave work early?
records.zomi: Nasepna pan pai masa dingin kua in hong phal hiam?

records.english: Who cleaned the whiteboard?
records.zomi: Whiteboard kua in a nul siang hiam?

records.english: Who are the two new nurses on our floor?
records.zomi: I dawl a om nurse thak nihte kua uh hiam?

records.english: Who is that man talking to the principal?
records.zomi: Sang makaipa tawh a kiho pa pen kua hiam?

records.english: He's the new custodian, and his name is Kham.
records.zomi: Amah pen inn ngaktu thak ahi a, a min Kham ahi hi.

records.english: The person who interviewed me for this job turned out to be the company's founder.
records.zomi: Hih nasep adingin hong dong mi pen company a phuankhiatu ahi hi.

records.english: Who teaches your math class this semester?
records.zomi: Tu semester sungin na kisim class kua in a hilh hiam?

records.english: Mr. Thang teaches it, and he always explains things slowly and clearly.
records.zomi: Pu Thang in a hilh a, zawlzawl leh cingtakin a hilhcian tawntung hi.

records.english: Who was hired to replace the old accountant?
records.zomi: Sum kemtu lui aiawh dingin kua a kisam hiam?

records.english: Who might be able to help me fix this spreadsheet?
records.zomi: Hih spreadsheet phuah dingin kua in hong huh thei kha ding hiam?

records.english: Grace might know, since she handles all the budget reports.
records.zomi: Sum zat report khempeuh a bawl ahih manin Grace in a thei kha ding hi.

records.english: Who trained you on the new cash register?
records.zomi: Cash register thak zat dan kua in hong hilh hiam?

records.english: Could you remind me who is leading tomorrow's training session?
records.zomi: Zingciang sinsakna kua in a makai ding hiam hong phawksak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Who approves these expense forms?
records.zomi: Hih sum zatna form te kua in a pom hiam?

records.english: In our country, the army answers to the national government, not to the states.
records.zomi: I gam ah galkapte gam ukna kiangah a pang uh a, state te kiangah a pang kei uh hi.

records.english: Both the state and the national government paid for the new highway.
records.zomi: State leh gam ukna nih tengteng in lam lianpi thak man a pia uh hi.

records.english: The governor made every state agency publish its budget online.
records.zomi: Governor in state department khempeuh in a sum zat ding online ah a phuang sak hi.

records.english: The governor had the damaged bridge repaired within a month.
records.zomi: Governor in kha khat sungin lei siat a phuah sak hi.

records.english: Please help me fill out this form for the state housing office.
records.zomi: State inn office adingin hih form dim dingin hong huh in.

records.english: In our country, a state can make its own rules about many things, but it cannot go against the national constitution.
records.zomi: I gam ah state khat in thu tampi ah amah' thukham a bawl thei hi, ahi zongin gam thukham lianpen a langpan thei kei hi.

records.english: The state and national governments argued for months over who should bear the cost of the new dam.
records.zomi: State leh gam ukna in tuikulh thak man kua in a pia ding hiam kha tampi a kinial uh hi.

records.english: Will the state keep giving free school lunches to every child next year?
records.zomi: Kum zom ciangin state in naupang khempeuh sang sun an a man om lo-in a pia lai ding hiam?

records.english: In cases where a state law conflicts with a national law, which court has the final say?
records.zomi: State thukham leh gam thukham a kituak loh ciangin, thukhenna bang in a khensat nunung hiam?

records.english: Speaking to the visiting minister, the mayor said, "Our town needs more help from the capital, not less."
