records.english: Our neighbor introduced us to his nephew, who later became my husband.
records.zomi: I inn veng in a tanau hong theisak a, tua pa nung ciangin ka pasal hong suak hi.

records.english: Would it be okay if my daughter came over to say hello to you?
records.zomi: Ka tanu in hello hong ci dingin a hong pai leh a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: Call me when your cousin arrives, and I'll come down to meet her.
records.zomi: Na sanggam a tun ciangin hong sam in, amah kong mu dingin ka hong kumsuk ding hi.

records.english: He isn't my boyfriend — he's my cousin on my father's side.
records.zomi: Amah ka it pa hi lo hi — ka pa lam pan ka sanggam ahi hi.

records.english: Watch out — my little sister will talk your ear off if you let her.
records.zomi: Pilvang in — ka nau numei na phal leh na bil a natsak dongin a gen ding hi.

records.english: My godmother, who traveled all the way from Canada for my graduation, is standing right over there.
records.zomi: Ka sang zawhna adingin Canada pan a hong pai ka pasian nu pen tua mun ah a ding hi.

records.english: Jake was invited to the party by mistake, but he ended up becoming one of our closest friends.
records.zomi: Jake pen a khial-in poai ah kisam hi, ahi zongin i lawm kinai pente lak pan khat hong suak hi.

records.english: Whose kids are these?
records.zomi: Hih naupangte kua' ta hi uh hiam?

records.english: They're my neighbor's, and I'm watching them for the afternoon.
records.zomi: Ka inn veng' tate ahi uh a, tu sun amaute ka ma hi.

records.english: Introducing my two closest friends to each other was a risk, but it paid off when they started dating.
records.zomi: Ka lawm kinai pen nihte kitheisak pen lau huai hi, ahi zongin a kingaih pan ciangun a hoih hi.

records.english: What's your friend's name?
records.zomi: Na lawm' min bang hiam?

records.english: Can I introduce you as my business partner, or would you rather I just say "friend"?
records.zomi: Ka sumbawl kikoppih bangin kong theisak thei ding hiam, ahih kei leh “lawm” bek ka cih na deih zaw hiam?

records.english: We were introduced at a wedding ten years ago.
records.zomi: Kum sawm lai-in kiteenna khat ah i kithei uh hi.

records.english: Here come my parents now.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh pa tu-in a hong tung uh hi.

records.english: Could I bring my roommate to your birthday dinner?
records.zomi: Na pianni nitak an ah ka inn tenpih ka paipih thei ding hiam?

records.english: Of course — the more the merrier!
records.zomi: Thei hi — mi tam semsem leh nuam semsem hi!

records.english: Ah, so you're the famous Kham I've heard so much about!
records.zomi: Ah, tua ahih leh nang ka zaksa mahmah Kham minthang na hi hi!

records.english: What a lovely family you have!
records.zomi: Na innkuan bangzah hoih hiam!

records.english: You remember my brother-in-law, don't you?
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu' pasal na phawk hi, hi lo maw?

records.english: Have you been introduced to everyone yet?
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh tawh na kithei khin hiam?

records.english: Please introduce me to your parents when they arrive.
records.zomi: Na nu leh pa a tun ciangun hong theisak in.

records.english: My stepfather raised me from the age of four, so he's simply Dad to me.
records.zomi: Ka pakik in ka kum li pan hong khoi ahih manin, kei adingin Pa mah ahi hi.

records.english: May I introduce my colleague, Dr. Patel, who will be joining our team next month?
records.zomi: Kha zom ciangin i pawl ah a hong kihel ding ka nasep pih Dr. Patel kong theisak thei ding hiam?

records.english: These are my twin daughters, Cing and Niang.
records.zomi: Hih te pen ka tanu apengte, Cing leh Niang ahi uh hi.

records.english: I've told my friends all about you, so they're excited to finally meet you.
records.zomi: Ka lawmte kiangah na thu khempeuh ka gen khin ahih manin, hong muh ding a lamen mahmah uh hi.

records.english: May I offer you a cup of coffee or tea?
records.zomi: Kawfi hiam niangtui hiam khuat khat kong pia thei ding hiam?

records.english: My aunt welcomed us with a huge pot of chicken soup, even though it was nearly midnight and she had to work early the next morning.
records.zomi: Zan laitak naih khin a, zingciang zingsang tuung nasem ding hi napi, ka ni in aksa tui beel lianpi khat tawh hong muak hi.

records.english: Our new neighbors were welcomed so warmly that they invited the whole street to dinner the following week.
records.zomi: I inn veng thakte lungdam mahmah takin kimuak ahih manin, a kal zom ciangin lampi bup mite nitak an ne dingin a sam uh hi.

records.english: Thank you so much for coming all this way to see us.
records.zomi: Hong mu dingin hih zah gamla pan na hong pai ahih manin ka lungdam mahmah hi.

records.english: Here, let me carry that suitcase upstairs for you.
records.zomi: Hih, na suitcase a tung lam ah kong puak sak ning.

records.english: Visiting relatives can be exhausting, but I wouldn't trade those noisy weekends for anything.
records.zomi: Beh leh phungte hong veh pen gim huai thei hi, ahi zongin tua kal bei buaibuai te bangmah tawh ka laih kei ding hi.

records.english: If it gets cold tonight, there are extra blankets in the closet.
records.zomi: Tu zanin a vot leh, puan behlap koihna sungah a om hi.

records.english: Supposing your train is late, would you rather we wait at the station or meet you at the house?
records.zomi: Na meileng a zekai leh, station ah i ngak ding na deih zaw hiam, inn ah hiam?

records.english: You can stay as long as you like — there's no need to rush back.
records.zomi: Na deih dong na om thei hi — kin takin na ciah kul kei hi.

records.english: The heavy rain delayed our guests, so dinner started an hour late.
records.zomi: Guah nasia in i zinte a zekai sak ahih manin, nitak an nai khat zekai-in kipan hi.

records.english: Do you mind if we eat a little later tonight?
records.zomi: Tu zanin zekai deuh-in an i nek leh na lungkim hiam?

records.english: We hope you'll feel at home here.
records.zomi: Hih munah inn bangin na kisak ding i lamen hi.

records.english: Our guests from overseas were so tired after their journey that they fell asleep before dinner.
records.zomi: Tuipi galkhat pan a hong pai i zinte a khualzinna uh gim mahmah ahih manin, nitak an ma-in a ihmu uh hi.

records.english: You might want to take your shoes off, because the floor was just polished.
records.zomi: Sual a kinul thak ahih manin, na khedap na suah leh hoih kha ding hi.

records.english: Hello there — is your mother at home?
records.zomi: Hello — na nu inn ah a om hiam?

records.english: Please excuse the mess; the kids were playing in here all morning.
records.zomi: A kiginloh hong maisak in; naupangte zingsang bup hih sungah a kimawl uh hi.

records.english: Our guest room is small, but the bed is comfortable.
records.zomi: I zin khan a neu hi, ahi zongin a lupna a nuam hi.

records.english: The kids have been looking forward to your visit all week.
records.zomi: Naupangte in kal bup sungin na hong veh ding a lamen uh hi.

records.english: Welcome to our home.
records.zomi: I inn ah na hong tun lungdam hi.

records.english: We've put fresh towels in the bathroom for you.
records.zomi: Kisilna inn ah nang adingin puan siangtho i koih hi.

records.english: Shall I show you to your room?
records.zomi: Na khan kong lak ding hiam?

records.english: It's such an honor to welcome you to our church, Pastor.
records.zomi: Pastor, i pawlpi ah kong muak thei pen thupi mahmah hi.

records.english: Make yourself at home while I finish cooking.
records.zomi: Ka an huan ka zawh dong inn bangin om in.

records.english: Visitors are asked to check in at the front desk before going upstairs.
records.zomi: Mikhualte in a tung lam a kah ma-un mai lam dawhkan ah a min uh a gelh ding uh hi.

records.english: Grandpa made everyone stand at the door to greet the guests as they arrived.
records.zomi: Pu in zinte a hong tun ciangun hopih dingin mi khempeuh kongkhak ah a dingsak hi.

records.english: Could you sign the visitors' book before you leave?
records.zomi: Na pai ma-in mikhual laibu ah na min na gelh thei ding hiam?

records.english: There's no need to bring anything except yourselves.
records.zomi: Note mah bek tawh hong pai un, bangmah tawi kul lo hi.

records.english: Please, sit down and rest.
records.zomi: Tu inla tawlnga in.

records.english: Would you like something to drink?
records.zomi: Dawn ding bangmah na deih hiam?

records.english: Just some water would be great, thanks.
records.zomi: Tui bek a hoih ding hi, ka lungdam hi.

records.english: We weren't expecting you until tomorrow, but you couldn't have picked a better day to surprise us!
records.zomi: Zingciang dong i lamen kei uh hi, ahi zongin hong lamdangsak dingin ni hoih zaw na teel thei kei ding hi!

records.english: The children painted a "Welcome Home" sign for their father, who had been working abroad for two years.
records.zomi: Naupangte in kum nih sung gamdang ah na a sem a pa uh adingin “Inn ah na hong tun kik lungdam hi” ci lim a gelh uh hi.

records.english: Is it all right if I park my car in your driveway?
records.zomi: Na inn mai ah ka mawtaw ka koih leh a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: Sure, but leave enough space for my husband's truck.
records.zomi: Hoih hi, ahi zongin ka pasal' truck adingin mun a cin dingin nusia in.

records.english: When visitors come to our house, my grandfather always insists on serving them tea first.
records.zomi: Mikhualte i inn a hong tun ciangun, ka pu in niangtui a pia masa ding a ngen ngiat tawntung hi.

records.english: Feel free to use the kitchen whenever you like.
records.zomi: Na deih ciangciang anbuk na zang thei hi.

records.english: Why don't you leave your bags here and freshen up first?
records.zomi: Na ipte hih munah koih inla, na kisil masa ding hiam?

records.english: You could take the bus into town tomorrow, or I could drive you myself.
records.zomi: Zingciang khua sung ah bus na tuan thei hi, ahih kei leh kei mah in kong paipih thei hi.

records.english: Hearing the doorbell, the children raced each other to see who would open it first.
records.zomi: Kongkhak daak ging a zak ciangun, kua in a hon masa ding hiam ci-in naupangte a kitai uh hi.

records.english: My uncle arrived at noon, unpacked his bags, and immediately asked to see the garden.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu sun laitak ciangin a hong tung a, a ipte a phel a, huan en dingin a ngen pah hi.

records.english: Help yourself to anything in the fridge.
records.zomi: Vot bawlna sungah a om khatpeuh la in.

records.english: Come in, come in — you must be freezing!
records.zomi: Hong lut in, hong lut in — na vot mahmah ding hi!

records.english: Did you find the house easily?
records.zomi: Inn na mu baih hiam?

records.english: Not really — my phone's map sent me down the wrong street twice.
records.zomi: Mu baih lo hi — ka phone map in lampi khial ah nihvei hong paisak hi.

records.english: Have a seat anywhere you like.
records.zomi: Na deihna mun ah tu in.

records.english: Being greeted at the airport by the whole family brought tears to my eyes.
records.zomi: Vanlengtual ah innkuan bup in hong muak ciangun ka mittui a luang hi.

records.english: Would your children like to play in the backyard while we talk?
records.zomi: I kiho laitakin na tate inn nunglam ah kimawl nuam uh hiam?

records.english: Can I take your coat?
records.zomi: Na puan sil kong la sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Welcome back!
records.zomi: Na hong tun kik lungdam hi!

records.english: Sorry, the dog gets excited around new people, but he won't bite.
records.zomi: Hong maisak in, ui in mi thak a muh ciangin a lungdam a, ahi zongin a ngoih kei ding hi.

records.english: How was your flight?
records.zomi: Na vanleng tuanna bangci om hiam?

records.english: On behalf of the whole school, I'd like to welcome our visitors from the education ministry.
records.zomi: Sang bup aiawhin, sinna ministry pan a hong veh mikhualte ka muak nuam hi.

records.english: Let me know if you need anything else.
records.zomi: Bang dang na kisap leh hong gen in.

records.english: Wipe your feet on the mat, please.
records.zomi: Na khe tung lei khe nulna tungah nul in.

records.english: What time should we expect you on Saturday?
records.zomi: Kiginni ciangin nai bangzah ciangin hong lamen ding i hi hiam?

records.english: Around six, unless the traffic is bad.
records.zomi: Mawtaw a buai kei leh nai guk bang ciangin.

records.english: Our neighbors may stop by later to say hello.
records.zomi: I inn vengte hello ci dingin a nung ciangin a hong pai kha ding uh hi.

records.english: Is this your first time visiting our town?
records.zomi: Hih pen i khua na hong veh masak pen hi hiam?

records.english: Yes, and I already love how friendly everyone is.
records.zomi: Hi hi, mi khempeuh bangzah lawmsiam uh hiam ka it khin hi.

records.english: My father had the guest room painted especially for your visit.
records.zomi: Ka pa in na hong veh nadingin zin khan a zai sak hi.

records.english: Before leaving the hospital, my father made a point of thanking every nurse on the ward.
records.zomi: Zato pan a pai ma-in, ka pa in nurse khempeuh lungdam a ko ciat hi.

records.english: Perhaps we'll run into each other at the conference next year.
records.zomi: Kum zom ciangin conference ah i kimu kha ding hi.

records.english: Is it okay if I keep your sweater until next time?
records.zomi: A zom ciang dong na sweater ka kem leh a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: Is this goodbye for good, or will you come back next summer?
records.zomi: Hih pen khentuamna tawntung hi hiam, khuakhal zom ciangin na hong ciah kik ding hiam?

records.english: The longer we stood at the station, the harder it was to say goodbye.
records.zomi: Station ah i din sawt semsem leh, kikhen a haksa semsem hi.

records.english: Drive safely, and call us when you get home.
records.zomi: Pilvang takin mawtaw mawng inla, inn na tun ciangin hong sam in.

records.english: I'll miss you so much!
records.zomi: Kong ngaih mahmah ding hi!

records.english: We hugged at the gate, she walked through security, and I stood there until I couldn't see her anymore.
records.zomi: Kongpi ah ka kipom uh a, amah enkaktute kal ah a pai a, ka muh nawn loh dong tua munah ka ding hi.

records.english: Saying goodbye to my students on the last day of school always makes me cry.
records.zomi: Sang ni nunung pen ah ka sangnaupangte tawh kikhen in ka kap sak tawntung hi.

records.english: Waving goodbye from the train window, she promised herself she would return one day.
records.zomi: Meileng tawhkhawng pan khut lap-in, ni khat ni-in ka ciah kik ding hi, ci-in amah le amah a kiciam hi.

records.english: Leaving my hometown was harder than I expected.
records.zomi: Ka khua paisan pen ka ngaihsut sangin a haksa zaw hi.

records.english: Goodbyes at airports are always the hardest for me.
records.zomi: Kei adingin vanlengtual a kikhenna a haksa pen tawntung hi.

records.english: Can we say goodbye to the puppy before we go?
records.zomi: I pai ma-in uino kiangah “Goodbye” i ci thei ding hiam?

records.english: Say goodbye to Grandma before we go.
records.zomi: I pai ma-in Pi kiangah “Goodbye” ci in.

records.english: The rain made us cut our goodbyes short.
records.zomi: Guah in i kikhenna a tomsak hi.

records.english: Have a safe trip!
records.zomi: Dam takin pai in!

records.english: I do hope you'll visit us again.
records.zomi: Hong veh kik ding na hi, ci-in ka lamen taktak hi.

records.english: It's been great catching up with you.
records.zomi: Nang tawh kiho kik a nuam mahmah hi.

records.english: I do want to stay longer, but I promised to be home by nine.
records.zomi: Om sawt zaw ka deih taktak hi, ahi zongin nai kua ma-in inn ka tung ding ka kiciam khin hi.

records.english: My grandparents waved from the porch until our car disappeared around the corner.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh ka pi in i mawtaw kikalna ah a mang dong inn mai pan khut a lap uh hi.

records.english: Wait, you forgot your umbrella!
records.zomi: Ngak in, na kawl lukhu na mangngilh hi!

records.english: Text me when you land.
records.zomi: Na tun ciangin text hong khak in.

records.english: We might not see each other for a long time, so I want to say a proper goodbye.
records.zomi: Hun sawtpi i kimu kei kha ding ahih manin, cingtakin “Goodbye” ka ci nuam hi.

records.english: The boss let everyone go home early so they could say goodbye to their retiring colleague.
records.zomi: A nasep tawp ding a nasep pih tawh a kikhen theih nadingun ukpa in mi khempeuh a pai masa sak hi.

records.english: I have to say goodbye now, or I'll be late for work.
records.zomi: Tu-in ka kikhen ding hi, ahih kei leh nasepna ah ka zekai ding hi.

records.english: Would you like to take some leftovers home?
records.zomi: An a lai tawm inn ah na tawi nuam hiam?

records.english: Good night, everyone, and thanks for a lovely evening.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh zanpha, nitak nuam hong piak ahih manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: My coworkers organized a farewell lunch for me on my last day.
records.zomi: Ka ni nunung ah ka nasep pihte in kikhenna sun an hong bawl sak uh hi.

records.english: I might be back in town next month, so this isn't really goodbye.
records.zomi: Kha zom ciangin khua ah ka hong tung kik kha ding ahih manin, hih pen kikhenna taktak hi lo hi.

records.english: Nobody warned me how strange it would feel to say goodbye to the house I grew up in.
records.zomi: Ka khanna inn tawh kikhen pen bangzah lamdang ding hiam kuamah in hong gen kei uh hi.

records.english: Do you really have to leave so soon?
records.zomi: Hih zah manlang takin na pai taktak ding hiam?

records.english: I'm afraid so; my bus leaves in twenty minutes.
records.zomi: Hi hi; ka bus minit sawmnih sungin a pai ding hi.

records.english: Could you wake me up before you leave in the morning?
records.zomi: Zingsangin na pai ma-in hong phawng sak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Our pastor had the whole congregation pray for the missionary family before they left.
records.zomi: I pastor in tangthu genna innkuan a pai ma-un pawlpi bup in a adingun thu a ngen sak hi.

records.english: Off you go, then — and behave yourselves at Grandpa's.
records.zomi: Tua ahih leh pai un — Pu' inn ah hoih takin om un.

records.english: I'm sorry I have to cut this short, but my daughter is waiting for me outside.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in a polam ah hong ngak ahih manin a tomin ka khawl ding hi, hong maisak in.

records.english: You can go now, but come straight back if the doctor says anything worrying.
records.zomi: Tu-in na pai thei hi, ahi zongin siavuan in lungkham huai thu khat a gen leh hong ciah pah kik in.

records.english: I'd better get going before it gets dark.
records.zomi: Khua a mial ma-in ka pai leh hoih zaw ding hi.

records.english: Leaving without saying goodbye would have been rude, so I went back inside to find our host.
records.zomi: Kikhen lo-in pai pen zahtak lohna hi ding ahih manin, inn neipa zong dingin sung ah ka lut kik hi.

records.english: Who's going to drive Aunt Mary to the airport tomorrow morning?
records.zomi: Zingciang zingsangin Ni Mary vanlengtual ah kua in a paipih ding hiam?

records.english: Pass on my best wishes to your parents when you see them.
records.zomi: Na nu leh pa na muh ciangin ka lungdamna gen sak in.

records.english: Until we meet again, keep us in your prayers.
records.zomi: I kimuh kik ma-in, na thungetna ah hong phawk den un.

records.english: She had her brother take a photo of us before we said goodbye.
records.zomi: I kikhen ma-un a sanggam pasal in i limlak a la sak hi.

records.english: My last day at the factory ended with a speech, a cake, and far more tears than I had expected.
records.zomi: Factory ah ka ni nunung pen thugen, cake leh ka lamet sangin mittui tampi zaw tawh a bei hi.

records.english: Can I leave a little early today to catch my train?
records.zomi: Ka meileng ka tuan theih nadingin tuni pai masa deuh thei ding ka hi hiam?

records.english: Yes, go ahead — just finish that email first.
records.zomi: Thei hi, pai in — tua email zo masa in.

records.english: See you tomorrow at school.
records.zomi: Zingciang sang ah kimu kik ni.

records.english: Shall I walk you to your car?
records.zomi: Na mawtaw dong kong paipih ding hiam?

records.english: Thanks for having me — I had a wonderful time.
records.zomi: Hong muak ahih manin ka lungdam hi — ka nuam mahmah hi.

records.english: Remember to lock the door behind you.
records.zomi: Na pai ciangin kongkhak kalh ding phawk in.

records.english: Promise you'll write to me every week.
records.zomi: Kal simin lai hong khak ding na kiciam in.

records.english: You may leave the meeting once you've signed the attendance sheet.
records.zomi: Kihelna lai ah na min na gelh khit ciangin kikhopna pan na pai thei hi.

records.english: Where are you heading after this?
records.zomi: Hih khit ciangin koi ah na pai ding hiam?

records.english: Straight home — I'm exhausted.
records.zomi: Inn ah ka ciah pah ding — ka gim mahmah hi.

records.english: Goodbye, and take care!
records.zomi: Goodbye, pilvang in!

records.english: Thank you for everything you've done for our family these past ten years.
records.zomi: Kum sawm sung i innkuan adingin na sepna khempeuh hangin ka lungdam mahmah hi.

records.english: Whatever happens next, I'm grateful our paths crossed during these years in the city.
records.zomi: A zom ah bang hong tung zongin, khuapi ah hih kumte sungin i kimuh theih ka lungdam hi.

records.english: Take this bag of mangoes with you for the road.
records.zomi: Lampi ah na nek nadingin hih haigah ip khat tawi in.

records.english: Before boarding the ship, my great-grandfather gave each of his children a small wooden cross.
records.zomi: Tembaw a tuan ma-in, ka pu' pa in a tate khat ciat sing kross neu khat a pia hi.

records.english: Bye for now — I'll call you over the weekend.
records.zomi: Tu-in goodbye — kal bei-in kong sam ding hi.

records.english: May I borrow the car tonight, Dad?
records.zomi: Pa, tu zanin mawtaw ka leitawi thei ding hiam?

records.english: Ever since my sister had her baby, the whole family has been taking turns helping her.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu in naungek a neih pan kipan innkuan bup in kilaih-in a huh uh hi.

records.english: Are you the oldest or the youngest in your family?
records.zomi: Na innkuan ah a upa pen na hi hiam, a neu pen na hi hiam?

records.english: My niece is only three, but she already bosses her older cousins around.
records.zomi: Ka tunu kum thum bek a pha napi, a upa zaw a sanggamte a uk khin hi.

records.english: Isn't the house quiet now that our youngest has started kindergarten?
records.zomi: I ta neu pen in naupang sang a kah pan ciangin inn a dai khin hi, hi lo maw?

records.english: I owe so much to my older brother, who looked after me when our parents were working long hours.
records.zomi: I nu leh pa in hun sawtpi a sep laitakun hong ma ka u pasal tungah ka leiba a tam mahmah hi.

records.english: Try to settle your arguments over a meal rather than by text message.
records.zomi: Na kinialna uh text message tawh hi lo-in an ne khawm-in a kituaksak dingin hanciam un.

records.english: Do you have any siblings?
records.zomi: Na u leh nau na nei hiam?

records.english: Just one — a younger brother who still lives with our parents.
records.zomi: Khat bek — i nu leh pa tawh a teeng lai nau pasal khat.

records.english: Are any of you coming to Grandpa's birthday dinner on Saturday?
records.zomi: Kiginni ciangin Pu' pianni nitak an ah na lak pan kua hong pai ding hiam?

records.english: Family comes first in our house.
records.zomi: I inn ah innkuan masa hi.

records.zomi: Puan meitut pen ka thuak zawh loh inn nasep khat bek ahi hi.

records.english: You need a ladder to hang these curtains.
records.zomi: Hih puan khaite khai dingin kahlei na kisam hi.

records.english: Ever since my husband lost his job, he's taken over most of the cooking and shopping.
records.zomi: Ka pasal in a nasepna a mansuah pan an huan leh an lei a tam zaw a sem hi.

records.english: Thanks for doing the dishes — you didn't have to!
records.zomi: Kuangte na sawp ahih manin ka lungdam hi — na sawp kul kei hi!

records.english: Fixing the broken fence took us the whole weekend.
records.zomi: Huang siat phuah in kal bei bup hong la hi.

records.english: We had the plumber fix the leaking kitchen sink last week.
records.zomi: Kal bei-in anbuk tui kholna a zui pen tui pipe phuahtu in i phuahsak hi.

records.english: Our grandmother still grinds rice into flour with a heavy wooden pestle.
records.zomi: I pi in buh pen sumtuk gik tawh vui-in a sum lai hi.

records.english: Unless everyone pitches in, this house will never be clean before the guests arrive.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh a kihel kei leh, zinte a tun ma-in hih inn siangtho ngei lo ding hi.

records.english: Each of the children has one job after dinner: clearing the table, washing, or drying.
records.zomi: Nitak an khit ciangin naupangte khat ciat in nasep khat a nei uh hi: dawhkan khiat, sawp, a hih kei leh keusak.

records.english: The roof was repaired just before the rainy season started.
records.zomi: Guahtui hun a kipat ma-in innkhum kiphuah hi.

records.english: When did you learn to cook so well?
records.zomi: Bang hun in hih zah hoih takin an huan na sin hiam?

records.english: Honestly, I'd rather scrub the bathroom than do the ironing.
records.zomi: Puan meitut sangin kisilna inn siangsak ka deih zaw hi.

records.english: Everyone in our house makes their own bed in the morning.
records.zomi: I inn ah mi khempeuh in zingsangin a lupna ciat a bawl uh hi.

records.english: Tidy up your room, and then you can go play outside.
records.zomi: Na khan siangsak in, tua khit ciangin a polam ah na kimawl thei hi.

records.english: Kids, the yard has to be raked before anyone goes outside to play.
records.zomi: Naupangte, kuamah kimawl dinga a pai ma-un inntual phiat siang ding hi.

records.english: The kitchen floor gets sticky no matter how often I mop it.
records.zomi: Bangzah vei ka nul zongin anbuk sual a kibelh hi.

records.english: My daughter does want to help, but she's still too young to use a sharp knife.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in huh a deih taktak hi, ahi zongin namsau hiam zat dingin a neu lai hi.

records.english: Nobody is allowed to leave dirty dishes in the sink overnight.
records.zomi: Kuang ninte zan khat tui kholna sungah kuamah in a nusia thei kei hi.

records.english: We keep the cleaning supplies on a high shelf so that the toddler can't reach them.
records.zomi: Naupang neu in a tun loh nadingin siangsakna vante dawh sang ah i koih hi.

records.english: Unclog the drain with a plunger before you try any chemicals.
records.zomi: Zatui na zat ma-in tui luanna kiphihna plunger tawh hon masa in.

records.english: Every Saturday morning, the whole family cleans the house together while listening to the radio.
records.zomi: Kiginni zingsang simin innkuan bup in radio ngai-in inn i siangsak khawm hi.

records.english: Our son convinced us to let him study abroad for a year.
records.zomi: I tapa in kum khat sung gamdang ah lai a sin dingin hong phalsak hi.

records.english: Why can't I go to the concert when all my friends are going?
records.zomi: Ka lawmte khempeuh a pai uh hangin bang hangin la khawmpi ah ka pai thei lo hiam?

records.english: Because it ends after midnight and you have school the next day.
records.zomi: Zan laitak khit ciangin a bei a, zingciang sang na kah ding ahih manin.

records.english: Honestly, I think we're all making this more complicated than it needs to be.
records.zomi: Ka gen taktak leh, a kisam sangin i khempeuh in a haksasak i hi hi, ka ci hi.

records.english: Are you sure you want to quit your job before you've found a new one?
records.zomi: Nasepna thak na muh ma-in na nasep na khawl ding taktak hiam?

records.english: Since our parents are getting older, we need to start planning how to support them.
records.zomi: I nu leh pa a upa semsem ahih manun, amaute bangci i huh ding hiam ngaihsun i kipan ding hi.

records.english: Can we please stop shouting and listen to each other?
records.zomi: Kikou nawn lo-in kingai tuah thei ding i hi hiam?

records.english: To avoid any more arguments, we wrote down a monthly budget and stuck it on the fridge.
records.zomi: Kinialna dang a om loh nadingin, kha simin sum zat ding i gelh a, vot bawlna tungah i belh hi.

records.english: How should we split the cost of Mom's birthday present?
records.zomi: Nu' pianni letsong man bangci i kikhen ding hiam?

records.english: Each of us pays the same amount, and Joseph adds a little extra because he earns the most.
records.zomi: I khat ciat in a kibang i pia a, Joseph in a ngah tam pen ahih manin tawm khat a behlap hi.

records.english: My sister made me apologize to our father before she would speak to me again.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu in hong kiho kik ma-in i pa kiangah hong maisak ngen dingin hong sawl hi.

records.english: We have to talk about your grades.
records.zomi: Na sitna ngah dan thu i kikum ding hi.

records.english: Could you explain why you think boarding school is a good idea?
records.zomi: Bang hangin boarding school a hoih hi, na ci hiam hong hilhcian thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Grandma called a family meeting to discuss who would take care of the farm.
records.zomi: Pi in lo kua in a kem ding hiam kikum dingin innkuan kikhopna a sam hi.

records.english: Do all of you agree, or does anyone want to say something else?
records.zomi: Na khempeuh uh na lungkim uh hiam, ahih kei leh kuamah in thu dang a gen nuam hiam?

records.english: Raising the topic of a nursing home for Grandpa made Mom cry.
records.zomi: Pu adingin upate kepna inn thu a kigen ciangin Nu a kap hi.

records.english: What do you think we should name the puppy?
records.zomi: Uino min bang i phuah ding na ci hiam?

records.english: Your mother and I have decided to sell the house and move closer to the city.
records.zomi: Na nu leh kei inn zuak-in khuapi kiang naih zawin pem dingin i khensat hi.

records.english: Mom wrote everyone's suggestions on the whiteboard so that nothing would be forgotten.
records.zomi: Bangmah a mangngilh loh nadingin Nu in mi khempeuh ngaihsutnate whiteboard tungah a gelh hi.

records.english: Nobody leaves this table until we've sorted this out.
records.zomi: Hih thu i bawlsiam ma-in kuamah hih dawhkan pan pai thei lo hi.

records.english: Finally, after an hour of discussion, we agreed to visit both families during the holiday.
records.zomi: A tawpna-ah, nai khat sung kikum khit ciangin, khawlna hun sungin innkuan nih tengteng va veh dingin i kituak hi.

records.english: Please don't bring up the wedding while Aunt Ruth is here — it's still a sore subject.
records.zomi: Ni Ruth hih munah a om laitakin kiteenna thu gen kei un — a lungsim a na lai hi.

records.english: Can we talk about where we're going for the holidays this year?
records.zomi: Tu kum khawlna hun ciangin koi ah i pai ding hiam kikum thei ding i hi hiam?

records.english: Is now a good time to talk about the money you borrowed?
records.zomi: Na leitawi sum thu kikum dingin tu hun a hoih hiam?

records.english: The decision was made without asking me, and that hurt my feelings.
records.zomi: Hong dong lo-in kikhensat ahih manin ka lungsim a na hi.

records.english: Everyone, please sit down — your father and I have something important to tell you.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, tu un — na pa leh kei note kiangah thu thupi khat gen ding ka nei uh hi.

records.english: Weighing the pros and cons, we decided to stay in our current town for another year.
records.zomi: A hoih leh a hoih lo lam kiteh khit ciangin, kum khat sung i khua tu-a om ah om lai dingin i khensat hi.

records.english: You have to promise not to tell your brother about the surprise party.
records.zomi: Thakhat poai thu na sanggam pasal na gen lo ding na kiciam ding hi.

records.english: We sat around the kitchen table and wrote our ideas on a big sheet of paper.
records.zomi: Anbuk dawhkan kiim ah i tu a, lai lianpi tungah i ngaihsutnate i gelh hi.

records.english: We rarely agree on politics, so we try to avoid the topic at family dinners.
records.zomi: Gam ukna thu ah i kituak ngei kei ahih manin, innkuan nitak an ciangin tua thu gen loh dingin i hanciam hi.

records.english: Sorry to interrupt, but dinner is getting cold.
records.zomi: Hong khamsak ka hih hang hong maisak in, nitak an a vot pan hi.

records.english: We need to decide tonight whether Grandpa moves in with us.
records.zomi: Pu i kiangah a teeng ding hiam lo ding hiam tu zanin i khensat ding hi.

records.english: Hold on — I haven't said yes yet.
records.zomi: Ngak in — ka lungkim nai kei hi.

records.english: Listen, both of you — fighting won't solve anything.
records.zomi: Ngai un, note nih — kilai in bangmah a bawlsiam kei ding hi.

records.english: What did your parents say when you told them about the new job?
records.zomi: Nasepna thak thu na gen ciangin na nu leh pa in bang a ci uh hiam?

records.english: They were worried at first, but now they're proud of me.
records.zomi: A masa-in a lungkham uh a, ahi zongin tu-in hong kisaktheih uh hi.

records.english: Let me finish what I was saying before you interrupt.
records.zomi: Na hong khamsak ma-in ka gen laitak zo masa ning.

records.english: In our house, phones are not allowed at the table when we're talking about something serious.
records.zomi: I inn ah thu thupi i kikum ciangin dawhkan ah phone phal lo hi.

records.english: You kids have to agree on one movie, or nobody watches anything.
records.zomi: Naupangte, movie khat ah na kituak ding uh hi, ahih kei leh kuamah bangmah en lo ding hi.

records.english: I don't want to argue; I just want you to understand how I feel.
records.zomi: Kinial ka deih kei hi; ka lungsim na theih ding bek ka deih hi.

records.english: I wish you had asked me before you agreed to host Christmas.
records.zomi: Christmas bawl dinga na lungkim ma-in hong dong leng ka deih hi.

records.english: Shall we ask the children what they think before we decide?
records.zomi: I khensat ma-in naupangte bang a ngaihsun uh hiam dong ding i hi hiam?

records.english: I'm sorry I raised my voice.
records.zomi: Ka aw ka kaisang ahih manin hong maisak in.

records.english: My uncle suggested that we sell the old car to pay for my cousin's school fees.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in ka sanggam' sang man pia dingin mawtaw lui zuak dingin a gen hi.

records.english: Maybe we could take turns hosting the family dinner each month.
records.zomi: Kha simin innkuan nitak an kilaih-in i bawl thei kha ding hi.

records.english: Why don't we take a short break and come back to this after dinner?
records.zomi: Tawmno khawl-in nitak an khit ciangin hih thu i kikum kik leh bang ci ding hiam?

records.english: Who gets the bigger bedroom when we move?
records.zomi: I pem ciangin lupna khan lian zaw kua in a ngah ding hiam?

records.english: We'll go to the lake on Saturday unless it rains.
records.zomi: Guah a zuk kei leh Kiginni ciangin dil ah i pai ding hi.

records.english: Deciding whether to move abroad was the hardest conversation our family has ever had.
records.zomi: Gamdang ah pem ding hiam cih khensat pen i innkuan i kikupna lak pan a haksa pen ahi hi.

records.english: Talking openly about money has made our family much closer.
records.zomi: Sum thu kiphawng takin kikum in i innkuan a kinaihsak zaw mahmah hi.

records.english: It's your decision, but we'd like you to think about it carefully.
records.zomi: Nangma' khensat ding ahi hi, ahi zongin pil takin na ngaihsun ding i deih hi.

records.english: The whole family voted, and the beach won over the mountains.
records.zomi: Innkuan bup in vote i khia a, tuipi gei in mualte a zo hi.

records.english: We used a video call so that our cousins abroad could join the discussion.
records.zomi: Gamdang a om i sanggamte in kikupna ah a kihel theih nadingun video call i zang hi.

records.english: I do understand your point of view; I just don't agree with it.
records.zomi: Na ngaihsutna ka thei taktak hi; ka lungkim kei bek hi.

records.english: Thank you all for listening — I know this wasn't easy to talk about.
records.zomi: Na khempeuh uh na ngaih ahih manin ka lungdam hi — hih thu gen a baih lo cih ka thei hi.

records.english: Every Sunday evening, we plan the week's meals and activities together.
records.zomi: Nipini nitak simin kal khat sung an nek ding leh nasep dingte i ngaihsun khawm hi.

records.english: The family discussion was postponed because Dad had to work late.
records.zomi: Pa zekai-in a sep kul manin innkuan kikupna kihawh hi.

records.english: You can't keep avoiding this conversation forever.
records.zomi: Hih kikupna tawntungin na pelh thei kei hi.

records.english: The argument started over something small and ended with everyone laughing.
records.zomi: Kinialna pen na neucik khat tungah kipan a, mi khempeuh nuih tawh a bei hi.

records.english: Is something bothering you, or are you just tired tonight?
records.zomi: Bangmah in hong buaisak hiam, ahih kei leh tu zanin na gim bek hiam?

records.english: Wash your hands before you pick up the baby.
records.zomi: Naungek na pom ma-in na khut sil in.

records.english: Grandma has to take her medicine with food.
records.zomi: Pi in a zatui an tawh a ne ding hi.

records.english: Grandpa fell in the garden last week, but luckily nothing was broken.
records.zomi: Kal bei-in Pu huan sungah a puk hi, ahi zongin bangmah kitan lo hi.

records.english: The kids made Grandpa a birthday card with their handprints on it.
records.zomi: Naupangte in a khut lim tawh Pu adingin pianni card a bawl uh hi.

records.english: No sweets before dinner, kids.
records.zomi: Naupangte, nitak an ma-in tui-namtui ne lo ding.

records.english: The twins were finally asleep, so we sat down for our first quiet cup of tea all day.
records.zomi: Apengte a ihmut tawp ciangun, ni bup sungin niangtui khuat masa pen dai takin i dawn hi.

records.english: We don't let the kids play near the road without an adult.
records.zomi: Upa om lo-in naupangte lampi kiangah i kimawl sak kei hi.

records.english: Bedtime is at eight o'clock, and no arguing.
records.zomi: Lup hun nai giat ahi a, kinial lo ding hi.

records.english: The power went out during the night, and Grandma's oxygen machine stopped working.
records.zomi: Zanin meivak a mang a, Pi' oxygen machine na sem nawn lo hi.

records.english: My aunt quit her job to take care of my grandfather full-time.
records.zomi: Ka ni in ka pu a ma dingin a nasep a khawl hi.

records.english: Thank you for driving Grandma to her appointment this morning.
records.zomi: Tu zingsangin Pi a hun ciamna ah mawtaw tawh na paipih ahih manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: Is it safe to give a three-year-old this cough syrup?
records.zomi: Kum thum naupang tungah hih khuh zatui piak a hoih hiam?

records.english: Ask the doctor first — the label says it isn't for children under six.
records.zomi: Siavuan dong masa in — a lai tungah kum guk nuai naupangte adingin hi lo hi, a ci hi.

records.english: The bath water should be warm, not hot, so test it with your elbow first.
records.zomi: Kisilna tui a lum ding a, a sa lo ding hi, tua ahih manin na khutkhiat tawh en masa in.

records.english: Moving Grandma into our home was the right decision, but it wasn't easy for anyone.
records.zomi: Pi i inn ah paipih pen khensatna dik ahi hi, ahi zongin kuamah adingin a baih kei hi.

records.english: Because Grandpa forgets things easily, we label every drawer in his room.
records.zomi: Pu in na a mangngilh baih ahih manin, a khan sung dawh sung khempeuh ah min i belh hi.

records.english: Looking after young children takes a lot of energy and patience.
records.zomi: Naupang neute kem in thahatna leh thuakzawhna tampi a kisam hi.

records.english: Please speak a little louder; my grandfather doesn't hear very well.
records.zomi: Aw khauh deuh in gen in; ka pu in hoih takin a za thei kei hi.

records.english: It's exhausting to care for a newborn and an elderly parent at the same time.
records.zomi: Naungek thak leh nu hiam pa upa khat kem khawm a gim mahmah hi.

records.english: Our son learned to tie his shoes all by himself this week.
records.zomi: I tapa in tu kal sungin a khedap khau amah mah in khih a sin hi.

records.english: Who's looking after Grandpa while you're at work?
records.zomi: Nasepna ah na om sungin Pu kua in a ma hiam?

records.english: A nurse comes in every morning, and my aunt stays with him in the afternoon.
records.zomi: Zingsang simin nurse khat a hong pai a, sun ciangin ka ni amah tawh a om hi.

records.english: We hired a babysitter so that we could attend my cousin's wedding.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam' kiteenna ah i pai theih nadingin naupang matu khat i lak hi.

records.english: Dad refuses to use a walking stick, even though he's unsteady on his feet.
records.zomi: A khe a kip lo napi, Pa in ciangkhut zang ding a nial hi.

records.english: Please keep the front gate closed so the dog and the children don't run into the street.
records.zomi: Ui leh naupangte lampi ah a tai loh nadingun mai lam kongpi khak den un.

records.english: Please make sure Grandma drinks enough water today.
records.zomi: Tuni Pi in tui a cin dongin a dawn hiam en un.

records.english: Never leave a small child alone in the bathtub, not even for a minute.
records.zomi: Naupang neu kisilna bel sungah amah bek nusia ngei kei in, minit khat zong.

records.english: Changing an adult's bandage is harder than I expected.
records.zomi: Upa khat' liamna puan laih pen ka ngaihsut sangin a haksa zaw hi.

records.english: Our pediatrician told us to keep all medicines in a locked cabinet.
records.zomi: I naupang siavuan in zatui khempeuh a kikalh bawm sungah koih dingin hong gen hi.

records.english: Grandma was given a new medicine, and she's been sleeping better since.
records.zomi: Pi zatui thak kipia a, tua pan kipan a ihmut a hoih zaw hi.

records.english: Our kids always wear helmets when they ride their bikes.
records.zomi: I tate in siiksakol a tuan ciangun lukhu khauh a khu tawntung uh hi.

records.english: The toddler's toys must be kept away from the stairs.
records.zomi: Naupang neu' kimawlna vante kahlei pan gamla takah koih ding hi.

records.english: My daughter is teaching her grandmother how to make video calls on a tablet.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in a pi tablet tungah video call bawl dan a hilh hi.

records.english: What do you do when the baby won't stop crying?
records.zomi: Naungek a kah tawp nuam lo ciangin bang na sem hiam?

records.english: Sometimes I just walk around the house with her until she calms down.
records.zomi: A lungsim a nem dong amah pom-in inn sungah ka vak kawikawi ngei hi.

records.english: Have you thought about hiring someone to help with Dad's care?
records.zomi: Pa' kemna ah huh dingin mi khat lak ding na ngaihsun ngei hiam?

records.english: The nurse showed us how to check his blood pressure with a home monitor.
records.zomi: Nurse in inn monitor tawh a si khauhna bangci en ding hiam hong lak hi.

records.english: I do worry about Mom living alone, especially in winter.
records.zomi: Nu amah bek a teen ka lungkham taktak hi, a diakin phalbi ciangin.

records.english: I had the pharmacist explain the new pills to my father twice.
records.zomi: Zatui zuakpa in zatui thakte ka pa kiangah nihvei a hilhcian sak hi.

records.english: How often does your mother need to see the doctor?
records.zomi: Na nu in siavuan bangzah vei a mu ding hiam?

records.english: The stroller wheel got stuck in a crack in the sidewalk.
records.zomi: Stroller khe pen lampi gei kuakna sungah a kibelh hi.

records.english: Can you read me a story before I go to sleep?
records.zomi: Ka ihmut ma-in tangthu hong sim sak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Visiting hours at the care home end at seven, so we need to leave soon.
records.zomi: Upate kepna inn ah veh hun nai sagih ciangin a bei ahih manin, kin takin i pai ding hi.

records.english: Could you help me get Grandma into her wheelchair?
records.zomi: Pi a wheelchair sungah a tut nadingin hong huh thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Respecting our elders is something our parents taught us from a very young age.
records.zomi: Upate zahtak pen i neu lai pan i nu leh pa in hong hilh na khat ahi hi.

records.english: Hold the baby's head carefully — she can't support it on her own yet.
records.zomi: Naungek' lu pil takin pom in — amah mah in a lu a dawm zo nai kei hi.

records.english: Grandma's hearing aid was found under the sofa.
records.zomi: Pi' bil-ngaihna sofa nuai ah kimu hi.

records.english: We moved Dad's bed downstairs so that he wouldn't have to climb the stairs.
records.zomi: Kahlei a kah kul loh nadingin Pa' lupna a nuai lam ah i suan hi.

records.english: Taking care of a sick relative can leave you feeling isolated, so it helps to ask friends for support.
records.zomi: Dam lo beh leh phung kem in amah bek om bang a kisak sak thei ahih manin, lawmte huhna ngen a hoih hi.

records.english: We use a blender to make Grandpa's vegetables soft because he has trouble chewing.
records.zomi: Pu in a haizaan haksa ahih manin blender tawh a anteh i nemsak hi.

records.english: The daycare called to say that our son had a slight fever.
records.zomi: I tapa in cisa neu a nei hi, ci-in naupang kepna mun in hong sam hi.

records.english: We take turns staying overnight with Uncle Thang at the hospital.
records.zomi: Zato ah Pu Thang kiangah zan khat ciat i kilaih-in i giak hi.

records.english: The children were put to bed early because they had school trips the next morning.
records.zomi: Zingciang zingsang sang khualzinna a nei uh ahih manin naupangte a tuungin a lupsak uh hi.

records.english: Grandpa likes us to sit with him in the evening, even when he doesn't feel like talking.
records.zomi: Kiho nuam lo ciangin zong, nitakin a kiangah i tut Pu in a deih hi.

records.english: Use the measuring spoon, not a kitchen spoon, when you give the baby her medicine.
records.zomi: Naungek zatui na piak ciangin anbuk sikkeu hi lo-in tehna sikkeu zang in.

records.english: The baby has to be fed again in two hours.
records.zomi: Nai nih khit ciangin naungek an vak kik ding hi.

records.english: Mind the step, Grandpa — it's a bit slippery.
records.zomi: Pu, kahlei pilvang in — a nal deuh hi.

records.english: Our neighbor made her son install handrails in the bathroom for his elderly father.
records.zomi: I inn veng nu in a pa upa adingin a tapa in kisilna inn ah khut tuahna a koihsak hi.

records.english: We're learning sign language to communicate with our deaf daughter.
records.zomi: I tanu bil ngong tawh i kiho theih nadingin khut pau i sin hi.

records.english: Caring for my mother after her stroke changed the way I see old age.
records.zomi: Ka nu a natna nasia khit ciangin ka kem manin upat hun ka et dan a kilai hi.

records.english: My eyes were so puffy this morning that I had to wear sunglasses to work.
records.zomi: Tu zingsangin ka mit a vung mahmah ahih manin nasepna ah mitlang a vom ka bulh hi.

records.english: My tie was crooked, so my wife straightened it before I left.
records.zomi: Ka tie a kawi ahih manin ka pai ma-in ka zi in a tangsak hi.

records.english: Comb your hair before we leave — it's sticking up at the back.
records.zomi: I pai ma-in na sam khui in — a nunglam ah a ding hi.

records.english: Grandpa wakes up before dawn every day to pray and read his Bible.
records.zomi: Pu in ni simin khua a vak ma-in thu ngen-in a Laisiangtho a sim dingin a tho hi.

records.english: You're not allowed to watch cartoons until you're dressed and have eaten breakfast.

records.english: "Where did all this junk come from?" Dad groaned as he opened the attic.

records.english: The closet door wouldn't shut because it was stuffed with old coats.
records.zomi: Puan sil luite a dim ahih manin puan koihna kongkhak a khak thei kei hi.

records.english: Put the toys back in the basket when you're done playing.
records.zomi: Na kimawl zawh ciangin kimawlna vante bawm sungah koih kik in.

records.english: Our basement flooded last spring, and half the stored boxes were ruined.
records.zomi: Spring nung in i inn nuai khan tui a dim a, kikoih bawmte a lang a siat hi.

records.english: Could you hand me that box of hangers?
records.zomi: Tua puan khaina bawm hong pia thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: I labeled every box in the garage so that we can find things quickly.
records.zomi: Vante manlang takin i muh theih nadingin mawtaw inn sung bawm khempeuh ah min ka belh hi.

records.english: How often do you wash the curtains?
records.zomi: Puan khaite bangzah vei na sawp ngei hiam?

records.english: My wife insisted that we clear out the spare room before the baby arrived.
records.zomi: Naungek a tun ma-in khan awng pen siangsak dingin ka zi in a ngen ngiat hi.

records.english: Leave the receipts on my desk, and I'll file them later.
records.zomi: Receipt te ka dawhkan tungah nusia in, a nung ciangin ka koih ding hi.

records.english: Please don't throw anything of mine away without asking me first.
records.zomi: Hong dong masa lo-in ka vante khatpeuh paikhia kei un.

records.english: Once a month, I go through the fridge and get rid of anything that's gone bad.
records.zomi: Kha simin vot bawlna sung ka en a, a siat khatpeuh ka paikhia hi.

records.english: Can we agree to clean the kitchen together every Saturday morning?
records.zomi: Kiginni zingsang simin anbuk siangsak khawm dingin i kituak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Keep the cleaning chemicals in the top cupboard, away from the children.
records.zomi: Siangsakna zatuite naupangte pan gamla takah koihna tung pen ah koih in.

records.english: Is it okay if I donate your old bicycle to the school?
records.zomi: Na siiksakol lui sang tungah ka pia leh a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: We sold the old sofa online and used the money to buy a bookshelf.
records.zomi: Sofa lui online ah i zuak a, tua sum tawh laibu koihna khat i lei hi.

records.english: We found my grandfather's old letters while clearing out the attic.
records.zomi: Inn tung khan i siangsak laitakin ka pu' laikhak luite i mu hi.

records.english: The children were asked to tidy their rooms before their grandparents arrived.
records.zomi: A pu leh a pite uh a tun ma-un naupangte in a khan uh siangsak dingin kingen uh hi.

records.english: Stack the chairs against the wall so we can sweep the hall.
records.zomi: Inn lianpi i phiat theih nadingin tutnate bang kiangah zom in.

records.english: Decluttering my wardrobe made getting dressed in the morning much less stressful.
records.zomi: Ka puan koihna ka siangsak manin zingsangin puan silh a lungkham huai nawn kei hi.

records.english: The shelf collapsed under the weight of all those books.
records.zomi: Laibu tampi' gikna hangin dawh a kiak hi.

records.english: Please, no shoes on the clean floor!
records.zomi: Sual siangtho tungah khedap tawh om kei un!

records.english: I usually bring leftovers from home to save money.
records.zomi: Sum kholh nadingin inn pan an a lai ka tawi ngei hi.

records.english: When does the training session after lunch start?
records.zomi: Sun an khit ciang sinsakna bang ciangin kipan ding hiam?

records.english: The system went down for an hour, and nobody could log in.
records.zomi: System nai khat sung a mang a, kuamah log in thei lo hi.

records.english: The meeting was moved to Thursday because the director was traveling.
records.zomi: Director in khualzin a pai ahih manin kikhopna Laizing ni ah kikhin hi.

records.english: I write a to-do list every evening so that I know where to start the next day.
records.zomi: Zingciang koi pan kipan ding hiam ka theih nadingin nitak simin sep ding list ka gelh hi.

records.english: You could ask to start an hour earlier so you can pick up your kids from school.
records.zomi: Na tate sang pan na la theih nadingin nai khat a masa-in kipan dingin na ngen thei hi.

records.english: We take turns making tea for the team.
records.zomi: Pawl adingin niangtui bawl i kilaih hi.

records.english: The bus was late again, so I missed the start of the meeting.
records.zomi: Bus a zekai kik ahih manin kikhopna kipatna ka mansuah hi.

records.english: The whole office was evacuated because of a fire alarm, which turned out to be a false alarm.
records.zomi: Mei kang alarm hangin office bup kikhia sak a, a dik lo alarm hi tawp hi.

records.english: Commuting by bike saves me money and keeps me fit.
records.zomi: Siiksakol tawh nasepna ah ka pai manin sum ka kholh a, ka dam hi.

records.english: Are you working late again tonight?
records.zomi: Tu zanin zekai-in na sem kik ding hiam?

records.english: I'm a teacher, so most of my day is spent in a classroom with thirty teenagers.
records.zomi: Sia ka hih manin ka ni a tam zaw khangno sawmthum tawh class sungah ka zang hi.

records.english: Is the office open on public holidays?
records.zomi: Mipi khawl ni ciangin office kihong hiam?

records.english: Did the shipment arrive this morning?
records.zomi: Tu zingsangin vante a tung hiam?

records.english: Not yet, but the driver called to say he might be there by noon.
records.zomi: Tung nai lo hi, ahi zongin mawngtu in sun laitak ciangin a tung kha ding hi, ci-in a sam hi.

records.english: Do you take a lunch break, or do you eat at your desk?
records.zomi: Sun an khawlna na nei hiam, ahih kei leh na dawhkan ah na ne hiam?

records.english: Working night shifts has completely changed my sleep schedule.
records.zomi: Zan nasep in ka ihmut hun a laih bup hi.

records.english: The cashier's till didn't balance at the end of the day, so she had to count everything twice.
records.zomi: Ni bei ciangin sum ngah leh sum kemna a kituak kei ahih manin, sum ngah nu in nihvei a sim kik hi.

records.english: What time does your shift start tomorrow?
records.zomi: Zingciang na nasep nai bangzah ciangin kipan ding hiam?

records.english: At seven, so I'll have to leave the house by six-thirty.
records.zomi: Nai sagih ciangin, tua ahih manin nai guk leh a lang ciangin inn pan ka pai ding hi.

records.english: How long is your commute?
records.zomi: Na nasepna pai bangzah sawt hiam?

records.english: About forty minutes by train, which gives me time to read.
records.zomi: Meileng tawh minit sawmli bang, tua in lai sim hun hong pia hi.

records.english: Is it possible to work from home on Fridays?
records.zomi: Laithai ni ciangin inn pan sep theih hiam?

records.english: How do you stay focused when the office is so noisy?
records.zomi: Office a ging buai lua ciangin bangci na lungsim na koih hiam?

records.english: I put on headphones and play quiet music.
records.zomi: Headphone ka bulh a, la nem ka ngai hi.

records.english: The new manager has asked everyone to arrive ten minutes early for a daily briefing.
records.zomi: Ukpa thak in ni simin thu theihna adingin minit sawm a masa-in tun dingin mi khempeuh a ngen hi.

records.english: Overtime is paid at a higher rate in our company.
records.zomi: I company ah hun behlap sepna man a sang zaw hi.

records.english: Could you cover my shift on Saturday so I can go to my daughter's recital?
records.zomi: Ka tanu' la sakna ah ka pai theih nadingin Kiginni ciangin ka nasep na sem sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: She makes a cup of tea, opens her laptop, and starts answering messages.
records.zomi: Niangtui khuat khat a bawl a, a laptop a hon a, thute a dawng pan hi.

records.english: My coworker spilled coffee all over my keyboard this morning.
records.zomi: Tu zingsangin ka nasep pih in ka keyboard tungah kawfi a buak hi.

records.english: What time is the client supposed to arrive?
records.zomi: Nai bangzah ciangin mikhual a tung ding hiam?

records.english: My shift ended at midnight, but I didn't get home until one because the last train was canceled.
records.zomi: Ka nasep zan laitak ciangin a bei a, ahi zongin meileng nunung pen kiphiat ahih manin nai khat ciang bekin inn ka tung hi.

records.english: I spent the entire morning in back-to-back meetings and barely got any real work done.
records.zomi: Zingsang bup kikhopna khat khit khat ah ka om a, nasep taktak tawm mahmah ka sem hi.

records.english: Should I call the customer back now or wait until after lunch?
records.zomi: Tu-in mikhual ka sam kik ding hiam, sun an khit dong ka ngak ding hiam?

records.english: Let me know if you need anything before I leave for the day.
records.zomi: Tuni ka pai ma-in bangmah na kisap leh hong theisak in.

records.english: Before leaving, I always tidy my desk and shut down my computer.
records.zomi: Ka pai ma-in ka dawhkan ka siangsak a, ka computer ka phel tawntung hi.

records.english: The shop opens at nine, but staff need to arrive half an hour earlier to get everything ready.
records.zomi: Dawl nai kua ciangin kihong hi, ahi zongin nasemte in na khempeuh a kigingsak nadingun nai lang a masa-in a tung ding uh hi.

records.english: After eight hours on my feet, all I want is a hot shower and a quiet evening.
records.zomi: Nai giat sung ka din khit ciangin, tui lum kisil leh nitak dai bek ka deih hi.

records.english: Our team meets for fifteen minutes every morning to plan the day.
records.zomi: I pawl in ni sung sep ding ngaihsun dingin zingsang simin minit sawm leh nga i kikhawm hi.

records.english: Hold on, I'm just finishing an email.
records.zomi: Ngak in, email khat ka zo dek hi.

records.english: What do you usually do after work?
records.zomi: Nasep khit ciangin bang na sem ngei hiam?

records.english: I'll probably be late tonight, so don't wait for me to start dinner.
records.zomi: Tu zanin ka zekai kha ding ahih manin nitak an ne dingin hong ngak kei un.

records.english: We might finish early today if the delivery arrives on time.
records.zomi: Vante hun takah a tun leh tuni i zo masa kha ding hi.

records.english: Our shop closes early on Sundays, so we finish by three.
records.zomi: I dawl Nipini ciangin a tuungin a kikhak ahih manin nai thum ciangin i zo hi.

records.english: I check my email first thing every morning, before anything else.
records.zomi: Zingsang simin bangmah ka sep ma-in ka email ka en masa hi.

records.english: Please send me the meeting notes when you have a moment.
records.zomi: Hun na neih ciangin kikhopna thu kigelhte hong khak in.

records.english: The farmers in our village are in the fields before sunrise and rarely stop before dark.
records.zomi: I khua a lo neite ni a suah ma-in lo ah a om uh a, khua a mial ma-in a khawl ngei kei uh hi.

records.english: It might rain later, so take an umbrella to work.
records.zomi: A nung ciangin guah a zuk kha ding ahih manin nasepna ah kawl lukhu tawi in.

records.english: The coffee machine broke down, and the whole office was grumpy all morning.
records.zomi: Kawfi machine a siat a, office bup zingsang bup a lungkia uh hi.

records.english: Working from home, I sometimes go the whole day without speaking to anyone.
records.zomi: Inn pan ka sep ciangin ni bup kuamah tawh kiho lo-in ka om ngei hi.

records.english: "Can you have the report ready by noon?" my manager asked as soon as I walked in.
records.zomi: “Sun laitak ciangin report na kigingsak thei ding hiam?” ci-in ka lut pakin ka ukpa in hong dong hi.

records.english: Halfway through the afternoon, I always need a short walk to clear my head.
records.zomi: Sun laitak khit ciangin ka lungsim a siangtho nadingin vak tomno ka kisam tawntung hi.

records.english: I clock in at eight and clock out at five, Monday through Friday.
records.zomi: Pizing ni pan Laithai ni dong nai giat ciangin ka kipan a nai nga ciangin ka zo hi.

records.english: The printer jammed just as I needed to print the contract.
records.zomi: Contract ka print ding laitak takin printer a buai hi.

records.english: My job involves a lot of driving between different construction sites.
records.zomi: Ka nasep in inn lamna mun tuamtuam kikal ah mawtaw mawng tampi a kisam hi.

records.english: I forgot my ID badge, so the guard had to let me in.
records.zomi: Ka ID badge ka mangngilh ahih manin ngaktu in hong lut sak hi.

records.english: By ten o'clock, I'd already answered thirty emails and joined two video calls.
records.zomi: Nai sawm ciangin email sawmthum ka dawng khin a, video call nih ah ka kihel khin hi.

records.english: Mondays are always the busiest day at the clinic.
records.zomi: Clinic ah Pizing ni pen a buai pen ni ahi tawntung hi.

records.english: My sister is a nurse, and she often works twelve-hour shifts without a proper break.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu nurse ahi a, khawlna hoih om lo-in nai sawm leh nih sung a sem ngei hi.

records.english: My boss told me, "Take the rest of the day off — you've earned it."
records.zomi: Ka ukpa in, “Ni lai khawl in — na kilawm hi,” hong ci hi.

records.english: Who's going to tuck me in tonight, you or Daddy?
records.zomi: Tu zanin kua in hong lupsak ding hiam, nang hiam Pa hiam?

records.english: Sleeping with the window open keeps the room nice and cool.
records.zomi: Tawhkhawng kihong tawh ihmut in khan a vot nuam sak hi.

records.english: Kiss Grandma good night before you go upstairs.
records.zomi: A tung lam na kah ma-in Pi “Zanpha” ci-in tawp in.

records.english: We say a short prayer together before the kids go to sleep.
records.zomi: Naupangte a ihmut ma-un thungetna tomno i nei khawm hi.

records.english: We read a chapter of a long book together each night, and the kids can't wait to find out what happens next.
records.zomi: Zan simin laibu sau khat sung pan cangpi khat i sim khawm a, naupangte in bang a piang ding hiam theih a lamen mahmah uh hi.

records.english: She fell asleep halfway through the story, so I quietly closed the book.
records.zomi: Tangthu a laitak ah a ihmu ahih manin dai takin laibu ka khak hi.

records.english: My daughter likes me to stay with her until she falls asleep.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in a ihmut dong a kiangah ka om ding a deih hi.

records.english: Can I have a glass of water before bed?
records.zomi: Ka lup ma-in tui khuat khat ka dawn thei ding hiam?

records.english: Mom checks that the doors are locked before she goes to bed.
records.zomi: Nu in a lup ma-in kongkhakte a kikalh hiam a en hi.

records.english: It's possible the fever will come back during the night, so keep the medicine nearby.
records.zomi: Zanin cisa a hong pai kik kha ding ahih manin zatui kiang ah koih in.

records.english: The blankets kept slipping off the bed, so the children woke up cold.
records.zomi: Puante lupna pan a kia tawntung ahih manin naupangte vot tawh a khanglo uh hi.

records.english: My husband sets out the children's school clothes every night so that the morning goes smoothly.
records.zomi: Zingsang hun a hoih nadingin ka pasal in zan simin naupangte' sang puan a koih sak hi.

records.english: He snores so loudly that I sometimes sleep on the sofa.
records.zomi: Amah a ngawk ging nasia mahmah ahih manin sofa tungah ka ihmu ngei hi.

records.english: By the time the last child was asleep, I was too tired to do anything but go to bed myself.
records.zomi: Naupang nunung pen a ihmut ciangin, keimah mah lup bek lo bangmah sem thei lo-in ka gim hi.

records.english: Did you remember to set your alarm?
records.zomi: Na alarm koih ding na phawk hiam?

records.english: Can I sleep in your bed tonight because I'm scared of the thunder?
records.zomi: Van-ging ka lau ahih manin tu zanin na lupna ah ka ihmu thei ding hiam?

records.english: Has anyone seen the reading glasses I left on the nightstand?
records.zomi: Lupna kiang dawhkan tungah ka koih laibu simna mitlimlang kua in a mu hiam?

records.english: The bedroom was so hot that nobody could sleep.
records.zomi: Lupna khan a sa lua ahih manin kuamah ihmu thei lo hi.

records.english: After reading the same bedtime story five nights in a row, I know every word by heart.
records.zomi: Zan nga sung lup ma-a tangthu khat mah ka sim khit ciangin a kammal khempeuh ka phawk khin hi.

records.english: Somebody switched off the fan in the night, and I woke up sweating.
records.zomi: Kuamah in zanin fan a phel a, guai luang-in ka khanglo hi.

records.english: Did you hear something downstairs?
records.zomi: A nuai lam ah bangmah na za hiam?

records.english: It's probably just the cat knocking something over.
records.zomi: Zawhngeu in bangmah a kiaksak bek kha ding hi.

records.english: We usually go to bed around ten, unless there's a good movie on.
records.zomi: Movie hoih a om kei leh nai sawm bang ciangin i lum ngei hi.

records.english: Good night, everyone — see you in the morning.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh zanpha — zingsang ciangin kimu kik ni.

records.english: Perhaps a cup of warm milk will help you fall asleep.
records.zomi: Nawi lum khuat khat in na ihmut hong huh kha ding hi.

records.english: Turn off the TV; it's way past your bedtime.
records.zomi: TV phel in; na lup hun a pelh mahmah khin hi.

records.english: I might read for a while, since I'm not sleepy yet.
records.zomi: Ka ihmu ngai nai kei ahih manin tawmno ka sim kha ding hi.

records.english: Hearing the rain on the roof always helps me fall asleep.
records.zomi: Inn tungah guah zuk ging in ka ihmut a huh tawntung hi.

records.english: Could you leave the hall light on, please?
records.zomi: Inn sung lampi meivak phel lo-in nusia thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Would you like me to rub your back until you fall asleep?
records.zomi: Na ihmut dong na nungzang ka nul sak ding na deih hiam?

records.english: My mother-in-law knits by the lamp for an hour before she goes to sleep.
records.zomi: Ka sungnu in a ihmut ma-in meivak kiangah nai khat sung a khui hi.

records.english: I pack tomorrow's lunch boxes for the kids before I go to bed.
records.zomi: Ka lup ma-in naupangte' zingciang sun an bawm ka koih sak hi.

records.english: Grandma used to sing to us every night until we fell asleep.
records.zomi: Ka pi in zan simin i ihmut dong la hong sak ngei hi.

records.english: Which story do you want tonight, the dragon one or the one about the lost puppy?
records.zomi: Tu zanin tangthu bang na deih hiam, dragon tangthu hiam uino mangthang tangthu hiam?

records.english: Close the curtains so the streetlight doesn't shine in your eyes.
records.zomi: Lampi meivak in na mit a tan loh nadingin puan khaite khak in.

records.english: Please keep your voices down; the baby is finally asleep.
records.zomi: Dai takin gen un; naungek a ihmu tawp hi.

records.english: That bedtime story was so funny that the children laughed instead of sleeping.
records.zomi: Lup ma-a tangthu a nuihzak mahmah ahih manin naupangte ihmu lo-in a nui uh hi.

records.english: "Sweet dreams," Dad whispered as he closed the door.
records.zomi: “Mang nuam ngah in,” ci-in Pa in kongkhak a khak laitakin a gen ciauciau hi.

records.english: Will you leave the door open a little?
records.zomi: Kongkhak tawmno kihong-in na nusia ding hiam?

records.english: The baby was rocked to sleep by her grandfather.
records.zomi: Naungek a pu in a hawng-in a ihmusak hi.

records.english: Could you fill my hot-water bottle before you go to bed?
records.zomi: Na lup ma-in ka tui lum um hong dimsak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: The little ones were already asleep by the time we got home from the wedding.
records.zomi: Kiteenna pan inn i tun ciangin naupang neute a ihmu khin uh hi.

records.english: Why do you always get hungry right before bed?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na lup ma-in na gil a kial tawntung hiam?

records.english: The house gets very quiet once everyone has gone to bed.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh a lup khit ciangin inn a dai mahmah hi.

records.english: I always write tomorrow's tasks on a sticky note so that I don't lie awake worrying about them.
records.zomi: Lungkham-in ka ihmut loh nadingin zingciang sep dingte lai neu tungah ka gelh tawntung hi.

records.english: I couldn't sleep because the neighbors' dog barked all night.
records.zomi: Inn veng' ui zan bup a ham ahih manin ka ihmu thei kei hi.

records.english: Are you still awake?
records.zomi: Na khanglo lai hiam?

records.english: Lights out in ten minutes, everyone!
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, minit sawm khit ciangin meivak phel ding hi!

records.english: A loud thunderstorm woke the whole family around two in the morning.
records.zomi: Zingsang nai nih bang ciangin van-ging nasia in innkuan bup a phawng hi.

records.english: "Just five more minutes," my son begged when I turned off the light.
records.zomi: Meivak ka phel ciangin, “Minit nga bek,” ci-in ka tapa in a ngen hi.

records.english: Our son woke up crying from a bad dream, so I sat with him for a while.
records.zomi: I tapa mang sia hangin kap-in a khanglo ahih manin a kiangah tawmno ka tu hi.

records.english: Since the twins started sharing a room, bedtime has become much noisier.
records.zomi: Apengte khan khat mah ah a lup pan nungun lup hun a ging buai zaw mahmah hi.

records.english: What do you usually do to relax before going to sleep?
records.zomi: Na ihmut ma-in na lungsim nopsak nadingin bang na sem ngei hiam?

records.english: I take a warm shower and write a few lines in my journal.
records.zomi: Tui lum tawh ka kisil a, ka nitak lai bu ah gual tawmno ka gelh hi.

records.english: The power went out just as I was getting into bed.
records.zomi: Lupna ka luut laitak takin meivak a mang hi.

records.english: Go back to sleep, sweetheart — it's still the middle of the night.
records.zomi: Ka it, ihmu kik in — zan laitak a hi lai hi.

records.english: Our youngest gets cranky and finds it harder to fall asleep when she's overtired.
records.zomi: I ta neu pen a gim lua ciangin a lungkia a, a ihmut a haksa zaw hi.

records.english: Reading in bed always makes my eyes heavy within a few pages.
records.zomi: Lupna tungah lai ka sim ciangin laimai tawmno sungin ka mit a gik tawntung hi.

records.english: Brush your teeth and put on your pajamas, and then I'll read to you.
records.zomi: Na ha nawt inla na zan puan silh in, tua khit ciangin kong sim sak ding hi.

records.english: My grandfather tells the children stories from his childhood in the village every night.
records.zomi: Ka pu in zan simin naupangte a khua a naupan lai tangthute a gen hi.

records.english: The shop down the street was closed for a holiday, so we drove to the next town.
records.zomi: Lampi tawp lam dawl khawlna ni ahih manin kikhak a, khua zom ah mawtaw tawh i pai hi.

records.english: Is there a discount if I buy two?
records.zomi: Nih ka lei leh man a kiam hiam?

records.english: We go grocery shopping every Saturday morning before the crowds arrive.
records.zomi: Mipi a tam ma-in Kiginni zingsang simin an lei dingin i pai hi.

records.english: Could you pick up some bread for me on your way home?
records.zomi: Inn na ciah ciangin moh tawmno hong lei sak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Please don't squeeze the peaches.
records.zomi: Peach te nen kei in.

records.english: At our night market, prices usually drop near closing time.
records.zomi: I zan zuakna mun ah khak hun a naih ciangin a man a kiam ngei hi.

records.english: We could order groceries online and have them delivered this week.
records.zomi: Tu kal sungin online ah an order-in i inn ah hong tun sak thei hi.

records.english: The store was so crowded that we gave up and left without buying anything.
records.zomi: Dawl sungah mi a tam lua ahih manin bangmah lei lo-in i ciah kik hi.

records.english: Is this fish fresh today?
records.zomi: Hih nga tuni a thak hi hiam?

records.english: How much did you spend on groceries this week?
records.zomi: Tu kal an leina ah sum bangzah na zang hiam?

records.english: Bring the reusable bags; the store charges for plastic ones now.
records.zomi: Ip zat kikte tawi un; tu-in dawl in plastic ip adingin man a la hi.

records.english: Maybe the corner shop is still open; it doesn't close until ten.

records.english: Our fridge broke down, and all the meat we had just bought went bad.

records.english: Somebody had left an open bottle of juice on the shelf, and it leaked onto the cereal boxes.

records.english: I'll buy the snacks for the picnic if you bring the drinks.

records.english: First I bought the vegetables, then I went to the butcher, and finally I stopped at the bakery.

records.english: Can I pay by card, or is it cash only?

records.english: Two kilos of potatoes and half a kilo of garlic, please.

records.english: My grocery bag split open, and oranges rolled all over the parking lot.

records.english: A few of the items on my list were out of stock, so I had to change my plans for dinner.

records.english: Fresh fruit is much cheaper when it's in season.

records.english: The bananas were bruised, so I asked for a different bunch.

records.english: The cashier gave me the wrong change, so I had to go back to the counter.

records.english: Grocery shopping with three hungry children is a real test of patience.

records.english: I forgot my wallet at home, so the shopkeeper let me pay the next day.

records.english: I really do want to cook more at home, so I'm trying to buy fewer ready-made meals.

records.english: Where do you usually buy your meat?

records.english: From the butcher near the bus station — his prices are fair, and he knows us well.

records.english: My aunt asked the jeweler how much he would pay for her old gold ring.
records.zomi: Ka ni in kham bawlpa kiangah a kham zungbuh lui bangzah in a lei ding hiam a dong hi.

records.english: Excuse me, sir — how much are the tickets for the evening show?
records.zomi: Hong maisak in, Pu — nitak lak lakna ticket bangzah hiam?

records.english: Which is cheaper, the large bottle or two small ones?

records.english: I can't afford it right now, but maybe next month.

records.english: Before buying a used car, I always compare prices online for a week or two.
records.zomi: Mawtaw kizangsa ka lei ma-in kal khat nih sung online ah a man ka kiteh tawntung hi.

records.english: Would you take less if I paid in cash today?
records.zomi: Tuni sum taktak tawh ka pia leh a man na kiamsak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Prices are marked on the shelf below each product.
records.zomi: Vante khat ciat nuai dawh tungah a man kigelh hi.

records.english: That's a little more than I wanted to spend.
records.zomi: Tua pen ka zat nop sangin tawm khat a tam zaw hi.

records.english: Sorry, I misread the price and thought it said fifteen, not fifty.
records.zomi: Hong maisak in, a man ka sim khial a, sawm leh nga ka ci a, sawmnga a hi hi.

records.english: Kids, look at the prices before you ask me to buy anything.
records.zomi: Naupangte, bangmah hong leisak dingin na ngen ma-un a man en un.

records.english: Is that the final price, or is there room to negotiate?
records.zomi: Tua pen a man nunung hi hiam, kikup theih lai hiam?

records.english: Do you have anything a little less expensive?
records.zomi: A man neu zaw deuh na nei hiam?

records.english: Could you tell me whether this price includes tax?
records.zomi: Hih man in siah a hel hiam hong gen thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: It might be cheaper to buy the whole set instead of individual pieces.
records.zomi: A tuamtuam lei sangin a bup lei a man neu zaw kha ding hi.

records.zomi: Hih puan sil ka lei man bangzah neu hiam na theih ngei kei ding hi!

records.english: What's the price difference between the two models?
records.zomi: Model nihte' man kibat lohna bangzah hiam?

records.zomi: A man hong gelh sak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.zomi: Pi' letsong adingin na khempeuh uh bangzah zang nuam na hi uh hiam?

records.english: Agree on the fare before you get into the taxi so there are no surprises later.
records.zomi: A nung ciangin lamdang a om loh nadingin taxi na tuan ma-in a man kituak masa un.

records.english: Wow, everything here is so expensive!
records.zomi: Wow, hih munah na khempeuh a man tam mahmah hi!

records.english: What does a haircut cost at the place near your office?
records.zomi: Na office kiang mun ah sam met man bangzah hiam?

records.english: Are tickets cheaper for children under twelve?
records.zomi: Kum sawm leh nih nuai naupangte adingin ticket a man neu zaw hiam?

records.english: Is there any chance you could lower the price a bit?
records.zomi: A man tawmno na kiamsak thei kha ding hiam?

records.english: How much does this jacket cost?
records.zomi: Hih puan sil bangzah hiam?

records.english: It's forty dollars, but it's on sale for thirty this week.

records.english: Would you check the price of this rice for me, since it doesn't have a label?

records.english: What are you asking for the old sewing machine?
records.zomi: Puan khuina machine lui bangzah in na zuak ding hiam?

records.english: Asking the price before ordering saved us from a very expensive surprise at the restaurant.
records.zomi: An order ma-in a man i dot manin ansai ah lamdang man tam mahmah pan i kikholh hi.

records.english: Can you hold this item for me until Friday while I save up?
records.zomi: Sum ka khol laitakin Laithai ni dong hih vante hong kem sak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: What's the charge for repairing a cracked screen?
records.zomi: Screen kitan phuahna man bangzah hiam?

records.english: My grandfather can't believe how much bread costs these days.
records.zomi: Tu hun moh man bangzah tam hiam ka pu in a um zo kei hi.

records.english: Food at the airport costs so much more that we bought snacks before we left.
records.zomi: Vanlengtual ah an man a tam zaw mahmah ahih manin i pai ma-in nek ding neute i lei hi.

records.english: What's the price of a return ticket to the coast?

records.english: To be honest, I'm not sure it's worth the price.
records.zomi: Ka gen taktak leh, a man tawh a kituak hiam ka thei ciang kei hi.

records.english: Would you mind finding out how much the repairs would cost before we decide?

records.english: What's today's price for a kilo of pork?
records.zomi: Tuni vok sa kilo khat bangzah hiam?

records.english: Once I heard the price, I put the vase back on the shelf very carefully.

records.english: How much is it altogether?

records.zomi: Hong maisak in, na sanggam nu in a kiteenna puan bangzah in a lei hiam?

records.english: The shoes I liked were sold out in my size, which was probably lucky for my wallet.

records.english: The seller laughed and said it wasn't for sale at any price.
records.zomi: Zuakpa in a nui a, bangzah man zongin zuak lo hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Are prices lower at the end of the season?
records.zomi: Hun bei ciangin a man a kiam hiam?

records.english: Here they usually are, because most shops hold big sales after the holidays.

records.english: What would you charge to have these trousers shortened?

records.english: I asked three different shops before I found a fair price for the bicycle.
records.zomi: Siiksakol man dik ka muh ma-in dawl thum ka dong hi.

records.english: Does the price include delivery?
records.zomi: A man in hong tun sakna a hel hiam?

records.english: Delivery is free if you spend more than fifty dollars.

records.english: Excuse me, is this price per piece or for the whole bag?
records.zomi: Hong maisak in, hih man pen khat ciat man hi hiam, ip bup man hi hiam?

records.english: Our neighbor bought a television for half price because the box was damaged.
records.zomi: A bawm a siat ahih manin i inn veng in television man lang tawh a lei hi.

records.zomi: Hih haigahte kha bei sangin a man nih a tam zaw hi.

records.zomi: Na phone plan man neu pen bang hiam hong gen thei ding na hi hiam?
