records.zomi: A dum pen ka deih taktak hi, ahi zongin tua man tawh hi lo hi.

records.english: Do you know roughly how much a plumber charges per hour around here?
records.zomi: Hih kiim ah tui pipe phuahtu in nai khat bangzah a la hiam na thei hiam?

records.english: I'd like to know the price before you start the work.
records.zomi: Nasep na kipat ma-in a man ka theih nuam hi.

records.english: He paid the deposit for us so that we could keep the apartment.
records.zomi: Inn i kem theih nadingin amah in i adingin sum masa a pia hi.

records.english: We might have to pay extra if we stay past checkout time.

records.english: The machine swallowed my card, and I had to go into the bank to get it back.

records.english: Tap your card on the reader when the light turns green.
records.zomi: Meivak a eng ciangin na card reader tungah koih in.

records.english: Everyone, please have your exact fare ready before you board the bus.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, bus na tuan ma-un na man dik uh kigingsak un.

records.english: We could split the bill evenly, or each pay for what we ordered.
records.zomi: Man i kikhen kibang thei hi, ahih kei leh i order khat ciat i pia ciat thei hi.

records.english: My grandfather still writes checks to pay his electricity bill.

records.english: The vending machine took my money but didn't give me a drink.
records.zomi: Vending machine in ka sum a la a, ahi zongin dawn ding hong pia kei hi.

records.zomi: Hih sawmnih — a kiapte la in.

records.english: I really do prefer paying in cash, because it helps me keep track of my spending.

records.english: We paid the plumber in cash, and he wrote us a receipt by hand.

records.english: Your total comes to twelve fifty.

records.english: I always ask for a receipt, even for small purchases.

records.english: Which bus goes to the city hospital?

records.english: How far is the next town?

records.english: An old man walked with us to the corner to make sure we didn't get lost again.

records.english: My phone battery died, so I had to ask strangers for directions.

records.english: We got lost because the street signs had been removed for repairs.

records.english: Take the second exit at the roundabout and follow the signs for the airport.

records.english: Turn around — you've gone past it.

records.english: Is there a quicker way to get there?

records.english: How long does it take to get to the beach on foot?

records.english: The road had been blocked by a fallen tree, so we turned back.

records.english: I always leave home early to avoid the rush-hour traffic.

records.english: Our neighbor taught me to drive in an empty parking lot on Sunday mornings.

records.english: Many roads in our district are unpaved, so drivers need to be careful in the rainy season.

records.english: Which lane do I need to be in to turn left?

records.english: I really do prefer driving at night, when the roads are empty.
records.zomi: Lampi a awng zan ciangin mawng ka deih zaw taktak hi.

records.english: The motorbike was badly damaged, but luckily the rider wasn't hurt.

records.english: My windshield was cracked by a stone thrown up from the truck in front.

records.english: After circling the stadium for an hour, we finally squeezed into a parking space two streets away.

records.english: Fill up the tank before we leave the city; there aren't many gas stations in the mountains.

records.english: I got a speeding ticket on my way to work yesterday.

records.english: I do want to learn to drive, but lessons are expensive.

records.english: When did you get your driver's license?

records.english: The road was closed for repairs, so we took a detour through the village.

records.english: How long have you been driving?
records.zomi: Bangzah sawt mawtaw na mawng khin hiam?

records.english: Watch out for children crossing near the school.
records.zomi: Sang kiang ah a kantan naupangte pilvang in.

records.english: Kids, keep your hands inside the windows while I'm driving.

records.english: Have you ever driven on the left side of the road?
records.zomi: Lampi veilam ah mawtaw na mawng ngei hiam?

records.english: Is it legal to park here overnight?
records.zomi: Hih munah zan bup mawtaw koih thukham tawh kituak hiam?

records.english: We had the brakes checked before the long trip.
records.zomi: Khualzinna sau ma-in brake te i en sak hi.

records.english: In our family, nobody drives after drinking, not even one glass.

records.english: Take the highway — it's faster at this time of day.

records.english: How often should I get the oil changed?

records.english: Every five thousand kilometers or so, depending on the car.

records.english: The road signs were covered with mud, so we missed our exit.

records.english: Slow down — there's a school just ahead.

records.english: Somebody scratched my car while it was parked outside the market.

records.english: Shall I drive for a while so you can rest?
records.zomi: Na tawlnga theih nadingin tawmno ka mawng ding hiam?

records.english: The car in front stopped suddenly, and I almost hit it.
records.zomi: Mai lam mawtaw thakhat a khawl a, ka sutdek hi.

records.english: Could you drop me off at the station on your way to work?
records.zomi: Na nasepna na pai laitakin station ah hong khiasak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: We were stuck in a traffic jam for two hours on the way back from the coast.

records.english: She drives an old pickup truck that belonged to her grandfather.

records.english: The police stopped us to check our license and registration.
records.zomi: I phalna lai leh mawtaw lai en dingin police in hong khawlsak uh hi.

records.english: The new bypass has made driving through town much quicker.

records.english: Everyone, please fasten your seatbelts before we leave.

records.english: My brother passed his driving test on the third try.

records.english: We drove all night to reach my grandmother's village before the funeral.

records.english: Can I park in front of your garage for a few minutes?

records.english: Pull over here; I'll walk the rest of the way.
records.zomi: Hih munah khawl in; a lai ka kaai ding hi.

records.english: The engine started making a strange noise, so I pulled into the nearest garage.
records.zomi: Mawtaw in ging lamdang a nei pan ahih manin mawtaw phuahna naih pen ah ka lut hi.

records.english: Thousands of commuters were affected when the subway workers went on strike.
records.zomi: Subway nasemte a nasep uh a khawl ciangin nasepna pai mi tul tampi a buai uh hi.

records.english: Excuse me, does this train go through the city center?

records.english: I bought a weekly pass to save money on my commute.

records.english: We bought snacks at the station and settled in for the long journey.

records.english: Public transport here is reliable, but it stops running quite early at night.

records.english: Could you tell me when we reach my stop?

records.english: Everyone, please move to the back of the bus so that more people can get on.

records.english: Is this seat taken?

records.english: How often do the buses run on Sundays?

records.english: I'll text you when I get on the bus.

records.english: Traveling by bus is slower, but it's much cheaper than flying.

records.english: Is there a direct bus, or do I have to change?

records.zomi: Lampi map pen kongkhak khat ciat kiangah kibelh hi.

records.english: Does this bus stop at the central market?

records.english: The trains run every ten minutes during rush hour.

records.english: I fell asleep on the train and missed my station.

records.english: Riding the metro every day has made me much better at reading maps.

records.english: Where do I buy a ticket for the tram?

records.english: You can pay on board with cash or a card.

records.english: How much is a one-way ticket to the airport?

records.english: My umbrella was crushed in the crowd at the station.

records.english: Could you press the button for the next stop, please?

records.english: The doors closed before I could get off, so I had to ride to the next station.

records.english: The city had the old buses replaced with electric ones last year.

records.english: Stamp your ticket in the machine before you board.

records.english: The fares went up again this year, and many students are struggling to pay.

records.english: We had to stand all the way because there wasn't a single empty seat.

records.english: Mind the gap between the train and the platform.

records.english: Grandma takes the bus into town every Friday to visit her sister.

records.english: Which platform does the train to the coast leave from?

records.english: The ferry was canceled because of strong winds.
records.zomi: Huih nasia hangin tembaw khuang a kiphiat hi.

records.english: The station was evacuated after someone reported a suspicious bag.

records.english: Ever since the new railway opened, our town has been much easier to reach.

records.english: I usually read or listen to podcasts during my commute.

records.english: Why is the train stopping here?

records.english: I really do miss the old trams that used to run along the river.
records.zomi: Lui gei a pai ngei tram luite ka ngaih taktak hi.

records.english: Which part of the city are you staying in?
records.zomi: Khuapi lam bang ah na om hiam?

records.english: The museum was closed for renovation, which was a big disappointment.
records.zomi: Museum phuahna adingin kikhak ahih manin i lungkia mahmah hi.

records.english: All of you need to be back at the bus by six, or we'll leave without you.
records.zomi: Na khempeuh nai guk ciangin bus ah na ciah kik ding uh hi, ahih kei leh note om lo-in i pai ding hi.

records.english: Have you packed everything you need for the trip?
records.zomi: Khualzinna adingin na kisap khempeuh na koih khin hiam?

records.english: You might want to exchange some money before you go.

records.english: The trip to the city takes about six hours on the winding mountain road.

records.english: I'm going to the city to visit my grandfather in the hospital.

records.english: Everyone, remember to keep your passports with you at all times.

records.zomi: Amah bek in sep a deih zaw a, tua pen a nasep pih pawlkhat in a theih haksa uh hi.

records.english: I hate waking up early, but I love watching the sunrise.
records.zomi: Zingsang tuunga khanglo ka huat hi, ahi zongin ni suah et ka it hi.

records.english: She saves her favorite chocolates for when she's had a hard day.
records.zomi: Ni haksa a neih ciangin a chocolate deih pente a kem hi.

records.english: Choose whichever one you like; they're all the same price.
records.zomi: Na deih khatpeuh teel in; a man kibang ciat uh hi.

records.english: I chose this job because I like working with my hands.
records.zomi: Ka khut tawh na sep ka deih ahih manin hih nasep ka teel hi.

records.english: Is it okay if I choose the music for the drive?
records.zomi: Mawtaw tuanna adingin la ka teel leh a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: The concert was so loud that I've decided I prefer small, quiet gigs.
records.zomi: La khawmpi a ging lua ahih manin la khawm neu dai ka deih zaw hi, ci-in ka khensat hi.

records.english: I really do love the old songs from my parents' time.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh pa' hun lai la luite ka it taktak hi.

records.english: The old bookshop where I spent my weekends was turned into a café.
records.zomi: Ka kal bei ka zatna laibu dawl lui kawfi dawl ah a kilai hi.

records.english: I'm more of a tea person than a coffee person.
records.zomi: Kawfi sangin niangtui ka deih zaw hi.

records.english: Everyone, raise your hand if you'd rather have the picnic by the lake.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, dil kiang picnic na deih zaw uh leh na khut uh dawh un.

records.english: My brother prefers to study late at night, while I'm at my best early in the morning.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in zan sawt ciangin lai sin a deih zaw a, kei zingsang tuung ah ka hoih pen hi.

records.english: My husband would rather fix things himself than pay someone else.
records.zomi: Ka pasal in mi dang pia sangin amah mah in a phuah ding a deih zaw hi.

records.english: What kind of music do you listen to when you're driving?
records.zomi: Mawtaw na mawng ciangin la bang na ngai hiam?

records.english: Grandpa prefers his old radio to any television.
records.zomi: Pu in television khatpeuh sangin a radio lui a deih zaw hi.

records.english: Do you like living on your own, or do you miss having roommates?
records.zomi: Na bek a teen na deih hiam, inn tenpihte na ngaih hiam?

records.english: Would you prefer a window seat or an aisle seat?
records.zomi: Tawhkhawng kiang tutna na deih zaw hiam, lampi kiang hiam?

records.english: Which do you enjoy more, playing football or watching it?
records.zomi: Football mawl hiam en hiam na deih zaw hiam?

records.english: I didn't care for jazz until a friend took me to a live performance.
records.zomi: Lawm khat in a taktak la sakna ah hong paipih ma-in jazz ka deih kei hi.

records.english: Did your parents ever tell you stories about their childhood?
records.zomi: Na nu leh pa in a naupan lai tangthu hong gen ngei uh hiam?

records.english: When I was twelve, our house was flooded, and we lived with my uncle for six months.
records.zomi: Ka kum sawm leh nih lai-in i inn tui a dim a, kha guk sung ka pa neu tawh i teeng hi.

records.english: We followed the football matches on a small radio when I was a boy.
records.zomi: Ka neu lai-in radio neu khat tungah football kimawlnate i ngai hi.

records.english: My little sister was born on the day we moved into our new house.
records.zomi: Ka nau numei i inn thak ah i pem ni-in a suak hi.

records.english: We wrote letters by hand because there was no phone in our village.
records.zomi: I khua ah phone a om kei ahih manin khut tawh lai i gelh hi.

records.english: How did you end up working as a nurse?
records.zomi: Bangci-in nurse na hong suak hiam?

records.english: I fell in love with the job while volunteering at a clinic during university.
records.zomi: Sangpi ka kah laitakin clinic khat ah thalawp taka ka sep laitakin nasep ka it hi.

records.english: My uncle loves to tell the story of how he caught a huge fish with his bare hands.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in a khut tawh nga lianpi a man thu gen a deih mahmah hi.

records.english: We used to walk two hours to school, carrying our shoes so they wouldn't wear out.
records.zomi: I khedap a mang loh nadingin pua-in sang ah nai nih i kaai ngei hi.

records.english: My hometown has changed so much that I barely recognized it last year.
records.zomi: Ka khua a kilai mahmah ahih manin kum bei-in ka thei kik dek kei hi.

records.english: Did you ever get into trouble at school?
records.zomi: Sang ah thu na tuak ngei hiam?

records.english: Once, for climbing the mango tree behind the classroom.
records.zomi: Khatvei, class nunglam haigah kung ka kah manin.

records.english: Have you ever lived in another country?
records.zomi: Gam dang ah na teeng ngei hiam?

records.english: That trip was the adventure of a lifetime.
records.zomi: Tua khualzinna pen nuntakna sung lamdang pen ahi hi.

records.english: I do want to tell my grandchildren about the war years, but it's still hard for me to talk about them.
records.zomi: Gal hun kumte thu ka tute ka gen nuam taktak hi, ahi zongin a thu gen ka adingin a haksa lai hi.

records.english: I once spent a whole night waiting at a border crossing.
records.zomi: Gam ciang kantanna ah zan bup ka ngak ngei hi.

records.english: My father worked abroad for ten years to pay for our education.
records.zomi: I lai sinna man pia dingin ka pa in kum sawm sung gamdang ah na a sem hi.

records.english: Ask your grandfather about the time he got lost in the forest.
records.zomi: Na pu gammang ah a mang hun thu dong in.

records.english: We recorded Grandma telling her stories so that the children would always have them.
records.zomi: Naupangte in a neih den nadingin Pi' tangthu gen i la hi.

records.english: The hardest part of growing up was saying goodbye to my older brother when he moved away.
records.zomi: Ka khan laitakin a haksa pen ka u pasal a pem ciangin goodbye ci ahi hi.

records.english: I was robbed on my first night in the city, and a stranger lent me money for the bus home.
records.zomi: Khuapi ka tun zan masa pen ah kiguk ka hi a, mikhual khat in inn ciahna bus man hong leitawi sak hi.

records.english: Share one happy memory from your childhood with the group.
records.zomi: Na naupan lai lungdamna phawkna khat pawl kiangah hawm in.

records.english: Learning to read as an adult opened up a whole new world for my aunt.
records.zomi: Upa hun ciangin lai sim sin in ka ni adingin leitung thak khat a hon hi.

records.english: I remember exactly where I was when I heard the good news.
records.zomi: Thu hoih ka zak ciangin koi ah ka om hiam ka phawk tektek hi.

records.english: What's one thing you'd do differently if you could go back?
records.zomi: Na ciah kik thei leh bang na sem tuam ding hiam?

records.english: I'd spend more time with my grandparents while they were still alive.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh ka pi a nungta lai-un amaute tawh hun tam zaw ka zang ding hi.

records.english: Have you ever met anyone famous?
records.zomi: Mi minthang khat na mu ngei hiam?

records.english: The best year of my life was the one I spent teaching in a mountain village.
records.zomi: Ka nuntakna sunga kum hoih pen mual khua khat ah sia ka sep kum ahi hi.

records.english: What was the hardest thing you've ever done?
records.zomi: Na sep ngei lak pan a haksa pen bang hiam?

records.english: Caring for my mother during her last year was the hardest and most meaningful thing I've ever done.
records.zomi: Ka nu' kum nunung sungin amah kem pen ka sep ngei lak pan a haksa pen leh khiatna nei pen ahi hi.

records.english: When I look back, I'm grateful even for the difficult years.
records.zomi: Ka et kik ciangin kum haksate zong ka lungdam hi.

records.english: When the bridge collapsed, we had to cross the river by boat for a whole year.
records.zomi: Lei a puk ciangin kum khat bup lui guunkuang tawh i kantan kul hi.

records.english: We planted a mango tree when my son was born, and now it gives us fruit every year.
records.zomi: Ka tapa a suah ciangin haigah kung khat i suan a, tu-in kum simin a gah hong pia hi.

records.english: My first job was selling newspapers at the bus station.
records.zomi: Ka nasep masa pen bus station ah thuthak lai zuak ahi hi.

records.english: I still remember the smell of my grandmother's kitchen.
records.zomi: Ka pi' anbuk gim ka phawk lai hi.

records.english: Tell me about the first time you left home.
records.zomi: Inn na paisan masak pen thu hong gen in.

records.english: My old camera has photos from every family wedding since I was a teenager.
records.zomi: Ka camera lui in ka khangno lai pan innkuan kiteenna khempeuh limlak a nei hi.

records.english: What did you learn from living abroad?
records.zomi: Gamdang ah teen pan bang na sin hiam?

records.english: That kindness looks a little different in every place, but it's always welcome.
records.zomi: Hehpihna pen mun khat ciat ah a tuam deuh hi, ahi zongin kimuak tawntung hi.

records.english: Losing my job taught me how much my friends really cared about me.
records.zomi: Ka nasep ka mansuah in ka lawmte in hong it taktak dan uh hong hilh hi.

records.english: How old were you when you got your first paid job?
records.zomi: Na nasep man ngah masa pen na ngah ciangin kum bangzah na hi hiam?

records.english: Kids, sit down and I'll tell you how your grandparents met.
records.zomi: Naupangte, tu un, na pu leh na pite bangci kimu uh hiam kong gen ding hi.

records.english: Traveling alone taught me to trust my instincts.
records.zomi: Ka bek khualzin in ka lungsim muan dingin hong hilh hi.

records.english: Getting lost in a foreign city taught me to ask strangers for help.
records.zomi: Gamdang khuapi ah mang in mikhualte kiangah huhna ngen dingin hong hilh hi.

records.english: Our village celebrated for three days when the new road finally reached us.
records.zomi: Lampi thak i khua a tun tawp ciangin ni thum sung i khua poai a bawl hi.

records.english: Experiences like that teach you more than any classroom.
records.zomi: Tua bang theihnate in class khatpeuh sangin tampi zaw hong hilh hi.

records.english: My first winter abroad was so cold that I wore three sweaters at once.
records.zomi: Gamdang ah ka phalbi masa pen a vot lua ahih manin sweater thum khatvei-in ka silh hi.

records.english: Have you ever been on a plane?
records.zomi: Vanleng na tuan ngei hiam?

records.english: Only once, when I flew to my cousin's wedding in the capital.
records.zomi: Khatvei bek, khuapi lian ah ka sanggam' kiteenna ah ka pai ciangin.

records.english: My first attempt at cooking for guests was a complete disaster.
records.zomi: Zinte adingin an huan ka sawm masak pen a siat bup hi.

records.english: Moving to a new country was frightening at first, but it made me stronger.
records.zomi: Gam thak ah pem pen a masa-in lau huai hi, ahi zongin hong hatsak hi.

records.english: I learned to swim in the river near our village.
records.zomi: I khua kiang lui ah tui peek ka sin hi.

records.english: The day my daughter was born changed my whole life.
records.zomi: Ka tanu a suah ni in ka nuntakna bup a laih hi.

records.english: You all need to hear the story of how this church was built.
records.zomi: Na khempeuh in hih biakinn bangci kilam hiam tangthu na zak ding uh hi.

records.english: Have any of you ever seen snow?
records.zomi: Na lak pan kuamah in vuuk na mu ngei hiam?

records.english: What's the most beautiful place you've ever visited?
records.zomi: Na veh ngei mun lak pan a hoih pen koi hiam?

records.english: I'll never forget the kindness of the nurse who looked after me in the hospital.
records.zomi: Zato ah hong ma nurse' hehpihna ka mangngilh ngei kei ding hi.

records.english: I really do miss the long summer evenings at my grandparents' house.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh ka pi' inn ah khuakhal nitak sau te ka ngaih taktak hi.

records.english: I still keep the pocketknife my grandfather gave me before he died.
records.zomi: Ka pu in a sih ma-a hong piak namsau neu ka kem lai hi.

records.english: I grew up on a farm, so I learned to milk cows before I could read.
records.zomi: Lo inn ah ka khan manin lai ka sim thei ma-in bawng nawi ka hai thei hi.

records.english: My husband and I met at church camp when we were sixteen, and we've been together ever since.
records.zomi: Ka pasal leh kei kum sawm leh guk i hih lai-in pawlpi camp ah i kimu a, tua pan kipan i om khawm hi.

records.english: My dad was a soldier, so we moved every two years.
records.zomi: Ka pa galkap a hih manin kum nih simin i pem hi.

records.english: Would you believe I used to be a professional singer before I had children?
records.zomi: Ta ka neih ma-in la sa nasem ka hi ngei hi, na um ding hiam?

records.english: What do you do when you're not at work?
records.zomi: Nasep na sep loh ciangin bang na sem hiam?

records.english: Mostly I'm at home with my twins, who keep me very busy.
records.zomi: A tam zaw inn ah ka apengte tawh ka om a, hong buaisak mahmah uh hi.

records.english: What do your friends call you?
records.zomi: Na lawmte in bang hong ci uh hiam?

records.english: Most people call me Mimi, which is what my little brother called me when he couldn't say my full name.
records.zomi: Mi tampi in Mimi hong ci uh hi, ka nau pasal in ka min bup a gen theih loh lai-in tua bangin hong sam hi.

records.english: How would your kids describe you?
records.zomi: Na tate in bangci-in hong gen ding uh hiam?

records.english: Would you like to see a picture of my grandson?
records.zomi: Ka tu pasal limlak na et nuam hiam?

records.english: Did you know our family has lived in this valley for five generations?
records.zomi: I innkuan in hih guam sungah suan nga sung a teeng khin hi, na thei hiam?

records.english: Could you tell us a little about your children?
records.zomi: Na tate thu tawmno hong gen thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: My older daughter studies medicine, and my younger one wants to be a pilot.
records.zomi: Ka tanu upa in siavuan sinna a sin a, ka tanu neu in vanleng mawngtu a suak nuam hi.

records.english: Are you married?
records.zomi: Na kiteeng khin hiam?

records.english: Yes, for twenty years now, and we have two grown-up sons.
records.zomi: Kiteeng hi, tu-in kum sawmnih a pha khin a, tapa lian nih ka nei uh hi.

records.english: My grandmother always said I could talk before I could walk.
records.zomi: Ka kaai thei ma-in ka gen thei hi, ci-in ka pi in a gen tawntung hi.

records.english: My children are grown, so I finally have time to learn the guitar.
records.zomi: Ka tate a lian khin uh ahih manin guitar sin dingin hun ka nei tawp hi.

records.english: Tell the class one interesting fact about your family.
records.zomi: Na innkuan thu lamdang khat class kiangah gen in.

records.english: I'm told I have my mother's laugh and my father's stubbornness.
records.zomi: Ka nu' nuih dan leh ka pa' lu khauhna ka nei hi, hong ci uh hi.

records.english: I really do love introducing my children to people from different backgrounds.
records.zomi: Ka tate tawh mi tuamtuam tawh kitheisak ka it taktak hi.

records.english: I might be the oldest student in this class, but I'm also the most excited to be here.
records.zomi: Hih class ah sangnaupang upa pen ka hi kha ding hi, ahi zongin hih munah ka om theih ka lungdam pen hi.

records.english: After ten years as a stay-at-home mom, I'm finally going back to work.
records.zomi: Kum sawm sung inn ah nu ka hih khit ciangin nasep ah ka ciah kik tawp hi.

records.english: Do you all mind if I share a little about my family before we start?
records.zomi: I kipat ma-in ka innkuan thu tawmno ka hawm leh na lungkim uh hiam?

records.english: Everyone, I'm Daniel's wife, Grace — thank you for welcoming me to your group.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, kei Daniel' zi Grace ka hi hi — na pawl ah hong muak uh ahih manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: My family calls me the peacemaker because I hate seeing people argue.
records.zomi: Mite a kinial muh ka huat manin ka innkuan in kilemsaktu hong ci uh hi.

records.english: I was born in a small hospital that was later turned into a school.
records.zomi: Nung ciangin sang a suak zato neu khat ah ka suak hi.

records.english: I'm Paul, and the woman waving at us over there is my wife.
records.zomi: Kei Paul ka hi a, tua mun pan hong khut lap numei pen ka zi ahi hi.

records.english: Introduce yourselves to the person next to you and find one thing you have in common.
records.zomi: Na kiang a om mi kiangah kiphawksak unla, na kibat uh na khat zong un.

records.english: My mother taught me to sew, and now I make clothes for my whole family.
records.zomi: Ka nu in puan khui hong hilh a, tu-in ka innkuan bup adingin puan ka bawl hi.

records.english: My husband jokes that he married me for my cooking.
records.zomi: Ka an huan hangin hong teenpih hi, ci-in ka pasal in ciamnuih a gen hi.

records.english: I'm the first person in my family to go to university, which makes my parents very proud.
records.zomi: Ka innkuan ah sangpi kah masa pen ka hih manin ka nu leh pa a kisaktheih mahmah uh hi.

records.english: Hi, I'm Ruth — a mother of three and a part-time baker.
records.zomi: Hello, kei Ruth ka hi — ta thum nu leh nai tawm moh bawl nasem.

records.english: I was adopted as a baby, and I've always felt lucky to have found my family.
records.zomi: Naungek lai-in hong kila a, ka innkuan ka muh theih vangphatna ka kisa tawntung hi.

records.english: Do you know the little tailoring shop in the market that my husband and I run?
records.zomi: Ka pasal leh kei i sem zuakna mun a puan khui dawl neu na thei hiam?

records.english: Let me introduce myself properly: I'm Esther, and I've just moved into the flat upstairs with my two kids.
records.zomi: Hoih takin kiphawksak ning: kei Esther ka hi a, ka ta nih tawh a tung lam inn ah ka hong pem thak hi.

records.english: Our family is small, but we're very close.
records.zomi: I innkuan a neu a, ahi zongin i kinai mahmah hi.

records.english: Here's a photo of my family — that's my daughter on the left, holding the cat.
records.zomi: Hih ka innkuan limlak ahi hi — a veilam ah zawhngeu a pom pen ka tanu ahi hi.

records.english: Don't you think I look just like my grandfather did at my age?
records.zomi: Ka kum bang a hih lai-in ka pu bang ka kibang tektek hi, na ci kei hiam?

records.english: My family moved around a lot when I was young, so I've lived in five different towns.
records.zomi: Ka neu lai-in ka innkuan a pem tam mahmah ahih manin khua tuamtuam nga ah ka teeng khin hi.

records.english: I come from a long line of teachers.
records.zomi: Sia suan pan ka hong pai hi.

records.english: My son told me to introduce myself as "the best dad in the world," but I'll let you decide.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in “leitung a pa hoih pen” ci-in kiphawksak dingin hong gen hi, ahi zongin nang khensat in.

records.english: What's something about you that might surprise people?
records.zomi: Na thu lak pan mite lamdang sakna khat bang hiam?

records.english: As the eldest of four, I've always been the one who looks after everyone.
records.zomi: Sanggam li lak pan a upa pen ka hih manin mi khempeuh a ma pen ka hi tawntung hi.

records.english: My friends say I'm the calmest person they know.
records.zomi: Ka lawmte in a theih mite lak pan a lungsim nem pen ka hi hi, a ci uh hi.

records.english: I'm Joseph, the father of the little girl who just joined your daughter's class.
records.zomi: Kei Joseph ka hi a, na tanu' class ah a hong lut thak naupang nu' pa ka hi hi.

records.english: Being a grandfather is the best job I've ever had.
records.zomi: Pu hihna pen ka sep ngei lak pan nasep hoih pen ahi hi.

records.english: You might know my brother; he teaches at the primary school.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal na thei kha ding hi; sang neu ah sia a sem hi.

records.english: Are you the only child in your family?
records.zomi: Na innkuan ah ta khat bek na hi hiam?

records.english: Not at all — I'm one of nine, and we're all still very close.
records.zomi: Hi lo mahmah hi — sanggam kua lak pan khat ka hi a, i kinai lai mahmah hi.

records.english: As a single dad, I spend most of my free time at football practice with my son.
records.zomi: Pa khat bek in naupang ka khoi ahih manin ka hun awng a tam zaw ka tapa tawh football sinna ah ka zang hi.

records.english: Where does your family come from?
records.zomi: Na innkuan koi pan hong pai hiam?

records.english: My mother's side is from the hills, and my father's family has always lived by the coast.
records.zomi: Ka nu lam mualte pan hi a, ka pa' innkuan tuipi gei ah a teeng tawntung uh hi.

records.english: My wife says I'm a terrible cook, but my children love my pancakes.
records.zomi: Ka zi in an huan ka siam kei hi, a ci hi, ahi zongin ka tate in ka pancake a it uh hi.

records.english: Gardening, cooking, and long phone calls with my sisters are my favorite things.
records.zomi: Huan bawl, an huan leh ka sanggam numeite tawh phone tungah sawtpi kiho ka deih pen ahi hi.

records.english: Every year I still help with the harvest on my parents' farm.
records.zomi: Kum simin ka nu leh pa' lo ah buh lakna ah ka huh lai hi.

records.english: My family runs a small guesthouse in the hills, so I grew up meeting travelers from all over.
records.zomi: Ka innkuan in mual tungah mikhual inn neu khat a nei uh ahih manin koi pan peuh a hong pai khualzinte mu-in ka khang hi.

records.english: Nursing is my training, but these days I mostly care for my elderly parents.
records.zomi: Nurse sinna ka nei hi, ahi zongin tu laitakin a tam zaw ka nu leh pa upate ka kem hi.

records.english: The tall man with the loud laugh is probably my brother.
records.zomi: A nuih ging khauh pa sang pen ka sanggam pasal ahi kha ding hi.

records.english: Since my husband died, I've lived with my youngest daughter and her family.
records.zomi: Ka pasal a sih pan ka tanu neu pen leh a innkuan tawh ka teeng hi.

records.english: You can probably tell from my muddy boots that I work on a farm.
records.zomi: Ka khedap buan kai pan lo ah na ka sem hi cih na theih kha ding hi.

records.english: My grandchildren keep me young, or at least that's what I tell myself.
records.zomi: Ka tute in hong khangno den sak uh hi, ahih kei leh tua bangin ka kigen hi.

records.english: My daughter explained to her classmates that her grandmother speaks only our home language.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in a class pihte kiangah a pi in i inn pau bek a zang hi, ci-in a hilh hi.

records.english: He introduced me to his family before he even asked me out.
records.zomi: Hong ngen ma-in a innkuan kiangah hong theisak hi.

records.english: You all know my wife, but I don't think you've met our new baby.
records.zomi: Ka zi na thei khempeuh uh hi, ahi zongin i naungek thak na mu nai kei uh hi, ka ci hi.

records.english: My son's best friend practically lives at our house these days.
records.zomi: Tu laitakin ka tapa' lawm pen i inn ah a teeng bang hi.

records.english: My grandparents adopted a boy from our village, and he's like an uncle to me now.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh ka pi in i khua pan tapa khat a kila uh a, tu-in kei adingin pa neu bang ahi hi.

records.english: This is my oldest friend's son, who just started working at my office.
records.zomi: Hih pen ka office ah na a sem pan thak ka lawm lui pen' tapa ahi hi.

records.english: My grandmother likes to introduce me as "the clever one," which embarrasses my brothers.
records.zomi: Ka pi in “a pil pen” ci-in hong theisak a deih a, tua in ka sanggam pasalte a maizumsak hi.

records.english: My cousin video-called us from abroad so that she could meet my new husband.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu in ka pasal thak a muh theih nadingin gamdang pan video call hong bawl hi.

records.english: Is it okay if my brother joins us for lunch, since he's in town for the day?
records.zomi: Ni khat sung khua ah a om ahih manin ka sanggam pasal sun an ah hong kihel leh a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: Our neighbors' twins are the same age as our daughter, so the three of them have become inseparable.
records.zomi: I inn vengte' apengte i tanu tawh kum kibang uh ahih manin a thum un a kikhen thei nawn kei uh hi.

records.english: Kids, come and say hello to Grandpa's old friend from the army.
records.zomi: Naupangte, Pu' galkap lawm lui “Hello” ci dingin hong pai un.

records.english: This is my cousin Hau, who taught me to ride a bike when I was six.
records.zomi: Hih pen ka kum guk lai-a siiksakol tuan hong hilh ka sanggam Hau ahi hi.

records.english: Would your parents mind if I called them by their first names?
records.zomi: Na nu leh pa a min tawh ka sam leh a lungkim ding uh hiam?

records.english: Would you mind introducing me to your sister, since I've heard so much about her?
records.zomi: Na sanggam nu thu tampi ka zak ahih manin hong theisak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Everyone, these are my nephews, who are visiting from the city for the summer.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, hih te pen khuakhal adingin khuapi pan hong veh ka tanaute ahi uh hi.

records.english: You may have seen my brother-in-law at the clinic; he's the new dentist.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu' pasal clinic ah na mu kha ding hi; ha siavuan thak ahi hi.

records.english: My uncle is a bit hard of hearing, so please speak up when you're introduced.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu' bil a za thei lo deuh ahih manin kitheisak ciangin aw khauh deuh in gen un.

records.english: My sister's husband is from a completely different part of the country, but he fits right in.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu' pasal gam lam tuam bup pan hi napi, a kituak mahmah hi.

records.english: He told me his name was Pau, but everyone in his family calls him Little Bear.
records.zomi: A min Pau ahi hi, hong ci a, ahi zongin a innkuan khempeuh in Vompi Neu a ci uh hi.

records.english: Would it be all right if I brought my fiancé to meet your family?
records.zomi: Ka kiteen ding pa na innkuan kiangah ka paipih leh a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: My friend asked whether she could bring her mother to meet us.
records.zomi: Ka lawm in a nu hong muh dingin a paipih thei ding hiam hong dong hi.

records.english: I'd love for my parents to meet your family someday.
records.zomi: Ni khat ni-in ka nu leh pa in na innkuan a muh ding ka deih mahmah hi.

records.english: This is the friend who drove me to the hospital the night my son was born.
records.zomi: Hih pen ka tapa a suah zan ka zato hong paipih lawm ahi hi.

records.english: My aunt is the one in the blue dress, laughing at her own joke.
records.zomi: Ka ni pen puan dum silh-in amah' ciamnuihna tungah a nui pen ahi hi.

records.english: He's my half-sister's husband, which I suppose makes him my brother-in-law.
records.zomi: Amah pen pa khat mah nu tuam ka sanggam nu' pasal ahi a, tua ahih manin ka sanggam nu' pasal ahi hi.

records.english: Our families have been friends for three generations.
records.zomi: I innkuante suan thum sung kilawm uh hi.

records.english: Can I introduce my mother-in-law to your parents at the wedding?
records.zomi: Kiteenna ah ka sungnu na nu leh pa kiangah ka theisak thei ding hiam?

records.english: These two are my best friends from nursing school.
records.zomi: Hih nihte pen nurse sang a ka lawm pente ahi uh hi.

records.english: We met my wife's childhood friend at the market, and she hugged me as if she'd known me for years.
records.zomi: Zuakna mun ah ka zi' naupan lai lawm i kimu a, kum tampi hong thei khin bangin hong kawi hi.

records.english: My husband says you two went to the same school, though neither of you remembers it.
records.zomi: Note nih sang khat mah ah na kah uh hi, ci-in ka pasal in a gen hi, ahi zongin na nih un na phawk kei uh hi.

records.english: You might recognize my sister — she reads the news on the local radio.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu na thei kha ding hi — hih mun radio tungah thuthak a sim hi.

records.english: My wife always says that her sister is her best friend.
records.zomi: Ka zi in a sanggam nu pen a lawm pen ahi hi, a ci tawntung hi.

records.english: She introduced her boyfriend to the family at the New Year lunch.
records.zomi: Kum Thak sun an ah a it pa innkuan kiangah a theisak hi.

records.english: I've told my children so much about you that they feel they already know you.
records.zomi: Ka tate kiangah na thu tampi ka gen khin ahih manin hong thei khin bang a kisa uh hi.

records.english: Could you remind me of your husband's name, since I forgot it right after we met?
records.zomi: I kimuh khit pakin ka mangngilh ahih manin na pasal' min hong phawksak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: My colleague's wife turned out to be my old classmate from primary school.
records.zomi: Ka nasep pih' zi pen sang neu ah ka class pih lui ahi tawp hi.

records.english: My friend Joy is the reason I moved to this town.
records.zomi: Ka lawm Joy hangin hih khua ah ka hong pem hi.

records.english: Mom, this is Daniel, the boy I told you about.
records.zomi: Nu, hih pen Daniel ahi hi, kong gen tapa.

records.english: Meet my brother, the best cook in the family!
records.zomi: Innkuan sungah an huan siam pen ka sanggam pasal tawh kithei un!

records.english: I hope you all get a chance to meet my mother while she's here.
records.zomi: Ka nu hih munah a om sungin na khempeuh in na muh theih ding uh ka lamen hi.

records.english: Please introduce me to your aunt before she leaves.
records.zomi: Na ni a pai ma-in hong theisak in.

records.english: How should I introduce my partner to my grandparents, who are very traditional?
records.zomi: Ngeina khauh mahmah ka pu leh ka pite kiangah ka kikoppih bangci ka theisak ding hiam?

records.english: Introduce him simply as your friend first, and let them get to know him.
records.zomi: A masa-in na lawm bek ci-in theisak inla, amaute in a thei uh hen.

records.english: Have you met my stepmother yet?
records.zomi: Ka nukik na mu khin hiam?

records.english: Not yet, but your father talks about her all the time.
records.zomi: Mu nai kei hi, ahi zongin na pa in a thu a gen tawntung hi.

records.english: Are you two cousins on your mother's side or on your father's?
records.zomi: Note nih na nu lam pan sanggam na hi uh hiam, na pa lam pan hiam?

records.english: Did your sister ever tell you how we first met?
records.zomi: I kimuh masak dan na sanggam nu in hong gen ngei hiam?

records.english: She said it was at a bus stop in the rain.
records.zomi: Guah sungah bus khawlna ah ahi hi, a ci hi.

records.english: We really do want you to get to know our children better.
records.zomi: I tate na thei zaw ding i deih taktak hi.

records.english: May I introduce my father, who will be giving a short speech tonight?
records.zomi: Tu zanin thugen tomno a gen ding ka pa kong theisak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Shall I introduce you to my parents now, or after dinner?
records.zomi: Tu-in ka nu leh pa kiangah kong theisak ding hiam, nitak an khit ciangin hiam?

records.english: She might be shy at first, but my niece loves meeting new people.
records.zomi: A masa-in a maizum kha ding hi, ahi zongin ka tunu in mi thak muh a deih mahmah hi.

records.english: My fiancée's father shook my hand and said, "Welcome to the family."
records.zomi: Ka kiteen ding nu' pa in ka khut a man a, “Innkuan ah na hong tun lungdam hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: These are my two closest friends, and between the three of us we have eleven children.
records.zomi: Hih te pen ka lawm kinai pen nihte ahi uh a, i thum in ta sawm leh khat i nei uh hi.

records.english: Let me show you a photo of my grandparents on their wedding day.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh ka pi' kiteenna ni limlak kong lak ning.

records.english: My son proudly introduced his baby sister to everyone at church.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in biakinn ah mi khempeuh kiangah a nau numei kisaktheih takin a theisak hi.

records.english: I'd like you to meet my grandmother, who raised me after my parents moved abroad.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh pa gamdang ah a pem khit ciangin hong khoi ka pi kong theisak nuam hi.

records.english: Could you take a picture of me with my cousins?
records.zomi: Ka sanggamte tawh limlak hong la sak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Come and meet my in-laws — they've been looking forward to it.
records.zomi: Hong pai inla ka sungte tawh kithei in — a lamen mahmah uh hi.

records.english: My grandfather insists on introducing himself to every new neighbor with a bag of oranges.
records.zomi: Ka pu in inn veng thak khempeuh lamsi ip khat tawh amah le amah kiphawksak ding a ngen ngiat hi.

records.english: What would your grandparents like to do while they're here?
records.zomi: Hih munah a om sungun na pu leh na pite in bang sem nuam uh hiam?

records.english: Mostly they want to rest and spend time with the children.
records.zomi: A tam zaw tawlnga-in naupangte tawh hun zat a deih uh hi.

records.english: My wife's brother told us he wanted to surprise his parents, so we kept his visit a secret.
records.zomi: Ka zi' sanggam pasal in a nu leh pa lamdangsak a deih hi, hong ci ahih manin a hong veh ding i sel hi.

records.english: It's so good to see you after all these years!
records.zomi: Kum tampi khit ciangin kong muh kik a nuam mahmah hi!

records.english: Dad cooked a feast to celebrate my brother's return from the army.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal galkap pan a hong ciah kik lungdam dingin Pa in ankhopna a huan hi.

records.english: Can we go to the airport to pick up Grandma?
records.zomi: Pi la dingin vanlengtual ah i pai thei ding hiam?

records.english: Make sure Grandma has a glass of water by her bed.
records.zomi: Pi' lupna kiang ah tui khuat khat a om hiam en in.

records.english: Grandma, come in and sit by the fire; you must be tired after the long bus ride.
records.zomi: Pi, hong lut inla mei kiang ah tu in; bus tuan sau khit ciangin na gim ding hi.

records.english: Our neighbors might come over to meet your mother this evening.
records.zomi: Tu nitakin na nu mu dingin i inn vengte a hong pai kha ding uh hi.

records.english: You're the first person from my wife's family to visit our new home.
records.zomi: Ka zi' innkuan pan i inn thak a hong veh masa pen nang na hi hi.

records.english: Our house is your house for as long as you're here.
records.zomi: Hih munah na om sungin i inn pen na inn ahi hi.

records.english: Would you like to rest for an hour before lunch?
records.zomi: Sun an ma-in nai khat sung na tawlnga nuam hiam?

records.english: The children cleaned their room themselves to make space for their cousins.
records.zomi: Naupangte in a sanggamte adingin mun a om nadingin a khan uh amau mah in a siangsak uh hi.

records.english: Welcome home, son — we've missed you so much!
records.zomi: Ka tapa, inn ah na hong tun kik lungdam hi — kong ngaih mahmah uh hi!

records.english: It meant a lot that you traveled so far to see our new baby.
records.zomi: I naungek thak mu dingin hih zah gamla pan na hong pai thupi mahmah hi.

records.english: My mother-in-law told me she'd bring her own pillow, since she can't sleep on soft ones.
records.zomi: Lukhum nem tungah a ihmu thei kei ahih manin amah' lukhum a tawi ding hi, ci-in ka sungnu in hong gen hi.

records.english: My aunt said she'd arrive around noon, so I've made her favorite soup.
records.zomi: Ka ni in sun laitak bang ciangin a tung ding hi, a ci ahih manin a an-tui deih pen ka huan khin hi.

records.english: My grandmother cried when she saw how much her grandson had grown.
records.zomi: A tu bangzah a khang khin hiam a muh ciangin ka pi a kap hi.

records.english: Is it all right if your uncle stays with us until his new apartment is ready?
records.zomi: Na pa neu' inn thak a kigingsak dong i kiangah a om leh a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: The visitors were greeted at the bus station by half the family.
records.zomi: Mikhualte bus station ah innkuan a lang in a muak uh hi.

records.english: Has anyone told Aunt Ruth which bus to take from the station?
records.zomi: Station pan bus bang tuan ding hiam Ni Ruth kuamah in a hilh khin hiam?

records.english: How was the trip from the village?
records.zomi: Khua pan na khualzinna bangci om hiam?

records.english: Long and bumpy, but worth it to see you all.
records.zomi: A sau a, a khi mahmah hi, ahi zongin note khempeuh kong muh adingin a man a tawh hi.

records.english: We're so happy you're finally here!
records.zomi: Na hong tun tawp ahih manin i lungdam mahmah hi!

records.english: My mother always says that a full table makes a happy home.
records.zomi: Dawhkan dim in inn nuam a bawl hi, ci-in ka nu in a gen tawntung hi.

records.english: My cousin wrote to say she might visit at Christmas with her new husband.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu in a pasal thak tawh Christmas ciangin a hong veh kha ding hi, ci-in a gelh hi.

records.english: We moved the baby's crib into our bedroom so that Grandpa could have the spare room.
records.zomi: Pu in khan awng a neih nadingin naungek' lupna i lupna khan ah i suan hi.

records.english: You might find the house a bit noisy with three children, but we hope you'll be comfortable.
records.zomi: Naupang thum tawh inn a ging buai deuh na ci kha ding hi, ahi zongin na om nuam ding i lamen hi.

records.english: My little brother hid behind the door because he was too shy to greet our relatives.
records.zomi: Ka nau pasal in i beh leh phungte a hopih ngam lo ahih manin kongkhak nung ah a bu hi.

records.english: Please sit down — dinner will be ready in a few minutes.
records.zomi: Tu in — minit tawmno sungin nitak an a kizo ding hi.

records.english: We video-called my uncle so that he could say hello to the visitors from home.
records.zomi: Inn pan hong veh mikhualte kiangah “Hello” a cih theih nadingin ka pa neu tawh video call i bawl hi.

records.english: I've cleared two shelves in the wardrobe for your clothes.
records.zomi: Na puante adingin puan koihna sung dawh nih ka suah awng sak khin hi.

records.english: My aunt warned us that she might bring all six of her grandchildren.
records.zomi: Ka ni in a tu gukte khempeuh a paipih kha ding hi, ci-in hong kidopsak hi.

records.english: My father-in-law said our home felt just like his village.
records.zomi: Ka sungpa in i inn pen a khua mah bang hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Our house is small, so the boys will share a mattress on the floor.
records.zomi: I inn a neu ahih manin tapate in sual tungah lupna nem khat ah a lum khawm ding uh hi.

records.english: Uncle, the children are asleep, so could we keep our voices down this evening?
records.zomi: Pu, naupangte a ihmu uh ahih manin tu nitakin dai deuh-in i gen thei ding hiam?

records.english: Welcome to the family, Naomi!
records.zomi: Naomi, innkuan ah na hong tun lungdam hi!

records.english: In this hospital, visitors to the nursery are asked to wash their hands first.
records.zomi: Hih zato ah naungek khan a veh mite in a khut uh a sil masa ding uh kingen hi.

records.english: Could you translate for my parents, since their English isn't very good?
records.zomi: Ka nu leh pa' English pau a hoih lua kei ahih manin amaute adingin na let sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: The house got very lively once my sister's family arrived with their four children.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu' innkuan a ta li tawh a hong tun ciangun inn a nuam mahmah hi.

records.english: We set up the old radio in Grandpa's room so that he could listen to the morning news.
records.zomi: Zingsang thuthak a ngaih theih nadingin Pu' khan ah radio lui i koih hi.

records.english: How long are your parents staying with you?
records.zomi: Na nu leh pa bangzah sawt nang tawh a om ding uh hiam?

records.english: Two weeks, unless my father gets homesick before then.
records.zomi: Kal nih, ka pa in inn a ngaih masak kei leh.

records.english: Everyone, this is my husband's grandmother, who is ninety-two and sharper than any of us.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, hih pen kum sawmkua leh nih a pha a, i khempeuh sangin a pil zaw ka pasal' pi ahi hi.

records.english: Please leave the bathroom light on so that Grandma can find her way at night.
records.zomi: Pi in zanin a lampi a muh theih nadingin kisilna inn meivak phel lo-in nusia un.

records.english: Here, let me hold the baby while you take off your coat.
records.zomi: Hih, na puan sil na suah laitakin naungek ka pom sak ning.

records.english: Can my cousins sleep in your room while they're visiting?
records.zomi: Ka sanggamte a hong veh sungun na khan ah a ihmu thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: Please leave your bags by the door, and I'll carry them upstairs later.
records.zomi: Na ipte kongkhak kiangah nusia un, a nung ciangin a tung lam ah ka puak ding hi.

records.english: Your room is ready, and the window has a lovely view of the hills.
records.zomi: Na khan a kigingsak khin a, tawhkhawng pan mualte muhna a hoih mahmah hi.

records.english: The children made a card for their grandparents to welcome them.
records.zomi: Naupangte in a pu leh pite uh muak dingin card khat a bawl uh hi.

records.english: Children, no jumping on the sofa while our guests are here.
records.zomi: Naupangte, i zinte hih munah a om sungun sofa tungah diang kei un.

records.english: My sister asked whether her children could bring their dog when they visit.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu in a tate a hong veh ciangun a ui uh a paipih thei ding uh hiam hong dong hi.

records.english: Grandpa says he's happy to sleep on the sofa, but we won't let him.
records.zomi: Pu in sofa tungah ihmu a lungdam hi, a ci hi, ahi zongin i phal kei hi.

records.english: We always welcome guests with a cup of hot ginger tea.
records.zomi: Zinte siing niangtui lum khuat khat tawh i muak tawntung hi.

records.english: We hired a van to bring all the relatives from the village to the wedding.
records.zomi: Kiteenna ah khua pan beh leh phungte khempeuh a tawi dingin van khat i hawh hi.

records.english: We could take your parents to the lake if the weather is good.
records.zomi: Khua dan a hoih leh na nu leh pa dil ah i paipih thei hi.

records.english: Kids, come and greet your great-aunt — she's come all the way from the coast.
records.zomi: Naupangte, na pi' sanggam nu hong hopih un — tuipi gei pan a hong pai hi.

records.english: Shall we show your parents around the town tomorrow?
records.zomi: Zingciang na nu leh pa khua sung i lak ding hiam?

records.english: In our house, nobody wakes Grandpa from his afternoon nap.
records.zomi: I inn ah kuamah in Pu' sun ihmut pan a phawng kei hi.

records.english: It's been ten years since your last visit — what took you so long?
records.zomi: Na hong veh nunung pen pan kum sawm a pha khin hi — bang hangin sawt na hiam?

records.english: Remember to send a message when you reach the border, so that we know you crossed safely.
records.zomi: Gam ciang na tun ciangin thu khak ding phawk in, bit takin na kantan cih i theih nadingin.

records.english: Before leaving home, I took a photo of the whole family on the front steps.
records.zomi: Inn ka paisan ma-in mai lam lamsai tungah innkuan bup limlak ka la hi.

records.english: Does saying goodbye to your parents ever get any easier?
records.zomi: Na nu leh pa tawh kikhen pen a baih zaw ngei hiam?

records.english: Grandma pressed some money into my hand and told me not to tell anyone.
records.zomi: Pi in ka khut sungah sum tawmno a koih a, kuamah gen lo dingin hong gen hi.

records.english: We left a note on the kitchen table for Mom, since she was asleep when we went.
records.zomi: I pai ciangin Nu a ihmu ahih manin anbuk dawhkan tungah lai khat i nusia hi.

records.english: Goodbye, my dear — come home soon.
records.zomi: Goodbye, ka it — manlang takin inn ah hong ciah in.

records.english: We planned a farewell picnic for our daughter and her best friend before the friend's family moved away.
records.zomi: I tanu' lawm pen' innkuan a pem ma-un i tanu leh a lawm pen adingin kikhenna picnic i bawl hi.

records.english: My son promised he would write to us in our own language.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in i pau tawh lai hong gelh ding a kiciam hi.

records.english: We'll keep your room exactly as it is until you come home.
records.zomi: Inn ah na hong ciah dong na khan a om bang mahin i kem ding hi.

records.english: My grandparents gave us their blessing before we moved abroad.
records.zomi: Gamdang ah i pem ma-in ka pu leh ka pi in thupha hong pia uh hi.

records.english: Could we video-call every weekend while you're away?
records.zomi: Na om lo sungin kal bei simin video call i bawl thei ding hiam?

records.english: Uncle Thang ran alongside the train, shouting last-minute advice.
records.zomi: Pu Thang in meileng gei ah tai-in a nunung hilhnate a kikou hi.

records.english: Bring us back some sweets from your hometown when you come next time.
records.zomi: A zom na hong pai ciangin na khua pan tui-namtui tawmno hong tawi in.

records.english: They were told that the bus would leave at six sharp.
records.zomi: Bus nai guk tak ciangin a pai ding hi, ci-in kigen uh hi.

records.english: Each time I leave, my father walks me to the end of the road.
records.zomi: Ka pai simin ka pa in lampi tawp dong hong paipih hi.

records.english: Dad told me he'd leave the porch light on for me every night until I came back.
records.zomi: Ka hong ciah kik dong zan simin inn mai meivak a phel lo ding hi, ci-in Pa in hong gen hi.

records.english: The whole family came to the bus station to see my cousin off.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam' pai khiatna ah innkuan bup bus station ah a pai uh hi.

records.english: Leaving the farm where I was born felt like leaving a part of myself behind.
records.zomi: Ka suahna lo paisan pen keimah' tawm khat ka nusia bang a kisa hi.

records.english: Grandpa held my hand and said, "Study hard and come home safely."
records.zomi: Pu in ka khut a len a, “Lai haksa takin sin inla, bit takin inn ah hong ciah in,” a ci hi.

records.english: He hugged his daughter at the school gate and told her he was proud of her.
records.zomi: Sang kongpi ah a tanu a kawi a, a kisaktheih hi, ci-in a gen hi.

records.english: My cousin left so suddenly that we never had a chance to say goodbye properly.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam thakhat in a pai ahih manin hoih takin kikhen theihna i nei kei hi.

records.english: You can borrow my suitcase for your trip to the city.
records.zomi: Khuapi na pai nadingin ka suitcase na leitawi thei hi.

records.english: Kids, give your cousins one last hug — their bus is here.
records.zomi: Naupangte, na sanggamte a nunung pen in kawi un — a bus uh a tung hi.

records.english: May I take one of your paintings to hang in my new room?
records.zomi: Ka khan thak ah khai dingin na lim zai khat ka la thei ding hiam?

records.english: Of course — choose whichever one you like best.
records.zomi: Thei hi — na deih pen teel in.

records.english: We drove my sister to her new job in the city and helped her unpack.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu khuapi a nasep thak ah i paipih a, a vante phel dingin i huh hi.

records.english: My son leaves for university tomorrow, and I'm trying not to cry.
records.zomi: Zingciang ka tapa sangpi ah a pai ding a, kap lo dingin ka hanciam hi.

records.english: Call us every Sunday, even if it's only for five minutes.
records.zomi: Minit nga bek zongin Nipini simin hong sam un.

records.english: We stood at the gate long after the bus had disappeared over the hill.
records.zomi: Bus mual galkhat ah a mang khit sawtpi dong kongpi ah i ding hi.

records.english: Is this the last time we'll all be together in this house?
records.zomi: Hih pen hih inn sungah i khempeuh i om khawm nunung pen ding hiam?

records.english: It might be, since the new owners move in next month.
records.zomi: Ahi kha ding hi, inn neipa thakte kha zom ciangin a hong pem ding uh ahih manin.

records.english: Please, no tears at the station — it'll only make leaving harder.
records.zomi: Station ah kap kei un — pai a haksa sak bek ding hi.

records.english: My brother's farewell speech before he moved overseas made everyone laugh and cry.
records.zomi: Tuipi galkhat a pem ma-in ka sanggam pasal' kikhenna thugen in mi khempeuh a nuihsak a, a kapsak hi.

records.english: Can I stay one more night before I go back to the city?
records.zomi: Khuapi ah ka ciah kik ma-in zan khat ka om behlap thei ding hiam?

records.english: Can you tell Grandma I'm sorry I couldn't stay longer?
records.zomi: Ka om sawt zo kei ahih manin hong maisak in, ci-in Pi na gen sak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: My brother left to work overseas when I was eight, and we said goodbye at the airport.
records.zomi: Ka kum giat lai-in ka sanggam pasal tuipi galkhat ah na sem dingin a pai a, vanlengtual ah goodbye i kici hi.

records.english: Leaving my parents' village to get married was the hardest goodbye of my life.
records.zomi: Kiteeng dingin ka nu leh pa' khua paisan pen ka nuntakna sunga kikhenna haksa pen ahi hi.

records.english: Is being so far from family the hardest part of working abroad?
records.zomi: Innkuan pan gamla takah om pen gamdang nasep sunga a haksa pen hi hiam?

records.english: My grandmother asked us to sing her favorite hymn before we left.
records.zomi: I pai ma-un a la deih pen sa dingin ka pi in hong ngen hi.

records.english: Write down Grandma's address so that you can send her a card from school.
records.zomi: Sang pan card na khak theih nadingin Pi' teenna mun gelh in.

records.english: It could be a whole year before the family is all together again.
records.zomi: Innkuan bup a kikhawm kik ma-in kum khat bup a pha kha ding hi.

records.english: Shall I drive you to the station, or would you rather take a taxi?
records.zomi: Station ah kong paipih ding hiam, taxi na tuan nuam zaw hiam?

records.english: The children cried when their favorite uncle had to go back to his ship.
records.zomi: A pa neu deih pen a tembaw ah a ciah kik kul ciangin naupangte a kap uh hi.

records.english: My nephew asked if he could come with us next time.
records.zomi: Ka tanau in a zom ciangin ko tawh a pai thei ding hiam hong dong hi.

records.english: The kitchen was full of dirty plates after our relatives left, but nobody minded.
records.zomi: I beh leh phungte a pai khit uh ciangin anbuk kuang nin tawh a dim hi, ahi zongin kuamah lungkia lo hi.

records.english: Will you come back for my wedding?
records.zomi: Ka kiteenna adingin na hong ciah ding hiam?

records.english: Nothing could keep me away.
records.zomi: Bangmah in hong khaksak thei lo ding hi.

records.english: My brother wrote a letter to each of us the night before he joined the army.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in galkap a suah ma zan in i khat ciat lai a gelh hi.

records.english: Nobody in this family leaves on a journey without eating breakfast first.
records.zomi: Hih innkuan ah kuamah zingsang an ne masa lo-in khualzin dingin pai ngei lo hi.

records.english: Could you look after my plants while I'm studying abroad?
records.zomi: Gamdang ah lai ka sin sungin ka pakte na kem thei ding hiam?

records.english: My mother always says, "Goodbyes are only for people who don't plan to meet again."
records.zomi: Ka nu in, “Goodbye pen kimu kik ding a lamen lo mite adingin bek ahi hi,” a ci tawntung hi.

records.english: My sister asked me to visit her new home in the capital before the end of the year.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu in kum a bei ma-in khuapi lian a om a inn thak va veh dingin hong ngen hi.

records.english: Mom packed so much food for my journey that my bag would barely close.
records.zomi: Ka khualzinna adingin Nu in an tampi mahmah a koih ahih manin ka ip a kikhak zo dek kei hi.

records.english: We said our goodbyes the night before, because my flight left at dawn.
records.zomi: Ka vanleng zingsang tuung pen ciangin a pai ding ahih manin zan ma-in i kikhen hi.

records.english: Hug your grandmother before you get in the car.
records.zomi: Mawtaw na tuan ma-in na pi kawi in.

records.english: Please, Grandpa, sit down — you don't have to walk us to the car.
records.zomi: Pu, tu in — mawtaw dong hong paipih kul lo hi.

records.english: It's hard to say goodbye to someone who might not be here next year.
records.zomi: Kum zom ciangin om nawn lo kha ding mi tawh kikhen a haksa hi.

records.english: My aunt said she'd send photos of the baby every week.
records.zomi: Ka ni in kal simin naungek limlak a khak ding hi, a ci hi.

records.english: My father's last words to me at the airport were, "Be kind, and keep praying."
records.zomi: Vanlengtual ah ka pa' nunung kammal pen, “Hehpih in, thu ngen den in,” ahi hi.

records.english: You may take the old bicycle with you if you think you'll use it.
records.zomi: Na zang ding na ci leh siiksakol lui na tawi thei hi.

records.english: As an only child, I always wished for a big family.
records.zomi: Ta khat bek ka hih manin innkuan lian ka deih tawntung hi.

records.english: Is it rude to call your aunt by her first name?
records.zomi: Na ni a min tawh sam zahtak lohna hi hiam?

records.english: Could you explain how we're related to the family next door?
records.zomi: Inn kiang innkuan tawh bangci i kizom hiam hong hilhcian thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Your great-grandmother and their grandfather were brother and sister.
records.zomi: Na pi' nu leh amaute' pu pen u leh nau ahi uh hi.

records.english: My cousin's son was given my grandfather's name.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam' tapa ka pu' min kipia hi.

records.english: My brother-in-law and my husband argue about football all the time, but they're good friends.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu' pasal leh ka pasal football thu ah a kinial tawntung uh hi, ahi zongin lawm hoih ahi uh hi.

records.english: Which of your parents are you more like?
records.zomi: Na nu leh pa lak pan kua tawh na kibang zaw hiam?

records.english: My mother, definitely — we're both stubborn and talkative.
records.zomi: Ka nu, ciangtakin — i nih in i lu a khauh a, i gen tam hi.

records.english: My son asked whether his new baby brother would sleep in his room.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in a nau pasal thak a khan ah a ihmu ding hiam hong dong hi.

records.english: "You're just like your father," my mother says whenever I lose my temper.
records.zomi: Ka heh ciangin, “Na pa mah bang na hi hi,” ci-in ka nu in a gen hi.

records.english: Our parents met at a cousin's wedding and married a year later.
records.zomi: I nu leh pa sanggam khat' kiteenna ah a kimu uh a, kum khat khit ciangin a kiteeng uh hi.

records.english: My grandmother keeps every letter her children ever sent her.
records.zomi: Ka pi in a tate in a khak ngei laikhak khempeuh a kem hi.

records.english: My grandmother's ring was passed down to me when I turned eighteen.
records.zomi: Kum sawm leh giat ka pha ciangin ka pi' zungbuh kei kiangah hong kipia hi.

records.english: Our family tends to talk loudly, so visitors sometimes think we're arguing.
records.zomi: I innkuan in aw khauh takin i gen ngei ahih manin mikhualte in i kinial hi, ci-in a ngaihsun ngei uh hi.

records.english: In our family, children always use a respectful title for older relatives.
records.zomi: I innkuan ah naupangte in upa beh leh phungte zahtakna min tawh a sam tawntung uh hi.

records.english: My great-aunt is ninety-four and still walks to church every Sunday.
records.zomi: Ka pi' sanggam nu kum sawmkua leh li a pha a, Nipini simin biakinn ah a kaai lai hi.

records.english: My stepfather never tried to replace my dad; he simply became another person who loved me.
records.zomi: Ka pakik in ka pa' mun la ding a sawm ngei kei a; hong it mi khat a suak bek hi.

records.english: How many grandchildren do your parents have?
records.zomi: Na nu leh pa in tu bangzah a nei uh hiam?

records.english: Seven, and another one is on the way.
records.zomi: Sagih, a dang khat zong a hong pai ding hi.

records.english: My wife's family is much bigger than mine, so I'm still learning everyone's names.
records.zomi: Ka zi' innkuan kei' sangin a lian zaw mahmah ahih manin mi khempeuh' min ka sin lai hi.

records.english: Does anyone in your family play the guitar at reunions?
records.zomi: Kikhopna ciangin na innkuan sungah kuamah in guitar a tum hiam?

records.english: My older brother and I didn't speak for a year after an argument about the farm.
records.zomi: Ka u pasal leh kei lo thu kinialna khit ciangin kum khat sung i kiho kei uh hi.

records.english: Our old family photos were damaged in a fire years ago, so only a few remain.
records.zomi: I innkuan limlak luite kum tampi lai-in mei kang in a siatsak ahih manin tawmno bek a lai hi.

records.english: Please be patient with Grandpa; his memory isn't what it used to be.
records.zomi: Pu thuakzawh un; a phawkna a masa bang hi nawn lo hi.

records.english: Our children are allowed to visit their grandparents' farm on their own now.
records.zomi: I tate in tu-in amau bek in a pu leh pite uh lo a va veh thei uh hi.

records.english: In this house, nobody teases your little cousin about her glasses.
records.zomi: Hih inn ah na sanggam nu neu a mitlimlang hangin kuamah in a nuihsat kei hi.

records.english: My father's brothers all live on the same street, so our childhood was full of cousins.
records.zomi: Ka pa' sanggam pasalte khempeuh lampi khat mah ah a teeng uh ahih manin i naupan lai sanggam tampi tawh a dim hi.

records.english: Our family has a rule that no one goes to bed angry.
records.zomi: I innkuan in heh tawh kuamah lup lo ding thukham a nei hi.

records.english: Grandma told us that her own grandmother lived to be a hundred and two.
records.zomi: Pi in amah' pi kum zakhat leh nih dong a nungta hi, hong ci hi.

records.english: How old is the eldest member of your family?
records.zomi: Na innkuan ah a upa pen kum bangzah a pha hiam?

records.english: Do your grandparents live with you?
records.zomi: Na pu leh na pite nang tawh a teeng uh hiam?

records.english: My aunt and uncle have no children of their own, so they treat all of us like their own.
records.zomi: Ka ni leh ka pu in amau ta a nei kei uh ahih manin i khempeuh amau ta bangin hong et uh hi.

records.english: Can I invite my stepbrother to the family reunion?
records.zomi: Innkuan kikhopna ah ka nukik' tapa ka sam thei ding hiam?

records.english: My grandfather has eleven grandchildren and remembers every one of our birthdays.
records.zomi: Ka pu in tu sawm leh khat a nei a, i pianni khempeuh a phawk hi.

records.english: Whatever happens, I know my brothers will always stand by me.
records.zomi: Bang a piang zongin ka sanggam pasalte hong pang den ding uh hi, ka thei hi.

records.english: The family business was handed over to my eldest brother when Dad retired.
records.zomi: Pa in a nasep a tawp ciangin innkuan sumbawlna ka u pasal upa pen kiangah kipia hi.

records.english: We share family news on a group call every Sunday, with relatives in four countries.
records.zomi: Nipini simin gam li a om beh leh phungte tawh group call ah innkuan thu i kihawm hi.

records.english: My uncle, who is a pastor, married my parents thirty years ago.
records.zomi: Pastor a hi ka pa neu in kum sawmthum lai-in ka nu leh pa a kiteensak hi.

records.english: May I call you "Auntie" even though we're not related?
records.zomi: I kizom kei hangin “Ni” kong ci thei ding hiam?

records.english: Who in your family are you closest to?
records.zomi: Na innkuan sungah kua tawh na kinai pen hiam?

records.english: My niece calls me "big uncle" because I'm her father's older brother.
records.zomi: A pa' u ka hih manin ka tunu in “pa lian” hong ci hi.

records.english: Mom said I could stay at my cousin's house during the school holidays.
records.zomi: Sang khawl hun sungin ka sanggam' inn ah ka om thei hi, ci-in Nu in a gen hi.

records.english: Show your cousins the photos from our trip on your tablet.
records.zomi: Na tablet tungah i khualzinna limlakte na sanggamte lak in.

records.english: Does your son still want to be a doctor like his grandfather?
records.zomi: Na tapa in a pu bangin siavuan suak a deih lai hiam?

records.english: My little sister borrows my clothes without asking, which really annoys me.
records.zomi: Ka nau numei in dong lo-in ka puante a leitawi a, tua in hong lungkiasak mahmah hi.

records.english: The family house was built by my great-grandfather with his own hands.
records.zomi: Innkuan inn pen ka pu' pa in a khut tawh a lam hi.

records.english: My brother called to say his wife had given birth to a healthy baby girl.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in a zi in tanu dam khat a nei hi, ci-in hong sam hi.

records.english: How are you related to the bride?
records.zomi: Kiteeng nu tawh bangci na kizom hiam?

records.english: Her mother and my mother are sisters, so we're first cousins.
records.zomi: A nu leh ka nu u leh nau ahi uh ahih manin sanggam ka hi uh hi.

records.english: Is your husband close to his brothers?
records.zomi: Na pasal a sanggam pasalte tawh a kinai hiam?

records.english: Very close — they call each other every evening.
records.zomi: Kinai mahmah — nitak simin a kisam uh hi.

records.english: We keep a family tree on the wall, drawn by my uncle with colored pens.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in meel tuamtuam laikung tawh a gelh innkuan sing lim bang ah i khai hi.

records.english: People say my daughter has her grandmother's eyes.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in a pi' mit a nei hi, mite in a ci uh hi.

records.english: I was told I had an older sister who died before I was born.
records.zomi: Ka suah ma-in a si u numei khat ka nei hi, ci-in hong gen uh hi.

records.english: Nobody told me that my cousin had moved back to the village.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam khua ah a hong ciah kik hi, ci kuamah in hong gen kei uh hi.

records.english: How often do you manage to visit your wife's parents?
records.zomi: Na zi' nu leh pa bangzah vei na va veh thei hiam?

records.english: My father always said, "Family is the one thing money can't buy."
records.zomi: Ka pa in, “Innkuan pen sum in a lei theih loh na khat bek ahi hi,” a ci tawntung hi.

records.english: My sister and her husband adopted two boys last year.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu leh a pasal in kum bei-in tapa nih a kila uh hi.

records.english: My father taught me to fix bicycles with nothing but a wrench and a lot of patience.
records.zomi: Ka pa in wrench leh thuakzawhna tampi bek tawh siiksakol phuah hong hilh hi.

records.english: My twin sister lives on the other side of the world, but we still finish each other's sentences.
records.zomi: Ka apeng numei leitung galkhat ah a teeng hi, ahi zongin i thugen i kizom sak lai hi.

records.english: My son told his teacher that his father can fix anything.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in a pa in na khempeuh a phuah thei hi, ci-in a sia kiangah a gen hi.

records.english: Did becoming parents change how you spend your money?
records.zomi: Nu leh pa na suah uh in na sum zat dan uh a laih hiam?

records.english: We were married in my wife's village, and the celebration lasted three days.
records.zomi: Ka zi' khua ah ka kiteeng uh a, poai ni thum sung a om hi.

records.english: We said yes, as long as it washes out before school starts.
records.zomi: Sang a kipat ma-in a kisil mang leh, a hoih hi, ka ci uh hi.

records.english: Is our son old enough to take the bus to school by himself?
records.zomi: I tapa amah bek in sang ah bus a tuan thei dingin a lian khin hiam?

records.english: Kids, your mother and I have decided that everyone will help with the garden this summer.
records.zomi: Naupangte, na nu leh kei tu khuakhal ciangin mi khempeuh in huan ah a huh ding uh i khensat hi.

records.english: Our son's school called because he'd been in a fight with another boy.
records.zomi: I tapa tapa dang khat tawh a kilai ahih manin a sang in hong sam hi.

records.english: The children's bikes were stolen from the yard, and they cried for an hour.
records.zomi: Naupangte' siiksakol inntual pan kiguk a, nai khat sung a kap uh hi.

records.english: "Your children are watching how you treat each other," our pastor told us at our wedding.
records.zomi: “Na tate in na kiet dan uh a en uh hi,” ci-in i kiteenna ah i pastor in hong gen hi.

records.english: Was your first year of marriage as hard as people say?
records.zomi: Na kiteenna kum masa pen mite' gen bangin a haksa hiam?

records.english: When our son was born, my husband cried more than I did.
records.zomi: I tapa a suah ciangin ka pasal kei sangin a kap zaw hi.

records.english: Is it normal for a two-year-old to have tantrums every day?
records.zomi: Kum nih naupang in ni simin a kiphun pen a pangai hiam?

records.english: Our doctor told us that it's a common phase and usually passes.
records.zomi: Tua pen a pangai hun khat ahi a, a bei ngei hi, ci-in i siavuan in hong gen hi.

records.english: We've told our son he can't ride his motorbike after dark.
records.zomi: Khua a mial khit ciangin a motorbike a tuan thei kei hi, ci-in i tapa i gen hi.

records.english: Our son broke his arm falling out of a tree, and he was so proud of his cast.
records.zomi: I tapa singkung pan a kiak-in a ban a kitan a, a ban khuhna a kisaktheih mahmah hi.

records.english: Tell the kids about growing up on the farm — they love those stories.
records.zomi: Lo inn a na khanna thu naupangte gen in — tua tangthute a it uh hi.

records.english: My husband stayed home with the baby for a year while I finished my studies.
records.zomi: Ka lai sinna ka zawh nadingin ka pasal in kum khat sung naungek tawh inn ah a om hi.

records.english: Our marriage survived some very difficult years, and we're stronger because of them.
records.zomi: I kiteenna in kum haksa mahmah pawlkhat a zo a, tua hangin i hat zaw hi.

records.english: Teaching our son to be honest matters more to us than good grades.
records.zomi: Sitna ngah hoih sangin i tapa thuman ding hilh pen i adingin a thupi zaw hi.

records.english: My parents-in-law insisted on paying for our honeymoon.
records.zomi: Ka sungpa leh sungnu in i kiteenna khit khualzinna man a pia ding a ngen ngiat uh hi.

records.english: My mother-in-law gives us advice about everything, from feeding the baby to choosing schools.
records.zomi: Ka sungnu in naungek an vak pan sang teel dong na khempeuh ah hilhna hong pia hi.

records.english: Shall we tell the children about the new baby tonight, or wait until after Christmas?
records.zomi: Naungek thak thu tu zanin naupangte i gen ding hiam, Christmas khit dong i ngak ding hiam?

records.english: Our daughter's first tooth fell out at school, and she brought it home in a tissue.
records.zomi: I tanu' ha masa pen sang ah a kiak a, puan neu sungah tuam-in inn ah a tawi hi.

records.english: My grandmother told me that a good marriage needs patience more than romance.
records.zomi: Kiteenna hoih in itna sangin thuakzawhna a kisam zaw hi, ci-in ka pi in hong gen hi.

records.english: The baby's room was painted soft yellow before she arrived.
records.zomi: Naungek a tun ma-in a khan ngaan nem tawh kizai hi.

records.english: Our twins were baptized at the same church where my husband and I got married.
records.zomi: I apengte ka pasal leh kei i kiteenna biakinn mah ah kibaptaiz uh hi.

records.english: Our children have taught us as much as we have taught them.
records.zomi: I tate in i hilh zah tawh kibangin hong hilh uh hi.

records.english: Please let your sister have a turn on the bicycle.
records.zomi: Na sanggam nu siiksakol tungah a khawl ngah sak in.

records.english: Becoming a stepmother taught me that love can grow slowly.
records.zomi: Nukik ka suah in itna zawlzawl in a khang thei hi, ci hong hilh hi.

records.english: Should our children grow up speaking both our home language and English?
records.zomi: I tate in i inn pau leh English pau nih tengteng zang-in a khang ding uh hiam?

records.english: After forty years of marriage, my parents still hold hands when they walk.
records.zomi: Kum sawmli kiteenna khit ciangin ka nu leh pa a vak ciangun khut a kilen lai uh hi.

records.english: My father-in-law told my husband, "Treat her the way you'd want someone to treat your daughter."
records.zomi: Ka sungpa in ka pasal kiangah, “Na tanu a kiet ding na deih bangin amah et in,” a ci hi.

records.english: Raising children in a different country from the one we grew up in is harder than we expected.
records.zomi: I khanna gam hi lo gam dang ah naupang khoi pen i lamet sangin a haksa zaw hi.

records.english: Parents' evening at the school was postponed because of the storm.
records.zomi: Huihpi hangin sang ah nu leh pate nitak kikhopna kihawh hi.

records.english: We let our daughter choose her own clothes now that she's seven.
records.zomi: I tanu kum sagih a phak manin amah' puan amah in a teel dingin i phal hi.

records.english: How do you and your wife decide who does what with the children?
records.zomi: Nang leh na zi in naupangte tawh kua in bang a sem ding hiam bangci na khensat uh hiam?

records.english: We sit down every Sunday night and plan the week together.
records.zomi: Nipini zan simin i tu a, kal khat sung sep ding i ngaihsun khawm hi.

records.english: My wife was offered a job in another city, so we're deciding whether to move as a family.
records.zomi: Ka zi khuapi dang ah nasep kipia ahih manin innkuan bup pem ding hiam i khensat hi.

records.english: Are you planning a big wedding or a small one?
records.zomi: Kiteenna lianpi na bawl ding hiam, a neu hiam?

records.english: My wife always says, "We're a team, not two separate players."
records.zomi: Ka zi in, “Pawl khat i hi a, kimawl mi tuam nih i hi kei hi,” a ci tawntung hi.

records.english: Before we got engaged, my husband asked my father for permission.
records.zomi: I kiciam ma-in ka pasal in ka pa kiangah phalna a ngen hi.
