records.english: My husband says I'm too strict with the kids, and maybe he's right.
records.zomi: Naupangte tungah ka khauh lua hi, ci-in ka pasal in a gen a, a dik kha ding hi.

records.english: Our neighbors adopted a little girl last year, and she already feels like part of the whole street.
records.zomi: I inn vengte in kum bei-in naupang nu khat a kila uh a, lampi bup' mi khat bang a suak khin hi.

records.english: Our teenage daughter asked whether she could dye her hair blue for the summer.
records.zomi: I tanu khangno in khuakhal adingin a sam dum tawh a zai thei ding hiam hong dong hi.

records.english: We were warned that the second baby would change everything, and it did.
records.zomi: Ta nihna in na khempeuh a laih ding hi, ci-in hong kidopsak uh a, a laih taktak hi.

records.english: Our son keeps asking when he'll be old enough to drive.
records.zomi: I tapa in bang ciangin mawtaw mawng thei dingin a lian ding hiam a dong tawntung hi.

records.english: Would you ever let your teenage son travel abroad alone?
records.zomi: Na tapa khangno amah bek in gamdang ah khualzin na phal ding hiam?

records.english: Is it all right if the children stay up late to watch the fireworks?
records.zomi: Meiphual et dingin naupangte zan sawt takin om uh leh a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: Of course, as long as they have a nap in the afternoon.
records.zomi: Hoih hi, sun lam ah a ihmut uh leh.

records.english: Grandma says we're too soft with the kids, but she's even softer with them.
records.zomi: Pi in naupangte tungah i nem lua hi, a ci a, ahi zongin amah i sangin a nem zaw hi.

records.english: My husband and I promised each other we'd always eat dinner together, however busy we are.
records.zomi: Ka pasal leh kei bangzah buai zongin nitak an ne khawm den ding i kiciam hi.

records.english: How did your parents react when you told them you were getting married?
records.zomi: Na kiteen ding na gen ciangin na nu leh pa in bangci a dawng uh hiam?

records.english: My father was quiet at first, but my mother cried with happiness.
records.zomi: A masa-in ka pa a dai a, ahi zongin ka nu lungdam takin a kap hi.

records.english: Nobody in our house is allowed to hit, not even when they're angry.
records.zomi: I inn ah heh ciangin zong kuamah kisat phal lo hi.

records.english: Twenty years of marriage have taught me to listen before I answer.
records.zomi: Kum sawmnih kiteenna in ka dawn ma-in ngai dingin hong hilh hi.

records.english: My wife's parents moved in with us after the baby was born, which was a big help.
records.zomi: Naungek a suah khit ciangin ka zi' nu leh pa i kiangah a hong teeng uh a, huhna lianpi ahi hi.

records.english: Our daughter made us breakfast for our anniversary, and the kitchen was a complete mess afterward.
records.zomi: I kiteenna kum ni adingin i tanu in zingsang an hong bawl sak a, a nung ciangin anbuk a buai bup hi.

records.english: Can you pick the kids up today, since I have a meeting until six?
records.zomi: Nai guk dong kikhopna ka nei ahih manin tuni naupangte na la thei ding hiam?

records.english: Can we let our daughter go on the school trip to the mountains?
records.zomi: I tanu mualte ah sang khualzinna ah i paisak thei ding hiam?

records.english: How much pocket money do you think the children should get?
records.zomi: Naupangte sum neu bangzah a ngah ding uh na ci hiam?

records.english: Sharing the cooking with my husband has given me time to study in the evenings.
records.zomi: Ka pasal tawh an huan i kihawm manin nitakin lai sin hun ka nei hi.

records.english: Our household runs smoothly only because everyone does their part.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh in a tawm ciat a sep manun i inn a pai hoih hi.

records.english: My father says that a boy who can't cook will go hungry one day.
records.zomi: An huan thei lo tapa ni khat ni-in a gil a kial ding hi, ci-in ka pa in a gen hi.

records.english: My sister pays the electricity bill for our mother every month.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu in kha simin i nu adingin meivak man a pia hi.

records.english: Could you sweep the porch for Grandma before she gets home?
records.zomi: Pi a tun ma-in inn mai na phiat sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Can you show me how to sew a button back on?
records.zomi: Button khui kik dan hong lak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Our dog chewed through the garden hose, so we had to buy a new one.
records.zomi: I ui in huan tui pipe a ngoih tan ahih manin a thak khat i lei kul hi.

records.english: The firewood was stacked under the roof so that it would stay dry.
records.zomi: A keu den nadingin meisi pen innkhum nuai ah kizom hi.

records.english: Why does the youngest always get the easiest jobs?
records.zomi: Bang hangin a neu pen in nasep baih pen a ngah tawntung hiam?

records.english: Who left the gate open and let the goats into the garden again?
records.zomi: Kongpi kua in a hon a, kelte huan sungah a lut kik sak hiam?

records.english: Shall we hire someone to help with the cleaning while you're recovering?
records.zomi: Na dam kik sungin siangsakna ah huh dingin mi khat i lak ding hiam?

records.english: When I was a child, my brothers and I fetched water from the spring before school.
records.zomi: Ka naupan lai-in ka sanggam pasalte leh kei sang i kah ma-un tuikhuk pan tui i khai uh hi.

records.english: Could you drop the rent money at the landlord's house on your way to work?
records.zomi: Na nasepna na pai laitakin inn man pen inn neipa' inn ah na koih sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Let the baby nap; we'll vacuum the living room later.
records.zomi: Naungek ihmu sak in; innsung khan a nung ciangin vacuum i bawl ding hi.

records.english: Ever since Dad hurt his back, my brothers have done the heavy lifting around the farm.
records.zomi: Pa in a nungzang a natsak pan ka sanggam pasalte in lo ah na gik khempeuh a sem uh hi.

records.english: The broken window in the children's room was finally replaced before winter.
records.zomi: Naupangte' khan a tawhkhawng kitan phalbi a tun ma-in a laih tawp hi.

records.english: Your room has to be tidy before your friends come over.
records.zomi: Na lawmte a hong pai ma-un na khan a siangtho ding hi.

records.english: Mom wrote each child's name next to a job on a small blackboard in the kitchen.
records.zomi: Nu in anbuk sung suanglaipi neu tungah naupang khat ciat min nasep khat kiangah a gelh hi.

records.english: Please remind your father to fix the leaking roof before the rains.
records.zomi: Guah a zuk ma-in innkhum a zui phuah dingin na pa phawksak in.

records.english: My son walks the dog every morning before school, without being reminded.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in kuamah in phawksak lo-in sang kah ma-in zingsang simin ui a vakpih hi.

records.english: I really do appreciate everything you do for this family.
records.zomi: Hih innkuan adingin na sepna khempeuh ka lungdam taktak hi.

records.english: My husband built shelves in the pantry so that we could store more food.
records.zomi: An tam zaw i koih theih nadingin ka pasal in an kholna khan ah dawhte a bawl hi.

records.english: Is it my turn to cook tonight?
records.zomi: Tu zanin an huan ka khawl hi hiam?

records.english: No, it's your brother's — you cooked last night.
records.zomi: Hi lo hi, na sanggam pasal' khawl ahi hi — zan in nang na huan hi.

records.english: My wife handles the money, and I handle the repairs.
records.zomi: Ka zi in sum a kem a, kei in phuahnate ka sem hi.

records.english: Grandpa still chops the wood himself, even though we've asked him to let us help.
records.zomi: I huh dingin i ngen khin hangin Pu in meisi amah mah in a sat lai hi.

records.english: My daughter washes her grandfather's clothes because his hands are too stiff now.
records.zomi: Ka pu' khut a khauh lua khin ahih manin ka tanu in a puante a sawp sak hi.

records.english: In our home, homework has to be cleared off the table before dinner is served.
records.zomi: I inn ah nitak an kipiak ma-in innlai dawhkan tung pan kila ding hi.

records.english: My husband irons all the school uniforms on Sunday night.
records.zomi: Ka pasal in Nipini zan ciangin sang puan khempeuh a meitut hi.

records.english: The goat got into the vegetable garden and ate half the cabbages.
records.zomi: Kel in anteh huan sungah a lut a, kaubi a lang a ne hi.

records.english: My daughter feeds the fish every morning and tells them about her day.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in zingsang simin ngate an a vak a, a ni sung thu a gen sak hi.

records.english: Kids, the dog needs fresh water — who's going to fill her bowl?
records.zomi: Naupangte, ui in tui thak a kisam hi — kua in a kuang a dimsak ding hiam?

records.english: "If everyone does a little, nobody has to do a lot," Dad likes to say.
records.zomi: “Mi khempeuh in tawmno a sep leh kuamah in tampi a sem kul kei hi,” ci-in Pa in a gen ding a deih hi.

records.english: Leaving the chores until Sunday night always ends in an argument.
records.zomi: Inn nasepte Nipini zan dong i nusiat leh kinialna tawh a bei tawntung hi.

records.english: How do you get teenagers to help without nagging?
records.zomi: Khangnote ngen-ngen lo-in bangci na huhsak hiam?

records.english: We give them one big job each and let them choose when to do it.
records.zomi: Nasep lian khat ciat i pia a, bang ciangin sem ding hiam amaute in a teel uh hi.

records.english: Before Christmas, every member of the family has a cleaning job, even the youngest.
records.zomi: Christmas ma-in innkuan mi khempeuh in siangsakna nasep khat ciat a nei uh hi, a neu pen zong.

records.english: Who will feed the cat while we're at the wedding?
records.zomi: Kiteenna ah i om sungin zawhngeu kua in an a vak ding hiam?

records.english: The vegetable garden was flattened by heavy rain, so we had to replant everything.
records.zomi: Guah nasia in anteh huan a siatsak bup ahih manin na khempeuh i suan kik kul hi.

records.english: As the oldest daughter, I was expected to cook for my younger brothers every evening.
records.zomi: Ta numei upa pen ka hih manin nitak simin ka nau pasalte adingin an ka huan ding kilamen hi.

records.english: Two of the chickens were taken by a fox during the night.
records.zomi: Zanin sial-ngal in akte nih a la hi.

records.english: Is it fair that my brother never has to help in the kitchen?
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in anbuk ah a huh kul ngei loh a dik hiam?

records.english: Everyone should help, boys and girls alike.
records.zomi: Tapa leh tanu kibangin mi khempeuh in a huh ding uh hi.

records.english: Every Saturday, my brother washes the car for our elderly neighbor.
records.zomi: Kiginni simin ka sanggam pasal in i inn veng upa' mawtaw a sil sak hi.

records.english: Grandma refuses to let anyone else make her tea.
records.zomi: Pi in amah' niangtui mi dang a bawlsak ding a nial hi.

records.english: The roof gutters are cleaned every autumn so that rainwater doesn't overflow.
records.zomi: Guahtui a lumleh loh nadingin kumphal simin innkhum tui luanna siangsak hi.

records.english: What chores do your children do at home?
records.zomi: Na tate in inn ah inn nasep bang a sem uh hiam?

records.english: The older ones wash the dishes, and the youngest puts away the spoons.
records.zomi: A upa zawte in kuangte a sawp uh a, a neu pen in sikkeute a koih hi.

records.english: Please put your shoes on the rack instead of leaving them on the stairs.
records.zomi: Na khedap kahlei tungah nusia lo-in a koihna ah koih in.

records.english: Can I do my chores after the football match?
records.zomi: Football kimawlna khit ciangin ka inn nasepte ka sem thei ding hiam?

records.english: Only if you promise to finish them before bedtime.
records.zomi: Lup hun ma-in na zawh ding na kiciam leh bek.

records.english: Shall I feed the animals, or would you rather I started on the dishes?
records.zomi: Ganhingte an ka vak ding hiam, kuangte sawp ka kipat na deih zaw hiam?

records.english: Please don't leave wet towels on the bed.
records.zomi: Puan keusakna a diak lupna tungah nusia kei in.

records.english: Paying the bills on time is my job, and I take it seriously.
records.zomi: Man piak dingte hun takah piak pen ka nasep ahi a, thupi takin ka sem hi.

records.english: When I was little, my job was to collect the eggs every morning.
records.zomi: Ka neu lai-in ka nasep pen zingsang simin aktuite kaikhawm ahi hi.

records.english: Who's in charge of feeding the chickens this week?
records.zomi: Tu kal sungin ak an vak kua in a mawhpuak hiam?

records.english: My grandfather says he learned more from farm work than from any school.
records.zomi: Ka pu in sang khatpeuh sangin lo nasep pan tam zaw a sin hi, a ci hi.

records.english: It's a small house, but keeping it clean with four children is a full-time job.
records.zomi: Inn neu ahi hi, ahi zongin ta li tawh siangtho taka kem pen ni bup nasep ahi hi.

records.english: My mother-in-law taught me how to keep the rice store free of insects.
records.zomi: Ka sungnu in buh kholna ah lawkhal om lo dinga kem dan hong hilh hi.

records.english: Our neighbor's son helps us carry water when the pump breaks down.
records.zomi: Tui pump a siat ciangin i inn veng' tapa in tui puak dingin hong huh hi.

records.english: What do you think about your sister marrying someone from another country?
records.zomi: Na sanggam nu in gam dang mi khat a teenpih ding thu bang na ci hiam?

records.english: My cousin's decision to move abroad was discussed by the whole family.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam' gamdang a pem ding khensatna innkuan bup in a kikum uh hi.

records.english: "Whatever you decide, we'll support you," my parents told me when I left my job.
records.zomi: Ka nasep ka khawl ciangin, “Bang na khensat zongin kong huh ding uh hi,” ci-in ka nu leh pa in hong gen uh hi.

records.english: My grandparents made every important decision together, and they always told us why.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh ka pi in khensatna thupi khempeuh a bawl khawm uh a, bang hang hiam hong gen tawntung uh hi.

records.english: He's kind, but I'm not sure he's ready to be a husband.
records.zomi: Amah a hehpih hi, ahi zongin pasal hih dingin a kigingsak hiam ka thei ciang kei hi.

records.english: Are you sure your parents agree with your plan?
records.zomi: Na nu leh pa in na ngaihsutna a lungkim uh cih na thei ciang hiam?

records.english: Mention the new job to your mother only after she's had her lunch.
records.zomi: Na nu in sun an a nek khit ciang bekin nasep thak thu gen in.

records.english: My uncle feels strongly that the family land should never be sold.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in innkuan gam zuak ngei lo ding hi, ci-in a lungsim khauh takin a ngaihsun hi.

records.english: My wife and I agreed early on to discuss every big purchase together.
records.zomi: Ka zi leh kei a masa-in lei lianpi khempeuh kikum khawm dingin i kituak hi.

records.english: We had a long family talk about respecting each other's privacy.
records.zomi: Khat leh khat' mimal thu zahtak thu innkuan in sawtpi i kikum hi.

records.english: My grandmother insisted that every grandchild should learn to speak our home language.
records.zomi: Ka pi in tu khempeuh in i inn pau a sin ding a ngen ngiat hi.

records.english: My brothers and I disagree about whether to keep our father's old shop.
records.zomi: Ka pa' dawl lui i kem ding hiam cih thu ah ka sanggam pasalte leh kei i kituak kei hi.

records.english: We kept the plans for Dad's surprise party secret for three weeks.
records.zomi: Pa' thakhat poai ngaihsutnate kal thum sung i sel hi.

records.english: Can we talk about something without anyone getting upset?
records.zomi: Kuamah lungkia lo-in thu khat i kikum thei ding hiam?

records.english: What would you do if your son wanted to marry someone you didn't approve of?
records.zomi: Na tapa in na lungkim loh mi khat a teenpih nop leh bang na sem ding hiam?

records.english: Listen to your brother's side before you decide who's right.
records.zomi: Kua a dik hiam na khensat ma-in na sanggam pasal' lam ngai in.

records.english: Should we let the children help choose which school they go to?
records.zomi: Sang bang ah kah ding hiam naupangte i teel sak ding hiam?

records.english: Could you explain to your brother why the trip has been canceled?
records.zomi: Bang hangin khualzinna kiphiat hiam na sanggam pasal na hilhcian thei ding hiam?

records.english: When my brother announced he was becoming a priest, the whole family was surprised.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in siampi a suak ding a gen ciangin innkuan bup lamdang a sa uh hi.

records.english: Please keep this between us until I've spoken to my husband.
records.zomi: Ka pasal tawh ka kiho ma-in hih thu i kikal ah koih in.

records.english: At Grandpa's house, family meetings always begin with a prayer and end with a meal.
records.zomi: Pu' inn ah innkuan kikhopna thungetna tawh a kipan a, an nek tawh a bei tawntung hi.

records.english: We talked late into the night about which of us would look after Grandma when she can no longer live alone.
records.zomi: Pi amah bek a teen theih nawn loh ciangin i lak pan kua in a kem ding hiam zan sawt dong i kikum hi.

records.english: My parents were worried when I said I wanted to join the army.
records.zomi: Galkap suak ka nuam hi, ka cih ciangin ka nu leh pa a lungkham uh hi.

records.english: Tell me honestly what you think of him.
records.zomi: Amah tungah bang na ngaihsun hiam thuman takin hong gen in.

records.english: Is it a good idea to lend money to relatives?
records.zomi: Beh leh phungte sum leitawi sak a hoih hiam?

records.english: To avoid hurt feelings, we agreed that everyone would get one piece of Grandma's jewelry.
records.zomi: Lungsim natna a om loh nadingin mi khempeuh in Pi' kizemna khat ciat a ngah ding i kituak hi.

records.english: Have you told your parents that you want to study art instead of medicine?
records.zomi: Siavuan sinna sangin lim gelh sin na deih hi, ci-in na nu leh pa na gen khin hiam?

records.english: Not yet — I'm waiting for the right moment.
records.zomi: Gen nai kei hi — hun kilawm ka ngak hi.

records.english: My sister was hurt that she wasn't asked for her opinion about the wedding plans.
records.zomi: Kiteenna ngaihsutna ah a ngaihsutna kidong lo ahih manin ka sanggam nu' lungsim a na hi.

records.english: My father rarely talks about his childhood, so I was amazed when he told us about the war.
records.zomi: Ka pa in a naupan lai thu a gen tawm ahih manin gal thu hong gen ciangin ka lamdang mahmah hi.

records.english: It was a hard conversation, but I'm glad we finally had it.
records.zomi: Kikupna haksa ahi hi, ahi zongin i kikup tawp ahih manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: Mom and Dad sat us down to explain why we were moving to the city.
records.zomi: Nu leh Pa in bang hangin khuapi ah i pem ding hiam hilhcian dingin hong tusak uh hi.

records.english: How do you talk to teenagers about money?
records.zomi: Khangnote tawh sum thu bangci na kiho hiam?

records.english: Honestly and early, before they start earning their own.
records.zomi: Thuman takin leh a tuungin, amau sum a ngah ma-un.

records.english: The family Bible was opened, and Grandpa read us the names of our ancestors.
records.zomi: Innkuan Laisiangtho kihon a, Pu in i pu i pute min hong sim sak hi.

records.english: Grandpa gathered us all in the living room and said, "There's something you need to know about our family."
records.zomi: Pu in innsung khan ah i khempeuh hong kaikhawm a, “I innkuan thu khat na theih ding uh kisam hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: Whose idea was it to sell the car without asking me?
records.zomi: Hong dong lo-in mawtaw zuak ding kua' ngaihsutna hiam?

records.english: Why didn't anyone tell me Uncle Pau was sick?
records.zomi: Pu Pau a dam lo hi, ci bang hangin kuamah in hong gen lo hiam?

records.english: We didn't want to worry you while you were taking your exams.
records.zomi: Na sitna na et laitakin hong lungkhamsak i deih kei hi.

records.english: Our family meets once a year to decide how the rice fields will be shared.
records.zomi: Buh lote bangci kihawm ding hiam khensat dingin i innkuan kum simin vei khat a kikhawm hi.

records.english: Kids, from now on, big decisions about the family will be made together.
records.zomi: Naupangte, tu pan kipanin innkuan thu khensatna lianpite i khawm-in i bawl ding hi.

records.english: Please listen to the whole plan before you say no.
records.zomi: Na nial ma-in ngaihsutna bup ngai masa in.

records.english: Why don't we give everyone two minutes to say what they think?
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh in a ngaihsutna gen dingin minit nih ciat bang hangin i pia lo ding hiam?

records.english: Would you be upset if I spent Christmas with my wife's family this year?
records.zomi: Tu kum Christmas ka zi' innkuan tawh ka zat leh na lungkia ding hiam?

records.english: A little, but I understand — you can come to us for New Year instead.
records.zomi: Tawmno, ahi zongin ka thei hi — Kum Thak ciangin hong pai thei hi.

records.english: The engagement was announced at dinner, and everyone started talking at once.
records.zomi: Nitak an laitakin kiciamna kiphuang a, mi khempeuh in khatvei-in a gen pan uh hi.

records.english: Could we talk about this tomorrow, when we're both calmer?
records.zomi: I nih in i lungsim a nem zawh zingciang ciangin hih thu i kikum thei ding hiam?

records.english: Next time, let's all sit down together before anyone makes a decision.
records.zomi: A zom ciangin kuamah a khensat ma-in i khempeuh tu khawm masa ni.

records.english: Talking about our grandfather's illness openly helped the children understand it.
records.zomi: I pu' natna thu kiphawng takin i kikup manin naupangte in a thei uh hi.

records.english: The question of who would inherit the house was never really settled.
records.zomi: Inn kua in a luah ding hiam thu kibawlsiam taktak ngei lo hi.

records.english: What did your family decide about the old farmhouse?
records.zomi: Lo inn lui thu ah na innkuan in bang a khensat uh hiam?

records.english: We're going to repair it and spend our summers there.
records.zomi: I phuah ding a, i khuakhal hunte tua munah i zang ding hi.

records.english: How should we tell Grandpa that we're selling his old house?
records.zomi: Pu' inn lui i zuak ding thu bangci i gen ding hiam?

records.english: Gently, and with the whole family there to support him.
records.zomi: Nem takin, amah huh dingin innkuan bup om khawm-in.

records.english: Is there anything you want to ask before we finish?
records.zomi: I zawh ma-in na dot nop bangmah a om hiam?

records.english: We all cried when Mom read out the letter Grandpa had written before he died.
records.zomi: Pu in a sih ma-a a gelh lai Nu in a sim ciangin i khempeuh i kap hi.

records.english: I'm not angry, just disappointed that you didn't trust me.
records.zomi: Ka heh kei hi, hong muan lo na hih manin ka lungkia bek hi.

records.english: Our family chat exploded with messages when my sister shared her baby news.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu in a naungek thu a hawm ciangin i innkuan chat ah thu tampi mahmah a lut hi.

records.english: My father finally admitted that he had been wrong about my career.
records.zomi: Ka nasep thu ah a khial hi, ci-in ka pa in a pom tawp hi.

records.english: The argument about the inheritance damaged the relationship between my aunts for years.
records.zomi: Gamluah thu kinialna in kum tampi sung ka nite kikal kizopna a siatsak hi.

records.english: Every evening, my daughter brushes her grandmother's hair before bed.
records.zomi: Nitak simin ka tanu in a lup ma-in a pi' sam a khui sak hi.

records.english: What happens to the children on days when both of you work late?
records.zomi: Na nih in zekai-in na sep ni ciangin naupangte bangci om uh hiam?

records.english: My aunt fetches them from school and gives them dinner until we get home.
records.zomi: Ka ni in sang pan a la a, i tun dong nitak an a pia hi.

records.english: Kids, be gentle with Grandpa — his back is very sore today.
records.zomi: Naupangte, Pu tungah nem takin om un — tuni a nungzang a na mahmah hi.

records.english: Grandpa insists on doing his own shopping, so we walk with him to the market.
records.zomi: Pu in amah' an amah mah in lei ding a ngen ngiat ahih manin zuakna mun ah amah tawh i kaai hi.

records.english: Our neighbor is raising her three grandchildren while their parents work in the city.
records.zomi: A nu leh pa uh khuapi ah na a sep laitakun i inn veng nu in a tu thumte a khoi hi.

records.english: Please speak slowly and kindly to Grandma; she gets frightened when people rush her.
records.zomi: Pi tungah zawlzawl leh nem takin gen un; mite in a kinsak ciangun a lau hi.

records.english: "You took care of me, and now it's my turn," I told my father when he moved in with us.
records.zomi: Ka pa i kiangah a hong teen ciangin, “Hong khoi hi, tu-in ka khawl ahi hi,” ci-in ka gen hi.

records.english: Is your father still living with your brother?
records.zomi: Na pa na sanggam pasal tawh a teeng lai hiam?

records.english: No, he's moved into a care home near the hospital.
records.zomi: Hi lo hi, zato kiang upate kepna inn ah a pem khin hi.

records.english: Our neighbor's daughter cooks extra food and brings it to her elderly parents every night.
records.zomi: I inn veng' tanu in an behlap a huan a, zan simin a nu leh pa upate kiangah a tawi hi.

records.english: Why is the baby so quiet today?
records.zomi: Bang hangin naungek tuni a dai mahmah hiam?

records.english: She's probably just tired after her vaccinations.
records.zomi: A sawpna khit ciangin a gim bek kha ding hi.

records.english: The old family photos were brought out to help Grandpa remember his younger years.
records.zomi: Pu in a khangno lai kumte a phawk nadingin innkuan limlak luite kila khia hi.

records.english: My brother and I share the cost of our mother's care.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal leh kei i nu' kemna man i kihawm hi.

records.english: Please, Grandpa, let me carry the water — it's too heavy for you.
records.zomi: Pu, tui hong puak sak ning — nang adingin a gik lua hi.

records.english: My husband built a ramp at the front door so that his father's wheelchair could get in.
records.zomi: Ka pasal in a pa' wheelchair a lut theih nadingin mai lam kongkhak ah lampi khiahna a bawl hi.

records.english: Families in our church organize a rota to bring meals to members who are sick.
records.zomi: I pawlpi a innkuante in a dam lo memberte an tawi dingin a kilaih uh hi.

records.english: What's the hardest part of caring for twins?
records.zomi: Apengte kem ah a haksa pen bang hiam?

records.english: Getting them both to sleep at the same time!
records.zomi: A nih un khatvei-in ihmusak!

records.english: Is it normal for Dad to get confused in the evenings?
records.zomi: Pa nitak ciangin a lungbuai pen a pangai hiam?

records.english: His doctor said it can happen with his condition and that a calm routine helps.
records.zomi: A natna tawh tua bang a piang thei a, lungsim nem taka nuntak dan kician in a huh hi, ci-in a siavuan in a gen hi.

records.english: Some weeks, I barely have time to sleep between the baby and my father's appointments.
records.zomi: Kal pawlkhat ciangin naungek leh ka pa' siavuan muhna kikal ah ihmut hun ka nei dek kei hi.

records.english: Our daughter was frightened when her grandfather was taken to the hospital in an ambulance.
records.zomi: A pu zato ah ambulance tawh kipuak ciangin i tanu a lau hi.

records.english: "Thank you for not forgetting me," my grandfather whispered when I visited.
records.zomi: Ka va veh ciangin, “Hong mangngilh lo na hih manin ka lungdam hi,” ci-in ka pu in a gen ciauciau hi.

records.english: Do you think it's time for Mom to stop driving?
records.zomi: Nu in mawtaw mawng a khawl hun a tung khin na ci hiam?

records.english: She had a small accident last month, so maybe it is.
records.zomi: Kha bei-in kituakna neu khat a nei ahih manin a tung kha ding hi.

records.english: Caring for my mother taught my teenage son more patience than any lesson at school.
records.zomi: Ka nu ka kem in ka tapa khangno sang sinna khatpeuh sangin thuakzawhna tam zaw a hilh hi.

records.english: Shall we hire a nurse for a few hours a day so that you can rest?
records.zomi: Na tawlnga theih nadingin ni simin nai tawmno sung nurse khat i lak ding hiam?

records.english: Grandma sometimes forgets my name, but she never forgets to ask whether I've eaten.
records.zomi: Pi in ka min a mangngilh ngei hi, ahi zongin an ka ne khin hiam dong ding a mangngilh ngei kei hi.

records.english: We do our best, but some days caring for everyone is really hard.
records.zomi: I hanciam zah i hanciam hi, ahi zongin ni pawlkhat ciangin mi khempeuh kem a haksa taktak hi.

records.english: Grandpa lost his glasses in the garden, and the children spent an hour searching for them.
records.zomi: Pu in huan sungah a mitlimlang a mansuah a, naupangte in nai khat sung a zong uh hi.

records.english: Visiting my grandparents every weekend is something I'll never regret.
records.zomi: Kal bei simin ka pu leh ka pi va veh pen ka lungkham ngei lo ding na khat ahi hi.

records.english: Grandpa's hospital bed was delivered this morning, and we set it up in the living room.
records.zomi: Tu zingsangin Pu' zato lupna hong tung a, innsung khan ah i bawl hi.

records.english: My children read to their great-grandmother every Sunday because her eyesight is poor.
records.zomi: Ka tate in a pi' nu' mit a hoih kei ahih manin Nipini simin lai a sim sak uh hi.

records.english: Bathing a newborn for the first time made me very nervous.
records.zomi: Naungek thak a masa pen-a ka kisilsak ciangin ka lau mahmah hi.

records.english: We moved back to the village so that our children could grow up near their grandparents.
records.zomi: I tate a pu leh pite uh kiang ah a khan theih nadingun khua ah i pem kik hi.

records.english: My sister lives closer, so she takes Mom to the doctor, and I handle the paperwork.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu a naih zaw ahih manin Nu siavuan kiangah a paipih a, kei in laite ka bawl hi.

records.english: My son was born early and had to stay in the hospital for three weeks.
records.zomi: Ka tapa a tuungin a suak a, kal thum sung zato ah a om kul hi.

records.english: Grandma likes to tell the children, "Respect your elders, and they will bless you."
records.zomi: Pi in naupangte kiangah, “Upate zahtak un, thupha hong pia ding uh hi,” ci a deih hi.

records.english: Our two-year-old fell off the sofa and bumped his head, but he's fine now.
records.zomi: I ta kum nih sofa pan a kiak a, a lu a kitawng hi, ahi zongin tu-in a dam hi.

records.english: Is there anything we can do to make Grandma's room more comfortable?
records.zomi: Pi' khan a nuam zaw nadingin bangmah i bawl thei ding a om hiam?

records.english: Maybe a softer mattress and a lamp she can switch on from bed.
records.zomi: Lupna nem zaw khat leh lupna tung pan a phel theih meivak khat kha ding hi.

records.english: The children made a "get well" card for their grandmother after her operation.
records.zomi: A pi' zato nasepna khit ciangin naupangte in “dam pah in” card khat a bawl uh hi.

records.english: Our toddler's favorite blanket was left at the park, and he cried all night.
records.zomi: I naupang neu' puan deih pen park ah kinusia a, zan bup a kap hi.

records.english: My wife left her job to stay home with our son, who has special needs.
records.zomi: Kepna tuam a kisam i tapa tawh inn ah om dingin ka zi in a nasep a khawl hi.

records.english: How is your mother managing on her own since your father passed away?
records.zomi: Na pa a sih nungin na nu amah bek in bangci om hiam?

records.english: She's lonely, so my sister and I visit her on alternate days.
records.zomi: A lungngai ahih manin ka sanggam nu leh kei ni khat kal ciat in ka va veh uh hi.

records.english: Since the doctor adjusted her diet, Grandma has had much more energy.
records.zomi: Siavuan in a an nek dan a laih pan Pi in tha tam zaw a nei hi.

records.english: I really do want my kids to grow up close to their grandparents.
records.zomi: Ka tate a pu leh pite uh tawh kinai takin a khan ding uh ka deih taktak hi.

records.english: My parents looked after my grandparents, and now I hope to do the same for them.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh pa in ka pu leh ka pite a kem uh a, tu-in kei zong amaute adingin tua bangin ka bawl ding ka lamen hi.

records.english: The baby was vaccinated at the clinic this morning and has been sleepy ever since.
records.zomi: Tu zingsangin naungek clinic ah sawpna a ngah a, tua pan a ihmu ngai den hi.

records.english: I sometimes feel guilty that I can't visit my parents more often.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh pa tam zawin ka va veh theih loh manin ka lungsim a nuam kei ngei hi.

records.english: How do you calm your daughter when she wakes up from a nightmare?
records.zomi: Mang sia pan na tanu a khanglo ciangin bangci na lungmuansak hiam?

records.english: I hold her and sing until she falls back asleep.
records.zomi: Ka pom a, a ihmut kik dong la ka sak hi.

records.english: Could you remind your grandmother to take her evening pills?
records.zomi: Na pi in a nitak zatui a nek nadingin na phawksak thei ding hiam?

records.english: My mother-in-law cared for our baby while I went back to work.
records.zomi: Nasep ah ka ciah kik laitakin ka sungnu in i naungek a kem hi.

records.english: Can I help you with your shoes, Grandpa?
records.zomi: Pu, na khedap ah kong huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Could you sit with Grandpa this afternoon while I take the baby to the clinic?
records.zomi: Naungek clinic ah ka paipih laitakin tu sun Pu kiangah na tu thei ding hiam?

records.english: Who looks after you while you're busy looking after everyone else?
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh na kem laitakin nang kua in hong kem hiam?

records.english: It's hard to get my husband out of bed on Mondays.
records.zomi: Pizing ni ciangin ka pasal lupna pan thosak a haksa hi.

records.english: The kitchen smells of fried eggs and coffee every morning.
records.zomi: Zingsang simin anbuk sungah aktui kikang leh kawfi gim a nam hi.

records.english: Our cat sits on my chest every morning until I get up to feed her.
records.zomi: An ka vak dinga ka thoh dong ka zawhngeu zingsang simin ka awm tungah a tu hi.

records.english: The children were hurried into the car without their breakfast.
records.zomi: Naupangte zingsang an ne lo-in mawtaw sungah kikinsak hi.

records.english: How does your family manage with only one bathroom?
records.zomi: Kisilna inn khat bek tawh na innkuan bangci na om uh hiam?

records.english: We have a schedule: the kids go first, then my husband, then me.
records.zomi: Hun ciamteh i nei hi: naupangte masa a, tua khit ciangin ka pasal, tua khit ciangin kei.

records.english: Before we leave the house, Dad likes the whole family to stand together for a short prayer.
records.zomi: Inn i paisan ma-in Pa in innkuan bup in thungetna tomno adingin i din khawm ding a deih hi.

records.english: Hold still while I tie your shoelaces.
records.zomi: Na khedap khau ka khih laitakin ding den in.

records.english: Our son's shoes were soaked from yesterday's rain, so he had to wear his sandals.
records.zomi: Zan a guah in i tapa' khedap a diak ahih manin a khedap neu a silh kul hi.

records.english: Good luck at school today, sweetheart!
records.zomi: Ka it, tuni sang ah hoih takin om in!

records.english: My husband reads the headlines to me while I pack the children's bags.
records.zomi: Naupangte' ip ka koih laitakin ka pasal in thuthak lutangte hong sim sak hi.

records.english: My little brother puts his shoes on the wrong feet almost every morning.
records.zomi: Ka nau pasal in zingsang tampi ah a khedap a khial-in a silh hi.

records.english: Can I wear my new dress to school today?
records.zomi: Tuni sang ah ka puan thak ka silh thei ding hiam?

records.english: It's a bit cold for that — how about your blue sweater instead?
records.zomi: Tua adingin a vot deuh hi — na sweater dum bang ci ding hiam?

records.english: Getting the baby ready takes longer than getting myself ready.
records.zomi: Naungek kigingsak pen keimah kigingsak sangin a sawt zaw hi.

records.english: My grandmother sweeps the yard every morning before anyone else is awake.
records.zomi: Ka pi in kuamah a khanglo ma-un zingsang simin inntual a phiat hi.

records.english: Weekends are the only mornings when our whole family eats breakfast together.
records.zomi: Kal bei pen i innkuan bup zingsang an ne khawm theih zingsang bek ahi hi.

records.english: My teenage son pulls the blanket over his head every time I open his curtains.
records.zomi: A puan khaite ka hon simin ka tapa khangno in puan a lu tungah a khuh hi.

records.english: The power went off overnight, so we washed with water heated on the gas stove.
records.zomi: Zanin meivak a mang ahih manin gas meibuk tungah tui i lumsak a, i kisil hi.

records.english: Do your children walk to school by themselves now?
records.zomi: Tu-in na tate amau bek in sang ah a kaai uh hiam?

records.english: We keep the children's uniforms on hooks by the door so that nobody has to search for them.
records.zomi: Kuamah in a zon kul loh nadingin naupangte' sang puante kongkhak kiang khaina ah i khai hi.

records.english: My son's school bag was so heavy that I made him take out half the books.
records.zomi: Ka tapa' sang ip a gik lua ahih manin laibu a lang ka lasak hi.

records.english: Waking up in my parents' house always makes me feel like a child again.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh pa' inn ah ka khanglo ciangin naupang bang ka kisa kik tawntung hi.

records.english: Mom used to wake us up by singing in the kitchen.
records.zomi: Nu in anbuk sungah la sa-in hong phawng ngei hi.

records.english: With six of us and only one bathroom, mornings are a race.
records.zomi: Mi guk leh kisilna inn khat bek ahih manin zingsang hun kitai bang ahi hi.

records.english: Could you help your sister find her other shoe?
records.zomi: Na sanggam nu' khedap khat a zon nadingin na huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: I'm trying to teach my son to get himself ready without my help.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in ka huhna om lo-in amah le amah a kigingsak nadingin ka hilh hi.

records.english: We all brush our teeth at the same time, crowded around one small sink.
records.zomi: I khempeuh tui kholna neu khat kiim ah kibelh-in khatvei-in i ha i nawt hi.

records.english: Mom always checks our school bags so that we don't forget anything.
records.zomi: Bangmah i mangngilh loh nadingin Nu in i sang ipte a en tawntung hi.

records.english: Grandma always makes sure the children's jackets are zipped up before they leave.
records.zomi: Naupangte a pai ma-un a puan sil a kikhak hiam Pi in a en tawntung hi.

records.english: Every morning, my wife and I drink our tea on the porch before the children wake up.
records.zomi: Zingsang simin naupangte a khanglo ma-un ka zi leh kei inn mai ah niangtui i dawn hi.

records.english: I really do enjoy those quiet minutes before the rest of the family wakes up.
records.zomi: Innkuan a dang a khanglo ma-a tua minit dai neute ka deih taktak hi.

records.english: Since my mother started working nights, my older sister has been getting us ready for school.
records.zomi: Ka nu zanin nasem a pan pan ka u numei in sang adingin hong kigingsak sak hi.

records.english: Our daughter was so excited about her first day of school that she woke up at four.
records.zomi: I tanu in a sang kah ni masa pen a lamen lua ahih manin nai li ciangin a khanglo hi.

records.english: My daughter likes to choose her own clothes, even if they don't match.
records.zomi: A kituak kei zongin ka tanu in amah' puan teel a deih hi.

records.english: Kids, it's raining, so put on your boots and take your raincoats.
records.zomi: Naupangte, guah a zuk ahih manin na khedap sau uh silh unla, na guah puan uh tawi un.

records.english: Who's going to wake Grandma, since she asked to be up by seven?
records.zomi: Nai sagih ma-in thoh a ngen ahih manin Pi kua in a phawng ding hiam?

records.english: Why are you still in your pajamas?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na zan puan na silh lai hiam?

records.english: I couldn't find my school tie, so I'm waiting for Mom to iron my spare one.
records.zomi: Ka sang tie ka mu kei ahih manin a behlap pen Nu in a meitut ding ka ngak hi.

records.english: The baby woke the whole house at five, so we all had breakfast early.
records.zomi: Naungek in nai nga ciangin inn bup a phawng ahih manin i khempeuh in zingsang an a tuungin i ne hi.

records.english: Make sure your little brother eats his breakfast before you leave.
records.zomi: Na pai ma-in na nau pasal in a zingsang an a ne hiam en in.

records.english: My wife gets the baby dressed while I make the porridge.
records.zomi: Buh-an tui ka huan laitakin ka zi in naungek puan a silhsak hi.

records.english: "It's Saturday — let me sleep!" my daughter groaned when I opened her door.
records.zomi: Ka kongkhak ka hon ciangin, “Kiginni ahi hi — hong ihmusak in!” ci-in ka tanu a ham hi.

records.english: My sister spends ages in front of the mirror before she leaves the house.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu in inn a paisan ma-in mai-et mai ah sawtpi a om hi.

records.english: Our morning routine changed completely when my father moved in with us.
records.zomi: Ka pa i kiangah a hong teen ciangin i zingsang ngeina a kilai bup hi.

records.english: Have you washed your face and brushed your teeth?
records.zomi: Na maai na sil a, na ha na nawt khin hiam?

records.english: Can we have pancakes for breakfast tomorrow?
records.zomi: Zingciang zingsang an ah pancake i ne thei ding hiam?

records.english: Everyone, breakfast is on the table, and the bus leaves in fifteen minutes!
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, zingsang an dawhkan tungah om a, minit sawm leh nga sungin bus a pai ding hi!

records.english: Grandpa is always the first one up, and he has the kettle boiling by five.
records.zomi: Pu a tho masa pen tawntung a, nai nga ciangin kettle a lumsak khin hi.

records.english: Leave your homework by the front door so that you don't forget it tomorrow.
records.zomi: Zingciang na mangngilh loh nadingin na innlai mai lam kongkhak kiangah nusia in.

records.english: Is Dad driving us to school, or are we walking?
records.zomi: Pa in sang ah hong paipih ding hiam, i kaai ding hiam?

records.english: Dad's driving today because it's too cold to walk.
records.zomi: Kaai dingin a vot lua ahih manin tuni Pa in hong paipih ding hi.

records.english: Grandpa told me, "An early start makes a long day feel shorter."
records.zomi: Pu in, “A tuunga kipat in ni sau a tomsak hi,” hong ci hi.

records.english: On Saturdays, the kids are woken up by the smell of pancakes.
records.zomi: Kiginni ciangin naupangte pancake gim in a phawng hi.

records.english: Could you braid my hair before school, Mom?
records.zomi: Nu, sang ka kah ma-in ka sam hong khiah sak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Shall I make you a packed lunch, or will you buy something at school?
records.zomi: Sun an kong koih sak ding hiam, sang ah na lei ding hiam?

records.english: You all need to be in the car in five minutes — no excuses!
records.zomi: Minit nga sungin na khempeuh mawtaw sungah na om ding uh hi — hanglah om lo ding!

records.english: My father has worn the same watch every morning for thirty years.
records.zomi: Ka pa in kum sawmthum sung zingsang simin nai khat mah a bulh hi.

records.english: The baby's bottle was warmed while I changed her diaper.
records.zomi: Naungek' diaper ka laih laitakin a nawi um kilumsak hi.

records.english: My brother and I fought over the mirror every morning when we were teenagers.
records.zomi: Khangno i hih lai-in zingsang simin ka sanggam pasal leh kei mai-et tungah i kilai uh hi.

records.english: Did your mother teach you to cook, or did you learn on your own?
records.zomi: Na nu in an huan hong hilh hiam, nangmah in na sin hiam?

records.english: My father taught me, because Mom worked long hours at the hospital.
records.zomi: Nu zato ah hun sawtpi a sep manin ka pa in hong hilh hi.

records.english: Kids, set the table, and somebody please fill the water jug.
records.zomi: Naupangte, dawhkan bawl unla, kuamah in tui um dimsak un.

records.english: Hand me that bowl, please, and keep an eye on the onions.
records.zomi: Tua kuang hong pia inla, lothaang en den in.

records.english: We made too much food, so we sent the extra home with our guests.
records.zomi: An tam lua i bawl ahih manin a behlap pen i zinte tawh inn ah i khak hi.

records.english: I learned to cook out of necessity when I moved away for university.
records.zomi: Sangpi kah dinga ka pai ciangin a kisam manin an huan ka sin hi.

records.english: "Too much salt will ruin a good dish," Grandma warned as I reached for the jar.
records.zomi: “Cii tam lua in an hoih a siatsak ding hi,” ci-in cii um ka la ding laitakin Pi in hong kidopsak hi.

records.english: Is it true that your father does all the cooking in your house?
records.zomi: Na inn ah na pa in an a huan khempeuh, cih a dik hiam?

records.english: Yes, and he won't let anyone else near the stove!
records.zomi: Dik hi, a dang kuamah meibuk kiang a omsak kei hi!

records.english: My husband cooks on weekdays, and I cook on weekends.
records.zomi: Ka pasal in kal sung ni ciangin an a huan a, kei in kal bei ciangin ka huan hi.

records.english: Who's cooking tonight, you or me?
records.zomi: Tu zanin kua in an a huan ding hiam, nang hiam kei hiam?

records.english: After my father died, my mother didn't cook his favorite dishes for a long time.
records.zomi: Ka pa a sih nungin ka nu in sawtpi a an deihte a huan kei hi.

records.english: My husband says my cooking tastes just like his mother's, which is the best compliment he could give.
records.zomi: Ka an huan in a nu' huan bang a lim hi, ci-in ka pasal in a gen a, tua pen a piak theih phat hoih pen ahi hi.

records.english: The first meal I cooked for my husband was so salty that he drank three glasses of water.
records.zomi: Ka pasal adingin ka huan masak pen an a al lua ahih manin tui khuat thum a dawn hi.

records.english: Our Sunday curry cooks slowly all morning so that the meat becomes tender.
records.zomi: Sa a nem nadingin i Nipini curry zingsang bup zawlzawl in a min hi.

records.english: My daughter and I have our best conversations while chopping vegetables together.
records.zomi: Ka tanu leh kei anteh i sat khawm laitakin i kikupna hoih pen i nei hi.

records.english: Making dinner together has become our family's favorite part of the day.
records.zomi: Nitak an bawl khawm pen i innkuan' ni sung deih pen a suak hi.

records.english: Can I help stir?
records.zomi: Ka hel thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, but stand on the stool, and keep your hands away from the edge of the pan.
records.zomi: Thei hi, ahi zongin tutna neu tungah ding inla, na khut bel gei pan gamla takah koih in.

records.english: My mother always says, "Cook with love, and people will taste it."
records.zomi: Ka nu in, “Itna tawh huan in, mite in a lim thei ding uh hi,” a ci tawntung hi.

records.english: Could you write down your recipe for that pork curry so that I can make it at home?
records.zomi: Inn ah ka huan theih nadingin tua vok sa curry huan dan hong gelh sak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: The smell of my mother's cooking always means home to me.
records.zomi: Ka nu' an huan gim kei adingin inn cihna ahi tawntung hi.

records.english: What's your earliest memory of cooking?
records.zomi: An huan na phawk masak pen bang hiam?

records.english: Standing on a chair to stir my grandmother's porridge.
records.zomi: Ka pi' buh-an tui hel dingin tutna tungah ka ding hi.

records.english: Let the little ones decorate the biscuits; it keeps them busy.
records.zomi: Naupang neute in biscuit te zem uh hen; a buaisak hi.

records.english: We use my grandmother's old clay pot for cooking beans because it gives them a special flavor.
records.zomi: Be adingin lim tuam a piak manin ka pi' leibeel lui tawh be i huan hi.

records.english: My teenage son has started cooking dinner every Friday to give me a break.
records.zomi: Ka tapa khangno in ka tawlnga theih nadingin Laithai ni simin nitak an a huan pan hi.

records.english: Cooking for one is lonely, so I often invite my nephew for dinner.
records.zomi: Mi khat bek adingin an huan a lungngai huai ahih manin ka tanau nitak an ne dingin ka sam ngei hi.

records.english: Our family recipe book has notes from three generations of cooks.
records.zomi: I innkuan an huan dan laibu ah an huan mi suan thumte' gelhna a om hi.

records.english: Every Christmas, my aunts and I cook together for the whole extended family.
records.zomi: Christmas simin ka nite leh kei innkuan lian bup adingin an i huan khawm hi.

records.english: Use the sharp knife for the meat and the small one for the vegetables.
records.zomi: Sa adingin namsau hiam zang inla, anteh adingin a neu zang in.

records.english: I keep my grandmother's wooden spoon, even though it's cracked.
records.zomi: A kikhak hangin ka pi' sing sikkeu ka kem hi.

records.english: Who wants to taste the soup before I add the noodles?
records.zomi: An-tui ka koih ma-in an-tui kua in a tasa sin nuam hiam?

records.english: My brother is the only one in the family who can make perfect pancakes.
records.zomi: Pancake hoih tektek bawl thei innkuan sungah ka sanggam pasal bek ahi hi.

records.english: Please pass me the big ladle on the hook behind you.
records.zomi: Na nung lam khaina a om sikkeu lian hong pia in.

records.english: When I lived abroad, I tried for months to cook rice the way my mother does.
records.zomi: Gamdang ka teen lai-in ka nu' huan bangin an huan dingin kha tampi ka hanciam hi.

records.english: Is there a family dish you'd like to learn to make?
records.zomi: Huan dan na sin nop innkuan an khat a om hiam?

records.english: I'd love to learn Grandma's pickled cabbage, but she never measures anything.
records.zomi: Pi' kaubi kithuk ka sin nuam mahmah hi, ahi zongin bangmah a teh ngei kei hi.

records.english: We sent a pot of rice and stew next door when our neighbors' father was taken to the hospital.
records.zomi: I inn vengte' pa zato ah a kipuak ciangin inn kiang ah an leh sa kihuan beel khat i khak hi.

records.english: The noodles were made by hand, the way my grandparents used to make them.
records.zomi: An-tui pen ka pu leh ka pi' bawl bangin khut tawh kibawl hi.

records.english: The cake sank in the middle because I opened the oven door too early.
records.zomi: Oven kongkhak a tuung lua-in ka hon ahih manin cake a laizang a kia hi.

records.english: The power went out halfway through, so we finished cooking on the neighbors' gas stove.
records.zomi: A laitak ah meivak a mang ahih manin inn vengte' gas meibuk tungah an i huan zo hi.

records.english: My kids complain about vegetables, but they eat them happily when they've helped cook them.
records.zomi: Ka tate in anteh a phun uh hi, ahi zongin a huan khawm uh ciangin lungdam takin a ne uh hi.

records.english: When Grandma moved in, we rearranged the whole house so that her room was near the bathroom.

records.zomi: Innkuan mi khempeuh in a khedap uh adingin inn sung lampi ah dawh khat ciat a nei uh hi.

records.english: I really do want the house to be tidy before your parents come to stay.
records.zomi: Na nu leh pa a hong om ma-un inn a siangtho ding ka deih taktak hi.

records.zomi: Ka nu' koihnate ka siangsak in ka naupan lai phawkna tampi hong tun sak hi.

records.english: Every toy goes back in its box before bedtime — that's the rule in our house.

records.zomi: I khempeuh in i huh leh lui ah i pai theih nadingin siangsakna i zo thei ding hiam?

records.english: Your father wants all the boxes out of the hallway by tonight.
records.zomi: Na pa in tu zan ma-in inn sung lampi pan bawm khempeuh kila ding a deih hi.

records.english: A tidy home makes our family feel calmer.
records.zomi: Inn siangtho in i innkuan a lungsim nemsak hi.

records.english: Is there a better way to store all these blankets?

records.zomi: Naupangte in siangsakna kimawlna-in a bawl uh a, hun lang bek a la hi.

records.english: We put pictures on the drawers so that our toddler can find her own socks and shirts.
records.zomi: I naupang neu in amah' khetuk leh puan a muh theih nadingin dawh sungte ah lim i belh hi.

records.zomi: Naupangte' puan neu khinte na sanggamte adingin ip sungah khen dingin hong huh thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: My son tidied his room without being asked, and I nearly fainted from surprise.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in a ngen lo-in a khan a siangsak a, lamdang ka sak lua manin ka lip dek hi.

records.english: The baby's clothes were washed and folded weeks before she was born.
records.zomi: Naungek a suah ma-in kal tampi lai-in a puante kisawp-in kikhawh hi.

records.english: Grandma keeps her buttons sorted by color in old biscuit tins.

records.english: How often do you wash the children's bedding?
records.zomi: Naupangte' lupna puante bangzah vei na sawp hiam?

records.english: Is it okay to throw away the children's old drawings, or should we keep some?
records.zomi: Naupangte' lim gelh luite paikhiat a hoih hiam, pawlkhat i kem ding hiam?

records.english: Keep the ones with their names and dates, and take photos of the rest.
records.zomi: A min leh a ni a om te kem inla, a dangte limlak la in.

records.english: Could you hold the ladder while I clean the ceiling fan?
records.zomi: Inn tung fan ka siangsak laitakin kahlei hong len sak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Kids, whoever finds the most rubbish in the garden gets an extra sweet.

records.english: My mother taught me to fold shirts so neatly that they look brand new.

records.english: My aunt keeps her house so spotless that we're afraid to sit down.

records.english: There's a basket by the front door for gloves, hats, and scarves.

records.english: Can I keep this old box of letters from Mom and Dad?
records.zomi: Nu leh Pa' laikhak lui bawm hih ka kem thei ding hiam?

records.english: Of course — those are part of our family's history.
records.zomi: Thei hi — tua te i innkuan tangthu sung ahi hi.

records.english: Maybe we could give the old cot to your sister, since she's expecting.

records.english: My teenage daughter rearranges her bedroom every few months.

records.english: Could we turn the storage room into a study corner for the kids?

records.english: We could store the summer clothes in vacuum bags to save space.

records.zomi: I apengte khut kilen-in a ihmu lai uh hi.

records.english: Do you want the night light on or off?
records.zomi: Zan meivak na deih hiam, phel na deih hiam?

records.english: On, please — and could you check under the bed for monsters?
records.zomi: Hon den in — lupna nuai ah dawi a om hiam hong en sak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: The baby falls asleep fastest in the cloth sling on my back.
records.zomi: Naungek ka nung tung puan sungah a ihmut a manlang pen hi.

records.english: Every night before bed, my daughter and I talk about the best part of our day.
records.zomi: Zan simin lup ma-in ka tanu leh kei i ni sung a hoih pen thu i kikum hi.

records.english: We keep the baby's cot right beside our bed so that I can reach her quickly at night.
records.zomi: Zanin manlang takin ka tun theih nadingin naungek' lupna i lupna kiang tak ah i koih hi.

records.english: How do you get a teenager to go to sleep before midnight?
records.zomi: Khangno zan laitak ma-in bangci na ihmusak hiam?

records.english: Honestly, we've stopped trying — we just ask him to be quiet.
records.zomi: Ka gen taktak leh, i hanciam nawn kei hi — dai takin om dingin bek i ngen hi.

records.english: My brothers and I shared one big bed when we visited our grandparents.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh ka pi i va veh ciangin ka sanggam pasalte leh kei lupna lian khat ah i lum hi.

records.english: We do want our children to keep our bedtime traditions when they have families of their own.
records.zomi: I tate in amau innkuan a neih ciangun i lup ma ngeinate a kem ding uh i deih taktak hi.

records.english: My wife feeds the baby at two, and I do the five o'clock feed.
records.zomi: Ka zi in nai nih ciangin naungek an a vak a, kei in nai nga ciang a vak ka vak hi.

records.english: Bedtime at Grandma's house is always much later than at home.
records.zomi: Pi' inn ah lup hun inn sangin a zekai zaw tawntung hi.

records.english: I keep a small bell by Grandma's bed so that she can call us if she needs anything.
records.zomi: Bangmah a kisap leh hong sam thei nadingin Pi' lupna kiang ah daak neu khat ka koih hi.

records.english: Grandma wraps a warm scarf around her neck before she lies down.
records.zomi: Pi in a lup ma-in ngawng puan lum a ngawng ah a kawi hi.

records.english: What do your children do before they go to sleep?
records.zomi: Na tate in a ihmut ma-un bang a sem uh hiam?

records.english: They put their clothes in the basket, say their prayers, and kiss us good night.
records.zomi: A puante bawm sungah a koih uh a, thu a ngen uh a, “Zanpha” ci-in hong tawp uh hi.

records.english: Brush your sister's hair before bed, please; she can't reach the back.
records.zomi: Lup ma-in na sanggam nu' sam khui sak in; a nunglam a tun zo kei hi.

records.english: Please don't let the dog sleep on the children's beds.
records.zomi: Ui naupangte' lupna tungah ihmusak kei un.

records.english: Shall we say good night to the moon before we close the curtains?
records.zomi: Puan khai i khak ma-in khapi kiangah “Zanpha” i ci ding hiam?

records.english: My son tries to stay awake until his father gets home from work.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in a pa nasep pan a hong tun dong khanglo den dingin a hanciam hi.

records.english: We used to fall asleep to the sound of Dad's radio in the next room.
records.zomi: Khan dang ah Pa' radio ging za-in i ihmu ngei hi.

records.english: Since my husband started working nights, I've been putting the children to bed on my own.
records.zomi: Ka pasal zanin a sep pan naupangte ka bek in ka lupsak hi.

records.english: Good night, Grandpa — sleep well!
records.zomi: Pu, zanpha — nuam takin ihmu in!

records.english: Can I sleep with the door open so that I can hear you in the kitchen?
records.zomi: Anbuk sungah kong zak theih nadingin kongkhak kihong tawh ka ihmu thei ding hiam?

records.english: Getting three children to bed is the hardest part of my day.
records.zomi: Naupang thum lupsak pen ka ni sung a haksa pen ahi hi.

records.english: We might let the kids camp in the garden tonight if it doesn't rain.
records.zomi: Guah a zuk kei leh tu zanin naupangte huan sungah puan inn tawh i giaksak kha ding hi.

records.english: I knitted this blanket for your new baby's cot.
records.zomi: Na naungek thak' lupna adingin hih puan ka khui hi.

records.english: I really do treasure those quiet bedtime talks with my teenage son.
records.zomi: Ka tapa khangno tawh lup ma-a dai taka kikupnate ka manpha sa taktak hi.

records.english: May I read for ten more minutes?
records.zomi: Minit sawm behlap ka sim thei ding hiam?

records.english: When I was little, my sister and I made up stories in the dark until we fell asleep.
records.zomi: Ka neu lai-in ka sanggam nu leh kei i ihmut dong khuamial sungah tangthu i phuah hi.

records.english: I made a little lamp for my daughter's room out of an old jar.
records.zomi: Ka tanu' khan adingin um lui tawh meivak neu khat ka bawl hi.

records.english: You're allowed to keep your light on until nine, and then it's time to sleep.
records.zomi: Nai kua dong na meivak na hon thei a, tua khit ciangin ihmut hun ahi hi.

records.english: You can choose one book each, and I'll read them both.
records.zomi: Na khat ciat in laibu khat na teel thei uh a, a nih tengteng ka sim ding hi.

records.english: Is your little one sleeping through the night yet?
records.zomi: Na naupang neu zan bup a ihmu thei khin hiam?

records.english: Not yet — she still wakes up twice for a feed.
records.zomi: Thei nai lo hi — an nek dingin nihvei a khanglo lai hi.

records.english: My grandmother used to put a sprig of herbs under our pillows to keep bad dreams away.
records.zomi: Ka pi in mang sia a om loh nadingin i lukhum nuai ah an-lim-nah tawmno a koih ngei hi.

records.english: It might be easier to put the baby to bed if we dim the lights an hour earlier.
records.zomi: Nai khat a masa-in meivak i niamsak leh naungek lupsak a baih zaw kha ding hi.

records.english: My brother records himself reading stories so that his kids can listen when he's traveling.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in a khualzin ciangin a tate in a ngaih theih nadingin tangthu a sim ging a la hi.

records.english: Can Grandma tell us a story in our own language tonight?
records.zomi: Tu zanin Pi in i pau tawh tangthu hong gen thei ding hiam?

records.english: We whispered and giggled until Grandpa knocked on the wall.
records.zomi: Pu in bang a kiu dong i gen ciauciau-in i nui uh hi.

records.english: Is it okay if the cousins have a sleepover in the living room tonight?
records.zomi: Tu zanin sanggamte innsung khan ah a giak khawm uh leh a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, as long as they're quiet after ten.
records.zomi: Hoih hi, nai sawm khit ciangin a dai uh leh.

records.english: Would you read the last chapter to me, Dad?
records.zomi: Pa, cangpi nunung pen hong sim sak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: After the children are asleep, my husband and I finally have time to talk.
records.zomi: Naupangte a ihmut khit uh ciangin ka pasal leh kei kiho hun i nei tawp hi.

records.english: My son insists that his teddy bear say good night to everyone in the family.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in a teddy bear in innkuan mi khempeuh kiangah “Zanpha” a cih ding a ngen ngiat hi.

records.english: Our bedtime routine hasn't changed in years: bath, story, song, and lights out.
records.zomi: I lup ma ngeina kum tampi sung kilai lo hi: kisil, tangthu, la, meivak phel.

records.english: Shall I bring you an extra pillow, Grandpa?
records.zomi: Pu, lukhum behlap kong tawi ding hiam?

records.english: My daughter asked whether her cousin could stay the night on Friday.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in a sanggam Laithai ni ciangin zan khat a giak thei ding hiam hong dong hi.

records.english: Sweet dreams, everyone!
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, mang nuam ngah un!

records.english: Would you like me to leave the radio on for you?
records.zomi: Na adingin radio phel lo-in ka nusia ding na deih hiam?

records.english: Every evening, my mother puts her Bible and glasses on the bedside table before she goes to sleep.
records.zomi: Nitak simin ka nu in a ihmut ma-in a Laisiangtho leh a mitlimlang lupna kiang dawhkan tungah a koih hi.

records.english: Could you sing the lullaby your mother used to sing to you?
records.zomi: Na nu in hong sak ngei naupang lupsakna la na sa thei ding hiam?

records.english: Before bed, Grandpa teaches the children one new word in our home language.
records.zomi: Lup ma-in Pu in naupangte i inn pau kammal thak khat a hilh hi.

records.english: Kids, if you're quiet, you might hear the owls outside.
records.zomi: Naupangte, na dai uh leh a polam ah zing-ngiau ging na za kha ding uh hi.

records.english: The kids love wearing the pajamas their aunt sent them from abroad.
records.zomi: Naupangte in a ni uh in gamdang pan a khak zan puante silh a deih mahmah uh hi.

records.english: Kids, say good night to everyone in the room before you go upstairs.
records.zomi: Naupangte, a tung lam na kah ma-un khan sung mi khempeuh kiangah “Zanpha” ci un.

records.english: My husband calls the kids every night from the ship to say good night.
records.zomi: Ka pasal in “Zanpha” ci dingin zan simin tembaw tung pan naupangte a sam hi.

records.english: Could you change the baby while I warm her bottle?
records.zomi: A nawi um ka lumsak laitakin naungek puan na laih sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: I'm so proud of you for remembering everything on the list!
records.zomi: List tung a om khempeuh na phawk ahih manin ka kisaktheih mahmah hi!

records.english: In our family, nobody puts anything in the cart without asking Mom first.
records.zomi: I innkuan ah Nu dong masa lo-in kuamah in cart sungah bangmah a koih kei hi.

records.english: Please don't open the packets before we've paid for them.
records.zomi: I piak ma-in ipte hong kei un.

records.english: I buy a little extra rice each week in case relatives arrive unexpectedly.
records.zomi: Beh leh phungte thakhat a hong tun kha ding ci-in kal simin buh tawmno ka lei behlap hi.

records.english: Remember to buy medicine for Grandpa's cough while you're at the pharmacy.
records.zomi: Zatui dawl ah na om laitakin Pu' khuh zatui lei ding phawk in.

records.english: The vegetables were delivered straight from my uncle's farm, so we didn't have to go shopping.
records.zomi: Anteh ka pa neu' lo pan tangtak hong tung ahih manin an lei i pai kul kei hi.

records.english: How much should we spend on food for the wedding?
records.zomi: Kiteenna an adingin bangzah i zang ding hiam?

records.english: My husband always buys too many snacks when he shops hungry.
records.zomi: Ka pasal in a gil a kial laitakin an a lei ciangin nek ding neute a lei tam lua tawntung hi.

records.english: Are you sure we need three kinds of cheese?
records.zomi: Cheese nam thum i kisam taktak hiam?

records.english: Kids, stay with the cart and keep your hands off the shelves.
records.zomi: Naupangte, cart kiangah om unla dawhte khoih kei un.

records.english: My aunt runs a small grocery shop, so we always buy our rice from her.
records.zomi: Ka ni in an dawl neu khat a nei ahih manin amah pan buh i lei tawntung hi.

records.english: When we were children, my brothers and I fought over who would push the cart.
records.zomi: I neu lai-in cart kua in a nawt ding hiam ka sanggam pasalte leh kei i kilai uh hi.

records.english: Who's making the shopping list for the week?
records.zomi: Kal khat sung lei ding list kua in a bawl ding hiam?

records.english: Everybody writes what they need on the board by the kitchen door.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh in a kisapna uh anbuk kongkhak kiang suanglaipi tungah a gelh uh hi.

records.english: My daughter reads the shopping list out loud while I find the items.
records.zomi: Vante ka zon laitakin ka tanu in lei ding list aw ngaih takin a sim hi.

records.english: Shall we buy a whole chicken for Sunday lunch, or just the legs?
records.zomi: Nipini sun an adingin aksa bup khat i lei ding hiam, a khe bek hiam?

records.english: My husband and I shop together on Saturday mornings and have coffee afterward.
records.zomi: Ka pasal leh kei Kiginni zingsang ciangin an i lei khawm a, a nung ciangin kawfi i dawn hi.

records.english: Use the shopping app to compare prices before we go.
records.zomi: I pai ma-in an lei app tawh a man kiteh in.

records.english: The shopkeeper gave my daughter a free orange because she said thank you so politely.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in zahtak takin lungdam a ko ahih manin dawl neipa in lamsi khat a man om lo-in a pia hi.

records.english: My mother taught me to buy what's in season and to cook what's cheap.
records.zomi: Ka nu in a hun takah a om lei-in a man neu huan dingin hong hilh hi.

records.english: You could buy the flour in a big bag and share it with your sister.
records.zomi: Moh vui ip lian khat na lei-in na sanggam nu tawh na kihawm thei hi.

records.english: Grandpa insists on choosing the fish himself, because nobody else can tell whether it's fresh.
records.zomi: A thak hiam kuamah in a theih kei manin Pu in nga amah mah in a teel ding a ngen ngiat hi.

records.english: Every Friday I take Grandma to the market and push the cart while she chooses.
records.zomi: Laithai ni simin Pi zuakna mun ah ka paipih a, a teel laitakin cart ka nawt hi.

records.english: My grandmother still carries a woven basket to the market instead of using plastic bags.
records.zomi: Ka pi in plastic ip zang lo-in zuakna mun ah bawm khawng a puak lai hi.

records.english: Is it all right if the kids pick out the fruit?
records.zomi: Naupangte in singgah a teel uh leh a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: My little sister always asks the vegetable seller for a free chili.
records.zomi: Ka nau numei in anteh zuakpa kiangah malcha khat a man om lo-in a ngen tawntung hi.

records.english: Could we stop at the bakery on the way home?
records.zomi: Inn i ciah laitakin moh bawlna ah i khawl thei ding hiam?

records.english: Our neighbor brings back fresh bread for us whenever she goes into town.
records.zomi: I inn veng nu in khua sung a pai simin moh thak hong tawi hi.

records.english: Mom gave me a list and enough money for exactly what was on it.
records.zomi: Nu in list khat leh a tung a om man cing sum hong pia hi.

records.english: Is there anything special you'd like me to buy for your birthday dinner?
records.zomi: Na pianni nitak an adingin ka lei ding tuam bangmah a om hiam?

records.english: Just a big mango cake and plenty of noodles!
records.zomi: Haigah cake lian khat leh an-tui tampi bek!

records.english: The market was so crowded before Christmas that we lost my little brother for ten minutes.
records.zomi: Christmas ma-in zuakna mun ah mi a tam lua ahih manin ka nau pasal minit sawm sung i mansuah hi.

records.english: Who's going to carry the sack of potatoes to the car?
records.zomi: Alu ip mawtaw dong kua in a puak ding hiam?

records.english: Before Christmas, we bought gifts for the children and food for the church dinner.
records.zomi: Christmas ma-in naupangte adingin letsong leh pawlpi nitak an adingin an i lei hi.

records.english: Our parents sent us a big box of dried fish from the village.
records.zomi: I nu leh pa in khua pan nga keu bawm lian khat hong khak uh hi.

records.english: Our grocery bill has doubled since the twins started eating solid food.
records.zomi: Apengte in an tak a nek kipat uh ciang pan i an lei man a nih in a khang hi.

records.english: My teenage son now does the weekly shopping, and he's better at it than I am.
records.zomi: Ka tapa khangno in tu-in kal simin an a lei a, kei sangin a siam zaw hi.

records.english: Everyone gets to choose one thing for the barbecue.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh in sa khuk adingin na khat ciat a teel thei uh hi.

records.english: Can I pay for the groceries this time, since you paid last week?
records.zomi: Kal bei-in nang na piak ahih manin tu-in an lei man kei ka pia thei ding hiam?

records.english: Would it be cheaper to grow our own vegetables?
records.zomi: Anteh i khawi leh a man a neu zaw ding hiam?

records.english: It might be, but it would take a lot of work.
records.zomi: A neu zaw kha ding hi, ahi zongin na tampi sep a kisam ding hi.

records.english: Would you mind getting nappies for the baby when you go to the pharmacy?
records.zomi: Zatui dawl ah na pai ciangin naungek' diaper hong lei sak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Please don't let the kids talk you into buying sweets.
records.zomi: Naupangte in a khum neute lei dingin hong sawl kha kei hen.

records.english: We pay for groceries with cash so that the children can see how much things cost.
records.zomi: Naupangte in nate a man bangzah hiam a muh theih nadingin an lei man sum tawh i pia hi.

records.english: Our family does one big shopping trip to town at the beginning of each month.
records.zomi: I innkuan in kha khat ciat a kipat ciangin khuapi ah an lei dingin vei khat i pai hi.

records.english: We can split the big bag of oranges between our two families.
records.zomi: Lamsi ip lian i innkuan nih in i kihawm thei hi.

records.english: We weigh the vegetables on the little scale at the stall before we pay.
records.zomi: I piak ma-in dawl tung a om bukna neu tawh anteh i buk hi.

records.english: Why do we always forget the salt?
records.zomi: Bang hangin cii i mangngilh tawntung hiam?

records.english: Because it's never on the list!
records.zomi: List tungah a om ngei kei ahih manin!

records.english: Shopping with a toddler takes twice as long as shopping alone.
records.zomi: Naupang neu tawh an lei pen amah bek in lei sangin hun a nih in a sau hi.

records.english: Can I choose one treat if I help carry the bags?
records.zomi: Ip ka puak huh leh nek ding nuam khat ka teel thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, but nothing with too much sugar.
records.zomi: Thei hi, ahi zongin sugar a tam lua kei ding hi.

records.english: Kids, whoever finds the cheapest eggs gets to choose dessert.
records.zomi: Naupangte, aktui a man neu pen a mu in an khit nek ding a teel ding hi.

records.english: We use a big cool box to keep the meat fresh on the drive home from town.
records.zomi: Khuapi pan inn i ciah laitakin sa a thak den nadingin ka khal bawm lian khat i zang hi.

records.english: We do our shopping at the village market because the farmers are our neighbors.
records.zomi: Lo neite in i inn veng ahih manun khua sung zuakna mun ah an i lei hi.

records.english: The pharmacy had run out of the baby's milk powder, so my brother drove to the next town to find some.
records.zomi: Zatui dawl ah naungek' nawi mal a bei ahih manin ka sanggam pasal in khua dang ah va zong dingin mawtaw a tuan hi.

records.english: My son is learning to count money by paying at the vegetable stall.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in anteh dawl ah a piak tawh sum sim a kisin hi.

records.english: Could you hold the shopping bags while I strap the baby into the car seat?
records.zomi: Naungek mawtaw tutna ah ka khih laitakin an ip na len sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: We might need to buy extra rice, since your brothers are coming for the holidays.
records.zomi: Na sanggam pasalte tawlngakni hun ah a hong pai ding uh ahih manin buh behlap i lei kul kha ding hi.

records.english: My wife has banned me from buying more coffee until we finish the old packet.
records.zomi: Ip lui i bei ma-in kawfi behlap lei ding ka zi in hong khak hi.

records.english: My son asked whether he could buy the toy with his birthday money.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in a pianni sum tawh a tawng a lei thei ding hiam hong dong hi.

records.english: Our neighbors asked us how much we paid the builder, because they want to fix their roof too.
records.zomi: I inn veng te in a inn tung uh a bawl nuam uh ahih manin inn lamte bangzah i pia hiam hong dong uh hi.

records.english: The seller lowered the price when he heard we were buying for our grandmother.
records.zomi: I pi adingin i lei hi, ci a zak ciangin a zuakpa in a man a niamsak hi.

records.english: The furniture shop gave us a discount because we're regular customers.
records.zomi: A lei tawntungte i hih manin innsung van dawl in man hong niamsak hi.

records.english: My daughter guessed the exact price, and the seller gave her a sweet.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in a man a kilawm takin a khen ahih manin zuakpa in a khum neu khat a pia hi.

records.english: How much do you want for the baby stroller, which I'm buying for my sister?
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu adingin ka lei ahih manin naungek tawlnelna leeng bangzah na deih hiam?

records.english: Is this the price for the frame alone, or does it include the photo?
records.zomi: Hih man pen a bawngkhawng bek ading hiam, a lim zong a kihel hiam?

records.english: You'll have to ask my wife — she handles the money.
records.zomi: Ka zi kiangah na dong kul ding hi — amah in sum a kem hi.

records.english: Our old car was valued by a mechanic before we sold it to my cousin.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam kiangah i zuak ma-in i mawtaw lui man pen mawtaw bawlpa in a khen hi.

records.english: School uniforms cost so much this year that we bought the older children's secondhand.
records.zomi: Tu kum sang puan man a sang lua ahih manin naupang upa zawte' a kizang khinte i lei hi.

records.english: Our family photos were printed at a small studio that charged half the usual price.
records.zomi: I innkuan limte a man tawntung kim tawh a kibawlna studio neu khat ah i suaksak hi.

records.english: Could you write down the prices so that I can show my husband?
records.zomi: Ka pasal ka etsak theih nadingin a man na gelh sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Please don't tell your grandmother how much this gift cost.
records.zomi: Hih letsong a man bangzah hiam na pi kiangah gen kei in.

records.english: Is it rude to ask your in-laws how much they paid for their house?
records.zomi: Na sungte kiangah a inn uh bangzah tawh a lei uh hiam dong pen zahtakna om lo ahi hiam?

records.english: Shall I ask the shopkeeper for a discount, since we're buying for the whole family?
records.zomi: Innkuan bup adingin i lei ahih manin dawl neipa kiangah a man niamsak dingin ka ngen ding hiam?

records.english: Honestly, the price doesn't matter if it makes Grandma happy.
records.zomi: Ka gen taktak leh, Pi a lungdam leh a man pen thupi lo hi.

records.english: What is a suitable amount to give as a wedding gift?
records.zomi: Kiteenna letsong-a piak ding bangzah a kilawm hiam?

records.english: Mom always checks the price of rice at three stalls before she buys any.
records.zomi: Nu in buh a lei ma-in dawl thum ah a man a en tawntung hi.

records.english: I cut the price tag off the necklace before I gave it to my wife.
records.zomi: Ka zi ka piak ma-in ngawngkhai pan a man kigelhna ka at hi.

records.english: The quote for the wedding food was much higher than we expected.
records.zomi: Kiteenna an adingin a kigen man pen i lamen sangin a sang zaw mahmah hi.

records.english: Could you check the price of flights for the family before we decide?
records.zomi: I khensat ma-in innkuan adingin vanleng man na en sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: On this ferry, children under five travel free, so our youngest won't need a ticket.
records.zomi: Hih tembaw tungah kum nga nuai naupangte a man om lo-in a tuang thei uh ahih manin i naupang neu pen in ticket a kisam kei ding hi.

records.english: In our family, we usually give money in an envelope, and the amount depends on how close we are to the couple.
records.zomi: I innkuan ah lai-ip sungah sum i pia zel a, a zah pen tua zi leh pasal tawh i kinai dan tawh kizui hi.

records.english: My grandmother still remembers when a bowl of noodles cost only a few coins.
records.zomi: Ka pi in an-ngum khuang khat pen sum neu tawmno bek a man lai hun a phawk lai hi.

records.english: My brother paid for our mother's glasses and wouldn't let anyone share the cost.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in i nu' mitlimlang a man pia a, a man kuamah a kihawm sak kei hi.

records.english: We might rent a hall for the reunion if the price is reasonable.
records.zomi: A man a kilawm leh kikhopna adingin inn lian khat i hal kha ding hi.

records.english: Is it all right if I pay you back next month?
records.zomi: Kha hong ding ciangin kong lohsak kik leh a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: Kids, you each have five dollars to spend at the fair, so choose carefully.
records.zomi: Naupangte, pawi ah na zat ding dollar nga ciat na nei uh ahih manin limtakin teel un.

records.english: The rent for our apartment went up, so my parents-in-law offered to help.
records.zomi: I inn man a khan ahih manin ka sungpa leh ka sungnu in hong huh dingin a kiciam uh hi.

records.english: How much did you pay for your daughter's wedding hall?
records.zomi: Na tanu' kiteenna inn lian bangzah tawh na hal hiam?

records.english: Too much — but my uncle knew the owner, so we got a small discount.
records.zomi: A tam lua hi — ahi zongin ka pa neu in a neipa a theih manin a man tawmno hong niamsak hi.

records.english: Kids, how much do you think this watermelon costs?
records.zomi: Naupangte, hih dawngkuang a man bangzah hi ding in na ngaihsun uh hiam?
