records.english: My husband found a cheaper price for the same fridge by comparing shops on his phone.
records.zomi: Ka pasal in a phone tungah dawlte a kiteh ahih manin khal bawm kibang khat a man neu zawin a mu hi.

records.english: Is the price per person or for the whole family?
records.zomi: A man pen mi khat ciat ading hiam, innkuan bup ading hiam?

records.english: It's per family, so it's a good deal for us.
records.zomi: Innkuan khat ciat ading ahih manin i adingin a hoih mahmah hi.

records.english: What did your parents pay for their first house?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa in a inn masa uh bangzah tawh a lei uh hiam?

records.english: Less than we pay for a car today, according to my father.
records.zomi: Ka pa' gen dan in, tuni-a mawtaw khat i piak sangin a neu zaw hi.

records.english: Grandpa always converts today's prices into what things cost when he was young.
records.zomi: Pu in tuni-a man pen a khangno lai-a man tawh a teh tawntung hi.

records.english: The village school asked every family to pay a little more this year to repair the roof.
records.zomi: Khua sung sang in inn tung bawl nadingin tu kum innkuan khempeuh in tawmno behlap a piak ding uh a ngen hi.

records.english: Can you find out how much a crib costs before your sister's baby arrives?
records.zomi: Na sanggam nu' naungek a pian ma-in naungek lupna khat bangzah a man hiam na zong thei ding hiam?

records.english: Prices at the festival are always higher, so we bring our own food.
records.zomi: Pawi ah a man sang den ahih manin i neihsa an i puak hi.

records.english: Could you ask your cousin what he charges to take family photos?
records.zomi: Innkuan lim la dingin bangzah a ngen hiam na sanggam kiangah na dong thei ding hiam?

records.english: Let my brother do the bargaining — the sellers always give him a better price.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in kitaang hen — zuakte in amah a man hoih zaw a pia tawntung uh hi.

records.english: We saved for two years to afford a new roof for my parents' house.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa' inn tung thak a lei theih nadingin kum nih sung sum i khol hi.

records.english: My cousin works at the furniture store, so she can tell us when prices will drop.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu in innsung van dawl ah na a sep manin a man a kiniam ding hun hong gen thei hi.

records.english: Nobody in our family pays full price for anything when my aunt is with us.
records.zomi: Ka ni i kiang ah a om ciangin i innkuan ah kuamah in na khat zong a man kim tawh a lei kei hi.

records.english: We could get a family ticket for the zoo, which is cheaper than four separate ones.
records.zomi: Ganhing huan adingin innkuan ticket khat i lei thei a, tua pen ticket tuam li sangin a man neu zaw hi.

records.english: Ask your aunt; she always knows where things are cheapest.
records.zomi: Na ni kiangah dong in; amah in nate a man neu pen mun a thei tawntung hi.

records.english: My aunt bought the fabric for all the bridesmaids' dresses, which saved us a lot of money.
records.zomi: Ka ni in moute' tawi numei khempeuh' puan a lei ahih manin sum tampi hong khol hi.

records.english: It might be cheaper to buy the school books secondhand from older students.
records.zomi: Sang laibute pen sangnaupang upa zawte kiang pan a kizang khin lei a man neu zaw kha ding hi.

records.english: Would you lend me the money for the school trip until payday?
records.zomi: Kha tawp sum ka ngah dong sang khualzinna adingin sum hong leitawi thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Dad, how much does a new bicycle cost?
records.zomi: Pa, siiksakol thak khat bangzah a man hiam?

records.english: More than your pocket money, I'm afraid, but we could save up together.
records.zomi: Na zat ding sum sangin a tam zaw hi, ahi zongin khawm in i khol thei hi.

records.english: We were told the price would be lower if we paid for the whole year at once.
records.zomi: Kum khat bup a man vei khat thu-in i piak leh a man a neu zaw ding hi, ci-in hong gen uh hi.

records.english: Mom, can I check the price before I try it on?
records.zomi: Nu, ka silh ma-in a man ka en thei ding hiam?

records.english: How much are the rooms for a family of five?
records.zomi: Innkuan mi nga adingin khan bangzah a man hiam?

records.english: Two rooms side by side would cost less than one big suite.
records.zomi: Khan nih kikiang pen khan lian khat sangin a man neu zaw ding hi.

records.english: How much do you charge for a cake big enough for fifty people?
records.zomi: Mi sawmnga adingin a lian cake khat bangzah na ngen hiam?

records.english: It depends on the flavor, but most of our big cakes start at forty dollars.
records.zomi: A lim dan tawh kizui hi, ahi zongin i cake lianten dollar sawmli pan kipan hi.

records.english: Why are baby clothes so expensive when babies grow so fast?
records.zomi: Naungekte a khan manlang mahmah hangin bang hangin naungek puan a man sang ahi hiam?

records.english: The cashier at the village shop knows everyone, so she lets children pay the next day.
records.zomi: Khua sung dawl a sum la nu in mi khempeuh a theih manin naupangte a zing ciangin a pia thei uh hi.

records.english: My cousin dropped his wallet in the market, and someone handed it back with every coin inside.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam' sum ip zuakna mun ah a kia a, kuamah khat in sum khempeuh a sung ah om lai-in hong lohsak kik hi.

records.english: Dad paid for the wedding in cash, which he had saved over many years.
records.zomi: Pa in kum tampi sung a khol sum tawh kiteenna man a pia hi.

records.english: Aunt Lydia always slips a little money into the children's pockets when she visits.
records.zomi: Ni Lydia in hong veh simin naupangte' puan ip sungah sum tawmno a guk-in a koih tawntung hi.

records.english: Would it be possible to pay the hospital in monthly amounts?
records.zomi: Zato man kha simin tawmno ciat-in ka pia thei ding hiam?

records.english: Is it safe to send money to my parents through a phone app?
records.zomi: Phone app tawh ka nu leh ka pa kiangah sum khak pen a bitna hiam?

records.english: Each of us puts a little money into the envelope for the church offering.
records.zomi: Pawlpi thupiakna adingin lai-ip sungah i khat ciat in sum tawmno i koih hi.

records.english: My little sister was given too much change, so she ran back to the shop to return it.
records.zomi: Ka nau numei in sum kik a tam lua a ngah ahih manin lohsak kik dingin dawl ah a tai kik hi.

records.english: The old shop near our house still doesn't accept cards.
records.zomi: I inn kiang dawl lui in card a sang nai kei hi.

records.english: Grandma keeps her money in a small cloth purse tied with string.
records.zomi: Pi in a sum puan ip neu khat sungah khau tawh a khih hi.

records.english: How much change did the shopkeeper give you?
records.zomi: Dawl neipa in sum kik bangzah hong pia hiam?

records.english: Three coins and a small note — I think it's right.
records.zomi: Dangka thum leh laidang neu khat — a man ding hi ka sa hi.

records.english: My brother lost his money in the parking machine at the hospital, so he had to pay again.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in zato mawtaw koihna machine ah a sum a mansuah ahih manin a pia kik kul hi.

records.english: I insist on paying this time — you treated us last month.
records.zomi: Tu-in kei ka pia ngiat ding hi — kha bei-in nang na hong vaak hi.

records.english: We were charged for three meals but only ate two.
records.zomi: Vei nih bek i nek hangin an vei thum man hong ngen uh hi.

records.english: Is it all right if I pay for my share later?
records.zomi: Ka tan ding a nung ciangin ka pia leh a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: My grandmother counts out the exact money before she leaves the house.
records.zomi: Ka pi in inn a paisan ma-in a pia ding sum a kilawm takin a sim hi.

records.english: Buy yourself a drink with whatever change is left.
records.zomi: Sum kik a om bangbang tawh dawn ding khat kilei in.

records.english: Please don't give the children money without asking me first.
records.zomi: Ka kiangah na dong masa lo-in naupangte sum pia kei in.

records.english: You can use my card to pay for your school books.
records.zomi: Na sang laibu man piak nadingin ka card na zang thei hi.

records.english: Who's paying for Grandma's birthday cake this year?
records.zomi: Tu kum Pi' pianni cake kua in a pia ding hiam?

records.english: We're all chipping in, so it won't cost anyone very much.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh in tawmno ciat i kikhawm ahih manin kuamah adingin a man tam lua kei ding hi.

records.english: The money left over from the family reunion was given to the church youth group for their trip.
records.zomi: Innkuan kikhopna pan sum a taang pen pawlpi khangnote' khualzinna adingin kipia hi.

records.english: My brother insisted on paying for the whole family's dinner, and nobody could stop him.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in innkuan bup' nitak an man pia dingin a ngiat a, kuamah in a khaktan zo kei uh hi.

records.english: We split the cost of Dad's hospital bill between the four of us.
records.zomi: Pa' zato man i li in i kihawm hi.

records.english: Somebody paid for our coffee before we reached the counter, and we never found out who.
records.zomi: Dawhkan i tun ma-in kuamah khat in i kawfi man hong pia a, kua hiam i thei ngei kei hi.

records.english: Uncle offered to pay for my driving lessons as a graduation gift.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in sang zawhna letsong-in mawtaw tuan kisinna man hong pia dingin a kiciam hi.

records.english: Uncle Thang always pretends he doesn't want to be paid back.
records.zomi: Pa neu Thang in sum lohsak kik a deih lo bangin a kibawl tawntung hi.

records.english: In our family, the eldest person at the table usually pays for the meal.
records.zomi: I innkuan ah dawhkan a om upa pen in an man a pia zel hi.

records.english: The school fees are paid at the office at the start of every term.
records.zomi: Sang man pen term khat ciat a kipat ciangin office ah kipia hi.

records.english: I really do appreciate that you paid for my train ticket home.
records.zomi: Inn ka ciah nadingin ka meileng ticket man na hong piak ka lungdam taktak hi.

records.english: Can I pay the bus driver myself this time?
records.zomi: Tu-in bus tuansakpa kiangah kei mah in ka pia thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes — just hold the coins tightly and wait for your change.
records.zomi: Thei hi — dangkate cing takin len inla na sum kik ngak in.

records.english: At our bank, children can open an account only with a parent.
records.zomi: I bank ah naupangte in nu hiam pa hiam tawh bek account a hong thei uh hi.

records.english: The wrong amount was taken from my account, and the bank had to fix it.
records.zomi: Ka account pan sum a man lo zah kila a, bank in a bawl kik kul hi.

records.english: My aunt sends money home to her parents every month through a shop in town.
records.zomi: Ka ni in khuapi sung dawl khat tungtawn-in kha simin a nu leh a pa kiangah sum a khak hi.

records.english: Who paid for the flowers on the table?
records.zomi: Dawhkan tung pak man kua in a pia hiam?

records.english: Grandma did, as a surprise for the anniversary.
records.zomi: Pi in a pia hi, kumpi ni adingin lungdamna-in.

records.english: Our phone bill was paid twice by mistake, and it took weeks to get the money back.
records.zomi: Ka phone man khialhna tawh vei nih kipia a, sum a lak kik nadingin kal tampi a sau hi.

records.english: It might be easier to pay the rent by bank transfer than to carry so much cash.
records.zomi: Sum tampi puak sangin bank tawh inn man piak a baih zaw kha ding hi.

records.english: My niece thought the parking machine was a game and fed it all her coins.
records.zomi: Ka tunu in mawtaw koihna machine pen kimawlna ahi sa-in a dangka khempeuh a khun hi.

records.english: How do you teach children to handle money?
records.zomi: Naupangte sum zat dan bangci na hilh hiam?

records.english: We let them pay for small things and check their change themselves.
records.zomi: Na neute man amau mah in a piak uh a, a sum kik uh amau mah in a en uh dingin i phal hi.

records.english: Our grandparents never had a bank account; they kept their savings in a tin under the bed.
records.zomi: I pu leh pite in bank account a nei ngei kei uh a, a sum kholte uh lupna nuai thekbawm sungah a koih uh hi.

records.english: Can you check that the shopkeeper gave you the right change?
records.zomi: Dawl neipa in sum kik a man takin hong pia hiam na en thei ding hiam?

records.english: Pay with the card I gave you, and keep the receipt for me.
records.zomi: Kong piak card tawh pia inla, receipt hong kem sak in.

records.english: Could you lend me some cash until I get to the bank, Auntie?
records.zomi: Ni, bank ka tun dong sum tawmno hong leitawi thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Why did the cashier give you so many small coins?
records.zomi: Bang hangin sum lapa in dangka neu tampi hong pia hiam?

records.english: She didn't have enough notes, so she gave me coins instead.
records.zomi: Laidang a tam lo ahih manin a sikin dangka hong pia hi.

records.english: Let me pay this time, since you drove us all the way here.
records.zomi: Hih dong hong paipih ahih manin tu-in kei ka pia ning.

records.english: My grandfather taught me never to count money in front of strangers.
records.zomi: Ka pu in mi theih lohte' mai ah sum sim kei dingin hong hilh hi.

records.english: Shall I pay for the taxi, and you pay for lunch?
records.zomi: Taxi man kei ka pia inla, sun an man nang na pia ding hiam?

records.english: Could you pay the electricity bill online for your grandparents?
records.zomi: Na pu leh na pite adingin meivak man online tawh na pia thei ding hiam?

records.english: The money for the school trip was collected by the class teacher.
records.zomi: Sang khualzinna adingin sum pen kilasi saya in a kaikhawm hi.

records.english: Payment for the trip has to be made by Friday, or the place will be given to someone else.
records.zomi: Khualzinna man Laithai ni ma-in kipia ding a, a kipia kei leh tua mun pen mi dang kipia ding hi.

records.english: Our son's first salary was given to his grandmother as a gift.
records.zomi: I tapa' kha man masa pen a pi kiangah letsong-in kipia hi.

records.english: Our daughter was so proud the first time a shopkeeper handed her change.
records.zomi: Dawl neipa in a masa pen-in sum kik a piak ciangin i tanu a kisaktheih mahmah hi.

records.english: My grandfather won't let anyone else pay when he takes us out for noodles.
records.zomi: Ka pu in an-ngum ne dingin hong paipih ciangin kuamah a man a piak a phal kei hi.

records.english: You might get the wrong change if you don't watch carefully.
records.zomi: Limtakin na en kei leh sum kik a man lo na ngah kha ding hi.

records.english: In our house, the children never buy anything online unless one of us is with them.
records.zomi: I inn ah i lak pan kuamah a kiang ah a om kei leh naupangte in online tawh bangmah a lei ngei kei uh hi.

records.english: Can I return this cooking pot if my grandmother finds it too heavy?
records.zomi: Ka pi in a gik lua a sak leh hih an huanna beel ka lohsak kik thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, within two weeks, as long as it hasn't been used.
records.zomi: Thei hi, a kizang nai kei phial leh kal nih sung.

records.english: Please don't return the sweater Aunt Ruth knitted — she'll be very hurt.
records.zomi: Ni Ruth' khuih sweater lohsak kik kei in — a lungkham mahmah ding hi.

records.english: Our family avoids returning gifts, because we would rather pass them on to someone who needs them.
records.zomi: Letsongte a kisapna mite kiangah i piak zawh hoih zaw ahih manin i innkuan in letsong lohsak kik i nawl hi.

records.english: We were given three rice cookers as wedding presents, so we exchanged two of them for plates.
records.zomi: Kiteenna letsong-in rice cooker thum hong kipia ahih manin a nih pen kuangte tawh i lai hi.

records.english: My aunt said, "If it doesn't fit, take it back — I won't be offended."
records.zomi: Ka ni in, “A kilawm kei leh lohsak kik in — ka lungkham kei ding hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: Was the dress a gift, or did you buy it yourself?
records.zomi: Hih puan pen letsong ahi hiam, nang mah in na lei hiam?

records.english: It was a gift from my sister, but it's two sizes too big.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu' letsong ahi hi, ahi zongin a lian lua nih a hi hi.

records.english: Do you really have to keep it just because Grandma chose it?
records.zomi: Pi in a teel ahih man bek-in na kem taktak kul hiam?

records.english: The family's old washing machine was taken away when the new one was delivered.
records.zomi: Puan sawpna machine thak a tun ciangin innkuan' a lui kipuak khia hi.

records.english: Uncle Pau bought the wrong charger for his phone, so his grandson took it back for him.
records.zomi: Pa neu Pau in a phone adingin charger a man lo a lei ahih manin a tu in a lohsak kik sak hi.

records.english: Is there anything wrong with the gift we sent your mother?
records.zomi: Na nu kiangah i khak letsong bangmah a siat om hiam?

records.english: Not at all — it just didn't fit in her small kitchen.
records.zomi: Om lo hi — a anbuk neu sungah a kilawm kei bek hi.

records.english: The cake stand we ordered for the wedding arrived in pieces.
records.zomi: Kiteenna adingin i sap cake koihna a tun ciangin a kitam hi.

records.english: Is it rude to return a gift that a relative gave you?
records.zomi: Beh leh phung khat in hong piak letsong lohsak kik pen zahtakna om lo ahi hiam?

records.english: Not if you're kind about it and never tell them.
records.zomi: Hi lo hi, lungsim nem takin na sep a, amaute kiangah na gen ngei kei leh.

records.english: Is it worth returning something that cost so little?
records.zomi: A man tawmno bek a om na khat lohsak kik pen a phatuam hiam?

records.english: The shop refused to take back the doll because my daughter had cut its hair.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in a sam a at ahih manin dawl in naupang lim tawng a la kik kei hi.

records.english: "We can't take it back if it's been opened," the shop assistant told my aunt.
records.zomi: “Na hon khin leh i la kik thei kei hi,” ci-in dawl a sem nu in ka ni a hilh hi.

records.english: Could you return these school shoes for me, since your brother has already outgrown them?
records.zomi: Na sanggam pasal in a khan khin ahih manin hih sang khedap na lohsak kik sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: We sent the baby monitor back because it kept switching itself off.
records.zomi: Naungek monitor amah le amah a kiphel den ahih manin i khak kik hi.

records.english: You might be able to exchange the blanket even without the receipt if you bring the gift card.
records.zomi: Gift card na tawi leh receipt om lo zongin puanzial na lai thei kha ding hi.

records.english: Remember to ask whether we can get the money back or only a voucher.
records.zomi: Sum i la kik thei ding hiam, voucher bek hiam dong dingin phawk in.

records.english: The toy broke on Christmas morning, and my nephew cried until we promised to get it replaced.
records.zomi: Christmas zingsangin tawng a kitam ahih manin a thak tawh lai ding i kiciam dong ka tanau a kap hi.

records.english: Next time, let's check the size before we buy anything for the kids.
records.zomi: A zom ciangin naupangte adingin bangmah i lei ma-in a lianzah en masa ni.

records.english: Our son broke the new kite on its first flight, so we didn't even try to return it.
records.zomi: I tapa in leng thak a masa pen a leng sak ciangin a sia sak ahih manin lohsak kik zong i sin kei hi.

records.english: I felt embarrassed returning the shirt my wife had bought me.
records.zomi: Ka zi in hong leisak puan ka lohsak kik ciangin ka zahlak hi.

records.english: Grandma's new glasses gave her headaches, so the optician changed the lenses for free.
records.zomi: Pi' mitlimlang thak in a lu a natsak ahih manin mitlimlang bawlpa in a man om lo-in a mit-ang a lai sak hi.

records.english: The jacket I bought for Dad was exchanged for a warmer one.
records.zomi: Pa adingin ka lei jacket pen a lum zaw khat tawh kilai hi.

records.english: My cousin's new phone stopped working after a day, and he was told to send it to the factory.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam' phone thak ni khat khit ciangin a sem nawn kei a, factory ah khak dingin kigen hi.

records.english: The return was refused because the box had been thrown away.
records.zomi: A bawm kiseh khin ahih manin a lohsak kik pen ki-nial hi.

records.english: My sister returned the dress and used the money to buy a gift for our mother.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu in puan a lohsak kik a, tua sum tawh i nu adingin letsong a lei hi.

records.english: My grandparents rarely return anything; they'd rather mend it themselves.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh ka pite in bangmah lohsak kik tawm uh a, amau mah in bawl kik a deih zaw uh hi.

records.english: My brother never returns anything; he just keeps it in a cupboard and forgets about it.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in bangmah lohsak kik ngei lo a, bawm sungah a koih a, a mangngilh bek hi.

records.english: Is the shop open on Sunday, so that we can return the lamp?
records.zomi: Meivak lohsak kik theih nadingin dawl in Nipini ciangin a hong hiam?

records.english: Only in the morning, until noon.
records.zomi: Zingsang bek, sun dong.

records.english: How long do we have to return the sofa?
records.zomi: Sofa lohsak kik nadingin hun bangzah i nei hiam?

records.english: They said we have fourteen days, so there's still time.
records.zomi: Ni sawm leh li i nei hi, a ci uh ahih manin hun om lai hi.

records.english: We were offered a refund or a replacement, and we chose the refund.
records.zomi: Sum lak kik hiam a thak tawh lai hiam hong kipia a, sum lak kik i teel hi.

records.english: The shop assistant checked the dress carefully before agreeing to take it back.
records.zomi: Dawl a sem nu in a la kik ding a lungkim ma-in puan limtakin a en hi.

records.english: What made you decide to take the coat back?
records.zomi: Bang hangin coat lohsak kik dingin na khensat hiam?

records.english: Because my husband already bought me the same one for my birthday.
records.zomi: Ka pianni-in ka pasal in a kibang khat hong leisak khin ahih manin.

records.english: Please put a gift receipt in the box in case the color isn't right.
records.zomi: A lim a kilawm kei kha leh ci-in bawm sungah gift receipt koih in.

records.english: Shall I keep the receipt in case your father wants to change the size?
records.zomi: Na pa in a lianzah a lai nuam kha leh ci-in receipt ka kem ding hiam?

records.english: The salesman promised my brother that he could bring the phone back within a week.
records.zomi: A zuakpa in kal khat sungin phone a lohsak kik thei ding ci-in ka sanggam pasal kiangah a kiciam hi.

records.english: The bicycle we ordered for our daughter arrived with a bent wheel.
records.zomi: I tanu adingin i sap siiksakol pen a kawngkual kingawi tawh hong tung hi.

records.english: My sister-in-law returns almost everything she buys online.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal' zi in online pan a lei khempeuh kik lohsak kik zel hi.

records.english: It was so hard to return something my grandmother had chosen for me.
records.zomi: Ka pi in hong teel sak na khat lohsak kik pen a haksa mahmah hi.

records.english: Our order of curtains was delivered to the wrong house, and the neighbors brought it over.
records.zomi: I sap kongkhak puan inn khialh ah kipuak a, i inn vengte in hong tawi uh hi.

records.english: It might be easier to give the shoes to your cousin than to return them.
records.zomi: Khedapte lohsak kik sangin na sanggam kiangah piak a baih zaw kha ding hi.

records.english: At this shop, shoes that have been worn outside can't be returned.
records.zomi: Hih dawl ah polam ah kisilh khin khedapte lohsak kik theih lo hi.

records.english: Grandpa's new radio was replaced after the volume button fell off.
records.zomi: Pu' radio thak ging khinna a kitat khit ciangin a thak tawh kilai hi.

records.english: Who's taking the broken fan back to the shop?
records.zomi: Fan siat dawl ah kua in a lohsak kik ding hiam?

records.english: I'll do it on my way to work tomorrow.
records.zomi: Zingciang nasep ka pai lam ah kei in ka sem ding hi.

records.english: My niece accidentally ordered ten boxes of crayons instead of one.
records.zomi: Ka tunu in a khialh-in bawm khat sangin crayon bawm sawm a sap hi.

records.english: The shop told us that unopened toys can be returned until the end of January.
records.zomi: Kihong nai lo tawngte January kha tawp dong lohsak kik theih hi, ci-in dawl in hong gen hi.

records.english: Could we exchange the baby clothes for a larger size, since he's growing so fast?
records.zomi: Amah a khang manlang mahmah ahih manin naungek puan a lian zaw tawh i lai thei ding hiam?

records.english: We decided to keep the slightly scratched table rather than wait weeks for a new one.
records.zomi: Kal tampi sung a thak ngak sangin a kikhuai zekai dawhkan kem dingin i khensat hi.

records.english: Our daughter's school bag was replaced for free after the strap broke.
records.zomi: I tanu' sang ip a khau a tat khit ciangin a man om lo-in a thak tawh kilai hi.

records.english: Can you help me pack the television back into its box?
records.zomi: Television a bawm sungah ka koih kik nadingin hong huh thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Our church asks families to give a tenth of their income, and we try to do that.
records.zomi: I pawlpi in innkuante a sum ngah sawm-a-khat piak dingin a ngen a, tua bangin sep i hanciam hi.

records.english: Is it fair that the oldest son pays his younger brothers' school fees?
records.zomi: Tapa upa pen in a nau pasalte' sang man a piak pen a dik ahi hiam?

records.english: In our family, it's expected, but we always thank him for it.
records.zomi: I innkuan ah tua bangin a kilamen hi, ahi zongin amah kiangah lungdam i ko tawntung hi.

records.english: Thank goodness we had some savings when the baby came early.
records.zomi: Naungek hun ma-a a suak ciangin sum kholsa tawmno i neih manin lungdam huai hi.

records.english: No new clothes for anyone until the school fees are paid.
records.zomi: Sang man kipia ma-in kuamah adingin puan thak om lo ding hi.

records.english: Should Grandma's pension go into the family account or stay with her?
records.zomi: Pi' pension pen innkuan account ah koih ding hiam, amah tawh om ding hiam?

records.english: She'd like to keep it so that she can buy the grandchildren treats.
records.zomi: Tu-te adingin nek ding nuam a lei theih nadingin amah in kem a deih hi.

records.english: Kids, from now on, part of every birthday gift goes straight into your savings.
records.zomi: Naupangte, tu-a kipan pianni letsong khempeuh pan tawmno pen na sum kholna ah koih pah ding hi.

records.english: Before we bought the land, we asked every adult in the family for their opinion.
records.zomi: Lei i lei ma-in innkuan sung a upa khempeuh' ngaihsutna i dong hi.

records.english: The roof had to be repaired after the storm, so we postponed buying a new motorbike.
records.zomi: Huihpi a nung ciangin inn tung bawl kik a kisam ahih manin motorbike thak lei i nusia hi.

records.english: Who decides how the money is spent in your house?
records.zomi: Na inn ah sum zat dan kua in a khensat hiam?

records.english: We decide together, but Grandma has the final word.
records.zomi: Khawm in i khensat hi, ahi zongin a tawpna thu pen Pi' thu ahi hi.

records.english: My uncle lost his job, so our family is helping with his rent for a few months.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in a nasep a mansuah ahih manin i innkuan in kha tawmno sung a inn man huh dingin i huh hi.

records.english: Shall we open a separate account for the children's school fees?
records.zomi: Naupangte' sang man adingin account tuam khat i hong ding hiam?

records.english: The bank was closed for the holiday, so we couldn't pay the school on time.
records.zomi: Tawlngakni ahih manin bank kikhak ahih manin sang man a hun takin i pia thei kei hi.

records.english: Every coin is counted in our house, because we're saving for my brother's operation.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal' khamna adingin i khol ahih manin i inn ah dangka khempeuh kisim hi.

records.english: Uncle Thang paid for our son's school uniform, and we'll never forget his kindness.
records.zomi: Pa neu Thang in i tapa' sang puan man a pia a, a hehpihna i mangngilh ngei kei ding hi.

records.english: The money for our daughter's wedding was saved over ten years.
records.zomi: I tanu' kiteenna adingin sum kum sawm sung kikhol hi.

records.english: The children each have a piggy bank, and they save half of any money they're given.
records.zomi: Naupangte in sum kholna bawm khat ciat a nei uh a, a ngah sum khempeuh a kim pen a khol uh hi.

records.english: I really do want our children to understand where the money comes from.
records.zomi: I tate in sum koi pan hong pai hiam a theih ding uh ka deih taktak hi.

records.english: How does your family plan for years when the harvest is poor?
records.zomi: Na innkuan in buh a phat loh kumte adingin bangci a kibawl hiam?

records.english: We put aside part of every good harvest so that we never go hungry in a bad year.
records.zomi: Kum hoih a buh lak simin tawmno i koih tuam ahih manin kum sia ah i gilkial ngei kei hi.

records.english: Saving for a house has meant fewer holidays, but the children understand why.
records.zomi: Inn lei dingin sum khol ahih manin tawlngakni khualzinna a tawm zaw a, ahi zongin bang hang hiam naupangte in a thei uh hi.

records.english: Our electricity was cut off once because a bill was forgotten, and we've been careful ever since.
records.zomi: Man piak ding mangngilh ahih manin vei khat meivak kitan a, tua pan kipan limtakin i kidawm hi.

records.english: Grandpa says we spend too much on mobile data.
records.zomi: Pu in mobile data ah sum tam lua i zang hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Is it all right if we skip the family holiday this year to pay for the new roof?
records.zomi: Inn tung thak man i piak theih nadingin tu kum innkuan tawlngakni khualzinna i nusia leh a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: We planned every expense for the move, but the truck still cost twice what we expected.
records.zomi: Inn pemna adingin sum zat ding khempeuh i gel a, ahi zongin mawtaw lian man i lamen sangin a nih in a tam hi.

records.english: Can we afford to send both girls to university in the city?
records.zomi: Tanu nih khuapi sangpi ah i khak zo ding hiam?

records.english: Only if we start saving now and give up some of our extras.
records.zomi: Tu-a kipan sum i khol a, i kisam lo nate tawmno i nusia leh bek.

records.english: Our relatives in the village receive a share of our income every month.
records.zomi: Khua sung a om i beh leh phungte in kha simin i sum ngah tan khat a ngah uh hi.

records.english: My brother-in-law offered to help with the cost of the wedding photographer.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu' pasal in kiteenna lim lapa' man huh dingin a kiciam hi.

records.english: We borrowed money from my uncle to start the shop, and we paid it back within two years.
records.zomi: Dawl kipat nadingin ka pa neu kiang pan sum i leitawi a, kum nih sungin i lohsak kik hi.

records.english: Planning our budget together has helped all three generations understand each other's needs.
records.zomi: Khawm-a i sum zat ding i gelh khawm manin suak thum in a kisapna uh a kithei khawm uh hi.

records.english: Do you keep track of what you spend each week?
records.zomi: Kal simin na zat sum na gelh hiam?

records.english: It's hard to say no to relatives who ask for money.
records.zomi: Sum a ngen beh leh phungte nial a haksa hi.

records.english: Are we saving for anything special this year?
records.zomi: Tu kum na tuam khat adingin i khol hiam?

records.english: Yes — a water tank, so that we don't have to carry water from the river.
records.zomi: Khol hi — tui tank khat, gun pan tui i puak nawn loh nadingin.

records.english: Grandpa keeps the household money in a locked box, and nobody touches it without asking him.
records.zomi: Pu in innsung sum pen bawm khatah a khak a, a kiang ah dong lo-in kuamah in a khoih kei hi.

records.english: My sister keeps a notebook of every gift and loan in the family so that nothing is forgotten.
records.zomi: Bangmah a mangngilh loh nadingin ka sanggam nu in innkuan sung letsong leh leitawi khempeuh notebook khat ah a gelh hi.

records.english: The money was divided equally between the brothers after the land was sold.
records.zomi: Lei a zuak khit uh ciangin sum pen sanggam pasalte kikal ah a kibang in kihawm hi.

records.english: You can buy one new thing this month, so choose wisely.
records.zomi: Tu kha na thak khat na lei thei ahih manin pil takin teel in.

records.english: My cousin sends us money from abroad when the harvest fails.
records.zomi: Buh a phat loh ciangin ka sanggam in gamdang pan sum hong khak hi.

records.english: Why does our grocery money always run out before the last week?
records.zomi: Bang hangin i an lei sum kal nunung pen ma-in a bei tawntung hiam?

records.english: Because your aunt's family always comes to stay right after payday!
records.zomi: Sum ngah ni khit pah-in na ni' innkuan in hong om dingin hong pai tawntung uh ahih manin!

records.english: "A family that saves together never has to borrow," my grandmother used to say.
records.zomi: “Khawm-a sum a khol innkuan in leitawi kul ngei lo hi,” ka pi in a ci zel hi.

records.english: Could we make a list of everything we spend in a month?
records.zomi: Kha khat sungin i zat sum khempeuh list khat i bawl thei ding hiam?

records.english: Has the rent been paid this month?
records.zomi: Tu kha inn man kipia khin hiam?

records.english: Yes, I paid it yesterday.
records.zomi: Kipia khin hi, zanni-in ka pia hi.

records.english: Should we have a big wedding, or use the money for a deposit on a house?
records.zomi: Kiteenna lian i bawl ding hiam, a sum tawh inn lei nadingin a man masa i pia ding hiam?

records.english: Our budget was ruined when the car broke down two days before Christmas.
records.zomi: Christmas ma ni nih-in mawtaw a siat ciangin i sum zat ding gelna a sia hi.

records.english: Could you help your grandparents work out their monthly budget?
records.zomi: Na pu leh na pite' kha khat sum zat ding gelna na huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: We share one car between three households, which saves everyone money.
records.zomi: Innkuan thum in mawtaw khat i kihawm a, tua in mi khempeuh sum hong khol sak hi.

records.english: Please don't lend money to your cousin again until he pays back the last loan.
records.zomi: Na sanggam in a leitawi nunung a lohsak kik ma-in sum leitawi nawn kei in.

records.english: Every New Year, the whole family sits down to decide what we can afford in the coming months.
records.zomi: Kum Thak simin innkuan bup tu-in kha hong ding sungin bang i lei zo ding hiam i khensat hi.

records.english: How much do you set aside each month for your children's education?
records.zomi: Na tate' pilna adingin kha simin bangzah na koih tuam hiam?

records.english: About a fifth of what we earn, though some months it's less.
records.zomi: I sum ngah a nga-a-khat bang, ahi zongin kha khenkhatah a tawm zaw hi.

records.english: We were told that the cost of the funeral would be shared among all the relatives.
records.zomi: Misi vuina man pen beh leh phung khempeuh in kihawm ding hi, ci-in hong gen uh hi.

records.english: Spending money on education is never a waste, our father always told us.
records.zomi: Pilna adingin sum zat pen a mawk ngei kei hi, ci-in i pa in hong hilh tawntung hi.

records.english: Medical bills from Dad's operation took most of our savings last year.
records.zomi: Pa' khamna adingin zato man in kum bei-in i sum kholsa a tam zaw a zang hi.

records.english: Since we started growing our own vegetables, our food bill has dropped a lot.
records.zomi: Anteh i khawi kipat pan i an lei man tampi a kiam hi.

records.english: Kids, play nicely with your cousins' friends — they're guests here too.
records.zomi: Naupangte, na sanggamte' lawmte tawh hoih takin kimawl un — amaute zong hih ah khual ahi uh hi.

records.english: Shall I ask your teacher whether you can sit with your friends?
records.zomi: Na lawmte tawh na tu thei ding hiam na saya kiangah ka dong ding hiam?

records.english: I was told that my father's best friend saved his life during the war.
records.zomi: Ka pa' lawm hoih pen in galkap lai-in a nuntakna a hum hi, ci-in hong gen uh hi.

records.english: Our two families became close after we helped each other rebuild following the storm.
records.zomi: Huihpi nung-a kihuh khawm-a i inn i lam kik khit ciangin i innkuan nih a kinai mahmah hi.

records.english: I really do want my children to choose their friends wisely.
records.zomi: Ka tate in a lawmte uh pil takin a teel ding uh ka deih taktak hi.

records.english: Making friends as a family takes time, but it's worth it.
records.zomi: Innkuan-in lawm bawl pen hun a sau a, ahi zongin a manpha hi.

records.english: Joining the parents' committee at school helped me meet other families in town.
records.zomi: Sang ah nu leh pate' committee ah ka kihel manin khua sung innkuan dangte ka mu thei hi.

records.english: Since kindergarten, Dad and his best friend have done everything together.
records.zomi: Kindergarten pan kipan Pa leh a lawm hoih pen in na khempeuh khawm in a sem uh hi.

records.english: Is it okay if your friends come to the farm this weekend?
records.zomi: Hih kal tawp-in na lawmte lo ah a hong pai uh leh a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: Sure, as long as their parents agree.
records.zomi: Hoih hi, a nu leh pate uh a lungkim uh leh.

records.english: My friend's parents treated me like their own son when I studied in the city.
records.zomi: Khuapi ah sang ka kah laitakin ka lawm' nu leh pa in amau tapa bangin hong koih uh hi.

records.english: Are you allowed to have friends over on school nights?
records.zomi: Sang kah ding zan ciangin na lawmte inn ah a hong pai thei uh hiam?

records.english: Only on Fridays, and only if our homework is done.
records.zomi: Laithai ni ciangin bek, inn-a sep ding i zawh khit leh bek.

records.english: Is it true that you and my uncle were friends at school?
records.zomi: Nang leh ka pa neu sang ah na kilawm uh hi, cih a man hiam?

records.english: We were, and we got into a lot of trouble together.
records.zomi: Kilawm hi, khawm in buaina tampi i tuak hi.

records.english: My nephew's best friend lives in another country, but they play games together online every evening.
records.zomi: Ka tanau' lawm hoih pen gamdang ah a om a, ahi zongin nitak simin online tawh games khawm in a mawl uh hi.

records.english: Kids, be kind to the new family — they don't know anyone here yet.
records.zomi: Naupangte, innkuan thakte tung ah hehpihna nei un — hih ah kuamah a thei nai kei uh hi.

records.english: Could we invite Grandpa's new friend from the park to the barbecue?
records.zomi: Pu' huan pan a lawm thak sa khuk an ah i sam thei ding hiam?

records.english: A misunderstanding between our wives nearly ended our friendship, but we talked it through.
records.zomi: I zite' kikal-a kitheih khialhna in i kilawmna a tawpsak kha dek a, ahi zongin i kikum siang hi.

records.english: How did your family become so close to the Lians?
records.zomi: Na innkuan Lian innkuan tawh bangci-in a kinai mahmah hiam?

records.english: Our children were in the same class, and we started sharing rides to school.
records.zomi: I tate kilasi khat ah a om uh a, sang ah mawtaw i kihawm kipan hi.

records.english: Did you make any friends at the summer camp?
records.zomi: Khal camp ah lawm na ngah hiam?

records.english: Lots, and we're going to write to each other every month!
records.zomi: Tam mahmah, kha simin lai i kikhak ding uh hi!

records.english: My little brother made friends with every child at the beach within an hour.
records.zomi: Ka nau pasal in nai khat sungin tuipi gei a om naupang khempeuh tawh a kilawm hi.

records.english: How long have you and Mary been friends?
records.zomi: Nang leh Mary kum bangzah na kilawm uh hiam?

records.english: Since we were nine, when our mothers started a sewing group together.
records.zomi: I nu te in puan khuina pawl a phut khawm uh pan, kum kua i phak uh lai pan.

records.english: She told me, "Friends are the family you choose."
records.zomi: Amah in, “Lawmte pen nang mah in na teel innkuan ahi hi,” hong ci hi.

records.english: Our families celebrate Christmas together every year, even though we aren't related.
records.zomi: Beh leh phung hi lo i hih hangin i innkuan te in kum simin Christmas khawm in i bawl hi.

records.english: Nobody expected my mother and my mother-in-law to become best friends.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka sungnu a kilawm pen ding uh kuamah in a lamen kei hi.

records.english: Grandpa's chess partner from the park now comes to our house every Sunday.
records.zomi: Huan pan Pu' chess mawl khawmpa tu-in Nipini simin i inn ah hong pai hi.

records.english: When my old friend moved back to the village, I was the last to hear about it.
records.zomi: Ka lawm lui khua ah a ciah kik ciangin a za nunung pen kei ka hi hi.

records.english: Please don't invite anyone over while we're out.
records.zomi: I om lo laitakin kuamah sam kei in.

records.english: My daughter's best friend was hurt when she wasn't invited to the party.
records.zomi: Ka tanu' lawm hoih pen pawi ah sap a hih loh manin a lungkham hi.

records.english: Why don't you invite your new classmate's family for lunch on Sunday?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na kilasi lawm thak' innkuan Nipini sun an ah na sam kei hiam?

records.english: "Any friend of my daughter's is welcome in this house," her father told me.
records.zomi: “Ka tanu' lawm khempeuh hih inn ah kidawn hi,” ci-in a pa in hong gen hi.

records.english: Our son finally found a friend who loves trains as much as he does.
records.zomi: I tapa in amah bangmah-a meileng a it lawm khat a mu tawp hi.

records.english: The friendship between our grandfathers started at the same village school seventy years ago.
records.zomi: I pute' kilawmna kum sawmsagih paisa-in khua sang khat ah kipan hi.

records.english: Our neighbor's daughter and ours were born a week apart and have been friends ever since.
records.zomi: I inn veng' tanu leh i tanu kal khat kikhel-in a suak uh a, tua pan a kilawm uh hi.

records.english: My pen pal from another country finally visited us after ten years of letters.
records.zomi: Gamdang a om lai kikhak lawm in kum sawm sung lai a kikhak khit ciangin hong veh tawp hi.

records.english: Our children's friendships have taught us to be more open to people from other backgrounds.
records.zomi: I tate' lawmte in mi khangthu tuamte tung ah lungsim honna hong hilh hi.

records.english: Thank you for being such a good friend to my daughter.
records.zomi: Ka tanu adingin lawm hoih mahmah na hih manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: Please don't let him play with those older boys after dark.
records.zomi: Khua a mial khit ciangin tua pasal upa zawte tawh kimawl sak kei in.

records.english: Can my friend stay for dinner, since her parents are working late?
records.zomi: Ka lawm' nu leh pa a nai sau sem ahih manin nitak an ah om thei ding hiam?

records.english: Friends who have known you since childhood are like family.
records.zomi: Naupan lai pan hong thei lawmte innkuan bang ahi uh hi.

records.english: We met our closest family friends on a camping trip twenty years ago.
records.zomi: Kum sawmnih paisa-in puan inn khualzinna khat ah innkuan lawm kinai pen i mu hi.

records.english: After Grandma died, Grandpa's old army friends visited him every week.
records.zomi: Pi a sih khit ciangin Pu' galkap lawm luite kal simin a veh uh hi.

records.english: We lost touch for years, but social media brought us back together.
records.zomi: Kum tampi kimu lo-in i om a, ahi zongin social media in hong kituahsak kik hi.

records.english: Old friends are the ones who remember your grandparents' names.
records.zomi: Lawm luite pen na pu leh na pite' min a phawk mite ahi uh hi.

records.english: What do you look for in a friend?
records.zomi: Lawm ah bang na zong hiam?

records.english: Someone who is honest and who stays when things get hard.
records.zomi: Thuman a gen a, haksatna hun ah om den mi khat.

records.english: Some of the friends I made at university are now godparents to my children.
records.zomi: Sangpi ah ka ngah lawm khenkhatte tu-in ka tate' tuiphumna-a pa leh nu ding a kiciamte ahi uh hi.

records.english: Moving abroad, I was afraid I'd never have close friends again.
records.zomi: Gamdang ah ka pem ciangin lawm kinai ka nei nawn kei ding ci-in ka lau hi.

records.english: My best friend from childhood is now my son's godfather.
records.zomi: Ka naupan lai-a lawm hoih pen tu-in ka tapa' tuiphumna-a pa ding a kiciampa ahi hi.

records.english: Who's the girl your daughter is always talking about?
records.zomi: Na tanu in a gen tawntung numei naupang pen kua ahi hiam?

records.english: Her new friend from the dance class, Grace.
records.zomi: Lam kisinna pan a lawm thak, Grace.

records.english: We do want our kids to have friends from all kinds of families.
records.zomi: I tate in innkuan namkim pan lawm a neih uh i deih taktak hi.

records.english: In our house, nobody goes to a friend's house without telling us first.
records.zomi: I inn ah kuamah in hong gen masa lo-in lawm' inn ah a pai kei hi.

records.english: Grandma has made more friends since joining the church choir than she had in years.
records.zomi: Pi in pawlpi la sa pawl ah a kihel pan kum tampi sung a neih sangin lawm tam zaw a ngah hi.

records.english: Is your mother still friends with the woman she met at the hospital?
records.zomi: Na nu in zato ah a theih numei tawh a kilawm lai uh hiam?

records.english: Yes, they meet for tea every Thursday.
records.zomi: Kilawm lai uh hi, Laizing ni simin tea dawn dingin a kimu uh hi.

records.english: Have you invited your grandmother's sisters to the wedding yet?
records.zomi: Kiteenna ah na pi' sanggam nute na sam khin hiam?

records.english: Yes, Dad drove to their village to invite them in person.
records.zomi: Sam khin hi, Pa in amaute mai tum-a sam dingin a khua uh ah mawtaw a tuan hi.

records.english: Everyone in the family is invited, including the cousins from abroad.
records.zomi: Gamdang a om sanggamte kihel-in innkuan sung mi khempeuh kisam hi.

records.english: Our daughter's friends were invited for a sleepover, and the house was noisy until midnight.
records.zomi: I tanu' lawmte zan giak dingin kisam uh a, zan lai dong inn a buai hi.

records.english: The invitation was delivered by hand, along with a bag of sweets.
records.zomi: Samna lai pen a khut tawh kipia a, a khum neu ip khat tawh kipia hi.

records.english: Inviting both sides of the family to the same dinner took a lot of courage.
records.zomi: Nitak an khat ah innkuan lam nih tengteng sam ding hangsanna tampi a kisam hi.

records.english: Would your family like to spend the festival with us this year?
records.zomi: Tu kum na innkuan in pawi pen hong khawm thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: We'd love to — the children have been asking when they can see their cousins.
records.zomi: Ka deih mahmah uh hi — naupangte in a sanggamte uh bang ciangin a mu thei ding uh hiam ci-in a dong den uh hi.

records.english: My aunt was offended because her invitation arrived after everyone else's.
records.zomi: Ka ni' samna lai mi dang khempeuh' nung ciangin a tun manin a lungkham hi.

records.english: Is it all right to invite my classmates to the family picnic?
records.zomi: Innkuan picnic ah ka kilasi lawmte ka sam thei ding hiam?

records.english: Sure, but tell them to bring their own drinks.
records.zomi: Thei hi, ahi zongin amau dawn ding a tawi ding uh gen in.

records.english: When Grandpa fell ill, the party was moved to his house so that he wouldn't miss it.
records.zomi: Pu a cina ciangin a mansuah loh nadingin pawi pen a inn ah kituah hi.

records.english: Please, Grandpa, come and sit at the head of the table tonight.
records.zomi: Pu, tu zanin dawhkan lu lam ah hong tu in.

records.english: What time do you want the relatives to arrive?
records.zomi: Beh leh phungte bang hun ciangin a hong tun ding uh na deih hiam?

records.english: Around eleven, so that there's time to eat before the speeches.
records.zomi: Nai sawm leh khat bang, thugente ma-in an nek theih nadingin.

records.english: You all must come to our house for lunch after church on Sunday.
records.zomi: Nipini pawlpi khit ciangin note khempeuh sun an dingin i inn ah na hong pai mawk ding uh hi.

records.english: Thank you for inviting us — we wouldn't miss it for the world!
records.zomi: Hong sap manin ka lungdam uh hi — bangci zongin mansuah lo ding hi!

records.english: We do hope your whole family can join us for our anniversary.
records.zomi: Kumpi ni-in na innkuan bup in hong kihel thei ding uh i lamen taktak hi.

records.english: Our door is always open to you and your children.
records.zomi: Nang leh na tate adingin i kongkhak kihong den hi.

records.english: Sorry, but we've already promised to visit my wife's parents that weekend.
records.zomi: Hehpih ning, tua kal tawp ciangin ka zi' nu leh pa veh dingin i kiciam khin hi.

records.english: We sent invitations to everyone in the village, because leaving anyone out would have been rude.
records.zomi: Kuamah nusia pen zahtakna om lo ahih manin khua sung mi khempeuh samna lai i khak hi.

records.english: I really do want your parents to come for the New Year this time.
records.zomi: Tu-in Kum Thak ah na nu leh na pa a hong pai ding uh ka deih taktak hi.

records.english: We invited the whole extended family, and more than a hundred people came.
records.zomi: Beh leh phung khempeuh i sam a, mi za khat val hong pai uh hi.

records.english: The family next door invited us to eat with them on the first night of the festival.
records.zomi: I inn veng innkuan in pawi zan masa pen-in an ne khawm dingin hong sam uh hi.

records.english: Grandma was invited to cut the cake because she's the oldest guest.
records.zomi: Khual upa pen ahih manin cake at dingin Pi kisam hi.

records.english: Who's on the guest list for the christening?
records.zomi: Tuiphumna adingin khual list ah kua te a om uh hiam?

records.english: Mostly family, plus a few close friends from church.
records.zomi: A tam zaw innkuan, pawlpi pan lawm kinai tawmno tawh.

records.english: "We'd be honored if you would bless our new house," we told the pastor.
records.zomi: “I inn thak na thupha piak leh zahtakna i sa ding hi,” ci-in pastor kiangah i gen hi.

records.english: Kids, help me fold these invitations and put them in the envelopes.
records.zomi: Naupangte, hih samna laite hong khiat sak unla lai-ip sungah koih un.

records.english: The cousins who live overseas joined the celebration by video call.
records.zomi: Gamdang a om sanggamte in video call tawh poai ah a kihel uh hi.

records.english: Uncle Thang was so happy to be invited that he arrived two hours early.
records.zomi: Pa neu Thang sap ahih manin a lungdam mahmah ahih manin nai nih ma-in hong tung hi.

records.english: It would mean a lot to us if your grandmother could come too.
records.zomi: Na pi zong a hong pai thei leh i adingin a thupi mahmah ding hi.

records.english: My cousin's invitation was lost in the post, so she didn't know about the party.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam' samna lai post sungah a mang ahih manin pawi thu a thei kei hi.

records.english: Could you write the invitations in our language for the older relatives?
records.zomi: Beh leh phung upate adingin samna laite i pau tawh na gelh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Should we bring the children, or is it just for adults?
records.zomi: Naupangte i paipih ding hiam, a upate bek ading hiam?

records.english: Would it be strange to invite my ex-wife to our daughter's graduation?
records.zomi: I tanu' sang zawhna poai ah ka zi lui sam pen a lamdang ding hiam?

records.english: Not at all — she's still your daughter's mother.
records.zomi: Lamdang lo hi — na tanu' nu ahi lai hi.

records.english: I'd love for you all to come and see our new home.
records.zomi: I inn thak en dingin na vekpi un hong pai uh leh ka deih mahmah hi.

records.english: In our family, the oldest relatives are always invited first, and always face to face.
records.zomi: I innkuan ah beh leh phung upa pente a masa-in kisam tawntung a, mai tum-in kisam tawntung hi.

records.english: Did you get the invitation to Lian's engagement party?
records.zomi: Lian' kiteen dinga kiciamna poai samna lai na ngah hiam?

records.english: Yes, it came in the mail yesterday with a lovely photo of the couple.
records.zomi: Ngah hi, zanni-in mail tawh a zi leh pasal ding lim hoih tawh hong tung hi.

records.english: When our new baby was born, we invited both grandmothers to stay for a month.
records.zomi: I naungek thak a suak ciangin pi nih tengteng kha khat sung om dingin i sam hi.

records.english: Bring everyone — there'll be plenty of food.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh hong paipih in — an tampi om ding hi.

records.english: Nobody had told Grandpa about the surprise, so the look on his face when he walked in was priceless.
records.zomi: Lamdang thu kuamah in Pu kiangah a gen kei uh ahih manin a hong lut ciangin a mai a kilatna man sim theih lo hi.

records.english: My grandmother insisted on inviting the whole street to her ninetieth birthday.
records.zomi: Ka pi in a kum sawmkua pianni ah lam bup mi khempeuh sam dingin a ngiat hi.

records.english: How do you invite older relatives in your family?
records.zomi: Na innkuan ah beh leh phung upate bangci-in na sam uh hiam?

records.english: We visit them with a small gift and ask them in person, never by phone.
records.zomi: Letsong neu khat tawh i veh uh a, mai tum-in i sam uh hi, phone tawh i sam ngei kei uh hi.

records.english: Kids, you can each invite three friends to your birthday party.
records.zomi: Naupangte, na pianni pawi ah lawm thum ciat na sam thei uh hi.

records.english: I'm afraid our family can't come; my brother is getting married the same day.
records.zomi: Hehpih ning, i innkuan i pai thei kei ding uh hi; tua ni mahmah-in ka sanggam pasal a kiteen ding hi.

records.english: My sister phoned every relative herself so that nobody would feel forgotten.
records.zomi: Kuamah in mangngilh in a om a kisak loh nadingin ka sanggam nu in beh leh phung khempeuh amah mah in phone tawh a sam hi.

records.english: We hadn't seen my wife's cousins for ten years until we invited them for Christmas.
records.zomi: Christmas ah i sap ma-in ka zi' sanggamte kum sawm sung i mu nai kei hi.

records.english: Could you call Aunt Ruth and invite her personally, since she's easily hurt?
records.zomi: Ni Ruth a lungkham baih ahih manin phone tawh amah mah na sam thei ding hiam?

records.english: Is it okay if I bring my grandfather, since he doesn't like being alone in the evenings?
records.zomi: Ka pu in nitak ciangin amah bek a om a deih loh manin ka paipih leh a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: Why don't we invite the new pastor and his family for lunch?
records.zomi: Bang hangin pastor thak leh a innkuan sun an ah i sam kei hiam?

records.english: Invite your friend's parents too, so that they can meet us.
records.zomi: Hong kitheih theih nadingun na lawm' nu leh pa zong sam in.

records.english: Shall we invite Uncle Pau, even though he and Dad haven't spoken for years?
records.zomi: Pa neu Pau leh Pa kum tampi a kiho kei uh hangin amah i sam ding hiam?

records.english: My brother-in-law has never refused an invitation to a meal in his life.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu' pasal in a nuntak sungin an nek dinga samna a nial ngei kei hi.

records.english: The invitations to the reunion were handwritten by the grandchildren.
records.zomi: Kikhopna samna laite tu-te in a khut tawh a gelh uh hi.

records.english: Could you invite your in-laws to the baby's naming ceremony?
records.zomi: Naungek min phuahna poai ah na sungte na sam thei ding hiam?

records.english: Our son's wedding invitations were printed in two languages for both families.
records.zomi: I tapa' kiteenna samna laite innkuan nih adingin pau nih tawh kisuaksak hi.

records.english: Kids, what do we say when Grandma gives us something?
records.zomi: Naupangte, Pi in na khat hong piak ciangin bang i ci ding hiam?

records.english: Thank you, Grandma!
records.zomi: Pi, ka lungdam hi!

records.english: We planted a tree outside the church to honor the couple who helped our family settle here.
records.zomi: I innkuan hih ah a om theih nadingin hong huh zi leh pasal zahtak nadingin pawlpi polam ah sing khat i suan hi.

records.english: The family photo album was made by our children as a thank-you gift for our anniversary.
records.zomi: I kumpi ni adingin lungdamna letsong-in innkuan lim bu pen i tate in a bawl uh hi.

records.english: We're so grateful to all of you for traveling such a long way for our wedding.
records.zomi: I kiteenna adingin hih bang khualzin sau na hong zin manun note khempeuh tungah ka lungdam mahmah uh hi.

records.english: Please tell your parents how much we enjoyed the dinner at their house.
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa' inn ah nitak an i nek nuam mahmah dan amaute kiangah gen sak in.

records.english: Is it enough to send a message, or should I visit to say thank you?
records.zomi: Message khak bek a cing hiam, lungdam ka kohna dingin ka veh ding hiam?

records.english: Visit if you can — it'll mean much more to her.
records.zomi: Na theih leh veh in — amah adingin a thupi zaw mahmah ding hi.

records.english: Shall we give the nurses a box of cookies to thank them for looking after Grandpa?
records.zomi: Pu a kem manun lungdam kohna-in nurse te cookie bawm khat i pia ding hiam?

records.english: My father-in-law's eyes filled with tears when the grandchildren sang for him.
records.zomi: Tu-te in a adingin la a sak ciangun ka sungpa' mit ah mittui a dim hi.

records.english: How can we show Aunt Mary how grateful we are for looking after the kids?
records.zomi: Naupangte a kep manin Ni Mary tung ah i lungdam dan bangci-in i lak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Maybe we could take her out for lunch and give her some flowers.
records.zomi: Sun an ne dingin i paipih inla pak tawmno i pia thei kha ding hi.

records.english: What's a good way to thank in-laws who have helped you a lot?
records.zomi: Hong huh mahmah sungte tung ah lungdam kohna dan hoih bang ahi hiam?

records.english: Spend time with them — that's what they want most.
records.zomi: Amaute tawh hun zang in — tua pen a deih pen uh ahi hi.

records.english: Our church thanked the families who cooked for the festival by giving each of them a small plant.
records.zomi: I pawlpi in pawi adinga an huan innkuante a khat ciat singkung neu khat pia-in lungdam a ko hi.

records.english: I didn't realize how much my parents had done for me until I had children of my own.
records.zomi: Kei mah in ta ka neih dong ka nu leh ka pa in kei adingin bangzah a sep uh hiam ka thei kei hi.

records.english: Grandma always says, "Gratitude costs nothing but means everything."
records.zomi: Pi in, “Lungdamna in bangmah a man om kei a, ahi zongin a thupi khempeuh ahi hi,” a ci tawntung hi.

records.english: What did your father say after your thank-you speech?
records.zomi: Na lungdam kohna thu na gen khit ciangin na pa in bang a ci hiam?

records.english: He just smiled and patted my shoulder, which said more than words.
records.zomi: Nuih bek a nui a, ka liang a dom hi, tua in kammal sangin a gen tam zaw hi.

records.english: My cousins put together a slideshow of old photos for our grandmother's eightieth birthday.
records.zomi: Ka sanggamte in i pi' kum sawmgiat pianni adingin lim lui tawh slideshow khat a bawl uh hi.

records.english: Why don't we cook dinner for Mom to thank her for organizing the reunion?
records.zomi: Kikhopna a vaihawm manin lungdam kohna-in bang hangin Nu adingin nitak an i huan kei hiam?

records.english: Could I give your father a small gift to thank him for the advice?
records.zomi: Thuhilhna a piak manin lungdam kohna-in na pa letsong neu khat ka pia thei ding hiam?

records.english: He'd love that, though he'll probably tell you it wasn't necessary.
records.zomi: A deih mahmah ding hi, ahi zongin a kisam kei hi, hong ci kha ding hi.

records.english: We do appreciate how much you help us with the twins.
records.zomi: Apengte tawh na hong huh mahmah dan i lungdam taktak hi.

records.english: Our uncle lent us his truck when we moved, and we've never forgotten it.
records.zomi: I pem ciangin i pa neu in a mawtaw lian hong leitawi a, i mangngilh ngei kei hi.

records.english: Our neighbor's kindness during my wife's illness will never be forgotten.
records.zomi: Ka zi a cina laitakin i inn veng' hehpihna kimangngilh ngei lo ding hi.

records.english: Thanking your elders properly is something every child in our family learns early.
records.zomi: Upate tungah a kilawm takin lungdam kohna pen i innkuan sung naupang khempeuh in a neu lai-in a sin uh hi.

records.english: I'm grateful that my cousin taught me to drive when nobody else had the patience.
records.zomi: Mi dang kuamah thuakzawhna a neih loh lai-in ka sanggam in mawtaw tuan hong hilh ahih manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: Hearing my own children thank me was the best birthday present I could have asked for.
records.zomi: Ka tate mah in lungdam hong kohna zak pen ka ngen thei pianni letsong hoih pen ahi hi.

records.english: The village school's new library was dedicated to my grandfather, who helped build the school.
records.zomi: Khua sang' laibu inn thak pen sang lam huh ka pu adingin kipia hi.

records.english: It was my mother who taught us always to thank people by name.
records.zomi: Mite' min tawh lungdam ko tawntung dingin hong hilh pen ka nu ahi hi.

records.english: Did you thank Grandma for the sweater she knitted?
records.zomi: Pi' khuih sweater adingin Pi tung ah lungdam na ko hiam?

records.english: Yes, I called her this morning, and she cried with happiness.
records.zomi: Ko hi, tu zingsangin ka sam a, a lungdamna tawh a kap hi.

records.english: We'll never be able to repay you, but we'll always remember what you did.
records.zomi: Kong thuk kik zo ngei lo ding uh hi, ahi zongin na sep na phawk den ding uh hi.

records.english: The children's drawings were taped to the fridge so that Grandpa could see how much they loved his gifts.
records.zomi: Pu' letsongte a it mahmah uh a muh theih nadingin naupangte' lim-gelhte khal bawm tungah kikap hi.

records.english: Thank you for treating me like your own daughter from the very first day.
records.zomi: Ni masa pen pan na tanu bangin hong koih manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: Thank you for the lovely gift — the kids haven't stopped playing with it.
records.zomi: Letsong hoih adingin ka lungdam hi — naupangte in a mawl tawp nai kei uh hi.

records.english: Do you know who sent Grandma the fruit basket?
records.zomi: Pi kiangah singgah bawm kua in a khak hiam na thei hiam?

records.english: It came from her old students, to thank her for years of teaching.
records.zomi: A sangnaupang luite pan a hong pai a, kum tampi sung a hilh manin lungdam a kohna uh ahi hi.

records.english: The thank-you card I sent to my host family arrived two months late.
records.zomi: Ka om sakna innkuan kiangah ka khak lungdam kohna card kha nih nung-in a tung hi.

records.english: Your thank-you note made my whole week.
records.zomi: Na lungdam kohna lai in ka kal bup hong lungdamsak hi.

records.english: Please give this jar of honey to your mother as a small thank-you.
records.zomi: Lungdam kohna neu-in hih khuaizu bel na nu kiangah pia sak in.

records.english: You've always been there for me, and I'm so grateful.
records.zomi: Kei adingin hong om den na hih manin ka lungdam mahmah hi.

records.english: Our family has a tradition of thanking the cook before anyone leaves the table.
records.zomi: I innkuan ah dawhkan kuamah a paisan ma-in an huan pa tungah lungdam kohna ngeina a om hi.

records.english: Our daughter wrote a speech to thank her grandparents at their golden wedding anniversary.
records.zomi: I tanu in a pu leh pi' kiteen kum sawmnga-na poai ah lungdam a kohna thu khat a gelh hi.

records.english: I really do want to thank my older sister for paying for my school books all those years.
records.zomi: Kum tampi sung ka sang laibu man a piak manin ka u nu tungah lungdam ka ko nuam taktak hi.

records.english: Kids, say thank you to Uncle Kap for driving us all the way here.
records.zomi: Naupangte, hih dong hong paipih manin Pa neu Kap tungah lungdam ko un.

records.english: I owe my cooking skills entirely to my grandmother.
records.zomi: Ka an huan siamna pen ka pi hang bek ahi hi.

records.english: My little sister thanked the bus driver with a drawing of his bus.
records.zomi: Ka nau numei in bus tuansakpa' bus lim a gelh tawh lungdam a ko hi.

records.english: Grandpa was given a standing ovation at his retirement party.
records.zomi: Pu' nasep khawlna poai ah mi khempeuh in a ding khia-in khut a beng uh hi.

records.english: I want to thank my in-laws for welcoming me into their family so warmly.
records.zomi: Lungsim lum takin a innkuan sungah hong muak manin ka sungte tungah lungdam ka ko nuam hi.

records.english: At our wedding, we thanked both sets of parents in front of all the guests.
records.zomi: I kiteenna ah khual khempeuh mai ah nu leh pa lam nih tengteng tungah lungdam i ko hi.

records.english: Would you help me write a thank-you letter to your teacher?
records.zomi: Na saya kiangah lungdam kohna lai ka gelh nadingin hong huh thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Every Christmas, the children make cards for the relatives who sent them gifts.
records.zomi: Christmas simin naupangte in letsong a hong khak beh leh phungte adingin card a bawl uh hi.

records.english: Grandpa, thank you for teaching me to fish — I'll never forget those mornings by the river.
records.zomi: Pu, nga man hong hilh manin ka lungdam hi — gun gei-a zingsangte ka mangngilh ngei lo ding hi.

records.english: We asked the whole family to sign a card for Dad's retirement.
records.zomi: Pa' nasep khawlna adingin card khat ah innkuan bup in min suaksak dingin i ngen hi.

records.english: Thank your aunt before you open the present.
records.zomi: Letsong na hon ma-in na ni tungah lungdam ko in.

records.english: Everyone, please raise your glasses to Mom and Dad on their fortieth anniversary!
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, Nu leh Pa' kiteen kum sawmli-na adingin na khuangte uh dawm un!

records.english: We wrote to the family who hosted our son abroad to thank them for their kindness.
records.zomi: Gamdang ah i tapa a om sakna innkuan kiangah a hehpihna uh lungdam kohna-in lai i khak hi.

records.english: "You gave up so much for us," I told my parents at my graduation.
records.zomi: “Kote adingin na tampi na nusia uh hi,” ci-in ka sang zawhna poai ah ka nu leh ka pa kiangah ka gen hi.

records.english: Do you teach your children to say sorry and to mean it?
records.zomi: Na tate maisak ngen dingin leh a lungsim taktak tawh gen dingin na hilh hiam?

records.english: Kids, both of you need to apologize to Grandpa for being so noisy during his nap.
records.zomi: Naupangte, Pu a ihmut laitakin na buai uh ahih manin note nih in Pu kiangah maisak ngen un.

records.english: My nephew apologized to his grandmother with a hug, and she forgave him instantly.
records.zomi: Ka tanau in a pi kiangah a kawi-in maisak a ngen a, a pi in pahtakin a maisak hi.

records.english: Who usually says sorry first in your family?
records.zomi: Na innkuan ah kua in maisak a ngen masa zel hiam?

records.english: Forgive me, Mom — I didn't mean to shout.
records.zomi: Nu, hong maisak in — kik ka sam ding ka ut kei hi.

records.english: How should children apologize to their grandparents in your family?
records.zomi: Na innkuan ah naupangte in a pu leh pite kiangah bangci-in maisak a ngen ding uh hiam?

records.english: They hold the grandparent's hand and promise to do better.
records.zomi: Pu hiam pi hiam' khut a len uh a, a hoih zaw-in sem dingin a kiciam uh hi.

records.english: Our family quarrel was finally settled when Grandma invited everyone to dinner.
records.zomi: Pi in mi khempeuh nitak an ah a sap ciangin i innkuan kiselna a bei tawp hi.

records.english: Did you and your old friend from the village ever patch things up?
records.zomi: Nang leh khua pan na lawm lui na kiphatuah kik uh hiam?

records.english: Yes, we laughed about it when we met at a wedding last spring.
records.zomi: Kiphatuah kik hi, spring nung in kiteenna khat ah i kimuh ciangin i nui khawm uh hi.

records.english: One careless comment at lunch spoiled the rest of the holiday.
records.zomi: Sun an laitakin pil lo taka thu khat gen in tawlngakni a taang a siatsak hi.

records.english: I'm sorry for not visiting more often; work has kept me so busy.
records.zomi: Ka veh tam loh manin hong maisak in; nasep in hong buai mahmah sak hi.

records.english: Why are you still angry with your cousin?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na sanggam tung ah na heh lai hiam?

records.english: Because he never apologized for what he said at the wedding.
records.zomi: Kiteenna ah a gen thu adingin maisak a ngen ngei kei ahih manin.

records.english: My daughter apologized to her teacher by writing a short poem.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in late tom khat gelh-in a saya kiangah maisak a ngen hi.

records.english: The phone call between the two sisters lasted three hours and ended in tears of relief.
records.zomi: Sanggam nu nih' phone kihona nai thum a sau a, lungdamna mittui tawh a tawp hi.

records.english: I apologized to my wife's parents for arriving so late on our first visit.
records.zomi: I veh masa pen-in ka tun nung lua ahih manin ka zi' nu leh pa kiangah maisak ka ngen hi.

records.english: Admitting he was wrong was never easy for Grandpa, but he always tried.
records.zomi: A khialhna pulak pen Pu adingin a baih ngei kei a, ahi zongin a hanciam tawntung hi.

records.english: It's hard for my grandmother to say sorry, but she shows it by cooking your favorite food.
records.zomi: Ka pi adingin maisak ngen a haksa a, ahi zongin na it pen an a huan sak tawh a lak hi.

records.english: My grandmother's letter of apology arrived on my wedding day, and I cried as I read it.
records.zomi: Ka pi' maisak ngenna lai ka kiteen ni-in hong tung a, ka sim laitakin ka kap hi.

records.english: Can I say sorry to Auntie tomorrow, when she's less upset?
records.zomi: Ni a lungkham tawm zaw ding zingciang ciangin maisak ka ngen thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, that's probably wise.
records.zomi: Thei hi, tua a pil zaw kha ding hi.

records.english: You all owe your mother an apology for leaving the kitchen in such a mess.
records.zomi: Anbuk na buaisak lua uh ahih manin note khempeuh in na nu kiangah maisak na ngen kul uh hi.

records.english: Shall we call Uncle Dal and say sorry together?
records.zomi: Pa neu Dal i sam inla khawm in maisak i ngen ding hiam?

records.english: Forgiveness kept our family together through some very difficult years.
records.zomi: Maisakna in kum haksa mahmah tampi sungin i innkuan hong kikhawmsak hi.

records.english: Forgiving my sister made me feel lighter than I had in years.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu ka maisak ciangin kum tampi sung ka kisak ngei loh dan-in ka lungsim a zang hi.

records.english: Could you help me write an apology letter to my in-laws?
records.zomi: Ka sungte kiangah maisak ngenna lai ka gelh nadingin hong huh thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: My little sister cried when she accidentally broke Mom's favorite bowl.
records.zomi: Nu' it pen khuang a khialh-in a khitam ciangin ka nau numei a kap hi.

records.english: Thank you for forgiving me so quickly.
records.zomi: Manlang takin hong maisak manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: How do you forgive a parent who wasn't there when you were growing up?
records.zomi: Na khanlai-in a om lo nu hiam pa hiam bangci-in na maisak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Slowly, and sometimes with help from people you trust.
records.zomi: Zawi takin, a kikhatvei na muang mite' huhna tawh.

records.english: It took years for Dad to forgive his brother, but now they go fishing together every Sunday.
records.zomi: Pa in a sanggam pasal maisak dingin kum tampi a sau a, ahi zongin tu-in Nipini simin nga man dingin khawm in a pai uh hi.

records.english: We glued the plate back together so that Grandma wouldn't be upset.
records.zomi: Pi a lungkham loh nadingin kuang i kikhuh kik hi.

records.english: My mother-in-law and I had a misunderstanding, but we sorted it out over a cup of tea.
records.zomi: Ka sungnu leh kei kitheih khialhna i nei a, ahi zongin tea khuang khat dawn kawmin i kikum siang hi.

records.english: I really do regret the things I said to my father before he moved away.
records.zomi: Ka pa a pem ma-in a kiangah ka gen thute ka khasia taktak hi.

records.english: After ten years of silence, my uncles finally forgave each other at their mother's funeral.
records.zomi: Kum sawm sung kiho lo-in a om khit uh ciangin ka pa neute in a nu uh' misi vuina ah a kimaisak tawp uh hi.

records.english: Is there anything I can do to show you I'm really sorry?
records.zomi: Maisak taktak ka ngen hi, cih kong lak theih nadingin bang ka sem thei ding hiam?

records.english: Just be on time next Sunday, that's all.
records.zomi: Nipini hong ding ciangin hun takah hong tung in, tua bek.

records.english: I do want to apologize to your parents in person, not just by phone.
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa kiangah phone tawh bek hi lo-in mai tum-in maisak ka ngen nuam taktak hi.

records.english: We repaired the fence we had broken so that the neighbors would accept our apology.
records.zomi: I inn vengte in i maisak ngenna a san theih nadingun i suksiat kulh i bawl kik hi.

records.english: Why don't you tell your father how you feel instead of staying angry?
records.zomi: Bang hangin heh lel lo-in na pa kiangah na lungsim na gen kei hiam?

records.english: I'm sorry I missed Grandma's birthday dinner; I should have called to explain.
records.zomi: Pi' pianni nitak an ka mansuah manin hong maisak in; ka sam-a ka gen kul hi.

records.english: When my brother-in-law admitted his mistake at dinner, the whole family respected him more.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu' pasal in nitak an laitakin a khialhna a pulak ciangin innkuan bup in a zahtak semsem uh hi.

records.english: Sorry for keeping you waiting — the baby wouldn't settle.
records.zomi: Hong ngaksak manin hong maisak in — naungek a dai thei kei hi.

records.english: My father-in-law said, "Let's forget the past and enjoy our grandchildren."
records.zomi: Ka sungpa in, “A bei khin thute mangngilh ni-in i tu-te tawh nuam takin om ni,” a ci hi.

records.english: Children, if you've hurt someone's feelings today, go and say sorry before dinner.
records.zomi: Naupangte, tuni-in kuamah' lungsim na natsak uh leh nitak an ma-in maisak va ngen un.

records.english: Will you forgive me if I promise to call every week?
records.zomi: Kal simin kong sam ding ci-in ka kiciam leh hong maisak ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Only if you actually do it this time!
records.zomi: Tu-in na sep taktak leh bek!

records.english: After years of silence, a single message from my cousin brought our families back together.
records.zomi: Kum tampi kiho lo-in i om khit ciangin ka sanggam' message khat in i innkuan te hong kituahsak kik hi.

records.english: Please forgive my son; he's only five and didn't understand.
records.zomi: Ka tapa hong maisak in; kum nga bek a pha a, a thei kei hi.

records.english: My parents taught us that saying sorry isn't enough unless you also try to fix things.
records.zomi: Na bawl kik dingin na hanciam kei leh maisak ngen bek in a cing kei hi, ci-in ka nu leh ka pa in hong hilh uh hi.

records.english: In our family, children apologize to their elders by bowing their heads and staying quiet.
records.zomi: I innkuan ah naupangte in a lu kun-in dai takin a om uh tawh a upate kiangah maisak a ngen uh hi.

records.english: Please don't punish him; he's already said sorry to everyone.
records.zomi: Amah gawt kei in; mi khempeuh kiangah maisak a ngen khin hi.

records.english: My grandfather never apologized in words, but he would bring me sweets after an argument.
records.zomi: Ka pu in kammal tawh maisak a ngen ngei kei a, ahi zongin i kiselna khit ciangin a khum neute hong tawi zel hi.

records.english: We called my aunt from the car to apologize for forgetting her anniversary.
records.zomi: Ka ni' kumpi ni i mangngilh manin maisak ngen dingin mawtaw sung pan amah i sam hi.

records.english: I hope you can accept my apology for what happened at the party.
records.zomi: Pawi ah a piang thu adingin ka maisak ngenna na san thei ding ka lamen hi.

records.english: Dad sent a long message to apologize for missing my graduation.
records.zomi: Pa in ka sang zawhna poai a mansuah manin maisak ngen dingin message sau khat hong khak hi.

records.english: Our family stopped speaking to my uncle for a while, but we've all forgiven him now.
records.zomi: I innkuan in hun tawmno sung ka pa neu tawh i kiho kei uh a, ahi zongin tu-in mi khempeuh in i maisak khin uh hi.

records.english: Have you apologized to your sister for breaking her bicycle?
records.zomi: Na sanggam nu' siiksakol na suksiat manin a kiangah maisak na ngen khin hiam?

records.english: Not yet, but I'm going to fix it first and then say sorry.
records.zomi: Ngen nai lo hi, ahi zongin a masa-in ka bawl kik ding a, tua khit ciangin maisak ka ngen ding hi.

records.english: "Talk to each other, not about each other," Grandma always told us.
records.zomi: “Khat leh khat kiho un, khat leh khat thu gen kei un,” ci-in Pi in hong hilh tawntung hi.

records.english: My father-in-law and I never agree about how to raise children, but we both love them dearly.
records.zomi: Ka sungpa leh kei naupang khak dan ah i kilem ngei kei a, ahi zongin i nih in amaute i it mahmah hi.

records.english: I'm not taking sides — I love you both.
records.zomi: Lam khat ka pang kei hi — note nih tengteng kong it hi.

records.english: After the argument, my brother sent me a funny picture, and I knew we were fine.
records.zomi: I kinial khit ciangin ka sanggam pasal in lim nuihsat huai khat hong khak a, i kilem kik hi, ka thei hi.

records.english: Grandpa and Dad disagree about farming, but they respect each other's experience.
records.zomi: Pu leh Pa lo sep thu ah a kilem kei uh a, ahi zongin khat leh khat' theihna a zahtak uh hi.

records.english: To avoid arguments, we agreed that the car is mine on weekdays and my sister's on weekends.
records.zomi: Kinial a om loh nadingin ni sem ni-in mawtaw pen keima' a hi a, kal tawp-in ka sanggam nu' a hi ding i kilem hi.

records.english: We disagree about whether the children should speak our home language in the house.
records.zomi: Naupangte in inn sungah i inn pau a zat ding uh hiam cih thu ah i kilem kei hi.

records.english: May I explain my side before you decide?
records.zomi: Na khensat ma-in ka lam thu ka gen thei ding hiam?

records.english: Mom and Dad disagreed about pocket money, so they agreed on a small amount plus a bonus for good grades.
records.zomi: Nu leh Pa naupangte' zat ding sum thu ah a kilem kei uh ahih manin sum tawmno leh sang mai-a ciam hoih ngah leh behlap piak dingin a kilem uh hi.

records.english: Could you two stop arguing long enough to help me carry this?
records.zomi: Note nih na kinial uh khawl unla hih ka puak nadingin hong huh thei ding na hi uh hiam?
