records.english: Put the kettle on, and we'll talk about it properly.
records.zomi: Tui-ukbel mei tungah koih inla, a kilawm takin i kikum ding hi.

records.english: Grandma listened to both grandchildren and gave each of them half of the last mango.
records.zomi: Pi in tu-te nih tengteng' thu a ngaikhia a, theihai nunung pen a kim ciat a pia hi.

records.english: Is it okay if I spend Christmas with my friends this year instead of with the family?
records.zomi: Tu kum innkuan tawh hi lo-in ka lawmte tawh Christmas ka zat leh a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: We'd rather you came home, but it's your decision.
records.zomi: Inn ah na hong ciah ding i deih zaw hi, ahi zongin nangma' khensatna ahi hi.

records.english: Our biggest family arguments usually happen right before holidays.
records.zomi: I innkuan kinialna lian pen tawlngakni ma pah ciangin a piang zel hi.

records.english: Grandpa wanted to sell the cows, but the rest of the family persuaded him to keep two.
records.zomi: Pu in bawngte zuak a deih a, ahi zongin innkuan a dangte in a nih kem dingin a sawl uh hi.

records.english: It took my parents years to agree on where to live, but they're very happy in the village now.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa a om nading mun ah a kilem nadingun kum tampi a sau a, ahi zongin tu-in khua ah a lungdam mahmah uh hi.

records.english: Can I keep the dog if I promise to walk him every day?
records.zomi: Ni simin ka kawikawi pih ding ci-in ka kiciam leh ui ka kem thei ding hiam?

records.english: We'll see — your father and I need to discuss it first.
records.zomi: En lai ni — na pa leh kei a masa-in i kikum kul hi.

records.english: Could each of us choose the TV program on different nights?
records.zomi: Zan tuam ciat-in i khat ciat in TV program i teel thei ding hiam?

records.english: Disagreeing with my parents taught me how to explain my opinions clearly.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa tawh ka kilem loh manin ka ngaihsutnate siangtak-a gen dan ka sin hi.

records.english: In our house, an argument isn't over until both people have said what they need to say.
records.zomi: I inn ah mi nih in a gen ding uh a gen khit mateng kinialna a bei kei hi.

records.english: Kids, if you can't share the bicycle, nobody rides it today.
records.zomi: Naupangte, siiksakol na kihawm thei kei uh leh tuni-in kuamah in a tuang kei ding hi.

records.english: Can we finish this conversation after the children are in bed?
records.zomi: Naupangte a ihmut khit uh ciangin hih kikupna i zom thei ding hiam?

records.english: Would it help if we asked your uncle to talk to both of you?
records.zomi: Note nih tawh hong kiho dingin na pa neu i ngen leh a huh ding hiam?

records.english: Maybe, since he's the only one they both listen to.
records.zomi: Huh kha ding hi, a nih in a thu a ngai uh mi khat bek ahih manin.

records.english: How do you settle arguments between your twins?
records.zomi: Na apengte' kinialna bangci-in na bawl siang hiam?

records.english: I listen to each of them separately before I decide anything.
records.zomi: Bangmah ka khensat ma-in a khat ciat' thu tuam ciat-in ka ngai hi.

records.english: Please talk more quietly — the neighbors can hear every word.
records.zomi: Dai zaw takin gen un — inn vengte in kammal khempeuh a za thei uh hi.

records.english: What do you do when your teenager won't listen to you?
records.zomi: Na ta khangno in na thu a ngaih kei ciangin bang na sem hiam?

records.english: I wait until we're both calm and then ask him what he really needs.
records.zomi: I nih in i lungsim a dai dong ka ngak a, tua khit ciangin a kisapna taktak ka dong hi.

records.english: Is it fair that I always have to share with my younger brother?
records.zomi: Ka nau pasal tawh ka kihawm tawntung kul pen a dik ahi hiam?

records.english: You're older, so you need to be a little more patient with him.
records.zomi: Na upa zaw ahih manin amah tungah thuakzawhna tawmno na nei zaw kul hi.

records.english: My sister and her husband have a rule that whoever is calmer speaks first.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu leh a pasal in a dai zaw pen in a gen masa ding, cih thukhun a nei uh hi.

records.english: The two brothers were made to shake hands before they could leave the table.
records.zomi: Sanggam pasal nih dawhkan a paisan theih ma-un khut kilen dingin kisawl hi.

records.english: After a long talk with our son, we agreed he could get a motorbike if he passed his test.
records.zomi: I tapa tawh sau takin i kikup khit ciangin a sitna a zawh leh motorbike a nei thei ding hi, i kilem hi.

records.english: My sister and I fought over the bedroom until Dad built a wall to divide it.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu leh kei Pa in a khen nadingin bang a lam dong lupna khan i kinial hi.

records.english: The quarrel about the wedding guest list was finally settled by my uncle.
records.zomi: Kiteenna khual list kinialna pen ka pa neu in a bawl siang tawp hi.

records.english: I really do want us to stop arguing about money in front of the children.
records.zomi: Naupangte' mai ah sum thu i kinial khawl ding ka deih taktak hi.

records.english: Why don't you both write down what's bothering you and swap papers?
records.zomi: Bang hangin note nih in hong lungkhamsak thu na gelh unla lai na kilai kei uh hiam?

records.english: Our neighbors' goats kept eating our vegetables until we agreed to build a better gate together.
records.zomi: Kongpi hoih zaw khat khawm-a lam dingin i kilem ma-in i inn vengte' kelte in i anteh a ne den uh hi.

records.english: Mom settled the argument by hiding the remote control until dinner was over.
records.zomi: Nu in nitak an a bei dong remote control a sel tawh kinialna a bawl siang hi.

records.english: Kids, nobody uses the computer until you agree on a schedule.
records.zomi: Naupangte, a hun zat ding na kilem ma-un kuamah in computer a zang kei ding hi.

records.english: Why are you two always arguing about the music?
records.zomi: Bang hangin note nih la thu ah na kinial tawntung uh hiam?

records.english: He plays it too loud, and I can't do my homework.
records.zomi: Ging sang lua-in a koih a, inn-a sep ding ka sem zo kei hi.

records.english: We couldn't agree on a name for the baby, so we each chose one and used both.
records.zomi: Naungek min ah i kilem thei kei ahih manin i khat ciat in khat i teel a, a nih tengteng i zang hi.

records.english: I do want to understand what really happened before anyone is punished.
records.zomi: Kuamah a kigawt ma-in a piang taktak ka theih ding ka deih taktak hi.

records.english: You can both use the laptop if you each have one hour.
records.zomi: Nai khat ciat na zat uh leh note nih in laptop na zang thei uh hi.

records.english: You both make good points, so let's try your idea first and mine next month.
records.zomi: Note nih na gen uh a hoih ciat ahih manin na ngaihsutna a masa-in i sem ding a, kei' pen kha hong ding ciangin.

records.english: We wrote our holiday ideas on slips of paper and drew one out of a hat.
records.zomi: I tawlngakni ngaihsutnate lai neute ah i gelh a, lukhu sung pan khat i la khia hi.

records.english: My cousins argued about whose turn it was to host the family, until my aunt offered her house.
records.zomi: Ka sanggamte in innkuan dawn ding kua' hun hiam a kinial uh a, ka ni in a inn a piak dong.

records.english: Children who argue a lot often grow up to be close friends, my grandmother says.
records.zomi: A kinial tam naupangte a khan ciangin lawm kinai suak zel uh hi, ci-in ka pi in a gen hi.

records.english: The disagreement between my aunts over the wedding seating lasted for weeks.
records.zomi: Kiteenna tutna thu ah ka nite' kilem lohna kal tampi sung a sau hi.

records.english: Should we let Grandma decide, since it's her house?
records.zomi: Amah' inn ahih manin Pi khensat sak ding hiam?

records.english: We agreed that whoever cooks doesn't have to wash the dishes.
records.zomi: An a huan pa in kuang a sil kul kei ding, i kilem hi.

records.english: Who started the fight this time?
records.zomi: Tu-in kua in kidona a kipat sak hiam?

records.english: It doesn't matter who started it; what matters is how we end it.
records.zomi: Kua in a kipat sak hiam a thupi kei hi; a thupi pen bangci i tawpsak ding hiam ahi hi.

records.english: Sometimes it's better to let the small arguments go.
records.zomi: Hun khenkhatah kinialna neute nusia a hoih zaw hi.

records.english: When I wanted to study abroad, my parents argued for weeks before Mom finally convinced Dad.
records.zomi: Gamdang ah sang kah ka deih ciangin ka nu leh ka pa kal tampi sung a kinial uh a, a tawp-in Nu in Pa a lungkimsak hi.

records.english: We moved the boys into separate rooms to stop them fighting every night.
records.zomi: Zan simin a kido loh nadingun pasal naupangte khan tuam ciat ah i koih hi.

records.english: Would it be all right if we parked in front of your parents' house?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa' inn mai ah mawtaw i koih leh a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: You may borrow my car if you know how to get to the farm.
records.zomi: Lo ah pai ding lampi na theih leh ka mawtaw na leitawi thei hi.

records.english: Aunt Mary got lost on her way to our new house, so I went out to meet her.
records.zomi: Ni Mary i inn thak hong pai lam ah lampi a mansuah ahih manin amah va dawn dingin ka pai khia hi.

records.english: Where should we meet if we get separated at the festival?
records.zomi: Pawi ah i kikhen kha leh koi ah i kimu kik ding hiam?

records.english: By the big tree at the entrance, where we always meet.
records.zomi: Lutna kongpi kiang singkung lian ah, i kimuh tawntungna mun ah.

records.english: Which ward is my grandmother in?
records.zomi: Ka pi ward bang ah a om hiam?

records.english: Take the lift to the third floor, and ask at the nurses' desk.
records.zomi: Lift tawh a thum-na dawl dong kah inla, nurse te' dawhkan ah dong in.

records.english: Is there a way to get to the farm without going through the city?
records.zomi: Khuapi tawng lo-in lo ah pai theih nading lampi a om hiam?

records.english: Yes, the old road through the forest, though it's bumpy.
records.zomi: Om hi, gam sung tawng lampi lui, a kuakuai napi.

records.english: Do you know which house my aunt moved into last month?
records.zomi: Ka ni kha bei-in inn bang ah a pem hiam na thei hiam?

records.english: Could you send the location of the wedding hall to my phone?
records.zomi: Kiteenna inn lian om na mun ka phone ah na khak thei ding hiam?

records.english: How do I explain the way to our house to someone who has never been here?
records.zomi: Hih ah hong tung ngei lo mi khat kiangah i inn lampi bangci-in ka gen ding hiam?

records.english: Tell them to take the second road after the petrol station and look for the church.
records.zomi: Petrol station khit ciangin a nihna lampi zui unla pawlpi zong dingin gen in.

records.english: Mom drove around the town three times before she found my sister's school.
records.zomi: Nu in ka sanggam nu' sang a muh ma-in khuapi vei thum a kawikawi hi.

records.english: Stay on this road until you see our family's name painted on the wall.
records.zomi: I innkuan min bang tungah a kigelh na muh dong hih lampi zui den in.

records.english: The way to my grandparents' house hasn't changed since I was a child.
records.zomi: Ka neu lai pan ka pu leh pite' inn lampi kikhel lo hi.

records.english: I really do want the kids to learn the way to their grandparents' village by heart.
records.zomi: Naupangte in a pu leh pite uh khua lampi a lungsim ah a phawk ding uh ka deih taktak hi.

records.english: Shall I write the directions in our language for your parents?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa adingin lampi i pau tawh ka gelh ding hiam?

records.english: In my village, people give directions by landmarks, like the old well or the big rock.
records.zomi: Ka khua ah mite in tuikhuk lui hiam suang lian hiam bang mun theih nading tawh lampi a gen uh hi.

records.english: Could you point me to the family who sells honey near the church?
records.zomi: Pawlpi kiang khuaizu a zuak innkuan om na mun hong lak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Everyone in the car was asleep except me, so I had to read the map myself.
records.zomi: Mawtaw sung ah kei bek tua lo mi khempeuh a ihmut uh ahih manin map kei mah in ka sim kul hi.

records.english: Look for the house covered in flowers; that's Grandma's.
records.zomi: Pak tawh a kikhuh inn zong in; tua pen Pi' inn ahi hi.

records.english: Turn left at the school where your mother used to teach.
records.zomi: Na nu' a hilhna sang ah veilam ah kiheei in.

records.english: Thank you for coming out to find us — we'd never have found the house alone.
records.zomi: Hong zong dingin na hong pai khiat manin ka lungdam hi — kote bek in inn i mu ngei lo ding uh hi.

records.english: We were guided to the right house by a group of children who ran ahead of the car.
records.zomi: Mawtaw ma-ah a tai naupang pawl khat in a man inn ah hong paipih uh hi.

records.english: Please ask your cousin to wait for us at the corner.
records.zomi: Na sanggam in a ki-ngawi mun ah hong ngak dingin ngen sak in.

records.english: Kids, if you ever get lost, find a shopkeeper and ask them to call us.
records.zomi: Naupangte, lampi na mansuah kha leh dawl neipa khat zong unla hong sam sak dingin ngen un.

records.english: My niece drew a little map so that her friends could find our house.
records.zomi: A lawmte in i inn a muh theih nadingun ka tunu in map neu khat a gelh hi.

records.english: Text me a photo of the gate so that I know which house is yours.
records.zomi: Na inn bang ahi hiam ka theih nadingin kongpi lim hong text in.

records.english: I'd rather you came to pick me up than tried to explain the way.
records.zomi: Lampi gen dingin na hanciam sangin hong la dingin na hong pai leh ka deih zaw hi.

records.english: How do we get to Grandpa's house from the bus station?
records.zomi: Bus station pan Pu' inn bangci-in i pai ding hiam?

records.english: Walk past the church, and it's the blue house with the mango tree in front.
records.zomi: Pawlpi kiang ah kaai inla, a mai ah theihai kung om inn dum ahi hi.

records.english: Our son walked his grandmother to the clinic and waited to show her the way back.
records.zomi: I tapa in a pi clinic ah a paipih a, a ciahna lampi lak dingin a ngak hi.

records.english: We nearly missed the funeral because the driver didn't know the village.
records.zomi: Mawtaw tuansakpa in khua a theih loh manin misi vuina i mansuah kha dek hi.

records.english: Do you remember the way to Uncle Dal's farm?
records.zomi: Pa neu Dal' lo lampi na phawk lai hiam?

records.english: Not really — it's been ten years since I was there.
records.zomi: Phawk lo hi — tua ah ka om pan kum sawm a cing khin hi.

records.english: The new road has made it much easier for relatives to reach our village.
records.zomi: Lampi thak in beh leh phungte i khua a tun theih nadingun a baihsak mahmah hi.

records.english: My little brother memorized the route to his friend's house after one visit.
records.zomi: Ka nau pasal in vei khat a pai khit ciangin a lawm' inn lampi a phawk hi.

records.english: Grandpa likes to take the long way so that he can wave to all his old friends.
records.zomi: Pu in a lawm lui khempeuh khut a vaai theih nadingin lampi sau a zui nuam hi.

records.english: Is your uncle's shop near the river or near the station?
records.zomi: Na pa neu' dawl gun kiang ah om hiam, station kiang ah om hiam?

records.english: It's right next to the station, opposite the bakery.
records.zomi: Station kiang tak ah a om a, moh bawlna inn tawh a kimai tuah hi.

records.english: Grandpa insists on giving directions using the names that shops had forty years ago.
records.zomi: Pu in kum sawmli paisa-a dawlte' min zang-in lampi a gen ngiat hi.

records.english: Kids, stay close and follow me — the market is very crowded today.
records.zomi: Naupangte, hong nai den unla hong zui un — tuni-in zuakna mun ah mi a tam mahmah hi.

records.english: We used the stars to find our way home after the bus broke down in the hills.
records.zomi: Mual tungah bus a siat khit ciangin inn i ciahna lampi aksite tawh i zong hi.

records.english: The village is so small that anyone can point you to the right house.
records.zomi: Khua a neu mahmah ahih manin kuamah in inn a man hong lak thei hi.

records.english: Dad always tells visitors to look for the red gate and the barking dog.
records.zomi: Pa in hong vehte kongpi san leh ui hawng zong dingin a gen tawntung hi.

records.english: Before phones had maps, we drew directions on the back of envelopes.
records.zomi: Phone in map a neih ma-in lai-ip nung lam ah lampi i gelh hi.

records.english: My mother gets confused in big cities, so we never let her travel alone.
records.zomi: Ka nu khuapi lian ah a lungsim a buai zel ahih manin amah bek khualzin i phal ngei kei hi.

records.english: Grandma gave the taxi driver directions in our language, and he understood perfectly.
records.zomi: Pi in taxi tuansakpa kiangah i pau tawh lampi a gen a, a thei kim hi.

records.english: Call me when you reach the bridge, and I'll come down to meet you.
records.zomi: Lei na tun ciangin hong sam inla, kong dawn dingin ka hong kum ding hi.

records.english: Our cousins found our new apartment by following the photos we sent them.
records.zomi: I sanggamte in i khak limte zui-in i inn thak a mu uh hi.

records.english: It might be quicker to take the shortcut through Grandma's rice fields.
records.zomi: Pi' buh lo tawng lampi tomzaw zui a manlang zaw kha ding hi.

records.english: Might it be easier just to send them a map?
records.zomi: Map bek khak a baih zaw kha ding hiam?

records.english: The children were taught to recognize the landmarks on the way home from school.
records.zomi: Sang pan inn ciahna lampi-a mun theih nadingte theih dingin naupangte kihilh hi.

records.english: May I use your phone to call my sister for directions?
records.zomi: Lampi dong dingin ka sanggam nu ka sam nadingin na phone ka zang thei ding hiam?

records.english: Can I walk to school by myself if I take the main road?
records.zomi: Lampi lian ka zui leh sang ah keimah bek ka pai thei ding hiam?

records.english: Only if you call me as soon as you get there.
records.zomi: Na tun pah ciangin hong sam leh bek.

records.english: Everyone, wait here while I ask that woman where the cemetery is.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, han mun koi ah om hiam tua numei kiangah ka dong laitakin hih ah ngak un.

records.english: Ask the old man by the well; he knows every family in the village.
records.zomi: Tuikhuk kiang a om pasal upa kiangah dong in; khua sung innkuan khempeuh a thei hi.

records.english: Getting lost on the way to my own wedding is a story my children love to hear.
records.zomi: Keima' kiteenna ah ka pai lam-a lampi ka mansuah thu pen ka tate in a zak nuam pen tangthu ahi hi.

records.english: Our son's first accident was a small one, but it made him a much more careful driver.
records.zomi: I tapa' kituakna masa pen a neu hi, ahi zongin mawtaw mawng-a a pilvang zaw mahmah sak hi.

records.english: We had a roof rack fitted so that the whole family's luggage would fit.
records.zomi: Innkuan bup' van a kim theih nadingin mawtaw tungah van koihna i bawlsak hi.

records.english: Does Grandpa still talk about the first car he ever owned?
records.zomi: Pu in a mawtaw masa pen thu a gen lai hiam?

records.english: Drive carefully, and remember that the children are sleeping in the back.
records.zomi: Pilvang takin mawng inla, naupangte a nung lam ah a ihmu uh hi, cih phawk in.

records.english: My father-in-law had his old jeep painted bright red for his seventieth birthday.
records.zomi: Ka sungpa in a kum sawmsagih pianni adingin a jeep lui san takin a lim a khai sak hi.

records.english: Grandpa finally agreed to stop driving after he backed into the neighbor's gate.
records.zomi: Pu in inn veng' kongpi a nung lam-a a tai sak khit ciangin mawtaw mawng nusia dingin a lungkim tawp hi.

records.english: Would you mind if your cousins rode with us to the festival?
records.zomi: Pawi ah na sanggamte i mawtaw tawh a tuang uh leh na lungkim ding hiam?

records.english: Not at all; there's plenty of room in the back.
records.zomi: Bangmah lo hi; a nung lam ah mun tampi a om hi.

records.english: Our trip took twice as long because we stopped at every relative's house on the way.
records.zomi: Lampi-a om beh leh phung khempeuh' inn ah i khawl ahih manin i khualzinna a nih in a sau hi.

records.english: My sister has refused to drive at night since her accident.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu in a kituakna nung pan zanin mawtaw mawng a nial hi.

records.english: Dad sold his motorbike so that he could buy a car for the family.
records.zomi: Innkuan adingin mawtaw a lei theih nadingin Pa in a motorbike a zuak hi.

records.english: It might be easier to rent a van than to take two cars to the reunion.
records.zomi: Kikhopna ah mawtaw nih tawh pai sangin van khat hal a baih zaw kha ding hi.

records.english: Our family's motorbike carried rice, chickens, and sometimes four people.
records.zomi: I innkuan' motorbike in buh, akte leh hun khenkhatah mi li a puak hi.

records.english: You all need to use the bathroom before we start — the next stop is two hours away.
records.zomi: I kipat ma-in note khempeuh in ek inn ah na pai kul uh hi — a zom khawlna nai nih a gamla hi.

records.english: Kids, buckle up, or we're not leaving the driveway.
records.zomi: Naupangte, na khau uh khih un, ahih kei leh inn kongpi i paisan kei ding hi.

records.english: Who's taking Grandpa to his eye appointment on Thursday?
records.zomi: Laizing ni ciangin Pu mit en dingin kua in a paipih ding hiam?

records.english: I can, if I leave work an hour early.
records.zomi: Nasepna pan nai khat ma-in ka pai khiat leh kei ka paipih thei hi.

records.english: Our old family car finally gave up after twenty years and three children.
records.zomi: I innkuan mawtaw lui kum sawmnih leh naupang thum khit ciangin a sia tawp hi.

records.english: Dad taught me to drive in his old pickup on the dirt road behind our farm.
records.zomi: Pa in i lo nung lam leilam ah a pickup lui tawh mawtaw mawng hong hilh hi.

records.english: The children played a counting game with red cars to pass the time.
records.zomi: Hun a bei theih nadingin naupangte in mawtaw san simna kimawlna a mawl uh hi.

records.english: I'll drive the first half, and you can drive the rest.
records.zomi: Kei in a kimlai dong ka mawng ding a, a taang nang na mawng thei hi.

records.english: The road to my grandparents' village was washed out, so we left the car and walked.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh pite' khua lampi tui in a pai sak ahih manin mawtaw i nusia a, i kaai hi.

records.english: The whole family rode on one motorbike when we were kids, which seems crazy now.
records.zomi: I neu lai-in innkuan bup motorbike khat tungah i tuang a, tu-in a lamdang hi.

records.english: Could you check whether there's enough fuel for the drive to the village?
records.zomi: Khua dong mawng dingin dat a cing hiam na en thei ding hiam?

records.english: My wife drives on the highway, and I take over on the mountain roads.
records.zomi: Ka zi in lam lianpi tungah a mawng a, mual lampite ah kei ka mawng hi.

records.english: Uncle Dal let me steer the tractor when I was seven.
records.zomi: Ka kum sagih lai-in Pa neu Dal in a tractor hong mawngsak hi.

records.english: Why do you always drive so slowly when Grandma is in the car?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pi mawtaw sung ah a om ciangin zawi takin na mawng tawntung hiam?

records.english: Because the road is bumpy, and her back hurts.
records.zomi: Lampi a kuakuai a, a nung a na ahih manin.

records.english: We could leave the car at the station and take the train the rest of the way.
records.zomi: Station ah mawtaw i nusia inla a taang lampi meileng tawh i pai thei hi.

records.english: Kids, look out the window — that's the hospital where you were both born!
records.zomi: Naupangte, tawhkhawng pan en un — tua pen note nih na suahna zato ahi hi!

records.english: Dad always says, "The road doesn't care how late you are."
records.zomi: Pa in, “Na tun nun lam pen lampi in a phawk kei hi,” a ci tawntung hi.

records.english: Mom made us all sing to keep Dad awake on the long drive home.
records.zomi: Inn ciahna lampi sau ah Pa a ihmut loh nadingin Nu in i khempeuh la hong sasak hi.

records.english: The nurse told us that the baby should always ride in the back seat.
records.zomi: Naungek nung lam tutna ah a tu den ding hi, ci-in nurse in hong gen hi.

records.english: How did you learn to ride a motorbike?
records.zomi: Motorbike tuan bangci-in na sin hiam?

records.english: My uncle taught me on his farm when I was fourteen.
records.zomi: Ka kum sawm leh li lai-in ka pa neu in a lo ah hong hilh hi.

records.english: Teaching my son to drive tested every bit of my patience.
records.zomi: Ka tapa mawtaw mawng ka hilh pen ka thuakzawhna khempeuh a sitsak hi.

records.english: Please don't let your little brother play with the windows while I'm driving.
records.zomi: Mawtaw ka mawng laitakin na nau pasal tawhkhawng tawh a mawl sak kei in.

records.english: We didn't own a car until I was twelve, so every trip felt like an adventure.
records.zomi: Ka kum sawm leh nih dong mawtaw i nei kei ahih manin khualzinna khempeuh a lamdang tak bang hi.

records.english: We were stopped by the police for driving with one broken headlight.
records.zomi: Mai meivak khat a siat ahih manin police in hong khaktan hi.

records.english: Three families share the school run, so each parent drives once or twice a week.
records.zomi: Innkuan thum in sang paipihna i kihawm ahih manin nu hiam pa hiam khat ciat in kal khat sungin vei khat hiam nih hiam a mawng uh hi.

records.english: My teenage daughter got her license last month, and now she wants the car every weekend.
records.zomi: Ka tanu khangno in kha bei-in a phalna lai a ngah a, tu-in kal tawp simin mawtaw a deih hi.

records.english: My cousin had his driving test postponed twice because of the rains.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam' mawtaw mawng sitna guahzuk hang-in vei nih kizekhia hi.

records.english: My mother still makes me text her every time I finish a long drive.
records.zomi: Ka nu in khualzinna sau ka zawh simin text hong khak dingin hong ngen lai hi.

records.english: Shall we stop for lunch at the halfway town, like we always do?
records.zomi: I sep tawntung bangin a kimlai khua ah sun an ne dingin i khawl ding hiam?

records.english: Dad's rule is simple: whoever borrows the car fills up the tank.
records.zomi: Pa' thukhun a baih hi: mawtaw a leitawi pa in dat a dimsak ding hi.

records.english: My little sister always gets carsick, so she sits in the front seat with the window open.
records.zomi: Ka nau numei mawtaw sung ah a lu a hai zel ahih manin tawhkhawng kihong tawh mai lam ah a tu hi.

records.english: How do four adults manage to share one car?
records.zomi: Upa li in mawtaw khat bangci-in a kihawm thei uh hiam?

records.english: Use the baby's car seat even for short trips.
records.zomi: Khualzinna tom zongin naungek mawtaw tutna zang in.

records.english: We bought a bigger car when the twins were born.
records.zomi: Apengte a suak ciangin mawtaw lian zaw khat i lei hi.

records.english: Is it okay if your friend's mother drives you to school this week?
records.zomi: Hih kal sungin na lawm' nu in sang ah hong paipih leh a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: Driving my grandmother to church every Sunday is my favorite part of the week.
records.zomi: Nipini simin ka pi pawlpi ah ka paipih pen ka kal sung-a ka nuam sak pen ahi hi.

records.english: The car radio is the only thing that keeps the kids quiet on long trips.
records.zomi: Khualzinna sau ah naupangte a daisak thei bek pen mawtaw radio ahi hi.

records.english: Can you drive the children to school tomorrow, since my car is at the garage?
records.zomi: Ka mawtaw bawlna mun ah a om ahih manin zingciang naupangte sang ah na paipih thei ding hiam?

records.english: Grandma never learned to drive, so she relies on her grandchildren.
records.zomi: Pi in mawtaw mawng a sin ngei kei ahih manin a tu-te tung ah a kinga hi.

records.english: Are we there yet?
records.zomi: I tung khin hiam?

records.english: Not yet — try to sleep for another hour.
records.zomi: Tung nai lo — nai khat behlap ihmu dingin hanciam in.

records.english: Can Grandpa still drive, or should we pick him up?
records.zomi: Pu in mawtaw a mawng thei lai hiam, i va la ding hiam?

records.english: We'd better pick him up, because he doesn't see well at night anymore.
records.zomi: Zanin a mu siang nawn kei ahih manin i va la leh a hoih zaw ding hi.

records.english: Can I drive us to Grandma's house this time?
records.zomi: Tu-in Pi' inn dong kei in ka mawng thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, but I'm sitting in the front, and you're driving slowly.
records.zomi: Thei hi, ahi zongin kei mai lam ah ka tu ding a, nang zawi takin na mawng ding hi.

records.english: Is the ferry to Grandpa's island running today?
records.zomi: Pu' tuikulh dong tembaw tuni-in a pai hiam?

records.english: Only in the afternoon, because of the strong tide this morning.
records.zomi: Tu zingsang tui a khang huai mahmah ahih manin nitak lam bek.

records.english: Shall we take the early train, or would the kids rather sleep in?
records.zomi: Meileng masa i tuang ding hiam, naupangte in a ihmut sau a deih zaw uh hiam?

records.english: Does the train go all the way to your grandparents' town?
records.zomi: Meileng in na pu leh pite' khua dong a pai hiam?

records.english: No, you have to change at the junction and take a small local bus.
records.zomi: Pai kei hi, lampi kituahna ah na lai kul a, khua sung bus neu khat na tuang kul hi.

records.english: You might want to sit near the front, since the road to the village is very bumpy.
records.zomi: Khua lampi a kuakuai mahmah ahih manin mai lam ah tu na deih kha ding hi.

records.english: The trip took twelve hours because the bus stopped in every village along the road.
records.zomi: Bus in lampi-a om khua khempeuh ah a khawl ahih manin khualzinna nai sawm leh nih a sau hi.

records.english: Hold your brother's hand when you get off the train.
records.zomi: Meileng pan na kiak ciangin na nau pasal' khut len in.

records.english: Grandpa always gives his seat to women with babies, even though he's over eighty.
records.zomi: Pu kum sawmgiat val a pha napi naungek pawi numeite a tutna a pia tawntung hi.

records.english: Is it safe for a twelve-year-old to ride the subway alone?
records.zomi: Kum sawm leh nih naupang khat amah bek subway a tuan pen a bitna hiam?

records.english: Perhaps, if she knows the route well and has a phone with her.
records.zomi: Lampi a theih kim a, phone a neih leh bitna kha ding hi.

records.english: The school gave every child a free bus pass this year.
records.zomi: Tu kum sang in naupang khempeuh bus pass a man om lo-in a pia hi.

records.english: My nephew fell asleep on my shoulder before the bus had even left town.
records.zomi: Bus in khua a paisan ma-in ka tanau ka liang tungah a ihmu hi.

records.english: Our neighbor's son rides the bus to the city every day for university.
records.zomi: I inn veng' tapa in sangpi kah dingin ni simin khuapi ah bus a tuang hi.

records.english: Uncle Dal keeps his bus tickets as souvenirs of every family visit.
records.zomi: Pa neu Dal in innkuan veh khempeuh a phawk nadingin a bus ticket te a kem hi.

records.english: Grandpa remembers when the only way to the city was a three-day walk.
records.zomi: Khuapi pai theih nading lampi pen ni thum kaai bek ahi lai hun Pu in a phawk hi.

records.english: My uncle works as a conductor on the train between our town and the city.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in i khua leh khuapi kikal meileng tungah ticket enpa in na a sem hi.

records.english: It's always good to see your faces at the end of a long journey.
records.zomi: Khualzinna sau tawp ciangin na mai uh muh a nuam tawntung hi.

records.english: We carried a sack of rice and two chickens on the bus to my uncle's village.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu' khua dong bus tungah buh ip khat leh ak nih i puak hi.

records.english: Can you text me the bus number so that I can meet you at the right stop?
records.zomi: A man bus khawlna ah kong dawn theih nadingin bus nambat hong text thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: We never let the children take the night bus alone.
records.zomi: Naupangte amau bek zan bus a tuang ding uh i phal ngei kei hi.

records.english: Our relatives sent a car to the bus station to pick us up.
records.zomi: I beh leh phungte in hong la dingin bus station ah mawtaw khat a sawl uh hi.

records.english: We bought the tickets online so that we wouldn't have to queue at the station.
records.zomi: Station ah i kizom kul loh nadingin online tawh ticket i lei hi.

records.english: Could you help your grandmother with her bags when you get to the station?
records.zomi: Station na tun ciangin na pi' van puak na huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Could you remind me which stop is closest to the hospital where Aunt Mary is?
records.zomi: Ni Mary a om na zato kiang pen khawlna bang ahi hiam hong phawksak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: The second stop after the bridge, near the big pharmacy.
records.zomi: Lei khit ciang a nihna khawlna, zatui dawl lian kiang ah.

records.english: On the river boat, passengers aren't allowed to stand up while it's moving.
records.zomi: Gun tembaw tungah a pai laitakin a tuangte ding thei lo uh hi.

records.english: Kids, keep your tickets in your pockets so that you don't lose them.
records.zomi: Naupangte, na mansuah loh nadingin na ticket uh na puan ip sungah koih un.

records.english: We'd better leave early so that we can get seats together on the train.
records.zomi: Meileng tungah khawm-a tutna i ngah theih nadingin manlang takin i pai khia leh hoih zaw ding hi.

records.english: The bus tickets were booked by my cousin, so I don't know our seat numbers.
records.zomi: Bus ticket pen ka sanggam in a bawl ahih manin i tutna nambat ka thei kei hi.

records.english: Waiting for the last ferry, we watched the sunset over the water with Grandpa.
records.zomi: Tembaw nunung pen ngak kawmin Pu tawh tui tungah ni tum i en hi.

records.english: We were made to wait at the border for three hours while our documents were checked.
records.zomi: I laite a kien laitakin gam ciang ah nai thum hong ngaksak uh hi.

records.english: The overnight bus to the hills is cheaper, but the children never sleep well on it.
records.zomi: Mual lam zan bus a man neu zaw a, ahi zongin naupangte in a tung ah a ihmu siang ngei kei uh hi.

records.english: The kids love waving at the farmers from the train window.
records.zomi: Naupangte in meileng tawhkhawng pan lo neite khut vaai a deih mahmah uh hi.

records.english: The minibus driver knows our family, so he always drops us right at my aunt's gate.
records.zomi: Minibus tuansakpa in i innkuan a theih manin ka ni' kongpi mai tak ah hong khiat sak tawntung hi.

records.english: Grandma insists on bringing a basket of food for the whole journey, however short it is.
records.zomi: Khualzinna a tom zongin Pi in khualzinna bup adingin an bawm khat puak a ngiat hi.

records.english: Everyone, stay together on the platform until the train has completely stopped.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, meileng a khawl kim dong platform tungah khawm in om un.

records.english: Can I take the bus to Grandma's house by myself this summer?
records.zomi: Tu khal ciangin Pi' inn ah keimah bek bus tawh ka pai thei ding hiam?

records.english: You can, once you've done the trip with me a few times.
records.zomi: Kei tawh vei tawmno na pai khit ciangin na pai thei hi.

records.english: Could we sit by the window so that the baby can watch the trees?
records.zomi: Naungek in singkungte a et theih nadingin tawhkhawng kiang ah i tu thei ding hiam?

records.english: The bus was so crowded that we had to put the baby's stroller on the roof.
records.zomi: Bus ah mi a tam lua ahih manin naungek leeng bus tungah i koih kul hi.

records.english: We may have to stand for the first part of the journey.
records.zomi: Khualzinna a kipatna ah i ding kul kha ding hi.

records.english: Is it okay if I listen to music with my headphones on the bus?
records.zomi: Bus tungah headphone tawh la ka ngai leh a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, but keep the volume low so that you can hear the announcements.
records.zomi: Hoih hi, ahi zongin thu kizasakte na zak theih nadingin a ging niam takin koih in.

records.english: Last year, a landslide delayed our train, and we missed my cousin's wedding.
records.zomi: Kum bei-in leiminpuk in i meileng a zekaisak a, ka sanggam' kiteenna i mansuah hi.

records.english: Dad made us count our bags every time we changed buses.
records.zomi: Bus i lai simin Pa in i vante hong simsak hi.

records.english: Keep an eye on your bags; the station is always busy before the holidays.
records.zomi: Na vante en den in; tawlngakni ma-in station ah mi a tam tawntung hi.

records.english: Our cousins met us at the station with a sign that had our names on it.
records.zomi: I sanggamte in i min a kigelhna lai tawh station ah hong dawn uh hi.

records.english: Our youngest is still small enough to sit on my lap for the whole trip.
records.zomi: I naupang neu pen khualzinna bup ka khuk tungah a tut theih dong a neu lai hi.

records.english: Our grandchildren came by train for the first time, and they talked about it for weeks.
records.zomi: I tu-te a masa pen-in meileng tawh hong pai uh a, kal tampi sung a gen uh hi.

records.english: Grandma wraps her money in a handkerchief before she gets on the bus.
records.zomi: Pi in bus a tuan ma-in a sum khut-ngumpuan tawh a tuam hi.

records.english: Taking the bus with three children and a grandmother is an adventure every time.
records.zomi: Naupang thum leh pi khat tawh bus tuan pen vei simin a lamdang tak ahi hi.

records.english: We never eat on the bus, because the smell makes Grandma feel sick.
records.zomi: A gim in Pi a cinasak ahih manin bus tungah an i ne ngei kei hi.

records.english: Do you feel sick on long bus rides?
records.zomi: Bus tawh khualzinna sau ah na lu a hai zel hiam?

records.english: A little, so I always sit near the front and look out the window.
records.zomi: Tawmno hai hi, tua ahih manin mai lam ah ka tu-a tawhkhawng pan ka en tawntung hi.

records.english: Mom had the bus driver call her when we reached our stop.
records.zomi: I khawlna i tun ciangin Nu in bus tuansakpa sam sak dingin a ngen hi.

records.english: Why are you taking the train instead of flying?
records.zomi: Bang hangin vanleng tawh pai lo-in meileng na tuang hiam?

records.english: It's cheaper, and I want the children to see the countryside.
records.zomi: A man neu zaw a, naupangte in khua neu gamte a muh ding ka deih hi.

records.english: Bring something to read; the train to the capital takes all day.
records.zomi: Sim ding khat tawi in; gam khuapi lian dong meileng ni bup a sau hi.

records.english: The bus company had the old seats replaced, so the journey is much more comfortable now.
records.zomi: Bus company in tutna luite a laih ahih manin tu-in khualzinna a nuam zaw mahmah hi.

records.english: Shall I meet you at the airport, or will your cousin pick you up?
records.zomi: Vanlengtual ah kong dawn ding hiam, na sanggam in hong la ding hiam?

records.english: Our relatives in the city insisted on paying for everything, even our bus tickets home.
records.zomi: Khuapi a om i beh leh phungte in inn ciahna bus ticket dong khempeuh a man piak a ngiat uh hi.

records.english: Dad packed a box of mangoes from our garden for the relatives in the capital.
records.zomi: Pa in gam khuapi lian a om beh leh phungte adingin i huan pan theihai bawm khat a thun hi.

records.english: Keep your passport in the inside pocket, not in your backpack.
records.zomi: Na passport na ip nung lam ah koih lo-in a sung lam puan ip ah koih in.

records.english: "Don't forget where you come from," my grandmother told me before I left for the city.
records.zomi: “Na hong suahna mangngilh kei in,” ci-in khuapi ah ka pai ma-in ka pi in hong hilh hi.

records.english: It's a long way, but the visit means the world to our parents.
records.zomi: Lampi a gamla hi, ahi zongin hih veh pen i nu leh pa adingin a thupi mahmah hi.

records.english: Can my cousin stay with you while she looks for a job in the city?
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu in khuapi ah nasep a zon laitakin na kiang ah a om thei ding hiam?

records.english: She's welcome to stay as long as she needs.
records.zomi: A kisap sung khempeuh a om theih ding kidawn hi.

records.english: We left the dog with our neighbors while we visited my wife's family.
records.zomi: Ka zi' innkuan i veh laitakin ui pen i inn vengte kiangah i nusia hi.

records.english: Nobody in our family had ever stayed in a hotel before the trip to the capital.
records.zomi: Gam khuapi lian khualzinna ma-in i innkuan sungah kuamah zinbuuk ah a giak ngei kei uh hi.

records.english: The children loved the zoo, but Grandma liked the big church most.
records.zomi: Naupangte in ganhing huan a deih mahmah uh a, ahi zongin Pi in pawlpi lian a deih pen hi.

records.english: We had our documents translated before we went to the embassy in the capital.
records.zomi: Gam khuapi lian-a embassy ah i pai ma-in i laite i let sak hi.

records.english: Grandpa said, "I've never seen so many cars in my whole life!"
records.zomi: Pu in, “Ka nuntak sungin hih zah mawtaw tam ka mu ngei kei hi!” a ci hi.

records.english: The trip was paid for by my brother-in-law, who works in the capital.
records.zomi: Khualzinna man pen gam khuapi lian ah na a sem ka sanggam nu' pasal in a pia hi.

records.english: Our parents had never been to a big city before they visited us last spring.
records.zomi: Spring nung in hong veh ma-un i nu leh pa khuapi lian ah a pai ngei kei uh hi.

records.english: We're already planning our next visit to see you all.
records.zomi: Note khempeuh hong veh kik nading i gel khin hi.

records.english: Do you think Grandma could manage such a long journey?
records.zomi: Pi in hih bang khualzinna sau a zo ding in na ngaihsun hiam?

records.english: Probably, if we stop often and let her rest.
records.zomi: Zo kha ding hi, tam vei i khawl a, a tawlngak sak leh.

records.english: Whose idea was it to bring the whole family on one bus?
records.zomi: Innkuan bup bus khat tawh paipih ding kua' ngaihsutna ahi hiam?

records.english: It was Grandpa's, and it worked out perfectly.
records.zomi: Pu' ngaihsutna ahi a, a kician kim hi.

records.english: Is it all right if we bring our baby to your apartment for a few days?
records.zomi: Ni tawmno sung i naungek na inn ah i paipih leh a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: The visit to my uncle's family was cut short when our son fell ill.
records.zomi: I tapa a cina ciangin ka pa neu' innkuan i veh pen tom takin a tawp hi.

records.english: We arrived just in time for the wedding, with our clothes still crumpled from the journey.
records.zomi: I puante khualzinna hang-in a kituap lai-in kiteenna dingin a hun takin i tung hi.

records.english: Use the app to call a taxi; it's safer than stopping one on the street.
records.zomi: Taxi sam dingin app zang in; lampi tungah khaktan sangin a bitna zaw hi.

records.english: Taking my parents to see the sea for the first time was one of the happiest days of my life.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa tuipi a masa pen-a ka etsak pen ka nuntak sung-a ni nuam pen khat ahi hi.

records.english: Our hosts gave up their own bedroom for us, which made us feel very welcome.
records.zomi: Hong dawngte in amau lupna khan hong pia uh a, hong kidawn mahmah dan i kisa hi.

records.english: My nephew took his first flight to visit us, and he waved at the clouds the whole time.
records.zomi: Ka tanau hong veh dingin vanleng a tuang masa pen a, a sung bup meiteite khut a vaai hi.

records.english: Remember to call your mother as soon as you arrive at your aunt's house.
records.zomi: Na ni' inn na tun pah ciangin na nu sam ding phawk in.

records.english: How long will you stay in the city?
records.zomi: Khuapi ah bangzah sung na om ding hiam?

records.english: Just until Dad's treatment is finished, maybe two weeks.
records.zomi: Pa' zato-a damna a bei dong bek, kal nih bang kha ding hi.

records.english: Everyone in the village gave us something to deliver to their relatives in the city.
records.zomi: Khua sung mi khempeuh in khuapi a om a beh leh phungte uh kiangah piak dingin na khat ciat hong pia uh hi.

records.english: We may not get back until Sunday night, depending on the traffic.
records.zomi: Lampi-a mawtaw tamna tawh kizui-in Nipini zan dong i ciah kik thei kha kei ding hi.

records.english: Could you show your grandparents how to use the subway map?
records.zomi: Na pu leh na pite subway map zat dan na hilh thei ding hiam?

records.english: It might be cheaper for the whole family to take the bus instead of flying.
records.zomi: Innkuan bup adingin vanleng sangin bus tawh pai a man neu zaw kha ding hi.

records.english: Grandpa kept saying that the city air smelled of smoke and noodles.
records.zomi: Pu in khuapi huih in meikhu leh an-ngum gim a nam hi, ci-in a gen den hi.

records.english: Could we stop at a market on the way so that we can buy a gift for our hosts?
records.zomi: Hong dawngte adingin letsong i lei theih nadingin lampi ah zuakna mun khat ah i khawl thei ding hiam?

records.english: You may need to show your ID card when you check in at the hostel.
records.zomi: Hostel ah na tun ciangin ID card na lak kul kha ding hi.

records.english: Mom made us wear our best clothes for the visit to our uncle's new apartment.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu' inn thak i veh nadingin Nu in i puan hoih pen hong silhsak hi.

records.english: How did your mother like the city?
records.zomi: Na nu in khuapi bangci-in a sa hiam?

records.english: She liked the food but missed the quiet of the village.
records.zomi: An a deih a, ahi zongin khua-a daina a ngaih hi.

records.english: We're taking Grandma to the city for her eye operation next week.
records.zomi: Kal hong ding ciangin a mit khamna adingin Pi khuapi ah i paipih ding hi.

records.english: When my sister moved to the city for university, the whole family helped her settle in.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu sangpi kah dingin khuapi ah a pem ciangin a om theih nadingin innkuan bup in i huh hi.

records.english: We stayed with my aunt, who lives on the tenth floor of a building with no lift.
records.zomi: Lift om lo inn sawn dawl sawm-na ah a om ka ni kiangah i om hi.

records.english: Why did you take the night bus instead of the train?
records.zomi: Bang hangin meileng sangin zan bus na tuang hiam?

records.english: The train was fully booked because of the holiday.
records.zomi: Tawlngakni hang-in meileng a dim kim khin hi.

records.english: In the city, the kids have to stay with an adult at all times.
records.zomi: Khuapi ah naupangte hun khempeuh-in upa khat tawh a om den kul uh hi.

records.english: We could take the children to the science museum while Grandpa rests.
records.zomi: Pu a tawlngak laitakin naupangte science museum ah i paipih thei hi.

records.english: Kids, wave goodbye to Grandma — we'll see her again at Christmas.
records.zomi: Naupangte, Pi kiangah goodbye ci-in khut vaai un — Christmas ciangin i mu kik ding hi.

records.english: Could you write down your address in case our phone runs out of battery?
records.zomi: I phone battery a bei kha leh ci-in na teenna mun hong gelh sak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Are you going to the wedding in the capital?
records.zomi: Gam khuapi lian-a kiteenna ah na pai ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, the whole family is going, even Grandma.
records.zomi: Pai ding hi, Pi dong innkuan bup i pai ding hi.

records.english: Grandma was nervous about the escalators, so we took the stairs.
records.zomi: Pi in kaplei kilawn a lau ahih manin kaplei i kah hi.

records.english: The cousins from the city were amazed that our village has no traffic lights.
records.zomi: Khuapi pan sanggamte in i khua ah lampi meivak om lo a lamdang sa mahmah uh hi.

records.english: Bring warm clothes; it gets cold at night in the mountain city.
records.zomi: Puan lum tawi in; mual khuapi ah zanin a vot hi.

records.english: Our cousins took us to see the lights downtown on our first night.
records.zomi: I zan masa pen-in i sanggamte in khuapi laizang meivakte et dingin hong paipih uh hi.

records.english: Can you lend us your suitcase for the trip to my sister's wedding?
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu' kiteenna khualzinna adingin na van bawm hong leitawi thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Uncle Dal had his son drive all the way to the bus station to collect us.
records.zomi: Pa neu Dal in bus station dong hong la dingin a tapa mawtaw a mawngsak hi.

records.english: Make sure Grandma has her medicine in her handbag, not in the suitcase.
records.zomi: Pi' zatui van bawm sungah hi lo-in a khut ip sungah a om hiam kician takin en in.

records.english: Dad's company sent him to the city for a month, so we all went with him.
records.zomi: Pa' company in kha khat sung khuapi ah a sawl ahih manin i khempeuh in i zui hi.

records.english: Grandpa refused to take the plane, so we spent two days on the train.
records.zomi: Pu in vanleng tuan a nial ahih manin meileng tungah ni nih i om hi.

records.english: We may need an extra night if my mother isn't well enough to travel.
records.zomi: Ka nu khualzin thei dingin a dam kei leh zan khat behlap i kisam kha ding hi.

records.english: The guesthouse owner phoned a taxi for us at four in the morning so that we wouldn't miss our flight.
records.zomi: I vanleng i mansuah loh nadingin zinbuuk neu neipa in zingsang nai li-in taxi hong sam sak hi.

records.english: The hotel was booked by my brother-in-law, who knows the owner.
records.zomi: Zinbuuk pen a neipa a thei ka sanggam nu' pasal in a bawl hi.

records.english: The noise from the street made it hard for Grandma to sleep.
records.zomi: Lampi pan ging in Pi' ihmut a haksasak hi.

records.english: Thank you for making our family feel at home.
records.zomi: I innkuan inn ah om bangin hong om sak manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: Why don't we book the same place we stayed last summer?
records.zomi: Bang hangin khal bei-a i giakna mun mah i bawl kei hiam?

records.english: Our honeymoon was spent in a tiny inn by the lake, and it was perfect.
records.zomi: I kiteen khit tawlngakni pen dil gei zinbuuk neu khat ah i zang a, a hoih kim hi.

records.english: The bathroom light didn't work, so a maintenance man came up with a ladder.
records.zomi: Ek inn meivak a sem kei ahih manin a bawlpa khat kaplei tawh hong kah hi.

records.english: My daughter made the hotel staff laugh with her questions about the elevator.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in elevator thu a dotnate tawh zinbuuk nasemte a nuisak hi.

records.english: We had an extra bed put in our room so that the kids could stay with us.
records.zomi: Naupangte i kiang ah a om theih nadingun i khan sungah lupna behlap khat i koih sak hi.

records.english: Is there anywhere nearby where the children can play?
records.zomi: Naupangte a mawl theihna mun kiang ah om hiam?

records.english: There's a park just behind the hotel.
records.zomi: Zinbuuk nung lam tak ah huan khat om hi.

records.english: Our cousins' farmhouse has no electricity, but sleeping there is the best part of the trip.
records.zomi: I sanggamte' lo inn ah meivak om lo hi, ahi zongin tua ah giak pen khualzinna-a a hoih pen ahi hi.

records.english: Remember to leave the key at reception when you go out.
records.zomi: Na pai khiat ciangin reception ah tawh nusia dingin phawk in.

records.english: Would it be possible to borrow a kettle for the baby's milk?
records.zomi: Naungek' nawi adingin tui-ukbel khat i leitawi thei ding hiam?

records.english: Here's one — and there are clean bottles in the cupboard.
records.zomi: Hih ah khat — bawm sungah nawi bel siangtho zong om hi.

records.english: Our grandparents stayed in a hotel for the first time at their granddaughter's wedding.
records.zomi: I pu leh pite in a tunu' kiteenna ah a masa pen-in zinbuuk ah a giak uh hi.

records.english: We left a thank-you note and some sweets for the cleaner on our last day.
records.zomi: I ni nunung pen-in a siangsak nu adingin lungdam kohna lai leh a khum neu tawmno i nusia hi.

records.english: Did you sleep well, or were the beds too hard?
records.zomi: Na ihmu siang hiam, lupnate a hak lua hiam?

records.english: Make sure the baby's cot is set up before we arrive.
records.zomi: I tun ma-in naungek lupna a kibawl khin hiam kician takin en in.

records.english: The kids still talk about the hotel with the swimming pool on the roof.
records.zomi: Inn tung ah tuidaipi om zinbuuk thu naupangte in a gen lai uh hi.

records.english: What time do you want breakfast tomorrow?
records.zomi: Zingciang zingsang an nai bangzah ciangin na deih hiam?

records.english: Around seven, before the kids wake up.
records.zomi: Nai sagih bang, naupangte a khanglo ma-un.

records.english: Could the children have pancakes for breakfast instead of rice?
records.zomi: Naupangte in zingsang an-in buh sangin pancake a ne thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: Can the children use the pool without an adult?
records.zomi: Naupangte in upa om lo-in tuidaipi a zang thei uh hiam?

records.english: No, children under twelve must be with a parent at all times.
records.zomi: Zang thei lo uh hi, kum sawm leh nih nuai naupangte hun khempeuh-in nu hiam pa hiam tawh a om kul uh hi.

records.english: My parents-in-law shared a room with us so that we could save money.
records.zomi: Sum i khol theih nadingin ka sungpa leh ka sungnu in khan khat hong kihawm uh hi.

records.english: Is it okay if Grandpa uses his own blanket instead of the hotel's?
records.zomi: Pu in zinbuuk' puanzial sangin amah' puanzial a zat leh a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: That's no problem at all.
records.zomi: Bangmah buaina om lo hi.

records.english: Our son was so tired that he fell asleep in the hotel lobby.
records.zomi: I tapa a gim mahmah ahih manin zinbuuk lutna khan ah a ihmu hi.

records.english: Our family room had bunk beds, which the children absolutely loved.
records.zomi: I innkuan khan ah lupna kituah a om a, naupangte in a deih mahmah uh hi.

records.english: In this guesthouse, shoes must be left at the door.
records.zomi: Hih zinbuuk neu ah khedapte kongkhak ah kinusia ding hi.

records.english: Uncle Dal says we're never allowed to stay at a hotel when we visit his town.
records.zomi: Pa neu Dal in a khua i veh ciangin zinbuuk ah i giak ngei lo ding, a ci hi.

records.english: It might be cheaper to rent a house for the whole family than to book five hotel rooms.
records.zomi: Zinbuuk khan nga bawl sangin innkuan bup adingin inn khat hal a man neu zaw kha ding hi.

records.english: Isn't staying at Grandma's better than any hotel?
records.zomi: Pi' inn ah om pen zinbuuk khempeuh sangin a hoih zaw hi lo hiam?

records.english: Do you have a family room with space for two small children?
records.zomi: Naupang neu nih adingin mun om innkuan khan na nei hiam?

records.english: Yes, and we can add a cot for the baby at no extra cost.
records.zomi: Nei hi, naungek adingin lupna neu khat a man behlap om lo-in i koih thei hi.

records.english: The hotel let us check in early because we had a sleeping baby with us.
records.zomi: Naungek ihmu i paipih ahih manin zinbuuk in hun ma-in hong lutsak hi.

records.english: Kids, no running in the hallways — other guests are sleeping.
records.zomi: Naupangte, lampi khan ah tai kei un — khual dangte a ihmu uh hi.

records.english: Our room was flooded during the storm, so the manager moved us to a bigger one.
records.zomi: Huihpi laitakin i khan ah tui a lut ahih manin a makaipa in khan lian zaw khat ah hong pemsak hi.

records.english: We stayed at my wife's uncle's house, where twelve of us shared three rooms.
records.zomi: Ka zi' pa neu' inn ah i om a, tua ah i sawm leh nih in khan thum i kihawm hi.

records.english: The receptionist said, "Your grandparents' room is on the ground floor, so they won't need the stairs."
records.zomi: Reception a om nu in, “Na pu leh na pite' khan lei tung dawl ah a om ahih manin kaplei a kisam kei ding hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: Would you mind if my cousins visited us in our room this evening?
records.zomi: Tu nitak i khan sungah ka sanggamte hong veh uh leh na lungkim ding hiam?

records.english: Visitors are welcome until ten o'clock.
records.zomi: Hong vehte nai sawm dong kidawn hi.

records.english: Grandma refused to stay in a hotel, so she slept at my cousin's house instead.
records.zomi: Pi in zinbuuk ah om a nial ahih manin ka sanggam' inn ah a giak hi.

records.english: We booked three rooms near the church for the relatives coming to the wedding.
records.zomi: Kiteenna hong pai ding beh leh phungte adingin pawlpi kiang ah khan thum i bawl hi.

records.english: Pets aren't allowed in the rooms, so the dog stayed with our neighbors.
records.zomi: Khan sungah ganhing phal lo ahih manin ui pen i inn vengte kiangah a om hi.

records.english: We usually stay with relatives when we travel, because hotels feel too quiet.
records.zomi: Zinbuuk a dai lua ahih manin khualzin ciangin beh leh phungte kiangah i om zel hi.

records.english: Is breakfast served early enough for us to catch the morning bus?
records.zomi: Zingsang bus i tuan theih nadingin zingsang an a manlang ding hiam?

records.english: The kitchen opens at six, so you'll have plenty of time.
records.zomi: Anbuk nai guk ciangin kihong ahih manin hun tampi na nei ding hi.

records.english: My nephew lost his teddy bear in the hotel, and the staff found it under the bed.
records.zomi: Ka tanau in zinbuuk ah a teddy bear a mansuah a, nasemte in lupna nuai ah a mu uh hi.

records.english: We were given a free cake because it was our daughter's birthday.
records.zomi: I tanu' pianni ahih manin cake khat a man om lo-in hong pia uh hi.

records.english: My aunt runs a small guesthouse, and the whole family helps during the busy season.
records.zomi: Ka ni in zinbuuk neu khat a nei a, mi tam hun ciangin innkuan bup in i huh hi.

records.english: Grandpa insisted on paying for the whole family's rooms as a wedding gift.
records.zomi: Pu in kiteenna letsong-in innkuan bup' khan man piak a ngiat hi.

records.english: Could you book a quiet room for my parents, away from the elevator?
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa adingin elevator pan gamla khan dai khat na bawl sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: The owner's wife made us breakfast every morning and wouldn't let us pay extra.
records.zomi: A neipa' zi in zingsang simin zingsang an hong huan sak a, behlap man hong piaksak kei hi.

records.english: Hotels near the hospital are always full, so we stayed in a room above a small shop.
records.zomi: Zato kiang zinbuukte a dim tawntung ahih manin dawl neu khat tung lam khan khat ah i om hi.

records.english: Could we have adjoining rooms so that the kids can be next to us?
records.zomi: Naupangte i kiang tak ah a om theih nadingun khan kikiang nih i ngah thei ding hiam?

records.english: The heater had been switched on before we arrived, so the room was lovely and warm.
records.zomi: I tun ma-in meisa a kihon khin ahih manin khan a nuam a, a lum mahmah hi.

records.english: The family who ran the guesthouse treated us like their own relatives.
records.zomi: Zinbuuk neu a kemte in amau beh leh phung bangin hong koih uh hi.

records.english: Shall I make a packed lunch for your journey to the city?
records.zomi: Khuapi na pai nadingin sun an kong thun sak ding hiam?

records.english: Can I peel the boiled eggs for the salad?
records.zomi: Salad adingin aktui kitawng ka ham thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, but let them cool down first.
records.zomi: Thei hi, ahi zongin a masa-in a vot nawn sak in.

records.english: How do you keep the vegetables fresh without a fridge?
records.zomi: Khal bawm om lo-in anteh bangci-in na thaksak den hiam?

records.english: We store them in a cool, dark corner and cook them within two days.
records.zomi: Mun vot leh mial ah i koih a, ni nih sungin i huan hi.

records.english: Is it all right to give the baby some soup broth?
records.zomi: Naungek kiangah an-tui tawmno piak a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: Ask the clinic nurse first; she'll know what's safe for her age.
records.zomi: A masa-in clinic nurse kiangah dong in; a kum adingin bang a bitna hiam a thei ding hi.

records.english: Before the wedding, my mother-in-law tested my patience by asking me to chop onions for an hour.
records.zomi: Kiteenna ma-in ka sungnu in nai khat sung lothaang tan dingin hong sawl-in ka thuakzawhna a sit hi.

records.english: Kids, wash the rice three times before you put it in the pot.
records.zomi: Naupangte, beel sungah na koih ma-un buh vei thum sil un.

records.english: Why is the rice always better when Grandpa cooks it?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pu in a huan ciangin buh a hoih zaw tawntung hiam?

records.english: He soaks it first and cooks it slowly over a wood fire.
records.zomi: A masa-in tui ah a nawng a, sing mei tungah zawi takin a huan hi.

records.english: Since my wife's illness, the children and I have learned to prepare simple dinners together.
records.zomi: Ka zi a cina pan naupangte leh kei khawm-in nitak an baih huan i sin hi.

records.english: My nephew dropped a whole basket of eggs on the kitchen floor.
records.zomi: Ka tanau in anbuk lei ah aktui bawm khat a khia khia hi.

records.english: The beans were left on the stove all afternoon, and by evening they were perfectly soft.
records.zomi: Be pen sun bup meibuk tungah kinusia a, nitak ciangin a nem kim hi.

records.english: Don't let the porridge stick to the bottom of the pot.
records.zomi: Buh-an tui beel khuk ah kibet sak kei in.

records.english: Grandma doesn't let anyone else make the chili paste for the festival.
records.zomi: Pi in pawi adingin malcha nek dang kuamah a bawlsak kei hi.

records.english: Cooking together on Sundays is how our family keeps its traditions alive.
records.zomi: Nipini simin khawm-a an huan pen i innkuan in i ngeinate a nungsak den nadan ahi hi.

records.english: The food smells wonderful — thank you for preparing all of this for us.
records.zomi: An gim a nam mahmah hi — kote adingin hih khempeuh na huan manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: Grandma tied her apron and said, "Now the real cooking begins."
records.zomi: Pi in a puan khawng a khih a, “Tu-in an huan taktak kipan ding hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: The rice pot boiled dry while we were talking, and the bottom was burned black.
records.zomi: I kiho laitakin buh beel a kang a, a khuk a kang vom hi.

records.english: We had the old wood stove repaired because Grandma says food tastes better on it.
records.zomi: Pi in sing meibuk tungah an a lim zaw hi, a cih manin meibuk lui i bawl kik sak hi.

records.english: The soup was ruined when someone added sugar instead of salt.
records.zomi: Kuamah khat in cii sangin sugar a koih ahih manin an-tui a sia hi.

records.english: I'm teaching our son to make rice, eggs, and soup before he leaves for university.
records.zomi: I tapa sangpi a pai ma-in buh, aktui leh an-tui huan ka hilh hi.

records.english: How many cups of rice should I cook for twelve people?
records.zomi: Mi sawm leh nih adingin buh khuang bangzah ka huan ding hiam?

records.english: About six, if there's also bread.
records.zomi: Moh zong a om leh guk bang.

records.english: We dry strips of beef over the fire so that they last through the rainy season.
records.zomi: Guah hun bup a kem theih nadingin bawngsa bawt mei tungah i khiang hi.

records.english: We cooked over a campfire during the family camping trip, and everything tasted smoky.
records.zomi: Innkuan puan inn khualzinna laitakin polam mei tungah an i huan a, khempeuh meikhu lim a nei hi.

records.english: Grandpa made us grind the corn by hand, just as he did as a boy.
records.zomi: Pu in a neu lai-a a sep bangin vaimim khut tawh hong suksak hi.

records.english: My cousin burned her hand on the hot pot and had to keep it in cold water.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu in beel sa ah a khut a kang a, tui vot sungah a koih den kul hi.

records.english: You can't cook with that pan; the handle is loose.
records.zomi: Tua beel tawh na huan thei kei ding hi; a lenna a kicim kei hi.

records.english: Is the baby old enough to eat mashed rice yet?
records.zomi: Naungek in buh kidiah a ne thei dong a khang khin hiam?

records.english: The nurse said we can start with a little rice porridge at six months.
records.zomi: Kha guk ciangin buh-an tui tawmno tawh i kipan thei hi, ci-in nurse in a gen hi.

records.english: Please keep the cat out of the kitchen while I'm cutting the meat.
records.zomi: Sa ka tan laitakin anbuk sungah zawhngeu lut sak kei in.

records.english: The pressure cooker hissed so loudly that the baby woke up.
records.zomi: Pressure cooker in ging sang takin a sawng ahih manin naungek a khanglo hi.

records.english: What's the secret to your grandmother's pickled vegetables?
records.zomi: Na pi' anteh thuk bawl dan thuguk bang ahi hiam?

records.english: She says it's patience — she leaves the jars in the sun for a whole week.
records.zomi: Thuakzawhna ahi hi, a ci hi — bel te kal khat bup ni sa ah a koih hi.

records.english: The jam jars were sealed tightly so that the fruit would keep all winter.
records.zomi: Khuavot bup singgah a kem theih nadingin jam bel te cing takin kikhak hi.

records.english: Let the baby taste a tiny bit of mango first.
records.zomi: A masa-in naungek theihai tawmno neu a liim sak in.

records.english: Our old kitchen had no chimney, so the smoke made everyone's eyes water.
records.zomi: I anbuk lui ah meikhu khiatna om lo ahih manin meikhu in mi khempeuh' mit a kaasak hi.

records.english: The power was cut while the cake was in the oven, so it came out flat.
records.zomi: Cake oven sungah a om laitakin meivak kitan ahih manin a khiat ciangin a pheisak hi.

records.english: Our neighbors' chickens got into the kitchen and knocked over the flour.
records.zomi: I inn vengte' akte anbuk sungah a lut uh a, buh-mal a hilh uh hi.

records.english: Mom always cooked a little extra in case an unexpected visitor arrived.
records.zomi: Khual lamen loh a hong tun kha leh ci-in Nu in an tawmno behlap a huan tawntung hi.

records.english: We might need more firewood if we're cooking for the whole village.
records.zomi: Khua bup adingin an i huan leh sing behlap i kisam kha ding hi.

records.english: Could you turn the fish over before it burns?
records.zomi: A kan ma-in nga na leh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Every New Year, my wife's family smokes fish over the kitchen fire for three days.
records.zomi: Kum Thak simin ka zi' innkuan in ni thum sung anbuk mei tungah nga a khiang uh hi.

records.english: Grandma's mashed pumpkin was the only thing the baby would eat.
records.zomi: Naungek in a nek theih bek pen Pi' mai kidiah ahi hi.

records.english: In our village, the festival meat is shared only after the elders have blessed it.
records.zomi: I khua ah upate in thupha a piak khit uh ciangin bek pawi sa kihawm hi.

records.english: When Grandpa lost his teeth, we started cutting his meat into tiny pieces.
records.zomi: Pu' ha a man khit ciangin a sa neu takin i tan kipan hi.

records.english: Could you help me prepare the food for the baby's naming ceremony on Saturday?
records.zomi: Kiginni ciangin naungek min phuahna poai adingin an bawl ka huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: "Never waste a single grain of rice," Grandma used to tell us.
records.zomi: “Buh ciang khat zong mawkin zang ngei kei un,” ci-in Pi in hong hilh zel hi.

records.english: The kitchen was filled with neighbors preparing food for the funeral.
records.zomi: Misi vuina adingin an a huan inn vengte in anbuk a dim hi.

records.english: Preparing the wedding feast brought three generations of our family into one small kitchen.
records.zomi: Kiteenna an huan in i innkuan suak thum anbuk neu khat sungah hong kaikhawm hi.

records.english: The children's grandmother let them crack the eggs, even though half the shells ended up in the bowl.
records.zomi: Naupangte' pi in aktui a khekkhiat sak a, a kaang a kim pen kuang sungah a tum hi.

records.english: It might rain, so let's cook inside instead of in the yard.
records.zomi: Guah zuk kha ding ahih manin inn mai ah hi lo-in inn sungah huan ni.

records.english: The children were made to taste every new dish at least once.
records.zomi: Naupangte in an thak khempeuh vei khat bek zongin a liim kul uh hi.

records.english: Could we make a smaller pot of curry, since only four of us are home tonight?
records.zomi: Tu zanin inn ah mi li bek i om ahih manin curry beel neu zaw khat i huan thei ding hiam?

records.english: Dad's job on festival days is to grill the meat, and nobody argues with him.
records.zomi: Pawi ni-in Pa' nasep pen sa khuk ahi a, kuamah in a kinial kei hi.

records.english: The fish has to be cleaned and salted before we smoke it.
records.zomi: I khiang ma-in nga pen kisil-in cii kinen ding hi.

records.english: We're preparing a big meal to welcome my brother home from the army.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal galkap pan inn a ciah kik muak nadingin an lian i huan hi.

records.english: We grow chilies in old paint tins outside the kitchen door.
records.zomi: Anbuk kongkhak polam ah khai thekbawm luite sungah malcha i suan hi.

records.english: My niece orders the same fried rice every single time we eat out.
records.zomi: Polam ah an i nek simin ka tunu in buh kikang kibang mah a sap tawntung hi.

records.english: My wife's parents made us try the fish-head curry, and it was delicious.
records.zomi: Ka zi' nu leh pa in nga lu curry hong liimsak uh a, a lim mahmah hi.

records.english: We ordered a huge birthday platter for Dad, and the waiters sang to him.
records.zomi: Pa adingin pianni an kuang lian khat i sap a, an zuakna dawl nasemte in la a sak sak uh hi.

records.english: That was the best family dinner we've had in years!
records.zomi: Tua pen kum tampi sung i neih innkuan nitak an hoih pen ahi hi!

records.english: Is it okay if we bring our own birthday candles?
records.zomi: Eima' pianni khawimeivaak i tawi leh a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: The baby's food was warmed by the kitchen staff without our even asking.
records.zomi: I ngen lo-in anbuk nasemte in naungek an a lumsak uh hi.

records.english: Grandpa said, "In my day, we ate what we were given and said thank you."
records.zomi: Pu in, “Ka hun lai-in i kipiak bang i ne a, lungdam i ko hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: Our rule is that the children get a sweet drink only after they've eaten their vegetables.
records.zomi: I thukhun pen naupangte in a anteh uh a nek khit uh ciangin bek dawn ding khum a ngah uh hi.

records.english: Could the kitchen make the soup less salty for my father?
records.zomi: Ka pa adingin an-tui ci tawm zawin anbuk in a huan thei ding hiam?

records.english: The waiter brought the wrong dishes, so Grandma ended up eating my uncle's spicy noodles.
records.zomi: An zuakna dawl nasem in an a man lo a tawi ahih manin Pi in ka pa neu' an-ngum hai a ne kha hi.

records.english: Can I have the same thing as my brother?
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal' bang mah ka ngah thei ding hiam?

records.english: They brought us an extra plate of fruit for our anniversary.
records.zomi: I kumpi ni ahih manin singgah kuang behlap khat hong tawi uh hi.

records.english: Could we have a high chair for the baby?
records.zomi: Naungek adingin tutna sang khat i ngah thei ding hiam?

records.english: Why did you order so much food?
records.zomi: Bang hangin an tampi lua na sap hiam?

records.english: Because your uncles always arrive hungry!
records.zomi: Na pa neute gilkial tawh hong tung tawntung uh ahih manin!

records.english: At our family dinners, the eldest always orders first.
records.zomi: I innkuan nitak an ah a upa pen in a sap masa tawntung hi.

records.english: The children's meals came with small toys, which made them very happy.
records.zomi: Naupangte' an tawh tawng neute a tung a, a lungdam mahmah uh hi.

records.english: My uncle's restaurant gives us a big discount whenever the family eats there.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu' an zuakna dawl in innkuan in a ne simin man tampi hong niamsak hi.

records.english: Can you order for me while I take the baby outside for a moment?
records.zomi: Naungek polam ah hun tawmno ka paipih laitakin hong sap sak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Our son spilled his drink before the food even arrived.
records.zomi: An a tun ma-in i tapa in a dawn ding a sung hi.

records.english: Would you like me to order for you, Grandpa?
records.zomi: Pu, kong sap sak ding na deih hiam?

records.english: Yes, please — you know what I like.
records.zomi: Deih hi — ka deih na thei hi.

records.english: Shall we order the family set, or does everyone want something different?
records.zomi: Innkuan an kuang i sap ding hiam, mi khempeuh in a tuam ciat a deih uh hiam?

records.english: The family set is cheaper, and there's enough for the kids to share.
records.zomi: Innkuan an kuang a man neu zaw a, naupangte a kihawm theih dong a cing hi.

records.english: Grandma made the waiter laugh by asking for her tea "as strong as her grandson."
records.zomi: Pi in a tea pen “a tu pa bangin a hat” ding a ngen-in an zuakna dawl nasem a nuisak hi.

records.english: Is there anything on the menu that Grandpa might like?
records.zomi: Menu tungah Pu' deih kha ding bangmah a om hiam?

records.english: The chicken soup, probably; it's mild and soft.
records.zomi: Ak an-tui kha ding hi; a hai lo a, a nem hi.

records.english: Our daughter ordered her own meal for the first time and was so proud.
records.zomi: I tanu in a masa pen-in amah' an amah mah in a sap a, a kisaktheih mahmah hi.

records.english: Shall we order dessert, or are you all too full?
records.zomi: An khit nek ding i sap ding hiam, na khempeuh na vah lua uh hiam?

records.english: Too full, but we'll take some cake home for later.
records.zomi: Vah lua hi, ahi zongin a nung ciang adingin cake tawmno inn ah i puak ding hi.

records.english: Our family's favorite restaurant closed last year, and we still miss it.
records.zomi: I innkuan' an zuakna dawl deih pen kum bei-in kikhak a, i ngaih lai hi.

records.english: How do you order in a restaurant when you can't read the menu?
records.zomi: Menu na sim theih kei ciangin an zuakna dawl ah bangci-in na sap hiam?

records.english: I point to what other people are eating and smile.
records.zomi: Mi dangte' nek ka lak a, ka nui hi.

records.english: Our order arrived so quickly that we thought it was someone else's.
records.zomi: I an a tung manlang lua ahih manin mi dang' a hi ding i sa hi.

records.english: Dad always orders too much and then makes everyone take the leftovers home.
records.zomi: Pa in a tam lua-in a sap tawntung a, tua khit ciangin mi khempeuh a taang inn ah a puaksak hi.

records.english: Ordering for all twelve of us took so long that the kids fell asleep at the table.
records.zomi: Mi sawm leh nih adingin an sap pen a sau lua ahih manin naupangte dawhkan ah a ihmu uh hi.

records.english: Grandpa had never eaten at a restaurant until my cousin's wedding dinner.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam' kiteenna nitak an ma-in Pu an zuakna dawl ah an a ne ngei kei hi.

records.english: Ordering at food stalls with my father taught me how to bargain politely.
records.zomi: Ka pa tawh an zuakna dawl neute ah an i sap manin zahtak takin a man kiniam ngen dan ka sin hi.

records.english: The kitchen ran out of rice, so our meal was served with bread instead.
records.zomi: Anbuk ah buh a bei ahih manin i an buh sangin moh tawh hong pia uh hi.

records.english: The bill was split between the three brothers, as usual.
records.zomi: A tawntung bangin a man pen sanggam pasal thumte' kikal ah kihawm hi.

records.english: Grandpa insists on paying for dinner, as he always does.
records.zomi: Pu in a sep tawntung bangin nitak an man piak a ngiat hi.

records.english: We had the restaurant pack the leftovers so that Grandma could have them for lunch.
records.zomi: Pi in sun an-in a neih theih nadingin an zuakna dawl in a taang hong thun sak hi.

records.english: My cousin ordered food delivery for our grandparents every night while they were sick.
records.zomi: I pu leh pite a cina laitakin ka sanggam in zan simin amaute adingin an a sap sak hi.

records.english: Ask the waiter whether the curry has peanuts in it, because Dad is allergic.
records.zomi: Pa in a kituak loh manin curry sungah bekang a om hiam an zuakna dawl nasem kiangah dong in.

records.english: Kids, no soft drinks today — we're having water.
records.zomi: Naupangte, tuni-in soft drink om lo ding — tui i dawn ding hi.

records.english: Our order was forgotten by the kitchen, and we waited almost an hour.
records.zomi: Anbuk in i an a mangngilh a, nai khat bang i ngak hi.

records.english: Please, kids, sit down and stop running between the tables.
records.zomi: Naupangte, tu unla dawhkan kikal ah tai nawn kei un.

records.english: We ordered pizza for the kids and a traditional meal for the grandparents.
records.zomi: Naupangte adingin pizza leh pu leh pite adingin i ngeina an i sap hi.

records.english: When Mom works late, we order from the dumpling shop on the corner.
records.zomi: Nu nai sau a sep ciangin ki-ngawi mun a om sambuk dawl pan i sap hi.

records.english: "Order whatever you like — today is my treat," Aunt Mary told us.
records.zomi: “Na deih bangbang sap un — tuni-in keima' vaak ahi hi,” ci-in Ni Mary in hong gen hi.

records.english: We found a restaurant where the staff speak our language, so Grandma could order by herself.
records.zomi: Nasemte in i pau a zat theihna an zuakna dawl khat i mu ahih manin Pi in amah mah in a sap thei hi.

records.english: The restaurant had the birthday cake decorated with our daughter's name.
records.zomi: An zuakna dawl in pianni cake tungah i tanu' min a gelh sak hi.

records.english: The menu was in a language his grandparents couldn't read, so my nephew translated it for them.
records.zomi: Menu pen a pu leh pite' sim theih loh pau tawh ahih manin ka tanau in amaute adingin a let sak hi.

records.english: Thank you for choosing such a lovely place for our celebration.
records.zomi: I poai adingin hih bang mun hoih na teel manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: We reserved the long table at the back for the whole family.
records.zomi: Innkuan bup adingin nung lam dawhkan sau i bawl hi.

records.english: Do your kids eat everything, or are they picky?
records.zomi: Na tate in khempeuh a ne uh hiam, an a teel uh hiam?

records.english: They eat almost everything except mushrooms.
records.zomi: Ngakhuai bek tua lo khempeuh a ne uh hi.

records.english: Let the children order for themselves this time.
records.zomi: Tu-in naupangte amau mah in sap sak un.

records.english: Could you order something soft for Grandma, since she can't chew very well?
records.zomi: Pi in a ham siang thei kei ahih manin a adingin a nem khat na sap thei ding hiam?

records.english: We were seated near the kitchen, which was very noisy for Grandma.
records.zomi: Anbuk kiang ah hong tusak uh a, Pi adingin a buai mahmah hi.

records.english: The guests arrived so late that dinner was served at midnight.
records.zomi: Khualte a tun nun lua uh ahih manin zan lai ciangin nitak an kipia hi.

records.english: Thank you for letting us stay — we'll host you next time!
