records.zomi: Hong om sak manin ka lungdam hi — a zom ciangin kote in kong dawn ding uh hi!

records.english: Grandpa always greets guests with the same words: "You've come a long way; sit and rest."
records.zomi: Pu in khualte kammal kibang tawh a muak tawntung hi: “Gamla taka hong pai na hi uh hi; tu unla tawlngak un.”

records.english: Who's bringing the extra chairs from Uncle Dal's house?
records.zomi: Pa neu Dal' inn pan tutna behlapte kua in a tawi ding hiam?

records.english: Hosting is hard work, but the stories we share make it worth it.
records.zomi: Khual dawn pen nasep haksa ahi hi, ahi zongin i kihawm tangthute in a manpha sak hi.

records.english: Our son's friend from abroad is staying with us for a month, and he's never tried rice porridge.
records.zomi: Gamdang pan i tapa' lawm kha khat sung i kiang ah a om a, buh-an tui a liim ngei kei hi.

records.english: The cake was eaten before the last guests even arrived.
records.zomi: Khual nunungte a tun ma-un cake kine khin hi.

records.english: Would the children like to perform a little play for our visitors after dinner?
records.zomi: Nitak an khit ciangin naupangte in hong vehte adingin lawng neu khat a lak nuam uh hiam?

records.english: My mother-in-law insisted on cooking every meal herself while she stayed with us.
records.zomi: Ka sungnu in i kiang ah a om sungin an khempeuh amah mah in a huan ngiat hi.

records.english: In our house, guests never wash dishes on their first night.
records.zomi: I inn ah khualte in zan masa pen-in kuang a sil ngei kei uh hi.

records.english: When do your guests from the village arrive?
records.zomi: Khua pan na khualte bang ciangin a tung ding uh hiam?

records.english: On Friday evening, if the bus isn't late.
records.zomi: Laithai ni nitak ciangin, bus a nun kei leh.

records.english: Our niece cried when her cousins went home after the summer holidays.
records.zomi: Khal hun khit ciangin a sanggamte inn ah a ciah uh ciangin i tunu a kap hi.

records.english: My aunt arrived with three extra guests nobody had expected.
records.zomi: Ka ni in kuamah' lamen loh khual thum tawh hong tung hi.

records.english: Kids, no fighting while our visitors are here, please.
records.zomi: Naupangte, i khualte hih ah a om sungun kido kei un.

records.english: The rice ran out halfway through dinner, so we quickly cooked another pot.
records.zomi: Nitak an a kimlai-in buh a bei ahih manin beel dang khat manlang takin i huan hi.

records.english: Our house was crowded with relatives for the whole wedding week.
records.zomi: Kiteenna kal bup sungin i inn beh leh phungte tawh a dim hi.

records.english: I really do enjoy having a full house.
records.zomi: Inn dim taka mi om pen ka nuam sa taktak hi.

records.english: Shall we invite the visitors to church with us on Sunday?
records.zomi: Nipini ciangin hong vehte pawlpi ah i sam ding hiam?

records.english: In our family, it's rude to let a guest leave without eating.
records.zomi: I innkuan ah khual an nek sak lo-in paisak pen zahtakna om lo ahi hi.

records.english: Our guests stayed for two weeks instead of two days, but we didn't mind.
records.zomi: I khualte ni nih sangin kal nih a om uh a, ahi zongin i lungkham kei hi.

records.english: "Eat as much as you like — there's plenty more in the kitchen," Dad told the guests.
records.zomi: “Na deih zah ne un — anbuk ah tampi om lai hi,” ci-in Pa in khualte kiangah a gen hi.

records.english: Make sure the guests know where the light switches are.
records.zomi: Meivak hon-phelna koi ah om hiam khualte in a theih uh kician takin en in.

records.english: Would you mind hosting my friend's family during the festival, since their house is being repaired?
records.zomi: Pawi laitakin ka lawm' inn a kibawl kik ahih manin a innkuan na dawn thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, but we'll need to borrow some extra blankets.
records.zomi: Thei hi, ahi zongin puanzial behlap tawmno i leitawi kul ding hi.

records.english: Could you meet our guests at the bus station while I finish cleaning?
records.zomi: Ka siansak zawh ma-in bus station ah i khualte na dawn thei ding hiam?

records.english: The grandparents' room was cleaned from top to bottom before they arrived.
records.zomi: A tun ma-un pu leh pite' khan a tung pan a nuai dong kisiangsak hi.

records.english: Our elderly neighbor joined us for every holiday meal after her husband died.
records.zomi: I inn veng nu upa in a pasal a sih khit ciangin tawlngakni an khempeuh ah hong kihel hi.

records.english: We do try to give every visitor our best room, even if it means sleeping on the sofa ourselves.
records.zomi: Eimah sofa tungah i ih kul zongin hong veh khempeuh i khan hoih pen piak i hanciam taktak hi.

records.english: Hosting a family reunion for sixty people taught me to ask for help early.
records.zomi: Mi sawmguk adingin innkuan kikhopna i dawn manin a manlang takin huhna ngen dingin ka sin hi.

records.english: The children gave up their bedrooms so that Grandma and Grandpa could sleep in comfort.
records.zomi: Pi leh Pu nuam taka a ihmut theih nadingun naupangte in a lupna khan uh a pia uh hi.

records.english: One of the guests knocked over a vase, and it shattered on the floor.
records.zomi: Khual khat in pak koihna bel a hilh a, lei ah a kitam hi.

records.english: We never let guests pay for anything while they're staying with us.
records.zomi: I kiang ah a om sungun khualte bangmah man i piaksak ngei kei hi.

records.english: Why don't we put the visitors in the front room, where it's quieter?
records.zomi: Bang hangin hong vehte mai lam khan a dai zawna ah i koih kei hiam?

records.english: The table was set the night before so that we'd have time to greet everyone.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh i hopih theih nadingin a zan ma-in dawhkan kibawl khin hi.

records.english: My cousin's children broke the swing in the garden, but we laughed about it.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam' tate in huan sung-a gengen a phiat uh a, ahi zongin i nui uh hi.

records.english: Hosting my husband's family was stressful at first, but now I look forward to it.
records.zomi: Ka pasal' innkuan dawn pen a kipatna ah lungkhamhuai hi, ahi zongin tu-in ka ngak nuam hi.

records.english: Our little house was so full of relatives that we ate in shifts.
records.zomi: I inn neu beh leh phungte tawh a dim mahmah ahih manin a kilaih-in an i ne hi.

records.english: My wife and I split the work: she cooks, and I make up the beds.
records.zomi: Ka zi leh kei nasep i kikhen hi: amah in an a huan a, kei in lupna ka bawl hi.

records.english: A pipe burst on the first night of the visit, and we had to wash in the river for two days.
records.zomi: Veh zan masa pen-in tui pipe a puak a, ni nih sung gun ah i kisil kul hi.

records.english: Kids, let our guests choose their seats first.
records.zomi: Naupangte, i khualte a tutna uh a teel masa uh hen.

records.english: It was the first time we had hosted so many people, and the house felt wonderfully alive.
records.zomi: Mi tampi i dawn masa pen ahi a, inn a nungta mahmah bang hi.

records.english: Could you take the kids to the park for an hour while I finish cooking?
records.zomi: An ka huan zawh ma-in nai khat sung naupangte huan ah na paipih thei ding hiam?

records.english: I do want my in-laws to feel comfortable the first time they stay with us.
records.zomi: Ka sungte i kiang ah a om masa pen-un nuam takin a om ding uh ka deih taktak hi.

records.english: Is it our turn to host Christmas for the whole family this year?
records.zomi: Tu kum innkuan bup adingin Christmas dawn ding i hun ahi hiam?

records.english: What do you usually serve when your in-laws visit?
records.zomi: Na sungte hong veh ciangun bang na pia zel hiam?

records.english: Their favorite fish curry and plenty of fresh fruit.
records.zomi: A deih pen uh nga curry leh singgah thak tampi.

records.english: We hosted the whole church choir after the Christmas concert.
records.zomi: Christmas la poai khit ciangin pawlpi la sa pawl bup i dawn hi.

records.english: Did your guests enjoy their stay?
records.zomi: Na khualte in a om sung uh a nuam sa uh hiam?

records.english: They loved it, especially the morning walks by the river.
records.zomi: Nuam sa mahmah uh hi, a tuam in gun gei-a zingsang kawikawi.

records.english: Grandpa told the same war story to every guest, and they all listened politely.
records.zomi: Pu in khual khempeuh kiangah gal tangthu kibang mah a gen a, khempeuh in zahtak takin a ngai uh hi.

records.english: We bought a new mattress before my wife's parents came to stay.
records.zomi: Ka zi' nu leh pa hong om ma-un mattress thak khat i lei hi.

records.english: Can our neighbors' kids join the party, or is it only for family?
records.zomi: I inn vengte' tate pawi ah a kihel thei uh hiam, innkuan ading bek hiam?

records.english: Everyone's welcome; there's plenty of food.

records.english: Our children love it when their cousins come to stay, because the rules are a little looser.

records.english: Leave your umbrellas by the door, everyone.

records.english: Our new friends from church were surprised by how much food we served.
records.zomi: Pawlpi pan i lawm thakte in an tampi i piak a lamdang sa uh hi.

records.english: What did you like to eat when you were a child?

records.english: "You'll like it once you try it," Mom always said, and she was usually right.

records.english: Our family's favorite recipes are written in a notebook so that the grandchildren can cook them one day.

records.english: Does everyone in your family love spicy food?
records.zomi: Na innkuan sung mi khempeuh in an hai a deih uh hiam?

records.english: Does Grandma really think pizza is just a snack?

records.english: Who in your family could ever say no to fresh mangoes?

records.zomi: Cheese na liim ngei kei, cih a man hiam?

records.zomi: An lian khat ka huan a, mi khempeuh in amau ciat a deih an-tui a behlap uh hi.

records.english: She says that food without heat is like a day without sun.

records.english: Kids, at least taste Grandma's soup before you decide you don't like it.

records.english: Do you ever cook the dishes your mother taught you?
records.zomi: Na nu' hong hilh ante na huan ngei hiam?

records.english: Our son's peanut allergy means we read every food label carefully.

records.english: My children still love their grandmother's steamed buns more than any fast food.
records.zomi: Ka tate in an manlang khempeuh sangin a pi uh' moh kitoh a deih zaw lai uh hi.

records.english: My husband's family eats dinner very late, which took me years to get used to.

records.english: Is your father happy with any meal, as long as there's rice?

records.english: Food is how our family says "I love you" without words.

records.english: Kids, raise your hand if you want noodles instead of rice tonight.

records.english: The old recipes were almost forgotten until my aunt wrote them all down.

records.english: Do you think our children will still love our food when they're grown up?
records.zomi: I tate a khan ciangun i an a deih lai ding uh in na ngaihsun hiam?

records.english: I really hope so; food is how we pass on who we are.
records.zomi: Ka lamen taktak hi; an pen i hihna i lui sawnna ahi hi.

records.english: When I was pregnant, I wanted mango with chili every single day.
records.zomi: Ka gai laitakin ni simin theihai malcha tawh ka deih hi.

records.english: Which dish does your father always ask for on his birthday?

records.zomi: Siing tawh nga kikang, a nu' huan dan bangin.

records.zomi: Na nu' malcha an-tui a hai lua ahih manin ka mittui a kia hi.

records.english: I do want my children to enjoy the food we grew up eating.

records.english: Everyone in our family knows about Grandma's sweet tooth.

records.english: Does your husband eat the food from your home village?
records.zomi: Na pasal in na khua' an a ne hiam?

records.english: He didn't at first, but now he asks for it every week.
records.zomi: A kipatna ah a ne kei a, ahi zongin tu-in kal simin a ngen hi.

records.zomi: Pu' ha a hat nawn kei ahih manin buh nem leh anteh kitawng a deih zaw hi.

records.english: Kids, everyone washes their hands before we sit down.
records.zomi: Naupangte, i tut ma-in mi khempeuh in khut i sil ding hi.

records.english: What's the best part of your family meals?
records.zomi: Na innkuan an nek khawm ah a hoih pen bang ahi hiam?

records.zomi: Nipini leh nipite bek, mi khempeuh inn ah a om ciangun.

records.english: Grandma's ginger tea is served at the end of every family celebration.
records.zomi: Innkuan poai khempeuh a tawp ciangin Pi' siing tea kipia hi.

records.english: Kids, come and help carry the big pots to the table.
records.zomi: Naupangte, beel lian dawhkan ah puak nadingin hong huh un.

records.english: Will my children cook these dishes for their own families one day, I wonder?
records.zomi: Ka tate in ni khat ni-in amau innkuan adingin hih ante a huan ding uh hiam?

records.english: We cooked my late father's favorite meal on the anniversary of his death.
records.zomi: Ka pa a sih kum ni-in a deih pen an i huan hi.

records.english: The meal for my parents' anniversary was cooked by all six of their children together.

records.zomi: Innkuan sungah hong muak dingin ka sungpa in an nek ma-in thu a gen hi.

records.zomi: Na innkuan kikhopna khempeuh naupangte in pu leh pite adingin la a sak tawh a tawp zel hiam?

records.english: Our baby's first-birthday meal lasted all afternoon, and over a hundred relatives came.

records.zomi: I buh lak an ah na inn veng thakte i sam ding hiam?

records.english: They'd be honored, I'm sure.

records.english: When I married into this family, I had to learn a dozen new dishes.

records.english: Everyone eats together on a video call every Sunday, even though we're in three countries.

records.zomi: Na pu kiangah buh a masa-in pia in.

records.english: At ninety, Grandma still decides what we eat at every family celebration.

records.english: Our Sunday family meal moved online when my parents went to live with my sister abroad.

records.zomi: Kum thak adingin i innkuan' tupnate i gelh a, bang ah i kap hi.

records.english: Grandpa's words gave me the courage to apply for the job.
records.zomi: Pu' kammalte in nasep ngen dingin hangsanna hong pia hi.

records.english: You'll find work again; you're too talented to stay unemployed for long.
records.zomi: Nasep na ngah kik ding hi; nasep om lo-in hun sau na om dingin na siam lua hi.

records.english: Your grandfather would have been so proud of you today.
records.zomi: Tuni-in na pu in nangma' tungah a kisaktheih mahmah ding hi.

records.english: Is there anything we can do to make your recovery easier?
records.zomi: Na dam kik nading baih zaw nadingin i sep thei bangmah a om hiam?

records.english: Just keep visiting — it means everything to me.
records.zomi: Hong veh den bek in — kei adingin a thupi pen ahi hi.

records.english: Good luck tomorrow — we're all thinking of you!
records.zomi: Zingciang vangphatna om hen — i khempeuh in hong ngaihsun i hi hi!

records.english: It may take time, but our family will rebuild the shop together.
records.zomi: Hun sau kha ding hi, ahi zongin i innkuan in khawm-in dawl i lam kik ding hi.

records.english: Losing our house in the fire brought our family closer than ever.
records.zomi: Mei in i inn a kat khit ciangin i innkuan a kinai zaw kul ngei lo dan-in a kinai hi.

records.english: You can use my old guitar until you're ready for a new one.
records.zomi: Thak khat na kisam dong ka guitar lui na zang thei hi.

records.english: Could I talk to Grandpa about my plans, since he always knows what to say?
records.zomi: Pu in a gen ding a thei tawntung ahih manin ka gelnate Pu kiangah ka gen thei ding hiam?

records.english: Everyone, let's give Aunt Mary a round of applause for finishing her degree!
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, a degree a zawh manin Ni Mary adingin khut beng ni!

records.english: Why don't you show your father the song you wrote?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na phuah la na pa na zasak kei hiam?

records.english: He'd love to hear it — he's always believed in you.
records.zomi: A zak a deih mahmah ding hi — nang a muang tawntung hi.

records.english: The whole family pooled their savings so that my cousin could study abroad.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu gamdang ah sang a kah theih nadingin innkuan bup in a sum kholte uh a kikhawm uh hi.

records.english: After the divorce, my aunt went back to school and became a nurse.
records.zomi: A kikhen khit ciangin ka ni sang ah a kah kik a, nurse a suak hi.

records.english: I do believe your mother will walk again; she's the strongest person I know.
records.zomi: Na nu a pai kik thei ding hi, ka um hi; ka theih mi lak ah a hat pen ahi hi.

records.english: When my brother's shop failed, our parents helped him start again with a smaller one.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal' dawl a puk ciangin i nu leh pa in a neu zaw khat tawh a kipan kik nadingin a huh uh hi.

records.english: Our son finally passed his driving test, and the whole family cheered.
records.zomi: I tapa in mawtaw mawng sitna a zo tawp a, innkuan bup in i sam uh hi.

records.english: Keep trying, sweetheart — you were much better today than yesterday.
records.zomi: Hanciam den in, ka it — tuni-in zanni sangin na hoih zaw mahmah hi.

records.english: Can I try out for the school football team, even though I've never played before?
records.zomi: Ka mawl ngei kei hangin sang football pawl ah ka kisin thei ding hiam?

records.english: Absolutely — just give it your best.
records.zomi: Thei mahmah hi — na theih tawp in sem in.

records.english: You might not win this time, but you'll learn something important.
records.zomi: Tu-in na zo kei kha ding hi, ahi zongin na thupi khat na sin ding hi.

records.english: My nephew wants to be a pilot, and we keep telling him he can do it.
records.zomi: Ka tanau in pilot suak a deih a, na sem thei ding hi, ci-in i gen den hi.

records.english: My father taught me that a bad harvest is not the end of the world.
records.zomi: Buh a phat loh pen leitung bei hi lo hi, ci-in ka pa in hong hilh hi.

records.english: I like to keep my grandfather's old watch in my pocket, even though it no longer works.
records.zomi: A sem nawn lo hangin ka pu' nai-ten lui ka puan ip sungah ka koih nuam hi.

records.english: Could you choose a gift for your cousin, since you know her tastes better than I do?
records.zomi: Kei sangin na sanggam nu' deih na thei zaw ahih manin a adingin letsong na teel thei ding hiam?

records.english: It might be nice to have a dog, but your father prefers cats.
records.zomi: Ui khat neih a hoih kha ding hi, ahi zongin na pa in zawhngeu a deih zaw hi.

records.english: Has anyone ever managed to get your brother to keep his room tidy?
records.zomi: Na sanggam pasal a khan siangsak den dingin kuamah in a sem zo ngei hiam?

records.english: My twin sister and I like completely different things, except for our grandmother's cooking.
records.zomi: Ka apeng sanggam nu leh kei i deih a kibang kim lo hi, ka pi' an huan bek tua lo.

records.english: Why do you always sit next to Grandma at dinner?
records.zomi: Bang hangin nitak an ciangin Pi kiang ah na tu tawntung hiam?

records.english: Because she tells the best stories and saves me the crispy rice.
records.zomi: Tangthu hoih pen a gen a, buh kang hong kemsak ahih manin.

records.english: My grandparents prefer the village, even though the city is easier for doctor's visits.
records.zomi: Khuapi in siavuan veh nadingin a baih zaw hangin ka pu leh pite in khua a deih zaw uh hi.

records.english: What kind of gift does your grandfather like best?
records.zomi: Na pu in letsong bang a deih pen hiam?

records.english: Anything homemade, especially if the grandchildren made it.
records.zomi: Inn-a kibawl khempeuh, a tuam in tu-te in a bawl leh.

records.english: Pick any bedroom you like; you're our guest.
records.zomi: Na deih lupna khan khatpeuh teel in; i khual na hi hi.

records.english: Everyone, write down your favorite meal, and I'll cook them one by one this month.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, na an deih pen gelh unla, hih kha sungin khat khit khat ka huan ding hi.

records.english: We let the children choose the names for the puppies.
records.zomi: Ui neute' min naupangte teel sak i phal hi.

records.english: You all decide on the movie, and I'll make the popcorn.
records.zomi: Note khempeuh in movie na teel unla, kei in popcorn ka bawl ding hi.

records.english: Which do your children prefer, the beach or their grandparents' farm?
records.zomi: Na tate in tuipi gei hiam, a pu leh pite' lo hiam, bang a deih zaw uh hiam?

records.english: The farm, because they can ride the tractor and feed the goats.
records.zomi: Lo, tractor a tuang thei uh a, kelte a vak thei uh ahih manin.

records.english: Every year, the birthday child chooses where the whole family eats.
records.zomi: Kum simin pianni naupang in innkuan bup' an nekna mun a teel hi.

records.english: Mom never liked cooking, so Dad made most of our meals when we were young.
records.zomi: Nu in an huan a deih ngei kei ahih manin i neu lai-in Pa in i an a tam zaw a huan hi.

records.english: My uncle prefers to give money rather than gifts, because he says he never knows what we want.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in i deih a theih ngei loh manin letsong sangin sum piak a deih zaw hi.

records.english: Our family likes simple holidays: a tent, a river, and plenty of time together.
records.zomi: I innkuan in tawlngakni baih a deih hi: puan inn khat, gun khat leh khawm-a hun tampi.

records.english: We each have our own favorite spot in the house, and nobody takes anyone else's.
records.zomi: Inn sungah i khat ciat in i deih pen mun i nei a, kuamah in mi dang' mun a la kei hi.

records.english: Follow your own path; the family will support you all the way.
records.zomi: Nangma' lampi zui in; innkuan in a tawp dong hong huh ding hi.

records.english: Grandpa would rather walk to church than take the bus, even at eighty-five.
records.zomi: Kum sawmgiat leh nga a pha napi Pu in bus tuan sangin pawlpi ah kaai a deih zaw hi.

records.english: My sister and I share a love of old movies, which we watch together every Sunday.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu leh kei movie lui i deih kibang a, Nipini simin khawm in i en hi.

records.english: You can borrow my camera for the trip if you'd like to take photos of the mountains.
records.zomi: Mualte lim la na deih leh khualzinna adingin ka camera na leitawi thei hi.

records.english: Would you like the window seat, Grandma, so that you can see the hills?
records.zomi: Pi, mualte na muh theih nadingin tawhkhawng kiang tutna na deih hiam?

records.english: My husband prefers his tea strong, so I always make his first.
records.zomi: Ka pasal in a tea a hat a deih ahih manin a' pen ka bawl masa tawntung hi.

records.english: Our son has started choosing his own music, and we're not always fans of it.
records.zomi: I tapa in amah' la a teel kipan a, i deih tawntung kei hi.

records.english: My children like their grandfather's stories more than any cartoon.
records.zomi: Ka tate in cartoon khempeuh sangin a pu' tangthute a deih zaw uh hi.

records.english: Why does your little brother insist on wearing his superhero cape to school?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na nau pasal in a superhero puan sang ah silh a ngiat hiam?

records.english: My husband likes the house quiet in the evenings, while the children prefer music and noise.
records.zomi: Ka pasal in nitak ciangin inn dai a deih a, naupangte in la leh buaina a deih zaw uh hi.

records.english: I'd love a small house near my parents rather than a big one far away.
records.zomi: Gamla-a inn lian sangin ka nu leh ka pa kiang-a inn neu khat ka deih zaw hi.

records.english: If I could choose, I'd spend every holiday at my grandmother's house.
records.zomi: Ka teel thei leh tawlngakni khempeuh ka pi' inn ah ka zang ding hi.

records.english: Our children prefer helping in the garden to doing homework, of course.
records.zomi: I tate in inn-a sep ding sangin huan sung huh a deih zaw uh hi.

records.english: Do you prefer to celebrate New Year with your family or with friends?
records.zomi: Kum Thak na innkuan tawh na bawl nuam zaw hiam, na lawmte tawh hiam?

records.english: Always with family — it wouldn't feel like New Year without them.
records.zomi: Innkuan tawh tawntung — amaute om lo-in Kum Thak bang lo ding hi.

records.english: Does Dad still save the newspaper crossword for Sunday mornings?
records.zomi: Pa in Nipini zingsang adingin thuthak lai kammal kimawlna a kem lai hiam?

records.english: My brothers love football, but I'd rather spend the afternoon reading with Grandpa.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasalte in football a deih uh a, ahi zongin kei in sun lam Pu tawh lai sim ka deih zaw hi.

records.english: I'd prefer a quiet birthday dinner with family to a big party.
records.zomi: Pawi lian sangin innkuan tawh pianni nitak an dai ka deih zaw hi.

records.english: My aunt prefers handwritten letters, so I still send her one every month.
records.zomi: Ka ni in khut tawh kigelh lai a deih zaw ahih manin kha simin khat ka khak lai hi.

records.english: Kids, each of you can choose one place for our summer trip.
records.zomi: Naupangte, i khal khualzinna adingin note khat ciat in mun khat na teel thei uh hi.

records.english: Is there a color you'd like for the baby's room?
records.zomi: Naungek khan adingin na deih lim khat a om hiam?

records.english: Maybe a soft green, so that it works for a boy or a girl.
records.zomi: Eng nem khat kha ding hi, pasal hiam numei hiam a kilawm theih nadingin.

records.english: Is it okay if I paint my room dark blue?
records.zomi: Ka khan dum nak takin ka khai leh a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: Sure, as long as you help with the painting.
records.zomi: Hoih hi, lim khaina na huh phial leh.

records.english: My daughter would rather wear traditional clothes than jeans at every festival.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in pawi khempeuh ah jeans sangin i ngeina puan silh a deih zaw hi.

records.english: Dad has always preferred working outside to sitting in an office.
records.zomi: Pa in office sungah tut sangin polam ah nasep a deih zaw tawntung hi.

records.english: Do you take after your mother or your father in your tastes?
records.zomi: Na deih dan ah na nu na kibang hiam, na pa na kibang hiam?

records.english: My father, definitely — we both love fishing and hate shopping.
records.zomi: Ka pa, a kician hi — i nih in nga man i deih a, van lei i huat hi.

records.english: Shall I buy the blue bicycle or the red one for your nephew?
records.zomi: Na tanau adingin siiksakol dum ka lei ding hiam, a san ka lei ding hiam?

records.english: The red one — he's been talking about it for weeks.
records.zomi: A san — kal tampi sung a gen hi.

records.english: Would you rather live with your parents or have your own apartment after university?
records.zomi: Sangpi khit ciangin na nu leh na pa tawh om na deih zaw hiam, nangma' inn neih na deih zaw hiam?

records.english: With my parents, at least for a while, so that I can save money.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa tawh, sum ka khol theih nadingin hun tawmno sung bek zongin.

records.english: Grandpa chose the name of each of his grandchildren, and he loved every one of them.
records.zomi: Pu in a tu-te khat ciat' min a teel a, khempeuh a it hi.

records.english: My cousins prefer the city, but I'll always be a village girl at heart.
records.zomi: Ka sanggamte in khuapi a deih zaw uh a, ahi zongin kei ka lungsim ah khua numei naupang ka hi den ding hi.

records.english: Grandma prefers sitting on the porch to watching television.
records.zomi: Pi in television en sangin inn mai ah tut a deih zaw hi.

records.english: My mother loves bright colors, so I knitted her a red-and-yellow scarf.
records.zomi: Ka nu in lim tang a deih ahih manin san leh ngaan tawh ngawng puan khat ka khuih sak hi.

records.english: Could we have the family photo taken outside, under the mango tree?
records.zomi: Innkuan lim pen polam theihai kung nuai ah i la thei ding hiam?

records.english: The children were allowed to decorate their own rooms however they liked.
records.zomi: Naupangte in amau khan a deih dan bangin a zeem thei uh hi.

records.english: You might enjoy the choir; your grandmother sang in it for forty years.
records.zomi: La sa pawl na deih kha ding hi; na pi in kum sawmli sung tua ah la a sa hi.

records.english: Our family's story is written in the old Bible, with every birth and marriage recorded inside.
records.zomi: I innkuan tangthu pen Laisiangtho lui sungah kigelh a, suahna leh kiteenna khempeuh a sung ah kigelh hi.

records.english: Kids, ask your great-uncle about the night the river flooded the whole village.
records.zomi: Naupangte, na pu neu kiangah gun in khua bup a dimsak zan thu dong un.

records.english: Those years were hard, but nobody in our family ever went to bed hungry.
records.zomi: Tua kumte haksa hi, ahi zongin i innkuan ah kuamah gilkial tawh a ihmu ngei kei uh hi.

records.english: Learning to ride on my father's old bicycle is one of my earliest memories.
records.zomi: Ka pa' siiksakol lui tawh tuan ka sin pen ka phawk masa pen khat ahi hi.

records.english: It took me years to understand why my father worked so hard.
records.zomi: Ka pa bang hangin hanciam takin na a sep hiam ka theih nadingin kum tampi a sau hi.

records.english: Growing up in a house with three generations taught me to respect people of every age.
records.zomi: Suak thum a omna inn ah ka khan manin kum khempeuh mite zahtak ka sin hi.

records.english: We weren't rich, but my parents always found a way to give us a birthday cake.
records.zomi: I hau kei hi, ahi zongin ka nu leh ka pa in pianni cake hong piak nading lampi a mu tawntung uh hi.

records.english: My grandparents' wedding lasted a whole week, and every family in the village helped.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh pite' kiteenna kal khat bup a sau a, khua sung innkuan khempeuh in a huh uh hi.

records.english: My parents crossed the mountains on foot to reach a safer town before I was born.
records.zomi: Ka suah ma-in ka nu leh ka pa khua bitna zaw a tun nadingun mualte khe tawh a kantan uh hi.

records.english: My uncle shares his war stories only when the grandchildren ask him directly.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in tu-te in amah tak a dot uh ciangin bek a gal tangthute a gen hi.

records.english: When I was small, children weren't allowed to speak at the table while the elders were eating.
records.zomi: Ka neu lai-in upate an a nek laitakin naupangte dawhkan ah kiho thei lo uh hi.

records.english: What was life like when you were a child, Grandma?
records.zomi: Pi, na neu lai-in nuntakna bangci ahi hiam?

records.english: Hard, but we were happy because the whole family lived and worked together.
records.zomi: Haksa hi, ahi zongin innkuan bup khawm-a i om a, khawm-a na i sep manin i lungdam hi.

records.english: Many of my parents' stories begin with the words "When we had nothing..."
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa' tangthu tampi “Bangmah i neih loh lai-in...” cih kammal tawh kipan hi.

records.english: My older sister taught me to read before I ever started school.
records.zomi: Sang ka kah ma-in ka u nu in lai sim hong hilh hi.

records.english: My mother learned to sew to make clothes for all eight of her children.
records.zomi: Ka nu in a tate giat khempeuh' puan bawl nadingin puan khui a sin hi.

records.english: Could I bring my children to hear your stories next Sunday?
records.zomi: Nipini hong ding ciangin na tangthute za dingin ka tate ka paipih thei ding hiam?

records.english: I'd be delighted; it's been years since anyone asked.
records.zomi: Ka lungdam mahmah ding hi; kuamah in hong dot pan kum tampi a cing khin hi.

records.english: You can borrow Grandpa's old photo albums, but please handle them carefully.
records.zomi: Pu' lim bu luite na leitawi thei hi, ahi zongin pilvang takin kem in.

records.english: Our family got its first television when I was ten, and the whole street came to watch.
records.zomi: Ka kum sawm lai-in i innkuan in television masa pen a nei a, lam bup in en dingin hong pai uh hi.

records.english: Dad tells the story of his first day in the city as if it happened yesterday.
records.zomi: Pa in khuapi-a a ni masa pen tangthu zanni-a piang bangin a gen hi.

records.english: Can I write down your story so that my children can read it one day?
records.zomi: Ka tate in ni khat ni-in a sim theih nadingun na tangthu ka gelh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Only if you promise to write it exactly as I tell it.
records.zomi: Ka gen bang kim-in na gelh ding na kiciam leh bek.

records.english: When I was small, my brothers and I built a raft and tried to cross the lake.
records.zomi: Ka neu lai-in ka sanggam pasalte leh kei sing tembaw khat i bawl a, dil kantan dingin i hanciam hi.

records.english: Why do you keep that old key?
records.zomi: Bang hangin tua tawh lui na kem hiam?

records.english: It's the key to the house where I was born, which no longer stands.
records.zomi: Ka suahna inn tawh ahi a, tua inn om nawn lo hi.

records.english: My cousin's family was the first in our village to own a telephone, and everyone queued to use it.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam' innkuan i khua ah telephone a nei masa pen uh a, mi khempeuh in zang dingin a kizom uh hi.

records.english: Mom kept a diary all her life, and reading it after she died was like hearing her voice again.
records.zomi: Nu in a nuntak sung bup diary a gelh a, a sih khit ciangin sim pen a aw za kik bang hi.

records.english: Thank you for sharing your story with us tonight.
records.zomi: Tu zanin na tangthu hong hawm manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: Please, Grandpa, tell us the story about the tiger again!
records.zomi: Pu, humpi tangthu hong gen kik in!

records.english: Shall I show you the letters my grandfather wrote from the army?
records.zomi: Ka pu in galkap pan a gelh laite kong etsak ding hiam?

records.english: Grandpa, will you tell us again how you met Grandma at the market?
records.zomi: Pu, zuakna mun ah Pi na kimuh dan hong gen kik ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Have you ever told the kids about the night their uncle was born during a storm?
records.zomi: Naupangte' pa neu huihpi laitakin a suah zan thu naupangte kiangah na gen ngei hiam?

records.english: Did your father ever tell you about his first job?
records.zomi: Na pa in a nasep masa pen thu hong gen ngei hiam?

records.english: He sold vegetables from a cart when he was only nine.
records.zomi: Kum kua bek a phak lai-in leeng tung pan anteh a zuak hi.

records.english: Grandma still saves every scrap of cloth, because she remembers when new clothes were rare.
records.zomi: Puan thak a tam loh hun a phawk ahih manin Pi in puan tam neu khempeuh a kem lai hi.

records.english: Be careful with Grandma's photo box; some of the pictures are almost a hundred years old.
records.zomi: Pi' lim bawm tungah pilvang in; lim khenkhat kum za khat bang a pha khin hi.

records.english: Our old house had no running water, so we carried buckets from the well every morning.
records.zomi: I inn lui ah tui pipe om lo ahih manin zingsang simin tuikhuk pan khuang tawh tui i puak hi.

records.english: Do you think your grandchildren will want to hear your stories one day?
records.zomi: Na tu-te in ni khat ni-in na tangthute a zak nuam ding uh in na ngaihsun hiam?

records.english: Before electricity reached our village, we did our homework by the light of an oil lamp.
records.zomi: I khua ah meivak a tun ma-in datmei vak tawh inn-a sep ding i sem hi.

records.english: Could you tell the children about the year you spent working on a fishing boat?
records.zomi: Nga manna tembaw tungah na sep kum thu naupangte kiangah na gen thei ding hiam?

records.english: Dad worked in a mine for six years so that his brothers could finish school.
records.zomi: A sanggam pasalte in sang a zawh theih nadingun Pa in kum guk sung suang tukna ah na a sem hi.

records.english: Every family has a story it doesn't talk about, and ours is my great-uncle's disappearance.
records.zomi: Innkuan khempeuh in a gen ngei loh tangthu khat a nei uh a, i' pen ka pu neu' mangthang thu ahi hi.

records.english: When we moved to the city, my brother and I got lost on our very first day.
records.zomi: Khuapi ah i pem ciangin ni masa pen mahmah-in ka sanggam pasal leh kei lampi i mansuah hi.

records.english: The first time I saw the sea, I was twenty-two and already a mother.
records.zomi: Tuipi ka muh masa pen-in kum sawmnih leh nih ka pha a, nu ka suak khin hi.

records.english: My grandmother kept her wedding dress for sixty years so that her granddaughters could see it.
records.zomi: Ka pi in a tunute in a muh theih nadingun a kiteenna puan kum sawmguk sung a kem hi.

records.english: My father-in-law built his first house with his own hands and the help of his neighbors.
records.zomi: Ka sungpa in a inn masa pen amah' khut leh a inn vengte' huhna tawh a lam hi.

records.english: Before he left to work abroad, Dad gave each of us a small job to do while he was gone.
records.zomi: Gamdang ah na sem dingin a pai ma-in a om lo sung-a i sep ding nasep neu khat ciat Pa in hong pia hi.

records.english: You may hear some sad stories tonight, so be gentle with Grandma.
records.zomi: Tu zanin tangthu dahhuai tawmno na za kha ding uh ahih manin Pi tung ah lungsim nem takin om un.

records.english: Is it true that you once walked all the way to the city for a job interview?
records.zomi: Nasep dotna dingin khuapi dong na kaai ngei hi, cih a man hiam?

records.english: Yes, and I got the job, so it was worth every step.
records.zomi: Man hi, nasep ka ngah ahih manin khe suan khempeuh a manpha hi.

records.english: My cousin and I spent our childhood summers swimming in the same river our parents swam in.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam leh kei i nu leh pa' kidiahna gun mah ah i naupan lai nipite i kidiah hi.

records.english: How did your parents decide to leave the village?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa in khua paisan dingin bangci-in a khensat uh hiam?

records.english: Dad was offered work in the city, and Mom agreed so that we could go to a better school.
records.zomi: Pa khuapi ah nasep kipia a, sang hoih zaw i kah theih nadingin Nu a lungkim hi.

records.english: Our first family trip abroad was full of mistakes, but it's the one we laugh about most.
records.zomi: I innkuan' gamdang khualzinna masa pen khialhna tawh a dim a, ahi zongin i nuihsat pen ahi hi.

records.english: My mother's hands were rough from years of farm work, but they were the gentlest hands I knew.
records.zomi: Kum tampi lo sepna in ka nu' khut a nonsak a, ahi zongin ka theih khut nem pen ahi hi.

records.english: Telling these stories keeps our family history alive for the next generation.
records.zomi: Hih tangthute i gen manin i innkuan tangthu suak hong ding adingin a nung den hi.

records.english: We used to collect firewood every afternoon before we were allowed to play.
records.zomi: I kimawl phal ma-in nitak simin sing i la zel hi.

records.english: My aunt was the first woman in our village to drive a car.
records.zomi: Ka ni pen i khua ah mawtaw mawng masa pen numei ahi hi.

records.english: We might never know the whole story of how our great-grandparents came to this valley.
records.zomi: I pu leh pite' nu leh pate hih guam ah bangci-in a tun uh hiam tangthu bup i thei ngei kei kha ding hi.

records.english: Please write your name and your department on the sticker.
records.zomi: Sticker tungah na min leh na department gelh in.

records.english: Tell us your name, your hometown, and what you hope to learn this year.
records.zomi: Na min, na khua leh tu kum na sin nuam hong gen in.

records.english: I moved here to work at the hospital, and I'm still finding my way around town.
records.zomi: Zato ah na sem dingin hih ah ka pem a, khua sung lampi ka zong lai hi.

records.english: No one may leave the orientation session until everyone has been introduced.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh a kitheisak khit ma-un kuamah in kipatna kikhopna a paisan thei kei ding hi.

records.english: My voice shook when I introduced myself at my first staff meeting.
records.zomi: Ka nasep kikhopna masa pen-in ka kitheisak ciangin ka aw a ling hi.

records.english: On my first day at the factory, I was introduced to forty people and forgot every name.
records.zomi: Factory ah ka ni masa pen-in mi sawmli kiangah hong theisak uh a, min khempeuh ka mangngilh hi.

records.english: Hello, I'm the parent volunteer who'll be helping in the library on Fridays.
records.zomi: Hello, Laithai ni simin laibu inn ah a huh ding nu leh pa thalawp ka hi hi.

records.english: The new students were asked to introduce themselves in pairs.
records.zomi: Sangnaupang thakte nih ciat-in kitheisak dingin kingen uh hi.

records.english: I'm a substitute teacher, so you may see me in a different class every week.
records.zomi: Saya laih ka hih manin kal simin kilasi tuam ah nong mu kha ding hi.

records.english: Could you say your name once more for the attendance list?
records.zomi: Sang om-lo list adingin na min vei khat gen kik thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: You might recognize me — I used to teach your older brother.
records.zomi: Nong thei kha ding hi — na u pasal ka hilh ngei hi.

records.english: Call me if anything breaks — I'm the one who repairs the computers.
records.zomi: Bangmah a siat leh hong sam in — computer bawlpa ka hi hi.

records.english: A mechanic by trade, I'm now studying to become a teacher.
records.zomi: Mawtaw bawlpa ka hi a, tu-in saya suak dingin ka kisin hi.

records.english: It's a pleasure to join such a friendly team.
records.zomi: Hih bang lawm hoih pawl ah ka kihel theih ka lungdam hi.

records.english: The new principal was introduced to parents at the start-of-year meeting.
records.zomi: Kum kipatna kikhopna ah sang makaipa thak nu leh pate kiangah kitheisak hi.

records.english: Introduce yourself to the parents at the door so that they know who is teaching their children.
records.zomi: Kua in a tate a hilh hiam a theih theih nadingun kongkhak ah nu leh pate kiangah kitheisak in.

records.english: Hello, I'm calling from the school to introduce myself as your son's new teacher.
records.zomi: Hello, na tapa' saya thak ka hih thu kitheisak dingin sang pan kong sam hi.

records.english: You'll find me in the nurse's office next to the library.
records.zomi: Laibu inn kiang nurse office ah nong mu ding hi.

records.english: What do you want to be when you finish school?
records.zomi: Sang na zawh ciangin bang suak na deih hiam?

records.english: A veterinarian, because I love animals.
records.zomi: Ganhing siavuan, ganhingte ka it ahih manin.

records.english: I worked as a translator for many years before I became a lecturer.
records.zomi: Lecturer ka suak ma-in kum tampi sung laiteipa in na ka sem hi.

records.english: I've been sent from the head office to help you set up the new branch.
records.zomi: Branch thak na phut nadingun hong huh dingin office lian pan hong sawl uh hi.

records.english: My first job was washing dishes in my uncle's restaurant.
records.zomi: Ka nasep masa pen ka pa neu' an zuakna dawl ah kuang sil ahi hi.

records.english: As the new intern in the marketing department, I'm here to learn as much as I can.
records.zomi: Marketing department ah intern thak ka hih manin ka sin theih tawp sin dingin hih ah ka om hi.

records.english: Could you introduce yourself to the class and tell us one thing you enjoy?
records.zomi: Kilasi kiangah kitheisak inla na deih na khat hong gen thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: I teach math in the mornings and run the chess club in the afternoons.
records.zomi: Zingsangin math ka hilh a, sun lam ciangin chess pawl ka kem hi.

records.english: Before we start, let's go around the room and introduce ourselves.
records.zomi: I kipat ma-in khan sung kimkot in kitheisak ni.

records.english: As the new head of the department, I'd like to meet each of you individually this week.
records.zomi: Department makaipa thak ka hih manin hih kal sungin note khat ciat tuam-in kong mu nuam hi.

records.english: Before you introduce yourselves, write your name on the card in front of you.
records.zomi: Na kitheisak ma-un na mai-a card tungah na min uh gelh un.

records.english: Introducing yourself to a room full of experienced colleagues can be intimidating.
records.zomi: Theihna nei nasem lawmte a dim khan ah kitheisak pen laukhuai thei hi.

records.english: Hi, everyone — I'm Lian, the youngest teacher at this school.
records.zomi: Hi, mi khempeuh — Lian ka hi hi, hih sang-a saya nau pen.

records.english: I'm a second-year nursing student, and I'll be shadowing you this week.
records.zomi: Nursing kum nihna sangnaupang ka hi a, hih kal sungin nang kong zui ding hi.

records.english: I'm Kim, and I'll be covering for Mr. Thang while he's on leave.
records.zomi: Kim ka hi a, Mr. Thang a khawl sungin a nasep ka laih ding hi.

records.english: I'm here to replace Mrs. Lun, who has retired after thirty years.
records.zomi: Kum sawmthum khit ciangin a khawl Mrs. Lun' mun laih dingin hih ah ka om hi.

records.english: Is this your first job after university?
records.zomi: Hih pen sangpi khit-a na nasep masa pen ahi hiam?

records.english: Yes, so please be patient with me while I learn.
records.zomi: Hi hi, tua ahih manin ka sin laitakin hong thuakzawh un.

records.english: Where did you study before you joined our company?
records.zomi: I company ah na hong lut ma-in koi ah sang na kah hiam?

records.english: I trained as an engineer in the capital and worked there for five years.
records.zomi: Gam khuapi lian ah engineer dingin ka kisin a, tua ah kum nga sung na ka sem hi.

records.english: Being introduced as "the new boss" made me very nervous on my first day.
records.zomi: “Makaipa thak” ci-in hong theisak uh ciangin ka ni masa pen-in ka lau mahmah hi.

records.english: I study engineering at night and work in a garage during the day.
records.zomi: Zanin engineering ka sin a, sun lam ciangin mawtaw bawlna mun ah na ka sem hi.

records.english: It might help if you mention which projects you've worked on before.
records.zomi: Na sep ngei project te na gen leh a huh kha ding hi.

records.english: I may be new to this school, but I've been teaching for fifteen years.
records.zomi: Hih sang ah ka thak kha ding hi, ahi zongin kum sawm leh nga sung lai ka hilh khin hi.

records.english: Nobody told me I'd have to give a speech on my first day.
records.zomi: Ka ni masa pen-in thu ka gen kul ding kuamah in hong gen kei uh hi.

records.english: The principal asked me to introduce myself to the new students at the assembly.
records.zomi: Sang kikhopna ah sangnaupang thakte kiangah kitheisak dingin sang makaipa in hong ngen hi.

records.english: What subject do you teach?
records.zomi: Bang laisim na hilh hiam?

records.english: History, and I coach the girls' basketball team.
records.zomi: Tangthu, numei naupangte' basketball pawl zong ka hilh hi.

records.english: I joined the company to gain experience in international trade.
records.zomi: Gam tuam tuam sumbawlna ah theihna ngah dingin company ah ka lut hi.

records.english: I'll be taking care of your new laptops, so let me know if you have any problems.
records.zomi: Na laptop thakte ka kem ding ahih manin buaina na neih leh hong gen un.

records.english: Since I'm new here, could you show me where the staff room is?
records.zomi: Hih ah ka thak ahih manin nasemte' khan koi ah om hiam hong lak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Excuse me, I'm the new cleaner — which floor should I start on?
records.zomi: Hong maisak in, siangsak thak ka hi hi — dawl bang pan ka kipan ding hiam?

records.english: You can call me by my first name; we don't use titles in this office.
records.zomi: Ka min mah tawh hong sam thei hi; hih office ah min tawh tuam i zang kei hi.

records.english: Please introduce yourself to the manager before your shift begins.
records.zomi: Na nasep hun a kipat ma-in manager kiangah kitheisak in.

records.english: Our new coworker introduced herself by bringing everyone homemade cookies.
records.zomi: I nasem lawm thak in mi khempeuh adingin inn-a bawl cookie tawi-in a kitheisak hi.

records.english: Were you introduced to the team yesterday?
records.zomi: Zanni-in pawl kiangah hong theisak uh hiam?

records.english: No, the manager was away, so I'll meet everyone this afternoon.
records.zomi: Theisak kei uh hi, manager a om kei ahih manin tu nitak ciangin mi khempeuh ka mu ding hi.

records.english: Good afternoon, everyone — I'm Ms. Cing, and I'll be your science teacher this year.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, Sunpha — Ms. Cing ka hi a, tu kum na science saya ka hi ding hi.

records.english: I've just transferred from a school in the north, so I don't know anyone yet.
records.zomi: Saklam sang khat pan ka pem thak ahih manin kuamah ka thei nai kei hi.

records.english: I was hired to help the team with the new accounting system.
records.zomi: Sum gelhna system thak ah pawl huh dingin hong sap uh hi.

records.english: I've been in charge of the warehouse for ten years, so ask me anything about deliveries.
records.zomi: Van koihna inn kum sawm sung ka kem ahih manin van puak thu khempeuh hong dong thei hi.

records.english: Could you tell the new staff a little about yourself and your role?
records.zomi: Nasem thakte kiangah na thu leh na nasep tawmno na gen thei ding hiam?

records.english: Children aren't allowed at the evening meeting, because it might run very late.
records.zomi: Nitak kikhopna a sau mahmah kha ding ahih manin naupangte kihel thei lo uh hi.

records.english: I introduced my roommate to my coworkers, and now she works here too.
records.zomi: Ka khan kihawm lawm ka nasem lawmte kiangah ka theisak a, tu-in hih ah na a sem zong hi.

records.english: Which of these children is your son?
records.zomi: Hih naupangte lak ah kua na tapa ahi hiam?

records.english: The one in the red cap, sitting next to the window.
records.zomi: Tawhkhawng kiang ah a tu, lukhu san khu pa.

records.english: The new teacher met the parents for the first time at the school fair.
records.zomi: Saya thak in sang poai ah nu leh pate a mu masa pen hi.

records.english: My son's teacher and I turned out to be old schoolmates.
records.zomi: Ka tapa' saya leh kei sang lawm lui i hi hi.

records.english: Everyone, my mother will be talking to the class about her work as a nurse on career day.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, nasep ni ah ka nu in a nurse nasep thu kilasi kiangah a gen ding hi.

records.english: I'd like you to meet my best friend from school; she's applying for a job here.
records.zomi: Sang pan ka lawm hoih pen na theih ding ka deih hi; hih ah nasep a ngen hi.

records.english: Who's the man you were talking to at the gate?
records.zomi: Kongpi kiang ah na kihopih pa kua ahi hiam?

records.english: That's my uncle; he drives the school bus.
records.zomi: Tua pen ka pa neu ahi hi; sang bus a mawng hi.

records.english: Is it okay if my friend sits with us at the graduation?
records.zomi: Sang zawhna poai ah ka lawm i kiang ah a tut leh a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: There's plenty of room; she's very welcome.
records.zomi: Mun tampi om hi; a kidawn mahmah hi.

records.english: Mom, this is Mr. Pau, my science teacher.
records.zomi: Nu, hih pen Mr. Pau, ka science saya ahi hi.

records.english: My father was introduced to my manager at the factory's open day.
records.zomi: Factory hon ni-in ka pa ka manager kiangah kitheisak hi.

records.english: At this school, students may not bring visitors into the classroom without permission.
records.zomi: Hih sang ah sangnaupangte in phalna om lo-in kilasi sungah khualte paipih thei lo uh hi.

records.english: It's a good idea to introduce your friends to your parents so that they know who you spend time with.
records.zomi: Kua tawh hun na zang hiam a theih theih nadingun na lawmte na nu leh na pa kiangah theisak pen a hoih hi.

records.english: Our neighbor's son started working at my company, and we now share a ride every morning.
records.zomi: I inn veng' tapa in ka company ah na a sem kipan a, tu-in zingsang simin mawtaw i kihawm hi.

records.english: This is my colleague Grace, who helped me finish the report on time.
records.zomi: Hih pen ka nasem lawm Grace ahi a, report hun takah ka zawh nadingin hong huh hi.

records.english: This is the friend who taught me how to use the new software at work.
records.zomi: Hih pen nasepna ah software thak zat dan hong hilh lawm ahi hi.

records.english: Can you tell the class a little about your family?
records.zomi: Kilasi kiangah na innkuan thu tawmno na gen thei ding hiam?

records.english: My father is a farmer, my mother is a teacher, and I have two little sisters.
records.zomi: Ka pa lo nei ahi a, ka nu saya ahi a, nau numei nih ka nei hi.

records.english: Please introduce your guest to the receptionist so that she can give him a visitor's badge.
records.zomi: Visitor badge a piak theih nadingin na khual reception nu kiangah theisak in.

records.english: Could you introduce your parents to the principal after the ceremony?
records.zomi: Poai khit ciangin na nu leh na pa sang makaipa kiangah na theisak thei ding hiam?

records.english: The visitors were shown around the factory by my uncle, who has worked there for thirty years.
records.zomi: Kum sawmthum sung tua ah na a sem ka pa neu in hong vehte factory sung a etsak hi.

records.english: Let me introduce my business partner, who also happens to be my cousin.
records.zomi: Ka sumbawl lawm kong theisak ning, amah ka sanggam zong ahi hi.

records.english: Is that your father in the photo on your desk?
records.zomi: Na dawhkan tung lim sung ah na pa ahi hiam?

records.english: Yes, it was taken on his last day at the bank before he retired.
records.zomi: Hi hi, a khawl ma-in bank ah a ni nunung pen-in kila ahi hi.

records.english: Did you introduce your fiancé to your colleagues at the office party?
records.zomi: Office pawi ah na kiteen ding pasal na nasem lawmte kiangah na theisak hiam?

records.english: You may have met my brother already; he works in the shipping department.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal na mu khin kha ding hi; shipping department ah na a sem hi.

records.english: Have you met my husband, who's joining us for the office dinner?
records.zomi: Office nitak an ah hong kihel ding ka pasal na mu khin hiam?

records.english: My sister might be able to help you; she works in the hospital's personnel office.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu in hong huh thei kha ding hi; zato' nasem kem office ah na a sem hi.

records.english: Can I bring my little brother to the school concert?
records.zomi: Sang la poai ah ka nau pasal ka paipih thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, family members are welcome in the hall.
records.zomi: Thei hi, innkuan mite inn lian ah kidawn hi.

records.english: Nobody at work knew I had a twin until she visited the office.
records.zomi: Ka apeng nu office hong veh dong nasepna ah kuamah in apeng ka neih a thei kei uh hi.

records.english: My mother-in-law came to my office to meet the people I work with.
records.zomi: Ka sungnu in ka nasem lawmte mu dingin ka office ah hong pai hi.

records.english: When I introduced my parents to my professor, Dad shook his hand for a whole minute.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa ka professor kiangah ka theisak ciangin Pa in minit khat bup a khut a len hi.

records.english: "I've heard so much about you," my boss said when I introduced my husband at the party.
records.zomi: Pawi ah ka pasal ka theisak ciangin, “Na thu tampi ka za khin hi,” ci-in ka makaipa in a gen hi.

records.english: Dad, these are the classmates I told you about from the robotics club.
records.zomi: Pa, hih te robotics pawl pan kong gen ngei ka kilasi lawmte ahi uh hi.

records.english: I'd like to recommend my friend for the job; she's the hardest worker I know.
records.zomi: Hih nasep adingin ka lawm ka gen sak nuam hi; ka theih mi lak ah a hanciam pen ahi hi.

records.english: My parents were so proud to meet my teachers at the prize-giving.
records.zomi: Laksap piakna poai ah ka nu leh ka pa in ka sayate a muh uh ciangin a kisaktheih mahmah uh hi.

records.english: Our two families became friends after our children were put in the same class.
records.zomi: I tate kilasi khat ah a kikoih khit ciangin i innkuan nih a kilawm uh hi.

records.english: Kids, please say hello to my coworkers before you sit down.
records.zomi: Naupangte, na tut ma-un ka nasem lawmte kiangah hello ci un.

records.english: Thank you for welcoming my family to your workplace.
records.zomi: Na nasepna mun ah ka innkuan hong muak manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: This is my friend Joseph, who's thinking of joining our team.
records.zomi: Hih pen ka lawm Joseph ahi a, i pawl ah kihel dingin a ngaihsun hi.

records.english: Could you show my parents around the school while I finish my exam?
records.zomi: Ka sitna ka zawh ma-in ka nu leh ka pa sang sung na etsak thei ding hiam?

records.english: I was introduced to my husband by a coworker who thought we'd get along.
records.zomi: Ka pasal pen i kilem ding a ci nasem lawm khat in hong theisak hi.

records.english: Have you two met before, or shall I introduce you?
records.zomi: Note nih na kimu ngei uh hiam, kong theisak ding hiam?

records.english: This is my daughter's teacher, who taught me as well, twenty years ago.
records.zomi: Hih pen ka tanu' saya ahi a, kum sawmnih paisa-in kei zong hong hilh hi.

records.english: My son was so shy when I introduced him to my colleagues that he hid behind my legs.
records.zomi: Ka nasem lawmte kiangah ka theisak ciangin ka tapa a zahlak lua ahih manin ka khe nung lam ah a bu hi.

records.english: I'd love for you to meet my mentor; she changed the way I think about my work.
records.zomi: Hong makaih nu na theih ding ka deih mahmah hi; ka nasep tung ah ka ngaihsutna a khel hi.

records.english: Did you know my coworker's daughter goes to the same kindergarten as yours?
records.zomi: Ka nasem lawm' tanu na ta' kindergarten mah ah a kah thu na thei hiam?

records.english: Kids, this is Ms. Grace, who will be looking after you on the field trip.
records.zomi: Naupangte, hih pen Ms. Grace ahi a, khualzinna ah hong kem ding hi.

records.english: My best friend's mother was my first boss, and she taught me everything about running a shop.
records.zomi: Ka lawm hoih pen' nu pen ka makaipa masa pen ahi a, dawl kem dan khempeuh hong hilh hi.

records.english: My cousin got me an interview at his company, but I had to earn the job myself.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam in a company ah dotna hong ngah sak a, ahi zongin nasep pen kei mah in ka ngah kul hi.

records.english: How do you know Mr. Thang?
records.zomi: Mr. Thang bangci-in na thei hiam?

records.english: He was my father's student many years ago.
records.zomi: Kum tampi paisa-in ka pa' sangnaupang ahi hi.

records.english: I introduced my sister to the head of the nursing program, and she was accepted the next year.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu nursing program makaipa kiangah ka theisak a, a kum zom ciangin a kisang hi.

records.english: My friend's father offered me an internship after we met at their dinner table.
records.zomi: A innkuan dawhkan ah i kimuh khit ciangin ka lawm' pa in internship hong pia hi.

records.english: You might recognize my daughter; she started at your school last term.
records.zomi: Ka tanu na thei kha ding hi; term bei-in na sang ah a kah kipan hi.

records.english: My colleagues were surprised to meet my grandmother, who still runs her own shop at eighty.
records.zomi: Kum sawmgiat a pha napi amah' dawl a kem lai ka pi a muh uh ciangin ka nasem lawmte a lamdang sa uh hi.

records.english: Guests can enter the laboratory only with a teacher.
records.zomi: Khualte saya tawh bek laboratory ah a lut thei uh hi.

records.english: Is there parking for visitors near the main building?
records.zomi: Inn lian kiang ah khualte adingin mawtaw koihna a om hiam?

records.english: Yes, behind the library, next to the teachers' cars.
records.zomi: Om hi, laibu inn nung lam ah, sayate' mawtaw kiang ah.

records.english: Could someone fetch an extra chair for our guest?
records.zomi: I khual adingin kuamah in tutna behlap khat hong la thei ding hiam?

records.english: Could you meet the new teacher at the bus station and bring her to the school?
records.zomi: Bus station ah saya thak na dawn a, sang ah na paipih thei ding hiam?

records.english: Can I offer you some tea while you wait for your interview?
records.zomi: Na dotna na ngak laitakin tea kong pia thei ding hiam?

records.english: Our receptionist always remembers visitors' names, which makes them feel welcome.
records.zomi: I reception nu in khualte' min a phawk tawntung a, amaute a kidawn bangin a kisak uh hi.

records.english: The students were told not to run in the corridors while the guests were in the building.
records.zomi: Khualte inn sungah a om sungun lampi khan ah tai lo dingin sangnaupangte kihilh hi.

records.english: "Thank you for coming all this way," the headmaster said as he shook each parent's hand.
records.zomi: “Hih dong hong pai manun ka lungdam hi,” ci-in sang makaipa in nu leh pa khat ciat' khut a len hi.

records.english: The interpreter helped our visitors from abroad understand the presentation.
records.zomi: Gamdang pan hong vehte in kigen thu a theih theih nadingun pau leipa in a huh hi.

records.english: Our team made a welcome video for the new staff who couldn't come in person.
records.zomi: I pawl in hong tung thei lo nasem thakte adingin muakna video khat a bawl hi.

records.english: Our visitors were given a basket of local fruit as a welcome gift.
records.zomi: I khualte muakna letsong-in khua sung singgah bawm khat kipia uh hi.

records.english: Please wait here; I'll let the manager know you've arrived.
records.zomi: Hih ah ngak in; na tun thu manager kiangah ka gen ding hi.

records.english: Have a seat; the meeting will begin shortly.
records.zomi: Tu in; kikhopna a kipan pah ding hi.

records.english: The visiting doctors were shown the new children's ward.
records.zomi: Hong veh siavuante in naupangte' ward thak kietsak hi.

records.english: We prepared a short slideshow to introduce the visitors to our work.
records.zomi: I nasep hong vehte kiangah theisak nadingin slideshow tom khat i bawl hi.

records.english: The new intern was so nervous on her first morning that she spilled coffee on the reception desk.
records.zomi: Intern thak a zingsang masa pen-in a lau lua ahih manin reception dawhkan tungah kawfi a sung hi.

records.english: The visitors' names were printed on cards and placed on the meeting table.
records.zomi: Khualte' min card tungah kisuaksak a, kikhopna dawhkan tungah kikoih hi.

records.english: Welcome to our open day, everyone — please help yourselves to coffee.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, i hon ni ah kidawn un — kawfi amau mah in la un.

records.english: Our class made a big banner to welcome the visiting choir from the city.
records.zomi: Khuapi pan hong veh la sa pawl muak nadingin i kilasi in lai lian khat a bawl hi.

records.english: New employees are welcomed with lunch with their team on their first day.
records.zomi: Nasem thakte a ni masa pen-in a pawl uh tawh sun an tawh kimuak hi.

records.english: Welcoming visitors well is part of every receptionist's job.
records.zomi: Khualte hoih taka muak pen reception nasem khempeuh' nasep ahi hi.

records.english: The visitors' bus broke down on the way, so the welcome ceremony started an hour late.
records.zomi: Khualte' bus lampi ah a siat ahih manin muakna poai nai khat nunin kipan hi.

records.english: We hung the visitors' national flag in the entrance hall to make them feel welcome.
records.zomi: Kidawn a kisak theih nadingun khualte' gam puanzan lutna khan ah i khai hi.

records.english: What time are the visitors from the head office arriving?
records.zomi: Office lian pan khualte nai bangzah ciangin a tung ding uh hiam?

records.english: Around ten, so we have time to prepare the room.
records.zomi: Nai sawm bang, tua ahih manin khan bawl nading hun i nei hi.

records.english: At our school, children aren't allowed into the staff room, even when visitors are waiting there.
records.zomi: I sang ah khualte a ngak lai zongin naupangte sayate' khan ah lut thei lo uh hi.

records.english: Who's meeting the inspectors at the gate?
records.zomi: Kongpi ah enkaktute kua in a dawn ding hiam?

records.english: The deputy head is, and I'll join them in the hall.
records.zomi: Sang makaipa laih in a dawn ding a, kei inn lian ah ka hong kihel ding hi.

records.english: Everyone visiting this factory must sign in at the gate and wear a safety helmet.
records.zomi: Hih factory hong veh khempeuh in kongpi ah min a suaksak ding uh a, lukhu hat a khu ding uh hi.

records.english: Kids, remember to say good morning to our visitors in the corridor.
records.zomi: Naupangte, lampi khan ah i khualte kiangah “Zingpha” ci ding phawk un.

records.english: When the inspectors arrived early, the whole school rushed to tidy up.
records.zomi: Enkaktute hun ma-in a tun uh ciangin sang bup a siangsak dingin a kinawh uh hi.

records.english: The welcome speech was written by a student and read out at the assembly.
records.zomi: Muakna thu pen sangnaupang khat in a gelh a, sang kikhopna ah kisim hi.

records.english: Ms. Lun will take your coats and show you to the conference room.
records.zomi: Ms. Lun in na coat uh a la ding a, kikhopna khan ah hong paipih ding hi.

records.english: Students from the village school were invited to spend a day at our college.
records.zomi: Khua sang pan sangnaupangte i college ah ni khat zang dingin kisam uh hi.

records.english: Could you show our visitors from the ministry around the science labs?
records.zomi: Ministry pan i khualte science lab te na etsak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Please don't photograph the machines; some of our designs are confidential.
records.zomi: Machine te lim la kei un; i bawl dan khenkhatte thuguk ahi hi.

records.english: "We're delighted to have you here," the director told the guests from the partner company.
records.zomi: “Hih ah hong om manun i lungdam mahmah hi,” ci-in director in kithuah company pan khualte kiangah a gen hi.

records.english: We hope you enjoyed your visit and will come back soon.
records.zomi: Na veh uh na nuam sa-in, manlang takin na hong pai kik ding uh i lamen hi.

records.english: Our new colleague's first day was planned so that she would meet every team.
records.zomi: I nasem lawm thak' ni masa pen pawl khempeuh a muh theih nadingin kigel hi.

records.english: Would you like a quick tour of the factory before the meeting starts?
records.zomi: Kikhopna a kipat ma-in factory sung tom takin kong etsak ding hiam?

records.english: The guest of honor was welcomed with music from the school band.
records.zomi: Zahtak khual pen sang la tumpawl in la tawh a muak hi.

records.english: The guests were so impressed by the students' performance that they stayed for lunch.
records.zomi: Khualte in sangnaupangte' lakna a lamdang sak lua uh ahih manin sun an dong a om uh hi.

records.english: Is the meeting room ready for the clients?
records.zomi: Kikhopna khan clients te adingin kibawl khin hiam?

records.english: Almost — the projector still needs to be set up.
records.zomi: Kibawl dek hi — projector kibawl nai lo hi.

records.english: Welcome to our school — the principal will be with you in just a moment.
records.zomi: I sang ah kidawn un — sang makaipa hun tawmno khit ciangin hong tung ding hi.

records.english: The parents' visit was canceled because of the storm.
records.zomi: Huihpi hang-in nu leh pate' veh ding kiphiat hi.

records.english: Mr. Pau led the visitors around the farm and answered all their questions.
records.zomi: Mr. Pau in khualte lo sung a paipih a, a dotna uh khempeuh a dawng hi.

records.english: The exchange students were greeted at the airport by their host families and two teachers.
records.zomi: Gamdang sangnaupang kilaihte vanlengtual ah a om sakna innkuante uh leh saya nih in a dawn uh hi.

records.english: May I take your bag?
records.zomi: Na ip kong la thei ding hiam?

records.english: Our principal greets every visitor in their own language if she can.
records.zomi: I sang makaipa in a theih leh hong veh khempeuh amau pau tawh a hopih hi.

records.english: How should we welcome the delegation from our sister school?
records.zomi: I sang sanggam pan hong pai pawl bangci-in i muak ding hiam?

records.english: The students could sing our school song and give each guest a small handmade gift.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte in i sang la a sa thei uh a, khual khat ciat letsong neu khut tawh kibawl a pia thei uh hi.

records.english: Can our guests join the staff for lunch in the canteen?
records.zomi: I khualte in canteen ah nasemte tawh sun an a ne khawm thei uh hiam?

records.english: Yes, there's a table reserved for them.
records.zomi: Thei uh hi, amaute adingin dawhkan khat kikoih tuam hi.

records.english: Our boss had the office cleaned and decorated before the investors arrived.
records.zomi: Sum khumte a tun ma-un i makaipa in office a siangsak a, a zeemsak hi.

records.english: Students, please stand and greet our guest speaker.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte, ding unla i thugen khual hopih un.

records.english: Please make sure the guests have water and a copy of the agenda.
records.zomi: Khualte in tui leh agenda khat ciat a ngah uh hiam kician takin en in.

records.english: The factory tour had to be shortened because one of the machines broke down.
records.zomi: Machine khat a siat ahih manin factory et dingte tom takin kibawl hi.

records.english: Taking the visitors to see our school garden was the highlight of their day.
records.zomi: I sang huan et dingin khualte i paipih pen a ni sung uh a nuam pen ahi hi.

records.english: Is it okay to give my teacher a small gift on the last day?
records.zomi: Ni nunung pen-in ka saya letsong neu khat ka pia leh a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, but something simple, like a card or flowers, is best.
records.zomi: Hoih hi, ahi zongin card hiam pak hiam bang a baih khat a hoih pen hi.

records.english: You can't leave yet — we haven't had cake!
records.zomi: Na pai thei nai kei hi — cake i ne nai kei hi!

records.english: When the exchange students left, the whole school came out to wave goodbye.
records.zomi: Gamdang sangnaupangte a pai ciangun sang bup in goodbye ci-in khut vaai dingin a pai khia uh hi.

records.english: The whole department stood and clapped when the old professor gave his last lecture.
records.zomi: Professor upa in a hilhna nunung pen a gen ciangin department bup a ding-in khut a beng uh hi.

records.english: Is it true that Ms. Grace is leaving at the end of the term?
records.zomi: Term tawp ciangin Ms. Grace a pai ding hi, cih a man hiam?

records.english: Yes, she's moving abroad to join her husband.
records.zomi: Man hi, a pasal kiang ah om dingin gamdang ah a pem ding hi.

records.english: Thank you for everything you've taught me.
records.zomi: Na hong hilh khempeuh adingin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: After the farewell assembly, the students walked their teacher to the bus stop.
records.zomi: Kikhenna kikhopna khit ciangin sangnaupangte in a saya uh bus khawlna dong a paipih uh hi.

records.english: Shall we take a group photo before everyone leaves?
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh a pai ma-un pawl lim khat i la ding hiam?

records.english: Leaving my first job was harder than I expected, because the team felt like family.
records.zomi: Pawl pen innkuan bang ahih manin ka nasep masa pen nusia pen ka lamen sangin a haksa zaw hi.

records.english: Departing staff may not take the school laptops home after their last day.
records.zomi: A paisan nasemte in a ni nunung uh khit ciangin sang laptop inn ah a puak thei kei ding uh hi.

records.english: Today is my last day at the company, and I want to thank everyone for these eight years.
records.zomi: Tuni company ah ka ni nunung pen ahi a, hih kum giat sung adingin mi khempeuh tungah lungdam ka ko nuam hi.

records.english: Good luck with your new job — they're lucky to have you.
records.zomi: Na nasep thak ah vangphatna om hen — nang na neih uh a vangphat uh hi.

records.english: Kids, give Mrs. Lun a big round of applause — today is her last day at our school.
records.zomi: Naupangte, Mrs. Lun adingin lian takin khut beng un — tuni i sang ah a ni nunung pen ahi hi.

records.english: Our school's much-loved bus driver retired after thirty-five years.
records.zomi: I sang' it mahmah bus tuansakpa kum sawmthum leh nga khit ciangin a khawl hi.

records.english: The farewell lunch was moved to the garden because the hall was too small.
records.zomi: Inn lian a neu lua ahih manin kikhenna sun an huan sungah kituah hi.

records.english: What are you planning for your final class with the seniors?
records.zomi: Sang tawp kumte tawh na kilasi nunung pen adingin bang na gel hiam?

records.english: I'll give each of them a short letter saying something I admire about them.
records.zomi: Amaute' tungah ka lamdang sak na khat gelh-in lai tom khat ciat ka pia ding hi.

records.english: The retirement party ended late, with stories and laughter from the old days.
records.zomi: Nasep khawlna pawi zan nun takin a tawp a, hun lui tangthu leh nuihna tawh a dim hi.

records.english: Please, no speeches — I'd rather just have lunch with you all.
records.zomi: Thugen om kei hen — note khempeuh tawh sun an ne khawm bek ka deih zaw hi.

records.english: We really do want you to be our guest at next year's graduation.
records.zomi: Kum hong ding sang zawhna poai ah i khual na hih ding i deih taktak hi.

records.english: We gave the retiring cleaner a watch and a card signed by every teacher.
records.zomi: Nasep khawl siangsak nu nai-ten khat leh saya khempeuh' min a kigelh card khat i pia hi.

records.english: My manager said, "The door is always open if you ever want to come back."
records.zomi: Ka manager in, “Na hong ciah kik nuam leh kongkhak kihong den hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: It was hard to leave, but I knew it was the right time.
records.zomi: Paisan a haksa hi, ahi zongin a hun takah ahi hi, ka thei hi.

records.english: The interns' last day ended with a small party in the office kitchen.
records.zomi: Intern te' ni nunung pen office anbuk sungah pawi neu khat tawh a tawp hi.

records.english: The old office was closed, and our team moved to the new building across town.
records.zomi: Office lui kikhak a, i pawl khuapi lam dang-a inn thak ah a pem hi.

records.english: Every graduate was handed a rose by the younger students.
records.zomi: Sang zawh khempeuh in naupang zawte' pan rose pak khat ciat a ngah uh hi.

records.english: Write your new address in the class book so that we can send you postcards.
records.zomi: Postcard kong khak theih nadingun kilasi laibu sungah na teenna thak gelh in.

records.english: The farewell party for our principal was organized by the parents' committee.
records.zomi: I sang makaipa adingin kikhenna pawi pen nu leh pate' committee in a vaihawm hi.

records.english: Don't leave without saying goodbye to the kitchen staff; they'll be hurt.
records.zomi: Anbuk nasemte kiangah goodbye ci lo-in pai kei in; a lungkham kha ding uh hi.

records.english: Tell everyone in the office that I'll miss them.
records.zomi: Office-a mi khempeuh ka ngaih ding hi, ci-in gen sak in.

records.english: Can I keep my desk until Friday, since I'm finishing a report?
records.zomi: Report khat ka zawh lai ahih manin Laithai ni dong ka dawhkan ka zang thei ding hiam?

records.english: That's fine — just leave your key with the secretary.
records.zomi: Hoih hi — na tawh secretary kiangah nusia bek in.

records.english: My best friend changed schools in the middle of the year, and I felt very lonely without her.
records.zomi: Ka lawm hoih pen kum kimlai-in sang a khel a, amah om lo-in ka kikhawmlum mahmah hi.

records.english: I'm sorry I won't be able to come to your leaving party.
records.zomi: Na paisan pawi ah ka hong pai thei lo ding ahih manin hong maisak in.

records.english: "Don't forget us when you're famous," my classmates joked as I left for art school.
records.zomi: Lim gelh sang ah ka pai ciangin, “Na min a than ciangin hong mangngilh kei in,” ci-in ka kilasi lawmte in hong nuihsat uh hi.

records.english: Will you keep in touch after graduation?
records.zomi: Sang zawhna khit ciangin na kizom den ding hiam?

records.english: Definitely — we'll meet every summer in the village.
records.zomi: Kizom den ding hi — khal simin khua ah i kimu ding hi.

records.english: We weren't told about the office closing until the last week.
records.zomi: Kal nunung dong office kikhak ding thu hong gen kei uh hi.

records.english: Who will tell jokes at our morning meetings now?
records.zomi: Tu-in i zingsang kikhopna ah kua in nuihza thu a gen ding hiam?

records.english: Saying goodbye to the students I'd taught since kindergarten broke my heart.
records.zomi: Kindergarten pan ka hilh sangnaupangte kiangah goodbye ka cih ciangin ka lungtang a kitam hi.

records.english: Our team made a photo book of all the projects we'd done together as a farewell gift.
records.zomi: I pawl in kikhenna letsong-in i sep khawm project khempeuh lim bu khat a bawl hi.

records.english: Our class wrote a song for our teacher, and we sang it on her last day.
records.zomi: I kilasi in i saya adingin la khat a phuah a, a ni nunung pen-in i sa hi.

records.english: Students must return their library books before they leave for the summer.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte in khal adingin a pai ma-un laibu inn laibute a lohsak kik ding uh hi.

records.english: Who's taking over your class after you leave?
records.zomi: Na paisan khit ciangin na kilasi kua in a la ding hiam?

records.english: A new teacher from the city, who starts next Monday.
records.zomi: Khuapi pan saya thak khat, Pizing ni hong ding ciangin a kipan ding hi.

records.english: The children's goodbye songs made the volunteers cry.
records.zomi: Naupangte' kikhenna la in thalawp nasemte a kapsak hi.

records.english: Our favorite teacher was transferred to another town, and the children cried.
records.zomi: I saya deih pen khua dang ah kisawn a, naupangte a kap uh hi.

records.english: The whole class signed a card for Mr. Thang before he retired.
records.zomi: Mr. Thang a khawl ma-in kilasi bup in card khat ah min a suaksak uh hi.

records.english: My contract ended in June, and I said goodbye to the hospital where I'd trained for three years.
records.zomi: June kha ciangin ka contract a bei a, kum thum sung ka kisinna zato kiangah goodbye ka ci hi.

records.english: Were you sad to leave your old job?
records.zomi: Na nasep lui na paisan ciangin na dah hiam?

records.english: A little, but I was ready for something new.
records.zomi: Tawmno, ahi zongin na thak khat adingin ka kiman khin hi.

records.english: My coworkers surprised me with a cake on my last day, and I couldn't stop smiling.
records.zomi: Ka ni nunung pen-in ka nasem lawmte in cake tawh hong lamdangsak uh a, ka nui tawp thei kei hi.

records.english: It's not goodbye — we'll see each other at the reunion next year.
records.zomi: Goodbye hi lo hi — kum hong ding kikhopna ah i kimu ding hi.

records.english: The factory workers held a dinner to say goodbye to their manager.
records.zomi: Factory nasemte in a manager uh kiangah goodbye cih nadingin nitak an khat a bawl uh hi.

records.english: I do want to say goodbye to every student before the holidays begin.
records.zomi: Tawlngakni a kipat ma-in sangnaupang khempeuh kiangah goodbye ka cih ding ka deih taktak hi.
