records.english: The graduating students threw their caps in the air as the ceremony ended.
records.zomi: Poai a tawp ciangin sang zawh sangnaupangte in a lukhu uh van lam ah a pai uh hi.

records.english: When I left the farm cooperative, the members gave me a basket of their best fruit.
records.zomi: Lo nei pawl ka paisan ciangin a mite in a singgah hoih pen bawm khat hong pia uh hi.

records.english: Please return your ID badge to the front desk on your way out.
records.zomi: Na pai khiat ciangin na ID badge mai dawhkan ah lohsak kik in.

records.english: Mom always says, "Your education is something nobody can take from you."
records.zomi: Nu in, “Na pilna pen kuamah in hong laksak thei lo na khat ahi hi,” a ci tawntung hi.

records.english: The twins were placed in different classes so that they could make their own friends.
records.zomi: Amau lawm a neih theih nadingun apengte kilasi tuam ciat ah kikoih uh hi.

records.english: You two need to stop arguing about whose turn it is to use the computer for homework.
records.zomi: Inn-a sep ding adingin computer zat kua' hun ahi hiam na kinial uh khawl kul uh hi.

records.english: The school was closed for a week, so the kids came to work with me.
records.zomi: Sang kal khat kikhak ahih manin naupangte ka nasepna ah hong zui uh hi.

records.english: Could you help your little sister with her spelling homework?
records.zomi: Na nau numei' lai gelh inn-a sep ding na huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Our son was given a part-time job at the bakery where his grandfather used to work.
records.zomi: I tapa in a pu' sepna moh bawlna inn ah hun kim lo nasep khat kipia hi.

records.english: "I want to be a doctor like Grandpa," my nephew told his class.
records.zomi: “Pu bangin siavuan suak ka deih hi,” ci-in ka tanau in a kilasi kiangah a gen hi.

records.english: Isn't it funny that every dinner conversation in our family ends up being about schools?
records.zomi: I innkuan nitak an kiho khempeuh sang thu-in a tawp den pen nuihza lo hiam?

records.english: I really do admire how my mother raised five children while working full-time.
records.zomi: Ka nu in hun kim-a na a sep laitakin ta nga a khak dan ka lamdang sa taktak hi.

records.english: My niece was so proud when her mother visited the school to talk about being a pilot.
records.zomi: A nu in pilot nasep thu gen dingin sang a veh ciangin ka tunu a kisaktheih mahmah hi.

records.english: Does Dad still keep every drawing his grandchildren bring home from school?
records.zomi: A tu-te in sang pan a hong puak lim-gelh khempeuh Pa in a kem lai hiam?

records.english: You all have a lot to live up to — your grandparents were both teachers.
records.zomi: Note khempeuh in na zuih ding tampi na nei uh hi — na pu leh na pi saya ahi uh hi.

records.english: My cousin and I are in the same class, so our teacher often mixes up our names.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam leh kei kilasi khat ah i om ahih manin i saya in i min a lam kha zel hi.

records.english: Are your husband's colleagues like a second family to him?
records.zomi: Na pasal' nasem lawmte a adingin innkuan nihna bang ahi uh hiam?

records.english: My grandparents are so proud that all their grandchildren finished school.
records.zomi: A tu-te khempeuh in sang a zawh uh ahih manin ka pu leh pite a kisaktheih mahmah uh hi.

records.english: The family farm needs everyone's help during the harvest, so the children miss a week of school.
records.zomi: Buh lak hun ah innkuan lo in mi khempeuh' huhna a kisam ahih manin naupangte in sang kal khat a mansuah uh hi.

records.english: My aunt and her daughter both graduated from university in the same year.
records.zomi: Ka ni leh a tanu kum khat mah-in sangpi a zo uh hi.

records.english: Our daughter's piano teacher is my wife's cousin.
records.zomi: I tanu' piano saya pen ka zi' sanggam ahi hi.

records.english: With my sister working in the same office, lunch breaks are much more fun.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu office khat mah ah na a sep manin sun an khawl hun a nuam zaw mahmah hi.

records.english: My sister was promoted to manager, and the whole family celebrated.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu manager-in kikaisang a, innkuan bup in poai i bawl hi.

records.english: Is it okay if Grandma picks the children up from school today?
records.zomi: Tuni-in Pi in naupangte sang pan a la leh a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: Sure — I'll let the teacher know.
records.zomi: Hoih hi — saya kiangah ka gen ding hi.

records.english: I do want my children to see how hard their parents work.
records.zomi: Ka tate in a nu leh pa uh bangzah hanciam takin na a sem uh hiam a muh ding uh ka deih taktak hi.

records.english: Our parents never went to university, but they made sure all of us did.
records.zomi: I nu leh pa in sangpi a kah ngei kei uh hi, ahi zongin i khempeuh i kah theih nadingin a hanciam uh hi.

records.english: Our son's teacher called to say how kind he had been to a new student.
records.zomi: I tapa in sangnaupang thak tung ah a hehpih dan i tapa' saya in hong sam-in a gen hi.

records.english: How do you balance work with caring for your family?
records.zomi: Na nasep leh na innkuan kepna bangci-in na kimkhai hiam?

records.english: My husband works mornings and I work evenings, so one of us is always home.
records.zomi: Ka pasal zingsangin a sem a, kei nitak ciangin ka sem ahih manin i lak pan khat inn ah a om den hi.

records.english: Can I walk my little brother to school this morning?
records.zomi: Tu zingsangin ka nau pasal sang ah ka paipih thei ding hiam?

records.english: My older brother helps me with my homework every evening after he finishes work.
records.zomi: Ka u pasal in a nasep a zawh khit ciangin nitak simin ka inn-a sep ding hong huh hi.

records.english: The children were picked up from school by their grandmother because both parents were working late.
records.zomi: Nu leh pa nih tengteng nai sau a sep uh ahih manin naupangte a pi uh in sang pan a la hi.

records.english: Are you related to the new math teacher?
records.zomi: Math saya thak tawh na kisai hiam?

records.english: Yes, she's my aunt, so I have to behave in her class!
records.zomi: Kisai hi, ka ni ahi a, a kilasi ah ka kizen kul hi!

records.english: Why does your brother work so many hours?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na sanggam pasal nai tampi na a sem hiam?

records.english: He's saving up to pay for our sister's university fees.
records.zomi: I sanggam nu' sangpi man piak nadingin sum a khol hi.

records.english: Is your brother still working abroad?
records.zomi: Na sanggam pasal gamdang ah na a sem lai hiam?

records.english: Yes, he sends money home every month for our parents.
records.zomi: Sem lai hi, kha simin i nu leh pa adingin inn ah sum a khak hi.

records.english: Do Dad and his three brothers all work at the same factory?
records.zomi: Pa leh a sanggam pasal thumte factory khat mah ah na a sem uh hiam?

records.english: Grandma taught at the village school for forty years, and half the town were her students.
records.zomi: Pi kum sawmli sung khua sang ah a hilh a, khua mi a kim in a sangnaupang ahi uh hi.

records.english: My sister's success at her company has inspired her younger brothers.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu' a company ah a zawhna in a nau pasalte a hanthawn hi.

records.english: Our family business has been passed down for three generations.
records.zomi: I innkuan sumbawlna suak thum sung kilui sawn hi.

records.english: Working with my husband in our shop has brought us closer, though we argue more.
records.zomi: I dawl ah ka pasal tawh na i sep khawm manin hong kinaisak zaw a, i kinial tam zaw napi.

records.english: My cousin's company hired me after he told them how hard I work.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam in bangzah ka hanciam hiam a gen khit ciangin a company in hong sap hi.

records.english: Who's coming to watch the school play tonight?
records.zomi: Tu zanin sang lawng kua in a en ding hiam?

records.english: The whole family, even Grandpa in his wheelchair.
records.zomi: Innkuan bup, a leeng tutna tawh Pu dong.

records.english: My uncle gave me my first job at his garage when I was sixteen.
records.zomi: Kum sawm leh guk ka phak lai-in ka pa neu in a mawtaw bawlna mun ah ka nasep masa pen hong pia hi.

records.english: Kids, show your father the science project you made at school.
records.zomi: Naupangte, sang ah na bawl science project na pa etsak un.

records.english: Working in the family shop taught me how to talk to customers.
records.zomi: Innkuan dawl ah na ka sep manin van leite tawh kiho dan ka sin hi.

records.english: My cousin and I applied for the same job, and luckily we were both hired.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam leh kei nasep kibang mah i ngen a, vangphatna takin i nih in kisam hi.

records.english: My brother-in-law teaches at my son's school, so my son can't get away with anything.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu' pasal ka tapa' sang ah a hilh ahih manin ka tapa in bangmah a guk-in a sem zo kei hi.

records.english: Did everyone in your family study at the village school?
records.zomi: Na innkuan sung mi khempeuh khua sang ah sang a kah uh hiam?

records.english: What did your parents do for a living?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa in nuntak nadingin bang na a sem uh hiam?

records.english: Dad was a carpenter, and Mom sold vegetables at the market.
records.zomi: Pa sing seempa ahi a, Nu zuakna mun ah anteh a zuak hi.

records.english: My aunt's company was sold, and she lost her job after twenty years.
records.zomi: Ka ni' company kizuak a, kum sawmnih khit ciangin a nasep a mansuah hi.

records.english: Since my wife started her new job, I've been doing most of the school runs.
records.zomi: Ka zi a nasep thak a kipat pan sang paipihna a tam zaw kei in ka sem hi.

records.english: Is it hard to have your parents as your teachers?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa na saya uh-a neih a haksa hiam?

records.english: A little — I can never pretend I forgot my homework.
records.zomi: Tawmno — ka inn-a sep ding ka mangngilh hi, ci-in ka kibawl thei ngei kei hi.

records.english: I'm proud of every one of you for working so hard this year.
records.zomi: Tu kum hanciam takin na sep manun note khat ciat tungah ka kisaktheih hi.

records.english: Our daughter's first school report was framed and hung in the living room.
records.zomi: I tanu' sang report masa pen bawngkhawng ah kikoih a, innsung khan ah kikhai hi.

records.english: It's strange to see my father in a suit, because at home he's always in his farm clothes.
records.zomi: Inn ah lo puan a silh tawntung ahih manin ka pa suit tawh muh a lamdang hi.

records.english: Kids, your grandfather helped build this school with his own hands, so treat it with respect.
records.zomi: Naupangte, na pu in amah' khut tawh hih sang a lam huh ahih manin zahtak takin kem un.

records.english: The parents were asked to help paint the classrooms during the holidays.
records.zomi: Tawlngakni sungin kilasi khante lim khai huh dingin nu leh pate kingen uh hi.

records.english: The children were enrolled in a weekend music class so that we could both work on Saturdays.
records.zomi: Kiginni ciangin i nih in na i sep theih nadingin naupangte kal tawp la kisinna ah i koih hi.

records.english: Every morning my husband and I take the train to work together, and it's our quiet time to talk.
records.zomi: Zingsang simin ka pasal leh kei nasep ah meileng khawm in i tuang a, i kiho nading hun dai ahi hi.

records.english: You all need to help more around the house now that I've started my night classes.
records.zomi: Zan sang ka kah kipan ahih manin note khempeuh in inn sung na huh tam zaw kul uh hi.

records.english: Can we afford private school for both girls?
records.zomi: Tanu nih tengteng private sang ah i khak zo ding hiam?

records.english: Not unless we both get raises this year.
records.zomi: Tu kum i nih in kha man a khan kei leh zo lo ding hi.

records.english: My husband and I run a small clinic together, and our kids grew up playing in the waiting room.
records.zomi: Ka pasal leh kei clinic neu khat khawm in i kem a, i tate ngakna khan ah mawl-in a khang uh hi.

records.english: My wife's promotion meant that I had to do more of the cooking, and I've become quite good at it.
records.zomi: Ka zi a kikaisan manin an huan a tam zaw kei in ka sem kul a, a siam mahmah ka suak hi.

records.english: Can you sign my permission slip for the school trip?
records.zomi: Sang khualzinna adingin ka phalna lai ah min na suaksak thei ding hiam?

records.english: We met at work, and the whole office came to our wedding.
records.zomi: Nasepna ah i kimu a, office bup i kiteenna ah hong pai uh hi.

records.english: The parents' meeting was postponed because the principal was ill.
records.zomi: Sang makaipa a dam loh manin nu leh pate' kikhopna kizekhia hi.

records.english: Please sign the reading log in her school bag before you leave for work.
records.zomi: Nasep na pai ma-in a sang ip sung-a lai sim gelhna ah min suaksak in.

records.english: What do you do when your child is sick and you have to work?
records.zomi: Na ta a dam lo a, nang na sep kul ciangin bang na sem hiam?

records.english: My mother-in-law usually comes over to look after him.
records.zomi: Ka sungnu in a kem dingin a hong pai zel hi.

records.english: Our son's grades improved after we limited his time on the computer.
records.zomi: Computer tung a hun zat i khaktan khit ciangin i tapa' ciamte a hoih zaw hi.

records.english: Combining a full-time job with raising two toddlers left me exhausted that first year.
records.zomi: Kum masa pen-in hun kim nasep leh naupang neu nih kepna in hong gimsak mahmah hi.

records.english: Kids, your mother has a big exam tomorrow, so please keep the noise down tonight.
records.zomi: Naupangte, zingciang na nu in sitna lian a nei ahih manin tu zanin dai takin om un.

records.english: After our first child was born, I went back to school to finish my degree.
records.zomi: I ta masa pen a suah khit ciangin ka degree zawh nadingin sang ah ka kah kik hi.

records.english: Should we send our son to the boarding school in the city?
records.zomi: I tapa khuapi-a giak-a kahna sang ah i khak ding hiam?

records.english: He's only twelve, so I'd rather keep him at home for a few more years.
records.zomi: Kum sawm leh nih bek a pha lai ahih manin kum tawmno inn ah kem ka deih zaw hi.

records.english: Text me rather than calling while I'm teaching, unless it's an emergency.
records.zomi: Ka hilh laitakin hong sam sangin hong text zaw in, haksatna hun hi lo leh.

records.english: We had a tutor come to the house twice a week to help our son with math.
records.zomi: I tapa' math huh nadingin kal khat sungin nihvei hilhpa khat inn ah hong pai hi.

records.english: My husband took three months of paternity leave when our daughter was born.
records.zomi: I tanu a suah ciangin ka pasal kha thum sung a nasep pan a khawl hi.

records.english: We've decided that one of us will always be home when the children come back from school.
records.zomi: Naupangte sang pan a ciah ciangun i lak pan khat inn ah om den ding i khensat hi.

records.english: Our son's school called because he'd forgotten his lunch, so I drove it over during my break.
records.zomi: I tapa in a sun an a mangngilh ahih manin a sang in hong sam a, ka khawl hun-in ka tawi hi.

records.english: I'm proud of both of you for working so hard this term.
records.zomi: Hih term sung hanciam takin na sep manun note nih tungah ka kisaktheih hi.

records.english: Does your daughter's teacher send you messages with photos of what the class is doing?
records.zomi: Na tanu' saya in kilasi in bang a sep uh hiam lim tawh message hong khak hiam?

records.english: Could you take the baby to the clinic while I'm at the meeting?
records.zomi: Kikhopna ah ka om laitakin naungek clinic ah na paipih thei ding hiam?

records.english: Ask your father to help you with the science project.
records.zomi: Science project adingin na pa kiangah hong huh dingin ngen in.

records.english: Our baby was born during my final exams, so I studied in the hospital waiting room.
records.zomi: Ka sitna nunungte laitakin i naungek a suak ahih manin zato ngakna khan ah ka kisin hi.

records.english: Our children grew up thinking that every family runs a restaurant.
records.zomi: I tate in innkuan khempeuh in an zuakna dawl a kem uh hi, ci-in a ngaihsun-in a khang uh hi.

records.english: My daughter wants to be a nurse like me, which makes me very proud.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in kei bangin nurse a suak nuam a, a kisaktheih huai mahmah hi.

records.english: The school asked parents to bring their children's old books for the library.
records.zomi: Laibu inn adingin naupangte' laibu luite tawi dingin sang in nu leh pate a ngen hi.

records.english: Will you show our son how to use the calculator for his homework?
records.zomi: I tapa' inn-a sep ding adingin calculator zat dan na etsak ding hiam?

records.english: Our baby cried every time I left for work, which broke my heart.
records.zomi: Nasep ka pai simin i naungek a kap a, ka lungtang a kitamsak hi.

records.english: Does your husband help the kids with their homework over a video call when he's working away?
records.zomi: Na pasal gamla ah na a sep ciangin video call tawh naupangte' inn-a sep ding a huh hiam?

records.english: We met at teacher training college, and now we teach at the same school.
records.zomi: Saya kisinna college ah i kimu a, tu-in sang khat mah ah i hilh hi.

records.english: We use a shared calendar on our phones to keep track of the children's activities.
records.zomi: Naupangte' sepnate i theih den nadingin i phone tungah calendar kihawm i zang hi.

records.english: Our daughter was so nervous on her first day of school that she held my hand until the bell rang.
records.zomi: I tanu' sang kah ni masa pen-in a lau lua ahih manin khawng a ging dong ka khut a len hi.

records.english: Who goes to the parent-teacher meetings in your family?
records.zomi: Na innkuan ah nu leh pa leh saya kikhopna ah kua in a pai zel hiam?

records.english: Usually my husband, because his office is closer to the school.
records.zomi: A tam zaw ka pasal, a office sang kiang ah a naih zawk manin.

records.english: We hired a nanny so that I could return to my job at the bank.
records.zomi: Bank-a ka nasep ah ka ciah kik theih nadingin naupang kemnu khat i sap hi.

records.english: Which school did you choose for your daughter?
records.zomi: Na tanu adingin sang bang na teel hiam?

records.english: The one near my office, so that I can pick her up on my way home.
records.zomi: Ka office kiang-a sang, inn ka ciah lam ah ka la theih nadingin.

records.english: Starting a business together tested our marriage, but we survived it.
records.zomi: Sumbawlna khawm-a i kipat in i kiteenna a sit a, ahi zongin i zo hi.

records.english: My husband said, "Your career matters as much as mine," when I was offered a job abroad.
records.zomi: Gamdang ah nasep hong kipiak ciangin ka pasal in, “Na nasep zong ka nasep bangmah in a thupi hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: Kids, put your homework on the table so that Dad can check it after dinner.
records.zomi: Naupangte, nitak an khit ciangin Pa in a en theih nadingin na inn-a sep ding dawhkan tungah koih un.

records.english: Did you finish your homework before you started playing?
records.zomi: Na mawl ma-in na inn-a sep ding na zo khin hiam?

records.english: I do want to be home in time to read to the kids, even on busy days.
records.zomi: Buai ni zongin naupangte adingin sim dingin hun takah inn ah tun ka deih taktak hi.

records.english: The teacher said, "Your son is clever, but he talks too much in class."
records.zomi: Saya in, “Na tapa a pil hi, ahi zongin kilasi ah a ho tam lua hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: Juggling work and parenting isn't easy, but it's worth it.
records.zomi: Nasep leh naupang khak kimkhai a baih kei hi, ahi zongin a manpha hi.

records.english: Working from home lets me see my children more, but it's hard to concentrate.
records.zomi: Inn pan nasep in ka tate a tam zawin hong mu sak a, ahi zongin lungsim koih a haksa hi.

records.english: Is it okay if I bring the baby to the office tomorrow?
records.zomi: Zingciang naungek office ah ka paipih leh a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: As long as she doesn't cry during the client meeting!
records.zomi: Client kikhopna laitakin a kap kei phial leh!

records.english: My boss lets me leave early on Fridays to collect my son from kindergarten.
records.zomi: Kindergarten pan ka tapa ka lak theih nadingin ka makaipa in Laithai ni simin hun ma-in hong paisak hi.

records.english: You two have to agree on one after-school activity each.
records.zomi: Note nih in sang khit nasep khat ciat ah na kilem kul uh hi.

records.english: The school play was so good that my husband filmed the whole thing on his phone.
records.zomi: Sang lawng a hoih lua ahih manin ka pasal in a phone tawh a bup in a la hi.

records.english: The kids' school fees take up almost half of my salary.
records.zomi: Naupangte' sang man in ka kha man a kim bang a zang hi.

records.english: Is it hard to work with your husband every day?
records.zomi: Na pasal tawh ni simin na sep khawm a haksa hiam?

records.english: Sometimes, but we have a rule never to discuss work at the dinner table.
records.zomi: Hun khenkhatah, ahi zongin nitak an dawhkan ah nasep thu kikum lo ding cih thukhun i nei hi.

records.english: Since I started working night shifts, my husband does the morning chores and I do the evening ones.
records.zomi: Zan nasep ka sep kipat pan ka pasal in zingsang inn nasep a sem a, kei in nitak lam ka sem hi.

records.english: You're old enough to pack your own school bag now.
records.zomi: Tu-in na sang ip nangma' thun thei dingin na khang khin hi.

records.english: If you're home first, please bring the washing in before it rains.
records.zomi: Na tung masa leh guah a zuk ma-in puan sawpte lak lut in.

records.english: When the school holidays start, the older children look after the house while we are at work.
records.zomi: Sang tawlngakni a kipat ciangin nasep ah i om laitakin naupang upa zawte in inn a kem uh hi.

records.english: Could you pick up some washing powder on your way home from work?
records.zomi: Nasep pan inn na ciah lam ah puan sawpna satpiang mal na lei thei ding hiam?

records.english: Can someone help me move my desk into the spare room so that I can work from home?
records.zomi: Inn pan ka sep theih nadingin ka dawhkan khan awng ah kuamah in hong pemsak huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: You'd better tidy your desk before your teacher comes for the home visit.
records.zomi: Na saya inn hong veh ma-in na dawhkan siangsak zaw in.

records.english: Don't leave your laptop charger on the kitchen floor where someone can trip over it.
records.zomi: Mi a khe kibetna ding anbuk lei ah na laptop charger nusia kei in.

records.english: Would you water the garden this week while I'm at the training course?
records.zomi: Kisinna ah ka om laitakin hih kal sungin huan tui na buak sak ding hiam?

records.english: Why should I make my bed if I'm getting back into it tonight?
records.zomi: Tu zanin ka lum kik ding a hih leh bang hangin ka lupna ka bawl ding hiam?

records.english: Because a tidy room makes it easier to find your homework in the morning.
records.zomi: Khan siang in zingsangin na inn-a sep ding zon a baihsak ahih manin.

records.english: My sister gets home from the hospital so tired that we never ask her to cook.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu zato pan a gim lua-in inn a tun ahih manin an huan dingin i ngen ngei kei hi.

records.english: Back when I was a student, I cleaned offices in the evening to pay my rent.
records.zomi: Sangnaupang ka hih lai-in ka inn man piak nadingin nitak ciangin office te ka siangsak hi.

records.english: The landlord said, "You can paint the walls, as long as you use a light color."
records.zomi: Inn neipa in, “Lim vom lo khat na zat leh bang na khai thei hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: Do teachers really expect students to clean their own classrooms?
records.zomi: Sayate in sangnaupangte in amau kilasi a siangsak ding uh a lamen taktak uh hiam?

records.english: At my school they did, and it taught us to keep the room tidy.
records.zomi: Ka sang ah a lamen uh a, khan siang taka kem hong hilh hi.

records.english: Students take turns washing the lunch pots in the school kitchen.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte in sang anbuk ah sun an beelte a kilaih-in a sil uh hi.

records.english: Children, hang up your school uniforms as soon as you get home.
records.zomi: Naupangte, inn na tun pah ciangun na sang puan uh khai un.

records.english: Clear your books off the dining table before I lay out the plates.
records.zomi: Kuang ka koih ma-in an nekna dawhkan tung pan na laibute la khia in.

records.english: Our chore chart changes every month to fit around everyone's work and school timetables.
records.zomi: I inn nasep kihawmna lai kha simin mi khempeuh' nasep leh sang hun tawh kilem dingin kikhel hi.

records.english: I left the cleaning to the end of the day, and by then I was too tired to start.
records.zomi: Siangsakna ni tawp ah ka nusia a, tua hun ciangin ka gim lua ahih manin ka kipan zo kei hi.

records.english: During the busy harvest weeks, the children help on the farm after school as well as at home.
records.zomi: Buh lak kal buaite sungin naupangte in sang khit ciangin inn bek hi lo-in lo ah zong a huh uh hi.

records.english: My daughter set up a reminder on the family tablet so that nobody forgets to feed the cat.
records.zomi: Kuamah in zawhngeu an piak a mangngilh loh nadingin ka tanu in innkuan tablet tungah phawkna a koih hi.

records.english: Polish your school shoes with the brush, not with your sock.
records.zomi: Na sang khedap na ngo tawh hi lo-in brush tawh nuai in.

records.english: Our daughter now does her own laundry since she moved into the university dormitory.
records.zomi: Sangpi giakna inn ah a pem pan i tanu in amah' puan amah mah in a sawp hi.

records.english: The night before school starts, we label all the children's new uniforms with a marker.
records.zomi: Sang a kipat zan ma-in naupangte' sang puan thak khempeuh tungah marker tawh min i gelh hi.

records.english: My son mended the broken chair leg with the glue and clamps he uses in woodwork class.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in sing seemna kilasi-a a zat glue leh clamp te tawh tutna khe kitat a bawl kik hi.

records.english: What's the hardest part of running a house while studying full-time?
records.zomi: Hun kim-a sang kah kawm inn kepna ah a haksa pen bang ahi hiam?

records.english: Finding time to cook proper meals instead of living on noodles.
records.zomi: An-ngum bek ne lo-in an kician huan nading hun zon.

records.english: Having shared a flat with five classmates, I know how quickly the dishes pile up.
records.zomi: Kilasi lawm nga tawh inn ka kihawm ngei ahih manin kuangte manlang takin a kituah dan ka thei hi.

records.english: Every evening after the shop closes, the whole family helps to mop the floor and count the money.
records.zomi: Nitak simin dawl a kikhak khit ciangin innkuan bup in lei nuai leh sum sim a huh uh hi.

records.english: May I use your sewing machine to fix the hem of my school skirt?
records.zomi: Ka sang puan khang a ki-at bawl nadingin na puan khuina machine ka zang thei ding hiam?

records.english: My wife and I write the week's chores on a whiteboard next to our work schedules.
records.zomi: Ka zi leh kei kal khat inn nasepte i nasep hun kiang-a whiteboard tungah i gelh hi.

records.english: Everyone, listen — the kitchen has to be spotless before Grandma's friends visit tomorrow.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, ngai un — zingciang Pi' lawmte hong veh ma-un anbuk a siang kim kul hi.

records.english: Grandpa sharpens the kitchen knives on a stone every Sunday after church.
records.zomi: Nipini pawlpi khit simin Pu in anbuk temte suang tungah a tat hi.

records.english: Can I finish my homework first and do the dishes afterward?
records.zomi: Ka inn-a sep ding ka zo masa inla a nung ciangin kuang ka sil thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, but they need to be done before you go to bed.
records.zomi: Thei hi, ahi zongin na lup ma-in kisil khin kul hi.

records.english: Our office has a cleaning rota, so each of us washes the mugs one week a month.
records.zomi: I office ah siangsak kilaihna a om ahih manin i khat ciat in kha khat sungin kal khat khuang i sil hi.

records.english: My manager lets me work from home on Mondays, which is when the plumber usually comes.
records.zomi: Ka manager in Pizing ni simin inn pan hong sepsak a, tua ni-in tui pipe bawlpa a hong pai zel hi.

records.english: Is it all right if I skip my chores tonight because I have a science test tomorrow?
records.zomi: Zingciang science sitna ka neih manin tu zanin ka inn nasep ka nusia leh a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: Just this once — your brother can cover for you.
records.zomi: Tu vei bek — na sanggam pasal in hong laih sak thei hi.

records.english: Our son swept the classroom without being asked, and his teacher sent a note home to tell us.
records.zomi: I tapa in a kingen lo-in kilasi a phiat a, a saya in hong gen dingin lai hong khak hi.

records.english: I do want to help with the housework, but my boss keeps me at the office until eight.
records.zomi: Inn nasep huh ka deih taktak hi, ahi zongin ka makaipa in nai giat dong office ah hong omsak hi.

records.english: The whole house gets cleaned on Saturday morning, since nobody has work or school.
records.zomi: Kuamah in nasep hiam sang hiam a neih loh manin Kiginni zingsangin inn bup kisiangsak hi.

records.english: Running a household is a job in itself, even if nobody pays you for it.
records.zomi: Kuamah in man hong piak kei zongin inn kepna pen amah mah in nasep khat ahi hi.

records.english: Our teacher gave us homework to help with one new chore at home and write about it.
records.zomi: I saya in inn ah nasep thak khat huh dingin leh tua thu gelh dingin inn-a sep ding hong pia hi.

records.english: Do you mind if I study at the kitchen table while you cook?
records.zomi: An na huan laitakin anbuk dawhkan ah ka kisin leh na lungkham ding hiam?

records.english: At our school, each class takes a week to sweep the yard and empty the bins.
records.zomi: I sang ah kilasi khat ciat in kal khat sung sang mai a phiat a, a nawhna bawm a suah uh hi.

records.english: We pay our teenage son a little for washing the car, and he's saving it for a bicycle.
records.zomi: I tapa khangno mawtaw a sil ciangin tawmno i pia a, siiksakol adingin a khol hi.

records.english: On weekdays we eat simple meals because both of us get home late from work.
records.zomi: I nih in nasep pan inn i tun nun manin ni sem ni-in an baih i ne hi.

records.english: Are you allowed to bring your dirty dishes back to the office kitchen?
records.zomi: Office anbuk ah na kuang nin lohsak kik thei hiam?

records.english: The house is always a mess during exam week because nobody has time to tidy.
records.zomi: Kuamah in siangsak hun a neih loh manin sitna kal sungin inn a buai tawntung hi.

records.english: Make sure the iron is unplugged before you leave for school.
records.zomi: Sang na pai ma-in meitut khau a kiphawh khin hiam kician takin en in.

records.english: Whoever comes home first starts the rice cooker.
records.zomi: Inn tung masa pen in rice cooker a hon ding hi.

records.english: Working from home means I can put a load of laundry on between meetings.
records.zomi: Inn pan na ka sep manin kikhopna kikal ah puan sawp ka koih thei hi.

records.english: Who irons your work shirts now that you live on your own?
records.zomi: Nangma' bek na om khit ciangin na nasep puante kua in a tut hiam?

records.english: Nobody — I buy the kind that doesn't need ironing.
records.zomi: Kuamah in — tut kisam lo nam ka lei hi.

records.english: When my wife got a job in the city, I learned to cook, clean, and braid our daughter's hair.
records.zomi: Ka zi khuapi ah nasep a ngah ciangin an huan, siangsak leh i tanu' sam phiat ka sin hi.

records.english: I really do try to keep the house tidy, but long working days make it hard.
records.zomi: Inn siang taka kem ka hanciam taktak hi, ahi zongin ni sau nasep in a haksasak hi.

records.english: Whenever my wife travels for work, the children and I eat far too much takeaway food.
records.zomi: Ka zi nasep adingin a khualzin simin naupangte leh kei an lei-ne tam lua i ne hi.

records.english: Can we talk about something other than school for once?
records.zomi: Vei khat bek sang thu hi lo thu dang i kikum thei ding hiam?

records.english: Would it be okay for me to discuss my salary with Dad before I accept the offer?
records.zomi: Ka san ma-in Pa tawh ka kha man thu ka kikum leh a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: The family agreed that my sister would finish her degree before getting married.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu in a kiteen ma-in a degree a zawh ding innkuan in a kilem uh hi.

records.english: My parents finally agreed to let me take a year off before college.
records.zomi: College ka kah ma-in kum khat ka khawl ding ka nu leh ka pa in a lungkim tawp uh hi.

records.english: We need to talk as a family about whether I should accept the job in the capital.
records.zomi: Gam khuapi lian-a nasep ka san ding hiam innkuan-in i kikum kul hi.

records.english: Before you decide, let's write down the advantages and disadvantages of each school.
records.zomi: Na khensat ma-in sang khat ciat' hoihna leh hoih lohna i gelh ni.

records.english: Children, nothing is decided yet, so please don't worry about changing schools.
records.zomi: Naupangte, bangmah kikhensat nai lo ahih manin sang khel ding thu lungkham kei un.

records.english: We used a calculator at the kitchen table to see whether we could afford the new school.
records.zomi: Sang thak i zo ding hiam en dingin anbuk dawhkan ah calculator i zang hi.

records.english: Kids, your mother and I have some good news about her new job.
records.zomi: Naupangte, na nu' nasep thak thu-ah na nu leh kei thu hoih i nei hi.

records.english: Let's keep this conversation calm so that your little brother doesn't get upset.
records.zomi: Na nau pasal a lungkham loh nadingin hih kikupna dai takin bawl ni.

records.english: Should I tell my parents that I've changed my major?
records.zomi: Ka laisim tuam ka khel thu ka nu leh ka pa kiangah ka gen ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, and the sooner the better, before they pay next term's fees.
records.zomi: Gen in, a manlang leh a hoih zaw hi, term zom man a piak ma-un.

records.english: All of you need to think about how the move would affect your schooling.
records.zomi: Pemna in na sang kahna bangci-in a hihsak ding hiam note khempeuh in na ngaihsun kul uh hi.

records.english: Our parents asked the teacher to join the conversation about whether I should repeat the year.
records.zomi: Kum khat ka kah kik ding hiam cih kikupna ah i nu leh pa in saya kihel dingin a ngen uh hi.

records.english: Explain to Grandma why you want to study nursing — she's worried about the night shifts.
records.zomi: Bang hangin nursing na sin nuam hiam Pi kiangah gen in — zan nasep thu a lungkham hi.

records.english: How will we pay for college if Dad's factory closes?
records.zomi: Pa' factory a kikhak leh college man bangci-in i pia ding hiam?

records.english: My husband and I disagreed about the job offer, so we asked my parents for advice.
records.zomi: Ka pasal leh kei nasep kipiak thu ah i kilem kei ahih manin ka nu leh ka pa kiangah thuhilhna i ngen hi.

records.english: The night my father lost his job, we talked for hours about what to cut back on.
records.zomi: Ka pa a nasep a mansuah zan-in bang i nusia ding hiam nai tampi i kikum hi.

records.english: My brother quit his job without telling anyone, and the news came out at Sunday lunch.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in kuamah gen lo-in a nasep a nusia a, Nipini sun an laitakin thu a kilang hi.

records.english: Don't make any promises to your boss until we've talked about it.
records.zomi: I kikup ma-in na makaipa kiangah bangmah kiciam kei in.

records.english: How should we tell the children that I'll be working in another city during the week?
records.zomi: Ni sem ni-in khuapi dang ah na ka sep ding thu naupangte kiangah bangci-in i gen ding hiam?

records.english: My brother announced that he'd been accepted to medical school, and Mom immediately called all her sisters.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in siavuan sang ah a kisang thu a gen a, Nu in a sanggam nute khempeuh a sam pah hi.

records.english: My sister cried when we said she couldn't take the job in the mines.
records.zomi: Suang tukna mun-a nasep a la thei kei ding hi, i cih ciangin ka sanggam nu a kap hi.

records.english: Everyone had a different opinion about whether Mom should go back to work.
records.zomi: Nu nasep ah a ciah kik ding hiam cih thu ah mi khempeuh in ngaihsutna tuam ciat a nei uh hi.

records.english: The question of who would run the family shop after Grandpa retired had been avoided for years.
records.zomi: Pu a khawl khit ciangin innkuan dawl kua in a kem ding hiam cih dotna kum tampi sung kipel hi.

records.english: Weighing up the move, we kept coming back to the question of the children's schools.
records.zomi: Pemna i ngaihsut laitakin naupangte' sang thu ah i ciah kik den hi.

records.english: Are you angry with me for wanting to leave the family business?
records.zomi: Innkuan sumbawlna nusia ka deih manin hong heh hiam?

records.english: Please listen to the end before you tell me it's a bad idea.
records.zomi: Ngaihsutna hoih lo ahi hi, na cih ma-in a tawp dong hong ngai in.

records.english: My sisters and I wrote our questions on slips of paper and put them in a jar for the family meeting.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nute leh kei innkuan kikhopna adingin i dotnate lai neute ah i gelh a, bel sungah i koih hi.

records.english: Can I join the school football team if my grades stay up?
records.zomi: Ka ciamte a hoih den leh sang football pawl ah ka kihel thei ding hiam?

records.english: Let's see your marks at the end of the term, and then we'll decide.
records.zomi: Term tawp ciangin na ciamte en ni, tua khit ciangin i khensat ding hi.

records.english: Your teacher called, and we'd like to talk about it after dinner.
records.zomi: Na saya hong sam a, nitak an khit ciangin tua thu i kikum nuam hi.

records.english: My parents were disappointed when I said I wanted to be a carpenter, but they listened.
records.zomi: Sing seempa suak ka deih ka cih ciangin ka nu leh ka pa a lungkia uh a, ahi zongin a ngai uh hi.

records.english: I'm telling you this now so that you won't hear it first from someone at school.
records.zomi: Sang ah kuamah pan na zak masa loh nadingin tu-in kong gen hi.

records.english: We sat down together to plan how the family could manage if I took a lower-paid job I'd actually enjoy.
records.zomi: Ka deih taktak sum tawm zaw nasep ka la leh innkuan in bangci-in i om zo ding hiam khawm-in i gel hi.

records.english: I really do think we should let her choose her own career.
records.zomi: Amah' nasep amah mah in a teel ding i phal ding hi, ka ci taktak hi.

records.english: We printed out the list of universities and circled the ones we could afford.
records.zomi: Sangpi list i suaksak a, i zawh theih te i kual hi.

records.english: What does everyone think about Dad working abroad for two years?
records.zomi: Pa gamdang ah kum nih na a sep ding thu mi khempeuh in bang na ngaihsun uh hiam?

records.english: My boss offered me a promotion, but I want to talk it over with my wife first.
records.zomi: Ka makaipa in kaisanna hong pia a, ahi zongin a masa-in ka zi tawh ka kikum nuam hi.

records.english: Mom opened a spreadsheet on the laptop to show us exactly where the school fees would come from.
records.zomi: Sang man koi pan hong pai ding hiam kician takin hong etsak dingin Nu in laptop tungah spreadsheet a hong hi.

records.english: When I said I wanted to teach in a village school, my parents were proud and worried at the same time.
records.zomi: Khua sang ah hilh ka deih ka cih ciangin ka nu leh ka pa kisaktheih leh lungkham kikhawm in a om uh hi.

records.english: I'm not angry about your grades; I just want to know what went wrong.
records.zomi: Na ciamte thu-ah ka heh kei hi; bang a khial hiam ka theih nuam bek hi.

records.english: If we all help with the farm, Joseph can stay in school until he finishes.
records.zomi: I khempeuh in lo i huh leh Joseph in a zawh dong sang a kah thei ding hi.

records.english: When my report card came home with two failing grades, Dad called a family meeting that same evening.
records.zomi: Ka report card ciamte nih tawh a tun ciangin Pa in tua nitak mahmah-in innkuan kikhopna a sam hi.

records.english: It took three family meetings before we agreed on which school my little sister should attend.
records.zomi: Ka nau numei' kah ding sang ah i kilem ma-in innkuan kikhopna vei thum a sau hi.

records.english: What would you study if money weren't a problem?
records.zomi: Sum buaina a om kei leh bang na sin ding hiam?

records.english: Music, though I know you'd rather I studied engineering.
records.zomi: La, ahi zongin engineering ka sin ding na deih zaw uh ka thei hi.

records.english: No one wants you to be unhappy at work, son.
records.zomi: Ka tapa, kuamah in nasepna ah na lungkham ding a deih kei uh hi.

records.english: Do you think I'm too old to go back to university?
records.zomi: Sangpi kah kik dingin ka upat lua in na ngaihsun hiam?

records.english: Not at all — Aunt Grace got her degree at fifty.
records.zomi: Upat lua lo hi — Ni Grace kum sawmnga ciangin a degree a ngah hi.

records.english: Why are you so set against my working at the restaurant on weekends?
records.zomi: Bang hangin kal tawp-in an zuakna dawl ah na ka sep na nial mahmah hiam?

records.english: Because your schoolwork comes first, and you already look tired.
records.zomi: Na sang sep ding a masa ding a, na gim khin bang na hih manin.

records.english: I'm grateful that my family talked my career choice through with me instead of deciding for me.
records.zomi: Ka innkuan in kei adingin khensat lo-in ka nasep teelna kei tawh a kikum manun ka lungdam hi.

records.english: Why didn't you tell us you were having trouble at work?
records.zomi: Nasepna ah buaina na neih bang hangin hong gen kei na hiam?

records.english: Is it all right if I go to my friend's house to study for the exam?
records.zomi: Sitna adingin kisin dingin ka lawm' inn ah ka pai leh a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: I do want to hear your reasons before I say no.
records.zomi: Ka nial ma-in na hang ka zak ka deih taktak hi.

records.english: Grandpa thinks a government job is the safest choice, but my sister wants to be a journalist.
records.zomi: Pu in kumpi nasep a bit pen hi, a ci a, ahi zongin ka sanggam nu in thuthak gelhpa suak a deih hi.

records.english: Our neighbor's daughter got a scholarship, and now my parents talk about nothing else.
records.zomi: I inn veng' tanu in scholarship a ngah a, tu-in ka nu leh ka pa in thu dang a gen nawn kei uh hi.

records.english: Every career my uncle suggested was one he had wanted for himself.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu' gen nasep khempeuh pen amah mah adinga a deih ngei ahi hi.

records.english: May I say something before you all make up your minds?
records.zomi: Na khempeuh in na khensat ma-un thu khat ka gen thei ding hiam?

records.english: It might be time to look for a day center where Grandma can spend the hours while we work.
records.zomi: I sep laitakin Pi a om theihna ni sung kemna mun khat zon hun ahi kha ding hi.

records.english: Let's ask the school if our son can take his medicine at lunch.
records.zomi: I tapa in sun an hun-in a zatui a ne thei ding hiam sang kiangah dong ni.

records.english: My grandfather asked if he could come to my graduation in his wheelchair.
records.zomi: Ka pu in a leeng tutna tawh ka sang zawhna poai ah a hong thei ding hiam hong dong hi.

records.english: My sister and I share Mom's hospital appointments according to our work schedules.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu leh kei i nasep hun tawh kizui-in Nu' zato pai nading ni i kihawm hi.

records.english: The teacher kept my daughter in the classroom until I arrived, even though school had finished an hour before.
records.zomi: Sang a khak khit nai khat a pha hangin ka tun dong saya in ka tanu kilasi sungah a koih hi.

records.english: May I leave work an hour early on Thursdays to take my father to his therapy?
records.zomi: Laizing ni simin ka pa a damna dingin ka paipih theih nadingin nai khat ma-in nasepna pan ka pai khia thei ding hiam?

records.english: We hired a student to sit with Grandpa in the afternoons while she studies for her exams.
records.zomi: Nitak simin Pu kiang ah a om ding sangnaupang khat i sap a, a sitna adingin a kisin kawm hi.

records.english: Children, Grandpa is going to walk you to school this week while Mom is away for work.
records.zomi: Naupangte, hih kal Nu nasep adingin a om lo sungin Pu in sang ah hong paipih ding hi.

records.english: When our son was diagnosed with asthma, his teacher learned how to use his inhaler.
records.zomi: I tapa in asthma a nei hi, ci-in a kitheih ciangin a saya in a inhaler zat dan a sin hi.

records.english: Working night shifts lets me be at home when my mother needs help during the day.
records.zomi: Zan nasep in ka nu in sun lam ah huhna a kisap ciangin inn ah hong omsak hi.

records.english: My wife teaches at the school next to her mother's house, so she visits her every lunchtime.
records.zomi: Ka zi in a nu' inn kiang sang ah a hilh ahih manin sun an hun simin a veh hi.

records.english: Our children go to an after-school club until six because neither of us can get home earlier.
records.zomi: I nih in hun ma-in inn i tun theih loh manin i tate nai guk dong sang khit pawl ah a om uh hi.

records.english: Students, please keep your voices down when you sing for the residents of the care home.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte, upate kemna inn-a omte adingin la na sak ciangun na aw uh niamsak un.

records.english: Why don't you ask your employer about flexible hours while your father is recovering?
records.zomi: Na pa a dam kik laitakin bang hangin na nasepna kiangah nasep hun kilai thei thu na dong kei hiam?

records.english: The caregiver my uncle hired showed us how to lift Grandma safely from her bed.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu' sap kemnu in Pi a lupna pan bitna taka a domkhiat dan hong etsak hi.

records.english: Who picks the children up from school when you're both at work?
records.zomi: Na nih in na na sep laitakin sang pan naupangte kua in a la hiam?

records.english: A neighbor collects them with her own kids, and we pay her a little each month.
records.zomi: Inn veng nu khat in amah' tate tawh a la a, kha simin tawmno i pia hi.

records.english: My sister and I take Mom to the hospital on different days of the week.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu leh kei kal khat sungin ni tuam ciat-in Nu zato ah i paipih hi.

records.english: Could you show me how the blood sugar meter works before you go back to the clinic?
records.zomi: Clinic ah na ciah kik ma-in sung khum tehna zat dan hong etsak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: All of you need to wash your hands before you visit the children's ward.
records.zomi: Naupangte' ward na veh ma-un note khempeuh in na khut uh na sil kul uh hi.

records.english: Would you mind if the kids did their homework in your waiting room until I finish my shift?
records.zomi: Ka nasep hun ka zawh dong na ngakna khan ah naupangte in inn-a sep ding a sem uh leh na lungkham ding hiam?

records.english: Can I bring my baby to the staff meeting if she stays quiet?
records.zomi: Ka naungek a dai den leh nasemte kikhopna ah ka paipih thei ding hiam?

records.english: Grandma looks after our toddler three days a week so that I can keep my job at the pharmacy.
records.zomi: Zatui dawl-a ka nasep ka kem theih nadingin kal khat sungin ni thum Pi in i naupang neu a kem hi.

records.english: How do you manage your job and your mother's care at the same time?
records.zomi: Na nasep leh na nu kepna hun khat mah-in bangci-in na sem zo hiam?

records.english: With a lot of help from my brothers and a very understanding boss.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasalte' huhna tampi leh thei siam mahmah makaipa khat tawh.

records.english: I do want to visit Dad every day, but the hospital is two hours from my office.
records.zomi: Ni simin Pa ka veh ka deih taktak hi, ahi zongin zato ka office pan nai nih a gamla hi.

records.english: Whose turn is it to stay home with the baby when she's too sick for nursery?
records.zomi: Naungek nursery ah a pai thei lo dong a dam loh ciangin kua' hun inn ah naungek tawh a om ding hiam?

records.english: Don't let Grandpa drive to the market while I'm at work.
records.zomi: Nasep ah ka om laitakin Pu zuakna mun ah mawtaw mawng sak kei in.

records.english: Teaching children with disabilities is demanding work, but my sister says she wouldn't do anything else.
records.zomi: Pilna lam ah haksatna nei naupangte hilh pen nasep haksa ahi hi, ahi zongin ka sanggam nu in nasep dang a sem lo ding hi, a ci hi.

records.english: If the babysitter can't come tomorrow, could you work from home?
records.zomi: Zingciang naupang kemnu a hong thei kei leh inn pan na sem thei ding hiam?

records.english: Dad could probably manage at home alone if someone checked on him at lunchtime.
records.zomi: Sun an hun-in kuamah in a en leh Pa amah bek inn ah a om zo kha ding hi.

records.english: My aunt trained as a nurse after years of caring for her own parents.
records.zomi: Kum tampi amah' nu leh pa a kem khit ciangin ka ni nurse dingin a kisin hi.

records.english: Please call me at the office if Grandma seems confused again.
records.zomi: Pi a lungsim a buai kik bang leh office ah hong sam in.

records.english: With the money from his part-time job, my nephew bought his grandmother a hearing aid.
records.zomi: Ka tanau in a hun kim lo nasep sum tawh a pi adingin bil zatna a lei hi.

records.english: Instead of hiring a nanny, we rearranged our work hours so that one of us is always with the baby.
records.zomi: Naupang kemnu sap sangin naungek kiang ah i lak pan khat a om den nadingin i nasep hun i bawl kik hi.

records.english: Kids, please be quiet in the mornings — your grandmother is a light sleeper.
records.zomi: Naupangte, zingsangin dai takin om un — na pi a ihmut a mang baih hi.

records.english: My son volunteers at the old people's home on Saturdays to earn hours for his school program.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in a sang program ading hun a ngah nadingin Kiginni simin upate inn ah thalawp takin na a sem hi.

records.english: You can count on us to look after the kids while you're at the conference.
records.zomi: Kikhopna lian ah na om laitakin naupangte i kem ding in hong muang thei hi.

records.english: Our daughter's kindergarten teacher noticed that she couldn't hear well and suggested a test.
records.zomi: I tanu' kindergarten saya in a za siang lo hi, a cih a, a sitna dingin a gen hi.

records.english: I left my job to care for my father, and I've never regretted it.
records.zomi: Ka pa kem dingin ka nasep ka nusia a, ka khasia ngei kei hi.

records.english: Are you allowed to take sick days when your child is ill?
records.zomi: Na ta a cina ciangin damlo ni na la thei hiam?

records.english: At my company we get five a year for family care.
records.zomi: Ka company ah innkuan kemna adingin kum khat-in ni nga i ngah hi.

records.english: We set up a camera in the living room so that I can check on Grandpa from the office.
records.zomi: Office pan Pu ka en theih nadingin innsung khan ah camera khat i koih hi.

records.english: Our office has a small nursery, which means I can feed the baby at lunchtime.
records.zomi: I office ah naupang kemna khan neu khat a om ahih manin sun an hun-in naungek nawi ka hawp thei hi.

records.english: Our son's teacher sends home a picture card so that we know what he ate and how he slept.
records.zomi: I tapa' saya in a nek leh a ihmut dan i theih theih nadingin lim card khat inn ah a khak hi.

records.english: My boss lets me answer when my mother calls during work.
records.zomi: Nasep laitakin ka nu in hong sam ciangin ka makaipa in hong dawngsak hi.

records.english: What would happen to the children if I got sick and couldn't work?
records.zomi: Ka dam lo a, na ka sem thei kei leh naupangte bang a hi ding uh hiam?

records.english: My manager said, "Family comes first — take the afternoon off and go to the hospital."
records.zomi: Ka manager in, “Innkuan a masa hi — nitak khawl inla zato ah pai in,” a ci hi.

records.english: My company gave me two weeks of carer's leave when my mother had her operation.
records.zomi: Ka nu' khamna laitakin ka company in kemna khawlna kal nih hong pia hi.

records.english: The school nurse called to say our son had a fever and needed to be picked up.
records.zomi: I tapa in lum a nei a, va la dingin sang nurse in hong sam hi.

records.english: Retired teachers in our village tutor the children whose parents work in the fields until dark.
records.zomi: I khua ah khawl saya luite in khua a mial dong lo ah na a sem nu leh pate' tate a hilh uh hi.

records.english: Is it possible for someone to read to Grandma while I'm at my job interview?
records.zomi: Nasep dotna ah ka om laitakin kuamah in Pi adingin a sim thei ding hiam?

records.english: Grandpa really does enjoy helping the children with their math homework.
records.zomi: Pu in naupangte' math inn-a sep ding huh a nuam sa taktak hi.

records.english: Can the school give our daughter extra time in exams because of her dyslexia?
records.zomi: I tanu in dyslexia a neih manin sitna ah sang in hun behlap a pia thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, but you'll need to bring a letter from her doctor.
records.zomi: Pia thei hi, ahi zongin a siavuan pan lai khat na tawi kul ding hi.

records.english: Each morning I sort Grandpa's pills into a weekly box before I leave for the bank.
records.zomi: Zingsang simin bank ah ka pai ma-in Pu' zatui mu kal khat bawm ah ka khen hi.

records.english: Could Grandpa's carer stay a little later on the days I have evening classes?
records.zomi: Nitak sang ka kah ni-in Pu' kemnu nai tawmno a om sau thei ding hiam?

records.english: Grandma helps the little ones with their reading after school while we're still at work.
records.zomi: Nasep ah i om lai-in sang khit ciangin Pi in naupang neute' lai sim a huh hi.

records.english: Grandpa may need a nurse at home once Mom goes back to work.
records.zomi: Nu nasep ah a ciah kik ciangin Pu in inn ah nurse khat a kisam kha ding hi.

records.english: Because Grandma taught school for forty years, she still corrects our grammar at dinner.
records.zomi: Pi kum sawmli sung sang ah a hilh ahih manin nitak an laitakin i pau zat dan a puahsak lai hi.

records.english: Factory workers on the morning shift have to clock in by six.
records.zomi: Zingsang nasep hun-a factory nasemte nai guk ma-in a tun uh kigelh kul hi.

records.english: Ironing my son's school shirt every morning, I wonder how he manages to get it so creased overnight.
records.zomi: Zingsang simin ka tapa' sang puan ka tut ciangin zan khat sungin bangci-in hih zah a kituap thei hiam ka lamdang sa hi.

records.english: Kids, put your lunch boxes in your school bags now so that nobody forgets them.
records.zomi: Naupangte, kuamah in a mangngilh loh nadingin na sun an bawm uh na sang ip sungah tu-in koih un.

records.english: Try to sleep a little longer — your interview isn't until the afternoon.
records.zomi: Tawmno ihmu sau zaw dingin hanciam in — na dotna nitak lam bek ahi hi.

records.english: Have you packed your swimming things for the school pool?
records.zomi: Sang tuidaipi adingin na kidiahna van na thun khin hiam?

records.english: I keep a spare shirt at the office in case I spill something on the way.
records.zomi: Lampi ah bangmah ka sung kha leh ci-in office ah puan behlap khat ka koih hi.

records.english: I check the train times on my phone while I'm still in bed.
records.zomi: Lupna tungah ka om lai-in ka phone tungah meileng hun ka en hi.

records.english: The school bus was late again, so half the class missed the first lesson.
records.zomi: Sang bus a nun kik ahih manin kilasi a kim in hilhna masa pen a mansuah uh hi.

records.english: My roommate gets up an hour before me so that she can study before her lectures.
records.zomi: Ka khan kihawm lawm in a hilhna ma-in a kisin theih nadingin kei sangin nai khat ma-in a thou hi.

records.english: I read through my presentation one last time while my coffee was brewing.
records.zomi: Ka kawfi a kihuan laitakin ka presentation vei nunung khat ka sim kik hi.

records.english: The farmers in our village are already in the fields before the children wake up for school.
records.zomi: Naupangte sang kah dingin a khanglo ma-un i khua lo neite lo ah a om khin uh hi.

records.english: My mother wakes me with a cup of hot ginger tea whenever I have an early exam.
records.zomi: Zingsang hun ma sitna ka neih simin ka nu in siing tea lum khuang khat tawh hong phongkhia hi.

records.english: I made my sister a quick breakfast so that she could sleep a little longer before her shift.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu in a nasep hun ma-in tawmno ihmu sau zaw thei dingin manlang takin zingsang an ka huan sak hi.

records.english: How do you get ready so fast?
records.zomi: Bangci-in manlang takin na kibawl hiam?

records.english: I shower at night, so all I have to do in the morning is get dressed.
records.zomi: Zanin ka kisil ahih manin zingsangin puan silh bek ka sem kul hi.

records.english: There's a chance the meeting will be moved, so check your email before you leave.
records.zomi: Kikhopna kituah kha ding ahih manin na pai ma-in na email en in.

records.english: Every morning, my husband makes a flask of tea for me to take to the market.
records.zomi: Zingsang simin ka pasal in zuakna mun ah ka tawi dingin tea bel khat hong bawl sak hi.

records.english: Our company runs a shuttle from the station, so I can sleep twenty minutes later.
records.zomi: I company in station pan mawtaw a paisak ahih manin minit sawmnih ka ihmu sau zaw thei hi.

records.english: Why do you always wake up so early when you don't have to be at work until nine?
records.zomi: Nai kua dong na sep kul kei hangin bang hangin manlang takin na thou tawntung hiam?

records.english: Because I like to walk for half an hour before the day starts.
records.zomi: Ni a kipat ma-in nai kim khat kaai ka deih ahih manin.

records.english: On exam mornings, my parents make sure I eat something even if I'm too nervous to be hungry.
records.zomi: Sitna zingsangin ka lau lua-in ka gilkial kei zongin ka nu leh ka pa in bangmah ka nek nadingin a en uh hi.

records.english: I prepare my lesson notes the night before, which gives me a calm start in the morning.
records.zomi: Ka hilh ding thu zan ma-in ka bawl ahih manin zingsangin dai takin ka kipan thei hi.

records.english: Waking a teenager for school is harder than any job I've ever had.
records.zomi: Khangno sang kah dingin phongkhiat pen ka sep ngei nasep khempeuh sangin a haksa zaw hi.

records.english: Did you remember to put your ID badge in your pocket?
records.zomi: Na ID badge na puan ip sungah koih dingin na phawk hiam?

records.english: In winter, the school allows students to wear jackets over their uniforms.
records.zomi: Khuavot hun ciangin sang in sangnaupangte a sang puan tungah jacket a silh uh a phal hi.

records.english: Can someone set a second alarm for me in case I sleep through the first?
records.zomi: A masa pen ka ihmut sak kha leh ci-in kuamah in alarm nihna khat hong koih sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Is it okay if I come in at ten tomorrow because of my dentist appointment?
records.zomi: Ka ha siavuan veh ding ka neih manin zingciang nai sawm ciangin ka hong tun leh a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: That's fine, as long as you're here for the eleven o'clock meeting.
records.zomi: Hoih hi, nai sawm leh khat kikhopna ah na om phial leh.

records.english: On the first day of the new job, I changed my shirt three times before I left the house.
records.zomi: Nasep thak ni masa pen-in inn ka paisan ma-in ka puan vei thum ka khel hi.

records.english: Don't wear perfume to the hospital, because some patients are sensitive to it.
records.zomi: Zato ah gim namtui zang kei in, damlo khenkhatte in a thuak zo kei uh hi.

records.english: What time do you have to leave the house to get to work on time?
records.zomi: Nasep ah hun takah na tun nadingin inn bang hun ciangin na paisan kul hiam?

records.english: Quarter to seven, or I miss the express bus.
records.zomi: Nai sagih tung minit sawmlinga, ahih kei leh bus manlang ka mansuah hi.

records.english: Every weekday, Grandpa walks my little sister to the school gate and waves until she's inside.
records.zomi: Ni sem ni simin Pu in ka nau numei sang kongpi dong a paipih a, a lut dong khut a vaai hi.

records.english: All of you, find your school shoes now, not when the bus is already outside.
records.zomi: Note khempeuh, bus polam ah a om khit ciangin hi lo-in tu-in na sang khedap uh zong un.

records.english: My neighbor drives my son to school on the days I start work early.
records.zomi: Ka nasep manlang taka ka kipat ni-in ka inn veng in ka tapa sang ah mawtaw tawh a paipih hi.

records.english: The doctors' changing room was full of people pulling on scrubs and checking their pagers.
records.zomi: Siavuante' puan lehna khan ah scrubs silh leh pager en mite a dim hi.

records.english: May I use the bathroom first today, since I have to catch the early train?
records.zomi: Meileng masa ka tuan kul ahih manin tuni-in ek inn ka zang masa thei ding hiam?

records.english: Before every shift, the bakery staff tie back their hair and put on hairnets.
records.zomi: Nasep hun khempeuh ma-in moh bawlna inn nasemte in a sam uh a khih uh a, sam khuhna a khu uh hi.

records.english: Can I wear sneakers to school today, since my black shoes are still wet?
records.zomi: Ka khedap vom a dip lai ahih manin tuni-in sang ah sneakers ka silh thei ding hiam?

records.english: My father used to wake us for school by playing the radio loudly in the hallway.
records.zomi: Ka pa in lampi khan ah ging sang takin radio a hon-in sang kah dingin hong phongkhia zel hi.

records.english: If the roads are icy, school might start an hour late.
records.zomi: Lampite tungah tuikhal a om leh sang nai khat nunin a kipan kha ding hi.

records.english: Would it help if I ironed your uniform tonight so you could sleep longer tomorrow?
records.zomi: Zingciang na ihmut sau zaw theih nadingin tu zanin na sang puan ka tut leh a huh ding hiam?

records.english: Students, you have five minutes to line up for morning assembly.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte, zingsang kikhopna adingin kizom dingin minit nga na nei uh hi.

records.english: Having worked nights for years, my aunt still struggles to sleep past five.
records.zomi: Kum tampi zan nasep a sep khit ciangin ka ni nai nga khit dong ihmu a haksa lai hi.

records.english: My daughter polished her shoes for her first day at work as carefully as she used to for school.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in nasep ni masa pen adingin sang kah lai-a a nuai bangmah-in pilvang takin a khedap a nuai hi.

records.english: The pilot checked the weather report on her tablet before leaving the hotel for the airport.
records.zomi: Pilot in vanlengtual pai dingin zinbuuk a paisan ma-in a tablet tungah khua thu a en hi.

records.english: You might want to leave earlier tomorrow, because the road to the office is being repaired.
records.zomi: Office lampi kibawl kik ahih manin zingciang manlang zawin na pai khiat nuam kha ding hi.

records.english: Could you check that my tie is straight before I go into the interview?
records.zomi: Dotna ah ka lut ma-in ka tie a dik hiam hong en sak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Please don't use all the hot water — I need to shower before work too.
records.zomi: Tui lum khempeuh zang kei in — kei zong nasep ma-in ka kisil kul hi.

records.english: Since I started working from home, I sometimes stay in my pajamas until lunch.
records.zomi: Inn pan na ka sep kipat pan hun khenkhatah sun dong ka ihmut puan tawh ka om hi.

records.english: If I hadn't overslept, I wouldn't have missed the start of my exam.
records.zomi: Ka ihmut sau lua kei leh ka sitna kipatna ka mansuah lo ding hi.

records.english: The construction workers pull on their steel-toed boots and helmets before climbing the scaffolding.
records.zomi: Lam lamte in sing sung kah ma-un khedap hat leh lukhu hat a silh uh hi.

records.english: My brother shaves with an electric razor in the car on his way to the office.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in office a pai lam ah mawtaw sungah electric razor tawh a khamul a meh hi.

records.english: On early-shift days, my alarm goes off at half past four.
records.zomi: Zingsang manlang nasep ni-in ka alarm nai li leh a kim ciangin a ging hi.

records.english: Our son brushes his teeth with the toothbrush his school gave out at the dental check.
records.zomi: I tapa in ha ennate ah a sang' piak ha nuaina tawh a ha a nuai hi.

records.english: We pray together at the breakfast table before the children leave for school and I leave for work.
records.zomi: Naupangte sang ah a pai ma-un leh kei nasep ka pai ma-in zingsang an dawhkan ah khawm in thu i ngen hi.

records.english: Could you braid your sister's hair while I pack the lunches?
records.zomi: Sun an ka thun laitakin na sanggam nu' sam na phiat sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Nurses on our ward arrive fifteen minutes before their shift to hear the night report.
records.zomi: I ward nurse te in zan report za dingin a nasep hun uh ma minit sawm leh nga-in a tung uh hi.

records.english: Lay your sports kit out tonight, since you'll be leaving before I wake up.
records.zomi: Ka khanglo ma-in na pai ding ahih manin tu zanin na kimawlna puan koih khin in.

records.english: Wake me at six if I sleep through the alarm, please — I have an exam.
records.zomi: Alarm ka ihmut sak kha leh nai guk ciangin hong phongkhia in — sitna ka nei hi.

records.english: My grandfather cooked for the miners for thirty years, and he still makes enough food for a crowd.
records.zomi: Ka pu kum sawmthum sung suang tukte adingin an a huan a, mi tampi vak zah an a huan lai hi.

records.english: My son packs an extra snack for a classmate who often comes to school hungry.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in gilkial tawh sang a kah zel kilasi lawm khat adingin nek ding behlap a thun hi.

records.english: My coworker shares her mother's spicy pickles with the whole office.
records.zomi: Ka nasem lawm in a nu' anteh thuk hai office bup tawh a kihawm hi.

records.english: The night before a big exam, my mother always cooks my favorite noodle soup.
records.zomi: Sitna lian zan ma-in ka nu in ka deih pen an-ngum an-tui a huan tawntung hi.

records.english: Kids, there's leftover rice in the fridge if you're hungry after school.
records.zomi: Naupangte, sang khit ciangin na gilkial uh leh khal bawm sungah buh taang a om hi.

records.english: Students, wash your hands at the sink before you touch any of the ingredients.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte, an bawlna van khatpeuh na khoih ma-un tui kiat mun ah na khut uh sil un.

records.english: I fill a thermos with hot soup so that my husband has something warm at the factory.
records.zomi: Ka pasal in factory ah a lum khat a neih theih nadingin thermos sungah an-tui lum ka khun hi.

records.english: Let me make you a sandwich to eat on the bus.
records.zomi: Bus tungah na nek dingin sandwich khat kong bawl sak ning.

records.english: After training as a chef, my brother realized he preferred cooking at home for his family.
records.zomi: An huanpa dingin a kisin khit ciangin ka sanggam pasal in a innkuan adingin inn-a an huan a deih zaw hi, a thei hi.

records.english: Can someone help me carry the food for the teachers' meeting?
records.zomi: Sayate' kikhopna adingin an puak kuamah in hong huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: On Sundays I cook a big pot of beans and rice so that I have lunches for the whole work week.
records.zomi: Nipini simin nasep kal bup sun an ka neih theih nadingin be leh buh beel lian khat ka huan hi.

records.english: During the harvest, lunch is carried out to the fields so that nobody has to stop working.
records.zomi: Buh lak hun ciangin kuamah in na a khawl loh nadingin sun an lo ah kipuak hi.

records.english: Lunch breaks at the factory are only thirty minutes, so most people bring food from home.
records.zomi: Factory ah sun an khawl hun minit sawmthum bek ahih manin mi tampi in inn pan an a tawi uh hi.

records.english: How do you find time to cook proper meals with a full-time job?
records.zomi: Hun kim nasep tawh an kician huan nading hun bangci-in na ngah hiam?

records.english: I chop all my vegetables on Sunday and keep them in boxes in the fridge.
records.zomi: Nipini ciangin ka anteh khempeuh ka tan a, khal bawm sung bawmte ah ka koih hi.

records.english: Could you show the new cook where we keep the big pots?
records.zomi: An huanpa thak beel lian i koihna na etsak thei ding hiam?

records.english: May I bring homemade cookies to class for my birthday, or do they have to be from a shop?
records.zomi: Ka pianni adingin inn-a bawl cookie kilasi ah ka tawi thei ding hiam, dawl pan a hi kul hiam?

records.english: Working in a hotel kitchen taught me to chop onions faster than I ever thought possible.
records.zomi: Zinbuuk anbuk ah na ka sep manin ka ngaihsut sangin manlang zawin lothaang tan ka siam hi.

records.english: Our class raised money for the trip by selling homemade cakes at lunchtime.
records.zomi: Sun an hun-in inn-a bawl cake zuak-in i kilasi in khualzinna adingin sum a kaikhawm hi.

records.english: Do you mind if I bring fish for lunch, or will the smell bother you?
records.zomi: Sun an adingin nga ka tawi leh na lungkham ding hiam, a gim in hong buaisak ding hiam?

records.english: Our team takes a cake to the office whenever someone has a birthday.
records.zomi: Kuamah' pianni ciangin i pawl in office ah cake a tawi zel hi.

records.english: The bread rolls for the school breakfast are baked every night by volunteers from the church.
records.zomi: Sang zingsang an ading moh neute pen pawlpi pan thalawp nasemte in zan simin a bawl uh hi.

records.english: Why does the school serve the same meal every Monday?
records.zomi: Bang hangin sang in Pizing ni simin an kibang mah a pia hiam?

records.english: Probably because it's cheap and most of the children like it.
records.zomi: A man neu a, naupang tampi in a deih uh ahih man kha ding hi.

records.english: No one is allowed in the restaurant kitchen without a hairnet and clean shoes.
records.zomi: Sam khuhna leh khedap siang om lo-in kuamah an zuakna dawl anbuk ah lut thei lo hi.

records.english: Could you cook something simple for the children tonight, since I'll be at the office late?
records.zomi: Office ah nai sau ka om ding ahih manin tu zanin naupangte adingin an baih khat na huan thei ding hiam?

records.english: My aunt sells fried snacks outside the school gate to pay for her children's fees.
records.zomi: Ka ni in a tate' sang man piak nadingin sang kongpi polam ah nek ding kikang a zuak hi.

records.english: The canteen ran out of food before the last class arrived, so we bought bread from the shop.
records.zomi: Kilasi nunung a tun ma-in canteen ah an a bei ahih manin dawl pan moh i lei hi.

records.english: Is it safe to reheat rice that was cooked yesterday?
records.zomi: Zanni-a kihuan buh lumsak kik a bitna hiam?

records.english: Our teacher said it's fine if you kept it in the fridge and heat it until it's very hot.
records.zomi: Khal bawm sungah na koih a, a sa mahmah dong na lumsak leh a hoih hi, ci-in i saya in a gen hi.

records.english: Should I cook for the staff dinner, or would it be easier to order from a restaurant?
records.zomi: Nasemte nitak an adingin ka huan ding hiam, an zuakna dawl pan sap a baih zaw ding hiam?

records.english: Mind the oil — it's spitting.
records.zomi: Sathau pilvang in — a kithei hi.

records.english: Who cooks for the workers on the building site?
records.zomi: Inn lamna mun-a nasemte adingin kua in an a huan hiam?

records.english: Two women from the village make a big pot of curry there every morning.
records.zomi: Khua pan numei nih in zingsang simin tua ah curry beel lian khat a huan uh hi.

records.english: If you study food science, you might end up developing recipes for a big company.
records.zomi: An thu pilna na sin leh company lian khat adingin an huan dan thak na bawl kha ding hi.

records.english: The parents cooked the meal for the school's sports day, and everything was eaten by noon.
records.zomi: Sang kimawl ni adingin nu leh pate in an a huan uh a, sun ma-in khempeuh kine khin hi.

records.english: When I lived in the student dormitory, I learned to cook almost anything in a single pan.
records.zomi: Sangpi giakna inn ah ka om lai-in beel khat bek tawh na khempeuh huan ka sin hi.

records.english: In our cooking class, we learned how to make bread from flour, water, yeast and salt.
records.zomi: I an huan kisinna ah buh-mal, tui, yeast leh cii tawh moh bawl dan i sin hi.

records.english: Using a rice cooker with a timer means dinner is ready when I get home from work.
records.zomi: Hun kikoih thei rice cooker zat in nasep pan inn ka tun ciangin nitak an kiman khin hi.

records.english: Our office has a rule that whoever finishes the coffee makes a fresh pot.
records.zomi: I office ah kawfi a beisak pa in a thak a bawl ding, cih thukhun a om hi.

records.english: When the head cook fell ill, the students served lunch for the whole school themselves.
records.zomi: An huanpa makai a dam loh ciangin sangnaupangte mah in sang bup sun an a pia uh hi.

records.english: If the dining hall is closed tomorrow, we might have to bring our own lunch.
records.zomi: Zingciang an nekna inn a kikhak leh eimah sun an i tawi kul kha ding hi.

records.english: Since starting night shifts, my husband eats his dinner at breakfast time.
records.zomi: Zan nasep a sep kipat pan ka pasal in zingsang an hun-in a nitak an a ne hi.

records.english: Unlike my office job, cooking for a restaurant is physically exhausting.
records.zomi: Ka office nasep tawh kibang lo-in an zuakna dawl adingin an huan pen pumpi gimna mahmah ahi hi.

records.english: Mom wraps my sandwiches in a cloth so that they stay fresh until lunch.
records.zomi: Sun an dong a thak den nadingin Nu in ka sandwich puan tawh a tuam hi.

records.english: Our school garden grows the tomatoes and beans that end up in the canteen.
records.zomi: I sang huan in canteen ah a tun khamtung leh be a suan hi.

records.english: Not until I started working in a restaurant did I appreciate how hard my mother worked in our kitchen.
records.zomi: An zuakna dawl ah na ka sep kipat dong ka nu i anbuk ah bangzah hanciam takin na a sem hiam ka thei kei hi.

records.english: My daughter came home from her first cooking lesson and made us an omelet for dinner.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in a an huan kisinna masa pen pan inn a tun ciangin nitak an-in omelet hong bawl sak hi.

records.english: At the hotel where I work, kitchen staff aren't allowed to wear rings or watches while preparing food.
records.zomi: Ka sepna zinbuuk ah anbuk nasemte in an a bawl laitakin khut-zungbuh hiam nai-ten hiam a bulh thei kei uh hi.

records.english: The cook at our school weighs every portion with a kitchen scale so that each child gets the same amount.
records.zomi: I sang an huanpa in naupang khempeuh in a kibang zah a ngah theih nadingin a tan khempeuh bukna tawh a buk hi.

records.english: You must not use the same chopping board for raw meat and cooked food.
records.zomi: Sa hing leh an kihuan khin adingin sing phek khat mah na zang kei ding hi.

records.english: What do they serve in the school canteen?
records.zomi: Sang canteen ah bang a pia uh hiam?

records.english: Mostly rice and vegetables, with chicken on Fridays.
records.zomi: A tam zaw buh leh anteh, Laithai ni ciangin aksa tawh.

records.english: Don't leave your lunch in the office fridge over the weekend, or it will be thrown out.
records.zomi: Kal tawp sung office khal bawm sungah na sun an nusia kei in, kipai ding hi.

records.english: There's a small fridge in the staff room, but it's always full by nine.
records.zomi: Nasemte' khan ah khal bawm neu khat a om a, ahi zongin nai kua ciangin a dim tawntung hi.

records.english: Because I work at a bakery, our house always smells of bread on Saturday mornings.
records.zomi: Moh bawlna inn ah na ka sep manin Kiginni zingsang simin i inn moh gim a nam tawntung hi.

records.english: We hired a caterer for the office party so that nobody had to cook.
records.zomi: Kuamah in an a huan kul loh nadingin office pawi adingin an bawlpa khat i sap hi.

records.english: Can I heat my soup in the office microwave, or is it only for staff?
records.zomi: Office microwave ah ka an-tui ka lumsak thei ding hiam, nasemte ading bek hiam?

records.english: Would it be possible to order vegetarian meals for the conference?
records.zomi: Kikhopna lian adingin sa om lo an sap theih ding hiam?

records.english: Please don't eat at your desk, because crumbs attract ants into the office.
records.zomi: Moh nen in office ah sihte a sam ahih manin na dawhkan ah an ne kei in.

records.english: During the move to the new building, several boxes of files went missing.
records.zomi: Inn thak ah i pem laitakin file bawm tawmno a mang hi.

records.english: There may not be room for all your books in the new apartment.
records.zomi: Inn thak ah na laibu khempeuh adingin mun a cing kei kha ding hi.

records.english: Why are there three broken printers in the corner of the meeting room?
records.zomi: Bang hangin kikhopna khan ki-ngawi mun ah printer siat thum a om hiam?

records.english: Is it all right if I move these boxes to make room for my desk?
records.zomi: Ka dawhkan mun a om theih nadingin hih bawmte ka pemsak leh a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: My father keeps every one of his tools in the same place he's kept them for forty years.
records.zomi: Ka pa in a nasep vante khempeuh kum sawmli sung a koihna mun mah ah a koih hi.

records.english: My locker at work is so small that I keep my spare uniform folded in a plastic bag.
records.zomi: Nasepna-a ka locker a neu lua ahih manin ka puan behlap plastic ip sungah ka khiat-in ka koih hi.

records.english: The electricity went off in the middle of the office clean-up, so we finished by candlelight.
records.zomi: Office siangsakna kimlai-in meivak a kitan ahih manin khawimeivaak tawh i zo hi.

records.english: I could organize your bookshelf for you while you're at work, if you'd like.
records.zomi: Na deih leh nasep ah na om laitakin na laibu koihna kong bawl sak thei hi.

records.english: May I stay after class to help tidy the art cupboard?
records.zomi: Lim gelh van koihna bawm siangsak huh dingin kilasi khit ciangin ka om thei ding hiam?

records.english: The school library was reorganized over the summer, and now the books are much easier to find.
records.zomi: Khal sungin sang laibu inn kibawl kik a, tu-in laibute muh a baih zaw mahmah hi.

records.english: Our office has a clean-desk rule, so everything has to be put away before we go home.
records.zomi: I office ah dawhkan siang thukhun a om ahih manin inn i ciah ma-in na khempeuh kikoih khin kul hi.

records.english: Food and drinks aren't allowed in the computer lab at our school.
