records.zomi: Ka ni in hilh kawm-in a cancer damna adingin kha simin khuapi ah a pai hi.

records.english: You can't take the school's cameras on the trip unless you sign them out first.
records.zomi: A masa-in na min na gelh kei leh sang camera te khualzinna ah na tawi thei kei hi.

records.english: Which city is the training course in this year?
records.zomi: Tu kum kisinna khuapi bang ah om hiam?

records.english: What surprised you most about the city when you went there to study?
records.zomi: Sang kah dingin khuapi ah na pai ciangin bang in hong lamdangsak pen hiam?

records.english: How fast everyone walked, as if they were all late for something.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh a nun uh bangin manlang takin a kaai uh hi.

records.english: The bus carrying the choir broke down on the highway, and they arrived just in time to sing.
records.zomi: La sa pawl puak bus lam lianpi tungah a sia a, la sak dingin a hun takah a tung uh hi.

records.english: Can I bring my wife on the business trip if I pay for her ticket myself?
records.zomi: Ka zi' ticket man kei mah in ka piak leh sumbawlna khualzinna ah ka paipih thei ding hiam?

records.english: Make sure you have the address of the hostel written down, in case your phone dies.
records.zomi: Na phone a bei kha leh ci-in hostel teenna na gelh kician hiam en in.

records.english: The trip was postponed when the teachers' strike was announced.
records.zomi: Sayate kikhawlna thu a kizak ciangin khualzinna kizekhia hi.

records.english: Who will look after the shop while you're at the trade fair?
records.zomi: Sumbawlna poai ah na om laitakin dawl kua in a kem ding hiam?

records.english: My nephew, as long as I call him every evening.
records.zomi: Ka tanau, nitak simin ka sam phial leh.

records.english: My husband's company pays for his flights home.
records.zomi: Ka pasal' company in inn a ciahna vanleng man a pia hi.

records.english: Our football team took the bus to the city for a big match.
records.zomi: I football pawl in kimawlna lian adingin khuapi ah bus a tuang hi.

records.english: Is the conference hotel within walking distance of the station?
records.zomi: Kikhopna zinbuuk station pan kaai theih zah a naih hiam?

records.english: When we reached the city, the hotel had no record of our booking for the conference.
records.zomi: Khuapi i tun ciangin zinbuuk in kikhopna adingin i bawl thu a theih kei hi.

records.english: My manager said, "Take the morning off when you get back; you'll be exhausted."
records.zomi: Ka manager in, “Na ciah kik ciangin zingsang khawl in; na gim mahmah ding hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: My suitcase was lost on the way to the conference, so I bought a shirt at the airport.
records.zomi: Kikhopna lian ka pai lam ah ka van bawm a mang ahih manin vanlengtual ah puan khat ka lei hi.

records.english: Do teachers get paid extra for taking students on trips to other cities?
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte khuapi dang ah a paipih ciangun sayate sum behlap a ngah uh hiam?

records.english: Not at our school, but they get a day off afterward.
records.zomi: I sang ah ngah kei uh hi, ahi zongin a nung ciangin ni khat khawl a ngah uh hi.

records.english: Don't leave your laptop on the train seat, even for a minute.
records.zomi: Minit khat bek hi zongin meileng tutna tungah na laptop nusia kei in.

records.english: My first train journey alone was to the city for a job interview, and I've never forgotten it.
records.zomi: Ka meileng khualzinna masa pen amah bek-a pai pen nasep dotna adingin khuapi ah ahi a, ka mangngilh ngei kei hi.

records.english: I've never been to the capital, but I'll go there next year for nursing college.
records.zomi: Gam khuapi lian ah ka pai ngei kei hi, ahi zongin kum hong ding ciangin nursing college adingin ka pai ding hi.

records.english: How are you getting to the conference in the city?
records.zomi: Khuapi-a kikhopna lian ah bangci-in na pai ding hiam?

records.english: By the night train, so that I can sleep on the way and go straight to the first session.
records.zomi: Zan meileng tawh, lampi ah ka ihmut theih a, kikhopna masa pen ah pahtakin ka pai theih nadingin.

records.english: Going to the city for the job fair was the first time my brother had ever taken a plane.
records.zomi: Nasep poai adingin khuapi ah a pai pen ka sanggam pasal vanleng a tuan masa pen ahi hi.

records.english: Should I wear my uniform on the plane or change when I arrive?
records.zomi: Vanleng tungah ka nasep puan ka silh ding hiam, ka tun ciangin ka lai ding hiam?

records.english: Traveling for work every week has made it hard to watch my children grow up.
records.zomi: Nasep adingin kal simin khualzin in ka tate a khanna muh a haksasak hi.

records.english: There's a chance the meeting will be moved online, which would save me a long trip.
records.zomi: Kikhopna online ah kituah kha ding a, tua in khualzinna sau hong khol sak ding hi.

records.english: Kids, your dad is flying to another city for work, so let's make him a card for his trip.
records.zomi: Naupangte, na pa nasep adingin khuapi dang ah vanleng tawh a pai ding ahih manin a khualzinna adingin card khat bawl sak ni.

records.english: Why does everyone in our office have to take the early flight?
records.zomi: Bang hangin i office-a mi khempeuh in zingsang manlang vanleng a tuan kul uh hiam?

records.english: Each group of students got a map of the city and a list of places to find.
records.zomi: Sangnaupang pawl khat ciat in khuapi map khat leh zon ding mun list khat a ngah uh hi.

records.english: My grandmother cried when I left for the city to start my apprenticeship.
records.zomi: Nasep kisin kipat dingin khuapi ah ka pai ciangin ka pi a kap hi.

records.english: After two years of working in the city, my cousin finally came home for the harvest.
records.zomi: Khuapi ah kum nih na a sep khit ciangin ka sanggam buh lak adingin inn ah a ciah tawp hi.

records.english: My boss told me, "Keep every receipt from the trip, or the company won't pay you back."
records.zomi: Ka makaipa in, “Khualzinna pan receipt khempeuh kem in, ahih kei leh company in hong lohsak kik lo ding hi,” hong ci hi.

records.english: Leaving the children for a week to attend a workshop in the capital was harder than I expected.
records.zomi: Gam khuapi lian-a workshop ah kihel dingin kal khat naupangte nusia ka lamen sangin a haksa zaw hi.

records.english: The mountain road was closed by a landslide, so the school group spent the night in a village.
records.zomi: Mual lampi leiminpuk in a khak ahih manin sang pawl khua khat ah a giak uh hi.

records.english: The farmers' group went to the city to learn about new ways of growing rice.
records.zomi: Lo nei pawl in buh suan dan thak sin dingin khuapi ah a pai uh hi.

records.english: However expensive it was to send me to school in the city, my parents never once complained.
records.zomi: Khuapi sang ah hong khak man bangzah a tam zongin ka nu leh ka pa in vei khat zong a phunsan kei uh hi.

records.english: Everyone, wear your school jackets so that we can find each other in the crowd.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, mi tam lak ah i kimuh theih nadingin na sang jacket uh silh un.

records.english: Taking the overnight bus to save money, I arrived at the interview tired but on time.
records.zomi: Sum khol dingin zan bus ka tuan ahih manin dotna ah ka gim napi hun takah ka tung hi.

records.english: Can you book me a hotel close to the client's office?
records.zomi: Client' office kiang ah zinbuuk khat hong bawl sak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: We really do want to see the national museum while we're in the city for the school trip.
records.zomi: Sang khualzinna adingin khuapi ah i om laitakin gam museum i muh ding i deih taktak hi.

records.english: Does Mr. Hau still sell farm machines in other cities?
records.zomi: Mr. Hau in khuapi dangte ah lo sepna machine a zuak lai hiam?

records.english: We were shown around the factory in the city by the manager himself.
records.zomi: Khuapi-a factory sung manager mah in hong etsak hi.

records.english: My company is sending me to the capital for a three-day training course next month.
records.zomi: Ka company in kha hong ding ciangin ni thum kisinna adingin gam khuapi lian ah hong sawl ding hi.

records.english: How much do they give you for meals when you travel for work?
records.zomi: Nasep adingin na khualzin ciangin an man bangzah hong pia uh hiam?

records.english: The night before the university entrance exam, my father and I stayed in a cheap guesthouse near the exam center.
records.zomi: Sangpi lutna sitna zan ma-in ka pa leh kei sitna mun kiang-a zinbuuk neu man neu khat ah i giak hi.

records.english: Phones aren't allowed in the exam hall, so leave yours at the hotel.
records.zomi: Sitna inn ah phone kiphal lo ahih manin zinbuuk ah na nusia in.

records.english: Had we known the salesman would stop in every town, we would have taken the train instead.
records.zomi: Van zuakpa khua khempeuh ah a khawl ding i theih leh meileng i tuang zaw ding hi.

records.english: On my first day as a bellboy, I took a guest's bags to the wrong room.
records.zomi: Zinbuuk van puakpa ka hih ni masa pen-in khual khat' van khan khial ah ka puak hi.

records.english: Why did they give you a room next to the kitchen?
records.zomi: Bang hangin anbuk kiang khan hong pia uh hiam?

records.english: My bags were carried up four floors by a boy who couldn't have been older than fifteen.
records.zomi: Kum sawm leh nga sang a upat lo kha pasal naupang khat in ka van dawl li dong a puak hi.

records.english: When the school group checked in, the receptionist was surprised to see forty children with sleeping bags.
records.zomi: Sang pawl a tun ciangin reception nu in giakna ip tawh naupang sawmli a muh ciangin a lamdang sa hi.

records.english: A bed was found for the visiting teacher in the headmaster's house.
records.zomi: Hong veh saya adingin sang makaipa' inn ah lupna khat kimu hi.

records.english: During the training course, we stayed in a college dormitory with very thin walls.
records.zomi: Kisinna laitakin bang pa mahmah college giakna inn khat ah i om hi.

records.english: We really do need a room with a table, because my colleague and I have to prepare tomorrow's presentation.
records.zomi: Ka nasem lawm leh kei zingciang presentation i bawl kul ahih manin dawhkan om khan khat i kisam taktak hi.

records.english: The teachers at our village school live in small houses built next to the classrooms.
records.zomi: I khua sang-a sayate kilasi kiang-a kilam inn neute ah a om uh hi.

records.english: When the river flooded the town, the hotel let the schoolchildren sleep in its hall.
records.zomi: Gun in khuapi a dimsak ciangin zinbuuk in sang naupangte a inn lian ah a giaksak hi.

records.english: Would it be possible to keep my room for one more night, since the meeting has been extended?
records.zomi: Kikhopna a kisausak ahih manin ka khan zan khat behlap ka kem thei ding hiam?

records.english: The best hotel workers notice what guests need before they ask.
records.zomi: Zinbuuk nasem hoih pente in khualte in a ngen ma-un a kisapna uh a mu uh hi.

records.english: The air conditioning in my room broke during the night, and I woke up soaked in sweat before my interview.
records.zomi: Zanin ka khan air conditioning a sia a, ka dotna ma-in khuasiat tawh ka dip kim-in ka khanglo hi.

records.english: No guests are allowed in the staff rooms at our hotel, not even family.
records.zomi: I zinbuuk ah nasemte' khan ah khualte lut thei lo uh hi, innkuan zong.

records.english: Can I check in early, since I've been traveling all night for work?
records.zomi: Nasep adingin zan bup ka khualzin ahih manin hun ma-in ka lut thei ding hiam?

records.english: How long can you stay in the workers' hostel?
records.zomi: Nasemte' hostel ah bangzah sung na om thei hiam?

records.english: As long as you have a job at the factory.
records.zomi: Factory ah nasep na neih sung khempeuh.

records.english: Is there a laundry service for guests staying longer than a week?
records.zomi: Kal khat val a om khualte adingin puan sawpna a om hiam?

records.english: Why do the hotel cleaners work so early in the morning?
records.zomi: Bang hangin zinbuuk siangsakte zingsang manlang takin na a sem uh hiam?

records.english: So that the rooms are ready for guests arriving on the morning flights.
records.zomi: Zingsang vanleng tawh hong tung khualte adingin khante a kiman khin theih nadingin.

records.english: Your room is ready, and your colleagues are waiting for you in the lobby.
records.zomi: Na khan kiman khin a, na nasem lawmte in lutna khan ah hong ngak uh hi.

records.english: My father managed a small hotel for thirty years and still notices every dusty corner when we travel.
records.zomi: Ka pa kum sawmthum sung zinbuuk neu khat a kem a, i khualzin ciangin ki-ngawi mun leivui khempeuh a mu lai hi.

records.english: The receptionist printed my report for free.
records.zomi: Reception nu in ka report a man om lo-in a suaksak sak hi.

records.english: Is breakfast included for conference guests, or do we pay separately?
records.zomi: Kikhopna khualte adingin zingsang an a kihel hiam, a tuam-in i pia ding hiam?

records.english: It's included, and it starts at six thirty for people with early sessions.
records.zomi: Kihel hi, zingsang manlang kikhopna nei mite adingin nai guk leh a kim ciangin kipan hi.

records.english: Can students get a discount if they're staying for the university open day?
records.zomi: Sangpi hon ni adingin a om sangnaupangte in man niamsak a ngah thei uh hiam?

records.english: Everyone, keep your room keys with you, because the front desk closes at eleven.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, mai dawhkan nai sawm leh khat ciangin a kikhak ahih manin na khan tawh na kiang ah kem un.

records.english: All of you will share rooms in pairs, and the teachers will be on the same floor.
records.zomi: Note khempeuh mi nih ciat-in khan na kihawm ding uh a, sayate dawl khat mah ah a om ding uh hi.

records.english: Students, if anything in your room is broken, tell a teacher before we leave.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte, na khan sungah bangmah a siat leh i pai ma-in saya kiangah gen un.

records.english: Staying in the same hotel for a month-long project made it feel almost like home.
records.zomi: Kha khat project adingin zinbuuk khat mah ah om in inn bang dek hong kisak sak hi.

records.english: We were moved to another hotel because the conference had more guests than expected.
records.zomi: Kikhopna in khual a lamen sangin a tam zaw ahih manin zinbuuk dang ah hong pemsak uh hi.

records.english: We had the cleaners leave the room alone for the week so that our papers wouldn't be moved.
records.zomi: I laite a kipem loh nadingin kal khat sung siangsakte in i khan a khoih loh nadingin i ngen hi.

records.english: The nurses who work at the hospital in the hills stay in a guesthouse run by the church.
records.zomi: Mual-a zato ah na sem nurse te pawlpi' kem zinbuuk neu khat ah a om uh hi.

records.english: Since the new factory opened, every guesthouse in town has been full of visiting engineers.
records.zomi: Factory thak kihon pan khuapi-a zinbuuk neu khempeuh hong veh engineer te tawh a dim hi.

records.english: The rooms were booked by the company, but nobody had told the hotel we'd arrive at midnight.
records.zomi: Khante company in a bawl a, ahi zongin zan lai ciangin i tun ding kuamah in zinbuuk kiangah a gen kei uh hi.

records.english: Does the room have a desk and reliable Wi-Fi?
records.zomi: Khan sungah dawhkan leh muanhuai Wi-Fi a om hiam?

records.english: Yes, and there's a quiet business room on the ground floor if you need to print anything.
records.zomi: Om hi, bangmah na suaksak kul leh lei tung dawl ah sumbawlna khan dai khat om hi.

records.english: Could you send the invoice to my company instead of to me?
records.zomi: Invoice pen kei kiangah hi lo-in ka company kiangah na khak thei ding hiam?

records.english: The hotel restaurant was closed for renovations, so we had to eat at the station.
records.zomi: Zinbuuk an zuakna dawl kibawl thak ahih manin kikhak a, station ah an i ne kul hi.

records.english: My manager booked me into a hotel so close to the office that I could walk there in two minutes.
records.zomi: Ka manager in office kiang mahmah zinbuuk khat hong bawl sak a, minit nih-in ka kaai thei hi.

records.english: The guesthouse owner said, "Leave your muddy boots outside; we'll clean them by morning."
records.zomi: Zinbuuk neu neipa in, “Na khedap buan nin polam ah nusia in; zingsang dong i siangsak ding hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: The manager told us, "Treat every guest as if they were visiting your own home."
records.zomi: Manager in, “Khual khempeuh na inn hong veh bangin koih un,” hong ci hi.

records.english: My aunt cleans rooms at a hotel by the beach and sends most of her pay home.
records.zomi: Ka ni tuipi gei zinbuuk khat ah khan a siangsak a, a kha man a tam zaw inn ah a khak hi.

records.english: The night porter woke me at four so that I wouldn't miss the early train to the factory.
records.zomi: Factory pai meileng masa ka mansuah loh nadingin zan kongpi kemtu in nai li ciangin hong phongkhia hi.

records.english: My cousin trained at a hotel school and now manages a guesthouse by the lake.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam zinbuuk sang ah a kisin a, tu-in dil gei zinbuuk neu khat a kem hi.

records.english: Hotel staff at our company must wear their name badges at all times.
records.zomi: I company-a zinbuuk nasemte in hun khempeuh-in a min badge a bulh kul uh hi.

records.english: Working at a big hotel taught me to stay polite even when guests are rude.
records.zomi: Zinbuuk lian ah na ka sep manin khualte a zahtak loh ciangun zong zahtak den dingin ka sin hi.

records.english: Ask the office whether the company apartment is free next week.
records.zomi: Company inn kal hong ding ciangin a awng hiam office ah dong in.

records.english: My brother works as a hotel cook and starts making breakfast at five every morning.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal zinbuuk an huanpa ahi a, zingsang simin nai nga ciangin zingsang an a bawl kipan hi.

records.english: Could someone bring an iron to my room before my meeting?
records.zomi: Ka kikhopna ma-in kuamah in ka khan ah meitut khat hong tawi thei ding hiam?

records.english: I worked the night shift at a hotel reception while I was studying for my accounting degree.
records.zomi: Accounting degree ka kisin laitakin zinbuuk reception ah zan nasep ka sem hi.

records.english: Can you recommend a cheap hostel near the university for students coming to the exams?
records.zomi: Sitna adingin hong pai sangnaupangte adingin sangpi kiang-a hostel man neu khat hong gen thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: The workers at the mine sleep in a long building with bunk beds and one shared kitchen.
records.zomi: Suang tukna mun-a nasemte inn sau khat ah lupna kituah leh anbuk kihawm khat tawh a ihmu uh hi.

records.english: When I started university, I shared a tiny room in the dormitory with two other students.
records.zomi: Sangpi ka kah kipat ciangin giakna inn ah sangnaupang dang nih tawh khan neu khat ka kihawm hi.

records.english: Should I leave a tip for the cleaner if I've stayed for a whole week?
records.zomi: Kal khat bup ka om leh siangsak nu adingin tip ka nusia ding hiam?

records.english: There was a power cut at the hotel, so the receptionist checked us in by candlelight.
records.zomi: Zinbuuk ah meivak a kitan ahih manin reception nu in khawimeivaak tawh hong lutsak hi.

records.english: My first job was folding towels in the hotel laundry, and I could fold a hundred an hour by the end of the summer.
records.zomi: Ka nasep masa pen zinbuuk puan sawpna ah puan nulna khiat ahi a, khal tawp ciangin nai khat-in za khat ka khiat thei hi.

records.english: Kids, the hotel is full of business people who need to sleep, so keep the noise down in the corridor.
records.zomi: Naupangte, zinbuuk sumbawl mi ihmu kisam tawh a dim ahih manin lampi khan ah dai takin om un.

records.english: What time do the cleaners start on the rooms in the morning?
records.zomi: Zingsang ciangin siangsakte in nai bangzah ciangin khante a siangsak kipan uh hiam?

records.english: The young engineers shared a rented house near the building site for the whole project.
records.zomi: Engineer khangnote project bup sungin inn lamna mun kiang-a inn hal khat a kihawm uh hi.

records.english: We arrived at the conference hotel, found the lift broken, and carried our boxes up the stairs.
records.zomi: Kikhopna zinbuuk i tun ciangin lift a sia ahih manin i bawmte kaplei tawh i puak tou hi.

records.english: My daughter's cooking teacher asked every student to bring one dish from home for the class lunch.
records.zomi: Ka tanu' an huan saya in kilasi sun an adingin sangnaupang khempeuh inn pan an khat ciat tawi dingin a ngen hi.

records.english: The head chef said, "Get everything ready before the first order comes in, and the evening will be easy."
records.zomi: An huanpa makai in, “Van sapna masa pen a tun ma-in na khempeuh kibawl khin inla, nitak a baih ding hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: After twenty years as a chef, my uncle still sharpens his knives every morning before work.
records.zomi: An huanpa-in kum sawmnih khit ciangin ka pa neu in nasep a pai ma-in zingsang simin a temte a tat lai hi.

records.english: Is there anything I can chop for you before I leave for work?
records.zomi: Nasep ka pai ma-in kong tan sak ding bangmah a om hiam?

records.english: When the gas ran out in the middle of lunch, the cooks finished the rice on a wood fire behind the school.
records.zomi: Sun an kimlai-in gas a bei ciangin an huante in sang nung lam ah sing mei tawh buh a huan zo uh hi.

records.english: Every morning before the restaurant opens, the junior cooks peel and chop all the vegetables for the day.
records.zomi: Zingsang simin an zuakna dawl a kihon ma-in an huan neute in ni khat ading anteh khempeuh a ham uh a, a tan uh hi.

records.english: Isn't it boring to make the same dish two hundred times a night?
records.zomi: Zan khat-in an kibang vei za nih huan a lungkiahuai hi lo hiam?

records.english: We really do need two more people in the kitchen for the wedding on Saturday.
records.zomi: Kiginni kiteenna adingin anbuk ah mi nih behlap i kisam taktak hi.

records.english: The bread dough for the hospital breakfast is mixed by a machine the size of a washing machine.
records.zomi: Zato zingsang an ading moh tang pen puan sawpna machine zah machine khat in a kituah sak hi.

records.english: Once the volunteers had been shown how to roll the noodles, they could make hundreds in an hour.
records.zomi: Thalawp nasemte an-ngum ziat dan kietsak khit ciangin nai khat sungin za tampi a bawl thei uh hi.

records.english: When I cook for the office party, I make everything the night before so that I only have to heat it.
records.zomi: Office pawi adingin an ka huan ciangin ka lumsak bek kul nadingin a zan ma-in na khempeuh ka bawl hi.

records.english: Our teacher made us cook with only five ingredients to show us how to save money.
records.zomi: Sum khol dan hong lak nadingin i saya in van nga bek tawh an hong huansak hi.

records.english: How long does it take to prepare lunch for three hundred factory workers?
records.zomi: Factory nasem za thum adingin sun an huan hun bangzah a sau hiam?

records.english: Four of us start at seven, and it's ready by twelve.
records.zomi: I li in nai sagih ciangin i kipan a, nai sawm leh nih ciangin a kiman hi.

records.english: Who can help me get dinner ready tonight, since I have a meeting at eight?
records.zomi: Nai giat ciangin kikhopna ka neih manin tu zanin nitak an kibawl nadingin kua in hong huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: The chicken for the conference dinner was marinated overnight in the hotel's big cold room.
records.zomi: Kikhopna nitak an adingin aksa zinbuuk' khan vot lian sungah zan bup kinen hi.

records.english: Would you mind stirring the sauce while I answer the phone in the office?
records.zomi: Office ah phone ka dawn laitakin an-tui na zuang sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: At culinary school, we were taught to clean as we cook so that the kitchen never gets out of control.
records.zomi: An huan sang ah anbuk a buai ngei loh nadingin huan kawm-in siangsak dingin hong hilh uh hi.

records.english: Our school's cook grinds the spices with a heavy stone because she says machines spoil the flavor.
records.zomi: I sang an huannu in machine in a lim a siatsak hi, a cih manin an-lim-nah suang gik tawh a sum hi.

records.english: Shall I bring a cooked dish or something you can heat at the office?
records.zomi: An kihuan khin khat ka tawi ding hiam, office ah na lumsak theih khat hiam?

records.english: The trainees were nervous when the hotel owner came into the kitchen to taste their dishes.
records.zomi: Zinbuuk neipa in a ante uh liim dingin anbuk ah a lut ciangin kisinte a lau uh hi.

records.english: A good kitchen manager plans the next day's meals before the current one has even been served.
records.zomi: Anbuk makaipa hoih in tu-a an kipia ma-in a zing ni an a gel hi.

records.english: My father used to cook for the miners and still makes enormous pots of soup for our small family.
records.zomi: Ka pa in suang tukte adingin an a huan ngei a, i innkuan neu adingin an-tui beel lian mahmah a huan lai hi.

records.english: When the meat was cut too thick, the whole batch had to be cooked for twice as long.
records.zomi: Sa a tan sah lua ciangin beel bup a nih in sau zawin kihuan kul hi.

records.english: The new apprentice burned his hand on the grill during his first week, so the chef showed him how to use the tongs properly.
records.zomi: Nasep kisin thak in a kal masa pen-in grill tungah a khut a kang ahih manin an huanpa in a lenna a zat dan a etsak hi.

records.english: Could you show me how you fold the dumplings so quickly?
records.zomi: Sambuk na hum manlang dan hong etsak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: My boss tasted my soup and said, "Too much salt — start again."
records.zomi: Ka makaipa in ka an-tui a liim a, “Cii a tam lua hi — kipan kik in,” a ci hi.

records.english: Can you cut the onions into small cubes for the soup?
records.zomi: An-tui adingin lothaang neu takin na tan thei ding hiam?

records.english: Let's cook the food for the school fair together on Friday night.
records.zomi: Laithai ni zan ciangin sang poai adingin an khawm-in huan ni.

records.english: Preparing food for a hundred guests taught me more about planning than any business course.
records.zomi: Khual za khat adingin an bawl in sumbawlna kisinna khempeuh sangin gelna thu tam zaw hong hilh hi.

records.english: Why don't we cook a big pot of beans before exam week starts?
records.zomi: Bang hangin sitna kal kipat ma-in be beel lian khat i huan kei hiam?

records.english: The rice for the factory canteen is washed three times in a big metal tub.
records.zomi: Factory canteen ading buh pen thau beel lian sungah vei thum kisil hi.

records.english: If you finish your homework early, you can help me make the rice cakes for my stall.
records.zomi: Na inn-a sep ding hun ma-in na zawh leh ka dawl adingin buh moh bawl hong huh thei hi.

records.english: Running a food stall means that my mornings start at four with a mountain of chopping.
records.zomi: An dawl neu khat kem in ka zingsang nai li ciangin tan ding tampi tawh a kipan hi.

records.english: I left the cake in the oven too long while I was on a work call, and the edges went black.
records.zomi: Nasep phone sam laitakin cake oven sungah ka nusia sau lua a, a gei a kang vom hi.

records.english: Can I take some of the leftover rice home after my shift?
records.zomi: Ka nasep hun khit ciangin buh taang tawmno inn ah ka tawi thei ding hiam?

records.english: Students, sharpen your knives with the steel before we start the vegetable cuts.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte, anteh tan i kipat ma-in na temte uh sik tawh tat un.

records.english: My sister learned to make bread at a training center and now supplies three shops in town.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu in kisinna mun ah moh bawl a sin a, tu-in khuapi-a dawl thum adingin a pia hi.

records.english: The kitchen at the hospital prepares special meals for patients who can't eat salt.
records.zomi: Zato anbuk in cii ne thei lo damlote adingin an tuam a huan hi.

records.english: My cousin weighs every ingredient for her bakery orders on a digital scale, down to the gram.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu in a moh bawlna sapna adingin van khempeuh digital bukna tawh gram dong a buk hi.

records.english: You two can peel the carrots, and the rest of you can wash the lettuce.
records.zomi: Note nih in carrot na ham thei uh a, a dangte in lettuce na sil thei uh hi.

records.english: Everyone, put on your aprons and wash your hands before you touch any food.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, an khatpeuh na khoih ma-un na puan khawng silh unla na khut uh sil un.

records.english: Our neighbor bakes the bread for the school's breakfast program in her own oven.
records.zomi: I inn veng nu in sang zingsang an program ading moh amah' oven sungah a bawl hi.

records.english: My first job in a kitchen was peeling potatoes, and I must have peeled a whole mountain of them.
records.zomi: Anbuk ah ka nasep masa pen alu ham ahi a, mual khat zah ka ham kha ding hi.

records.english: What's the first thing you do when you arrive at the restaurant kitchen?
records.zomi: An zuakna dawl anbuk na tun ciangin a masa pen-in bang na sem hiam?

records.english: I check the fridge and write a list of what needs to be prepared.
records.zomi: Khal bawm ka en a, bawl kisam list khat ka gelh hi.

records.english: The fish arrived late from the market, so the whole menu had to be changed at the last minute.
records.zomi: Zuakna mun pan nga a nun ahih manin a nunung pen hun-in menu bup kikhel kul hi.

records.english: What did you have to cook for your practical exam at catering school?
records.zomi: An huan sang na sitna ah bang na huan kul hiam?

records.english: A three-course meal for four people in under two hours.
records.zomi: Mi li adingin nai nih nuai-in an kuang thum.

records.english: Using a sharp knife is actually safer than using a blunt one, our instructor told us.
records.zomi: Temte hiam zang pen temte tum zang sangin a bitna zaw hi, ci-in i hilhpa in hong gen hi.

records.english: Do you think we'll have enough vegetables for the staff lunch tomorrow?
records.zomi: Zingciang nasemte sun an adingin anteh a cing ding in na ngaihsun hiam?

records.english: I prepare all my lunches for the week on Sunday afternoon while the children do their homework.
records.zomi: Naupangte in a inn-a sep ding uh a sep laitakin Nipini nitak ciangin kal khat sun an khempeuh ka bawl hi.

records.english: Why does the chef make the new cooks taste every sauce?
records.zomi: Bang hangin an huanpa in an huan thakte an-tui khempeuh a liimsak hiam?

records.english: So that they learn what it should taste like when it's right.
records.zomi: A dik ciangin bangci-a lim ding hiam a sin theih nadingun.

records.english: The soup for the night-shift workers is kept warm in a huge pot on the stove until midnight.
records.zomi: Zan nasemte ading an-tui pen zan lai dong meibuk tung beel lian sungah a lum den hi.

records.english: With a blender and a few bananas, the kids made smoothies for the whole class.
records.zomi: Blender leh banana tawmno tawh naupangte in kilasi bup adingin smoothie a bawl uh hi.

records.english: Grandma has been cooking for the school's teachers every Friday since she retired from teaching.
records.zomi: Pi in hilhna pan a khawl khit pan Laithai ni simin sang sayate adingin an a huan hi.

records.english: The students cooked a meal for their parents as the final project of the term.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte in term tawp project-in a nu leh pa uh adingin an a huan uh hi.

records.english: My husband cooks dinner on the nights I work late at the clinic.
records.zomi: Clinic ah nai sau ka sep zan ciangin ka pasal in nitak an a huan hi.

records.english: Nobody in the kitchen goes home until the pots are washed and the floor is clean.
records.zomi: Beelte kisil a lei a siang dong anbuk-a kuamah in inn a ciah kei hi.

records.english: There's a chance the caterer can add more dishes if you call before Friday.
records.zomi: Laithai ni ma-in na sam leh an bawlpa in an behlap a bawl thei kha ding hi.

records.english: The food for the school sports day was ordered weeks in advance.
records.zomi: Sang kimawl ni an kal tampi ma-in kisap khin hi.

records.english: The first time I ordered food abroad on a work trip, I pointed at a picture and hoped for the best.
records.zomi: Nasep khualzinna-in gamdang ah an ka sap masa pen-in lim khat ka lak a, a hoih ding ka lamen hi.

records.english: Excuse me, we ordered the meals for a group of thirty teachers, but only twenty have arrived.
records.zomi: Hong maisak in, saya sawmthum pawl adingin an i sap a, ahi zongin sawmnih bek hong tung uh hi.

records.english: Do you take orders by phone for large groups?
records.zomi: Mi tam pawl adingin phone tawh an sap na sang hiam?

records.english: Yes, but we need at least a day's notice for more than twenty people.
records.zomi: Sang hi, ahi zongin mi sawmnih val adingin ni khat ma-in hong gen kul hi.

records.english: Can you tell me whether the lunch special is ready yet?
records.zomi: Sun an tuam a kiman khin hiam hong gen thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: My boss said, "Order whatever you like — the company is paying tonight."
records.zomi: Ka makaipa in, “Na deih bangbang sap un — tu zanin company in a pia ding hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: The delivery driver brought the office's lunch to the wrong building, so we ate at three.
records.zomi: An puakpa in office sun an inn khial ah a tawi ahih manin nai thum ciangin an i ne hi.

records.english: Would it be cheaper to order from the canteen or to bring food from home?
records.zomi: Canteen pan sap a man neu zaw ding hiam, inn pan an tawi a man neu zaw ding hiam?

records.english: When I worked at the café, I learned to remember six orders at once without writing them down.
records.zomi: Cafe ah na ka sep lai-in gelh lo-in an sapna guk vei khat-in phawk ka sin hi.

records.english: Waiters at our restaurant must ask about allergies before they take an order.
records.zomi: I an zuakna dawl nasemte in an sapna a lak ma-un kituak lohna nei mi a om hiam a dong kul uh hi.

records.english: My manager always lets the newest employee order first at team dinners.
records.zomi: Pawl nitak an ah ka manager in nasem thak pen a sap masa a phal tawntung hi.

records.english: The waiter typed our order into a small machine, and it was printed in the kitchen at once.
records.zomi: An zuakna dawl nasem in i sapna machine neu khat sungah a koih a, anbuk ah pahtakin kisuaksak hi.

records.english: If we order now, the food might arrive before the visitors do.
records.zomi: Tu-in i sap leh khualte a tun ma-un an a tung kha ding hi.

records.english: Everyone, write your lunch order on this list, and I'll call the restaurant at eleven.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, hih list tungah na sun an sapna gelh unla, nai sawm leh khat ciangin an zuakna dawl ka sam ding hi.

records.english: When the visiting inspectors arrived, the head teacher ordered lunch from the best restaurant in town.
records.zomi: Enkaktute hong tun ciangin sang makaipa in khuapi-a an zuakna dawl hoih pen pan sun an a sap hi.

records.english: My daughter's school lets parents order lunches online for the whole week.
records.zomi: Ka tanu' sang in nu leh pate kal bup ading sun an online tawh a sap theih uh a phal hi.

records.english: We really do need the food delivered by twelve, because the workshop starts at half past.
records.zomi: Workshop nai sawm leh nih leh a kim ciangin a kipat ding ahih manin nai sawm leh nih ma-in an a tun ding i kisam taktak hi.

records.english: Nobody at the meeting wanted to order first, so the director chose for everyone.
records.zomi: Kikhopna ah kuamah in a sap masa a deih kei uh ahih manin director in mi khempeuh adingin a teel hi.

records.english: Ordering lunch for a hundred conference guests, I forgot that some of them couldn't eat pork.
records.zomi: Kikhopna khual za khat adingin sun an ka sap ciangin khenkhatte in vok sa a ne thei kei uh, cih ka mangngilh hi.

records.english: My brother works at a fast-food counter and takes about four hundred orders a day.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal an manlang dawl ah na a sem a, ni khat-in an sapna za li bang a la hi.

records.english: You'd better order now, because the kitchen closes at nine.
records.zomi: Anbuk nai kua ciangin kikhak ahih manin tu-in sap zaw in.

records.english: The chef asked the waiters to tell customers that the fish would take twenty minutes.
records.zomi: An huanpa in nga minit sawmnih a sau ding hi, ci-in van leite kiangah gen dingin an zuakna dawl nasemte a ngen hi.

records.english: Our office orders from the same noodle shop so often that they know our orders by heart.
records.zomi: I office in an-ngum dawl khat mah pan a sap tam lua ahih manin i sapnate a lungsim uh ah a phawk uh hi.

records.english: The kitchen sent out the wrong order twice, so the manager gave the whole table free tea.
records.zomi: Anbuk in an khial vei nih a sawl ahih manin manager in dawhkan bup tea a man om lo-in a pia hi.

records.english: Taking orders from a table of tired night-shift nurses taught me to be quick and polite.
records.zomi: Zan nasem nurse gim dawhkan khat pan an sapna lak in manlang taka leh zahtak taka om hong hilh hi.

records.english: The staff room phone is mostly used for ordering lunch on exam days.
records.zomi: Sitna ni-in nasemte' khan phone a tam zaw sun an sap nadingin kizang hi.

records.english: Students, if you want to order a school lunch, put your name on the list by the door.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte, sang sun an na sap nuam uh leh kongkhak kiang-a list tungah na min uh koih un.

records.english: The university café was so crowded that I ordered my lunch through the window.
records.zomi: Sangpi cafe ah mi a tam lua ahih manin tawhkhawng tawng-in ka sun an ka sap hi.

records.english: What's quickest on the menu, since I have to be back at work in twenty minutes?
records.zomi: Minit sawmnih sungin nasep ah ka ciah kik kul ahih manin menu tungah a manlang pen bang ahi hiam?

records.english: The night we celebrated my promotion, my colleagues ordered every dessert on the menu.
records.zomi: Ka kaisanna poai i bawl zan-in ka nasem lawmte in menu tung-a an khit nek ding khempeuh a sap uh hi.

records.english: The new waiter repeated every order back to the customers so that nothing would go wrong.
records.zomi: An zuakna dawl nasem thak in bangmah a khial loh nadingin sapna khempeuh van leite kiangah a gen kik hi.

records.english: Could I order the soup without meat, since some of the students don't eat it?
records.zomi: Sangnaupang khenkhatte in sa a ne kei uh ahih manin sa om lo an-tui ka sap thei ding hiam?

records.english: When the ordering system crashed during the lunch rush, the waiters went back to pen and paper.
records.zomi: Sun an buai hun-in sapna system a sia ciangin an zuakna dawl nasemte in kawl leh lai tawh a sem kik uh hi.

records.english: Since the company started paying for Friday lunches, ordering has become a weekly debate.
records.zomi: Company in Laithai ni sun an man a piak kipat pan an sapna pen kal simin kinialna a suak hi.

records.english: If the restaurant is too busy, we might have to order something to take back to the office.
records.zomi: An zuakna dawl ah mi a tam lua leh office ah tawi kik ding khat i sap kul kha ding hi.

records.english: Order the same dish as the client, so that you finish eating at the same time.
records.zomi: An nek khawm ding na zawh theih nadingin client' an kibang mah sap in.

records.english: Who's ordering the food for the farewell lunch?
records.zomi: Kikhenna sun an adingin kua in an a sap ding hiam?

records.english: Lian is, since she knows what everyone likes.
records.zomi: Lian, mi khempeuh' deih a theih manin.

records.english: Shall I order for the whole team, if you tell me what you'd like by noon?
records.zomi: Sun ma-in na deih hong gen leh pawl bup adingin ka sap ding hiam?

records.english: Our class ordered pizza to celebrate the end of exams, and the teacher paid for the drinks.
records.zomi: Sitna bei poai bawl dingin i kilasi in pizza a sap a, saya in dawn ding man a pia hi.

records.english: Your order will be ready in ten minutes, if you'd like to wait at the bar.
records.zomi: Bar ah na ngak nuam leh minit sawm sungin na an kiman ding hi.

records.english: How do I order a meal for a patient who can't eat sugar?
records.zomi: Sugar ne thei lo damlo khat adingin bangci-in an ka sap ding hiam?

records.english: Kids, decide what you want before we get to the counter, because there's a long line behind us.
records.zomi: Naupangte, i nung lam ah mi tampi a kizom ahih manin dawhkan i tun ma-in na deih uh khensat un.

records.english: Can I take your order, or are you waiting for your colleagues?
records.zomi: Na sapna ka la thei ding hiam, na nasem lawmte na ngak hiam?

records.english: We'll wait, thanks — they're just parking the van.
records.zomi: I ngak ding hi, ka lungdam hi — van a koih uh hi.

records.english: Is the teachers' lunch ordered separately from the students' meals?
records.zomi: Sayate' sun an pen sangnaupangte' an tawh kikhen-in kisap hiam?

records.english: On my first night as a waiter, I wrote the orders so badly that the cook couldn't read them.
records.zomi: An zuakna dawl nasem ka hih zan masa pen-in sapnate ka gelh sia lua ahih manin an huanpa in a sim thei kei hi.

records.english: Students can order lunch from the canteen in the morning and collect it at the break.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte in zingsang ciangin canteen pan sun an a sap thei uh a, khawl hun-in a la thei uh hi.

records.english: My cousin runs a small business delivering lunches to factory workers who order by text message.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam in text message tawh a sap factory nasemte kiangah sun an puak sumbawlna neu khat a kem hi.

records.english: Had we placed the order a day earlier, the caterer could have fed everyone at the workshop.
records.zomi: Ni khat ma-in i sap leh workshop-a mi khempeuh an bawlpa in a vak thei ding hi.

records.english: What do you usually order when you take a client out for lunch?
records.zomi: Client sun an ne dingin na paipih ciangin bang na sap zel hiam?

records.english: Something that's easy to eat while talking, like soup or rice.
records.zomi: Kiho kawm-a nek baih, an-tui hiam buh hiam bang.

records.english: Let's order something light, because we have a long afternoon of meetings.
records.zomi: Nitak sau kikhopna i neih ding ahih manin a zang khat sap ni.

records.english: Using the app, I can order my coffee on the bus and pick it up on the way to my desk.
records.zomi: App zang-in bus tungah ka kawfi ka sap thei a, ka dawhkan pai lam ah ka la thei hi.

records.english: Could you order sandwiches for twelve people for the meeting at one?
records.zomi: Nai khat kikhopna adingin mi sawm leh nih ading sandwich na sap thei ding hiam?

records.english: Two teas and a plate of samosas for the table by the window, please.
records.zomi: Tawhkhawng kiang dawhkan adingin tea nih leh samosa kuang khat, hong pia in.

records.english: Do the builders still order their tea from the stall by the gate?
records.zomi: Inn lamte in kongpi kiang dawl pan a tea uh a sap lai uh hiam?

records.english: Is it possible to order a vegetarian meal for one of our guests?
records.zomi: I khual khat adingin sa om lo an sap theih ding hiam?

records.english: My wife used her grandmother's best tea set when the school inspector came to our house.
records.zomi: Sang enkaktu i inn a tun ciangin ka zi in a pi' tea khuang hoih pente a zang hi.

records.english: The family who hosted me during my internship still sends me a card every New Year.
records.zomi: Ka internship laitakin hong dawn innkuan in Kum Thak simin card hong khak lai uh hi.

records.english: Since the hotel was full, the visiting engineers stayed with families in the village.
records.zomi: Zinbuuk a dim ahih manin hong veh engineer te khua sung innkuante kiangah a om uh hi.

records.english: We're having my husband's colleagues over for dinner on Friday, so the house has to be tidy by six.
records.zomi: Laithai ni ciangin ka pasal' nasem lawmte nitak an ah i sam ahih manin nai guk ma-in inn a siang kul hi.

records.english: Hosting a visiting choir meant forty extra people in our small church for a whole weekend.
records.zomi: Hong veh la sa pawl i dawn manin kal tawp bup i pawlpi neu ah mi sawmli behlap a om hi.

records.english: Do you think the visitors from the city would enjoy a meal cooked over an open fire?
records.zomi: Khuapi pan hong vehte in polam mei tungah kihuan an a deih ding uh in na ngaihsun hiam?

records.english: We moved the sewing machines out of the front room so that the visiting buyers could sit down.
records.zomi: Hong veh van leite a tut theih nadingun mai lam khan pan puan khuina machine te i pemsak hi.

records.english: When our school hosted a team from another district, each family took in two players for the weekend.
records.zomi: I sang in district dang pan kimawl pawl khat a dawn ciangin innkuan khat ciat in kal tawp adingin kimawlte nih ciat a dawn hi.

records.english: Students, when you stay with your host family, help with the dishes after every meal.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte, na om sakna innkuan tawh na om ciangin an nek khit simin kuang sil huh un.

records.english: We hired a cook for the evening, so that I could talk to my husband's clients instead of staying in the kitchen.
records.zomi: Anbuk ah ka om loh nadingin ka pasal' clients tawh ka kihopih theih nadingin nitak khat adingin an huanpa khat i sap hi.

records.english: There might not be enough chairs if all the volunteers come to the planning meeting at our house.
records.zomi: Thalawp nasem khempeuh i inn-a gelna kikhopna ah a hong uh leh tutna a cing kei kha ding hi.

records.english: Can we host the parents' meeting at our house, since the school hall is being repaired?
records.zomi: Sang inn lian kibawl kik ahih manin nu leh pate' kikhopna i inn ah i bawl thei ding hiam?

records.english: The best part of hosting exchange students is seeing our town through their eyes.
records.zomi: Gamdang sangnaupang dawn ah a hoih pen i khuapi amaute' mit tawh muh ahi hi.

records.english: The visiting doctor slept in our spare room while she worked at the village clinic.
records.zomi: Hong veh siavuan nu khua clinic ah na a sep laitakin i khan awng ah a ihmu hi.

records.english: My boss arrived an hour early, and I was still in my apron.
records.zomi: Ka makaipa nai khat ma-in hong tung a, ka puan khawng ka silh lai hi.

records.english: My aunt hosts a student teacher at her house every year.
records.zomi: Ka ni in kum simin saya kisin khat a inn ah a dawn hi.

records.english: Could you put the projector in the living room, so that the team can watch the presentation after dinner?
records.zomi: Pawl in nitak an khit ciangin presentation a et theih nadingun projector innsung khan ah na koih thei ding hiam?

records.english: Hosting the study group every week means our kitchen is always full of hungry teenagers.
records.zomi: Kal simin kisinna pawl i dawn manin i anbuk khangno gilkialte tawh a dim tawntung hi.

records.english: Is there anything the guest speaker doesn't eat?
records.zomi: Thugen khual in a nek loh bangmah a om hiam?

records.english: If the delegation arrives late, we could serve dinner at the hotel instead of at home.
records.zomi: Hong veh pawl a tun nun leh inn sangin zinbuuk ah nitak an i pia thei hi.

records.english: My grandmother insisted on cooking for the young doctors who came to work at the clinic.
records.zomi: Ka pi in clinic ah na sem dingin hong pai siavuan khangnote adingin an huan a ngiat hi.

records.english: My father welcomed every new teacher in the village with a meal at our house.
records.zomi: Ka pa in khua-a saya thak khempeuh i inn ah an tawh a muak hi.

records.english: Hosting colleagues at home can bring a team closer than any meeting in the office.
records.zomi: Nasem lawmte inn ah dawn in office-a kikhopna khempeuh sangin pawl a kinaisak zaw thei hi.

records.english: Thank you for having us — your home made the training week feel much shorter.
records.zomi: Hong dawn manin ka lungdam hi — na inn in kisinna kal hong tomsak mahmah hi.

records.english: All of you are welcome to stay for lunch after the study session.
records.zomi: Kisinna khit ciangin note khempeuh sun an ah na om thei uh hi.

records.english: Could you help me carry the extra mattresses upstairs before the visiting team arrives?
records.zomi: Hong veh pawl a tun ma-un mattress behlapte tung lam ah ka puak nadingin hong huh thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: My mother-in-law cooked for three days when my husband's boss came to visit.
records.zomi: Ka pasal' makaipa hong veh ciangin ka sungnu ni thum sung an a huan hi.

records.english: An exchange student from Japan stayed with us for a term and taught the children to fold paper cranes.
records.zomi: Japan pan gamdang sangnaupang khat term khat sung i kiang ah a om a, naupangte lai tawh vasa khiat a hilh hi.

records.english: The guest speaker was given my daughter's room, and she slept on the sofa without complaining.
records.zomi: Thugen khual ka tanu' khan kipia a, ka tanu phunsan lo-in sofa tungah a ihmu hi.

records.english: How do you host a dinner for colleagues without spending too much?
records.zomi: Sum tam lua zang lo-in nasem lawmte adingin nitak an bangci-in na bawl hiam?

records.english: Ask everyone to bring one dish, and you provide the rice and drinks.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh an khat ciat tawi dingin ngen inla, nang buh leh dawn ding na koih hi.

records.english: We keep a spare bed ready for anyone who comes to work at the clinic.
records.zomi: Clinic ah na sem dingin hong pai kuapeuh adingin lupna behlap khat i bawl khin den hi.

records.english: Would your students like to visit our farm and stay for lunch?
records.zomi: Na sangnaupangte in i lo veh-in sun an ah a om nuam uh hiam?

records.english: Let's put the visiting teacher's name on the guest room door so that she feels welcome.
records.zomi: Kidawn a kisak theih nadingin hong veh saya nu' min khual khan kongkhak tungah koih ni.

records.english: We set up a long table in the yard so that the farm workers could eat together after the harvest.
records.zomi: Buh lak khit ciangin lo nasemte an a ne khawm theih nadingun inn mai ah dawhkan sau khat i koih hi.

records.english: Why don't we invite the new nurse to stay with us until her room at the hospital is ready?
records.zomi: Nurse thak' zato khan a kiman dong bang hangin i kiang ah om dingin i sam kei hiam?

records.english: The pastor told us, "Treat the students staying with you as if they were your own children."
records.zomi: Pastor in, “Note kiang-a om sangnaupangte nangma' tate bangin koih un,” hong ci hi.

records.english: Using the big rice cooker from the church, we cooked enough rice for forty visiting students.
records.zomi: Pawlpi pan rice cooker lian zang-in hong veh sangnaupang sawmli vak zah buh i huan hi.

records.english: Everyone, please help yourselves to tea before we start the meeting.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, kikhopna i kipat ma-in tea amau mah in la un.

records.english: My son's classmates stayed at our house after the late concert because the buses had stopped.
records.zomi: Bus te a khawl khin ahih manin la poai nun khit ciangin ka tapa' kilasi lawmte i inn ah a giak uh hi.

records.english: Our office hosts a lunch for new employees on their first Friday, so that they can meet everyone.
records.zomi: Nasem thakte in mi khempeuh a muh theih nadingun i office in a Laithai ni masa pen-un sun an a bawl hi.

records.english: The night we hosted my team's end-of-year party, the neighbors complained about the singing.
records.zomi: Ka pawl' kum tawp pawi i dawn zan-in i inn vengte in la ging a phunsan uh hi.

records.english: When my husband brought home three colleagues without warning, I stretched one chicken to feed six people.
records.zomi: Ka pasal in gen lo-in nasem lawm thum inn ah a paipih ciangin ak khat tawh mi guk ka vaksak hi.

records.english: What time will your colleagues arrive?
records.zomi: Na nasem lawmte nai bangzah ciangin a tung ding uh hiam?

records.english: Around seven, after the office closes.
records.zomi: Nai sagih bang, office a kikhak khit ciangin.

records.english: What should I cook when my boss comes to dinner?
records.zomi: Ka makaipa nitak an ah a hong ciangin bang ka huan ding hiam?

records.english: Something you've made many times, so that you're not nervous in the kitchen.
records.zomi: Anbuk ah na lau loh nadingin vei tampi na huan ngei khat.

records.english: When the exchange student arrived, she was so tired that she slept for fourteen hours.
records.zomi: Gamdang sangnaupang a tun ciangin a gim lua ahih manin nai sawm leh li a ihmu hi.

records.english: Kids, our guests have had a long day at the conference, so let them rest before you ask questions.
records.zomi: Naupangte, i khualte kikhopna lian ah ni sau a zang uh ahih manin na dot ma-un tawlngak sak un.

records.english: Is it all right to invite the whole department to our small flat?
records.zomi: I inn neu ah department bup sam a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: If they don't mind sitting on the floor, why not?
records.zomi: Lei ah tut a lungkham kei uh leh bang hang lo ding hiam?

records.english: The children showed our foreign guest their school, and she showed them photos of hers.
records.zomi: Naupangte in i gamdang khual a sang uh a etsak uh a, amah in amah' sang lim a etsak hi.

records.english: I made a simple map of the town for our guests so that they could find their way to the training center.
records.zomi: Kisinna mun a muh theih nadingun i khualte adingin khuapi map baih khat ka bawl hi.

records.english: Our office kitchen was turned into a dining room for the visitors' lunch.
records.zomi: Hong vehte' sun an adingin i office anbuk an nekna khan ah kibawl hi.

records.english: Our new colleague from abroad stayed with my family for two weeks until she found an apartment.
records.zomi: Gamdang pan i nasem lawm thak inn a muh dong kal nih sung ka innkuan kiang ah a om hi.

records.english: Our neighbors lent us their folding tables for the staff party in the garden.
records.zomi: Huan sung-a nasemte' pawi adingin i inn vengte in a dawhkan khiat theihte hong leitawi uh hi.

records.english: We really do want the visiting teachers to feel at home while they're working at our school.
records.zomi: Hong veh sayate i sang ah na a sep sungun a inn ah om bangin a kisak ding uh i deih taktak hi.

records.english: Shall I pick up your guests from the station on my way home from work?
records.zomi: Nasep pan inn ka ciah lam ah station pan na khualte ka la ding hiam?

records.english: When the business delegation visited our factory, we hosted a dinner for them at the best restaurant in town.
records.zomi: Sumbawl pawl in i factory a veh uh ciangin khuapi-a an zuakna dawl hoih pen ah nitak an i bawl sak hi.

records.english: You may want to tell your guests that the water is off in the mornings.
records.zomi: Zingsang ciangin tui kitan hi, ci-in na khualte na gen nuam kha ding hi.

records.english: Does anyone in the staff room drink coffee, or is it all green tea?
records.zomi: Nasemte' khan ah kuamah in kawfi a dawn hiam, tea eng bek ahi hiam?

records.english: Kids, you might not like the food at camp, but try at least one bite of everything.
records.zomi: Naupangte, camp-a an na deih kei kha ding uh hi, ahi zongin khempeuh vei khat bek zongin liim un.

records.english: Why does the school serve fish on Fridays?
records.zomi: Bang hangin sang in Laithai ni ciangin nga a pia hiam?

records.english: The cook said it's because the market has the freshest fish that day.
records.zomi: Tua ni-in zuakna mun ah nga thak pen a om ahih manin, ci-in an huannu in a gen hi.

records.english: Our team leader told us he had stopped eating sugar to stay awake in the afternoons.
records.zomi: I pawl makaipa in nitak lam a khanglo den nadingin sugar a ne nawn kei hi, hong ci hi.

records.english: My manager told me she can't think clearly before her morning coffee.
records.zomi: Ka manager in a zingsang kawfi a dawn ma-in siangtak takin a ngaihsun thei kei hi, hong ci hi.

records.english: Is it possible to order a meal without meat at the staff dinner?
records.zomi: Nasemte' nitak an ah sa om lo an sap theih ding hiam?

records.english: My cousin, who's a chef, says the hardest customers to cook for are other chefs.
records.zomi: An huanpa-a na a sem ka sanggam in an huanpa dangte adingin huan a haksa pen hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Could the kitchen make a version without peanuts for the new boy in our class?
records.zomi: I kilasi-a pasal naupang thak adingin anbuk in bekang om lo khat a bawl thei ding hiam?

records.english: Let's eat outside today instead of at our desks.
records.zomi: Tuni-in i dawhkan ah hi lo-in polam ah an ne ni.

records.english: Using a small lunch box with sections, I can pack a little of everything my son likes.
records.zomi: Khen tuam om sun an bawm neu khat zang-in ka tapa' deih khempeuh tawmno ciat ka thun thei hi.

records.english: What kind of snacks do the students like best at the school shop?
records.zomi: Sang dawl ah sangnaupangte in nek ding neu bang a deih pen uh hiam?

records.english: Our office has a fridge shelf just for people who don't eat meat, so that nothing gets mixed up.
records.zomi: Kuamah a kihel loh nadingin i office ah sa ne lo mite ading khal bawm dawh khat a om hi.

records.english: Cooking for a whole office means you can never please everyone.
records.zomi: Office bup adingin an huan in mi khempeuh na lungdamsak ngei lo ding hi.

records.english: Do you prefer eating with your coworkers or alone at your desk?
records.zomi: Na nasem lawmte tawh an ne na deih zaw hiam, na dawhkan ah nangma' bek hiam?

records.english: With my coworkers, because it's the only time we talk about anything except work.
records.zomi: Ka nasem lawmte tawh, nasep thu hi lo thu dang i kikum hun bek ahih manin.

records.english: Doesn't your husband get bored of eating the same sandwich every day?
records.zomi: Na pasal ni simin sandwich kibang mah a nek a lungkia kei hiam?

records.english: You two can choose the restaurant for the team lunch, since you're the newest.
records.zomi: Note nih na thak pen uh ahih manin pawl sun an adingin an zuakna dawl na teel thei uh hi.

records.english: The builders like their tea very sweet, so the stall owner adds three spoons of sugar.
records.zomi: Inn lamte in a tea uh a khum mahmah a deih uh ahih manin dawl neipa in sugar kawm thum a koih hi.

records.english: What do you usually eat for lunch at work?
records.zomi: Nasepna ah sun an-in bang na ne zel hiam?

records.english: Whatever I cooked the night before, usually rice and vegetables.
records.zomi: A zan ma-a ka huan bangbang, a tam zaw buh leh anteh.

records.english: My grandfather, who worked on the railway, still wants his rice with a fried egg on top.
records.zomi: Meileng lampi ah na a sem ngei ka pu in a buh tungah aktui kikang a deih lai hi.

records.english: How do the camp cooks manage so many picky eaters?
records.zomi: Camp an huante in an teel mi tampi bangci-in a kem uh hiam?

records.english: The canteen asked us to vote for our favorite meals, and noodle soup won easily.
records.zomi: Canteen in i an deih pen vote dingin hong ngen a, an-ngum an-tui in a zo baih hi.

records.english: We really do want the canteen to offer more fresh fruit and fewer fried snacks.
records.zomi: Canteen in singgah thak tam zaw leh nek ding kikang tawm zaw a piak ding i deih taktak hi.

records.english: Since I started working nights, I can't eat anything heavy before my shift.
records.zomi: Zan nasep ka sep kipat pan ka nasep hun ma-in a gik bangmah ka ne thei kei hi.

records.english: My tastes changed completely after a year of working in a restaurant kitchen.
records.zomi: An zuakna dawl anbuk ah kum khat na ka sep khit ciangin ka an deih dan a kikhel kim hi.

records.english: There might be a vegetarian option, but you'd better ask the organizers.
records.zomi: Sa om lo an a om kha ding hi, ahi zongin a vaihawmte na dong zaw ding hi.

records.english: Who keeps finishing the office milk without buying more?
records.zomi: Kua in office nawi a beisak den a, a thak a lei kei hiam?

records.english: The farm workers prefer a big breakfast because lunch is often late in the fields.
records.zomi: Lo-a sun an a nun zel ahih manin lo nasemte in zingsang an lian a deih zaw uh hi.

records.english: My aunt, who is a nurse, says she eats whatever is quickest between patients.
records.zomi: Nurse-a na a sem ka ni in damlote kikal ah a manlang pen bangbang ka ne hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Our school cook remembers which children hate onions and leaves them off their plates.
records.zomi: I sang an huannu in lothaang a huat naupangte a phawk a, a kuang uh ah a koih kei hi.

records.english: The night-shift workers asked for hot soup instead of sandwiches, and the manager agreed.
records.zomi: Zan nasemte in sandwich sangin an-tui lum a ngen uh a, manager in a lungkim hi.

records.english: The chef said that customers in the city prefer their food less spicy than people in the villages.
records.zomi: Khuapi-a van leite in khua-a mite sangin a hai tawm zaw a deih uh hi, ci-in an huanpa in a gen hi.

records.english: My daughter eats the school lunch without complaint, but at home she's very fussy.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in sang sun an phunsan lo-in a ne a, ahi zongin inn ah a teel mahmah hi.

records.english: When I asked the trainees what they wanted for the farewell lunch, every one of them said pizza.
records.zomi: Kikhenna sun an adingin bang a deih uh hiam kisinte ka dot ciangin khempeuh in pizza a ci uh hi.

records.english: My classmate from the north told me that she had never tasted fresh fish before university.
records.zomi: Saklam pan ka kilasi lawm in sangpi a kah ma-in nga thak a liim ngei kei hi, hong ci hi.

records.english: Spicy food helps me stay awake during long night shifts, or so I like to believe.
records.zomi: An hai in zan nasep sau laitakin hong khanglosak hi, ka um nuam hi.

records.english: If I had known how much the students disliked beans, I would have cooked something else for the fair.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte in be bangzah a huat uh hiam ka theih leh poai adingin an dang khat ka huan ding hi.

records.english: A survey was sent out to find out what students wanted on the new menu.
records.zomi: Menu thak ah sangnaupangte in bang a deih uh hiam theih nadingin dotna lai kikhak hi.

records.english: Is there anything the guest speaker would rather not eat?
records.zomi: Thugen khual in a nek nuam loh bangmah a om hiam?

records.english: My boss can't eat gluten, so whoever buys the office cake has to choose carefully.
records.zomi: Ka makaipa in gluten a ne thei kei ahih manin office cake a lei kua peuh in pilvang takin a teel kul hi.

records.english: Do you think the visiting engineers would enjoy local food, or should we order something familiar?
records.zomi: Hong veh engineer te in khua sung an a deih ding uh in na ngaihsun hiam, a theih uh an i sap ding hiam?

records.english: Food that reminds me of home helps me feel less lonely in the city.
records.zomi: Inn hong phawksak an in khuapi ah hong kikhawmlum tawm zawsak hi.

records.english: The doctor told me to eat smaller meals during the workday to avoid feeling tired.
records.zomi: A gim loh nadingin nasep ni-in an neu zaw ne dingin siavuan in hong gen hi.

records.english: I bring my own chili sauce to work in a small jar, because the canteen food is too plain for me.
records.zomi: Canteen an a lim lua kei ahih manin nasep ah bel neu khat sungah keimah' malcha an-tui ka tawi hi.

records.english: When I worked abroad, I missed rice so much that I cooked it in my hotel kettle.
records.zomi: Gamdang ah na ka sep lai-in buh ka ngaih lua ahih manin ka zinbuuk tui-ukbel sungah ka huan hi.

records.english: The new teacher was surprised that the students preferred rice porridge to bread for breakfast.
records.zomi: Saya thak in sangnaupangte in zingsang an-in moh sangin buh-an tui a deih zawk uh a lamdang sa hi.

records.english: The canteen labels every dish so that people with allergies can choose safely.
records.zomi: Kituak lohna nei mite in bitna takin a teel theih nadingun canteen in an khempeuh a min a koih hi.

records.english: Everyone, please write your meal choice next to your name for the conference dinner.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, kikhopna nitak an adingin na min kiang ah na an teelna gelh un.

records.english: Students, fill in this form so that the kitchen knows who has food allergies before the trip.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte, khualzinna ma-in an kituak lohna kua in a nei hiam anbuk in a theih theih nadingin hih lai dimsak un.

records.english: Before the team dinner, I asked everyone whether there was anything they couldn't eat.
records.zomi: Pawl nitak an ma-in mi khempeuh kiangah a nek theih loh bangmah a om hiam ka dong hi.

records.english: I love the food at my wife's office canteen more than the food at mine.
records.zomi: Ka canteen an sangin ka zi' office canteen an ka deih zaw hi.

records.english: My son's teacher told me that he refuses everything green at school lunch.
records.zomi: Ka tapa' saya in sang sun an ah eng khempeuh a nial hi, hong ci hi.

records.english: Working in a bakery made me lose my taste for sweet things.
records.zomi: Moh bawlna inn ah na ka sep manin a khum nek ka deih nawn kei hi.

records.english: When the new canteen started serving salads, hardly anyone in the factory ate them.
records.zomi: Canteen thak in salad a piak kipat ciangin factory-a mi tawmno bek in a ne uh hi.

records.english: Would you rather have the lunch meeting at the noodle shop or the café?
records.zomi: Sun an kikhopna an-ngum dawl ah na deih zaw hiam, cafe ah hiam?

records.english: Is the soup in the staff canteen usually spicy?
records.zomi: Nasemte' canteen an-tui a hai zel hiam?

records.english: A little, but there's always plain soup for anyone who asks.
records.zomi: Tawmno, ahi zongin a ngen kua peuh adingin an-tui hai lo a om tawntung hi.

records.english: In my first year at university, I lived on instant noodles and bananas.
records.zomi: Sangpi kum masa pen-in instant noodles leh banana bek tawh ka om hi.

records.english: Could you leave work early on Friday so that you can help me prepare for Grandma's birthday dinner?
records.zomi: Pi' pianni nitak an adingin hong huh theih nadingin Laithai ni ciangin nasep pan hun ma-in na pai khia thei ding hiam?

records.english: The harvest meal was cooked by the workers' families and eaten in the barn.
records.zomi: Buh lak an pen nasemte' innkuante in a huan uh a, buh inn sungah kine hi.

records.english: A newspaper wrote a story about our family's festival meal.
records.zomi: Thuthak lai khat in i innkuan pawi an thu tangthu a gelh hi.

records.english: Why does your family fill the rice jar to the top before the New Year begins?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Kum Thak a kipat ma-in na innkuan in buh bel a dimsak uh hiam?

records.english: My father says it means we'll have more than enough in the coming year.
records.zomi: Kum hong ding ah a cin sangin i nei ding hi, cihna ahi hi, ci-in ka pa in a gen hi.

records.english: When my brother started working nights, we moved our family meal from dinner to breakfast.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal zan nasep a sep kipat ciangin i innkuan an nek khawm nitak an pan zingsang an ah i kituah hi.

records.english: My sister wrote all the family recipes in a notebook before she moved away for work.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu in nasep adingin a pem ma-in innkuan an huan dan khempeuh notebook khat ah a gelh hi.

records.english: Using the old stone grinder that belonged to my great-grandmother, we made the spice paste for the feast.
records.zomi: Ka pi' nu' suang an-lim sumna lui zang-in poai adingin an-lim-nah a sum i bawl hi.

records.english: My cousin opened a café that serves our grandmother's noodles, and now people queue in the street.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam in i pi' an-ngum a zuak cafe khat a hong a, tu-in mite lampi ah a kizom uh hi.

records.english: The children aren't allowed to leave the table until the eldest has finished eating.
records.zomi: Upa pen in a nek a zawh ma-in naupangte dawhkan a paisan thei kei uh hi.

records.english: Let's cook the whole meal together this year, so that the young ones learn how it's done.
records.zomi: Naupang neute in bangci-in a kibawl hiam a sin theih nadingun tu kum an bup khawm-in huan ni.

records.english: We eat together as a family on Sunday evenings, when nobody has to work.
records.zomi: Kuamah in na a sep kul loh Nipini nitak simin innkuan-in an i ne khawm hi.

records.english: There's a chance the whole family can't come this year, because two of my cousins have exams.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nih in sitna a neih uh ahih manin tu kum innkuan bup a hong thei kei kha ding uh hi.

records.english: My aunt makes us all wear our traditional clothes for the New Year meal, even the youngest.
records.zomi: Ka ni in Kum Thak an adingin a neu pen dong i khempeuh i ngeina puan hong silhsak hi.

records.english: Having worked in restaurants for years, my uncle still insists that nothing beats his mother's cooking.
records.zomi: Kum tampi an zuakna dawl ah na a sep khit ciangin ka pa neu in a nu' an huan sangin a hoih zaw om lo hi, a ci den hi.

records.english: The company sent every employee home with a box of the traditional festival sweets.
records.zomi: Company in nasem khempeuh ngeina pawi a khum neu bawm khat tawh inn ah a ciahsak hi.

records.english: You two can set the long table, and the rest of you can bring the chairs from the school.
records.zomi: Note nih in dawhkan sau na bawl thei uh a, a dangte in sang pan tutnate na tawi thei uh hi.

records.english: If the train is on time, I could still make it home for the Christmas lunch.
records.zomi: Meileng a hun takah a tun leh Christmas sun an adingin inn ka tung thei lai ding hi.

records.english: Do you still eat with your family every evening, now that you have a job?
records.zomi: Tu-in nasep na neih manin na innkuan tawh nitak simin an na ne lai hiam?

records.english: Not every evening, but I never miss Sunday lunch.
records.zomi: Nitak simin hi lo hi, ahi zongin Nipini sun an ka mansuah ngei kei hi.

records.english: For a school project, my daughter interviewed her grandmother about the dishes our family cooks for festivals.
records.zomi: Sang project adingin ka tanu in i innkuan in pawi adingin a huan ante thu a pi kiangah a dong hi.

records.english: What does your family eat after a wedding?
records.zomi: Kiteenna khit ciangin na innkuan in bang a ne uh hiam?

records.english: A big pot of beef stew, which the uncles cook outside over a fire.
records.zomi: Pa neute in polam mei tungah a huan bawngsa an-tui beel lian khat.

records.english: My husband had the old family table repaired so that all twenty of us could sit together again.
records.zomi: I sawmnih in khawm-a i tut thei kik nadingin ka pasal in innkuan dawhkan lui a bawl kik sak hi.

records.english: In our home economics class, we cooked the traditional festival bread of each student's family.
records.zomi: I inn kepna kilasi ah sangnaupang khat ciat' innkuan pawi moh i bawl hi.

records.english: My boss let me leave the market stall early to help cook for my grandfather's memorial meal.
records.zomi: Ka pu' phawkna an huan huh dingin ka makaipa in zuakna dawl pan hun ma-in hong paisak hi.

records.english: Every year our office closes early on the day before the festival so that staff can travel home for the family meal.
records.zomi: Nasemte in innkuan an adingin inn a ciah theih nadingun kum simin pawi ma ni-in i office hun ma-in kikhak hi.

records.english: The old men in our village say that the festival rice tastes better when it's cooked by the whole family.
records.zomi: I khua pasal upate in innkuan bup in a huan ciangin pawi buh a lim zaw hi, a ci uh hi.

records.english: I'd love to learn my grandmother's way of smoking the meat before she gets too old to show me.
records.zomi: Ka pi a upat lua-in a etsak zawh ma-in sa khiang dan ka sin ka deih mahmah hi.

records.english: Will you be home for the New Year meal, or do you have to work?
records.zomi: Kum Thak an adingin inn ah na om ding hiam, na sep kul hiam?

records.english: My manager gave me the day off, so I'll be there by noon.
records.zomi: Ka manager in ni khat khawl hong pia ahih manin sun ma-in ka tung ding hi.

records.english: Students, bring a dish that your family cooks for special occasions, and tell the class its story.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte, na innkuan in ni tuam adingin a huan an khat tawi unla a tangthu kilasi kiangah gen un.

records.english: Does your uncle's restaurant still serve his mother's dishes?
records.zomi: Na pa neu' an zuakna dawl in a nu' ante a pia lai hiam?

records.english: Is it possible to take a day off for my family's harvest feast?
records.zomi: Ka innkuan' buh lak poai adingin ni khat ka khawl thei ding hiam?

records.english: Studying abroad, I missed our family's Sunday rice and pork more than anything else.
records.zomi: Gamdang ah sang ka kah lai-in i innkuan' Nipini buh leh vok sa na dang khempeuh sangin ka ngaih pen hi.

records.english: My colleagues brought their own family's festival dishes to share at the staff lunch.
records.zomi: Ka nasem lawmte in nasemte' sun an ah kihawm dingin amau innkuan pawi ante a tawi uh hi.

records.english: My grandmother's chicken curry is the dish all the grandchildren ask for when they come home from the city.
records.zomi: Ka pi' aksa curry pen khuapi pan inn a ciah ciangun tu-te khempeuh in a ngen an ahi hi.

records.english: My first paycheck paid for the meat at our family's Christmas meal, and my parents were very proud.
records.zomi: Ka kha man masa pen in i innkuan Christmas an sa man a pia a, ka nu leh ka pa a kisaktheih mahmah uh hi.

records.english: Grandpa said that when he was a schoolboy, the festival meal was the only time he ate meat all year.
records.zomi: Sangnaupang a hih lai-in pawi an bek-in kum khat sungin sa a ne hi, ci-in Pu in a gen hi.

records.english: My brother and I cooked the family festival meal for the first time while our parents were working abroad.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa gamdang ah na a sep laitakin ka sanggam pasal leh kei innkuan pawi an a masa pen-in i huan hi.

records.english: Our teacher had us write a short essay about the meal our family eats on the most important day of the year.
records.zomi: I saya in kum sung ni thupi pen-a i innkuan nek an thu laigelh tom khat hong gelhsak hi.

records.english: My father always brought home the best fish from the market for our Friday dinners.
records.zomi: Ka pa in Laithai ni nitak an adingin zuakna mun pan nga hoih pen inn ah a tawi tawntung hi.

records.english: The smell of the festival soup brings back every New Year of my childhood.
records.zomi: Pawi an-tui gim in ka naupan lai Kum Thak khempeuh hong phawksak kik hi.

records.english: The cooking teacher said that family recipes are a kind of history that is written in food.
records.zomi: Innkuan an huan dante pen an tawh kigelh tangthu ahi hi, ci-in an huan saya in a gen hi.

records.english: Our teacher told us that sharing food is one of the oldest ways people show friendship.
records.zomi: An kihawm pen mite in kilawmna a lak nadan lui pen khat ahi hi, ci-in i saya in hong gen hi.

records.english: A recipe for my great-grandmother's soup was found in an old school notebook in the attic.
records.zomi: Ka pi' nu' an-tui huan dan inn tung khan-a sang notebook lui khat sungah kimu hi.

records.english: My mother-in-law made me practice the festival dumplings for weeks before the family gathering.
records.zomi: Innkuan kikhopna ma-in ka sungnu in kal tampi sung pawi sambuk hong kisinsak hi.

records.english: Our school holds a meal every year where each family brings one traditional dish.
records.zomi: I sang in kum simin innkuan khat ciat in ngeina an khat a tawi uh an khat a bawl hi.

records.english: I record Grandma on my phone while she cooks, because she never measures anything.
records.zomi: Pi in bangmah a teh ngei loh manin a huan laitakin ka phone tawh ka la hi.

records.english: We might have to move the family dinner to Saturday, because Dad's shift has changed.
records.zomi: Pa' nasep hun a kikhel ahih manin innkuan nitak an Kiginni ah i kituah kul kha ding hi.

records.english: Who cooks the festival rice now that your father has retired from teaching?
records.zomi: Na pa hilhna pan a khawl khit ciangin pawi buh kua in a huan hiam?

records.english: Will the factory give us a holiday for the festival this year?
records.zomi: Tu kum factory in pawi adingin tawlngakni hong pia ding hiam?

records.english: What dish from home would you cook for your colleagues?
records.zomi: Na nasem lawmte adingin na inn pan an bang na huan ding hiam?

records.english: My mother told me that her grandmother cooked the same chicken soup for every wedding in the village.
records.zomi: Ka nu' pi in khua sung kiteenna khempeuh ah aksa an-tui kibang mah a huan hi, ci-in ka nu in hong gen hi.

records.english: Could you show my students how to make the rice cakes we eat at harvest time?
records.zomi: Buh lak hun-a i nek buh moh bawl dan ka sangnaupangte na etsak thei ding hiam?

records.english: This year we ate the family meal in the school hall, because our house was too small.
records.zomi: I inn a neu lua ahih manin tu kum innkuan an pen sang inn lian ah i ne hi.

records.english: Everyone, please sit down — Grandpa wants to say a few words before we eat.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, tu un — i nek ma-in Pu in kammal tawmno a gen nuam hi.

records.english: Can I bring my colleague from work to our family dinner, since she can't go home this year?
records.zomi: Tu kum ka nasem lawm inn a ciah thei kei ahih manin i innkuan nitak an ah ka paipih thei ding hiam?

records.english: My grandfather had his old recipe book copied so that each of us could take one to university.
records.zomi: Ka pu in i khat ciat in sangpi ah i tawi theih nadingin a an huan dan laibu lui a suaksak kik hi.

records.english: Kids, put your books away and help carry the dishes, because the whole family is here.
records.zomi: Naupangte, innkuan bup hih ah a om uh ahih manin na laibu uh koih unla kuangte puak huh un.

records.english: My teacher told me that she was proud of how hard I'd worked this year.
records.zomi: Tu kum hanciam taka ka sep manin ka tung ah a kisaktheih hi, ci-in ka saya in hong gen hi.

records.english: Kids, let's make a card for Mrs. Lun, because she's leaving our school.
records.zomi: Naupangte, Mrs. Lun i sang a paisan ding ahih manin a adingin card khat bawl ni.

records.english: Our team was told that the project we'd worked on for a year had been canceled.
records.zomi: Kum khat sung i sep project kiphiat khin hi, ci-in i pawl kihilh hi.

records.english: Losing the school football final hurt, but the coach said he had never been prouder of us.
