records.zomi: Sang football tawpna kimawlna i zo kei in hong natsak hi, ahi zongin coach in hih bang a kisaktheih ngei kei hi, a ci hi.

records.english: My uncle was heartbroken when his apprentice left to work for another garage.
records.zomi: A nasep kisinpa mawtaw bawlna dang ah na sem dingin a pai ciangin ka pa neu a lungtang a kitam hi.

records.english: Is it normal to feel sad after you finish school?
records.zomi: Sang na zawh khit ciangin dah pen a hih ding bang ahi hiam?

records.english: Seeing my students graduate makes all the hard years worth it.
records.zomi: Ka sangnaupangte sang a zawh uh ka muh in kum haksa khempeuh a manphatsak hi.

records.english: The night I lost my job, my children made me dinner and told me jokes until I laughed.
records.zomi: Ka nasep ka mansuah zan-in ka tate in nitak an hong huan sak uh a, ka nui dong nuihza thu hong gen uh hi.

records.english: We sent the retiring headmaster a video from all his former students so that he'd know how much he meant to us.
records.zomi: Nasep a khawl sang makaipa' adingin amah a thupi dan a theih theih nadingin a sangnaupang lui khempeuh pan video khat i khak hi.

records.english: Are you happy in your new job?
records.zomi: Na nasep thak ah na lungdam hiam?

records.english: Proud as I was of my friend's new job abroad, I couldn't help feeling a little left behind.
records.zomi: Ka lawm' gamdang nasep thak tungah ka kisaktheih mahmah hangin tawmno kinusia bangin ka kisa hi.

records.english: How did you feel when you got your first promotion?
records.zomi: Na kaisanna masa pen na ngah ciangin bangci-in na kisa hiam?

records.english: Happy, but also nervous, because now I was in charge of my old friends.
records.zomi: Ka lungdam hi, ahi zongin ka lau zong hi, tu-in ka lawm luite' makaipa ka suak ahih manin.

records.english: My sister was so happy about her new job that she couldn't sleep the night before.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu a nasep thak tungah a lungdam lua ahih manin a zan ma-in a ihmu thei kei hi.

records.english: There's a chance you'll get the next job, so don't give up.
records.zomi: Nasep zom pen na ngah kha ding ahih manin nusia kei in.

records.english: Hearing that the school had won the national prize, the old teachers wept with joy.
records.zomi: Sang in gam laksap a ngah thu a zak ciangun saya upate lungdamna tawh a kap uh hi.

records.english: Leaving the shop my grandfather built was the saddest thing I've ever had to do.
records.zomi: Ka pu' lam dawl paisan pen ka sep ngei kul na dah pen ahi hi.

records.english: You've been quiet all morning — is something wrong?
records.zomi: Zingsang bup na dai hi — bangmah a om hiam?

records.english: The factory is closing, and I'll lose my job at the end of the month.
records.zomi: Factory kikhak ding a, kha tawp ciangin ka nasep ka mansuah ding hi.

records.english: The students were so happy with their results that they danced in the corridor.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte in a ciamte uh a lungdam lua uh ahih manin lampi khan ah a lam uh hi.

records.english: What made you happiest about your first year of teaching?
records.zomi: Na hilhna kum masa pen-in bang in hong lungdamsak pen hiam?

records.english: Seeing a boy who couldn't read in September reading a whole book by June.
records.zomi: September kha-in lai a sim thei lo pasal naupang khat June kha-in laibu bup a sim ka muh.

records.english: The day our little restaurant got its first good review, my wife framed it and hung it by the door.
records.zomi: I an zuakna dawl neu in a ngaihsutna hoih masa pen a ngah ni-in ka zi in bawngkhawng ah a koih a, kongkhak kiang ah a khai hi.

records.english: Would it help if I took your shift tomorrow, so that you can rest?
records.zomi: Na tawlngak theih nadingin zingciang na nasep hun ka laih leh a huh ding hiam?

records.english: My boss made me take a week off after my mother died, and I'm grateful she did.
records.zomi: Ka nu a sih khit ciangin ka makaipa in kal khat hong khawlsak a, a sep manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: My father cried when he saw my name on the list of university students.
records.zomi: Sangpi sangnaupang list tungah ka min a muh ciangin ka pa a kap hi.

records.english: Don't send any emails when you're upset; wait until tomorrow.
records.zomi: Na lungkham ciangin email khak kei in; zingciang dong ngak in.

records.english: My colleagues made me laugh all day, even though it was my last day at the company.
records.zomi: Company ah ka ni nunung pen ahi hangin ka nasem lawmte in ni bup hong nuisak uh hi.

records.english: What's wrong with Daniel?
records.zomi: Daniel bang a buai hiam?

records.english: My first paycheck made me so happy that I bought cakes for my whole family.
records.zomi: Ka kha man masa pen in hong lungdamsak lua ahih manin ka innkuan bup adingin cake ka lei hi.

records.english: You might feel better if you talk to someone at the student counseling office.
records.zomi: Sangnaupang thuhilhna office ah kuamah tawh na kiho leh na lungsim a nuam zaw kha ding hi.

records.english: Could you tell the team the good news yourself?
records.zomi: Thu hoih pawl kiangah nangma' mah in na gen thei ding hiam?

records.english: My husband lost his job last spring, and for months he barely smiled.
records.zomi: Ka pasal spring nung in a nasep a mansuah a, kha tampi sung a nui tawm mahmah hi.

records.english: Please don't cry — you can try the exam again next year.
records.zomi: Kap kei in — kum hong ding ciangin sitna na sit kik thei hi.

records.english: Grandpa said that the happiest day of his working life was when he paid off the farm.
records.zomi: A nasep nuntak sung-a ni lungdam pen pen lo leitawi a lohsak bei ni ahi hi, ci-in Pu in a gen hi.

records.english: It was a sad day for everyone when our favorite teacher retired.
records.zomi: I saya deih pen a khawl ni pen mi khempeuh adingin ni dah ahi hi.

records.english: Can I go home early, since I haven't been feeling well since I heard the news?
records.zomi: Thu ka zak pan ka dam kei ahih manin hun ma-in inn ah ka ciah thei ding hiam?

records.english: The whole office went quiet when the manager told us about the job cuts.
records.zomi: Manager in nasep kiphiat ding thu a gen ciangin office bup a dai hi.

records.english: Failing my driving test for the second time left me close to tears.
records.zomi: Ka mawtaw mawng sitna vei nihna ka zo lo in hong kap dek sak hi.

records.english: Let's call Mom on the video call, so that she can see your graduation gown.
records.zomi: Nu in na sang zawhna puan a muh theih nadingin video call tawh Nu sam ni.

records.english: What a lovely surprise to see all my old students at the party!
records.zomi: Pawi ah ka sangnaupang lui khempeuh muh a lamdang nuam mahmah hi!

records.english: I had the photo of my first class enlarged and hung it in my classroom.
records.zomi: Ka kilasi masa pen lim ka khaisak lian a, ka kilasi ah ka khai hi.

records.english: I wrote down three good things that happened at work every evening, and slowly I started to feel better.
records.zomi: Nitak simin nasepna-a na hoih thum ka gelh a, zawi takin ka lungsim a nuam kipan hi.

records.english: Don't be too hard on yourself — everyone fails an exam at some point.
records.zomi: Na tung ah na haksa lua kei in — mi khempeuh in hun khatpeuh ah sitna a zo kei uh hi.

records.english: The office felt empty after the oldest member of staff retired.
records.zomi: Nasem upa pen a khawl khit ciangin office a awng bang hi.

records.english: Do you ever miss working at the hospital?
records.zomi: Zato-a na sep na ngaih ngei hiam?

records.english: My grandmother was overjoyed when I told her I'd become a teacher like her.
records.zomi: Amah bangin saya ka suak hi, ka cih ciangin ka pi a lungdam mahmah hi.

records.english: It's okay to feel sad when a job doesn't work out.
records.zomi: Nasep khat a hoih kei ciangin dah pen a hoih hi.

records.english: Have you heard that Thomas got into medical school?
records.zomi: Thomas siavuan sang ah a lut hi, cih na za hiam?

records.english: Shall we go out to celebrate your new job?
records.zomi: Na nasep thak poai bawl dingin i pai khia ding hiam?

records.english: Ask your teacher for help if something at school is making you unhappy.
records.zomi: Sang ah na khat in hong lungkham sak leh na saya kiangah huhna ngen in.

records.english: When I opened the letter and saw that I'd passed, I screamed so loudly that the neighbors came running.
records.zomi: Lai ka hon a, ka zo hi, cih ka muh ciangin ging sang lua-in ka sam ahih manin inn vengte hong tai uh hi.

records.english: My colleague told me she'd been crying in the bathroom, and I didn't know what to say.
records.zomi: Ka nasem lawm in ek inn ah a kap hi, hong ci a, bang ka gen ding hiam ka thei kei hi.

records.english: I got the job!
records.zomi: Nasep ka ngah hi!

records.english: No one is allowed to make fun of a classmate who cries at our school.
records.zomi: I sang ah kap kilasi lawm khat kuamah in a nuihsat thei kei hi.

records.english: My mother says that being a nurse means sharing both the happiest and the saddest days of people's lives.
records.zomi: Nurse suak pen mite' nuntak sung-a ni lungdam pen leh ni dah pen kihawm cihna ahi hi, ci-in ka nu in a gen hi.

records.english: The news that our school would close made the whole village sad.
records.zomi: I sang kikhak ding thu in khua bup a dahsak hi.

records.english: Why are the children so excited today?
records.zomi: Bang hangin tuni-in naupangte a lungdam mahmah uh hiam?

records.english: It's the last day of school before the holidays.
records.zomi: Tawlngakni ma sang ni nunung pen ahi hi.

records.english: When my business finally made a profit, I took my parents out for dinner.
records.zomi: Ka sumbawlna in a tawp-in phatna a ngah ciangin ka nu leh ka pa nitak an ne dingin ka paipih hi.

records.english: Stop worrying about the deadline — we'll finish it together tonight.
records.zomi: Hun ciang lungkham khawl in — tu zanin khawm in i zo ding hi.

records.english: Hearing that the bank was cutting jobs, my uncle started looking for work straight away.
records.zomi: Bank in nasepte a tawmsak ding a zak ciangin ka pa neu in pahtakin nasep a zong kipan hi.

records.english: How do you stay calm before an important exam?
records.zomi: Sitna thupi ma-in bangci-in na lungsim na daisak hiam?

records.english: I go for a walk and remind myself that I've studied enough.
records.zomi: Ka kawikawi a, ka kisin cing khin hi, ci-in ka kiphawksak hi.

records.english: Is it safe to work at the machine without gloves?
records.zomi: Gloves om lo-in machine ah na sep a bitna hiam?

records.english: My boss said not to worry about the mistake, but I couldn't stop thinking about it all weekend.
records.zomi: Ka makaipa in khialhna lungkham lo dingin hong gen a, ahi zongin kal tawp bup ka ngaihsun tawp thei kei hi.

records.english: Why are you so worried about the inspection?
records.zomi: Bang hangin enkaknate tungah na lungkham mahmah hiam?

records.english: Because the inspector could close the restaurant if the kitchen isn't clean enough.
records.zomi: Anbuk a siang lua kei leh enkaktu in an zuakna dawl a khaksak thei ahih manin.

records.english: A cracked beam was discovered in the classroom ceiling, and the children were moved to the hall.
records.zomi: Kilasi inn tung sungah sing kikek khat kimu a, naupangte inn lian ah kipemsak uh hi.

records.english: Are you worried about losing your job?
records.zomi: Na nasep mansuah ding na lungkham hiam?

records.english: A little, because the company has already let ten people go.
records.zomi: Tawmno, company in mi sawm a paisak khin ahih manin.

records.english: When the alarm went off in the middle of the exam, half the class thought it was a real fire.
records.zomi: Sitna kimlai-in alarm a ging ciangin kilasi a kim in mei taktak a kang hi, a sa uh hi.

records.english: During my first week alone in the shop, every unfamiliar customer made me nervous.
records.zomi: Dawl ah ka bek ka om kal masa pen-in van lei theih lo khempeuh in hong lausak hi.

records.english: There's a chance the harvest will fail if the rain doesn't come soon.
records.zomi: Guah pahtakin a zuk kei leh buh a phat kei kha ding hi.

records.english: Students mustn't go near the science room until the gas leak has been fixed.
records.zomi: Gas a puakna a kibawl kik ma-in sangnaupangte science khan a nai thei kei ding uh hi.

records.english: My daughter told me she was scared of the older boys at her new school, so I spoke to her teacher.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in a sang thak-a pasal naupang upa zawte a lau hi, hong ci ahih manin a saya tawh ka kiho hi.

records.english: The wages hadn't been paid for two months, and the workers were worried about their rent.
records.zomi: Kha nih sung kha man kipia nai lo a, nasemte in a inn man uh a lungkham uh hi.

records.english: The nurse told my mother that the operation had gone well, and we all breathed again.
records.zomi: Nurse in khamna a hoih hi, ci-in ka nu kiangah a gen a, i khempeuh i huih i ngah kik hi.

records.english: My manager told me she had been just as nervous at her first conference.
records.zomi: Ka manager in amah zong a kikhopna lian masa pen-in a lau bang mah hi, hong ci hi.

records.english: My worst fear as a new teacher was that the students wouldn't listen to me.
records.zomi: Saya thak ka hih lai-in ka lau pen sangnaupangte in ka thu a ngai kei ding uh cih ahi hi.

records.english: My hands were shaking so much on my first day as a nurse that I dropped a tray of medicine.
records.zomi: Nurse ka hih ni masa pen-in ka khut a ling lua ahih manin zatui kuang khat ka khia hi.

records.english: The teacher had us write our worries on paper and put them in a box, which made us feel lighter.
records.zomi: Saya in i lungkhamnate lai tungah hong gelhsak a, bawm sungah hong koihsak a, i lungsim a zang hi.

records.english: Can someone come with me to see the manager, since I'm too nervous to go alone?
records.zomi: Kei bek-a pai dingin ka lau lua ahih manin manager mu dingin kuamah in hong zui thei ding hiam?

records.english: Please don't tell my parents about the warning letter yet.
records.zomi: Vaulna lai thu ka nu leh ka pa kiangah gen nai kei in.

records.english: Could you check my report before I send it to the director?
records.zomi: Director kiangah ka khak ma-in ka report na en sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: According to the school counselor, many young children are afraid of the dark at some point.
records.zomi: Sang thuhilhpa' gen dan in naupang neu tampi in hun khatpeuh ah khuamial a lau uh hi.

records.english: Should I tell my boss that I'm struggling, or will he think I can't do the job?
records.zomi: Ka haksat thu ka makaipa kiangah ka gen ding hiam, ka sem zo lo hi, a sa ding hiam?

records.english: Try not to panic if the computer freezes during the test; just raise your hand.
records.zomi: Sitna laitakin computer a khawl leh lau kei in; na khut khing bek in.

records.english: The night before my first shift at the hospital, I dreamed that I'd forgotten everything I'd learned.
records.zomi: Zato-a ka nasep hun masa pen zan ma-in ka sin khempeuh ka mangngilh ka mang hi.

records.english: Driving the bus full of children on the icy road kept me on edge the whole morning.
records.zomi: Lampi tuikhal tungah naupangte a dim bus ka mawng in zingsang bup hong lausak hi.

records.english: You've hardly said a word since we moved — what's bothering you about the new school?
records.zomi: I pem pan na kiho tawm mahmah hi — sang thak thu-ah bang in hong lungkham sak hiam?

records.english: That nobody will want to sit with me at lunch.
records.zomi: Sun an hun-in kuamah in ka kiang ah a tut nuam kei ding uh hi, cih.

records.english: Are you afraid of making mistakes in front of the class?
records.zomi: Kilasi mai ah na khialh ding na lau hiam?

records.english: There were rumors that the factory might close, and nobody could sleep properly for weeks.
records.zomi: Factory kikhak kha ding thu a kigen a, kal tampi sung kuamah a ihmu siang kei uh hi.

records.english: I'm so nervous about my job interview that I couldn't eat breakfast.
records.zomi: Ka nasep dotna ka lau lua ahih manin zingsang an ka ne zo kei hi.

records.english: Don't worry if you forget a word during the presentation; just keep going.
records.zomi: Presentation laitakin kammal khat na mangngilh leh lungkham kei in; zom den in.

records.english: Do you think the teacher will be angry that I lost my homework?
records.zomi: Ka inn-a sep ding ka mansuah manin saya a heh ding in na ngaihsun hiam?

records.english: Fishermen in our village worry more about the weather than about the price of fish.
records.zomi: I khua nga manmite in nga man sangin khua thu a lungkham zaw uh hi.

records.english: When I lost my phone with all my work contacts in it, I nearly panicked.
records.zomi: Ka nasep thu kizopte khempeuh a om ka phone ka mansuah ciangin ka lau dek hi.

records.english: Whatever happens at the interview, we'll be proud of you.
records.zomi: Dotna ah bang piang zongin nang tungah i kisaktheih ding hi.

records.english: Nobody is allowed to climb the ladder without someone holding it at our workshop.
records.zomi: I nasepna inn ah kuamah a len lo-in kuamah in kaplei a kah thei kei hi.

records.english: You might feel less anxious if you prepare your answers the night before.
records.zomi: A zan ma-in na dawnnate na bawl leh na lungkham tawm zaw kha ding hi.

records.english: Don't leave the patients alone while the power is off.
records.zomi: Meivak a kitan laitakin damlote a bek-in nusia kei in.

records.english: Our manager made us practice the fire drill twice so that nobody would panic in a real emergency.
records.zomi: Haksatna taktak ah kuamah a lau loh nadingin i manager in mei kat kisinna vei nih hong sem sak hi.

records.english: What if I fail and have to repeat the whole year?
records.zomi: Ka zo kei a, kum bup ka kah kik kul leh bang ka sem ding hiam?

records.english: Do you get nervous before you speak in meetings?
records.zomi: Kikhopna ah na gen ma-in na lau zel hiam?

records.english: We had the old wiring in the school checked, because the teachers were worried about fires.
records.zomi: Sayate in mei a lungkham uh ahih manin sang meivak khau luite i ensak hi.

records.english: What would we do if the shop had to close?
records.zomi: Dawl i khak kul leh bang i sem ding hiam?

records.english: The office was evacuated when smoke was seen coming from the basement.
records.zomi: Nuai lam khan pan meikhu a kimuh ciangin office pan mi khempeuh kipaikhiat sak hi.

records.english: Is it normal to feel this scared before your first day at a new job?
records.zomi: Nasep thak ah ni masa pen ma-in hih zah lau pen a hih ding bang ahi hiam?

records.english: My father used to worry that I'd never find a job with an art degree.
records.zomi: Lim gelh degree tawh nasep ka ngah ngei lo ding ci-in ka pa in a lungkham ngei hi.

records.english: My wife lies awake worrying about our children whenever they travel for work.
records.zomi: I tate nasep adingin a khualzin simun ka zi i tate lungkham-in a khanglo hi.

records.english: The results will be posted online at midnight, so I doubt I'll sleep tonight.
records.zomi: Ciamte zan lai ciangin online ah kikoih ding ahih manin tu zanin ka ihmu thei kei kha ding hi.

records.english: I might lose the scholarship if my grades drop again.
records.zomi: Ka ciamte a kiam kik leh ka scholarship ka mansuah kha ding hi.

records.english: Worrying about tomorrow won't change it, so get some sleep.
records.zomi: Zingciang thu lungkham in a khel kei ding ahih manin ihmu in.

records.english: My colleague says she checks the oven three times before she leaves the bakery, just in case.
records.zomi: Ka nasem lawm in a kisap kha leh ci-in moh bawlna inn a paisan ma-in oven vei thum a en hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Kids, there's nothing to be afraid of; the school nurse is very gentle.
records.zomi: Naupangte, lau ding bangmah om lo hi; sang nurse a nem mahmah hi.

records.english: Working on the roof of a six-story building terrified me during my first month as a builder.
records.zomi: Inn lampa ka hih kha masa pen-in dawl guk inn tung ah na sep in hong lausak mahmah hi.

records.english: My son was afraid to tell us that he'd been moved to a lower class.
records.zomi: Ka tapa kilasi niam zaw ah a kipemsak thu hong gen dingin a lau hi.

records.english: Let me drive you to the exam, so you don't have to worry about the bus.
records.zomi: Bus thu na lungkham kul loh nadingin sitna ah kong paipih ning.

records.english: The headmaster had every student's name painted on the wall so that they would feel they belonged.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte in kikhel a kisak theih nadingun sang makaipa in sangnaupang khempeuh' min bang tungah a gelh sak hi.

records.english: Students, nobody here is allowed to call themselves stupid — we all learn at different speeds.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte, hih ah kuamah in amah le amah a mawl hi, ci thei lo hi — i khempeuh hun tuam ciat-in i sin hi.

records.english: My daughter's teacher sent home a note saying how kind she had been to a new classmate.
records.zomi: Ka tanu' saya in kilasi lawm thak khat tung ah a hehpih dan gen-in inn ah lai hong khak hi.

records.english: You're getting faster at the cash register every day.
records.zomi: Ni simin sum la machine ah na manlang semsem hi.

records.english: The team was hit by three resignations in one month, but the ones who stayed grew closer.
records.zomi: Pawl pan kha khat sungin mi thum a khawl uh a, ahi zongin a om lai te a kinai zaw uh hi.

records.english: There's still time to improve your grade before the end of the term.
records.zomi: Term a tawp ma-in na ciamte bawl hoih nading hun a om lai hi.

records.english: The first sale at my little shop made me believe I'd made the right choice.
records.zomi: Ka dawl neu-a zuak masa pen in a dik ka teel hi, cih hong umsak hi.

records.english: Have you thought about asking your supervisor for more training?
records.zomi: Na enkaipa kiangah kisinna behlap ngen ding na ngaihsun ngei hiam?

records.english: My grandfather told me that he learned to read at sixty, so I have no excuse to stop now.
records.zomi: Ka pu in kum sawmguk ciangin lai sim a sin hi, hong ci ahih manin tu-in khawl ding hang ka nei kei hi.

records.english: My teacher wrote on my report that she believed I could become a doctor.
records.zomi: Ka saya in ka report tungah siavuan ka suak thei ding a um hi, ci-in a gelh hi.

records.english: My teacher's words still help me on bad days at work.
records.zomi: Ka saya' kammalte in nasepna-a ni hoih lo ciangin hong huh lai hi.

records.english: Keep sending applications; the right job is out there.
records.zomi: Ngetna lai khak den in; nasep a man pen a om hi.

records.english: My mentor told me that every good carpenter has ruined at least one table.
records.zomi: Sing seempa hoih khempeuh in dawhkan khat bek zong a suksia ngei hi, ci-in hong makaihpa in hong gen hi.

records.english: Please don't let one bad review make you stop baking.
records.zomi: Ngaihsutna hoih lo khat in moh bawl hong khawlsak kei hen.

records.english: My brother failed his apprenticeship exam twice and passed with top marks on the third try.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in a nasep kisinna sitna vei nih a zo kei a, vei thumna-in ciamte sang pen tawh a zo hi.

records.english: The trainee's confidence grew every week, and by the end of the month she was teaching others.
records.zomi: Kisinnu' muanna kal simin a khang a, kha tawp ciangin mi dangte a hilh khin hi.

records.english: No student should feel ashamed to ask for extra help.
records.zomi: Huhna behlap ngen ding sangnaupang kuamah a zahlak kul kei hi.

records.english: Don't give up on the course just because the first test went badly.
records.zomi: Sitna masa pen a hoih kei man bek-in kisinna nusia kei in.

records.english: When the harvest failed, the cooperative lent the farmers seeds so that they could plant again.
records.zomi: Buh a phat loh ciangin lo neite in a suan kik theih nadingun lo nei pawl in cil hong leitawi hi.

records.english: My first manager's encouragement was the reason I stayed in nursing.
records.zomi: Ka manager masa pen' hanthawnna in nursing ah hong omsak hi.

records.english: Will you come to watch my presentation, so that I can see a friendly face?
records.zomi: Mai lungdam khat ka muh theih nadingin ka presentation en dingin na hong pai ding hiam?

records.english: When the new school building was opened, the children who'd studied under a tree for years cheered.
records.zomi: Sang inn thak a kihon ciangin kum tampi sing nuai-a kisin naupangte a sam uh hi.

records.english: My aunt says that she kept the rejection letters from every publisher until her first book came out.
records.zomi: A laibu masa pen a suah dong lai suaksak khempeuh pan a nialna laite a kem hi, ci-in ka ni in a gen hi.

records.english: You might not get this job, but every interview makes you better at the next one.
records.zomi: Hih nasep na ngah kei kha ding hi, ahi zongin dotna khempeuh in a zom ah hong siamsak zaw hi.

records.english: Don't compare yourself with the others; compare yourself with who you were last year.
records.zomi: Mi dangte tawh kiteh kei in; kum bei-a na hihna tawh kiteh in.

records.english: You've done the hard part already; the rest is just practice.
records.zomi: A haksa tan na zo khin hi; a taang pen kisinna bek ahi hi.

records.english: My mother says she knew I'd be a teacher because I used to teach my dolls.
records.zomi: Ka naupang lim tawngte ka hilh zel ahih manin saya ka suak ding ka nu in a thei hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Hearing a former student say I'd changed her life made thirty years of teaching worthwhile.
records.zomi: Sangnaupang lui khat in ka nuntakna na khel hi, a cih ka zak in kum sawmthum hilhna a manphatsak hi.

records.english: Whatever the panel decides, you've already shown how much you've grown this year.
records.zomi: Khensatte in bang khensat zongin tu kum na khanna bangzah hiam na lak khin hi.

records.english: My boss said, "I'd rather you make a mistake while trying than do nothing."
records.zomi: Ka makaipa in, “Bangmah sep lo sangin hanciam kawm-a na khialh ka deih zaw hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: What would you tell a young person who's afraid to start their own business?
records.zomi: Amah' sumbawlna kipat lau khangno khat kiangah bang na gen ding hiam?

records.english: My father had my old exam papers framed, including the ones I failed, to remind me how far I'd come.
records.zomi: Bangzah gamla ka tung hiam hong phawksak nadingin ka pa in ka zawh loh te kihel-in ka sitna lai luite bawngkhawng ah a koih hi.

records.english: If you keep practicing like this, you could play in the school orchestra next year.
records.zomi: Hih bangin na kisin den leh kum hong ding ciangin sang la tumpawl ah na tum thei kha ding hi.

records.english: Let's look at what went well this week before we plan the next one.
records.zomi: A zom kal i gel ma-in hih kal bang a hoih hiam en masa ni.

records.english: Do you think I should apply for the manager's job?
records.zomi: Manager nasep ka ngen ding in na ngaihsun hiam?

records.english: Absolutely — you already do half of it without the title.
records.zomi: Ngen mahmah in — min om lo-in a kim khin na sem hi.

records.english: A new library was opened at the village school, and reading scores went up within a year.
records.zomi: Khua sang ah laibu inn thak kihong a, kum khat sungin lai sim ciamte a khang hi.

records.english: Every small step counts, especially in your first year at a new job.
records.zomi: Khe suan neu khempeuh a thupi hi, a tuam in nasep thak-a na kum masa pen-in.

records.english: Twenty companies said no before one finally offered me a job.
records.zomi: Company sawmnih in hong nial uh a, a tawp-in khat in nasep hong pia hi.

records.english: Is it too late to go back to school at forty?
records.zomi: Kum sawmli ciangin sang kah kik a nun lua hiam?

records.english: Not at all — my aunt did it at fifty-two and became a nurse.
records.zomi: Nun lua lo hi — ka ni kum sawmnga leh nih ciangin a kah a, nurse a suak hi.

records.english: Our small business nearly failed in the first year, but my wife kept telling me to hold on.
records.zomi: I sumbawlna neu kum masa pen-in a puk dek a, ahi zongin ka zi in hanciam den dingin hong gen den hi.

records.english: Would it help to talk to someone who's done the same course?
records.zomi: Kisinna kibang mah a kah ngei mi khat tawh kiho in a huh ding hiam?

records.english: Will you ask me some hard interview questions, so I'm ready for anything?
records.zomi: Bangpeuh adingin ka kiman theih nadingin dotna haksa tawmno hong dong thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Why are you so sure I'll pass the exam this time?
records.zomi: Bang hangin tu-in sitna ka zo ding na um mahmah hiam?

records.english: Because you've been studying every evening, and I've seen how much you've improved.
records.zomi: Nitak simin na kisin a, na hoih semsem dan ka muh khin manin.

records.english: My colleague reminded me that I'd handled worse problems before, and that helped me calm down.
records.zomi: A sia zaw buaina ka bawl siang ngei hi, ci-in ka nasem lawm in hong phawksak a, ka lungsim hong daisak hi.

records.english: Try one more time, and ask the instructor to watch you.
records.zomi: Vei khat behlap hanciam inla, hilhpa in hong en dingin ngen in.

records.english: The doctors told my uncle he might never work again, but he was back in his workshop within a year.
records.zomi: Siavuante in ka pa neu na a sem kik ngei kei kha ding hi, a ci uh a, ahi zongin kum khat sungin a nasepna inn ah a ciah kik hi.

records.english: Ask me again in a year, and I bet you'll be the one giving advice.
records.zomi: Kum khat khit ciangin hong dong kik in, nang thuhilh piakpa na hi ding hi, ka um hi.

records.english: Kids, I'm proud of you for finishing the race, even though we came last.
records.zomi: Naupangte, i nunung pen hangin tai kidemna na zawh manun note tungah ka kisaktheih hi.

records.english: Our class wrote letters of encouragement to the students in the hospital school.
records.zomi: I kilasi in zato sang-a sangnaupangte adingin hanthawnna lai a gelh uh hi.

records.english: Could you write a few kind words to the new teacher, since she's had a difficult first month?
records.zomi: Saya thak in kha masa pen haksa a neih manin a adingin kammal hoih tawmno na gelh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Our coach made each of us say one thing we'd done well before we talked about our mistakes.
records.zomi: I khialhnate i kikup ma-in i coach in i khat ciat in i sep hoih khat hong gensak hi.

records.english: We do want you to succeed, so ask us whenever you need help.
records.zomi: Na zawh i deih taktak ahih manin huhna na kisap simin hong dong in.

records.english: After my accident at the factory, my coworkers visited me every week to keep my spirits up.
records.zomi: Factory ah ka kituakna khit ciangin ka nasem lawmte in ka lungsim a hat den nadingin kal simin hong veh uh hi.

records.english: The shop was rebuilt after the fire, and our old customers came back on the first day.
records.zomi: Mei kat khit ciangin dawl kilam kik a, i van lei luite ni masa pen-in hong ciah kik uh hi.

records.english: The workers' spirits were lifted when the factory announced it would stay open.
records.zomi: Factory om den ding hi, a cih ciangin nasemte' lungsim a nuam kik hi.

records.english: How do you encourage a student who's lost interest in school?
records.zomi: Sang a deih nawn lo sangnaupang khat bangci-in na hanthawn hiam?

records.english: I find out what they love, and I connect it to the lessons.
records.zomi: Bang a deih uh hiam ka zong a, hilhnate tawh ka kizopsak hi.

records.english: Tell me what you like doing, and I'll help you find a course that fits.
records.zomi: Na sep nuam hong gen inla, na tawh kilawm kisinna khat na muh nadingin kong huh ding hi.

records.english: Could we have the meeting outside under the trees, since it's so hot in the office?
records.zomi: Office a sa mahmah ahih manin polam singkung nuai ah kikhopna i nei thei ding hiam?

records.english: Phones aren't allowed at the dinner table in our house, which suits me fine after a day of work calls.
records.zomi: I inn ah an nekna dawhkan ah phone kiphal lo a, ni bup nasep phone sam khit ciangin kei adingin a hoih hi.

records.english: My favorite part of the day is the quiet hour before the shop opens.
records.zomi: Ka ni sung-a ka deih pen dawl a kihon ma-a nai khat dai ahi hi.

records.english: Shall we take the bus or walk to the training center?
records.zomi: Kisinna mun ah bus i tuang ding hiam, i kaai ding hiam?

records.english: My brother likes his desk messy and says he can find anything on it.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in a dawhkan buai a deih a, a tung ah bangpeuh a mu thei hi, a ci hi.

records.english: I chose nursing over teaching because I prefer working with adults.
records.zomi: Upate tawh na sep ka deih zaw ahih manin hilhna sangin nursing ka teel hi.

records.english: You can choose any book for your report, as long as it's in the school library.
records.zomi: Sang laibu inn ah a om phial leh na report adingin laibu khatpeuh na teel thei hi.

records.english: Why do you always take the stairs instead of the lift?
records.zomi: Bang hangin lift sangin kaplei na kah tawntung hiam?

records.english: It's the only exercise I get on workdays.
records.zomi: Nasep ni-in ka pumpi kisinna ngah bek ahi hi.

records.english: Working with my hands makes me happier than any office job I've had.
records.zomi: Ka khut tawh na sep in ka sep ngei office nasep khempeuh sangin hong lungdamsak zaw hi.

records.english: Unlike most of my classmates, who need complete silence, I study best with a little noise around me.
records.zomi: Dai kim a kisam ka kilasi lawm tam zaw tawh kibang lo-in ka kiim ah ging tawmno a om ciangin ka kisin hoih pen hi.

records.english: I'm not a morning person, so I take the afternoon shifts whenever I can.
records.zomi: Zingsang mi ka hi kei ahih manin ka theih ciangin nitak lam nasep hun ka la hi.

records.english: I'd rather work early in the morning than stay late in the evening.
records.zomi: Nitak zan sau om sangin zingsang manlang na sep ka deih zaw hi.

records.english: Would you rather have a higher salary or more time with your family?
records.zomi: Kha man sang zaw hiam, na innkuan tawh hun tam zaw hiam, bang na deih zaw ding hiam?

records.english: More time, without a doubt — the kids are only young once.
records.zomi: Hun tam zaw, a kician hi — naupangte vei khat bek a neu uh hi.

records.english: Is it all right if I wear my own shoes instead of the uniform ones?
records.zomi: Sang puan khedap sangin keimah' khedap ka silh leh a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: My daughter's favorite subject used to be art, but now she can't get enough of science.
records.zomi: Ka tanu' laisim deih pen lim gelh ahi ngei a, ahi zongin tu-in science a deih lua hi.

records.english: Hot drinks are banned in the computer lab, so I drink my tea before class.
records.zomi: Computer lab ah dawn ding lum kiphal lo ahih manin kilasi ma-in ka tea ka dawn hi.

records.english: Can I sit by the window in the exam hall, since the light helps me concentrate?
records.zomi: Meivak in lungsim koih hong huh ahih manin sitna inn ah tawhkhawng kiang ah ka tu thei ding hiam?

records.english: Do you like working from home, or do you miss the office?
records.zomi: Inn pan na sep na deih hiam, office na ngaih hiam?

records.english: I took the job at the bakery because I love the smell of bread in the morning.
records.zomi: Zingsang ciangin moh gim ka deih mahmah ahih manin moh bawlna inn-a nasep ka la hi.

records.english: Do you prefer working alone or in a team?
records.zomi: Nangma' bek-a na sep na deih zaw hiam, pawl tawh hiam?

records.english: In a team, because I get my best ideas when I'm talking to people.
records.zomi: Pawl tawh, mite tawh ka kiho ciangin ka ngaihsutna hoih pente ka ngah ahih manin.

records.english: When the office was rearranged, my desk was moved next to the window, which I love.
records.zomi: Office kibawl kik ciangin ka dawhkan tawhkhawng kiang ah kipemsak a, ka deih mahmah hi.

records.english: My manager prefers short emails, so I keep mine to three lines.
records.zomi: Ka manager in email tom a deih zaw ahih manin keima' kam khau thum dong bek ka gelh hi.

records.english: Wearing a uniform suits me, because I never have to decide what to wear.
records.zomi: Silh ding ka khensat kul ngei loh manin sang puan silh in kei hong kilawm hi.

records.english: My grandfather told me that he chose farming because he couldn't stand being indoors.
records.zomi: Inn sung omna a thuak zo kei ahih manin lo sepna a teel hi, ci-in ka pu in hong gen hi.

records.english: What kind of job would you choose if you could start again?
records.zomi: Na kipan kik thei leh bang nasep na teel ding hiam?

records.english: What's your favorite thing about working at the market?
records.zomi: Zuakna mun ah na sepna ah bang na deih pen hiam?

records.english: Which subject did you like best at school?
records.zomi: Sang ah bang laisim na deih pen hiam?

records.english: My wife prefers to start work at six so that she can pick up the children at three.
records.zomi: Ka zi in nai thum ciangin naupangte a lak theih nadingin nai guk ciangin nasep kipat a deih zaw hi.

records.english: Our teacher said, "You can write in pen or pencil, whichever you're more comfortable with."
records.zomi: I saya in, “Pen hiam khedap kawl hiam, na deih zawk tawh gelh thei hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: Everyone, write down which project you'd like to work on, and I'll try to give you your first choice.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, project bang ah na sep nuam hiam gelh unla, na teel masa pen pia dingin ka hanciam ding hi.

records.english: My mother has always said that a job you love never feels like work.
records.zomi: Na it nasep pen nasep bangin a kisa ngei kei hi, ci-in ka nu in a gen tawntung hi.

records.english: If I could choose, I'd work four long days and have three days off.
records.zomi: Ka teel thei leh ni sau li na ka sem a, ni thum ka khawl ding hi.

records.english: My sister likes night shifts because the hospital is calmer, but I could never sleep during the day.
records.zomi: Zato a dai zawk manin ka sanggam nu in zan nasep a deih a, ahi zongin kei sun ah ka ihmu thei ngei lo ding hi.

records.english: Nobody is allowed to change the temperature of the office air conditioning without asking.
records.zomi: Dong lo-in kuamah in office air conditioning' lum leh vot a khel thei kei hi.

records.english: If you prefer, we could meet at the library instead of the café.
records.zomi: Na deih leh cafe sangin laibu inn ah i kimu thei hi.

records.english: Are you allowed to choose your own hours at your new job?
records.zomi: Na nasep thak ah na sep hun nangma' mah in na teel thei hiam?

records.english: Students who prefer to work alone can sit at the back tables.
records.zomi: Amau bek-a sep a deih zaw sangnaupangte nung lam dawhkan ah a tu thei uh hi.

records.english: Do you like your new teacher better than the old one?
records.zomi: Na saya thak a lui sangin na deih zaw hiam?

records.english: Our teacher asked each of us to bring a photo of the place where we like to study.
records.zomi: I saya in i kisin nuam mun lim khat ciat tawi dingin hong ngen hi.

records.english: When my favorite café near the office closed, my whole morning routine was ruined.
records.zomi: Office kiang-a ka deih pen cafe a kikhak ciangin ka zingsang ngeina bup a sia hi.

records.english: Given the choice, most of my students would rather do a project than sit an exam.
records.zomi: Teel thei uh leh ka sangnaupang tam zaw in sitna sit sangin project sep a deih zaw ding uh hi.

records.english: The radio in the workshop was turned off after the new manager arrived, and nobody was happy.
records.zomi: Manager thak a tun khit ciangin nasepna inn-a radio kiphel a, kuamah a lungdam kei uh hi.

records.english: I like teachers who explain things slowly and let us ask questions.
records.zomi: Zawi taka gen siang a, dotna i dot theih uh a phal sayate ka deih hi.

records.english: My boss lets each of us decorate our own corner of the office however we like.
records.zomi: Ka makaipa in i khat ciat in office-a i mun i deih bangin i zeem thei hi.

records.english: The canteen's spicy soup was taken off the menu, and half the factory complained.
records.zomi: Canteen' an-tui hai menu pan kila khia a, factory a kim in a phunsan uh hi.

records.english: Asked to choose between a promotion and moving to the city, my colleague chose to stay at home.
records.zomi: Kaisanna leh khuapi-a pem kikal ah teel dingin a kingen ciangin ka nasem lawm in inn ah om a teel hi.

records.english: May I use my own laptop at work instead of the office computer?
records.zomi: Office computer sangin nasepna ah keimah' laptop ka zang thei ding hiam?

records.english: Which do you enjoy more, planning the lessons or teaching them?
records.zomi: Hilhna gel leh hilh, bang na nuam sa zaw hiam?

records.english: Teaching, definitely — planning is the part I put off.
records.zomi: Hilh, a kician hi — gel pen ka zekhia zel tan ahi hi.

records.english: My son would rather fix a bicycle than read a book, so we found him an apprenticeship.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in laibu sim sangin siiksakol bawl a deih zaw ahih manin nasep kisinna khat i zong sak hi.

records.english: Would it be possible to work in the quiet room this afternoon?
records.zomi: Tu nitak dai khan ah ka sem thei ding hiam?

records.english: Kids, choose one activity each for after school, and we'll talk about it at dinner.
records.zomi: Naupangte, sang khit ciang ading sepna khat ciat teel unla, nitak an ciangin i kikum ding hi.

records.english: Fixing machines has always appealed to me more than selling them.
records.zomi: Machine bawl in a zuak sangin hong lungdamsak zaw tawntung hi.

records.english: My first boss taught me that what you enjoy doing is usually what you do best.
records.zomi: Na sep nuam pen na sep siam pen ahi zel hi, ci-in ka makaipa masa pen in hong hilh hi.

records.english: My cousin left a well-paid job in the city because she preferred the slower pace of village teaching.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu in khua-a hilhna-a zawi taka nuntak a deih zawk manin khuapi-a kha man sang nasep a nusia hi.

records.english: I always choose the front seat on the bus so that I can read my notes without feeling sick.
records.zomi: Ka lu hai lo-in ka gelhte ka sim theih nadingin bus tungah mai lam tutna ka teel tawntung hi.

records.english: I started my business with one sewing machine in my bedroom, and now I employ six people.
records.zomi: Ka lupna khan ah puan khuina machine khat tawh ka sumbawlna ka kipan a, tu-in mi guk ka sap hi.

records.english: My brother was hired, trained, and promoted in the same year, which nobody in our family had ever done.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal kum khat mah-in kisam, kisin, kaisang a, i innkuan ah kuamah in tua bang a sem ngei kei hi.

records.english: Did you always want to be a doctor?
records.zomi: Siavuan suak na deih tawntung hiam?

records.english: Let me tell you how I got my first job — it's a funny story.
records.zomi: Ka nasep masa pen bangci-in ka ngah hiam kong gen ning — tangthu nuihza ahi hi.

records.english: During my internship, I spent most of my time making coffee and photocopies, but I learned a lot by listening.
records.zomi: Ka internship laitakin ka hun tam zaw kawfi bawl leh photocopy in ka zang a, ahi zongin ngai-in tampi ka sin hi.

records.english: Every job I've had has taught me something about patience.
records.zomi: Ka nasep khempeuh in thuakzawhna thu khat ciat hong hilh hi.

records.english: Children in my village used to leave school at twelve to help on the farms.
records.zomi: Ka khua-a naupangte kum sawm leh nih ciangin lo-a huh dingin sang a nusia zel uh hi.

records.english: What's the best piece of advice you were given at work?
records.zomi: Nasepna ah thuhilhna hoih pen bang na ngah hiam?

records.english: Why did you leave the army and become a nurse?
records.zomi: Bang hangin galkap na nusia a, nurse na suak hiam?

records.english: I realized I wanted to heal people, not just protect them.
records.zomi: Mite hum bek hi lo-in damsak ka deih hi, ka thei hi.

records.english: Each of you can talk about your work for three minutes, and then we'll ask questions.
records.zomi: Note khat ciat in minit thum sung na nasep thu na gen thei uh a, tua khit ciangin dotna i dong ding hi.

records.english: Working on the railway for forty years, my grandfather saw the steam trains replaced by electric ones.
records.zomi: Kum sawmli sung meileng lampi ah na a sep laitakin ka pu in meikhu meileng te meivak meileng tawh a kilaih a mu hi.

records.english: As a schoolgirl, I walked two hours to school every day.
records.zomi: Numei sangnaupang ka hih lai-in ni simin sang ah nai nih ka kaai hi.

records.english: Looking back, the year I spent unemployed taught me more than any job.
records.zomi: A nung lam ka et kik ciangin nasep om lo-a ka om kum in nasep khempeuh sangin tam zaw hong hilh hi.

records.english: We had no phones at school, so we passed notes in class.
records.zomi: Sang ah phone i nei kei ahih manin kilasi ah lai neute i kipia hi.

records.english: What was the hardest job you've ever had?
records.zomi: Na sep ngei nasep haksa pen bang ahi hiam?

records.english: Picking tea on a hillside in the rain, when I was sixteen.
records.zomi: Ka kum sawm leh guk lai-in guah zuk lai-in mual gei ah tea hah lak.

records.english: Does your old teacher still remember you?
records.zomi: Na saya lui in hong phawk lai hiam?

records.english: Is it true that you once taught a class of sixty children by yourself?
records.zomi: Vei khat naupang sawmguk kilasi khat nangma' bek in na hilh ngei hi, cih a man hiam?

records.english: The year our company nearly went bankrupt, the owner paid us from his own savings.
records.zomi: I company a puk dek kum-in a neipa in amah' sum kholsa tawh hong pia hi.

records.english: When the floods destroyed our school, we studied in the church for a whole year.
records.zomi: Tuiciim in i sang a suksiat ciangin kum khat bup pawlpi ah i kisin hi.

records.english: Can you remember your first day at work?
records.zomi: Nasepna-a na ni masa pen na phawk thei hiam?

records.english: Before computers, all the office records were kept in big books.
records.zomi: Computer om ma-in office lai khempeuh laibu lian sungah kikem hi.

records.english: Our school was given its first computer when I was twelve, and the whole village came to see it.
records.zomi: Ka kum sawm leh nih lai-in i sang in a computer masa pen a ngah a, khua bup in en dingin hong pai uh hi.

records.english: I lost my first job because I was always late, and I've never been late since.
records.zomi: Ka nun den manin ka nasep masa pen ka mansuah a, tua pan ka nun ngei nawn kei hi.

records.english: Were you nervous when you gave your first speech at work?
records.zomi: Nasepna ah na thugen masa pen na gen ciangin na lau hiam?

records.english: The teachers weren't allowed to speak our home language in class when my parents were at school.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa sang a kah lai-un sayate in kilasi ah i inn pau a zang thei kei uh hi.

records.english: My uncle's hand was injured in a machine at the sawmill, and he had to learn a new trade.
records.zomi: Sing atna mun ah machine khat in ka pa neu' khut a liamsak a, nasep thak a sin kul hi.

records.english: Writing down my work memories helped me see how much I'd achieved.
records.zomi: Ka nasep phawknate ka gelh in bangzah ka zo hiam hong musak hi.

records.english: When the shop burned down, my parents rebuilt it with help from every family on the street.
records.zomi: Dawl mei a kat ciangin ka nu leh ka pa in lampi-a innkuan khempeuh' huhna tawh a lam kik uh hi.

records.english: On my first day as a teacher, a boy asked me if I was a new student, and the whole class laughed.
records.zomi: Saya ka hih ni masa pen-in pasal naupang khat in sangnaupang thak na hi hiam hong dong a, kilasi bup a nui uh hi.

records.english: I've worked in five countries, but I've never felt as welcome as I did in my first village posting.
records.zomi: Gam nga ah na ka sem khin a, ahi zongin ka khua sep masa pen bangin kidawn ka kisa ngei kei hi.

records.english: What did studying abroad teach you?
records.zomi: Gamdang-a sang na kah in bang hong hilh hiam?

records.english: I was sent to a village school as a young teacher so that I could get experience before working in the city.
records.zomi: Khuapi ah na ka sep ma-in theihna ka ngah theih nadingin saya khangno-in khua sang ah hong sawl uh hi.

records.english: My grandmother sold vegetables at the same market corner for fifty years.
records.zomi: Ka pi kum sawmnga sung zuakna mun ki-ngawi khat mah ah anteh a zuak hi.

records.english: No one in my family had finished secondary school before me, so my graduation was a big event.
records.zomi: Kei ma-in ka innkuan ah kuamah in sang lian a zo kei uh ahih manin ka sang zawhna poai lian ahi hi.

records.english: My first boss shouted at everyone, which taught me exactly how not to manage people.
records.zomi: Ka makaipa masa pen in mi khempeuh a kik sam a, mite bangci-in kem lo ding hiam kician takin hong hilh hi.

records.english: My friend and I started school on the same day, and forty years later we retired from the same hospital.
records.zomi: Ka lawm leh kei ni khat mah-in sang i kipan a, kum sawmli khit ciangin zato khat mah pan i khawl hi.

records.english: Moving to the capital for work taught me to budget, to cook, and to ask strangers for help.
records.zomi: Nasep adingin gam khuapi lian ah ka pem in sum zat gel, an huan leh mi theih lohte kiangah huhna ngen hong hilh hi.

records.english: Would you share your story with the new trainees, so that they know what's possible?
records.zomi: Bang a sem thei uh hiam a theih theih nadingun kisin thakte kiangah na tangthu na hawm thei ding hiam?

records.english: The bank I worked for was closed overnight, and two hundred of us lost our jobs.
records.zomi: Ka sepna bank zan khat sungin kikhak a, i za nih in i nasep i mansuah hi.

records.english: My cousin went abroad to study, met her husband in the library, and never came back.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu sang kah dingin gamdang ah a pai a, laibu inn ah a pasal a mu a, a ciah kik ngei kei hi.

records.english: When the factory workers went on strike, my mother cooked rice for all of them at the gate.
records.zomi: Factory nasemte a khawl uh ciangin ka nu in kongpi ah amaute khempeuh adingin buh a huan hi.

records.english: I worked in a shoe factory for ten years before I went back to school to become an accountant.
records.zomi: Sum gelhpa suak dingin sang ah ka kah kik ma-in khedap factory ah kum sawm na ka sem hi.

records.english: Tell us about a teacher who changed your life.
records.zomi: Na nuntakna a khel saya khat thu hong gen in.

records.english: Our old classroom was so cold in winter that we wrote with our gloves on.
records.zomi: I kilasi lui khuavot ciangin a vot lua ahih manin khut-ngumna silh-in lai i gelh hi.

records.english: What surprised you most about your first year at university?
records.zomi: Sangpi-a na kum masa pen-in bang in hong lamdangsak pen hiam?

records.english: Students, your homework is to ask an older relative about their first job and write it down.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte, na inn-a sep ding pen beh leh phung upa khat kiangah a nasep masa pen thu dong unla gelh un.

records.english: Who taught you to repair radios?
records.zomi: Radio bawl kua in hong hilh hiam?

records.english: Nobody — I took old ones apart at the market and worked it out myself.
records.zomi: Kuamah — zuakna mun ah a luite ka phel a, kei mah in ka sin hi.

records.english: Hearing my students' parents describe their own school days helped me understand the village better.
records.zomi: Ka sangnaupangte' nu leh pate in amau sang kah lai thu a gen uh ka zak in khua hong theisak zaw hi.

records.english: What would you tell your younger self about work?
records.zomi: Nasep thu-ah na khangno lai kiangah bang na gen ding hiam?

records.english: If I hadn't failed that exam, I would never have discovered how much I loved carpentry.
records.zomi: Tua sitna ka zo lo kei leh sing seemna bangzah ka it hiam ka thei ngei lo ding hi.

records.english: I was the first woman in our town to drive a bus, and some passengers refused to get on.
records.zomi: I khuapi ah bus mawng masa pen numei ka hi a, tuangte khenkhat in a tuang nuam kei uh hi.

records.english: My manager once said, "Everyone here has made a big mistake; what matters is what you did next."
records.zomi: Ka manager in vei khat, “Hih ah mi khempeuh in khialhna lian a nei khin uh hi; a thupi pen a nung ciangin bang na sep hiam ahi hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: I trained as an engineer but ended up running a bakery, and I don't regret it.
records.zomi: Engineer dingin ka kisin a, ahi zongin moh bawlna inn khat ka kem a, ka khasia kei hi.

records.english: When the mine closed, my grandfather and his friends started a cooperative that grows coffee.
records.zomi: Suang tukna mun a kikhak ciangin ka pu leh a lawmte in kawfi suan pawl khat a phut uh hi.

records.english: The day I passed my driving test, I drove straight to my first job interview.
records.zomi: Ka mawtaw mawng sitna ka zawh ni-in ka nasep dotna masa pen ah pahtakin ka mawng hi.

records.english: Have you ever been fired?
records.zomi: Nasep pan hong khawlsak ngei uh hiam?

records.english: Once, from a café, because I kept giving free coffee to my friends.
records.zomi: Vei khat, cafe khat pan, ka lawmte kiangah kawfi a man om lo-in ka pia den manin.

records.english: Nobody should be ignored at the clinic desk, however busy we are.
records.zomi: Bangzah i buai zongin clinic dawhkan ah kuamah kinusia lo ding hi.

records.english: Greeting customers at the bank counter all day made my face ache from smiling.
records.zomi: Bank dawhkan ah ni bup van leite ka hopih ahih manin ka nui lua-in ka mai a na hi.

records.english: When does the post office close in the evening?
records.zomi: Post office nitak ciangin nai bangzah ciangin kikhak hiam?

records.english: Had the clerk at the town hall not recognized my mother, we would have waited all morning for the certificate.
records.zomi: Khuapi office-a nasempa in ka nu a theih kei leh lai-ciam adingin zingsang bup i ngak ding hi.

records.english: Visitors aren't allowed into the ward before ten, so the nurse greeted us at the door and asked us to wait.
records.zomi: Nai sawm ma-in ward ah hong vehte lut thei lo ahih manin nurse in kongkhak ah hong hopih a, ngak dingin hong ngen hi.

records.english: Good night, and thank you for coming to help at the clinic today.
records.zomi: Zanpha, tuni-in clinic ah huh dingin na hong pai manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: Strangers aren't allowed past the gate of the water plant, so the guard greets visitors from his little hut.
records.zomi: Tui bawlna mun kongpi mi theih lohte kantan thei lo ahih manin kongpi kemtu in a inn neu sung pan hong vehte a hopih hi.

records.english: When the fire was finally out, the firefighters were greeted by the whole street with tea and bread.
records.zomi: Mei a mit tawp ciangin mei mitsakte lampi bup in tea leh moh tawh a muak uh hi.

records.english: The library was closed when we arrived, but the cleaner greeted us and told us to come back at nine.
records.zomi: I tun ciangin laibu inn kikhak a, ahi zongin siangsak nu in hong hopih a, nai kua ciangin hong pai kik dingin hong gen hi.

records.english: Hi, good evening — I'm calling from the clinic to remind you about tomorrow's appointment.
records.zomi: Hi, Nitakpha — zingciang siavuan veh nading hong phawksak dingin clinic pan kong sam hi.

records.english: We greet the bus driver every morning, and on his birthday the whole bus sang to him.
records.zomi: Zingsang simin bus tuansakpa i hopih a, a pianni-in bus bup in la a sak uh hi.

records.english: Waving good morning to the street sweeper has become part of my walk to work.
records.zomi: Lampi phiatpa kiangah Zingpha ci-in khut vaai pen nasep ka pai lam ngeina khat a suak hi.

records.english: Say good evening to the night nurse before you leave, sweetheart.
records.zomi: Ka it, na paisan ma-in zan nurse kiangah Nitakpha ci in.

records.english: Who greets the visitors at the community center on weekends?
records.zomi: Kal tawp-in mipi inn ah hong vehte kua in a hopih hiam?

records.english: Two retired teachers who know almost everyone in town.
records.zomi: Khuapi-a mi tam zaw a thei saya khawl nih.

records.english: A cheerful good morning from the woman at the ticket office made my long journey feel shorter.
records.zomi: Ticket office-a numei' lungdam Zingpha in ka khualzinna sau hong tomsak hi.

records.english: Good afternoon — is this where I pay the water bill?
records.zomi: Sunpha — tui man piakna pen hih ah ahi hiam?

records.english: Good afternoon — could you tell me where the tax office is?
records.zomi: Sunpha — siah office koi ah om hiam hong gen thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Good evening — we're from the neighborhood committee, collecting for the new street lights.
records.zomi: Nitakpha — inn veng committee pan ka hi uh a, lampi meivak thak adingin sum ka kaikhawm uh hi.

records.english: Morning, everyone — the water will be off from ten until two today.
records.zomi: Zingpha, mi khempeuh — tuni nai sawm pan nai nih dong tui kitan ding hi.

records.english: How are you this morning, Mrs. Niang, and is your knee any better?
records.zomi: Mrs. Niang, tu zingsangin bangci om na hi hiam, na khuk a hoih zaw hiam?

records.english: The rubbish collectors wave and shout good morning to the children waiting for the school bus.
records.zomi: Van niin la mite in sang bus ngak naupangte kiangah khut vaai-in Zingpha ci-in a sam uh hi.

records.english: The new mayor surprised everyone by greeting each stall owner at the market personally.
records.zomi: Khuapi ukpa thak in zuakna mun-a dawl nei khat ciat amah mah in a hopih manin mi khempeuh a lamdang sa uh hi.

records.english: Good morning, officer — I'm here to report a lost bag.
records.zomi: Zingpha, police — ip mangthang thu gen dingin hong pai ka hi hi.

records.english: No one at our health center starts the day without greeting the security guard at the door.
records.zomi: I damna inn ah kongpi kemtu hopih lo-in kuamah in ni a kipan kei hi.

records.english: Could you greet the elderly visitors at the gate and help them up the steps?
records.zomi: Kongpi ah hong veh upate na hopih a, kaplei kah nadingin na huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: So well do the shopkeepers in our town know their customers that they greet them before they've even stepped inside.
records.zomi: I khuapi-a dawl neite in a van leite uh a thei mahmah uh ahih manin a lut ma-un a hopih uh hi.

records.english: The pharmacist greeted my grandmother by name and asked about her blood pressure.
records.zomi: Zatui zuakpa in ka pi a min tawh a hopih a, a sisan nuamna thu a dong hi.

records.english: Ever since the bank installed machines, I miss being greeted by the cashier.
records.zomi: Bank in machine a koih pan sum la nu' hopihna ka ngaih hi.

records.english: Every morning the market opens with the sellers calling good morning to each other across the stalls.
records.zomi: Zingsang simin zuakna mun pen zuakte in dawl tung pan Zingpha a kisam uh tawh a kipan hi.

records.english: Greet the patients when they come in, and offer them a seat while they wait.
records.zomi: Damlote a hong lut ciangun hopih unla, a ngak sungun tutna pia un.

records.english: Our postman greets every dog on his route by name.
records.zomi: I lai puakpa in a lampi-a ui khempeuh a min tawh a hopih hi.

records.english: Every Sunday, two members of the church stand at the door to greet people as they arrive.
records.zomi: Nipini simin pawlpi mi nih in mite a tun ciangun hopih dingin kongkhak ah a ding uh hi.

records.english: Shall I say good morning to the council members in the local language?
records.zomi: Khuapi vaihawmte kiangah khua pau tawh Zingpha ka ci ding hiam?

records.english: Can I greet the visitors in our own language first and then translate for them?
records.zomi: Hong vehte i pau tawh a masa-in ka hopih inla tua khit ciangin ka let sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Good afternoon, and welcome to the town library.
records.zomi: Sunpha, khuapi laibu inn ah kidawn un.

records.english: The ambulance driver greeted us with a calm smile, which made my mother feel much safer.
records.zomi: Ambulance tuansakpa in lungsim dai nuihna tawh hong hopih a, ka nu a bit zaw hi, a kisa hi.

records.english: On my first visit to the tax office, nobody even looked up to say hello.
records.zomi: Siah office ka veh masa pen-in kuamah in hello ci dingin a dak kei uh hi.

records.english: However long the queue, the woman at the post office greets every customer as if they were the first.
records.zomi: Kizomna bangzah a sau zongin post office-a numei in van lei khempeuh a masa pen bangin a hopih hi.

records.english: Good morning — I'd like to send this parcel to the capital, please.
records.zomi: Zingpha — hih ip gam khuapi lian ah ka khak nuam hi.

records.english: Do the market sellers here greet customers in the local language or in the national one?
records.zomi: Hih ah zuakna mun-a zuakte in van leite khua pau tawh a hopih uh hiam, gam pau tawh hiam?

records.english: Usually in the local one, but they switch quickly if you don't understand.
records.zomi: A tam zaw khua pau tawh, ahi zongin na theih kei leh pahtakin a khel uh hi.

records.english: The bus driver says good morning to every passenger, even when the bus is packed.
records.zomi: Bus a dim kim zongin bus tuansakpa in tuang khempeuh kiangah Zingpha a ci hi.

records.english: All of you, say good morning to Mr. Kim, who will show you around the fire station.
records.zomi: Note khempeuh, mei mitsakna inn hong etsak ding Mr. Kim kiangah Zingpha ci un.

records.english: Morning, Thomas — the usual?
records.zomi: Zingpha, Thomas — a tawntung bang hiam?

records.english: Good evening, everyone, and thank you for coming to the community meeting.
records.zomi: Nitakpha, mi khempeuh, mipi kikhopna ah na hong pai manun ka lungdam hi.

records.english: The volunteers were told to greet every person who comes to the shelter with a smile and a hot drink.
records.zomi: Om sakna mun ah hong pai mi khempeuh nuihna leh dawn ding lum tawh hopih dingin thalawp nasemte kihilh uh hi.

records.english: Do the police officers on the night patrol say good evening to people they pass?
records.zomi: Zan kawikawi police te in a kantan mite kiangah Nitakpha a ci uh hiam?

records.english: When the power came back on at the community hall, people cheered and greeted each other all over again.
records.zomi: Mipi inn lian ah meivak a hong ciangin mite a sam uh a, a kihopih kik uh hi.

records.english: Good evening, and welcome to the town's first night market!
records.zomi: Nitakpha, khuapi zan zuakna mun masa pen ah kidawn un!

records.english: Good morning, sir — your number is forty-two, and you'll be called in about ten minutes.
records.zomi: Zingpha, Pu — na nambat sawmli leh nih ahi a, minit sawm bang khit ciangin hong sam ding hi.

records.english: When I walked into the clinic at seven, the receptionist greeted me as if she'd been waiting for me all morning.
records.zomi: Nai sagih ciangin clinic ah ka lut ciangin reception nu in zingsang bup hong ngak bangin hong hopih hi.

records.english: How do you usually greet the village elders at a public meeting?
records.zomi: Mipi kikhopna ah khua upate bangci-in na hopih zel hiam?

records.english: We bow our heads slightly and wait for them to speak first.
records.zomi: I lu tawmno i kun a, amaute a gen masa dong i ngak hi.

records.english: Hello, good morning, and sorry to keep you waiting — the computers were slow today.
records.zomi: Hello, Zingpha, hong ngaksak manin hong maisak in — tuni-in computer te a zawi hi.

records.english: Is it polite to greet the doctor before she greets you?
records.zomi: Siavuan nu in hong hopih ma-in nang in na hopih masa pen zahtakna ahi hiam?

records.english: I do want the volunteers to greet every family warmly, especially the ones who come for the first time.
records.zomi: Thalawp nasemte in innkuan khempeuh lungsim lum takin a hopih ding uh ka deih taktak hi, a tuam in a masa pen-a hong pai te.

records.english: When the new doctor arrived in the village, the whole street came out to say good morning.
records.zomi: Siavuan thak khua ah a tun ciangin lampi bup Zingpha ci dingin a pai khia uh hi.

records.english: Why does the old man at the bakery always say good evening, even at noon?
records.zomi: Bang hangin moh bawlna inn-a pasal upa in sun ah zong Nitakpha a ci tawntung hiam?

records.english: He works through the night, so for him it's always evening.
records.zomi: Zan bup na a sep ahih manin a adingin nitak tawntung ahi hi.

records.english: Hi, I'm Daniel from the youth club, and we're looking for people to help paint the playground.
records.zomi: Hi, khangno pawl pan Daniel ka hi a, kimawlna mun lim khai huh ding mite ka zong uh hi.

records.english: Good afternoon — I'm the pharmacist, and I'll explain how to take this medicine.
records.zomi: Sunpha — zatui zuakpa ka hi a, hih zatui bangci-in na nek ding hiam kong gen siang ding hi.

records.english: I'm afraid I've forgotten your name — we met at the clinic fundraiser.
records.zomi: Hong maisak in, na min ka mangngilh hi — clinic sum kaikhawmna poai ah i kimu hi.

records.english: When the new chief arrived, he introduced himself to every household in the village within a week.
records.zomi: Khua makaipa thak a tun ciangin kal khat sungin khua sung innkuan khempeuh kiangah a kitheisak hi.

records.english: How do you introduce yourself to elders in your village?
records.zomi: Na khua ah upate kiangah bangci-in na kitheisak hiam?

records.english: I say my father's name and my clan first, and then my own name.
records.zomi: Ka pa' min leh ka phung a masa-in ka gen a, tua khit ciangin ka min ka gen hi.

records.english: When you visit the village for your research, call on the elders before anyone else.
records.zomi: Na sittelna adingin khua na veh ciangin mi dang ma-in upate va veh in.

records.english: When the new postman introduced himself, the dog barked at him until my son took it inside.
records.zomi: Lai puakpa thak a kitheisak ciangin ka tapa in inn sungah a paipih dong ui in a hawng hi.

records.english: My name is Lian, and I'm standing for the village council because I want a better road to the school.
records.zomi: Ka min Lian ahi a, sang lampi hoih zaw ka deih manin khua vaihawm ah ka ding hi.

records.english: What should I say when I introduce myself at the job center?
records.zomi: Nasep zonna mun ah ka kitheisak ciangin bang ka gen ding hiam?

records.english: As a retired teacher, I'd like to help with the reading club at the library.
records.zomi: Saya khawl ka hih manin laibu inn-a lai sim pawl ka huh nuam hi.

records.english: I'm Doctor Kim, and I'll be visiting the village clinic every second Tuesday.
records.zomi: Doctor Kim ka hi a, Pithai ni a nihna simin khua clinic ka veh ding hi.

records.english: Each new volunteer is introduced to the whole team on their first Saturday.
records.zomi: Thalawp nasem thak khempeuh a Kiginni masa pen-un pawl bup kiangah kitheisak uh hi.

records.english: Hi, I'm from the water company — I'm here to read your meter.
records.zomi: Hi, tui company pan ka hi — na tui tehna sim dingin hong pai ka hi hi.

records.english: Who should I introduce myself to when I arrive at the community center?
records.zomi: Mipi inn ka tun ciangin kua kiangah ka kitheisak ding hiam?

records.english: Ask for Mary at the front desk; she organizes all the volunteers.
records.zomi: Mai dawhkan ah Mary dong in; thalawp nasem khempeuh a vaihawm hi.

records.english: The volunteers were asked to introduce themselves to each patient before they started helping.
records.zomi: Thalawp nasemte in huh a kipat ma-un damlo khat ciat kiangah kitheisak dingin kingen uh hi.

records.english: My application was lost by the council, so I had to introduce myself and explain everything again.
records.zomi: Ka ngetna lai khuapi vaihawm in a mangsak ahih manin ka kitheisak kik a, na khempeuh ka gen siang kik kul hi.

records.english: I introduced myself to the bus driver on the first day, and now he waits for me if I'm late.
records.zomi: Ni masa pen-in bus tuansakpa kiangah ka kitheisak a, tu-in ka nun leh hong ngak hi.

records.english: Hello — I'm Paul, a volunteer firefighter, and I'm here to talk about fire safety in your homes.
records.zomi: Hello — Paul ka hi a, thalawp mei mitsakpa ka hi a, na inn-a mei bitna thu gen dingin hong pai ka hi hi.

records.english: My name is Thomas, and I'm here because the street light outside my house has been broken for a month.
records.zomi: Ka min Thomas ahi a, ka inn polam lampi meivak kha khat a sia ahih manin hih ah ka om hi.

records.english: What's your name, and which village are you from?
records.zomi: Na min bang ahi a, koi khua pan na hi hiam?

records.english: When I introduced myself as the new teacher, the children's grandparents brought eggs and vegetables to my door.
records.zomi: Saya thak-in ka kitheisak ciangin naupangte' pu leh pite in ka kongkhak ah aktui leh anteh hong tawi uh hi.

records.english: The new health worker's visit made my grandmother so happy that she talked about it for days.
records.zomi: Damna nasem thak' veh in ka pi a lungdamsak lua ahih manin ni tampi sung a gen hi.

records.english: Should I introduce myself to the neighbors before or after we move in?
records.zomi: I pem ma-in inn vengte kiangah ka kitheisak ding hiam, i pem khit ciangin hiam?

records.english: Good morning, my name is Joseph, and I'm here for my appointment with the housing officer.
records.zomi: Zingpha, ka min Joseph ahi a, inn thu vaihawmpa tawh kimuhna adingin hih ah ka om hi.

records.english: However shy you feel, telling people your name is the first step to being part of a community.
records.zomi: Bangzah na zahlak zongin mite kiangah na min gen pen mipi sung-a om nading khe suan masa pen ahi hi.

records.english: Are you the new nurse at the health post?
records.zomi: Damna mun-a nurse thak na hi hiam?

records.english: Yes, I'm Esther — I started on Monday and I'll be here every weekday.
records.zomi: Hi hi, Esther ka hi — Pizing ni-in ka kipan a, ni sem ni simin hih ah ka om ding hi.

records.english: My name is Hau, and I've lived in this town for sixty years, so I remember when the river had no bridge.
records.zomi: Ka min Hau ahi a, hih khuapi ah kum sawmguk ka om khin ahih manin gun tungah lei om lo hun ka phawk hi.

records.english: The mayor introduced herself to the flood victims and promised that help was coming.
records.zomi: Khuapi ukpa nu in tuiciim thuakte kiangah a kitheisak a, huhna hong tung ding hi, ci-in a kiciam hi.

records.english: I do want to get to know every family in this parish, so please come and say hello after the service.
records.zomi: Hih pawlpi sung innkuan khempeuh ka theih ka deih taktak ahih manin pawlpi khit ciangin hong pai unla hello ci un.

records.english: All of you, please introduce yourselves and say which street you live on.
records.zomi: Note khempeuh, kitheisak unla lampi bang ah na om uh hiam gen un.

records.english: Not until I checked the voters' list did I notice that my name had been misspelled.
records.zomi: Vote piakte list ka en ma-in ka min kigelh khialh ka thei kei hi.

records.english: Hi, nice to meet you — I'm the one who fixed your gate last spring.
records.zomi: Hi, nong kimuh ka lungdam hi — spring nung in na kongpi a bawl kei ka hi hi.

records.english: Would the chairperson mind if I said a few words about the clinic at the start?
records.zomi: A kipatna ah clinic thu kammal tawmno ka gen leh makaipa in a lungkham ding hiam?

records.english: Having introduced herself in three languages, the new doctor won over the whole waiting room.
records.zomi: Pau thum tawh a kitheisak khit ciangin siavuan thak in ngakna khan bup a lungsim a la hi.

records.english: Excuse me, I'm new to the area — is this where I register for the bus pass?
records.zomi: Hong maisak in, hih ah ka thak hi — bus pass adingin min gelhna hih ah ahi hiam?

records.english: Hello, I'm Pau, and I clean the streets in this part of town, so please call me if you see a problem.
records.zomi: Hello, Pau ka hi a, khuapi hih tan-a lampite ka siangsak ahih manin buaina na muh leh hong sam un.

records.english: Hi, I'm Cing, and I run the sewing class at the women's center on Thursday afternoons.
records.zomi: Hi, Cing ka hi a, Laizing ni nitak simin numei inn ah puan khuina kilasi ka kem hi.

records.english: Hello, everyone — I'm Officer Thang, and I'll be patrolling your street from now on.
records.zomi: Hello, mi khempeuh — Officer Thang ka hi a, tu-a kipan na lampi uh ka kawikawi ding hi.

records.english: Good evening — I'm the interpreter for tonight's meeting, so please speak slowly.
records.zomi: Nitakpha — tu zan kikhopna-a pau leipa ka hi ahih manin zawi takin gen un.

records.english: Visitors aren't allowed past reception until they've introduced themselves and signed in.
records.zomi: Hong vehte in a kitheisak a min a gelh ma-un reception a kantan thei kei uh hi.

records.english: Everyone, this is Joseph, who has just joined the neighborhood watch.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, hih pen Joseph ahi a, inn veng kemna pawl ah a kihel thak hi.

records.english: Hello, Mrs. Niang — this is the library calling to say your book has arrived.
records.zomi: Hello, Mrs. Niang — na laibu a tung hi, ci-in laibu inn pan kong sam hi.

records.english: Children, stand up one by one and tell the fire officer your name.
records.zomi: Naupangte, khat khit khat ding unla mei mitsakpa kiangah na min uh gen un.

records.english: Can you introduce me to the leader of the market sellers?
records.zomi: Zuakna mun zuakte' makaipa kiangah hong theisak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Hello — are you the person I spoke to on the phone about the rent?
records.zomi: Hello — inn man thu-a phone tawh ka kihopih pa na hi hiam?

records.english: Hello, I'm Officer Lun, and this is my partner — we're here about the noise complaint.
records.zomi: Hello, Officer Lun ka hi a, hih pen ka thuah lawm ahi a — ging phunsanna thu adingin hong pai ka hi uh hi.

records.english: The new librarian said, "I'm Ruth, and if a book isn't on the shelf, I'll find it for you."
records.zomi: Laibu inn kem thak in, “Ruth ka hi a, laibu khat dawh tungah a om kei leh kong zong sak ding hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: I'm the social worker who called last week about your mother's care.
records.zomi: Kal bei-in na nu' kepna thu-ah hong sam mipi huhna nasempa ka hi hi.

records.english: Could you say hello to the new family on our street and invite them to the meeting?
records.zomi: I lampi-a innkuan thak kiangah hello na ci a, kikhopna ah na sam thei ding hiam?

records.english: Why do the police officers wear name badges?
records.zomi: Bang hangin police te min badge a bulh uh hiam?

records.english: So that people know who they're talking to and can ask for them again.
records.zomi: Mite in kua tawh a kiho uh hiam a theih uh a, a ngen kik theih nadingun.

records.english: Hello, I'm one of the election officers — may I see your identity card, please?
records.zomi: Hello, vote enkaktu khat ka hi — na ID card ka en thei ding hiam?

records.english: Introducing myself at the town meeting was terrifying, but people clapped when I finished.
records.zomi: Khuapi kikhopna ah ka kitheisak in hong lausak mahmah a, ahi zongin ka zawh ciangin mite in khut a beng uh hi.

records.english: My name is Grace, from the cooperative bank, and I'd like to explain how our small loans work.
records.zomi: Ka min Grace ahi a, lo nei pawl bank pan ka hi a, i leitawi neute bangci-in a kizang hiam ka gen nuam hi.

records.english: Good morning — I'm Grace, the new community health worker for this part of the valley.
records.zomi: Zingpha — Grace ka hi a, hih guam tan adingin mipi damna nasem thak ka hi hi.

records.english: When the electricity was cut during the meeting, I had to introduce myself to the mayor in the dark.
records.zomi: Kikhopna laitakin meivak a kitan ciangin khuamial sungah khuapi ukpa kiangah ka kitheisak kul hi.

records.english: Hi, I'm Lydia, and I'm collecting names for the new bus route petition.
records.zomi: Hi, Lydia ka hi a, bus lampi thak ngetna adingin min ka kaikhawm hi.

records.english: These are my parents, who used to run the bakery where the bank is now.
records.zomi: Hih te ka nu leh ka pa ahi uh a, tu-a bank omna mun ah moh bawlna inn a kem ngei uh hi.

records.english: Is this your son who's training to be a firefighter?
records.zomi: Hih pen mei mitsakpa suak dinga kisin na tapa ahi hiam?

records.english: Yes, and he's already helped put out a fire at the market.
records.zomi: Hi hi, zuakna mun-a mei kat zong a mitsak huh khin hi.

records.english: A photo of my aunt was shown at the town meeting when they announced that the new clinic would carry her name.
records.zomi: Clinic thak in a min a pua ding cih a gen uh ciangin khuapi kikhopna ah ka ni' lim kietsak hi.

records.english: Pastor, may I introduce my fiancé, who'd like to talk to you about our wedding?
records.zomi: Pastor, i kiteenna thu na kiangah a kikum nuam ka kiteen ding pasal kong theisak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Please meet my colleague Lian, who'll be translating for us at the council office.
records.zomi: Khuapi vaihawm office ah hong let sak ding ka nasem lawm Lian hong thei un.

records.english: Using the microphone at the town meeting, the mayor introduced her husband and thanked him for his patience.
records.zomi: Khuapi kikhopna ah microphone zang-in khuapi ukpa nu in a pasal a theisak a, a thuakzawhna adingin lungdam a ko hi.

records.english: This is my nephew, who'll be carrying your shopping to the car.
records.zomi: Hih pen ka tanau ahi a, na van mawtaw dong a puak sak ding hi.

records.english: My sister's introduction at the clinic was so long that the doctor started laughing.
records.zomi: Clinic ah ka sanggam nu' kitheisakna a sau lua ahih manin siavuan a nui kipan hi.

records.english: Once you meet my grandfather, you'll understand why everyone in town knows his name.
records.zomi: Ka pu na theih khit ciangin khuapi-a mi khempeuh in bang hangin a min a theih uh hiam na thei ding hi.

records.english: When the new teacher came, Grandpa introduced her to everyone at the market, one stall at a time.
records.zomi: Saya thak a tun ciangin Pu in zuakna mun-a mi khempeuh kiangah dawl khat khit khat-in a theisak hi.

records.english: No sooner had I introduced my grandmother to the librarian than they realized they'd been at school together.
records.zomi: Ka pi laibu inn kem kiangah ka theisak pah-in sang ah a kah khawm ngei uh a thei uh hi.

records.english: When my grandfather met the young policeman, he realized he'd taught the boy's father to read.
records.zomi: Ka pu in police khangno a muh ciangin tua pasal naupang' pa lai sim a hilh ngei a thei hi.

records.english: How do you introduce a friend to the village chief?
