records.zomi: Khuapi neu ah lungdamna manlang takin a kizeel a, dahna zong tua bangmah in a kizeel hi.

records.english: Please keep your voices down near the hospital, out of respect for the patients.
records.zomi: Damlote zahtakna-in zato kiang ah na aw uh niamsak un.

records.english: Is it all right to bring flowers to the fire station for the firefighter who died?
records.zomi: A si mei mitsakpa adingin mei mitsakna inn ah pak tawi a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: News that the factory would stay open spread through the market in minutes.
records.zomi: Factory a om den ding thu minit tawmno sungin zuakna mun bup ah a kizeel hi.

records.english: The bakery gave everyone free bread when the war memorial was restored.
records.zomi: Gal phawkna suang a kibawl kik ciangin moh bawlna inn in mi khempeuh moh a man om lo-in a pia hi.

records.english: Did you hear that the old cinema might reopen as a community hall?
records.zomi: Cinema lui mipi inn lian-in a kihong kik kha ding thu na za hiam?

records.english: The community held a candlelit evening in the square to remember the people lost in the flood.
records.zomi: Tuiciim-a mangthang mite phawk dingin mipi in laizang ah khawimeivaak halna nitak khat a bawl hi.

records.english: Thank you for coming to the memorial — your presence meant a lot to the family.
records.zomi: Phawkna poai ah na hong manin ka lungdam hi — na om in innkuan adingin a thupi mahmah hi.

records.english: What made the town so proud last week?
records.zomi: Kal bei-in bang in khuapi a kisaktheihsak hiam?

records.english: Our school choir won the national competition for the first time.
records.zomi: I sang la sa pawl in a masa pen-in gam kidemna a zo hi.

records.english: The refugee family's first Christmas in our town was spent at the community center, surrounded by new friends.
records.zomi: Gam taimang innkuan' i khuapi-a Christmas masa pen mipi inn ah lawm thakte' kikal ah kizang hi.

records.english: When the old doctor retired, his patients lined the road and some of them cried.
records.zomi: Siavuan upa a khawl ciangin a damlote lampi gei ah a kizom uh a, khenkhatte a kap uh hi.

records.english: The cinema closed last year, and the young people still talk about how much they miss it.
records.zomi: Kum bei-in cinema kikhak a, khangnote in bangzah a ngaih uh hiam a gen lai uh hi.

records.english: Do you think the clinic will still be open next year?
records.zomi: Kum hong ding ciangin clinic a kihong lai ding in na ngaihsun hiam?

records.english: Can the police come to the school and talk to the children about strangers?
records.zomi: Police in sang ah hong pai-in naupangte kiangah mi theih lohte thu a gen thei ding hiam?

records.english: The dog that had been frightening children in the park was taken away by the council's animal officer.
records.zomi: Huan sungah naupangte a lausak ui pen khuapi vaihawm' ganhing nasempa in a la khia hi.

records.english: The police officer said, "Never give your bank details to anyone who calls you, even if they say they're from the bank."
records.zomi: Police in, “Bank pan hong sam ka hi, a ci zongin hong sam kuamah na bank thu pia ngei kei in,” a ci hi.

records.english: Please don't panic; the gas leak in the street has been found and fixed.
records.zomi: Lau kei un; lampi-a gas zuh kimu a, kibawl khin hi.

records.english: What should we do if there's an earthquake during the school day?
records.zomi: Sang ni sungin ling a om leh bang i sem ding hiam?

records.english: Get under your desks, hold on, and wait for the teacher to lead you outside.
records.zomi: Na dawhkan nuai ah lut unla, len un, saya in polam ah hong paipih dong ngak un.

records.english: My grandmother was afraid of the hospital until a volunteer started visiting her every day.
records.zomi: Thalawp nasem khat in ni simin a veh kipat ma-in ka pi in zato a lau hi.

records.english: Is it safe to drink the water from the village well again?
records.zomi: Khua tuikhuk tui dawn a bit kik hiam?

records.english: Our neighbor was so worried about her son on the night patrol that she waited up for him every night.
records.zomi: I inn veng in zan kawikawi-a a tapa thu a lungkham lua ahih manin zan simin a ngak den hi.

records.english: Children mustn't play near the river while the flood warning is in place.
records.zomi: Tuiciim vaulna a om sungin naupangte gun kiang ah a mawl kei ding uh hi.

records.english: Walking home from the bus stop has felt far less frightening ever since the council put up new street lights.
records.zomi: Khuapi vaihawm in lampi meivak thakte a koih pan bus khawlna pan inn ah kaai a lauhuai tawm zaw mahmah hi.

records.english: Why does the dog next door bark every time the ambulance passes?
records.zomi: Bang hangin inn kiang-a ui in ambulance a kantan simin a hawng hiam?

records.english: I do worry that the clinic will close if the new doctor doesn't come.
records.zomi: Siavuan thak a hong kei leh clinic a kikhak ding ka lungkham taktak hi.

records.english: There's a chance the bus service will stop if the road isn't repaired before winter.
records.zomi: Khuavot ma-in lampi a kibawl kei leh bus a khawl kha ding hi.

records.english: Could you check on the old man next door during the heatwave?
records.zomi: Ni sa nasiat laitakin inn kiang-a pasal upa na en thei ding hiam?

records.english: Can someone from the neighborhood watch walk my mother home after the evening service?
records.zomi: Nitak pawlpi khit ciangin inn veng kemna pawl pan kuamah in ka nu inn dong a paipih thei ding hiam?

records.english: Fear spreads faster than facts, so the mayor posted the real numbers on the town hall door.
records.zomi: Lauhna thutak sangin manlang takin a kizeel ahih manin khuapi ukpa nu in nambat taktakte khuapi office kongkhak ah a kap hi.

records.english: The rumor that the factory was polluting the river turned out to be false, but people were scared for weeks.
records.zomi: Factory in gun a niinsak hi, cih thu zuau ahi a, ahi zongin kal tampi sung mite a lau uh hi.

records.english: My grandmother was so frightened by the scam call that she unplugged her phone for a week.
records.zomi: Zuau phone sam in ka pi a lausak lua ahih manin kal khat sung a phone a phel hi.

records.english: Swimming isn't allowed at the lake this month because of the strong currents.
records.zomi: Tui luang hat hang-in tu kha sungin dil ah tui kidiah kiphal lo hi.

records.english: When the flood siren sounded at midnight, the whole street hurried up the hill to the school.
records.zomi: Zan lai-in tuiciim khawng a ging ciangin lampi bup mual tung-a sang ah a tai uh hi.

records.english: Everyone in the village was searching the forest until the police found the missing girl asleep in a barn.
records.zomi: Police in numei naupang mangthang buh inn sungah a ihmu a muh dong khua sung mi khempeuh in gam sungah a zong uh hi.

records.english: The volunteers were warned not to enter any house where the walls had been damaged by the flood.
records.zomi: Tuiciim in a bang a suksiat inn khatpeuh ah lut lo dingin thalawp nasemte kivaul uh hi.

records.english: Having a plan for emergencies makes the whole family less afraid of the rainy season.
records.zomi: Haksatna hun adingin gelna neih in innkuan bup guah hun a lau tawm zawsak hi.

records.english: Visitors aren't allowed on the hillside road while the landslide warning lasts.
records.zomi: Leiminpuk vaulna a om sungin hong vehte mual lampi ah kiphal lo uh hi.

records.english: So frightened were the villagers by the rising river that they slept in the church for three nights.
records.zomi: Gun a khang ahih manin khua mite a lau lua uh a, zan thum pawlpi ah a ihmu uh hi.

records.english: Thank you for staying with me at the hospital — I was too scared to be alone.
records.zomi: Zato ah ka kiang ah na om manin ka lungdam hi — ka bek in om dingin ka lau lua hi.

records.english: The children were reassured when the firefighters said the school was safe to enter.
records.zomi: Mei mitsakte in sang lut a bitna hi, a cih uh ciangin naupangte a lungsim uh a dai hi.

records.english: The council made every school practice an evacuation drill before the rainy season.
records.zomi: Guah hun ma-in khuapi vaihawm in sang khempeuh taimang kisinna a bawlsak hi.

records.english: When the doctor said he needed more tests, my grandfather went pale.
records.zomi: Sitna behlap a kisam hi, ci-in siavuan in a gen ciangin ka pu a mai a kang hi.

records.english: My mother lay awake all night when the radio said the dam might overflow.
records.zomi: Tui khakna a liam kha ding hi, ci-in radio in a gen ciangin ka nu zan bup a khanglo hi.

records.english: People locked their doors in the daytime after the break-ins, until the police caught the thief.
records.zomi: Inn guk khit ciangin police in a gukpa a man dong mite in sun ah zong a kongkhak uh a khak uh hi.

records.english: Is the siren that goes off every Monday a real warning?
records.zomi: Pizing ni simin a ging khawng pen vaulna taktak ahi hiam?

records.english: No, it's only a test, so you don't need to worry.
records.zomi: Hi lo hi, sitna bek ahih manin na lungkham kul kei hi.

records.english: My aunt keeps a bag ready by the door with water, medicine, and documents, just in case.
records.zomi: Ka ni in a kisap kha leh ci-in tui, zatui leh laite tawh ip khat kongkhak kiang ah a koih khin den hi.

records.english: Why are people so worried about the new road through the forest?
records.zomi: Bang hangin gam sung tawng lampi thak thu mite a lungkham mahmah uh hiam?

records.english: They're afraid the trucks will make the village unsafe for children.
records.zomi: Mawtaw lian te in khua naupangte adingin a bit lo sak ding uh a lau uh hi.

records.english: Would the health center tell us if the fever in the next village spreads here?
records.zomi: A kiang khua-a lum natna hih ah a kizeel leh damna inn in hong gen ding hiam?

records.english: My little brother was terrified of the doctor until the nurse let him listen to his own heart.
records.zomi: Nurse in amah' lungtang ging a ngaihsak dong ka nau pasal in siavuan a lau mahmah hi.

records.english: Are the schools closing because of the storm warning?
records.zomi: Huihpi vaulna hang-in sangte kikhak ding hiam?

records.english: The fire officer showed the children how to check a door for heat before opening it.
records.zomi: Mei mitsak makai in kongkhak na hon ma-in a lum hiam en dan naupangte a etsak hi.

records.english: No one should be ashamed to ask the counselor for help after a frightening experience.
records.zomi: Lauhuai thu khat khit ciangin kuamah in thuhilhpa kiangah huhna ngen dingin a zahlak kul kei hi.

records.english: When the earthquake shook the town, the school was the first building the engineers checked.
records.zomi: Ling in khuapi a ling ciangin engineer te' en masa pen inn sang ahi hi.

records.english: Worry about the mine closing kept half the town awake.
records.zomi: Suang tukna mun kikhak ding lungkhamna in khuapi a kim a khanglosak hi.

records.english: The fire in the market spread so fast that the sellers had only minutes to save their goods.
records.zomi: Zuakna mun-a mei a zel manlang lua ahih manin zuakte in a van uh hum dingin minit tawmno bek a nei uh hi.

records.english: Shall I ask the council whether the trees on our street are safe after the storm?
records.zomi: Huihpi khit ciangin i lampi-a singkungte a bit hiam khuapi vaihawm ka dong ding hiam?

records.english: When the power failed at the hospital, the nurses calmed the frightened patients with flashlights and soft voices.
records.zomi: Zato ah meivak a kitan ciangin nurse te in meivak neu leh aw nem tawh damlo laute a daisak uh hi.

records.english: Is there a number I can call if I'm worried about a neighbor who lives alone?
records.zomi: A bek-a om inn veng khat ka lungkham leh ka sam theih nambat a om hiam?

records.english: How do we know when the flood is over?
records.zomi: Tuiciim a bei ciangin bangci-in i thei ding hiam?

records.english: The council will announce it on the radio, and the siren will sound twice.
records.zomi: Khuapi vaihawm in radio tungah a gen ding a, khawng vei nih a ging ding hi.

records.english: We do feel safer since the neighbors started looking out for each other's houses.
records.zomi: Inn vengte khat leh khat' inn a en kipat uh pan i bit zaw hi, i kisa taktak hi.

records.english: My father has never trusted the dam since the year it nearly broke.
records.zomi: A puk dek kum pan ka pa in tui khakna a muang ngei kei hi.

records.english: My mother's fear eased when the social worker explained exactly what would happen next.
records.zomi: Mipi huhna nasempa in a zom ciangin bang a piang ding hiam kician takin a gen siang ciangin ka nu' lauhna a kiam hi.

records.english: Kids, if you hear the fire alarm, leave your bags and walk straight to the playground.
records.zomi: Naupangte, mei alarm na zak leh na ip uh nusia unla kimawlna mun ah pai pah un.

records.english: Students, stay calm, follow the teacher, and don't run on the stairs.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte, lungsim dai unla, saya zui unla, kaplei tungah tai kei un.

records.english: The old bridge was closed after engineers found cracks, and people were nervous about crossing the new one at first.
records.zomi: Engineer te in a kikek a muh uh khit ciangin lei lui kikhak a, a kipatna ah mite in a thak kantan a lau uh hi.

records.english: The bank closed its branch in our town, leaving the old people worried about where to get their pensions.
records.zomi: Bank in i khuapi-a a khen a khak a, upate in a pension uh koi ah a la ding uh hiam a lungkham uh hi.

records.english: The council has told everyone to boil their water until the tests show it's safe.
records.zomi: Sitnate in a bit hi, ci-in a lak dong a tui uh tuk dingin khuapi vaihawm in mi khempeuh a gen hi.

records.english: Did the water company say when the boil notice would end?
records.zomi: Tui tuk ding thukhun bang ciangin a bei ding hiam tui company in a gen hiam?

records.english: We really do believe the factory will reopen if we keep pressing the council.
records.zomi: Khuapi vaihawm i nawt den leh factory a kihon kik ding i um taktak hi.

records.english: The council gave grants to five young people to start their own businesses in the empty shops on the main street.
records.zomi: Khuapi vaihawm in lampi lian-a dawl awngte ah amau sumbawlna kipat nadingin khangno nga sum huhna a pia hi.

records.english: There's a chance the government will fund a bigger clinic if our numbers keep growing.
records.zomi: I mi tamna a khang den leh kumpi in clinic lian zaw khat adingin sum a pia kha ding hi.

records.english: Whenever I feel like giving up, I think of the women who rebuilt the market after the fire.
records.zomi: Nusia ka deih simin mei kat khit ciangin zuakna mun a lam kik numeite ka ngaihsun hi.

records.english: Is there a club that could help my son make friends and feel more confident?
records.zomi: Ka tapa lawm a ngah a, a muanna a ngah nadingin a huh thei pawl khat a om hiam?

records.english: The old cinema was turned into a youth center, and the street feels alive again.
records.zomi: Cinema lui khangno inn-in kikhel a, lampi a nungta kik bang hi.

records.english: Notes from former guests who now have homes cover the walls of the night shelter.
records.zomi: Tu-in inn a nei khual luite' laite in zan om sakna mun bangte a khuh hi.

records.english: My little sister was so inspired by the firefighters' visit that she joined the youth fire brigade.
records.zomi: Mei mitsakte' veh in ka nau numei a hanthawn lua ahih manin khangno mei mitsak pawl ah a kihel hi.

records.english: Our church has been rebuilt three times, and it's still standing, the pastor reminded us.
records.zomi: I pawlpi vei thum kilam kik a, a ding lai hi, ci-in pastor in hong phawksak hi.

records.english: My father made us promise that we would finish school, whatever happened to the farm.
records.zomi: Lo bang a hi zongin sang i zawh ding ka pa in hong kiciamsak hi.

records.english: When the rain came after two years of drought, the farmers stood in their fields and laughed.
records.zomi: Kum nih khuakhal khit ciangin guah a zuk ciangin lo neite a lo uh ah a ding uh a, a nui uh hi.

records.english: Students, if you need help with your applications, the library volunteers are there every Thursday.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte, na ngetna lai uh adingin huhna na kisap uh leh Laizing ni simin laibu inn thalawp nasemte a om uh hi.

records.english: Could the youth club find a mentor for my nephew, who could use some encouragement this year?
records.zomi: Tu kum hanthawnna a kisam ka tanau adingin khangno pawl in makaihpa khat a zong thei ding hiam?

records.english: So encouraging were the teachers at the evening school that my father, at sixty, finally took his exams.
records.zomi: Nitak sang-a sayate' hanthawnna a hoih lua ahih manin ka pa kum sawmguk ciangin a tawp-in sitna a sit hi.

records.english: Is it too late for me to train as a nurse at forty-five?
records.zomi: Kum sawmli leh nga ciangin nurse dingin ka kisin ding a nun lua khin hiam?

records.english: We do hope the young people who leave for the city will one day come home to help the town.
records.zomi: Khuapi ah a pai khangnote in ni khat ni-in khuapi huh dingin inn ah a ciah kik ding uh i lamen taktak hi.

records.english: The adviser at the job center told me, "Your first job doesn't have to be your last one."
records.zomi: Nasep zonna mun-a thuhilhpa in, “Na nasep masa pen na nunung pen ahi kul kei hi,” hong ci hi.

records.english: Every child who finishes the library's reading challenge gets a certificate from the mayor.
records.zomi: Laibu inn' lai sim kidemna a zo naupang khempeuh in khuapi ukpa pan lai-ciam khat a ngah uh hi.

records.english: My mother was told by the nurse that small steps every day would bring her strength back.
records.zomi: Ni simin khe suan neute in a hatna a ciah kiksak ding hi, ci-in nurse in ka nu a gen hi.

records.english: What gave the village hope after the mine closed?
records.zomi: Suang tukna mun a kikhak khit ciangin bang in khua lametna a pia hiam?

records.english: The cooperative, which found work for half the miners within a year.
records.zomi: Pawl dawl, kum khat sungin suang tukte a kim adingin nasep a zong sak hi.

records.english: A new bus route was opened, and suddenly the young people in the hills could reach the college.
records.zomi: Bus lampi thak kihon a, pahtakin mual-a khangnote in college a tung thei uh hi.

records.english: Who paid for your university fees?
records.zomi: Na sangpi man kua in a pia hiam?

records.english: The town's scholarship fund, which is paid for by the market sellers and the church.
records.zomi: Khuapi' scholarship sum, zuakna mun zuakte leh pawlpi in a piak.

records.english: My neighbor started volunteering at the food bank after it had helped her family through a hard winter.
records.zomi: Khuavot haksa khat sungin a innkuan a huh khit ciangin ka inn veng in an kaikhawmna mun ah thalawp takin a sem kipan hi.

records.english: Do you think the town will ever have its own hospital?
records.zomi: Khuapi in ni khat ni-in amah' zato a nei ding in na ngaihsun hiam?

records.english: The volunteers at the recovery center never give up on anyone.
records.zomi: Damna mun-a thalawp nasemte in kuamah a nusia ngei kei uh hi.

records.english: My cousin was the first person from our village to become a doctor, and now she works at our clinic.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu pen i khua pan siavuan suak masa pen ahi a, tu-in i clinic ah na a sem hi.

records.english: Why does the community center put up photos of people who have found jobs?
records.zomi: Bang hangin mipi inn in nasep a ngah mite' lim a khai hiam?

records.english: To show newcomers that it really can happen to them too.
records.zomi: A tung thakte kiangah amaute tungah zong a piang thei hi, cih lak dingin.

records.english: Thank you for believing in me when the job center said I had no chance.
records.zomi: Nasep zonna mun in na ngah lo ding hi, a cih lai-in hong um manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: Volunteers walked with my grandmother every morning, and slowly she got stronger.
records.zomi: Thalawp nasemte in zingsang simin ka pi tawh a kaai uh a, zawi takin a hat semsem hi.

records.english: My brother was encouraged by the coach to apply for the regional team, and he got in.
records.zomi: Coach in ka sanggam pasal gam pawl ah ngen dingin a hanthawn a, a kisang hi.

records.english: Would a letter from the council help my daughter get the apprenticeship?
records.zomi: Khuapi vaihawm pan lai khat in ka tanu nasep kisinna a ngah nadingin a huh ding hiam?

records.english: Can I join the mentoring program at the library, even though I've already left school?
records.zomi: Sang ka paisan khin hangin laibu inn' makaihna program ah ka kihel thei ding hiam?

records.english: Don't give up on the job center; my brother found work on his fifth visit.
records.zomi: Nasep zonna mun nusia kei in; ka sanggam pasal in a veh vei nga-na-in nasep a ngah hi.

records.english: Did the youth club's football team ever win a match?
records.zomi: Khangno pawl' football pawl in vei khat a zo ngei hiam?

records.english: Not last year, but they've won three already this season, and the whole town comes to watch.
records.zomi: Kum bei-in zo lo hi, ahi zongin tu kum sungin vei thum a zo khin uh a, khuapi bup in en dingin a hong uh hi.

records.english: Can the counselor at the health center see my friend, who has lost hope since losing his job?
records.zomi: A nasep a mansuah pan lametna a mansuah ka lawm damna inn-a thuhilhpa in a mu thei ding hiam?

records.english: Hearing that the town had raised enough money for the new roof, the old pastor wept with joy.
records.zomi: Khuapi in inn tung thak adingin sum a cing kaikhawm hi, cih a zak ciangin pastor upa lungdamna tawh a kap hi.

records.english: Could you write a few words of encouragement for the students sitting their exams next week?
records.zomi: Kal hong ding ciangin sitna sit ding sangnaupangte adingin hanthawnna kammal tawmno na gelh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Every name on the board of former students now working at the clinic began with a single encouraging teacher.
records.zomi: Tu-in clinic ah na a sem sangnaupang luite' min phek tunga min khempeuh saya hanthawn khat pan a kipan hi.

records.english: Hope returned to the valley the day the new school bell rang for the first time.
records.zomi: Sang khawng thak a ging masa pen ni-in guam ah lametna a ciah kik hi.

records.english: The children's choir sang at the hospital every Christmas, and the patients said it was the best medicine.
records.zomi: Christmas simin naupangte' la sa pawl zato ah la a sa uh a, damlote in zatui hoih pen ahi hi, a ci uh hi.

records.english: Tell the council what you need; they listened to us about the bus, and they'll listen to you.
records.zomi: Na kisapna khuapi vaihawm kiangah gen in; bus thu-ah hong ngai uh a, nang zong hong ngai ding uh hi.

records.english: My father learned to read at the library's evening class, and now he reads the newspaper to my grandmother.
records.zomi: Ka pa in laibu inn' nitak kilasi ah lai sim a sin a, tu-in ka pi adingin thuthak lai a sim sak hi.

records.english: The volunteers were so kind that my mother began to trust strangers again.
records.zomi: Thalawp nasemte a hehpih lua uh ahih manin ka nu in mi theih lohte a muang kik kipan hi.

records.english: All of you who helped rebuild the bridge, look how many people are crossing it this morning.
records.zomi: Lei lam kik huh note khempeuh, tu zingsangin mi bangzah in a kantan uh hiam en un.

records.english: A community that encourages its young people never really runs out of hope.
records.zomi: A khangnote a hanthawn mipi khat in lametna a bei ngei kei hi.

records.english: The social worker's patience gave my uncle the courage to try again.
records.zomi: Mipi huhna nasempa' thuakzawhna in ka pa neu vei khat behlap hanciam dingin hangsanna a pia hi.

records.english: A year after the flood, the first new houses were finished, and people began to smile again.
records.zomi: Tuiciim khit kum khat-in inn thak masa pente a zo a, mite a nui kik kipan uh hi.

records.english: Small victories, like a new street light or a repaired road, remind people that change is possible.
records.zomi: Lampi meivak thak hiam lampi kibawl kik bang zawhna neute in kikhelna a om thei hi, cih mite a phawksak hi.

records.english: The first harvest from the community garden was shared with every family on the street.
records.zomi: Mipi huan pan a masa pen buh lak lampi-a innkuan khempeuh tawh kihawm hi.

records.english: Keep coming to the language class; in a year you'll be helping the new arrivals yourself.
records.zomi: Pau kisinna kilasi ah hong pai den in; kum khat sungin a tung thakte nangma' mah in na huh ding hi.

records.english: Shall we start a homework club at the community center for children who have nowhere quiet to study?
records.zomi: Kisin nading mun dai a nei lo naupangte adingin mipi inn ah inn-a sep ding pawl khat i phut ding hiam?

records.english: The library's computer class gave my grandmother the confidence to video-call her grandchildren abroad.
records.zomi: Laibu inn' computer kilasi in ka pi gamdang-a a tu-te tawh video call bawl dingin muanna a pia hi.

records.english: The memorial garden was planted where the old school stood, so that something beautiful would grow there.
records.zomi: Na hoih khat a khan theih nadingin sang lui omna mun ah phawkna huan kisuan hi.

records.english: When the doctor said my father could go home, the whole ward clapped.
records.zomi: Ka pa inn ah a ciah thei hi, ci-in siavuan in a gen ciangin ward bup in khut a beng uh hi.

records.english: Everyone, this new clinic is proof of what a small town can do when it works together.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, hih clinic thak pen khuapi neu khat in khawm-a a sep ciangin bang a sem thei hiam a lakna ahi hi.

records.english: Kids, every one of you can be anything you want if you keep learning.
records.zomi: Naupangte, na sin den uh leh note khat ciat na deih bangbang na suak thei uh hi.

records.english: So many people preferred the old bus route that the company brought it back after a month.
records.zomi: Mi tampi in bus lampi lui a deih zawk uh ahih manin kha khat khit ciangin company in a ciahsak kik hi.

records.english: I really do prefer cycling to work now that the council has built a proper bike lane.
records.zomi: Khuapi vaihawm in siiksakol lampi hoih khat a lam pan siiksakol tawh nasep ah pai ka deih zaw taktak hi.

records.english: Our street voted for a pedestrian crossing rather than speed bumps, and the council agreed.
records.zomi: I lampi in mawtaw zawisakna sangin lampi kantanna khat a teel a, khuapi vaihawm in a lungkim hi.

records.english: Could the café at the community center serve tea in proper cups instead of paper ones?
records.zomi: Mipi inn-a cafe in lai khuang sangin khuang taktak tawh tea a pia thei ding hiam?

records.english: Kids, raise your hand if you'd like the story read in the garden instead of indoors.
records.zomi: Naupangte, tangthu inn sung sangin huan sungah sim na deih uh leh na khut uh dom un.

records.english: The bench by the river was taken away, and the old men who loved sitting there now meet at the bus shelter.
records.zomi: Gun gei-a tutna sau kila a, tua ah tut a deih pasal upate tu-in bus ngakna inn ah a kimu uh hi.

records.english: Given the choice, most parents in our street would rather walk their children to school than use the bus.
records.zomi: Teel thei uh leh i lampi-a nu leh pa tam zaw in bus zat sangin a tate uh sang ah kaai pih a deih zaw uh hi.

records.english: My neighbor refused to move to the new flats, because she preferred her small house near the church.
records.zomi: Ka inn veng in pawlpi kiang-a a inn neu a deih zawk manin inn thakte ah pem a nial hi.

records.english: My husband prefers the small health post in the village to the big hospital in town.
records.zomi: Ka pasal in khuapi-a zato lian sangin khua-a damna mun neu a deih zaw hi.

records.english: My grandmother was delighted when the church allowed her to choose the hymns for her ninetieth birthday.
records.zomi: A kum sawmkua na pianni adingin pawlpi in la a teel dingin a phal ciangin ka pi a lungdam mahmah hi.

records.english: Did the youth club ever get the music room the teenagers asked for?
records.zomi: Khangnote' ngen la khan khangno pawl in a ngah ngei hiam?

records.english: Personal choices matter more when a town is small enough for everyone to be heard.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh' thu a kizak theih zah khuapi a neu ciangin mimal teelna a thupi zaw hi.

records.english: When the post office moved into the supermarket, many villagers began taking the bus to town instead.
records.zomi: Post office supermarket sungah a pem ciangin khua mi tampi in khuapi ah bus a tuang kipan uh hi.

records.english: Had the council asked the residents first, the new playground would have had more shade.
records.zomi: Khuapi vaihawm in teengte a dong masa leh kimawlna mun thak in ni sa khuhna tam zaw a nei ding hi.

records.english: My cousin chose to train as a firefighter rather than join the family shop.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam in innkuan dawl ah a kihel sangin mei mitsak dingin a kisin hi.

records.english: The swimming pool's opening hours were changed after most residents said they preferred early mornings.
records.zomi: Teeng tam zaw in zingsang manlang a deih zawk uh a gen khit uh ciangin tuidaipi hon hun kikhel hi.

records.english: Most of the residents at the care home prefer watching the garden to watching television.
records.zomi: Upate kemna inn-a om tam zaw in television et sangin huan et a deih zaw uh hi.

records.english: My little sister always picks the red seat on the bus, even if she has to wait for it.
records.zomi: Ka nau numei in a ngak kul zongin bus tungah tutna san a teel tawntung hi.

records.english: Would you rather join the walking group or the community choir?
records.zomi: Kaai pawl ah na kihel nuam zaw hiam, mipi la sa pawl ah hiam?

records.english: I do want to try the online form, but I still prefer talking to someone at the town hall.
records.zomi: Online lai zat ka sin nuam taktak hi, ahi zongin khuapi office ah mi khat tawh kiho ka deih zaw lai hi.

records.english: Students, tell us whether you'd like the school trip to go to the museum or the nature reserve.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte, sang khualzinna museum ah na pai nuam uh hiam, gam kemna mun ah hiam hong gen un.

records.english: My aunt likes the self-service checkout at the library, because nobody sees which books she borrows.
records.zomi: Ka ni in a leitawi laibute kuamah in a muh loh manin laibu inn' amah le amah a lakna machine a deih hi.

records.english: When the library let readers vote for new books, detective stories won by a mile.
records.zomi: Laibu inn in laibu thakte adingin vote a piaksak ciangin guk zon tangthute in a zo baih hi.

records.english: Which do you like better, the library's quiet room or the café downstairs?
records.zomi: Laibu inn' khan dai na deih zaw hiam, nuai lam-a cafe hiam?

records.english: All of you who prefer the Saturday market, please sign the petition to keep it open.
records.zomi: Kiginni zuakna mun na deih zaw note khempeuh, a kihon den nadingin ngetna lai ah min suaksak un.

records.english: The old cinema seats were replaced, and the regular customers complained that the new ones were too soft.
records.zomi: Cinema lui tutnate kilai a, a tung tawntung mite in a thakte a nem lua hi, ci-in a phunsan uh hi.

records.english: Which do you prefer, the early ferry or the late one?
records.zomi: Tembaw manlang na deih zaw hiam, a nunung hiam?

records.english: My brother prefers volunteering at the animal shelter to working at the food bank.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in an kaikhawmna mun ah sep sangin ganhing om sakna mun ah thalawp takin sep a deih zaw hi.

records.english: I'd rather pay my bills at the post office counter than on the machine, because the clerk always says hello.
records.zomi: Nasempa in hello a ci tawntung ahih manin machine sangin post office dawhkan ah ka man piak ding ka pia ka deih zaw hi.

records.english: My grandmother's favorite place in town is the bench outside the bakery, where everyone stops to chat.
records.zomi: Ka pi' khuapi sung-a mun deih pen moh bawlna inn polam-a tutna sau ahi a, tua ah mi khempeuh a khawl-in a kiho uh hi.

records.english: How do you find the bus company's new winter timetable?
records.zomi: Bus company' khuavot hun gelhna thak bangci na sa hiam?

records.english: Not really, because the last bus now leaves before my shift ends.
records.zomi: Ka deih lua kei hi, tu-in ka nasep hun a bei ma-in bus nunung a pai khin ahih manin.

records.english: My grandmother prefers the old market to the new supermarket, because she knows every seller by name.
records.zomi: Ka pi in zuakna mun-a zuak khempeuh a min tawh a theih manin supermarket thak sangin zuakna mun lui a deih zaw hi.

records.english: Where do you like to sit when you visit the library?
records.zomi: Laibu inn na veh ciangin koi ah tut na deih hiam?

records.english: By the big window, where I can watch the market while I read.
records.zomi: Tawhkhawng lian kiang ah, ka sim laitakin zuakna mun ka et theihna ah.

records.english: My sister likes the night bus because it's quiet, but I find it lonely.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu in a dai ahih manin zan bus a deih a, ahi zongin kei adingin a kikhawmlum hi.

records.english: Thank you for remembering that I like my tea without sugar.
records.zomi: Sugar om lo tea ka deih na phawk manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: Since the community radio started playing old songs in the mornings, my grandfather has stopped listening to the city station.
records.zomi: Mipi radio in zingsang ciangin la lui a sak kipat pan ka pu in khuapi radio a ngai nawn kei hi.

records.english: The council's survey showed that people valued clean streets more than new benches.
records.zomi: Khuapi vaihawm' dotna in mite in tutna sau thakte sangin lampi siang a manpha sa zaw uh hi, a lak hi.

records.english: What kind of classes would you like the community center to offer?
records.zomi: Mipi inn in bang kilasi a piak ding na deih hiam?

records.english: Computer lessons for older people, and maybe a sewing class.
records.zomi: Upate adingin computer kilasi, puan khuina kilasi zong kha ding hi.

records.english: The volunteers chose the most difficult jobs at the clean-up, leaving the easy ones for the children.
records.zomi: Siangsakna ah thalawp nasemte in nasep haksa pente a teel uh a, a baihte naupangte adingin a nusia uh hi.

records.english: Shall I book you the appointment with the doctor you saw last time?
records.zomi: Nikum na muh siavuan tawh kimuhna kong bawl sak ding hiam?

records.english: Can I choose which day the council collects my bulky rubbish?
records.zomi: Khuapi vaihawm in ka van lian a lak ni ka teel thei ding hiam?

records.english: Do older people in your town prefer paying in cash or by card?
records.zomi: Na khuapi ah upate in sum taktak hiam, card hiam tawh piak a deih zaw uh hiam?

records.english: Kids, choose one book each from the mobile library, and then we'll go home.
records.zomi: Naupangte, kawikawi laibu inn pan laibu khat ciat teel unla, tua khit ciangin inn ah i ciah ding hi.

records.english: The park's new flower beds were planted with the colors the schoolchildren had chosen.
records.zomi: Huan pak suanna thakte sang naupangte' teel lim tawh kisuan hi.

records.english: Why do the children always want the swings rather than the new climbing frame?
records.zomi: Bang hangin naupangte in kahna thak sangin gengen a deih zaw tawntung uh hiam?

records.english: What would most people in our town choose, a new library or a new sports hall?
records.zomi: I khuapi mi tam zaw in bang a teel ding uh hiam, laibu inn thak hiam, kimawlna inn thak hiam?

records.english: Can you ask the librarian whether they have the newspaper in large print?
records.zomi: Thuthak lai lai lian tawh a nei uh hiam laibu inn kemnu na dong thei ding hiam?

records.english: Do you prefer seeing the doctor in the morning or the afternoon?
records.zomi: Zingsangin siavuan muh na deih zaw hiam, nitak lam hiam?

records.english: In the morning, before the waiting room fills up.
records.zomi: Zingsangin, ngakna khan a dim ma-in.

records.english: There might be a vegetarian stall at the festival this year, since so many people asked for one.
records.zomi: Mi tampi in a ngen uh ahih manin tu kum pawi ah sa om lo an dawl khat om kha ding hi.

records.english: Using the touch screen at the station, I can choose a seat by the window on every train.
records.zomi: Station-a khoih screen zang-in meileng khempeuh ah tawhkhawng kiang tutna ka teel thei hi.

records.english: Is there a quieter time to visit the swimming pool?
records.zomi: Tuidaipi veh nading hun dai zaw a om hiam?

records.english: Everyone, put a sticker next to the activity you'd like the youth club to run this summer.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, tu khal ciangin khangno pawl in a bawl ding na deih uh sepna kiang ah sticker khat koih un.

records.english: Waiting in the queue at the bank, my grandmother told me she would never trust a machine with her money.
records.zomi: Bank kizomna ah i ngak laitakin ka pi in machine a sum a muang ngei lo ding hi, hong ci hi.

records.english: Is it all right if I see a female doctor instead?
records.zomi: A sikin numei siavuan ka mu leh a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: Would you prefer a phone call or a letter when your test results are ready?
records.zomi: Na sitna ciamte a kiman ciangin phone sam na deih zaw hiam, lai hiam?

records.english: My mother always asks for the same nurse at the clinic, because she explains things slowly.
records.zomi: Zawi takin a gen siang ahih manin ka nu in clinic ah nurse kibang mah a ngen tawntung hi.

records.english: Will you come back next month and tell the children the rest of the story?
records.zomi: Kha hong ding ciangin hong pai kik inla tangthu taang naupangte kiangah na gen ding hiam?

records.english: My neighbor was a teacher at the night school, where she taught farmers to read after work.
records.zomi: Ka inn veng nitak sang ah saya ahi a, tua ah nasep khit ciangin lo neite lai sim a hilh hi.

records.english: Have you ever volunteered after a disaster?
records.zomi: Haksatna lian khit ciangin thalawp takin na sem ngei hiam?

records.english: Once, after the earthquake, and I learned more in that week than in years of school.
records.zomi: Vei khat, ling khit ciangin, tua kal sungin kum tampi sang kahna sangin tam zaw ka sin hi.

records.english: The volunteers who rebuilt the school after the fire still meet once a year to remember it.
records.zomi: Mei kat khit ciangin sang a lam kik thalawp nasemte tua phawk dingin kum simin vei khat a kimu lai uh hi.

records.english: Had the elders not written down the history, the town would have forgotten how it was founded.
records.zomi: Upate in tangthu a gelh kei uh leh khuapi in bangci-in a kiphut hiam a mangngilh ding hi.

records.english: When the hospital moved to the new building, the nurses carried the patients across the street one by one.
records.zomi: Zato inn thak ah a pem ciangin nurse te in damlote khat khit khat lampi a kantan pih uh hi.

records.english: The retired firefighter told us about the night the market burned, and nobody in the room said a word.
records.zomi: Mei mitsak khawl in zuakna mun a kan zan thu hong gen a, khan sung kuamah in kammal khat zong a gen kei uh hi.

records.english: When our family arrived as refugees, a teacher at the community center helped us fill in every form.
records.zomi: I innkuan gam taimang-in a tun ciangin mipi inn-a saya khat in lai khempeuh dimsak dingin hong huh hi.

records.english: Were the students' stories ever printed as a book for the families on the street?
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte' tangthute lampi-a innkuante adingin laibu-in kisuaksak ngei hiam?

records.english: All of you who helped after the storm, please come to the library and add your memories to the book.
records.zomi: Huihpi khit-a huh note khempeuh, laibu inn ah hong pai unla na phawknate uh laibu sungah behlap un.

records.english: What was it like to vote for the first time?
records.zomi: Vote na piak masa pen bangci ahi hiam?

records.english: We walked for two hours to the school, and I was shaking as I put my paper in the box.
records.zomi: Sang ah nai nih i kaai a, ka lai bawm sungah ka koih laitakin ka ling hi.

records.english: Everyone who came to the history evening wrote one memory on a card and pinned it to the board.
records.zomi: Tangthu nitak ah hong pai mi khempeuh in card khat tungah phawkna khat a gelh uh a, phek tungah a kap uh hi.

records.english: The town's first mayor used to hold council meetings under the mango tree because there was no hall.
records.zomi: Inn lian a om kei ahih manin khuapi ukpa masa pen in theihai kung nuai ah khuapi vaihawm kikhopna a bawl zel hi.

records.english: Sharing our memories at the history evening made the newcomers feel part of the town's story.
records.zomi: Tangthu nitak ah i phawknate i hawm in a tung thakte khuapi tangthu sung mi hi, cih a kisaksak hi.

records.english: Students, each of you will interview one older neighbor and record their story on the school's tablet.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte, note khat ciat in inn veng upa khat na dong ding a, a tangthu sang tablet tungah na la ding uh hi.

records.english: When the first ambulance arrived in our town, the driver let the children sit in the front seat.
records.zomi: I khuapi ah ambulance masa pen a tun ciangin tuansakpa in naupangte mai lam tutna ah a tusak hi.

records.english: Shall we ask the museum to film the elders telling their stories?
records.zomi: Upate in a tangthu uh a gen uh video tawh la dingin museum i ngen ding hiam?

records.english: How did people get help in an emergency before there were phones?
records.zomi: Phone om ma-in haksatna hun ah mite bangci-in huhna a ngah uh hiam?

records.english: Someone ran to ring the church bell, and every man in the village came running.
records.zomi: Kuamah khat pawlpi khawng khawn dingin a tai a, khua sung pasal khempeuh a tai uh hi.

records.english: My grandmother's diary from her years as a teacher was given to the library after she died.
records.zomi: Ka pi' saya a hih kum sung-a a diary a sih khit ciangin laibu inn kipia hi.

records.english: So many people came to hear the old nurse's stories that the library had to borrow chairs from the church.
records.zomi: Nurse upa' tangthu za dingin mi tampi a hong uh ahih manin laibu inn in pawlpi pan tutna a leitawi kul hi.

records.english: Did your grandparents ever talk about life before the clinic opened?
records.zomi: Clinic a kihon ma-a nuntakna thu na pu leh na pite in a gen ngei uh hiam?

records.english: The day the telephone line reached the village, everyone queued outside the shop to make their first call.
records.zomi: Phone khau khua a tun ni-in mi khempeuh in a phone sam masa pen bawl dingin dawl polam ah a kizom uh hi.

records.english: Did you really carry water from the river every morning before school?
records.zomi: Sang na kah ma-in zingsang simin gun pan tui na puak taktak hiam?

records.english: My grandfather's hands shook as he told the class about the year the river took the old church.
records.zomi: Gun in pawlpi lui a lak kum thu kilasi kiangah a gen laitakin ka pu' khut a ling hi.

records.english: Using an old tape recorder, my aunt saved the songs the women sang while planting rice.
records.zomi: Tape recorder lui zang-in ka ni in buh a suan laitakun numeite' sak la a kem hi.

records.english: Why did you decide to become a social worker?
records.zomi: Bang hangin mipi huhna nasempa suak dingin na khensat hiam?

records.english: A social worker helped my family when I was a child, and I never forgot her kindness.
records.zomi: Ka naupan lai-in mipi huhna nasempa khat in i innkuan a huh a, a hehpihna ka mangngilh ngei kei hi.

records.english: The museum asked the oldest residents to bring photos for an exhibition about the town's first school.
records.zomi: Museum in khuapi sang masa pen lim etsakna adingin teeng upa pente lim tawi dingin a ngen hi.

records.english: What's the most important thing you learned in your years on the council?
records.zomi: Khuapi vaihawm-a na om kumte sungin na sin thupi pen bang ahi hiam?

records.english: My uncle served on the village council for twenty years and still says the hardest job was choosing where to put the well.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu kum sawmnih sung khua vaihawm ah a om a, nasep haksa pen tuikhuk koihna mun teel ahi hi, a ci lai hi.

records.english: My grandmother worked as the village nurse for forty years, and she delivered most of the people now on the council.
records.zomi: Ka pi kum sawmli sung khua nurse-in na a sem a, tu-a khuapi vaihawm-a om tam zaw a suahsak hi.

records.english: When the clinic opened, my mother was the first patient, and she still keeps the appointment card.
records.zomi: Clinic a kihon ciangin ka nu pen damlo masa pen ahi a, a kimuhna card a kem lai hi.

records.english: I do want young people to know how hard their grandparents worked to build the school.
records.zomi: Sang lam dingin a pu leh pite uh bangzah hanciam takin na a sep uh hiam khangnote in a theih ding uh ka deih taktak hi.

records.english: It might be the last chance to hear the stories of the people who built the dam.
records.zomi: Tui khakna a lam mite' tangthu zak nading hun nunung pen hi kha ding hi.

records.english: Kids, listen carefully, because Grandpa is going to tell you how the bridge was built by hand.
records.zomi: Naupangte, limtakin ngai un, Pu in lei khut tawh bangci-in kilam hiam hong gen ding hi.

records.english: The library is collecting stories from people who remember the day electricity first reached the valley.
records.zomi: Laibu inn in guam ah meivak a tun masa pen ni a phawk mite' tangthu a kaikhawm hi.

records.english: Could I record your memories of the old post office for the town's history project?
records.zomi: Khuapi tangthu project adingin post office lui na phawknate ka la thei ding hiam?

records.english: My brother still talks about the summer he spent helping the doctors at the mobile clinic.
records.zomi: Kawikawi clinic ah siavuante a huh khal thu ka sanggam pasal in a gen lai hi.

records.english: Old stories about the first bus service made the whole lunch club laugh.
records.zomi: Bus masa pen thu tangthu luite in sun an pawl bup a nuisak hi.

records.english: The oldest woman in the village still remembers the name of every family who lived on our street.
records.zomi: Khua-a numei upa pen in i lampi-a om ngei innkuan khempeuh' min a phawk lai hi.

records.english: Did the valley's first postman really deliver letters on a mule?
records.zomi: Guam' lai puakpa masa pen in sakor-la tungah lai a puak taktak hiam?

records.english: Tell the children about the year the whole village shared one radio.
records.zomi: Khua bup in radio khat a kihawm kum thu naupangte kiangah gen in.

records.english: My neighbor's son, who emigrated thirty years ago, came back to tell the school how the town had changed.
records.zomi: Kum sawmthum paisa-in gamdang ah a pem ka inn veng' tapa khuapi bangci-in a kikhel hiam sang kiangah gen dingin a hong ciah kik hi.

records.english: Is there a museum where the town's old tools and photos are kept?
records.zomi: Khuapi' van lui leh lim luite kikemna museum khat a om hiam?

records.english: When the first road was built to our village, the children ran beside the trucks all the way to the church.
records.zomi: I khua ah lampi masa pen a kilam ciangin naupangte in mawtaw lian te gei ah pawlpi dong a tai uh hi.

records.english: Hearing the old miners describe their work underground, the students finally understood the town's history.
records.zomi: Suang tukte upate in lei nuai-a a nasep uh a gen siang uh a zak ciangun sangnaupangte in khuapi tangthu a thei tawp uh hi.

records.english: Would you share your story about the floods with the new families who have just moved here?
records.zomi: A tung thak innkuante kiangah tuiciim thu na tangthu na hawm ding hiam?

records.english: The old school register, with my grandfather's name in it, was found when the building was cleared out.
records.zomi: Inn a kisiangsak ciangin ka pu' min a kigelhna sang lai bu lui kimu hi.

records.english: I'm proud that I helped build the community center with my own hands.
records.zomi: Keima' khut tawh mipi inn ka lam huh manin ka kisaktheih hi.

records.english: There may be a book of the stories if the council gives the library a small grant.
records.zomi: Khuapi vaihawm in laibu inn sum huhna neu khat a piak leh tangthute laibu khat kibawl kha ding hi.

records.english: My mother cried when she found her own childhood photo in the museum's exhibition.
records.zomi: Museum lim etsakna sungah amah' naupan lai lim a muh ciangin ka nu a kap hi.

records.english: Can the old men from the lunch club come to the school and talk about their working lives?
records.zomi: Sun an pawl-a pasal upate in sang ah hong pai-in a nasep nuntakna uh a gen thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: Grandma remembers when the doctor came only once a month, on a horse.
records.zomi: Siavuan sakol tungah kha khat-in vei khat bek a hong hun Pi in a phawk hi.

records.english: The old bus driver remembered every passenger he had ever carried to the hospital.
records.zomi: Bus tuansak upa in zato ah a puak ngei tuang khempeuh a phawk hi.

records.english: The community radio plays one elder's life story every Sunday evening.
records.zomi: Mipi radio in Nipini nitak simin upa khat' nuntakna tangthu a sak hi.

records.english: My aunt was one of the first women in our town to stand for election.
records.zomi: Ka ni pen i khuapi ah teelna ah ding masa pen numeite lak pan khat ahi hi.

records.english: Every town keeps its history in the memories of its oldest people, and those memories can be lost in a single winter.
records.zomi: Khuapi khempeuh in a tangthu a upa pente' phawknate sungah a kem a, tua phawknate khuavot khat sungin a mang thei hi.

records.english: Is it all right to introduce myself to the new neighbors, or should I wait for them to come to me?
records.zomi: Inn veng thakte kiangah ka kitheisak ding hiam, kei kiangah a hong ding uh ka ngak ding hiam?

records.english: Go and knock on their door with a small gift; in our street, that's how it's done.
records.zomi: Letsong neu khat tawh a kongkhak va khawng in; i lampi ah tua bangin kibawl hi.

records.english: What should the children say when they meet the visiting bishop?
records.zomi: Hong veh bishop a muh ciangun naupangte in bang a gen ding uh hiam?

records.english: They should bow their heads, say their names, and wait for him to speak.
records.zomi: A lu uh kun ding uh a, a min uh gen ding uh a, amah a gen dong ngak ding uh hi.

records.english: Where did you learn to speak so well in front of people?
records.zomi: Mite mai ah hih bang hoih takin gen koi ah na sin hiam?

records.english: In the debate club at school, where we had to stand up and speak every week.
records.zomi: Sang-a kinial pawl ah, kal simin i ding-in i gen kul hi.

records.english: What's the polite way to begin an email to a stranger?
records.zomi: Mi theih lo khat kiangah email kipat nading zahtakna dan bang ahi hiam?

records.english: Say who you are, how you found their address, and why you're writing, all in the first few lines.
records.zomi: Kam khau masa tawmno sungin kua na hi hiam, a teenna koi pan na mu hiam leh bang hangin na gelh hiam gen in.

records.english: Does anyone ever shorten your name?
records.zomi: Kuamah in na min tom-in hong sam ngei hiam?

records.english: Most of them call me Mang, which is short for my full name.
records.zomi: A tam zaw in Mang hong ci uh a, ka min bup' tom ahi hi.

records.english: How much should I say on my first day as a volunteer?
records.zomi: Thalawp nasem-a ka ni masa pen-in bangzah ka gen ding hiam?

records.english: Just your name and what you'd like to help with; the rest will come with time.
records.zomi: Na min leh bang huh na deih hiam bek gen in; a taang hun tawh hong tung ding hi.

records.english: Shall we go round the room, starting with you, sir?
records.zomi: Pu, nang pan kipan-in khan sung kiim i kitheisak ding hiam?

records.english: I'm Pau from Church Street, and I've lived here since I was born.
records.zomi: Church Street pan Pau ka hi a, ka suah pan hih ah ka om hi.

records.english: Are you the new pharmacist everyone has been talking about?
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh in a gen zatui zuakpa thak nang na hi hiam?

records.english: I suppose I am, though I hope they've been saying nice things!
records.zomi: Kei ka hi kha ding hi, ahi zongin thu hoih a gen uh ka lamen hi!

records.english: Which name should I write on the form, my full name or the one I usually use?
records.zomi: Lai tungah min bang ka gelh ding hiam, ka min bup hiam, ka zat tawntung hiam?

records.english: Write your full name exactly as it appears on your identity card.
records.zomi: Na ID card tunga a om bangin na min bup gelh in.

records.english: What's the hardest part of introducing yourself in a new country?
records.zomi: Gam thak ah kitheisak ah a haksa pen bang ahi hiam?

records.english: Explaining where you're from when people have never heard of your home town.
records.zomi: Na khua a za ngei lo mite kiangah koi pan na hong pai hiam gen siang.

records.english: Do you want me to introduce you to the others, or would you rather do it yourself?
records.zomi: A dangte kiangah kong theisak ding hiam, nangma' mah in na sem nuam zaw hiam?

records.english: I do want to try it myself, but please stay nearby in case I forget anyone's name.
records.zomi: Kei mah in ka sem nuam taktak hi, ahi zongin kuamah' min ka mangngilh kha leh ci-in ka kiang ah om in.

records.english: If you had known the director was coming, would you have warned me?
records.zomi: Director hong pai ding na theih leh hong vaul ding na hi hiam?

records.english: I didn't know either, so we were both surprised when he introduced himself first.
records.zomi: Kei zong ka thei kei hi, tua ahih manin amah a kitheisak masa ciangin i nih in i lamdang sa hi.

records.english: Asked to introduce herself at the town meeting, the old woman simply said that she had lived on the hill for ninety years.
records.zomi: Khuapi kikhopna ah kitheisak dingin a kingen ciangin numei upa in mual tungah kum sawmkua a om khin hi, a ci bek hi.

records.english: Did you introduce yourself to your daughter's new teacher?
records.zomi: Na tanu' saya thak kiangah na kitheisak hiam?

records.english: Yes, at the gate this morning, and she already knew my daughter's name.
records.zomi: Kitheisak hi, tu zingsangin kongpi ah, ka tanu' min a thei khin hi.

records.english: What do you do for a living, if you don't mind my asking?
records.zomi: Na dot ka phal leh nuntak nadingin bang na sem hiam?

records.english: I repair phones at the market, and on weekends I help my uncle on the farm.
records.zomi: Zuakna mun ah phone ka bawl a, kal tawp-in ka pa neu' lo ah ka huh hi.

records.english: Can you help me write a short introduction for the church newsletter?
records.zomi: Pawlpi thuthak lai adingin kitheisakna tom khat gelh dingin hong huh thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Gladly — start with your name and why you've joined the parish.
records.zomi: Lungdam takin — na min leh bang hangin pawlpi ah na kihel hiam tawh kipan in.

records.english: How long have you lived in this town?
records.zomi: Hih khuapi ah bangzah sau na om khin hiam?

records.english: Only six months, but I already feel at home, thanks to my neighbors.
records.zomi: Kha guk bek, ahi zongin ka inn vengte hang-in inn ah om bangin ka kisa khin hi.

records.english: Could you speak a little more slowly, please?
records.zomi: Tawmno zawi zawin na gen thei ding hiam?

records.english: Sorry — I'm Thang, and I'm calling about my mother's appointment.
records.zomi: Hong maisak in — Thang ka hi a, ka nu' kimuhna thu-ah kong sam hi.

records.english: How should I introduce myself at a job interview?
records.zomi: Nasep dotna ah bangci-in ka kitheisak ding hiam?

records.english: Say your name clearly, smile, and mention one thing you're good at.
records.zomi: Na min kician takin gen in, nui in, na siamna khat gen in.

records.english: Would it help if I wore a name badge at the welcome lunch?
records.zomi: Muakna sun an ah min badge ka bulh leh a huh ding hiam?

records.english: Definitely, because there will be at least fifty new faces there.
records.zomi: Huh mahmah ding hi, tua ah mai thak sawmnga tan om ding ahih manin.

records.english: What would you like the garden group to know about you?
records.zomi: Huan pawl in na thu bang a theih ding uh na deih hiam?

records.english: Well, I'm Grace, I teach at the primary school, and I love growing beans.
records.zomi: Grace ka hi a, sang neu ah ka hilh a, be suan ka deih mahmah hi.

records.english: Is it true that you introduced yourself to the mayor without knowing who she was?
records.zomi: Kua ahi hiam thei lo-in khuapi ukpa nu kiangah na kitheisak hi, cih a man hiam?

records.english: It is, and she laughed and told me she was just the woman who sweeps the steps on Sundays.
records.zomi: Man hi, a nui a, Nipini simin kaplei phiat numei bek ka hi hi, hong ci hi.

records.english: Have we met before, or do you just remind me of someone?
records.zomi: I kimu ngei hiam, mi khat nang hong phawksak bek hiam?

records.english: We met at the clinic last spring, when you brought your father for his checkup.
records.zomi: Spring nung in clinic ah na pa a kienna adingin na paipih ciangin i kimu hi.

records.english: Is there time for me to say who I am at the start of the meeting?
records.zomi: Kikhopna kipatna ah kua ka hi hiam ka gen nading hun a om hiam?

records.english: Yes — everyone here would like to know who the new nurse is.
records.zomi: Om hi — hih ah mi khempeuh in nurse thak kua hiam a theih nuam uh hi.

records.english: Could you introduce yourself to the class using the microphone, so that everyone at the back can hear?
records.zomi: Nung lam-a mi khempeuh in a zak theih nadingun microphone zang-in kilasi kiangah na kitheisak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Good morning, everyone — I'm Mr. Kam, and I'll be your history teacher this year.
records.zomi: Zingpha, mi khempeuh — Mr. Kam ka hi a, tu kum na tangthu saya ka hi ding hi.

records.english: Will the elders want to know about my parents and grandparents?
records.zomi: Upate in ka nu leh ka pa leh ka pu leh pite thu a theih nuam ding uh hiam?

records.english: Yes, because they'll want to know whose child you are before anything else.
records.zomi: Theih nuam ding uh hi, na dang ma-in kua' ta na hi hiam a theih nuam ding uh ahih manin.

records.english: Do people in your village give their clan name when they introduce themselves?
records.zomi: Na khua ah mite in a kitheisak ciangun a phung min uh a gen uh hiam?

records.english: Yes, the older people always do, so that you know which family they come from.
records.zomi: Gen uh hi, upate in a gen tawntung uh a, koi innkuan pan a hong uh hiam na theih theih nadingin.

records.english: Is it rude to ask someone's age when you first meet them?
records.zomi: Na kimuh masa ciangin mi khat' kum dong pen zahtakna om lo ahi hiam?

records.english: Where I come from, older people don't mind, but young people often prefer not to say.
records.zomi: Ka hong suahna mun ah upate in a lungkham kei uh a, ahi zongin khangnote in gen lo a deih zaw uh hi.

records.english: Why did you introduce yourself in the local language?
records.zomi: Bang hangin khua pau tawh na kitheisak hiam?

records.english: Because I wanted the elders to see that I'm trying to learn it.
records.zomi: Ka sin hi, cih upate in a muh ding uh ka deih manin.

records.english: What would you say if someone asked you to describe yourself in three words?
records.zomi: Kammal thum tawh nangma' thu gen dingin kuamah in hong dot leh bang na ci ding hiam?

records.english: Patient, curious, and probably a little too fond of tea.
records.zomi: Thuakzawh, theih nuam, leh tea ka deih lua tawmno kha ding hi.

records.english: Introducing yourself well is less about what you say than about showing that you're interested in the other person.
records.zomi: Hoih taka kitheisak pen na gen thu sangin mi dang tungah na lungsim na koih hi, cih lak a thupi zaw hi.

records.english: Who's the tall young man standing next to your grandmother?
records.zomi: Na pi kiang-a ding khangno sang kua ahi hiam?

records.english: That's my cousin Mang, who's just come back from studying in the city.
records.zomi: Tua pen ka sanggam Mang ahi a, khuapi ah sang a kah pan hong ciah thak hi.

records.english: Could you introduce me to your neighbor who works at the hospital?
records.zomi: Zato ah na a sem na inn veng kiangah hong theisak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Gladly, and she might know someone who can help your mother.
records.zomi: Lungdam takin, na nu a huh thei kuamah a thei kha ding hi.

records.english: When did you first introduce your boyfriend to your parents?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa kiangah na lawm pasal bang ciangin na theisak masa hiam?

records.english: At my grandmother's birthday, which made it a little less frightening.
records.zomi: Ka pi' pianni-in, tua in a lauhuai tawmno a tawmsak hi.

records.english: Is it all right if I introduce you as my sister, even though you're my cousin?
records.zomi: Ka sanggam na hih hangin ka sanggam nu-in kong theisak leh a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: Go ahead, since we grew up in the same house.
records.zomi: Hoih hi, inn khat mah-ah i khan khawm manin.

records.english: If you could introduce your great-grandparents to your children, what would you want them to know?
records.zomi: Na pu leh pite' nu leh pate na tate kiangah na theisak thei leh bang a theih ding uh na deih ding hiam?

records.english: That they walked for days to start a new life here, so that we could have a better one.
records.zomi: Kote nuntakna hoih zaw i neih theih nadingun hih ah nuntakna thak kipat dingin ni tampi a kaai uh hi, cih.

records.english: Do your twins mind being introduced as "the twins"?
records.zomi: “Apengte” ci-a theisak na apengte in a lungkham uh hiam?

records.english: They hate it, so we always use their names, Cing and Niang.
records.zomi: A huat uh ahih manin a min uh Cing leh Niang i zang tawntung hi.

records.english: Would your brother be able to show my nephew around the college?
records.zomi: Na sanggam pasal in ka tanau college sung a etsak thei ding hiam?

records.english: I'm sure he would, since he's in his final year and knows everyone.
records.zomi: A etsak ding hi, ka thei hi, a kum nunung pen ahi a, mi khempeuh a thei hi.

records.english: Who taught your daughter to introduce people so politely?
records.zomi: Na tanu kua in zahtak taka mite theisak a hilh hiam?

records.english: Her grandmother made her practice with every visitor until she got it right.
records.zomi: A pi in a hoih dong hong veh khempeuh tawh a kisinsak hi.

records.english: Kids, would you show my colleagues the tree house you built?
records.zomi: Naupangte, na bawl uh sing tung inn neu ka nasem lawmte na etsak ding uh hiam?

records.english: Only if they promise not to climb up — it's only strong enough for us!
records.zomi: A kah lo ding uh a kiciam uh leh bek — kote bek adingin a hat hi!

records.english: Introducing a friend to your family is a way of telling them that this person matters to you.
records.zomi: Na innkuan kiangah lawm khat theisak pen hih mi in kei adingin a thupi hi, cih a gen nadan khat ahi hi.

records.english: Everyone, have you all met my husband's brother, who's visiting from the coast?
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, tuipi gei pan hong veh ka pasal' sanggam pasal na mu khin uh hiam?

records.english: Not yet, but he's already fixed the broken gate, so we like him very much.
records.zomi: Mu nai lo uh hi, ahi zongin kongpi kitam a bawl khin ahih manin i deih mahmah hi.

records.english: Would you like to meet my grandfather, who built half the houses on this street?
records.zomi: Hih lampi-a inn a kim a lam ka pu na muh nuam hiam?

records.english: I'd love to, because my own house might be one of them.
records.zomi: Ka deih mahmah hi, keima' inn zong a lak pan khat hi kha ding ahih manin.

records.english: Should I introduce my friend to the pastor before the service or after it?
records.zomi: Pawlpi ma-in ka lawm pastor kiangah ka theisak ding hiam, a nung ciangin hiam?

records.english: After, because he's always busy getting ready beforehand.
records.zomi: A nung ciangin, a ma-in a kiman dingin a buai tawntung ahih manin.

records.english: Is the boy you brought to church your son or your nephew?
records.zomi: Pawlpi ah na paipih naupang pasal na tapa hiam, na tanau hiam?

records.english: My nephew, but he lives with us while his parents work abroad.
records.zomi: Ka tanau, ahi zongin a nu leh pa gamdang ah na a sep laitakun i kiang ah a om hi.

records.english: Did you know that my new colleague is your old classmate?
records.zomi: Ka nasem lawm thak na sang lawm lui ahi hi, cih na thei hiam?

records.english: I had no idea — we sat next to each other in the last year of school!
records.zomi: Ka thei ngei kei — sang kum nunung pen-in i kikiang-in i tu hi!

records.english: What would you say if your parents disliked the friend you brought home?
records.zomi: Na inn ah na paipih lawm na nu leh na pa in a deih kei uh leh bang na ci ding hiam?

records.english: I'd ask them to give her a second chance, because first meetings are always awkward.
records.zomi: Kimuhna masa pen a lamdang tawntung ahih manin hun nihna a piak ding uh ka ngen ding hi.

records.english: Why does everyone call your aunt "Big Mother"?
records.zomi: Bang hangin mi khempeuh in na ni “Nu Lian” a ci uh hiam?

records.english: Because she's the eldest of eight, and she raised most of her brothers and sisters.
records.zomi: Giat lak ah a upa pen ahi a, a sanggam tam zaw a khak hi.

records.english: So warmly was my roommate welcomed by my family that she now spends every holiday with us.
records.zomi: Ka khan kihawm lawm ka innkuan in lungsim lum takin a muak uh ahih manin tu-in tawlngakni khempeuh i kiang ah a zang hi.

records.english: Could you take a photo of me with my cousins before they leave?
records.zomi: Ka sanggamte a pai ma-un amaute tawh lim hong lak sak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Stand closer together, all of you, or I won't get everyone in.
records.zomi: Note khempeuh kinai zawin ding un, ahih kei leh mi khempeuh ka la zo lo ding hi.

records.english: How should I introduce my stepfather to my teachers?
records.zomi: Ka sayate kiangah ka pakik bangci-in ka theisak ding hiam?

records.english: Say whatever feels natural to you; many children simply say "my dad."
records.zomi: Na kisak bangin gen in; naupang tampi in “ka pa” ci bek uh hi.

records.english: Have you introduced your fiancé to the whole family yet?
records.zomi: Na kiteen ding pasal innkuan bup kiangah na theisak khin hiam?

records.english: Not the whole family — there are sixty of us, so it'll take a few more weekends.
records.zomi: Innkuan bup hi lo hi — sawmguk i hih manin kal tawp tawmno a sau lai ding hi.

records.english: How did you end up being friends with your neighbor's grandmother?
records.zomi: Na inn veng' pi tawh bangci-in na kilawm hiam?

records.english: I helped her carry her shopping one day, and she's been inviting me to tea ever since.
records.zomi: Ni khat a van a puak ka huh a, tua pan tea dawn dingin hong sam den hi.

records.english: How are you and the bride related?
records.zomi: Nang leh moulai bangci-in na kizom uh hiam?

records.english: Her mother and my father are brother and sister, so we're first cousins.
records.zomi: A nu leh ka pa sanggam ahi uh ahih manin sanggam kinai i hi hi.

records.english: Can I bring my best friend to the family dinner on Sunday?
records.zomi: Nipini innkuan nitak an ah ka lawm hoih pen ka paipih thei ding hiam?

records.english: Bring her, and we'll set an extra place at the table.
records.zomi: Paipih in, dawhkan ah mun behlap khat i koih ding hi.

records.english: Did your father-in-law really make you sing at your first family dinner?
records.zomi: Na innkuan nitak an masa pen-in na sungpa in la hong sasak taktak hiam?

records.english: He did, and I've been asked to sing at every family dinner since.
records.zomi: Sasak hi, tua pan innkuan nitak an khempeuh ah la sa dingin hong ngen uh hi.

records.english: What's the polite way to introduce an older relative to a younger friend in your family?
records.zomi: Na innkuan ah beh leh phung upa khat lawm naupang zaw kiangah theisak dan zahtakna bang ahi hiam?

records.english: We always say the older person's name first and add a title like "Uncle" or "Grandmother."
records.zomi: Upa' min a masa-in i gen a, “Pu” hiam “Pi” bang min i behlap tawntung hi.

records.english: Do you think your grandfather would mind if I asked him about the old days?
records.zomi: Hun lui thu ka dot leh na pu a lungkham ding in na ngaihsun hiam?

records.english: Not at all — he'll talk for hours, so make sure you've eaten first.
records.zomi: Lungkham lo ding hi — nai tampi a gen ding ahih manin na ne khin hiam kician takin en in.

records.english: Why did your son introduce me to his friends as "the best cook in the world"?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na tapa in a lawmte kiangah “leitung-a an huan siam pen” ci-in hong theisak hiam?

records.english: Because you fed him every day when I was in hospital, and he's never forgotten it.
records.zomi: Zato ah ka om laitakin ni simin na vak ahih manin, a mangngilh ngei kei hi.

records.english: Where did your parents meet?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa koi ah a kimu uh hiam?

records.english: At the market, where my mother sold vegetables and my father kept buying more than he needed.
records.zomi: Zuakna mun ah, ka nu in anteh a zuak a, ka pa in a kisap sangin a tam zaw a lei den hi.

records.english: Is that your sister in the photo, or your mother when she was young?
records.zomi: Lim sung ah na sanggam nu hiam, na nu a khangno lai hiam?

records.english: It's my mother at twenty, and everyone says I look exactly like her.
records.zomi: Kum sawmnih a phak lai ka nu ahi a, mi khempeuh in a kibang kim ka hi uh hi, a ci uh hi.

records.english: May I show your grandmother the photos of my family on my phone?
records.zomi: Ka phone tung-a ka innkuan limte na pi ka etsak thei ding hiam?

records.english: She'd love that, but hold the phone close, because her eyes aren't good.
records.zomi: A deih mahmah ding hi, ahi zongin a mit a hoih kei ahih manin phone a kiang ah koih in.

records.english: Will you look at my science project this week?
records.zomi: Hih kal sungin ka science project na en ding hiam?

records.english: I'll write some comments on it and give it back to you on Monday.
records.zomi: A tung ah ngaihsutna tawmno ka gelh ding a, Pizing ni ciangin kong pia kik ding hi.

records.english: I've left my book at home, so would you mind if I shared with Pau?
records.zomi: Ka laibu inn ah ka nusia ahih manin Pau tawh ka kihawm leh na lungkham ding hiam?

records.english: You might do better next time if you read each question twice.
records.zomi: Dotna khat ciat nihvei na sim leh a zom ciangin na hoih zaw kha ding hi.

records.english: Please don't copy your friend's answers; I want to see what you think.
records.zomi: Na lawm' dawnnate gelh kik kei in; bang na ngaihsun hiam ka muh nuam hi.

records.english: The more questions I asked, the more my teacher seemed to enjoy explaining.
records.zomi: Dotna tam zaw ka dot ciangin ka saya in gen siang a nuam sa semsem bang hi.

records.english: Sorry, I wasn't listening — could you say that again?
records.zomi: Hong maisak in, ka ngai kei hi — na gen kik thei ding hiam?

records.english: Why weren't you at school yesterday?
records.zomi: Bang hangin zanni-in sang na kah kei hiam?

records.english: I had a fever, and my mother wrote you a note.
records.zomi: Cisa ka nei a, ka nu in lai hong gelh sak hi.

records.english: Excuse me, Ms. Lian, could you explain the last question again?
records.zomi: Hong maisak in, Ms. Lian, dotna nunung pen na gen siang kik thei ding hiam?

records.english: Gladly — come to my desk, and we'll go through it together.
records.zomi: Lungdam takin — ka dawhkan ah hong pai inla khawm in i sem ding hi.

records.english: You seem worried today — is everything all right at home?
records.zomi: Tuni-in na lungkham bang hi — inn ah khempeuh a hoih hiam?

records.english: Which part didn't you understand?
records.zomi: Tan bang na thei kei hiam?

records.english: I followed the first example, but I got lost when you started dividing fractions.
records.zomi: A etsakna masa pen ka thei a, ahi zongin khen tan na khen kipat ciangin ka mang hi.

records.english: The note my teacher wrote on my report was so kind that my parents read it twice.
records.zomi: Ka report tungah ka saya' gelh thu a hoih lua ahih manin ka nu leh ka pa in nihvei a sim uh hi.

records.english: You're allowed to use a calculator for this part of the test, but not for the rest.
records.zomi: Hih sitna tan ah calculator na zang thei a, ahi zongin a taang ah zang thei lo hi.

records.english: Could you speak a little louder, please, because we can't hear you at the back?
records.zomi: Nung lam pan i za thei kei ahih manin tawmno ging sang zawin na gen thei ding hiam?

records.english: What the teacher noticed most was that I had stopped putting my hand up in class.
records.zomi: Saya in a muh pen kilasi ah ka khut ka dom nawn loh ahi hi.

records.english: Did I do this exercise the right way?
records.zomi: Hih nasep a dik takin ka sem hiam?

records.english: Almost — you just forgot to show how you got the answer.
records.zomi: Dik dek hi — dawnna bangci-in na ngah hiam lak na mangngilh bek hi.

records.english: Having noticed me squinting at the board, my teacher quietly moved me to the front row.
records.zomi: Bang tung ah ka mit ka zim ka muh manin ka saya in dai takin mai lam tutna ah hong pemsak hi.

records.english: When is the next test?
records.zomi: Sitna zom bang ciangin ahi hiam?

records.english: Next Friday, and it will cover everything we did this month.
records.zomi: Laithai ni hong ding, tu kha sung i sep khempeuh kihel ding hi.

records.english: Phones aren't allowed during my lessons, so please put yours in your bag.
records.zomi: Ka hilhna sungin phone kiphal lo ahih manin na phone na ip sungah koih in.

records.english: Thank you for staying behind to help me clean the classroom after the art lesson.
records.zomi: Lim gelh hilhna khit ciangin kilasi siangsak dingin hong huh dingin na om manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: I'm sorry I'm late, but the bus broke down halfway to school.
records.zomi: Hong maisak in, ka nun hi, ahi zongin sang pai lampi kimlai-in bus a sia hi.

records.english: Could you tell me what I got on the math test, and where I lost marks?
records.zomi: Math sitna ah bangzah ka ngah a, koi ah ciamte ka mansuah hiam hong gen thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: The teacher asked me why I was so quiet, and I finally told her I was nervous.
records.zomi: Bang hangin na dai mahmah hiam ci-in saya in hong dong a, a tawp-in ka lau hi, ka ci hi.

records.english: Had I asked for help sooner, I wouldn't have failed the first test.
records.zomi: Huhna hun ma-in ka ngen leh sitna masa pen ka zo lo kei ding hi.

records.english: My teacher made me rewrite the story, and the second version was much better.
records.zomi: Ka saya in tangthu hong gelh kiksak a, a nihna pen a hoih zaw mahmah hi.

records.english: Our teacher greets each of us by name every morning, which makes us feel noticed.
records.zomi: I saya in zingsang simin i khat ciat i min tawh hong hopih a, tua in i om hiam a mu hi, i kisaksak hi.

records.english: I'm proud of you for trying so hard, even though the test was difficult.
records.zomi: Sitna a haksa hangin hanciam takin na sep manin na tung ah ka kisaktheih hi.

records.english: Is it okay to ask questions during the lesson, or should I wait until the end?
records.zomi: Hilhna laitakin dotna dot a hoih ding hiam, a tawp dong ka ngak ding hiam?

records.english: Ask whenever you're confused, because other students probably have the same question.
records.zomi: Na buai simin dong in, sangnaupang dangte in zong dotna kibang a nei kha ding uh ahih manin.

records.english: Please give this letter to your parents and bring it back signed.
records.zomi: Hih lai na nu leh na pa pia inla min a suaksak khit ciangin hong tawi kik in.

records.english: The teacher said, "There's no such thing as a silly question in this room."
records.zomi: Saya in, “Hih khan ah dotna mawk om ngei lo hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: Would it be all right if I handed in my homework tomorrow, since I was ill last night?
records.zomi: Zanni zanin ka dam kei ahih manin zingciang ka inn-a sep ding ka pia leh a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: Rather than scolding me for the mistake, my teacher showed me how to fix it.
records.zomi: Khialhna adingin hong taai sangin ka saya in a bawl kik dan hong etsak hi.

records.english: My teacher let me take the book home so that I could finish the story.
records.zomi: Ka saya in tangthu ka zawh theih nadingin laibu inn ah hong tawisak hi.

records.english: Good teachers listen to their students as carefully as they explain things to them.
records.zomi: Saya hoihte in a gen siang uh bangmah in pilvang takin a sangnaupangte uh thu a ngai uh hi.

records.english: How can I get better at speaking in front of the class?
records.zomi: Kilasi mai ah gen ah bangci-in ka hoih zaw thei ding hiam?

records.english: Practice at home in front of a mirror, and start with short talks.
records.zomi: Inn ah mai-et mai ah kisin inla, thugen tomte tawh kipan in.

records.english: Students mustn't leave the room without asking the teacher first.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte in saya dong masa lo-in khan a paisan thei kei ding uh hi.

records.english: I'm sorry I was rude to you yesterday.
records.zomi: Zanni-in kong kik gen manin hong maisak in.

records.english: If you need more time, just ask me before the deadline.
records.zomi: Hun behlap na kisap leh a ni a tun ma-in hong dong bek in.

records.english: Your handwriting has improved so much this term that I can read every word.
records.zomi: Hih term sungin na laigelh a hoih zaw lua ahih manin kammal khempeuh ka sim thei hi.

records.english: May I talk to you after class?
records.zomi: Kilasi khit ciangin kong kiho thei ding hiam?

records.english: Could you check my essay before I give it in?
records.zomi: Ka piak ma-in ka laigelh na en sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Can I go to the toilet, please?
records.zomi: Ek inn ah ka pai thei ding hiam?

records.english: Tell me if anyone is unkind to you, and I'll deal with it.
records.zomi: Kuamah in hong hehpih kei leh hong gen in, ka bawl siang ding hi.

records.english: Who should I ask if you're not here?
records.zomi: Na om kei leh kua ka dong ding hiam?

records.english: Ask Mr. Kam in the next classroom; he knows our lessons.
records.zomi: A kiang kilasi-a Mr. Kam dong in; i hilhnate a thei hi.

records.english: Can I say sorry for what I said yesterday?
