records.zomi: Zanni-a ka gen thu adingin maisak ngen thei ding ka hi hiam?

records.english: Thank you for saying sorry; let's start again today.
records.zomi: Maisak na ngen manin ka lungdam hi; tuni-in kipan kik ni.

records.english: If you finish early, you can help someone who is still working.
records.zomi: A man masa leh na sep laitak lai a om kuamah na huh thei hi.

records.english: I don't understand this word — what does it mean?
records.zomi: Hih kammal ka thei kei hi — bang a cih nopna ahi hiam?

records.english: There may be extra lessons on Saturday for anyone who needs help before the exam.
records.zomi: Sitna ma-in huhna a kisapte adingin Kiginni-in hilhna behlap a om kha ding hi.

records.english: Not once did my teacher complain about staying after school to help me with my reading.
records.zomi: Ka simna a huh dingin sang khit ciangin a om manin ka saya in khatvei zong a phun ngei kei hi.

records.english: Can you help me with this word in the story?
records.zomi: Tangthu sung-a hih kammal ah hong huh thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Look it up in the dictionary first, and then tell me what you found.
records.zomi: Kammal laibu ah a masa-in zong inla, tua ciangin na muh hong gen in.

records.english: Could you carry Grandpa's suitcase up to the guest room for him?
records.zomi: Na pu' van bawm khualzin khan ah a ding in na pua thei ding hiam?

records.english: Sure, and I'll open the window, since the room has been closed all week.
records.zomi: Hi ka, kal bup khan a kikhak ahih manin tukvuang ka hong ding hi.

records.english: Did you have the guest room painted before your in-laws came?
records.zomi: Na sungte a hong tun ma-un khualzin khan na zeek sak hiam?

records.english: We did, and my husband even fixed the wardrobe door that had been broken for years.
records.zomi: Zeek sak hi, ka pasal in kum tampi a sia puan bawm kongkhak zong a bawl siang hi.

records.english: Could you translate for the visitors during the village meeting?
records.zomi: Khua kikhopna sungin khual hongte adingin na lehkik sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: I'll try, but please ask the speakers to talk slowly.
records.zomi: Ka sin ding hi, ahi zongin thugente in zawl takin a gen nadingun ngen in.

records.english: What would you do if guests arrived while you were still cooking?
records.zomi: An na huan laitakin khual a hong tun leh bang na hih ding hiam?

records.english: Give them tea, put on some music, and ask them to tell me about their trip.
records.zomi: Tea pia inla, la tawmno sak inla, a khualzinna uh thu hong gen dingin ngen in.

records.english: Had you known how many relatives were coming, would you have hired the community hall?
records.zomi: Na sanggam bangzah a hong ding uh hiam na theih leh mipi inn na hal ding hiam?

records.english: Absolutely, because forty people in our little house was more than anyone expected.
records.zomi: Hal ding mahmah ing, i inn neu sung ah mi sawmli pen kuamah' ngaihsut sangin a tam zaw ahih manin.

records.english: Is there anything you can't eat, so that I can plan tonight's dinner?
records.zomi: Tuni nitak an ka gel theih nadingin na ne theih loh bangmah a om hiam?

records.english: Nothing at all, though I'm not used to very spicy food.
records.zomi: Bangmah om lo hi, ahi zongin a ha mahmah an ka ne zia kei hi.

records.english: Why don't the visitors stay at the hotel instead?
records.zomi: Bang hangin khual hongte zinbuuk ah om lo uh hiam?

records.english: Because in our family, relatives always stay with relatives, however small the house is.
records.zomi: I innkuan ah inn bangzah ta in neu zongin sanggamte sanggamte kiang ah a om tawntung uh ahih manin.

records.english: Who will meet the visiting doctors at the station?
records.zomi: Khual hong siavuante meileng dinna ah kua in a dawn ding hiam?

records.english: The mayor's driver, and he'll bring them straight to the clinic.
records.zomi: Khuapi makaipa' mawtaw mawngpa in, tua pen siavuan inn ah a tang takin a paipih ding hi.

records.english: Have you told the visitors that the water is off on Tuesday mornings?
records.zomi: Pithai ni zingsang tui a om lo hi, ci-in khual hongte na hilh khin hiam?

records.english: Not yet, so I'll fill some buckets for them tonight.
records.zomi: Hilh nai lo ka hi, tua ahih manin tuni zanin amaute adingin bawm tawmno ka dimsak ding hi.

records.english: Can visitors walk around the hospital garden, or only patients?
records.zomi: Khual hongte zato huan sung ah a vak thei uh hiam, natnate bek ahi hiam?

records.english: Anyone can walk there, as long as they keep to the paths.
records.zomi: Lampi tung bek ah a kalsuan uh leh kua peuhpeuh in tua ah a vak thei hi.

records.english: What is it about your grandmother's house that makes every visitor feel at home?
records.zomi: Na pi' inn ah bang in khual hong khempeuh a inn bangin a kisaksak hiam?

records.english: She remembers everyone's favorite food and has it waiting on the table when they arrive.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh' an deih pen a phawk a, a hong tun ciangun dawhkan tungah a ngak khin hi.

records.english: When do you have to be back at work?
records.zomi: Bang ciangin na nasepna ah na kik ding hiam?

records.english: On Monday, so I'll catch the bus home on Sunday afternoon, if that's not too much trouble.
records.zomi: Pizing ni, tua ahih manin a buaipih lua kei leh Nipini nitak lam ciangin inn ah bus tawh ka ciah ding hi.

records.english: May I use your phone to tell my family I've arrived safely?
records.zomi: Damtak ka tung hi, ci-in ka innkuan ka hilh nadingin na phone ka zang thei ding hiam?

records.english: Go ahead, and use the Wi-Fi too — the password is on the fridge.
records.zomi: Zang in, Wi-Fi zong zang in — password pen khal bawm tungah a om hi.

records.english: How was the journey from the coast?
records.zomi: Tuipi gei pan na khualzinna bangci hiam?

records.english: Long, but the bus driver stopped twice so that we could stretch our legs.
records.zomi: A sau hi, ahi zongin i khe i zan theih nadingun bus mawngpa in nihvei a tawlngak hi.

records.english: Are visitors allowed to take photos inside the factory?
records.zomi: Khual hongte in factory sung ah lim a la thei uh hiam?

records.english: Not near the machines, but you're welcome to take them in the garden.
records.zomi: Set kiang ah la thei lo hi, ahi zongin huan sung ah na la thei hi.

records.english: Shall we leave a key under the mat in case the visitors arrive before we get home?
records.zomi: I inn i tun ma-un khual hongte a hong tun kha leh tuutphah nuai ah tawh khat i koih ding hiam?

records.english: Better to leave it with the neighbor, who'll be home all afternoon.
records.zomi: Nitak lam bup inn ah a om ding inn veng kiang ah koih leh a hoih zaw hi.

records.english: Can I take my shoes off here, or do you keep them on inside?
records.zomi: Hih ah ka khedap ka sut thei ding hiam, inn sung ah na bulh tawntung uh hiam?

records.english: We take them off, but there are slippers by the door for guests.
records.zomi: I sut hi, ahi zongin kongkhak kiang ah khual hongte adingin khedap neu a om hi.

records.english: Why did your mother make everyone wait at the gate before the guests arrived?
records.zomi: Khual a hong tun ma-un bang hangin na nu in mi khempeuh kongpi ah a ngaksak hiam?

records.english: In our village, it's rude to let guests walk to the door alone.
records.zomi: I khua ah khualte kongkhak dong amau bek a kalsuansak pen zahtakna om lo ahi hi.

records.english: Do you think the guests would mind sharing a room?
records.zomi: Khualte in khan khat a kihawm leh a lungkham ding uh in na ngaihsun hiam?

records.english: They're sisters, so I'm sure they'll be happy together.
records.zomi: Sanggam nute ahi uh ahih manin khawm-in a lungdam ding uh hi, ka thei hi.

records.english: Why did the hotel give the elderly guests rooms on the ground floor?
records.zomi: Bang hangin zinbuuk in khual upate nuai lam inn tuang ah khan a piak hiam?

records.english: Because the lift had broken, and the manager didn't want them climbing stairs.
records.zomi: Lift a sia a, a makaipa in kahleite a kah ding uh a deih kei ahih manin.

records.english: Welcoming visitors well is less about a perfect house than about making people feel expected.
records.zomi: Khual hongte hoih taka muak pen inn kicing nei sangin mite kingak bangin kisaksak lam ahi zaw hi.

records.english: Is it true that you met the new teacher at the bus stop with a sign?
records.zomi: Saya thak bus dinna ah lai tawh na dawn hi, cih a tak ahi hiam?

records.english: Yes, I wrote her name on a piece of cardboard, because I had never seen her before.
records.zomi: Hi hi, a ma-in ka mu ngei kei ahih manin laipek khat tungah a min ka gelh hi.

records.english: What should we say to the visitors from the ministry when they arrive at the school?
records.zomi: Sang ah a hong tun ciangun ministry pan hong khual hongte bang i ci ding uh hiam?

records.english: Say good morning, tell them your name, and offer to show them your classroom.
records.zomi: “Zingpha” ci un, na min uh gen un, na kilasi uh etsak dingin ngen un.

records.english: Would the children be safe in the garden while the adults have lunch inside?
records.zomi: Upate in inn sungah sun an a nek laitakun naupangte huan sungah a bitna ding uh hiam?

records.english: Yes, but please keep them away from the pond.
records.zomi: Bit hi, ahi zongin tuili kiang ah a pai lo nadingun en un.

records.english: If the train is delayed, could you wait for my parents at the station?
records.zomi: Meileng a sawt leh meileng dinna ah ka nu leh ka pa na ngak thei ding hiam?

records.english: No problem — I'll take a book and wait in the café on the platform.
records.zomi: Bangmah om lo — laibu khat ka tawi ding a, platform tung-a cafe ah ka ngak ding hi.

records.english: How did the village welcome the medical team last year?
records.zomi: Kum nung in khua in siavuan pawl bangci-in a muak uh hiam?

records.english: With songs at the bridge and a meal that every family helped to cook.
records.zomi: Lei ah la tawh, innkuan khempeuh in a huan khawm an tawh.

records.english: Have we reserved any parking spaces for the inspectors?
records.zomi: Enkaktute adingin mawtaw koihna mun i koih khol uh hiam?

records.english: In front of the main building — we've kept three spaces free for them.
records.zomi: Inn lianpi mai ah — amaute adingin mun thum i koih khin hi.

records.english: Would you like to rest first, or shall I show you around the house?
records.zomi: A masa-in na tawldam nuam hiam, inn kong etsak ding hiam?

records.english: A short rest, please, and then I'd love to see the garden.
records.zomi: Tawlkhat tawldam ka deih hi, tua ciangin huan en ka deih mahmah hi.

records.english: Not until the guests had gone did we realize that nobody had taken a single photo.
records.zomi: Khualte a pai khit uh ciangin bek kuamah in lim khat zong la lo hi, cih i thei hi.

records.english: Would it be rude to ask our guests to take their shoes off?
records.zomi: I khualte uh khedap sut dingin ngen pen zahtakna om lo ahi ding hiam?

records.english: Not at all, as long as you ask kindly and show them where to leave them.
records.zomi: Hi lo ding hi, nuam takin na ngen a, koi ah koih ding uh hiam na etsak leh.

records.english: Is it customary in your town to bring a gift when you visit someone's home?
records.zomi: Na khua ah mi' inn na veh ciangin letsong tawi pen ngeina ahi hiam?

records.english: Yes, usually some fruit or a cake, but never anything too expensive.
records.zomi: Hi hi, a tamzaw-in gah tawmno hiam cake hiam, ahi zongin a man tam lua bangmah tawi ngei lo hi.

records.english: How do you say goodbye to colleagues when you leave a job?
records.zomi: Nasep na nusiat ciangin na nasem lawmte bangci-in goodbye na ci hiam?

records.english: I usually bring a cake on my last day and write a short note to each person I worked closely with.
records.zomi: Ka ni nunung pen-in cake ka tawi den a, ka kiang-a nasem khawm mi khat ciat adingin lai tomno ka gelh hi.

records.english: Do you mind if I don't come to the airport?
records.zomi: Vanlengtual ah ka hong kei leh na lungkham ding hiam?

records.english: Not at all — I'd rather say goodbye here than cry in front of strangers.
records.zomi: Lungkham lo ing — mi theih lohte mai ah kap sangin hih ah goodbye ci ka deih zaw hi.

records.english: Shall I pack some food for your journey?
records.zomi: Na khualzinna adingin an tawmno kong thuk sak ding hiam?

records.english: Just a little, because the bus stops at a market halfway.
records.zomi: Tawmno bek, bus in lampi kimlai-a zuakna mun ah a tawl ding ahih manin.

records.english: What time does your bus leave tomorrow?
records.zomi: Zingciang na bus nai bangzah ciangin a pai ding hiam?

records.english: At six, so I'll say goodbye to everyone tonight.
records.zomi: Nai guk ciangin, tua ahih manin tuni zanin mi khempeuh goodbye ka ci ding hi.

records.english: Watching the bus disappear round the corner, the old man stood waving long after it had gone.
records.zomi: Lampi kiheina ah bus a mang a en-in, a pai khit sawt nung dong pasal upa in ding-in a khut a vaai hi.

records.english: Please don't make a speech at my farewell party, will you?
records.zomi: Ka kikhenna pawi ah thugen bawl kei in, maw?

records.english: Just a short one, and I promise not to tell the story about the goat.
records.zomi: A tomno khat bek, kel tangthu ka gen kei ding hi, ka kiciam hi.

records.english: How long did your goodbye at the bus station take?
records.zomi: Bus dinna ah na goodbye cihna bangzah a sawt hiam?

records.english: So long that the driver started the engine twice to hurry us.
records.zomi: A sau lua ahih manin hong hanthawn dingin mawngpa in set nihvei a khuk hi.

records.english: Isn't it a pity to leave just as the festival is beginning?
records.zomi: Pawi a kipat laitakin pai khia pen a lungkhamhuai hi lo hiam?

records.english: I'd love to, but my boss expects me at the office first thing tomorrow.
records.zomi: Om ka deih hi, ahi zongin ka makaipa in zingciang zingsang tung ah office ah hong ngak hi.

records.english: Why did the teacher make the whole class write farewell letters to Mrs. Lun?
records.zomi: Bang hangin saya in kilasi bup Mrs. Lun adingin kikhenna lai a gelhsak hiam?

records.english: Because she's retiring after thirty years, and the teacher wanted her to have something to keep.
records.zomi: Kum sawmthum nasem khit ciangin a tawl ding ahih manin, saya in a kemcing ding bangmah a neih a deih manin.

records.english: Was it hard for your parents when you left for university?
records.zomi: Sangpi ah na pai ciangin na nu leh na pa adingin a haksa hiam?

records.english: My mother cooked my favorite meal every night for a week before I went.
records.zomi: Ka pai ma-in kal khat sung zan simin ka nu in ka an deih pen a huan hi.

records.english: Who's going to feed your chickens while you're working abroad?
records.zomi: Gamdang ah na nasep laitakin na akte kua in an a vak ding hiam?

records.english: My neighbor, who has promised to check on them every morning.
records.zomi: Ka inn veng in, zingsang simin a en ding a kiciam hi.

records.english: What's the hardest goodbye you've ever had to say?
records.zomi: Na goodbye cih haksat pen bang ahi hiam?

records.english: Leaving my children with their grandparents when I went to work in the city.
records.zomi: Khuapi ah nasem dingin ka pai ciangin ka tate a pu leh pite kiangah ka nusiat ahi hi.

records.english: Is it true that you waved from the ship until you couldn't see the harbor anymore?
records.zomi: Tuipi gei mun na muh nawn loh dong tembaw tung pan na khut na vaai hi, cih a tak ahi hiam?

records.english: It is, and my arm ached for the rest of the day, though I didn't care.
records.zomi: A tak hi, ni bup ka ban a na hi, ahi zongin ka lungkham kei hi.

records.english: Why are you crying, sweetheart?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na kap hiam, ka it?

records.english: Because my best friend is moving to another town, and I won't see her at school anymore.
records.zomi: Ka lawm hoih pen khua dang ah a tuah ding a, sang ah ka mu nawn kei ding ahih manin.

records.english: Could you take a photo of us all before the car leaves?
records.zomi: Mawtaw a pai ma-in eite khempeuh lim hong la sak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Everyone, move a little closer, and try not to cry this time!
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, tawmno kinai zaw un, tuin kap lo dingin sin un!

records.english: Can I keep your scarf until you come back?
records.zomi: Na hong ciah kik dong na ngawngkhih ka kem thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, and wear it when you miss me.
records.zomi: Thei hi, hong lungngaih ciangin bulh in.

records.english: However often we say goodbye at the station, it never gets any easier.
records.zomi: Meileng dinna ah bangzah vei goodbye i ci zongin a nuam semsem ngei kei hi.

records.english: Is it bad luck in your family to look back as you leave the house?
records.zomi: Na innkuan ah inn na nusiat ciangin nung lam en pen siatna ahi hiam?

records.english: My aunt thinks so, but the rest of us always turn and wave.
records.zomi: Ka ni in tua bangin a ngaihsun hi, ahi zongin a dang khempeuh in i kihei kik-in khut i vaai tawntung hi.

records.english: When will we see you again?
records.zomi: Bang ciangin kong mu kik ding uh hiam?

records.english: At Christmas, if I can get time off work.
records.zomi: Christmas ciangin, nasepna pan hun ka ngah thei leh.

records.english: What will you miss most about this town?
records.zomi: Hih khuapi ah bang na lungngai pen ding hiam?

records.english: The market on Saturday mornings and the way everyone says hello in the street.
records.zomi: Kiginni zingsang-a zuakna mun leh lampi ah mi khempeuh in a kihopih dan.

records.english: Is there anything you'd like us to send after you, in case you've forgotten it?
records.zomi: Na mangngilh kha leh na nung ah kong khak ding na deih bangmah a om hiam?

records.english: Just my reading glasses, if you find them — I think I left them in the kitchen.
records.zomi: Ka laisimna mitlimlang bek, na muh leh — an huanna ah ka nusia kha in ka ngaihsun hi.

records.english: Should we wake the children to say goodbye, or let them sleep?
records.zomi: Goodbye a cih nadingun naupangte i phawngsak ding hiam, a ihmut uh i nusia ding hiam?

records.english: Wake them, because they'll be upset all day if they miss it.
records.zomi: Phawngsak un, a mansuah uh leh ni bup a lungkham ding uh ahih manin.

records.english: Can we walk you to the station?
records.zomi: Meileng dinna dong kong paipih thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: I'd like that, but only if you let me carry my own bag.
records.zomi: Ka deih hi, ahi zongin keima' ip keimah in hong pua sak leh bek.

records.english: Are we allowed to stay at the hospital after visiting hours to say goodbye?
records.zomi: Goodbye cih dingin veh hun khit ciangin zato ah i om thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: In a case like this, yes, but please keep your voices low.
records.zomi: Hih bang thu ah om thei hi, ahi zongin dai takin gen un.

records.english: Did you manage to say goodbye to your grandfather before he went into the care home?
records.zomi: Upate kemna inn ah a pai ma-in na pu kiangah goodbye na ci thei hiam?

records.english: I did, and the staff let me visit him on his first evening there as well.
records.zomi: Ka ci hi, nasemte in a tua-a a zan masa pen-in zong a veh dingin hong phal uh hi.

records.english: What would make saying goodbye easier for the children whose father works at sea?
records.zomi: A pa uh tuipi tung-a nasem naupangte adingin bang in goodbye cih a nuamsak zaw ding hiam?

records.english: A calendar where they cross off each day until his ship comes home.
records.zomi: A pa uh' tembaw inn a tun kik dong ni khat ciat a khaam theih uh kalenda khat.

records.english: How will we know that you've arrived safely?
records.zomi: Damtak na tung hi, cih bangci-in i thei ding hiam?

records.english: I'll send a message from the bus station the moment I get off.
records.zomi: Ka paikhiat ma-in bus dinna pan thu kong khak ding hi.

records.english: If you could go back, would you have left the village at all?
records.zomi: Na kik thei leh khua na nusia lo ding hiam?

records.english: Probably, but I would have said a proper goodbye to my grandparents first.
records.zomi: Ka nusia kha ding hi, ahi zongin a masa-in ka pu leh pite kiangah goodbye dik takin ka ci ding hi.

records.english: Would anyone be offended if I slipped away before the dancing starts?
records.zomi: Lam a kipat ma-in dai takin ka pai khiat leh kuamah in a lungkham ding uh hiam?

records.english: Not at all, and thank you for coming all this way.
records.zomi: Lungkham lo ing, hih bang tan-a sawt hong pai na hih manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: What did your uncle say when he left for the army?
records.zomi: Galkap ah a pai ciangin na pa neu in bang a ci hiam?

records.english: He said, "Look after your mother, and keep my bicycle clean until I'm back."
records.zomi: “Na nu kem inla, ka hong ciah kik dong ka siiksakol siang takin kem in,” a ci hi.

records.english: How did the village say goodbye to the old doctor?
records.zomi: Khua in siavuan upa kiangah bangci-in goodbye a ci uh hiam?

records.english: Everyone lined the road and threw flowers onto his car as it passed.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh lampi gei ah a ding uh a, a mawtaw a pai ciangin a tungah pak a lawn uh hi.

records.english: Could you help me find out more about my great-grandparents?
records.zomi: Ka pu leh pite' nu leh pate thu tam zaw theih nadingin hong huh thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Ask the pastor, because their names should be in the old church records.
records.zomi: Pastor dong in, a min uh pawlpi laibu lui sung ah a om ding ahih manin.

records.english: Did your parents make you share a room with your brother?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa in na sanggam pasal tawh khan khat na kihawmsak uh hiam?

records.english: Until I was fifteen, and we argued about the light every single night.
records.zomi: Kum sawm leh nga ka phak dong, zan simin meivak thu-ah i kinial hi.

records.english: What would your family do if someone broke the tradition of Sunday lunch?
records.zomi: Kuamah in Nipini sun an ngeina a siat leh na innkuan in bang a hih ding uh hiam?

records.english: My aunt would phone them every hour until they promised to come next week.
records.zomi: Kal zom ciangin hong ding a kiciam dong ka ni in nai khat ciat ah phone a sam ding hi.

records.english: How did your parents decide what to name you?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa in na min bangci-in a ngaihsut uh hiam?

records.english: I was given my grandmother's name, because I was born on her birthday.
records.zomi: Ka pi' pianni-in ka suak ahih manin ka pi' min hong phuak uh hi.

records.english: What does your family call the youngest child?
records.zomi: Na innkuan in naupang neu pen bang a ci uh hiam?

records.english: We call him "the little one," even though he's taller than all of us now.
records.zomi: Tu-in i khempeuh sangin a sang zaw napi “a neu” i ci hi.

records.english: Is your cousin the one who repaired the church roof?
records.zomi: Na sanggam pen pawlpi inn tung a bawl siang pa ahi hiam?

records.english: That's my second cousin, whose mother is my father's cousin.
records.zomi: Tua pen ka sanggam gamla ahi a, a nu pen ka pa' sanggam ahi hi.

records.english: Who taught you to fix bicycles?
records.zomi: Siiksakol bawl siam dan kua in hong hilh hiam?

records.english: My older brother, who used to make me hold the tools for hours.
records.zomi: Ka u pasal in, nai tampi sung nasepna vante hong len sak den hi.

records.english: Had your parents not moved to the city, would you have grown up on the farm?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa khuapi ah tuah lo hi leh lo ah na khang ding hiam?

records.english: Probably, and I'd be the one milking the cows at dawn instead of my cousins.
records.zomi: Khang kha ding hi, ka sanggamte sangin keimah in zingsang khuavak ma-in bawng nawi ka sik ding hi.

records.english: Do you get along with your brother-in-law?
records.zomi: Na sanggam nu' pasal tawh na kilem uh hiam?

records.english: Very well, now that we've stopped arguing about football.
records.zomi: Kilem mahmah hi, football thu-ah i kinial nawn loh ciangin.

records.english: Who looks after your grandparents now that they can't live alone?
records.zomi: Amau bek a om theih nawn loh ciangin tu-in na pu leh pite kua in a kem hiam?

records.english: My aunt does most of it, and we help on weekends.
records.zomi: Ka ni in a tamzaw a kem a, kal tawp ciangin ka huh uh hi.

records.english: Should I ask my uncle for advice before I accept the job?
records.zomi: Nasep ka sang ma-in ka pa neu thuhilhna ka ngen ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, because he'll be hurt if he hears about it from someone else.
records.zomi: Ngen in, mi dang pan a zak leh a lungkham ding ahih manin.

records.english: Why did your sister move back in with your parents?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na sanggam nu na nu leh na pa kiang ah a om kik hiam?

records.english: To look after our mother after her operation, though she says it's because she missed the cooking.
records.zomi: I nu' zatui khit ciangin kem dingin, ahi zongin anhuan a lungngaih manin a ci hi.

records.english: Are you and your sister ever mistaken for each other?
records.zomi: Nang leh na sanggam nu mite in a kikhial sak ngei uh hiam?

records.english: All the time, even by our own aunt.
records.zomi: Hun tawntungin, i ni mahmah in zong.

records.english: What happened to the family photos after the flood?
records.zomi: Tuiciim khit ciangin innkuan limte bang a suak hiam?

records.english: Most of them were ruined, but my aunt had copies of the important ones.
records.zomi: A tamzaw a sia hi, ahi zongin ka ni in a thupi te' copy a nei hi.

records.english: Who in your family can you always count on?
records.zomi: Na innkuan ah kua tung ah na ngak tawntung thei hiam?

records.english: My older sister, who has never once said no when I've asked for help.
records.zomi: Ka u nu in, huhna ka ngen ciangin khatvei zong “Hi lo” a ci ngei kei hi.

records.english: Should we tell Grandpa that his grandson failed the exam?
records.zomi: A tu in sitna a zo lo hi, ci-in na pu i hilh ding uh hiam?

records.english: He'll find out anyway, so it's better if the boy tells him himself.
records.zomi: Bangbang ahi zongin a thei ding ahih manin naupang pasal mah in a hilh leh a hoih zaw hi.

records.english: Who owns the family house now?
records.zomi: Tu-in innkuan inn kua in a nei hiam?

records.english: My mother and her two sisters, who share it.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh a sanggam nu nihte in, a kihawm uh hi.

records.english: Is your stepmother close to your real mother?
records.zomi: Na nukik na nu taktak tawh a kinai uh hiam?

records.english: They're friends now, and they plan our birthdays together.
records.zomi: Tu-in lawm a hi uh a, i pianni uh khawm-in a gel uh hi.

records.english: Gathered around the table at New Year, four generations of the family laughed at the same old stories.
records.zomi: Kum thak ciangin dawhkan kim-ah kikhawm-in innkuan khang li in tangthu lui kibang a nuih uh hi.

records.english: What should I call your mother when I meet her on Sunday?
records.zomi: Nipini-a na nu ka muh ciangin bang ka ci ding hiam?

records.english: Better to call her Auntie, because that's what she's used to from young people.
records.zomi: “Ni” ci leh a hoih zaw hi, khangnote pan a zak zia ahih manin.

records.english: Who will inherit your grandparents' rice fields?
records.zomi: Na pu leh pite' buh lo kua in a luah ding hiam?

records.english: They'll be shared among all the grandchildren, as my grandparents have already written down.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh pite in a gelh khin bangin tate' tate khempeuh in a kihawm ding uh hi.

records.english: What a family remembers together matters as much as the blood its members share.
records.zomi: Innkuan in khawm-a a phawk thu pen a sung-a mite' kihawm sisan bangin a thupi hi.

records.english: Can my cousin stay with us while she looks for work in town?
records.zomi: Khuapi ah nasep a zon laitakin ka sanggam i kiang ah a om thei ding hiam?

records.english: She can have the small room, as long as she helps with the cooking.
records.zomi: An huan a huh leh khan neu a zang thei hi.

records.english: Who's the oldest person in your family?
records.zomi: Na innkuan ah kua a upa pen hiam?

records.english: My great-aunt Niang, who still makes her own bread at ninety-four.
records.zomi: Ka pi neu Niang, kum sawmkua leh li hi napi amah mah in a moh a bawl lai hi.

records.english: Was your uncle really the first in the family to go to university?
records.zomi: Na pa neu pen innkuan sung-ah sangpi a kah masa pen ahi taktak hiam?

records.english: He was, and the whole village paid for his books.
records.zomi: Hi hi, a laibute khua bup in a lei sak uh hi.

records.english: How many brothers and sisters does your mother have?
records.zomi: Na nu in sanggam bangzah a nei hiam?

records.english: Five, and she's the youngest.
records.zomi: Nga, amah a neu pen ahi hi.

records.english: Are children allowed to sit at the adults' table at your family gatherings?
records.zomi: Na innkuan kikhopna ah naupangte upate' dawhkan ah a tu thei uh hiam?

records.english: Not until they're married, which my cousins think is very unfair.
records.zomi: A kiteen ma-un tu thei lo uh hi, tua pen ka sanggamte in a dik lo mahmah hi a ci uh hi.

records.english: How do you keep in touch with relatives who live abroad?
records.zomi: Gamdang ah a om na sanggamte tawh bangci-in na kizom uh hiam?

records.english: We send voice messages, because Grandma can't type.
records.zomi: Ka pi in lai a khen thei kei ahih manin aw thu i khak uh hi.

records.english: Do you look more like your mother's side of the family or your father's?
records.zomi: Na nu lam innkuan hiam na pa lam innkuan hiam koi na kibat zaw hiam?

records.english: Everyone says I have my mother's eyes and my father's stubbornness.
records.zomi: Ka nu' mit leh ka pa' lung khauhna ka nei hi, mi khempeuh in a ci uh hi.

records.english: Does your little brother still copy everything you do?
records.zomi: Na nau pasal in na hih khempeuh a zui lai hiam?

records.english: Yes, because he thinks I know everything, which I'm not going to tell him isn't true.
records.zomi: Zui lai hi, khempeuh ka thei in a ngaihsun ahih manin, a tak hi lo hi, ci-in ka hilh kei ding hi.

records.english: What did your grandfather say when you told him you were getting married?
records.zomi: Kiteen ding ka hi, ci-in na pu na hilh ciangin bang a ci hiam?

records.english: He said, "Finally — now I can stop praying about it!"
records.zomi: “A tawp-in — tu-in tua thu ka thungetsak nawn kei ding hi!” a ci hi.

records.english: Is it okay if our daughter spends the night at her friend's house?
records.zomi: I tanu in a lawm' inn ah zan khat a giak leh a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: Only if we've met the friend's parents first.
records.zomi: A lawm' nu leh pa i muh masak leh bek.

records.english: Should we punish our son for breaking the window, or is the shock enough?
records.zomi: Tukvuang a suksiat manin i tapa i gawt ding hiam, a lauhna in a kicing hiam?

records.english: Let him pay for part of the new glass from his pocket money.
records.zomi: A zat ding sum pan glass thak man a khen khat a piak ding uh.

records.english: When did you know you wanted to marry her?
records.zomi: Bang ciangin amah na kiteenpih nuam hi, cih na thei hiam?

records.english: When she laughed at my terrible cooking and asked for a second plate anyway.
records.zomi: Ka an huan hoih lo a nuih a, tua mah napi kuang nihna a ngen ciangin.

records.english: What's the secret of a long marriage?
records.zomi: Kiteenna sau ah thuguk bang ahi hiam?

records.english: Laughing at the same jokes for forty years, my grandfather says.
records.zomi: Kum sawmli sung nuihza kibangte nuih, ka pu in a ci hi.

records.english: What happened when the baby was born early?
records.zomi: Naungek a hun ma-in a suak ciangin bang a piang hiam?

records.english: She was taken straight to the hospital in the city, and we followed on the bus.
records.zomi: Khuapi-a zato ah a tang takin a paipih uh a, bus tawh i zui uh hi.

records.english: What made you decide to have your children baptized at the same church where you married?
records.zomi: Na kiteenna pawlpi mahmah ah na tate tuiphum na sak dingin bang in na ngaihsutsak hiam?

records.english: We wanted them to belong to the same community that welcomed us as a young couple.
records.zomi: Kiteen thak i hih laitakin hong muak pawl kibang mah ah a om nadingun i deih hi.

records.english: Have you told the children about the new baby yet?
records.zomi: Naungek thak thu naupangte na hilh khin uh hiam?

records.english: We told them last night, and our son asked whether it could sleep in the cupboard.
records.zomi: Zanni zanin i hilh uh a, i tapa in van bawm sung ah a ihmu thei ding hiam a dong hi.

records.english: What does your daughter call your husband's mother?
records.zomi: Na tanu in na pasal' nu bang a ci hiam?

records.english: Big Grandma, because she's taller than everyone else in the family.
records.zomi: “Pi Lian,” innkuan sung-a mi khempeuh sangin a sang zaw ahih manin.

records.english: How often do you and your husband go out without the children?
records.zomi: Nang leh na pasal naupangte tel lo-in bangzah vei na pai khia uh hiam?

records.english: Once a month, when my sister offers to babysit.
records.zomi: Kha khat ah khatvei, ka sanggam nu in naupang kem dingin a kiciam ciangin.

records.english: How do you stop your children from fighting over the computer?
records.zomi: Computer thu-ah na tate a kilaih lo nadingun bangci-in na kham hiam?

records.english: Each of them gets one hour a day, and the timer on the kitchen wall decides when it ends.
records.zomi: Ni khat ah nai khat ciat a ngah uh a, an huanna bang tung-a nai in a bei hun a khensat hi.

records.english: What did your mother tell you on your wedding day?
records.zomi: Na kiteen ni-in na nu in bang hong hilh hiam?

records.english: She said, "Never go to sleep angry, and always eat breakfast together."
records.zomi: “Heh-in ihmu ngei kei un, zingsang an khawm-in ne tawntung un,” a ci hi.

records.english: Why did you two decide to get married in the winter?
records.zomi: Bang hangin note nih khuavot lai-in kiteen dingin na khensat uh hiam?

records.english: Because that's when the harvest is finished and everyone in the village is free.
records.zomi: Tua hun pen buh lak a bei a, khua sung-a mi khempeuh a awng hun ahih manin.

records.english: So patient was my husband with our newborn twins that our neighbors asked him for advice.
records.zomi: Ka pasal in i naungek apengte tungah a thuakzawh lua ahih manin i inn vengte in thuhilhna a ngen uh hi.

records.english: Do you and your wife share a bank account?
records.zomi: Nang leh na zi bank account khat na kihawm uh hiam?

records.english: Yes, and we look at it together at the end of every month.
records.zomi: Kihawm hi, kha tawp simin khawm-in i en hi.

records.english: Would you ever let your son leave school to work on the farm?
records.zomi: Lo ah nasem dingin na tapa sang a nusiat na phal ngei ding hiam?

records.english: Never, because his grandfather made us promise he'd finish his studies.
records.zomi: Phal ngei lo ding hi, a pu in a laisinna a zawh ding hong kiciamsak ahih manin.

records.english: Raising children, my parents always said, is the only job you keep learning until the day you die.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in a ci tawntung bangin, ta khoina pen i sih ni dong i sin lai ding nasep khat bek ahi hi.

records.english: Who chooses your children's clothes in the morning?
records.zomi: Zingsangin na tate' puan kua in a teel hiam?

records.english: They do, unless they want to wear shorts in the snow.
records.zomi: Amau mah in a teel uh hi, vuk sung ah kekawi tom a silh nuam kei uh leh.

records.english: Where did you and your wife go for your honeymoon?
records.zomi: Nang leh na zi na kiteen khit ciangin koi ah na pai uh hiam?

records.english: To her uncle's farm in the hills, because we couldn't afford a hotel.
records.zomi: Mual tung-a a pa neu' lo ah, zinbuuk man i pia zo kei ahih manin.

records.english: What went wrong at your wedding?
records.zomi: Na kiteenna ah bang a kikhial hiam?

records.english: The power went out during the meal, so we danced by candlelight.
records.zomi: An nek laitakin meivak a mit ahih manin khawimeivaak tawh lam i hi uh.

records.english: If you could change one thing about how you raised your children, what would it be?
records.zomi: Na tate na khoih dan ah khat na laih thei leh bang ahi ding hiam?

records.english: I would have listened more and worried less.
records.zomi: Ngai zaw-in lungkham tawm zaw ding ka hi hi.

records.english: Why is the baby crying so much tonight?
records.zomi: Bang hangin tuni zanin naungek a kap mahmah hiam?

records.english: Her first tooth is coming through, the nurse thinks.
records.zomi: A ha masa pen a suak hi, nurse in a ngaihsun hi.

records.english: Why won't you let the children walk to school alone?
records.zomi: Bang hangin naupangte amau bek sang ah na paisak kei hiam?

records.english: Because the road by the market has no crossing yet.
records.zomi: Zuakna mun kiang-a lampi ah kantan mun a om nai loh manin.

records.english: How do you two share the night feeds?
records.zomi: Note nih zan-a nawi piakna bangci-in na kihawm uh hiam?

records.english: My husband does the first one, and I do the one before dawn.
records.zomi: Ka pasal in a masa pen a pia a, keimah in khuavak ma-a khat ka pia hi.

records.english: Do your children ever argue about bedtime?
records.zomi: Na tate in ihmut hun thu ah a kinial ngei uh hiam?

records.english: Every night, especially the older one, who reads with a flashlight until nine.
records.zomi: Zan simin, a upa zaw in nai kua dong flashlight tawh laibu a sim hi.

records.english: How did you get your son to stop biting his nails?
records.zomi: Na tapa in a khut tin a bawh nawn loh nadingin bangci-in na hih hiam?

records.english: We didn't — his teacher made him a deal, and he stopped within a week.
records.zomi: Hih lo hi — a saya in thukimna a bawlpih a, kal khat sungin a tawp hi.

records.english: Who taught you how to bathe a newborn baby?
records.zomi: Naungek suak thak kisilsak dan kua in hong hilh hiam?

records.english: A nurse at the clinic, and my mother-in-law checked I was doing it right for a month.
records.zomi: Siavuan inn-a nurse khat in, ka sungnu in kha khat sung ka hih dik hiam a en hi.

records.english: Can the kids watch television before they've done their homework?
records.zomi: Naupangte in inn-a sep ding a zawh ma-un TV a en thei uh hiam?

records.english: Not in our house — homework comes first, every single day.
records.zomi: I inn ah hi lo — inn-a sep ding a masa hi, ni khempeuh.

records.english: Do husbands in your village help with the cooking?
records.zomi: Na khua ah pasalte in an huan a huh uh hiam?

records.english: More than they used to, especially when their wives work at the market.
records.zomi: A ma-a sangin a tam zaw, a zite uh zuakna mun ah a nasep uh ciangin a thupi zaw hi.

records.english: Is it true that your parents met only twice before their wedding?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa a kiteen ma-un nihvei bek a kimu uh hi, cih a tak hiam?

records.english: It is, because the families arranged it, and yet they've been happy for fifty years.
records.zomi: A tak hi, innkuante in a gel uh ahih manin, ahi zongin kum sawmnga sung a lungdam uh hi.

records.english: Were you nervous when your daughter brought her fiancé home for the first time?
records.zomi: Na tanu in a kiteen ding pasal a vei masa pen-in inn ah a paipih ciangin na lungkham hiam?

records.english: Less nervous than he was — his hands were shaking as he poured the tea.
records.zomi: Amah sangin ka lungkham tawm zaw hi — tea a sun laitakin a khut a ling hi.

records.english: Are teenagers in your family allowed to go out after dark?
records.zomi: Na innkuan-a khangnote nitak mial ciangin a pai khia thei uh hiam?

records.english: Only with a cousin, and they have to be home by ten.
records.zomi: Sanggam khat tawh bek, nai sawm ma-in inn ah a tung ding uh hi.

records.english: My throat is so sore that I can hardly swallow.
records.zomi: Ka dangka a na lua ahih manin ka val zo dek kei hi.

records.english: Use the thermometer to check her temperature again tonight.
records.zomi: Tuni zanin a cisa a sang hiam thermometer tawh en kik in.

records.english: Does your son still get ear infections every winter?
records.zomi: Na tapa in khuavot simin a bilnatna a nei lai hiam?

records.english: Why does he get sick every time the weather changes?
records.zomi: Bang hangin huihkhua a kilaih simin a dam lo hiam?

records.english: I caught a cold from my sister, who caught it from her classmate.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu pan khuasik ka ngah a, amah in a kilasi lawm pan a ngah hi.

records.english: I've had a headache since I woke up.
records.zomi: Ka thoh pan ka lu a na hi.

records.english: Do your eyes itch every spring, when the trees are in flower?
records.zomi: Spring simin singte pak a vul ciangin na mit a lak hiam?

records.english: My wife got food poisoning on our trip, so we spent the last day in the hotel.
records.zomi: I khualzinna ah ka zi in an siat a nek manin a dam lo a, tua ahih manin ni nunung pen zinbuuk ah i om hi.

records.english: Wash your hands often, so that you don't pass the cold to the baby.
records.zomi: Naungek tungah khuasik na lut sak lo nadingin na khut tawntung sil in.

records.english: Using a damp cloth on her forehead, my mother kept me cool through the night.
records.zomi: Puan nawng tawh ka nu in ka talsuang a tuam a, zan bup hong vawtsak hi.

records.english: The doctor told my mother that my cough was caused by dust, not a cold.
records.zomi: Ka khuh pen khuasik hi lo-in leivui hang ahi hi, ci-in siavuan in ka nu a hilh hi.

records.english: Did the whole family catch it, or only the children?
records.zomi: Innkuan bup in a ngah uh hiam, naupangte bek ahi hiam?

records.english: The baby might be teething rather than sick, the nurse said.
records.zomi: Naungek pen a dam lo sangin a ha suak kha ding hi, nurse in a ci hi.

records.english: Why does everybody get a cold at the start of the school year?
records.zomi: Bang hangin sang kum kipat ciangin mi khempeuh khuasik a ngah uh hiam?

records.english: I really do hate being ill on a holiday.
records.zomi: Nopsakna ni-in dam lo pen ka huat mahmah hi.

records.english: Rather than going to work with a fever, I stayed home and slept for most of the day.
records.zomi: Cisa tawh nasepna ah pai sangin inn ah ka om a, ni bup dek ka ihmu hi.

records.english: My nose is blocked, and I can't taste my food.
records.zomi: Ka nak a kikhak a, ka an a tui ka thei kei hi.

records.english: How long does a cold usually last?
records.zomi: Khuasik pen a tamzaw-in bangzah sung a om hiam?

records.english: About a week for most people, though my cough always stays longer.
records.zomi: Mi tamzaw adingin kal khat bang hi, ahi zongin ka khuh a sau zaw tawntung hi.

records.english: Is it just a cold, or could it be the flu?
records.zomi: Khuasik bek ahi hiam, flu ahi kha ding hiam?

records.english: The doctor said it was only a bad cold and that I should rest for a few days.
records.zomi: Khuasik lian bek ahi a, ni tawmno sung ka tawldam ding hi, ci-in siavuan in a ci hi.

records.english: Please don't share your cup with me; I've got a sore throat.
records.zomi: Ka dangka a na ahih manin na haai kei tawh hong hawm kei in.

records.english: We think the chicken at the party gave everyone food poisoning.
records.zomi: Pawi-a akngeina in mi khempeuh a dam losak in i ngaihsun hi.

records.english: I think I'm getting a cold.
records.zomi: Khuasik ka ngah ding bang hi.

records.english: Is chickenpox dangerous for adults who never had it as children?
records.zomi: Naupan lai-a a ngah ngei lo upate adingin khuaphiat a lauhuai hiam?

records.english: The nurse told us it can be worse for adults, so they should see a doctor.
records.zomi: Upate adingin a hoih lo zaw thei ahih manin siavuan a muh ding uh hi, ci-in nurse in hong hilh hi.

records.english: The flu spread through the care home so quickly that visits were stopped for a week.
records.zomi: Upate kemna inn sung ah flu a zel lua ahih manin kal khat sung veh kikham hi.

records.english: Not until the fever finally broke did my parents get any sleep.
records.zomi: A cisa a kiam ciang bek ka nu leh ka pa a ihmu thei uh hi.

records.english: Can I come back to work tomorrow, or should I wait another day?
records.zomi: Zingciang nasepna ah ka kik thei ding hiam, ni khat behlap ka ngak ding hiam?

records.english: Feeling a little better today, Grandma asked for her usual cup of tea for the first time in a week.
records.zomi: Tuni-in tawmno a hoih zaw ahih manin kal khat sung ah a masa pen-in ka pi in a tea haai a ngen hi.

records.english: My aunt made soup for the whole family when we all had the flu.
records.zomi: I khempeuh flu i neih ciangin ka ni in innkuan bup adingin an tui a huan hi.

records.english: My uncle caught chickenpox at thirty and says it was the itchiest week of his life.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in kum sawmthum ah khuaphiat a ngah a, a nuntak sung-a a lak pen kal ahi hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Had I stayed at home when I first felt ill, I wouldn't have given the flu to my whole team.
records.zomi: Ka dam loh masak ciangin inn ah ka om leh ka pawl bup tungah flu ka lut sak kei ding hi.

records.english: Last winter the flu kept my father-in-law in bed for two weeks.
records.zomi: Kum nung khuavot in ka sungpa kal nih sung flu in lupna tungah a koih hi.

records.english: Everyone in our house had a stomach bug last week, one after another.
records.zomi: Kal nung in i inn-a mi khempeuh a khat khit khat-in gil na i nei hi.

records.english: When I had the flu, my roommate brought me hot tea and left it outside my door.
records.zomi: Flu ka neih ciangin ka khan kihawm lawm in tea lum hong tawi a, ka kongkhak pua ah a koih hi.

records.english: Students who have a fever should stay at home until they feel better.
records.zomi: Cisa a nei sangnaupangte a hoih zawk dong inn ah a om ding uh hi.

records.english: Do you feel hot, or is it just the weather?
records.zomi: Na kisa hiam, huihkhua bek ahi hiam?

records.english: Could you look after the children tomorrow, since I'm feeling too ill to get up?
records.zomi: Thou zo lo dingin ka dam kei ahih manin zingciang naupangte na kem thei ding hiam?

records.english: There might be a flu going around the office, because three people are off today.
records.zomi: Tuni-in mi thum a om kei uh ahih manin office ah flu a zel kha ding hi.

records.english: My grandfather's stomach bug lasted only a day, but it left him very weak.
records.zomi: Ka pu' gil na ni khat bek a om a, ahi zongin a hat lo mahmah sak hi.

records.english: Half of my class is off school with the flu this week.
records.zomi: Hih kal sungin ka kilasi a khen khat flu hangin sang a pai kei uh hi.

records.english: Kids, cover your mouths when you cough, please.
records.zomi: Naupangte, na khuh ciangun na kam uh khuh un.

records.english: My sister had her son's ears checked after he kept pulling at them.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu in a tapa in a bil a lawn den ahih manin a bil a etsak hi.

records.english: What worries parents most about common illnesses is how quickly a small child can become very weak.
records.zomi: Natna tavuante ah nu leh pate in a lungkhamhuai pen pen naupang neu khat a manlang taka hat lo thei hi, cih ahi hi.

records.english: My son coughed all night, so neither of us slept.
records.zomi: Ka tapa zan bup a khuh ahih manin ka nih un i ihmu kei hi.

records.english: The clinic was full of children with coughs and runny noses.
records.zomi: Siavuan inn khuh leh naktui luang naupangte tawh a dim hi.

records.english: The more I tried to ignore my cold, the worse it seemed to get.
records.zomi: Ka khuasik ka phawk loh tum semsem ciangin a hoih lo semsem bang hi.

records.english: If you start sneezing, stay away from Grandpa, because he catches everything.
records.zomi: Na het kipat leh na pu kiang ah pai kei in, amah in natna khempeuh a ngah ahih manin.

records.english: Although a cold is rarely serious, it can be hard on very old or very young people.
records.zomi: Khuasik pen a lauhuai tawm hangin upa mahmah leh naupang neu mahmah adingin a haksa thei hi.

records.english: I do want to go to the wedding, but I don't want everyone to catch my cough.
records.zomi: Mopawi ah pai ka deih mahmah hi, ahi zongin mi khempeuh in ka khuh a ngah ding uh ka deih kei hi.

records.english: My mother made me stay in bed until my fever was gone.
records.zomi: Ka cisa a bei dong ka nu in lupna tungah hong omsak hi.

records.english: Gargling with warm salt water was my grandmother's answer to every sore throat in the family.
records.zomi: Ka pi in innkuan sung-a dangka na khempeuh adingin tui lum cii tawh kam sil a zang hi.

records.english: My daughter's school sent a letter home because some children have head lice.
records.zomi: Naupang khenkhatte in lu-ah hik a nei uh ahih manin ka tanu' sang in inn ah lai a khak hi.

records.english: Is this rash something to worry about?
records.zomi: Hih vun san pen a lungkhamhuai ahi hiam?

records.english: It's probably nothing, but show it to the doctor if it spreads.
records.zomi: Bangmah hi lo kha ding hi, ahi zongin a zel leh siavuan etsak in.

records.english: Can you buy some tissues on your way home?
records.zomi: Inn na ciahna lampi ah tissue tawmno na lei thei ding hiam?

records.english: I don't feel like eating anything today.
records.zomi: Tuni-in bangmah ne ka nuam kei hi.

records.english: My little brother has chickenpox, so he can't go to school.
records.zomi: Ka nau pasal in khuaphiat a nei ahih manin sang a pai thei kei hi.

records.english: I felt sick all night after eating the shrimp.
records.zomi: Shrimp ka nek khit ciangin zan bup ka lua nuam hi.

records.english: Did the roof get fixed before the rain came?
records.zomi: Guah a zuk ma-in innkhum kibawl siang hiam?

records.english: Just in time — my uncle and the neighbors finished it the evening before the storm.
records.zomi: Hun mah-in — huihpi ma-a nitak lam ah ka pa neu leh inn vengte in a zo uh hi.

records.english: If you had more time, what part of the house would you finally sort out?
records.zomi: Hun tam zaw na neih leh inn ah koi mun na bawl siang ding hiam?

records.english: The attic, which hasn't been touched since we moved in twelve years ago.
records.zomi: Inn tung khan, kum sawm leh nih paisa-a i tuah pan kuamah in a khoih ngei loh.

records.english: How did the kitchen tap get broken?
records.zomi: An huanna tui khuk bangci-in a sia hiam?

records.english: Somebody turned it too hard, and nobody will admit who it was.
records.zomi: Kuamah in a hat lua-in a hei a, kua ahi hiam kuamah in a pang kei hi.

records.english: Why do you hang the washing inside today?
records.zomi: Bang hangin tuni-in puan sung lam ah na tan hiam?

records.english: The radio said it might rain this afternoon, and I don't want to bring it all in again.
records.zomi: Tuni nitak lam guah a zuk kha ding a ci-in radio in a gen a, khempeuh ka la lut kik nuam kei hi.

records.english: Who forgot to lock the back door last night?
records.zomi: Zanni zanin nung lam kongkhak khak kua in a mangngilh hiam?

records.english: That was me, sorry — I was carrying the rubbish out and forgot to come back.
records.zomi: Keimah ka hi, hong maisak in — nawi ka paai khia a, ka ciah kik ka mangngilh hi.

records.english: Why is the fridge always empty on Fridays?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Laithai ni simin khal bawm a awng tawntung hiam?

records.english: Because nobody remembers that shopping day is Saturday.
records.zomi: Van lei ni pen Kiginni ahi hi, cih kuamah in a phawk kei manin.

records.english: How long does it take to clean the whole house?
records.zomi: Inn bup siangsak dingin bangzah sawt hiam?

records.english: About three hours, if the children help and don't stop to play.
records.zomi: Nai thum bang, naupangte in a huh uh a, a kimawl dingin a tawl kei uh leh.

records.english: Should the older children be paid for chores that the younger ones do for free?
records.zomi: Naupang neute in a man om lo-a a sep inn nasep adingin a upa zawte i piak ding uh hiam?

records.english: We pay them all the same small amount, so that nobody can complain.
records.zomi: Kuamah in a phun theih lo nadingin a vekpi un sum tawmno kibang i pia hi.

records.english: Should I separate the white clothes from the colored ones?
records.zomi: Puan kangte leh a dang a rong te ka khen ding hiam?

records.english: Always, unless you want pink shirts like your father had last year.
records.zomi: Tawntungin, kum nung in na pa' neih bang angki sandup na deih kei leh.

records.english: Is there anything I can do to help before the guests arrive?
records.zomi: Khualte a hong tun ma-un ka huh theih ding bangmah a om hiam?

records.english: You could sweep the porch and put the extra chairs outside.
records.zomi: Kongmai na phiat inla, tutna behlapte pua ah na koih thei hi.

records.english: Why does your daughter do the laundry for the whole family?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na tanu in innkuan bup' puan a sil hiam?

records.english: She asked to, because she's saving the pocket money we give her for it.
records.zomi: Amah in a ngen hi, tua adingin i piak sum a khol ahih manin.

records.english: Who has been watering the neighbors' tomatoes while they're on holiday?
records.zomi: Inn vengte nopsakna ah a pai laitakun a tomato kua in tui a lei hiam?

records.english: My little brother, who's been so careful that he even talks to the plants.
records.zomi: Ka nau pasal in, a pilvang lua ahih manin singkungte tawh zong a kiho hi.

records.english: Why do the boys never have to help with the cooking?
records.zomi: Bang hangin naupang pasalte in an huan a huh ngei kei uh hiam?

records.english: That's changing — from now on, everyone in this house cooks one evening a week.
records.zomi: Tua a kilaih ding hi — tu pan kipan, hih inn sung-a mi khempeuh in kal khat ah nitak khat an a huan ding hi.

records.english: How do you get your teenagers to make their beds?
records.zomi: Na khangno tate na lupna uh a bawl nadingun bangci-in na hih hiam?

records.english: I don't anymore — I just close their doors so that I can't see the mess.
records.zomi: Ka hih nawn kei hi — a buaina ka muh loh nadingin a kongkhak uh ka khak bek hi.

records.english: Can I do my chores in the morning instead of tonight?
records.zomi: Ka inn nasep tuni zan sangin zingsang ah ka sem thei ding hiam?

records.english: Only if they're finished before you leave for school.
records.zomi: Sang na pai ma-in na zawh leh bek.

records.english: Do you mind if I use your vacuum cleaner while mine is being repaired?
records.zomi: Keima' bawlsiang laitakin na vacuum cleaner ka zat leh na lungkham ding hiam?

records.english: Take it, but be careful, because the cord is a little loose.
records.zomi: La in, ahi zongin a khau tawmno a kiloh ahih manin pilvang in.

records.english: What job does your grandfather still refuse to hand over?
records.zomi: Na pu in bang nasep a piak nuam lo lai hiam?

records.english: Looking after the bees, which he's done since he was a boy.
records.zomi: Khuaite kemna, naupang a hih lai-a kipan a sep.

records.english: Can someone help me move the fridge so that I can clean behind it?
records.zomi: Khal bawm nung ka siangsak theih nadingin kuamah in hong huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Wait for your brother, because it's too heavy for the two of us.
records.zomi: Na sanggam pasal ngak in, i nih adingin a gik lua ahih manin.

records.english: Who pays the electricity bill in your shared flat?
records.zomi: Na kihawm inn ah meivak man kua in a pia hiam?

records.english: We split it four ways, and whoever pays writes it on the board in the kitchen.
records.zomi: Mi li in i khen a, a pia peuhpeuh in an huanna bang tungah a gelh hi.

records.english: However tired we are, our house rule is that nobody goes to bed while there are dishes in the sink.
records.zomi: Bangzah ta in i tawl zongin, kuang silna ah kuang a om lai sungin kuamah in a lum lo ding hi, cih i inn thupiak ahi hi.

records.english: Sharing the housework fairly took our family years to learn, and we're still arguing about the details.
records.zomi: Inn nasep dik takin kihawm pen i innkuan in kum tampi sung a sin a, tu dong a neu tetete ah i kinial lai hi.

records.english: What did your mother say when she saw the kitchen after the party?
records.zomi: Pawi khit ciangin an huanna a muh ciangin na nu in bang a ci hiam?

records.english: She said, "I'll be back in an hour, and I expect to see my floor again."
records.zomi: “Nai khat sungin ka hong kik ding a, ka tual ka mu kik ding hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: Who taught you to iron a shirt so neatly?
records.zomi: Angki hoih taka phawk dan kua in hong hilh hiam?

records.english: My older brother, who used to pay me to iron his school shirts.
records.zomi: Ka u pasal in, a sang angkite phawk dingin sum hong pia den hi.

records.english: Do you get paid for your chores?
records.zomi: Na inn nasep adingin sum na ngah hiam?

records.english: Only for the big ones, like washing the car or clearing the garden.
records.zomi: A lian te adingin bek, mawtaw sil hiam huan siangsak hiam bang.

records.english: What happened to the washing machine?
records.zomi: Puan silna set bang a piang hiam?

records.english: It flooded the kitchen floor last night, so we're washing clothes by hand until the repairman comes.
records.zomi: Zanni zanin an huanna tual tui in a liam sak ahih manin a bawlsiang pa a hong dong khut tawh puan i sil hi.

records.english: What would happen if nobody in this family did any housework for a week?
records.zomi: Hih innkuan sung-a kuamah in kal khat sung inn nasep a sep kei leh bang a piang ding hiam?

records.english: We'd have no clean plates by Tuesday and no clean socks by Thursday.
records.zomi: Pithai ni ciangin kuang siang om lo ding a, Laizing ni ciangin khedap-ip siang om lo ding hi.

records.english: Are you allowed to use the lawnmower by yourself yet?
records.zomi: Na kim ah lopa satna set nangma bek in na zang thei khin hiam?

records.english: Not yet; Dad says I have to watch him do it a few more times first.
records.zomi: Thei nai lo ing; a masa-in a sep vei tawmno ka en lai ding hi, ci-in Pa in a ci hi.

records.english: Why won't you let me use the stove?
records.zomi: Bang hangin meikhuk hong zangsak kei hiam?

records.english: You can use it when you're ten, and only when an adult is in the kitchen.
records.zomi: Kum sawm na phak ciangin, upa khat an huanna ah a om ciang bek na zang thei ding hi.

records.english: Is it true that you did all the housework while your wife was in hospital?
records.zomi: Na zi zato ah a om laitakin inn nasep khempeuh na sem hi, cih a tak hiam?

records.english: It is, and I've never appreciated her more than I did that month.
records.zomi: A tak hi, tua kha sung bangin a tung ah ka lungdam ngei kei hi.

records.english: Who looks after the house when you're working abroad?
records.zomi: Gamdang ah na nasep laitakin na inn kua in a kem hiam?

records.english: My cousin lives there, and in return she pays no rent.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam a om a, a thuk dingin inn man a pia kei hi.

records.english: When did the gutters last get cleaned?
records.zomi: Innkhum tui luanna bang ciangin a kisiangsak nunung hiam?

records.english: Not since last autumn, which is why the water overflowed during the storm.
records.zomi: Kum nung kumtawp pan siangsak nawn lo ahih manin huihpi laitakin tui a liam hi.

records.english: So carefully did my parents explain the divorce that none of us children felt it was our fault.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in a kikhen thu pilvang lua takin a gen siang uh ahih manin tate khat zong in eima' khialhna hi, ci-in i kisa kei hi.

records.english: Can we vote on where to spend the holidays this year?
records.zomi: Tu kum nopsakna ni-in koi ah i zat ding vote tawh i teel thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: We can, but the grandparents' votes count twice.
records.zomi: Teel thei hi, ahi zongin pu leh pite' vote nihvei kisim hi.

records.english: How do your parents make big decisions?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa in thu lian bangci-in a khensat uh hiam?

records.english: They go for a long walk and come back with an answer.
records.zomi: Sau taka a vak uh a, dawnna tawh a hong kik uh hi.

records.english: Why are you whispering in the kitchen?
records.zomi: Bang hangin an huanna ah na kihol hiam?

records.english: We're planning Mom's surprise party, so please don't come in.
records.zomi: Nu' adingin a theih loh pawi i gel uh ahih manin hong lut kei in.

records.english: Is it all right if I bring my boyfriend into the discussion about the wedding?
records.zomi: Mopawi thu i kihona ah ka lawm pasal ka paipih leh a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: Please do, since it's his wedding too.
records.zomi: Paipih in, amah' mopawi zong ahi ahih manin.

records.english: Do you think we're making the right choice about Grandma's house?
records.zomi: Ka pi' inn thu-ah teelna dik i bawl in na ngaihsun hiam?

records.english: I do think so, but let's ask her once more before we sign anything.
records.zomi: Tua bangin ka ngaihsun hi, ahi zongin bangmah i suaksak ma-in khatvei amah dong kik ni.

records.english: What's the one rule everyone in your family follows during discussions?
records.zomi: Kihona sungin na innkuan-a mi khempeuh in a zuih thupiak khat bang ahi hiam?

records.english: We pass a wooden spoon around, and only the person holding it may speak.
records.zomi: Sing kheng khat i kipia kawikawi a, a len pa bek in a gen thei hi.

records.english: Are the children allowed to join the family meeting?
records.zomi: Innkuan kikhopna ah naupangte a kihel thei uh hiam?

records.english: Only the ones over twelve, and they have to listen before they speak.
records.zomi: Kum sawm leh nih tung bek, a gen ma-un a ngai masa ding uh hi.

records.english: What happens when your brothers can't agree?
records.zomi: Na sanggam pasalte a kithukim zo kei ciangun bang a piang hiam?

records.english: Our mother sends them both outside until they've calmed down.
records.zomi: A lung uh a nem dong i nu in a nih un pua ah a paisak hi.

records.english: What did your parents say when you told them you wanted to be a musician?
records.zomi: La sak siam ka suak nuam hi, ci-in na nu leh na pa na hilh ciangin bang a ci uh hiam?

records.english: My father said, "Learn a trade as well, and then play as much as you like."
records.zomi: Ka pa in, “Khutsiamna zong sin inla, tua ciangin na deih tan sak in,” a ci hi.

records.english: Who goes to the council meetings for your family?
records.zomi: Na innkuan adingin khua upa kikhopna ah kua in a pai hiam?

records.english: Your grandfather, as always, unless he asks one of us to.
records.zomi: Na pu, tawntung bangin, ei lak-a khat a sawl kei leh.

records.english: Why does your family always argue at weddings?
records.zomi: Bang hangin mopawi ah na innkuan in a kinial tawntung uh hiam?

records.english: Because it's the only time all forty of us are in the same room.
records.zomi: I mi sawmli khempeuh khan khat sung a om khawm hun khat bek ahih manin.

records.english: Can I finish what I was saying before you answer?
records.zomi: Na dawng ma-in ka gen laitak ka zo thei ding hiam?

records.english: Sorry, go on — I'm listening.
records.zomi: Hong maisak in, gen in — ka ngai hi.

records.english: Had your parents asked your opinion, would you have agreed to the move?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa in na ngaihsutna hong dong le uh, tuah dingin na lungkim ding hiam?

records.english: Probably not, but I'd have felt less angry about it.
records.zomi: Lungkim lo kha ding ing, ahi zongin ka heh tawm zaw ding hi.

records.english: Why didn't anyone tell me that Grandma had been ill?
records.zomi: Bang hangin ka pi a dam lo hi, ci-in kuamah in hong hilh kei uh hiam?

records.english: She made us promise not to, because you had exams that week.
records.zomi: Tua kal sungin sitna na nei ahih manin gen lo dingin hong kiciamsak hi.

records.english: How did you tell your parents about the accident?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa kiangah accident thu bangci-in na gen hiam?

records.english: Having waited until they were both sitting down, I began by telling them I was unhurt.
records.zomi: A nih un a tut dong ka ngak a, ka liam kei hi, cih ka gen masa hi.

records.english: Why is everyone so quiet tonight?
records.zomi: Bang hangin tuni zanin mi khempeuh a dai mahmah uh hiam?

records.english: Dad told us at dinner that he might lose his job.
records.zomi: Nitak an nek laitakin a nasep a mansuah kha ding hi, ci-in Pa in hong hilh hi.

records.english: What was decided about Grandpa's birthday?
records.zomi: Ka pu' pianni thu bang kikhensat hiam?

records.english: It was decided that we'd all cook one dish and eat at the old house.
records.zomi: I khempeuh in an khat ciat i huan ding a, inn lui ah i ne khawm ding hi, ci-in kikhensat hi.

records.english: Should we tell the children that we might move to the city?
records.zomi: Khuapi ah i tuah kha ding hi, ci-in naupangte i hilh ding uh hiam?

records.english: Not until we're sure, or they'll worry for nothing.
records.zomi: I kician dong hilh lo ni, a hi kei leh a mawk lungkham ding uh hi.

records.english: How long did the argument about the inheritance go on?
records.zomi: Gamluah thu-ah kinialna bangzah sung a om hiam?

records.english: Almost a year, and without the pastor's help it might still be going on.
records.zomi: Kum khat dek, pastor' huhna om lo hi leh tu dong a om lai kha ding hi.

records.english: Do you discuss money in front of your children?
records.zomi: Na tate mai ah sum thu na kiho uh hiam?

records.english: Sometimes, because we'd rather they understood why money is tight than imagined something worse.
records.zomi: Khatveivei, a hoih lo zaw a ngaihsut sangin sum bang hangin a haksa hiam a theih uh i deih zaw ahih manin.

records.english: What did the family finally agree about the old car?
records.zomi: Mawtaw lui thu-ah a tawp-in innkuan in bang a kithukim uh hiam?

records.english: To keep it for Grandpa's trips to the clinic and to sell it after that.
records.zomi: Ka pu siavuan inn a pai nadingin kem dingin, tua khit ciangin zuak dingin.

records.english: What made your sister change her mind about the move?
records.zomi: Tuah thu-ah na sanggam nu' ngaihsutna bang in a laihsak hiam?

records.english: Her daughter cried all evening.
records.zomi: A tanu nitak bup a kap hi.

records.english: When is the best time to tell the family about the new job?
records.zomi: Nasep thak thu innkuan hilh dingin hun hoih pen bang ciang ahi hiam?

records.english: At Sunday lunch, when everyone is relaxed and full.
records.zomi: Nipini sun an ciangin, mi khempeuh a nuam uh a, a vah uh ciangin.

records.english: Would you be upset if I moved out after university?
records.zomi: Sangpi ka zawh khit ciangin ka paikhiat leh na lungkham ding hiam?

records.english: A little, but we'd be proud of you too.
records.zomi: Tawmno, ahi zongin na tung ah i kisaktheih ding uh hi.

records.english: If you could change one thing about how your family talks, what would it be?
records.zomi: Na innkuan' kihona dan ah khat na laih thei leh bang ahi ding hiam?

records.english: I'd make sure the youngest ones get heard as much as the loudest ones.
records.zomi: Ging sang pente bangin a neu pente zong kingai dingin ka bawl ding hi.

records.english: How did the family decide who would look after the farm?
records.zomi: Lo kua in a kem ding hiam innkuan in bangci-in a khensat uh hiam?

records.english: The youngest of my uncles offered, because he was the only one who still lived nearby.
records.zomi: Ka pa neute lak-a a neu pen in a kipia hi, a kiang ah a om lai pa khat bek ahih manin.

records.english: Is it true that your family meets every New Year to plan the year ahead?
records.zomi: Kum thak simin kum thak gel dingin na innkuan a kikhawm uh hi, cih a tak hiam?

records.english: It is, and the children write their wishes on paper and put them in a jar.
records.zomi: A tak hi, naupangte in a deihnate uh lai tungah a gelh uh a, bel sung ah a koih uh hi.

records.english: Why did Grandpa leave the table so suddenly?
records.zomi: Bang hangin ka pu dawhkan a manlang takin a nusia hiam?

records.english: Ever since someone suggested selling the old orchard, he has refused to discuss it.
records.zomi: Kuamah in singgah huan lui zuak ding a gen pan kipan, tua thu a kiho nuam nawn kei hi.

records.english: Who usually starts the difficult conversations in your family?
records.zomi: Na innkuan ah kihona haksate a tamzaw-in kua in a kipatsak hiam?

records.english: Usually my aunt, because she says silence only makes problems grow.
records.zomi: A tamzaw-in ka ni, dai pen in buaina a khangsak bek hi, a ci ahih manin.

records.english: What matters most in a family discussion is not who wins but whether everyone still feels part of the family afterward.
records.zomi: Innkuan kihona ah a thupi pen pen kua in a zo hiam cih hi lo-in, a khit ciangin mi khempeuh innkuan-a om in a kisa lai hiam cih ahi hi.

records.english: Do the grandparents mind looking after the baby every Friday?
records.zomi: Laithai ni simin naungek kem dingin pu leh pite a lungkham uh hiam?

records.english: They say Friday is the best day of their week.
records.zomi: Laithai ni pen a kal sung-a ni hoih pen ahi hi, a ci uh hi.

records.english: Why does Grandpa keep asking the same question?
records.zomi: Bang hangin ka pu in dotna kibang a dong den hiam?

records.english: His memory isn't what it was, so just answer him kindly each time.
records.zomi: A phawkna a ma-a bangin a om nawn kei ahih manin hun khempeuh ah nuam takin dawng in.

records.english: Who taught you to be so patient with old people?
records.zomi: Upate tungah thuakzawh dan kua in hong hilh hiam?

records.english: Growing up with my grandmother, who lived with us until she was ninety-six.
records.zomi: Kum sawmkua leh guk a phak dong i kiang ah a om ka pi tawh ka khang ahih manin.

records.english: Is it hard to care for a parent who doesn't recognize you anymore?
records.zomi: Hong thei nawn lo nu hiam pa hiam kem pen a haksa hiam?

records.english: It is, but she still smiles when I sing her favorite hymn, and that keeps me going.
records.zomi: Haksa hi, ahi zongin a la deih pen ka sak ciangin a nuih lai a, tua in hong hanthawn hi.

records.english: Was the medicine delivered to Grandma's house this morning?
records.zomi: Tuni zingsangin ka pi' inn ah zatui kipuak hiam?

records.english: It was left with the neighbor, because nobody answered the door.
records.zomi: Kuamah in kongkhak a dawng kei ahih manin inn veng kiang ah kinusia hi.

records.english: What time should the children be in bed while you're out?
records.zomi: Na pai laitakin naupangte nai bangzah ciangin lupna ah a om ding uh hiam?

records.english: By eight, after a story and a glass of milk.
records.zomi: Nai giat ma-in, tangthu khat leh nawi haai khat khit ciangin.

records.english: Will you read to Grandpa this evening, since his eyes are tired?
records.zomi: Ka pu' mit a tawl ahih manin tuni nitak in na simsak ding hiam?

records.english: I do want to, but I have to finish my homework first.
records.zomi: Simsak ka deih mahmah hi, ahi zongin ka inn-a sep ding ka zo masa ding hi.

records.english: What's the hardest part of looking after your mother-in-law?
records.zomi: Na sungnu kemna ah a haksa pen bang ahi hiam?

records.english: Watching someone so strong become so frail, and pretending I'm not sad about it.
records.zomi: A hat mahmah mi khat a hat lo mahmah a suak en leh lungkham lo bang-a kibawl.

records.english: Who will collect the children from school if I'm stuck at the hospital?
records.zomi: Zato ah ka kikhak kha leh sang pan naupangte kua in a la ding hiam?

records.english: I will, so don't worry about them at all.
records.zomi: Keimah in, tua ahih manin amaute adingin lungkham kei in.

records.english: How do you keep your grandfather from getting lonely?
records.zomi: Na pu a lungngaih lo nadingin bangci-in na hih uh hiam?

records.english: Someone visits him every day, and on Sundays the whole family eats at his house.
records.zomi: Ni simin kuamah in a veh a, Nipini simin innkuan bup in a inn ah an a ne uh hi.

records.english: How is your father managing since his fall?
records.zomi: A kiat khit pan na pa bangci-in a om hiam?

records.english: Better, now that we've put a rail beside his bed and moved the rugs.
records.zomi: A hoih zaw hi, a lupna kiang ah khut lenna i koih a, tuutphahte i suan khit ciangin.

records.english: What did the nurse say about your grandmother's leg?
records.zomi: Na pi' khe thu-ah nurse in bang a ci hiam?

records.english: She said, "Keep it raised in the evenings, and call me if the swelling gets worse."
records.zomi: “Nitak lam simin a sang-in koih inla, a vung a hoih lo semsem leh hong sam in,” a ci hi.

records.english: Why are the children so quiet this morning?
records.zomi: Bang hangin tuni zingsangin naupangte a dai mahmah uh hiam?

records.english: They were told last night that Grandpa is going into hospital.
records.zomi: Ka pu zato ah a lut ding hi, ci-in zanni zanin kihilh uh hi.

records.english: Does your son need help getting dressed in the morning?
records.zomi: Na tapa in zingsangin puan silh dingin huhna a kisap hiam?

records.english: Only with his shoelaces, which he's still learning to tie.
records.zomi: A khedap khau bek, a khih dan a sin lai ahih manin.

records.english: How old were you when you first looked after your little brother alone?
records.zomi: Na nau pasal na kem masak pen ciangin kum bangzah na hi hiam?

records.english: Nine, and I was so nervous that I checked on him every five minutes.
records.zomi: Kum kua, ka lau lua ahih manin minit nga simin ka en hi.

records.english: Kids, can you play quietly while Grandma has her afternoon rest?
records.zomi: Naupangte, nitak lam ka pi a tawldam laitakin dai takin na kimawl thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: Can we play in the garden instead, so that we can be loud?
records.zomi: Ging sang taka i kimawl theih nadingin huan sung ah i kimawl thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: What happened when the baby swallowed the button?
records.zomi: Naungek in button a val ciangin bang a piang hiam?

records.english: We rushed him to the clinic, and luckily the doctor said it would pass on its own.
records.zomi: Siavuan inn ah manlang takin i paipih a, siavuan in amah mah in a pai khia ding hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Everyone, could you please take your shoes off before you go into the baby's room?
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, naungek' khan na lut ma-un na khedap uh na sut thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: Gladly, and we've all washed our hands as well.
records.zomi: Lungdam takin, i khempeuh in i khut zong i sil khin uh hi.

records.english: How did your family decide who would care for your grandfather?
records.zomi: Na pu kua in a kem ding hiam na innkuan in bangci-in a khensat uh hiam?

records.english: Each of us has one week a month, and my cousin, who's a nurse, organizes the calendar.
records.zomi: I khat ciat in kha khat ah kal khat ciat i nei a, nurse ahi ka sanggam in kalenda a bawl hi.

records.english: What do you do when your son has a nightmare?
records.zomi: Na tapa in mang hoih lo a mang ciangin bang na hih hiam?

records.english: I sit with him and tell him a funny story until he falls asleep again.
records.zomi: A kiang ah ka tu a, a ihmut kik dong tangthu nuihzat huai khat ka gen hi.

records.english: Should we let our daughter walk home from school alone now that she's eleven?
records.zomi: Kum sawm leh khat a phak khit ciangin i tanu sang pan inn ah amah bek a ciahsak ding uh hiam?

records.english: Let her try with a friend first, and see how it goes.
records.zomi: A masa-in lawm khat tawh sin sak inla, bangci a om hiam en in.

records.english: Is the baby old enough to try soft rice?
records.zomi: Naungek in an nem a sin thei ding tan a phak khin hiam?

records.english: The health visitor said we can start in a few weeks.
records.zomi: Cidamna nasempa in kal tawmno ciangin i kipan thei ding hi, a ci hi.

records.english: So tenderly did the boy feed his grandfather that the nurses stopped to watch.
records.zomi: Naupang pasal in a pu nem lua takin an a vaksak ahih manin nursete a tawl-in a en uh hi.

records.english: How do you get the twins to sleep at the same time?
records.zomi: Apengte hun kibang-in bangci-in na ihmusak uh hiam?

records.english: We don't — one always wakes the other, and then nobody sleeps.
records.zomi: Ihmusak thei lo hi — khat in a dang a phawngsak tawntung a, kuamah ihmu lo hi.

records.english: Why did the doctor ask you to keep a diary of Grandpa's sleep?
records.zomi: Bang hangin ka pu' ihmutna diary kem dingin siavuan in hong ngen hiam?

records.english: So that she could see whether the new medicine was helping him at night.
records.zomi: Zatui thak in zan ah a huh hiam a muh theih nadingin.

records.english: Can the baby sleep in our room until she's a little older?
records.zomi: Naungek a upa zaw tawmno dong i khan sung ah a ihmu thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, and then we'll move her cot into the room next door.
records.zomi: Thei hi, tua ciangin a lupna a kiang khan ah i suan ding hi.

records.english: Is it safe to leave Grandma alone for an afternoon?
records.zomi: Ka pi nitak lam khat amah bek nusia pen a bit ding hiam?

records.english: Only if the neighbor can look in on her at lunchtime.
records.zomi: Sun an hun ciangin inn veng in a en thei leh bek.

records.english: If you had to do it again, would you have cared for your father at home?
records.zomi: Kik-in na hih kik ding hi leh na pa inn ah na kem ding hiam?

records.english: Without a doubt, even though there were nights I thought I couldn't go on.
records.zomi: Lungmanglah om lo-in, ka zo nawn lo ding in ka ngaihsut zan tampi om hangin.

records.english: Who looks after your children during the school holidays?
records.zomi: Sang tawlngak hun sungin na tate kua in a kem hiam?

records.english: They spend half the time with their grandparents and half at the holiday club.
records.zomi: A hun khen khat a pu leh pite kiang ah a om uh a, a khen khat naupang kimawlna pawl ah a om uh hi.

records.english: Caring for both a newborn and an elderly parent taught us to accept help from anyone who offered it.
records.zomi: Naungek suak thak leh nu hiam pa upa a kem khawm in, hong huh dingin a kipia kua peuhpeuh' huhna sang dingin hong hilh hi.

records.english: Why did your sister give up her job last year?
records.zomi: Bang hangin kum nung in na sanggam nu in a nasep a nusia hiam?

records.english: To take care of our father after his stroke, though she says she'll go back one day.
records.zomi: Lu sung natna a neih khit ciangin i pa kem dingin, ahi zongin ni khat ni ciangin a kik ding hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Watching the sun rise over the hills from the kitchen window, my grandfather drinks his first cup of tea in silence.
records.zomi: An huanna tukvuang pan mual tung ah ni a suak a en-in, ka pu in a tea masa pen dai takin a dawn hi.
