records.english: Why are you up so early on a Saturday?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Kiginni-in zingsang mahmah na thou hiam?

records.english: The market opens at six, and I want the best tomatoes before they're gone.
records.zomi: Zuakna mun nai guk ciangin a kihong a, a bei ma-un tomato hoih pen ka deih hi.

records.english: What does your grandfather do as soon as he wakes up?
records.zomi: Na pu in a thoh ciangin bang a hih masa hiam?

records.english: He opens the window, listens to the birds, and then reads one chapter of the Bible.
records.zomi: Tukvuang a hong a, vasa ging a ngai a, tua ciangin Lai Siangtho khen khat a sim hi.

records.english: What woke you up so early?
records.zomi: Bang in zingsang mahmah hong phawngsak hiam?

records.english: The dogs started barking at the rubbish truck, and after that I couldn't get back to sleep.
records.zomi: Uite in nawi mawtaw a hop uh a, tua khit ciangin ka ihmu kik zo kei hi.

records.english: However carefully we plan the night before, something always goes missing in the morning rush.
records.zomi: Zan ma-in bangzah ta in pilvang takin i gel zongin zingsang buaina ah bangmah khat a mang tawntung hi.

records.english: How do you stay so cheerful at six in the morning?
records.zomi: Zingsang nai guk ciangin bangci-in na nuam lai thei hiam?

records.english: I do want to be grumpy sometimes, but a cup of strong tea always wins.
records.zomi: Khatveivei lungkia ka deih mahmah hi, ahi zongin tea hat khat in a zo tawntung hi.

records.english: Would you mind braiding my hair before you leave for work?
records.zomi: Nasepna na pai ma-in ka sam na khih sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Sit down quickly, then, because I've only got five minutes.
records.zomi: Manlang takin tu in, minit nga bek ka nei ahih manin.

records.english: Why is the bathroom floor soaking wet?
records.zomi: Bang hangin kisilna inn tual a dikdek hiam?

records.english: Your brother forgot to close the shower curtain again.
records.zomi: Na sanggam pasal in kisilna puan khak a mangngilh kik hi.

records.english: Did you hear the alarm this morning?
records.zomi: Tuni zingsang alarm na za hiam?

records.english: No, my phone ran out of battery during the night.
records.zomi: Za lo ing, zan sungin ka phone battery a bei hi.

records.english: Why is the bathroom door locked?
records.zomi: Bang hangin kisilna inn kongkhak kikhak hiam?

records.english: Your sister has been doing her hair in there for half an hour.
records.zomi: Na sanggam nu nai khen khat sung tua sung ah a sam a bawl hi.

records.english: Had the bus been on time, would you have made it to the exam?
records.zomi: Bus hun takin hong tung le, sitna ah na tung in ding hiam?

records.english: Easily, but I'd still have forgotten my calculator in the rush.
records.zomi: Baihlam takin, ahi zongin buaina sungah ka calculator ka mangngilh lai ding hi.

records.english: Is it true that you once went to school in your slippers?
records.zomi: Khatvei khedap neu tawh sang na pai hi, cih a tak hiam?

records.english: It is, and I didn't notice until the teacher pointed at my feet.
records.zomi: A tak hi, saya in ka khe a lak dong ka thei kei hi.

records.english: Why didn't you wake me when you got up?
records.zomi: Na thoh ciangin bang hangin hong phawngsak kei hiam?

records.english: You looked so peaceful that I let you sleep.
records.zomi: Na nuam lua bangin na om ahih manin kong ihmusak hi.

records.english: Should I wear my school uniform or my own clothes for the trip?
records.zomi: Khualzinna adingin ka sang puan ka silh ding hiam, keima' puan ka silh ding hiam?

records.english: Your uniform, because the teacher wants to spot everyone easily in the crowd.
records.zomi: Na sang puan, mipi lak ah saya in mi khempeuh baihlam takin a muh theih nadingin.

records.english: Why are you wearing two different socks?
records.zomi: Bang hangin khedap-ip kibang lo nih na bulh hiam?

records.english: I got dressed in the dark so that I wouldn't wake my brother.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal ka phawngsak lo nadingin mial sung ah puan ka silh hi.

records.english: Is there time for breakfast, or should we eat on the bus?
records.zomi: Zingsang an nek hun a om hiam, bus tung ah i ne ding uh hiam?

records.english: Take some bread with you, because the bus leaves in ten minutes.
records.zomi: Bus minit sawm ciangin a pai ding ahih manin moh tawmno tawi in.

records.english: Who left the toothpaste open on the sink again?
records.zomi: Ha silna khempeuh kuang tungah kua in a hong nusia kik hiam?

records.english: Not me — I haven't even brushed my teeth yet!
records.zomi: Keimah hi lo — ka ha zong ka sil nai kei hi!

records.english: Why does your mother wake you up by singing?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na nu in la sa-in hong phawngsak hiam?

records.english: Her own mother did the same, and she says nobody can be grumpy after a song.
records.zomi: Amah' nu in zong tua bangin a hih a, la khit ciangin kuamah lungkia thei lo hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Do you get ready differently on your days off?
records.zomi: Na tawlngak ni-in tuamtuam takin na kiman hiam?

records.english: Yes, I don't even look in a mirror until noon.
records.zomi: Hi hi, sun dong mai-et zong ka en kei hi.

records.english: How do you wake up without an alarm clock?
records.zomi: Alarm om lo-in bangci-in na thou hiam?

records.english: The rooster next door does the job better than any clock.
records.zomi: Inn veng-a akpa in nai khempeuh sangin a sem hoih zaw hi.

records.english: What happened to your shirt?
records.zomi: Na angki bang a piang hiam?

records.english: The iron was too hot, and now there's a brown mark on the collar.
records.zomi: Phawkna a sa lua ahih manin tu-in a ngawng ah a sanglawh mun a om hi.

records.english: Can I sleep for ten more minutes?
records.zomi: Minit sawm behlap ka ihmu thei ding hiam?

records.english: Five, and then I'm opening the curtains whether you like it or not.
records.zomi: Nga, tua ciangin na deih zongin na deih kei zongin tukvuang puan ka hong ding hi.

records.english: How did you manage to get the baby dressed so quickly?
records.zomi: Naungek manlang takin bangci-in puan na silhsak thei hiam?

records.english: I sang to her the whole time, and she forgot to complain.
records.zomi: Hun bup la ka sa a, a phun ding a mangngilh hi.

records.english: Why are you getting ready by candlelight?
records.zomi: Bang hangin khawimeivaak tawh na kiman hiam?

records.english: The power went off before dawn, and it still hasn't come back.
records.zomi: Khuavak ma-in meivak a mit a, tu dong a hong vak kik nai kei hi.

records.english: Are you sure you've got your keys, your phone, and your lunch?
records.zomi: Na tawh, na phone leh na sun an na nei hi, cih na kician hiam?

records.english: Keys and phone, yes, but I've just remembered the lunch box on the table.
records.zomi: Tawh leh phone nei ing, ahi zongin dawhkan tung-a an bawm ka phawk thak hi.

records.english: What would make mornings in this house less of a race?
records.zomi: Bang in hih inn-a zingsangte kikhenkhaina tawmsak ding hiam?

records.english: Laying out clothes the night before and getting up fifteen minutes earlier, but nobody listens.
records.zomi: Zan ma-in puan koih khol leh minit sawm leh nga ma-in thoh, ahi zongin kuamah in a ngai kei hi.

records.english: Is it cold enough for a coat this morning?
records.zomi: Tuni zingsang kawt silh dingin a vot hiam?

records.english: Take one anyway, because the radio says it'll rain later.
records.zomi: Bangbang ahi zongin khat la in, a nung ciangin guah zuk ding hi, ci-in radio in a ci hi.

records.english: Kids, have you all packed your bags for school?
records.zomi: Naupangte, sang adingin na ip uh na thuk khin uh hiam?

records.english: Everyone except Mang, who can't find his math book again.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, Mang bek a math laibu a mu kik zo kei hi.

records.english: If you didn't have to work, what time would you get up?
records.zomi: Na nasep kei leh nai bangzah ciangin na thou ding hiam?

records.english: Probably at the same time, because my body can't sleep past six anymore.
records.zomi: Hun kibang mah ah kha ding hi, ka pumpi in nai guk zawh nawn ihmu thei nawn lo ahih manin.

records.english: What's your morning like when the children have exams?
records.zomi: Naupangte sitna a neih ciangun na zingsang bangci-in a om hiam?

records.english: Chaos, because everybody wants the bathroom and nobody can find a pencil.
records.zomi: Kibuai mahmah hi, mi khempeuh in kisilna inn a deih uh a, kuamah in khedal a mu kei hi.

records.english: How early do you have to get up on market days?
records.zomi: Zuakna ni-in zingsang bangzah ciangin na thou hiam?

records.english: At half past three, because the vegetables have to be loaded before dawn.
records.zomi: Nai thum leh a khen ciangin, khuavak ma-in anteh a kikoih ding ahih manin.

records.english: Although the vote was close, the bill passed, and the new school was finally built.
records.zomi: Vote a kinai mahmah hangin thukham ding a kipia a, sang thak a tawp-in kilam hi.

records.english: Members of parliament are elected by the people of their district.
records.zomi: Parliament member te a khua sung-a mite in a teel uh hi.

records.english: The farmers came to the capital so that parliament would hear about the drought.
records.zomi: Khuakhal thu parliament in a zak nadingin lo neite khuapi lian ah a hong uh hi.

records.english: Everyone, please switch off your phones before we go into the public gallery.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, mipi tutna ah i lut ma-un na phone uh khek un.

records.english: There may be a vote on the new road plan before the end of the month.
records.zomi: Kha bei ma-in lampi thak gelna tungah vote a om kha ding hi.

records.english: Is the speaker of parliament allowed to vote?
records.zomi: Parliament makaipa in vote a pia thei hiam?

records.english: In our parliament, only if the votes on both sides are equal.
records.zomi: I parliament ah, a lam nih-a vote a kibat ciang bek.

records.english: Kids, look at the screen — that's where the votes are counted.
records.zomi: Naupangte, screen en un — tua ah vote a kisim hi.

records.english: A good representative listens to the people who did not vote for them as well as to those who did.
records.zomi: Aiawhtu hoih in amah a teel lote' thu zong a teel te' thu bangin a ngai hi.

records.english: The petition from our village was given to parliament by our representative.
records.zomi: I khua' ngetna lai i aiawhtu in parliament a pia hi.

records.english: The debate went on so late that the members didn't vote until midnight.
records.zomi: Kikupna a nai lua ahih manin member te in zanlai dong vote a pia kei uh hi.

records.english: Did the bill about clean water pass?
records.zomi: Tui siang thu-a thukham ding a kipia hiam?

records.english: Not yet, because the members are still arguing about who will pay for it.
records.zomi: Kipia nai lo hi, member te in kua in a pia ding hiam a kinial lai uh ahih manin.

records.english: Could you help me write to my representative, since I don't know what to say?
records.zomi: Bang ka gen ding ka thei kei ahih manin ka aiawhtu kiangah lai ka gelh nadingin hong huh thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Had more people written to their representatives, the bill might have been changed.
records.zomi: Mi tam zaw in a aiawhtu uh kiangah lai a gelh uh le, thukham ding a kilaih kha ding hi.

records.english: Our representative came to the school to explain how a law is made.
records.zomi: Thukham bangci-in kibawl hiam a gen siang dingin i aiawhtu sang ah a hong hi.

records.english: The more people attend the town meetings, the more seriously our representative listens.
records.zomi: Khua kikhopna ah mi a tam semsem ciangin i aiawhtu in a ngai semsem hi.

records.english: What surprised the students most was how politely the members disagreed with each other.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte a lamdang sak pen pen member te a kithukim lo laitakin zahtak taka a kikup dan uh ahi hi.

records.english: Not until the floods did parliament agree to spend money on the river walls.
records.zomi: Tuiciim khit ciang bek parliament in gun kulh adingin sum zat a kithukim hi.

records.english: The new law might change how much farmers pay for water.
records.zomi: Thukham thak in lo neite' tui man a laihsak kha ding hi.

records.english: My sister works in parliament, keeping a written record of every debate.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu parliament ah na a sem a, kikupna khempeuh a gelh hi.

records.english: A committee of members looked at the bill carefully before the whole parliament voted on it.
records.zomi: Parliament bup in vote a piak ma-un member committee khat in thukham ding pilvang takin a et uh hi.

records.english: The new law about school buses was passed last week.
records.zomi: Sang bus thu-a thukham thak kal nung in kipia hi.

records.english: Rather than voting straight away, the members asked the committee to study the bill for another month.
records.zomi: Tua mah-in vote pia sangin member te in thukham ding kha khat behlap sin dingin committee a ngen uh hi.

records.english: The members of parliament voted by pressing buttons on their desks.
records.zomi: Parliament member te in a dawhkan tung-a button nek-in vote a pia uh hi.

records.english: Parliament made a new law to protect the forests near our village.
records.zomi: I khua kiang-a gamte veng dingin parliament in thukham thak a bawl hi.

records.english: Parliament closes for the summer and meets again in September.
records.zomi: Parliament khal hun ah a kikhak a, September ciangin a kikhawm kik hi.

records.english: When does the new law start?
records.zomi: Bang ciangin thukham thak a kipan ding hiam?

records.english: Our representative holds a meeting at the town hall every month so that people can ask her questions.
records.zomi: Mite in dotna a dot theih nadingun i aiawhtu in kha simin khuapi inn ah kikhopna a bawl hi.

records.english: My uncle worked as a cleaner in parliament for thirty years.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu kum sawmthum sung parliament ah a siangsaktu hi.

records.english: Watching parliament on television, my son decided that he wants to be a member one day.
records.zomi: Parliament TV ah a en-in, ka tapa in ni khat ni ciangin member khat suak a deih hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Who is our representative in parliament?
records.zomi: Parliament ah i aiawhtu kua ahi hiam?

records.english: A former teacher from our district, who was elected two years ago.
records.zomi: I khua pan saya lui khat, kum nih paisa-a kiteel.

records.english: Having watched the debate for an hour, my grandfather said it reminded him of our family dinners.
records.zomi: Nai khat sung kikupna a en khit ciangin, ka pu in i innkuan nitak ante a phawksak hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Why are there police officers outside parliament today?
records.zomi: Bang hangin tuni-in parliament pua ah palik te a om uh hiam?

records.english: There's a big vote this afternoon, and many people have come to watch.
records.zomi: Tuni nitak lam vote lian khat a om a, mi tampi en dingin a hong uh hi.

records.english: So many letters arrived about the bus law that the committee asked for more time to read them.
records.zomi: Bus thukham thu-ah lai tam lua a tun ahih manin committee in sim dingin hun behlap a ngen hi.

records.english: What does a member of parliament do all day?
records.zomi: Parliament member khat in ni bup bang a sem hiam?

records.english: They meet people from their district, discuss new laws, and vote on them.
records.zomi: A khua pan mite a mu a, thukham thakte a kikup a, a tungah vote a pia hi.

records.english: The debate was shown on television so that people at home could watch it.
records.zomi: Inn-a mite in a muh theih nadingun kikupna TV ah kilak hi.

records.english: Our class visited parliament and watched a debate from the public gallery.
records.zomi: I kilasi in parliament a veh a, mipi tutna pan kikupna khat i en hi.

records.english: Where can I find out how my representative voted?
records.zomi: Ka aiawhtu in bangci-in vote a pia hiam koi ah ka thei thei ding hiam?

records.english: On parliament's website, which lists every vote by name.
records.zomi: Parliament' website tung ah, vote khempeuh min tawh a om hi.

records.english: How many members are there in parliament?
records.zomi: Parliament ah member bangzah a om hiam?

records.english: I'm not sure, but the guide said there's one for every district in the country.
records.zomi: Ka kician kei hi, ahi zongin gam sung-a khua khat ciat adingin khat a om hi, ci-in lampi lak pa in a ci hi.

records.english: I do want to meet our representative, because nobody has fixed the road to the clinic.
records.zomi: Siavuan inn pai lampi kuamah in a bawl siang kei ahih manin i aiawhtu ka muh nuam mahmah hi.

records.english: What happens if parliament can't agree on a bill?
records.zomi: Parliament in thukham ding tungah a kithukim zo kei leh bang a piang hiam?

records.english: In our system, the bill goes back to a committee to be changed, and then they try again.
records.zomi: I ngeina ah, thukham ding laih dingin committee kiang ah a kik a, tua ciangin a sin kik uh hi.

records.english: Students, today you'll each play a member of parliament and vote on a new school rule.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte, tuni-in note khat ciat in parliament member hi-in sang thupiak thak tungah vote na pia ding uh hi.

records.english: The members stood and clapped when the bill for free school meals was passed.
records.zomi: Sang an man om lo adingin thukham ding a kipiak ciangin member te a ding uh a, khut a beng uh hi.

records.english: I wrote a letter to our representative about the broken bridge.
records.zomi: Lei sia thu-ah i aiawhtu kiangah lai ka gelh hi.

records.english: Do members of parliament live in the capital?
records.zomi: Parliament member te khuapi lian ah a om uh hiam?

records.english: During the sessions they do, but most go home to their districts at the weekend.
records.zomi: Kikhopna hun sungin om uh hi, ahi zongin a tamzaw kal tawp ciangin a khua uh ah a ciah uh hi.

records.english: A bill is a plan for a new law that parliament has not yet agreed to.
records.zomi: Thukham ding pen parliament in a thukim nai loh thukham thak gelna khat ahi hi.

records.english: Let me show you where our district's member sits in the chamber.
records.zomi: Kikhopna khan sung ah i khua' member koi ah a tu hiam kong etsak ni.

records.english: Can anyone watch parliament when it meets?
records.zomi: Parliament a kikhop ciangin kua peuhpeuh in a en thei hiam?

records.english: Yes, but in our country you have to book a seat in the gallery a few days before.
records.zomi: Thei hi, ahi zongin i gam ah ni tawmno ma-in tutna ah mun na koih khol ding hi.

records.english: Parliament meets in the big building by the river.
records.zomi: Parliament gun kiang-a inn lianpi ah a kikhawm hi.

records.english: Is there a small parliament for young people in your country?
records.zomi: Na gam ah khangnote adingin parliament neu khat a om hiam?

records.english: There is, and students from every district meet once a year to debate real problems.
records.zomi: Om hi, khua khempeuh pan sangnaupangte kum khat ah khatvei a kikhawm uh a, buaina taktakte a kikup uh hi.

records.english: How do you know when the oil is hot enough?
records.zomi: Sathau a sa kicing hi, cih bangci-in na thei hiam?

records.english: Drop in a tiny piece of bread, and if it sizzles at once, the oil is ready.
records.zomi: Moh neu khat khia inla, a man takin a kawk leh sathau a kim khin hi.

records.english: Why does the rice taste burnt?
records.zomi: Bang hangin an in a kang bang a tui hiam?

records.english: I forgot to turn the heat down while I was on the phone.
records.zomi: Phone ka zat laitakin mei ka nemsak ding ka mangngilh hi.

records.english: How do you know when the chicken is cooked?
records.zomi: Aksa a min khin hi, cih bangci-in na thei hiam?

records.english: Push a fork into it, and if the juice runs clear, it's ready.
records.zomi: Fork tawh sun inla, a tui a siang leh a min khin hi.

records.english: So many relatives came for the festival that we cooked rice in the big copper pot borrowed from the church.
records.zomi: Pawi adingin sanggam tam lua a hong uh ahih manin pawlpi pan i ngetsak sik beel lianpi sung ah an i huan hi.

records.english: Can you taste the curry for me, since I've got a cold?
records.zomi: Khuasik ka nei ahih manin curry na tetsak thei ding hiam?

records.english: It needs a little more salt, but otherwise it's perfect.
records.zomi: Cii tawmno a kisap lai hi, ahi zongin a dang khempeuh a hoih hi.

records.english: What made you decide to cook every meal at home?
records.zomi: Bang in an khempeuh inn ah huan dingin na ngaihsutsak hiam?

records.english: The doctor told me to eat less salt, and restaurant food is full of it.
records.zomi: Cii tawm zaw ne dingin siavuan in hong hilh a, anneekna mun an ah cii a tam hi.

records.english: Is it true that your grandfather can cook a whole pig over a fire?
records.zomi: Na pu in mei tungah vok bup a huan thei hi, cih a tak hiam?

records.english: It is, though nowadays he mostly tells the young men what they're doing wrong.
records.zomi: A tak hi, tu hun ciangin khangno pasalte' a hih khialhte a gen tam zaw hi.

records.english: Had the oven not broken, would you have baked the bread yourself?
records.zomi: Oven a sia kei le, moh nangma-in na em ding hiam?

records.english: Without a doubt, because bought bread never tastes the same at a wedding.
records.zomi: Lungmanglah om lo-in, mopawi ah moh lei pen a tui kibang ngei lo ahih manin.

records.english: Could you show me how to use the pressure cooker?
records.zomi: Pressure cooker zat dan hong etsak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Watch carefully, because if you open the lid too early, the steam will burn you.
records.zomi: Pilvang takin en in, a khuhna manlang lua-in na hon leh a meikhu in hong kang ding hi.

records.english: What the children remember most about their grandmother's kitchen is the smell of bread on Saturday mornings.
records.zomi: Naupangte in a pi uh' an huanna-a a phawk pen pen Kiginni zingsang-a moh namtui ahi hi.

records.english: What would you cook if you had only rice, eggs, and one onion?
records.zomi: Buh, aktui leh lothaang khat bek na neih leh bang na huan ding hiam?

records.english: Fried rice, which is what I lived on for most of my first year at university.
records.zomi: Buh kikang, sangpi ka kah kum masa pen sung a tamzaw ka nek.

records.english: Who does the cooking in your house on weekends?
records.zomi: Kal tawp ciangin na inn ah kua in an a huan hiam?

records.english: Whoever wakes up first, which is usually Grandpa.
records.zomi: A thou masa pen peuhpeuh, a tamzaw-in ka pu ahi hi.

records.english: What's the secret of your grandmother's pickles?
records.zomi: Na pi' anteh thuksa' thuguk bang ahi hiam?

records.english: She won't tell anyone, not even my mother.
records.zomi: Kuamah a hilh kei hi, ka nu zong a hilh kei hi.

records.english: Is it all right to freeze the leftover soup?
records.zomi: An tui a hiam a khalsak leh a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, but let it cool down completely first.
records.zomi: Hoih hi, ahi zongin a masa-in a vot kim dong ngak in.

records.english: Do you think the guests will like the sour fish?
records.zomi: Khualte in nga thuk a deih ding uh in na ngaihsun hiam?

records.english: They might find it strange at first, but they'll ask for more.
records.zomi: A masa-in a lamdang sa kha ding uh a, ahi zongin a behlap a ngen ding uh hi.

records.english: What's in the big pot on the stove?
records.zomi: Meikhuk tung-a beel lian sung ah bang a om hiam?

records.english: Fish soup, because your uncle brought fish from the river this morning.
records.zomi: Nga tui, na pa neu in tuni zingsangin gun pan nga a tawi ahih manin.

records.english: How did the noodles end up on the ceiling?
records.zomi: An-ngum bangci-in innkhum nuai ah a kibelh hiam?

records.english: My little brother wanted to see whether they were cooked, and someone told him to throw one.
records.zomi: Ka nau pasal in a min khin hiam a theih nuam a, kuamah in khat lawn dingin a hilh hi.

records.english: Do you cook with gas or with wood?
records.zomi: Gas tawh na huan hiam, sing tawh hiam?

records.english: Gas in the kitchen, but we still use wood outside for the big festival pots.
records.zomi: An huanna ah gas, ahi zongin pawi beel lian adingin pua ah sing i zang lai hi.

records.english: Why do you always make extra food on Sundays?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Nipini simin an behlap na huan tawntung hiam?

records.english: Because somebody always arrives without warning, and nobody should leave hungry.
records.zomi: Kuamah gen lo-in a hong tawntung a, kuamah gilkial-in a pai khia ding hi lo ahih manin.

records.english: Who cooks when you and your wife both work late?
records.zomi: Nang leh na zi a nai-in na nasep ciangun kua in an a huan hiam?

records.english: Our son, who wants to practice before he leaves home for university.
records.zomi: I tapa in, sangpi kah dingin inn a nusiat ma-in a kisin nuam hi.

records.english: Kids, who wants to help me make dumplings?
records.zomi: Naupangte, dumpling bawl dingin kua in hong huh nuam hiam?

records.english: Me, as long as I can make the funny-shaped ones!
records.zomi: Keimah, a lim nuihzathuai te ka bawl thei leh!

records.english: When did the power go off?
records.zomi: Bang ciangin meivak a mit hiam?

records.english: Just before the guests came, so we lit the old charcoal stove in the yard.
records.zomi: Khualte a hong tun ma-in, tua ahih manin tual-a meihol meikhuk lui i hal hi.

records.english: How much rice do we need for twelve people?
records.zomi: Mi sawm leh nih adingin buh bangzah i kisam hiam?

records.english: Make three cups, because your brothers always eat more than you expect.
records.zomi: Haai thum bawl in, na sanggam pasalte in na ngaihsut sangin a ne tam zaw tawntung uh ahih manin.

records.english: Who taught you to make such soft bread?
records.zomi: Moh nem hih bang bawl dan kua in hong hilh hiam?

records.english: A baker in the next village, who let me stand beside him every Saturday until I'd learned all his tricks.
records.zomi: Khua kiang-a moh bawl pa khat in, a theih khempeuh ka sin dong Kiginni simin a kiang ah hong dingsak hi.

records.english: Is this soup spicy enough for your father?
records.zomi: Hih an tui na pa adingin a ha kicing hiam?

records.english: He'll add more chili anyway, so it doesn't really matter.
records.zomi: Bangbang ahi zongin malcha a behlap ding ahih manin a thupi kei hi.

records.english: What happened to the cake?
records.zomi: Cake bang a piang hiam?

records.english: The dog jumped up and ate half of it while we were setting the table.
records.zomi: Dawhkan i bawl laitakin ui a diang a, a khen khat a ne hi.

records.english: Would it be easier to buy the dumplings than to make them?
records.zomi: Dumpling bawl sangin lei a baih zaw ding hiam?

records.english: Easier, yes, but nobody in this family would forgive us.
records.zomi: Baih zaw hi, ahi zongin hih innkuan-a kuamah in hong maisak kei ding uh hi.

records.english: What's the hardest part of cooking dried beans?
records.zomi: Be keu huan ah a haksa pen bang ahi hiam?

records.english: Remembering to put them in water the night before.
records.zomi: Zan ma-in tui sung ah koih ding phawk.

records.english: Where did you learn to cook so many dishes from the coast?
records.zomi: Tuipi gei-a an tampi huan dan koi ah na sin hiam?

records.english: My wife, who grew up in a fishing town, taught me most of them in our first year of marriage.
records.zomi: Nga manna khua ah a khang ka zi in, i kiteen kum masa pen sungin a tamzaw hong hilh hi.

records.english: Can I help you peel the potatoes?
records.zomi: Alu na khilh nadingin kong huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, but use the small knife, and peel away from your fingers.
records.zomi: Thei hi, ahi zongin namsau neu zang inla, na khutzungte pan a gamla lam ah khilh in.

records.english: Why is everyone crying in the kitchen?
records.zomi: Bang hangin an huanna ah mi khempeuh a kap uh hiam?

records.english: We're chopping twenty onions for the wedding curry.
records.zomi: Mopawi curry adingin lothaang sawmnih i at uh hi.

records.english: How often does the chimney need cleaning?
records.zomi: Meikhu khuamna bang zah vei siangsak a kisam hiam?

records.english: Once a year, before the cold season starts, or the smoke comes back into the house.
records.zomi: Kum khat ah khatvei, khuavot hun kipat ma-in, a hi kei leh meikhu inn sung ah a hong kik hi.

records.english: How did the cupboard get so full of old shoes?
records.zomi: Van bawm in khedap lui tawh bangci-in a dim hiam?

records.english: Nobody has thrown out a single pair since we moved in.
records.zomi: I tuah pan kuamah in khedap khat zong a paai kei hi.

records.english: Why do you clean the house before every festival?
records.zomi: Bang hangin pawi khempeuh ma-in inn na siangsak hiam?

records.english: In our family, we believe a clean house welcomes a good year.
records.zomi: I innkuan ah inn siang in kum hoih a muak hi, ci-in i um hi.

records.english: Where have all the spoons gone?
records.zomi: Kawmte khempeuh koi ah a pai hiam?

records.english: Most of them are in your brother's room, under a pile of cereal bowls.
records.zomi: A tamzaw na sanggam pasal' khan sung ah, cereal kuang tampi nuai ah a om hi.

records.english: If you could get rid of one thing in this house, what would it be?
records.zomi: Hih inn sung pan bangmah khat na paai thei leh bang ahi ding hiam?

records.english: That enormous cupboard, which takes up half the hall and holds nothing useful.
records.zomi: Tua van bawm lianpi, inn lam khen khat a luah a, bangmah manphatna a koih lo.

records.english: Is it worth fixing the old vacuum cleaner, or should we buy a new one?
records.zomi: Vacuum cleaner lui bawl siang a manphat hiam, a thak khat i lei ding uh hiam?

records.english: Take it to the repair café first; they might be able to save it.
records.zomi: A masa-in bawlsiang na mun ah tawi in; a hon zo kha ding uh hi.

records.english: What's the quickest way to get the house ready for visitors?
records.zomi: Khual hongte adingin inn kiman manlang pen bang ahi hiam?

records.english: Clear the table, sweep the floor, and close the bedroom doors.
records.zomi: Dawhkan siangsak inla, tual phiat inla, lupna khan kongkhakte khak in.

records.english: Why are all the books on the floor?
records.zomi: Bang hangin laibu khempeuh tual ah a om hiam?

records.english: The shelf came off the wall in the night, so I'll need the drill to put it back.
records.zomi: Zan sungin laibu koihna bang pan a kiat ahih manin a koih kik nadingin drill ka kisam ding hi.

records.english: Would it help if I made a cleaning list for everyone?
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh adingin siangsakna list khat ka bawl leh a huh ding hiam?

records.english: It might, as long as you put your own name on it first.
records.zomi: Huh kha ding hi, a masa-in na min na gelh leh.

records.english: What would you save first if the house flooded?
records.zomi: Inn tui a liam leh bang na honkhia masa ding hiam?

records.english: The box of family photos, which is why it now lives on the top shelf.
records.zomi: Innkuan lim bawm, tua ahih manin tu-in a tung pen koihna ah a om hi.

records.english: How did you get the coffee stain out of the carpet?
records.zomi: Tuutphah tung-a khawfi bawk bangci-in na siangsak hiam?

records.english: I scrubbed it with cold water, a little soap and an old toothbrush.
records.zomi: Tui vot, satpiang tawmno leh ha sil lui khat tawh ka sil hi.

records.english: Who cleaned the windows so beautifully?
records.zomi: Tukvuangte hoih takin kua in a siangsak hiam?

records.english: My son did, as a surprise for his grandmother's visit.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in, a pi a hong veh ciangin lamdang a sak nadingin.

records.english: Had you sorted the papers last month, would you have found the receipt sooner?
records.zomi: Kha nung in laite na kikhen le, laimal na mu masa zaw ding hiam?

records.english: Probably, but then I wouldn't have found my old love letters as well.
records.zomi: Mu kha ding ing, ahi zongin tua ciangin ka it lai luite ka mu kei ding hi.

records.english: Is it true that you found money while cleaning the old sofa?
records.zomi: Tutphah lui na siangsak laitakin sum na mu hi, cih a tak hiam?

records.english: Only a few coins, but also my grandmother's lost wedding ring.
records.zomi: Dangka tawmno bek, ahi zongin ka pi' mang mopawi zungbuh zong ka mu hi.

records.english: Can I put my clothes in your wardrobe while I stay with you?
records.zomi: Na kiang ka om laitakin ka puante na puan bawm sung ah ka koih thei ding hiam?

records.english: Please do — I've cleared the bottom two shelves for you.
records.zomi: Koih in — a nuai lam koihna nih kong siangsak khin hi.

records.english: Why does tidying always take longer than you expect?
records.zomi: Bang hangin kiman pen na ngaihsut sangin a sawt zaw tawntung hiam?

records.english: Because you keep stopping to look at old photos and letters.
records.zomi: Lim lui leh lai luite en dingin na tawl den ahih manin.

records.english: Who's going to wash the dog?
records.zomi: Ui kua in a sil ding hiam?

records.english: Whoever let him roll in the mud this morning.
records.zomi: Tuni zingsangin bual sung ah a liipsak peuhpeuh in.

records.english: How long has that pile of newspapers been by the door?
records.zomi: Kongkhak kiang-a laithak bu bangzah sung a om khin hiam?

records.english: Since the summer, because nobody wants to carry it to the recycling bin.
records.zomi: Khal hun pan, kuamah in nawi koihna ah a pua nuam kei uh ahih manin.

records.english: Why does the bathroom mirror steam up so badly?
records.zomi: Bang hangin kisilna inn-a mai-et meikhu tawh a kikhuh lua hiam?

records.english: The fan has been broken for months, and nobody has had it repaired.
records.zomi: Fan kha tampi sung a sia a, kuamah in a bawlsak kei hi.

records.english: Could you put the clean dishes away while I wash the pots?
records.zomi: Beel ka sil laitakin kuang siangte na koih sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Sure, but tell me where the big plates go, because I always forget.
records.zomi: Thei hi, ahi zongin kuang liante koi ah a koih hiam hong gen in, ka mangngilh tawntung ahih manin.

records.english: However often we tidy, the kitchen table always ends up covered in papers by Friday.
records.zomi: Bangzah vei i kiman zongin Laithai ni ciangin an huanna dawhkan lai tawh a kikhuh tawntung hi.

records.english: What happened when you finally cleared out the garage?
records.zomi: Mawtaw inn na siangsak tawp ciangin bang a piang hiam?

records.english: We found an old bicycle that had been my father's, and my son rode it to school the next day.
records.zomi: Ka pa' siiksakol lui khat i mu a, a zing ciangin ka tapa in sang ah a tuang hi.

records.english: What's that strange smell coming from the fridge?
records.zomi: Khal bawm pan a hong nam lamdang bang ahi hiam?

records.english: A bowl of soup that somebody hid at the back two weeks ago.
records.zomi: Kal nih paisa-in kuamah in a nung lam ah a sel an tui kuang khat.

records.english: Does anyone know where the spare light bulbs are?
records.zomi: Meivak bulb behlapte koi ah a om hiam kuamah in a thei hiam?

records.english: In the kitchen drawer, next to the candles and the torch.
records.zomi: An huanna bawm sung ah, khawimeivaak leh dawimei kiang ah.

records.english: Clearing out my parents' house after they moved, I found every school report I had ever brought home.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa a tuah khit uh ciangin a inn ka siangsak laitakin, inn ah ka tawi ngei sang report khempeuh ka mu hi.

records.english: Can you help Grandpa clean out his shed this weekend?
records.zomi: Hih kal tawp ciangin ka pu' van inn siangsak dingin na huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: I'd love to, as long as he lets me throw something away.
records.zomi: Ka deih mahmah hi, bangmah khat paai dingin hong phal leh.

records.english: Kids, can each of you tidy one room before lunch?
records.zomi: Naupangte, sun an ma-in note khat ciat in khan khat na siangsak thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: Only if we can choose which room!
records.zomi: Koi khan hiam i teel thei leh bek!

records.english: Do you really need fifteen plastic bags under the sink?
records.zomi: Kuang silna nuai ah plastic ip sawm leh nga na kisam taktak hiam?

records.english: You never know when you'll need one, my mother-in-law always says.
records.zomi: Bang ciangin khat na kisap ding hiam na thei ngei kei hi, ka sungnu in a ci tawntung hi.

records.english: Is there anything in this box that you still use?
records.zomi: Hih bawm sung ah na zat lai bangmah a om hiam?

records.english: Only the old radio, which I'd like to give to my cousin.
records.zomi: Radio lui bek, ka sanggam ka piak nuam.

records.english: How do you keep the spices in order?
records.zomi: Antui namtuite bangci-in na koih kiphatsak hiam?

records.english: Every jar has a label, and they stand in alphabetical order on one shelf.
records.zomi: Bel khat ciat ah min a kigelh a, koihna khat tungah ABC zui-in a ding uh hi.

records.english: Why is there sand all over the hallway?
records.zomi: Bang hangin inn lam bup ah piaktui a om hiam?

records.english: The children came back from the river and forgot to shake their shoes outside.
records.zomi: Naupangte gun pan a hong kik uh a, pua ah a khedap uh nawk dingin a mangngilh uh hi.

records.english: Is it true that you walk to work along the river every day?
records.zomi: Ni simin gun gei zui-in nasepna ah na pai hi, cih a tak hiam?

records.english: It is, and it's the only time all day that nobody needs anything from me.
records.zomi: A tak hi, ni bup-in kuamah in bangmah a ngetloh hun khat bek ahi hi.

records.english: Why are you so tired on Mondays?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pizing ni simin na tawl mahmah hiam?

records.english: I help at my uncle's restaurant all weekend, so I never really rest.
records.zomi: Kal tawp bup ka pa neu' anneekna inn ah ka huh ahih manin ka tawldam taktak ngei kei hi.

records.english: What do you do during the quiet afternoons at the market?
records.zomi: Zuakna mun ah nitak lam dai hun sungin bang na hih hiam?

records.english: I mend the baskets and chat with the woman at the next stall.
records.zomi: Bawm ka bawl siang a, a kiang-a zuakna mun-a numei tawh ka kiho hi.

records.english: What makes a working day pass quickly is usually the people you share it with.
records.zomi: Nasep ni khat manlang taka a bei sak pen a tamzaw-in na kihawm khawm mite ahi hi.

records.english: Is your job the same every day, or does it change?
records.zomi: Na nasep ni simin a kibang hiam, a kilai hiam?

records.english: It changes completely, because I never know which patients will come in.
records.zomi: Koi natnate hong lut ding hiam ka thei ngei kei ahih manin a kilai kim hi.

records.english: Who locks up the office at night?
records.zomi: Zan ciangin office kua in a khak hiam?

records.english: Whoever leaves last, and they have to check every window first.
records.zomi: A pai nunung pen peuhpeuh in, a masa-in tukvuang khempeuh a en ding hi.

records.english: Can I leave my bicycle in the staff room during my shift?
records.zomi: Ka nasep hun sungin nasemte khan ah ka siiksakol ka nusia thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, but lock it to the pipe, because the door is always open.
records.zomi: Thei hi, ahi zongin kongkhak a kihong tawntung ahih manin tui khuam ah khak in.

records.english: What's the first thing you do when you get to the office?
records.zomi: Office na tun ciangin bang na hih masa hiam?

records.english: I make tea and read my messages before anyone else arrives.
records.zomi: Midang a hong tun ma-un tea ka bawl a, ka thu khakte ka sim hi.

records.english: How do you remember all your customers' orders?
records.zomi: Na leite' ngetnate khempeuh bangci-in na phawk hiam?

records.english: I write them in a little notebook that I keep in my apron pocket.
records.zomi: Ka puan khaktaw ip sung-a ka koih laibu neu khat ah ka gelh hi.

records.english: How many cups of coffee do you drink at work?
records.zomi: Nasepna ah khawfi haai bangzah na dawn hiam?

records.english: Too many to count, especially during the busy season.
records.zomi: Sim zo lo dingin a tam hi, a diakin buai hun ciangin.

records.english: Why are you wearing your work boots to the wedding?
records.zomi: Bang hangin mopawi ah na nasep khedap na bulh hiam?

records.english: I came straight from the building site, and there wasn't time to go home.
records.zomi: Inn lamna mun pan a tang takin ka hong a, inn ah ciah hun a om kei hi.

records.english: Everyone, could you finish your reports by Thursday, since the director arrives on Friday?
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, director Laithai ni-in a hong tun ding ahih manin Laizing ni ma-in na report uh na zo thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: Thursday is fine, but please don't call another meeting before then.
records.zomi: Laizing ni a hoih hi, ahi zongin tua ma-in kikhopna dang sam nawn kei in.

records.english: Who taught you how to use the cash register?
records.zomi: Sum koihna set zat dan kua in hong hilh hiam?

records.english: The owner's daughter, who was so patient that I learned it in a day.
records.zomi: A neipa' tanu in, a thuakzawh lua ahih manin ni khat sungin ka sin hi.

records.english: When do the fishermen come back with the catch?
records.zomi: Nga mante nga tawh bang ciangin a hong kik uh hiam?

records.english: Around dawn, if the sea has been calm during the night.
records.zomi: Khuavak kim ah, zan sungin tuipi a dai leh.

records.english: What does your job involve on a normal Tuesday?
records.zomi: Pithai ni pangai ah na nasep in bang a huam hiam?

records.english: Mostly phone calls, two site visits, and far too many forms.
records.zomi: A tamzaw phone samna, mun et nih, leh form tam lua.

records.english: Why do you check the weather before you leave for the boat?
records.zomi: Bang hangin long lam na pai ma-in huihkhua na en hiam?

records.english: Because a storm can turn a normal working day into a dangerous one.
records.zomi: Huihpi in nasep ni pangai khat lauhuai ni a suaksak thei ahih manin.

records.english: How do you stay awake on the night shift?
records.zomi: Zan nasep ah bangci-in na mit na khak lo hiam?

records.english: I walk around the ward every hour and talk to the patients who can't sleep.
records.zomi: Nai khat simin zato khan bup ka vak a, a ihmu thei lo natnate tawh ka kiho hi.

records.english: What happens at the mill when the power goes off?
records.zomi: Meivak a mit ciangin buh guaina inn ah bang a piang hiam?

records.english: Everything stops, and we sweep the floors until it comes back on.
records.zomi: Khempeuh a tawp a, a hong vak kik dong tual i phiat hi.

records.english: If you could change one thing about your working day, what would it be?
records.zomi: Na nasep ni ah khat na laih thei leh bang ahi ding hiam?

records.english: I'd start an hour later and finish an hour later, because my mornings are useless.
records.zomi: Nai khat nung zaw-in ka kipan ding a, nai khat nung zaw-in ka zo ding hi, ka zingsangte a manphat kei ahih manin.

records.english: How did your boss react when you were late for the third time?
records.zomi: Thum veina na nun ciangin na makai in bangci-in a dawng hiam?

records.english: She made me promise to catch the earlier bus, and I haven't been late since.
records.zomi: Bus masa zaw la dingin hong kiciamsak a, tua pan ka nun ngei nawn kei hi.

records.english: Why does the bakery close at two in the afternoon?
records.zomi: Bang hangin moh bawlna nitak lam nai nih ciangin a kikhak hiam?

records.english: The bakers start at three in the morning, so by lunchtime they're exhausted.
records.zomi: Moh bawlte zingsang nai thum ciangin a kipan uh ahih manin sun ciangin a tawl mahmah uh hi.

records.english: Who opens the shop when the owner is away?
records.zomi: A neipa a om kei ciangin dawr kua in a hong hiam?

records.english: His nephew, who has his own key and knows the alarm code.
records.zomi: A tanau, amah' tawh nei-in alarm code a thei pa.

records.english: What time does the factory siren go off?
records.zomi: Factory siren nai bangzah ciangin a ging hiam?

records.english: At seven for the morning shift and at three for the afternoon one.
records.zomi: Zingsang nasep adingin nai sagih ciangin, nitak lam nasep adingin nai thum ciangin.

records.english: Had the bus not broken down, would you have made it to the interview?
records.zomi: Bus a sia kei le, interview ah na tung in ding hiam?

records.english: Easily, but the manager liked my story about walking the last two miles so much that she hired me anyway.
records.zomi: Baihlam takin, ahi zongin a nunung mile nih ka kalsuan tangthu a manager in a deih lua ahih manin hong la mah hi.

records.english: Would you like me to bring you something from the canteen?
records.zomi: Anneekna pan bangmah kong tawi sak ding hiam?

records.english: Just a sandwich, please — I can't leave the desk until the phones are quiet.
records.zomi: Sandwich khat bek — phone te a dai dong dawhkan ka nusia thei kei hi.

records.english: Could you fix the printer before the meeting starts?
records.zomi: Kikhopna a kipat ma-in printer na bawl siang thei ding hiam?

records.english: I'll try, but if the paper is stuck again, we'll need the technician.
records.zomi: Ka sin ding hi, ahi zongin lai a kikhak kik leh technician i kisam ding hi.

records.english: Did the delivery driver bring the right boxes this time?
records.zomi: Van puak pa in tuin bawm dik a tawi hiam?

records.english: Two of them were for the shop next door, so I had him take them back.
records.zomi: A nih pen a kiang dawr adingin ahih manin a tawi kiksak hi.

records.english: Do you have to wear a uniform at the hotel?
records.zomi: Zinbuuk ah puan kibang na silh ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, and it has to be ironed every single morning.
records.zomi: Silh ding hi, zingsang simin phawk ding hi.

records.english: How do farmers know when to start work in the morning?
records.zomi: Lo neite in zingsangin nasep kipat hun bangci-in a thei uh hiam?

records.english: When the sun is up and the dew has gone from the fields.
records.zomi: Ni a suak a, lo sung pan daitui a bei ciangin.

records.english: Why does the clinic close for an hour at noon?
records.zomi: Bang hangin siavuan inn sun ciangin nai khat a kikhak hiam?

records.english: The nurses need a break, and the doctor visits patients at home then.
records.zomi: Nursete in tawlngakna a kisam uh a, tua hun ciangin siavuan in natnate a inn uh ah a veh hi.

records.english: So regular is the old baker's routine that the neighbors set their clocks by the smell of his bread.
records.zomi: Moh bawl pa upa' ngeina a kician lua ahih manin inn vengte in a moh namtui tawh a nai uh a bawl uh hi.

records.english: How do you get the baby to sleep in the car?
records.zomi: Mawtaw sung ah naungek bangci-in na ihmusak uh hiam?

records.english: We drive around the village twice with quiet music on.
records.zomi: La dai tawh khua bup nihvei i kimawng hi.

records.english: Is it safe to leave the candle burning while we sleep?
records.zomi: I ihmut laitakin khawimeivaak a vak lai-in nusia a bit ding hiam?

records.english: Never — blow it out and use the torch if you need to get up.
records.zomi: Ngei kei in — mut mit inla, na thoh kisap leh dawimei zang in.

records.english: How many blankets do you need when you sleep in the mountains?
records.zomi: Mual tung ah na ihmut ciangin puannak bangzah na kisam hiam?

records.english: At least three, and a hat if the fire goes out during the night.
records.zomi: A tawm penin thum, zan sungin mei a mit leh lukhu khat.

records.english: What did the doctor say about your trouble sleeping?
records.zomi: Na ihmut haksatna thu-ah siavuan in bang a ci hiam?

records.english: She told me to stop drinking coffee after lunch and to go to bed at the same time every night.
records.zomi: Sun an khit ciangin khawfi dawn nawn lo dingin, zan simin hun kibang-in lum dingin hong hilh hi.

records.english: Did the baby wake up again last night?
records.zomi: Zanni zanin naungek a khanglawh kik hiam?

records.english: Three times, so your father and I walked her up and down in shifts.
records.zomi: Thumvei, tua ahih manin na pa leh kei a kikhel-in i pom-in i vak hi.

records.english: Why does your brother sleep with the radio on?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na sanggam pasal radio ging tawh a ihmu hiam?

records.english: He says the silence in the village keeps him awake after years in the city.
records.zomi: Khuapi ah kum tampi a om khit ciangin khua' daihna in a ihmusak kei hi, a ci hi.

records.english: How do you keep mosquitoes away at night?
records.zomi: Zan ah thangkhuk bangci-in na hawl hiam?

records.english: We sleep under nets, and the windows have screens.
records.zomi: Thangkhuk puan nuai ah i ihmu a, tukvuangte in sel a nei hi.

records.english: Why did your parents make you sleep in separate rooms?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na nu leh na pa in khan tuamtuam ah hong ihmusak uh hiam?

records.english: Because my sister and I talked until two every night.
records.zomi: Kei leh ka sanggam nu zan simin nai nih dong i kiho ahih manin.

records.english: Can we finish the jigsaw puzzle before bed?
records.zomi: Ihmut ma-in jigsaw puzzle i zo thei ding hiam?

records.english: Only the corner you're working on, and the rest can wait until tomorrow.
records.zomi: Na bawl laitak gil bek, a dang zingciang dong a ngak thei hi.

records.english: What does your grandmother always say before she goes to sleep?
records.zomi: Na pi in a ihmut ma-in bang a ci tawntung hiam?

records.english: She says, "Thank you for today, and please let everyone wake up tomorrow."
records.zomi: “Tuni adingin ka lungdam hi, zingciang mi khempeuh thou kik dingin hong phal in,” a ci hi.

records.english: If you could go to bed at any time, when would it be?
records.zomi: Hun peuhpeuh ah na lum thei leh bang ciang ahi ding hiam?

records.english: At nine, though my children seem to think that's only for babies.
records.zomi: Nai kua ciangin, ka tate in naungekte adingin bek ahi hi, a ci uh hangin.

records.english: Why is there a bucket under the window?
records.zomi: Bang hangin tukvuang nuai ah bawm khat a om hiam?

records.english: The roof leaks when it rains at night, and we haven't had it fixed yet.
records.zomi: Zan ah guah a zuk ciangin innkhum a zu a, i bawl siang nai kei hi.

records.english: Why do you put your phone in the kitchen at night?
records.zomi: Bang hangin zan ah na phone an huanna ah na koih hiam?

records.english: So that I'm not tempted to check messages when I should be sleeping.
records.zomi: Ka ihmut ding hun ciangin thu khakte en ding ka ut loh nadingin.

records.english: Lying awake listening to the rain on the roof, my grandfather says he feels like a boy again.
records.zomi: Innkhum tung-a guah ging ngai-in a lup laitakin, ka pu in naupang a suak kik bangin a kisa hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Who snores so loudly in this house?
records.zomi: Hih inn sung ah kua in ihmut ciangin a nak ging sang mahmah hiam?

records.english: Your grandfather, and he insists that he has never snored in his life.
records.zomi: Na pu, a nuntak sung khatvei zong a nak a ging ngei kei hi, a ci den hi.

records.english: Could you cover the birdcage before you turn off the light?
records.zomi: Meivak na mit ma-in vasa inn na khuh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, otherwise the bird will start singing at four in the morning.
records.zomi: Thei hi, a hi kei leh zingsang nai li ciangin vasa la sa ding hi.

records.english: Had you gone to bed earlier, would you have heard the storm?
records.zomi: A ma zaw-in na lum le, huihpi na za ding hiam?

records.english: Probably not, because I sleep so deeply that even thunder doesn't wake me.
records.zomi: Za lo kha ding ing, ka ihmut a nak lua ahih manin van ging in zong hong phawngsak kei hi.

records.english: Can you check that the gas is off before you go up?
records.zomi: Na tun ma-in gas a kikhek khin hiam na en thei ding hiam?

records.english: I already have, and I've locked the back door too.
records.zomi: Ka en khin a, nung lam kongkhak zong ka khak khin hi.

records.english: Did you sleep well in the guest room?
records.zomi: Khualzin khan ah hoih takin na ihmu hiam?

records.english: Like a baby, until the rooster started at five.
records.zomi: Naungek bangin, nai nga ciangin akpa a khuan dong.

records.english: Kids, have you all brushed your teeth and put your clothes away?
records.zomi: Naupangte, na ha uh na sil khin uh a, na puan uh na koih khin uh hiam?

records.english: Everyone except Pau, who's hiding under the blanket with a comic.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, Pau bek comic khat tawh puannak nuai ah a bu hi.

records.english: What helps you sleep after a night shift?
records.zomi: Zan nasep khit ciangin bang in na ihmutna hong huh hiam?

records.english: Thick curtains, earplugs, and a family who promises to be quiet until noon.
records.zomi: Tukvuang puan tawtawh, bil khakna, leh sun dong dai dingin a kiciam innkuan khat.

records.english: Who will tell the children their story tonight?
records.zomi: Tuni zanin naupangte kua in tangthu a gen sak ding hiam?

records.english: Their uncle, who has promised a new one about a clever goat.
records.zomi: A pa neu uh, kel pil khat thu tangthu thak khat gen dingin a kiciam hi.

records.english: Why do you write in your diary every night?
records.zomi: Bang hangin zan simin na diary ah na gelh hiam?

records.english: It empties my head, so that I can sleep without worrying.
records.zomi: Ka lu a awngsak ahih manin lungkham lo-in ka ihmu thei hi.

records.english: Is there anything you'd like from the kitchen before I lock up?
records.zomi: Ka khak ma-in an huanna pan bangmah na deih hiam?

records.english: A glass of warm milk, if it isn't too much trouble.
records.zomi: Nawi lum haai khat, na buaipih lua kei leh.

records.english: What would make bedtime easier for your twins?
records.zomi: Na apengte adingin bang in ihmut hun a baihsak ding hiam?

records.english: Separate rooms, a quiet story, and parents who don't fall asleep before them.
records.zomi: Khan tuamtuam, tangthu dai khat, leh amaute ma-a ihmu lo nu leh pa.

records.english: What do you think about when you can't sleep?
records.zomi: Na ihmu zo kei ciangin bang na ngaihsun hiam?

records.english: All the things I should have said during the day.
records.zomi: Ni sung-a ka gen ding hi napi ka gen loh thu khempeuh.

records.english: Where should our guests sleep tonight?
records.zomi: Tuni zanin i khualte koi ah a ihmu ding uh hiam?

records.english: In the children's room, and the children can sleep on mats in ours.
records.zomi: Naupangte' khan ah, naupangte i khan sung ah phah tungah a ihmu thei uh hi.

records.english: When does the house finally go quiet?
records.zomi: Bang ciangin inn a tawp-in a dai hiam?

records.english: Around eleven, after the last teenager has stopped texting.
records.zomi: Nai sawm leh khat kim ah, khangno nunung pen in phone tawh thu a khak tawp khit ciangin.

records.english: Why do the children sleep at their grandparents' house on Fridays?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Laithai ni simin naupangte a pu leh pite inn ah a ihmu uh hiam?

records.english: So that we can go out together, and so that the grandparents can spoil them.
records.zomi: Khawm-a i pai theih nadingun, pu leh pite in a deih bangun a itsak theih nadingun.

records.english: So tired were the children after the festival that they fell asleep in their clothes.
records.zomi: Pawi khit ciangin naupangte a tawl lua uh ahih manin a puan uh tawh a ihmu uh hi.

records.english: Why can't you fall asleep tonight?
records.zomi: Bang hangin tuni zanin na ihmu zo kei hiam?

records.english: I keep thinking about the school trip tomorrow, and I'm too excited.
records.zomi: Zingciang sang khualzinna ka ngaihsun den a, ka lungdam lua hi.

records.english: Since I turned off the notifications, I've been able to read a whole book without checking my phone.
records.zomi: Notifications ka khek pan kipan ka phone en lo-in laibu bup ka sim thei hi.

records.english: Put a strong password on your phone in case it's ever stolen.
records.zomi: Kiguk kha leh na phone ah password hat khat koih in.

records.english: Not until the power came back did we realize how much we depended on our phones for news.
records.zomi: Meivak a hong vak kik ciang bek thu theih nadingin i phone tungah bangzah i kinga hiam i thei hi.

records.english: Had I backed up my photos, I wouldn't have lost the pictures from my daughter's wedding.
records.zomi: Ka limte backup bawl le ka tanu' mopawi limte ka mansuah kei ding hi.

records.english: Rather than handing the children a phone in the car, we play word games until we arrive.
records.zomi: Mawtaw sung ah naupangte phone pia sangin i tun dong kammal kimawlna i kimawl hi.

records.english: Turn on the flashlight so we can find the keys.
records.zomi: Tawh i muh theih nadingin flashlight vaksak in.

records.english: Could you show me how to send a voice message?
records.zomi: Aw thu khak dan hong etsak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Press and hold the microphone, speak, and then let go.
records.zomi: Microphone nek-in len inla, gen inla, tua ciangin khah in.

records.english: We'll need to buy a local SIM card when we land.
records.zomi: I tun ciangin hih gam SIM card khat i lei ding hi.

records.english: Which phone did you finally decide to buy?
records.zomi: A tawp-in koi phone na lei dingin na khensat hiam?

records.english: A cheaper model with a big battery, because I'm always away from a socket.
records.zomi: Battery lian nei man neu zaw khat, mei khukna pan ka gamla tawntung ahih manin.

records.english: However carefully you protect it, a phone dropped from that height is unlikely to survive.
records.zomi: Bangzah ta in na veng zongin tua bang a sanna pan a kia phone a dam ding hi lo hi.

records.english: My phone battery is almost dead.
records.zomi: Ka phone battery a bei dek hi.

records.english: Some apps keep running in the background and quietly drain the battery.
records.zomi: App khenkhatte a nung lam ah a pai den uh a, dai takin battery a bawl bei uh hi.

records.english: Everyone, put your phones face down on the table until dinner is over.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, nitak an a bei dong na phone uh dawhkan tungah a mai nuai lam ah koih un.

records.english: Restart the phone and see whether the problem goes away.
records.zomi: Phone khek inla vaksak kik inla, buaina a bei hiam en in.

records.english: Thang made his little brother delete the photos he had taken without asking.
records.zomi: Thang in a nau pasal in dong lo-a a lak limte phiat dingin a hilh hi.

records.english: I accidentally sent the message to the whole class instead of to my friend.
records.zomi: Ka lawm kiang hi lo-in kilasi bup kiangah thu ka khak khialh hi.

records.english: Let me save your number before I forget.
records.zomi: Ka mangngilh ma-in na number kong koih ning.

records.english: A cheap case would have saved you the cost of a new screen.
records.zomi: Case man neu khat in screen thak man pan hong hun ding hi.

records.english: Before you sell your old phone, make sure you erase everything on it.
records.zomi: Na phone lui na zuak ma-in a sung-a om khempeuh na phiat kim hiam en in.

records.english: This old phone still works, but it's far too slow for the new apps.
records.zomi: Hih phone lui a sem lai hi, ahi zongin app thakte adingin a zawi lua hi.

records.english: The more time she spends scrolling at night, the worse she sleeps.
records.zomi: Zan ah phone a en sawt semsem ciangin a ihmut a hoih lo semsem hi.

records.english: It might be the charging cable rather than the phone itself.
records.zomi: Phone mah hi lo-in charging cable ahi kha ding hi.

records.english: Our church uses a group chat to tell members when the meeting time changes.
records.zomi: I pawlpi in kikhopna hun a kilaih ciangin member te a hilh nadingin group chat khat a zang hi.

records.english: Kim bought her mother a phone with large buttons so that she could read the numbers easily.
records.zomi: Kim in a nu adingin number te baihlam taka a sim theih nadingin button lian nei phone khat a lei hi.

records.english: Did you get my message about the change of plans?
records.zomi: Gelna kilaih thu-a ka thu khak na ngah hiam?

records.english: Without the translation app on my phone, I would have been completely lost at the clinic.
records.zomi: Ka phone tung-a lehkikna app om lo hi leh siavuan inn ah ka mang kim ding hi.

records.english: I use my phone as an alarm clock every morning.
records.zomi: Zingsang simin ka phone alarm ah ka zang hi.

records.english: I lowered the screen brightness to make the battery last longer.
records.zomi: Battery a sau zawk nadingin screen vakna ka niamsak hi.

records.english: My son set up the new phone for me and copied all my contacts.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in phone thak hong bawl sak a, ka contacts khempeuh a copy hi.

records.english: Ni Ni ran out of storage, so she moved her old videos to a memory card.
records.zomi: Ni Ni' storage a dim ahih manin a video luite memory card ah a suan hi.

records.english: I keep my phone in a plastic bag when it rains.
records.zomi: Guah a zuk ciangin plastic ip sung ah ka phone ka koih hi.

records.english: Is your phone waterproof?
records.zomi: Na phone tui in a lut thei hiam?

records.english: Our neighbor, who repairs phones in his front room, can usually fix a charging port within the hour.
records.zomi: I inn veng, a inn mai khan ah phone bawl siangpa in charging port nai khat sung a bawl siang thei hi.

records.english: Having lost two phones in a year, Lian now keeps hers on a cord around her neck.
records.zomi: Kum khat sungin phone nih a mansuah khit ciangin Lian in tu-in a ngawng ah khau tawh a khih hi.

records.english: You can scan the code with your camera to pay at the market stall.
records.zomi: Zuakna mun ah sum pia dingin na camera tawh code na scan thei hi.

records.english: Whether a cheap phone is worth buying depends on how long you expect it to last.
records.zomi: Phone man neu khat lei a manphat hiam cih pen bangzah sawt a zat theih ding na ngaihsut tungah a kinga hi.

records.english: Shall I call you back on the landline?
records.zomi: Inn phone tawh kong sam kik ding hiam?

records.english: Could you take a photo of us in front of the waterfall?
records.zomi: Tuikhawng mai ah lim hong la sak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Keep the phone out of the sun, or the battery could be damaged.
records.zomi: Phone ni sa pan gamla takin koih in, a hi kei leh battery a sia thei hi.

records.english: Text me when your bus arrives.
records.zomi: Na bus a tun ciangin thu hong khak in.

records.english: What's the password for the Wi-Fi here?
records.zomi: Hih mun-a Wi-Fi password bang ahi hiam?

records.english: Can I borrow your charger for an hour?
records.zomi: Nai khat sung na charger ka zang thei ding hiam?

records.english: Sure, it's in the side pocket of my bag.
records.zomi: Thei hi, ka ip' a gei lam ip neu sung ah a om hi.

records.english: The screen cracked when I dropped the phone on the bathroom floor.
records.zomi: Kisilna inn tual ah phone ka khiat ciangin screen a kek hi.

records.english: I couldn't hear you because the signal kept dropping in the valley.
records.zomi: Guam sung ah signal a mang den ahih manin ka za thei kei hi.

records.english: I had the screen replaced at a small shop near the bus station.
records.zomi: Bus dinna kiang-a dawr neu khat ah screen ka lai sak hi.

records.english: The phone may update itself overnight if you leave it plugged in.
records.zomi: Mei na khuk lai-in na nusiat leh zan sungin phone amah mah in a update kha ding hi.

records.english: The volume button on the side has stopped working.
records.zomi: A gei lam-a ging button a sem nawn kei hi.

records.english: What frustrates my father most is that every update moves the buttons he finally learned to find.
records.zomi: Ka pa a lungkhamsak pen pen update khempeuh in a tawp-a a muh theih button te a suan hi, cih ahi hi.

records.english: My grandmother calls us on video every Sunday evening.
records.zomi: Ka pi in Nipini nitak simin video tawh hong sam hi.

records.english: Mang had his phone unlocked so that he could use a different network abroad.
records.zomi: Gamdang ah network dang a zat theih nadingin Mang in a phone unlock a bawl sak hi.

records.english: My phone gets hot when I play games for too long.
records.zomi: Game sawt lua ka kimawl ciangin ka phone a sa hi.

records.english: My brother uses his phone to check the weather before he goes out to the fields.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in lo ah a pai ma-in huihkhua en dingin a phone a zang hi.

records.english: Hold the phone sideways if you want a wider picture.
records.zomi: Lim zai zaw na deih leh phone a kawi-in len in.

records.english: The phone that once seemed like a luxury has become something most families here can't do without.
records.zomi: Ma-in hauhna bangin a kimu phone pen hih mun-a innkuan tamzaw in a om lo-in a om theih loh ding a suak khin hi.

records.english: Please turn your phones to silent before the service begins.
records.zomi: Pawlpi kikhopna a kipat ma-in na phone uh dai sak un.

records.english: When the call drops, wait a minute before you try again.
records.zomi: Phone samna a tan ciangin na sin kik ma-in minit khat ngak in.

records.english: If someone you don't know asks for the code sent to your phone, you should never share it.
records.zomi: Na theih loh kuamah in na phone ah a kikhak code a ngen leh na hawm ngei ding hi lo hi.

records.english: Which bag has the frozen peas in it?
records.zomi: Koi ip sung ah be khal a om hiam?

records.english: The blue one, next to the ice cream.
records.zomi: A dum pen, ice cream kiang ah.

records.english: Who ate the bananas I bought yesterday?
records.zomi: Zanni-a ka lei nahtangte kua in a ne hiam?

records.english: Your brothers, after football practice.
records.zomi: Na sanggam pasalte in, football kisin khit ciangin.

records.english: Do you want me to pick up anything for the baby?
records.zomi: Naungek adingin bangmah kong lei sak ding hiam?

records.english: Just some soft fruit and another packet of rice cereal, please.
records.zomi: Theigah nem tawmno leh buh cereal pakat khat behlap, hong lei sak in.

records.english: Why are there two bags of sugar on the table?
records.zomi: Bang hangin dawhkan tungah sugar ip nih a om hiam?

records.english: Your aunt bought one too, because she didn't know I'd already gone.
records.zomi: Ka pai khin hi, cih a theih loh manin na ni in khat a lei hi.

records.english: Can you read the date on this yogurt for me?
records.zomi: Hih yogurt tung-a ni hong sim sak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: It says it's good until Thursday, so it's fine.
records.zomi: Laizing ni dong a hoih hi, a ci ahih manin a hoih hi.

records.english: Why do you bring your own cloth bags?
records.zomi: Bang hangin nangma' puan ip na tawi hiam?

records.english: The shop charges for plastic ones, and they tear anyway.
records.zomi: Dawr in plastic ip adingin sum a la a, tua ahih kei zongin a kek hi.

records.english: How much rice do we have left?
records.zomi: Buh bangzah i nei lai hiam?

records.english: Enough for about three days.
records.zomi: Ni thum bang adingin a kicing hi.

records.english: Why did you buy so many onions?
records.zomi: Bang hangin lothaang tam lua na lei hiam?

records.english: They were half price, and they'll keep for weeks in the dry store.
records.zomi: A man a kiam a, van koihna kang ah kal tampi sung a om thei ahih manin.

records.english: Could you get the heavy things for Mrs. Niang when you go?
records.zomi: Na pai ciangin Mrs. Niang adingin a gik vante na lei sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Happily, and I'll bring them straight to her door.
records.zomi: Lungdam takin, a kongkhak dong ka tawi ding hi.

records.english: What would you buy if money were no problem this week?
records.zomi: Hih kal sungin sum buaina om lo hi leh bang na lei ding hiam?

records.english: Mangoes, good cheese, and enough meat to invite the whole street for dinner.
records.zomi: Haigah, cheese hoih, leh lampi bup nitak an sam theih dingin sa.

records.english: How did you carry all of this on the motorbike?
records.zomi: Hih khempeuh motorbike tungah bangci-in na tawi hiam?

records.english: With a rope, two baskets, and a great deal of care.
records.zomi: Khau khat, bawm nih, leh pilvangna tampi tawh.

records.english: What happened to the milk?
records.zomi: Nawi bang a piang hiam?

records.english: I left it in the car all afternoon, and it went sour.
records.zomi: Nitak lam bup mawtaw sung ah ka nusia a, a thuk hi.

records.english: Having forgotten her purse at home, Dim had to leave her full basket at the counter and run back for it.
records.zomi: Dim in a sum ip inn ah a mangngilh ahih manin a dim bawm sum piakna mun ah a nusia a, la dingin a tai kik hi.

records.english: Who told you that the market closes early on Saturdays?
records.zomi: Kiginni simin zuakna mun manlang zaw-in a kikhak hi, ci-in kua in hong hilh hiam?

records.english: The woman who sells eggs, and she should know.
records.zomi: Aktui zuak numei in, amah in a thei ding hi.

records.english: Did you remember the eggs?
records.zomi: Aktui na phawk hiam?

records.english: I did, but two of them broke in the bag on the way home.
records.zomi: Ka phawk hi, ahi zongin inn ciahna lampi ah ip sung ah nih a kek hi.

records.english: Why did the shop assistant make you open your bag?
records.zomi: Bang hangin dawr nasem in na ip hong honsak hiam?

records.english: She thought I'd taken a lemon, but it was one I'd bought somewhere else.
records.zomi: Lemon khat ka la in a ngaihsun a, ahi zongin mun dang ah ka lei khat ahi hi.

records.english: Is the scale at this stall accurate?
records.zomi: Hih zuakna mun-a gikna khaina a dik hiam?

records.english: The inspector checked it last month, and the seller keeps the certificate on the wall.
records.zomi: Kha nung in enkaktu in a en a, a zuakpa in a laipek bang ah a khai hi.

records.english: Is it worth driving to the wholesale market for a family our size?
records.zomi: I innkuan bangzah hi-a adingin van tam taka zuakna mun ah mawtaw tawh pai a manphat hiam?

records.english: Only if we go once a month and make a careful list beforehand.
records.zomi: Kha khat ah khatvei i pai a, a ma-in list pilvang takin i bawl leh bek.

records.english: How could we spend less on groceries without eating worse?
records.zomi: Hoih lo zaw-in ne lo-in an man bangci-in i tawmsak thei ding hiam?

records.english: By cooking beans and seasonal vegetables more often, and buying meat only twice a week.
records.zomi: Be leh a hun-a anteh tam zaw-in huan-in, kal khat ah nihvei bek sa lei-in.

records.english: Why do you always shop on the way home rather than on the weekend?
records.zomi: Bang hangin kal tawp sangin inn ciahna lampi ah na lei den hiam?

records.english: Buying a little at a time means less waste, and the bags aren't too heavy for the bus.
records.zomi: Tawmno tawmno lei pen a tawm zaw-in a mang a, ipte bus adingin a gik lua kei hi.

records.english: Are you making a list, or are you trusting your memory again?
records.zomi: List na bawl hiam, na phawkna na um kik hiam?

records.english: A list this time, because last week I came home without the rice.
records.zomi: Tuin list, kal nung in buh om lo-in inn ah ka hong tung ahih manin.

records.english: Should we buy the vegetables now or after the meeting?
records.zomi: Anteh tu-in i lei ding hiam, kikhopna khit ciangin hiam?

records.english: After, so that they don't wilt in the hot car.
records.zomi: A khit ciangin, mawtaw sa sung ah a vuai lo nadingin.

records.english: Where did you find such sweet pineapples?
records.zomi: Hih bang a lim pineapple koi ah na mu hiam?

records.english: At the roadside stall just before the bridge.
records.zomi: Lei ma-a lampi gei zuakna mun ah.

records.english: If the shop doesn't have fresh coriander, what should I get?
records.zomi: Dawr in coriander thak a nei kei leh bang ka lei ding hiam?

records.english: Get some spring onions instead, and I'll change the recipe.
records.zomi: Tua sangin lothaang hing tawmno lei inla, an huan dan ka laih ding hi.

records.english: Whoever unpacks the shopping tonight gets to choose what we have for dessert.
records.zomi: Tuni zanin lei vante a la khia peuhpeuh in an khit ciang-a an lim a teel ding hi.

records.english: Had you checked the cupboard first, would you still have bought more salt?
records.zomi: Van bawm na en masa le, cii behlap na lei lai ding hiam?

records.english: Probably not, since there turned out to be three unopened packets behind the jars.
records.zomi: Lei lo kha ding ing, bel nung ah kihong lo pakat thum a om hi, ci-in a kimu ahih manin.

records.english: Why does the shopkeeper wrap the fish in newspaper?
records.zomi: Bang hangin dawr neipa in nga laithak tawh a tuam hiam?

records.english: It soaks up the water, and she says it keeps the bag from smelling.
records.zomi: Tui a dawp a, ip a nam lo nadingin a huh hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Are we allowed to taste the grapes before we buy them?
records.zomi: I lei ma-in grape i tet thei ding hiam?

records.english: Not here — the stall owner has a sign asking customers not to touch the fruit.
records.zomi: Hih ah hi lo — zuakna mun neipa in leite theigah khoih lo dingin lai a khai hi.

records.english: What should I look for when I choose a ripe melon?
records.zomi: Melon min khat ka teel ciangin bang ka en ding hiam?

records.english: Press the end gently, and if it gives a little and smells sweet, it's ready.
records.zomi: A tawp nem takin nek inla, tawmno a kun a, a namtui a lim leh a min khin hi.

records.english: Could you use the trolley instead of carrying everything in your arms?
records.zomi: Khempeuh na ban tawh pua sangin trolley na zang thei ding hiam?

records.english: I would have, but all the trolleys were chained together outside.
records.zomi: Ka zang ding hi, ahi zongin trolley khempeuh pua ah thih khau tawh kikhih hi.

records.english: What made you change shops?
records.zomi: Bang in dawr na laihsak hiam?

records.english: The old shop kept selling us bread that was stale by the next morning.
records.zomi: Dawr lui in zingciang zingsang ciangin a lui moh hong zuak den hi.

records.english: Did you ask how much the tailor charges for a school uniform?
records.zomi: Sang puan khat adingin puan khui numei in bangzah a la hiam na dong hiam?

records.english: I did, and she'll do two for the price of one and a half.
records.zomi: Ka dong hi, khat leh a khen man in nih a bawl ding hi.

records.english: What would the carpenter charge to make a table that seats twelve?
records.zomi: Mi sawm leh nih tutna dawhkan khat bawl dingin sing seemmi in bangzah a la ding hiam?

records.english: More than a shop table, but he says it would outlast all of us.
records.zomi: Dawr dawhkan sangin a tam zaw, ahi zongin i khempeuh sangin a sau zaw ding hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Can we take photos of the price list?
records.zomi: Man list lim i la thei ding hiam?

records.english: Please don't — the owner says it changes every week and he doesn't want old prices passed around.
records.zomi: La kei un — kal simin a kilai a, man luite a kizel ding a deih kei hi, ci-in a neipa in a ci hi.

records.english: Is it rude to ask the price before you agree to have something repaired?
records.zomi: Bangmah bawl siang dingin na lungkim ma-in a man dong pen zahtakna om lo ahi hiam?

records.english: Not at all, and a good repairer would rather you asked than complained afterwards.
records.zomi: Hi lo mahmah hi, bawlsiang hoih in a khit ciangin na phun sangin na dot a deih zaw ding hi.

records.english: Are we allowed to bargain in this market?
records.zomi: Hih zuakna mun ah man kikum thei hiam?

records.english: At the fruit stalls, yes, but not in the shops with printed prices.
records.zomi: Theigah zuakna mun ah thei hi, ahi zongin man kigelh dawr ah thei lo hi.

records.english: Is the price of the rice different if I bring my own sack?
records.zomi: Keima' ip ka tawi leh buh man a kilai hiam?

records.english: Yes, it's a little cheaper, because I don't have to give you a bag.
records.zomi: Kilai hi, ip kong piak loh ding ahih manin tawmno a neem zaw hi.

records.english: Could you ask the price for me, since I don't speak the local language well yet?
records.zomi: Hih mun pau ka thei hoih nai loh manin man hong dong sak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Sure, I'll ask him and tell you in our language.
records.zomi: Thei hi, amah ka dong ding a, i pau tawh kong hilh ding hi.

records.english: How much would it be to fix the zip on this bag?
records.zomi: Hih ip-a zip bawl siang man bangzah ahi ding hiam?

records.english: Not much, but leave it with me until tomorrow.
records.zomi: Tam lo hi, ahi zongin zingciang dong ka kiang ah nusia in.

records.english: Is this the price with the frame or without it?
records.zomi: Hih man pen frame tawh ahi hiam, frame om lo-in ahi hiam?

records.english: With it, and I can wrap it for you as well.
records.zomi: Tua tawh, kong tuam sak thei zong hi.

records.english: If you buy the whole set, how much would you save?
records.zomi: Set bup na lei leh bangzah na kem thei ding hiam?

records.english: About a fifth, which is enough to pay for the extra plates.
records.zomi: A khen nga-a khat bang, kuang behlapte man piak zawh dingin a kicing hi.

records.english: How much are the mangoes today?
records.zomi: Tuni-in haigah bangzah ahi hiam?

records.english: Three for a dollar, or a whole box for ten.
records.zomi: Dollar khat ah thum, bawm khat bup sawm.

records.english: Why is the bread more expensive today?
records.zomi: Bang hangin tuni-in moh a man tam zaw hiam?

records.english: Flour went up, so the baker had to raise the price.
records.zomi: Buh-mal man a khang ahih manin moh bawl pa in a man a khangsak hi.

records.english: What does it cost to send a parcel to my brother in another country?
records.zomi: Gamdang-a ka sanggam pasal kiangah van bawm khat khak man bangzah ahi hiam?

records.english: That depends on the weight, so put it on the scale and I'll tell you.
records.zomi: A gikna tungah a kinga ahih manin gikna khaina tungah koih inla kong hilh ding hi.

records.english: What made you walk out of the furniture shop so quickly?
records.zomi: Bang in van dawr pan manlang takin na pai khiatsak hiam?

records.english: The salesman wouldn't tell me any prices until I'd given him my phone number.
records.zomi: Ka phone number ka piak ma-in a zuakpa in man khatpeuh hong gen kei hi.

records.english: Who told you the bus fare had gone up?
records.zomi: Bus man a khang hi, ci-in kua in hong hilh hiam?

records.english: The driver, when I handed him the usual coins this morning.
records.zomi: Tuni zingsangin dangka pangai ka piak ciangin mawngpa in.

records.english: How much do you want for the chickens?
records.zomi: Akte bangzah na deih hiam?

records.english: The brown ones are a little more, because they lay every day.
records.zomi: A sanlawh te tawmno a man sang zaw hi, ni simin aktui a tui uh ahih manin.
