records.english: What's the price of the blue dress in the window?
records.zomi: Tukvuang sung-a puan dum man bangzah ahi hiam?

records.english: I'm sorry, that one isn't for sale — it's only for display.
records.zomi: Hong maisak in, tua pen zuak ding hi lo hi — etsak ding bek ahi hi.

records.english: No price had been written on the jar of honey, so the boy ran to ask his mother.
records.zomi: Khuaizu bel tungah man a kigelh kei ahih manin naupang pasal in a nu dong dingin a tai hi.

records.english: What's the fare to the hospital?
records.zomi: Zato dong man bangzah ahi hiam?

records.english: For you, the usual price, and I'll wait if you need me.
records.zomi: Nang adingin, man pangai, na kisap leh kong ngak ding hi.

records.english: What did the mechanic say it would cost?
records.zomi: Set bawlpa in bangzah ahi ding hi, a ci hiam?

records.english: He said, "Somewhere between fifty and eighty, depending on the part."
records.zomi: “Sawmnga leh sawmgiat kikal, a vanzat tungah a kinga hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: What does the sign by the door say about prices?
records.zomi: Kongkhak kiang-a lai in man thu bang a ci hiam?

records.english: It says, "Prices are fixed — please do not bargain."
records.zomi: “Man kikhensat ahi hi — man kikum kei un,” a ci hi.

records.english: Rather than asking the price of every item, Grandma totals the basket in her head and pays exactly what she thinks is fair.
records.zomi: Van khat ciat man dong sangin ka pi in bawm sung-a man a lungsim sungah a kisim a, a dik a sak tan a pia hi.

records.english: Why do sellers sometimes ask visitors for double the usual price?
records.zomi: Bang hangin zuakte in khual hongte kiangah khatveivei man pangai nihvei a ngen uh hiam?

records.english: Some assume visitors won't know the local price, so it helps to ask a neighbor first.
records.zomi: Khenkhatte in khual hongte in hih mun man a thei kei ding uh a ci uh ahih manin, inn veng khat a masa-in dong leh a hoih hi.

records.english: Why are the shoes in this shop so much cheaper?
records.zomi: Bang hangin hih dawr-a khedapte a man neu mahmah hiam?

records.english: They're last year's colors, and the shop needs the space for new stock.
records.zomi: Kum nung-a rong ahi uh a, dawr in van thakte adingin mun a kisam hi.

records.english: Why aren't there any prices on these shirts?
records.zomi: Bang hangin hih angkite tungah man a om kei hiam?

records.english: The owner likes to talk to every customer first, so you have to ask him.
records.zomi: A neipa in lei hong khempeuh tawh a masa-in kiho a deih ahih manin amah na dong ding hi.

records.english: Should I trust a price that seems too good to be true?
records.zomi: A dik ding tan-a hoih lua man khat ka um ding hiam?

records.english: Hardly ever — ask what's included, and check whether the item is new or used.
records.zomi: Um ngei lo ding hi — bang a kihel hiam dong inla, van a thak hiam a lui hiam en in.

records.english: Why did the price change between the shelf and the till?
records.zomi: Bang hangin van koihna leh sum piakna mun kikal ah man a kilai hiam?

records.english: The shelf label was old, and the manager agreed to give you the lower price.
records.zomi: Van koihna tung-a min a lui a, manager in man niam zaw pen pia dingin a lungkim hi.

records.english: Why did you make the shopkeeper write the price on a piece of paper?
records.zomi: Bang hangin dawr neipa in laipek tungah man a gelhsak hiam?

records.english: Last time he quoted one price and then charged me another at the till.
records.zomi: A ma-in man khat a gen a, tua ciangin sum piakna mun ah a dang hong la hi.

records.english: How much do we owe you for looking after the house while we were away?
records.zomi: I om loh laitakin inn hong kem sak manin bangzah kong pia ding uh hiam?

records.english: Nothing at all — just bring me back some tea from the mountains.
records.zomi: Bangmah om lo — mual tung pan tea tawmno hong tawi sak bek in.

records.english: How could I find out what a fair price is for a used motorbike?
records.zomi: Motorbike zat khin khat' man dik bangci-in ka thei thei ding hiam?

records.english: Ask two or three mechanics in town and compare what they say.
records.zomi: Khuapi sung-a set bawlpa nih thum dong inla, a genna uh kikhaikhin in.

records.english: Had you known the price beforehand, would you still have ordered the lobster?
records.zomi: A ma-in a man na theih le, lobster na ngen lai ding hiam?

records.english: Never — I nearly fainted when the waiter brought the bill.
records.zomi: Ngei lo ding — an zuakpa in bill a tawi ciangin ka bawp dek hi.

records.english: Where did that coin go?
records.zomi: Tua dangka koi ah a pai hiam?

records.english: It rolled under the counter, but I'll get it out with the broom.
records.zomi: Sum piakna dawhkan nuai ah a liim hi, ahi zongin phiatna tawh ka la khia ding hi.

records.english: Who's going to collect the money for the class gift?
records.zomi: Kilasi letsong adingin sum kua in a kaikhawm ding hiam?

records.english: Thida offered, and she'll give everyone a receipt.
records.zomi: Thida in a kipia a, mi khempeuh laimal a pia ding hi.

records.english: Are customers allowed to pay with large notes at night?
records.zomi: Zan ciangin leite in sum lian tawh a pia thei uh hiam?

records.english: Not after nine, because the shop doesn't keep much change in the till.
records.zomi: Nai kua zawh ciangin thei lo hi, dawr in sum kilaih tam a kem kei ahih manin.

records.english: Is this the right change?
records.zomi: Hih sum kilaih a dik hiam?

records.english: Let me count it again — no, I owe you another fifty cents.
records.zomi: Sim kik ning — hi lo hi, cent sawmnga behlap kong pia lai ding hi.

records.english: Did the man at the gate take your money?
records.zomi: Kongpi-a pasal in na sum a la hiam?

records.english: He did, but he didn't give me a ticket.
records.zomi: A la hi, ahi zongin ticket hong pia kei hi.

records.english: The coins were counted twice, wrapped in paper, and taken to the bank before the shop closed.
records.zomi: Dawr a kikhak ma-in dangkate nihvei kisim a, lai tawh kituam a, bank ah kitawi hi.

records.english: What did the cashier say when you gave her too much?
records.zomi: Tam lua na piak ciangin sum lata in bang a ci hiam?

records.english: She said, "You're very honest — most people wouldn't have noticed."
records.zomi: “Na thuman mahmah hi — mi tamzaw in a thei kei ding uh hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: Who gave you this foreign coin?
records.zomi: Hih gamdang dangka kua in hong pia hiam?

records.english: It must have come in my change at the train station.
records.zomi: Meileng dinna ah ka sum kilaih sung ah a hong kihel kha ding hi.

records.english: Why is the card machine not working?
records.zomi: Bang hangin card set a sem kei hiam?

records.english: The connection dropped during the storm and hasn't come back yet.
records.zomi: Huihpi laitakin connection a mang a, tu dong a hong kik nai kei hi.

records.english: Did you get a receipt for the cement?
records.zomi: Cement adingin laimal na ngah hiam?

records.english: Yes, it's folded inside my wallet with the delivery note.
records.zomi: Ngah hi, ka sum ip sung ah van puakna lai tawh kituam-in a om hi.

records.english: Why do the shopkeepers in the market keep small notes in a separate tin?
records.zomi: Bang hangin zuakna mun-a dawr neite in sum neute bawm tuam ah a koih uh hiam?

records.english: So that they can give change quickly without opening the main box.
records.zomi: Bawm lian hong lo-in sum kilaih manlang taka a piak theih nadingun.

records.english: Why do you count your change before leaving the counter?
records.zomi: Bang hangin sum piakna mun na nusiat ma-in na sum kilaih na sim hiam?

records.english: Once I walked away and found I was ten short.
records.zomi: Khatvei ka pai khia a, sawm a tawm hi, ka thei hi.

records.english: What should I do if the cashier gives me the wrong change?
records.zomi: Sum lata in sum kilaih dik lo hong piak leh bang ka hih ding hiam?

records.english: Tell her politely before you leave, and count it together.
records.zomi: Na pai ma-in nem takin gen inla, khawm-in sim un.

records.english: Why does the café ask whether you'd like to round your bill up?
records.zomi: Bang hangin cafe in na bill a dim zaw-a pia nuam hiam a dong hiam?

records.english: Whatever is added goes into a fund for the children's ward, and the owner matches it every month.
records.zomi: Bangzah a behlap peuhpeuh naupangte zato khan adingin sum kholna ah a lut a, a neipa in kha simin a kibang a behlap hi.

records.english: How should children be taught to check their change?
records.zomi: Naupangte in a sum kilaih uh a en nadingun bangci-in kisinsak ding hiam?

records.english: By paying for small things themselves and counting the coins out loud with an adult nearby.
records.zomi: Van neute amau mah in a lei-in, upa khat kiang ah om-in dangkate ging sang takin a sim uh tawh.

records.english: Why did Dad make you go back to the shop?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pa in dawr ah hong kiksak hiam?

records.english: The shopkeeper had given me too much change, and Dad said we couldn't keep it.
records.zomi: Dawr neipa in sum kilaih tam lua hong pia a, Pa in i kem thei kei hi, a ci hi.

records.english: If the waiter had kept the extra money, would you have noticed?
records.zomi: An zuakpa in sum behlap a kem le, na thei ding hiam?

records.english: Only the next morning, when I tried to work out where my last twenty had gone.
records.zomi: A zing zingsang bek, ka sawmnih nunung koi ah a pai hiam ka ngaihsut ciangin.

records.english: Can I pay with this coupon and cash together?
records.zomi: Hih coupon leh sum tawh khawm-in ka pia thei ding hiam?

records.english: You can, but the coupon can't be exchanged for change.
records.zomi: Thei hi, ahi zongin coupon tawh sum kilaih kilaih thei lo hi.

records.english: Is it all right to leave the change on the table for the waiter?
records.zomi: An zuakpa adingin dawhkan tungah sum kilaih nusia a hoih hiam?

records.english: Here people usually do, so go ahead.
records.zomi: Hih ah mite in a hih tawntung uh ahih manin nusia in.

records.english: Why did the shopkeeper ask you to check the note under the light?
records.zomi: Bang hangin dawr neipa in meivak nuai ah sum en dingin hong ngen hiam?

records.english: Counterfeit notes have been turning up in town, so shops are checking every large one.
records.zomi: Khuapi ah sum zuau a kimu den ahih manin dawrte in sum lian khempeuh a en uh hi.

records.english: Can I pay for the medicine at the counter instead of the machine?
records.zomi: Set sangin sum piakna mun ah zatui man ka pia thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, and the pharmacist will explain how to take it while you pay.
records.zomi: Thei hi, na piak laitakin zatui zuakpa in bangci-in na ne ding hiam a gen siang ding hi.

records.english: Why did the seller refuse your note?
records.zomi: Bang hangin zuakpa in na sum a sang nuam kei hiam?

records.english: It was so old and soft that she thought it might be fake.
records.zomi: A lui lua a, a nem lua ahih manin a zuau kha ding in a ngaihsun hi.

records.english: Could you pay for my coffee while I find a seat for us?
records.zomi: Tutna ka zon laitakin ka khawfi man na pia sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, and you can buy the next round.
records.zomi: Thei hi, a zom ciangin nang na lei ding hi.

records.english: No sooner had I handed over the money than the bus pulled away, leaving me with a ticket but no change.
records.zomi: Sum ka piak bek in bus a pai khia a, ticket ka nei a, sum kilaih ka nei kei hi.

records.english: Can I give you the exact amount?
records.zomi: A dik tan sum kong pia thei ding hiam?

records.english: That would help, because I'm almost out of small coins.
records.zomi: Tua in a huh ding hi, dangka neu ka bei dek ahih manin.

records.english: Is it possible to pay for the next three lessons now?
records.zomi: A zom hilhna thum man tu-in ka pia thei ding hiam?

records.english: Certainly, and I'll write it in your booklet so neither of us forgets.
records.zomi: Thei mahmah hi, i nih un i mangngilh loh nadingin na laibu neu ah ka gelh ding hi.

records.english: Why did the price come to so much?
records.zomi: Bang hangin man a tam mahmah hiam?

records.english: The machine charged you twice for the bananas.
records.zomi: Set in nahtang man nihvei a la hi.

records.english: Did the parking machine give you any change?
records.zomi: Mawtaw koihna set in sum kilaih hong pia hiam?

records.english: No, it only takes coins and doesn't give change at all.
records.zomi: Pia lo hi, dangka bek a sang a, sum kilaih a pia ngei kei hi.

records.english: What would you say to a seller who refuses to give change for a large note?
records.zomi: Sum lian adingin sum kilaih pia nuam lo zuak khat kiangah bang na ci ding hiam?

records.english: I'd ask whether a neighboring stall could break it, rather than buy something I don't need.
records.zomi: Ka kisap loh bangmah lei sangin a kiang zuakna mun in a khen thei hiam ka dong ding hi.

records.english: What happened to the money in your pocket?
records.zomi: Na ip sung-a sum bang a piang hiam?

records.english: It went through the washing machine, so now it's drying on the radiator.
records.zomi: Puan silna set sung ah a lut a, tu-in mei lumna tungah a khang hi.

records.english: How do you feel when someone counts their change slowly in front of you?
records.zomi: Na mai ah kuamah in a sum kilaih zawl taka a sim ciangin bangci-in na kisa hiam?

records.english: A little impatient, though I'd rather they took their time than walked off short.
records.zomi: Tawmno ka thuak zo kei hi, a tawm-in a pai khiat sangin a hun uh a lak uh ka deih zaw hangin.

records.english: What would you do if the shop simply refused to help?
records.zomi: Dawr in huh nuam lo leh bang na hih ding hiam?

records.english: I'd write down the date and the name of the person I spoke to, and then ask for the manager.
records.zomi: Ni leh ka kihopih pa' min ka gelh ding a, tua ciangin manager ka ngen ding hi.

records.english: Can I bring the shoes back if my daughter doesn't like the color?
records.zomi: Ka tanu in a rong a deih kei leh khedap ka tawi kik thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, as long as she hasn't worn them outside.
records.zomi: Thei hi, pua ah a bulh khin kei leh.

records.english: The returned clothes are checked, folded, and put back on the rails before the shop opens.
records.zomi: Dawr a kihon ma-in a kitawi kik puante kien a, kituam a, a koihna ah kikoih kik hi.

records.english: Why are you so angry with the furniture shop?
records.zomi: Bang hangin inn van dawr tungah na heh mahmah hiam?

records.english: They delivered a chair with a broken leg and then said it must have happened in our house.
records.zomi: Khe kek nei tutna khat a puak uh a, tua ciangin i inn ah a piang hi, a ci uh hi.

records.english: Why is the kettle back in its box?
records.zomi: Bang hangin tui suangna a bawm sung ah a om kik hiam?

records.english: It started leaking on the first day, so I'm taking it back.
records.zomi: Ni masa pen-in a zu kipan ahih manin ka tawi kik ding hi.

records.english: Where should I take a faulty phone that I bought online?
records.zomi: Online-a ka lei phone sia koi ah ka tawi ding hiam?

records.english: Check the seller's page first, because some sellers want you to post it rather than take it to a shop.
records.zomi: A zuakpa' page a masa-in en in, zuakpa khenkhatte in dawr ah tawi sangin na khak a deih zaw uh ahih manin.

records.english: What did you do with the wrong charger they sent?
records.zomi: A hong khak charger dik lo bang na hih hiam?

records.english: I sent it back in the same envelope, and they're posting the right one.
records.zomi: Lai ip kibang mah sung ah ka khak kik a, a dik pen a khak ding uh hi.

records.english: Why do you think so many people never bother returning things?
records.zomi: Bang hangin mi tampi in van a tawi kik ngei lo uh in na ngaihsun hiam?

records.english: Most people would rather lose a little money than spend an afternoon queuing and explaining.
records.zomi: Mi tamzaw in nitak lam khat a kikhai-in gen siang sangin sum tawmno mansuah a deih zaw uh hi.

records.english: Could you take this back for me, since I've had to change my plans?
records.zomi: Ka gelna ka laih ding ahih manin hih hong tawi kik sak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: No problem — I go past that shop every day on my way to work.
records.zomi: Bangmah om lo — ni simin nasepna ka pai lampi ah tua dawr ka pai khak hi.

records.english: Should I return the blender or just ask for a new blade?
records.zomi: Blender ka tawi kik ding hiam, namsau thak khat bek ka ngen ding hiam?

records.english: Ask for a new blade first, because the motor still works perfectly.
records.zomi: Namsau thak a masa-in ngen in, a set a sem hoih lai ahih manin.

records.english: What did the manager say about the torn jacket?
records.zomi: Kawt kek thu-ah manager in bang a ci hiam?

records.english: He said, "Bring it in this week and we'll replace it."
records.zomi: “Hih kal sungin tawi inla, i lai sak ding hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: If you'd tested the radio in the shop, would you have noticed the crackle?
records.zomi: Dawr sung ah radio na et le, a ging kek na thei ding hiam?

records.english: I doubt it, because the shop was so noisy that I could barely hear anything.
records.zomi: Ka um kei hi, dawr a ging lua ahih manin bangmah ka za thei dek kei hi.

records.english: Should you have checked the parcel before signing for it?
records.zomi: Na min na suaksak ma-in van bawm na en masa ding hi hiam?

records.english: Yes, because once I'd signed, the courier said the damage was no longer his responsibility.
records.zomi: Hi hi, min ka suaksak khit ciangin a siatna pen amah mawh hi nawn lo hi, ci-in a puakpa in a ci hi.

records.english: Did the shop give you your money back?
records.zomi: Dawr in na sum hong pia kik hiam?

records.english: Only half, because I'd lost the receipt.
records.zomi: A khen khat bek, laimal ka mansuah ahih manin.

records.english: Who told you the sale items couldn't be returned?
records.zomi: Man kiam vante kitawi kik thei lo hi, ci-in kua in hong hilh hiam?

records.english: There's a notice above the till that says, "No refunds on reduced items."
records.zomi: Sum piakna mun tungah “Man kiam vante adingin sum pia kik lo hi,” ci lai khat a om hi.

records.english: Is it fair for a shop to charge a fee when someone returns a large item?
records.zomi: Kuamah in van lian khat a tawi kik ciangin dawr in man a lak pen a dik hiam?

records.english: It depends on whether the item was faulty, in which case the shop should cover the cost.
records.zomi: Van a sia hiam cih tungah a kinga a, a sia leh dawr in a man a pia ding hi.

records.english: Is the rice cooker still under guarantee?
records.zomi: Buh huanna set guarantee nuai ah a om lai hiam?

records.english: It is, for another three months, so they'll have to repair it for free.
records.zomi: Om lai hi, kha thum behlap, tua ahih manin a man om lo-in a bawl siang ding uh hi.

records.english: Having been told twice that the manager was away, Hau finally wrote a letter and left it at the counter.
records.zomi: Manager a om kei hi, ci-in nihvei a kihilh khit ciangin Hau in a tawp-in lai a gelh a, sum piakna mun ah a nusia hi.

records.english: Why did the shop refuse to take the dress back?
records.zomi: Bang hangin dawr in puan a sang kik nuam kei hiam?

records.english: The label had been cut off, and they said it looked worn.
records.zomi: A min a kitan khin a, a lui bang hi, a ci uh hi.

records.english: When did the zip break?
records.zomi: Bang ciangin zip a sia hiam?

records.english: The second time I wore the trousers, just as I sat down.
records.zomi: Nihvei veina ka bulh ciangin, ka tut laitakin.

records.english: Why didn't you complain about the cold soup?
records.zomi: Bang hangin an tui vot thu na phun kei hiam?

records.english: The waiter was so busy that I didn't want to make his day worse.
records.zomi: An zuakpa a buai lua ahih manin a ni ka hoih losak nuam kei hi.

records.english: How long will the refund take to reach my account?
records.zomi: Sum pia kik ka account ah a tun dingin bangzah sawt ding hiam?

records.english: Usually about five working days, but sometimes a little longer.
records.zomi: A tamzaw-in nasep ni nga bang, ahi zongin khatveivei tawmno a sau zaw hi.

records.english: Are we allowed to return food that was bought on special offer?
records.zomi: Man kiam-a lei an i tawi kik thei ding hiam?

records.english: Only if it was spoiled when you bought it, according to the shop's rules.
records.zomi: Na lei laitakin a sia khin leh bek, dawr' thupiak bangin.

records.english: What happened to the bicycle you bought last week?
records.zomi: Kal nung-a na lei siiksakol bang a piang hiam?

records.english: The chain snapped on the hill, and I nearly fell off.
records.zomi: Mual tung ah a khau a tan a, ka kia dek hi.

records.english: What should I say if they ask why I'm returning it?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na tawi kik hiam a dot leh bang ka ci ding hiam?

records.english: Just tell them it doesn't fit, which is true.
records.zomi: Ka kituak kei hi, ci bek in, tua pen a tak ahi hi.

records.english: Which shop did you buy the cracked plates from?
records.zomi: Kuang kek te koi dawr pan na lei hiam?

records.english: The one on the corner, but they've already promised to swap them.
records.zomi: Lampi kiheina-a dawr, ahi zongin a laih sak dingin a kiciam khin uh hi.

records.english: Was anything else damaged when the box was dropped?
records.zomi: Bawm a kiat ciangin bangmah dang a sia hiam?

records.english: Two of the glasses were broken, but the jug survived.
records.zomi: Glass nih a kek hi, ahi zongin tui bel a dam hi.

records.english: Why is Grandpa going back to the hardware shop again?
records.zomi: Bang hangin ka pu thih van dawr ah a pai kik hiam?

records.english: The paint was mixed in the wrong color, and he wants it done properly.
records.zomi: Zeek pen rong dik lo-in kihel ahih manin dik takin a bawl sak ding a deih hi.

records.english: Why did the shop make you fill in a form?
records.zomi: Bang hangin dawr in form hong gelhsak hiam?

records.english: They need it so that the factory can see what went wrong with the heater.
records.zomi: Mei lumna set bang a sia hiam factory in a muh theih nadingin a kisam uh hi.

records.english: Why can't I return these earphones?
records.zomi: Bang hangin hih earphone ka tawi kik thei kei hiam?

records.english: For hygiene reasons, the shop doesn't take back earphones once they've been opened.
records.zomi: Siangtho thu hangin, dawr in a kihong khin earphone a sang kik kei hi.

records.english: How did the shop treat you when you brought the broken lamp back?
records.zomi: Meivak sia na tawi kik ciangin dawr in bangci-in hong dawng hiam?

records.english: Better than I'd expected — they apologized, replaced it, and gave me a discount on my next visit.
records.zomi: Ka ngaihsut sangin a hoih zaw — maisak a ngen uh a, a lai sak uh a, ka hong zom ciang adingin man hong kiamsak uh hi.

records.english: Do any of your relatives still live in the hills, or have they all moved to town?
records.zomi: Na sanggam khenkhatte mual tung ah a om lai uh hiam, a vekpi un khuapi ah a tuah khin uh hiam?

records.english: The more relatives come to stay, the more rice my mother has to cook, but she never complains.
records.zomi: Sanggam tam zaw hong om ciangin ka nu in buh tam zaw a huan ding a, ahi zongin a phun ngei kei hi.

records.english: Rather than divide the land among the brothers, my grandfather left it to all of them to farm together.
records.zomi: Leitang sanggam pasalte lak ah khen sangin ka pu in khawm-a a lo bawl dingin amaute khempeuh a nusia hi.

records.english: At family gatherings, the older relatives sit down and eat first.
records.zomi: Innkuan kikhopna ah sanggam upate a tu-in a ne masa uh hi.

records.english: My brother-in-law fixed our roof with tools he borrowed from his father.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu' pasal in a pa pan a ngetsak nasepna vante tawh i innkhum a bawl siang hi.

records.english: Could you ask your aunt whether she remembers the day you were born?
records.zomi: Na suak ni a phawk lai hiam na ni na dong thei ding hiam?

records.english: How do you and your brothers share the work of looking after your elderly parents?
records.zomi: Nang leh na sanggam pasalte in na nu leh na pa upate kemna nasep bangci-in na kihawm uh hiam?

records.english: My sister carefully keeps the shawl that our grandmother wove for her wedding.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu in i pi in a mopawi adingin a tah puan pilvang takin a kem hi.

records.english: What I admire most about my grandmother is how she remembers every relative's birthday without writing anything down.
records.zomi: Ka pi tungah ka lamdang sak pen pen bangmah gelh lo-in sanggam khempeuh' pianni a phawk thei hi, cih ahi hi.

records.english: Our house was damaged by the storm, so my uncles came to rebuild it.
records.zomi: Huihpi in i inn a susia ahih manin ka pa neute in a lam kik dingin a hong uh hi.

records.english: Shall we take some of the new rice to your mother's older brother when we visit him?
records.zomi: Na nu' u pasal i veh ciangin buh thak tawmno i tawi ding hiam?

records.english: My little brother was scolded for not greeting our uncle properly.
records.zomi: Ka nau pasal i pa neu hoih takin a hopih loh manin kihau hi.

records.english: Whenever someone in the clan is getting married, all the relatives help with the cooking.
records.zomi: Phung sung-a kuamah a kiteen ciangin sanggam khempeuh in an huan a huh uh hi.

records.english: How many brothers and sisters do you have?
records.zomi: Sanggam pasal leh sanggam nu bangzah na nei hiam?

records.english: Whoever marries into our family is treated as a son or daughter, not as a guest.
records.zomi: I innkuan ah a kiteen peuhpeuh khual bangin hi lo-in tapa hiam tanu bangin kizang hi.

records.english: My cousin and I grew up in the same village, so we are almost like sisters.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam leh kei khua khat mah ah i khang ahih manin sanggam nu taktak bang dek i hi hi.

records.english: Had my uncle not paid my school fees, I would never have finished secondary school.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in ka sang man a pia kei le, sang lian ka zo ngei kei ding hi.

records.english: My father carved this wooden spoon for my mother when they were first married.
records.zomi: Ka pa in a kiteen thak lai uh-in ka nu adingin hih sing kawm a ki hi.

records.english: My grandparents live with us, and my grandmother cooks every evening.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh pite i kiang ah a om uh a, ka pi in nitak simin an a huan hi.

records.english: Everyone, please write your names in the family book before you leave tonight.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, tuni zanin na pai ma-un innkuan laibu ah na min uh gelh un.

records.english: I was raised mostly by my grandparents while my parents worked in the fields.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa lo ah a nasep laitakun ka pu leh pite in a tamzaw-in hong khoi uh hi.

records.english: In our family, the youngest son usually stays in the parents' house and looks after them.
records.zomi: I innkuan ah tapa neu pen in a tamzaw-in nu leh pa' inn ah a om a, amaute a kem hi.

records.english: Our aunts may come for the whole week if the harvest finishes early.
records.zomi: Buh lak a man masak leh i nite kal bup a hong kha ding uh hi.

records.english: Although our family is spread across three countries, we still feel connected through our weekly video calls.
records.zomi: I innkuan gam thum ah a kizel hangin kal simin video tawh i kisam ahih manin i kizom lai hi.

records.english: Whose turn might it be to host the family meal this year?
records.zomi: Tu kum innkuan an adingin kua' hun ahi kha ding hiam?

records.english: When my grandfather speaks at family meetings, everyone listens.
records.zomi: Innkuan kikhopna ah ka pu a gen ciangin mi khempeuh in a ngai uh hi.

records.english: Families in my village who lost relatives during hard times often raised their nieces and nephews as their own children.
records.zomi: Hun haksa sungin sanggam a mansuah ka khua-a innkuante in a tanau leh tunute a tate uh bangin a khoi uh hi.

records.english: When my parents argued, my grandmother was the one who brought them back together.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa a kinial ciangun ka pi in a kilemsak kik hi.

records.english: My grandfather keeps a notebook with the names of five generations of our family.
records.zomi: Ka pu in i innkuan khang nga' min a gelhna laibu neu khat a kem hi.

records.english: In my family, a newborn baby is given its name at a small meal with the relatives.
records.zomi: Ka innkuan ah naungek suak thak pen sanggamte tawh an neu khat ah min kiphuak hi.

records.english: Respect for older relatives, which my parents taught us from a very young age, shapes how we speak at every family gathering.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in a neu mahmah lai pan hong hilh uh sanggam upate zahtakna in innkuan kikhopna khempeuh ah i kihona a bawl hi.

records.english: If you need help with the wedding, my cousins could come from the next village.
records.zomi: Mopawi adingin huhna na kisap leh ka sanggamte a kiang khua pan a hong thei uh hi.

records.english: Does your family name come from your father's side or your mother's?
records.zomi: Na innkuan min na pa lam pan hiam, na nu lam pan hiam a hong hiam?

records.english: Remember to bring a gift for your grandparents when we go to their house at New Year.
records.zomi: Kum thak ciangin na pu leh pite inn i pai ciangin amaute adingin letsong tawi ding phawk in.

records.english: Having grown up surrounded by cousins, my son finds the quiet of the city strange.
records.zomi: Sanggam tampi kim ah a khan ahih manin ka tapa in khuapi daihna a lamdang sa hi.

records.english: Do you know how you are related to the family next door?
records.zomi: Inn veng innkuan tawh bangci-in na kizom uh hiam na thei hiam?

records.english: I do know — our grandfathers were brothers.
records.zomi: Ka thei hi — i pute sanggam pasal ahi uh hi.

records.english: Not until I had children of my own did I understand why my mother worried about us so much.
records.zomi: Keima' ta ka neih ciang bek ka nu in bang hangin hong lungkhamsak mahmah hiam ka thei hi.

records.english: Try not to interrupt when your great-grandmother is telling a story about the old days.
records.zomi: Na pi' nu in hun lui tangthu a gen ciangin a gen kikal ah gen kei in.

records.english: My aunt teaches the girls in our family to weave on the old loom in her house.
records.zomi: Ka ni in i innkuan-a numei naupangte a inn-a puan tahna lui tungah tah dan a hilh hi.

records.english: Who is the first person you call when you have good news?
records.zomi: Thu hoih na neih ciangin na sam masa pen kua ahi hiam?

records.english: My nephew was named after my father, who died before he was born.
records.zomi: Ka tanau a suak ma-a a si ka pa' min tawh kiphuak hi.

records.english: Would you like to see the photo of my whole family?
records.zomi: Ka innkuan bup' lim na muh nuam hiam?

records.english: I do want my children to know the names of all their relatives.
records.zomi: Ka tate in a sanggam khempeuh' min a theih ding uh ka deih mahmah hi.

records.english: Children, come and greet your great-aunt before you go out to play.
records.zomi: Naupangte, kimawl dingin na pai khiat ma-un na pi neu hong hopih un.

records.english: Which side of the family is your grandmother from?
records.zomi: Na pi innkuan koi lam pan ahi hiam?

records.english: She's from my father's side, and her village is two days' walk from ours.
records.zomi: Ka pa lam pan ahi a, a khua ei khua pan ni nih kalsuan gamla ahi hi.

records.english: My grandfather walked to the village on foot.
records.zomi: Ka pu in khua ah a khe tawh a pai hi.

records.english: He carried a bag of rice on his back for his sister's family.
records.zomi: A sanggam nu' innkuan adingin a nung ah buh ip khat a pua hi.

records.english: When he arrived, his sister cried with joy and killed a chicken for dinner.
records.zomi: A tun ciangin a sanggam nu in lungdam kap a kap a, nitak an adingin ak khat a go hi.

records.english: We call all of our father's older brothers by the same respectful word.
records.zomi: I pa' u pasal khempeuh zahtakna kammal kibang tawh i sam hi.

records.english: My sister's husband is from another clan, and his family has welcomed her warmly.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu' pasal phung dang pan ahi a, a innkuan in lungsim lum takin a muak uh hi.

records.english: My mother still sends money to her brother's children, even though they are adults now.
records.zomi: Ka nu in a sanggam pasal' tate upa a hih khit uh hangin sum a khak lai hi.

records.english: Is your father the eldest of his brothers?
records.zomi: Na pa a sanggam pasalte lak ah a upa pen ahi hiam?

records.english: No, he's the third, but he's the one everybody comes to for advice.
records.zomi: Hi lo hi, a thumna ahi a, ahi zongin mi khempeuh thuhilhna ngen dingin a kiang ah a hong uh hi.

records.english: My father says that a family is like a basket, because each strand holds the others in place.
records.zomi: Innkuan pen bawm bang ahi hi, a khau khat ciat in a dangte a len hi, ci-in ka pa in a ci hi.

records.english: Last year my older sister moved to the city, and now we talk on the phone every Sunday.
records.zomi: Kum nung in ka u nu khuapi ah a tuah a, tu-in Nipini simin phone tawh i kiho hi.

records.english: Our family has its own way of choosing who speaks first at a funeral.
records.zomi: I innkuan in mithi vuina ah kua in a gen masa ding hiam teelna ngeina tuam a nei hi.

records.english: Why do your parents keep the old family photos in a tin box under their bed?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na nu leh na pa in innkuan lim luite a lupna nuai-a thih bawm sung ah a kem uh hiam?

records.english: Kinship matters so much in our village that a stranger is usually asked who his family is before anything else.
records.zomi: I khua ah sanggam kizopna a thupi lua ahih manin mi theih loh khat a innkuan kua ahi hiam bangmah ma-in kidong den hi.

records.english: What did the bank manager tell you?
records.zomi: Bank makaipa in bang hong hilh hiam?

records.english: She said, "Pay the most expensive debt first and don't take on any new ones."
records.zomi: “Leiba man tam pen a masa-in pia inla, a thak la nawn kei in,” a ci hi.

records.english: How did the washing machine break?
records.zomi: Puan silna set bangci-in a sia hiam?

records.english: Nobody broke it — it just stopped in the middle of a wash.
records.zomi: Kuamah in a susia kei hi — puan a sil laitakin a tawp bek hi.

records.english: Where did all the money go this month?
records.zomi: Hih kha sungin sum khempeuh koi ah a pai hiam?

records.english: Mostly on the car, after the tire burst on the way to work.
records.zomi: A tamzaw mawtaw ah, nasepna pai lampi ah tire a puak khit ciangin.

records.english: Why did the price of the bus pass go up?
records.zomi: Bang hangin bus pass man a khang hiam?

records.english: The fuel costs rose, so the bus company raised its prices in January.
records.zomi: Datsi man a khang ahih manin January ah bus company in a man a khangsak hi.

records.english: Why did you write every expense in that little notebook?
records.zomi: Bang hangin sum zatna khempeuh tua laibu neu ah na gelh hiam?

records.english: I wanted to see exactly where our money was going.
records.zomi: I sum koi ah a pai hiam kician takin muh ka deih hi.

records.english: Do you pay the rent before anything else?
records.zomi: Bangmah dang ma-in inn man na pia masa hiam?

records.english: Always, because without a roof nothing else matters.
records.zomi: Tawntungin, innkhum om lo-in bangmah dang a thupi kei ahih manin.

records.english: What's the first thing you do when your salary arrives?
records.zomi: Na nasep man a tun ciangin bang na hih masa hiam?

records.english: I move some into savings before I can spend it.
records.zomi: Ka zat ma-in khenkhat sum khol ah ka koih hi.

records.english: Did the electricity company really cut you off?
records.zomi: Meivak company in na meivak a tan taktak hiam?

records.english: They did, after three warning letters that went to our old address.
records.zomi: A tan hi, i omna lui ah a pai lai thum a khak khit uh ciangin.

records.english: Last spring our savings were wiped out when my father was taken to hospital.
records.zomi: Kum nung spring in ka pa zato ah a kipuak ciangin i sum khol a bei kim hi.

records.english: Since then we've put a little aside every week, and this year we finally have enough for an emergency.
records.zomi: Tua pan kal simin tawmno i koih a, tu kum ciangin a tawp-in lauhuaina hun adingin a kicing i nei hi.

records.english: Who made you start keeping a budget?
records.zomi: Budget kem dingin kua in hong kipatsak hiam?

records.english: My grandmother, who has never once been in debt.
records.zomi: Ka pi, leiba khatvei zong a nei ngei lo pa.

records.english: Are we allowed to use the emergency money for a holiday?
records.zomi: Lauhuaina sum nopsakna khualzinna adingin i zang thei ding hiam?

records.english: No, that jar is only for illness or repairs, and we agreed on that.
records.zomi: Thei lo hi, tua bel pen natna hiam bawlsiang adingin bek ahi a, tua i kithukim khin hi.

records.english: Why is the heating off?
records.zomi: Bang hangin mei lumna a kikhek hiam?

records.english: The bill was much higher last winter, so we're only using it in the evenings.
records.zomi: Kum nung khuavot in a man a tam lua ahih manin nitak lam bek ah i zang hi.

records.english: How much should I give you for my share of the electricity?
records.zomi: Meivak man adingin ka khen bangzah kong pia ding hiam?

records.english: About a third, since there are three of us in the flat.
records.zomi: A khen thum-a khat bang, inn ah mi thum i hih manin.

records.english: What do you think is the hardest part of planning a budget together?
records.zomi: Khawm-a budget gel ah a haksa pen bang ahi in na ngaihsun hiam?

records.english: Agreeing on what counts as a necessity, since my husband thinks football tickets are essential.
records.zomi: Bang a kisap taktak hiam kithukim, ka pasal in football ticket a kisam taktak hi a ci ahih manin.

records.english: Did your parents ever talk to you about money?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa in sum thu hong gen ngei uh hiam?

records.english: Rarely, which is why I make a point of talking to my own children about it.
records.zomi: Gen ngei tawm hi, tua ahih manin keima' tate kiangah ka gen tawntung hi.

records.english: What should we cut first if money gets tight?
records.zomi: Sum a haksat ciangin bang i tan masa ding uh hiam?

records.english: Eating out, and then the second phone plan.
records.zomi: Pua-a an nek, tua ciangin phone plan nihna.

records.english: Why did you have the car serviced when money is so short?
records.zomi: Bang hangin sum a tawm lua laitakin mawtaw na en sak hiam?

records.english: A small repair now is cheaper than a breakdown on the motorway later.
records.zomi: Tu-a bawlsiang neu khat pen a nung ciangin lampi lian tungah a sia sangin a neem zaw hi.

records.english: Had you planned for the car repairs, would this month have been easier?
records.zomi: Mawtaw bawlsiang adingin na gel le, hih kha a baih zaw ding hiam?

records.english: Much easier, because we wouldn't have had to borrow from my brother.
records.zomi: Baih zaw mahmah ding hi, ka sanggam pasal pan i ngetsak kei ding ahih manin.

records.english: Is there any money left over for Christmas presents?
records.zomi: Christmas letsong adingin sum a om lai hiam?

records.english: Enough for one small gift each, if we start saving now.
records.zomi: Tu-a i khol kipat leh mi khat ciat adingin letsong neu khat a kicing hi.

records.english: What would you do with an unexpected bonus?
records.zomi: A theih loh bonus khat na ngah leh bang na hih ding hiam?

records.english: Half would go towards the loan, and the rest would pay for a weekend away we've postponed for years.
records.zomi: A khen khat leiba piak ding ah a pai ding a, a dang pen kum tampi i sawnsawn kal tawp khualzinna man ah a pai ding hi.

records.english: How do you stick to a budget when the children keep asking for things?
records.zomi: Naupangte in bangbang a ngen den laitakin budget bangci-in na zui hiam?

records.english: By explaining what we're saving for, so that saying no feels like a choice rather than a punishment.
records.zomi: Bang adingin i khol hiam gen siang-in, “Hi lo” cih pen gawtna hi lo-in teelna bangin a kisak theih nadingin.

records.english: How much do we spend on snacks without noticing?
records.zomi: Theih lo-in an neu adingin bangzah i zang hiam?

records.english: More than on electricity, according to the receipts I've kept since March.
records.zomi: March pan ka kem laimalte bangin meivak sangin a tam zaw hi.

records.english: Why is your sister living with your parents again?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na sanggam nu na nu leh na pa kiang ah a om kik hiam?

records.english: Her rent was raised twice in a year, and she couldn't keep up with it.
records.zomi: Kum khat sungin a inn man nihvei a khang a, a pia zo kei hi.

records.english: What did the advice worker say about our credit card?
records.zomi: I credit card thu-ah thuhilhna nasem in bang a ci hiam?

records.english: She told us to cut it up and pay the balance off in small amounts.
records.zomi: Tat dingin, a leiba tawmno tawmno-in pia dingin hong hilh hi.

records.english: Why do so many families find January so difficult?
records.zomi: Bang hangin innkuan tampi in January a haksa sa uh hiam?

records.english: The bills from the holidays all arrive at once, just when the winter heating costs are highest.
records.zomi: Nopsakna hun-a bill te khatvei-in a hong tung a, khuavot mei lumna man a sang pen hun mah ah.

records.english: Why can't I buy those trainers this month?
records.zomi: Bang hangin hih kha sungin tua khedapte ka lei thei kei hiam?

records.english: The school trip has to be paid for first, and we can't do both.
records.zomi: Sang khualzinna man a masa-in a kipia ding a, a nih i pia zo kei hi.

records.english: How would our budget change if we moved closer to my work?
records.zomi: Ka nasepna kiang zaw ah i tuah leh i budget bangci-in a kilai ding hiam?

records.english: The rent would be higher, but we'd save almost as much on the daily bus fares.
records.zomi: Inn man a sang zaw ding a, ahi zongin ni sim bus man ah a kibang dek i kem thei ding hi.

records.english: Should we pay someone to fix it or try to repair it ourselves?
records.zomi: Bawl siang dingin kuamah i sawl ding hiam, eimah in i bawl siang ding hiam?

records.english: Let's get a quote first, and then decide whether it's worth replacing.
records.zomi: A man a masa-in dong ni, tua ciangin a lai manphat hiam i khensat ding hi.

records.english: What happened to the money we put aside for the wedding?
records.zomi: Mopawi adingin i koih sum bang a piang hiam?

records.english: Some of it was used when the roof was damaged in the storm.
records.zomi: Huihpi in innkhum a susiat ciangin a khen khat kizang hi.

records.english: Can the children have pocket money this year?
records.zomi: Tu kum naupangte in a zat ding sum a ngah thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: A little, if they help with the chores and save half of it.
records.zomi: Tawmno, inn nasep a huh uh a, a khen khat a khol uh leh.

records.english: Did the welcome evening help you meet people?
records.zomi: Muakna nitak in mite na theihna hong huh hiam?

records.english: It did, and three of us now walk home together every Friday.
records.zomi: Huh hi, tu-in i thum un Laithai ni simin inn ah khawm-in i ciah hi.

records.english: What brought the two of you together?
records.zomi: Bang in note nih hong kikholhsak hiam?

records.english: It started when we were put in the same group for a school project.
records.zomi: Sang project khat adingin pawl khat mah ah hong koih uh ciangin a kipan hi.

records.english: Why did your father insist on inviting the new family to dinner?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na pa in innkuan thak nitak an ah sam dingin a ngen den hiam?

records.english: When we arrived in this country, someone did the same for us, and he has never forgotten it.
records.zomi: Hih gam i tun ciangin kuamah in tua bangin hong bawl a, a mangngilh ngei kei hi.

records.english: Why is it easier for children to make friends than for adults?
records.zomi: Bang hangin upate sangin naupangte in lawm a bawl baih zaw uh hiam?

records.english: Children don't worry about being rejected, so they simply walk up and ask to play.
records.zomi: Naupangte in nawlkhinna a lau kei uh ahih manin a pai-in kimawl dingin a ngen bek uh hi.

records.english: Why don't you text the friend you met at the wedding?
records.zomi: Bang hangin mopawi ah na theih lawm thu na khak kei hiam?

records.english: I lost her number when my phone was stolen, and now I can't find her.
records.zomi: Ka phone a kiguk ciangin a number ka mansuah a, tu-in ka mu thei kei hi.

records.english: How do you keep a new friendship going when you're both so busy?
records.zomi: Na nih un na buai lua uh ciangin lawmta thak bangci-in na kem hiam?

records.english: We've agreed to have breakfast together once a month, whatever else is happening.
records.zomi: Bangbang a piang zongin kha khat ah khatvei zingsang an khawm-in ne dingin i kithukim hi.

records.english: Are you still friends with the boys you grew up with?
records.zomi: Na khan khawm naupang pasalte tawh na kilawm lai hiam?

records.english: With two of them, and we still meet every year when I go home for the holidays.
records.zomi: A nih tawh, nopsakna hun-a inn ka ciah ciangin kum simin i kimu lai hi.

records.english: Are we allowed to bring friends to the swimming pool?
records.zomi: Tui kidiahna mun ah lawmte i paipih thei ding hiam?

records.english: Not on weekdays, but on Saturdays each member can bring one guest.
records.zomi: Kal sung ni ah thei lo hi, ahi zongin Kiginni-in member khat ciat in khual khat a paipih thei hi.

records.english: Who is the boy you were laughing with at the bus stop?
records.zomi: Bus dinna ah na nuih khawm naupang pasal kua ahi hiam?

records.english: That's Tuan, from my new class, and he lives on our street.
records.zomi: Tua pen Tuan, ka kilasi thak pan, i lampi ah a om hi.

records.english: Do you remember the day we first met?
records.zomi: I kimuh masak ni na phawk hiam?

records.english: Of all days, it was the day I locked myself out and you lent me your phone.
records.zomi: Ni khempeuh lak ah, keima' inn pua ah ka kikhak a, na phone hong zang sak ni ahi hi.

records.english: Why are you so happy today?
records.zomi: Bang hangin tuni-in na lungdam mahmah hiam?

records.english: Someone at work asked me to join them for lunch, and they were really kind.
records.zomi: Nasepna ah kuamah in sun an khawm ne dingin hong sam a, a hehpih mahmah uh hi.

records.english: Where do you find people to talk to in a new city?
records.zomi: Khuapi thak khat ah kiho dingin mite koi ah na mu hiam?

records.english: At the market, at church, and on the long bench outside the library.
records.zomi: Zuakna mun ah, pawlpi ah, leh laibu inn pua-a tutna sau tungah.

records.english: Why did you sit alone at lunch?
records.zomi: Bang hangin sun an ah nangma bek na tu hiam?

records.english: I didn't know anyone, and every table seemed to be full already.
records.zomi: Kuamah ka thei kei a, dawhkan khempeuh a dim khin bang hi.

records.english: What happened at the party that made you leave early?
records.zomi: Pawi ah bang a piang a, manlang takin na pai khiat hiam?

records.english: Nothing bad, but I didn't know anyone and the music was too loud to talk.
records.zomi: Bangmah hoih lo om lo hi, ahi zongin kuamah ka thei kei a, la ging a sang lua ahih manin kiho thei lo hi.

records.english: How did you and Pau get talking?
records.zomi: Nang leh Pau bangci-in na kiho kipan uh hiam?

records.english: Our dogs started playing together in the park, and we just stood there chatting.
records.zomi: Huan lian ah i uite khawm-in a kimawl kipan uh a, i ding-in i kiho bek hi.

records.english: Is it strange to want new friends at my age?
records.zomi: Ka kum ah lawm thak deih pen a lamdang hiam?

records.english: Not at all — my grandmother made her best friend when she was seventy-five.
records.zomi: Lamdang lo mahmah hi — ka pi in kum sawmsagih leh nga a phak ciangin a lawm hoih pen a mu hi.

records.english: What did the new neighbor say when you took her the cake?
records.zomi: Cake na tawi sak ciangin inn veng thak in bang a ci hiam?

records.english: She said, "You're the first person here who's knocked on my door."
records.zomi: “Hih mun ah ka kongkhak a kiu masa pen mi na hi hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: Should I accept a friend request from someone I've met only once?
records.zomi: Khatvei bek ka muh ngei mi khat pan friend request ka sang ding hiam?

records.english: Only if you'd be happy to talk to them in person, which is a good test for most things online.
records.zomi: A mai-in kiho dingin na lungdam leh bek, tua pen online thu tamzaw adingin etna hoih ahi hi.

records.english: Can I tell the new boy that he can play with us?
records.zomi: Naupang pasal thak i kiang ah a kimawl thei hi, ci-in ka hilh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, and show him where we keep the ball.
records.zomi: Thei hi, koi ah bawlung i koih hiam etsak in.

records.english: What should I say to someone I'd like to get to know?
records.zomi: Ka theih nuam mi khat kiangah bang ka ci ding hiam?

records.english: Ask them a question about themselves, and then really listen to the answer.
records.zomi: Amaute' thu dotna khat dong inla, a dawnna taktak in ngai in.

records.english: Why did you and Lun stop being friends?
records.zomi: Bang hangin nang leh Lun na kilawm nawn kei uh hiam?

records.english: We didn't fall out — we just drifted apart after she moved to the coast.
records.zomi: I kinial kei hi — tuipi gei a tuah khit ciangin zawl takin i kigamla bek hi.

records.english: Is it hard to make friends when you're shy?
records.zomi: Na zak ciangin lawm bawl pen a haksa hiam?

records.english: It is, but it gets easier once you find people who like the same things.
records.zomi: Haksa hi, ahi zongin na deih kibang deihte na muh ciangin a baih semsem hi.

records.english: How did your son get on at the first football practice?
records.zomi: Football kisin masa pen ah na tapa bangci a om hiam?

records.english: Better than we'd hoped — he came home with a new friend and a bruised knee.
records.zomi: I lametna sangin a hoih zaw — lawm thak khat leh khuk liam khat tawh inn ah a hong tung hi.

records.english: What would you have done if nobody at the new school had spoken to you?
records.zomi: Sang thak ah kuamah in hong kiho kei le bang na hih ding hiam?

records.english: I suppose I'd have joined a club and hoped someone there would notice me.
records.zomi: Club khat ah ka lut a, tua ah kuamah in hong mu ding in ka lamen ding hi, ka ngaihsun hi.

records.english: Are you new in the building?
records.zomi: Hih inn ah na thak hiam?

records.english: I am — I'm Cing, and I've just moved into the flat upstairs.
records.zomi: Thak hi — Cing ka hi a, a tung lam inn ah ka tuah thak hi.

records.english: Had your neighbor not knocked on the door that night, would you two ever have met?
records.zomi: Tua zan na inn veng in kongkhak a kiu kei le, na nih un na kimu ngei ding uh hiam?

records.english: Probably not, since we'd lived next to each other for a year without saying a word.
records.zomi: Kimu lo kha ding hi, kammal khat zong kiho lo-in kum khat sung i kiang ah i om khin manin.

records.english: On my first day at the factory, I was left alone at a machine I didn't understand.
records.zomi: Factory ah ka ni masa pen-in ka theih loh set khat kiang ah keimah bek hong nusia uh hi.

records.english: A woman beside me showed me what to do, and twenty years later she is still my closest friend.
records.zomi: Ka kiang-a numei khat in hih ding hong etsak a, kum sawmnih khit ciangin tu dong ka lawm kinai pen ahi lai hi.

records.english: What makes someone easy to be friends with?
records.zomi: Bang in mi khat lawm bawl baihsak hiam?

records.english: They listen, they remember small things, and they don't gossip.
records.zomi: A ngai uh a, thu neute a phawk uh a, mi dang thu a gen kei uh hi.

records.english: Who invited you to join the hiking club?
records.zomi: Mual kahna pawl ah lut dingin kua in hong sam hiam?

records.english: Nobody — I saw a poster at the shop and just turned up.
records.zomi: Kuamah — dawr ah lai khat ka mu a, ka hong tung bek hi.

records.english: Do you want to be friends with the new girl?
records.zomi: Numei naupang thak tawh kilawm na deih hiam?

records.english: I do want to, but I'm not sure she likes me yet.
records.zomi: Ka deih mahmah hi, ahi zongin amah in hong deih khin hiam ka kician kei hi.

records.english: Is it rude to invite someone at the very last minute?
records.zomi: A nunung pen hun ciangin kuamah sam pen zahtakna om lo ahi hiam?

records.english: Not if you explain that the plans changed suddenly and that you'd genuinely like them to come.
records.zomi: Gelna manlang takin a kilai a, a hong ding na deih taktak hi, cih na gen siang leh hi lo hi.

records.english: Why was your uncle so upset about the wedding invitation?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na pa neu mopawi samna thu-ah a lungkham mahmah hiam?

records.english: His name had been left off by mistake, and he took it as a sign that he wasn't wanted.
records.zomi: A min khialh-in kinusia a, amah deih lo uh hi, cih lim in a ngaihsun hi.

records.english: Who are all these chairs for?
records.zomi: Hih tutnate khempeuh kua adingin ahi hiam?

records.english: We've invited the whole choir after the concert tonight.
records.zomi: Tuni zan la pawi khit ciangin la sakte pawl bup i sam hi.

records.english: Did your aunt say she's coming to the party?
records.zomi: Na ni pawi ah a hong ding hi, a ci hiam?

records.english: She did, and she's bringing her famous rice cake.
records.zomi: A ci hi, a min a than buh moh a tawi ding hi.

records.english: Had you invited fewer people, would the party have been more relaxed?
records.zomi: Mi tawm zaw na sam le, pawi a nuam zaw ding hiam?

records.english: Perhaps, but half the fun was seeing relatives who hadn't been together for years.
records.zomi: Nuam zaw kha ding hi, ahi zongin a nuamna khen khat kum tampi sung kimu khawm lo sanggamte muh ahi hi.

records.english: Did you put anything funny on the invitation?
records.zomi: Samna lai tungah bangmah nuihzathuai na gelh hiam?

records.english: Yes — under the date and time, I wrote, "Please come hungry."
records.zomi: Gelh hi — ni leh hun nuai ah, “Gilkial takin hong pai un,” ka gelh hi.

records.english: Why are you inviting the new family from across the road?
records.zomi: Bang hangin lampi gal lam-a innkuan thak na sam hiam?

records.english: They don't know anyone here yet, and I remember how lonely that felt.
records.zomi: Hih ah kuamah a thei nai kei uh a, tua in bangzah a lungngaihhuai hiam ka phawk hi.

records.english: Should your parents be our first guests in the new house?
records.zomi: Inn thak ah na nu leh na pa i khual masa pen ahi ding uh hiam?

records.english: Yes, and my mother will want to see every room.
records.zomi: Hi ding hi, ka nu in khan khempeuh en a deih ding hi.

records.english: Why is the cake in pieces?
records.zomi: Bang hangin cake a kek hiam?

records.english: It slid off the plate when the car stopped suddenly.
records.zomi: Mawtaw manlang takin a tawp ciangin kuang tung pan a liim khia hi.

records.english: What will we do if it rains during the barbecue?
records.zomi: Sa kanna pawi laitakin guah a zuk leh bang i hih ding hiam?

records.english: We'll move everything into the garage and open the big door.
records.zomi: Khempeuh mawtaw inn sung ah i suan ding a, kongkhak lian i hong ding hi.

records.english: Did you invite your grandmother's old friend from the village?
records.zomi: Khua pan na pi' lawm lui na sam hiam?

records.english: I did, and she was so pleased that she cried on the phone.
records.zomi: Ka sam hi, a lungdam lua ahih manin phone tungah a kap hi.

records.english: Do you really want to invite all of your classmates?
records.zomi: Na kilasi lawm khempeuh na sam nuam taktak hiam?

records.english: I do want to, because nobody should be left out on my birthday.
records.zomi: Ka sam nuam mahmah hi, ka pianni-in kuamah kinusia lo ding ahih manin.

records.english: How do you decide who to invite when the house is so small?
records.zomi: Inn a neu lua laitakin kua na sam ding hiam bangci-in na khensat hiam?

records.english: We invite the people we see least often, since the others will understand.
records.zomi: I muh tawm pen mite i sam hi, a dangte in a thei ding uh ahih manin.

records.english: Why was the party moved to the community hall?
records.zomi: Bang hangin pawi mipi inn ah kisuan hiam?

records.english: Our house was flooded last week, and the floors are still drying out.
records.zomi: Kal nung in i inn tui in a liam a, tual a keu lai hi.

records.english: How should I invite my boss without making it awkward?
records.zomi: Ka makaipa a buaihuai lo-in bangci-in ka sam ding hiam?

records.english: Mention it casually, and make it clear that the whole team is coming.
records.zomi: Pangai takin gen inla, pawl bup a hong ding uh hi, cih kician takin gen in.

records.english: If you could invite anyone at all to dinner, who would it be?
records.zomi: Kua peuhpeuh nitak an ah na sam thei leh kua ahi ding hiam?

records.english: My great-grandmother, so that I could ask her about the village where she grew up.
records.zomi: Ka pi' nu, a khanna khua thu ka dot theih nadingin.

records.english: Why didn't you tell me you were having guests?
records.zomi: Bang hangin khual na nei hi, ci-in hong hilh kei hiam?

records.english: I did tell you — twice, in fact, but you were watching the football.
records.zomi: Kong hilh hi — nihvei mahmah, ahi zongin football na en hi.

records.english: How many people should I cook for on Sunday?
records.zomi: Nipini-in mi bangzah adingin an ka huan ding hiam?

records.english: About fifteen, though my cousins never tell me until the last minute.
records.zomi: Sawm leh nga bang, ka sanggamte in a nunung pen hun dong hong gen ngei kei uh hangin.

records.english: What time did the guests say they'd arrive?
records.zomi: Khualte in nai bangzah ciangin a tung ding uh hi, a ci uh hiam?

records.english: Around seven, but the last ones came after nine.
records.zomi: Nai sagih kim ah, ahi zongin a nunung pente nai kua zawh ciangin a hong tung uh hi.

records.english: Could each of you bring something for the table?
records.zomi: Note khat ciat in dawhkan adingin bangmah na tawi thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: Sure — just tell us whether you need a salad or a dessert.
records.zomi: Thei hi — anteh nawi hiam an lim hiam na kisap hong gen bek in.

records.english: Was the garden ready in time for the guests?
records.zomi: Khualte adingin huan hun takin a kiman hiam?

records.english: Only just — the grass had been cut and the lanterns were hung ten minutes before they arrived.
records.zomi: Tawmno bek — a hong tun ma-un minit sawm-in lopa kiat khin a, meivak bawmte kikhai khin hi.

records.english: Why haven't the invitations arrived?
records.zomi: Bang hangin samna laite a tung nai kei hiam?

records.english: They were lost in the post, so I'm going to phone everyone instead.
records.zomi: Lai khakna ah a mang ahih manin mi khempeuh phone tawh ka sam ding hi.

records.english: Everyone, can you all come to our house for dinner after the match?
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, kimawlna khit ciangin nitak an ah i inn ah na hong thei khempeuh ding uh hiam?

records.english: We'd love to, as long as we can bring something to eat.
records.zomi: Kong pai nuam mahmah uh hi, nek ding bangmah i tawi thei leh.

records.english: What did Grandpa say when you invited him to stay for the weekend?
records.zomi: Kal tawp sung om dingin na sam ciangin ka pu in bang a ci hiam?

records.english: He said, "I'll come if you promise not to make a fuss."
records.zomi: “Buaipih lo ding na kiciam leh ka hong ding hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: What makes a guest feel truly welcome in your home?
records.zomi: Na inn ah bang in khual khat a muak taktak bangin a kisaksak hiam?

records.english: Being offered tea before they've even sat down, and being asked about their family.
records.zomi: A tut ma-un tea kipia leh a innkuan thu kidong.

records.english: Last New Year we invited our new neighbors, who had only arrived from the hills a month before.
records.zomi: Kum thak nung in mual tung pan kha khat paisa-a hong tung thak i inn veng thakte i sam hi.

records.english: They came with a basket of vegetables, stayed until midnight, and now they eat with us every Sunday.
records.zomi: Anteh bawm khat tawh a hong uh a, zanlai dong a om uh a, tu-in Nipini simin i kiang ah an a ne uh hi.

records.english: Why did the guests leave so early?
records.zomi: Bang hangin khualte manlang takin a pai khia uh hiam?

records.english: The power went off, and nobody wanted to eat in the dark.
records.zomi: Meivak a mit a, kuamah in mial sung ah ne a deih kei uh hi.

records.english: Have you sent the invitations for the anniversary yet?
records.zomi: Kum kimna pawi adingin samna lai na khak khin hiam?

records.english: Most of them, but a few came back because the addresses were wrong.
records.zomi: A tamzaw, ahi zongin omna dik lo ahih manin khenkhatte a hong kik hi.

records.english: Who's going to welcome the guests at the door?
records.zomi: Kongkhak ah khualte kua in a muak ding hiam?

records.english: Your little sister, who has been practicing her greeting all afternoon.
records.zomi: Na nau nu, nitak lam bup a hopihna kammal a kisin.

records.english: Is it too late to invite the neighbors for tonight?
records.zomi: Tuni zan adingin inn vengte sam a nun lua khin hiam?

records.english: Not if you go round now and ask them in person.
records.zomi: Tu-in na pai inla amaute mah dong leh nun nai lo hi.

records.english: Do you really appreciate all the cooking your mother does?
records.zomi: Na nu' an huan khempeuh na lungdampih taktak hiam?

records.english: I do appreciate it, even if I don't say so often enough.
records.zomi: Ka lungdampih mahmah hi, a tawntung-in ka gen kei hangin.

records.english: How can I show my coach that I'm grateful?
records.zomi: Ka hilhtu tungah ka lungdam hi, cih bangci-in ka etsak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Keep coming to practice and help the younger players, because that's what she'll value most.
records.zomi: Kisinna ah pai den inla, naupang neu zaw kimawlte huh in, tua pen a manphat sak pen ding ahih manin.

records.english: What made you write to the bus company?
records.zomi: Bang in bus company kiangah lai na gelhsak hiam?

records.english: A driver waited for my mother when she was running late, and I wanted his manager to know.
records.zomi: Ka nu a nun laitakin mawngpa khat in a ngak a, a manager in a theih ding ka deih hi.

records.english: Had nobody thanked her, would she still have kept volunteering?
records.zomi: Kuamah in lungdam a gen kei le, thalawp nasep a sem lai ding hiam?

records.english: Probably, though I suspect the letter from the children made her stay another five years.
records.zomi: Sem lai kha ding hi, ahi zongin naupangte' lai in kum nga behlap a omsak ding in ka ngaihsun hi.

records.english: Who fixed my bicycle while I was at school?
records.zomi: Sang ah ka om laitakin ka siiksakol kua in a bawl siang hiam?

records.english: Your grandfather, with the old tools he keeps in the shed.
records.zomi: Na pu, a van inn sung-a a kem nasepna van luite tawh.

records.english: What did you say to the nurse who looked after you?
records.zomi: Hong kem nurse kiangah bang na ci hiam?

records.english: I told her I'd never forget how patient she had been with me.
records.zomi: Hong thuakzawh dan ka mangngilh ngei kei ding hi, ka ci hi.

records.english: Did the volunteers know how much their work meant to the children?
records.zomi: Thalawpte in a nasep uh naupangte adingin bangzah a thupi hiam a thei uh hiam?

records.english: They found out when the children made a big banner with all their names on it.
records.zomi: Naupangte in a min uh khempeuh kigelh puan lian khat a bawl uh ciangin a thei uh hi.

records.english: What did the neighbor say when you thanked him for clearing the snow?
records.zomi: Vuk na phiat sak manin lungdam na gen ciangin inn veng in bang a ci hiam?

records.english: He said, "That's what neighbors are for," and went back inside.
records.zomi: “Inn vengte in tua bang a hih ding uh hi,” a ci a, sung lam ah a lut kik hi.

records.english: Class, what do you want to say to the bus driver on his last day?
records.zomi: Kilasi, bus mawngpa' ni nunung pen-in bang na gen nuam uh hiam?

records.english: Thank you for driving us safely every morning!
records.zomi: Zingsang simin bit takin hong mawng manin ka lungdam uh hi!

records.english: How do you thank someone who has done far more for you than you could ever repay?
records.zomi: Na thuk kik zawh loh dingin hong hih tam lua mi khat bangci-in lungdam na gen ding hiam?

records.english: By doing the same for someone else, which is what my teacher told me to do.
records.zomi: Mi dang khat tungah tua bangin hih-in, tua pen ka saya in hong hilh hi.

records.english: Everyone, would you raise your glasses to the cooks?
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, an huante adingin na haai uh na lap ding uh hiam?

records.english: To the cooks — we couldn't have asked for anything better!
records.zomi: An huante adingin — hih sangin a hoih zaw i ngen thei kei ding hi!

records.english: How did you thank the woman who found your purse?
records.zomi: Na sum ip a mu numei kiangah bangci-in lungdam na gen hiam?

records.english: I bought her a cake from the bakery and wrote her a short note.
records.zomi: Moh bawlna pan cake khat ka lei sak a, lai tomno khat ka gelh sak hi.

records.english: Why did you mention the cleaners in your retirement speech?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na nasep tawpna thugen ah siangsakte na genpih hiam?

records.english: Without them the building would have fallen apart long ago, yet hardly anyone ever notices their work.
records.zomi: Amaute om lo hi leh inn a sawt khin-in a puk ding hi, ahi zongin kuamah in a nasep uh a phawk ngei kei uh hi.

records.english: Why did the whole team clap when Mai came in?
records.zomi: Mai a hong lut ciangin bang hangin pawl bup in khut a beng uh hiam?

records.english: She stayed late every night last week so that the report would be finished on time.
records.zomi: Report hun takin a zawh nadingin kal nung zan simin a nai-in a om hi.

records.english: Is a text message enough to thank someone for a wedding gift?
records.zomi: Mopawi letsong adingin lungdam genna thu khak khat a kicing hiam?

records.english: For close friends, perhaps, but older relatives usually prefer a phone call or a card.
records.zomi: Lawm kinaite adingin kicing kha ding hi, ahi zongin sanggam upate in phone samna hiam card hiam a deih zaw uh hi.

records.english: Last winter our car broke down on a dark road, and a farmer towed it to his barn with his tractor.
records.zomi: Kum nung khuavot in lampi mial ah i mawtaw a sia a, lo nei khat in a tractor tawh a buh inn dong a kai hi.

records.english: The next week we went back with a basket of fruit, and he laughed and said we'd made his month.
records.zomi: A zom kal in theigah bawm khat tawh i kik a, amah a nui a, a kha bup a nuamsak uh hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Who painted this card for me?
records.zomi: Hih card kua in hong zeek sak hiam?

records.english: The children did, with the brushes you gave them for Christmas.
records.zomi: Naupangte in, Christmas ciangin na piak zeekna tawh.

records.english: If you could thank one person from your childhood, who would it be?
records.zomi: Na naupan lai-a mi khat tungah lungdam na gen thei leh kua ahi ding hiam?

records.english: The librarian who let me stay after closing because my house was too noisy for homework.
records.zomi: Ka inn a ging lua ahih manin inn-a sep ding ka sep theih nadingin a kikhak khit zawh ah hong omsak laibu inn kemtu.

records.english: Why are you smiling at that letter?
records.zomi: Bang hangin tua lai na en-in na nui hiam?

records.english: It's from a student I taught twenty years ago, thanking me for believing in her.
records.zomi: Kum sawmnih paisa-a ka hilh sangnaupang khat pan, amah ka um manin lungdam a gen hi.

records.english: What would you have done without your neighbors after the fire?
records.zomi: Mei kangna khit ciangin na inn vengte om lo hi leh bang na hih ding hiam?

records.english: I can't imagine, since they fed us and gave us beds for nearly a month.
records.zomi: Ka ngaihsun thei kei hi, kha khat dek sung an hong vak uh a, lupna hong pia uh ahih manin.

records.english: Why do some people find it so hard to accept thanks?
records.zomi: Bang hangin mi khenkhatte in lungdam genna sang a haksa sa uh hiam?

records.english: They may feel they were only doing their duty, so being praised embarrasses them.
records.zomi: A sep ding uh bek a sem uh hi, a ci kha uh ahih manin phatna in a zahsak hi.

records.english: Did you like the scarf I sent you?
records.zomi: Ka khak ngawngkhih na deih hiam?

records.english: I love it, and I've worn it every day this week.
records.zomi: Ka deih mahmah a, hih kal ni khempeuh ka bulh hi.

records.english: Did you thank your uncle for the lift to the airport?
records.zomi: Vanlengtual dong hong paipih manin na pa neu kiangah lungdam na gen hiam?

records.english: I did, and I promised to bring him something back from the city.
records.zomi: Ka gen a, khuapi pan bangmah khat tawi sak dingin ka kiciam hi.

records.english: Why did your grandmother cry at the party?
records.zomi: Bang hangin pawi ah na pi a kap hiam?

records.english: Everyone stood up and thanked her for raising so many of us.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh a ding uh a, ei tampi a khoih manin lungdam a gen uh hi.

records.english: Why are you so tired today?
records.zomi: Bang hangin tuni-in na tawl mahmah hiam?

records.english: I stayed up sewing the last corner of a quilt for my parents' anniversary.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa' kum kimna adingin puannak gil nunung pen ka khui-in ka nai hi.

records.english: Was the old man pleased with the photograph?
records.zomi: Pasal upa in lim a deih hiam?

records.english: So pleased that he hung it next to his wedding picture.
records.zomi: A deih lua ahih manin a mopawi lim kiang ah a khai hi.

records.english: How did the fence get repaired so quickly?
records.zomi: Kulh bangci-in manlang takin a kibawl siang hiam?

records.english: The whole street came out on Saturday, and it was finished by lunchtime.
records.zomi: Kiginni-in lampi bup a pai khia uh a, sun ciangin a zo hi.

records.english: What do you appreciate most about your best friend?
records.zomi: Na lawm hoih pen tungah bang na lungdampih pen hiam?

records.english: She always tells me the truth, even when it's not what I want to hear.
records.zomi: Ka zak nuam loh thu hi zongin a tak hong gen tawntung hi.

records.english: Why does your father always thank the waiter twice?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na pa in an zuakpa kiangah nihvei lungdam a gen den hiam?

records.english: He worked in a restaurant for years, and he knows how hard the job is.
records.zomi: Anneekna inn ah kum tampi a sem a, tua nasep bangzah a haksa hiam a thei hi.

records.english: What happened to the flowers you were given?
records.zomi: Hong kipia pakte bang a piang hiam?

records.english: They were knocked over by the cat, but I saved most of them.
records.zomi: Zawh in a lin sak a, ahi zongin a tamzaw ka hon hi.

records.english: Why do people sometimes feel afraid when they think about God's holiness?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pasian' siangthona a ngaihsut ciangun mite khatveivei a lau uh hiam?

records.english: They become aware of their own wrongdoing, but many Christians also speak of finding comfort in God's mercy.
records.zomi: Amau mawhnate a thei uh hi, ahi zongin Christian tampi in Pasian' hehpihna ah hehnepna a mu uh hi, a ci uh hi.

records.english: God can forgive people who are truly sorry, according to Christian teaching.
records.zomi: Christian hilhna bangin, a kisik taktak mite Pasian in a maisak thei hi.

records.english: Which Bible passages describe God as a fair judge?
records.zomi: Laisiangtho koi mun in Pasian thukhen dik ahi hi, ci-in a gen hiam?

records.english: Everyone, please open your Bibles to the Book of Leviticus.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, na Laisiangtho uh Leviticus laibu ah hong un.

records.english: My little brother asked whether God ever gets tired of being good, and nobody at the table knew what to say.
records.zomi: Ka nau pasal in Pasian a hoih den ah a tawl ngei hiam a dong a, dawhkan-a kuamah in bang gen ding a thei kei uh hi.

records.english: After we had lit candles in the church, we stayed and prayed quietly for a long time.
records.zomi: Pawlpi sungah khawimeivaak i hal khit ciangin i om lai a, hun sawt sung dai takin thu i ngen hi.

records.english: When the storm destroyed our church, the people of the village rebuilt it in one month.
records.zomi: Huihpi in i pawlpi inn a susiat ciangin khua mite in kha khat sungin a lam kik uh hi.

records.english: On the first Sunday back, the pastor preached about God's faithfulness.
records.zomi: A kik Nipini masa pen-in pastor in Pasian' thuman dan thu a gen hi.

records.english: Everyone sang so loudly that the neighbors came out to listen.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh ging sang lua takin la a sa uh ahih manin inn vengte ngai dingin a pai khia uh hi.

records.english: What does it mean to be righteous in the way the Bible describes?
records.zomi: Laisiangtho' gen bangin midik hih cih bang a cih nopna ahi hiam?

records.english: My father reads the Bible with a magnifying glass because the print is so small.
records.zomi: Lai a neu lua ahih manin ka pa in khuaitet tawh Laisiangtho a sim hi.

records.english: Children, please be quiet now, because we are going to pray.
records.zomi: Naupangte, thu i ngen ding ahih manin tu-in dai un.

records.english: Not until he read the prophet Amos did my brother see how strongly the Bible speaks about justice for the poor.
records.zomi: Kamsang Amos a sim ciang bek ka sanggam pasal in mi zawngte adingin thuman thukhenna thu Laisiangtho in bangzah a gen hat hiam a thei hi.

records.english: Would you all pray this week for those in our congregation who are sick?
records.zomi: Hih kal sungin i pawlpi sung-a a dam lote adingin na khempeuh un thu na ngen ding uh hiam?

records.english: Christians believe that God is holy and completely good.
records.zomi: Pasian siangtho a, a bup-in a hoih hi, ci-in Christiante in a um uh hi.

records.english: A righteous person, in the Bible's sense, treats others fairly and honestly.
records.zomi: Laisiangtho' cih nopna bangin midik in midangte dik takin leh thuman takin a ngaihsut hi.

records.english: Many Christians take off their shoes or bow their heads to show respect when they pray.
records.zomi: Christian tampi in thu a nget ciangun zahtakna lahna-in a khedap uh a sut uh hiam a lu uh a kun uh hi.

records.english: Rather than hiding his mistake, the deacon confessed it to the church and asked for forgiveness.
records.zomi: A khialhna selsang-in deacon in pawlpi mai ah a pulak a, maisakna a ngen hi.

records.english: Let's read the psalm together and then talk about it.
records.zomi: Late khat khawm-in i sim ding a, tua ciangin a thu i kikup ding hi.

records.english: Our pastor preached about God's righteousness last Sunday.
records.zomi: A paisa Nipini-in i pastor in Pasian' dikna thu a gen hi.

records.english: Before the service begins, would you help me set out the hymn books for the visitors?
records.zomi: Pawlpi kikhopna a kipat ma-in khual hongte adingin labute koih dingin hong huh ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Moses was told to take off his sandals because he was standing on holy ground.
records.zomi: Mun siangtho tungah a din manin Moses a khedap sut dingin kihilh hi.

records.english: Do you think God sees everything we do?
records.zomi: I hihna khempeuh Pasian in a mu in na ngaihsun hiam?

records.english: My mother prays every morning before she does anything else.
records.zomi: Ka nu in zingsang simin bangmah a hih ma-in thu a ngen hi.

records.english: Had the prophets not spoken out against injustice, the poor in Israel might have been forgotten.
records.zomi: Kamsangte in thuman lohna a dot kei le, Israel-a mi zawngte kimangngilh kha ding hi.

records.english: Although God's holiness can seem distant, many Christians say they experience God as close and caring.
records.zomi: Pasian' siangthona a gamla bang hi zongin, Christian tampi in Pasian a kiang-a om leh a kem bangin a thei uh hi, a ci uh hi.

records.english: Why do Christians pray, "Hallowed be your name"?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Christiante in, “Na min siangtho ta hen,” ci-in thu a ngen uh hiam?

records.english: It's a way of asking that God's name be treated as holy, according to many Bible teachers.
records.zomi: Laisiangtho hilhtu tampi' cih bangin, Pasian' min siangtho bangin kizang hen, ci-a ngenna ahi hi.

records.english: Can we thank God for his goodness before we eat?
records.zomi: I nek ma-in Pasian' hoihna adingin lungdam i gen thei ding hiam?

records.english: My grandmother says that God always does what is right.
records.zomi: Pasian in a dik bang a hih tawntung hi, ci-in ka pi in a ci hi.

records.english: The pastor visited the prisoners and read them psalms about God's justice and mercy.
records.zomi: Pastor in thongkiate a veh a, Pasian' thuman thukhenna leh hehpihna thu Late ah a sim sak hi.

records.english: In our church, the children learn a short verse about God's goodness every week.
records.zomi: I pawlpi ah naupangte in kal simin Pasian' hoihna thu cang tomno khat a sin uh hi.

records.english: Many hymns are written to praise God for his holiness.
records.zomi: La tampi Pasian' siangthona phat dingin kigelh hi.

records.english: Our youth group volunteered at the shelter because we believe that God cares about justice.
records.zomi: Pasian in thuman thukhenna a ngaihsut hi, ci-in i um manin i khangno pawl in kemna inn ah thalawp nasep a sem hi.

records.english: In the Bible, Isaiah sees a vision of angels calling out, "Holy, holy, holy."
records.zomi: Laisiangtho sungah Isaiah in vantungmite in, “Siangtho, siangtho, siangtho,” ci-in a sam uh mangmuhna khat a mu hi.

records.english: What Christians often find most striking about God's righteousness is that it goes together with mercy.
records.zomi: Pasian' dikna ah Christiante' lamdang sak pen pen hehpihna tawh a kithuah hi, cih ahi hi.

records.english: Who taught you to pray when you were a child?
records.zomi: Na naupan lai-in thu nget dan kua in hong hilh hiam?

records.english: My grandmother, who prayed for each of us by name every night.
records.zomi: Ka pi, zan simin ei khat ciat i min tawh thu a ngetsak pa.

records.english: According to Leviticus, God told the people, "Be holy, because I am holy."
