records.zomi: Leviticus bangin Pasian in mite kiangah, “Keimah siangtho ka hih manin, note zong na siangtho ta un,” a ci hi.

records.english: My grandfather wrote out the Ten Commandments by hand and hung them on the wall.
records.zomi: Ka pu in Thupiak Sawm a khut tawh a gelh a, bang ah a khai hi.

records.english: What does it mean when we say that God is holy?
records.zomi: Pasian siangtho hi, i cih ciangin bang a cih nopna ahi hiam?

records.english: It means that God is pure and set apart from everything evil, as Christians understand it.
records.zomi: Christiante' theih bangin, Pasian a siangtho a, hoih lo khempeuh pan a kikhen hi, cih ahi hi.

records.english: The church elders helped a widow repair her roof, saying that faith should be shown in action.
records.zomi: Upna pen hihna tawh kilak ding hi, ci-in pawlpi upate in meigong khat' innkhum bawl siang dingin a huh uh hi.

records.english: The more she learned about God's holiness, the more seriously she took her promises to others.
records.zomi: Pasian' siangthona a sin semsem ciangin midangte tung-a a kiciamnate a ngaihsut thupi semsem hi.

records.english: Many Christians believe that God's holiness and love are never in conflict.
records.zomi: Pasian' siangthona leh itna a kituak lo ngei kei hi, ci-in Christian tampi in a um uh hi.

records.english: I do want to live in a way that pleases God.
records.zomi: Pasian a lungdamsak dingin nungta ka deih mahmah hi.

records.english: My aunt teaches Bible stories to children using little wooden figures.
records.zomi: Ka ni in sing lim neute zang-in naupangte Laisiangtho tangthu a hilh hi.

records.english: For many believers, God's righteousness is not only a standard to meet but also a gift they receive by faith.
records.zomi: Um mi tampi adingin Pasian' dikna pen a phak ding kipsakna bek hi lo-in upna tawh a ngah letsong zong ahi hi.

records.english: If God is perfectly just, many people ask, why does the world still contain so much suffering?
records.zomi: Mi tampi in a dot bangin, Pasian a bup-in a dik leh bang hangin leitung ah gimna a tam lai hiam?

records.english: We sometimes sing the old hymn "Holy, Holy, Holy" in our church.
records.zomi: I pawlpi ah la lui “Siangtho, Siangtho, Siangtho” khatveivei i sa hi.

records.english: Is God fair to everyone?
records.zomi: Pasian in mi khempeuh tungah a dik hiam?

records.english: Christians believe that he is, even when people do not understand what is happening.
records.zomi: Bang a piang hiam mite in a theih kei uh hangin, a dik hi, ci-in Christiante in a um uh hi.

records.english: You might find the Book of Psalms helpful when you are worried.
records.zomi: Na lungkham ciangin Late laibu in hong huh kha ding hi.

records.english: Is it possible for a person to be holy?
records.zomi: Mi khat a siangtho thei hiam?

records.english: Many Christians believe that God makes people holy over time as they follow him.
records.zomi: Mite in Pasian a zuih ciangun Pasian in zawl takin a siangthosak hi, ci-in Christian tampi in a um uh hi.

records.english: Christian writers have long asked how a holy God can welcome people who have done wrong.
records.zomi: Pasian siangtho in a khialh mite bangci-in a muak thei hiam, ci-in Christian laigelhte in hun sawt a dong uh hi.

records.english: Could you explain what the Bible means by God's justice?
records.zomi: Pasian' thuman thukhenna in Laisiangtho in bang a cih nopna hiam na gen siang thei ding hiam?

records.english: Having studied the Psalms for many years, our pastor speaks about God's holiness with great gentleness.
records.zomi: Kum tampi sung Late a sin khit ciangin i pastor in Pasian' siangthona thu nem mahmah takin a gen hi.

records.english: Sometimes I wonder whether I could ever be good enough to stand before God.
records.zomi: Pasian mai-ah ding thei dingin ka hoih zo ngei ding hiam, ci-in khatveivei ka ngaihsun hi.

records.english: What made you change your mind about forgiving him?
records.zomi: Amah maisak thu-ah bang in na ngaihsutna hong laihsak hiam?

records.english: He wrote me a letter by hand, and I could see how much it had cost him.
records.zomi: A khut tawh lai hong gelh a, tua in bangzah a haksa sak hiam ka mu thei hi.

records.english: Had you apologized straight away, would your sister have been so upset?
records.zomi: A man takin maisak na ngen le, na sanggam nu a lungkham mahmah ding hiam?

records.english: Probably not, because what hurt her most was that I pretended nothing had happened.
records.zomi: Lungkham lo kha ding hi, a lungkham sak pen bangmah piang lo bangin ka kibawl ahih manin.

records.english: What does a good apology include, in your view?
records.zomi: Na ngaihsutna ah maisak ngetna hoih in bang a huam ding hiam?

records.english: Admitting what you did, saying how it affected the other person, and doing what you can to put it right.
records.zomi: Na hih na pulak, mi dang tungah bang a piangsak hiam gen, leh a dik kik nadingin na hih theih hih.

records.english: Has the shop apologized for the broken washing machine?
records.zomi: Puan silna set sia thu-ah dawr in maisak a ngen khin hiam?

records.english: Not yet, but the manager has promised to call me back today.
records.zomi: Ngen nai lo hi, ahi zongin manager in tuni-in hong sam kik dingin a kiciam hi.

records.english: Who scratched the new table?
records.zomi: Dawhkan thak kua in a khuai hiam?

records.english: Your little brother did it with his toy car, and he's already said sorry.
records.zomi: Na nau pasal in a mawtaw kimawlna tawh a khuai a, maisak a ngen khin hi.

records.english: Last week I forgot my best friend's birthday completely.
records.zomi: Kal nung in ka lawm hoih pen' pianni ka mangngilh kim hi.

records.english: The next morning I baked her a cake, wrote "Sorry" on it in icing, and left it at her door.
records.zomi: A zing zingsangin cake khat ka bawl sak a, a tung ah “Hong maisak in” ka gelh a, a kongkhak ah ka koih hi.

records.english: What did your boss say when you apologized for missing the meeting?
records.zomi: Kikhopna na mansuah manin maisak na ngen ciangin na makai in bang a ci hiam?

records.english: She said, "Thank you for telling me — just send me the notes you missed."
records.zomi: “Hong gen manin ka lungdam hi — na mansuah thu gelhte hong khak bek in,” a ci hi.

records.english: Children, what do you need to say to Mrs. Hoih about her window?
records.zomi: Naupangte, Mrs. Hoih' tukvuang thu-ah a kiangah bang na gen ding uh hiam?

records.english: We're sorry, and we'll be more careful where we kick the ball.
records.zomi: Hong maisak in, bawlung i khawh nading mun ah pilvang zaw ding ka hi uh hi.

records.english: Why are there sweets on everyone's desk?
records.zomi: Bang hangin mi khempeuh' dawhkan tungah an lim a om hiam?

records.english: Thida left them to apologize for being late for the group presentation.
records.zomi: Pawl thu etsakna ah a nun manin maisak ngen dingin Thida in a koih hi.

records.english: How did the cup get broken?
records.zomi: Haai bangci-in a kek hiam?

records.english: It slipped out of my hand while I was washing up.
records.zomi: Kuang ka sil laitakin ka khut pan a liim hi.

records.english: How long did it take your parents to forgive each other after the argument?
records.zomi: Kinialna khit ciangin na nu leh na pa a kimaisak nadingun bangzah sawt hiam?

records.english: About a week, during which the whole house went unusually quiet.
records.zomi: Kal khat bang, tua sungin inn bup a pangai lo-in a dai hi.

records.english: Why is it sometimes easier to forgive a stranger than a family member?
records.zomi: Bang hangin khatveivei innkuan mi sangin mi theih loh maisak a baih zaw hiam?

records.english: With a stranger there's no history, whereas with family every new hurt reminds us of the old ones.
records.zomi: Mi theih loh tawh tangthu om lo a, innkuan tawh lungkhamna thak khempeuh in a luite hong phawksak hi.

records.english: How do you apologize to someone who has already moved far away?
records.zomi: Gamla taka a tuah khin mi khat kiangah bangci-in maisak na ngen ding hiam?

records.english: A sincere letter can still mean a great deal, even if it arrives years later.
records.zomi: Lai taktak khat kum tampi khit ciangin tung zongin a thupi mahmah thei hi.

records.english: Can a friendship be repaired after a serious lie?
records.zomi: Zuau lian khat khit ciangin lawmta a dam kik thei hiam?

records.english: It can, but only if the person who lied is completely honest from then on.
records.zomi: Thei hi, ahi zongin zuau mi in tua pan kipan a bup-in thuman taka a om leh bek.

records.english: Is your friend still angry about the party?
records.zomi: Pawi thu-ah na lawm a heh lai hiam?

records.english: Not anymore — we talked for an hour and laughed about it in the end.
records.zomi: Heh nawn lo hi — nai khat i kiho a, a tawp-in i nuih hi.

records.english: What should you say if you bump into someone in the street?
records.zomi: Lampi ah kuamah na sut leh bang na ci ding hiam?

records.english: Just "Sorry," with a smile.
records.zomi: Nuih tawh “Hong maisak in” ci bek in.

records.english: Will your cousin ever forgive you, do you think?
records.zomi: Na sanggam in hong maisak ngei ding in na ngaihsun hiam?

records.english: In time, I hope, but I really do want her to know that I'm sorry now.
records.zomi: Hun ciangin, ka lamen hi, ahi zongin tu-in ka kisik hi, cih a theih ka deih mahmah hi.

records.english: What happened to my blue shirt?
records.zomi: Ka angki dum bang a piang hiam?

records.english: I'm afraid it was ruined in the wash, and I'll buy you a new one.
records.zomi: Silna sung ah a sia hi, kong lei sak thak ding hi.

records.english: Why did your father finally forgive his old business partner?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na pa in a sumbawl lawm lui a tawp-in a maisak hiam?

records.english: His partner came to the hospital when my father was ill, and that changed everything.
records.zomi: Ka pa a dam loh ciangin a lawm zato ah a hong a, tua in khempeuh a laihsak hi.

records.english: Why did you send flowers to the woman next door?
records.zomi: Bang hangin a kiang inn-a numei kiangah pak na khak hiam?

records.english: My car blocked her drive for a whole morning, and she missed an appointment.
records.zomi: Ka mawtaw in zingsang bup a lampi a khak a, a ngak khak thu a mansuah hi.

records.english: Who broke Grandma's teapot?
records.zomi: Ka pi' tea bel kua in a sukek hiam?

records.english: I did, and I'm going to tell her before she finds the pieces.
records.zomi: Keimah, a kekte a muh ma-in ka hilh ding hi.

records.english: Should I apologize even though I wasn't the only one who was wrong?
records.zomi: A khialh pa kei bek hi lo hangin maisak ka ngen ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, because someone has to go first, and it might as well be you.
records.zomi: Ngen in, kuamah in a masa-in a pai ding a, nangmah na hih leh a hoih hi.

records.english: Why do you always apologize when somebody else bumps into you?
records.zomi: Bang hangin kuamah in hong sut ciangin maisak na ngen tawntung hiam?

records.english: It's a habit from childhood, and I'm trying to stop.
records.zomi: Naupan lai pan ngeina ahi a, tawp dingin ka sin hi.

records.english: Did your brother say sorry for taking your phone?
records.zomi: Na phone a lak manin na sanggam pasal in maisak a ngen hiam?

records.english: He did, and he even charged it for me before giving it back.
records.zomi: Ngen hi, hong pia kik ma-in a mei zong a khuk sak hi.

records.english: Is it ever right to refuse an apology?
records.zomi: Maisak ngetna nial pen a dik ngei hiam?

records.english: Perhaps when the person keeps repeating the same harm, though even then many people choose to forgive in their own hearts.
records.zomi: Mi khat in siatna kibang a bawl kik den ciangin kha ding hi, tua bang hun zongin mi tampi in a lungsim sungah maisak a teel uh hi.

records.english: If you could apologize to one person from your past, who would it be?
records.zomi: Na hun lui pan mi khat kiangah maisak na ngen thei leh kua ahi ding hiam?

records.english: A boy I teased at school, who I later heard had been going through a very hard time at home.
records.zomi: Sang ah ka khem naupang pasal khat, a nung ciangin inn ah hun haksa mahmah a tuak hi, ka zak.

records.english: How can I make it up to you?
records.zomi: Bangci-in kong dik sak kik thei ding hiam?

records.english: Help me paint the fence on Saturday, and we'll call it even.
records.zomi: Kiginni-in kulh zeek dingin hong huh in, tua ciangin i kibang ding hi.

records.english: Why haven't you touched your dinner?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na nitak an na khoih kei hiam?

records.english: I was unkind to a friend at school, and I keep thinking about it.
records.zomi: Sang ah ka lawm khat ka hehpih kei a, ka ngaihsun den hi.

records.english: What did Grandpa say when you admitted losing his watch?
records.zomi: Na pu' nai na mansuah na pulak ciangin bang a ci hiam?

records.english: He told me that a watch could be replaced but an honest grandson could not.
records.zomi: Nai pen kilai thei hi, ahi zongin tu thuman pen kilai thei lo hi, hong ci hi.

records.english: Did the airline apologize for losing your suitcase?
records.zomi: Na van bawm a mansuah manin vanleng company in maisak a ngen hiam?

records.english: They did, and a driver brought it to our hotel the next evening.
records.zomi: Ngen hi, a zing nitak in mawngpa khat in i zinbuuk ah a tawi hi.

records.english: Why did the two farmers measure the field again?
records.zomi: Bang hangin lo nei nihte in lo a teh kik uh hiam?

records.english: Each believed the other's fence was on his land, so they hired someone to check with proper equipment.
records.zomi: Khat ciat in a dang' kulh a leitang tungah a om hi, a ci uh ahih manin vanzat kician tawh en dingin kuamah a sawl uh hi.

records.english: Why aren't you two speaking to each other?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na nih un na kiho kei uh hiam?

records.english: We argued about the holiday, and neither of us wants to give in.
records.zomi: Nopsakna hun thu-ah i kinial a, i nih un a kiphal nuam kei hi.

records.english: Is it ever better to walk away from an argument?
records.zomi: Kinialna pan pai khia pen a hoih zaw ngei hiam?

records.english: Sometimes, especially if one person is too angry to listen, as long as you come back to it later.
records.zomi: Khatveivei, a diakin mi khat a heh lua-in a ngai thei kei ciangin, a nung ciangin na kik leh.

records.english: Why do some families argue more at holidays than at other times?
records.zomi: Bang hangin innkuan khenkhatte nopsakna hun ciangin hun dang sangin a kinial zaw uh hiam?

records.english: People are tired, they expect everything to be perfect, and old disagreements are easier to remember.
records.zomi: Mite a tawl uh a, khempeuh a kicing ding a lamen uh a, kithukimlohna luite a phawk baih zaw hi.

records.english: Could you help me talk to my sister without getting angry?
records.zomi: Heh lo-in ka sanggam nu tawh ka kiho theih nadingin hong huh thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: I'd be glad to, since I know how much you both care about each other.
records.zomi: Lungdam takin, na nih un bangzah na kingaihsun uh hiam ka theih manin.

records.english: Whose turn is it to wash the car?
records.zomi: Mawtaw sil kua' hun ahi hiam?

records.english: Mine, but I'll swap with you if you take the rubbish out tonight.
records.zomi: Keima' hun, ahi zongin tuni zanin nawi na paai leh kong kilaih ding hi.

records.english: Did you really want to keep arguing?
records.zomi: Kinial lai na deih taktak hiam?

records.english: No, I really do want us to be friends again.
records.zomi: Deih lo ing, lawm kik i hih ka deih mahmah hi.

records.english: What did your mother say when you and your brother started shouting?
records.zomi: Nang leh na sanggam pasal na kiko kipat ciangun na nu in bang a ci hiam?

records.english: She said, "Sit down, both of you, and nobody leaves until this is sorted."
records.zomi: “Na nih un tu un, hih thu a kician dong kuamah pai khia kei un,” a ci hi.

records.english: Who should decide when the whole family can't agree?
records.zomi: Innkuan bup a kithukim zo kei ciangin kua in a khensat ding hiam?

records.english: In our house, Grandma has the last word, and nobody argues with her.
records.zomi: I inn ah ka pi in thu nunung a gen a, kuamah in a nial kei hi.

records.english: What would have happened if nobody had stepped in between them?
records.zomi: Kuamah in a kikal uh ah a lut kei le bang a piang ding hiam?

records.english: It would probably have turned into a real fight, since both of them had been drinking.
records.zomi: Kidona taktak a suak kha ding hi, a nih un zu a dawn khin uh ahih manin.

records.english: Who won the argument about the paint color?
records.zomi: Zeek rong thu-a kinialna kua in a zo hiam?

records.english: Nobody — we chose a third color that we both liked.
records.zomi: Kuamah — i nih un i deih rong thumna khat i teel hi.

records.english: How do the neighbors decide who parks in the shared space?
records.zomi: Kihawm mun ah kua in mawtaw a koih ding hiam inn vengte in bangci-in a khensat uh hiam?

records.english: They take alternate weeks, which is written on a calendar by the gate.
records.zomi: Kal khat ciat a kikhel uh a, tua pen kongpi kiang-a kalenda tungah kigelh hi.

records.english: Is it possible for us to share the room without fighting?
records.zomi: Kido lo-in khan khat i kihawm thei ding hiam?

records.english: It is, if you keep your side tidy and I keep the music down.
records.zomi: Thei hi, na lam siang takin na kem a, kei in la ging ka niamsak leh.

records.english: How did you and your flatmate settle the argument about the kitchen?
records.zomi: Nang leh na inn kihawm lawm an huanna thu-a kinialna bangci-in na kilemsak uh hiam?

records.english: We made a cleaning chart and stuck it on the fridge with a magnet.
records.zomi: Siangsakna chart khat i bawl a, khal bawm tungah magnet tawh i belh hi.

records.english: Had the landlord fixed the heating sooner, would the tenants have complained to the council?
records.zomi: Inn neipa in mei lumna a manlang zaw-a bawl siang le, inn luahte in council kiangah a phun ding uh hiam?

records.english: Certainly not, since they had been asking him politely for three winters.
records.zomi: Phun lo mahmah ding uh hi, khuavot thum sung nem takin a ngen uh ahih manin.

records.english: Why did the team captain call everyone together?
records.zomi: Bang hangin pawl makaipa in mi khempeuh a kaikhawm hiam?

records.english: Two players had been arguing in front of the coach, and she wanted to stop it.
records.zomi: Kimawl nih hilhtu mai ah a kinial uh a, a tawpsak nuam hi.

records.english: Last summer my cousins and I quarreled over who would inherit our grandfather's bicycle.
records.zomi: Khal nung in ka sanggamte leh kei ka pu' siiksakol kua in a luah ding hiam i kinial hi.

records.english: In the end we agreed to keep it at Grandma's house, and whoever visits rides it.
records.zomi: A tawp-in ka pi' inn ah i koih ding a, a veh peuhpeuh in a tuang ding hi, ci-in i kithukim hi.

records.english: What do you do when both sides in a dispute are partly right?
records.zomi: Kinialna-a a lam nihte a khen khat a dik ciangin bang na hih hiam?

records.english: I try to find what each side needs most, rather than deciding who is to blame.
records.zomi: Kua mawh hiam khensat sangin a lam khat ciat in bang a kisap pen hiam ka zong hi.

records.english: How could the school have handled the argument between the parents better?
records.zomi: Nu leh pate' kikal-a kinialna sang in bangci-in a hoih zaw-a a khoih thei ding hiam?

records.english: By meeting each family separately first, so that nobody felt embarrassed in front of the others.
records.zomi: Innkuan khat ciat a tuam-in a masa-in kimu-in, kuamah a dangte mai ah a zahlak lo nadingin.

records.english: What should I do if my friend disagrees with everything I say?
records.zomi: Ka gen khempeuh ka lawm in a nial leh bang ka hih ding hiam?

records.english: Ask her what she thinks first, and listen properly before you reply.
records.zomi: A ngaihsutna a masa-in dong inla, na dawng ma-in hoih takin ngai in.

records.english: Who helped your parents make peace with the neighbors?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa inn vengte tawh a kilemna dingin kua in a huh hiam?

records.english: Our pastor invited both families to dinner and simply let them talk.
records.zomi: I pastor in innkuan nihte nitak an ah a sam a, a kiho dingin a phal bek hi.

records.english: What happened between you and your business partner?
records.zomi: Nang leh na sumbawl lawm kikal ah bang a piang hiam?

records.english: We disagreed about expanding the shop, but in the end we decided to wait another year.
records.zomi: Dawr lian sak thu-ah i kithukim kei hi, ahi zongin a tawp-in kum khat behlap ngak dingin i khensat hi.

records.english: Can you both live with the new plan?
records.zomi: Na nih un gelna thak tawh na om thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: I can, as long as we look at it again after a month.
records.zomi: Thei ing, kha khat khit ciangin i en kik leh.

records.english: Everyone, can we agree on a time for the next meeting?
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, kikhopna zom adingin hun khat i kithukim thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: Thursday evening suits most of us, so let's go with that.
records.zomi: Laizing ni nitak in i tamzaw adingin a kituak ahih manin tua i zui ding hi.

records.english: Can we stop arguing and just get the job done?
records.zomi: Kinial i tawp-in nasep i zo bek thei ding hiam?

records.english: Fine, but I still think my way is quicker.
records.zomi: Hoih hi, ahi zongin keima' lampi a manlang zaw hi, ka ci lai hi.

records.english: How do you keep an argument from getting out of hand?
records.zomi: Kinialna a lian lua lo nadingin bangci-in na hih hiam?

records.english: I try to talk about the problem, not about the person.
records.zomi: Mi thu hi lo-in buaina thu bek ka gen hi.

records.english: Is your father still upset with your uncle?
records.zomi: Na pa na pa neu tungah a lungkham lai hiam?

records.english: A little, but they shook hands at the wedding, so things are getting better.
records.zomi: Tawmno, ahi zongin mopawi ah a khut a kilen uh ahih manin a hoih semsem hi.

records.english: Why did you suggest a walk instead of talking in the house?
records.zomi: Bang hangin inn sung-a kiho sangin vak dingin na gen hiam?

records.english: It's easier to stay calm when you're side by side instead of face to face.
records.zomi: Kimaitang sangin kiang khawm-a i om ciangin dai takin om a baih zaw hi.

records.english: Why is there a line of tape across the bedroom floor?
records.zomi: Bang hangin lupna khan tual ah tape khat a kiza hiam?

records.english: The twins drew it this morning after an argument about space.
records.zomi: Mun thu-ah a kinial khit uh ciangin tuni zingsangin apengte in a khai uh hi.

records.english: Why did you send your brother an apology before he sent one to you?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na sanggam pasal in maisak a ngen ma-in nang na ngen masa hiam?

records.english: Waiting for him to go first would have kept us apart for months, and I'd rather lose a little pride than a brother.
records.zomi: A masa-in a ngen dingin ngak leh kha tampi sung i kigamla ding a, sanggam pasal mansuah sangin kisaktheihna tawmno mansuah ka deih zaw hi.

records.english: How will I recognize the house?
records.zomi: Inn bangci-in ka thei ding hiam?

records.english: It's the only one with a yellow door and chickens in the yard.
records.zomi: Kongkhak eng leh tual ah ak nei inn khat bek ahi hi.

records.english: Which way did the tour guide say we should go?
records.zomi: Lampi lak pa in koi lam ah pai ding hi, a ci hiam?

records.english: Straight up the hill, past the church with the red roof.
records.zomi: Mual tung lam a tang takin, innkhum san nei pawlpi inn khen-in.

records.english: Is it possible to walk to the waterfall from the village?
records.zomi: Khua pan tuikhawng dong kalsuan thei hiam?

records.english: It is, but the path is steep, so wear proper shoes and take water.
records.zomi: Thei hi, ahi zongin lampi a ding ahih manin khedap hoih bulh inla tui tawi in.

records.english: Could you draw the route on this napkin so I don't forget it?
records.zomi: Ka mangngilh loh nadingin hih laipek tungah lampi na lim sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Sure, and I'll mark the petrol station so you know when to turn.
records.zomi: Thei hi, bang ciangin na kihei ding hiam na theih nadingin datsi zuakna zong ka khai sak ding hi.

records.english: Is there a footpath, or do we have to walk along the road?
records.zomi: Kalsuanna lampi a om hiam, lampi lian tungah i kalsuan ding hiam?

records.english: There's a path behind the houses, which is much safer for the children.
records.zomi: Innte nung ah lampi neu a om a, naupangte adingin a bit zaw mahmah hi.

records.english: How do you give directions to someone who can't read the signs?
records.zomi: Lai a sim thei lo mi khat kiangah lampi bangci-in na hilh hiam?

records.english: Describe what they'll see and hear along the way, like the mosque, the bus depot, and the noisy market.
records.zomi: Lampi ah a muh leh a zak ding uh gen in, mosque, bus koihna leh a ging zuakna mun bang.

records.english: Had you asked for directions at the station, would you have missed the meeting?
records.zomi: Meileng dinna ah lampi na dot le, kikhopna na mansuah ding hiam?

records.english: No, because I'd have known that the office had moved to the other end of town.
records.zomi: Mansuah lo ding ing, office khuapi tawp lam dang ah a tuah hi, cih ka thei ding ahih manin.

records.english: Why did the taxi driver take such a long route?
records.zomi: Bang hangin taxi mawngpa in lampi sau a zang hiam?

records.english: He said the main road floods after heavy rain, though I suspect he also wanted a bigger fare.
records.zomi: Guah hat khit ciangin lampi lian tui in a liam hi, a ci hi, ahi zongin man tam zaw zong a deih kha in ka ngaihsun hi.

records.english: What landmark should I look for?
records.zomi: Bang lim ka zon ding hiam?

records.english: A tall white water tower, and our street is just beside it.
records.zomi: Tui koihna kang sang khat, i lampi a kiang ah a om hi.

records.english: Where did you get lost on your way here?
records.zomi: Hih ah na hong pai lampi ah koi ah na mang hiam?

records.english: Near the market, where every street looks the same.
records.zomi: Zuakna mun kiang ah, lampi khempeuh a kibang bang na ah.

records.english: Why did you stop to ask a stranger when you have a map?
records.zomi: Map na neih hangin bang hangin mi theih loh khat dong dingin na ding hiam?

records.english: The map is so old that half these streets aren't on it.
records.zomi: Map a lui lua ahih manin hih lampite a khen khat a tung ah a om kei hi.

records.english: Who can show the new teacher where the staff room is?
records.zomi: Saya thak kiangah nasemte khan koi ah a om hiam kua in a etsak thei ding hiam?

records.english: I'll take her, since I'm going there anyway.
records.zomi: Keimah in ka paipih ding hi, tua lam ah ka pai mah ding ahih manin.

records.english: Is it rude to ask for directions when someone is clearly busy?
records.zomi: Kuamah a buai kician laitakin lampi dot pen zahtakna om lo ahi hiam?

records.english: Not if you apologize for interrupting and keep your question short.
records.zomi: Hi lo hi, na sut manin maisak na ngen a, na dotna a tom leh.

records.english: Why did you write the directions on your hand?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na khut tungah lampi na gelh hiam?

records.english: So that I wouldn't need to keep taking my phone out in the rain.
records.zomi: Guah sung ah ka phone ka la khia den lo nadingin.

records.english: Excuse me, is the swimming pool on this side of the river?
records.zomi: Hong maisak in, tui kidiahna mun gun lam khat ah a om hiam?

records.english: No, you'll need to cross the bridge and turn left.
records.zomi: Om lo hi, lei na kan ding a, veilam ah na kihei ding hi.

records.english: On our first evening in the city, we got completely lost looking for a restaurant.
records.zomi: Khuapi ah i zan masa pen-in anneekna inn zong-in i mang kim hi.

records.english: An old man walked us all the way there, and then he refused to stay for even a cup of tea.
records.zomi: Pasal upa khat in tua dong hong paipih a, tea haai khat dawn dingin zong a om nuam kei hi.

records.english: Where exactly is your new flat?
records.zomi: Na inn thak koi ah a om taktak hiam?

records.english: Above the shoe shop, opposite the school, on the third floor.
records.zomi: Khedap dawr tung lam, sang kalh lam, tuang thumna ah.

records.english: If we had taken the other road, would we have arrived sooner?
records.zomi: Lampi dang i zuih le, i tung masa zaw ding hiam?

records.english: Perhaps, but we'd have missed the view from the top of the pass.
records.zomi: Tung masa kha ding hi, ahi zongin mual kikal lampi tung pan muhna i mansuah ding hi.

records.english: Should we turn here or at the next junction?
records.zomi: Hih ah i kihei ding hiam, a zom lampi kituahna ah hiam?

records.english: At the next one — this road only goes to the farm.
records.zomi: A zom pen ah — hih lampi lo dong bek a pai hi.

records.english: Did the app take you the right way?
records.zomi: App in lampi dik ah hong paipih hiam?

records.english: Not really — it sent me down a road that was closed for repairs.
records.zomi: Paipih lo hi — bawl siang dinga kikhak lampi khat ah hong paisak hi.

records.english: What would you do if you got lost in a city where nobody spoke your language?
records.zomi: Na pau a thei mi om lo khuapi khat ah na mang leh bang na hih ding hiam?

records.english: I'd show people the hotel's card and rely on gestures, which work surprisingly well.
records.zomi: Zinbuuk' card mite ka etsak ding a, khut lahna ka zang ding hi, tua in a lamdang takin a sem hi.

records.english: How far is it to the bakery?
records.zomi: Moh bawlna dong bangzah a gamla hiam?

records.english: About five minutes on foot, just after the second traffic light.
records.zomi: Khe tawh minit nga bang, meivak lam lahna nihna khit ciangin.

records.english: Why do people here give directions using shops instead of street names?
records.zomi: Bang hangin hih mun-a mite in lampi min sangin dawrte zang-in lampi a hilh uh hiam?

records.english: Most streets have changed their names twice, but the shops have been here for years.
records.zomi: Lampi tamzaw in a min uh nihvei a laih khin a, ahi zongin dawrte kum tampi sung hih ah a om uh hi.

records.english: Could you walk with me as far as the corner?
records.zomi: Lampi kiheina dong hong paipih thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Gladly, and from there you'll see the pharmacy sign.
records.zomi: Lungdam takin, tua pan zatui zuakna lai na mu ding hi.

records.english: Why are you using a compass in the middle of the city?
records.zomi: Bang hangin khuapi laizang ah compass na zang hiam?

records.english: My phone battery is dead, and I really do want to find the hotel before dark.
records.zomi: Ka phone battery a bei a, khua a mial ma-in zinbuuk ka mu nuam mahmah hi.

records.english: Is the museum far enough to need a taxi?
records.zomi: Museum pen taxi kisam dingin a gamla hiam?

records.english: No, it's a pleasant walk if you go along the river.
records.zomi: Gamla lo hi, gun gei zui-in na pai leh kalsuan a nuam hi.

records.english: How did you find our house without the address?
records.zomi: Omna om lo-in i inn bangci-in na mu hiam?

records.english: I asked at the tea shop, and the owner knew exactly who you were.
records.zomi: Tea dawr ah ka dong a, a neipa in na kua hiam a thei kician hi.

records.english: Everyone, does anybody know how to get to the picnic area from here?
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, hih pan an kinehna mun ah bangci-in pai ding hiam kuamah in a thei hiam?

records.english: Follow the yellow signs along the lake, and you'll see the tables.
records.zomi: Dil gei-a lai eng te zui un, dawhkante na mu ding uh hi.

records.english: What's the quickest way to the stadium on match days?
records.zomi: Kimawlna ni-in kimawlna mun lian ah pai dingin a manlang pen lampi bang ahi hiam?

records.english: Take the train, because the roads around it are completely blocked.
records.zomi: Meileng tuang un, a kim-a lampite a kikhak kim ahih manin.

records.english: Can you tell me where the lifts are?
records.zomi: Lift koi ah a om hiam hong gen thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Go past the reception desk and they're on your right.
records.zomi: Mi muakna dawhkan khen inla, na taklam ah a om hi.

records.english: How do you stay awake on long night drives?
records.zomi: Zan sau mawtaw mawngna ah bangci-in na mit na khak lo hiam?

records.english: I stop every two hours, walk around, and drink something cold.
records.zomi: Nai nih simin ka tawl a, ka vak kawikawi a, a vot bangmah ka dawn hi.

records.english: How do you know when the tires need changing?
records.zomi: Tire laih hun a tung hi, cih bangci-in na thei hiam?

records.english: I put a coin into the tread, and if I can see the whole edge, it's time.
records.zomi: A khuam sung ah dangka khat ka koih a, a gei bup ka muh thei leh a hun a tung hi.

records.english: What would you do if your car broke down on the motorway?
records.zomi: Lampi lian tungah na mawtaw a sia leh bang na hih ding hiam?

records.english: I'd pull onto the hard shoulder, switch on the hazard lights, and wait behind the barrier for help.
records.zomi: Lampi gei ah ka koih ding a, lauhuaina meivak ka vaksak ding a, huhna a tun dong kulh nung ah ka ngak ding hi.

records.english: Last winter our car broke down on the mountain pass in heavy snow.
records.zomi: Kum nung khuavot in vuk hat laitakin mual kikal lampi tungah i mawtaw a sia hi.

records.english: We waited for three hours until a passing bus driver gave us a lift to the next village.
records.zomi: A pai khak bus mawngpa in a zom khua dong hong tuangsak dong nai thum i ngak hi.

records.english: Why did the traffic suddenly start moving again?
records.zomi: Bang hangin mawtawte manlang takin a pai kik kipan uh hiam?

records.english: The broken-down lorry has finally been towed away.
records.zomi: A sia lorry a tawp-in kikai khia hi.

records.english: Who taught you to drive?
records.zomi: Mawtaw mawng dan kua in hong hilh hiam?

records.english: My older brother, in a field behind our house.
records.zomi: Ka u pasal in, i inn nung-a lo khat ah.

records.english: Why are all the cars flashing their lights at us?
records.zomi: Bang hangin mawtaw khempeuh in i tung ah meivak a vaksak uh hiam?

records.english: I think we forgot to turn our headlights on.
records.zomi: I mai lam meivak vaksak i mangngilh in ka ngaihsun hi.

records.english: Did you have the car serviced before driving to the wedding?
records.zomi: Mopawi ah na mawng ma-in mawtaw na en sak hiam?

records.english: Yes, the mechanic changed the oil and checked the tires on Friday.
records.zomi: En sak hi, Laithai ni-in set bawlpa in sathau a lai a, tire a en hi.

records.english: Could you give my mother a lift to the market on Friday?
records.zomi: Laithai ni-in ka nu zuakna mun ah na tuangsak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Happily, as long as she's ready by eight.
records.zomi: Lungdam takin, nai giat ciangin a kiman khin leh.

records.english: Why did you pull over?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na tawlsak hiam?

records.english: I heard a strange noise from the back wheel.
records.zomi: Nung lam ke pan ging lamdang khat ka za hi.

records.english: Should I use the horn when I come round the bend?
records.zomi: Lampi kiheina ka tun ciangin horn ka ging ding hiam?

records.english: On these mountain roads, yes, so that drivers coming the other way know you're there.
records.zomi: Hih mual lampite tungah ging in, a dang lam pan hong mawng mite in na om hi, cih a theih nadingun.

records.english: Why is the car making that clicking sound?
records.zomi: Bang hangin mawtaw in tua ging a bawl hiam?

records.english: I think the battery is almost flat.
records.zomi: Battery a bei dek in ka ngaihsun hi.

records.english: Why do so many accidents happen on that corner?
records.zomi: Bang hangin tua lampi kiheina ah accident tampi a piang hiam?

records.english: The trees hide the junction until the last moment, and drivers coming down the hill are usually going too fast.
records.zomi: Singte in a nunung pen hun dong lampi kituahna a sel a, mual pan hong tum mawngte a tamzaw-in a manlang lua uh hi.

records.english: How did you get the car out of the mud?
records.zomi: Bual sung pan mawtaw bangci-in na la khia hiam?

records.english: We put branches under the wheels and pushed while my uncle drove.
records.zomi: Ke nuai ah singkhawng i koih a, ka pa neu in a mawng laitakin i nawt hi.

records.english: Had you not swerved, would you have hit the cyclist?
records.zomi: Na pial kei le, siiksakol tuang pa na sut ding hiam?

records.english: Almost certainly, because he came out of the side road without looking.
records.zomi: Sut kha ding mahmah hi, en lo-in lampi neu pan a hong pai khia ahih manin.

records.english: Where can I fill up the tank before the mountain road?
records.zomi: Mual lampi ma-in koi ah datsi ka dimsak thei ding hiam?

records.english: At the last petrol station in town, because there isn't another one for fifty kilometers.
records.zomi: Khuapi sung-a datsi zuakna nunung pen ah, kilometer sawmnga sung dang om lo ahih manin.

records.english: Who left the car door open all night?
records.zomi: Zan bup mawtaw kongkhak kua in a nusia hiam?

records.english: I did, and now the battery's dead.
records.zomi: Keimah, tu-in battery a bei hi.

records.english: Why did you make your son retake his driving lessons?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na tapa mawtaw mawng hilhna kik dingin na sawl hiam?

records.english: He passed the test, but he still panicked at roundabouts, and I wanted him to be confident before driving alone.
records.zomi: Sitna a zo hi, ahi zongin lampi kihelna ah a lau lai a, amah bek a mawng ma-in a kician ka deih hi.

records.english: Can you all keep quiet while I reverse into this space?
records.zomi: Hih mun ah nung lam-in ka luttan laitakin na khempeuh un na dai thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: Sorry — we'll stop singing until you've parked.
records.zomi: Hong maisak in — na koih zawh dong la i sa kei ding uh hi.

records.english: Is it possible to get to the coast before the rush hour?
records.zomi: Mawtaw tam hun ma-in tuipi gei i tung thei ding hiam?

records.english: Only if we leave by six, so set your alarm.
records.zomi: Nai guk ciangin i pai khiat leh bek, tua ahih manin na alarm koih in.

records.english: How has the new bypass changed traffic in the town center?
records.zomi: Lampi thak in khuapi laizang ah mawtaw pai dan bangci-in a laihsak hiam?

records.english: The lorries no longer come through the market, so the streets are quieter and safer for children.
records.zomi: Lorry te zuakna mun ah a pai nawn kei uh ahih manin lampite a dai zaw a, naupangte adingin a bit zaw hi.

records.english: Why do you always keep a torch in the glove box?
records.zomi: Bang hangin mawtaw bawm neu sung ah dawimei na koih tawntung hiam?

records.english: So that I can check the tires if I break down at night.
records.zomi: Zan ah mawtaw a sia leh tire ka et theih nadingin.

records.english: Is it worth buying an electric car if you live in the countryside?
records.zomi: Lo gam ah na om leh electric mawtaw lei a manphat hiam?

records.english: It depends on whether there are charging points along the roads you use most.
records.zomi: Na zat tam pen lampite tungah mei khukna mun a om hiam cih tungah a kinga hi.

records.english: How long will the road works go on?
records.zomi: Lampi bawlna bangzah sung a om ding hiam?

records.english: The sign says until the end of the month, but nobody believes it.
records.zomi: Lai in kha tawp dong a ci hi, ahi zongin kuamah in a um kei hi.

records.english: What's the speed limit on this road?
records.zomi: Hih lampi tungah a manlang theih pen bangzah ahi hiam?

records.english: In our town it's thirty near the schools and fifty everywhere else.
records.zomi: I khuapi ah sangte kiang ah sawmthum, a dang mun khempeuh ah sawmnga.

records.english: Why did the police officer wave you over?
records.zomi: Bang hangin palik in hong tawlsak hiam?

records.english: One of my brake lights wasn't working, so he told me to have it fixed this week.
records.zomi: Ka tawlsakna meivak khat a vak kei a, hih kal sungin bawl siang dingin hong hilh hi.

records.english: What happened to the side mirror?
records.zomi: A gei-a mai-et bang a piang hiam?

records.english: A bus came too close in the narrow street and knocked it off.
records.zomi: Lampi neu ah bus khat a kiang lua-in a hong pai a, a khia hi.

records.english: Is everyone wearing a seat belt?
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh in seat belt a khih uh hiam?

records.english: Yes, and the little ones are strapped in at the back.
records.zomi: Khih hi, naupang neute nung lam ah a kikhih uh hi.

records.english: What do you find most stressful about driving in the city?
records.zomi: Khuapi ah mawtaw mawngna ah bang in hong lungkham sak pen hiam?

records.english: The motorbikes that appear from nowhere on both sides, especially at night.
records.zomi: A lam nih pan theih lo-in hong suak motorbike te, a diakin zan ah.

records.english: What made the driver in front stop so suddenly?
records.zomi: Bang hangin a mai-a mawngpa manlang takin a tawp hiam?

records.english: A goat ran across the road right in front of him.
records.zomi: A mai ah kel khat in lampi a kan hi.

records.english: What's the matter with the baby?
records.zomi: Naungek bang a piang hiam?

records.english: She's teething, so she's been crying all afternoon.
records.zomi: A ha a suak ahih manin nitak lam bup a kap hi.

records.english: What would you like for your birthday?
records.zomi: Na pianni adingin bang na deih hiam?

records.english: Just a day at the river with the whole family.
records.zomi: Innkuan bup tawh gun ah ni khat bek.

records.english: What would you have done if the shop had been closed?
records.zomi: Dawr a kikhak kha le bang na hih ding hiam?

records.english: I'd have borrowed some rice from the neighbors and gone shopping in the morning.
records.zomi: Inn vengte pan buh ka ngetsak ding a, zingsang ciangin van lei ka pai ding hi.

records.english: What surprised me most about the city was how quiet it became after ten.
records.zomi: Khuapi ah ka lamdang sak pen pen nai sawm zawh ciangin bangzah a dai hiam, cih ahi hi.

records.english: What happened to the bridge?
records.zomi: Lei bang a piang hiam?

records.english: It was washed away in the flood last night.
records.zomi: Zanni zanin tuiciim in a la mang hi.

records.english: What are you cooking?
records.zomi: Bang na huan hiam?

records.english: Chicken soup with ginger, because your father has a cold.
records.zomi: Siing tawh aksa tui, na pa khuasik a nei ahih manin.

records.english: Nobody could tell me what had become of the key that had hung by the door for twenty years.
records.zomi: Kum sawmnih sung kongkhak kiang-a kikhai tawh bang a suak hiam kuamah in hong gen thei kei hi.

records.english: What time does the clinic open on Saturdays?
records.zomi: Kiginni-in siavuan inn nai bangzah ciangin a kihong hiam?

records.english: At nine, but there's usually a queue by half past eight.
records.zomi: Nai kua ciangin, ahi zongin nai giat leh a khen ciangin mite a kikhai khin tawntung uh hi.

records.english: I asked the guard what we were supposed to do, but he didn't know either.
records.zomi: Bang i hih ding hiam kongpi kemtu ka dong a, amah zong in a thei kei hi.

records.english: What do you think made her change her mind?
records.zomi: Bang in a ngaihsutna a laihsak in na ngaihsun hiam?

records.english: Probably the letter from her old teacher, who encouraged her to apply again.
records.zomi: A saya lui' lai, kik-in ngen dingin a hanthawn pa, ahi kha ding hi.

records.english: What did the teacher say about your homework?
records.zomi: Na inn-a sep ding thu-ah saya in bang a ci hiam?

records.english: She said, "Good work, but please hand it in on time next week."
records.zomi: “A hoih hi, ahi zongin kal zom ciangin hun takin hong pia in,” a ci hi.

records.english: Guess what — I passed my driving test this morning!
records.zomi: Thei in — tuni zingsangin mawtaw mawng sitna ka zo hi!

records.english: What would happen if we missed the last bus?
records.zomi: Bus nunung pen i mansuah leh bang a piang ding hiam?

records.english: We'd have to call my uncle, who would grumble about it for weeks.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu i sam ding a, kal tampi sung a phun ding hi.

records.english: What does your sister do at the bank?
records.zomi: Na sanggam nu bank ah bang a sem hiam?

records.english: She checks loan applications and helps customers open accounts.
records.zomi: Leiba ngetna laite a en a, leite account hon dingin a huh hi.

records.english: What's in this box?
records.zomi: Hih bawm sung ah bang a om hiam?

records.english: Old photos and letters from my grandmother.
records.zomi: Ka pi' lim lui leh lai luite.

records.english: What a beautiful garden you have!
records.zomi: Na huan bangzah a hoih hiam!

records.english: What's this button for?
records.zomi: Hih button bang adingin ahi hiam?

records.english: It turns off the alarm, so don't press it unless you need to.
records.zomi: Alarm a khek a, na kisap kei leh nek kei in.

records.english: What little money he had, he spent on books for his children.
records.zomi: A sum neih tawmno, a tate adingin laibu lei-in a zang hi.

records.english: What made that loud bang outside?
records.zomi: Pua ah bang in ging sang khat a bawl hiam?

records.english: A tire burst on the truck across the road.
records.zomi: Lampi gal lam-a mawtaw lian tung ah tire khat a puak hi.

records.english: What does our school say we can't bring into the exam room?
records.zomi: Sitna khan sung ah bang tawi thei lo hi, ci-in i sang in a ci hiam?

records.english: Phones, notes, and anything with writing on it.
records.zomi: Phone, thu gelhte, leh a tungah lai kigelh bangmah.

records.english: What did you learn at the first-aid course?
records.zomi: Huhna masa kisinna ah bang na sin hiam?

records.english: How to help someone who is choking, and how to put a person on their side safely.
records.zomi: A dangka a kikhak mi khat bangci-in huh ding hiam, leh mi khat a ngei lam ah bit takin bangci-in lup sak ding hiam.

records.english: The children were told what to do if the alarm went off.
records.zomi: Alarm a ging leh bang hih ding hiam naupangte kihilh uh hi.

records.english: What caused the power cut last night?
records.zomi: Zanni zanin bang in meivak a mitsak hiam?

records.english: A tree fell onto the lines during the storm.
records.zomi: Huihpi laitakin sing khat meivak khau tungah a puk hi.

records.english: What is it about this town that keeps bringing you back?
records.zomi: Hih khuapi ah bang in hong kik den sak hiam?

records.english: The people, mostly, and the fact that nobody here ever seems to be in a hurry.
records.zomi: A tamzaw mite, leh hih ah kuamah a manlang ngei lo bang a hih uh.

records.english: What are the rules about visiting hours here?
records.zomi: Hih ah veh hun thupiakte bang ahi hiam?

records.english: Two visitors at a time, and no children under twelve after six o'clock.
records.zomi: Khatvei-in hong veh nih, nai guk zawh ciangin kum sawm leh nih nuai naupang om lo ding.

records.english: What exactly did the manager tell you about the new schedule?
records.zomi: Hun gelna thak thu-ah manager in bang hong hilh taktak hiam?

records.english: He told us that the night shift would start an hour earlier from next month.
records.zomi: A zom kha pan zan nasep nai khat ma-in a kipan ding hi, hong ci hi.

records.english: What color is your new bicycle?
records.zomi: Na siiksakol thak rong bang ahi hiam?

records.english: Dark green, with a black seat.
records.zomi: A eng mial, a tutna a vom.

records.english: What was broken during the move?
records.zomi: Tuah laitakin bang a kek hiam?

records.english: Two plates and the glass on the big mirror.
records.zomi: Kuang nih leh mai-et lian tung-a glass.

records.english: What does the red light on that ticket machine mean?
records.zomi: Tua ticket set tung-a meivak san in bang a cih nopna ahi hiam?

records.english: It means the machine isn't working, so you'll have to pay at the counter.
records.zomi: Set a sem kei hi, a cih nopna ahi a, sum piakna mun ah na pia ding hi.

records.english: What should I wear to the interview?
records.zomi: Interview ah bang ka silh ding hiam?

records.english: Something smart but comfortable, like a plain shirt and dark trousers.
records.zomi: A hoih a, a nuam zong, angki pangai leh kekawi mial bang.

records.english: Tell me exactly what you saw when you arrived at the station, before anyone else had got there.
records.zomi: Kuamah a tun ma-un meileng dinna na tun ciangin na muh khempeuh kician takin hong gen in.

records.english: What did you have done to your car?
records.zomi: Na mawtaw bang na bawlsak hiam?

records.english: I had the brakes replaced and the windows tinted.
records.zomi: Tawlsakna ka lai sak a, tukvuang mial sak hi.

records.english: What kind of music does your brother listen to?
records.zomi: Na sanggam pasal in bang la a ngai hiam?

records.english: Old rock songs, and he plays them far too loudly.
records.zomi: Rock la luite, ging sang lua takin a sa hi.

records.english: What do you need the ladder for?
records.zomi: Bang adingin kahlei na kisap hiam?

records.english: To clean the leaves out of the gutter before the rain comes.
records.zomi: Guah a zuk ma-in innkhum tui luanna pan sing nate siangsak dingin.

records.english: How did you know when to get off?
records.zomi: Bang ciangin na tum ding hiam bangci-in na thei hiam?

records.english: I followed the map on my phone and watched the little dot move.
records.zomi: Ka phone tung-a map ka zui a, a dot neu a kisuan ka en hi.

records.english: What's the quickest way to the airport by public transport?
records.zomi: Mipi mawtaw tawh vanlengtual ah pai a manlang pen bang ahi hiam?

records.english: The express train from the central station, which takes about forty minutes.
records.zomi: Meileng dinna lian pan meileng manlang, minit sawmli bang a la hi.

records.english: Where should I tap my card?
records.zomi: Koi ah ka card ka belh ding hiam?

records.english: On the yellow reader next to the driver.
records.zomi: Mawngpa kiang-a set eng tungah.

records.english: Why is the bus so crowded today?
records.zomi: Bang hangin tuni-in bus a dim mahmah hiam?

records.english: The schools finish early on Fridays, so all the students are going home at once.
records.zomi: Laithai ni simin sangte manlang zaw-in a beng ahih manin sangnaupang khempeuh khatvei-in inn ah a ciah uh hi.

records.english: Why did the transport company change the route past the market?
records.zomi: Bang hangin mawtaw company in zuakna mun khenna lampi a laih hiam?

records.english: The street was so narrow that buses kept scraping parked cars, and shopkeepers had complained for years.
records.zomi: Lampi a neu lua ahih manin bus te in koih mawtawte a nawk den uh a, dawr neite in kum tampi a phun uh hi.

records.english: If the city built a metro, how would your journey to work change?
records.zomi: Khuapi in metro khat a lam leh na nasepna pai dan bangci-in a kilai ding hiam?

records.english: It would take twenty minutes instead of an hour, which would give me time to have breakfast with my children.
records.zomi: Nai khat sangin minit sawmnih a la ding a, ka tate tawh zingsang an ne khawm dingin hun hong pia ding hi.

records.english: How do blind passengers know which stop they're at?
records.zomi: Mitcip khualzinte in koi dinna ah a om uh hiam bangci-in a thei uh hiam?

records.english: Each stop is announced aloud, and some drivers call it out as well.
records.zomi: Dinna khat ciat ging sang takin kigen a, mawng khenkhatte in zong a sam uh hi.

records.english: Could you hold my bag while I find my pass?
records.zomi: Ka pass ka zon laitakin ka ip hong len sak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Sure, take your time.
records.zomi: Thei hi, zawl takin zong in.

records.english: What did the announcement just say?
records.zomi: Tu-a kigen thu in bang a ci hiam?

records.english: It said that the delayed train to the capital will now leave from platform four.
records.zomi: Khuapi lian lam-a pai ding meileng sawt pen platform li pan a pai khia ding hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Can I bring my dog on the tram?
records.zomi: Tram tungah ka ui ka paipih thei ding hiam?

records.english: Small dogs can travel in a bag, but larger ones need a muzzle.
records.zomi: Ui neute ip sung ah a pai thei uh a, a lian zawte in a kam khuhna a kisam hi.

records.english: Could you tell the driver that my son is getting off at the school?
records.zomi: Ka tapa sang ah a tum ding hi, ci-in mawngpa na hilh sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Certainly — he'll make sure the boy gets off at the right stop.
records.zomi: Thei mahmah hi — naupang pasal dinna dik ah a tum nadingin a en ding hi.

records.english: Should I stamp this ticket before I get on?
records.zomi: Ka tuan ma-in hih ticket ka nek ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, in the little machine on the platform, or the inspector may fine you.
records.zomi: Nek in, platform tung-a set neu sung ah, a hi kei leh enkaktu in hong lai thei hi.

records.english: Why are you standing when there are empty seats?
records.zomi: Tutna awng a om hangin bang hangin na ding hiam?

records.english: I've been sitting at a desk all day, so I'd rather stand.
records.zomi: Ni bup dawhkan ah ka tu ahih manin ding ka deih zaw hi.

records.english: What would make public transport easier for parents with young children?
records.zomi: Naupang neu nei nu leh pate adingin bang in mipi mawtaw a baihsak ding hiam?

records.english: Lifts at every station, more space for prams, and drivers who wait until everyone is seated.
records.zomi: Dinna khempeuh ah lift, naungek leng adingin mun tam zaw, leh mi khempeuh a tut dong a ngak mawngte.

records.english: Why do so many people here prefer the shared taxis to the buses?
records.zomi: Bang hangin hih mun-a mi tampi in bus sangin kihawm taxi a deih zaw uh hiam?

records.english: They leave as soon as they're full and drop you almost at your door, although they cost a little more.
records.zomi: A dim ciangin a pai a, na kongkhak dek dong hong tum sak uh hi, tawmno a man sang zaw hangin.

records.english: Did the driver let you on without a ticket?
records.zomi: Ticket om lo-in mawngpa in hong tuangsak hiam?

records.english: He did, because the machine at the stop was broken.
records.zomi: Tuangsak hi, dinna-a set a sia ahih manin.

records.english: How do you pass the time on your long commute?
records.zomi: Na nasepna pai lampi sau ah hun bangci-in na zang hiam?

records.english: I read, or I listen to language lessons with my earphones.
records.zomi: Ka sim a, a hi kei leh ka earphone tawh pau sinna ka ngai hi.

records.english: Why do you always sit at the front of the bus?
records.zomi: Bang hangin bus mai lam ah na tu tawntung hiam?

records.english: I get sick if I sit at the back, where it bounces more.
records.zomi: Nung lam ah ka tut leh a kihuk zaw ahih manin ka lua nuam hi.

records.english: Why did you buy a monthly pass instead of single tickets?
records.zomi: Bang hangin ticket khat ciat sangin kha khat pass na lei hiam?

records.english: I take the bus twice a day, so the pass pays for itself in two weeks.
records.zomi: Ni khat ah nihvei bus ka tuang ahih manin kal nih sungin pass in a man a kikhawm kik hi.

records.english: On my first morning in the city, I took the tram in the wrong direction.
records.zomi: Khuapi ah ka zingsang masa pen-in lam dik lo ah tram ka tuang hi.

records.english: A schoolgirl noticed my confused face, got off with me, and showed me the right platform.
records.zomi: Sang numei naupang khat in ka mai lungkham a mu a, ka kiang ah a tum a, platform dik hong etsak hi.

records.english: Would the minibus driver wait for us if we were a few minutes late?
records.zomi: Minit tawmno i nun leh minibus mawngpa in hong ngak ding hiam?

records.english: He'd probably wait, because he knows nearly everyone in the village.
records.zomi: Ngak kha ding hi, khua sung-a mi khempeuh dek a thei ahih manin.

records.english: Who's going to meet Grandma at the bus station?
records.zomi: Bus dinna ah ka pi kua in a dawn ding hiam?

records.english: I will, and I'll carry her suitcase up the hill.
records.zomi: Keimah, a van bawm mual tung dong ka pua ding hi.

records.english: Why did the train stop between stations?
records.zomi: Bang hangin dinna nih kikal ah meileng a tawp hiam?

records.english: There's a fallen tree on the line ahead, so we're waiting until it's cleared.
records.zomi: Mai lam ah meileng lampi tungah sing khat a puk a, a kisiansak dong i ngak hi.

records.english: Is it fair that pensioners travel free while students pay full price?
records.zomi: Pension ngah upate a man om lo-a a tuan laitakin sangnaupangte in man bup a piak pen a dik hiam?

records.english: Many students think not, but the council says the pensions in our region are too small to cover fares.
records.zomi: Sangnaupang tampi in dik lo hi a ci uh hi, ahi zongin i gam-a pension in man a kicin kei hi, ci-in council in a ci hi.

records.english: Can I give my seat to the old man by the door?
records.zomi: Kongkhak kiang-a pasal upa ka tutna ka pia thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, that's kind of you, and he looks tired.
records.zomi: Thei hi, tua pen na hehpihna ahi hi, a tawl bang zong hi.

records.english: Is smoking allowed at the bus stops here?
records.zomi: Hih mun-a bus dinna ah meidawn kiphal hiam?

records.english: Not anymore — in our city it's banned under every shelter.
records.zomi: Kiphal nawn lo hi — i khuapi ah inn khuh khempeuh nuai ah kikham hi.

records.english: Are we allowed to eat on the train?
records.zomi: Meileng tungah an i ne thei ding hiam?

records.english: Snacks are fine, but hot food isn't allowed in our local trains.
records.zomi: An neu a hoih hi, ahi zongin i khua meileng ah an sa kiphal lo hi.

records.english: Is it possible to change buses with the same ticket?
records.zomi: Ticket kibang mah tawh bus ka lai thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, within an hour, as long as you keep the ticket with you.
records.zomi: Thei hi, nai khat sungin, na ticket na kem lai sungin.

records.english: Where can I leave my bicycle near the station?
records.zomi: Meileng dinna kiang ah ka siiksakol koi ah ka nusia thei ding hiam?

records.english: There's a covered rack on the left, and you'll need your own lock.
records.zomi: Veilam ah khuh nei koihna khat a om a, nangma' khakna na kisam ding hi.

records.english: Had the last bus not been canceled, would you have stayed in the city?
records.zomi: Bus nunung pen a kikhak kei le, khuapi ah na om ding hiam?

records.english: No, I'd have come home, because I had to start work at six the next morning.
records.zomi: Om lo ding ing, inn ah ka hong ding hi, a zing zingsang nai guk ciangin nasep ka kipan ding ahih manin.

records.english: What time does our bus leave for the city?
records.zomi: Khuapi lam-a i bus nai bangzah ciangin a pai hiam?

records.english: At six in the morning, so we need to be at the station by half past five.
records.zomi: Zingsang nai guk ciangin, tua ahih manin nai nga leh a khen ciangin dinna ah i om ding hi.

records.english: What happened on the way to the city?
records.zomi: Khuapi pai lampi ah bang a piang hiam?

records.english: The bus broke down, and we waited three hours for another one.
records.zomi: Bus a sia a, a dang khat nai thum i ngak hi.

records.english: May I bring my guitar on the coach?
records.zomi: Bus lian tungah ka guitar ka tawi thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, but it has to go in the luggage hold underneath.
records.zomi: Thei hi, ahi zongin a nuai lam van koihna ah a om ding hi.

records.english: Why are you so nervous about the trip?
records.zomi: Bang hangin khualzinna thu-ah na lau mahmah hiam?

records.english: I've never been to such a big city, and I'm worried I'll get lost.
records.zomi: Tua bang khuapi lian ah ka pai ngei kei a, ka mang kha ding ka lau hi.

records.english: What do you miss most when you're away from home?
records.zomi: Inn pan na gamlat ciangin bang na lungngai pen hiam?

records.english: My mother's cooking and the sound of the river at night.
records.zomi: Ka nu' an huan leh zan ciang-a gun ging.

records.english: Did you remember to bring your identity card?
records.zomi: Na mimal card tawi ding na phawk hiam?

records.english: Yes, it's in the front pocket of my bag with the tickets.
records.zomi: Phawk hi, ka ip mai lam ip neu sung ah ticket te tawh a om hi.

records.english: Where will you sleep when you get there?
records.zomi: Na tun ciangin koi ah na ihmu ding hiam?

records.english: At my friend's flat, on a mattress in her living room.
records.zomi: Ka lawm' inn ah, a tutna khan sung-a mattress tungah.

records.english: Why do people from the countryside often find the city exhausting?
records.zomi: Bang hangin lo gam pan hong mite in khuapi a tawlsak sa uh hiam?

records.english: There's noise everywhere, nobody greets you, and even crossing the road requires concentration.
records.zomi: Mun khempeuh ah ging a om a, kuamah in hong hopih kei a, lampi kan zong lungsim koih a kisam hi.

records.english: Is it possible to get there and back in one day?
records.zomi: Ni khat sungin pai-in kik thei ding hiam?

records.english: Only if you take the first train and don't mind getting home after midnight.
records.zomi: Meileng masa pen na tuan a, zanlai zawh ciangin inn na tun na lungkham kei leh bek.

records.english: Can we stop at the halfway town to stretch our legs?
records.zomi: Kalsuan kimlai-a khua ah i khe i zan nadingin i tawl thei ding hiam?

records.english: We can, but only for fifteen minutes if we want to arrive before dark.
records.zomi: Thei hi, ahi zongin khua a mial ma-in i tun i deih leh minit sawm leh nga bek.

records.english: Why did you choose the night train?
records.zomi: Bang hangin zan meileng na teel hiam?

records.english: It saves the cost of a hotel, and I can sleep most of the way.
records.zomi: Zinbuuk man a kem a, lampi a tamzaw ka ihmu thei hi.

records.english: Is it worth taking the scenic route even though it's slower?
records.zomi: A zawi zaw hangin muhnop lampi zuih a manphat hiam?

records.english: It is, if you're not in a hurry, because the views over the mountains are unforgettable.
records.zomi: Manphat hi, na manlang kei leh, mual tung-a muhnate mangngilh theih lo ahih manin.

records.english: Who's going to water the plants while we're in the city?
records.zomi: Khuapi ah i om laitakin singkungte kua in tui a lei ding hiam?

records.english: Our neighbor has offered, and I've left her a key.
records.zomi: I inn veng in a kipia a, tawh khat ka nusia sak hi.

records.english: How will we find each other at the station?
records.zomi: Meileng dinna ah bangci-in i kimu ding hiam?

records.english: I'll be waiting by the big clock in the main hall.
records.zomi: Inn lianpi sung-a nai lian kiang ah kong ngak ding hi.

records.english: Why is your brother moving to another city?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na sanggam pasal khuapi dang ah a tuah ding hiam?

records.english: He's got a place at the university there to study engineering.
records.zomi: Engineering sin dingin tua mun-a sangpi ah mun a ngah hi.

records.english: Can children travel on the coach without an adult?
records.zomi: Upa om lo-in naupangte bus lian tungah a tuang thei uh hiam?

records.english: Not under fourteen, according to the coach company's rules.
records.zomi: Bus company' thupiak bangin kum sawm leh li nuai thei lo hi.

records.english: Last spring my father and I took the train to the capital for my sister's graduation.
records.zomi: Kum nung spring in ka sanggam nu' sang zawhna adingin kei leh ka pa meileng tawh khuapi lian ah i pai hi.

records.english: We arrived just as the ceremony began, and she waved at us from the stage.
records.zomi: Pawi a kipat laitakin i tung a, dawhsang tung pan hong khut vai hi.

records.english: Could you buy some of the famous city sweets for your grandmother?
records.zomi: Na pi adingin khuapi-a min thang an lim tawmno na lei thei ding hiam?

records.english: I will, and I'll bring back some for the neighbors too.
records.zomi: Lei ding ing, inn vengte adingin zong ka tawi ding hi.

records.english: Would your uncle let us stay with him for a night?
records.zomi: Na pa neu in zan khat a kiang ah hong omsak ding hiam?

records.english: I'm sure he would, as long as we don't mind sharing a room with his parrot.
records.zomi: Omsak ding hi, ka thei hi, a vasa-pau tawh khan khat kihawm i lungkham kei leh.

records.english: On this airline, what am I not allowed to take in my hand luggage?
records.zomi: Hih vanleng ah ka khut-a tawi ip sung ah bang ka koih thei lo hiam?

records.english: Large bottles of liquid and anything sharp, according to the airline's list.
records.zomi: Vanleng company' list bangin tui bel lian leh a hiam bangmah.

records.english: How has traveling to other cities changed your view of your own town?
records.zomi: Khuapi dangte ah khualzinna in na khua tungah na ngaihsutna bangci-in a laihsak hiam?

records.english: I appreciate how quiet it is, though I've also noticed how few opportunities there are for young people.
records.zomi: Bangzah a dai hiam ka lungdampih a, ahi zongin khangnote adingin hun bangzah a tawm hiam zong ka mu hi.

records.english: Who's paying for the trip to the training course?
records.zomi: Kisinna pai khualzinna man kua in a pia hiam?

records.english: The company pays for the travel, and we pay for our own meals.
records.zomi: Company in khualzin man a pia a, eite in i an man i pia hi.

records.english: What did your cousin say when you told her you were coming?
records.zomi: Na hong ding hi, ci-in na sanggam na hilh ciangin bang a ci hiam?

records.english: She said, "Stay as long as you like, and bring your appetite."
records.zomi: “Na deih tan om inla, na an deihna tawi in,” a ci hi.

records.english: What advice would you give someone visiting a big city for the first time?
records.zomi: Khuapi lian ah a masa pen-a pai mi khat bang thuhilhna na pia ding hiam?

records.english: Keep your bag in front of you, ask for directions in shops rather than on the street, and give yourself extra time.
records.zomi: Na ip na mai lam ah koih in, lampi tung sangin dawr ah lampi dong in, leh hun behlap kipia in.

records.english: Why are you taking so much food on the journey?
records.zomi: Bang hangin khualzinna ah an tam lua na tawi hiam?

records.english: The bus doesn't stop for lunch, and the food at the stations is expensive.
records.zomi: Bus sun an adingin a tawl kei a, dinna-a an a man tam hi.

records.english: Should I tell the hotel that we'll arrive late?
records.zomi: Nun takin i tung ding hi, ci-in zinbuuk ka hilh ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, or they might give our room to someone else.
records.zomi: Hilh in, a hi kei leh i khan mi dang a pia kha ding uh hi.

records.english: How did your grandparents travel to the city when they were young?
records.zomi: Na pu leh pite a khangno lai uh-in khuapi ah bangci-in a pai uh hiam?

records.english: They walked for two days to the main road and then rode on the back of a truck.
records.zomi: Lampi lian dong ni nih a kalsuan uh a, tua ciangin mawtaw lian nung lam ah a tuang uh hi.

records.english: What should I pack for three days in the capital?
records.zomi: Khuapi lian ah ni thum adingin bang ka thuk ding hiam?

records.english: Comfortable shoes, an umbrella, and one smart outfit for the meeting.
records.zomi: Khedap nuam, kawl lukhu khat, leh kikhopna adingin puan hoih khat.

records.english: Had you booked the tickets earlier, would they have been cheaper?
records.zomi: Ticket na koih masa zaw le, a man neu zaw ding hiam?

records.english: Much cheaper, because the price nearly doubles in the last week before a holiday.
records.zomi: Neu zaw mahmah ding hi, nopsakna hun ma-a kal nunung ah a man nihvei dek a khang ahih manin.

records.english: If you could live in any city, which would you choose?
records.zomi: Khuapi peuhpeuh ah na om thei leh koi na teel ding hiam?

records.english: Probably one near the sea, where I could swim after work and still have a good job.
records.zomi: Tuipi kiang-a khat kha ding hi, nasep khit ciangin ka kidiah thei a, nasep hoih zong ka nei thei ding mun.

records.english: If you ran a hotel, what would you change about the way guests are treated?
records.zomi: Zinbuuk na nei leh khualte' kizat dan bang na laih ding hiam?

records.english: I'd ask every guest what they need on arrival, instead of waiting for them to complain.
records.zomi: A phun ding uh ngak sangin khual khat ciat a tun ciangun bang a kisam uh hiam ka dong ding hi.

records.english: Should I report the stain on the carpet when we leave?
records.zomi: I pai ciangin tuutphah tung-a bawk thu ka gen ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, or they might think we caused it and charge us for cleaning.
records.zomi: Gen in, a hi kei leh eite in i bawl hi, a ci kha ding uh a, siangsak man hong la kha ding uh hi.

records.english: What happened to the Wi-Fi?
records.zomi: Wi-Fi bang a piang hiam?

records.english: It went down during the storm, and the technician is coming this afternoon.
records.zomi: Huihpi laitakin a mang a, technician tuni nitak lam a hong ding hi.

records.english: Why did the farmer refuse to take money for our night in his barn?
records.zomi: Bang hangin lo nei in a buh inn-a i zan khat adingin sum a sang nuam kei hiam?

records.english: He said that travelers had always been welcome on his land, and that we'd done him no harm.
records.zomi: A leitang tungah khualzinte kimuak tawntung hi, a ci a, siatna khat zong i bawl kei hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Why do some travelers prefer staying with local families?
records.zomi: Bang hangin khualzin khenkhatte in tua mun-a innkuante kiang ah om a deih zaw uh hiam?

records.english: They learn far more about daily life, and the money goes directly to the people who live there.
records.zomi: Ni sim nuntakna thu a sin tam zaw uh a, sum tua mun ah a om mite kiang ah a tang takin a pai hi.

records.english: What makes a guesthouse feel more welcoming than a large hotel?
records.zomi: Bang in zinbuuk neu khat zinbuuk lian sangin a muak hoih zaw bangin a kisaksak hiam?

records.english: Being greeted by the people who own the place, and having breakfast cooked by someone who asks how you slept.
records.zomi: Mun a neite in hong hopih a, na ihmut bangci hiam a dong mi in zingsang an hong huan sak.

records.english: Did they say why the bill was so high?
records.zomi: Bang hangin bill a tam mahmah hiam a gen uh hiam?

records.english: They'd charged us for the minibar, which we hadn't even opened.
records.zomi: I hon zong hon lo minibar man hong la uh hi.

records.english: How did the window get broken?
records.zomi: Tukvuang bangci-in a kek hiam?

records.english: It slammed shut in the wind while we were out.
records.zomi: I pai laitakin huih in hat takin a khak hi.

records.english: Are guests allowed to cook in the rooms?
records.zomi: Khualte in khan sung ah an a huan thei uh hiam?

records.english: No, but there's a shared kitchen on the first floor that you can use until ten.
records.zomi: Thei lo uh hi, ahi zongin tuang khatna ah nai sawm dong na zat theih kihawm an huanna a om hi.

records.english: On our honeymoon, the hotel lost our booking and had no rooms left.
records.zomi: I kiteen khit nopsakna hun-in zinbuuk in i ngetna a mansuah a, khan a om nawn kei hi.

records.english: The manager drove us to his sister's guesthouse, where we ended up having the best week of our lives.
records.zomi: Manager in a sanggam nu' zinbuuk neu ah hong paipih a, tua ah i nuntak sung-a kal hoih pen i nei hi.

records.english: Can visitors stay overnight in the hostel?
records.zomi: Khual hongte zinbuuk neu ah zan khat a om thei uh hiam?

records.english: Not in the shared rooms, but you can book them a private room if one is free.
records.zomi: Kihawm khan ah thei lo hi, ahi zongin awng leh amaute adingin khan tuam khat na ngen thei hi.

records.english: Who carried our suitcases up to the room?
records.zomi: I van bawmte khan dong kua in a pua hiam?

records.english: A young porter, and he wouldn't take a tip.
records.zomi: Van puak khangno khat, letsong sum a sang nuam kei hi.

records.english: What's that smell in the corridor?
records.zomi: Inn lam ah hih namtui bang ahi hiam?

records.english: They're painting the rooms on this floor, so they've left the windows open.
records.zomi: Hih tuang-a khante a zeek uh ahih manin tukvuangte a hong uh hi.

records.english: Is it all right if my son brings his friend to swim in the hotel pool?
records.zomi: Ka tapa in a lawm zinbuuk tui kidiahna ah a paipih leh a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: Only registered guests are allowed to use the pool, but there's a public pool down the road.
records.zomi: Kigelh khualte bek in tui kidiahna a zang thei uh hi, ahi zongin lampi nuai lam ah mipi tui kidiahna a om hi.

records.english: Could you keep this parcel for my colleague until she arrives?
records.zomi: Ka nasem lawm a tun dong hih van bawm na kem sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Gladly — I'll put her name on it and keep it behind the desk.
records.zomi: Lungdam takin — a min ka gelh ding a, dawhkan nung ah ka kem ding hi.

records.english: What did the receptionist say about the noise?
records.zomi: Ging thu-ah mi muakpa in bang a ci hiam?

records.english: She said, "I'm so sorry — we'll move you to a quieter room straight away."
records.zomi: “Hong maisak in — tu-in khan dai zaw khat ah kong suan ding uh hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: How would you describe the worst place you've ever stayed?
records.zomi: Na omna ngei hoih lo pen mun bangci-in na gen ding hiam?

records.english: A room so damp that our clothes were wet in the morning, with a door that wouldn't lock.
records.zomi: Khan a nawng lua-in zingsangin i puante a dikdek a, kongkhak a kikhak thei lo.

records.english: Why is the lift out of order?
records.zomi: Bang hangin lift a sem kei hiam?

records.english: It stopped working during the power cut last night.
records.zomi: Zanni zanin meivak a mit laitakin a tawp hi.

records.english: Why do you always stay in the same small hotel?
records.zomi: Bang hangin zinbuuk neu kibang mah ah na om tawntung hiam?

records.english: The owner remembers my name, and she always keeps the room with the garden view for me.
records.zomi: A neinu in ka min a phawk a, huan muhna nei khan ka adingin a kem tawntung hi.

records.english: Why are there two keys on the ring?
records.zomi: Bang hangin khau ah tawh nih a om hiam?

records.english: One is for the room, and the smaller one is for the safe in the wardrobe.
records.zomi: Khat khan adingin, a neu zaw pen puan bawm sung-a sum bawm adingin ahi hi.

records.english: Who left these flowers in our room?
records.zomi: I khan sung ah hih pakte kua in a koih hiam?

records.english: The hotel, to welcome us on our anniversary.
records.zomi: Zinbuuk in, i kum kimna ah hong muak dingin.

records.english: Why did the guesthouse owner give us extra blankets?
records.zomi: Bang hangin zinbuuk neu neipa in puannak behlap hong pia hiam?

records.english: The heating in the old part of the house doesn't work well in winter.
records.zomi: Inn khen lui ah khuavot ciangin mei lumna a sem hoih kei hi.

records.english: Is it possible to change rooms after the first night?
records.zomi: Zan masa khit ciangin khan ka lai thei ding hiam?

records.english: If one becomes free, we'll move you without any extra charge.
records.zomi: Khat a awng leh man behlap om lo-in kong suan ding uh hi.

records.english: Can we smoke on the balcony?
records.zomi: Balcony tungah meidawn i dawn thei ding hiam?

records.english: I'm afraid not — the whole hotel is smoke-free, including the balconies.
records.zomi: Hong maisak in — zinbuuk bup, balcony te tawh, meidawn kiphal lo hi.

records.english: Why is the floor in our bathroom wet?
records.zomi: Bang hangin i kisilna inn tual a dikdek hiam?

records.english: The pipe under the sink has been leaking since this morning.
records.zomi: Kuang silna nuai-a tui khuam tuni zingsang pan a zu hi.

records.english: Why did you ask for a room on the ground floor?
records.zomi: Bang hangin nuai lam tuang-a khan na ngen hiam?

records.english: My mother can't manage stairs anymore, and I didn't want to rely on the lift.
records.zomi: Ka nu in kahlei a kah zo nawn kei a, lift tungah ka kinga nuam kei hi.

records.english: Did the hotel let you check out late?
records.zomi: Zinbuuk in a nun zaw-in hong pai khiatsak hiam?

records.english: They did, because the cleaner said our room wasn't needed until the evening.
records.zomi: Pai khiatsak hi, siangsaktu in nitak dong i khan a kisam kei hi, a ci ahih manin.

records.english: Is it rude to ask for a discount when you stay a long time?
records.zomi: Hun sawt na om ciangin man kiam ngen pen zahtakna om lo ahi hiam?

records.english: Not at all, and many guesthouses here expect long-staying guests to ask.
records.zomi: Hi lo mahmah hi, hih mun-a zinbuuk neu tampi in sawt om khualte in a ngen ding uh a lamen uh hi.

records.english: Can you arrange a cot for our baby?
records.zomi: I naungek adingin naungek lupna khat na bawl sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Certainly, and housekeeping will bring it up within the hour.
records.zomi: Thei mahmah hi, nai khat sungin inn kemte in a tawi ding uh hi.

records.english: Had the hotel told you about the building work, would you have booked a different one?
records.zomi: Inn lamna thu zinbuuk in hong hilh le, a dang khat na ngen ding hiam?

records.english: Certainly, because we were woken by drilling at seven every morning.
records.zomi: Ngen mahmah ding ing, zingsang simin nai sagih ciangin sut ging in hong phawngsak ahih manin.

records.english: Why is the milk all over the stove?
records.zomi: Bang hangin meikhuk tungah nawi a om bup hiam?

records.english: It boiled over while I was answering the door.
records.zomi: Kongkhak ka dawn laitakin a suang-in a liam hi.

records.english: Who told you not to open the oven door so often?
records.zomi: Oven kongkhak hon den lo dingin kua in hong hilh hiam?

records.english: My aunt, who says the cake will sink if the cold air gets in.
records.zomi: Ka ni, huih vot a lut leh cake a kiam ding hi, a ci pa.

records.english: What can I add to make the sauce thicker?
records.zomi: An tui a tawt zawk nadingin bang ka behlap thei ding hiam?

records.english: Stir in a spoonful of flour mixed with a little cold water.
records.zomi: Buh-mal kawm khat tui vot tawmno tawh kihel sung ah koih-in ngom in.

records.english: Did the soup taste salty to you?
records.zomi: An tui a al bang na sa hiam?

records.english: A little, but some potatoes might soak up the extra salt.
records.zomi: Tawmno, ahi zongin alu khenkhatte in cii behlap a dawp kha ding hi.

records.english: Who was hurt in the kitchen this afternoon?
records.zomi: Tuni nitak lam an huanna ah kua a liam hiam?
