records.english: One of the cooks was burned by hot oil, but the nurse says it's not serious.
records.zomi: An huan khat sathau sa in a kang a, ahi zongin a lauhuai kei hi, ci-in nurse in a ci hi.

records.english: Why are there tears in your eyes?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na mit sung ah mittui a om hiam?

records.english: I've been chopping onions for the whole family.
records.zomi: Innkuan bup adingin lothaang ka at hi.

records.english: Can I lick the spoon?
records.zomi: Kawm ka liak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, but only after the cake is in the oven.
records.zomi: Thei hi, ahi zongin cake oven sung a om khit ciang bek.

records.english: What did Grandma say about adding sugar to the curry?
records.zomi: Curry ah sugar koih thu-ah ka pi in bang a ci hiam?

records.english: She said, "Just a pinch, and never tell your grandfather."
records.zomi: “Tawmno bek, leh na pu hilh ngei kei in,” a ci hi.

records.english: Last Christmas my brother tried to roast a whole chicken for the first time.
records.zomi: Christmas nung in ka sanggam pasal in a masa pen-in aksa bup a em hi.

records.english: The oven was turned up too high, the smoke alarm went off, and we ate rice and eggs instead.
records.zomi: Oven a sa lua a, meikhu alarm a ging a, tua sangin buh leh aktui i ne hi.

records.english: Who burned the toast?
records.zomi: Moh kang kua in a kangsak hiam?

records.english: Nobody — the toaster's timer is broken.
records.zomi: Kuamah — moh kanna set' nai a sia hi.

records.english: Why are you soaking the beans tonight?
records.zomi: Bang hangin tuni zanin be tui sung ah na koih hiam?

records.english: So that they cook faster tomorrow and don't upset anyone's stomach.
records.zomi: Zingciang a min manlang zawk nadingin, leh kuamah' gil a na lo nadingin.

records.english: If you could learn one dish from your grandmother, which would it be?
records.zomi: Na pi pan an khat na sin thei leh koi ahi ding hiam?

records.english: Her pumpkin soup, which nobody else in the family has ever managed to copy.
records.zomi: A mai an tui, innkuan sung-a kuamah in a bawl zo ngei loh.

records.english: What's the purpose of letting the dough rest?
records.zomi: Moh tawm a tawlsak pen bang adingin ahi hiam?

records.english: It gives the yeast time to work, so the bread comes out soft and light.
records.zomi: Moh khamna in a sep nading hun a ngah a, moh a nem-in a zang hi.

records.english: Why are you cooking so much on a Sunday evening?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Nipini nitak in an tam lua na huan hiam?

records.english: I'm preparing lunches for the whole week so that I don't have to cook after work.
records.zomi: Nasep khit ciangin an ka huan lo nadingin kal bup adingin sun an ka bawl khol hi.

records.english: What should I do with the fish bones?
records.zomi: Nga guhte bang ka hih ding hiam?

records.english: Put them in a pot with water and make a stock for tomorrow.
records.zomi: Tui tawh beel sung ah koih inla, zingciang adingin a tui bawl in.

records.english: How did the cake turn out so flat?
records.zomi: Bang hangin cake a pai mahmah hiam?

records.english: I forgot to add the baking powder.
records.zomi: Baking powder koih ka mangngilh hi.

records.english: Why do many families here still cook over wood rather than gas?
records.zomi: Bang hangin hih mun-a innkuan tampi in gas sangin sing tawh an a huan lai uh hiam?

records.english: Wood is cheaper in the villages, and many cooks believe it gives the food a better flavor.
records.zomi: Khua ah sing a neem zaw a, an huan tampi in an a tui zaw sak hi, a ci uh hi.

records.english: Had you tasted the dish before serving it, would you have noticed the salt?
records.zomi: Na pia ma-in an na tet le, cii na thei ding hiam?

records.english: Certainly, and I'd have added rice to balance it rather than serving it as it was.
records.zomi: Thei mahmah ding ing, a om bangin pia sangin a kibatsak nadingin buh ka behlap ding hi.

records.english: How do you manage to cook for twenty relatives in such a small kitchen?
records.zomi: Hih bang an huanna neu ah sanggam sawmnih adingin bangci-in an na huan thei hiam?

records.english: By preparing most of the food the night before and borrowing pots from every neighbor on the street.
records.zomi: An a tamzaw zan ma-in bawl khol-in, lampi bup-a inn veng khempeuh pan beel ngetsak-in.

records.english: What do you think children learn by helping to prepare meals?
records.zomi: An bawlna ah huh tawh naupangte in bang a sin uh in na ngaihsun hiam?

records.english: Patience, how to follow instructions, and respect for the work that goes into every plate.
records.zomi: Thuakzawhna, thupiak zui dan, leh kuang khat ciat ah a kihel nasep zahtakna.

records.english: Is it all right to freeze the leftover stew?
records.zomi: An nusia a hiam a khalsak leh a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, as long as it's cooled down first and eaten within a month.
records.zomi: Hoih hi, a masa-in a vot khit a, kha khat sungin ne leh.

records.english: Why can't we use the new pan on high heat?
records.zomi: Bang hangin bel thak mei hat tungah i zang thei kei hiam?

records.english: The instructions say high heat will damage the coating.
records.zomi: Mei hat in a khuhna a susia ding hi, ci-in zat dan lai in a ci hi.

records.english: What would happen if you left the yogurt out overnight?
records.zomi: Zan bup yogurt pua ah na nusia leh bang a piang ding hiam?

records.english: In this heat it would probably spoil, so it's safer to keep it in the fridge.
records.zomi: Hih bang lum ah a sia kha ding ahih manin khal bawm sung ah koih leh a bit zaw hi.

records.english: Why did the jam jars crack?
records.zomi: Bang hangin jam bel te a kek hiam?

records.english: They were cold when we poured the hot jam into them.
records.zomi: Jam sa i sun lut laitakin a vot lai uh hi.

records.english: What did the cookery teacher tell you about knives?
records.zomi: An bawl saya in namsau thu bang hong hilh hiam?

records.english: She told us to curl our fingers under when we chop and never to leave a knife in the washing-up water.
records.zomi: I at laitakin i khutzungte kawi-in, kuang silna tui sung ah namsau nusia ngei lo dingin hong hilh hi.

records.english: What happened to the rice?
records.zomi: Buh bang a piang hiam?

records.english: It stuck to the bottom of the pot because the heat was too high.
records.zomi: Mei a sa lua ahih manin beel nuai ah a belh hi.

records.english: May I use your oven while mine is being repaired?
records.zomi: Keima' kibawlsiang laitakin na oven ka zang thei ding hiam?

records.english: You may, and stay for a cup of tea while it bakes.
records.zomi: Na zang thei hi, a min laitakin tea haai khat dawn dingin om in.

records.english: Are children allowed to use the big knife?
records.zomi: Naupangte in namsau lian a zang thei uh hiam?

records.english: Not until they're older, but you can cut the bananas with this small one.
records.zomi: A upat zawk dong thei lo uh hi, ahi zongin hih neu tawh nahtang na at thei hi.

records.english: Why do you wash the chicken separately from the vegetables?
records.zomi: Bang hangin aksa anteh tawh kikhen-in na sil hiam?

records.english: So that the raw juices don't spread to food we eat uncooked.
records.zomi: A min lo-a i nek ding an tungah a hing tui a zel lo nadingin.

records.english: Can the guests help in the kitchen?
records.zomi: Khualte in an huanna ah a huh thei uh hiam?

records.english: In my mother's house, guests sit down and rest, and that's the rule.
records.zomi: Ka nu' inn ah khualte a tu-in a tawldam uh a, tua pen thupiak ahi hi.

records.english: Which of you can tell me what we do when we hear the bell?
records.zomi: Note lak ah kua in khawngging i zak ciangin bang i hih ding hiam hong gen thei ding hiam?

records.english: Remember to thank your teacher before you come home, and tell her your name again in case she's forgotten.
records.zomi: Inn na hong ma-in na saya kiangah lungdam gen ding phawk inla, a mangngilh kha leh na min kik in gen in.

records.english: My father had made me a wooden pencil box, and I was very proud of it.
records.zomi: Ka pa in sing khedal bawm khat hong bawl sak a, ka kisaktheih mahmah hi.

records.english: When my daughter started school, she insisted on carrying her own lunch box.
records.zomi: Ka tanu sang a kah kipat ciangin amah mah in a sun an bawm a tawi nuam hi.

records.english: At the gate she turned round, waved, and walked in without looking back.
records.zomi: Kongpi ah a kihei a, a khut a vai a, nung lam en lo-in a lut hi.

records.english: I was the one who cried all the way home.
records.zomi: Inn dong a kap pa keimah ka hi hi.

records.english: Could you help me tie my shoes before we go outside?
records.zomi: Pua i pai ma-in ka khedap khih dingin hong huh thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Were you nervous on your first day?
records.zomi: Na ni masa pen-in na lau hiam?

records.english: Very, because I didn't know a single child in the class.
records.zomi: Ka lau mahmah hi, kilasi sung-a naupang khat zong ka thei kei ahih manin.

records.english: The more questions I asked on that first day, the more patient the teacher seemed to become.
records.zomi: Tua ni masa pen-in dotna ka dot tam semsem ciangin saya a thuakzawh semsem bang hi.

records.english: At my school, new pupils were allowed to go home an hour early during the first week.
records.zomi: Ka sang ah kal masa pen sungin sangnaupang thakte nai khat ma-in inn a ciah thei uh hi.

records.english: How did you get to school when you were little?
records.zomi: Na neu lai-in sang ah bangci-in na pai hiam?

records.english: My father took me on the back of his bicycle, and I held on to his shirt.
records.zomi: Ka pa in a siiksakol nung lam ah hong tuangsak a, a angki ka len hi.

records.english: If schools gave every new child an older partner, far fewer of them would spend their first day in tears.
records.zomi: Sangte in naupang thak khat ciat upa zaw lawm khat a piak uh leh, tampi zaw in a ni masa uh kap-in a zang kei ding uh hi.

records.english: Why did the teacher let you keep your hat on?
records.zomi: Bang hangin saya in na lukhu hong bulhsak hiam?

records.english: It was raining when we arrived, and she said I could take it off once my hair was dry.
records.zomi: I tun ciangin guah a zu a, ka sam a keu ciangin ka sut thei hi, a ci hi.

records.english: The teacher wrote our names on little cards so that she could learn them quickly.
records.zomi: Manlang taka a theih theih nadingin saya in card neu tungah i min a gelh hi.

records.english: Would you like me to walk you to your classroom?
records.zomi: Na kilasi dong kong paipih ding hiam?

records.english: You might feel shy at first, but by Friday you'll know everyone's name.
records.zomi: A masa-in na zak kha ding hi, ahi zongin Laithai ni ciangin mi khempeuh' min na thei ding hi.

records.english: Nobody had told me that I would need my own cup, so the girl beside me let me share hers.
records.zomi: Keimah' haai ka kisap ding kuamah in hong hilh kei uh ahih manin ka kiang-a numei naupang in amah' haai hong zangsak hi.

records.english: My grandmother sewed my school bag from an old rice sack so that I wouldn't have to carry my books in my arms.
records.zomi: Laibu ka ban tawh ka pua lo nadingin ka pi in buh ip lui pan sang ip hong khui sak hi.

records.english: Our teacher asked each of us to bring one thing from home that made us feel happy.
records.zomi: I saya in i khat ciat inn pan hong lungdamsak bangmah khat tawi dingin hong ngen hi.

records.english: Rather than starting with lessons, our teacher spent the whole first morning teaching us songs and games.
records.zomi: Hilhnate tawh kipan sangin i saya in zingsang masa bup la leh kimawlnate hong hilh hi.

records.english: Looking back, I suspect that the teacher was almost as nervous as we were, since it was her first year too.
records.zomi: Nung lam en kik-in, a kum masa pen zong ahih manin saya zong eite bang dek-in a lau kha ding in ka ngaihsun hi.

records.english: Shall we take a photo of you in your new uniform before we leave?
records.zomi: I pai ma-in na sang puan thak tawh lim khat i la ding hiam?

records.english: Everybody, put your hand up if this is your first time in a classroom.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, kilasi sung ah a masa pen-a na om uh hi leh na khut uh dom un.

records.english: On my first day at school, my mother walked me to the gate and held my hand very tightly.
records.zomi: Sang ka kah ni masa pen-in ka nu in kongpi dong hong paipih a, ka khut a len cip hi.

records.english: I didn't want to let go, so I cried until a teacher came out to meet us.
records.zomi: Khah ka deih kei ahih manin saya khat hong dawn dingin a pai khiat dong ka kap hi.

records.english: She knelt down, gave me a red crayon, and asked me to draw my house for her.
records.zomi: A khukdin a, crayon san khat hong pia a, a adingin ka inn lim gelh dingin hong ngen hi.

records.english: By lunchtime I had forgotten all about crying.
records.zomi: Sun an hun ciangin ka kap thu ka mangngilh kim hi.

records.english: Having grown up on a farm far from other children, I had never seen so many people my own age in one place.
records.zomi: Naupang dangte pan a gamla lo ah ka khan ahih manin ka kum kibang mi tam hih bang mun khat ah ka mu ngei kei hi.

records.english: Parents are welcome to stay until the first bell, but after that the children settle better on their own.
records.zomi: Nu leh pate khawngging masa dong a om thei uh hi, ahi zongin tua khit ciangin naupangte amau bek in a om hoih zaw uh hi.

records.english: Whoever designed our classroom had painted animals on every wall, which made it feel less frightening.
records.zomi: I kilasi a gelpa in bang khempeuh ah ganhingte lim a gelh a, tua in a lauhuai tawmsak hi.

records.english: Not until I was much older did I realize how much my parents had sacrificed to buy my first uniform.
records.zomi: Ka upat mahmah ciang bek ka sang puan masa pen lei dingin ka nu leh ka pa in bangzah a sung hiam ka thei hi.

records.english: I brought a small stone from the river near our house, and I kept it in my pocket all year.
records.zomi: I inn kiang-a gun pan suang neu khat ka tawi a, kum bup ka ip sung ah ka koih hi.

records.english: Good morning, children — please hang your bags on the hooks and sit on the carpet.
records.zomi: Zingpha, naupangte — na ip uh khaina ah khai un a, tuutphah tungah tu un.

records.english: What did you like best about your first day?
records.zomi: Na ni masa pen-in bang na deih pen hiam?

records.english: Painting with my fingers, and the songs we sang before going home.
records.zomi: Khutzung tawh lim zeek, leh inn i ciah ma-a i la sak.

records.english: A new boy once arrived in my class halfway through the term, speaking only a few words of our language.
records.zomi: Khatvei term kimlai-in i pau kammal tawmno bek a thei naupang pasal thak khat ka kilasi ah a hong tung hi.

records.english: I asked two children to look after him and to show him how everything worked.
records.zomi: Naupang nih amah kem dingin, khempeuh a sep dan etsak dingin ka ngen hi.

records.english: Within a month, he was helping the next new pupil in exactly the same way.
records.zomi: Kha khat sungin amah in sangnaupang thak zom tua bang mahmah in a huh hi.

records.english: What I remember most about my first day is the sound of thirty children talking at once.
records.zomi: Ka ni masa pen-a ka phawk pen pen naupang sawmthum khatvei-a kiho ging ahi hi.

records.english: Please write your child's name inside every piece of clothing.
records.zomi: Puan khat ciat sung ah na ta' min gelh un.

records.english: My older sister promised to wait for me at the gate after school, and she kept her promise.
records.zomi: Ka u nu in sang khit ciangin kongpi ah hong ngak dingin a kiciam a, a kiciamna a zui hi.

records.english: I remember the smell of new books and chalk more clearly than the teacher's face.
records.zomi: Saya' mai sangin laibu thak leh chalk namtui ka phawk kician zaw hi.

records.english: Could you have imagined, on that first frightened morning, that you would one day become a teacher yourself?
records.zomi: Tua zingsang lauhuai masa pen-in ni khat ni ciangin nangmah zong saya na suak ding hi, cih na ngaihsun thei ding hiam?

records.english: The headmaster rang a bell to tell us that it was time to line up.
records.zomi: Sang makaipa in kikhai dingin hun a tung hi, ci-in khawngging a ging sak hi.

records.english: Is it all right if I stay with him for the first half hour?
records.zomi: Nai khen masa sungin a kiang ah ka om leh a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: Our class was taken on a walk around the school so that we would know where everything was.
records.zomi: Khempeuh koi ah a om hiam i theih nadingin i kilasi sang kim ah vak dingin kipaipih hi.

records.english: A boy called Nang shared his mango with me at break, and we have been friends ever since.
records.zomi: Nang kici naupang pasal khat in tawlngak hun ah a haigah hong hawm a, tua pan kipan i kilawm hi.

records.english: May I go to the toilet, please?
records.zomi: Ek inn ah ka pai thei ding hiam?

records.english: My brother and I started school on the same day, even though he was a year older.
records.zomi: Kei leh ka sanggam pasal kum khat a upa zaw hangin ni kibang mah ah sang i kah kipan hi.

records.english: The school was an hour's walk from our village, across two rivers.
records.zomi: Sang pen i khua pan nai khat kalsuan, gun nih kan ahi hi.

records.english: On the way, we crossed the deeper river on our uncle's shoulders.
records.zomi: Lampi ah gun thuk zaw pen i pa neu' liang tungah i kan hi.

records.english: When we arrived, our clothes were wet, but nobody laughed at us.
records.zomi: I tun ciangin i puan a dikdek a, ahi zongin kuamah in hong nui kei uh hi.

records.english: Had my mother not packed my favorite biscuits, I might never have stopped crying that morning.
records.zomi: Ka nu in ka deih pen biscuit a thuk kei le, tua zingsang ka kap tawp ngei kei kha ding hi.

records.english: Although I could barely hold a pencil, I was determined to write my name before the day was over.
records.zomi: Khedal ka len zo dek kei hangin ni a bei ma-in ka min gelh dingin ka hanciam hi.

records.english: Who would like to show the new girl where the water tap is?
records.zomi: Numei naupang thak kiangah tui khuk koi ah a om hiam kua in a etsak nuam hiam?

records.english: Can I sit next to my cousin?
records.zomi: Ka sanggam kiang ah ka tu thei ding hiam?

records.english: My grandson tells me that his first day was boring, which I take as a sign that it went well.
records.zomi: Ka tu in a ni masa pen a nuam kei hi, hong ci a, tua pen a hoih takin a pai hi, cih lim in ka ngaihsun hi.

records.english: What made you change your order at the last minute?
records.zomi: Bang in a nunung pen hun ciangin na ngetna hong laihsak hiam?

records.english: I saw the next table's dumplings and couldn't resist.
records.zomi: A kiang dawhkan-a dumpling ka mu a, ka thuak zo kei hi.

records.english: Why did the owner give us free tea?
records.zomi: Bang hangin a neipa in a man om lo tea hong pia hiam?

records.english: Our food took almost an hour, so he wanted to apologize.
records.zomi: I an nai khat dek a sawt ahih manin maisak a ngen nuam hi.

records.english: Who ordered the cake with candles?
records.zomi: Khawimeivaak nei cake kua in a ngen hiam?

records.english: Your colleagues did, to surprise you on your birthday.
records.zomi: Na pianni-in lamdang na sak nadingin na nasem lawmte in.

records.english: Is it all right to order only starters?
records.zomi: An masa bek ngen a hoih hiam?

records.english: Certainly, and many people share three or four between them.
records.zomi: Hoih mahmah hi, mi tampi in thum li a kihawm uh hi.

records.english: How did the kitchen get so far behind tonight?
records.zomi: Tuni zanin an huanna bangci-in a nun lua hiam?

records.english: Two cooks called in sick, and a coach full of tourists arrived without booking.
records.zomi: An huan nih a dam kei uh a, ngen lo-in khualzin bus lian khat a hong tung hi.

records.english: Can we bring our own drinks?
records.zomi: Eima' dawn ding i tawi thei ding hiam?

records.english: Not here, I'm afraid — the restaurant only serves its own.
records.zomi: Hih ah thei lo hi — anneekna inn in amah' te bek a zuak hi.

records.english: Why aren't children allowed in the restaurant after nine?
records.zomi: Bang hangin nai kua zawh ciangin anneekna inn ah naupangte kiphal lo hiam?

records.english: The owner wants the late evening to be quiet for couples, so he made it a rule last year.
records.zomi: Zan nitak lam pen kiteen nihte adingin a dai a deih ahih manin kum nung in a neipa in thupiak a bawl hi.

records.english: Which of these dishes is the least spicy?
records.zomi: Hih ante lak ah koi in a ha tawm pen hiam?

records.english: The chicken with cashews, which even children enjoy.
records.zomi: Cashew tawh aksa, naupangte in zong a deih uh.

records.english: Is it rude to send food back to the kitchen?
records.zomi: An huanna ah an pia kik pen zahtakna om lo ahi hiam?

records.english: Not if you explain politely what's wrong, and most cooks would rather know than lose a customer.
records.zomi: Bang a sia hiam nem takin na gen siang leh hi lo hi, an huan tamzaw in lei mi a mansuah sangin a theih a deih zaw uh hi.

records.english: How do you handle a customer who keeps changing his order?
records.zomi: A ngetna a laih den lei mi khat bangci-in na khoih hiam?

records.english: I write down every change and read the final order back to him before it goes to the kitchen.
records.zomi: Laihna khempeuh ka gelh a, an huanna ah a pai ma-in a ngetna nunung a kiangah ka sim kik hi.

records.english: What makes ordering in a busy street market different from ordering in a restaurant?
records.zomi: Mi tam lampi zuakna mun-a ngetna leh anneekna inn-a ngetna bang in a kilamdang sak hiam?

records.english: In the market you point, smile, and pay straight away, while in a restaurant there's a menu and a bill at the end.
records.zomi: Zuakna mun ah na lak a, na nui a, a man takin na pia a, anneekna inn ah an list leh a tawp ah bill a om hi.

records.english: How long will our food take?
records.zomi: I an bangzah a sawt ding hiam?

records.english: About twenty minutes, because everything is cooked fresh.
records.zomi: Minit sawmnih bang, khempeuh a thak-in kihuan ahih manin.

records.english: If you could order anything at all for your last meal, what would it be?
records.zomi: Na an nunung pen adingin bangpeuh na ngen thei leh bang ahi ding hiam?

records.english: My grandmother's chicken soup, which no restaurant has ever managed to copy.
records.zomi: Ka pi' aksa tui, anneekna inn khatpeuh in a bawl zo ngei loh.

records.english: What should I order if I've never tried the local food before?
records.zomi: Hih mun an ka ne ngei kei leh bang ka ngen ding hiam?

records.english: Start with the mixed plate, so that you can taste a little of everything.
records.zomi: Kihel kuang tawh kipan in, khempeuh tawmno na tet theih nadingin.

records.english: Why do some people always order the same dish, wherever they go?
records.zomi: Bang hangin mi khenkhatte in koi peuh ah a pai zongun an kibang mah a ngen tawntung uh hiam?

records.english: They'd rather be sure of enjoying their meal than risk being disappointed by something new.
records.zomi: Bangmah thak in a lungkiasak kha ding sangin a nek uh a deih ding uh kician a deih zaw uh hi.

records.english: Why did the waiter take my plate back to the kitchen?
records.zomi: Bang hangin an zuakpa in ka kuang an huanna ah a tawi kik hiam?

records.english: The chef saw that the fish was undercooked and asked for it to be done again.
records.zomi: An huan lian in nga a min kim nai lo a mu a, kik-in huan dingin a ngen hi.

records.english: Why did you ask them to leave the chili out?
records.zomi: Bang hangin malcha koih lo dingin na ngen hiam?

records.english: My stomach can't handle too much chili these days.
records.zomi: Tu hun ciangin ka gil in malcha tam lua a thuak zo kei hi.

records.english: Did you order the extra rice?
records.zomi: Buh behlap na ngen hiam?

records.english: I did, but it hasn't arrived yet.
records.zomi: Ka ngen hi, ahi zongin a tung nai kei hi.

records.english: Why are the prices on the board different from the menu?
records.zomi: Bang hangin bang tung-a man an list sung bangin a kibang kei hiam?

records.english: The board was updated this morning, but the printed menus haven't been changed yet.
records.zomi: Bang tung-a man tuni zingsangin a kilai a, ahi zongin a kikhen an listte kilai nai lo hi.

records.english: Can you make the curry without onions?
records.zomi: Lothaang om lo-in curry na bawl thei ding hiam?

records.english: I'll ask the chef, but some of the sauce is prepared in advance.
records.zomi: An huan lian ka dong ding hi, ahi zongin a tui khenkhat a ma-in kibawl khol hi.

records.english: Can I pay for my friend's meal without her knowing?
records.zomi: Ka lawm a theih loh-in a an man ka pia thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, just tell me quietly at the counter before you leave.
records.zomi: Thei hi, na pai ma-in sum piakna mun ah dai takin hong gen bek in.

records.english: What did the waiter say when you asked for the special?
records.zomi: A tuamtuam an na ngen ciangin an zuakpa in bang a ci hiam?

records.english: He said, "Sorry, the last one was sold ten minutes ago."
records.zomi: “Hong maisak in, a nunung pen minit sawm paisa-in a kizuak khin hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: Last night we ordered pizza for the whole family, but the delivery driver went to the wrong street.
records.zomi: Zanni zanin innkuan bup adingin pizza i ngen a, ahi zongin a puakpa lampi dik lo ah a pai hi.

records.english: By the time it arrived, it was cold, so the shop gave us the next one free.
records.zomi: A tun ciangin a vot khin ahih manin dawr in a zom pen a man om lo-in hong pia hi.

records.english: Did the delivery driver bring everything we ordered?
records.zomi: A puakpa in i ngen khempeuh a tawi hiam?

records.english: Everything except the drinks, which he'd left in the car.
records.zomi: Khempeuh, dawn dingte bek a mawtaw sung ah a nusia hi.

records.english: Why are you ordering in such a quiet voice?
records.zomi: Bang hangin dai mahmah takin na ngen hiam?

records.english: I don't want my children to hear that I'm ordering dessert for myself.
records.zomi: Keimah adingin an lim ka ngen hi, cih ka tate in a zak ding uh ka deih kei hi.

records.english: What happened to my order?
records.zomi: Ka ngetna bang a piang hiam?

records.english: It was given to another table by mistake, and the kitchen is making yours again now.
records.zomi: Khialh-in dawhkan dang ah kipia a, an huanna in na adingin a huan kik hi.

records.english: Who spilled the soup on the tablecloth?
records.zomi: Dawhkan puan tungah an tui kua in a sun hiam?

records.english: Nobody — the bowl slid when the table wobbled.
records.zomi: Kuamah — dawhkan a kihuk ciangin kuang a liim hi.

records.english: What are you having?
records.zomi: Bang na ne ding hiam?

records.english: The fried noodles, because I had rice for lunch.
records.zomi: An-ngum kikang, sun an ah buh ka ne khin ahih manin.

records.english: What did you think of the new café on the corner?
records.zomi: Lampi kiheina-a cafe thak bang na sa hiam?

records.english: The coffee was excellent, but the cakes were rather dry.
records.zomi: Khawfi a hoih mahmah hi, ahi zongin cake te a keu tawmno hi.

records.english: Had you read the menu more carefully, would you have ordered the octopus?
records.zomi: An list pilvang zaw takin na sim le, octopus na ngen ding hiam?

records.english: Definitely not, since I thought I was ordering fried fish.
records.zomi: Ngen lo mahmah ding ing, nga kikang ka ngen in ka ngaihsun hi.

records.english: Who broke the glass in the kitchen?
records.zomi: An huanna ah glass kua in a sukek hiam?

records.english: Nobody broke it — it slipped off the wet tray as I was carrying it.
records.zomi: Kuamah in a sukek kei hi — ka tawi laitakin kuang lian dikdek tung pan a liim hi.

records.english: Do you really want me to stay another night?
records.zomi: Zan khat behlap ka om ding na deih taktak hiam?

records.english: Yes, I really do want you to stay — the children love having you here.
records.zomi: Deih hi, na om ding ka deih mahmah hi — naupangte in hih ah na om a deih mahmah uh hi.

records.english: Where should I put my shoes?
records.zomi: Ka khedap koi ah ka koih ding hiam?

records.english: Just leave them by the door, like everyone else.
records.zomi: Mi dang khempeuh bangin kongkhak kiang ah nusia bek in.

records.english: Can we let the guests sleep in tomorrow?
records.zomi: Zingciang khualte a ihmut sawt nadingun i nusia thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, and we'll keep their breakfast warm until they come down.
records.zomi: Thei hi, a hong tum dong uh zingsang an a lum takin i kem ding hi.

records.english: Was the house damaged when all those children came to stay?
records.zomi: Tua naupangte khempeuh hong om uh ciangin inn a sia hiam?

records.english: Only a little — a lamp was knocked over and a curtain was torn.
records.zomi: Tawmno bek — meivak khat a kiat a, tukvuang puan khat a kek hi.

records.english: Why did your grandmother insist on giving our guest the best bed?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na pi in i khual lupna hoih pen pia dingin a ngen den hiam?

records.english: In our family, a guest is treated better than anyone else in the house.
records.zomi: I innkuan ah khual pen inn sung-a mi dang khempeuh sangin hoih zaw-in kizang hi.

records.english: What happened to the power during dinner?
records.zomi: Nitak an laitakin meivak bang a piang hiam?

records.english: It went off in the storm, so we finished eating by candlelight.
records.zomi: Huihpi sung ah a mit ahih manin khawimeivaak tawh i nek i zo hi.

records.english: Why is there a towel on the end of my bed?
records.zomi: Bang hangin ka lupna tawp ah puan nul khat a om hiam?

records.english: My mother put it there for you, in case you want a shower after your journey.
records.zomi: Na khualzinna khit ciangin kisil na deih kha leh, ci-in ka nu in na adingin a koih hi.

records.english: What is the hardest part of hosting relatives for a long time?
records.zomi: Sanggamte hun sawt kem ah a haksa pen bang ahi hiam?

records.english: Finding moments of quiet, since someone is always wanting to talk, eat, or go somewhere.
records.zomi: Daihna hun zon, kuamah in kiho, an ne, hiam koi ah hiam pai a deih tawntung uh ahih manin.

records.english: Can I help you wash up?
records.zomi: Kuang sil dingin kong huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Absolutely not — guests don't work in this house.
records.zomi: Hi lo mahmah hi — hih inn ah khualte in na a sem kei uh hi.

records.english: Are guests allowed to smoke in the house?
records.zomi: Khualte in inn sung ah meidawn a dawn thei uh hiam?

records.english: No, but there's a chair on the porch for anyone who wants to.
records.zomi: Thei lo hi, ahi zongin a deih te adingin kongmai ah tutna khat a om hi.

records.english: Should I bring a gift when I stay with your family?
records.zomi: Na innkuan kiang ka om ciangin letsong ka tawi ding hiam?

records.english: Something small is enough, like fruit or a cake from your town.
records.zomi: Bangmah neu khat a kicing hi, theigah hiam na khua pan cake khat bang.

records.english: How do you make guests from another culture feel at home?
records.zomi: Ngeina dang pan hong khualte inn bangin bangci-in na kisaksak hiam?

records.english: I ask them what they usually eat and how they like to spend the evening, rather than guessing.
records.zomi: Ka ngaihsun sangin bang a ne den uh hiam, nitak bangci-in zang a deih uh hiam ka dong hi.

records.english: Why did the visitors leave so early?
records.zomi: Bang hangin khual hongte manlang takin a pai khia uh hiam?

records.english: Their car was blocked in by a delivery van, and they had to move it before it got dark.
records.zomi: Van puakna mawtaw in a mawtaw uh a khak a, khua a mial ma-in a suan ding uh hi.

records.english: How did the dinner go last night?
records.zomi: Zanni zan nitak an bangci-in a pai hiam?

records.english: Very well, apart from the moment the dog stole a piece of chicken from the table.
records.zomi: A hoih mahmah hi, ui in dawhkan tung pan aksa khen khat a guk hun bek simloh.

records.english: If you could host anyone at your table, who would it be?
records.zomi: Na dawhkan ah kua peuhpeuh na muak thei leh kua ahi ding hiam?

records.english: My grandparents when they were young, so that I could hear their stories while they were still new.
records.zomi: Khangno lai-a ka pu leh pite, a tangthu uh a thak lai-in ka zak theih nadingin.

records.english: How long are your in-laws staying?
records.zomi: Na sungte bangzah sawt a om ding uh hiam?

records.english: Only a week this time, but they always say that and then stay for three.
records.zomi: Tu-in kal khat bek, ahi zongin tua bangin a ci tawntung uh a, kal thum a om uh hi.

records.english: Why are the children so quiet tonight?
records.zomi: Bang hangin tuni zanin naupangte a dai mahmah uh hiam?

records.english: They've been told to be on their best behavior while the guests are here.
records.zomi: Khualte hih ah a om lai sungin a hoih pen-in om dingin kihilh uh hi.

records.english: Why did your husband stay up so late with our guests?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na pasal i khualte tawh a nai mahmah hiam?

records.english: He and your uncle were looking at old photographs and couldn't stop talking.
records.zomi: Amah leh na pa neu lim luite a en uh a, a kiho tawp zo kei uh hi.

records.english: What should we do if the guests don't like the food?
records.zomi: Khualte in an a deih kei uh leh bang i hih ding hiam?

records.english: Offer them some bread and fruit, and don't take it personally.
records.zomi: Moh leh theigah tawmno pia inla, na tungah gawhsak kei in.

records.english: Why do you always put the guests' bags in the best room before they arrive?
records.zomi: Bang hangin khualte a tun ma-un a ip uh khan hoih pen ah na koih tawntung hiam?

records.english: My mother taught me that the first thing a guest sees should tell them they were expected.
records.zomi: Khual khat in a muh masak pen in kingak hi, cih a hilh ding hi, ci-in ka nu in hong hilh hi.

records.english: Had the guests told you they were vegetarian, would you have cooked something different?
records.zomi: Khualte in sa ka ne kei hi, a ci uh le, a dang khat na huan ding hiam?

records.english: Certainly, because I'd spent hours preparing the lamb that evening and nobody could eat it.
records.zomi: Huan mahmah ding ing, tua nitak in nai tampi tuu sa ka huan a, kuamah in a ne thei kei uh hi.

records.english: Last Christmas fifteen relatives arrived, and our house had only three beds.
records.zomi: Christmas nung in sanggam sawm leh nga a hong tung uh a, i inn ah lupna thum bek a om hi.

records.english: The children slept on mats in the living room, and they still say it was the best holiday ever.
records.zomi: Naupangte tutna khan sung ah phah tungah a ihmu uh a, nopsakna hun hoih pen ahi hi, a ci lai uh hi.

records.english: Is it ever acceptable to ask guests to leave?
records.zomi: Khualte pai khia dingin ngen pen a dik ngei hiam?

records.english: Only very gently, and usually by saying that you have to get up early the next morning.
records.zomi: Nem mahmah takin bek, a tamzaw-in a zing zingsang tung ah thou ding ka hi hi, ci-in.

records.english: What do you say when guests thank you for having them?
records.zomi: Khualte in hong kem manin lungdam a gen ciangun bang na ci hiam?

records.english: I tell them that our door is always open, which is what my parents used to say.
records.zomi: I kongkhak a kihong tawntung hi, ka ci a, tua pen ka nu leh ka pa' gen den ahi hi.

records.english: What did your father say when the guests praised his cooking?
records.zomi: Khualte in na pa' an huan a phat ciangun bang a ci hiam?

records.english: He said, "It's only rice and beans," but he was smiling all evening.
records.zomi: “Buh leh be bek ahi hi,” a ci a, ahi zongin nitak bup a nui hi.

records.english: Did the guests like the room you prepared for them?
records.zomi: Na bawl sak khan khualte in a deih uh hiam?

records.english: They loved it, especially the flowers on the windowsill.
records.zomi: A deih mahmah uh a, a diakin tukvuang tung-a pakte.

records.english: Is it all right to ask guests to take their shoes off?
records.zomi: Khualte khedap sut dingin ngen a hoih hiam?

records.english: In our house it is, and most people do it without being asked.
records.zomi: I inn ah hoih hi, mi tamzaw in ngen lo-in a sut uh hi.

records.english: Who's going to sit next to the guest of honor?
records.zomi: Khual thupi kiang ah kua in a tu ding hiam?

records.english: Your father, because they were at school together.
records.zomi: Na pa, sang ah a kah khawm uh ahih manin.

records.english: Why did you light the fire so early?
records.zomi: Bang hangin mei manlang mahmah-in na hal hiam?

records.english: Our guests are coming from the warm south, and I didn't want them to feel cold.
records.zomi: I khualte simlam lum pan a hong uh a, a vot ding uh ka deih kei hi.

records.english: How do you cook for guests whose preferences you don't know?
records.zomi: A deihna na theih loh khualte adingin bangci-in an na huan hiam?

records.english: I make several simple dishes, so that everyone can find at least one thing they enjoy.
records.zomi: An baih tampi ka huan a, mi khempeuh in a deih khat bek a mu thei uh hi.

records.english: Are there any foods you simply can't stand?
records.zomi: Na thuak zawh loh an a om hiam?

records.english: Raw onions — even the smell makes me feel ill.
records.zomi: Lothaang ham — a namtui in zong hong dam losak hi.

records.english: Which fruit do you like best?
records.zomi: Koi theigah na deih pen hiam?

records.english: Mangoes, but only when they're perfectly ripe.
records.zomi: Haigah, ahi zongin a min kim ciang bek.

records.english: Why do tastes change as people grow older?
records.zomi: Bang hangin mite a upat ciangun an tui theihna a kilai hiam?

records.english: Some people say our sense of taste becomes less sharp, so strong flavors that once seemed too much become pleasant.
records.zomi: Mi khenkhatte in i an tui theihna a hiam lo zaw ahih manin ma-a a hat lua bang a kisa an tui hatte a nuam suak hi, a ci uh hi.

records.english: What do you usually have for breakfast?
records.zomi: Zingsang an ah bang na ne den hiam?

records.english: Just tea and a piece of bread, because I'm never hungry early.
records.zomi: Tea leh moh khen khat bek, zingsang tung ah ka gilkial ngei kei ahih manin.

records.english: Why do you always order the same dish here?
records.zomi: Bang hangin hih ah an kibang mah na ngen tawntung hiam?

records.english: It's the best thing on the menu, so why change?
records.zomi: An list tung-a a hoih pen ahi a, bang hangin ka laih ding hiam?

records.english: What did you think of the food when you first arrived here?
records.zomi: Hih ah na tun masak ciangin an bang na sa hiam?

records.english: Everything tasted too sweet at first, but now I put sugar in everything myself.
records.zomi: A masa-in khempeuh a khum lua hi, ahi zongin tu-in keimah in khempeuh ah sugar ka koih hi.

records.english: How did the children like the new dish at school?
records.zomi: Sang-a an thak naupangte in bangci-in a deih uh hiam?

records.english: Most of them left it on their plates, so the cook won't make it again.
records.zomi: A tamzaw in a kuang uh tungah a nusia uh ahih manin an huanpa in a huan kik nawn kei ding hi.

records.english: What happened to all the strawberries?
records.zomi: Strawberry khempeuh bang a piang hiam?

records.english: They were eaten by the birds before we could pick them.
records.zomi: I lak ma-un vasate in a ne uh hi.

records.english: If you could eat only one cuisine for the rest of your life, which would you choose?
records.zomi: Na nuntak sung bup an namkhat bek na ne thei leh koi na teel ding hiam?

records.english: Our own village cooking, though I'd miss the noodle soups I discovered in the city.
records.zomi: Eima' khua an, khuapi ah ka muh an-ngum tuite ka lungngai ding hangin.

records.english: Why did your grandfather stop eating salty food?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na pu in an al a nek tawp hiam?

records.english: His doctor told him to cut down because of his blood pressure.
records.zomi: A sisan hatna hangin tawmsak dingin a siavuan in a hilh hi.

records.english: Why is your sister so fussy about her food?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na sanggam nu a an teel mahmah hiam?

records.english: She was very ill as a child, and since then she's been careful about what she eats.
records.zomi: Naupan lai-in a dam lo mahmah a, tua pan kipan a nek ding pilvang takin a teel hi.

records.english: Why do some children refuse to eat anything new?
records.zomi: Bang hangin naupang khenkhatte in an thak khatpeuh ne a nial uh hiam?

records.english: Many of them are cautious by nature, and they need to see a food several times before they'll even touch it.
records.zomi: A tamzaw amau ngeina-in a pilvang uh a, a khoih ma-un an khat vei tampi a mu masa ding uh a kisam hi.

records.english: When did you start liking coffee?
records.zomi: Bang ciangin khawfi na deih kipan hiam?

records.english: At university, when I needed it to stay awake for exams.
records.zomi: Sangpi ah, sitna adingin ka mit khak lo nadingin ka kisap ciangin.

records.english: When I was eight, I refused to eat anything but rice and eggs for a whole year.
records.zomi: Kum giat ka phak ciangin kum bup buh leh aktui simloh bangmah ka ne nuam kei hi.

records.english: Then my grandmother taught me to cook her vegetable soup, and suddenly I wanted to taste everything.
records.zomi: Tua ciangin ka pi in a anteh tui huan dan hong hilh a, khempeuh tet ka deih pah hi.

records.english: Kids, who wants pancakes and who wants eggs?
records.zomi: Naupangte, kua in pancake a deih a, kua in aktui a deih hiam?

records.english: Pancakes for all of us, please!
records.zomi: I khempeuh adingin pancake, hong pia un!

records.english: Do you like your rice soft or a little firm?
records.zomi: Na buh a nem hiam, tawmno a khauh deih zaw hiam?

records.english: A little firm, the way my mother used to cook it.
records.zomi: Tawmno a khauh, ka nu' huan den bangin.

records.english: Had you tried the durian before buying a whole one, would you still have bought it?
records.zomi: Bup khat na lei ma-in durian na tet le, na lei lai ding hiam?

records.english: Certainly not, since one bite was enough to convince me I'd made a mistake.
records.zomi: Lei lo mahmah ding ing, khatvei ka kek in ka khialh hi, cih hong theisak ahih manin.

records.english: What happened to the cheese in the fridge?
records.zomi: Khal bawm sung-a cheese bang a piang hiam?

records.english: It went moldy while we were away on holiday.
records.zomi: Nopsakna khualzinna ah i pai laitakin a mu hi.

records.english: Why does your mother cook two different dinners every night?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na nu in zan simin nitak an tuamtuam nih a huan hiam?

records.english: My father won't eat anything spicy, and the rest of us can't eat without chili.
records.zomi: Ka pa in a ha bangmah a ne nuam kei a, a dang i khempeuh malcha om lo-in i ne thei kei hi.

records.english: Can you eat anything spicy?
records.zomi: A ha bangmah na ne thei hiam?

records.english: A little, but not as hot as the curry your brother makes.
records.zomi: Tawmno, ahi zongin na sanggam pasal' bawl curry bangin a ha kei leh.

records.english: Which do you prefer, river fish or sea fish?
records.zomi: Koi na deih zaw hiam, gun nga hiam tuipi nga hiam?

records.english: River fish, because that's what I grew up eating.
records.zomi: Gun nga, ka khanna-a ka nek ahih manin.

records.english: Why don't you eat pork anymore?
records.zomi: Bang hangin vok sa na ne nawn kei hiam?

records.english: I stopped after I read about how the pigs on big farms are kept.
records.zomi: Lo lian-a vokte bangci-in a kikem uh hiam ka sim khit ciangin ka tawp hi.

records.english: Is it true that your husband won't eat anything green?
records.zomi: Na pasal in a eng bangmah a ne kei hi, cih a tak hiam?

records.english: It's true, but he's finally started eating peas.
records.zomi: A tak hi, ahi zongin a tawp-in be a ne kipan hi.

records.english: What did your son say when he tasted the bitter melon?
records.zomi: Na tapa in khatthak a tet ciangin bang a ci hiam?

records.english: He said, "Never again," and drank a whole glass of water.
records.zomi: “Ne nawn ngei lo ding,” a ci a, tui glass khat bup a dawn hi.

records.english: Should I tell my hosts that I don't eat meat?
records.zomi: Ka hong kemtute kiangah sa ka ne kei hi, ci-in ka hilh ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, before the meal, so that they have time to prepare something else.
records.zomi: Hilh in, an nek ma-in, a dang bawl nading hun a neih theih nadingun.

records.english: Everyone, does anyone not eat fish?
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, kuamah in nga a ne lo a om hiam?

records.english: I'm allergic to shellfish, but ordinary fish is fine.
records.zomi: Tuipi-a ngagak te ka ne thei kei hi, ahi zongin nga pangai a hoih hi.

records.english: Is it polite to refuse a dish that the host has made especially for you?
records.zomi: Hong kemtu in na adingin a tuam-a a bawl an khat nial pen a zahtakhuai hiam?

records.english: It's better to take a small amount and thank them sincerely than to refuse it outright.
records.zomi: Nial sangin tawmno la-in thuman takin lungdam gen a hoih zaw hi.

records.english: What made you start eating more vegetables?
records.zomi: Bang in anteh tam zaw ne dingin hong kipatsak hiam?

records.english: My daughter grows them in the garden, and I didn't want them to go to waste.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in huan sung ah a suan a, a mang ding ka deih kei hi.

records.english: Are you sure you don't want any chicken?
records.zomi: Aksa na deih lo taktak hiam?

records.english: I really do prefer the vegetables, thank you.
records.zomi: Anteh ka deih zaw taktak hi, ka lungdam hi.

records.english: Can I use a fork, or is it rude here?
records.zomi: Fork ka zang thei ding hiam, hih ah zahtakna om lo ahi hiam?

records.english: Not at all — my grandmother eats everything with a spoon anyway.
records.zomi: Hi lo mahmah hi — ka pi in khempeuh kawm tawh a ne hi.

records.english: Why did your grandmother cry at the dinner table?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na pi an nekna dawhkan ah a kap hiam?

records.english: My brother cooked her mother's recipe, and it tasted exactly as she remembered.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in a nu' an huan dan a huan a, a phawk bang mahmah-in a tui hi.

records.english: Who taught you to wrap the rice in leaves?
records.zomi: Buh teh tawh tuam dan kua in hong hilh hiam?

records.english: My aunt, who could wrap fifty parcels in the time it takes me to wrap ten.
records.zomi: Ka ni, ka tuam sawm sung ah sawmnga a tuam thei pa.

records.english: How do you pass on traditional recipes to children who prefer fast food?
records.zomi: Fast food a deih zaw naupangte kiangah ngeina an huan dan bangci-in na hilh hiam?

records.english: Let them help in the kitchen, and they'll be far more willing to eat what they've made themselves.
records.zomi: An huanna ah huh sak in, amau mah in a bawl uh ne dingin a deih zaw mahmah ding uh hi.

records.english: How have family meals changed since you were a child?
records.zomi: Na naupan lai pan innkuan an nekna bangci-in a kilai hiam?

records.english: There are fewer people at the table, and phones have crept in, but the food itself has hardly changed.
records.zomi: Dawhkan ah mi a tawm zaw a, phone te a hong lut uh a, ahi zongin an mah a kilai dek kei hi.

records.english: What happened to the big cooking pot?
records.zomi: An huanna beel lian bang a piang hiam?

records.english: It cracked on the fire last year, so we use two smaller ones now.
records.zomi: Kum nung in mei tungah a kek a, tu-in a neu zaw nih i zang hi.

records.english: Why is the soup always cooked the night before?
records.zomi: Bang hangin an tui zan ma-in a kihuan tawntung hiam?

records.english: My grandmother says the flavors need time to mix, and she's never been wrong.
records.zomi: A namtuite a kihel nadingin hun a kisam hi, ci-in ka pi in a ci a, a khial ngei kei hi.

records.english: Why was the meal so late this year?
records.zomi: Bang hangin tu kum an a sawt mahmah hiam?

records.english: The rice was delayed by the floods, and it only arrived this morning.
records.zomi: Tuiciim hangin buh a nun a, tuni zingsang bek-in a tung hi.

records.english: Do you really want to learn how to make Grandma's stew?
records.zomi: Ka pi' an tui bawl dan na sin nuam taktak hiam?

records.english: I really do want to, before nobody is left who knows how.
records.zomi: Ka sin nuam mahmah hi, a thei kuamah om nawn lo ma-in.

records.english: If you could add one new tradition to your family meals, what would it be?
records.zomi: Na innkuan an nekna ah ngeina thak khat na behlap thei leh bang ahi ding hiam?

records.english: Each person would say one thing they were grateful for before we started eating.
records.zomi: I nek kipat ma-in mi khat ciat in a lungdampih thu khat a gen ding hi.

records.english: Why are there so many leftovers?
records.zomi: Bang hangin an nusia tam mahmah hiam?

records.english: Every family brought far more food than anyone could eat.
records.zomi: Innkuan khempeuh in kuamah' nek zawh sangin an tam zaw a tawi uh hi.

records.english: Is it all right if I bring a dish from my own country?
records.zomi: Keima' gam pan an khat ka tawi leh a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: We'd love that, and my aunt will want the recipe.
records.zomi: I deih mahmah ding hi, ka ni in a bawl dan a deih ding hi.

records.english: Who washes all the dishes after such a big meal?
records.zomi: Tua bang an lian khit ciangin kuangte khempeuh kua in a sil hiam?

records.english: Everyone helps, and the youngest dry the plates.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh in a huh uh a, a neu pente in kuangte a nul uh hi.

records.english: What's this little bowl of salt and chili for?
records.zomi: Cii leh malcha kuang neu hih bang adingin ahi hiam?

records.english: You dip the boiled vegetables in it before you eat them.
records.zomi: Na nek ma-in anteh kisuang hih sung ah na sun hi.

records.english: What would you do if your children stopped coming to the family meal?
records.zomi: Na tate innkuan an nekna ah a hong nawn kei uh leh bang na hih ding hiam?

records.english: I'd ask them why, and perhaps change the day, rather than insisting that everything stay the same.
records.zomi: Khempeuh a om bangin om ding ka ngen sangin bang hang hiam ka dong ding a, ni ka laih kha ding hi.

records.english: Why did you cook the chicken outside over the fire?
records.zomi: Bang hangin pua ah mei tungah aksa na huan hiam?

records.english: The smoke gives it the taste we remember from the village, which you can't get on a gas stove.
records.zomi: Meikhu in khua-a i phawk an tui a piak hi, gas meikhuk tungah na ngah thei lo.

records.english: Why does your mother grind the spices by hand?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na nu in antui namtuite a khut tawh a gaw hiam?

records.english: She uses the old stone mortar because she says the flavor is stronger.
records.zomi: A namtui a hat zaw hi, a ci ahih manin suang sum lui a zang hi.

records.english: How was the meat preserved before people had fridges?
records.zomi: Khal bawm a om ma-in sa bangci-in kikem hiam?

records.english: It was salted and smoked over the fire, and then hung from the roof.
records.zomi: Cii koih-in mei tungah meikhu tawh kiphual a, tua ciangin inn tung ah kikhai hi.

records.english: What did your father say when you brought your fiancé to the family meal?
records.zomi: Na kiteen ding pasal innkuan an nekna ah na paipih ciangin na pa in bang a ci hiam?

records.english: He said, "Sit down and eat — then we'll talk."
records.zomi: “Tu inla ne in — tua ciangin i kiho ding hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: What does your family always eat on Sunday evenings?
records.zomi: Na innkuan in Nipini nitak simin bang a ne tawntung uh hiam?

records.english: Chicken soup with rice, just as my grandparents did.
records.zomi: Buh tawh aksa tui, ka pu leh pite' hih bangmah in.

records.english: How many people came to the family meal at New Year?
records.zomi: Kum thak-a innkuan an nekna ah mi bangzah a hong hiam?

records.english: Nearly forty, including cousins we hadn't seen for years.
records.zomi: Sawmli dek, kum tampi sung i muh loh sanggamte tawh.

records.english: Who sits at the head of the table in your family?
records.zomi: Na innkuan ah dawhkan lu ah kua a tu hiam?

records.english: My grandfather, and nobody starts eating until he does.
records.zomi: Ka pu, amah a nek kipat ma-in kuamah in a ne kipan kei hi.

records.english: Had your mother not written down her recipes, would they have been lost?
records.zomi: Na nu in a an huan dan a gelh kei le, a mang ding hiam?

records.english: Most of them, since none of us had paid enough attention while she was cooking.
records.zomi: A tamzaw, a an huan laitakin i khempeuh in hoih takin i en kei ahih manin.

records.english: Why do the men cook the meat at your family gatherings?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na innkuan kikhopna ah pasalte in sa a huan uh hiam?

records.english: In our family, that's always been their job, while the women prepare the rice and vegetables.
records.zomi: I innkuan ah tua pen a nasep uh ahi tawntung a, numeite in buh leh anteh a bawl uh hi.

records.english: What do you miss most about family meals now that you live abroad?
records.zomi: Gamdang ah na om khit ciangin innkuan an nekna ah bang na lungngai pen hiam?

records.english: The noise, the arguments about politics, and the way my mother kept filling my plate.
records.zomi: Ging, ukna thu kinialna, leh ka nu in ka kuang a dimsak den dan.

records.english: What's the long wooden paddle by the fire for?
records.zomi: Mei kiang-a sing sau hih bang adingin ahi hiam?

records.english: It's for stirring the rice in the big pot, so that it doesn't burn.
records.zomi: Beel lian sung-a buh a kang lo nadingin ngom nading ahi hi.

records.english: Every harvest, my grandfather kills a pig, and the whole family spends two days cooking.
records.zomi: Buh lak simin ka pu in vok khat a go a, innkuan bup in ni nih an a huan uh hi.

records.english: On the last night, we all eat together in the yard, and the old songs are sung until midnight.
records.zomi: Zan nunung pen-in tual ah i khempeuh i ne khawm a, zanlai dong la luite kisa hi.

records.english: What do the children do while the adults are cooking?
records.zomi: Upate in an a huan laitakun naupangte in bang a hih uh hiam?

records.english: They play outside until someone calls them to set the table.
records.zomi: Dawhkan bawl dingin kuamah in a sam dong pua ah a kimawl uh hi.

records.english: Why do you think shared meals matter so much to families?
records.zomi: Bang hangin kihawm an nekna innkuante adingin a thupi mahmah in na ngaihsun hiam?

records.english: Eating together is often the only time everyone stops working and actually talks to one another.
records.zomi: Khawm-a an nek pen a tamzaw-in mi khempeuh in nasep a tawp-in a kiho taktak hun khat bek ahi hi.

records.english: Everyone, can you come and help carry the dishes outside?
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, pua ah kuangte pua dingin hong huh thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: Coming — and we'll bring the extra mats too.
records.zomi: Ka hong ding — phah behlapte zong i tawi ding hi.

records.english: Could you print this worksheet for me at your office?
records.zomi: Na office ah hih worksheet hong print sak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Why are you doing your homework in the kitchen?
records.zomi: Bang hangin an huanna ah na inn-a sep ding na sem hiam?

records.english: The light is better here, and I can ask Mom when I get stuck.
records.zomi: Hih ah meivak a hoih zaw a, ka kikhak ciangin Nu ka dong thei hi.

records.english: How long does your homework usually take?
records.zomi: Na inn-a sep ding a tamzaw-in bangzah a sawt hiam?

records.english: About an hour, unless there's an essay to write.
records.zomi: Nai khat bang, essay gelh ding a om kei leh.

records.english: I forgot my notebook at school, so I couldn't do the exercises.
records.zomi: Sang ah ka laibu ka mangngilh ahih manin sinna te ka sem thei kei hi.

records.english: You should start your assignment early so that you have time to ask questions.
records.zomi: Dotna na dot theih nading hun na neih nadingin na nasep a ma-in kipan in.

records.english: Although homework can be tiring, many teachers believe it helps children remember what they have learned.
records.zomi: Inn-a sep ding a tawlsak hangin, naupangte in a sinte uh a phawk nadingin a huh hi, ci-in saya tampi in a um uh hi.

records.english: My friend lent me his calculator because mine had stopped working.
records.zomi: Ka calculator a sem nawn kei ahih manin ka lawm in amah' hong zangsak hi.

records.english: The teacher returned our essays with comments written in green ink.
records.zomi: Saya in khuai eng tawh gelh thu tawh i essay te hong pia kik hi.

records.english: My father checks my homework every evening after work.
records.zomi: Ka pa in nasep khit ciangin nitak simin ka inn-a sep ding a en hi.

records.english: The page got torn when my little brother grabbed my book.
records.zomi: Ka nau pasal in ka laibu a lak ciangin a laimai a kek hi.

records.english: The homework was so hard that even my parents couldn't help me.
records.zomi: Inn-a sep ding a haksa lua ahih manin ka nu leh ka pa in zong hong huh zo kei hi.

records.english: Have you finished your homework yet?
records.zomi: Na inn-a sep ding na zo khin hiam?

records.english: Almost — I just have one more page of reading.
records.zomi: Zo dek — sim ding laimai khat bek a om lai hi.

records.english: Why did you get a low mark on the assignment?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na nasep ah ciamte niam na ngah hiam?

records.english: I answered the wrong question, which I only noticed when I got it back.
records.zomi: Dotna dik lo ka dawng a, hong kipiak kik ciang bek ka thei hi.

records.english: My grandmother can't read, but she always sits with me while I do my homework.
records.zomi: Ka pi in lai a sim thei kei hi, ahi zongin ka inn-a sep ding ka sep laitakin ka kiang ah a tu tawntung hi.

records.english: Would it really be so terrible to hand in the assignment a day late, given how ill you've been?
records.zomi: Na dam loh lua hangin na nasep ni khat nung zaw-a piak pen a lauhuai mahmah taktak ding hiam?

records.english: My older sister helped me with my science project last weekend.
records.zomi: Kal tawp nung in ka u nu in ka science project hong huh hi.

records.english: Rather than giving us worksheets, our new teacher asks us to interview people in our families.
records.zomi: Worksheet hong pia sangin i saya thak in i innkuan-a mite dotna dong dingin hong ngen hi.

records.english: Our class is collecting old newspapers for an art assignment.
records.zomi: I kilasi in lim zeek nasep adingin laithak luite a kaikhawm hi.

records.english: The teacher made us rewrite the whole assignment because it was so messy.
records.zomi: A buai lua ahih manin saya in i nasep bup hong gelh kiksak hi.

records.english: Don't leave your homework until Sunday night, or you'll regret it.
records.zomi: Na inn-a sep ding Nipini zan dong nusia kei in, a hi kei leh na kisik ding hi.

records.english: Who can tell me what the homework was for today?
records.zomi: Tuni adingin inn-a sep ding bang ahi hiam kua in hong gen thei ding hiam?

records.english: Copying from a friend's homework is not allowed at our school.
records.zomi: I sang ah lawm' inn-a sep ding copy pen kiphal lo hi.

records.english: I'm writing a report about the history of our village for my social studies class.
records.zomi: Ka social studies kilasi adingin i khua' tangthu thu report khat ka gelh hi.

records.english: Can I hand in my essay tomorrow instead of today?
records.zomi: Ka essay tuni sangin zingciang ka pia thei ding hiam?

records.english: What did the teacher say about your project?
records.zomi: Na project thu-ah saya in bang a ci hiam?

records.english: She said, "This is your best work so far — keep going."
records.zomi: “Tu dong na sep lak ah a hoih pen ahi hi — zom in,” a ci hi.

records.english: Some parents feel that young children are given too much homework and too little time to play.
records.zomi: Nu leh pa khenkhatte in naupang neute in inn-a sep ding a tam lua a ngah uh a, kimawl hun a tawm lua hi, a ci uh hi.

records.english: Whoever finishes the group project first should help the others in the class.
records.zomi: Pawl project a zo masa peuhpeuh in kilasi sung-a a dangte a huh ding hi.

records.english: I was asked to give a short presentation about my project in front of the class.
records.zomi: Kilasi mai ah ka project thu tom takin etsak dingin hong ngen uh hi.

records.english: Having missed a week of school through illness, Mai spent the weekend catching up on assignments.
records.zomi: Dam loh hangin sang kal khat a mansuah khit ciangin Mai in kal tawp bup a nasepte a zom hi.

records.english: The school library stays open until six so that students can do their homework there.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte in tua ah inn-a sep ding a sep theih nadingun sang laibu inn nai guk dong a kihong hi.

records.english: My teacher told me, "Show your working, even if the answer is right."
records.zomi: Ka saya in, “Dawnna a dik hangin na sep dan etsak in,” hong ci hi.

records.english: If you could change one thing about the homework you're given, what would it be?
records.zomi: Na ngah inn-a sep ding ah khat na laih thei leh bang ahi ding hiam?

records.english: Not until the night before the deadline did I realize that the project needed photographs.
records.zomi: A tawp ni ma-a zan bek project in lim a kisam hi, cih ka thei hi.

records.english: Did the teacher let you redo the test?
records.zomi: Saya in sitna kik dingin hong phal hiam?

records.english: Why don't you ask the teacher to explain the question again tomorrow?
records.zomi: Bang hangin zingciang dotna kik-in gen siang dingin saya na ngen kei hiam?

records.english: Can you check my spelling before I hand this in?
records.zomi: Ka piak ma-in ka laimal gelh dan na en sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: My parents had the internet installed so that we could do online research for school.
records.zomi: Sang adingin online-a i zon theih nadingin ka nu leh ka pa in internet a koih sak uh hi.

records.english: In our house, the television stays off until everyone's homework is done.
records.zomi: I inn ah mi khempeuh' inn-a sep ding a bei dong TV a kikhek hi.

records.english: If I finish my homework early, may I go out and play?
records.zomi: Ka inn-a sep ding a man masak leh pua ah kimawl dingin ka pai thei ding hiam?

records.english: Somebody spilled water on my exercise book, and now the ink has run.
records.zomi: Kuamah in ka laibu tungah tui a sun a, tu-in khuai a luang hi.

records.english: Teachers in our school try not to set homework during festival weeks, so that families can spend time together.
records.zomi: Innkuante hun khawm a zat theih nadingun i sang-a sayate in pawi kal sungin inn-a sep ding a pia lo dingin a sin uh hi.

records.english: Shall we go through your answers together before you pack your bag?
records.zomi: Na ip na thuk ma-in na dawnnate khawm-in i en ding hiam?

records.english: Please write your name at the top of every page.
records.zomi: Laimai khempeuh tung lam ah na min gelh in.

records.english: The more I practiced the multiplication tables at home, the faster I became in class.
records.zomi: Inn ah kiphawlna sim ka kisin tam semsem ciangin kilasi ah ka manlang semsem hi.

records.english: I have to finish my math homework before dinner.
records.zomi: Nitak an ma-in ka math inn-a sep ding ka zo ding hi.

records.english: Had I read the instructions properly, I wouldn't have written about the wrong book.
records.zomi: Zat dan lai hoih takin ka sim le, laibu dik lo thu ka gelh kei ding hi.

records.english: Do we need to type the assignment, or can we write it by hand?
records.zomi: Nasep i type ding hiam, khut tawh i gelh thei ding hiam?

records.english: I asked my uncle, who is an engineer, to explain the physics problem to me.
records.zomi: Engineer ahi ka pa neu in physics dotna hong gen siang dingin ka ngen hi.

records.english: My cousin and I study together at the library so that we can share the books.
records.zomi: Laibute i kihawm theih nadingin ka sanggam leh kei laibu inn ah khawm-in i sin hi.

records.english: Our teacher gives us homework every night except Friday.
records.zomi: I saya in Laithai ni simloh zan simin inn-a sep ding hong pia hi.

records.english: What I find hardest about homework is starting it, not finishing it.
records.zomi: Inn-a sep ding ah ka haksa sak pen pen a zawh hi lo-in a kipat ahi hi.

records.english: Our teacher had the project deadline moved because half the class was sick.
records.zomi: Kilasi a khen khat a dam kei uh ahih manin i saya in project a tawp ni a suan hi.

records.english: I stayed up late to finish the poster for my history project.
records.zomi: Ka tangthu project adingin poster zo dingin ka nai hi.

records.english: My son's essay was chosen to be read aloud at the school assembly, and he was too shy to read it himself.
records.zomi: Ka tapa' essay sang kikhopna ah sim dingin kiteel a, amah mah in sim dingin a zak lua hi.

records.english: We have to read two chapters of the novel by Monday.
records.zomi: Pizing ni ma-in novel khen nih i sim ding hi.

records.english: Were you upset when your team lost the final?
records.zomi: Na pawl in a nunung pen kimawlna a zawh loh ciangin na lungkham hiam?

records.english: For about an hour, until my friends took me out for noodles.
records.zomi: Nai khat bang, ka lawmte in an-ngum ne dingin hong paipih uh dong.

records.english: How was your grandmother after the funeral?
records.zomi: Mithi vuina khit ciangin na pi bangci-in a om hiam?

records.english: Quiet, but she said she felt comforted by everyone who came.
records.zomi: A dai hi, ahi zongin a hong khempeuh in a hehnemsak hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Why is Grandma so cheerful today?
records.zomi: Bang hangin tuni-in ka pi a lungdam mahmah hiam?

records.english: All her grandchildren are coming home for the weekend.
records.zomi: A tu khempeuh kal tawp ciangin inn ah a hong ciah ding uh hi.

records.english: Why is the dog so sad?
records.zomi: Bang hangin ui a lungkham mahmah hiam?

records.english: He's been lying by the door since my brother left for the army.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal galkap ah a pai pan kipan kongkhak kiang ah a lum hi.

records.english: Who made you so happy this morning?
records.zomi: Tuni zingsangin kua in hong lungdamsak mahmah hiam?

records.english: The old man next door, who brought me mangoes from his tree.
records.zomi: A kiang inn-a pasal upa, a singkung pan haigah hong tawi sak pa.

records.english: Class, how do you feel now that the school year is over?
records.zomi: Kilasi, sang kum a bei khit ciangin bangci-in na kisa uh hiam?

records.english: Happy, but a bit sad that we won't see our teacher every day.
records.zomi: I lungdam hi, ahi zongin ni simin i saya i mu nawn kei ding ahih manin tawmno i lungkham hi.

records.english: Why did you keep the letter for so many years?
records.zomi: Bang hangin lai kum tampi sung na kem hiam?

records.english: My father wrote it the day I was born, and it still makes me happy to read it.
records.zomi: Ka suak ni-in ka pa in a gelh a, a sim ciangin tu dong hong lungdamsak lai hi.

records.english: How did the village celebrate the new well?
records.zomi: Tuikhuk thak adingin khua in bangci-in pawi a bawl uh hiam?

records.english: Everyone danced in the square, and the children splashed in the first bucket of water.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh khua laizang ah a lam uh a, naupangte in tui bawm masa pen ah tui a phiat uh hi.

records.english: Is it possible to feel happy and sad at the same time?
records.zomi: Hun khat mah-in lungdam leh lungkham thei hiam?

records.english: It is — that's exactly how I felt on my wedding day, because my father wasn't there.
records.zomi: Thei hi — tua mah ka kiteen ni-in ka kisak dan ahi hi, ka pa a om kei ahih manin.

records.english: Did the news make you happy?
records.zomi: Thu in hong lungdamsak hiam?

records.english: I really do want to be happy for her, but I'll miss her terribly.
records.zomi: Amah adingin lungdam ka deih mahmah hi, ahi zongin ka lungngai mahmah ding hi.

records.english: Had you known how hard it would be to leave, would you still have emigrated?
records.zomi: Pai khiat bangzah a haksa ding hiam na theih le, gamdang ah na tuah lai ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, though I wish someone had warned me how much I'd miss ordinary things like the market.
records.zomi: Tuah lai ding ing, ahi zongin zuakna mun bang thu pangaite bangzah ka lungngai ding hiam kuamah in hong hilh leh ka deih hi.

records.english: Is it all right to cry in front of your children?
records.zomi: Na tate mai ah kap a hoih hiam?

records.english: I think so, because it shows them that sadness is a normal part of life.
records.zomi: Hoih in ka ngaihsun hi, lungkhamna pen nuntakna sung-a pangai khat ahi hi, cih a etsak ahih manin.

records.english: When my grandmother died, our house felt empty for months.
records.zomi: Ka pi a sih ciangin i inn kha tampi sung a awng bang hi.

records.english: Then my aunt began cooking her recipes on Sundays, and slowly the laughter came back to the kitchen.
records.zomi: Tua ciangin ka ni in Nipini simin a an huan dante a huan kipan a, zawl takin an huanna ah nuihna a hong kik hi.

records.english: What cheers you up when you're feeling low?
records.zomi: Na lungkham ciangin bang in hong lungdamsak hiam?

records.english: A long walk by the river and a phone call with my sister.
records.zomi: Gun gei-a vak sau leh ka sanggam nu tawh phone kiho.

records.english: Why are the flags at half-mast?
records.zomi: Bang hangin puanzalte a kimlai dong bek a kikhai hiam?

records.english: A teacher who worked at the school for forty years died last week.
records.zomi: Kal nung in sang ah kum sawmli sung a nasem saya khat a si hi.

records.english: Why are you smiling at your phone?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na phone en-in na nui hiam?

records.english: My son just sent a video of himself on the school stage for the first time.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in sang dawhsang tungah a masa pen-a a om video hong khak hi.

records.english: Why were you crying at the airport?
records.zomi: Bang hangin vanlengtual ah na kap hiam?

records.english: My daughter was leaving for three years, and I couldn't help it.
records.zomi: Ka tanu kum thum adingin a pai ding a, ka kham zo kei hi.

records.english: What happened to your garden?
records.zomi: Na huan bang a piang hiam?

records.english: It was destroyed by the hailstorm, and I'd been working on it all spring.
records.zomi: Gial in a susia a, spring bup ka sem khin hi.

records.english: Why do some people hide their sadness from their families?
records.zomi: Bang hangin mi khenkhatte in a lungkhamna uh a innkuan uh tungah a sel uh hiam?

records.english: They may not want to worry anyone, or they may feel that admitting it would be a sign of weakness.
records.zomi: Kuamah lungkhamsak a deih kei kha uh a, a gen leh hatlohna lim hi, a ci kha uh hi.

records.english: What do you think makes people truly happy?
records.zomi: Bang in mite lungdamsak taktak in na ngaihsun hiam?

records.english: Not money, in my experience, but having people to care for and something useful to do each day.
records.zomi: Ka theih bangin sum hi lo-in, kemcing ding mite leh ni simin sep ding manphatna neih ahi hi.

records.english: Why did the whole office cheer?
records.zomi: Bang hangin office bup a kikou uh hiam?

records.english: Our manager told us that nobody would lose their job after all.
records.zomi: Kuamah in a nasep a mansuah lo ding hi, ci-in i manager in hong hilh hi.

records.english: Did your brother ever get over the breakup?
records.zomi: Na sanggam pasal a kikhen khit-a lungkhamna pan a dam kik hiam?

records.english: Slowly, and now he jokes about how sad he was.
records.zomi: Zawl takin, tu-in bangzah a lungkham hiam a nuihza pih hi.

records.english: What was the saddest moment of your life?
records.zomi: Na nuntak sung-a hun lungkhamhuai pen bang ahi hiam?

records.english: Leaving my village for the city and seeing my mother at the gate.
records.zomi: Khuapi lam-a ka khua ka nusiat a, kongpi ah ka nu ka muh ciangin.

records.english: Why did your father play the old guitar last night?
records.zomi: Bang hangin zanni zanin na pa in guitar lui a tum hiam?

records.english: It was my mother's birthday, and he wanted to sing the songs she loved.
records.zomi: Ka nu' pianni ahi a, a deih lai sak a deih hi.

records.english: What would you say to a friend who has just lost his job?
records.zomi: A nasep a mansuah thak lawm khat kiangah bang na gen ding hiam?

records.english: I'd tell him it's all right to feel sad, and then offer to help him look for another one.
records.zomi: Lungkham pen a hoih hi, ka ci ding a, tua ciangin a dang khat zong dingin ka huh ding hi.

records.english: If you could relive one happy day, which would it be?
records.zomi: Ni lungdamhuai khat na nungta kik thei leh koi ahi ding hiam?

records.english: The afternoon my whole family sat under the mango tree, before any of us had moved away.
records.zomi: I lak-a kuamah a tuah ma-in innkuan bup in haigah kung nuai ah i tut nitak lam.

records.english: How do you cope with sadness that doesn't seem to go away?
records.zomi: A bei lo bang lungkhamna bangci-in na thuak hiam?

records.english: I talk to someone I trust, and if it lasts more than a few weeks, I'd see a doctor.
records.zomi: Ka um mi khat tawh ka kiho a, kal tawmno sangin a sawt leh siavuan ka mu ding hi.

records.english: How do you comfort a child who has lost a pet?
records.zomi: Ganhing a mansuah naupang khat bangci-in na hehnem hiam?

records.english: Let them talk about the animal, and perhaps help them plant a tree in its memory.
records.zomi: Ganhing thu gen sak in, a phawkna dingin singkung khat suan dingin huh kha in.

records.english: Are you happy with your exam results?
records.zomi: Na sitna ciamte tungah na lungdam hiam?

records.english: Happier than I expected, especially in history.
records.zomi: Ka lamen sangin ka lungdam zaw hi, a diakin tangthu ah.

records.english: What made your grandfather laugh so much at dinner?
records.zomi: Bang in nitak an ah na pu a nuisak mahmah hiam?

records.english: My little brother tried to eat soup with a fork.
records.zomi: Ka nau pasal in fork tawh an tui ne dingin a sin hi.

records.english: Will you send me a message from the station, so that I can stop pacing the kitchen?
records.zomi: An huanna ah ka vak kawikawi nawn loh nadingin meileng dinna pan thu hong khak ding na hi hiam?

records.english: I'll text you the moment the bus arrives.
records.zomi: Bus a tun pah-in thu kong khak ding hi.

records.english: During the earthquake, my little sister and I hid under the kitchen table.
records.zomi: Leiling laitakin kei leh ka nau nu an huanna dawhkan nuai ah i bu hi.

records.english: When the shaking stopped, our father carried us outside, and we sat in the yard until morning.
records.zomi: A ling tawp ciangin i pa in pua ah hong pua a, zingsang dong tual ah i tu hi.

records.english: What did you do when you got lost in the forest?
records.zomi: Gam sung ah na mang ciangin bang na hih hiam?

records.english: I stayed by a big tree and blew my whistle until someone came.
records.zomi: Singkung lian khat kiang ah ka om a, kuamah a hong tun dong ka whistle ka mut hi.

records.english: What would you do if you had to face your greatest fear tomorrow?
records.zomi: Zingciang na lauh pen pen na tuak ding hi leh bang na hih ding hiam?

records.english: I'd ask a friend to come with me, since everything feels less frightening when you're not alone.
records.zomi: Lawm khat hong pai khawm dingin ka ngen ding hi, nangma bek na hih kei ciangin khempeuh a lauhuai tawm zaw ahih manin.

records.english: Do you really want to try the high bridge?
records.zomi: Lei sang na kan nuam taktak hiam?

records.english: I really do want to, even though my legs are shaking.
records.zomi: Ka kan nuam mahmah hi, ka khe a ling hangin.

records.english: Can I sleep in your room tonight?
records.zomi: Tuni zanin na khan ah ka ihmu thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, but only tonight, and then you'll be brave again in your own bed.
records.zomi: Thei hi, ahi zongin tuni zan bek, tua ciangin na lupna ah na hang kik ding hi.

records.english: Why did your father buy a fire extinguisher for the kitchen?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na pa in an huanna adingin mei mitna set a lei hiam?

records.english: After the fire at our neighbor's house, he wanted to be ready.
records.zomi: I inn veng' inn mei a kang khit ciangin kiman a deih hi.

records.english: Why do you check the door three times before bed?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na lup ma-in kongkhak thumvei na en hiam?

records.english: We were burgled once, and I've never quite stopped worrying about it.
records.zomi: Khatvei guta in i inn a lut a, tua pan ka lungkham tawp ngei kei hi.

records.english: Is it possible that the river will flood the village again?
records.zomi: Gun in khua tui a liam kik thei hiam?

records.english: It's possible, so the council has given every family sandbags just in case.
records.zomi: Thei hi, tua ahih manin council in innkuan khempeuh piaktui ip a pia hi.

records.english: Did the thunder wake you up?
records.zomi: Van ging in hong phawngsak hiam?

records.english: It did, and I hid under the blanket until it stopped.
records.zomi: Phawngsak hi, a tawp dong puannak nuai ah ka bu hi.

records.english: Who checks on your grandfather when you're at work?
records.zomi: Na nasep laitakin na pu kua in a en hiam?

records.english: Our neighbor goes round at lunchtime and phones me if anything is wrong.
records.zomi: I inn veng in sun an hun ciangin a pai a, bangmah a sia leh hong sam hi.

records.english: What's the worst thing about waiting for exam results?
records.zomi: Sitna ciamte ngak ah a hoih lo pen bang ahi hiam?

records.english: Not knowing, because my mind keeps imagining the worst.
records.zomi: Theih loh, ka lungsim in a hoih lo pen a ngaihsun den ahih manin.

records.english: Why did the children run out of the old house?
records.zomi: Bang hangin naupangte inn lui pan a tai khia uh hiam?

records.english: A door slammed shut in the wind, and they thought it was a ghost.
records.zomi: Huih in kongkhak khat a khak a, dawi in a ngaihsun uh hi.

records.english: What did the doctor say to calm you down?
records.zomi: Hong ngaisak dingin siavuan in bang a ci hiam?

records.english: He said, "Most people with this problem are completely better within a month."
records.zomi: “Hih buaina nei mi tamzaw kha khat sungin a dam kim uh hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: Why won't you go into the sea?
records.zomi: Bang hangin tuipi sung ah na lut nuam kei hiam?
