records.english: I nearly drowned when I was little, and I've been afraid of deep water ever since.
records.zomi: Ka neu lai-in tui ka liap dek a, tua pan tui thuk ka lau hi.

records.english: Is worry ever useful?
records.zomi: Lungkhamna in a huh ngei hiam?

records.english: A little of it can make us prepare carefully, but too much stops us from acting at all.
records.zomi: Tawmno in pilvang taka kiman dingin hong huh thei a, ahi zongin a tam lua in bangmah hih zo lo dingin hong khamsak hi.

records.english: How do you calm the baby during a storm?
records.zomi: Huihpi laitakin naungek bangci-in na ngaisak hiam?

records.english: I hold her close and sing quietly until the noise passes.
records.zomi: Ka pom cip a, ging a bei dong dai takin la ka sa sak hi.

records.english: Why is your mother so worried about the rain?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na nu guah thu-ah a lungkham mahmah hiam?

records.english: Our roof leaked badly last year, and she's afraid it'll happen again.
records.zomi: Kum nung in i innkhum a zu mahmah a, a piang kik ding a lau hi.

records.english: Why didn't you tell anyone you were being bullied?
records.zomi: Hong vawt den uh hi, ci-in bang hangin kuamah na hilh kei hiam?

records.english: I was afraid it would only get worse if the other boys found out.
records.zomi: Naupang pasal dangte in a theih uh leh a hoih lo semsem ding ka lau hi.

records.english: What would help you feel less anxious before speaking?
records.zomi: Na gen ma-in na lauhna tawmsak dingin bang in hong huh ding hiam?

records.english: Practicing in front of my family the night before, and breathing slowly while I wait.
records.zomi: Zan ma-in ka innkuan mai ah kisin-in, ka ngak laitakin zawl takin huih diah.

records.english: What are you afraid of?
records.zomi: Bang na lau hiam?

records.english: Spiders, mostly, and big dogs that bark.
records.zomi: A tamzaw maimom, leh a hop ui lian te.

records.english: Why are you so nervous about meeting her parents?
records.zomi: Bang hangin a nu leh a pa kimuh thu-ah na lau mahmah hiam?

records.english: They're very traditional, and I'm worried they won't like me.
records.zomi: Ngeina lui a zui mahmah uh a, hong deih kei kha ding uh ka lau hi.

records.english: Why are older people often more afraid of falling than of being ill?
records.zomi: Bang hangin upate in dam loh sangin kiat a lau zaw uh hiam?

records.english: A fall can take away their independence overnight, and many have seen it happen to their friends.
records.zomi: Kiatna in zan khat sungin amau mah-a a omna a la thei a, tampi in a lawmte tungah a piang a mu khin uh hi.

records.english: Are you still scared of the dentist?
records.zomi: Ha siavuan na lau lai hiam?

records.english: A little, but the new one explains everything before she starts.
records.zomi: Tawmno, ahi zongin a thak pen in a kipat ma-in khempeuh a gen siang hi.

records.english: Why do some people worry far more than others?
records.zomi: Bang hangin mi khenkhatte a dangte sangin a lungkham tam zaw uh hiam?

records.english: It may partly be their nature and partly what they've lived through, but nobody fully understands it.
records.zomi: A khen khat amau ngeina leh a khen khat a tuakte uh hi kha ding hi, ahi zongin kuamah in a bup-in a thei kei hi.

records.english: Everyone, is there anything about the trip that you're worried about?
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, khualzinna thu-ah na lungkham uh bangmah a om hiam?

records.english: Only the long bus ride, because some of us get sick.
records.zomi: Bus tuan sau bek, ei khenkhatte i lua nuam ahih manin.

records.english: How do you help a child who is afraid to go to school?
records.zomi: Sang pai a lau naupang khat bangci-in na huh hiam?

records.english: Find out exactly what frightens them, and then work with the teacher to change it, one small step at a time.
records.zomi: Bang in kician takin a lausak hiam zong inla, tua ciangin saya tawh khawm-in kal neu khat ciat in laih in.

records.english: How did you get over your fear of flying?
records.zomi: Vanleng tuan na lauhna bangci-in na zo hiam?

records.english: I took a short course where a pilot explained every sound the plane makes.
records.zomi: Vanleng mawngpa khat in vanleng ging khempeuh a gen siang kisinna tom khat ka kah hi.

records.english: Had you known how dangerous the road was, would you have driven at night?
records.zomi: Lampi bangzah a lauhuai hiam na theih le, zan ah na mawng ding hiam?

records.english: Never, because I spent the whole journey gripping the wheel and praying.
records.zomi: Mawng lo ngei ding ing, khualzinna bup sung ah ka len cip a, thu ka ngen den hi.

records.english: Who stayed with you when you were frightened in hospital?
records.zomi: Zato ah na lau ciangin kua in na kiang ah a om hiam?

records.english: A young nurse, who held my hand until I fell asleep.
records.zomi: Nurse khangno khat, ka ihmut dong ka khut a len pa.

records.english: What did your grandfather tell you before your exam?
records.zomi: Na sitna ma-in na pu in bang hong hilh hiam?

records.english: He said, "Read every question twice, and don't panic if you don't know one."
records.zomi: “Dotna khempeuh nihvei sim inla, khat na theih kei leh lau kei in,” a ci hi.

records.english: Class, who would like to try the hard question first?
records.zomi: Kilasi, dotna haksa kua in a sin masa nuam hiam?

records.english: I'll try, even if I get it wrong.
records.zomi: Ka khialh kha zongin ka sin ding hi.

records.english: What would you say to someone starting a business for the first time?
records.zomi: A masa pen-a sumbawl kipan mi khat kiangah bang na gen ding hiam?

records.english: Find one customer who loves what you make, and listen to everything they tell you.
records.zomi: Na bawl a deih mahmah lei mi khat zong inla, a gen khempeuh ngai in.

records.english: Why did you write "Keep going" on the wall above your desk?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na dawhkan tung-a bang ah “Zom den in” na gelh hiam?

records.english: So that I see it every morning when I'm tempted to give up.
records.zomi: Ka khah nuam ciangin zingsang simin ka muh theih nadingin.

records.english: Why did you put a note in my lunch box?
records.zomi: Bang hangin ka sun an bawm sung ah lai na koih hiam?

records.english: I wanted you to remember that I'm proud of you, even on hard days.
records.zomi: Ni haksa ciangin zong na tungah ka kisaktheih hi, cih na phawk ding ka deih hi.

records.english: Why does encouragement sometimes matter more than advice?
records.zomi: Bang hangin hanthawnna in thuhilhna sangin a thupi zaw khatveivei hiam?

records.english: People who are struggling often already know what to do, but they need someone to believe they can do it.
records.zomi: A haksa tuak mite in bang hih ding hiam a thei khin tamzaw uh a, ahi zongin a hih thei uh hi, a um kuamah a kisam uh hi.

records.english: How do you encourage someone without putting pressure on them?
records.zomi: Mi khat a buaisak lo-in bangci-in na hanthawn hiam?

records.english: Praise the effort rather than the result, and let them know you'll be proud of them either way.
records.zomi: A kipaina sangin a hanciamna phat inla, bang ahi zongin a tungah na kisaktheih ding hi, cih theisak in.

records.english: If you could send a message to your younger self, what would it say?
records.zomi: Na neu lai-a nangma kiangah thu na khak thei leh bang a ci ding hiam?

records.english: Be patient with yourself, because the hardest years turn out to be the ones you learn most from.
records.zomi: Nangma tungah thuakzawh in, kum haksa pente na sin tam penna ahi ding ahih manin.

records.english: Why did the whole village come to the airport?
records.zomi: Bang hangin khua bup vanlengtual ah a hong uh hiam?

records.english: They wanted to see off the first girl from our village to study abroad.
records.zomi: Gamdang ah sin dingin i khua pan numei naupang masa pen paikhiat a en nuam uh hi.

records.english: What gives you hope for the next generation?
records.zomi: Khang zom adingin bang in hong lametna pia hiam?

records.english: Young people today seem more willing to help strangers and to speak up when something is unfair.
records.zomi: Tu hun khangnote in mi theih lohte a huh nuam zaw a, bangmah a dik lo ciangin a gen nuam zaw uh hi.

records.english: How did the team stay positive after losing every game last season?
records.zomi: Kum nung-a kimawlna khempeuh a sum khit ciangin pawl in bangci-in lungsim hoih a kem uh hiam?

records.english: The coach praised each small improvement, and slowly we began to win.
records.zomi: Hilhtu in hoihna neu khat ciat a phat a, zawl takin i zo kipan hi.

records.english: How can a whole community encourage young people who have lost their way?
records.zomi: Mipi bup in lampi a mang khangnote bangci-in a hanthawn thei hiam?

records.english: By giving them real responsibilities and trusting them to rise to the challenge.
records.zomi: Mawhpuakna taktak pia-in, a zo ding uh um-in.

records.english: Can you help me fill in the scholarship form?
records.zomi: Scholarship form gelh dingin hong huh thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Gladly, and we'll ask your teacher to write you a letter as well.
records.zomi: Lungdam takin, na saya zong lai khat hong gelh sak dingin i ngen ding hi.

records.english: Team, are you ready for the second half?
records.zomi: Pawl, a khen nihna adingin na kiman uh hiam?

records.english: Ready, and we're not giving up until the final whistle!
records.zomi: Kiman hi, whistle nunung pen a ging dong i khah kei ding hi!

records.english: Why did you send flowers to your teacher?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na saya kiangah pak na khak hiam?

records.english: She believed in me when nobody else did.
records.zomi: Kuamah in hong um kei uh laitakin amah in hong um hi.

records.english: Did the farmers lose hope after the drought?
records.zomi: Khuakhal khit ciangin lo neite lametna a bei uh hiam?

records.english: Some did, but most planted again as soon as the rain came.
records.zomi: Khenkhatte a bei hi, ahi zongin a tamzaw in guah a zuk pah-in a suan kik uh hi.

records.english: Do you still want to be a doctor after failing chemistry?
records.zomi: Chemistry na zawh loh khit ciangin siavuan suak na deih lai hiam?

records.english: I really do want to, so I'm going to take the course again next year.
records.zomi: Ka deih mahmah hi, tua ahih manin kum zom ciangin kisinna ka kah kik ding hi.

records.english: Is it possible to learn to read at sixty?
records.zomi: Kum sawmguk ciangin lai sim sin thei hiam?

records.english: It certainly is — my mother learned at sixty-two and now reads to her grandchildren.
records.zomi: Thei mahmah hi — ka nu in kum sawmguk leh nih ciangin a sin a, tu-in a tute adingin a sim hi.

records.english: Do you think I can win the race?
records.zomi: Tai kidemna ka zo thei in na ngaihsun hiam?

records.english: If you keep training like this, you've got a real chance.
records.zomi: Hih bangin na kisin den leh hun taktak na nei hi.

records.english: Had your coach not believed in you, would you have kept playing?
records.zomi: Na hilhtu in hong um kei le, na kimawl den ding hiam?

records.english: Probably not, because I was ready to quit after my first season.
records.zomi: Kimawl lo kha ding ing, ka kum masa pen khit ciangin khah dingin ka kiman khin hi.

records.english: Will my leg ever be strong again?
records.zomi: Ka khe a hat kik ngei ding hiam?

records.english: It will, if you do your exercises every day.
records.zomi: Hat kik ding hi, ni simin na kisinna na sep leh.

records.english: Who encouraged you to start painting?
records.zomi: Lim zeek kipan dingin kua in hong hanthawn hiam?

records.english: My art teacher, who hung one of my pictures in the school hall.
records.zomi: Ka lim zeek saya, sang inn lian ah ka lim khat a khai sak pa.

records.english: What got you through the year you were unemployed?
records.zomi: Nasep na neih loh kum sungin bang in hong pai suaksak hiam?

records.english: My wife's patience and a neighbor who kept telling me about jobs he'd seen.
records.zomi: Ka zi' thuakzawhna leh a muh nasep thu hong gen den inn veng khat.

records.english: Why are you practicing the piano for so long every evening?
records.zomi: Bang hangin nitak simin piano hun sawt na kisin hiam?

records.english: The music teacher said I might be ready for the competition in spring.
records.zomi: Spring ciangin kidemna adingin ka kiman kha ding hi, ci-in la saya in a ci hi.

records.english: After my business failed, I stayed in bed for a week.
records.zomi: Ka sumbawl a puk khit ciangin kal khat lupna tungah ka om hi.

records.english: Then my old teacher came to visit, lent me some money, and told me to try again.
records.zomi: Tua ciangin ka saya lui hong veh a, sum hong ngetsak a, kik-in sin dingin hong hilh hi.

records.english: How can I help my friend who has lost hope?
records.zomi: Lametna a bei ka lawm bangci-in ka huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Visit her often, listen more than you speak, and remind her of the things she does well.
records.zomi: A tawntung-in veh inla, na gen sangin ngai tam zaw inla, a hih siam thute phawksak in.

records.english: Why are you smiling after such a hard day?
records.zomi: Ni haksa khit ciangin bang hangin na nui hiam?

records.english: My son phoned to say he got the job he applied for.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in a ngetna nasep a ngah hi, ci-in phone hong sam hi.

records.english: Is it worth applying when there are so many other candidates?
records.zomi: Ngen dang tam lua a om laitakin ngen a manphat hiam?

records.english: Yes, because someone has to get the job, and it might as well be you.
records.zomi: Manphat hi, kuamah in nasep a ngah ding a, nangmah na hih leh a hoih hi.

records.english: What helps you stay hopeful when the news is so bad?
records.zomi: Thu a hoih lo lua laitakin lametna nei den dingin bang in hong huh hiam?

records.english: Small acts of kindness that I see every day in my own street.
records.zomi: Keima' lampi ah ni simin ka muh hehpihna neute.

records.english: Should I give up the violin because my fingers hurt?
records.zomi: Ka khutzungte a na ahih manin violin ka khah ding hiam?

records.english: Not yet — everyone's fingers hurt at first, and it gets easier in a few weeks.
records.zomi: Khah nai kei in — mi khempeuh' khutzung a masa-in a na a, kal tawmno sungin a baih semsem hi.

records.english: Are you a morning person or a night person?
records.zomi: Zingsang mi na hi hiam, zan mi na hi hiam?

records.english: Definitely a morning person — I'm asleep by ten.
records.zomi: Zingsang mi mahmah — nai sawm ciangin ka ihmu khin hi.

records.english: What's the reason you always write in pencil?
records.zomi: Bang hangin khedal tawh na gelh tawntung hiam?

records.english: I like being able to rub out my mistakes.
records.zomi: Ka khialhnate ka phiat thei ka deih hi.

records.english: Why did you have your hair cut so short?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na sam tom mahmah-in na at hiam?

records.english: It's cooler in the summer, and I don't have to spend time drying it.
records.zomi: Khal hun ah a vot zaw a, a keu sak nadingin hun ka zang kei hi.

records.english: Why do you use that old knife when you have a new one?
records.zomi: Namsau thak na neih hangin bang hangin namsau lui na zang hiam?

records.english: My father gave it to me, and it cuts better than any knife I've bought.
records.zomi: Ka pa in hong pia a, ka lei namsau khempeuh sangin a hiam zaw hi.

records.english: If you could change one thing about your daily routine, what would it be?
records.zomi: Na ni sim ngeina ah khat na laih thei leh bang ahi ding hiam?

records.english: I'd start work an hour later, so that I could have breakfast with my children.
records.zomi: Ka tate tawh zingsang an ka nek theih nadingin nai khat nung zaw-in nasep ka kipan ding hi.

records.english: Why do you listen to the radio instead of watching television?
records.zomi: Bang hangin TV en sangin radio na ngai hiam?

records.english: I can do other things while I'm listening, like cooking or mending clothes.
records.zomi: Ka ngaih laitakin an huan hiam puan khui bang a dang ka hih thei hi.

records.english: What made your grandmother move to the city?
records.zomi: Bang in na pi khuapi ah a tuahsak hiam?

records.english: She wanted to be closer to the hospital, though she still prefers the village.
records.zomi: Zato kiang zaw-a om a deih hi, khua a deih zaw lai hangin.

records.english: I used to hate vegetables, so my grandmother had me plant my own in her garden.
records.zomi: Ma-in anteh ka huat ahih manin ka pi in a huan ah keima' te hong suansak hi.

records.english: By the end of the summer, I was eating everything I'd grown, even the beans.
records.zomi: Khal hun a bei ciangin ka suan khempeuh, be tawh, ka ne hi.

records.english: Is it possible to change the color of the shirt I ordered?
records.zomi: Ka ngetna angki rong ka laih thei ding hiam?

records.english: It is, as long as you tell us before it's sent.
records.zomi: Thei hi, a kikhak ma-in hong gen leh.

records.english: What makes you choose one shop over another when they sell the same things?
records.zomi: Van kibang a zuak uh laitakin bang in dawr khat na teelsak hiam?

records.english: The way the owner treats me, since I'd rather pay a little more and be greeted by name.
records.zomi: A neipa in hong kizang dan, tawmno man tam zaw pia-in min tawh hong hopih ka deih zaw ahih manin.

records.english: What's your favorite way to spend a rainy afternoon?
records.zomi: Guah zuk nitak lam khat zat dan na deih pen bang ahi hiam?

records.english: With a good book and a pot of ginger tea.
records.zomi: Laibu hoih khat leh siing tea beel khat tawh.

records.english: What made you choose a small car?
records.zomi: Bang in mawtaw neu na teelsak hiam?

records.english: I drive in the old town every day, and big cars can't get through the narrow streets.
records.zomi: Ni simin khuapi lui ah ka mawng a, mawtaw lian te lampi neu ah a pai zo kei uh hi.

records.english: Why do some people prefer living in the countryside even when the city pays better?
records.zomi: Bang hangin khuapi in nasep man tam zaw a pia hangin mi khenkhatte in lo gam ah om a deih zaw uh hiam?

records.english: They value fresh air, space and knowing their neighbors more than a bigger salary.
records.zomi: Nasep man tam zaw sangin huih siang, mun zai leh inn vengte theih a manphat sa zaw uh hi.

records.english: What kind of holiday would suit your parents best?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa adingin nopsakna hun bang namkhat in a kituak pen ding hiam?

records.english: Somewhere quiet by a lake, where my father can fish and my mother can read.
records.zomi: Dil kiang-a mun dai khat, ka pa in nga a man thei a, ka nu in lai a sim thei mun.

records.english: Everyone, what kind of pizza should we order?
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, pizza bang namkhat i ngen ding hiam?

records.english: Vegetable for half and chicken for the other half, please.
records.zomi: A khen khat adingin anteh, a khen khat adingin aksa, hong pia un.

records.english: Would you prefer to sit with your friends or with your cousins at the wedding?
records.zomi: Mopawi ah na lawmte tawh na tu deih zaw hiam, na sanggamte tawh hiam?

records.english: With my cousins, since I hardly ever see them.
records.zomi: Ka sanggamte tawh, ka mu ngei tawm ahih manin.

records.english: How have your tastes in music changed as you've grown older?
records.zomi: Na upat semsem ciangin na la deihna bangci-in a kilai hiam?

records.english: I used to like only loud music, but now I find myself enjoying the old songs my parents played.
records.zomi: Ma-in ging sang la bek ka deih hi, ahi zongin tu-in ka nu leh ka pa' sak la luite ka deih hi.

records.english: Would you like me to choose the paint for your room?
records.zomi: Na khan adingin zeek kong teel sak ding hiam?

records.english: No, thank you — I'd rather pick it myself.
records.zomi: Hi lo ing, ka lungdam hi — keimah in teel ka deih zaw hi.

records.english: What do you like most about living near the sea?
records.zomi: Tuipi kiang-a om ah bang na deih pen hiam?

records.english: The sound of the waves at night, and fresh fish every morning.
records.zomi: Zan-a tuipi kihawk ging, leh zingsang simin nga thak.

records.english: Do you think our preferences are shaped more by our families or by our friends?
records.zomi: I deihnate i innkuan in hiam, i lawmte in hiam a bawl zaw in na ngaihsun hiam?

records.english: By our families when we're young, and by our friends once we become teenagers.
records.zomi: I neu laitakin i innkuan in, khangno i suak ciangin i lawmte in.

records.english: Do you sleep better with the window open or closed?
records.zomi: Tukvuang kihong-in hiam, kikhak-in hiam na ihmu hoih zaw hiam?

records.english: Open, even in winter, because I can't sleep in a stuffy room.
records.zomi: Kihong-in, khuavot ah zong, huih om lo khan ah ka ihmu thei kei ahih manin.

records.english: Why does your brother hate wearing a tie?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na sanggam pasal in ngawngkhih bulh a huat hiam?

records.english: He says it makes him feel like he can't breathe.
records.zomi: Huih diah thei lo bangin hong kisaksak hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Could you choose a book for my son's birthday?
records.zomi: Ka tapa' pianni adingin laibu khat na teel sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: I'd love to — does he prefer adventure stories or true ones?
records.zomi: Ka deih mahmah hi — tangthu lamdang hiam, tangthu tak hiam a deih zaw hiam?

records.english: Had you been allowed to choose your own career, would you have become a teacher?
records.zomi: Na nasep nangma-in na teel thei le, saya na suak ding hiam?

records.english: Probably not, but now I can't imagine doing anything else.
records.zomi: Suak lo kha ding ing, ahi zongin tu-in a dang khatpeuh sep ka ngaihsun thei kei hi.

records.english: How come you buy flowers every Friday?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Laithai ni simin pak na lei hiam?

records.english: My late husband always brought them home on Fridays, and I've kept up the habit.
records.zomi: Ka pasal a sih ma-in Laithai ni simin inn ah a tawi den a, tua ngeina ka zom hi.

records.english: Why do you always choose the corner table?
records.zomi: Bang hangin kil-a dawhkan na teel tawntung hiam?

records.english: I can see the whole room from here, and it's quieter.
records.zomi: Hih pan khan bup ka mu thei a, a dai zaw hi.

records.english: Why did your mother make you wear a coat?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na nu in kawt hong silhsak hiam?

records.english: She said I'd catch a cold if I went out without one.
records.zomi: Silh lo-in ka pai khiat leh khuasik ka ngah ding hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Do you prefer cooking for yourself or eating out?
records.zomi: Nangma adingin an huan na deih zaw hiam, pua-a an ne hiam?

records.english: Cooking, because I know exactly what goes into the food.
records.zomi: An huan, an sung ah bang a kihel hiam ka thei kician ahih manin.

records.english: Do you like going to the cinema alone?
records.zomi: Nangma bek-in cinema pai na deih hiam?

records.english: Sometimes, because then I can choose any film I want.
records.zomi: Khatveivei, tua ciangin ka deih film peuhpeuh ka teel thei ahih manin.

records.english: Which do you enjoy more, writing letters or sending messages?
records.zomi: Koi na deih zaw hiam, lai gelh hiam thu khak hiam?

records.english: Letters, though I hardly have time to write them anymore.
records.zomi: Lai, tu-in gelh nading hun ka nei dek nawn kei hangin.

records.english: My eyes sting after I've been reading in poor light.
records.zomi: Meivak hoih lo-in ka sim khit ciangin ka mit a sik hi.

records.english: You should rest your arm for a few days so that it can heal.
records.zomi: A dam theih nadingin ni tawmno sung na ban tawldamsak ding hi.

records.english: Had I warmed up properly before the match, I probably wouldn't have strained my leg.
records.zomi: Kimawlna ma-in hoih takin ka kiman le, ka khe ka sukna kei kha ding hi.

records.english: Whether the pain is serious or not, it's always better to tell someone than to suffer in silence.
records.zomi: Natna a lauhuai hiam a lauhuai kei hiam, dai-a thuak sangin kuamah hilh a hoih zaw tawntung hi.

records.english: A hot water bottle on my stomach usually helps when I have cramps.
records.zomi: Gil a nat ciangin ka gil tungah tui lum bel khat koih in a huh den hi.

records.english: Why are you holding your side like that?
records.zomi: Bang hangin tua bangin na gei na len hiam?

records.english: Although the operation was a success, she was told that the pain might take months to disappear completely.
records.zomi: Zatui sat a hoih hangin a natna a bei kim dingin kha tampi a la kha ding hi, ci-in kihilh hi.

records.english: Tell me if this hurts when I press it.
records.zomi: Ka nek ciangin a na leh hong gen in.

records.english: Not until the swelling had gone down could the doctor tell whether the bone was broken.
records.zomi: A vung a kiam ciang bek siavuan in guh a kek hiam a thei thei hi.

records.english: My father won't admit that his knee hurts, but I can see him wincing.
records.zomi: Ka pa in a khuk a na hi, a pang kei hi, ahi zongin a mai a kisan ka mu hi.

records.english: My grandfather has had pain in his joints for years, but he still works in the garden.
records.zomi: Ka pu in kum tampi sung a guh kizopnate ah natna a nei a, ahi zongin huan ah a sem lai hi.

records.english: It might just be a pulled muscle, but you should get it checked.
records.zomi: Tha a kiloh bek kha ding hi, ahi zongin en sak in.

records.english: I'm sorry I'm walking so slowly — my hip is bothering me today.
records.zomi: Zawl taka ka kalsuan manin hong maisak in — tuni-in ka kawng a na hi.

records.english: On a scale of one to ten, how bad is the pain?
records.zomi: Khat pan sawm dong ah, natna bangzah a hat hiam?

records.english: The cut on my hand opened again when I was washing the dishes.
records.zomi: Kuang ka sil laitakin ka khut-a liamna a kihong kik hi.

records.english: Having stood behind the counter for twelve hours, my aunt could barely feel her feet by the evening.
records.zomi: Nai sawm leh nih sung sum piakna dawhkan nung ah a din khit ciangin nitak ciangin ka ni in a khe a thei dek nawn kei hi.

records.english: Can you show me exactly where the pain is?
records.zomi: Natna koi ah a om hiam kician takin hong etsak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Here, on the left side, just below my ribs.
records.zomi: Hih ah, veilam ah, nakguh nuai mahmah ah.

records.english: Everybody, please stop and stretch your arms before you lift anything else.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, bangmah dang na lak ma-un tawl inla na ban uh zan un.

records.english: If the pain comes back after you've finished the treatment, you may need to see a specialist.
records.zomi: Zatui na zawh khit ciangin natna a hong kik leh siavuan tuamtuam na mu kha ding hi.

records.english: Shall I get you a cushion so that your back is more comfortable?
records.zomi: Na nung a nuam zawk nadingin lukhung khat kong la sak ding hiam?

records.english: The more I ignored the pain in my shoulder, the worse it seemed to get.
records.zomi: Ka liang-a natna ka phawk loh tum semsem ciangin a hoih lo semsem bang hi.

records.english: How long have you had this pain?
records.zomi: Hih natna bangzah sung na nei khin hiam?

records.english: Since Tuesday, and it's getting worse at night.
records.zomi: Pithai ni pan, zan ciangin a hoih lo semsem hi.

records.english: Many people who work in the fields learn to live with back pain, though they shouldn't have to.
records.zomi: Lo-a nasem mi tampi in nung natna tawh om a sin uh hi, tua bangin om lo ding uh hi napi.

records.english: Does anyone have a plaster for my finger?
records.zomi: Ka khutzung adingin plaster kuamah in a nei hiam?

records.english: My mother made me see a doctor because I'd been limping for a week.
records.zomi: Kal khat sung ka khebai ahih manin ka nu in siavuan hong etsak hi.

records.english: I have a terrible headache, so I'm going to lie down in the dark for a while.
records.zomi: Ka lu a na mahmah ahih manin hun tawmno mial sung ah ka lum ding hi.

records.english: Could the pain in your arm have anything to do with the fall you had last month?
records.zomi: Na ban-a natna in kha nung-a na kiatna tawh kizopna a nei kha ding hiam?

records.english: The dentist had to take the tooth out because it was too damaged to save.
records.zomi: A sia lua-in a kem theih nawn loh manin ha siavuan in ha a khawh khia hi.

records.english: Pain can be hard to describe, so doctors often ask patients to compare it to something familiar.
records.zomi: Natna gen siang a haksa thei ahih manin siavuante in a natnate a theih ngeina bangmah tawh kikhaikhin dingin a dong uh hi.

records.english: Would you like me to call the doctor for you?
records.zomi: Siavuan kong sam sak ding hiam?

records.english: I put ice on my ankle to bring the swelling down.
records.zomi: A vung a kiam nadingin ka khe zungkhuk ah tuikhal ka koih hi.

records.english: The physiotherapist gave me some exercises to strengthen my back.
records.zomi: Ka nung a hat nadingin tha kizap siam in kisinna khenkhat hong pia hi.

records.english: Can I do anything to help?
records.zomi: Huh dingin bangmah ka hih thei ding hiam?

records.english: Just bring me some water and close the curtains, please.
records.zomi: Tui hong tawi sak inla, tukvuang puan khak sak bek in.

records.english: My grandmother rubs a little warm oil on her shoulders when they're stiff.
records.zomi: Ka pi in a liangte a khauh ciangin sathau lum tawmno a nul hi.

records.english: My knees ache every time it gets cold.
records.zomi: Khua a vot simin ka khuk a na hi.

records.english: Is the pain sharp or dull?
records.zomi: Natna a hiam hiam, a kuah hiam?

records.english: Sharp when I move, but dull when I'm lying still.
records.zomi: Ka kilawn ciangin a hiam a, ka lup ciangin a kuah hi.

records.english: She had her wisdom teeth removed, and her face was swollen for a week.
records.zomi: A ha nunungte a khawh khia ahih manin kal khat sung a mai a vung hi.

records.english: Could you carry my bag up the stairs, since my back is sore?
records.zomi: Ka nung a na ahih manin kahlei tung dong ka ip na pua sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Can you rub my neck for a minute?
records.zomi: Minit khat ka ngawng na nul sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Did the doctor say what was causing your headaches?
records.zomi: Bang in na lu a nasak hiam siavuan in a gen hiam?

records.english: She thinks it's my eyes, so she's sent me to have them tested.
records.zomi: Ka mit hi in a ngaihsun ahih manin en sak dingin hong sawl hi.

records.english: Rather than taking time off work, he carried on for weeks with a pain he should have had checked.
records.zomi: Nasep pan tawlngak sangin, a et sak ding natna khat tawh kal tampi a sem den hi.

records.english: My son fell off his bike and scraped both knees.
records.zomi: Ka tapa a siiksakol tung pan a kia a, a khuk nih a nawl hi.

records.english: My feet hurt so much after the wedding that I danced the last hour barefoot.
records.zomi: Mopawi khit ciangin ka khe a na lua ahih manin nai nunung khat khedap om lo-in ka lam hi.

records.english: My stomach hurts, and I don't feel like eating anything.
records.zomi: Ka gil a na a, bangmah ne ka nuam kei hi.

records.english: What worries me most is not the pain itself but not knowing what's causing it.
records.zomi: Hong lungkhamsak pen pen natna mah hi lo-in bang in a piangsak hiam theih loh ahi hi.

records.english: I've had this cough for so long that my chest aches.
records.zomi: Hih khuh sawt lua ka neih manin ka awm a na hi.

records.english: Don't lift that box with your back bent — bend your knees instead.
records.zomi: Na nung kun-in tua bawm la kei in — na khuk kun zaw in.

records.english: Have you ever had this kind of pain before?
records.zomi: Hih bang natna na nei ngei hiam?

records.english: The nurse used a small light to look into my ear.
records.zomi: Nurse in ka bil sung en dingin meivak neu khat a zang hi.

records.english: It hurts when I swallow, and my throat feels very dry.
records.zomi: Ka val ciangin a na a, ka dangka a keu mahmah hi.

records.english: The new shoes gave me blisters on both heels.
records.zomi: Khedap thakte in ka khe nung nih ah a vawk sak hi.

records.english: My back hurts after carrying the rice sacks all morning.
records.zomi: Zingsang bup buh ip ka pua khit ciangin ka nung a na hi.

records.english: The pain in my wrist started after I'd been typing for hours without a break.
records.zomi: Tawlngak lo-in nai tampi ka type khit ciangin ka khut zungkhuk natna a kipan hi.

records.english: Sitting at the computer all day gave her a stiff neck.
records.zomi: Ni bup computer kiang ah a tut ahih manin a ngawng a khauh hi.

records.english: I couldn't sleep because my tooth was aching so badly.
records.zomi: Ka ha a na lua ahih manin ka ihmu thei kei hi.

records.english: Have you ever been really lost?
records.zomi: Na mang taktak ngei hiam?

records.english: Once, in a desert, until a shepherd pointed me toward the road.
records.zomi: Khatvei, gamkeu khat ah, tuucing khat in lampi lam hong lak dong.

records.english: Could you show us the photos from your trip to the mountains?
records.zomi: Mual tung lam na khualzinna lim hong etsak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Gladly, and I'll tell you the story behind each one.
records.zomi: Lungdam takin, a khat ciat' tangthu kong gen ding hi.

records.english: What is the most valuable thing you've learned from older people?
records.zomi: Upate pan na sin manphat pen bang ahi hiam?

records.english: That most problems that feel enormous today will look much smaller in a year.
records.zomi: Tuni-a lian mahmah bang buaina tamzaw kum khat sungin a neu mahmah bang kimu ding hi, cih ahi hi.

records.english: What was it like to grow up without electricity?
records.zomi: Meivak om lo-in khanglian pen bangci a om hiam?

records.english: We went to bed when it got dark and woke with the birds, so the days felt very long.
records.zomi: Khua a mial ciangin i lum a, vasate tawh i thou a, tua ahih manin ni te a sau mahmah bang hi.

records.english: What would you have done differently if you'd known how your life would turn out?
records.zomi: Na nuntakna bangci-in a pai ding hiam na theih le, bang na hih tuam ding hiam?

records.english: Very little, though I'd have learned my mother's recipes before it was too late.
records.zomi: Tawmno bek, a nun lua ma-in ka nu' an huan dante ka sin ding hi.

records.english: Who taught you to use a sewing machine?
records.zomi: Puan khuina set zat dan kua in hong hilh hiam?

records.english: My aunt, on the old machine she brought from the city.
records.zomi: Ka ni, khuapi pan a tawi set lui tungah.

records.english: Why did you decide to become a teacher?
records.zomi: Bang hangin saya suak dingin na khensat hiam?

records.english: A teacher believed in me when I was failing, and I wanted to give other children the same chance.
records.zomi: Ka zawh loh laitakin saya khat in hong um a, naupang dangte tungah hun kibang pia ka deih hi.

records.english: What happened the first time you cooked for your in-laws?
records.zomi: Na sungte adingin an na huan masak pen-in bang a piang hiam?

records.english: I burned the rice, but my mother-in-law ate it all anyway.
records.zomi: Buh ka kangsak a, ahi zongin ka sungnu in a vekpi-in a ne hi.

records.english: When did you have to be braver than you thought you could be?
records.zomi: Bang ciangin na ngaihsut sangin na hang zaw ding a kisam hiam?

records.english: Probably standing up in front of the whole village to say that the new dam was a bad idea.
records.zomi: Khua bup mai ah ding-in tui kham thak a hoih kei hi, ka cih hun kha ding hi.

records.english: What did you do with your first salary?
records.zomi: Na nasep man masa pen bang na hih hiam?

records.english: I bought my mother a new cooking pot and kept the rest for school.
records.zomi: Ka nu adingin an huan beel thak khat ka lei a, a dang sang adingin ka koih hi.

records.english: What did you learn from losing your business?
records.zomi: Na sumbawl na mansuah pan bang na sin hiam?

records.english: That I'd tried to do everything myself, instead of asking for help.
records.zomi: Huhna ngen sangin khempeuh keimah bek in ka sem tum hi, cih.

records.english: Are you allowed to talk about your time in the army?
records.zomi: Galkap-a na om hun thu na gen thei hiam?

records.english: Some of it, but there are things I promised never to discuss.
records.zomi: A khen khat, ahi zongin gen ngei lo dinga ka kiciam thu a om hi.

records.english: Should young people be told about the hardships their grandparents went through?
records.zomi: A pu leh pite' haksatna tuakte khangnote kihilh ding hiam?

records.english: I believe so, because knowing what came before helps them understand why things are the way they are now.
records.zomi: Kihilh ding in ka um hi, a ma-a piangte theih in tu-in bang hangin a om bangin a om hiam a theih nadingun hong huh ahih manin.

records.english: Can I record you telling the story about the flood?
records.zomi: Tuiciim tangthu na gen laitakin ka record thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, but wait until the children are here too.
records.zomi: Thei hi, ahi zongin naupangte zong hih ah a om dong ngak in.

records.english: Why do you still keep your first pair of work boots?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na nasep khedap masa pen na kem lai hiam?

records.english: They remind me how far I've come since my first day on the building site.
records.zomi: Inn lamna mun-a ka ni masa pen pan bangzah ka khang khin hiam hong phawksak hi.

records.english: Why did you go back to university at fifty?
records.zomi: Bang hangin kum sawmnga ciangin sangpi ah na kik hiam?

records.english: I'd always wanted to study history, and my children were finally grown up.
records.zomi: Tangthu sin ka deih tawntung a, ka tate a tawp-in a khang khin uh hi.

records.english: When I was nineteen, I left home with one bag and a phone number written on my hand.
records.zomi: Kum sawm leh kua ka phak ciangin ip khat leh ka khut tungah kigelh phone number khat tawh inn ka nusia hi.

records.english: The number belonged to a cousin I'd never met, and he gave me a bed and my first job in the city.
records.zomi: Number pen ka muh ngei loh ka sanggam khat' ahi a, khuapi ah lupna leh nasep masa pen hong pia hi.

records.english: What was the hardest part of moving to a new country?
records.zomi: Gam thak khat ah tuah ah a haksa pen bang ahi hiam?

records.english: Not understanding the jokes, because laughter is the last thing you learn.
records.zomi: Nuihzatna thu theih loh, nuihna pen na sin nunung pen ahih manin.

records.english: Is it possible to visit the house where you were born?
records.zomi: Na suahna inn na veh thei hiam?

records.english: It is, though a different family lives there now and has painted it bright yellow.
records.zomi: Thei hi, tu-in innkuan dang a om a, eng mahmah-in a zeek uh hangin.

records.english: Where did you learn to climb trees like that?
records.zomi: Tua bang singkung kah dan koi ah na sin hiam?

records.english: In the forest behind our village, where my brothers dared me to go higher every day.
records.zomi: I khua nung-a gam sung ah, ka sanggam pasalte in ni simin a sang zaw-a kah dingin hong ham uh hi.

records.english: Why weren't you allowed to go to secondary school?
records.zomi: Bang hangin sang lian kah dingin kiphal lo na hi hiam?

records.english: My parents needed me on the farm, and girls in our village rarely studied then.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in lo ah hong kisam uh a, tua hun-in i khua-a numei naupangte sang a kah tawm uh hi.

records.english: Did anyone ever help you when you were in trouble abroad?
records.zomi: Gamdang ah buaina na tuak ciangin kuamah in hong huh ngei hiam?

records.english: A family I'd never met let me sleep in their house for three nights.
records.zomi: Ka muh ngei loh innkuan khat in a inn ah zan thum hong ihmusak hi.

records.english: What advice did your father give you before you left home?
records.zomi: Inn na nusiat ma-in na pa in bang thuhilhna hong pia hiam?

records.english: He told me to always carry a little money in my shoe for emergencies.
records.zomi: Lauhuaina hun adingin ka khedap sung ah sum tawmno tawi tawntung dingin hong hilh hi.

records.english: How has sharing your experiences helped other people?
records.zomi: Na tuakte na hawm in midangte bangci-in a huh hiam?

records.english: Several young mothers have told me that my story made them feel less alone after their babies were born.
records.zomi: Nu khangno tampi in a naungek a suak khit ciangin ka tangthu in amau bek om lo bangin a kisaksak hi, hong ci uh hi.

records.english: Which job taught you the most?
records.zomi: Koi nasep in hong hilh tam pen hiam?

records.english: Washing dishes in a hotel, because I learned to work fast and stay polite.
records.zomi: Zinbuuk ah kuang sil, manlang taka sem leh zahtak taka om ka sin ahih manin.

records.english: May I tell your story at the meeting tonight?
records.zomi: Tuni zan kikhopna ah na tangthu ka gen thei ding hiam?

records.english: You may, as long as you don't use my name.
records.zomi: Na gen thei hi, ka min na zat kei leh.

records.english: Had you not taken that job in the city, would you ever have met your wife?
records.zomi: Khuapi-a tua nasep na la kei le, na zi na mu ngei ding hiam?

records.english: Almost certainly not, since she'd never set foot in our village.
records.zomi: Mu lo mahmah ding ing, amah i khua ah a khe a koih ngei kei ahih manin.

records.english: How did you learn to fix motorbikes?
records.zomi: Motorbike bawl siam dan bangci-in na sin hiam?

records.english: My uncle let me help in his workshop every afternoon after school.
records.zomi: Sang khit ciangin nitak lam simin ka pa neu in a nasepna inn ah hong huh sak hi.

records.english: Why do some people find it so hard to talk about their past?
records.zomi: Bang hangin mi khenkhatte in a hun lui uh thu gen a haksa sa uh hiam?

records.english: Some memories are painful, and speaking about them can feel like living through them again.
records.zomi: Phawkna khenkhatte a na a, a thu gen pen kik-in tuak bang a hi thei hi.

records.english: How did you meet your best friend?
records.zomi: Na lawm hoih pen bangci-in na mu hiam?

records.english: We sat next to each other on our first day at university.
records.zomi: Sangpi i kah ni masa pen-in i kiang ah i tu uh hi.

records.english: Whoever arrives first in the morning switches on the lights and greets the others as they come in.
records.zomi: Zingsang a tung masa peuhpeuh in meivak a vaksak a, a dangte a hong tun ciangun a hopih hi.

records.english: Please don't greet the patients loudly in the early morning, since many are still asleep.
records.zomi: Zingsang tung ah natnate ging sang takin hopih kei un, tampi a ihmu lai uh ahih manin.

records.english: Her manager stood beside her for the first week to show her how to welcome people.
records.zomi: A manager in mite muak dan etsak dingin kal masa sung a kiang ah a ding hi.

records.english: Children aren't allowed into the classroom until they've greeted the teacher at the door.
records.zomi: Naupangte kongkhak ah saya a hopih ma-un kilasi ah lut thei lo uh hi.

records.english: My father always says, "A greeting costs nothing but opens every door."
records.zomi: Ka pa in, “Hopihna in bangmah a man kei hi, ahi zongin kongkhak khempeuh a hong hi,” a ci tawntung hi.

records.english: Our new neighbor greeted us in her own language, and we were too embarrassed to admit we didn't understand.
records.zomi: I inn veng thak in amah' pau tawh hong hopih a, i thei kei hi, ci-in pan dingin i zak lua uh hi.

records.english: The next day we asked her to teach us the greeting, and now we use it every time we see her.
records.zomi: A zing ni-in a hopihna hong hilh dingin i ngen a, tu-in a kimuh simun i zang hi.

records.english: Do I need to greet everyone again when I come back from lunch?
records.zomi: Sun an pan ka hong kik ciangin mi khempeuh ka hopih kik ding hiam?

records.english: No, a quick smile is enough, unless someone new has arrived.
records.zomi: Hi lo hi, kuamah thak a om kei leh nuihna tom khat a kicing hi.

records.english: In our office, we're asked not to shout greetings across the room during phone calls.
records.zomi: I office ah phone samna laitakin khan gal lam pan hopihna kou lo dingin kingen hi.

records.english: My son mumbles a greeting without looking up, so I've asked him to look at people when he greets them.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in en lo-in a hopihna a phuk ahih manin a hopih ciangin mite en dingin ka ngen hi.

records.english: If you aren't sure how formal to be, a polite greeting and a smile are always safe.
records.zomi: Bangzah zahtak taka om ding hiam na kician kei leh zahtak taka hopihna leh nuihna in a bit tawntung hi.

records.english: How can I greet people in a noisy factory where nobody can hear me?
records.zomi: Kuamah in hong za thei lo factory ging khat ah mite bangci-in ka hopih thei ding hiam?

records.english: May I open the door and welcome the guests myself, Mom?
records.zomi: Nu, kongkhak hong-in khualte keimah in ka muak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Nobody greeted me on my first morning at the factory, and I almost went home.
records.zomi: Factory ah ka zingsang masa pen-in kuamah in hong hopih kei a, inn ah ka ciah dek hi.

records.english: Then the supervisor asked everyone to welcome new workers.
records.zomi: Tua ciangin enkaipa in nasem thakte muak dingin mi khempeuh a ngen hi.

records.english: Don't greet older relatives with your hands in your pockets, because in our family that seems disrespectful.
records.zomi: Sanggam upate na khut ip sung koih-in hopih kei in, i innkuan ah tua pen zahtakna om lo bang hi.

records.english: The more often you greet your neighbors, the easier it becomes to ask them for help when you need it.
records.zomi: Na inn vengte na hopih den semsem ciangin na kisap ciangin huhna ngen a baih semsem hi.

records.english: Rather than correcting the children's greetings in front of others, our teacher speaks to each child quietly.
records.zomi: Midangte mai ah naupangte' hopihna bawl siang sangin i saya in naupang khat ciat dai takin a kiho pih hi.

records.english: My grandfather was sad because I didn't greet him.
records.zomi: Ka pu ka hopih kei ahih manin a lungkham hi.

records.english: I forgot to greet my boss today.
records.zomi: Tuni-in ka makaipa hopih ka mangngilh hi.

records.english: Smile when you greet people, or your words may sound unfriendly.
records.zomi: Mite na hopih ciangin nui in, a hi kei leh na kammal lawmta lo bangin a ging kha ding hi.

records.english: My phone's alarm reminds me to call my parents every evening and wish them good night.
records.zomi: Ka phone alarm in nitak simin ka nu leh ka pa sam-in zan nuam ding ka deihsak nadingin hong phawksak hi.

records.english: I felt awkward greeting the same colleague five times in one morning.
records.zomi: Zingsang khat sungin nasem lawm kibang ngavei ka hopih ciangin ka zak hi.

records.english: A friend told me that a small nod is enough after the first greeting of the day.
records.zomi: Ni khat-a hopihna masa khit ciangin lu kun neu khat a kicing hi, ci-in ka lawm khat in hong hilh hi.

records.english: Next time, stop and greet the older people first, even if you're in a hurry.
records.zomi: A zom ciangin, na manlang zongin, tawl inla upate a masa-in hopih in.

records.english: At the clinic, the nurses greet each patient by name so that nobody feels forgotten.
records.zomi: Siavuan inn ah nursete in kuamah mangngilh lo bangin a kisak nadingun natna khat ciat a min tawh a hopih uh hi.

records.english: What I find hardest is knowing when to stop greeting someone I've already seen earlier in the day.
records.zomi: Ka haksa sak pen pen ni sung-a ka muh khin mi khat hopih tawp ding hun theih ahi hi.

records.english: Do you mind being greeted before you've had your coffee?
records.zomi: Na khawfi na dawn ma-in kuamah in hong hopih leh na lungkham hiam?

records.english: Could you welcome my parents at the gate for me while I park the car?
records.zomi: Mawtaw ka koih laitakin kongpi ah ka nu leh ka pa na muak sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: To avoid waking her, I now check the time difference before I phone my aunt abroad.
records.zomi: A phawngsak lo nadingin gamdang-a ka ni ka sam ma-in tu-in hun kilamdanna ka en hi.

records.english: If greetings are causing tension in your office, it might help to agree together on what feels respectful.
records.zomi: Na office ah hopihna in buaina a piangsak leh bang a zahtakhuai hiam khawm-in kithukim a huh kha ding hi.

records.english: We solved the problem by making a habit of greeting him by name every time we leave.
records.zomi: I pai khiat simin a min tawh amah hopih ngeina i bawl in buaina i bawl siang hi.

records.english: Greetings that feel natural in one culture can seem far too formal in another, which can cause misunderstandings.

records.english: What if I greet someone the wrong way?
records.zomi: Kuamah dik lo takin ka hopih leh bang a piang ding hiam?

records.english: Apologize with a smile, and most people will forgive you at once.
records.zomi: Nuih-in maisak ngen in, mi tamzaw in a man takin hong maisak ding uh hi.

records.english: When the power was cut one evening, our neighbors greeted us with candles and invited us in.
records.zomi: Nitak khat meivak a mit ciangin i inn vengte in khawimeivaak tawh hong hopih uh a, hong sam uh hi.

records.english: The shopkeeper never smiled, so I started greeting him first, and now he always greets me back.
records.zomi: Dawr neipa a nui ngei kei ahih manin a masa-in ka hopih kipan a, tu-in hong hopih kik tawntung hi.

records.english: Is it rude not to say good morning to people on the bus?
records.zomi: Bus tungah mite “Zingpha” ci lo pen zahtakna om lo ahi hiam?

records.english: Not in the city, but in my village we greet everyone.
records.zomi: Khuapi ah hi lo hi, ahi zongin ka khua ah mi khempeuh i hopih hi.

records.english: Is it all right to greet the principal casually, or should I be more formal?
records.zomi: Sang makaipa pangai takin hopih a hoih hiam, zahtak zaw takin ka om ding hiam?

records.english: Would it help if the school asked older pupils to welcome each new family at the gate during the first week?
records.zomi: Kal masa sungin sang in sangnaupang upate kongpi ah innkuan thak khat ciat muak dingin a ngen leh a huh ding hiam?

records.english: Had I known that my mother-in-law expected a formal greeting, I would never have simply waved at her.
records.zomi: Ka sungnu in zahtakna hopihna a lamen hi, cih ka theih le, khut vaai bek ka hih ngei kei ding hi.

records.english: Having moved to a city where nobody greets strangers, I had to stop greeting everyone I passed in the street.
records.zomi: Kuamah in mi theih lohte a hopih loh khuapi khat ah ka tuah khit ciangin lampi tung-a ka khen khempeuh hopih ka tawpsak hi.

records.english: My grandmother can't hear well, so I greet her slowly and clearly, face to face.
records.zomi: Ka pi a za hoih kei ahih manin a mai lam pan zawl taka kician takin ka hopih hi.

records.english: The new receptionist was too nervous to greet anyone.
records.zomi: Mi muakna nasem thak a lau lua ahih manin kuamah a hopih zo kei hi.

records.english: Nobody greets the night guard, and he feels lonely.
records.zomi: Zan kongpi kemtu kuamah in a hopih kei uh a, a lungngai hi.

records.english: I keep forgetting that it's already evening in my sister's country when I call her in the morning.
records.zomi: Zingsangin ka sanggam nu ka sam ciangin a gam ah nitak khin hi, cih ka mangngilh den hi.

records.english: Whenever I lose my voice, I greet my neighbors with a wave and a smile instead.
records.zomi: Ka aw a mang ciangin tua sangin khut vaai leh nuihna tawh ka inn vengte ka hopih hi.

records.english: Should I greet the cleaner, even though she seems too busy to talk?
records.zomi: Kiho dingin a buai lua bang hangin siangsaktu ka hopih ding hiam?

records.english: The bus driver greets every passenger, and it makes the long ride feel friendlier.
records.zomi: Bus mawngpa in tuang khempeuh a hopih a, tua in khualzinna sau a nuamsak zaw hi.

records.english: Although a simple greeting may seem unimportant, it can be the only kind word some people hear all day.
records.zomi: Hopihna baih khat a thupi lo bang hangin mi khenkhatte in ni bup a zak kammal nem khat bek ahi thei hi.

records.english: Please don't stop a busy colleague for a long chat — just greet them quietly.
records.zomi: Nasem lawm buai khat sawt taka kiho dingin tawlsak kei in — dai takin hopih bek in.

records.english: Not until I worked night shifts did I realize how lonely an evening without any greetings could be.
records.zomi: Zan nasep ka sep ciang bek hopihna om lo nitak bangzah a lungngaihhuai hiam ka thei hi.

records.english: How do you greet someone whose name you've forgotten?
records.zomi: Na mangngilh mi khat bangci-in na hopih hiam?

records.english: Greet them warmly and wait for the conversation to remind you.
records.zomi: Lungsim lum takin hopih inla, kihona in hong phawksak dong ngak in.

records.english: You can greet the whole class at once instead of greeting each student separately.
records.zomi: Sangnaupang khat ciat hopih sangin kilasi bup khatvei-in na hopih thei hi.

records.english: My little brother greets everyone in the street.
records.zomi: Ka nau pasal in lampi tung-a mi khempeuh a hopih hi.

records.english: Why does your grandmother get upset if we don't greet her first?
records.zomi: Bang hangin a masa-in i hopih kei leh ka pi a lungkham hiam?

records.english: In her family, the youngest always greeted the oldest, and she still expects it.
records.zomi: Amah' innkuan ah a neu pen in a upa pen a hopih tawntung a, tu dong a lamen lai hi.

records.english: Please don't introduce yourself by talking about your salary.
records.zomi: Na nasep man thu gen-in na kitheisak kei in.

records.english: The microphone stopped working just as I stood up to introduce myself.
records.zomi: Kitheisak dingin ka din laitakin microphone a sem nawn kei hi.

records.english: I talked louder and walked closer to the audience, and it was fine.
records.zomi: Ging sang zawin ka gen a, ngaite kiang zaw ah ka pai a, a hoih hi.

records.english: Whoever chairs the meeting should give new members time to introduce themselves properly.
records.zomi: Kikhopna makaipa in member thakte hoih taka a kitheisak nadingun hun a pia ding hi.

records.english: The more often you introduce yourself to strangers, the less frightening it becomes.
records.zomi: Mi theih lohte kiangah na kitheisak den semsem ciangin a lauhuai tawm semsem hi.

records.english: Why do you introduce yourself with your father's name as well as your own?
records.zomi: Bang hangin nangma' min tawh na pa' min zong gen-in na kitheisak hiam?

records.english: May I say a few words about myself before we start planning?
records.zomi: Gel kipan ma-in keimah thu kammal tawmno ka gen thei ding hiam?

records.english: If people keep forgetting your name, it may help to connect it to something they'll remember.
records.zomi: Mite in na min a mangngilh den uh leh a phawk thei ding uh bangmah tawh kizopsak in a huh kha ding hi.

records.english: Since my accent is strong, I speak a little more slowly when I meet people for the first time.
records.zomi: Ka pau gin a hat ahih manin mite ka muh masak ciangin tawmno zawl zawin ka gen hi.

records.english: Our church asks newcomers to stand up and introduce themselves, which some people find frightening.
records.zomi: I pawlpi in hong thakte ding-a kitheisak dingin a ngen a, tua pen mi khenkhatte in a lauhuai sa uh hi.

records.english: The pastor now invites them to meet people over tea after the service instead.
records.zomi: Pastor in tu-in tua sangin pawlpi kikhopna khit ciangin tea dawn-in mite mu dingin a sam hi.

records.english: When the teacher asked us to introduce ourselves, my mind went completely blank.
records.zomi: Saya in kitheisak dingin hong ngen ciangin ka lungsim a awng kim hi.

records.english: She let me sit down and try again at the end of the lesson, which helped a lot.
records.zomi: A tut sak a, hilhna tawp ciangin kik-in sin dingin hong phal a, tua in a huh mahmah hi.

records.english: At our factory, visitors must give the guard their name and the reason for their visit before they enter.
records.zomi: I factory ah khual hongte in a lut ma-un kongpi kemtu kiangah a min leh a hong hang uh a gen ding uh hi.

records.english: The online meeting froze just as I began to introduce myself.
records.zomi: Ka kitheisak kipat laitakin online kikhopna a tawp hi.

records.english: I always introduce my grandmother first, because she likes to be recognized.
records.zomi: Ka pi a masa-in ka kitheisak tawntung hi, a kitheih a deih ahih manin.

records.english: What's a good way to show an interviewer who you are in the first minute?
records.zomi: Minit masa sungin interview la kiangah kua na hi hiam etsak dan hoih bang ahi hiam?

records.english: Talk about your training first, and then mention one thing you're proud of.
