records.zomi: I gam ah tua adingin mipi vote a kisam ding a, tua ahih manin mipi in thu nunung a nei ding uh hi.

records.english: The president signed the new law with a special pen, which was later given to a museum.
records.zomi: President in thukham thak khuai tuam khat tawh a suaksak a, a nung ciangin museum kiangah kipia hi.

records.english: Whoever becomes the next mayor will have to deal with the town's water shortage first.
records.zomi: Khuapi makaipa zom a suak peuhpeuh in khuapi tui kiamna a masa-in a bawl siang ding hi.

records.english: Ministers in our country must report to parliament regularly to explain their decisions.
records.zomi: I gam-a minister te in a khensatnate gen siang dingin parliament kiangah a tawntung-in a gen ding uh hi.

records.english: Our town council asked the Ministry of Health for a new clinic.
records.zomi: I khuapi council in Ministry of Health kiangah siavuan inn thak khat a ngen hi.

records.english: My sister works as a secretary in the prime minister's office.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu prime minister' office ah secretary-in a sem hi.

records.english: Who is the head of the government in your country?
records.zomi: Na gam ah kumpi lu kua ahi hiam?

records.english: In our country, it's the prime minister, while the president has a mostly ceremonial role.
records.zomi: I gam ah prime minister ahi a, president in pawi nasep bek a nei hi.

records.english: The new minister of education wants every village to have a library.
records.zomi: Education minister thak in khua khempeuh in laibu inn a neih a deih hi.

records.english: The prime minister's office released a statement about the strike this morning.
records.zomi: Prime minister' office in tuni zingsangin nasep tawpna thu-ah thu a suaksak hi.

records.english: Why did the minister resign?
records.zomi: Bang hangin minister in a nasep a nusia hiam?

records.english: He was accused of using government money for his family's travel.
records.zomi: A innkuan khualzinna adingin kumpi sum a zang hi, ci-in kihek hi.

records.english: Which ministry looks after the national parks?
records.zomi: Koi ministry in gam huan lian te a kem hiam?

records.english: Civil servants in the ministries prepare the reports that ministers present to the public.
records.zomi: Ministry te sung-a kumpi nasemte in minister te in mipi kiangah a gen ding report te a bawl uh hi.

records.english: The Ministry of Finance decides how much money each region will receive.
records.zomi: Ministry of Finance in gam khen khat ciat in sum bangzah a ngah ding hiam a khensat hi.

records.english: Are we allowed to take photos inside the government building?
records.zomi: Kumpi inn sung ah lim i la thei ding hiam?

records.english: Not inside, but you can take as many as you like in the garden.
records.zomi: Sung lam ah thei lo hi, ahi zongin huan sung ah na deih tan na la thei hi.

records.english: The president gave a speech on television last night.
records.zomi: Zanni zanin president in TV tungah thu a gen hi.

records.english: The prime minister was criticized for appointing his close friends to senior positions.
records.zomi: Prime minister in a lawm kinaite mun sang ah a koih manin kihek hi.

records.english: The minister visited our school to see the new classrooms.
records.zomi: Kilasi thakte en dingin minister in i sang a veh hi.

records.english: Rather than announcing the new policy on television, the minister chose to visit the villages and explain it in person.
records.zomi: TV tungah gelna thak gen sangin minister in khuate a veh-in amah mah in a gen siang dingin a teel hi.

records.english: Having served as mayor for twelve years, she knew almost every family in the town by name.
records.zomi: Kum sawm leh nih sung khuapi makaipa a hih khit ciangin khuapi-a innkuan khempeuh dek a min tawh a thei hi.

records.english: Not until the minister visited the hospital herself did she understand how crowded the wards had become.
records.zomi: Minister amah mah in zato a veh ciang bek zato khante bangzah a dim hiam a thei hi.

records.english: The governor announced that schools would stay closed because of the floods.
records.zomi: Tuiciim hangin sangte a kikhak lai ding hi, ci-in governor in a gen hi.

records.english: Who should I contact if the government office keeps losing my documents?
records.zomi: Kumpi office in ka laite a mansuah den leh kua ka sam ding hiam?

records.english: The Ministry of Transport is building a new road to connect the mountain villages.
records.zomi: Ministry of Transport in mual tung khuate kizopsak dingin lampi thak khat a bawl hi.

records.english: The president visited the families who had lost their homes in the earthquake.
records.zomi: Leiling ah a inn mansuah innkuante president in a veh hi.

records.english: The more relaxed the host is, the more comfortable the visitors usually feel.
records.zomi: Inn neipa a nuam semsem ciangin khual hongte zong a nuam semsem uh hi.

records.english: The welcome banner fell down in the wind just before the bride's family arrived.
records.zomi: Moulai innkuan a tun ma-un muakna puan lian huih in a kiatsak hi.

records.english: Two cousins climbed up and tied it again with fishing line.
records.zomi: Sanggam nih a kah uh a, nga mat khau tawh a khih kik uh hi.

records.english: How do you welcome guests when you're too ill to get out of bed?
records.zomi: Lupna pan na thou zo lo dingin na dam kei ciangin khualte bangci-in na muak hiam?

records.english: Why did the visitors look so uncomfortable?
records.zomi: Bang hangin khual hongte a nuam lo bang uh hiam?

records.english: Nobody had offered them a seat, and they didn't like to ask.
records.zomi: Kuamah in tutna a pia kei uh a, ngen zong a nuam kei uh hi.

records.english: We weren't expecting so many people, so the neighbors lent us chairs and plates.
records.zomi: Mi tam lua i lamen kei ahih manin inn vengte in tutna leh kuang hong ngetsak uh hi.

records.english: How can we make visitors who don't speak our language feel welcome?
records.zomi: I pau a thei lo khual hongte kimuak bangin bangci-in i kisaksak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Smile, use simple gestures, and learn at least one word of greeting in their language.
records.zomi: Nui inla, khut lahna baih zang inla, a pau uh-a hopihna kammal khat bek sin in.

records.english: Our guests arrived an hour early, while I was still cleaning the floor.
records.zomi: I khualte nai khat ma-in a hong tung uh a, tual ka siangsak laitak ahi hi.

records.english: I gave them tea on the porch, and they didn't seem to mind waiting.
records.zomi: Kongmai ah tea ka pia a, ngak dingin a lungkham bang kei uh hi.

records.english: Where should the guests put their bags?
records.zomi: Khualte in a ip uh koi ah a koih ding uh hiam?

records.english: Had we known that our guests were vegetarian, we wouldn't have prepared a whole roast chicken.
records.zomi: I khualte sa a ne lo uh hi, cih i theih le, aksa bup kiem i bawl kei ding hi.

records.english: My grandmother says, "A guest who leaves hungry is a shame on the house."
records.zomi: Ka pi in, “Gilkial-a pai khia khual pen inn adingin zahlakna ahi hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: However small their house was, my parents never let a visitor leave without sharing a meal with us.
records.zomi: A inn uh bangzah ta in neu zongin ka nu leh ka pa in khual hong khat i an ne khawm lo-in a pai khiatsak ngei kei uh hi.

records.english: Not until the visitors had left did we notice that the guest towels were still in the washing machine.
records.zomi: Khual hongte a pai khit uh ciang bek khualte' puan nulte puan silna set sung ah a om lai hi, cih i thei hi.

records.english: Is it all right to ask visitors to leave their umbrellas outside?
records.zomi: Khual hongte a kawl lukhu uh pua ah nusia dingin ngen a hoih hiam?

records.english: Our dog jumped on the visitor and tore her sleeve.
records.zomi: I ui khual tungah a diang a, a puan ban a kek sak hi.

records.english: I offered to have the sleeve mended, and now the dog stays in the yard when guests come.
records.zomi: A ban bawl siang sak dingin ka kipia a, tu-in khualte a hong ciangun ui tual ah a om hi.

records.english: What made you hire a translator for the visit?
records.zomi: Bang in veh adingin lehkiktu na sawlsak hiam?

records.english: Last year the visitors and our staff couldn't understand each other, and the whole meeting was wasted.
records.zomi: Kum nung in khual hongte leh i nasemte a kitheih kei uh a, kikhopna bup a mang hi.

records.english: Rather than apologizing for our small house, my father simply makes every visitor feel that there's plenty of room.
records.zomi: I inn neu adingin maisak ngen sangin ka pa in khual khempeuh mun a tam hi, cih a kisaksak bek hi.

records.english: When visitors come to our house, we always offer them water first.
records.zomi: Khual hongte i inn a hong ciangun a masa-in tui i pia tawntung hi.

records.english: My uncle arrived with no warning, and we had no bed for him.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu gen lo-in a hong tung a, amah adingin lupna i nei kei hi.

records.english: We moved the children into our room so that he could have theirs.
records.zomi: Naupangte' khan amah' a hih theih nadingin naupangte i khan sung ah i suan hi.

records.english: The guest room had been painted the day before, and it still smelled strongly of paint.
records.zomi: Khualzin khan zanni-in kizeek a, zeek namtui a nam lai mahmah hi.

records.english: We opened every window and put a bowl of vinegar in the corner to take away the smell.
records.zomi: Tukvuang khempeuh i hong a, namtui a bei nadingin kil ah thuk tui kuang khat i koih hi.

records.english: A visitor's coat was accidentally taken home by another guest.
records.zomi: Khual khat' kawt khual dang khat in khialh-in inn ah a tawi hi.

records.english: We phoned everyone who had been at the party, and the coat was returned the next morning.
records.zomi: Pawi-a om mi khempeuh phone tawh i sam a, a zing zingsangin kawt a hong kik hi.

records.english: In our house, shoes are not allowed in the prayer room, so we keep slippers by the door for visitors.
records.zomi: I inn ah thungetna khan sung ah khedap kiphal lo ahih manin khual hongte adingin kongkhak kiang ah khedap neu i koih hi.

records.english: Whoever opens the door should offer the visitor a seat before asking why they've come.
records.zomi: Kongkhak a hong peuhpeuh in bang hangin a hong hiam a dot ma-in khual hong tutna a pia ding hi.

records.english: Would you mind showing our guest where the bathroom is?
records.zomi: I khual kiangah ek inn koi ah a om hiam na etsak thei ding hiam?

records.english: The power went off just as our visitors sat down to dinner.
records.zomi: Khual hongte nitak an ne dingin a tut laitakun meivak a mit hi.

records.english: We lit candles and told stories, and the evening turned out to be the best of the year.
records.zomi: Khawimeivaak i hal a, tangthu i gen a, tua nitak kum sung-a a hoih pen a suak hi.

records.english: Having welcomed hundreds of visitors over the years, my grandmother still prepares for each one as if they were royalty.
records.zomi: Kum tampi sung khual hong za tampi a muak khit ciangin ka pi in khat ciat kumpipa' innkuan bangin a kiman lai hi.

records.english: Please don't leave guests standing at the gate while you finish your phone call.
records.zomi: Na phone samna na zawh laitakin khualte kongpi ah dingsak kei in.

records.english: Don't let visitors carry their own bags upstairs.
records.zomi: Khual hongte a ip uh tung lam ah a pua sak kei in.

records.english: What should we do if a visitor arrives while we're eating?
records.zomi: I an nek laitakin khual hong khat a tun leh bang i hih ding hiam?

records.english: Invite them to join us, even if there's only a little food left.
records.zomi: An tawmno bek a om hangin ne khawm dingin sam in.

records.english: If you're expecting important visitors, it might help to prepare a short list of things to tell them about the town.
records.zomi: Khual thupite na lamen leh khuapi thu a hilh ding list tom khat bawl khol in a huh kha ding hi.

records.english: Although welcoming strangers can feel risky, many families in our village still offer shelter to travelers caught by bad weather.
records.zomi: Mi theih lohte muak a lauhuai bang hangin i khua-a innkuan tampi in huihkhua hoih lo-a tuak khualzinte omna a pia lai uh hi.

records.english: The guests' car broke down on the road to our village.
records.zomi: Khualte' mawtaw i khua lampi tungah a sia hi.

records.english: My brother drove out with a rope and towed them the rest of the way.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in khau tawi-in a pai a, a dang lampi bup a kaai hi.

records.english: The visitors were shown around the factory and given lunch in the canteen.
records.zomi: Khual hongte factory kim a kipaipih uh a, anneekna ah sun an a kipia uh hi.

records.english: Visitors to the school must sign in at the office before going to any classroom.
records.zomi: Sang-a khual hongte in kilasi khatpeuh a pai ma-un office ah a min uh a gelh ding uh hi.

records.english: The new receptionist didn't know where to send the visitors, so they waited for an hour.
records.zomi: Mi muakna nasem thak in khual hongte koi ah sawl ding hiam a thei kei ahih manin nai khat a ngak uh hi.

records.english: Now there's a printed map of the building on the reception desk.
records.zomi: Tu-in mi muakna dawhkan tungah inn' map kikhen khat a om hi.

records.english: Could we have avoided the misunderstanding if someone had explained our customs to the visitors before they arrived?
records.zomi: A tun ma-un kuamah in khual hongte kiangah i ngeinate a gen siang le, kithei khialhna i pelh thei ding hiam?

records.english: What I find hardest is welcoming visitors who arrive without warning when the house is a mess.
records.zomi: Ka haksa sak pen pen inn a buai laitakin gen lo-a hong tung khual hongte muak ahi hi.

records.english: The doorbell was broken, so our visitors knocked for ten minutes before we heard them.
records.zomi: Kongkhak ging a sia ahih manin i zak ma-in khual hongte minit sawm sung kongkhak a kiu uh hi.

records.english: We had the doorbell repaired the next day.
records.zomi: A zing ni-in kongkhak ging i bawl siang sak hi.

records.english: Who's going to meet the visitors at the airport?
records.zomi: Vanlengtual ah khual hongte kua in a dawn ding hiam?

records.english: The visitor from the city was nervous because he didn't know our customs.
records.zomi: Khuapi pan hong khual in i ngeinate a theih loh manin a lau hi.

records.english: My aunt put him at ease by asking about his family and his journey.
records.zomi: Ka ni in a innkuan leh a khualzinna thu a dot tawh a lungmuangsak hi.

records.english: My father made me apologize to the neighbor who had waited outside in the rain.
records.zomi: Guah sung-a pua ah a ngak inn veng kiangah ka pa in maisak hong ngetsak hi.

records.english: The guest said, "Please don't go to any trouble for me," but my mother cooked five dishes anyway.
records.zomi: Khual in, “Ka adingin buaipih kei un,” a ci a, ahi zongin ka nu in an nga a huan lai hi.

records.english: Should we meet the visitors at the bus station, or will they find their own way here?
records.zomi: Bus dinna ah khual hongte i dawn ding hiam, amau mah in hih dong lampi a mu ding uh hiam?

records.english: Can you welcome our guests while I finish cooking?
records.zomi: An ka zawh laitakin i khualte na muak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Children, please greet our visitors before you go back to your game.
records.zomi: Naupangte, na kimawlna uh na kik ma-un i khual hongte hopih un.

records.english: Why didn't anyone tell me that the inspectors were coming today?
records.zomi: Bang hangin tuni-in enkaktute a hong ding uh hi, ci-in kuamah in hong hilh kei hiam?

records.english: Could you tell the others I said goodbye, since I can't wait any longer?
records.zomi: Ka ngak zo nawn kei ahih manin goodbye ka ci hi, ci-in a dangte na hilh sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: If you find goodbyes difficult, it may help to plan the next meeting before you part.
records.zomi: Goodbye cih na haksa sak leh na kikhen ma-in kimuh zom gel in a huh kha ding hi.

records.english: I give my mother a long hug every time I leave, just in case.
records.zomi: Ka pai simin a kha ding ka thei kei ahih manin ka nu sawt takin ka pom hi.

records.english: At the funeral, I didn't know what to say to the family as I left.
records.zomi: Mithi vuina ah ka pai ciangin innkuan kiangah bang gen ding hiam ka thei kei hi.

records.english: An older friend told me that a quiet handshake and a few kind words are enough.
records.zomi: Lawm upa khat in khut kilen dai khat leh kammal nem tawmno a kicing hi, hong ci hi.

records.english: The more often you move, the easier saying goodbye becomes, though it never stops hurting.
records.zomi: Na tuah den semsem ciangin goodbye cih a baih semsem hi, a na tawp ngei kei hangin.

records.english: Rather than a sad goodbye, my family prefers a big meal the night before someone leaves.
records.zomi: Goodbye lungkhamhuai sangin ka innkuan in kuamah a pai ma zan-in an lian khat a deih zaw uh hi.

records.english: The call was cut off before I could say goodbye to my brother.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal kiangah goodbye ka cih ma-in samna a tan hi.

records.english: He sent me a message a minute later, and we laughed about it.
records.zomi: Minit khat khit ciangin thu hong khak a, i nuihza pih hi.

records.english: When my grandfather says goodbye, he always tells us, "Go safely, and come back soon."
records.zomi: Ka pu in goodbye a cih ciangin, “Bit takin pai inla, manlang takin hong ciah kik in,” hong ci tawntung hi.

records.english: Can I leave now, or would that upset the host?
records.zomi: Tu-in ka pai thei ding hiam, inn neipa a lungkhamsak ding hiam?

records.english: Please don't leave without saying goodbye to your grandfather.
records.zomi: Na pu kiangah goodbye ci lo-in pai kei in.

records.english: Give your grandmother this letter when you say goodbye, so that she has something to read on the journey.
records.zomi: Khualzinna-ah a sim ding a neih theih nadingin goodbye na cih ciangin na pi hih lai pia in.

records.english: I really do want to say goodbye to everyone, but the bus leaves in five minutes.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh kiangah goodbye ci ka deih mahmah hi, ahi zongin bus minit nga ciangin a pai ding hi.

records.english: I hate saying goodbye at airports, so I usually leave before the plane boards.
records.zomi: Vanlengtual ah goodbye cih ka huat ahih manin vanleng a lut ma-in ka pai khia den hi.

records.english: When I moved abroad, saying goodbye to my parents was the hardest thing I'd ever done.
records.zomi: Gamdang ah ka tuah ciangin ka nu leh ka pa kiangah goodbye cih pen ka hih ngei haksa pen ahi hi.

records.english: We agreed to call each other every Sunday, and we've never missed a week.
records.zomi: Nipini simin kisam dingin i kithukim a, kal khat zong i mansuah ngei kei hi.

records.english: Children, say goodbye to your teacher before you get on the bus.
records.zomi: Naupangte, bus na tuan ma-un na saya uh kiangah goodbye ci un.

records.english: The ship's horn sounded, and the families on the shore began to wave.
records.zomi: Tembaw' ging a ging a, tuipi gei-a innkuante in khut a vaai kipan uh hi.

records.english: Saying goodbye to colleagues when I retired was harder than I expected.
records.zomi: Nasep ka tawp ciangin nasem lawmte kiangah goodbye cih ka lamen sangin a haksa zaw hi.

records.english: However many times my parents leave, my little brother still runs after the car until it disappears.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa bangzah vei a pai zongun ka nau pasal in mawtaw a mang dong a delh lai hi.

records.english: Shall we have a farewell lunch for Mrs. Niang before she moves to the city?
records.zomi: Khuapi ah a tuah ma-in Mrs. Niang adingin kikhenna sun an i bawl ding hiam?

records.english: The farewell cake was dropped on the way to the office.
records.zomi: Kikhenna cake office pai lampi ah a kia hi.

records.english: We bought fruit instead, and Mrs. Niang said it was the healthiest party she'd ever had.
records.zomi: Tua sangin theigah i lei a, Mrs. Niang in a neih ngei pawi lak ah cidam pen ahi hi, a ci hi.

records.english: What do you say to a friend who is moving far away?
records.zomi: Gamla taka tuah ding lawm khat kiangah bang na gen hiam?

records.english: Tell her how much you'll miss her, and ask her to send her new address.
records.zomi: Bangzah na lungngai ding hiam gen inla, a omna thak hong khak dingin ngen in.

records.english: Why did you cry when the neighbors' children left?
records.zomi: Inn vengte' naupangte a pai ciangun bang hangin na kap hiam?

records.english: I'd looked after them every afternoon for three years.
records.zomi: Kum thum sung nitak lam simin ka kem hi.

records.english: Who will say goodbye on behalf of the whole class at the farewell assembly?
records.zomi: Kikhenna sang kikhopna ah kilasi bup aiawh-in kua in goodbye a ci ding hiam?

records.english: Should I hug my boss when I leave the company, or just shake hands?
records.zomi: Company ka nusiat ciangin ka makaipa ka pom ding hiam, khut kilen bek ding hiam?

records.english: How long do goodbyes usually take in your family?
records.zomi: Na innkuan ah goodbye cih a tamzaw-in bangzah a sawt hiam?

records.english: My aunt left so suddenly that nobody had time to thank her for her help.
records.zomi: Ka ni manlang lua takin a pai khia a, a huhna adingin kuamah in lungdam gen hun a nei kei hi.

records.english: We wrote her a card the same evening and sent photos of the children.
records.zomi: Tua nitak mah in card khat i gelh sak a, naupangte' lim i khak hi.

records.english: My little sister hides when visitors leave, because she doesn't like goodbyes.
records.zomi: Ka nau nu in goodbye a deih kei ahih manin khual hongte a pai ciangun a bu hi.

records.english: Having said goodbye to so many students over the years, our old teacher still cries at every graduation.
records.zomi: Kum tampi sung sangnaupang tampi kiangah goodbye a cih khit ciangin i saya lui in sang zawhna pawi khempeuh ah a kap lai hi.

records.english: Wouldn't it be kinder to tell the children about the move now, rather than saying goodbye at the last minute?
records.zomi: A nunung pen hun ciangin goodbye cih sangin naupangte tu-in tuah thu hilh a hehpihna zaw hi lo ding hiam?

records.english: Had I known it was the last time I'd see my grandfather, I would have stayed much longer.
records.zomi: Ka pu ka muh nunung pen ahi hi, cih ka theih le, sawt zaw mahmah-in ka om ding hi.

records.english: Although goodbyes can be painful, they remind us how much the people we leave mean to us.
records.zomi: Goodbye a na thei hangin i nusiat mite bangzah a thupi hiam hong phawksak hi.

records.english: My friend's train was delayed, so we had to say goodbye three times on the platform.
records.zomi: Ka lawm' meileng a sawt ahih manin platform tungah thumvei goodbye i ci hi.

records.english: In some families, leaving a gathering without greeting each elder in turn would be considered disrespectful.
records.zomi: Innkuan khenkhatte ah upa khat ciat a zui-in hopih lo-in kikhopna nusia pen zahtakna om lo-in kingaihsun hi.

records.english: Visitors aren't allowed to stay on the ward after eight, so we say goodbye to Mother at the door.
records.zomi: Khual hongte nai giat zawh ciangin zato khan ah om thei lo ahih manin kongkhak ah Nu kiangah goodbye i ci hi.

records.english: Not until the bus had pulled away did I realize I'd forgotten to give my brother his present.
records.zomi: Bus a pai khiat ciang bek ka sanggam pasal a letsong piak ka mangngilh hi, cih ka thei hi.

records.english: How do I leave a party early without seeming rude?
records.zomi: Zahtakna om lo bang lo-in pawi manlang takin bangci-in ka nusia thei ding hiam?

records.english: Thank the host quietly, explain that you have an early start, and slip out.
records.zomi: Inn neipa dai takin lungdam gen inla, zingsang tung ah na kipan ding hi, cih gen inla, dai takin pai khia in.

records.english: Our guests kept saying goodbye but didn't leave for another hour.
records.zomi: I khualte in goodbye a ci den uh a, ahi zongin nai khat behlap a pai khia kei uh hi.

records.english: My father finally offered to walk them to their car, and that did the trick.
records.zomi: A tawp-in ka pa in a mawtaw dong paipih dingin a kipia a, tua in a sem hi.

records.english: My son was so upset when his best friend left that he wouldn't eat.
records.zomi: A lawm hoih pen a pai ciangin ka tapa a lungkham lua ahih manin an a ne nuam kei hi.

records.english: We let him call his friend every Friday, and slowly he began to smile again.
records.zomi: Laithai ni simin a lawm sam dingin i phal a, zawl takin a nui kik kipan hi.

records.english: My son refuses to say goodbye when I drop him off at school.
records.zomi: Sang ah ka nusiat ciangin ka tapa in goodbye a ci nuam kei hi.

records.english: The teacher suggested a quick wave at the gate instead of a long hug, and now he's much happier.
records.zomi: Saya in sau taka pom sangin kongpi ah khut vaai tom khat a gen a, tu-in a lungdam zaw mahmah hi.

records.english: We forgot to say goodbye to our neighbor before we moved away.
records.zomi: I tuah ma-in i inn veng kiangah goodbye ci i mangngilh hi.

records.english: The next week, we sent her a letter and a photo of our new house.
records.zomi: A zom kal in lai khat leh i inn thak lim khat i khak hi.

records.english: What I find hardest about goodbyes is not knowing when I'll see the person again.
records.zomi: Goodbye ah ka haksa sak pen pen tua mi bang ciangin ka mu kik ding hiam ka theih loh ahi hi.

records.english: Whoever leaves the office last on Friday should say goodbye to the night guard and lock the side door.
records.zomi: Laithai ni-in office a nusia nunung pen peuhpeuh in zan kongpi kemtu kiangah goodbye a ci ding a, a gei lam kongkhak a khak ding hi.

records.english: Why do you always walk your guests all the way to the end of the road?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na khualte lampi tawp dong na paipih tawntung hiam?

records.english: My grandmother cries every time we leave, so we promise to call her as soon as we get home.
records.zomi: I pai simin ka pi a kap ahih manin inn i tun pah-in sam dingin i kiciam hi.

records.english: Would it be all right if we said goodbye here, rather than at the station?
records.zomi: Meileng dinna sangin hih ah goodbye i ci leh a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: Is it rude to leave a meeting without saying goodbye?
records.zomi: Goodbye ci lo-in kikhopna nusia pen zahtakna om lo ahi hiam?

records.english: Not if the meeting is large, but a small nod to the chair is polite.
records.zomi: Kikhopna a lian leh hi lo hi, ahi zongin makaipa kiangah lu kun neu khat a zahtakhuai hi.

records.english: Don't promise to visit if you know you won't be able to.
records.zomi: Na veh zo lo ding na theih leh veh dingin kiciam kei in.

records.english: What I find hardest is staying neutral when two of my relatives are quarreling.
records.zomi: Ka haksa sak pen pen ka sanggam nih a kinial laitakun lam khatpeuh pang lo-a om ahi hi.

records.english: Not until my father fell ill did my brothers and I realize how much we needed each other.
records.zomi: Ka pa a dam loh ciang bek kei leh ka sanggam pasalte bangzah i kisam hiam i thei hi.

records.english: My twin brothers are always compared, and they hate it.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal apengte kikhaikhin tawntung uh a, a huat uh hi.

records.english: Our parents now celebrate each twin's achievements separately.
records.zomi: Tu-in i nu leh pa in apeng khat ciat' zawhnate tuamtuam takin a lungdampih uh hi.

records.english: My grandmother feels lonely since my grandfather died.
records.zomi: Ka pu a sih pan kipan ka pi a lungngai hi.

records.english: Each of us visits her on a different evening, so she has company every night.
records.zomi: Zan simin a lawm a neih theih nadingin ei khat ciat in nitak tuamtuam ah i veh hi.

records.english: How did your parents stay close to their own brothers and sisters?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa in amau sanggamte tawh bangci-in a kinai den uh hiam?

records.english: Rather than taking sides, my grandmother listens to both of her sons and then makes them shake hands.
records.zomi: Lam khat pang sangin ka pi in a tapa nihte a ngai a, tua ciangin a khut a kilensak hi.

records.english: Who decides where the family spends the New Year holiday?
records.zomi: Kum thak nopsakna hun innkuan in koi ah a zat ding hiam kua in a khensat hiam?

records.english: The family group chat became so noisy that my grandmother left it.
records.zomi: Innkuan group chat a ging lua ahih manin ka pi in a nusia hi.

records.english: We made a separate chat just for photos, and she rejoined the next day.
records.zomi: Lim adingin bek chat tuam khat i bawl a, a zing ni-in a lut kik hi.

records.english: Why does Grandpa always tell the same stories at dinner?
records.zomi: Bang hangin nitak an ah ka pu in tangthu kibang a gen tawntung hiam?

records.english: Please don't compare your children with each other in front of them.
records.zomi: Na tate a mai uh ah kikhaikhin kei in.

records.english: What should I do if my in-laws keep giving advice I didn't ask for?
records.zomi: Ka sungte in ka ngetloh thuhilhna a pia den uh leh bang ka hih ding hiam?

records.english: Thank them politely and then do what you and your husband think is best.
records.zomi: Zahtak takin lungdam gen inla, tua ciangin nang leh na pasal in a hoih pen na ngaihsut uh hih un.

records.english: My little brother was blamed for breaking the window, but it was the wind.
records.zomi: Tukvuang a sukek in ka nau pasal kimawhsak a, ahi zongin huih ahi hi.

records.english: When my parents found out, they apologized to him and bought him ice cream.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in a theih ciangun maisak a ngen uh a, ice cream a lei sak uh hi.

records.english: My parents stopped speaking to my uncle after an argument about land.
records.zomi: Leitang thu-ah kinialna khat khit ciangin ka nu leh ka pa ka pa neu tawh a kiho nawn kei uh hi.

records.english: It was my little cousin's wedding that finally brought them back together.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam neu' mopawi in a tawp-in a kilemsak kik hi.

records.english: Would you call your brother tonight and tell him you're sorry?
records.zomi: Tuni zanin na sanggam pasal sam-in maisak na ngen ding hiam?

records.english: Can I tell Dad the truth, even though it might make him angry?
records.zomi: Pa a heh kha ding hangin a tak ka hilh thei ding hiam?

records.english: My brother and I argue every time we share a room on holiday.
records.zomi: Nopsakna hun ah khan khat i kihawm simin kei leh ka sanggam pasal i kinial hi.

records.english: This year we each booked a small room, and we got along perfectly.
records.zomi: Tu kum i khat ciat khan neu khat i ngen a, kilem takin i om hi.

records.english: The more my parents tried to control my sister, the more she pulled away from them.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in ka sanggam nu a uk tum semsem ciangin a gamla semsem hi.

records.english: My older sister always takes charge, and the rest of us feel left out.
records.zomi: Ka u nu in a makai tawntung a, a dang i khempeuh kinusia bangin i kisa hi.

records.english: At the last family meeting, we asked her to listen first and decide afterward.
records.zomi: Innkuan kikhopna nunung pen ah a ngai masa-in a nung ciangin khensat dingin i ngen hi.

records.english: Could your uncle help us find a solution, since everyone respects him?
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh in a zahtak ahih manin na pa neu in dawnna i muh nadingin hong huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: How can parents treat their children equally when each child needs something different?
records.zomi: Ta khat ciat in tuamtuam a kisap laitakin nu leh pate in a tate bangci-in kibang takin a kem thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: Would it be fair to ask the eldest son to look after our parents on his own, when there are five of us?
records.zomi: Mi nga i hih laitakin tapa upa pen bek i nu leh pa kem dingin ngen pen a dik ding hiam?

records.english: My stepson wouldn't talk to me for the first year after I married his father.
records.zomi: A pa ka kiteenpih khit ciangin ka tapa kik kum masa sung hong kiho nuam kei hi.

records.english: Things changed when I started driving him to football practice every Saturday.
records.zomi: Kiginni simin football kisinna ah ka paipih kipan ciangin a kilai hi.

records.english: My mother says, "Families argue, but they don't give up on each other."
records.zomi: Ka nu in, “Innkuante a kinial uh hi, ahi zongin a kinusia ngei kei uh hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: Had my brother told us he was struggling, we would have helped him much sooner.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in a haksa hi, ci-in hong hilh le, a ma zaw-in i huh ding hi.

records.english: Kids, if you can't agree on the television, nobody watches it tonight.
records.zomi: Naupangte, TV thu-ah na kithukim zo kei leh tuni zanin kuamah in a en kei ding hi.

records.english: If an old disagreement is spoiling every gathering, it might help to talk about it openly with someone everyone trusts.
records.zomi: Kithukimlohna lui khat in kikhopna khempeuh a susiat leh mi khempeuh' um mi khat tawh kician takin kiho a huh kha ding hi.

records.english: The family photo album was damaged when the roof leaked.
records.zomi: Innkhum a zu ciangin innkuan lim bu a sia hi.

records.english: My cousin scanned the pictures that survived and sent copies to everyone.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam in a dam lai limte a scan a, mi khempeuh copy a khak hi.

records.english: Having grown up with seven siblings, my mother has a solution for almost every family argument.
records.zomi: Sanggam sagih tawh a khan khit ciangin ka nu in innkuan kinialna khempeuh dek adingin dawnna a nei hi.

records.english: My grandmother insists that grudges in a family are like weeds: the longer you leave them, the deeper their roots grow.
records.zomi: Innkuan sung-a lungkhamna pen lopa bang ahi hi, sawt na nusiat semsem ciangin a zung a thuk semsem hi, ci-in ka pi in a gen den hi.

records.english: My parents had my grandfather's old house repaired so that he could live near us.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in i kiang ah a om theih nadingin ka pu' inn lui a bawl siang sak uh hi.

records.english: Although family members may hurt each other, many families find that time and patience heal most wounds.
records.zomi: Innkuan mite a kisuna thei hangin innkuan tampi in hun leh thuakzawhna in liamna tamzaw a dam sak hi, a mu uh hi.

records.english: My cousin was hurt when nobody remembered his birthday.
records.zomi: Kuamah in a pianni a phawk kei ahih manin ka sanggam a lungkham hi.

records.english: How can I get closer to my teenage daughter?
records.zomi: Ka tanu khangno tawh bangci-in ka kinai zaw thei ding hiam?

records.english: Do something she enjoys with her every week, even if it's only a walk to the shop.
records.zomi: Dawr pai bek hi zongin kal simin a deih bangmah khat a tawh khawm-in hih in.

records.english: Whoever hosts the family meal this year should make sure that nobody is left out.
records.zomi: Tu kum innkuan an a bawl peuhpeuh in kuamah a kinusia lo nadingin a en ding hi.

records.english: Why don't you invite your cousins to stay for the holidays?
records.zomi: Bang hangin nopsakna hun adingin na sanggamte om dingin na sam kei hiam?

records.english: Everyone, can we agree not to talk about money at Grandma's birthday?
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, ka pi' pianni-in sum thu kiho lo dingin i kithukim thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: Tell your sister how you feel instead of slamming the door.
records.zomi: Kongkhak hat taka khak sangin na sanggam nu kiangah na kisak dan gen in.

records.english: My aunt and my mother haven't spoken since the funeral.
records.zomi: Ka ni leh ka nu mithi vuina pan kipan a kiho kei uh hi.

records.english: I invited them both to my graduation, hoping they'd sit together.
records.zomi: Khawm-a a tut ding uh ka lamen-in ka sang zawhna ah a nih un ka sam hi.

records.english: I really do want to spend more time with my father, but we live so far apart.
records.zomi: Ka pa tawh hun tam zaw zat ka deih mahmah hi, ahi zongin i kigamla lua hi.

records.english: Now we watch the same football match on Saturdays and talk on the phone during it.
records.zomi: Tu-in Kiginni simin football kimawlna kibang i en a, a sungin phone tawh i kiho hi.

records.english: Is it normal for brothers to fight so much?
records.zomi: Sanggam pasalte a kido mahmah pen a pangai hiam?

records.english: Quite normal, and most of them become good friends when they're older.
records.zomi: A pangai mahmah hi, a tamzaw a upat ciangun lawm hoih a suak uh hi.

records.english: My sister borrowed my favorite dress without asking and spilled coffee on it.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu in dong lo-in ka puan deih pen a zang a, a tung ah khawfi a sun hi.

records.english: She paid to have it cleaned and promised to ask next time.
records.zomi: Siangsak man a pia a, a zom ciangin dong dingin a kiciam hi.

records.english: Shall we write everyone's birthday on the calendar in the kitchen?
records.zomi: An huanna-a kalenda tungah mi khempeuh' pianni i gelh ding hiam?

records.english: My father is too proud to ask for help, even when he's ill.
records.zomi: Ka pa a dam loh ciangin zong huhna ngen dingin a kisathei lua hi.

records.english: I don't ask him anymore; I simply turn up with soup and do the shopping.
records.zomi: Ka dong nawn kei hi; an tui tawh ka hong a, van ka lei sak bek hi.

records.english: What can we do to help Mom and Grandma get along?
records.zomi: Nu leh ka pi a kilem nadingun bang i hih thei ding hiam?

records.english: How did your parents stay married for fifty years?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa kum sawmnga sung bangci-in kiteen den uh hiam?

records.english: Don't make promises to your children that you can't keep.
records.zomi: Na tate kiangah na zuih zawh loh ding kiciamna bawl kei in.

records.english: Many new parents feel so exhausted in the first months that small disagreements turn into big arguments.
records.zomi: Nu leh pa thak tampi in kha masate sungin a tawl lua uh ahih manin kithukimlohna neute kinialna lian a suak hi.

records.english: Had we talked about where to live before the wedding, we could have avoided our first big argument.
records.zomi: Kiteen ma-in koi ah om ding hiam i kiho le, i kinialna lian masa pen i pelh thei ding hi.

records.english: The more we listened to our daughter, the more willing she became to tell us what was really happening at school.
records.zomi: I tanu i ngai semsem ciangin sang ah bang a piang taktak hiam hong gen nuam semsem hi.

records.english: Our son's bicycle was stolen from outside the school.
records.zomi: I tapa' siiksakol sang pua pan a kiguk hi.

records.english: We bought a strong lock, and now he chains the bike to the railings every morning.
records.zomi: Khakna hat khat i lei a, tu-in zingsang simin siiksakol kulh ah a khih hi.

records.english: Shall we ask your parents to look after the children while we fix the roof?
records.zomi: Innkhum i bawl siang laitakin na nu leh na pa in naupangte a kem nadingun i ngen ding hiam?

records.english: Would you help me teach our son to ride his bike this weekend?
records.zomi: Hih kal tawp ciangin i tapa siiksakol tuang dan sinsak dingin hong huh ding hiam?

records.english: The baby's bottle was dropped and broken on the way to the clinic.
records.zomi: Siavuan inn pai lampi ah naungek' nawi bel a kia-in a kek hi.

records.english: A pharmacist kindly sold us a new one even though the shop was closing.
records.zomi: Dawr a kikhak dek hangin zatui zuakpa khat in hehpih takin a thak khat hong zuak hi.

records.english: Tell me what's worrying you, and we'll work it out together.
records.zomi: Bang in hong lungkhamsak hiam hong gen in, khawm-in i bawl siang ding hi.

records.english: I really do want to be a patient father, but some evenings I'm just too tired.
records.zomi: Pa thuakzawh khat suak ka deih mahmah hi, ahi zongin nitak khenkhat ka tawl lua hi.

records.english: Children, please put your shoes away so that nobody trips over them.
records.zomi: Naupangte, kuamah a liim lo nadingin na khedap uh koih un.

records.english: Having raised four children of her own, my mother is the first person I call when I'm unsure what to do.
records.zomi: Amah' ta li a khoi khit ciangin ka nu pen bang hih ding hiam ka kician loh ciangin ka sam masa pen ahi hi.

records.english: How do you get a toddler to eat vegetables?
records.zomi: Naupang neu khat anteh bangci-in na nesak hiam?

records.english: Cut them into funny shapes with a cookie cutter, and let him help in the kitchen.
records.zomi: Lim nuihzathuai-in at inla, an huanna ah huh sak in.

records.english: Rather than punishing our son for the broken window, we had him pay for part of the repair from his pocket money.
records.zomi: Tukvuang kek adingin i tapa gawt sangin a zat ding sum pan bawlsiang man khen khat i piasak hi.

records.english: Could the school counselor help us talk to our son about his grades?
records.zomi: Sang thuhilhtu in i tapa' ciamte thu a kiangah gen dingin hong huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Is it ever right to argue in front of the children?
records.zomi: Naupangte mai ah kinial pen a dik ngei hiam?

records.english: What should we do when our children fight in the car?
records.zomi: Mawtaw sung ah i tate a kido uh ciangin bang i hih ding hiam?

records.english: Stop the car somewhere safe and wait quietly until they've calmed down.
records.zomi: Mun bit khat ah mawtaw tawlsak inla, a ngaih dong uh dai takin ngak in.

records.english: Why do you two always argue about who does the dishes?
records.zomi: Bang hangin kuang kua in a sil ding hiam na nih un na kinial tawntung uh hiam?

records.english: My husband and I kept arguing about money.
records.zomi: Ka pasal leh kei sum thu-ah i kinial den hi.

records.english: We started writing a monthly budget together, and the arguments mostly stopped.
records.zomi: Kha simin budget khawm-in i gelh kipan a, kinialnate a tamzaw a tawp hi.

records.english: Could we have avoided the argument if I'd asked you before agreeing to host your whole family?
records.zomi: Na innkuan bup kem dingin ka lungkim ma-in kong dong le, kinialna i pelh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Our teenager was caught skipping school.
records.zomi: I tapa khangno sang a nusiat in kimu hi.

records.english: Instead of shouting, we asked him why, and found out he was being bullied.
records.zomi: Kikou sangin bang hang hiam i dong a, hong vawt den uh hi, cih i thei hi.

records.english: What would you do if your teenage daughter wanted to leave school?
records.zomi: Na tanu khangno in sang nusia a deih leh bang na hih ding hiam?

records.english: If you and your partner disagree about discipline, it may help to agree on a few simple rules before the children are present.
records.zomi: Nang leh na lawm in hilhna thu-ah na kithukim kei uh leh naupangte a om ma-in thupiak baih tawmno kithukim in a huh kha ding hi.

records.english: My husband forgot our anniversary for the second year in a row.
records.zomi: Kum nih zom-in ka pasal in i kum kimna a mangngilh hi.

records.english: This year he set a reminder on his phone, and he surprised me with flowers.
records.zomi: Tu kum a phone ah a phawksakna a koih a, pak tawh hong lamdangsak hi.

records.english: What I find hardest about parenting is knowing when to step in and when to let my children learn from their mistakes.
records.zomi: Ta khoina ah ka haksa sak pen pen bang ciangin ka lut ding hiam, bang ciangin ka tate a khialhna pan a sin ding uh ka nusia ding hiam theih ahi hi.

records.english: My grandfather says that a marriage is like a garden, which needs care every single day.
records.zomi: Kiteenna pen huan bang ahi a, ni khempeuh kemna a kisam hi, ci-in ka pu in a ci hi.

records.english: However busy my parents were, one of them always walked us to the school gate.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa bangzah ta in buai zongun a khat in sang kongpi dong hong paipih tawntung hi.

records.english: How do you find time for each other with three young children?
records.zomi: Naupang neu thum tawh khat leh khat adingin bangci-in hun na mu uh hiam?

records.english: Every Sunday morning we go for a walk while my mother watches the children.
records.zomi: Nipini zingsang simin ka nu in naupangte a kem laitakin i vak hi.

records.english: Although every marriage has difficult times, couples who keep talking usually find their way through them.
records.zomi: Kiteenna khempeuh in hun haksa a neih hangin kiho den zi leh pasalte in a tamzaw-in lampi a mu uh hi.

records.english: Where's the best place to buy a cheap pram?
records.zomi: Naungek leng man neu koi ah lei hoih pen hiam?

records.english: Should we let our son choose his own school, or decide for him?
records.zomi: I tapa in a sang amah mah in teelsak ding hiam, amah adingin i khensat ding hiam?

records.english: My wife and I agreed that whoever is less tired puts the children to bed.
records.zomi: Ka zi leh kei a tawl tawm zaw peuhpeuh in naupangte a lumsak ding hi, ci-in i kithukim hi.

records.english: My wife says, "We're a team, so we make big decisions together."
records.zomi: Ka zi in, “Pawl khat i hi a, tua ahih manin thu lian khawm-in i khensat hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: Not until our first child was born did I understand how much my own parents had given up for us.
records.zomi: I ta masa pen a suak ciang bek keima' nu leh pa in ei adingin bangzah a nusia uh hiam ka thei hi.

records.english: Our baby wouldn't sleep unless she was being carried.
records.zomi: I naungek pom kei leh a ihmu nuam kei hi.

records.english: A nurse showed us how to wrap her snugly in a blanket, and she slept for four hours.
records.zomi: Nurse khat in puannak tawh hoih takin tuam dan hong etsak a, nai li a ihmu hi.

records.english: Whoever comes home first starts dinner, and the other one washes up afterward.
records.zomi: A tung masa peuhpeuh in nitak an a kipatsak a, a dang khat in a khit ciangin kuang a sil hi.

records.english: Our daughter refuses to wear a coat, even in winter.
records.zomi: I tanu in khuavot ah zong kawt a silh nuam kei hi.

records.english: We let her choose one in her favorite color, and now she wears it every day.
records.zomi: A deih pen rong khat a teel dingin i phal a, tu-in ni simin a silh hi.

records.english: Who should stay home when the children are ill, if we both work?
records.zomi: I nih un i nasep leh naupangte a dam lo ciangun kua in inn ah a om ding hiam?

records.english: My daughter's phone was taking over her life.
records.zomi: Ka tanu' phone in a nuntakna a la khin hi.

records.english: We agreed that all phones go in a basket in the kitchen after nine, including ours.
records.zomi: Nai kua zawh ciangin phone khempeuh, ei' te tawh, an huanna-a bawm sung ah a om ding hi, ci-in i kithukim hi.

records.english: Kids, if you finish your homework before six, we'll all go to the park.
records.zomi: Naupangte, nai guk ma-in na inn-a sep ding na zawh uh leh i khempeuh huan lian ah i pai ding hi.

records.english: Our youngest was frightened of the dark.
records.zomi: I ta neu pen mial a lau hi.

records.english: We bought a small night light, and he hasn't woken up crying since.
records.zomi: Zan meivak neu khat i lei a, tua pan kap-in a khanglawh nawn kei hi.

records.english: My husband works nights, and we hardly see each other.
records.zomi: Ka pasal zan ah na a sem a, i kimu dek kei hi.

records.english: We now have breakfast together every morning before he goes to sleep.
records.zomi: Tu-in a ihmut ma-in zingsang simin zingsang an khawm-in i ne hi.

records.english: Can we visit my parents this weekend, even though we went last month?
records.zomi: Kha nung in i pai khin hangin hih kal tawp ciangin ka nu leh ka pa i veh thei ding hiam?

records.english: My parents never praised us, so I try hard to praise my own children.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in hong phat ngei kei uh ahih manin keima' tate phat dingin ka hanciam hi.

records.english: The washing machine broke the week the twins were born.
records.zomi: Apengte a suah kal in puan silna set a sia hi.

records.english: My mother-in-law came to stay and washed everything by hand until it was fixed.
records.zomi: Ka sungnu hong om a, a kibawl siang dong khempeuh a khut tawh a sil hi.

records.english: The office manager made everyone change their passwords after the computer was attacked by a virus.

records.english: Don't switch off the computer while it says that an update is being installed.
records.zomi: Update kikoih lai hi, a cih laitakin computer khek kei in.

records.english: The screen froze, so I had to hold down the power button to turn it off.
records.zomi: Screen a tawp ahih manin a khek nadingin power button ka nek sawt hi.

records.english: My brother installed a free operating system on my old laptop, and now it runs much faster.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in ka laptop lui ah free operating system khat a koih a, tu-in a manlang zaw mahmah hi.

records.english: Where can I find the version of the operating system I'm using?
records.zomi: Ka zat operating system version koi ah ka mu thei ding hiam?

records.english: Many small businesses rely on the same operating system for years because changing would mean retraining their staff.
records.zomi: Sumbawl neu tampi in a laih ding uh pen a nasemte uh kisinsak kik ding ahih manin operating system kibang kum tampi a zang uh hi.

records.english: Please tell me before you change any settings on my computer.
records.zomi: Ka computer tung-a settings khatpeuh na laih ma-in hong gen in.

records.english: How long has your computer been making that noise?
records.zomi: Na computer in tua ging bangzah sung a bawl khin hiam?

records.english: Why is my laptop so slow this morning?
records.zomi: Bang hangin tuni zingsangin ka laptop a zawi mahmah hiam?

records.english: It's probably updating in the background, so give it a few minutes.
records.zomi: Nung lam ah a update kha ding ahih manin minit tawmno pia in.

records.english: Wouldn't it be wiser to wait a week before installing a major update, in case it causes problems for other users first?
records.zomi: Update lian khat a koih ma-in mi dangte tungah buaina a piangsak kha ding hi, ci-in kal khat ngak a pil zaw ding hi lo hiam?

records.english: Could you make the letters on the screen bigger for my father?
records.zomi: Ka pa adingin screen tung-a laimalte na lian sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: What happens if I don't install the updates?
records.zomi: Update te ka koih kei leh bang a piang ding hiam?

records.english: The computer will still work, but it might become less secure over time.
records.zomi: Computer a sem lai ding hi, ahi zongin hun ciangin a bit tawm semsem kha ding hi.

records.english: Restart the computer and see whether the problem goes away.
records.zomi: Computer khek inla vaksak kik inla, buaina a bei hiam en in.

records.english: My son set up a separate user account for me so that I wouldn't delete his files.
records.zomi: Ka tapa' file te ka phiat lo nadingin ka adingin user account tuam khat a bawl sak hi.

records.english: You can change the language of the operating system in the settings menu.
records.zomi: Settings menu ah operating system' pau na laih thei hi.

records.english: I turned on dark mode so that the screen is easier on my eyes at night.
records.zomi: Zan ah ka mit adingin screen a nuam zawk nadingin dark mode ka koih hi.

records.english: Could a virus really spread from my computer to my phone?
records.zomi: Virus pen ka computer pan ka phone ah a zel taktak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Use the search box to find a program if you can't see it on the desktop.
records.zomi: Desktop tungah na muh kei leh program zon dingin search box zang in.

records.english: Students are not allowed to install programs on the school computers.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte in sang computer te tungah program a koih thei kei uh hi.

records.english: The new version of the operating system looks different, but most things are in the same place.
records.zomi: Operating system version thak a kibang lo bang hi, ahi zongin a tamzaw mun kibang mah ah a om hi.

records.english: My grandfather learned to open his email after I wrote the steps on a card for him.
records.zomi: A khahna card khat tungah ka gelh sak khit ciangin ka pu in a email hon dan a sin hi.

records.english: Although modern operating systems are easier to use, many older people still find them confusing at first.
records.zomi: Tu hun operating system te zat a baih zaw hangin upa tampi in a masa-in a buaihuai sa uh lai hi.

records.english: I had the computer repaired at a shop because it wouldn't start at all.
records.zomi: A kipan zo lo mahmah ahih manin dawr khat ah computer ka bawl siang sak hi.

records.english: Everyone, please save your work and log out before you leave the computer room.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, computer khan na nusiat ma-un na nasep uh save un a, log out un.

records.english: The more programs you run at the same time, the slower the computer is likely to become.
records.zomi: Program tam semsem hun kibang-in na zat ciangin computer a zawi semsem kha ding hi.

records.english: Having used the same computer for ten years, my father refused to learn a new operating system.
records.zomi: Kum sawm sung computer kibang a zat khit ciangin ka pa in operating system thak sin a nial hi.

records.english: Can you help me find the file I saved yesterday?
records.zomi: Zanni-a ka save file mu dingin hong huh thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: The library helps older people learn how to use computers every Tuesday morning.
records.zomi: Laibu inn in Pithai ni zingsang simin upate computer zat dan sin dingin a huh hi.

records.english: Rather than buying a new laptop, I had more memory installed in my old one.
records.zomi: Laptop thak lei sangin ka lui ah memory behlap ka koih sak hi.

records.english: Had I backed up my files before the update, I wouldn't have lost my thesis.
records.zomi: Update ma-in ka file te backup ka bawl le, ka thesis ka mansuah kei ding hi.

records.english: This computer is too old to run the newest operating system.
records.zomi: Hih computer operating system thak pen zang dingin a lui lua hi.

records.english: My little sister accidentally deleted the family photos, but we found them in the recycle bin.
records.zomi: Ka nau nu in khialh-in innkuan limte a phiat a, ahi zongin recycle bin sung ah i mu hi.

records.english: The operating system controls everything else that runs on the computer.
records.zomi: Operating system in computer tung-a a sem dang khempeuh a uk hi.

records.english: Do I need to update my computer?
records.zomi: Ka computer ka update ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, because updates often fix security problems.
records.zomi: Update ding hi, update te in bitna buaina a tamzaw-in a bawl siang ahih manin.

records.english: My laptop restarted in the middle of my online class, and I missed the teacher's instructions.
records.zomi: Ka online kilasi kimlai-in ka laptop a kivaksak kik a, saya' thuhilhna ka mansuah hi.

records.english: Next time, I'll check for updates the night before.
records.zomi: A zom ciangin zan ma-in update a om hiam ka en ding hi.

records.english: Not until the computer crashed did I realize that I hadn't saved my work all afternoon.
records.zomi: Computer a sia ciang bek nitak lam bup ka nasep ka save kei hi, cih ka thei hi.

records.english: It may take an hour to install the new operating system, so plug the laptop in first.
records.zomi: Operating system thak koih dingin nai khat a la kha ding ahih manin laptop a masa-in mei khuk in.

records.english: The update made my old printer stop working.
records.zomi: Update in ka printer lui a sem nawn lo sak hi.

records.english: My laptop and my phone use different operating systems, but I can still share photos between them.
records.zomi: Ka laptop leh ka phone in operating system tuamtuam a zang uh a, ahi zongin a kikal ah lim ka hawm thei lai hi.

records.english: My computer is installing an update, so I can't use it right now.
records.zomi: Ka computer in update a koih ahih manin tu-in ka zang thei kei hi.

records.english: What I find most confusing is that every update seems to move the settings to a different place.
records.zomi: Ka buaisak pen pen update khempeuh in settings mun dang ah a suan bang hi, cih ahi hi.

records.english: Shall I show you how to organize your files into folders?
records.zomi: Na file te folder sung ah bangci-in koih ding hiam kong etsak ding hiam?

records.english: Who changed the background picture on the office computer?
records.zomi: Office computer tung-a background lim kua in a laih hiam?

records.english: Whoever uses the shared computer last should shut it down properly at the end of the day.
records.zomi: Kihawm computer a zang nunung peuhpeuh in ni tawp ciangin hoih takin a khek ding hi.

records.english: When the battery is low, the computer automatically dims the screen to save power.
records.zomi: Battery a niam ciangin mei kem nadingin computer in amah mah in screen a mialsak hi.

records.english: I use the keyboard shortcut to copy text because it's faster than the mouse.
records.zomi: Mouse sangin a manlang zaw ahih manin lai copy dingin keyboard shortcut ka zang hi.

records.english: Which operating system does the school use?
records.zomi: Sang in koi operating system a zang hiam?

records.english: Why does the computer keep asking me to restart?
records.zomi: Bang hangin computer in restart dingin hong ngen den hiam?

records.english: Click the icon at the bottom of the screen to open the settings.
records.zomi: Settings hon dingin screen nuai lam-a icon click in.

records.english: Is it safe to download programs from websites I don't know?
records.zomi: Ka theih loh website pan program download a bit hiam?

records.english: Only from websites you trust, or your computer could be infected with a virus.
records.zomi: Na um website pan bek, a hi kei leh na computer virus in a lut kha ding hi.

records.english: Would you mind turning off the automatic updates on the presentation laptop before the meeting?
records.zomi: Kikhopna ma-in etsakna laptop tung-a automatic update na khek sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: If the computer won't start after an update, you may be able to return to the previous version.
records.zomi: Update khit ciangin computer a kipan kei leh version ma-a om ah na kik thei kha ding hi.

records.english: Why don't you set the computer to install updates at night, when you're not using it?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na zat loh hun zan ciangin update koih dingin computer na koih kei hiam?

records.english: The operating system asks for permission before any new program can make changes.
records.zomi: Program thak khatpeuh in a laih ma-in operating system in phalna a ngen hi.

records.english: You can't use this computer without a password, so ask the office for one.
records.zomi: Password om lo-in hih computer na zang thei kei ding ahih manin office ah khat ngen in.

records.english: My husband says, "If you cook, I wash up — that's only fair."
records.zomi: Ka pasal in, “Nang an na huan leh kei kuang ka sil ding — tua bek a dik hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: My roommate never buys toilet paper or soap.
records.zomi: Ka khan kihawm lawm in ek inn lai leh satpiang a lei ngei kei hi.

records.english: We started a shared money jar for household supplies, and the problem was solved.
records.zomi: Inn sung vanzat adingin kihawm sum bel khat i kipatsak a, buaina a bei hi.

records.english: My mother uses an old toothbrush to clean the corners of the bathroom tiles.
records.zomi: Ka nu in kisilna inn suang tungte' kil siangsak dingin ha sil lui khat a zang hi.

records.english: The roof gutters were full of leaves, and rain was pouring down the wall.
records.zomi: Innkhum tui luanna sing nate tawh a dim a, guah tui bang tungah a luang hi.

records.english: My uncle climbed up with a ladder and cleaned them out before the storm.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu kahlei tawh a kah a, huihpi ma-in a siangsak hi.

records.english: Is it possible to share the housework fairly when we all work different hours?
records.zomi: I khempeuh hun tuamtuam-in i nasep laitakin inn nasep dik takin i kihawm thei ding hiam?

records.english: In many families, responsibilities that once belonged to women alone are now shared between everyone.
records.zomi: Innkuan tampi ah ma-in numeite bek' mawhpuakna ahi tu-in mi khempeuh in a kihawm uh hi.

records.english: Why don't you put the clothes away as soon as they're dry?
records.zomi: Bang hangin puante a keu pah-in na koih kei hiam?

records.english: Rather than arguing about the chores every week, we sat down and divided them once and for all.
records.zomi: Kal simin inn nasep thu kinial sangin i tu-in khatvei-in i khen kim hi.

records.english: Nobody in our house wanted to take out the rubbish.
records.zomi: I inn ah kuamah in nawi paai a deih kei uh hi.

records.english: We made a chart on the fridge, and now each person has one week a month.
records.zomi: Khal bawm tungah chart khat i bawl a, tu-in mi khat ciat in kha khat ah kal khat a nei uh hi.

records.english: If one person is always doing more than the others, it may help to write down every task and count them.
records.zomi: Mi khat in a dangte sangin a sem tam zaw tawntung leh nasep khempeuh gelh-in sim leh a huh kha ding hi.

records.english: Would you mind sweeping the yard while I wash the car?
records.zomi: Mawtaw ka sil laitakin tual na phiat sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Where do we keep the screwdriver?
records.zomi: Screwdriver koi ah i koih hiam?

records.english: May I finish my homework before I start sweeping?
records.zomi: Phiat ka kipat ma-in ka inn-a sep ding ka zo thei ding hiam?

records.english: Children, if you each clean one room, we'll be finished before lunch.
records.zomi: Naupangte, na khat ciat in khan khat na siangsak uh leh sun an ma-in i zo ding hi.

records.english: My little brother always says he's too young to wash the dishes.
records.zomi: Ka nau pasal in kuang sil dingin ka neu lua hi, a ci tawntung hi.

records.english: We gave him a small stool so that he could reach the sink, and now he enjoys it.
records.zomi: Kuang silna a phak theih nadingin tutna neu khat i pia a, tu-in a nuam sa hi.

records.english: The kitchen cupboard door fell off its hinges this morning.
records.zomi: Tuni zingsangin an huanna van bawm kongkhak a kibelhna pan a kia hi.

records.english: My grandfather says that a tidy house is like a calm mind, because both make the day easier.
records.zomi: Inn siang pen lungsim dai bang ahi a, a nih in ni a baihsak hi, ci-in ka pu in a ci hi.

records.english: What I find hardest is keeping the house tidy when three small children are home all day.
records.zomi: Ka haksa sak pen pen naupang neu thum ni bup inn ah a om laitakun inn siang taka kem ahi hi.

records.english: The kitchen sink was blocked with rice and vegetable peelings.
records.zomi: An huanna kuang silna buh leh anteh khilhte tawh a kikhak hi.

records.english: My father cleared it with a plunger and put a small strainer over the drain.
records.zomi: Ka pa in plunger tawh a hon a, tui luanna tungah sel neu khat a koih hi.

records.english: Whoever cooks dinner shouldn't have to clean the kitchen afterward.
records.zomi: Nitak an a huan peuhpeuh in a khit ciangin an huanna a siangsak lo ding hi.

records.english: Had we fixed the leaking tap sooner, the water bill wouldn't have been so high.
records.zomi: Tui khuk zu i bawl siang manlang le, tui man a tam lua kei ding hi.

records.english: Who's going to fix the dripping tap?
records.zomi: A zu tui khuk kua in a bawl siang ding hiam?

records.english: Everyone, please put your dirty dishes in the sink, not on the table.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, na kuang nin uh dawhkan tungah hi lo-in kuang silna sung ah koih un.

records.english: How can I get my teenagers to help with the housework?
records.zomi: Ka tate khangnote inn nasep a huh nadingun bangci-in ka hih thei ding hiam?

records.english: Give each of them one job they choose themselves, and don't redo it after them.
records.zomi: A khat ciat amau mah in a teel nasep khat pia inla, a nung ah kik-in bawl kei in.

records.english: Why does the dog always need a bath right after I've cleaned the floor?
records.zomi: Bang hangin tual ka siangsak khit pah ciangin ui in kisil a kisap tawntung hiam?

records.english: My grandmother insists on doing all the cooking, even though her back hurts.
records.zomi: A nung a na hangin ka pi in an huan khempeuh amah in a huan ding a deih hi.

records.english: We let her choose the dishes, and we do the chopping and stirring for her.
records.zomi: An a teel dingin i phal a, at leh ngom i sem sak hi.

records.english: The vacuum cleaner stopped working in the middle of the spring cleaning.
records.zomi: Spring siansuahna kimlai-in vacuum cleaner a sem nawn kei hi.

records.english: We borrowed the neighbor's and had ours repaired the following week.
records.zomi: Inn veng' i ngetsak a, a zom kal in eima' i bawl siang sak hi.

records.english: How do you keep the house clean with so many visitors?
records.zomi: Khual hong tam lua tawh inn bangci-in na siangsak hiam?

records.english: Could you hang the washing out before you leave for school?
records.zomi: Sang na pai ma-in puan sil na tan sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Not until my mother went into hospital did we realize how much she did around the house.
records.zomi: Ka nu zato ah a lut ciang bek inn ah bangzah a sem hiam i thei hi.

records.english: Although household chores can seem endless, sharing them makes the work lighter and the family closer.
records.zomi: Inn nasep a bei lo bang hangin a kihawm leh nasep a zaang a, innkuan a kinai zaw hi.

records.english: Who left the lights on in every room?
records.zomi: Khan khempeuh ah meivak kua in a nusia hiam?

records.english: Is it fair that I do all the shopping while my brother does nothing?
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in bangmah a sem lo laitakin van lei khempeuh kei in ka hih pen a dik hiam?

records.english: The washing was ruined because someone put a red sock in with the white shirts.
records.zomi: Kuamah in khedap-ip san khat angki kangte tawh a koih ahih manin puan silte a sia hi.

records.english: Since then, we sort the laundry into separate baskets before washing it.
records.zomi: Tua pan kipan i sil ma-in puante bawm tuamtuam ah i khen hi.

records.english: The broken window in the kitchen was covered with cardboard until we could afford new glass.
records.zomi: Glass thak i lei zawh dong an huanna-a tukvuang kek laipek tawh kikhuh hi.

records.english: The more often you clean the stove, the less time it takes each time.
records.zomi: Meikhuk na siangsak den semsem ciangin hun a tawm semsem hi.

records.english: Could we buy a dishwasher, or is that too expensive for us?
records.zomi: Kuang silna set khat i lei thei ding hiam, eite adingin a man tam lua hiam?

records.english: Wouldn't it make more sense to pay someone to clean the windows than to risk falling off the ladder ourselves?
records.zomi: Eimah in kahlei pan kia ding a lauhuai sangin tukvuang siangsak dingin kuamah sawl a hoih zaw hi lo hiam?

records.english: Please hang your wet coat by the stove, not on the back of the chair.
records.zomi: Na kawt dikdek tutna nung ah hi lo-in meikhuk kiang ah khai in.

records.english: What should we do if the washing machine breaks during the rainy season?
records.zomi: Guah hun sungin puan silna set a sia leh bang i hih ding hiam?

records.english: Having lived alone for years, my brother found it hard to share the chores when he got married.
records.zomi: Kum tampi sung amah bek a om khit ciangin ka sanggam pasal a kiteen ciangin inn nasep kihawm a haksa sa hi.

records.english: Why is the floor so sticky?
records.zomi: Bang hangin tual a belh mahmah hiam?

records.english: Someone spilled juice and didn't wipe it up properly.
records.zomi: Kuamah in theigah tui a sun a, hoih takin a nul kei hi.

records.english: My parents argue about who should clean the bathroom.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa kisilna inn kua in a siangsak ding hiam a kinial uh hi.

records.english: Now they alternate weeks and write their names on the calendar.
records.zomi: Tu-in kal khat ciat a kikhel uh a, kalenda tungah a min uh a gelh uh hi.

records.english: I really do want to help more at home, but I work late every night.
records.zomi: Inn ah huh tam zaw ka deih mahmah hi, ahi zongin zan simin ka nai hi.

records.english: Now I do the shopping and the ironing on Saturdays, so my wife has a rest.
records.zomi: Tu-in Kiginni simin van lei leh puan phawk ka sem a, tua ahih manin ka zi a tawldam hi.

records.english: Shall we ask the children to feed the chickens before breakfast?
records.zomi: Zingsang an ma-in akte an vak dingin naupangte i ngen ding hiam?

records.english: The garden was overgrown because nobody had time to weed it.
records.zomi: Kuamah in lopa sing hun a nei kei ahih manin huan a ngiam hi.

records.english: Every Sunday morning, the whole family spends an hour in it with hoes and buckets.
records.zomi: Nipini zingsang simin innkuan bup tuthau leh bawm tawh a sung ah nai khat a zang uh hi.

records.english: The cat knocked over a plant, and soil was scattered all over the carpet.
records.zomi: Zawh in singkung khat a lin a, tuutphah tungah lei a zel hi.

records.english: I really do want to tell my family about my new job, but I'm afraid they won't approve.
records.zomi: Ka nasep thak thu ka innkuan hilh ka deih mahmah hi, ahi zongin a pom kei kha ding uh ka lau hi.

records.english: My sister offered to sit with me when I tell them, so that I don't feel alone.
records.zomi: Ka hilh ciangin keimah bek om lo bangin ka kisak nadingin ka sanggam nu in ka kiang ah om dingin a kipia hi.

records.english: My father compares a family discussion to weaving, because every thread has to be pulled gently.
records.zomi: Ka pa in innkuan kihona puan tah tawh a kikhaikhin a, khau khat ciat nem takin kai ding a kisam hi.

records.english: Don't decide anything important when you're angry.
records.zomi: Na heh laitakin thu thupi bangmah khensat kei in.

records.english: Had we discussed the costs earlier, we wouldn't have been surprised by the bill for the roof.
records.zomi: Man thu a ma zaw-in i kiho le, innkhum bill in hong lamdangsak kei ding hi.

records.english: Whoever disagrees with the plan should say so now, rather than complaining afterward.
records.zomi: Gelna a nial peuhpeuh in a nung ciangin phun sangin tu-in gen uh hen.

records.english: If a discussion keeps going in circles, it might help to take a break and come back with fresh ideas.
records.zomi: Kihona in a kipelh den leh tawlngak-in ngaihsutna thak tawh kik leh a huh kha ding hi.

records.english: My little sister cried during the discussion because she thought we were angry with her.
records.zomi: Ka nau nu in a tungah i heh in a ngaihsut manin kihona laitakin a kap hi.

records.english: We explained that we were only disagreeing about the plan, not about her.
records.zomi: Gelna thu bek ah i kithukim kei a, amah thu hi lo hi, ci-in i gen siang hi.

records.english: My grandparents argued gently for an hour and then decided to keep the old house.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh pite nai khat sung nem takin a kinial uh a, tua ciangin inn lui kem dingin a khensat uh hi.

records.english: Why do we always talk about serious things at the dinner table?
records.zomi: Bang hangin an nekna dawhkan ah thu thupite i kiho tawntung hiam?

records.english: Please don't bring up old arguments when we're trying to solve a new problem.
records.zomi: Buaina thak khat i bawl siang tum laitakin kinialna luite khoih kei in.

records.english: My mother wrote down everything we agreed on and stuck the list on the fridge.
records.zomi: Ka nu in i kithukimna khempeuh a gelh a, list khal bawm tungah a belh hi.

records.english: Having talked about the problem for three evenings, we finally agreed on a solution that suited everyone.
records.zomi: Nitak thum sung buaina thu i kiho khit ciangin a tawp-in mi khempeuh a kituak dawnna khat ah i kithukim hi.

records.english: Is it possible to change a family decision once it has been made?
records.zomi: Innkuan khensatna khat a kibawl khit ciangin a laih thei hiam?

records.english: Could we invite a neutral friend to help us talk about the inheritance?
records.zomi: Gamluah thu i kiho nadingin lam pang lo lawm khat hong huh dingin i sam thei ding hiam?

records.english: How do you discuss money with your parents without upsetting them?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa a lungkhamsak lo-in sum thu bangci-in na kiho uh hiam?

records.english: Choose a calm moment, and start by asking how you can help rather than what they should do.
records.zomi: Hun dai khat teel inla, bang a hih ding uh hiam sangin bangci-in na huh thei ding hiam dot-in kipan in.

records.english: Can we talk about Grandma's care after the children have gone to bed?
records.zomi: Naupangte a ihmut khit uh ciangin ka pi' kemna thu i kiho thei ding hiam?

records.english: Not until my grandmother spoke did the rest of the family realize how worried she had been.
records.zomi: Ka pi a gen ciang bek innkuan a dangte in bangzah a lungkham hiam a thei uh hi.

records.english: The discussion about the wedding went badly because everyone was tired and hungry.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh a tawl uh a, a gilkial uh ahih manin mopawi thu kihona a hoih kei hi.

records.english: We agreed to talk again after dinner, and it went much more smoothly.
records.zomi: Nitak an khit ciangin kik-in kiho dingin i kithukim a, a nuam zaw mahmah hi.

records.english: Where should we hold the family meeting this year?
records.zomi: Tu kum innkuan kikhopna koi ah i bawl ding hiam?

records.english: Why didn't anyone tell me that we were discussing my future tonight?
records.zomi: Bang hangin tuni zanin ka hun zom thu i kiho ding hi, ci-in kuamah in hong hilh kei hiam?

records.english: Would it be easier to discuss this over a meal?
records.zomi: An nek kawm-in hih thu i kiho leh a baih zaw ding hiam?

records.english: How can we make sure the quieter people in the family are heard?
records.zomi: Innkuan sung-a dai zawte kingai hi, cih bangci-in i kician thei ding hiam?

records.english: What would you say to your parents if they wanted to move back to the village?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa khua ah ciah kik a deih uh leh bang na gen ding hiam?

records.english: In some families, children are expected to listen rather than speak at family meetings.
records.zomi: Innkuan khenkhatte ah naupangte innkuan kikhopna ah gen sangin ngai dingin kilamen hi.

records.english: My grandfather says, "In this family, every voice is heard, even the smallest one."
records.zomi: Ka pu in, “Hih innkuan ah aw khempeuh, a neu pen zong, kingai hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: Did everyone agree in the end?
records.zomi: A tawp-in mi khempeuh a kithukim uh hiam?

records.english: Every family discussion at our house ends with everyone shouting.
records.zomi: I inn-a innkuan kihona khempeuh mi khempeuh kikou-in a tawp hi.

records.english: Now we agree on three rules before we start, and the first is that nobody raises their voice.
records.zomi: Tu-in i kipat ma-in thupiak thum ah i kithukim a, a masa pen kuamah in ging sang a gen lo ding hi.

records.english: My parents always decide things without asking the children.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in naupangte dong lo-in thu a khensat tawntung uh hi.

records.english: Last month they asked for our ideas about the new house, and we felt much more involved.
records.zomi: Kha nung in inn thak thu-ah i ngaihsutna hong dong uh a, i kihel zaw bangin i kisa hi.

records.english: My aunt was hurt because nobody asked her opinion about the funeral.
records.zomi: Mithi vuina thu-ah kuamah in a ngaihsutna a dot kei ahih manin ka ni a lungkham hi.

records.english: At the next meeting, she was the first person we asked.
records.zomi: A zom kikhopna ah i dong masa pen ahi hi.

records.english: Shall we ask Uncle Pau to lead the discussion, since he's always fair?
records.zomi: Pa Neu Pau a dik tawntung ahih manin kihona makai dingin i ngen ding hiam?

records.english: My father talked for so long that nobody else had a chance to speak.
records.zomi: Ka pa sawt lua takin a gen ahih manin kuamah in gen nading hun a nei kei uh hi.

records.english: My mother started using a small kitchen timer, and each person gets five minutes.
records.zomi: Ka nu in an huanna nai neu khat a zang kipan a, mi khat ciat in minit nga a ngah hi.

records.english: Could you help me explain to Dad why I want to study abroad?
records.zomi: Gamdang ah bang hangin sin ka deih hiam Pa kiangah ka gen siang nadingin hong huh thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: What should we do when we can't agree about where to spend New Year?
records.zomi: Kum thak koi ah zang ding hiam i kithukim zo kei ciangin bang i hih ding hiam?

records.english: Let each side of the family choose in alternate years, and write down whose year it is.
records.zomi: Innkuan lam khat ciat in kum kikhel-in teel uh hen, kua' kum ahi hiam gelh un.

records.english: My cousins and I write our questions down before family meetings, so that we don't forget them.
records.zomi: I mangngilh lo nadingin innkuan kikhopna ma-in ka sanggamte leh kei i dotnate i gelh hi.

records.english: Our children were worried about moving, so we let them visit the new town before deciding.
records.zomi: I tate tuah thu-ah a lungkham uh ahih manin i khensat ma-in khuapi thak a veh dingin i phal hi.

records.english: My brother never comes to family meetings because he lives in another city.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal khuapi dang ah a om ahih manin innkuan kikhopna ah a hong ngei kei hi.

records.english: Now we send him the notes after each meeting, and he phones with his opinion the next day.
records.zomi: Tu-in kikhopna khat ciat khit ciangin thu gelhte i khak a, a zing ni-in a ngaihsutna tawh phone a sam hi.

records.english: Why did the discussion take so long?
records.zomi: Bang hangin kihona a sawt mahmah hiam?

records.english: Everyone had a different idea, and we had to listen to all of them.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh in ngaihsutna tuamtuam a nei uh a, a vekpi i ngai ding hi.

records.english: Who's going to tell Grandpa what we decided?
records.zomi: I khensatna ka pu kua in a hilh ding hiam?

records.english: Everyone, let's switch off our phones before we talk about the holiday plans.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, nopsakna hun gelna i kiho ma-in i phone khek ni.

records.english: Rather than voting on every decision, our family tries to reach an agreement that everyone can accept.
records.zomi: Khensatna khempeuh ah vote pia sangin i innkuan in mi khempeuh in a pom theih kithukimna khat ngah dingin a sin hi.

records.english: Should children be allowed to vote on family decisions?
records.zomi: Innkuan khensatna ah naupangte in vote a pia thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: The family meeting was interrupted when the power went off.
records.zomi: Meivak a mit ciangin innkuan kikhopna kitawpsak hi.

records.english: We carried on by candlelight, and somehow everyone spoke more quietly.
