records.zomi: Khawimeivaak tawh i zom a, bangbang hiam mi khempeuh a dai zaw-in a gen uh hi.

records.english: The more openly we talk about our worries, the less they seem to grow.
records.zomi: I lungkhamnate kician zawin i kiho semsem ciangin a khang tawm semsem bang hi.

records.english: Who should decide whether we sell the family farm?
records.zomi: Innkuan lo i zuak ding hiam kua in a khensat ding hiam?

records.english: However heated the discussion becomes, my mother always ends it by asking everyone to eat together.
records.zomi: Kihona bangzah a sa zongin ka nu in mi khempeuh khawm-in an ne dingin a ngen-in a tawpsak tawntung hi.

records.english: What I find hardest is listening to my parents' opinions without interrupting them.
records.zomi: Ka haksa sak pen pen ka nu leh ka pa' ngaihsutnate a kikal ah gen lo-a ngai ahi hi.

records.english: Although family discussions can be tiring, avoiding them often makes problems much worse.
records.zomi: Innkuan kihona a tawlsak thei hangin a pelh pen in buaina a hoih lo semsem sak tawntung hi.

records.english: Children, you can each say one thing you like and one thing you don't like about the plan.
records.zomi: Naupangte, gelna ah na deih khat leh na deih loh khat na khat ciat in na gen thei uh hi.

records.english: Children, hold hands when we cross the road to the park.
records.zomi: Naupangte, huan lian lam lampi i kan ciangin khut kilen un.

records.english: Rather than moving my parents into the city, we found a carer who lives in their village.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa khuapi ah suan sangin a khua uh ah a om kemtu khat i mu hi.

records.english: Where can we find a babysitter we can trust?
records.zomi: I um theih naupang kemtu koi ah i mu thei ding hiam?

records.english: How can I keep my father company when I work all day?
records.zomi: Ni bup ka nasep laitakin ka pa bangci-in ka lawmpih thei ding hiam?

records.english: Ask a neighbor to drop in at lunchtime, and call him during your break.
records.zomi: Sun an hun ciangin inn veng khat lut dingin ngen inla, na tawlngak hun ah sam in.

records.english: Can my mother stay with us for a few months after her operation?
records.zomi: A zatui sat khit ciangin ka nu kha tawmno sung i kiang ah a om thei ding hiam?

records.english: Is it possible to find a day center for older people near our village?
records.zomi: I khua kiang ah upate adingin sun kemna mun khat mu thei ding hiam?

records.english: Everyone, please don't kiss the baby on the face, even if you feel perfectly well.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, na dam kim zongun naungek a mai ah nam kei un.

records.english: My grandmother kept forgetting to take her tablets in the evening.
records.zomi: Ka pi in nitak lam a zatui ne dingin a mangngilh den hi.

records.english: We bought a pill box with the days of the week on it, and now she rarely misses a dose.
records.zomi: Kal sung ni min nei zatui bawm khat i lei a, tu-in a mansuah ngei tawm hi.

records.english: Although caring for an elderly parent can be exhausting, many people say it brought them closer together.
records.zomi: Nu hiam pa hiam upa kem a tawlsak thei hangin mi tampi in a kinai zawsak hi, a ci uh hi.

records.english: If you're caring for someone at home, it may help to ask the health center about support groups for carers.
records.zomi: Inn ah kuamah na kem leh kemtute adingin huhna pawl thu cidamna inn na dong leh a huh kha ding hi.

records.english: The more patiently you explain things to small children, the less they tend to argue.
records.zomi: Naupang neute kiangah thuakzawh takin na gen siang semsem ciangin a kinial tawm semsem uh hi.

records.english: My mother says, "Look after your parents the way they looked after you."
records.zomi: Ka nu in, “Na nu leh na pa in hong kem bangin amaute kem in,” a ci hi.

records.english: What can I do when my son refuses to go to bed?
records.zomi: Ka tapa in lum a nial ciangin bang ka hih thei ding hiam?

records.english: Keep the same bedtime every night, and read him a story once he's in bed.
records.zomi: Zan simin ihmut hun kibang kem inla, lupna tungah a om khit ciangin tangthu khat sim sak in.

records.english: In many families, grandparents look after the children while the parents are at work.
records.zomi: Innkuan tampi ah nu leh pate nasepna ah a om laitakun pu leh pite in naupangte a kem uh hi.

records.english: Why won't the baby take her bottle today?
records.zomi: Bang hangin tuni-in naungek in a nawi bel a sang nuam kei hiam?

records.english: Could you read the newspaper to Grandpa this afternoon, since his glasses are broken?
records.zomi: Ka pu' mitlimlang a kek ahih manin tuni nitak lam laithak na sim sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: The baby wouldn't stop crying on the long bus journey.
records.zomi: Bus khualzinna sau ah naungek a kap tawp kei hi.

records.english: An old woman sitting nearby sang to her, and she fell asleep within minutes.
records.zomi: A kiang-a tu numei upa khat in la a sak sak a, minit tawmno sungin a ihmu hi.

records.english: Who's going to pick the children up from school while I'm at the hospital with Mother?
records.zomi: Zato ah Nu tawh ka om laitakin sang pan naupangte kua in a la ding hiam?

records.english: My grandfather fell in the bathroom last winter.
records.zomi: Kum nung khuavot in ka pu kisilna inn ah a kia hi.

records.english: My uncle fixed handles to the wall and put a rubber mat in the shower so that it wouldn't happen again.
records.zomi: A piang kik lo nadingin ka pa neu in bang ah lenna a khen a, kisilna mun ah rubber phah a koih hi.

records.english: What would you do if your parents could no longer live alone?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa amau bek a om thei nawn kei uh leh bang na hih ding hiam?

records.english: Having cared for her mother for ten years, my aunt now volunteers to help other families in the same situation.
records.zomi: Kum sawm sung a nu a kem khit ciangin ka ni in tu-in tua bang tuak innkuan dangte huh dingin thalawp-in a sem hi.

records.english: My aunt cares for her husband all day and has no time to rest.
records.zomi: Ka ni in ni bup a pasal a kem a, tawldam hun a nei kei hi.

records.english: Shall we take her out for lunch on Sundays while someone else sits with him?
records.zomi: Mi dang khat a kiang ah a om laitakin Nipini simin amah sun an ah i paipih ding hiam?

records.english: Did the nurse say when Grandpa can come home?
records.zomi: Bang ciangin ka pu inn ah a hong thei ding hiam nurse in a gen hiam?

records.english: Why do you visit the old man next door every evening?
records.zomi: Bang hangin nitak simin a kiang inn-a pasal upa na veh hiam?

records.english: His children live abroad, and he has nobody else to talk to.
records.zomi: A tate gamdang ah a om uh a, kiho dingin kuamah dang a nei kei hi.

records.english: Why does Grandpa always want the window open, even in winter?
records.zomi: Bang hangin khuavot ah zong ka pu in tukvuang kihong a deih tawntung hiam?

records.english: How do you look after a sick child when both parents work?
records.zomi: Nu leh pa a nih un a nasep ciangun dam lo naupang khat bangci-in na kem uh hiam?

records.english: I really do want to look after my parents myself, but I also have three small children.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa keimah in kem ka deih mahmah hi, ahi zongin naupang neu thum zong ka nei hi.

records.english: So my brothers and I found a day center near my house, where our parents now spend their weekdays.
records.zomi: Tua ahih manin ka sanggam pasalte leh kei in ka inn kiang ah sun kemna mun khat i mu a, tua ah i nu leh pa kal sung ni a zang uh hi.

records.english: Whoever is looking after the baby tonight should keep the monitor switched on.
records.zomi: Tuni zanin naungek a kem peuhpeuh in monitor a vaksak den ding hi.

records.english: Can you read to your little sister while I make dinner?
records.zomi: Nitak an ka bawl laitakin na nau nu na simsak thei ding hiam?

records.english: The children's grandmother lives far away, so they rarely see her.
records.zomi: Naupangte' pi gamla ah a om ahih manin a mu ngei tawm uh hi.

records.english: Now they send her drawings every week, and she sends them letters back.
records.zomi: Tu-in kal simin lim a khak uh a, amah in lai a khak kik hi.

records.english: What I find hardest is persuading my grandfather to accept help without hurting his pride.
records.zomi: Ka haksa sak pen pen ka pu' kisaktheihna susia lo-in huhna sang dingin ka hanthawn ahi hi.

records.english: The babysitter was late, so I had to take my son to work with me.
records.zomi: Naupang kemtu a nun ahih manin ka tapa nasepna ah ka paipih ding a kisam hi.

records.english: Would it help if I came over on Thursdays to give you a break?
records.zomi: Tawlngakna kong piak nadingin Laizing ni simin ka hong leh a huh ding hiam?

records.english: Our toddler kept climbing onto the kitchen counter.
records.zomi: I naupang neu in an huanna dawhkan tungah a kah den hi.

records.english: We moved the chairs away from the counter and put a lock on the cupboard with the knives.
records.zomi: Tutnate dawhkan pan i suan a, namsau koihna van bawm ah khakna i koih hi.

records.english: Make sure the gate to the pond is always shut when the toddlers are playing outside.
records.zomi: Naupang neute pua ah a kimawl laitakun tuili kongpi a kikhak tawntung hiam en in.

records.english: Should we tell Grandma the truth about her illness, or would it frighten her?
records.zomi: Ka pi kiangah a natna thu a tak i hilh ding hiam, a lausak ding hiam?

records.english: Is it all right to leave the children with their aunt for the weekend?
records.zomi: Kal tawp sung naupangte a ni uh kiangah nusia a hoih hiam?

records.english: My grandmother gets confused in the evenings and sometimes forgets where she is.
records.zomi: Ka pi nitak lam ciangin a buai a, khatveivei koi ah a om hiam a mangngilh hi.

records.english: Her doctor suggested keeping the room well lit and talking to her calmly about familiar things.
records.zomi: A siavuan in khan vak takin kem-in a theih ngeina thute dai takin a kiangah gen dingin a gen hi.

records.english: My daughter is scared of the dentist, so I let her sit on my lap during the check-up.
records.zomi: Ka tanu ha siavuan a lau ahih manin etna laitakin ka pheng tungah ka tusak hi.

records.english: My father refuses to use a walking stick because he says it makes him look old.
records.zomi: Ka pa in a upa bang a hihsak hi, a ci-in ciangkhut a zang nuam kei hi.

records.english: We bought him a handsome wooden one, and now he carries it proudly.
records.zomi: Sing ciangkhut hoih khat i lei sak a, tu-in kisaktheih takin a tawi hi.

records.english: The twins both caught a cold the week my wife was away.
records.zomi: Ka zi a om loh kal in apengte a nih un khuasik a ngah uh hi.

records.english: My neighbor brought soup every evening, which saved me from cooking.
records.zomi: Ka inn veng in nitak simin an tui a tawi a, tua in an huan pan hong hun hi.

records.english: My mother can't hear the doorbell anymore.
records.zomi: Ka nu in kongkhak ging a za thei nawn kei hi.

records.english: We had a light fitted that flashes whenever someone rings.
records.zomi: Kuamah in a ging sak ciangin a tang meivak khat i koih sak hi.

records.english: Not until I spent a night in the hospital with my son did I understand how frightening illness is for a child.
records.zomi: Ka tapa tawh zato ah zan khat ka om ciang bek natna in naupang khat adingin bangzah a lauhuai hiam ka thei hi.

records.english: Had we noticed the signs earlier, we might have found the right care for my grandmother sooner.
records.zomi: Lahnate a ma zaw-in i mu le, ka pi adingin kemna dik a manlang zaw-in i mu kha ding hi.

records.english: My grandmother says that caring for others is like lighting a lamp, because it brightens your own life too.
records.zomi: Midangte kem pen meivak hal bang ahi a, na nuntakna zong a vaksak hi, ci-in ka pi in a ci hi.

records.english: We hired a nurse to visit three times a week so that my father could stay in his own home.
records.zomi: Ka pa a inn mah ah a om theih nadingin kal khat ah thumvei hong veh nurse khat i sawl hi.

records.english: My grandfather makes everyone get up at five, even on holidays.
records.zomi: Nopsakna ni ah zong ka pu in mi khempeuh nai nga ciangin a thoksak hi.

records.english: I can't decide what to wear, so I spend twenty minutes changing my clothes.
records.zomi: Bang silh ding hiam ka khensat zo kei ahih manin ka puan laih-in minit sawmnih ka zang hi.

records.english: My sister suggested choosing my outfit the night before, and it saves me so much time.
records.zomi: Zan ma-in ka puan teel dingin ka sanggam nu in a gen a, hun tampi hong hun hi.

records.english: I always forget my keys when I'm in a hurry.
records.zomi: Ka manlang ciangin ka tawh ka mangngilh tawntung hi.

records.english: Now I hang them on a hook by the door, right next to my bag.
records.zomi: Tu-in kongkhak kiang-a khaina ah ka ip kiang mahmah ah ka khai hi.

records.english: Would it save time if I showered in the evening instead of the morning?
records.zomi: Zingsang sangin nitak lam ka kisil leh hun a hun ding hiam?

records.english: Did you remember to charge your phone, or will it die before lunch again?
records.zomi: Na phone mei khuk na phawk hiam, sun an ma-in a bei kik ding hiam?

records.english: Would you mind waking me at six, since my phone isn't working?
records.zomi: Ka phone a sem kei ahih manin nai guk ciangin hong phawngsak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Although the school is only five minutes away, my children are somehow late every Monday.
records.zomi: Sang minit nga bek a gamla hangin ka tate Pizing ni simin a nun den uh hi.

records.english: What I find hardest is getting up when it's still dark outside.
records.zomi: Ka haksa sak pen pen pua ah a mial lai laitakin thou ahi hi.

records.english: How do you get three children ready for school by half past seven?
records.zomi: Nai sagih leh a khen ma-in naupang thum sang adingin bangci-in na kimansak hiam?

records.english: We pack the bags the night before, and everyone has one job at breakfast.
records.zomi: Zan ma-in ipte i thuk a, zingsang an ah mi khat ciat in nasep khat a nei hi.

records.english: Whoever is up first should switch on the kettle and open the curtains.
records.zomi: A thou masa peuhpeuh in tui suangna a vaksak ding a, tukvuang puan a hon ding hi.

records.english: My grandmother made me drink a glass of warm water every morning to wake me up.
records.zomi: Ka pi in hong phawngsak nadingin zingsang simin tui lum glass khat hong dawnsak hi.

records.english: My roommate's loud music woke me up every morning at six.
records.zomi: Ka khan kihawm lawm' la ging sang in zingsang simin nai guk ciangin hong phawngsak hi.

records.english: We agreed that she would use headphones until I was up.
records.zomi: Ka thoh dong headphone a zat dingin i kithukim hi.

records.english: What would you do if you woke up and the whole house had no water?
records.zomi: Na thoh ciangin inn bup ah tui a om kei leh bang na hih ding hiam?

records.english: How do you wake up a teenager who won't get out of bed?
records.zomi: Lupna pan thou nuam lo khangno khat bangci-in na phawngsak hiam?

records.english: Why do you set three alarms every morning?
records.zomi: Bang hangin zingsang simin alarm thum na koih hiam?

records.english: My little boy cries every morning because he doesn't want to wear his school uniform.
records.zomi: Ka tapa neu in a sang puan a silh nuam loh manin zingsang simin a kap hi.

records.english: We let him choose his own socks, and now he gets dressed without complaining.
records.zomi: Amah' khedap-ip a teel dingin i phal a, tu-in phun lo-in puan a silh hi.

records.english: I kept sleeping through my alarm and arriving late to work.
records.zomi: Ka alarm ka za lo den a, nasepna ah ka nun den hi.

records.english: Now I put the phone on the other side of the room, so I have to get up to switch it off.
records.zomi: Tu-in phone khan gal lam ah ka koih a, khek dingin ka thou ding a kisam hi.

records.english: The car wouldn't start on the coldest morning of the year.
records.zomi: Kum sung-a zingsang vot pen-in mawtaw a kipan nuam kei hi.

records.english: My brother gave me a lift to work, and I had the battery replaced that afternoon.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in nasepna ah hong tuangsak a, tua nitak lam ka battery ka lai sak hi.

records.english: Not until I moved closer to my office did I stop arriving late every morning.
records.zomi: Ka office kiang zaw ah ka tuah ciang bek zingsang simin ka nun tawp hi.

records.english: Could you iron my shirt while I make the coffee?
records.zomi: Khawfi ka bawl laitakin ka angki na phawk sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Is it really such a bad idea to skip breakfast if you're not hungry until ten?
records.zomi: Nai sawm dong na gilkial kei leh zingsang an nusia pen ngaihsutna hoih lo mahmah ahi taktak hiam?

records.english: Kids, if you lay out your clothes tonight, the morning will be much easier.
records.zomi: Naupangte, tuni zanin na puan uh koih khol un leh zingsang a baih zaw mahmah ding hi.

records.english: Many people say that a short walk in the morning helps them feel awake for the rest of the day.
records.zomi: Mi tampi in zingsang-a vak tomno in a ni bup a mit khak lo dingin a huh hi, a ci uh hi.

records.english: My father says that mornings are like a river, because once you start moving, everything flows.
records.zomi: Ka pa in zingsangte pen gun bang ahi a, na kisuan kipat ciangin khempeuh a luang hi, a ci hi.

records.english: The more I looked at my phone in the morning, the later I left the house.
records.zomi: Zingsangin ka phone ka en tam semsem ciangin inn ka nusia nun semsem hi.

records.english: Do you prefer a quiet morning or a busy one?
records.zomi: Zingsang dai na deih zaw hiam, buai na deih zaw hiam?

records.english: Everyone, breakfast is on the table, so please come down now.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, zingsang an dawhkan tungah a om khin ahih manin tu-in hong tum un.

records.english: Why does the bathroom always smell of burnt toast in the morning?
records.zomi: Bang hangin zingsang simin kisilna inn in moh kang namtui a nam tawntung hiam?

records.english: My son stopped being late after his teacher made him stay behind for five minutes each time.
records.zomi: A nun simin a saya in minit nga a omsak khit ciangin ka tapa a nun tawp hi.

records.english: My husband gets up first and makes tea for everyone, so the morning starts calmly.
records.zomi: Ka pasal a thou masa a, mi khempeuh adingin tea a bawl ahih manin zingsang dai takin a kipan hi.

records.english: If you find mornings stressful, it may help to prepare as much as possible the night before.
records.zomi: Zingsang na lungkhamsak leh zan ma-in a theih tan kiman khol in a huh kha ding hi.

records.english: Which of you left the front door open all night?
records.zomi: Note lak ah kua in zan bup mai lam kongkhak a hong nusia hiam?

records.english: If I promise to be quick in the shower, can I stay in bed until seven?
records.zomi: Manlang takin ka kisil ding hi, ci-in ka kiciam leh nai sagih dong lupna tungah ka om thei ding hiam?

records.english: Having worked night shifts for years, my mother still finds it hard to wake up early.
records.zomi: Kum tampi sung zan nasep a sep khit ciangin ka nu in zingsang thoh a haksa sa lai hi.

records.english: Is it possible to wake up early without feeling tired all day?
records.zomi: Ni bup tawl lo-in zingsang tung ah thou thei hiam?

records.english: Rather than rushing to get ready, I now wake up half an hour earlier and enjoy a quiet cup of tea.
records.zomi: Kiman dingin manlang sangin tu-in nai khen khat ma-in ka thou a, tea haai dai khat ka dawn hi.

records.english: Where did you put my glasses last night?
records.zomi: Zanni zanin ka mitlimlang koi ah na koih hiam?

records.english: The milk had gone sour, so there was nothing for the children's breakfast.
records.zomi: Nawi a thuk khin ahih manin naupangte' zingsang an adingin bangmah a om kei hi.

records.english: I ran to the corner shop in my slippers and came back with fresh milk and bread.
records.zomi: Lampi kiheina-a dawr ah ka khedap neu tawh ka tai a, nawi thak leh moh tawh ka hong kik hi.

records.english: Could you help me plait my hair before the bus comes?
records.zomi: Bus a tun ma-in ka sam khih dingin hong huh thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: The power went off just as I was drying my hair.
records.zomi: Ka sam ka keusak laitakin meivak a mit hi.

records.english: I tied it back and went to work with it still damp.
records.zomi: Nung lam ah ka khih a, a nawng lai-in nasepna ah ka pai hi.

records.english: What makes it so hard to get out of bed on winter mornings?
records.zomi: Khuavot zingsang ciangin lupna pan thou bang in a haksasak hiam?

records.english: My alarm clock broke, so my neighbor knocked on my door at six for a whole week.
records.zomi: Ka alarm nai a sia ahih manin ka inn veng in kal bup nai guk ciangin ka kongkhak a kiu hi.

records.english: My daughter can never find her shoes in the morning.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in zingsangin a khedap a mu ngei kei hi.

records.english: We put a basket by the front door, and all the shoes go in it at night.
records.zomi: Mai lam kongkhak kiang ah bawm khat i koih a, zan ciangin khedap khempeuh a sung ah a lut hi.

records.english: I'm too tired to cook breakfast, so we're having fruit and yogurt today.
records.zomi: Zingsang an bawl dingin ka tawl lua ahih manin tuni-in theigah leh yogurt i ne ding hi.

records.english: The hot water ran out before I could have a shower.
records.zomi: Ka kisil ma-in tui lum a bei hi.

records.english: We had the water heater repaired, and now there's enough for the whole family.
records.zomi: Tui lumsakna set i bawl siang sak a, tu-in innkuan bup adingin a kicing hi.

records.english: Had I gone to bed earlier, I wouldn't have overslept on the morning of my exam.
records.zomi: A ma zaw-in ka lum le, ka sitna zingsang-in ka ihmu lua kei ding hi.

records.english: Who used all the toothpaste and didn't buy more?
records.zomi: Ha silna khempeuh kua in a zang bei a, a thak a lei kei hiam?

records.english: My son takes so long in the bathroom that his sisters are always late.
records.zomi: Ka tapa kisilna inn ah a sawt lua ahih manin a sanggam nute a nun tawntung uh hi.

records.english: We bought a small timer, and each child gets ten minutes.
records.zomi: Nai neu khat i lei a, naupang khat ciat in minit sawm a ngah uh hi.

records.english: My grandfather taught me to respect older people and to listen before I speak.
records.zomi: Ka pu in upate zahtak dingin leh ka gen ma-in ngai dingin hong hilh hi.

records.english: Why do people in your village always help with each other's harvest?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na khua-a mite in khat leh khat buh lak ah a kihuh tawntung uh hiam?

records.english: Because next year it may be their own harvest that needs extra hands.
records.zomi: Kum zom ciangin amau' buh lak in khut behlap a kisam kha ding ahih manin.

records.english: Children, who can tell me why we help people we don't know?
records.zomi: Naupangte, bang hangin i theih loh mite i huh hiam kua in hong gen thei ding hiam?

records.english: Having grown up in a close community, my cousin found city life lonely at first.
records.zomi: Mipi kinai lak ah a khan khit ciangin ka sanggam in khuapi nuntakna a masa-in a lungngaihhuai sa hi.

records.english: It is considered rude in my family to eat before the guests have been served.
records.zomi: Ka innkuan ah khualte a kipiak ma-in an nek pen zahtakna om lo-in kingaihsun hi.

records.english: When a family loses someone, the neighbors bring rice and firewood for days.
records.zomi: Innkuan khat in mi a mansuah ciangin inn vengte in ni tampi sung buh leh sing a tawi uh hi.

records.english: What does your community value most?
records.zomi: Na mipi in bang a manphat sak pen hiam?

records.english: Helping one another, especially in hard times.
records.zomi: Khat leh khat kihuh, a diakin hun haksa ciangin.

records.english: In my family, we always share food with neighbors who have less than we do.
records.zomi: Ka innkuan ah ei sangin a nei tawm zaw inn vengte tawh an i hawm tawntung hi.

records.english: Tell the newcomers that they're welcome to join us at the community meal.
records.zomi: Hong thakte mipi an nekna ah i kiang ah kihel thei uh hi, ci-in hilh un.

records.english: What would you teach a child about being a good neighbor?
records.zomi: Inn veng hoih hih dan naupang khat bang na hilh ding hiam?

records.english: The more our young people move to the cities, the harder it becomes to keep old traditions alive.
records.zomi: I khangnote khuapi ah a pai tam semsem ciangin ngeina luite kem a haksa semsem hi.

records.english: Everyone, please bring a tool on Saturday, because we're repairing the village path together.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, Kiginni-in khua lampi khawm-in i bawl siang ding ahih manin nasepna van khat tawi un.

records.english: Volunteers from our church repaired the roof of an elderly couple's house.
records.zomi: I pawlpi pan thalawpte in zi leh pasal upa nih' inn innkhum a bawl siang uh hi.

records.english: How do you show respect to an elder when you visit their home?
records.zomi: Upa khat' inn na veh ciangin bangci-in zahtakna na lak hiam?

records.english: Where does the village keep the tools that everyone shares?
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh' kihawm nasepna vante khua in koi ah a koih hiam?

records.english: I learned from my father that a good name is worth more than money.
records.zomi: Min hoih pen sum sangin a manphat zaw hi, cih ka pa pan ka sin hi.

records.english: When the rains destroyed the bridge, the whole village worked for three days to rebuild it.
records.zomi: Guah in lei a susiat ciangin khua bup ni thum a lam kik dingin a sem uh hi.

records.english: The women cooked for the workers, and the children carried water.
records.zomi: Numeite in nasemte adingin an a huan uh a, naupangte in tui a pua uh hi.

records.english: When the bridge was finished, the elders thanked everyone and prayed together.
records.zomi: Lei a zawh ciangin upate in mi khempeuh lungdam a gen uh a, khawm-in thu a ngen uh hi.

records.english: In our village, disagreements are often settled by the elders rather than by the police.
records.zomi: I khua ah kithukimlohnate a tamzaw-in palik sangin upate in a khensat uh hi.

records.english: If we want our children to share our values, we have to show those values in our own lives.
records.zomi: I tate in i manphatsakte a zuih ding uh i deih leh i nuntakna mah ah tua manphatnate i lak ding hi.

records.english: We were taught that keeping a promise is more important than being right.
records.zomi: Kiciamna zuih pen dik sangin a thupi zaw hi, ci-in kihilh hi.

records.english: Could you help me carry this rice to the widow at the end of the road?
records.zomi: Lampi tawp-a meigong kiangah hih buh pua dingin hong huh thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Can I join the group that visits older people on Sundays?
records.zomi: Nipini simin upate a veh pawl ah ka kihel thei ding hiam?

records.english: Not until I lived abroad did I understand how much my community had shaped who I am.
records.zomi: Gamdang ah ka om ciang bek ka mipi in kua ka hi hiam bangzah a bawl hiam ka thei hi.

records.english: My mother wove a blanket for the new baby next door.
records.zomi: Ka nu in kiang inn-a naungek thak adingin puannak khat a tah hi.

records.english: Rather than asking for payment, the carpenter accepted a meal and our family's thanks.
records.zomi: Man ngen sangin sing seemmi in an khat leh i innkuan' lungdam genna a sang hi.

records.english: Respect for others, in my grandfather's view, matters more than wealth or education.
records.zomi: Ka pu' ngaihsutna ah midangte zahtakna pen hauhna hiam pilna sangin a thupi zaw hi.

records.english: Is it possible to keep these values alive when families are spread across different countries?
records.zomi: Innkuante gam tuamtuam ah a kizel uh laitakin hih manphatnate kem thei ding hiam?

records.english: Shall we visit the family whose house burned down and take them some blankets?
records.zomi: A inn kang innkuan i veh-in puannak tawmno i tawi ding hiam?

records.english: Our community keeps a small fund so that families can borrow money in an emergency.
records.zomi: I mipi in innkuante lauhuaina hun ciangin sum a leitawi theih nadingun sum kholna neu khat a kem hi.

records.english: Many older people in our community believe that hard work and patience bring respect.
records.zomi: I mipi sung-a upa tampi in hanciamna leh thuakzawhna in zahtakna a tawi hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: Do you think young people still care about community values?
records.zomi: Khangnote in mipi manphatnate a ngaihsun lai uh in na ngaihsun hiam?

records.english: Nobody in our village has to face trouble alone, and that's what I treasure most about it.
records.zomi: I khua ah kuamah in buaina amah bek a tuak lo hi, a tua pen ka manphat sak pen ahi hi.

records.english: Children in our community learn to greet every older person they meet.
records.zomi: I mipi sung-a naupangte in a muh upa khempeuh hopih dingin a sin uh hi.

records.english: I do want my children to grow up knowing that they belong to a community.
records.zomi: Ka tate mipi khat sung-a mi ahi uh hi, cih theih-in a khan ding uh ka deih mahmah hi.

records.english: Although people in our town have different opinions, they still come together whenever a family is in need.
records.zomi: I khuapi-a mite ngaihsutna tuamtuam a neih hangin innkuan khat a kisap ciangin a kikhawm lai uh hi.

records.english: Had our neighbors not taken us in after the fire, we would have had nowhere to sleep.
records.zomi: Mei kangna khit ciangin i inn vengte in hong sang kei le, ihmutna mun i nei kei ding hi.

records.english: Some members of our community worry that modern life is weakening the habit of helping one another.
records.zomi: I mipi sung-a mi khenkhatte in tu hun nuntakna in kihuhna ngeina a hat losak hi, ci-in a lungkham uh hi.

records.english: Would you like to help us prepare food for the community meal?
records.zomi: Mipi an nekna adingin an bawl dingin hong huh nuam na hi hiam?

records.english: My grandmother compares our community to a woven basket, in which every strand supports the others.
records.zomi: Ka pi in i mipi bawm tah tawh a kikhaikhin a, a khau khat ciat in a dangte a len hi.

records.english: My grandmother says that a guest should never leave a house hungry.
records.zomi: Khual khat gilkial-in inn khat a nusia ngei lo ding hi, ci-in ka pi in a ci hi.

records.english: My uncle uses his truck to take sick people from the village to the hospital.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in khua pan zato ah a dam lo mite puak dingin a mawtaw lian a zang hi.

records.english: Why does everyone in the village go to every wedding?
records.zomi: Bang hangin khua sung-a mi khempeuh mopawi khempeuh ah a pai uh hiam?

records.english: Every family gives a little rice to the church at harvest time.
records.zomi: Buh lak hun ciangin innkuan khempeuh in pawlpi kiangah buh tawmno a pia uh hi.

records.english: My father lent his ox to a neighbor whose own animal had died.
records.zomi: Ka pa in a ganhing a si inn veng khat kiangah a bawng a ngetsak hi.

records.english: Kids, remember to thank the cook before you leave the table.
records.zomi: Naupangte, dawhkan na nusiat ma-un an huanpa kiangah lungdam gen ding phawk un.

records.english: The young men carried the old woman's furniture up the hill on their backs.
records.zomi: Khangno pasalte in numei upa' inn vante mual tung dong a nung tungah a pua uh hi.

records.english: If someone is sick, a neighbor might cook for the whole family until they recover.
records.zomi: Kuamah a dam loh leh a dam dong inn veng khat in innkuan bup adingin an a huan kha ding hi.

records.english: Our church collects money every month for families who need help with school fees.
records.zomi: I pawlpi in sang man adingin huhna a kisap innkuante adingin kha simin sum a kaikhawm hi.

records.english: We say that a village is strong when nobody is left behind.
records.zomi: Kuamah kinusia lo ciangin khua a hat hi, i ci hi.

records.english: Honesty is very important to my grandparents.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh pite adingin thumanna a thupi mahmah hi.

records.english: Who looks after the children in your village when their parents work in the fields?
records.zomi: Na khua ah nu leh pate lo ah a nasep laitakun naupangte kua in a kem hiam?

records.english: Did your parents teach you to share with your neighbors?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa in na inn vengte tawh hawm dingin hong hilh uh hiam?

records.english: In our village, people help each other build new houses.
records.zomi: I khua ah mite inn thak lam ah a kihuh uh hi.

records.english: Whoever has a little extra is expected to share it with those who have less.
records.zomi: Tawmno a behlap nei peuhpeuh in a nei tawm zawte tawh a hawm dingin kilamen hi.

records.english: The youth group cleans the cemetery before every festival.
records.zomi: Pawi khempeuh ma-in khangno pawl in han mun a siangsak uh hi.

records.english: It might take years for newcomers to feel fully part of the community.
records.zomi: Hong thakte mipi sung-a mi bup a kisak nadingun kum tampi a la kha ding hi.

records.english: Not until the electricity was cut for a week did we learn to cook everything over a fire.
records.zomi: Kal khat sung meivak a kitan ciang bek mei tungah khempeuh huan i sin hi.

records.english: Although cooking every day can be tiring, it's usually cheaper than eating out.
records.zomi: Ni simin an huan a tawlsak thei hangin a tamzaw-in pua-a an nek sangin a neem zaw hi.

records.english: Can I use your blender to make the sauce?
records.zomi: An tui bawl dingin na blender ka zang thei ding hiam?

records.english: Did you remember to soak the beans last night?
records.zomi: Zanni zanin be tui sung ah koih na phawk hiam?

records.english: How do you cook for a large family on a small budget?
records.zomi: Sum tawm tawh innkuan lian adingin bangci-in an na huan hiam?

records.english: Would you mind peeling the potatoes while I start the sauce?
records.zomi: An tui ka kipat laitakin alu na khilh sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Children aren't allowed to use the oven without an adult in our house.
records.zomi: I inn ah upa om lo-in naupangte in oven a zang thei kei uh hi.

records.english: Could we make the curry less spicy for the children and add chili to ours afterward?
records.zomi: Naupangte adingin curry a ha tawm zaw-in i bawl a, a nung ciangin eite' ah malcha i behlap thei ding hiam?

records.english: Why does the bread never rise when I bake it?
records.zomi: Bang hangin ka bawl ciangin moh a zang ngei kei hiam?

records.english: I never have time to cook on weekdays.
records.zomi: Kal sung ni ah an huan hun ka nei ngei kei hi.

records.english: Now I buy lunch from a woman at the market who sells home-cooked rice and beans.
records.zomi: Tu-in zuakna mun-a inn-a huan buh leh be a zuak numei khat pan sun an ka lei hi.

records.english: Our old fridge kept freezing the vegetables.
records.zomi: I khal bawm lui in anteh a khal den hi.

records.english: A repairman adjusted the temperature, and now nothing gets frozen by mistake.
records.zomi: Bawlsiangpa in a vot dan a bawl siang a, tu-in khialh-in bangmah a khal nawn kei hi.

records.english: How can I stop the noodles from sticking together?
records.zomi: An-ngum a kibelh lo nadingin bangci-in ka hih thei ding hiam?

records.english: Rinse them in cold water as soon as they're cooked, and add a little oil.
records.zomi: A min pah-in tui vot sung ah sil inla, sathau tawmno behlap in.

records.english: My husband and I both like to cook, and we kept getting in each other's way.
records.zomi: Ka pasal leh kei a nih un an huan i deih a, i kikham den hi.

records.english: Now one of us chops while the other one stirs, and dinner is ready in half the time.
records.zomi: Tu-in khat in a at laitakin a dang khat in a ngom a, nitak an hun khen khat sungin a kim hi.

records.english: Why don't we buy a rice cooker, since we eat rice every day?
records.zomi: Ni simin buh i nek manin bang hangin buh huanna set khat i lei kei ding hiam?

records.english: Had I read the recipe properly, I wouldn't have used salt instead of sugar in the cake.
records.zomi: An huan dan lai hoih takin ka sim le, cake ah sugar sangin cii ka zang kei ding hi.

records.english: If you don't have much time in the evenings, it might help to prepare the vegetables in the morning.
records.zomi: Nitak lam hun tam na nei kei leh zingsang ciangin anteh bawl khol in a huh kha ding hi.

records.english: Why don't you write the shopping list while I check what's left in the cupboards?
records.zomi: Van bawm sung ah bang a om lai hiam ka en laitakin bang hangin van lei list na gelh kei hiam?

records.english: Who left the milk out all night?
records.zomi: Zan bup nawi kua in a pua ah a nusia hiam?

records.english: Many families in our town now cook on electric stoves because gas has become so expensive.
records.zomi: Gas a man tam lua ahih manin i khuapi-a innkuan tampi in tu-in meivak meikhuk tawh an a huan uh hi.

records.english: My mother says, "Cook with what you have, not with what you wish you had."
records.zomi: Ka nu in, “Na deih tawh hi lo-in na neih tawh huan in,” a ci hi.

records.english: Cooking without a plan is like walking without a map, because you rarely end up where you wanted.
records.zomi: Gelna om lo-a an huan pen map om lo-a kalsuan bang ahi a, na deihna mun ah na tung ngei tawm hi.

records.english: Which pan should I use for the eggs?
records.zomi: Aktui adingin koi bel ka zang ding hiam?

records.english: Having cooked for a family of eight for thirty years, my aunt can make a meal out of almost anything.
records.zomi: Kum sawmthum sung mi giat innkuan adingin an a huan khit ciangin ka ni in bangpeuh tawh an a bawl thei hi.

records.english: The soup was far too salty to eat.
records.zomi: An tui ne dingin a al lua hi.

records.english: I added more water and a peeled potato, which soaked up some of the salt.
records.zomi: Tui behlap leh alu kikhilh khat ka koih a, tua in cii khenkhat a dawp hi.

records.english: My son is allergic to nuts, so we check every label before we buy anything.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in theigah keu a ne thei kei ahih manin bangmah i lei ma-in a min khempeuh i en hi.

records.english: The smoke alarm goes off every time I fry fish.
records.zomi: Nga ka kang simin meikhu alarm a ging hi.

records.english: We opened the window and switched on the fan, and it hasn't gone off since.
records.zomi: Tukvuang i hong a, fan i vaksak a, tua pan a ging nawn kei hi.

records.english: Use a wooden spoon so that you don't scratch the new pan.
records.zomi: Bel thak na khuai lo nadingin sing kawm zang in.

records.english: May I taste the curry before you add more chili?
records.zomi: Malcha behlap na koih ma-in curry ka tet thei ding hiam?

records.english: Could you cook something soft for Grandpa, since his teeth hurt?
records.zomi: Ka pu' ha a nat ahih manin a nem bangmah na huan sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Shall I make enough dinner for your friends as well?
records.zomi: Na lawmte adingin zong nitak an kicing ka bawl ding hiam?

records.english: Whoever finishes eating first should start clearing the table.
records.zomi: A ne zo masa peuhpeuh in dawhkan siangsak a kipan ding hi.

records.english: I cook extra rice every evening so that the children can take it to school for lunch.
records.zomi: Naupangte in sun an adingin sang ah a tawi theih nadingun nitak simin buh behlap ka huan hi.

records.english: The rice always burns at the bottom of our old pot.
records.zomi: I beel lui nuai ah buh a kang tawntung hi.

records.english: We bought a heavy pan with a thick base, and now the rice cooks evenly.
records.zomi: A nuai tawtawh bel gik khat i lei a, tu-in buh a kibang takin a min hi.

records.english: The more often you cook a dish, the less you need to look at the recipe.
records.zomi: An khat na huan den semsem ciangin a huan dan lai na en tawm semsem hi.

records.english: The cooker stopped working halfway through dinner.
records.zomi: Nitak an kimlai-in meikhuk a sem nawn kei hi.

records.english: We finished the soup on the neighbor's stove and had the cooker repaired the next day.
records.zomi: Inn veng' meikhuk tungah an tui i zo a, a zing ni-in meikhuk i bawl siang sak hi.

records.english: Rather than throwing away leftover vegetables, we turn them into soup the next day.
records.zomi: Anteh nusiate paai sangin a zing ni-in an tui ah i bawl hi.

records.english: Where's the lid for this pan?
records.zomi: Hih bel khuhna koi ah a om hiam?

records.english: The bread went stale before we could finish it.
records.zomi: I nek zawh ma-in moh a lui hi.

records.english: Now we slice it on the first day and keep half in the freezer.
records.zomi: Tu-in ni masa pen-in i at a, a khen khat khal bawm ah i koih hi.

records.english: The kitchen gets so hot in summer that nobody wants to cook.
records.zomi: Khal hun ah an huanna a sa lua ahih manin kuamah in an huan a deih kei uh hi.

records.english: We started cooking in the cool early mornings and eating cold dishes at night.
records.zomi: Zingsang tung a vot hun ah an i huan kipan a, zan ah an vot i ne hi.

records.english: What can I cook when there's almost nothing in the fridge?
records.zomi: Khal bawm sung ah bangmah dek a om kei ciangin bang ka huan thei ding hiam?

records.english: Fried rice with an egg and whatever vegetables are left over.
records.zomi: Aktui khat leh a nusia anteh tawh buh kikang.

records.english: Is it possible to bake a cake without eggs?
records.zomi: Aktui om lo-in cake khat bawl thei hiam?

records.english: Yes, you can use mashed banana instead, and the cake stays moist.
records.zomi: Thei hi, a sangin nahtang kinawi na zang thei a, cake a nem den hi.

records.english: Please don't put metal dishes in the microwave.
records.zomi: Microwave sung ah thih kuang koih kei in.

records.english: The knife was so blunt that it squashed the tomatoes instead of slicing them.
records.zomi: Namsau a at lo lua ahih manin tomatote at sangin a nek nawi hi.

records.english: A neighbor sharpened it on a stone for us, and it cuts perfectly again.
records.zomi: Inn veng khat in suang tungah a hiamsak a, a hoih takin a at kik hi.

records.english: What would you cook if guests arrived with no warning?
records.zomi: Gen lo-in khualte a tun leh bang na huan ding hiam?

records.english: The children complain that we eat the same thing every week.
records.zomi: Kal simin an kibang i ne den hi, ci-in naupangte in a phun uh hi.

records.english: Each child now chooses one dinner a week, and they help to cook it.
records.zomi: Tu-in naupang khat ciat in kal khat ah nitak an khat a teel uh a, a huan nadingin a huh uh hi.

records.english: What I find hardest is cooking something that everyone in the family will eat.
records.zomi: Ka haksa sak pen pen innkuan sung-a mi khempeuh in a nek ding bangmah huan ahi hi.

records.english: Is it worth paying someone to clean the carpets?
records.zomi: Tuutphah siangsak dingin kuamah sawl a manphat hiam?

records.english: If the clutter feels overwhelming, it may help to start with a single drawer.
records.zomi: Van buaite in hong lungkhamsak leh bawm neu khat tawh kipan in a huh kha ding hi.

records.english: The more things you own, the more time you spend looking after them.
records.zomi: Van tam na neih semsem ciangin amaute kemna ah hun tam na zang semsem hi.

records.english: Why does every flat surface in this house end up covered in letters?
records.zomi: Bang hangin hih inn-a mun dai khempeuh lai tawh a kikhuh tawntung hiam?

records.english: Which box are the plates in?
records.zomi: Kuangte koi bawm sung ah a om hiam?

records.english: Not until we emptied the shed did we discover that mice had been living in the old sofa.
records.zomi: Van inn i awngsak ciang bek zusate sofa lui sung ah a om khin uh hi, cih i thei hi.

records.english: The kitchen drawer was so crowded that we couldn't find a single spoon.
records.zomi: An huanna bawm a dim lua ahih manin kawm khat zong i mu thei kei hi.

records.english: My husband made small wooden dividers so that every tool has its own place.
records.zomi: Ka pasal in nasepna van khempeuh in a mun a neih theih nadingin sing khenna neute a bawl hi.

records.english: In smaller flats, people often keep their belongings under the bed or on high shelves.
records.zomi: Inn neu zaw ah mite in a vante lupna nuai hiam koihna sang tungah a koih den uh hi.

records.english: An untidy room is like a noisy mind, because both make it hard to concentrate.
records.zomi: Khan buai pen lungsim ging bang ahi a, a nih in lungsim koih a haksasak hi.

records.english: My roommate leaves dirty dishes in the sink for days.
records.zomi: Ka khan kihawm lawm in kuang nin ni tampi sung kuang silna ah a nusia hi.

records.english: We agreed that dishes must be washed before bedtime, and she has kept her promise.
records.zomi: Ihmut ma-in kuang kisil ding hi, ci-in i kithukim a, a kiciamna a zui hi.

records.english: What would you keep if you could save only three things from your house?
records.zomi: Na inn pan van thum bek na hon thei leh bang na kem ding hiam?

records.english: Rather than cleaning the whole house on Saturday, we do one room each evening.
records.zomi: Kiginni-in inn bup siangsak sangin nitak simin khan khat i siangsak hi.

records.english: Had we labeled the boxes when we moved, we wouldn't have spent a week looking for the kettle.
records.zomi: I tuah ciangin bawmte min i gelh le, tui suangna zong-in kal khat i zang kei ding hi.

records.english: Who borrowed the scissors and didn't put them back?
records.zomi: Namtemna kua in a zang a, a koih kik kei hiam?

records.english: Where should we keep the cleaning products so that the baby can't reach them?
records.zomi: Naungek in a phak loh nadingin siangsakna vante koi ah i koih ding hiam?

records.english: May I take your old textbooks to the school library, or are you keeping them?
records.zomi: Na sang laibu luite sang laibu inn ah ka tawi thei ding hiam, na kem ding hiam?

records.english: Don't use bleach on the wooden table, or it will leave white marks.
records.zomi: Sing dawhkan tungah bleach zang kei in, a hi kei leh mun kang a nusia ding hi.

records.english: The garage was so full that the car hadn't been inside it for years.
records.zomi: Mawtaw inn a dim lua ahih manin kum tampi sung mawtaw a sung ah a lut kei hi.

records.english: My brothers spent a weekend clearing it out and selling the old tools at the market.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasalte kal tawp khat a siangsak dingin a zang uh a, nasepna van luite zuakna mun ah a zuak uh hi.

records.english: Sorting the photos took weeks, but now my children can find any birthday in seconds.
records.zomi: Limte khen kal tampi a la hi, ahi zongin tu-in ka tate in pianni khatpeuh a manlang takin a mu thei uh hi.

records.english: Can I borrow your ladder to clean the top of the cupboards?
records.zomi: Van bawmte tung lam siangsak dingin na kahlei ka ngetsak thei ding hiam?

records.english: How do you keep the house tidy when everyone is so busy?
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh a buai lua laitakin inn bangci-in na siangsak den hiam?

records.english: It's raining, so let's sort the old clothes instead of working in the garden.
records.zomi: Guah a zuk ahih manin huan ah sem sangin puan luite khen ni.

records.english: Please don't put anything on the stairs, because someone could trip.
records.zomi: Kuamah a kisut thei ahih manin kahlei tungah bangmah koih kei in.

records.english: I clean the windows with old newspaper because it leaves no streaks.
records.zomi: Bawk a nusia lo ahih manin laithak lui tawh tukvuang ka siangsak hi.

records.english: Let me show you where everything goes, so that you can tidy up on your own next time.
records.zomi: A zom ciangin nangma bek in na siangsak theih nadingin khempeuh koi ah a pai hiam kong etsak ning.

records.english: Although a tidy home takes effort, it saves time when you're in a hurry.
records.zomi: Inn siang in hanciamna a la hangin na manlang ciangin hun hong hun hi.

records.english: Wouldn't it be easier to rent a storage unit than to keep arguing about the boxes in the hallway?
records.zomi: Inn lam-a bawmte thu kinial den sangin van koihna mun khat hal a baih zaw hi lo ding hiam?

records.english: Why don't we give the old furniture to the family that's just moved in?
records.zomi: Bang hangin inn van luite tuah thak innkuan kiangah i pia kei ding hiam?

records.english: I could never find the right key for the shed.
records.zomi: Van inn adingin tawh dik ka mu thei ngei kei hi.

records.english: Now each key has a colored tag, and they all hang on hooks by the back door.
records.zomi: Tu-in tawh khat ciat in rong a nei a, a vekpi nung lam kongkhak kiang-a khaina ah a om uh hi.

records.english: Is it possible to keep a small flat tidy with two children and a dog?
records.zomi: Naupang nih leh ui khat tawh inn neu khat siang takin kem thei hiam?

records.english: Did you put the spare light bulbs somewhere safe?
records.zomi: Meivak bulb behlapte mun bit khat ah na koih hiam?

records.english: How can I stop losing important papers?
records.zomi: Lai thupite ka mansuah lo nadingin bangci-in ka hih thei ding hiam?

records.english: Keep them all in one folder, and put the folder in the same drawer every time.
records.zomi: A vekpi folder khat sung ah koih inla, folder bawm kibang mah ah hun khempeuh koih in.

records.english: We aren't allowed to leave bicycles in the hallway of our building.
records.zomi: I inn lian inn lam ah siiksakol nusia kiphal lo hi.

records.english: My wife says, "If you haven't used it in two years, you don't need it."
records.zomi: Ka zi in, “Kum nih sung na zat kei leh na kisam kei hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: The children's toys were scattered all over the house.
records.zomi: Naupangte' kimawlnate inn bup ah a kizel hi.

records.english: We put a large basket in each room, and the toys go back in it before dinner.
records.zomi: Khan khat ciat ah bawm lian khat i koih a, nitak an ma-in kimawlnate a sung ah a kik hi.

records.english: Everything in the bathroom cabinet was out of date.
records.zomi: Kisilna inn van bawm sung-a khempeuh a hun a bei khin hi.

records.english: I took the old medicines to the pharmacy, where they were disposed of safely.
records.zomi: Zatui luite zatui zuakna ah ka tawi a, tua ah bit takin a paai uh hi.

records.english: My son's desk is covered with papers, and he can never find his homework.
records.zomi: Ka tapa' dawhkan lai tawh a kikhuh a, a inn-a sep ding a mu ngei kei hi.

records.english: We bought him a cheap set of trays, one for each subject.
records.zomi: Laibu khat ciat adingin khat ciat, koihna kuang man neu set khat i lei sak hi.

records.english: Could we fit more shelves in the hallway, or would that make it too narrow?
records.zomi: Inn lam ah koihna behlap i koih thei ding hiam, a neu lua ding hiam?

records.english: Shall I label the jars so that nobody confuses the salt with the sugar again?
records.zomi: Kuamah in cii leh sugar a kikhialh nawn lo nadingin belte min ka gelh ding hiam?

records.english: Could you help me clear out my mother's flat before the new tenants arrive?
records.zomi: Inn luah thakte a tun ma-un ka nu' inn siangsak dingin hong huh thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: My grandson cleans my kitchen every Saturday, and he never asks for anything in return.
records.zomi: Ka tu in Kiginni simin ka an huanna a siangsak a, bangmah a ngen ngei kei hi.

records.english: Would you mind folding the laundry while I sweep?
records.zomi: Ka phiat laitakin puan silte na khiak sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: What I find hardest is throwing away things that belonged to people I loved.
records.zomi: Ka haksa sak pen pen ka it mite' van paai ahi hi.

records.english: The spare room had become a storeroom full of boxes.
records.zomi: Khan behlap bawm tawh a dim van koihna a suak khin hi.

records.english: We sorted everything into three piles to keep, to give away, and to recycle.
records.zomi: Khempeuh bu thum ah i khen hi, kem ding, pia ding, leh bawl kik ding.

records.english: Our cupboard was so full that things fell out every time we opened it.
records.zomi: I van bawm a dim lua ahih manin i hon simin vante a kia hi.

records.english: We moved the summer clothes to a box under the bed, and now the door closes easily.
records.zomi: Khal puante lupna nuai-a bawm khat ah i suan a, tu-in kongkhak a khak baih hi.

records.english: Mold appeared on the bathroom ceiling after the rainy season.
records.zomi: Guah hun khit ciangin kisilna inn innkhum nuai ah a mu kipan hi.

records.english: We cleaned it with vinegar and now leave the window open after every shower.
records.zomi: Thuk tui tawh i siangsak a, tu-in kisil khempeuh khit ciangin tukvuang i hong nusia hi.

records.english: Whoever uses the last of something should write it on the shopping list.
records.zomi: Bangmah a nunung pen a zang peuhpeuh in van lei list ah a gelh ding hi.

records.english: Who put the winter blankets in the same box as the shoes?
records.zomi: Khuavot puannakte khedap tawh bawm kibang ah kua in a koih hiam?

records.english: Having moved house four times in five years, my cousin now owns only what fits in two suitcases.
records.zomi: Kum nga sungin livei inn a tuah khit ciangin ka sanggam in tu-in van bawm nih sung ah a lut tan bek a nei hi.

records.english: Tell the new staff where the first-aid box is kept before their first shift.
records.zomi: Nasemte thak a nasep hun masa ma-un huhna masa bawm koi ah a om hiam hilh un.

records.english: Why does the lift always break down on Monday mornings?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pizing ni zingsang simin lift a sia tawntung hiam?

records.english: My wife packs my lunch every morning, so I never have to buy food at work.
records.zomi: Ka zi in zingsang simin ka sun an a thuk sak ahih manin nasepna ah an ka lei ngei kei hi.

records.english: Why don't we start the meeting at nine instead of eight, when everyone is awake?
records.zomi: Bang hangin nai giat sangin mi khempeuh a mit a hak nai kua ciangin kikhopna i kipan kei ding hiam?

records.english: Which part of your working day would you happily give up?
records.zomi: Na nasep ni sung ah koi khen lungdam taka na nusia ding hiam?

records.english: Who took my coffee cup from the kitchen?
records.zomi: An huanna pan ka khawfi haai kua in a la hiam?

records.english: Having worked night shifts for ten years, my brother still wakes up at three in the morning.
records.zomi: Kum sawm sung zan nasep a sep khit ciangin ka sanggam pasal zingsang nai thum ciangin a thou lai hi.

records.english: The water cooler leaked overnight, and the carpet by the door was soaked.
records.zomi: Zan sungin tui vot set a zu a, kongkhak kiang-a tuutphah a dikdek hi.

records.english: Would you mind answering my phone while I'm in the meeting?
records.zomi: Kikhopna ah ka om laitakin ka phone na dawn sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Could you cover my desk for an hour while I go to the dentist?
records.zomi: Ha siavuan kiang ka pai laitakin nai khat sung ka dawhkan na kem sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Which day does the canteen serve fish?
records.zomi: Anneekna in bang ni-in nga a zuak hiam?

records.english: Did anyone tell the delivery driver that the gate is locked after six?
records.zomi: Nai guk zawh ciangin kongpi kikhak hi, ci-in van puak pa kuamah in a hilh hiam?

records.english: The bus to the factory was cancelled without warning.
records.zomi: Factory pai bus gen lo-in a kikhak hi.

records.english: Four of us shared a taxi and split the fare.
records.zomi: Ei mi li taxi khat i kihawm a, a man i khen hi.

records.english: Wouldn't it make sense to share the late shifts more evenly among the team?
records.zomi: Zan nasepte pawl sung ah kibang zawin hawm a dik zaw hi lo ding hiam?

records.english: Please don't eat at your desk, because crumbs damage the keyboards.
records.zomi: Moh nenate in keyboard a susia ahih manin na dawhkan ah an ne kei in.

records.english: The more meetings I attend, the less time I have for my actual work.
records.zomi: Kikhopna tam semsem ka kah ciangin ka nasep taktak adingin hun ka nei tawm semsem hi.

records.english: Had I written the deadline in my diary, I wouldn't have forgotten the report.
records.zomi: Ka diary ah a tawp ni ka gelh le, report ka mangngilh kei ding hi.

records.english: May I leave early on Friday to collect my daughter from the airport?
records.zomi: Vanlengtual pan ka tanu la dingin Laithai ni-in manlang zaw-in ka pai thei ding hiam?

records.english: Not until the new manager arrived did anyone fix the broken heating in our office.
records.zomi: Manager thak a tun ciang bek i office-a mei lumna sia kuamah in a bawl siang hi.

records.english: The new trainee was too shy to ask questions.
records.zomi: Sinna mi thak in dotna dot dingin a zak lua hi.

records.english: I asked her to write her questions down and bring them to me every afternoon.
records.zomi: A dotnate gelh-in nitak lam simin hong tawi dingin ka ngen hi.

records.english: My colleague keeps forgetting to pass on my messages.
records.zomi: Ka nasem lawm in ka thu khakte a pia ding a mangngilh den hi.

records.english: We started writing them in a notebook by the phone, and nothing has been missed since.
records.zomi: Phone kiang-a laibu neu khat ah i gelh kipan a, tua pan bangmah kimansuah nawn lo hi.

records.english: Can I work from home on Wednesday, since the builders are coming?
records.zomi: Inn lamte a hong ding uh ahih manin Nilai ni-in inn ah ka sem thei ding hiam?

records.english: My manager compares a workday to a juggling act, because something always seems about to fall.
records.zomi: Ka manager in nasep ni bangmah khat a kia dek tawntung manin bawlung khawng kimawl tawh a kikhaikhin hi.

records.english: The shop's lights flickered all morning, and customers thought we were closed.
records.zomi: Zingsang bup dawr meivak a ling a, leite in i kikhak in a ngaihsun uh hi.

records.english: We had an electrician replace the wiring, and the problem disappeared.
records.zomi: Meivak khau lai dingin electrician khat i sawl a, buaina a bei hi.

records.english: In our town, many shop workers start before sunrise so that they can rest during the hottest hours.
records.zomi: I khuapi ah dawr nasem tampi in a sat pen hun ah a tawldam theih nadingun ni suak ma-in a kipan uh hi.

records.english: Although long hours may seem impressive, most people work better when they take regular breaks.
records.zomi: Nai sau sem a lamdang bang hangin mi tamzaw in a tawlngak den ciangun a sem hoih zaw uh hi.

records.english: Who's going to lock up tonight?
records.zomi: Tuni zanin kua in a khak ding hiam?

records.english: How do you concentrate when colleagues keep stopping by your desk?
records.zomi: Nasem lawmte in na dawhkan ah a tawl den uh laitakin bangci-in na lungsim na koih hiam?

records.english: I put a small sign on my desk when I need an hour without interruptions.
records.zomi: Kikham lo-in nai khat ka kisap ciangin ka dawhkan tungah lai neu khat ka koih hi.

records.english: When was the last time you took a proper holiday?
records.zomi: Nopsakna hun taktak na lak nunung pen bang ciang ahi hiam?

records.english: Shall I order lunch for the whole team, since nobody has time to go out?
records.zomi: Kuamah in pai khiat hun a nei kei ahih manin pawl bup adingin sun an ka ngen ding hiam?

records.english: Whoever arrives first should switch on the lights and open the shutters.
records.zomi: A tung masa peuhpeuh in meivak a vaksak ding a, kongkhak khuhte a hon ding hi.

records.english: At our factory, phones are not allowed on the floor, so we leave them in lockers.
records.zomi: I factory ah nasepna mun ah phone kiphal lo ahih manin locker sung ah i koih hi.

records.english: What I find hardest about my job is finishing on time when new tasks keep arriving.
records.zomi: Ka nasep ah ka haksa sak pen pen nasep thakte a hong den laitakin hun takin zawh ahi hi.

records.english: Everyone, please sign the visitors' book before going upstairs.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, tung lam na pai ma-un khual hong laibu ah min gelh un.

records.english: Is it fair that the cleaners start work two hours before everyone else?
records.zomi: Siangsakte mi khempeuh sangin nai nih ma-in nasep a kipan uh pen a dik hiam?

records.english: The power went off in the middle of the afternoon, and all the computers shut down.
records.zomi: Nitak lam kimlai-in meivak a mit a, computer khempeuh a mit hi.

records.english: Since then, we save our work every ten minutes.
records.zomi: Tua pan kipan minit sawm simin i nasep i save hi.

records.english: I never have time to eat lunch because the phone never stops ringing.
records.zomi: Phone ging a tawp ngei kei ahih manin sun an nek hun ka nei ngei kei hi.

records.english: We now switch the phones to voicemail between one and two so that everyone can eat.
records.zomi: Tu-in mi khempeuh in an a nek theih nadingun nai khat leh nih kikal ah phone te voicemail ah i koih hi.

records.english: My boss always says, "Tell me about a problem early, not late."
records.zomi: Ka makai in, “Buaina thu a nung ciangin hi lo-in a ma-in hong gen in,” a ci tawntung hi.

records.english: How do you get through a twelve-hour shift without feeling exhausted?
records.zomi: Tawl lua lo-in nai sawm leh nih nasep bangci-in na zo hiam?

records.english: Rather than eating lunch alone at my desk, I now walk to the park with two colleagues.
records.zomi: Ka dawhkan ah keimah bek sun an ne sangin tu-in nasem lawm nih tawh huan lian ah ka vak hi.

records.english: Our team meetings went on for two hours and achieved very little.
records.zomi: I pawl kikhopnate nai nih sung a om a, bangmah tawmno bek a ngah hi.

records.english: Now we stand during meetings, and they rarely last more than twenty minutes.
records.zomi: Tu-in kikhopna laitakin i ding a, minit sawmnih sangin a sau ngei tawm hi.

records.english: I kept missing the morning bus and arriving late for my shift.
records.zomi: Zingsang bus ka mansuah den a, ka nasep hun ah ka nun den hi.

records.english: My manager let me start half an hour later, and I stay half an hour longer in the evening.
records.zomi: Ka manager in nai khen khat nung zaw-in kipan dingin hong phal a, nitak ciangin nai khen khat behlap ka om hi.

records.english: Could the company provide a bus for the workers who live far from the factory?
records.zomi: Factory pan gamla-a om nasemte adingin company in bus khat a pia thei ding hiam?

records.english: The printer jammed just before an important meeting.
records.zomi: Kikhopna thupi khat ma-in printer a kikhak hi.

records.english: A colleague printed the documents on another floor and brought them to me.
records.zomi: Nasem lawm khat in tuang dang ah laite a print a, hong tawi sak hi.

records.english: My emails pile up so quickly that I can't find the important ones.
records.zomi: Ka email te manlang takin a kikhawm ahih manin a thupite ka mu thei kei hi.

records.english: I now check them three times a day instead of every few minutes.
records.zomi: Tu-in minit tawmno simin sangin ni khat ah thumvei ka en hi.

records.english: Is it all right if I work from home on the days the school is closed?
records.zomi: Sang a kikhak ni-in inn ah ka sem leh a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: If your workload is too heavy, it may help to explain to your manager what you can realistically finish.
records.zomi: Na nasep a gik lua leh bangzah na zo thei taktak hiam na manager kiangah na gen siang leh a huh kha ding hi.

records.english: Where do I hand in my time sheet?
records.zomi: Ka nasep hun lai koi ah ka pia ding hiam?

records.english: I make tea for the night guard before I go home, since he works alone until morning.
records.zomi: Zingsang dong amah bek a sem ahih manin inn ka ciah ma-in zan kongpi kemtu adingin tea ka bawl hi.

records.english: Not until we moved away from the main road did we realize how much the traffic had disturbed our sleep.
records.zomi: Lampi lian pan i tuah ciang bek mawtaw ging in i ihmutna bangzah a buaisak hiam i thei hi.

records.english: Our neighbors play loud music until midnight on Saturdays.
records.zomi: I inn vengte Kiginni simin zanlai dong ging sang takin la a sa uh hi.

records.english: We spoke to them politely, and they agreed to turn it down after ten.
records.zomi: Zahtak takin i kiho pih a, nai sawm zawh ciangin a niamsak dingin a kithukim uh hi.

records.english: Why is the baby awake again at three in the morning?
records.zomi: Bang hangin zingsang nai thum ciangin naungek a khanglawh kik hiam?

records.english: If a child keeps waking at night, it may help to keep the room quiet and the light dim.
records.zomi: Naupang khat zan ah a khanglawh den leh khan dai takin kem inla, meivak niam takin koih in a huh kha ding hi.

records.english: The more relaxed the evening, the more easily the children fall asleep.
records.zomi: Nitak a nuam semsem ciangin naupangte a ihmut baih semsem uh hi.

records.english: May I read under the blanket with a torch for ten minutes?
records.zomi: Minit sawm sung puannak nuai ah dawimei tawh ka sim thei ding hiam?

records.english: Shall I bring you a hot water bottle, since you're shivering?
records.zomi: Na ling ahih manin tui lum bel khat kong tawi sak ding hiam?

records.english: Could the children share a room, or would they keep each other awake?
records.zomi: Naupangte khan khat a kihawm thei ding uh hiam, khat leh khat a kiphawngsak ding uh hiam?

records.english: In many homes in our village, the whole family sleeps in one room during the coldest months.
records.zomi: I khua-a inn tampi ah a vot pen kha sungin innkuan bup khan khat ah a ihmu uh hi.

records.english: The bed creaked so loudly that it woke the baby every time I turned over.
records.zomi: Ka kiheih simin lupna ging a sang lua ahih manin naungek a phawngsak hi.

records.english: My husband tightened the screws, and the noise stopped.
records.zomi: Ka pasal in thih khutte a cip sak a, ging a tawp hi.

records.english: How do you get to sleep when you're worried about tomorrow?
records.zomi: Zingciang thu na lungkham ciangin bangci-in na ihmu hiam?

records.english: Sleep is like a shy visitor, because the harder you call it, the less likely it is to come.
records.zomi: Ihmut pen khual zak bang ahi a, na sam hat semsem ciangin a hong tawm semsem hi.

records.english: Had we bought a longer bed, my tall son wouldn't have had to sleep with his feet hanging over the end.
records.zomi: Lupna sau zaw i lei le, ka tapa sang in a tawp ah a khe khai-in a ihmu kei ding hi.

records.english: Which of you left the bathroom light on all night?
records.zomi: Note lak ah kua in zan bup kisilna inn meivak a nusia hiam?

records.english: The street lamp outside shines straight into our bedroom.
records.zomi: Pua-a lampi meivak in i lupna khan ah a tang takin a vak hi.

records.english: We hung thick curtains, and now the room is dark enough to sleep.
records.zomi: Tukvuang puan tawtawh i khai a, tu-in khan ihmut theih dingin a mial hi.

records.english: Whoever goes to bed last should make sure the stove is cold and the candles are out.
records.zomi: A lum nunung peuhpeuh in meikhuk a vot a, khawimeivaakte a mit hiam a en ding hi.

records.english: My grandson says, "I'm not tired," and then falls asleep in the middle of his story.
records.zomi: Ka tu in, “Ka tawl kei hi,” a ci a, tua ciangin a tangthu kimlai ah a ihmu hi.

records.english: My wife likes to read in bed, but the light keeps me awake.
records.zomi: Ka zi in lupna tungah sim a deih a, ahi zongin meivak in hong ihmusak kei hi.

records.english: She bought a small clip-on lamp, so I can sleep while she reads.
records.zomi: Meivak neu khat a lei a, a sim laitakin ka ihmu thei hi.

records.english: The old mattress has a broken spring that sticks into my back.
records.zomi: Mattress lui in a sia spring khat ka nung ah a sun hi.

records.english: We turned it over and slept on the other side until we could afford a new one.
records.zomi: A thak khat i lei zawh dong i heih a, a lam dang tungah i ihmu hi.

records.english: Why don't we hang a bell on the door, so that we hear if the toddler gets up?
records.zomi: Naupang neu a thoh leh i zak theih nadingin kongkhak ah khawngging khat i khai kei ding hiam?

records.english: In July, the upstairs bedroom stayed hot long after the sun had gone down.
records.zomi: July ah ni a tum khit sawt nung dong tung lam lupna khan a sa lai hi.

records.english: We put a bowl of ice in front of the fan, and the air felt much cooler.
records.zomi: Fan mai ah tuikhal kuang khat i koih a, huih a vot zaw mahmah hi.

records.english: Rather than arguing about bedtime every night, we agreed on a fixed time with our teenagers.
records.zomi: Zan simin ihmut hun thu kinial sangin i khangnote tawh hun kikhensat khat ah i kithukim hi.

records.english: Did you remember to switch off the heater?
records.zomi: Mei lumna set khek na phawk hiam?

records.english: The cat kept jumping onto the bed in the middle of the night.
records.zomi: Zawh zanlai-in lupna tungah a diang den hi.

records.english: We started closing the bedroom door, and the cat now sleeps in the kitchen.
records.zomi: Lupna khan kongkhak i khak kipan a, zawh tu-in an huanna ah a ihmu hi.

records.english: Although bedtime routines can seem strict, many children feel safer when they know what comes next.
records.zomi: Ihmut ma-a ngeinate a khauh bang hangin naupang tampi in a zom ding a theih ciangun a bit zaw-in a kisa uh hi.

records.english: The power went off in the night, and the fan stopped working.
records.zomi: Zan sungin meivak a mit a, fan a tawp hi.

records.english: We opened every window and slept on mats near the door, where it was cooler.
records.zomi: Tukvuang khempeuh i hong a, a vot zawk mun kongkhak kiang ah phah tungah i ihmu hi.

records.english: What would you do if a rooster next door crowed at four every morning?
records.zomi: Inn veng-a akpa in zingsang simin nai li ciangin a khuan leh bang na hih ding hiam?

records.english: I drink coffee too late, so I lie awake for hours.
records.zomi: Khawfi a nun lua-in ka dawn ahih manin nai tampi ka mit hak-in ka lum hi.

records.english: Now I switch to ginger tea after lunch, and I fall asleep much more easily.
records.zomi: Tu-in sun an khit ciangin siing tea ka dawn a, ka ihmut a baih zaw mahmah hi.

records.english: Is it all right to let the baby sleep in our bed?
records.zomi: Naungek i lupna ah ihmusak a hoih hiam?

records.english: My son spends hours gaming at night and is exhausted at school.
records.zomi: Ka tapa zan ah game nai tampi a kimawl a, sang ah a tawl mahmah hi.

records.english: We moved the computer into the living room, so he now stops playing when we go to bed.
records.zomi: Computer tutna khan ah i suan a, tu-in i lum ciangin a kimawl tawp hi.

records.english: My daughter refuses to brush her teeth before bed.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in a lum ma-in ha sil a nial hi.

records.english: We let her choose her own toothbrush, and now she brushes without arguing.
records.zomi: Amah' ha silna a teel dingin i phal a, tu-in kinial lo-in a sil hi.

records.english: The children's blankets were damaged by moths over the summer.
records.zomi: Khal hun sungin naupangte' puannakte bawngtawl in a ne hi.

records.english: Please keep the dog out of the bedrooms, since your sister is allergic.
records.zomi: Na sanggam nu in ui a thuak zo kei ahih manin ui lupna khante ah lut sak kei in.

records.english: If I promise to get up on time, can I stay up to watch the end of the match?
records.zomi: Hun takin ka thou ding hi, ci-in ka kiciam leh kimawlna tawp dong en dingin ka om thei ding hiam?

records.english: Would you mind turning the television down, since the children are asleep?
records.zomi: Naupangte a ihmu khin uh ahih manin TV ging na niamsak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Children, please put your clothes on the chair before you get into bed.
records.zomi: Naupangte, lupna tungah na lut ma-un na puan uh tutna tungah koih un.

records.english: Where did you put the spare pillows?
records.zomi: Lukhung behlapte koi ah na koih hiam?

records.english: What I find hardest is switching off my thoughts when the lights go out.
records.zomi: Ka haksa sak pen pen meivak a mit ciangin ka ngaihsutnate khek ahi hi.

records.english: Screens are not allowed in the bedrooms after nine in our house.
records.zomi: I inn ah nai kua zawh ciangin lupna khan ah screen kiphal lo hi.

records.english: What helps a toddler settle down at night?
records.zomi: Naupang neu khat zan ah a ngaih nadingin bang in a huh hiam?

records.english: A warm bath, a short song, and the same bedtime every evening.
records.zomi: Kisilna lum khat, la tom khat, leh nitak simin ihmut hun kibang.

records.english: My little brother was frightened by a scary film and couldn't sleep.
records.zomi: Ka nau pasal film lauhuai khat in a lausak a, a ihmu thei kei hi.

records.english: Our mother sat with him and read his favorite book until he relaxed.
records.zomi: I nu a kiang ah a tu a, a ngaih dong a laibu deih pen a sim sak hi.

records.english: Having worked late every night for a month, my brother finally made a rule never to check emails in bed.
records.zomi: Kha khat sung zan simin a nai khit ciangin ka sanggam pasal in lupna tungah email en ngei lo ding thupiak a bawl hi.

records.english: Who's going to read the bedtime story tonight?
records.zomi: Tuni zanin ihmut ma-a tangthu kua in a sim ding hiam?

records.english: My feet are always cold at night, so I wear thick socks to bed.
records.zomi: Zan ah ka khe a vot tawntung ahih manin lupna ah khedap-ip tawtawh ka bulh hi.

records.english: I set an alarm on my phone to remind me to go to bed at eleven.
records.zomi: Nai sawm leh khat ciangin lum dingin hong phawksak nadingin ka phone ah alarm ka koih hi.

records.english: The mosquito net was torn, and we were bitten all night.
records.zomi: Thangkhuk puan a kek a, zan bup hong se uh hi.

records.english: We mended it with a needle and thread the next morning and tucked the edges under the mattress.
records.zomi: A zing zingsangin zangbuh leh khau tawh i khui a, a gei te mattress nuai ah i lut sak hi.

records.english: In the parable of the prodigal son, the father runs to welcome his son home.
records.zomi: Tapa mangthang gentehna sungah a pa in a tapa muak dingin a tai hi.

records.english: Christian traditions differ in how they describe God's mercy, but all of them speak of forgiveness.
records.zomi: Christian ngeina tuamtuam in Pasian' hehpihna a gen dan uh a kibang kei a, ahi zongin a vekpi un maisakna a gen uh hi.

records.english: We light candles in our church to remember that God's love is with us in dark times.
records.zomi: Hun mial lai-in Pasian' itna i tawh a om hi, cih i phawk nadingin i pawlpi ah khawimeivaak i hal hi.

records.english: Many people find it easier to believe in God's love for others than in God's love for themselves.
records.zomi: Mi tampi in amau tunga Pasian' itna sangin midangte tunga Pasian' itna um a baih zaw sa uh hi.

records.english: Christians often say that because God loves them, they should love their neighbors too.
records.zomi: Pasian in a it ahih manin i inn vengte zong i it ding hi, ci-in Christiante in a gen den uh hi.

records.english: Could you help us carry the food parcels to the families on the hill?
records.zomi: Mual tung-a innkuante kiangah an bawmte pua dingin hong huh thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Where does the Bible talk about God's mercy?
records.zomi: Laisiangtho koi mun ah Pasian' hehpihna a gen hiam?

records.english: A well-known verse says that God so loved the world that he gave his only Son.
records.zomi: Cang min thang khat in Pasian in leitung mite it luat ahih manin a Tapa khat neihsun hong pia hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Christians believe that God loves every person.
records.zomi: Pasian in mi khempeuh a it hi, ci-in Christiante in a um uh hi.

records.english: The volunteers cook meals for homeless people every Friday because they want to share God's love.
records.zomi: Pasian' itna hawm a deih uh ahih manin thalawpte in Laithai ni simin inn neilo mite adingin an a huan uh hi.

records.english: Christians believe that God's love was shown most clearly in the life and death of Jesus.
records.zomi: Pasian' itna Jesu' nuntakna leh sihna ah kician pen-in kilak hi, ci-in Christiante in a um uh hi.

records.english: Thank God for the food before you start eating.
records.zomi: Na nek kipat ma-in an adingin Pasian kiangah lungdam gen in.

records.english: My grandson asked whether God still loves us when we're naughty, and I told him that he does.
records.zomi: Ka tu in i gitlohna hun ciangin zong Pasian in hong it lai hiam a dong a, hong it hi, ka ci hi.

records.english: Is it possible for God to forgive someone who has done something terrible?
records.zomi: Bangmah lauhuai mahmah a hih mi khat Pasian in a maisak thei hiam?

records.english: According to Christian teaching, God's mercy is offered to anyone who truly repents.
records.zomi: Christian hilhna bangin Pasian' hehpihna a kisik taktak mi khempeuh tungah kipia hi.

records.english: Jesus told his followers to love even their enemies, according to the Gospels.
records.zomi: Lungdamna Thu laibute bangin Jesu in a nungzuite a galte zong it dingin a hilh hi.

records.english: Many psalms describe God as patient and slow to anger.
records.zomi: Late tampi in Pasian thuakzawh a, a heh manlang lo hi, ci-in a gen uh hi.

records.english: My aunt keeps a small card with a Bible verse about God's love in her wallet.
records.zomi: Ka ni in a sum ip sung ah Pasian' itna thu Laisiangtho cang tomno kigelh card neu khat a kem hi.

records.english: Why do you think the story of the prodigal son is so loved?
records.zomi: Bang hangin tapa mangthang tangthu mite in a it mahmah uh in na ngaihsun hiam?

records.english: What many believers find most comforting is that God's love does not change with their mood.
records.zomi: Um mi tampi in a hehnepsak pen pen Pasian' itna in amau lungsim tawh a kilai kei hi, cih ahi hi.

records.english: Rather than condemning the woman, Jesus told her to go and sin no more, according to the Gospel of John.
records.zomi: Johan' Lungdamna Thu bangin numei a mawhsak sangin Jesu in pai inla mawh nawn kei in, a ci hi.

records.english: How can I show God's love to someone who has hurt me?
records.zomi: Hong suna mi khat tungah Pasian' itna bangci-in ka lak thei ding hiam?

records.english: A Bible study group uses a small notebook to write down answers to prayer.
records.zomi: Laisiangtho sinna pawl khat in thungetna dawnnate gelh dingin laibu neu khat a zang hi.

records.english: I bought my mother a small wooden cross, which she keeps by her bed.
records.zomi: Ka nu adingin sing singlamteh neu khat ka lei a, a lupna kiang ah a koih hi.

records.english: Please remember the sick and the lonely in your prayers this week.
records.zomi: Hih kal sungin a dam lote leh a lungngaite na thungetna uh ah phawk un.

records.english: We read the story of the lost sheep, and the children drew pictures of the shepherd.
records.zomi: Tuu mangthang tangthu i sim a, naupangte in tuucing lim a gelh uh hi.
