records.english: The church choir sang a hymn about God's mercy at the funeral.
records.zomi: Mithi vuina ah pawlpi la sakte in Pasian' hehpihna thu la khat a sa uh hi.

records.english: Can I pray for you, since you seem so worried?
records.zomi: Na lungkham mahmah bang ahih manin nang adingin thu kong ngetsak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Christians believe that nothing can separate them from the love of God.
records.zomi: Bangmah in Pasian' itna pan amaute a khen thei kei hi, ci-in Christiante in a um uh hi.

records.english: Had the church not taken them in, the family would have spent the winter without a home.
records.zomi: Pawlpi in a sang kei le, innkuan in inn om lo-in khuavot a zang ding uh hi.

records.english: Our pastor often reminds us that God's love does not depend on how good we are.
records.zomi: Pasian' itna pen i hoihna tungah a kinga kei hi, ci-in i pastor in hong phawksak den hi.

records.english: Do you think God's mercy has limits?
records.zomi: Pasian' hehpihna in a tawpna a nei in na ngaihsun hiam?

records.english: The old woman said that God's love had carried her through the war.
records.zomi: Pasian' itna in gal sung ah a pua hi, ci-in numei upa in a ci hi.

records.english: Shall we sing the hymn about God's mercy at the end of the service?
records.zomi: Pawlpi kikhopna tawp ciangin Pasian' hehpihna thu la i sa ding hiam?

records.english: The church collects clothes for refugees so that they can feel welcomed and cared for.
records.zomi: Tai mite in muakna leh kemna a ngah bangin a kisak theih nadingun pawlpi in puan a kaikhawm hi.

records.english: Although Christians speak of God's justice, many say that his mercy is even greater.
records.zomi: Christiante in Pasian' thuman thukhenna a gen uh hangin tampi in a hehpihna a lian zaw hi, a ci uh hi.

records.english: Would you like me to read a psalm with you before you sleep?
records.zomi: Na ihmut ma-in Late khat kong sim pih ding hiam?

records.english: Why do Christians talk so much about grace?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Christiante in hehpihna thu a gen tam mahmah uh hiam?

records.english: In Christian teaching, grace is God's love given freely to people who have not earned it.
records.zomi: Christian hilhna ah hehpihna pen a ngah dingin a kilawm lo mite tungah a man om lo-a kipia Pasian' itna ahi hi.

records.english: Not until he lost his job did my uncle discover how much his church community cared for him.
records.zomi: A nasep a mansuah ciang bek ka pa neu in a pawlpi mite in bangzah a ngaihsun uh hiam a thei hi.

records.english: Many Christians pray every morning to thank God for his love.
records.zomi: Christian tampi in a itna adingin Pasian kiangah lungdam gen dingin zingsang simin thu a ngen uh hi.

records.english: Some theologians compare God's love to the love of a parent who never stops hoping for a child's return.
records.zomi: Pasian thu sin mi khenkhatte in Pasian' itna ta khat a kik ding lamet tawp ngei lo nu leh pa' itna tawh a kikhaikhin uh hi.

records.english: Everyone, please take a candle as a sign of God's love for this family.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, hih innkuan tunga Pasian' itna lahna-in khawimeivaak khat ciat la un.

records.english: Our pastor visited the prisoners and told them that God had not forgotten them.
records.zomi: I pastor in thongkiate a veh a, Pasian in a mangngilh kei hi, ci-in a hilh hi.

records.english: The pastor used a simple drawing of an open door to explain God's welcome.
records.zomi: Pasian' muakna gen siang dingin pastor in kongkhak kihong lim baih khat a zang hi.

records.english: Having been forgiven by his brother, the young man said he finally understood what mercy meant.
records.zomi: A sanggam pasal in a maisak khit ciangin khangno pasal in hehpihna bang a cih nopna hiam a tawp-in ka thei hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Our youth group visits the hospital every month to show God's love to the patients.
records.zomi: Natnate tungah Pasian' itna lak dingin i khangno pawl in kha simin zato a veh hi.

records.english: Children, today we're going to learn a story about God's love from the Gospel of Luke.
records.zomi: Naupangte, tuni-in Luka' Lungdamna Thu pan Pasian' itna tangthu khat i sin ding hi.

records.english: Whoever comes to the church hall tonight will be given a hot meal and a warm welcome.
records.zomi: Tuni zanin pawlpi inn ah a hong peuhpeuh an sa leh lungsim lum taka muakna a ngah ding uh hi.

records.english: Who first told you about God's love?
records.zomi: Pasian' itna thu kua in nang hong gen masa hiam?

records.english: If God is love, as the First Letter of John says, then love should shape how believers treat others.
records.zomi: Johan' Lai Masa in a gen bangin Pasian pen itna a hih leh um mite in midangte a kizat dan itna in a bawl ding hi.

records.english: What does it mean that God is merciful?
records.zomi: Pasian hehpihna nei hi, cih in bang a cih nopna ahi hiam?

records.english: Christians understand it to mean that God forgives people and does not treat them as harshly as their wrongs deserve.
records.zomi: Pasian in mite a maisak a, a khialhna uh tawh a kilawm bangin a khauh lua-in a hih kei hi, cih ahi hi, ci-in Christiante in a thei uh hi.

records.english: Did the pastor speak about forgiveness again this Sunday?
records.zomi: Hih Nipini-in pastor in maisakna thu a gen kik hiam?

records.english: Love your neighbor, Jesus said, as you love yourself.
records.zomi: Nangmah na kiit bangin na inn veng it in, ci-in Jesu in a ci hi.

records.english: When my friend was ill, the whole church prayed for her every evening.
records.zomi: Ka lawm a dam loh ciangin pawlpi bup in nitak simin amah adingin thu a ngen uh hi.

records.english: We pray together as a family every Sunday evening.
records.zomi: Nipini nitak simin innkuan-in khawm-in thu i ngen hi.

records.english: The more she reflected on God's mercy, the more patient she became with her own children.
records.zomi: Pasian' hehpihna a ngaihsun semsem ciangin a tate tungah a thuakzawh semsem hi.

records.english: I do want my children to know that they are loved, whatever happens.
records.zomi: Bang a piang zongin kiit uh hi, cih ka tate in a theih ding uh ka deih mahmah hi.

records.english: What would it look like for our town to show mercy to people who have made mistakes?
records.zomi: I khuapi in khialhna a bawl mite tungah hehpihna a lak leh bangci-in a om ding hiam?

records.english: Since the vegetable stalls close before I finish work, I've started growing tomatoes and herbs on my balcony.
records.zomi: Ka nasep ka zawh ma-in anteh zuakna a kikhak ahih manin ka balcony tungah tomato leh anteh namtui ka suan kipan hi.

records.english: The price of cooking oil went up so quickly that we started buying it in large tins.
records.zomi: An huan sathau man a khang lua ahih manin thih bawm lian tawh i lei kipan hi.

records.english: Our nearest shop closed down, and now the nearest one is a long walk away.
records.zomi: I kiang pen dawr a kikhak a, tu-in a kiang pen pen kalsuan gamla ahi hi.

records.english: A neighbor with a car takes three of us to the big market every Friday.
records.zomi: Mawtaw nei inn veng khat in Laithai ni simin ei mi thum zuakna mun lian ah hong paipih hi.

records.english: The fish I bought yesterday was already going bad.
records.zomi: Zanni-a ka lei nga a sia kipan khin hi.

records.english: I took it back, and the seller replaced it with a fresh one.
records.zomi: Ka tawi kik a, a zuakpa in a thak khat tawh a lai sak hi.

records.english: Tell the seller you'll buy three kilos if she lowers the price a little.
records.zomi: Man tawmno a niamsak leh kilo thum ka lei ding hi, ci-in a zuak numei hilh in.

records.english: My son always made me buy sweets at the checkout.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in sum piakna mun ah an lim lei dingin hong ngen den hi.

records.english: Now I shop while he's at school, and the arguments have stopped.
records.zomi: Tu-in sang ah a om laitakin van ka lei a, kinialnate a tawp hi.

records.english: Not until I started cooking for myself did I realize how expensive meat had become.
records.zomi: Keimah adingin an ka huan kipat ciang bek sa man bangzah a sang hiam ka thei hi.

records.english: Is it worth buying the large sack of flour if we only bake once a month?
records.zomi: Kha khat ah khatvei bek i em leh buh-mal ip lian lei a manphat hiam?

records.english: The more carefully you plan your meals, the less food you end up throwing away.
records.zomi: Na an gelna pilvang takin na gel semsem ciangin an na paai tawm semsem hi.

records.english: What I find hardest is shopping with three tired children at the end of the day.
records.zomi: Ka haksa sak pen pen ni tawp ciangin naupang tawl thum tawh van lei ahi hi.

records.english: Why is the shop always out of bread by noon?
records.zomi: Bang hangin sun ciangin dawr ah moh a bei tawntung hiam?

records.english: Which shop near here sells fresh tofu?
records.zomi: Hih kiang-a koi dawr in be-tui thak a zuak hiam?

records.english: The supermarket's card machine stopped working while I was at the till.
records.zomi: Sum piakna mun ah ka om laitakin supermarket' card set a sem nawn kei hi.

records.english: The cashier kept my basket aside while I went to the cash machine across the road.
records.zomi: Lampi gal lam-a sum lakna set ah ka pai laitakin sum lata in ka bawm a kem sak hi.

records.english: Did you check that the eggs weren't broken before you paid?
records.zomi: Na piak ma-in aktuite a kek kei hiam na en hiam?

records.english: Shopping without a list is like fishing without bait, because you rarely bring home what you wanted.
records.zomi: List om lo-in van lei pen ngadawh om lo-in nga man bang ahi a, na deih na tawi ngei tawm hi.

records.english: If prices keep rising, it may help to share bulk purchases with another family.
records.zomi: Man a khang den leh innkuan dang khat tawh van tam lei kihawm in a huh kha ding hi.

records.english: Which stall sells the cheapest onions?
records.zomi: Koi zuakna mun in lothaang a neem pen a zuak hiam?

records.english: The delivery van broke down, so the shop had no fresh vegetables that morning.
records.zomi: Van puakna mawtaw a sia ahih manin tua zingsangin dawr in anteh thak a nei kei hi.

records.english: The shopkeeper said, "Sorry, we've run out of flour until Thursday."
records.zomi: Dawr neipa in, “Hong maisak in, Laizing ni dong buh-mal a bei hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: We borrowed a cup from the neighbor and made the bread anyway.
records.zomi: Inn veng pan haai khat i ngetsak a, tua mah in moh i bawl hi.

records.english: However tight our budget is, my mother always buys a little fruit for the children.
records.zomi: I sum bangzah a tawm zongin ka nu in naupangte adingin theigah tawmno a lei tawntung hi.

records.english: Who forgot to buy the milk?
records.zomi: Nawi lei kua in a mangngilh hiam?

records.english: The rice we bought was full of small stones.
records.zomi: I lei buh suang neute tawh a dim hi.

records.english: We spread it on a tray and picked them out by hand before cooking it.
records.zomi: Kuang lian tungah i zal a, i huan ma-in khut tawh i teel khia hi.

records.english: Is it all right to ask the shopkeeper to keep my bag while I fetch more money?
records.zomi: Sum behlap ka la laitakin dawr neipa ka ip kem sak dingin ngen a hoih hiam?

records.english: The cashier told me, "You've been charged twice for the bananas," and gave me the money back.
records.zomi: Sum lata in, “Nahtang man nihvei kilak hi,” hong ci a, sum hong pia kik hi.

records.english: Had I checked the bags before leaving, I would have noticed that the yogurt was missing.
records.zomi: Ka pai ma-in ip te ka en le, yogurt a om kei hi, cih ka thei ding hi.

records.english: Everyone, please hold on to your shopping bags while we cross the busy road.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, mawtaw tam lampi i kan laitakin na van ip uh len cip un.

records.english: Shall I bring the trolley back to the entrance?
records.zomi: Trolley lutna ah ka tawi kik ding hiam?

records.english: How do you stop the grocery bill from growing every month?
records.zomi: An man kha simin a khan lo nadingin bangci-in na kham hiam?

records.english: Plan your meals before you go, and buy vegetables that are in season.
records.zomi: Na pai ma-in na an gel inla, a hun-a anteh lei in.

records.english: The handle of my basket broke, and the potatoes tumbled into the gutter.
records.zomi: Ka bawm' len na a kek a, alute lampi gei tui luanna ah a liim uh hi.

records.english: A boy on a bicycle helped me pick them up, and I gave him a coin for his trouble.
records.zomi: Siiksakol tuang naupang pasal khat in hong la sak a, a buaipih man dangka khat ka pia hi.

records.english: I never have time to shop after work.
records.zomi: Nasep khit ciangin van lei hun ka nei ngei kei hi.

records.english: A farmer now delivers a box of vegetables to our door every Saturday.
records.zomi: Tu-in lo nei khat in Kiginni simin i kongkhak dong anteh bawm khat a puak hi.

records.english: Would you mind grabbing a bag of rice from the corner shop?
records.zomi: Lampi kiheina-a dawr pan buh ip khat na la sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: What would you buy if you had only ten dollars for the whole week?
records.zomi: Kal bup adingin dollar sawm bek na neih leh bang na lei ding hiam?

records.english: My roommate and I kept buying the same things twice.
records.zomi: Ka khan kihawm lawm leh kei van kibang nihvei i lei den hi.

records.english: We started a shared shopping list on our phones, and we haven't wasted money since.
records.zomi: I phone tungah kihawm van lei list khat i kipatsak a, tua pan sum i paai nawn kei hi.

records.english: My grandson made me write my shopping list in large letters so that I could read it without glasses.
records.zomi: Mitlimlang om lo-in ka sim theih nadingin ka tu in ka van lei list laimal lian tawh hong gelhsak hi.

records.english: Could the shop deliver groceries to older people who can't carry heavy bags?
records.zomi: Ip gik pua zo lo upate adingin dawr in an a puak sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Please don't squeeze the tomatoes, or the seller will get annoyed.
records.zomi: Tomatote nawi kei in, a hi kei leh a zuakpa a heh ding hi.

records.english: Having been sold rotten mangoes twice, my aunt now always cuts one open before paying.
records.zomi: Haigah sia nihvei a kizuak khit ciangin ka ni in a piak ma-in khat a at tawntung hi.

records.english: How do you carry so many bags on the bus?
records.zomi: Bus tungah ip tam lua bangci-in na pua hiam?

records.english: We always came home from the market without half the things we needed.
records.zomi: Zuakna mun pan i kisap a khen khat om lo-in i hong ciah tawntung hi.

records.english: Now we keep a list on the fridge, and whoever notices something is finished writes it down.
records.zomi: Tu-in khal bawm tungah list khat i kem a, bangmah a bei hi, a mu peuhpeuh in a gelh hi.

records.english: The bread was squashed under the heavy bag of potatoes.
records.zomi: Moh alu ip gik nuai ah a kinawi hi.

records.english: Next time, put the soft things on top, not at the bottom.
records.zomi: A zom ciangin a nem vante a nuai lam ah hi lo-in a tung lam ah koih in.

records.english: Customers aren't allowed to bring their own bags into the supermarket here, so they leave them at the door.
records.zomi: Hih mun-a leite in supermarket sung ah amau ip a tawi thei kei uh ahih manin kongkhak ah a nusia uh hi.

records.english: Whoever finishes the last of the rice should add it to the list.
records.zomi: Buh a nunung pen a zang peuhpeuh in list ah a behlap ding hi.

records.english: Rather than going to the market every day, we now shop once a week with a careful plan.
records.zomi: Ni simin zuakna mun ah pai sangin tu-in gelna pilvang tawh kal khat ah khatvei van i lei hi.

records.english: Why don't we grow our own herbs instead of buying them every week?
records.zomi: Bang hangin kal simin lei sangin eimah in anteh namtuite i suan kei ding hiam?

records.english: The market was flooded after the heavy rain, and most stalls were closed.
records.zomi: Guah hat khit ciangin zuakna mun tui in a liam a, zuakna mun tamzaw a kikhak hi.

records.english: We bought rice and beans at the small shop on the hill instead.
records.zomi: Tua sangin mual tung-a dawr neu ah buh leh be i lei hi.

records.english: Although supermarkets can be cheaper, many people in our town still prefer to buy from sellers they know.
records.zomi: Supermarket te a neem zaw thei hangin i khuapi-a mi tampi in a theih zuakte pan lei a deih zaw lai uh hi.

records.english: The eggs were cracked when I got them home, so I made an omelet for dinner.
records.zomi: Inn ah ka tun ciangin aktuite a kek khin ahih manin nitak an adingin aktui kikang ka bawl hi.

records.english: Could you find out what the spare part costs before you order it?
records.zomi: Na ngen ma-in a vanzat behlap man bangzah hiam na thei sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: At the government shop in our town, bargaining is not allowed, so the prices are the same for everyone.
records.zomi: I khuapi-a kumpi dawr ah man kikum kiphal lo ahih manin mi khempeuh adingin man a kibang hi.

records.english: How do I know if a price is fair at the market?
records.zomi: Zuakna mun ah man khat a dik hiam bangci-in ka thei ding hiam?

records.english: Ask at two or three stalls before you buy anything.
records.zomi: Bangmah na lei ma-in zuakna mun nih thum ah dong in.

records.english: The electrician quoted a price over the phone and then charged much more.
records.zomi: Electrician in phone tungah man khat a gen a, tua ciangin a tam zaw mahmah a la hi.

records.english: Now I always ask for a written quote before anyone starts work in the house.
records.zomi: Tu-in inn sung ah kuamah in nasep a kipat ma-in kigelh man ka ngen tawntung hi.

records.english: The more often you shop at the same stall, the more likely the seller is to give you a good price.
records.zomi: Zuakna mun kibang ah na lei den semsem ciangin a zuakpa in man hoih hong pia ding a om semsem hi.

records.english: Shall I ask the seller whether he'll take less for two?
records.zomi: Nih na lei leh a tawm zaw a sang ding hiam a zuakpa ka dong ding hiam?

records.english: I was too shy to ask how much the dress cost.
records.zomi: Puan man bangzah ahi hiam dong dingin ka zak lua hi.

records.english: My friend asked for me, and it was cheaper than I expected.
records.zomi: Ka lawm in hong dong sak a, ka lamen sangin a neem zaw hi.

records.english: The seller told me one price and then asked for more when I tried to pay.
records.zomi: A zuakpa in man khat hong gen a, ka piak tum ciangin a tam zaw a ngen hi.

records.english: Now I ask him to write the price on paper before I agree to buy anything.
records.zomi: Tu-in ka lei dingin ka lungkim ma-in laipek tungah man a gelh dingin ka ngen hi.

records.english: Had I asked the price before the haircut, I wouldn't have been so shocked by the bill.
records.zomi: Sam at ma-in a man ka dong le, bill in hong lamdangsak mahmah kei ding hi.

records.english: In our market, sellers expect a little bargaining, but not for bread or rice.
records.zomi: I zuakna mun ah zuakte in man kikum tawmno a lamen uh hi, ahi zongin moh leh buh adingin hi lo hi.

records.english: Can you tell me how much this costs without the box?
records.zomi: Bawm om lo-in hih man bangzah ahi hiam hong gen thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: I didn't buy the shoes because the price had been scratched off the label.
records.zomi: Min tung pan man a kikhuai khin ahih manin khedap ka lei kei hi.

records.english: The shopkeeper says, "Ask me the price, and I'll tell you the truth."
records.zomi: Dawr neipa in, “Man hong dong in, a tak kong gen ding hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: The prices in the tourist area were so high that we ate at the market instead.
records.zomi: Khualzin mite mun-a man a sang lua ahih manin tua sangin zuakna mun ah an i ne hi.

records.english: The taxi driver said, "It's double after midnight," so we walked home instead.
records.zomi: Taxi mawngpa in, “Zanlai zawh ciangin nihvei ahi hi,” a ci ahih manin inn dong i kalsuan hi.

records.english: My sister was charged twice the normal price because the seller thought she was a tourist.
records.zomi: A zuakpa in khualzin mi in a ngaihsut manin ka sanggam nu man pangai nihvei a kipia hi.

records.english: The next day, she went back with a local friend, and the price was much lower.
records.zomi: A zing ni-in hih mun-a lawm khat tawh a kik a, a man a niam zaw mahmah hi.

records.english: Where can I find the price of a train ticket to the capital?
records.zomi: Khuapi lian lam meileng ticket man koi ah ka mu thei ding hiam?

records.english: When will the new prices be announced?
records.zomi: Bang ciangin man thakte kigen ding hiam?

records.english: What I find hardest is asking about prices without sounding as if I can't afford anything.
records.zomi: Ka haksa sak pen pen bangmah ka lei zo lo bangin ging lo-in man dong ahi hi.

records.english: The bus fare was raised without any notice.
records.zomi: Bus man gen lo-in a kikhangsak hi.

records.english: Several passengers complained, and the company put up a sign explaining the change.
records.zomi: Khualzin tampi in a phun uh a, company in kilaihna gen siangna lai khat a khai hi.

records.english: I really do want to buy the bicycle, but I need to know the final price first.
records.zomi: Siiksakol lei ka deih mahmah hi, ahi zongin a man nunung a masa-in ka thei ding a kisam hi.

records.english: If a seller refuses to tell you the price, it may be wise to shop somewhere else.
records.zomi: Zuak khat in a man gen a nial leh mun dang ah lei a pil zaw kha ding hi.

records.english: Asking a price is like knocking on a door, because the answer tells you whether to go in.
records.zomi: Man dot pen kongkhak kiu bang ahi a, a dawnna in na lut ding hiam hong hilh hi.

records.english: What would you do if a seller refused to show you the price list?
records.zomi: Zuak khat in man list etsak a nial leh bang na hih ding hiam?

records.english: The old man at the stall never says a price; he just smiles and waits for your offer.
records.zomi: Zuakna mun-a pasal upa in man a gen ngei kei hi; a nui bek a, na piak ding a ngak hi.

records.english: Did you ask whether the price includes fitting the new tires?
records.zomi: Tire thak koih man zong a kihel hiam na dong hiam?

records.english: Who decided that the price of school uniforms should go up again?
records.zomi: Sang puan man a khang kik ding hi, ci-in kua in a khensat hiam?

records.english: Is it rude to ask a colleague what she earns?
records.zomi: Nasem lawm khat a nasep man bangzah a ngah hiam dot pen zahtakna om lo ahi hiam?

records.english: Not until we compared the bills did we realize that the clinic charged us more than our neighbors.
records.zomi: Bill te i kikhaikhin ciang bek siavuan inn in i inn vengte sangin a tam zaw hong la hi, cih i thei hi.

records.english: Which of these phones is the cheapest?
records.zomi: Hih phonete lak ah koi a man neu pen hiam?

records.english: The website showed one price, but the shop wanted much more.
records.zomi: Website in man khat a lak a, ahi zongin dawr in a tam zaw mahmah a ngen hi.

records.english: I showed the shopkeeper the page on my phone, and he agreed to match it.
records.zomi: Ka phone tung-a page dawr neipa ka etsak a, tua man tawh a kibat dingin a lungkim hi.

records.english: Please don't touch the fruit unless you're going to buy it.
records.zomi: Na lei ding hi kei leh theigah khoih kei in.

records.english: The mechanic wouldn't tell me the cost until he had taken the engine apart.
records.zomi: Set bawlpa in set a khiat ma-in a man hong gen nuam kei hi.

records.english: I asked him to call me before doing any work that cost more than fifty dollars.
records.zomi: Dollar sawmnga sangin a man tam zaw nasep khatpeuh a sep ma-in hong sam dingin ka ngen hi.

records.english: The scale at the stall looked wrong, so I asked the seller to weigh the beans again.
records.zomi: Zuakna mun-a gikna khaina a dik lo bang ahih manin a zuakpa kiangah be kik-in khai dingin ka ngen hi.

records.english: The second time they were half a kilo lighter, and he lowered the price.
records.zomi: Nihveina ciangin kilo khen khat a zaang zaw a, a man a niamsak hi.

records.english: Is the price the same if I pay by card?
records.zomi: Card tawh ka piak leh man a kibang hiam?

records.english: Having been overcharged on her first visit, my cousin now checks every price before she orders.
records.zomi: A veh masa pen-in man tam lua a kilak khit ciangin ka sanggam in tu-in a ngen ma-in man khempeuh a en hi.

records.english: Although asking about prices can feel awkward, most sellers prefer customers who are clear about what they can spend.
records.zomi: Man dot a zahhuai thei hangin zuak tamzaw in bangzah a zang thei uh hiam a kician lei mite a deih zaw uh hi.

records.english: The price list fell off the wall in the wind, and nobody knew what anything cost.
records.zomi: Huih in man list bang pan a kiatsak a, kuamah in bangmah man a thei kei uh hi.

records.english: The owner wrote a new one on a board with chalk.
records.zomi: A neipa in bang tungah chalk tawh a thak khat a gelh hi.

records.english: None of the shirts in the shop had price tags.
records.zomi: Dawr sung-a angki khatpeuh man min a nei kei hi.

records.english: I asked the assistant to check them all, and she wrote the prices on a list for me.
records.zomi: A khempeuh en dingin dawr nasem ka ngen a, list khat tungah man hong gelh sak hi.

records.english: What would you charge to sharpen these kitchen knives?
records.zomi: Hih an huanna namsaute hiamsak man bangzah na la ding hiam?

records.english: Whoever does the shopping this week should keep the receipts so that we can compare prices.
records.zomi: Hih kal sungin van a lei peuhpeuh in man i kikhaikhin theih nadingin laimalte a kem ding hi.

records.english: My grandson always asks the price in a very quiet voice, as if it were a secret.
records.zomi: Ka tu in man thuguk bangin dai mahmah takin a dong tawntung hi.

records.english: Why do prices go up before every festival?
records.zomi: Bang hangin pawi khempeuh ma-in man a khang hiam?

records.english: How long will this special price last?
records.zomi: Hih man tuam bangzah sung a om ding hiam?

records.english: The price tag was hidden under a sticker, so I asked the assistant to remove it.
records.zomi: Man min sticker nuai ah a bu ahih manin dawr nasem a hon dingin ka ngen hi.

records.english: Why don't they put prices on anything in this shop?
records.zomi: Bang hangin hih dawr ah bangmah tungah man a koih kei uh hiam?

records.english: Everyone, ask the price before you order, because this restaurant has no menu.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, hih anneekna inn in an list a nei kei ahih manin na ngen ma-un man dong un.

records.english: Could the market committee put up a board with fair prices for everyday goods?
records.zomi: Zuakna mun committee in ni sim van adingin man dik bang khat tungah a khai thei ding hiam?

records.english: Rather than guessing the price, it's always better to ask politely before you choose.
records.zomi: Man ngaihsun sangin na teel ma-in zahtak taka dot a hoih zaw tawntung hi.

records.english: The receipt had faded so much that the shop couldn't read the date.
records.zomi: Laimal a mang lua ahih manin dawr in ni a sim thei kei hi.

records.english: Now I take a photo of every receipt before I put it in my wallet.
records.zomi: Tu-in ka sum ip sung ka koih ma-in laimal khempeuh lim ka la hi.

records.english: How do you split the bill fairly when some people only had soup?
records.zomi: Mi khenkhatte in an tui bek a nek uh laitakin bill dik takin bangci-in na khen uh hiam?

records.english: Everyone pays for what they ordered, and we share the tip equally.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh in a ngen man a pia uh a, letsong sum kibang-in i hawm hi.

records.english: Instead of coins, the shop gave me sweets as change, and I didn't want them.
records.zomi: Dangka sangin dawr in sum kilaih in an lim hong pia a, ka deih kei hi.

records.english: I asked politely for the coins, and the manager found some in the back office.
records.zomi: Zahtak takin dangka ka ngen a, manager in nung lam office ah khenkhat a mu hi.

records.english: Can I pay you back next week, since I've left my wallet at home?
records.zomi: Ka sum ip inn ah ka nusia ahih manin kal zom ciangin kong pia kik thei ding hiam?

records.english: Would you mind lending me some coins for the parking machine?
records.zomi: Mawtaw koihna set adingin dangka tawmno hong ngetsak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Who left these coins on the counter?
records.zomi: Sum piakna dawhkan tungah hih dangkate kua in a nusia hiam?

records.english: What would you do if the cashier refused to give you a receipt?
records.zomi: Sum lata in laimal pia a nial leh bang na hih ding hiam?

records.english: I lost my purse in the taxi, so a colleague paid my fare.
records.zomi: Taxi sung ah ka sum ip ka mansuah ahih manin nasem lawm khat in ka man hong pia sak hi.

records.english: Having lived abroad for years, my uncle still converts every price into his old currency before paying.
records.zomi: Gamdang ah kum tampi a om khit ciangin ka pa neu in a piak ma-in man khempeuh a sum lui ah a lai lai hi.

records.english: My grandson counted his pocket money so slowly that a line formed behind him.
records.zomi: Ka tu in a zat ding sum zawl lua takin a sim ahih manin a nung ah mite a kikhai uh hi.

records.english: The shopkeeper smiled and told everyone to wait, because the boy was learning.
records.zomi: Dawr neipa a nui a, naupang pasal a kisin ahih manin mi khempeuh ngak dingin a hilh hi.

records.english: I was a dollar short when the shopkeeper added up my basket.
records.zomi: Dawr neipa in ka bawm man a kaikhawm ciangin dollar khat ka kiam hi.

records.english: I put back the biscuits, and he kindly let me keep the bread.
records.zomi: Biscuit te ka koih kik a, hehpih takin moh hong kem sak hi.

records.english: If you're unsure whether the change is right, it's better to ask straight away than later.
records.zomi: Sum kilaih a dik hiam na kician kei leh a nung ciangin sangin tu-in dot pah a hoih zaw hi.

records.english: My wife keeps a small purse of coins in the car for parking and tolls.
records.zomi: Ka zi in mawtaw koihna leh lampi man adingin mawtaw sung ah dangka ip neu khat a kem hi.

records.english: Although paying by card is convenient, many older people in our town still prefer cash.
records.zomi: Card tawh piak a baih hangin i khuapi-a upa tampi in sum taktak a deih zaw lai uh hi.

records.english: Rather than arguing about who owes what, my friends and I now use an app that keeps track.
records.zomi: Kua in bangzah a pia ding hiam kinial sangin tu-in ka lawmte leh kei a sim app khat i zang hi.

records.english: The payment on my phone failed three times at the till.
records.zomi: Sum piakna mun ah ka phone tung-a piakna thumvei a puk hi.

records.english: The cashier let me pay the rest in cash, and I sorted out the app at home.
records.zomi: Sum lata in a dang sum taktak tawh pia dingin hong phal a, inn ah app ka bawl siang hi.

records.english: Not until I got home did I notice that the cashier had given me far too much change.
records.zomi: Inn ka tun ciang bek sum lata in sum kilaih tam lua hong pia hi, cih ka thei hi.

records.english: Whoever collected the money for the gift should keep a list of who has paid.
records.zomi: Letsong adingin sum a kaikhawm peuhpeuh in kua in a pia khin hiam list khat a kem ding hi.

records.english: Kids, give the driver your coins one at a time so that he can count them.
records.zomi: Naupangte, mawngpa in a sim theih nadingin na dangka uh khat khit khat-in pia un.

records.english: How do you pay at a stall that only accepts mobile money?
records.zomi: Phone sum bek a sang zuakna mun khat ah bangci-in na pia hiam?

records.english: My son paid for his lunch with a torn note, and the café refused it.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in sum kek tawh a sun an man a pia a, cafe in a sang nuam kei hi.

records.english: We took the note to the bank, where it was exchanged for a new one.
records.zomi: Sum bank ah i tawi a, tua ah a thak khat tawh kilai hi.

records.english: Everyone, please pay for your own drinks at the bar before we sit down.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, i tut ma-in dawn dingte man nangma' man na pia un.

records.english: The more people pay by phone, the fewer coins small shops seem to keep.
records.zomi: Mite phone tawh a pia tam semsem ciangin dawr neute in dangka a kem tawm semsem bang uh hi.

records.english: Is it possible to pay the rent by bank transfer?
records.zomi: Inn man bank pan khak tawh ka pia thei ding hiam?

records.english: The cashier said, "I'm sorry, I can't change a note this big so early in the morning."
records.zomi: Sum lata in, “Hong maisak in, zingsang tung mahmah ah hih bang sum lian ka khen thei kei hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: Had I counted the change before leaving, I wouldn't have walked home ten dollars short.
records.zomi: Ka pai ma-in sum kilaih ka sim le, dollar sawm kiam-in inn ah ka kalsuan kei ding hi.

records.english: The market seller had no change, so she ran to the next stall to get some.
records.zomi: Zuakna mun-a zuak numei in sum kilaih a nei kei ahih manin a kiang zuakna mun ah la dingin a tai hi.

records.english: When should I pay the plumber, before or after the work?
records.zomi: Tui khuam bawlpa nasep ma-in ka pia ding hiam, a khit ciangin hiam?

records.english: In some markets here, sellers round prices down for regular customers.
records.zomi: Hih mun-a zuakna mun khenkhatte ah zuakte in lei den mite adingin man a niamsak uh hi.

records.english: Did the shop give you a receipt for the washing machine?
records.zomi: Puan silna set adingin dawr in laimal hong pia hiam?

records.english: Counting change is like reading a map, because a moment's care saves you a long walk back.
records.zomi: Sum kilaih sim pen map sim bang ahi a, hun tawmno pilvangna in lampi sau kik pan hong hun hi.

records.english: Why does the café only accept cash on weekends?
records.zomi: Bang hangin cafe in kal tawp ciangin sum taktak bek a sang hiam?

records.english: Shall I pay now, or at the end of the meal?
records.zomi: Tu-in ka pia ding hiam, an nek tawp ciangin hiam?

records.english: The fare had gone up, but nobody had told the passengers.
records.zomi: Man a khang hi, ahi zongin kuamah in khualzinte a hilh kei uh hi.

records.english: Why don't we pay for the taxi together and split it later?
records.zomi: Bang hangin taxi man khawm-in i pia a, a nung ciangin i khen kei ding hiam?

records.english: The money I sent to my sister arrived in the wrong account.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu kiangah ka khak sum account dik lo ah a tung hi.

records.english: The bank traced it, and it reached her account three days later.
records.zomi: Bank in a zui a, ni thum khit ciangin a account ah a tung hi.

records.english: The cash machine kept my card after I typed the wrong number twice.
records.zomi: Number dik lo nihvei ka nek khit ciangin sum lakna set in ka card a kem hi.

records.english: The bank sent me a new card within a week.
records.zomi: Kal khat sungin bank in card thak hong khak hi.

records.english: The waiter brought the bill for the wrong table.
records.zomi: An zuakpa in dawhkan dik lo' bill a tawi hi.

records.english: We pointed it out, and he came back with ours and an apology.
records.zomi: I lak a, ei' tawh leh maisak ngetna tawh a hong kik hi.

records.english: The shop charged me for six eggs, but there were only five in the box.
records.zomi: Dawr in aktui guk man hong la a, ahi zongin bawm sung ah nga bek a om hi.

records.english: The ice-cream seller gave the little girl her change in a paper twist so that she wouldn't drop it.
records.zomi: Ice cream zuakpa in numei naupang in a khiat lo nadingin a sum kilaih lai tawh a tuam sak hi.

records.english: Where can I change foreign money in this town?
records.zomi: Hih khuapi ah gamdang sum koi ah ka lai thei ding hiam?

records.english: What I find hardest is working out the change in my head when the queue is long.
records.zomi: Ka haksa sak pen pen mi a kikhai sau laitakin ka lungsim sungah sum kilaih ngaihsut ahi hi.

records.english: I really do want to pay you back today, but the bank is closed until Monday.
records.zomi: Tuni-in kong pia kik ka deih mahmah hi, ahi zongin Pizing ni dong bank a kikhak hi.

records.english: Could the school accept payment for the trip in two parts, since it's so expensive?
records.zomi: Khualzinna a man tam lua ahih manin sang in a man khen nih-in a sang thei ding hiam?

records.english: The ticket machine swallowed my coins and gave me nothing.
records.zomi: Ticket set in ka dangkate a val a, bangmah hong pia kei hi.

records.english: I pressed the help button, and a guard opened the gate for me.
records.zomi: Huhna button ka nek a, kongpi kemtu khat in kongpi hong hon sak hi.

records.english: When the shop's power failed, the cashier wrote every sale in a notebook and gave handwritten receipts.
records.zomi: Dawr' meivak a mit ciangin sum lata in zuak khempeuh laibu neu khat ah a gelh a, khut tawh gelh laimal a pia hi.

records.english: Which of you still owes money for the pizza?
records.zomi: Note lak ah kua in pizza man a pia nai kei hiam?

records.english: The electricity company charged us for our neighbor's flat by mistake.
records.zomi: Meivak company in khialh-in i inn veng' inn man hong la hi.

records.english: The company returned the extra money to my account after I phoned them.
records.zomi: Phone ka sam khit ciangin company in sum behlap ka account ah a pia kik hi.

records.english: The screen of the new laptop flickered, so I took it back the next morning.
records.zomi: Laptop thak' screen a ling ahih manin a zing zingsangin ka tawi kik hi.

records.english: Would you mind taking these broken headphones back to the shop for me?
records.zomi: Hih headphone sia te dawr ah hong tawi kik sak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: The book I bought had twenty pages missing in the middle.
records.zomi: Ka lei laibu kimlai ah laimai sawmnih a om kei hi.

records.english: The bookseller apologized and ordered a new copy for me.
records.zomi: Laibu zuakpa in maisak a ngen a, ka adingin a thak khat a ngen sak hi.

records.english: Why are so many people returning the new phones this week?
records.zomi: Bang hangin hih kal sungin mi tampi in phone thakte a tawi kik uh hiam?

records.english: How long do I have to return a dress that doesn't fit?
records.zomi: A kituak lo puan khat tawi kik dingin hun bangzah ka nei hiam?

records.english: Who put the receipt in the washing machine?
records.zomi: Puan silna set sung ah laimal kua in a koih hiam?

records.english: Not until I opened the parcel at home did I realize that the shop had sent the wrong size.
records.zomi: Inn ah van bawm ka hon ciang bek dawr in a lian dik lo a khak hi, cih ka thei hi.

records.english: Shall I keep the box in case we need to send it back?
records.zomi: A khak kik ding i kisap kha leh bawm ka kem ding hiam?

records.english: If a shop refuses a fair return, it may help to ask to speak to the manager.
records.zomi: Dawr khat in tawi kikna dik a nial leh manager tawh kiho dingin ngen in a huh kha ding hi.

records.english: The more expensive the item, the more carefully you should keep the receipt and the box.
records.zomi: Van khat a man tam semsem ciangin a laimal leh a bawm pilvang zaw-in na kem ding hi.

records.english: The phone case I ordered online didn't fit my phone.
records.zomi: Online-a ka ngen phone case in ka phone a kituak kei hi.

records.english: I sent the case back in its original envelope, and the refund arrived two days later.
records.zomi: A lai ip masa sung ah ka khak kik a, ni nih khit ciangin sum pia kik a tung hi.

records.english: Having returned three pairs of trousers that didn't fit, my brother now insists on trying everything on in the shop.
records.zomi: A kituak lo kekawi thum a tawi kik khit ciangin ka sanggam pasal in tu-in dawr sung ah khempeuh a silh-in a en hi.

records.english: Although returning things can be a nuisance, most shops in our town handle it politely.
records.zomi: Van tawi kik a buaihuai thei hangin i khuapi-a dawr tamzaw in zahtak takin a khoih uh hi.

records.english: I really do want to return this jacket, but I've lost the receipt.
records.zomi: Hih kawt tawi kik ka deih mahmah hi, ahi zongin laimal ka mansuah hi.

records.english: Luckily, I'd paid by card, and the shop found the sale on its computer.
records.zomi: Lungdamhuai takin card tawh ka pia a, dawr in a computer tungah zuakna a mu hi.

records.english: The new shoes squeaked so loudly that everyone in the office turned round.
records.zomi: Khedap thakte ging sang lua takin a ging ahih manin office sung-a mi khempeuh a kihei uh hi.

records.english: They replaced them without asking any questions.
records.zomi: Dotna khatpeuh om lo-in a lai sak uh hi.

records.english: Did they give you cash or store credit?
records.zomi: Sum hong pia uh hiam, dawr-a zat ding man hiam?

records.english: What would you do if a shop refused to accept a faulty kettle?
records.zomi: Dawr khat in tui suangna sia khat a sang nuam kei leh bang na hih ding hiam?

records.english: Can I take back a gift if I don't know where it was bought?
records.zomi: Koi ah kilei hiam ka theih loh letsong khat ka tawi kik thei ding hiam?

records.english: My son's new school uniform was two sizes too big.
records.zomi: Ka tapa' sang puan thak a lian lua nih zah hi.

records.english: The shop exchanged it the same day, and they even shortened the trousers for free.
records.zomi: Dawr in tua ni mah-in a lai sak a, man om lo-in kekawi zong a tomsak uh hi.

records.english: Children, if the game is broken, bring it back to me with the box.
records.zomi: Naupangte, kimawlna a sia leh a bawm tawh hong tawi kik un.

records.english: My phone shop has closed down.
records.zomi: Ka phone dawr a kikhak khin hi.

records.english: I contacted the company directly, and they repaired it under guarantee.
records.zomi: Company tawh a tang takin ka kizom a, guarantee nuai ah a bawl siang sak uh hi.

records.english: My grandson was given a sweater he didn't like, but he was too polite to return it.
records.zomi: Ka tu in a deih loh puan vot khat a ngah a, ahi zongin tawi kik dingin a zahtak lua hi.

records.english: Had I checked the box before leaving the shop, I would have noticed that the charger was missing.
records.zomi: Dawr ka nusiat ma-in bawm ka en le, charger a om kei hi, cih ka thei ding hi.

records.english: My store credit expired before I had time to use it.
records.zomi: Ka zat ma-in dawr-a zat ding man hun a bei hi.

records.english: Next time, I'll ask for my money back instead.
records.zomi: A zom ciangin tua sangin ka sum ka ngen kik ding hi.

records.english: The sofa was damaged during delivery, and one leg was broken.
records.zomi: Puak laitakin sofa a sia a, khe khat a kek hi.

records.english: The delivery company collected it and sent a new one the following week.
records.zomi: Van puakna company in a la kik a, a zom kal in a thak khat a khak hi.

records.english: The curtains looked blue in the shop but turned out to be green at home.
records.zomi: Tukvuang puan dawr ah a dum bang a, ahi zongin inn ah a eng hi.

records.english: I brought a photo of the room, and the assistant helped me choose a better color.
records.zomi: Khan lim khat ka tawi a, dawr nasem in rong hoih zaw teel dingin hong huh hi.

records.english: Keeping a receipt is like keeping a key, because without it many doors stay closed.
records.zomi: Laimal kem pen tawh kem bang ahi a, a om kei leh kongkhak tampi a kikhak lai hi.

records.english: Can I return a lamp that I've already used once?
records.zomi: Khatvei ka zat khin meivak khat ka tawi kik thei ding hiam?

records.english: Why don't you exchange the shirt for a larger size?
records.zomi: Bang hangin angki a lian zaw tawh na lai kei hiam?

records.english: Rather than sending the heavy printer back, the company sent a technician to fix it at our office.
records.zomi: Printer gik khak kik sangin company in i office ah bawl siang dingin technician khat a sawl hi.

records.english: The return queue was so long that I nearly gave up.
records.zomi: Tawi kikna mun-a mite kikhaina a sau lua ahih manin ka khah dek hi.

records.english: A manager opened a second counter, and the line moved much faster.
records.zomi: Manager khat in sum piakna mun nihna a hon a, kikhaina a manlang zaw mahmah hi.

records.english: I had the faulty heater collected by the shop and replaced at no cost.
records.zomi: Mei lumna set sia dawr in a la a, man om lo-in a lai sak hi.

records.english: The toy car broke on the first afternoon.
records.zomi: Mawtaw kimawlna nitak lam masa pen-in a sia hi.

records.english: When we took it back, the shopkeeper tested the new one in front of us before wrapping it.
records.zomi: I tawi kik ciangin dawr neipa in a tuam ma-in i mai ah a thak khat a en hi.

records.english: Why did the shop ask for my phone number when I returned the shoes?
records.zomi: Khedap ka tawi kik ciangin bang hangin dawr in ka phone number a ngen hiam?

records.english: The flat-pack table arrived with three screws missing.
records.zomi: Kikhen-a kipuak dawhkan thih khut thum om lo-in a hong tung hi.

records.english: The company posted the screws to us, and my brother put the table together with his own screwdriver.
records.zomi: Company in thih khutte hong khak a, ka sanggam pasal in amah' screwdriver tawh dawhkan a bawl hi.

records.english: My aunt used scissors to cut the tags off before she realized the skirt was too small.
records.zomi: Puan a neu lua hi, cih a theih ma-in ka ni in namtemna tawh a minte a tan hi.

records.english: Could the shop collect the washing machine, since it's too heavy for us to carry?
records.zomi: Eite pua dingin a gik lua ahih manin dawr in puan silna set a la thei ding hiam?

records.english: The mattress was so hard that my back ached every morning.
records.zomi: Mattress a khauh lua ahih manin zingsang simin ka nung a na hi.

records.english: The shop let us exchange it within thirty days, so we chose a softer one.
records.zomi: Ni sawmthum sungin a laih dingin dawr in hong phal a, a nem zaw khat i teel hi.

records.english: Whoever ordered the wrong paint should take it back to the hardware store.
records.zomi: Zeek dik lo a ngen peuhpeuh in thih van dawr ah a tawi kik ding hi.

records.english: Do I get my money back in cash or on my card?
records.zomi: Ka sum sum taktak-in hiam, ka card tungah hiam ka ngah kik ding hiam?

records.english: Where's the nearest place to drop off an online return?
records.zomi: Online-a tawi kik ding nusiat nading mun a kiang pen koi ah a om hiam?

records.english: We were given two identical toasters as wedding presents.
records.zomi: Mopawi letsong-in toaster kibang nih i ngah hi.

records.english: We took one back and chose a set of cooking pots instead.
records.zomi: Khat i tawi kik a, tua sangin an huanna beel set khat i teel hi.

records.english: What I find hardest is returning gifts without hurting the feelings of the person who chose them.
records.zomi: Ka haksa sak pen pen a teel mi' lungsim susia lo-in letsongte tawi kik ahi hi.

records.english: In many shops here, items bought on sale can only be exchanged, not refunded.
records.zomi: Hih mun-a dawr tampi ah man kiam-a lei vante kilai thei bek a, sum pia kik thei lo hi.

records.english: Everyone, please keep your receipts until the end of the trip, in case anything needs to be returned.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, bangmah tawi kik ding a om kha leh khualzinna tawp dong na laimal uh kem un.

records.english: Which counter do I go to for returns?
records.zomi: Tawi kikna adingin koi dawhkan ah ka pai ding hiam?

records.english: When will the results be announced?
records.zomi: Bang ciangin a kipaina kigen ding hiam?

records.english: On Friday morning, on the board outside the office.
records.zomi: Laithai ni zingsangin, office pua-a bang tungah.

records.english: When exactly did you first notice the leak?
records.zomi: Tui a zu na muh masak bang ciang taktak ahi hiam?

records.english: Three days ago, when I saw water dripping from the ceiling light.
records.zomi: Ni thum paisa-in, innkhum nuai-a meivak pan tui a tak ka muh ciangin.

records.english: When asked why he had been late, the boy simply said that his bicycle had broken.
records.zomi: Bang hangin a nun hiam a kidot ciangin naupang pasal in a siiksakol a sia hi, a ci bek hi.

records.english: When do you think you'll be ready to leave?
records.zomi: Bang ciangin pai dingin na kiman ding in na ngaihsun hiam?

records.english: Give me ten more minutes to finish this letter.
records.zomi: Hih lai ka zawh nadingin minit sawm behlap hong pia in.

records.english: When should we leave if we want to avoid the traffic?
records.zomi: Mawtaw tam i pelh nuam leh bang ciangin i pai ding hiam?

records.english: Before seven, or after ten, when the roads are quieter.
records.zomi: Nai sagih ma-in, hiam nai sawm zawh ciangin, lampite a dai zawk hun.

records.english: When I was a child, we walked an hour to school every morning.
records.zomi: Ka neu lai-in zingsang simin sang ah nai khat i kalsuan hi.

records.english: When the rains came, the river rose, and we stayed home for days.
records.zomi: Guah a zuk ciangin gun a liam a, ni tampi inn ah i om hi.

records.english: Please don't call me when I'm driving, because I won't answer.
records.zomi: Mawtaw ka mawng laitakin hong sam kei in, ka dawng kei ding ahih manin.

records.english: When it comes to keeping promises, my brother is the most reliable person I know.
records.zomi: Kiciamna zuih thu ah ka sanggam pasal pen ka theih mi lak ah um huai pen ahi hi.

records.english: I'll never forget when my daughter took her first steps.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in a khe a sut masak hun ka mangngilh ngei kei ding hi.

records.english: When was it that you realized you'd lost your wallet?
records.zomi: Na sum ip na mansuah hi, cih bang ciangin na thei hiam?

records.english: When I tried to pay for lunch, which was rather embarrassing.
records.zomi: Sun an man ka piak tum ciangin, tua pen zahhuai mahmah hi.

records.english: What I'd like to know is when the council plans to repair the road.
records.zomi: Ka theih nuam pen pen council in bang ciangin lampi a bawl siang ding hiam, cih ahi hi.

records.english: Could you let me know when the parcel arrives?
records.zomi: Van bawm a tun ciangin hong gen thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: When is the shop open on holidays?
records.zomi: Nopsakna ni-in dawr bang ciangin a kihong hiam?

records.english: Only in the morning, from eight until noon.
records.zomi: Zingsang bek, nai giat pan sun dong.

records.english: Tell me when you get home, so that I know you're safe.
records.zomi: Na bit ka theih nadingin inn na tun ciangin hong gen in.

records.english: When would be a convenient time for us to visit?
records.zomi: Kong veh ding uh hun kituak bang ciang ahi ding hiam?

records.english: Any evening after six, when the children have finished their homework.
records.zomi: Nai guk zawh nitak peuhpeuh, naupangte in a inn-a sep ding a zawh khit ciangun.

records.english: Do you know when the pharmacy closes on Sundays?
records.zomi: Nipini-in zatui zuakna bang ciangin a kikhak hiam na thei hiam?

records.english: I asked the doctor when I could go back to work, and she said, "Not before Monday."
records.zomi: Bang ciangin nasep ah ka kik thei ding hiam siavuan ka dong a, “Pizing ni ma-in thei lo hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: By the time we realized when the festival actually started, we had missed the opening ceremony.
records.zomi: Pawi bang ciangin a kipan taktak hiam i theih ciangin a kihonna pawi i mansuah khin hi.

records.english: Had I known when the train was leaving, I wouldn't have waited at the station for two hours.
records.zomi: Meileng bang ciangin a pai ding hiam ka theih le, meileng dinna ah nai nih ka ngak kei ding hi.

records.english: When did your grandfather move to the city?
records.zomi: Bang ciangin na pu khuapi ah a tuah hiam?

records.english: After the floods destroyed his fields, when my father was still a baby.
records.zomi: Tuiciim in a lote a susiat khit ciangin, ka pa naungek a hih lai-in.

records.english: How old were you when you started learning the guitar?
records.zomi: Guitar na sin kipat ciangin kum bangzah na hi hiam?

records.english: When I was twelve, after my uncle gave me his old one.
records.zomi: Kum sawm leh nih ka phak ciangin, ka pa neu in amah' lui hong piak khit ciangin.

records.english: Do you remember when the power went off last night?
records.zomi: Zanni zanin meivak a mit hun na phawk hiam?

records.english: Just after nine, while we were watching the news.
records.zomi: Nai kua zawh pah-in, thu thak i en laitakin.

records.english: When are we allowed to open our presents?
records.zomi: Bang ciangin i letsongte i hon thei ding hiam?

records.english: Not until everyone has finished breakfast.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh in zingsang an a zawh ciang bek.

records.english: When did people in your village first get electricity?
records.zomi: Bang ciangin na khua-a mite in meivak a ngah masa uh hiam?

records.english: According to my grandmother, it was when she was about ten, and everyone came out to see the first light.
records.zomi: Ka pi' gen bangin kum sawm bang a phak lai-in ahi a, meivak masa en dingin mi khempeuh a pai khia uh hi.

records.english: When will you finally tell your parents about your new job?
records.zomi: Na nasep thak thu bang ciangin na nu leh na pa na hilh ding hiam?

records.english: When do the children usually go to bed?
records.zomi: Naupangte a tamzaw-in bang ciangin a lum uh hiam?

records.english: At eight on school nights, and a little later on weekends.
records.zomi: Sang ni zan ciangin nai giat ciangin, kal tawp ciangin tawmno nung zaw-in.

records.english: When did you have your car serviced last?
records.zomi: Na mawtaw bang ciangin na en sak nunung hiam?

records.english: About six months ago, at the garage near the market.
records.zomi: Kha guk bang paisa-in, zuakna mun kiang-a set bawlna inn ah.

records.english: Did the teacher say when the exam would be?
records.zomi: Sitna bang ciangin ahi ding hiam saya in a gen hiam?

records.english: She said, "In two weeks, so start revising now."
records.zomi: “Kal nih sungin, tua ahih manin tu-in kisin kik kipan in,” a ci hi.

records.english: When is your sister's wedding?
records.zomi: Na sanggam nu' mopawi bang ciangin ahi hiam?

records.english: On the last Saturday in May, if the rain stays away.
records.zomi: May kha-a Kiginni nunung pen-in, guah a zuk kei leh.

records.english: When will the new bridge be finished?
records.zomi: Lei thak bang ciangin a zo ding hiam?

records.english: The sign says next spring, but nobody believes it.
records.zomi: Lai in kum zom spring a ci hi, ahi zongin kuamah in a um kei hi.

records.english: When is the best time to plant tomatoes here?
records.zomi: Hih mun ah tomato suan hun hoih pen bang ciang ahi hiam?

records.english: At the start of the rainy season, so that the young plants get plenty of water.
records.zomi: Guah hun kipat ciangin, a thak te in tui tam a ngah theih nadingun.

records.english: When did the doctor make you stop drinking coffee?
records.zomi: Bang ciangin siavuan in khawfi dawn hong tawpsak hiam?

records.english: Last year, after my blood pressure test.
records.zomi: Kum nung in, ka sisan hatna et khit ciangin.

records.english: When the alarm rang, everyone left the building calmly.
records.zomi: Alarm a ging ciangin mi khempeuh dai takin inn a nusia uh hi.

records.english: Ask the nurse when visiting hours start before you buy the flowers.
records.zomi: Pak na lei ma-in veh hun bang ciangin a kipan hiam nurse dong in.

records.english: Nobody could remember when the old mill had stopped working.
records.zomi: Buh guaina inn lui bang ciangin a tawp hiam kuamah in a phawk kei uh hi.

records.english: When does the next bus leave for the city?
records.zomi: Khuapi lam-a bus zom bang ciangin a pai ding hiam?

records.english: In twenty minutes, from the stop outside the bank.
records.zomi: Minit sawmnih sungin, bank pua-a dinna pan.

records.english: When was the roof damaged?
records.zomi: Bang ciangin innkhum a sia hiam?

records.english: During the storm last week, when a branch fell on it.
records.zomi: Kal nung huihpi laitakin, a tungah singkhawng khat a kiat ciangin.

records.english: Since when has your little brother been allowed to stay out until midnight?
records.zomi: Bang ciang pan na nau pasal zanlai dong pua ah om dingin kiphal hiam?

records.english: Everyone, the cash for each week goes into these envelopes, and when an envelope is empty, that's it.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, kal khat ciat-a sum hih lai ip sung ah a lut a, lai ip khat a awn ciangin tua ciang bek ahi hi.

records.english: If your income changes from month to month, it may help to plan your budget around the lowest month.
records.zomi: Na sum ngah kha simin a kilai leh kha niam pen tungah na budget gel in a huh kha ding hi.

records.english: My aunt pays all her bills on the first day of the month, so she never forgets any.
records.zomi: Ka ni in kha ni masa pen-in a bill khempeuh a pia a, tua ahih manin khatpeuh a mangngilh ngei kei hi.

records.english: Our car insurance went up even though we hadn't made a claim.
records.zomi: Bangmah i ngen kei hangin i mawtaw insurance a khang hi.

records.english: My brother compared other offers online and found one that was much cheaper.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in online ah a dangte a kikhaikhin a, a neem zaw mahmah khat a mu hi.

records.english: Is it possible to live on one salary if we're very careful?
records.zomi: I pilvang mahmah leh nasep man khat tawh i nungta thei ding hiam?

records.english: My phone bill tripled after a week abroad because I forgot to switch off roaming.
records.zomi: Roaming khek ka mangngilh ahih manin gamdang ah kal khat ka om khit ciangin ka phone bill thumvei a khang hi.

records.english: Now I buy a local SIM card as soon as I land.
records.zomi: Tu-in ka tun pah-in hih mun SIM card khat ka lei hi.

records.english: Kids, if you turn the lights off when you leave a room, you can keep half of what we save.
records.zomi: Naupangte, khan khat na nusiat ciangun meivak na khek uh leh i kem sum a khen khat na kem thei ding uh hi.

records.english: How do you plan for costs that only come once a year?
records.zomi: Kum khat ah khatvei bek hong tung man adingin bangci-in na gel hiam?

records.english: Did you remember to cancel the free trial before it started charging us?
records.zomi: Man hong lak ma-in a man om lo sin hun khek na phawk hiam?

records.english: My flatmate lost her job and couldn't pay her share of the rent.
records.zomi: Ka inn kihawm lawm in a nasep a mansuah a, a inn man khen a pia zo kei hi.

records.english: I covered it for two months, and she paid me back when she found new work.
records.zomi: Kha nih sung ka pia sak a, nasep thak a muh ciangin hong pia kik hi.

records.english: Had we read the contract more carefully, we wouldn't have signed up for such an expensive phone plan.
records.zomi: Thukimna lai pilvang zaw takin i sim le, man tam lua phone plan ah i kigelh kei ding hi.

records.english: A budget without savings is like a roof without a gutter, because every storm causes damage.
records.zomi: Sum khol om lo budget pen tui luanna om lo innkhum bang ahi a, huihpi khempeuh in siatna a piangsak hi.

records.english: I asked the shop to keep the jacket for me until payday.
records.zomi: Ka nasep man ka ngah dong kawt ka kem sak dingin dawr ka ngen hi.

records.english: Which bills have to be paid this week?
records.zomi: Hih kal sungin koi bill te pia ding ahi hiam?

records.english: Our children outgrow their school shoes every six months.
records.zomi: I tate in kha guk simin a sang khedap uh a pelh uh hi.

records.english: We now swap shoes and uniforms with two other families at the end of each term.
records.zomi: Tu-in term tawp simin innkuan dang nih tawh khedap leh sang puan i kilai hi.

records.english: Although it can feel uncomfortable to talk about money with relatives, it often prevents bigger misunderstandings later.
records.zomi: Sanggamte tawh sum thu kiho a nuam lo thei hangin a nung ciang-a kithei khialhna lian zaw a kham tamzaw hi.

records.english: Our old fridge used so much electricity that it was cheaper to replace it.
records.zomi: I khal bawm lui in meivak tam lua a zang ahih manin a lai a neem zaw hi.

records.english: Would you mind checking whether we've paid the internet bill?
records.zomi: Internet bill i pia khin hiam na en thei ding hiam?

records.english: Can we afford to fix the motorbike, or should we sell it?
records.zomi: Motorbike bawl siang man i pia zo ding hiam, i zuak ding hiam?

records.english: Could you help me understand the charges on this electricity bill?
records.zomi: Hih meivak bill tung-a man lakte theih dingin hong huh thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: The loan had hidden fees that nobody had explained to us.
