records.zomi: Dawr neipa khat in anteh leh lemon tawmno a gen a, a tui a kinai lamdang mahmah hi.

records.english: My little niece was given her first job at the feast: handing out the spoons.
records.zomi: Ka tunu neu in pawi ah a nasep masa pen a ngah hi: kawmte khen.

records.english: When my aunt cooked the dish instead of my mother, it didn't taste the same.
records.zomi: Ka nu sangin ka ni in an a huan ciangin a tui a kibang kei hi.

records.english: My mother finally wrote down the secret: she adds a little tamarind at the very end.
records.zomi: Ka nu in a tawp-in a thuguk a gelh hi: a tawp mahmah ah mangpakawm tawmno a koih hi.

records.english: How do you keep the food warm when the relatives arrive late?
records.zomi: Sanggamte a nun-in a tun ciangun an bangci-in na lumsak den hiam?

records.english: My sister-in-law doesn't eat meat, and our traditional feast is mostly pork.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal' zi in sa a ne kei a, i ngeina pawi an a tamzaw vok sa ahi hi.

records.english: We now cook a bean stew with the same spices so that she can share the meal with us.
records.zomi: Tu-in a tawh an a nek theih nadingin antui namtui kibang tawh be an tui i huan hi.

records.english: If the older cooks are getting tired, it may help to give each grandchild one dish to learn.
records.zomi: An huan upate a tawl kipat leh tu khat ciat in an khat sin dingin pia in a huh kha ding hi.

records.english: Rather than letting the tradition die, my cousins started a monthly dinner in the city.
records.zomi: Ngeina a bei sakpih sangin ka sanggamte in khuapi ah kha simin nitak an khat a kipatsak uh hi.

records.english: My cousin carved new serving spoons from wood for the reunion.
records.zomi: Kikhopna adingin ka sanggam in sing pan an khenna kawm thakte a ki hi.

records.english: At our local court, taking photos in the courtroom is not allowed.
records.zomi: I khua thukhenna inn ah thukhenna khan sung ah lim lak kiphal lo hi.

records.english: My uncle has to go to court next week as a witness.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu kal zom ciangin teci-in thukhenna inn ah a pai ding a kisam hi.

records.english: The judge had the room cleared because people were shouting.
records.zomi: Mite a kikou uh ahih manin thukhenpa in khan sung a awngsak hi.

records.english: The scales that statues of justice often hold are meant to show that both sides are weighed equally.
records.zomi: Thuman thukhenna lim te' len gikna khaina pen a lam nih kibang-a kikhai hi, cih lahna ahi hi.

records.english: The court sent a letter telling my father the date of the hearing.
records.zomi: Thukhenna inn in thu ngaihna ni gen-in ka pa kiangah lai a khak hi.

records.english: Which floor is courtroom number four on?
records.zomi: Thukhenna khan number li koi tuang ah a om hiam?

records.english: Everyone, please stand when the judge enters the courtroom.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, thukhenpa thukhenna khan a lut ciangin ding un.

records.english: In some countries, a group of ordinary citizens called a jury decides whether a person is guilty.
records.zomi: Gam khenkhatte ah gam mi pangai pawl khat in mi khat a mawh hiam a khensat uh hi.

records.english: Had the witness not come forward, the innocent man might have gone to prison.
records.zomi: Teci in a kilak kei le, mawh lo mi pen thong ah a tang kha ding hi.

records.english: What surprised me most about the court was how quietly everyone spoke.
records.zomi: Thukhenna inn ah ka lamdang sak pen pen mi khempeuh bangzah dai takin a gen uh hiam, cih ahi hi.

records.english: Did the judge announce the decision today?
records.zomi: Thukhenpa in tuni-in khensatna a gen hiam?

records.english: Having worked as a judge for thirty years, my grandfather still believes that everyone deserves to be heard.
records.zomi: Kum sawmthum sung thukhenpa a hih khit ciangin ka pu in mi khempeuh kingai ding hi, ci-in a um lai hi.

records.english: My cousin works as a court clerk, writing down everything that is said.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam thukhenna inn ah gen thu khempeuh a gelh nasem ahi hi.

records.english: The case was postponed because one of the witnesses was ill.
records.zomi: Teci khat a dam loh manin thu kisuan hi.

records.english: The trial lasted three days, and the courtroom was full every morning.
records.zomi: Thu khen ni thum a sau a, zingsang simin thukhenna khan a dim hi.

records.english: The judge used a small wooden hammer to call the court to order.
records.zomi: Thukhenpa in thukhenna dai sak dingin sing sut neu khat a zang hi.

records.english: If people can't afford a lawyer, the court in our country may appoint one for them.
records.zomi: Mite in lawyer man a pia zo kei uh leh i gam-a thukhenna inn in amaute adingin khat a koih thei hi.

records.english: Although courts can seem frightening, they exist to settle disagreements fairly.
records.zomi: Thukhenna inn te a lauhuai bang hangin kithukimlohnate dik taka khen dingin a om hi.

records.english: Many people believe that courts should explain their decisions in language that ordinary people can understand.
records.zomi: Mi tampi in thukhenna inn in a khensatnate mi pangaite in a theih theih pau tawh gen siang ding hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: An interpreter was provided for the witness who didn't speak the court's language.
records.zomi: Thukhenna inn' pau a thei lo teci adingin lehkiktu khat kipia hi.

records.english: My father keeps all the court papers in a folder so that nothing gets lost.
records.zomi: Bangmah a mang lo nadingin ka pa in thukhenna lai khempeuh folder khat sung ah a kem hi.

records.english: When does the court open in the morning?
records.zomi: Thukhenna inn zingsangin bang ciangin a kihong hiam?

records.english: The judge made the two neighbors agree to share the cost of the new fence.
records.zomi: Thukhenpa in inn veng nihte kulh thak man kihawm dingin a kithukimsak hi.

records.english: Kids, the judge in this game is the person who decides who wins.
records.zomi: Naupangte, hih kimawlna sung-a thukhenpa pen kua in a zo hiam a khensat mi ahi hi.

records.english: Why was the trial moved to another city?
records.zomi: Bang hangin thu khen khuapi dang ah kisuan hiam?

records.english: Who will speak for my brother at the hearing?
records.zomi: Thu ngaihna ah ka sanggam pasal adingin kua in a gen ding hiam?

records.english: Not until the judge read out the decision did the whole room fall silent.
records.zomi: Thukhenpa in khensatna a sim ciang bek khan bup a dai hi.

records.english: Why does the judge wear a black robe?
records.zomi: Bang hangin thukhenpa in puan vom a silh hiam?

records.english: Could the court arrange a quiet room for the child witness?
records.zomi: Thukhenna inn in naupang teci adingin khan dai khat a bawl thei ding hiam?

records.english: If you disagree with the court's decision, you may be able to appeal to a higher court.
records.zomi: Thukhenna inn' khensatna na nial leh thukhenna inn sang zaw ah na ngen kik thei kha ding hi.

records.english: Do I need a lawyer to settle a small dispute with my landlord?
records.zomi: Inn neipa tawh kinialna neu khat bawl siang dingin lawyer ka kisam ding hiam?

records.english: How long will the trial last?
records.zomi: Thu khen bangzah sawt ding hiam?

records.english: My neighbor took the builder to court because he never finished the roof.
records.zomi: Innkhum a zo ngei loh manin ka inn veng in inn lampa thukhenna inn ah a tawi hi.

records.english: The court ordered the builder to pay back the money.
records.zomi: Thukhenna inn in inn lampa sum pia kik dingin thu a pia hi.

records.english: Would you mind explaining what happens at a bail hearing?
records.zomi: Bail thu ngaihna ah bang a piang hiam hong gen siang thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: You may have to wait several months before your case is heard.
records.zomi: Na thu a kingai ma-in kha tampi na ngak ding a kisam kha ding hi.

records.english: Is it possible to watch a trial if you're not involved in the case?
records.zomi: Thu sung ah na kihel kei leh thu khen na en thei hiam?

records.english: In our town, most trials are open to the public, but you must sit quietly at the back.
records.zomi: I khuapi ah thu khen tamzaw mipi adingin kihong a, ahi zongin nung lam ah dai takin na tu ding hi.

records.english: What does a lawyer do?
records.zomi: Lawyer in bang a sem hiam?

records.english: A lawyer gives people legal advice and speaks for them in court.
records.zomi: Lawyer in mite thukham thuhilhna a pia a, thukhenna inn ah amaute adingin a gen hi.

records.english: Where can I find someone to give me free legal advice?
records.zomi: Man om lo thukham thuhilhna hong pia ding kuamah koi ah ka mu thei ding hiam?

records.english: Tell the court officer your name when you arrive, and he'll show you where to wait.
records.zomi: Na tun ciangin thukhenna inn nasempa kiangah na min gen in, koi ah ngak ding hiam hong etsak ding hi.

records.english: The family was relieved when the judge found their son not guilty.
records.zomi: Thukhenpa in a tapa uh a mawh kei hi, a ci ciangin innkuan a lungmuang uh hi.

records.english: The lawyer explained the papers to my grandmother in simple words.
records.zomi: Lawyer in ka pi kiangah laite kammal baih tawh a gen siang hi.

records.english: The more complicated the case, the longer the court usually takes to reach a decision.
records.zomi: Thu a buai semsem ciangin thukhenna inn in khensat dingin a tamzaw-in a sawt semsem hi.

records.english: My brother studied law for five years before he became a lawyer.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal lawyer a suak ma-in kum nga thukham a sin hi.

records.english: Our teacher took the class to visit the court so that we could see how it works.
records.zomi: Bangci-in a sem hiam i muh theih nadingin i saya in kilasi thukhenna inn ah a paipih hi.

records.english: The courtroom was so cold that the lawyers kept their coats on.
records.zomi: Thukhenna khan a vot lua ahih manin lawyerte in a kawt uh a silh lai uh hi.

records.english: A free lawyer helped my aunt when she couldn't afford to pay for one.
records.zomi: Ka ni in lawyer man a pia zo loh ciangin man om lo lawyer khat in a huh hi.

records.english: The judge listened carefully to both sides before making a decision.
records.zomi: Khensatna a bawl ma-in thukhenpa in a lam nih pilvang takin a ngai hi.

records.english: Could you come to court with me so that I don't feel so nervous?
records.zomi: Ka lau lua lo nadingin thukhenna inn ah hong pai khawm thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Rather than going to court, the two families agreed to let a respected elder settle the dispute.
records.zomi: Thukhenna inn ah pai sangin innkuan nihte in zahtak upa khat in kinialna a khensat dingin a kithukim uh hi.

records.english: Phones must be switched off inside the courtroom.
records.zomi: Thukhenna khan sung ah phone kikhek ding hi.

records.english: Children under twelve aren't allowed in the courtroom during some trials.
records.zomi: Thu khen khenkhat laitakin kum sawm leh nih nuai naupangte thukhenna khan ah kiphal lo hi.

records.english: In our country, small disputes about money can be settled in a local court without a lawyer.
records.zomi: I gam ah sum thu kinialna neute lawyer om lo-in khua thukhenna inn ah kibawl siang thei hi.

records.english: What should I wear when I go to court?
records.zomi: Thukhenna inn ka pai ciangin bang ka silh ding hiam?

records.english: The court building is next to the town hall.
records.zomi: Thukhenna inn pen khuapi inn kiang ah a om hi.

records.english: The witness said, "I saw the car go through the red light."
records.zomi: Teci in, “Mawtaw meivak san a khen ka mu hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: Shall I write down what happened while I still remember it clearly?
records.zomi: Kician takin ka phawk laitakin bang a piang hiam ka gelh ding hiam?

records.english: Whoever is called as a witness must tell the truth, or they may be punished.
records.zomi: Teci-in kisam peuhpeuh in a tak a gen ding a, a hi kei leh kigawt kha ding hi.

records.english: The rain ruined our outdoor wedding photos, and my sister cried all evening.
records.zomi: Guah in i pua-a mopawi limte a susia a, ka sanggam nu nitak bup a kap hi.

records.english: The photographer took new photos the next morning in the sunshine, and they were even better.
records.zomi: Lim la pa in a zing zingsangin ni sa sung ah lim thak a la a, a hoih zaw lai hi.

records.english: My grandmother has been sad since she stopped being able to garden.
records.zomi: Ka pi huan sem a zawh nawn loh pan a lungkham hi.

records.english: We built her a raised flower bed so that she can work in it from her chair.
records.zomi: A tutna pan a sep theih nadingin pak suanna sang khat i lam sak hi.

records.english: If sadness lasts for many weeks, it may help to speak to a doctor or counselor.
records.zomi: Lungkhamna kal tampi sung a om leh siavuan hiam thuhilhtu tawh kiho in a huh kha ding hi.

records.english: What makes me saddest is not being able to help when someone I love is struggling.
records.zomi: Hong lungkhamsak pen pen ka it mi khat a haksat laitakin ka huh theih loh ahi hi.

records.english: Can I tell my teacher why I've been so quiet in class?
records.zomi: Bang hangin kilasi ah ka dai mahmah hiam ka saya ka hilh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Having moved to a city where she knew nobody, my cousin joined a choir and found her happiness again.
records.zomi: Kuamah a theih loh khuapi khat ah a tuah khit ciangin ka sanggam nu la sakte pawl ah a lut a, a lungdamna a mu kik hi.

records.english: The long-awaited letter finally arrived, and the whole family cheered.
records.zomi: Sawt taka ngak lai a tawp-in a tung a, innkuan bup a kikou uh hi.

records.english: Kids, you can each choose one game for the party, so nobody feels left out.
records.zomi: Naupangte, kuamah kinusia lo bangin a kisak lo nadingin pawi adingin kimawlna khat ciat na teel thei uh hi.

records.english: My mother says, "Tears are nothing to be ashamed of."
records.zomi: Ka nu in, “Mittui pen zahlak ding hi lo hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: Where do you go when you need to feel calm?
records.zomi: Na lungsim nemsak na kisap ciangin koi ah na pai hiam?

records.english: Did the good news cheer your father up?
records.zomi: Thu hoih in na pa a lungdamsak hiam?

records.english: My son was heartbroken when he didn't make the football team.
records.zomi: Football pawl ah a kiteel kei ciangin ka tapa a lungkham mahmah hi.

records.english: His coach let him help with training, and the next season he was chosen.
records.zomi: A hilhtu in kisinna ah huh dingin a phal a, a zom kum ciangin kiteel hi.

records.english: My son was so happy with his new bicycle that he slept next to it.
records.zomi: Ka tapa a siiksakol thak tungah a lungdam lua ahih manin a kiang ah a ihmu hi.

records.english: Shall we take Grandma to the river, since she loves it there?
records.zomi: Ka pi in gun a deih mahmah ahih manin tua ah i paipih ding hiam?

records.english: Not until my friend called did I realize how long I'd been staying indoors alone.
records.zomi: Ka lawm in hong sam ciang bek bangzah sawt inn sung ah keimah bek ka om khin hiam ka thei hi.

records.english: When did you last do something just because it made you happy?
records.zomi: Hong lungdamsak bek ahih manin bangmah na hih nunung bang ciang ahi hiam?

records.english: Although sadness can feel endless, it often eases little by little when we share it.
records.zomi: Lungkhamna a bei lo bang thei hangin i hawm ciangin tawmno tawmno-in a nem tamzaw hi.

records.english: Why do some people cry when they're very happy?
records.zomi: Bang hangin mi khenkhatte a lungdam mahmah ciangun a kap uh hiam?

records.english: My father won't talk about how sad he is since he retired.
records.zomi: Ka pa in a nasep a tawp pan bangzah a lungkham hiam a gen nuam kei hi.

records.english: I asked him to teach me to repair furniture, and he seems happier with something to do.
records.zomi: Inn van bawl siang dan hong hilh dingin ka ngen a, sep ding a neih ciangin a lungdam zaw bang hi.

records.english: I lost my grandfather's old watch.
records.zomi: Ka pu' nai lui ka mansuah hi.

records.english: A boy found it in the park and brought it to the police station, where my name was on the back.
records.zomi: Naupang pasal khat in huan lian ah a mu a, palik inn ah a tawi a, a nung ah ka min a om hi.

records.english: Whoever finishes first can go and sit with Grandma, because she's feeling lonely today.
records.zomi: Tuni-in ka pi a lungngai ahih manin a zo masa peuhpeuh in a kiang ah va tu thei hi.

records.english: May I take a few days off to be with my family after my aunt's death?
records.zomi: Ka ni a sih khit ciangin ka innkuan tawh om dingin ni tawmno ka tawlngak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Would you mind sitting with my mother while I go to the pharmacy?
records.zomi: Zatui zuakna ah ka pai laitakin ka nu kiang ah na tu thei ding hiam?

records.english: How do you comfort a friend who doesn't want to talk?
records.zomi: Kiho nuam lo lawm khat bangci-in na hehnem hiam?

records.english: Children aren't allowed to visit the ward, so my daughter made her grandfather a video message.
records.zomi: Zato khan ah naupangte kiphal lo ahih manin ka tanu in a pu adingin video thu khat a bawl hi.

records.english: Who can I talk to when I feel sad at school?
records.zomi: Sang ah ka lungkham ciangin kua tawh ka kiho thei ding hiam?

records.english: Could the school arrange for the children to talk to someone after their classmate moved away?
records.zomi: A kilasi lawm a tuah khit ciangin naupangte kuamah tawh a kiho theih nadingin sang in a bawl thei ding hiam?

records.english: My neighbor is overjoyed about her new grandson but worried that he lives so far away.
records.zomi: Ka inn veng in a tu thak tungah a lungdam mahmah a, ahi zongin gamla taka a om manin a lungkham hi.

records.english: I really do want to celebrate my exam results, but my brother failed his.
records.zomi: Ka sitna kipaina lungdampih ka deih mahmah hi, ahi zongin ka sanggam pasal a zo kei hi.

records.english: We went out for a quiet dinner together, and I let him choose the restaurant.
records.zomi: Khawm-in nitak an dai khat ah i pai a, anneekna inn amah in a teel dingin ka phal hi.

records.english: The more I compared myself with others online, the worse I felt about my own life.
records.zomi: Online ah midangte tawh ka kikhaikhin semsem ciangin keima' nuntakna tungah ka hoih lo sa semsem hi.

records.english: Which song always makes you happy?
records.zomi: Koi la in hong lungdamsak tawntung hiam?

records.english: I felt sad when the old bakery closed, so I asked the baker for his bread recipe.
records.zomi: Moh bawlna lui a kikhak ciangin ka lungkham a, moh bawlpa kiangah a moh bawl dan ka ngen hi.

records.english: The village celebrated when the new clinic finally opened.
records.zomi: Siavuan inn thak a tawp-in a kihon ciangin khua in pawi a bawl hi.

records.english: I was rejected for the job I wanted most, and I couldn't stop thinking about it.
records.zomi: Ka deih pen nasep ah hong nial uh a, ka ngaihsun tawp zo kei hi.

records.english: My mentor asked the company for feedback, which helped me prepare for the next interview.
records.zomi: Hong hilhtu in company kiangah a ngaihsutna uh a ngen a, tua in a zom interview adingin hong kimansak hi.

records.english: Please don't post photos of the funeral online without asking the family first.
records.zomi: Innkuan dong masa lo-in mithi vuina lim online ah koih kei un.

records.english: I got engaged in the same week that my best friend's father died.
records.zomi: Ka lawm hoih pen' pa a sih kal mah ah kiteen dingin ka kiciam hi.

records.english: I waited until after the funeral to share the news, and she was the first person I told.
records.zomi: Thu hawm dingin mithi vuina khit dong ka ngak a, amah ka hilh masa pen ahi hi.

records.english: We lost the match, but the coach said, "Tonight we're having ice cream anyway."
records.zomi: Kimawlna i sum a, ahi zongin hilhtu in, “Tuni zanin ice cream i ne lai ding hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: Nobody at work remembered my birthday.
records.zomi: Nasepna ah kuamah in ka pianni a phawk kei uh hi.

records.english: I told a close colleague how I felt, and the next year the whole office brought a cake.
records.zomi: Nasem lawm kinai khat kiangah ka kisak dan ka gen a, a zom kum ciangin office bup in cake khat a tawi uh hi.

records.english: Rather than hiding his sadness, my uncle began writing letters to his late wife in a notebook.
records.zomi: A lungkhamna sel sangin ka pa neu in a zi sikhin kiangah laibu khat sung ah lai a gelh kipan hi.

records.english: Spending the holidays alone in a foreign city made me feel very homesick.
records.zomi: Gamdang khuapi khat ah keimah bek nopsakna hun zat in inn hong lungngaisak mahmah hi.

records.english: My landlady invited me to her family's dinner, and I didn't feel alone anymore.
records.zomi: Ka inn neinu in a innkuan nitak an ah hong sam a, keimah bek om bangin ka kisa nawn kei hi.

records.english: The dark winter months always make me feel low.
records.zomi: Khuavot kha mialte in hong lungkiasak tawntung hi.

records.english: I now take a walk in the daylight every lunchtime, and it lifts my mood.
records.zomi: Tu-in sun simin ni vak sung ah ka vak a, ka lungsim a domsang hi.

records.english: My little sister uses a box of crayons to draw how she feels when she can't explain it.
records.zomi: Ka nau nu in a gen siang zawh loh ciangin a kisak dan lim gelh dingin crayon bawm khat a zang hi.

records.english: Do you think it's all right to laugh at a funeral when you remember something funny?
records.zomi: Mithi vuina ah bangmah nuihzathuai na phawk ciangin nui a hoih in na ngaihsun hiam?

records.english: The old photo album was found in the attic, and Grandma laughed at every page.
records.zomi: Inn tung khan ah lim bu lui kimu a, ka pi laimai khempeuh ah a nui hi.

records.english: When my friend got the promotion I'd hoped for, I felt jealous instead of happy for her.
records.zomi: Ka deih mahmah mun sang ka lawm in a ngah ciangin a tungah lungdam sangin ka hazat hi.

records.english: I admitted it to her honestly, and we laughed about it over dinner.
records.zomi: Thuman takin ka pang a, nitak an nek kawm-in i nuihza pih hi.

records.english: Had I talked to someone sooner, I wouldn't have felt so alone for so long.
records.zomi: Kuamah tawh a ma zaw-in ka kiho le, hun sawt sung keimah bek om bangin ka kisa kei ding hi.

records.english: What would make your grandfather smile again?
records.zomi: Bang in na pu kik-in a nuisak ding hiam?

records.english: Happiness shared with others is like a candle that lights another candle.
records.zomi: Midangte tawh kihawm lungdamna pen khawimeivaak dang khat a hal khawimeivaak bang ahi hi.

records.english: My grandfather is afraid of lifts and always takes the stairs.
records.zomi: Ka pu lift a lau a, kahlei a zang tawntung hi.

records.english: The hospital let him use the staff staircase so that he could reach the fifth floor slowly.
records.zomi: Tuang ngana zawl takin a tun theih nadingin zato in nasemte' kahlei zang dingin a phal hi.

records.english: Is it possible to stop worrying about things that haven't happened yet?
records.zomi: Piang nai lo thute lungkham tawp thei hiam?

records.english: Although fear can protect us from danger, too much of it can stop us from living fully.
records.zomi: Lauhna in lauhuaina pan hong veng thei hangin a tam lua in a bup-a nuntakna pan hong kham thei hi.

records.english: Had I talked about my fear of flying sooner, I might have visited my sister years ago.
records.zomi: Vanleng tuan ka lauhna ka gen masa le, kum tampi ma-in ka sanggam nu ka veh kha ding hi.

records.english: My mother got a message saying her bank account would be closed unless she clicked a link.
records.zomi: Link khat a nek kei leh a bank account kikhak ding hi, ci thu khat ka nu in a ngah hi.

records.english: She called me first, and we phoned the bank, which said the message was a scam.
records.zomi: A masa-in hong sam a, bank i sam a, thu pen zuau ahi hi, a ci uh hi.

records.english: Are you scared of the big dog next door?
records.zomi: A kiang inn-a ui lian na lau hiam?

records.english: Did the test results ease your mind?
records.zomi: Etna kipaina in na lungsim a ngaisak hiam?

records.english: The rains came late, and every farmer in the village feared for the harvest.
records.zomi: Guah a nun a, khua sung-a lo nei khempeuh in buh lak adingin a lau uh hi.

records.zomi: Na khualzinnate lak ah koi na hih kik nuam pen hiam?

records.english: A friend posted my story about the accident online without asking me.
records.zomi: Lawm khat in dong lo-in ka accident tangthu online ah a koih hi.

records.english: I asked her to take it down, and she apologized and deleted it the same day.
records.zomi: La khia dingin ka ngen a, maisak a ngen a, tua ni mah-in a phiat hi.

records.english: Please don't share what I told you with anyone else.
records.zomi: Ka gen thu kuamah dang tawh hawm kei in.

records.english: The photo album was rescued from the fire, although its cover was badly burned.
records.zomi: Lim bu' khuhna a kang mahmah hangin mei kangna pan kihon hi.

records.english: Who in your family tells the best stories?
records.zomi: Na innkuan ah kua in tangthu a gen hoih pen hiam?

records.english: The recording was lost when my phone was stolen.
records.zomi: Ka phone a kiguk ciangin aw lakna a mang hi.

records.english: Fortunately, my sister had saved a copy on her computer.
records.zomi: Lungdamhuai takin ka sanggam nu in a computer tungah copy khat a save hi.

records.english: Not until I heard my mother's story did I understand why she was so careful with money.
records.zomi: Ka nu' tangthu ka zak ciang bek bang hangin sum tungah a pilvang mahmah hiam ka thei hi.

records.english: Would you mind telling the children what school was like when you were young?
records.zomi: Na naupan lai-in sang bangci a om hiam naupangte na hilh thei ding hiam?

records.english: My mother said, "Some memories are too heavy to carry alone, so I'm glad I told you."
records.zomi: Ka nu in, “Phawkna khenkhatte amah bek pua dingin a gik lua ahih manin kong hilh manin ka lungdam hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: The old gate where my grandfather stood each morning was taken down last year.
records.zomi: Ka pu zingsang simin a dinna kongpi lui kum nung in kisusia hi.

records.english: Kids, I'm going to tell you how I met your grandmother at the bus stop one rainy morning.
records.zomi: Naupangte, guah zuk zingsang khat bus dinna ah na pi bangci-in ka mu hiam kong gen ding hi.

records.english: My old teacher's morning greeting was like sunshine through a window, because it warmed the whole room.
records.zomi: Ka saya lui' zingsang hopihna pen tukvuang tungtawn ni vak bang ahi a, khan bup a lumsak hi.

records.english: Years ago, my aunt worked the night shift at the hospital.
records.zomi: Kum tampi paisa-in ka ni zato ah zan nasep a sem hi.

records.english: Every evening she greeted the patients one by one before the lights went out.
records.zomi: Nitak simin meivak a mit ma-in natnate khat khit khat-in a hopih hi.

records.english: Some of them told her later that her voice was the last kind thing they heard each day.
records.zomi: A khenkhatte in a nung ciangin a aw pen ni simin a zak nunung pen thu nem ahi hi, ci-in a hilh uh hi.

records.english: Why did people in your village bow when they greeted the headman?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na khua-a mite in khua makaipa a hopih ciangun a kun uh hiam?

records.english: When we first moved to the city, nobody in our building said a word to us.
records.zomi: Khuapi ah i tuah masak ciangin i inn lian-a kuamah in kammal khat zong hong gen kei uh hi.

records.english: My mother started greeting everyone on the stairs each evening, even when they didn't answer.
records.zomi: Ka nu in a dawng kei uh zongin nitak simin kahlei tungah mi khempeuh a hopih kipan hi.

records.english: By the end of the year, the neighbors were inviting us to their weddings.
records.zomi: Kum tawp ciangin inn vengte in a mopawi uh ah hong sam uh hi.

records.english: My little brother was scolded for greeting the guests with his mouth full of rice.
records.zomi: Ka nau pasal in a kam sung buh dim-in khualte a hopih manin kihau hi.

records.english: How did people greet each other in your village before there were phones?
records.zomi: Phone a om ma-in na khua-a mite bangci-in a kihopih uh hiam?

records.english: The power went off one winter evening, and the whole village was dark.
records.zomi: Khuavot nitak khat meivak a mit a, khua bup a mial hi.

records.english: Families walked from house to house with lamps, greeting each other in the cold.
records.zomi: Innkuante meivak tawi-in inn khat pan khat ah a pai uh a, vot sung ah a kihopih uh hi.

records.english: It was the friendliest evening anyone could remember.
records.zomi: Kuamah' phawkna sung ah nitak nuam pen ahi hi.

records.english: Did you ever get into trouble for not greeting a guest?
records.zomi: Khual khat na hopih kei manin buaina ah na tuak ngei hiam?

records.english: What did your teacher do if you forgot to greet her in the morning?
records.zomi: Zingsangin na hopih na mangngilh leh na saya in bang a hih hiam?

records.english: She waited at the door with her arms folded until we said it properly.
records.zomi: Dik takin i gen dong a ban khawm-in kongkhak ah a ngak hi.

records.english: During the floods, we were stuck on the roof of the school until morning.
records.zomi: Tuiciim laitakin zingsang dong sang innkhum tungah i om hi.

records.english: When the first boat arrived at dawn, the fisherman shouted a cheerful greeting as if it were an ordinary day.
records.zomi: Khuavak ciangin long masa pen a tun ciangin nga mat pa in ni pangai bangin nuam takin a hopih hi.

records.english: I'll never forget how much that simple greeting comforted us.
records.zomi: Tua hopihna baih in bangzah hong hehnem hiam ka mangngilh ngei kei ding hi.

records.english: Did your grandparents greet each other in any special way?
records.zomi: Na pu leh pite tuam takin a kihopih ngei uh hiam?

records.english: Every morning, Grandpa made Grandma's tea before he said a single word to anyone.
records.zomi: Zingsang simin kuamah tawh kammal khat a gen ma-in ka pu in ka pi' tea a bawl hi.

records.english: When did you start greeting your teachers in the corridor?
records.zomi: Bang ciangin inn lam ah na sayate na hopih kipan hiam?

records.english: Rather than shouting across the yard, my grandmother always walked over to greet visitors properly.
records.zomi: Tual gal lam pan kikou sangin ka pi in khual hongte hoih taka hopih dingin a pai tawntung hi.

records.english: On my first day at the office, I greeted the director in the lift without knowing who he was.
records.zomi: Office ah ka ni masa pen-in kua ahi hiam theih lo-in lift sung ah director ka hopih hi.

records.english: We chatted about the weather all the way to the tenth floor.
records.zomi: Tuang sawmna dong huihkhua thu i kiho hi.

records.english: An hour later, he walked into my training session and smiled at me.
records.zomi: Nai khat khit ciangin ka kisinna ah a lut a, hong nui hi.

records.english: Not until I lived alone did I realize how much I missed my family's morning greetings.
records.zomi: Keimah bek ka om ciang bek ka innkuan' zingsang hopihnate bangzah ka lungngai hiam ka thei hi.

records.english: In my grandparents' village, children weren't allowed to walk past an elder without greeting them.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh pite' khua ah naupangte upa khat a hopih lo-in a khen thei kei uh hi.

records.english: The more often the shopkeeper greeted me, the more I wanted to buy from his shop.
records.zomi: Dawr neipa in hong hopih den semsem ciangin a dawr pan lei ka deih semsem hi.

records.english: Having been away for ten years, I was greeted at the airport by relatives I no longer recognized.
records.zomi: Kum sawm a om khit ciangin ka theih nawn loh sanggamte in vanlengtual ah hong hopih uh hi.

records.english: Had I greeted my new neighbor that first morning, we might have become friends much sooner.
records.zomi: Tua zingsang masa-in ka inn veng thak ka hopih le, a ma zaw-in lawm i suak kha ding hi.

records.english: Although my grandfather couldn't hear well, he never once failed to greet a guest at the door.
records.zomi: Ka pu a za hoih kei hangin kongkhak ah khual khat hopih khatvei zong a mansuah ngei kei hi.

records.english: Every Sunday evening, my father called his mother just to wish her a good night.
records.zomi: Nipini nitak simin ka pa in zan nuam a deihsak dingin a nu a sam hi.

records.english: The village bell was rung every evening to tell the farmers to come home from the fields.
records.zomi: Lo nei te lo pan inn ah ciah dingin a hilh nadingin nitak simin khua khawngging kitum hi.

records.english: When I was a student abroad, I greeted my landlady in her language on my first morning.
records.zomi: Gamdang ah ka sin laitakin zingsang masa pen-in ka inn neinu amah' pau tawh ka hopih hi.

records.english: I got the words completely wrong, and she laughed until she cried.
records.zomi: Kammalte ka khial kim a, a kap dong a nui hi.

records.english: Then she taught me the right greeting, and we were friends for the rest of the year.
records.zomi: Tua ciangin hopihna dik hong hilh a, kum bup lawm i hi hi.

records.english: Why did your grandmother always greet the sun in the morning?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na pi in zingsangin ni a hopih tawntung hiam?

records.english: Would you have recognized your cousin if she hadn't greeted you first?
records.zomi: Na sanggam in a masa-in hong hopih kei le na thei ding hiam?

records.english: Did your teacher really make you greet her in three languages?
records.zomi: Na saya in pau thum tawh hopih dingin hong sawl taktak hiam?

records.english: Whoever arrived last at my grandmother's house had to greet every relative before sitting down.
records.zomi: Ka pi' inn ah a tung nunung pen peuhpeuh in a tut ma-in sanggam khempeuh a hopih ding hi.

records.english: Who greeted you at the station when you first arrived?
records.zomi: Na tun masak ciangin meileng dinna ah kua in hong hopih hiam?

records.english: My father said, "Greet the cook first, because she worked hardest today."
records.zomi: Ka pa in, “An huan a masa-in hopih un, tuni-in a sem hat pen ahi hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: What was the first thing your grandmother said to you each morning?
records.zomi: Zingsang simin na pi in hong gen masa pen bang ahi hiam?

records.english: Everyone, the story I'm going to tell you happened on my first evening in this village.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, kong gen ding tangthu pen hih khua ah ka nitak masa pen-in a piang ahi hi.

records.english: Who used to greet you when you came home from school?
records.zomi: Sang pan inn na tun ciangin kua in hong hopih den hiam?

records.english: Do you remember how your mother used to wake you up in the morning?
records.zomi: Zingsangin na nu in bangci-in hong phawngsak den hiam na phawk hiam?

records.english: She opened the curtains and sang the same little song every day.
records.zomi: Tukvuang puan a hon a, ni simin la neu kibang a sa hi.

records.english: Did your mother always greet you with a hug, even when she was angry?
records.zomi: A heh laitakin zong na nu in hong pom-in hong hopih tawntung hiam?

records.english: Was your father strict about greetings when you were young?
records.zomi: Na neu lai-in na pa hopihna thu-ah a khauh hiam?

records.english: Every morning when I was a child, my grandfather stood at the gate and greeted each neighbor who passed.
records.zomi: Ka naupan lai-in zingsang simin ka pu kongpi ah a ding a, a khen inn veng khempeuh a hopih hi.

records.english: Nobody walked by without stopping to ask about his health.
records.zomi: Kuamah in a cidamna dong lo-in a khen kei uh hi.

records.english: When he died, the whole street came to the house to say how much they missed those mornings.
records.zomi: A sih ciangin tua zingsangte bangzah a lungngai uh hiam gen dingin lampi bup inn ah a hong uh hi.

records.english: What I remember most about my first job is the cleaner who greeted every worker by name.
records.zomi: Ka nasep masa pen-a ka phawk pen pen nasem khempeuh a min tawh a hopih siangsaktu ahi hi.

records.english: My mother was hurt when I came home from university and forgot to greet my grandmother first.
records.zomi: Sangpi pan inn ka tun ciangin ka pi a masa-in hopih ka mangngilh ahih manin ka nu a lungkham hi.

records.english: I really did want to greet the old man every morning, but I was too shy to speak.
records.zomi: Zingsang simin pasal upa hopih ka deih mahmah hi, ahi zongin gen dingin ka zak lua hi.

records.english: One day he greeted me first, and after that we talked every day.
records.zomi: Ni khat a masa-in hong hopih a, tua khit ciangin ni simin i kiho hi.

records.english: Last winter, a stranger at the bus stop wished me a good evening, and it lifted my mood all week.
records.zomi: Kum nung khuavot in bus dinna-a mi theih loh khat in nitak nuam hong deihsak a, kal bup ka lungsim a domsang hi.

records.english: My little sister introduced herself to the doctor and then asked him his age.
records.zomi: Ka nau nu siavuan kiangah a kitheisak a, tua ciangin a kum a dong hi.

records.english: Do you remember introducing yourself on your first day at school?
records.zomi: Sang na kah ni masa pen-in na kitheisakna na phawk hiam?

records.english: I said my name so quietly that the teacher had to ask me three times.
records.zomi: Ka min dai lua takin ka gen ahih manin saya in thumvei hong dong hi.

records.english: What did you say about yourself at your first meeting with the team?
records.zomi: Pawl tawh na kikhopna masa pen-in nangma thu bang na gen hiam?

records.english: I told them I had grown up on a farm, and someone asked me to bring eggs the next day.
records.zomi: Lo ah ka khang hi, ka ci a, kuamah in a zing ni-in aktui tawi dingin hong ngen hi.

records.english: Everyone, I'd like you to introduce yourselves by telling us where your grandparents came from.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, na pu leh pite koi pan a hong uh hiam gen-in kitheisak un.

records.english: Was it hard to introduce yourself at the new church?
records.zomi: Pawlpi thak ah kitheisak a haksa hiam?

records.english: What did your wife's parents think of you at first?
records.zomi: Na zi' nu leh pa in a masa-in bang hong sa uh hiam?

records.english: Having introduced myself to so many strangers as a salesman, I lost all my fear of meeting people.
records.zomi: Van zuak mi-in mi theih loh tampi kiangah ka kitheisak khit ciangin mite muh ka lauhna khempeuh a bei hi.

records.english: Where did you first meet the people you work with now?
records.zomi: Tu-a na nasem khawm mite koi ah na mu masa hiam?

records.english: Although I introduced myself in their language, the villagers answered me in mine to make me feel welcome.
records.zomi: Amaute' pau tawh ka kitheisak hangin khua mite in hong muak bangin ka kisak nadingin keima' pau tawh hong dawng uh hi.

records.english: My first introduction at school was like jumping into cold water, because the shock lasted only a moment.
records.zomi: Sang ah ka kitheisakna masa pen tui vot sung ah diang bang ahi a, a lauhna tawmno bek a sau hi.

records.english: When I arrived at the village as a young teacher, the headman asked me to introduce myself on the radio.
records.zomi: Saya khangno-in khua ka tun ciangin khua makaipa in radio tungah kitheisak dingin hong ngen hi.

records.english: My voice was shaking, but the whole village was listening.
records.zomi: Ka aw a ling a, ahi zongin khua bup in a ngai uh hi.

records.english: The next morning, every child at school already knew my name.
records.zomi: A zing zingsangin sang-a naupang khempeuh in ka min a thei khin uh hi.

records.english: When did you first have to introduce yourself to a large audience?
records.zomi: Mi tam mai ah bang ciangin na kitheisak masa ding a kisam hiam?

records.english: I was asked to introduce myself at the wedding because I was the only guest nobody knew.
records.zomi: Kuamah in hong theih loh khual khat bek ka hih manin mopawi ah kitheisak dingin hong ngen uh hi.

records.english: Not until I introduced myself did the old woman realize that I was her sister's grandson.
records.zomi: Ka kitheisak ciang bek numei upa in a sanggam nu' tu ka hi hi, cih a thei hi.

records.english: Rather than giving a long speech, my grandfather simply told the guests his name and the name of his village.
records.zomi: Thugen sau gen sangin ka pu in khualte kiangah a min leh a khua min bek a gen hi.

records.english: Were your parents proud of the speech you gave on your first day?
records.zomi: Na ni masa pen-a na thugen tungah na nu leh na pa a kisathei uh hiam?

records.english: Who was the first person you met when you moved to the city?
records.zomi: Khuapi ah na tuah ciangin na muh masa pen kua ahi hiam?

records.english: My father was introduced to the village council as the man who had built the new bridge.
records.zomi: Ka pa lei thak a lam mi hi, ci-in khua upate kiangah kitheisak hi.

records.english: Shall I tell you how your mother introduced herself to me?
records.zomi: Na nu kei kiangah bangci-in a kitheisak hiam kong gen ding hiam?

records.english: What I remember most about my first day at university is introducing myself to a hundred people in one afternoon.
records.zomi: Sangpi-a ka ni masa pen-a ka phawk pen pen nitak lam khat sungin mi za khat kiangah ka kitheisak ahi hi.

records.english: At my first job interview, the lights went out just as I started to introduce myself.
records.zomi: Ka nasep interview masa pen-in ka kitheisak kipat laitakin meivak a mit hi.

records.english: I kept talking in the dark, and the manager said that showed calm.
records.zomi: Mial sung ah ka gen den a, tua in dai taka om a lak hi, ci-in manager in a ci hi.

records.english: I got the job, and we still joke about it.
records.zomi: Nasep ka ngah a, tu dong tua thu i nuihza pih lai hi.

records.english: Do you remember who sat next to you on your first day?
records.zomi: Na ni masa pen-in na kiang ah kua a tu hiam na phawk hiam?

records.english: How did you introduce yourself to your future in-laws?
records.zomi: Na sungte ding kiangah bangci-in na kitheisak hiam?

records.english: Which teacher remembered your name first?
records.zomi: Koi saya in na min a phawk masa pen hiam?

records.english: On my first day at the factory, I was introduced to sixty workers in five minutes.
records.zomi: Factory ah ka ni masa pen-in minit nga sungin nasem sawmguk kiangah hong theisak uh hi.

records.english: By lunchtime I had forgotten every single name.
records.zomi: Sun an hun ciangin min khatpeuh ka mangngilh kim hi.

records.english: The supervisor wrote them all on a list for me, which I kept in my pocket for weeks.
records.zomi: Enkaipa in list khat tungah a vekpi hong gelh sak a, kal tampi sung ka ip sung ah ka kem hi.

records.english: The teacher said, "Stand up, tell us your name, and tell us one thing you love."
records.zomi: Saya in, “Ding unla, na min uh gen un, na deih uh khat gen un,” a ci hi.

records.english: My mother's introduction at the conference was drowned out by rain on the tin roof.
records.zomi: Kikhopna lian ah ka nu' kitheisakna thih innkhum tung-a guah ging in a khuh hi.

records.english: Years ago, I introduced myself to a woman at the bus stop because she looked lost.
records.zomi: Kum tampi paisa-in a mang bang ahih manin bus dinna ah numei khat kiangah ka kitheisak hi.

records.english: She turned out to be my new manager, starting the same day as me.
records.zomi: Ni kibang mah-in a kipan ka manager thak ahi hi, cih a kimu hi.

records.english: We have been friends ever since.
records.zomi: Tua pan kipan lawm i hi hi.

records.english: Had I introduced myself properly to the director, he wouldn't have mistaken me for a visitor.
records.zomi: Director kiangah dik takin ka kitheisak le, khual hong khat in hong ngaihsun khial kei ding hi.

records.english: Whoever arrived at the training last had to introduce themselves with a song.
records.zomi: Kisinna ah a tung nunung pen peuhpeuh in la khat tawh a kitheisak ding hi.

records.english: What did you wear to your first day at work?
records.zomi: Nasep ni masa pen-in bang na silh hiam?

records.english: The first time I met my wife's parents, I was so nervous that I introduced myself twice.
records.zomi: Ka zi' nu leh pa ka muh masak ciangin ka lau lua ahih manin nihvei ka kitheisak hi.

records.english: Her father laughed and said that once was enough for him to remember me.
records.zomi: A pa a nui a, hong phawk dingin khatvei a kicing hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Twenty years later, he still tells the story at every family dinner.
records.zomi: Kum sawmnih khit ciangin innkuan nitak an khempeuh ah tua tangthu a gen lai hi.

records.english: The more times I introduced myself that week, the easier it became.
records.zomi: Tua kal sungin ka kitheisak tam semsem ciangin a baih semsem hi.

records.english: When we moved abroad, I didn't know how to introduce myself in the new language.
records.zomi: Gamdang ah i tuah ciangin pau thak tawh bangci-in kitheisak ding hiam ka thei kei hi.

records.english: A neighbor's little girl taught me, giggling at every mistake.
records.zomi: Inn veng' numei naupang neu khat in ka khialhna khempeuh ah nui-in hong hilh hi.

records.english: By the end of the month, I could introduce myself to anyone in the street.
records.zomi: Kha tawp ciangin lampi tung-a kua peuhpeuh kiangah ka kitheisak thei hi.

records.english: Could you have introduced yourself more confidently if you had practiced?
records.zomi: Na kisin le, kician zaw-in na kitheisak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Children, today you're going to tell the class about the day you were born, if your parents told you the story.
records.zomi: Naupangte, tuni-in na nu leh na pa in tangthu hong gen uh leh na suah ni thu kilasi na hilh ding uh hi.

records.english: I really did want to make a good impression, so I practiced my introduction in front of the mirror all week.
records.zomi: Ngaihsutna hoih pia ka deih mahmah ahih manin kal bup mai-et mai ah ka kitheisakna ka kisin hi.

records.english: The old photo shows my grandfather on the day he introduced himself to my grandmother's family.
records.zomi: Lim lui in ka pi' innkuan kiangah ka pu a kitheisak ni a lak hi.

records.english: Last year, I introduced myself to my new neighbors with a basket of oranges.
records.zomi: Kum nung in ka inn veng thakte kiangah lamtui bawm khat tawh ka kitheisak hi.

records.english: My name was read out wrongly at the graduation, and nobody noticed except my mother.
records.zomi: Sang zawhna pawi ah ka min dik lo-in kisim a, ka nu simloh kuamah in a thei kei uh hi.

records.english: My grandmother told us that she introduced herself to the whole school when she was only six.
records.zomi: Kum guk bek a phak lai-in sang bup kiangah a kitheisak hi, ci-in ka pi in hong gen hi.

records.english: How old were you when you first sang in public?
records.zomi: Mipi mai ah la na sak masak ciangin kum bangzah na hi hiam?

records.english: Why did you start using your middle name at university?
records.zomi: Bang hangin sangpi ah na min kimlai na zang kipan hiam?

records.english: Tell me what happened when you met the club president.
records.zomi: Club makaipa na muh ciangin bang a piang hiam hong gen in.

records.english: Did anyone ever confuse you with your brother?
records.zomi: Kuamah in na sanggam pasal tawh hong kikhial ngei hiam?

records.english: At my cousin's engagement, the uncle who introduced me called me by my brother's name all evening.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam' kiteen kiciamna pawi ah hong theisak pa neu in nitak bup ka sanggam pasal' min tawh hong sam hi.

records.english: Why did your mother introduce your friend as your cousin?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na nu in na lawm na sanggam hi, ci-in a theisak hiam?

records.english: Do you remember the day you introduced me to your parents?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa kiangah hong theisak ni na phawk hiam?

records.english: You were so nervous that you called my father by the wrong name.
records.zomi: Na lau lua ahih manin ka pa min dik lo tawh na sam hi.

records.english: Not until the old woman mentioned our village did I realize that she was my mother's childhood friend.
records.zomi: Numei upa in i khua a gen ciang bek ka nu' naupan lai lawm ahi hi, cih ka thei hi.

records.english: When did you first meet your husband's family?
records.zomi: Bang ciangin na pasal' innkuan na mu masa hiam?

records.english: When I first brought my fiancé home, my grandmother refused to speak to him for an hour.
records.zomi: Ka kiteen ding pasal inn ah ka paipih masak ciangin ka pi in nai khat sung a kiho nuam kei hi.

records.english: Then he offered to fix her broken radio with the little screwdriver he always carries.
records.zomi: Tua ciangin a tawi tawntung screwdriver neu tawh a radio sia bawl siang dingin a kipia hi.

records.english: By dinner time, she was introducing him to the neighbors as her favorite grandson.
records.zomi: Nitak an hun ciangin inn vengte kiangah a tu deih pen bangin a theisak hi.

records.english: Would you have become friends if your mothers hadn't introduced you at the market?
records.zomi: Na nu uh in zuakna mun ah hong theisak kei le lawm na suak ding uh hiam?

records.english: The more relatives I was introduced to, the more confused I became about who was whose child.
records.zomi: Sanggam tam semsem hong theisak ciangin kua' ta kua hiam ka buai semsem hi.

records.english: At my grandfather's funeral, a stranger introduced herself as his first teacher's daughter.
records.zomi: Ka pu' mithi vuina ah mi theih loh khat in a saya masa pen' tanu ka hi hi, ci-in a kitheisak hi.

records.english: She had brought a photo of him as a boy, which none of us had ever seen.
records.zomi: A naupan lai lim khat a tawi a, ei khatpeuh in i mu ngei kei hi.

records.english: We had it copied and framed for every branch of the family.
records.zomi: Copy i bawl sak a, innkuan khen khempeuh adingin frame tawh i koih hi.

records.english: Could you tell the children how you met their grandmother?
records.zomi: A pi uh bangci-in na mu hiam naupangte na hilh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Years ago, my sister introduced me to a quiet girl from her class.
records.zomi: Kum tampi paisa-in ka sanggam nu in a kilasi-a numei naupang dai khat hong theisak hi.

records.english: We didn't like each other at first.
records.zomi: A masa-in i kideih kei hi.

records.english: Now she's my closest friend, and my sister still says she deserves the credit.
records.zomi: Tu-in ka lawm kinai pen ahi a, ka sanggam nu in amah' hihna ahi hi, a ci lai hi.

records.english: Meeting my husband's family for the first time was like walking into a room where everyone already knew the rules.
records.zomi: Ka pasal' innkuan ka muh masak pen mi khempeuh in thupiakte a thei khin khan khat sung ah lut bang ahi hi.

records.english: Tell me about the first time you met your best friend.
records.zomi: Na lawm hoih pen na muh masak hun hong gen in.

records.english: Had you met my brother before I introduced you, or had you only heard about him?
records.zomi: Kong theisak ma-in ka sanggam pasal na mu khin hiam, a thu bek na za hiam?

records.english: What I remember most about meeting my wife's family is how many cousins there were.
records.zomi: Ka zi' innkuan ka muh ciangin ka phawk pen pen sanggam bangzah a tam hiam, cih ahi hi.

records.english: Had my friend not introduced me to her brother, I would never have found my job.
records.zomi: Ka lawm in a sanggam pasal hong theisak kei le, ka nasep ka mu ngei kei ding hi.

records.english: When my brother came home after five years abroad, he brought his wife with him.
records.zomi: Gamdang ah kum nga a om khit ciangin ka sanggam pasal inn a tun ciangin a zi a paipih hi.

records.english: He introduced her to the whole family at once in the kitchen.
records.zomi: An huanna ah innkuan bup kiangah khatvei-in a theisak hi.

records.english: My mother cried, hugged her, and then made her sit down and eat.
records.zomi: Ka nu a kap a, a pom a, tua ciangin a tusak a, an a nesak hi.

records.english: Where were you when your sister introduced you to her boyfriend?
records.zomi: Na sanggam nu in a lawm pasal hong theisak ciangin koi ah na om hiam?

records.english: Why did your brother wait a whole year before introducing his girlfriend to the family?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na sanggam pasal in innkuan kiangah a lawm numei theisak ma-in kum khat a ngak hiam?

records.english: Children, today I'll tell you how I first met your aunt, who came to our class as a new girl.
records.zomi: Naupangte, tuni-in i kilasi ah numei naupang thak-in a hong na ni bangci-in ka mu masa hiam kong gen ding hi.

records.english: What did your aunt say when you introduced her to your teacher?
records.zomi: Na saya kiangah na ni na theisak ciangin bang a ci hiam?

records.english: My grandmother's old address book was found in a drawer, full of names nobody recognized.
records.zomi: Ka pi' omna laibu lui bawm khat sung ah kimu a, kuamah in a theih loh minte tawh a dim hi.

records.english: I really did want my two best friends to like each other, but they argued all evening.
records.zomi: Ka lawm hoih pen nihte a kideih ding uh ka deih mahmah hi, ahi zongin nitak bup a kinial uh hi.

records.english: The letter introducing my uncle to the family in the city was written by our village headman.
records.zomi: Khuapi-a innkuan kiangah ka pa neu a theisak lai i khua makaipa in a gelh hi.

records.english: Everyone, I want you to meet the woman who taught me to read when I was forty.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, kum sawmli ka phak ciangin lai sim hong hilh numei na muh ding uh ka deih hi.

records.english: Did your grandparents ever tell you how they were introduced?
records.zomi: Na pu leh pite in bangci-in a kitheisak uh hiam hong gen ngei uh hiam?

records.english: A matchmaker from the next village introduced them, and they married three months later.
records.zomi: A kiang khua pan kiteenpih zongpa khat in a theisak a, kha thum khit ciangin a kiteen uh hi.

records.english: How did you get to know your stepfather?
records.zomi: Na pakik bangci-in na thei hiam?

records.english: They took me to the beach, and he spent the whole day building sandcastles with me.
records.zomi: Tuipi gei ah hong paipih uh a, ni bup ka tawh piaktui inn a lam hi.

records.english: Were you shy when you met your cousins from the city?
records.zomi: Khuapi pan hong na sanggamte na muh ciangin na zak hiam?

records.english: Although I had heard about him for years, meeting my grandfather's brother still felt like meeting a stranger.
records.zomi: Kum tampi sung a thu ka zak hangin ka pu' sanggam pasal muh pen mi theih loh muh bang ahi lai hi.

records.english: My little brother once introduced our new teacher to my mother as his girlfriend.
records.zomi: Ka nau pasal in khatvei ka nu kiangah i saya thak a lawm numei hi, ci-in a theisak hi.

records.english: The teacher laughed so much that she had to sit down.
records.zomi: Saya a nui lua ahih manin a tut ding a kisam hi.

records.english: He still blushes when we remind him about it.
records.zomi: Tua thu i phawksak ciangin a mai a san lai hi.

records.english: What did your friends think of your new boyfriend?
records.zomi: Na lawm pasal thak tungah na lawmte in bang a sa uh hiam?

records.english: My father introduced me to his oldest friend on a fishing trip when I was eight.
records.zomi: Kum giat ka phak ciangin nga manna khualzinna ah ka pa in a lawm lui pen hong theisak hi.

records.english: The man taught me to tie a hook, and I caught my first fish that afternoon.
records.zomi: Pasal in ngakhaih khih dan hong hilh a, tua nitak lam ah ka nga masa pen ka man hi.

records.english: Thirty years later, he spoke at my wedding.
records.zomi: Kum sawmthum khit ciangin ka mopawi ah thu a gen hi.

records.english: The photo of my parents' first meeting was lost when our house flooded.
records.zomi: I inn tui in a liam ciangin ka nu leh ka pa' kimuh masa lim a mang hi.

records.english: Remind me how you and your business partner were first introduced.
records.zomi: Nang leh na sumbawl lawm bangci-in na kitheisak masa uh hiam hong phawksak kik in.

records.english: What did your parents say when you introduced the man you wanted to marry?
records.zomi: Na kiteenpih nuam pasal na theisak ciangin na nu leh na pa in bang a ci uh hiam?

records.english: How long have you known your oldest friend?
records.zomi: Na lawm lui pen bangzah sawt na thei khin hiam?

records.english: Show me the photo of the day you met Dad.
records.zomi: Pa na muh ni lim hong etsak in.

records.english: I was introduced to my best friend's family on the night their cow gave birth.
records.zomi: Ka lawm hoih pen' bawng a suak zan-in a innkuan kiangah hong theisak uh hi.

records.english: Having been introduced at a cousin's wedding, my parents wrote to each other for two years before they married.
records.zomi: Sanggam' mopawi ah a kitheisak khit uh ciangin ka nu leh ka pa a kiteen ma-un kum nih lai a kigelh uh hi.

records.english: Did you like your sister's husband when you first met him?
records.zomi: Na sanggam nu' pasal na muh masak ciangin na deih hiam?

records.english: Who came to say hello when the new neighbors moved in?
records.zomi: Inn veng thakte a tuah ciangun kua in hopih dingin a hong hiam?

records.english: Rather than writing a letter, my uncle traveled for two days to introduce his bride to his mother in person.
records.zomi: Lai gelh sangin ka pa neu in a nu kiangah a moulai amah mah in theisak dingin ni nih a khualzin hi.

records.english: Last summer, I introduced my children to the friends I grew up with.
records.zomi: Khal nung in ka tate ka khanpih lawmte kiangah ka theisak hi.

records.english: My cousin was introduced to her future husband at a village football match.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam khua football kimawlna ah a kiteenpih ding pasal kiangah kitheisak hi.

records.english: Was your father pleased when you introduced your new friend?
records.zomi: Na lawm thak na theisak ciangin na pa a lungdam hiam?

records.english: Who introduced you to your wife?
records.zomi: Na zi kua in hong theisak hiam?

records.english: My grandparents tell us how the village looked before there was a road.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh pite in lampi a om ma-in khua bangci a om hiam hong gen uh hi.

records.english: The elders in our church sit at the front, and the young people sit behind them.
records.zomi: I pawlpi ah upate mai lam ah a tu uh a, khangnote a nung uh ah a tu uh hi.

records.english: My grandparents saved for years to send my father to school.
records.zomi: Ka pa sang kah sak dingin ka pu leh pite kum tampi sum a khol uh hi.

records.english: My grandmother teaches me the old songs while we cook together.
records.zomi: Khawm-in an i huan laitakin ka pi in la luite hong hilh hi.

records.english: Rather than telling the young people what to do, my uncle asks them what they think first.
records.zomi: Khangnote kiangah bang hih ding hiam gen sangin ka pa neu in bang a ngaihsun uh hiam a masa-in a dong hi.

records.english: Young people in our village often ask the elders for advice before they marry.
records.zomi: I khua-a khangnote in a kiteen ma-un upate kiangah thuhilhna a ngen tamzaw uh hi.

records.english: Some elders in our community worry that phones are taking the place of family conversation.
records.zomi: I mipi sung-a upa khenkhatte in phone te in innkuan kihona mun a la hi, ci-in a lungkham uh hi.

records.english: My son taught his grandmother to make video calls so that she could see her relatives abroad.
records.zomi: Gamdang-a a sanggamte a muh theih nadingin ka tapa in a pi video samna a hilh hi.

records.english: My nephew uses a phone app to record our grandfather telling his stories.
records.zomi: Ka tanau in i pu' tangthu gen aw lak dingin phone app khat a zang hi.

records.english: If young people and elders cook together, they often find more to talk about than they expected.
records.zomi: Khangnote leh upate khawm-in an a huan uh leh a lamen sangin kiho ding a mu tam zaw uh hi.

records.english: My aunt weaves cloth on an old wooden loom and is teaching my cousins how to use it.
records.zomi: Ka ni in sing puan tahna lui tungah puan a tah a, ka sanggamte a zat dan a hilh hi.

records.english: How do you show respect to your grandparents?
records.zomi: Na pu leh pite bangci-in na zahtak hiam?

records.english: The old songbook was found in my great-grandfather's trunk and given to the church choir.
records.zomi: Ka pu' pu' van bawm sung ah la laibu lui kimu a, pawlpi la sakte pawl kiangah kipia hi.

records.english: My grandparents and I sometimes disagree about music, but we laugh about it.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh pite leh kei la thu-ah khatveivei i kithukim kei a, ahi zongin i nuihza pih hi.

records.english: My little sister reads the Bible aloud to our grandmother, whose eyes are weak.
records.zomi: Ka nau nu in a mit a hat lo i pi adingin Laisiangtho ging sang takin a sim hi.

records.english: Who in your family looks after Grandpa's garden now?
records.zomi: Tu-in ka pu' huan i innkuan sung ah kua in a kem hiam?

records.english: We cooked a special meal for my grandfather's eightieth birthday so that he wouldn't have to do anything.
records.zomi: Bangmah a hih ding a kisap lo nadingin ka pu' pianni kum sawmgiat adingin an tuam khat i huan hi.

records.english: Kids, ask your grandfather about the year the river flooded the whole valley.
records.zomi: Naupangte, gun in guam bup tui a liamsak kum thu na pu dong un.

records.english: Why do the young people kneel when they greet the oldest relatives?
records.zomi: Bang hangin khangnote in sanggam upa pente a hopih ciangun a khukdin uh hiam?

records.english: Shall we ask Grandma to show us how she makes the rice cakes?
records.zomi: Buh moh a bawl dan hong etsak dingin ka pi i ngen ding hiam?

records.english: Did your grandmother teach you how to sew?
records.zomi: Na pi in puan khui dan hong hilh hiam?

records.english: Whoever is youngest at the table serves the tea to the oldest first.
records.zomi: Dawhkan-a a neu pen peuhpeuh in a upa pen kiangah a masa-in tea a pia hi.

records.english: My grandmother made each of us a blanket before we left for university.
records.zomi: Sangpi i kah ma-in ka pi in i khat ciat adingin puannak khat hong bawl sak hi.

records.english: Although the elders and the young people sometimes see things differently, they share the same love for the community.
records.zomi: Upate leh khangnote in khatveivei thu tuamtuam-in a muh hangin mipi tungah itna kibang a nei uh hi.

records.english: Is it possible to keep the old customs when so many young people move away?
records.zomi: Khangno tampi a tuah laitakin ngeina luite kem thei ding hiam?

records.english: My father learned to use a computer from my younger brother.
records.zomi: Ka pa in ka nau pasal pan computer zat dan a sin hi.

records.english: Older people in our community often say that young people learn more from listening than from talking.
records.zomi: I mipi sung-a upate in khangnote in gen sangin ngai tawh a sin tam zaw uh hi, a ci den uh hi.

records.english: It might be hard for the elders to accept that the young people want to live in the city.
records.zomi: Khangnote in khuapi ah om a deih uh, cih upate in a pom haksa kha ding uh hi.

records.english: I do want my children to know their grandparents well.
records.zomi: Ka tate in a pu leh pite uh hoih takin a theih ding uh ka deih mahmah hi.

records.english: Why do you spend every Saturday with your grandfather?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Kiginni simin na pu tawh na zang hiam?

records.english: He tells me stories about our village, and I help him in his garden.
records.zomi: I khua tangthu hong gen a, a huan ah ka huh hi.

records.english: Do your grandparents still live with you?
records.zomi: Na pu leh pite na kiang uh ah a om lai uh hiam?

records.english: Many families in our town now share a house with three generations because it helps everyone.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh a huh ahih manin i khuapi-a innkuan tampi tu-in khang thum inn khat ah a om khawm uh hi.

records.english: Had my grandfather not taught me to fish, I would never have discovered how patient I can be.
records.zomi: Ka pu in nga man dan hong hilh kei le, bangzah ka thuakzawh thei hiam ka thei ngei kei ding hi.

records.english: My grandfather says that a family is like a tree, whose roots and branches need each other.
records.zomi: Ka pu in innkuan pen singkung bang ahi a, a zung leh a ngate a kisam tuah uh hi, a ci hi.

records.english: My grandfather sometimes finds it hard to understand the jokes my friends make.
records.zomi: Ka pu in ka lawmte' nuihzat thu khatveivei a thei haksa hi.

records.english: When my grandmother fell ill, each grandchild spent one evening a week sitting with her.
records.zomi: Ka pi a dam loh ciangin tu khat ciat in kal khat ah nitak khat a kiang ah a tu uh hi.

records.english: We read to her, brushed her hair, and listened to her stories.
records.zomi: I sim sak a, a sam i khui sak a, a tangthute i ngai hi.

records.english: She said those weeks were the happiest she had known in years.
records.zomi: Tua kal te kum tampi sung a lungdam pen hun ahi hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Would you like me to teach you how to play the old drum?
records.zomi: Khuang lui tum dan kong hilh ding hiam?

records.english: Could the youth group visit the older people who live alone?
records.zomi: Amau bek a om upate khangno pawl in a veh thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: When my grandmother speaks, the younger members of the family listen without interrupting.
records.zomi: Ka pi a gen ciangin innkuan-a a neu zawte in a gen kikal ah gen lo-in a ngai uh hi.

records.english: Having grown up with three generations under one roof, my cousin finds living alone very strange.
records.zomi: Innkhum khat nuai ah khang thum tawh a khan khit ciangin ka sanggam in amah bek om a lamdang sa mahmah hi.

records.english: My grandfather shows me how to plant rice the way his father showed him.
records.zomi: Ka pu in a pa in a etsak bangin buh suan dan hong etsak hi.

records.english: My mother says that respect for elders is the first thing she wants to teach her children.
records.zomi: Upate zahtak pen a tate a hilh nuam masa pen ahi hi, ci-in ka nu in a ci hi.

records.english: My grandfather uses a small knife to carve toys for his great-grandchildren.
records.zomi: Ka pu in a tute' tute adingin namsau neu khat tawh kimawlna a ki hi.

records.english: We visit my great-grandmother every Sunday, even though she lives an hour away.
records.zomi: Nai khat gamla ah a om hangin Nipini simin ka pi' nu i veh hi.

records.english: In our family, the grandchildren bring water to the grandparents before anyone else in the morning.
records.zomi: I innkuan ah zingsangin tute in kuamah dang ma-in pu leh pite kiangah tui a tawi uh hi.

records.english: Could you help Grandpa carry the firewood into the kitchen?
records.zomi: An huanna ah sing pua lut dingin ka pu na huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Where do the elders of the village meet?
records.zomi: Khua upate koi ah a kikhawm uh hiam?

records.english: Children, please give your seats to the older guests when they arrive.
records.zomi: Naupangte, khual upate a tun ciangun na tutna uh pia un.

records.english: Which of your grandparents tells the best stories?
records.zomi: Na pu leh pite lak ah kua in tangthu a gen hoih pen hiam?

records.english: The longer I lived with my grandparents, the better I understood why my parents are the way they are.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh pite kiang ah ka om sawt semsem ciangin ka nu leh ka pa bang hangin tua bangin a om uh hiam ka thei semsem hi.

records.english: The young people in our church help the elders to read their letters and fill in forms.
records.zomi: I pawlpi-a khangnote in upate a lai uh sim leh form gelh dingin a huh uh hi.

records.english: What have you learned from your grandparents?
records.zomi: Na pu leh pite pan bang na sin hiam?

records.english: What my grandmother values most is that her grandchildren still come to her for advice.
records.zomi: Ka pi in a manphat sak pen pen a tute in thuhilhna ngen dingin a kiang ah a hong lai uh hi, cih ahi hi.

records.english: Every New Year, the oldest person in our family blesses each of the grandchildren.
records.zomi: Kum thak simin i innkuan-a a upa pen in tu khat ciat thupha a pia hi.

records.english: Wouldn't it help if the young people taught the elders to use the internet in exchange for lessons in weaving?
records.zomi: Khangnote in puan tah hilhna tawh kilai-in upate internet zat dan a hilh uh leh a huh ding hi lo hiam?

records.english: When did you last call your grandmother?
records.zomi: Na pi na sam nunung bang ciang ahi hiam?

records.english: Tell your grandmother what you learned at school today, because she loves hearing about it.
records.zomi: Na pi in a zak a deih mahmah ahih manin tuni-in sang ah na sin a hilh in.

records.english: Welcoming those visitors was like opening a window in a stuffy room, because they brought new ideas with them.
records.zomi: Tua khual hongte muak pen huih om lo khan ah tukvuang hon bang ahi a, ngaihsutna thak a tawi uh hi.

records.english: The visitors were shown around the new school by the oldest pupils.
records.zomi: Sang thak kim ah khual hongte sangnaupang upa pente in a paipih uh hi.

records.english: Having driven through the night, the visitors fell asleep before dinner was even served.
records.zomi: Zan bup a mawng khit uh ciangin nitak an a kipiak ma-in khual hongte a ihmu uh hi.

records.english: Had we known the visitors were coming, we would have prepared a proper meal.
records.zomi: Khual hongte a hong ding uh i theih le, an kicing i bawl ding hi.

records.english: One winter evening, two travelers knocked on our door because the snow had blocked the road.
records.zomi: Khuavot nitak khat vuk in lampi a khak ahih manin khualzin nih i kongkhak a kiu uh hi.

records.english: We gave the travelers dry clothes and a mattress by the stove.
records.zomi: Khualzinte puan keu leh meikhuk kiang ah mattress khat i pia hi.

records.english: In the morning, they shoveled our path before they left, to thank us.
records.zomi: Zingsangin a pai ma-un lungdam gen dingin i lampi-a vuk a phiat sak uh hi.

records.english: Who was the first visitor you ever welcomed to your new home?
records.zomi: Na inn thak ah na muak masa pen khual kua ahi hiam?

records.english: Our old neighbor, who brought a loaf of bread and a bag of salt for luck.
records.zomi: I inn veng lui, vangphatna adingin moh leh cii ip khat a tawi pa.

records.english: Rather than staying in a hotel, the visiting choir slept in families' homes across the village.
records.zomi: Zinbuuk ah om sangin hong veh la sakte pawl khua bup-a innkuante' inn ah a ihmu uh hi.

records.english: The welcome cake was dropped on the doorstep just as the guests arrived.
records.zomi: Khualte a tun laitakun kongkhak mai ah muakna cake a kia hi.

records.english: How did your village welcome the first car that ever drove up the hill?
records.zomi: Mual tung a kah masa pen mawtaw na khua in bangci-in a muak uh hiam?

records.english: Everyone came out to look at the car, and the children ran behind it all the way to the church.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh mawtaw en dingin a pai khia uh a, naupangte pawlpi dong a nung ah a tai uh hi.

records.english: Last year, a group of students cycled through our town on their way to the coast.
records.zomi: Kum nung in sangnaupang pawl khat tuipi gei lam a pai ding siiksakol tawh i khuapi a kan uh hi.

records.english: The town hall opened its doors so that the students could sleep on the floor.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte tual ah a ihmut theih nadingun khuapi inn in a kongkhak a hong hi.

records.english: Some of the families cooked breakfast for all thirty of the students the next morning.
records.zomi: A zing zingsangin innkuan khenkhatte in sangnaupang sawmthum khempeuh adingin zingsang an a huan uh hi.

records.english: Why did your grandparents keep a bed ready for unexpected visitors?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na pu leh pite in theih loh-a hong khualte adingin lupna khat a kem khol tawntung uh hiam?

records.english: Did you ever welcome a stranger into your home?
records.zomi: Na inn ah mi theih loh khat na muak ngei hiam?

records.english: Shall I tell you about the day the president's car drove through our town?
records.zomi: President' mawtaw i khuapi a pai khak ni thu kong gen ding hiam?

records.english: When a team of doctors visited our village, the women cooked for them for three days.
records.zomi: Siavuan pawl khat i khua a veh ciangin numeite in ni thum sung an a huan sak uh hi.

records.english: The doctors were so well fed that they joked about needing a doctor themselves.
records.zomi: Siavuante an a ngah tam lua ahih manin amaute zong siavuan a kisam ding uh hi, ci-in a nuihza uh hi.

records.english: The next year, the same doctors came back and asked for the same chicken soup.
records.zomi: A zom kum ciangin siavuan kibang mah a hong kik uh a, aksa tui kibang a ngen uh hi.

records.english: When my cousin brought her husband home from abroad, he was terrified of our big dog.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam in gamdang pan a pasal inn ah a paipih ciangin i ui lian a lau mahmah hi.

records.english: Our aunt introduced the dog to him slowly, keeping it on a lead.
records.zomi: I ni in ui khau tawh khih-in zawl takin a kiangah a theisak hi.

records.english: By the end of the week, the dog was sleeping at the cousin's husband's feet.
records.zomi: Kal tawp ciangin ui ka sanggam' pasal' khe kiang ah a ihmu hi.

records.english: What did the children sing for the visiting bishop?
records.zomi: Hong veh bishop adingin naupangte in bang la a sa uh hiam?

records.english: I really did want the visitors to feel at home, so I learned a few words of their language.
records.zomi: Khual hongte inn bangin a kisak ding uh ka deih mahmah ahih manin a pau uh kammal tawmno ka sin hi.

records.english: The more often the volunteers came back, the more they felt like part of our family.
records.zomi: Thalawpte a hong kik den semsem ciangin i innkuan sung-a mi bangin a kisa semsem uh hi.

records.english: Years ago, our family welcomed an exchange student from Japan for a whole school year.
records.zomi: Kum tampi paisa-in i innkuan in sang kum bup Japan pan sangnaupang khat a muak hi.

records.english: At first, the exchange student was too shy to ask for a second helping at dinner.
records.zomi: A masa-in sangnaupang in nitak an ah a nihna ngen dingin a zak lua hi.

records.english: By the end of the year, she was teaching my little brother to cook rice her way.
records.zomi: Kum tawp ciangin ka nau pasal amah' dan in buh huan dan a hilh hi.

records.english: Did the visitors bring you any presents?
records.zomi: Khual hongte in letsong bangmah hong tawi sak uh hiam?

records.english: Although the visitors spoke a different language, they understood our welcome perfectly.
records.zomi: Khual hongte in pau dang a gen uh hangin i muakna a thei kim uh hi.

records.english: What I remember most about that visit is how our guests helped us with the harvest.
records.zomi: Tua vehna ah ka phawk pen pen i khualte in buh lak ah hong huh uh hi, cih ahi hi.

records.english: Which visitor do you remember best from your childhood?
records.zomi: Na naupan lai pan koi khual hong na phawk pen hiam?

records.english: Who cooked for the visitors when your grandmother was ill?
records.zomi: Na pi a dam loh ciangin khual hongte adingin kua in an a huan hiam?

records.english: Last spring, my brother welcomed his old schoolfriend after twenty years apart.
records.zomi: Kum nung spring in ka sanggam pasal in kum sawmnih kikhen khit ciangin a sang lawm lui a muak hi.

records.english: Whoever saw the visitors first ran to ring the church bell.
records.zomi: Khual hongte a mu masa peuhpeuh in pawlpi khawngging tum dingin a tai hi.

records.english: We used a hand-painted sign to show the visitors the way to the school.
records.zomi: Khual hongte sang lampi etsak dingin khut tawh zeek lai khat i zang hi.

records.english: Every family gave the new pastor something from their garden.
records.zomi: Innkuan khempeuh in pastor thak kiangah a huan pan bangmah a pia uh hi.

records.english: Our grandmother's old guest book is full of names from forty years of visitors.
records.zomi: I pi' khual laibu lui kum sawmli sung khual hongte' min tawh a dim hi.

records.english: A blind visitor came to our church last spring, and my sister guided her to a seat by the window.
records.zomi: Kum nung spring in mitcip khual khat i pawlpi ah a hong a, ka sanggam nu in tukvuang kiang-a tutna ah a paipih hi.

records.english: Our guests' car got stuck in the mud at the bottom of the hill.
records.zomi: I khualte' mawtaw mual nuai-a bual sung ah a tang hi.

records.english: The whole family went down with ropes and pulled the car out.
records.zomi: Innkuan bup khau tawh a tum uh a, mawtaw a kai khia uh hi.

records.english: Kids, I'll tell you about the day a famous singer stopped at our village shop.
records.zomi: Naupangte, la sak min thang khat i khua dawr ah a tawl ni thu kong gen ding hi.

records.english: When my uncle came home from the army, the whole street was waiting outside our gate.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu galkap pan inn a ciah ciangin lampi bup i kongpi pua ah a ngak uh hi.

records.english: The neighbors had hung a banner across the road with his name on it.
records.zomi: Inn vengte in lampi tungah a min kigelh puan lian khat a khai uh hi.

records.english: My uncle stood in the street and cried before he could even reach the door.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu kongkhak a tun ma-in lampi ah a ding a, a kap hi.

records.english: The school inspector was welcomed with a song that the children had practiced for weeks.
records.zomi: Sang enkaktu kal tampi naupangte' kisin la tawh kimuak hi.

records.english: Do you remember the day the bishop arrived without warning?
records.zomi: Bishop gen lo-in a tun ni na phawk hiam?

records.english: Our grandmother served him tea in her old dressing gown and never let anyone forget it.
records.zomi: I pi in a lupna puan lui tawh tea a pia a, kuamah a mangngilhsak ngei kei hi.

records.english: Where did the visitors sleep when the house was full?
records.zomi: Inn a dim ciangin khual hongte koi ah a ihmu uh hiam?

records.english: However tired our guests were, they always asked to help with the washing up.
records.zomi: I khualte bangzah ta in tawl zongun kuang sil a huh dingin a ngen tawntung uh hi.

records.english: When did the first foreign visitor come to your village?
records.zomi: Na khua ah gamdang khual masa pen bang ciangin a hong hiam?

records.english: Would the visit have gone so well if the whole village hadn't helped?
records.zomi: Khua bup in a huh kei le, vehna tua bang hoih takin a pai ding hiam?

records.english: Could you have imagined, back then, that the visitors would become lifelong friends?
records.zomi: Tua hun-in khual hongte nuntak sung lawm a suak ding uh hi, cih na ngaihsun thei ding hiam?
