records.english: It might have been the warmest welcome the old teacher had ever received.
records.zomi: Tua pen saya lui in a ngah ngei muakna lum pen hi kha ding hi.

records.english: Was the house always this busy when you were young?
records.zomi: Na neu lai-in inn hih bangin a buai tawntung hiam?

records.english: Our grandfather once invited a tired delivery man in for tea, and the man stayed for dinner.
records.zomi: Ka pu in khatvei a tawl van puak pa khat tea dawn dingin a sam a, nitak an dong a om hi.

records.english: Everyone, gather at the gate, because the bus from the city will arrive any minute.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, khuapi pan bus a hong tung ding ahih manin kongpi ah kikhawm un.

records.english: It might have been easier to leave if the children hadn't run after the car.
records.zomi: Naupangte mawtaw nung ah a tai kei uh le, pai khiat a baih zaw kha ding hi.

records.english: What did the blacksmith make for each child before he closed the forge?
records.zomi: Thih bawlpa in a thih inn a khak ma-in naupang khat ciat adingin bang a bawl hiam?

records.english: Before my cousin left for military service, his friends painted his name on the village wall.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam galkap nasep a pai ma-in a lawmte in khua bang tungah a min a zeek uh hi.

records.english: The farewell party for our neighbor was held in the church hall, and nearly a hundred people came.
records.zomi: I inn veng' kikhenna pawi pawlpi inn ah kibawl a, mi za khat dek a hong uh hi.

records.english: Last summer I said goodbye to my childhood home when my parents sold it.
records.zomi: Khal nung in ka nu leh ka pa in a zuak ciangin ka naupan lai inn kiangah goodbye ka ci hi.

records.english: On the last morning before the old bus driver retired, the whole school waited at the stop.
records.zomi: Bus mawngpa upa a nasep a tawp ma zingsang nunung pen-in sang bup dinna ah a ngak uh hi.

records.english: The children had made the driver a card signed by every pupil he had ever driven.
records.zomi: Naupangte in a tuangsak ngei sangnaupang khempeuh min a suaksak card khat mawngpa adingin a bawl uh hi.

records.english: The bus driver kept the card on his kitchen wall for the rest of his life.
records.zomi: Bus mawngpa in a nuntak sung bup card an huanna bang tungah a kem hi.

records.english: Why did your brother leave without telling anyone?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na sanggam pasal kuamah hilh lo-in a pai khia hiam?

records.english: Where did you say goodbye to your brother before he went abroad?
records.zomi: Gamdang a pai ma-in na sanggam pasal kiangah koi ah goodbye na ci hiam?

records.english: The old ferry made its final crossing, and the whole town stood on the shore to watch.
records.zomi: Long lui in a kanna nunung pen a bawl a, khuapi bup en dingin tuipi gei ah a ding uh hi.

records.english: Tell me about the day you left for the city.
records.zomi: Khuapi lam na pai ni thu hong gen in.

records.english: Children, take a last look at the classroom, because next year you'll be in the new building.
records.zomi: Naupangte, kum zom ciangin inn thak ah na om ding uh ahih manin kilasi a nunung pen-in en un.

records.english: Whoever left the village first had to ring the old bell at the crossroads.
records.zomi: Khua a nusia masa peuhpeuh in lampi kituahna-a khawngging lui a tum ding hi.

records.english: My uncle used his old camera to take one last photo of the house before we moved.
records.zomi: I tuah ma-in ka pa neu in a camera lui tawh inn lim nunung pen khat a la hi.

records.english: When our village blacksmith grew too old to work, he closed his forge and moved to his son's home in the city.
records.zomi: I khua thih bawlpa a upat lua-in a sep zawh nawn loh ciangin a thih inn a khak a, khuapi-a a tapa' inn ah a tuah hi.

records.english: Every family came to the forge to say goodbye, carrying fruit and eggs.
records.zomi: Innkuan khempeuh theigah leh aktui tawi-in goodbye ci dingin thih inn ah a hong uh hi.

records.english: The blacksmith couldn't take all the gifts, so he gave most of them to the school kitchen.
records.zomi: Thih bawlpa in letsong khempeuh a la zo kei ahih manin a tamzaw sang an huanna kiangah a pia hi.

records.english: However far away I live, I still call my grandmother every Sunday evening.
records.zomi: Bangzah ta in gamla ah om zongin Nipini nitak simin ka pi ka sam lai hi.

records.english: What did you take with you when you left your village?
records.zomi: Na khua na nusiat ciangin bang na tawi hiam?

records.english: Only a small bag of clothes and a photo of my parents.
records.zomi: Puan ip neu khat leh ka nu leh ka pa' lim khat bek.

records.english: I really did want to say goodbye to my best friend, but her family left before dawn.
records.zomi: Ka lawm hoih pen kiangah goodbye ci ka deih mahmah hi, ahi zongin a innkuan khuavak ma-in a pai khia uh hi.

records.english: A week later, a letter arrived from her with a drawing of the two of us.
records.zomi: Kal khat khit ciangin i nih lim gelh tawh amah pan lai khat a hong tung hi.

records.english: Would you have stayed if the factory hadn't closed?
records.zomi: Factory a kikhak kei le, na om ding hiam?

records.english: Which of your friends wrote to you most after you moved?
records.zomi: Na tuah khit ciangin na lawmte lak ah kua in lai hong gelh tam pen hiam?

records.english: My cousin's goodbye message was read aloud at the end of the service.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam' goodbye thu pawlpi kikhopna tawp ciangin ging sang takin kisim hi.

records.english: What I remember most about leaving home is the silence in the car.
records.zomi: Inn nusiatna ah ka phawk pen pen mawtaw sung-a daihna ahi hi.

records.english: On the last day before the old school building was pulled down, the teachers let us write on the walls.
records.zomi: Sang inn lui a kisuksiat ma ni nunung pen-in sayate in bang tungah gelh dingin hong phal uh hi.

records.english: We wrote our names, our dreams, and the names of our favorite teachers.
records.zomi: I min, i lametnate, leh i deih pen sayate' min i gelh hi.

records.english: A photographer from the town took pictures of every wall before the builders came.
records.zomi: Khuapi pan lim la khat in inn lamte a hong ma-un bang khempeuh lim a la hi.

records.english: The longer the farewell speeches went on, the more the old carpenter wanted to escape.
records.zomi: Kikhenna thugente a sau semsem ciangin sing seemmi upa in pai khiat a deih semsem hi.

records.english: When did you last see your old school friends?
records.zomi: Na sang lawm luite na muh nunung bang ciang ahi hiam?

records.english: Although we promised to stay in touch, my school friends and I slowly lost contact.
records.zomi: Kizom den dingin i kiciam hangin ka sang lawmte leh kei zawl takin i kizopna a mang hi.

records.english: The farewell cake was made by the pupils in the cookery class.
records.zomi: Kikhenna cake an huan kilasi-a sangnaupangte in a bawl uh hi.

records.english: My brother wrote a song for his friends before he moved abroad, and he played it at the farewell dinner.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal gamdang a tuah ma-in a lawmte adingin la khat a phuak a, kikhenna nitak an ah a sa hi.

records.english: Who drove you to the station when you left home for the first time?
records.zomi: Inn na nusiat masa pen-in meileng dinna ah kua in hong paipih hiam?

records.english: My aunt, who cried so much that I had to comfort her instead.
records.zomi: Ka ni, a kap lua ahih manin tua sangin keimah in ka hehnem ding a kisam hi.

records.english: Having packed everything into one small suitcase, my cousin was surprised by how little she really needed.
records.zomi: Van bawm neu khat sung ah khempeuh a thuk khit ciangin ka sanggam in bangzah tawmno a kisap taktak hiam a lamdang sa hi.

records.english: Leaving my hometown felt like closing a favorite book before the last chapter.
records.zomi: Ka khua nusiat pen khen nunung ma-in laibu deih pen khat khak bang ahi hi.

records.english: Had I known it was my last visit to my grandmother, I would have stayed another week.
records.zomi: Ka pi ka veh nunung pen ahi hi, cih ka theih le, kal khat behlap ka om ding hi.

records.english: Was it hard to leave the city after so many years?
records.zomi: Kum tampi khit ciangin khuapi nusia a haksa hiam?

records.english: How did your grandfather say goodbye when the grandchildren went home?
records.zomi: Tute inn a ciah ciangun na pu in bangci-in goodbye a ci hiam?

records.english: He pressed a coin into each child's hand and told us to buy something sweet.
records.zomi: Naupang khat ciat' khut sung ah dangka khat a koih a, an lim lei dingin hong hilh hi.

records.english: When our family sold the farm, my grandfather walked around every field one last time.
records.zomi: I innkuan in lo a zuak ciangin ka pu in a nunung pen-in lo khempeuh a kim a vak hi.

records.english: He touched each of the old mango trees as if he were saying goodbye to friends.
records.zomi: Haigah kung lui khempeuh lawmte kiangah goodbye ci bangin a khoih hi.

records.english: Then he got into the truck and never once looked back.
records.zomi: Tua ciangin mawtaw lian tungah a tuang a, khatvei zong nung lam a en kei hi.

records.english: Shall I tell you what your great-grandfather said before he left for the war?
records.zomi: Na pi' pa gal ah a pai ma-in bang a ci hiam kong gen ding hiam?

records.english: We once nursed an injured bird back to health in a shoebox.
records.zomi: Khatvei khedap bawm sung ah liam vasa khat a dam dong i kem hi.

records.english: When its wing healed, my little brother carried it to the garden.
records.zomi: A kha a dam ciangin ka nau pasal in huan ah a pua hi.

records.english: He opened his hands, and the bird flew straight up into the tree.
records.zomi: A khut a hon a, vasa singkung tung ah a tang takin a leng hi.

records.english: Rather than a big party, our teacher asked for a quiet lunch with her class on her last day.
records.zomi: Pawi lian sangin i saya in a ni nunung pen-in a kilasi tawh sun an dai khat a ngen hi.

records.english: Everyone, please sign this photo for Mr. Khai before he retires.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, Mr. Khai a nasep a tawp ma-in hih lim tungah min suaksak un.

records.english: How long did the farewell party last?
records.zomi: Kikhenna pawi bangzah sawt a om hiam?

records.english: Did your grandparents come to see you off at the airport?
records.zomi: Na pu leh pite vanlengtual ah hong paisak dingin a hong uh hiam?

records.english: Did anyone cry at your farewell party?
records.zomi: Na kikhenna pawi ah kuamah a kap hiam?

records.english: Who looked after your cat when you moved away?
records.zomi: Na tuah ciangin na zawh kua in a kem hiam?

records.english: Why did your grandmother always stand at the gate until the car was out of sight?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na pi mawtaw a mang dong kongpi ah a ding tawntung hiam?

records.english: Do you remember the letter you found in your suitcase when you left for university?
records.zomi: Sangpi na pai ciangin na van bawm sung-a na muh lai na phawk hiam?

records.english: My grandmother had hidden it under my clothes, and I read it on the bus.
records.zomi: Ka pi in ka puan nuai ah a sel a, bus tungah ka sim hi.

records.english: Could the school have kept the old building as a library instead of pulling it down?
records.zomi: Sang in inn lui susia sangin laibu inn bangin a kem thei ding hiam?

records.english: Was your grandmother strict with her children?
records.zomi: Na pi a tate tungah a khauh hiam?

records.english: What did your grandfather do when the children were naughty?
records.zomi: Naupangte a gitlo ciangun na pu in bang a hih hiam?

records.english: My nephew was named after his great-grandfather, whom he never met.
records.zomi: Ka tanau a muh ngei loh a pu' pa' min tawh kiphuak hi.

records.english: My cousin and I fought over one bicycle every summer until my uncle bought a second one.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in a nihna khat a lei dong khal simin ka sanggam leh kei siiksakol khat thu-ah i kido hi.

records.english: How did your family celebrate when your little brother was born?
records.zomi: Na nau pasal a suah ciangin na innkuan in bangci-in pawi a bawl uh hiam?

records.english: It might have been easier for my mother if she had had a sister to help her.
records.zomi: Ka nu in huh dingin sanggam nu khat a neih le a baih zaw kha ding hi.

records.english: The old family Bible was passed from my great-grandmother to my aunt.
records.zomi: Innkuan Laisiangtho lui ka pi' nu pan ka ni kiangah kipia hi.

records.english: Rather than dividing the land, the four brothers decided to farm it together.
records.zomi: Leitang khen sangin sanggam pasal lite in khawm-in lo bawl dingin a khensat uh hi.

records.english: I really did want to know my half-brother, but I was too nervous to call him.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal pa kibang lo theih ka deih mahmah hi, ahi zongin sam dingin ka lau lua hi.

records.english: When we finally met at a café, we talked for four hours and discovered we laughed the same way.
records.zomi: A tawp-in cafe khat ah i kimuh ciangin nai li i kiho a, kibang takin i nui hi, cih i thei hi.

records.english: Did you share a bedroom with your brothers?
records.zomi: Na sanggam pasalte tawh lupna khan na kihawm uh hiam?

records.english: For years, our family lost touch with my grandmother's younger brother.
records.zomi: Kum tampi sung i innkuan in ka pi' nau pasal tawh kizopna a mang hi.

records.english: Then my cousin found his old letters in a trunk and wrote to the address on the envelope.
records.zomi: Tua ciangin ka sanggam in van bawm sung ah a lai luite a mu a, lai ip tung-a omna ah a gelh hi.

records.english: Six months later, the two families sat down together for the first time in forty years.
records.zomi: Kha guk khit ciangin innkuan nihte kum sawmli sung ah a masa pen-in khawm-in a tu uh hi.

records.english: Tell me about the cousin you spent every summer with.
records.zomi: Khal simin na zat khawm na sanggam thu hong gen in.

records.english: Why did your brother move in with your grandparents?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na sanggam pasal na pu leh pite kiang ah a tuah hiam?

records.english: Could you have managed university without your older sister's help?
records.zomi: Na u nu' huhna om lo-in sangpi na zo thei ding hiam?

records.english: Which relative taught you the most when you were small?
records.zomi: Na neu lai-in koi sanggam in hong hilh tam pen hiam?

records.english: My aunt, who let me help in her bakery every Saturday morning.
records.zomi: Ka ni, Kiginni zingsang simin a moh bawlna ah huh dingin hong phal pa.

records.english: My uncle used his carpentry tools to build a wooden cradle for every baby in the family.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in innkuan sung-a naungek khempeuh adingin a sing nasepna van tawh sing naungek lupna a bawl hi.

records.english: For a school project, my daughter drew our family tree on a long roll of paper.
records.zomi: Sang project adingin ka tanu in laipek sau tungah i innkuan singkung a gelh hi.

records.english: She phoned every relative to ask about their parents and grandparents.
records.zomi: Sanggam khempeuh a nu leh pa uh leh a pu leh pite uh thu dong dingin a sam hi.

records.english: The finished family tree now hangs in my grandmother's hallway.
records.zomi: A zo innkuan singkung tu-in ka pi' inn lam ah kikhai hi.

records.english: When did you last see your cousins from the city?
records.zomi: Khuapi pan na sanggamte na muh nunung bang ciang ahi hiam?

records.english: Wouldn't it be wonderful to bring all the cousins together again, as we did when we were young?
records.zomi: I neu lai-a i hih bangin sanggamte khempeuh kik-in kaikhawm a nuam mahmah ding hi lo hiam?

records.english: Shall I show you the letters your grandfather wrote to your grandmother?
records.zomi: Na pu in na pi kiangah a gelh laite kong etsak ding hiam?

records.english: Years ago, my two uncles both claimed the same plot of land by the river.
records.zomi: Kum tampi paisa-in ka pa neu nihte in gun kiang-a leitang khat a kineih uh hi.

records.english: At their mother's ninetieth birthday, she asked them to carry her cake together.
records.zomi: A nu uh' pianni kum sawmkua-in a cake khawm-in pua dingin a ngen hi.

records.english: They shook hands over the cake, and nobody ever mentioned the argument again.
records.zomi: Cake tungah a khut a kilen uh a, kuamah in kinialna a gen nawn ngei kei hi.

records.english: Do you remember how your family nickname started?
records.zomi: Na innkuan min neu bangci-in a kipan hiam na phawk hiam?

records.english: My grandfather called me "little owl" because I never wanted to go to sleep.
records.zomi: Ihmu ka deih ngei kei ahih manin ka pu in “zuh neu” hong ci hi.

records.english: Why did your grandparents raise your cousin as their own son?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na pu leh pite in na sanggam a tapa uh bangin a khoi uh hiam?

records.english: His parents worked abroad for many years, so he grew up in our house as my brother.
records.zomi: A nu leh pa kum tampi sung gamdang ah a sem uh ahih manin i inn ah ka sanggam pasal bangin a khang hi.

records.english: Did your grandparents ever tell you about their own brothers and sisters?
records.zomi: Na pu leh pite in amau sanggamte thu hong gen ngei uh hiam?

records.english: What I remember most about my grandfather is the way he whistled while he worked.
records.zomi: Ka pu tungah ka phawk pen pen a sep laitakin a kam tawh a mut dan ahi hi.

records.english: When my younger sister was born, I was jealous of all the attention she received.
records.zomi: Ka nau nu a suah ciangin a ngah phawkna khempeuh tungah ka hazat hi.

records.english: My grandmother gave me the job of choosing the baby's clothes each morning.
records.zomi: Ka pi in zingsang simin naungek' puan teel nasep hong pia hi.

records.english: After that, I felt proud to be the big sister.
records.zomi: Tua khit ciangin u nu hih ka kisathei hi.

records.english: Our family photo album was kept in a tin box so that the pages wouldn't get damp.
records.zomi: I innkuan lim bu laimaite a nawng lo nadingin thih bawm khat sung ah kikem hi.

records.english: Last summer, my brother and I painted our parents' house as a surprise.
records.zomi: Khal nung in ka sanggam pasal leh kei lamdang a sak nadingin i nu leh pa' inn i zeek hi.

records.english: The more my sister and I argued as children, the closer we seem to be now.
records.zomi: Naupan lai-in ka sanggam nu leh kei i kinial tam semsem bangin tu-in i kinai semsem bang hi.

records.english: Where did your grandparents live when your mother was a child?
records.zomi: Na nu naupang a hih lai-in na pu leh pite koi ah a om uh hiam?

records.english: Although my cousin lived far away, she wrote to me every month for twenty years.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam gamla ah a om hangin kum sawmnih sung kha simin lai hong gelh hi.

records.english: Had my brother not lent me his savings, I could never have opened my shop.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in a khol sum hong ngetsak kei le, ka dawr ka hong thei ngei kei ding hi.

records.english: When I was ten, my oldest sister left school to work in a shop so that my brothers and I could study.
records.zomi: Kum sawm ka phak ciangin ka u nu upa pen in ka sanggam pasalte leh kei i sin theih nadingun sang a nusia a, dawr ah a sem hi.

records.english: She sent part of her wages home every month for eight years.
records.zomi: Kum giat sung kha simin a nasep man khenkhat inn ah a khak hi.

records.english: At my graduation, I gave my oldest sister the first copy of my certificate.
records.zomi: Ka sang zawhna pawi ah ka u nu upa pen ka certificate copy masa pen ka pia hi.

records.english: Our grandfather wrote a letter to each grandchild on their eighteenth birthday.
records.zomi: I pu in tu khat ciat' pianni kum sawm leh giat-in lai khat a gelh hi.

records.english: When my parents worked late, my older brother cooked dinner for the three of us.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa a nai-in a sep ciangun ka u pasal in i thum adingin nitak an a huan hi.

records.english: However busy she was, my grandmother found time to listen to each of us.
records.zomi: Bangzah ta in buai zongin ka pi in i khat ciat ngai dingin hun a mu hi.

records.english: Everyone, come and see the photo of all five generations of our family.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, i innkuan khang nga khempeuh' lim en dingin hong pai un.

records.english: Children, I'll tell you how your grandparents met at the village well.
records.zomi: Naupangte, na pu leh pite khua tuikhuk ah bangci-in a kimu uh hiam kong gen ding hi.

records.english: Would your father have become a teacher if his family hadn't needed him on the farm?
records.zomi: A innkuan in lo ah a kisap kei le, na pa saya a suak ding hiam?

records.english: Having been raised by her grandmother, my aunt always said she had two mothers.
records.zomi: A pi in a khoi khit ciangin ka ni in nu nih ka nei hi, a ci tawntung hi.

records.english: Which of your aunts taught you to cook?
records.zomi: Na nite lak ah kua in an huan hong hilh hiam?

records.english: My twin brother and I once swapped places for a whole day at school.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal apeng leh kei khatvei sang ah ni bup i kikhel hi.

records.english: Our teacher didn't notice until my brother answered a math question correctly.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in math dotna khat a dik takin a dawn dong i saya in a thei kei hi.

records.english: The teacher laughed and made us sit at opposite ends of the room for the rest of the year.
records.zomi: Saya a nui a, kum bup khan tawp nih ah hong tusak hi.

records.english: Growing up with seven cousins in one house was like living in a small, noisy village.
records.zomi: Inn khat sung ah sanggam sagih tawh khan pen khua neu ging tak sung ah om bang ahi hi.

records.english: Whoever was oldest at the table in our grandparents' house was always served first.
records.zomi: I pu leh pite' inn ah dawhkan-a a upa pen a masa-in kipia tawntung hi.

records.english: When my wife was in hospital for a month, I had to learn to braid our daughter's hair.
records.zomi: Ka zi kha khat zato ah a om ciangin i tanu' sam khih ka sin ding a kisam hi.

records.english: The first braid was so crooked that my daughter refused to go to school.
records.zomi: Khihna masa pen a kawi lua ahih manin ka tanu in sang pai a nial hi.

records.english: By the end of the month, the other girls were asking me to braid theirs too.
records.zomi: Kha tawp ciangin numei naupang dangte in amau' zong khih sak dingin hong ngen uh hi.

records.english: How many guests came to your wedding?
records.zomi: Na mopawi ah khual bangzah a hong uh hiam?

records.english: Which of your children was the noisiest as a baby?
records.zomi: Na tate lak ah kua in naungek a hih lai-in a ging pen hiam?

records.english: My husband taught our son to ride a bicycle on the empty road behind the church.
records.zomi: Ka pasal in i tapa pawlpi nung-a lampi awng tungah siiksakol tuang dan a hilh hi.

records.english: What was the hardest thing about raising children in the city?
records.zomi: Khuapi ah naupang khoi ah a haksa pen bang ahi hiam?

records.english: Finding a safe place for them to play, because there was so much traffic.
records.zomi: A kimawl nadingun mun bit zon, mawtaw a tam mahmah ahih manin.

records.english: What I remember most about my parents' marriage is how they laughed together in the kitchen.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa' kiteenna ah ka phawk pen pen an huanna ah khawm-in a nui dan uh ahi hi.

records.english: Do you remember the day our son got lost at the market?
records.zomi: I tapa zuakna mun ah a mang ni na phawk hiam?

records.english: A fruit seller kept him on her stall with a mango until we found him.
records.zomi: Theigah zuak numei khat in i muh dong haigah khat tawh a zuakna mun ah a kem hi.

records.english: It might have been easier to stay in the village, but we wanted our children to see more of the world.
records.zomi: Khua ah om a baih zaw kha ding hi, ahi zongin i tate in leitung a tam zaw muh ding uh i deih hi.

records.english: Whoever finished their homework first was allowed to choose the radio station in our house.
records.zomi: I inn ah a inn-a sep ding a zo masa peuhpeuh in radio a teel thei hi.

records.english: Having raised five children on a farmer's income, my grandmother never wasted a single grain of rice.
records.zomi: Lo nei' sum ngah tawh ta nga a khoi khit ciangin ka pi in buh mal khat zong a paai ngei kei hi.

records.english: Why did you decide to have only two children?
records.zomi: Bang hangin ta nih bek nei dingin na khensat hiam?

records.english: Where did you and your husband live when you were first married?
records.zomi: Nang leh na pasal na kiteen thak lai-un koi ah na om uh hiam?

records.english: What did your husband do the first time the baby was sick?
records.zomi: Naungek a dam loh masak ciangin na pasal in bang a hih hiam?

records.english: When our first baby was born, neither of us knew how to bathe her.
records.zomi: I naungek masa pen a suah ciangin i nih un bangci-in kisilsak ding hiam i thei kei hi.

records.english: An older neighbor showed us how, using a plastic bowl and a soft towel.
records.zomi: Inn veng upa khat in plastic kuang leh puan nul nem khat zang-in hong etsak hi.

records.english: Now our daughter laughs when we tell her how frightened we were of her tiny arms.
records.zomi: Tu-in a ban neute bangzah i lau hiam i gen ciangin i tanu a nui hi.

records.english: Everyone, raise your glasses to the couple who have been married for sixty years.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, kum sawmguk sung kiteen nihte adingin na haai uh lap un.

records.english: The cot that my husband made for our first child has been used by all seven grandchildren.
records.zomi: I ta masa pen adingin ka pasal' bawl naungek lupna tu sagih khempeuh in a zang uh hi.

records.english: The more children my grandparents had, the bigger their table seemed to grow.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh pite in ta a neih tam semsem ciangin a dawhkan a lian semsem bang hi.

records.english: Rather than buying a car, my parents saved the money for our education.
records.zomi: Mawtaw lei sangin ka nu leh ka pa in i laisinna adingin sum a khol uh hi.

records.english: Wouldn't it be lovely to show the grandchildren where we lived as newlyweds?
records.zomi: Kiteen thak i hih lai-a i omna tute i etsak leh a nuam mahmah ding hi lo hiam?

records.english: Children, sit down, and I'll tell you about the day your grandfather asked for your grandmother's hand.
records.zomi: Naupangte, tu un, na pu in na pi a ngen ni thu kong gen ding hi.

records.english: Why did your parents get married in the rainy season?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na nu leh na pa guah hun ah a kiteen uh hiam?

records.english: When my sister died, my husband and I adopted her two-year-old son.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu a sih ciangin ka pasal leh kei in a tapa kum nih a phak a kila uh hi.

records.english: At first, the little boy cried for his mother every night.
records.zomi: A masa-in naupang pasal zan simin a nu adingin a kap hi.

records.english: Now he is twelve, and he calls us both by the names his mother used for us.
records.zomi: Tu-in kum sawm leh nih a phak a, a nu in eite a sam dan min tawh hong sam hi.

records.english: Shall I show you the photo from our wedding day?
records.zomi: I mopawi ni lim kong etsak ding hiam?

records.english: Tell me what you ate at your wedding feast.
records.zomi: Na mopawi an lian ah bang na ne uh hiam hong gen in.

records.english: Our wedding was so small that the whole party fitted into my aunt's courtyard.
records.zomi: I mopawi a neu lua ahih manin pawi bup ka ni' tual ah a lut hi.

records.english: Last spring, our oldest daughter married a boy she had known since nursery school.
records.zomi: Kum nung spring in i tanu upa pen in naupang sang pan a theih naupang pasal khat a kiteenpih hi.

records.english: We moved to the town so that our children could go to a better school.
records.zomi: I tate in sang hoih zaw a kah theih nadingun khuapi ah i tuah hi.

records.english: Was it hard to be a parent so young?
records.zomi: Khangno mahmah-in nu leh pa hih a haksa hiam?

records.english: Our grandparents' parents chose who they would marry, but our grandparents insisted on choosing for themselves.
records.zomi: I pu leh pite' nu leh pate in a kiteen ding uh a teel uh a, ahi zongin i pu leh pite in amau mah in teel dingin a ngen uh hi.

records.english: Why did you name your daughter after a river?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na tanu gun min tawh na phuak hiam?

records.english: Her grandmother was born beside that river, and we wanted her to remember it.
records.zomi: A pi tua gun kiang ah a suak a, a phawk ding i deih hi.

records.english: For the first five years of our marriage, my husband worked in another country.
records.zomi: I kiteenna kum nga masa sungin ka pasal gam dang ah na a sem hi.

records.english: We wrote letters every week and saved every one of them in a shoebox.
records.zomi: Kal simin lai i kigelh a, a khempeuh khedap bawm khat sung ah i kem hi.

records.english: Last year, our children read the letters and finally understood how much we had missed each other.
records.zomi: Kum nung in i tate in laite a sim uh a, bangzah i kilungngai hiam a tawp-in a thei uh hi.

records.english: Bringing up four children in a two-room flat was like packing a suitcase that never quite closed.
records.zomi: Khan nih nei inn ah ta li khoi pen a kikhak kim ngei lo van bawm thuk bang ahi hi.

records.english: Did your parents let you choose your own husband?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa in na pasal teel dingin hong phal uh hiam?

records.english: When did your son say his first word?
records.zomi: Bang ciangin na tapa in a kammal masa pen a gen hiam?

records.english: Could we have managed without your mother's help when the twins were born?
records.zomi: Apengte a suah ciangin na nu' huhna om lo-in i zo thei ding hiam?

records.english: After they married, my grandparents built their first house with their own hands.
records.zomi: A kiteen khit uh ciangin ka pu leh pite in a inn masa uh amau khut tawh a lam uh hi.

records.english: My grandfather carried the stones up the hill, and my grandmother mixed the mud for the walls.
records.zomi: Ka pu in mual tung dong suangte a pua a, ka pi in bang adingin leibuan a ngom hi.

records.english: The house took two years to finish, and three of their children were born in it.
records.zomi: Inn zawh dingin kum nih a la a, a tate thum tua sung ah a suak uh hi.

records.english: Would you have married so young if your parents hadn't arranged it?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa in a gel kei uh le, tua bang khangno-in na kiteen ding hiam?

records.english: I really did want to help my son with his reading, but I had never learned to read well myself.
records.zomi: Ka tapa a laisimna ah huh ka deih mahmah hi, ahi zongin keimah zong hoih takin sim ka sin ngei kei hi.

records.english: So the two of us went to the evening class together, and we both learned.
records.zomi: Tua ahih manin i nih un nitak kilasi ah khawm-in i pai a, i nih un i sin hi.

records.english: However little money we had, we always bought the children new shoes for the school year.
records.zomi: Sum bangzah ta in tawm zongin sang kum adingin naupangte khedap thak i lei sak tawntung hi.

records.english: Had my wife not encouraged me, I would never have gone back to school at thirty-five.
records.zomi: Ka zi in hong hanthawn kei le, kum sawmthum leh nga ciangin sang ah ka kik ngei kei ding hi.

records.english: Did your children ever run away from home?
records.zomi: Na tate inn pan a tai khia ngei uh hiam?

records.english: Our son was given his grandfather's watch on the day he became a father himself.
records.zomi: Ka tapa amah mah pa a suah ni-in a pu' nai kipia hi.

records.english: Who looked after the children when you both worked in the fields?
records.zomi: Na nih un lo ah na sem ciangun naupangte kua in a kem hiam?

records.english: May I tell the children how you proposed to me?
records.zomi: Bangci-in hong ngen hiam naupangte ka hilh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Although they argued often, my grandparents never went to sleep angry with each other.
records.zomi: A kinial den uh hangin ka pu leh pite a heh-in a ihmu ngei kei uh hi.

records.english: Can I tell you how your mother and I first met?
records.zomi: Na nu leh kei bangci-in i kimu masa hiam kong gen thei ding hiam?

records.english: How many days of creation are described in Genesis?
records.zomi: Piancilna sungah piangsakna ni bangzah kigen hiam?

records.english: Christians hold different views on how to read the creation story alongside modern science.
records.zomi: Christiante in piangsakna tangthu tu hun science tawh bangci-in sim ding hiam tuamtuam takin a ngaihsun uh hi.

records.english: Students aren't allowed to pick the flowers in the church garden.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte in pawlpi huan-a pakte a lo thei kei uh hi.

records.english: According to Genesis, God saw everything he had made and called it very good.
records.zomi: Piancilna bangin Pasian in a piangsak khempeuh a mu a, a hoih mahmah hi, a ci hi.

records.english: What does the story of creation in Genesis teach?
records.zomi: Piancilna-a piangsakna tangthu in bang a hilh hiam?

records.english: Christians read it as teaching that the world is good and that God made it with purpose.
records.zomi: Leitung a hoih a, Pasian in deihna nei-in a piangsak hi, cih a hilh hi, ci-in Christiante in a sim uh hi.

records.english: The night sky was so clear at the camp that the children stopped talking and just stared.
records.zomi: Mun ah zan van a siang lua ahih manin naupangte a kiho tawp uh a, a en bek uh hi.

records.english: The children made a big painting of the creation story for the church wall.
records.zomi: Naupangte in pawlpi bang adingin piangsakna tangthu lim lian khat a zeek uh hi.

records.english: Rather than arguing about how the world began, our study group focused on what the story says about God.
records.zomi: Leitung bangci-in a kipan hiam kinial sangin i sinna pawl in tangthu in Pasian thu bang a gen hiam a en hi.

records.english: Did the story of creation frighten you or comfort you as a child?
records.zomi: Na naupan lai-in piangsakna tangthu in hong lausak hiam, hong hehnem hiam?

records.english: Shall we read the first chapter of Genesis together this evening?
records.zomi: Tuni nitak in Piancilna khen masa pen khawm-in i sim ding hiam?

records.english: Could the church use its land to grow food for families in need?
records.zomi: Pawlpi in kisapna nei innkuante adingin an suan dingin a leitang a zang thei ding hiam?

records.english: Many Christians believe that God created the world out of love, not out of need.
records.zomi: Kisapna hang hi lo-in itna hangin Pasian in leitung a piangsak hi, ci-in Christian tampi in a um uh hi.

records.english: Many Christians describe creation as a book in which God's care can be read.
records.zomi: Christian tampi in piangsakna pen Pasian' kemna a kisim theih laibu khat bangin a gen uh hi.

records.english: Would you like to help us plant flowers around the church?
records.zomi: Pawlpi kim ah pak suan dingin hong huh nuam na hi hiam?

records.english: When do you feel most thankful for the world around you?
records.zomi: Na kim-a leitung adingin bang ciangin na lungdam pen hiam?

records.english: Why do you think the creation story begins with light?
records.zomi: Bang hangin piangsakna tangthu meivak tawh a kipan in na ngaihsun hiam?

records.english: Having watched the sunrise from the mountain, my uncle said he understood why people praise the Creator.
records.zomi: Mual tung pan ni suak a en khit ciangin bang hangin mite in Piangsakpa a phat uh hiam ka thei hi, ci-in ka pa neu in a ci hi.

records.english: Could you explain why some Christians keep one day a week for rest?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Christian khenkhatte in kal khat ah ni khat tawldam dingin a kem uh hiam na gen siang thei ding hiam?

records.english: The more she learned about the stars, the more my sister wondered at the world.
records.zomi: Aksite thu a sin semsem ciangin ka sanggam nu leitung tungah a lamdang sa semsem hi.

records.english: Please don't leave rubbish in the forest, because it belongs to everyone.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh' ahih manin gam sung ah nawi nusia kei un.

records.english: Whoever finds the most different leaves on the nature walk will show them to the class.
records.zomi: Gam vakna ah singnah tuamtuam a mu tam pen peuhpeuh in kilasi a etsak ding hi.

records.english: Our neighbor uses a magnifying glass to show the children the patterns on butterfly wings.
records.zomi: I inn veng in naupangte kiangah khuaitet tawh phalbi kha tung-a limte a etsak hi.

records.english: Can I keep the shell I found on the beach?
records.zomi: Tuipi gei ah ka muh kheng ka kem thei ding hiam?

records.english: The Bible begins with the words, "In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth."
records.zomi: Laisiangtho in, “A cilin Pasian in vante leh leitung a piangsak hi,” cih kammal tawh a kipan hi.

records.english: When the farmers bring in the harvest, our church holds a service to thank God for the land.
records.zomi: Lo neite in buh a lak uh ciangin i pawlpi in leitang adingin Pasian kiangah lungdam gen dingin kikhopna a bawl hi.

records.english: Everyone, please bring something from nature to put on the table for the harvest service.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, buh lak kikhopna adingin dawhkan tungah koih dingin leitung pan bangmah khat tawi un.

records.english: Where can we go to see the night sky clearly, away from the city lights?
records.zomi: Khuapi meivak pan gamla-in zan van kician takin en dingin koi ah i pai thei ding hiam?

records.english: My aunt says she feels closest to God when she is working in her garden.
records.zomi: A huan ah a sep laitakin Pasian tawh a kinai pen bangin a kisa hi, ci-in ka ni in a ci hi.

records.english: Our pastor used a globe to show the children how many different countries God made room for.
records.zomi: I pastor in Pasian in gam tuamtuam bangzah adingin mun a bawl hiam naupangte etsak dingin leitung lim bawlung khat a zang hi.

records.english: Many Christians believe that God rested on the seventh day as an example for people to follow.
records.zomi: Mite in a zuih ding uh etsakna-in Pasian ni sagihna-in a tawldam hi, ci-in Christian tampi in a um uh hi.

records.english: Is it possible to believe in God and study science at the same time?
records.zomi: Pasian um-in science sin khawm thei hiam?

records.english: Many scientists who are Christians say that their faith and their work go together.
records.zomi: Christian hi science mi tampi in a upna uh leh a nasep uh a kithuah hi, a ci uh hi.

records.english: God created people in his own image, according to the book of Genesis.
records.zomi: Piancilna laibu bangin Pasian in mite amah' lim tawh a piangsak hi.

records.english: Children, look at the stars tonight and think about how big God's creation is.
records.zomi: Naupangte, tuni zanin aksite en unla, Pasian' piangsakna bangzah a lian hiam ngaihsun un.

records.english: Our pastor once compared the seven days of creation to the building of a house.
records.zomi: I pastor in khatvei piangsakna ni sagihte inn lam tawh a kikhaikhin hi.

records.english: Do you think the world would look different if people treated it as a gift?
records.zomi: Mite in leitung letsong bangin a kem uh leh leitung a kilamdang ding in na ngaihsun hiam?

records.english: My grandfather uses a small telescope to show the grandchildren the moon and the planets.
records.zomi: Ka pu in a tute kiangah kha leh aksite etsak dingin telescope neu khat a zang hi.

records.english: Christians often sing songs that praise God for the beauty of the world.
records.zomi: Christiante in leitung hoihna adingin Pasian phat la a sa den uh hi.

records.english: The youth group cleaned the riverbank because they believe creation should be looked after.
records.zomi: Piangsakna kem ding hi, ci-in a um uh ahih manin khangno pawl in gun gei a siangsak uh hi.

records.english: Which part of creation do you find most beautiful?
records.zomi: Piangsakna lak ah koi khen in a hoih pen na sa hiam?

records.english: May I take the class outside to look at the clouds during our lesson on creation?
records.zomi: Piangsakna hilhna laitakin meiputte en dingin kilasi pua ah ka paipih thei ding hiam?

records.english: If people saw nature as a gift, they might be more careful about how they use it.
records.zomi: Mite in leitung letsong bangin a muh uh leh a zat dan uh ah a pilvang zaw kha ding uh hi.

records.english: Who taught you the names of the stars?
records.zomi: Aksite' min kua in hong hilh hiam?

records.english: In the Psalms, the writer says that the heavens declare the glory of God.
records.zomi: Late sungah a gelhpa in vante in Pasian' minthanna a gen uh hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Look how many colors the birds have!
records.zomi: Vasate rong bangzah a tam hiam en un!

records.english: Kids, how many animals can you name from the creation story?
records.zomi: Naupangte, piangsakna tangthu pan ganhing bangzah min na gen thei uh hiam?

records.english: We collected rainwater in barrels so that the church garden could be watered in the dry season.
records.zomi: Khuakhal hun ah pawlpi huan tui lei theih nadingin bel lian sung ah guah tui i kaikhawm hi.

records.english: Had the early Christians not copied the scriptures by hand, the creation story might have been lost.
records.zomi: Christian masate in Laisiangtho khut tawh a gelh kik kei le, piangsakna tangthu a mang kha ding hi.

records.english: Our church planted trees on the hill to give thanks for creation.
records.zomi: Piangsakna adingin lungdam gen dingin i pawlpi in mual tungah singkung a suan hi.

records.english: I do want my children to care for the earth as part of God's creation.
records.zomi: Ka tate in Pasian' piangsakna khen khat bangin leitung a kem ding uh ka deih mahmah hi.

records.english: We gave thanks before the meal for the food that grows from the earth.
records.zomi: An nek ma-in leitung pan a khang an adingin lungdam i gen hi.

records.english: The early church writers often spoke about creation when they taught about God's power.
records.zomi: Pawlpi masa laigelhte in Pasian' vangliatna thu a hilh ciangun piangsakna thu a gen den uh hi.

records.english: Christians believe that God created the heavens and the earth.
records.zomi: Pasian in vante leh leitung a piangsak hi, ci-in Christiante in a um uh hi.

records.english: The Bible teaches that people are given the task of caring for the earth, according to many Christians.
records.zomi: Christian tampi' gen bangin Laisiangtho in mite leitung kem nasep kipia hi, ci-in a hilh hi.

records.english: What do you think God's creation teaches us about caring for animals?
records.zomi: Pasian' piangsakna in ganhingte kemna thu bang hong hilh in na ngaihsun hiam?

records.english: Although the creation story is very old, Christians still read it for guidance today.
records.zomi: Piangsakna tangthu a lui mahmah hangin Christiante in tuni dong lampi lakna adingin a sim lai uh hi.

records.english: What amazes many believers is that the same God who made the stars also cares for each person.
records.zomi: Um mi tampi a lamdang sak pen pen aksite a piangsak Pasian mah in mi khat ciat a kem hi, cih ahi hi.

records.english: Some Christian traditions celebrate a special season each year to give thanks for creation.
records.zomi: Christian ngeina khenkhatte in piangsakna adingin lungdam gen dingin kum simin hun tuam khat a bawl uh hi.

records.english: The old church window shows the sun, the moon and the animals of creation.
records.zomi: Pawlpi tukvuang lui in ni, kha leh piangsakna ganhingte a lak hi.

records.english: The old well was cleaned out every spring by the young men of the street.
records.zomi: Spring simin lampi-a khangno pasalte in tuikhuk lui a siangsak uh hi.

records.english: When the roof began to leak, six neighbors came to help us rethatch it.
records.zomi: Innkhum a zu kipat ciangin inn veng guk in a khum kik dingin hong huh uh hi.

records.english: The men cut the grass by the river, and the women tied it into bundles.
records.zomi: Pasalte in gun kiang-a lopa a at uh a, numeite in a bu-in a khih uh hi.

records.english: In one day, the roof was finished, and we cooked a big meal for everyone.
records.zomi: Ni khat sungin innkhum a zo a, mi khempeuh adingin an lian i huan hi.

records.english: Everyone, put your shoes in a line at the door before you come in.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, na lut ma-un kongkhak ah na khedap uh kizui-in koih un.

records.english: Why did your family do the laundry only on Saturdays?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na innkuan in Kiginni bek ah puan a sil uh hiam?

records.english: One morning, our goats escaped and climbed onto the neighbor's roof.
records.zomi: Zingsang khat i kelte a tai khia uh a, inn veng' innkhum tungah a kah uh hi.

records.english: We spent the afternoon coaxing them down with handfuls of fresh grass.
records.zomi: Lopa thak khut dim tawh nitak lam bup i khem-in i tumsak hi.

records.english: The neighbor forgave us when we brought her a jar of goat's milk every day for a month.
records.zomi: Kha khat sung ni simin kel nawi bel khat i tawi sak ciangin inn veng numei in hong maisak hi.

records.english: The first time I cooked dinner for the whole family, I forgot to add salt.
records.zomi: Innkuan bup adingin nitak an ka huan masak ciangin cii koih ka mangngilh hi.

records.english: Nobody said a word until my little brother asked whether the soup was supposed to taste of water.
records.zomi: An tui in tui bang a tui ding ahi hiam, ci-in ka nau pasal in a dot dong kuamah in kammal khat a gen kei uh hi.

records.english: Everyone laughed, and then my grandfather added salt and ate two bowls.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh a nui uh a, tua ciangin ka pu in cii a behlap a, kuang nih a ne hi.

records.english: It might have been easier to buy bread, but my grandmother baked it herself every morning.
records.zomi: Moh lei a baih zaw kha ding hi, ahi zongin ka pi in zingsang simin amah mah in a em hi.

records.english: However tired our parents were, the floor was always swept before we went to bed.
records.zomi: I nu leh pa bangzah ta in tawl zongun i lum ma-in tual kiphiat tawntung hi.

records.english: Was your father strict about chores?
records.zomi: Na pa inn nasep thu-ah a khauh hiam?

records.english: May I use the ladder to clean the gutters, or should I wait for Dad?
records.zomi: Innkhum tui luanna siangsak dingin kahlei ka zang thei ding hiam, Pa ka ngak ding hiam?

records.english: Tell me what your grandmother used to put in her homemade soap.
records.zomi: Na pi in a inn-a bawl satpiang sung ah bang a koih den hiam hong gen in.

records.english: Our neighbor's new roof was blown off in a storm, so we let them sleep in our house for a week.
records.zomi: I inn veng' innkhum thak huihpi in a mut ahih manin kal khat sung i inn ah a ihmusak hi.

records.english: Whoever broke something had to tell the adults before dinner.
records.zomi: Bangmah a sukek peuhpeuh in nitak an ma-in upate a hilh ding hi.

records.english: Did you ever try to avoid doing the dishes?
records.zomi: Kuang sil pelh dingin na sin ngei hiam?

records.english: If we finished our chores early, our grandmother let us go swimming in the river.
records.zomi: I inn nasep a man masak leh ka pi in gun ah kidiah dingin hong phal hi.

records.english: My aunts and I used to wash the family's clothes at the river every Saturday.
records.zomi: Ka nite leh kei Kiginni simin gun ah innkuan' puan i sil hi.

records.english: They sang the whole time, and I learned every song before I learned to scrub properly.
records.zomi: Hun bup la a sa uh a, hoih taka sil ka sin ma-in la khempeuh ka thei hi.

records.english: When I was a boy, I had to carry the shopping home from the market on my head.
records.zomi: Ka naupan lai-in zuakna mun pan lei vante ka lu tungah inn dong ka pua ding a kisam hi.

records.english: My brother was supposed to sweep the stairs, but he paid me with his sweets to do it for him.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in kahlei a phiat ding a, ahi zongin amah adingin ka hih nadingin a an lim tawh hong thuk hi.

records.english: Looking back, I realize that those chores taught me more patience than any lesson at school.
records.zomi: Nung lam en kik-in tua inn nasepte in sang-a hilhna khatpeuh sangin thuakzawhna hong hilh tam zaw hi, ka thei hi.

records.english: Shall I tell you how we used to make soap at home?
records.zomi: Inn ah satpiang bangci-in i bawl den hiam kong gen ding hiam?

records.english: Who used to wake up first to light the fire in your house?
records.zomi: Na inn ah mei hal dingin kua in a thou masa den hiam?

records.english: Children weren't allowed to touch the kerosene lamp in our house.
records.zomi: I inn ah naupangte in datsi meivak a khoih thei kei uh hi.

records.english: Could you help me sort these old clothes for the church sale?
records.zomi: Pawlpi zuakna adingin hih puan luite khen dingin hong huh thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: How did you keep the house cool before you had a fan?
records.zomi: Fan na neih ma-in inn bangci-in na vot sak hiam?

records.english: We were given pocket money only after the chickens had been fed and the floor swept.
records.zomi: Akte an vak khit-in tual phiat khit ciang bek a zat ding sum kipia hi.

records.english: Please don't put the knives in the sink with the other dishes.
records.zomi: Kuang dangte tawh namsaute kuang silna sung ah koih kei in.

records.english: Last year, my son painted the garden fence for his grandparents without being asked.
records.zomi: Kum nung in ka tapa in ngen lo-in a pu leh pite' huan kulh a zeek sak hi.

records.english: Did you have to help with the harvest too?
records.zomi: Buh lak ah zong na huh ding a kisam hiam?

records.english: It was only when the snow came that we understood why Grandpa had made us stack so much wood.
records.zomi: Vuk a tun ciang bek bang hangin ka pu in sing tam lua hong koihsak hiam i thei hi.

records.english: What I remember most about my childhood chores is the smell of the woodsmoke in the mornings.
records.zomi: Ka naupan lai inn nasepte ah ka phawk pen pen zingsang-a sing meikhu namtui ahi hi.

records.english: Although housework seemed endless as a child, I now understand how much it taught me.
records.zomi: Naupan lai-in inn nasep a bei lo bang hangin tu-in bangzah hong hilh hiam ka thei hi.

records.english: When I was nine, my grandfather taught me to chop firewood with a small axe.
records.zomi: Kum kua ka phak ciangin ka pu in heipi neu khat tawh sing sat dan hong hilh hi.

records.english: He made me practice on thin branches for a whole week before I touched a log.
records.zomi: Singtum ka khoih ma-in kal bup singkhawng neute tungah hong kisinsak hi.

records.english: By winter, I was proud to fill the woodpile by myself.
records.zomi: Khuavot ciangin keimah bek in sing bu ka dimsak thei ahih manin ka kisathei hi.

records.english: The more my father complained about the mess, the faster we pretended to tidy it.
records.zomi: Ka pa in buaina thu a phun semsem ciangin manlang zawin i kiman bang i kibawl hi.

records.english: My grandfather believed that a tidy yard showed respect for anyone who visited.
records.zomi: Ka pu in tual siang pen a hong veh kua peuhpeuh tungah zahtakna a lak hi, ci-in a um hi.

records.english: Whatever the weather, someone in our family had to walk to the spring for drinking water.
records.zomi: Huihkhua bang ahi zongin i innkuan sung-a kuamah in dawn ding tui adingin tui zuk ah a pai ding hi.

records.english: What was your job in the house when you were small?
records.zomi: Na neu lai-in inn ah na nasep bang ahi hiam?

records.english: I fed the chickens and swept the yard before I went to school.
records.zomi: Sang ka pai ma-in akte an ka vak a, tual ka phiat hi.

records.english: The kitchen floor was scrubbed every Friday with a stiff brush and cold water.
records.zomi: Laithai ni simin an huanna tual phiatna khauh leh tui vot tawh kisil hi.

records.english: When did you first mend your own torn trousers?
records.zomi: Bang ciangin na kekawi kek nangma-in na khui masa hiam?

records.english: Cleaning the house before the festival felt like getting ready to meet an important guest.
records.zomi: Pawi ma-in inn siangsak pen khual thupi khat muh dingin kiman bang ahi hi.

records.english: Rather than arguing about the dishes, my brothers and I made it a race to see who finished first.
records.zomi: Kuang thu-ah kinial sangin ka sanggam pasalte leh kei kua a zo masa ding hiam kidemna in i bawl hi.

records.english: By the time I left home, I could cook, sew, mend a fence and look after the goats.
records.zomi: Inn ka nusiat ciangin an ka huan thei a, puan ka khui thei a, kulh ka bawl thei a, kelte ka kem thei hi.

records.english: Every year before the New Year, we cleaned the whole house from top to bottom.
records.zomi: Kum thak ma-in kum simin inn bup tung pan nuai dong i siangsak hi.

records.english: Which chore did you hate most as a child?
records.zomi: Naupan lai-in koi inn nasep na huat pen hiam?

records.english: Do you remember who broke the blue plate when we were children?
records.zomi: I neu lai-in kuang dum kua in a sukek hiam na phawk hiam?

records.english: I did, and I hid the pieces under the sink for a whole year.
records.zomi: Keimah, kum bup kuang silna nuai ah a kekte ka sel hi.

records.english: The summer I turned fifteen, our whole family painted the house together.
records.zomi: Kum sawm leh nga ka phak khal in i innkuan bup khawm-in inn i zeek hi.

records.english: My little sister was given the smallest brush and the lowest part of the wall.
records.zomi: Ka nau nu zeekna neu pen leh bang nuai pen kipia hi.

records.english: We still laugh at the photo of all of us covered in white paint.
records.zomi: Zeek kang tawh i kikhuh khempeuh lim tungah i nui lai hi.

records.english: We bought a second-hand washing machine so that my grandmother wouldn't have to wash clothes by hand.
records.zomi: Ka pi in khut tawh puan a sil nawn lo nadingin puan silna set zat khin khat i lei hi.

records.english: Where did your grandmother keep the soap she made herself?
records.zomi: Na pi in amah mah a bawl satpiang koi ah a kem hiam?

records.english: The longer the discussion went on, the quieter my little brother became.
records.zomi: Kihona a sau semsem ciangin ka nau pasal a dai semsem hi.

records.english: How long did it take your family to agree on a name for the baby?
records.zomi: Naungek min ah na innkuan a kithukim nadingin bangzah a sawt hiam?

records.english: Our family discussions were like a slow river, because they always reached the sea in the end.
records.zomi: I innkuan kihonate pen gun zawi bang ahi a, a tawp-in tuipi ah a tung tawntung hi.

records.english: Would we have stayed in the village if Grandma hadn't spoken up that evening?
records.zomi: Tua nitak in ka pi a gen kei le, khua ah i om ding hiam?

records.english: By the end of the evening, even my stubborn uncle had agreed to the plan.
records.zomi: Nitak tawp ciangin ka pa neu lu khauh pen zong gelna ah a kithukim hi.

records.english: In hindsight, my parents were protecting us by keeping some discussions private.
records.zomi: Nung lam en kik-in, kihona khenkhatte a sel uh tawh ka nu leh ka pa in hong veng uh hi.

records.english: Why did your parents ask the children before buying the new house?
records.zomi: Inn thak a lei ma-un bang hangin na nu leh na pa in naupangte a dong uh hiam?

records.english: You weren't allowed to leave the table until everyone had had a chance to speak.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh in gen nading hun a ngah dong dawhkan na nusia thei kei hi.

records.english: Children, your grandfather has a surprise to talk about with you after dinner.
records.zomi: Naupangte, nitak an khit ciangin na pu in note tawh kiho ding lamdang thu khat a nei hi.

records.english: When did your family decide to leave the village?
records.zomi: Bang ciangin na innkuan in khua nusia dingin a khensat uh hiam?

records.english: When I was small, our family argued for weeks about buying the first television in the village.
records.zomi: Ka neu lai-in khua sung-a TV masa pen lei thu-ah i innkuan kal tampi a kinial uh hi.

records.english: Grandpa said it would stop the children from studying, and my aunts said it would bring the world to us.
records.zomi: Ka pu in naupangte a sin lo ding uh hi, a ci a, ka nite in leitung eite kiangah a tawi ding hi, a ci uh hi.

records.english: In the end, they bought it, and half the village came to our yard every evening to watch.
records.zomi: A tawp-in a lei uh a, nitak simin khua khen khat i tual ah en dingin a hong uh hi.

records.english: It was only after the meeting that my grandmother told us she had already made up her mind.
records.zomi: Kikhopna khit ciang bek ka pi in a khensat khin hi, ci-in hong hilh hi.

records.english: Our family decided to plant a garden on the empty land instead of selling it.
records.zomi: I innkuan in zuak sangin leitang awng tungah huan suan dingin a khensat hi.

records.english: Looking back, my parents' habit of explaining every decision taught us to think for ourselves.
records.zomi: Nung lam en kik-in ka nu leh ka pa' khensatna khempeuh gen siang ngeina in eimah in ngaihsun dingin hong hilh hi.

records.english: Whoever wanted to speak at the meeting had to stand up first.
records.zomi: Kikhopna ah gen nuam peuhpeuh in a masa-in a ding ding hi.

records.english: Were you allowed to give your opinion when you were small?
records.zomi: Na neu lai-in na ngaihsutna gen dingin kiphal hiam?

records.english: By the time the discussion ended, the candles had burned down and the children were asleep on the mats.
records.zomi: Kihona a bei ciangin khawimeivaakte a kang bei a, naupangte phah tungah a ihmu uh hi.

records.english: Why did your aunt leave the meeting so early?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na ni kikhopna manlang mahmah-in a nusia hiam?

records.english: May I bring my friend to the family meeting so that she can explain the plan?
records.zomi: Gelna a gen siang theih nadingin innkuan kikhopna ah ka lawm ka paipih thei ding hiam?

records.english: Although we disagreed about the move, we all helped to pack when the day came.
records.zomi: Tuah thu-ah i kithukim kei hangin a ni a tun ciangin i khempeuh in thuk dingin i huh hi.

records.english: My grandmother said, "Speak softly, and people will listen more carefully."
records.zomi: Ka pi in, “Nem takin gen in, mite in pilvang zawin a ngai ding uh hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: It was during one of those long family meetings that I first realized my sister was braver than me.
records.zomi: Tua innkuan kikhopna sau khat sungin ka sanggam nu kei sangin a hang zaw hi, cih ka thei masa hi.

records.english: Was it your idea to adopt the dog?
records.zomi: Ui khoi pen na ngaihsutna ahi hiam?

records.english: One year, my parents couldn't decide whether to buy a cow or a motorbike.
records.zomi: Kum khat ka nu leh ka pa in bawng hiam motorbike hiam lei ding a khensat zo kei uh hi.

records.english: My father wanted the motorbike to get to market faster, and my mother wanted milk for the children.
records.zomi: Ka pa in zuakna mun ah manlang zaw-in a tun nadingin motorbike a deih a, ka nu in naupangte adingin nawi a deih hi.

records.english: They bought the cow, and my father walked to market for three more years.
records.zomi: Bawng a lei uh a, ka pa in kum thum behlap zuakna mun ah a kalsuan hi.

records.english: Shall I tell you how we decided where to bury Grandpa's old dog?
records.zomi: Ka pu' ui lui koi ah vui ding hiam bangci-in i khensat hiam kong gen ding hiam?

records.english: Rather than raising his voice, my grandfather would simply stop talking until everyone else was quiet.
records.zomi: Ka pu in a aw domsang sangin mi dang khempeuh a dai dong a kiho tawp bek hi.

records.english: Who usually had the last word in your family when you were young?
records.zomi: Na neu lai-in na innkuan ah a tamzaw-in kua in thu nunung a gen hiam?

records.english: My grandfather did, but only after he had heard what everyone else thought.
records.zomi: Ka pu, ahi zongin mi dang khempeuh in bang a ngaihsun uh hiam a zak khit ciang bek.

records.english: Do you remember how we chose the name for the family shop?
records.zomi: Innkuan dawr min bangci-in i teel hiam na phawk hiam?

records.english: Everyone wrote a name on a slip of paper, and Grandma pulled one out of a hat.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh in laipek neu khat tungah min khat a gelh uh a, ka pi in lukhu sung pan khat a la khia hi.

records.english: Tell me how you chose your wedding date.
records.zomi: Na mopawi ni bangci-in na teel hiam hong gen in.

records.english: Please don't mention the price of the wedding in front of the guests.
records.zomi: Khualte mai ah mopawi man gen kei in.

records.english: It might have been easier to decide if we hadn't all talked at once.
records.zomi: I khempeuh khatvei-in i gen kei le khensat a baih zaw kha ding hi.

records.english: We bought the house that my mother liked best, even though it was farther from the town.
records.zomi: Khuapi pan a gamla zaw hangin ka nu' deih pen inn i lei hi.

records.english: Did you ever argue with your parents about pocket money?
records.zomi: Na zat ding sum thu-ah na nu leh na pa tawh na kinial ngei hiam?

records.english: Who was the loudest person at your family meetings?
records.zomi: Na innkuan kikhopna ah kua in a ging sang pen hiam?

records.english: Which family decision do you still disagree with?
records.zomi: Koi innkuan khensatna na nial lai hiam?

records.english: If the children had been asked earlier, the move would have been much easier for them.
records.zomi: Naupangte a ma zaw-in kidong le tuah a baih zaw mahmah ding uh hi.

records.english: My uncle offered to lend us his car so that we could visit the school before choosing it.
records.zomi: A teel ma-un sang i va et theih nadingin ka pa neu in a mawtaw hong ngetsak dingin a kipia hi.

records.english: What did your parents say when you wanted to marry so young?
records.zomi: Khangno mahmah-in kiteen na deih ciangin na nu leh na pa in bang a ci uh hiam?

records.english: My father asked me to wait a year, and I'm glad I listened.
records.zomi: Ka pa in kum khat ngak dingin hong ngen a, ka ngaih manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: How did your family decide where to go on holiday?
records.zomi: Na innkuan in nopsakna hun-a pai ding mun bangci-in a khensat uh hiam?

records.english: When my brother said he wanted to become a musician, nobody spoke for a whole minute.
records.zomi: La sak siam suak ka deih hi, ci-in ka sanggam pasal in a gen ciangin minit khat bup kuamah a gen kei uh hi.

records.english: Then our grandmother said, "Let him play for us before you decide."
records.zomi: Tua ciangin i pi in, “Na khensat ma-un eite adingin tum sak un,” a ci hi.

records.english: He played his guitar in the kitchen, and by the end of the song my father was smiling.
records.zomi: An huanna ah a guitar a tum a, la a bei ciangin ka pa a nui hi.

records.english: Did the family agree to sell the old truck?
records.zomi: Mawtaw lian lui zuak dingin innkuan a kithukim uh hiam?

records.english: Did your grandparents ever change their minds after a family meeting?
records.zomi: Na pu leh pite in innkuan kikhopna khit ciangin a ngaihsutna uh a laih ngei uh hiam?

records.english: The decision about the land was written down and signed by all the brothers.
records.zomi: Leitang thu-a khensatna kigelh a, sanggam pasal khempeuh in min a suaksak uh hi.

records.english: After my grandfather stopped fishing, the family discussed whether to sell his old boat.
records.zomi: Ka pu nga man a tawp khit ciangin a long lui zuak ding hiam innkuan in a kiho uh hi.

records.english: My cousins wanted the money, but my aunt wanted to keep it in memory of him.
records.zomi: Ka sanggamte in sum a deih uh a, ka ni in amah phawkna-in kem a deih hi.

records.english: They agreed to repair the boat and take the children out on it every summer.
records.zomi: Long bawl siang-in khal simin naupangte a tung ah paipih dingin a kithukim uh hi.

records.english: Last month, my children asked to join our discussion about the family budget.
records.zomi: Kha nung in ka tate innkuan budget kihona ah kihel dingin a ngen uh hi.

records.english: We held the family meeting at the river because the house was too small for everyone.
records.zomi: Inn a neu lua ahih manin gun gei ah innkuan kikhopna i bawl hi.

records.english: What I remember most about our family meetings is the smell of the tea my aunt made.
records.zomi: I innkuan kikhopnate ah ka phawk pen pen ka ni' bawl tea namtui ahi hi.

records.english: We discussed for a long time whether my sister should sell her sewing machine to pay for driving lessons.
records.zomi: Mawtaw mawng kisinna man piak nadingin ka sanggam nu in a puan khuina set a zuak ding hiam hun sawt i kikup hi.

records.english: How did your little sister react when she heard she was getting her own room?
records.zomi: Amah' khan a ngah ding hi, a zak ciangin na nau nu in bangci-in a dawng hiam?

records.english: On market days, I was left in charge of my three younger brothers.
records.zomi: Zuakna ni simin ka nau pasal thumte kem dingin hong nusia uh hi.

records.english: I fed them rice, kept them away from the river, and told them stories until our parents came home.
records.zomi: Buh ka nesak a, gun pan ka kham a, i nu leh pa a tun dong tangthu ka gen sak hi.

records.english: I was only eleven, but I felt like the most important person in the village.
records.zomi: Kum sawm leh khat bek ka hi hi, ahi zongin khua sung ah mi thupi pen bangin ka kisa hi.

records.english: However busy the farm was, someone always stayed home with the babies.
records.zomi: Lo bangzah ta in buai zongin kuamah in naungekte tawh inn ah a om tawntung hi.

records.english: Did you ever lose your little brother at the market?
records.zomi: Zuakna mun ah na nau pasal na mansuah ngei hiam?

records.english: Who looked after you when your parents worked in the fields?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa lo ah a nasep laitakun kua in hong kem hiam?

records.english: My grandmother, who taught me to weave while the others were away.
records.zomi: Ka pi, a dangte a om loh laitakun puan tah dan hong hilh pa.

records.english: Looking back, those years of caring for my grandmother taught me more than university did.
records.zomi: Nung lam en kik-in ka pi ka kemna kumte in sangpi sangin hong hilh tam zaw hi.

records.english: Although my grandmother no longer recognized me, she always smiled when I sang to her.
records.zomi: Ka pi in hong thei nawn kei hangin la ka sak sak ciangin a nui tawntung hi.

records.english: Why did your grandfather insist on walking to church even when he could hardly stand?
records.zomi: Bang hangin ka pu a ding zo dek nawn kei hangin pawlpi ah kalsuan dingin a ngen den hiam?

records.english: Caring for my grandfather was like tending a garden, because small daily attention mattered most.
records.zomi: Ka pu kemna pen huan kemna bang ahi a, ni sim-a ngaihsutna neute a thupi pen hi.

records.english: My grandmother's glasses were sat on by the dog, so we bought her a new pair.
records.zomi: Ka pi' mitlimlang ui in a tut ahih manin a thak khat i lei sak hi.

records.english: Why did your aunt move in with you?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na ni na kiang uh ah a tuah hiam?

records.english: The old man's walking stick was broken in the crowd at the market.
records.zomi: Zuakna mun-a mi tam lak ah pasal upa' ciangkhut a kek hi.

records.english: A carpenter made him a new one from a mango branch the same afternoon.
records.zomi: Tua nitak lam mah in sing seemmi khat in haigah singkhawng pan a thak khat a bawl sak hi.

records.english: We moved my grandfather's bed beside the window, from where he could watch the children walking to school.
records.zomi: Naupangte sang a pai a muh theih nadingin ka pu' lupna tukvuang kiang ah i suan hi.

records.english: Our neighbor's baby was born early, so the women of the street cooked for the family for a month.
records.zomi: I inn veng' naungek a hun ma-in a suak ahih manin lampi-a numeite in kha khat sung innkuan adingin an a huan uh hi.

records.english: Everyone, please speak quietly, because Grandpa is resting.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, ka pu a tawldam ahih manin dai takin gen un.

records.english: What did you do the first time your baby brother said your name?
records.zomi: Na nau pasal neu in na min a sam masak ciangin bang na hih hiam?

records.english: I ran through the whole house shouting so that everyone would hear.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh in a zak theih nadingin inn bup ah ka kikou-in ka tai hi.

records.english: My little brother used to read the newspaper aloud to our blind grandfather every evening.
records.zomi: Ka nau pasal in nitak simin i pu mitcip adingin laithak ging sang takin a sim hi.

records.english: The baby's first tooth was found by her grandfather, who announced it to the whole family.
records.zomi: Naungek' ha masa pen a pu in a mu a, innkuan bup kiangah a gen hi.

records.english: Children weren't allowed to enter the room where my great-grandmother slept in the afternoon.
records.zomi: Naupangte ka pi' nu nitak lam a ihmutna khan ah a lut thei kei uh hi.

records.english: My aunt gave up her evenings for years to look after her husband's elderly father.
records.zomi: Ka ni in kum tampi sung a pasal' pa upa kem dingin a nitakte a nusia hi.

records.english: May I take the baby for a walk while you rest?
records.zomi: Na tawldam laitakin naungek ka vakpih thei ding hiam?

records.english: Could you tell me what your grandmother taught you about caring for babies?
records.zomi: Na pi in naungek kemna thu bang hong hilh hiam hong gen thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Where did you take your grandmother on her ninetieth birthday?
records.zomi: Na pi' pianni kum sawmkua-in koi ah na paipih hiam?

records.english: Did your grandparents ever live with your family?
records.zomi: Na pu leh pite na innkuan tawh a om khawm ngei uh hiam?

records.english: When my grandfather turned eighty, we took him to see the sea for the first time.
records.zomi: Ka pu kum sawmgiat a phak ciangin a masa pen-in tuipi en dingin i paipih hi.

records.english: He took off his shoes and stood in the waves for a long time without saying anything.
records.zomi: A khedap a sut a, bangmah gen lo-in hun sawt tuipi kihawk sung ah a ding hi.

records.english: On the way home, he told us it was the best present he had ever received.
records.zomi: Inn lam ah a ngah ngei letsong hoih pen ahi hi, ci-in hong hilh hi.

records.english: Please don't let your little sister climb the mango tree.
records.zomi: Na nau nu haigah kung tungah kahsak kei in.

records.english: If my aunt hadn't taught me to cook, I couldn't have looked after my brothers that year.
records.zomi: Ka ni in an huan hong hilh kei le, tua kum ka sanggam pasalte ka kem thei kei ding hi.

records.english: Whoever came home from school first had to check on Grandma and make her tea.
records.zomi: Sang pan inn a tung masa peuhpeuh in ka pi a en ding a, tea a bawl sak ding hi.

records.english: Last spring, my son pushed his grandmother's wheelchair all the way around the lake.
records.zomi: Kum nung spring in ka tapa in a pi' tutna leng dil kim bup ah a nawt hi.

records.english: Do you remember carrying me to school on your back when the road was deep in mud?
records.zomi: Lampi a bual thuk laitakin na nung tungah sang ah hong pua na phawk hiam?

records.english: Every morning for a month, and you complained the whole way.
records.zomi: Kha khat sung zingsang simin, lampi bup na phun hi.

records.english: Tell me about the day your little sister was born.
records.zomi: Na nau nu a suah ni thu hong gen in.

records.english: Shall I tell you how we looked after Grandpa during his last winter?
records.zomi: Ka pu' khuavot nunung pen-in bangci-in i kem hiam kong gen ding hiam?

records.english: When my grandfather got his first hearing aid, he complained that the world was suddenly far too noisy.
records.zomi: Ka pu in a bil set masa pen a ngah ciangin leitung a ging lua thak hi, ci-in a phun hi.

records.english: After a week, he admitted he had missed the sound of the birds for years.
records.zomi: Kal khat khit ciangin kum tampi sung vasa ging a lungngai hi, ci-in a pang hi.

records.english: What I remember most about caring for my grandmother is the stories she told while I peeled vegetables beside her.
records.zomi: Ka pi kemna ah ka phawk pen pen a kiang ah anteh ka khilh laitakin a gen tangthute ahi hi.

records.english: Did your grandmother ever look after the whole street's children?
records.zomi: Na pi in lampi bup-a naupangte a kem ngei hiam?

records.english: The more time I spent with my grandmother, the more patient I became with everyone else.
records.zomi: Ka pi tawh hun tam ka zat semsem ciangin mi dang khempeuh tungah ka thuakzawh semsem hi.

records.english: Rather than sending my grandfather to a care home, the whole family shared looking after him.
records.zomi: Upate kemna inn ah ka pu sawl sangin innkuan bup in a kem kihawm uh hi.

records.english: How did your family manage when both your parents were ill?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa a nih un a dam loh ciangin na innkuan bangci-in a om uh hiam?

records.english: Was your grandfather a patient man?
records.zomi: Na pu thuakzawh mi ahi hiam?

records.english: We bought a small bell for my grandmother to ring if she needed help at night.
records.zomi: Zan ah huhna a kisap leh a sak nadingin ka pi adingin khawngging neu khat i lei hi.

records.english: After my aunt became ill, my cousin came to live with us for two years.
records.zomi: Ka ni a dam loh khit ciangin ka sanggam kum nih sung i kiang ah a om hi.

records.english: We shared a bedroom, and I lent her my bicycle so that she could get to school.
records.zomi: Lupna khan i kihawm a, sang a tun theih nadingin ka siiksakol ka ngetsak hi.

records.english: She still calls me her sister, even though we're cousins.
records.zomi: Sanggam i hih hangin a sanggam nu hong ci lai hi.

records.english: How old were you when you first cooked for your grandparents?
records.zomi: Na pu leh pite adingin an na huan masak ciangin kum bangzah na hi hiam?

records.english: Before she grew too frail to travel, my grandmother asked to visit her home village one last time.
records.zomi: Khualzin zawh loh dingin a hat lo ma-in ka pi in a khua a veh nunung pen dingin a ngen hi.

records.english: My uncle drove her there, and she showed us the house where she was born.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in a paipih a, a suahna inn hong etsak hi.

records.english: An old friend of hers recognized her at once and cried as they held hands.
records.zomi: A lawm lui khat in a man takin a thei a, khut kilen-in a kap uh hi.

records.english: Who taught you to change a nappy?
records.zomi: Naungek puan lai dan kua in hong hilh hiam?

records.english: It was only when my own children were born that I understood how tired my parents must have been.
records.zomi: Keima' tate a suah ciang bek ka nu leh ka pa bangzah a tawl ding uh hiam ka thei hi.

records.english: The nurse said, "Talk to her, even if she doesn't answer, because she can still hear you."
records.zomi: Nurse in, “A dawng kei zongin a kiangah gen in, a za lai hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: When did you first look after a baby on your own?
records.zomi: Bang ciangin nangma bek in naungek na kem masa hiam?

records.english: Which of your grandparents did you spend most time with?
records.zomi: Na pu leh pite lak ah kua tawh hun tam pen na zang hiam?

records.english: In my grandparents' house, my grandfather beat a small drum at dawn to wake everyone for prayer.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh pite' inn ah ka pu in mi khempeuh thungetna adingin a phawngsak nadingin khuavak ciangin khuang neu khat a tum hi.

records.english: I was given my first watch at twelve so that I could get myself to school on time.
records.zomi: Hun takin sang ah ka pai theih nadingin kum sawm leh nih ciangin ka nai masa pen hong pia uh hi.

records.english: Which morning do you remember best from your childhood?
records.zomi: Na naupan lai pan koi zingsang na phawk pen hiam?

records.english: Can I wear my brother's old sweater to school?
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal' puan vot lui sang ah ka silh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Tell me about your first morning at boarding school.
records.zomi: Om-in kah sang ah na zingsang masa pen thu hong gen in.

records.english: Why did your grandfather always shave by the window?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na pu tukvuang kiang ah a khamul a met tawntung hiam?

records.english: However late we had gone to bed, my grandfather expected us at the breakfast table by six.
records.zomi: Bangzah nai-in i lum zongin ka pu in nai guk ciangin zingsang an dawhkan ah hong lamen hi.

records.english: The bus driver honked twice outside our gate every morning so that nobody would miss the school bus.
records.zomi: Kuamah in sang bus a mansuah lo nadingin bus mawngpa in zingsang simin i kongpi pua ah nihvei a ging sak hi.

records.english: On our first night camping, we woke up soaked because the tent had been put up on a slope.
records.zomi: I zan masa pen puan inn ah i om zan-in puan inn mual ding ah kilam ahih manin dikdek-in i khanglawh hi.

records.english: Where did you wash in the mornings when you lived in the village?
records.zomi: Khua ah na om laitakin zingsangin koi ah na kisil hiam?

records.english: Who cooked breakfast in your house?
records.zomi: Na inn ah zingsang an kua in a huan hiam?

records.english: Every morning, my older sister checked my homework while I ate my breakfast.
records.zomi: Zingsang simin zingsang an ka nek laitakin ka u nu in ka inn-a sep ding a en hi.

records.english: What time did you have to get up when you were a child?
records.zomi: Na naupan lai-in nai bangzah ciangin na thou ding a kisam hiam?

records.english: Before sunrise, because we had to fetch water from the spring before school.
records.zomi: Ni suak ma-in, sang ma-in tui zuk pan tui i la ding ahih manin.

records.english: Although we had no running water, we were always clean and tidy for school.
records.zomi: Tui khuk i nei kei hangin sang adingin i siang a, i kiman tawntung hi.

records.english: On my sister's wedding morning, the whole house was awake by four.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu' mopawi zingsang-in inn bup nai li ciangin a thou khin hi.

records.english: Our aunts did her hair, the cousins ironed the dresses, and I polished everyone's shoes.
records.zomi: I nite in a sam a bawl sak uh a, sanggamte in puante a phawk uh a, kei in mi khempeuh' khedap ka nul hi.

records.english: By eight, we were all ready, and nobody had slept more than three hours.
records.zomi: Nai giat ciangin i khempeuh i kiman khin a, kuamah nai thum sangin a ihmu kei uh hi.

records.english: The colder the morning, the longer we stayed under our blankets.
records.zomi: Zingsang a vot semsem ciangin i puannak nuai ah sawt zawin i om hi.

records.english: Whatever the season, my aunt took a cold bath every morning and insisted that it kept her healthy.
