records.zomi: Huihkhua bang ahi zongin ka ni zingsang simin tui vot tawh a kisil a, a cidam nadingin a huh hi, a ci hi.

records.english: My father's old wind-up alarm clock was so loud that it woke the whole house.
records.zomi: Ka pa' alarm nai lui a ging sang lua ahih manin inn bup a phawngsak hi.

records.english: The morning bread was always delivered to our door before six.
records.zomi: Zingsang moh nai guk ma-in i kongkhak ah kipuak tawntung hi.

records.english: When my uncle joined the army, the sergeant woke the soldiers by shouting, "Up, up, up!"
records.zomi: Ka pa neu galkap ah a lut ciangin a makaipa in, “Thou un, thou un, thou un!” ci-in galkapte a phawngsak hi.

records.english: Why did your family always get up so early on Sundays?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Nipini simin na innkuan a thou ma uh hiam?

records.english: My school uniform was always laid out on the chair the night before.
records.zomi: Ka sang puan zan ma-in tutna tungah kikoih khol tawntung hi.

records.english: When I started work at the bakery, I had to get up at four every morning.
records.zomi: Moh bawlna ah ka sep kipat ciangin zingsang simin nai li ciangin ka thou ding a kisam hi.

records.english: For the first week, I walked to work half asleep and once put sugar in the bread instead of salt.
records.zomi: Kal masa sungin ihmu lai-in nasepna ah ka kalsuan a, khatvei moh ah cii sangin sugar ka koih hi.

records.english: The baker laughed and told me that every new baker makes that mistake once.
records.zomi: Moh bawlpa a nui a, moh bawl thak khempeuh in khatvei tua khialhna a bawl uh hi, hong ci hi.

records.english: The village loudspeaker woke everyone with music at six on festival days.
records.zomi: Pawi ni-in khua ging sanna in nai guk ciangin la tawh mi khempeuh a phawngsak hi.

records.english: Looking back, those cold mornings taught me to be grateful for a hot shower.
records.zomi: Nung lam en kik-in tua zingsang votte in tui lum kisilna adingin lungdam dingin hong hilh hi.

records.english: Last winter, our pipes froze, and we had to boil snow to wash.
records.zomi: Kum nung khuavot in i tui khuamte a khal a, kisil dingin vuk i suang ding a kisam hi.

records.english: Mornings in our crowded house were like a busy market, because everyone needed the same things at once.
records.zomi: I inn mi tam-a zingsangte pen zuakna mun buai bang ahi a, mi khempeuh in khatvei-in van kibang a kisam uh hi.

records.english: How did your grandparents know what time it was without a clock?
records.zomi: Nai om lo-in na pu leh pite in hun bangzah ahi hiam bangci-in a thei uh hiam?

records.english: On the morning of my final exam, I rushed out of the house in two different shoes.
records.zomi: Ka sitna nunung pen zingsang-in khedap kibang lo nih tawh inn pan ka tai khia hi.

records.english: I only noticed when a classmate pointed at my feet and laughed.
records.zomi: Kilasi lawm khat in ka khe a lak a, a nuih ciang bek ka thei hi.

records.english: I passed the exam anyway, and I kept the odd shoes as a lucky charm.
records.zomi: Tua mah in sitna ka zo a, khedap kibang lote vangphatna lahna-in ka kem hi.

records.english: Please don't wake your brother; he worked the night shift.
records.zomi: Na sanggam pasal phawngsak kei in; zan nasep a sem hi.

records.english: Did you ever sleep through your alarm on an important day?
records.zomi: Ni thupi khat ah na alarm na za lo-in na ihmu ngei hiam?

records.english: Children, wash your faces in the river and come back for breakfast.
records.zomi: Naupangte, gun ah na mai uh sil unla, zingsang an adingin hong kik un.

records.english: Who woke you up when you were small?
records.zomi: Na neu lai-in kua in hong phawngsak hiam?

records.english: My grandmother, who sang the same hymn every morning as she opened the shutters.
records.zomi: Ka pi, tukvuang khuhte a hon laitakin zingsang simin la kibang a sa pa.

records.english: Did you have to make your own bed?
records.zomi: Na lupna nangma-in na bawl ding a kisam hiam?

records.english: Shall I tell you how your grandfather got ready for church?
records.zomi: Na pu pawlpi adingin bangci-in a kiman hiam kong gen ding hiam?

records.english: We weren't allowed to leave the house without eating breakfast, however late we were.
records.zomi: Bangzah nun zongin zingsang an ne lo-in inn nusia dingin kiphal lo hi.

records.english: What I remember most about those early mornings is the sound of cattle bells as the herders passed our house.
records.zomi: Tua zingsang tungte ah ka phawk pen pen gan kemte i inn a khen ciangun bawng khawngging ging ahi hi.

records.english: If the rooster hadn't crowed, half the village would have overslept.
records.zomi: Akpa a khuan kei le, khua a khen khat in ihmut a lua ding uh hi.

records.english: May I sleep a little longer, since it's a holiday?
records.zomi: Nopsakna ni ahih manin tawmno sawt zawin ka ihmu thei ding hiam?

records.english: It was during those dark winter mornings that I learned to dress quickly without making a sound.
records.zomi: Tua khuavot zingsang mialte sungin ging bawl lo-in manlang takin puan silh ka sin hi.

records.english: Would we have been so punctual if the school bus driver hadn't honked at our gate?
records.zomi: Sang bus mawngpa in i kongpi ah ging a sak kei le, hun takin i om ding hiam?

records.english: Whoever woke up first had to light the stove for everyone else.
records.zomi: A thou masa peuhpeuh in mi dang khempeuh adingin meikhuk a hal ding hi.

records.english: Rather than shouting at us to get up, my grandfather would open the curtains and start singing.
records.zomi: Thou dingin hong kou sangin ka pu in tukvuang puan a hon a, la a sa kipan hi.

records.english: Our cockerel crowed so early that the neighbors complained to my grandmother.
records.zomi: I akpa a ma lua-in a khuan ahih manin inn vengte in ka pi kiangah a phun uh hi.

records.english: She moved the cockerel to the far side of the yard, and peace returned.
records.zomi: Akpa tual gal lam ah a suan a, daihna a hong kik hi.

records.english: It was only after I left home that I realized how early my parents must have got up to prepare our breakfast.
records.zomi: Inn ka nusiat khit ciang bek i zingsang an bawl dingin ka nu leh ka pa bangzah ma-in a thou uh hiam ka thei hi.

records.english: When did you first have to get yourself ready for school?
records.zomi: Bang ciangin sang adingin nangma-in na kiman masa hiam?

records.english: Do you remember the winter when the water in the washbasin froze every night?
records.zomi: Zan simin kisilna kuang sung-a tui a khal khuavot na phawk hiam?

records.english: We had to break the ice with a cup before we could wash our faces.
records.zomi: I mai i sil ma-in haai tawh tuikhal i kek ding a kisam hi.

records.english: At boarding school, a bell rang at six, and we had ten minutes to wash and dress.
records.zomi: Om-in kah sang ah nai guk ciangin khawngging a ging a, kisil-in puan silh dingin minit sawm i nei hi.

records.english: Anyone who arrived late at breakfast had to sweep the dining hall.
records.zomi: Zingsang an ah a nun peuhpeuh in an nekna inn a phiat ding hi.

records.english: I was late only once, and I've been early for everything ever since.
records.zomi: Khatvei bek ka nun a, tua pan kipan bangkim ah ka tung masa tawntung hi.

records.english: The map showed where the treasure was buried, but it turned out to be a joke.
records.zomi: Map in sum guk koi ah kivui hiam a lak a, ahi zongin nuihzat bek ahi hi.

records.english: Nobody knows where the old key to the church was hidden.
records.zomi: Pawlpi tawh lui koi ah kisel hiam kuamah in a thei kei hi.

records.english: When I was small, I hid my grandmother's keys and forgot where I had put them.
records.zomi: Ka neu lai-in ka pi' tawhte ka sel a, koi ah ka koih hiam ka mangngilh hi.

records.english: The whole family searched the house for an hour.
records.zomi: Innkuan bup in nai khat sung inn a zong uh hi.

records.english: In the end, my little brother found them inside my shoe.
records.zomi: A tawp-in ka nau pasal in ka khedap sung ah a mu hi.

records.english: Where was the old school before it was moved?
records.zomi: Sang lui a kisuan ma-in koi ah a om hiam?

records.english: Behind the church, where the car park is now.
records.zomi: Pawlpi nung ah, tu-a mawtaw koihna mun ah.

records.english: Tell me where you were when you heard the news.
records.zomi: Thu na zak ciangin koi ah na om hiam hong gen in.

records.english: Where can I leave my bicycle?
records.zomi: Ka siiksakol koi ah ka nusia thei ding hiam?

records.english: There's a rack by the side door, but bring your own lock.
records.zomi: A gei kongkhak kiang ah koihna a om hi, ahi zongin nangma' khakna tawi in.

records.english: The teacher asked, "Where would you go if you could travel anywhere?"
records.zomi: Saya in, “Koi peuh ah na khualzin thei leh koi ah na pai ding hiam?” a ci hi.

records.english: Where did the money go?
records.zomi: Sum koi ah a pai hiam?

records.english: Most of it was spent on repairing the roof after the storm.
records.zomi: A tamzaw huihpi khit ciangin innkhum bawl siang ah kizang hi.

records.english: Ask the driver where we should get off.
records.zomi: Koi ah i tum ding hiam mawngpa dong in.

records.english: Where the old mill once stood, there is now a small playground for the village children.
records.zomi: Buh guaina inn lui a din mun ah tu-in khua naupangte adingin kimawlna mun neu khat a om hi.

records.english: Wherever the children are playing, someone should be able to see them from the house.
records.zomi: Naupangte koi ah kimawl zongun inn pan kuamah in a mu thei ding hi.

records.english: What I'd like to know is where the old photographs ended up after the move.
records.zomi: Ka theih nuam pen pen tuah khit ciangin lim luite koi ah a tung hiam, cih ahi hi.

records.english: Where did you put my glasses?
records.zomi: Ka mitlimlang koi ah na koih hiam?

records.english: They're on the kitchen table, next to the newspaper.
records.zomi: An huanna dawhkan tungah, laithak kiang ah a om hi.

records.english: Where did your grandparents live when they were young?
records.zomi: Na pu leh pite a khangno lai uh-in koi ah a om uh hiam?

records.english: In a village by the river, before the road was built.
records.zomi: Lampi a kibawl ma-in gun kiang-a khua khat ah.

records.english: Could you tell me where the toilets are?
records.zomi: Ek inn koi ah a om hiam hong gen thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Where should we meet after the concert?
records.zomi: La pawi khit ciangin koi ah i kimu ding hiam?

records.english: By the main gate, under the big tree.
records.zomi: Kongpi lian kiang ah, singkung lian nuai ah.

records.english: Where were the photos taken?
records.zomi: Limte koi ah kila hiam?

records.english: At my cousin's wedding, in the garden behind her house.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam' mopawi ah, a inn nung-a huan sung ah.

records.english: Where does this road lead?
records.zomi: Hih lampi koi ah a pai hiam?

records.english: To the next village, about ten kilometers away.
records.zomi: A kiang khua ah, kilometer sawm bang gamla ah.

records.english: Where should I put these boxes?
records.zomi: Hih bawmte koi ah ka koih ding hiam?

records.english: In the storeroom, but don't block the door.
records.zomi: Van koihna khan ah, ahi zongin kongkhak khak kei in.

records.english: Could you write down where the clinic is, so that my mother can find it?
records.zomi: Ka nu in a muh theih nadingin siavuan inn koi ah a om hiam na gelh sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Rather than asking where the station was, my grandfather followed the sound of the trains.
records.zomi: Meileng dinna koi ah a om hiam dong sangin ka pu in meileng ging a zui hi.

records.english: If I knew where my old diary was, I'd read it to you.
records.zomi: Ka diary lui koi ah a om hiam ka theih leh kong sim sak ding hi.

records.english: However hard we tried, we couldn't work out where the strange noise was coming from.
records.zomi: Bangzah ta in hanciam zongin ging lamdang koi pan a hong hiam i thei zo kei hi.

records.english: Where is the nearest pharmacy?
records.zomi: A kiang pen zatui zuakna koi ah a om hiam?

records.english: Just past the bank, on the left side of the street.
records.zomi: Bank khen pah-in, lampi veilam ah.

records.english: Looking at the map, the children tried to guess where their grandparents had been born.
records.zomi: Map en-in naupangte in a pu leh pite uh koi ah a suak uh hiam a ngaihsun uh hi.

records.english: Where the road divides, keep to the left unless you want to end up at the quarry.
records.zomi: Lampi a kikhen mun ah suang taina ah na tun nuam kei leh veilam ah zui in.

records.english: Wherever you live in the world, you'll always be welcome in our home.
records.zomi: Leitung ah koi peuh ah om zongin i inn ah na kimuak tawntung ding hi.

records.english: I really do want to know where you found such a beautiful scarf.
records.zomi: Tua bang ngawngkhih hoih koi ah na mu hiam theih ka deih mahmah hi.

records.english: No one could explain where the strange stones in the field had come from.
records.zomi: Lo sung-a suang lamdangte koi pan a hong hiam kuamah in a gen siang thei kei uh hi.

records.english: Where are you from?
records.zomi: Koi pan na hong hiam?

records.english: I grew up in a small town in the hills, but I live in the city now.
records.zomi: Mual tung-a khuapi neu khat ah ka khang a, ahi zongin tu-in khuapi lian ah ka om hi.

records.english: Show me on the map where your village is.
records.zomi: Map tungah na khua koi ah a om hiam hong etsak in.

records.english: Where will you live when you start university?
records.zomi: Sangpi na kah kipat ciangin koi ah na om ding hiam?

records.english: In a shared flat near the campus, with two friends from school.
records.zomi: Sangpi kiang-a kihawm inn khat ah, sang pan lawm nih tawh.

records.english: I can't remember where I parked the car.
records.zomi: Mawtaw koi ah ka koih hiam ka phawk thei kei hi.

records.english: In this town, where are we not allowed to take photos?
records.zomi: Hih khuapi ah koi ah lim la dingin kiphal lo hiam?

records.english: Inside the museum and anywhere near the military base.
records.zomi: Museum sung leh galkap mun kiang khempeuh ah.

records.english: Where exactly did you leave the car keys last night?
records.zomi: Zanni zanin mawtaw tawhte koi ah na nusia taktak hiam?

records.english: Wherever we went, my little sister wanted to come too.
records.zomi: Koi ah i pai zongin ka nau nu in a hong khawm nuam hi.

records.english: Do you remember where we went on our first holiday together?
records.zomi: I nopsakna hun masa pen-in koi ah i pai hiam na phawk hiam?

records.english: Although we searched everywhere, nobody could find where the cat had hidden her kittens.
records.zomi: Mun khempeuh i zon hangin zawh in a tate koi ah a selsak hiam kuamah in a mu kei uh hi.

records.english: It was only when we reached the top of the hill that we could see where the river began.
records.zomi: Mual tung i tun ciang bek gun koi pan a kipan hiam i mu thei hi.

records.english: Where do the children play when it rains?
records.zomi: Guah a zuk ciangin naupangte koi ah a kimawl uh hiam?

records.english: In the church hall, which the pastor opens for them.
records.zomi: Pastor in a hon sak pawlpi inn ah.

records.english: Do you know where the meeting is being held?
records.zomi: Kikhopna koi ah kibawl hiam na thei hiam?

records.english: Where there's a will, there's a way, my grandfather used to say.
records.zomi: Deihna a om leh lampi a om hi, ci-in ka pu in a gen den hi.

records.english: Where do you usually buy your vegetables?
records.zomi: A tamzaw-in koi ah anteh na lei hiam?

records.english: From the market, because the farmers bring them in fresh every morning.
records.zomi: Zuakna mun pan, lo neite in zingsang simin a thak a tawi uh ahih manin.

records.english: Our first attempt at baking a birthday cake ended with flour all over the kitchen.
records.zomi: Pianni cake i bawl masakna an huanna bup ah buh-mal zel tawh a tawp hi.

records.english: Every summer, we picked wild berries on the hillside and made jam with our aunt.
records.zomi: Khal simin mual gei ah gam theigah i lo a, i ni tawh jam i bawl hi.

records.english: What I remember most about those summers is the taste of jam on warm bread.
records.zomi: Tua nipite ah ka phawk pen pen moh lum tung-a jam tui ahi hi.

records.english: Why did the cooks at the festival always start before dawn?
records.zomi: Bang hangin pawi-a an huante khuavak ma-in a kipan tawntung uh hiam?

records.english: Where did you learn to make such good dumplings?
records.zomi: Tua bang dumpling hoih bawl dan koi ah na sin hiam?

records.english: The jam jars were sealed with wax and stored under the bed.
records.zomi: Jam bel te khuai-at tawh kikhak a, lupna nuai ah kikoih hi.

records.english: It was only after the guests had gone that we realized nobody had eaten the dessert.
records.zomi: Khualte a pai khit ciang bek kuamah in an lim a ne kei uh hi, cih i thei hi.

records.english: Do you remember the cooking competition at our school?
records.zomi: I sang-a an huan kidemna na phawk hiam?

records.english: Our team made banana pancakes and won second prize, even though one of them fell on the floor.
records.zomi: I pawl in nahtang pancake a bawl a, khat tual ah a kia hangin letsong nihna i ngah hi.

records.english: Tell me what you ate on the fishing trips with your uncle.
records.zomi: Na pa neu tawh nga man khualzinna ah bang na ne uh hiam hong gen in.

records.english: Shall I tell you about the time we cooked for a hundred guests?
records.zomi: Khual za khat adingin an i huan hun thu kong gen ding hiam?

records.english: Why did your aunt always cook with a wood fire instead of gas?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na ni in gas sangin sing mei tawh an a huan tawntung hiam?

records.english: After I moved abroad, I missed my sister's chicken curry so much that I phoned her for the recipe.
records.zomi: Gamdang ah ka tuah khit ciangin ka sanggam nu' aksa curry ka lungngai lua ahih manin a bawl dan dingin ka sam hi.

records.english: She talked me through every step while I cooked in my tiny kitchen.
records.zomi: Ka an huanna neu mahmah ah an ka huan laitakin khekhap khempeuh a gen sak hi.

records.english: It didn't taste quite like hers, but it made me feel at home.
records.zomi: Amah' bangin a tui kim kei hi, ahi zongin inn bangin hong kisaksak hi.

records.english: The neighbors were invited to taste our first harvest of sweet potatoes.
records.zomi: I kaihawl masak kawl lumte' lim et dingin inn vengte i sam hi.

records.english: The old cooking pot was cracked, so we used it to grow flowers.
records.zomi: An huanna beel lui a kek ahih manin pak suan nadingin i zang hi.

records.english: On our school trip to the mountains, we cooked dinner over a campfire for the first time.
records.zomi: Sang pan mual lam khualzinna ah meikuang tungah nitak an i huan masak pen ahi hi.

records.english: The rice was half raw and the sausages were black, but nobody complained.
records.zomi: Buh a min a kim kei a, sa-tum te a vom hangin kuamah in a phun kei uh hi.

records.english: Our teacher said it was the best meal she had eaten all year.
records.zomi: I saya in kum khat sungah a an nek hoih pen ahi hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Did your family ever cook outdoors?
records.zomi: Na innkuan in inn pua ah an a huan ngei uh hiam?

records.english: By the time the guests arrived, every pot in the house had been used at least twice.
records.zomi: Khualte a tun ciangin inn sung-a beel khempeuh khat nihvei bek hi zongin kizang khin hi.

records.english: Our bus broke down on a mountain road, miles from any town.
records.zomi: I bus in khuapi khat peuh pan gamla mahmah mual lampi tungah a sia hi.

records.english: The passengers shared whatever food they had, and a farmer brought us boiled corn.
records.zomi: Khualzinte in an a neih peuhpeuh uh a kihawm uh a, lo nei khat in vaimim lum hong tawi hi.

records.english: It turned into a picnic that none of us has forgotten.
records.zomi: Tua pen kuamah in i mangngilh nai loh khualzin an nekna khat suak hi.

records.english: Kids, I'll tell you how we made ice cream with snow when I was a boy.
records.zomi: Naupangte, ka neu lai-in vuk tawh ice cream bangci-in i bawl hiam kong gen ding hi.

records.english: Whoever caught the most fish got to choose how they were cooked.
records.zomi: Nga tampen a man peuhpeuh in bangci-in huan ding hiam a teel thei hi.

records.english: The stew we cooked for the festival tasted even better the next morning.
records.zomi: Pawi adingin i huan an tui in a zing zingsang ciangin a lim zaw lai hi.

records.english: We were told that the recipe for the festival bread had been kept secret for generations.
records.zomi: Pawi moh bawl dan pen khang tampi sung kisel hi, ci-in hong kigen hi.

records.english: How did your family keep food fresh before you had a fridge?
records.zomi: Vot sak setna na neih ma-in na innkuan in an bangci-in a kem uh hiam?

records.english: May I taste the sauce before it goes on the table?
records.zomi: Dawhkan tungah a kikoih ma-in a tui ka lim et thei ding hiam?

records.english: We used to bake bread in a clay oven that my uncle had built in the yard.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in huan sungah a bawl leivui meikhuk sungah moh i em ngei hi.

records.english: We cooked rice in bamboo tubes on the fire, the way our grandparents had done.
records.zomi: I pu leh pite' bawl bangin meikuang tungah gua sungah buh i huan hi.

records.english: The longer the soup simmered, the more neighbors seemed to find a reason to visit.
records.zomi: An tui a sawt huan semsem ciangin inn vengte in hong pai nading thu a mu semsem bang uh hi.

records.english: Would the bread have tasted the same if we had baked it in an ordinary oven?
records.zomi: Meikhuk tavuan-a i em hileh moh a lim kibang ding hiam?

records.english: When I was twelve, my uncle taught me to smoke fish by the river.
records.zomi: Kum sawm leh nih ka phak ciangin ka pa neu in gun kiang ah nga khu-a hal dan hong sin sak hi.

records.english: We hung the fish over a slow fire made from green branches.
records.zomi: Sing hing tawh i hal mei neu tungah nga i khai hi.

records.english: By evening, the whole village could smell it, and three neighbors came to buy some.
records.zomi: Nitak ciangin khua bup in a gim a za uh a, inn vengte thum in lei dingin hong pai uh hi.

records.english: I really did want to help with the cooking, but I was always sent out to fetch water.
records.zomi: An huan huh ka deih taktak hi, ahi zongin tui la dingin hong sawl tawntung uh hi.

records.english: Last year, my son made his first loaf of bread and gave it to his teacher.
records.zomi: Kum nung in ka tapa in a moh bawl masak pen a bawl a, a saya a pia hi.

records.english: Which dish did your aunt make for every celebration?
records.zomi: Na ni in pawi khempeuh adingin an bang a bawl tawntung hiam?

records.english: Did you ever help at a wedding feast?
records.zomi: Mopawi an kuan ah na huh ngei hiam?

records.english: Everyone, the story I'm going to tell you happened in a kitchen in the mountains.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh aw, kong gen ding thu pen mual tung-a an huanna khat ah a piang hi.

records.english: Who taught you to make noodles by hand?
records.zomi: Khut tawh khauhsawk bawl dan kua in hong sin sak hiam?

records.english: An old woman in the market, who let me watch her every Saturday.
records.zomi: Zuakna mun-a numei upa khat in, Kiginni simin a bawl a en dingin hong phal hi.

records.english: If my uncle hadn't shown me how to clean a fish, I would have gone hungry on that fishing trip.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in nga silh dan hong lak kei hileh, tua nga man khualzinna ah ka gil a kial ding hi.

records.english: Rather than buying sweets, my aunt taught us to make our own from coconut and sugar.
records.zomi: Thei khum lei sangin ka ni in onkuang leh sugar tawh nangmah i bawl ding hong sin sak hi.

records.english: When our neighbor's daughter married, ten women from the street cooked for three days.
records.zomi: I inn vengte' tanu a ten ciangin lampi pan numei sawm in ni thum sung an a huan uh hi.

records.english: Although we had very little, there was always enough food for an unexpected guest.
records.zomi: Tawmno bek i nei hangin a lamdang-a hong tung khual adingin an a kicing tawntung hi.

records.english: Looking back, those simple meals cooked over the fire were the best I've ever had.
records.zomi: Nung lam en kik-in tua meikuang tung-a i huan an neute pen ka nek ngei hoih pen ahi hi.

records.english: The cook shouted, "Don't you dare touch that pot!"
records.zomi: An huanpa in, “Tua beel na khoih ngam kei in!” ci-in a kiko hi.

records.english: What did you cook when you first lived alone?
records.zomi: Nangma bek na om masak ciangin bang na huan hiam?

records.english: Can you show me how your aunt rolled the dumplings?
records.zomi: Na ni in dumpling bangci-in a lum hiam hong lak thei ding hiam?

records.english: What did you eat on your first evening with your host family abroad?
records.zomi: Gamdang ah na om khopna innkuan tawh na nitak masak pen-in bang na ne hiam?

records.english: A soup I couldn't name, eaten with a spoon so wide that I spilled half of it.
records.zomi: A min ka theih loh an tui khat, kawm zai mahmah tawh ka nek ahih manin a kim ka sungkhia hi.

records.english: When did you first cook a meal for the whole family?
records.zomi: Bang ciangin innkuan bup adingin an na huan masa hiam?

records.english: A whole basket of tomatoes was knocked over by the goats.
records.zomi: Kel te in mehtuuk bawm khat bup a lehlap uh hi.

records.english: Was the food at your boarding school any good?
records.zomi: Na om-in kah sang-a an hoih hiam?

records.english: Cooking with my aunt was like going to school, because every dish came with a lesson.
records.zomi: Ka ni tawh an huan pen sang kah bang ahi a, an khempeuh in thu sin khat a nei hi.

records.english: Children weren't allowed to touch the hot jars until they had cooled completely.
records.zomi: Bel lum te a vot kim mateng naupangte in a khoih dingin kiphal lo hi.

records.english: Why did your family keep everything in labeled boxes?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na innkuan in bangkim min kigelh bawm sungah a koih uh hiam?

records.english: How did your family get the house ready for the New Year?
records.zomi: Kum Thak adingin na innkuan in inn bangci-in a kiman sak uh hiam?

records.english: My brother's room was so messy that our aunt refused to go in.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal' inndei a buai lua ahih manin i ni in lut a nuam kei hi.

records.english: If the books hadn't been sorted, the library could never have opened on time.
records.zomi: Laibu te kikhen kei hileh laibu inn hun takin kihong thei lo ding hi.

records.english: Could you have imagined how much rubbish was hidden under that old bridge?
records.zomi: Tua lei lui nuai ah bang zah eek kisel hiam na ngaihsun thei ding hiam?

records.english: Everyone, check under the benches for anything you've left behind.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh aw, na nusiat peuh om leh tutphah nuai ah en un.

records.english: Did you ever find anything valuable while you were cleaning?
records.zomi: Na sianseh lai-in man-gen khat peuh na mu ngei hiam?

records.english: Looking back, those cleaning days brought the whole family together more than any holiday.
records.zomi: Nung lam en kik-in tua inn sianseh nite in nopsakna ni khempeuh sangin innkuan bup a kikhawmsak zaw hi.

records.english: What I remember most about cleaning days is the music my uncle played while we worked.
records.zomi: Inn sianseh nite thu ah ka phawk pen pen i sep laitakin ka pa neu' la a sak ahi hi.

records.english: Why did your aunt label the seed jars with pictures instead of words?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na ni in khaici bel te kammal sangin lim tawh a gelh hiam?

records.english: Children, wipe the blackboard and water the plants before you go home.
records.zomi: Naupangte, inn na pai ma-un laigelhna phek nul unla, pak te tui buak un.

records.english: Whatever we found during the spring clean, our aunt would tell us a story about it.
records.zomi: Spring siansuahna lai-in bang peuh i mu zongin i ni in tua thu a gen hi.

records.english: Do you remember sorting all those donated books for the new village library?
records.zomi: Khua laibu inn thak adingin kipiak laibu te i khen na phawk hiam?

records.english: It took us a whole month, and we found three books that had belonged to our old teacher.
records.zomi: Kha khat bup hong sawt a, i saya lui' laibu thum i mu hi.

records.english: I really did want to help our aunt sort her seeds, but I kept mixing up the beans and the peas.
records.zomi: I ni' khaici khen huh ka deih taktak a, ahi zongin bepi leh bekang ka kilamdang thei kei hi.

records.english: She labeled every jar with a picture, so that even I couldn't get it wrong.
records.zomi: Bel khempeuh lim tawh a gelh ahih manin keimah in zong ka khial thei kei hi.

records.english: You weren't allowed to throw anything into the river near our house.
records.zomi: I inn kiang-a gun sungah bangmah na paih dingin kiphal lo hi.

records.english: The broken toys were mended with glue and given to the younger children.
records.zomi: Kimawlna van kitam te sik-at tawh kibawl a, naupang neu zaw te kipia hi.

records.english: Whoever finished their part of the cleaning first was allowed to choose the music.
records.zomi: Inn sianseh a kim tawp masa peuhpeuh in la a teel thei hi.

records.english: Rather than throwing away the old curtains, my aunt cut them up to make cushions.
records.zomi: Tukvuang puan lui te paih sangin ka ni in a at a lupna khuh a bawl hi.

records.english: Who kept your house tidiest?
records.zomi: Na inn ah kua in a siang sak pen hiam?

records.english: After my birthday party, we found cake on the ceiling and a balloon inside the oven.
records.zomi: Ka pianni pawi khit ciangin innkhum nuai ah cake leh meikhuk sungah balloon i mu hi.

records.english: After the storm, volunteers from three villages spent a weekend clearing rubbish from the beach.
records.zomi: Huihpi khit ciangin khua thum pan thalawpte in tuipi gei ah eek siang dingin kal tawp khat a zang uh hi.

records.english: The children found an old fishing net tangled around a rock and dragged it up the beach together.
records.zomi: Naupangte in suang khat ah a kisial nga lenpi lui khat a mu uh a, tuipi gei ah khawm in a kai tou uh hi.

records.english: What did you find under your bed?
records.zomi: Na lupna nuai ah bang na mu hiam?

records.english: Wouldn't it have been easier to throw away the old toys than to mend them all?
records.zomi: Kimawlna van lui te a vekpi bawl dam sangin paih leng a baih zaw kei ding hiam?

records.english: What did your aunt do with all the clothes you had outgrown?
records.zomi: Na ni in na lian khit puan te bang a bawl hiam?

records.english: She mended them and sent them to the families in the next valley.
records.zomi: A bawl dam a, a kiang guam-a innkuante kiangah a khak hi.

records.english: Where did your grandparents keep their important papers?
records.zomi: Na pu leh pite in a lai thupite koi ah a koih uh hiam?

records.english: Although the workshop was small, my grandfather could build almost anything in it.
records.zomi: Nasepna inn a neu hangin ka pu in bangkim kik dekin a bawl thei hi.

records.english: Tell me about the day you organized the school library.
records.zomi: Sang laibu inn na bawlkhiat ni thu hong gen in.

records.english: While we were cleaning under the old cupboard, my sister found a small silver bell covered in dust.
records.zomi: Van koihna lui nuai i sianseh laitakin ka sanggam nu in leh-ngun khawngging neu leivui tawh kikhuh khat a mu hi.

records.english: Our aunt said it was the bell her mother had used to call the children in from the fields.
records.zomi: Tua khawngging pen a nu in lo sung pan naupangte kou dingin a zat ahi hi, ci-in i ni in a gen hi.

records.english: Our aunt rang it at dinner, and everyone came running as if we were children again.
records.zomi: Nitak an ah i ni in a ging sak a, naupang i hih kik bangin mi khempeuh a tai uh hi.

records.english: Our kitchen shelves were organized by color, which made my uncle laugh.
records.zomi: I an huanna van koihna te a rong bangin kikoih ahih manin ka pa neu a nui hi.

records.english: Shall I tell you what we found when we emptied the old shed?
records.zomi: Van koihna inn lui i bawk ciangin bang i mu hiam kong gen ding hiam?

records.english: By the end of the week, even the oldest corners of the house had been swept.
records.zomi: Kal tawp ciangin inn sung-a ki lui pen te zong kiphiat khin hi.

records.english: Which job did you hate most on cleaning day?
records.zomi: Inn sianseh ni-in nasep bang na huat pen hiam?

records.english: It was only when the cupboard was empty that we saw how much space we really had.
records.zomi: Van koihna a bawk ciang bek mun bangzah taktak i nei hiam i mu hi.

records.english: The more we cleaned, the more forgotten things we discovered.
records.zomi: I sianseh semsem ciangin kimangngilh van tam semsem i mu hi.

records.english: Tidying my grandfather's workshop felt like reading a diary of his whole life.
records.zomi: Ka pu' nasepna inn kiman sak pen a nuntak bup diary sim bang ahi hi.

records.english: On the morning of my cousin's wedding, the boys washed and polished the old car.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam' mopawi zingsang-in tangvalte in mawtaw lui a sil uh a, a tang sak uh hi.

records.english: The girls tied ribbons and flowers to the doors and the mirrors.
records.zomi: Nungakte in kongkhak leh mai-et te ah puan zang leh pak a khih uh hi.

records.english: By noon, the car looked so beautiful that nobody recognized it.
records.zomi: Sun tak ciangin mawtaw a hoih lua ahih manin kuamah in a thei nawn kei uh hi.

records.english: Our neighbor said, "A clean yard tells visitors that they are welcome."
records.zomi: I inn vengpa in, “Huan siang in khualte a kimuak uh hi, ci-in a hilh hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: Who used to clean the church before the Sunday service?
records.zomi: Nipini kikhopna ma-in kua in pawlpi a sianseh ngei hiam?

records.english: A group of older women, who swept and dusted every Saturday afternoon.
records.zomi: Kiginni nitak lam simin a phiat a, leivui a sianseh numei upa pawl khat.

records.english: Last spring, my children helped me clear out the attic and found their own baby clothes.
records.zomi: Spring nung in ka tate in innkhum nuai-a van koihna siang dingin hong huh uh a, amau' naupang neu puan te a mu uh hi.

records.english: Was cleaning day fun or boring for you?
records.zomi: Inn sianseh ni pen nangma adingin nuam hiam, a ning lua hiam?

records.english: The old photographs were found in a biscuit tin at the back of the wardrobe.
records.zomi: Lim lui te puan koihna nung lam-a biscuit bawm khat sungah kimu hi.

records.english: When did you first clean your own room without being asked?
records.zomi: Hong kisawl lo-in na inndei nangma-in bang ciangin na siang sak masa hiam?

records.english: The day before the school inspectors arrived, every pupil was given a cleaning job.
records.zomi: Sang enkaktute a tun ma ni-in sangnaupang khempeuh sianseh nasep kipia hi.

records.english: We scrubbed the desks, swept the yard and painted the gate.
records.zomi: Dawhkan te i nul a, huan i phiat a, kongpi rong i nul hi.

records.english: The inspectors praised the school, but they never noticed that the paint was still wet.
records.zomi: Enkaktute in sang a phat uh a, ahi zongin rong a bil nai hi, cih a thei ngei kei uh hi.

records.english: Did you have to clean the classroom at your school?
records.zomi: Na sang ah sang inndei na siang sak ding a kisam hiam?

records.english: Every morning, the fruit seller arranged her mangoes in perfect pyramids on the stall.
records.zomi: Zingsang simin theigah zuakpa numei in a haigahte a zuakna dawhkan tungah a hoih takin a ngam hi.

records.english: However messy the house became during the week, it was always spotless by Sunday morning.
records.zomi: Kal sungin inn bangzah in buai zongin Nipini zingsang ciangin a siang tawntung hi.

records.english: When my grandfather's hands grew too weak for carpentry, my brother and I tidied his workshop.
records.zomi: Ka pu' khut in sing nasep a sep zawh nawn loh ciangin kei leh ka sanggam pasal in a nasepna inn i kiman sak hi.

records.english: We hung every tool on the wall and drew its outline around it so that nothing would be lost.
records.zomi: Bangmah a mang lohna dingin nasepna van khempeuh bang ah i khai a, a kiim i gelh hi.

records.english: Grandpa came in, looked around, and said it was the first time he could find his favorite saw.
records.zomi: Ka pu hong lut a, a kiim a et khit ciangin a deih pen vuai a muh theih masakna ahi hi, a ci hi.

records.english: What was the hardest part of your first job?
records.zomi: Na nasep masa pen ah a haksa pen bang ahi hiam?

records.english: Getting up before the sun, because I had never been an early riser.
records.zomi: Ni suak ma-in thou ding, banghangziam cih leh zingsang ma-a thou mi ka hi ngei kei hi.

records.english: Whoever arrived last at the workshop had to make tea for everyone.
records.zomi: Nasepna inn ah a nunung pen a tung peuhpeuh in mi khempeuh adingin tea a bawl ding hi.

records.english: We were told to wear white shirts on Mondays, when the director visited the shop floor.
records.zomi: Director in nasepna mun a veh Pizing ni ciangin puan ngou silh dingin hong kigen hi.

records.english: Can I tell you about the strangest customer I ever served?
records.zomi: Ka nasep sak ngei mi lamdang pen thu kong gen thei ding hiam?

records.english: My first salary was paid in cash in a brown envelope.
records.zomi: Ka khasum masa pen dangka-in lai-ip sung tawh hong kipia hi.

records.english: On my first night as a waiter, I brought a vegetarian guest a plate of fried chicken.
records.zomi: An zuakna inn-a an tawisak nasem ka hih zan masak pen-in sa ne lo khual khat kiangah ak sa kang ka tawi hi.

records.english: The head waiter said, "Apologize, take it back, and bring her the vegetable curry."
records.zomi: An tawisak makaipa in, “Maisak ngen inla, la kik inla, anteh curry pia in,” a ci hi.

records.english: How many people worked on the boat with you?
records.zomi: Na tawh mi bangzah in long tungah na sem khawm uh hiam?

records.english: Who taught you how to use the old typewriter?
records.zomi: Typewriter lui zat dan kua in hong sin sak hiam?

records.english: A secretary who had worked in the office for thirty years and knew every key by heart.
records.zomi: Office ah kum sawm thum a sem a, tawh khempeuh a theih siang secretary khat.

records.english: Tell me about your first day at the factory.
records.zomi: Factory na nasep ni masak pen thu hong gen in.

records.english: By the time I left the restaurant, I could carry six plates at once without spilling anything.
records.zomi: An zuakna inn ka nusiat ciangin bangmah sung lo-in kuang guk khatvei-in ka tawi thei hi.

records.english: Which job did you enjoy most when you were young?
records.zomi: Na khangno lai-in nasep bang na nopsak pen hiam?

records.english: In my first week as an apprentice mechanic, I wasn't allowed to touch a single engine.
records.zomi: Mawtaw bawl sin ka hih kal masa sungin engine khat zong ka khoih dingin kiphal lo hi.

records.english: I swept the floor, cleaned the tools and watched the older men work.
records.zomi: Inn ka phiat a, nasepna van te ka sianseh a, mi upa zawte' sep ka en hi.

records.english: On Friday, the owner handed me a spanner and said, "Now show me what you've learned."
records.zomi: Laithai ni-in a neipa in spanner hong pia a, “Tu-in na sinte hong lak in,” a ci hi.

records.english: Everyone, the story I'm about to tell happened on my very first day at the hospital.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh aw, kong gen ding thu pen siavuan inn-a ka nasep ni masak pen-in a piang hi.

records.english: Were you ever late for work?
records.zomi: Nasepna ah na nunung ngei hiam?

records.english: Our office was moved to a new building, and nobody could find the canteen for a week.
records.zomi: I office inn thak ah kituan a, kal khat sung kuamah in an nekna inn a mu kei uh hi.

records.english: Who drove you to work in those days?
records.zomi: Tua hunte-in nasepna ah kua in hong tawi hiam?

records.english: When I worked on my uncle's fishing boat, we left the harbor at three in the morning.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu' nga man long tungah ka sep lai-in zingsang nai thum ciangin long dinna pan i pai hi.

records.english: By sunrise, the nets were full, and my hands were too cold to feel the ropes.
records.zomi: Ni a suah ciangin lente a dim a, ka khut a vot lua ahih manin khau te ka thei zo kei hi.

records.english: We sold the catch at the market before most people had eaten breakfast.
records.zomi: Mi tamzaw in zingsang an a nek ma-un i man nga te zuakna mun ah i zuak hi.

records.english: Where did you eat lunch when you worked in the fields?
records.zomi: Lo sungah na sep lai-in sun an koi ah na ne hiam?

records.english: However early we started, the market traders were always there before us.
records.zomi: Bangzah ma-in i kipan zongin zuakna mun-a sumbawlte i ma-ah a tung tawntung uh hi.

records.english: Rather than complaining about the long hours, my aunt sang to the other pickers.
records.zomi: Hun sawt nasep phun sangin ka ni in lo-a a tawh khawmte adingin la a sa hi.

records.english: It was only when the season ended that I realized how strong my arms had become.
records.zomi: Hun a bei ciang bek ka ban bangzah in a hat hiam ka thei hi.

records.english: How did people get to work before there were buses in your town?
records.zomi: Na khua ah bus a om ma-in mite nasepna ah bangci-in a pai uh hiam?

records.english: Why did your uncle always go to work an hour early?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na pa neu in nasepna ah nai khat ma-in a pai tawntung hiam?

records.english: Looking back, the hardest jobs taught me the most about patience.
records.zomi: Nung lam en kik-in nasep haksa pen te in thuakzawhna thu ka tamzaw hong sin sak hi.

records.english: During harvest week, the school closed so that the children could help carry the rice home.
records.zomi: Kaihawl kal sungin naupangte in buh inn ah a puak huh theih nadingun sang kikhak hi.

records.english: Did you like your first boss?
records.zomi: Na nasep masa-a na makaipa na deih hiam?

records.english: Do you remember what time the market traders started work?
records.zomi: Zuakna mun-a sumbawlte in nai bangzah ciangin nasep a kipan uh hiam na phawk hiam?

records.english: By five they were setting up their stalls with lanterns, and by six the first customers arrived.
records.zomi: Nai nga ciangin meivak tawh a zuakna dawhkan uh a koih uh a, nai guk ciangin a lei mi masa te a tung uh hi.

records.english: Was the work on the boat dangerous?
records.zomi: Long tung-a nasep pen lauhuai hiam?

records.english: During the picking season, my aunt worked on a tea plantation in the hills.
records.zomi: Lo hun ciangin ka ni in mual tung-a lakphak huan khat ah a sem hi.

records.english: She carried a basket on her back and picked leaves from dawn until the afternoon heat.
records.zomi: A nungah empeng a pua a, zingsang pan sun lum dong a nah a lo hi.

records.english: At the end of each day, the leaves were weighed, and she was paid by the kilo.
records.zomi: Ni simin a nisa ciangin a nah te kibuk a, kilo bangin a kha kipia hi.

records.english: On the day our family opened its first shop, nobody came in until noon.
records.zomi: I innkuan in i zuakna inn masa pen i hon ni-in sun dong kuamah a lut kei uh hi.

records.english: Then an old man bought a box of matches and wished us good luck.
records.zomi: Tua ciangin pu upa khat in meitang bawm khat a lei a, vangphatna hong thum sak hi.

records.english: We framed the coin he paid with and hung it above the counter.
records.zomi: A piak dangka sik i kilh a, sum lakna dawhkan tungah i khai hi.

records.english: The shop's first sign was painted by hand by my uncle.
records.zomi: Zuakna inn' min suang masa pen ka pa neu in khut tawh a gelh hi.

records.english: Last month, my daughter started her first job, and I gave her my old work bag.
records.zomi: Kha nung in ka tanu in a nasep masa pen a kipan a, ka nasep ip lui ka pia hi.

records.english: Did you have a uniform at your first job?
records.zomi: Na nasep masa pen ah puan kibang na silh uh hiam?

records.english: Shall I tell you how much I earned in my first job?
records.zomi: Ka nasep masa pen ah bangzah ka ngah hiam kong gen ding hiam?

records.english: Would you have stayed at the factory if the wages had been better?
records.zomi: Kha a tam zaw le factory ah na om lai ding hiam?

records.english: My cousin worked as a bus conductor, calling out the stops in a voice you could hear from the street.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam in bus tungah sum la-in a sem a, lampi pan a zak theih aw tawh dinna te a kiko hi.

records.english: Children, listen carefully, because I'm going to tell you how I earned my first wage.
records.zomi: Naupangte, kong gen ding ka kha masa bangci-in ka ngah hiam cih limtakin ngai un.

records.english: What I remember most about working on the boat is the silence before the sun came up.
records.zomi: Long tung-a nasep thu ah ka phawk pen pen ni a suah ma-a daihna ahi hi.

records.english: Although the pay was small, I was proud to bring my first wage home.
records.zomi: Kha a neu hangin ka kha masa pen inn ah ka tawi ciangin ka kipak mahmah hi.

records.english: The harder we worked during the harvest, the bigger the feast at the end of it.
records.zomi: Kaihawl lai-in i sep hat semsem ciangin a tawp ciang-a ankuang a lian semsem hi.

records.english: I really did want to do well at my first interpreting job, but my hands shook the whole time.
records.zomi: Ka pau let nasep masa pen ah ka sep hoih nuam taktak a, ahi zongin a hun bup sung ka khut a ling hi.

records.english: The doctor was so patient that by the end of the morning I had forgotten to be nervous.
records.zomi: Siavuan in thuak a zawh lua ahih manin zingsang a bei ciangin lau dingin ka mangngilh khin hi.

records.english: What did you buy with your first wage?
records.zomi: Na kha masa pen tawh bang na lei hiam?

records.english: When did you first work a full week?
records.zomi: Bang ciangin kal khat bup na sem masa hiam?

records.english: If the old mechanic hadn't been so patient, I might have given up in the first week.
records.zomi: Mawtaw bawlpa upa in thuak a zawh kei le kal masa sungin ka khawl kha ding hi.

records.english: The factory whistle was blown at seven, and the gates were locked five minutes later.
records.zomi: Factory aw ging nai sagih ciangin kimut a, minit nga khit ciangin kongpi kikhak hi.

records.english: My first year at the factory was like learning a new language, because every machine had its own rhythm.
records.zomi: Factory-a ka kum masa pen pau thak sin bang ahi a, set khempeuh in a ging tuamtuam a nei hi.

records.english: Why did your uncle walk to work even in the pouring rain?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na pa neu in guah zuk lua lai zongin nasepna ah a pai hiam?

records.english: How did you keep warm at night in the mountains?
records.zomi: Mual tungah zanin bangci-in na lum hiam?

records.english: Do you remember the nights we spent in the hut in the rice field?
records.zomi: Buh lo sung-a lobuk ah zan i ihmut na phawk hiam?

records.english: Each of us stayed awake for two hours with a drum to scare the wild pigs away from the crops.
records.zomi: Lo sung-a gam vok te hawl dingin i khat ciat in khuang tawh nai nih sung i khanglawh hi.

records.english: The quieter the house became, the louder the crickets seemed outside.
records.zomi: Inn sung a daih semsem ciangin pua-a khuai te a ging bang semsem hi.

records.english: By the time the story ended, every child in the room was fast asleep.
records.zomi: Tangthu a bei ciangin inndei sung-a naupang khempeuh a ihmu khin uh hi.

records.english: Where did you sleep when you visited your grandparents?
records.zomi: Na pu leh pite na veh ciangin koi ah na ihmu hiam?

records.english: Looking back, those crowded nights at family weddings were some of the happiest of my childhood.
records.zomi: Nung lam en kik-in innkuan mopawi-a mi tam zante pen ka naupan lai hun nuam pen te lak-ah kihel hi.

records.english: Tell me why you were frightened of the dark as a child.
records.zomi: Na neu lai-in bang hangin mial na lau hiam hong gen in.

records.english: Why did your grandfather always check the animals before he went to bed?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na pu in a ihmut ma-in ganhing te a en tawntung hiam?

records.english: Wouldn't it be wonderful to sleep under the stars again, the way we did as children?
records.zomi: Naupang i hih lai bangin aksi nuai ah ihmu kik leng nuam mahmah ding hi lo ding hiam?

records.english: Rather than reading to us, our uncle made up a new story every night.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in hong sim sak sangin zan simin tangthu thak a phuah hi.

records.english: Our bedroom curtains were made by my aunt from an old wedding dress.
records.zomi: I inndei tukvuang puan te ka ni in mopawi puan lui pan a bawl hi.

records.english: If my sister hadn't held my hand that first night, I would never have fallen asleep.
records.zomi: Tua zan masa pen ah ka sanggam nu in ka khut a len kei le ka ihmu ngei lo ding hi.

records.english: When did you first sleep away from home?
records.zomi: Bang ciangin inn pua ah na ihmu masa hiam?

records.english: Why did the children all want to sleep in the same bed?
records.zomi: Bang hangin naupang khempeuh in lupna khat mah ah ihmut a deih uh hiam?

records.english: Shall I tell you about the night the goats got into the house?
records.zomi: Kel te inn sung a lut zan thu kong gen ding hiam?

records.english: Everyone, blow out the lamps and say your prayers.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh aw, meivak te mut unla, thu ngen un.

records.english: Before bed, our grandfather pointed out the stars and told us their names.
records.zomi: Ihmut ma-in i pu in aksi te hong lak a, a min te hong hilh hi.

records.english: He said that sailors had used the same stars to find their way home.
records.zomi: Tuipi tung khualzinte in inn a ciahna lampi zon nadingin aksi kibang mah a zang uh hi, a ci hi.

records.english: It was only when I stayed in a city hotel that I realized how much I missed the sound of the crickets.
records.zomi: Khuapi zinbuuk ah ka om ciang bek khuai ging bangzah ka lungngai hiam ka thei hi.

records.english: On hot summer nights, our whole family carried mattresses up to the flat roof.
records.zomi: Khal zan lum te ah i innkuan bup in lupna phah te innkhum phei tungah i puak tou hi.

records.english: We lay under the open sky and listened to the neighbors talking on their own roofs.
records.zomi: Van hong nuai ah i lum a, inn vengte amau' innkhum tungah thu a kikum uh i ngai hi.

records.english: In the morning, the sun woke us long before anyone wanted to get up.
records.zomi: Zingsang ciangin kuamah thou a nop ma-un ni in hong phawngsak hi.

records.english: On my first night in the boarding-school dormitory, I couldn't stop crying.
records.zomi: Om-in kah sang ihmutna inn ah ka zan masa pen-in ka kap tawp thei kei hi.

records.english: The girl in the next bed passed me a sweet and whispered that she had cried too.
records.zomi: A gei lupna-a nungak in thei khum khat hong pia a, amah zong a kap hi, ci-in hong suk hi.

records.english: We became best friends, and she was a bridesmaid at my wedding.
records.zomi: Lawm hoih pen i suak a, ka mopawi ah ka huhtu nungak hi.

records.english: What I remember most about those nights on the roof is the smell of jasmine from the yard below.
records.zomi: Innkhum tung-a tua zante thu ah ka phawk pen pen a nuai-a huan pan jasmine pak gim ahi hi.

records.english: Would you have slept so well on the roof if the mosquitoes had been as bad as they are now?
records.zomi: Tu bangin thosi te a tam leh innkhum tungah hoih takin na ihmu thei ding hiam?

records.english: Falling asleep on the roof was like drifting on a boat under the stars.
records.zomi: Innkhum tungah ihmut pen aksi nuai-a long tungah kilei bang ahi hi.

records.english: Could you hear the river from your bedroom when you were young?
records.zomi: Na neu lai-in na inndei pan gun ging na za thei hiam?

records.english: What did you do when you couldn't sleep as a child?
records.zomi: Na neu lai-in na ihmut theih loh ciangin bang na bawl hiam?

records.english: I counted the geckos on the ceiling until my eyes closed.
records.zomi: Ka mit a mit dong innkhum nuai-a bawngtau te ka sim hi.

records.english: The old wooden bed was carried up the stairs by four of my uncles.
records.zomi: Sing lupna lui pen ka pa neu li in kahlei tungah a puak tou uh hi.

records.english: Was your bedroom cold in winter?
records.zomi: Khuavot hun ciangin na inndei a vot hiam?

records.english: The cot was rocked by my little sister, who was proud to have such an important job.
records.zomi: Naupang lupna pen ka nau nu in a lawk a, tua bang nasep thupi a neih ahih manin a kipak hi.

records.english: However tired we were, our grandmother made us wash our feet before bed.
records.zomi: Bangzah in i ol zongin ka pi in ihmut ma-in i khe hong silsak hi.

records.english: What was it like to sleep in a hut in the middle of the field?
records.zomi: Lo laizang-a lobuk ah ihmut bangci hiam?

records.english: Our neighbor used to sing her baby to sleep in a language none of us understood.
records.zomi: I inn vengnu in kuamah i theih loh pau tawh a nau ihmut nadingin la a sak sak hi.

records.english: Which bedtime song do you remember best?
records.zomi: Ihmut ma-a la bang na phawk pen hiam?

records.english: Last night, my daughter asked me to tell her about the roof again.
records.zomi: Zanin ka tanu in innkhum thu gen kik dingin hong ngen hi.

records.english: I really did want to stay awake for the New Year fireworks, but I fell asleep at ten.
records.zomi: Kum Thak meisa te en dingin ka khanglawh nuam taktak a, ahi zongin nai sawm ciangin ka ihmu hi.

records.english: At my cousin's wedding, twelve of us slept on mats in one small room.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam' mopawi ah, i sawm leh nih in inndei neu khat ah phahte tungah i ihmu hi.

records.english: Every time someone turned over, somebody else woke up.
records.zomi: Mi khat a kileh peuhin mi dang khat a phawng hi.

records.english: By morning, we were exhausted, but we laughed about it all through the wedding.
records.zomi: Zingsang ciangin i ol mahmah a, ahi zongin mopawi sung bup ah tua thu i nuihsan hi.

records.english: Can I stay up until the visitors leave?
records.zomi: Khualte a pai mateng ka khanglawh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Whoever fell asleep first had to make breakfast for the others in the morning.
records.zomi: A ihmu masa peuhpeuh in zingsang ciangin mi dangte adingin zingsang an a bawl ding hi.

records.english: At my cousins' sleepover, my oldest cousin told ghost stories with a torch under her chin.
records.zomi: Ka sanggamte' kiang-a zan i ihmut ciangin ka sanggam upa pen in a kha nuai ah meivak tawh kau tangthu a gen hi.

records.english: The little ones were so frightened that they all climbed into one bed.
records.zomi: Naupang neute a lau lua ahih manun lupna khat mah ah a kai uh hi.

records.english: Nobody slept until our aunt came in and promised that ghosts never visited her house.
records.zomi: I ni hong lut a, kau te in a inn a veh ngei kei uh hi, ci-in a ciam mateng kuamah a ihmu kei uh hi.

records.english: Did your family have a bedtime prayer?
records.zomi: Na innkuan in ihmut ma-a thungetna na nei uh hiam?

records.english: On the overnight ferry, we slept on the deck with our bags as pillows.
records.zomi: Zan khualzin long tungah i ip te lupna khuh-in long tungah i ihmu hi.

records.english: The dog slept at the foot of my bed every night for twelve years.
records.zomi: Kum sawm leh nih sung zan simin ui in ka lupna khe lam ah a ihmu hi.

records.english: Children, if you're quiet now, I'll tell you about the night I saw a shooting star.
records.zomi: Naupangte, tu-in na daih uh leh aksi tai ka muh zan thu kong gen ding hi.

records.english: We used a small oil lamp to read in bed when the village had no electricity.
records.zomi: Khua in mei-ok a neih loh lai-in lupna tungah sim dingin sathau meivak neu khat i zang hi.

records.english: Did your grandparents tell stories before bed, or did they sing?
records.zomi: Na pu leh pite in ihmut ma-in tangthu a gen uh hiam, la a sa uh hiam?

records.english: Whatever the season, our aunt kept a jar of water and a lamp beside every bed.
records.zomi: Hun bang ahi zongin i ni in lupna khempeuh gei ah tui bel khat leh meivak khat a koih hi.

records.english: Who put you to bed when your parents were working late?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa a sep nunung ciangun kua in hong lupsak hiam?

records.english: My older brother, who always let me stay up for ten more minutes.
records.zomi: Ka u pasal, minit sawm khanglawh lai dingin hong phal tawntung pa.

records.english: Although we had only one blanket between three of us, we never felt cold.
records.zomi: I thum in puannak khat bek i nei hangin vot i sa ngei kei hi.

records.english: We weren't allowed to talk once the lamps were out.
records.zomi: Meivak te a kimut khit ciangin thu i gen dingin kiphal lo hi.

records.english: Everyone, think carefully before you choose your courses, because they'll shape your future.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh aw, na sin ding te na teel ma-un limtakin ngaihsun un, na hun ding uh a bawl ding hi.

records.english: Don't let anyone else make this decision for you.
records.zomi: Hih thukhenna mi dang in hong bawl sak kei hen.

records.english: If I hadn't taken that risk, I would never have met the people who became my closest friends.
records.zomi: Tua lauhuai ka thuak kei le ka lawm kinai pen suakte ka kimu ngei lo ding hi.

records.english: Children under eighteen aren't allowed to sign the contract without a parent.
records.zomi: Kum sawm leh giat nuai naupangte in nu leh pa om lo-in kiciamna lai ah a min a gelh thei kei uh hi.

records.english: Could you help me write a list of the reasons for and against moving?
records.zomi: Kitawn ding leh kitawn lo ding hangte gelh dingin hong huh thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Why did you decide to become a doctor?
records.zomi: Bang hangin siavuan hih dingin na thukhen hiam?

records.english: When I was a child, a doctor walked two days to our village to save my mother's life.
records.zomi: Ka neu lai-in ka nu' nuntakna hotkhiat dingin siavuan khat in i khua ah ni nih sung a pai hi.

records.english: It was only after I had moved that I understood why my parents had worried so much.
records.zomi: Ka kitawn khit ciang bek ka nu leh ka pa in bang hangin a lungkham lua uh hiam ka thei hi.

records.english: Shall we ask your grandfather for advice before we decide?
records.zomi: I thukhen ma-in na pu kiangah thuhilhna i ngen ding hiam?

records.english: I decided to start my own business after I lost my job.
records.zomi: Ka nasep ka mansuah khit ciangin keimah sumbawlna kipat dingin ka thukhen hi.

records.english: When the factory offered me a promotion, it meant moving to a city far away.
records.zomi: Factory in nasep sang zaw hong piak ciangin gamla khuapi khat ah kitawn ding a kisam hi.

records.english: My wife and I talked about it every evening for a month.
records.zomi: Ka zi leh kei in kha khat sung nitak simin tua thu i kikum hi.

records.english: In the end, we stayed, because our children were happy at their school.
records.zomi: A tawp-in i ta te in a sang uh ah a nuam uh ahih manin i om lai hi.

records.english: Who helped you make up your mind?
records.zomi: Na thukhenna ah kua in hong huh hiam?

records.english: My teacher, who asked me what I would regret more in ten years.
records.zomi: Ka saya, kum sawm khit ciangin bang ka lungkhamsak zaw ding hiam, hong dong pa.

records.english: Whoever makes the final decision should be the person who has to live with it.
records.zomi: Thukhenna nunung a bawl peuhpeuh pen tua tawh a nungta ding mi ahi ding hi.

records.english: Can I take the job, even though it means working on Sundays?
records.zomi: Nipini ni-in sep ding a kisam hangin nasep ka la thei ding hiam?

records.english: Last year, my cousin was offered a scholarship in another country.
records.zomi: Kum nung in ka sanggam nu khat in gamdang ah laisinna sum a ngah hi.

records.english: Her parents were worried, but her grandmother said, "Let the bird fly while its wings are strong."
records.zomi: A nu leh a pa a lungkham uh a, ahi zongin a pi in, “Vasa a ha a hat lai-in leng sak in,” a ci hi.

records.english: She left in September and calls home every Sunday.
records.zomi: September kha in a pai a, Nipini simin inn ah phone a sam hi.

records.english: Tell me why you chose this town.
records.zomi: Bang hangin hih khua na teel hiam hong gen in.

records.english: Where were you when you decided to change your career?
records.zomi: Na nasep khek dingin na thukhen ciangin koi ah na om hiam?

records.english: When did you know it was the right decision?
records.zomi: Bang ciangin thukhenna dik ahi hi, cih na thei hiam?

records.english: Last spring, my brother finally decided to propose to his girlfriend.
records.zomi: Spring nung in ka sanggam pasal in a it nungak kiang zi dingin ngen dingin a thukhen hi.

records.english: Did you ever regret leaving the city?
records.zomi: Khuapi na nusiat a lungkhamna na nei ngei hiam?

records.english: I decided to forgive my brother, even though he never apologized.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in maisak a ngen ngei kei hangin amah maisak dingin ka thukhen hi.

records.english: The decision to sell the land was made by all the brothers together.
records.zomi: Gam zuak ding thukhenna sanggam pasal khempeuh in khawm-in a bawl uh hi.

records.english: My aunt sold her jewelry to pay for her son's university fees.
records.zomi: Ka ni in a tapa' sangpi sum piak nadingin a sui leh ngun a zuak hi.

records.english: The biggest decision of my life was to marry the man my parents had doubts about.
records.zomi: Ka nuntakna sung-a thukhenna lian pen ka nu leh ka pa' muanlohna pasal tawh ki-ten ding ahi hi.

records.english: Is it possible to change your mind once you've signed the papers?
records.zomi: Lai tungah na min na gelh khit ciangin na ngaihsutna na khek thei lai ding hiam?

records.english: However frightening the choice seemed, my sister never asked anyone else to make it for her.
records.zomi: Teelna bangzah in lauhuai zongin ka sanggam nu in amah adingin a bawl sak dingin mi dang a ngen ngei kei hi.

records.english: Although the decision was painful, I have never once wished I had chosen differently.
records.zomi: Thukhenna a natna hangin a dang ka teel hileh ci-in ka deih ngei kei hi.

records.english: I decided to learn to drive at fifty, and it changed my life.
records.zomi: Kum sawm nga ka phak ciangin mawtaw mawng sin dingin ka thukhen a, ka nuntakna a khek hi.

records.english: Some decisions can't be made with the head alone; they also need the heart.
records.zomi: Thukhenna pawl khat lu bek tawh bawl theih lo ahi a, lungsim zong a kisam hi.

records.english: I really do want to make the right choice, but every option has its problems.
records.zomi: Teelna dik bawl ka deih taktak a, ahi zongin teelna khempeuh in a haksatna a nei hi.

records.english: The longer I waited to decide, the more difficult the choice became.
records.zomi: Thukhen dingin ka ngak sawt semsem ciangin teelna a haksa semsem hi.

records.english: Rather than choosing the safest path, my sister followed her dream of becoming a musician.
records.zomi: Lampi bit pen teel sangin ka sanggam nu in la phuak la sa hih ding a mang a zui hi.

records.english: We moved closer to the hospital so that my mother could get treatment more easily.
records.zomi: Ka nu in damna a ngah baih nadingin siavuan inn kiang ah i kitawn hi.

records.english: We bought a small shop instead of a car, and it has fed our family ever since.
records.zomi: Mawtaw sangin zuakna inn neu khat i lei a, tua pan kipan i innkuan a vak hi.

records.english: When I was eighteen, I had to choose between a job in the city and a place at the teachers' college.
records.zomi: Kum sawm leh giat ka phak ciangin khuapi-a nasep leh saya sang-a mun khat teel ding ka hi hi.

records.english: My uncle told me, "Money comes and goes, but what you learn stays with you."
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in, “Sum a hong a pai hi, ahi zongin na sinte na tawh om tawntung hi,” hong ci hi.

records.english: I chose the college, and I have taught in the village school for twenty years.
records.zomi: Sang ka teel a, kum sawm nih sung khua sang ah ka hilh hi.

records.english: What I remember most about that decision is how calm I felt once it was made.
records.zomi: Tua thukhenna thu ah ka phawk pen pen ka thukhen khit ciangin ka lungsim a nopna ahi hi.

records.english: You can't decide something this important when you're angry.
records.zomi: Na heh laitakin hih bang thu thupi na khen thei kei hi.

records.english: My brother decided to stay on the farm so that our parents wouldn't be alone.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa a kia uh lohna dingin ka sanggam pasal in lo ah om dingin a thukhen hi.

records.english: Which choice would you make again if you could?
records.zomi: Na hih theih leh teelna bang na teel kik ding hiam?

records.english: May I take a day to think before I give you my answer?
records.zomi: Ka dawnna kong piak ma-in ngaihsun dingin ni khat ka la thei ding hiam?

records.english: Looking back, the hardest decisions were often the ones that taught me the most.
records.zomi: Nung lam en kik-in thukhenna haksa pen te in thu tampen hong sin sak hi.

records.english: Would you have taken the scholarship if your grandmother hadn't encouraged you?
records.zomi: Na pi in hong hasuah kei le laisinna sum na la ding hiam?

records.english: Why did you decide to come back to the village?
records.zomi: Bang hangin khua ah ciah kik dingin na thukhen hiam?

records.english: How did your parents react when you told them your plans?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa kiangah na geelnate na gen ciangin bangci-in a dawng uh hiam?

records.english: It might be wiser to wait until after the harvest before you decide.
records.zomi: Na thukhen ma-in kaihawl khit dong ngak leng a pil zaw ding hi.

records.english: My parents let me choose my own subjects at school, which surprised everyone.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in sang-a ka sin ding te keimah in teel dingin hong phal uh a, mi khempeuh a lamdang sa uh hi.

records.english: What was the hardest decision you've ever made?
records.zomi: Na bawl ngei thukhenna haksa pen bang ahi hiam?

records.english: Leaving my home village to find work, because I knew I might never live there again.
records.zomi: Nasep zong dingin ka khua ka nusiat ding, tua ah ka om kik ngei nawn lo ding hi, cih ka theih manin.

records.english: My sister decided to move abroad to work as a nurse.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu in nurse nasem dingin gamdang ah pai dingin a thukhen hi.

records.english: It was a hard decision, because she had never lived away from home.
records.zomi: Thukhenna haksa ahi hi, banghangziam cih leh inn pan a om khia ngei kei hi.

records.english: Now she sends money every month so that our younger brothers can stay in school.
records.zomi: Tu-in i nau pasalte sang a kah theih nadingun kha simin sum a khak hi.

records.english: Making that decision was like crossing a river on stepping stones, because each step felt uncertain.
records.zomi: Tua thukhenna bawl pen suang tung lam ah gun kantan bang ahi a, khe kalsuanna khempeuh a kician kei hi.

records.english: Choosing a school for our son took us months.
records.zomi: I tapa adingin sang teel pen kha tampi hong sawt hi.

records.english: How did people keep their shopping cool before there were fridges?
records.zomi: Vot sak setna a om ma-in mite in a van leite uh bangci-in a vot sak uh hiam?

records.english: What I remember most about market days is the smell of roasted corn at the gate.
records.zomi: Zuakna ni thu ah ka phawk pen pen kongpi-a vaimim kang gim ahi hi.

records.english: What was the first thing you bought for yourself?
records.zomi: Nangma adingin na lei masak pen bang ahi hiam?

records.english: It was only when the road was built that fresh fruit began to reach our village.
records.zomi: Lampi a kibawl ciang bek theigah thakte i khua ah a tung kipan hi.

records.english: Our basket was stolen while we were looking at the cloth stall.
records.zomi: Puan zuakna dawhkan i et laitakin i empeng a kigu hi.

records.english: Looking back, those trips to the market taught me more arithmetic than any school lesson.
records.zomi: Nung lam en kik-in tua zuakna mun pai te in sang thusin khempeuh sangin kisim dan tam zaw hong sin sak hi.

records.english: By the time we reached home, the ice cream we had bought had completely melted.
records.zomi: Inn i tun ciangin i lei ice cream a vekpi in a tui suak khin hi.

records.english: Whoever carried the heaviest basket home got the first piece of bread.
records.zomi: Empeng gik pen inn ah a pua peuhpeuh in moh a tum masa pen a ngah hi.

records.english: I really did want to choose the vegetables myself, but the seller always picked them for me.
records.zomi: Anteh te keimah in teel ka deih taktak a, ahi zongin zuakpa in hong teel sak tawntung hi.

records.english: Can I carry the basket this time?
records.zomi: Tu-in empeng ka pua thei ding hiam?

records.english: We bought our flour from a mill where the miller ground it in front of us.
records.zomi: I buh-mal pen buh guaina inn pan i lei a, a neipa in i mai ah a gua hi.

records.english: Our grandmother could tell whether a melon was ripe just by tapping it with her finger.
records.zomi: Ka pi in a khutzung tawh a kik bek tawh mai a min hiam theih thei hi.

records.english: We were given a free orange by the fruit seller every time we said hello.
records.zomi: Lumen i cih simin theigah zuakpa in sangtam khat a man lo-in hong pia hi.

records.english: Shall I tell you about the day I bought a chicken that escaped?
records.zomi: Ka lei ak a tai ni thu kong gen ding hiam?

records.english: Was the market far from your house?
records.zomi: Zuakna mun na inn pan gamla hiam?

records.english: Wouldn't it be wonderful if the old market could open again on Saturdays?
records.zomi: Zuakna mun lui Kiginni ni-in kihong kik leh nuam mahmah ding hi lo ding hiam?

records.english: Rather than paying cash, many families paid the miller with a share of their grain.
records.zomi: Dangka-in piak sangin innkuan tampi in buh guaipa a buh khen khat tawh a pia uh hi.

records.english: Do you remember the shopkeeper who let families buy on credit after the bad harvest?
records.zomi: Kaihawl hoih loh khit ciangin innkuante leiba-in lei dingin a phal zuakna inn neipa na phawk hiam?

records.english: He wrote every debt in a notebook and never once asked anyone to pay before they could.
records.zomi: Leiba khempeuh laibu ah a gelh a, a piak theih ma-un piak dingin kuamah a ngen ngei kei hi.

records.english: However long the walk to market was, the children begged to come along.
records.zomi: Zuakna mun pai bangzah in gamla zongin naupangte in zui dingin a ngen uh hi.

records.english: Who taught you how to bargain at the market?
records.zomi: Zuakna mun ah a man kisut dan kua in hong sin sak hiam?

records.english: My aunt, who could get the price halved with just a smile and a sigh.
records.zomi: Ka ni, a nuihna leh a thaw tawh bek a man a kim a kiamsak thei pa.

records.english: The scale at the old shop was checked by an inspector every year.
records.zomi: Zuakna inn lui-a gikna setna kum simin enkaktu khat in a en hi.

records.english: Tell me what the market looked like when you were young.
records.zomi: Na neu lai-in zuakna mun bangci-in a om hiam hong gen in.

records.english: Who carried the shopping home?
records.zomi: Van leite inn ah kua in a puak hiam?

records.english: The first time I went shopping alone, I was seven and carried the coins knotted in a handkerchief.
records.zomi: Keimah bek in van lei dingin ka pai masak ciangin kum sagih ka hi a, dangka sik te khut puan sungah ka khih hi.

records.english: I had a list written in my mother's careful handwriting.
records.zomi: Ka nu' laigelh hoih tawh kigelh lai khat ka nei hi.

records.english: I came home with everything except the salt, which I had swapped for a bag of sweets.
records.zomi: Cii simloh bangkim tawh inn ah ka ciah a, cii pen thei khum ip khat tawh ka laih hi.

records.english: The market on a Saturday morning was like a festival, because the whole valley came to town.
records.zomi: Kiginni zingsang-a zuakna mun pen pawi bang ahi a, guam bup in khuapi ah a hong uh hi.

records.english: Children, stay close to me, because the market is very crowded on festival days.
records.zomi: Naupangte, kei kiang ah om un, pawi ni-in zuakna mun ah mi a tam mahmah hi.

records.english: If the trader hadn't given us credit that winter, many families would have gone hungry.
records.zomi: Tua khuavot in sumbawlpa in leiba-in hong pia kei le innkuan tampi in a gil a kial ding uh hi.

records.english: What did your family buy at the market every week?
records.zomi: Kal simin na innkuan in zuakna mun ah bang a lei uh hiam?

records.english: Rice, oil, salt, and whatever vegetables we couldn't grow ourselves.
records.zomi: Buh, sathau, cii, leh i kisuan thei loh anteh te.

records.english: It might have been cheaper to buy in town, but the walk took half a day.
records.zomi: Khuapi ah lei leng a man neu zaw kha ding hi, ahi zongin pai ding ni lang a sawt hi.

records.english: Whatever the weather, the fish sellers were on the beach by six.
records.zomi: Huihkhua bang ahi zongin nga zuakte nai guk ciangin tuipi gei ah a om uh hi.

records.english: When did the first shop open in your village?
records.zomi: Na khua ah zuakna inn masa pen bang ciangin kihong hiam?

records.english: Did you ever buy anything with your own money as a child?
records.zomi: Na neu lai-in nangma' sum tawh bangmah na lei ngei hiam?

records.english: Last week, my son went shopping alone for the first time and came back with the right change.
records.zomi: Kal nung in ka tapa amah bek in van lei dingin a pai masa a, sum kilaih dik tawh a ciah kik hi.

records.english: When I was a boy, we took eggs to the village market and swapped them for salt and soap.
records.zomi: Ka neu lai-in khua zuakna mun ah aktui i tawi a, cii leh satpiang tawh i laih hi.

records.english: The trader weighed everything with an old brass scale.
records.zomi: Sumbawlpa in bangkim dal gikna setna lui tawh a buk hi.

records.english: If the eggs were large, he sometimes added a handful of sugar for free.
records.zomi: Aktui a lian leh khatvei khat sugar khut khat a man lo-in a behlap hi.

records.english: Would the village have survived that winter if the shopkeeper hadn't trusted everyone?
records.zomi: Zuakna inn neipa in mi khempeuh a muan kei le tua khuavot khua in a zo ding hiam?

records.english: When the first supermarket opened in our town, people queued outside before dawn.
records.zomi: I khuapi ah supermarket masa pen a kihon ciangin mite in khuavak ma-in a pua ah a dingkhawm uh hi.

records.english: My aunt came home with a trolley full of things she had never seen before.
records.zomi: Ka ni in a muh ngei loh van tampi tawh a dim leng tawh inn ah a ciah hi.

records.english: Half of them stayed in her cupboard for years because nobody knew how to cook them.
records.zomi: Kuamah in huan dan a theih loh manin a kim te kum tampi sung a van koihna ah a om uh hi.

records.english: Where did your family buy meat before there was a butcher in the village?
records.zomi: Khua ah sa zuakpa a om ma-in na innkuan in sa koi pan a lei uh hiam?

records.english: Why did your aunt always shop late in the afternoon?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na ni in nitak lam ciangin van a lei tawntung hiam?

records.english: My uncle carried a whole sack of rice home on the back of his bicycle.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in a siiksakol nung lam ah buh ip khat bup inn ah a puak hi.

records.english: The earlier we arrived, the better the choice of vegetables.
records.zomi: I tun ma semsem ciangin anteh teel ding a hoih semsem hi.

records.english: Which stall did you like best as a child?
records.zomi: Na neu lai-in zuakna dawhkan bang na deih pen hiam?

records.english: Did you ever go to the market with your grandparents?
records.zomi: Na pu leh pite tawh zuakna mun ah na pai ngei hiam?

records.english: On my way to the market, I lost the money my aunt had given me.
records.zomi: Zuakna mun ka pai lampi ah ka ni' hong piak sum ka mansuah hi.

records.english: I walked home in tears, sure that I would be punished.
records.zomi: Hong kigawt ding hi, ci-in kap kawm-in inn ah ka ciah hi.

records.english: That evening, a neighbor knocked on our door with the coins, which she had found on the path.
records.zomi: Tua nitak in inn vengnu khat lampi tungah a muh dangka sik te tawh i kongkhak a kik hi.

records.english: We used to buy fish on the beach as soon as the boats came in.
records.zomi: Long te a tun pah ciangin tuipi gei ah nga i lei ngei hi.

records.english: The fishermen shouted their prices, and the women bargained over every basket.
records.zomi: Nga mante in a man uh a kiko uh a, numeite in empeng khempeuh a man a kisut uh hi.

records.english: Everyone, keep your money in your inside pockets while we're in the market.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh aw, zuakna mun ah i om laitakin na sum uh na puan sung lam ip ah koih un.

records.english: The old market hall was pulled down, and a car park was built in its place.
records.zomi: Zuakna inn lui kiphukham a, a mun ah mawtaw koihna kibawl hi.

records.english: Why did the traders arrive before sunrise?
records.zomi: Bang hangin sumbawlte ni suak ma-in a tung uh hiam?

records.english: Although we had very little money, we always came home with something for the neighbors.
records.zomi: Sum tawmno bek i nei hangin inn vengte adingin bangmah khat i tawi tawntung hi.

records.english: How much pocket money did you get?
records.zomi: Zat ding sum bangzah na ngah hiam?

records.english: By the time we had agreed on a price, the shop was ready to close.
records.zomi: A man i kilemsak ciangin zuakna inn khak dingin kiman khin hi.

records.english: Children, ask the price before you pick anything up, or the seller will expect you to buy it.
records.zomi: Naupangte, bangmah na tawi ma-un a man dong un, ahih kei leh zuakpa in na lei ding uh hi, ci-in a ngak ding hi.

records.english: Did you have to bargain for everything?
records.zomi: Bangkim a man na kisut ding a kisam hiam?

records.english: Looking back, the prices of those days seem impossibly small.
records.zomi: Nung lam en kik-in tua hun-a van man te a neu lua bang hi.

records.english: Our family bought its first radio in monthly installments.
records.zomi: I innkuan in i radio masa pen kha simin tawmtawm piak-in i lei hi.

records.english: Every month, my aunt walked to the shop to pay a little more.
records.zomi: Kha simin ka ni in tawmno behlap piak dingin zuakna inn ah a pai hi.

records.english: When the last payment was made, the shopkeeper tied a ribbon around the radio.
