records.zomi: Piak nunung a kibawl ciangin zuakna inn neipa in radio ah puan zang a khih hi.

records.english: Tell me what happened when you tried to bargain for the first time.
records.zomi: A man na kisut masak ciangin bang a piang hiam hong gen in.

records.english: Where did your family buy clothes before the shops opened in town?
records.zomi: Khuapi ah zuakna inn te a kihon ma-in na innkuan in puan koi pan a lei uh hiam?

records.english: The cloth seller measured the material with his arm and named a price for each length.
records.zomi: Puan zuakpa in a ban tawh puan a teh a, a sau ciat a man a gen hi.

records.english: When did prices start rising so quickly?
records.zomi: Van man te bang ciangin manlang takin a khang kipan hiam?

records.english: The longer the seller talked, the more my grandmother suspected the price was too high.
records.zomi: Zuakpa a gen sawt semsem ciangin ka pi in a man a sang lua hi, ci-in a ngaihsun semsem hi.

records.english: Rather than arguing over a few coins, my grandfather would offer to buy a second item.
records.zomi: Dangka sik tawmno a kinial sangin ka pu in van nihna lei dingin a gen hi.

records.english: Everyone, write down what you think a kilo of tomatoes cost fifty years ago.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh aw, kum sawm nga paisa-in mehtuuk kilo khat bangzah ahi ding hiam na ngaihsut uh gelh un.

records.english: How much did a loaf of bread cost when you were young?
records.zomi: Na neu lai-in moh khat bangzah ahi hiam?

records.english: A few coins, and the baker usually gave the children a free bun.
records.zomi: Dangka sik tawmno, leh moh bawlpa in naupangte moh neu khat a man lo-in a pia tawntung hi.

records.english: Which was the most expensive thing your family ever bought?
records.zomi: Na innkuan in a lei ngei man tam pen bang ahi hiam?

records.english: My grandfather once spent a whole day at the livestock fair bargaining for one cow.
records.zomi: Ka pu in khatvei ganhing zuakna pawi ah bawng khat a man kisut dingin ni khat bup a zang hi.

records.english: Every hour, he and the seller drank tea together and lowered or raised the price a little.
records.zomi: Nai khat simin amah leh zuakpa in tea khawm-in a dawn uh a, a man tawmno a kiamsak a, a khangsak uh hi.

records.english: By sunset they had agreed, and the seller threw in a rope for free.
records.zomi: Ni tum ciangin a kilem uh a, zuakpa in khau khat a man lo-in a behlap hi.

records.english: Who did the shopping in your family?
records.zomi: Na innkuan ah kua in van a lei hiam?

records.english: My uncle always asked the price of everything, then laughed and walked away without buying.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in bangkim a man a dong tawntung a, tua ciangin a nui a, a lei lo-in a pai hi.

records.english: My cousin helped her grandfather sell his vegetables by writing the prices on cards.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu in laidal tungah a man te gelh-in a pu' anteh zuak a huh hi.

records.english: The old price tags were kept in a drawer, and my aunt still has them.
records.zomi: Van man kigelh lui te kenkuan sungah kikoih a, ka ni in a nei lai hi.

records.english: If the shopkeeper hadn't let us pay in installments, we would never have owned a radio.
records.zomi: Zuakna inn neipa in tawmtawm piak dingin hong phal kei le radio i nei ngei lo ding hi.

records.english: When I was ten, I asked the shopkeeper the price of the same red bicycle every Saturday.
records.zomi: Kum sawm ka phak ciangin Kiginni simin zuakna inn neipa kiangah siiksakol san kibang a man ka dong hi.

records.english: He always told me patiently, even though he knew I couldn't afford it.
records.zomi: Ka lei zawh loh ding a theih hangin thuak zawh takin hong gen tawntung hi.

records.english: A year later, I put my savings on his counter, and he gave me a discount for being so loyal.
records.zomi: Kum khat khit ciangin ka sum kikoihte a dawhkan tungah ka koih a, muanhuai ka hih manin a man hong kiamsak hi.

records.english: Why did the shopkeeper give discounts to people who paid in eggs?
records.zomi: Bang hangin zuakna inn neipa in aktui tawh a pia mite a man a kiamsak hiam?

records.english: Although the shoes were expensive, they lasted me for five years.
records.zomi: Khedap te a man tam hangin kum nga sung ka zang hi.

records.english: Can I tell you how much a cinema ticket cost when I was your age?
records.zomi: Na kum ka phak lai-in cinema lakkhia ding lai khat bangzah ahi hiam kong gen thei ding hiam?

records.english: Which shop in your town had the fairest prices?
records.zomi: Na khuapi ah zuakna inn bang in a man dik pen a nei hiam?

records.english: Tell me how much your wedding cost.
records.zomi: Na mopawi bangzah a bei hiam hong gen in.

records.english: Last year, my son asked the price of a car and nearly fainted.
records.zomi: Kum nung in ka tapa in mawtaw khat man a dong a, a lim a mang dek hi.

records.english: On my first trip abroad, I couldn't understand the new money and kept paying with the largest notes.
records.zomi: Gamdang ah ka khualzin masak pen-in sum thak ka thei kei a, sum lai lian pen tawh ka pia tawntung hi.

records.english: Did your family ever sell things at the market?
records.zomi: Na innkuan in zuakna mun ah van a zuak ngei uh hiam?

records.english: Why did your grandfather drink tea with the cow seller every hour?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na pu in nai khat simin bawng zuakpa tawh tea a dawn hiam?

records.english: I really did want to buy my mother a gold necklace, but the price was far beyond my savings.
records.zomi: Ka nu adingin sui ngawngkhih khat lei ka deih taktak a, ahi zongin a man ka sum kikoih sangin a tam lua hi.

records.english: Bargaining at the fair was like a game of chess, because each move was carefully planned.
records.zomi: Pawi-a a man kisut pen chess kimawlna bang ahi a, kalsuanna khempeuh limtakin kigeel hi.

records.english: Was everything cheaper in the village?
records.zomi: Khua ah bangkim a man neu zaw hiam?

records.english: Would you have bought the radio if you had known how long the payments would take?
records.zomi: A piak sawt ding na theih leh radio na lei ding hiam?

records.english: Did you ever pay too much for something without realizing it?
records.zomi: Na theih loh-in bangmah adingin sum tam lua na pia ngei hiam?

records.english: The price of rice doubled the year the rains failed.
records.zomi: Guah a zuk loh kum in buh man a nih-in a khang hi.

records.english: Whoever asked the price first was expected to make the first offer.
records.zomi: A man a dong masa peuhpeuh in a man ding a gen masa ding hi, ci-in kingak hi.

records.english: In those days, the village shop had no price labels, and the owner kept every price in his head.
records.zomi: Tua hunte-in khua zuakna inn ah van man kigelh a om kei a, a neipa in van man khempeuh a lu sungah a kem hi.

records.english: It was only after I started earning my own money that I understood why my parents were so careful.
records.zomi: Keimah sum ka ngah kipat khit ciang bek bang hangin ka nu leh ka pa a kidawm lua uh hiam ka thei hi.

records.english: However high the price, my grandmother never paid it without asking for a little off.
records.zomi: A man bangzah in sang zongin ka pi in tawmno kiamsak dingin a ngen lo-in a pia ngei kei hi.

records.english: Shall I tell you what I paid for my first pair of shoes?
records.zomi: Ka khedap masa pen bangzah tawh ka lei hiam kong gen ding hiam?

records.english: What I remember most about the old market is how every price was a conversation.
records.zomi: Zuakna mun lui thu ah ka phawk pen pen van man khempeuh kikupna ahi hi, cih ahi hi.

records.english: Whatever we bought at the fair, my uncle always insisted that it had been a bargain.
records.zomi: Pawi ah bang peuh i lei zongin ka pa neu in a man neu hi, ci-in a gen tawntung hi.

records.english: Do you remember when the two tea stalls by the station kept lowering their prices?
records.zomi: Meileng dinna kiang-a tea zuakna dawhkan nih in a man a kiamsak tawntung uh na phawk hiam?

records.english: By the end of the week, a cup of tea cost less than a sweet, and both owners were laughing about it.
records.zomi: Kal tawp ciangin tea haai khat thei khum khat sangin a neu zaw a, a neipa nih in a nuihsan uh hi.

records.english: It might have been cheaper to buy the shoes in the city, but the bus fare cost more than the difference.
records.zomi: Khuapi ah khedap lei leng a man neu zaw kha ding hi, ahi zongin bus man in a kilamdanna sangin a tam zaw hi.

records.english: We used a little notebook to compare prices at the three shops in town.
records.zomi: Khuapi-a zuakna inn thum-a van man kiteh nadingin laibu neu khat i zang hi.

records.english: How did people know the price of things without labels?
records.zomi: Van man kigelh om lo-in mite in van man bangci-in a thei uh hiam?

records.english: Who in your family was the best at bargaining?
records.zomi: Na innkuan ah kua in a man kisut a siam pen hiam?

records.english: My grandmother, who could get a better price just by mentioning the seller's mother.
records.zomi: Ka pi, zuakpa' nu min a gen bek tawh a man hoih zaw ngah thei pa.

records.english: When my aunt began selling her baskets, she had no idea what price to ask.
records.zomi: Ka ni in a empeng te a zuak kipat ciangin bangzah a man ding hiam a thei kei hi.

records.english: An old trader told her to count the hours of work and then add a little for the skill.
records.zomi: Sumbawl upa khat in nasep nai te sim inla, a siamna adingin tawmno behlap in, ci-in a hilh hi.

records.english: We were allowed to keep any change that was smaller than a coin.
records.zomi: Dangka sik khat sangin a neu zaw sum kilaih peuhpeuh i kem thei hi.

records.english: Last month, my daughter paid for our dinner with her first salary.
records.zomi: Kha nung in ka tanu in a khasum masa pen tawh i nitak an a pia hi.

records.english: The old cash register was so loud that it rang like a bell every time it opened.
records.zomi: Sum koihna setna lui a ging lua ahih manin a kihon simin khawngging bangin a ging hi.

records.english: Was it hard to get used to paper money?
records.zomi: Sum lai zat a haksa hiam?

records.english: It might have been easier to pay by card, but my aunt liked to see the money leave her hand.
records.zomi: Card tawh piak a baih zaw kha ding hi, ahi zongin ka ni in a khut pan sum a pai a et a deih hi.

records.english: What I remember most about the old shop is the sound of coins dropping into the wooden drawer.
records.zomi: Zuakna inn lui thu ah ka phawk pen pen sing kenkuan sung-a dangka sik kiat ging ahi hi.

records.english: Counting the wages on Friday evenings was like a small ceremony in our house.
records.zomi: Laithai ni nitak simin kha sim pen i inn ah pawi neu khat bang ahi hi.

records.english: Our school fees were paid in two parts, after the harvest and before the rainy season.
records.zomi: I sang man pen kaihawl khit ciang leh guah hun ma-in khen nih-in kipia hi.

records.english: Can I pay you back next week, after I've sold the vegetables?
records.zomi: Anteh te ka zuak khit ciangin kal hong pai ding ah kong pia kik thei ding hiam?

records.english: Did your parents ever give you money to pay for things on your own?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa in nangma bek in van lei dingin sum hong pia ngei uh hiam?

records.english: Show me the coins you kept from those days.
records.zomi: Tua hunte pan na kem dangka sik te hong lak in.

records.english: My cousin used a small calculator to check every bill before he paid it.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam in a piak ma-in laimal khempeuh en dingin calculator neu khat a zang hi.

records.english: Shall I tell you how I paid for my first bicycle?
records.zomi: Ka siiksakol masa pen bangci-in ka lei hiam kong gen ding hiam?

records.english: Children, hold the coins tightly in your fist until we reach the shop.
records.zomi: Naupangte, zuakna inn i tun mateng dangka sik te na khut sungah hoih takin len un.

records.english: Every Friday, my uncle counted out his wages on the kitchen table and divided them into envelopes.
records.zomi: Laithai ni simin ka pa neu in an huanna dawhkan tungah a kha a sim a, lai-ip te sungah a khen hi.

records.english: The old coins were collected by my uncle and kept in a glass jar.
records.zomi: Dangka sik lui te ka pa neu in a khawm a, khuangkhai bel sungah a koih hi.

records.english: The coin we found in a drawer came from a country that no longer exists.
records.zomi: Kenkuan sungah i muh dangka sik pen tu-in om nawn lo gam khat pan a hong hi.

records.english: If the shopkeeper hadn't trusted us to pay later, we couldn't have bought medicine that winter.
records.zomi: Zuakna inn neipa in a nung ciangin pia dingin hong muan kei le tua khuavot in zatui i lei thei lo ding hi.

records.english: Which coin was worth the most when you were young?
records.zomi: Na neu lai-in dangka sik bang a man tam pen hiam?

records.english: Tell me about the first time you paid for something yourself.
records.zomi: Nangma-in bangmah na lei masak pen thu hong gen in.

records.english: Do you remember working in the school garden to pay part of your fees?
records.zomi: Na sang man khen khat piak nadingin sang huan ah na sep na phawk hiam?

records.english: Every Saturday morning, and I still know how to grow the best cabbages in the district.
records.zomi: Kiginni zingsang simin, leh tu-in zong gam sung-a kawlmukbe hoih pen suan dan ka thei lai hi.

records.english: Did the conductor ever give anyone the wrong change?
records.zomi: Bus sum lapa in kuamah sum kilaih khial a pia ngei hiam?

records.english: Never, and if you were short, he let you pay him the next day.
records.zomi: Pia ngei kei hi, na kiam leh a zing ciangin piak dingin hong phal hi.

records.english: How did people pay for things before there were banks in your village?
records.zomi: Na khua ah bank a om ma-in mite in van bangci-in a lei uh hiam?

records.english: Mostly in cash or in kind, and the shopkeeper kept a record of who owed what.
records.zomi: A tamzaw-in dangka-in ahih kei leh van tawh, leh zuakna inn neipa in kua in bang a ba hiam a gelh hi.

records.english: What did you buy with your first wages?
records.zomi: Na kha masa pen tawh bang na lei hiam?

records.english: A pair of boots for my father, who had walked barefoot to the fields for years.
records.zomi: Kum tampi sung khe sawn tawh lo ah a pai ka pa adingin khedap sau khat.

records.english: By the time the conductor reached the back of the bus, his bag was so heavy he could hardly lift it.
records.zomi: Bus sum lapa in bus nung lam a tun ciangin a ip a gik lua ahih manin a dawi zo kha kei hi.

records.english: My little sister once paid for a bread roll with a button, and the baker laughed and accepted it.
records.zomi: Ka nau nu in khatvei moh neu khat tawh kawmthap khat tawh a pia a, moh bawlpa in a nui a, a la hi.

records.english: Everyone, put your coins in the basket as it comes round.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh aw, empeng hong tun ciangin na dangka sik uh tua sungah koih un.

records.english: Whoever found a coin on the road had to give it to the church box.
records.zomi: Lampi tungah dangka sik a mu peuhpeuh in pawlpi sum koihna ah a koih ding hi.

records.english: Although we had very little cash, nobody in the village ever went without food.
records.zomi: Dangka tawmno bek i nei hangin khua ah kuamah an om lo-in a om ngei kei hi.

records.english: It was only when I paid my own bills that I understood how carefully my parents had managed money.
records.zomi: Keimah' laimal ka piak ciang bek ka nu leh ka pa in sum bangzah in limtakin a zang uh hiam ka thei hi.

records.english: When I was small, families in our village paid the healer with rice or chickens instead of money.
records.zomi: Ka neu lai-in i khua-a innkuante in damsakpa numei pen sum sangin buh ahih kei leh ak tawh a pia uh hi.

records.english: After my brother's fever broke, we took her two hens and a basket of eggs.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal' cisa a dam khit ciangin ak pi nih leh aktui empeng khat i tawi hi.

records.english: She gave one hen back and said that the eggs were more than enough.
records.zomi: Ak khat a pia kik a, aktui te a kicing lua hi, a ci hi.

records.english: My grandfather once paid the carpenter with a goat.
records.zomi: Ka pu in khatvei sing bawlpa kel khat tawh a pia hi.

records.english: The more coins I saved, the heavier the money box became, and the prouder I felt.
records.zomi: Dangka sik ka kikoih tam semsem ciangin sum bawm a gik semsem a, ka kipak semsem hi.

records.english: Who taught you to count money?
records.zomi: Sum sim dan kua in hong sin sak hiam?

records.english: I really did want to pay for my grandmother's glasses myself, so I saved for six months.
records.zomi: Ka pi' mitlimlang keimah in lei ka deih taktak ahih manin kha guk sung ka kikoih hi.

records.english: Why did your grandmother hide her money under the floor?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na pi in a sum inn phah nuai ah a sel hiam?

records.english: The bus conductor on our route carried a heavy leather bag full of coins.
records.zomi: I bus lampi-a bus sum lapa in dangka sik tawh a dim savun ip gik khat a pua hi.

records.english: He could give change to forty passengers without once looking down at his hands.
records.zomi: A khut a en ngei lo-in khualzin sawm li te sum kilaih a pia thei hi.

records.english: We children used to test him with large notes just to watch him do it.
records.zomi: Naupang i hih lai-un a bawl dan et nadingin sum lai lian tawh i sin hi.

records.english: Rather than taking money for the eggs, the farmer asked us to help him with the harvest.
records.zomi: Aktui man la sangin lo neipa in a kaihawl ah huh dingin hong ngen hi.

records.english: Was the healer ever paid in cash?
records.zomi: Damsakpa numei pen dangka tawh kipia ngei hiam?

records.english: Looking back, paying with chickens seems strange, but it worked well for everyone.
records.zomi: Nung lam en kik-in ak tawh piak pen lamdang bang hi, ahi zongin mi khempeuh adingin a hoih hi.

records.english: When did you first open a bank account?
records.zomi: Bang ciangin bank ah sum koihna na hon masa hiam?

records.english: Who looked after the money in your family?
records.zomi: Na innkuan ah kua in sum a kem hiam?

records.english: My grandmother, who kept it in a tin box under the floorboards.
records.zomi: Ka pi, inn phah nuai-a dal bawm khat sungah a kem pa.

records.english: When the shop got its first card machine, the older customers refused to use it.
records.zomi: Zuakna inn in card setna a ngah masak ciangin a lei mi upa zawte in zat a nuam kei uh hi.

records.english: My grandfather said that money you couldn't hold in your hand wasn't real money.
records.zomi: Ka pu in na khut tawh na len theih loh sum pen sum taktak hi lo hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Five years later, he was the first in the village to pay his bills by phone.
records.zomi: Kum nga khit ciangin amah in a laimal te phone tawh khua ah a pia masa pen ahi hi.

records.english: Where did you keep your savings when you were a child?
records.zomi: Na neu lai-in na sum kikoih koi ah na kem hiam?

records.english: The ticket seller let us travel for less because she couldn't find any change.
records.zomi: Lakkhia ding lai zuaknu in sum kilaih a mu kei ahih manin man neu zaw tawh hong pai sak hi.

records.english: For my mother's birthday, I broke open the clay money box I had kept for two years.
records.zomi: Ka nu' pianni adingin kum nih sung ka kem leivui sum bawm ka sukkham hi.

records.english: I sorted the coins on the kitchen floor into neat little towers.
records.zomi: An huanna inn phah tungah dangka sik te hoih takin ka ngam hi.

records.english: There was just enough to buy her a blue scarf from the market.
records.zomi: Zuakna mun pan ngawngkhih dum khat lei dingin a kicing hi.

records.english: I paid my first rent with money I had earned picking fruit all summer.
records.zomi: Khal bup theigah lo-in ka ngah sum tawh inn man masa pen ka pia hi.

records.english: Last week, my son returned a game he had bought with his birthday money.
records.zomi: Kal nung in ka tapa in a pianni sum tawh a lei kimawlna van a pia kik hi.

records.english: The radio we bought from a travelling salesman buzzed like a bee whenever it rained.
records.zomi: Khualzin zuakpa pan i lei radio pen guah a zuk simin khuai bangin a ging hi.

records.english: Looking back, the shopkeepers of those days seem much more generous than the rules allowed.
records.zomi: Nung lam en kik-in tua hun-a zuakna inn neite in thukham in a phal sangin a lungsim hoih zaw bang uh hi.

records.english: The mirror we bought for the wedding cracked on the bumpy bus ride home.
records.zomi: Mopawi adingin i lei mai-et pen inn ciahna bus kilawk lai-in a kek hi.

records.english: My aunt refused to take it back, because she said returning a broken mirror would bring bad luck.
records.zomi: Ka ni in a pia kik nuam kei a, mai-et kek pia kik pen vangsiatna a hong tun ding hi, a ci hi.

records.english: How long did your grandfather keep the goat?
records.zomi: Na pu in kel bangzah sung a kem hiam?

records.english: Did you ever take something back without telling your parents?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa' theih loh-in bangmah na pia kik ngei hiam?

records.english: Everyone, bring back any library books you bought by mistake at the school fair.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh aw, sang pawi ah khial-in na lei laibu inn laibu te hong tawi kik un.

records.english: Although the shop was a long walk away, my grandmother returned every single cracked plate.
records.zomi: Zuakna inn gamla mahmah hangin ka pi in kuang kek khempeuh a pia kik hi.

records.english: Please don't laugh, but I once returned a hat because my dog barked at it.
records.zomi: Nui kei un, ahi zongin ka ui in a hawng ahih manin khatvei lukhu khat ka pia kik hi.

records.english: The sack of rice my mother bought from the mill was full of small stones.
records.zomi: Ka nu in buh guaina pan a lei buh ip pen suang neute tawh a dim hi.

records.english: She carried it straight back and poured a handful onto the miller's table.
records.zomi: Tua pah-in a tawi kik a, buh guaipa' dawhkan tungah khut khat a sung hi.

records.english: He went red, apologized, and gave her a new sack from his own store.
records.zomi: Amah a san a, maisak a ngen a, a van koihna pan ip thak khat a pia hi.

records.english: My brother was too shy to take his new football boots back, even though they pinched his toes.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in a khezung a sinsak hangin a football khedap thak a pia kik dingin a maizum lua hi.

records.english: My sister marched into the shop with the boots and came out with a bigger pair.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu in khedap te tawh zuakna inn ah a lut a, a lian zaw khat tawh a pusuak hi.

records.english: He played in them for two seasons and never once thanked her.
records.zomi: Kum nih sung tua khedap tawh a kimawl a, khatvei zong lungdam a ci ngei kei hi.

records.english: Rather than taking his money back, my uncle asked the carpenter to make the table again properly.
records.zomi: A sum la kik sangin ka pa neu in sing bawlpa kiangah dawhkan hoih takin bawl kik dingin a ngen hi.

records.english: I went back to the bakery to return a loaf that was still raw in the middle.
records.zomi: A laizang ah a min nai loh moh khat pia kik dingin moh bawlna ah ka ciah kik hi.

records.english: The faulty kettles were collected by the shop and sent back to the factory.
records.zomi: A sia tuilumna bel te zuakna inn in a khawm a, factory ah a khak kik hi.

records.english: It might have been easier to keep the broken lamp, but my aunt wanted the money for her son's school books.
records.zomi: A sia meivak kem leng a baih zaw kha ding hi, ahi zongin ka ni in a tapa' sang laibu adingin sum a deih hi.

records.english: Could we have asked for our money back for the seeds?
records.zomi: Khaici adingin i sum ngen kik thei ding hiam?

records.english: I really did try to fix the umbrella myself before I took it back.
records.zomi: Ka pia kik ma-in kawl lukhu keimah in bawl dam dingin ka sin taktak hi.

records.english: We sent the camera back to the factory so that they could find out why the pictures were blurred.
records.zomi: Lim te bang hangin a vom hiam a theih nadingun camera pen factory ah i khak kik hi.

records.english: Shall I tell you about the shirt I returned three times?
records.zomi: Thum vei ka pia kik puan-akhi thu kong gen ding hiam?

records.english: My father used a pair of pliers to show the shopkeeper how loose the handle was.
records.zomi: Ka pa in a khutkhak bangzah in a nem hiam zuakna inn neipa a lak nadingin kawlkep a zang hi.

records.english: Was the shopkeeper angry when you brought the bicycle back?
records.zomi: Siiksakol na pia kik ciangin zuakna inn neipa a heh hiam?

records.english: We were given a free bag of oranges to say sorry for the bad ones.
records.zomi: A hoih lo te adingin maisak ngenna-in sangtam ip khat a man lo-in hong kipia hi.

records.english: My grandfather once bought a goat that was supposed to give plenty of milk.
records.zomi: Ka pu in khatvei nawi tampi pia ding ci kel khat a lei hi.

records.english: After a week without a single cupful, he led it back to the market on a rope.
records.zomi: Kal khat sung haai khat zong a piak loh khit ciangin khau tawh zuakna mun ah a kai kik hi.

records.english: The seller laughed, returned half the money, and let him keep the goat for its company.
records.zomi: Zuakpa a nui a, sum a kim a pia kik a, lawm dingin kel a kem dingin a phal hi.

records.english: Can I take the toy back if my nephew already has one?
records.zomi: Ka tanau in khat a nei khin leh kimawlna van ka pia kik thei ding hiam?

records.english: May I swap these sandals for the brown ones?
records.zomi: Hih khedap neu te a sangdup te tawh ka laih thei ding hiam?

records.english: The shoe seller let me change them, but only after I had cleaned the dust off the soles.
records.zomi: Khedap zuakpa in a laih dingin hong phal a, ahi zongin a khe nuai-a leivui ka sianseh khit ciang bek ahi hi.

records.english: Who in your family was brave enough to take things back?
records.zomi: Na innkuan ah kua in van pia kik dingin a hang hiam?

records.english: My mother, who once returned a cake because the icing was the wrong color for my sister's birthday.
records.zomi: Ka nu, ka sanggam nu' pianni adingin a tung-a rong a kilawm loh manin khatvei cake khat a pia kik pa.

records.english: Whoever bought a faulty item at the village shop could exchange it on market day.
records.zomi: Khua zuakna inn ah van sia a lei peuhpeuh in zuakna ni-in a laih thei hi.

records.english: Where did you take the clock when it stopped working?
records.zomi: Nai-ten a khawl ciangin koi ah na tawi hiam?

records.english: What did the market seller say when you tried to return the chickens?
records.zomi: Ak te na pia kik ciangin zuakpa in bang a ci hiam?

records.english: Why didn't your brother take the boots back himself?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na sanggam pasal in khedap te amah in a pia kik kei hiam?

records.english: At the autumn fair, I spent all my pocket money on a shiny watch.
records.zomi: Khuavot kipat hun pawi ah ka zat ding sum khempeuh nai tang khat tawh ka zang khin hi.

records.english: It stopped that same evening, just as I was showing it to my friends.
records.zomi: Tua nitak mah in ka lawmte ka lak laitakin a khawl hi.

records.english: When I went back the next weekend, the stall and its owner had disappeared.
records.zomi: Kal tawp hong pai ciangin ka ciah kik ciangin zuakna dawhkan leh a neipa a mang khin hi.

records.english: What I remember most about returning things as a child is how fast my heart beat at the counter.
records.zomi: Ka neu lai-in van pia kik thu ah ka phawk pen pen dawhkan kiang-a ka lungtang a sat dan ahi hi.

records.english: Which shop was the hardest to return things to?
records.zomi: Zuakna inn bang ah van pia kik a haksa pen hiam?

records.english: Was it common to return animals at the market?
records.zomi: Zuakna mun ah ganhing pia kik pen a tam hiam?

records.english: If my sister hadn't kept the box, the shop would never have accepted the radio.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu in bawm a kem kei le zuakna inn in radio a sang ngei lo ding hi.

records.english: Do you remember the blue cloth that turned the whole washing pink?
records.zomi: Puan sil khempeuh a san-ngoh sak puan dum na phawk hiam?

records.english: My grandmother took it back to the market and made the seller wash a piece in front of her.
records.zomi: Ka pi in zuakna mun ah a tawi kik a, zuakpa in a mai ah a khen khat silh dingin a sawl hi.

records.english: Did the miller ever sell your family bad rice again?
records.zomi: Buh guaipa in na innkuan kiangah buh hoih lo a zuak kik ngei hiam?

records.english: Never, and every new year he sent us a small bag of flour as a gift.
records.zomi: Zuak ngei kei hi, leh kum thak simin letsong-in buh-mal ip neu khat hong khak hi.

records.english: By the time the replacement arrived by post, my brother had grown out of the jacket.
records.zomi: Laikhak tawh a laih ding a tun ciangin ka sanggam pasal in kawt a lian khin hi.

records.english: When did shops in your town start giving refunds?
records.zomi: Na khuapi-a zuakna inn te in bang ciangin sum a pia kik kipan uh hiam?

records.english: Children, if your new pencils break, show them to me and I'll write to the shop.
records.zomi: Naupangte, na khedal thak uh a kek leh hong lak unla, zuakna inn ah lai kong gelh ding hi.

records.english: Tell me what happened when you returned the wedding shoes.
records.zomi: Mopawi khedap te na pia kik ciangin bang a piang hiam hong gen in.

records.english: The longer we waited to return the heater, the less willing the shop was to help.
records.zomi: Lum sakna setna pia kik dingin i ngak sawt semsem ciangin zuakna inn in huh a nuam semsem kei hi.

records.english: How did people return things before shops gave receipts?
records.zomi: Zuakna inn te in laimal a piak ma-un mite in van bangci-in a pia kik uh hiam?

records.english: The shopkeeper knew every customer, so your face was your receipt.
records.zomi: Zuakna inn neipa in a lei mi khempeuh a thei ahih manin na mai pen na laimal ahi hi.

records.english: It was only when the watch stopped that I realized why it had been so cheap.
records.zomi: Nai a khawl ciang bek bang hangin a man a neu lua hiam ka thei hi.

records.english: None of the seeds we bought that spring came up, not even one row.
records.zomi: Tua spring-a i lei khaici te khat zong a khang kei a, a tang khat zong a om kei hi.

records.english: The seed seller believed us and gave us a fresh packet the next season.
records.zomi: Khaici zuakpa in hong um a, a zom hun ciangin khaici ip thak khat hong pia hi.

records.english: If you disagree with someone, explain why without making fun of them.
records.zomi: Mi khat tawh na kilem kei leh amah nuihsan lo-in bang hangin hiam gen in.

records.english: Eating isn't allowed in the computer room.
records.zomi: Computer inndei sungah an nek kiphal lo hi.

records.english: You're welcome to ask questions, but wait until I've finished explaining.
records.zomi: Thu na dong thei hi, ahi zongin ka gen siang zawh mateng ngak in.

records.english: Thank you for helping the new girl find her way.
records.zomi: Nungak thak in a lampi a muh nadingin na huh lungdam hi.

records.english: By keeping her voice low, the teacher made everyone lean in to listen.
records.zomi: A aw niam-in a gen ahih manin saya in mi khempeuh ngai dingin a nai sak hi.

records.english: Could you please stop tapping your pen on the desk?
records.zomi: Dawhkan tungah na khedal tawh na kik khawl thei ding hiam?

records.english: Nobody is allowed to leave the room until the work has been checked.
records.zomi: Nasep a kien khit mateng kuamah inndei pan pusuak dingin kiphal lo hi.

records.english: I was moved to the front row because I kept chatting with Tuang.
records.zomi: Tuang tawh thu ka gen den ahih manin a ma pen lam ah hong koih uh hi.

records.english: Yesterday, Kim copied her friend's homework.
records.zomi: Zanin Kim in a lawm' innlai a gelh kik hi.

records.english: The teacher noticed that both had made exactly the same mistake.
records.zomi: A nih in khialhna kibang mah a bawl uh, cih saya in a mu hi.

records.english: Kim was asked to do the work again during the break.
records.zomi: Kim pen tawlngakna hun sungin a nasep bawl kik dingin kisawl hi.

records.english: Are we allowed to use calculators in the exam?
records.zomi: Sitna ah calculator zang thei ding i hi hiam?

records.english: No, only pencils, rulers, and an eraser.
records.zomi: Hi kei hi, khedal, teh-na leh phiatna bek.

records.english: May I leave the room for a minute, please?
records.zomi: Minit khat inndei pan ka pusuak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, but come straight back.
records.zomi: Pusuak thei hi, ahi zongin manlang takin hong kik in.

records.english: This morning, a football came through the classroom window.
records.zomi: Tu zingsang in football khat sang inndei tukvuang ah hong lut hi.

records.english: Nobody was hurt, but there was glass all over Nuam's desk.
records.zomi: Kuamah a liam kei hi, ahi zongin Nuam' dawhkan tungah khuangkhai khempeuh a om hi.

records.english: The boys who were playing came in, apologized, and helped sweep it up.
records.zomi: A kimawl tangvalte hong lut uh a, maisak a ngen uh a, phiat dingin a huh uh hi.

records.english: Respectful pupils can still disagree with a teacher, as long as they explain their reasons calmly.
records.zomi: Zahtakna nei sangnaupangte in a hangte uh dai takin a gen sung teng saya tawh a kilem lo thei uh hi.

records.english: Rude comments about other people's families are not tolerated in this classroom.
records.zomi: Hih sang inndei sungah mi dangte' innkuan thu gen siatna kiphal lo hi.

records.english: When the head teacher walked in, the whole class stood up.
records.zomi: Sang makaipa a lut ciangin sangnaupang khempeuh a ding uh hi.

records.english: Good behavior is noticed and praised in our school, not only good marks.
records.zomi: I sang ah sitna-a mak hoih bek hi lo-in hihna hoih zong kimu a, kiphat hi.

records.english: Is it all right if I finish my drawing at home?
records.zomi: Ka lim gelh inn ah ka zo thei ding hiam?

records.english: I felt terrible after I laughed at Ciin's wrong answer.
records.zomi: Ciin' dawnna khial ka nuihsan khit ciangin ka lungsim a na mahmah hi.

records.english: You can sit with Lia if you promise to work.
records.zomi: Na sep ding na ciam leh Lia tawh na tu thei hi.

records.english: If the rules are agreed together, pupils are far more likely to keep them.
records.zomi: Thukham te khawm-in i kilem leh sangnaupangte in a zui zaw ding uh hi.

records.english: The teacher said, "If you finish early, read your book quietly."
records.zomi: Saya in, “Na zo masa leh na laibu dai takin sim in,” a ci hi.

records.english: A classroom works best when pupils feel safe enough to make mistakes.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte in khial ding a lau loh ciangun sang inndei a hoih pen hi.

records.english: Phones must stay in your bags during lessons.
records.zomi: Thu sin hun sungin phone te na ip uh sungah om ding hi.

records.english: The broken chair has been taken away and will be replaced tomorrow.
records.zomi: Tutna sia kila khin a, zingciang ciangin a thak kikoih ding hi.

records.english: Why are you standing outside the classroom?
records.zomi: Bang hangin sang inndei pua ah na ding hiam?

records.english: The teacher sent me out for laughing during the test.
records.zomi: Sitna lai-in ka nui ahih manin saya in hong sawl khia hi.

records.english: Who left the paint brushes in the sink?
records.zomi: Kua in rong nulna te tuisilna sungah a nusia hiam?

records.english: Please put your chairs under the desks before you leave.
records.zomi: Na pai ma-un na tutna uh dawhkan nuai ah koih un.

records.english: The more responsibility the children were given, the better they behaved.
records.zomi: Naupangte' kipiak mawhpuakna a tam semsem ciangin a hihna uh a hoih semsem hi.

records.english: My son's teacher says he's polite but talks too much.
records.zomi: Ka tapa' saya in, amah zahtakna nei hi, ahi zongin thu a gen tam lua hi, a ci hi.

records.english: It was the quietest girl in the class who finally told the others to stop teasing him.
records.zomi: Amah nuihsan te khawl dingin a tawp-in mi dangte a hilh pen sang inndei sung-a nungak daih pen ahi hi.

records.english: How do you keep a class of forty children so calm?
records.zomi: Naupang sawm li sang inndei khat bangci-in daih takin na kem hiam?

records.english: I give them a job each, so everyone feels responsible for something.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh bangmah khat adingin mawhpuakna a neih nadingun a khat ciat nasep ka pia hi.

records.english: Sorry I'm late, Mr. Thang — the bus was full.
records.zomi: Pu Thang, ka nun ahih manin maisak ngen ing — bus a dim hi.

records.english: Can we work in pairs for this exercise?
records.zomi: Hih sin ding ah nih ciat-in i sem thei ding hiam?

records.english: Whenever the class gets noisy, our teacher claps a rhythm and we clap it back.
records.zomi: Sang inndei a buai ciangin i saya in khut beng a, kei te in i beng kik hi.

records.english: Ben said sorry to Mai for taking her ruler.
records.zomi: Ben in Mai' teh-na a laksak ahih manin maisak a ngen hi.

records.english: Line up by the door when the bell rings.
records.zomi: Khawngging a ging ciangin kongkhak kiang ah kigual un.

records.english: Shall we make our own class rules on the first day of term?
records.zomi: Sang kihon ni masa pen-in i sang inndei thukham te i bawl ding hiam?

records.english: What bothers our teacher most is not noise but unkindness.
records.zomi: I saya' lungkham pen ging hi lo-in mi siatna ahi hi.

records.english: Stop talking and look at the board, please.
records.zomi: Thu gen khawl unla, suanglaipi en un.

records.english: We listen quietly when someone else is speaking.
records.zomi: Mi khat a gen laitakin dai takin i ngai hi.

records.english: Well done, everyone — that was the calmest lesson we've had all week!
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh hoih mahmah — kal khat sung-a thu sin daih pen ahi hi!

records.english: The classroom is tidied at the end of every day.
records.zomi: Ni simin nitak lam ciangin sang inndei kiman sak hi.

records.english: Please raise your hand if you want to speak.
records.zomi: Thu na gen nop leh na khut dawh in.

records.english: Don't run in the corridor.
records.zomi: Inn lampi sungah tai kei un.

records.english: Strict as she was about homework, she was fair to every pupil.
records.zomi: Innlai thu ah a khauh hangin sangnaupang khempeuh tungah a dik hi.

records.english: The pupil who wrote on the wall was asked to clean it off after school.
records.zomi: Bang tungah a gelh sangnaupang pen sang khit ciangin phiat dingin kisawl hi.

records.english: Every Friday, our teacher chooses one pupil who has been especially kind.
records.zomi: Laithai ni simin i saya in a lungsim hoih mahmah sangnaupang khat a teel hi.

records.english: Last week, she chose Hau for sharing his lunch with a boy who had forgotten his.
records.zomi: Kal nung in a sun an a mangngilh tangval khat tawh a sun an a hawm ahih manin Hau a teel hi.

records.english: Hau went red, but I could see that he was proud.
records.zomi: Hau a san a, ahi zongin a kipak hi, cih ka mu thei hi.

records.english: What happens if someone is late three times in a week?
records.zomi: Mi khat kal khat sungin thum vei a nun leh bang a piang ding hiam?

records.english: Rather than punishing the whole class, the teacher spoke privately to the two boys involved.
records.zomi: Sang inndei bup gawt sangin saya in a kihel tangval nih kiangah a tuamin a gen hi.

records.english: Some children misbehave simply because they are bored, not because they want to cause trouble.
records.zomi: Naupang pawl khat haksatna bawl a deih uh hang hi lo-in a lungsim uh a ning lua hang bek-in a hihna uh a hoih kei hi.

records.english: A full pantry is worth more than a full purse, my grandmother used to say.
records.zomi: An kholna khan dim pen sum ip dim sangin a man tam zaw hi, ci-in ka pi in a gen ngei hi.

records.english: Buying a solar lamp meant we no longer had to spend money on kerosene every week.
records.zomi: Ni vak meivak khat i lei ciangin kal simin meisi adingin sum i zat nawn ding a kisam kei hi.

records.english: Once my parents paid off their debts, they invited the whole family to dinner.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in a leiba uh a piak khit ciangun innkuan bup nitak an ah a sam uh hi.

records.english: We might have saved more if we had cooked at home, but we were too tired after work.
records.zomi: Inn ah an huan leng sum tam zaw i kikoih kha ding hi, ahi zongin nasep khit ciangin i ol lua hi.

records.english: How did your family pay for your cousin's train ticket to university?
records.zomi: Na innkuan in na sanggam' sangpi pai ding meileng lakkhia ding lai man bangci-in a pia uh hiam?

records.english: We all agreed to give up meat on weekdays until we had saved enough.
records.zomi: Kicing i kikoih mateng kal sung ni-in sa nek khawl dingin i khempeuh i kilem hi.

records.english: Why did your mother keep the rice money separate from everything else?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na nu in buh sum pen a dang khempeuh tawh a khen hiam?

records.english: Living on one salary for a year taught us the difference between what we wanted and what we needed.
records.zomi: Kum khat sung khasum khat bek tawh nuntak in i deih leh i kisap kikal kilamdanna hong sin sak hi.

records.english: Although we were never rich, our parents made sure we never felt poor.
records.zomi: I hau ngei kei hangin ka nu leh ka pa in i zawng hi, ci-in i ngaihsut lohna dingin a kidawm uh hi.

records.english: We bought a goat instead of a television, and its milk saved us money every day.
records.zomi: Television sangin kel khat i lei a, a nawi in ni simin sum hong kem sak hi.

records.english: If my grandfather hadn't saved so carefully, we would have lost the farm in that dry year.
records.zomi: Ka pu in limtakin a kikoih kei le tua kum keu in i lo i mansuah ding hi.

records.english: Guess what we did with the money we saved on haircuts.
records.zomi: Sam at man-a i kikoih sum tawh bang i bawl hiam ngaihsun in.

records.english: However carefully we planned, something always broke in the last week of the month.
records.zomi: Bangzah in limtakin i geel zongin kha tawp kal ah bangmah khat a sia tawntung hi.

records.english: Our grocery bill fell after we started growing our own tomatoes.
records.zomi: Keimah mehtuuk i suan kipat khit ciangin an lei man laimal a niam hi.

records.english: A small chalkboard by the kitchen door showed how close we were to buying a water filter.
records.zomi: An huanna kongkhak kiang-a suanglaipi neu khat in tui siangsakna setna lei dingin bangzah in i nai hiam a lak hi.

records.english: Every time someone saved a little, my brother drew another line on it with a stub of chalk.
records.zomi: Mi khat in tawmno a kikoih simin ka sanggam pasal in suangvum tawm khat tawh a tungah gual khat a khai hi.

records.english: My aunt cooked one big pot of soup on Sundays to last us until Wednesday.
records.zomi: Ka ni in Nilai ni dong i neih nadingin Nipini simin an tui beel lian khat a huan hi.

records.english: How did people save before there was a bank nearby?
records.zomi: A kiang ah bank a om ma-in mite in sum bangci-in a kikoih uh hiam?

records.english: By the time we had paid for the wedding, there was barely enough left for the honeymoon.
records.zomi: Mopawi man i piak khit ciangin ki-ten khit khualzinna adingin tawmno bek a om hi.

records.english: Were you ever given pocket money?
records.zomi: Zat ding sum hong kipia ngei hiam?

records.english: The money for the new well was raised by the families on our street.
records.zomi: Tuikhuk thak adingin sum pen i lampi-a innkuante in a khawm uh hi.

records.english: Our budget was so tight that a single broken window became a family crisis.
records.zomi: I sum zat geel a kiim lua ahih manin tukvuang khat a kek bek zong innkuan haksatna suak hi.

records.english: In our first month of marriage, the money ran out on the twentieth day.
records.zomi: I ki-ten kha masa pen-in ni sawm nihna ciangin sum a bei hi.

records.english: For the last ten days, we lived on lentils, rice, and a great deal of laughter.
records.zomi: Ni sawm nunung sungin be, buh, leh nuih tampi tawh i nungta hi.

records.english: After that, my husband and I planned every month before it began.
records.zomi: Tua khit ciangin ka pasal leh kei in kha khempeuh a kipat ma-in i geel hi.

records.english: Not having a fridge meant my mother had to plan meals for one day at a time.
records.zomi: Vot sak setna i neih loh manin ka nu in ni khat ciat adingin an a geel ding a kisam hi.

records.english: What did a week's shopping cost when you were first married?
records.zomi: Na ki-ten masa lai-in kal khat van lei bangzah a bei hiam?

records.english: Whatever we saved from the egg money went toward a trip to the coast each summer.
records.zomi: Aktui sum pan i kikoih peuhpeuh khal simin tuipi gei khualzinna adingin kizang hi.

records.english: Would you like to see the old account book my grandmother kept?
records.zomi: Ka pi' a kem sum lut leh pai laibu lui na et nuam hiam?

records.english: Do you remember how the family next door taught us to preserve vegetables for the winter?
records.zomi: A kiang inn-a innkuan in khuavot adingin anteh kem dan hong sin sak na phawk hiam?

records.english: It was only when I paid for my own groceries that I understood my mother's careful shopping lists.
records.zomi: Keimah an lei man ka piak ciang bek ka nu' van lei ding lai limtakin a gelhna ka thei hi.

records.english: My parents didn't allow us to buy anything on credit, not even a bicycle.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in leiba-in bangmah lei dingin hong phal kei uh a, siiksakol zong hong phal kei uh hi.

records.english: What was the first big thing your family saved up for?
records.zomi: Na innkuan in lei dingin a kikoih masak pen van lian bang ahi hiam?

records.english: A radio, and we listened to it so much that the batteries cost more than the radio.
records.zomi: Radio khat, a tam lua-in i ngai ahih manin a battery man in radio man sangin a tam zaw hi.

records.english: When I turned fifteen, my father let me plan the family budget for one month.
records.zomi: Kum sawm leh nga ka phak ciangin ka pa in kha khat sung innkuan sum zat geel dingin hong phal hi.

records.english: I spent far too much on meat in the first week and had to serve beans for the rest.
records.zomi: Kal masa pen-in sa ah sum tam lua ka zang a, a dang ni sungin bepi ka pia ding a kisam hi.

records.english: He never said a word, but he smiled every time I put the beans on the table.
records.zomi: Amah in thu khat zong a gen kei a, ahi zongin dawhkan tungah bepi ka koih simin a nui hi.

records.english: I was allowed to sit in on the budget meeting for the first time when I was twelve.
records.zomi: Kum sawm leh nih ka phak ciangin sum zat geel kikhopna ah tu dingin hong phal masa uh hi.

records.english: Could your family afford new shoes every year?
records.zomi: Na innkuan in kum simin khedap thak a lei zo uh hiam?

records.english: Who kept the household accounts when you were growing up?
records.zomi: Na khanlai-in kua in inn sum lut leh pai a gelh hiam?

records.english: I'll help you plan your first budget if you promise to stick to it.
records.zomi: Na zui ding na ciam leh na sum zat geel masa pen geel dingin kong huh ding hi.

records.english: I remember the night my parents sat up late, working out how to pay for my brother's glasses.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal' mitlimlang man bangci-in a pia ding uh hiam ka nu leh ka pa in zan sawt a ngaihsut zan ka phawk hi.

records.english: My parents saved for a whole year to buy a bread oven.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in moh emna meikhuk khat lei dingin kum khat bup a kikoih uh hi.

records.english: Within months, my mother was baking bread for half the village.
records.zomi: Kha tawmno sungin ka nu in khua a kim adingin moh a em hi.

records.english: The money she earned paid for my older sister's nursing course.
records.zomi: A ngah sum in ka u nu' nurse sinna man a pia hi.

records.english: What a relief it was when the last payment on the house was made!
records.zomi: Inn man piak nunung a kibawl ciangin lungmuanna bangzah ahi hiam!

records.english: My uncle walked to work for a whole year to save for his daughter's wedding.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in a tanu' mopawi adingin kikoih dingin kum khat bup nasepna ah a pai hi.

records.english: I asked my mother once why we never went on holiday.
records.zomi: Khatvei bang hangin nopsakna khualzin i pai ngei kei hiam ka nu ka dong hi.

records.english: She said the holiday money was sitting in my school bag, in the form of books.
records.zomi: Nopsakna khualzin sum pen ka sang ip sungah laibu bangin a om hi, a ci hi.

records.english: What I most admired was how calmly my mother handled our money in the worst year.
records.zomi: Ka lamdang sak pen kum haksa pen sungin ka nu in i sum a kem dan dai takin a kem ahi hi.

records.english: What did you decide to do with the money your great-aunt left you?
records.zomi: Na pi neu in hong nusiat sum tawh bang bawl dingin na thukhen hiam?

records.english: Half went into the bank, and the rest paid for a new roof on her old house.
records.zomi: A kim bank ah kikoih a, a dang in a inn lui adingin innkhum thak a pia hi.

records.english: When the last of us left home, our parents moved to a smaller house to save on rent.
records.zomi: I nunung pen inn a nusiat ciangin i nu leh i pa in inn man a kiam nadingin inn neu zaw ah a kitawn uh hi.

records.english: My father decided to learn to cut hair so that we wouldn't have to pay the barber.
records.zomi: Sam at man i piak lohna dingin ka pa in sam at sin dingin a thukhen hi.

records.english: The first few haircuts were so uneven that my brothers wore caps to school.
records.zomi: A sam at masa te a kibang lo lua ahih manin ka sanggam pasalte in sang ah lukhu a khu uh hi.

records.english: By the end of the year, the neighbors were asking him to cut theirs too.
records.zomi: Kum tawp ciangin inn vengte in amau' sam zong at dingin a ngen uh hi.

records.english: Did your parents ever argue about money in front of you?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa in na mai ah sum thu-in a kinial ngei uh hiam?

records.english: My grandfather planned the whole season's spending on an old wooden abacus.
records.zomi: Ka pu in hun bup sum zat ding sing kisimna lui khat tawh a geel hi.

records.english: Please don't tell Grandma how much we spent on the party.
records.zomi: Pawi adingin bangzah i zang hiam Pi kiangah gen kei in.

records.english: Have you forgotten the year we learned to mend our own shoes?
records.zomi: Keimah khedap bawl dam i sin kum na mangngilh khin hiam?

records.english: Our friendship began with a wrong number, when she rang my phone looking for a plumber.
records.zomi: I lawmta pen sum dial khial khat tawh a kipan a, tuikhuam bawlpa zon-in ka phone ah a sam hi.

records.english: We talked for twenty minutes before either of us realized the mistake.
records.zomi: I nih in khialhna i theih ma-un minit sawm nih sung thu i kikum hi.

records.english: What began as a quarrel over a swing became a friendship of fifty years.
records.zomi: Lawk a kinialna-in a kipan pen kum sawm nga lawmta a suak hi.

records.english: If my friend hadn't lent me her notes, I would have failed my first year.
records.zomi: Ka lawm in a laigelh te hong pia kei le ka kum masa ah ka sit ding hi.

records.english: When I was twelve, our class was given pen friends at a school in another country.
records.zomi: Kum sawm leh nih ka phak ciangin i sang inndei in gamdang sang khat-a laikhak lawm te kipia hi.

records.english: Mine was a girl named Sofia, and we wrote to each other for nearly thirty years.
records.zomi: Ka lawm pen Sofia a kici nungak khat ahi a, kum sawm thum dek sung lai i kikhak hi.

records.english: Last summer, we finally met at an airport, and we recognized each other at once.
records.zomi: Khal kum nung in a tawp-in vanlengtual ah i kimu a, tua pah-in i kithei hi.

records.english: Could we have stayed friends if I hadn't moved away?
records.zomi: Ka kitawn kei le lawm-in i om thei ding hiam?

records.english: Please give Sofia my love when you next write to her.
records.zomi: Sofia kiangah lai na khak kik ciangin ka itna gen sak in.

records.english: Which of your childhood friends do you miss the most?
records.zomi: Na naupan lai lawmte lakah kua na lungngai pen hiam?

records.english: My brother taught the new boy our local games so that he wouldn't feel left out.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in tangval thak a kikhen lohna dingin i khua kimawlnate a sin sak hi.

records.english: My parents didn't let me play by the river unless my older friends came too.
records.zomi: Ka lawm upa zawte a hong kei uh leh ka nu leh ka pa in gun kiang ah kimawl dingin hong phal kei uh hi.

records.english: Did you keep in touch with anyone from your first school?
records.zomi: Na sang masa pan kuamah tawh na kikum lai hiam?

records.english: However often we argued, we always made up before bedtime.
records.zomi: Bangzah vei i kinial zongin ihmut ma-in i kilem kik tawntung hi.

records.english: Two lonely people, a long train journey, and a bag of mangoes were all it took.
records.zomi: Lungngai mi nih, meileng khualzinna sawt khat, leh haigah ip khat bek a kisam hi.

records.english: What made you trust Sofia enough to tell her your secrets?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na thusim te gen dingin Sofia na muang hiam?

records.english: Nobody in my new class spoke to me until the teacher asked me to sing.
records.zomi: Saya in la sa dingin hong sawl mateng ka sang inndei thak ah kuamah in hong kikum kei hi.

records.english: As a boy, I spent every afternoon watching an old man repair radios in his tiny shop.
records.zomi: Tangval ka hih lai-in a zuakna inn neu-ah radio bawl dam pu upa khat en dingin nitak simin ka zang hi.

records.english: One day, he handed me a screwdriver and said, "You might as well help."
records.zomi: Ni khat in thau-it bawlna khat hong pia a, “Hong huh mah in,” a ci hi.

records.english: He became my closest friend, even though he was sixty years older than me.
records.zomi: Kum sawm guk in hong upat zaw hangin ka lawm kinai pen a suak hi.

records.english: I was sent to stay with my aunt for a summer, and her neighbor's daughter became my first real friend.
records.zomi: Khal khat sung ka ni kiang ah om dingin hong sawl uh a, a inn vengte' tanu in ka lawm taktak masa pen a suak hi.

records.english: Waiting outside the school for our exam results, I started talking to the boy next to me.
records.zomi: I sitna dawnnate ngak-in sang pua ah i om laitakin ka kiang-a tangval tawh thu ka kikum kipan hi.

records.english: My friend's mother always set an extra place at the table in case I came by.
records.zomi: Ka lawm' nu in ka hong kha ding hi, ci-in dawhkan ah mun khat a koih tawntung hi.

records.english: By the time we finished university, we had been friends for longer than we had been apart.
records.zomi: Sangpi i zawh ciangin i kikhen sang-in lawm-in sawt zawin i om khin hi.

records.english: I'm so glad you said hello to me on that first awful day!
records.zomi: Tua ni masa hoih lo pen-in hong hopih na hih manin ka lungdam mahmah hi!

records.english: Although we came from very different families, we understood each other from the start.
records.zomi: Innkuan kibang lo mahmah pan i hong hangin a kipat cil pan i kithei hi.

records.english: Don't let anyone tell you that friendships can't start late in life.
records.zomi: Nuntakna nunung lam ah lawmta a kipan thei kei hi, ci-in kuamah in hong hilh kei hen.

records.english: We might never have met if the bus hadn't broken down outside her village.
records.zomi: A khua pua ah bus a sia kei le i kimu ngei lo kha ding hi.

records.english: Do you still have the bracelet your best friend made for you?
records.zomi: Na lawm hoih pen in hong bawlsak khutkhih na nei lai hiam?

records.english: The girl next door gave me her old bicycle when she grew too tall for it.
records.zomi: A kiang inn-a nungak in a sang lua ciangin a siiksakol lui hong pia hi.

records.english: When we were children, my best friend and I made a promise never to keep secrets from each other.
records.zomi: Naupang i hih lai-in ka lawm hoih pen leh kei in thu kisel ngei lo dingin i kiciam hi.

records.english: My friend Lal carried my school bag for a month when I broke my arm.
records.zomi: Ka ban a kitan ciangin ka lawm Lal in kha khat sung ka sang ip a pua hi.

records.english: Who was the first person to be kind to you in the city?
records.zomi: Khuapi ah kua in hong itna masa pen a lak hiam?

records.english: We saved our pocket money for weeks to buy our teacher a farewell present.
records.zomi: I saya kikhenna letsong lei dingin kal tampi sung zat ding sum i kikoih hi.

records.english: Were you allowed to visit your friends' houses when you were small?
records.zomi: Na neu lai-in na lawmte' inn ah na veh thei hiam?

records.english: Only on Saturdays, and only if we were home before the lamps were lit.
records.zomi: Kiginni ni bek, leh meivak a kihal ma-in inn ah i tun leh bek.

records.english: We met at a wedding and danced together all night without knowing each other's names.
records.zomi: Mopawi khat ah i kimu a, i min i kitheih lo-in zan bup khawm-in i lam hi.

records.english: Why did you stop speaking to your neighbor for a whole year?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na inn vengpa kum khat bup na kikum kei hiam?

records.english: What did you and your friends do after school when you were young?
records.zomi: Na neu lai-in sang khit ciangin nang leh na lawmte in bang na bawl uh hiam?

records.english: Looking back, the friends I made in hard times turned out to be the most loyal.
records.zomi: Nung lam en kik-in hun haksa lai-a ka lawmte in a muanhuai pen uh hi.

records.english: A boy at the camp shared his blanket with me on the coldest night.
records.zomi: Om-na mun ah tangval khat in zan vot pen-in a puannak hong hawm hi.

records.english: Does Mang still remember the tree house we built?
records.zomi: I bawl singkung tung inn Mang in a phawk lai hiam?

records.english: I knitted a scarf for my new friend so that she wouldn't be cold on the walk to school.
records.zomi: Sang pai lampi ah a vot lohna dingin ka lawm thak adingin ngawngkhih khat ka phiat hi.

records.english: It was my friend who first told me I should apply to the teachers' college.
records.zomi: Saya sang ah lut dingin hong hilh masa pen ka lawm ahi hi.

records.english: I once waved at a woman across the street, thinking she was my cousin.
records.zomi: Khatvei ka sanggam ahi hi, ci-in lampi gal lam-a numei khat ka khut ka vai hi.

records.english: She waved back, crossed the road to say hello, and we've had tea together every week since.
records.zomi: Amah zong a khut a vai kik a, hopih dingin lampi a kan a, tua pan kipan kal simin tea khawm-in i dawn hi.

records.english: Who taught you to swim?
records.zomi: Tuipeek sin dingin kua in hong sin sak hiam?

records.english: A girl from the next village, who held my chin above the water until I stopped panicking.
records.zomi: A kiang khua pan nungak khat, ka lau khawl mateng tui tung ah ka khabe a dawh pa.

records.english: It was only when I left home that I realized how much my childhood friends had shaped me.
records.zomi: Inn ka nusiat ciang bek ka naupan lai lawmte in bangzah in hong bawl uh hiam ka thei hi.

records.english: My closest friendship grew out of a single kind word on a bad day.
records.zomi: Ka lawmta kinai pen ni hoih lo khat-a kammal hoih khat pan a khang hi.

records.english: How long did it take you to feel at home in your new class?
records.zomi: Na sang inndei thak ah na inn bangin na kisak dingin bangzah sawt hiam?

records.english: The friendship survived two wars, three moves, and a broken engagement.
records.zomi: Lawmta in gal nih, kitawnna thum, leh kiteenna kiciamna kitan khat a zo hi.

records.english: How did you get to know the woman who sold fruit at the corner?
records.zomi: Lampi kikona ah theigah a zuak numei bangci-in na thei hiam?

records.english: I bought a banana from her every morning on my way to work, and one day she asked about my mother.
records.zomi: Nasepna ka pai lampi ah zingsang simin a kiang pan nahtang khat ka lei a, ni khat in ka nu thu a dong hi.

records.english: On a two-day train journey, I shared a compartment with an old couple.
records.zomi: Ni nih meileng khualzinna ah inn kiteng upa nih tawh mun khat ka hawm hi.

records.english: They offered me their boiled eggs, and I offered them my mangoes.
records.zomi: A aktui lum te hong pia uh a, kei zong ka haigahte ka pia hi.

records.english: We exchanged addresses at the last station, and they sent me a card every New Year.
records.zomi: Dinna nunung pen ah i omna mun i kipia a, Kum Thak simin card hong khak uh hi.

records.english: On my first day of school, a boy called Kap pushed me off the swing.
records.zomi: Sang ka kah ni masa pen-in Kap a kici tangval khat in lawk pan hong sawn hi.

records.english: We rolled in the dust until a teacher pulled us apart by our collars.
records.zomi: Saya khat in i ngawng puan te tawh hong khen mateng leivui sungah i kilet hi.

records.english: By Friday, he was defending me in the playground, and he is still my closest friend.
records.zomi: Laithai ni ciangin kimawlna mun ah hong hu a, tu dong ka lawm kinai pen ahi lai hi.

records.english: In my family, invitations to a wedding were always carried by hand with a small packet of tea.
records.zomi: Ka innkuan ah mopawi samna te tea ip neu khat tawh khut tawh kipuak tawntung hi.

records.english: We sewed new cushions for the guest room before my aunt came to stay.
records.zomi: Ka ni ka inn ah a om ding ma-in khualte' inndei adingin lupna khuh thak i khui hi.

records.english: By the time the last guest had gone, the sun was already coming up.
records.zomi: Khual nunung pen a pai ciangin ni a suak khin hi.

records.english: Were children allowed to sit with the adult guests?
records.zomi: Naupangte in khual upate tawh tu dingin a kiphal uh hiam?

records.english: No, we ate in the kitchen and listened to the stories through the door.
records.zomi: Kiphal kei hi, an huanna ah i ne a, kongkhak pan tangthu te i ngai hi.

records.english: We invited the exchange student from our school to her first harvest festival.
records.zomi: I sang-a gamdang sangnaupang khat a kaihawl pawi masa pen ah i sam hi.

records.english: By the end of the evening, she had learned two folk dances and eaten three helpings of rice.
records.zomi: Nitak a bei ciangin khua lam nih a sin khin a, buh kuang thum a ne khin hi.

records.english: A whole goat was cooked for the guests, and nothing was left by the morning.
records.zomi: Khualte adingin kel khat bup kihuan a, zingsang ciangin bangmah a om nawn kei hi.

records.english: How did people find out about a wedding before there were printed invitations?
records.zomi: Samna lai a om ma-in mite in mopawi thu bangci-in a thei uh hiam?

records.english: Someone from the family visited each house in person and told them the date.
records.zomi: Innkuan pan mi khat in inn khempeuh a veh a, ni a gen hi.

records.english: How I wish I had invited my grandfather's old friend before he moved away!
records.zomi: Ka pu' lawm upa a kitawn ma-in ka sam kei bang hiam ka lungkham hi!

records.english: My mother said, "A guest who comes without warning is still a guest."
records.zomi: Ka nu in, “Gen lo-in a hong khual zong khual ahi hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: My uncle shouted, "Come in, come in, the soup is getting cold!" to everyone who passed the gate.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in kongpi a kantan mi khempeuh kiangah, “Lut un, lut un, an tui a vot ding hi!” ci-in a kiko hi.

records.english: The invitations for my brother's wedding were written by a calligrapher in the market.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal' mopawi samna lai te zuakna mun-a laigelh siampa in a gelh hi.

records.english: Why did your mother always invite one more person than she had food for?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na nu in an a neih sangin mi khat behlap a sam tawntung hiam?

records.english: When did you first invite friends to your own home?
records.zomi: Bang ciangin na inn ah na lawmte na sam masa hiam?

records.english: I felt so proud the first time a guest asked for my recipe.
records.zomi: Khual khat in ka an huan dan a dot masak ciangin ka kipak mahmah hi.

records.english: Would the house have been finished that year if the neighbors hadn't come to help?
records.zomi: Inn vengte a hong huh kei uh le tua kum in inn a zo ding hiam?

records.english: Our door was open to anyone who knocked, whether we knew them or not.
records.zomi: I kongkhak pen i thei hi zongin i thei kei hi zongin a kik peuhpeuh adingin kihong hi.

records.english: My parents let me invite one friend to stay for every school holiday.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in sang khawlna simin lawm khat om sak dingin hong phal uh hi.

records.english: Where did your family put up guests who came from far away?
records.zomi: Gamla pan a hong khualte na innkuan in koi ah a om sak uh hiam?

records.english: Please don't invite the whole street this time, because we have only six chairs.
records.zomi: Tutna guk bek i neih manin tu-in lampi bup sam kei in.

records.english: How many people came to your sister's naming ceremony?
records.zomi: Na sanggam nu' min phuahna pawi ah mi bangzah a hong uh hiam?

records.english: For my eighth birthday, I secretly invited my whole class without telling my parents.
records.zomi: Ka pianni giatna ah ka nu leh ka pa' theih loh-in ka sang inndei bup ka sam hi.

records.english: When my mother found out the night before, she cooked until three in the morning.
records.zomi: A zan ma-in ka nu in a theih ciangin zingsang nai thum dong an a huan hi.

records.english: Twenty-six children came, and she never once let them see how tired she was.
records.zomi: Naupang sawm nih leh guk a hong uh a, a ol dan khatvei zong a lak ngei kei hi.

records.english: We sent a boy ahead to tell the guests that the road was blocked.
records.zomi: Lampi kitan hi, ci-in khualte kiangah gen dingin tangval khat a ma-in i sawl hi.

records.english: The tables were carried down from the church and set out under the mango trees.
records.zomi: Dawhkan te pawlpi pan kipuak a, haigah kung nuai ah kikoih hi.

records.english: Do you remember the guest who arrived a week early for the anniversary dinner?
records.zomi: Kiteenna kum tawpna nitak an adingin kal khat ma-in a tung khual na phawk hiam?

records.english: We fed him anyway, and he came back the following week as well.
records.zomi: Bang hi zongin an i pia a, a zom kal zong a hong kik hi.

records.english: An invitation to the chief's house was a great honor in our village.
records.zomi: I khua ah khua hausa' inn ah kisam pen thupi mahmah ahi hi.

records.english: However many guests arrived, my mother always found room for one more at the table.
records.zomi: Khual bangzah a tung zongin ka nu in dawhkan ah mi khat adingin mun a mu tawntung hi.

records.english: The guests brought so many dishes that our own cooking was hardly touched.
records.zomi: Khualte in an tampi a tawi uh ahih manin i huan an te a kikhoih zo kei hi.

records.english: If my father hadn't invited the stranded musician home, we would never have heard those songs.
records.zomi: Ka pa in a kikhak la sa pa inn ah a sam kei le tua la te i za ngei lo ding hi.

records.english: Did anyone ever refuse an invitation to your father's table?
records.zomi: Na pa' dawhkan ah samna kuamah in a nial ngei hiam?

records.english: We were told never to invite anyone in while our parents were at work.
records.zomi: I nu leh i pa nasepna ah a om laitakun kuamah sam lut lo dingin hong kigen hi.

records.english: Whether the guests were rich or poor, they were all served from the same pot.
records.zomi: Khualte a hau zongin a zawng zongin beel khat mah pan kipia hi.

records.english: My father once met a travelling musician who was stranded at the bus station.
records.zomi: Ka pa in khatvei bus dinna ah a kikhak khualzin la sa pa khat a kimu hi.

records.english: He brought him home for dinner without warning my mother.
records.zomi: Ka nu a hilh lo-in nitak an adingin inn ah a tawi hi.

records.english: After the meal, the musician played for us until midnight to thank her.
records.zomi: An nek khit ciangin la sa pa in ka nu lungdam a cih nadingin zan laitak dong la hong tum sak hi.

records.english: Who carried the wedding invitations to the villages up the valley?
records.zomi: Guam tung lam-a khuate ah mopawi samna te kua in a puak hiam?

records.english: My two cousins, who walked for three days and came back with blistered feet.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nih, ni thum sung a pai uh a, khe a mul tawh a hong kik uh pa.

records.english: The neighbor's daughter asked, "Am I invited too?", and my mother laughed and set another place.
records.zomi: Inn vengte' tanu in, “Kei zong hong sam uh hiam?” ci-in a dong a, ka nu a nui a, mun khat a koih behlap hi.

records.english: I invited the bus driver who had taken me to school for twelve years to my graduation.
records.zomi: Kum sawm leh nih sung sang ah hong tawi bus mawngpa ka laizo pawi ah ka sam hi.

records.english: Although our house was small, there was never a week without a visitor.
records.zomi: I inn a neu hangin khual om lo kal khat a om ngei kei hi.

records.english: To this day, I can't host a meal without cooking enough for an extra guest.
records.zomi: Tu ni dong khual khat behlap adingin a kicing an ka huan lo-in nitak an ka pia thei kei hi.

records.english: What I remember most about those dinners is the noise of twenty people talking at once.
records.zomi: Tua nitak an thu ah ka phawk pen pen mi sawm nih in khatvei-in thu a gen ging ahi hi.

records.english: My brother picked up the guests from the station in his old truck.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in a mawtaw lian lui tawh meileng dinna pan khualte a la hi.

records.english: I invited my best friend's mother as well, so that she wouldn't spend the festival alone.
records.zomi: Pawi sungin a kia lohna dingin ka lawm hoih pen' nu zong ka sam hi.

records.english: An old friend of my father's arrived for the wedding with a live chicken under his arm.
records.zomi: Ka pa' lawm lui khat in a zakbeng nuai ah ak hing khat tawh mopawi adingin a tung hi.

records.english: Inviting someone into your home, my father believed, was the best way to know them.
records.zomi: Mi khat na inn ah sam pen amah theihna lampi hoih pen ahi hi, ci-in ka pa in a um hi.

records.english: Would you mind addressing these envelopes while I finish the cake?
records.zomi: Cake ka zawh mateng hih lai-ip te tungah omna mun na gelh sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: It was only when I hosted my own first dinner that I understood how hard my parents had worked.
records.zomi: Keimah nitak an masa pen ka bawl ciang bek ka nu leh ka pa bangzah in a sem uh hiam ka thei hi.

records.english: What was the biggest party your family ever hosted?
records.zomi: Na innkuan in a bawl ngei pawi lian pen bang ahi hiam?

records.english: The first time we invited our teacher home, my sisters and I scrubbed the floor three times.
records.zomi: I saya inn ah i sam masak ciangin ka sanggam nute leh kei in inn phah thum vei i nul hi.

records.english: She stayed for only an hour, but our mother talked about the visit for months.
records.zomi: Nai khat bek a om a, ahi zongin i nu in a veh thu kha tampi sung a gen hi.

records.english: Which guest do you remember best from your childhood?
records.zomi: Na naupan lai-a khualte lakah kua na phawk pen hiam?

records.english: When my grandfather built his new house, there were no phones in the hills.
records.zomi: Ka pu in a inn thak a bawl ciangin mual tungah phone a om kei hi.

records.english: He sent me round every farm on my bicycle to invite people to help raise the roof.
records.zomi: Innkhum dawh huh dingin mite sam dingin siiksakol tawh lo inn khempeuh ah hong sawl hi.

records.english: On the day, forty neighbors turned up with tools, and the roof was finished by sunset.
records.zomi: Tua ni-in inn vengte sawm li in nasepna van tawh a hong uh a, ni tum ciangin innkhum a zo hi.

records.english: Please thank your mother for the bread; it was the best we've had in years.
records.zomi: Moh adingin na nu kiangah lungdam ka ci gen sak in; kum tampi sung i nek hoih pen ahi hi.

records.english: By the time I could afford a proper gift, the carpenter had already passed away.
records.zomi: Letsong hoih khat ka lei zawh ciangin sing bawlpa a si khin hi.

records.english: Is it true that you walked twenty miles to thank the doctor in person?
records.zomi: Siavuan kiangah lungdam ci dingin mile sawm nih na pai, cih a man hiam?

records.english: My brother's broken arm was set by a stranger on the bus, who turned out to be a nurse.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal' ban kitan pen bus tung-a a theih loh mi khat in a bawl dam a, nurse ahi hi.

records.english: After my accident, the village carpenter made me a pair of crutches.
records.zomi: Ka liamna khit ciangin khua-a sing bawlpa in tawnkol khat hong bawl sak hi.

records.english: He refused to take any money, so I saved my first month's wages to buy him a new saw.
records.zomi: Sum la a nuam kei ahih manin vuai thak khat lei dingin ka kha masa pen ka kikoih hi.

records.english: He kept that saw on the wall of his workshop and never once used it.
records.zomi: Tua vuai pen a nasepna inn bang ah a khai a, khatvei zong a zang ngei kei hi.

records.english: You might have saved my life that day, and I never even asked your name.
records.zomi: Tua ni-in ka nuntakna na hotkhia kha ding hi, ahi zongin na min zong ka dong ngei kei hi.

records.english: We planted a tree in the school yard to thank the family who gave the land.
records.zomi: Gam a pia innkuan lungdam ci nadingin sang huan ah singkung khat i suan hi.

records.english: Someone left a basket of eggs on our step with a note that said, "Thank you for the ladder."
records.zomi: Mi khat in i kongkhak ah aktui empeng khat a koih a, “Kahlei adingin lungdam hi,” ci laikhak khat a om hi.

records.english: On the morning of my final exam, the river was too high for the footbridge.
records.zomi: Ka sitna nunung zingsang-in tui a let lua ahih manin lei neu tungah kantan theih a hi kei hi.

records.english: An old ferryman rowed me across for nothing and told me to run.
records.zomi: Long khiatpa upa khat in a man lo-in hong kantan sak a, tai dingin hong hilh hi.

records.english: Years later, I went back with a new pair of oars, and he laughed until he cried.
records.zomi: Kum tampi khit ciangin long leh thak khat tawh ka ciah kik a, a kap dong a nui hi.

records.english: What touched me most was not the gift itself but that she had remembered my birthday.
records.zomi: Ka lungsim a khoih pen letsong hi lo-in ka pianni a phawk ahi hi.

records.english: The neighbor who looked after our goats while we were away was given a sack of rice.
records.zomi: I om lohna sungin i kel te a kem inn vengpa in buh ip khat kipia hi.

records.english: The school was painted by the parents to thank the teachers for staying through the hard year.
records.zomi: Kum haksa sung a om saya te lungdam ci nadingin nu leh pa te in sang a nul uh hi.

records.english: My little brother hugged the doctor so hard that her glasses fell off.
records.zomi: Ka nau pasal in siavuan a kawi lua ahih manin a mitlimlang a kia hi.

records.english: I wrote to the newspaper to thank the woman who had found my son wandering in the market.
records.zomi: Zuakna mun ah ka tapa a mangthang a muh numei lungdam ci nadingin laithak ah lai ka gelh hi.

records.english: I was so moved by her kindness that I couldn't speak.
records.zomi: A itna in ka lungsim a khoih lua ahih manin thu ka gen zo kei hi.

records.english: Did you ever find a way to thank the ferryman properly?
records.zomi: Long khiatpa hoih takin lungdam ci dan na mu ngei hiam?

records.english: Have you ever thanked someone years too late?
records.zomi: Kum tampi nunung lua-in mi khat kiangah lungdam na ci ngei hiam?

records.english: Yes, I finally wrote to my first piano teacher when she was ninety.
records.zomi: Ci ngei ing, ka piano saya masa pen kum sawm kua a phak ciangin a tawp-in lai ka khak hi.

records.english: Those thank-you letters from my students are among the few things I would save in a fire.
records.zomi: Ka sangnaupangte' lungdam laikhakte pen mei kang lai-in ka hotkhiat ding tawmno lakah kihel hi.

records.english: My uncle once said, "Gratitude that stays in your heart is no use to anyone."
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in khatvei, “Na lungsim sung bek-a om lungdamna kuamah adingin a phattuam kei hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: Where did you find the courage to thank him in front of everyone?
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh mai ah amah lungdam ci dingin hanna koi pan na ngah hiam?

records.english: When did you last write someone a letter of thanks?
records.zomi: Bang ciangin mi khat kiangah lungdam laikhak na gelh nunung hiam?

records.english: My mother let us stay up late on the night we made her a birthday card.
records.zomi: A pianni card i bawl zan in ka nu in khanglawh dingin hong phal hi.

records.english: Don't ever forget who helped you when you had nothing.
records.zomi: Bangmah na neih loh lai-in kua in hong huh hiam mangngilh ngei kei in.

records.english: The old ferryman's face lit up when he saw the new oars.
records.zomi: Long leh thak a muh ciangin long khiatpa upa' mai a vak hi.

records.english: What a kind thing it was for him to row me across without asking for a coin!
records.zomi: Dangka sik khat ngen lo-in hong kantan sak pen bangzah in lungsim hoih ahi hiam!

records.english: I still keep the note my neighbor left on my door after I helped her move.
records.zomi: Kitawn dingin ka huh khit ciangin ka inn vengnu in ka kongkhak ah a nusiat laikhak ka kem lai hi.

records.english: When we first arrived in the city, a stranger came to the office with us to interpret.
records.zomi: Khuapi i tun masak ciangin a theih loh mi khat in pau let dingin office ah hong zui hi.

records.english: We never learned her name, but my mother still mentions her in her prayers.
records.zomi: A min i thei ngei kei a, ahi zongin ka nu in a thungetna ah a gen lai hi.

records.english: In our house, we were not allowed to leave the table until we had thanked whoever had cooked.
records.zomi: I inn ah an a huan peuhpeuh lungdam i cih mateng dawhkan pan i ding thei kei hi.

records.english: How did people in your village show that they were grateful?
records.zomi: Na khua-a mite in a lungdamna uh bangci-in a lak uh hiam?

records.english: They usually brought food or offered a day of work in return.
records.zomi: A tamzaw-in an a tawi uh hiam, a thuk-in ni khat nasep a pia uh hi.

records.english: Gratitude, as my teacher used to say, is the only debt that grows when you pay it.
records.zomi: Lungdamna pen na piak ciangin a khang semsem leiba khat bek ahi hi, ci-in ka saya in a gen ngei hi.

records.english: My mother, who had grown up with very little, was grateful for the smallest kindness.
