records.zomi: Tawmno bek tawh a khang ka nu in itna neu pen adingin zong a lungdam hi.

records.english: Were you taught to thank the cook after every meal?
records.zomi: An nek simin an huanpa lungdam ci dingin hong kisin sak hiam?

records.english: Although the ferryman refused payment, he accepted a cup of tea every time I passed.
records.zomi: Long khiatpa in a man a nial hangin ka kantan simin tea haai khat a sang hi.

records.english: How did the old woman next door thank people?
records.zomi: A kiang inn-a numei upa in mite lungdam bangci-in a ci hiam?

records.english: She sang them a short song, whether they wanted one or not.
records.zomi: A deih uh hiam deih lo uh hiam la tom khat a sak sak hi.

records.english: Why did your father give the postman a chicken every New Year?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na pa in Kum Thak simin laikhak puakpa ak khat a pia hiam?

records.english: My father never said thank you out loud.
records.zomi: Ka pa in lungdam ci-in aw-in a gen ngei kei hi.

records.english: Instead, every Sunday he quietly mended whatever was broken on my bicycle.
records.zomi: Tua sangin Nipini simin ka siiksakol tung-a a sia peuhpeuh dai takin a bawl dam hi.

records.english: It took me years to understand that this was his way of showing he was proud of me.
records.zomi: Tua pen keimah tungah a kipahna lak dan ahi hi, cih theih dingin kum tampi hong sawt hi.

records.english: Remind me to send the carpenter's family a card this year.
records.zomi: Hih kum in sing bawlpa' innkuan kiangah card khak dingin hong phawksak in.

records.english: It was only when I became a father that I understood how much my own father had done without a word.
records.zomi: Pa ka hih ciang bek ka pa in kammal om lo-in bangzah a bawl hiam ka thei hi.

records.english: If the stranger hadn't come with us to the office, we might have been sent home.
records.zomi: Mi theih lohpa office ah hong zui kei le inn ah hong kiciahsak kha ding hi.

records.english: Would you help me choose a gift for the woman who taught me to sew?
records.zomi: Puan khui dan hong sin sak numei adingin letsong teel dingin hong huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: However poor we were, my parents always found something to give the people who had helped us.
records.zomi: Bangzah in i zawng zongin ka nu leh ka pa in hong huh mite piak ding bangmah khat a mu tawntung uh hi.

records.english: Did you ever thank the family who hosted you that summer?
records.zomi: Tua khal-a hong om sak innkuan kiangah lungdam na ci ngei hiam?

records.english: When I was ten, my sister and I cooked dinner for our parents to thank them for a holiday.
records.zomi: Kum sawm ka phak ciangin nopsakna khualzinna adingin lungdam ci nadingin ka sanggam nu leh kei in ka nu leh ka pa adingin nitak an i huan hi.

records.english: The rice was burnt, but they ate every grain and asked for more.
records.zomi: Buh a kang a, ahi zongin a tang khempeuh a ne uh a, behlap a ngen uh hi.

records.english: I didn't learn to read until I was forty.
records.zomi: Kum sawm li ka phak dong lai sim ka thei kei hi.

records.english: A retired clerk in our street taught me every evening for a year, using old newspapers.
records.zomi: I lampi-a nasep a khawl laigelhpa khat in laithak lui te zang-in kum khat sung nitak simin hong sin sak hi.

records.english: The first letter I ever wrote was to him, and it said only, "Thank you, teacher."
records.zomi: Ka gelh masak pen laikhak amah kiangah ahi a, “Saya, lungdam ing,” cih bek a om hi.

records.english: We still laugh about the day my father tried to thank the mayor and forgot his name.
records.zomi: Ka pa in khuapi makaipa lungdam ci dingin a sin a, a min a mangngilh ni thu i nuihsan lai hi.

records.english: I knitted a hat for the bus conductor so that his ears wouldn't freeze on the early route.
records.zomi: Bus sum lapa' bil zingsang lampi ah a khal lohna dingin lukhu khat ka phiat sak hi.

records.english: At the end of ploughing, my grandfather would pat each ox and say, "Well done, old friend."
records.zomi: Lo leh a zawh ciangin ka pu in bawngpi khempeuh a beng a, “Hoih mahmah, lawm lui,” a ci hi.

records.english: Eat some vegetables with every meal, even if it's only a few.
records.zomi: An nek simin tawmno bek hi zongin anteh ne un.

records.english: My grandfather says the secret to his good health is a short nap after lunch.
records.zomi: Ka pu in a cidamna thusim pen sun an khit ciang-a ihmut tom ahi hi, a ci hi.

records.english: She cooks with less salt now, for her husband's sake.
records.zomi: A pasal hangin tu-in cii tawm zaw tawh an a huan hi.

records.english: Do you find it easier to exercise in the morning or in the evening?
records.zomi: Zingsang ah hiam, nitak ah hiam, pumpi kisin na baih sak zaw hiam?

records.english: In the evening, because I'm too sleepy to do anything before work.
records.zomi: Nitak ah, banghangziam cih leh nasep ma-in bangmah bawl dingin ka ihmuh lua hi.

records.english: Don't skip lunch just because you're busy.
records.zomi: Na buai hang bek-in sun an nusia kei in.

records.english: Can I have some fruit instead of biscuits?
records.zomi: Biscuit sangin theigah ka ne thei ding hiam?

records.english: I always carry a water bottle in my bag.
records.zomi: Ka ip sungah tui bel khat ka tawi tawntung hi.

records.english: Do you walk to work or take the bus?
records.zomi: Nasepna ah na pai hiam, bus na tuang hiam?

records.english: I usually walk, unless it's raining hard.
records.zomi: Guah a zuk lua kei leh a tamzaw-in ka pai hi.

records.english: Turning off screens an hour before bed has helped me sleep better.
records.zomi: Ihmut ma nai khat-in screen te ka mut ciangin ka ihmut a hoih zaw hi.

records.english: Why do you go to bed so early?
records.zomi: Bang hangin ma lua-in na ihmu hiam?

records.english: My neighbor and I walk together in the mornings, so neither of us can give up.
records.zomi: Ka inn vengpa leh kei in zingsang simin khawm-in i pai ahih manin i nih khat zong i khawl thei kei hi.

records.english: Is it all right if I go for a run before breakfast?
records.zomi: Zingsang an ma-in tai dingin ka pai thei ding hiam?

records.english: I drink a glass of water as soon as I wake up.
records.zomi: Ka thoh pah-in tui haai khat ka dawn hi.

records.english: My doctor told me, "Small changes you can keep are better than big ones you can't."
records.zomi: Ka siavuan in, “Na kem theih kikhekna neute pen na kem theih loh lian te sangin a hoih zaw hi,” hong ci hi.

records.english: Could you open the window for some fresh air?
records.zomi: Huih siang adingin tukvuang na hong thei ding hiam?

records.english: If you drink more water during the day, you might not feel so tired in the afternoon.
records.zomi: Sun lai-in tui tam zaw na dawn leh nitak lam ciangin na ol lua kei kha ding hi.

records.english: Rather than forcing myself to run, I chose a sport I actually enjoy.
records.zomi: Tai dingin keimah kisawl sangin ka deih taktak kimawlna khat ka teel hi.

records.english: I packed some carrots for you to eat on the way.
records.zomi: Lampi ah na nek dingin carrot pawl khat kong koih sak hi.

records.english: My teenage daughter used to stay up until two in the morning on her phone.
records.zomi: Ka tanu khangno in a phone tawh zingsang nai nih dong a khanglawh ngei hi.

records.english: We agreed that she would leave it to charge in the kitchen at night.
records.zomi: Zanin an huanna ah charge dingin a koih ding hi, ci-in i kilem hi.

records.english: After a few weeks, she said she was waking up in a much better mood.
records.zomi: Kal pawl khat khit ciangin lungsim hoih zaw tawh ka thou hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Have you tried drinking your tea without sugar?
records.zomi: Na tea sugar om lo-in na dawn sin ngei hiam?

records.english: I eat breakfast every morning, even if it's just a banana.
records.zomi: Nahtang khat bek hi zongin zingsang simin zingsang an ka ne hi.

records.english: It is not one perfect day but many ordinary days that build a healthy routine.
records.zomi: Cidamna nuntak dan a lam pen ni hoih khat hi lo-in ni tavuan tampi ahi hi.

records.english: Shall we take the stairs instead of the lift?
records.zomi: Lift sangin kahlei tawh i kai ding hiam?

records.english: My aunt's habit of writing down what she eats has made her far more aware of her meals.
records.zomi: Ka ni' a nek te gelh ngeina in a an nekna a theih zaw sak mahmah hi.

records.english: Wash your hands before you eat.
records.zomi: Na nek ma-in na khut sil in.

records.english: Please don't eat in front of the television every night.
records.zomi: Zan simin television mai ah an ne kei un.

records.english: You're welcome to use the gym at work, but you have to book a time.
records.zomi: Nasepna-a gym na zang thei hi, ahi zongin hun na kilai khol ding a kisam hi.

records.english: After dinner, the whole family goes for a short walk.
records.zomi: Nitak an khit ciangin innkuan bup in tawmno a pai uh hi.

records.english: How many hours do you usually sleep?
records.zomi: A tamzaw-in nai bangzah na ihmu hiam?

records.english: About seven, but I'd like to get more.
records.zomi: Nai sagih bang, ahi zongin tam zaw ihmut ka deih hi.

records.english: Although I know sugar isn't good for me, I find it very hard to give up.
records.zomi: Sugar in ka cidamna adingin a hoih kei hi, cih ka theih hangin khawl dingin ka haksa sa mahmah hi.

records.english: Building a new habit, I've found, is mostly a matter of making it easy to start.
records.zomi: Ngeina thak bawl pen a kipat a baih nadingin bawl ahi hi, cih ka mu hi.

records.english: However busy the day, I try to sit down for at least one meal with my family.
records.zomi: Ni bangzah in buai zongin ka innkuan tawh an khat bek hi zongin tu khawm dingin ka hanciam hi.

records.english: Last month, I decided to walk for twenty minutes every day.
records.zomi: Kha nung in ni simin minit sawm nih pai dingin ka thukhen hi.

records.english: For the first week, I made excuses almost every evening.
records.zomi: Kal masa sungin nitak simin kik dekin ka kilawm sak hi.

records.english: Now my dog waits by the door at six o'clock, so I can't forget even if I want to.
records.zomi: Tu-in ka ui in nai guk ciangin kongkhak kiang ah a ngak ahih manin ka deih hangin ka mangngilh thei kei hi.

records.english: Smoking isn't allowed anywhere on the hospital grounds.
records.zomi: Siavuan inn gam sung koi peuh ah meikhu dawn kiphal lo hi.

records.english: I bought my mother a pair of good walking shoes so that she could join the walking group.
records.zomi: Ka nu pai pawl ah a kihel theih nadingin pai ding khedap hoih khat ka lei sak hi.

records.english: My office job had me sitting at a desk for eight hours a day.
records.zomi: Ka office nasep in ni khat nai giat dawhkan kiang ah hong tusak hi.

records.english: So I set a reminder on my phone to stand up and stretch every hour.
records.zomi: Tua ahih manin nai khat simin ding-in kizai dingin ka phone ah hong phawksak ding ka koih hi.

records.english: My back stopped aching, and now half the office stretches with me.
records.zomi: Ka nung a na khawl a, tu-in office a kim in hong kizai khawm hi.

records.english: What do you do when you feel stressed at work?
records.zomi: Nasepna ah na lungsim a buai ciangin bang na bawl hiam?

records.english: Our children are allowed sweets only on Saturdays.
records.zomi: I ta te in Kiginni ni bek thei khum a ne thei uh hi.

records.english: Whatever the weather, my grandfather goes out for his morning walk.
records.zomi: Huihkhua bang ahi zongin ka pu in zingsang pai dingin a pusuak hi.

records.english: Phones stay in the kitchen after nine o'clock in our house.
records.zomi: I inn ah nai kua khit ciangin phone te an huanna ah a om hi.

records.english: What makes the biggest difference for me is getting outside in daylight every morning.
records.zomi: Keimah adingin a kilamdanna lian pen zingsang simin ni vak sungah pusuak ahi hi.

records.english: You may watch one cartoon after you've finished your homework.
records.zomi: Na innlai na zawh khit ciangin cartoon khat na en thei hi.

records.english: I cut up fruit for the children every evening so that they can take it to school.
records.zomi: Naupangte in sang ah a tawi theih nadingun nitak simin theigah ka at hi.

records.english: Healthy habits are easier to keep when the whole family shares them.
records.zomi: Innkuan bup in a zui khawm uh ciangin cidamna ngeina te kem a baih zaw hi.

records.english: My grandfather does his exercises in the yard every morning at six.
records.zomi: Ka pu in zingsang simin nai guk ciangin huan sungah pumpi a kisin hi.

records.english: Would it help if we cooked our meals for the week on Sunday?
records.zomi: Nipini ni-in kal khat sung an i huan khol leh a huh ding hiam?

records.english: Eating slowly gives you time to notice when you're full.
records.zomi: Dai takin an nek in na vah ciangin theih nading hun hong pia hi.

records.english: My son brushes his teeth twice a day without being reminded.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in hong phawksak kei zongin ni khat nih vei a ha a sil hi.

records.english: The more regularly I sleep, the less I seem to need coffee.
records.zomi: Hun takin ka ihmut semsem ciangin coffee ka kisam tawm semsem bang hi.

records.english: My wife reminded me to drink more water, so I put a jug on my desk.
records.zomi: Ka zi in tui tam zaw dawn dingin hong phawksak ahih manin ka dawhkan tungah tui um khat ka koih hi.

records.english: If I hadn't started walking to work, I would never have discovered the park by the river.
records.zomi: Nasepna ah ka pai kipan kei le gun kiang-a huanpi ka mu ngei lo ding hi.

records.english: My mother told us, "Don't ever go to bed angry with your brother."
records.zomi: Ka nu in, “Na sanggam pasal tawh heh-in ihmu ngei kei un,” hong ci hi.

records.english: The old man's fence was mended by the boys who had broken it.
records.zomi: Pu upa' huang pen a susia tangvalte in a bawl dam uh hi.

records.english: Whether or not she forgave me, I knew that I had to tell her the truth.
records.zomi: Hong maisak hiam hong maisak lo hiam, a kiangah thu man ka gen ding hi, cih ka thei hi.

records.english: Would you have forgiven me if I had never told you?
records.zomi: Hong hilh ngei lo ka hih leh hong maisak ding hiam?

records.english: Why did you wait twenty years to tell the old man about the mangoes?
records.zomi: Bang hangin haigah thu pu upa kiangah gen dingin kum sawm nih na ngak hiam?

records.english: Did you ever apologize to your brother for breaking his kite?
records.zomi: Na sanggam pasal' leng-ngam na susiat ahih manin amah kiangah maisak na ngen ngei hiam?

records.english: Why did Mai give her neighbor all her marbles?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Mai in a inn vengpa a kawlsi khempeuh a pia hiam?

records.english: She wanted to say sorry for losing his football in the river.
records.zomi: A football gun sungah a mansuah ahih manin maisak ngen a deih hi.

records.english: My father had never once said sorry to me.
records.zomi: Ka pa in khatvei zong kei kiangah maisak a ngen ngei kei hi.

records.english: On my thirtieth birthday, he took me aside and apologized for being so hard on me as a boy.
records.zomi: Ka pianni sawm thumna ah a tuamin hong pi a, tangval ka hih lai-in a khauh lua ahih manin maisak a ngen hi.

records.english: I didn't know what to say, so I just held his hand.
records.zomi: Bang gen ding hiam ka thei kei ahih manin a khut bek ka len hi.

records.english: What did your grandfather say when you confessed?
records.zomi: Na mawhna na pulak ciangin na pu in bang a ci hiam?

records.english: I was so ashamed that I couldn't look my mother in the eye for days.
records.zomi: Ka maizum lua ahih manin ni tampi sung ka nu' mit ka en zo kei hi.

records.english: I said, "I'm sorry, Grandpa," and he pretended not to hear until I said it louder.
records.zomi: “Pu, maisak ngen ing,” ka ci a, a ging zaw-in ka gen mateng a za lo bangin a om hi.

records.english: I really did mean every word of that apology.
records.zomi: Tua maisak ngenna-a kammal khempeuh ka lungsim takpi tawh ka gen hi.

records.english: My grandfather's face softened the moment I admitted what I had done.
records.zomi: Ka bawl ka pulak pah ciangin ka pu' mai a nem hi.

records.english: He accepted my apology with a nod, as if nothing more needed to be said.
records.zomi: Gen behlap ding om nawn lo bangin a lu a ngawh-in ka maisak ngenna a sang hi.

records.english: Please call your brother tonight and make peace with him.
records.zomi: Tu zanin na sanggam pasal phone tawh sam inla, amah tawh kilem kik in.

records.english: Who taught you how to apologize properly?
records.zomi: Hoih takin maisak ngen dan kua in hong sin sak hiam?

records.english: I do want to say sorry to my old classmate, but I've lost touch with him.
records.zomi: Ka sang lawm lui kiangah maisak ngen ka deih taktak a, ahi zongin amah tawh i kikum nawn kei hi.

records.english: If my friend hadn't sat next to me on that bus, we might never have spoken again.
records.zomi: Ka lawm tua bus tungah ka kiang ah a tu kei le i kikum kik ngei lo kha ding hi.

records.english: My aunt never mentioned the broken vase again, which somehow made me feel even worse.
records.zomi: Ka ni in pak bel kek thu a gen kik ngei kei a, tua in ka lungsim hong nasak semsem hi.

records.english: Even now, I'm grateful that my father found the courage to apologize while there was still time.
records.zomi: Tu dong in hun a om lai-in ka pa in maisak ngen dingin hanna a ngah ahih manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: Were you punished when the teacher found out the truth?
records.zomi: Saya in thu man a theih ciangin na kigawt hiam?

records.english: No, but the boy who had copied my answers had to stay behind for a week.
records.zomi: Kigawt kei ing, ahi zongin ka dawnnate a gelh kik tangval in kal khat sung a om ding a kisam hi.

records.english: While my friend was abroad, I was supposed to feed his goldfish.
records.zomi: Ka lawm gamdang ah a om laitakin a nga neu te vak ding ka hi hi.

records.english: I forgot for a week, and when I remembered, it was floating at the top of the bowl.
records.zomi: Kal khat sung ka mangngilh a, ka phawk ciangin a bel tung lam ah a ngawng hi.

records.english: I bought a new one, but he noticed at once that it was a slightly different orange.
records.zomi: A thak khat ka lei a, ahi zongin a rong tawmno a kilamdang hi, cih a mu pah hi.

records.english: My brother's feelings were badly hurt when I laughed at his first poem.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal' la phuak masa pen ka nuihsan ciangin a lungsim a na mahmah hi.

records.english: Each day I put off the apology, the gap between us seemed to grow a little wider.
records.zomi: Maisak ngenna ka nawlkhin ni simin i kikal a gamla semsem bang hi.

records.english: Of all my apologies, the one that cost me most was also the one that mattered most.
records.zomi: Ka maisak ngennate lakah a haksa pen in a thupi pen zong ahi hi.

records.english: Please don't be too hard on him; he's been sorry about it all week.
records.zomi: A tungah na khauh lua kei in; kal bup sung a lungkham khin hi.

records.english: My oldest friend and I didn't speak for six years after a silly argument about money.
records.zomi: Ka lawm lui pen leh kei in sum thu-a kinialna neu khat khit ciangin kum guk sung i kikum kei hi.

records.english: We ended up on the same overnight bus by chance, and by morning we had forgiven each other.
records.zomi: Zan bus khat mah ah i tuang kha a, zingsang ciangin i kimaisak kik khin hi.

records.english: Can you believe it took us ten years to make up over a borrowed ladder?
records.zomi: Kahlei kicaih khat thu ah i kilem kik dingin kum sawm hong sawt hi, cih na um thei ding hiam?

records.english: When I was nine, I stole mangoes from an old man's tree every afternoon for a month.
records.zomi: Kum kua ka phak ciangin kha khat sung nitak simin pu upa khat' haigah kung pan haigah ka gu hi.

records.english: Twenty years later, I went back to his house to confess and pay for them.
records.zomi: Kum sawm nih khit ciangin pulak dingin leh a man piak dingin a inn ah ka ciah kik hi.

records.english: He laughed and said he had watched me from his window the whole time.
records.zomi: A nui a, a hun bup sung a tukvuang pan hong en hi, a ci hi.

records.english: My sister borrowed my best dress for a dance without asking.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu in hong dong lo-in lam pawi adingin ka puan hoih pen a caih hi.

records.english: She came home with a red wine stain right across the collar.
records.zomi: A ngawng puan tungah zu san mai tawh inn ah a ciah hi.

records.english: To make up for it, she sewed a new lace collar by hand, and the dress looked better than before.
records.zomi: Tua a sik nadingin khut tawh ngawng puan thak a khui a, puan pen a masa sangin a hoih zaw hi.

records.english: A note of apology was left in our letterbox by the driver who had dented our car.
records.zomi: I mawtaw a sukkhuk mawngpa in i laikhak koihna ah maisak ngenna lai khat a nusia hi.

records.english: How did your sister make up for spoiling your dress?
records.zomi: Na puan a susiat ahih manin na sanggam nu in bangci-in a sik hiam?

records.english: The whole argument was forgotten by the time the rice was ready.
records.zomi: Buh a min ciangin kinialna bup kimangngilh khin hi.

records.english: Did your friend ever forgive you for the goldfish?
records.zomi: Na lawm in nga neu thu-in hong maisak ngei hiam?

records.english: He did, but he still tells the story at every party.
records.zomi: Hong maisak hi, ahi zongin pawi khempeuh ah tua tangthu a gen lai hi.

records.english: In my family, any quarrel had to be settled before we sat down to the evening meal.
records.zomi: Ka innkuan ah kinialna khempeuh nitak an i nek ma-in kilem sak ding hi.

records.english: I had prepared a long speech, but in the end all I managed was a whispered sorry.
records.zomi: Thugen sau khat ka kiman sak a, ahi zongin a tawp-in maisak ngen ing, ci-in suk bek ka gen zo hi.

records.english: My cousin wrote, "I was wrong, and I miss you," on the back of an old photograph.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam in lim lui khat nung ah, “Ka khial a, kong lungngai hi,” ci-in a gelh hi.

records.english: Did your parents ever make you shake hands after a fight, even when you were still angry?
records.zomi: Na heh lai hangin kidona khit ciangin na nu leh na pa in khut kilen dingin hong sawl ngei uh hiam?

records.english: Was it hard to forgive your friend after so many years?
records.zomi: Kum tampi khit ciangin na lawm maisak a haksa hiam?

records.english: Realizing that I had blamed the wrong person, I went straight to her house to apologize.
records.zomi: Mi khial ka mawhsak hi, cih ka theih ciangin maisak ngen dingin a inn ah ka pai pah hi.

records.english: In my second year at school, a teacher accused me of copying my neighbor's answers.
records.zomi: Sang ka kah kum nihna ah saya khat in ka kiang mi' dawnnate ka gelh kik hi, ci-in hong mawhsak hi.

records.english: When she discovered that my neighbor had copied mine, she apologized to me in front of the head teacher.
records.zomi: Ka kiang mi in keimah' ka gelh kik hi, cih a theih ciangin sang makaipa mai ah kei kiangah maisak a ngen hi.

records.english: What hurt him was not the lie itself but how long I had kept it from him.
records.zomi: Amah a nasak pen zuau hi lo-in bangzah sawt ka sel hiam cih ahi hi.

records.english: Isn't it strange that forgiving my brother turned out to be easier than forgiving myself?
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal maisak pen keimah maisak sangin a baih zaw hi, cih lamdang hi lo hiam?

records.english: Who was the first to apologize after your parents' big argument?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa' kinialna lian khit ciangin kua in maisak a ngen masa hiam?

records.english: My mother, who simply put a cup of tea in front of my father and sat down beside him.
records.zomi: Ka nu, ka pa' mai ah tea haai khat a koih a, a kiang ah a tu pa.

records.english: Our puppy chewed the neighbor's shoes, which had been left outside her door to dry.
records.zomi: I ui neu in a keu nadingin inn vengnu' kongkhak pua ah a koih khedap te a se hi.

records.english: We bought her a new pair, and she gave the puppy one of the old ones to keep.
records.zomi: A thak khat i lei sak a, amah in ui neu kem dingin a lui khat a pia hi.

records.english: Some of our fiercest arguments turned into family jokes that we still tell today.
records.zomi: I kinialna lian pen pawl khat tu dong i gen lai innkuan nuihza thu suak hi.

records.english: One morning, my uncle's fishing net got tangled with the net from the next boat.
records.zomi: Zingsang khat in ka pa neu' nga len pen a kiang long-a len tawh a kisial hi.

records.english: He and the other fisherman shouted at each other for an hour about whose fish were whose.
records.zomi: Amah leh nga man dang khat in kua' nga ahi hiam ci-in nai khat sung a kiko uh hi.

records.english: In the end, they hauled both nets in together, shared the catch, and fished side by side for years.
records.zomi: A tawp-in len nih khawm-in a kai uh a, a man nga uh a hawm uh a, kum tampi sung kiang ah nga a man khawm uh hi.

records.english: My mother would say, "You two can argue as much as you like, but do it outside."
records.zomi: Ka nu in, “Na nih in na deih bangin kinial un, ahi zongin pua ah kinial un,” a ci ngei hi.

records.english: Who usually settled the arguments in your family?
records.zomi: Na innkuan ah kinialna te kua in a kilemsak hiam?

records.english: My aunt, who would make us sit on the same bench until we were both laughing.
records.zomi: Ka ni, i nih i nuih mateng tutphah khat mah ah hong tusak pa.

records.english: Once my sister apologized for the hurtful remark, the rest of the argument simply disappeared.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu in kammal nasak adingin maisak a ngen khit ciangin kinialna a dang khempeuh a mang hi.

records.english: The quarrel faded away so slowly that nobody noticed when it ended.
records.zomi: Kinialna dai takin a mang ahih manin bang ciangin a bei hiam kuamah in a thei kei uh hi.

records.english: I do want to understand why you were so angry that day.
records.zomi: Tua ni-in bang hangin na heh lua hiam theih ka deih taktak hi.

records.english: The old friendship was badly damaged by a few careless words.
records.zomi: Lawmta lui pen kidawm lo kammal tawmno in a susia mahmah hi.

records.english: Whatever we disagreed about, my brother and I always walked to school together the next day.
records.zomi: Bang thu-in i kilem kei zongin ka sanggam pasal leh kei in a zing ciangin sang ah khawm-in i pai tawntung hi.

records.english: Could you imagine arguing about chili for a whole afternoon?
records.zomi: Malcha thu-in nitak bup kinial ding na ngaihsun thei ding hiam?

records.english: The broken chair was quietly mended before my father came home.
records.zomi: Ka pa inn a tun ma-in tutna sia dai takin kibawl dam hi.

records.english: What did your brothers argue about most when you were young?
records.zomi: Na neu lai-in na sanggam pasalte in bang thu a kinial pen uh hiam?

records.english: It took me years to see that winning an argument and solving it are two different things.
records.zomi: Kinialna zawh leh tua thu bawl siang pen kibang lo nih ahi hi, cih theih dingin kum tampi hong sawt hi.

records.english: How long did the quarrel about the football goal go on?
records.zomi: Football gol thu-a kinialna bangzah sawt a om hiam?

records.english: At university, my flatmate complained every evening about the smell of my cooking.
records.zomi: Sangpi ah ka inn hawm pa in nitak simin ka an huan gim thu a phun hi.

records.english: I complained just as often about his loud music.
records.zomi: Kei zong a la ging thu kibang mah-in ka phun hi.

records.english: One night, I offered him a plate of my fish curry, and after that we cooked together and played his music while we ate.
records.zomi: Zan khat in ka nga curry kuang khat ka pia a, tua khit ciangin khawm-in an i huan a, i nek laitakin a la te i tum hi.

records.english: Would the stew have tasted better with less chili?
records.zomi: Malcha tawm zaw tawh an tui a lim zaw ding hiam?

records.english: Did you and your sister ever fight over clothes?
records.zomi: Nang leh na sanggam nu puan thu-in na kidou ngei uh hiam?

records.english: Our coach said, "You have five minutes to agree, or neither of you plays on Saturday."
records.zomi: I sin sakpa in, “Kilem dingin minit nga na nei uh hi, ahih kei leh Kiginni ni-in na nih in na kimawl kei ding uh hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: Were you ever asked to settle an argument between two friends?
records.zomi: Lawm nih kikal-a kinialna kilemsak dingin hong ngen ngei uh hiam?

records.english: No one was allowed to leave the meeting until the two sides had shaken hands.
records.zomi: Lam nih in khut a kilen mateng kikhopna pan kuamah pusuak dingin kiphal lo hi.

records.english: If the captains hadn't agreed to replay the penalty, the two villages might still be angry.
records.zomi: Makaipa te in penalty kap kik dingin a kilem kei uh leh khua nih a heh lai kha ding uh hi.

records.english: Our school band nearly broke up over which songs to play at the concert.
records.zomi: La pawi ah la bang sa ding hiam cih thu-in i sang la pawl a kikhen dek hi.

records.english: Our music teacher said, "Each of you chooses one, and nobody complains about anyone else's."
records.zomi: I la saya in, “Na khat ciat in khat teel un, leh kuamah in mi dang' teel thu phun kei un,” a ci hi.

records.english: How did the village decide on a name for the new school?
records.zomi: Khua in sang thak min bangci-in a thukhen hiam?

records.english: Nobody could agree, so each classroom was named after a different family who had given land.
records.zomi: Kuamah a kilem zo kei uh ahih manin sang inndei khempeuh gam a pia innkuan tuamtuam min tawh kiphuak hi.

records.english: Which of you broke the chair, and why was it mended in secret?
records.zomi: Na lak uh-ah kua in tutna a susia a, bang hangin a selin kibawl dam hiam?

records.english: At the harvest festival, the two cooks argued about how much chili to put in the stew.
records.zomi: Kaihawl pawi ah an huante nih in an tui ah malcha bangzah koih ding hiam ci-in a kinial uh hi.

records.english: Neither would give in, so the stew was divided into two pots.
records.zomi: Khat zong a ngawl kei uh ahih manin an tui pen beel nih-in kikhen hi.

records.english: By the end of the evening, the spicy pot was empty and the mild one was still half full.
records.zomi: Nitak a bei ciangin a hai beel a bei a, a hai lo beel a kim a dim lai hi.

records.english: My little brother's feelings were hurt because nobody listened to his side.
records.zomi: Kuamah in a thu a ngaih kei uh ahih manin ka nau pasal' lungsim a na hi.

records.english: Our neighbor's boat was returned to him with a hole in the side.
records.zomi: I inn vengpa' long pen a pang ah a kua tawh a kiciah kik hi.

records.english: Instead of arguing about who should pay, the two men spent a Saturday repairing it together.
records.zomi: Kua in a pia ding hiam ci-in kinial sangin mi nih in Kiginni ni khat khawm-in a bawl dam uh hi.

records.english: What made the two shopkeepers fall out?
records.zomi: Zuakna inn neipa nih bang hangin a kituah nawn kei uh hiam?

records.english: One of them painted his half of the shared sign blue without asking the other.
records.zomi: A khat in a kihawm min suang a khen a khat dong lo-in dum-in a nul hi.

records.english: What finally ended the quarrel was a joke that made both of them laugh.
records.zomi: A tawp-in kinialna a bei sak pen a nih in a nuihsan uh nuihza thu khat ahi hi.

records.english: We were told never to argue at the dinner table, whatever the reason.
records.zomi: Bang hang hi zongin an nekna dawhkan ah kinial ngei lo dingin hong kigen hi.

records.english: How did you and your husband decide to come home?
records.zomi: Nang leh na pasal in inn ah ciah kik dingin bangci-in na thukhen uh hiam?

records.english: My grandparents disagreed for fifty years about whether the milk goes in before the tea.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh ka pi in tea ma-in nawi koih ding hiam cih thu-in kum sawm nga sung a kilem kei uh hi.

records.english: Neither of them ever gave in, so they always made their own cups.
records.zomi: A nih in khat zong a ngawl ngei kei uh ahih manin amau' haai ciat a bawl tawntung uh hi.

records.english: In the village football final, nobody could agree whether the ball had crossed the line.
records.zomi: Khua football kidemna nunung ah bawl in gual a kantan hiam cih kuamah in a kilem zo kei uh hi.

records.english: The two captains argued until it was too dark to see.
records.zomi: Makaipa nih in en theih loh dong a mial mateng a kinial uh hi.

records.english: The next morning, both teams came back and the penalty was taken again in front of everyone.
records.zomi: A zing zingsang ciangin pawl nih a hong kik uh a, mi khempeuh mai ah penalty kikap kik hi.

records.english: Not wanting to upset my mother, I kept my opinion to myself until after dinner.
records.zomi: Ka nu ka lungsim nasak nuam lo ahih manin nitak an khit dong ka ngaihsutna ka sel hi.

records.english: My husband wanted to move abroad, and I wanted to stay near my parents.
records.zomi: Ka pasal in gamdang ah pai a deih a, kei in ka nu leh ka pa kiang ah om ka deih hi.

records.english: We agreed to try it for one year, and we came home after eleven months.
records.zomi: Kum khat sung sin dingin i kilem a, kha sawm leh khat khit ciangin inn ah i ciah kik hi.

records.english: Don't let the sun go down on your anger, my father always told us.
records.zomi: Na hehna uh ni na tumsak kei un, ci-in ka pa in hong hilh tawntung hi.

records.english: I really did try to stay out of my cousins' argument, but they both wanted me on their side.
records.zomi: Ka sanggamte' kinialna ah ka kihel lo dingin ka sin taktak a, ahi zongin a nih in amau' lam ah hong deih uh hi.

records.english: My father had a way of listening to both sides that made each of us feel heard.
records.zomi: Ka pa in lam nih a ngaih dan in i khat ciat in hong ngai hi, cih hong kisak sak hi.

records.english: Please, let's not have the same fight we had last year.
records.zomi: Kum nung-a i kidou bang kibang kidou kik kei ni.

records.english: A compromise about the water was finally written down and signed by both farmers.
records.zomi: Tui thu-a kilemna pen a tawp-in lo nei nih in a gelh uh a, a min uh a gelh uh hi.

records.english: Can we finally agree on what our childhood dog was called?
records.zomi: I naupan lai-a i ui min bang ahi hiam a tawp-in i kilem thei ding hiam?

records.english: We laughed about the tea argument at my grandparents' fiftieth anniversary.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh ka pi' kiteenna kum sawm nga tawpna ah tea kinialna thu i nuihsan hi.

records.english: Ask your grandmother about the tea argument, because she loves telling it.
records.zomi: Na pi in a gen nuam mahmah ahih manin tea kinialna thu na pi dong in.

records.english: The argument wasn't really about the boat at all; it was about years of small misunderstandings.
records.zomi: Kinialna pen long thu taktak hi lo-in kum tampi sung kithei khialhna neute thu ahi hi.

records.english: The argument was settled over a cup of tea at the corner shop.
records.zomi: Kinialna pen lampi kikona-a zuakna inn ah tea haai khat tawh kilemsak hi.

records.english: Where were you going when you met the tourist?
records.zomi: Khualzin gamdang mi na kimuh ciangin koi ah na pai hiam?

records.english: Would you recognize your grandfather's street if you went back today?
records.zomi: Tu-in na ciah kik leh na pu' lampi na thei kik lai ding hiam?

records.english: Our directions were written on a scrap of paper that blew out of the window.
records.zomi: I lampi lahna pen tukvuang pan huih in a mut khiat laidal neu khat tungah kigelh hi.

records.english: Some of my happiest memories began with a wrong turn.
records.zomi: Ka phawk nuam pen pawl khat lampi khial khat tawh a kipan hi.

records.english: When fog came down on the mountain, a shepherd boy led our group safely to the road.
records.zomi: Mual tungah meii a tuk ciangin tuu cing tangval khat in i pawl lampi ah bit takin hong pi hi.

records.english: He refused our money and asked for a pencil instead, because he wanted to draw.
records.zomi: Lim gelh a deih ahih manin i sum a nial a, khedal khat a ngen hi.

records.english: The path to the hot springs was marked with piles of stones by earlier travelers.
records.zomi: Tui lum zukna lampi pen a ma-a khualzinte in suang tawh a ciamteh uh hi.

records.english: How did the tourist thank you in the end?
records.zomi: A tawp-in khualzin gamdang mi in bangci-in lungdam hong ci hiam?

records.english: I really did think the station was on the other side of the river.
records.zomi: Meileng dinna gun gal lam ah a om hi, ci-in ka ngaihsun taktak hi.

records.english: I do want to visit that waterfall again, but I'm not sure I could find it.
records.zomi: Tua tui kia ka veh kik nuam taktak a, ahi zongin ka mu kik thei ding hiam ka thei kei hi.

records.english: Do you still have the map your pen friend drew?
records.zomi: Na laikhak lawm in a gelh map na nei lai hiam?

records.english: On a cycling trip, my friend and I took a wrong turn on a dirt road.
records.zomi: Siiksakol khualzinna khat ah ka lawm leh kei in lei lampi ah lampi khial i zui hi.

records.english: Instead of the next town, we found a waterfall that wasn't on any map.
records.zomi: A zom khuapi sangin map khatpeuh tungah om lo tui kia khat i mu hi.

records.english: I went back there many times, because the girl who sold us water that day later became my wife.
records.zomi: Tua ni-in tui hong zuak nungak in ka zi a suah nung ciangin tua mun ah tampi vei ka pai kik hi.

records.english: Could you point me toward the old market, please?
records.zomi: Zuakna mun lui lam hong lak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: How did your grandfather find his way home from the market at night?
records.zomi: Na pu in zanin zuakna mun pan inn ciahna lampi bangci-in a mu hiam?

records.english: He followed the stars, and he said the brightest one always stood above our valley.
records.zomi: Aksi te a zui a, a vak pen in i guam tung ah a ding tawntung hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Please write down the name of the hotel in case I need to show someone.
records.zomi: Mi khat ka lak ding a kisam leh zinbuuk min gelh sak in.

records.english: When did you last ask a stranger for directions?
records.zomi: Bang ciangin a theih loh mi khat kiangah lampi na dong nunung hiam?

records.english: Getting lost in a foreign city turned out to be the best part of the whole trip.
records.zomi: Gamdang khuapi ah lampi mangthang pen khualzinna bup ah a hoih pen ahi hi.

records.english: My parents argued about the route for an hour while I read every road sign aloud from the back seat.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in nai khat sung lampi thu a kinial uh a, kei in a nung tutna pan lampi min kigelh khempeuh ka sim hi.

records.english: My grandmother's neighbor always said, "If you're lost, look for the church tower and walk toward it."
records.zomi: Ka pi' inn vengnu in, “Na mangthang leh pawlpi inn sang en inla, tua lam ah pai in,” a ci ngei hi.

records.english: We followed a dog that seemed to know exactly where we were going.
records.zomi: Koi ah i pai hiam a thei taktak bang ui khat i zui hi.

records.english: Listen, everybody — if you get separated, wait by the statue and don't wander off.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh aw ngai un — na kikhen uh leh lim suang kiang ah ngak unla, koi mah ah pai kei un.

records.english: Stay close behind me, all of you, and step only where I step.
records.zomi: Na khempeuh un ka nung ah om unla, ka khe sutna bek ah sut un.

records.english: A woman at the bus stop said, "Don't go that way; take the road by the school instead."
records.zomi: Bus dinna-a numei khat in, “Tua lam ah pai kei un; sang kiang lampi zui un,” a ci hi.

records.english: My father trusted a stranger's directions more than any map he had ever owned.
records.zomi: Ka pa in a neih ngei map khempeuh sangin a theih loh mi' lampi lahna a muang zaw hi.

records.english: We had a good laugh when we realized we had walked in a complete circle.
records.zomi: Kim takin i kiheikik hi, cih i theih ciangin i nui mahmah hi.

records.english: The driver seemed so certain of the way that none of us dared to question him.
records.zomi: Mawngpa in lampi a thei taktak bang ahih manin i lak-ah kuamah in dot i ngam kei hi.

records.english: The old signpost had been knocked down, so we chose the road with fresher tire tracks.
records.zomi: Lampi lahna sing lui a puk ahih manin mawtaw khe kal thak zaw a om lampi i teel hi.

records.english: I was so relieved to see the lights of the village that I almost cried.
records.zomi: Khua' meivak te ka muh ciangin ka lungmuang lua ahih manin ka kap dek hi.

records.english: The poor taxi driver was sent round the same square three times by my confused aunt.
records.zomi: Taxi mawngpa in ka ni a lungbuai in mun kibang thum vei a kiheiksak hi.

records.english: Did you ever get completely lost when you were a child?
records.zomi: Na neu lai-in kim takin na mangthang ngei hiam?

records.english: Once, at the fair, until a woman lifted me onto a table so my mother could see me.
records.zomi: Khatvei, pawi ah, numei khat in ka nu' muh theih nadingin dawhkan tungah hong dawh mateng.

records.english: Asking the way taught me more about the city than any guidebook ever did.
records.zomi: Lampi dot in laibu khempeuh sangin khuapi thu tam zaw hong sin sak hi.

records.english: Mark the waterfall with a cross so that I can find it one day.
records.zomi: Ni khat ka muh theih nadingin tui kia pen kilhtehna tawh ciamteh in.

records.english: My pen friend sent me a hand-drawn map of her village before my first visit.
records.zomi: Ka veh masak ma-in ka laikhak lawm in a khua map khut tawh a gelh hong khak hi.

records.english: Every turning, every gate and even the crooked plum tree were exactly where she had drawn them.
records.zomi: Lampi kiheina khempeuh, kongpi khempeuh leh theipi kung kawi zong a gelh mun takpi ah a om uh hi.

records.english: If the shepherd boy hadn't found us, we might have spent the night on the mountain.
records.zomi: Tuu cing tangval in hong mu kei le mual tungah zan i lum kha ding hi.

records.english: Was the shepherd boy's village far from the road?
records.zomi: Tuu cing tangval' khua lampi pan gamla hiam?

records.english: What surprised me was how many strangers were willing to stop and help.
records.zomi: Ka lamdang sak pen a theih loh mi bangzah in a khawl-in huh a nuam uh hiam cih ahi hi.

records.english: In my grandfather's town, people gave directions by smell.
records.zomi: Ka pu' khuapi ah mite in gim tawh lampi a lak uh hi.

records.english: "Walk past the bakery, turn away from the tannery, and stop when you can smell the fish," he told me.
records.zomi: “Moh bawlna kantan inla, savun bawlna pan pial inla, nga gim na zak ciangin khawl in,” hong ci hi.

records.english: It sounded like a joke, but I found the harbor without asking anyone else.
records.zomi: Nuihza thu bang hi, ahi zongin kuamah ka dong lo-in long dinna ka mu hi.

records.english: Instead of giving us directions, the old man got on his bicycle and led us there himself.
records.zomi: Lampi hong lak sangin pu upa in a siiksakol a tuang a, amah mah in hong pi hi.

records.english: Whichever road we took, we always seemed to end up at the same tea shop.
records.zomi: Lampi bang i zui zongin tea zuakna inn kibang mah ah i tung tawntung bang hi.

records.english: My cousin's sandals were ruined by the muddy shortcut a farmer had suggested.
records.zomi: Lo nei khat in a gen lampi tom buan in ka sanggam' khedap neu te a susia hi.

records.english: How did travelers find their way before there were road signs?
records.zomi: Lampi lahna a om ma-in khualzinte in lampi bangci-in a mu uh hiam?

records.english: It took us three hours to find a house that was ten minutes from the station.
records.zomi: Meileng dinna pan minit sawm bek gamla inn khat zong dingin nai thum hong sawt hi.

records.english: Who taught you to read a map?
records.zomi: Map sim dan kua in hong sin sak hiam?

records.english: My father, who made me guide him through the city on my eleventh birthday.
records.zomi: Ka pa, ka pianni sawm leh khatna ah khuapi sung lampi pi dingin hong sawl pa.

records.english: What did the police officer say to you at the station?
records.zomi: Meileng dinna ah palik in bang hong ci hiam?

records.english: A tourist once stopped me in the street and asked for the museum using only gestures.
records.zomi: Khualzin gamdang mi khat in khatvei lampi tungah hong khawlsak a, a khut bek tawh museum a dong hi.

records.english: It was easier to walk him there than to explain, so I did.
records.zomi: Gen siang sangin pi a baih zaw ahih manin ka pi hi.

records.english: By the time we arrived, we had become friends, and he insisted on buying me tea.
records.zomi: I tun ciangin lawm i suak khin a, tea hong lei sak dingin a ngen tawntung hi.

records.english: Which route did your family take to the coast every summer?
records.zomi: Khal simin na innkuan in tuipi gei ah lampi bang a zui uh hiam?

records.english: At sixteen, I went to the capital on my own for the first time.
records.zomi: Kum sawm leh guk ka phak ciangin keimah bek in gam khuapi ah ka pai masa hi.

records.english: I came out of the station and had no idea which way to turn.
records.zomi: Meileng dinna pan ka pusuak a, lam bang ah pial ding hiam ka thei kei hi.

records.english: A police officer saw my face, asked where I was going, and walked me all the way to the right bus.
records.zomi: Palik khat in ka mai a mu a, koi ah na pai hiam hong dong a, bus dik dong hong pi hi.

records.english: A new bridge was built the year after we got lost, so the long detour disappeared.
records.zomi: Lampi i mangthang kum zom in lei thak kibawl ahih manin lampi sau a mang hi.

records.english: The old bridge was closed to trucks after a crack was found in it.
records.zomi: Lei lui ah kekna a kimuh khit ciangin mawtaw lian te a tuang dingin kikhak hi.

records.english: On my third lesson, I drove straight into a hedge.
records.zomi: Ka sinna thumna ah huang singkung ah ka mawng lut hi.

records.english: My instructor didn't even raise his voice; he just said, "Reverse, please."
records.zomi: Ka sin sakpa in a aw zong a dawh kei a, “Nung lam ah kik in,” a ci bek hi.

records.english: By evening, half the village had heard that I had passed my test.
records.zomi: Nitak ciangin khua a kim in ka sitna ka zo hi, cih a za uh hi.

records.english: Our neighbor's fence was knocked over by a learner driver who panicked.
records.zomi: I inn vengpa' huang mawtaw mawng sin pa khat a lau ciangin a sukpuk hi.

records.english: A whole bus of passengers was delayed when a cow sat down at the crossroads.
records.zomi: Lampi kikona ah bawng khat a tut ciangin bus tung-a khualzin khempeuh a nunsak hi.

records.english: Our car was towed home by a tractor with a long rope.
records.zomi: I mawtaw pen khau sau tawh tractor in inn ah a kai hi.

records.english: An ox cart slowly overtook our car while my uncle was trying to fix the engine.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in engine a bawl dam laitakin bawng leng khat in i mawtaw a kantan hi.

records.english: Halfway through my driving test, the examiner's hat blew out of the open window.
records.zomi: Ka mawtaw mawng sitna laizang ah a sit pa' lukhu tukvuang hong pan huih in a mut khia hi.

records.english: I stopped the car, ran back down the road, and handed it to him.
records.zomi: Mawtaw ka khawlsak a, lampi ah ka tai kik a, ka pia hi.

records.english: He said nothing, but I passed, and I've always wondered whether the hat helped.
records.zomi: Amah in bangmah a gen kei a, ahi zongin ka zo a, lukhu in hong huh hiam ka ngaihsun den hi.

records.english: I really did think I'd failed when I stalled the car at the first junction.
records.zomi: Lampi kikona masa pen ah mawtaw ka sih sak ciangin ka sit hi, ci-in ka ngaihsun taktak hi.

records.english: Do you remember cleaning the windscreen with newspaper when the wipers broke?
records.zomi: Wiper a sia ciangin laithak tawh mawtaw ma-a khuangkhai i nul na phawk hiam?

records.english: What was the road to the city like in those days?
records.zomi: Tua hunte-in khuapi lampi bangci-in a om hiam?

records.english: My bicycle was flattened by a reversing truck, but luckily I wasn't on it.
records.zomi: Nung lam kik mawtaw lian khat in ka siiksakol a nensia a, ahi zongin ka tung kei hi.

records.english: The traffic in the capital seemed frightening after years of quiet country roads.
records.zomi: Kum tampi sung khua lampi daihte khit ciangin gam khuapi-a mawtaw tamna lauhuai bang hi.

records.english: When did the first bus come to your village?
records.zomi: Na khua ah bus masa pen bang ciangin a hong hiam?

records.english: The first time I drove alone, I talked to myself the whole way to calm my nerves.
records.zomi: Keimah bek-in ka mawng masak ciangin ka lungsim dai nadingin lampi bup ah keimah kiangah thu ka gen hi.

records.english: Why did your grandfather always drive in the middle of the road?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na pu in lampi laizang ah a mawng tawntung hiam?

records.english: What was the first car your family owned?
records.zomi: Na innkuan in a neih masak pen mawtaw bang ahi hiam?

records.english: When the first traffic light was put up in our town, people came just to watch it.
records.zomi: I khuapi ah mawtaw meivak masa pen a kikoih ciangin mite en dingin bek a hong uh hi.

records.english: Some of them stood on the corner for an hour, waiting for it to turn green again.
records.zomi: A pawl khat nai khat sung lampi kikona ah a ding uh a, a eng kik ding a ngak uh hi.

records.english: Drivers ignored it for months, until a police officer was sent to stand beside it.
records.zomi: Mawngpate in kha tampi sung a limsak kei uh a, a kiang ah ding dingin palik khat kisawl hi.

records.english: Were there any traffic lights in your town when you were young?
records.zomi: Na neu lai-in na khuapi ah mawtaw meivak a om hiam?

records.english: Not knowing how to drive, my aunt learned every bus timetable in the district by heart.
records.zomi: Mawtaw mawng a theih loh manin ka ni in gam sung-a bus hun khempeuh a lu sungah a kem hi.

records.english: Instead of honking, drivers in our village used to wave and wait for each other.
records.zomi: I khua-a mawngpate in ging sak sangin khut vai-in a kingak uh hi.

records.english: Out you get, all of you, and push!
records.zomi: Na khempeuh un pusuak unla, sawn un!

records.english: We pushed until we were covered in mud, and then he drove off and forgot to wait for us.
records.zomi: Buan in hong khuh mateng i sawn a, tua ciangin a mawng a, hong ngak dingin a mangngilh hi.

records.english: How did you get the car across the river before there was a bridge?
records.zomi: Lei a om ma-in gun ah mawtaw bangci-in na kantan sak uh hiam?

records.english: We rolled it onto a wooden raft, and four men pulled it across with ropes.
records.zomi: Sing pheipi tungah i let tou a, mi li in khau tawh a kai kantan uh hi.

records.english: Imagine a whole street waiting for a traffic light to change!
records.zomi: Mawtaw meivak kikhek ding lampi bup in a ngak ngaihsun in!

records.english: My father used a paper map and a pencil to plan every long journey.
records.zomi: Ka pa in khualzinna sau khempeuh geel nadingin laidal map leh khedal a zang hi.

records.english: Driving on those roads required more patience than skill.
records.zomi: Tua lampi te tungah mawtaw mawng pen siamna sangin thuakzawhna a kisam zaw hi.

records.english: My grandfather drove so slowly that cyclists used to overtake him and wave.
records.zomi: Ka pu in nawlkhin takin a mawng ahih manin siiksakol tuangte in a kantan uh a, khut a vai uh hi.

records.english: The day our first car arrived, the whole street came out to look at it.
records.zomi: I mawtaw masa pen a tun ni-in lampi bup in en dingin a pusuak uh hi.

records.english: The children touched the shiny paint, and the old men opened and closed the doors.
records.zomi: Naupangte in a tang rong a khoih uh a, pu upate in kongkhak te a hong uh a, a khak uh hi.

records.english: My father drove everyone round the block in turns until the fuel tank was nearly empty.
records.zomi: Sathau a bei dek mateng ka pa in mi khempeuh a khat ciat in a kiim ah a tawi kual hi.

records.english: One summer, a broken-down lorry blocked the highway, and nobody could move for four hours.
records.zomi: Khal khat in mawtaw lian sia khat in lampi lian a khak a, nai li sung kuamah a pai zo kei uh hi.

records.english: People got out of their cars, shared their food, and played cards on the warm road.
records.zomi: Mite a mawtaw uh pan a pusuak uh a, a an uh a kihawm uh a, lampi lum tungah card a kimawl uh hi.

records.english: When the traffic finally moved, I had three new phone numbers and half a bag of oranges.
records.zomi: Mawtaw te a tawp-in a pai ciangun phone nambat thak thum leh sangtam ip a kim ka nei khin hi.

records.english: The road into town was finally paved the year I started school.
records.zomi: Sang ka kah kipat kum in khuapi lut lampi a tawp-in kituh hi.

records.english: Have you ever been overtaken by an ox cart?
records.zomi: Bawng leng in hong kantan ngei hiam?

records.english: Who taught you to change a tire?
records.zomi: Mawtaw khe khek dan kua in hong sin sak hiam?

records.english: My aunt, with an old jack that she kept in the boot wrapped in a sack.
records.zomi: Ka ni, mawtaw nung bawm sungah ip tawh a tuam jack lui khat a kem pa.

records.english: Whatever the road was like, my mother insisted that we leave at dawn.
records.zomi: Lampi bangci-in om zongin ka nu in khuavak ciangin pai ding hi, a ci tawntung hi.

records.english: I do want to drive that mountain road again, but this time in daylight.
records.zomi: Tua mual lampi ah mawtaw mawng kik ka deih taktak a, ahi zongin tu-in sun lai-in.

records.english: Can you still start a car with a crank handle?
records.zomi: Mawtaw pen khut kheina sik tawh na kipat sak thei lai hiam?

records.english: Mind the potholes, because the springs in this car are older than you are!
records.zomi: Lampi kua te limtakin pelh un, hih mawtaw-a spring te nangma sangin a upa zaw hi!

records.english: Did you ever run out of fuel in the middle of nowhere?
records.zomi: Mi om lohna mun ah sathau na bei ngei hiam?

records.english: Twice, and both times a farmer sold us a bottle of fuel from his shed.
records.zomi: Nih vei, leh a nih vei in lo nei khat in a van koihna inn pan sathau bel khat hong zuak hi.

records.english: Did I ever tell you about the lift we got in a truck full of chickens?
records.zomi: Ak tawh a dim mawtaw lian khat tungah i tuang thu kong gen ngei hiam?

records.english: Which road did your father refuse to drive on at night?
records.zomi: Na pa in lampi bang ah zanin mawng a nial hiam?

records.english: Please don't tell your mother I let you drive the car down the lane.
records.zomi: Lampi neu ah mawtaw mawng dingin kong phal hi, cih na nu kiangah gen kei in.

records.english: On cold mornings, our old car could only be started with a metal crank handle at the front.
records.zomi: Zingsang vot te-in i mawtaw lui pen a ma lam-a sik khut kheina tawh bek kipat sak thei hi.

records.english: My mother turned it while my father pressed the pedal, and the whole street could hear the engine cough.
records.zomi: Ka pa in a khe tawh a nen laitakin ka nu in a hei a, lampi bup in engine a khuh ging a za uh hi.

records.english: The front of our car was dented when a branch fell on it in a storm.
records.zomi: Huihpi lai-in singkung bawng khat a kiat ciangin i mawtaw ma lam a khuk hi.

records.english: Once the highway was built, the journey that had taken a whole day took only three hours.
records.zomi: Lampi lian a kibawl khit ciangin ni khat bup a sawt khualzinna nai thum bek a sawt hi.

records.english: If the farmer hadn't sold us that fuel, we would have slept in the car.
records.zomi: Lo neipa in tua sathau hong zuak kei le mawtaw sungah i ihmu ding hi.

records.english: Late one night, a herd of buffalo stood in the middle of the road and refused to move.
records.zomi: Zan khat in lui tampi lampi laizang ah a ding uh a, pai a nuam kei uh hi.

records.english: What I remember most about our family trips is my father humming the same song for hours.
records.zomi: I innkuan khualzinna thu ah ka phawk pen pen ka pa in nai tampi sung la kibang a hum ahi hi.

records.english: I translated the forms for my parents so that they could apply together.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in khawm-in a ngen theih nadingun lai te ka let sak hi.

records.english: Our teacher explained that being a citizen means having both rights and responsibilities.
records.zomi: Gam mi hihna pen thuneihna leh mawhpuakna nei ahi hi, ci-in i saya in a gen siang hi.

records.english: My neighbor volunteers at the library to help newcomers prepare for the test.
records.zomi: Ka inn vengpa in hong thak mite sitna adingin a kiman nadingun laibu inn ah thalawp-in a sem hi.

records.english: Don't forget to sign the back of your new passport.
records.zomi: Na passport thak nung lam ah na min gelh dingin mangngilh kei in.

records.english: Young people in our town are encouraged to register to vote as soon as they turn eighteen.
records.zomi: I khuapi-a khangnote kum sawm leh giat a phak pah uh ciangin teelna ah a min uh lut sak dingin kihanthawn hi.

records.english: When I applied for citizenship, one of my documents was lost by the office.
records.zomi: Gam mi hihna ka ngen ciangin office in ka lai khat a mansuah hi.

records.english: I had to send another copy and wait three more months.
records.zomi: A dang khat ka khak a, kha thum behlap ka ngak hi.

records.english: When the letter finally arrived, my whole family celebrated with a big dinner.
records.zomi: Lai a tun ciangin ka innkuan bup in nitak an lian tawh i lungdam hi.

records.english: Would it help if I came with you to the interview?
records.zomi: Kidotna ah kong zui leh a huh ding hiam?

records.english: Please don't sign the form until you've read every page carefully.
records.zomi: Lai phek khempeuh limtakin na sim ma-in na min gelh kei in.

records.english: Could you help me fill in this form?
records.zomi: Hih lai gelh dingin hong huh thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: What should I do if I lose my ID card?
records.zomi: Ka ID card ka mansuah leh bang ka bawl ding hiam?

records.english: We joined the neighborhood clean-up to do something useful for the place we now call home.
records.zomi: Tu-in i inn ci mun adingin bangmah phattuam bawl nadingin inn vengte sianseh nasep ah i kihel hi.

records.english: The citizenship office is closed on public holidays, so check before you go.
records.zomi: Gam mi hihna office pen gam pawi ni te-in kikhak ahih manin na pai ma-in en masa in.

records.english: Is your brother a citizen too?
records.zomi: Na sanggam pasal zong gam mi ahi hiam?

records.english: Can I vote in the next election?
records.zomi: A zom teelna ah ka teel thei ding hiam?

records.english: Holding citizenship in two places can make travel easier but paperwork more complicated.
records.zomi: Gam nih ah gam mi hihna neih in khualzinna a baih sak a, ahi zongin lai thu a haksa sak hi.

records.english: People who are waiting for citizenship aren't allowed to vote yet, according to the officer we spoke to.
records.zomi: I kikum office mi in, gam mi hihna a ngak mite in tu-in teelna ah a teel thei nai kei uh hi, a ci hi.

records.english: My uncle still keeps his old citizenship certificate in a frame above the television.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in a gam mi hihna lai-ciam lui television tung lam ah kilh-in a kem lai hi.

records.english: Taking part in local decisions is, in my view, the most practical way to be a good citizen.
records.zomi: Ka ngaihsutna-in khua thukhenna ah kihel pen gam mi hoih hih nading lampi hoih pen ahi hi.

records.english: However long the process takes, keep copies of every letter you send and receive.
records.zomi: A sawt bangzah zongin na khak leh na ngah lai khempeuh a kawpi kem in.

records.english: What moved me most at the ceremony was hearing so many accents say the same promise.
records.zomi: Poai ah ka lungsim a khoih pen pau ging tuamtuam tampi in ciamna kibang mah a gen uh na za ahi hi.

records.english: You can't use a photo with sunglasses.
records.zomi: Mit-om khuh lim tawh na zang thei kei hi.

records.english: In the country where I live now, every new citizen gets a small booklet about local government.
records.zomi: Tu-a ka omna gam ah gam mi thak khempeuh in khua uk dan thu laibu neu khat a ngah uh hi.

records.english: Do you have a passport?
records.zomi: Passport na nei hiam?

records.english: Not yet, but my application was sent last week.
records.zomi: Nei nai kei ing, ahi zongin ka ngetna kal nung in kikhak khin hi.

records.english: What do you need to become a citizen here?
records.zomi: Hih gam ah gam mi suah dingin bang na kisam hiam?

records.english: Citizens in our town can visit the council meetings.
records.zomi: I khuapi-a gam mite in khua upa kikhopna a veh thei uh hi.

records.english: The judge said, "Welcome, and thank you for choosing to be part of this community."
records.zomi: Thukhenpa in, “Kong muak hi, leh hih khua-a kihel dingin na teel manin lungdam ing,” a ci hi.

records.english: By helping new arrivals with their forms, my mother has become a kind of unofficial guide at the town hall.
records.zomi: Hong thak mite' lai gelh a huh manin ka nu pen khuapi office ah lampi lakpa bang a suak hi.

records.english: My card was sent to me by post.
records.zomi: Ka card laikhak tawh hong kikhak hi.

records.english: I'm studying for the citizenship test.
records.zomi: Gam mi hihna sitna adingin ka sin hi.

records.english: I was called to serve on a jury for the first time last month.
records.zomi: Kha nung in thukhenna jury ah sem dingin a masa pen-in hong kisam hi.

records.english: Rather than seeing it as the end of a long process, I see my citizenship as a beginning.
records.zomi: Hun sawt nasep tawpna bangin et sangin ka gam mi hihna pen kipatna bangin ka en hi.

records.english: My parents are very proud of their new passports.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in a passport thak uh a kipak mahmah uh hi.

records.english: Is it possible to keep my old nationality if I become a citizen here?
records.zomi: Hih gam ah gam mi ka suah leh ka gam lui mi hihna ka kem thei lai ding hiam?

records.english: Where do I apply for a national ID card?
records.zomi: Gam ID card koi ah ka ngen ding hiam?

records.english: At the town hall, on the second floor.
records.zomi: Khuapi office ah, a tung dawl nihna ah.

records.english: My daughter was born here, so she is a citizen.
records.zomi: Ka tanu hih gam ah a suak ahih manin gam mi ahi hi.

records.english: Becoming a citizen of a new country can bring mixed feelings, especially for older people.
records.zomi: Gam thak khat-a gam mi suah in a lungsim kibang lo tampi a tun thei a, mi upate adingin a tuamin ahi hi.

records.english: Getting my passport meant I could finally visit my relatives abroad.
records.zomi: Ka passport ka ngah ciangin gamdang-a ka sanggamte a tawp-in ka veh thei hi.

records.english: If my parents hadn't kept every document, my application would have taken years.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in lai khempeuh a kem kei uh le ka ngetna kum tampi a sawt ding hi.

records.english: My son asked me why some of his classmates have two passports.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in bang hangin a sang lawm pawl khat in passport nih a nei uh hiam hong dong hi.

records.english: How long have you lived in this country?
records.zomi: Hih gam ah bangzah sawt na om khin hiam?

records.english: Almost twelve years, and I feel at home here now.
records.zomi: Kum sawm leh nih bang, leh tu-in ka inn bangin ka kisa hi.

records.english: Please bring two photos and your birth certificate.
records.zomi: Lim nih leh na pianna lai hong tawi in.

records.english: May I bring my children to the ceremony?
records.zomi: Poai ah ka ta te ka tawi thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, and your whole family is welcome.
records.zomi: Tawi thei hi, leh na innkuan bup kimuak hi.

records.english: It took me years to understand that belonging to a place is something you build, not something you are given.
records.zomi: Mun khat ah kihelna pen kipia hi lo-in na bawl ahi hi, cih theih dingin kum tampi hong sawt hi.

records.english: We registered our son's birth the week after he was born.
records.zomi: I tapa a suah khit kal in a pianna i gelh sak hi.

records.english: Whatever passport you hold, you can still care deeply about the country you came from.
records.zomi: Passport bang na nei zongin na hong suahna gam na it thei lai hi.

records.english: The more I learned about local government, the more I wanted to take part in it.
records.zomi: Khua uk dan ka sin semsem ciangin kihel ka deih semsem hi.

records.english: I became a citizen last year.
records.zomi: Kum nung in gam mi ka suak hi.

records.english: You might need to show proof of your address, so bring a recent bill.
records.zomi: Na omna lahna na lak ding a kisam kha ding ahih manin tu-a laimal khat tawi in.

records.english: How did you feel when you first voted as a citizen?
records.zomi: Gam mi-in na teel masak ciangin bangci-in na kisa hiam?

records.english: Nervous, but also very proud, as if my voice finally counted.
records.zomi: Ka lau a, ahi zongin ka aw a tawp-in a kisim bangin ka kipak mahmah hi.

records.english: Last spring, my grandmother finally became a citizen at the age of seventy-two.
records.zomi: Spring nung in ka pi kum sawm sagih leh nih a phak ciangin a tawp-in gam mi a suak hi.

records.english: She had studied for the test every evening with my little brother, who asked her the questions.
records.zomi: Ka nau pasal tawh nitak simin sitna adingin a sin a, ka nau pasal in thu dot te a dong hi.

records.english: At the ceremony, she wore her best dress and cried when they called her name.
records.zomi: Poai ah a puan hoih pen a silh a, a min a kikou ciangin a kap hi.

records.english: Citizenship is not only a document but also a sense of belonging.
records.zomi: Gam mi hihna pen lai bek hi lo-in kihelna lungsim zong ahi hi.

records.english: The rickshaw drivers knew every shortcut in the city, including several that didn't officially exist.
records.zomi: Rickshaw mawngte in khuapi sung-a lampi tom khempeuh a thei uh a, a pawl khat pen kiciamteh lo ahi hi.

records.english: Children, keep your heads inside the windows, or the soot will blacken your faces!
records.zomi: Naupangte, tukvuang sung ah na lu uh koih un, ahih kei leh meikhu vom in na mai uh a vom sak ding hi!

records.english: Have you ever taken a cable car?
records.zomi: Khau tung mawtaw na tuang ngei hiam?

records.english: Whatever the weather, the old bus to the hills left at exactly six every morning.
records.zomi: Huihkhua bang ahi zongin mual lam pai bus lui zingsang simin nai guk tak ciangin a pai hi.

records.english: Which was the longest journey you ever made by bus?
records.zomi: Bus tawh na khualzin ngei sau pen bang ahi hiam?

records.english: Instead of complaining about the delay, the passengers started a game of cards on the platform.
records.zomi: A nunna thu phun sangin khualzinte in dinna mun ah card kimawlna a kipat sak uh hi.

records.english: A whole basket of mangoes was spilled when the bus braked suddenly.
records.zomi: Bus a khawl thawlawh ciangin haigah empeng khat bup a sung hi.

records.english: How much did a tram ticket cost when it first opened?
records.zomi: Tram a kihon masak ciangin a lakkhia ding lai bangzah ahi hiam?

records.english: The bus driver let me sit beside him and showed me how he changed the gears.
records.zomi: Bus mawngpa in a kiang ah hong tusak a, gear a khek dan hong lak hi.

records.english: Why did the tram stop running after only ten years?
records.zomi: Bang hangin kum sawm bek khit ciangin tram a khawl hiam?

records.english: My new white shirt was ruined by a passenger's leaking bottle of oil.
records.zomi: Ka puan-akhi ngou thak pen khualzin khat' sathau bel a luang in a susia hi.

records.english: My first job was selling boiled peanuts through the windows of the buses at the market stop.
records.zomi: Ka nasep masa pen zuakna mun dinna-a bus tukvuang tawh bekang lum zuak ahi hi.

records.english: Every passenger's ticket was punched by hand with a small metal clip.
records.zomi: Khualzin khempeuh' lakkhia ding lai dal neu khat tawh khut tawh kivit hi.

records.english: I really did fall asleep standing up on the crowded morning train.
records.zomi: Zingsang meileng mi tam ah ding-in ka ihmu taktak hi.

records.english: Hold on tight, all of you, because the road gets bumpy after the bridge!
records.zomi: Na khempeuh un hoih takin len un, lei khit ciangin lampi a kilawk ding hi!

records.english: Was the cable car ever closed because of the wind?
records.zomi: Khau tung mawtaw huih hangin kikhak ngei hiam?

records.english: Traveling by night train felt like being rocked to sleep by a huge, noisy cradle.
records.zomi: Zan meileng tawh khualzin pen naupang lawkna lian, ging buai khat sungah ihmut bang ahi hi.

records.english: Did you ever ride on the roof of a bus?
records.zomi: Bus tung lam ah na tuang ngei hiam?

records.english: Once, but only for a mile, and my mother never found out.
records.zomi: Khatvei, ahi zongin mile khat bek, leh ka nu in a thei ngei kei hi.

records.english: Our school choir sang all the way to the competition on the train.
records.zomi: I sang la pawl in kidemna dong meileng tungah la a sa uh hi.

records.english: When we got home, the station master told us we had sounded better on the train than on the stage.
records.zomi: Inn i tun ciangin meileng dinna makaipa in dawhsang tung sangin meileng tungah na la uh a hoih zaw hi, hong ci hi.

records.english: On my first visit to a big foreign city, I marked every stop on the metro map with a pencil.
records.zomi: Gamdang khuapi lian ka veh masak ciangin metro map tung-a dinna khempeuh khedal tawh ka ciamteh hi.

records.english: We arrived so early that we watched the station sweepers clean the platforms.
records.zomi: Ma lua-in i tung ahih manin meileng dinna phiatte in dinna mun a phiat uh i en hi.

records.english: It must have been strange for my grandparents to see their first train.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh ka pi in a meileng masa uh a muh uh ciangin lamdang a sa kha ding uh hi.

records.english: What I remember most about that train is the sound of the wheels changing on the bridge.
records.zomi: Tua meileng thu ah ka phawk pen pen lei tungah a khe a ging kikhek ahi hi.

records.english: Once the new highway opened, the trains to our town slowly disappeared.
records.zomi: Lampi lian thak a kihon khit ciangin i khuapi lam meileng te dai takin a mang hi.

records.english: Where did people wait for the bus before there were shelters?
records.zomi: Ngakna inn a om ma-in mite in bus koi ah a ngak uh hiam?

records.english: When did the first train come to your town?
records.zomi: Na khuapi ah meileng masa pen bang ciangin a hong hiam?

records.english: If the cable car hadn't been built, my mother would have walked three hours to school.
records.zomi: Khau tung mawtaw kibawl kei le ka nu in sang ah nai thum a pai ding hi.

records.english: I'll never forget the smell of diesel and oranges on that long bus ride.
records.zomi: Tua bus khualzinna sau-a diesel leh sangtam gim ka mangngilh ngei lo ding hi.

records.english: We missed the last bus and walked home under the stars, singing all the way.
records.zomi: Bus nunung pen i kia a, aksi nuai ah la sa kawm-in inn ah i pai hi.

records.english: On the night train to the capital, an old woman told stories to the whole carriage.
records.zomi: Gam khuapi pai zan meileng tungah numei upa khat in tuangna inn bup kiangah tangthu a gen hi.

records.english: Even the grumpy businessman in the corner put down his newspaper to listen.
records.zomi: Kiim-a sumbawlpa lungsim nasa zong a ngaih nadingin a laithak a koih hi.

records.english: Would you take the night train again if you had the chance?
records.zomi: Hun na ngah leh zan meileng na tuang kik ding hiam?

records.english: An old man's hat blew off the ferry, and a boy dived into the water to rescue it.
records.zomi: Pu upa khat' lukhu tembaw pan huih in a mut khia a, tangval khat in hotkhiat dingin tui sungah a tum hi.

records.english: My little sister's shoe fell between the train and the platform.
records.zomi: Ka nau nu' khedap meileng leh dinna mun kikal ah a kia hi.

records.english: The station porter fished it out with a long hook and handed it back with a bow.
records.zomi: Meileng dinna-a van puakpa in khual sau tawh a la a, a kun-in a pia kik hi.

records.english: In my mother's village, the children went to school in a small cable car.
records.zomi: Ka nu' khua ah naupangte in khau tung mawtaw neu khat tawh sang ah a pai uh hi.

records.english: It swung above the valley so high that the river looked like a silver thread.
records.zomi: Guam tung ah a sang lua-in a lawk ahih manin gun pen ngun khau bang hi.

records.english: She says she was terrified for a week and then started doing her homework on the way.
records.zomi: Kal khat sung a lau mahmah a, tua ciangin lampi ah a innlai a gelh kipan hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Wake me when we cross the border, will you?
records.zomi: Gam ciang i kantan ciangin hong phawngsak in, a hi hiam?

records.english: Every summer, we took the old steam train to the coast.
records.zomi: Khal simin tuipi gei ah meileng lui i tuang hi.

records.english: If you put your head out of the window, your face was covered in soot within minutes.
records.zomi: Tukvuang pan na lu na khiat leh minit tawmno sungin na mai meikhu vom in a khuh hi.

records.english: Our mother scrubbed us with a wet handkerchief before we got off, but it never quite worked.
records.zomi: I suk ma-in i nu in khut puan buan tawh hong nul a, ahi zongin a siang kim ngei kei hi.

records.english: Sharing a bench with strangers for twelve hours has a way of turning them into friends.
records.zomi: Nai sawm leh nih sung theih loh mite tawh tutphah khat hawm in lawm a suaksak thei hi.

records.english: The old ticket office had a tiny window, and you had to bend down to talk to the clerk.
records.zomi: Lakkhia ding lai zuakna lui in tukvuang neu khat a nei a, a nasempa tawh na kikum nadingin na kun ding a kisam hi.

records.english: How did you get to school when you were a child?
records.zomi: Na neu lai-in sang ah bangci-in na pai hiam?

records.english: By boat in the rainy season and on foot the rest of the year.
records.zomi: Guah hun ciangin long tawh, a dang hun ciangin khe tawh.

records.english: One afternoon, a bride's whole family got on our bus with drums and baskets of food.
records.zomi: Nitak khat in moulai khat' innkuan bup in khuang leh an empeng tawh i bus ah a tuang uh hi.

records.english: Within ten minutes, the passengers were clapping and the driver was singing along.
records.zomi: Minit sawm sungin khualzinte in khut a beng uh a, mawngpa in la a sa khawm hi.

records.english: Nobody minded that we arrived an hour late.
records.zomi: Nai khat nunung-in i tun kuamah in a lungkham kei uh hi.

records.english: Who used to meet you at the station when you came home from college?
records.zomi: Sang lian pan inn na ciah ciangin meileng dinna ah kua in hong dawn ngei hiam?

records.english: The long journeys of my childhood taught me to enjoy watching the world go by.
records.zomi: Ka naupan lai-a khualzinna sau te in leitung kikhek en nopsak dingin hong sin sak hi.

records.english: When the tram line opened in our town, the first week's rides were free.
records.zomi: I khuapi ah tram lampi a kihon ciangin kal masa-a tuangna te a man om lo hi.

records.english: My friends and I rode it from one end to the other all day long.
records.zomi: Ka lawmte leh kei in ni bup a tawp khat pan a tawp khat dong i tuang hi.

records.english: By Friday, the drivers knew our names and let us ring the bell at every stop.
records.zomi: Laithai ni ciangin mawngpate in i min a thei uh a, dinna khempeuh ah khawngging hong ging sak uh hi.

records.english: Do you remember the rickshaw driver who sang to his passengers?
records.zomi: A khualzinte adingin la a sa rickshaw mawngpa na phawk hiam?

records.english: He sang so loudly that shopkeepers stepped into the street and waved as we went by.
records.zomi: A ging lua-in a sak ahih manin i kantan ciangin zuakna inn neite lampi ah a pusuak uh a, khut a vai uh hi.

records.english: My aunt traveled by bus for two days just to see me in the school play.
records.zomi: Sang-a lawng ah hong en dingin ka ni in ni nih sung bus tawh a khualzin hi.

records.english: I do want to ride that cable car one day, even though my mother says it's been replaced.
records.zomi: Tua khau tung mawtaw ni khat ka tuang nuam taktak hi, kikhek khin hi, ci-in ka nu in a gen hangin.

records.english: My cousin used a little notebook to write down every new word she heard in the city.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu in khuapi ah a zak kammal thak khempeuh gelh nadingin laibu neu khat a zang hi.

records.english: How old was your grandfather when he first saw the sea?
records.zomi: Na pu in tuipi a muh masak ciangin kum bangzah ahi hiam?

records.english: Seventy, and he stood on the beach for an hour without saying a word.
records.zomi: Kum sawm sagih, leh tuipi gei ah nai khat sung kammal khat zong a gen lo-in a ding hi.

records.english: To get to my cousin's graduation, we had to cross the capital on three different buses.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam' laizo pawi tun nadingin gam khuapi bus tuamtuam thum tawh i kantan ding a kisam hi.

records.english: Traveling with my grandmother meant stopping to talk to every stranger who smiled at her.
records.zomi: Ka pi tawh khualzin pen a tungah a nui theih loh mi khempeuh tawh kikum dingin khawl ahi hi.

records.english: Why did you go to the city on your own at fourteen?
records.zomi: Bang hangin kum sawm leh li na phak ciangin nangma bek in khuapi ah na pai hiam?

records.english: Was the train journey longer than you expected?
records.zomi: Meileng khualzinna na ngaihsut sangin a sau zaw hiam?

records.english: Who looked after the farm while you were away?
records.zomi: Na om lohna sungin kua in lo a kem hiam?

records.english: How did you find your way around without a phone?
records.zomi: Phone om lo-in lampi bangci-in na mu hiam?

records.english: With a paper map, and by asking anyone who looked friendly.
records.zomi: Laidal map tawh, leh lawmhoih bang mi khempeuh dot-in.

records.english: Before I left the village, my grandfather put his old brass compass in my hand.
records.zomi: Khua ka nusiat ma-in ka pu in a dal lam theihna setna lui ka khut ah a koih hi.

records.english: He said, "You won't need it in the city, but it will remind you which way home is."
records.zomi: “Khuapi ah na kisam kei ding hi, ahi zongin inn lam koi ah a om hiam hong phawksak ding hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: Our school debate team traveled to the city for the regional competition.
records.zomi: I sang kinialna pawl gam sung kidemna adingin khuapi ah a pai uh hi.

records.english: We lost in the first round, but nobody cared very much.
