records.zomi: A kipat masa pen ah i sung a, ahi zongin kuamah in a lungkham mahmah kei uh hi.

records.english: What we talked about all the way home was the ice cream, which most of us had never tasted before.
records.zomi: Inn ciahna lampi bup ah i kikup pen ice cream ahi a, i tamzaw in i lim et ngei nai kei hi.

records.english: My aunt went to the city to buy a sewing machine and came home with a parrot as well.
records.zomi: Ka ni in puan khuina setna lei dingin khuapi ah a pai a, vaphual khat zong a tawi hi.

records.english: I saved for a year to take my mother to see the cathedral she had always talked about.
records.zomi: Ka nu in a gen den pawlpi inn lian en dingin ka pi nadingin kum khat ka kikoih hi.

records.english: Five women from our village took their baskets to a craft fair in the capital.
records.zomi: I khua pan numei nga in a empeng te uh gam khuapi-a khutsiam van pawi ah a tawi uh hi.

records.english: They came back with empty bags, new friends, and orders for two hundred more baskets.
records.zomi: Ip ngawng, lawm thak, leh empeng za nih behlap adingin ngetnate tawh a ciah kik uh hi.

records.english: My brother cycled the whole way to the city to save the bus fare.
records.zomi: Bus man a kem nadingin ka sanggam pasal in khuapi dong siiksakol a tuang hi.

records.english: Which city would you most like to visit again?
records.zomi: Khuapi bang na veh kik nuam pen hiam?

records.english: Did the capital look the way you had imagined?
records.zomi: Gam khuapi in na ngaihsut bangin a om hiam?

records.english: People in the northern city spoke a dialect I could hardly understand.
records.zomi: Mal lam khuapi-a mite in ka theih zawh kei pau a zang uh hi.

records.english: I pointed at a word in my phrasebook and expected a bowl of noodles.
records.zomi: Ka pau laibu-a kammal khat ka khut tawh ka lak a, khauhsawk kuang khat ka ngak hi.

records.english: Instead, the waiter brought me a plate of fried frogs, which turned out to be delicious.
records.zomi: Tua sangin an tawisakpa in uikang kang kuang khat hong tawi a, a lim mahmah hi.

records.english: We were so tired after the first day that we fell asleep before dinner.
records.zomi: Ni masa khit ciangin i ol lua ahih manin nitak an ma-in i ihmu hi.

records.english: What did your aunt do with the parrot?
records.zomi: Na ni in vaphual bang a bawl hiam?

records.english: Once I had learned the bus routes, the city stopped feeling like a maze.
records.zomi: Bus lampi te ka theih khit ciangin khuapi pen lampi buai bang a hi nawn kei hi.

records.english: Whichever street we turned into, there seemed to be another market.
records.zomi: Lampi bang ah i lut zongin zuakna mun dang khat a om bang hi.

records.english: We might have stayed longer if the hostel hadn't been so expensive.
records.zomi: Om-na inn a man tam lua kei le sawt zawin i om kha ding hi.

records.english: I do want to show my children the bakery where I lived as a student.
records.zomi: Sangnaupang ka hih lai-a ka omna moh bawlna ka ta te lak ka deih taktak hi.

records.english: When did you last go back to the city where you studied?
records.zomi: Na sinna khuapi ah bang ciangin na ciah kik nunung hiam?

records.english: Stay together, all of you, and don't stop to look at the shop windows!
records.zomi: Na khempeuh un khawm-in om unla, zuakna inn tukvuang te en dingin khawl kei un!

records.english: Right, everyone — if you lose the group, go back to the fountain and wait.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh aw — na pawl na mansuah leh tui puakna mun ah ciah kik unla ngak un.

records.english: Have I ever told you about my first ride in a lift?
records.zomi: Lift ka tuang masak thu kong gen ngei hiam?

records.english: We bought a cheap map at the station and drew a circle around every place we wanted to see.
records.zomi: Meileng dinna ah map man neu khat i lei a, i et nop mun khempeuh i kual hi.

records.english: The lights of the city at night looked like a sky turned upside down.
records.zomi: Zanin khuapi meivak te pen van a kilehkhiat bang hi.

records.english: At fourteen, I took twenty jars of my family's honey to sell at a fair in the city.
records.zomi: Kum sawm leh li ka phak ciangin khuapi pawi ah zuak dingin ka innkuan' khuaizu bel sawm nih ka tawi hi.

records.english: I was afraid nobody would buy them, so I gave away tiny spoonfuls to taste.
records.zomi: Kuamah in a lei kei kha ding uh hi, ci-in ka lau ahih manin lim et dingin kawm neu khat ciat ka pia hi.

records.english: Every jar was gone within an hour, and I spent the afternoon walking around with my pockets full of coins.
records.zomi: Nai khat sungin bel khempeuh a bei a, ka ip te dangka sik tawh a dim-in nitak bup ka vak hi.

records.english: When I went to study in the capital, my bus arrived long after midnight.
records.zomi: Gam khuapi ah sin dingin ka pai ciangin ka bus zan laitak khit nung sawt mahmah ciangin a tung hi.

records.english: I had nowhere to go, so I slept on a bench in the station with my bag under my head.
records.zomi: Ka pai ding mun ka nei kei ahih manin ka ip ka lu nuai ah koih-in meileng dinna-a tutphah tungah ka ihmu hi.

records.english: At dawn, a cleaner woke me gently and brought me a cup of sweet tea.
records.zomi: Khuavak ciangin phiatpa khat in nem takin hong phawngsak a, tea khum haai khat hong tawi hi.

records.english: Instead of visiting the famous sights, we spent most of the day in my uncle's tiny kitchen.
records.zomi: Min thang mun te veh sangin ni a tamzaw ka pa neu' an huanna neu ah i zang hi.

records.english: Did you ever see the famous clock tower?
records.zomi: Min thang nai-ten inn sang na mu ngei hiam?

records.english: We came home with sore feet, empty pockets, and enough stories to last all winter.
records.zomi: Khe na, ip ngawng, leh khuavot bup adingin a kicing tangthu tawh inn ah i ciah hi.

records.english: If the cleaner hadn't been so kind that first morning, I might have gone straight back home.
records.zomi: Tua zingsang masa pen-in phiatpa a lungsim hoih kei le inn ah ka ciah pah kha ding hi.

records.english: Shall we go back next spring, when the gardens are in bloom?
records.zomi: A zom spring, huan te a pak ciangin i ciah kik ding hiam?

records.english: Every trip to the city ended with my mother counting the money she had left and sighing.
records.zomi: Khuapi khualzinna khempeuh ka nu in a om lai sum a sim a, a thaw tawh a tawp hi.

records.english: What stays with me from that trip is not the buildings but the people we met.
records.zomi: Tua khualzinna pan ka lungsim ah a om pen inn lian te hi lo-in i kimuh mite ahi hi.

records.english: Please keep a seat for me on the bus home, because I'm going to buy some sweets for the children.
records.zomi: Naupangte adingin thei khum ka lei ding ahih manin inn ciahna bus ah tutna khat hong koih sak in.

records.english: Seeing the sea for the first time, my grandfather simply took off his shoes and walked in.
records.zomi: Tuipi a muh masak ciangin ka pu in a khedap a suah a, a sung ah a lut hi.

records.english: Where did you stay on your first visit to the city?
records.zomi: Khuapi na veh masak ciangin koi ah na om hiam?

records.english: In a tiny room above a bakery, and I woke up every morning to the smell of bread.
records.zomi: Moh bawlna tung-a inndei neu mahmah khat ah, leh zingsang simin moh gim tawh ka thou hi.

records.english: I really did believe the city streets would be paved with marble.
records.zomi: Khuapi lampi te marble suang tawh kibawl ding hi, ci-in ka um taktak hi.

records.english: Coming from a village of two hundred people, I found the crowds both thrilling and exhausting.
records.zomi: Mi za nih bek a om khua pan ka hong ahih manin mi tam pen nuam leh olna ka sa hi.

records.english: On our first trip to the city, I took photos all day with a borrowed camera.
records.zomi: Khuapi i veh masak ciangin ka caih camera tawh ni bup lim ka la hi.

records.english: Back home, we discovered that there had never been any film in it.
records.zomi: Inn i tun ciangin a sungah film om ngei lo hi, cih i thei hi.

records.english: My first visit to the capital changed what I believed was possible for someone like me.
records.zomi: Gam khuapi ka veh masak in keimah bang mi adingin bang bawl theih hiam ka upna a khek hi.

records.english: Do you remember the morning we sat on the museum steps waiting for it to open?
records.zomi: Museum a kihon ding ngak-in a kahlei tungah i tut zingsang na phawk hiam?

records.english: Some of the most memorable nights of my life were spent in the least comfortable places.
records.zomi: Ka nuntakna-a zan phawk pen pawl khat nuam lo pen mun te-ah ka zang hi.

records.english: Imagine twenty hikers trying to fall asleep while one of them snored like a bear!
records.zomi: Mual kah mi sawm nih ihmut a sin uh laitakin a khat in vompi bangin a ngawk ngaihsun in!

records.english: We might have stayed another night if the soup had been a little more varied.
records.zomi: An tui tawmno a tuamtuam zaw le zan khat behlap i om kha ding hi.

records.english: How many people could the mountain hut sleep?
records.zomi: Mual tung-a lobuk in mi bangzah ihmusak thei hiam?

records.english: Does the owner's daughter still run the inn by the road, I wonder?
records.zomi: A neipa' tanu in lampi kiang-a khualzin inn a kem lai ding hiam?

records.english: We opened the stiff window with a butter knife from the breakfast table.
records.zomi: Zingsang an dawhkan pan sathau namsau tawh tukvuang khauh i hong hi.

records.english: We stayed a week in a hotel where the only dish at dinner was cabbage soup.
records.zomi: Nitak an-a an khat bek kawlmukbe an tui ahi zinbuuk khat ah kal khat i om hi.

records.english: By the last night, we were dreaming about rice and fried eggs.
records.zomi: Zan nunung ciangin buh leh aktui kang i mang hi.

records.english: What was the strangest place you've ever slept?
records.zomi: Na ihmut ngei mun lamdang pen bang ahi hiam?

records.english: Cleaning rooms that summer taught me never to leave a mess for someone else.
records.zomi: Tua khal-a inndei sianseh in mi dang adingin buaina nusia ngei lo dingin hong sin sak hi.

records.english: Do you remember the guesthouse with the big grey cat?
records.zomi: Zawh san-ngoh lian a om zinbuuk neu na phawk hiam?

records.english: It slept on a different guest's bed every night, and everyone hoped it would choose theirs.
records.zomi: Zan simin khual tuamtuam' lupna tungah a ihmu a, mi khempeuh in amau' lupna a teel ding a deih uh hi.

records.english: The owner drew us a map of the village on the back of our bill.
records.zomi: A neipa in i laimal nung lam ah khua map hong gelh sak hi.

records.english: The night porter made my mother a hot drink when she couldn't sleep.
records.zomi: Ka nu a ihmu thei kei ciangin zan kempa in dawn ding lum khat a bawl sak hi.

records.english: Who carried the bags up to the mountain hut?
records.zomi: Mual tung-a lobuk ah ip te kua in a puak tou hiam?

records.english: The old hotel in my uncle's town still used heavy iron keys.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu' khuapi-a zinbuuk lui in tawh gik te a zang lai hi.

records.english: I carried one home in my pocket by mistake and found it a week later.
records.zomi: Khial-in ka ip sungah khat ka tawi a, kal khat khit ciangin ka mu hi.

records.english: Twenty years afterwards, I finally posted it back with a letter of apology, and the owner wrote to thank me.
records.zomi: Kum sawm nih khit ciangin maisak ngenna lai tawh a tawp-in ka khak kik a, a neipa in lungdam hong ci hi.

records.english: Please leave the key under the flowerpot when you go.
records.zomi: Na pai ciangin pak bel nuai ah tawh koih in.

records.english: If the owner hadn't put up that tent, we would have slept in the car.
records.zomi: A neipa in tua puan inn a dawh kei le mawtaw sungah i ihmu ding hi.

records.english: The innkeeper's wife sewed up the hole in my jacket while I ate breakfast.
records.zomi: Zingsang an ka nek laitakin khualzin inn neipa' zi in ka kawt kua a khui hi.

records.english: In those days, you booked a room by writing a letter to the hotel.
records.zomi: Tua hunte-in zinbuuk kiangah lai gelh-in inndei na kilai khol hi.

records.english: Once, the reply confirming our room arrived three days after we had come home.
records.zomi: Khatvei, i inndei kiciam lahna dawnna inn i tun khit ni thum ciangin a tung hi.

records.english: One summer, I worked as a cleaner in a seaside hotel.
records.zomi: Khal khat in tuipi gei zinbuuk khat ah inn sianseh-in ka sem hi.

records.english: As I made the bed one morning, I found a book on the pillow with a note inside for me.
records.zomi: Zingsang khat in lupna ka bawl laitakin lupna khuh tungah keimah adingin laikhak kikoih laibu khat ka mu hi.

records.english: It said, "Thank you for the folded towels shaped like swans; they made my children laugh every morning."
records.zomi: “Vapual bangin na thuah puan nulna te adingin lungdam ing; zingsang simin ka ta te a nuisak hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: Was the monastery guesthouse very cold at night?
records.zomi: Biakna inn zinbuuk neu pen zanin a vot mahmah hiam?

records.english: At the monastery guesthouse, guests were asked not to speak after dark.
records.zomi: Biakna inn zinbuuk neu ah khualte in a mial khit ciangin thu gen lo dingin kingen hi.

records.english: Once you have slept in a mountain hut, even a simple hotel feels like a palace.
records.zomi: Mual tung-a lobuk ah na ihmut khit ciangin zinbuuk neu zong kumpi inn bang a hi hi.

records.english: Shall we look for that lakeside cabin again next summer?
records.zomi: A zom khal ciangin tuili kiang-a sing inn neu i zong kik ding hiam?

records.english: The owner lit the stove with a match and a twist of newspaper.
records.zomi: A neipa in meitang leh laithak tawh meikhuk a hal hi.

records.english: Whatever the hotel lacked in comfort, it made up for in kindness.
records.zomi: Zinbuuk in nuamna a kiam bangzah zongin itna tawh a sik hi.

records.english: When did you first stay in a hotel on your own?
records.zomi: Bang ciangin nangma bek-in zinbuuk ah na om masa hiam?

records.english: Instead of a lobby, the guesthouse had a kitchen table where everyone ate together.
records.zomi: Lutna khan sangin zinbuuk neu in mi khempeuh khawm-a an nekna an huanna dawhkan a nei hi.

records.english: We left a box of chocolates for the cleaners who had looked after our room.
records.zomi: I inndei a kem phiatte adingin chocolate bawm khat i nusia hi.

records.english: Right, everyone, leave your boots by the door and your wet coats by the stove.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh aw, na khedap sau uh kongkhak kiang ah, na puan kidip buan uh meikhuk kiang ah koih un.

records.english: Can you still hear the lake lapping against the wooden steps?
records.zomi: Tuili in sing kahlei a tawk ging na za thei lai hiam?

records.english: What I remember about that inn is not the rooms but the stories the drivers told.
records.zomi: Tua khualzin inn thu ah ka phawk pen inndei te hi lo-in mawngpate' tangthu gen ahi hi.

records.english: My grandparents ran a small inn beside the main road.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh ka pi in lampi lian kiang ah khualzin inn neu khat a kem uh hi.

records.english: Before school, my cousins and I served breakfast to the truck drivers.
records.zomi: Sang ma-in ka sanggamte leh kei in mawtaw lian mawngte zingsang an i pia hi.

records.english: The drivers paid us in jokes, news from the city, and sometimes a coin each.
records.zomi: Mawngpate in nuihza thu, khuapi thu, leh khatvei khat dangka sik khat ciat tawh hong pia uh hi.

records.english: Listen, all of you: the hut door is locked at nine, and nobody goes outside after dark.
records.zomi: Na khempeuh un ngai un: lobuk kongkhak nai kua ciangin kikhak a, a mial khit ciangin kuamah pusuak lo ding hi.

records.english: How did you find a room without a phone or the internet?
records.zomi: Phone leh internet om lo-in inndei bangci-in na mu hiam?

records.english: Guests who arrive as strangers sometimes leave as friends, my grandmother used to say about the inn.
records.zomi: Theih loh mi bangin a tung khualte pawl khat lawm-in a pai uh hi, ci-in ka pi in khualzin inn thu a gen ngei hi.

records.english: Every room in town was taken during the festival, so the hotel owner put up a tent for us in his garden.
records.zomi: Pawi sungin khuapi-a inndei khempeuh a kim ahih manin zinbuuk neipa in a huan sungah puan inn hong dawh sak hi.

records.english: I really did think the hotel lift was a tiny room that moved by magic.
records.zomi: Zinbuuk lift pen lamdang tawh a kitawn inndei neu khat ahi hi, ci-in ka um taktak hi.

records.english: Running an inn meant that my grandparents never once had a holiday of their own.
records.zomi: Khualzin inn kem hangin ka pu leh ka pi in amau' nopsakna khualzin khatvei zong a nei ngei kei uh hi.

records.english: Where did you stay on your honeymoon?
records.zomi: Na ki-ten khit khualzinna ah koi ah na om hiam?

records.english: In a cabin by a lake, where the only other guests were ducks.
records.zomi: Tuili kiang-a sing inn neu khat ah, khual dang pen va-ngang te bek ahi hi.

records.english: The cleaner used an old toothbrush to scrub the corners of every bathroom.
records.zomi: Inn sianseh pa in kisilna inn kil khempeuh nul nadingin ha nulna lui khat a zang hi.

records.english: What did the truck drivers tell you about the city?
records.zomi: Mawtaw lian mawngte in khuapi thu bang hong gen uh hiam?

records.english: Why did your aunt book the best room in the hotel?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na ni in zinbuuk-a inndei hoih pen a kilai hiam?

records.english: I do want to take my children to that hut one day, even if we have to sleep on the floor.
records.zomi: Inn phah tungah i ihmut ding a kisam zongin ni khat tua lobuk ah ka ta te ka pi nuam taktak hi.

records.english: We stayed in a cheaper room so that we could afford a boat trip on the lake.
records.zomi: Tuili ah long tuang i lei theih nadingin inndei man neu zaw ah i om hi.

records.english: The silence of the monastery was so deep that I could hear my own heartbeat.
records.zomi: Biakna inn daihna a thuk lua ahih manin ka lungtang sat ging ka za thei hi.

records.english: Did you ever stay in a hotel as a child?
records.zomi: Na neu lai-in zinbuuk ah na om ngei hiam?

records.english: Only once, and I spent the whole time riding up and down in the lift.
records.zomi: Khatvei bek, leh a hun bup lift-in ka kai a, ka kiak hi.

records.english: On our first hiking trip, we spent the night in a mountain hut with twenty strangers.
records.zomi: I mual kah khualzinna masa pen-in theih loh mi sawm nih tawh mual tung-a lobuk ah zan i lum hi.

records.english: We slept in a row on the wooden floor, wrapped in every blanket we could find.
records.zomi: I muh theih puannak khempeuh tawh kituam-in sing phah tungah i ihmu hi.

records.english: Before the lamps went out, the warden played his flute until the whole hut was quiet.
records.zomi: Meivak te a mit ma-in a kempa in lobuk bup a daih mateng a phengphung a tum hi.

records.english: If my brother hadn't learned to cook, we would have lived on bread and tea for months.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in an huan a sin kei le kha tampi sung moh leh tea bek tawh i nungta ding hi.

records.english: Why did your grandfather keep everyone out of the kitchen?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na pu in an huanna pan mi khempeuh a khak hiam?

records.english: Come and sit down, everyone — the soup is on the table!
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, hong tu un — an tui dawhkan tungah a om khin hi!

records.english: What I miss most is the smell of the clay oven on Friday afternoons.
records.zomi: Ka lungngai pen Laithai ni nitak lam simin leivui meikhuk gim ahi hi.

records.english: Perhaps the radio program's recipes are still in my brother's old exercise book.
records.zomi: Radio an huan dan te ka sanggam pasal' laibu lui sungah a om lai kha ding hi.

records.english: My sister got up early to make my favorite pancakes on my birthday.
records.zomi: Ka pianni-in ka deih pen pancake bawl dingin ka sanggam nu ma takin a thou hi.

records.english: Who taught you to make bread?
records.zomi: Moh bawl dan kua in hong sin sak hiam?

records.english: A baker in the town where I studied, who let me help in exchange for breakfast.
records.zomi: Ka sinna khuapi-a moh bawlpa khat, zingsang an tawh ka huh theih nadingin hong phal pa.

records.english: Instead of a recipe, my grandfather had a long list of rules that he never wrote down.
records.zomi: An huan dan sangin ka pu in a gelh ngei loh thukham tampi a nei hi.

records.english: When did you first cook a whole meal by yourself?
records.zomi: Bang ciangin nangma bek-in an kim khat na huan masa hiam?

records.english: Where did you learn to cook such good curry?
records.zomi: Tua bang curry hoih huan dan koi ah na sin hiam?

records.english: Do you remember when we got our first microwave?
records.zomi: Microwave masa pen i ngah ciang na phawk hiam?

records.english: How could I forget, after your sister put an egg in it and it exploded all over the door?
records.zomi: Na sanggam nu in a sungah aktui a koih a, kongkhak tungah a puak dalh ahih manin bangci-in ka mangngilh thei ding hiam?

records.english: The fish was cleaned by my brothers at the river before we brought it home.
records.zomi: Inn ah i tawi ma-in ka sanggam pasalte in gun ah nga a silh uh hi.

records.english: My first attempt at a family dinner taught me humility and the importance of reading a recipe to the end.
records.zomi: Innkuan nitak an ka bawl sinna masa pen in kiniamkhiatna leh an huan dan a tawp dong sim thupi dan hong sin sak hi.

records.english: My aunt crushed the spices with a smooth stone she had carried from her home village.
records.zomi: Ka ni in a khua pan a tawi suang nem khat tawh an lim te a deng hi.

records.english: Could I have the crispy rice from the bottom of the pot?
records.zomi: Beel nuai-a buh kang ka ngah thei ding hiam?

records.english: How long did it take to bake bread in the clay oven?
records.zomi: Leivui meikhuk sungah moh em bangzah sawt hiam?

records.english: The kitchen was the warmest room in the house and, somehow, the place where every family decision was made.
records.zomi: An huanna pen inn sung-a a lum pen inndei ahi a, innkuan thukhenna khempeuh a kibawlna mun zong ahi hi.

records.english: Whatever was in the pot, my uncle always added one more chili than anyone wanted.
records.zomi: Beel sungah bang om zongin ka pa neu in kuamah deih sangin malcha khat a behlap tawntung hi.

records.english: When I was ten, I made my first omelette for the whole family.
records.zomi: Kum sawm ka phak ciangin innkuan bup adingin aktui kang masa pen ka bawl hi.

records.english: I was so nervous that half the eggshell ended up in the pan.
records.zomi: Ka lau lua ahih manin aktui khal a kim a bel sungah a kia hi.

records.english: Everyone ate it anyway, and my uncle said it was the crunchiest omelette he had ever tasted.
records.zomi: Bang hi zongin mi khempeuh in a ne uh a, ka pa neu in a nek ngei aktui kang awng pen ahi hi, a ci hi.

records.english: I learned to make soup so that I could take care of my mother when she was ill.
records.zomi: Ka nu a cina ciangin ka kem theih nadingin an tui bawl ka sin hi.

records.english: It might have been easier to buy bread, but my mother said the baking was the best part of the week.
records.zomi: Moh lei leng a baih zaw kha ding hi, ahi zongin moh em pen kal sung-a a hoih pen ahi hi, ci-in ka nu in a gen hi.

records.english: After the bread came out, we used to roast corn on the hot embers.
records.zomi: Moh a pusuak khit ciangin meiling lum tungah vaimim i kang ngei hi.

records.english: We cooked twice as much rice so that the neighbors could share our meal.
records.zomi: Inn vengte in i an a hawm theih nadingun buh a nih-in i huan hi.

records.english: Before the school's harvest feast, our whole class sat in the yard shelling peas.
records.zomi: Sang kaihawl pawi ma-in i sang inndei bup in huan sungah tu-in bekang i hual hi.

records.english: We ate almost as many as we shelled, and the teacher pretended not to notice.
records.zomi: I hual zah dekin i ne a, saya in a mu lo bangin a om hi.

records.english: Right, all of you, one person peels, one person chops, and nobody eats the carrots before they're cooked!
records.zomi: Na khempeuh un, mi khat in a hawng hual, mi khat in a at, leh a min ma-in kuamah in carrot ne kei un!

records.english: My mother tried for years to teach me how to fold dumplings.
records.zomi: Ka nu in kum tampi sung dumpling khip dan hong sin sak dingin a hanciam hi.

records.english: Mine always came apart in the water, and she called them "open-mouthed fish."
records.zomi: Keimah' te tui sungah a kikhen tawntung a, “Nga kam hong” ci-in a min a phuak hi.

records.english: Now my own children fold them better than I ever could.
records.zomi: Tu-in ka ta te in kei sangin a khip siam zaw uh hi.

records.english: Watching my grandfather cook was like watching a musician who had played the same song all his life.
records.zomi: Ka pu an huan et pen a nuntak sung la kibang a tum la tumpa et bang ahi hi.

records.english: We cracked the coconuts with the back of a heavy knife.
records.zomi: Namsau gik nung lam tawh onkuang te i sukkham hi.

records.english: My uncle used an old tin can to cut perfect circles of dough.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in buh-mal nim kual hoih at nadingin dal bawm lui khat a zang hi.

records.english: Once I understood that cooking was about patience, my food started to improve.
records.zomi: An huan pen thuakzawhna ahi hi, cih ka theih khit ciangin ka an a hoih kipan hi.

records.english: I do want to learn my grandfather's noodle soup before the recipe is lost.
records.zomi: Ka pu' khauhsawk an tui bawl dan a mang ma-in sin ka deih taktak hi.

records.english: Every Sunday, my cousin cooked for the elderly couple next door.
records.zomi: Nipini simin ka sanggam in a kiang inn-a inn kiteng upa nih adingin an a huan hi.

records.english: Hand me the big wooden spoon, and keep stirring while I find the salt.
records.zomi: Sing kawm lian hong pia inla, cii ka zon laitakin kheh-in om in.

records.english: Our neighbor had a big clay oven, and on Fridays the whole street brought their bread to bake in it.
records.zomi: I inn vengpa in leivui meikhuk lian a nei a, Laithai ni simin lampi bup in em dingin a moh uh a tawi uh hi.

records.english: How did you cook rice when you went camping as a boy?
records.zomi: Tangval na hih lai-in gam ah na om ciangin buh bangci-in na huan hiam?

records.english: We packed it into bamboo tubes with water and laid them in the fire until the bamboo blackened.
records.zomi: Tui tawh gua sungah i koih a, gua a vom mateng mei sungah i koih hi.

records.english: We baked a cake for our teacher, but it sank in the middle.
records.zomi: I saya adingin cake khat i em a, ahi zongin a laizang ah a kiam hi.

records.english: At harvest time, we carried lunch to the fields in a tall metal tiffin carrier.
records.zomi: Kaihawl hun ciangin lo ah sun an dal an bawm sang tawh i puak hi.

records.english: Each tin held something different: rice in one, curry in another, and pickles at the top.
records.zomi: Bawm khempeuh in a tuamtuam a nei a: khat ah buh, khat ah curry, leh a tung pen ah an thuk.

records.english: Were you allowed to use the stove when you were young?
records.zomi: Na neu lai-in meikhuk na zang thei hiam?

records.english: Which dish did you hate as a child but love now?
records.zomi: Na neu lai-in an bang na huat a, tu-in na deih hiam?

records.english: Did your family ever cook outside?
records.zomi: Na innkuan in inn pua ah an a huan ngei uh hiam?

records.english: My grandfather cooked only once a year, on New Year's morning.
records.zomi: Ka pu in kum khat khatvei bek, Kum Thak zingsang-in an a huan hi.

records.english: He made a noodle soup that took him six hours and every pot in the kitchen.
records.zomi: Nai guk a sawt a, an huanna sung-a beel khempeuh a zang khauhsawk an tui khat a bawl hi.

records.english: Nobody was allowed in while he worked, but we could smell it from the street.
records.zomi: A sep laitakin kuamah lut dingin kiphal lo a, ahi zongin lampi pan a gim i za thei hi.

records.english: By the evening, the whole kitchen smelled of ginger and smoke.
records.zomi: Nitak ciangin an huanna bup in siing leh meikhu gim a nam hi.

records.english: I really did try to follow the recipe, but the dough just wouldn't rise.
records.zomi: An huan dan zui dingin ka sin taktak a, ahi zongin buh-mal nim a kang thei kei hi.

records.english: What did your mother cook on special days?
records.zomi: Na nu in ni thupite-in bang a huan hiam?

records.english: You may stir the pot, but don't touch the handle.
records.zomi: Beel na kheh thei hi, ahi zongin a khutkhak khoih kei in.

records.english: When my mother worked night shifts, my older brother learned to cook from a radio program.
records.zomi: Ka nu in zan nasep a sep ciangin ka u pasal in radio pan an huan a sin hi.

records.english: He wrote every recipe down in a school exercise book as the presenter read it out.
records.zomi: Gen sakpa in a sim laitakin an huan dan khempeuh sang laibu ah a gelh hi.

records.english: Some of his dinners were terrible, but he never once let us go to bed hungry.
records.zomi: A nitak an pawl khat a hoih kei mahmah a, ahi zongin khatvei zong a gilkial-in hong ihmusak ngei kei hi.

records.english: Cooking for my family taught me that a meal is a way of saying things without words.
records.zomi: Ka innkuan adingin an huan in an pen kammal om lo-in thu gen dan ahi hi, cih hong sin sak hi.

records.english: The screen goes black after a few seconds.
records.zomi: Second tawmno khit ciangin screen a vom hi.

records.english: The technician said, "Your hard drive is fine, but the fan is full of dust."
records.zomi: Bawl dampa in, “Na hard drive a hoih hi, ahi zongin fan sungah leivui a dim hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: What frustrates me most is when the computer freezes without any warning.
records.zomi: Ka lungsim a nasak pen computer in gen lo-in a khawl ciang ahi hi.

records.english: The cable had been chewed by our puppy, which explains why nothing worked.
records.zomi: Cable pen i ui neu in a se khin a, tua in bangmah a sep loh hang ahi hi.

records.english: The printer has jammed again.
records.zomi: Printer a khak kik hi.

records.english: My phone isn't charging.
records.zomi: Ka phone charge a lut kei hi.

records.english: A whole morning's work was lost when the computer restarted itself to install an update.
records.zomi: Computer in update koih dingin amah mah in a kipat kik ciangin zingsang bup nasep a mang hi.

records.english: My screen cracked when I dropped my phone on the stairs.
records.zomi: Ka phone kahlei tungah ka kiatsak ciangin ka screen a kek hi.

records.english: However careful you are, a phone dropped on stone will usually crack.
records.zomi: Bangzah in na kidawm zongin suang tungah a kia phone a tamzaw in a kek hi.

records.english: May I use your charger for a few minutes?
records.zomi: Minit tawmno na charger ka zang thei ding hiam?

records.english: I used a toothpick to clean the dust out of the charging port, and it worked again.
records.zomi: Charging port sung-a leivui siang dingin ha thuakna ka zang a, a sem kik hi.

records.english: Try a different cable first.
records.zomi: Cable dang khat masa-in sin in.

records.english: Can you check whether the Wi-Fi is working?
records.zomi: Wi-Fi a sem hiam na en thei ding hiam?

records.english: My laptop froze again this morning.
records.zomi: Tu zingsang in ka laptop a khawl kik hi.

records.english: All the computers in the office were updated overnight.
records.zomi: Office-a computer khempeuh zanin kiupdate hi.

records.english: Have you tried turning it off and on again?
records.zomi: Mut-in hal kik-in na sin khin hiam?

records.english: Yes, twice, and it still won't start.
records.zomi: Sin khin ing, nih vei, ahi zongin a kipan nuam lai kei hi.

records.english: Fixing my grandmother's phone took ten minutes, but explaining what I had done took an hour.
records.zomi: Ka pi' phone bawl dam minit sawm bek a sawt a, ahi zongin ka bawl gen siang nai khat a sawt hi.

records.english: The update is taking forever.
records.zomi: Update pen a sawt lua hi.

records.english: It's often a small thing, like a loose cable, that makes a device seem completely broken.
records.zomi: Setna khat a sia kim bangin a om sak pen cable nem bang thu neu khat ahi tam hi.

records.english: Is the mouse working now?
records.zomi: Tu-in mouse a sem hiam?

records.english: It was only the battery, so I put in a new one.
records.zomi: Battery bek ahih manin a thak khat ka koih hi.

records.english: What does this error message mean?
records.zomi: Hih error message in bang a ci nopna hiam?

records.english: When was the last time you updated your phone?
records.zomi: Na phone bang ciangin na update nunung hiam?

records.english: The printer kept saying it was out of paper, even though the tray was full.
records.zomi: Tray a dim hangin printer in laidal a bei hi, a ci tawntung hi.

records.english: Most problems with our home computer are solved by simply restarting it.
records.zomi: I inn computer haksatna a tamzaw a kipat kik sak bek tawh kibawl dam hi.

records.english: My laptop was repaired for free, because it was still under warranty.
records.zomi: Warranty sung a om lai ahih manin ka laptop a man lo-in kibawl dam hi.

records.english: I helped my grandmother fix the sound on her phone.
records.zomi: Ka pi' phone ging bawl dam dingin ka huh hi.

records.english: Who can help me with my tablet?
records.zomi: Ka tablet adingin kua in hong huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Ask at the help desk on the ground floor.
records.zomi: Leitual dawl-a help desk ah dong in.

records.english: Why does my phone get so hot when I watch videos?
records.zomi: Video ka et ciangin bang hangin ka phone a sa lua hiam?

records.english: My keyboard is sticky because I spilled tea on it.
records.zomi: Tea ka sung ahih manin ka keyboard a ngaktak hi.

records.english: My grandfather called me three times on Sunday because his phone screen had turned upside down.
records.zomi: Ka pu' phone screen a kilehkhia ahih manin Nipini ni-in thum vei hong sam hi.

records.english: I explained over the phone how to turn the screen lock on.
records.zomi: Phone tungah screen lock hon dan ka gen siang hi.

records.english: He was so pleased that he called a fourth time just to say thank you.
records.zomi: A kipak lua ahih manin lungdam ci bek dingin lina vei hong sam hi.

records.english: Close some of those windows, and the computer will run faster.
records.zomi: Tua window pawl khat khak inla, computer a manlang zaw ding hi.

records.english: By the time the technician arrived, the problem had mysteriously fixed itself.
records.zomi: Bawl dampa a tun ciangin haksatna a lamdang takin amah mah in a dam khin hi.

records.english: Please don't eat or drink near the computers.
records.zomi: Computer te kiang ah ne kei unla dawn kei un.

records.english: Whatever the problem is, the help desk asks you to restart the computer first.
records.zomi: Haksatna bang ahi zongin help desk in computer kipat kik sak masa dingin a ngen hi.

records.english: Why is there no sound from the speakers?
records.zomi: Bang hangin speaker te pan ging a om kei hiam?

records.english: The volume was turned all the way down.
records.zomi: Volume a niam pen dong kikoih hi.

records.english: I'll lend you my old phone while yours is being repaired.
records.zomi: Na phone a kibawl dam laitakin ka phone lui kong caih sak ding hi.

records.english: Never try to open the back of a phone while it's still charging.
records.zomi: Charge a lut laitakin phone nung lam hon dingin sin ngei kei in.

records.english: Our school's technician spent the whole morning fixing the projector for the assembly.
records.zomi: I sang-a bawl dampa in kikhopna adingin projector bawl dam dingin zingsang bup a zang hi.

records.english: Don't leave your phone in the sun; it can overheat.
records.zomi: Na phone ni sungah nusia kei in; a sa lua thei hi.

records.english: Rather than buying a new printer, we had the old one cleaned and repaired.
records.zomi: Printer thak lei sangin a lui i sianseh sak a, i bawl dam sak hi.

records.english: Could you take a look at my laptop when you have a minute?
records.zomi: Hun na neih ciangin ka laptop hong en sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Last night, my laptop suddenly made a loud clicking noise and shut down.
records.zomi: Zanin ka laptop in thawlawh takin ging lian a bawl a, a khawl hi.

records.english: I panicked, because my essay was due the next morning.
records.zomi: Ka laigelh a zing zingsang piak ding ahih manin ka lau mahmah hi.

records.english: Luckily, my cousin works in a repair shop, and he had it running again in an hour.
records.zomi: Vangphat takin ka sanggam bawl damna inn ah a sem a, nai khat sungin a sem kik sak hi.

records.english: Could you show my mother how to connect her new phone to the Wi-Fi?
records.zomi: Ka nu' phone thak Wi-Fi ah zom dan hong lak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Is it safe to unplug it now?
records.zomi: Tu-in plug khiat bit hiam?

records.english: Learning to solve small computer problems myself has saved me a lot of money.
records.zomi: Computer haksatna neute keimah in bawl dam sin in sum tampi hong kem sak hi.

records.english: The more programs you run at once, the slower an old laptop tends to become.
records.zomi: Program tam khatvei-in na zat semsem ciangin laptop lui a nawlkhin semsem hi.

records.english: If I had backed up my photos, losing my phone wouldn't have been such a disaster.
records.zomi: Ka lim te backup ka koih le ka phone mansuah a haksa lua lo ding hi.

records.english: Before you call the help desk, write down exactly what the error message says.
records.zomi: Help desk na sam ma-in error message in bang a ci hiam limtakin gelh in.

records.english: My son reset my phone for me after it kept switching itself off.
records.zomi: Ka phone amah mah in a kimut tawntung ahih manin ka tapa in hong reset sak hi.

records.english: You're not allowed to install programs on the school computers without permission.
records.zomi: Phalna om lo-in sang computer tungah program na koih thei kei hi.

records.english: I restarted the router so that the internet would come back on.
records.zomi: Internet a hong om kik nadingin router ka kipat kik sak hi.

records.english: Is it all right if I borrow your laptop to print my ticket?
records.zomi: Ka lakkhia ding lai print nadingin na laptop ka caih thei ding hiam?

records.english: It took the kitchen an hour to cook the enormous fish, and we spent the time laughing.
records.zomi: An huanna in nga lian mahmah huan dingin nai khat a sawt a, tua hun i nuihsan in i zang hi.

records.english: We weren't allowed to order fizzy drinks, so we always asked for orange juice.
records.zomi: Tui hai sem pia dingin kiphal lo ahih manin sangtam tui i ngen tawntung hi.

records.english: Did the noodle seller ever get an order wrong?
records.zomi: Khauhsawk zuakpa in a ngetna khial a pia ngei hiam?

records.english: Whatever we ordered at that stall, it came with a free comment about the weather.
records.zomi: Tua zuakna dawhkan ah bang i ngen zongin huihkhua thu gen khat a man lo-in a kipia hi.

records.english: When did you first try ordering food by phone?
records.zomi: Phone tawh an ngen dingin bang ciangin na sin masa hiam?

records.english: Instead of a menu, the café had a blackboard that changed every morning.
records.zomi: An min laibu sangin an zuakna inn in zingsang simin kikhek suanglaipi khat a nei hi.

records.english: We ordered a cake from the bakery to surprise our teacher on her last day.
records.zomi: I saya a ni nunung ah lamdang sak nadingin moh bawlna pan cake khat i ngen hi.

records.english: How did you pay for lunch at your school?
records.zomi: Na sang ah sun an man bangci-in na pia hiam?

records.english: With little tin tokens that our parents bought at the office every Monday.
records.zomi: Pizing ni simin i nu leh i pa in office pan a lei dal ciamtehna neute tawh.

records.english: I really did think the waiter would laugh at my pronunciation.
records.zomi: Ka kam ging an tawisakpa in a nuihsan ding hi, ci-in ka ngaihsun taktak hi.

records.english: What did your family order on special occasions?
records.zomi: Ni thupite-in na innkuan in bang a ngen uh hiam?

records.english: We might have ordered more if we had known how small the portions would be.
records.zomi: A neu dan uh i theih leh tam zaw i ngen kha ding hi.

records.english: Why did your grandfather always order the same breakfast?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na pu in zingsang an kibang mah a ngen tawntung hiam?

records.english: Who in your family was the most adventurous eater at restaurants?
records.zomi: Na innkuan ah an zuakna inn ah an thak sin dingin a hang pen kua hiam?

records.english: On our first date, I was so nervous that I ordered the cheapest thing on the menu.
records.zomi: I kimuh masak ni-in ka lau lua ahih manin an min laibu-a a man neu pen ka ngen hi.

records.english: She ordered soup, a main course, and then three different desserts.
records.zomi: An tui, an lian, leh tua khit ciangin an lim tuamtuam thum a ngen hi.

records.english: We've been married for thirty years, and I still haven't let her forget it.
records.zomi: Kum sawm thum i ki-ten khin a, tu dong mangngilh dingin ka phal nai kei hi.

records.english: The waiter balanced eight plates along his arm without spilling a drop.
records.zomi: An tawisakpa in a ban tungah kuang giat a koih a, khat zong a sung kei hi.

records.english: Was the fish really as big as the table?
records.zomi: Nga pen dawhkan zah in a lian taktak hiam?

records.english: Which restaurant served the best noodles when you were young?
records.zomi: Na neu lai-in an zuakna inn bang in khauhsawk hoih pen a zuak hiam?

records.english: Please don't order anything you won't finish, our parents always said.
records.zomi: Na ne zo lo ding bangmah ngen kei un, ci-in i nu leh i pa in a gen tawntung uh hi.

records.english: The noodle seller's shouting could be heard three streets away, and it made everyone hungry.
records.zomi: Khauhsawk zuakpa' kikona lampi thum gamla pan kiza a, mi khempeuh a gilkialsak hi.

records.english: If the waiter hadn't recommended the fish, I would never have discovered my favorite dish.
records.zomi: An tawisakpa in nga hong hilh kei le ka deih pen an ka mu ngei lo ding hi.

records.english: The noodle seller near our school never wrote anything down.
records.zomi: I sang kiang-a khauhsawk zuakpa in bangmah a gelh ngei kei hi.

records.english: He just shouted each order across the road to his wife, who cooked at a stall on the other side.
records.zomi: Ngetna khempeuh lampi gal lam-a an a huan a zi kiangah a kiko bek hi.

records.english: In all those years, I never once saw her bring anyone the wrong bowl.
records.zomi: Tua kum tampi sungin kuamah kiangah kuang khial a tawi ka mu ngei kei hi.

records.english: Perhaps the café still serves my grandfather's breakfast, though I haven't been back for years.
records.zomi: Kum tampi ka ciah kik kei hangin an zuakna inn in ka pu' zingsang an a zuak lai kha ding hi.

records.english: The waiter let me choose the dessert for the whole table because it was my birthday.
records.zomi: Ka pianni ahih manin an tawisakpa in dawhkan bup adingin an lim teel dingin hong phal hi.

records.english: Some of the best meals of my life were ordered from a stall with no name.
records.zomi: Ka nuntakna-a an hoih pen pawl khat min om lo zuakna dawhkan pan ka ngen hi.

records.english: In the village tea shop, the owner chalked every order on a slate behind the counter.
records.zomi: Khua-a tea zuakna inn ah a neipa in ngetna khempeuh sum lakna dawhkan nung-a suangpek tungah suangvum tawh a gelh hi.

records.english: When you paid, he simply wiped your line away with his thumb.
records.zomi: Na piak ciangin a khutpi tawh na gual a nul mang hi.

records.english: Can you imagine ordering a meal by lowering a basket from your balcony?
records.zomi: Na inn innkhawng pan empeng khiak-in an ngen ding na ngaihsun thei ding hiam?

records.english: Were children allowed to order for themselves in restaurants when you were young?
records.zomi: Na neu lai-in an zuakna inn ah naupangte in amau' adingin a ngen thei uh hiam?

records.english: Rarely, and never anything that cost more than what the adults were having.
records.zomi: Kik dekin, leh mi upate' nek sangin a man tam zaw khatpeuh ngen ngei lo hi.

records.english: The menu was written in such fancy handwriting that nobody could read it.
records.zomi: An min laibu pen kuamah in sim thei lo dingin laigelh hoih lua tawh kigelh hi.

records.english: Ordering in a restaurant for the first time made me feel suddenly grown up.
records.zomi: An zuakna inn ah ka ngen masak ciangin thawlawh takin mi upa bangin ka kisa hi.

records.english: Do you remember the café where we ordered one milkshake with five straws?
records.zomi: Milkshake khat sial nga tawh i ngetna an zuakna inn na phawk hiam?

records.english: We made it last the whole afternoon, and the owner never once asked us to leave.
records.zomi: Nitak bup i sawt sak a, a neipa in pai dingin khatvei zong hong ngen ngei kei hi.

records.english: May I order the same as last time?
records.zomi: A masa bangin ka ngen thei ding hiam?

records.english: For forty years, my grandfather ordered "the usual" at the same corner café.
records.zomi: Kum sawm li sung ka pu in lampi kikona-a an zuakna inn kibang mah ah “a ngeina bang” a ngen hi.

records.english: It was always two fried eggs, rice, and very sweet tea.
records.zomi: Aktui kang nih, buh, leh tea khum mahmah ahi tawntung hi.

records.english: On his eightieth birthday, the café added it to the menu and named it after him.
records.zomi: A pianni kum sawm giatna ah an zuakna inn in an min laibu ah a koih a, a min tawh a phuak hi.

records.english: My uncle phoned the restaurant in advance so that they would make his mother's favorite dish.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in a nu' deih pen an a bawl nadingun an zuakna inn ah a ma-in phone a sam hi.

records.english: From our balcony, my aunt lowered a basket on a rope to buy hot bread from the seller below.
records.zomi: Innkhawng pan ka ni in a nuai-a zuakpa kiang pan moh lum lei dingin khau tawh empeng a khiak hi.

records.english: He put the bread in, took the coins out, and she pulled it back up still steaming.
records.zomi: Amah in moh a koih a, dangka sik a la a, ka ni in a lum lai-in a kai tou kik hi.

records.english: Watching my grandfather order, you would have thought he was signing an important contract.
records.zomi: Ka pu a ngen na et leh kiciamna lai thupi khat a gelh hi, ci-in na ngaihsun ding hi.

records.english: Where did you eat when you first moved to the city?
records.zomi: Khuapi ah na kitawn masak ciangin koi ah an na ne hiam?

records.english: Once the waiter learned our names, he started bringing our drinks before we asked.
records.zomi: An tawisakpa in i min a theih khit ciangin i ngen ma-in i dawn ding hong tawi kipan hi.

records.english: In the dining car, the waiter took our order with a stub of pencil he kept behind his ear.
records.zomi: Meileng an nekna ah an tawisakpa in a bil nung ah a kem khedal tom khat tawh i ngetna a gelh hi.

records.english: Ordering for twelve hungry cousins required the skills of a general.
records.zomi: Sanggam gilkial sawm leh nih adingin ngen pen galkap makaipa' siamna a kisam hi.

records.english: Once, at a seaside restaurant, my brother ordered one fish.
records.zomi: Khatvei tuipi gei an zuakna inn ah ka sanggam pasal in nga khat a ngen hi.

records.english: What arrived was a fish so long that its tail hung over the end of the table.
records.zomi: A hong tung pen a mei dawhkan tawp ah a khai nga sau mahmah khat ahi hi.

records.english: Not knowing a word of the language, I ordered by drawing a chicken on a napkin.
records.zomi: Pau kammal khat zong ka theih loh manin khut nulna puan tungah ak lim gelh-in ka ngen hi.

records.english: My mother told the waiter, "No chili for the children, please, whatever they say."
records.zomi: Ka nu in an tawisakpa kiangah, “Bang ci zongin naupangte malcha pia kei un,” a ci hi.

records.english: What I remember about that tea shop is not the tea but the slate covered in names.
records.zomi: Tua tea zuakna inn thu ah ka phawk tea hi lo-in min tawh a dim suangpek ahi hi.

records.english: I ordered a bowl of soup for the old man at the next table, who had only enough money for tea.
records.zomi: Tea man bek a nei a kiang dawhkan-a pu upa adingin an tui kuang khat ka ngen sak hi.

records.english: My first job taking orders taught me how much patience a single table can require.
records.zomi: Ngetna lakna ka nasep masa pen in dawhkan khat in bangzah thuakzawhna a kisam thei hiam hong sin sak hi.

records.english: Would you have ordered the fish if you had known how big it was?
records.zomi: A lian dan na theih leh nga na ngen ding hiam?

records.english: We ordered early so that we could catch the last bus home.
records.zomi: Inn ciahna bus nunung i tuan theih nadingin ma-in i ngen hi.

records.english: My cousin always ordered an extra portion of rice to take home for her dog.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu in a ui adingin inn ah tawi dingin buh behlap a ngen tawntung hi.

records.english: I do want to host the whole family next New Year, even if the house is small.
records.zomi: Inn a neu hangin a zom Kum Thak ah innkuan bup ka mak ding ka deih taktak hi.

records.english: My uncle carved a wooden spoon for every guest who stayed more than a week.
records.zomi: Kal khat sangin sawt zawin a om khual khempeuh adingin ka pa neu in sing kawm a khek hi.

records.english: We moved into the kitchen so that the visiting family could have the two bedrooms.
records.zomi: Veh khual innkuan in inndei nih a neih theih nadingun an huanna ah i kitawn hi.

records.english: Remind me to write to the bookseller's family this winter.
records.zomi: Hih khuavot in laibu zuakpa' innkuan kiangah lai gelh dingin hong phawksak in.

records.english: Looking after guests was the one task my grandmother never handed to anyone else.
records.zomi: Khualte kem pen ka pi in mi dang a piak ngei loh nasep khat bek ahi hi.

records.english: When our courtyard was full of wedding guests, we children slept on the flat roof under the stars.
records.zomi: I inn huan mopawi khualte tawh a dim ciangin naupangte in aksi nuai ah innkhum phei tungah i ihmu hi.

records.english: Please don't tell our visitors that the cake is from the shop.
records.zomi: Cake zuakna inn pan ahi hi, cih i khualte kiangah gen kei in.

records.english: Were you allowed to eat with the guests when you were small?
records.zomi: Na neu lai-in khualte tawh an na ne thei hiam?

records.english: We were told never to sit down before the guests had taken their seats.
records.zomi: Khualte a tut ma-un tu ngei lo dingin hong kigen hi.

records.english: The traveling bookseller's visit is the reason I became a teacher.
records.zomi: Khualzin laibu zuakpa' veh hang-in saya ka suak hi.

records.english: What I remember most about those visits is how late the adults stayed up talking.
records.zomi: Tua vehnate thu ah ka phawk pen pen mi upate thu kikum-in bangzah sawt a khanglawh uh hiam cih ahi hi.

records.english: How did your family manage when thirty relatives came for the festival?
records.zomi: Pawi adingin sanggam sawm thum a hong ciangin na innkuan in bangci-in a bawl uh hiam?

records.english: Everyone brought a blanket and a dish, and we simply squeezed together.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh in puannak khat leh an khat ciat a tawi uh a, i kinai tawm-in i om hi.

records.english: May I offer you some more tea before you go?
records.zomi: Na pai ma-in tea behlap kong pia thei ding hiam?

records.english: Why did your mother always cook more than the guests could eat?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na nu in khualte' nek zawh sangin a tam zaw a huan tawntung hiam?

records.english: You're welcome to stay as long as the rain lasts.
records.zomi: Guah a zuk sung teng na om thei hi.

records.english: Instead of a guest book, my aunt asked every visitor to sign the kitchen wall.
records.zomi: Khual laibu sangin ka ni in khual khempeuh an huanna bang ah a min gelh dingin a ngen hi.

records.english: If the guest had stayed any longer, he could have voted in our village election.
records.zomi: Khual sawt zawin om le i khua teelna ah a teel thei kha ding hi.

records.english: We might have hosted the wedding at a hall, but my grandmother wanted it at home.
records.zomi: Kikhopna inn ah mopawi i bawl kha ding hi, ahi zongin ka pi in inn ah a deih hi.

records.english: Our dog always slept at the feet of whichever guest had arrived most recently.
records.zomi: I ui in a tung nunung pen khual' khe kiang ah a ihmu tawntung hi.

records.english: My grandfather always offered guests the best seat, the one closest to the fire.
records.zomi: Ka pu in khualte tutna hoih pen, mei kiang pen a pia tawntung hi.

records.english: One old visitor refused just as politely, and the two of them argued about it for half an hour.
records.zomi: Veh khual upa khat in zahtak takin a nial a, a nih in nai kim sung tua thu a kinial uh hi.

records.english: In the end, they both sat on the bench by the door, and the best seat stayed empty all evening.
records.zomi: A tawp-in a nih in kongkhak kiang-a tutphah tungah a tu uh a, tutna hoih pen nitak bup a om ngawng hi.

records.english: Some guests arrive as strangers and leave as part of the family.
records.zomi: Khual pawl khat theih loh mi bangin a tung uh a, innkuan mi bangin a pai uh hi.

records.english: Where did the guests sleep in your old house?
records.zomi: Na inn lui ah khualte koi ah a ihmu uh hiam?

records.english: When did you first host a meal on your own?
records.zomi: Bang ciangin nangma bek-in an nekna na bawl masa hiam?

records.english: If my brother hadn't given up his bed, our aunt would have slept on the sofa.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in a lupna a nusia kei le i ni in sofa tungah a ihmu ding hi.

records.english: The guests were allowed to choose the music, even when we hated it.
records.zomi: I huat hangin khualte in la a teel thei uh hi.

records.english: Hosting so many visitors taught us children to share without being asked.
records.zomi: Khual tampi kem in naupangte kisawl lo-in hawm dingin hong sin sak hi.

records.english: The best seat by the fire is still empty in my memory of that evening.
records.zomi: Tua nitak ka phawkna ah mei kiang-a tutna hoih pen a om ngawng lai hi.

records.english: What did your grandparents give guests when they left?
records.zomi: Na pu leh pite in khualte a pai ciangin bang a pia uh hiam?

records.english: Do you remember the visitor who arrived on horseback?
records.zomi: Sakol tungah a tung khual na phawk hiam?

records.english: We children fed his horse so many carrots that it wouldn't leave the next morning.
records.zomi: Naupangte in a sakol carrot tampi i pia ahih manin a zing zingsang ciangin pai a nuam kei hi.

records.english: For my sister's engagement lunch, my mother borrowed plates from four different neighbors.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu' kiteenna ciamna sun an adingin ka nu in inn vengte li pan kuang a caih hi.

records.english: Afterwards, we spent an hour sorting them by pattern so that each family got its own back.
records.zomi: Tua khit ciangin innkuan khempeuh in amau' kuang a ngah kik nadingun a lim bangin nai khat sung i khen hi.

records.english: When I hosted my first dinner as a student, I owned exactly three plates.
records.zomi: Sangnaupang ka hih lai-in ka nitak an masa pen ka bawl ciangin kuang thum bek ka nei hi.

records.english: My six guests ate in two shifts and washed the plates between courses.
records.zomi: Ka khual guk te nih vei-in a ne uh a, an kikal ah kuang te a sil uh hi.

records.english: It was the noisiest, happiest evening that tiny flat ever saw.
records.zomi: Tua inndei neu in a muh ngei nitak ging tam pen, nuam pen ahi hi.

records.english: My cousin's friend came to stay with us for one night on his way to the coast.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam' lawm khat tuipi gei a pai lampi ah zan khat i kiang ah om dingin a hong hi.

records.english: Then the rains started, the road was closed, and he stayed until the end of the season.
records.zomi: Tua ciangin guah a zuk kipan a, lampi kikhak a, hun tawp dong a om hi.

records.english: Before he left, he mended every leak in our roof to say thank you.
records.zomi: A pai ma-in lungdam a cih nadingin i innkhum kua khempeuh a bawl dam hi.

records.english: Would you host a stranger the way your grandparents did?
records.zomi: Na pu leh pite bangin theih loh mi khat na kem ding hiam?

records.english: Who was the most memorable guest your family ever had?
records.zomi: Na innkuan in a neih ngei khual phawk pen kua hiam?

records.english: A traveling bookseller, who left every child in the house a book before he went.
records.zomi: Khualzin laibu zuakpa khat, a pai ma-in inn sung-a naupang khempeuh laibu khat ciat a nusia pa.

records.english: My mother said, "A guest's plate must never be empty, so watch it like a hawk."
records.zomi: Ka nu in, “Khual' kuang a ngawng ngei lo ding hi, tua ahih manin muvanlai bangin en in,” a ci hi.

records.english: I really did want our visitors to see the waterfall, but it rained every day.
records.zomi: I khualte in tui kia a muh nadingun ka deih taktak a, ahi zongin ni simin guah a zuk hi.

records.english: Did the horse ever come back?
records.zomi: Sakol a hong kik ngei hiam?

records.english: My parents never had much money, yet our home was always full of guests.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in sum tam a nei ngei kei uh a, ahi zongin i inn khualte tawh a dim tawntung hi.

records.english: One summer, a guest of ours sang every evening after dinner.
records.zomi: Khal khat in i khual khat in nitak an khit simin la a sa hi.

records.english: By the third night, half the street was sitting on our wall to listen.
records.zomi: Zan thumna ciangin lampi a kim in ngai dingin i bang tungah a tu uh hi.

records.english: Can you guess how many people slept in our house that festival?
records.zomi: Tua pawi lai-in i inn ah mi bangzah a ihmu uh hiam na ngaihsun thei ding hiam?

records.english: My brother cooked his famous fish stew for the visitors from the city.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in khuapi pan hong veh khualte adingin a min thang nga an tui a huan hi.

records.english: I drove our guests to the station at dawn so that they wouldn't miss the early train.
records.zomi: Zingsang meileng a kiat lohna dingun khuavak ciangin i khualte meileng dinna ah ka tawi hi.

records.english: My little brother was asked to give up his bed for our aunt.
records.zomi: I ni adingin ka nau pasal in a lupna nusia dingin kingen hi.

records.english: He agreed, but he made a sign that said "Borrowed, not given."
records.zomi: A phal a, ahi zongin “Caih hi, piak hi lo” ci lai khat a gelh hi.

records.english: Our aunt laughed so much that she kept the sign for twenty years.
records.zomi: I ni in a nuih lua ahih manin tua lai kum sawm nih sung a kem hi.

records.english: My mother sewed new curtains for the guest room before her old teacher came to stay.
records.zomi: A saya lui hong om ding ma-in ka nu in khual inndei adingin tukvuang puan thak a khui hi.

records.english: Shall we put the old wall with the guests' names on it in a photo album?
records.zomi: Khualte' min a om bang lui pen lim laibu ah i koih ding hiam?

records.english: Whoever came through our door, my mother treated them as though they were royalty.
records.zomi: Kua peuh i kongkhak ah a lut zongin ka nu in kumpi bangin a kem hi.

records.english: Once the guests had gone, the house always seemed far too quiet.
records.zomi: Khualte a pai khit ciangin inn pen a daih lua tawntung bang hi.

records.english: My uncle shouted, "More chili!" every time a dish arrived at the table.
records.zomi: An khat dawhkan ah a tun simin ka pa neu in, “Malcha behlap!” ci-in a kiko hi.

records.english: Where did you first try food from another country?
records.zomi: Gamdang an koi ah na lim et masa hiam?

records.english: I saved the crispy edges of the rice for my brother, who loved them.
records.zomi: A deih mahmah ka sanggam pasal adingin buh kang awng te ka kem hi.

records.english: We weren't allowed to leave the table until we had tasted everything.
records.zomi: Bangkim i lim et mateng dawhkan pan i ding thei kei hi.

records.english: My cousin's fussiness about food turned out to be the beginning of a career.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam' an teel lua pen nasep khat kipatna a suak hi.

records.english: Not liking a dish at seven tells you very little about whether you'll like it at forty.
records.zomi: Kum sagih lai-a an khat na deih loh in kum sawm li ciangin na deih ding hiam cih tawmno bek hong hilh hi.

records.english: Under the table, my cousins and I used to feed our vegetables to the dog.
records.zomi: Ka sanggamte leh kei in dawhkan nuai ah i anteh te ui i pia ngei hi.

records.english: Our parents only found out when the dog started refusing its own food.
records.zomi: Ui in amah' an a nial kipat ciang bek i nu leh i pa in a thei uh hi.

records.english: We grew strawberries in the yard so that my sister would eat some fruit.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu in theigah tawmno a nek nadingin huan sungah strawberry i suan hi.

records.english: Eat slowly, and tell me honestly what you think.
records.zomi: Dai takin ne inla, bang na ngaihsun hiam man takin hong gen in.

records.english: I do want my son to taste his great-grandfather's favorite soup at least once.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in a pu-pi' deih pen an tui khatvei bek hi zongin a lim et ding ka deih taktak hi.

records.english: Would you try your grandfather's fermented fish if I made it?
records.zomi: Ka bawl leh na pu' nga thu na lim et ding hiam?

records.english: Which dish did your mother make only for you?
records.zomi: Na nu in nangma adingin bek an bang a bawl hiam?

records.english: My mother said, "One spoonful for every year of your age, and then you may stop."
records.zomi: Ka nu in, “Na kum khat ciat adingin kawm khat ciat, tua ciangin na khawl thei hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: Who would have guessed that the boy who hated fish would grow up to be a fisherman?
records.zomi: Nga a huat tangval nga man a suak ding hi, ci-in kua in a ngaihsun ding hiam?

records.english: For seventy years, my grandfather refused to try ice cream.
records.zomi: Kum sawm sagih sung ka pu in ice cream lim et a nial hi.

records.english: He said food should never be colder than the weather.
records.zomi: An pen huihkhua sangin a vot zaw ngei lo ding hi, a ci hi.

records.english: When he finally tasted it at his granddaughter's wedding, he asked for a second bowl before he had finished the first.
records.zomi: A tu nu' mopawi ah a tawp-in a lim et ciangin a masa a zawh ma-in a nihna a ngen hi.

records.english: A whole tray of cakes was eaten by the guests before we could even taste one.
records.zomi: Khat zong i lim et ma-in khualte in cake kuang khat bup a ne khin uh hi.

records.english: I really did think that carrots would help me see in the dark.
records.zomi: Carrot in mial sungah en theih nadingin hong huh ding hi, ci-in ka um taktak hi.

records.english: The bitter leaves were boiled three times before we children would eat them.
records.zomi: Naupangte in i nek ma-un a kha nah te thum vei kilouh hi.

records.english: Did your brother really stop hating fish after one afternoon?
records.zomi: Na sanggam pasal in nitak khat khit ciangin nga huat a khawl taktak hiam?

records.english: When my sister was four, she would only eat food that was shaped like a star.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu kum li a phak ciangin aksi bang a lim an bek a ne hi.

records.english: Our mother bought a little metal cutter and turned every sandwich and slice of melon into stars.
records.zomi: I nu in dal atna neu khat a lei a, moh leh mai khen khempeuh aksi bangin a bawl hi.

records.english: Years later, my sister admitted she had simply enjoyed watching her do it.
records.zomi: Kum tampi khit ciangin ka sanggam nu in a bawl a et a nopsak bek ahi hi, ci-in a pulak hi.

records.english: Sweets were forbidden before dinner, so we hid them in our socks.
records.zomi: Nitak an ma-in thei khum nek kiphal lo ahih manin i khetuam sungah i sel hi.

records.english: May I have the crust instead of the soft part?
records.zomi: A nem lam sangin a vun lam ka ngah thei ding hiam?

records.english: Whatever was on the table, my grandfather ate it slowly, as though it might be his last meal.
records.zomi: Dawhkan tungah bang om zongin ka pu in a an nunung pen ding bangin dai takin a ne hi.

records.english: The chili sauce was hidden on the top shelf so that the children couldn't reach it.
records.zomi: Naupangte' tun theih lohna dingin malcha tui pen van koihna tung pen ah kisel hi.

records.english: How did your mother get you to eat vegetables?
records.zomi: Na nu in anteh hong nesak dingin bangci-in a bawl hiam?

records.english: On a school trip to the mountains, I tasted sour pickled cabbage for the first time.
records.zomi: Sang pan mual lam khualzinna ah kawlmukbe thu thuk a lim ka et masa hi.

records.english: I liked it so much that the woman who made it gave me a jar to take home.
records.zomi: Ka deih lua ahih manin a bawl numei in inn ah tawi dingin bel khat hong pia hi.

records.english: My aunt kept a jar of plain biscuits for the children who couldn't bear her spicy cooking.
records.zomi: Ka ni in a an hai a ne zo lo naupangte adingin biscuit tavuan bel khat a kem hi.

records.english: Shall I make you the star-shaped sandwiches, just for old times' sake?
records.zomi: Hun lui phawkna-in aksi bang a lim moh kong bawl sak ding hiam?

records.english: Living abroad taught me that I missed the smells of home more than the tastes.
records.zomi: Gamdang ah om in inn lim sangin inn gim ka lungngai zaw hi, cih hong sin sak hi.

records.english: What changed my mind about spicy food was a single bowl of soup on a cold night.
records.zomi: An hai thu-a ka ngaihsutna a khek pen zan vot khat-a an tui kuang khat ahi hi.

records.english: Please pass the pickled cabbage before your uncle finishes it.
records.zomi: Na pa neu in a zawh ma-in kawlmukbe thu hong pia in.

records.english: When did you start liking bitter tea?
records.zomi: Bang ciangin lakphak kha na deih kipan hiam?

records.english: If my uncle hadn't taken him fishing, my brother might still be refusing fish today.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in nga man dingin a pi kei le ka sanggam pasal in tu dong nga a nial lai kha ding hi.

records.english: My mother added honey to the medicine to make it easier for us to swallow.
records.zomi: Ka nu in i dawn baih nadingin zatui sungah khuaizu a koih hi.

records.english: Did anyone in your family grow up to love a food they once refused?
records.zomi: Na innkuan ah a nial ngei an a khan ciangin a deih mi a om hiam?

records.english: My cousin, who now works as a chef and cooks dishes he wouldn't touch as a boy.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam, tu-in an huanpa-in a sem a, tangval a hih lai-in a khoih ngei loh an te a huan pa.

records.english: Do you remember swapping lunches with Mai every day at school?
records.zomi: Sang ah ni simin Mai tawh sun an i kilaih na phawk hiam?

records.english: She loved my mother's fried rice, and I was fascinated by her cheese sandwiches.
records.zomi: Ka nu' buh kang a deih mahmah a, kei in a cheese moh ka lamdang sa mahmah hi.

records.english: Swapping lunches with Mai taught me more about her family than any conversation could.
records.zomi: Mai tawh sun an kilaih in kikupna khempeuh sangin a innkuan thu tam zaw hong sin sak hi.

records.english: When my uncle came home after ten years abroad, all he wanted for a month was plain rice.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu kum sawm gamdang ah a om khit ciangin inn a tun ciangin kha khat sung buh tavuan bek a deih hi.

records.english: Why did your grandfather think ice cream was dangerous?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na pu in ice cream lauhuai hi, a ci hiam?

records.english: My little brother refused to eat fish for years.
records.zomi: Ka nau pasal in kum tampi sung nga ne a nial hi.

records.english: Then our uncle took him to the river, and he caught a small one on his own.
records.zomi: Tua ciangin i pa neu in gun ah a pi a, amah mah in nga neu khat a man hi.

records.english: He ate every bite of it that evening and announced that fish was now his favorite food.
records.zomi: Tua nitak in a vekpi a ne a, tu-in nga pen a deih pen an ahi hi, ci-in a pulak hi.

records.english: Instead of forcing us to eat, my mother simply ate the food herself and looked delighted.
records.zomi: Ne dingin hong kisawl sangin ka nu in an amah mah in a ne a, a kipak bangin a om hi.

records.english: What did you refuse to eat when you were little?
records.zomi: Na neu lai-in bang ne dingin na nial hiam?

records.english: Mushrooms, because I was sure they were poisonous, even the ones from the market.
records.zomi: Ngakhuai, zuakna mun-a te zong gu a nei hi, ci-in ka um ahih manin.

records.english: Once I tasted my friend's mother's cooking, I understood why she never ate school lunches.
records.zomi: Ka lawm' nu' an huan ka lim et khit ciangin bang hangin sang sun an a ne ngei kei hiam ka thei hi.

records.english: Have you ever been tricked into eating something you hated?
records.zomi: Na huat an khat nek dingin hong khem ngei uh hiam?

records.english: It amazes me now how many foods I refused before I had even tasted them.
records.zomi: Ka lim et ma-in an bangzah ka nial hiam tu-in ka lamdang sa hi.

records.english: Our teacher told us, "Never laugh at what someone else has in their lunch box."
records.zomi: I saya in, “Mi dang' sun an bawm sung-a om thu nuihsan ngei kei un,” hong ci hi.

records.english: Were you allowed to leave food on your plate?
records.zomi: Na kuang tungah an na nusia thei hiam?

records.english: Every festival, my two aunts argued about whether rice dumplings should be sweet or salty.
records.zomi: Pawi simin ka ni nih in buh dumpling khum ding hiam, al ding hiam, ci-in a kinial uh hi.

records.english: In the end, both kinds were made every year, and everyone ate both.
records.zomi: A tawp-in kum simin a nih kibawl a, mi khempeuh in a nih a ne uh hi.

records.english: Squeezed shoulder to shoulder around one table, we felt richer than we really were.
records.zomi: Dawhkan khat kiim ah liang kituah-in i kinai ciangin i hauh taktak sangin hau zaw bangin i kisa hi.

records.english: How old were you when you were first allowed to sit at the adults' table?
records.zomi: Mi upate' dawhkan ah tu dingin hong phal masak uh ciangin kum bangzah na hi hiam?

records.english: Thirteen, and I was so proud that I hardly said a word all evening.
records.zomi: Kum sawm leh thum, leh ka kipak lua ahih manin nitak bup kammal khat zong ka gen kik dek kei hi.

records.english: Have you kept the old tablecloth from our parents' house?
records.zomi: I nu leh i pa' inn pan dawhkan khuh puan lui na kem lai hiam?

records.english: The day before the New Year feast, the pig we had been fattening escaped from its pen.
records.zomi: Kum Thak ankuang ma ni-in i vak vok a huang pan a tai hi.

records.english: Half the village chased it through the gardens, shouting and slipping in the mud.
records.zomi: Khua a kim in huan sung ah a delh uh a, a kiko uh a, buan ah a kipalh uh hi.

records.english: It was finally caught in the schoolyard, and the feast went ahead with everyone telling the story.
records.zomi: A tawp-in sang huan ah kiman a, ankuang a om lai a, mi khempeuh in tua tangthu a gen uh hi.

records.english: At the end of every feast, my aunt stood up and said, "Next year, at my house!"
records.zomi: Ankuang khempeuh tawp ah ka ni a ding a, “A zom kum, ka inn ah!” a ci hi.

records.english: Our guests' shoes were soaked by the sudden rain on the way to the riverbank meal.
records.zomi: Gun gei an nekna i pai lampi ah guah thawlawh in i khualte' khedap a dik khin hi.

records.english: I really did think the pig was going to escape into the forest forever.
records.zomi: Vok pen gam sungah a tai mang tawntung ding hi, ci-in ka ngaihsun taktak hi.

records.english: The old cooking pots were scrubbed with sand at the river the day after every feast.
records.zomi: Ankuang khempeuh zom ni-in an huanna beel lui te gun ah piakneel tawh kinul hi.

records.english: Who carved the meat at your family feasts?
records.zomi: Na innkuan ankuang ah kua in sa a at hiam?

records.english: You may have a second helping once your grandfather has finished his first.
records.zomi: Na pu in a masa a zawh khit ciangin a nihna na la thei hi.

records.english: Tell your children about the year the table got stuck in the door.
records.zomi: Dawhkan kongkhak ah a kiat kum thu na ta te gen sak in.

records.english: Why did your family eat the New Year breakfast at midnight?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na innkuan in Kum Thak zingsang an zan laitak ah a ne uh hiam?

records.english: The last dumpling on the plate was left for whoever had traveled the farthest.
records.zomi: Kuang tung-a dumpling nunung pen gamla pen pan a hong peuhpeuh adingin kinusia hi.

records.english: We cooked the soft rice dish for my great-uncle, who had lost most of his teeth.
records.zomi: A ha a tamzaw a mangsuah ka pu neu adingin buh nem an i huan hi.

records.english: Instead of speeches, our family meals ended with everyone singing the same old song.
records.zomi: Thugen sangin i innkuan an nekna te mi khempeuh in la lui kibang a sak uh tawh a bei hi.

records.english: My brother drove for two days to bring our parents the fish they loved from the coast.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in i nu leh i pa' deih tuipi gei nga a tawi nadingin ni nih sung a mawng hi.

records.english: Did your uncles ever get the table through the door without a saw?
records.zomi: Na pa neute in vuai om lo-in dawhkan kongkhak pan a lut sak zo ngei uh hiam?

records.english: Which relative always arrived last at the festival meal?
records.zomi: Pawi an nekna ah na sanggam bang in a tung nunung tawntung hiam?

records.english: The festival rice was wrapped in banana leaves and buried under hot stones.
records.zomi: Pawi buh nahtang nah tawh kituam a, suang lum nuai ah kivui hi.

records.english: Do you think our grandchildren will still be passing the dishes to the left?
records.zomi: I tute in an te veilam ah a khin lai ding uh hi, na ci hiam?

records.english: Some traditions in our family began as accidents and simply refused to stop.
records.zomi: I innkuan ngeina pawl khat khial pan a kipan a, a khawl nuam kei hi.

records.english: Would the feast have felt the same without the pig chase?
records.zomi: Vok delhna om lo-in ankuang a kibang ding hiam?

records.english: It still makes me laugh to think of four grown men arguing with a table.
records.zomi: Mi upa li in dawhkan tawh a kinial uh ka ngaihsut ciangin tu dong ka nui hi.

records.english: One New Year's Eve, our bus home was so late that we arrived after midnight.
records.zomi: Kum Thak ma zan khat in i inn ciahna bus a nun lua ahih manin zan laitak khit ciangin i tung hi.

records.english: Too hungry to wait for morning, we cooked the New Year breakfast in the middle of the night.
records.zomi: Zingsang dong ngak dingin i gil a kial lua ahih manin zan laitakin Kum Thak zingsang an i huan hi.

records.english: Now we eat that breakfast at midnight every year, and the youngest children don't even know it began by accident.
records.zomi: Tu-in kum simin zan laitakin tua zingsang an i ne a, naupang neu pen te in khial-in a kipan hi, cih a thei kei uh hi.

records.english: Every year, the long family table got stuck in the narrow kitchen doorway.
records.zomi: Kum simin innkuan dawhkan sau pen an huanna kongkhak neu ah a kiat hi.

records.english: It took four uncles and, one year, a saw before it finally went through.
records.zomi: A tawp-in a lut ma-in pa neu li leh kum khat in vuai a kisam hi.

records.english: What made those meals special was not the food but the fact that nobody was missing.
records.zomi: Tua an nekna te a tuam sak pen an hi lo-in kuamah a om lo om lo ahi hi.

records.english: What did your family always cook for weddings?
records.zomi: Mopawi adingin na innkuan in bang a huan tawntung uh hiam?

records.english: A whole goat, stewed for a day with ginger and herbs from the hills.
records.zomi: Kel khat bup, mual tung pan siing leh an lim tawh ni khat sung kilouh.

records.english: I do want to keep the midnight breakfast going, even when my children have families of their own.
records.zomi: Ka ta te in amau' innkuan a neih uh ciangin zong zan laitak zingsang an kem ka deih taktak hi.

records.english: If the bus hadn't been late that year, we would never have started our strangest tradition.
records.zomi: Tua kum in bus a nun kei le i ngeina lamdang pen i kipan ngei lo ding hi.

records.english: My aunt's famous stew was knocked over by the dog the year it was invited inside.
records.zomi: Ka ni' a min thang an tui pen ui sung lut dingin a kisam kum in ui in a lehlap hi.

records.english: Our first meal in the new house was eaten on the floor among the boxes.
records.zomi: Inn thak-a i an nekna masa pen bawm te kikal ah inn phah tungah i ne hi.

records.english: We turned a packing box upside down for a table and used saucepans as bowls.
records.zomi: Bawm khat dawhkan-in i lehkhia a, bel neute kuang-in i zang hi.

records.english: My mother said it was the finest dinner the house would ever see.
records.zomi: Hih inn in a muh ngei ding nitak an hoih pen ahi hi, ci-in ka nu in a gen hi.

records.english: Nobody was to touch the festival cakes before the blessing.
records.zomi: Thupha ngetna ma-in kuamah in pawi cake a khoih ding hi lo hi.

records.english: Were children allowed to talk during the family meal?
records.zomi: Innkuan an nekna ah naupangte in thu a gen thei uh hiam?

records.english: Only after the eldest had spoken, and only if we had something useful to say.
records.zomi: A upa pen a gen khit ciang bek, leh gen ding phattuam i neih leh bek.

records.english: My mother's best bowl was cracked when the table finally squeezed through the door.
records.zomi: Dawhkan a tawp-in kongkhak pan a lut ciangin ka nu' kuang hoih pen a kek hi.

records.english: Shall we invite the neighbors who chased the pig to next year's feast?
records.zomi: Vok a delh inn vengte a zom kum ankuang ah i sam ding hiam?

records.english: In our family, the dishes were always passed to the left, so the youngest got the last spoonful.
records.zomi: I innkuan ah an te veilam ah kipia tawntung ahih manin a neu pen in kawm nunung a ngah hi.

records.english: Once my cousin had cooked that festival meal, nobody ever treated her as a child again.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu in tua pawi an a huan khit ciangin kuamah in naupang bangin a en nawn kei uh hi.

records.english: Every family meal, however simple, felt like a small celebration of being together.
records.zomi: Innkuan an nekna khempeuh bangzah in neu zongin khawm-in i omna pawi neu bang ahi hi.

records.english: The year the adults all caught the flu, my cousin cooked the festival meal by herself.
records.zomi: Mi upate khempeuh in hawm a tuah kum in ka sanggam nu in amah bek in pawi an a huan hi.
