records.english: She was only sixteen and had never made more than an omelette.
records.zomi: Kum sawm leh guk bek a hi a, aktui kang sangin a tam zaw a huan ngei kei hi.

records.english: The rice was a little hard, but the uncles praised every dish as if it were perfect.
records.zomi: Buh tawmno a khauh a, ahi zongin pa neute in an khempeuh a kicing bangin a phat uh hi.

records.english: We weren't allowed to start eating until everyone had been served.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh an a ngah mateng nek i kipan thei kei hi.

records.english: Where did everyone sit when the house was full?
records.zomi: Inn a dim ciangin mi khempeuh koi ah a tu uh hiam?

records.english: Whoever cooked the main dish was excused from washing up for the rest of the festival.
records.zomi: An lian a huan peuhpeuh pawi a bei dong kuang sil a kisam kei hi.

records.english: The children made paper crowns for every guest at my parents' anniversary dinner.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa' kiteenna kum tawpna nitak an ah naupangte in khual khempeuh adingin laidal lukhu a bawl uh hi.

records.english: After the harvest, we ate together on the riverbank under a shelter made of bamboo.
records.zomi: Kaihawl khit ciangin gun gei ah gua tawh kibawl tauna nuai ah khawm-in an i ne hi.

records.english: When did your family stop eating from one shared pot?
records.zomi: Bang ciangin na innkuan in beel khat mah pan an nek a khawl uh hiam?

records.english: My uncle always said, "Eat first, argue later."
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in, “Ne masa unla, a nung ciangin kinial un,” a ci tawntung hi.

records.english: Please don't put your elbows on the table when the elders are eating.
records.zomi: Upate an a nek laitakun dawhkan tungah na khiu koih kei in.

records.english: A new tablecloth was sewn for the feast every ten years.
records.zomi: Kum sawm simin ankuang adingin dawhkan khuh puan thak kikhui hi.

records.english: May I join the choir even though I've only just arrived?
records.zomi: Tu-a ka tun bek ahi hangin la pawl ah ka kihel thei ding hiam?

records.english: My parents still keep our house in the village, in case any of us want to return.
records.zomi: Kua peuh i ciah kik nop leh ci-in ka nu leh ka pa in khua-a i inn a kem lai uh hi.

records.english: Rather than losing our traditions, many families abroad have found new ways to keep them alive.
records.zomi: I ngeinate mansuah sangin gamdang-a innkuan tampi in a nungta nadingin lampi thak a mu uh hi.

records.english: Do your children speak our language?
records.zomi: Na ta te in i pau a zang uh hiam?

records.english: They understand it well, but they usually answer in the local language.
records.zomi: Hoih takin a thei uh a, ahi zongin a tamzaw-in gam pau tawh a dawng uh hi.

records.english: How did you find the Zomi community when you first moved here?
records.zomi: Hih ah na hong masak ciangin Zomi mipi bangci-in na mu hiam?

records.english: Last summer, my daughter visited the village where I grew up for the first time.
records.zomi: Khal kum nung in ka tanu in ka khanna khua a veh masa hi.

records.english: She had only seen it in photos and heard about it in my stories.
records.zomi: Lim tungah bek a mu a, ka tangthu te sungah bek a za hi.

records.english: When she came back, she asked me to teach her the songs her grandmother had sung to her.
records.zomi: A ciah kik ciangin a pi in a sak sak la te sin sak dingin hong ngen hi.

records.english: Is there a Zomi church in the city where you live?
records.zomi: Na omna khuapi ah Zomi pawlpi a om hiam?

records.english: Yes, and the service is in our own language every Sunday.
records.zomi: Om hi, leh Nipini simin pawlpi kikhopna i pau mah tawh kibawl hi.

records.english: Whatever country we live in, our church remains the center of our community life.
records.zomi: Gam bang ah i om zongin i pawlpi pen i mipi nuntakna laizang ahi lai hi.

records.english: Could you help me send this parcel to my mother before the holidays?
records.zomi: Nopsakna hun ma-in hih thuamhual ka nu kiangah khak dingin hong huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Can I bring my friends to the community picnic?
records.zomi: Mipi khualzin an nekna ah ka lawmte ka tawi thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, they're welcome, and tell them to bring their appetite.
records.zomi: Tawi thei hi, kimuak uh a, a gilkial-in hong pai dingin gen sak in.

records.english: Growing up between two cultures has taught my children to move easily between different worlds.
records.zomi: Ngeina nih kikal ah khanna in ka ta te leitung tuamtuam kikal ah baih takin a pai theih nadingin a sin sak hi.

records.english: When did your brother move abroad for work?
records.zomi: Bang ciangin na sanggam pasal nasep dingin gamdang ah a pai hiam?

records.english: Is it possible to watch the service online if we can't come in person?
records.zomi: Mimal-in i hong theih kei leh online tawh kikhopna i en thei ding hiam?

records.english: Our weekend language class helps children who were born abroad learn to read and write in our language.
records.zomi: I kal tawp pau sinna in gamdang-a suak naupangte i pau sim leh gelh a sinsak hi.

records.english: Children, sit together at the front so that you can see the dancers.
records.zomi: Naupangte, lamte na muh theih nadingun a ma lam ah khawm-in tu un.

records.english: The church helps new families find a place to live.
records.zomi: Pawlpi in innkuan thakte omna mun a zon a huh hi.

records.english: The young people asked whether they could perform a modern dance at the festival, and the elders agreed.
records.zomi: Khangnote in pawi ah tulai lam a lam thei ding hiam a dong uh a, upate in a phal uh hi.

records.english: We cooked a traditional meal for the new family so that they would feel at home.
records.zomi: Innkuan thak in inn bangin a kisak nadingun ngeina an i huan sak hi.

records.english: However far apart we live, a wedding or a funeral brings relatives together from everywhere.
records.zomi: Bangzah in gamla-in i om zongin mopawi ahih kei leh mithi vuina in mun tuamtuam pan sanggamte a kikhawm sak hi.

records.english: We might visit our home village next year, if we can save enough.
records.zomi: I kikoih zawh leh a zom kum in i khua i veh kha ding hi.

records.english: When we first arrived, we didn't know anyone in the city.
records.zomi: I tun masak ciangin khuapi ah kuamah i thei kei hi.

records.english: On our second Sunday, a family from the Zomi church invited us home for lunch.
records.zomi: I Nipini nihna ah Zomi pawlpi pan innkuan khat in sun an adingin a inn uh ah hong sam uh hi.

records.english: By the end of the meal, we had a list of phone numbers and offers of help with everything.
records.zomi: An nekna a bei ciangin phone nambat tampi leh bangkim ah huh dingin hong ciamnate i nei hi.

records.english: My friend translated the school letters for families who were still learning the local language.
records.zomi: Gam pau a sin lai innkuante adingin ka lawm in sang lai te a let sak hi.

records.english: The more our children learn about their roots, the more confident they seem in both cultures.
records.zomi: I ta te in a bulpi uh thu a sin semsem ciangin ngeina nih ah a kimuan semsem bang uh hi.

records.english: Shall we call the cousins abroad after church on Sunday?
records.zomi: Nipini pawlpi khit ciangin gamdang-a sanggamte phone tawh i sam ding hiam?

records.english: My sister sends money home every month to help our parents.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu in i nu leh i pa a huh nadingin kha simin inn ah sum a khak hi.

records.english: Volunteers at the community center help older people fill in forms they can't read.
records.zomi: Mipi inn-a thalawpte in sim zo lo mi upate a lai gelh a huh uh hi.

records.english: The festival committee borrowed a sound system from the church so that everyone could hear the speeches.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh in thugen te a zak theih nadingun pawi kikhopna pawl in pawlpi pan ging setna a caih uh hi.

records.english: What I value most about our community abroad is that nobody faces hard times alone.
records.zomi: Gamdang-a i mipi ah ka manpha sak pen kuamah in hun haksa a kia-in a thuak kei uh hi, cih ahi hi.

records.english: Where can I buy the spices we use at home?
records.zomi: Inn-a i zat an lim te koi ah ka lei thei ding hiam?

records.english: Do you miss the food from home?
records.zomi: Inn-a an te na lungngai hiam?

records.english: Living far from home makes our gatherings feel even more precious.
records.zomi: Inn pan gamla-a om in i kikhopna te a manpha sak zaw semsem hi.

records.english: If our neighbors hadn't welcomed us so warmly, the first year abroad would have been much harder.
records.zomi: I inn vengte in lungsim nuam takin hong muak kei uh le gamdang-a kum masa pen a haksa zaw mahmah ding hi.

records.english: It took me years to feel at home abroad without feeling that I had left something behind.
records.zomi: Bangmah ka nusia kei hi, cih kisa lo-in gamdang ah inn bangin kisak dingin kum tampi hong sawt hi.

records.english: Everyone, please write your names on the list so that we can plan the meal.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh aw, an nekna i geel theih nadingin na min uh laidal tungah gelh un.

records.english: Who started the Zomi association in your city?
records.zomi: Na khuapi ah Zomi kipawlna kua in a kipat sak hiam?

records.english: A few families who arrived together, about fifteen years ago.
records.zomi: Kum sawm leh nga bang paisa-in khawm-in a tung innkuan pawl khat.

records.english: For many families, a weekly video call has become the closest thing to sitting together at one table.
records.zomi: Innkuan tampi adingin kal sim video call pen dawhkan khat ah khawm-a tut kiang pen a suak hi.

records.english: My uncle uses an online map to find Zomi families when he travels for work.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in nasep adingin a khualzin ciangin Zomi innkuante zon nadingin online map a zang hi.

records.english: When is the next community meeting?
records.zomi: A zom mipi kikhopna bang ciangin ahi hiam?

records.english: Whenever someone from home visits, the whole community gathers to hear the news.
records.zomi: Inn lam pan mi khat a hong ciangin mipi bup in thu za dingin a kikhawm uh hi.

records.english: By sharing recipes, songs, and stories online, people in different countries feel part of one community.
records.zomi: An huan dan, la leh tangthu te online ah kihawm-in gam tuamtuam-a mite in mipi khat ah a kihel bangin a kisa uh hi.

records.english: I'd like to find a Zomi family who could host my son while he studies in your city.
records.zomi: Ka tapa na khuapi ah a sin sung a om sak thei ding Zomi innkuan khat zon ka deih hi.

records.english: When my grandfather visited us abroad, he couldn't believe how cold the winters were.
records.zomi: Ka pu gamdang ah hong veh ciangin khuavot bangzah in a vot hiam a um zo kei hi.

records.english: Some people in our community have never been to the homeland of their parents.
records.zomi: I mipi-a mi pawl khat a nu leh a pa uh' gam ah a pai ngei kei uh hi.

records.english: My grandmother sends us dried vegetables in a parcel every winter.
records.zomi: Ka pi in khuavot simin thuamhual sungah anteh khal hong khak hi.

records.english: We use a video app to see our relatives in three different countries.
records.zomi: Gam tuamtuam thum-a i sanggamte i muh nadingin video app khat i zang hi.

records.english: My cousin met her husband at a Zomi youth camp abroad.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu in gamdang-a Zomi khangno kikhopna ah a pasal a kimu hi.

records.english: At my cousin's wedding, guests came from five different countries.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam' mopawi ah gam tuamtuam nga pan khualte a hong uh hi.

records.english: Our community holds a festival every year in the town hall.
records.zomi: I mipi in kum simin khuapi kikhopna inn ah pawi a bawl hi.

records.english: Keeping our language alive abroad depends largely on what parents speak at home.
records.zomi: Gamdang ah i pau a nungta nadingin nu leh pate in inn ah a zat pau tungah tampi a kinga hi.

records.english: Young people in our community organize a football tournament every summer.
records.zomi: I mipi-a khangnote in khal simin football kidemna a bawl uh hi.

records.english: My aunt and her family live overseas now.
records.zomi: Ka ni leh a innkuan tu-in gamdang ah a om uh hi.

records.english: Our family group chat is busy at all hours because everyone lives in a different time zone.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh hun kibang lo gam ah a om uh ahih manin i innkuan group chat hun khempeuh ah a buai hi.

records.english: Sometimes I felt sad for no reason at all, and that confused me as a child.
records.zomi: Khatvei khat hang om lo-in ka lungkham a, naupang ka hih lai-in tua in hong lungbuaisak hi.

records.english: What was the happiest day of your childhood?
records.zomi: Na naupan lai-a ni nuam pen bang ahi hiam?

records.english: Why did your grandfather cry at your sister's wedding?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na sanggam nu' mopawi ah na pu a kap hiam?

records.english: Do you remember running all the way home the day you passed your exams?
records.zomi: Na sitna na zawh ni-in inn dong na tai na phawk hiam?

records.english: My grandfather told us, "Don't waste a beautiful day being sad about yesterday."
records.zomi: Ka pu in, “Zanni thu lungkham-in ni hoih khat zang mang kei un,” hong ci hi.

records.english: I had to be brave for my little brothers the day our parents left to work abroad.
records.zomi: I nu leh i pa gamdang ah nasep dingin a pai ni-in ka nau pasalte adingin ka hang ding a kisam hi.

records.english: The year our family house was sold, I cried all the way to the city on the bus.
records.zomi: I innkuan inn kizuak kum in khuapi dong bus tungah ka kap hi.

records.english: An old woman across the aisle said nothing, but she handed me a sweet wrapped in paper.
records.zomi: Lampi gal lam-a numei upa khat in bangmah a gen kei a, ahi zongin laidal tawh kituam thei khum khat hong pia hi.

records.english: I don't remember the journey, but I still remember the taste of that sweet.
records.zomi: Khualzinna ka phawk kei hi, ahi zongin tua thei khum lim ka phawk lai hi.

records.english: An hour before my first concert, a string on my violin snapped.
records.zomi: Ka la pawi masa pen ma nai khat-in ka violin khau khat a tan hi.

records.english: I sat in the corridor and cried, sure that the evening was ruined.
records.zomi: Inn lampi sungah ka tu a, nitak a siat khin hi, ci-in ka kap hi.

records.english: My music teacher simply handed me her own violin and said, "Play it as if it were yours."
records.zomi: Ka la saya in amah' violin hong pia a, “Nangma' ahi bangin tum in,” a ci hi.

records.english: Were you sad to leave your first school?
records.zomi: Na sang masa na nusiat ciangin na lungkham hiam?

records.english: My sister's wedding dress was ruined by a sudden shower, but she laughed and danced anyway.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu' mopawi puan guah thawlawh in a susia a, ahi zongin a nui a, a lam hi.

records.english: Happiness, I've learned, often arrives in the smallest and least expected ways.
records.zomi: Nopna pen lampi neu pen leh ngaihsut loh pen tawh a hong tam hi, cih ka thei hi.

records.english: Did your family talk openly about sad things?
records.zomi: Na innkuan in lungkhamhuai thu te kician takin a kikum uh hiam?

records.english: Once the baby was born, the long years of waiting seemed to vanish.
records.zomi: Naungek a suah khit ciangin kum sawt ngakna a mang bang hi.

records.english: The news of my cousin's recovery was passed from house to house within an hour.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam' a dam thu nai khat sungin inn khat pan inn khat ah kipuak hi.

records.english: My cousin's impression of our headmaster made us laugh until our stomachs hurt.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam in i sang makaipa a lahna in i gil a na dong hong nuisak hi.

records.english: Watching my grandfather stand before my drawing, I understood how much he loved me.
records.zomi: Ka pu ka lim gelh ma-ah a din ka et ciangin bangzah in hong it hiam ka thei hi.

records.english: When my best friend moved away, we each planted a seedling from the same tree.
records.zomi: Ka lawm hoih pen a kitawn ciangin singkung khat mah pan a nau khat ciat i suan hi.

records.english: Hers grew faster, and she still sends me photos of it every spring.
records.zomi: Amah' a khang manlang zaw a, spring simin a lim hong khak lai hi.

records.english: My grandfather's face lit up when he saw all his grandchildren at the door.
records.zomi: A tute khempeuh kongkhak ah a muh ciangin ka pu' mai a vak hi.

records.english: Our old neighbor had barely smiled since his illness.
records.zomi: I inn vengpa upa a cina khit ciangin a nui kik dek kei hi.

records.english: Then my little niece told him a joke about a chicken, and he laughed until he had to sit down.
records.zomi: Tua ciangin ka tunu neu in ak thu nuihza thu khat a gen a, a tut ding a kisam dong a nui hi.

records.english: Who comforted you when you were sad as a child?
records.zomi: Na neu lai-in na lungkham ciangin kua in hong hehnem hiam?

records.english: My older brother, who would let me sleep in his room until I felt better.
records.zomi: Ka u pasal, ka lungsim a hoih kik mateng a inndei ah ihmu dingin hong phal pa.

records.english: Instead of crying when his friend moved away, my brother wrote him a letter every week.
records.zomi: A lawm a kitawn ciangin kap sangin ka sanggam pasal in kal simin lai a gelh hi.

records.english: Shall we plant a seedling in the new garden, the way you did with your friend?
records.zomi: Na lawm tawh na bawl bangin huan thak ah singkung nau khat i suan ding hiam?

records.english: When did you last laugh so hard that you cried?
records.zomi: Bang ciangin na kap dong na nui nunung hiam?

records.english: If my teacher hadn't lent me her violin, I would have missed my first concert.
records.zomi: Ka saya in a violin hong caih kei le ka la pawi masa pen ka kia kha ding hi.

records.english: It still surprises me how quickly a single kind gesture can change a terrible day.
records.zomi: Itna lahna khat bek in ni hoih lo khat bangzah in manlang takin a khek thei hiam tu dong ka lamdang sa hi.

records.english: The whole street was woken by the church bells ringing for a wedding.
records.zomi: Mopawi adingin pawlpi khawngging a ging ciangin lampi bup a phawng hi.

records.english: What I remember from that rainy afternoon is not the storm but my neighbor's smile.
records.zomi: Tua guah zuk nitak pan ka phawk huihpi hi lo-in ka inn vengnu' nuihna ahi hi.

records.english: You mustn't keep all your sadness inside, my uncle used to say.
records.zomi: Na lungkhamna khempeuh na sung ah na kem lo ding hi, ci-in ka pa neu in a gen ngei hi.

records.english: The old cherry tree in our yard was cut down, and it felt like losing a friend.
records.zomi: I huan sung-a cherry kung lui kiphuk a, lawm khat mansuah bang hi.

records.english: Would you like to see the drawing that won the prize?
records.zomi: Laksap a ngah lim gelh na et nuam hiam?

records.english: On the last evening of the harvest, the seasonal workers sang for us before they left.
records.zomi: Kaihawl nitak nunung pen ah hun sung nasem te in a pai ma-un hong la sak uh hi.

records.english: We had to say goodbye the next morning, and the farm felt empty for weeks.
records.zomi: A zing zingsang ciangin goodbye i ci ding a kisam a, kal tampi sung lo inn a ngawng bang hi.

records.english: Even now, the smell of rain on dry earth makes me happy.
records.zomi: Tu dong in lei khal tung-a guah gim in hong kipaksak hi.

records.english: Can you believe I cried at the end of a cartoon last week?
records.zomi: Kal nung in cartoon khat tawp ah ka kap hi, cih na um thei ding hiam?

records.english: Our teacher said, "Nobody laughs at anyone's tears in this classroom."
records.zomi: I saya in, “Hih sang inndei sungah kuamah in mi' mitthli a nuihsan kei ding hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: How long did the dry season last that year?
records.zomi: Tua kum in khuakhal hun bangzah sawt a om hiam?

records.english: Whatever sadness I felt about leaving home faded the day I made my first friend in the city.
records.zomi: Inn nusia thu-a ka lungkhamna khempeuh khuapi ah ka lawm masa pen ka neih ni-in a mang hi.

records.english: My little brother's sandcastle was washed away by one big wave, and he howled.
records.zomi: Ka nau pasal' piakneel inn tuiphu lian khat in a mut mang a, a kiko hi.

records.english: When I was nine, my drawing of our river won a children's competition.
records.zomi: Kum kua ka phak ciangin i gun ka lim gelh in naupang kidemna khat a zo hi.

records.english: It was put up in the window of the post office for a whole month.
records.zomi: Laikhak office tukvuang ah kha khat bup kikoih hi.

records.english: My grandfather walked into town every single day just to stand in front of it.
records.zomi: Ka pu in a mai ah ding bek dingin ni simin khuapi ah a pai hi.

records.english: Please don't tell my brother yet; I want to give him the news myself.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal tu-in gen nai kei in; keimah in thu ka gen ding ka deih hi.

records.english: The saddest goodbyes of my childhood were the ones I didn't know were goodbyes at the time.
records.zomi: Ka naupan lai-a kikhenna lungkhamhuai pen te tua hun lai-in kikhenna ahi hi, cih ka theih loh te ahi hi.

records.english: After months without rain, the first storm arrived late one afternoon.
records.zomi: Kha tampi guah om lo khit ciangin huihpi masa pen nitak khat ah a tung hi.

records.english: We children ran into the yard and danced until we were soaked through.
records.zomi: Naupangte in huan ah i tai a, i dik kim mateng i lam hi.

records.english: Even our serious old neighbor came out and stood with his face turned up to the sky.
records.zomi: I inn vengpa upa lungsim khauh zong a pusuak a, a mai van lam ah a dawh-in a ding hi.

records.english: Do you remember when Pau walked in on New Year's Eve without telling anyone?
records.zomi: Pau in kuamah hilh lo-in Kum Thak ma zan in a lut ciang na phawk hiam?

records.english: Nobody had seen him for five years, and his mother dropped a whole plate of dumplings.
records.zomi: Kum nga sung kuamah in a mu ngei kei uh a, a nu in dumpling kuang khat bup a kiatsak hi.

records.english: I'd give anything to hear my grandfather laugh like that again.
records.zomi: Ka pu tua bangin a nuih kik ka zak theih nadingin bangkim ka pia ding hi.

records.english: We needed to sell the old piano, but nobody wanted to be the one to say it.
records.zomi: Piano lui i zuak ding a kisam a, ahi zongin kuamah in gen nuam kei uh hi.

records.english: Remember to send Pau a message on New Year's Eve this year.
records.zomi: Hih kum Kum Thak ma zan ciangin Pau kiangah message khak dingin phawk in.

records.english: How did your parents react when your sister told them about the baby?
records.zomi: Na sanggam nu in naungek thu a gen ciangin na nu leh na pa in bangci-in a dawng uh hiam?

records.english: My father put down his spoon, stood up, and hugged everyone at the table, even the neighbor.
records.zomi: Ka pa in a kawm a koih a, a ding a, dawhkan-a mi khempeuh a kawi a, inn vengpa zong.

records.english: Why did your brother never tell you he was afraid of the dark?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na sanggam pasal in mial a lau hi, ci-in hong hilh ngei kei hiam?

records.english: Worrying about my daughter that afternoon taught me how my own parents must have felt.
records.zomi: Tua nitak ka tanu thu ka lungkham in ka nu leh ka pa bangci-in a kisa kha ding uh hiam hong sin sak hi.

records.english: Whatever I was afraid of as a child, my older sister always seemed to be afraid of it first.
records.zomi: Naupang ka hih lai-in bang ka lau zongin ka u nu in a lau masa tawntung bang hi.

records.english: Who did you go to when you were scared at night?
records.zomi: Zanin na lau ciangin kua kiangah na pai hiam?

records.english: Please don't tell anyone I was crying, I begged my brother.
records.zomi: Ka kap hi, cih kuamah hilh kei in, ci-in ka sanggam pasal ka ngen hi.

records.english: One evening, my brother didn't come back from fishing until long after dark.
records.zomi: Nitak khat in ka sanggam pasal mial khit sawt mahmah dong nga man pan a ciah kei hi.

records.english: We stood on the shore with lanterns, too worried to speak.
records.zomi: Meivak tawh tui gei ah i ding a, i lungkham lua ahih manin thu i gen zo kei hi.

records.english: He had stopped to help another boat whose engine had failed, and he couldn't understand why we were so upset.
records.zomi: Engine a sia long dang khat huh dingin a khawl a, bang hangin i lungkham lua uh hiam a thei kei hi.

records.english: Lying awake before my wedding, I counted every possible disaster and slept for barely an hour.
records.zomi: Ka mopawi ma-in ka ihmut theih loh lai-in buaina piang thei khempeuh ka sim a, nai khat bek dek ka ihmu hi.

records.english: When did you first travel alone?
records.zomi: Bang ciangin nangma bek-in na khualzin masa hiam?

records.english: What were you most afraid of as a child?
records.zomi: Na neu lai-in bang na lau pen hiam?

records.english: Thunder, and the long corridor to the toilet in my grandparents' house.
records.zomi: Van ging, leh ka pu leh ka pi' inn-a ek inn pai lampi sau.

records.english: The things I worried about most as a young man almost never actually happened.
records.zomi: Tangval ka hih lai-a ka lungkham pen te kik dekin a piang ngei kei hi.

records.english: My uncle said, "It's fine to be afraid, as long as you keep walking."
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in, “Na kalsuan lai teng na lau zongin a hoih hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: Were you nervous on your first day at work?
records.zomi: Na nasep ni masa pen ah na lau hiam?

records.english: Have you ever worried for a whole week about something that never happened?
records.zomi: A piang ngei lo thu khat kal bup sung na lungkham ngei hiam?

records.english: Courage, my uncle believed, was simply fear that had decided to keep walking.
records.zomi: Hanna pen kalsuan lai dingin a kithukhen launa bek ahi hi, ci-in ka pa neu in a um hi.

records.english: Instead of laughing at my fear, my grandfather walked with me past the well every morning.
records.zomi: Ka launa nuihsan sangin ka pu in zingsang simin tuikhuk kantan dingin hong zui hi.

records.english: Why were you so worried when your aunt's bus was late?
records.zomi: Na ni' bus a nun ciangin bang hangin na lungkham lua hiam?

records.english: It was six hours late, and it turned out the passengers had stopped to join a wedding by the road.
records.zomi: Nai guk a nung a, khualzinte in lampi kiang-a mopawi khat ah kihel dingin a khawl uh hi, cih kimu hi.

records.english: Do you remember forgetting your lines in the school play?
records.zomi: Sang lawng ah na gen ding na mangngilh na phawk hiam?

records.english: I froze completely until Lia whispered the next line from behind the curtain.
records.zomi: Lia in tukvuang puan nung pan a zom gen ding a suk mateng ka khawl kim hi.

records.english: The first time I guarded our rice field alone at night, I was twelve.
records.zomi: Kum sawm leh nih ka phak ciangin a masa pen-in zanin keimah bek in i buh lo ka kem hi.

records.english: Every rustle in the dark sounded like a tiger creeping toward me.
records.zomi: Mial sung-a ging khempeuh hong nai sawn ngiapi bang hi.

records.english: At dawn, I finally saw the culprit: a porcupine eating our corn.
records.zomi: Khuavak ciangin a bawlpa a tawp-in ka mu hi: i vaimim a ne sathu khat.

records.english: The bridge over the gorge was mended a year after I first crossed it on shaking legs.
records.zomi: Guam tung-a lei ka khe a ling-in ka kantan masak khit kum khat ciangin kibawl dam hi.

records.english: My heart was pounding as I knocked on the headmaster's door.
records.zomi: Sang makaipa' kongkhak ka kik laitakin ka lungtang a sat mahmah hi.

records.english: My grandfather's lantern was knocked over by the wind, and we were suddenly in total darkness.
records.zomi: Ka pu' meivak huih in a puk sak a, thawlawh takin mial bup sungah i om hi.

records.english: Every pupil was afraid of Mr. Kham, who never smiled in class.
records.zomi: Sang inndei sungah a nui ngei lo Pu Kham sangnaupang khempeuh in a lau uh hi.

records.english: When I broke my arm, he visited me at home with a bag of oranges and a joke book.
records.zomi: Ka ban a kitan ciangin sangtam ip khat leh nuihza thu laibu khat tawh ka inn ah hong veh hi.

records.english: As a boy, I was terrified of the old well at the edge of our village.
records.zomi: Tangval ka hih lai-in i khua tawp-a tuikhuk lui ka lau mahmah hi.

records.english: My grandfather tried to help by telling me a story about a friendly spirit who lived at the bottom.
records.zomi: Ka pu in a nuai pen ah a om kha hoih khat thu tangthu gen-in hong huh dingin a sin hi.

records.english: It had the opposite effect, and I walked the long way round for the next three years.
records.zomi: A ngaihsut lohna a piang a, kum thum sung lampi sau tawh ka pai hi.

records.english: Did your parents ever worry about you too much?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa in nangma thu a lungkham lua ngei uh hiam?

records.english: We were told never to go near the river after dark.
records.zomi: A mial khit ciangin gun kiang ah pai ngei lo dingin hong kigen hi.

records.english: It took me years to admit that my fear of the barber had been a little ridiculous.
records.zomi: Sam atpa ka lauhna a nuihza tawmno hi, cih pulak dingin kum tampi hong sawt hi.

records.english: What frightened me was not the dark itself but the stories my cousins told about it.
records.zomi: Hong lausak pen mial mah hi lo-in ka sanggamte in a gen tangthu ahi hi.

records.english: Don't go into the forest alone, my grandfather would say, or the wild pigs will find you.
records.zomi: Gam sungah kia-in pai kei in, gam vok te in hong mu ding hi, ci-in ka pu in a gen ngei hi.

records.english: We had to wait outside the clinic all night for news of my uncle.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu thu za dingin siavuan inn pua ah zan bup i ngak ding a kisam hi.

records.english: Does the old well still frighten you when you go home?
records.zomi: Inn na ciah ciangin tuikhuk lui na lau lai hiam?

records.english: My sister's kite was torn away by the wind, and she was sure it would land on someone's head.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu' leng-ngam huih in a mut tan a, mi khat' lu tungah a kia ding hi, ci-in a ngaihsun hi.

records.english: Once the calf was safely on its feet, we all laughed at how frightened we had been.
records.zomi: Bawngno a bit takin a ding khit ciangin i lauh dan i nuihsan hi.

records.english: Can you believe I was once scared of butterflies?
records.zomi: Khatvei pheipheh ka lau ngei hi, cih na um thei ding hiam?

records.english: I do want to be brave for my children, even when I'm worried inside.
records.zomi: Ka sung lam ah ka lungkham laitak zongin ka ta te adingin hang ka deih taktak hi.

records.english: Shall I walk you to the bus stop, since it's getting dark?
records.zomi: A mial ding ahih manin bus dinna dong kong zui ding hiam?

records.english: As a small child, I screamed every time the barber took out his razor.
records.zomi: Naupang neu ka hih lai-in sam atpa in a namsau a lak khiat simin ka kiko hi.

records.english: He eventually let me hold a comb so that I would keep still.
records.zomi: Ka om ding nadingin a tawp-in khui hong len sak hi.

records.english: I really did think that the porcupine was a tiger.
records.zomi: Sathu pen ngiapi ahi hi, ci-in ka um taktak hi.

records.english: Fear has a way of turning ordinary sounds into monsters at night.
records.zomi: Launa in zanin ging tavuan te dawi bang a suaksak thei hi.

records.english: The night before my wedding, I lay awake worrying that I would trip on the church steps.
records.zomi: Ka mopawi zan ma-in pawlpi kahlei tungah ka kipalh ding hi, ci-in ka lungkham-in ka ihmu zo kei hi.

records.english: Our little boat was pushed off course by a sudden gust, and we drifted for an hour.
records.zomi: I long neu huih thawlawh in a pai lam pan a sawn a, nai khat sung i kilei hi.

records.english: The village headman shouted, "Close your doors, everyone — the elephants are coming through!"
records.zomi: Khua hausa in, “Mi khempeuh na kongkhak uh khak un — sai te hong kantan ding hi!” ci-in a kiko hi.

records.english: When my daughter rode her bicycle to town alone for the first time, I waited at the gate for two hours.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in a masa pen-in amah bek-in siiksakol tawh khuapi ah a pai ciangin kongpi ah nai nih ka ngak hi.

records.english: She came back with a loaf of bread and couldn't understand why I looked so pale.
records.zomi: Moh khat tawh a ciah kik a, bang hangin ka mai a vom hiam a thei kei hi.

records.english: Imagine how the fishermen's wives felt every time the boats came home late!
records.zomi: Long te a ciah nun simin nga mante' zite bangci-in a kisa kha ding uh hiam ngaihsun in!

records.english: If Lia hadn't whispered my lines, I would have run off the stage.
records.zomi: Lia in ka gen ding hong suk kei le dawhsang pan ka tai khia ding hi.

records.english: Would you let your own son guard a field alone at night?
records.zomi: Na tapa mah zanin kia-in lo kem dingin na phal ding hiam?

records.english: I was so nervous before my speech that my knees were knocking.
records.zomi: Ka thugen ma-in ka lau lua ahih manin ka khuk a ling hi.

records.english: Our cow started calving in the middle of the night, and something seemed to be wrong.
records.zomi: I bawng in zan laitakin a nau a suak kipan a, bangmah khat a hoih lo bang hi.

records.english: We all held our breath until the calf finally stood up on its wobbly legs.
records.zomi: Bawngno a khe ling-in a tawp-in a din mateng i khempeuh in i hu i khawlsak hi.

records.english: Isn't it wonderful that the orange trees are still bearing fruit?
records.zomi: Sangtam kung te in a gah a suah lai, cih lamdang hi lo hiam?

records.english: When I joined the church choir at ten, the choirmaster put me in the very back row.
records.zomi: Kum sawm ka phak ciangin pawlpi la pawl ah ka kihel ciangin la makaipa in a nung pen ah hong koih hi.

records.english: Every week he said, "Louder, and with your heart," even though I was always slightly out of tune.
records.zomi: Kal simin, “Ging zaw in, na lungsim tawh,” a ci a, kei in ka sak dan tawmno a dik kei tawntung hangin.

records.english: A year later, he gave me my first solo, and I sang it without missing a note.
records.zomi: Kum khat khit ciangin keimah bek sak ding la masa pen hong pia a, khat zong khial lo-in ka sa hi.

records.english: Whatever the result, my grandfather always asked one question: "Did you try your best?"
records.zomi: A dawnna bang ahi zongin ka pu in, “Na hanciam thei tawp-in na hanciam hiam?” ci-in thu khat bek a dong tawntung hi.

records.english: Would you be willing to coach the younger runners next year?
records.zomi: A zom kum ciangin tai neu zawte sin sak ding na deih ding hiam?

records.english: What would you say to the boy at the back of the choir now?
records.zomi: Tu-in la pawl nung pen-a tangval kiangah bang na gen ding hiam?

records.english: When we volunteered to paint the village hall, none of us had ever held a paintbrush.
records.zomi: Khua kikhopna inn nul dingin thalawp-in i kipiak ciangin i lak-ah kuamah in rong nulna a len ngei kei hi.

records.english: The oldest man in the village watched us all day and said, "Not bad for beginners, not bad at all."
records.zomi: Khua-a upa pen in ni bup hong en a, “Sin thakte adingin a hoih, a hoih mahmah hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: Encouraged by my teacher's postcards, I applied for a place at the teachers' college.
records.zomi: Ka saya' laidal te in hong hasuah ahih manin saya sang ah mun khat ka ngen hi.

records.english: My father told me, "You don't have to be the best, only better than you were yesterday."
records.zomi: Ka pa in, “A hoih pen na hih ding a kisam kei hi, zanni-a na hih sangin a hoih zaw bek,” hong ci hi.

records.english: How did your sister become a tailor?
records.zomi: Na sanggam nu puan khuipa bangci-in a suak hiam?

records.english: She sewed clothes for the neighbors for free until she was good enough to open her own little shop.
records.zomi: Amah' zuakna inn neu a hon theih dong a siam mateng inn vengte adingin a man lo-in puan a khui hi.

records.english: Every New Year, my old teacher sent me a postcard with the same three words: "Keep going, always."
records.zomi: Kum Thak simin ka saya lui in kammal thum kibang tawh laidal khat hong khak hi: “Kalsuan in, tawntung.”

records.english: My brother's broken guitar was fixed by a neighbor so that he could play at the festival.
records.zomi: Pawi ah a tum theih nadingin ka sanggam pasal' guitar kitan inn vengpa khat in a bawl dam hi.

records.english: In the village race, I came last by nearly ten minutes.
records.zomi: Khua tai kidemna ah minit sawm dek in a nunung pen ka hi hi.

records.english: I wanted to stop, but I could hear people shouting my name from the finish line.
records.zomi: Khawl ka deih a, ahi zongin a tawpna gual pan mite in ka min a kiko uh ka za hi.

records.english: When I finally crossed it, the whole village was still there, clapping as if I had won.
records.zomi: A tawp-in ka kantan ciangin khua bup a om lai uh a, ka zo bangin khut a beng uh hi.

records.english: Plant one tree for every grandchild, and you'll never be forgotten, my grandfather used to say.
records.zomi: Tu khat ciat adingin singkung khat ciat suan in, kimangngilh ngei lo ding hi, ci-in ka pu in a gen ngei hi.

records.english: We cheered so loudly for my cousin that the referee told us to be quiet.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam adingin ging lua-in i kiko ahih manin thukhenpa in daih dingin hong hilh hi.

records.english: Shall I send a postcard to my own students this New Year?
records.zomi: Hih Kum Thak in ka sangnaupangte kiangah laidal khat ka khak ding hiam?

records.english: Who encouraged you to keep singing?
records.zomi: La sak lai dingin kua in hong hasuah hiam?

records.english: My choirmaster, who believed in my voice long before I did.
records.zomi: Ka la makaipa, keimah ka um ma-in ka aw a um pa.

records.english: What did your grandfather say when the neighbors laughed at his orange trees?
records.zomi: Inn vengte in na pu' sangtam kung te a nuihsan uh ciangin bang a ci hiam?

records.english: He just smiled and said that trees are planted for the people who come after us.
records.zomi: A nui bek a, singkung te i nung-a hong pai mite adingin kisuan hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Come on, all of you — just one more lap, and then we'll rest!
records.zomi: Hong pai un, na khempeuh un — kual khat bek behlap, tua ciangin i tawlnga ding hi!

records.english: Once I stopped comparing myself with others, I began to enjoy learning again.
records.zomi: Mi dangte tawh keimah ka kiteh khawl khit ciangin sinna ka nopsak kik hi.

records.english: My aunt wrote, "I'm proud of you," on a scrap of paper and tucked it into my suitcase.
records.zomi: Ka ni in laidal neu khat tungah, “Na tungah ka kipak hi,” a gelh a, ka van bawm sungah a koih hi.

records.english: Listen, everyone: nobody in this class is too old or too slow to learn.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh aw ngai un: hih sang inndei sungah kuamah sin dingin a upa lua hiam, a nawlkhin lua hiam om kei hi.

records.english: You're doing better than you think, my teacher whispered as she passed my desk.
records.zomi: Na ngaihsut sangin na hoih zaw hi, ci-in ka saya in ka dawhkan a kantan ciangin a suk hi.

records.english: Can you believe I almost didn't enter the race?
records.zomi: Tai kidemna ah ka kihel lo dek hi, cih na um thei ding hiam?

records.english: I really did believe I would never finish that race.
records.zomi: Tua tai kidemna ka zo ngei lo ding hi, ci-in ka um taktak hi.

records.english: I do want my children to know that failing once doesn't mean failing forever.
records.zomi: Khatvei sit in tawntung sit cihna hi lo hi, cih ka ta te in a theih ding ka deih taktak hi.

records.english: The postcards my teacher sent were small, but they carried me through some very difficult years.
records.zomi: Ka saya' a khak laidal te a neu a, ahi zongin kum haksa mahmah pawl khat sungah hong tawi hi.

records.english: Have you ever been cheered on by people you barely knew?
records.zomi: Na theih tawm mite in hong hasuah-in a kiko ngei uh hiam?

records.english: My uncle learned to ride a bicycle at fifty, and his grandchildren ran beside him cheering.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in kum sawm nga a phak ciangin siiksakol tuang a sin a, a tute in a kiang ah a tai uh a, a kiko uh hi.

records.english: He fell off twice, got back on, and rode all the way to the end of the lane.
records.zomi: Nih vei a kia a, a tuang kik a, lampi neu tawp dong a tuang hi.

records.english: Instead of telling me I was wrong, my teacher asked me to explain my answer again more slowly.
records.zomi: Na khial hi, ci-in hong hilh sangin ka saya in ka dawnna nawlkhin zawin gen kik dingin hong ngen hi.

records.english: Why did the choirmaster keep you in the choir?
records.zomi: Bang hangin la makaipa in la pawl ah hong kem hiam?

records.english: Our village school had no science laboratory at all.
records.zomi: I khua sang in science sinna inn khatpeuh a nei kei hi.

records.english: Our teacher built test tubes from old bottles and a microscope from a broken camera lens.
records.zomi: I saya in bel lui te tawh sinna setna a bawl a, camera mit kitan pan microscope a bawl hi.

records.english: One of his pupils from that tiny classroom is now an engineer at a big hospital.
records.zomi: Tua sang inndei neu pan a sangnaupang khat tu-in siavuan inn lian khat ah engineer ahi hi.

records.english: Were you tempted to give up during the race?
records.zomi: Tai kidemna lai-in khawl dingin na ngaihsun hiam?

records.english: Did your teacher ever find out that you became a teacher too?
records.zomi: Nangma zong saya na suak hi, cih na saya in a thei ngei hiam?

records.english: The old school was repainted by former pupils, and the children came back to brighter walls.
records.zomi: Sang lui pen a sangnaupang lui te in a nul kik uh a, naupangte bang vak zaw ah a hong kik uh hi.

records.english: If the choirmaster had sent me home, I would never have discovered how much I love singing.
records.zomi: La makaipa in inn ah hong ciahsak le la sak bangzah ka deih hiam ka thei ngei lo ding hi.

records.english: My grandfather planted twelve orange trees when he was already sixty-five.
records.zomi: Ka pu in kum sawm guk leh nga a phak khit ciangin sangtam kung sawm leh nih a suan hi.

records.english: The neighbors laughed and said he would never live to taste the fruit.
records.zomi: Inn vengte a nui uh a, a gah a lim et dong a nungta lo ding hi, a ci uh hi.

records.english: He did, for fifteen happy years, and now my son picks oranges from those same trees.
records.zomi: A nungta a, kum sawm leh nga sung a nuam hi, leh tu-in ka tapa in tua singkung mah pan sangtam a lo hi.

records.english: I was so encouraged by her note that I read it every morning for a month.
records.zomi: A laikhak in hong hasuah lua ahih manin kha khat sung zingsang simin ka sim hi.

records.english: A small bakery was opened by three women who had never run a business before.
records.zomi: Sumbawlna a kem ngei lo numei thum in moh bawlna neu khat a hon uh hi.

records.english: My confidence was badly shaken when I failed my first interview.
records.zomi: Ka kidotna masa pen ka sit ciangin ka kimuanna a kiam mahmah hi.

records.english: Our neighbor clapped every time my little sister managed a new word.
records.zomi: Ka nau nu in kammal thak khat a gen zawh simin i inn vengpa in khut a beng hi.

records.english: Encouragement from a stranger can sometimes reach us more deeply than praise from family.
records.zomi: Theih loh mi pan hasuahna in khatvei khat innkuan phatna sangin hong khoih thuk zaw thei hi.

records.english: Which teacher made the biggest difference in your life?
records.zomi: Saya bang in na nuntakna ah kilamdanna lian pen a bawl hiam?

records.english: My grandfather's orange trees were nearly killed by a hard frost one winter, but he planted new ones beside them.
records.zomi: Khuavot khat in khuhtui in ka pu' sangtam kung te a si dek sak a, ahi zongin a kiang ah a thak a suan hi.

records.english: What kept me going was not the finish line but the voices of the people waiting there.
records.zomi: Hong tawi lai pen a tawpna gual hi lo-in tua ah a ngak mite' aw ahi hi.

records.english: Seeing my uncle wobble down the lane on his bicycle gave the whole family courage to try new things.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu siiksakol tungah lampi neu ah a ling-in a pai i et ciangin innkuan bup in a thak sin dingin hanna i ngah hi.

records.english: How did your uncle feel after his first bicycle ride?
records.zomi: Na pa neu in a siiksakol tuang masak khit ciangin bangci-in a kisa hiam?

records.english: Planting those trees taught my grandfather's grandchildren the meaning of patience.
records.zomi: Tua singkung suan in ka pu' tute thuakzawhna hong sin sak hi.

records.english: We liked our eggs in completely different ways, so breakfast took forever.
records.zomi: I aktui deih dan a kibang lo kim ahih manin zingsang an a sawt mahmah hi.

records.english: At the animal shelter, my children could choose any dog they liked.
records.zomi: Ganhing kemna mun ah ka ta te in a deih peuhpeuh ui a teel thei uh hi.

records.english: They walked straight past the puppies and stopped in front of a grey old dog with one ear.
records.zomi: Ui neute a kantan pah uh a, bil khat bek nei ui upa san-ngoh khat mai ah a khawl uh hi.

records.english: He lived with us for six more years and slept at the foot of their bunk beds every night.
records.zomi: Kum guk behlap i kiang ah a nungta a, zan simin amau' lupna khe lam ah a ihmu hi.

records.english: Why did your sister love those red boots so much?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na sanggam nu in tua khedap sau san te a deih mahmah hiam?

records.english: My grandfather wrote everything with an old fountain pen.
records.zomi: Ka pu in bangkim khedal lui khat tawh a gelh hi.

records.english: When we gave him a box of ballpoint pens for his birthday, he used them to stir his tea.
records.zomi: A pianni-in khedal bawm khat i piak ciangin a tea kheh nadingin a zang hi.

records.english: Every letter I received from him had small ink blots in the corners, and I kept them all.
records.zomi: A kiang pan ka ngah laikhak khempeuh a kil ah laigelh tui mai neute a om a, ka kem vek hi.

records.english: When I was sixteen, I decided to grow my hair down to my shoulders.
records.zomi: Kum sawm leh guk ka phak ciangin ka sam ka liang dong a sau nadingin ka khui dingin ka thukhen hi.

records.english: My father complained for months, and then one day he admitted that it suited me.
records.zomi: Ka pa in kha tampi sung a phun a, tua ciangin ni khat in hong kilawm hi, ci-in a pulak hi.

records.english: My aunt drank tea only from her own chipped blue cup.
records.zomi: Ka ni in amah' haai dum kek bek pan tea a dawn hi.

records.english: She carried it in her handbag to weddings, funerals, and even to the doctor's.
records.zomi: Mopawi, mithi vuina, leh siavuan kiang ah zong a khut ip sungah a tawi hi.

records.english: My grandmother used a tiny pair of scissors to trim the edges of every photo she framed.
records.zomi: Ka pi in a kilh lim khempeuh a kiim at nadingin namtem neu mahmah khat a zang hi.

records.english: What I liked about my grandfather's letters was not the news but the ink blots.
records.zomi: Ka pu' laikhak te-a ka deih pen thu thak hi lo-in laigelh tui mai te ahi hi.

records.english: Our preferences as children often say more about who we will become than our school reports.
records.zomi: Naupang i hih lai-a i deih dan te in i sang laimal sangin kua i suak ding hiam a gen tam zaw hi.

records.english: When we moved to the new house, each of us was allowed to choose the color of our own room.
records.zomi: Inn thak ah i kitawn ciangin i khat ciat in amau' inndei rong a teel thei uh hi.

records.english: My youngest brother chose black, and to everyone's surprise, it looked wonderful with the stars he painted.
records.zomi: Ka nau pasal neu pen in a vom a teel a, mi khempeuh lamdang sak-in a nul aksi te tawh a kilawm mahmah hi.

records.english: My long hair was finally cut when I started my first job at the bank.
records.zomi: Bank ah ka nasep masa pen ka kipat ciangin ka sam sau a tawp-in kiat hi.

records.english: Why did your brother sleep on the floor when he had a bed?
records.zomi: Lupna a neih hangin bang hangin na sanggam pasal in inn phah tungah a ihmu hiam?

records.english: He said the mattress was too soft and that the floor helped him dream.
records.zomi: Lupna phah a nem lua a, inn phah in mang dingin a huh hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Our favorite picnic rock was washed smooth by years of rain and water.
records.zomi: I deih pen khualzin an nekna suangpi kum tampi guah leh tui in a nulsak nem hi.

records.english: Tell your sister she may borrow my boots, as long as she gives them back.
records.zomi: Na sanggam nu kiangah, a pia kik teng ka khedap sau te a caih thei hi, ci-in gen in.

records.english: Instead of following the fashion, my aunt dressed exactly as she pleased her whole life.
records.zomi: Mi ngeina zui sangin ka ni in a nuntak sung a deih bangin puan a silh hi.

records.english: When did you start liking spicy food?
records.zomi: Bang ciangin an hai na deih kipan hiam?

records.english: The red boots were finally thrown away when my sister wasn't looking.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu a et loh laitakin khedap sau san te a tawp-in kipaih hi.

records.english: Shall I give you my grandfather's pen, since you write more letters than I do?
records.zomi: Kei sangin lai tam zaw na gelh ahih manin ka pu' khedal kong pia ding hiam?

records.english: When my sister was five, she was given a pair of shiny red boots.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu kum nga a phak ciangin khedap sau san tang khat a kipia hi.

records.english: She wore them every single day for a year, even in the hottest weeks of summer.
records.zomi: Kum khat sung ni khempeuh in a silh a, khal kal lum pen te sungah zong.

records.english: By the end, the toes had been cut open so that her feet could still fit inside.
records.zomi: A tawp ciangin a khe a lut theih lai nadingin a khezung lam kihawng hi.

records.english: Can you believe my brother ate his rice with a teaspoon for years?
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in kum tampi sung kawm neu tawh buh a ne hi, cih na um thei ding hiam?

records.english: I do want my daughter to choose her own clothes, even if she picks the strangest ones.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in a lamdang pen a teel zongin amah' puan amah in a teel ding ka deih taktak hi.

records.english: A cup of her own made my aunt feel at home wherever she went.
records.zomi: Amah' haai khat in ka ni koi ah a pai zongin inn bangin a kisaksak hi.

records.english: Which was your favorite hiding place as a child?
records.zomi: Na neu lai-in na kiselna mun deih pen koi ahi hiam?

records.english: Where did your family go for picnics?
records.zomi: Na innkuan in khualzin an nekna adingin koi ah a pai uh hiam?

records.english: Always to the same flat rock beside the waterfall, and nobody ever suggested anywhere else.
records.zomi: Tui kia kiang-a suangpi phei kibang mah ah tawntung, leh kuamah in mun dang a gen ngei kei uh hi.

records.english: Once my father accepted my long hair, he started giving me advice about shampoo.
records.zomi: Ka pa in ka sam sau a phal khit ciangin sam sil sathau thu-in thuhilhna hong pia kipan hi.

records.english: Looking at the black walls with painted stars, I realized that my brother had always seen the world differently.
records.zomi: Aksi kinul bang vom te ka et ciangin ka sanggam pasal in leitung a kibang lo-in a mu tawntung hi, cih ka thei hi.

records.english: Right, everyone, choose a corner of the garden, and that will be your own patch to plant.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh aw, huan sung-a kil khat ciat teel un, tua pen na suan ding mun uh ahi ding hi.

records.english: Who in your family had the strangest habits?
records.zomi: Na innkuan ah kua in ngeina lamdang pen a nei hiam?

records.english: Listen, all of you: whoever picks the music tonight has to dance first.
records.zomi: Na khempeuh un ngai un: tu zanin la a teel peuhpeuh in a lam masa ding hi.

records.english: Was your grandfather's handwriting easy to read?
records.zomi: Na pu' laigelh sim a baih hiam?

records.english: Would you rather have a puppy or an old dog that needs a home?
records.zomi: Ui neu hiam, inn a kisam ui upa hiam, bang na deih zaw hiam?

records.english: Our old bicycle was painted three different colors because none of us could agree.
records.zomi: I kuamah i kilem kei ahih manin i siiksakol lui rong tuamtuam thum tawh kinul hi.

records.english: My cousin always cut his sandwiches with a ruler so that the halves were exactly equal.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam in a khen nih kibang taktak nadingin a moh teh-na tawh a at tawntung hi.

records.english: Choosing the oldest dog at the shelter taught my children something about kindness.
records.zomi: Ganhing kemna mun-a ui upa pen teel in ka ta te itna thu khat hong sin sak hi.

records.english: Do you still take the slow train when you visit the city?
records.zomi: Khuapi na veh ciangin meileng nawlkhin na tuang lai hiam?

records.english: I always chose the last seat on the school bus because I liked watching the road disappear.
records.zomi: Lampi a mang ka et a nop manin sang bus-a tutna nunung pen ka teel tawntung hi.

records.english: Did you ever wish you had grown up somewhere else?
records.zomi: Mun dang khat ah ka khang hileh, ci-in na deih ngei hiam?

records.english: Whatever the weather, my sister insisted on walking to school by the longest path.
records.zomi: Huihkhua bang ahi zongin ka sanggam nu in lampi sau pen tawh sang ah pai dingin a ngen tawntung hi.

records.english: I really did prefer that old dog to any of the puppies.
records.zomi: Ui neute khempeuh sangin tua ui upa ka deih zaw taktak hi.

records.english: My uncle always chose the slowest train to the city, even when he was in a hurry.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in a manlang ding a kisam lai zongin khuapi lam meileng nawlkhin pen a teel tawntung hi.

records.english: He said the fast train went through tunnels, while the slow one went along the river.
records.zomi: Meileng manlang in kua sungah a pai a, a nawlkhin in gun gei ah a pai hi, a ci hi.

records.english: He arrived late to almost everything, but he never once regretted the view.
records.zomi: Bangkim dek ah a tung nunung a, ahi zongin a muh mun te adingin khatvei zong a lungkham ngei kei hi.

records.english: Some of my family's strangest preferences have become the stories we love telling most.
records.zomi: Ka innkuan deih dan lamdang pen pawl khat i gen nuam pen tangthu a suak hi.

records.english: What did you like doing most when you were a teenager?
records.zomi: Khangno na hih lai-in bang bawl na deih pen hiam?

records.english: If my uncle had taken the fast train, he would never have met the woman he married.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in meileng manlang a tuan le a zi suak numei a kimu ngei lo ding hi.

records.english: Why did your uncle love the slow train so much?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na pa neu in meileng nawlkhin a deih mahmah hiam?

records.english: My aunt's blue cup was cracked in two, but she glued it back together with great care.
records.zomi: Ka ni' haai dum khen nih-in a kek a, ahi zongin limtakin a kilh kik hi.

records.english: The black walls were repainted when we sold the house, and my brother refused to watch.
records.zomi: Inn i zuak ciangin bang vom te kinul kik a, ka sanggam pasal in en a nuam kei hi.

records.english: My grandfather's fountain pen was handed down to me after he died.
records.zomi: Ka pu' khedal lui pen a sih khit ciangin kei hong kipia hi.

records.english: Is it true that, in Genesis, people were made on the sixth day?
records.zomi: Piancilna sungah mite ni guk ni-in kibawl hi, cih a man hiam?

records.english: Our church teaches that men and women are equally made in God's image.
records.zomi: I pawlpi in pasal leh numeite Pasian lim bangin kibang-in kibawl hi, ci-in a hilh hi.

records.english: Christians believe that every person is made in the image of God.
records.zomi: Khristiante in mi khempeuh Pasian lim bangin kibawl hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: The choir sang a hymn about humanity being created in God's image.
records.zomi: La pawl in mihingte Pasian lim bangin kipiangsak thu la khat a sa uh hi.

records.english: The belief that every person is made in God's image has shaped how many churches care for the poor.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh Pasian lim bangin kibawl hi, cih upna in pawlpi tampi in mizawngte a kem dan a lam hi.

records.english: According to Genesis, God made the first man from the dust of the ground.
records.zomi: Piancilna bangin Pasian in mihing masa pen lei leivui pan a bawl hi.

records.english: The more I studied Genesis, the more I noticed how much responsibility it gives to human beings.
records.zomi: Piancilna ka sin semsem ciangin mihingte tungah mawhpuakna bangzah a pia hiam ka mu semsem hi.

records.english: Did God make me too, Mummy?
records.zomi: Nu aw, Pasian in kei zong hong bawl hiam?

records.english: It was in a Bible study on Genesis that I first understood why my parents spoke of every child as a gift.
records.zomi: Piancilna Laisiangtho sinna khat ah ka nu leh ka pa in bang hangin naupang khempeuh letsong bangin a gen uh hiam ka thei masa hi.

records.english: If every person bears God's image, then no one can be treated as worthless, our pastor argued.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh in Pasian lim a puak uh leh kuamah phattuam lo bangin kikem thei lo hi, ci-in i pastor in a gen hi.

records.english: Many Christians see work in the garden as part of God's plan for people.
records.zomi: Khristian tampi in huan nasep pen mite adingin Pasian' geelna khen khat bangin a mu uh hi.

records.english: Reflecting on the creation of humanity, the preacher reminded us that we are both made from dust and loved by God.
records.zomi: Mihing piangsakna thu a ngaihsut ciangin thugenpa in leivui pan kibawl leh Pasian' itna ngah i hi hi, ci-in hong phawksak hi.

records.english: Christians often thank God for the gift of life.
records.zomi: Khristiante in nuntakna letsong adingin Pasian lungdam a ci tawntung uh hi.

records.english: God placed the first people in a garden called Eden, according to Genesis.
records.zomi: Piancilna bangin Pasian in mi masate Eden a kici huan khat ah a koih hi.

records.english: Last Sunday, my son came home from church full of questions.
records.zomi: A paisa Nipini in ka tapa pawlpi pan dotna tampi tawh inn ah a ciah hi.

records.english: He wanted to know why God had made people out of dust instead of gold.
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pasian in mite sui pan hi lo-in leivui pan a bawl hiam theih a deih hi.

records.english: I told him that some Christians see the dust as a reminder that we are humble creatures who depend on God.
records.zomi: Khristian pawl khat in leivui pen Pasian tungah a kinga kiniamkhiat piansak i hihna phawksakna bangin a mu uh hi, ka ci hi.

records.english: According to Genesis, God warned Adam not to eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.
records.zomi: Piancilna bangin Pasian in hoih leh hoih lo theihna singkung pan ne lo dingin Adam a vaikhak hi.

records.english: Could the Garden of Eden have been a real place?
records.zomi: Eden Huan pen mun taktak ahi thei ding hiam?

records.english: Scholars and believers have suggested different answers, and the Bible does not settle the question.
records.zomi: Laisiam mite leh upmite in dawnna tuamtuam a gen uh a, Laisiangtho in tua dotna a khensat kei hi.

records.english: According to Genesis 2, God said that it was not good for the man to be alone.
records.zomi: Piancilna 2 bangin Pasian in pasal a kia-in a om pen a hoih kei hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Some Christians read the creation story literally, while others understand it as a symbolic account.
records.zomi: Khristian pawl khat in piangsakna tangthu a kammal bangin a sim uh a, a dang te in lahna tangthu bangin a thei uh hi.

records.english: Can you read me the creation story again before bed?
records.zomi: Ihmut ma-in piangsakna tangthu hong sim kik thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: What struck me most in the creation story was that God called humanity "very good."
records.zomi: Piangsakna tangthu sungah ka lungsim a khoih pen Pasian in mihingte “hoih mahmah” a cih ahi hi.

records.english: Why did God make people?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pasian in mite a bawl hiam?

records.english: Don't laugh at anyone's appearance, because God made each of us.
records.zomi: Pasian in i khat ciat hong bawl ahih manin kuamah' lim nuihsan kei in.

records.english: Grandpa prays every morning to thank God for making him.
records.zomi: Pu in amah a bawl hangin Pasian lungdam a cih nadingin zingsang simin thu a ngen hi.

records.english: The children acted out the story of Adam naming the animals.
records.zomi: Naupangte in Adam in ganhing te min a phuak tangthu a lawng uh hi.

records.english: Please read the first two chapters of Genesis before next week's class.
records.zomi: A zom kal sinna ma-in Piancilna a masa leh a nihna sim un.

records.english: Why do Christians believe that human life is sacred?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Khristiante in mihing nuntakna siangtho hi, ci-in a um uh hiam?

records.english: Because they believe each person bears the image of God, as Genesis teaches.
records.zomi: Piancilna in a hilh bangin mi khat ciat in Pasian lim a puak hi, ci-in a um uh ahih manin.

records.english: Christians believe that people were created to have a relationship with God.
records.zomi: Khristiante in mite Pasian tawh kizopna nei dingin kipiangsak hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: Our pastor said that every human life has great value.
records.zomi: I pastor in mihing nuntakna khempeuh a manpha mahmah hi, a ci hi.

records.english: For many believers, the breath God gave Adam is a picture of the life that comes from God alone.
records.zomi: Upmi tampi adingin Pasian in Adam a piak hu pen Pasian kiang bek pan hong pai nuntakna lim ahi hi.

records.english: In the story, God gives the first humans permission to eat from every tree except one.
records.zomi: Tangthu sungah Pasian in mihing masate khat simloh singkung khempeuh pan ne dingin a phal hi.

records.english: However people interpret the details, the story invites readers to see themselves as created for a purpose.
records.zomi: Mite in a thu neute bangci-in a theih zongin tangthu in simte in ngimna nei-in kipiangsak i hi hi, cih mu dingin a sam hi.

records.english: The Bible says that Adam gave names to all the animals.
records.zomi: Laisiangtho in Adam in ganhing khempeuh min a phuak hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Rather than seeing people as accidents, the Genesis account presents them as intended and loved.
records.zomi: Mite pen khial-a piang bangin et sangin Piancilna tangthu in ngim-a kibawl leh kiit bangin a lak hi.

records.english: My grandfather often said, "God made you, so be kind to what he made."
records.zomi: Ka pu in, “Pasian in hong bawl ahih manin a bawlte tungah lungsim hoih in,” a ci ngei hi.

records.english: In Genesis, God breathes life into the man he has formed.
records.zomi: Piancilna sungah Pasian in a bawl pasal sungah nuntakna hu a mut sak hi.

records.english: Does being made in God's image mean that we should look after one another?
records.zomi: Pasian lim bangin kibawl i hihna in i kikem tuah ding cihna hiam?

records.english: Christians have long debated how the creation of humanity relates to scientific accounts of human origins.
records.zomi: Khristiante in mihing piangsakna thu leh science in mihing kipatna a gen dan kizopna kum tampi a kinial uh hi.

records.english: Many Christians believe that people must care for creation because God entrusted it to them.
records.zomi: Pasian in amaute tungah a ap ahih manin mite in piangsakna a kem ding hi, ci-in Khristian tampi in a um uh hi.

records.english: Was Eve made from Adam's rib?
records.zomi: Eve pen Adam' nakguh pan kibawl hiam?

records.english: That's how the second chapter of Genesis tells it.
records.zomi: Piancilna a nihna in tua bangin a gen hi.

records.english: Look after the plants and animals, because Christians believe God gave them into our care.
records.zomi: Pasian in i kem dingin hong ap hi, ci-in Khristiante in a um uh ahih manin singkung leh ganhing te kem un.

records.english: The Bible study group discussed what it means that humans were given care of the earth.
records.zomi: Laisiangtho sinna pawl in mihingte leitung kemna kipia hi, cih a khiatna a kikum uh hi.

records.english: Before lunch, our family thanks God for making us and for the food on the table.
records.zomi: Sun an ma-in i innkuan in hong bawl hangin leh dawhkan tung-a an adingin Pasian lungdam i ci hi.

records.english: Our pastor explained that being made in God's image gives every person dignity.
records.zomi: Pasian lim bangin kibawl hihna in mi khempeuh zahtakna a pia hi, ci-in i pastor in a gen siang hi.

records.english: Christians believe that God made people for love and not by accident.
records.zomi: Khristiante in Pasian in mite khial-in hi lo-in itna adingin a bawl hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: The teacher read Genesis aloud so that the younger children could follow the story.
records.zomi: Naupang neu zawte in tangthu a zui theih nadingun saya in Piancilna aw-in a sim hi.

records.english: Our youth group planted trees as a way of caring for the world that God made.
records.zomi: I khangno pawl in Pasian' bawl leitung kemna lahna-in singkung a suan uh hi.

records.english: Do all Christians understand the creation story in the same way?
records.zomi: Khristian khempeuh in piangsakna tangthu kibang-in a thei uh hiam?

records.english: Why did God tell Adam not to eat from that tree?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pasian in tua singkung pan ne lo dingin Adam a vaikhak hiam?

records.english: Who first told you the story of Adam and Eve?
records.zomi: Adam leh Eve tangthu kua in hong gen masa hiam?

records.english: Who was the first man in the Bible?
records.zomi: Laisiangtho sungah mihing masa pen kua hiam?

records.english: Adam, according to the book of Genesis.
records.zomi: Adam, Piancilna laibu bangin.

records.english: In Genesis, God rests on the seventh day after creating the world and people.
records.zomi: Piancilna sungah Pasian in leitung leh mite a piangsak khit ciangin ni sagih ni-in a tawlnga hi.

records.english: Whatever their differences, Christian traditions generally agree that humans have a special place in creation.
records.zomi: Kilamdanna bang nei zongin Khristian ngeina tuamtuam in mihingte piangsakna sungah mun tuam a nei uh hi, ci-in a tamzaw-in a kilem uh hi.

records.english: The children drew pictures of the Garden of Eden.
records.zomi: Naupangte in Eden Huan lim a gelh uh hi.

records.english: Would your aunt sing that song for us if we asked nicely?
records.zomi: Hoih takin i ngen leh na ni in tua la hong sak sak ding hiam?

records.english: My grandfather used a broom handle to show us how he had walked on a tightrope.
records.zomi: Ka pu in khau tungah bangci-in a pai hiam hong lak nadingin phiatna sing khat a zang hi.

records.english: My neighbor and I laughed when we realized we had swum in the same river as boys.
records.zomi: Ka inn vengpa leh kei in tangval i hih lai-in gun khat mah ah tuipeek i hi hi, cih i theih ciangin i nui hi.

records.english: Once my aunt had told her secret, everyone else found it easier to share theirs.
records.zomi: Ka ni in a thusim a gen khit ciangin a dangte in amau' a gen a baih zaw uh hi.

records.english: When did you first talk about your journey to this country?
records.zomi: Bang ciangin hih gam a hong na khualzinna thu na gen masa hiam?

records.english: We might never have known about the circus if my grandfather hadn't spilled his water at dinner.
records.zomi: Ka pu in nitak an ah a tui a sung kei le circus thu i thei ngei lo kha ding hi.

records.english: At my brother's wedding, his best friend told a story that my brother had begged him to keep secret.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal' mopawi ah a lawm hoih pen in ka sanggam pasal in sel dingin a ngetna tangthu khat a gen hi.

records.english: Everyone laughed, and my brother turned the color of the tablecloth.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh a nui uh a, ka sanggam pasal dawhkan khuh puan bangin a san hi.

records.english: When my uncle was teaching me to shave, he admitted how terrified he had been on his first day at work.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in khamul hiat dan hong sin sak laitakin a nasep ni masa pen ah bangzah a lau hiam a pulak hi.

records.english: I had always thought of him as fearless, so his story made me feel much braver.
records.zomi: Lau ngei lo mi bangin ka ngaihsun tawntung ahih manin a tangthu in hong hangsak zaw mahmah hi.

records.english: Right, everyone, sit around the fire, and nobody sleeps until we've all told a story.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh aw, meikuang kiim ah tu unla, i khempeuh in tangthu i gen mateng kuamah ihmu kei un.

records.english: Why did your cousin blush when everyone looked at the clock?
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh in nai-ten a et uh ciangin bang hangin na sanggam a san hiam?

records.english: One evening at dinner, my grandfather mentioned that he had once worked in a circus.
records.zomi: Nitak khat in nitak an ah ka pu in khatvei circus ah a sem ngei hi, a ci hi.

records.english: We all stopped eating and stared at him, because none of us had ever heard this before.
records.zomi: I khempeuh in an nek i khawl a, a ma-in kuamah in hih thu i zak ngei loh manin i en hi.

records.english: He smiled, stood up, and balanced a full glass of water on his forehead for a whole minute.
records.zomi: A nui a, a ding a, tui a dim haai khat a taltang tungah minit khat bup a koih hi.

records.english: Do you still keep in touch with the woman from the waiting room?
records.zomi: Ngakna inn-a numei tawh na kikum lai hiam?

records.english: The waiting room felt less frightening once we started talking.
records.zomi: Thu i kikum kipat khit ciangin ngakna inn a lauhuai zaw nawn kei hi.

records.english: What I remember about that campfire is how differently I saw my classmates afterwards.
records.zomi: Tua meikuang thu ah ka phawk tua khit ciangin ka sang lawmte bangci-in a kibang lo-in ka mu hiam cih ahi hi.

records.english: Instead of telling us what to do, my uncle simply told me about his own fears.
records.zomi: Bang bawl ding hiam hong hilh sangin ka pa neu in amah' launate thu hong gen bek hi.

records.english: The stories people tell in waiting rooms are often the ones they have never told anyone else.
records.zomi: Ngakna inn-a mite' gen tangthu te a tamzaw-in kuamah kiangah a gen ngei loh te ahi hi.

records.english: How did you find out that your neighbor came from your village?
records.zomi: Na inn vengpa na khua pan a hong hi, cih bangci-in na thei hiam?

records.english: We were mending the fence between our gardens, and he started humming a song only our village sings.
records.zomi: I huan kikal-a huang i bawl dam laitakin i khua bek in a sak la khat a hum kipan hi.

records.english: I really did believe my uncle had never been afraid of anything.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu bangmah a lau ngei kei hi, ci-in ka um taktak hi.

records.english: On a school camping trip, our teacher asked each of us to tell the story of our strangest day.
records.zomi: Sang gam om khualzinna ah i saya in i khat ciat in i ni lamdang pen tangthu gen dingin hong ngen hi.

records.english: A quiet boy told us about the morning he woke up to find a cow in his bedroom.
records.zomi: Tangval daih khat in a inndei sungah bawng khat a muh zingsang thu hong gen hi.

records.english: After that night, he was never quiet with us again.
records.zomi: Tua zan khit ciangin i kiang ah a daih ngei nawn kei hi.

records.english: My notes for the assembly talk were so crumpled that I couldn't read them.
records.zomi: Kikhopna thugen adingin ka laigelh te a kiphiat lua ahih manin ka sim zo kei hi.

records.english: Last winter, our family played a game in which each person had to share one secret about their past.
records.zomi: Khuavot nung in i innkuan in mi khat ciat in a hun lui thusim khat gen ding kimawlna khat i kimawl hi.

records.english: My aunt confessed that she had once sung on the radio under a false name.
records.zomi: Ka ni in khatvei min khem tawh radio ah la a sa ngei hi, ci-in a pulak hi.

records.english: My little cousin admitted that he was the one who had broken the kitchen clock.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam neu in an huanna nai-ten a susia pen amah ahi hi, ci-in a pulak hi.

records.english: Why did your aunt keep her radio singing a secret?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na ni in a radio la sak a sel hiam?

records.english: Telling my story at assembly turned a frightening memory into something I could be proud of.
records.zomi: Kikhopna ah ka tangthu ka gen ciangin phawk lauhuai khat ka kipahna khat a suak hi.

records.english: In my second year at a new school, I was asked to talk at assembly about arriving in this country.
records.zomi: Sang thak ah kum nihna ka kah ciangin hih gam ka tun thu kikhopna ah gen dingin hong ngen uh hi.

records.english: My hands shook so much that I could hardly hold my notes.
records.zomi: Ka khut a ling lua ahih manin ka laigelh te ka len zo kei dek hi.

records.english: Afterwards, a younger boy came up to me and whispered, "The same thing happened to my family."
records.zomi: Tua khit ciangin tangval neu zaw khat hong pai a, “Ka innkuan tungah zong tua bang mah a piang hi,” ci-in hong suk hi.

records.english: While we waited for news at the hospital, a woman beside me told me her whole life story.
records.zomi: Siavuan inn ah thu i ngak laitakin ka kiang-a numei khat in a nuntakna tangthu bup hong gen hi.

records.english: By the time the doctor came out, I knew the names of all her grandchildren.
records.zomi: Siavuan a pusuak ciangin a tute khempeuh min ka thei khin hi.

records.english: Which relative could make the dullest story exciting?
records.zomi: Na sanggam bang in tangthu ningsakhuai pen zong nuamsak thei hiam?

records.english: My great-uncle, who could make even a trip to the market sound like an adventure.
records.zomi: Ka pu neu, zuakna mun pai zong lamdang khualzinna bangin gen thei pa.

records.english: My aunt played us her old radio song on a cassette player she had kept for decades.
records.zomi: Ka ni in kum sawm tampi sung a kem cassette setna tawh a radio la lui hong ngaisak hi.

records.english: Hearing that boy's whisper made me realize that my story belonged to many other people too.
records.zomi: Tua tangval' a suk ka zak ciangin ka tangthu pen mi dang tampi' zong ahi hi, cih ka thei hi.

records.english: What was the most surprising thing you ever learned about your grandparents?
records.zomi: Na pu leh pite thu-a na theih lamdang pen bang ahi hiam?

records.english: I was so moved by the boy's whisper that I couldn't speak for a moment.
records.zomi: Tangval' a suk in ka lungsim a khoih lua ahih manin tawmno sung thu ka gen zo kei hi.

records.english: Where were you when you heard your neighbor humming that song?
records.zomi: Na inn vengpa in tua la a hum na zak ciangin koi ah na om hiam?

records.english: Can you imagine your grandfather on a tightrope?
records.zomi: Na pu khau tungah a pai na ngaihsun thei ding hiam?

records.english: My aunt said that honesty about her past was the best gift she could give us.
records.zomi: Ka ni in a hun lui thu-a a thuman pen hong piak theih letsong hoih pen ahi hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Listen, all of you: what is said in this circle stays in this circle.
records.zomi: Na khempeuh un ngai un: hih kual sung-a kigen thu hih kual sungah om ding hi.

records.english: Tell us again how you found the cow in your bedroom.
records.zomi: Na inndei sungah bawng bangci-in na mu hiam hong gen kik in.

records.english: My brother's dignity was badly damaged by that wedding speech.
records.zomi: Tua mopawi thugen in ka sanggam pasal' zahtakna a susia mahmah hi.

records.english: Did your grandfather ever show you any other circus tricks?
records.zomi: Na pu in circus siamna dang hong lak ngei hiam?

records.english: Sharing a hard experience with strangers can sometimes be easier than sharing it with family.
records.zomi: Thuakna haksa khat theih loh mite tawh hawm pen khatvei khat innkuan tawh hawm sangin a baih zaw thei hi.

records.english: Were you nervous when you spoke at assembly?
records.zomi: Kikhopna ah na gen ciangin na lau hiam?

records.english: Would you ever tell a room full of strangers about your first year here?
records.zomi: Hih ah na kum masa pen thu theih loh mi tawh a dim inndei khat ah na gen ngei ding hiam?

records.english: Looking back, I think my uncle shared his fear with me on purpose.
records.zomi: Nung lam en kik-in ka pa neu in a launa ngim-in hong gen hi, ka ci hi.

records.english: The kitchen clock was finally repaired, twenty years after my cousin broke it.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam in a susiat kum sawm nih khit ciangin an huanna nai-ten a tawp-in kibawl dam hi.

records.english: I do want to learn at least one of my grandfather's circus tricks.
records.zomi: Ka pu' circus siamna khat bek hi zongin sin ka deih taktak hi.

records.english: Whatever we expected to hear from my grandfather, it certainly wasn't a story about elephants.
records.zomi: Ka pu pan bang za ding i ngak zongin sai thu tangthu ding hi, ci-in i ngaihsun kei hi.

records.english: Imagine finding out at forty that your grandfather once juggled for a crowd of thousands!
records.zomi: Kum sawm li na phak ciangin na pu in khatvei mi tul tampi mai ah van a pai-in a kimawl ngei hi, cih na theih ngaihsun in!

records.english: Shall we play the secrets game again this New Year?
records.zomi: Hih Kum Thak in thusim kimawlna i kimawl kik ding hiam?

records.english: My grandfather's old juggling clubs were found in the shed, wrapped in a blanket.
records.zomi: Ka pu' van pai kimawlna sing lui te van koihna inn sungah puannak tawh kituam-in kimu hi.

records.english: If the train is on time, I'll be able to say good night to the children before they sleep.
records.zomi: Meileng hun takin a tun leh naupangte a ihmut ma-un Zanpha ka ci thei ding hi.

records.english: Next year, our neighborhood will start a greeting week, when everyone says hello to someone new.
records.zomi: A zom kum ciangin i inn venglam in kihopihna kal khat a kipat sak ding a, mi khempeuh in mi thak khat a hopih ding uh hi.

records.english: When I open my shop, I'm going to learn every regular customer's name.
records.zomi: Ka zuakna inn ka hon ciangin a hong den mi khempeuh min ka sin ding hi.

records.english: When are you going to call your grandfather to wish him a happy new year?
records.zomi: Na pu Kum Thak nuam a cih nadingin bang ciangin phone tawh na sam ding hiam?

records.english: Wish me luck, because I'm about to give my first welcome speech!
records.zomi: Vangphatna hong thum sak in, ka muakna thugen masa pen ka gen ding hi!
