records.english: My brother is going to use his old paintbrushes to decorate a board by the gate for the wedding guests.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in mopawi khualte adingin kongpi kiang-a sing phek khat a rong nulna lui tawh a nul ding hi.

records.english: How should I greet people when I start my night shift next week?
records.zomi: A zom kal-a ka zan nasep ka kipat ciangin mite bangci-in ka hopih ding hiam?

records.english: You could just say good evening, and they'll probably say it back.
records.zomi: Nitakpha na ci bek thei hi, amaute zong a ci kik kha ding uh hi.

records.english: Learning how to greet his relatives is going to be my way of showing respect to his family.
records.zomi: A sanggamte hopih dan sin pen a innkuan zahtakna ka lahna lampi ahi ding hi.

records.english: When the new school year starts, I'm going to begin every morning with a greeting circle.
records.zomi: Sang kum thak a kipat ciangin zingsang khempeuh kihopihna kual tawh ka kipan ding hi.

records.english: Each child will choose how to greet the person next to them: a handshake, a wave, or a smile.
records.zomi: Naupang khat ciat in a kiang mi bangci-in hopih ding hiam a teel ding uh hi: khut kilen, khut vai, ahih kei leh nuihna.

records.english: I hope it will help the shy children feel part of the class from the first day.
records.zomi: Ni masa pan kipan maizum naupangte in sang inndei-a kihel bangin a kisak nadingin a huh ding hi, ka lametna ahi hi.

records.english: Will you hold the baby while I welcome our visitors?
records.zomi: Ka khualte ka muak laitakin naungek na pawm ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, and I'll bring her out to meet them once they've sat down.
records.zomi: Pawm ning, leh a tut khit uh ciangin kimu dingin kong pi khia ding hi.

records.english: Rather than sending a message, I plan to wish my old teacher a happy new year in person.
records.zomi: Message khak sangin ka saya lui kiangah mimal-in Kum Thak nuam ci dingin ka geel hi.

records.english: Would it be all right if I greeted the class in my own language on my first day?
records.zomi: Ka ni masa pen-in ka pau mah tawh sang inndei ka hopih leh a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: You're supposed to greet the oldest person in the room first.
records.zomi: Inndei sung-a mi upa pen na hopih masa ding hi.

records.english: Will you teach me how to greet your grandparents before Sunday?
records.zomi: Nipini ma-in na pu leh na pi hopih dan hong sin sak ding hiam?

records.english: Will people still greet each other on the street in twenty years' time?
records.zomi: Kum sawm nih khit ciangin mite in lampi tungah a kihopih lai ding uh hiam?

records.english: I expect most of them will, at least in small towns like ours.
records.zomi: A tamzaw in a kihopih lai ding uh hi, i khuapi neu bang ah bel, ka ci hi.

records.english: Shall we greet the new teacher with flowers on her first day?
records.zomi: Saya thak a ni masa pen-in pak tawh i hopih ding hiam?

records.english: By the end of my first month, I'll have greeted every family in the street at least once.
records.zomi: Ka kha masa a bei ciangin lampi-a innkuan khempeuh khatvei bek hi zongin ka hopih khin ding hi.

records.english: The more confidently you greet people at the start, the easier the rest of the visit will be.
records.zomi: A kipat ciangin mite na hopih hang semsem ciangin a dang veh hun a baih semsem ding hi.

records.english: I do want to greet your parents properly when I meet them on Sunday.
records.zomi: Nipini ni-in na nu leh na pa ka kimuh ciangin hoih takin hopih ka deih taktak hi.

records.english: Grandma lands at six tomorrow evening, after twelve years abroad.
records.zomi: Pi gamdang ah kum sawm leh nih a om khit ciangin zingciang nitak nai guk ciangin a tung ding hi.

records.english: We're going to meet her at the airport with a big painted banner.
records.zomi: Vanlengtual ah puan dalh lian kinul tawh i dawn ding hi.

records.english: The children have been practicing a welcome song all week, and they'll sing it the moment she appears.
records.zomi: Naupangte in kal bup muakna la a sin uh a, a hong kilak pah ciangin a sa ding uh hi.

records.english: Should I start the meeting with a few words of welcome in each language?
records.zomi: Kikhopna pen pau khempeuh tawh muakna kammal tawmno tawh ka kipat sak ding hiam?

records.english: Imagine how surprised the neighbors will be when the shy boy next door says good morning to them!
records.zomi: Inn kiang-a tangval maizum in Zingpha a cih ciangin inn vengte bangzah in lamdang a sa ding uh hiam ngaihsun in!

records.english: If you come back after dark, remember to say good evening to the guard.
records.zomi: A mial khit ciangin na hong kik leh kongpi kemtu kiangah Nitakpha ci dingin phawk in.

records.english: I really do hope the children will remember to say good morning to the bus driver.
records.zomi: Naupangte in bus mawngpa kiangah Zingpha ci dingin a phawk ding uh ka lametna taktak ahi hi.

records.english: I might greet the new manager in her own language, if I can learn the words in time.
records.zomi: A hun takin kammal te ka sin zawh leh makaipa thak pen amah' pau tawh ka hopih kha ding hi.

records.english: Children, tomorrow you'll each say good morning to our visitors in a different way.
records.zomi: Naupangte, zingciang ciangin na khat ciat un i khualte kiangah lampi tuamtuam tawh Zingpha na ci ding uh hi.

records.english: Whatever happens at the interview, I'm going to greet everyone warmly, including the receptionist.
records.zomi: Kidotna ah bang piang zongin mi khempeuh, mai lam ngaktu tel in, lungsim nuam takin ka hopih ding hi.

records.english: It would mean a great deal to the old man if someone greeted him by name tomorrow.
records.zomi: Zingciang ciangin mi khat in a min tawh a hopih leh pu upa adingin a thupi mahmah ding hi.

records.english: Once the new families have settled in, we'll invite them all for an evening of tea and stories.
records.zomi: Innkuan thakte a om khit ciangun tea leh tangthu nitak khat adingin i sam vek ding hi.

records.english: My nephew is going to welcome people at the church entrance, so please be patient with him.
records.zomi: Ka tanau in pawlpi lutna ah mite a muak ding ahih manin amah tungah thuakzawh takin om un.

records.english: Could you remind me to wish Mrs. Lun a good evening when she passes?
records.zomi: Lun nu a kantan ciangin Nitakpha ka cih nadingin hong phawksak thei ding hiam?

records.english: My daughter starts school on Monday, so we're practicing how she'll greet her teacher.
records.zomi: Ka tanu Pizing ni-in sang a kah kipan ding ahih manin a saya bangci-in a hopih ding hiam i sin hi.

records.english: Will you say good morning to the new neighbors when you see them?
records.zomi: Inn veng thakte na muh ciangin Zingpha na ci ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, and I'll take them a few eggs from our hens as well.
records.zomi: Ci ning, leh i ak te' aktui pawl khat zong ka tawi sak ding hi.

records.english: Next month, I'm visiting my fiancé's village for the first time.
records.zomi: A zom kha in ka zi ding' khua ka veh masa ding hi.

records.english: Before I go, I'm going to learn how to greet each of his relatives properly.
records.zomi: Ka pai ma-in a sanggam khat ciat hoih takin hopih dan ka sin ding hi.

records.english: His sister has promised to practice with me on the phone every evening this week.
records.zomi: A sanggam nu in hih kal sung nitak simin phone tawh hong sinpih dingin a ciam hi.

records.english: What time will you be home this evening?
records.zomi: Tu nitakin nai bangzah ciangin inn ah na om ding hiam?

records.english: I'm about to leave, so I'll say good night to everyone now.
records.zomi: Ka pai ding ahih manin tu-in mi khempeuh kiangah Zanpha ka ci ding hi.

records.english: Everyone, when the bishop comes in tomorrow, please stand up and greet him together.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh aw, zingciang bishop a lut ciangin ding unla khawm-in hopih un.

records.english: By the time Grandma's plane lands, the children will have sung their song a hundred times.
records.zomi: Pi' vanleng a tun ciangin naupangte in a la uh za khat vei a sa khin ding uh hi.

records.english: When I'm a grandmother, I hope my grandchildren will still greet me with a hug every morning.
records.zomi: Pi ka suah ciangin ka tute in zingsang simin hong kawi-in hong hopih lai ding uh ka lametna ahi hi.

records.english: Shall I wake you with a cup of tea tomorrow morning?
records.zomi: Zingciang zingsang ciangin tea haai khat tawh kong phawngsak ding hiam?

records.english: When you get to your aunt's house, greet her before you put down your bag.
records.zomi: Na ni' inn na tun ciangin na ip na koih ma-in amah hopih in.

records.english: We'll have to greet everyone quickly, because the ceremony starts at ten sharp.
records.zomi: Poai nai sawm tak ciangin a kipan ding ahih manin mi khempeuh manlang takin i hopih ding a kisam hi.

records.english: This time tomorrow, I'll be greeting my first guests at the hotel reception desk.
records.zomi: Zingciang tu hun ciangin zinbuuk mai lam ngakna dawhkan ah ka khual masa pen te ka hopih ding hi.

records.english: I'll use the little bell on the counter to let customers know I've seen them.
records.zomi: Lei mite ka mu hi, cih a theih nadingun dawhkan tung-a khawngging neu ka zang ding hi.

records.english: I'm going to paint a cheerful welcome sign for the shop window.
records.zomi: Zuakna inn tukvuang adingin muakna lai nuamhuai khat ka nul ding hi.

records.english: Who's going to welcome the visitors when they arrive?
records.zomi: Khualte a tun ciangin kua in a muak ding hiam?

records.english: We're planning a street breakfast on Saturday so that the new families can meet everyone.
records.zomi: Innkuan thakte in mi khempeuh a kimuh theih nadingun Kiginni ni-in lampi zingsang an khat i geel hi.

records.english: Practice your greeting in front of the mirror, and you'll feel more confident tomorrow.
records.zomi: Mai-et mai ah na hopihna sin inla, zingciang ciangin na kimuang zaw ding hi.

records.english: Do you think greetings will change as more people talk through their phones?
records.zomi: Mite in phone tawh a kikum tam semsem ciangin kihopihna a kikhek ding hi, na ci hiam?

records.english: If greeting strangers becomes a habit, the street will feel friendlier within a few months.
records.zomi: Theih loh mite hopih pen ngeina a suah leh kha tawmno sungin lampi a nuam zaw ding hi.

records.english: At the opening ceremony, I'm supposed to introduce myself in three languages.
records.zomi: Kihonna poai ah pau thum tawh keimah kitheisak ding ka hi hi.

records.english: Whatever I say in the first minute, I'm going to say it slowly and clearly.
records.zomi: Minit masa sungin bang ka gen zongin nawlkhin leh kician takin ka gen ding hi.

records.english: Could I introduce myself at the start of the meeting, since nobody here knows me yet?
records.zomi: Hih ah kuamah in hong thei nai kei uh ahih manin kikhopna kipatna ah keimah ka kitheisak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Everyone, tomorrow morning you'll each have one minute to tell us something surprising about yourself.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh aw, zingciang zingsang ciangin na khat ciat un nangmah thu lamdang khat gen dingin minit khat na nei ding uh hi.

records.english: Perhaps I'll introduce myself to the woman who walks her dog past our house every morning.
records.zomi: Zingsang simin i inn kiang ah a ui tawh a pai numei kiangah keimah ka kitheisak kha ding hi.

records.english: I might introduce myself with a joke, if I'm feeling brave enough.
records.zomi: Ka hang lua leh nuihza thu khat tawh keimah ka kitheisak kha ding hi.

records.english: How are you going to introduce yourself to your new manager?
records.zomi: Na makaipa thak kiangah nangmah bangci-in na kitheisak ding hiam?

records.english: Probably with a handshake and a short story about why I chose this job.
records.zomi: Khut kilen leh bang hangin hih nasep ka teel hiam tangthu tom khat tawh, ka ci hi.

records.english: Are you going to introduce yourself in your own language at the conference?
records.zomi: Kikhopna lian ah na pau mah tawh nangmah na kitheisak ding hiam?

records.english: Our new pharmacist plans to introduce herself to every shop on the street during her first week.
records.zomi: I zatui zuakpa numei thak in a kal masa sungin lampi-a zuakna inn khempeuh kiangah amah a kitheisak ding hi.

records.english: If I introduce myself properly on the first day, people will feel more comfortable asking me for help.
records.zomi: Ni masa pen-in hoih takin keimah ka kitheisak leh mite in huh hong ngen dingin a nuam zaw ding uh hi.

records.english: I'll read out my grandmother's introduction at the new club, since her voice is very quiet now.
records.zomi: Ka pi' aw a niam mahmah ta ahih manin kipawlna thak ah a kitheisakna ka sim sak ding hi.

records.english: Who's going to introduce the new volunteers at the meeting on Friday?
records.zomi: Laithai ni kikhopna ah thalawp thakte kua in a kitheisak ding hiam?

records.english: I really do hope I'll remember everyone's name this time.
records.zomi: Tu-in mi khempeuh min ka phawk ding ka lametna taktak ahi hi.

records.english: Will you help me practice my introduction before the interview?
records.zomi: Kidotna ma-in ka kitheisakna sin dingin hong huh ding hiam?

records.english: Shall I make some name cards for your new market stall?
records.zomi: Na zuakna dawhkan thak adingin min laidal pawl khat kong bawl sak ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, please, and put the phone number in big letters so that people can call me.
records.zomi: Bawl sak in, leh mite in hong sam theih nadingun phone nambat laimal lian tawh koih in.

records.english: You could start by saying where you're from, because people always ask that first.
records.zomi: Mite in a dong masa tawntung uh ahih manin koi pan na hong hiam gen-in na kipan thei hi.

records.english: My interview is next Thursday, and they've asked me to introduce myself in thirty seconds.
records.zomi: Ka kidotna a zom kal Laizing ni ahi a, second sawm thum sungin keimah kitheisak dingin hong ngen uh hi.

records.english: I'm going to start with my name and the job I'm applying for.
records.zomi: Ka min leh ka ngetna nasep tawh ka kipan ding hi.

records.english: Then I'll explain why I want to work with children, because that's what really matters to me.
records.zomi: Tua ciangin bang hangin naupangte tawh sep ka deih hiam ka gen ding hi, keimah adingin tua a thupi taktak hi.

records.english: Once I've introduced myself, the rest of the interview should be easier.
records.zomi: Keimah ka kitheisak khit ciangin kidotna a dang a baih zaw ding hi.

records.english: What will you say when the new class asks about you?
records.zomi: Sang inndei thak in nangmah thu a dot ciangun bang na gen ding hiam?

records.english: I'll tell them my name, where I come from, and that I love football.
records.zomi: Ka min, koi pan ka hong hiam, leh football ka deih hi, cih ka gen ding hi.

records.english: Of all the things I'm worried about, introducing myself is the smallest.
records.zomi: Ka lungkham thu khempeuh lakah keimah kitheisak pen a neu pen ahi hi.

records.english: I'll print my name in large letters on a card, so that the older members can read it easily.
records.zomi: Kipawlna upate in baih takin a sim theih nadingun laidal tungah ka min laimal lian tawh ka gelh ding hi.

records.english: Bring a small gift when you introduce yourself to your new neighbors.
records.zomi: Na inn veng thakte kiangah nangmah na kitheisak ciangin letsong neu khat tawi in.

records.english: My nephew is going to introduce himself to the class with a drawing of his family.
records.zomi: Ka tanau in a innkuan lim gelh tawh sang inndei kiangah amah a kitheisak ding hi.

records.english: In a few years, I imagine I'll be the one introducing new colleagues to the team.
records.zomi: Kum tawmno khit ciangin nasem thakte pawl kiangah a kitheisak pen kei ka hi ding hi, ka ngaihsun hi.

records.english: Can you think of a good way to introduce myself to a room full of strangers?
records.zomi: Theih loh mi tawh a dim inndei khat ah keimah kitheisak dan hoih khat na ngaihsun thei ding hiam?

records.english: The more relaxed I am when I introduce myself, the more relaxed everyone else will be.
records.zomi: Keimah ka kitheisak ciangin ka lungsim a nop semsem ciangin mi dang khempeuh zong a nop semsem ding uh hi.

records.english: Don't worry, because I'll introduce you to my colleagues so that you won't have to walk in alone.
records.zomi: Lungkham kei in, kia-in na lut lohna dingin ka nasem pawlte kiangah kong kitheisak ding hi.

records.english: By Friday, I'll have introduced myself to every department in the building.
records.zomi: Laithai ni ciangin inn sung-a nasep pawl khempeuh kiangah keimah ka kitheisak khin ding hi.

records.english: When I write to my new pen friend, I'll tell her about my family and the village where I live.
records.zomi: Ka laikhak lawm thak kiangah lai ka gelh ciangin ka innkuan leh ka omna khua thu ka gen ding hi.

records.english: Will you be the one introducing the speakers at the festival?
records.zomi: Pawi ah thugente a kitheisak pen nangma na hi ding hiam?

records.english: On Saturday, I'm the best man at my brother's wedding.
records.zomi: Kiginni ni-in ka sanggam pasal' mopawi ah amah huhtu pasal ka hi ding hi.

records.english: Half the guests won't know me, so I'll have to introduce myself before the speech.
records.zomi: Khual a kim in hong thei kei ding uh ahih manin thugen ma-in keimah ka kitheisak ding a kisam hi.

records.english: I'm planning to say that I'm the brother who taught him to ride a bicycle and then crashed it.
records.zomi: Siiksakol tuang dan a sin sak a, tua ciangin a sukkham sanggam pa ka hi hi, ka ci ding hi.

records.english: However nervous I feel, I'm going to look people in the eye when I say my name.
records.zomi: Bangzah in ka lau zongin ka min ka gen ciangin mite' mit ka en ding hi.

records.english: Shall we introduce ourselves to the family who moved in across the road?
records.zomi: Lampi gal lam ah a hong tum innkuan kiangah i kitheisak ding hiam?

records.english: Next month I'm joining a walking club, and I have no idea what to say to the others.
records.zomi: A zom kha in pai pawl khat ah ka kihel ding a, mi dangte kiangah bang gen ding hiam ka thei kei hi.

records.english: For my online course, I have to record a one-minute video introducing myself.
records.zomi: Ka online sinna adingin keimah kitheisakna minit khat video ka la ding a kisam hi.

records.english: My plan is to prop my phone against a pile of books so that it doesn't shake.
records.zomi: A ling lohna dingin laibu tamtak ah ka phone ka nga ding hi, ka geelna ahi hi.

records.english: When the visitors arrive, introduce yourself before you show them around.
records.zomi: Khualte a tun ciangin a kiim na lak ma-in nangmah kitheisak in.

records.english: Next week I'll be standing in front of fifty new students, introducing myself as their teacher.
records.zomi: A zom kal ciangin sangnaupang thak sawm nga mai ah ding-in amau' saya bangin keimah ka kitheisak ding hi.

records.english: It would help me a great deal if someone could introduce me to the elders first.
records.zomi: Mi khat in upate kiangah hong kitheisak masa thei leh hong huh mahmah ding hi.

records.english: If they ask about my hobbies, I'll tell them about my bees.
records.zomi: Ka nopsakna thu a dot uh leh ka khuaite thu ka gen ding hi.

records.english: All of you will get a chance to introduce yourselves after the opening prayer.
records.zomi: Kipatna thungetna khit ciangin na khempeuh un nangma kitheisak dingin hun na ngah ding uh hi.

records.english: Write down three things about yourself, and you'll never be lost for words.
records.zomi: Nangma thu thum gelh inla, gen ding na kiam ngei lo ding hi.

records.english: My sister has promised to introduce me to her friends when I visit her city in June.
records.zomi: June kha-in a khuapi ka veh ciangin ka sanggam nu in a lawmte kiangah hong kitheisak dingin a ciam hi.

records.english: I do want to sound confident, so I'm going to record myself tonight and listen back.
records.zomi: Kimuang takin gen ka deih taktak ahih manin tu zanin keimah ka la a, ka ngai kik ding hi.

records.english: Imagine introducing yourself to a whole stadium of people!
records.zomi: Kimawlna mun lian-a mi khempeuh kiangah nangma kitheisak ngaihsun in!

records.english: When I start university, I'm going to introduce myself by my full name instead of my childhood nickname.
records.zomi: Sangpi ka kah kipat ciangin ka naupan lai min sangin ka min kim tawh keimah ka kitheisak ding hi.

records.english: Next year, my family is moving to a country where I don't speak the language.
records.zomi: A zom kum ciangin ka innkuan in ka pau theih loh gam khat ah a kitawn ding uh hi.

records.english: Before we leave, I'm going to learn how to introduce myself and ask a few simple questions.
records.zomi: I pai ma-in keimah kitheisak dan leh dotna neu pawl khat dot dan ka sin ding hi.

records.english: By the time we land, I hope I'll be able to tell people who I am without looking at my notes.
records.zomi: I tun ciangin ka laigelh en lo-in kua ka hi hiam mite kiangah ka gen thei ding ka lametna ahi hi.

records.english: Which name should I put on my badge at the conference?
records.zomi: Kikhopna lian ah ka min ciamtehna ah min bang ka koih ding hiam?

records.english: Will you come with me when I knock on the neighbors' doors tomorrow?
records.zomi: Zingciang inn vengte' kongkhak ka kik ciangin hong zui ding hiam?

records.english: Instead of a long speech, I'm going to introduce myself with a single photograph of my village.
records.zomi: Thugen sau sangin ka khua lim khat bek tawh keimah ka kitheisak ding hi.

records.english: When will you be ready to introduce yourself to the choir?
records.zomi: La pawl kiangah nangma kitheisak dingin bang ciangin na kiman ding hiam?

records.english: We're putting name cards on every table so that wedding guests can introduce themselves to the people beside them.
records.zomi: Mopawi khualte in a kiang-a mite kiangah amau' kitheisak theih nadingun dawhkan khempeuh tungah min laidal i koih hi.

records.english: What will you say when you introduce your new friend to Grandma?
records.zomi: Na lawm thak Pi kiangah na kitheisak ciangin bang na gen ding hiam?

records.english: Everyone, when my friends arrive tonight, please make them feel at home.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh aw, tu zanin ka lawmte a tun ciangun amau' inn bangin kisak sak un.

records.english: My new stepbrother starts at my school next week.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal kik thak a zom kal ciangin ka sang ah a kah kipan ding hi.

records.english: I'm going to introduce him to my friends at lunch so that he doesn't have to sit alone.
records.zomi: Amah bek in a tut lohna dingin sun an hun ciangin ka lawmte kiangah ka kitheisak ding hi.

records.english: If he likes football, he might be able to join our team before the season starts.
records.zomi: Football a deih leh hun a kipat ma-in i pawl ah a kihel thei kha ding hi.

records.english: Which cousin is going to give the welcome speech?
records.zomi: Sanggam bang in muakna thugen a gen ding hiam?

records.english: Is your brother going to be at the picnic next weekend?
records.zomi: A zom kal tawp-a khualzin an nekna ah na sanggam pasal a om ding hiam?

records.english: May I bring my rabbit to school on Friday to introduce him to the class?
records.zomi: Laithai ni-in sang inndei kiangah ka kitheisak nadingin ka sazuk sang ah ka tawi thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, but he'll have to stay in his box unless I say he can come out.
records.zomi: Tawi thei hi, ahi zongin ka phal kei leh a bawm sungah a om ding hi.

records.english: Bring your sister along on Saturday, and I'll introduce her to everyone.
records.zomi: Kiginni ni-in na sanggam nu tawi inla, mi khempeuh kiangah kong kitheisak ding hi.

records.english: Whatever happens, I'm going to introduce my friend to my grandparents before she leaves the country.
records.zomi: Bang piang zongin ka lawm gam a nusiat ma-in ka pu leh ka pi kiangah ka kitheisak ding hi.

records.english: If my friends come early, I'll introduce them to my parents before the others arrive.
records.zomi: Ka lawmte ma-in a tun uh leh a dangte a tun ma-un ka nu leh ka pa kiangah ka kitheisak ding hi.

records.english: Children, on Monday our new classmate is arriving from another country, so I'd like each of you to tell her your name.
records.zomi: Naupangte, Pizing ni-in i sang lawm thak gamdang pan a tung ding ahih manin na khat ciat un na min uh hilh un.

records.english: Could you introduce me to the cousin who plays the drums at church?
records.zomi: Pawlpi ah khuang a tum sanggam kiangah hong kitheisak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Am I allowed to bring my roommate to the reunion, or is it only for relatives?
records.zomi: Kikhopna ah ka inn hawm pa ka tawi thei ding hiam, sanggamte adingin bek ahi hiam?

records.english: How will the guests know which side of the family everyone is from?
records.zomi: Khualte in mi khempeuh innkuan lam bang pan ahi hiam bangci-in a thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: My grandfather has asked to meet my new business partner before we sign anything.
records.zomi: I min i gelh ma-in ka pu in ka sumbawl lawm thak a kimuh nop hi, a ci hi.

records.english: I'll print a little booklet with photos of all the relatives so that my husband can learn their names before the reunion.
records.zomi: Kikhopna ma-in ka pasal in a min te a sin theih nadingin sanggam khempeuh lim tawh laibu neu khat ka bawl ding hi.

records.english: Please don't introduce me as "the baby of the family" this time!
records.zomi: Tu-in “innkuan naungek” ci-in hong kitheisak kei un!

records.english: Next spring, our grandfather turns ninety, and relatives are coming from four countries.
records.zomi: A zom spring ciangin i pu kum sawm kua a phak ding a, sanggamte gam li pan a hong ding uh hi.

records.english: Many of the younger cousins will be meeting each other for the very first time.
records.zomi: Sanggam khangno tampi a masa pen-in a kimu ding uh hi.

records.english: We're going to make name badges with each person's branch of the family written underneath.
records.zomi: Mi khat ciat' innkuan bawng a nuai ah kigelh min ciamtehna i bawl ding hi.

records.english: My sister is drawing a big family tree on a poster so that everyone at the reunion knows who is who.
records.zomi: Kikhopna ah kua ahi hiam mi khempeuh in a theih nadingun ka sanggam nu in laidal lian tungah innkuan singkung lian khat a gelh hi.

records.english: She'll pin it by the door, and people can add their own photos next to their names.
records.zomi: Kongkhak kiang ah a kilh ding a, mite in a min uh kiang ah amau' lim a koih thei ding uh hi.

records.english: Who are you going to bring to the wedding?
records.zomi: Mopawi ah kua na tawi ding hiam?

records.english: Probably my best friend from college, if she can get the day off work.
records.zomi: Nasep pan ni khat a ngah zawh leh sang lian pan ka lawm hoih pen, ka ci hi.

records.english: You may sit next to my grandfather at dinner, if you don't mind hearing his stories.
records.zomi: A tangthu te na ngaih theih leh nitak an ah ka pu kiang ah na tu thei hi.

records.english: My little brother will probably introduce his imaginary friend to the guests, as usual.
records.zomi: Ka nau pasal in a ngeina bangin a ngaihsutna lawm khualte kiangah a kitheisak kha ding hi.

records.english: Tomorrow I'll bring my photo album to school so that I can introduce my family to the new teacher.
records.zomi: Saya thak kiangah ka innkuan ka kitheisak theih nadingin zingciang ka lim laibu sang ah ka tawi ding hi.

records.english: However shy my nephew is, I'm sure he'll make friends with his cousins within an hour.
records.zomi: Ka tanau bangzah in maizum zongin nai khat sungin a sanggamte tawh a kilawm ding hi, ka thei hi.

records.english: My pen friend from overseas is coming to stay with us next summer.
records.zomi: Gamdang pan ka laikhak lawm a zom khal ciangin i kiang ah om dingin a hong ding hi.

records.english: On her first evening, I'm going to take her round the street and introduce her to all the neighbors.
records.zomi: A nitak masa pen-in lampi a kiim ah ka pi ding a, inn vengte khempeuh kiangah ka kitheisak ding hi.

records.english: The old couple next door have already said they'll bake a cake for her.
records.zomi: A kiang inn-a inn kiteng upa nih in amah adingin cake khat a em ding uh hi, a ci khin uh hi.

records.english: It would mean a lot to me if you agreed to meet my grandmother before she moves away.
records.zomi: Ka pi a kitawn ma-in a kimuh dingin na phal leh keimah adingin a thupi mahmah ding hi.

records.english: Shall I introduce you to my aunt, or would you prefer to wait until after the speeches?
records.zomi: Ka ni kiangah kong kitheisak ding hiam, thugen khit dong ngak na deih zaw hiam?

records.english: In a few years, I imagine my children will be introducing their own friends to us.
records.zomi: Kum tawmno khit ciangin ka ta te in amau' lawmte kei kiangah hong kitheisak ding uh hi, ka ngaihsun hi.

records.english: I can't wait to introduce you to my oldest friend; I think you'll love her.
records.zomi: Ka lawm lui pen kiangah kong kitheisak ding ka ngak zo kei hi; na it mahmah ding hi, ka ci hi.

records.english: We might ask my uncle to introduce the families at the start of the meal.
records.zomi: An nekna kipatna ah innkuante kitheisak dingin ka pa neu i ngen kha ding hi.

records.english: Next month, my best friend and my cousin will finally meet, and I'm sure they'll get on well.
records.zomi: A zom kha in ka lawm hoih pen leh ka sanggam a tawp-in a kimu ding uh a, a kilawm ding uh hi, ka thei hi.

records.english: Rather than introducing everyone at once, I'll take my friend round the room one group at a time.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh khatvei-in kitheisak sangin ka lawm pawl khat ciat kiangah ka pi ding hi.

records.english: Once everyone has been introduced, the real fun of the party can begin.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh a kitheisak khit ciangin pawi nuam taktak a kipan thei ding hi.

records.english: I'll introduce you to my uncle, who knows everyone in the music business.
records.zomi: La nasep sung-a mi khempeuh a thei ka pa neu kiangah kong kitheisak ding hi.

records.english: Imagine how loud the house will be when all forty cousins are in one room!
records.zomi: Sanggam sawm li khempeuh inndei khat ah a om ciangin inn bangzah in a buai ding hiam ngaihsun in!

records.english: When are you going to introduce the baby to her great-grandmother?
records.zomi: Bang ciangin naungek a pi upa kiangah na kitheisak ding hiam?

records.english: We're driving to the village next Sunday, and we'll stay for lunch.
records.zomi: A zom Nipini ni-in khua ah i pai ding a, sun an dong i om ding hi.

records.english: Perhaps you could introduce your colleague to my sister, since they're both interested in nursing.
records.zomi: A nih in nurse nasep a deih uh ahih manin na nasem pawl ka sanggam nu kiangah na kitheisak thei kha ding hi.

records.english: Will your parents be at the concert, so that I can finally meet them?
records.zomi: A tawp-in ka kimuh theih nadingin na nu leh na pa la pawi ah a om ding uh hiam?

records.english: Do you think our two grandmothers will have anything to talk about?
records.zomi: I pi nih in a kikup ding uh bangmah a nei ding uh hiam, na ci hiam?

records.english: The more relatives we introduce to the children now, the more family they'll have when they grow up.
records.zomi: Tu-in naupangte kiangah sanggam tam i kitheisak semsem ciangin a khan ciangun innkuan tam a nei semsem ding uh hi.

records.english: When you meet my grandfather, shake his hand firmly and look him in the eye.
records.zomi: Ka pu na kimuh ciangin a khut hat takin len inla, a mit en in.

records.english: My cousin is going to show the new family around and introduce them to the shopkeepers.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam in innkuan thakte a kiim a lak ding a, zuakna inn neite kiangah a kitheisak ding hi.

records.english: By the end of the reunion, I hope the youngest cousins will know each other's names.
records.zomi: Kikhopna a bei ciangin sanggam neu pen te in a kimin a kithei ding uh ka lametna ahi hi.

records.english: Practice saying everyone's names tonight, so that you don't mix them up tomorrow.
records.zomi: Zingciang ciangin na kilamdang khial lohna dingin tu zanin mi khempeuh min gen sin in.

records.english: I'm going to text my brother a photo of you so that he recognizes you at the station.
records.zomi: Meileng dinna ah hong theih nadingin na lim ka sanggam pasal kiangah ka khak ding hi.

records.english: I'm going to introduce my grandmother to my teacher, because they grew up in the same valley.
records.zomi: Guam khat mah ah a khang uh ahih manin ka pi ka saya kiangah ka kitheisak ding hi.

records.english: Can you guess who will be the first to cry when the cousins meet?
records.zomi: Sanggamte a kimuh ciangin kua in a kap masa ding hiam na ngaihsun thei ding hiam?

records.english: You'll get to meet my whole family when they come down from the hills for New Year.
records.zomi: Kum Thak adingin mual tung pan a hong ciangun ka innkuan bup na kimu ding hi.

records.english: If the two families get to know each other before the wedding, the day itself will be much more relaxed.
records.zomi: Mopawi ma-in innkuan nih a kithei uh leh tua ni a nuam zaw mahmah ding hi.

records.english: My niece will be introducing her new puppy to the family on Sunday.
records.zomi: Ka tunu in Nipini ni-in a ui neu thak innkuan kiangah a kitheisak ding hi.

records.english: Deciding which questions to ask at an interview can be as important as answering them well.
records.zomi: Kidotna ah dotna bang dong ding hiam thukhen pen hoih taka dawng bangin a thupi thei hi.

records.english: Which window was broken in the storm?
records.zomi: Huihpi lai-in tukvuang bang a kek hiam?

records.english: The small one in the bathroom, but it's been boarded up.
records.zomi: Kisilna inn-a neu pen, ahi zongin sing tawh kikhak khin hi.

records.english: Which room is the class in today?
records.zomi: Tuni-in sinna inndei bang ah ahi hiam?

records.english: Room twelve, at the end of the corridor.
records.zomi: Inndei sawm leh nih, inn lampi tawp ah.

records.english: Which tree was cut down to make room for the new road?
records.zomi: Lampi thak adingin singkung bang a kiphuk hiam?

records.english: Which of these two shirts looks better?
records.zomi: Hih puan-akhi nih lakah bang in a kilawm zaw hiam?

records.english: The blue one, because it matches your eyes.
records.zomi: A dum pen, na mit tawh a kilawm ahih manin.

records.english: If you could relive one day from your childhood, which would it be?
records.zomi: Na naupan lai-a ni khat na nuntak kik thei leh bang ni na teel ding hiam?

records.english: Which of you left the gate open?
records.zomi: Na lak uh-ah kua in kongpi a nusia hiam?

records.english: Choosing which university to apply to was the hardest decision I made that year.
records.zomi: Sangpi bang ngen ding hiam teel pen tua kum-a ka thukhenna haksa pen ahi hi.

records.english: Which month is the festival in this year?
records.zomi: Hih kum in pawi kha bang ah ahi hiam?

records.english: Which day suits you best for the meeting?
records.zomi: Kikhopna adingin ni bang na kilawm sak pen hiam?

records.english: Thursday afternoon, if that's all right with everyone.
records.zomi: Laizing ni nitak lam, mi khempeuh adingin a hoih leh.

records.english: Knowing which battles to fight is a skill that many people learn only with age.
records.zomi: Kidou bang ah kidou ding hiam theihna pen mi tampi in upat khit ciang bek a sin uh siamna khat ahi hi.

records.english: Whichever option you choose, make sure it's one you can live with for a long time.
records.zomi: Bang na teel zongin hun sawt sung tua tawh na nuntak theih ding khat ahi ding hi.

records.english: Do you know which key opens the shed?
records.zomi: Van koihna inn tawh bang in a hon hiam na thei hiam?

records.english: The real question is not which car is cheaper, but which one will last longer.
records.zomi: Dotna taktak pen mawtaw bang in a man neu zaw hiam hi lo-in bang in a sawt zaw ding hiam ahi hi.

records.english: We can't agree on which photo to put in the frame.
records.zomi: Kilh sung ah lim bang koih ding hiam i kilem zo kei hi.

records.english: We still don't know which house the noise was coming from.
records.zomi: Ging pen inn bang pan a hong hiam i thei nai kei hi.

records.english: I really can't remember which drawer I put the passports in.
records.zomi: Passport te kenkuan bang sungah ka koih hiam ka phawk zo taktak kei hi.

records.english: Which road is quicker at this time of day?
records.zomi: Hih hun ciangin lampi bang in a manlang zaw hiam?

records.english: The one by the river, because the main road is always busy.
records.zomi: Gun kiang lampi, lampi lian pen a buai tawntung ahih manin.

records.english: Which language do you speak at home?
records.zomi: Inn ah pau bang na zang hiam?

records.english: Which way is the station?
records.zomi: Meileng dinna lam bang ah ahi hiam?

records.english: Straight ahead, then left at the bakery.
records.zomi: Ma lam ah zui inla, moh bawlna ah veilam ah pial in.

records.english: Class, which of these animals do you think can swim?
records.zomi: Naupangte, hih ganhing te lakah bang in tuipeek thei ding hi na ci uh hiam?

records.english: Tell me which one you like, and I'll buy it for you.
records.zomi: Bang na deih hiam hong gen inla, kong lei sak ding hi.

records.english: I do want to know which of my answers were wrong, so that I can learn from them.
records.zomi: Ka dawnna bang te a khial hiam theih ka deih taktak a, tua pan ka sin theih nadingin.

records.english: It doesn't matter which path you take up the hill, because they all reach the top eventually.
records.zomi: Mual tung lam ah lampi bang na zui zongin a tawp-in a vekpi tung ah a tung uh ahih manin a thupi kei hi.

records.english: Last spring, our neighbor's dog had six puppies.
records.zomi: Spring nung in i inn vengpa' ui in a ta guk a nei hi.

records.english: We were told we could take one, but we couldn't decide which.
records.zomi: Khat la thei hi, ci-in hong kigen a, ahi zongin bang ding hiam i khen zo kei hi.

records.english: In the end, the smallest puppy climbed into my son's lap and fell asleep, so the choice was made for us.
records.zomi: A tawp-in ui neu a neu pen ka tapa' khuk tungah a kai a, a ihmu ahih manin teelna hong kibawl sak hi.

records.english: Which of your grandchildren lives nearest to you?
records.zomi: Na tute lakah kua in na kiang pen ah a om hiam?

records.english: My eldest granddaughter, who's just two streets away.
records.zomi: Ka tu nu upa pen, lampi nih bek gamla-ah a om pa.

records.english: Which bus goes to the hospital?
records.zomi: Bus bang in siavuan inn ah a pai hiam?

records.english: The number nine, from the stop outside the bank.
records.zomi: Nambat kua, bank pua-a dinna pan.

records.english: Our teacher said, "Think carefully about which question you answer first."
records.zomi: I saya in, “Dotna bang na dawng masa ding hiam limtakin ngaihsun un,” a ci hi.

records.english: My sister asked me which school I wanted to go to.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu in sang bang ah kah ka deih hiam hong dong hi.

records.english: Can you tell which plates got chipped in the move?
records.zomi: Kitawnna lai-in kuang bang te a kek hiam na thei thei ding hiam?

records.english: Which song are you going to sing at the concert?
records.zomi: La pawi ah la bang na sak ding hiam?

records.english: An old folk song that my grandfather taught me.
records.zomi: Ka pu in hong sin sak khua la lui khat.

records.english: Everyone, write down which topic you'd like to study next term.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh aw, a zom hun ciangin thu bang sin na deih hiam gelh un.

records.english: Which of the two jobs would give you more time with your family?
records.zomi: Nasep nih lakah bang in na innkuan tawh hun tam zaw hong pia ding hiam?

records.english: Which size do you usually wear?
records.zomi: A tamzaw-in a lian zah bang na silh hiam?

records.english: Medium, but sometimes large if the shirt is tight.
records.zomi: A laizang, ahi zongin puan-akhi a kiim leh khatvei khat a lian.

records.english: The doctor asked, "Which side of your head hurts most?"
records.zomi: Siavuan in, “Na lu lam bang in a na zaw hiam?” a ci hi.

records.english: Which parts of the old town were restored, and which were simply knocked down?
records.zomi: Khuapi lui-a mun bang te kibawl dam a, bang te kiphuk bek hiam?

records.english: Do you know which platform the train leaves from?
records.zomi: Meileng dinna mun bang pan a pai hiam na thei hiam?

records.english: Which door should I use at night?
records.zomi: Zanin kongkhak bang ka zang ding hiam?

records.english: The side door, because the main entrance is locked after eight.
records.zomi: A pang kongkhak, nai giat khit ciangin lutna lian kikhak ahih manin.

records.english: Which team do you support?
records.zomi: Pawl bang na deih hiam?

records.english: The one from my hometown, even though they always lose.
records.zomi: Ka khua pan a hong pawl, a sung tawntung uh hangin.

records.english: I can't decide which cake to bake for her birthday.
records.zomi: A pianni adingin cake bang em ding hiam ka khen zo kei hi.

records.english: Which dish would you recommend for a first visit?
records.zomi: A veh masa adingin an bang na gen ding hiam?

records.english: Try the fish curry; it's what people come here for.
records.zomi: Nga curry ne sin in; mite in tua adingin hih ah a hong uh hi.

records.english: Which color do you want for your new bag?
records.zomi: Na ip thak adingin rong bang na deih hiam?

records.english: The dark green one, please.
records.zomi: A eng nawn khat pia in.

records.english: It's often hard to tell which of two arguments is stronger until you hear both sides.
records.zomi: A lam nih na zak ma-in kinialna nih lakah bang in a hat zaw hiam theih a haksa tam hi.

records.english: Which film shall we watch tonight?
records.zomi: Tu zanin film bang i en ding hiam?

records.english: What will you cook when your old school friends come for dinner on Friday?
records.zomi: Laithai ni-in na sang lawm luite nitak an adingin a hong ciangun bang na huan ding hiam?

records.english: Something simple, so that I can sit and talk instead of staying in the kitchen.
records.zomi: A baih khat, an huanna ah om sangin tu-in ka kikum theih nadingin.

records.english: Where will the visitors sleep if the guest room isn't ready?
records.zomi: Khual inndei a kiman nai kei leh khualte koi ah a ihmu ding uh hiam?

records.english: However tired we are after work, we'll take our visitors somewhere special every evening.
records.zomi: Nasep khit ciangin bangzah in i ol zongin nitak simin i khualte mun tuam khat ah i pi ding hi.

records.english: Before my cousin's husband visits, I'm going to find out which dishes he enjoys.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam' pasal a veh ma-in an bang a deih hiam ka zong ding hi.

records.english: I'll print a little map of the neighborhood so that our guests can find the shops.
records.zomi: I khualte in zuakna inn te a muh theih nadingun i inn veng map neu khat ka print ding hi.

records.english: I do want our visitors to feel completely at home, even if the house is small.
records.zomi: Inn a neu hangin i khualte in amau' inn bangin a kisak ding ka deih taktak hi.

records.english: Do you think they'd enjoy a walk up the hill on their first evening?
records.zomi: A nitak masa pen-in mual tung lam pai a nopsak ding uh hiam, na ci hiam?

records.english: Perhaps your parents would like to come to the market with us on Saturday morning.
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa in Kiginni zingsang ciangin zuakna mun ah hong zui nuam kha ding uh hi.

records.english: Rather than filling every day with trips, we'll leave our visitors some time to rest.
records.zomi: Ni khempeuh khualzinna tawh dimsak sangin i khualte tawlngak hun i nusia sak ding hi.

records.english: From next summer, we're going to rent out our spare room to visitors.
records.zomi: A zom khal pan kipan i inndei a om ngawng khualte i hawl ding hi.

records.english: Guests will be welcome to use the kitchen, but smoking won't be allowed anywhere in the house.
records.zomi: Khualte in an huanna a zang thei ding uh a, ahi zongin inn sung koi peuh ah meikhu dawn kiphal lo ding hi.

records.english: We'll also ask everyone to keep the noise down after ten, because the baby sleeps next door.
records.zomi: Naungek in a kiang inndei ah a ihmut ahih manin nai sawm khit ciangin mi khempeuh ging niam dingin i ngen ding hi.

records.english: If the river is calm, we might take our visitors out in my uncle's boat.
records.zomi: Gun a daih leh ka pa neu' long tawh i khualte i pi khia kha ding hi.

records.english: Shall I clear a shelf in the bathroom for our guests' things?
records.zomi: I khualte' van adingin kisilna inn ah van koihna khat ka siang sak ding hiam?

records.english: Visitors will be allowed into the new ward only during the afternoon, according to the hospital.
records.zomi: Siavuan inn' gen bangin khual vehte inndei thak ah nitak lam bek-in lut thei ding uh hi.

records.english: My son will meet you at the bus stop with a wheelbarrow for your luggage.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in na van te adingin leng neu khat tawh bus dinna ah hong dawn ding hi.

records.english: Making a foster child feel welcome will take patience rather than presents.
records.zomi: Ta kem khat kimuak a kisak nadingin letsong sangin thuakzawhna a kisam ding hi.

records.english: When the students come home from university at Christmas, the village band is going to meet them at the bus stop.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte Christmas ciangin sangpi pan inn a ciah ciangun khua la pawl in bus dinna ah a dawn ding uh hi.

records.english: We'll lend our visitors bicycles so that they can explore the village on their own.
records.zomi: Amau' bek-in khua a kiim a et theih nadingun i khualte siiksakol i caih sak ding hi.

records.english: It might be better to meet them at the station, since our street is hard to find.
records.zomi: I lampi a muh a haksa ahih manin meileng dinna ah dawn leng a hoih zaw kha ding hi.

records.english: During festival week, our bakery will give a free sweet bun to every visitor who comes in.
records.zomi: Pawi kal sungin i moh bawlna in a lut khual khempeuh moh khum neu khat a man lo-in a pia ding hi.

records.english: Will the guests need blankets, or will the heater be enough?
records.zomi: Khualte in puannak a kisam ding uh hiam, lum sakna kicing ding hiam?

records.english: This time next week, we'll be welcoming forty relatives into a house built for six.
records.zomi: A zom kal tu hun ciangin mi guk adingin kibawl inn khat ah sanggam sawm li i muak ding hi.

records.english: Will your parents want to rest after the journey, or go straight out?
records.zomi: Khualzinna khit ciangin na nu leh na pa in tawlngak a deih ding uh hiam, a pusuak pah ding uh hiam?

records.english: Our neighbors have offered to cook dinner for our visitors on the first night.
records.zomi: I inn vengte in a zan masa pen-in i khualte adingin nitak an huan dingin a ciam uh hi.

records.english: Who's going to show the new pastor's children around the school?
records.zomi: Pastor thak' ta te sang a kiim kua in a lak ding hiam?

records.english: My niece has offered, because she's in the same class as their eldest daughter.
records.zomi: Ka tunu in a ciam a, a tanu upa pen tawh sang inndei khat mah ah a om uh ahih manin.

records.english: Whatever we cook, the most important thing is that our guests feel welcome.
records.zomi: Bang i huan zongin a thupi pen i khualte in kimuak a kisak uh ahi hi.

records.english: You mustn't tell Aunt Hoih that we bought the cake from a shop.
records.zomi: Cake zuakna inn pan i lei hi, cih Ni Hoih kiangah na gen lo ding hi.

records.english: I'm planning to take the day off so that I can show my friend around the city.
records.zomi: Ka lawm khuapi a kiim ka lak theih nadingin ni khat khawl dingin ka geel hi.

records.english: We could ask the visitors whether they'd like to try our local dishes.
records.zomi: I khualte kiangah i khua an a lim et nop uh hiam i dong thei hi.

records.english: The guest room is going to be painted on Thursday, so it should be dry by Saturday.
records.zomi: Khual inndei Laizing ni-in kinul ding ahih manin Kiginni ciangin a keu ding hi.

records.english: Grandpa is coming to stay in our city flat for the first time next month.
records.zomi: Pu a zom kha in a masa pen-in i khuapi inn ah om dingin a hong ding hi.

records.english: Before he arrives, my husband is going to fit a handrail on the stairs with his new drill.
records.zomi: A tun ma-in ka pasal in a thau-it thak tawh kahlei ah khut lenna sing a khai ding hi.

records.english: We'll also move his bed closer to the window, because he likes to wake up with the sun.
records.zomi: Ni tawh thoh a deih ahih manin a lupna tukvuang kiang zawin i tawn ding hi.

records.english: Once the ramp is in place, our friend will be able to visit us as often as she likes.
records.zomi: Kaitouna lampi a kikoih khit ciangin i lawm in a deih zah zah hong veh thei ding hi.

records.english: Shall I put fresh flowers in the guest room before they arrive?
records.zomi: A tun ma-un khual inndei ah pak thak ka koih ding hiam?

records.english: If they arrive late, I'll leave some soup on the stove for them.
records.zomi: A tun nun uh leh meikhuk tungah amaute adingin an tui pawl khat ka nusia ding hi.

records.english: I'm going to use the old sewing machine to make new curtains for the guest room.
records.zomi: Khual inndei adingin tukvuang puan thak bawl nadingin puan khuina setna lui ka zang ding hi.

records.english: I really do hope the rain stops before the guests arrive.
records.zomi: Khualte a tun ma-in guah a khawl ding ka lametna taktak ahi hi.

records.english: If we prepare everything the day before, we'll be able to relax when the visitors arrive.
records.zomi: A ma ni-in bangkim i kiman khol leh khualte a tun ciangin i tawlnga thei ding hi.

records.english: Kids, tomorrow you'll each teach our visitors one game we play at break time.
records.zomi: Naupangte, zingciang ciangin na khat ciat un tawlngakna hun-a i kimawlna khat i khualte na sin sak ding uh hi.

records.english: It would be lovely if the visitors could stay long enough to see the harvest festival.
records.zomi: Khualte in kaihawl pawi a muh theih dong a om thei uh leh hoih mahmah ding hi.

records.english: By the time our friends land, the beds will have been made and the soup will be ready.
records.zomi: I lawmte a tun ciangin lupna te kibawl khin ding a, an tui a kiman khin ding hi.

records.english: When are your friends from the north arriving?
records.zomi: Mal lam pan na lawmte bang ciangin a tung ding uh hiam?

records.english: A foster child is coming to live with us next month.
records.zomi: A zom kha in ta kem khat i kiang ah om dingin a hong ding hi.

records.english: We're going to let her choose the color of her new bedroom.
records.zomi: A inndei thak rong amah in teel dingin i phal ding hi.

records.english: For the first few weeks, we won't ask her too many questions, so that she can settle in at her own pace.
records.zomi: Kal masa pawl khat sungin amah' hun bangin a om theih nadingin dotna tam lua i dong lo ding hi.

records.english: May our visitors park in front of your garage on Sunday afternoon?
records.zomi: Nipini nitak lam ciangin i khualte na mawtaw inn ma-ah a koih thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: Yes, they may, as long as they've gone by six.
records.zomi: Koih thei uh hi, nai guk ma-in a pai uh leh.

records.english: Can we borrow an extra mattress from your sister for the weekend?
records.zomi: Kal tawp sung adingin na sanggam nu kiang pan lupna phah behlap khat i caih thei ding hiam?

records.english: Will they be able to find our house on their own?
records.zomi: Amaute bek in i inn a mu thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: Our visitor next week uses a wheelchair, so we're borrowing a ramp for the front step.
records.zomi: A zom kal-a i khual in khe nei tutna a zang ahih manin ma lam kahlei adingin kaitouna lampi i caih ding hi.

records.english: Could you help me carry it from the community center on Saturday?
records.zomi: Kiginni ni-in mipi inn pan puak dingin hong huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Please don't let the dog jump on Grandpa when he arrives.
records.zomi: Pu a tun ciangin ui in a tungah kai sak kei in.

records.english: Everyone, our guests will be here in ten minutes, so please put your phones away.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh aw, i khualte minit sawm sungin a tung ding uh ahih manin na phone uh koih un.

records.english: Will you let me know as soon as their plane lands?
records.zomi: A vanleng a tun pah ciangin hong hilh ding hiam?

records.english: The children are going to plant flowers along the path before our new neighbors move in.
records.zomi: I inn veng thakte a tun ma-un naupangte in lampi kiang ah pak a suan ding uh hi.

records.english: Wish us luck, because twelve cousins are arriving tomorrow!
records.zomi: Vangphatna hong thum sak un, zingciang ciangin sanggam sawm leh nih a tung ding uh hi!

records.english: I'm going to bake my friend's favorite biscuits so that she has something to eat on the journey.
records.zomi: Ka lawm in khualzinna ah a nek ding a neih nadingin a deih pen biscuit ka em ding hi.

records.english: If the weather is bad, the ferry might leave early, so we'll say goodbye at the house.
records.zomi: Huihkhua a hoih kei leh tembaw a ma-in a pai kha ding ahih manin inn ah goodbye i ci ding hi.

records.english: I do want to say goodbye to every one of my neighbors before I move.
records.zomi: Ka kitawn ma-in ka inn vengte khempeuh kiangah goodbye ci ka deih taktak hi.

records.english: Once the boxes are packed, the goodbyes will suddenly feel very real.
records.zomi: Bawm te a kituam khit ciangin goodbye cih a taktak bangin a kisa thawlawh ding hi.

records.english: We're having a farewell lunch on Friday for a colleague who is moving to our branch in the north.
records.zomi: Mal lam-a i nasepna mun ah a kitawn nasem pawl khat adingin Laithai ni-in kikhenna sun an i nei ding hi.

records.english: We'll plant a tree in the garden before we leave, so that part of us stays here.
records.zomi: I pai ma-in i khen khat hih ah a om nadingin huan sungah singkung khat i suan ding hi.

records.english: Saying goodbye will be easier if we already know when we'll meet again.
records.zomi: Bang ciangin i kimu kik ding hiam i theih khol leh goodbye cih a baih zaw ding hi.

records.english: Children, after the farewell song, you'll each give our visitors one of the cards you made.
records.zomi: Naupangte, kikhenna la khit ciangin na khat ciat un na bawl card khat i khualte na pia ding uh hi.

records.english: The leaving gifts will be wrapped tonight and handed over at the party.
records.zomi: Kikhenna letsong te tu zanin kituam ding a, pawi ah kipia ding hi.

records.english: Can we keep the shirts afterwards, or do we have to wash them?
records.zomi: Tua khit ciangin puan-akhi te i kem thei ding hiam, i silh ding a kisam hiam?

records.english: You can keep them, but please don't write anything you'll be sorry about later.
records.zomi: Na kem thei uh hi, ahi zongin a nung ciangin na lungkham ding bangmah gelh kei un.

records.english: My cousin is joining a ship's crew next week and won't be home for nine months.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam a zom kal ciangin tembaw lian nasemte ah a kihel ding a, kha kua sung inn ah a om lo ding hi.

records.english: Half the street is planning to come to the port and wave as his ship sails.
records.zomi: A tembaw a pai ciangin lampi a kim in long dinna ah khut vai dingin a geel uh hi.

records.english: My aunt says she won't cry, but she's already packed three handkerchiefs.
records.zomi: Ka ni in ka kap lo ding hi, a ci a, ahi zongin khut puan thum a tawi khin hi.

records.english: If I start crying at the airport, I'm sure my whole family will start too.
records.zomi: Vanlengtual ah ka kap kipat leh ka innkuan bup zong a kap kipan ding uh hi, ka thei hi.

records.english: Shall I come to the station to see you off?
records.zomi: Na pai ciangin meileng dinna ah kong pai ding hiam?

records.english: Promise me you'll write, even if it's only a few lines.
records.zomi: Kammal tawmno bek hi zongin lai na khak ding hong ciam in.

records.english: Whatever happens, we'll make sure you never feel far from home.
records.zomi: Bang piang zongin inn pan gamla-in na kisa ngei lo nadingin i kidawm ding hi.

records.english: You mustn't open the letter until you're on the train.
records.zomi: Meileng tungah na om ma-in lai na hon lo ding hi.

records.english: My little sister said, "If you go, I'm coming in your suitcase."
records.zomi: Ka nau nu in, “Na pai leh na van bawm sungah kong zui ding hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: We could have a small party on Saturday, if you'd like to see everyone before you go.
records.zomi: Na pai ma-in mi khempeuh na kimuh nop leh Kiginni ni-in pawi neu khat i nei thei hi.

records.english: Have you decided what to pack first?
records.zomi: Bang masa tuam ding hiam na khen khin hiam?

records.english: Rather than one big farewell, I'd like to have dinner with each of my friends separately.
records.zomi: Kikhenna lian khat sangin ka lawm khat ciat tawh nitak an ne ka deih hi.

records.english: By this time on Sunday, my sister will be halfway across the ocean.
records.zomi: Nipini tu hun ciangin ka sanggam nu tuipi laizang ah a om ding hi.

records.english: We're moving to the coast at the end of next month.
records.zomi: A zom kha tawp ciangin tuipi gei ah i kitawn ding hi.

records.english: Before we go, I'll leave a note for the new family explaining which window sticks.
records.zomi: I pai ma-in innkuan thak adingin tukvuang bang in a kiat hiam a gen siang laikhak khat ka nusia ding hi.

records.english: I'll also tell them that the old man next door likes to be greeted every morning.
records.zomi: A kiang inn-a pu upa in zingsang simin hopih a deih hi, cih zong ka hilh ding hi.

records.english: However hard it is to leave, I'm sure this new job will open doors for me.
records.zomi: Nusiat bangzah in haksa zongin hih nasep thak in kongkhak hong hon ding hi, ka thei hi.

records.english: On the last day of primary school, we're going to sign each other's shirts with markers.
records.zomi: Sang neu ni nunung pen-in i puan-akhi te tungah khedal tawh i min i kigelh sak ding hi.

records.english: When the time comes to go, I'll hug everyone quickly and walk away without looking back.
records.zomi: Pai hun a tun ciangin mi khempeuh manlang takin ka kawi ding a, nung lam en lo-in ka pai ding hi.

records.english: My uncle will probably say, "Don't forget where you come from," as he always does.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in a ngeina bangin, “Koi pan na hong hiam mangngilh kei in,” a ci kha ding hi.

records.english: I really do hope we'll stay friends after you move to the other side of the country.
records.zomi: Gam gal lam ah na kitawn khit ciangin lawm-in i om lai ding ka lametna taktak ahi hi.

records.english: Perhaps I'll be able to visit at Christmas, if I can save enough for the ticket.
records.zomi: Lakkhia ding lai man ka kikoih zawh leh Christmas ciangin ka veh thei kha ding hi.

records.english: Will you be able to take your guitar on the plane?
records.zomi: Na guitar vanleng tungah na tawi thei ding hiam?

records.english: Is it all right if I leave early to say goodbye to my brother?
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal goodbye ka cih nadingin ma-in ka pai thei ding hiam?

records.english: When my best friend moves abroad, we'll give her a video made of messages from everyone in our class.
records.zomi: Ka lawm hoih pen gamdang ah a kitawn ciangin i sang inndei mi khempeuh' message tawh kibawl video khat i pia ding hi.

records.english: Each of us is going to record a short clip on our phones, and my brother will put them together.
records.zomi: I khat ciat in i phone tungah video tom khat i la ding a, ka sanggam pasal in a gawm ding hi.

records.english: Do you think the cat will remember us when we come back?
records.zomi: I ciah kik ciangin zawh in hong phawk lai ding hiam, na ci hiam?

records.english: The house keys are going to be left with the agent on Friday afternoon.
records.zomi: Inn tawh te Laithai ni nitak lam ciangin inn zuakpa kiangah kinusia ding hi.

records.english: Could my cousin have your bicycle while you're away, since she needs one for school?
records.zomi: Na om lohna sungin ka sanggam nu in sang adingin a kisam ahih manin na siiksakol a zang thei ding hiam?

records.english: May I use your room while you're away?
records.zomi: Na om lohna sungin na inndei ka zang thei ding hiam?

records.english: Everyone, please write a few words in Mai's goodbye book before she leaves tomorrow.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh aw, zingciang Mai a pai ma-in a goodbye laibu ah kammal tawmno gelh un.

records.english: Next week, I'll be saying goodbye to the town where I've lived all my life.
records.zomi: A zom kal ciangin ka nuntak sung ka omna khuapi kiangah goodbye ka ci ding hi.

records.english: Will you call us as soon as you land?
records.zomi: Na tun pah ciangin hong sam ding hiam?

records.english: It would mean a great deal to me if you came to the station, even for five minutes.
records.zomi: Minit nga bek hi zongin meileng dinna ah na hong leh keimah adingin a thupi mahmah ding hi.

records.english: Which part of this town do you think you'll dream about?
records.zomi: Hih khuapi-a mun bang na mang ding hiam, na ci hiam?

records.english: Send me a photo of the view from your new window.
records.zomi: Na tukvuang thak pan mun lim hong khak in.

records.english: What will you give your students as a parting gift?
records.zomi: Na sangnaupangte kikhenna letsong bang na pia ding hiam?

records.english: In a few years, I imagine we'll laugh about how dramatic this goodbye was.
records.zomi: Kum tawmno khit ciangin hih goodbye bangzah in a lamdang hiam i nuihsan ding hi, ka ngaihsun hi.

records.english: While we're abroad next year, our neighbors have agreed to look after our cat.
records.zomi: A zom kum gamdang ah i om sungin i inn vengte in i zawh kem dingin a phal uh hi.

records.english: My grandmother is planning to slip a letter into my brother's suitcase before he leaves.
records.zomi: Ka pi in ka sanggam pasal a pai ma-in a van bawm sungah lai khat koih dingin a geel hi.

records.english: He won't find it until he unpacks, which is exactly what she wants.
records.zomi: A van a lak khiat ma-in a mu lo ding a, tua bek amah in a deih hi.

records.english: When are you leaving for the city?
records.zomi: Bang ciangin khuapi ah na pai ding hiam?

records.english: On the early bus on Monday, so I'll say goodbye on Sunday night.
records.zomi: Pizing ni-in zingsang bus tawh, tua ahih manin Nipini zanin goodbye ka ci ding hi.

records.english: My brother is going to drive our grandmother to the airport so that she can say goodbye in person.
records.zomi: I pi in mimal-in goodbye a cih theih nadingin ka sanggam pasal in vanlengtual ah a tawi ding hi.

records.english: Will the goodbye at the airport be quick, or will the whole family come?
records.zomi: Vanlengtual-a goodbye pen manlang ding hiam, innkuan bup a hong ding hiam?

records.english: Just my parents, because a crowd at the gate would make it much harder.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa bek, kongpi ah mi tam in a haksa zaw sak mahmah ding ahih manin.

records.english: Next term, I'm going away to boarding school for the first time.
records.zomi: A zom hun ciangin om-in kah sang ah ka pai masa ding hi.

records.english: On my last Saturday at home, my friends and I are going to have a picnic by the river.
records.zomi: Inn-a ka Kiginni nunung pen-in ka lawmte leh kei in gun kiang ah khualzin an i ne ding hi.

records.english: We've promised to send each other a voice message every Sunday evening.
records.zomi: Nipini nitak simin aw message i kikhak ding a i kiciam hi.

records.english: I do want my children to know their cousins well, even though they live far away.
records.zomi: Gamla-in a om uh hangin ka ta te in a sanggamte hoih takin a theih ding uh ka deih taktak hi.

records.english: Can my nephew stay with us while his parents are abroad?
records.zomi: A nu leh a pa gamdang ah a om sungin ka tanau i kiang ah a om thei ding hiam?

records.english: I really do hope my brothers will stay close after our parents are gone.
records.zomi: I nu leh i pa a om nawn loh khit ciangin ka sanggam pasalte a kinai lai ding uh ka lametna taktak ahi hi.

records.english: Next year, our twins will go to different secondary schools for the first time.
records.zomi: A zom kum ciangin i apeng te a masa pen-in sang lian tuamtuam ah a pai ding uh hi.

records.english: They've never been apart for a single day, so we're a little nervous about it.
records.zomi: Ni khat zong a kikhen ngei kei uh ahih manin tawmno i lungkham hi.

records.english: Taking over the shop will be a big responsibility for my brother, but he's ready for it.
records.zomi: Zuakna inn la in ka sanggam pasal adingin mawhpuakna lian ahi ding hi, ahi zongin a kiman khin hi.

records.english: You mustn't tell your brother about the surprise party.
records.zomi: Lamdang pawi thu na sanggam pasal na hilh lo ding hi.

records.english: By the time my son is ten, he'll have three younger siblings.
records.zomi: Ka tapa kum sawm a phak ciangin a nau thum a nei khin ding hi.

records.english: Imagine how quiet the house will be when the twins go to different schools!
records.zomi: Apeng te sang tuamtuam ah a pai ciangun inn bangzah in a daih ding hiam ngaihsun in!

records.english: I'll drive my parents to the village every Sunday so that they can see their old friends.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in a lawm luite a muh theih nadingun Nipini simin khua ah ka tawi ding hi.

records.english: Whatever happens with my job, I'll make sure I'm home for the family dinners.
records.zomi: Ka nasep bang piang zongin innkuan nitak an adingin inn ah ka om ding hi.

records.english: The old family house will be repaired before my parents move back into it.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa a lut kik ma-un innkuan inn lui kibawl dam ding hi.

records.english: Will she be allowed to travel alone at fifteen?
records.zomi: Kum sawm leh nga a phak ciangin amah bek-in khualzin dingin kiphal ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, as long as an airline staff member stays with her during the change of planes.
records.zomi: Kiphal ding hi, vanleng kikhek lai-in vanleng nasem khat in a zui leh.

records.english: If we start a family video call every week, the children won't grow up as strangers to their cousins.
records.zomi: Kal simin innkuan video call i kipat leh naupangte in a sanggamte tawh theih loh mi bangin a khang lo ding uh hi.

records.english: A new room is going to be built at the back for my grandmother.
records.zomi: Ka pi adingin a nung lam ah inndei thak khat kibawl ding hi.

records.english: The family photos will be scanned and shared with every cousin next month.
records.zomi: Innkuan lim te a zom kha in kiscan ding a, sanggam khempeuh kiangah kikhak ding hi.

records.english: Are your parents excited about becoming grandparents?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa pu leh pi suak ding a kipak uh hiam?

records.english: This time next year, my sister will be living on the other side of the world.
records.zomi: A zom kum tu hun ciangin ka sanggam nu leitung gal lam ah a om ding hi.

records.english: In a few years, I imagine my children will be teaching their own little cousins to swim.
records.zomi: Kum tawmno khit ciangin ka ta te in amau' sanggam neute tuipeek a sin sak ding uh hi, ka ngaihsun hi.

records.english: Shall we call Grandpa on his birthday, or visit him instead?
records.zomi: Pu a pianni-in phone tawh i sam ding hiam, i veh zaw ding hiam?

records.english: My cousin will help my son with his maths when he starts secondary school.
records.zomi: Ka tapa sang lian a kah kipat ciangin ka sanggam in a kisim sinna ah a huh ding hi.

records.english: Will you take the baby to the village to meet everyone before winter?
records.zomi: Khuavot ma-in mi khempeuh a kimuh nadingin naungek khua ah na tawi ding hiam?

records.english: Shall we plan a surprise trip for our parents' anniversary?
records.zomi: I nu leh i pa' kiteenna kum tawpna adingin lamdang khualzinna khat i geel ding hiam?

records.english: Perhaps the cousins could spend the summer together at the farm next year.
records.zomi: A zom kum ciangin sanggamte khal bup lo inn ah khawm-in a om thei kha ding uh hi.

records.english: My brother said, "I'll be the best uncle in the world, just wait and see."
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in, “Leitung bup ah pa neu hoih pen ka hi ding hi, ngak un la en un,” a ci hi.

records.english: This summer, my daughter is going to visit her cousins abroad on her own.
records.zomi: Hih khal in ka tanu in gamdang-a a sanggamte amah bek-in a veh ding hi.

records.english: When my uncle steps back from the business, my older brother is going to run the family shop.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu sumbawlna pan a khawl ciangin ka u pasal in innkuan zuakna inn a kem ding hi.

records.english: Everyone, next Sunday we're going to plan Grandma's eightieth birthday, so please come.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh aw, a zom Nipini ciangin Pi' pianni kum sawm giatna i geel ding ahih manin hong pai un.

records.english: Should we ask our parents to come and live closer to us one day?
records.zomi: Ni khat ciangin i nu leh i pa i kiang ah hong om dingin i ngen ding hiam?

records.english: My four-year-old son is getting a baby brother in June.
records.zomi: Ka tapa kum li June kha-in a nau pasal a ngah ding hi.

records.english: He says he's going to teach the baby how to climb trees and catch frogs.
records.zomi: Naungek singkung kai leh uikang man dan a sin sak ding hi, a ci hi.

records.english: We've told him the baby won't be ready for frogs for a few years, but he's not convinced.
records.zomi: Naungek kum tawmno sung uikang adingin a kiman nai lo ding hi, i ci a, ahi zongin a um kei hi.

records.english: Would it be all right if my sister brought her children to the picnic?
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu in a ta te khualzin an nekna ah a tawi leh a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: We're saving money so that our children can study wherever they choose.
records.zomi: I ta te in a deihna mun peuh ah a sin theih nadingun sum i kikoih hi.

records.english: If my brother gets the job in the city, he'll be able to visit us every weekend.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in khuapi ah nasep a ngah leh kal tawp simin hong veh thei ding hi.

records.english: Next spring, I'm going to become an aunt for the first time.
records.zomi: A zom spring ciangin a masa pen-in ni ka suak ding hi.

records.english: I've promised my sister that I'll stay with her for the first two weeks after the baby is born.
records.zomi: Naungek a suah khit kal nih masa sung amah kiang ah ka om ding hi, ci-in ka sanggam nu ka ciam hi.

records.english: I'm going to do the cooking and the washing so that she can rest.
records.zomi: A tawlngak theih nadingin an ka huan ding a, puan ka sil ding hi.

records.english: How will you and your siblings decide who looks after your parents?
records.zomi: Nang leh na sanggamte in na nu leh na pa kua in a kem ding hiam bangci-in na khen ding uh hiam?

records.english: We'll sit down together at Christmas and make a plan that's fair to everyone.
records.zomi: Christmas ciangin khawm-in i tu ding a, mi khempeuh adingin a dik geelna khat i bawl ding hi.

records.english: Which of your cousins is getting married next?
records.zomi: Na sanggamte lakah kua in a zom ah a ki-ten ding hiam?

records.english: My grandmother is moving in with us next month.
records.zomi: Ka pi a zom kha in i kiang ah om dingin a hong ding hi.

records.english: We're going to give her the downstairs room so that she won't have to climb the stairs.
records.zomi: Kahlei a kai ding a kisam lohna dingin a nuai lam inndei i pia ding hi.

records.english: The children have already asked if they can have breakfast with her every morning.
records.zomi: Naupangte in zingsang simin amah tawh zingsang an ne thei ding hiam a dong khin uh hi.

records.english: When is your cousin's baby due?
records.zomi: Na sanggam' naungek bang ciangin a suak ding hiam?

records.english: Kids, when your little cousin arrives, I'd like you to show her all your toys.
records.zomi: Naupangte, na sanggam neu a tun ciangin na kimawlna van khempeuh lak dingin ka deih hi.

records.english: Whose house will be first?
records.zomi: Kua' inn masa ding hiam?

records.english: My oldest brother, because his house is the biggest.
records.zomi: Ka u pasal upa pen, a inn a lian pen ahih manin.

records.english: From next year, each of us will host the New Year meal in turn, starting with the eldest.
records.zomi: A zom kum pan kipan, a upa pen pan kipan-in, i khat ciat in Kum Thak an nekna i bawl ding hi.

records.english: When the grandchildren are grown, I hope we'll still gather around one table once a month.
records.zomi: Tute a lian khit uh ciangin kha khat khatvei dawhkan khat kiim ah i kikhawm lai ding ka lametna ahi hi.

records.english: Do you think your son will be jealous of the new baby?
records.zomi: Na tapa in naungek thak a thikzawh ding hiam, na ci hiam?

records.english: My aunt is going to knit a blanket for each of her grandchildren this winter.
records.zomi: Hih khuavot in ka ni in a tute khat ciat adingin puannak khat ciat a phiat ding hi.

records.english: Rather than letting the old quarrels continue, my sister and I plan to invite everyone to one big lunch.
records.zomi: Kinialna luite a om lai sak sangin ka sanggam nu leh kei in mi khempeuh sun an lian khat ah i sam ding hi.

records.english: As our parents get older, my sisters and I will share the job of looking after them.
records.zomi: I nu leh i pa a upat semsem ciangin ka sanggam nute leh kei in amau' kemna nasep i hawm ding hi.

records.english: Grandpa told us, "When I'm ninety, I want all of you in one photograph."
records.zomi: Pu in, “Kum sawm kua ka phak ciangin na khempeuh un lim khat sungah ka deih hi,” hong ci hi.

records.english: Caring for our parents together will either bring us closer or test us in new ways.
records.zomi: I nu leh i pa khawm-in kem in hong kinaisak zaw ding hiam, lampi thak tawh hong sin ding hiam.

records.english: It would mean a lot to my grandmother if all her grandchildren came home for Easter.
records.zomi: Ka pi' tute khempeuh Easter ciangin inn ah a ciah uh leh ka pi adingin a thupi mahmah ding hi.

records.english: Please don't let the baby near the stove when she starts walking.
records.zomi: Naungek a pai kipat ciangin meikhuk kiang ah a nai kei ding hi.

records.english: Are your grandparents coming to the wedding next month?
records.zomi: Na pu leh na pi a zom kha-a mopawi ah a hong ding uh hiam?

records.english: Shall we move the children's beds into one room so that the baby can have her own?
records.zomi: Naungek in amah' inndei a neih theih nadingin naupangte lupna inndei khat ah i koih ding hiam?

records.english: My son's school trip might be cancelled if the road isn't repaired in time.
records.zomi: A hun takin lampi kibawl dam kei leh ka tapa' sang khualzinna kikhak kha ding hi.

records.english: It would mean a great deal to my husband if his parents could hold the baby before they return home.
records.zomi: Inn a ciah ma-un a nu leh a pa in naungek a pawm thei uh leh ka pasal adingin a thupi mahmah ding hi.

records.english: Where are you going to celebrate your twenty-fifth anniversary?
records.zomi: Na kiteenna kum sawm nih leh ngana bang ah na lungdam ding uh hiam?

records.english: In the village where we met, with as many of our old school friends as we can find.
records.zomi: I kimuhna khua ah, i sang lawm luite i muh zah tawh.

records.english: The children's swing will be moved to the shady side of the garden before summer.
records.zomi: Khal ma-in naupangte lawk huan sung-a mun hiau lam ah kitawn ding hi.

records.english: Do you think we'll be strict parents or relaxed ones?
records.zomi: Nu leh pa khauh i hi ding hiam, a nem i hi ding hiam, na ci hiam?

records.english: Could I start work an hour earlier so that I can collect the children at three?
records.zomi: Nai thum ciangin naupangte ka lak theih nadingin nai khat ma-in nasep ka kipan thei ding hiam?

records.english: Will you ask your mother to stay for the first week after the baby arrives?
records.zomi: Naungek a tun khit kal masa sungin na nu om dingin na ngen ding hiam?
