records.zomi: Naupangte in a ma zan ciangin sang adingin amau' sun an amau' in a bawl ding uh hi.

records.english: My husband will collect them from school, and my mother will stay with them until I get home.
records.zomi: Ka pasal in sang pan a la ding a, ka inn tun mateng ka nu in a kem ding hi.

records.english: Next year, when our daughter starts work, she'll pay a small amount toward the household bills.
records.zomi: A zom kum ciangin i tanu nasep a kipat ciangin inn laimal adingin sum tawmno a pia ding hi.

records.english: Kids, when Grandma comes to stay, you'll need to keep the bathroom tidy every morning.
records.zomi: Naupangte, Pi hong om ciangin zingsang simin kisilna inn na siangsak ding uh a kisam ding hi.

records.english: Next month, I'm moving into a flat with three people I've never met.
records.zomi: A zom kha in ka kimuh ngei loh mi thum tawh inn khat ah ka om ding hi.

records.english: We're going to agree on who uses which shelf in the fridge before anyone unpacks.
records.zomi: Kuamah in a van a lak khiat ma-in vot sak setna sung-a van koihna kua in bang a zang ding hiam i kilem ding hi.

records.english: Then we'll set up a cleaning plan in a shared app, so that nobody can say they forgot.
records.zomi: Tua ciangin kuamah in ka mangngilh hi, a cih theih lohna dingin kihawm app khat ah sianseh geelna i bawl ding hi.

records.english: Once we buy a dishwasher next year, there'll be no more arguments about the dishes.
records.zomi: A zom kum ciangin kuang silna setna i lei khit ciangin kuang thu-a kinialna om nawn lo ding hi.

records.english: Do you really think a machine will stop your children arguing?
records.zomi: Setna khat in na ta te' kinialna a khawlsak ding hi, na ci taktak hiam?

records.english: Is it all right if I use your drill to put up the new shelves?
records.zomi: Van koihna thak khai dingin na thau-it bawlna ka zang thei ding hiam?

records.english: Everyone, from tomorrow each of you will be in charge of one room for the whole week.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh aw, zingciang pan kipan na khat ciat un kal bup inndei khat ciat na kem ding uh hi.

records.english: If everyone does one small job each evening, the weekend will be free for something fun.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh in nitak simin nasep neu khat a sep uh leh kal tawp pen bang nuam bawl nadingin a om ngawng ding hi.

records.english: Teaching the children to cook now will save them a great deal of trouble when they live alone.
records.zomi: Tu-in naupangte an huan sin sak in amau' bek a om ciangun haksatna tampi pan a hotkhia ding hi.

records.english: The washing machine is going to be repaired on Thursday, so save your dirty clothes until then.
records.zomi: Puan silna setna Laizing ni-in kibawl dam ding ahih manin tua dong na puan nin te kem un.

records.english: Sharing a flat with strangers will either teach me patience or teach me to live alone.
records.zomi: Theih loh mite tawh inn hawm in thuakzawhna hong sin sak ding hiam, kia-in om dan hong sin sak ding hi.

records.english: However busy the term gets, the children will still be responsible for their own rooms.
records.zomi: Sang hun bangzah in buai zongin naupangte in amau' inndei a kem lai ding uh hi.

records.english: Now that we're married, how shall we share the cooking and the cleaning?
records.zomi: Tu-in i ki-ten khin ahih manin an huan leh sianseh bangci-in i hawm ding hiam?

records.english: We could both cook and both clean, and see how it goes.
records.zomi: I nih in an i huan ding a, i nih in i sianseh ding a, bangci-in a pai hiam i en thei hi.

records.english: Once the solar heater is working, our electricity bill should fall quite a lot.
records.zomi: Ni vak tui lumsakna a sep khit ciangin i mei-ok laimal a niam mahmah ding hi.

records.english: My son announced, "When I'm twelve, I'm going to cook dinner for everyone every Friday."
records.zomi: Ka tapa in, “Kum sawm leh nih ka phak ciangin Laithai ni simin mi khempeuh adingin nitak an ka huan ding hi,” ci-in a pulak hi.

records.english: How often will the new flatmates need to clean the bathroom?
records.zomi: Inn hawm thakte in bangzah vei kisilna inn a siang sak ding uh hiam?

records.english: We're going to repaint the kitchen together next weekend.
records.zomi: A zom kal tawp ciangin an huanna khawm-in i nul kik ding hi.

records.english: I'll leave a list on the fridge so that the house sitter knows when to water the plants.
records.zomi: Inn kempa in pak te bang ciangin tui buak ding hiam a theih nadingin vot sak setna tungah lai khat ka nusia ding hi.

records.english: This summer, my daughter is going to earn some pocket money by cleaning the neighbors' windows.
records.zomi: Hih khal in ka tanu in inn vengte' tukvuang nul-in zat ding sum a ngah ding hi.

records.english: Will you need a ladder, or are the windows low enough to reach?
records.zomi: Kahlei na kisam ding hiam, tukvuang te tun theih dingin a niam hiam?

records.english: I do want my sons to know how to look after a home before they leave.
records.zomi: Ka tapate a pai ma-un inn kem dan a theih ding uh ka deih taktak hi.

records.english: It would help me enormously if someone else took charge of paying the bills.
records.zomi: Mi dang khat in laimal piak a kem leh hong huh mahmah ding hi.

records.english: My mother said, "When you have your own home, you'll understand why I wanted the floor dry."
records.zomi: Ka nu in, “Nangma' inn na neih ciangin bang hangin inn phah keu ka deih hiam na thei ding hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: Before my son leaves for university in September, he's going to learn five simple dishes.
records.zomi: September kha-in ka tapa sangpi ah a pai ma-in an baih nga a sin ding hi.

records.english: His grandmother has promised to teach him one every Sunday until he goes.
records.zomi: A pi in a pai mateng Nipini simin khat ciat sin sak dingin a ciam hi.

records.english: He'll also have to iron his own shirt for the farewell dinner, which he says is the hardest part.
records.zomi: Kikhenna nitak an adingin a puan-akhi amah in a phawk ding a kisam a, tua a haksa pen ahi hi, a ci hi.

records.english: By the end of the summer, we'll have cleared out the whole attic.
records.zomi: Khal a bei ciangin innkhum nuai-a van koihna bup i siang khin ding hi.

records.english: A solar water heater will be installed on our roof next month.
records.zomi: A zom kha in i innkhum tungah ni vak tui lumsakna kikoih ding hi.

records.english: After that, the hot water won't run out halfway through the children's baths.
records.zomi: Tua khit ciangin naupangte' kisil laizang ah tui lum a bei nawn lo ding hi.

records.english: If the roof isn't mended before the rains, the children's bedroom will be soaked again.
records.zomi: Guah hun ma-in innkhum kibawl dam kei leh naupangte' inndei a dik kik ding hi.

records.english: Which jobs will the children be old enough to do next year?
records.zomi: A zom kum ciangin naupangte in nasep bang a sep thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: From now on, we'll speak our own language at dinner so that the children don't lose it.
records.zomi: Tu pan kipan naupangte in i pau a mansuah lohna dingun nitak an ah i pau mah i zang ding hi.

records.english: When will we have time to sit down and plan next year's budget together?
records.zomi: A zom kum sum zat geel khawm-in i geel nadingin bang ciangin hun i nei ding hiam?

records.english: Once the decision is made, I don't want anyone reopening the argument at every meal.
records.zomi: Thukhenna a kibawl khit ciangin an nekna khempeuh ah kuamah in kinialna a hon kik ding ka deih kei hi.

records.english: My son announced, "If we move, I'm taking the dog and the football."
records.zomi: Ka tapa in, “I kitawn leh ui leh football ka tawi ding hi,” ci-in a pulak hi.

records.english: Next month, we're going to decide whether to move closer to the town with the better secondary school.
records.zomi: A zom kha in sang lian hoih zaw a om khuapi kiang ah i kitawn ding hiam i khen ding hi.

records.english: Before the meeting, each of the children will write down what they'd gain and what they'd miss.
records.zomi: Kikhopna ma-in naupangte in a khat ciat in bang a ngah ding uh a, bang a lungngai ding uh hiam a gelh ding uh hi.

records.english: We'll read the lists aloud together, and nobody will be allowed to laugh at anyone else's.
records.zomi: Gelhna te khawm-in aw-in i sim ding a, kuamah in mi dang' gelh a nuihsan thei lo ding hi.

records.english: I do want everyone to have a say, even the youngest.
records.zomi: A neu pen zong, mi khempeuh in gen ding nei ding ka deih taktak hi.

records.english: Nobody should feel pressured to agree on the first evening.
records.zomi: Nitak masa pen-in kuamah kilem dingin a kinen lo ding hi.

records.english: This time next year, we could be living in a new town with a whole new school.
records.zomi: A zom kum tu hun ciangin sang thak bup nei khuapi thak khat ah i om thei hi.

records.english: I'll bring a notebook and write down everyone's ideas so that nothing gets forgotten.
records.zomi: Bangmah a kimangngilh lohna dingin laibu khat ka tawi ding a, mi khempeuh ngaihsutna ka gelh ding hi.

records.english: However the discussion goes, we'll finish the evening with dessert, as always.
records.zomi: Kikupna bangci-in pai zongin a ngeina bangin an lim tawh nitak i khak ding hi.

records.english: Our neighbor, who has eight children, said, "Give everyone a voice, even the baby."
records.zomi: Ta giat a nei i inn vengnu in, “Mi khempeuh, naungek zong, gen ding piak un,” a ci hi.

records.english: Which way are you going to vote on Saturday?
records.zomi: Kiginni ni-in lam bang ah na teel ding hiam?

records.english: For the panels, because the electricity bills keep rising.
records.zomi: Ni vak phek te adingin, mei-ok laimal a khang den ahih manin.

records.english: From next year, each of our children will manage a small monthly allowance of their own.
records.zomi: A zom kum pan kipan i ta te khat ciat in kha sim sum neu khat amau' in a kem ding uh hi.

records.english: We're going to sit down with them first and explain how saving works.
records.zomi: Sum kikoih bangci-in a sem hiam a masa-in amau' tawh i tu ding a, i gen siang ding hi.

records.english: My cousins and I are thinking of opening a small grocery shop together.
records.zomi: Ka sanggamte leh kei in khawm-in an zuakna inn neu khat hon dingin i ngaihsun hi.

records.english: We'll meet at my uncle's house next weekend to talk about money before anything else.
records.zomi: A dang khempeuh ma-in sum thu kikum dingin a zom kal tawp ciangin ka pa neu' inn ah i kimu ding hi.

records.english: If we can't agree on that, we've promised each other that we'll stay friends and drop the idea.
records.zomi: Tua thu-ah i kilem zo kei leh lawm-in i om lai ding a, ngaihsutna i khawl ding hi, ci-in i kiciam hi.

records.english: Is anyone going to object if we invite your cousins to the meeting?
records.zomi: Kikhopna ah na sanggamte i sam leh kuamah in a nial ding hiam?

records.english: Shall we order food so that nobody has to cook on meeting night?
records.zomi: Kikhopna zanin kuamah an a huan lohna dingin an i ngen ding hiam?

records.english: Please don't announce anything until everyone has arrived.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh a tun mateng bangmah pulak kei in.

records.english: In ten years, I imagine our children will be running these meetings without us.
records.zomi: Kum sawm khit ciangin i ta te in kei te om lo-in hih kikhopna te a kem ding uh hi, ka ngaihsun hi.

records.english: Children, tomorrow evening you'll each get five minutes to say what you think about the move.
records.zomi: Naupangte, zingciang nitak ciangin kitawnna thu-a na ngaihsutna gen dingin na khat ciat un minit nga na ngah ding uh hi.

records.english: The money for the trip is going to be divided equally between the three children.
records.zomi: Khualzinna sum pen naupang thum kikal ah kibang-in kikhen ding hi.

records.english: If we move, my daughter will have to leave the football team she's played with for six years.
records.zomi: I kitawn leh ka tanu in kum guk sung a kimawlpih football pawl a nusia ding a kisam ding hi.

records.english: If my parents agree, I'm going to spend next summer working on my uncle's farm.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa a phal uh leh a zom khal ciangin ka pa neu' lo ah ka sem ding hi.

records.english: Can we postpone the meeting until your father is back from his trip?
records.zomi: Na pa a khualzinna pan a ciah mateng kikhopna i nawlkhin thei ding hiam?

records.english: I really do hope we can agree without anyone storming out this time.
records.zomi: Tu-in kuamah a heh-in a pusuak lo-in i kilem thei ding ka lametna taktak ahi hi.

records.english: For the first time, our two teenagers are going to chair the family meeting on Sunday.
records.zomi: A masa pen-in i khangno nih in Nipini ni-in innkuan kikhopna a kem ding uh hi.

records.english: They've already written an agenda and stuck it to the fridge with a magnet.
records.zomi: Kikupna thu te a gelh khin uh a, vot sak setna ah a kilh khin uh hi.

records.english: Item three says, "Later bedtimes for everyone over fourteen," which I suspect will be discussed at length.
records.zomi: A thumna in, “Kum sawm leh li tung mi khempeuh adingin ihmut hun nunung zaw,” a ci a, tua pen sawt takin kikum ding hi, ka ngaihsun hi.

records.english: Could you make a list of questions for the bank before we decide?
records.zomi: I thukhen ma-in bank adingin dotna gelh khat na bawl thei ding hiam?

records.english: What should we do if the discussion turns into an argument again?
records.zomi: Kikupna in kinialna a suak kik leh bang i bawl ding hiam?

records.english: The plan will be explained to the younger children in simple words.
records.zomi: Geelna pen naupang neu zawte kiangah kammal baih tawh kigen siang ding hi.

records.english: We might ask a teacher we trust to help us understand the school options.
records.zomi: Sang teelna te i theih nadingin i muan saya khat in hong huh dingin i ngen kha ding hi.

records.english: Letting the teenagers chair the meeting will show them that their opinions matter.
records.zomi: Khangnote in kikhopna kem sak in amau' ngaihsutna a thupi hi, cih a lak ding hi.

records.english: Write down your three biggest worries before Sunday.
records.zomi: Nipini ma-in na lungkhamna lian pen thum gelh in.

records.english: Have you thought about what you'll say to Dad?
records.zomi: Pa kiangah bang na gen ding hiam na ngaihsun khin hiam?

records.english: Who will keep the notes during the meeting?
records.zomi: Kikhopna lai-in kua in thu a gelh ding hiam?

records.english: If we keep talking openly, I'm sure we'll find a plan that works for all of us.
records.zomi: Kician takin i kikum lai leh i khempeuh adingin a sem thei geelna khat i mu ding hi, ka thei hi.

records.english: How do you think your parents will take the news?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa in tua thu bangci-in a sang ding uh hiam, na ci hiam?

records.english: My father will worry about the money, but my mother will probably start planning a restaurant.
records.zomi: Ka pa in sum thu a lungkham ding a, ahi zongin ka nu in an zuakna inn a geel kipan kha ding hi.

records.english: Will the children be allowed to answer in the language they use at school?
records.zomi: Naupangte in sang-a a zat pau uh tawh a dawng thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: Only for the first month, and then we'll see how they're managing.
records.zomi: Kha masa sung bek, tua ciangin bangci-in a om uh hiam i en ding hi.

records.english: At the next meeting, all phones will go into a basket by the door.
records.zomi: A zom kikhopna ah phone khempeuh kongkhak kiang-a empeng sungah koih ding hi.

records.english: Nobody will interrupt anyone else, and whoever breaks the rule will make the tea.
records.zomi: Kuamah in mi dang' thu a tan lo ding a, thukham a palsat peuhpeuh in tea a bawl ding hi.

records.english: It would mean a lot to my parents if we asked for their advice before we decided.
records.zomi: I thukhen ma-in ka nu leh ka pa thuhilhna i ngen leh amaute adingin a thupi mahmah ding hi.

records.english: Do you think it's fair for the children to have an equal vote?
records.zomi: Naupangte in teelna kibang a neih uh dik hi, na ci hiam?

records.english: Everyone, the meeting starts at seven, so please eat before you come.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh aw, kikhopna nai sagih ciangin a kipan ding ahih manin na hong ma-un ne un.

records.english: Could we hold the meeting at the park, where everyone is calmer?
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh a lungsim a nop zawhna huanpi ah kikhopna i nei thei ding hiam?

records.english: The final decision will be explained to Grandma first, out of respect.
records.zomi: Thukhenna nunung pen zahtakna-in Pi kiangah a masa-in kigen siang ding hi.

records.english: The old house will probably be sold if nobody in the family wants to live in it.
records.zomi: Innkuan ah kuamah in om a deih kei uh leh inn lui kizuak kha ding hi.

records.english: Whatever the vote decides, I'm going to support it without complaining.
records.zomi: Teelna in bang a khen zongin phun lo-in ka huh ding hi.

records.english: At Sunday lunch, my sister is going to tell our parents that she's leaving her job to train as a chef.
records.zomi: Nipini sun an ah ka sanggam nu in an huanpa hih sin dingin a nasep a nusia ding hi, ci-in i nu leh i pa a hilh ding hi.

records.english: Next Saturday, the family is going to vote on whether to spend our savings on solar panels or a second-hand car.
records.zomi: A zom Kiginni ni-in innkuan in i sum kikoih ni vak phek adingin zang ding hiam, mawtaw lui khat adingin zang ding hiam a teel ding uh hi.

records.english: You're not to tell your little brother about the move until we've talked to him together.
records.zomi: Khawm-in i kikup ma-in na nau pasal kiangah kitawnna thu na gen lo ding hi.

records.english: My little brother's feelings will be hurt if we don't let him speak at the meeting.
records.zomi: Kikhopna ah gen dingin i phal kei leh ka nau pasal' lungsim a na ding hi.

records.english: By the end of the month, we'll have made a decision about the house.
records.zomi: Kha tawp ciangin inn thu-a thukhenna i bawl khin ding hi.

records.english: By the time Grandpa comes home from hospital, his room will have been rearranged.
records.zomi: Pu siavuan inn pan inn a tun ciangin a inndei kikhek khin ding hi.

records.english: I'm going to ask for a four-day week so that I can collect the children on Fridays.
records.zomi: Laithai ni-in naupangte ka lak theih nadingin ni li nasep kal ka ngen ding hi.

records.english: From September, my cousin and I will look after each other's children two Saturdays a month.
records.zomi: September pan kipan ka sanggam leh kei in kha khat Kiginni nih i kitate kem tuah ding hi.

records.english: We're going to put picture labels on the kitchen cupboards so that Grandma can find things easily.
records.zomi: Pi in baih takin van a muh theih nadingin an huanna van koihna te ah lim ciamtehna i kilh ding hi.

records.english: Will she be upset if we change the kitchen around?
records.zomi: An huanna i khek leh a lungkham ding hiam?

records.english: Remind me to buy Grandpa a large-print calendar for next year.
records.zomi: A zom kum adingin laimal lian kalendar khat Pu adingin lei dingin hong phawksak in.

records.english: This summer, I'm going to volunteer in the vegetable garden at the care home.
records.zomi: Hih khal in upa kemna inn-a anteh huan ah thalawp-in ka sem ding hi.

records.english: The residents will tell me what to plant, and I'll do the digging.
records.zomi: Tua-a omte in bang suan ding hiam hong hilh ding uh a, kei in ka tou ding hi.

records.english: Children, when your great-grandfather visits, you can each show him one thing you've made.
records.zomi: Naupangte, na pu upa a hong ciangin na khat ciat un na bawl khat na lak thei uh hi.

records.english: My grandfather's eyesight is getting worse, and he can no longer read the newspaper.
records.zomi: Ka pu' mit a hoih kei semsem a, laithak a sim zo nawn kei hi.

records.english: From next week, my son is going to read it aloud to him every Wednesday after school.
records.zomi: A zom kal pan kipan ka tapa in Nilai ni sang khit simin aw-in a sim sak ding hi.

records.english: Grandpa has already warned him that he'll want the football results first.
records.zomi: Pu in football dawnna te a masa-in a deih ding hi, ci-in a vaikhak khin hi.

records.english: If the path isn't cleared, someone could slip on the ice and break a hip.
records.zomi: Lampi kisiang kei leh mi khat tuikhal tungah a kipalh-in a phei guh a kitan thei hi.

records.english: Everyone, from next week Grandma will be living with us, so please keep the stairs clear.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh aw, a zom kal pan kipan Pi i kiang ah a om ding ahih manin kahlei siang takin kem un.

records.english: Will you be able to drive your mother to the eye clinic every month?
records.zomi: Kha simin na nu mit siavuan inn ah na tawi thei ding hiam?

records.english: Our neighbor's broken stair rail will be mended before her grandchildren come to stay.
records.zomi: I inn vengnu' kahlei khut lenna kitan a tute a hong om ma-un kibawl dam ding hi.

records.english: I do want my children to learn patience by helping their great-grandmother.
records.zomi: Ka ta te in a pi upa huh-in thuakzawhna a sin ding uh ka deih taktak hi.

records.english: Shall we take Grandma to the market on Saturday, since she enjoys the noise and the colors?
records.zomi: Pi in a ging leh rong tuamtuam a deih ahih manin Kiginni ni-in zuakna mun ah i pi ding hiam?

records.english: When will the baby be old enough to stay with her grandparents for a night?
records.zomi: Naungek bang ciangin a pu leh a pi kiang ah zan khat om thei dingin a lian ding hiam?

records.english: Who will stay with Grandpa when we go to the wedding?
records.zomi: Mopawi ah i pai ciangin kua in Pu a kem ding hiam?

records.english: My brother has offered, as long as he can watch the football with him.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in a ciam hi, amah tawh football a en thei leh.

records.english: Grandpa said, "I'll be ninety next year, and I still want to walk to church on my own."
records.zomi: Pu in, “A zom kum ciangin kum sawm kua ka hi ding a, keimah bek-in pawlpi ah pai ka deih lai hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: Is she old enough to go into the water without one of us?
records.zomi: I lak-ah khat om lo-in tui sungah a lut thei dingin a lian khin hiam?

records.english: Not yet, so I'll be in the pool with her every time.
records.zomi: Lian nai kei hi, tua ahih manin a vekpi ah tuiphuk sungah amah tawh ka om ding hi.

records.english: The baby's sleep will be disturbed if we keep moving her bed around.
records.zomi: A lupna i tawn den leh naungek' ihmut a buai ding hi.

records.english: Next year, my youngest will be old enough to walk to school with her brother.
records.zomi: A zom kum ciangin ka ta neu pen in a u pasal tawh sang ah pai thei dingin a lian ding hi.

records.english: In twenty years, I suppose my children will be the ones arranging my care.
records.zomi: Kum sawm nih khit ciangin ka ta te in kei kemna a geel ding uh hi, ka ngaihsun hi.

records.english: Giving my sister a week off is the least we can do after everything she has done.
records.zomi: A sep khempeuh khit ciangin ka sanggam nu kal khat tawlngak piak pen i bawl theih neu pen ahi hi.

records.english: My son asked, "When I'm older, can I push Grandma's wheelchair by myself?"
records.zomi: Ka tapa in, “Ka lian ciangin Pi' khe nei tutna keimah bek-in ka sawn thei ding hiam?” hong ci hi.

records.english: I'll cook extra on Sundays and take some round to my father's flat.
records.zomi: Nipini simin ka huan behlap ding a, ka pa' inn ah ka tawi ding hi.

records.english: Once the swimming lessons start, the children will be much safer near the river.
records.zomi: Tuipeek sinna a kipat khit ciangin naupangte gun kiang ah a bit zaw mahmah ding uh hi.

records.english: Could you show me how to give the baby her medicine before you go?
records.zomi: Na pai ma-in naungek a zatui piak dan hong lak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Whatever happens, we're not going to leave Grandma alone for the whole day.
records.zomi: Bang piang zongin ni bup Pi kia-in i nusia lo ding hi.

records.english: Ask the doctor whether Grandpa can travel by bus next month.
records.zomi: A zom kha in Pu bus tawh a khualzin thei ding hiam siavuan dong in.

records.english: Beautiful, though the speeches went on far too long.
records.zomi: A hoih mahmah hi, thugen te a sawt lua hangin.

records.english: When I bought my first sewing machine, I had no idea how to thread it.
records.zomi: Ka puan khuina setna masa pen ka lei ciangin a khau bangci-in ka khiak ding hiam ka thei kei hi.

records.english: My neighbor came over with her reading glasses and showed me step by step.
records.zomi: Ka inn vengnu in a lai sim mitlimlang tawh hong pai a, khat zawh khat hong lak hi.

records.english: By the evening, I had made a small bag for my daughter's school books.
records.zomi: Nitak ciangin ka tanu' sang laibu adingin ip neu khat ka bawl khin hi.

records.english: Learning how to ask for help politely is one of the most useful things a child can be taught.
records.zomi: Zahtak takin huh ngen dan sin pen naupang khat kisin sak theih phattuam pen lakah khat ahi hi.

records.english: How are you feeling after the operation?
records.zomi: Zatui bawlna khit ciangin bangci-in na om hiam?

records.english: Much better, although I still can't lift anything heavy.
records.zomi: A hoih zaw mahmah hi, bangmah gik ka dawi zo nai kei hangin.

records.english: My son asked me how airplanes stay in the sky.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in vanleng te van ah bangci-in a om thei uh hiam hong dong hi.

records.english: How can I help my grandmother remember to take her tablets?
records.zomi: Ka pi in a zatui ne dingin a phawk nadingin bangci-in ka huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Put them in a box with the days of the week written on it.
records.zomi: Kal sung ni te kigelh bawm khat sungah koih in.

records.english: If the instructions had explained how to assemble the shelf, it wouldn't have taken us all afternoon.
records.zomi: Vaikhakna in van koihna bangci-in kizom ding hiam a gen siang leh nitak bup a sawt lo ding hi.

records.english: How do I change the language on this phone?
records.zomi: Hih phone tung-a pau bangci-in ka khek ding hiam?

records.english: Go to the settings, and it's the third option from the top.
records.zomi: Settings ah pai inla, a tung pan a thumna ahi hi.

records.english: How the village managed without a doctor for so many years, nobody can quite explain.
records.zomi: Kum tampi sung siavuan om lo-in khua in bangci-in a zo hiam, kuamah in a gen siang zo kei uh hi.

records.english: How kind of you to bring us dinner!
records.zomi: Nitak an hong tawi na hih manin na lungsim hoih mahmah hi!

records.english: Can you show me how to tie this knot?
records.zomi: Hih khih dan hong lak thei ding hiam?

records.english: The nurse showed us how to clean the wound and change the bandage.
records.zomi: Nurse in a liamna sil dan leh puan tuam khek dan hong lak hi.

records.english: How on earth did the cat get onto the roof?
records.zomi: Bangci-in zawh in innkhum tungah a kai thei hiam?

records.english: How long will the repairs to the roof take?
records.zomi: Innkhum bawl dam bangzah sawt ding hiam?

records.english: Two days, if the rain holds off.
records.zomi: Ni nih, guah a zuk kei leh.

records.english: How many children are there in your class?
records.zomi: Na sang inndei ah naupang bangzah a om uh hiam?

records.english: Thirty-two, but four of them are away this week.
records.zomi: Sawm thum leh nih, ahi zongin hih kal ah li a om kei uh hi.

records.english: How did you fix the leak under the sink?
records.zomi: Tuisilna nuai-a tui luang bangci-in na bawl dam hiam?

records.english: I tightened the pipe with a wrench and wrapped some tape around the joint.
records.zomi: Tui khuam ka kheih khauh a, a kizopna ah tape ka tuam hi.

records.english: Nobody explained how the machine worked, so the new workers were afraid to touch it.
records.zomi: Setna bangci-in a sem hiam kuamah in a gen siang kei ahih manin nasem thakte in a khoih ding a lau uh hi.

records.english: I don't know how she manages to work and study at the same time.
records.zomi: Khatvei-in a sep leh a sin bangci-in a zo hiam ka thei kei hi.

records.english: I do want to learn how to swim before the summer holiday.
records.zomi: Khal khawlna ma-in tuipeek sin ka deih taktak hi.

records.english: The bakery's new owner is planning to split the early shift between two bakers.
records.zomi: Moh bawlna neipa thak in zingsang nasep moh bawlpa nih kikal ah khen dingin a geel hi.

records.english: I'll leave detailed notes for the person who takes over my class.
records.zomi: Ka sang inndei a la ding mi adingin thu kician ciamtehna ka nusia ding hi.

records.english: Working shorter weeks could give people the opportunity to rest properly and come back with fresh ideas.
records.zomi: Kal tom zaw nasep in mite hoih takin tawlngak-in ngaihsutna thak tawh a hong kik theih nadingin hun a pia thei hi.

records.english: When will the new photocopier be delivered?
records.zomi: Photocopier thak bang ciangin hong kipuak ding hiam?

records.english: Shall we schedule the training for Tuesday morning, when the office is quieter?
records.zomi: Office a daih zawh Pithai ni zingsang ciangin sinna i bawl ding hiam?

records.english: How are you going to manage the school run once you start your new job?
records.zomi: Na nasep thak na kipat ciangin naupangte sang tawina bangci-in na kem ding hiam?

records.english: My husband will drop the children off, and I'll collect them on my way home.
records.zomi: Ka pasal in naupangte a tawi ding a, kei in inn ka ciahna lampi ah ka la ding hi.

records.english: Everyone, from Monday the front entrance will be closed, so please use the side door.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh aw, Pizing ni pan kipan ma lam kongkhak kikhak ding ahih manin a pang kongkhak zang un.

records.english: If the office move goes smoothly, nobody will even notice that we've changed buildings.
records.zomi: Office kitawnna hoih takin a pai leh inn i khek hi, cih kuamah in a thei lo ding hi.

records.english: Remind me to update my email signature before the move.
records.zomi: Kitawn ma-in ka email signature khek dingin hong phawksak in.

records.english: If the trial goes well, the company might offer the four-day week to every department.
records.zomi: Sinna a hoih leh company in nasep pawl khempeuh ni li nasep kal a pia kha ding hi.

records.english: Let me know if you'd like me to show you the new system.
records.zomi: System thak kong lak ding na deih leh hong hilh in.

records.english: Could you cover my calls while I'm on holiday?
records.zomi: Nopsakna hun ka om sungin ka phone sam te na dawng sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: From next month, our office is going to try a four-day working week.
records.zomi: A zom kha pan kipan i office in ni li nasep kal a sin ding hi.

records.english: We'll work slightly longer days from Monday to Thursday and have every Friday off.
records.zomi: Pizing ni pan Laizing ni dong ni sau zaw-in i sem ding a, Laithai ni khempeuh i khawl ding hi.

records.english: I think it'll make us more productive, but my manager isn't convinced yet.
records.zomi: Tam zaw i sem thei ding hi, ka ci a, ahi zongin ka makaipa in a um nai kei hi.

records.english: What will you do on your free Fridays?
records.zomi: Na Laithai ni om ngawng te-in bang na bawl ding hiam?

records.english: I'll take my mother to her appointments and finally learn to play the guitar.
records.zomi: Ka nu a siavuan kimuhna te ah ka tawi ding a, a tawp-in guitar tum ka sin ding hi.

records.english: I'm going to mentor the new engineer and show her the ropes for her first few months.
records.zomi: Engineer thak numei ka sin sak ding a, a kha masa pawl khat sungin nasep dan ka lak ding hi.

records.english: Next week, we're all being trained on the new scheduling software.
records.zomi: A zom kal ciangin hun geelna software thak zat dan i khempeuh in i sin ding hi.

records.english: All of you will get a chance to try the new machines before they're switched on properly.
records.zomi: Setna thakte hoih takin a kihal ma-un na khempeuh un zat sin dingin hun na ngah ding uh hi.

records.english: However busy the new role becomes, I'm determined to leave the office by six.
records.zomi: Nasep thak bangzah in buai zongin nai guk ciangin office pan pai khia dingin ka kithukhen hi.

records.english: I really do hope the new building has better coffee.
records.zomi: Inn thak ah coffee hoih zaw a om ding ka lametna taktak ahi hi.

records.english: Sorry, could you say that again?
records.zomi: Maisak ing, na gen kik thei ding hiam?

records.english: Next year, I'm hoping to train as a manager through the company's program.
records.zomi: A zom kum ciangin company' sinna tawh makaipa hih dingin sin ka lamen hi.

records.english: In a few years, I imagine half our meetings will happen online.
records.zomi: Kum tawmno khit ciangin i kikhopna a kim online-in a kibawl ding hi, ka ngaihsun hi.

records.english: It would make a real difference to the night staff if the canteen stayed open until midnight.
records.zomi: An nekna inn zan laitak dong a kihon leh zan nasemte adingin kilamdanna taktak a om ding hi.

records.english: This time next week, I'll be sitting at a new desk in a new building.
records.zomi: A zom kal tu hun ciangin inn thak khat-a dawhkan thak khat ah ka tu ding hi.

records.english: Do you think standing meetings will really be shorter?
records.zomi: Ding-in kikhopna in a tom zaw taktak ding hiam, na ci hiam?

records.english: Probably, because nobody likes standing for long.
records.zomi: A tom zaw kha ding hi, kuamah in sawt ding a deih kei uh ahih manin.

records.english: When I become team leader next month, I'm going to keep our meetings to fifteen minutes.
records.zomi: A zom kha in pawl makaipa ka suah ciangin i kikhopna te minit sawm leh nga sung bek-in ka kem ding hi.

records.english: The new rota will be posted on the noticeboard by Wednesday.
records.zomi: Nasep kikhen thak Nilai ni ciangin thu laikhai bang ah kikhai ding hi.

records.english: After a year at home with the baby, I'm going back to teaching in September.
records.zomi: Naungek tawh inn ah kum khat ka om khit ciangin September kha-in saya nasep ah ka ciah kik ding hi.

records.english: For the first month, I'll work three days a week so that we can all adjust.
records.zomi: Kha masa sungin i khempeuh i kizat theih nadingin kal khat ah ni thum ka sem ding hi.

records.english: My mother has offered to look after the baby on those days, which is a huge relief.
records.zomi: Ka nu in tua ni te-in naungek kem dingin a ciam a, tua in hong lungmuangsak mahmah hi.

records.english: By the end of the year, I'll have worked at the bakery for a decade.
records.zomi: Kum tawp ciangin moh bawlna ah kum sawm ka sem khin ding hi.

records.english: Shall I ask for a desk near the window when we move?
records.zomi: I kitawn ciangin tukvuang kiang-a dawhkan khat ka ngen ding hiam?

records.english: Is there any chance I could start an hour later on Mondays?
records.zomi: Pizing ni te-in nai khat nunung zaw-in ka kipan thei ding hiam?

records.english: I do want to take on more responsibility, but I'm not sure I'm ready to manage people.
records.zomi: Mawhpuakna tam zaw la ka deih taktak a, ahi zongin mite ka kem dingin ka kiman hiam ka thei kei hi.

records.english: My new job is an hour away by train, so I'll have a long commute every day.
records.zomi: Ka nasep thak meileng tawh nai khat gamla ahih manin ni simin khualzinna sau ka nei ding hi.

records.english: I'm planning to use the time to listen to audiobooks and study for my accounting exams.
records.zomi: Tua hun pen aw laibu ngai nadingin leh sum gelhna sitna adingin sin nadingin zang dingin ka geel hi.

records.english: If that works, the journey might turn out to be the most useful part of my day.
records.zomi: Tua a sem leh khualzinna pen ka ni sung-a phattuam pen a suak kha ding hi.

records.english: Who will water the office plants while we're at the conference?
records.zomi: Kikhopna lian ah i om sungin office singkung te kua in tui a buak ding hiam?

records.english: Our office is moving to a new building next week, so we're packing our desks on Friday.
records.zomi: I office a zom kal ciangin inn thak ah a kitawn ding ahih manin Laithai ni-in i dawhkan te i tuam ding hi.

records.english: Team, the deadline has moved to Thursday, so let's agree on the plan today.
records.zomi: Pawl aw, a tawpna ni Laizing ni ah kituan ahih manin tuni-in geelna i kilem ding hi.

records.english: If I'm going to work from home twice a week, I'll need a proper chair and a laptop stand.
records.zomi: Kal khat ah nih vei inn pan ka sep ding leh tutna hoih khat leh laptop koihna khat ka kisam ding hi.

records.english: Do you think the company will keep the trial going after the summer?
records.zomi: Khal khit ciangin company in sinna a kem lai ding hiam, na ci hiam?

records.english: I'm going to bring a cake on Friday to thank the team for their help this month.
records.zomi: Hih kha sung huhna adingin pawl lungdam ci nadingin Laithai ni-in cake khat ka tawi ding hi.

records.english: Mentoring someone new will probably teach me as much as it teaches her.
records.zomi: Mi thak khat sin sak in amah a sin sak zah mah keimah zong hong sin sak kha ding hi.

records.english: My workload is going to double when my colleague leaves next month.
records.zomi: Ka nasem pawl a zom kha a pai ciangin ka nasep a nih-in a khang ding hi.

records.english: Could you remind me what time the client is arriving tomorrow?
records.zomi: Zingciang nasepna lawm nai bangzah ciangin a tung ding hiam hong phawksak thei ding hiam?

records.english: I think the new system will save time once everyone gets used to it.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh in a zat khit uh ciangin system thak in hun a kem ding hi, ka ci hi.

records.english: Once the new software is running, we should be able to plan the shifts in minutes.
records.zomi: Software thak a sep khit ciangin nasep kikhen te minit tawmno sungin i geel thei ding hi.

records.english: From next week, my sister will be working day shifts at the hospital instead of nights.
records.zomi: A zom kal pan kipan ka sanggam nu in siavuan inn ah zan sangin sun nasep a sem ding hi.

records.english: Will she finally be able to have dinner with the family?
records.zomi: A tawp-in innkuan tawh nitak an a ne thei ding hiam?

records.english: Whatever happens with the trial, I'm going to keep my Friday mornings for exercise.
records.zomi: Sinna bang piang zongin ka Laithai zingsang te pumpi kisinna adingin ka kem ding hi.

records.english: We could share one car to the new office, since we live on the same street.
records.zomi: Lampi khat mah ah i om ahih manin office thak ah mawtaw khat i tuang khawm thei hi.

records.english: To be honest, I'm not sure the four-day week will suit everyone.
records.zomi: Thu man takin, ni li nasep kal in mi khempeuh a kilawm ding hiam ka thei kei hi.

records.english: You're right that the commute is long, but the salary makes it worthwhile.
records.zomi: Khualzinna a sau hi, na cih a man hi, ahi zongin khasum in a man a kilawm sak hi.

records.english: I'll use the label maker to mark every box before the move.
records.zomi: Kitawn ma-in bawm khempeuh ciamteh nadingin min ciamtehna setna ka zang ding hi.

records.english: Put your slippers by the bed so that you don't step on the cold floor.
records.zomi: Inn phah vot na sut lohna dingin na khedap neu lupna kiang ah koih in.

records.english: Everyone, the lights in the dormitory will go out at half past nine, so get ready early.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh aw, ihmutna inn meivak te nai kua leh a kim ciangin kimut ding ahih manin ma-in kiman un.

records.english: We're going to try a little machine that plays the sound of rain, to help the twins settle.
records.zomi: Apeng te a dai nadingin guah ging a sak setna neu khat i zang sin ding hi.

records.english: Once she gets used to the new bed, we'll finally have our evenings back.
records.zomi: Lupna thak a zat khit ciangin i nitak te a tawp-in i ngah kik ding hi.

records.english: Do you think the toddler will stay in her new bed all night?
records.zomi: Naupang neu in a lupna thak ah zan bup a om ding hiam, na ci hiam?

records.english: Will the tent be warm enough for the baby?
records.zomi: Puan inn in naungek adingin a lum kicing ding hiam?

records.english: The new bunk bed arrives on Thursday, and both boys want the top bunk.
records.zomi: Lupna dawl nih thak Laizing ni-in a tung ding a, tangval nih in a tung lam a deih uh hi.

records.english: How are you going to decide who sleeps on top?
records.zomi: Kua in a tung ah a ihmu ding hiam bangci-in na khen ding hiam?

records.english: They'll swap every month, and the younger one gets the first turn because he's never had it.
records.zomi: Kha simin a kilaih ding uh a, a neu zaw in a neih ngei loh ahih manin a masa-in a ngah ding hi.

records.english: We could move bedtime later in the summer, since it stays light until nine.
records.zomi: Nai kua dong a vak ahih manin khal ciangin ihmut hun i nunung sak thei hi.

records.english: This time tomorrow night, we'll be lying in a tent and listening to the wind.
records.zomi: Zingciang zan tu hun ciangin puan inn sungah i lum ding a, huih ging i ngai ding hi.

records.english: Can I have a sleepover at Mai's house on Friday?
records.zomi: Laithai ni-in Mai' inn ah zan ka om thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, if her parents agree and you're home by ten the next morning.
records.zomi: Om thei hi, a nu leh a pa a phal uh a, a zing zingsang nai sawm ciangin inn ah na tun leh.

records.english: Next month, my parents are coming to stay, so the children will sleep in our room for a week.
records.zomi: A zom kha in ka nu leh ka pa hong om ding uh ahih manin naupangte kal khat sung i inndei ah a ihmu ding uh hi.

records.english: I'll warm some milk for Grandpa before he goes to bed.
records.zomi: Pu a ihmut ma-in nawi ka lumsak ding hi.

records.english: Which lullaby do you think the baby will like best?
records.zomi: Naungek in naupang lupsakna la bang a deih pen ding hiam, na ci hiam?

records.english: Tomorrow I'll be getting up early, so I'm going to bed straight after dinner.
records.zomi: Zingciang ma takin ka thou ding ahih manin nitak an khit pah-in ka ihmu ding hi.

records.english: I'm going to tidy the children's room tonight so that they can find their pyjamas easily.
records.zomi: Naupangte in a ihmut puan uh baih takin a muh theih nadingun tu zanin a inndei uh ka kiman sak ding hi.

records.english: Which story will you choose for your first night in the tent?
records.zomi: Puan inn sungah na zan masa pen adingin tangthu bang na teel ding hiam?

records.english: If the weather is warm, we might let the children sleep on the balcony.
records.zomi: Huihkhua a lum leh naupangte innkhawng ah i ihmusak kha ding hi.

records.english: My husband is learning three lullabies in my language so that he can sing them to the baby.
records.zomi: Ka pasal in naungek a sak sak theih nadingin ka pau tawh naupang lupsakna la thum a sin hi.

records.english: Have you packed the children's pyjamas for the trip?
records.zomi: Khualzinna adingin naupangte' ihmut puan na tuam khin hiam?

records.english: Can the cousins share the big bed when they visit next month?
records.zomi: A zom kha in sanggamte a hong ciangun lupna lian a hawm thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: On Saturday, the children will sleep in a tent for the first time, on a mountain campsite.
records.zomi: Kiginni ni-in naupangte in mual tung-a puan inn sungah a masa pen-in a ihmu ding uh hi.

records.english: We've borrowed warm sleeping bags from our neighbors and packed two torches.
records.zomi: Inn vengte kiang pan ihmut ip lum i caih a, meivak nih i tuam hi.

records.english: I suspect we'll all be awake at dawn, listening to the birds.
records.zomi: Khuavak ciangin i khempeuh vasa ngai-in i khanglawh ding hi, ka ci hi.

records.english: May I sleep in my brother's room on the night before his birthday?
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal' pianni ma zanin a inndei ah ka ihmu thei ding hiam?

records.english: Next week, our two-year-old is moving from her cot into a big girl's bed.
records.zomi: A zom kal ciangin i ta kum nih in naungek lupna pan naupang lian lupna ah a tawn ding hi.

records.english: We're going to let her choose the sheets, so that she feels proud of it.
records.zomi: A kipahna dingin lupna puan amah in teel dingin i phal ding hi.

records.english: For the first few nights, one of us will sit beside her until she falls asleep.
records.zomi: Zan masa pawl khat sungin a ihmut mateng i khat in a kiang ah i tu ding hi.

records.english: What time will the children need to be in bed once school starts again?
records.zomi: Sang a kihon kik ciangin naupangte nai bangzah ciangin a lupna uh ah a om ding uh a kisam ding hiam?

records.english: By eight, so we'll start moving bedtime earlier a week before term.
records.zomi: Nai giat ciangin, tua ahih manin sang kihon ma kal khat-in ihmut hun i ma sak kipan ding hi.

records.english: In a few years, I imagine the children will be the ones telling us to go to bed.
records.zomi: Kum tawmno khit ciangin naupangte in ihmu dingin hong hilh ding uh hi, ka ngaihsun hi.

records.english: My daughter has promised to sing her little brother to sleep on Thursday nights.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in Laizing ni zan simin a nau pasal ihmut nadingin la sak sak dingin a ciam hi.

records.english: Perhaps I'll start reading a chapter book to them instead of picture books.
records.zomi: Lim laibu sangin laibu sung khen nei laibu khat amaute adingin ka sim sak kipan kha ding hi.

records.english: Setting his own bedtime could teach our son more responsibility than any rule we make.
records.zomi: I tapa in amah' ihmut hun a khen in i bawl thukham khempeuh sangin mawhpuakna tam zaw a sin sak kha ding hi.

records.english: By the end of the summer, the twins will have learned to fall asleep without us in the room.
records.zomi: Khal a bei ciangin apeng te in inndei sungah kei te om lo-in ihmut a sin khin ding uh hi.

records.english: I do want bedtime to be calm, even on the nights when everyone is tired.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh a ol zan te zongin ihmut hun a daih ding ka deih taktak hi.

records.english: Whatever time we get home from the wedding, the children will still have to brush their teeth.
records.zomi: Mopawi pan bang hun ciangin inn i tung zongin naupangte in a ha a sil lai ding uh a kisam hi.

records.english: This term, my son and I are going to read twenty books together at bedtime.
records.zomi: Hih hun sungin ka tapa leh kei in ihmut hun ciangin laibu sawm nih khawm-in i sim ding hi.

records.english: He'll color in a star on the chart on his door every time we finish one.
records.zomi: Khat i zawh simin a kongkhak tung-a lai phek ah aksi khat a nul ding hi.

records.english: If he fills the chart by summer, we'll celebrate with a trip to the big bookshop in town.
records.zomi: Khal ma-in lai phek a dimsak leh khuapi-a laibu zuakna inn lian ah i pai-in i lungdam ding hi.

records.english: Do you think the boys will argue about the top bunk?
records.zomi: Tangvalte in lupna tung lam thu-in a kinial ding uh hiam, na ci hiam?

records.english: However late the guests stay, I'm going to put the baby to bed at seven.
records.zomi: Khualte bangzah sawt a om zongin naungek nai sagih ciangin ka lupsak ding hi.

records.english: Children, tonight you'll each tell me one good thing that happened today.
records.zomi: Naupangte, tu zanin na khat ciat un tuni-a a piang thu hoih khat hong gen un.

records.english: This year, we're letting our fifteen-year-old set his own bedtime, as long as his schoolwork doesn't suffer.
records.zomi: Hih kum in i ta kum sawm leh nga in a sang nasep a kiam kei teng amah' ihmut hun amah in a khen dingin i phal hi.

records.english: It would help me a great deal if someone else did bedtime on Thursdays.
records.zomi: Laizing ni te-in mi dang khat in ihmut hun a kem leh hong huh mahmah ding hi.

records.english: Shall I fetch an extra blanket from the cupboard for you?
records.zomi: Van koihna pan puannak behlap khat kong la sak ding hiam?

records.english: We'll put a soft mat beside the new bed in case she rolls out.
records.zomi: A kilet leh cih adingin lupna thak kiang ah phah nem khat i koih ding hi.

records.english: When the baby arrives, our eldest will move into the bigger bedroom at the end of the hall.
records.zomi: Naungek a tun ciangin i ta upa pen inn lampi tawp-a inndei lian zaw ah a tawn ding hi.

records.english: Will he mind giving up the room he's slept in since he was born?
records.zomi: A suah pan kipan a ihmutna inndei nusia a lungkham ding hiam?

records.english: If we keep the same routine every night, the move to the new house shouldn't upset the children too much.
records.zomi: Zan simin ngeina kibang i kem leh inn thak kitawnna in naupangte a lungbuaisak lua lo ding hi.

records.english: I'll use the old blanket as a curtain for the tent door.
records.zomi: Puan inn kongkhak adingin puannak lui tukvuang puan bangin ka zang ding hi.

records.english: While she's living abroad, my mother will phone every Sunday evening to tell the children a bedtime story.
records.zomi: Gamdang ah a om sungin ka nu in naupangte ihmut ma tangthu gen sak dingin Nipini nitak simin phone tawh a sam ding hi.

records.english: Remind me to pack the night light for the trip.
records.zomi: Khualzinna adingin zan meivak tuam dingin hong phawksak in.

records.english: All of you need to be quiet after ten, because the guests will be sleeping.
records.zomi: Khualte a ihmut ding uh ahih manin nai sawm khit ciangin na khempeuh un na daih ding uh a kisam hi.

records.english: I really do hope the baby sleeps better in her own room.
records.zomi: Naungek amah' inndei ah hoih zaw-in a ihmut ding ka lametna taktak ahi hi.

records.english: Is it all right if the dog sleeps in the kitchen while we're away?
records.zomi: I om lohna sungin ui an huanna ah a ihmu leh a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: My son is going to make a sign for his bedroom door that says when he wants to be left alone.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in a kia-in om a deih hun gen nadingin a inndei kongkhak adingin lai khat a bawl ding hi.

records.english: I think the sound machine will help, but my husband says rain sounds will keep him awake.
records.zomi: Ging setna in a huh ding hi, ka ci a, ahi zongin ka pasal in guah ging in hong phawngsak ding hi, a ci hi.

records.english: The fresh bread will be delivered at seven, so the shop will open a little later tomorrow.
records.zomi: Moh thak nai sagih ciangin hong kipuak ding ahih manin zingciang zuakna inn tawmno nunung zaw-in kihong ding hi.

records.english: If we leave the bananas in the car, they'll be ruined by the heat.
records.zomi: Nahtang te mawtaw sungah i nusia leh a lum in a susia ding hi.

records.english: From now on, we're going to buy vegetables loose instead of wrapped in plastic.
records.zomi: Tu pan kipan anteh te plastic tawh kituam sangin a tuam lo i lei ding hi.

records.english: By the end of the month, we'll have saved enough on snacks to buy the children new shoes.
records.zomi: Kha tawp ciangin an neute adingin naupangte khedap thak lei dingin a kicing i kikoih khin ding hi.

records.english: Next Saturday, my eleven-year-old daughter is going to the corner shop on her own for the first time.
records.zomi: A zom Kiginni ni-in ka tanu kum sawm leh khat in a masa pen-in amah bek-in lampi kikona zuakna inn ah a pai ding hi.

records.english: She'll take a short list, the exact money, and my phone number written on her hand.
records.zomi: Gelhna tom khat, sum kicing, leh a khut tungah ka phone nambat kigelh a tawi ding hi.

records.english: I'll be watching from the window, although I've promised not to follow her.
records.zomi: Ka zui lo ding, ci-in ka ciam hangin tukvuang pan ka en ding hi.

records.english: Write the prices next to each item, so that we can compare them next week.
records.zomi: A zom kal ciangin i kiteh theih nadingin van khempeuh kiang ah a man gelh in.

records.english: I'm going to use the market's new scale to check the weight of the potatoes myself.
records.zomi: Zuakna mun-a gikna setna thak tawh alu gik keimah in ka en ding hi.

records.english: I do want to cook more fresh food, but I never know what to do with half the vegetables I see.
records.zomi: An thak tam zaw huan ka deih taktak a, ahi zongin ka muh anteh a kim bang bawl ding hiam ka thei ngei kei hi.

records.english: Would your mother like us to bring her anything from the new market?
records.zomi: Zuakna mun thak pan na nu adingin bangmah i tawi ding a deih ding hiam?

records.english: Will the shop still be open when I finish work at seven?
records.zomi: Nitak nai sagih ciangin ka nasep ka zawh ciangin zuakna inn a kihong lai ding hiam?

records.english: I really do hope the new market sells the spices we can't find in town.
records.zomi: Zuakna mun thak in khuapi ah i muh loh an lim te a zuak ding ka lametna taktak ahi hi.

records.english: However busy the week gets, I'm going to do one proper shop for fresh vegetables.
records.zomi: Kal bangzah in buai zongin anteh thak adingin van lei hoih khatvei ka bawl ding hi.

records.english: Supporting the small shops nearby might cost a little more, but it keeps our street alive.
records.zomi: A kiang-a zuakna inn neute huh in tawmno man tam zaw kha ding a, ahi zongin i lampi a nungta sak hi.

records.english: How will you stop the children from asking for sweets at the checkout?
records.zomi: Sum piakna mun ah naupangte in thei khum a nget lohna dingun bangci-in na khawlsak ding hiam?

records.english: We'll let them choose one healthy treat each before we reach the till.
records.zomi: Sum piakna mun i tun ma-in an hoih khat ciat teel dingin i phal ding hi.

records.english: Who's going to buy the bread for tomorrow's breakfast?
records.zomi: Zingciang zingsang an adingin moh kua in a lei ding hiam?

records.english: Before the baby arrives, we'll stock up on nappies and soap so that we don't have to go out in the first weeks.
records.zomi: Naungek a tun ma-in kal masate-a i pusuak lohna dingin naungek nuai puan leh satpiang tampi i lei khol ding hi.

records.english: We'll share the shopping list in an app, so that whoever passes the shop can buy what's missing.
records.zomi: Van lei ding gelhna app khat ah i hawm ding a, zuakna inn a kantan peuhpeuh in a kiam a lei thei ding hi.

records.english: Will you come with Grandma to the new market on its opening day?
records.zomi: A kihon ni-in zuakna mun thak ah Pi tawh na pai ding hiam?

records.english: Can I choose the cereal this week?
records.zomi: Hih kal in zingsang an ne ding ka teel thei ding hiam?

records.english: Next year, when my son starts university, he'll have to do his own shopping for the first time.
records.zomi: A zom kum ciangin ka tapa sangpi a kah kipat ciangin a masa pen-in amah' van amah in a lei ding a kisam ding hi.

records.english: May I pay with my own pocket money?
records.zomi: Keimah' zat ding sum tawh ka pia thei ding hiam?

records.english: Is it all right if I bring my dog into the market?
records.zomi: Zuakna mun ah ka ui ka tawi thei ding hiam?

records.english: Next month, we're going to try spending half as much on snacks.
records.zomi: A zom kha in an neute adingin a kim bek zat dingin i sin ding hi.

records.english: Whatever the new market charges, I'll still buy my eggs from the old woman by the bridge.
records.zomi: Zuakna mun thak in bangzah a man zongin lei kiang-a numei upa pan ka aktui ka lei lai ding hi.

records.english: Everyone, we're meeting at the market gate at eight, so bring your bags and your lists.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh aw, nai giat ciangin zuakna mun kongpi ah i kimu ding ahih manin na ip leh na gelhna uh tawi un.

records.english: Remind me to bring the empty egg boxes back to the farmer.
records.zomi: Aktui bawm ngawng te lo neipa kiangah tawi kik dingin hong phawksak in.

records.english: When are you going to buy the things for the harvest festival?
records.zomi: Kaihawl pawi adingin van te bang ciangin na lei ding hiam?

records.english: On Thursday, before the prices go up for the weekend.
records.zomi: Laizing ni-in, kal tawp adingin van man a khan ma-in.

records.english: This time next week, I'll be wandering around the new market with a cup of tea in my hand.
records.zomi: A zom kal tu hun ciangin ka khut ah tea haai khat tawh zuakna mun thak ah ka vak ding hi.

records.english: If the prices at the new market are fair, we might do all our shopping there.
records.zomi: Zuakna mun thak-a van man a dik leh i van lei khempeuh tua ah i lei kha ding hi.

records.english: Do you think the new market will have parking?
records.zomi: Zuakna mun thak ah mawtaw koihna mun a om ding hiam, na ci hiam?

records.english: To be honest, I'm not sure the bigger packs will save us much money.
records.zomi: Thu man takin, bawm lian zaw in sum tam a kem sak ding hiam ka thei kei hi.

records.english: We're shopping for fifty guests for my grandfather's birthday party next weekend.
records.zomi: A zom kal tawp-a ka pu' pianni pawi adingin khual sawm nga adingin van i lei hi.

records.english: Each cousin will buy one part of the list: drinks, fruit, rice, or meat.
records.zomi: Sanggam khat ciat in gelhna khen khat ciat a lei ding uh hi: dawn ding, theigah, buh, ahih kei leh sa.

records.english: If anything is forgotten, my aunt has promised to send her son to the market on his motorbike.
records.zomi: Bangmah kimangngilh leh ka ni in a tapa a motorbike tawh zuakna mun ah sawl dingin a ciam hi.

records.english: It would make shopping much easier for older people if the new market had a few benches.
records.zomi: Zuakna mun thak in tutphah tawmno a nei leh mi upate adingin van lei a baih zaw mahmah ding hi.

records.english: Is buying loose vegetables really cheaper, or just better for the environment?
records.zomi: Anteh a tuam lo lei in a man neu zaw taktak hiam, leitung adingin a hoih zaw bek hiam?

records.english: Both, if we only buy what we need for the week.
records.zomi: A nih, kal khat adingin i kisap bek i lei leh.

records.english: Could the children help me plan next week's meals before we write the list?
records.zomi: Gelhna i gelh ma-in a zom kal-a an te geel dingin naupangte in hong huh thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: I'll take my grandmother's old wicker basket for the bread.
records.zomi: Moh adingin ka pi' empeng lui ka tawi ding hi.

records.english: I'll buy extra flour for the neighbor who's baking the wedding cake.
records.zomi: Mopawi cake a em inn vengnu adingin buh-mal behlap ka lei ding hi.

records.english: Once my daughter has done her first shop alone, she'll want to go every Saturday.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in a masa pen-in amah bek-in van a lei khit ciangin Kiginni simin pai a deih ding hi.

records.english: I'm going to buy a shopping bag on wheels so that my mother doesn't hurt her back carrying the groceries.
records.zomi: Ka nu in van leite a puak ciangin a nung a nat lohna dingin khe nei van lei ip khat ka lei ding hi.

records.english: Please don't buy any more rice until we've finished the big sack.
records.zomi: Buh ip lian i zawh mateng buh lei behlap kei in.

records.english: You mustn't run with the trolley, because the floor is wet.
records.zomi: Inn phah a dik ahih manin van tawina leng tawh na tai lo ding hi.

records.english: If we plan our meals in advance, we'll waste less food and spend less money.
records.zomi: I an te ma-in i geel leh an tawm zaw i paih ding a, sum tawm zaw i zang ding hi.

records.english: A new covered market is opening in the square next month.
records.zomi: A zom kha in khua laizang ah zuakna mun khuh thak khat a kihong ding hi.

records.english: I think it'll be cheaper than the supermarket, because the farmers will sell directly.
records.zomi: Lo neite in amau' in a zuak ding uh ahih manin supermarket sangin a man neu zaw ding hi, ka ci hi.

records.english: My neighbor isn't so sure, but she's agreed to come with me on the first morning to see.
records.zomi: Ka inn vengnu in a thei siang kei a, ahi zongin et dingin zingsang masa pen-in hong zui dingin a phal hi.

records.english: Tomorrow I'll be shopping for twelve people, so I'm making the list tonight.
records.zomi: Zingciang ciangin mi sawm leh nih adingin van ka lei ding ahih manin tu zanin gelhna ka bawl hi.

records.english: In a few years, I imagine the corner shop will have a little café at the back.
records.zomi: Kum tawmno khit ciangin lampi kikona zuakna inn in a nung lam ah an zuakna neu khat a nei ding hi, ka ngaihsun hi.

records.english: All of you who ordered vegetable boxes will be able to collect them from Friday.
records.zomi: Anteh bawm a ngen na khempeuh un Laithai ni pan kipan na la thei ding uh hi.

records.english: We could buy a second fridge if we start shopping only once a week.
records.zomi: Kal khat khatvei bek van i lei kipat leh vot sak setna nihna i lei thei hi.

records.english: Kids, tomorrow each of you can find one item on the list and put it in the trolley.
records.zomi: Naupangte, zingciang ciangin na khat ciat un gelhna-a van khat zong unla, van tawina leng sungah koih un.

records.english: Children won't be allowed on the new market's stalls without an adult, according to the sign.
records.zomi: Lai khai in a gen bangin mi upa om lo-in naupangte zuakna mun thak-a zuakna dawhkan te ah kiphal lo ding hi.

records.english: We're going to buy our meat from the butcher next to the school, to support his small shop.
records.zomi: A zuakna inn neu i huh nadingin sang kiang-a sa zuakpa pan i sa i lei ding hi.

records.english: Buying less packaging will mean fewer trips to the recycling bins and a tidier kitchen.
records.zomi: Tuamna tawm zaw lei in zat kikna bawm ah pai tawm zaw ding a, an huanna a siang zaw ding hi.

records.english: What makes a sentence memorable is often its rhythm rather than its length.
records.zomi: Kammal tang khat phawk theih a suaksak pen a sau hi lo-in a ging kibanna ahi tam hi.

records.english: How do you know when a sentence is too complicated?
records.zomi: Kammal tang khat a haksa lua hi, cih bangci-in na thei hiam?

records.english: When you have to read it twice to understand it, it probably needs to be simpler.
records.zomi: A theih nadingin nih vei na sim ding a kisam leh a baih zaw ding a kisam kha ding hi.

records.english: Could you check whether these two sentences are joined correctly?
records.zomi: Hih kammal tang nih a kizom dan a dik hiam na en thei ding hiam?

records.english: My father writes his letters slowly, checking every sentence before he moves on.
records.zomi: Ka pa in a laikhak te nawlkhin takin a gelh a, a zom a gelh ma-in kammal tang khempeuh a en hi.

records.english: Write one sentence about the picture on the board.
records.zomi: Suanglaipi tung-a lim thu kammal tang khat gelh in.

records.english: I was embarrassed when I saw how many sentences in my report didn't make sense.
records.zomi: Ka report sung-a kammal tang bangzah in khiatna a nei kei hiam ka muh ciangin ka maizum hi.

records.english: Is this a complete sentence, or is something missing?
records.zomi: Hih kammal tang a kim hiam, bangmah a kiam hiam?

records.english: Something is missing, because it doesn't tell us what happened.
records.zomi: Bangmah a kiam hi, bang a piang hiam hong hilh kei ahih manin.

records.english: When my daughter started school, she wrote everything as one long sentence.
records.zomi: Ka tanu sang a kah kipat ciangin bangkim kammal tang sau khat bangin a gelh hi.

records.english: Her teacher gave her a little stamp with a dot on it for the end of each sentence.
records.zomi: A saya in kammal tang khempeuh tawp adingin dot khat a nei ciamtehna neu khat a pia hi.

records.english: By the end of the term, her stories were full of short, clear sentences and many stamped dots.
records.zomi: Hun a bei ciangin a tangthu te kammal tang tom, kician leh dot tampi tawh a dim hi.

records.english: Don't forget the full stop at the end.
records.zomi: A tawp ah dot koih dingin mangngilh kei in.

records.english: Our teacher said, "A good sentence is like a good path: easy to follow from start to finish."
records.zomi: I saya in, “Kammal tang hoih pen lampi hoih bang ahi a, a kipatna pan a tawp dong zui a baih hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: Although long sentences can be elegant, they easily lose the reader halfway through.
records.zomi: Kammal tang sau te a kilawm thei hangin simpa laizang ah a mansuah baih hi.

records.english: The best sentences were pinned on the classroom wall.
records.zomi: Kammal tang hoih pen te sang inndei bang ah kikhai hi.

records.english: I do want my writing to be clear, but my sentences always come out too long.
records.zomi: Ka laigelh a kician ding ka deih taktak a, ahi zongin ka kammal tang te a sau lua tawntung hi.

records.english: Class, use the cards on your desks to build three sentences with your partner.
records.zomi: Naupangte, na lawm tawh kammal tang thum bawl dingin na dawhkan tung-a laidal te zang un.

records.english: Show me the sentence you're not sure about.
records.zomi: Na thei siang lo kammal tang hong lak in.

records.english: Why did you start a new sentence here?
records.zomi: Bang hangin hih ah kammal tang thak na kipan hiam?

records.english: This sentence is too long; can you split it into two?
records.zomi: Hih kammal tang a sau lua hi; nih-in na khen thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, I'll put the second idea in a new sentence.
records.zomi: Khen thei ning, ngaihsutna nihna kammal tang thak khat ah ka koih ding hi.

records.english: When you join two ideas, use a word that shows how they are connected.
records.zomi: Ngaihsutna nih na zom ciangin bangci-in a kizom hiam a lak kammal khat zang in.

records.english: Please don't start every sentence in the same way.
records.zomi: Kammal tang khempeuh lampi kibang tawh kipan kei in.

records.english: Learning to build a clear sentence is the first step toward writing a clear argument.
records.zomi: Kammal tang kician bawl dan sin pen kinialna kician gelh nading kalsuan masa pen ahi hi.

records.english: Can you add a detail to make your sentence more interesting?
records.zomi: Na kammal tang a nuam zawk nadingin thu neu khat na behlap thei ding hiam?

records.english: I rewrote the first sentence three times before I was happy with it.
records.zomi: Ka kipak ma-in kammal tang masa pen thum vei ka gelh kik hi.

records.english: Having rewritten the paragraph, she noticed that every sentence now said exactly what she meant.
records.zomi: Khen pen a gelh kik khit ciangin kammal tang khempeuh in a gen nop taktak a gen hi, cih a mu hi.

records.english: Everyone, write a sentence about what you did at the weekend.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh aw, kal tawp-in na bawl thu kammal tang khat gelh un.

records.english: Varying the length of your sentences keeps the reader's attention.
records.zomi: Na kammal tang te' sauzah kikhek in simpa' lungsim a kem hi.

records.english: Every Friday, we practice making one long sentence from three short ones.
records.zomi: Laithai ni simin kammal tang tom thum pan sau khat bawl i sin hi.

records.english: It was only after I began reading my sentences aloud that I noticed how many were incomplete.
records.zomi: Ka kammal tang te aw-in ka sim kipat khit ciang bek bangzah in a kim kei hiam ka mu hi.

records.english: Whatever you are writing, it helps to read it aloud before anyone else sees it.
records.zomi: Bang na gelh zongin mi dang in a et ma-in aw-in sim in a huh hi.

records.english: Where should I put the comma in this sentence?
records.zomi: Hih kammal tang sungah comma koi ah ka koih ding hiam?

records.english: Your sentences are much clearer than they were last month.
records.zomi: Na kammal tang te kha nung sangin a kician zaw mahmah hi.

records.english: Read your sentence aloud and listen to whether it sounds right.
records.zomi: Na kammal tang aw-in sim inla, a ging a dik hiam ngai in.

records.english: Start every sentence with a capital letter.
records.zomi: Kammal tang khempeuh laimal lian tawh kipan in.

records.english: My essay was returned with red marks under every sentence that was unclear.
records.zomi: Ka laigelh a kician lo kammal tang khempeuh nuai ah ciamtehna san tawh hong kiciah hi.

records.english: The more you read, the more naturally good sentences seem to come to you.
records.zomi: Na sim tam semsem ciangin kammal tang hoih te baih zaw-in hong pai bang hi.

records.english: A message without punctuation was misunderstood, and my friend waited at the wrong station.
records.zomi: Ciamtehna om lo message khat kithei khial a, ka lawm meileng dinna khial ah a ngak hi.

records.english: Which sentence in your story do you like best?
records.zomi: Na tangthu sungah kammal tang bang na deih pen hiam?

records.english: The teacher underlined the parts of the sentence that were in the wrong order.
records.zomi: Saya in kammal tang sung-a a kigual khial khen te a nuai ah gual a khai hi.

records.english: At forty, my uncle decided to learn to write properly so that he could fill in forms himself.
records.zomi: Kum sawm li a phak ciangin ka pa neu in lai gelh te amah in a gelh theih nadingin hoih takin laigelh sin dingin a thukhen hi.

records.english: Every evening, he copied five sentences from the newspaper and then wrote five of his own.
records.zomi: Nitak simin laithak pan kammal tang nga a gelh kik a, tua ciangin amah' nga a gelh hi.

records.english: Last month, he wrote his first letter to the council without anyone's help.
records.zomi: Kha nung in kuamah' huhna om lo-in khua upate kiangah a lai masa pen a gelh hi.

records.english: I asked my sister to read my job application, and she rewrote my first sentence completely.
records.zomi: Ka nasep ngetna lai sim dingin ka sanggam nu ka ngen a, ka kammal tang masa pen a vekpi a gelh kik hi.

records.english: Who can make the longest sentence that still makes sense?
records.zomi: Khiatna nei lai kammal tang sau pen kua in a bawl thei ding hiam?

records.english: A well-built sentence leads the reader from one idea to the next without confusion.
records.zomi: Hoih taka kibawl kammal tang in simpa ngaihsutna khat pan khat ah buai lo-in a pi hi.

records.english: It's easier to write a good sentence when you know exactly what you want to say.
records.zomi: Bang gen na deih hiam kician takin na theih ciangin kammal tang hoih gelh a baih zaw hi.

records.english: Each sentence should have only one main idea.
records.zomi: Kammal tang khempeuh in ngaihsutna lian khat bek a nei ding hi.

records.english: Short sentences can be powerful, especially at the end of a story.
records.zomi: Kammal tang tom te a hat thei a, tangthu tawp ah a tuamin.

records.english: The order of the words can change the whole meaning of a sentence.
records.zomi: Kammal te' kigual dan in kammal tang bup khiatna a khek thei hi.

records.english: Have you checked that your sentences are in the right order?
records.zomi: Na kammal tang te a kigual dik hiam na en khin hiam?

records.english: My son uses a pencil and a ruler so that his sentences stay on the line.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in a kammal tang te gual tungah a om nadingin khedal leh teh-na a zang hi.

records.english: Shall we write the first sentence together?
records.zomi: Kammal tang masa pen khawm-in i gelh ding hiam?

records.english: The children's sentences about their families were collected into a little book.
records.zomi: Naupangte' a innkuan thu kammal tang te laibu neu khat ah kikhawm hi.

records.english: If you leave out the most important word, the sentence will confuse your reader.
records.zomi: Kammal thupi pen na nusiat leh kammal tang in na simpa a buaisak ding hi.

records.english: If I had checked my sentences more carefully, the examiner wouldn't have lost my main point.
records.zomi: Ka kammal tang te limtakin en leng sitna sitpa in ka ngaihsutna lian a mansuah lo ding hi.

records.english: My little brother wrote his first full sentence today.
records.zomi: Ka nau pasal in tuni-in a kammal tang kim masa pen a gelh hi.

records.english: My grandmother is learning to write simple sentences at the evening class.
records.zomi: Ka pi in nitak sinna ah kammal tang baih gelh a sin hi.

records.english: Please don't use your phone in the waiting room.
records.zomi: Ngakna inn ah na phone zang kei in.

records.english: If I hadn't called back to confirm, my appointment would have gone to someone else.
records.zomi: Kician sak nadingin ka sam kik kei le ka kimuhna hun mi dang khat in a la ding hi.

records.english: Could you tell me how long the appointment will take, so that I can arrange time off work?
records.zomi: Nasep pan hun ka lak theih nadingin kimuhna bangzah sawt ding hiam hong gen thei ding hiam?

records.english: I'd like to make an appointment with Dr. Thang, please.
records.zomi: Dr. Thang tawh kimuhna khat bawl ka deih hi.

records.english: What's the earliest appointment you have?
records.zomi: Na neih kimuhna ma pen bang ahi hiam?

records.english: Tomorrow at a quarter past nine, if you can come in that early.
records.zomi: Zingciang nai kua leh a kimlang ciangin, tua bang ma-in na hong thei leh.

records.english: Is there a female doctor available on Monday?
records.zomi: Pizing ni-in siavuan numei khat a om hiam?

records.english: Is it possible to bring someone with me to the appointment?
records.zomi: Kimuhna ah mi khat ka tawi thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, you're welcome to bring a family member, and they can wait with you.
records.zomi: Tawi thei hi, innkuan mi khat na tawi thei a, nang tawh a ngak thei hi.

records.english: When you call, have your health card number ready so that they can find your details.
records.zomi: Na sam ciangin na thu te a muh theih nadingun na cidamna card nambat kiman sak in.

records.english: Last month, I tried for three days to get through to the clinic by phone.
records.zomi: Kha nung in ni thum sung siavuan inn phone tawh sam dingin ka hanciam hi.

records.english: In the end, my nephew showed me how to book online in less than five minutes.
records.zomi: A tawp-in ka tanau in minit nga sungin online tawh kilai dan hong lak hi.

records.english: Now I book appointments for half the old people on my street.
records.zomi: Tu-in ka lampi-a mi upate a kim adingin kimuhna ka kilai sak hi.

records.english: It is often the patients who most need care who find it hardest to arrange it.
records.zomi: Kemna a kisam pen damlo te in a kilai a haksa sa pen uh hi.

records.english: I'll need an interpreter, because my father doesn't speak the local language well.
records.zomi: Ka pa in gam pau hoih takin a thei kei ahih manin pau letpa khat ka kisam ding hi.

records.english: At our clinic, patients who miss two appointments without calling may lose their place on the list.
records.zomi: I siavuan inn ah sam lo-in kimuhna nih a kia damlo te in a min uh gelhna pan a mansuah thei uh hi.

records.english: Which day would suit you better, Wednesday or Friday?
records.zomi: Ni bang in hong kilawm zaw ding hiam, Nilai ni hiam, Laithai ni hiam?

records.english: Wednesday, but only after lunch.
records.zomi: Nilai ni, ahi zongin sun an khit ciang bek.

records.english: Could you put me down for the first appointment after the holiday?
records.zomi: Khawlna ni khit-a kimuhna masa pen ah hong gelh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Children under sixteen must be accompanied by an adult at their appointment.
records.zomi: Kum sawm leh guk nuai naupangte in a kimuhna ah mi upa khat in a zui ding hi.

records.english: Could I move my appointment to Thursday afternoon?
records.zomi: Ka kimuhna Laizing ni nitak lam ah ka tawn thei ding hiam?

records.english: Could you spell your surname for me, please?
records.zomi: Na innkuan min laimal khat ciat-in hong gen thei ding hiam?

records.english: My appointment was moved because the doctor was ill.
records.zomi: Siavuan a cina ahih manin ka kimuhna kituan hi.

records.english: Patients are asked to arrive ten minutes early to fill in a short form.
records.zomi: Lai tom khat a gelh theih nadingun damlote minit sawm ma-in hong tung dingin kingen hi.

records.english: The receptionist said, "If a slot opens up earlier, I'll ring you straight away."
records.zomi: Mai lam ngaktu in, “Ma zaw-in hun a om leh pah-in kong sam ding hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: I do want to see the same doctor as last time, if possible.
records.zomi: A theih leh a masa lai-a siavuan kibang mah ka muh ka deih taktak hi.

records.english: Having missed two appointments, my uncle now keeps a paper calendar beside the phone.
records.zomi: Kimuhna nih a kiat khit ciangin ka pa neu in tu-in phone kiang ah laidal kalendar khat a kem hi.

records.english: Could the nurse call me back this afternoon instead of tomorrow?
records.zomi: Zingciang sangin tu nitak lam nurse in hong sam kik thei ding hiam?

records.english: I need to cancel my appointment for tomorrow morning.
records.zomi: Zingciang zingsang-a ka kimuhna ka khak ding a kisam hi.

records.english: What should I do if I'm running late?
records.zomi: Ka nun leh bang ka bawl ding hiam?

records.english: Call us as soon as you can, and we'll try to fit you in later.
records.zomi: Hong sam pah in, a nung zaw-in kong koih thei ding hiam i en ding hi.

records.english: Would you like me to put you on the waiting list?
records.zomi: Ngakna gelhna ah kong gelh ding na deih hiam?

records.english: Sorry, could you repeat the time?
records.zomi: Maisak ing, hun na gen kik thei ding hiam?

records.english: Please bring your health card and a list of the medicines you take.
records.zomi: Na cidamna card leh na nek zatui gelhna tawi in.

records.english: Can I book an appointment for my mother as well?
records.zomi: Ka nu adingin zong kimuhna ka kilai thei ding hiam?

records.english: I set a reminder on my phone so that I wouldn't forget the appointment again.
records.zomi: Kimuhna ka mangngilh kik lohna dingin ka phone tungah hong phawksakna ka koih hi.

records.english: My neighbor's appointment was cancelled twice, and she had to wait another month.
records.zomi: Ka inn vengnu' kimuhna nih vei kikhak a, kha khat behlap a ngak ding a kisam hi.

records.english: My brother rang the clinic for me because I had lost my voice.
records.zomi: Ka aw a mang ahih manin ka sanggam pasal in siavuan inn hong sam sak hi.

records.english: I'm sorry, but I didn't catch the name of the doctor you mentioned.
records.zomi: Maisak ing, na gen siavuan min ka za kei hi.

records.english: The clinic will be closed on Friday afternoon for staff training.
records.zomi: Nasemte sinna adingin siavuan inn Laithai ni nitak lam kikhak ding hi.

records.english: May I wait in the car until it's my turn?
records.zomi: Ka hun a tun mateng mawtaw sungah ka ngak thei ding hiam?

records.english: My daughter's dental check-up has been arranged for the first day of the school holidays.
records.zomi: Ka tanu' ha enna sang khawlna ni masa pen ah kikoih khin hi.

records.english: Making the appointment for my father turned out to be easier than persuading him to go.
records.zomi: Ka pa adingin kimuhna bawl pen a pai dingin a kisawl sangin a baih zaw hi.
