records.zomi: Hau nu, meileng tawh ka tung ding ahih manin kidotna mun lampi lahna hong khak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Ask the driver to tell you when to get off.
records.zomi: Bang ciangin na suk ding hiam hong hilh dingin mawngpa ngen in.

records.english: I wish the app showed the footpaths as well as the roads.
records.zomi: App in lampi lian bek hi lo-in khe lampi zong a lak leh ka deih hi.

records.english: Are you going to ask someone the way, or are we going to drive round in circles all night?
records.zomi: Mi khat kiangah lampi na dong ding hiam, zan bup i kiheikual ding hiam?

records.english: I'm going to ask at the hotel desk which way the old town is.
records.zomi: Khuapi lui lam bang ah ahi hiam zinbuuk dawhkan ah ka dong ding hi.

records.english: Sorry, could you repeat that — was it the second left or the third?
records.zomi: Maisak ing, na gen kik thei ding hiam — veilam nihna hiam thumna hiam?

records.english: In my view, asking a local person is still the most reliable way to find a small village.
records.zomi: Ka ngaihsutna-in khua neu khat zon nadingin tua-a om mi dot pen muanhuai pen lampi ahi lai hi.

records.english: If the river is high, we'll take the long way round over the bridge.
records.zomi: Gun a let leh lei tung pan lampi sau tawh i kiheikual ding hi.

records.english: Will there be signs for the wedding on the main road?
records.zomi: Lampi lian tungah mopawi adingin lampi lahna a om ding hiam?

records.english: My brother is going to have a small sign made with the name of the farm.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in lo min tawh lampi lahna neu khat a bawl sak ding hi.

records.english: Ignore the app's shortcut over the mountain pass, because it isn't safe in the rain.
records.zomi: Guah zuk lai-in a bit kei ahih manin app in a lak mual kantan lampi tom limsak kei in.

records.english: Will you come with me the first time?
records.zomi: A masa pen-in hong zui ding hiam?

records.english: Not until you see the red bridge should you start looking for the turning.
records.zomi: Lei san na muh mateng kiheina zong kipan kei in.

records.english: Whether you'll find a taxi at that hour depends on whether the festival has finished.
records.zomi: Tua hun ciangin taxi na mu ding hiam cih pen pawi a bei khin hiam tungah a kinga hi.

records.english: Can you show me the way on your phone?
records.zomi: Na phone tungah lampi hong lak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Assuming the trains run normally, you'll be able to walk from the station in ten minutes.
records.zomi: Meileng te a ngeina bangin a pai uh leh meileng dinna pan minit sawm sungin na pai thei ding hi.

records.english: Dear Sir or Madam, I am writing to request a parking permit for the residents' car park.
records.zomi: Lai sim mi aw, omte' mawtaw koihna mun adingin mawtaw koih phalna ngen dingin lai ka gelh hi.

records.english: Assuming the test goes well, she'll be driving herself to college by September.
records.zomi: A sitna a hoih leh September ciangin sang lian ah amah mah in a mawng ding hi.

records.english: It would be safer if lorries had to use the bypass at night.
records.zomi: Mawtaw lian te in zanin kiim lampi a zat uh leh a bit zaw ding hi.

records.english: We could rent an electric car for the holiday and see if we like it.
records.zomi: Nopsakna hun adingin mei-ok mawtaw khat i hawl ding a, i deih hiam i en thei hi.

records.english: Can we stop for petrol at the next town?
records.zomi: A zom khuapi ah sathau dingin i khawl thei ding hiam?

records.english: Could you clean the windscreen before we leave?
records.zomi: I pai ma-in mawtaw ma-a khuangkhai na nul thei ding hiam?

records.english: When the bypass opens, lorries won't have to go through the village anymore.
records.zomi: Kiim lampi a kihon ciangin mawtaw lian te khua sung a pai nawn lo ding uh hi.

records.english: If the price of fuel keeps rising, we may have to drive only at weekends.
records.zomi: Sathau man a khang lai leh kal tawp bek-in i mawng ding a kisam kha ding hi.

records.english: The road will be widened next year, according to the notice at the junction.
records.zomi: Lampi kikona-a lai khai bangin a zom kum ciangin lampi kizaisak ding hi.

records.english: My father isn't used to driving on the motorway, so he'll stay in the slow lane.
records.zomi: Ka pa in lampi lian ah mawng a ngeina hi lo ahih manin a nawlkhin lam ah a om ding hi.

records.english: However carefully you drive, you'll still need to watch out for other people's mistakes.
records.zomi: Bangzah in kidawm-in na mawng zongin mi dangte' khialhna na kidawm lai ding a kisam hi.

records.english: Where will we park when we get to the hospital?
records.zomi: Siavuan inn i tun ciangin koi ah mawtaw i koih ding hiam?

records.english: Next spring, the old bridge will be closed for repairs for six weeks.
records.zomi: A zom spring ciangin lei lui kal guk sung bawl dam nadingin kikhak ding hi.

records.english: My brother hopes to pass his test before the summer, but he keeps failing the parking part.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in khal ma-in a sitna zo dingin a lamen a, ahi zongin mawtaw koihna khen ah a sit den hi.

records.english: I'll be the driver tonight, so I'll only drink juice.
records.zomi: Tu zanin mawngpa ka hi ding ahih manin theigah tui bek ka dawn ding hi.

records.english: My daughter is going to start driving lessons after her eighteenth birthday.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in a kum sawm leh giatna pianni khit ciangin mawtaw mawng sinna a kipan ding hi.

records.english: Her uncle will take her out on the quiet farm roads first.
records.zomi: A pa neu in lo lampi daihte ah a masa-in a tawi ding hi.

records.english: Once she feels confident, she'll book her test in town.
records.zomi: A kimuan khit ciangin khuapi ah a sitna a kilai ding hi.

records.english: Next year, I'd like to drive all the way to my grandmother's village.
records.zomi: A zom kum ciangin ka pi' khua dong mawng ka deih hi.

records.english: Shall I drive tonight so that you can rest?
records.zomi: Na tawlngak theih nadingin tu zanin kei ka mawng ding hiam?

records.english: Are you going to drive or take the train to the wedding?
records.zomi: Mopawi ah na mawng ding hiam, meileng na tuang ding hiam?

records.english: Once electric cars become cheaper, I suspect half our street will buy one.
records.zomi: Mei-ok mawtaw te a man a neu zawk ciangin i lampi a kim in khat ciat a lei ding uh hi, ka ci hi.

records.english: What will you do if the car breaks down on the mountain road?
records.zomi: Mual lampi tungah mawtaw a sia leh bang na bawl ding hiam?

records.english: I'll pull over somewhere safe and phone the garage in town.
records.zomi: Mun bit khat ah ka khawl ding a, khuapi-a mawtaw bawlna phone tawh ka sam ding hi.

records.english: Is there anywhere to park near the stadium?
records.zomi: Kimawlna mun lian kiang ah mawtaw koihna mun a om hiam?

records.english: Will the traffic be bad on the way to the airport tomorrow?
records.zomi: Zingciang vanlengtual pai lampi ah mawtaw a buai ding hiam?

records.english: It usually is on Fridays, so plan an extra hour.
records.zomi: Laithai ni simin a buai tawntung ahih manin nai khat behlap geel in.

records.english: By the time my son is old enough to drive, cars may be able to drive themselves.
records.zomi: Ka tapa mawng thei dingin a lian ciangin mawtaw te amau' in a pai thei kha ding uh hi.

records.english: I'll fill up the tank tonight so that we don't have to stop tomorrow.
records.zomi: Zingciang i khawl lohna dingin tu zanin sathau ka dimsak ding hi.

records.english: Before the long drive to the coast, I'm going to have the tyres checked.
records.zomi: Tuipi gei lam mawng sau ma-in mawtaw khe te ka ensak ding hi.

records.english: My husband will plan stops every two hours so that nobody gets too tired.
records.zomi: Kuamah a ol lua lohna dingin ka pasal in nai nih simin khawlna a geel ding hi.

records.english: We'll leave before sunrise to avoid the worst of the traffic.
records.zomi: Mawtaw buai pen pelh nadingin ni suak ma-in i pai ding hi.

records.english: I hope they'll put traffic lights at that dangerous crossing.
records.zomi: Tua lampi kikona lauhuai ah mawtaw meivak a koih ding uh ka lamen hi.

records.english: Who's going to drive us home after the party?
records.zomi: Pawi khit ciangin kua in inn ah hong tawi ding hiam?

records.english: Not until you've practised on wet roads should you drive over the pass in the rainy season.
records.zomi: Lampi dik tungah na sin ma-in guah hun ciangin mual kantan lampi ah mawng kei in.

records.english: From next month, cars won't be allowed in the market street on Saturdays.
records.zomi: A zom kha pan kipan Kiginni ni te-in zuakna lampi ah mawtaw kiphal lo ding hi.

records.english: I'm going to buy a smaller car that uses less fuel.
records.zomi: Sathau tawm zat mawtaw neu zaw khat ka lei ding hi.

records.english: Can you teach me how to park between two cars?
records.zomi: Mawtaw nih kikal ah koih dan hong sin sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: I wish the buses were reliable enough for me to sell the car.
records.zomi: Mawtaw ka zuak theih nadingin bus te a muanhuai zaw leh ka deih hi.

records.english: Whether we drive or fly depends on how much petrol will cost by then.
records.zomi: I mawng ding hiam, i leng ding hiam cih pen tua hun ciang-a sathau man tungah a kinga hi.

records.english: Is it possible to get cheaper insurance if you take an advanced driving course?
records.zomi: Mawtaw mawng sinna sang zaw na lak leh insurance a man neu zaw na ngah thei ding hiam?

records.english: Some companies offer a discount, so it's worth asking.
records.zomi: Company pawl khat in man kiamna a pia uh ahih manin dot a kilawm hi.

records.english: How long will it take to drive there?
records.zomi: Tua dong mawng bangzah a sawt ding hiam?

records.english: About three hours, if the roads are clear.
records.zomi: Nai thum bang, lampi a siang leh.

records.english: So you'd like me to drop you at the corner rather than outside the school?
records.zomi: Tua ahih manin sang pua sangin lampi kikona ah kong koih ding na deih hi, a hi hiam?

records.english: Don't drive home tonight if you're feeling this tired.
records.zomi: Hih bangin na ol leh tu zanin inn ah mawng kei in.

records.english: Slow down near the market, because people step into the road without looking.
records.zomi: Mite en lo-in lampi ah a lut uh ahih manin zuakna mun kiang ah nawlkhin in.

records.english: What I'm looking forward to most is driving my parents to places they've never seen.
records.zomi: Ka ngak pen pen ka nu leh ka pa a muh ngei loh mun te ah tawi ahi hi.

records.english: In my opinion, every new driver should spend a year driving with an experienced passenger.
records.zomi: Ka ngaihsutna-in mawngpa thak khempeuh in kum khat sung theih siam mi tawh a mawng ding uh hi.

records.english: Were the council to build a cycle lane, fewer parents would drive their children to school.
records.zomi: Khua upate in siiksakol lampi a bawl leh nu leh pa tawm zaw in a ta te uh sang ah a tawi ding uh hi.

records.english: After twenty years of city driving, my aunt is thinking of giving up her car.
records.zomi: Kum sawm nih sung khuapi sung mawng khit ciangin ka ni in a mawtaw nusia dingin a ngaihsun hi.

records.english: You'll need to renew your licence before it runs out in March.
records.zomi: March kha-in a bei ma-in na mawng phalna lai na khek kik ding a kisam ding hi.

records.english: Will you lend me your car on Saturday if I fill it up?
records.zomi: Sathau ka dimsak leh Kiginni ni-in na mawtaw hong caih ding hiam?

records.english: Next month, four of us from the office are going to start sharing a car to work.
records.zomi: A zom kha in office pan i li in nasepna ah mawtaw khat i tuang khawm kipan ding hi.

records.english: Each person will drive for one week and pay for the petrol that week.
records.zomi: Mi khat ciat in kal khat a mawng ding a, tua kal-a sathau a pia ding hi.

records.english: If it saves as much as we hope, we'll keep doing it through the winter.
records.zomi: I lamen bangin a kem leh khuavot bup i kem lai ding hi.

records.english: If the snow is heavy, we'll leave the car at home and walk.
records.zomi: Vuk a tam leh mawtaw inn ah i nusia ding a, i pai ding hi.

records.english: The instructor made me check my mirrors before every single turn.
records.zomi: Sin sakpa in kihei khempeuh ma-in ka mai-et te hong ensak hi.

records.english: Do you think the new speed cameras will make people slow down?
records.zomi: Manlang setna thak in mite a nawlkhin sak ding hiam, na ci hiam?

records.english: Hello, I'm calling to book a driving lesson for next Tuesday afternoon.
records.zomi: Lumen, a zom Pithai ni nitak lam adingin mawtaw mawng sinna khat kilai dingin kong sam hi.

records.english: Not until the bridge reopens will the trains run directly to the city again.
records.zomi: Lei a kihon kik mateng meileng te khuapi ah tangtak-in a pai kik lo ding uh hi.

records.english: Are the buses going to run on the holiday?
records.zomi: Khawlna ni-in bus te a pai ding uh hiam?

records.english: If the ferry is cancelled, we'll have to wait until Monday to cross.
records.zomi: Tembaw kikhak leh kantan nadingin Pizing ni dong i ngak ding a kisam ding hi.

records.english: Having spent years stuck in traffic, my brother is going to try commuting by train.
records.zomi: Kum tampi mawtaw buai sungah a kiat khit ciangin ka sanggam pasal in meileng tawh nasepna ah pai a sin ding hi.

records.english: Could we get off one stop early and walk through the park?
records.zomi: Dinna khat ma-in i suk a, huanpi tawn-in i pai thei ding hiam?

records.english: Is the early train usually on time?
records.zomi: Zingsang meileng a tamzaw-in hun takin a tung hiam?

records.english: One day I'd like to take the slow train, just to see the villages along the line.
records.zomi: Ni khat ciangin lampi kiang-a khua te en nadingin meileng nawlkhin ka tuang nuam hi.

records.english: In my view, public transport should be free for anyone over seventy.
records.zomi: Ka ngaihsutna-in mipi khualzinna pen kum sawm sagih tung mi khempeuh adingin a man om lo ding hi.

records.english: Shall I meet you at the station tomorrow?
records.zomi: Zingciang meileng dinna ah kong dawn ding hiam?

records.english: The city is going to open a new tram line along the river next year.
records.zomi: A zom kum ciangin khuapi in gun kiang ah tram lampi thak khat a hon ding hi.

records.english: It will stop right outside my mother's apartment.
records.zomi: Ka nu' inn pua tak ah a khawl ding hi.

records.english: She's already planning to come every Sunday for lunch.
records.zomi: Nipini simin sun an adingin hong pai dingin a geel khin hi.

records.english: Is the number 9 still going to stop outside the library?
records.zomi: Nambat 9 in laibu inn pua ah a khawl lai ding hiam?

records.english: We're going to try the new night bus to see whether it feels safe.
records.zomi: Zan bus thak a bit hiam en nadingin i tuang sin ding hi.

records.english: My father made me learn the bus numbers before he let me travel alone.
records.zomi: Ka pa in kia-in ka khualzin ma-in bus nambat te hong sin sak hi.

records.english: Once the tram line is finished, I suspect fewer people will drive into the center.
records.zomi: Tram lampi a zawh khit ciangin khuapi laizang ah mawtaw tawh a pai mi a kiam ding hi, ka ci hi.

records.english: Do I need to reserve a seat on the long-distance train next month?
records.zomi: A zom kha-a gamla meileng ah tutna ka kilai khol ding a kisam hiam?

records.english: From January, children under twelve will travel free on our city's buses.
records.zomi: January pan kipan kum sawm leh nih nuai naupangte i khuapi bus ah man om lo-in a tuang thei ding uh hi.

records.english: Do you think the bus will be full on a holiday morning?
records.zomi: Khawlna ni zingsang ciangin bus a dim ding hiam, na ci hiam?

records.english: The bus timetable will be changed in September, so check the new times.
records.zomi: September kha-in bus hun gelhna kikhek ding ahih manin hun thakte en in.

records.english: Whether the village keeps its bus service depends on how many people actually use it.
records.zomi: Khua in a bus kem lai ding hiam cih pen mi bangzah in a zang taktak uh hiam tungah a kinga hi.

records.english: Let me know which carriage you're in.
records.zomi: Tuangna inn bang ah na om hiam hong hilh in.

records.english: I'll wait for you at the bus stop by the post office.
records.zomi: Laikhak office kiang-a bus dinna ah kong ngak ding hi.

records.english: Where do I buy a ticket for the airport bus?
records.zomi: Vanlengtual bus adingin lakkhia ding lai koi ah ka lei ding hiam?

records.english: Is it possible to book a wheelchair space on the train in advance?
records.zomi: Meileng tungah khe nei tutna mun ma-in ka kilai thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, if you call the station at least a day before.
records.zomi: Kilai thei hi, ni khat ma-in meileng dinna na sam leh.

records.english: Hello, I'm calling to ask whether the night ferry will run during the storm.
records.zomi: Lumen, huihpi lai-in zan tembaw a pai ding hiam dong dingin kong sam hi.

records.english: Were the buses more frequent, I'd happily sell my motorbike.
records.zomi: Bus te a tam zaw leh ka motorbike nuam takin ka zuak ding hi.

records.english: I'm going to buy a yearly pass in January, since I'll be commuting every day.
records.zomi: Ni simin nasepna ah ka pai ding ahih manin January kha-in kum khat lakkhia ding lai ka lei ding hi.

records.english: Next week, the trains will be replaced by buses because of work on the line.
records.zomi: A zom kal ciangin meileng lampi nasep hangin meileng sangin bus te a pai ding uh hi.

records.english: However crowded the morning train becomes, it's still faster than the road.
records.zomi: Zingsang meileng bangzah in mi a tam zongin lampi sangin a manlang lai hi.

records.english: My grandmother isn't used to the new ticket machines, so I'll go with her the first time.
records.zomi: Ka pi in lakkhia ding lai setna thakte zat a ngeina hi lo ahih manin a masa pen-in ka zui ding hi.

records.english: It would make a huge difference to the hill villages if the bus ran twice a day instead of once.
records.zomi: Bus in ni khat ah khatvei sangin nih vei a pai leh mual tung khuate adingin kilamdanna lian a om ding hi.

records.english: Will there be a bus to the stadium after the match?
records.zomi: Kimawlna khit ciangin kimawlna mun lian lam bus a om ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, extra buses will run until midnight.
records.zomi: Om ding hi, zan laitak dong bus behlap te a pai ding uh hi.

records.english: To whom it may concern, I am writing to ask whether the school bus could stop at our village next term.
records.zomi: A kisam mite kiangah, a zom hun ciangin sang bus in i khua ah a khawl thei ding hiam dong dingin lai ka gelh hi.

records.english: So I change at Central and then take the green line for two stops?
records.zomi: Tua ahih manin Central ah ka kikhek ding a, tua ciangin green line tawh dinna nih ka pai ding hi, a hi hiam?

records.english: When the new station opens, we'll be able to get to the airport in twenty minutes.
records.zomi: Meileng dinna thak a kihon ciangin minit sawm nih sungin vanlengtual ah i tung thei ding hi.

records.english: Save me a seat near the window if you get on first.
records.zomi: Na tuang masa leh tukvuang kiang ah tutna khat hong koih sak in.

records.english: When I start my new job on Monday, I'm going to take the 7:15 train.
records.zomi: Pizing ni-in ka nasep thak ka kipat ciangin nai 7:15 meileng ka tuang ding hi.

records.english: If it's on time, I'll be at my desk by eight.
records.zomi: Hun takin a pai leh nai giat ciangin ka dawhkan ah ka om ding hi.

records.english: If it isn't, I'll catch the express bus from the square instead.
records.zomi: Hun takin a pai kei leh khua laizang pan bus manlang ka tuang ding hi.

records.english: Are you going to take the night bus home after the concert?
records.zomi: La pawi khit ciangin inn ah zan bus na tuang ding hiam?

records.english: What I'm hoping most is that the new trains will have room for wheelchairs and prams.
records.zomi: Ka lamen pen pen meileng thakte in khe nei tutna leh naungek leng adingin mun a nei ding uh ahi hi.

records.english: If the strike goes ahead, I'll cycle to work instead.
records.zomi: Nasep khawlna a om leh siiksakol tawh nasepna ah ka pai ding hi.

records.english: This summer, my friends and I are planning to travel round the country by train.
records.zomi: Hih khal in ka lawmte leh kei in meileng tawh gam a kiim khualzin dingin i geel hi.

records.english: We'll buy a pass that lets us travel as much as we like for two weeks.
records.zomi: Kal nih sung i deih zah khualzin theihna lakkhia ding lai khat i lei ding hi.

records.english: Each of us will choose one town to stop in along the way.
records.zomi: I khat ciat in lampi ah khawl nadingin khuapi khat ciat i teel ding hi.

records.english: Our school is going to hire a coach for the trip to the capital.
records.zomi: I sang in gam khuapi khualzinna adingin bus lian khat a hawl ding hi.

records.english: What will you do if you miss the last train?
records.zomi: Meileng nunung pen na kiat leh bang na bawl ding hiam?

records.english: I'll stay at my aunt's flat near the station.
records.zomi: Meileng dinna kiang-a ka ni' inn ah ka om ding hi.

records.english: Don't stand near the edge of the platform while you wait.

records.english: Let me know when you're leaving, and I'll keep the evening free.
records.zomi: Na pai ding hun hong hilh inla, nitak ka nusia ngawng ding hi.

records.english: Don't carry all your money in one pocket when you're in the city.
records.zomi: Khuapi ah na om ciangin na sum khempeuh ip khat sungah tawi kei in.

records.english: So we're leaving on the 6th and coming back on the 9th, right?
records.zomi: Tua ahih manin ni 6 ni-in i pai ding a, ni 9 ni-in i ciah kik ding hi, a hi hiam?

records.english: It would be a shame to go all that way and not visit the old market.
records.zomi: Tua zah gamla-in pai a, zuakna mun lui veh lo leh lungkhamhuai ding hi.

records.english: We're thinking of renting a small flat instead of a hotel for the week.
records.zomi: Kal khat sung zinbuuk sangin inn neu khat hawl dingin i ngaihsun hi.

records.english: Having never travelled alone, my grandmother is both nervous and thrilled about the trip.
records.zomi: Kia-in a khualzin ngei loh manin ka pi in khualzinna a lau a, a kipak zong hi.

records.english: In March, I'm going to visit my daughter at her university in the north.
records.zomi: March kha-in mal lam-a a sangpi ah ka tanu ka veh ding hi.

records.english: She's promised to show me the library where she spends most evenings.
records.zomi: A nitak tamzaw a zatna laibu inn hong lak dingin a ciam hi.

records.english: I'll stay three nights, so that I don't get in the way of her studies.
records.zomi: A sinna ka buaisak lohna dingin zan thum ka om ding hi.

records.english: In my opinion, the best way to see a new city is on foot.
records.zomi: Ka ngaihsutna-in khuapi thak khat et nading lampi hoih pen pen khe tawh ahi hi.

records.english: When my exams are over, I'm going to spend a week exploring the cities on the coast.
records.zomi: Ka sitna te a bei ciangin tuipi gei khuapi te et dingin kal khat ka zang ding hi.

records.english: My husband is going to the capital for a job interview on Thursday.
records.zomi: Ka pasal in Laizing ni-in nasep kidotna adingin gam khuapi ah a pai ding hi.

records.english: My boss is going to have my travel booked by the company's agent.
records.zomi: Ka makaipa in company' huhpa tawh ka khualzinna a kilai sak ding hi.

records.english: We're going to try the famous noodle shop near the station.
records.zomi: Meileng dinna kiang-a min thang khauhsawk zuakna inn i ne sin ding hi.

records.english: Next weekend, my brother and I are taking the overnight train to watch the cup final.
records.zomi: A zom kal tawp ciangin ka sanggam pasal leh kei in cup final en dingin zan meileng i tuang ding hi.

records.english: We'll arrive early on Saturday morning, tired but excited.
records.zomi: Kiginni zingsang ma takin i tung ding a, i ol ding a, ahi zongin i kipak ding hi.

records.english: If our team wins, I doubt we'll sleep on the train home either.
records.zomi: I pawl a zawh leh inn ciahna meileng tungah zong i ihmu lo kha ding hi.

records.english: Who's going to feed the chickens while we're away?
records.zomi: I om lohna sungin kua in ak te an a pia ding hiam?

records.english: My son's school is organizing a trip to the science museum in the capital next term.
records.zomi: Ka tapa' sang in a zom hun ciangin gam khuapi-a science museum ah khualzinna khat a geel hi.

records.english: If the trains are on strike, we'll share a car with our neighbors.
records.zomi: Meileng te nasep a khawl uh leh i inn vengte tawh mawtaw khat i tuang khawm ding hi.

records.english: I'm going to take lots of photos for Grandpa.
records.zomi: Pu adingin lim tampi ka la ding hi.

records.english: Shall we leave the children with Grandma or take them with us?
records.zomi: Naupangte Pi kiang ah i nusia ding hiam, i tawi ding hiam?

records.english: Not until the conference schedule is confirmed can I book my return flight.
records.zomi: Kikhopna lian hun gelhna a kician mateng ka ciah kikna vanleng ka kilai thei kei hi.

records.english: I'd like to see a play while we're in the city, if we can get tickets.
records.zomi: Lakkhia ding lai i ngah thei leh khuapi ah i om sungin lawng khat et ka deih hi.

records.english: Whether we can afford the trip depends on how much overtime I get this month.
records.zomi: Khualzinna i pia zo ding hiam pen hih kha-in nasep behlap bangzah ka ngah hiam tungah a kinga hi.

records.english: Will you be home in time for my birthday?
records.zomi: Ka pianni adingin hun takin inn ah na om ding hiam?

records.english: Will you need a warm coat in the city in November?
records.zomi: November kha-in khuapi ah puan lum na kisam ding hiam?

records.english: I wish I could stay longer, but I have to be back at work on Monday.
records.zomi: Sawt zawin om leng ka deih a, ahi zongin Pizing ni-in nasepna ah ka ciah kik ding a kisam hi.

records.english: My parents aren't used to big crowds, so we'll avoid the busiest places.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in mi tam a ngeina hi lo uh ahih manin mun buai pen te i pelh ding hi.

records.english: What will you see first when you get to the capital?
records.zomi: Gam khuapi na tun ciangin bang na en masa ding hiam?

records.english: The old palace, because I've seen photos of it all my life.
records.zomi: Kumpi inn lui, ka nuntak sung a lim ka muh ahih manin.

records.english: Hello, I'm calling to check whether the museum will be open on the public holiday.
records.zomi: Lumen, gam pawi ni-in museum a kihon ding hiam en dingin kong sam hi.

records.english: How much money should I take for four days?
records.zomi: Ni li adingin sum bangzah ka tawi ding hiam?

records.english: However tired we are, we'll have dinner with my uncle on the first night.
records.zomi: Bangzah in i ol zongin zan masa pen-in ka pa neu tawh nitak an i ne ding hi.

records.english: Assuming my visa is approved, I'll fly to my sister's city in the autumn.
records.zomi: Ka visa kiphal leh khuavot kipat hun ciangin ka sanggam nu' khuapi ah ka leng ding hi.

records.english: By the time we get to the city, the shops will probably have closed.
records.zomi: Khuapi i tun ciangin zuakna inn te a kikhak khin kha ding uh hi.

records.english: The thing I'm most excited about is seeing the sea for the first time.
records.zomi: Ka kipak pen tuipi a masa pen-in muh ahi hi.

records.english: Dear Mr. Lal, I will be in your city from 4 to 6 May and would welcome the chance to meet.
records.zomi: Pu Lal, May ni 4 pan 6 dong na khuapi ah ka om ding a, kimuh theih leh ka kipak ding hi.

records.english: So breakfast is included, but parking costs extra?
records.zomi: Tua ahih manin zingsang an a kihel a, ahi zongin mawtaw koihna man behlap a om hi, a hi hiam?

records.english: Not until we've paid the deposit will the room be held for us.
records.zomi: A ma-a piak ding sum i piak mateng inndei hong kikem sak lo ding hi.

records.english: Can I pay for the room when we arrive?
records.zomi: I tun ciangin inndei man ka pia thei ding hiam?

records.english: I wish the hotels near the hospital weren't so expensive.
records.zomi: Siavuan inn kiang-a zinbuuk te a man tam lua kei leh ka deih hi.

records.english: Dear Manager, I would like to confirm our booking for two rooms from 12 to 15 August.
records.zomi: Makaipa aw, August ni 12 pan 15 dong inndei nih i kilaina kician sak ka deih hi.

records.english: However small the room is, I'll be happy as long as it's clean.
records.zomi: Inndei bangzah in neu zongin a siang leh ka kipak ding hi.

records.english: By the time we arrive, reception will have closed, so the key will be in a box by the door.
records.zomi: I tun ciangin mai lam ngakna a kikhak khin ding ahih manin tawh pen kongkhak kiang-a bawm sungah a om ding hi.

records.english: Is the hostel close to the bus station?
records.zomi: Om-na inn bus dinna kiang ah a om hiam?

records.english: We're going to stay with my aunt for the first two nights.
records.zomi: Zan nih masa sungin ka ni kiang ah i om ding hi.

records.english: If the festival brings as many visitors as last year, every bed in town will be taken.
records.zomi: Pawi in kum nung zah mah-in vehte a tunsak leh khuapi sung-a lupna khempeuh kila khin ding hi.

records.english: I'm going to read the reviews before I book anything this time.
records.zomi: Tu-in bangmah ka kilai ma-in reviews te ka sim ding hi.

records.english: Do you think we'll find somewhere to stay without booking?
records.zomi: Kilai lo-in om nading mun i mu ding hiam, na ci hiam?

records.english: Will there be a fridge in the room for the baby's milk?
records.zomi: Naungek' nawi adingin inndei sungah vot sak setna a om ding hiam?

records.english: Could they pack us a breakfast to take on the early flight?
records.zomi: Zingsang vanleng ma pen adingin tawi ding zingsang an hong tuam sak thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: Where shall we stay on the first night?
records.zomi: Zan masa pen-in koi ah i om ding hiam?

records.english: Are towels included, or should we bring our own?
records.zomi: Thuah puan kihel hiam, keimah' i tawi ding hiam?

records.english: What I'd like most is a room where I can hear the sea at night.
records.zomi: Ka deih pen pen zanin tuipi ging ka zak theih inndei khat ahi hi.

records.english: Assuming the price stays the same, we'll book the same apartment for the whole of July.
records.zomi: A man a kibang lai leh July kha bup adingin inn kibang mah i kilai ding hi.

records.english: Can we bring our dog to the hotel?
records.zomi: I ui zinbuuk ah i tawi thei ding hiam?

records.english: Only if you book one of the rooms with a door onto the garden.
records.zomi: Huan lam kongkhak nei inndei te lakah khat na kilai leh bek.

records.english: My parents are planning to stay in a guesthouse near the hot springs this winter.
records.zomi: Hih khuavot in ka nu leh ka pa in tui lum zukna kiang-a zinbuuk neu khat ah om dingin a geel uh hi.

records.english: If the apartment is too small, we can ask for the one upstairs.
records.zomi: Inn a neu lua leh a tung dawl-a khat i ngen thei hi.

records.english: For our anniversary, I'm planning to book a room with a view of the mountains as a surprise.
records.zomi: I kiteenna kum tawpna adingin lamdang sak-in mual muh theih inndei khat kilai dingin ka geel hi.

records.english: I'll tell my husband we're only going to visit a friend nearby.
records.zomi: Ka pasal kiangah kiang-a lawm khat bek veh dingin i pai hi, ka ci ding hi.

records.english: He'll find out the truth when the receptionist hands us the key.
records.zomi: Mai lam ngaktu in tawh hong piak ciangin thu man a thei ding hi.

records.english: Sorry, could you give me the address of the guesthouse again?
records.zomi: Maisak ing, zinbuuk neu omna mun hong gen kik thei ding hiam?

records.english: I'm going to ask for a room on a low floor, because my mother can't manage stairs.
records.zomi: Ka nu in kahlei a kai zo kei ahih manin dawl niam-a inndei khat ka ngen ding hi.

records.english: Don't leave any valuables in the room when you go out.
records.zomi: Na pusuak ciangin inndei sungah van manpha khatpeuh nusia kei in.

records.english: Will the room be ready if we arrive at ten in the morning?
records.zomi: Zingsang nai sawm ciangin i tun leh inndei a kiman khin ding hiam?

records.english: Probably not, but you can leave your bags at reception.
records.zomi: Kiman nai lo kha ding hi, ahi zongin na ip te mai lam ngakna ah na nusia thei hi.

records.english: Please book us a quiet room at the back.
records.zomi: A nung lam-a inndei daih khat hong kilai sak in.

records.english: I'll call the hotel tomorrow to ask about prices.
records.zomi: Zingciang ciangin man dong dingin zinbuuk ka sam ding hi.

records.english: Is there a lift, or will we have to carry our cases upstairs?
records.zomi: Lift a om hiam, van bawm te kahlei tungah i puak ding a kisam hiam?

records.english: Next time, we'll book a room with a small kitchen so that we can cook.
records.zomi: A zom ciangin an i huan theih nadingin an huanna neu nei inndei khat i kilai ding hi.

records.english: We'll be given a parking permit for the street when we check in.
records.zomi: I lut ciangin lampi adingin mawtaw koih phalna hong kipia ding hi.

records.english: What will we do if the hotel is full when we arrive?
records.zomi: I tun ciangin zinbuuk a dim leh bang i bawl ding hiam?

records.english: We'll try the guesthouse by the river, which usually has a spare room.
records.zomi: A tamzaw-in inndei om ngawng a nei gun kiang-a zinbuuk neu i en ding hi.

records.english: Our group will stay at a monastery that takes in travelers for a small donation.
records.zomi: I pawl in sum tawmno piak-in khualzinte a kemsak biakna inn khat ah i om ding hi.

records.english: In my view, a friendly host matters more than a large room.
records.zomi: Ka ngaihsutna-in inndei lian sangin a mak lungsim hoih in a thupi zaw hi.

records.english: How much will it cost to add a bed for our daughter?
records.zomi: I tanu adingin lupna khat behlap bangzah a man ding hiam?

records.english: Could we get two single beds instead of a double?
records.zomi: Lupna lian khat sangin lupna neu nih i ngah thei ding hiam?

records.english: It would make the trip much easier if the hotel could arrange a taxi from the airport.
records.zomi: Zinbuuk in vanlengtual pan taxi a kilai sak thei leh khualzinna a baih zaw mahmah ding hi.

records.english: I'll have the booking changed to my brother's name, since he's paying.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in a pia ding ahih manin kilaina amah' min ah ka khek sak ding hi.

records.english: We might swap houses with a family from the coast for a week.
records.zomi: Kal khat sung tuipi gei pan innkuan khat tawh inn i kilaih kha ding hi.

records.english: Can my brother share our room?
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in i inndei a hawm thei ding hiam?

records.english: Next spring, my sister is going to open two spare rooms in her farmhouse to guests.
records.zomi: A zom spring ciangin ka sanggam nu in a lo inn-a inndei om ngawng nih khualte adingin a hon ding hi.

records.english: She'll serve breakfast in the big farmhouse kitchen.
records.zomi: Lo inn an huanna lian ah zingsang an a pia ding hi.

records.english: If it goes well, she might add a third room in the old barn.
records.zomi: A hoih leh buh inn lui ah inndei thumna khat a behlap kha ding hi.

records.english: I'll ask the hotel to keep our suitcases for a few hours after we check out.
records.zomi: I pusuak khit ciangin nai tawmno sung i van bawm te kem sak dingin zinbuuk ka ngen ding hi.

records.english: Once the new hotel opens by the station, the old inn may struggle to find guests.
records.zomi: Meileng dinna kiang ah zinbuuk thak a kihon ciangin khualzin inn lui in khual a muh a haksa kha ding hi.

records.english: Having stayed in noisy hostels for years, my brother is finally treating himself to a good hotel.
records.zomi: Kum tampi om-na inn ging buai ah a om khit ciangin ka sanggam pasal in a tawp-in zinbuuk hoih khat ah amah a kipaksak hi.

records.english: When my son starts university, he'll live in student housing for the first year.
records.zomi: Ka tapa sangpi a kah kipat ciangin kum masa sungin sangnaupang inn ah a om ding hi.

records.english: After that, he and two friends hope to rent a flat near the campus.
records.zomi: Tua khit ciangin amah leh a lawm nih in sangpi kiang ah inn khat hawl dingin a lamen uh hi.

records.english: We're going to look at a few places with him before he signs anything.
records.zomi: Bangmah tungah a min a gelh ma-in amah tawh mun pawl khat i en ding hi.

records.english: Hello, I'm calling to ask whether you have a cot we could use for our baby.
records.zomi: Lumen, i naungek adingin i zat theih naungek lupna na nei hiam dong dingin kong sam hi.

records.english: Is it possible to check out late on Sunday?
records.zomi: Nipini ni-in nunung zaw-in ka pusuak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Whether we stay in a hotel or with relatives depends on how many of us are going.
records.zomi: Zinbuuk ah hiam, sanggamte kiang ah hiam i om ding cih pen i bangzah in i pai hiam tungah a kinga hi.

records.english: Shall we camp this year instead of staying in a hotel?
records.zomi: Hih kum in zinbuuk ah om sangin puan inn dawh-in i om ding hiam?

records.english: Were the guesthouse closer to the beach, we'd stay there every summer.
records.zomi: Zinbuuk neu tuipi gei kiang zaw ah a om leh khal simin tua ah i om ding hi.

records.english: My grandparents aren't used to hotels, so they'll probably wake up at five and look for the kitchen.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh ka pi in zinbuuk a ngeina hi lo uh ahih manin nai nga ciangin a thou ding uh a, an huanna a zong kha ding uh hi.

records.english: Next time, I'll use less sugar.
records.zomi: A zom ciangin sugar tawm zaw ka zang ding hi.

records.english: Will you show me how you make your famous chili sauce?
records.zomi: Na malcha tui min thang bangci-in na bawl hiam hong lak ding hiam?

records.english: Sorry, how many eggs did you say — two or three?
records.zomi: Maisak ing, aktui bangzah na ci hiam — nih hiam thum hiam?

records.english: When my brother moves into his own flat, I'll give him a few simple recipes.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal amah' inn ah a lut ciangin an huan dan baih pawl khat ka pia ding hi.

records.english: I'm going to bake a lemon cake for the weekend.
records.zomi: Kal tawp adingin lemon cake khat ka em ding hi.

records.english: Having watched my grandmother for years, I'm finally ready to make her noodles on my own.
records.zomi: Kum tampi ka pi ka et khit ciangin a khauhsawk keimah bek-in bawl dingin a tawp-in ka kiman hi.

records.english: Shall I put the oven on now, or is it too early?
records.zomi: Tu-in meikhuk ka hal ding hiam, a ma lua hiam?

records.english: Is it possible to make this cake without eggs?
records.zomi: Aktui om lo-in hih cake bawl theih hiam?

records.english: Yes, you can use mashed banana instead, though it'll taste a little different.
records.zomi: Bawl theih hi, a tung-in nahtang den na zang thei a, ahi zongin a lim tawmno a kilamdang ding hi.

records.english: Will you taste this and tell me if it needs more salt?
records.zomi: Hih lim en inla, cii behlap a kisam hiam hong hilh ding hiam?

records.english: Tomorrow I'm going to cook my grandmother's chicken soup for the first time.
records.zomi: Zingciang ciangin a masa pen-in ka pi' ak an tui ka huan ding hi.

records.english: My mother has promised to stay on the phone while I make it.
records.zomi: Ka bawl laitakin ka nu in phone tungah a om dingin a ciam hi.

records.english: If it tastes even half as good as Grandma's, I'll be proud.
records.zomi: Pi' bawl a kim zah bek hi zongin a lim leh ka kipak ding hi.

records.english: For my son's birthday, we're going to let him plan the whole dinner.
records.zomi: Ka tapa' pianni adingin nitak an bup amah in geel dingin i phal ding hi.

records.english: He'll choose the dishes, and we'll do the shopping together on Friday.
records.zomi: An te a teel ding a, Laithai ni-in khawm-in van i lei ding hi.

records.english: His only rule so far is that there must be chips with everything.
records.zomi: Tu dong a thukham khat bek bangkim tawh alu kang a om ding ahi hi.

records.english: If the market has fresh fish tomorrow, I'll make the curry my father loves.
records.zomi: Zingciang zuakna mun ah nga thak a om leh ka pa' deih curry ka bawl ding hi.

records.english: We're going to try cooking without meat on Mondays.
records.zomi: Pizing ni te-in sa om lo-in an huan dingin i sin ding hi.

records.english: Whether I cook or we eat out depends on how late I finish work.
records.zomi: Kei in ka huan ding hiam, pua ah i ne ding hiam cih pen ka nasep bangzah nunung-in ka zo hiam tungah a kinga hi.

records.english: Tonight, I'm making noodles with the leftover chicken.
records.zomi: Tu zanin a om lai ak sa tawh khauhsawk ka bawl hi.

records.english: Once the new stove is installed, I'll finally be able to cook two dishes at once.
records.zomi: Meikhuk thak a kikoih khit ciangin a tawp-in khatvei-in an nih ka huan thei ding hi.

records.english: Hello, I'm calling to order a large tray of rice for Saturday's party.
records.zomi: Lumen, Kiginni pawi adingin buh kuang lian khat ngen dingin kong sam hi.

records.english: Who's going to cook on Christmas Day this year?
records.zomi: Hih kum Christmas ni-in kua in an a huan ding hiam?

records.english: The vegetables will be chopped the night before, so the morning won't be such a rush.
records.zomi: Zingsang a buai lua lohna dingin anteh te a zan ma-in kiat ding hi.

records.english: Were I to open a café, I'd serve only the dishes my mother taught me.
records.zomi: An zuakna inn ka hon leh ka nu' hong sin sak an te bek ka zuak ding hi.

records.english: I'll make the salad if you start the rice.
records.zomi: Buh na kipat leh kei in salad ka bawl ding hi.

records.english: Can I help you with the cooking tonight?
records.zomi: Tu zanin an huan dingin kong huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, please grate the cheese and lay the table.
records.zomi: Huh in, cheese ngawi inla, dawhkan kiman sak in.

records.english: My husband isn't used to cooking for so many people, so I'll help him on the day.
records.zomi: Ka pasal in mi tampi adingin an huan a ngeina hi lo ahih manin tua ni-in ka huh ding hi.

records.english: In my view, a simple meal eaten slowly together is better than a fancy one eaten in a hurry.
records.zomi: Ka ngaihsutna-in khawm-in dai taka nek an baih pen manlang taka nek an hoih sangin a hoih zaw hi.

records.english: So the pastry goes in the fridge for an hour before I roll it out?
records.zomi: Tua ahih manin ka lum ma-in buh-mal nim vot sak setna sungah nai khat a om ding hi, a hi hiam?

records.english: My biggest hope is that my son will learn to cook before he leaves home.
records.zomi: Ka lamen lian pen ka tapa in inn a nusiat ma-in an huan a sin ding ahi hi.

records.english: Should I warm the plates before we serve?
records.zomi: I piak ma-in kuang te ka lumsak ding hiam?

records.english: However busy the week gets, we'll still cook one proper meal together on Friday.
records.zomi: Kal bangzah in buai zongin Laithai ni-in an hoih khat khawm-in i huan lai ding hi.

records.english: I'll keep the leftovers for tomorrow's lunch.
records.zomi: A om lai te zingciang sun an adingin ka kem ding hi.

records.english: I'd like to learn how to cook fish properly before the summer.
records.zomi: Khal ma-in hoih takin nga huan dan sin ka deih hi.

records.english: I wish I had a bigger kitchen for cooking with the children.
records.zomi: Naupangte tawh an huan nadingin an huanna lian zaw ka nei leh ka deih hi.

records.english: I'm going to have the old oven repaired before the holidays.
records.zomi: Khawlna hun ma-in meikhuk lui ka bawl dam sak ding hi.

records.english: It would save a lot of time if we planned the week's meals on Sunday.
records.zomi: Nipini ni-in kal sung an te i geel leh hun tampi a kem ding hi.

records.english: Our cooking teacher is going to let us design our own menu for the last lesson.
records.zomi: I an huan saya in sinna nunung adingin keimah an gelhna bawl dingin hong phal ding hi.

records.english: Remind me to buy ginger on the way home.
records.zomi: Inn ciahna lampi ah siing lei dingin hong phawksak in.

records.english: Are we having soup again tomorrow?
records.zomi: Zingciang zong an tui i ne kik ding hiam?

records.english: Don't leave the pan alone while the oil is heating.
records.zomi: Sathau a lum laitakin bel nusia kei in.

records.english: My daughter wants to bake bread for the whole family next weekend.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in a zom kal tawp ciangin innkuan bup adingin moh em a deih hi.

records.english: Will the bread be ready in time for lunch?
records.zomi: Moh sun an adingin hun takin a kiman ding hiam?

records.english: Next month, our street is going to hold a cooking evening for the new families.
records.zomi: A zom kha in i lampi in innkuan thakte adingin an huan nitak khat a bawl ding hi.

records.english: Each household will teach the others one simple dish from home.
records.zomi: Inn khat ciat in inn pan an baih khat a dangte a sin sak ding uh hi.

records.english: Would you rather have soup or salad as a starter?

records.english: Next time we go out, could we choose somewhere that does vegetarian dishes?

records.english: What would you like to eat on your birthday?
records.zomi: Na pianni-in bang ne na deih hiam?

records.english: In that situation, I'd usually make one simple dish that most people enjoy and a few extras on the side.
records.zomi: Tua bang ah mi tamzaw in a deih an baih khat leh a pang ah behlap tawmno ka huan tam hi.

records.english: Don't put sugar in the children's drinks, even if they ask for it.
records.zomi: Naupangte in a ngen zongin a dawn ding uh ah sugar koih kei in.

records.english: The benefit of trying new dishes while travelling is that you discover what you really like.
records.zomi: Khualzin lai-in an thak sin a hoihna pen bang na deih taktak hiam na mu hi.

records.english: I'm going to try cooking with less salt, because my father has high blood pressure.
records.zomi: Ka pa' sisan hatna a sang ahih manin cii tawm zaw tawh an huan ka sin ding hi.

records.english: What kind of food do you think the children will like at the new school?
records.zomi: Sang thak ah naupangte in an bang a deih ding uh hiam, na ci hiam?

records.english: My mother has been trying to persuade my father to eat brown rice for years, with very little success.
records.zomi: Ka nu in kum tampi sung ka pa buh san ne dingin a hanciam a, a zo kei hi.

records.english: Changing your diet requires patience, especially when the whole family is used to eating a certain way.
records.zomi: An nek dan khek in thuakzawhna a kisam a, innkuan bup in nek dan khat a ngeina uh ciangin a tuamin.

records.english: Both of my brothers love durian, but neither of my sisters can stand the smell.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal nih in durian a deih uh a, ahi zongin ka sanggam nu nih in a gim a ning uh hi.

records.english: Will your parents eat the food at the wedding, or should we order something plainer for them?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa in mopawi-a an a ne ding uh hiam, amaute adingin an baih zaw i ngen ding hiam?

records.english: My grandmother taught the girl next door how to sew a button.
records.zomi: Ka pi in a kiang inn-a nungak kawmthap khui dan a sin sak hi.

records.english: Years later, the boy we used to help with his homework came back as a doctor to thank us.
records.zomi: Kum tampi khit ciangin a innlai i huh ngei tangval siavuan-in lungdam hong ci dingin a hong kik hi.

records.english: Our neighbor's tree fell across the road, and everyone came out with saws and ropes.
records.zomi: I inn vengpa' singkung lampi tungah a puk a, mi khempeuh vuai leh khau tawh a pusuak uh hi.

records.english: My father lent his car to the neighbor whose wife had gone into labor.
records.zomi: Ka pa in a zi naungek suak dingin a kipat inn vengpa a mawtaw a caih hi.

records.english: We cleared the snow from the old teacher's path before she woke up.
records.zomi: Saya upa numei a thoh ma-in a lampi tung-a vuk i phiat hi.

records.english: Helping a neighbor rarely requires much effort, but it can make an enormous difference to their week.
records.zomi: Inn vengpa huh in hatna tampi a kisam kei a, ahi zongin a kal sung ah kilamdanna lian a bawl thei hi.

records.english: I didn't know my neighbor's name until the day she helped me catch my escaped chickens.
records.zomi: Ka inn vengnu in ka ak tai te man dingin hong huh ni ciang bek a min ka thei hi.

records.english: If my neighbor hadn't noticed the smoke, our kitchen might have burned down while we were out.
records.zomi: Ka inn vengnu in meikhu a mu kei le i om lohna sungin i an huanna a kang kha ding hi.

records.english: When our oven broke the day before my sister's wedding, the woman next door offered to bake the bread in hers.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu' mopawi ma ni-in i meikhuk a sia ciangin a kiang inn-a numei in amah' ah moh em dingin a ciam hi.

records.english: She baked forty loaves in one long night.
records.zomi: Zan sau khat sungin moh sawm li a em hi.

records.english: Nobody on our street has forgotten her kindness.
records.zomi: I lampi ah kuamah in a itna a mangngilh kei uh hi.

records.english: The young couple upstairs offered to drive my grandmother to her appointments.
records.zomi: Tung dawl-a inn kiteng khangno nih in ka pi a kimuhna te ah tawi dingin a ciam uh hi.

records.english: I was asked to keep a spare key for the couple next door.
records.zomi: A kiang inn-a inn kiteng adingin tawh behlap khat kem dingin hong ngen uh hi.

records.english: The boy upstairs carries Mrs. Lian's shopping every Saturday.
records.zomi: Tung dawl-a tangval in Kiginni simin Lian nu' van leite a puak hi.

records.english: My mother waters our neighbor's plants when she goes away.
records.zomi: I inn vengnu a pai ciangin ka nu in a singkung te tui a buak sak hi.

records.english: When we moved in, the family across the road brought us a pot of soup.
records.zomi: I lut ciangin lampi gal lam-a innkuan in an tui beel khat hong tawi uh hi.

records.english: May we pick some of the plums that hang over our side of the wall?
records.zomi: I lam ah a ki-tuam theipi pawl khat i lo thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, please do, and take some for your children too.
records.zomi: Lo un, leh na ta te uh adingin zong la un.

records.english: The more we got to know the family next door, the more we realized how much we had in common.
records.zomi: A kiang inn-a innkuan i theih semsem ciangin bangzah i kibat hiam i thei semsem hi.

records.english: My grandfather believed that a good neighbor is worth more than a distant relative.
records.zomi: Ka pu in inn vengpa hoih pen gamla-a sanggam sangin a manpha zaw hi, ci-in a um hi.

records.english: Why don't we make a card for the new baby next door?
records.zomi: Bang hangin a kiang inn-a naungek thak adingin card khat i bawl kei ding hiam?

records.english: Is anyone looking after the dog while the Thangs are in hospital?
records.zomi: Thang te siavuan inn ah a om sungun ui kua in a kem hiam?

records.english: I am, and my daughter takes him for a walk after school.
records.zomi: Kei, leh ka tanu in sang khit ciangin a pi-in a pai hi.

records.english: Thank you for taking in our parcel yesterday.
records.zomi: Zanni-in i thuamhual na sang sak manin lungdam ing.

records.english: Do you think the new family would like some help with their garden?
records.zomi: Innkuan thak in a huan adingin huhna a deih ding uh hiam, na ci hiam?

records.english: Please don't park in front of Mr. Pau's gate, because his wife uses a wheelchair.
records.zomi: Pu Pau' zi in khe nei tutna a zat ahih manin a kongpi mai ah mawtaw koih kei in.

records.english: Shall we start a group chat for our street, so that people can ask for help quickly?
records.zomi: Mite in manlang takin huhna a ngen theih nadingun i lampi adingin group chat khat i kipat ding hiam?

records.english: Everyone on the street came to say goodbye when the Mangs moved away.
records.zomi: Mang te a kitawn ciangin lampi-a mi khempeuh goodbye ci dingin a hong uh hi.

records.english: The neighbors' cat was found sleeping in our washing basket.
records.zomi: Inn vengte' zawh i puan koihna empeng sungah a ihmu-in kimu hi.

records.english: Shall I ask the neighbors to keep an eye on the house while we're away?
records.zomi: I om lohna sungin inn en sak dingin inn vengte ka ngen ding hiam?

records.english: The man downstairs fixed my bicycle without being asked.
records.zomi: A nuai dawl-a pa in kingen lo-in ka siiksakol a bawl dam hi.

records.english: Please help me move this table into the garden.
records.zomi: Hih dawhkan huan sungah sawn dingin hong huh in.

records.english: Don't worry about the noise, because we know the baby is teething.
records.zomi: Naungek' ha a suak lai hi, cih i theih manin ging thu lungkham kei un.

records.english: Although we had only just met, our neighbor stayed up all night with my sick son so that I could rest.
records.zomi: I kimuh tom bek hangin ka tawlngak theih nadingin i inn vengnu in ka tapa a cina tawh zan bup a khanglawh hi.

records.english: Could you help us carry the new fridge up the stairs?
records.zomi: Vot sak setna thak kahlei tungah puak dingin hong huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: What surprised me most was how quickly the whole street organized meals for the new mother at number 5.
records.zomi: Ka lamdang sak pen nambat 5-a nu thak adingin lampi bup in manlang takin an a geel uh ahi hi.

records.english: Helping each other has made our street feel like one big family.
records.zomi: Kihuh tuah in i lampi innkuan lian khat bangin a kisaksak hi.

records.english: The fence between our gardens was blown down in the storm.
records.zomi: I huan kikal-a huang huihpi in a sukpuk hi.

records.english: The children on our street organized a sale to raise money for a neighbor's operation.
records.zomi: I lampi-a naupangte in inn vengpa khat' zatui bawlna adingin sum khawm nadingin zuakna khat a bawl uh hi.

records.english: We collected money for the family whose house was damaged by the fire.
records.zomi: Mei in a inn a susiat innkuan adingin sum i khawm hi.

records.english: By the time the repair men came, our neighbors had already fixed the broken pipe themselves.
records.zomi: Bawl dampa te a tun ciangin i inn vengte in tui khuam kitan a bawl dam khin uh hi.

records.english: Would you like to share our lawnmower?
records.zomi: I loupi atna setna na hawm nuam hiam?

records.english: It was my neighbor's quiet, practical kindness that helped me through my first lonely year in the city.
records.zomi: Khuapi ah ka kum masa kia pen hong tawi pen ka inn vengnu' daih leh nasep tak itna ahi hi.

records.english: I left a note under the door to say I'd taken in their parcel.
records.zomi: Amaute' thuamhual ka sang sak hi, ci-in kongkhak nuai ah laikhak ka nusia hi.

records.english: Every evening, someone on our street checks on the widow at number 8.
records.zomi: Nitak simin i lampi-a mi khat in nambat 8-a meigong a veh hi.

records.english: Can I borrow your ladder for an hour?
records.zomi: Nai khat sung na kahlei ka caih thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, it's in the shed, so help yourself.
records.zomi: Caih thei hi, van koihna inn sungah a om hi, la bek in.

records.english: Living next to such generous people has taught my children to notice when someone needs help.
records.zomi: Lungsim hoih mite kiang ah om in ka ta te in mi khat huhna a kisap ciangin a theih sin sak hi.

records.english: We rebuilt it together on a sunny Saturday, and his wife made lunch for everyone.
records.zomi: Ni vak Kiginni ni khat ah khawm-in i bawl kik a, a zi in mi khempeuh adingin sun an a bawl hi.

records.english: Our neighbor said, "Just knock if you ever need anything."
records.zomi: I inn vengpa in, “Bangmah na kisam leh kik bek in,” a ci hi.

records.english: In a situation like that, most people on our street would drop everything to help.
records.zomi: Tua bang hun ah i lampi-a mi tamzaw in huh dingin bangkim a nusia ding uh hi.

records.english: When I broke my arm, my neighbors brought us dinner every evening for a week.
records.zomi: Ka ban a kitan ciangin ka inn vengte in kal khat sung nitak simin nitak an hong tawi uh hi.

records.english: Who looked after you when your parents were working?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa a sep laitakun kua in hong kem hiam?

records.english: The lady next door, who gave us bread and jam every afternoon.
records.zomi: A kiang inn-a numei, nitak lam simin moh leh jam hong pia pa.

records.english: Our neighbor's son taught my father how to video-call his brother abroad.
records.zomi: I inn vengpa' tapa in ka pa gamdang-a a u pasal video call sam dan a sin sak hi.

records.english: Last winter, the old man next door slipped on the ice outside his gate.
records.zomi: Khuavot nung in a kiang inn-a pu upa a kongpi pua-a tuikhal tungah a kipalh hi.

records.english: My son heard him calling and ran out with a blanket.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in a kikona a za a, puannak tawh a tai khia hi.

records.english: We stayed with him until the ambulance arrived, and now my son visits him every Sunday.
records.zomi: Damlo mawtaw a tun mateng a kiang ah i om a, tu-in ka tapa in Nipini simin a veh hi.

records.english: Can your daughter babysit for us on Friday evening?
records.zomi: Laithai ni nitak ciangin na tanu in i naupangte a kem thei ding hiam?

records.english: My little sister was allowed to stay with our neighbors while my mother was in hospital.
records.zomi: Ka nu siavuan inn ah a om sungin ka nau nu i inn vengte kiang ah om dingin kiphal hi.

records.english: We used an abacus at primary school to learn how to carry numbers.
records.zomi: Sang neu ah nambat te behlap dan sin nadingin sing kisimna khat i zang hi.

records.english: Don't use a calculator for the first part of the test.
records.zomi: Sitna khen masa ah calculator zang kei in.

records.english: The real challenge in word problems is deciding which calculation the situation requires.
records.zomi: Thu dotna te-a haksatna taktak pen thu in kisimna bang a kisam hiam thukhen ahi hi.

records.english: My son is learning his times tables this term.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in hih hun sungin a pung kisimna a sin hi.

records.english: I do want to get better at mental arithmetic, but I always panic when people are watching.
records.zomi: Lu sung-a kisim siam zaw ka deih taktak a, ahi zongin mite in hong et ciangun ka lau tawntung hi.

records.english: Write the answer as a whole number, not as a decimal.
records.zomi: Dawnna nambat kim tawh gelh in, decimal tawh gelh kei in.

records.english: What is 7 times 8?
records.zomi: 7 vei 8 bangzah hiam?

records.english: It's 56.
records.zomi: 56 ahi hi.

records.english: If the bus leaves every 15 minutes, how many buses leave in an hour?

records.zomi: Li, hun gelhna a zui uh leh.

records.english: I made a mistake in the third line, so the final answer was wrong.
records.zomi: Tang thumna ah ka khial ahih manin dawnna nunung a khial hi.

records.english: Shall we play a quick number game before lunch?
records.zomi: Sun an ma-in nambat kimawlna manlang khat i kimawl ding hiam?

records.english: Class, write the numbers from 1 to 20 in your books.
records.zomi: Naupangte, na laibu uh ah nambat 1 pan 20 dong gelh un.

records.english: Is 100 a square number?

records.english: Yes, because 10 times 10 is 100.
records.zomi: Ahi hi, 10 vei 10 pen 100 ahih manin.

records.english: Rounding prices to the nearest dollar makes it much easier to keep a running total in the supermarket.

records.english: I'd tend to estimate first and calculate afterwards, because it shows me if I've slipped somewhere.

records.english: The students were surprised to learn that multiplying two negative numbers gives a positive answer.
records.zomi: Nambat kiam nih pung in dawnna kibehlap a pia hi, cih a theih ciangun sangnaupangte lamdang a sa uh hi.

records.english: Mental arithmetic is a useful ability, especially when you're shopping on a tight budget.

records.zomi: Hih nambat nih na lu sungah na gawm thei ding hiam?

records.zomi: Gawm ciangin a thupi kei a, ahi zongin na lak ciangin hiam na khen ciangin hiam a thupi hi.

records.english: I wrote out the multiplication table for my nephew so that he could stick it on his wall.
records.zomi: Ka tanau in a bang ah a kilh theih nadingin pung kisimna ka gelh sak hi.

records.english: Everyone, put your pencils down and check your sums with a partner.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh aw, na khedal uh koih unla, na kisim uh na lawm tawh en un.

records.english: When you subtract a larger number from a smaller one, the answer is negative.

records.english: By the end of the year, most of the class could multiply two-digit numbers without help.

records.english: A dozen eggs means 12 eggs, so two dozen is 24.

records.english: My little sister can count to a hundred in two languages.

records.english: Whether you use a calculator or not, it's worth understanding what each step means.

records.english: My daughter used her fingers to count, and her teacher said that was perfectly fine.

records.english: I'll check the figures again so that the report has no mistakes.

records.zomi: Na dawnna te en nadingin calculator zang in.

records.english: How did you work that out so quickly?

records.english: Half of 50 is 25.

records.english: One benefit of learning to calculate by hand is that you notice when a machine gives a strange result.

records.english: The teacher wrote a long division problem on the board and asked us to solve it step by step.

records.zomi: Bank ah ka khak ma-in hih kisimna hong en kik sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: My grandfather, who never finished school, could calculate the price of a whole harvest without writing anything down.
records.zomi: Sang a zo ngei lo ka pu in bangmah gelh lo-in kaihawl bup man a sim thei hi.

records.zomi: I li kikal ah laimal khen dingin hong huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Having checked the sums three times, the treasurer was confident that the accounts were correct.
records.zomi: Kisimna te thum vei a en khit ciangin sum kempa in sum gelhna te a dik hi, cih a kimuang hi.

records.english: My father taught me to estimate the total before I reached the checkout.

records.zomi: Apple 9 na nei lai ding hi.

records.english: I counted the chairs twice, and there are 32.
records.zomi: Tutna te nih vei ka sim a, 32 a om hi.

records.english: We're going to practise adding and subtracting money with real coins.
records.zomi: Dangka sik taktak tawh sum gawm leh lak i sin ding hi.

records.english: Is 21 an even number or an odd number?
records.zomi: 21 pen nambat kibang khen theih ahi hiam, khen theih lo ahi hiam?

records.english: It's odd, because you can't divide it into two equal whole numbers.

records.english: Can I help you fold the dumplings tonight?
records.zomi: Tu zanin dumpling khip dingin kong huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: One benefit of cooking together is that the younger ones absorb the recipes without being taught.
records.zomi: Khawm-in an huan a hoihna khat pen a neu zawte in kisin sak lo-in an huan dan a sin uh ahi hi.

records.english: Would anyone mind if I brought a dish from my wife's family this year?
records.zomi: Hih kum in ka zi' innkuan pan an khat ka tawi leh kuamah a lungkham ding uh hiam?

records.english: Are we having the usual Sunday lunch at Grandma's this week?
records.zomi: Hih kal in Pi' inn ah Nipini sun an ngeina bangin i ne ding hiam?

records.english: I hope so, because I've been looking forward to her chicken all week.
records.zomi: Ka lamen hi, kal bup a ak sa ka ngak ahih manin.

records.english: When my son starts work in the city, he wants to learn his father's fish soup first.
records.zomi: Ka tapa khuapi ah nasep a kipat ciangin a pa' nga an tui a masa-in sin a deih hi.

records.english: They're going to cook it together every Saturday until he gets it right.
records.zomi: A dik mateng Kiginni simin khawm-in a huan ding uh hi.

records.english: After that, he says he'll cook it for his flatmates on their first Friday together.
records.zomi: Tua khit ciangin a inn hawmte adingin a Laithai ni masa pen-in a huan ding hi, a ci hi.

records.english: I don't mind which day we have the meal, as long as everyone can come.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh a hong thei uh leh ni bang ah an i ne zongin ka lungkham kei hi.

records.english: I agree that the meal should stay at Grandma's house, but we should do the cooking for her now.
records.zomi: An nekna Pi' inn ah om lai ding hi, cih ka phal a, ahi zongin tu-in amah adingin kei te in an i huan ding hi.

records.english: By the time everyone has eaten, it'll be dark, so we'll need lights in the garden.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh a nek khit ciangin a mial ding ahih manin huan sungah meivak i kisam ding hi.

records.english: Both my grandmothers make a version of this dish, and neither will admit the other's is better.
records.zomi: Ka pi nih in hih an a bawl uh a, khat zong in a dang' a hoih zaw hi, a ci kei uh hi.

records.english: Organizing a meal for three generations requires more patience than cooking skill.
records.zomi: Khang thum adingin an nekna geel in an huan siamna sangin thuakzawhna tam zaw a kisam hi.

records.english: I'm not so sure, because she loves being in charge of the kitchen.
records.zomi: Ka thei siang kei hi, an huanna kem a deih mahmah ahih manin.

records.english: What time does the meal usually start?
records.zomi: An nekna a tamzaw-in nai bangzah ciangin a kipan hiam?

records.english: Around two, but people arrive whenever they like.
records.zomi: Nai nih bang, ahi zongin mite a deih hun ciangin a tung uh hi.

records.english: Next year, I'd like us to cook less food, because so much of it is thrown away.
records.zomi: A tam lua kipaih ahih manin a zom kum ciangin an tawm zaw i huan ding ka deih hi.

records.english: This year, for the first time, I'm going to cook the New Year meal for the whole family.
records.zomi: Hih kum in a masa pen-in innkuan bup adingin Kum Thak an ka huan ding hi.

records.english: My mother has agreed to stay out of the kitchen, although I suspect she'll come in to taste the soup.
records.zomi: Ka nu in an huanna pan om khia dingin a phal a, ahi zongin an tui lim et dingin a lut kha ding hi, ka ci hi.

records.english: If something goes wrong, I'll simply serve it with confidence and say it's a new version.
records.zomi: Bangmah a khial leh kimuang takin ka pia ding a, a thak ahi hi, ka ci bek ding hi.

records.english: The biggest challenge is finding a date when the relatives who work shifts are all free.
records.zomi: Haksatna lian pen hun kikhen-a sem sanggamte khempeuh a om ngawng ni zon ahi hi.

records.english: Would you like to take some food home?
records.zomi: Inn ah an tawi na deih hiam?

records.english: My sister abroad is going to cook the same dish on the same day, so it'll feel as if she's with us.
records.zomi: Gamdang-a ka sanggam nu in ni kibang mah ah an kibang a huan ding ahih manin i kiang ah a om bangin a kisak ding hi.

records.english: You're coming to the family dinner on Friday, aren't you?
records.zomi: Laithai ni-in innkuan nitak an ah na hong ding hi, a hi hiam?

records.english: Hello, Auntie — I'm calling to ask whether you'd like us to bring anything on Sunday.

records.english: Serve the oldest guests first, and then help yourselves.
records.zomi: Khual upa pente a masa-in pia unla, tua ciangin nangma te' la un.

records.english: Could you show me how much water you add to the rice?
records.zomi: Buh ah tui bangzah na koih hiam hong lak thei ding hiam?

records.english: If the price of pork keeps rising, we'll have to make the dish with chicken instead.
records.zomi: Vok sa man a khang lai leh tua an ak sa tawh i bawl ding a kisam ding hi.

records.english: My children aren't used to eating with their hands, but they'll enjoy trying.
records.zomi: Ka ta te in khut tawh an nek a ngeina hi lo uh a, ahi zongin sin a nopsak ding uh hi.

records.english: My daughter has become a vegetarian, so I'll make a version of the stew without meat.
records.zomi: Ka tanu sa ne lo mi a suak khin ahih manin sa om lo an tui ka bawl ding hi.

records.english: Next month, my brothers and I are going to take it in rotation to host Sunday lunch.
records.zomi: A zom kha in ka sanggam pasalte leh kei in Nipini sun an kibang lo-in i bawl tuah ding hi.

records.english: So will I, if you share the recipe for the vegetable version.
records.zomi: Kei zong, anteh bawl dan na hawm leh.

records.english: That sounds lovely, and I'm sure they'd appreciate it.
records.zomi: Tua a nuam mahmah ding a, a lungdam ding uh hi, ka thei hi.

records.english: I'd love some more, but I really couldn't eat another bite.
records.zomi: Behlap ka deih a, ahi zongin khat zong ka ne zo nawn kei hi.

records.english: Do you think the children will still want to eat these dishes when they're older?
records.zomi: Naupangte a lian ciangun hih an te a ne nuam lai ding uh hiam, na ci hiam?

records.english: My cousin has been offered a job abroad, so this may be her last family meal with us for a while.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu gamdang ah nasep a kipia ahih manin hih pen hun sawt sung i tawh innkuan an nekna nunung ahi kha ding hi.

records.english: In that situation, it's probably better to hold two smaller meals than one that half the family misses.

records.english: Shall we ask the young couple from church to join us for the festival meal?
records.zomi: Pawlpi pan inn kiteng khangno nih pawi an nekna ah hong kihel dingin i ngen ding hiam?

records.english: I'm going to wear my grandmother's old apron while I cook.
records.zomi: An ka huan laitakin ka pi' an huan puan lui ka silh ding hi.

records.english: Is it true that the meal is going to be held outside this year?
records.zomi: Hih kum in an nekna pua ah kibawl ding hi, cih a man hiam?

records.english: Yes, because there isn't enough room in the house for sixty people.
records.zomi: Man hi, inn sungah mi sawm guk adingin mun a kicing kei ahih manin.

records.english: It's worth making a list of who brings what, so that we don't end up with five desserts.
records.zomi: An lim nga i ngah lohna dingin kua in bang a tawi ding hiam gelhna khat bawl a kilawm hi.

records.english: Whether we keep the tradition going will depend on whether my generation is willing to do the work.

records.english: Please don't start eating until Grandpa has said grace.
records.zomi: Pu in thu a nget mateng ne kipan kei un.

records.english: My grandmother has been making this soup for the New Year since before my mother was born.
records.zomi: Ka pi in ka nu a suah ma pan kipan Kum Thak adingin hih an tui a bawl khin hi.

records.english: Who's going to make the sticky rice this year?
records.zomi: Hih kum in kua in buh-pi a bawl ding hiam?

records.zomi: Bawng sa bangzah sawt a min ding hiam?

records.english: At least three hours, so we should start before lunch.
records.zomi: Nai thum bek hi zongin, tua ahih manin sun an ma-in i kipan ding hi.

records.english: Will you sit next to me at dinner?
records.zomi: Nitak an ah ka kiang ah na tu ding hiam?

records.english: Shall I bring my special salad?
records.zomi: Ka salad tuam ka tawi ding hiam?

records.english: Rather than one huge meal, I'd prefer smaller dinners throughout the festival.
records.zomi: An nekna lian khat sangin pawi sungin nitak an neu zawte ka deih zaw hi.

records.english: I wish my father could taste this curry, because it was his favorite.
records.zomi: Ka pa' deih pen ahih manin hih curry a lim et thei leh ka deih hi.

records.english: My aunt is going to have the big pots cleaned and returned to the church after the meal.
records.zomi: Ka ni in an nekna khit ciangin beel lian te a sil sak ding a, pawlpi ah a pia kik ding hi.

records.english: Having moved away years ago, my uncle says these meals are what he misses most about home.

records.english: We could give the leftovers to the shelter instead of letting them go to waste.
records.zomi: A om lai an te kipaih sak sangin kemna inn ah i pia thei hi.

records.english: I'll come early to help with the chopping, if that's all right.
records.zomi: A hoih leh at huh dingin ma-in ka hong ding hi.

records.english: I'm afraid I can't this time, because I'm working late, but save me a plate.
records.zomi: Maisak ing, nunung-in ka sep ding ahih manin tu-in ka hong thei kei hi, ahi zongin kuang khat hong kem sak in.

records.english: The table will be set the night before, so that the morning is calmer.

records.english: I'd tend to keep the main dish exactly the same and experiment only with the side dishes.
records.zomi: An lian a kibang mah-in ka kem ding a, a pang-a an te bek ka sin kha ding hi.

records.english: My little brother is going to say the blessing for the first time.
records.zomi: Ka nau pasal in a masa pen-in thupha ngetna a gen ding hi.

records.english: I'll feel much happier once the exams are over.
records.zomi: Sitna te a bei ciangin ka lungsim a nuam zaw mahmah ding hi.

records.english: My friend has been feeling low since her mother moved into a care home, so we've made a plan for the weekend.

records.english: On Saturday morning, we're going to take her to the pottery class she's always wanted to try.
records.zomi: Kiginni zingsang ciangin a sin nop tawntung leivui bel bawl sinna ah i pi ding hi.

records.english: In the evening, we'll cook her favorite meal and let her choose the film.

records.english: Next spring, I'm going to join a choir, because singing always cheers me up.
records.zomi: A zom spring ciangin la sak in hong kipaksak tawntung ahih manin la pawl khat ah ka kihel ding hi.

records.english: Shall I come round tonight, or would you rather be alone?
records.zomi: Tu zanin kong hong ding hiam, kia-in na om nuam zaw hiam?

records.english: Thanks, but I think I just need a quiet evening.
records.zomi: Lungdam ing, ahi zongin nitak daih khat bek ka kisam hi, ka ci hi.

records.english: Is your grandmother feeling a bit happier now?
records.zomi: Na pi tu-in tawmno a kipak zaw hiam?

records.english: We're planning a small party for my aunt, who's finally coming home from hospital.
records.zomi: A tawp-in siavuan inn pan inn a ciah ding ka ni adingin pawi neu khat i geel hi.

records.english: Don't worry, it'll be fine once you've settled in.
records.zomi: Lungkham kei in, na om khit ciangin a hoih ding hi.

records.english: Congratulations on the new job, and I hope you'll love it there.
records.zomi: Nasep thak adingin kong lungdam pih a, tua ah na nopsak ding ka lamen hi.

records.english: That must be really hard for your family.
records.zomi: Tua pen na innkuan adingin a haksa taktak ding hi.

records.english: Next week I'll plant sunflowers along the fence, because they always make me feel cheerful.
records.zomi: Kipakna hong pia tawntung uh ahih manin a zom kal ciangin huang kiang ah ni pak ka suan ding hi.

records.english: Happiness, in my experience, comes more from the people around you than from the things you own.
records.zomi: Ka theih bangin nopna pen na neih van te sangin na kiim-a mite pan a hong zaw hi.

records.english: Thrilled and exhausted, to be honest.
records.zomi: Ka kipak a, ka ol mahmah hi, thu man takin.

records.english: With luck, I'll hear from the company by Friday, but I'm trying not to think about it.
records.zomi: Vangphat leh Laithai ni ma-in company pan thu ka za ding a, ahi zongin ngaihsut lo dingin ka hanciam hi.

records.english: In that situation, I'd probably let my friend decide whether she wanted company or not.
records.zomi: Tua bang ah lawm om a deih hiam deih lo hiam ka lawm in khen dingin ka phal kha ding hi.

records.english: One benefit of having a big family is that there's always someone to share good news with.
records.zomi: Innkuan lian neih a hoihna khat pen thu hoih hawm nadingin mi khat a om tawntung ahi hi.

records.english: Are you feeling any better today?
records.zomi: Tuni-in na hoih zaw hiam?

records.english: A little, thanks, but I'm still very tired.

records.english: If the operation goes well, my mother will finally be able to enjoy her garden again.
records.zomi: Zatui bawlna a hoih leh ka nu in a tawp-in a huan a nuamsa kik thei ding hi.

records.english: I'd tend to give someone time to talk rather than rushing to cheer them up.
records.zomi: A kipaksak dingin manlang sangin mi khat thu gen nading hun ka pia kha ding hi.

records.english: I'm sorry to hear that your grandfather is unwell.
records.zomi: Na pu a dam lo thu ka zak ciangin ka lungkham hi.

records.english: Both of my sisters cried at the wedding, but neither of them would admit it.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu nih in mopawi ah a kap uh a, ahi zongin khat zong in a pulak kei hi.

records.english: It's worth remembering that sadness usually passes, even when it doesn't feel that way.

records.english: One challenge after losing someone is knowing what to do with the days that used to be theirs.

records.english: Looking forward to small things, like a walk on Sunday, helps me through difficult weeks.
records.zomi: Nipini ni-a pai bang thu neute ngak in kal haksa te hong tawi hi.

records.english: Tell me something that made you smile today.
records.zomi: Tuni-in hong nuisak thu khat hong gen in.

records.english: Can we go to the beach when Dad comes home?
records.zomi: Pa inn a tun ciangin tuipi gei ah i pai thei ding hiam?

records.english: My daughter has been happier since she started helping at the community garden.
records.zomi: Mipi huan ah a huh kipat khit ciangin ka tanu a kipak zaw hi.

records.english: My grandmother isn't used to living alone, so I'm going to call her every evening.
records.zomi: Ka pi in kia-in om a ngeina hi lo ahih manin nitak simin ka sam ding hi.

records.english: The news will be shared with the whole family at Sunday lunch.
records.zomi: Thu thak pen Nipini sun an ah innkuan bup kiangah kihawm ding hi.

records.english: My father has been much more cheerful since he started volunteering at the library.

records.english: By the time the baby arrives, I hope my brother will have found a job closer to home.

records.english: This photo is going in a frame, because everyone looks so happy in it.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh a kipak mahmah bang uh ahih manin hih lim kilh sungah a om ding hi.

records.zomi: Nasep thu bang ciangin na za ding hiam?
