records.zomi: Nasep ka ngah leh mi khempeuh nitak an ka pia ding hi.

records.english: I can't wait to see my parents next month.
records.zomi: A zom kha-in ka nu leh ka pa kimuh ka ngak zo kei hi.

records.english: If you ever feel low, you can always call me, even late at night.
records.zomi: Na lungkham ciangin zan nunung lai zongin hong sam thei tawntung hi.

records.english: Whether the move makes us happier will depend on how quickly we feel at home.
records.zomi: Kitawnna in hong kipaksak zaw ding hiam pen bangzah in manlang takin inn bangin i kisa hiam tungah a kinga ding hi.

records.english: I know how you feel, because I felt exactly the same when my best friend moved to the capital.
records.zomi: Na kisak dan ka thei hi, ka lawm hoih pen gam khuapi ah a kitawn ciangin kibang mah-in ka kisa hi.

records.english: I don't mind where we celebrate, as long as the whole family is there.
records.zomi: Innkuan bup a om leh koi ah i lungdam zongin ka lungkham kei hi.

records.english: You look a bit down today, don't you?
records.zomi: Tuni-in tawmno na lungkham bang hi, a hi hiam?

records.english: My husband made me promise to take a proper holiday this year.

records.english: Because I've just heard that I passed my driving test!

records.english: Who's going to tell Grandma about the engagement?

records.english: I wish I could be there for your graduation.

records.english: Sorry to interrupt, but I just wanted to say how pleased we all are for you.

records.english: One bad interview isn't going to ruin my whole week.

records.english: Do you think the children will be sad when we move to the new town?

records.english: A little at first, but they'll make new friends quickly.

records.english: My son will be so excited when he sees the new puppy.

records.zomi: Thu te a hoih zaw ding hi, na ci taktak hiam?

records.english: Although she smiled all evening, I could see that my aunt was still grieving.

records.english: You must be thrilled about the new baby!

records.english: So you're worried about the cost, not about the operation itself?

records.english: I'm worried that the new job will leave me no time for my family.

records.english: I've been lying awake for weeks, wondering whether I made the right decision about the move.

records.english: My little boy is scared of the dark, so we'll leave the hall light on.

records.english: Whether my son enjoys the camp will depend on whether he makes a friend on the first day.

records.english: Stay close to me on the old bridge, because some of the boards are loose.

records.english: I'd tend to tell children the truth about a problem, in words they can understand, rather than hide it.

records.zomi: Zahtakna kician hiam, lawmhoih ging hiam na zat ding pen mi na theih dan tungah a kinga hi.

records.english: My grandmother's first email to us was written entirely in capital letters.
records.zomi: Ka pi' email masa pen laimal lian khempeuh tawh kigelh hi.

records.english: Write back soon, and send my love to everyone.
records.zomi: Manlang takin hong dawng kik inla, mi khempeuh kiangah ka itna gen sak in.

records.english: An email written in a hurry can easily sound ruder than you intended.
records.zomi: Manlang taka kigelh email in na ngaihsut sangin zahtak lo bang a ging thei hi.

records.english: Write a clear subject line, so that people know what the email is about before they open it.
records.zomi: Mite in a hon ma-un email in bang thu a gen hiam a theih nadingun subject line kician khat gelh in.

records.english: Please send me the photos by email.
records.zomi: Lim te email tawh hong khak in.

records.english: Did you get my email about the meeting?
records.zomi: Kikhopna thu ka email na ngah hiam?

records.english: Yes, and I've already replied.
records.zomi: Ngah ing, leh ka dawng khin hi.

records.english: Dear Ms. Varte, thank you for meeting me yesterday to discuss the internship.
records.zomi: Varte nu, zanni-in nasep sinna thu kikum dingin hong kimuh manin lungdam ing.

records.english: Who sent this email?
records.zomi: Hih email kua in a khak hiam?

records.english: Please reply to this email by Monday.
records.zomi: Pizing ni ma-in hih email hong dawng in.

records.english: Our office agreed not to send emails after seven in the evening, which has made everyone less stressed.
records.zomi: I office in nitak nai sagih khit ciangin email khak lo dingin a kilem uh a, mi khempeuh lungsim a buai tawm zaw hi.

records.english: I'm writing to ask whether the position is still available.
records.zomi: Nasep mun a om lai hiam dong dingin lai ka gelh hi.

records.english: A polite follow-up email a week after an interview shows that you're genuinely interested in the job.
records.zomi: Kidotna khit kal khat-in zahtakna email zomna khat in nasep na deih taktak hi, cih a lak hi.

records.english: My father isn't used to emails, so he still prints every important one.
records.zomi: Ka pa in email zat a ngeina hi lo ahih manin a thupi khempeuh a print lai hi.

records.english: Kind regards, and I look forward to hearing from you.
records.zomi: Zahtakna tawh, leh na dawnna ka ngak hi.

records.english: Your email went into my spam folder, so I only saw it today.
records.zomi: Na email ka spam folder ah a lut ahih manin tuni bek-in ka mu hi.

records.english: Last month, I emailed six companies about summer jobs.
records.zomi: Kha nung in khal nasep thu-ah company guk kiangah email ka khak hi.

records.english: Only two replied, but one invited me for an interview.
records.zomi: Nih bek in hong dawng uh a, ahi zongin khat in kidotna ah hong sam hi.

records.english: I sent a thank-you email the same evening, and they offered me the job a week later.
records.zomi: Tua nitak mah in lungdam email khat ka khak a, kal khat khit ciangin nasep hong pia uh hi.

records.english: Did you put the right address?
records.zomi: Address dik na koih hiam?

records.english: The email was sent to the wrong customer, so the company apologized to both of them.
records.zomi: Email pen lei mi khial kiangah kikhak ahih manin company in a nih kiangah maisak a ngen hi.

records.english: Is it all right to email the teacher directly, or should I go through the school office?
records.zomi: Saya kiangah email tangtak-in ka khak thei ding hiam, sang office tawn ding a kisam hiam?

records.english: You can email her directly, but she usually replies only on weekdays.
records.zomi: Tangtak-in na khak thei hi, ahi zongin a tamzaw-in kal sung ni te-in bek a dawng hi.

records.english: I wish people wouldn't send emails with no subject line.
records.zomi: Mite in subject line om lo email a khak lo uh leh ka deih hi.

records.english: Please find attached the form you asked for.
records.zomi: Na ngetna lai a zom ah om hi.

records.english: I set up an email account for my father so that he could receive his pension statements.
records.zomi: Ka pa in a pension laimal te a ngah theih nadingin email account khat ka bawl sak hi.

records.english: When you're writing to someone for the first time, explain briefly who you are and why you're contacting them.
records.zomi: Mi khat kiangah a masa pen-in na gelh ciangin kua na hi hiam leh bang hangin na sam hiam tom takin gen siang in.

records.english: Never send your bank details in reply to an email you weren't expecting.
records.zomi: Na ngak loh email khat dawngna-in na bank thu khak ngei kei in.

records.english: I've just sent you the link, so let me know if it doesn't arrive.
records.zomi: Link kong khak khin ahih manin a tun kei leh hong hilh in.

records.english: Although email is convenient, some conversations are better held face to face.
records.zomi: Email a baih hangin kikupna pawl khat mai kituah-in a hoih zaw hi.

records.english: Please don't use email for anything urgent, because I don't check it at weekends.
records.zomi: Kal tawp-in ka en kei ahih manin manlang a kisam thu adingin email zang kei in.

records.english: What's your email address?
records.zomi: Na email address bang ahi hiam?

records.english: Why hasn't my email arrived yet?
records.zomi: Bang hangin ka email a tung nai kei hiam?

records.english: Is there a limit on the size of the attachment?
records.zomi: Attachment lian zah ah ciang a om hiam?

records.english: If a visitor seems shy, ask them about something easy to answer, such as their journey.
records.zomi: Khual khat a maizum bang leh a khualzinna bang a dawn baih thu khat dong in.

records.english: Write the wifi password and your phone number on a card in the guest room.
records.zomi: Khual inndei ah laidal khat tungah wifi password leh na phone nambat gelh in.

records.english: Welcoming visitors properly requires a little preparation, but it makes a lasting impression.
records.zomi: Khualte hoih taka muak in kiman sakna tawmno a kisam a, ahi zongin a om tawntung lim hoih a nusia hi.

records.english: The reason we put a jug of water in every room is that the tap water isn't safe to drink here.
records.zomi: Inndei khempeuh ah tui um khat i koih hang pen hih ah tui khuk tui dawn a bit kei ahih manin ahi hi.

records.english: Don't ask visitors too many personal questions on their first evening.
records.zomi: A nitak masa pen-in khualte mimal thu dotna tam lua dong kei in.

records.english: Please sit by the fire while I finish setting the table.
records.zomi: Dawhkan ka kiman sak zawh mateng mei kiang ah tu in.

records.english: The difficulty with large groups of visitors is making sure nobody feels ignored.
records.zomi: Khual pawl lian haksatna pen kuamah a kinusia kisa lo dingin kidawm ahi hi.

records.english: Clear instructions, such as where to park and which door to use, can save visitors a lot of confusion.
records.zomi: Koi ah mawtaw koih ding hiam leh kongkhak bang zang ding hiam bang vaikhakna kician in khualte buaina tampi pan a hotkhia thei hi.

records.english: Here's how our recycling works: paper in the blue bin, bottles in the green one, and food in the small box by the sink.
records.zomi: I zat kikna bangci-in a sem hiam: laidal pen eek bawm dum ah, bel te a eng ah, leh an pen tuisilna kiang-a bawm neu ah.

records.english: Turn left at the end of the hall for the bathroom.
records.zomi: Kisilna inn adingin inn lampi tawp ah veilam ah pial in.

records.english: In my opinion, a warm welcome matters more than an expensive meal.
records.zomi: Ka ngaihsutna-in muakna lum pen an man tam sangin a thupi zaw hi.

records.english: Your room is the second door on the right, next to the bathroom.
records.zomi: Na inndei pen taklam-a kongkhak nihna, kisilna inn kiang ah ahi hi.

records.english: Whether we welcome guests at the gate or at the door depends on the custom of the family we're visiting.
records.zomi: Kongpi ah hiam kongkhak ah hiam khualte i muak ding pen i veh ding innkuan' ngeina tungah a kinga hi.

records.english: When a delivery driver comes to the door, offer them a glass of water if it's very hot.
records.zomi: Van puakpa kongkhak ah a hong ciangin a lum mahmah leh tui haai khat pia in.

records.english: Could you explain to our visitors why the service starts with a song?
records.zomi: Bang hangin kikhopna la tawh a kipan hiam i khualte kiangah na gen siang thei ding hiam?

records.english: What time would you like to have dinner?
records.zomi: Nai bangzah ciangin nitak an ne na deih hiam?

records.english: Our church trains volunteers to welcome newcomers without overwhelming them with questions.
records.zomi: I pawlpi in hong thakte dotna tampi tawh buaisak lo-in a muak nadingun thalawpte a sin sak hi.

records.english: If the guests don't eat meat, tell the cook before Friday, so that she has time to plan.
records.zomi: Khualte in sa a ne kei uh leh an huanpa in geel nading hun a neih nadingin Laithai ni ma-in hilh in.

records.english: If your guest uses a wheelchair, check beforehand whether the bathroom door is wide enough.
records.zomi: Na khual in khe nei tutna a zang leh kisilna inn kongkhak a zai kicin hiam ma-in en in.

records.english: The neighbors are going to lend us a mattress for our guests.
records.zomi: Inn vengte in i khualte adingin lupna phah khat hong caih ding uh hi.

records.english: When we welcomed the refugee family, we focused on practical help before anything else.
records.zomi: Taimang innkuan i muak ciangin a dang khempeuh ma-in huhna taktak i pia hi.

records.english: As a volunteer guide, you'll welcome each group at the door and explain how the tour works.
records.zomi: Thalawp lampi lakpa-in pawl khat ciat kongkhak ah na muak ding a, khualzinna bangci-in a pai hiam na gen siang ding hi.

records.english: Who's going to cook for the visitors on Saturday?
records.zomi: Kiginni ni-in khualte adingin kua in an a huan ding hiam?

records.english: Offer your guests a drink first, and then ask whether they're hungry.
records.zomi: Na khualte a masa-in dawn ding pia inla, tua ciangin a gil a kial uh hiam dong in.

records.english: Is it all right if I show our guests around the garden before dinner?
records.zomi: Nitak an ma-in i khualte huan a kiim ka lak leh a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: Please do, and pick a few tomatoes for them to take home.
records.zomi: Lak in, leh inn ah a tawi nadingun mehtuuk tawmno lo sak in.

records.english: The hot water takes a minute to come through, so let the tap run for a while.
records.zomi: Tui lum a hong tun nadingin minit khat a sawt ahih manin tui khuk tawmno sawt luang sak in.

records.english: Do your visitors need anything special for breakfast?
records.zomi: Na khualte in zingsang an adingin bangmah tuam a kisam uh hiam?

records.english: Just tea, but my aunt can't have sugar.
records.zomi: Tea bek, ahi zongin ka ni in sugar a ne thei kei hi.

records.english: Why do we always offer guests tea before anything else?
records.zomi: Bang hangin khualte a dang khempeuh ma-in tea i pia tawntung hiam?

records.english: Because it gives them a moment to rest after the journey.
records.zomi: Khualzinna khit ciangin tawlngak nading hun tawmno a pia ahih manin.

records.english: Was the traffic bad on the way here?
records.zomi: Hih ah hong pai lampi ah mawtaw a buai mahmah hiam?

records.english: Not too bad, but the bridge was slow.
records.zomi: Buai lua kei hi, ahi zongin lei a nawlkhin hi.

records.english: Would you like to leave your umbrella by the door?
records.zomi: Na kawl lukhu kongkhak kiang ah na nusia nuam hiam?

records.english: Explain the house rules kindly, so that guests don't feel they're being told off.
records.zomi: Khualte in hong kikhum sa lo nadingin inn thukham te nem takin gen siang in.

records.english: My grandmother explained that the best seat in the house always goes to the guest who has travelled furthest.
records.zomi: Inn sung-a tutna hoih pen gamla pen pan a hong khual a kipia tawntung hi, ci-in ka pi in a gen siang hi.

records.english: Come in out of the rain, and let me take that bag.
records.zomi: Guah sung pan lut inla, tua ip kong la ning.

records.english: When our relatives arrive from abroad, we're going to explain how the buses work before they try them alone.
records.zomi: Gamdang pan i sanggamte a tun ciangun amau' bek-in a tuan ma-un bus te bangci-in a pai hiam i gen siang ding hi.

records.english: I'm not used to hosting important visitors, so could you tell me what to say?
records.zomi: Khual thupite kem ka ngeina hi lo ahih manin bang ka gen ding hiam hong gen thei ding hiam?

records.english: Just greet them warmly, thank them for coming, and show them where to sit.
records.zomi: Lungsim lum takin hopih bek inla, a hong manun lungdam ci inla, koi ah a tut ding uh hiam lak in.

records.english: Before the inspectors arrive, make sure every desk is clear and the fire exits are not blocked.
records.zomi: Enkaktute a tun ma-un dawhkan khempeuh siang takin om inla, mei kangna-a pusuakna lampi te kikhak lo ding hi, cih kician sak in.

records.english: If visitors know what to expect, they're much more likely to enjoy their stay.
records.zomi: Khualte in bang ngak ding hiam a theih uh leh a om sungun a nopsak zaw ding uh hi.

records.english: How should we welcome the exchange teachers at the airport?
records.zomi: Vanlengtual ah kilaih saya te bangci-in i muak ding hiam?

records.english: Hold up a sign with their names, and have some snacks ready, because they'll be tired.
records.zomi: A min uh kigelh lai dawh inla, a ol ding uh ahih manin an neu tawmno kiman sak in.

records.english: So, to check, the visitors arrive at ten and the tour starts at half past?
records.zomi: Tua ahih manin, kician sak nadingin, khualte nai sawm ciangin a tung ding uh a, khualzinna nai sawm leh a kim ciangin a kipan ding hi, a hi hiam?

records.english: That's right, so we have time for tea and introductions first.
records.zomi: Man hi, tua ahih manin a masa-in tea leh kitheisakna adingin hun i nei hi.

records.english: Let the visitors sit in the shade, because they've walked a long way in the sun.
records.zomi: Ni sungah gamla mahmah a pai uh ahih manin khualte mun hiau ah tusak in.

records.english: When a new colleague arrives on Monday, meet her at reception rather than letting her find her own way.
records.zomi: Pizing ni-in nasem pawl thak a tun ciangin amah mah in lampi a zon sangin mai lam ngakna ah dawn in.

records.english: Show her where the kitchen and the toilets are before you show her the computer system.
records.zomi: Computer system na lak ma-in an huanna leh ek inn koi ah a om hiam lak in.

records.english: At lunchtime, introduce her to the people she'll work with most, so that she isn't eating alone.
records.zomi: Sun an hun ciangin amah bek in a nek lohna dingin a sem khawm ding pen te kiangah kitheisak in.

records.english: Although the visitors arrived two hours late, the whole village was still waiting to greet them.
records.zomi: Khualte nai nih a nun hangin khua bup in hopih dingin a ngak lai uh hi.

records.english: Where would you like to sit?
records.zomi: Koi ah tu na deih hiam?

records.english: Both of our guests are vegetarian, but neither of them minds if we cook meat for ourselves.
records.zomi: I khual nih in sa a ne kei uh a, ahi zongin keimah adingin sa i huan leh khat zong in a lungkham kei hi.

records.english: Would you like a towel for the shower?
records.zomi: Kisilna adingin thuah puan na deih hiam?

records.english: Explain to the visitors that the shop closes at noon on Saturdays.
records.zomi: Kiginni te-in zuakna inn sun tak ciangin kikhak hi, ci-in khualte kiangah gen siang in.

records.english: We've cleared a space in the cupboard for your clothes.
records.zomi: Na puan adingin van koihna sungah mun khat i siang sak hi.

records.english: When visitors come to the farm, explain the safety rules before they go near the animals.
records.zomi: Khualte lo inn ah a hong ciangun ganhing kiang a nai ma-un bitna thukham te gen siang in.

records.english: Kids, show our guests where to hang their coats.
records.zomi: Naupangte, i khualte in a puan lum uh koi ah a khai ding uh hiam lak un.

records.english: One way to make foreign visitors feel at ease is to explain local customs before they make a mistake.
records.zomi: Gamdang khualte nuam takin a kisak nadingun lampi khat pen a khial ma-un mun ngeinate gen siang ahi hi.

records.english: I'll text you the code for the gate before you set off.
records.zomi: Na pai ma-in kongpi code kong text ding hi.

records.english: Who's packing the sandwiches for the journey?
records.zomi: Khualzinna adingin kua in moh a tuam ding hiam?

records.english: How do I end a phone call politely when someone keeps talking?
records.zomi: Mi khat in a gen tawntung ciangin phone sam zahtak takin bangci-in ka khak ding hiam?

records.english: Say that you've enjoyed talking, and then explain that you have to go and make dinner.
records.zomi: Na kikup nuam hi, ci inla, tua ciangin nitak an huan dingin na pai ding hi, ci-in gen siang in.

records.english: Our team is going to plant a tree outside the office as a goodbye present for our manager.
records.zomi: I pawl in i makaipa adingin goodbye letsong-in office pua ah singkung khat a suan ding hi.

records.english: My aunt always packs food for anyone who leaves her house, however short the journey.
records.zomi: Ka ni in a inn a nusia peuhpeuh adingin, khualzinna bangzah in tom zongin an a tuam sak tawntung hi.

records.english: Although she'd only worked there a year, her colleagues gave her the warmest send-off I'd ever seen.
records.zomi: Kum khat bek a sem hangin a nasem pawlte in ka muh ngei kikhenna lum pen a pia uh hi.

records.english: Is everything packed?
records.zomi: Bangkim kituam khin hiam?

records.english: Almost, but I can't find my charger.
records.zomi: Dek hi, ahi zongin ka charger ka mu kei hi.

records.english: I wish I'd said a proper goodbye to my teacher before she retired.
records.zomi: Ka saya a khawl ma-in hoih takin goodbye ka ci leh ka deih hi.

records.english: When children move to a new school, a proper goodbye helps them close one chapter before starting the next.
records.zomi: Naupangte sang thak ah a tawn ciangun hoih taka goodbye cih in a zom a kipat ma-un khen khat a khaksak hi.

records.english: My grandmother explained that you should never sweep the floor straight after a guest leaves, because it looks as if you're glad they've gone.
records.zomi: Khual a pai pah ciangin inn phah phiat ngei kei in, a pai uh ahih manin na kipak bang a kilak ding hi, ci-in ka pi in a gen siang hi.

records.english: Leaving a job on good terms matters, because the same people may be asked for a reference later.
records.zomi: Nasep khat hoih takin nusia a thupi hi, mi kibang te a nung ciangin hong hilhcian dingin kingen kha ding uh ahih manin.

records.english: Before you leave a job, finish your handover notes so that your replacement knows where everything is.
records.zomi: Nasep khat na nusiat ma-in na mun a la ding mi in bangkim koi ah a om hiam a theih nadingin na apna lai zo sak in.

records.english: On your last day, send a short goodbye email thanking your colleagues and giving them a personal address.
records.zomi: Na ni nunung pen-in na nasem pawlte lungdam ci-in leh na mimal address pia-in goodbye email tom khat khak in.

records.english: Then return your keys and badge, and leave your desk the way you'd like to find it.
records.zomi: Tua ciangin na tawh leh na ciamtehna pia kik inla, na muh nop bangin na dawhkan nusia in.

records.english: The volunteers are going to write short notes to the children before the summer program ends.
records.zomi: Khal sinna a bei ma-in thalawpte in naupangte kiangah laikhak tom a gelh ding uh hi.

records.english: Why do you always switch the porch light on when guests leave?
records.zomi: Bang hangin khualte a pai ciangun kongkhak ma-a meivak na hal tawntung hiam?

records.english: My father did it, and he said it helps them see the steps in the dark.
records.zomi: Ka pa in a bawl a, mial sungah kahlei a muh nadingun a huh hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Is it rude to leave a wedding before the dancing starts?
records.zomi: Lam a kipat ma-in mopawi nusia pen zahtak lohna ahi hiam?

records.english: Not if you explain to the couple that you have a long drive home.
records.zomi: Inn ciahna mawng sau na nei hi, ci-in kiteng nih kiangah na gen siang leh hi lo hi.

records.english: Both of my brothers hate long goodbyes, but neither of them will admit it.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal nih in goodbye sau a huat uh a, ahi zongin khat zong in a pulak kei hi.

records.english: When are you coming back?
records.zomi: Bang ciangin na ciah kik ding hiam?

records.english: If you have to leave a conversation suddenly, a brief apology and a reason are enough.
records.zomi: Kikupna khat thawlawh takin na nusiat ding a kisam leh maisak ngenna tom leh hang khat a kicing hi.

records.english: The difficulty with saying goodbye to elderly relatives is never knowing whether it might be the last time.
records.zomi: Sanggam upate kiangah goodbye cih haksatna pen a nunung pen ahi kha ding hiam theih ngei loh ahi hi.

records.english: What time do you have to leave?
records.zomi: Nai bangzah ciangin na pai ding a kisam hiam?

records.english: When my uncle emigrated, the whole family explained to the younger children why he was leaving and when he might visit.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu gamdang ah a kitawn ciangin innkuan bup in naupang neu zawte kiangah bang hangin a pai hiam leh bang ciangin a veh kha ding hiam a gen siang uh hi.

records.english: Before you leave the hospital, the nurse will explain your medicines and give you a letter for your doctor.
records.zomi: Siavuan inn na nusiat ma-in nurse in na zatui te a gen siang ding a, na siavuan adingin laikhak khat hong pia ding hi.

records.english: Here's what to do at the end of the volunteer project: return the tools, sign the logbook, and collect your certificate.
records.zomi: Thalawp nasep tawp ah bang bawl ding hiam: nasepna van te pia kik inla, gelhna laibu ah na min gelh inla, na lai-ciam la in.

records.english: The patients are discharged in the morning, so families should come before eleven to collect them.
records.zomi: Damlote zingsang ciangin kikhah ding ahih manin innkuante in la dingin nai sawm leh khat ma-in hong pai ding uh hi.

records.english: So, just to check, we're leaving straight after lunch, not in the evening?
records.zomi: Tua ahih manin, kician sak nadingin, sun an khit pah-in i pai ding a, nitak ciangin hi lo hi, a hi hiam?

records.english: That's right, because I want to be home before it gets dark.
records.zomi: Man hi, a mial ma-in inn ah om ka deih ahih manin.

records.english: Shall we wait with you until the taxi comes?
records.zomi: Taxi a tun mateng na kiang ah i ngak ding hiam?

records.english: Hello, I'm calling to say goodbye before I fly tomorrow, and to thank you for everything.
records.zomi: Lumen, zingciang ka leng ma-in goodbye ci dingin leh bangkim adingin lungdam ci dingin kong sam hi.

records.english: In my opinion, the way you leave a place says as much about you as the way you arrive.
records.zomi: Ka ngaihsutna-in mun khat na nusiat dan in na tun dan zah mah-in nangma thu a gen hi.

records.english: If you're leaving the flat, give the landlord a month's notice and agree on a date to return the keys.
records.zomi: Inn na nusiat ding leh inn neipa kiangah kha khat ma-in hilh inla, tawh te pia kik nading ni kilem un.

records.english: Call us when you've landed, even if it's the middle of the night.
records.zomi: Zan laitak zongin na tun ciangin hong sam un.

records.english: If you're the last guest to leave, offer to help with the washing-up.
records.zomi: Nangma khual nunung pen-in na pai leh kuang sil huh dingin ciam in.

records.english: See you next week!
records.zomi: A zom kal ciangin i kimu ding hi!

records.english: I must be going, because my bus leaves in ten minutes.
records.zomi: Ka bus minit sawm sungin a pai ding ahih manin ka pai ding a kisam hi.

records.english: Whether you hug, shake hands, or simply wave depends on the person and the place.
records.zomi: Na kawi ding hiam, khut na kilen ding hiam, khut na vai bek ding hiam pen mi leh mun tungah a kinga hi.

records.english: We'll miss you, so don't stay away too long.
records.zomi: Kong lungngai ding uh ahih manin sawt lua-in om kei in.

records.english: At the end of a video meeting, thank everyone before you leave the call.
records.zomi: Video kikhopna tawp ah na pusuak ma-in mi khempeuh lungdam ci in.

records.english: Don't forget your umbrella, and send my love to your parents.
records.zomi: Na kawl lukhu mangngilh kei inla, na nu leh na pa kiangah ka itna gen sak in.

records.english: Explain to your son that his friend is moving, but that they can still talk on video calls.
records.zomi: Na tapa kiangah a lawm a kitawn ding a, ahi zongin video call tawh a kikum thei lai ding uh hi, ci-in gen siang in.

records.english: Please don't wait at the window until we've gone, because it's cold.
records.zomi: A vot ahih manin i pai mateng tukvuang ah ngak kei in.

records.english: Do you need anything for the journey?
records.zomi: Khualzinna adingin bangmah na kisam hiam?

records.english: Ending a visit politely is a skill, especially when the host keeps offering more food.
records.zomi: Veh khat zahtak taka khak pen siamna khat ahi a, a mak in an behlap a pia den ciangin a tuamin.

records.english: I'm not used to saying goodbye to colleagues, because I stayed in my last job for fifteen years.
records.zomi: Ka nasep nunung ah kum sawm leh nga ka om ahih manin nasem pawlte kiangah goodbye cih ka ngeina hi lo hi.

records.english: Write to us when you're settled.
records.zomi: Na om nuam khit ciangin hong gelh un.

records.english: A short, sincere goodbye email is usually better than a long one full of in-jokes.
records.zomi: Goodbye email tom leh lungsim takpi in kipawl sung nuihza thu tawh a dim sau sangin a hoih zaw tam hi.

records.english: Can I give you a lift to the station?
records.zomi: Meileng dinna dong kong tawi thei ding hiam?

records.english: Thanks, but my brother is picking me up.
records.zomi: Lungdam ing, ahi zongin ka sanggam pasal in hong la ding hi.

records.english: It was really nice talking to you, and I hope we meet again soon.
records.zomi: Na tawh kikup a nuam mahmah a, manlang takin i kimu kik ding ka lamen hi.

records.english: Take photos of each room on the day you move out, in case there's a question about the deposit.
records.zomi: A ma-a piak sum thu dotna a om leh cih adingin na pusuah ni-in inndei khempeuh lim la in.

records.english: Well, I'd better let you go, but it was lovely to hear from you.
records.zomi: Tu-in kong pai sak ding hi, ahi zongin na thu zak a nuam mahmah hi.

records.english: Wave goodbye to your aunt from the window.
records.zomi: Tukvuang pan na ni kiangah goodbye ci-in khut vai in.

records.english: If a friend is moving abroad, help them make a list of the people they want to see before they go.
records.zomi: Lawm khat gamdang ah a kitawn ding leh a pai ma-in a muh nop mite gelhna bawl dingin huh in.

records.english: Say thank you to your grandmother before you leave.
records.zomi: Na pai ma-in na pi kiangah lungdam ci in.

records.english: Thanks for coming, and drive carefully.
records.zomi: Na hong manin lungdam ing, kidawm takin mawng in.

records.english: When you say goodbye to the host family, give them a small present from your home country.
records.zomi: Na omna innkuan kiangah goodbye na cih ciangin na gam pan letsong neu khat pia in.

records.english: When parents separate, it helps children if both of them explain the new arrangements together.
records.zomi: Nu leh pa a kikhen ciangin a nih in khawm-in geelna thak a gen siang uh leh naupangte a huh hi.

records.english: Although my brother and I argue constantly, I know he would do anything for me.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal leh kei i kinial tawntung hangin kei adingin bangkim a bawl ding hi, ka thei hi.

records.english: Could you show me how to add photos to the online family tree?
records.zomi: Online innkuan singkung ah lim behlap dan hong lak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Click on a name, choose "add photo", and pick one from your computer.
records.zomi: Min khat nen inla, “add photo” teel inla, na computer pan khat teel in.

records.english: Relationships between brothers and sisters often change once they leave home.
records.zomi: Inn a nusiat khit uh ciangin sanggam pasal leh nute kizopna a kikhek tam hi.

records.english: Here's how our weekends work: we stay with Mum on Saturdays and with Dad on Sundays.
records.zomi: I kal tawp bangci-in a pai hiam: Kiginni te-in Nu kiang ah i om a, Nipini te-in Pa kiang ah i om hi.

records.english: Who in your family is best at fixing things?
records.zomi: Na innkuan ah kua in bawl dam a siam pen hiam?

records.english: My uncle, because he can repair anything with a piece of wire.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu, dal khau khat tawh bangkim a bawl dam thei ahih manin.

records.english: Who's going to sit with Grandma at the wedding?
records.zomi: Mopawi ah kua in Pi kiang ah a tu ding hiam?

records.english: We're going to record Grandpa explaining how the family came to live in this town.
records.zomi: Innkuan in hih khuapi ah bangci-in a hong om hiam Pu' gen siang i la ding hi.

records.english: My stepfather has two sons, so I suddenly have two brothers who are almost my age.
records.zomi: Ka pakik in tapa nih a nei ahih manin thawlawh takin ka kum dek sanggam pasal nih ka nei hi.

records.english: I'm not used to noisy family meals, because there were only three of us at home.
records.zomi: Inn ah i thum bek i om ahih manin innkuan an nekna ging buai ka ngeina hi lo hi.

records.english: Who looks after your baby when you're at work?
records.zomi: Nasepna ah na om ciangin kua in na naungek a kem hiam?

records.english: His grandfather does, until he starts nursery in the spring.
records.zomi: A pu in a kem a, spring ciangin naupang kemna inn a kah kipan mateng.

records.english: My grandfather's patience with small children is something I've always tried to copy.
records.zomi: Ka pu' naupang neute tungah a thuakzawhna pen ka zui dingin ka hanciam tawntung khat ahi hi.

records.english: Where does your eldest daughter live now?
records.zomi: Tu-in na tanu upa pen koi ah a om hiam?

records.english: We have lunch with my brother's family every second Sunday.
records.zomi: Nipini nih simin ka sanggam pasal' innkuan tawh sun an i ne hi.

records.english: Is it all right if my cousin stays with us for a few nights while she has her hospital tests?
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu in siavuan inn sitna a neih sungin zan tawmno i kiang ah a om leh a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, as long as she doesn't mind sharing a room.
records.zomi: Hoih hi, inndei hawm a lungkham kei leh.

records.english: Why does Grandpa live with us now?
records.zomi: Bang hangin tu-in Pu i kiang ah a om hiam?

records.english: Because he can't manage the stairs in his old house, and we want to look after him.
records.zomi: A inn lui-a kahlei a kai zo kei a, i kem nuam ahih manin.

records.english: Write Grandma's phone number on the fridge for the babysitter.
records.zomi: Naupang kempa adingin vot sak setna tungah Pi' phone nambat gelh in.

records.english: Remember that your aunt doesn't eat meat when you cook for her.
records.zomi: Na ni adingin an na huan ciangin sa a ne kei hi, cih phawk in.

records.english: My grandparents are going to renew their wedding vows next summer.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh ka pi in a zom khal ciangin a kiteenna kiciamna a thak sak kik ding uh hi.

records.english: Who is Uncle Thang exactly?
records.zomi: Pa neu Thang pen taktak in kua hiam?

records.english: He's my mother's younger brother, so he's your great-uncle.
records.zomi: Ka nu' nau pasal ahih manin na pu neu ahi hi.

records.english: Please call your grandmother this evening, because it's her birthday.
records.zomi: A pianni ahih manin tu nitakin na pi phone tawh sam in.

records.english: Whether the grandparents move in with us depends on how much care they'll need next year.
records.zomi: Pu leh pi te i kiang ah a om ding uh hiam pen a zom kum ciangin bangzah kemna a kisam uh hiam tungah a kinga hi.

records.english: The family tree my son made for school showed us relatives we had completely forgotten.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in sang adingin a bawl innkuan singkung in i mangngilh kim sanggamte hong lak hi.

records.english: I'll help my sister move into her new flat.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu a inn thak ah a lut nadingin ka huh ding hi.

records.english: Why does your little sister always sit on your lap?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na nau nu na khuk tungah a tu tawntung hiam?

records.english: My grandmother taught me to sew, and now I'm teaching my daughter.
records.zomi: Ka pi in puan khui hong sin sak a, tu-in ka tanu ka sin sak hi.

records.english: Explaining a large family to a newcomer can be a challenge, especially when three people share the same name.
records.zomi: Hong thak mi khat kiangah innkuan lian gen siang pen haksatna ahi thei a, mi thum in min kibang a neih uh ciangin a tuamin.

records.english: For the school project, start your family tree with yourself at the bottom of the page.
records.zomi: Sang nasep adingin na innkuan singkung phek nuai pen ah nangma tawh kipan in.

records.english: Then add your parents above you, and your grandparents above them.
records.zomi: Tua ciangin na tung ah na nu leh na pa behlap inla, amaute' tung ah na pu leh na pi.

records.english: If you're not sure of a date, ask your grandmother rather than guessing.
records.zomi: Ni khat na thei siang kei leh ngaihsun sangin na pi dong in.

records.english: If my sister and I lived closer, our children would grow up more like brothers and sisters than cousins.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu leh kei kiang zaw-in i om leh i ta te sanggam bang sangin sanggam pasal leh nu bangin a khang ding uh hi.

records.english: Ask your brother to explain the rules of the game to Grandma.
records.zomi: Kimawlna thukham te Pi kiangah gen siang dingin na sanggam pasal ngen in.

records.english: Explain to your little sister that the new baby won't take her place.
records.zomi: Naungek thak in a mun a la lo ding hi, ci-in na nau nu kiangah gen siang in.

records.english: Tell me about your grandparents.
records.zomi: Na pu leh na pi thu hong gen in.

records.english: I wish I had known my grandfather, because everyone says I'm just like him.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh in amah ka bang hi, a ci uh ahih manin ka pu ka thei leh ka deih hi.

records.english: My father used to work away for months, so my uncle was like a second father to us.
records.zomi: Ka pa kha tampi gamla-ah a sem ngei ahih manin ka pa neu pen kei te adingin pa nihna bang ahi hi.

records.english: Show me a photo of your nephew.
records.zomi: Na tanau lim hong lak in.

records.english: My two older sisters are twins, but they don't look alike at all.
records.zomi: Ka u nu upa nih apeng ahi uh a, ahi zongin a kibang kei mahmah uh hi.

records.english: Please be kind to your little cousin.
records.zomi: Na sanggam neu tungah lungsim hoih in.

records.english: When my parents travel, my aunt comes to stay and makes sure we do our homework.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa a khualzin ciangun ka ni hong om a, i innlai i sem hiam a en hi.

records.english: So, if I've understood, your cousin's mother is your father's sister?
records.zomi: Tua ahih manin, ka theih dik leh, na sanggam' nu pen na pa' sanggam nu ahi hi, a hi hiam?

records.english: Exactly, and that's why we spend every holiday together.
records.zomi: Man hi, tua ahih manin nopsakna hun khempeuh khawm-in i zang hi.

records.english: Ever since my aunt came to live with us, my mother has had someone to share the housework with.
records.zomi: Ka ni i kiang ah a om pan kipan ka nu in inn nasep a hawm pih mi khat a nei hi.

records.english: Both of my grandmothers were teachers, but neither of them ever taught me.
records.zomi: Ka pi nih in saya ahi uh a, ahi zongin khat zong in hong sin sak ngei kei hi.

records.english: When you look after your little brother, keep the front door locked and don't let him play on the balcony.
records.zomi: Na nau pasal na kem ciangin ma lam kongkhak khak inla, innkhawng ah kimawl sak kei in.

records.english: If he cries, give him his blanket and read him the book about the train.
records.zomi: A kap leh a puannak pia inla, meileng thu laibu sim sak in.

records.english: Don't tell the children about the surprise visit, because they'll never keep it secret.
records.zomi: Naupangte in a sel thei ngei lo ding uh ahih manin lamdang veh thu gen kei in.

records.english: Can my brother come with us to the park?
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal huanpi ah i tawh a pai thei ding hiam?

records.english: My brother and I share a room, so we've agreed that the light goes off at ten.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal leh kei in inndei khat i hawm ahih manin nai sawm ciangin meivak mut dingin i kilem hi.

records.english: My aunt is only two years older than me.
records.zomi: Ka ni kei sangin kum nih bek a upa zaw hi.

records.english: By the time my youngest child was born, my eldest was old enough to help look after her.
records.zomi: Ka ta neu pen a suah ciangin ka ta upa pen amah kem huh dingin a lian khin hi.

records.english: Before you meet my family on Sunday, let me explain who everyone is.
records.zomi: Nipini ni-in ka innkuan na kimuh ma-in kua kua ahi hiam kong gen siang ding hi.

records.english: My mother explained that the oldest son in our family traditionally looks after the parents.
records.zomi: I innkuan ah tapa upa pen in a ngeina bangin nu leh pa a kem hi, ci-in ka nu in a gen siang hi.

records.english: In my opinion, the strongest families are the ones where everyone feels listened to.
records.zomi: Ka ngaihsutna-in innkuan hat pen mi khempeuh in kingai bangin a kisak uh innkuan ahi hi.

records.english: In the parable of the talents, servants are judged by how they used what they were given.
records.zomi: Talen gentehna sungah sila te a kipiak te bangci-in a zat uh hiam tawh kikhen uh hi.

records.english: May we borrow the church's tools for the clean-up on Saturday?
records.zomi: Kiginni ni-a sianseh adingin pawlpi' nasepna van te i caih thei ding hiam?

records.english: Why does your church celebrate a harvest festival every autumn?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na pawlpi in khuavot kipat hun simin kaihawl pawi a bawl hiam?

records.english: To thank God for the food we have and to share it with people who have less.
records.zomi: I neih an adingin Pasian lungdam ci nadingin leh a nei tawm zawte tawh hawm nadingin.

records.english: Some Christian writers argue that damaging the environment is a failure to respect the Creator.
records.zomi: Khristian gelhpa pawl khat in leitung susiat pen Piangsakpa zahtak lohna ahi hi, a ci uh hi.

records.english: Our pastor walks to church to set an example.
records.zomi: I pastor in lahna pia nadingin pawlpi ah khe tawh a pai hi.

records.english: For many Christians, stewardship means remembering that nothing we own is truly ours.
records.zomi: Khristian tampi adingin kemna mawhpuakna in i neih bangmah keimah' taktak hi lo hi, cih phawk ahi hi.

records.english: Where does the money from the offering go?
records.zomi: Pia sum koi ah a pai hiam?

records.english: Some of it pays for the building, and the rest helps families in need.
records.zomi: A khen khat in inn man a pia a, a dang in haksatna tuak innkuante a huh hi.

records.english: Many churches give a part of their income to help people in need.
records.zomi: Pawlpi tampi in a ngah sum khen khat haksatna tuak mite huh nadingin a pia uh hi.

records.english: Could our church share its car park with the school on weekdays?
records.zomi: I pawlpi in kal sung ni te-in a mawtaw koihna sang tawh a hawm thei ding hiam?

records.english: Some Christians see caring for the poor as part of their stewardship of the world.
records.zomi: Khristian pawl khat in mizawngte kem pen leitung kemna mawhpuakna khen khat bangin a mu uh hi.

records.english: The old hymn book was rebound instead of being thrown away.
records.zomi: Pawlpi la laibu lui paih sangin kikhui kik hi.

records.english: Turn the tap off properly, please.
records.zomi: Tui khuk hoih takin khak in.

records.english: Do Christians think animals matter to God?
records.zomi: Khristiante in ganhing te Pasian adingin a thupi hi, a ci uh hiam?

records.english: Many Christians point to passages that describe God caring for birds and wild animals.
records.zomi: Khristian tampi in Pasian in vasa leh gam ganhing a kem dan a gen Laisiangtho tang te a lak uh hi.

records.english: Can I use the church garden to grow vegetables for the food bank?
records.zomi: An kemna inn adingin anteh suan nadingin pawlpi huan ka zang thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, as long as you share the harvest with the families who need it.
records.zomi: Zang thei hi, kaihawl pen a kisam innkuante tawh na hawm leh.

records.english: The church council decided to stop using plastic plates at community meals.
records.zomi: Pawlpi upa pawl in mipi an nekna ah plastic kuang zat khawl dingin a thukhen uh hi.

records.english: Theologians have debated whether the command to rule over the earth means control or responsible care.
records.zomi: Pasian thu siamte in leitung uk dingin vaikhakna pen ukna hiam, mawhpuakna nei kemna hiam cih kum tampi a kinial uh hi.

records.english: In Genesis, Adam is placed in the garden to work it and look after it.
records.zomi: Piancilna sungah Adam pen huan sungah a sep nadingin leh a kem nadingin kikoih hi.

records.english: Christian teaching on stewardship asks believers to think about the people who will live on the earth after them.
records.zomi: Kemna mawhpuakna thu Khristian thuhilhna in upmite amau' nung-a leitung tungah a om ding mite thu ngaihsun dingin a ngen hi.

records.english: The church roof was fitted with solar panels last year.
records.zomi: Kum nung in pawlpi innkhum tungah ni vak phek te kikoih hi.

records.english: Our pastor reminded us that looking after our health is also a form of stewardship.
records.zomi: I cidamna kem zong kemna mawhpuakna khen khat ahi hi, ci-in i pastor in hong phawksak hi.

records.english: If every congregation reduced its waste, the combined effect on our town would be considerable.
records.zomi: Pawlpi khempeuh in a eek a kiamsak uh leh i khuapi tungah a gawm lam a lian mahmah ding hi.

records.english: Don't throw plastic bottles in the river, because it's part of God's creation.
records.zomi: Pasian' piangsakna khen khat ahih manin gun sungah plastic bel paih kei in.

records.english: Please turn off the lights when you leave the hall.
records.zomi: Kikhopna inn na nusiat ciangin meivak te mut in.

records.english: The challenge for churches is turning teaching about stewardship into everyday habits.
records.zomi: Pawlpi te adingin haksatna pen kemna mawhpuakna thuhilhna ni sim ngeina ah khek ahi hi.

records.english: Who looks after the church garden?
records.zomi: Pawlpi huan kua in a kem hiam?

records.english: The Bible describes the earth as the Lord's, which shapes how many believers think about ownership.
records.zomi: Laisiangtho in leitung pen Topa neihsa ahi hi, a ci a, tua in upmi tampi' neihna ngaihsutna a lam hi.

records.english: By caring for the river near the church, the young people felt they were putting their faith into practice.
records.zomi: Pawlpi kiang-a gun a kem uh ahih manin khangnote in a upna uh a sep bangin a kisa uh hi.

records.english: Could we fix the leaking roof ourselves and save money for the mission fund?
records.zomi: Sum kem-in mission sum adingin innkhum kua keimah in i bawl dam thei ding hiam?

records.english: What can our family do to waste less?
records.zomi: I innkuan in tawm zaw paih nadingin bang a bawl thei ding hiam?

records.english: We could start by buying only what we need and mending things before we replace them.
records.zomi: I kisap bek lei leh i laih ma-in bawl dam tawh i kipan thei hi.

records.english: My grandmother taught me to give thanks before every meal and to waste nothing.
records.zomi: Ka pi in an nek ma simin lungdam ci dingin leh bangmah paih lo dingin hong sin sak hi.

records.english: The children planted sunflowers along the church fence.
records.zomi: Naupangte in pawlpi huang kiang ah ni pak a suan uh hi.

records.english: Is it possible to be a good steward and still own a car?
records.zomi: Kem hoih mi hih a, mawtaw nei thei hiam?

records.english: Most Christians would say yes, but they might ask how often and how carefully it's used.
records.zomi: Khristian tamzaw in thei hi, a ci ding uh a, ahi zongin bangzah vei leh bangzah in kidawm-in a zang hiam a dong kha ding uh hi.

records.english: Why do you save the seeds from your best tomatoes?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na mehtuuk hoih pen te' khaici na kem hiam?

records.english: My uncle, who farms the same land his grandfather did, describes himself as a tenant rather than an owner.
records.zomi: A pu' lo kibang mah a kuan ka pa neu in amah pen neipa hi lo-in hawlpa bangin a gen hi.

records.english: Christians believe that God has given people the responsibility to care for the earth.
records.zomi: Khristiante in Pasian in mite leitung kem dingin mawhpuakna a pia hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: A farmer in our congregation explained how he rests one field each year, as he believes the Bible encourages.
records.zomi: I pawlpi-a lo nei khat in Laisiangtho in a hanthawn hi, a ci bangin kum simin lo khat a tawlngaksak dan a gen siang hi.

records.english: The children were asked to write down one way they could look after creation at home.
records.zomi: Naupangte in inn ah piangsakna a kem nading lampi khat gelh dingin kingen uh hi.

records.english: Our Sunday school class made bird boxes from old wood for the churchyard.
records.zomi: I Nipini sang pawl in sing lui tawh pawlpi huan adingin vasa bu bawm a bawl uh hi.

records.english: Is it a sin to waste food?
records.zomi: An paih pen mawhna ahi hiam?

records.english: Christians answer that question differently, but many see wasting food as ungrateful.
records.zomi: Khristiante in tua dotna tuamtuam-in a dawng uh a, ahi zongin a tamzaw in an paih pen lungdam lohna bangin a mu uh hi.

records.english: We were asked to bring our own cups to the church picnic instead of using paper ones.
records.zomi: Pawlpi khualzin an nekna ah laidal haaite zat sangin keimah' haaite tawi dingin hong kingen hi.

records.english: The youth group is going to plant trees on the hill behind the church.
records.zomi: Khangno pawl in pawlpi nung-a mual tungah singkung a suan ding uh hi.

records.english: Stewardship also includes how we use our time, according to our minister.
records.zomi: I pastor' gen bangin kemna mawhpuakna in i hun zat dan zong a kihel hi.

records.english: Shall we start a compost heap behind the hall?
records.zomi: Kikhopna inn nung ah eek siat koihna khat i kipat ding hiam?

records.english: Although our church is small, its recycling scheme has encouraged the whole neighborhood to take part.
records.zomi: I pawlpi a neu hangin a zat kikna geelna in inn veng bup a kihel dingin a hanthawn hi.

records.english: Our pastor said, "The earth belongs to God, and we are only looking after it."
records.zomi: I pastor in, “Leitung pen Pasian' ahi a, kei te i kem bek hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: I'm going to give part of my first salary to the church.
records.zomi: Ka khasum masa pen khen khat pawlpi ah ka pia ding hi.

records.english: Not every Christian tradition draws the same practical conclusions from the idea of stewardship.
records.zomi: Khristian ngeina khempeuh in kemna mawhpuakna ngaihsutna pan dawnna kibang a mu kei uh hi.

records.english: Whether believers give a tenth of their income or a different amount, many see generosity as part of their faith.
records.zomi: Upmite in a ngah sum khen sawm khen khat a pia uh hiam, a dang zah a pia uh hiam, a tamzaw in piakna pen a upna uh khen khat bangin a mu uh hi.

records.english: Some Christians fast from meat during certain seasons, partly as an act of self-discipline.
records.zomi: Khristian pawl khat in hun pawl khat sungin sa an a ngawl uh a, a khen khat keimah kithunun nadingin ahi hi.

records.english: In my view, stewardship is less about guilt than about gratitude for what we've been given.
records.zomi: Ka ngaihsutna-in kemna mawhpuakna pen mawhna kisak sangin i ngah te adingin lungdamna ahi zaw hi.

records.english: What does stewardship mean for a Christian?
records.zomi: Khristian khat adingin kemna mawhpuakna in bang a ci nopna hiam?

records.english: It means looking after what God has entrusted to us, including the earth, our time and our money.
records.zomi: Pasian in hong apte, leitung, i hun leh i sum zong kihel-in, kem cihna ahi hi.

records.english: Christians often pray for good weather before the planting season.
records.zomi: Khristiante in suan hun ma-in huihkhua hoih adingin thu a ngen tam uh hi.

records.english: Why do you want your children to learn Zomi when they already speak two other languages?
records.zomi: Na ta te in pau dang nih a thei khin uh hangin bang hangin Zomi pau a sin ding uh na deih hiam?

records.english: Because it's the language their grandparents understand best.
records.zomi: Amau' pu leh pite in a theih hoih pen pau ahih manin.

records.english: Our young people are going to make short videos in our language for younger children.
records.zomi: I khangnote in naupang neu zawte adingin i pau tawh video tom te a bawl ding uh hi.

records.english: May I record your stories for the children's class?
records.zomi: Naupang sinna adingin na tangthu te ka la thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, but come in the morning, when my voice is stronger.
records.zomi: La thei hi, ahi zongin ka aw a hat zawh zingsang ciangin hong pai in.

records.english: When my grandfather speaks, I write down any words I don't know and ask him about them later.
records.zomi: Ka pu a gen ciangin ka theih loh kammal te ka gelh a, a nung ciangin ka dong hi.

records.english: Although my cousins were born abroad, they speak our language better than some of us who grew up at home.
records.zomi: Ka sanggamte gamdang ah a suak uh hangin inn ah a khang i lak-a pawl khat sangin i pau a gen siam zaw uh hi.

records.english: By the end of the year, the children were able to sing three songs and read short stories in Zomi.
records.zomi: Kum tawp ciangin naupangte in Zomi pau tawh la thum a sa thei uh a, tangthu tom te a sim thei uh hi.

records.english: My parents made us speak our language at the dinner table.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in an nekna dawhkan ah i pau gen dingin hong sawl uh hi.

records.english: At the wedding, the speeches were given in our language and then explained for the guests from other communities.
records.zomi: Mopawi ah thugen te i pau tawh kigen a, tua ciangin mipi dang pan khualte adingin kigen siang hi.

records.english: When did you start learning to read Zomi?

records.english: Both of my children can sing in our language, but neither of them can write it yet.
records.zomi: Ka ta nih in i pau tawh la a sa thei uh a, ahi zongin khat zong in a gelh thei nai kei hi.

records.english: I wish I had practised our language more when I was a teenager.

records.english: We sing hymns in our language at church every Sunday.

records.english: Teaching the language through games has made the Saturday class much more popular with the children.

records.english: Let me read you this story in our language.
records.zomi: Hih tangthu i pau tawh kong sim sak ning.

records.english: Our church holds a Zomi language class for children every Saturday morning.
records.zomi: I pawlpi in Kiginni zingsang simin naupangte adingin Zomi pau sinna a nei hi.

records.english: Our language class is free, but families are asked to bring snacks for the children.
records.zomi: I pau sinna a man om lo a, ahi zongin innkuante in naupangte adingin an neu tawi dingin kingen uh hi.

records.english: My aunt volunteers to read stories in Zomi to the children at the community center.

records.english: Is there a dictionary for our language that I can buy?

records.zomi: Mipi inn ah khat a om a, phone tungah app khat zong a om hi.

records.english: The challenge for families abroad is finding time for the language among school, work, and other activities.
records.zomi: Gamdang-a innkuante adingin haksatna pen sang, nasep leh a dang te kikal ah pau adingin hun zon ahi hi.

records.english: Which songs do you sing in the children's choir?
records.zomi: Naupang la pawl ah la bang na sa uh hiam?

records.english: Mostly old hymns, and a few songs the teachers wrote themselves.

records.english: Keeping a language alive requires effort from every generation, not only from teachers.

records.english: My grandmother tells the children stories in our language every evening.

records.english: We put labels in our language on everything in the kitchen.

records.english: My grandmother said, "If you forget the language, you forget where you came from."

records.english: A shared dictionary project gave the young people a reason to talk to the elders every week.

records.english: The children are going to perform a short play in our language at the festival.

records.english: I'm going to use only our language with my son during the summer holidays.
records.zomi: Khal khawlna sungin ka tapa tawh i pau bek ka zang ding hi.

records.english: Children who grow up abroad often understand more of their parents' language than they can speak.
records.zomi: Gamdang-a khang naupangte in a nu leh a pa' pau a gen theih sangin a thei tam zaw tam uh hi.

records.english: My father believes that every family has a part to play in protecting our language.
records.zomi: Ka pa in i pau kem nadingin innkuan khempeuh in a nasep ding a nei uh hi, ci-in a um hi.

records.english: Ask your aunt to help you with your homework for the language class.
records.zomi: Pau sinna adingin na innlai na ni hong huh dingin ngen in.

records.english: My grandfather corrects my grammar gently, without making me feel stupid.
records.zomi: Ka pu in hong mawlsak lo-in ka pau gen dan nem takin a bawl dik sak hi.

records.english: My daughter is writing a letter to her grandmother in Zomi for the first time.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in a masa pen-in a pi kiangah Zomi pau tawh laikhak a gelh hi.

records.english: In my opinion, speaking the language at home matters more than any class.

records.english: Whether the language survives abroad depends largely on whether parents keep using it with their children.

records.english: Many in our community believe that the language carries knowledge that cannot easily be translated.

records.english: The old hymn books were reprinted so that the young people could use them.

records.english: I'm going to practise with my grandfather on the phone every Sunday.

records.english: My son understands our language, but he always answers in the local language.

records.english: Don't laugh when your cousin makes a mistake, because he's trying hard.
records.zomi: Na sanggam in a khial ciangin nuihsan kei in, a hanciam mahmah ahih manin.

records.english: My nephew isn't used to reading our language, so he reads aloud very slowly.

records.english: Can you teach me some words in your language?
records.zomi: Na pau-a kammal pawl khat hong sin sak thei ding hiam?

records.zomi: Sin sak ning, an kammal tawh ka kipan ding hi, a phattuam pen ahih manin.

records.english: Our community has asked the library to keep a shelf of books in our language.
records.zomi: I mipi in laibu inn kiangah i pau laibu te koihna khat kem dingin a ngen hi.

records.zomi: Pau sinna ah ka lawm ka tawi thei ding hiam?

records.english: We speak Zomi at home so that the children don't forget it.

records.english: Would you like to join the language class this term?
records.zomi: Hih hun sungin pau sinna ah kihel na deih hiam?

records.english: If the elders' stories are recorded now, future generations will be able to hear their voices.
records.zomi: Upate' tangthu te tu-in kila leh khang hong pai dingte in a aw uh a za thei ding uh hi.

records.english: The elders were recorded explaining the names of plants and the stories behind them.

records.english: When young people see their language used on websites and in songs, they are more likely to value it.

records.english: Explain to your son why you're angry, instead of just raising your voice.

records.english: Brush your teeth, and then choose one book.
records.zomi: Na ha sil inla, tua ciangin laibu khat teel in.

records.english: Please put the baby's bottle in the fridge.
records.zomi: Naungek' nawi bel vot sak setna sungah koih in.

records.english: Get down to your child's level when you talk to them, so that they feel listened to.

records.english: When couples explain their decisions to children calmly, the children usually cope better with change.

records.english: When we disagree about the children, we talk about it later, never in front of them.

records.english: If your teenager stops talking to you, invite them for short walks rather than long talks.
records.zomi: Na ta khangno in hong kikum khawl leh kikupna sau sangin pai tom ah sam in.

records.english: Lovely morning, isn't it?
records.zomi: Tuni zingsang a nuam mahmah hi, a hi hiam?

records.english: It is, and for once the children weren't late.
records.zomi: Hoih hi, leh tu-in naupangte a nun kei uh hi.

records.english: When your father works nights, he sleeps in the mornings, so play quietly until lunch.

records.english: Our health visitor explained that bringing up children well also means looking after your own health.

records.english: Before the wedding, we had to fill in forms at the town hall and show our birth certificates.

records.english: Could you explain how the school's reading scheme works, so that we can help at home?
records.zomi: Inn ah i huh theih nadingin sang-a lai sim geelna bangci-in a sem hiam na gen siang thei ding hiam?

records.english: The biggest challenge for working parents is finding time that isn't already promised to someone else.
records.zomi: Nasem nu leh pate adingin haksatna lian pen mi dang kiangah kiciam khin lo hun zon ahi hi.

records.english: The parenting class showed us how to talk to toddlers when they have a tantrum.
records.zomi: Nu leh pa sinna in naupang neute a heh lai-in bangci-in kikum ding hiam hong lak hi.

records.english: Don't compare her with her brother, because she'll only feel worse.

records.zomi: Ka pasal in naungek zanin a thoh a ngeina hi lo ahih manin a ol mahmah hi.

records.english: How are the twins getting on at nursery?
records.zomi: Apeng te naupang kemna inn ah bangci-in a om uh hiam?

records.english: Much better, thanks, now that they've made some friends.
records.zomi: A hoih zaw mahmah uh hi, lungdam ing, tu-in lawm pawl khat a nei uh hi.

records.english: We've explained to the children that Grandma is going to live with us for a while.
records.zomi: Pi hun tawmno sung i kiang ah a om ding hi, ci-in naupangte kiangah i gen siang hi.

records.english: Can you collect the children from swimming at five?

records.english: If the baby won't settle, try walking around with her or singing quietly.
records.zomi: Naungek a dai kei leh amah pawm-in pai in, ahih kei leh dai takin la sa in.

records.zomi: Ka zi leh kei in a zom kha in kiteenna kum sawm i lungdam ding hi.

records.english: Before you bath the baby, get the towel, a clean nappy and her clothes ready within reach.

records.english: We're going to teach the children to swim this summer.

records.english: By the time our son starts school, we hope he'll be able to dress himself.

records.english: Because her memory mixes up the years, so try not to be hurt by it.

records.english: When your grandmother tells the same story again, just listen and smile.

records.english: We're going to visit Grandma at the care home on Sunday.

records.english: Here's how the video calls work: tap the green button when the screen lights up, and the grandchildren will appear.
records.zomi: Video call te a sep dan hih ahi hi: screen a vak ciangin a eng button nek inla, tute a kilang ding uh hi.

records.english: Could I swap my Friday shift, so that I can take my mother to her appointment?
records.zomi: Ka nu a kimuhna ah ka paipih theih nadingin ka Laithai ni nasep hun ka laih thei ding hiam?

records.english: Absolutely, as long as your work is covered.
records.zomi: Thei hi, na nasep mi dang in a sep sak leh.

records.english: A respite carer is coming on Tuesdays, so that my mother can have a few hours to herself.
records.zomi: Ka nu in hun tawmno amah adingin a neih theih nadingin Pithai ni simin kemtu khat a hong ding hi.

records.english: Once we started a shared calendar, the whole family could see who was visiting Grandma and when.
records.zomi: Kihawm ni kigelhna khat i kipat khit ciangin innkuan bup in Pi kua in bang ciangin a veh hiam a mu thei uh hi.

records.english: Personally, I think the best care combines practical help with plenty of company.
records.zomi: Keimah adingin kemna hoih pen in huhna taktak leh kiangah omna tampi a khawm hi, ci-in ka ngaihsun hi.

records.english: The carer showed us how to turn Grandpa in bed without hurting his back.

records.english: The hardest part of caring for my father was accepting that I couldn't do everything myself.

records.english: The day centre has made a real difference to my father, who used to sit alone all day.
records.zomi: Sun lam kemna inn in ni bup amah bek-in a tu zel ka pa adingin kikhelna taktak a bawl hi.

records.english: Does your father like the new carer?
records.zomi: Na pa in kemtu thak a deih hiam?

records.english: He does, mostly because she laughs at his jokes.
records.zomi: A deih hi, a tamzaw in a nuihsan thu-ah a nui ahih manin.

records.english: How is your father settling into the care home?
records.zomi: Na pa upa kemna inn ah bangci-in a om kipan hiam?

records.english: Better than we expected, thanks, and he's made friends with the man next door.
records.zomi: I ngaihsut sangin a hoih zaw hi, lungdam ing, leh a kiang-a pasal tawh a kilawm khin hi.

records.english: The children were asked to keep their voices down while their grandmother rested.
records.zomi: A pi a tawl laitakin naupangte aw niam takin gen dingin kingen uh hi.

records.english: Excuse me, I don't want to make a fuss, but my mother's lunch was cold again today.
records.zomi: Hong maisak in, buaina bawl ka deih kei a, ahi zongin tuni zong ka nu' sun an a vot kik hi.

records.english: If you ask me, carers deserve far more recognition than they get.
records.zomi: Kei hong dong leh kemtu te in a ngah sangin pahtawina tam zaw a ngah ding uh hi.

records.english: My brother is going to move in with our mother for a fortnight while she recovers.
records.zomi: I nu a hoih kik sungin kal nih sung ka sanggam pasal in amah tawh a om ding hi.

records.english: I wish I lived closer, so that I could help my parents more often.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa tam zaw-in ka huh theih nadingin a kiang zaw-ah ka om leh ka deih hi.

records.english: I'm teaching my daughter to cook a few simple meals for her grandfather.
records.zomi: Ka tanu a pu adingin an baih tawmno huan ka sin sak hi.

records.english: If Grandpa falls, don't try to lift him on your own.
records.zomi: Pu a kiak leh nangmah bek-in dawm sawm kei in.

records.english: Make him comfortable with a cushion and a blanket, and then phone me or the emergency number.
records.zomi: Lukhung leh puannak tawh a nuam nadingin bawl inla, tua khit ciangin kei hiam haksatna nambat hiam sam in.

records.english: While you wait, keep talking to him calmly, so that he doesn't panic.
records.zomi: Na ngak laitakin a lau lohna dingin dai takin amah tawh kikum den in.

records.english: Thank you for looking after the children so well.
records.zomi: Naupangte hoih taka na kem manin lungdam ing.

records.english: Put the baby's hat on, because it's cold outside.
records.zomi: Pua ah a vot ahih manin naungek' lukhu khu sak in.

records.english: In a heatwave, keep Grandma's curtains closed during the day and open the windows at night.
records.zomi: Lum nasia hun ciangin sun ah Pi' tukvuang puante khak inla, zan ah tukvuangte hong in.

records.english: I'm sorry to hear that, and I'll speak to the kitchen this afternoon.
records.zomi: Tua ka zak ciangin ka lungkham hi, leh tu sun nung ciangin an huanna pawl kiangah ka gen ding hi.

records.english: Is your mother feeling any stronger?
records.zomi: Na nu a hat zaw hiam?

records.english: A little, but she still gets tired quickly.
records.zomi: Tawmno, ahi zongin manlang takin a tawl lai hi.

records.english: Explaining illness honestly to children usually frightens them less than silence does.
records.zomi: Naupangte kiangah natna thuman takin gen siang in dai sangin a lausak tawm zaw zel hi.

records.english: Who's picking the baby up from nursery?
records.zomi: Naungek naupang kemna inn pan kua in a la ding hiam?

records.english: We've put a photo of each of us on Grandpa's phone, so that he can call us with one touch.
records.zomi: Khat vei bek a nek-in hong sam theih nadingin Pu' phone tungah i khat ciat lim i koih hi.

records.english: Neither of my grandparents can drive now, so we take them shopping on Saturdays.

records.english: My mother isn't used to accepting help, so she says she's fine even when she isn't.
records.zomi: Ka nu huhna sang a ngeina hi lo ahih manin a hoih kei hangin hoih ing, a ci hi.

records.english: Could you explain to the children why Grandpa can't play football with them anymore?

records.english: Anyway, I'd better get back, because the carer leaves at five.

records.english: I'll help Grandpa with his crossword after lunch.
records.zomi: Sun an khit ciangin Pu a kammal kimawlna ah ka huh ding hi.

records.english: If the baby won't settle after his feed, try a short walk in the pram.
records.zomi: Naungek nawi a dawn khit ciangin a dai kei leh naungek leeng tawh pai tom sin in.

records.english: Caring for both children and elderly parents at the same time can leave little energy for anything else.
records.zomi: Naupangte leh nu leh pa upate kikhawm-a kem in a dang adingin hatna tawmno bek a nusia thei hi.

records.english: So you'll collect the children on Monday and Wednesday, and I'll do the other days?
records.zomi: Tua ahih leh Pizing ni leh Nilai ni ciangin naupangte na la ding a, ni dangte kei in ka la ding hiam?

records.english: That's right, and I can do Friday too if you're stuck.
records.zomi: Hi hi, leh na buai leh Laithai ni zong ka la thei hi.

records.english: Thanks, that's a big help.
records.zomi: Lungdam ing, tua in hong huh mahmah hi.

records.english: If the baby gets a fever at night, call the out-of-hours number on the fridge.
records.zomi: Zan in naungek a cisa leh khal bawm tung-a nasep hun pua lam nambat sam in.

records.english: Can you sit with Grandma while I go to the chemist?
records.zomi: Zatui dawl ah ka pai sungin Pi kiangah na tu thei ding hiam?

records.english: No problem, and give your mother my love.
records.zomi: Buaina om lo hi, leh na nu kiangah ka itna gen in.

records.english: If the council hadn't offered a day centre place, my aunt would have had to give up her job.
records.zomi: Khuapi vaihawm in sun lam kemna inn-a mun a piak kei leh ka ni in a nasep a nusia ding hi.

records.english: Looking after a parent with memory loss requires patience, humour, and a lot of support from others.
records.zomi: Theihna mangthang nu hiam pa hiam kem in thuakzawhna, nuihzaakna leh mi dang pan huhna tampi a kisam hi.

records.english: Don't leave the baby on the changing table, even for a moment.
records.zomi: Naungek puan laihna dawhkan tungah hun tawmno bek zong nusia kei in.

records.english: Hold your sister's hand on the stairs.
records.zomi: Kahlei tungah na sanggam numei' khut len in.

records.english: Young carers often take on responsibilities that most adults would find difficult.
records.zomi: Kemtu khangnote in upa tamzaw in haksa a sak ding mawhpuaknate a la zel uh hi.

records.english: Does Grandpa need anything from the shop?
records.zomi: Pu in dawl pan bangmah a kisam hiam?

records.english: Just some bread and the newspaper.
records.zomi: Moh tawmno leh thuthak lai bek.

records.english: My son asked whether he could invite three friends for a sleepover, and we said two.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in lawm thum zan lum dingin a sam thei ding hiam a dong a, nih i ci hi.

records.english: I borrowed my brother's bike without asking, and he was furious.
records.zomi: Dong lo-in ka sanggam pasal' siiksakol ka zang a, a heh mahmah hi.

records.english: I asked my neighbor if I could hang washing on her line while mine was broken.
records.zomi: Keimah' khau a sia sungin a puan khaina khau ah puan ka khai thei ding hiam ka inn veng ka dong hi.

records.english: Could I have a quick word with you after the meeting?
records.zomi: Kikhopna khit ciangin nang tawh tom takin ka kikum thei ding hiam?

records.english: Sure, come to my office at four.
records.zomi: Thei hi, nai li ciangin ka office ah hong in.

records.english: Would it be OK if I brought my sister to the barbecue?
records.zomi: Barbecue ah ka sanggam numei ka tawi leh a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: Sure, as long as she doesn't mind dogs.
records.zomi: Hoih hi, ui te a lau kei leh.

records.english: Before you use someone's photo online, always ask them first.
records.zomi: Online-in mi khat' lim na zat ma-in amah dong masa tawntung in.

records.english: May I have another biscuit?
records.zomi: Biscuit khat ka ne beh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Only one more, because dinner's soon.
records.zomi: Khat bek beh in, nitak an a kiang khin ahih manin.

records.english: Don't use my laptop without asking me first.
records.zomi: Hong dong masa lo-in ka laptop zang kei in.

records.english: Can I go out to play?

records.english: Some workplaces expect staff to ask permission for almost everything, while others trust people to decide.

records.zomi: Sui-a kankhia te in sinna adingin kuapeuh dotna a neih ma-un kigelh phalna a ngah ding uh hi.

records.english: If the builders had asked before blocking the lane, the neighbors wouldn't have been so angry.

records.english: The challenge for teenagers is learning when to ask permission and when to make their own decisions.

records.english: Is it all right to bring my dog into the café?

records.english: We were given permission to use the school hall for our dance class on Tuesday evenings.

records.english: If you want to use the community garden, you have to sign up at the library.

records.english: Just to check, do I need to show my identity card, or is the polling card enough?
records.zomi: En kik ning, ka min-lai ka lak ding a kisam hiam, ahih kei leh teelna card in a tawk hiam?

records.english: My son will vote for the first time in the next local election.

records.english: Nobody is allowed to take photos of their ballot paper in our country.

records.english: The candidates are holding a public debate at the library on Thursday evening.

records.english: How old do you have to be to vote here?
records.zomi: Hih ah teel thei dingin kum bangzah na phak ding a kisam hiam?

records.english: The local election decides who runs the schools, the parks and the bin collections in our area.

records.english: Whatever the result, the candidates are expected to accept the count once it has been checked.

records.english: I see your point, but I still think the voting age should stay at eighteen.

records.english: The votes were counted overnight in the town hall.

records.english: On election day, my grandmother put on her best dress and walked to the polling station with me.
