records.zomi: Hashtag bang adingin ahi hiam?

records.english: It groups your post with others on the same topic, so that people searching for it can find it.
records.zomi: Na post thulu kibang nei a dangte tawh a kikhawmsak a, tua zong mite in a mu thei uh hi.

records.english: Who took this beautiful photo?
records.zomi: Hih lim hoih kua in a la hiam?

records.english: Should I post the video now or wait until the weekend?
records.zomi: Video tu-in ka koih ding hiam, kal tawp dong ka ngak ding hiam?

records.english: Wait until Saturday, because most of your followers are busy during the week.
records.zomi: Kiginni dong ngak in, na follower tamzaw kal sungin a buai uh ahih manin.

records.english: Is it better to post one good photo or ten average ones?
records.zomi: Lim hoih khat koih a hoih zaw hiam, laizang lim sawm koih a hoih zaw hiam?

records.english: One good photo, almost always, because people scroll past long albums.
records.zomi: Lim hoih khat, a tamzaw-in, mite in album sau a pelh uh ahih manin.

records.english: How many people have seen my post?
records.zomi: Ka post mi bangzah in a mu khin hiam?

records.english: Tap the post, and it shows the number of views.
records.zomi: Post nek in, tua ciangin view zah a lak hi.

records.english: Write a short caption that tells people what the photo shows.
records.zomi: Lim in bang a lak hiam mite hilh caption tom khat gelh in.

records.english: A post that asks a question usually gets more replies than one that only makes a statement.
records.zomi: Dotna dong post khat in thugen bek post sangin dawnna tam zaw a ngah zel hi.

records.english: Add the date and the place to your post, so that people know when and where the event happened.
records.zomi: Poai bang ciangin koi ah a piang hiam mite in a theih nadingin na post ah ni leh mun behlap in.

records.english: Hold the phone still while you record.
records.zomi: Na lak laitakin phone dai takin len in.

records.english: My post got only three likes, and one of them was from my mum.
records.zomi: Ka post in like thum bek a ngah a, khat pen ka nu' ahi hi.

records.english: Why isn't my video uploading?
records.zomi: Bang hangin ka video upload thei lo hiam?

records.english: Your internet is too slow, so try again on the school Wi-Fi.
records.zomi: Na internet a zawl lua ahih manin sang Wi-Fi tawh sin kik in.

records.english: Live videos feel more personal, but any mistake you make is seen by everyone at the same moment.
records.zomi: Live video te in keimah thu bang-in kisa a, ahi zongin na khialh peuhpeuh mi khempeuh in hun kibang mah-in a mu uh hi.

records.english: When a post includes a link, check that it opens before you share it with hundreds of people.
records.zomi: Post khat in link a neih ciangin mi za tampi tawh na hawm ma-in a kihong hiam en in.

records.english: Images with too much text on them are hard to read on a small phone screen.
records.zomi: Laimal tam lua nei limte phone screen neu tungah sim a haksa hi.

records.english: Many small businesses rely on posts made by the owners themselves in their spare time.
records.zomi: Sumbawl neu tampi in a neite mah in a hun awng uh sungin a koih post te tungah a kinga uh hi.

records.english: My cousin wanted more customers for her small bakery, so she started posting a photo of fresh bread every morning.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam numei in a moh bawlna neu adingin lei tam zaw a deih ahih manin zingsang simin moh thak lim khat a koih kipan hi.

records.english: At first she wrote long captions, but her friends told her that short ones with the price worked better.
records.zomi: A kipat ciangin caption sau a gelh a, ahi zongin a lawmte in man tawh a tom te a sem hoih zaw hi, ci-in a hilh uh hi.

records.english: Within a month, people were messaging her the night before to reserve loaves.
records.zomi: Kha khat sungin mite in moh kilai dingin a zan ma-in message a khak uh hi.

records.english: What makes a post memorable is often a small personal detail rather than a perfect photo.
records.zomi: Post khat a phawk huai sak pen lim kicing sangin keimah thu neu khat ahi zel hi.

records.english: Creators are expected to say clearly when a post has been paid for by a company.
records.zomi: Bawltute in post khat company in a man a pia hi, ci kician takin a gen ding uh kilamen hi.

records.english: My son made a short video of our village festival and added music without words.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in i khua pawi video tom khat a bawl a, kammal om lo la a behlap hi.

records.english: Christians look to the Bible to guide how they live.
records.zomi: Khristiante in bangci-in nungta ding hiam a makaih nadingin Laisiangtho en uh hi.

records.english: Christians in different cultures apply the same passage in different ways, while still accepting its authority.
records.zomi: Ngeina tuamtuam-a Khristiante in khen kibang mah tuamtuam-in a zang uh a, a thuneihna a pom lai uh hi.

records.english: What does the Bible say about forgiving someone who keeps hurting you?
records.zomi: Hong natsak den mi khat maisak thu-ah Laisiangtho in bang a gen hiam?

records.english: Many Christians point to Jesus telling Peter to forgive not seven times but many more.
records.zomi: Khristian tampi in Jesu in Piter kiangah sagih vei hi lo-in tam zaw maisak dingin a gen thu a lak uh hi.

records.english: Read the verse again, slowly.
records.zomi: Tang zawl takin sim kik in.

records.english: Reading difficult passages together with other believers helps protect a person from strange interpretations.
records.zomi: Upmi dangte tawh khen haksa te khawm-in sim in mi khat lamdang taka a theih lohna dingin a kemsak hi.

records.english: Changed lives, more than clever arguments, are what convince many people that the Bible carries authority.
records.zomi: Ngaihsutna siam sangin nuntak kikhelte in mi tampi Laisiangtho in thuneihna a nei hi, ci a um sak hi.

records.english: Christians disagree on many questions, yet they share a deep respect for the Bible as a guide in matters of faith.
records.zomi: Khristiante dotna tampi ah a kilem kei uh a, ahi zongin upna thu-ah lampi lakna bangin Laisiangtho a zahtak mahmah uh hi.

records.english: Many Christians memorize verses to guide them in hard times.
records.zomi: Khristian tampi in hun haksa ah a makaih nadingin Laisiangtho tang te a phawk uh hi.

records.english: The old woman's words carried weight in the village because everyone knew she lived by the Bible she quoted.
records.zomi: A gen Laisiangtho bangin a nungta hi, ci mi khempeuh in a theih uh ahih manin numei upa' kammalte khua ah a gik hi.

records.english: Do you have to believe everything in the Bible to be a Christian?
records.zomi: Khristian hi dingin Laisiangtho sung-a khempeuh na um ding a kisam hiam?

records.english: Christians answer that question differently, so it's best to ask your own pastor what your church teaches.
records.zomi: Khristiante in tua dotna tuamtuam-in a dawng uh ahih manin na pawlpi in bang a hilh hiam na pastor dong leh a hoih pen hi.

records.english: Our pastor checks every sermon against the Bible before he preaches it.
records.zomi: I pastor in thugenna khempeuh a gen ma-in Laisiangtho tawh a en hi.

records.english: My mother's Bible is worn soft from fifty years of daily reading.
records.zomi: Ka nu' Laisiangtho kum sawm nga ni sim simna hangin a nem khin hi.

records.english: Why does the pastor always say, "Let's see what the text says"?
records.zomi: Bang hangin pastor in “Laimal in bang a gen hiam i en ni” a ci tawntung hiam?

records.english: Because he wants the Bible, not his own opinion, to lead the sermon.
records.zomi: Amah' ngaihsutna hi lo-in Laisiangtho in thugenna a makaih nadingin a deih ahih manin.

records.english: Shall we see what the Bible says about it?
records.zomi: Tua thu-ah Laisiangtho in bang a gen hiam i en ding hiam?

records.english: When I have a hard decision to make, I read the Bible and pray before I choose.
records.zomi: Thukhen haksa khat ka neih ciangin ka teel ma-in Laisiangtho ka sim a, thu ka ngen hi.

records.english: When two Christians disagree, they often begin by asking what the Bible actually says.
records.zomi: Khristian nih a kilem kei uh ciangin Laisiangtho in bang a gen taktak hiam dot-in a kipan zel uh hi.

records.english: In some countries, witnesses in court may choose to make their promise with a hand on the Bible.
records.zomi: Gam pawl khat ah thukhenna inn-a teci te in Laisiangtho tungah khut koih-in a kiciamna uh a bawl thei uh hi.

records.english: The council's decision was accepted because it was clearly based on the teaching of the Gospels.
records.zomi: Vaihawm pawl' thukhenna pen Lungdamna Thu laibute' thuhilhna tungah kician takin a kinga ahih manin kipom hi.

records.english: When the wording of a verse is unclear, our pastor compares several translations before he preaches on it.
records.zomi: Tang khat' kammal a kician kei ciangin i pastor in tua tungah a gen ma-in lai letna tuamtuam a teh hi.

records.english: In our family, nobody puts the Bible on the floor, out of respect.
records.zomi: I innkuan ah zahtakna hangin kuamah in Laisiangtho leitung ah a koih kei hi.

records.english: Please don't quote a single verse to win an argument.
records.zomi: Kinialna zo dingin tang khat bek gen kei in.

records.english: Are Christians expected to obey every command in the Old Testament?
records.zomi: Khristiante in Thuciam Lui sung-a thupiak khempeuh a zui ding uh kilamen hiam?

records.english: Many churches teach that some laws were for ancient Israel, while the moral teaching still applies.
records.zomi: Pawlpi tampi in thukham pawl khat tanglai Israel adingin ahi a, hoih leh sia thuhilhna a kizang lai hi, ci-in a hilh uh hi.

records.english: What does "the authority of Scripture" mean?
records.zomi: “Laisiangtho' thuneihna” in bang a ci nopna hiam?

records.english: It means that Christians treat the Bible as God's word, which they should trust and follow.
records.zomi: Khristiante in Laisiangtho pen a muan leh a zuih ding uh Pasian' thu bangin a koih uh hi, ci nopna hi.

records.english: Accepting the Bible's authority does not mean agreeing with every interpretation of it.
records.zomi: Laisiangtho' thuneihna pom in a theih dan khempeuh tawh kithukim ci nopna hi lo hi.

records.english: Our youth group was asked to find what the Bible says about honesty at work.
records.zomi: I khangno pawl kiangah nasepna-a thuman thu-ah Laisiangtho in bang a gen hiam zong dingin kingen hi.

records.english: Please look up the verse before Sunday.
records.zomi: Nipini ma-in tang zong in.

records.english: The Bible was read aloud at the start of the meeting.
records.zomi: Kikhopna kipatna ah Laisiangtho aw-in kisim hi.

records.english: Is the Bible still relevant today?
records.zomi: Laisiangtho tu hun-in a kituak lai hiam?

records.english: Christians believe its message speaks to every generation.
records.zomi: Khristiante in a thu in khang khempeuh kiangah thu a gen hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: Does the Bible tell us how to treat strangers?
records.zomi: Laisiangtho in zin mite bangci-in i kem ding hiam hong hilh hiam?

records.english: Yes, it often tells God's people to welcome strangers and care for them.
records.zomi: Hong hilh hi, Pasian' mite kiangah zin mite muak dingin leh kem dingin a tamvei-in a hilh hi.

records.english: Some Christians feel the Bible's authority most strongly when it challenges their own habits rather than when it confirms them.
records.zomi: Khristian pawl khat in Laisiangtho' thuneihna pen a ngeina uh a kipsak ciangin sangin a langpan ciangin a kisa zaw uh hi.

records.english: My father read us a psalm before every important family decision.
records.zomi: Ka pa in innkuan thukhenna thupi khempeuh ma-in late khat hong sim sak hi.

records.english: Believers sometimes find the Bible's teaching hard to follow, but they still try to live by it.
records.zomi: Upmite in Laisiangtho' thuhilhna zui a haksa sa zel uh a, ahi zongin tua bangin nungta dingin a hanciam lai uh hi.

records.english: Our church's rules for leaders were written to follow the qualities described in Paul's letters.
records.zomi: I pawlpi' makaite adingin thukhamte Paul' laikhak sung-a kigen omzia te zui dingin kigelh hi.

records.english: Children, if a friend tells you something about God, you can check it in the Bible yourselves.
records.zomi: Naupangte, lawm khat in Pasian thu khat hong gen leh Laisiangtho sungah note mah in na en thei uh hi.

records.english: A preacher who claims the Bible's authority has a duty to explain it faithfully rather than to use it for his own ideas.
records.zomi: Laisiangtho' thuneihna a gen thugen pa in amah' ngaihsutna adingin zang sangin citak taka gen siang ding mawhpuakna a nei hi.

records.english: When our church disagreed about how to spend a large gift, the elders called a meeting.
records.zomi: Letsong lian khat bangci-in zang ding hiam thu-ah i pawlpi a kilem kei ciangin upate in kikhopna khat a sam uh hi.

records.english: Each group was asked to explain its view from the Bible, not only from its own preferences.
records.zomi: Pawl khat ciat in amau' deihna bek hi lo-in Laisiangtho pan a ngaihsutna uh gen siang dingin kingen hi.

records.english: By the end of the evening, the members had agreed to use half for the school and half for the poor, as several passages encourage.
records.zomi: Nitak a bei ciangin memberte in khen tampi in a hanthawn bangin a kim sang adingin a kim mi zawngte adingin zang dingin a kithukim uh hi.

records.english: Is that really in the Bible, or is it just a saying?
records.zomi: Tua pen Laisiangtho sungah a om taktak hiam, paunak bek ahi hiam?

records.english: It's a popular saying, but you won't find it in the Bible.
records.zomi: Mi tampi' gen paunak ahi a, ahi zongin Laisiangtho sungah na mu lo ding hi.

records.english: Who decides what a passage means?
records.zomi: Khen khat in bang a ci nopna hiam kua in a thukhen hiam?

records.english: Why do Christians say the Bible has authority?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Khristiante in Laisiangtho in thuneihna a nei hi, a ci uh hiam?

records.english: Because they believe God speaks through it, so its teaching matters more than anyone's opinion.
records.zomi: Pasian in tua tungtawn-in thu a gen hi, ci-in a um uh ahih manin a thuhilhna kuapeuh' ngaihsutna sangin a thupi zaw hi.

records.english: Our church follows the Bible, not just tradition.
records.zomi: I pawlpi in ngeina bek hi lo-in Laisiangtho a zui hi.

records.english: Can a church leader teach something that the Bible doesn't support?
records.zomi: Pawlpi makai khat in Laisiangtho in a pom loh thu a hilh thei hiam?

records.english: Many Christians would say no, and that members should test every teaching against Scripture.
records.zomi: Khristian tampi in hilh thei lo hi, ci ding uh a, memberte in thuhilhna khempeuh Laisiangtho tawh a en ding uh hi.

records.english: Our pastor's sermons always begin with a reading from Scripture.
records.zomi: I pastor' thugenna te Laisiangtho simna tawh a kipan tawntung hi.

records.english: Is it wrong to ask questions about the Bible?
records.zomi: Laisiangtho thu-ah dotna dong pen a khial hiam?

records.english: No, many faithful believers have asked hard questions about it.
records.zomi: Khial lo hi, citak upmi tampi in tua thu-ah dotna haksa a dong khin uh hi.

records.english: My grandfather quoted a proverb from the Bible whenever we were tempted to be lazy.
records.zomi: Thadah ding i kisa ciangin ka pu in Laisiangtho pan paunak khat a gen zel hi.

records.english: Early Christians came to treat the apostles' letters with the same respect as the older Scriptures.
records.zomi: Khristian masate in sawltakte' laikhak te Laisiangtho lui te zahtakna kibang tawh a pom kipan uh hi.

records.english: What challenged the students most was the idea that the Bible might ask them to change their minds.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte a langpan pen Laisiangtho in a ngaihsutna uh khel dingin a ngen kha thei hi, cih ngaihsutna ahi hi.

records.english: Throughout history, reformers have appealed to Scripture when they believed church leaders had gone astray.
records.zomi: Tangthu sung khempeuh ah pawlpi makaite in lampi a khial uh hi, ci-in a ngaihsut ciangun bawl dikna mite in Laisiangtho a lak uh hi.

records.english: Should we wait for the last guests before we start?
records.zomi: I kipat ma-in khual nunungte i ngak ding hiam?

records.english: Give them ten more minutes, and then we'll begin.
records.zomi: Minit sawm beh pia in, tua ciangin i kipan ding hi.

records.english: Guests from different backgrounds may have different ideas about how long a visit should last.
records.zomi: Mun tuamtuam pan khualte in khual pai bangzah a sawt ding hiam ngaihsutna tuamtuam a nei kha uh hi.

records.english: Could you say a few words before we eat?
records.zomi: I nek ma-in kammal tawmno na gen thei ding hiam?

records.english: Just raise your glass, thank everyone for coming, and keep it short.
records.zomi: Na haai lap bek inla, mi khempeuh na hong manun lungdam ci inla, tom takin gen in.

records.english: Prepare one dish you can make with your eyes closed, so that you're not stressed when the doorbell rings.
records.zomi: Kongkhak ging a ging ciangin na lungkham lohna dingin na mit sin-in na huan thei an khat bawl in.

records.english: Should I open the gift now or after the guests have gone?
records.zomi: Letsong tu-in ka hon ding hiam, khualte a pai khit ciangin ka hon ding hiam?

records.english: In our family we open it later, so that nobody feels their present is being compared.
records.zomi: I innkuan ah kuamah in a letsong uh kiteh bang-in a kisak lohna dingun a nung ciangin i hon hi.

records.english: I put a sign-up sheet on the church noticeboard, so that we don't end up with ten desserts and no salad.
records.zomi: An khum sawm leh anteh hing om lo-a i tawp lohna dingin pawlpi thu genna suanglaipi tungah min gelhna lai khat ka belh hi.

records.english: Ask our guests whether they'd like the window open.
records.zomi: I khualte kiangah tukvuang hon a deih uh hiam dong in.

records.english: Our guest is fasting until sunset, so we'll serve dinner as soon as it gets dark.
records.zomi: I khual ni tum dong an ngawl a hih manin a mial pah-in nitak an i pia ding hi.

records.english: Pour the juice for the children first, because they get restless while the adults talk.
records.zomi: Upate a kikum laitakin naupangte a om nuam lo uh ahih manin naupangte adingin juice thun masa in.

records.english: Put a jug of water and some glasses on every table.
records.zomi: Dawhkan khempeuh tungah tui bel khat leh haai tawmno koih in.

records.english: Kids, when the guests arrive, take their coats and hang them in the hall.
records.zomi: Naupangte, khualte a tun ciangin a puan lum uh la unla, inn sung lampi ah khai un.

records.english: Put the coats on our bed for now.
records.zomi: Tu-in puan lumte i lupna tungah koih in.

records.english: Asking a guest to help with a small task can make them feel like part of the family rather than a visitor.
records.zomi: Khual khat nasep neu khat huh dingin ngen in khual hi lo-in innkuan khen khat bangin a kisak sak thei hi.

records.english: Light the candles just before we sit down, so that they haven't burned halfway by dessert.
records.zomi: An khum i nek ma-in a kim a kan lohna dingin i tut ma pah-in khawimeivaakte hal in.

records.english: Is everyone ready to eat?
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh an ne dingin kiman khin uh hiam?

records.english: Almost, but my uncle is still washing his hands.
records.zomi: Kiman dek hi, ahi zongin ka pa neu a khut a sil lai hi.

records.english: Hosting in the hot season is easier if you prepare cold dishes that can wait on the table.
records.zomi: Lum hun-a khual muak pen dawhkan tungah ngak thei an vot te na kiman sak leh a baih zaw hi.

records.english: Each guest was asked to bring one song for the singing after dinner.
records.zomi: Nitak an khit-a la sakna adingin khual khat ciat la khat tawi dingin kingen uh hi.

records.english: In many families, the way a guest is welcomed says more than any words about how much they are valued.
records.zomi: Innkuan tampi ah khual khat a kimuak dan in kammal bangpeuh sangin bangzah a manphat hiam a gen zaw hi.

records.english: Explain to your friends that the dog isn't allowed upstairs, even if he looks sad.
records.zomi: A lungkham bang hangin ui inn tung lam ah kiphal lo hi, ci-in na lawmte kiangah gen siang in.

records.english: If a guest says they're full, don't keep filling their plate.
records.zomi: Khual khat in ka vah hi, a ci leh a kuang dimsak den kei in.

records.english: Fill the kettle again, please.
records.zomi: Kettle tui dimsak kik in.

records.english: Ask your guests about allergies when you invite them, not when the food is on the table.
records.zomi: Na khualte na sam ciangin a ne thei lo te uh dong in, an dawhkan tungah a om ciangin hi lo-in.

records.english: Write the names of the dishes on little cards, and mark the ones with nuts.
records.zomi: Card neute tungah an min gelh inla, nuts nei te ciamteh in.

records.english: Could you fold the napkins into triangles?
records.zomi: Khut nul puante kil thum-in na khul thei ding hiam?

records.english: Take this plate to the man by the window.
records.zomi: Hih kuang tukvuang kiang-a pasal kiangah tawi in.

records.english: Offer the guests a towel after the long journey.
records.zomi: Khualzinna sau khit ciangin khualte puan keusakna pia in.

records.english: Why do you serve the tea in small cups?
records.zomi: Bang hangin tea haai neu tawh na pia hiam?

records.english: So that we can keep pouring fresh, hot tea for our guests all evening.
records.zomi: Nitak bup i khualte adingin tea thak leh lum i thun den theih nadingin.

records.english: Plan the evening around your guests' needs, not around the most impressive recipe you can find.
records.zomi: An huan dan lamdang pen na muh theih tungah hi lo-in na khualte' kisapna tungah nitak geel in.

records.english: Keep the dishes warm in the oven at a low heat until everyone has arrived.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh a tun dong an te oven sungah mei niam tawh lum takin kem in.

records.english: Set the laptop at the end of the table, so that Grandma can see everyone on the video call.
records.zomi: Video call tungah Pi in mi khempeuh a muh theih nadingin dawhkan tawp ah laptop koih in.

records.english: Teach the children to say goodbye to every guest at the door.
records.zomi: Naupangte khual khempeuh kiangah kongkhak ah goodbye ci dingin sin sak in.

records.english: A bowl of fruit by the door lets guests take something home without having to ask.
records.zomi: Kongkhak kiang-a theigah kuang khat in khualte in ngen lo-in inn ah bangmah a tawi theih nadingin a phal hi.

records.english: Why do you put your knife and fork together on the plate?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na namsau leh na fork kuang tungah khawm-in na koih hiam?

records.english: It tells the host that you've finished, so they don't offer you more.
records.zomi: Na zo khin hi, ci-in inn neipa a hilh a, tua ahih manin tam zaw hong pia lo ding hi.

records.english: When a guest offers to wash up, the polite reply in our house is to refuse once and accept the second time.
records.zomi: Khual khat in kuang sil a ngen ciangin i inn-a zahtakna dawnna pen vei khat nial-a a nihna ciangin sang ahi hi.

records.english: We left a small basket in the guest room with water, fruit and a map of the town.
records.zomi: Khual inndei sungah tui, theigah leh khuapi map nei empeng neu khat i nusia hi.

records.english: Preparing a guest room with a few thoughtful details tells visitors they were truly expected.
records.zomi: Khual inndei khat ngaihsutna tawh kiman sak in khualte a kilamen taktak uh hi, ci a hilh hi.

records.english: Before the meal, show your guests where the bathroom is, so that they don't have to ask.
records.zomi: An nek ma-in a dot kul lohna dingin na khualte kisilna inn koi ah a om hiam lak in.

records.english: Children who help to host learn how to notice other people's comfort.
records.zomi: Khual muak huh naupangte in mi dangte' nuamna muh dan a sin uh hi.

records.english: Seat the shy cousin next to someone talkative, and she'll relax much sooner.
records.zomi: Zumthak sanggam numei pen kikum hat mi khat kiang ah tu sak in, tua ciangin manlang zaw-in a lungsim a dai ding hi.

records.english: What makes a buffet work is not the amount of food but how easily people can move around the table.
records.zomi: Buffet khat a sep hoih nadingin an tam zah sangin mite dawhkan kiim ah baih takin a pai thei uh hiam a thupi zaw hi.

records.english: Explaining the house rules kindly on the first evening saves awkward moments later in the visit.
records.zomi: Nitak masa pen-in inn thukhamte hehpih takin gen siang in a nung ciangin zumhuai hunte a kham hi.

records.english: Turn the music down a little during the meal.
records.zomi: An nek laitakin la aw tawmno niamsak in.

records.english: Which glasses should we use for the guests?
records.zomi: Khualte adingin haai bangte i zang ding hiam?

records.english: The tall ones from the top shelf.
records.zomi: Dawh tung pen pan a sau te.

records.english: We bought a new pan and cooked our friend's meal separately, because her faith doesn't allow her to eat pork.
records.zomi: I lawm' upna in vok sa a nek phal kei ahih manin bel thak khat i lei a, amah' an tuam-in i huan hi.

records.english: The cake was cut into small pieces so that every guest could have some.
records.zomi: Khual khempeuh in a ngah theih nadingun cake khen neu-in kiat hi.

records.english: A host who sits down and eats with the guests often makes them feel more at ease than a perfect meal.
records.zomi: Khualte tawh a tu-a an ne inn neipa in an kicing sangin a lungsim uh a dai sak zaw zel hi.

records.english: My brother had me phone each guest the day before to check that they still knew the way.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in lampi a thei lai uh hiam en dingin a zan ma-in khual khat ciat hong sam sak hi.

records.english: In my mother's village, a guest may refuse food the first time to be polite, so you offer it again.
records.zomi: Ka nu' khua ah khual khat in zahtakna hangin a masa vei-in an a nial thei ahih manin na pia kik hi.

records.english: Tuck the sheet in tightly at the corners, so that it stays smooth all night.
records.zomi: Lupna puan zan bup a phah den nadingin a kil te ah khauh takin sun in.

records.english: Offering food again after a polite refusal is generous in some communities and pushy in others.
records.zomi: Zahtak taka nialna khit ciangin an pia kik pen mipi pawl khat ah hehpihna ahi a, a dang ah sawlna ahi hi.

records.english: For a buffet, put the plates at the start of the table and the forks and napkins at the end.
records.zomi: Buffet adingin kuangte dawhkan kipatna ah koih inla, fork leh khut nul puante a tawp ah koih in.

records.english: Place the rice and bread before the main dishes, so that people don't fill their plates with meat first.
records.zomi: Mite in a masa-in sa tawh a kuang uh a dimsak lohna dingun an lian te ma-in buh leh moh koih in.

records.english: Keep the desserts on a separate table, or the queue will never move.
records.zomi: An khumte dawhkan tuam ah koih in, ahih kei leh kigual a pai ngei lo ding hi.

records.english: What do you usually eat when you're ill?
records.zomi: Na cina ciangin bang na ne zel hiam?

records.english: Plain rice soup, like my mother used to make.
records.zomi: Ka nu' huan ngei bang buh-an tui baih.

records.english: Asking someone what they enjoy eating is a more welcoming question than asking what they can't eat.
records.zomi: Mi khat kiangah bang a nek nuam hiam dot pen bang a ne thei lo hiam dot sangin muak zaw dotna ahi hi.

records.english: Please pass me the salt.
records.zomi: Cii hong pia in.

records.english: A vegetarian doesn't eat meat or fish, but a vegan doesn't eat eggs or milk either.
records.zomi: Sa ne lo mi in sa hiam nga a ne kei a, ahi zongin vegan in aktui hiam nawi zong a ne kei hi.

records.english: When you ask for no dairy, remember that butter and cheese count too.
records.zomi: Nawi a om lo na nget ciangin butter leh cheese zong kihel hi, ci phawk in.

records.english: My father loves the deep, savory taste of mushrooms and soy sauce, which some cooks call umami.
records.zomi: Ka pa in mushroom leh soy sauce' lim thuk a it mahmah a, an huan pawl khat in umami a ci uh hi.

records.english: Ask your guests what they don't eat, but don't make them explain the reason.
records.zomi: Na khualte kiangah bang a ne kei uh hiam dong in, ahi zongin a hang gen siang dingin sawl kei in.

records.english: Explaining a food allergy clearly to a restaurant can be a matter of safety, not just preference.
records.zomi: An zuakna inn khat kiangah na ne thei lo an kician takin gen siang pen deihna bek hi lo-in bitna thu ahi thei hi.

records.english: My cousin eats fish but no other meat, which surprises people who think every vegetarian avoids fish.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam in nga a ne a, ahi zongin sa dang a ne kei a, tua in sa ne lo mi khempeuh in nga a ne kei uh hi, a ci mite a lamdangsak hi.

records.english: Some foods are avoided for religious reasons, so it's kinder to ask than to guess.
records.zomi: An pawl khat upna hangin kipelh ahih manin ngaihsun sangin dot a hehpihna zaw hi.

records.english: Many people's preferences are really about habit, and habits can change with patience.
records.zomi: Mi tampi' deihna pen ngeina thu ahi a, ngeinate thuakzawhna tawh a kikhel thei hi.

records.english: Our tastes are shaped by what we ate as children, which is why foreign food can seem strange at first.
records.zomi: I lim deihnate i naupan lai-a i nek tawh kibawl ahih manin gamdang an a kipat ciangin lamdang bang-in a kisa thei hi.

records.english: What one family calls ordinary breakfast food may seem completely unusual to another.
records.zomi: Innkuan khat in zingsang an ngeina a cih in a dang khat adingin lamdang mahmah bang-in a kisa thei hi.

records.english: Bitterness is often disliked by children, yet many adults come to enjoy bitter coffee, dark chocolate and green tea.
records.zomi: Naupangte in a kha a huat zel uh a, ahi zongin upa tampi in coffee kha, chocolate vom leh tea eng a it zel uh hi.

records.english: I prefer brown bread.
records.zomi: Moh sangdup ka deih zaw hi.

records.english: Are you still a vegetarian?
records.zomi: Sa ne lo mi na hi lai hiam?

records.english: Food preferences are personal, but respecting them is a simple way of showing respect for the person.
records.zomi: An deihnate keimah thu ahi a, ahi zongin zahtak in mi pa zahtakna lahna baih khat ahi hi.

records.english: I'm not very keen on mushrooms, but please don't change the whole meal for me.
records.zomi: Mushroom ka deih mahmah kei a, ahi zongin kei adingin an bup khel kei un.

records.english: What's the difference between an allergy and an intolerance?
records.zomi: An ne thei lo leh an kituak lo kikal ah bang a kibang lo hiam?

records.english: An allergy can make you seriously ill, while an intolerance usually just upsets your stomach.
records.zomi: An ne thei lo in hong cina sak mahmah thei a, an kituak lo in na gil bek a buaisak zel hi.

records.english: Taste it first, then add the pepper.
records.zomi: A masa-in lim en inla, tua ciangin malcha koih in.

records.english: Comfort food is the kind of meal you want when you're tired, sad or far from home.
records.zomi: Lungsim nuamna an pen na tawl, na lungkham hiam inn pan na gamlat ciangin na deih an ahi hi.

records.english: My little brother was made to sit at the table until he had eaten his carrots, which only made him hate them more.
records.zomi: Ka nau pasal a carrot a nek zawh dong dawhkan kiang ah tusak ahih manin a huat zaw sak bek hi.

records.english: Is there milk in this cake?
records.zomi: Hih cake sungah nawi a om hiam?

records.english: Coffee is an acquired taste, so don't judge it by your first cup.
records.zomi: Coffee pen sin-a deih ding ahih manin na haai masa pen tawh thukhen kei in.

records.english: My grandfather likes his tea very hot.
records.zomi: Ka pu in a tea a sa mahmah a deih hi.

records.english: I'd rather skip the sauce than ask the cook to make a new one just for me.
records.zomi: An huanpa kiangah keimah adingin a thak bawl dingin ngen sangin tuihang nusia ka deih zaw hi.

records.english: The wedding invitation asked us to tick a box if we needed a meal without meat.
records.zomi: Mopawi sapna lai in sa om lo an i kisam leh bawm khat ciamteh dingin hong ngen hi.

records.english: Labels that list every ingredient help people with allergies far more than labels that only say "natural".
records.zomi: A sung-a om khempeuh a gelh laimaite in “a ngeina” ci bek laimai sangin an ne thei lo mite a huh zaw mahmah hi.

records.english: Do you eat eggs?
records.zomi: Aktui na ne hiam?

records.english: Yes, but no meat or fish.
records.zomi: Ka ne hi, ahi zongin sa hiam nga ka ne kei hi.

records.english: Many people prefer warm, heavy food in winter and lighter food when it's hot.
records.zomi: Mi tampi in khuavot ciangin an lum leh gik a deih zaw uh a, a lum ciangin an zang zaw a deih uh hi.

records.english: "May contain traces of nuts" means the food was made near nuts, so my son can't risk it.
records.zomi: “Nuts tawmno a kihel kha thei” cih in an pen nuts kiang ah kibawl hi, ci nopna ahih manin ka tapa in a ne ngam kei hi.

records.english: A host who offers several simple dishes rarely has to worry about guests going hungry.
records.zomi: An baih tuamtuam a pia inn neipa in khualte a gilkial ding a lungkham kul zel kei hi.

records.english: Eat a little spicy food every week, and you'll find you can handle more over time.
records.zomi: Kal simin an ha tawmno ne in, tua ciangin hun sawt sungin tam zaw na ne zo ding hi.

records.english: How do you say politely that you're full?
records.zomi: Ka vah hi, ci-in zahtak takin bangci-in na gen hiam?

records.english: Say that it was delicious and that you couldn't eat another bite.
records.zomi: A tui mahmah hi, ci inla, khat beh zong ka ne zo nawn kei hi, ci in.

records.english: My mother made me try a spoonful of every new dish before I was allowed to refuse it.
records.zomi: Ka nu in ka nial ma-in an thak khempeuh sikkeu khat ciat hong ciam sak hi.

records.english: For some people, the texture of a food matters more than the taste.
records.zomi: Mi pawl khat adingin an khat' lim sangin a khoih dan a thupi zaw hi.

records.english: Plant-based means the meal is made mostly or entirely from plants.
records.zomi: Singkung pan kibawl, ci nopna pen an pen a tamzaw hiam a khempeuh singkung pan kibawl ahi hi.

records.english: Is this soup made with meat stock?
records.zomi: Hih an tui sa tui tawh kibawl ahi hiam?

records.english: Do you like it hot or mild?
records.zomi: A ha na deih hiam, a ha lo na deih hiam?

records.english: Mild, please.
records.zomi: A ha lo, ka ngen hi.

records.english: Could you explain why you won't eat anything from the frying pan?
records.zomi: Bang hangin kanna bel pan bangmah na ne nuam kei hiam gen siang thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: The doctor told me to avoid fried food for a few weeks after my operation.
records.zomi: Ka zai khit ciangin kal tawmno sung an kikang pelh dingin siavuan in hong hilh hi.

records.english: Liver is the only thing I can't bring myself to eat.
records.zomi: Sin pen ka ne ngam loh khat bek ahi hi.

records.english: When chilli burns your mouth, eat some plain rice, because water only spreads the heat around.
records.zomi: Malcha in na kam a kansak ciangin buh baih tawmno ne in, tui in a sat a zelsak bek ahih manin.

records.english: Which do you like more, apples or pears?
records.zomi: Bang na deih zaw hiam, apple hiam pear hiam?

records.english: Pears, when they're soft.
records.zomi: Pear, a nem ciangin.

records.english: Why does coriander taste like soap to some people?
records.zomi: Bang hangin coriander in mi pawl khat adingin satpiang lim a nei hiam?

records.english: Scientists think it's partly in their genes, so it isn't just fussiness.
records.zomi: Science siamte in a khen khat a pianpih hang ahi hi, ci-in a ngaihsun uh ahih manin teel lua bek hi lo hi.

records.english: When you tell a host about a food you don't eat, start by thanking them for the invitation.
records.zomi: Inn neipa kiangah na nek loh an khat na hilh ciangin hong sam manin lungdam ci-in kipan in.

records.english: Then name the food simply, without a long explanation of why.
records.zomi: Tua ciangin bang hang hiam gen siangna sau om lo-in an min baih takin gen in.

records.english: Finally, mention something you do love, so that they have an easy idea for the meal.
records.zomi: A tawp-in an adingin ngaihsutna baih khat a neih nadingun na it mahmah khat gen in.

records.english: Does your daughter drink milk?
records.zomi: Na tanu in nawi a dawn hiam?

records.english: Only with chocolate in it.
records.zomi: Chocolate a kihel leh bek.

records.english: My son likes his toast cut into squares.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in a moh kang bawm lim-in at a deih hi.

records.english: Tell the waiter clearly if a food could make you ill, not just that you don't like it.
records.zomi: An khat in hong cina sak thei leh a deih lo bek hi lo-in an tawisakpa kiangah kician takin gen in.

records.english: Spicy dishes were marked with a red dot at the buffet, so the children knew which ones to avoid.
records.zomi: Buffet ah an ha te ciamtehna san tawh kiciamteh ahih manin naupangte in bang te pelh ding hiam a thei uh hi.

records.english: We weren't allowed to start eating until the elders had sat down.
records.zomi: Upate a tut dong an i ne kipan thei kei hi.

records.english: Which day is the wedding?
records.zomi: Mopawi bang ni-in ahi hiam?

records.english: Who usually speaks for the groom's family when the families first meet?
records.zomi: Innkuan nih a kimuh masak uh ciangin kiteeng ding pasal' innkuan adingin kua in a gen zel hiam?

records.english: In my family, it's an uncle or an older relative who is good with words.
records.zomi: Ka innkuan ah gen siam pa neu hiam upa sanggam khat ahi hi.

records.english: The oldest relative in our family blesses the couple at the end of the ceremony.
records.zomi: I innkuan-a upa pen in poai tawp ciangin kiteeng nihte thupha a pia hi.

records.english: Marriage in our community has always joined two families, not just two people.
records.zomi: I mipi ah kiteenna in mi nih bek hi lo-in innkuan nih a zom tawntung hi.

records.english: My uncle had to travel for three days to reach the bride's village for the first meeting.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in kimuh masa adingin kiteeng ding numei' khua tun dingin ni thum a khualzin hi.

records.english: Customs differ even between neighboring villages, so it's wise to ask the family what they expect.
records.zomi: A kiang khua tuamtuam kikal ah zong ngeinate a kibang lo ahih manin innkuan kiangah bang a lamen uh hiam dong leh a pil hi.

records.english: Two generations ago, our families agreed on gifts before the wedding date was set.
records.zomi: Khang nih ma-in i innkuante in mopawi ni a koih ma-un letsongte a kithukim uh hi.

records.english: My parents were married in the village church, and the feast went on until late at night.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa khua pawlpi ah a kiteeng uh a, ankhopna zan sawt mahmah dong a om hi.

records.english: I do want my daughter's wedding to follow our traditions, even though we live so far from home.
records.zomi: Inn pan gamla mahmah-in i teen hangin ka tanu' mopawi i ngeinate a zui ding ka deih taktak hi.

records.english: Children, please help carry the food to the tables when the guests arrive.
records.zomi: Naupangte, khualte a tun ciangun an dawhkante ah pua huh un.

records.english: Our pastor meets every couple several times before the wedding to talk about marriage.
records.zomi: I pastor in mopawi ma-in kiteeng ding nih khempeuh kiteenna thu kikum dingin vei tampi a kimu hi.

records.english: Shall we take a gift to the couple's new home?
records.zomi: Kiteeng nihte' inn thak ah letsong khat i tawi ding hiam?

records.english: Relatives from far away brought rice, chickens and money to help the bride's family.
records.zomi: Gamla pan sanggamte in kiteeng ding numei' innkuan huh dingin buh, ak leh sum a tawi uh hi.

records.english: Please sign the guest book before you leave.
records.zomi: Na pai khiat ma-in khual min gelhna laibu ah na min gelh in.

records.english: When did you get married?
records.zomi: Bang ciangin na kiteeng hiam?

records.english: Ten years ago, in the church where my parents married.
records.zomi: Kum sawm ma-in, ka nu leh ka pa' kiteenna pawlpi ah.

records.english: Before my parents married, my father's family sent two elders to visit my mother's family.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa a kiteen ma-un ka pa' innkuan in ka nu' innkuan veh dingin upa nih a sawl uh hi.

records.english: They talked for a whole evening over tea before anyone mentioned the wedding.
records.zomi: Kuamah in mopawi thu a gen ma-un tea dawn kawm-in nitak bup a kikum uh hi.

records.english: Only when both families were satisfied did my grandfather give his blessing.
records.zomi: Innkuan nih a lungkim uh ciangin bek ka pu in thupha a pia hi.

records.english: How much rice do we need for two hundred guests?
records.zomi: Khual za nih adingin buh bangzah i kisam ding hiam?

records.english: The way the two families treat each other during the preparations often shows how the marriage will be supported later.
records.zomi: Kiman laitakin innkuan nih a kizat tuah dan in kiteenna a nung ciangin bangci-in kihuh ding hiam a lak zel hi.

records.english: My brother asked our father's permission before he proposed, as our family expects.
records.zomi: I innkuan in a lamen bangin ka sanggam pasal in zi a ngen ma-in i pa' phalna a ngen hi.

records.english: Wedding gifts in our village were once given in goods, but today most families give money.
records.zomi: I khua-a mopawi letsongte van tawh kipia ngei a, ahi zongin tu-in innkuan tamzaw in sum a pia uh hi.

records.english: In my mother's family, her brother played a special part in the arrangements for her wedding.
records.zomi: Ka nu' innkuan ah a sanggam pasal in a mopawi geelna ah mun tuam khat a nei hi.

records.english: How long were your parents engaged?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa bangzah sung a kiciam uh hiam?

records.english: Almost a year, because my father was working abroad.
records.zomi: Kum khat dek, ka pa gamdang ah a sem ahih manin.

records.english: The wedding songs were sung by the church choir and then by the whole village.
records.zomi: Mopawi la te pawlpi la pawl in a sa masa uh a, tua ciangin khua bup in a sa uh hi.

records.english: After the wedding, the bride went to live in the groom's family home, as was the custom when my parents were young.
records.zomi: Mopawi khit ciangin ka nu leh ka pa' khangno lai-a ngeina bangin kiteeng numei pasal' innkuan inn ah teeng dingin a pai hi.

records.english: Is it true that weddings in your community last for several days?
records.zomi: Na mipi-a mopawi ni tampi a sawt hi, cih a tak hiam?

records.english: In my grandparents' village, yes, but in the city most weddings are over in one day now.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh ka pite' khua ah a tak hi, ahi zongin khuapi ah tu-in mopawi tamzaw ni khat sungin a bei hi.

records.english: The bride and groom thanked every guest at the door as they left.
records.zomi: Kiteeng nihte in a pai khiat uh laitakin khual khempeuh kongkhak ah lungdam a ci uh hi.

records.english: My parents met at a wedding in the next village.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa a zom khua-a mopawi ah a kimu uh hi.

records.english: How did your parents' families agree on the wedding?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa' innkuante mopawi thu-ah bangci-in a kithukim uh hiam?

records.english: After several visits, the elders on both sides shook hands and named a date.
records.zomi: Vei tampi a kiveh khit uh ciangin lam nih-a upate in khut a kilen uh a, ni a koih uh hi.

records.english: Our neighbors lent us their biggest cooking pots for the wedding.
records.zomi: I inn vengte in mopawi adingin a an huanna beel lian pente uh hong ngetsak uh hi.

records.english: Many young couples abroad try to keep the old customs while adding new ones.
records.zomi: Gamdang-a kiteeng thak tampi in ngeina thak a behlap kawm-un ngeina luite a kem sawm uh hi.

records.english: Many young couples today choose their own partners but still ask for their families' blessing.
records.zomi: Tu hun-a kiteeng thak tampi in amau' it a teel uh a, ahi zongin a innkuan uh' thupha a ngen lai uh hi.

records.english: Weddings bring together relatives who may not have seen each other for many years.
records.zomi: Mopawi in kum tampi sung a kimu ngei lo kha sanggamte a kaikhawm hi.

records.english: My cousin's wedding was streamed online so that relatives abroad could watch it.
records.zomi: Gamdang-a sanggamte in a et theih nadingun ka sanggam' mopawi online-in kikhak hi.

records.english: Some of the old wedding customs are fading, especially among families who have moved to the cities.
records.zomi: Mopawi ngeina lui pawl khat a mang kipan a, a diak in khuapi ah a kitawn innkuante lak ah.

records.english: The bride wore her grandmother's necklace.
records.zomi: Kiteeng ding numei in a pi' ngawngkhih a bulh hi.

records.english: Congratulations on your engagement!
records.zomi: Na kiciamna adingin ka lungdam hi!

records.english: Please don't wear white to the wedding, because only the bride wears white at ours.
records.zomi: Mopawi ah puan ngo silh kei in, i mopawi ah kiteeng ding numei bek in a ngo a silh ahih manin.

records.english: For families living abroad, holding a traditional wedding can be a way of passing culture on to the children.
records.zomi: Gamdang-a teeng innkuante adingin ngeina mopawi bawl pen naupangte kiangah ngeina ap nading lampi khat ahi thei hi.

records.english: Write a card for the bride and groom.
records.zomi: Kiteeng nihte adingin card khat gelh in.

records.english: The young couple were given a blessing by every elder in turn.
records.zomi: Kiteeng khangno nihte upa khempeuh in khat zawh khat thupha a pia uh hi.

records.english: Who is cooking for the wedding?
records.zomi: Mopawi adingin kua in an a huan ding hiam?

records.english: The women from both families, with help from the neighbors.
records.zomi: Innkuan nih-a numeite, inn vengte' huhna tawh.

records.english: In our village, the whole community helps to prepare the wedding feast.
records.zomi: I khua ah mipi bup in mopawi ankhopna kiman sak huh hi.

records.english: Did you go to your cousin's wedding?
records.zomi: Na sanggam' mopawi ah na pai hiam?

records.english: Yes, and I sang with the choir.
records.zomi: Pai ing, leh la pawl tawh la ka sa hi.

records.english: Everyone danced after the meal, even the elders who said they were too old.
records.zomi: An khit ciangin ka upa lua hi, a ci upate zong kihel-in mi khempeuh a lam uh hi.

records.english: The couple received so many blankets that they gave some to their younger cousins.
records.zomi: Kiteeng nihte in puannak tam lua a ngah uh ahih manin pawl khat a sanggam neu zawte uh a pia uh hi.

records.english: My little sister carried the flowers at our brother's wedding.
records.zomi: Ka nau numei in i sanggam pasal' mopawi ah pakte a tawi hi.

records.english: Had my grandparents not insisted on a church wedding, my parents might have married with only a family feast.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh ka pite in pawlpi mopawi a ngen kei uh leh ka nu leh ka pa innkuan ankhopna bek tawh a kiteeng kha ding uh hi.

records.english: What moved my mother most at my wedding was hearing the songs she had sung at her own.
records.zomi: Ka mopawi ah ka nu' lungsim a khoih pen amah' mopawi-a a sak late a zak ahi hi.

records.english: Why do the young men in your village carry the bride's belongings?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na khua-a pasal khangnote in kiteeng ding numei' vante a pua uh hiam?

records.english: It shows that her new family welcomes her and will look after her.
records.zomi: A innkuan thak in amah a muak a, a kem ding uh hi, ci a lak hi.

records.english: If you borrow something, return it in the same condition.
records.zomi: Bangmah na ngetsak leh a om dan kibang mah-in lohsak kik in.

records.english: Our neighbor's son mows the old lady's grass every Saturday without being asked.
records.zomi: I inn veng' tapa in ngen lo-in Kiginni simin numei upa' lopa a at hi.

records.english: How did you feel when the teacher left you in charge of the class?
records.zomi: Saya in kilasi hong kemsak ciangin bangci-in na kisa hiam?

records.english: Responsibility for the elderly in our community is shared by the whole family, not left to one person.
records.zomi: I mipi ah upate kemna mawhpuakna innkuan bup in a hawm uh a, mi khat tungah nusia lo hi.

records.english: You promised to help, so please don't let them down.
records.zomi: Huh dingin na kiciam khin ahih manin amaute lungkiasak kei in.

records.english: Many traditional stories teach that a person who cares for small things can be trusted with great ones.
records.zomi: Ngeina tangthu tampi in na neute a kem mi pen na lian te tawh muan theih hi, ci-in a sin sak hi.

records.english: Clean up your own mess, please.
records.zomi: Nangmah' buaina siangsak in.

records.english: The team captain was blamed for the loss, but she said the whole team should share it.
records.zomi: Pawl makai in sun manin mawhsak a, ahi zongin amah in pawl bup in i hawm ding hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Please put your plate in the sink when you've finished.
records.zomi: Na zawh ciangin na kuang tui sil kuang sungah koih in.

records.english: A leader's responsibility is not only to make decisions but also to stand by them when they turn out badly.
records.zomi: Makaipa' mawhpuakna pen thukhen bek hi lo-in a hoih lo-in a suah ciangin zong a kiang ah ding ahi hi.

records.english: The boy who broke the bench spent his Saturday helping the caretaker mend it.
records.zomi: Tutphah a kitansak pasal naupang in a bawl dam dingin a Kiginni sang kemtu huh-in a zang hi.

records.english: When my son was trusted with a key to the church hall, he learned more about responsibility than any lecture could teach.
records.zomi: Ka tapa pawlpi kikhopna inn tawh tawh a kipiak ciangin thuhilhna bangpeuh sangin mawhpuakna tam zaw a sin hi.

records.english: My little sister looks after the chickens before school.
records.zomi: Ka nau numei in sang a kah ma-in akte a kem hi.

records.english: Did you feed the cat?
records.zomi: Zawhngeu an na pia hiam?

records.english: I'm sorry, the broken cup was my fault.
records.zomi: Hong maisak in, haai kitan pen kei' mawhna ahi hi.

records.english: Who is responsible for locking the classroom?
records.zomi: Kilasi khak mawhpuakna kua in a nei hiam?

records.english: The class monitor, and today that's Lian.
records.zomi: Kilasi kemtu, leh tuni Lian ahi hi.

records.english: Looking after a shared space, such as a park or a well, is a responsibility that every neighbor carries.
records.zomi: Huan hiam tuikhuk bang kihawm mun kem pen inn veng khempeuh' mawhpuakna ahi hi.

records.english: What impressed the villagers most was that the young driver came back to report the accident himself.
records.zomi: Khua mite a lamdang sak pen mawtaw mawng khangno amah mah in kipalhna thu gen dingin a hong kik ahi hi.

records.english: Turn off the lights when you leave a room.
records.zomi: Inndei khat na nusiat ciangin meivakte mit in.

records.english: Looking after my baby brother for an evening made me feel very grown up.
records.zomi: Nitak khat ka naungek nau pasal ka kem ciangin ka upa bang-in ka kisa hi.

records.english: The new manager admitted that the delay was her department's fault and promised to fix it.
records.zomi: Manager thak in a nunna pen a nasepna khen' mawhna ahi hi, ci-in a pom a, a bawl dam ding a kiciam hi.

records.english: Whose turn is it to take out the rubbish?
records.zomi: Eek pua khia ding kua' hun ahi hiam?

records.english: Mine, but I'll do it after dinner.
records.zomi: Kei hun hi, ahi zongin nitak an khit ciangin ka bawl ding hi.

records.english: Why did you offer to pay for the broken window?
records.zomi: Bang hangin tukvuang kitan man pia dingin na ngen hiam?

records.english: Because my ball broke it, even though it was an accident.
records.zomi: Kiciamteh lo-a a hih hangin ka bawl in a kitansak ahih manin.

records.english: When the teacher was ill, the oldest pupils kept the younger ones quiet and busy.
records.zomi: Saya a cina ciangin sangnaupang upa pente in a neu zawte a daisak uh a, a nasepsak uh hi.

records.english: Can I trust you to look after your sister?
records.zomi: Na sanggam numei kem dingin kong muang thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, I'll hold her hand the whole time.
records.zomi: Muang thei hi, hun bup a khut ka len ding hi.

records.english: The bridge was repaired by the villagers themselves when the council said it had no money.
records.zomi: Khuapi vaihawm in sum a nei kei hi, a cih ciangin khua mite amau mah in lei a bawl dam uh hi.

records.english: Every child in our house has one task to do before going out to play.
records.zomi: I inn-a naupang khempeuh in pua ah a kimawl ma-un nasep khat ciat a sem uh hi.

records.english: When I was twelve, my parents left me in charge of the family shop for one afternoon.
records.zomi: Kum sawm leh nih ka phak ciangin ka nu leh ka pa in sun nung khat sung innkuan dawl hong kemsak uh hi.

records.english: A customer paid with a large note, and I gave her far too much change by mistake.
records.zomi: Lei nu khat in sum lai lian tawh a pia a, khialh-in sum lehkik tam lua ka pia hi.

records.english: That evening I counted the money twice, found the mistake, and walked to her house to explain.
records.zomi: Tua nitak sum nihvei ka sim a, khialhna ka mu a, gen siang dingin a inn ah ka kalsuan hi.

records.english: Children who are given small responsibilities early often grow into reliable adults.
records.zomi: Tung takin mawhpuakna neute kipia naupangte muanhuai upa-in a khang zel uh hi.

records.english: Had the guard checked the door before leaving, the paintings would not have been stolen.
records.zomi: Kemtu in a pai khiat ma-in kongkhak a en leh limte kiguk lo ding hi.

records.english: It is easy to blame others when things go wrong, but it takes maturity to say, "That was my fault."
records.zomi: Thu a hoih kei ciangin mi dangte mawhsak a baih a, ahi zongin “Tua pen kei' mawhna ahi hi” ci dingin pilna a kisam hi.

records.english: My cousin saves part of every pay packet for his parents' medicine.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam in a khasum ngah simin a khen khat a nu leh a pa' zatui adingin a koih hi.

records.english: Our class was given a small vegetable garden to look after for the whole year.
records.zomi: I kilasi kum bup kem dingin anteh huan neu khat kipia hi.

records.english: In the summer holidays, nobody remembered to water it, and most of the plants died.
records.zomi: Khal tawlngakni sungin kuamah in tui buak a phawk kei uh a, a singkung tamzaw a si hi.

records.english: The next spring, we made a rota on the classroom wall, and the garden produced enough beans for a school lunch.
records.zomi: A zom spring ciangin kilasi bang ah kilaih ding gelhna khat i bawl a, huan in sang sun an khat adingin be a tawk a suak hi.

records.english: My grandfather never misses a day of watering his trees.
records.zomi: Ka pu in a singkungte tui buak ni khat zong a mansuah ngei kei hi.

records.english: My brother forgot to lock the shop, and some boxes were stolen during the night.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in dawl khak a mangngilh a, zan sungin bawm pawl khat kiguk hi.

records.english: Did you remember to give Grandpa his tablets at lunchtime?
records.zomi: Sun an hun ciangin Pu a zatuite na pia phawk hiam?

records.english: Yes, and I wrote the time in the notebook, as the nurse asked.
records.zomi: Phawk ing, leh nurse in a ngen bangin laibu neu sungah hun ka gelh hi.

records.english: It's your job to feed the dog every morning.
records.zomi: Zingsang simin ui an pia pen na nasep ahi hi.

records.english: Taking responsibility means accepting the consequences of your choices, not only the rewards.
records.zomi: Mawhpuakna la in na teelnate' letsong bek hi lo-in a nung-a tung thute pom ci nopna hi.

records.english: Rather than waiting to be told, good team members notice what needs doing and do it.
records.zomi: Kihilh ngak sangin pawl sung-a mi hoihte in bang sep ding hiam a mu uh a, a sem uh hi.

records.english: Shall I write a list of what needs to be done while you're away?
records.zomi: Na om loh sungin sep ding list khat ka gelh ding hiam?

records.english: Who left the gate open?
records.zomi: Kongpi kua in a hong nusia hiam?

records.english: I did, and I'll go and find the goats.
records.zomi: Kei ka hi a, kelte ka va zong ding hi.

records.english: Children, each of you will be responsible for one plant on the windowsill.
records.zomi: Naupangte, note khat ciat in tukvuang dawh tung-a singkung khat ciat ah mawhpuakna na nei ding uh hi.

records.english: My father taught me to finish a job properly, even if nobody is checking.
records.zomi: Ka pa in kuamah in a en kei zongin nasep khat hoih takin zo dingin hong sin sak hi.

records.english: Would you own up to a mistake if you knew nobody would ever find out?
records.zomi: Kuamah in a thei ngei lo ding hi, ci na theih leh khialhna khat na pom ding hiam?

records.english: I promised to look after my friend's fish while she was away, and I fed them every day.
records.zomi: Ka lawm a om loh sungin a ngate kem dingin ka kiciam a, ni simin an ka pia hi.

records.english: Finish your homework before you play.
records.zomi: Na kimawl ma-in na innlai zo in.

records.english: Why do you always check the stove twice before you leave the house?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na inn na nusiat ma-in meikhuk nihvei na en tawntung hiam?

records.english: Thank you for taking care of everything while I was ill.
records.zomi: Ka cina sungin bangkim na kem manin lungdam ing.

records.english: What will you do if you lose the key?
records.zomi: Tawh na mansuah leh bang na bawl ding hiam?

records.english: I'll tell you straight away, so that we can change the lock.
records.zomi: Kong hilh pah ding a, tua ciangin khakna i laih thei ding hi.

records.english: What keeps the moon from flying off into space?
records.zomi: Bang in kha vantung ah a leng khiat lohna dingin a kem hiam?

records.english: The Earth's gravity pulls on it and keeps it moving in a circle around us.
records.zomi: Leitung' kaihna in a kai a, i kiim ah a kual-in a pai den sak hi.

records.english: Earthquakes happen when huge pieces of the Earth's crust suddenly move against each other.
records.zomi: Leitung' vun khen lian mahmah te pah-in a kisuh tuah ciangin lei ling a piang hi.

records.english: There are eight planets in our solar system.
records.zomi: I solar system ah planet giat a om hi.

records.english: Never look straight at the sun, even through sunglasses.
records.zomi: Mit khuh mitlimlang tawh zong ni tang takin en ngei kei in.

records.english: Astronauts on the space station see about sixteen sunrises every day.
records.zomi: Space station-a astronaut te in ni khat ah ni suak sawm leh guk bang a mu uh hi.

records.english: Our class used a torch and a ball to show how an eclipse happens.
records.zomi: I kilasi in eclipse bangci-in a piang hiam lak nadingin tawmei leh bawl khat a zang hi.

records.english: Shooting stars are small pieces of rock burning up as they fall through the atmosphere.
records.zomi: Aksi kia te van huih tungtawn-in a kiat laitakin a kang suang neute ahi hi.

records.english: Fossils show us plants and animals that lived long before there were any people.
records.zomi: Fossil te in mihing a om ma sawt mahmah-a a nungta singkung leh ganhingte hong lak hi.

records.english: Put the globe on the table so that everyone can see it.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh in a muh theih nadingun globe dawhkan tungah koih in.

records.english: Rocks are slowly broken down by wind, water and ice into the sand and soil around us.
records.zomi: Suangte huih, tui leh tuikhal in zawl takin a sut a, i kiim-a piakneel leh lei a suak hi.

records.english: Can you see the Milky Way from the city?
records.zomi: Khuapi pan Milky Way na mu thei hiam?

records.english: Rarely, because the street lights make the sky too bright.
records.zomi: Tawm hi, lampi meivak te in van a vaksak lua ahih manin.

records.english: Is the sun bigger than the Earth?
records.zomi: Ni pen Leitung sangin a lian zaw hiam?

records.english: Much bigger, about a hundred times wider.
records.zomi: Lian zaw mahmah hi, za khat bang a zai zaw hi.

records.english: What fascinates many children most is that there may be planets around other stars where life is possible.
records.zomi: Naupang tampi a lamdang sak pen aksi dangte kiim ah nuntak a om thei planet te a om kha thei hi, cih ahi hi.

records.english: The moon doesn't make its own light; it reflects light from the sun.
records.zomi: Kha in amah' vak a bawl kei a, ni' vak a lang sak hi.

records.english: Why does the moon seem to change shape during the month?
records.zomi: Bang hangin kha in kha sungin a lim a kikhel bang hiam?

records.english: We see different amounts of its sunlit side as it travels around the Earth.
records.zomi: Leitung kiim a vel laitakin a ni vak lam khen tuamtuam i mu hi.

records.english: How far away is the moon?
records.zomi: Kha bangzah in a gamla hiam?

records.english: About 384,000 kilometers, so its light reaches us in just over a second.
records.zomi: Kilometre 384,000 bang, tua ahih manin a vak second khat val sungin hong tung hi.

records.english: The sky is full of stars in the village.
records.zomi: Khua ah van in aksi a dim hi.

records.english: On a clear night, our teacher took the class up the hill behind the school with a small telescope.
records.zomi: Zan siang khat in i saya in telescope neu khat tawh kilasi sang nung-a mual tungah a paipih hi.

records.english: One by one, we looked at the moon and saw the shadows of its craters along the edge of the light.
records.zomi: Khat zawh khat in kha i en a, a vak tawp ah a kuamte' limliam i mu hi.

records.english: Later she pointed out Jupiter, and the sharpest-eyed pupil spotted three tiny moons beside it.
records.zomi: A nung ciangin Jupiter a lak a, mit hoih pen sangnaupang in a kiang ah kha neu thum a mu hi.

records.english: Is the moon really bigger when it's near the horizon?
records.zomi: Kha pen van ciang kiang ah a om ciangin a lian zaw taktak hiam?

records.english: No, it only looks bigger; its real size stays the same.
records.zomi: Lian zaw lo hi, a lian zaw bang-in kilang bek a, a lianzah taktak a kibang den hi.

records.english: Because the Earth is tilted, the length of the day changes through the year in most places.
records.zomi: Leitung a ngaksai ahih manin mun tamzaw ah kum sungin ni sau dan a kikhel hi.

records.english: The layers of rock in a cliff can be read like the pages of a very old book.
records.zomi: Suangpang sung-a suang tang te laibu lui mahmah khat' phekte bangin kisim thei hi.

records.english: Point to the North Star.
records.zomi: North Star lak in.

records.english: Geologists date some rocks by measuring the slow breakdown of certain elements inside them.
records.zomi: Suang siamte in suang pawl khat a sung-a van pawl khat a zawl taka a kisiat dan teh-in a kum a sim uh hi.

records.english: Shall we watch the sunrise from the hill tomorrow?
records.zomi: Zingciang mual tung pan ni suak i en ding hiam?

records.english: The seasons are reversed in the southern half of the world, so December is a summer month there.
records.zomi: Leitung sim lam khen ah hun te a kileh ahih manin tua lam ah December pen khal kha ahi hi.

records.english: Without its atmosphere, the Earth would be far colder at night and far hotter during the day.
records.zomi: A van huih om lo leh Leitung zan ah a vot zaw mahmah ding a, sun ah a sa zaw mahmah ding hi.

records.english: Children, draw the planets in order, starting with the one closest to the sun.
records.zomi: Naupangte, ni tawh a nai pen pan kipan-in planet te a kizui dan bangin gelh un.

records.english: Mars looks red because its soil contains a lot of iron oxide, which is a kind of rust.
records.zomi: Mars a lei in iron oxide a kici sik ziaui tampi a nei ahih manin a san bang hi.

records.english: Volcanoes form where hot, melted rock from deep inside the Earth reaches the surface.
records.zomi: Leitung sung thuk pan suang lum leh a tui te a tung lam a tun ciangin meimual a piang hi.

records.english: Write down the time the sun sets every day this week.
records.zomi: Hih kal ni simin ni tum hun gelh in.

records.english: The highest mountains were pushed up over millions of years as these pieces collided.
records.zomi: Hih khen te a kisuh tuah uh ciangin kum za tul tampi sungin mual sang pente a kisawn tou hi.

records.english: Stars twinkle because their light passes through moving air.
records.zomi: Aksite in a vak uh huih kikhem tungtawn-in a pai ahih manin a vak kilaplap uh hi.

records.english: A compass needle points north because the Earth behaves like a giant magnet.
records.zomi: Leitung in magnet lian mahmah bangin a sem ahih manin compass pen in mal lam a lak hi.

records.english: Rather than being fixed, the continents are still moving a few centimeters every year.
records.zomi: Kician-a om sangin gam lian te kum simin centimetre tawmno a kikhel lai uh hi.

records.english: Look, the moon is full tonight!
records.zomi: En in, tu zanin kha a dim hi!

records.english: My son was so excited by the solar system model that he hung the planets from his bedroom ceiling.
records.zomi: Ka tapa solar system lim in a kipaksak lua ahih manin a lupna inn tung ah planet te a khai hi.

records.english: Satellites in orbit help us forecast storms, find our way and send messages around the world.
records.zomi: Van tung-a satellite te in huihpi thu gen khol, lampi zon leh leitung bup ah message khak dingin hong huh hi.

records.english: Scientists estimate that the Earth is about four and a half billion years old.
records.zomi: Science siamte in Leitung pen kum tul tul tul li leh a kim bang a upa hi, ci-in a ngaihsun uh hi.

records.english: Is Pluto still a planet?
records.zomi: Pluto planet ahi lai hiam?

records.english: Scientists now call it a dwarf planet.
records.zomi: Science siamte in tu-in dwarf planet a ci uh hi.

records.english: Light from the sun takes about eight minutes to reach the Earth.
records.zomi: Ni pan vak Leitung a tun nadingin minit giat bang a sawt hi.

records.english: The sun is a star, much closer to us than any other.
records.zomi: Ni pen aksi khat ahi a, aksi dang khempeuh sangin eite tawh a nai zaw mahmah hi.

records.english: Which planet is the biggest?
records.zomi: Planet bang in a lian pen hiam?

records.english: Jupiter, by a long way.
records.zomi: Jupiter, tampi in.

records.english: The tides rise and fall mainly because of the pull of the moon.
records.zomi: Tuipi tui a kahtou leh a kiak pen a tamzaw kha' kaihna hang ahi hi.

records.english: Studying other planets helps scientists understand how the Earth's own climate works.
records.zomi: Planet dangte sin in science siamte in Leitung' huihkhua ngeina bangci-in a sem hiam a thei nadingun a huh hi.

records.english: Why do we have day and night?
records.zomi: Bang hangin sun leh zan i nei hiam?

records.english: Because the Earth spins, so each side faces the sun and then turns away from it.
records.zomi: Leitung a kihei ahih manin lam khat ciat in ni a ngat a, tua ciangin a kihei khia hi.

records.english: Had the early sailors not watched the stars so carefully, they could never have crossed the oceans.
records.zomi: Tanglai tembaw mawngte in aksite limtakin a en kei uh leh tuipi lian a kantan zo ngei kei ding uh hi.

records.english: The Earth goes around the sun once a year.
records.zomi: Leitung in kum khat ah vei khat ni a kiimvel hi.

records.english: Do you know the names of any stars?
records.zomi: Aksi min khat peuhpeuh na thei hiam?

records.english: The stars we see at night are so far away that their light may have left them thousands of years ago.
records.zomi: Zan-a i muh aksite a gamla lua ahih manin a vak kum tul tampi ma-in a pai khia kha thei hi.

records.english: We cook this dish only when someone in the family has a new baby.
records.zomi: Innkuan sungah naungek thak a om ciangin bek hih an i huan hi.

records.english: Taste this and tell me if it's right.
records.zomi: Hih lim en inla, a dik hiam hong hilh in.

records.english: Stir it slowly, the way Grandma does.
records.zomi: Pi' bawl dan bangin zawl takin hel in.

records.english: Wrap the rice basket in a cloth, and it will stay warm until the last guest arrives.
records.zomi: Buh empeng puan tawh tuam in, tua ciangin khual nunung a tun dong a lum den ding hi.

records.english: Explaining what each dish means helps children see a family meal as more than just food.
records.zomi: An khat ciat bang a ci nopna hiam gen siang in naupangte in innkuan an pen an bek sangin a thupi zaw hi, ci a mu thei uh hi.

records.english: Hold the hot pot with a folded cloth on each handle, and ask someone to open the door for you.
records.zomi: Beel sa pen a ciahna khat ciat ah puan khul tawh len inla, kuamah kongkhak hong sak dingin ngen in.

records.english: The dumplings can be made a week ahead and frozen, but the sauce must be fresh.
records.zomi: Dumpling te kal khat ma-in bawl-in khal sak theih a, ahi zongin tuihang pen a thak ding hi.

records.english: Each grandchild is given one dish to learn, so that no recipe depends on a single person.
records.zomi: Bawlna khat mi khat bek tungah a kinga lohna dingin tu khat ciat an khat sin dingin kipia hi.

records.english: Fold the leaves twice and tie them with a thin strip of bamboo, as your grandmother showed you.
records.zomi: Na pi in a lak bangin nahte nihvei khul inla, mau khau neu tawh khih in.

records.english: Which dish is your favorite?
records.zomi: An bang na deih pen hiam?

records.english: The sweet rice cakes, because we only have them once a year.
records.zomi: Buh moh khum, kum khat ah vei khat bek i ne ahih manin.

records.english: When my grandmother's hands became too weak to knead, she sat beside us and told us when the dough was ready.
records.zomi: Ka pi' khut nal zo lo dingin a thadah ciangin i kiang ah a tu a, moh nal a kiman ciangin hong hilh hi.

records.english: Three days before the festival, we soak the beans and buy the meat, because the butcher closes early that week.
records.zomi: Pawi ma ni thum ciangin sa zuakpa tua kal a tung takin a khak ahih manin be te i nen a, sa i lei hi.

records.english: Two days before, my mother makes the spice paste and the pickles, which taste better after a night in the jar.
records.zomi: Ni nih ma-in ka nu in an lim nal leh an thuk te a bawl a, tua te bel sungah zan khat a om khit ciangin a tui zaw hi.

records.english: On the morning itself, we only cook the rice and warm everything else, so that the elders aren't kept waiting.
records.zomi: A zingsang mah ciangin upate a ngak lohna dingun buh bek i huan a, a dang khempeuh i lumsak hi.

records.english: We don't use the good plates for everyday meals; they come out only on feast days.
records.zomi: Kuang hoihte ni sim an adingin i zang kei hi; ankhopna ni ciangin bek i la khia hi.

records.english: What should I say before we start eating?
records.zomi: I nek kipat ma-in bang ka gen ding hiam?

records.english: Nothing special, just wait until Father picks up his spoon.
records.zomi: Tuamtuam om lo hi, Pa in a sikkeu a lak dong ngak bek in.

records.english: Why does your grandmother always put a spoonful of rice aside before serving?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na pi in an a pia ma-in buh sikkeu khat a koih tuam tawntung hiam?

records.english: She says it's a thank-you for the harvest, a habit from her own mother.
records.zomi: Lo lak adingin lungdam kohna ahi hi, a ci a, amah' nu pan ngeina khat ahi hi.

records.english: The family meal was postponed by a week so that my sister could fly home for it.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam numei a ciah theih nadingin innkuan an kal khat kinungta hi.

records.english: When the family grew too large for one pot, my aunt began cooking the stew in two and mixing them at the end.
records.zomi: Innkuan beel khat adingin a lian lua ciangin ka ni in an tui beel nih-in a huan kipan a, a tawp ciangin a hel khawm hi.

records.english: A traditional meal is easier to keep alive when the work is shared among the generations.
records.zomi: Ngeina an pen khang tuamtuam kikal ah nasep a kihawm ciangin a nungta den baih zaw hi.

records.english: Preparing food for a large family over several days requires planning more than skill.
records.zomi: Ni tampi sung innkuan lian adingin an kiman sak in siamna sangin geelna a kisam zaw hi.

records.zomi: An huanna-a an huan upa pen, cii behlap a kisam hiam a thukhen pa.

records.zomi: Ka tapa in innkuan bawlna khat ciat a zawh an lim tawh card khat tungah hong gelh sak hi.

records.english: Save a plate for your uncle.
records.zomi: Na pa neu adingin kuang khat kem in.

records.english: At our table the soup comes last, to help the meal settle, although my friend's family serves it first.
records.zomi: I dawhkan ah an a kituak nadingin an tui a nunung pen-in kipia a, ka lawm' innkuan in a masa-in a pia uh hangin.

records.english: Put the cushions around the table.
records.zomi: Dawhkan kiim ah lukhungte koih in.

records.english: In our family, the round dumplings stand for everyone being together, so we make one for each person.
records.zomi: I innkuan ah dumpling kualte in mi khempeuh kikhawm na lak ahih manin mi khat ciat adingin khat i bawl hi.

records.english: If you arrive late to the family meal, greet the eldest before you sit down.
records.zomi: Innkuan an ah na nun leh na tut ma-in a upa pen hopih in.

records.english: Pass the plates down the table.
records.zomi: Dawhkan tungah kuangte hawm thang un.

records.english: Can I help you carry the soup?
records.zomi: An tui pua dingin kong huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Explain to your cousin that we eat together from the big dish, so he shouldn't wait for his own plate.
records.zomi: Na sanggam kiangah kuang lian khat pan khawm-in i ne ahih manin amah' kuang a ngak kul lo hi, ci-in gen siang in.

records.english: Ask Grandpa to tell the story behind the dish, because he loves to explain it.
records.zomi: Pu in a gen siang a it mahmah ahih manin an nung-a tangthu gen dingin ngen in.

records.english: Is this the dish your father always made?

records.english: Keep the lid on the pot while the rice rests, or it will dry out before the meal.

records.english: The order in which dishes are served can say a great deal about a family's values.
records.zomi: An te kipiak dan in innkuan khat' thupi sak te tampi a gen thei hi.

records.english: Some days I still wake up sad, but fewer than before.
records.zomi: Ni pawl khat ka lungkham lai-in ka thou a, ahi zongin a ma sangin a tawm zaw hi.

records.english: When you share good news with someone who is going through a hard time, keep it brief and ask about them too.
records.zomi: Hun haksa a tuah mi khat tawh thu hoih na hawm ciangin tom takin gen inla, amah thu zong dong in.

records.english: My little girl was given a memory box for her grandfather's photos and letters.
records.zomi: Ka tanu neu in a pu' lim leh laikhak te adingin phawkna bawm khat a ngah hi.

records.english: Here, have my handkerchief.
records.zomi: Hih, ka khut puan la in.

records.english: Some grieving people want company, while others need quiet, so ask which they'd prefer.
records.zomi: Lungkham mi pawl khat in kiang-a om a deih uh a, a dangte in daina a kisam uh ahih manin bang a deih zaw uh hiam dong in.

records.english: Is it normal to feel guilty when you start to feel happy again after a loss?
records.zomi: Mansuahna khit ciangin na lungdam kik kipat ciangin mawhna kisa pen a ngeina mah hiam?

records.english: Very normal, and it doesn't mean you've forgotten the person.

records.english: Make a list of people you can call, and keep it by the phone.

records.english: Take a deep breath, and tell me slowly.
records.zomi: Huih thuk takin la inla, zawl takin hong hilh in.

records.zomi: Lungsim huh siam in mansuahna khit ciangin dahna pen a ngeina mah a, kha tampi sung a om lungsim niamna in huhna a kisam hi, ci-in a gen siang hi.

records.english: Happiness doesn't mean feeling cheerful all the time; it often feels more like being calm.

records.english: In a condolence card, it's enough to say you're sorry and share one good memory of the person.
records.zomi: Lungkhamna card khat ah lungkham ing, ci inla, mi pa thu-ah phawkna hoih khat hawm in a tawk hi.

records.english: Do you want me to sit with you?
records.zomi: Na kiang ah ka tut ding na deih hiam?

records.english: It's all right to laugh at a happy memory, even in the middle of a sad week.
records.zomi: Kal dahhuai kimlai-in zong phawkna nuam khat-ah nui pen a hoih hi.

records.english: Is there anything I can do?
records.zomi: Ka bawl theih bangmah a om hiam?

records.english: Just keep calling me, like you have been.
records.zomi: Na sam bangin hong sam den bek in.

records.english: What helps most after a loss is usually not advice but the steady presence of people who care.
records.zomi: Mansuahna khit ciangin a huh pen thuhilhna hi lo-in lungsim nei mite' kiang-a om den ahi zel hi.

records.english: Offer practical help, such as cooking a meal or collecting the children from school.
records.zomi: An huan hiam sang pan naupangte la bang huhna taktak pia in.

records.english: Celebrate small wins, like getting out of bed early or finishing one task.
records.zomi: Zingsang tung takin thoh hiam nasep khat zawh bang zawhna neute adingin lungdam in.

records.english: Grief can return unexpectedly years later, triggered by a smell, a song or a familiar place.

records.english: When a friend is grieving, sit with them and let them talk, without trying to fix anything.

records.english: Ask simple questions, such as what their mother was like, and listen to the stories.

records.english: A week later, send a short message, because that's often when the visitors stop coming.
