records.zomi: Tung nai lo hi, ahi zongin hih kal sungin a tung ding hi.

records.english: Learning to play an instrument teaches a kind of patience that few other activities can.
records.zomi: Khuang tum van khat tum sin in sepna dang tawmno bek in a sin theih thuakzawhna a sin sak hi.

records.english: When my father's business struggled, he refused to give up, and slowly the customers came back.
records.zomi: Ka pa' sumbawlna a haksat ciangin a nusia nuam kei a, zawl takin leite a hong kik uh hi.

records.english: Slow down, there's no rush.
records.zomi: Zawl in, manlang kul lo hi.

records.english: Let the paint dry before you touch it.
records.zomi: Na khoih ma-in zeek a keu sak in.

records.english: A patient nurse can make a frightened child feel safe.
records.zomi: Thuakzawhna nei nurse khat in naupang lau khat a bit kisak sak thei hi.

records.english: I'm trying to be patient.
records.zomi: Thuakzawh dingin ka hanciam hi.

records.english: Impatient decisions, made in anger or hunger, are often the ones we regret most.
records.zomi: Heh hiam gilkial-a bawl thuakzawhna om lo thukhennate pen i lungkham pen te ahi zel hi.

records.english: The young carpenter wanted to make furniture straight away, but his master made him sand wood for a month first.
records.zomi: Sing seemmi khangno in pah-in inn van bawl a deih a, ahi zongin a makaipa in kha khat sung sing nul masa dingin a sawl hi.

records.english: My mother waited three years for my father to come home from working abroad.
records.zomi: Ka nu in ka pa gamdang pan inn a ciah nadingin kum thum a ngak hi.

records.english: Please don't rush the old man; he needs time to count his coins.
records.zomi: Pasal upa manlang sak kei in; a dangka a sim nadingin hun a kisam hi.

records.english: The mango tree my father planted gave its first fruit only after six years.
records.zomi: Ka pa' suan haigah kung in kum guk khit ciangin bek a gah masa a nei hi.

records.english: When the post office queue stretched out of the door, a young man gave his place to an old woman who couldn't stand for long.
records.zomi: Laikhak inn kigual kongkhak pua dong a sau ciangin pasal khangno khat in sawt a ding zo lo numei upa khat kiangah a mun a pia hi.

records.english: My neighbor was told that her leg would heal slowly, so she learned to do everything one step at a time.
records.zomi: Ka inn vengnu a khe zawl takin a dam ding hi, ci-in kihilh ahih manin bangkim kalsuan khat ciat-in a bawl sin hi.

records.english: Can't you wait just five more minutes?
records.zomi: Minit nga beh na ngak thei kei hiam?

records.english: No, I've been waiting for an hour already.
records.zomi: Ngak thei lo ing, nai khat ka ngak khin hi.

records.english: Patience means waiting without losing hope, not simply doing nothing.
records.zomi: Thuakzawhna in lametna mansuah lo-in ngak ci nopna a, bangmah bawl lo bek ci nopna hi lo hi.

records.english: My grandfather taught me to fish when I was eight, and I hated how long it took.
records.zomi: Kum giat ka phak ciangin ka pu in nga man hong sin sak a, a sawt dan ka huat hi.

records.english: Every few minutes I pulled the line out to check it, and every time the fish swam away.
records.zomi: Minit tawmno simin en dingin khau ka la khia a, vei khat ciat-in nga a lei hi.

records.english: By the end of the summer I had learned to sit still, and I caught more fish than my cousins.
records.zomi: Khal a bei ciangin dai takin tu ka sin a, ka sanggamte sangin nga tam zaw ka man hi.

records.english: The best teachers know that some pupils need to hear an explanation many times.
records.zomi: Saya hoih pente in sangnaupang pawl khat in gen siangna vei tampi a zak ding uh a kisam hi, ci a thei uh hi.

records.english: Building trust in a new community takes years, not weeks.
records.zomi: Mipi thak khat sungah muanna lam in kal hi lo-in kum tampi a la hi.

records.english: Rather than pushing her shy son to speak, the teacher waited until he was ready.
records.zomi: A zumthak tapa gen dingin sawl sangin saya in a kiman dong a ngak hi.

records.english: Stop asking, and just wait.
records.zomi: Dong khawl inla, ngak bek in.

records.english: Teaching my son to read took months, but now he reads to his little sister every night.
records.zomi: Ka tapa lai sim sin sak in kha tampi a sawt a, ahi zongin tu-in zan simin a nau numei kiangah a sim sak hi.

records.english: I do want to learn the violin, even if it takes me years.
records.zomi: Kum tampi a sawt zongin violin sin ka deih taktak hi.

records.english: The old woman waited all morning at the clinic without a single complaint.
records.zomi: Numei upa in phunna khat zong om lo-in siavuan inn ah zingsang bup a ngak hi.

records.english: Why do I have to wait for the others?
records.zomi: Bang hangin a dangte ka ngak ding hiam?

records.english: Because we're all going together.
records.zomi: I khempeuh khawm-in i pai ding ahih manin.

records.english: My grandfather never hurried anyone.
records.zomi: Ka pu in kuamah a manlang sak ngei kei hi.

records.english: Wait your turn, please.
records.zomi: Na hun ngak in.

records.english: Why are you always so calm in traffic?
records.zomi: Bang hangin mawtaw kidiahna sungah na lungsim a dai tawntung hiam?

records.english: Getting angry doesn't move the cars any faster.
records.zomi: Heh in mawtaw te a manlang zaw sak kei hi.

records.english: Children, please wait quietly until everyone has finished the test.
records.zomi: Naupangte, mi khempeuh in sitna a zawh dong dai takin ngak un.

records.english: Be patient — the bread needs another ten minutes.
records.zomi: Thuakzawh in — moh in minit sawm beh a kisam hi.

records.english: Would you be able to wait a whole year for something you really wanted?
records.zomi: Na deih taktak thu khat adingin kum khat bup na ngak thei ding hiam?

records.english: How long do we have to wait?
records.zomi: Bangzah sung i ngak ding hiam?

records.english: Until the doctor calls your name.
records.zomi: Siavuan in na min a sam dong.

records.english: Thank you for waiting so patiently.
records.zomi: Thuakzawh taka na ngak manin lungdam ing.

records.english: Patience with other people usually begins with patience with ourselves.
records.zomi: Mi dangte tungah thuakzawhna pen keimah le keimah tungah thuakzawhna tawh a kipan zel hi.

records.english: The bus was late, but nobody complained.
records.zomi: Bus a nun a, ahi zongin kuamah in a phun kei hi.

records.english: Patience is hard when you're hungry.
records.zomi: Na gilkial ciangin thuakzawh a haksa hi.

records.english: Had the farmer waited one more week, his whole harvest would have been ripe.
records.zomi: Lo neipa in kal khat beh a ngak leh a lo bup a min ding hi.

records.english: A patient listener often learns far more than someone who is always ready to speak.
records.zomi: Thuakzawh taka ngaikhia mi khat in gen dingin kiman tawntung mi sangin tam zaw a sin zel hi.

records.english: The seeds need time to grow.
records.zomi: Khaicite a khan nadingin hun a kisam hi.

records.english: In an old story, a farmer was so impatient for his rice to grow that he pulled every seedling a little higher.
records.zomi: Tangthu lui khat ah lo neipa khat in a buh khan nadingin thuakzawh lo lua-in buh kung khempeuh tawmno a la tou hi.

records.english: He went home proud, telling his family that he had helped the plants grow taller in one day.
records.zomi: Ni khat sungin singkungte a sang zaw nadingin ka huh hi, ci-in a innkuan a hilh kawm-in kisaktheih takin inn ah a ciah hi.

records.english: The next morning his son ran to the field and found every seedling lying dead in the sun.
records.zomi: A zing zingsang in a tapa lo ah a tai a, buh kung khempeuh ni sungah a si-in a lum a mu hi.

records.english: The teacher explained the sum five times until every pupil understood it.
records.zomi: Sangnaupang khempeuh in a theih dong saya in kanaan vei nga a gen siang hi.

records.english: Is the rice ready yet?
records.zomi: Buh a min khin hiam?

records.english: Almost, but the water hasn't all gone yet.
records.zomi: Min dek hi, ahi zongin tui a kang bei nai kei hi.

records.english: Why does learning a language take so long?
records.zomi: Bang hangin pau khat sin a sawt mahmah hiam?

records.english: Because your brain needs to hear new words many times before they stay.
records.zomi: Kammal thakte a om den ma-un na lungsim in vei tampi a zak ding a kisam ahih manin.

records.english: Count to ten before you answer.
records.zomi: Na dawn ma-in sawm dong sim in.

records.english: Solar panels change sunlight into electricity.
records.zomi: Solar panel te in ni vak meivak-in a khel hi.

records.english: Food gives our bodies the energy they need to move, grow and stay warm.
records.zomi: An in i taksa kiangah a kalsuan, a khan leh a lum den nadingin a kisap hatna a pia hi.

records.english: Put the ice cubes in the freezer.
records.zomi: Tuikhal tangte khal setna bawk sungah koih in.

records.english: Children, which things in this room do you think are made of metal?
records.zomi: Naupangte, hih inndei sung-a van bang te sik tawh kibawl hi, na ci uh hiam?

records.english: Understanding how energy changes form helps engineers design cleaner ways to power our towns.
records.zomi: Hatna lim a kikhel dan theih in engineer te in i khuapite hatna pia nading lampi siang zaw a geel nadingun a huh hi.

records.english: When you rub your hands together, the movement turns into heat.
records.zomi: Na khut na nul ciangin a kikhoih dan in a lum ah a kikhel hi.

records.english: What kind of energy does a kettle use, and what does it change it into?
records.zomi: Kettle in hatna bang a zang a, bang ah a khel hiam?

records.english: Dry your hands before you touch the switch.
records.zomi: Phongna na khoih ma-in na khut keusak in.

records.english: Light travels faster than anything else we know, at about 300,000 kilometers per second.
records.zomi: Vak pen i theih bangmah dang sangin a manlang zaw a, second khat ah kilometre 300,000 bang a pai hi.

records.english: Can you name three kinds of energy?
records.zomi: Hatna lim thum na gen thei hiam?

records.english: Heat, light and sound.
records.zomi: Lum, vak leh aw.

records.english: The dam uses falling water to turn turbines that produce electricity.
records.zomi: Tui khakna in turbine te a lehhei nadingin a kia tui a zang a, tua in meivak a bawl hi.

records.english: When a candle burns, the wax combines with oxygen and releases heat and light.
records.zomi: Khawimeivaak a kang ciangin a thau in oxygen tawh a kihel a, lum leh vak a suah sak hi.

records.english: Wood floats because it is less dense than water.
records.zomi: Sing pen tui sangin a gik zaw lo ahih manin a dawn hi.

records.english: Hold the magnet near the nail and watch.
records.zomi: Magnet thih-tang kiang ah naih takin len inla, en in.

records.english: A dark shirt feels hotter in the sun than a white one, because it absorbs more light.
records.zomi: Puan-ak vom pen a ngo sangin vak tam zaw a dawp ahih manin ni-in a sa zaw hi.

records.english: Why do we wear wool in winter?
records.zomi: Bang hangin khuavot ciangin wool i silh hiam?

records.english: Wool traps air, which slows down the loss of heat from our bodies.
records.zomi: Wool in huih a kemsak a, tua in i taksa pan lum a mang dan a zawlsak hi.

records.english: Feel how warm the window is in the afternoon.
records.zomi: Sun nung ciangin tukvuang bangzah a lum hiam khoih in.

records.english: Pull the plug out before you touch anything inside the toaster.
records.zomi: Toaster sung-a bangmah na khoih ma-in a sutna phawi in.

records.english: Switch off the light when you leave the room.
records.zomi: Inndei na nusiat ciangin meivak mit in.

records.english: Steam can burn you even more badly than boiling water.
records.zomi: Tui meikhu in tui kik sangin a kangsak zaw thei hi.

records.english: Where does the salt go when you stir it into water?
records.zomi: Tui sungah cii na hel ciangin koi ah a pai hiam?

records.english: A chemical change produces a new substance, while a physical change, such as melting, does not.
records.zomi: Chemical kikhelna in van thak khat a piangsak a, a tuai bang lim kikhelna in a piangsak kei hi.

records.english: Matter is anything that has mass and takes up space.
records.zomi: Matter pen a gik a nei a, mun a luah bangpeuh ahi hi.

records.english: Why does a metal spoon get hot in a cup of tea?
records.zomi: Bang hangin sik sikkeu tea haai khat sungah a sa hiam?

records.english: Metal conducts heat well, so the heat travels up the handle.
records.zomi: Sik in lum a puak hoih ahih manin lum a ciahna dong a pai hi.

records.english: What makes a bulb light up?
records.zomi: Bang in meivak bel a vaksak hiam?

records.english: Electricity flowing through a thin wire inside it, which gets hot enough to glow.
records.zomi: A sung-a khau neu khat tungtawn-in meivak a luang a, tua in a vak dong a sa hi.

records.english: Which melts faster, butter or chocolate?
records.zomi: Bang in manlang zaw-in a tui hiam, butter hiam chocolate hiam?

records.english: Is air really made of matter?
records.zomi: Huih pen matter tawh kibawl taktak hiam?

records.english: Yes, it has mass, even though you can't see it.
records.zomi: Kibawl hi, na muh theih kei hangin a gik a nei hi.

records.english: Is a cloud a solid, a liquid or a gas?
records.zomi: Meipi pen a khauh hiam, a tui hiam, gas hiam?

records.english: Mostly tiny drops of liquid water floating in the air.
records.zomi: A tamzaw huih sungah a leng tui tang neu mahmah te ahi hi.

records.english: Why does a balloon get bigger in the sun?
records.zomi: Bang hangin balloon ni-in a lian zaw hiam?

records.english: The air inside warms up and expands, so it pushes the rubber outwards.
records.zomi: A sung-a huih a lum a, a zau ahih manin rubber pua lam ah a nawt hi.

records.english: The particles in a gas move freely and spread out to fill whatever container they are in.
records.zomi: Gas sung-a particle te suakta takin a vak uh a, a om nading bawm bangpeuh a dimsak dingin a kithehthang uh hi.

records.english: Sugar dissolves faster in hot water than in cold water.
records.zomi: Thei khum tui vot sangin tui lum sungah manlang zaw-in a tui hi.

records.english: When fuels such as coal and oil are burned, energy stored over millions of years is released in minutes.
records.zomi: Suangtaang leh sathau bang meisuang hal ciangin kum za tul tampi sung kikoih hatna minit tawmno sungin a suak hi.

records.english: No machine is perfectly efficient, because some energy is always lost as heat or sound.
records.zomi: Set khat zong a kicing kei hi, hatna pawl khat lum hiam aw bangin a mang tawntung ahih manin.

records.english: Everything around us, from rocks to people, is made of tiny particles called atoms.
records.zomi: Suang pan mihing dong i kiim-a bangkim atom kici particle neu mahmah te tawh kibawl hi.

records.english: A wind turbine changes the energy of moving air into electricity.
records.zomi: Huih turbine in huih kikhem' hatna meivak-in a khel hi.

records.english: Our class weighed a closed bottle of water before and after freezing it, and the mass stayed the same.
records.zomi: I kilasi in tui bel kikhak khat a khal ma leh a khal khit i teh a, a gik a kibang den hi.

records.english: Ice melts when it gets warm.
records.zomi: Tuikhal a lum ciangin a tui hi.

records.english: Rust forms when iron reacts with oxygen and water over time.
records.zomi: Hun sawt sungin sik in oxygen leh tui tawh a kituak ciangin sik ziaui a piang hi.

records.english: Scientists measure energy in joules, although food labels often use calories.
records.zomi: Science siamte in hatna joule tawh a teh uh a, an laimaite in calorie a zang zel uh hi.

records.english: Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius at sea level.
records.zomi: Tuipi zah ah tui degree Celsius 100 ciangin a kik hi.

records.english: Does a stone weigh more in air or in water?
records.zomi: Suang khat huih sungah hiam tui sungah hiam a gik zaw hiam?

records.english: In air, because the water pushes it up a little.
records.zomi: Huih sungah, tui in tawmno a dawi tou ahih manin.

records.english: Water expands when it freezes, which is why pipes can burst in very cold weather.
records.zomi: Tui a khal ciangin a zau ahih manin vot mahmah huihkhua ah tui khuamte a puak thei hi.

records.english: A ball at the top of a hill has stored energy, which becomes movement as it rolls down.
records.zomi: Mual tung-a bawl khat in hatna kikoih a nei a, a liam kiak ciangin kalsuan ah a kikhel hi.

records.english: Insulating a house keeps heat in during winter and out during summer, which saves both money and energy.
records.zomi: Inn khat khuh in khuavot ciangin lum a kem a, khal ciangin lum a khak a, tua in sum leh hatna a khol hi.

records.english: Our teacher put an ice cube, a glass of water and a steaming kettle on the desk.
records.zomi: I saya in dawhkan tungah tuikhal tang khat, tui haai khat leh meikhu suak kettle khat a koih hi.

records.english: She explained that all three were the same substance, water, in its solid, liquid and gas forms.
records.zomi: A thum in van kibang, tui, a khauh, a tui leh gas lim-in ahi hi, ci-in a gen siang hi.

records.english: Then she asked us to predict what would happen to the ice cube by the end of the lesson.
records.zomi: Tua ciangin sinna tawp ciangin tuikhal tang bang a suak ding hiam ngaihsun dingin hong ngen hi.

records.english: Energy can't be created or destroyed, only changed from one form to another.
records.zomi: Hatna bawl theih hiam susiat theih lo a, lim khat pan lim dang ah khel theih bek hi.

records.english: When a car brakes, its movement energy doesn't vanish; it turns into heat in the brakes.
records.zomi: Mawtaw khat in brake a nek ciangin a kalsuan hatna a mang kei a, brake te sungah lum ah a kikhel hi.

records.english: A battery stores chemical energy and turns it into electrical energy.
records.zomi: Battery khat in chemical hatna a kem a, meivak hatna ah a khel hi.

records.english: Why do engineers leave small gaps between the sections of a long bridge?
records.zomi: Bang hangin engineer te in lei sau khat' khen te kikal ah a awng neu a nusia uh hiam?

records.english: A pressure cooker raises the boiling point of water, so food cooks more quickly.
records.zomi: Pressure cooker in tui a kik nading lum zah a khangsak ahih manin an manlang zaw-in a min hi.

records.english: Ask before you take anything new.
records.zomi: Zatui thak na nek ma-in dong in.

records.english: Older people who take many medicines are more likely to suffer harmful combinations, so careful records matter.
records.zomi: Zatui tampi a ne upate in a sia kihelnate a thuak baih zaw uh ahih manin limtaka ciamteh a thupi hi.

records.english: Sharing antibiotics with family members can make infections harder to treat in the future.
records.zomi: Innkuan mite tawh antibiotic hawm in ma lam ah natna dawi a haksa zaw sak thei hi.

records.english: Clear labels in the patient's own language reduce the risk of mistakes at home.
records.zomi: Damlo' pau tawh laimai kician te in inn ah khialhna a kiamsak hi.

records.english: Keeping medicines in their original packaging means the instructions and expiry date are always at hand.
records.zomi: Zatuite a kipatna bawm sungah kem in thuhilhna leh a hun bei ni na kiang ah a om tawntung hi.

records.english: Medicine for children is often measured with a special spoon or syringe, not a kitchen spoon.
records.zomi: Naupangte' zatui an huanna sikkeu tawh hi lo-in sikkeu tuam hiam zatui sunna tawh kiteh zel hi.

records.english: The pharmacy called to warn us that a batch of cough syrup had been recalled.
records.zomi: Zatui dawl in khuh zatui tui khat kila kik hi, ci-in hong kidopsak dingin hong sam hi.

records.english: Close the lid tightly.
records.zomi: Khuhna khauh takin khak in.

records.english: My mother counts her tablets every Sunday.
records.zomi: Ka nu in Nipini simin a zatuite a sim hi.

records.english: Check the name on the box.
records.zomi: Bawm tung-a min en in.

records.english: The nurse checked my name and date of birth before she gave me the injection.
records.zomi: Nurse in zatui hong sun ma-in ka min leh ka suahni a en hi.

records.english: Is it safe to take these tablets with my usual painkillers?
records.zomi: Hih zatuite ka ngeina natna zatui tawh nek a bit hiam?

records.english: Ask the pharmacist, because some combinations can cause problems.
records.zomi: Zatui zuakpa dong in, kihelna pawl khat in buaina a piangsak thei ahih manin.

records.english: Hospitals use wristbands and double checks so that patients receive the right medicine.
records.zomi: Siavuan inn te in damlote in zatui dik a ngah nadingun khut khihna leh nihvei enna a zang uh hi.

records.english: The child-resistant caps are hard for my grandfather to open, so the pharmacy gave him easier ones.
records.zomi: Naupang in a hon thei lo khuhnate ka pu in a hon zo kei ahih manin zatui dawl in a baih zaw a pia hi.

records.english: Leaving tablets in a hot car can damage them, so carry them in your bag instead.
records.zomi: Mawtaw lum sungah zatui nusia in a siatsak thei ahih manin na ip sungah tawi zaw in.

records.english: Never give your own tablets to someone else, even if their symptoms seem the same.
records.zomi: Natna lim kibang bang a hih zongin nangmah' zatui mi dang pia ngei kei in.

records.english: Could you write the instructions in larger letters for my father?
records.zomi: Ka pa adingin thuhilhnate laimal lian zaw-in na gelh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Please read the leaflet before you take the first dose.
records.zomi: Zatui masa na nek ma-in laimai sim in.

records.english: Put the tablets back in the box.
records.zomi: Zatuite bawm sungah koih kik in.

records.english: My father keeps a list of all his medicines in his wallet, in case of an emergency.
records.zomi: Haksatna hun a om kha leh ci-in ka pa in a zatui khempeuh list a sum ip sungah a kem hi.

records.english: Who looks after Grandpa's tablets?
records.zomi: Pu' zatuite kua in a kem hiam?

records.english: His daughter, because she lives next door.
records.zomi: A tanu, a kiang inn ah a teen ahih manin.

records.english: My grandmother uses a box with a section for each day of the week.
records.zomi: Ka pi in kal sung ni khat ciat adingin khenna nei bawm khat a zang hi.

records.english: A regular review of all a patient's medicines can reveal ones that are no longer needed.
records.zomi: Damlo khat' zatui khempeuh a tawntung-a en kik in a kisap nawn loh te a lak thei hi.

records.english: Take your medicines in their original boxes when you travel, with a copy of your prescription.
records.zomi: Na khualzin ciangin na zatuite a kipatna bawm sungah na siavuan zatui gelhna copy khat tawh tawi in.

records.english: Keep all medicines in a locked cupboard, out of children's reach.
records.zomi: Zatui khempeuh naupangte' tun theih loh kikhak van bawm sungah kem in.

records.english: Medicines bought online from unknown sellers may be fake or unsafe.
records.zomi: Theih loh zuakte pan online-a lei zatuite a zuau hiam a bit lo kha thei hi.

records.english: Last year my two-year-old nephew climbed onto a chair and reached the medicine shelf.
records.zomi: Kum nung in kum nih ka tanau tutphah tungah a kah a, zatui dawh a tun hi.

records.english: Luckily his mother found him before he had opened anything, but the whole family was shaken.
records.zomi: Vangphat takin bangmah a hon ma-in a nu in a mu a, ahi zongin innkuan bup a lau uh hi.

records.english: The next day we moved every medicine in the house into a locked box on top of the wardrobe.
records.zomi: A zing ciangin inn sung-a zatui khempeuh puan bawm tung-a kikhak bawm khat sungah i suan hi.

records.english: Can I crush this tablet for my mother?
records.zomi: Ka nu adingin hih zatui ka nen thei ding hiam?

records.english: Not this one, but I can give you a liquid version.
records.zomi: Hih pen thei lo hi, ahi zongin a tui khat kong pia thei hi.

records.english: Students, never take any pill that a friend offers you, however harmless it looks.

records.zomi: Muakna kician khat in kumpi khualte a kituak a, ahi zongin lawm luite adingin a khauh bang-in a kisa thei hi.

records.english: Would your parents rather stay in a hotel or in our spare room?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa in zinbuuk ah hiam i inndei awng ah hiam om a deih zaw ding uh hiam?

records.english: The spare room, because they'd rather see the children in the morning than have a bigger bed.
records.zomi: Inndei awng, lupna lian zaw sangin zingsang ciangin naupangte muh a deih zaw ding uh ahih manin.

records.english: The view from the balcony is the best thing about our flat.
records.zomi: Inn dawh pan muh ding pen i inn-a a hoih pen ahi hi.

records.english: Hosting relatives for a week is very different from hosting a colleague for one evening.
records.zomi: Kal khat sung sanggamte muak pen nitak khat sung nasep pih khat muak tawh a kibang lo mahmah hi.

records.english: A visitor who arrives tired needs a quiet evening more than a big welcome party.
records.zomi: A tawl-a tung khual khat in muakna pawi lian sangin nitak dai khat a kisam zaw hi.

records.english: Over-planning a visit can be as uncomfortable for guests as having nothing to do.
records.zomi: Khual pai khat geel lua in bangmah sep ding om lo bangin khualte adingin a nuam lo thei hi.

records.english: Asking guests what they would like to do works better than guessing.
records.zomi: Khualte kiangah bang bawl a deih uh hiam dot pen ngaihsun-in gen sangin a sem hoih zaw hi.

records.english: Homemade bread on the table says more than an expensive cake from a shop.
records.zomi: Dawhkan tung-a inn-a bawl moh in dawl pan cake man tam khat sangin tam zaw a gen hi.

records.english: Is it better to offer visitors tea first or a full meal?
records.zomi: Khualte tea masa-in pia a hoih zaw hiam, an kicing masa-in pia a hoih zaw hiam?

records.english: Tea first, because most people want to rest before they eat.
records.zomi: Tea masa, mi tamzaw in a nek ma-un tawldam a deih uh ahih manin.

records.english: My mother would rather give up her own bed than let a guest sleep badly.
records.zomi: Ka nu in khual khat ihmut hoih lo ding sangin amah' lupna a nusia zaw ding hi.

records.english: Guests feel most at home when they're free to make their own tea.
records.zomi: Khualte in amau' tea a bawl thei uh ciangin inn bangin a kisa pen uh hi.

records.english: I'd rather cook at home than take them to a restaurant.
records.zomi: An zuakna inn ah paipih sangin inn ah an huan ka deih zaw hi.

records.english: Which day suits your parents best for a visit?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa adingin ni bang in a hong nadingun a kituak pen hiam?

records.english: Saturday, because the roads are quieter.
records.zomi: Kiginni, lampite a dai zaw ahih manin.

records.english: Welcoming one guest is easier than welcoming a whole group, but a group brings more laughter.
records.zomi: Khual khat muak pen pawl bup muak sangin a baih zaw a, ahi zongin pawl in nuihzaakna tam zaw a tawi hi.

records.english: Welcoming visitors in winter takes more preparation than in summer, because of the extra blankets and heating.
records.zomi: Puannak behlap leh meilum hangin khuavot ciangin khualte muak in khal sangin kiman tam zaw a kisam hi.

records.english: Do you think guests notice clean towels more than a tidy kitchen?
records.zomi: Khualte in an huanna siang sangin puan keusakna siang a mu zaw uh hi, na ci hiam?

records.english: A host who admits that the house is simple often puts visitors more at ease than one who apologizes all evening.
records.zomi: Inn a baih hi, ci-a pom inn neipa khat in nitak bup maisak ngen pa sangin khualte' lungsim a nemsak zaw zel hi.

records.english: A simple meal is fine.
records.zomi: An baih khat a hoih hi.

records.english: You won't fill every hour of their visit this time, will you?
records.zomi: Tu vei a hong veh uh nai khempeuh na dimsak lo ding hi, a hi hiam?

records.english: No, I've learned my lesson from last time.
records.zomi: Dimsak lo ding ing, a nunung vei pan ka sin khin hi.

records.english: Who in your family is best at making visitors laugh?
records.zomi: Na innkuan sungah kua in khualte nuisak a siam pen hiam?

records.english: Our neighbors welcome guests more formally than we do, with everyone standing at the door.
records.zomi: I inn vengte in mi khempeuh kongkhak ah ding-in eite sangin kician zaw-in khualte a muak uh hi.

records.english: Children often welcome guests more naturally than adults, because they simply ask them to play.
records.zomi: Naupangte in khualte kimawl dingin a sam bek uh ahih manin upate sangin a ngeina takin a muak zel uh hi.

records.english: Welcoming visitors with the whole village present is impressive, but a quiet family meal may feel warmer to a shy guest.
records.zomi: Khua bup om-in khualte muak in a lamdang huai a, ahi zongin zumthak khual khat adingin innkuan an dai khat in a lum zaw kha thei hi.

records.english: Business visitors expect a clear plan, whereas relatives usually prefer a relaxed day.
records.zomi: Sumbawl khualte in geelna kician a lamen uh a, sanggamte in ni nuam khat a deih zaw zel uh hi.

records.english: My grandmother is the most welcoming person I know, even when she has very little to offer.
records.zomi: Bangmah tawmno bek a neih zongin ka pi pen ka theih mi lak ah a muak siam pen ahi hi.

records.english: Is it true that Jesus got tired and hungry like us?
records.zomi: Jesu eite bangin a tawl a, a gilkial hi, cih a tak hiam?

records.english: Yes, the Gospels describe him being hungry, sleeping in a boat and weeping at a friend's grave.
records.zomi: Tak hi, Lungdamna Thu laibute in a gilkial, tembaw sungah a ihmut leh lawm khat' han ah a kap thu a gen hi.

records.english: Christians believe that Mary was the mother of Jesus.
records.zomi: Khristiante in Mari pen Jesu' nu ahi hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: Our youth group discussed what it means for God to experience childhood.
records.zomi: I khangno pawl in Pasian in naupan lai a tuah cih in bang a ci nopna hiam a kikum uh hi.

records.english: Our church gives food to poor families every Christmas.
records.zomi: I pawlpi in Christmas simin innkuan zawngte an a pia hi.

records.english: For many believers, the Incarnation means that the body and everyday life are not unimportant to God.
records.zomi: Upmi tampi adingin Pasian mihing a suahna in taksa leh ni sim nuntak Pasian adingin a thupi lo kei hi, ci nopna hi.

records.english: The children made a star for the top of the nativity scene.
records.zomi: Naupangte in Jesu suahna lim tung pen adingin aksi khat a bawl uh hi.

records.english: Some theologians say the Incarnation shows that God draws near to people rather than waiting for them to climb up to him.
records.zomi: Pasian thu siam pawl khat in Pasian mihing a suahna in Pasian in mite a kiangah a kah tou ding a ngak sangin mite kiangah a hong naih hi, ci a lak hi, a ci uh hi.

records.english: How does your church prepare for Christmas during Advent?
records.zomi: Advent sungin na pawlpi in Christmas adingin bangci-in a kiman hiam?

records.english: What do you love most about Christmas?
records.zomi: Christmas ah bang na it pen hiam?

records.english: Singing carols with the whole village by candlelight.
records.zomi: Khawimeivaak vak tawh khua bup tawh Christmas la sak.

records.english: John's Gospel opens by saying that the one who was with God from the beginning became a human being and lived among us.
records.zomi: Johan Lungdamna Thu in a kipatna pan Pasian tawh a om pa mihing a suak a, eite lak ah a om hi, ci-in a kipan hi.

records.english: Which part of the Christmas story moves you the most?
records.zomi: Christmas tangthu sung-a bang khen in na lungsim a khoih pen hiam?

records.english: Believing that God became human raises deep questions that Christians have reflected on for two thousand years.
records.zomi: Pasian mihing a suak hi, ci-a um in Khristiante in kum tul nih sung a ngaihsut uh dotna thuk te a piangsak hi.

records.english: Children, why do you think God chose to be born in a simple stable?
records.zomi: Naupangte, bang hangin Pasian in bawng inn baih khat ah piang dingin a teel hi, na ci uh hiam?

records.english: What would Christmas be like without the story of the birth?
records.zomi: Suahna tangthu om lo-in Christmas bangci om ding hiam?

records.english: Many churches celebrate Christmas on 25 December, while some Orthodox churches celebrate it in January.
records.zomi: Pawlpi tampi in December ni 25 ciangin Christmas a bawl uh a, Orthodox pawlpi pawl khat in January kha in a bawl uh hi.

records.english: At the Christmas service, our pastor held up a newborn baby from the congregation.
records.zomi: Christmas kikhopna ah i pastor in pawlpi sung pan naungek piang thak khat a lap hi.

records.english: She said that Christians believe God came into the world as helpless as this child.
records.zomi: Khristiante in Pasian hih naupang bangin a kikem zo lo-in leitung ah a hong hi, ci-in a um uh hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Nobody in the church moved, and even the noisy children went quiet for a moment.
records.zomi: Pawlpi sungah kuamah a kikhem kei uh a, a ngaih naupangte zong hun tawmno sung a dai uh hi.

records.english: Where was Jesus born?
records.zomi: Jesu koi ah a suak hiam?

records.english: In Bethlehem, according to the Gospels.
records.zomi: Lungdamna Thu laibute in a gen bangin, Bethlehem khua ah.

records.english: Why did Mary and Joseph travel to Bethlehem?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Mari leh Josef Bethlehem ah a pai uh hiam?

records.english: Luke's Gospel says that a census made everyone register in their family's town.
records.zomi: Luka Lungdamna Thu in mi khempeuh kisim dingin a innkuan khua ciatah a pai uh hi, ci-in a gen hi.

records.english: Who visited the baby Jesus?
records.zomi: Naungek Jesu kua in a veh hiam?

records.english: Shepherds from the fields, and later wise men from the east.
records.zomi: Gam lak pan tuucingte, a khit ciangin nisuahna lam pan mipilte.

records.english: Christians believe that Jesus was fully God and fully human at the same time.
records.zomi: Khristiante in Jesu pen hun kibang ah Pasian kicing leh mihing kicing ahi hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: My son is playing a shepherd in the play this year.
records.zomi: Kum in ka tapa in lamdang lakna sungah tuucing khat a lai hi.

records.english: Every Christmas, my father reads the birth story aloud from his old Bible.
records.zomi: Christmas simin ka pa in a Laisiangtho lui pan suahna tangthu ging takin a sim hi.

records.english: My grandmother says the Christmas story shows that God cares for poor and ordinary people.
records.zomi: Ka pi in Christmas tangthu in Pasian in mi zawngte leh mi ngeina te a ngaihsut hi, ci a lak hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Light the candle for the first Sunday of Advent.
records.zomi: Advent Nipini masa pen adingin khawimeivaak tawh tak in.

records.english: The Gospels say that Jesus was born in Bethlehem and laid in a manger.
records.zomi: Lungdamna Thu laibute in Jesu Bethlehem ah a suak a, bawng ankuang sungah a kikoih hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Many Christians believe that because Jesus shared human life, he can understand human weakness.
records.zomi: Khristian tampi in Jesu in mihing nuntakna a thuak khawm ahih manin mihing thanemna a thei thei hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: Christmas carols often express the wonder that the creator of the world was born as a baby.
records.zomi: Christmas la tampi in leitung bawlpa naungek-in a suak hi, cih lamdanna a gen zel hi.

records.english: The angels' message to the shepherds was one of good news and great joy.
records.zomi: Vantung mite in tuucingte kiangah a gen uh thu pen thu hoih leh nakpi nuamna thu ahi hi.

records.english: Early church leaders argued for centuries about how Jesus could be both God and man.
records.zomi: Pawlpi makaipi masate in Jesu bangci-in Pasian leh mihing a hih thei hiam kum za tampi sung a kinial uh hi.

records.english: Why do Christians insist that Jesus was truly human, not just appearing to be?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Khristiante in Jesu mihing bang bek-a kilang hi lo-in mihing tak ahi hi, ci-in a ciamteh uh hiam?

records.english: The humility of a birth in a stable contrasts sharply with the power that people expected from a king.
records.zomi: Bawng inn-a suahna niamkhiatna in kumpipa khat pan mite in a lamen uh vangliatna tawh a kibang lo mahmah hi.

records.english: Artists over many centuries have painted the nativity in the clothes and landscapes of their own countries.
records.zomi: Kum za tampi sung lim gelhmite in Jesu suahna pen amau gam puansilh leh gam lim tawh a gelh uh hi.

records.english: For Christians, a child born in poverty became the turning point of human history.
records.zomi: Khristiante adingin zawngkhal sungah a suak naungek khat mihing tangthu kheelna a suak hi.

records.english: The doctrine of the Incarnation is central to most Christian traditions, although they explain it in different ways.
records.zomi: Pasian mihing a suahna thuhilhna pen Khristian ngeina tamzaw-a lai ahi a, ahi zongin a kibang lo lampi tawh a genteh uh hi.

records.english: The Incarnation is sometimes described as a mystery, meaning something to be wondered at rather than fully explained.
records.zomi: Pasian mihing a suahna pen thuguk khat ci-in a kigen zel a, a kicing-in genteh thei hi lo, lamdang sak ding thu khat cihna ahi hi.

records.english: Why do some churches put a nativity scene at the front during Advent?
records.zomi: Bang hangin pawlpi pawl khat in Advent sungin a mai lam ah Jesu suahna lim a koih uh hiam?

records.english: It helps the congregation, especially the children, picture the birth of Jesus as they prepare for Christmas.
records.zomi: Christmas a kiman laitakun pawlpi, a diak in naupangte, in Jesu suahna a lungsim sungah a muh nading uh a huh hi.

records.english: Was Jesus ever a child who had to learn things?
records.zomi: Jesu zong thu sin kisam naupang khat a hi ngei hiam?

records.english: Luke's Gospel says that he grew in wisdom as he grew older.
records.zomi: Luka Lungdamna Thu in a khang semsem ciangin lungpilna tawh a khang hi, ci-in a gen hi.

records.english: Please sit quietly during the Christmas reading.
records.zomi: Christmas thu simna sungin dai takin tu un.

records.english: Our pastor reminded us that Christmas is about God's gift, not about the gifts under the tree.
records.zomi: I pastor in Christmas pen Pasian' letsong thu ahi a, sing nuai-a letsongte thu hi lo hi, ci-in hong phawksak hi.

records.english: What do Christians mean by the Incarnation?
records.zomi: Khristiante in Pasian mihing a suahna in bang a ci nopna uh hiam?

records.english: That God took on a human body and a human life in Jesus.
records.zomi: Pasian in Jesu sungah mihing pumpi leh mihing nuntakna a la hi, cihna.

records.english: Many Christians find comfort in believing that God knows human pain from the inside.
records.zomi: Khristian tampi in Pasian in mihing natna sung pan a thei hi, ci-a um in lungmuanna a ngah uh hi.

records.english: The youngest children wear tea towels on their heads to play the shepherds.
records.zomi: Naupang a neu pente in tuucingte a lai nadingun a lu tungah puan neu a khu uh hi.

records.english: In 451, a council of church leaders at Chalcedon stated that Jesus is one person with two natures.
records.zomi: Kum 451 in Chalcedon ah pawlpi makaipi kikhopna khat in Jesu pen ahihna nih nei mi khat ahi hi, ci-in a pulak hi.

records.english: The name Emmanuel, given to Jesus in Matthew's Gospel, is explained there as meaning "God with us".
records.zomi: Matthai Lungdamna Thu ah Jesu tung-a kipia Emmanuel min pen "Eite tawh Pasian hong om khawm hi" cihna ahi hi, ci-in tua ah a kigenteh hi.

records.english: Do you light candles at home during Advent?
records.zomi: Advent sungin inn ah khawimeivaak na tak uh hiam?

records.english: We sing carols on Christmas Eve.
records.zomi: Christmas zan masa in Christmas la i sa uh hi.

records.english: Our children act out the story of the shepherds and the angels every December.
records.zomi: I naupangte in December simin tuucingte leh vantung mite tangthu a lak uh hi.

records.english: This belief is called the Incarnation.
records.zomi: Hih upna pen Pasian mihing a suahna ci-in kisam hi.

records.english: Christians believe that God became a human being in Jesus.
records.zomi: Khristiante in Pasian Jesu sungah mihing a suak hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: Christmas celebrates the birth of Jesus.
records.zomi: Christmas in Jesu' suahna a phawk hi.

records.english: If a guest arrives during a meal, we add another plate rather than asking them to wait.
records.zomi: An a nek laitakun khual khat a hong tun leh ngak dingin ngen sangin kuang khat i behlap hi.

records.english: Is there enough food for everyone?
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh adingin an a tam ding hiam?

records.english: There's always enough, because the neighbors are bringing more.
records.zomi: A tam tawntung hi, inn vengte in tam zaw a tawi uh ahih manin.

records.english: Take some of these bananas home with you.
records.zomi: Hih banhla pawl khat na inn ah tawi in.

records.english: My grandmother keeps a pot of rice warm all evening in case someone drops by.
records.zomi: Kuamah a hong lut kha leh ci-in ka pi in nitak bup an beel khat a lumsak den hi.

records.english: Who's staying with us this week?
records.zomi: Hih kal sungin kua in eite tawh a om ding hiam?

records.english: Your uncle's friend from the hills.
records.zomi: Na pa neu' lawm, mualtung pan.

records.english: Give the guest the softest blanket.
records.zomi: Khual kiangah puannak nem pen pia in.

records.english: Come back whenever you like.
records.zomi: Na deih ciangin hong pai kik in.

records.english: Who will walk our guest to the bus?
records.zomi: Kua in i khual bus dinna dong a paipih ding hiam?

records.english: My brother will, because he's going that way.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in, tua lam ah a pai ding ahih manin.

records.english: When a stranger's motorbike broke down outside our village, my father invited him to stay the night.
records.zomi: I khua pua ah mikhual khat' motor neu a siat ciangin ka pa in zan khat a giak dingin a sam hi.

records.english: My mother cooked a chicken that she had been saving for Sunday, and the children gave up their mats.
records.zomi: Ka nu in Nipini adingin a koih a ak khat a huan a, naupangte in amau' phakte a pia uh hi.

records.english: Years later, the stranger came back with his own family to thank us, and he still visits every harvest.
records.zomi: Kum tampi khit ciangin, tua mikhual pen kong lungdam ci dingin a innkuan tawh a hong kik a, lo at hun simin a hong veh lai hi.

records.english: Sit here, in the best place.
records.zomi: Hih ah tu in, mun hoih pen ah.

records.english: Guests are always given the best seat, even if it's the only chair in the house.
records.zomi: Inn sung-a tutphah khat bek om zongin, khualte in tutna hoih pen a ngah tawntung uh hi.

records.english: Thank you for looking after us so well.
records.zomi: Hong kem hoih mahmah na hi, ka lungdam hi.

records.english: Hospitality in our villages often depends on neighbors, because no single family could feed so many guests alone.
records.zomi: I khuate-a zindo pen inn vengte tungah a kinga zel hi, innkuan khat bek in khual tampi a vak zo lo ding ahih manin.

records.english: Did the visitors enjoy their stay?
records.zomi: Khualte in a om lai uh a nuam sa uh hiam?

records.english: They said they felt like part of the family.
records.zomi: Innkuan sung mi bangin kisa ung, a ci uh hi.

records.english: Our neighbors lent us extra mats and blankets when twenty relatives came for the funeral.
records.zomi: Mithi vuina ah sanggam mi sawmnih a hong ciangin i inn vengte in phak leh puannak behlap hong pia uh hi.

records.english: When a guest leaves, my mother walks with them to the end of the path.
records.zomi: Khual khat a pai ciangin ka nu in lampi tawp dong a paipih hi.

records.english: The way a family treats a stranger was once seen as a measure of its honor.
records.zomi: Innkuan khat in mikhual khat a bawl dan pen a zahtak huaina tehna ahi hi, ci-in kisa ngei hi.

records.english: In my family, the host eats last, after making sure every guest has had enough.
records.zomi: Ka innkuan ah inn neipa in khual khempeuh in a vak kicing uh hi, ci a theih khit ciangin a nunung pen-in a ne hi.

records.english: Is the guest room ready?
records.zomi: Khual inndei a kiman khin hiam?

records.english: My father taught us to offer water to anyone who comes to the door, even a salesman.
records.zomi: Ka pa in kongkhak ah a hong peuhpeuh, van zuakpa zong, tui pia dingin hong hilh hi.

records.english: My mother sends every visitor home with a jar of her pickles.
records.zomi: Ka nu in a hong veh mi khempeuh a anlum bel khat tawh a inn uh ah a ciahsak hi.

records.english: Our door is always open to travelers.
records.zomi: I kongkhak khualzinte adingin a hong tawntung hi.

records.english: My father would rather borrow rice from a neighbor than let a guest leave without a proper meal.
records.zomi: Ka pa in khual khat an kicing nek lo-in pai sak sangin inn veng khat kiang pan buh a puk zaw ding hi.

records.english: I do want my children to learn to welcome strangers the way my parents did.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa' bawl bangin ka tate in mikhualte a muak siam nadingun ka deih mahmah hi.

records.english: Many families abroad keep these customs, even in small flats with no spare room.
records.zomi: Gamdang ah innkuan tampi in inndei awng om lo inn neute sungah zong hih ngeinate a zui lai uh hi.

records.english: In our village, no traveler is turned away when night is falling.
records.zomi: I khua ah zan a hong tun ciangin khualzin kuamah kiang kik sak lo hi.

records.english: A guest who praises the food sincerely gives the host more pleasure than any gift.
records.zomi: An a thanghuai hi, ci-a lungsim takpi tawh a phat khual in inn neipa letsong bangpeuh sangin a lungdamsak zaw hi.

records.english: Children, make sure every guest has a cup before you sit down.
records.zomi: Naupangte, na tut ma-un khual khempeuh in haai a nei uh hiam en un.

records.english: We always cook extra on Sundays, because someone usually turns up unexpectedly.
records.zomi: Nipini simin an behlap i huan tawntung hi, kuamah lamen loh-in a hong zel ahih manin.

records.english: Please don't wash your own plate; our guests never do the washing up.
records.zomi: Na kuang na sil lo ding hi; i khualte in kuang a sil ngei kei uh hi.

records.english: Bring the visitor some water.
records.zomi: Khual kiangah tui tawi in.

records.english: A guest's arrival is announced to the neighbors, who often come by to greet them.
records.zomi: Khual khat a tun ciangin inn vengte kiangah kigen a, amau in hopih dingin a hong zel uh hi.

records.english: Some younger people find the old customs tiring, yet most still feel proud when guests leave happy.
records.zomi: Khangno pawl khat in ngeina luite a tawlsak sa uh a, ahi zongin a tamzaw in khualte a lungdam-a a pai ciangin a kisaktheih lai uh hi.

records.english: Families who move abroad sometimes find that their custom of welcoming unexpected visitors surprises their new neighbors.
records.zomi: Gamdang ah a pai innkuante in khual a lamen loh muak ngeina uh in a inn veng thakte a lamdangsak zel hi, ci-in a mu uh hi.

records.english: Is it rude to refuse food when you visit a family here?
records.zomi: Hih ah innkuan khat na veh ciangin an nial pen zahtak lohna ahi hiam?

records.english: It's better to accept a little, even if you've just eaten.
records.zomi: Tu-in na ne khin zongin tawmno la in, tua a hoih zaw hi.

records.english: Visitors are often surprised that nobody expects payment for food or a place to sleep.
records.zomi: An hiam ihmut nading mun hiam adingin kuamah in sum a lamen lo uh ahih manin khualte a lamdang sa zel uh hi.

records.english: In our community, hospitality has always been seen as a duty as well as a pleasure.
records.zomi: I khua ah zindo pen nuamna bek hi lo-in sepding khat zong ahi hi, ci-in kisa tawntung hi.

records.english: Why does your family cook so much when visitors come?
records.zomi: Bang hangin khualte a hong ciangin na innkuan in an tam mahmah a huan uh hiam?

records.english: In our community, it would be shameful if a guest went home hungry.
records.zomi: I khua ah khual khat a gilkial-in a inn ah a ciah leh a zumhuai ding hi.

records.english: When relatives arrive from the city, neighbors bring vegetables and eggs to help feed them.
records.zomi: Khuapi pan sanggamte a hong ciangin inn vengte in amaute vak nading huh dingin anteh leh aktui a tawi uh hi.

records.english: A widow in our village was praised by everyone for looking after a sick traveler for a week.

records.zomi: Naupangte in kammal sangin gil na hiam heh tawh a lungkhamna uh a lak zel uh hi.

records.english: I feel calmer after a long walk.
records.zomi: Pai sau khat khit ciangin ka lungsim a nem zaw hi.

records.english: Stress gave me headaches every afternoon last winter.
records.zomi: Phalbi nunung in lungkhamna in nitak lam simin lu hong nasak hi.

records.english: Taking short breaks during a long day helps me work better, not worse.
records.zomi: Ni sau khat sungin tawldamna tomte la in a sia zaw hi lo-in a hoih zaw-in nasep dingin hong huh hi.

records.english: Please ask for help when you need it.
records.zomi: Na kisam ciangin huhna ngen in.

records.english: Who can I talk to about this?
records.zomi: Hih thu kua tawh ka kikum thei ding hiam?

records.english: The school counselor, or any teacher you trust.
records.zomi: Sang-a lungsim huh siam, hiam na muan saya kuapeuh.

records.english: My brother is under a lot of pressure at university.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal sangpi ah lungkhamna tampi a thuak hi.

records.english: Are you sleeping all right?

records.english: Not really, I keep waking at three.

records.english: Stress is a normal reaction to pressure, but when it continues for months it deserves attention.
records.zomi: Lungkhamna pen gimna tungtawn-a pumpi ngeina dawnna ahi a, ahi zongin kha tampi a om leh limtak ngaihsut kisam hi.

records.english: Exams always make my son anxious, so we plan his revision together.
records.zomi: Sitna in ka tapa a lungkhamsak tawntung ahih manin a sinna kik a khawm-in i geel uh hi.

records.english: What would help you most right now, time off or someone to share the work with?
records.zomi: Tu-in bang in hong huh pen ding hiam, tawlngak hun hiam, nasep hawm pih ding mi khat hiam?

records.english: Long-term stress can affect both physical and mental health, according to many doctors.
records.zomi: Siavuan tampi' gen bangin hun sawt lungkhamna in pumpi damna leh lungsim damna a khoih thei hi.

records.english: Burnout often develops slowly, so friends and colleagues may notice it before the person does.
records.zomi: Gimluatna pen dawngdawng-in a khang zel ahih manin lawmte leh nasep pihte in amah sangin a phawk masa kha thei uh hi.

records.english: My boss told me to take a few days off.
records.zomi: Ka makaipa in ni tawmno tawlngak dingin hong hilh hi.

records.english: Caring for my mother every day has left my father exhausted and stressed.
records.zomi: Ni simin ka nu kem in ka pa a gim mahmah sak a, a lungkhamsak hi.

records.english: How can I support a friend who is too stressed to see anyone?
records.zomi: Kuamah muh nuam lo dingin a lungkham lua lawm khat bangci-in ka huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Keep inviting her, even if she says no, so that she knows the door is open.
records.zomi: Nial zongin sam den in, kongkhak a hong hi, a theih nadingin.

records.english: I do want to talk to someone, but I don't know whether a counselor would understand my situation.
records.zomi: Mi khat tawh kikum ka nuam taktak a, ahi zongin lungsim huh siam khat in ka om dan a thei thei ding hiam ka thei kei hi.

records.english: Reducing stress sometimes means changing the situation, not only learning to cope with it.
records.zomi: Lungkhamna neusak pen thuak siam sin bek hi lo-in a om dan kheel cihna zong a hi zel hi.

records.english: Did the counselor help?
records.zomi: Lungsim huh siam in hong huh hiam?

records.english: Yes, just talking to someone outside the family made a big difference.

records.english: Last year my sister worked such long hours that she stopped sleeping properly and lost her appetite.
records.zomi: Kum nunung in ka sanggam numei in hun sau mahmah nasep a sep ahih manin a ihmut hoih nawn lo a, an a ne nuam nawn kei hi.

records.english: Her doctor said the symptoms were probably caused by stress and suggested she talk to a counselor.
records.zomi: A siavuan in a natna limte lungkhamna hang ahi kha thei hi, ci-in lungsim huh siam khat tawh kikum dingin a hilh hi.

records.english: After a few months of sessions and a lighter workload, she felt like herself again.

records.english: Students, please tell someone if exam pressure is affecting your sleep or your health.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte, sitna gimna in na ihmut hiam na damna hiam a khoih leh kuapeuh kiangah gen un.

records.english: Had my uncle spoken to his doctor sooner, he might not have needed so much time off work.

records.english: Why do some people hide their stress from their families?
records.zomi: Bang hangin mi pawl khat in a lungkhamna uh a innkuan uh kiangah a sel uh hiam?

records.english: Many don't want to seem weak or to worry the people they love.
records.zomi: Tampi in hatlo bangin a kilang nuam kei uh a, a it mite uh a lunghimawhsak nuam kei uh hi.

records.english: Switch your phone off after dinner.

records.english: Talk to your manager if your workload has become too heavy.

records.english: My neighbor joined a support group for people caring for relatives with dementia.
records.zomi: Ka inn veng in dementia nei sanggamte kemte adingin huhna pawl khat ah a kihel hi.

records.english: My doctor asked me how many hours I was working and whether I was taking any breaks.
records.zomi: Ka siavuan in nai bangzah nasep ka sem hiam, tawldamna ka la hiam ci-in hong dong hi.

records.english: Is your job very stressful?
records.zomi: Na nasep a lungkhamhuai mahmah hiam?

records.english: Only at the end of each month.

records.english: I've been feeling very stressed at work lately.

records.english: Why did you change your mind about the car?

records.zomi: Mawtaw bawlsiam pa in zuakpa in a gen loh a nuai lam-a sik ngaw a mu hi.

records.english: Is there a deadline for the decision?

records.english: Can you help me choose between these two jobs?
records.zomi: Hih nasep nih lak ah teel dingin hong huh thei ding na hi hiam?

records.zomi: Na adingin bang in a thupi pen hiam hong gen in, tua pan i kipan ding hi.

records.english: Is it better to decide quickly or to wait for more information?
records.zomi: Manlang takin thukhen a hoih zaw hiam, thu tam zaw ngak a hoih zaw hiam?

records.english: It depends on how much you could lose by waiting.
records.zomi: Ngak in bangzah na mansuah thei hiam tungah a kinga hi.

records.english: Should I sleep on it before I sign the contract?
records.zomi: Thukham lai ka at ma-in zan khat ka ngaihsun phot ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, and read it again in the morning when you're less tired.
records.zomi: Hi, zingsang ciangin na tawl tawm zawh ciangin sim kik in.

records.zomi: Ni simin bang huan ding na hi hiam bangci-in na thukhen hiam?

records.english: I look in the fridge and use whatever is closest to its date.
records.zomi: Khal bawm sung ka en a, a ni tawp nai pen ka zang hi.

records.english: Did you regret your decision to leave the city?
records.zomi: Khuapi nusia dingin na thukhenna na sikkik hiam?

records.english: Only in the first winter, when the village felt very quiet.
records.zomi: Phalbi masa pen bek, khua a dai mahmah lai-in.

records.english: Why do some people find even small decisions exhausting?
records.zomi: Bang hangin mi pawl khat in thukhenna neute zong a gimsak uh hiam?

records.english: Perhaps because they worry so much about choosing wrongly that every option feels risky.

records.english: How long did it take you to decide to get married?

records.zomi: Minit sawm bang, tua khit ciangin mopawi adingin sum khawl dingin kum nih.

records.english: Was it your decision to move schools, or your parents'?
records.zomi: Sang kheel pen nangma' thukhenna hiam, na nu leh na pa' thukhenna hiam?

records.english: Has the committee reached a decision about the new hall?

records.english: Not yet, because half the members want to repair the old one instead.

records.english: Who decided to paint the kitchen green?

records.english: Which one did you pick in the end?

records.english: The blue one, because it was cheaper.
records.zomi: A dum pen, a man neu zaw ahih manin.

records.english: Do you need more time to think?
records.zomi: Ngaihsut dingin hun tam zaw na kisam hiam?

records.english: What would you advise someone who can never make up their mind?
records.zomi: A lungsim thu khen zo ngei lo mi khat bang hong hilh ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Choose a small decision, make it quickly, and notice that nothing terrible happens.
records.zomi: Thukhenna neu khat teel in, manlang takin bawl in, bangmah lauhuai a pian loh phawk in.

records.english: What made you decide to become a nurse?
records.zomi: Bang in nurse hih dingin thu hong khensak hiam?

records.english: Watching the nurse who looked after my grandfather.
records.zomi: Ka pu a kem nurse ka et ahih manin.

records.english: Do you think people make better decisions in groups or alone?
records.zomi: Mite in pawl tawh hiam amau kia hiam thukhenna hoih zaw a bawl uh hi, na ci hiam?

records.english: In groups for practical problems, but alone for personal ones, in my experience.
records.zomi: Ka theih dan in nasep lam buaina adingin pawl tawh, ahi zongin mimal thu adingin kia.

records.english: Would you have made the same choice if you'd known about the extra costs?

records.english: When my uncle was offered a job in another country, he couldn't decide whether to take it.

records.english: In the end, he asked himself which choice he would regret more in ten years, and he stayed.

records.english: Could you tell me how the council decides which roads to repair first?
records.zomi: Khuapi vaihawm in bang lampite bawlpha masa ding hiam bangci-in thu a khen hiam hong gen thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: How did you decide where to live?
records.zomi: Koi ah teeng dingin bangci-in thu na khen hiam?

records.english: We chose the town with the best school for our children.
records.zomi: I tate adingin sang hoih pen nei khuapi i teel uh hi.

records.english: Is it wise to make important decisions when you're angry?

records.english: Is it fair to let children make decisions about their own schooling?
records.zomi: Naupangte amau' sangkahna tungtang thu khen sak a dik hiam?

records.english: Shall we toss a coin?
records.zomi: Sum i khiatsak ding hiam?

records.english: What helps you make a difficult decision?
records.zomi: Thukhenna haksa khat bawl dingin bang in hong huh hiam?

records.english: Writing down the advantages and disadvantages of each choice.
records.zomi: Teelna khatciat' phattuamna leh a hoih lohna gelh.

records.english: Did the family decide together where Grandma would live?
records.zomi: Pi koi ah om ding hiam innkuan in a khawm-in thu a khen uh hiam?

records.english: Yes, and Grandma had the final word, as she should.
records.zomi: Hi, a om ding bangin Pi in thu nunung a gen hi.

records.english: When do you need an answer?
records.zomi: Dawnna bang ciangin na kisam hiam?

records.english: By the end of the week, if possible.

records.english: Have you made up your mind?
records.zomi: Na lungsim thu na khen khin hiam?

records.english: Do you usually trust your first feeling, or do you think things through?
records.zomi: Na kisak masa na muang zel hiam, thu limtak na ngaihsun zel hiam?

records.zomi: Thu limtak ka ngaihsun a, ahi zongin ka kisak masa a dik zel hi.

records.english: Have you decided which course to take?
records.zomi: Bang sinna la ding hiam na khen khin hiam?

records.english: Not yet, but I have to choose by Friday.

records.english: So you'd like us to spend Christmas with your parents and New Year with mine, is that right?

records.english: I wish we'd chosen a name that teachers could spell more easily.

records.english: We agreed on one sweet after dinner, not two, didn't we?
records.zomi: Nitak an khit ciangin a khum khat bek, nih hi lo, ci-in i kithei uh hi, hi lo hiam?

records.english: What a relief that we both picked the same name!
records.zomi: Min kibang i nih in i teel uh ahih manin lungmuanhuai hi mah e!

records.english: Which is worse, a baby who won't sleep or a teenager who won't wake up?

records.english: I'd rather my children learned to lose gracefully than won every game.
records.zomi: Ka tate in kimawlna khempeuh a zawh sangin zahtak takin a lel siam a sin uh ka deih zaw hi.

records.english: Which cake would you like for your birthday, chocolate or lemon?

records.english: Which do you find harder, the baby years or the teenage years?

records.english: The teenage years, because a cuddle no longer fixes their problems.

records.english: Is it better to tell children the truth about a family problem or to protect them from it?

records.english: Tell them the truth, in words that suit their age.
records.zomi: A tak gen in, a kum uh tawh kituak kammal tawh.

records.english: A long engagement gave us time to save for a house, although my mother would have preferred a wedding within months.
records.zomi: Kiteen ciamna sawt in inn khat adingin sum khawl hun hong pia a, ka nu in kha tawmno sung mopawi a deih zaw ding hi.

records.english: Who's the stricter parent in your house?
records.zomi: Na inn ah kua in a khauh zaw nu hiam pa hiam ahi hiam?

records.english: My wife, though the children would say it's me.
records.zomi: Ka zi, naupangte in kei hi, a ci ding uh hangin.

records.english: Is it better to have children close together or a few years apart?
records.zomi: Ta kinai takin hiam kum tawmno kikal-in hiam nei a hoih zaw hiam?

records.english: Thanks, but I'd rather not have a party for our anniversary this year.

records.english: The baby seems happier in the sling than in the pram, doesn't she?

records.english: Our second child is far calmer than our first, though we're not sure whether that's him or us.

records.english: When our first baby was on the way, my husband wanted to buy everything new, while I wanted to borrow from friends.

records.english: In the end, we bought a new car seat and borrowed almost everything else.

records.english: Two years later, the borrowed clothes have been handed on to a third family, while the expensive car seat sits in the garage waiting for a second baby.

records.english: I'm afraid we have to choose between your cousin's wedding and my nephew's christening, because they're on the same day.

records.english: A cheap present can make a child just as happy as an expensive one, as our son proved with a cardboard box.

records.english: Do you bathe the children in the morning or at night?
records.zomi: Naupangte zingsang ciangin hiam zan ciangin hiam na kisilsak hiam?

records.english: At night, because it calms them down before bed.
records.zomi: Zan ciangin, a ihmut ma-un a lungsim uh a nemsak ahih manin.

records.english: Raising children with two languages at home takes more effort than raising them with one, but ours already translate for their grandparents.

records.english: Pick the story you want, and Daddy will read it to you.
records.zomi: Na deih tangthu teel in, Pa in hong simsak ding hi.

records.zomi: Kiteenna ah bang in a thupi zaw hiam, deihna kibang hiam, manphatna kibang hiam?

records.english: Shared values, because interests can change over the years.
records.zomi: Manphatna kibang, deihnate kum sung a kikheel thei ahih manin.

records.english: Twins are twice the work and twice the fun!

records.english: Thanks to the baby monitor, we can sit in the garden while she naps instead of staying upstairs.

records.english: Some couples keep their money separate and others share everything, but we have a joint account for the house and our own accounts for everything else.

records.english: Everyone, would you prefer to eat in the garden or in the hall after the christening?

records.english: Our son looks like me but laughs like his father.
records.zomi: I tapa in kei bang a kilawm a, ahi zongin a pa bangin a nui hi.

records.english: Just to be clear, are we choosing the school near the house or the one with the bigger library?

records.english: Is it fairer to give all the children the same pocket money, or to give the older ones more?
records.zomi: Naupang khempeuh zat sum kibang piak a dik zaw hiam, a upa zawte tam zaw piak a dik zaw hiam?

records.english: We would sooner live near my parents and have their help than stay in the city and pay for childcare.
