records.zomi: Online form in a lang ah hong khiatkhia ahih manin ka kipan kik kisam hi.

records.english: Wait until the family has told everyone before you post about the baby.
records.zomi: Naungek tungtang na post ma-in innkuan in mi khempeuh kiangah a gen dong ngak in.

records.english: Please take down the photo of me at the party.
records.zomi: Pawi-a ka lim pen hong lakhia in.

records.english: Read the whole article before you share it.
records.zomi: Na hawm ma-in thugelh bup sim in.

records.english: That picture is from 2015, not from last week's storm!
records.zomi: Tua lim pen kum 2015 pan ahi a, kal nunung-a huihpi pan hi lo hi!

records.english: Old photos are sometimes passed around as if they were new, which is why checking the date matters.
records.zomi: Lim luite a thak bangin a kihawm zel ahih manin ni en a thupi hi.

records.english: Could you check whether this charity is real before we donate?
records.zomi: I piak ma-in hih huhna pawl a tak hiam na en thei ding hiam?

records.english: Just to check, is it all right if I share the recording with the whole class?
records.zomi: Ka en kik nadingin, class bup kiangah ka record hawm leh a hoih hiam?

records.english: My uncle forwarded a health tip to the whole family, but our doctor said it was wrong.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in damna thu khat innkuan bup kiangah a khak a, ahi zongin i siavuan in a khial hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Sharing someone's good news before they've had a chance to announce it can spoil a moment that belonged to them.
records.zomi: Mi khat in a lungdamna thu a gen ma-in hawm in amaute' hun khat a susia thei hi.

records.english: The school asked parents not to post videos of the concert, because some families don't want their children online.
records.zomi: Sang in nu leh pate kiangah concert video post lo dingin a ngen a, innkuan pawl khat in a tate online ah om a deih kei uh ahih manin.

records.english: Thanks for telling me the post was fake.
records.zomi: Post pen a zuau hi, hong ci na hih manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: Content made by artificial intelligence should be clearly labelled, so that viewers aren't misled about what is real.
records.zomi: AI in a bawl te kician takin ciamteh kisam hi, a etmite in bang a tak hiam a khial lo nadingun.

records.english: Quoting someone out of context can make them seem to say the opposite of what they meant.
records.zomi: Mi khat' kammal a kiang thu tawh kizom lo-in gen in a gen nopna tawh a kalh bangin a kilang sak thei hi.

records.english: Is this news true?
records.zomi: Hih thu a tak hiam?

records.english: Is this picture real, or was it made by a computer?
records.zomi: Hih lim a tak hiam, computer in a bawl hiam?

records.english: It was made with an AI app, and it says so in the corner.
records.zomi: AI app khat tawh kibawl a, a ningkawm ah tua bangin a gen hi.

records.english: When you share a song or a video, mention who made it.
records.zomi: La hiam video hiam na hawm ciangin kua in a bawl hiam gen in.

records.english: Ask your sister before you post her news.
records.zomi: Na sanggam numei' thu na post ma-in amah dong in.

records.english: Don't post photos of an accident.
records.zomi: Accident lim post kei in.

records.english: I deleted the post as soon as my friend told me she was upset by it.
records.zomi: Ka lawm in a lungsim a natsak hi, hong ci pah ciangin post ka phiat hi.

records.english: Before I share a warning about a scam, I look for it on the bank's official website.
records.zomi: Khemna tungtang lauhuai thu ka hawm ma-in bank' website taktak tungah ka zong hi.

records.english: Where did you hear that?
records.zomi: Koi pan na za hiam?

records.english: In the family chat, but I haven't checked it yet.
records.zomi: Innkuan chat ah, ahi zongin ka en nai kei hi.

records.english: There seems to be a problem with your post, because the photo shows our street name and house number.
records.zomi: Na post tungah buaina khat om bang hi, lim in i lampi min leh inn nambat a lak hi.

records.english: News about a missing person should come from the family or the police, not from rumors.
records.zomi: Mi mangthang tungtang thu pen innkuan hiam palik pan hong pai ding a, thu zuau pan hi lo ding hi.

records.english: The video was shared without the teacher's permission, and the school made the student remove it.
records.zomi: Video pen saya' phalna om lo-in kihawm a, sang in sangnaupang in a phiat dingin a sawl hi.

records.english: Posting a photo of a relative in hospital may comfort the family, but it can also expose the patient at a vulnerable time.
records.zomi: Siavuan inn-a om sanggam khat' lim post in innkuan a hehnem thei a, ahi zongin a hatlo laitakin damlo a kilangsak thei hi.

records.english: Can I share your photo on my page?
records.zomi: Na lim ka page tungah ka hawm thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, but please don't tag me.
records.zomi: Thei hi, ahi zongin hong tag kei in.

records.english: Thank goodness you checked first!
records.zomi: Na en masa ahih manin lungdamhuai hi mah e!

records.english: Please don't screenshot my private messages and send them to other people.
records.zomi: Ka guk thu khakte screenshot la-in mi dangte kiangah khak kei in.

records.english: This is a private group, so don't share anything outside it.
records.zomi: Hih pen guk pawl ahih manin a pua lam ah bangmah hawm kei in.

records.english: Is it ever right to share a video of a stranger behaving badly in public?
records.zomi: Mipi lak-a hoih lo-a gamta mikhual khat' video hawm a dik ngei hiam?

records.english: Did you take this photo yourself?
records.zomi: Hih lim nangmah in na la hiam?

records.english: No, my cousin did, so I've added her name.
records.zomi: Hi lo, ka sanggam numei in a la a, tua ahih manin a min ka behlap hi.

records.english: Who sent you this?
records.zomi: Kua in hih hong khak hiam?

records.english: Even a well-meant post can cause harm if it reveals where a vulnerable person is staying.
records.zomi: Lungsim hoih tawh post zong in a hatlo mi khat a omna a lak leh siatna a piangsak thei hi.

records.english: Don't forward a message just because a friend sent it.
records.zomi: Lawm khat in hong khak hi, ci bek-in thu khak khat khak kik kei in.

records.english: Right, I'd better go and fix that post before more people see it.
records.zomi: Hoih hi, mi tam zawte in a muh ma-un tua post va bawlpha zaw ning.

records.english: Had I read past the headline, I wouldn't have shared an article that said something quite different.
records.zomi: Thupi min bek sim lo-in ka sim leh thu dang mahmah gen thugelh khat ka hawm lo ding hi.

records.english: My son asked me before posting a picture of his little sister, which made me proud.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in a nau numei lim a post ma-in hong dong a, tua in hong kisaktheih sak hi.

records.english: A joke article was shared as real news, and some people believed it.
records.zomi: Nuihzaak thugelh khat thu tak bangin kihawm a, mi pawl khat in a um uh hi.

records.english: The more often a false story is repeated, the more familiar and believable it seems.
records.zomi: Tangthu zuau khat a kigen kik tam semsem leh a theih ngei bang leh a upmawh semsem bangin a kilang hi.

records.english: Responsible sharing means asking not only whether something is true, but also whether it's kind and necessary.
records.zomi: Mawhpuakna nei hawmna in a tak hiam cih bek hi lo-in a hoih hiam, a kisam hiam cih zong dong cihna ahi hi.

records.english: During an emergency, passing on unconfirmed reports can cause more panic than the event itself.
records.zomi: Lauhuai hun khat sungin a kiciamteh lo thute khak kik in a piang tak sangin lauhuaina tam zaw a piangsak thei hi.

records.english: Report harmful videos instead of sharing them to complain about them.
records.zomi: Video hoih lo te a phun nadingin hawm sangin report in.

records.english: I never share photos of my friends' children.
records.zomi: Ka lawmte' tate lim ka hawm ngei kei hi.

records.english: If you find out you've shared something false, post a correction instead of just deleting it.
records.zomi: Thu zuau khat na hawm hi, ci na theih leh phiat bek lo-in a dik post in.

records.english: In our family group, nobody forwards a message unless they can say where it came from.
records.zomi: I innkuan pawl ah koi pan hong pai hiam a gen thei kei leh kuamah in thu khak a khak kik kei uh hi.

records.english: So you're saying I should ask everyone in the photo, not just my best friend?
records.zomi: Tua ahih leh ka lawm hoih pen bek hi lo-in lim sung-a mi khempeuh ka dong ding hi, na ci hiam?

records.english: Do you think it's okay to share a picture of someone if their face doesn't show?
records.zomi: A mai a kilang kei leh mi khat lim hawm a hoih hi, na ci hiam?

records.english: It's better to ask anyway, because people can recognize clothes and places.
records.zomi: Bang hi zongin dong a hoih zaw hi, mite in puan leh munte a thei thei uh ahih manin.

records.english: You checked the link before you shared it, didn't you?
records.zomi: Na hawm ma-in link na en hi, hi lo hiam?

records.english: I'm afraid I can't share your fundraiser until I know who will receive the money.
records.zomi: Sum kua in a ngah ding hiam ka theih ma-in na sum kaikhawmna ka hawm thei kei hi, ci ka lau hi.

records.english: Please don't share my phone number in the group.
records.zomi: Pawl sungah ka phone nambat hawm kei in.

records.english: Parents who teach children to pause before sharing are giving them a habit that will protect them for life.
records.zomi: Naupangte hawm ma-a ngak dingin a hilh nu leh pate in a nuntak sung hong kem ding ngeina khat a pia uh hi.

records.english: Sorry, I shared that video before I checked it.
records.zomi: Maisak in, tua video ka en ma-in ka hawm hi.

records.english: How can I tell if a picture has been changed?
records.zomi: Lim khat a kikheel hiam bangci-in ka thei thei ding hiam?

records.english: Search for it online and see where it first appeared.
records.zomi: Online ah zong inla, koi ah a kilang masa hiam en in.

records.english: Children, ask me before you share anything online.
records.zomi: Naupangte, online ah bangmah na hawm ma-un hong dong un.

records.english: Read Mark 2 with your partner, and find the man who was let down through the roof.
records.zomi: Na lawm tawh Marka 2 sim inla, innkhum pan a kikhiasuk pa zong in.

records.english: In the garden of Gethsemane, the Gospels say, Jesus prayed in great distress before his arrest.
records.zomi: Lungdamna Thu laibute in a gen bangin, Gethsemani huan ah Jesu in a kiman ma-in si dek takin a dah-in thu a ngen hi.

records.english: Who were Jesus' parents?
records.zomi: Jesu' nu leh pa kua te ahi hiam?

records.english: Mary was his mother, and Joseph raised him as his son.
records.zomi: Mari pen a nu ahi a, Josef in a tapa bangin a khoi hi.

records.english: Christians call Jesus "Lord" in their prayers.
records.zomi: Khristiante in a thungetna uh ah Jesu pen "Topa" ci-in a sam uh hi.

records.english: Was Jesus a real person?
records.zomi: Jesu pen mi taktak khat ahi hiam?

records.english: Most historians agree that he lived in Galilee in the first century.
records.zomi: Tangthu siam a tamzaw in kum za khatna in Galile gam ah a nungta hi, ci-in a kipom uh hi.

records.english: In all four Gospels, Jesus drives the traders out of the temple courts.
records.zomi: Lungdamna Thu laibu li-a khempeuh ah Jesu in sumbawlte biakinn huang sung pan a hawlkhia hi.

records.english: Our pastor preached about the night Jesus prayed in the garden.
records.zomi: I pastor in Jesu huan sungah thu a nget zan thu a gen hi.

records.english: Theologians have long warned against stressing Christ's divinity so much that his real human life is forgotten.
records.zomi: Pasian thu siamte in Khazih' Pasian hihna ciamteh lua in a mihing nuntak taktak a mangngilh sak ding a kidop sak sawt mahmah khin uh hi.

records.english: Why did people call Jesus "Teacher"?
records.zomi: Bang hangin mite in Jesu pen "Sia" ci-in a sam uh hiam?

records.english: Because he taught crowds, and his followers learned from him like students.
records.zomi: Mihonpite a hilh a, a nungzuite in sangnaupangte bangin a kiang pan a sin uh ahih manin.

records.english: Is Jesus God?
records.zomi: Jesu pen Pasian ahi hiam?

records.english: Most Christians believe so, and many churches say it in their creed every Sunday.
records.zomi: Khristian a tamzaw in tua bangin a um uh a, pawlpi tampi in Nipini simin a upna gen uh sungah a gen uh hi.

records.english: Many Christians say that Jesus' habit of praying shows how much he relied on his Father.
records.zomi: Khristian tampi in Jesu' thu ngen ngeina in a Pa tungah bangzah a kinga hiam a lak hi, a ci uh hi.

records.english: Sorry, I can't answer that question tonight, but we can look at it together next week.
records.zomi: Maisak in, tu zan-in tua dotna ka dawng thei kei hi, ahi zongin a zom kal ah i khawm-in i en thei ding hi.

records.english: John's Gospel records that Jesus said he was thirsty while he was on the cross.
records.zomi: Johan Lungdamna Thu in Jesu in singlamteh tungah a om laitakin "Tui ka duh hi" a ci hi, ci-in a ciamteh hi.

records.english: When my daughter heard that Jesus was a carpenter, she asked whether he ever hurt his thumb.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in Jesu pen khutsiampa ahi hi, ci a zak ciangin a khutpi a liam ngei hiam ci-in a dong hi.

records.english: My son asked whether Jesus ever got sick.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in Jesu a damlo ngei hiam ci-in a dong hi.

records.english: Our youth leader asked us to list the moments in Mark's Gospel when Jesus shows strong feelings.
records.zomi: I khangno makaipa in Marka Lungdamna Thu sungah Jesu in lungsim hat a lak hunte gelh dingin hong ngen hi.

records.english: So you're saying that Christians see Jesus as completely human and completely divine, not half of each?
records.zomi: Tua ahih leh Khristiante in Jesu pen mihing kicing leh Pasian kicing in a mu uh a, khatciat a lang hi lo hi, na ci hiam?

records.english: After Jesus calmed the storm, the disciples asked each other who this man could be.
records.zomi: Jesu in huihpi a nemsak khit ciangin nungzuite in "Hihpa in bangci mi ahi hiam?" ci-in a kidong uh hi.

records.english: Did Jesus go to school?
records.zomi: Jesu in sang a kah ngei hiam?

records.english: We aren't told, but Luke says that he read from the Scriptures in the synagogue.
records.zomi: Kigen kei hi, ahi zongin Luka in kikhopna inn ah Laisiangtho a sim hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Jesus went to weddings and dinners with his friends.
records.zomi: Jesu in a lawmte tawh mopawi leh nitak an ah a pai hi.

records.english: The accounts in which the risen Jesus eats and is touched are read by many Christians as showing that his risen body was real.
records.zomi: A thokik Jesu in an a nek leh kikhoih tangthute pen Khristian tampi in a thokik pumpi a tak hi, a lakna in a sim uh hi.

records.english: Many Christians read Jesus' words "before Abraham was, I am" as a claim that he existed before he was born.
records.zomi: Khristian tampi in Jesu' "Abraham pian ma in ka om khin hi" cih kammal pen a suah ma-in a om khin hi, cih a pulakna in a sim uh hi.

records.english: Children, draw a picture of Jesus working in a carpenter's shop.
records.zomi: Naupangte, khutsiampa' nasepna inn ah Jesu nasep lim gelh un.

records.english: Children often find it easier to imagine Jesus as a friend than as the eternal Son of God, and good teachers make room for both.
records.zomi: Naupangte in Jesu pen tawntung Pasian Tapa sangin lawm khat bangin ngaihsut a baih sa zaw zel uh a, sayate hoih in a nih adingin mun a pia uh hi.

records.english: Jesus had close friends, such as Martha, Mary and Lazarus.
records.zomi: Jesu in Martha, Mari leh Lazaras bang lawm nai a nei hi.

records.english: If Jesus were only a good teacher, many Christians argue, his claims to forgive sins would be hard to explain.
records.zomi: Jesu pen saya hoih khat bek hi leh mawhna a maisak thei hi, a cihnate genteh haksa ding hi, ci-in Khristian tampi in a gen uh hi.

records.english: Paul's letter to the Philippians describes Christ as one who did not cling to equality with God but took the form of a servant.
records.zomi: Paul in Philippi mite kiangah a gelh lai in Khazih pen Pasian tawh kibatna a khah lo-in sila lim a la hi, ci-in a gen hi.

records.english: Jesus was a Jewish man from Galilee.
records.zomi: Jesu pen Galile gam pan Judah mi khat ahi hi.

records.english: Jesus often called himself "the Son of Man", a title that Christians link to a vision in the book of Daniel.
records.zomi: Jesu in amah le amah "Mihing Tapa" ci-in a kisam zel a, tua min pen Khristiante in Daniel laibu-a mangmuhna khat tawh a kizopsak uh hi.

records.english: What language did Jesus speak?
records.zomi: Jesu in bang pau a zang hiam?

records.english: Most scholars think he spoke Aramaic, the everyday language of Galilee.
records.zomi: Thu siam a tamzaw in Galile gam-a ni sim pau Aramaic a zang hi, ci-in a ngaihsun uh hi.

records.english: Muslims honor Jesus as a great prophet, but they do not believe that he is divine.
records.zomi: Muslimte in Jesu pen kamsang lian khat ahi hi, ci-in a zahtak uh a, ahi zongin Pasian ahi hi, ci-in a um kei uh hi.

records.english: The Nicene Creed calls Jesus "true God from true God."
records.zomi: Nicene Creed in Jesu pen "Pasian tak pan Pasian tak" ci-in a sam hi.

records.english: Christians believe in one God, so they don't think of Jesus as a second god alongside the Father.
records.zomi: Khristiante in Pasian khat a um uh ahih manin Jesu pen Pa kiang-a Pasian nihna khat bangin a ngaihsun kei uh hi.

records.english: Open your Bibles to John 20.
records.zomi: Na Laisiangtho uh Johan 20 ah hong un.

records.english: The Gospels present a Jesus who knows thirst and distress, yet who also forgives sins and calms the sea.
records.zomi: Lungdamna Thu laibute in tui duh leh dahna thei, ahi zongin mawhna maisak-a tuipi a nemsak Jesu khat a lak uh hi.

records.english: Again and again, Matthew and Mark say that Jesus felt compassion when he saw crowds of people in need.
records.zomi: Matthai leh Marka in Jesu in mi kisam mihonpite a muh ciangin hehpihhuai a sa hi, ci-in vei tampi a gen uh hi.

records.english: Believers often find that the humanity of Jesus makes him approachable, while his divinity gives them confidence to trust him.
records.zomi: Upmite in Jesu' mihing hihna in amah a naih theih sak a, a Pasian hihna in amah muan nading muanna a pia hi, ci-in a mu zel uh hi.

records.english: Thank you for explaining that so clearly!
records.zomi: Kician takin na genteh manin ka lungdam hi!

records.english: Many children's songs say that Jesus is their friend.
records.zomi: Naupang la tampi in Jesu pen ka lawm ahi hi, a ci uh hi.

records.english: When Jesus asked his disciples who they thought he was, Peter answered that he was the Messiah.
records.zomi: Jesu in a nungzuite kiangah kua ka hi hiam a dot ciangin Piter in Khazih na hi hi, ci-in a dawng hi.

records.english: In our church, we say the Nicene Creed together every Sunday.
records.zomi: I pawlpi ah Nipini simin Nicene Creed a khawm-in i gen uh hi.

records.english: Jesus called God "Father" when he prayed, didn't he?
records.zomi: Jesu in thu a nget ciangin Pasian pen "Pa" ci-in a sam hi, hi lo hiam?

records.english: Some readers find the cry from the cross, "My God, why have you forsaken me?", the most human moment in the Gospels.
records.zomi: Simmi pawl khat in singlamteh tung pan "Ka Pasian Ka Pasian aw! bang hangin hong taisan na hi hiam?" cih kikona pen Lungdamna Thu laibute sung-a mihing bang pen hun ahi hi, ci-in a mu uh hi.

records.english: What do Christians mean when they call Jesus the Son of God?
records.zomi: Khristiante in Jesu pen Pasian Tapa a cih uh ciangin bang a ci nopna uh hiam?

records.english: That he shares God's nature and has a unique relationship with the Father.
records.zomi: Pasian' ahihna a nei khawm a, Pa tawh kizopna tuam khat a nei hi, cihna.

records.english: When some teachers heard Jesus forgive a paralyzed man's sins, they asked who but God could forgive sins.
records.zomi: Sayate pawl khat in Jesu in khut leh khe si mi khat' mawhnate a maisak a zak ciangin Pasian longal kua in mawhna a maisak thei hiam ci-in a dong uh hi.

records.english: Did Jesus have a job?
records.zomi: Jesu in nasep a nei hiam?

records.english: Mark's Gospel calls him a carpenter, and Matthew calls him the carpenter's son.
records.zomi: Marka Lungdamna Thu in khutsiampa ci-in a sam a, Matthai in khutsiampa tapa ci-in a sam hi.

records.english: The Letter to the Hebrews says that Jesus was tested in every way as we are, yet without sin.
records.zomi: Hebru mite kiang lai in Jesu pen eite thuak mah bangin ze-etna namcin a thuak a, ahi zongin mawhna om lo hi, ci-in a gen hi.

records.english: In John's Gospel, Thomas calls the risen Jesus "My Lord and my God."
records.zomi: Johan Lungdamna Thu ah Thomas in a thokik Jesu pen "Ka Topa leh ka Pasian aw" ci-in a sam hi.

records.english: Why do Christians pray to Jesus?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Khristiante in Jesu kiangah thu a ngen uh hiam?

records.english: Because they believe that he is God's Son and that he is alive today.
records.zomi: Amah pen Pasian Tapa ahi a, tuni-in a nungta hi, ci-in a um uh ahih manin.

records.english: Did Jesus ever laugh?
records.zomi: Jesu a nui ngei hiam?

records.english: The Gospels don't say, but many readers imagine that he did at weddings and meals.
records.zomi: Lungdamna Thu laibute in a gen kei uh hi, ahi zongin simmi tampi in mopawi leh an nekna ah a nui hi, ci-in a ngaihsun uh hi.

records.english: Tact and honesty sometimes pull in opposite directions, and good family conversations need a little of both.
records.zomi: Pilna tawh genna leh thuman pen a kikalh lam ah a kaai zel uh a, innkuan kihona hoih in a nih tawmno ciat a kisam hi.

records.english: Both of you are right in a way.
records.zomi: Na nih in lam khat ah na dik uh hi.

records.english: I'd choose a long talk over a short argument.
records.zomi: Kinialna tom khat sangin kihona sau khat ka teel zaw ding hi.

records.english: Is it better to say sorry first, even when you're not the only one at fault?
records.zomi: Khialhna nei khat bek na hih kei zongin maisak ngen masa a hoih zaw hiam?

records.english: Is your aunt a better listener than your mother?
records.zomi: Na ni pen na nu sangin a ngaihkhia siam zaw hiam?

records.english: Giving children a real choice between two options teaches them more than letting them choose anything at all.
records.zomi: Naupangte kiangah teel ding nih lak ah teelna taktak piak in bangpeuh teel sak sangin tam zaw a sinsak hi.

records.english: We don't have to decide tonight.
records.zomi: Tu zan-in thu i khen kisam kei hi.

records.english: Asking each person what they'd choose, and why, took longer than voting, but nobody felt ignored.
records.zomi: Mi khatciat kiangah bang teel ding hiam, bang hang hiam dot in teel sangin hun sawt zaw a la a, ahi zongin kuamah in a kipaaimawh sa kei uh hi.

records.english: It's often wiser to ask what someone is afraid of than to argue about what they've said.
records.zomi: Mi khat in a gen thu kinial sangin bang a lau hiam dot a pil zaw zel hi.

records.english: Nobody in our family is good at saying sorry, but my little brother is the best of us.
records.zomi: I innkuan sungah kuamah in maisak ngen a siam kei uh a, ahi zongin ka nau pasal pen i lak uh ah a siam pen ahi hi.

records.english: A family that can disagree openly is often closer than one where nobody dares to disagree at all.
records.zomi: Kilang takin a kikalh thei innkuan khat pen kuamah in kikalh ding a hangsan loh innkuan sangin a kinai zaw zel hi.

records.english: Given the choice, would you keep the peace or speak your mind?
records.zomi: Teelna na neih leh daina na kem ding hiam, na lungsim thu na gen ding hiam?

records.english: So you'd prefer us to ask you before inviting your cousins, rather than after?

records.english: Only if you don't understand a question, not for the answers.
records.zomi: Dotna khat na theih kei leh bek, dawnna adingin hi lo.

records.english: Had I asked my colleagues sooner, I would have finished the report in half the time.
records.zomi: Ka nasep pihte ka dong ngal leh report pen hun a lang sungin ka zo ding hi.

records.english: Who do you usually ask when your computer stops working?
records.zomi: Na computer a sep khawl ciangin kua na dong zel hiam?

records.english: My nephew, who fixes everything for the price of a meal.
records.zomi: Ka tanau, an khat man tawh khempeuh a bawlpha pa.

records.english: Is it a sign of weakness to ask for help?
records.zomi: Huhna ngen pen hatlohna lakna ahi hiam?

records.english: Most people think the opposite, because it shows you know your limits.
records.zomi: Mi tamzaw in a kalh lam a ngaihsun uh hi, na zawh zah na thei hi, a lak ahih manin.

records.english: Could you check my letter before I send it, if you have time?
records.zomi: Hun na neih leh ka khak ma-in ka lai hong en sak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: I'd be glad to, if you can wait until lunchtime.
records.zomi: Sun an hun dong na ngak thei leh, lungdam takin.

records.english: Some people refuse every offer of help, not out of pride but because accepting would mean admitting how hard things have become.
records.zomi: Mi pawl khat in huhna kipia khempeuh a nial uh hi, kiphatsakna hang hi lo-in a pom leh thu a bangzah haksa hiam a pulak bang ahih manin.

records.english: Is anyone free to help me set up the chairs?
records.zomi: Tutphahte koih dingin hong huh thei mi kuamah om hiam?

records.english: I can, once I've finished this call.
records.zomi: Kei ka thei hi, hih phone ka zawh khit ciangin.

records.english: Can you show me how to use the photocopier?
records.zomi: Photocopier bangci zang ding hiam hong lak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Is there any chance you could cover my shift on Saturday?
records.zomi: Kiginni ciangin ka nasep hun hong sem sak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: I'm afraid I can't, but try asking Mary.
records.zomi: Ka sem thei kei hi, ci ka lau hi, ahi zongin Mari dong in.

records.english: Do you need any help?
records.zomi: Huhna na kisam hiam?

records.english: Thanks, but I think I can manage.
records.zomi: Ka lungdam hi, ahi zongin ka zo ding hi, ka ci hi.

records.english: Can I ask you something about the homework?
records.zomi: Inn sinna tungtang dotna khat ka dong thei ding hiam?

records.english: Go ahead, but I might not know the answer.
records.zomi: Dong in, ahi zongin a dawnna ka thei kha lo thei hi.

records.english: Would you mind holding the door for me?
records.zomi: Kongkhak hong len sak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: There you go.
records.zomi: Hih ah.

records.english: I hate to ask, but could you lend me some money for the bus?
records.zomi: Ngen ka nuam kei hi, ahi zongin bus adingin sum tawmno hong pukbawh thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: How much is the fare?
records.zomi: Tuanna man bangzah hiam?

records.english: Neighbors who have helped each other with small things find it much easier to ask for help in an emergency.
records.zomi: Nasep neu te ah a kihuh inn vengte in lauhuai hun ciangin huhna ngen a baih zaw mahmah uh hi.

records.english: A specific request, such as asking someone to drive you on Tuesday, is easier to say yes to than a vague one.
records.zomi: Pithai ni ciangin mawtaw tawh hong paipih in, ci bang ngetna kician khat in kician lo khat sangin hi ci a baih zaw hi.

records.english: How do you ask a stranger for help without seeming rude?
records.zomi: Zahtak lo bangin kilang lo-in mikhual khat kiangah huhna bangci-in na ngen ding hiam?

records.english: Apologize for interrupting, smile, and keep the request short.
records.zomi: Na buaisak ahih manin maisak ngen inla, nui inla, na ngetna tom takin gen in.

records.english: Excuse me, could someone help this lady with her suitcase?
records.zomi: Maisak un, kuamah in hih numei a van bawm tawh na huh thei uh hiam?

records.english: When you ask a busy person for help, it is polite to say how long it will take.
records.zomi: Buai mi khat kiangah huhna na ngen ciangin hun bangzah a la ding hiam gen pen zahtakna ahi hi.

records.english: Are you sure you don't want some help with those bags?
records.zomi: Tua ip te tawh huhna na deih lo taktak hiam?

records.english: Well, if you're offering, I'd be very grateful.
records.zomi: Huh na nuam leh ka lungdam mahmah ding hi.

records.english: Asking for help early usually saves more time than struggling alone until the last minute.
records.zomi: Huhna a ngal-in ngen in hun nunung dong kia haksa taka sep sangin hun tam zaw a khawl zel hi.

records.english: Do you have a minute?
records.zomi: Minit khat na nei hiam?

records.english: Sure, what do you need?
records.zomi: Nei hi, bang na kisam hiam?

records.english: Does anyone here know how to change a tire?
records.zomi: Hih ah kuamah in mawtaw khe kheel dan a thei uh hiam?

records.english: I'd really appreciate your help with the move on Sunday.
records.zomi: Nipini ciangin inn tai ah na huhna ka lungdam mahmah ding hi.

records.english: Sorry to bother you, but do you know where the post office is?
records.zomi: Kong buaisak ahih manin maisak in, post office koi ah om hiam na thei hiam?

records.english: Turn left at the bank, and it's on your right.
records.zomi: Bank ah veilam ah kawi inla, na ziatlam ah om hi.

records.english: Who should I ask about my missing parcel?
records.zomi: Ka ip mangthang tungtang kua ka dong ding hiam?

records.english: The woman at the front desk deals with deliveries.
records.zomi: Mai lam dawhkan-a numei in van tunnate a vai a hawm hi.

records.english: Offering something in return, even just a meal, can make it easier to ask a neighbor for a favor.
records.zomi: An khat bek hi zongin bangmah khat a ciah-in piak in inn veng khat kiangah huhna ngen a baihsak thei hi.

records.english: People often find it easier to offer help than to ask for it.
records.zomi: Mite in huhna ngen sangin huhna pia a baih sa zaw zel uh hi.

records.english: Why didn't you ask me for help?
records.zomi: Bang hangin huhna hong ngen lo na hi hiam?

records.english: I didn't want to bother you when you were so busy.
records.zomi: Na buai mahmah laitakin kong buaisak nuam kei hi.

records.english: Could you keep an eye on my bag while I buy a ticket?
records.zomi: Lai ka lei laitakin ka ip hong en sak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Could you give me a hand with this box?
records.zomi: Hih bawm tawh hong huh thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Yes, if you take the other end.
records.zomi: Thei ing, a tawp khat lam na len leh.

records.english: In some workplaces, asking a question is seen as a sign of interest, not of ignorance.
records.zomi: Nasepna mun pawl khat ah dotna dong pen theih lohna lakna hi lo-in deihna lakna ahi hi, ci-in kimu hi.

records.english: Would it be too much trouble to water my plants next week?
records.zomi: A zom kal ka singkungte tui hong buak sak in buaina tam lua ding hiam?

records.english: It's no trouble, so just leave me the key.
records.zomi: Buaina hi lo hi, tawh bek hong nusia in.

records.english: Who can I turn to if my landlord won't fix the heating?
records.zomi: Ka inn neipa in meilum a bawlpha nuam kei leh kua kiangah ka pai thei ding hiam?

records.english: The tenants' advice office, which can write to him for you.
records.zomi: Inn luahmite' thuhilhna office, na adingin amah kiangah lai a gelh sak thei.

records.english: What's the best way to ask your boss for help with a heavy workload?
records.zomi: Na nasep gik lua tungtang na makaipa kiangah huhna ngen dan hoih pen bang hiam?

records.english: Explain what you've already tried, and suggest one specific change.
records.zomi: Na sin khinte genteh inla, kikheelna kician khat gen in.

records.english: So you'll lend me the ladder on Saturday, and I'll bring it back on Monday?
records.zomi: Tua ahih leh Kiginni ciangin kahlei hong pukbawh ding na hi a, Pizing ni ciangin kong tawi kik ding hi, hi hiam?

records.english: Many older people hesitate to ask for help because they don't want to be a burden on their families.
records.zomi: Mi upa tampi in a innkuan uh tungah puakgik a suah nop loh manin huhna ngen a lau uh hi.

records.english: Could you possibly spare an hour this weekend?
records.zomi: Hih kal tawp hun khat na awng thei ding hiam?

records.english: We went around the roundabout three times!
records.zomi: Lampi kikawi kual vei thum i kual uh hi!

records.english: I have no sense of direction at all.
records.zomi: Lampi theih ka siam tuan kei hi.

records.english: Panic makes people walk faster and further, which is often exactly the wrong thing to do when they're lost.
records.zomi: Lauhuaina in mite manlang zaw leh gamla zaw-in a kalsuansak a, tua pen lampi a pial uh ciangin bawl ding hi lo mahmah ahi zel hi.

records.english: Children who know their parents' phone number by heart are much easier to reunite with their families.
records.zomi: A nu leh a pa' phone nambat a lungsim sungah a thei naupangte a innkuan uh tawh kimu kik sak a baih zaw mahmah hi.

records.english: My heart was beating fast when I couldn't see my son anywhere.
records.zomi: Ka tapa koi ah zong ka muh loh ciangin ka lungtang a ging manlang hi.

records.english: Was our house easy to find?
records.zomi: I inn muh a baih hiam?

records.english: Yes, apart from one wrong turn near the bridge.
records.zomi: Baih hi, lei kiang-a kawm khial khat simloh.

records.english: In the airport, I followed the signs for arrivals instead of connections and had to go through security again.
records.zomi: Vanlengtual ah kizopna sangin tunnate ciamtehna ka zui a, kicinna kiseenna ah ka pai kik kisam hi.

records.english: My little sister got lost in the shopping center for half an hour.
records.zomi: Ka nau numei in dawl lian sungah minit sawmthum sung lampi a pial hi.

records.english: Our dog found the way home before we did.
records.zomi: I ui in eite ma-in inn ciahna lampi a mu hi.

records.english: Sorry I'm late — I got off at the wrong stop and walked twenty minutes in the wrong direction.
records.zomi: Ka hong nunung ahih manin hong maisak in — dinna mun khial ah ka kiat a, lam khial ah minit sawmnih ka kalsuan hi.

records.english: Do you remember where we parked the car?
records.zomi: Mawtaw koi ah i khawl uh hiam na phawk hiam?

records.english: Stay here, and I'll come and find you.
records.zomi: Hih ah om in, kong zong ding hi.

records.english: So we turn left at the mosque, and then it's the second street on the right?
records.zomi: Tua ahih leh mosque ah veilam ah i kawi ding a, tua khit ciangin ziatlam-a lampi nihna ahi hiam?

records.english: Don't panic, because we'll find the way.
records.zomi: Lau kei in, lampi i mu ding hi.

records.english: Relying completely on a phone for directions means that many of us no longer notice the streets we walk through.
records.zomi: Lampi adingin phone tungah kinga kim in eite tampi in i kalsuanna lampite i phawk nawn kei uh hi.

records.english: Can you tell me where we are on this map?
records.zomi: Hih map tungah koi ah i om uh hiam hong gen thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: The festival was so crowded that we agreed to meet by the big clock if anyone got separated.
records.zomi: Pawi a mi tam lua ahih manin kuamah kikhen leh nai lian kiangah kimu dingin i kithei uh hi.

records.english: Doesn't this street look familiar?
records.zomi: Hih lampi i theih ngei bang kilang lo hiam?

records.english: What should I do if I get lost in the forest?
records.zomi: Gammang sungah lampi ka pial leh bang ka bawl ding hiam?

records.english: Stay where you are and keep warm, because it's easier for others to find you.
records.zomi: Na om na mun ah om inla, na pumpi lumsak in, mi dangte in hong muh a baih zaw ahih manin.

records.english: Asked how he had found his way home after three days, the old shepherd simply said that the mountain had told him.
records.zomi: Ni thum khit ciangin inn ciahna lampi bangci-in na mu hiam ci-a a kidot ciangin tuucing upa in mual in hong hilh hi, a ci bek hi.

records.english: Signs written only in the local script can leave visitors completely lost, even in a small station.
records.zomi: Mun lai laimal bek tawh kigelh ciamtehnate in dinna mun neu khat ah zong khualte a buaisak thei hi.

records.english: Is your phone getting a signal?
records.zomi: Na phone in signal a ngah hiam?

records.english: My grandfather never gets lost in the forest, because he notices which way the streams run.
records.zomi: Ka pu in luite bang lam ah a luang hiam a phawk ahih manin gammang sungah lampi a pial ngei kei hi.

records.english: On the night bus, I fell asleep and woke up at the last stop on the other side of the city.
records.zomi: Zan bus tungah ka ihmu kha a, khuapi lam dang-a dinna mun nunung pen ah ka khanglawh hi.

records.english: The hospital is so big that I got lost looking for the X-ray department.
records.zomi: Siavuan inn a lian lua ahih manin X-ray khan ka zon laitakin lampi ka pial hi.

records.english: Last autumn, my father and I went walking in the hills and were caught in thick fog.
records.zomi: Kum nunung a tuikhial ciangin ka pa leh kei mualte ah i pai uh a, meivom tah in hong tuam hi.

records.english: We couldn't see the path, so we stayed where we were and listened.
records.zomi: Lampi i mu thei kei uh ahih manin i om na mun ah i om uh a, i ngai uh hi.

records.english: After an hour, we heard sheep bells and followed the sound down to a farm, where the farmer's wife gave us hot tea.
records.zomi: Hun khat khit ciangin tuu khuang ging i za uh a, a ging zui-in lo inn khat dong i tum uh a, tua lai-a lo neipa' zi in tea lum hong pia hi.

records.english: Losing your way in a city you know well can be more unsettling than getting lost somewhere new.
records.zomi: Na theih hoih khuapi khat ah lampi pial pen mun thak khat ah pial sangin a lungkhamhuai zaw thei hi.

records.english: Wait for me at the gate if we get separated.
records.zomi: I kikhen leh kongpi ah hong ngak in.

records.english: That's the third time we've passed this shop!
records.zomi: Hih dawl i kantan thumna ahi hi!

records.english: When we were children, my brother and I got lost in a field of tall maize and shouted for our mother until she found us.
records.zomi: I naupan lai-in ka sanggam pasal leh kei vaimim sang lo sungah lampi i pial uh a, ka nu in hong muh dong i sam uh hi.

records.english: The underground stations all looked the same, and I came up the wrong exit twice.
records.zomi: Lei nuai meileng dinna mun khempeuh a kibang a, vei nih lampi khial ah ka pusuak hi.

records.english: Which way did we come in?
records.zomi: Bang lam pan i hong lut uh hiam?

records.english: Had the fog lifted an hour later, we would have spent the night on the mountain.
records.zomi: Meivom in hun khat nung zaw-in a tawp leh mual tungah zan i giak ding uh hi.

records.english: Old maps can mislead modern walkers, because paths that once linked villages may have disappeared under fields.
records.zomi: Map luite in tu-a kalsuan mite a khial sak thei hi, khuate a kizopsak lampi luite lo nuai ah a mang khin kha thei ahih manin.

records.english: Whenever we're lost, my husband refuses to ask for directions, and I refuse to stop asking.
records.zomi: I lampi pial ciangin ka pasal in lampi dot a nial a, kei in dot khawl ka nial hi.

records.english: I was too embarrassed to admit to my friends that I had no idea where we were.
records.zomi: Koi ah i om uh hiam ka theih loh ka lawmte kiangah gen dingin ka zum lua hi.

records.english: If you think you're lost, stop walking and look for something you remember.
records.zomi: Lampi na pial hi, na ci leh kalsuan khawl inla, na phawk khat zong in.

records.english: A child who is lost may hide from strangers, so searchers often call the child's name and wait quietly for an answer.
records.zomi: Lampi a pial naupang khat in mikhualte pan a kisel thei ahih manin a zongte in naupang' min a sam zel uh a, dai takin dawnna a ngak uh hi.

records.english: Shall we turn round and try the other road?
records.zomi: I kihei-in lampi dang i sin ding hiam?

records.english: Are you sure this train goes north?
records.zomi: Hih meileng in mallam ah a pai hi, ci na thei taktak hiam?

records.english: The map on our phone sent us down a farm track that got narrower and muddier with every turn.
records.zomi: I phone tung-a map in lo lampi khat ah hong pai sak a, a kawi simin a kiak semsem leh a ngaw semsem hi.

records.english: In the end, the track disappeared completely, and we had to reverse half a mile in the dark.
records.zomi: A tawpna ah lampi a mang khin a, mial sungah mile a lang nung lam ah i pai kik kisam hi.

records.english: A farmer on a tractor came to see what the lights were and led us back to the main road, laughing.
records.zomi: Tractor tung-a lo nei khat in meivakte bang ahi hiam en dingin hong pai a, a nui kawm-in lampi lian ah hong paipih kik hi.

records.english: The rescue team said that most lost walkers are found close to where they first left the path.
records.zomi: Huhkhiatna pawl in lampi a pial kalsuan mite a tamzaw a lampi a nusiat masakna mun kiangah kimu zel hi, a ci uh hi.

records.english: How did you find your way back?
records.zomi: Na lampi kik bangci-in na mu hiam?

records.english: We followed the river downhill until we reached the village.
records.zomi: Khua i tun dong gun zui-in i tum uh hi.

records.english: Where are we?
records.zomi: Koi ah i om uh hiam?

records.english: Some people find their way by street names, while others remember shops, colours and smells.
records.zomi: Mi pawl khat in lampi min tawh lampi a mu uh a, a dangte in dawlte, rongte leh gim te a phawk uh hi.

records.english: On a school trip to the city, I followed the wrong group of children out of the museum.
records.zomi: Khuapi ah sang khualzinna ah museum pan naupang pawl khial ka zui hi.

records.english: By the time I realized that none of the faces were familiar, we were two streets away.
records.zomi: Mai khatpeuh ka theih ngei lo hi, ci ka phawk ciangin lampi nih gamla ah i om khin uh hi.

records.english: Their teacher walked me back, and my own teacher hugged me so hard that my glasses fell off.
records.zomi: A saya uh in hong paipih kik a, ka saya in hong kawikawi hat lua ahih manin ka mitlimlang a kia hi.

records.english: Admitting that you're lost is often harder than finding the way again.
records.zomi: Lampi na pial hi, ci pom pen lampi muh kik sangin a haksa zaw zel hi.

records.english: Hold my hand in the crowd.
records.zomi: Mihonpi lakah ka khut len in.

records.english: My son had written our address on a card in his pocket, which is how the police knew where to bring him.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in a puan ip sung-a card khat tungah i teenna mun a gelh khin a, tua ahih manin palik in koi ah a paipih ding hiam a thei uh hi.

records.english: I think we're lost.
records.zomi: Lampi i pial hi, ka ci hi.

records.english: Is this the right platform for the airport train?
records.zomi: Hih pen vanlengtual meileng adingin dinna mun dik ahi hiam?

records.english: My doctor checked whether I was safe at home before she arranged the referral.
records.zomi: Ka siavuan in mi dang kiang a hong sawl ma-in inn ah ka bit hiam a en hi.

records.english: Will the counselor tell my parents?
records.zomi: Lungsim huh siam in ka nu leh ka pa kiangah a gen ding hiam?

records.english: It took me a long time to ask for help.
records.zomi: Huhna ngen dingin hun sawtpi hong la hi.

records.english: Finding the right therapist can take time, because the relationship between counselor and client matters as much as the method.
records.zomi: Lungsim huh siam dik muh in hun a la thei hi, lungsim huh siam leh a kiang hongpai mi kizopna in a lampi tawh a thupi kibang ahih manin.

records.english: For some older people, talking to a stranger about feelings is so unfamiliar that a family doctor's encouragement makes all the difference.
records.zomi: Mi upa pawl khat adingin mikhual kiangah lungsim kisakna gen a ngeina lo lua ahih manin innkuan siavuan' hanthotna in kibatlohna lian a bawl hi.

records.english: I felt nervous before my first session, but the therapist was very kind.
records.zomi: Ka kimuhna masa ma-in ka lau a, ahi zongin lungsim huh siam a hoih mahmah hi.

records.english: My sister found a therapist who speaks our language.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam numei in i pau a zang thei lungsim huh siam khat a mu hi.

records.english: Is it fair that free counseling is so much easier to find in cities than in the countryside?
records.zomi: A man om lo lungsim huhna khuapite ah gamlak sangin a muh baih zawk mahmah a dik hiam?

records.english: Had my friend not offered to come with me to the clinic, I might have turned back at the door.
records.zomi: Ka lawm in siavuan inn ah hong zui dingin a kiciam kei leh kongkhak pan ka kik kha ding hi.

records.english: Many counselors offer a short first call so that you can see whether you feel comfortable with them.
records.zomi: Lungsim huh siam tampi in amaute tawh na kituak hiam na theih theih nadingin phone tom masa khat a pia uh hi.

records.english: The group sessions were less frightening than I expected, because everyone was there for the same reason.
records.zomi: Pawl kimuhnate ka lamen sangin a lauhuai tawm zaw hi, mi khempeuh hang kibang tawh a om uh ahih manin.

records.english: There's a waiting list of six weeks.
records.zomi: Kal guk ngakna list khat om hi.

records.english: Who should I talk to first, my doctor or a counselor?
records.zomi: Kua tawh ka kikum masa ding hiam, ka siavuan hiam lungsim huh siam hiam?

records.english: Your doctor, who can refer you to the right service.
records.zomi: Na siavuan, nasepna dik kiangah hong sawl thei ahih manin.

records.english: What happens at the first appointment?
records.zomi: Kimuhna masa ah bang a piang hiam?

records.english: The counselor asks a few questions and listens, and you decide what to talk about.
records.zomi: Lungsim huh siam in dotna tawmno a dong a, a ngaihkhia a, nang in bang thu kikum ding hiam na khen hi.

records.english: My first session is on Monday.
records.zomi: Ka kimuhna masa pen Pizing ni ah om hi.

records.english: In many places, the waiting lists for mental health services are long, so it helps to ask what support is available in the meantime.
records.zomi: Mun tampi ah lungsim damna nasepna ngakna list a sau ahih manin tua kikal-ah bang huhna om hiam dot a huh hi.

records.english: My father was against therapy at first, but he came to one family session and changed his mind.
records.zomi: Ka pa in a masa-in lungsim huhna a langpang a, ahi zongin innkuan kimuhna khat ah hong pai a, a lungsim a kheel hi.

records.english: Parents who seek help for their own difficulties often find that their children benefit as well.
records.zomi: Amau' haksatna adingin huhna zong nu leh pate in a tate uh zong a phattuam hi, ci-in a mu zel uh hi.

records.english: Seeking professional help is not a sign of failure but a practical step, like seeing a doctor for a broken arm.
records.zomi: Siamna nei huhna zong pen lawhsapna lakna hi lo-in khut kiat adingin siavuan kiang pai bangin pai thei kalsuan khat ahi hi.

records.english: Can I have the sessions online?
records.zomi: Kimuhnate online-in ka nei thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, many counselors now offer video sessions.
records.zomi: Thei hi, lungsim huh siam tampi in tu-in video kimuhna a pia uh hi.

records.english: How did the session go?
records.zomi: Kimuhna bangci om hiam?

records.english: Better than I expected.
records.zomi: Ka lamen sangin a hoih zaw hi.

records.english: A good professional will explain what they can and cannot keep confidential before the conversation begins.
records.zomi: Siamna nei hoih khat in kikupna a kipat ma-in bang thu guk-in a kem thei hiam, a kem thei lo hiam a genteh ding hi.

records.english: I've decided to get some help.
records.zomi: Huhna khat ngah dingin thu ka khen khin hi.

records.english: Do I need a letter from my doctor?
records.zomi: Ka siavuan pan lai khat ka kisam ding hiam?

records.english: Online sessions suit some people well, but others need the privacy of a room away from home to speak freely.
records.zomi: Online kimuhnate mi pawl khat tawh a kituak mahmah a, ahi zongin a dangte in zalen taka gen theih nadingin inn tawh gamla inndei khat' gukna a kisam uh hi.

records.english: My doctor referred me to a specialist who works with people after accidents.
records.zomi: Ka siavuan in accident khit-a mite tawh nasep sem siam khat kiangah hong sawl hi.

records.english: My brother sees a psychologist once a week.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in kal simin psychologist khat a mu hi.

records.english: Our pastor listened kindly, but he suggested that I also see a professional counselor.
records.zomi: I pastor in hehpih takin hong ngaihkhia a, ahi zongin siamna nei lungsim huh siam khat zong mu dingin hong hilh hi.

records.english: Is everything I say kept private?
records.zomi: Ka gen khempeuh guk-in kikem ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, except in rare cases when someone is in danger, and the counselor will explain those to you.
records.zomi: Kem ding hi, mi khat lauhuai sungah a om hun tawmno simloh, lungsim huh siam in tuate hong genteh ding hi.

records.english: If one counselor doesn't suit you, it's fine to try someone else.
records.zomi: Lungsim huh siam khat na tawh a kituak kei leh mi dang khat sin a hoih hi.

records.english: When my teenage son refused to talk to us, his teacher suggested the youth counseling service.
records.zomi: Ka khangno tapa in eite tawh kiho a nial ciangin a saya in khangno lungsim huhna nasepna a hilh hi.

records.english: I'm afraid we can't see you this week, but there's a drop-in service at the health center on Friday.
records.zomi: Hih kal in kong mu thei kei ding uh hi, ci ka lau hi, ahi zongin Laithai ni ciangin damna inn ah lut thei huhna khat om hi.

records.english: Before my first session, I wrote down three things I wanted the counselor to know.
records.zomi: Ka kimuhna masa ma-in lungsim huh siam in a theih ding ka deih thu thum ka gelh hi.

records.english: I'm glad you went.
records.zomi: Na pai ahih manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: My friend's therapist helped her to start sleeping properly again.
records.zomi: Ka lawm' lungsim huh siam in a ihmut hoih kik nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Professional help does not replace the support of family and friends, but it can offer skills and perspective that they cannot.
records.zomi: Siamna nei huhna in innkuan leh lawmte' huhna a laih kei a, ahi zongin amaute in a piak theih loh siamna leh muh dan a pia thei hi.

records.english: The therapist suggested small steps, like walking to the shop on my own.
records.zomi: Lungsim huh siam in dawl ah keimah kia kalsuan bang kalsuan neute a hilh hi.

records.english: My son talks to the school psychologist every Thursday.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in Laizing ni simin sang psychologist tawh a kiho hi.

records.english: The doctor gave me a list of local counselors.
records.zomi: Siavuan in mun lai lungsim huh siamte list khat hong pia hi.

records.english: How do I know whether a counselor is properly qualified?
records.zomi: Lungsim huh siam khat in siamna lai a nei taktak hiam bangci-in ka thei thei ding hiam?

records.english: Ask which professional body they belong to, and check it on that body's website.
records.zomi: Bang siamna nei pawl ah a kihel uh hiam dong inla, tua pawl' website tungah en in.

records.english: Some workplaces pay for a few sessions with a counselor through their staff support program.
records.zomi: Nasepna mun pawl khat in nasemte huhna program tungtawn-in lungsim huh siam tawh kimuhna tawmno adingin man a pia uh hi.

records.english: Thank you for listening to me today.
records.zomi: Tuni-in hong ngaihkhia na hih manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: People sometimes wait until a crisis before seeking help, although earlier support is often simpler and shorter.
records.zomi: Mite in buaina lian a tun dong huhna ngen a ngak zel uh a, a ngal-a huhna in a baih zaw leh a tom zaw zel hi.

records.english: Is it expensive to see a therapist?
records.zomi: Lungsim huh siam muh in man a tam hiam?

records.english: Some charge a lot, but the clinic here offers free sessions to students.
records.zomi: Pawl khat in a man a tam mahmah a, ahi zongin hih-a siavuan inn in sangnaupangte kiangah a man om lo kimuhna a pia hi.

records.english: Should I tell my employer that I'm seeing a therapist?
records.zomi: Lungsim huh siam khat ka mu hi, ci ka nasep piaktu kiangah ka gen ding hiam?

records.english: Only if you want to, although it can help if you need time off for appointments.
records.zomi: Na deih leh bek, kimuhnate adingin hun na kisam leh a huh thei hangin.

records.english: What kind of help do you think I need?
records.zomi: Bang huhna ka kisam hi, na ci hiam?

records.english: Sorry, I didn't finish the exercises you gave me last week.
records.zomi: Maisak in, kal nunung-a hong piak sinna te ka zo kei hi.

records.english: Interpreters can make therapy possible for people who would otherwise struggle to describe their feelings in a second language.
records.zomi: Pau letmite in pau nihna-a a lungsim kisak gen haksa sa ding mite adingin lungsim huhna a hih theih sak hi.

records.english: Deciding to stop therapy is also worth discussing with the therapist, instead of simply missing sessions.
records.zomi: Lungsim huhna khawl dingin thukhen zong kimuhna pelh bek sangin lungsim huh siam tawh kikum a manpha hi.

records.english: So I'll see you every Tuesday for six weeks, and then we'll decide whether to continue?
records.zomi: Tua ahih leh kal guk sung Pithai ni simin kong mu ding a, tua khit ciangin i zom ding hiam i khen ding hi, hi hiam?

records.english: After a few months of sessions, I noticed that I was handling arguments at home much more calmly.
records.zomi: Kha tawmno kimuhna khit ciangin inn-a kinialnate ka vai a hawm dan a nem zaw mahmah hi, ci ka phawk hi.

records.english: A psychiatrist is a medical doctor who can prescribe medicine, while a psychologist usually works through talking therapies.
records.zomi: Psychiatrist pen zatui a gelh thei siavuan ahi a, psychologist in a tamzaw kiho tawh lungsim huhna a bawl hi.

records.english: What a difference an early night makes!
records.zomi: A ngal-a ihmut in kibatlohna bangzah a bawl hiam!

records.english: Are your mornings busier on Mondays or on Fridays?
records.zomi: Na zingsangte Pizing ni ciangin hiam Laithai ni ciangin hiam a buai zaw hiam?

records.english: For shift workers, the choice between sleeping longer and seeing the family at breakfast is made almost every day.
records.zomi: Hun kheel-a nasemte adingin sawt zaw-a ihmut leh zingsang an ciangin innkuan muh lak-a teelna ni simin dekin kibawl hi.

records.english: A ponytail takes two minutes, but a braid lasts all day.
records.zomi: Sam kigak in minit nih a la a, ahi zongin sam kibel in ni bup a tang hi.

records.english: Mornings in the city are noisier than in my grandmother's village, where only the birds wake you.
records.zomi: Khuapi-a zingsangte ka pi' khua sangin a ging zaw a, tua ah vate bek in hong khanglawhsak hi.

records.english: Blackout curtains help the baby sleep later, but they make it harder for me to wake up.
records.zomi: Puankhai mial in naungek a nung zaw-in a ihmusak a, ahi zongin kei a khanglawh haksa zaw sak hi.

records.english: Does strong tea wake you up as well as coffee does?
records.zomi: Tea khauh in coffee bangin hong khanglawhsak hiam?

records.english: Since I cut my hair short, I get ready in half the time.
records.zomi: Ka sam a tom-in ka at khit pan hun a lang sungin ka kiman hi.

records.english: Shall we leave now or after the rain stops?
records.zomi: Tu-in i pai ding hiam, guah a khawl khit ciangin hiam?

records.english: Now, or we'll be late either way.
records.zomi: Tu-in, ahih kei leh bangci hi zongin i nunung ding hi.

records.english: My daughter gets ready faster than her brother, but she wakes up later.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in a sanggam pasal sangin a kiman manlang zaw a, ahi zongin a khanglawh nung zaw hi.

records.english: I'd rather get ready in silence than with the radio on.
records.zomi: Radio a ging sangin dai takin kiman ka deih zaw hi.

records.english: A predictable routine often matters more to young children than the exact time they wake up.
records.zomi: Naupang neute adingin a khanglawh hun diktak sangin theih theih ngeina khat a thupi zaw zel hi.

records.english: On school days we eat bread, but on Sundays my mother makes rice soup.
records.zomi: Sangkah ni ciangin moh i ne uh a, ahi zongin Nipini ciangin ka nu in buh-an tui a huan hi.

records.english: You're more awake than usual this morning, aren't you?
records.zomi: Tu zingsang in a ngeina sangin na khanglawh zaw hi, hi lo hiam?

records.english: Is it better to eat breakfast at home or buy something on the way?
records.zomi: Zingsang an inn ah ne a hoih zaw hiam, lampi tungah bangmah lei a hoih zaw hiam?

records.english: At home, because it's cheaper and I actually sit down.
records.zomi: Inn ah, a man a neu zaw a, ka tu taktak ahih manin.

records.english: A long commute changes the whole shape of the morning, because every minute saved at home matters on the road.
records.zomi: Nasepna pai lampi sau in zingsang bup a kheel hi, inn-a minit khatciat khawl in lampi tungah a thupi ahih manin.

records.english: Would you rather wake up early or stay up late?
records.zomi: Zingsang ngal-in khanglawh na deih zaw hiam, zan sawt ihmu lo-in om hiam?

records.english: Wake up early, because my brain stops working after ten at night.
records.zomi: Zingsang ngal-in khanglawh, zan nai sawm khit ciangin ka lungsim a sem nawn lo ahih manin.

records.english: A shower wakes me up faster than a bath.
records.zomi: Kisilna tui kaai in tuikulh sangin hong khanglawh manlang zaw sak hi.

records.english: I wake up more easily in my own bed than in a hotel.
records.zomi: Zinbuuk sangin keimah' lupna ah ka khanglawh baih zaw hi.

records.english: Thanks, but I'd rather walk than wait for a lift.
records.zomi: Ka lungdam hi, ahi zongin tuanna ngak sangin ka kalsuan zaw ding hi.

records.english: Exercising in the morning wakes me up, whereas in the evening it keeps me awake.
records.zomi: Zingsang ciangin pumpi kisinsak in hong khanglawhsak a, nitak ciangin ihmu lo-in hong omsak hi.

records.english: Working from home, I still dress as if I'm going to the office, because it helps me concentrate.
records.zomi: Inn pan nasep ka sep zongin office ah ka pai ding bangin puan ka silh lai hi, ka lungsim koih nadingin hong huh ahih manin.

records.english: Shared bathrooms force families to choose between getting up earlier and accepting a little chaos.
records.zomi: Kisilna inn kihawm in innkuante a ngal-in thoh hiam buaina tawmno pom hiam a teel sak hi.

records.english: Choosing clothes the night before saves time, but some people prefer to dress according to their mood on the day.
records.zomi: A zan masa-in puan teel in hun a khawl a, ahi zongin mi pawl khat in tua ni-a a lungsim bangin silh a deih zaw uh hi.

records.english: Summer mornings are easier, because the sun wakes me before the alarm.
records.zomi: Khal zingsangte a baih zaw hi, alarm ma-in ni in hong khanglawhsak ahih manin.

records.english: Do you find that a uniform makes school mornings easier for parents?
records.zomi: Sang puan kibang in nu leh pate adingin sang zingsang a baihsak hi, na ci hiam?

records.english: We chose a flat near the school, so the children can sleep half an hour longer than their friends.
records.zomi: Sang kiang-a inn khat i teel uh ahih manin naupangte in a lawmte uh sangin minit sawmthum sawt zaw-in a ihmu thei uh hi.

records.english: Should I wear my glasses or my contact lenses for the long drive?
records.zomi: Mawtaw mawng sau adingin ka mitlimlang ka zang ding hiam, contact lens ka zang ding hiam?

records.english: Your glasses, because your eyes get dry on long journeys.
records.zomi: Na mitlimlang, khualzin sau ah na mit a keu ahih manin.

records.english: If I leave at seven, the drive takes twenty minutes, but at half past it can take an hour.
records.zomi: Nai sagih ciangin ka pai leh mawng in minit sawmnih a la a, ahi zongin nai sagih lang ciangin hun khat a la thei hi.

records.english: Which is harder for you, getting up in the dark or getting up after a late night?
records.zomi: Na adingin bang in a haksa zaw hiam, mial sungah thoh hiam, zan sawt khit ciangin thoh hiam?

records.english: Since the clocks changed, the children have been waking up an hour earlier than usual.
records.zomi: Nai a kikheel khit pan naupangte a ngeina sangin hun khat a ngal-in a khanglawh uh hi.

records.english: Whether an early start feels like a gift or a burden depends largely on how well you slept the night before.
records.zomi: Zingsang ngal-a kipat in letsong bang hiam puakgik bang hiam a kisak pen a zan masa-a na ihmut hoih dan tungah a tamzaw a kinga hi.

records.english: A gentle alarm wakes me more pleasantly than a loud one, but it doesn't always get me out of bed.
records.zomi: Alarm nem in alarm ging sangin nuam zaw-in hong khanglawhsak a, ahi zongin lupna pan hong thohsak tawntung kei hi.

records.english: My father prefers a cold shower in the morning, even in winter, while the rest of us wait for hot water.
records.zomi: Ka pa in phalbi ah zong zingsang ciangin tui vot tawh kisil a deih zaw a, ka dangte in tui lum i ngak uh hi.

records.english: Do you shave in the morning or at night?
records.zomi: Zingsang ciangin hiam zan ciangin hiam na khamul na hiat hiam?

records.english: At night, once the children are asleep.
records.zomi: Zan ciangin, naupangte a ihmut khit ciangin.

records.english: Porridge keeps the children full longer than toast does.
records.zomi: Buh-an tui in naupangte moh lum sangin sawt zaw-in a vaksak hi.

records.english: Mornings in a large family teach patience, whereas living alone teaches you that nobody will remind you of anything.
records.zomi: Innkuan lian-a zingsangte in thuakzawhna a sinsak a, kia-a teeng in kuamah in bangmah hong phawksak lo ding hi, ci a sinsak hi.

records.english: Teenagers' sleep patterns tend to shift later, so their parents' early mornings can feel like a punishment to them.
records.zomi: Khangnote' ihmut ngeina a nung lam ah a pai zel ahih manin a nu leh pa' zingsang ngal te amaute adingin gawtna bangin a kisa thei hi.

records.english: I'd choose a quick breakfast with the family over a long breakfast alone.
records.zomi: Kia-a zingsang an sau sangin innkuan tawh zingsang an manlang khat ka teel zaw ding hi.

records.english: My son brushes his teeth more carefully with the timer than without it.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in nai teh tawh a ha a sil ciangin a om loh sangin limtak zaw-in a sil hi.

records.english: Ironed clothes once signalled respect for school or work, but many families now choose comfort over a sharp crease.
records.zomi: Puan kiteh pen sang hiam nasep hiam zahtakna lakna ahi ngei a, ahi zongin tu-in innkuan tampi in puan kituak sangin nuamna a teel zaw uh hi.

records.english: Is an electric toothbrush really better than an ordinary one?
records.zomi: Electric ha sil in a ngeina khat sangin a hoih zaw taktak hiam?

records.english: The dentist said either works well, as long as you brush gently and thoroughly.
records.zomi: Nem takin limtakin na sil leh a nih in a sem hoih hi, ci-in ha siavuan in a gen hi.

records.english: My wife is cheerful at six, while I can't say a word before eight.
records.zomi: Ka zi in nai guk ciangin a lungdam a, kei in nai giat ma-in kammal khat zong ka gen thei kei hi.

records.english: Some people do their best thinking in the first quiet hour of the day, while others can barely hold a conversation before lunch.
records.zomi: Mi pawl khat in ni' hun dai masa pen sungin a ngaihsutna hoih pen a nei uh a, a dangte in sun an ma-in kikum zong a zo ngei kei uh hi.

records.english: The hotel's breakfast started after our train left, so we chose to eat on the platform instead.
records.zomi: Zinbuuk' zingsang an pen i meileng a pai khit ciangin a kipan ahih manin dinna mun ah ne dingin i teel uh hi.

records.english: Which looks smarter for the interview, the grey suit or the navy one?
records.zomi: Kidotna adingin bang in a kilawm zaw hiam, suit vom gukguk hiam suit dum ngei hiam?

records.english: The navy one, with the white shirt.
records.zomi: A dum ngei pen, angki ngo tawh.

records.english: Working from home has blurred the difference between getting up and getting ready.
records.zomi: Inn pan nasep in thoh leh kiman kikal kibatlohna a phiat hi.

records.english: Which is better for school, the red bag or the blue one?
records.zomi: Sang adingin bang in a hoih zaw hiam, ip san hiam ip dum hiam?

records.english: The blue one, because it has more pockets.
records.zomi: A dum pen, a sung ah ip neu a tam zaw ahih manin.

records.english: Had I chosen the later shift, I could have slept longer, but I would have missed my children's breakfasts.
records.zomi: Nasep hun nunung zaw ka teel nak leh sawt zaw ka ihmu thei ding a, ahi zongin ka tate' zingsang an ka mansuah ding hi.

records.english: Sorry, I took the last of the hot water without thinking.
records.zomi: Maisak in, ngaihsut lo-in tui lum a nunung ka la hi.

records.english: Getting up at the first alarm is harder, but I feel better than when I press snooze three times.
records.zomi: Alarm masa ah thoh a haksa zaw a, ahi zongin vei thum snooze ka nek sangin ka kisa hoih zaw hi.

records.english: Breakfast eaten slowly at a table often sets a calmer tone for the day than one eaten standing at the door.
records.zomi: Dawhkan ah zawi taka nek zingsang an in kongkhak ah ding-a nek sangin ni adingin lungmuanna a koih zel hi.

records.english: Many countries have regions where people speak a different first language from the one used by the national government.
records.zomi: Gam tampi in kumpi in a zat pau sangin pau masa dang a zang mite' gamkhente a nei uh hi.

records.english: Is Australia a country or a continent?
records.zomi: Australia pen gam ahi hiam, leitung gam lian ahi hiam?

records.english: Both, which is why it's a favorite quiz question!
records.zomi: A nih in, tua ahih manin dotna deih pen khat ahi hi!

records.english: Our grandparents' villages are in the hills near where Myanmar, India and Bangladesh meet.
records.zomi: I pu leh pite' khuate pen Myanmar, India leh Bangladesh a kituahna kiang-a mualte ah om hi.

records.english: Which country are you from?
records.zomi: Bang gam pan na hi hiam?

records.english: I'm from Myanmar, but I live in Malaysia now.
records.zomi: Myanmar pan ka hi a, ahi zongin tu-in Malaysia ah ka teeng hi.

records.english: Our teacher asked us to compare the climate of our region with one on the other side of the world.
records.zomi: I saya in i gam khen' huihkhua leitung lam dang-a khat tawh teh dingin hong ngen hi.

records.english: Some countries, such as Indonesia and the Philippines, are made up of thousands of islands.
records.zomi: Indonesia leh Philippines bang gam pawl khat pen tuikulh tul tampi tawh kibawl hi.

records.english: Sorry, I mixed up Austria and Australia in the quiz.
records.zomi: Maisak in, dotna sungah Austria leh Australia ka buaisak hi.

records.english: Describing a country only by its problems gives students a narrow and unfair picture of the people who live there.
records.zomi: Gam khat a buainate bek tawh gen in sangnaupangte kiangah tua ah a teeng mite' lim kiak leh dik lo khat a pia hi.

records.english: Write the names of five countries in Asia.
records.zomi: Asia gam-a gam nga' min gelh in.

records.english: Regions within one country sometimes have closer ties to a neighboring country than to their own capital.
records.zomi: Gam khat sung-a gamkhen pawl khat in amau' gam khuapi lian sangin a kiang gam khat tawh kizopna nai zaw a nei uh hi.

records.english: So Laos has no coastline at all?
records.zomi: Tua ahih leh Laos in tuipi gei a nei tuan lo hi, hi hiam?

records.english: In our country, the south is much hotter than the north.
records.zomi: I gam ah sim lam mallam sangin a sa zaw mahmah hi.

records.english: In our country, summers are hot and winters are cool.
records.zomi: I gam ah khal a sa a, phalbi a vot deuh hi.

records.english: The size of a country on a world map can be misleading, because flat maps stretch the areas near the poles.
records.zomi: Leitung map tung-a gam khat' lianna in a khem thei hi, map phei in leitung tawp nih kiang-a munte a zaisak ahih manin.

records.english: Mount Everest stands on the border between Nepal and China.
records.zomi: Mount Everest pen Nepal leh China kikal-a gamgi tungah ding hi.

records.english: Is Canada bigger than the United States?
records.zomi: Canada in United States sangin a lian zaw hiam?

records.english: Yes, slightly, although far fewer people live there.
records.zomi: Lian zaw hi, tawmno, mi tawm zaw mahmah tua ah a teeng uh hangin.

records.english: Japan is an island country.
records.zomi: Japan pen tuikulh gam ahi hi.

records.english: Find Brazil on the globe.
records.zomi: Leitung tum tungah Brazil zong in.

records.english: The United Nations has 193 member countries.
records.zomi: United Nations in gam 193 a nei hi.

records.english: A country can be divided into states, provinces or regions, depending on how it is governed.
records.zomi: Gam khat bangci-in kiuk hiam tungah kinga-in state, province hiam gamkhen ah kikhen thei hi.

records.english: Have you ever been to another country?
records.zomi: Gam dang khat ah na pai ngei hiam?

records.english: For most of its length, the border between the two countries follows a river.
records.zomi: A sauna tamzaw ah gam nih kikal-a gamgi in gun khat a zui hi.

records.english: Population density varies enormously, so a small country can be far more crowded than a large one.
records.zomi: Mi tam dan a kibang lo mahmah ahih manin gam neu khat in gam lian khat sangin a kiak zaw thei mahmah hi.

records.english: Which continent is Egypt in?
records.zomi: Izipt pen bang leitung gam lian ah om hiam?

records.english: Africa, although a small part of it lies in Asia.
records.zomi: Africa, a khen neu khat Asia ah a om hangin.

records.english: How many countries are there in Africa?
records.zomi: Africa ah gam bangzah om hiam?

records.english: Fifty-four, according to our textbook.
records.zomi: Sawmnga leh li, i sinna laibu' gen bangin.

records.english: Had our class not studied the region's geography, we would not have understood why the old trade route went through the mountain pass.
records.zomi: I class in tua gamkhen' leitung lim a sin kei uh leh sumbawlna lampi lui bang hangin mual kantanna tungtawn-in a pai hiam i thei lo ding uh hi.

records.english: We learned the capitals of ten countries today.
records.zomi: Tuni-in gam sawm' khuapi lian te i sin uh hi.

records.english: Why is it hotter near the equator?
records.zomi: Bang hangin leitung laizang kiangah a sa zaw hiam?

records.english: Because the sun is more directly overhead there for most of the year.
records.zomi: Kum sung a tamzaw ni in tua lai-a tung tak ah a om zaw ahih manin.

records.english: Which country would you most like to visit, and why?
records.zomi: Bang gam veh na deih pen hiam, bang hang hiam?

records.english: Norway, because I'd love to see the northern lights.
records.zomi: Norway, mallam vaksak te ka muh nuam mahmah ahih manin.

records.english: People in the mountains and people on the coast of the same country can live very different lives.
records.zomi: Gam kibang-a mualtung mite leh tuipi gei mite in a kibang lo mahmah nuntakna a nei thei uh hi.

records.english: Myanmar's government moved the capital from Yangon to Naypyidaw in the mid-2000s.
records.zomi: Myanmar kumpi in kum 2000 sung a laizang ah gam khuapi lian Yangon pan Naypyidaw ah a sawn hi.

records.english: What's the capital of Japan?
records.zomi: Japan' gam khuapi lian bang hiam?

records.english: Borders drawn on maps do not always match where languages and cultures begin and end.
records.zomi: Map tung-a kigelh gamgite in paute leh ngeinate a kipatna leh a tawpna tawh a kituak tawntung kei hi.

records.english: Studying a country's rivers and mountains often explains where its towns and roads were built.
