records.zomi: Saya khat in ngaihsutna haksa khat kammal kibang tawh gen kik ding hiam, lampi dang mahmah khat sin ding hiam?

records.english: Misunderstandings between generations sometimes arise because the same expression has changed its meaning over time.
records.zomi: Khangthak kikal-a kitheih khialhnate kammal kibang khat' khiatna hun sung a kikheel hang-in a piang zel hi.

records.english: Is it far, or can we walk?
records.zomi: A gamla hiam, i kalsuan thei ding hiam?

records.english: When you say early, how early do you mean?
records.zomi: A ngal-in na cih ciangin bangzah a ngal na ci nopna hiam?

records.english: Before seven, if you can manage it.
records.zomi: Nai sagih ma-in, na zawh leh.

records.english: Asking for clarification shows that you take the other person's words seriously.
records.zomi: Kiciangsakna ngen in mi dang' kammal na ngaihsun taktak hi, a lak hi.

records.english: Do you need it today, or is tomorrow all right?
records.zomi: Tuni-in na kisam hiam, zingciang a hoih hiam?

records.english: Tomorrow morning is fine.
records.zomi: Zingciang zingsang a hoih hi.

records.english: Written agreements reduce confusion, but only if both sides read the same meaning into each line.
records.zomi: Kigelh kituahnate in buaina a neusak a, ahi zongin lam nih in kawm khatciat khiatna kibang a sim uh leh bek.

records.english: When a message could be read in two ways, it is usually kinder to ask than to assume the worse meaning.
records.zomi: Thu khak khat lampi nih-in sim thei a hih ciangin a khiatna gilo zaw ngaihsut sangin dong pen hehpihna zaw zel hi.

records.english: Do you want me to fix it, or just to listen?
records.zomi: Ka bawlpha ding na deih hiam, ka ngaihkhia bek ding na deih hiam?

records.english: Just to listen, please.
records.zomi: Ngaihkhia bek in, kong ngen hi.

records.english: We had agreed to meet at the station, but she meant the bus station and I meant the train station.
records.zomi: Dinna mun ah kimu dingin i kituak uh a, ahi zongin amah in bus dinna a ci nopna a, kei in meileng dinna ka ci nopna hi.

records.english: Before you sign, ask exactly what the monthly fee includes.
records.zomi: Na min na gelh ma-in kha simin sum piak in bang a huam hiam diktakin dong in.

records.english: Do you mean all of us or only the teachers?
records.zomi: Eite khempeuh na ci nopna hiam, sayate bek hiam?

records.english: Vague promises cause disappointment, because each person quietly fills in a different meaning.
records.zomi: Kiciamna kician lo te in lungkiatna a piangsak hi, mi khatciat in dai takin khiatna kibang lo a koih uh ahih manin.

records.english: Had I asked what the client meant by urgent, I wouldn't have worked through the night for nothing.
records.zomi: Client in manlang mahmah a cih in bang a ci nopna hiam ka dong leh zan bup bangmah lo-in nasep ka sem lo ding hi.

records.english: She cried, and then she tried again.
records.zomi: Amah a kap a, tua khit ciangin a sin kik hi.

records.english: Had the neighbors not taken us in after the fire, we would have had to leave the village altogether.
records.zomi: Mei kang khit ciangin inn vengte in hong la kei uh leh khua i nusia kisam ding hi.

records.english: Learning English was hard for my mother, but she never stopped trying.
records.zomi: Ka nu adingin English sin a haksa a, ahi zongin a sin khawl ngei kei hi.

records.english: The year the rains failed, our family's harvest was half its usual size.
records.zomi: Guah a zuk loh kum in i innkuan' lo at a ngeina' lang bek ahi hi.

records.english: My father took work on a building site in town, and we children helped my mother sell vegetables at the market.
records.zomi: Ka pa in khuapi ah inn lamna mun ah nasep a la a, naupangte in ka nu zuakna mun ah anteh zuak dingin i huh uh hi.

records.english: We ate simply that year, but none of us went to bed hungry, and the next harvest was the best in ten years.
records.zomi: Tua kum in baih takin i ne uh a, ahi zongin kuamah gilkial-in i ihmu kei uh a, a zom lo at pen kum sawm sung-a hoih pen ahi hi.

records.english: At sixty-five, my grandmother learned to read, after a lifetime of signing her name with a thumbprint.
records.zomi: Kum sawmguk leh nga ciangin ka pi in a nuntak sung khut lim tawh a min a gelh khit ciangin lai sim a sin hi.

records.english: She practised every evening with my little brother's school books, sounding out each word aloud.
records.zomi: Ka nau pasal' sang laibute tawh nitak simin a kisin a, kammal khatciat ging takin a sim hi.

records.english: Last Christmas, she read the Bible passage in church herself, and half the congregation was in tears.
records.zomi: Christmas nunung in pawlpi ah Laisiangtho sung-a thu amah mah in a sim a, pawlpi mite a lang in a kap uh hi.

records.english: As a boy, I stammered so badly that I dreaded being asked to read aloud in class.
records.zomi: Tangval neu ka hih lai-in ka kam a kikhuk lua ahih manin class sungah ging taka sim dingin kingen ding ka lau mahmah hi.

records.english: A patient teacher let me practise with her after school, one short paragraph at a time.
records.zomi: Thuakzawhna nei saya khat in sang khit ciangin amah tawh, khatvei ah thu khen tom khat, kisin dingin hong phal hi.

records.english: Twenty years later, I gave a speech at her retirement party without stumbling once.
records.zomi: Kum sawmnih khit ciangin a nasep khawlna pawi ah khatvei zong ka khial lo-in thugenna ka bawl hi.

records.english: How long did it take your sister to walk again after the accident?
records.zomi: Accident khit ciangin na sanggam numei a pai kik nadingin hun bangzah a la hiam?

records.english: Everyone said she couldn't do it, but she did.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh in a zo lo ding hi, a ci uh a, ahi zongin a zo hi.

records.english: My son was shy, but now he plays football with the other boys.
records.zomi: Ka tapa a zum siam a, ahi zongin tu-in tangval dangte tawh football a kimawl hi.

records.english: After losing his sight in an accident, my uncle learned to cook, travel and work again with the help of a training centre.
records.zomi: Accident khat ah a mit a khuh khit ciangin ka pa neu in kisinsakna mun khat' huhna tawh an huan, khualzin leh nasep a sin kik hi.

records.english: Difficulties rarely disappear all at once; more often they become manageable little by little.
records.zomi: Haksatnate khatvei thu-in a mang ngei tuan kei a; a tamzaw in dawngdawng-in a thuak theih zah a suak hi.

records.english: The bridge was washed away, so we walked to school the long way for months.
records.zomi: Lei tui in a pua ahih manin kha tampi sung lampi sau tawh sang ah i pai uh hi.

records.english: Shall we fix the roof ourselves, since we can't afford a builder?
records.zomi: Inn lam siam i man zo kei ahih manin inn tung eite mah in i bawlpha ding hiam?

records.english: Should we move to a smaller house to save money?
records.zomi: Sum khawl dingin inn neu zaw khat ah i tai ding hiam?

records.english: People who have overcome hardship often say that the support of others mattered more than their own determination.
records.zomi: Haksatna a zo mite in amau' hanciamna sangin mi dangte' huhna a thupi zaw hi, a ci zel uh hi.

records.english: Is it ever too late to learn something new?
records.zomi: Thu thak sin dingin a nunung lua ngei hiam?

records.english: My neighbor learned to swim at seventy, so I don't think so.
records.zomi: Ka inn veng in kum sawmsagih ciangin tuipeek a sin a, tua ahih manin nunung lua lo hi, ka ci hi.

records.english: Our team lost every match in the first season, but we trained harder and won the cup the next year.
records.zomi: I pawl in kum masa sungin kimawlna khempeuh a lel a, ahi zongin a hat zaw-in i kisin uh a, a zom kum in cup i zo uh hi.

records.english: Sorry, I wasn't much help when you were going through all that.
records.zomi: Maisak in, tua khempeuh na thuak laitakin kei hong huh tam kei ing.

records.english: It wasn't easy, but we didn't give up.
records.zomi: A baih kei a, ahi zongin i khawl kei uh hi.

records.english: Practise a little every day.
records.zomi: Ni simin tawmno kisin in.

records.english: I was scared, but I kept going.
records.zomi: Ka lau a, ahi zongin ka pai zom hi.

records.english: We had to sell the car, which meant cycling to work in all weathers for two years.
records.zomi: Mawtaw i zuak kisam a, tua in kum nih sung huihkhua bangpeuh ah nasepna ah siiksakol tawh pai cihna ahi hi.

records.english: Struggling with something is not proof that you are failing; it is often proof that you are learning.
records.zomi: Bangmah khat tawh haksa taka bawl pen na lawhsap lakna hi lo hi; a tamzaw in na sin lakna ahi hi.

records.english: The first winter in the city was so lonely that I almost went home, but a neighbor invited me to her church.
records.zomi: Khuapi ah phalbi masa pen in ka kisuksi lua ahih manin ka ciah kik dek a, ahi zongin inn veng khat in a pawlpi ah hong sam hi.

records.english: Did your cousin really apply to seven universities before one accepted her?
records.zomi: Na sanggam numei in sangpi khat in a pom ma-in sangpi sagih ah a ngen taktak hiam?

records.english: Children who watch their parents face difficulties calmly learn that problems can be survived.
records.zomi: A nu leh a pa in haksatnate dai taka a tuah a en naupangte in buainate thuak zo thei hi, ci a sin uh hi.

records.english: My brother failed his first maths exam, so he studied with a tutor all summer.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in a maths sitna masa a lel ahih manin khal bup sinsakpa khat tawh a sin hi.

records.english: Resilience is not the absence of fear but the decision to keep going despite it.
records.zomi: Thuak siamna pen launa om lohna hi lo-in launa om zongin pai zom dingin thukhenna ahi hi.

records.english: I'm afraid I can't lend you money, but I can help you write a budget.
records.zomi: Sum kong pukbawh thei kei hi, ci ka lau hi, ahi zongin sum zat geelna gelh dingin kong huh thei hi.

records.english: What kept you going when you felt like giving up?
records.zomi: Khawl nuam na sak ciangin bang in hong pai zomsak hiam?

records.english: Remembering why I had started in the first place.
records.zomi: Bang hangin ka kipan hiam phawk kik.

records.english: Telling the story of a hard time years later can turn painful memories into a source of strength for others.
records.zomi: Kum tampi khit ciangin hun haksa khat' tangthu gen in phawkna natte mi dangte adingin hatna khat ah a kheel thei hi.

records.english: My friends helped me find a new flat after the fire.
records.zomi: Mei kang khit ciangin ka lawmte in inn thak khat zong dingin hong huh uh hi.

records.english: I'm proud of you for not quitting.
records.zomi: Na khawl loh manin kong kisaktheih hi.

records.english: How did your aunt manage to raise four children alone after her husband died?
records.zomi: Na ni in a pasal a sih khit ciangin amah kia-in ta li bangci-in a khoi zo hiam?

records.english: Communities that share what they have in bad years are usually quicker to recover when better times return.
records.zomi: Kum hoih lo te ah a neih a kihawm khuate in hun hoih zaw a hong kik ciangin a dam kik manlang zaw zel uh hi.

records.english: Don't give up now — you're nearly there!
records.zomi: Tu-in khawl kei in — na tung dek ta hi!

records.english: Wasn't today better than yesterday?
records.zomi: Tuni pen zan sangin a hoih zaw hi lo hiam?

records.english: The hardest part of starting again is often deciding to begin, not the work that follows.
records.zomi: Kipat kik ah haksa pen pen a zom nasep hi lo-in kipan dingin thukhen ahi zel hi.

records.english: When my daughter was bullied, she joined a drama club, which slowly gave her back her confidence.
records.zomi: Ka tanu a kisuksak ciangin drama pawl khat ah a kihel a, tua in dawngdawng-in a kingapna a pia kik hi.

records.english: Recovering from the operation took longer than the doctors expected, but I was walking again by spring.
records.zomi: Khamna nasep pan dam kik in siavuante' lamen sangin hun sawt zaw a la a, ahi zongin spring ciangin ka pai kik khin hi.

records.english: Was your first year in the new country very hard?
records.zomi: Gam thak-a na kum masa pen a haksa mahmah hiam?

records.english: Is it possible to be grateful for a difficult experience without pretending it was good?
records.zomi: Haksatna khat a hoih hi, ci-a kilak lo-in lungdam thei hiam?

records.english: Did things get better after a while?
records.zomi: Hun khat khit ciangin a hoih zaw hiam?

records.english: Can you imagine starting again with nothing?
records.zomi: Bangmah nei lo-in kipan kik na ngaihsun thei hiam?

records.english: My father's hands shook after his stroke, so he learned to write with his other hand.
records.zomi: Ka pa' lu natna khit ciangin a khut a ling ahih manin a khut dang tawh gelh a sin hi.

records.english: How did you get through such a hard year?
records.zomi: Tua bang kum haksa bangci-in na pelh hiam?

records.english: One day at a time, with a lot of help from my family.
records.zomi: Ni khat khat in, ka innkuan pan huhna tampi tawh.

records.english: Comparing your progress with other people's can make a difficult journey feel even harder.
records.zomi: Na khantouna mi dangte' tawh teh in khualzinna haksa khat a haksa zaw sak thei hi.

records.english: Who helped you most when things were difficult?
records.zomi: Thu a haksat ciangin kua in hong huh pen hiam?

records.english: My older brother, who called me every single evening.
records.zomi: Ka u pasal, nitak simin hong sam pa.

records.english: So you finished your degree while working nights and raising two children?
records.zomi: Tua ahih leh zan nasep sem kawm-in leh ta nih khoi kawm-in na degree na zo hi, hi hiam?

records.english: When our shop was robbed, the whole street helped us repair the door and restock the shelves.
records.zomi: I dawl a kigu ciangin lampi bup in kongkhak bawlpha leh van koihnate dimsak kik dingin hong huh uh hi.

records.english: Christian prayers are often addressed to the Father, through the Son, in the Spirit.
records.zomi: Khristian thungetnate Kha sungah, Tapa tungtawn-in, Pa kiangah a kipia zel hi.

records.english: Our Sunday school teacher drew three circles that overlapped in the middle.
records.zomi: I Nipini sang saya in a laizang ah a kituah kual thum a gelh hi.

records.english: May I ask a difficult question?
records.zomi: Dotna haksa khat ka dong thei ding hiam?

records.english: The shamrock, with its three leaves on one stem, is a well-known teaching picture of the Trinity.
records.zomi: Kung khat tungah a nah thum nei shamrock pen Trinity hilhna lim min thang khat ahi hi.

records.english: Christians who hold this teaching insist that the Father, the Son and the Spirit are equal and eternal, not three separate gods or three masks worn by one person.
records.zomi: Hih thuhilhna a pom Khristiante in Pa, Tapa leh Kha Siangtho pen a kibang leh tawntung ahi a, pasian tuam thum hi lo, mi khat in a zat mai lim thum zong hi lo hi, ci-in a ciamteh uh hi.

records.english: The window above our church door shows three linked rings for the Trinity.
records.zomi: I pawlpi kongkhak tung-a tukvuang in Trinity adingin a kizom kual thum a lak hi.

records.english: Some Christians make the sign of the cross when they pray.
records.zomi: Khristian pawl khat in thu a nget ciangin singlamteh lim a bawl uh hi.

records.english: Many prayers end with the words "in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit."
records.zomi: Thungetna tampi in "Pa' min tawh, Tapa' min tawh, Kha Siangtho' min tawh" cih kammalte tawh a tawp hi.

records.english: My daughter asked how God can be three and one at the same time.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in Pasian bangci-in hun kibang ah thum leh khat a hi thei hiam ci-in a dong hi.

records.english: When I was a child, the Trinity confused me more than any other part of my faith.
records.zomi: Ka naupan lai-in Trinity in ka upna sung-a a dang khempeuh sangin hong buaisak zaw hi.

records.english: Is it possible to believe in the Trinity while admitting that you cannot fully explain it?
records.zomi: A kicing-in na genteh thei kei hi, ci pom kawm-in Trinity um thei hiam?

records.english: Paul ends one of his letters to the Corinthians with a blessing that names the Lord Jesus Christ, God and the Holy Spirit.
records.zomi: Paul in Korin mite kiang a lai khat Topa Jesu Khazih, Pasian leh Kha Siangtho a min sam thupha khat tawh a tawp hi.

records.english: Early church leaders rejected the idea that the Son was a created being, a view associated with a priest named Arius.
records.zomi: Pawlpi makaipi masate in Tapa pen kibawl khat ahi hi, cih ngaihsutna, Arius kici siampi khat tawh kizom ngaihsutna, a nial uh hi.

records.english: At Jesus' baptism, the Gospels describe the Spirit coming down like a dove and a voice speaking from heaven.
records.zomi: Jesu' tuiphumna ah Lungdamna Thu laibute in Kha pen vakhu bangin hong kum suk a, van pan aw khat a ging hi, ci-in a gen uh hi.

records.english: So you're saying there aren't three gods, only one?
records.zomi: Tua ahih leh pasian thum om lo-in khat bek om hi, na ci hiam?

records.english: Jews and Muslims believe that God is one and do not accept the Christian teaching of the Trinity.
records.zomi: Judah mite leh Muslimte in Pasian khat bek om hi, ci-in a um uh a, Khristian' Trinity thuhilhna a pom kei uh hi.

records.english: Some groups, such as Jehovah's Witnesses, teach that Jesus is not equal to God the Father.
records.zomi: Jehovah's Witnesses bang pawl pawl khat in Jesu pen Pasian Pa tawh a kibang kei hi, ci-in a hilh uh hi.

records.english: Bow your heads for the blessing.
records.zomi: Thupha adingin na lu uh kun un.

records.english: Read Matthew 28 together.
records.zomi: Matthai 28 a khawm-in sim un.

records.english: The doctrine shapes Christian worship, since believers praise the Father, follow the Son and rely on the Spirit.
records.zomi: Thuhilhna in Khristian biakna a bawl hi, upmite in Pa a phat uh a, Tapa a zui uh a, Kha a kinga uh ahih manin.

records.english: For many believers, the Trinity matters less as a puzzle to solve than as a description of the God they meet in prayer.
records.zomi: Upmi tampi adingin Trinity pen sut ding puzzle khat sangin thungetna-a a kimuh uh Pasian' genna khat bangin a thupi zaw hi.

records.english: Is today Trinity Sunday?
records.zomi: Tuni pen Trinity Nipini ahi hiam?

records.english: In Matthew's Gospel, Jesus tells his followers to baptize in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit.
records.zomi: Matthai Lungdamna Thu ah Jesu in a nungzuite kiangah Pa' min tawh, Tapa' min tawh, Kha Siangtho' min tawh tuiphum dingin a hilh hi.

records.english: The Holy Spirit is the third person of the Trinity.
records.zomi: Kha Siangtho pen Trinity' a thumna ahi hi.

records.english: In our church, the blessing at the end of the service names all three persons of the Trinity.
records.zomi: I pawlpi ah biakna tawpna-a thupha in Trinity' a thum khempeuh a min a sam hi.

records.english: Reading the Gospels with the Trinity in mind, some readers notice how often Jesus speaks of the Father and promises the Spirit.
records.zomi: Trinity lungsim sungah koih-in Lungdamna Thu laibute sim in simmi pawl khat in Jesu in Pa thu bangzah a gen a, Kha a kiciamsak hiam a phawk uh hi.

records.english: Respectful conversations between Christians and people of other faiths often begin by acknowledging that they disagree about the Trinity.
records.zomi: Khristiante leh biakna dang nei mite kikal-a zahtakna kikupnate in Trinity tungtang a kikalh uh hi, ci pom tawh a kipan zel hi.

records.english: Christians believe that the Son did not begin to exist at Christmas but has always been with the Father.
records.zomi: Khristiante in Tapa pen Christmas ciangin a om kipan hi lo-in Pa tawh a om tawntung khin hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: Some teachers compare the Trinity to water, ice and steam, but they usually add that the comparison is imperfect.
records.zomi: Saya pawl khat in Trinity pen tui, tuikhal leh tui-ngial tawh a teh uh a, ahi zongin tua tehna a kicing lo hi, ci-in a behlap zel uh hi.

records.english: Is Jesus the same as God the Father?
records.zomi: Jesu pen Pasian Pa tawh a kibang hiam?

records.english: Christians believe they are one God but distinct persons.
records.zomi: Khristiante in Pasian khat ahi uh a, ahi zongin mi tuam ahi uh hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: Did you hear the pastor's sermon on the Trinity?
records.zomi: Pastor' Trinity tungtang thugenna na za hiam?

records.english: Do all Christians believe in the Trinity?
records.zomi: Khristian khempeuh in Trinity a um uh hiam?

records.english: Most do, but a few groups that call themselves Christian don't.
records.zomi: A tamzaw in a um uh a, ahi zongin Khristian kici pawl tawmno in a um kei uh hi.

records.english: Teaching children about the Trinity requires simple language that does not distort what the churches actually teach.
records.zomi: Naupangte Trinity tungtang hilh in pawlpite' hilhna taktak a susia lo kammal baih a kisam hi.

records.english: The three persons are the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit.
records.zomi: Mi thumte pen Pa, Tapa leh Kha Siangtho ahi uh hi.

records.english: Because every comparison for the Trinity falls short, many teachers prefer to begin with what the Bible says each person does.
records.zomi: Trinity adingin tehna khempeuh a cing lo ahih manin saya tampi in mi khatciat in bang a bawl hiam Laisiangtho in a gen tawh kipan a deih zaw uh hi.

records.english: Our youth group spent the whole evening asking questions about the Trinity.
records.zomi: I khangno pawl in Trinity tungtang dotnate nitak bup a dong uh hi.

records.english: Many theologians describe the Trinity as an eternal relationship of love, which they see as a pattern for human community.
records.zomi: Pasian thu siam tampi in Trinity pen itna kizopna tawntung khat ahi a, mihing khua adingin entawn ding khat a mu uh hi.

records.english: Many churches celebrate Trinity Sunday on the Sunday after Pentecost.
records.zomi: Pawlpi tampi in Pentecost khit Nipini ciangin Trinity Nipini a bawl uh hi.

records.english: Shall we sing the hymn to the Father, the Son and the Spirit?
records.zomi: Pa, Tapa leh Kha phatna la i sa ding hiam?

records.english: Hymns written over many centuries often end with a verse praising the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit together.
records.zomi: Kum za tampi sung kigelh late in Pa, Tapa leh Kha Siangtho a khawm-a phatna kawm khat tawh a tawp zel hi.

records.english: Eastern and Western churches have long disagreed over whether the Nicene Creed should say that the Spirit proceeds from the Father alone or from the Father and the Son.
records.zomi: Nisuahna lam leh nitumna lam pawlpite in Nicene Creed in Kha pen Pa kiang pan bek a pusuak hiam, Pa leh Tapa kiang pan a pusuak hiam a cih ding tungtang hun sawtpi a kikalh uh hi.

records.english: The doctrine of the Trinity was set out in detail at church councils in the fourth century, especially at Nicaea and Constantinople.
records.zomi: Trinity thuhilhna pen kum za lina-a pawlpi kikhopna lianpite ah, a diak in Nicaea leh Constantinople ah, kician takin kigelh hi.

records.english: Children often ask hard questions about God.
records.zomi: Naupangte in Pasian tungtang dotna haksate a dong zel uh hi.

records.english: Christians also hold that God is one, as the ancient words "Hear, O Israel: the Lord our God, the Lord is one" declare.
records.zomi: Khristiante in "Israel mite aw ngai un! Eite Topa Pasian in Topa khat bek ahi hi" cih kammal lui te' gen bangin Pasian pen khat ahi hi, ci-in a pom uh hi.

records.english: Is the Trinity in the Bible?
records.zomi: Trinity pen Laisiangtho sungah om hiam?

records.english: The term isn't used, but Christians believe the teaching comes from the Bible.
records.zomi: Tua kammal kizang kei a, ahi zongin Khristiante in tua thuhilhna Laisiangtho pan hong pai hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: How would you explain the Trinity to a ten-year-old?
records.zomi: Kum sawm naupang khat kiangah Trinity bangci-in na genteh ding hiam?

records.english: I'd start with the stories in which all three appear together, like Jesus' baptism.
records.zomi: Jesu' tuiphumna bang a thum a khawm-a a kilang tangthute tawh ka kipan ding hi.

records.english: Read the story of Jesus' baptism in Mark 1.
records.zomi: Marka 1 sung-a Jesu' tuiphumna tangthu sim in.

records.english: Do you keep your bills on paper or on your computer?

records.zomi: Lai tungah, screen sangin folder ka muang zaw ahih manin.

records.english: Professional organizers often advise sorting things by how often they're used, not by what they are.
records.zomi: Siamna nei gelh siamte in van a ahihna sangin a zat tam dan tawh khen dingin a hilh zel uh hi.

records.english: Children who help decide where things belong are more likely to put them back.
records.zomi: Van koi ah om ding hiam a khen huh naupangte in a koih kik zawk ding uh hi.

records.english: Which cupboard should the glasses go in?
records.zomi: Haaite bang van bawm sungah koih ding hiam?

records.english: Storage that is easy to reach gets used, whereas a perfect system on a high shelf is soon ignored.
records.zomi: Tun baih van koihna a kizang a, van koihna sang tung-a gelhna kicing khat pah-in kipaaimawh hi.

records.english: Washing the car by hand takes longer than going to the car wash, but it's cheaper and more thorough.

records.english: Microfibre cloths cost more at first, but they work out cheaper than paper towels in the long run.

records.english: Is it better to sell old furniture online or give it to someone who needs it?
records.zomi: Inn van luite online-in zuak a hoih zaw hiam, a kisam mi khat kiangah pia a hoih zaw hiam?

records.english: Do you arrange your books by colour or by author?

records.zomi: A gelhpa tawh, ka tanu in rong a deih zaw hangin.

records.english: Sorting the cupboard took less time than I expected, because I didn't stop to read every letter.
records.zomi: Lai khempeuh sim dingin ka khawl loh manin van bawm khen ka lamen sangin hun tawm zaw a la hi.

records.english: Paper records can't be hacked, while digital copies can't be lost in a fire.
records.zomi: Lai ciamtehnate hack thei lo a, digital copy te mei-ah a kang thei kei hi.

records.english: Some families choose to own very little, while others see full cupboards as security after hard times.
records.zomi: Innkuan pawl khat in van tawmno bek nei a teel uh a, a dangte in hun haksa khit ciangin van bawm dim te muanna bangin a mu uh hi.

records.english: Choosing good storage once usually costs less over the years than replacing cheap boxes again and again.

records.english: My husband is tidier than I am, but I'm better at cleaning.

records.english: Sweaters keep their shape better folded than on hangers.
records.zomi: Puan lum te khai sangin khuk-in koih ciangin a lim a kem zaw uh hi.

records.english: We chose a bed with drawers underneath instead of buying another wardrobe.
records.zomi: Puan koihna dang khat lei sangin a nuai ah bawm neu nei lupna khat i teel uh hi.

records.english: Do you want to keep this lamp or give it away?
records.zomi: Hih meivak na kem ding hiam, na pia ding hiam?

records.english: Give it away, because we never use it.
records.zomi: Pia in, i zang ngei kei ahih manin.

records.english: Strong-smelling cleaning products are not necessarily more effective than mild ones.

records.english: What looks like clutter to one person may be a carefully kept collection to another.
records.zomi: Mi khat adingin van buai bangin a kilang in mi dang khat adingin limtak-a a kem van kaikhawm hi thei hi.

records.english: Rotating children's toys keeps them more interested than having everything out at once.

records.english: Open shelves look nice, but closed cupboards hide the mess.

records.english: Had we chosen the flat with the larger kitchen instead of the extra bedroom, our cooking things would finally have a home.
records.zomi: Inndei behlap sangin an huanna inn lian zaw nei inn i teel nak leh i an huanna vante in a tawpna ah mun a nei ding uh hi.

records.english: My son knows where everything is in his messy room, but I lose things in my tidy one!
records.zomi: Ka tapa in a inndei buai sungah khempeuh koi ah om hiam a thei a, ahi zongin kei in ka inndei siang sungah van ka mangsak hi!

records.english: Of all the rooms in our house, the bathroom is the easiest to keep clean and the hall is the hardest.
records.zomi: I inn-a inndei khempeuh lak ah kisilna inn siangtak-a kem a baih pen a, inn sung lampi a haksa pen hi.

records.english: My son's room is tidier than mine!
records.zomi: Ka tapa' inndei ka inndei sangin a siang zaw hi!

records.english: Should old cables be kept in one big box or sorted into small bags?
records.zomi: Cable luite bawm lian khat sungah koih ding hiam, ip neu te sungah khen ding hiam?

records.english: Small bags with labels, or you'll spend an hour untangling them.
records.zomi: Ciamtehna nei ip neute, ahih kei leh a kikhihte sut dingin hun khat na zang ding hi.

records.english: The old wooden chest holds more than the new plastic boxes, but it's much heavier to move.
records.zomi: Sing bawm lui in plastic bawm thakte sangin tam zaw a koih thei a, ahi zongin sawn dingin a gik zaw mahmah hi.

records.english: Some people feel calm only when everything is put away, while others work best surrounded by their things.

records.english: Is it easier to keep a big house clean or a small flat?
records.zomi: Inn lian siangtak-a kem a baih zaw hiam, inn neu kem a baih zaw hiam?

records.english: A small flat, although there's nowhere to hide the mess!
records.zomi: Inn neu, buaina selna mun om lo ahi zongin!

records.english: A clean sink makes the whole kitchen look better.
records.zomi: Kuang silna siang khat in an huanna inn bup a hoih zawsak hi.

records.english: Where shall I put the Christmas decorations?
records.zomi: Christmas kizeemna vante koi ah ka koih ding hiam?

records.english: My sister keeps almost nothing, while my brother can't throw away a single magazine.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam numei in bangmah dekin kem lo a, ka sanggam pasal in magazine khat zong paai thei lo hi.

records.english: A cupboard arranged by meal is easier to use than one arranged by size.
records.zomi: An nekna hun tawh kikoih van bawm khat in a lianna tawh kikoih khat sangin zat a baih zaw hi.

records.english: Is a perfectly organized home worth the time it takes to keep it that way?
records.zomi: A kicing taka kigelh inn khat pen tua bangin kem nading hun tawh a man a phu hiam?

records.english: Which is messier, your desk at work or your desk at home?
records.zomi: Bang in a buai zaw hiam, nasepna-a na dawhkan hiam, inn-a na dawhkan hiam?

records.english: My desk at home, because nobody else sees it.
records.zomi: Inn-a ka dawhkan, kuamah in a muh loh manin.

records.english: I'd choose one good cupboard over three cheap ones that fall apart.
records.zomi: A kitam thei man neu thum sangin van bawm hoih khat ka teel ding hi.

records.english: Cleaning before guests arrive is more stressful than cleaning after they've gone.
records.zomi: Khualte a tun ma-in siangsak pen a pai khit uh ciangin siangsak sangin a lungkhamhuai zaw hi.

records.english: I had no idea the floor was this colour!
records.zomi: Leitang hih rong ahi hi, ci ka thei ngei kei hi!

records.english: Why not use hooks instead of hangers for the children's coats?
records.zomi: Naupangte' puan lum adingin khaina sangin khaina hiil zang lo ding i hi hiam?

records.english: Shall we put a small bin in every room instead of one big one in the kitchen?
records.zomi: An huanna inn-a bawm lian khat sangin inndei khempeuh ah eekbawm neu khat i koih ding hiam?

records.english: A shoe rack by the door works better than asking everyone to take their shoes upstairs.
records.zomi: Kongkhak kiang-a khedap koihna in mi khempeuh khedap inn tung ah tawi dingin ngen sangin a sem hoih zaw hi.

records.english: A bowl for keys on the hall table is cheaper than any clever gadget for finding them.
records.zomi: Inn sung lampi dawhkan tung-a tawh koihna kuang khat in tawh zonna set siam bangpeuh sangin a man neu zaw hi.

records.english: My father prefers a toolbox he can carry, whereas my mother likes the tools hanging on the wall.
records.zomi: Ka pa in a tawi theih vanzat bawm a deih zaw a, ka nu in vanzatte inn bang tungah a khai a deih hi.

records.english: I like a clean kitchen even more than a clean bathroom.
records.zomi: Kisilna inn siang sangin an huanna inn siang ka deih zaw lai hi.

records.zomi: Khuapi ah nasep a deih uh hi.

records.english: Is there always only one cause?
records.zomi: A hang khat bek a om tawntung hiam?

records.english: What changed after the school opened?
records.zomi: Sang a kihon khit ciangin bang a kikheel hiam?

records.english: More girls learned to read and write.
records.zomi: Numei naupang tam zaw in lai sim leh gelh a sin uh hi.

records.english: The arrival of mobile phones changed how families who live far apart keep in touch.
records.zomi: Phone te a tun in gamla-a teeng innkuante kizopna a kheel hi.

records.english: Sorry, I wrote the effect before the cause in my answer.
records.zomi: Maisak in, ka dawnna sungah a hang ma-in a lohna ka gelh hi.

records.english: In many periods of history, rising bread prices led to protests.
records.zomi: Tangthu hun tampi ah moh man a khan in nialna te a piangsak hi.

records.english: Some causes are long-term, such as poverty, while others are sudden, such as a storm.

records.english: What happened because of the new road?
records.zomi: Lampi thak hangin bang a piang hiam?

records.english: More people came to the market, and the village grew.
records.zomi: Zuakna mun ah mi tam zaw a hong uh a, khua a khang hi.

records.english: The stock market crash of 1929 was followed by years of hardship in many countries.
records.zomi: Kum 1929-a stock market tuksiatna khit ciangin gam tampi ah kum tampi haksatna a om hi.

records.english: The railway brought new jobs to the valley.
records.zomi: Meileng lampi in guam ah nasep thakte a tawi hi.

records.english: A chain of small causes, each harmless on its own, can sometimes lead to a large and sudden change.

records.english: When the mine closed, the shops that depended on the miners closed too.

records.english: A short-term cause is like a spark, while long-term causes are like the dry wood that lets a fire spread.

records.english: The same event can be a cause in one story and an effect in another, depending on where the historian begins.

records.zomi: A masa-a piang khat in a nung-a piang a piangsak tawntung kei ahih manin tangthu siamte in kizopna taktak lahna a zong uh hi.

records.english: The Black Death in the fourteenth century killed so many people in Europe that the workers who survived could demand higher wages.

records.english: Ask your grandparents how electricity changed their daily lives.
records.zomi: Meivak in amaute' ni sim nuntakna bangci-in a kheel hiam na pu leh na pi dong in.

records.english: Write one cause and one effect.
records.zomi: A hang khat leh a lohna khat gelh in.

records.english: The killing of an archduke in 1914 is often called the spark of the First World War.

records.english: The famine in Ireland in the 1840s led about a million people to emigrate, many of them to America.

records.zomi: A hang khatciat pan a lohna dong thal lim khat gelh in.

records.zomi: I saya in zuakna mun bang hangin a tai hiam genteh dingin hong ngen hi.

records.english: Vaccination campaigns led to smallpox being declared eradicated in 1980.

records.english: Think about why it happened, not just when.
records.zomi: Bang ciangin cih bek hi lo-in bang hangin a piang hiam ngaihsun in.

records.english: Why did the war start?
records.zomi: Bang hangin gal a kipan hiam?

records.english: There were many causes, not just one.
records.zomi: A hang tampi a om a, khat bek hi lo hi.

records.english: Historians usually look for several causes, because major events rarely have a single explanation.
records.zomi: Tangthu siamte in a hang tampi a zong zel uh hi, thu piang lianpite in genteh khat bek a nei ngei tuan kei uh ahih manin.

records.english: Rain ruined the harvest, and food became expensive.
records.zomi: Guah in lo at a susia a, an a man tam hi.

records.english: Unintended consequences, such as new roads emptying villages instead of helping them, often teach as much as planned ones.
records.zomi: Lamen loh lohnate, lampi thakte in khuate a huh sangin a awngsak bang, in geel lohnate bangin a sinsak tam zel hi.

records.english: Asking what-if questions can help students see which causes really mattered.

records.english: Was it a good change or a bad one?
records.zomi: Kikheelna hoih ahi hiam, hoih lo ahi hiam?

records.english: Both, depending on who you ask.
records.zomi: A nih, kua na dong hiam tungah kinga-in.

records.english: Technological changes often have social effects, such as the way factory work changed family life.
records.zomi: Set lam kikheelnate in mipi tungah lohna a nei zel a, factory nasep in innkuan nuntakna a kheel dan bangin.

records.english: One change can have effects that nobody planned or expected.
records.zomi: Kikheelna khat in kuamah in a geel loh hiam a lamen loh lohnate a nei thei hi.

records.english: So the new road came first, and the market grew because of it?
records.zomi: Tua ahih leh lampi thak a masa a, tua hangin zuakna mun a khang hi, hi hiam?

records.english: After the school bus started, fewer children left school early.
records.zomi: Sang bus a kipat khit ciangin naupang tawm zaw in sang a nusia ngal uh hi.

records.english: Effects can last long after their causes are forgotten, such as borders drawn for reasons nobody remembers.
records.zomi: Lohnate a hangte a kimangngilh khit sawt mahmah zongin a om thei a, kuamah in a phawk loh hang-a kigelh gamgite bangin.

records.english: When ships became larger, small harbours lost trade to deep-water ports.
records.zomi: Tembaw te a lian semsem ciangin tuipi gei neute in tui thuk tembaw khawlna munte tungah sumbawlna a mansuah uh hi.

records.english: When railways were built, fresh food could reach cities before it spoiled.
records.zomi: Meileng lampite a kilam ciangin an thak te a siat ma-in khuapite a tung thei hi.

records.english: How do historians decide which cause was most important?
records.zomi: Tangthu siamte in bang a hang in a thupi pen hiam bangci-in a khen uh hiam?

records.english: They compare the evidence and ask what would have happened without each cause.
records.zomi: Lahnate a teh uh a, a hang khatciat om lo leh bang a piang ding hiam a dong uh hi.

records.english: Understanding causes helps communities prepare for the future, although history never repeats itself exactly.
records.zomi: A hangte theih in khuate a hong tung ding adingin a kiman nadingin a huh a, tangthu in diktakin a kik ngei kei hangin.

records.english: Potatoes, which came to Europe from the Americas, changed what millions of people ate.

records.english: Who can apply for the housing grant?

records.english: Clear guidance on who is eligible can save both applicants and officials a great deal of wasted time.

records.english: Most applications are decided within a month, but complicated cases can take longer.

records.english: Check the list of documents before you go.
records.zomi: Na pai ma-in lai kisam list en in.

records.english: Why was my application returned?

records.english: In a crisis, practical help, such as finding a quiet place or calling a relative, often matters more than finding perfect words.

records.english: A claim is only as strong as the evidence that supports it.
records.zomi: Gen khat pen a thuak lahna zah bek in a hat hi.

records.english: Testimonials on a company's website are chosen by the company, so they may not be typical.
records.zomi: Company' website tung-a phatnate company mah in a teel ahih manin a ngeina hi kha lo thei hi.

records.english: The salesman's claim that the car had never been in an accident turned out to be false.
records.zomi: Mawtaw zuakpa in mawtaw accident a tuah ngei kei hi, a cih pen a zuau hi, ci-in a kimu hi.

records.english: A single dramatic example often spreads faster than careful research, even when the research is more accurate.
records.zomi: Entehna lamdang khat in limtaka sinna sangin a manlang zaw-in a zel zel hi, sinna a dik zaw zongin.

records.english: A confident tone is not evidence, however persuasive it sounds.
records.zomi: Kingapna aw pen lahna hi lo hi, bangzah lungsim kheelsak bang a ging zongin.

records.english: When you write an argument, give at least one reason and one piece of evidence for each claim.
records.zomi: Kinialna khat na gelh ciangin gen khatciat adingin a hang khat leh lahna khat tal pia in.

records.english: What counts as good evidence in a science essay?
records.zomi: Science essay khat ah bang in lahna hoih ahi hiam?

records.english: Measurements, results from experiments, and reliable published studies.
records.zomi: Tehnate, sinna lohnate leh muanhuai kikhet sinnate.

records.english: Evidence from different kinds of sources, such as records, interviews and measurements, is more convincing when it all points the same way.
records.zomi: Ciamtehna, kidotna leh tehna bang kipatna tuamtuam pan lahnate in a khempeuh lam khat ah a lak ciangin lungsim a kheelsak zaw hi.

records.english: If a claim sounds too good to be true, look for evidence before you share it.
records.zomi: Gen khat a hoih lua-in a tak hi kha lo bangin a ging leh na hawm ma-in lahna zong in.

records.english: My brother claims he saw a wolf in the forest.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in gammang sungah ngiaksi lian khat ka mu hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Sorry, I said the figure was from the government, but I can't find where I read it.
records.zomi: Maisak in, nambat pen kumpi pan ahi hi, ka ci a, ahi zongin koi ah ka sim hiam ka mu thei kei hi.

records.english: Let me see the data.
records.zomi: Data hong etsak in.

records.english: Our class tested the claim that hot water freezes faster than cold water, and the results were mixed.
records.zomi: I class in tui lum in tui vot sangin a khal manlang zaw hi, cih gen a sit uh a, a lohnate a kihel hi.

records.english: Can you show me the report?
records.zomi: Report hong etsak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: My neighbor didn't call for help at first, because she didn't want to make a fuss.
records.zomi: Ka inn veng in buaina bawl a nop loh manin a masa-in huhna a sam kei hi.

records.english: When you call for help, give your location first, in case the line is cut.
records.zomi: Huhna na sam ciangin line a tat kha leh ci-in na omna mun a masa-in gen in.

records.english: Somebody fetch the first-aid kit!
records.zomi: Kuamah in huhna masa bawm tawi un!

records.english: Many phones can share their exact location with the emergency services.
records.zomi: Phone tampi in lauhuai hun huh nasepte kiangah a omna mun diktak a hawm thei hi.

records.english: Bystanders who call for help and then follow the handler's instructions can make a life-saving difference before professionals arrive.
records.zomi: Huhna a sam-a a sam pa' hilhnate a zui kiang-a om mite in siamna nei mite a tun ma-in nuntakna hon kibatlohna a bawl thei uh hi.

records.english: Can you see any street signs near you?
records.zomi: Na kiangah lampi min ciamtehna na mu thei hiam?

records.english: Our house is the blue one next to the school.
records.zomi: I inn pen sang kiang-a dum pen ahi hi.

records.english: There's been an accident on the main road.
records.zomi: Lampi lian tungah accident khat a piang hi.

records.english: In many European countries, the emergency number is 112.
records.zomi: Europe gam tampi ah lauhuai hun nambat pen 112 ahi hi.

records.english: Had the boy not known his address, the ambulance might have gone to the wrong village.
records.zomi: Tangval neu in a teenna mun a theih kei leh ambulance in khua khial ah a pai kha ding hi.

records.english: After the storm, the lines were busy, so we kept trying every few minutes.
records.zomi: Huihpi khit ciangin line te a buai ahih manin minit tawmno simin i sin den uh hi.

records.english: Interpreting services allow some emergency lines to help callers who do not speak the main language.
records.zomi: Pau letna nasepnate in lauhuai hun phone pawl khat in pau lianpen zang thei lo samte a huh thei hi.

records.english: Please hurry!
records.zomi: Manlang takin pai un!

records.english: Turn on the outside light so that they can find the house.
records.zomi: Inn a muh theih nadingun pua lam meivak vaksak in.

records.english: I can smell gas in the flat.
records.zomi: Inn sungah gas gim ka nam hi.

records.english: Clear house numbers and signs help emergency crews find people quickly, especially at night.
records.zomi: Inn nambat leh ciamtehna kician te in lauhuai hun huh nasemte mite manlang takin a muh nadingin a huh hi, a diak in zan ciangin.

records.english: My child swallowed some pills.
records.zomi: Ka naupang in zatui tawmno a val hi.

records.english: Help, someone has fallen into the river!
records.zomi: Hong huh un, mi khat gun sungah a kia hi!

records.english: If you see smoke coming from a neighbor's house, call for help before you knock on the door.
records.zomi: Inn veng khat' inn pan meikhu a suak na muh leh kongkhak na kiu ma-in huhna sam in.

records.english: Many people hesitate to call for help because they fear wasting the services' time, but delays can be far more costly.
records.zomi: Mi tampi in nasepnate' hun mawk zat ding a lau uh ahih manin huhna sam a lau zel uh a, ahi zongin ngakna in a man tam zaw mahmah thei hi.

records.english: For problems that aren't emergencies, such as a stolen bicycle, use the police non-emergency number.
records.zomi: Siiksakol kiguk bang lauhuai hun hi lo buainate adingin palik' lauhuai hun hi lo nambat zang in.

records.english: If someone is choking and can't breathe or speak, call for help immediately.
records.zomi: Mi khat a ngawng a dek-a huih a la thei lo hiam a gen thei lo leh pah-in huhna sam in.

records.english: Do you need the fire service, the police or an ambulance?
records.zomi: Mei mitna nasep, palik hiam ambulance na kisam hiam?

records.english: What's the address?
records.zomi: Teenna mun bang hiam?

records.english: My father has fallen and can't get up.
records.zomi: Ka pa a puk a, a thou thei kei hi.

records.english: Callers who stay calm and answer the handler's questions help the emergency services decide what kind of help to send.
records.zomi: Dai taka om-a a sam pa' dotnate a dawng samte in lauhuai hun huh nasepte in bang huhna sawl ding hiam a khen nadingin a huh uh hi.

records.english: Emergency services in rural areas may take longer to arrive, which makes basic first-aid knowledge especially valuable.
records.zomi: Gamlak-a lauhuai hun huh nasepte a tun sawt zaw thei ahih manin huhna masa theihna kipatna a manpha diak hi.

records.english: Stay on the line, please.
records.zomi: Line tungah om lai un, kong ngen hi.

records.english: So you want me to put her on her side and check that she's still breathing?
records.zomi: Tua ahih leh a ning lam ah lum sak-in a huih a la lai hiam en dingin hong deih hi, hi hiam?

records.english: Practising what to do in an emergency, as schools do with fire drills, makes calm action more likely when it really happens.
records.zomi: Sangte in mei kidawm kisinna a bawl bangin lauhuai hun ah bang bawl ding hiam kisin in a piang taktak ciangin dai taka bawl a baihsak zaw hi.

records.english: Save your doctor's number in your phone.
records.zomi: Na siavuan' nambat na phone sungah koih in.

records.english: Don't hang up until they tell you to.
records.zomi: Amaute in a hong gen dong phone khak kei in.

records.english: Write the emergency number on the fridge.
records.zomi: Khal bawm tungah lauhuai hun nambat gelh in.

records.english: Should I move someone who has been hurt in a fall?
records.zomi: Puk-in a liam mi khat ka sawn ding hiam?

records.english: Not unless they're in danger, because moving them could make an injury worse.
records.zomi: Lauhuai sungah a om kei leh sawn kei in, sawn in a liamna a gilo zaw sak thei ahih manin.

records.english: Keep talking to him until help arrives.
records.zomi: Huhna a tun dong amah tawh kiho den in.

records.english: Learning a few emergency words in the local language is wise before travelling abroad.
records.zomi: Gamdang ah khualzin ma-in mun lai pau-a lauhuai hun kammal tawmno sin pen a pil hi.

records.english: A false alarm made in good faith is very different from a prank call, which can put lives at risk.
records.zomi: Lungsim hoih tawh kibawl lauhuai sapna khial khat pen nuihzaak sapna, nuntakna lauhuai sak thei, tawh a kibang lo mahmah hi.

records.english: It's better to call and be told it wasn't serious than not to call at all.
records.zomi: A gik kei hi, ci-a kigen sam pen sam lo sangin a hoih zaw hi.

records.english: How old is the patient?
records.zomi: Damlo kum bangzah a cing hiam?

records.english: In the United States and Canada, the emergency number is 911.
records.zomi: United States leh Canada ah lauhuai hun nambat pen 911 ahi hi.

records.english: What should I say when I call for an ambulance?
records.zomi: Ambulance ka sam ciangin bang ka gen ding hiam?

records.english: Say where you are, what has happened, and how many people need help.
records.zomi: Koi ah na om hiam, bang a piang hiam, mi bangzah in huhna a kisam uh hiam gen in.

records.english: The shop assistant called for help when a customer fainted at the till.
records.zomi: Van lei mi khat sum piakna mun ah a kia ciangin dawl nasem in huhna a sam hi.

records.english: Sorry, I called the emergency number by mistake when my phone was in my pocket.
records.zomi: Maisak in, ka phone ka puan ip sungah a om laitakin lauhuai hun nambat khial takin ka sam hi.

records.english: Is the fire spreading?
records.zomi: Mei a zel hiam?

records.english: Is the person breathing?
records.zomi: Mi pen huih a la hiam?

records.english: There's smoke coming from the kitchen.
records.zomi: An huanna inn pan meikhu a suak hi.

records.english: Should every school teach children how to make an emergency call?
records.zomi: Sang khempeuh in naupangte lauhuai hun sapna bangci bawl ding hiam a sinsak ding uh hiam?

records.english: Send someone to wait at the gate for the ambulance.
records.zomi: Ambulance ngak dingin mi khat kongpi ah sawl in.

records.english: If you can't speak safely, some emergency services let you send a text message instead.
records.zomi: Bit takin na gen thei kei leh lauhuai hun huh nasep pawl khat in text message khak sak hi.

records.english: Unlock the front door so that they can get in.
records.zomi: A lut theih nadingun mai lam kongkhak hong in.

records.english: Older people living alone may need a simple way to call for help that does not depend on reaching a phone.
records.zomi: Kia-a teeng mi upate in phone tun kisam lo-in huhna sam nading lampi baih khat a kisam kha thei uh hi.

records.english: Leave the building first, and call the fire service once you're outside.
records.zomi: Inn a masa-in nusia inla, pua ah na om khit ciangin mei mitna nasep sam in.

records.english: Children should practise saying their full address and a parent's phone number.
records.zomi: Naupangte in a teenna mun kicing leh nu hiam pa' phone nambat gen a kisin ding uh hi.

records.english: The call handler told me how to press on his chest until the ambulance arrived.
records.zomi: Sapna dawngpa in ambulance a tun dong a awm bangci-in nawi ding hiam hong hilh hi.

records.english: The operator stayed on the phone with my mother until the firefighters arrived.
records.zomi: Phone dawngpa in mei mitte a tun dong ka nu tawh phone tungah a om hi.

records.english: When several people are present, it helps to point at one person and ask them directly to call for help.
records.zomi: Mi tampi a om ciangin mi khat lak-a amah tangtak huhna sam dingin ngen a huh hi.

records.english: Poison centres can tell you what to do if a child swallows something dangerous.
records.zomi: Gu nekna huhna munte in naupang khat in lauhuai bangmah a val leh bang bawl ding hiam a hilh thei hi.

records.english: I'm afraid I can't tell you exactly where we are, but we're on the road between the two villages.
records.zomi: Koi ah i om uh hiam diktakin kong gen thei kei hi, ci ka lau hi, ahi zongin khua nih kikal lampi tungah i om uh hi.

records.english: The village looks like a picture postcard in winter.
records.zomi: Phalbi ciangin khua in postcard lim bangin a kilawm hi.

records.english: A village's name often carries a story about the people who first settled there.
records.zomi: Khua khat' min in a masa pen-a teeng mite tungtang tangthu khat a pua zel hi.

records.english: Everyone knows everyone here.
records.zomi: Hih ah mi khempeuh a kithei uh hi.

records.english: The sounds of a village change with the seasons, from the frogs of the rainy months to the silence of a frosty morning.
records.zomi: Khua' ging te hun tawh a kikheel a, guah kha te-a uute pan vuk zingsang' daina dong.

records.english: Most houses have a small vegetable garden.
records.zomi: Inn a tamzaw in anteh huan neu khat a nei uh hi.

records.english: There are rice fields all around the village.
records.zomi: Khua kim leh pam ah buh lo te a om hi.

records.english: As the village grew, the old footpaths were slowly replaced by roads wide enough for trucks.
records.zomi: Khua a khan ciangin kalsuanna lampi luite dawngdawng-in mawtaw lian te a pai thei lampi zai te in a laih hi.

records.english: When it rains, the main path turns into a stream of red mud.
records.zomi: Guah a zuk ciangin lampi lian lei san tuiluang khat ah a kheel hi.

records.english: What's your village like?
records.zomi: Na khua bangci om hiam?

records.english: Quiet, green and very friendly.
records.zomi: Dai, eng, leh mi hoih mahmah.

records.english: Our village is small but beautiful.
records.zomi: I khua a neu a, ahi zongin a kilawm hi.

records.english: The only sound at midday is the wind in the bamboo.
records.zomi: Sun lai-in ging khat bek pen ua lak-a huih ahi hi.

records.english: Every family keeps a few pigs and chickens behind the house.
records.zomi: Innkuan khempeuh in inn nung ah vok leh ak tawmno a vak uh hi.

records.english: How far is the nearest town?
records.zomi: Khuapi a nai pen bangzah gamla hiam?

records.english: Most of the young people have moved to the city, so the village is quieter than it used to be.
records.zomi: Khangno a tamzaw khuapi ah a tai uh ahih manin khua a masa sangin a dai zaw hi.

records.english: The river runs along the bottom of the valley.
records.zomi: Gun in guam nuai lam ah a luang hi.

records.english: On market day, the quiet square fills with stalls before the sun is up.
records.zomi: Zuakna ni ciangin ni a suak ma-in mun lai dai van zuakna mun tawh a dim hi.

records.english: Women from the hills bring baskets of beans and ginger, and the fishmonger arrives from the river with his cart.
records.zomi: Mualtung pan numeite in be leh siing paikawng a tawi uh a, nga zuakpa gun pan a leng tawh a tung hi.

records.english: By noon the square is empty again, except for the dogs searching for scraps.
records.zomi: Sun lai ciangin mun lai a awng kik a, an neu zong uite simloh.

records.english: What do people in your village do for a living?
records.zomi: Na khua-a mite nuntak nadingin bang nasep a sem uh hiam?

records.english: Most of them farm, and a few work in the town during the week.
records.zomi: A tamzaw in lo a sem uh a, tawmno in kal sung khuapi ah nasep a sem uh hi.

records.english: Villages that once depended entirely on farming now often rely on money sent home by relatives working elsewhere.
records.zomi: Lo nasep tungah a kinga kim ngei khuate in tu-in mun dang ah nasep a sem sanggamte' a khak sum tungah a kinga zel uh hi.

records.english: Is it possible to describe a place fairly if you have only ever visited it on holiday?
records.zomi: Tawlngakni ah bek na veh ngeih mun khat dik takin na gen thei hiam?

records.english: The terraced fields climb the hillside like giant green steps.
records.zomi: Lo kisuang te mual nai tungah kahlei eng lian bangin a kah hi.

records.english: The houses at the top of the village have the best view but the longest walk to the river.
records.zomi: Khua tung lam-a inn te in muh nop pen a nei uh a, ahi zongin gun dong lampi a sau pen hi.

records.english: Writers who describe villages from memory sometimes make them more beautiful than they really were.
records.zomi: Phawkna pan khuate a gen laigelhmite in a taktak sangin a kilawm zawsak zel uh hi.

records.english: In the middle of the village, there's a big tree where the old men sit and talk.
records.zomi: Khua lai ah pasal upate a tut-a a kikupna sing lian khat a om hi.

records.english: Good descriptive writing helps readers see a place through the senses, not just through a list of buildings.
records.zomi: Genna laigelh hoih in simmite in inn list bek hi lo-in kisakna tungtawn-in mun khat a muh nadingun a huh hi.

records.english: Sorry, I can't describe it properly, so you'll have to come and see it for yourself.
records.zomi: Maisak in, dik takin ka gen thei kei ahih manin nangmah mah in hong en dingin na pai kisam ding hi.

records.english: The layout of an old village often reflects its history, with the oldest houses near the spring or the church.
records.zomi: Khua lui khat' kigelh dan in a tangthu a lak zel a, inn lui pente tui khuk hiam pawlpi kiang ah a om uh hi.

records.english: I'm afraid there's no hotel in the village, but my aunt would happily put you up.
records.zomi: Khua ah zinbuuk a om kei hi, ci ka lau hi, ahi zongin ka ni in lungdam takin hong giaksak ding hi.

records.english: Is the road to the village steep?
records.zomi: Khua dong lampi a tou mahmah hiam?

records.english: At night, the village is completely dark except for a few lamps.
records.zomi: Zan ciangin meivak tawmno simloh khua a mial kim hi.

records.english: A small stream divides the village into an upper half and a lower half.
records.zomi: Luite neu khat in khua tung lam leh nuai lam ah a khen hi.

records.english: Is there a clinic in your village?
records.zomi: Na khua ah siavuan inn a om hiam?

records.english: No, the nearest one is in the next valley.
records.zomi: Om lo hi, a nai pen a zom guam ah om hi.

records.english: Is there a shop in the village?
records.zomi: Khua ah dawl a om hiam?

records.english: Children play football on the field behind the school.
records.zomi: Naupangte in sang nung-a mun lian ah football a kimawl uh hi.

records.english: Had the new road been built ten years earlier, many families might never have left the village.
records.zomi: Lampi thak kum sawm a ngal zaw-in a kilam leh innkuan tampi in khua a nusia ngei kha lo ding uh hi.

records.english: Small communities can offer a strong sense of belonging, although some young people find them too limiting.
records.zomi: Khua neute in kihel kisakna hat a pia thei uh a, khangno pawl khat in a kiak lua sa uh hi.

records.english: How many people live in your village?
records.zomi: Na khua ah mi bangzah a teeng uh hiam?

records.english: About three hundred, I think.
records.zomi: Za thum bang, ka ci hi.

records.english: Come in spring, when the hills turn bright green.
records.zomi: Spring ciangin hong pai in, mualte a eng vak ciangin.

records.english: Is the village very different from the town?
records.zomi: Khua pen khuapi tawh a kibang lo mahmah hiam?

records.english: Completely, because here you hear birds instead of traffic.
records.zomi: A kibang kim lo hi, hih ah mawtaw ging sangin vate ging na za hi.

records.english: So the school is at the bottom of the hill and the church is at the top?
records.zomi: Tua ahih leh sang mual nuai ah om a, pawlpi a tung ah om hi, hi hiam?

records.english: On summer evenings, families sit on their verandas and call out to neighbors passing by.
records.zomi: Khal nitak te ah innkuante a inn dawh uh ah a tu uh a, a kantan inn vengte a sam uh hi.

records.english: Be careful on the old wooden bridge.
records.zomi: Sing lei lui tungah kidawm in.

records.english: Would you like me to show you around the village?
records.zomi: Khua kong etsak na deih hiam?

records.english: The market sells everything from rice and salt to batteries and plastic buckets.
records.zomi: Zuakna mun in buh leh cii pan battery leh plastic khuang dong khempeuh a zuak hi.

records.english: The village water comes from a spring higher up the hill, through a long pipe.
records.zomi: Khua' tui pen mual tung lam-a tui khuk pan pipe sau khat tungtawn-in hong pai hi.

records.english: Chickens run freely along the paths.
records.zomi: Akte lampite tungah zalen takin a tai uh hi.

records.english: Our village sits on a ridge, with a view of three valleys.
records.zomi: I khua mualdawn tungah om a, guam thum muh theihna nei hi.

records.english: The houses are built close together along a single winding road, with the church at the top and the school at the bottom.
records.zomi: Inn te lampi kikawi khat tungah a kinai takin kilam a, pawlpi a tung ah, sang a nuai ah om hi.

records.english: From the church steps on a clear morning, you can see smoke rising from the next village two hills away.
records.zomi: Zingsang siang khat ah pawlpi kahlei pan mual nih gamla-a khua dang pan meikhu a suak na mu thei hi.

records.english: Describing a village well means noticing small details, such as the colour of the roofs or the smell after rain.
records.zomi: Khua khat hoih takin gen pen inn khumte rong hiam guah khit-a gim bang neute phawk cihna ahi hi.

records.english: Why does the school have only three classrooms?
records.zomi: Bang hangin sang in sangnaupang inndei thum bek a nei hiam?

records.english: A village can look peaceful to visitors while its own people are worried about water, roads or jobs.
records.zomi: Khua khat khualte adingin a dai bangin a kilang thei a, a mite in tui, lampi hiam nasep a lunghimawh laitakin.

records.english: The paths between the houses are so narrow that two people can hardly pass each other.
records.zomi: Inn kikal-a lampite a kiak lua ahih manin mi nih a kikantan zo kei uh hi.

records.english: Can you see our house, the one near the old well?
records.zomi: I inn, tuikhuk lui kiang-a om pen, na mu thei hiam?

records.english: A basket stops me from buying more than I need.
records.zomi: Paikawng khat in ka kisam sangin tam zaw lei pan hong kem hi.

records.english: Choosing products with less packaging is easier at markets than in supermarkets, where almost everything comes wrapped.
records.zomi: Tuamna tawm zaw nei van teel pen supermarket, a tamzaw kituam, sangin zuakna mun ah a baih zaw hi.

records.english: Loose tea is cheaper than tea bags, and my grandfather says it tastes better.
records.zomi: Tea nah in tea bag sangin a man neu zaw a, ka pu in a lim zaw hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Paying a little more for fair-trade coffee helps the farmers who grow it.
records.zomi: Fair-trade coffee adingin tawmno behlap piak in a suan lo nasemte a huh hi.

records.english: The cheaper brand of washing powder works just as well.
records.zomi: Puan silna man neu zaw in a kibang mah-in a sem hi.

records.english: Fresh juice or juice from a carton?
records.zomi: Juice thak hiam carton juice hiam?

records.english: Fresh, if we have time to squeeze the oranges.
records.zomi: Thak, orange te nawi dingin hun i neih leh.

records.english: Do you want the red onions or the white ones?
records.zomi: Lothaang san te na deih hiam, a ngo te hiam?

records.english: Sorry, I bought the wrong kind of flour.
records.zomi: Maisak in, buh-mal nam khial ka lei hi.

records.english: I'm afraid I can't afford the expensive cheese this week.
records.zomi: Hih kal in cheese man tam ka lei zo kei hi, ci ka lau hi.

records.english: Do you have a smaller bag of rice?
records.zomi: Buh ip neu zaw na nei hiam?

records.english: When prices rise, many families switch to cheaper brands before they cut down on the amount they buy.
records.zomi: Man a khan ciangin innkuan tampi in a lei zah uh a neusak ma-un man neu zaw te ah a kheel uh hi.

records.english: So you'd like the brown sugar, not the white?
