records.english: Send it by ordinary post, since it doesn't need to arrive tomorrow.
records.zomi: Lai khakna ngeina tawh khak in, zingciang a tun kisam lo ahih manin.

records.english: How can I stop the plants from drying out while I'm on holiday?
records.zomi: Tawlngakni-a ka om loh laitakin singkungte a keu loh nadingin bangci-in ka kem thei ding hiam?

records.english: Put the pots in a tray of water, or ask someone to water them.
records.zomi: Beelte tui kuang sungah koih in, hiam kuamah in tui buak sak dingin ngen in.

records.english: How can we make sure the medicine is taken on time?
records.zomi: Zatui hun takin kine hiam bangci-in i ciamteh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Set an alarm on Grandpa's phone and keep a chart on the fridge.
records.zomi: Pu' phone tungah alarm koih inla, khal bawm tungah chart khat koih in.

records.english: My manager said, "Bring me two possible solutions, not just the problem."
records.zomi: Ka manager in, "Buaina bek hi lo-in vaihawmna nih hong tawi in" a ci hi.

records.english: What should we do if it rains on the day of the picnic?
records.zomi: Pua an nek ni ciangin guah a zuk leh bang i bawl ding hiam?

records.english: Move it into the church hall.
records.zomi: Pawlpi inn lian ah sawn in.

records.english: Could we ask a neighbor to feed the cat while we're away?
records.zomi: I om loh laitakin inn veng khat kiangah zaang an pia dingin i ngen thei ding hiam?

records.english: Mrs. Hau would probably be happy to do it for us.
records.zomi: Mrs. Hau in eite adingin lungdam takin a bawl kha ding hi.

records.english: Shall we ask someone who's done this before?
records.zomi: Hih a bawl ngei mi khat i dong ding hiam?

records.english: What are our options if the bus doesn't come?
records.zomi: Bus a hong kei leh bang teelnate i nei uh hiam?

records.english: We can share a taxi or walk to the main road and catch the train.
records.zomi: Taxi khat i kihawm thei uh hiam, lampi lian dong i kalsuan-a meileng i tuang thei uh hi.

records.english: How else could we get the sofa up the stairs?
records.zomi: Sofa kahlei tung ah lampi dang bangci-in i tawi tou thei ding hiam?

records.english: We could take the legs off and turn it on its side.
records.zomi: A khete i suahkhia-in a ning lam ah i heilum thei uh hi.

records.english: Any other ideas?
records.zomi: Ngaihsutna dang om lai hiam?

records.english: Some solutions create new problems, as when a wider road simply attracts more traffic.
records.zomi: Vaihawmna pawl khat in buaina thakte a piangsak hi, lampi zai zaw in mawtaw tam zaw a hong sak bangin.

records.english: Sometimes the best solution is to change the question rather than look for a better answer.
records.zomi: Pawl khat ciangin vaihawmna hoih pen pen dawnna hoih zaw zon sangin dotna kheel ahi hi.

records.english: Our kitchen tap kept dripping all night.
records.zomi: I an huanna inn tui kuang zan bup a zuk den hi.

records.english: My son searched online for solutions and found a short video about changing the washer.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in online-ah vaihawmnate a zong a, washer kheel dan video tom khat a mu hi.

records.english: Twenty minutes later, the tap was fixed, and we had saved the cost of a plumber.
records.zomi: Minit sawmnih khit ciangin tui kuang kibawlpha a, pipe bawlsiampa man i khawl uh hi.

records.english: Is there a quicker way to do this?
records.zomi: Hih bawl nading lampi manlang zaw om hiam?

records.english: Yes, if you copy the first row, the rest fills in automatically.
records.zomi: Om hi, kawm masa na copy leh a dangte amah mah in a dim hi.

records.english: Please don't throw any ideas away until we've discussed them all.
records.zomi: I kikum khit ma-un ngaihsutna khatpeuh paai kei un.

records.english: Comparing the risks of each option is as important as comparing their benefits.
records.zomi: Teelna khatciat' lauhuaina teh pen a phattuamna teh tawh a thupi kibang hi.

records.english: Exploring several solutions before choosing one often leads to a better decision than acting on the first idea.
records.zomi: Khat na teel ma-in vaihawmna tampi sin in ngaihsutna masa tungah bawl sangin thukhenna hoih zaw a tun sak zel hi.

records.english: Why don't we try it a different way?
records.zomi: Bang hangin lampi dang tawh i sin lo ding uh hiam?

records.english: Doctors often consider several possible explanations before reaching a diagnosis.
records.zomi: Siavuante in natna a theih ma-un genteh theihna tampi a ngaihsun zel uh hi.

records.english: Because the soil was dry and the leaves were yellow, the farmer concluded that the plants needed more water.
records.zomi: Lei a keu a, teh-a nahte a gial ahih manin lo neipa in singkungte in tui tam zaw a kisam uh hi, ci-in a khen hi.

records.english: The milk was delivered, but nobody took it in, so the neighbors may be away.
records.zomi: Nawi a tung a, ahi zongin kuamah in a la kei ahih manin inn vengte a om kei kha ding uh hi.

records.english: Every report was read by two teachers, so that one person's opinion wouldn't decide the result.
records.zomi: Mi khat' ngaihsutna in a lohna a khen loh nadingin report khempeuh saya nih in a sim uh hi.

records.english: Let's wait for the test results before we decide.
records.zomi: I thukhen ma-un sitna lohnate ngak ni.

records.english: Should a jury ever reach a verdict when the evidence is incomplete?
records.zomi: Lahna a kicin kei ciangin thukhen pawl in thukhenna a bawl ngei ding uh hiam?

records.english: So what's your conclusion?
records.zomi: Tua ahih leh na thukhenna bang hiam?

records.english: The cheaper bus pass is better for us, because we travel every day.
records.zomi: Bus pass man neu zaw in eite adingin a hoih zaw hi, ni simin i khualzin uh ahih manin.

records.english: We can't say the new medicine works just because one patient felt better.
records.zomi: Damlo khat a kisa hoih zaw hangin zatui thak a sem hi, i ci thei kei uh hi.

records.english: Drawing a conclusion means deciding what the evidence shows, while admitting what it does not show.
records.zomi: Thukhenna bawl pen lahna in bang a lak hiam khen a, bang a lak lo hiam pom cihna ahi hi.

records.english: In our science class, students are not allowed to change their results to fit the conclusion they expected.
records.zomi: I science class ah sangnaupangte in a lamen uh thukhenna tawh a kituak nadingin a lohnate uh kheel dingin kiphal lo hi.

records.english: People often reach the conclusion they wanted before they look at the evidence.
records.zomi: Mite in lahna a en ma-un a deih uh thukhenna a tun khin zel uh hi.

records.english: Can we be sure it was the cat?
records.zomi: Zaang ahi hi, ci i thei taktak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Not completely, but there are cat hairs all over the cushion.
records.zomi: Kicing tak kei hi, ahi zongin lukhung tungah zaang mul a dim hi.

records.english: I made a quick decision about my new colleague, and I was completely wrong about her.
records.zomi: Ka nasep pih thak tungtang manlang takin thu ka khen a, amah tungtang ka khial kim hi.

records.english: The baby is rubbing her eyes, so she's probably tired.
records.zomi: Naungek in a mit a nul ahih manin a tawl kha ding hi.

records.english: A conclusion drawn from one bad experience can turn into an unfair judgement about a whole group of people.
records.zomi: Theihna hoih lo khat pan kila thukhenna khat in mipi bup tungtang thukhenna dik lo khat ah a kheel thei hi.

records.english: Sorry, I assumed you had already eaten.
records.zomi: Maisak in, an na ne khin hi, ka ci hi.

records.english: The shop was closed again on Monday, and my neighbor concluded that it had gone out of business.
records.zomi: Pizing ni ciangin dawl a kikhak kik a, ka inn veng in sumbawlna a khawl khin hi, ci-in thu a khen hi.

records.english: Who do you think ate the last biscuit?
records.zomi: Moh khum nunung pen kua in a ne hiam, na ci hiam?

records.english: The empty bowl suggests that the dog has already been fed.
records.zomi: Kuang awng in ui an a ne khin hi, cih a lak hi.

records.english: Her coat isn't on the hook, so she can't be home yet.
records.zomi: A puan lum khaina tungah a om kei ahih manin inn ah a tung nai kei hi.

records.english: Does the evidence point to one answer, or to several?
records.zomi: Lahna in dawnna khat lam ah a lak hiam, tampi lam ah a lak hiam?

records.english: New evidence can overturn a conclusion that seemed certain for years.
records.zomi: Lahna thak in kum tampi sung kician bang a kisa thukhenna khat a lehkhia thei hi.

records.english: A conclusion is only as strong as the evidence and reasoning that lead to it.
records.zomi: Thukhenna khat pen a tun sak lahna leh ngaihsutna zah bek in a hat hi.

records.english: Our teacher said, "Tell me what you saw first, and then tell me what you think it means."
records.zomi: I saya in, "Na muh a masa-in hong gen inla, tua khit ciangin a khiatna bang na ngaihsun hiam hong gen in" a ci hi.

records.english: Tell me how you worked that out.
records.zomi: Tua bangci-in na thei hiam hong gen in.

records.english: He's smiling, so the interview must have gone well.
records.zomi: A nui ahih manin kidotna a hoih ding hi.

records.english: The car is still warm, so he can't have gone far.
records.zomi: Mawtaw a lum lai ahih manin gamla ah a pai thei kei ding hi.

records.english: Why do you think the shop is so busy today?
records.zomi: Bang hangin tuni-in dawl a buai mahmah hiam, na ci hiam?

records.english: Can you tell from those clouds whether it's going to rain this afternoon?
records.zomi: Tua meiite pan sun nung lam ah guah a zuk ding hiam na thei thei hiam?

records.english: We asked only ten people, so we can't draw any firm conclusions from the survey.
records.zomi: Mi sawm bek i dong uh ahih manin dotna pan thukhenna kician i bawl thei kei uh hi.

records.english: There are three empty cups on the table, so we probably had visitors.
records.zomi: Dawhkan tungah haai awng thum a om ahih manin khual i nei kha ding uh hi.

records.english: What does this result tell us?
records.zomi: Hih lohna in bang hong gen hiam?

records.english: If every plant by the window grew faster, light is a likely reason, but it may not be the only one.
records.zomi: Tukvuang kiang-a singkung khempeuh a khang manlang zaw leh vak pen a hang hi kha thei a, ahi zongin a hang khat bek hi kha lo thei hi.

records.english: I thought my friend was angry with me, but she had simply lost her phone.
records.zomi: Ka lawm in hong heh hi, ka ci a, ahi zongin a phone a mansuah bek hi.

records.english: The road is wet, but the sky is clear, so maybe a street cleaner came by.
records.zomi: Lampi a nawng a, ahi zongin van a siang ahih manin lampi siangsakpa khat a hong kha ding hi.

records.english: The best conclusions are often stated with care, using words like "probably" and "likely".
records.zomi: Thukhenna hoih pente "kha ding" leh "hi kha thei" bang kammal zang-in kidawm takin kigen zel hi.

records.english: It's raining, so the match will probably be postponed.
records.zomi: Guah a zuk ahih manin kimawlna kisawn kha ding hi.

records.english: Ruth hasn't answered my messages all day, which isn't like her.
records.zomi: Ruth in ni bup ka thu khakte a dawng kei a, tua pen amah' ngeina hi lo hi.

records.english: Finding a pattern in a few cases does not prove that the pattern holds everywhere.
records.zomi: Thu tawmno sungah lim khat muh in tua lim mun khempeuh ah a om hi, cih a lak kei hi.

records.english: Witnesses who saw the same event can reach different conclusions, depending on where they stood.
records.zomi: Thu piang kibang a mu tecite in a din na mun uh tungah kinga-in thukhenna kibang lo a tun thei uh hi.

records.english: A careful reader asks whether the conclusion follows from the facts or merely sits beside them.
records.zomi: Limtaka sim mi khat in thukhenna in thu takte pan a hong pai hiam, a kiangah a om bek hiam a dong hi.

records.english: Is that what the graph really shows?
records.zomi: Graph in tua pen a lak taktak hiam?

records.english: It's late, and the bus hasn't come, so it might have been cancelled.
records.zomi: A zan khin a, bus a hong nai kei ahih manin kikhak kha ding hi.

records.english: How did you know I'd been to the beach?
records.zomi: Tuipi gei ah ka pai hi, bangci-in na thei hiam?

records.english: There's sand in your shoes and salt in your hair.
records.zomi: Na khedap sungah ngal a om a, na sam sungah cii a om hi.

records.english: You may only use the facts in the text when you answer this question.
records.zomi: Hih dotna na dawn ciangin laigelh sung-a thu takte bek na zang thei hi.

records.english: Don't jump to conclusions before you've heard the whole story.
records.zomi: Tangthu bup na zak ma-in manlang lua-in thu khen kei in.

records.english: Look at the clues again.
records.zomi: Lim ciamtehnate en kik in.

records.english: The lights are off, so they must be asleep.
records.zomi: Meivakte a mit ahih manin a ihmu khin ding uh hi.

records.english: What can you tell from these footprints?
records.zomi: Hih khe lim te pan bang na thei thei hiam?

records.english: Someone small walked here after the rain stopped.
records.zomi: Guah a khawl khit ciangin mi neu khat hih ah a kalsuan hi.

records.english: When I came home, the back door was open, and there was mud on the kitchen floor.
records.zomi: Inn ka tun ciangin nung lam kongkhak a kihong a, an huanna inn leitang tungah buan a om hi.

records.english: At first, I thought someone had broken in.
records.zomi: A masa-in kuamah in a lut gu hi, ka ci hi.

records.english: Then I saw my son's football boots by the door and realized he had come home early.
records.zomi: Tua khit ciangin kongkhak kiang-a ka tapa' football khedap ka mu a, a ngal-in inn ah a tung hi, ci ka thei hi.

records.english: Having studied the photos carefully, the investigators concluded that the bridge had been damaged long before the storm.
records.zomi: Limte limtakin a sin khit uh ciangin sittelte in huihpi ma-in hun sawtpi lei a siat khin hi, ci-in thu a khen uh hi.

records.english: What do you think happened here?
records.zomi: Hih ah bang a piang hi, na ci hiam?

records.english: The dog must have knocked the vase off the table.
records.zomi: Ui in dawhkan tung pan pak bel a sukkia kha ding hi.

records.english: Write one sentence that sums up what the experiment showed.
records.zomi: Sinna in bang a lak hiam tomna kammal tang khat gelh in.

records.english: My grandmother taught me that God sees us even in the dark.
records.zomi: Ka pi in Pasian in mial sungah zong eite hong mu hi, ci-in hong sinsak hi.

records.english: Who made God?
records.zomi: Kua in Pasian a bawl hiam?

records.english: Christians answer that nobody made God, because God has always existed.
records.zomi: Khristiante in kuamah in Pasian a bawl kei hi, Pasian a om tawntung ahih manin, ci-in a dawng uh hi.

records.english: Many Christians believe that God sustains the world from moment to moment, and that nothing would exist without him.
records.zomi: Khristian tampi in Pasian in hun khatciat-in leitung a kem hi, amah om lo-in bangmah a om lo ding hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: You don't need to understand everything about God to trust him.
records.zomi: Pasian muan nadingin Pasian tungtang khempeuh na theih kisam kei hi.

records.english: According to many churches, God knows each person by name and cares about the smallest details of their life.
records.zomi: Pawlpi tampi' gen bangin Pasian in mi khatciat min tawh a thei a, a nuntakna sung-a neu pente zong a ngaihsun hi.

records.english: Many churches teach that God is all-powerful, but that God never acts against his own goodness.
records.zomi: Pawlpi tampi in Pasian vangliatna khempeuh nei ahi a, ahi zongin Pasian in amah' hoihna langpanin a gamta ngei kei hi, ci-in a hilh uh hi.

records.english: Read the first verse of the Bible aloud, and notice how it introduces God.
records.zomi: Laisiangtho' cang masa pen ging takin sim inla, Pasian bangci-in a kilaak hiam phawk in.

records.english: A short prayer was written on the board: "Thank you, God, for being with us today."
records.zomi: Board tungah thungetna tom khat kigelh hi: "Pasian aw, tuni-in hong om khawm na hih manin ka lungdam uh hi."

records.english: It comforts many Christians to believe that God knows their thoughts before they speak.
records.zomi: Pasian in a gen ma-un a ngaihsutnate a thei hi, ci-a um in Khristian tampi a hehnem hi.

records.english: Christian traditions use different words for God's nature, but almost all describe him as eternal, wise and good.
records.zomi: Khristian ngeinate in Pasian' ahihna adingin kammal kibang lo a zang uh a, ahi zongin a tamzaw in a tawntung, a pil leh a hoih hi, ci-in a gen uh hi.

records.english: The belief that God is present everywhere does not mean, in Christian teaching, that God is the same thing as the world.
records.zomi: Pasian mun khempeuh ah a om hi, cih upna in Khristian thuhilhna ah Pasian pen leitung tawh a kibang hi, cihna hi lo hi.

records.english: Christians often describe God as faithful, meaning that he always keeps his promises.
records.zomi: Khristiante in Pasian pen a thuman hi, ci-in a gen zel uh a, a kiciamnate a kem tawntung hi, cihna ahi hi.

records.english: Most Christian teachers say that God is neither male nor female, although the Bible often uses words like "Father" to describe him.
records.zomi: Khristian saya a tamzaw in Pasian pen pasal hi lo, numei hi lo hi, a ci uh a, Laisiangtho in amah gen dingin "Pa" bang kammal a zang zel hangin.

records.english: When my grandmother moved into the care home, the thought that God doesn't change was a great comfort to her.
records.zomi: Ka pi upa kemna inn ah a tai ciangin Pasian a kikheel kei hi, cih ngaihsutna in a lungsim a hehnem mahmah hi.

records.english: Our pastor said that God's greatness should make us humble, and God's closeness should make us brave.
records.zomi: I pastor in Pasian' thupitna in eite hong kiniamkhiatsak ding a, Pasian' naihna in eite hong hangsan sak ding hi, a ci hi.

records.english: If God made the world, why would he also want to be known by the people in it?
records.zomi: Pasian in leitung a bawl leh bang hangin a sung-a mite' theih zong a deih ding hiam?

records.english: The psalm says that a thousand years are like a single day in God's sight.
records.zomi: Late laibu in Pasian mitmuh ah kum tul khat pen ni khat bang ahi hi, a ci hi.

records.english: In Christian belief, God does not change, even when everything around us does.
records.zomi: Khristian upna ah eite kim leh pam khempeuh a kikheel zongin Pasian a kikheel kei hi.

records.english: Far from being distant, the God who created the world wants to be known, many Christians say.
records.zomi: Gamla-a om hi lo-in leitung bawlpa Pasian in kitheih a deih hi, ci-in Khristian tampi in a gen uh hi.

records.english: Does God know my name?
records.zomi: Pasian in ka min a thei hiam?

records.english: My little cousin asked, "Was God ever a baby?"
records.zomi: Ka sanggam neu in, "Pasian naungek a hi ngei hiam?" ci-in a dong hi.

records.english: The prophet Isaiah describes God as the one who measured the oceans in the palm of his hand.
records.zomi: Kamsang Isaiah in Pasian pen tuipite a khutpeek sungah a teh pa ahi hi, ci-in a gen hi.

records.english: Is God the same in the Old Testament and the New Testament?
records.zomi: Pasian pen Thukham Lui leh Thukham Thak ah a kibang hiam?

records.english: Christians believe that he is, although they read the Old Testament in the light of Jesus.
records.zomi: Khristiante in a kibang hi, ci-in a um uh a, Thukham Lui pen Jesu' vak sungah a sim uh hangin.

records.english: Where is God?
records.zomi: Pasian koi ah om hiam?

records.english: Christians believe God is everywhere, not in one place only.
records.zomi: Khristiante in Pasian mun khat bek ah hi lo-in mun khempeuh ah a om hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: If God already knows everything, why do we pray?
records.zomi: Pasian in khempeuh a thei khin leh bang hangin thu i ngen uh hiam?

records.english: Children, today we're going to think about what God is like.
records.zomi: Naupangte, tuni-in Pasian bangci om hiam i ngaihsun ding uh hi.

records.english: My son asked whether God is bigger than the sky.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in Pasian van sangin a lian zaw hiam ci-in a dong hi.

records.english: Christians believe that God has no beginning and no end.
records.zomi: Khristiante in Pasian kipatna leh tawpna nei lo hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: The Christian teaching that God rules over all things is often called God's sovereignty.
records.zomi: Pasian in khempeuh tungah a uk hi, cih Khristian thuhilhna pen Pasian' ukna ci-in a kisam zel hi.

records.english: Does God ever sleep?
records.zomi: Pasian a ihmu ngei hiam?

records.english: We can learn something about God from the world, but Christians believe we learn the most from Jesus.
records.zomi: Leitung pan Pasian tungtang bangmah i sin thei uh a, ahi zongin Khristiante in Jesu pan a tam pen i sin uh hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: If God is in control, do my choices still matter?
records.zomi: Pasian in a uk leh ka teelnate a thupi lai hiam?

records.english: Most Christians would say yes, because God holds people responsible for what they choose.
records.zomi: Khristian a tamzaw in thupi hi, a ci ding uh hi, Pasian in mite a teelnate adingin mawhpuakna a piak manin.

records.english: When my father was very ill, he asked me to read him a psalm about God's greatness.
records.zomi: Ka pa a damlo mahmah lai-in Pasian' thupitna tungtang la khat simsak dingin hong ngen hi.

records.english: He listened with his eyes closed and then said quietly, "God was here before me, and he will be here after me."
records.zomi: A mit khuh-in a ngaikhia a, dai takin, "Pasian kei ma-in a om khin a, ka nung ciangin zong a om ding hi" a ci hi.

records.english: Those words have stayed with me ever since.
records.zomi: Tua kammalte tua pan kei tawh a om den hi.

records.english: Everyone, let's begin by thanking God for the world he made.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, a bawl leitung adingin Pasian lungdam ci-in i kipan ni.

records.english: Christian thinkers have long taught that people can know God truly without knowing him completely.
records.zomi: Khristian ngaihsun siamte in mite in Pasian a kicing-in thei lo-in a taktak-in a thei thei uh hi, ci-in hun sawtpi a hilh uh hi.

records.english: Can God hear everyone's prayers at the same time?
records.zomi: Pasian in mi khempeuh' thungetna hun kibang ah a za thei hiam?

records.english: Is God a man or a woman?
records.zomi: Pasian pen pasal ahi hiam, numei ahi hiam?

records.english: Can anyone fully understand God?
records.zomi: Kuamah in Pasian a kicing-in a thei thei hiam?

records.english: Many believers say that God's sovereignty and human responsibility are both taught in the Bible, even if they find it hard to explain how they fit together.
records.zomi: Upmi tampi in Pasian' ukna leh mihing mawhpuakna a nih Laisiangtho in a hilh hi, a ci uh a, bangci-in a kituak uh hiam genteh a haksa sa uh hangin.

records.english: When Moses asked God's name, God answered, "I am who I am," according to the Book of Exodus.
records.zomi: Pawtna laibu' gen bangin Moses in Pasian' min a dot ciangin Pasian in, "Kei pen kei ka hi hi" ci-in a dawng hi.

records.english: The questions about God that children ask are often the same ones that theologians ask.
records.zomi: Naupangte' dot Pasian tungtang dotnate pen Pasian thu siamte' dot kibang mah ahi zel hi.

records.english: For many believers, learning about God's nature is meant to lead to worship, not only to knowledge.
records.zomi: Upmi tampi adingin Pasian' ahihna sin pen theihna bek hi lo-in biakna dong a pi ding ahi hi.

records.english: When Christians call God eternal, they mean not only that God lasts forever but that God is not bound by time as we are.
records.zomi: Khristiante in Pasian a tawntung hi, a cih uh ciangin Pasian tawntung-in a om bek hi lo-in eite bangin hun in a khen kei hi, cihna ahi hi.

records.english: Every promise in the Bible, many believers say, depends on the faithfulness of the one who made it.

records.zomi: Mipi ciamtehnate in tangthu laibute in a gen ngei loh ngeina nuntaknate a lak zel hi.

records.english: Should public records ever be destroyed, or should everything be kept forever?
records.zomi: Mipi ciamtehnate susia ngei ding hiam, khempeuh khantawn-in kem ding hiam?

records.english: Records that are easy to search are much more useful than records that only one clerk understands.
records.zomi: Zon baih ciamtehnate lai gelh khat bek in a theih ciamtehnate sangin a phattuam zaw mahmah hi.

records.english: Sorry, I don't know what she took; I only found the empty packet.

records.english: She has diabetes, and she hasn't eaten since breakfast.

records.english: Tablets for his blood pressure and something for his heart, which are in this bag.

records.english: We'll need your permission before we can operate.

records.english: Saying exactly when symptoms began, rather than "a while ago", helps doctors judge how urgent a case is.

records.english: Only one of you can ride with her, I'm afraid.
records.zomi: Na lak uh ah khat bek in amah tawh a tuang thei hi, ci ka lau hi.

records.english: When did the pain start?

records.english: Doctors may ask the same questions several times, partly to check that the answers stay consistent.

records.english: You're doing really well; we're nearly at the hospital.
records.zomi: Na bawl hoih mahmah hi; siavuan inn i tung dek ta hi.

records.english: Is she allergic to anything?
records.zomi: Amah bangmah tawh allergy a nei hiam?

records.english: Yes, to penicillin.
records.zomi: Nei hi, penicillin tawh.

records.english: A note on your phone listing your medical conditions can help emergency staff if you cannot speak for yourself.
records.zomi: Na damna dinmunte lakna na phone tung-a thu gelh khat in nangmah mah in na gen theih loh leh lauhuai hun nasemte a huh thei hi.

records.english: Are you pregnant, or could you be?

records.english: Have you taken anything for the pain already?
records.zomi: Natna adingin bangmah na ne khin hiam?

records.english: He's had a cough for a week, but the breathing problems started an hour ago.
records.zomi: Kal khat sung a cil a, ahi zongin huih lak buainate hun khat masa-in a kipan hi.

records.english: I do want you to tell me the truth about how serious it is.
records.zomi: Bangzah a gik hiam a tak hong gen ding ka deih taktak hi.

records.english: The paramedic asked me to hold the drip bag while she lifted my brother onto the stretcher.
records.zomi: Ambulance nasem nu in ka sanggam pasal lupna leng tungah a koih laitakin tui khai ip len dingin hong ngen hi.

records.english: My son wears a bracelet that says he's allergic to nuts.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in bekang tawh allergy a nei hi, ci-a gen khutkhih khat a bun hi.

records.english: Can you tell me your name and date of birth?
records.zomi: Na min leh na suahni hong gen thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Squeeze my hand if you can hear me.
records.zomi: Hong za thei leh ka khut nawi in.

records.english: Asking a patient to repeat the instructions back is a simple way to check that they have understood.
records.zomi: Damlo kiangah hilhnate gen kik dingin ngen pen a thei hiam en nading lampi baih khat ahi hi.

records.english: Is there anyone we should contact for you?
records.zomi: Na adingin i sam ding kuamah om hiam?

records.english: When a relative translates in an emergency, important details can be softened or left out, which is why many hospitals offer trained interpreters.
records.zomi: Lauhuai hun ah sanggam khat in a let ciangin thu thupi te nemsak hiam nusia kha thei ahih manin siavuan inn tampi in kisinsak pau letmite a pia uh hi.

records.english: The doctor drew a picture to show us where the bone was broken.
records.zomi: Siavuan in guh koi ah a tat hiam hong lak dingin lim khat a gelh hi.

records.english: Clear, simple words help patients understand what is happening, especially when they are in pain or in shock.
records.zomi: Kammal kician leh baih te in a diak in a natna hiam lamdang a sak laitakin damlote in bang a piang hiam a theih nadingun a huh hi.

records.english: Can I come in the ambulance with him?
records.zomi: Ambulance ah amah tawh ka tuang thei ding hiam?

records.english: Some people carry a small card with their medical details in their wallet, next to their identity card.
records.zomi: Mi pawl khat in a sum ip sungah a ID card kiang ah a damna thu nei card neu khat a pua uh hi.

records.english: The ambulance crew gave my mother oxygen on the way to the hospital.
records.zomi: Ambulance nasemte in siavuan inn pai lampi ah ka nu oxygen a pia uh hi.

records.english: In an emergency, a short, accurate list of medicines and allergies can be more useful than a long story.
records.zomi: Lauhuai hun ah zatuite leh allergy te list tom leh dik khat in tangthu sau khat sangin a phattuam zaw thei hi.

records.english: Tell the nurse if the pain gets worse.
records.zomi: Natna a gilo zawk leh nurse kiangah gen in.

records.english: Being honest about alcohol or drugs taken can change which treatment is safe, so it matters more than any embarrassment.
records.zomi: Zu hiam zatui gilo na nek thu thuman takin gen in bang zatui zat a bit hiam a kheel thei ahih manin zumna bangpeuh sangin a thupi zaw hi.

records.english: He takes blood thinners, so please tell the doctor straight away.
records.zomi: Amah in sisan nemsak zatui a ne ahih manin siavuan kiangah pah-in gen un.

records.english: Paramedics often explain what they are doing as they work, because a frightened patient feels calmer when nothing comes as a surprise.
records.zomi: Ambulance nasemte in a nasep laitakin bang a bawl uh hiam a genteh zel uh hi, a lau damlo in bangmah lamen lo-in a tung kei ciangin a lungsim a nem zaw ahih manin.

records.english: Thank you for staying with my father until we arrived.
records.zomi: Eite i tun dong ka pa tawh na om manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: Does it hurt when I press here?

records.english: Yes, right there.
records.zomi: Hi, tua lai mah ah.

records.english: Her lips started to swell a few minutes after she ate the cake.
records.zomi: Cake a nek khit minit tawmno ah a mur a pum kipan hi.

records.english: When a patient cannot give consent, doctors in many countries may act in the patient's best interests and inform the family as soon as possible.
records.zomi: Damlo in a phalna a pia thei kei ciangin gam tampi-a siavuante in damlo' phattuamna adingin a sem thei uh a, innkuan kiangah manlang takin a gen uh hi.

records.english: Did she lose consciousness, even for a moment?
records.zomi: Hun tawmno bek zong a kia hiam?

records.english: Breathe slowly with me.
records.zomi: Kei tawh zawi takin huih la in.

records.english: Information passed from the paramedics to the hospital team helps the doctors start treatment without delay.
records.zomi: Ambulance nasemte pan siavuan inn pawl kiangah kipia thute in siavuante a zatui zat nunung lo-in a kipat nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: What's your phone number, in case we need to call you?
records.zomi: Kong sam kisam leh ci-in na phone nambat bang hiam?

records.english: Who is your family doctor?
records.zomi: Na innkuan siavuan kua ahi hiam?

records.english: Please call my wife and tell her which hospital I'm in.
records.zomi: Ka zi sam inla, bang siavuan inn ah ka om hiam gen in.

records.english: When my grandfather collapsed at the market, a young nurse happened to be buying bread.
records.zomi: Ka pu zuakna mun ah a kia ciangin nurse khangno khat moh a lei lai hi.

records.english: She knelt beside him, asked his name, and kept talking to him while she checked his breathing.
records.zomi: A kiang ah a khukdin a, a min a dong a, a huih lak a en laitakin amah tawh a kiho den hi.

records.english: By the time the ambulance came, she had written his symptoms on a scrap of paper for the paramedics.
records.zomi: Ambulance a tun hun ciangin ambulance nasemte adingin lai neu khat tungah a natna limte a gelh khin hi.

records.english: Bring his medicines with you, so the doctors can see exactly what he takes.
records.zomi: Siavuante in bang a ne hiam diktakin a muh theih nadingun a zatuite tawi in.

records.english: Patients sometimes play down their symptoms out of embarrassment, so staff ask direct questions gently.
records.zomi: Damlote in zumna hangin a natna limte a neusak zel uh ahih manin nasemte in nem takin dotna tangtak a dong uh hi.

records.english: My mother doesn't speak English well, so I'll translate for her.
records.zomi: Ka nu in English hoih takin a gen thei kei ahih manin amah adingin ka let ding hi.

records.english: Try to stay still while we check your neck.
records.zomi: Na ngawng i en laitakin kiling lo-in om sawm in.

records.english: My daughter has epilepsy, and this is the medicine she takes when she has a seizure.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in tawpi natna a nei a, hih pen a tawpi natna a tuah ciangin a nek zatui ahi hi.

records.english: I'm her husband, and I can answer any questions.
records.zomi: Amah' pasal ka hi a, dotna bangpeuh ka dawng thei hi.

records.english: Is he going to be all right?
records.zomi: A dam ding hiam?

records.english: Has he hit his head?
records.zomi: A lu a dong hiam?

records.english: I don't think so, but I didn't see him fall.
records.zomi: Ka ngaihsut in dong lo hi, ahi zongin a puk ka mu kei hi.

records.english: Can you feel your toes?
records.zomi: Na khezungte na theih thei hiam?

records.english: Where exactly does it hurt?
records.zomi: Koi diktak ah a na hiam?

records.english: A calm voice from a stranger can be the first comfort an injured person receives.
records.zomi: Mikhual khat' aw dai in a liam mi khat' ngah hehnemna masa pen hi thei hi.

records.english: Who do you tell first when something good happens?
records.zomi: Bangmah hoih a piang ciangin kua kiangah na gen masa hiam?

records.english: My brother would choose a friend who is loyal over one who is fun.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in a nuam lawm sangin muanhuai lawm a teel zaw ding hi.

records.english: A group activity is less awkward than a coffee for two, because there is always something to talk about.
records.zomi: Pawl kimawlna in nih bek coffee nekna sangin a zum huai tawm zaw hi, gen ding a om tawntung ahih manin.

records.english: I like to meet new people in a group at first, and one to one only later.
records.zomi: A masa-in pawl sungah mi thakte kimu ka deih a, a nung ciangin nih bek.

records.english: Making friends through work is quicker, but friendships made through hobbies often last longer.
records.zomi: Nasep tungtawn-in lawm bawl a manlang zaw a, ahi zongin nuamna nasep tungtawn-in lawmtate a sawt zaw zel hi.

records.english: Friendships that begin at the school gate can fade once the pupils move on to different schools.
records.zomi: Sang kongpi pan a kipan lawmtate sangnaupangte sang kibang lo ah a pai uh ciangin a mang thei hi.

records.english: My cousin always picks the friend who needs help over the friend who is the most fun.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam in a nuam pen lawm sangin huhna kisam lawm a teel tawntung hi.

records.english: Saying yes to everything helped at first, but later I chose the groups where I felt most like myself.
records.zomi: Khempeuh pom in a masa-in hong huh a, ahi zongin a nung ciangin keimah bangin ka kisak pen pawlte ka teel hi.

records.english: Big parties tire me out, so I see friends one or two at a time.
records.zomi: Pawi lian te in hong gimsak ahih manin lawmte khat hiam nih bek ka mu zel hi.

records.english: Choose the club that meets near your home, so that going there never feels like a chore.
records.zomi: Na inn kiang-a kikhawm pawl teel in, tua ah pai pen nasep bangin a kisak ngei loh nadingin.

records.english: A friend who lives nearby is easier to see, but a faraway friend can still be the one you call first.
records.zomi: Nai-a teeng lawm khat muh a baih zaw a, ahi zongin gamla lawm khat na sam masa pen hi thei lai hi.

records.english: My grandfather said, "Choose friends you'd be proud to introduce to your mother."

records.english: It's a hard choice, but I think the cooking class suits me better.

records.english: I'd rather have two close friends than twenty people I barely know.
records.zomi: Ka theih kha lo mi sawmnih sangin lawm nai nih ka nei zaw ding hi.

records.english: Please don't choose your friends just because they're popular.
records.zomi: Na lawmte min a than uh hangin bek teel kei in.

records.english: A small town gives you fewer people to choose from but more chances to see the same faces.

records.english: Which would you prefer, a friend who gives advice or a friend who just listens?

records.english: A friend who just listens, please!
records.zomi: A ngaikhia bek lawm, kong ngen hi!

records.english: Being honest with a friend can be harder than being kind, but the best friends manage both.
records.zomi: Lawm khat tungah thuman in hehpihna sangin a haksa zaw thei a, ahi zongin lawm hoih pente in a nih a zo uh hi.

records.english: My daughter chose to sit with the quiet girl rather than the loud group.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in pawl ging sangin numei naupang dai tawh tu a teel hi.

records.english: I used a video call to introduce my two best friends, who live in different countries.

records.english: Some friendships suit the café, and others suit long walks.

records.english: Do you think it's easier to make friends with people your own age?

records.english: Is it better to have friends who are like you or friends who challenge you?
records.zomi: Nang bang lawmte nei a hoih zaw hiam, hong sawl lawmte nei a hoih zaw hiam?

records.english: A bit of both, because the first comfort you and the second help you grow.
records.zomi: A nih tawmno ciat, a masa in hong hehnem a, a nihna in hong khangsak ahih manin.

records.english: Which club is friendlier, the choir or the chess club?

records.english: A message every week does more for a friendship than a long visit once a year.

records.english: Our dog makes friends faster than we do.
records.zomi: I ui in eite sangin manlang zaw-in lawm a bawl hi.

records.english: Inviting someone home feels more personal than meeting in a café.
records.zomi: Mi khat inn ah sam pen cafe ah kimuh sangin a nai zaw hi.

records.english: Making friends online suits shy people, but in-person friendships often feel more solid.

records.english: In the village, friendships came with the family, but in the city I had to choose my own.

records.english: Which party should I go to on Saturday?
records.zomi: Kiginni ciangin bang pawi ah ka pai ding hiam?

records.english: Go to Lia's, because she invited you first.

records.english: Is it better to call a new friend or just send a message?
records.zomi: Lawm thak khat sam a hoih zaw hiam, thu khak bek a hoih zaw hiam?

records.english: Do you prefer making plans in advance or meeting on the spur of the moment?
records.zomi: A ma-in geel na deih zaw hiam, thakhat-in kimuh na deih zaw hiam?

records.english: Is it wiser to keep work friends and home friends separate?
records.zomi: Nasep lawmte leh inn lawmte khen a pil zaw hiam?

records.english: Spending the weekend with old friends is relaxing, but meeting new people keeps life interesting.

records.english: Is it better to forgive a friend quickly or to wait until you're calm?
records.zomi: Lawm khat manlang takin maisak a hoih zaw hiam, na lungsim a dai dong ngak a hoih zaw hiam?

records.english: Shall we meet for coffee, or would you prefer a walk?
records.zomi: Coffee adingin i kimu ding hiam, kalsuan na deih zaw ding hiam?

records.english: Teenagers often choose friends by shared interests, while adults may choose them by shared values.
records.zomi: Khangnote in deihna kibang tawh lawm a teel uh a, upate in manphatna kibang tawh a teel kha thei uh hi.

records.english: My sister makes friends by talking to everyone in the room, while I make them slowly, one at a time.

records.english: Some people find that one honest friend is worth more than a dozen who only agree with them.

records.english: Old friends know my history, while new friends only know who I am now.
records.zomi: Lawm luite in ka tangthu a thei uh a, lawm thakte in tu-a ka hihna bek a thei uh hi.

records.english: Some people need a wide circle of friends to feel happy, while others are content with one or two they can trust completely.

records.english: A lunchtime walk is easier to fit in than an evening out.

records.english: Friends who share your past and friends who share your present give you different kinds of support.

records.english: The friends we choose say a good deal about the person we hope to become.

records.english: Do you find it easier to make friends at work or in your neighborhood?

records.zomi: Ka inn veng ah, nasepna ah mi khempeuh a manlang den uh ahih manin.

records.english: You may bring one friend to the camp, so choose carefully.

records.english: Paying for each other's coffee in turn feels friendlier to us than splitting every bill.

records.english: My aunt prefers friends who drop in without warning, but my mother likes a phone call first.

records.english: My son prefers playing with one friend at a time.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in khatvei ah lawm khat tawh kimawl a deih zaw hi.

records.english: Choosing between two invitations on the same evening can feel like choosing between two friends.

records.english: Would you rather make friends at a dance class or a cooking class?

records.english: Shall we invite the whole class or just a few close friends?

records.english: Nuam, after my husband's mother.

records.english: When someone answers a family question briefly, it may be kinder to ask about something else.

records.english: Cing, Thang and little Lian, who is only two.

records.english: My mother burst into tears, while my father quietly opened the box of sweets he had been saving for a special day.

records.english: What does your family eat on New Year's Day?

records.english: What was the best present your parents ever gave you?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa in hong piak letsong hoih pen bang hiam?

records.english: A second-hand bicycle that my father painted bright red himself.
records.zomi: Ka pa mah in san vak tawh a zeek zang khin siiksakol khat.

records.english: What do you usually do together as a family on Sundays?

records.english: We go to church, eat lunch at Grandma's, and fall asleep on her sofa.
records.zomi: Pawlpi ah i pai uh a, Pi' inn ah sun an i ne uh a, a sofa tungah i ihmu uh hi.

records.english: When you were ill as a child, what did your mother cook?
records.zomi: Naupan lai-a na damlo ciangin na nu in bang a huan hiam?

records.english: What time do your kids go to bed on school nights?

records.english: Eight o'clock, though the oldest may read for another half hour.
records.zomi: Nai giat, a upa pen in minit sawmthum behlap a sim thei hangin.

records.english: What we choose to ask about a person's family often shows what we ourselves care about.
records.zomi: Mi khat' innkuan tungtang i dot teel in eite mah in bang i ngaihsut hiam a lak zel hi.

records.english: What do your parents think of your new flat?
records.zomi: Na inn thak tungtang na nu leh na pa in bang a ngaihsun uh hiam?

records.english: My mother thinks it's too small, and my father thinks it's too far away.
records.zomi: Ka nu in a neu lua hi, a ci a, ka pa in a gamla lua hi, a ci hi.

records.english: In some families, questions about age or income are fine, while in others they feel too personal.
records.zomi: Innkuan pawl khat ah kum hiam sum lut dotnate a hoih a, a dangte ah a guk lua bangin a kisa hi.

records.zomi: Na pasal in bang nasep a sem hiam ka dong thei ding hiam?

records.english: He repairs mobile phones in the market.
records.zomi: Zuakna mun ah phone a bawlpha hi.

records.english: A simple question like "What did your father do?" may be easy for one person and painful for another.
records.zomi: "Na pa in bang nasep a sem hiam?" bang dotna baih khat mi khat adingin a baih a, mi dang khat adingin a na thei hi.

records.english: What was your grandfather's job before he retired?
records.zomi: Na pu in nasep a khawl ma-in bang nasep a sem hiam?

records.english: He drove a bus between our village and the town for thirty years.
records.zomi: Kum sawmthum sung i khua leh khuapi kikal bus a mawng hi.

records.english: Children, what would you like me to make for your grandmother's visit?
records.zomi: Naupangte, na pi' vehna adingin bang ka bawl na deih uh hiam?

records.english: Her favourite coconut cake!
records.zomi: A deih pen cake!

records.english: What a family chooses to celebrate tells you a great deal about what it values.
records.zomi: Innkuan khat in bang poai dingin a teel hiam in bang a manpha sak hiam tampi a gen hi.

records.english: Asking someone what their family did in the past can be a warm way to begin, as long as you are ready to hear sad stories as well as happy ones.

records.english: What did your family do for you when you were in hospital?
records.zomi: Siavuan inn na om lai-in na innkuan in na adingin bang a bawl uh hiam?

records.english: They took turns sleeping on a hard chair beside my bed, so that I was never alone at night.
records.zomi: Zan ciangin kei kia ka om loh nadingin ka lupna kiang-a tutphah khauh tungah a kikheel-in a ihmu uh hi.

records.english: What's the funniest thing your little brother has ever said?
records.zomi: Na nau pasal' gen nuihzaak pen bang hiam?

records.english: He once asked whether the moon followed our car because it liked us.
records.zomi: Vei khat kha in hong it ahih manin i mawtaw a zui hiam ci-in a dong hi.

records.english: What kind of fun did your grandparents have when they were young?
records.zomi: Na pu leh pi a khangno lai-un bang nuamna a nei uh hiam?

records.english: They danced at the village festivals and told stories round the fire.
records.zomi: Khua pawite ah a lam uh a, mei kim ah tangthu a gen uh hi.

records.english: What should I bring when I meet your parents?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa ka kimuh ciangin bang ka tawi ding hiam?

records.english: Some fruit is enough, and please don't worry.
records.zomi: Theigah tawmno a tam hi, lunghimawh kei in.

records.english: What does your daughter want to be when she grows up?
records.zomi: Na tanu in a khan ciangin bang hih a deih hiam?

records.english: A vet, because she can't walk past a stray cat.
records.zomi: Ganhing siavuan, zaang mangthang khat a kantan zo kei ahih manin.

records.english: What do you and your brother usually argue about?
records.zomi: Nang leh na sanggam pasal bang thu na kinial zel uh hiam?

records.english: Whose turn it is to visit our parents on Sunday.
records.zomi: Nipini ciangin kua' kikheel in i nu leh i pa veh ding hiam.

records.english: What would your grandfather say if he could see the farm now?
records.zomi: Na pu in tu-a lo a muh theih leh bang a ci ding hiam?

records.english: He'd probably say that we had planted the beans in the wrong field.
records.zomi: Be pen lo khial ah na suan uh hi, a ci kha ding hi.

records.english: When I was ten, my father asked me what I wanted for my birthday.
records.zomi: Kum sawm ka cin ciangin ka pa in ka suahni adingin bang ka deih hiam hong dong hi.

records.english: I told him I wanted to see the sea, which none of us had ever seen.
records.zomi: Kuamah in a muh ngei loh tuipi muh ka deih hi, ka ci hi.

records.english: He saved for months, and that summer the whole family took the bus to the coast.
records.zomi: Kha tampi sum a khawl a, tua khal in innkuan bup bus tawh tuipi gei ah i pai uh hi.

records.english: What languages do people speak in your family?
records.zomi: Na innkuan ah mite in bang paute a zang uh hiam?

records.english: My parents speak their first language at home, and we children answer in English.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in inn ah a pau masa a zang uh a, naupangte in English tawh i dawng uh hi.

records.english: What did your parents teach you about money?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa in sum tungtang bang hong hilh uh hiam?

records.english: Never to borrow what you can't repay, and to give something away even when you have little.
records.zomi: Na pia kik theih loh puk ngei kei in, leh tawmno bek na neih zongin bangmah pia in.

records.english: What is your favourite thing to do with your grandchildren?
records.zomi: Na tuute tawh bawl na deih pen bang hiam?

records.english: Walk to the river and feed the ducks.

records.english: Highlighting whole pages may feel productive, but it rarely helps people remember what matters.
records.zomi: Sungtang bup highlight in sem bangin a kisa thei a, ahi zongin a thupi mite phawk dingin a huh ngei tuan kei hi.

records.english: Where's my pencil case?
records.zomi: Ka pencil bawm koi ah om hiam?

records.english: Rewards help some students, such as a walk or a snack after an hour of work.
records.zomi: Letsongte in sangnaupang pawl khat a huh hi, hun khat nasep khit-a kalsuan hiam an neu bang.

records.english: Short study sessions spread over several days are often more effective than one long session the night before.
records.zomi: Ni tampi sungah kizelh sinna hun tomte in sitna ma-a zan-a hun sau khat sangin a sem hoih zaw zel hi.

records.english: Children who see their parents reading often come to enjoy books themselves.
records.zomi: A nu leh a pa uh a sim a mu naupangte in laibu a it zel uh hi.

records.english: The best study place is often the one where nothing else competes for your attention.

records.english: Our school stays open until six so that pupils can do their homework there.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte in tua ah a inn sinna uh a bawl theih nadingun i sang nai guk dong a kihong hi.

records.english: Shall we practise the spelling words in the car?
records.zomi: Mawtaw sungah laimal kammalte i kisin ding hiam?

records.english: I always make a cup of tea before I start.
records.zomi: Ka kipat ma-in tea haai khat ka bawl tawntung hi.

records.english: I study better in the morning, before anyone else is awake.
records.zomi: Mi dang khempeuh a khanglawh ma-in zingsang ciangin ka sin hoih zaw hi.

records.english: Drawing a simple diagram can make a long explanation much easier to remember.
records.zomi: Lim baih khat gelh in genteh sau khat phawk a baih zaw mahmah sak thei hi.

records.english: Our class keeps a list of the questions we got wrong, and we try them again every Friday.
records.zomi: I class in i khialh dotnate list khat a kem a, Laithai ni simin i sin kik uh hi.

records.english: I study better at the kitchen table than in my bedroom.
records.zomi: Ka inndei sangin an huanna inn dawhkan ah ka sin hoih zaw hi.

records.english: Take a short break every forty minutes.
records.zomi: Minit sawmli simin tawldamna tom khat la in.

records.english: Testing yourself on what you have read usually helps you remember it better than reading the same page again.
records.zomi: Na sim nangmah le nangmah kidot in sungtang kibang sim kik sangin na phawk hoih zaw sak zel hi.

records.english: Please don't talk in the reading room.
records.zomi: Simna inndei ah kiho kei un.

records.english: A tidy desk makes it easier to start work.
records.zomi: Dawhkan siang in nasep kipat a baih zawsak hi.

records.english: Students who ask questions in class often learn more than those who simply take notes.
records.zomi: Class sungah dotna a dong sangnaupangte in thu a gelh bek te sangin tam zaw a sin zel uh hi.

records.english: My sister explains each chapter to our little brother, which helps her understand it herself.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam numei in i nau pasal kiangah sung khen khatciat a genteh a, tua in amah mah a theih nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: The library lends laptops to students who don't have a computer at home.
records.zomi: Laibu koihna in inn ah computer nei lo sangnaupangte kiangah laptop a pukbawh hi.

records.english: We study together on Thursdays and test each other on Sundays.
records.zomi: Laizing ni simin i khawm-in i sin uh a, Nipini simin i kisit uh hi.

records.english: Put your phone in another room while you study.
records.zomi: Na sin laitakin na phone inndei dang ah koih in.

records.english: Do you study with music on?
records.zomi: La a ging laitakin na sin hiam?

records.english: Are you going to the study group tomorrow?
records.zomi: Zingciang sinna pawl ah na pai ding hiam?

records.english: Knowing why a study method works makes it easier to keep using it when results are slow to appear.
records.zomi: Sinna lampi khat bang hangin a sem hiam theih in lohnate a zawi ciangin zang zom a baihsak hi.

records.english: Can you check my answers, please?
records.zomi: Ka dawnnate hong en sak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Studying in a group helps when everyone has prepared, but it can turn into a chat if nobody has.
records.zomi: Pawl-a sin in mi khempeuh a kiman ciangin a huh a, ahi zongin kuamah a kiman kei leh kikupna bek ah a kheel thei hi.

records.english: I underline only the words I don't know, so that my notes stay clear.
records.zomi: Ka thu gelhte a siang nadingin ka theih loh kammalte bek ka nuai ah gual ka kaih hi.

records.english: My mother helped me make a timetable so that I study a little of every subject each week.
records.zomi: Kal simin sinna khempeuh tawmno ciat ka sin nadingin ka nu in hun gelhna khat bawl dingin hong huh hi.

records.english: Turn off the television, please; your brother is studying.
records.zomi: Television sumit in, kong ngen hi; na sanggam pasal a sin hi.

records.english: Every evening, my father sat beside me while I did my homework, even though he had never been to school.
records.zomi: Nitak simin ka pa sang a kah ngei kei hangin ka inn sinna ka bawl laitakin ka kiang ah a tu hi.

records.english: When a page is too difficult, I read it once quickly, then once slowly with a pencil.
records.zomi: Sungtang khat a haksa lua ciangin manlang takin khatvei ka sim a, tua khit ciangin pencil tawh zawi takin khatvei ka sim hi.

records.english: I forgot to bring my notes.
records.zomi: Ka thu gelhte tawi ka mangngilh hi.

records.english: Studying for understanding takes longer at first, but it saves time later because you forget less.
records.zomi: Theih nadinga sin in a kipat ciangin hun sawt zaw a la a, ahi zongin tawm zaw na mangngilh ahih manin a nung ciangin hun a khawl hi.

records.english: My brother reads his notes aloud while he walks around the garden.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in huan sungah a kalsuan laitakin a thu gelhte ging takin a sim hi.

records.english: Copying a friend's homework saves time today but costs you much more at exam time.
records.zomi: Lawm khat' inn sinna suaksak in tuni-in hun a khawl a, ahi zongin sitna hun ciangin tam zaw mahmah na man ding hi.

records.english: Sleep helps the brain store what you have learned, so staying up all night can undo a day of studying.
records.zomi: Ihmut in lungsim in na sin a kem nadingin a huh ahih manin zan bup ihmut lo in ni khat sinna a susia thei hi.

records.english: Did you finish your reading for today?
records.zomi: Tuni adingin na sim ding na zo khin hiam?

records.english: My grandfather taught himself to read at forty, by studying the newspaper every evening.
records.zomi: Ka pu in kum sawmli ciangin nitak simin laithak sin-in amah mah in lai sim a kisin hi.

records.english: Explaining a topic to someone else quickly shows you which parts you have not really understood.
records.zomi: Thu khat mi dang kiangah genteh in bang khen na thei taktak lo hiam manlang takin a lak hi.

records.english: Students, write one question at the end of each page of notes.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte, thu gelh sungtang khatciat tawpna ah dotna khat gelh un.

records.english: Can I study with you tonight?
records.zomi: Tu zan-in nang tawh ka sin thei ding hiam?

records.english: Let's go over the vocabulary once more before dinner.
records.zomi: Nitak an ma-in kammalte vei khat i en kik ni.

records.english: I'm afraid I can't come out tonight, because I have a chemistry test tomorrow.
records.zomi: Zingciang chemistry sitna ka nei ahih manin tu zan-in pua ah ka pai thei kei hi, ci ka lau hi.

records.english: How do you remember all those dates?
records.zomi: Tua kum leh ni khempeuh bangci-in na phawk hiam?

records.english: I write each one on a card and test myself on the bus.
records.zomi: Khatciat card khat tungah ka gelh a, bus tungah ka kisit hi.

records.english: I do want to study harder this year, but I keep getting distracted.
records.zomi: Kum in hat zaw-in sin ka deih taktak a, ahi zongin ka lungsim a pial den hi.

records.zomi: Sitna ma-in ka lawm in a phawk khempeuh lai awng khat tungah a gelh a, tua khit ciangin laibu a en hi.

records.english: My friend records herself reading her notes and listens to them on the way to school.
records.zomi: Ka lawm in a thu gelhte a sim a record a, sang pai lampi ah a ngaikhia hi.

records.english: Where do you do your homework?
records.zomi: Na inn sinna koi ah na bawl hiam?

records.english: At the library after school, because it's quiet there.
records.zomi: Sang khit ciangin laibu koihna ah, tua lai a dai ahih manin.

records.english: Last year, I kept failing my maths tests even though I studied for hours.
records.zomi: Kum nunung in nai tampi ka sin zongin ka maths sitnate ka lel den hi.

records.english: My teacher suggested that I stop rereading the book and start doing practice questions instead.
records.zomi: Ka saya in laibu sim kik khawl-in kisinna dotnate bawl kipan dingin hong hilh hi.

records.english: By the end of the term, my marks had improved more than I had dared to hope.
records.zomi: Sang hun tawp ciangin ka mark ka lamen sangin a khang zaw mahmah hi.

records.english: Good study habits are built slowly, by repeating small actions until they no longer need willpower.
records.zomi: Sinna ngeina hoihte zawi takin kilam a, sepna neute deihna kisam nawn lo dong a bawl kik den in kilam hi.

records.english: When you get a test back, look first at your mistakes, not just at the mark.
records.zomi: Sitna khat na ngah kik ciangin mark bek hi lo-in na khialhnate a masa-in en in.

records.english: Write your notes in your own words.
records.zomi: Na thu gelhte nangma' kammal tawh gelh in.

records.english: My son does his homework as soon as he gets home.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in inn a tun pah-in a inn sinna a bawl hi.

records.english: What's the hardest subject for you?
records.zomi: Na adingin sinna haksa pen bang hiam?

records.english: Mixing different types of problems in one session can feel harder, yet it often prepares students better for real exams.

records.english: The whole street came out to welcome the football team home.
records.zomi: Football pawl inn ah muak dingin lampi bup a pusuak uh hi.

records.english: Describe the room where the party was held.
records.zomi: Pawi a kibawlna inndei gen in.

records.english: The best descriptions of crowds pick out a few individual faces instead of describing everyone at once.
records.zomi: Mihonpi genna hoih pente in mi khempeuh khatvei-in gen sangin mai tawmno a teel uh hi.

records.english: What a day it was!
records.zomi: Ni lamdang hi mah e!

records.english: My grandmother still describes her wedding day as if it happened last week.
records.zomi: Ka pi in a mopawi ni kal nunung-a piang bangin a gen lai hi.

records.english: At the harvest festival, the church was filled with baskets of rice, pumpkins and fruit.

records.english: After the service, the food was carried to the hall and shared among all the families.

records.english: Late in the evening, the elders sang the old songs while the young people listened.
records.zomi: Nitak sawt ciangin upate in la luite a sa uh a, khangnote in a ngaikhia uh hi.

records.english: When describing a festival, it helps to mention what happened before and after, not only the main moment.
records.zomi: Pawi khat na gen ciangin hun lianpen bek hi lo-in a ma leh a khit-a piangte gen a huh hi.

records.english: The wedding was small, but every guest had helped to prepare it.
records.zomi: Mopawi a neu a, ahi zongin khual khempeuh in a kiman nadingin a huh uh hi.

records.english: How many people came to the festival?
records.zomi: Pawi ah mi bangzah a hong uh hiam?

records.english: At the end of the evening, the organizers thanked the volunteers who had cooked for three hundred guests.
records.zomi: Nitak tawp ciangin a geelte in khual za thum adingin an a huan thalawpte lungdam a ci uh hi.

records.english: Who won the cooking competition?
records.zomi: An huan kiteelna kua in a zo hiam?

records.english: The bell rang, and the classroom emptied in seconds.
records.zomi: Khuang a ging a, sangnaupang inndei second tawmno sungin a awng hi.

records.english: Why are the events we describe most vividly so often the ones that went wrong?
records.zomi: Bang hangin i gen kilang pen thu piangte a khial te a hi zel hiam?

records.english: Hundreds of people lined the road to watch the runners pass.
records.zomi: Taimite a kantan en dingin mi za tampi lampi gei ah a ding uh hi.

records.english: Describing an event from the point of view of a child can make even an ordinary day seem extraordinary.
records.zomi: Naupang khat muh dan tawh thu piang khat gen in ni ngeina khat zong a lamdang bangin a kilang sak thei hi.

records.english: My cousin had the whole hall decorated with paper lanterns for her daughter's first birthday.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam numei in a tanu' suahni masa adingin inn lian bup lai meivak tawh a zeem sak hi.

records.english: The graduation hall was full of proud parents holding flowers and cameras.
records.zomi: Sang zawhna inn lian pen pak leh camera tawi kisaktheih nu leh pate tawh a dim hi.

records.english: Two people at the same event may remember it completely differently.
records.zomi: Thu piang kibang ah om mi nih in a kibang lo mahmah-in a phawk thei uh hi.

records.english: The funeral was quiet and simple, and the singing at the end made many people cry.
records.zomi: Mithi vuina a dai a, a baih a, a tawpna-a la in mi tampi a kapsak hi.

records.english: I do want to remember every moment of this day.
records.zomi: Hih ni' hun khempeuh phawk ka deih taktak hi.

records.english: The music started, and suddenly everyone was dancing.
records.zomi: La a kipan a, thakhatin mi khempeuh a lam uh hi.

records.english: The speeches went on so long that the food went cold.
records.zomi: Thugennate a sau lua ahih manin an a vot hi.

records.english: Choosing which moments to leave out is as important as choosing which ones to describe.
records.zomi: Bang hunte nusia ding hiam teel pen bang te gen ding hiam teel tawh a thupi kibang hi.

records.english: The event ended in a joyful mess of confetti, broken balloons and tired children.

records.english: It was the hottest day of the year, and the ice cream sellers ran out by noon.

records.english: Everyone stood up and clapped when the old teacher walked onto the stage.
records.zomi: Saya upa in a dinna tung ah a kah ciangin mi khempeuh a ding-in khut a beng uh hi.

records.english: Can you smell the smoke from the food stalls?
records.zomi: An zuakna munte pan meikhu gim na nam thei hiam?

records.english: An event that lasted only an hour can fill a whole chapter of a memoir.
records.zomi: Hun khat bek a sau thu piang khat in nuntak tangthu laibu sung khen bup a dimsak thei hi.

records.english: A report of an event lists what happened, while a description helps readers imagine being there.
records.zomi: Thu piang report khat in bang a piang hiam a list a, genna khat in simmite tua lai ah a om bangin a ngaihsut nadingun a huh hi.

records.english: The new bridge was opened by the mayor, who cut a red ribbon in front of the cameras.
records.zomi: Lei thak pen camera mai ah khuapi makaipa in puan khau san a at-in a hong hi.

records.english: Did you take any photos at the wedding?
records.zomi: Mopawi ah lim tawmno na la hiam?

records.english: Should a description of a sad event, such as a funeral, include moments of humour?

records.english: The first snow of the winter turned the school playground into a battlefield of snowballs.

records.english: A good description of an event moves through time, so the reader feels it beginning, building and ending.

records.english: Tell us about the best party you have ever been to.
records.zomi: Na pai ngeih pawi hoih pen tungtang hong gen un.

records.english: Who made the beautiful cake at the wedding?
records.zomi: Mopawi ah cake kilawm kua in a bawl hiam?

records.english: Writers often slow down at the most important moment of an event, describing a few seconds in great detail.

records.english: The fireworks lit up the river, and the children screamed with delight.
records.zomi: Meiphual in gun a vaksak a, naupangte lungdam takin a kikou uh hi.

records.zomi: Bang pia ding hiam na theih kei leh theigah bang kihawm thei bangmah khat pen teelna bit ahi hi.

records.english: For a neighbor who never accepts gifts, helping in the garden may be the best way to say thank you.
records.zomi: Letsong pom ngei lo inn veng khat adingin huan nasep huh pen lungdam cihna lampi hoih pen hi thei hi.

records.english: Sending a thank-you card by post takes longer than a message, but it can be kept on a shelf.
records.zomi: Lai khakna tawh lungdam cihna card khak in thu khak sangin a sawt zaw a, ahi zongin van koihna tungah kikoih thei hi.

records.english: I'd rather say thank you with a meal I've cooked than with something from a shop.
records.zomi: Dawl pan bangmah sangin ka huan an khat tawh lungdam ci ka deih zaw hi.

records.english: Giving the whole office a box of sweets is simpler than buying small gifts for each person who helped.
records.zomi: Office bup kiangah an khum bawm khat piak in a huh mi khatciat adingin letsong neu lei sangin a baih zaw hi.

records.english: A gift voucher feels more personal than cash, but cash is more useful to a student.
records.zomi: Letsong voucher in sum sangin mimal-in a kisa zaw a, ahi zongin sangnaupang khat adingin sum a phattuam zaw hi.

records.english: A drawing from a grandchild is worth more to my father than any gift we could buy.
records.zomi: Ka pa adingin tu khat' lim gelh in i lei theih letsong bangpeuh sangin a manpha zaw hi.

records.english: A formal letter suits the council, but a quick message is fine for a friend.
records.zomi: Kician lai khat khuapi vaihawm tawh a kituak a, ahi zongin lawm khat adingin thu khak tom khat a hoih hi.

records.english: Choosing a thank-you gift is easier when you know what the person actually enjoys.
records.zomi: Mi khat in bang a nuam sa taktak hiam na theih ciangin lungdam cihna letsong teel a baih zaw hi.

records.english: A handwritten note or an email, which would the manager like?
records.zomi: Khut tawh kigelh lai hiam email hiam, bang in manager a lungdamsak zaw ding hiam?

records.english: Being able to choose a gift that suits someone shows how well you know them.
records.zomi: Mi khat tawh a kituak letsong khat teel thei in amah bangzah na thei hiam a lak hi.

records.english: Should we send the thank-you cards now or wait until the wedding photos are ready?
records.zomi: Lungdam cihna card te tu-in i khak ding hiam, mopawi limte a kiman dong i ngak ding hiam?

records.english: Wait for the photos, so that every guest gets one with their card.
records.zomi: Limte ngak in, khual khempeuh in a card uh tawh khat a ngah theih nadingun.

records.english: A good online review helps a small business more than a private thank-you to the owner.
records.zomi: Online-a ngaihsutna gelh hoih khat in neipa kiang-a guk lungdam cihna sangin sumbawlna neu khat a huh zaw hi.

records.english: My aunt thinks flowers are a waste, so we always take her vegetables instead.
records.zomi: Ka ni in pakte mawk zatna ahi hi, a ci ahih manin amah kiangah anteh i tawi tawntung uh hi.

records.english: Thanking a whole team together saves time, but it may leave the person who worked hardest feeling unnoticed.
records.zomi: Pawl bup a khawm-in lungdam ci in hun a khawl a, ahi zongin a hanciam pen mi a kipaaimawh bangin a kisaksak thei hi.

records.english: Fruit from our garden is cheaper than a bought gift, and it seems to please people more.
records.zomi: I huan pan theigah in letsong kilei sangin a man neu zaw a, mite a lungdamsak zaw bang hi.

records.english: A short speech at the dinner or a letter afterwards, which would mean more to her?
records.zomi: Nitak an ah thugenna tom khat hiam a khit ciangin lai khat hiam, bang in amah adingin a thupi zaw ding hiam?

records.english: A thank-you present is chosen by the whole family in our house, so everyone feels part of it.
records.zomi: I inn ah lungdam cihna letsong innkuan bup in a teel ahih manin mi khempeuh a kihel bangin a kisa uh hi.

records.english: Some people feel uncomfortable when a thank-you gift is too generous, as if they now owe something in return.
records.zomi: Lungdam cihna letsong a man tam lua ciangin mi pawl khat a nuam lo-in a kisa uh hi, a kik piak ding a nei bangin.

records.english: Do you thank people more often at home or at work?
records.zomi: Inn ah hiam nasepna ah hiam lungdam na ci tam zaw hiam?

records.english: We chose a plant instead of flowers, because it will last longer.
records.zomi: A sawt zaw-in a om ding ahih manin pak sangin singkung neu khat i teel uh hi.

records.english: Do you think a gift card would look lazy?
records.zomi: Gift card khat a thadah bangin a kilang ding hi, na ci hiam?

records.english: Thanks can be given in words, in gifts or in help, and people differ in which one they value most.
records.zomi: Lungdam cihna kammal, letsong hiam huhna tawh kipia thei a, mite in bang a manpha pen sa uh hiam a kibang kei hi.

records.english: A thank-you gift that is useful every day is often remembered longer than one that is only beautiful.
records.zomi: Ni simin a phattuam lungdam cihna letsong khat a kilawm bek khat sangin sawt zaw-in kiphawk zel hi.

records.english: Who decides what the computer should learn?
records.zomi: Computer in bang a sin ding hiam kua in a khen hiam?

records.english: Our school used machine learning to predict which buses would be late in winter.
records.zomi: I sang in phalbi ciangin bang bus te a nunung ding hiam genkholh dingin machine learning a zang hi.

records.english: Can machine learning decide what is fair?
records.zomi: Machine learning in bang a dik hiam a khen thei hiam?

records.english: My brother's job is to label photos so that a computer can learn from them.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal' nasep pen computer in a sin theih nadingin limte min gelh ahi hi.

records.english: A system trained only on sunny photos may fail when it sees a road covered in snow.
records.zomi: Ni sa lim bek tawh kisinsak system khat in vuk tawh kikhuh lampi a muh ciangin a lohsap thei hi.

records.english: Does your little sister really think the computer is magic?
records.zomi: Na nau numei in computer pen lamdang thuguk ahi hi, ci-in a um taktak hiam?

records.english: A system can learn the wrong lesson, for example linking wolves with snow because most wolf photos had snow in the background.
records.zomi: System khat in sinna khial a sin thei hi, entehna-in ngiaksi lian limte a tamzaw in a nung ah vuk a om ahih manin ngiaksi lian leh vuk a kizopsak hi.

records.english: Why does the shopping site keep showing me shoes?
records.zomi: Bang hangin van lei website in khedap hong etsak den hiam?

records.english: Because you looked at shoes last week, it guesses that you want more.
records.zomi: Kal nunung in khedap na en ahih manin tam zaw na deih hi, ci-in a ngaihsun hi.

records.english: If a system's examples come mostly from one group of people, it may work worse for everyone else.
records.zomi: System khat' entehnate a tamzaw mi pawl khat pan hong pai leh mi dang khempeuh adingin a sem hoih lo kha thei hi.

records.english: A model trained in one country may give poor results in another, where people speak, shop or travel differently.
records.zomi: Gam khat ah kisinsak model khat gam dang ah, mite a gen, a lei hiam a khualzin dan uh a kibat loh mun ah, lohna hoih lo a pia thei hi.

records.english: Data from our village's rain gauges was used to train a model that warns farmers about dry spells.
records.zomi: I khua-a guah tehna set te' data zang-in lo nasemte khuakeu hun tungtang a phawksak model khat kisinsak hi.

records.english: The translation got better after millions of example sentences were added.
records.zomi: Entehna kammal tang tul za tampi kibehlap khit ciangin pau letna a hoih zaw hi.

records.english: The bank's system flagged my card when I bought something abroad.
records.zomi: Gamdang ah bangmah ka lei ciangin bank' system in ka card a ciamteh hi.

records.english: Please don't share private photos with apps you don't trust.
records.zomi: Na muan loh app te tawh guk limte hawm kei in.

records.english: Is the computer actually thinking?
records.zomi: Computer in a ngaihsun taktak hiam?

records.english: Machine learning helps doctors look through scans faster, but the doctor still makes the final decision.
records.zomi: Machine learning in siavuante scan te manlang zaw-in en dingin a huh a, ahi zongin siavuan in thukhenna nunung a bawl lai hi.

records.english: A machine learning system finds patterns in examples, then uses those patterns to make guesses about new cases.
records.zomi: Machine learning system khat in entehnate sungah lim a zong a, tua lim te zang-in thu thakte tungtang a ngaihsun hi.

records.english: A model can seem accurate in testing but still make strange mistakes in the real world.
records.zomi: Model khat sitna ah a dik bangin a kilang thei a, ahi zongin leitung taktak ah khialhna lamdang a bawl lai thei hi.

records.english: The model was retrained after users reported its mistakes.
records.zomi: A zangte in a khialhnate a gen khit uh ciangin model kisinsak kik hi.

records.english: Teach the program with more examples.
records.zomi: Program entehna tam zaw tawh sinsak in.

records.english: A recommendation system can keep people inside a narrow bubble of the things they already like.
records.zomi: Hilhna system khat in mite a deih khin uh vante' kiak sungah a kem thei hi.

records.english: When a system makes a decision about a person, such as a loan, people should be able to ask why.
records.zomi: System khat in mi khat tungtang thukhenna, leiba bang, a bawl ciangin mite in bang hang hiam a dong thei ding uh hi.

records.english: The factory uses machine learning to find faulty parts before they leave the building.
records.zomi: Factory in inn a nusiat ma-un khen siatte zong dingin machine learning a zang hi.

records.english: Our class trained a tiny model to tell apples from oranges.
records.zomi: I class in apple leh orange khen dingin model neu khat a sinsak uh hi.

records.english: How did the map app know about the traffic jam before we reached it?
records.zomi: Map app in i tun ma-in mawtaw kiak thu bangci-in a thei hiam?

records.english: How does the app know which songs I like?
records.zomi: App in bang la ka deih hiam bangci-in a thei hiam?

records.english: It learns from the songs you play, skip and repeat.
records.zomi: Na sak, na pelh leh na sak kik late pan a sin hi.

records.english: Using an app on his phone, my uncle can now identify every plant in her garden.
records.zomi: A phone tung-a app khat zang-in ka pa neu in tu-in a huan sung-a singkung khempeuh a thei thei hi.

records.english: To teach a computer to recognize cats, people first show it thousands of labelled photos.
records.zomi: Computer khat zaang theih dingin sinsak nadingin mite in a masa-in min gelh lim tul tampi a etsak uh hi.

records.english: The farm app learned to spot sick plants from photos taken by thousands of farmers.
records.zomi: Lo app in lo nasem tul tampi' lak limte pan singkung damlote muh a sin hi.

records.english: Does the camera at the shop count the customers?
records.zomi: Dawl-a camera in van lei mite a sim hiam?

records.english: Machine learning needs a lot of data, and that data has to be collected from somewhere.
records.zomi: Machine learning in data tampi a kisam a, tua data koi pan hiam kikaikhawm kisam hi.

records.english: A system that learns from mistakes still needs people to tell it which answers were mistakes.
records.zomi: Khialhna pan a sin system khat in bang dawnnate khialhna ahi hiam a hilh ding mite a kisam lai hi.

records.english: Predictions from machine learning are about likelihood, not certainty.
records.zomi: Machine learning pan genkholhnate pen hi kha thei ahi a, kician hi lo hi.

records.english: Students are not allowed to upload other people's photos to train their class project, according to our school's rules.
records.zomi: I sang thukham' gen bangin sangnaupangte in a class project sinsak dingin mi dangte' lim upload dingin kiphal lo uh hi.

records.english: The more good examples a system learns from, the better its guesses usually become.
records.zomi: System khat in entehna hoih tam zaw pan a sin semsem leh a ngaihsutnate a hoih semsem zel hi.

records.english: The quality of a system's examples matters more than their number, if many of them are wrong.
records.zomi: Entehna tampi a khial leh system khat' entehnate' hoihna in a tam zah sangin a thupi zaw hi.

records.english: The streaming service suggested a film that I actually loved.
records.zomi: Streaming service in ka deih taktak film khat a hilh hi.

records.english: Can a computer learn to recognize birdsong?
records.zomi: Computer khat in va la theih a sin thei hiam?

records.english: Yes, and some apps can now name a bird from a short recording.
records.zomi: Thei hi, tu-in app pawl khat in record tom khat pan va khat min a gen thei hi.

records.english: The voice assistant now understands my accent much better than it did last year.
records.zomi: Voice assistant in kum nunung sangin ka gen dan a thei hoih zaw mahmah hi.

records.english: Can machine learning help us save water?
records.zomi: Machine learning in tui khawl dingin hong huh thei hiam?

records.english: The spam filter learned which emails I don't want.
records.zomi: Spam filter in ka deih loh email te a sin hi.

records.english: Weather forecasts improve when computers learn from many years of past weather.
records.zomi: Computer te in kum tampi huihkhua lui pan a sin ciangin huihkhua genkholhnate a hoih zaw hi.

records.english: How long does it take to train a model?
records.zomi: Model khat sinsak dingin hun bangzah a la hiam?

records.english: It depends, because large models take weeks, while small ones can be trained in minutes on a laptop.
records.zomi: A kinga hi, model lian te in kal tampi a la a, neute laptop tungah minit tawmno sungin kisinsak thei hi.

records.english: Show me how the app sorts the photos.
records.zomi: App in limte bangci-in a khen hiam hong lak in.

records.english: Explaining how a model reached its answer is often harder than building the model itself.
records.zomi: Model khat in a dawnna bangci-in a tun hiam genteh pen model mah bawl sangin a haksa zaw zel hi.

records.english: Every time I mark a message as spam, the filter gets a little better.
records.zomi: Thu khak khat spam ci-in ka ciamteh simin filter a hoih zaw tawmno hi.

records.english: Our teacher said, "A machine learning program is only as good as the examples we give it."
records.zomi: I saya in, "Machine learning program khat pen i piak entehna zah bek in a hoih hi" a ci hi.
