records.english: The keyboard on my phone guesses the next word I'm going to type.
records.zomi: Ka phone tung-a keyboard in ka type ding kammal zom a ngaihsun hi.

records.english: It is necessary to test a model on examples it has never seen, or its accuracy will look better than it really is.
records.zomi: Model khat a muh ngei loh entehnate tawh sit a kisam hi, ahih kei leh a diktakna a taktak sangin a hoih zaw bangin a kilang ding hi.

records.english: When the app suggested the wrong word, I corrected it, and it learned from that.
records.zomi: App in kammal khial a hilh ciangin ka bawlpha a, tua pan a sin hi.

records.english: The photos were sorted into albums automatically, by face and by place.
records.zomi: Limte mai leh mun tawh amah mah in album sungah kikhen hi.

records.english: Did the computer learn that by itself?
records.zomi: Computer in tua pen amah mah in a sin hiam?

records.english: Not completely, because people chose the examples and checked its answers.
records.zomi: Kicing tak lo hi, mite in entehnate a teel uh a, a dawnnate a en uh ahih manin.

records.english: I don't like it when apps guess too much about me.
records.zomi: App te in ka tungtang tam lua a ngaihsut uh ciangin ka deih kei hi.

records.english: Is it possible to teach a computer to understand jokes?
records.zomi: Computer khat nuihzaak thu theih dingin sinsak thei hiam?

records.english: My phone recognizes my face even when I wear glasses.
records.zomi: Mitlimlang ka zat ciangin zong ka phone in ka mai a thei hi.

records.english: Did Jesus ever visit people who were not Jewish?
records.zomi: Jesu in Judah mi hi lo mite a veh ngei hiam?

records.english: In one of Luke's parables, a woman who loses a coin searches her whole house until she finds it.
records.zomi: Luka' thugentehna khat ah dangka khat a mansuah numei khat in a muh dong a inn bup a zong hi.

records.english: Did people who disagreed with Jesus ever invite him to dinner?
records.zomi: Jesu tawh a kikalh mite in amah nitak an ne dingin a sam ngei uh hiam?

records.english: Yes, the Gospels say he ate at the homes of Pharisees as well as tax collectors.
records.zomi: Sam hi, Lungdamna Thu laibute in siah-dongte' inn bangin Farisaite' inn ah zong an a ne hi, a ci uh hi.

records.english: To understand the Gospels well, it helps to know a little about life in first-century Galilee.
records.zomi: Lungdamna Thu laibute hoih takin theih nadingin kum za khatna Galile gam-a nuntakna tawmno theih a huh hi.

records.english: Every Thursday, our study group reads one story from the ministry of Jesus and talks about it over tea.
records.zomi: Laizing ni simin i sinna pawl in Jesu' nasepna pan tangthu khat a sim uh a, tea ne kawm-in a kikum uh hi.

records.english: Jesus often stayed in the homes of his friends.
records.zomi: Jesu in a lawmte' inn ah a om zel hi.

records.english: Children, today we'll read about four friends who carried a man to Jesus.
records.zomi: Naupangte, tuni-in Jesu kiangah mi khat a pua lawm li tungtang i sim ding uh hi.

records.english: Please don't skip the hard stories when you teach the children.
records.zomi: Naupangte na sinsak ciangin tangthu haksate pelh kei in.

records.english: Jesus asked his followers, "Who do you say I am?"
records.zomi: Jesu in a nungzuite kiangah, "Note in kei kua hi nong ci uh hiam?" ci-in a dong hi.

records.english: According to Matthew's Gospel, Peter answered that Jesus was the Messiah.
records.zomi: Matthai Lungdamna Thu' gen bangin Piter in Jesu pen Khazih ahi hi, ci-in a dawng hi.

records.english: It is important to read each story in its setting, rather than taking one verse on its own.
records.zomi: Cang khat bek la sangin tangthu khatciat a omna sungah sim a thupi hi.

records.english: Tax collectors were often disliked in Jesus' time, which made his friendship with them surprising to many.
records.zomi: Jesu' hun lai-in siah-dongte mi tampi in a huat uh ahih manin amaute tawh a lawmta in mi tampi a lamdangsak hi.

records.english: Many Christians read the Gospels as four portraits of the same person, each painted from a different angle.
records.zomi: Khristian tampi in Lungdamna Thu laibu li pen mi kibang' lim li, lam kibang lo pan kigelh bangin a sim uh hi.

records.english: Jesus ended the Sermon on the Mount, in Matthew's account, with a story about two builders.
records.zomi: Matthai' gen bangin Jesu in Mual Tung Thuhilhna inn lam pa nih tungtang tangthu khat tawh a tawpsak hi.

records.english: One built on rock and the other on sand, and only the first house was still standing after the storm.
records.zomi: Khat in suang tungah a lam a, a dang khat in ngal tungah a lam a, huihpi khit ciangin a masa' inn bek a ding lai hi.

records.english: My grandmother made us learn the names of the twelve apostles in order.
records.zomi: Ka pi in sawltak sawm leh nihte' min a kizui dan tawh hong sinsak hi.

records.english: Jesus called a tax collector named Matthew to follow him.
records.zomi: Jesu in Matthai kici siah-dong khat amah zui dingin a sam hi.

records.english: The Gospels tell how Jesus took Peter, James and John up a mountain, where his appearance was changed.
records.zomi: Lungdamna Thu laibute in Jesu in Piter, Jakob leh Johan mual tungah a paipih a, a meel a kilamdang hi, a ci uh hi.

records.english: Christians call this event the transfiguration.
records.zomi: Khristiante in hih thu piang pen Jesu meel kilamdangna ci-in a sam uh hi.

records.english: Many Christians find the story of the rich young man uncomfortable, because it asks what they themselves would give up.
records.zomi: Khristian tampi in tangval hau tangthu a nuam lo-in a sa uh hi, amaute mah in bang a nusia ding uh hiam a dong ahih manin.

records.english: Many teachers say Jesus used everyday images so that farmers, fishermen and children could all understand.
records.zomi: Saya tampi in Jesu in lo nasem, nga mante leh naupangte khempeuh in a theih theih nadingun ni sim lim te a zang hi, a ci uh hi.

records.english: Why did Nicodemus visit Jesus at night?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Nikodemas in zan ciangin Jesu a veh hiam?

records.english: The Gospel of John doesn't say, but many readers think he was afraid of being seen.
records.zomi: Johan Lungdamna Thu in a gen kei a, ahi zongin simmi tampi in a kimuh ding a lau hi, ci-in a ngaihsun uh hi.

records.english: I do want my students to picture the dusty roads and small villages where Jesus taught.
records.zomi: Jesu' hilhna lampi leivui leh khua neute ka sangnaupangte in a lungsim sungah a muh nadingun ka deih taktak hi.

records.english: In Mark's Gospel, a blind man called Bartimaeus kept shouting to Jesus, even when the crowd told him to be quiet.
records.zomi: Marka Lungdamna Thu ah Bartimai kici mittaw khat in mihonpi in dai dingin a hilh uh zongin Jesu a sam den hi.

records.english: The Gospels do describe Jesus as tired, hungry and even asleep in a boat.
records.zomi: Lungdamna Thu laibute in Jesu a tawl, a gil a kial leh tembaw sungah a ihmu zong hi, ci-in a gen uh hi.

records.english: The children acted out the story of the widow's coins with two buttons.
records.zomi: Naupangte in meigong' dangka tangthu button nih tawh a lak uh hi.

records.english: Who was Nicodemus?
records.zomi: Nikodemas kua ahi hiam?

records.english: According to Mark, Jesus said that the widow had given more than all the rich people.
records.zomi: Marka' gen bangin Jesu in meigong in mi hau khempeuh sangin tam zaw a pia hi, a ci hi.

records.english: According to Luke, when Jesus sent his followers out to the villages, he told them not to take a bag or spare sandals.
records.zomi: Luka' gen bangin Jesu in a nungzuite khuate ah a sawl ciangin ip hiam khedap behlap tawi lo dingin a hilh hi.

records.english: Many Christians understand the public ministry of Jesus to have lasted about three years.
records.zomi: Khristian tampi in Jesu' mipi nasepna kum thum bang a sau hi, ci-in a thei uh hi.

records.english: Which sister do you think you are more like, Mary or Martha?
records.zomi: Bang sanggam numei tawh na kibang zaw hiam, na ci hiam, Mari hiam Martha hiam?

records.english: Why did Jesus go up the mountain to pray?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Jesu thu ngen dingin mual tungah a kah hiam?

records.english: The story of the paralyzed man shows, many readers say, how much faith friends can have on someone else's behalf.
records.zomi: Khut leh khe si mi tangthu in lawmte in mi dang adingin upna bangzah a nei thei uh hiam a lak hi, ci-in simmi tampi in a gen uh hi.

records.english: Christians often read the story of the ten lepers as a lesson about gratitude.
records.zomi: Khristiante in mi phak sawm tangthu pen lungdamna tungtang sinna khat bangin a sim zel uh hi.

records.english: The Gospels describe Jesus noticing a poor widow who gave two small coins at the temple.
records.zomi: Lungdamna Thu laibute in Jesu in biakinn ah dangka neu nih a pia meigong zawng khat a phawk hi, ci-in a gen uh hi.

records.english: Which story about Jesus do you like best?
records.zomi: Jesu tungtang bang tangthu na deih pen hiam?

records.english: I like the one where the friends open the roof.
records.zomi: Lawmte in innkhum a hon tangthu ka deih hi.

records.english: The parable of the mustard seed compares God's kingdom to a tiny seed that grows into a large plant.
records.zomi: Ankam tang thugentehna in Pasian' gam pen singkung lian ah a khang ci neu khat tawh a teh hi.

records.english: Mary sat listening to Jesus while her sister Martha did the work, as Luke tells the story.
records.zomi: Luka' gen bangin Mari in Jesu' thu a ngaikhia-in a tu a, a sanggam numei Martha in nasep a sem hi.

records.english: Read the story of Bartimaeus aloud, please.
records.zomi: Bartimai tangthu ging takin sim in.

records.english: In Mark's Gospel, Jesus healed Peter's mother-in-law, and she got up and served them a meal.
records.zomi: Marka Lungdamna Thu ah Jesu in Piter' zi nu a damsak a, a thou-in an a vak hi.

records.english: In Luke's Gospel, ten men with a skin disease were healed, but only one came back to say thank you.
records.zomi: Luka Lungdamna Thu ah vun natna nei pasal sawm a dam uh a, ahi zongin khat bek lungdam ci dingin a kik hi.

records.english: In Mark's account, the friends made a hole in the roof and lowered the man down to Jesus.
records.zomi: Marka' gen bangin lawmte in innkhum ah kua khat a bawl uh a, mi pen Jesu kiangah a khia suk uh hi.

records.english: Christians disagree about how to apply the story of Jesus clearing the temple today.
records.zomi: Khristiante in Jesu in biakinn a siangsak tangthu tuni-in bangci-in zang ding hiam a kikalh uh hi.

records.english: All four Gospels report that Jesus drove the traders out of the temple and overturned their tables.
records.zomi: Lungdamna Thu laibu li khempeuh in Jesu in sumbawlte biakinn pan a hawlkhia a, a dawhkante a lehkhia hi, a ci uh hi.

records.english: Did Jesus have a home of his own during his ministry?
records.zomi: A nasepna sungin Jesu in amah' inn a nei hiam?

records.english: In the Gospels, a Roman officer asked Jesus to heal his servant without even coming to his house.
records.zomi: Lungdamna Thu laibute ah Rom galkap mangpa khat in Jesu kiangah a inn ah hong pai lo-in a sila damsak dingin a ngen hi.

records.english: A rich young man asked Jesus what he must do, and he went away sad, according to the Gospels.
records.zomi: Lungdamna Thu laibute' gen bangin tangval hau khat in Jesu kiangah bang a bawl ding hiam a dong a, a lungkim lo-in a paikhia hi.

records.english: Students, write down one question you would ask Jesus if you could.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte, na theih leh Jesu kiangah na dot ding dotna khat gelh un.

records.english: Christians believe that Jesus' ministry shows what God is like, not only what God wants.
records.zomi: Khristiante in Jesu' nasepna in Pasian' deih bek hi lo-in Pasian bangci om hiam a lak hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: Shall we make a map of the places Jesus visited?
records.zomi: Jesu' veh munte map khat i bawl ding hiam?

records.english: We used a children's Bible atlas to find Capernaum and the Sea of Galilee.
records.zomi: Kapernaum leh Galile tuili zong dingin naupangte' Laisiangtho map laibu khat i zang uh hi.

records.english: Where did Jesus do most of his teaching?
records.zomi: Jesu in a hilhna a tamzaw koi ah a bawl hiam?

records.english: In and around Galilee, according to the Gospels.
records.zomi: Lungdamna Thu laibute' gen bangin Galile gam leh a kim leh pam ah.

records.english: Let's learn the Lord's Prayer by heart this month.
records.zomi: Hih kha in Topa' Thungetna lungsim sungah i sin ni.

records.english: Luke's Gospel tells how the boy Jesus stayed behind in the temple when he was twelve.
records.zomi: Luka Lungdamna Thu in naupang Jesu kum sawm leh nih a cin ciangin biakinn ah a om zom hi, ci-in a gen hi.

records.english: Christians believe that Jesus taught his disciples the prayer now known as the Lord's Prayer.
records.zomi: Khristiante in Jesu in a nungzuite kiangah tu-in Topa' Thungetna kici thungetna a sinsak hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: Why do you think Jesus told so many stories about ordinary things like seeds and coins?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Jesu in khaici leh dangka bang ni sim van tungtang tangthu tampi a gen hi, na ci hiam?

records.english: Where are your parents spending the winter?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa phalbi koi ah a om ding uh hiam?

records.english: With my sister, because her house is warmer.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam numei tawh, a inn a lum zaw ahih manin.

records.english: When all the relatives came to stay, where did you sleep?
records.zomi: Sanggam khempeuh a hong giak uh ciangin koi ah na ihmu hiam?

records.english: On a mat in the kitchen, with three of my cousins.
records.zomi: An huanna inn sungah phak tungah, ka sanggam thum tawh.

records.english: Where did you and your wife first meet?
records.zomi: Nang leh na zi koi ah na kimu masa uh hiam?

records.english: On a bus to the city, when she dropped her bag on my foot.
records.zomi: Khuapi pai bus khat tungah, amah in ka khe tungah a ip a khiat ciangin.

records.english: Where did your parents get married?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa koi ah a kiteeng uh hiam?

records.english: In the old church in my mother's village, under a leaking roof.
records.zomi: Ka nu' khua-a pawlpi lui ah, a zuk inn tung nuai ah.

records.english: Do you know where your parents had their wedding photos taken?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa in a mopawi limte koi ah a la uh hiam na thei hiam?

records.english: By the river in the town park, where we later had ours taken too.
records.zomi: Khuapi huan sung-a gun kiang ah, a nung ciangin eite' zong tua ah i la uh hi.

records.english: Where is your grandfather buried?
records.zomi: Na pu koi ah kivui hiam?

records.english: In the churchyard of the village where he was born, next to his parents.
records.zomi: A suahna khua-a pawlpi han mun ah, a nu leh a pa kiang ah.

records.english: Where people choose to be buried often says something about where they felt they truly belonged.
records.zomi: Mite in koi ah kivui dingin a teel uh hiam in koi ah a kihel taktak uh hi, ci-in a kisa uh hiam bangmah khat a gen zel hi.

records.english: Where was your father when he learned to cook like that?
records.zomi: Na pa tua bangin an huan a sin lai-in koi ah a om hiam?

records.english: He learned in the army, where he ran the kitchen for two years.
records.zomi: Galkap ah a sin a, tua ah kum nih sung an huanna inn a uk hi.

records.english: May I ask where your family is from originally?
records.zomi: Na innkuan a kipatna-in koi pan ahi hiam ka dong thei ding hiam?

records.english: From the hills in the north, though we moved to the city when I was a baby.
records.zomi: Mallam-a mualte pan, naungek ka hih lai-in khuapi ah i tai uh hangin.

records.english: When I was eight, I asked my mother where she had been born.
records.zomi: Kum giat ka cin ciangin ka nu kiangah koi ah a suak hiam ka dong hi.

records.english: She took me on a long bus journey to a tiny village with a single shop.
records.zomi: Dawl khat bek nei khua neu mahmah khat ah bus tawh khualzinna sau khat ah hong paipih hi.

records.english: Standing outside a small wooden house, she said quietly, "This is where it all began."
records.zomi: Sing inn neu khat pua ah ding-in, dai takin, "Hih ah khempeuh a kipan hi" a ci hi.

records.english: Where do you want us to scatter Grandpa's ashes?
records.zomi: Pu' vutte koi ah i theh ding na deih hiam?

records.english: On the hill behind the village, where he used to watch the sun go down.
records.zomi: Khua nung-a mual tungah, ni tum a en ngeihna mun ah.

records.english: Where would you go for the holidays as a child?
records.zomi: Naupan lai-in tawlngakni ciangin koi ah na pai zel hiam?

records.english: At my grandparents' house, helping on the farm from dawn to dusk.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh pi' inn ah, zingsang pan nitak dong lo ah huh.

records.english: Questions about where people grew up often lead to stories about schools, rivers and neighbors long gone.
records.zomi: Mite koi ah a khang uh hiam cih dotnate in a mang khin sangte, gunte leh inn vengte tungtang tangthu ah a pi zel hi.

records.english: A family map with everyone's birthplace marked on it can start conversations that last a whole evening.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh' suahna mun ciamteh innkuan map khat in nitak bup a sau kikupna a hong thei hi.

records.english: Where does your daughter want to study?
records.zomi: Na tanu koi ah sin a deih hiam?

records.english: Somewhere close enough to come home at weekends.
records.zomi: Kal tawp simin inn ah a hong theih nading zah-in a nai mun khat ah.

records.english: Where do you keep the family photo albums?
records.zomi: Innkuan lim laibute koi ah na kem uh hiam?

records.english: Grandma keeps them in the trunk at the foot of her bed.
records.zomi: Pi in a lupna khe lam-a van bawm sungah a kem hi.

records.english: Asking children where they feel most at home can reveal more than asking where they live.
records.zomi: Naupangte kiangah koi ah inn bangin na kisa pen hiam dot in koi ah na teeng hiam dot sangin tam zaw a lak thei hi.

records.english: Where do you all sit at dinner?
records.zomi: Nitak an ciangin na khempeuh koi ah na tu uh hiam?

records.english: Grandpa at the head of the table and the children nearest the kitchen.
records.zomi: Pu dawhkan lu lam ah, naupangte an huanna inn kiang nai pen ah.

records.english: Where do your children go after school?
records.zomi: Na tate sang khit ciangin koi ah a pai uh hiam?

records.english: To their grandparents' house until I finish work.
records.zomi: Ka nasep ka zawh dong a pu leh a pi uh' inn ah.

records.english: How do you answer when someone asks where home is, if you have lived in four countries?
records.zomi: Gam li ah na teen khin leh mi khat in inn koi ahi hiam a dot ciangin bangci-in na dawng hiam?

records.english: For some families, home is not a single place but wherever the oldest relative happens to live.
records.zomi: Innkuan pawl khat adingin inn pen mun khat bek hi lo-in sanggam upa pen a teenna mun peuh ahi hi.

records.english: Asking where someone's family comes from can be friendly, but for people who had to leave their homes it may bring back painful memories.
records.zomi: Mi khat' innkuan koi pan hong pai hiam dot in lawmtakna hi thei a, ahi zongin a inn uh nusia kisam mite adingin phawkna natte a kik sak thei hi.

records.english: Where would you most like to take your parents on holiday?
records.zomi: Tawlngakni adingin na nu leh na pa koi ah paipih na deih pen hiam?

records.english: To the sea, because my father has never swum in salt water.
records.zomi: Tuipi ah, ka pa in tui al ah a peek ngei kei ahih manin.

records.english: Where were the sweets hidden in your grandmother's house?
records.zomi: Na pi' inn ah an khum koi ah kisel hiam?

records.english: Behind the rice jars, though we always found them.
records.zomi: Buh bel nung ah, i mu tawntung uh hangin.

records.english: Where is your sister working these days?
records.zomi: Tu laitakin na sanggam numei koi ah nasep a sem hiam?

records.english: At a bakery near the station, and she loves it.
records.zomi: Dinna mun kiang-a moh bawlna dawl khat ah, a deih mahmah hi.

records.english: Where will the family reunion be this year?
records.zomi: Kum in innkuan kikhopna koi ah om ding hiam?

records.english: At my uncle's farm, if the road is dry enough.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu' lo ah, lampi a keu kicin leh.

records.english: Where should we put the baby's cot?
records.zomi: Naungek lupna koi ah i koih ding hiam?

records.english: Next to our bed for the first few months.
records.zomi: Kha masa tawmno sung i lupna kiang ah.

records.english: Where does your brother live now?
records.zomi: Na sanggam pasal tu-in koi ah a teeng hiam?

records.english: In the capital, near the hospital where he works.
records.zomi: Gam khuapi lian ah, a nasepna siavuan inn kiang ah.

records.english: Where did you get that beautiful old clock?
records.zomi: Tua nai lui kilawm koi pan na ngah hiam?

records.english: It belonged to my great-grandfather, and I had it repaired last year.
records.zomi: Ka pu' pa' ahi a, kum nunung in ka bawlpha sak hi.

records.english: Where did your family live during the war?
records.zomi: Gal laitakin na innkuan koi ah a teeng uh hiam?

records.english: In a small village in the mountains, with relatives who shared everything they had.
records.zomi: Mualte lak-a khua neu khat ah, a neih khempeuh a hawm sanggamte tawh.

records.english: Where a family settles often depends on work, schools and where relatives already live.
records.zomi: Innkuan khat koi ah a teeng hiam pen nasep, sang leh sanggamte a teenna mun tungah a kinga zel hi.

records.english: Where would you like to be living in ten years' time?
records.zomi: Kum sawm khit ciangin koi ah teeng na deih hiam?

records.english: Close to my parents, so that I can look after them as they get older.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa kiang ah, a upat ciangin ka kem theih nadingin.

records.english: Children of migrants are sometimes asked where they are really from, a question that can feel like a challenge to their belonging.
records.zomi: Gam taimite' tate kiangah a taktak in koi pan na hi hiam ci-in kidong zel a, tua dotna in a kihelna uh langpan bangin a kisa thei hi.

records.english: Children, where shall we hang Grandpa's birthday banner?
records.zomi: Naupangte, Pu' suahni puan ciamtehna koi ah i khai ding hiam?

records.english: Over the front door, so that he sees it first!
records.zomi: Mai lam kongkhak tungah, a muh masak nadingin!

records.english: We had the wiring checked after the fuse blew twice, and the electrician found the real fault.
records.zomi: Fuse vei nih a kan khit ciangin meivak khau i en sak uh a, electrician in a siat taktak a mu hi.

records.english: My brother crashed his bike because he was looking at his phone.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in a phone a en ahih manin a siiksakol tawh a kituah hi.

records.english: How can children learn to fix their own mistakes?
records.zomi: Naupangte in amau' khialhnate bawlpha dan bangci-in a sin thei uh hiam?

records.english: Try it again, more slowly this time.
records.zomi: Sin kik in, tu vei in zawi zaw-in.

records.english: Some workplaces hold short meetings after every mistake, not to blame anyone but to change the system.
records.zomi: Nasepna mun pawl khat in khialhna khatciat khit ciangin kuamah mawhsak ding hi lo-in system kheel dingin kikhopna tom a nei uh hi.

records.english: I really want to try again, even though I failed the first time.
records.zomi: A masa vei ka lohsap zongin sin kik ka deih taktak hi.

records.english: What went wrong with the recipe?
records.zomi: An huan dan ah bang a khial hiam?

records.english: My father made me go back and apologize to the shopkeeper after I broke the vase.
records.zomi: Pak bel ka sukkham khit ciangin ka pa in dawl neipa kiangah maisak ngen dingin hong ciahsak kik hi.

records.english: We lost the first game badly, and that made us train harder for the rest of the season.
records.zomi: Kimawlna masa i lel mahmah uh a, tua in kum sung a dang adingin a hat zaw-in hong kisinsak hi.

records.english: Children, it's all right to get the answer wrong, as long as you try.
records.zomi: Naupangte, na sin zah-in dawnna khial pen a hoih hi.

records.english: Admitting a mistake early usually causes less trouble than hiding it.
records.zomi: Khialhna khat a ngal-in pom in a sel sangin buaina tawm zaw a piangsak zel hi.

records.english: Making a mistake in front of others feels terrible, but the feeling fades much faster than people expect.
records.zomi: Mi dangte mai-ah khialhna bawl in a hoih lo mahmah bangin a kisa a, ahi zongin mite' lamen sangin manlang zaw-in a mang hi.

records.english: Every mistake I made in my first year of teaching taught me something about my pupils.
records.zomi: Ka sinsak kum masa-a ka khialhna khempeuh in ka sangnaupangte tungtang bangmah hong sinsak hi.

records.english: Can I have another try?
records.zomi: Vei khat ka sin kik thei ding hiam?

records.english: Should schools give marks for effort as well as for correct answers?
records.zomi: Sangte in dawnna dik bangin hanciamna adingin zong mark a pia ding uh hiam?

records.english: The doctor admitted that the first test had been read wrongly and arranged a new one.
records.zomi: Siavuan in sitna masa khial-in kisim hi, ci a pom a, a thak khat a geel hi.

records.english: My mother laughed when I used salt instead of sugar in her tea.
records.zomi: A tea sungah sugar sangin cii ka zat ciangin ka nu a nui hi.

records.english: Asking for help after a mistake shows strength, not weakness.
records.zomi: Khialhna khit ciangin huhna ngen in hatna a lak a, hatlohna hi lo hi.

records.english: Next time, read the question twice before you answer.
records.zomi: A zom vei ah na dawn ma-in dotna vei nih sim in.

records.english: Blaming others for a mistake usually stops you from learning anything from it.
records.zomi: Khialhna khat adingin mi dangte mawhsak in a pan bangmah na sin lo dingin a khaam zel hi.

records.english: I mixed up the dates and arrived at the party a week early.
records.zomi: Ni te ka buaisak a, pawi ah kal khat a ngal-in ka tung hi.

records.english: What did you learn from losing the match?
records.zomi: Kimawlna lel pan bang na sin hiam?

records.english: That we need to practise our passing, not just our shooting.
records.zomi: Kap bek hi lo-in kikhen piak i kisin kisam uh hi, cih.

records.english: Fear of making mistakes can stop people from speaking a new language at all.
records.zomi: Khialhna bawl launa in mite pau thak gen pan a khaam kim thei hi.

records.english: Teachers who show their own mistakes help pupils feel safe enough to make theirs.
records.zomi: Amau' khialhnate a lak sayate in sangnaupangte amau' khialhna bawl nadingin bit takin a kisaksak uh hi.

records.english: When our team missed the deadline, we changed the way we divided the work.
records.zomi: I pawl in ni tawp a pelh ciangin nasep i kikhen dan i kheel uh hi.

records.english: Doesn't everyone make mistakes when they are learning something new?
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh in thu thak a sin ciangin khialhna a bawl uh hi lo hiam?

records.english: I burned the rice again, but this time I know why.
records.zomi: Buh ka kangkham kik a, ahi zongin tu vei in bang hang hiam ka thei hi.

records.english: I'll never forget the day I called my teacher "Mum" in front of the whole class.
records.zomi: Class bup mai-ah ka saya "Nu" ka sap ni ka mangngilh ngei lo ding hi.

records.english: The best lessons sometimes come from the most embarrassing moments.
records.zomi: Sinna hoih pente pawl khat ciangin a zumhuai pen hunte pan hong pai zel hi.

records.english: Who hasn't sent a message to the wrong person?
records.zomi: Kua in mi khial kiangah thu khak a khak ngei lo hiam?

records.english: Don't be so hard on yourself.
records.zomi: Nangmah tungah khauh lua kei in.

records.english: People often learn more from a small failure than from an easy success.
records.zomi: Mite in lawhcinna baih khat sangin lohsapna neu khat pan tam zaw a sin zel uh hi.

records.english: I planted the beans too early, and the frost killed them all.
records.zomi: Be ka suan ngal lua a, vuk khal in a khempeuh a thah hi.

records.english: Being told kindly what you did wrong is very different from being shamed for it.
records.zomi: Na khialh nem taka kigen pen zumsakna tawh a kibang lo mahmah hi.

records.english: Experience is often just the name we give to the mistakes we have learned from.
records.zomi: Theihna pen i sinna khialhnate' min i piak bek ahi zel hi.

records.english: Students, write one mistake you made this week and what you learned from it.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte, hih kal-a na khialhna khat leh tua pan na sin gelh un.

records.english: Writing down what went wrong in a project helps the next team avoid the same problem.
records.zomi: Project khat sungah bang a khial hiam gelh in pawl zom in buaina kibang a pelh nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: A mistake made twice is a choice, my grandmother used to say.
records.zomi: Vei nih bawl khialhna pen teelna ahi hi, ci-in ka pi in a ci zel hi.

records.english: A mistake that hurts someone else needs an apology first and a lesson second.
records.zomi: Mi dang a natsak khialhna khat in maisak ngenna a masa-in a kisam a, sinna a nihna ahi hi.

records.english: The bridge was rebuilt with stronger supports after the first one cracked.
records.zomi: A masa a keh khit ciangin lei khuam hat zaw tawh kilam kik hi.

records.english: Why did the cake sink in the middle?
records.zomi: Bang hangin cake a laizang ah a kiam hiam?

records.english: I left the oven door open too long, so I'll keep it shut next time.
records.zomi: Oven kongkhak sawt lua ka hong ahih manin a zom vei ah ka khak den ding hi.

records.english: A child who is punished for every mistake may simply learn to hide them.
records.zomi: Khialhna khempeuh adingin kigawt naupang khat in a sel dan bek a sin kha thei hi.

records.english: Mistakes in medicine or engineering can be so serious that whole systems are designed to catch them early.
records.zomi: Zatui lam hiam engineering lam-a khialhnate a gik thei mahmah ahih manin a ngal-in mat dingin system bup kigeel hi.

records.english: Let's look at what went wrong and try again.
records.zomi: Bang a khial hiam i en ding a, i sin kik ding hi.

records.english: Why does your sister keep a notebook of her driving mistakes?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na sanggam numei in a mawtaw mawng khialhnate notebook khat sungah a gelh hiam?

records.english: I'm sorry, I forgot to save the file, and now the work is lost.
records.zomi: Maisak in, file save ka mangngilh a, tu-in nasep a mang hi.

records.english: My son learned to count change after a shopkeeper gave him too little.
records.zomi: Dawl neipa khat in tawm lua a piak khit ciangin ka tapa in sum kik sim a sin hi.

records.english: Was it my fault?
records.zomi: Kei' mawhna ahi hiam?

records.english: Not entirely, because the instructions were confusing.
records.zomi: Kicing-in hi lo hi, hilhnate a buai ahih manin.

records.english: A mistake is easier to learn from when it is discussed calmly the same day.
records.zomi: Khialhna khat ni kibang ah dai taka kikup ciangin a pan sin a baih zaw hi.

records.english: Oops, I added the numbers wrong.
records.zomi: Aw, nambatte khial takin ka behlap hi.

records.english: On my first day as a waiter, I dropped a whole tray of glasses.
records.zomi: An pia nasem ka hih ni masa ah haai kuang bup ka khiat hi.

records.english: The manager helped me sweep up and showed me how to hold the tray with both hands.
records.zomi: Manager in phiat dingin hong huh a, kuang khut nih tawh len dan hong lak hi.

records.english: I never dropped a tray again, and now I teach new staff the same way.
records.zomi: Kuang ka khiat kik ngei kei a, tu-in nasem thakte lampi kibang tawh ka sinsak hi.

records.english: Mistakes are a normal part of learning, but repeating them is not.
records.zomi: Khialhnate sinna sung-a ngeina khen khat ahi a, ahi zongin bawl kik pen hi lo hi.

records.english: A mistake becomes useful only when someone stops to ask what caused it.
records.zomi: Khialhna khat pen kuamah in bang in a piangsak hiam dot dingin a khawl ciangin bek a phattuam hi.

records.english: What would you do differently if you could start again?
records.zomi: Na kipan kik thei leh bang kibang lo-in na bawl ding hiam?

records.english: When I misread the bus timetable, I missed my interview, and since then I always check twice.
records.zomi: Bus pai hun gelhna ka sim khial ciangin ka kidotna ka pelh a, tua pan vei nih ka en tawntung hi.

records.english: Choosing to forgive someone is a decision about the future, not a judgement about the past.
records.zomi: Mi khat maisak dingin teel pen tanglai tungtang thukhenna hi lo-in a hong tung ding tungtang thukhenna ahi hi.

records.english: Sorry for being so quiet tonight; I'm just tired.
records.zomi: Tu zan-in ka dai lua ahih manin hong maisak in; ka tawl bek hi.

records.english: Nobody can be made to forgive, and nobody should pretend to forgive when they haven't.
records.zomi: Kuamah maisak dingin kisawl thei lo a, kuamah in a maisak lo-in maisak bangin kibawl ding hi lo hi.

records.english: When both of us were wrong, we agreed to apologize at the same time.
records.zomi: I nih in i khial uh ciangin hun kibang ah maisak ngen dingin i kituak uh hi.

records.english: Do you think a joke can ever replace an apology?
records.zomi: Nuihzaak khat in maisak ngenna a laih thei ngei hiam, na ci hiam?

records.english: Saying sorry to a colleague in private is often kinder than doing it in front of the whole office.
records.zomi: Nasep pih khat kiangah guk-in maisak ngen pen office bup mai-ah ngen sangin a hehpihna zaw zel hi.

records.english: Forgiving my brother was easy; trusting him again took longer.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal maisak a baih a; amah muang kik in hun sawt zaw a la hi.

records.english: Who should we say sorry to first, the teacher or the other boy?
records.zomi: Kua kiangah maisak i ngen masa ding hiam, saya kiangah hiam, tangval dang kiangah hiam?

records.english: The other boy, because he was the one who got hurt.
records.zomi: Tangval dang, a liam pa ahih manin.

records.english: My sister prefers a short apology, while my brother needs to talk everything through.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam numei in maisak ngenna tom a deih zaw a, ka sanggam pasal in khempeuh kikum a kisam hi.

records.english: Apologizing to a child matters just as much as apologizing to an adult, though it may need simpler words.
records.zomi: Naupang khat kiangah maisak ngen pen upa khat kiangah ngen tawh a thupi kibang hi, kammal baih zaw a kisam kha thei hangin.

records.english: Some people apologize with flowers, others with a phone call, and some with a hug.
records.zomi: Mi pawl khat in pak tawh maisak a ngen uh a, a dangte phone tawh, pawl khat kawikawi tawh.

records.english: Being able to apologize without making excuses is a skill that many adults are still learning.
records.zomi: A hang gen lo-in maisak ngen thei pen upa tampi in a sin lai uh siamna khat ahi hi.

records.english: Forgiveness can be offered to someone who never apologizes, but reconciliation usually needs both people.
records.zomi: Maisak ngen ngei lo mi khat zong maisak thei a, ahi zongin kilemna in mi nih a kisam zel hi.

records.english: The older we get, the easier it seems to say sorry and the harder it is to forget.
records.zomi: I upat semsem leh maisak ngen a baih semsem bang a, mangngilh a haksa semsem hi.

records.english: Should I tell my manager about the mistake now, or fix it first?
records.zomi: Khialhna tungtang ka manager kiangah tu-in ka gen ding hiam, a masa-in ka bawlpha ding hiam?

records.english: Tell her now, because she'll hear about it anyway.
records.zomi: Tu-in gen in, bang hi zongin a za ding ahih manin.

records.english: Saying sorry first does not mean you were the only one who was wrong.
records.zomi: A masa-in maisak ngen in nang bek na khial hi, cihna hi lo hi.

records.english: Would you rather I paid for the repair or fixed it myself?
records.zomi: Bawlphatna man ka pia ding hiam, keimah mah in ka bawlpha ding hiam, na deih zaw hiam?

records.english: Fix it yourself, if you know how, because the shop is very expensive.
records.zomi: Na theih leh nangmah mah in bawlpha in, dawl a man tam mahmah ahih manin.

records.english: In some families, an apology is made through an older relative rather than directly.
records.zomi: Innkuan pawl khat ah maisak ngenna pen tangtak hi lo-in sanggam upa khat tungtawn-in kibawl hi.

records.english: I'd like to apologize to your parents, but I'm not sure whether to call or visit.
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa kiangah maisak ngen ka deih a, ka sam ding hiam ka veh ding hiam ka thei kei hi.

records.english: Apologies sent by text are quick, but they can easily be misunderstood.
records.zomi: Text tawh kikhak maisak ngennate a manlang a, ahi zongin kitheih khial a baih hi.

records.english: Apologizing to a large group, such as customers or a whole village, needs different words from apologizing to one friend.
records.zomi: Van lei mite hiam khua bup bang pawl lian khat kiangah maisak ngen in lawm khat kiangah ngen tawh kibang lo kammal a kisam hi.

records.english: Sorry, I'll pay for the cup I broke, or would you prefer a new one from the market?
records.zomi: Maisak in, ka sukkham haai man ka pia ding hi, a hih kei leh zuakna mun pan a thak khat na deih zaw hiam?

records.english: A new one, please.
records.zomi: A thak khat, kong ngen hi.

records.english: Should I apologize to my friend by message tonight or wait until I see her on Monday?
records.zomi: Ka lawm kiangah tu zan-in thu khak tawh maisak ka ngen ding hiam, Pizing ni ciangin ka muh dong ka ngak ding hiam?

records.english: Waiting until Monday shows more respect, but a short message tonight might stop her worrying.
records.zomi: Pizing ni dong ngak in zahtakna tam zaw a lak a, ahi zongin tu zan thu khak tom khat in a lunghimawh pan a khawlsak thei hi.

records.english: Is it right to apologize for something your brother did?
records.zomi: Na sanggam pasal' bawl adingin maisak ngen a dik hiam?

records.english: Shall we apologize now or wait until Dad gets home?
records.zomi: Tu-in maisak i ngen ding hiam, Pa inn a tun dong i ngak ding hiam?

records.english: Let's wait, so that we can say it together.
records.zomi: I ngak ni, a khawm-in i gen theih nadingin.

records.english: Do you apologize first, or do you wait for the other person?
records.zomi: A masa-in maisak na ngen hiam, mi dang na ngak hiam?

records.english: Which would you prefer, a letter or a visit?
records.zomi: Bang na deih zaw hiam, lai khat hiam vehna khat hiam?

records.english: Some people find it easier to forgive a mistake than a lie.
records.zomi: Mi pawl khat in zuau khat sangin khialhna khat maisak a baih sa zaw uh hi.

records.english: An apology to a neighbor is easier face to face than through a note under the door.
records.zomi: Inn veng khat kiangah maisak ngenna pen kongkhak nuai-a lai neu tungtawn sangin mai leh mai-in a baih zaw hi.

records.english: We decided to apologize to each other in front of the children, so that they could see how it is done.
records.zomi: Naupangte in bangci-in kibawl hiam a muh theih nadingun a mai uh ah kimaisak ngen dingin i khen uh hi.

records.english: Some people feel that a gift makes an apology look like a payment.
records.zomi: Mi pawl khat in letsong khat in maisak ngenna man piak bangin a kilangsak hi, ci-in a kisa uh hi.

records.english: A smile and a cup of tea ended the quarrel faster than any speech could have.
records.zomi: Nuih leh tea haai khat in thugenna bangpeuh sangin kinialna manlang zaw-in a tawpsak hi.

records.english: Should the whole class apologize together, or should each child do it separately?
records.zomi: Class bup in a khawm-in maisak a ngen ding uh hiam, naupang khatciat in a tuam-in hiam?

records.english: Each child separately, so that every one of them thinks about what they did.
records.zomi: Naupang khatciat tuam-in, amaute khatciat in a bawl uh a ngaihsut nadingun.

records.english: Is it better to forgive quickly or to take time and mean it?
records.zomi: Manlang takin maisak a hoih zaw hiam, hun la-a lungsim takpi tawh maisak a hoih zaw hiam?

records.english: A small token, such as a cake, can soften an apology, but it can't replace the words.
records.zomi: Cake bang ciamtehna neu khat in maisak ngenna a nemsak thei a, ahi zongin kammalte a laih thei kei hi.

records.english: I'd rather say sorry today than lie awake worrying about it all night.
records.zomi: Zan bup tua tungtang lunghimawh-a ihmut lo sangin tuni-in maisak ngen ka deih zaw hi.

records.english: My father apologizes by cooking dinner, while my mother apologizes with words.
records.zomi: Ka pa in nitak an huan-in maisak a ngen a, ka nu in kammal tawh maisak a ngen hi.

records.english: Accepting an apology politely is different from pretending that nothing happened.
records.zomi: Maisak ngenna zahtak taka pom pen bangmah piang lo bangin kibawl tawh a kibang lo hi.

records.english: A written apology can be read again, but a spoken one shows your face and your voice.
records.zomi: Kigelh maisak ngenna sim kik thei a, ahi zongin kigen khat in na mai leh na aw a lak hi.

records.english: It is necessary to apologize to the person you hurt, not just to the people who saw it.
records.zomi: Na natsak mi kiangah maisak ngen a kisam a, a mu mite kiangah bek hi lo hi.

records.english: A promise to change means little if the same mistake happens again the next week.
records.zomi: Kikheel ding kiciamna in khialhna kibang a zom kal a piang kik leh a khiatna tawm hi.

records.english: My mother says, "Apologize for what you did, not for who you are."
records.zomi: Ka nu in, "Na bawl adingin maisak ngen in, na hihna adingin hi lo" a ci hi.

records.english: Children who are forced to apologize may learn to say the words without feeling them.
records.zomi: Maisak ngen dingin kisawl naupangte in a lungsim tawh kisa lo-in kammalte gen a sin kha thei uh hi.

records.english: Is it harder to apologize to someone you love or to someone you hardly know?
records.zomi: Na it mi khat kiangah hiam, na theih lo dek mi khat kiangah hiam maisak ngen a haksa zaw hiam?

records.english: A well-timed apology can stop a quarrel from hardening into years of silence.
records.zomi: Hun takin maisak ngenna khat in kinialna khat kum tampi daina ah a khauh pan a khawlsak thei hi.

records.english: Some families settle quarrels with a long talk, while others prefer a quiet meal and a fresh start.
records.zomi: Innkuan pawl khat in kinialnate kikupna sau tawh a bawlsiang uh a, a dangte in an nek dai leh kipatna thak a deih zaw uh hi.

records.english: Don't worry about the children; they were only playing.
records.zomi: Naupangte tungtang lunghimawh kei in; a kimawl bek uh hi.

records.english: Is a quick sorry enough when you bump into someone?
records.zomi: Mi khat na dong ciangin maisak manlang khat a tam hiam?

records.english: Saying sorry in my mother-in-law's language meant more to her than a long speech in mine.
records.zomi: Ka pasal' nu' pau tawh maisak ngen in kei' pau tawh thugenna sau khat sangin amah adingin a thupi zaw hi.

records.english: An apology made because someone was caught is different from one offered freely.
records.zomi: Mi khat a kimat hang-a maisak ngenna in a deih taka kipia khat tawh a kibang lo hi.

records.english: Sometimes an explanation is more useful than an apology, especially when nobody was really at fault.
records.zomi: Pawl khat ciangin, a diak in kuamah a khial taktak kei ciangin, genteh in maisak ngen sangin a phattuam zaw hi.

records.english: Choose a quiet place to apologize, not the middle of a party.
records.zomi: Maisak ngen dingin pawi laizang hi lo-in mun dai khat teel in.

records.english: Was the apology for you or for your mother?
records.zomi: Maisak ngenna pen nang adingin ahi hiam, na nu adingin ahi hiam?

records.english: Which family tradition do you want your children to keep?
records.zomi: Bang innkuan ngeina na tate in a kem dingin na deih hiam?

records.english: Eating together on Sunday evenings, whatever else is happening.
records.zomi: Bangmah dang a piang zongin Nipini nitak simin a khawm-in an nek.

records.english: Which job did your father do before he retired?
records.zomi: Na pa in nasep a khawl ma-in bang nasep a sem hiam?

records.english: He was a postman for over thirty years.
records.zomi: Kum sawmthum val sung lai khakna nasem ahi hi.

records.english: Which song did your parents dance to at their wedding?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa in a mopawi ah bang la tawh a lam uh hiam?

records.english: An old love song from the radio that my father still hums.
records.zomi: Ka pa in tu dong a hum lai radio pan itna la lui khat.

records.english: Which room was yours when you were a child?
records.zomi: Naupan lai-in bang inndei na' ahi hiam?

records.english: The small one at the back, next to the kitchen.
records.zomi: Nung lam-a neu pen, an huanna inn kiang ah.

records.english: Which bedroom will the baby sleep in?
records.zomi: Naungek bang inndei ah a ihmu ding hiam?

records.english: The small one next to ours, once we've painted it.
records.zomi: I' kiang-a neu pen, i zeek khit ciangin.

records.english: Which of you broke Grandpa's glasses?
records.zomi: Na lak uh ah kua in Pu' mitlimlang a sukkham hiam?

records.english: I did, by sitting on them, and I've already said sorry.
records.zomi: Kei, a tungah ka tu-in, maisak ka ngen khin hi.

records.english: Asking which memories someone treasures most is a gentle way to learn about their family.
records.zomi: Mi khat kiangah bang phawknate a manpha sak pen hiam dot pen a innkuan tungtang sin nading lampi nem khat ahi hi.

records.english: Which of our family stories will our grandchildren still be telling in fifty years?
records.zomi: I innkuan tangthute lak ah bang in kum sawmnga khit ciangin i tuute in a gen lai ding uh hiam?

records.english: Deciding which relatives to visit during a short holiday can cause more arguments than the holiday itself.
records.zomi: Tawlngakni tom khat sungin bang sanggamte veh ding hiam khen in tawlngakni mah sangin kinialna tam zaw a piangsak thei hi.

records.english: Which family photographs are kept and which are thrown away decides, in part, how a family remembers itself.
records.zomi: Bang innkuan limte kikem a, bang te kipaai hiam in innkuan khat amah le amah bangci-in a phawk hiam a khen khen khat hi.

records.english: Which present did you like best when you were small?
records.zomi: Na neu lai-in bang letsong na deih pen hiam?

records.english: A wooden truck that my grandfather made for me.
records.zomi: Ka pu in hong bawl sak sing mawtaw lian khat.

records.english: Children, which game shall we play when your cousins arrive?
records.zomi: Naupangte, na sanggamte a tun ciangin bang kimawlna i kimawl ding uh hiam?

records.english: Hide and seek in the garden!
records.zomi: Huan sungah kisel-kizon!

records.english: Which school did your parents go to?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa bang sang ah a kah uh hiam?

records.english: The same village school, though ten years apart.
records.zomi: Khua sang kibang, kum sawm kigamla hangin.

records.english: Which child takes after you the most?
records.zomi: Bang naupang in nang a zui pen hiam?

records.english: My second son, who is just as stubborn as I am.
records.zomi: Ka tapa nihna, kei bangin a lungtaang mah.

records.english: Which photo should we put on Grandma's birthday cake?
records.zomi: Pi' suahni cake tungah bang lim i koih ding hiam?

records.english: The one of her as a young teacher, standing outside the school.
records.zomi: Saya khangno a hih lai-a sang pua ah a ding lim.

records.english: Asking children which relative they feel closest to can tell parents a great deal about the family.
records.zomi: Naupangte kiangah bang sanggam tawh a kinai pen uh hiam dot in nu leh pate kiangah innkuan tungtang tampi a gen thei hi.

records.english: Which of the twins is older?
records.zomi: Apengte lak ah kua a upa zaw hiam?

records.english: Thomas, by about ten minutes, and he never lets his sister forget it.
records.zomi: Thomas, minit sawm bang, a sanggam numei a mangngilh sak ngei kei hi.

records.english: Which brother do you look most like?
records.zomi: Bang sanggam pasal tawh na kibang pen hiam?

records.english: The youngest, especially when we laugh.
records.zomi: A neu pen, a diak in i nuih ciangin.

records.english: Siblings often disagree about which of them was treated more strictly by their parents.
records.zomi: Sanggamte in a nu leh a pa uh in kua tungah a khauh zaw hiam a kikalh zel uh hi.

records.english: When I was twelve, my parents asked which country I would most like to visit.
records.zomi: Kum sawm leh nih ka cin ciangin ka nu leh ka pa in bang gam veh ka deih pen hiam hong dong uh hi.

records.english: I said Japan, because I had read so many stories about it.
records.zomi: Japan, tua tungtang tangthu tampi ka sim ahih manin, ka ci hi.

records.english: Ten years later, they surprised me with two tickets for my graduation.
records.zomi: Kum sawm khit ciangin ka sang zawhna adingin lai nih tawh hong lamdangsak uh hi.

records.english: Which relative taught you to sew?
records.zomi: Bang sanggam in puan khui hong sinsak hiam?

records.english: Aunt Cing, who still makes all her own clothes.
records.zomi: Ni Cing, amah' puan khempeuh amah mah in a khui lai pa.

records.english: Which day does your grandfather usually visit?
records.zomi: Na pu bang ni ciangin a hong veh zel hiam?

records.english: Every Wednesday, after the market.
records.zomi: Nilai ni simin, zuakna mun khit ciangin.

records.english: Asking an older relative which year something happened may produce a story instead of a date.
records.zomi: Sanggam upa khat kiangah bang kum in thu khat a piang hiam dot in kum sangin tangthu khat a hong suak thei hi.

records.english: Which of the two flats would be better for your mother?
records.zomi: Inn nih lak ah bang in na nu adingin a hoih zaw ding hiam?

records.english: The one on the ground floor, because she can't manage stairs any more.
records.zomi: Leitang kawm-a om pen, kahlei a kah zo nawn kei ahih manin.

records.english: Which of your grandmother's dishes do you miss most?
records.zomi: Na pi' an lak ah bang na phawk pen hiam?

records.english: Her pork with bamboo shoots, which nobody else can make the same way.
records.zomi: A vok sa mim tawh, kuamah in a kibang mah-in a bawl thei kei.

records.english: When grandparents are asked which grandchild visits most, the answer is often the one who lives nearest rather than the one who loves them most.
records.zomi: Pu leh pite kiangah bang tu in a hong veh tam pen hiam kidot ciangin a dawnna pen amaute a it pen hi lo-in a nai pen-a teeng pa ahi zel hi.

records.english: May I ask which of your relatives raised you?
records.zomi: Na sanggamte lak ah kua in hong khoi hiam ka dong thei ding hiam?

records.english: My grandmother, while my parents worked in the city.
records.zomi: Ka pi, ka nu leh ka pa khuapi ah nasep a sep lai-un.

records.english: When a family must decide which relative will care for an ageing parent, old tensions can come to the surface.
records.zomi: Innkuan khat in bang sanggam in a upa nu hiam pa kem ding hiam a khen kisam ciangin kinialna luite a pusuak thei hi.

records.english: When parents are asked which child is their favourite, most say they love them all differently.
records.zomi: Nu leh pate kiangah bang naupang a deih pen hiam kidot ciangin a tamzaw in khempeuh a kibang lo-in ka it hi, a ci uh hi.

records.english: Which language did your grandparents speak to each other?
records.zomi: Na pu leh na pi in bang pau tawh a kiho uh hiam?

records.english: Their own village language, and they switched to ours only when we children were listening.
records.zomi: Amau' khua pau, naupangte i ngaikhiat ciangin bek i pau ah a kheel uh hi.

records.english: Choosing which name to give a child can involve relatives from both sides of the family in long discussions.
records.zomi: Naupang khat adingin bang min piak ding hiam teel in innkuan lam nih pan sanggamte kikupna sau ah a kihelsak thei hi.

records.english: Which house in the village did your family live in before the move?
records.zomi: Na innkuan tai ma-in khua ah bang inn ah a teeng uh hiam?

records.english: Which side of the family are you closer to?
records.zomi: Innkuan bang lam tawh na kinai zaw hiam?

records.english: My mother's side, because we spent every holiday with them.
records.zomi: Ka nu lam, tawlngakni khempeuh amaute tawh i zat ahih manin.

records.english: Each generation must decide which old family customs to keep and which to let fade.
records.zomi: Khangthak khatciat in innkuan ngeina lui bang te kem ding hiam, bang te a mang sak ding hiam a khen kisam hi.

records.english: Which cousins are coming to the wedding?
records.zomi: Bang sanggamte mopawi ah a hong ding uh hiam?

records.english: All of them except the two who live abroad.
records.zomi: Gamdang ah a teeng nih simloh a khempeuh.

records.english: Which of your parents do you call when something goes wrong?
records.zomi: Bangmah a khial ciangin na nu leh na pa lak ah kua na sam hiam?

records.english: My father, because he never panics.
records.zomi: Ka pa, a lau ngal ngei lo ahih manin.

records.english: It is important for the school to know if a child takes medicine every day.
records.zomi: Naupang khat ni simin zatui a ne leh sang in a theih a thupi hi.

records.english: Sometimes the most useful conversation between a teacher and a family happens at the school gate.
records.zomi: Pawl khat ciangin saya leh innkuan kikal-a kikupna phattuam pen sang kongpi ah a piang hi.

records.english: My mother speaks no English, so my older sister translates at every school meeting.
records.zomi: Ka nu in English a gen thei kei ahih manin ka u numei in sang kikhopna khempeuh ah a let hi.

records.english: Can we meet after work, since I can't leave the shop before five?
records.zomi: Nai nga ma-in dawl ka nusia thei kei ahih manin nasep khit ciangin i kimu thei ding hiam?

records.english: Have you shown Dad your drawing?
records.zomi: Pa kiangah na lim gelh na etsak khin hiam?

records.english: I told my teacher that my parents were divorcing, and she let me sit by the window when I needed quiet.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa a kikhen ding uh hi, ci-in ka saya kiangah ka gen a, daina ka kisam ciangin tukvuang kiang ah tu dingin hong phal hi.

records.english: A pupil may tell a teacher things they are too embarrassed to tell their parents.
records.zomi: Sangnaupang khat in a nu leh a pa kiangah gen dingin a zum thu te saya kiangah a gen thei hi.

records.english: May I bring my son to the meeting?
records.zomi: Ka tapa kikhopna ah ka paipih thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, it's better if he hears what we say.
records.zomi: Thei hi, i gen a zak leh a hoih zaw hi.

records.english: Tell your teacher if you need help with the reading.
records.zomi: Sim ah huhna na kisam leh na saya kiangah gen in.

records.english: Being honest with a teacher about problems at home is hard, but it often helps.
records.zomi: Inn-a buainate tungtang saya kiangah thuman pen a haksa a, ahi zongin a huh zel hi.

records.english: What did your teacher write on your report?
records.zomi: Na saya in na report tungah bang a gelh hiam?

records.english: Messages between teachers and families should be short, clear and kind.
records.zomi: Sayate leh innkuante kikal-a thu khakte a tom, a kician leh a nem ding hi.

records.english: Should teachers be allowed to send messages to parents late in the evening?
records.zomi: Sayate in nitak sawt ciangin nu leh pate kiangah thu khak dingin kiphal ding uh hiam?

records.english: Who will collect your little sister if your mother is late?
records.zomi: Na nu a nunung leh na nau numei kua in a la ding hiam?

records.english: The teacher phoned my father to say how well I had done in the science fair.
records.zomi: Saya in science fair ah bangzah hoih takin ka bawl hiam gen dingin ka pa a sam hi.

records.english: When teachers and parents share what they notice, a child's difficulties are often spotted much sooner.
records.zomi: Sayate leh nu leh pate in a phawk uh a kihawm ciangin naupang khat' haksatnate a ngal zaw-in kimu zel hi.

records.english: Our teacher said, "Your parents should be proud of how hard you worked this year."
records.zomi: I saya in, "Kum in na hanciam dan uh adingin na nu leh na pa uh a kisaktheih ding uh hi" a ci hi.

records.english: A parent's quiet word with a teacher can sometimes solve a problem faster than a formal complaint.
records.zomi: Nu hiam pa khat' saya tawh dai taka kammal khat in phunna kician sangin buaina manlang zaw-in a vai a hawm thei hi.

records.english: Our teacher asked each of us to bring a photo of our family for the classroom wall.
records.zomi: I saya in i khatciat kiangah class bang adingin i innkuan lim khat tawi dingin hong ngen hi.

records.english: When a family speaks another language at home, the school may need an interpreter for meetings.
records.zomi: Innkuan khat in inn ah pau dang a zat ciangin sang in kikhopna adingin pau letmi khat a kisam kha thei hi.

records.english: The teacher made a short list of words for us to practise at home with our parents.
records.zomi: Saya in inn ah i nu leh i pa tawh i kisin nading kammal list tom khat a bawl hi.

records.english: Parents should feel that they can ask a teacher a question without being judged.
records.zomi: Nu leh pate in kithukhen lo-in saya kiangah dotna a dong thei uh hi, ci-in a kisa ding uh hi.

records.english: My son's teacher made him explain the problem to me himself, which taught him a lot.
records.zomi: Ka tapa' saya in buaina keimah kiangah amah mah in genteh dingin a sawl a, tua in tampi a sinsak hi.

records.english: Could you tell my daughter's teacher that she was ill on Monday?
records.zomi: Ka tanu Pizing ni ciangin a damlo hi, ci-in a saya kiangah na gen thei ding hiam?

records.english: Families who cannot read the school's letters may miss important information, so some schools explain them by phone.
records.zomi: Sang' laite a sim thei lo innkuante in thu thupi a pelh kha thei uh ahih manin sang pawl khat in phone tawh a genteh uh hi.

records.english: Everyone, remember to give your parents the letter about the school photos.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, sang lim tungtang lai na nu leh na pa kiangah pia ding phawk un.

records.english: The school asked every family to fill in a form about how the children get home.
records.zomi: Sang in innkuan khempeuh kiangah naupangte bangci-in inn ah a ciah uh hiam tungtang form khat dimsak dingin a ngen hi.

records.english: My father wrote a note to the teacher to explain why my homework was late.
records.zomi: Ka pa in bang hangin ka inn sinna a nunung hiam genteh dingin saya kiangah lai neu khat a gelh hi.

records.english: Did the teacher say anything about my handwriting?
records.zomi: Saya in ka laigelh dan tungtang bangmah a gen hiam?

records.english: She said it's much neater than last term.
records.zomi: Sang hun nunung sangin a siang zaw mahmah hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Students, take this letter home and show it to your parents tonight.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte, hih lai inn ah tawi unla, tu zan-in na nu leh na pa kiangah etsak un.

records.english: Do you speak to your parents about what happens at school?
records.zomi: Sang ah bang a piang hiam na nu leh na pa kiangah na gen zel hiam?

records.english: A teacher who knows a pupil's family situation can be more patient on difficult days.
records.zomi: Sangnaupang khat' innkuan dinmun a thei saya khat in ni haksate ah thuakzawhna tam zaw a nei thei hi.

records.english: Can you come to school a little early tomorrow, so that we can talk?
records.zomi: I kikup theih nadingin zingciang sang ah tawmno a ngal-in na hong thei ding hiam?

records.english: My aunt teaches at my school, so I have to call her "Miss" in class and "Auntie" at home.
records.zomi: Ka ni in ka sang ah a sinsak ahih manin class sungah "Miss" leh inn ah "Ni" ka sam kisam hi.

records.english: The teacher was given a list of every child's allergies by the parents.
records.zomi: Nu leh pate in naupang khempeuh' allergy list khat saya kiangah a pia uh hi.

records.english: How is my son getting on in class?
records.zomi: Ka tapa class sungah bangci-in a pai hiam?

records.english: Very well, though he could speak up a little more.
records.zomi: Hoih mahmah hi, ging zaw tawmno-in gen thei zaw ding hangin.

records.english: Teachers who send home good news, not only problems, often find that parents trust them more.
records.zomi: Buaina bek hi lo-in thu hoih zong inn ah a khak sayate in nu leh pate in a muang zaw uh hi, ci-in a mu zel uh hi.

records.english: I'm sorry I missed the parents' evening, but could we speak by phone this week?
records.zomi: Nu leh pate nitak kikhopna ka pelh ahih manin maisak in, ahi zongin hih kal phone tawh i kiho thei ding hiam?

records.english: My uncle, who is a teacher, gave me advice about how to talk to my own teacher.
records.zomi: Saya ahi ka pa neu in keimah' saya tawh bangci-in kiho ding hiam thuhilhna hong pia hi.

records.english: The teacher sent the forms home with the children so that every family received them.
records.zomi: Innkuan khempeuh in a ngah theih nadingun saya in form te naupangte tawh inn ah a khak hi.

records.english: At our school, parents mustn't go into the classrooms during lessons, but they may wait in the hall.
records.zomi: I sang ah sinna hun sungin nu leh pate sangnaupang inndei sungah a lut thei kei uh a, ahi zongin inn lian ah a ngak thei uh hi.

records.english: I do want my parents to meet my new teacher.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in ka saya thak a kimuh nadingun ka deih taktak hi.

records.english: A home visit from a teacher can show the teacher a side of the pupil never seen at school.
records.zomi: Saya khat' inn vehna in sangnaupang' sang ah kimu ngei lo lam khat saya kiangah a lak thei hi.

records.english: Please let me know if anything at home is making it hard for him to concentrate.
records.zomi: Inn ah bangmah in a lungsim koih a haksasak leh hong theisak in.

records.english: Teachers sometimes have to give parents news that they don't want to hear, such as a child falling behind.
records.zomi: Sayate in nu leh pate kiangah a zak nop loh thu, naupang khat a nunung bang, a gen kisam zel uh hi.

records.english: The school uses a messaging app to tell parents about homework and trips.
records.zomi: Sang in nu leh pate kiangah inn sinna leh khualzinnate tungtang gen dingin messaging app khat a zang hi.

records.english: Why didn't you tell me the school had phoned?
records.zomi: Bang hangin sang in hong sam hi, ci hong gen lo na hi hiam?

records.english: My mother asked the teacher how I was doing in maths, and I waited outside the classroom, very nervous.
records.zomi: Ka nu in maths ah bangci-in ka pai hiam saya a dong a, kei sangnaupang inndei pua ah lau mahmah-in ka ngak hi.

records.english: My grandmother came to the parents' evening, because my parents were both working.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa a nih in nasep a sep uh ahih manin ka pi nu leh pate nitak kikhopna ah a hong hi.

records.english: Our teacher sent a short message to every family after the school trip.
records.zomi: I saya in sang khualzinna khit ciangin innkuan khempeuh kiangah thu khak tom khat a khak hi.

records.english: Some parents left school early themselves, so meetings with teachers can make them nervous.
records.zomi: Nu leh pa pawl khat amau mah zong sang a nusia ngal uh ahih manin sayate tawh kikhopna in a lausak thei hi.

records.english: Please don't send your child to school with a fever.
records.zomi: Na naupang lum natna tawh sang ah sawl kei in.

records.english: My teacher knows my grandfather, because he taught her when she was a girl.
records.zomi: Ka saya in ka pu a thei hi, numei naupang a hih lai-in ka pu in a sinsak ahih manin.

records.english: When parents and teachers disagree about a child, the child can feel caught in the middle.
records.zomi: Nu leh pate leh sayate naupang khat tungtang a kikalh ciangin naupang in laizang ah a kikhum bangin a kisa thei hi.

records.english: Last term, my daughter stopped wanting to go to school.
records.zomi: Sang hun nunung in ka tanu in sang kah a deih nawn kei hi.

records.english: Her teacher noticed that she was always alone at break and asked us to come in.
records.zomi: A saya in tawldam hun ciangin a kia-in a om den hi, ci-in a phawk a, hong pai dingin hong ngen hi.

records.english: Together we found out that a new girl had been unkind to her, and the problem was sorted out within a week.
records.zomi: A khawm-in numei naupang thak khat in a hoih lo-in a bawl hi, ci i thei uh a, kal khat sungin buaina kibawlsiang hi.

records.english: Missing an appointment at a government office can mean waiting several weeks for another one.
records.zomi: Kumpi office-a kimuhna khat pelh in a dang khat adingin kal tampi ngak cihna hi thei hi.

records.english: What should I bring to the registry office?
records.zomi: Ciamtehna office ah bang ka tawi ding hiam?

records.english: Your identity card, the birth certificate and a copy of each.
records.zomi: Na ID card, pianna lai leh khatciat' copy.

records.english: My cousin missed her appointment because the bus never came.
records.zomi: Bus a hong ngei loh manin ka sanggam numei in a kimuhna a pelh hi.

records.english: Every document was checked twice before the officer stamped the form.
records.zomi: Office nasempa in form ah ciamtehna a khet ma-in lai khempeuh vei nih kien hi.

records.english: Can I bring my brother to translate for me?
records.zomi: Hong let sak dingin ka sanggam pasal ka paipih thei ding hiam?

records.english: Where do I wait for my number to be called?
records.zomi: Ka nambat kisam ding koi ah ka ngak ding hiam?

records.english: Appointments that run late are less stressful when someone tells the people waiting what is happening.
records.zomi: A nunung kimuhnate in ngakmite kiangah bang a piang hiam kuamah in a gen ciangin a lungkhamhuai tawm zaw hi.

records.english: The appointment took only ten minutes, but the journey there took two hours.
records.zomi: Kimuhna in minit sawm bek a la a, ahi zongin tua lai dong khualzinna in nai nih a la hi.

records.english: Our appointment was confirmed by email within a few minutes.
records.zomi: I kimuhna minit tawmno sungin email tawh kiciamteh hi.

records.english: An official letter confirming the time, the office and the documents needed prevents many wasted trips.
records.zomi: Hun, office leh lai kisamte ciamteh kumpi lai khat in mawk pai tampi a kem hi.

records.english: The housing office only sees people by appointment on Mondays.
records.zomi: Inn office in Pizing ni ciangin kimuhna tawh bek mite a mu hi.

records.english: Clear signs at the entrance help people find the right counter without asking.
records.zomi: Lutna-a ciamtehna kiciang te in mite dot lo-in counter dik a muh nadingun a huh hi.

records.english: Some offices keep a few walk-in places each day for people who cannot book online.
records.zomi: Office pawl khat in online-a kilai thei lo mite adingin ni simin a lut thei mun tawmno a kem hi.

records.english: A missed appointment is sometimes the office's fault, as when a letter is sent to an old address.
records.zomi: Kimuhna kipelh khat pen pawl khat ciangin office' khialhna ahi a, lai khat teenna mun lui ah a kikhak bang.

records.english: Using the office's website, my son booked appointments for the whole family in one evening.
records.zomi: Office' website zang-in ka tapa in nitak khat sungin innkuan bup adingin kimuhnate a kilai hi.

records.english: Do I need an appointment to register my new address?
records.zomi: Ka teenna mun thak ciamteh dingin kimuhna ka kisam ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, but you can book one online the same week.
records.zomi: Kisam hi, ahi zongin kal kibang ah online-in na kilai thei hi.

records.english: When my number was called, I realized I had left the form on the bus.
records.zomi: Ka nambat a kisam ciangin form bus tungah ka nusia hi, ci ka phawk hi.

records.english: Please switch off your phone in the interview room.
records.zomi: Kidotna inndei sungah na phone sumit in.

records.english: Officials who explain clearly what will happen at an appointment make people far less anxious.
records.zomi: Kimuhna ah bang a piang ding hiam kician takin a genteh kumpi nasemte in mite' lungkhamna a neusak mahmah hi.

records.english: Online booking forms are often available only in one language, which can be a barrier for newcomers.
records.zomi: Online kilaina form te pau khat bek ah a om zel ahih manin mi thakte adingin khaamna hi thei hi.

records.english: Thank you for staying open a little late for me.
records.zomi: Kei adingin tawmno sawt zaw-in na hon manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: When public offices cut staff, the first sign is often a longer wait for appointments.
records.zomi: Mipi office te in nasemte a neusak ciangin a lak masa pen pen kimuhna ngak sau zaw ahi zel hi.

records.english: Sorry, I'm late; the bus stopped at every village.
records.zomi: Ka hong nunung ahih manin maisak in; bus in khua khempeuh ah a khawl hi.

records.english: My appointment was moved to the afternoon because the system was down.
records.zomi: System a siat ahih manin ka kimuhna sun nung lam ah kisawn hi.

records.english: When an office closes without warning, people who travelled from far away lose a whole day's pay.
records.zomi: Office khat phawksak lo-in a kikhak ciangin gamla pan a hong mite in ni khat sum ngah a mansuah uh hi.

records.english: Keeping copies of every letter from an office can prove that you did your part.
records.zomi: Office khat pan lai khempeuh' copy kem in na khen na bawl hi, cih a lak thei hi.

records.english: Do I need to bring the original documents or are copies enough?
records.zomi: Lai taktakte ka tawi kisam ding hiam, copy te a tam hiam?

records.english: At our council office, if you arrive more than fifteen minutes late, you may be asked to book again.
records.zomi: I khuapi vaihawm office ah minit sawm leh nga sang a nunung na hih leh kilai kik dingin kingen kha thei hi.

records.english: Can I change my appointment if I'm working that day?
records.zomi: Tua ni-in nasep ka sep leh ka kimuhna ka kheel thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, as long as you tell us at least a day before.
records.zomi: Thei hi, ni khat ma-in tal hong gen leh.

records.english: Booking systems for public offices save waiting time, but they can shut out people who don't use the internet.
records.zomi: Mipi office-a kilaina system te in ngakna hun a khawl a, ahi zongin internet zang lo mite a khaam thei hi.

records.english: My father made me check the appointment letter three times before we left the house.
records.zomi: Inn pan i pai ma-un ka pa in kimuhna lai vei thum hong en sak hi.

records.english: Is there parking near the office?
records.zomi: Office kiang ah mawtaw khawlna om hiam?

records.english: Book the earliest slot, because the office is quieter in the morning.
records.zomi: A ngal pen hun kilai in, zingsang ciangin office a dai zaw ahih manin.

records.english: Could you book the appointment for my mother, since she doesn't use the internet?
records.zomi: Ka nu in internet a zang kei ahih manin amah adingin kimuhna na kilai sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Take a ticket from the machine and wait for your number.
records.zomi: Set pan lai neu khat la inla, na nambat ngak in.

records.english: I printed the confirmation in case my phone battery died.
records.zomi: Ka phone battery a bei kha leh ci-in ciamtehna ka print hi.

records.english: The clerk was helpful, but the queue moved very slowly.
records.zomi: Office nasempa a huh thei a, ahi zongin kingakna zawi mahmah-in a pai hi.

records.english: We were told to come back with a photocopy of the lease.
records.zomi: Inn luahna lai copy khat tawh hong kik dingin kihilh hi.

records.english: I've booked a slot at the tax office for nine on Tuesday.
records.zomi: Pithai ni nai kua ciangin siah office ah hun khat ka kilai khin hi.

records.english: Being turned away for one missing paper after a long wait is one of the most frustrating parts of dealing with offices.
records.zomi: Ngakna sau khit ciangin lai khat a kiat hang-a kinial pen office tawh kizopna sung-a lungkhamhuai pen khen khat ahi hi.

records.english: Appointments at the immigration office are booked weeks ahead, so plan early.
records.zomi: Gam lutna office-a kimuhnate kal tampi ma-in kilai ahih manin a ngal-in geel in.

records.english: The licence office sent me a text reminder the day before my appointment.
records.zomi: Phalna lai office in ka kimuhna ma-a ni khat ah text phawksakna hong khak hi.

records.english: The waiting room was so full that people stood in the corridor.
records.zomi: Ngakna inndei a dim lua ahih manin mite lampi ah a ding uh hi.

records.english: Which counter do I go to for the tax appointment?
records.zomi: Siah kimuhna adingin bang counter ah ka pai ding hiam?

records.english: At the passport office, you mustn't bring food or drink into the waiting area.
records.zomi: Passport office ah ngakna mun ah an hiam dawn ding na tawi thei kei hi.

records.english: I'm afraid we can't see you today without an appointment.
records.zomi: Kimuhna om lo-in tuni-in kong mu thei kei ding uh hi, ci ka lau hi.

records.english: Last month, I needed a new work permit.
records.zomi: Kha nunung in nasep phalna lai thak khat ka kisam hi.

records.english: The first available appointment was six weeks away, so I asked to be put on the cancellation list.
records.zomi: Kimuhna masa pen kal guk gamla ahih manin kikhak list ah koih dingin ka ngen hi.

records.english: Two days later, the office called, and I was seen that same afternoon.
records.zomi: Ni nih khit ciangin office in hong sam a, tua sun nung lam mah in hong mu uh hi.

records.english: Please arrive ten minutes before your slot so that the guard can check your bag.
records.zomi: Kem nasempa in na ip a en theih nadingin na hun ma-in minit sawm tung in.

records.english: My grandmother's appointment was arranged by the social worker, who also came with her.
records.zomi: Ka pi' kimuhna mipi huhna nasempa in a geel a, amah tawh zong a pai hi.

records.english: A short phone call to the office the day before can save a long journey for nothing.
records.zomi: A zan masa-in office kiangah phone tom khat in bangmah lo-a khualzinna sau khat a kem thei hi.

records.english: My uncle had his appointment moved because he couldn't get time off work.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu nasep pan tawlngak hun a ngah thei loh manin a kimuhna kisawn hi.

records.english: Write the reference number on your hand if you have no paper.
records.zomi: Lai na nei kei leh na khut tungah reference nambat gelh in.

records.english: The office opens at eight, but the queue starts forming at seven.
records.zomi: Office nai giat ciangin kihong a, ahi zongin kingakna nai sagih ciangin a kipan hi.

records.english: Should government offices offer evening appointments for people who work during the day?
records.zomi: Kumpi office te in sun lai nasep sem mite adingin nitak kimuhna a pia ding uh hiam?

records.english: The clerk said, "Come back on Thursday, and bring the signed form with you."
records.zomi: Office nasempa in, "Laizing ni ciangin hong kik inla, min kigelh form tawi in" a ci hi.

records.english: The librarian made me show my card before I could use the computers.
records.zomi: Laibu koihna kemtu in computer ka zat ma-in ka card hong etsak hi.

records.english: Thank you for keeping the newspaper for me.
records.zomi: Laithak hong kem sak na hih manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: Last winter, my son lost a library book on the bus.
records.zomi: Phalbi nunung in ka tapa in laibu koihna laibu khat bus tungah a mansuah hi.

records.english: We were sure we'd have to pay for it, so we went in to explain.
records.zomi: A man i pia kisam ding hi, ci i kithei kician uh ahih manin genteh dingin i lut uh hi.

records.english: The librarian smiled and told us that someone had already handed it in.
records.zomi: Laibu koihna kemtu in a nui a, kuamah in a pia kik khin hi, hong ci hi.

records.english: A librarian who knows the local community can point people to services they never knew existed.
records.zomi: Mun lai mipi a thei laibu koihna kemtu khat in mite a theih ngei loh nasepnate lam a lak thei hi.

records.english: Reading groups at the library give lonely people a regular reason to leave the house and talk to others.
records.zomi: Laibu koihna-a sinna pawlte in a kisuksi mite inn nusia-a mi dangte tawh kiho nading a hang ngeina khat a pia hi.

records.english: If the library doesn't have a book, it can usually borrow one from another library for you.
records.zomi: Laibu koihna in laibu khat a nei kei leh a tamzaw in laibu koihna dang pan na adingin a puk thei hi.

records.english: Don't eat in the computer room, please.
records.zomi: Computer inndei sungah an ne kei un, kong ngen hi.

records.english: The book I wanted was out, so I reserved it, and the library sent me a message when it came back.
records.zomi: Ka deih laibu kipuk khin ahih manin ka kilai a, a kik ciangin laibu koihna in thu hong khak hi.

records.english: My son's first library card made him feel very grown up.
records.zomi: Ka tapa' laibu koihna card masa in a picin bangin a kisaksak hi.

records.english: Using the library's catalogue on my phone, I can see whether a book is on the shelf before I walk there.
records.zomi: Ka phone tung-a laibu koihna' catalogue zang-in ka pai ma-in laibu van koihna tungah a om hiam ka en thei hi.

records.english: For people who cannot read small print or hold a heavy book, audiobooks from the library can be a lifeline.
records.zomi: Lai neu sim thei lo hiam laibu gik len thei lo mite adingin laibu koihna pan audiobook te nuntakna khauh khat hi thei hi.

records.english: Could you show me how to download e-books with my library card?
records.zomi: Ka laibu koihna card tawh e-book download dan hong lak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: My library card was replaced for free after the old one cracked.
records.zomi: A lui a keh khit ciangin ka laibu koihna card man om lo-in kikheel hi.

records.english: The children's corner has small chairs, picture books and a box of puppets.
records.zomi: Naupangte' kil ah tutphah neute, lim laibute leh kimawlna milim bawm khat a om hi.

records.english: Everyone, please return the study room keys to the desk before you leave.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, na pai ma-un sinna inndei tawhte dawhkan ah pia kik un.

records.english: How do I find out whether a book has been reserved by someone else?
records.zomi: Laibu khat mi dang in a kilai khin hiam bangci-in ka thei thei ding hiam?

records.english: Many libraries now lend things other than books, such as tools, games and even musical instruments.
records.zomi: Laibu koihna tampi in tu-in laibu bek hi lo-in vanzat, kimawlna leh la tumna vante zong a puksak uh hi.

records.english: The librarian helped my mother find old newspapers from the year she arrived in the country.
