records.zomi: Laibu koihna kemtu in ka nu gam a tun kum-a laithak luite zong dingin a huh hi.

records.english: I'd like to join the library, please.
records.zomi: Laibu koihna ah ka kihel nuam hi.

records.english: My grandfather reads large-print books now that his eyes are weaker.
records.zomi: Ka pu' mit a hatlo khit pan lai lian laibu te a sim hi.

records.english: A public library is one of the few places where anyone can stay for hours without being expected to buy anything.
records.zomi: Mipi laibu koihna pen kua peuh in bangmah lei dingin kilamen lo-in nai tampi a om theihna mun tawmno lak-a khat ahi hi.

records.english: The library's exhibition of old photographs made many older residents cry with recognition.
records.zomi: Laibu koihna-a lim lui kilakna in teeng upa tampi a theih uh ahih manin a kapsak hi.

records.english: When a library closes, the people who lose most are often those with the fewest other options.
records.zomi: Laibu koihna khat a kikhak ciangin a mansuah pen mite pen teelna dang a tawm pen mite ahi zel uh hi.

records.english: Libraries give people without a computer at home a fair chance to apply for jobs and fill in official forms.
records.zomi: Laibu koihnate in inn ah computer nei lo mite nasep ngen leh kumpi form dimsak nading hun dik a pia hi.

records.english: Our library had its entrance rebuilt with a ramp, so that wheelchair users no longer need help at the steps.
records.zomi: I laibu koihna in a lutna kahtouna tawh a lam kik sak a, tutna leng zangte in kahlei ah huhna kisam nawn lo hi.

records.english: You can renew your books online or by phone if you need them for longer.
records.zomi: Sawt zaw-in na kisam leh online-in hiam phone tawh hiam na laibute na sawnsak thei hi.

records.english: Can I use the photocopier?
records.zomi: Photocopier ka zang thei ding hiam?

records.english: Shall we take the children to the library on Saturday?
records.zomi: Kiginni ciangin naupangte laibu koihna ah i paipih ding hiam?

records.english: Is there a charge for printing?
records.zomi: Print adingin man om hiam?

records.english: Volunteers deliver library books to older people who can no longer leave their homes.
records.zomi: Thalawpte in inn nusia thei nawn lo mi upate kiangah laibu koihna laibute a tawi uh hi.

records.english: What do I need to get a library card?
records.zomi: Laibu koihna card ngah dingin bang ka kisam hiam?

records.english: Just something with your name and address on it, such as a bill.
records.zomi: Na min leh na teenna mun a om bangmah khat, laimal bang.

records.english: Is the library open on Sunday afternoons?
records.zomi: Nipini sun nung lam ciangin laibu koihna a kihong hiam?

records.english: When a book comes back damaged, the library may ask the borrower to pay for a replacement.
records.zomi: Laibu khat a siat-in a kik ciangin laibu koihna in a pukpa kiangah a laih man piak dingin a ngen thei hi.

records.english: Some libraries open late one evening a week for people who work during the day.
records.zomi: Laibu koihna pawl khat in sun lai-a nasem mite adingin kal khat ah nitak khat sawt zaw-in a kihong hi.

records.english: Could you help me find a book about bees for my daughter?
records.zomi: Ka tanu adingin khuai tungtang laibu khat zong dingin hong huh thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Many libraries forgive late fines for children, so that they are not afraid to come back.
records.zomi: Laibu koihna tampi in naupangte' nunung man a maisak uh hi, a kik ding a lau lo nadingun.

records.zomi: Sangnaupangte, tawlngakni khualzinna na kilai ma-un na visa ni te en un.

records.english: My visa was sent back to me by post, inside my passport.

records.english: How long is my visa valid for?
records.zomi: Ka visa bangzah sawt a zat theih hiam?

records.english: Ninety days from the date you enter the country.

records.english: Is a visa needed for a stopover of just a few hours?
records.zomi: Nai tawmno bek khawlna adingin visa kisam hiam?

records.english: Could you check my visa form before I send it?
records.zomi: Ka khak ma-in ka visa form hong en sak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: A residence permit allows a person to live in a country for a longer period, often with the right to work.
records.zomi: Teenna phalna lai in mi khat gam khat ah hun sawt zaw a teen nadingin a phal a, a tamzaw in nasep sep theihna tawh.

records.english: Citizens of some countries can travel to others without a visa, but only for a limited time.
records.zomi: Gam pawl khat-a gam mite visa om lo-in gam dangte ah khualzin thei uh a, ahi zongin hun kician sung bek.

records.english: Being refused a visa is disappointing, but a clear reason makes it easier to apply successfully next time.

records.english: A family visa may allow a husband, wife or child to join a relative who already lives in the country.

records.english: My friend waited six weeks for her student visa.
records.zomi: Ka lawm in a sangnaupang visa adingin kal guk a ngak hi.

records.english: The terms on a visa, such as the dates and the number of entries, are legally binding, so it is worth reading them carefully.
records.zomi: Ni leh lut zah bang visa tung-a thukhamte thukham tawh kikhih ahih manin limtakin sim a phu hi.

records.english: Keep a copy of your visa in a separate bag in case your passport is lost.
records.zomi: Na passport a mang leh ci-in na visa copy khat ip tuam sungah kem in.

records.english: A visa does not always guarantee entry, because border officers may still ask questions on arrival.
records.zomi: Visa in lut theihna a kiciamsak tawntung kei hi, gamgi kem nasemte in na tun ciangin dotna a dong lai thei uh ahih manin.

records.english: We had to pay the visa fee in cash at the embassy.

records.english: Sorry, but your visa has expired, so you can't board this flight.

records.english: Bring your passport, two photos and the printed form to the appointment.
records.zomi: Kimuhna ah na passport, lim nih leh kikhet form tawi in.

records.english: The visa officer asked why I wanted to visit and where I would stay.

records.english: The interview at the consulate lasted only five minutes.

records.english: A sponsor is a person or organization that promises to support an applicant during their stay.
records.zomi: Sponsor pen ngetpa a om laitakin huh dingin a kiciam mi hiam pawl khat ahi hi.

records.english: Visa fees are sometimes higher for longer stays or for faster processing.

records.english: My cousin had her documents translated and certified before she applied for a work visa.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam numei in nasep visa a ngen ma-in a laite a let sak a, a ciamteh sak hi.

records.english: My brother applied to extend his visa before it ran out.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in a visa a bei ma-in sawnsak dingin a ngen hi.

records.english: Is my visa still valid if I get a new passport?
records.zomi: Passport thak ka ngah leh ka visa a zat theih lai hiam?

records.english: Usually, you'll need to carry both the old and the new passport.
records.zomi: A tamzaw ah passport lui leh thak a nih na pua kisam ding hi.

records.english: Where do I apply for a visa?

records.zomi: Na veh nop gam' embassy hiam visa center ah.

records.english: What kind of visa do I need to study abroad?
records.zomi: Gamdang ah sin dingin bang visa ka kisam hiam?

records.english: A student visa, which you apply for after the university accepts you.
records.zomi: Sangnaupang visa, sangpi in hong pom khit ciangin na ngen ding.

records.english: On a tourist visa, you usually aren't allowed to work, even for a few days.
records.zomi: Khualzin visa tawh ni tawmno zong nasep sem dingin a tamzaw kiphal lo hi.

records.english: Visa rules differ greatly between countries, so travellers should always check the official government website before booking.
records.zomi: Visa thukhamte gam tuamtuam ah a kibang lo mahmah ahih manin khualzinte in a kilai ma-un kumpi website taktak a en tawntung ding uh hi.

records.english: Can I work while my visa extension is being processed?
records.zomi: Ka visa sawnsakna a kibawl laitakin nasep ka sem thei ding hiam?

records.english: In some countries, a work visa depends on having a job offer from an employer who agrees to act as a sponsor.
records.zomi: Gam pawl khat ah nasep visa pen sponsor bangin pang dingin a kiciam nasep piaktu pan nasep ngetna neih tungah a kinga hi.

records.english: My visa application was refused, but the letter explained that I could appeal.
records.zomi: Ka visa ngetna kinial a, ahi zongin lai in ngen kik thei hi, ci-in a genteh hi.

records.english: How long does it take to get a visa?

records.english: It depends on the country, but it can take anything from a few days to several months.
records.zomi: Gam tungah a kinga a, ahi zongin ni tawmno pan kha tampi dong a la thei hi.

records.english: A tourist visa usually lets you visit a country but not work there.
records.zomi: Khualzin visa in a tamzaw-in gam khat veh dingin a phal a, ahi zongin tua ah nasep sem dingin a phal kei hi.

records.english: I had to show proof that I could support myself during my stay.
records.zomi: Ka om laitakin keimah le keimah ka kivak zo hi, cih lakna ka lak kisam hi.

records.english: Is this a single-entry or a multiple-entry visa?
records.zomi: Hih pen khatvei lut visa ahi hiam, vei tampi lut visa ahi hiam?

records.english: Overstaying a visa, even by a few days, can make it much harder to visit that country again.
records.zomi: Visa sangin, ni tawmno zong, sawt zaw-in om in tua gam veh kik a haksa zaw mahmah sak thei hi.

records.english: An immigration adviser can explain which type of visa fits a person's situation.
records.zomi: Gam lutna thuhilhpa khat in mi khat' dinmun tawh bang visa a kituak hiam a genteh thei hi.

records.english: Some visas are tied to a single employer, so changing jobs may mean applying again.
records.zomi: Visa pawl khat nasep piaktu khat bek tawh kikhih ahih manin nasep kheel in ngen kik cihna hi thei hi.

records.english: My parents' visitor visas were approved just in time for our wedding.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa' veh visa i mopawi adingin hun takin a kipom hi.

records.english: What does the date on the visa sticker mean?

records.english: It's the last day you can enter the country, not the last day you can stay.
records.zomi: Gam na lut theih ni nunung pen ahi a, na om theih ni nunung hi lo hi.

records.english: The difference between a visa and a residence permit is often confusing for people applying for the first time.
records.zomi: Visa leh teenna phalna lai kibatlohna in a masa pen-a a ngen mite adingin a buaihuai zel hi.

records.english: A transit visa allows travellers to pass through a country on the way to somewhere else, usually without leaving the airport area.
records.zomi: Kantan visa khat in khualzinte mun dang lam ah gam khat kantan dingin a phal a, a tamzaw vanlengtual mun nusia lo-in.

records.english: In many cases, a sponsor has to show that they can support the visitor financially.

records.english: My uncle's residence permit has to be renewed every two years.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu' teenna phalna lai kum nih simin kithak kisam hi.

records.english: Long-term visas often require a medical check before they are issued.
records.zomi: Hun sawt visa te kipiak ma-in damna sitna a kisam zel hi.

records.english: The officer stamped my passport with the date of entry.
records.zomi: Office nasempa in ka passport tungah lutna ni tawh ciamtehna a khet hi.

records.english: My visa expires at the end of March.
records.zomi: March kha tawp ciangin ka visa a bei ding hi.

records.english: Do children need their own visas?
records.zomi: Naupangte in amau' visa a kisam uh hiam?

records.english: The visa centre made me book an appointment online before I could hand in my passport.
records.zomi: Ka passport ka piak theih ma-in visa center in online-in kimuhna kilai dingin hong sawl hi.

records.english: The embassy asked for my fingerprints and a photo.
records.zomi: Embassy in ka khutzung lim leh lim khat a ngen hi.

records.english: Tourists are often asked to show a return ticket before their visa is approved.
records.zomi: Khualzinte a visa uh a kipom ma-in a kik nading lai a lak kisam zel uh hi.

records.english: When rules change suddenly, families waiting for visas can be separated for months.
records.zomi: Thukhamte thakhatin a kikheel ciangin visa a ngak innkuante kha tampi kikhen thei uh hi.

records.english: My sister's student visa allows her to work a few hours a week during term.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam numei' sangnaupang visa in sang hun sungin kal khat ah nai tawmno nasep sem dingin a phal hi.

records.english: Should visas for students be easier to get than visas for workers?
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte adingin visa pen nasemte adingin visa sangin ngah a baih zaw ding hiam?

records.english: A shopkeeper usually gives clearer directions than a passer-by in a hurry.
records.zomi: Dawl neipa khat in manlang taka kantan pa khat sangin lampi kician zaw a gen zel hi.

records.english: My father always takes the same route, even when there's a shorter one.
records.zomi: Ka pa in lampi tom zaw khat a om zongin lampi kibang mah a zang tawntung hi.

records.english: A well-chosen landmark can make a route easier to remember than any number of turns.
records.zomi: Hoih taka kiteel mun theih nading khat in kawi bangzah zong sangin lampi khat phawk a baih zawsak thei hi.

records.english: The best route for a delivery van may be very different from the best route for a family on bicycles.
records.zomi: Van tun mawtaw adingin lampi hoih pen siiksakol tuang innkuan adingin lampi hoih pen tawh a kibang lo mahmah thei hi.

records.english: The quickest route on a map is not always the easiest one to follow, especially in a town you don't know.
records.zomi: Map tung-a lampi manlang pen na theih loh khuapi khat ah a diak in zui a baih pen a hi tawntung kei hi.

records.english: Some people understand a quick sketch far better than a list of written directions.
records.zomi: Mi pawl khat in lim manlang khat kigelh lampi hilhna list sangin a thei zaw uh hi.

records.english: We went the way the farmer suggested, and it saved us nearly an hour.
records.zomi: Lo neipa' hilh lampi i zui uh a, hun khat dek hong khawlsak hi.

records.english: Shall I drive, or would you rather we took the train?
records.zomi: Kei in mawtaw ka mawng ding hiam, meileng i tuang na deih zaw hiam?

records.english: Let's take the train, so we can both read on the way.
records.zomi: Meileng tuang ni, lampi ah i nih in i sim theih nadingin.

records.english: Is it better to leave the motorway at the first exit or the second?
records.zomi: Mawtaw lampi lian pen pusuakna masa ah nusia a hoih zaw hiam, nihna ah hiam?

records.english: The toll road is faster, but the old road is free and much prettier.
records.zomi: Man piak lampi a manlang zaw a, ahi zongin lampi lui man om lo a, a kilawm zaw mahmah hi.

records.english: A paper map never runs out of battery, but a phone can tell you when a road is closed.
records.zomi: Lai map in battery a bei ngei kei a, ahi zongin phone in lampi khat a kikhak ciangin hong gen thei hi.

records.english: Which is easier for your parents, a route with one change or a longer bus with none?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa adingin bang in a baih zaw hiam, vei khat kikheelna nei lampi hiam, kikheelna om lo bus sau zaw hiam?

records.english: I'd sooner go the long way round than try to drive through the market on a Saturday morning, when the stalls block half the street.

records.english: A route that is easy by car can be confusing on foot, because the signs are written for drivers.
records.zomi: Mawtaw tawh a baih lampi khat pai-in a buaihuai thei hi, ciamtehnate mawngmite adingin kigelh ahih manin.

records.english: My mother made us take the longer road, because she didn't trust the old bridge.
records.zomi: Lei lui a muang lo ahih manin ka nu in lampi sau zaw hong zuisak hi.

records.english: Driving in the city centre saves walking, but finding a parking space can take longer than the journey.
records.zomi: Khuapi lailung ah mawtaw mawng in kal a khol a, ahi zongin mawtaw koihna mun zon in khualzinna sangin hun sawt zaw a la thei hi.

records.english: Would you rather walk through the park or along the main road?
records.zomi: Huan sung tawng-in na pai nuam zaw hiam, lampi lian kiangah hiam?

records.english: Through the park, because it's quieter.
records.zomi: Huan sung tawng-in, a dai zaw ahih manin.

records.english: Is it quicker to take the ferry or to drive round by the bridge?
records.zomi: Tembaw tuang a manlang zaw hiam, lei lam ah mawtaw tawh kikhum-a mawng a manlang zaw hiam?

records.english: The ferry, unless you miss it, because the next one is an hour later.
records.zomi: Tembaw, na ma-in a pai khit kei leh; a zom pen nai khat khit ciangin a pai ding ahih manin.

records.english: When there are two equally good routes, people tend to choose the one they already know.

records.english: For a first visit, it may be wiser to choose the simpler route and learn the shortcuts later.
records.zomi: A veh masa pen ciangin lampi baih zaw teel-in a nung ciangin lampi tomte sin a pil zaw kha ding hi.

records.english: Is the path by the lake quicker than the road?
records.zomi: Dil gei lampi in lampi lian sangin a manlang zaw hiam?

records.english: Taking a taxi from the station is easier the first time, and next time you can try the bus.
records.zomi: A masa pen ciangin dinna pan taxi tuang a baih zaw a, a zom vei ciangin bus na tuang sin thei hi.

records.english: Should we follow the signs or trust the app?
records.zomi: Ciamtehnate i zui ding hiam, app i muang ding hiam?

records.english: The signs, because the app sent us into a field last time.
records.zomi: Ciamtehnate, a vei nunung in app in lo sungah hong paisak ahih manin.

records.english: Choosing the way by the river added ten minutes, but nobody minded, because the evening was so beautiful.
records.zomi: Lui gei lampi teel in minit sawm a behlap a, ahi zongin nitak a kilawm mahmah ahih manin kuamah lungkham lo uh hi.

records.english: Cycling along the canal takes longer than the road, but it's much safer for children.
records.zomi: Tuiluang gei-a siiksakol tuang in lampi lian sangin hun a la zaw a, ahi zongin naupangte adingin a bitzaw mahmah hi.

records.english: We chose the mountain road, which was slower but far less crowded.
records.zomi: Mual lampi i teel uh a, a nuam zaw a, ahi zongin mi a tam lo mahmah hi.

records.english: Choosing a route for a group means thinking about the slowest walker, not the fastest.
records.zomi: Mi pawl khat adingin lampi teel in a kal manlang pen hi lo-in a kal nuam pen ngaihsut cihna hi.

records.english: We'd rather arrive late by the safe road than early by the dangerous one.
records.zomi: Lampi lauhuai tungtawnin a hun ma-a tung sangin lampi bitzaw tungtawnin a hun nung-a tung i deih zaw uh hi.

records.english: The bridge route is longer, but it avoids the hill, which is hard for my grandmother.
records.zomi: Lei lampi a sau zaw a, ahi zongin ka pi adingin a haksa mual a pelh hi.

records.english: The night bus is slower than a taxi, but it stops right outside our door.
records.zomi: Zan bus in taxi sangin a nuam zaw a, ahi zongin i inn kongkhak mai taktak ah a khawl hi.

records.english: The longer route was chosen for the school trip because it had safer crossings.
records.zomi: Sang khualzinna adingin lampi kantan munte a bitzaw ahih manin lampi sau zaw kiteel hi.

records.english: Do you prefer someone to explain the way or to walk you there?
records.zomi: Mi khat in lampi hong gen sak na deih zaw hiam, tua dong hong paipih na deih zaw hiam?

records.english: Which way would you go if the main road were closed?

records.english: Following the river is longer, but you can't get lost, because it leads straight to the town.

records.english: Choosing between a short, confusing route and a longer, simpler one often depends on how tired you are.
records.zomi: Lampi tom buaihuai leh lampi sau baih kikal-a teel in a tamzaw-in na gim dan tungah a kinga hi.

records.english: The quickest way to the beach is through the town, but the prettiest is along the cliffs.

records.english: If you're carrying heavy bags, the bus is worth it, even for two stops.
records.zomi: Ip gik na tawi leh khawlna nih bek ahi zongin bus tuang a phatuam hi.

records.english: In winter, the high road is often closed, so drivers have to use the valley road.
records.zomi: Phalbi ciangin mual tung lampi a tamzaw-in kikhak a, mawtaw mawngte in kuam lampi a zang kul uh hi.

records.english: Do you think walking would be faster than waiting for the bus?
records.zomi: Bus ngak sangin kal in a manlang zaw ding na ci hiam?

records.english: A shortcut that crosses private land may save time, but it can also cause trouble with the owner.
records.zomi: Mi dang' gam tawng lampi tom in hun a khol thei a, ahi zongin a neipa tawh buaina zong a piang sak thei hi.

records.english: Choose whichever route you'll remember, since both are fine.
records.zomi: Na phawk ding lampi koi pen hiam teel in, a nih in a hoih hi.

records.english: Taking the lift is easier with a pushchair, even if the stairs are quicker.
records.zomi: Kahlei sangin a manlang zaw zongin naungek leeng tawh lift tuang a baih zaw hi.

records.english: Turn left for the quick way or right for the pretty way.
records.zomi: Lampi manlang adingin veilam ah, lampi kilawm adingin taklam ah kihei in.

records.english: Asking two people for directions and comparing their answers is a simple way to avoid a long mistake.

records.english: A route you have been shown once is often easier to follow than one you have been told twice.

records.english: In the morning the river road is quicker, but in the evening everyone uses the ring road.
records.zomi: Zingsang ciangin lui gei lampi a manlang zaw a, ahi zongin nitak ciangin mi khempeuh in khuapi kimkot lampi a zang uh hi.

records.english: Shall we take the scenic route or the motorway?

records.english: The underground is quicker, but the bus lets you see where you're going.
records.zomi: Leinuai meileng in a manlang zaw a, ahi zongin bus in na pai nading mun hong musak hi.

records.english: Signs at the junction pointed two ways to the same village, which confused everyone.
records.zomi: Lampi kikhawlna ah ciamtehnate in khua kibang lam ah lampi nih a lak manin mi khempeuh a buai uh hi.

records.english: The fastest train stops only at the big stations, so we'd have to change for the village.
records.zomi: Meileng manlang pen dinna lianpite bek ah a khawl ahih manin khua lam pai dingin i kheel kul ding hi.

records.english: Whichever way you go, call me when you're nearly there.
records.zomi: Koi lampi na zui zongin na tun dek ciangin hong sam in.

records.english: Which entrance is closer to the children's ward, the front or the side?
records.zomi: Naupangte' damdawi inn khan tawh a nai zaw lutna koi ahi hiam, mai lam hiam, a sih lam hiam?

records.english: The side entrance, next to the car park.
records.zomi: A sih lam lutna, mawtaw koihna mun kiangah.

records.english: Walking takes twenty minutes, while a taxi takes ten but costs a fortune at this hour.
records.zomi: Kal in minit sawmnih a la a, taxi in minit sawm a la a, ahi zongin hih hun ah a man a tam mahmah hi.

records.english: The coast road has wonderful views, while the inland road is straighter and quicker in bad weather.
records.zomi: Tuipi gei lampi ah muhnop lamdang a om a, gam sung lampi in a tang zaw-in huihkhua a hoih loh ciangin a manlang zaw hi.

records.english: Asking for the safest route rather than the quickest one is wise when you're walking alone at night.
records.zomi: Zan ciangin nangmah kia na pai ciangin lampi manlang pen sangin lampi bit pen dong a pil hi.

records.english: How did you and Dad first meet?
records.zomi: Nang leh Pa koi ah na kimu masa uh hiam?

records.english: At a bus stop in the rain, when he offered me half of his umbrella.

records.english: Nobody warned me how exhausting it would be to look after a newborn and a toddler while still answering work emails.

records.english: How can I stop my teenage son from staying up all night on his phone?

records.zomi: Inn sung-a phone khempeuh, nangmah' zong, an huanna inn-a bawm sungah koih hun khat kiciamsak un.

records.english: How are you and your sister getting on these days?

records.english: How should we tell the children that we're moving to another town?

records.english: Together, and with enough time for them to ask all their questions.

records.english: I asked my uncle how he had managed to stay so cheerful after losing his farm.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu kiangah a lo a mansuah khit ciangin bangci lungdam takin a om thei hiam ka dong hi.

records.english: My daughter asked me how I knew I wanted to be a nurse, and I realized I had never really decided.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in nurse hi nuam cih bangci ka theih hiam hong dong a, ka teel taktak ngei lo hi, ci-in ka phawk hi.

records.english: Children often ask how they were born long before their parents feel ready to answer.
records.zomi: A nu leh a pa uh a dawng dingin kiginkhol ma-un naupangte in bangci a suak uh hiam a dong zel uh hi.

records.english: How will I know when the baby is hungry?
records.zomi: Naungek a gil a kial ciangin bangci ka theih ding hiam?

records.english: How are your parents coping since they retired?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa in nasep a tawp khit uh pan bangci a om uh hiam?

records.english: I wonder how we should divide Grandpa's books between the grandchildren so that nobody feels left out.
records.zomi: Kuamah kinusia a kisak loh nadingin Pu' laibute tuta sanggamte kikal-ah bangci i hawm ding hiam ka ngaihsun hi.

records.english: My son wanted to know how his great-grandparents had met, but nobody in the family could remember.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in a pu leh a pi' nu leh pa uh bangci kimu uh hiam a theih nuam a, ahi zongin innkuan sungah kuamah in a phawk kei uh hi.

records.english: How are the twins doing at their new school?
records.zomi: Apengte a sang thak uah bangci a om uh hiam?

records.english: One loves it, and the other misses his old friends terribly.
records.zomi: Khat in a nuam sa mahmah a, a dang khat in a lawm luite a ngaih mahmah hi.

records.english: How do your parents feel about you studying so far from home?
records.zomi: Inn pan gamla mahmah ah na sin thu na nu leh na pa in bangci a ngaihsun uh hiam?

records.english: Proud, I think, though my mother phones me every single evening.
records.zomi: A kipak uh hi, ka ci hi, ka nu in nitak simin hong sam zongin.

records.english: How the family business survived three difficult years is a story my father loves to tell.
records.zomi: Innkuan sumbawlna in kum haksa thum bangci a hing khiat hiam pen ka pa' gen nopna tangthu khat ahi hi.

records.english: How on earth did you two agree on a name for the baby?
records.zomi: Bangci-in nangma nih in naungek min khat ah na kituak uh hiam?

records.english: We didn't, so in the end his big sister chose it.
records.zomi: I kituak kei uh a, a tawpna ah a u numei in a teel hi.

records.english: How tall you've grown since the last time I saw you!
records.zomi: Ka muh nunun pan na sang dan bangzah hiam!

records.english: How do you keep your plants alive when you travel so much?
records.zomi: Na khualzin tam mahmah hangin na singnah teng bangci na hingsak hiam?

records.english: My neighbour waters them, and I bring her back a small present.
records.zomi: Ka innveng in tui a sung sak a, ka kik ciangin letsong neu khat ka lak sak hi.

records.english: When you were small, how did your family celebrate birthdays?
records.zomi: Na neu lai-in na innkuan in pianni bangci a lawp uh hiam?

records.english: How a person treats their elderly relatives says a lot about what they were taught at home.
records.zomi: Mi khat in a sanggam upate a bawl dan in inn ah bang a kihilh hiam a lak mahmah hi.

records.english: How old was Grandpa when he started working?
records.zomi: Pu in nasep a kipat ciangin kum bangzah a cing hiam?

records.english: Just twelve, and he gave every coin he earned to his mother.
records.zomi: Kum sawm leh nih bek, a ngah sum khempeuh a nu a pia hi.

records.english: How did Mum get that scar on her hand?
records.zomi: Nu in a khut tung-a liamna ma bangci a ngah hiam?

records.english: She cut it on a broken jar when she was a girl, helping her own mother in the kitchen.
records.zomi: Numei naupang a hih lai-in an huanna inn ah a nu a huh laitakin um kitan khat in a hiam hi.

records.english: Ask your grandmother how she made the bread when there was no oven in the house.
records.zomi: Inn ah oven a om loh lai-in moh bangci a bawl hiam na pi kiangah dong in.

records.english: Do you remember how we used to spend whole summers at the lake?
records.zomi: Dil ah khal hun bup i zat ngeina uh na phawk hiam?

records.english: You can often tell how close two siblings really are not by how they agree but by how they argue.
records.zomi: Sanggam nih bangzah in a kinai taktak uh hiam pen a kituak dan uh hi lo-in a kinial dan uh tungtawnin na thei thei zel hi.

records.english: How much pocket money should a ten-year-old get?
records.zomi: Kum sawm naupang khat in sum neu bangzah a ngah ding hiam?

records.english: How do you remember everyone's birthday?
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh' pianni bangci na phawk hiam?

records.english: I write them all on the calendar in the kitchen every January.
records.zomi: January kha simin an huanna inn-a calendar tungah a khempeuh ka gelh hi.

records.english: How much time do you spend with your kids on weekdays?
records.zomi: Kal sung ni te ah na tate tawh hun bangzah na zang hiam?

records.english: How did your cousin take the news that she hadn't got the place?
records.zomi: Mun a ngah loh thu na sanggam numei in bangci a ngaihsun hiam?

records.english: Badly at first, but by the next morning she was already planning to apply again.
records.zomi: A masa ah a lungkia mahmah a, ahi zongin a zing zingsang ciangin ngen kik dingin a kilai khin hi.

records.english: How far is it from your house to your parents' house?
records.zomi: Na inn pan na nu leh na pa' inn dong bangzah gamla hiam?

records.english: About an hour by train, so we visit every other weekend.
records.zomi: Meileng tawh nai khat bang ahih manin kal nih simin i veh uh hi.

records.english: How happy your grandmother looked when you walked in!
records.zomi: Na lut ciangin na pi bangzah in a lungdam hiam!

records.english: How is your brother settling into his new job?
records.zomi: Na sanggam pasal a nasep thak ah bangci a om hiam?

records.english: How a family spends its evenings together often tells you more about it than any photograph.
records.zomi: Innkuan khat in nitak hun khawm a zat dan in lim khatpeuh sangin a tungtang thu tam zaw hong gen zel hi.

records.english: How do you calm the baby down when nothing else works?
records.zomi: A dang khatpeuh in a phatuam loh ciangin naungek bangci na nuamsak hiam?

records.english: I put him in the pram and walk round the block until he falls asleep.
records.zomi: Naungek leeng sungah ka koih a, a ihmut dong inn kimkot ah ka paipih hi.

records.english: How exactly did you break the news to your family that you were leaving your job?
records.zomi: Na nasep na nusiat ding thu na innkuan kiangah bangci taktak na gen hiam?

records.english: I told them over dinner, and to my surprise they were relieved.
records.zomi: Nitak an nek laitakin ka gen a, lamdang ka sak in amaute in a lungkham uh a beisak hi.

records.english: I still have no idea how my parents managed to raise five children in a two-room flat without ever seeming short of patience.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in khan nih bek a om inn khat ah naupang nga thuakzawhna a tasam ngei lo bang-in bangci a khanglian sak thei uh hiam ka thei nai kei hi.

records.english: How my mother found time to read to us every night, I will never understand.
records.zomi: Ka nu in zan simin laibu hong sim sak dingin hun bangci a ngah hiam, ka thei ngei kei ding hi.

records.english: How are we supposed to fit everyone around one table for the holiday meal?
records.zomi: Tawlngakni an adingin dawhkan khat kiim ah mi khempeuh bangci i tut sak ding uh hiam?

records.english: We'll borrow the neighbours' folding table and put the children at one end.
records.zomi: Innvengte' dawhkan kituap thei i leitawi ding uh a, naupangte a tawp lam khat ah i tut sak ding uh hi.

records.english: How long have your grandparents been married?
records.zomi: Na pu leh na pi kiteen kum bangzah a cing uh hiam?

records.english: Fifty-three years this spring.
records.zomi: Hih spring ciangin kum sawmnga leh thum.

records.english: How a child is spoken to at home shapes the way that child speaks to others later.
records.zomi: Inn ah naupang khat kiangah a kigen dan in tua naupang in a nung ciangin mi dangte kiangah a gen dan a bawl hi.

records.english: How did you manage when the children were little and you were both working?
records.zomi: Naupangte a neu lai-un na nih in nasep na sem laitakun bangci na zawh uh hiam?

records.english: My mother looked after them, and we couldn't have done it without her.
records.zomi: Ka nu in a kem a, amah om lo hi leh i zo kei ding uh hi.

records.english: In Grandma's language, how do you say goodnight?
records.zomi: Pi' pau ah zanpha bangci ci hiam?

records.english: How can I help my father after his operation without making him feel helpless?
records.zomi: Ka pa a zatui khit ciangin amah a kipan zo lo bang a kisak loh nadingin bangci ka huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: How much should a family change its routine during a child's exam month without making the exams seem even more frightening?
records.zomi: Naupang khat' sitna kha sungin sitna lauhuai zaw a kisak loh nadingin innkuan khat in a ngeina bangzah a kheel ding hiam?

records.english: Can I stay at Grandma's house this week so I can revise in peace?
records.zomi: Daitak-a ka kisin kik theih nadingin hih kal sungin Pi' inn ah ka om thei ding hiam?

records.english: During exam season, the whole house goes quiet after eight o'clock so that my brother can study.
records.zomi: Sitna hun sungin ka sanggam pasal a sin theih nadingin nai giat khit ciangin inn bup a dai hi.

records.english: Shall I make you some tea while you revise?
records.zomi: Na kisin kik laitakin niangtui kong bawl sak ding hiam?

records.english: Living with grandparents during exams can be a comfort, because they remember how stressful it was.
records.zomi: Sitna hun sungin pu leh pite tawh teeng in hehnepna a hi thei hi, a lungkhamhuai dan a phawk uh ahih manin.

records.english: Mum, please don't ask me about the exam until I've had something to eat.
records.zomi: Nu aw, an khat peuhpeuh ka nek ma-in sitna thu hong dong kei in.

records.english: Who told you that your cousin had passed?
records.zomi: Na sanggam numei a zo hi, kua in hong gen hiam?

records.english: You mustn't phone your brother today, because he's in the middle of his final exam.
records.zomi: Na sanggam pasal a sitna nunung pen a sit laitak ahih manin tuni-in sam kei in.

records.english: Tell Grandma the news yourself, because she's been waiting by the phone all morning.
records.zomi: Pi kiangah thu nangmah mah in gen in, zingsang bup phone kiangah a ngak khin ahih manin.

records.english: Living in a crowded house, I learned to revise with earplugs and a torch under the blanket.
records.zomi: Mi tam inn sungah ka teen manin bil-a khuh tawh, puan nuai-ah meivak tawh kisin kik ka sin hi.

records.english: If my brother passes this one, he'll be the first person in our family to go to university.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in hih a zo leh, i innkuan sung-a sangpi pai masa pen a hi ding hi.

records.english: My grandfather still keeps the certificate from the only exam he ever took.
records.zomi: Ka pu in a sit ngei sitna khat bek' laipi a kem lai hi.

records.english: Results were posted online at midnight, so the whole family stayed up to see them.
records.zomi: Zan lai ciangin online ah sitna gah kilak ahih manin amaute en dingin innkuan bup a ihmu kei uh hi.

records.english: Parents who compare one child's results with another's often do more harm than they realize.
records.zomi: Ta khat' sitna gah ta dang khat tawh a kiteh nu leh pate in a theih sangun siatna tam zaw a bawl zel uh hi.

records.english: My little brother kept bursting into my room while I was trying to study, so I put a sign on the door.
records.zomi: Ka sin laitakin ka nau pasal in ka khan ah thakhatin a lut zel ahih manin kongkhak tungah ciamtehna khat ka khet hi.

records.english: My mother wasn't allowed to finish school, so my exams mean a great deal to her.
records.zomi: Ka nu in sang a zawh ding kiphal lo ahih manin ka sitnate amah adingin thupi mahmah hi.

records.english: Are you nervous about your exams next week?
records.zomi: A zom kal-a na sitnate na lau hiam?

records.english: A little, but my sister says the first one is always the worst.
records.zomi: Tawmno, ahi zongin a masa pen a hoih lo pen ahi tawntung hi, ci-in ka u numei in a ci hi.

records.english: My parents sat their language exams in the same week as I sat mine.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in ka sitna ka sit kal mah ah a pau sitna uh a sit uh hi.

records.english: It is important to eat breakfast before an exam, even if you're too nervous to feel hungry.
records.zomi: Na lau mahmah ahih manin gilkial na kisak kei zongin sitna ma-in zingsang an ne a thupi hi.

records.english: My father said, "Whatever happens tomorrow, we'll be proud of you."
records.zomi: Ka pa in, “Zingciang bang hong piang zongin nang tungah i kipak ding uh hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: My grandmother lit a candle for me on the morning of every exam I took.
records.zomi: Ka sit sitna khempeuh' zingsang ciangin ka pi in kei adingin khawimeivaak khat a tawisak hi.

records.english: My parents bought me a new pen for the exam, and I still use it now.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in sitna adingin lai gelhna thak khat hong lei sak uh a, tu dong ka zang lai hi.

records.english: My son needs to pass this exam to get into the school his friends are going to.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in a lawmte' pai ding sang ah a lut theih nadingin hih sitna a zawh kisam hi.

records.english: When older siblings do brilliantly in their exams, younger ones can feel that they're expected to do the same.
records.zomi: Sanggam upate in a sitna uh ah hoih mahmah-a a zawh ciangin a neute in tua bang mah a bawl dingin kilamen bangin a kisa thei uh hi.

records.english: Some families celebrate exam results with a big meal, whatever the grades are.
records.zomi: Innkuan pawl khat in sitna gah bang hi zongin an lianpi tawh a lawp uh hi.

records.english: My sister cried with relief when she heard she had passed.
records.zomi: A zo hi, a zak ciangin ka u numei in a lungdam manin a kap hi.

records.english: Studying at the kitchen table meant that everyone who walked past wanted to help.
records.zomi: An huanna inn-a dawhkan tungah sin in a kantan mi khempeuh huh nuam uh cihna hi.

records.english: Would you mind keeping the baby quiet this afternoon, since I have an online exam?
records.zomi: Online sitna ka neih ahih manin tu nitak lam naungek na daisak thei ding hiam?

records.english: What did your parents say when you failed your driving theory test?
records.zomi: Mawtaw mawng theory sitna na zawh loh ciangin na nu leh na pa in bang a ci uh hiam?

records.english: Mum laughed and told me she had failed hers twice.
records.zomi: Nu in a nuihsan a, amah zong nihvei a zo lo hi, hong ci hi.

records.english: Results day was the only time I ever saw my grandfather cry.
records.zomi: Sitna gah ni bek ka pu' kah ka muh ngei ahi hi.

records.english: Why do you look so worried?
records.zomi: Bang hangin lungkham mahmah bangin na kilang hiam?

records.english: Because my parents are coming to collect my results with me.
records.zomi: Ka sitna gah la dingin ka nu leh ka pa kei tawh hong pai ding uh ahih manin.

records.english: When a student's family depends on a scholarship, every exam can feel like a test of the whole household.
records.zomi: Sangnaupang khat' innkuan in scholarship tungah a kinga ciangin sitna khempeuh innkuan bup' sitna bangin kisa thei hi.

records.english: Should parents reward good exam results with money, or does that teach children to study only for a prize?
records.zomi: Nu leh pate in sitna gah hoih sum tawh a laksap ding uh hiam, ahih kei leh tua in naupangte letsong bek adingin sin dingin a hilh hiam?

records.english: I failed my maths exam the first time, and I was too ashamed to tell my parents for a week.
records.zomi: Ka masa pen-in ka maths sitna ka zo kei a, kal khat sung ka nu leh ka pa kiangah gen dingin ka zum lua hi.

records.english: Did you tell your parents your score yet?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa kiangah na mak na gen khin hiam?

records.english: My mother used index cards and a kitchen timer to help me learn the dates for history.
records.zomi: Tangthu sung-a nite ka sin theih nadingin ka nu in lai tawmnote leh an huanna inn-a hun tehna nai a zang hi.

records.english: Our neighbours' daughter came over to explain the chemistry I didn't understand.
records.zomi: I innvengte' tanu in ka theih loh chemistry hong genteh dingin hong pai hi.

records.english: Please don't put the television on while your sister is revising.
records.zomi: Na u numei a kisin kik laitakin television hong kei in.

records.english: I don't want my family to feel that my exam results are the only thing that matters about me.
records.zomi: Ka sitna gah bek kei tungtang-a thupi pen ahi bangin ka innkuan a ngaihsut ding ka deih kei hi.

records.english: Let's go for a walk after your exam, just the two of us.
records.zomi: Na sitna khit ciangin i nih bek pai vialvial ni.

records.english: The exam was moved to a Saturday, which meant missing my cousin's wedding.
records.zomi: Sitna Kiginni ah a kikheel a, tua in ka sanggam' mopawi ka tel lo ding cihna hi.

records.english: A parent's calm voice on the morning of an exam can matter more than a last hour of revision.
records.zomi: Sitna zingsang-a nu hiam pa' aw nem in kisin kik nai nunung sangin a thupi zaw thei hi.

records.english: My parents never asked about my marks, only whether I had done my best.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in ka mak a dong ngei kei uh a, ka hoih theih pen ka bawl hiam bek a dong uh hi.

records.english: Did your dad really sit his exams in a tent after the school burned down?
records.zomi: Sang a kangmang khit ciangin na pa in puan inn sungah a sitna a sit taktak hiam?

records.english: Exams that fall during a family crisis, such as a serious illness at home, often deserve special consideration from the school.
records.zomi: Innkuan buaina hun, inn ah natna gikpi bang hun sung-a sitnate in sang pan ngaihsutna tuam a ngah ding uh a kilawm zel hi.

records.english: Dad tested me on my French verbs while he was cooking dinner.
records.zomi: Pa in nitak an a huan laitakin ka French verb te hong sit hi.

records.english: On the morning of my final exam, I found a little note of encouragement that my mother had hidden in my pencil case.
records.zomi: Ka sitna nunung pen' zingsang ciangin ka nu in ka lai gelhna bawm sungah a sel hasuahna lai neu khat ka mu hi.

records.english: When my results arrived, my father read the letter out loud to the whole family before I had even seen it.
records.zomi: Ka sitna gah a tun ciangin ka muh ma-in ka pa in innkuan bup kiangah lai aw ngaih takin a sim hi.

records.english: My twin and I sat the same exam, and we got exactly the same mark.
records.zomi: Ka apeng leh kei sitna kibang ka sit uh a, mak kibang taktak ka ngah uh hi.

records.english: My aunt drove me to the exam centre because the buses were on strike.
records.zomi: Bus te nasep khawl uh ahih manin ka ni in sitna mun ah mawtaw tawh hong paipih hi.

records.english: Talking honestly with your children about your own exam failures can make theirs feel less frightening.
records.zomi: Na tate kiangah nangmah' sitna zawh lohnate thu dikin gen in amaute' zawh lohna a laudan zaw sak thei hi.

records.english: The family chat filled with messages the moment my results came in.
records.zomi: Ka sitna gah a tun ciangin innkuan chat ah thu tampi tawh a dim pah hi.

records.english: My dad took the day off work so that he could drive me to my first exam.
records.zomi: Ka sitna masa ah hong paipih theih nadingin ka pa nasep pan ni khat a tawl hi.

records.english: What would your parents do if you failed?
records.zomi: Na zawh kei leh na nu leh na pa in bang a bawl ding uh hiam?

records.english: Help me plan a retake, I hope, after a long talk.
records.zomi: Sawt pi kihopih khit ciangin sit kik nading hong gelsak ding uh hi, ka lamen hi.

records.english: How did your family react to your exam results?
records.zomi: Na sitna gah tungah na innkuan in bang a ci uh hiam?

records.english: They were thrilled, and my uncle phoned everyone he knew.
records.zomi: A lungdam mahmah uh a, ka pa neu in a theih mi khempeuh a sam hi.

records.english: Our family received help with heating bills during the coldest months of the year.
records.zomi: Kum sung-a a vot pen khate sungin i innkuan in inn lumna man adingin huhna i ngah uh hi.

records.english: Long waiting times for support can push families further into debt.
records.zomi: Huhna ngak hun sawt in innkuante leiba sung ah a pai zaw sak thei hi.

records.english: Who should I contact if my payment doesn't arrive?
records.zomi: Ka sum a tun kei leh kua ka sam ding hiam?

records.english: We really did need that help last winter, and I'm grateful we asked for it.
records.zomi: Phalbi nunung in tua huhna i kisam taktak a, i nget manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: Bring your children if you need to; there's a play corner in the waiting room.
records.zomi: Na kisam leh na tate tawi in; ngakna khan ah naupang kimawlna mun a om hi.

records.english: I lost my job last month, so I've applied for income support.
records.zomi: Kha nunung in ka nasep ka mansuah ahih manin sum huhna ka ngen hi.

records.english: Everyone in the queue was given a cup of tea while they waited.
records.zomi: A ngak laitakun dawn dingin a kizang mi khempeuh niangtui haai khat kipia hi.

records.english: Can I apply online, or do I have to come in person?
records.zomi: Online-in ka ngen thei ding hiam, ka pai kul ding hiam?

records.english: You can do it online, but we'll still need to see your documents once.
records.zomi: Online-in na bawl thei a, ahi zongin na laite khatvei i muh kisam lai ding hi.

records.english: Clear letters written in plain language help people understand what support they can receive and why.
records.zomi: Pau baih taka kigelh lai kician in mite in bang huhna a ngah thei uh hiam, bang hangin hiam a theih nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Asking for help is not a sign of failure; it is a sensible thing to do when times are hard.
records.zomi: Huhna ngen pen zawh lohna lahna hi lo a, hun haksa ciangin a pil thu bawlna ahi hi.

records.english: Many people who receive social assistance are working but still don't earn enough to pay for food and housing.
records.zomi: Kumpi huhna a ngah mi tampi nasep a sem uh a, ahi zongin an leh teenna adingin a kicing sum a ngah zo lo uh hi.

records.english: My cousin only found out about the energy grant by chance, from a leaflet someone had left on a table at the library.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam in energy huhna sum thu laibu inn-a dawhkan tungah mi khat' nusiat lai neu khat pan a kiman lo-in a thei hi.

records.english: No one should have to choose between heating their home and feeding their children.
records.zomi: Kuamah in a inn lumsak leh a tate an vak kikal-ah a teel kul kei ding hi.

records.english: Is the local food bank open on Fridays as well as Tuesdays?
records.zomi: Mun-a an piakna inn Pithai ni bek hi lo-in Laithai ni zong-in a kihong hiam?

records.english: A housing allowance can make the difference between keeping a home and losing it.
records.zomi: Inn man huhna in inn kem leh inn mansuah kikal kibatlohna a bawl thei hi.

records.english: Free school meals mean that children from low-income families get at least one hot meal a day.
records.zomi: Sang an man om lo in sum tawm innkuan naupangte ni khat ah an lum vei khat a ngah tawntung ding uh cihna hi.

records.english: My grandmother gets a small pension top-up because her own pension is so low.
records.zomi: Ka pi in a pension a tawm mahmah ahih manin pension behlap neu khat a ngah hi.

records.english: Social assistance works best when the people who receive it are also helped to find stable work and housing.
records.zomi: Kumpi huhna in a ngah mite nasep leh teenna kip a zon nadingin a kihuh ciangin a hoih pen ahi hi.

records.english: The office asked me to send copies of my last three bank statements.
records.zomi: Office in ka bank lai kha thum nunung te' copy hong khak dingin a ngen hi.

records.english: My mother had a caseworker explain all the benefits she could claim after my father died.
records.zomi: Ka pa a sih khit ciangin ka nu in a ngah theih huhna khempeuh caseworker khat in a genteh hi.

records.english: You don't have to explain everything at once; we can go through it step by step.
records.zomi: Khatvei-in a khempeuh na genteh kul kei hi; khat zawh khat i en thei hi.

records.english: Where can I ask about help with my rent?
records.zomi: Ka inn man adingin huhna koi ah ka dong thei ding hiam?

records.english: At the council's advice desk, on the ground floor of the town hall.
records.zomi: Khuapi office' thuhilhna dawhkan ah, khuapi inn' lei tung khan ah.

records.english: Without the childcare grant, I wouldn't have been able to go back to work.
records.zomi: Naupang kemna huhna sum om lo hi leh nasep ah ka ciah kik thei kei ding hi.

records.english: My neighbour helped me fill in the form, because the questions were confusing.
records.zomi: Dotnate a buaihuai ahih manin ka innveng in form hong dimsak hi.

records.english: Can someone help me read this letter from the benefits office?
records.zomi: Huhna office pan hih lai sim dingin kuamah in hong huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Food vouchers can be used at most supermarkets in town.
records.zomi: An lei lai te khuapi sung-a supermarket a tamzaw ah kizang thei hi.

records.english: When the factory closed, many families in our street had to rely on social assistance for a while.
records.zomi: Factory a kikhak ciangin i lampi-a innkuan tampi in hun khat sung kumpi huhna tungah a kinga kul uh hi.

records.english: You two can wait here while I find someone who speaks your language.
records.zomi: Na pau a gen thei mi khat ka zon laitakin na nih in hih ah ngak un.

records.english: Will I lose my support if I start a part-time job?
records.zomi: Hun tawmno nasep khat ka kipat leh ka huhna ka mansuah ding hiam?

records.english: Not straight away; it will be reduced gradually as you earn more.
records.zomi: Tu-in hi lo; na ngah a tam semsem ciangin kiamkiam ding hi.

records.english: Because the family had no money left for food, the emergency payment was approved on the same day they applied.
records.zomi: Innkuan in an adingin sum a nei nawn lo uh ahih manin haksatna huhna sum a nget ni uh mah-in kipom hi.

records.english: You do have the right to ask for a review if you think the decision was wrong.
records.zomi: Thukhenna dik lo hi, na ci leh en kik dingin na ngen thei taktak hi.

records.english: My sister had her disability allowance reviewed, and the payment was increased.
records.zomi: Ka u numei' disability huhna kien kik a, a sum kikhangsak hi.

records.english: Come back next week with your rental agreement, and we'll finish the form.
records.zomi: Kal zom ciangin na inn luahna lai tawi-in hong pai kik in, form i zo ding hi.

records.english: Everyone, please take a number and wait until you are called.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, nambat khat la un a, hong kisam ma-un ngak un.

records.english: You should all receive a letter confirming your appointment within a week.
records.zomi: Na kimuhna ciamtehna lai kal khat sungin na vekpi-un na ngah ding uh hi.

records.english: Social assistance often covers a mixture of cash payments and practical services, such as help with childcare.
records.zomi: Kumpi huhna in sum piakna leh naupang kemna huhna bang nasep huhna kihel a huam zel hi.

records.english: The advice centre gives free help to anyone who doesn't understand their rights.
records.zomi: Thuhilhna inn in a thuneihnate a theih lohte kiangah man om lo-in huhna a pia hi.

records.english: Volunteers at the drop-in centre can help you write a letter of appeal.
records.zomi: Lutna om lo huhna inn ah deihsakna nasemte in ngen kikna lai na gelh nadingin hong huh thei uh hi.

records.english: Respectful treatment at the benefits office made the whole process far less frightening for my parents.
records.zomi: Huhna office ah zahtak taka kibawl manin ka nu leh ka pa adingin a kalsuan bup a lauhuai mahmah nawn lo hi.

records.english: A charity paid for my son's glasses when we couldn't afford them.
records.zomi: I lei zawh loh ciangin charity khat in ka tapa' mitlimlang man a pia hi.

records.english: Do you know if I can get help paying for my children's school uniforms?
records.zomi: Ka tate' sang puan man piak nadingin huhna ka ngah thei ding hiam na thei hiam?

records.english: Fill in the form in black ink and sign it at the bottom.
records.zomi: Form sung khuk dum tawh dim inla a nuai lam ah na min khet in.

records.english: If your circumstances change, you must tell the office as soon as possible.
records.zomi: Na dinmun a kikheel leh office kiangah a theih tawpin manlang takin na gen ding hi.

records.english: How soon will I hear whether my application has been accepted?
records.zomi: Ka ngetna a kipom hiam bangtan hun-in ka za ding hiam?

records.english: Usually about four weeks, but you can ask for an emergency payment if you can't wait.
records.zomi: A tamzaw-in kal li bang, ahi zongin na ngak zo kei leh haksatna huhna sum na ngen thei hi.

records.english: The social worker visits my grandfather once a month to make sure he's managing.
records.zomi: Social worker in ka pu a zawh hiam en dingin kha khat ah vei khat a veh hi.

records.english: Is there any support for carers who look after a sick relative at home?
records.zomi: Inn ah sanggam a natpa kemte adingin huhna om hiam?

records.english: You'll need to bring proof of your address and your income.
records.zomi: Na teenna mun leh na sum ngahna lakna na tawi kisam ding hi.

records.english: Social assistance helps people who cannot cover their basic needs on their own.
records.zomi: Kumpi huhna in amau kia-in a kisapna tawmpi a kizopsak zo lo mite a huh hi.

records.english: Some older people never claim the help they are entitled to, because they feel embarrassed to ask.
records.zomi: Mi upa pawl khat in a ngen dingin a zum uh ahih manin a ngah theih uh huhna a ngen ngei kei uh hi.

records.english: Shall I come with you to the appointment, so you don't have to go alone?
records.zomi: Nangmah kia na pai kul loh nadingin kimuhna ah kong zui ding hiam?

records.english: Rules about who can receive social assistance vary between regions, so it's worth checking local information.
records.zomi: Kua in kumpi huhna a ngah thei hiam cih thukhamte gamkhen tuamtuam ah a kibang lo ahih manin mun-a thu en a phatuam hi.

records.english: My friend uses the community fridge, where people leave food that would otherwise be thrown away.
records.zomi: Ka lawm in mipi kizang an vot bawm a zang a, tua ah kipaikhiatsak ding ante mite in a koih uh hi.

records.english: My uncle uses a community transport service to get to his hospital appointments for free.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in damdawi inn kimuhna-ah man om lo-in a pai theih nadingin mipi mawtaw huhna a zang hi.

records.english: I did apply on time, but my letter must have been lost in the post.
records.zomi: Hun takin ka ngen taktak a, ahi zongin ka lai lai khakna ah a mang kha ding hi.

records.english: Please call this number if you are worried that you won't have enough food this week.
records.zomi: Hih kal sungin an kicing na nei lo ding hi, ci-in na lungkham leh hih nambat sam in.

records.english: The payments go straight into my bank account every two weeks.
records.zomi: Sumte kal nih simin ka bank account ah a tang-in a lut hi.

records.english: Shall we ask the oldest members of the club to lead the history walk?
records.zomi: Tangthu kalna makaih dingin kikhopna pawl' mi upa pente i ngen ding hiam?

records.english: In the early days, there was no school in our village.
records.zomi: A masa ni te-in i khua ah sang om lo hi.

records.english: The families got together and turned an empty barn into a classroom.
records.zomi: Innkuante kikhawm uh a, van koihna inn awng khat sangkhan ah a bawl uh hi.

records.english: That barn is still standing, and the children visit it every year.
records.zomi: Tua van koihna inn a ding lai a, naupangte in kum simin a veh uh hi.

records.english: When the last shop closed, residents opened a small community shop run by volunteers.
records.zomi: Dawl nunung a kikhak ciangin khua mite in deihsakna nasemte' kepna dawl neu khat a hong uh hi.

records.english: Some historic buildings are protected by law, so they cannot be changed without permission.
records.zomi: Tangthu inn pawl khat thukham in a kem ahih manin phalna om lo-in kikheel thei lo hi.

records.english: A community's history includes not only its famous events but also the everyday lives of ordinary people.
records.zomi: Mipi khat' tangthu in a minthang thupiangte bek hi lo-in mi tavuante' ni simin nuntakna zong a huam hi.

records.english: My neighbour still remembers the day the first bus came to our village.
records.zomi: Ka innveng in i khua ah bus masa pen a tun ni a phawk lai hi.

records.english: Is that statue in the park of someone from our town?
records.zomi: Huan sung-a tua milim suang pen i khua mi khat ahi hiam?

records.english: Who built the stone bridge over the river?
records.zomi: Lui tung-a suang lei kua in a lam hiam?

records.english: Children, please don't touch the old maps; they're very fragile.
records.zomi: Naupangte, map luite khoih kei un; a nem mahmah hi.

records.english: This square used to be the place where farmers sold their animals every Thursday.
records.zomi: Hih mun pen Laizing ni simin lo neite in a ganhingte uh a zuakna mun ahi ngei hi.

records.english: Local history is easier for children to understand when they can walk past the places they are learning about.
records.zomi: Naupangte in a sin uh munte a kantan thei uh ciangin mun-a tangthu a theih a baih zaw hi.

records.english: Community history is often kept alive in old photographs, letters and the memories of long-time residents.
records.zomi: Mipi tangthu pen lim lui, lai leh hun sawt teeng mite' phawkna-ah a hing den zel hi.

records.english: Volunteers recorded interviews with elderly residents using a small digital recorder.
records.zomi: Deihsakna nasemte in khua mi upate tawh kidotna digital recorder neu khat tawh a la uh hi.

records.english: Before the road was built, the only way to reach the next village was by boat.
records.zomi: Lampi a kilam ma-in a kiang khua tun nading lampi tembaw bek ahi hi.

records.english: The church bell was rung to call people together whenever there was important news.
records.zomi: Thu thupi a om ciangin mite kikhawm dingin pawlpi khawng kitum hi.

records.english: We need more young people to join the history group, or the stories will be lost.
records.zomi: Tangthu pawl ah khangnote tam zaw a kihel kisam a, kihel lo uh leh tangthute a mang ding hi.

records.english: Did our grandparents really dance at the town hall every Saturday night?
records.zomi: I pu leh pite Kiginni zan simin khuapi inn ah lam taktak uh hiam?

records.english: You can learn a lot about a neighbourhood just by reading the names on its streets.
records.zomi: Lampi minte sim bek tawh mun khat tungtang thu tampi na thei thei hi.

records.english: The ruins on the hill were once a castle, but nobody knows exactly when it was built.
records.zomi: Mual tung-a a siat khinte kulh khat ahi ngei a, ahi zongin bang hun-in kilam hiam kuamah in a thei kician kei uh hi.

records.english: Our town grew up around the railway station about a hundred years ago.
records.zomi: I khuapi pen kum za khat bang pan meileng dinna kiim ah a khang hi.

records.english: Has anyone written down the history of our neighbourhood?
records.zomi: I mun' tangthu kuamah in a gelh khin hiam?

records.english: The history society had the old photographs scanned so that everyone could see them online.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh in online-in a muh theih nadingun tangthu pawl in lim luite scan sak uh hi.

records.english: The old railway line is now a cycle path.
records.zomi: Meileng lampi lui tu-in siiksakol lampi a hi ta hi.

records.english: Why were the miners' houses built in such long rows so close to the pit?
records.zomi: Bang hangin suangtum kua nasemte' inn kua kiang mahmah ah tuat sau pi-in kilam hiam?

records.english: A local teacher wrote a short history of the village for the children to read.
records.zomi: Mun-a saya khat in naupangte' sim dingin khua' tangthu tomno khat a gelh hi.

records.english: Families who arrived at different times all added something to the story of our street.
records.zomi: Hun tuamtuam-a a tung innkuante khempeuh in i lampi' tangthu ah khat peuhpeuh a behlap uh hi.

records.english: A plaque on the corner marks the house where the town's first doctor lived.
records.zomi: Kil-a suangpek khat in khuapi' siavuan masa pen' tenna inn a ciamteh hi.

records.english: Have you ever looked through the old newspapers in the library to see how much the price of bread has changed?
records.zomi: Moh man bangzah a kikheel hiam en dingin laibu inn-a thuthak lai luite na en ngei hiam?

records.english: You must sign in at the archive desk before you can look at the old records.
records.zomi: Lai lui ciamtehnate na en theih ma-in lai kemna dawhkan ah na min na gelh kisam hi.

records.english: Our club is collecting stories from people who have lived here for more than fifty years.
records.zomi: I kikhopna pawl in hih ah kum sawmnga sang a teeng mite' tangthu a kaikhawm hi.

records.english: Fishing remained the main way of life here until the harbour gradually silted up and the larger boats could no longer come in.
records.zomi: Tembaw khawlna ah leivui a dim kiamkiam-a tembaw lianzawte a lut theih nawn loh dong ngasa man hih ah nuntakna lian pen ahi lai hi.

records.english: This bench was put here in memory of the woman who ran the bakery for forty years.
records.zomi: Hih tutphah pen kum sawmli sung moh bawlna dawl a kem numei phawkna dingin hih ah kikoih hi.

records.english: The town's name comes from an old word meaning "crossing by the river".
records.zomi: Khuapi' min pen “lui kiang kantanna” cihna kammal lui khat pan hong pai hi.

records.english: Local records show that the school has never closed for a single year since it opened.
records.zomi: Mun-a ciamtehnate in sang a kihon pan kum khat zong kikhak ngei lo hi, ci-in a lak hi.

records.english: Everyone, bring any old family photos of the town to the meeting next week.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, khuapi' innkuan lim lui na neih khempeuh kal zom-a kikhopna ah tawi un.

records.english: Every community history has gaps, especially where the stories of poorer families were never written down.
records.zomi: Mipi tangthu khempeuh ah a awng mun a om a, a diak in innkuan zawngte' tangthu kigelh ngei lo munte ah.

records.english: Please return the archive boxes to the shelf exactly where you found them.
records.zomi: Lai kemna bawmte na muhna mun taktak ah shelf tungah koih kik un.

records.english: Do you two know why the river bridge is painted green?
records.zomi: Bang hangin lui lei eng zeek hiam na nih in na thei uh hiam?

records.english: The war memorial lists the names of men from every family in the parish.
records.zomi: Gal phawkna suang in pawlpi gamsung-a innkuan khempeuh pan pasalte' min a lak hi.

records.english: Every year, the village gathers by the old oak to remember its founders.
records.zomi: Kum simin khua in a kiphuh masate phawk dingin sing lianpi lui kiangah kikhawm hi.

records.english: When did the factory close?
records.zomi: Factory bang hun-in kikhak hiam?

records.english: In the early nineties, and half the street lost their jobs that year.
records.zomi: Kum 1990 kipat lam ah, tua kum in lampi' a langkhat in a nasep uh a mansuah uh hi.

records.english: Older residents remember when the whole village shared one telephone in the post office.
records.zomi: Khua mi upate in khua bup in post office-a phone khat a kizat khawm hun a phawk uh hi.

records.english: The village fair has been held on the same field for over two hundred years.
records.zomi: Khua pumpi kipahna pen kum za nih sang lo kibang mah ah kibawl hi.

records.english: Why is this street called Mill Lane?
records.zomi: Bang hangin hih lampi Mill Lane kici hiam?

records.english: There used to be a flour mill at the bottom of it, by the stream.
records.zomi: A nuai lam-a tuiluang kiangah mim gaina khat a om ngei hi.

records.english: Old maps show that our school was built on land that was once an orchard.
records.zomi: Map luite in i sang pen singgah huan hi ngei gam tungah kilam hi, ci-in a lak hi.

records.english: A town's history is not fixed, because each new generation asks different questions about the past.
records.zomi: Khuapi khat' tangthu a kip kei hi, khangthak khempeuh in hun bei tungtang dotna tuamtuam a dot uh ahih manin.

records.english: The old well in the middle of the village was the only source of water until the pipes were laid.
records.zomi: Tuiburi a kikhum ma-in khua lailung-a tuikhuk lui bek tui ngahna mun ahi hi.

records.english: The local museum has a room full of tools that farmers once used to plough the fields by hand.
records.zomi: Mun-a museum in lo neite in khut tawh lo a leh uh hun-a a zat uh vanzatte tawh a dim khan khat a nei hi.

records.english: The clock tower was built with money raised by local families.
records.zomi: Nai inn sang pen mun-a innkuante' kaikhop sum tawh kilam hi.

records.english: A community history project brought together people who had lived on the same street for years without ever really talking.
records.zomi: Mipi tangthu nasep khat in kum tampi lampi kibang ah teeng a, a kihopih ngei lo mite a kaikhawm hi.

records.english: Listening to the stories of older neighbours can change how young people see the streets they walk every day.
records.zomi: Innveng upate' tangthu ngaihkhiat in khangnote in ni simin a kalna lampite a muh dan a kheel thei hi.

records.english: Can you show us where the old cinema used to be?
records.zomi: Cinema lui a omna mun hong lak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Why did so many people leave the island in the last century?
records.zomi: Bang hangin kum za nunung sungin mi tampi in tuikulh a nusia uh hiam?

records.english: When the cotton mills opened, they brought hundreds of workers to the valley, and within a generation the town had doubled in size.
records.zomi: La puan bawlna factory te a kihon ciangin kuam ah nasem za tampi a tun sak uh a, khangkhat sungin khuapi a lianzah nih a pha hi.

records.english: The old market hall is now a library.
records.zomi: Zuakna inn lui tu-in laibu inn a hi ta hi.

records.english: Knowing the history of a place can give newcomers a stronger sense of belonging.
records.zomi: Mun khat' tangthu theih in mi thakte in a kihelna a kisak zawsak thei hi.

records.english: Some drivers prefer paper maps because they can see the whole route at once.
records.zomi: Mawtaw mawngmi pawl khat in lampi bup khatvei-in a muh theih uh ahih manin lai map a deih zaw uh hi.

records.english: Driving lessons in winter are harder, but they prepare you for ice and early darkness.
records.zomi: Phalbi-a mawtaw mawng sinna a haksa zaw a, ahi zongin tuikhal leh mial manlangna adingin hong kiginsak hi.

records.english: Do you think a learner should start in a quiet village or on busy roads?
records.zomi: Sin lai mi khat in khua dai khat ah hiam, lampi buai tungah hiam a kipan ding na ci hiam?

records.english: A van would be more useful for the business, though it's harder to park.
records.zomi: Van mawtaw in sumbawlna adingin a phatuam zaw ding a, ahi zongin koih a haksa zaw hi.

records.english: Learning with a parent is cheaper, but a qualified instructor notices bad habits that a parent may share.
records.zomi: Nu hiam pa tawh sin a man neem zaw a, ahi zongin a kicing hilhpa khat in nu hiam pa in zong a neih kha thei ngeina hoih lote a mu hi.

records.english: Taking the motorway costs more in tolls, but the old road wears out your tyres.
records.zomi: Mawtaw lampi lian zui in lampi man tam zaw a pia a, ahi zongin lampi lui in na tyre te a siasak hi.

records.english: Cycling to work takes longer than driving, but I arrive feeling awake.
records.zomi: Nasep ah siiksakol tawh pai in mawtaw mawng sangin hun a la zaw a, ahi zongin ka tun ciangin ka kihalh hi.

records.english: A small car is cheaper to run, while a bigger one is more comfortable on long journeys.
records.zomi: Mawtaw neu zat man a neem zaw a, a lian zaw khat in khualzin sau ah a nuam zaw hi.

records.english: Which seat is safer for a small child, behind the driver or in the middle?
records.zomi: Naupang neu khat adingin koi tutna a bit zaw hiam, mawngpa' nung lam ah hiam, a lai ah hiam?

records.english: We really did save money when we sold the second car and bought bicycles.
records.zomi: Mawtaw nihna i zuak-in siiksakol i lei uh ciangin sum i khol taktak uh hi.

records.english: Which colour is easier to see at night, white or dark blue?
records.zomi: Zan ciangin koi rong muh a baih zaw hiam, kang hiam, a dum hiam?

records.english: Which do you find harder, parallel parking or reversing round a corner?
records.zomi: Koi na haksat sak zaw hiam, mawtaw tuat-a koih hiam, kil kiim-a nunglam kik hiam?

records.english: Parallel parking, especially when someone is waiting behind me.
records.zomi: Mawtaw tuat-a koih, a diak in ka nung ah mi khat a ngak ciangin.

records.english: Some families keep one car and use taxis for the rest, which can cost less than owning a second car.
records.zomi: Innkuan pawl khat in mawtaw khat bek a kem uh a, a dang adingin taxi a zang uh a, tua in mawtaw nihna neih sangin a man neem zaw thei hi.

records.english: We picked the car with five doors so that Grandma could get in and out easily.
records.zomi: Pi in baih takin a lut a pusuak theih nadingin kongkhak nga nei mawtaw i teel uh hi.

records.english: Is it safer to brake hard or to steer around a pothole?
records.zomi: Lampi kua khat ah a gik takin khawlsak a bit zaw hiam, kiheisak-a pelh a bit zaw hiam?

records.english: My mother sold her car and now walks everywhere, and she says she has never felt better.
records.zomi: Ka nu in a mawtaw a zuak a, tu-in koi ah zong a kal a, tu bangin a damna a hoih ngei kei hi, a ci hi.

records.english: When the old car finally broke down for good, the decision about a new one was made for us.
records.zomi: Mawtaw lui a tawpna dingin a siat ciangin a thak tungtang thukhenna eite adingin kibawl khin hi.

records.english: Is it better to overtake the tractor now or wait until the road straightens out?
records.zomi: Tu-in tractor i khen ding hiam, lampi a tang ma-in i ngak ding hiam?

records.english: Last year I had to choose between a reliable old car and a shiny one with high mileage.
records.zomi: Kum nunung in mawtaw lui muanhuai leh mawng tam khin taang mawtaw kikal-ah ka teel kul hi.

records.english: My father told me to listen to the engines rather than look at the paint.
records.zomi: Ka pa in zeek en sangin engine aw ngaikhia in, hong ci hi.

records.english: I bought the old one, and it hasn't let me down once.
records.zomi: A lui ka lei a, khatvei zong hong siasak ngei kei hi.

records.english: A roundabout keeps traffic moving, whereas traffic lights make everyone wait, even when the road is empty.
records.zomi: Lampi kimkot in mawtawte a kalsuan sak den a, meivak ciamtehnate in lampi a awng ciangin zong mi khempeuh a ngaksak hi.

records.english: A dashboard camera costs a little, but it can settle an argument after an accident.
records.zomi: Mawtaw camera in man tawmno a la a, ahi zongin accident khit ciangin kinialna a khensak thei hi.

records.english: Driving at dawn is quieter, but the low sun can be blinding on the eastern road.
records.zomi: Khuavak hun ah mawng a dai zaw a, ahi zongin nisuahna lam lampi ah ni niam in mit a vaaksak thei hi.

records.english: When you're choosing a used car, its service history matters more than its colour.
records.zomi: Mawtaw zang khin na teel ciangin a rong sangin a kibawl kik dan tangthu a thupi zaw hi.

records.english: For a nervous driver, a quiet route with more turns may be better than a fast road with heavy lorries.
records.zomi: A lau mawtaw mawngpa khat adingin kikheelna tam lampi dai khat in mawtaw gik lianpi tampi om lampi manlang sangin a hoih zaw thei hi.

records.english: Wide tyres grip well on dry roads, but narrow ones can be safer in snow.
records.zomi: Tyre zai in lampi keu tungah hoih takin a len a, ahi zongin a kiat te vuk sungah a bit zaw thei hi.

records.english: Should we leave at five to beat the traffic or at nine when the roads are clearer?
records.zomi: Mawtaw buaina pelh dingin nai nga ciangin i pai ding hiam, lampite a awng zawk nai kua ciangin i pai ding hiam?

records.english: You do save fuel by driving smoothly instead of speeding up and braking all the time.
records.zomi: Manlang takin khangsak-in khawlsak den sangin daitak-a na mawng ciangin dat na khol taktak hi.

records.english: Is a diesel car worth it if I only drive in town?
records.zomi: Khuapi sung bek ah ka mawng leh diesel mawtaw a phatuam ding hiam?

records.english: Buying from a dealer costs more than buying from a private seller, but you usually get a guarantee.

records.english: Shall I take the bypass or go straight through the town centre?

records.english: I'd rather pay a little more for a car park than leave the car on a dark street.
records.zomi: Lampi mial khat ah mawtaw nusia sangin mawtaw koihna mun man tawmno tam zaw piak ka deih zaw hi.

records.english: Do you prefer driving on motorways or on country roads?
records.zomi: Mawtaw lampi lian tungah mawng na deih zaw hiam, gam lampi tungah hiam?

records.english: Country roads, because I'd rather go slowly and see the fields.
records.zomi: Gam lampi, nuam takin pai-in lote en ka deih zaw ahih manin.

records.english: We chose the car with the bigger boot, because we needed room for the pushchair.

records.english: Should I buy a new car or a second-hand one?
records.zomi: Mawtaw thak ka lei ding hiam, zang khin khat ka lei ding hiam?

records.english: A second-hand one, if a mechanic you trust looks at it first.

records.english: We switched to a smaller car, and the parking problems disappeared.
records.zomi: Mawtaw neu zaw ah i kheel uh a, koihna buainate a bei hi.

records.english: Would you rather sit in traffic for an hour or take the longer road that keeps moving?
records.zomi: Mawtaw buaina sungah nai khat na tut ding hiam, a kalsuan den lampi sau zaw na zui ding hiam?

records.english: The longer road, because sitting still makes me far more impatient.

records.english: Do you two want to share the driving, or shall I do the whole trip?

records.english: Shall we take your car or mine?
records.zomi: Na mawtaw i zang ding hiam, kei-a pen?

records.english: The cheaper petrol station is ten minutes away, which hardly makes sense for a small top-up.
records.zomi: Dat man neem zaw zuakna mun minit sawm gamla ah a om a, tawmno behlap adingin a kilawm khol kei hi.

records.english: An automatic car is easier to learn in, but a manual licence lets you drive both.
records.zomi: Automatic mawtaw tawh sin a baih zaw a, ahi zongin manual licence in a nih na mawng theisak hi.

records.english: In the city I prefer the bus, but in the countryside the car is the only real choice.
records.zomi: Khuapi sungah bus ka deih zaw a, ahi zongin gam sungah mawtaw bek teel theih taktak ahi hi.

records.english: Let's take the smaller car, since there are only two of us.
records.zomi: I nih bek i om uh ahih manin mawtaw neu zaw i zang ni.

records.english: I'll drive there, and you can drive back.

records.english: Overtaking on a bend is never worth the few seconds it might save.
records.zomi: Lampi kawi ah khen in a khol theih second tawmno adingin a phatuam ngei kei hi.

records.english: On a motorbike you get through traffic faster, but you feel every drop of rain.

records.english: Choosing a car often says more about a family's routine than about its taste.
records.zomi: Mawtaw teel in innkuan khat' deih dan sangin a ni simin nuntak dan a lak zaw zel hi.

records.english: Renting a car on holiday gives you freedom, but in old towns with narrow streets it can be more trouble than it's worth.

records.english: Hiring a driver for the wedding day was more expensive, but nobody had to worry about drinking.
records.zomi: Mopawi ni adingin mawngpa khat luah in a man tam zaw a, ahi zongin zu dawn thu kuamah in a lungkham kul kei uh hi.

records.english: Children, choose now whether you want the window or the middle seat, because nobody is swapping halfway.
records.zomi: Naupangte, tukkhuak kiang na deih hiam, a lai tutna na deih hiam tu-in teel un, lam kikal ah kuamah in a kikheel kei ding uh ahih manin.

records.english: Cheap insurance looks attractive until you read how little it covers.
records.zomi: Insurance man neem pen a huam tawmdan na sim ma-in a kilawm bangin a kilang hi.

records.english: Parking a little further away and walking is often quicker than circling the block.
records.zomi: Gamla deuh-ah koih-in kal in inn kimkot ah kihei sangin a manlang zaw zel hi.

records.english: A heavier car feels steadier on the motorway, but it uses more fuel in town.
records.zomi: Mawtaw gik zaw in mawtaw lampi lian tungah a kip zaw bangin a kisa a, ahi zongin khuapi sungah dat a zang tam zaw hi.

records.english: My grandfather always chose the slow lane, even when the fast one was empty.
records.zomi: Ka pu in lampi manlang a awng ciangin zong lampi nuam a teel tawntung hi.

records.english: My brother bought a cheaper car so that he could pay for better insurance.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in insurance hoih zaw a piak theih nadingin mawtaw man neem zaw a lei hi.

records.english: Old photographs show that our grandparents wore traditional clothes on ordinary working days, not only at festivals.
records.zomi: Lim luite in i pu leh pite in pawi ni bek hi lo-in ni simin nasep ni te ah zong ngeina puan a silh uh hi, ci-in a lak hi.

records.english: Weavers often add a small personal mark to their cloth, almost like a signature.
