records.english: Craftsmanship connects us to the people who lived and worked in our villages long before us.
records.zomi: Khutsiamna in i ma-a i khua-a teeng-a nasep sem mite tawh hong kizopsak hi.

records.english: We bought a small saw so that the children could practise woodwork safely.
records.zomi: Naupangte bit taka sing nasep a sin theih nadingin heek neu khat i lei uh hi.

records.english: The bamboo must be cut in the dry season, or insects will get into it.
records.zomi: Gua pen khuakeu hun ah kiat ding a, a kei leh ganhing neuneute in a lut ding uh hi.

records.english: In our village, many families still make their own mats, baskets and tools by hand.
records.zomi: I khua ah innkuan tampi in phah, bawm leh vanzatte khut tawh a bawl lai uh hi.

records.english: My mother had a new handle fitted to her old cooking knife instead of buying a new one.
records.zomi: Ka nu in a namsau thak a lei sangin an huanna namsau lui ah a kaihna thak a bulhsak hi.

records.english: We had the broken chair repaired by a carpenter who still uses wooden pegs instead of nails.
records.zomi: Tutphah kitan khutsiampa sik kilhna sangin sing kilhna zang lai khat in i bawlphatsak uh hi.

records.english: Who made this beautiful wooden box?
records.zomi: Hih sing bawm hoih kua in a bawl hiam?

records.english: Young people sometimes see crafts as old-fashioned until they discover how much skill they require.
records.zomi: Khangnote in khutsiamna a siamna bangzah a kisam hiam a theih ma-un hun lui-a nate bangin a mu zel uh hi.

records.english: With a heated iron rod, my father burned small holes in the wooden handle.
records.zomi: Sik khuam lum tawh ka pa in sing kaihna ah kua neunote a kangsak hi.

records.english: The blacksmith in the next village still makes knives and farming tools by hand.
records.zomi: A kiang khua-a sik seek mi in namsau leh lo vanzatte khut tawh a bawl lai hi.

records.english: Please don't sit on the new mat until the edges have been finished.
records.zomi: A gei te a kizawh ma-in phah thak tungah tu kei in.

records.english: Craft festivals give makers a chance to sell their work and meet each other.
records.zomi: Khutsiamna pawi te in a bawlte a nasep uh zuak nading leh a kimuh nading hun a pia hi.

records.english: Shall I hold the frame while you tie the corners?
records.zomi: A kil te na khih laitakin a bawm kong len ding hiam?

records.english: Making something useful with your own hands brings a satisfaction that buying never does.
records.zomi: Na khut tawh na phatuam khat bawl in lei in a piak ngei loh lungkimna hong pia hi.

records.english: A carrying basket is shaped to fit comfortably on a person's back.
records.zomi: Pua bawm in mi khat' nung tungah nuam takin a kipuak nadingin kibawl hi.

records.english: Patience is the most important tool any craftsman can have.
records.zomi: Thuakzawhna pen khutsiampa khatpeuh in a neih theih vanzat thupi pen ahi hi.

records.english: Fewer young people are learning these crafts, so some families are recording the methods on video.
records.zomi: Khangnote tawmno bek in hih khutsiamnate a sin uh ahih manin innkuan pawl khat in a bawl dante video ah a la uh hi.

records.english: My uncle carves spoons and bowls from wood that has fallen in the forest.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in gam sung-a a puk sing tawh kawm leh kuang a khen hi.

records.english: The village has asked the older craftsmen to teach weekend classes for young people.
records.zomi: Khua in khutsiam upate khangnote adingin kal tawp sinna hilh dingin a ngen hi.

records.english: The children made small baskets at school and gave them to their grandparents.
records.zomi: Naupangte in sang ah bawm neunote a bawl uh a, a pu leh pi uh kiangah a pia uh hi.

records.english: Some crafts are easier to learn from a video, but most still need a patient teacher.
records.zomi: Khutsiamna pawl khat video pan sin a baih zaw a, ahi zongin a tamzaw in thuakzawhna nei hilhpa khat a kisam lai hi.

records.english: The best craftsmen are often the most modest about their skill.
records.zomi: Khutsiampa hoih pente a siamna tungah a kiniamkhiat pen uh a hi zel uh hi.

records.english: You must let the clay dry slowly, or the pot will crack in the fire.
records.zomi: Leinel nuam takin keusak ding a, a kei leh bel meisung ah a kiak ding hi.

records.english: My neighbour weaves hats from palm leaves, which keep the sun off in the fields.
records.zomi: Ka innveng in lo ah ni a khuh lukhu ziing teh tawh a tah hi.

records.english: Splitting bamboo into thin, even strips takes years of practice.
records.zomi: Gua zang leh kibang-a khen in kum tampi kisinna a kisam hi.

records.english: In our community, a new house is often furnished with things that neighbours have made by hand.
records.zomi: I mipi ah inn thak khat innvengte' khut tawh a bawl nate tawh kikoih zel hi.

records.english: Every basket has a slightly different pattern, depending on who made it.
records.zomi: Bawm khempeuh kua in a bawl hiam tungah kinga-in lim tuam deuh a nei hi.

records.english: Do you sell your carvings, or do you make them only for your family?
records.zomi: Na sing khente na zuak hiam, na innkuan adingin bek na bawl hiam?

records.english: Every craftsman in our family has a small mark that they add to their work.
records.zomi: I innkuan-a khutsiampa khempeuh in a nasep uh tungah a behlap ciamtehna neu khat a nei uh hi.

records.english: When will the large basket be finished?
records.zomi: Bawm lian bang hun-in a zo ding hiam?

records.english: In about three days, if the bamboo has already been split and dried.
records.zomi: Gua a kikhen-in a keu khin leh ni thum bang ciangin.

records.english: Rub the wood with oil every few months, so that it doesn't dry out and split.
records.zomi: Sing a keu-in a kiphel loh nadingin kha tawmno simin sathau tawh nul in.

records.english: I'm making a basket for my sister's new baby, so that she has somewhere to keep the blankets.
records.zomi: Ka u numei' naungek thak adingin puante a koih nading mun a neih nadingin bawm khat ka bawl hi.

records.english: Shall we ask your grandfather to show the children how he makes fish traps?
records.zomi: Na pu kiangah ngasa manna bawl dan naupangte lak sak dingin i ngen ding hiam?

records.english: Can you teach me how to start the bottom of a basket?
records.zomi: Bawm' a nuai lam kipatsak dan hong sinsak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Craftsmen in our community often trade their work for food or help on the farm.
records.zomi: I mipi-a khutsiampate in a nasep uh an hiam lo-a huhna tawh a kikheel zel uh hi.

records.english: The rope was made from twisted plant fibres, and it was surprisingly strong.
records.zomi: Khau pen singnah khau kihial tawh kibawl a, lamdang takin a hat hi.

records.english: Thank you for showing us how to make the little bamboo cups.
records.zomi: Gua haai neunote bawl dan hong lak manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: The more you practise, the more even your weaving becomes.
records.zomi: Na kisin tam semsem leh na tah a kibang semsem hi.

records.english: Use the small knife for the fine strips and the big one for cutting the poles.
records.zomi: Zang neute adingin namsau neu zang inla, khuamte atna adingin a lian zang in.

records.english: Look how neatly the edges of this mat have been finished!
records.zomi: Hih phah' a gei te bangzah a kician-in kizo hiam en in!

records.english: My cousin learned pottery from a neighbour and now sells bowls to shops in town.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam in innveng khat kiang pan leibel bawl a sin a, tu-in khuapi-a dawlte kiangah kuang a zuak hi.

records.english: The old man said, "Never rush the last few rows, because that's where a basket shows its quality."
records.zomi: Pasal upa in, “Tawpna-a tuat tawmno nunungte manlang takin bawl ngei kei in, bawm' hoihna tua ah a kilang ahih manin,” a ci hi.

records.english: Good tools are worth looking after, because a blunt knife makes careless work.
records.zomi: Vanzat hoihte kem a phu hi, namsau a hiam lo in nasep a limlo sak ahih manin.

records.english: These wooden plates were each carved from a single piece of wood, without a single join or nail.
records.zomi: Hih sing kuangte khatciat sing tum khat pan kikhen a, kizopna hiam kilhna khat zong om lo hi.

records.english: My aunt made me redo the corner of my first mat three times.
records.zomi: Ka ni in ka phah masa pen' kil vei thum hong bawl kiksak hi.

records.english: When cheap plastic goods arrived in the markets, many local crafts almost disappeared.
records.zomi: Zuakna munte ah plastic van man neemte a tun ciangin mun-a khutsiamna tampi a mang dek hi.

records.english: My grandfather makes baskets from bamboo that he cuts behind the house.
records.zomi: Ka pu in inn nung-a a at gua tawh bawm a bawl hi.

records.english: A sleeping mat woven by my great-aunt is still used in our house today.
records.zomi: Ka pi' u leh nau numei khat' tah lupna phah khat i inn ah tu dong kizang lai hi.

records.english: Are handmade baskets sold at the Saturday market?
records.zomi: Kiginni zuakna mun ah khut tawh bawl bawm kizuak hiam?

records.english: Hold the strip tightly with your thumb while you weave it under the next one.
records.zomi: A zom khat' nuai ah na tah laitakin zang na khutpi tawh kip takin len in.

records.english: Who taught you to carve so beautifully?
records.zomi: Bangzah hoih-in sing khen dingin kua in hong sinsak hiam?

records.english: Is this basket made from bamboo or from rattan?
records.zomi: Hih bawm gua tawh kibawl hiam, rattan tawh kibawl hiam?

records.english: We soak the cane overnight so that it bends without breaking.
records.zomi: A kitan lo-a a kawi theih nadingin rattan zan bup tui sungah i ciah uh hi.

records.english: Craftsmanship is passed down not only through instructions but through years of watching and copying.
records.zomi: Khutsiamna thuhilhna bek tungtawn hi lo-in kum tampi enna leh zuina tungtawnin kipia khia hi.

records.english: We need to collect the grass for the mats before the rains begin.
records.zomi: Guah a zuk kipat ma-in phah adingin lopa i la kisam hi.

records.english: Can I watch you work for a while?
records.zomi: Hun tawmno na nasep ka en thei ding hiam?

records.english: When my grandmother's eyesight weakened, she kept weaving by feeling the strips with her fingers.
records.zomi: Ka pi' mit a hat nawn loh ciangin a khutme tawh zangte khoih-in a tah den hi.

records.english: Can you two come to my graduation, or will it clash with your trip?
records.zomi: Ka sang zawhna ah na nih in na hong pai thei uh ding hiam, na khualzinna tawh a kituah kha ding hiam?

records.english: We'll change our flights, because we wouldn't miss it for anything.
records.zomi: I vanleng i kheel ding uh hi, bangmah adingin a i nusiat nop loh ahih manin.

records.english: When everyone in the family works shifts, even finding time for one meal together takes planning.
records.zomi: Innkuan-a mi khempeuh hun kikheel-in nasep a sep uh ciangin khawm-a an khat nek nading hun zon zong gelna a kisam hi.

records.english: Are you all free for a video call with Grandma on her birthday?
records.zomi: Pi' pianni-in amah tawh video sapna adingin na vekpi-un na awng uh hiam?

records.english: My cousin is free every afternoon this week, so she's offered to help us paint the kitchen.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam numei hih kal sungin nitak lam simin a awng ahih manin an huanna inn zeek dingin hong huh nuam hi.

records.english: Is your daughter available to babysit on Friday?
records.zomi: Na tanu Laithai ni-in naupang kem dingin a awng hiam?

records.english: She has exams next week, so she's only free at weekends.
records.zomi: Kal zom ciangin sitna a nei ahih manin kal tawp ciang bek-in a awng hi.

records.english: Is anyone free to feed the cat while we're away?
records.zomi: I om lo laitakin zawhngeu an vak dingin kuamah a awng hiam?

records.english: Is the cottage still free for the first week of July?
records.zomi: July kha-a kal masa ah inn neu a awng lai hiam?

records.english: Unfortunately, my cousins have already booked it, but the second week is free.
records.zomi: Lungkham huai takin ka sanggamte in a lai khin uh a, ahi zongin kal nihna a awng hi.

records.english: My aunt is never free on Sundays, because she spends the whole day with her grandchildren.
records.zomi: Ka ni Nipini ah a awng ngei kei hi, ni bup a tute tawh a om ahih manin.

records.english: We had to postpone the christening because the godparents weren't free until spring.
records.zomi: Pasian nu leh pate spring dong a awng kei uh ahih manin naungek tuiphumna i sawnsak kul uh hi.

records.english: Before we booked the reunion, my cousin phoned every household to check who could come.
records.zomi: Innkuan kikhopna i lai ma-in ka sanggam in kua a hong pai thei ding hiam en dingin innkuan khempeuh a sam hi.

records.english: Whoever is free on Friday afternoon could help Grandma sort through the boxes she's been meaning to clear for years.
records.zomi: Laithai nitak lam a awng kua peuh in kum tampi a siangsak nop bawmte Pi in a khen nadingin a huh thei hi.

records.english: Are your parents free to visit us in August?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa August kha ah eite hong veh dingin a awng uh hiam?

records.english: They'd love to, but only after my father's operation in July.
records.zomi: A deih mahmah uh hi, ahi zongin July kha-a ka pa' zatui khit ciang bek-in.

records.english: My sister keeps a family calendar on the fridge so that nobody books two things on the same day.
records.zomi: Ka u numei in kuamah in ni kibang ah na nih a lai loh nadingin fridge tungah innkuan calendar khat a kem hi.

records.english: When my grandparents' anniversary fell on a weekday, we moved the celebration to the Saturday so that everyone could come.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh pi' kiteenna kum cinna kal sung ni khat ah a kiat ciangin mi khempeuh a hong pai theih nadingin Kiginni ah lawpna i suan uh hi.

records.english: We moved the family photo to the afternoon, since my brother couldn't get there before lunch.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal sun an ma-in a tung zo lo ahih manin innkuan lim lakna nitak lam ah i suan uh hi.

records.english: Asking relatives about their availability early is a kindness, especially to those who travel far.
records.zomi: Sanggamte kiangah a awng hun uh hun ma-in dot pen hehpihna khat ahi a, a diak in gamla pan a khualzinte adingin.

records.english: Let me check with my wife before I say yes, because she keeps our family calendar and I'm always getting the dates wrong.
records.zomi: Ka ci ma-in ka zi tawh en masa ning, amah in i innkuan calendar a kem a, kei in ni te ka khial tawntung ahih manin.

records.english: Could you find out whether Grandpa still feels well enough to come on Tuesday?
records.zomi: Pu Pithai ni-a hong pai dingin a dam kicing lai hiam na theih thei ding hiam?

records.english: After weeks of messages, my sister finally found a date when all five of us were free, and it was in November.
records.zomi: Kal tampi thu kikhak khit ciangin ka u numei in eite nga khempeuh i awng ni khat a tawpna-ah a mu a, November kha ah ahi hi.

records.english: Checking everyone's availability for a family holiday can take longer than planning the holiday itself.
records.zomi: Innkuan tawlngakni adingin mi khempeuh' awng hun en in tawlngakni gel sangin hun a la zaw thei hi.

records.english: Does Uncle Thomas still have room in his car for two more people?
records.zomi: Pa neu Thomas' mawtaw sungah mi nih adingin mun a om lai hiam?

records.english: Only one, because he's bringing his dog.
records.zomi: Khat bek, a ui a paipih ding ahih manin.

records.english: Is Grandma free to talk, or is she having her afternoon nap?
records.zomi: Pi kihopih dingin a awng hiam, a sun ihmut laitak hiam?

records.english: She's awake, but give her ten minutes to find her glasses.
records.zomi: A khanglawh hi, ahi zongin a mitlimlang a zon nadingin minit sawm pia in.

records.english: Mum, are you free to look after the kids on Saturday night?
records.zomi: Nu aw, Kiginni zan naupangte kem dingin na awng hiam?

records.english: I am, as long as you're back by eleven.
records.zomi: Ka awng hi, nai sawm leh khat ciangin na ciah kik leh.

records.english: Can your sister lend us her high chair while the baby's grandparents are visiting?
records.zomi: Naungek' pu leh pi a hong veh laitakun na u numei in a naungek tutphah sang hong leitawi sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: She'll bring it round on Saturday, because hers is in the loft.
records.zomi: Amah' pen inn tung khan ah a om ahih manin Kiginni ciangin hong tawi ding hi.

records.english: Ask your father whether he can take a day off for your school concert, since he missed the last one because of work.
records.zomi: Na pa nasep hangin a nunung pen a tel lo ahih manin na sang la kikhopna adingin ni khat tawl thei ding hiam dong in.

records.english: Is Grandpa well enough to come to the wedding?
records.zomi: Pu mopawi ah hong pai dingin a dam kicing hiam?

records.english: He says he'll come for the ceremony but leave before the dancing.
records.zomi: Kiteenna pawi adingin a hong pai ding a, lam ma-in a ciah ding hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Most mornings my father is free, but he won't miss his walk with the neighbours.
records.zomi: Zingsang a tamzaw ah ka pa a awng a, ahi zongin a innvengte tawh a kalna a nusia ngei kei hi.

records.english: Do you have time to help me with my homework tonight?
records.zomi: Tu zanin ka inn sinna ah hong huh nading hun na nei hiam?

records.english: After dinner, if you set the table first.
records.zomi: Nitak an khit ciangin, dawhkan na koih masak leh.

records.english: Shall I check whether the restaurant has a table big enough for all of us?
records.zomi: An zuakna inn in eite khempeuh adingin a lian kicing dawhkan a nei hiam ka en ding hiam?

records.english: Are you free to drive me to the airport early on Tuesday?
records.zomi: Pithai ni zingsang tung-in vanlengtual ah hong paipih dingin na awng hiam?

records.english: I'll have to start work late, but yes, I can take you.
records.zomi: Nasep nung deuh-in ka kipat kul ding a, ahi zongin kong paipih thei hi.

records.english: Our family uses a shared online calendar, which has ended most of the arguments about who's free when.
records.zomi: I innkuan in online calendar kihawm khat a zang a, tua in kua bang hun-in a awng hiam kinialna a tamzaw a bei sak hi.

records.english: Is the spare room free next weekend, or is your aunt still staying?
records.zomi: Kal tawp zom ciangin khan awng a awng hiam, na ni a om lai hiam?

records.english: She leaves on Friday, so it's all yours.
records.zomi: Laithai ni-in a pai ding ahih manin nang' a hi ding hi.

records.english: Are you busy this evening, or can we finally talk about the holiday?
records.zomi: Tu nitak na buai hiam, tawlngakni thu a tawpna-ah i kihopih thei ding hiam?

records.english: I'm free after eight, once the kids are in bed.
records.zomi: Naupangte a lupna ah a om khit uh ciangin nai giat khit ciangin ka awng hi.

records.english: Will your brother be around at Christmas, or is he working abroad again?
records.zomi: Na sanggam pasal Christmas ciangin a om ding hiam, gamdang ah nasep a sem kik ding hiam?

records.english: He'll be home for three days, so we're planning everything around those.
records.zomi: Ni thum inn ah a om ding ahih manin tua kiim ah a khempeuh i gel uh hi.

records.english: I checked whether the community hall was free before I invited forty relatives to my father's birthday.
records.zomi: Ka pa' pianni ah sanggam sawmli ka sam ma-in mipi inn a awng hiam ka en hi.

records.english: My brother never answers when we ask about his plans, so we always assume he's coming.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in a gelnate i dot ciangin a dawng ngei lo ahih manin a hong pai ding hi, i ci tawntung uh hi.

records.english: Finding a weekend when the whole family is free gets harder every year as the children grow up.
records.zomi: Naupangte a khan semsem ciangin innkuan bup a awng kal tawp khat zon kum simin a haksa semsem hi.

records.english: Is there any chance your mum could pick up the children from school tomorrow?
records.zomi: Zingciang na nu in naupangte sang pan a la thei ding hiam?

records.english: I'll ask her tonight, but she usually has her dance class on Thursdays.
records.zomi: Tu zanin ka dong ding a, ahi zongin Laizing ni-in a lamna sinna a nei zel hi.

records.english: Will the house be empty while you're away, or is someone staying there?
records.zomi: Na om lo laitakin inn a awng ding hiam, kuamah tua ah a om ding hiam?

records.english: My nephew is house-sitting, so it won't be empty.
records.zomi: Ka tanau in inn a kem ding ahih manin a awng kei ding hi.

records.english: Could you ask your parents whether they're free for lunch next Sunday?
records.zomi: Nipini zom ciangin sun an adingin a awng uh hiam na nu leh na pa dong thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: My mother is so busy since she retired that we have to book her a week in advance.
records.zomi: Ka nu a nasep a tawp pan a buai mahmah ahih manin kal khat ma-in i lai kul uh hi.

records.english: Tell your grandmother we can collect her any time after four.
records.zomi: Nai li khit ciangin bang hun ciangin zong i la thei hi, ci-in na pi gen in.

records.english: Because my parents' diary is always full, we arranged the surprise party for a weekday evening.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa' hun ciamteh laibu a dim tawntung ahih manin lamdang sakna kipahna kal sung nitak khat ah i bawl uh hi.

records.english: When nobody in the family was free to look after the dog, our neighbour kindly took him for the week.
records.zomi: Innkuan-a kuamah ui kem dingin a awng loh ciangin i innveng in kal khat sung a kem hi.

records.english: Can you tell me in a few words what the teacher wrote in your report?
records.zomi: Na report ah saya in bang a gelh hiam kammal tawmno tawh hong gen thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: After every parents' evening, I give my husband a two-minute summary of what the teachers said.
records.zomi: Nu leh pate' nitak kikhopna khempeuh khit ciangin saya te' gen ka pasal kiangah minit nih-in ka tomsak hi.

records.english: Just tell me the main thing: is Grandma coming or not?
records.zomi: A thupi pen bek hong gen in: Pi a hong pai ding hiam, pai lo ding hiam?

records.english: You two can summarise the holiday for Grandpa, and I'll show him the photos.
records.zomi: Na nih in Pu adingin tawlngakni thu na tomsak uh a, kei in lim te ka lak ding hi.

records.english: My grandmother received a long letter about her pension.
records.zomi: Ka pi in a pension tungtang lai sau khat a ngah hi.

records.english: She asked me to read it and tell her what it meant.
records.zomi: Sim-in a khiatna gen dingin hong ngen hi.

records.english: In the end, the whole letter said one thing: her payments would rise in April.
records.zomi: A tawpna-ah lai bup in thu khat bek a gen hi: April kha ciangin a sum a khang ding hi.

records.english: At the end of each week, our children summarise one thing they learned and one thing they enjoyed.
records.zomi: Kal tawp simin i naupangte in a sin uh thu khat leh a nuam sak uh thu khat a tomsak uh hi.

records.english: Our family group chat is so busy that my father asks me for a daily summary.
records.zomi: I innkuan pawl chat a buai mahmah ahih manin ka pa in ni simin a tomna hong ngen hi.

records.english: My daughter summarised the news for her grandmother every morning during the election.
records.zomi: Teelna hun sungin ka tanu in zingsang simin a pi adingin thuthak a tomsak hi.

records.english: My cousin made a one-page summary of our family history for the reunion.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam in innkuan kikhopna adingin i innkuan tangthu' tomna phek khat a bawl hi.

records.english: Our son's teacher sent home a short summary of what the class would study this term.
records.zomi: I tapa' saya in hih sang hun sungin sangkhan in bang a sin ding hiam tomna tomno khat inn ah a khak hi.

records.english: My son's summary of the football match took longer than the match itself.
records.zomi: Ka tapa' bawlung kimawlna tomna in kimawlna sangin hun a la zaw hi.

records.english: Can you give me the short version of what happened at the family meeting?
records.zomi: Innkuan kikhopna ah bang a piang hiam a tom zawk-in hong gen thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: We're selling the farm, but Grandma keeps the house.
records.zomi: Lo i zuak ding uh a, ahi zongin inn Pi in a kem ding hi.

records.english: Could you summarise the school's new rules for me, because the letter is five pages long?
records.zomi: Lai phek nga a sau ahih manin sang' thukham thakte hong tomsak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: When my grandfather tells a story, my grandmother summarises it at the end in case we missed the point.
records.zomi: Ka pu in tangthu a gen ciangin a thupi i nusia kha leh ci-in ka pi in a tawpna ah a tomsak hi.

records.zomi: Tua ahih leh siavuan in Pa tungtang bang a ci taktak hiam?

records.english: In short, his heart is fine, but he needs to walk more and eat less salt.
records.zomi: Tomkim-in, a lungtang a hoih a, ahi zongin a kal tam zaw-a cii a ne tawm zaw kisam hi.

records.english: My son summarised his science project for us at dinner, and we finally understood it.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in nitak an ah a science nasep a tomsak a, a tawpna-ah i thei uh hi.

records.english: My aunt's summaries of family gossip are famous for being short and very funny.
records.zomi: Ka ni' innkuan thu kigen tomnate a tom leh a nuihhuai mahmah manin minthang hi.

records.english: Summarise your day for me in three sentences, and then you can watch television.
records.zomi: Na ni kammal thum tawh hong tomsak inla, tua khit ciangin television na en thei hi.

records.english: When a family member is ill, a short written summary of the latest news saves everyone repeating the same story.
records.zomi: Innkuan mi khat a nat ciangin thuthak nunung kigelh tomna tomno khat in mi khempeuh in tangthu kibang a gen kik den pan a hondoh hi.

records.english: My husband summarised the insurance letter as bad news with a small discount.
records.zomi: Ka pasal in insurance lai man neem neuno nei thu hoih lo ci-in a tomsak hi.

records.english: Can you summarise the instructions for the new washing machine?
records.zomi: Puan sawpna seet thak' zatdan hong tomsak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Did you understand what the bank said, or shall I summarise it for you?
records.zomi: Bank in bang a ci hiam na thei hiam, kong tomsak ding hiam?

records.english: At his retirement party, my father summed up his forty years at the factory in a single sentence.
records.zomi: A nasep tawpna kipahna ah ka pa in factory-a a kum sawmli kammal khat tawh a tomsak hi.

records.english: After the funeral, my uncle summed up our grandfather's life in a few warm, simple words.
records.zomi: Misi vuina khit ciangin ka pa neu in i pu' nuntakna kammal lum leh baih tawmno tawh a tomsak hi.

records.english: What did the plumber say, in brief?
records.zomi: Tuiburi bawlpa in bang a ci hiam, tomkim-in?

records.english: I asked my teenage son to summarise his plans for the evening, and he said, "Out."
records.zomi: Ka tapa tangval neu kiangah a nitak gelnate tomsak dingin ka ngen a, “Pua lam,” a ci hi.

records.english: The ability to summarise clearly is useful in every family that has to deal with forms and letters.
records.zomi: Kician taka tomsak theihna in form leh lai tawh a buai innkuan khempeuh ah a phatuam hi.

records.english: Summarising a family argument fairly is almost impossible when you were part of it.
records.zomi: Innkuan kinialna khat ah na kihel leh dik takin tomsak a haksa mahmah hi.

records.english: My daughter summed up her whole first week at school in one word: tiring.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in sang-a a kal masa bup kammal khat tawh a tomsak hi: gim.

records.english: I summarised the letter from the school in a text so that my husband could read it at work.
records.zomi: Ka pasal in nasep ah a sim theih nadingin sang pan lai text khat ah ka tomsak hi.

records.english: Summarising a difficult conversation in a calm message can stop a family quarrel from growing.
records.zomi: Kihopihna haksa khat thu dai khat ah tomsak in innkuan kinialna a khan loh nadingin a dal thei hi.

records.english: A shared summary of everyone's medicines helped the whole family care for Grandpa.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh' damdawi tomna kihawm khat in innkuan bup in Pu a kem nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: My grandfather's summary of my first job interview was simple: be on time and listen.
records.zomi: Ka nasep kidotna masa pen tungtang ka pu' tomna a baih hi: hun takin tung inla ngaikhia in.

records.english: My mother reads the long letters from the council and tells us only what we need to do.
records.zomi: Ka nu in khuapi office pan lai saute a sim a, i bawl kisam bek hong gen hi.

records.english: In a nutshell, the family reunion will be at our house in August.
records.zomi: Tomkim-in, innkuan kikhopna August kha ah i inn ah om ding hi.

records.english: Who can summarise what we decided about the summer holiday?
records.zomi: Khal tawlngakni tungtang bang i khensat uh hiam kua in a tomsak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Each evening, our son summarises his day for his grandfather over the phone.
records.zomi: Nitak simin i tapa in a pu adingin phone tungah a ni a tomsak hi.

records.english: A summary that leaves out a family member's side of the story can cause real hurt.
records.zomi: Innkuan mi khat' tangthu lang khat nusia tomna khat in natna taktak a piangsak thei hi.

records.english: Summing up the year in our Christmas letter, my mother wrote that we were all healthy and that was enough.
records.zomi: I Christmas lai-ah kum a tomsak ciangin ka nu in i khempeuh i dam uh a, tua a kicing hi, ci-in a gelh hi.

records.english: When I came back from the hospital, I wrote a short summary of the doctor's advice and stuck it on the fridge.
records.zomi: Damdawi inn pan ka ciah kik ciangin siavuan' thuhilhna tomna tomno khat ka gelh a, fridge tungah ka bulh hi.

records.english: After an hour of arguing, my mother summed up the whole disagreement in one sentence, and even the angriest of us laughed.
records.zomi: Nai khat kinial khit ciangin ka nu in kituak lohna bup kammal khat tawh a tomsak a, a heh pen zong a nuih hi.

records.english: A good summary for an elderly relative leaves out the jargon and keeps the dates.
records.zomi: Sanggam upa khat adingin tomna hoih khat in pau haksate a nusia a, nite a kem hi.

records.english: Tell Grandma the main points, not every detail.
records.zomi: Pi kiangah thu khempeuh hi lo-in a thupi pente gen in.

records.english: My brother summarised the whole wedding for our aunt, who couldn't travel.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in khualzin zo lo i ni adingin mopawi bup a tomsak hi.

records.english: When my parents moved abroad, I sent them a weekly summary of family news.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa gamdang ah a pai uh ciangin kal simin innkuan thuthak tomna ka khak hi.

records.english: What's the gist of Auntie's message?
records.zomi: Ni' thu in a lailung bang a ci hiam?

records.english: She's arriving on Monday and wants us to meet her at the station.
records.zomi: Pizing ni-in a tung ding a, dinna ah i muak dingin a deih hi.

records.english: My little sister summarised the story so well that her teacher read it to the class.
records.zomi: Ka nau numei in tangthu hoih mahmah-in a tomsak ahih manin a saya in sangkhan kiangah a sim hi.

records.english: The summary my father wrote of his own life story is only two pages long, yet nothing important seems to be missing.
records.zomi: Ka pa' amah nuntakna tangthu a tomna phek nih bek a sau a, ahi zongin thu thupi khat zong a mang bang lo hi.

records.english: Summarising medical information for a worried family takes both accuracy and gentleness.
records.zomi: Lungkham innkuan khat adingin damdawi thu tomsak in a dikna leh a nemna a nih a kisam hi.

records.english: My sister keeps a notebook summarising each of our mother's hospital appointments.
records.zomi: Ka u numei in i nu' damdawi inn kimuhna khempeuh' tomna lai neu khat ah a kem hi.

records.english: Why do children summarise a film by telling you every single scene?
records.zomi: Bang hangin naupangte in film khat a tomsak uh ciangin a kenkhat khempeuh a gen uh hiam?

records.english: Summarising helps children understand a story, because they must decide what really matters.
records.zomi: Tomsak in naupangte tangthu a theih nadingin a huh hi, a thupi taktak bang ahi hiam a khensat kul uh ahih manin.

records.english: Please summarise the phone call for Mum, because she couldn't hear it properly.
records.zomi: Nu in hoih takin a za zo lo ahih manin phone sapna amah adingin tomsak in.

records.english: My parents summarised their trip in three words: hot, crowded, wonderful.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in a khualzinna kammal thum tawh a tomsak uh hi: a sa, mi tam, nuam mahmah.

records.english: Write me a short summary of the book before you ask for a new one.
records.zomi: Laibu thak na nget ma-in laibu' tomna tomno khat hong gelhsak in.

records.english: Thank you for telling me about the free legal clinic; it helped us a great deal.
records.zomi: Man om lo thukham huhna mun thu hong gen manin ka lungdam hi; hong huh mahmah hi.

records.english: Can I use the computers at the library to apply for a job?
records.zomi: Nasep ngen dingin laibu inn-a computer te ka zang thei ding hiam?

records.english: Is there anywhere nearby where I can get free advice about my debts?
records.zomi: Ka leiba tungtang man om lo thuhilhna ka ngahna kiang lam mun khat a om hiam?

records.english: The advice centre on Market Street has a debt adviser on Tuesday mornings.
records.zomi: Market Street-a thuhilhna inn in Pithai ni zingsang ciangin leiba thuhilhpa khat a nei hi.

records.english: The library's homework club is free and open to every child in the area.
records.zomi: Laibu inn' inn sinna pawl man om lo a, mun-a naupang khempeuh adingin kihong hi.

records.english: The officer said, "If you're not sure which service you need, start at the front desk and we'll guide you."
records.zomi: Office nasempa in, “Koi nasep na kisam hiam na theih kician kei leh mai lam dawhkan ah kipan in, kong lampi lak ding hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: The free swimming lessons for children are paid for by the council.
records.zomi: Naupangte adingin man om lo tuipeek sinna khuapi office in a man a pia hi.

records.english: Is the free bus to the hospital still running on Saturdays?
records.zomi: Damdawi inn lam man om lo bus Kiginni ah a pai lai hiam?

records.english: Our neighbourhood has a free repair café where volunteers fix broken toasters and bicycles.
records.zomi: I mun ah deihsakna nasemte in a siat toaster leh siiksakolte a bawlphatna man om lo bawlphatna cafe khat a om hi.

records.english: Local resources are only useful if the people who need them can actually reach them.
records.zomi: Mun-a huhnate a kisam mite in a tun theih taktak uh leh bek a phatuam hi.

records.english: Ask at the reception desk if you need a translator for your appointment.
records.zomi: Na kimuhna adingin pau lettu na kisam leh kimuakna dawhkan ah dong in.

records.english: Can I borrow a wheelchair from the health centre for a few weeks?
records.zomi: Kal tawmno sung damna inn pan wheelchair khat ka leitawi thei ding hiam?

records.english: Local charities often know about support that even council staff haven't heard of.
records.zomi: Mun-a charity te in khuapi office nasemte zong in a zak ngei loh huhnate a thei zel uh hi.

records.english: Is there a place where students can study quietly in the evenings?
records.zomi: Nitak lam sangnaupangte daitak-a a sinna ding mun khat a om hiam?

records.english: Asking for help with local services is a sign of good sense, not weakness.
records.zomi: Mun-a nasepte tungtang huhna ngen pen pilna lahna hi a, hatlohna hi lo hi.

records.english: Shall I find out whether the leisure centre has cheaper prices for families?
records.zomi: Kipahna inn in innkuante adingin man neem zaw a nei hiam ka zong ding hiam?

records.english: The library also offers free help with filling in official forms.
records.zomi: Laibu inn in kumpi form te dim nading huhna man om lo zong a pia hi.

records.english: When our washing machine broke, the community centre let us use theirs for a week.
records.zomi: I puan sawpna seet a siat ciangin mipi inn in kal khat sung amaute' a zangsak hi.

records.english: We found a free legal clinic by asking at the town hall.
records.zomi: Khuapi inn ah dot tungtawnin man om lo thukham huhna mun khat i mu uh hi.

records.english: Free parenting classes are held at the children's centre every Thursday.
records.zomi: Naupangte' inn ah Laizing ni simin man om lo nu leh pa sinna kibawl hi.

records.english: Older residents can get help with shopping through a volunteer service.
records.zomi: Mi upa teeng mite in deihsakna nasep tungtawnin van lei huhna a ngah thei uh hi.

records.english: Can anyone use the free outdoor gym in the park?
records.zomi: Huan sung-a man om lo pua lam gym kuamah in a zang thei hiam?

records.english: Many local resources are run entirely by volunteers who give their time for nothing.
records.zomi: Mun-a huhna tampi in a hun uh man om lo-in a pia deihsakna nasemte bek in a kem uh hi.

records.english: Children mustn't use the library's computers without a parent's permission.
records.zomi: Nu hiam pa' phalna om lo-in naupangte in laibu inn' computer te a zang kei ding uh hi.

records.english: My mother uses the free hearing-aid repair service at the health centre.
records.zomi: Ka nu in damna inn-a man om lo bil zak huhna bawlphatna a zang hi.

records.english: You must book a place on the free first-aid course at least a week in advance.
records.zomi: Man om lo khatvei damna huh sinna ah a tawm pen kal khat ma-in mun na lai kisam hi.

records.english: The food bank asks visitors to bring a referral letter from a doctor or social worker.
records.zomi: An piakna inn in hong vehte siavuan hiam social worker pan lai khat tawi dingin a ngen hi.

records.english: Who should I call if my elderly neighbour needs help at home?
records.zomi: Ka innveng upa in inn ah huhna a kisam leh kua ka sam ding hiam?

records.english: You can collect free sandbags from the depot before a storm.
records.zomi: Huihpi ma-in van koihna mun pan man om lo leivui ip na la thei hi.

records.english: A good local website explains services in plain language and keeps opening hours up to date.
records.zomi: Mun-a website hoih khat in nasepte pau baih tawh a genteh a, kihonna hunte a thaksak den hi.

records.english: Do you know whether the tool library is open on Sundays?
records.zomi: Vanzat leitawina inn Nipini ah a kihong hiam na thei hiam?

records.english: If the library can't answer your question, the staff will usually know who can.
records.zomi: Laibu inn in na dotna a dawng zo kei leh nasemte in kua in a dawng thei hiam a thei zel uh hi.

records.english: A newcomer to a town often relies on neighbours to learn which services are worth using.
records.zomi: Khuapi khat-a hong tung thak in koi nasepte zat a phu hiam theih nadingin a innvengte tungah a kinga zel hi.

records.english: Our neighbourhood noticeboard is the quickest way to learn what's happening locally.
records.zomi: I mun-a thuzaksak phek in mun ah bang a piang hiam theih nading manlang pen ahi hi.

records.english: Where can I find out what help is available for new parents?
records.zomi: Nu leh pa thakte adingin bang huhna a om hiam koi ah ka thei thei ding hiam?

records.english: Ask at the health centre, or look at the noticeboard in the library.
records.zomi: Damna inn ah dong in, hiam laibu inn-a thuzaksak phek en in.

records.english: Local museums are free for residents on the first Sunday of every month.
records.zomi: Mun-a museum te kha simin Nipini masa ah teeng mite adingin man om lo hi.

records.english: A free directory of local services is delivered to every home once a year.
records.zomi: Mun-a nasepte' min laibu man om lo kum khat ah vei khat inn khempeuh ah kitunsak hi.

records.english: A short phone call to the right office can save hours of searching online.
records.zomi: Office dik khat ah phone sapna tomno khat in online-a zon nai tampi a khol thei hi.

records.english: Our town has a tool library where you can borrow a drill instead of buying one.
records.zomi: I khuapi in drill lei sangin na leitawi theihna vanzat leitawina inn khat a nei hi.

records.english: The council offers free bins for garden waste if you register online.
records.zomi: Online-in na kigelh leh khuapi office in huan eek koihna bawm man om lo a pia hi.

records.english: Where's the nearest place to recycle old batteries?
records.zomi: Battery lui te zat kik nadingin a nai pen mun koi ah a om hiam?

records.english: The council had information leaflets printed in five languages so that more residents could read them.
records.zomi: Teeng mi tam zaw in a sim theih nadingin khuapi office in thuhilhna lai neute pau nga tawh a khetsak hi.

records.english: Some families miss out on support because the forms are only available online.
records.zomi: Form te online bek ah a om ahih manin innkuan pawl khat in huhna a mansuah uh hi.

records.english: You need proof of address to register for most local services.
records.zomi: Mun-a nasep a tamzaw adingin kigelh nadingin teenna mun lakna na kisam hi.

records.english: Many people never use local services simply because nobody has told them they exist.
records.zomi: Mi tampi in a om uh hi, ci-in kuamah in a gen loh manin mun-a nasepte a zang ngei kei uh hi.

records.english: The community garden gives free plots to families who don't have their own land.
records.zomi: Mipi huan in amau' gam nei lo innkuante man om lo huan mun a pia hi.

records.english: Please don't throw away old clothes; the charity shop on the corner will take them.
records.zomi: Puan luite paikhia kei in; kil-a charity dawl in a la ding hi.

records.english: Information about local resources should reach people where they already are, such as schools and clinics.
records.zomi: Mun-a huhna tungtang thu sang leh clinic bang mite a om khinna mun ah tung ding hi.

records.english: Accessing help can be hard for people who work long hours, since many offices close at five.
records.zomi: Office tampi nai nga ciangin a kikhak ahih manin nai sau nasep sem mite adingin huhna ngah a haksa thei hi.

records.english: Free eye tests are available for children and people over sixty.
records.zomi: Naupangte leh kum sawmguk tung mite adingin man om lo mit sitna a om hi.

records.english: Does the job centre still run free workshops on writing a CV?
records.zomi: Nasep zonna inn in CV gelh dan tungtang man om lo sinna a nei lai hiam?

records.english: Using the council's app, I reported the broken street light in two minutes.
records.zomi: Khuapi office' app zang-in lampi meivaak siat minit nih sungin ka gen hi.

records.english: Making the most of local resources can make a small income stretch much further.
records.zomi: Mun-a huhnate hoih takin zat in sum ngah tawmno a sawt zaw mahmah sak thei hi.

records.english: I didn't know about the energy advice service until a neighbour mentioned it.
records.zomi: Innveng khat in a gen ma-in meivaak man thuhilhna nasep ka thei kei hi.

records.english: The free nappy exchange at the children's centre saves young families a lot of money.
records.zomi: Naupangte' inn-a man om lo naungek puan kikheelna in innkuan khangnote sum tampi a khol sak hi.

records.english: The town map at the station shows where the public toilets and drinking fountains are.
records.zomi: Dinna-a khuapi map in mipi ek inn leh tui dawnna munte koi ah a om hiam a lak hi.

records.english: The free cycling lessons helped my father feel confident on the road again.
records.zomi: Man om lo siiksakol tuang sinna in ka pa lampi tungah kimuang kik dingin a huh hi.

records.english: The council's website lists every free service available to residents.
records.zomi: Khuapi office' website in teeng mite adingin man om lo nasep khempeuh a lak hi.

records.english: Local resources work best when the organisations that run them talk to one another.
records.zomi: Mun-a huhnate a kem pawlte a kihopih uh ciangin a hoih pen-in a sem hi.

records.english: Should we invite everyone at once or have two smaller dinners?
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh khatvei-in i sam ding hiam, nitak an neu nih i bawl ding hiam?

records.english: Two smaller dinners, so that we can actually talk to people.
records.zomi: Nitak an neu nih, mite tawh i kihopih taktak theih nadingin.

records.english: We decided to host the party at the community hall, because our flat is too small for thirty people.
records.zomi: I inn mi sawmthum adingin a neu lua ahih manin kipahna mipi inn ah bawl dingin i khensat uh hi.

records.english: Do you think it's rude to ask guests to bring their own drinks?
records.zomi: Mikhualte amau' dawn ding tawi dingin ngen a zahtak lo ding na ci hiam?

records.english: Do you think the guests would prefer a walk after lunch or a game of cards?
records.zomi: Mikhualte in sun an khit ciangin pai vialvial a deih zaw ding uh hiam, card kimawl a deih zaw ding uh hiam na ci hiam?

records.english: Sharing the hosting between three families makes the holidays less exhausting for everyone.
records.zomi: Innkuan thum kikal-ah mikhual dawn kihawm in mi khempeuh adingin tawlngakni a gim tawm zawsak hi.

records.english: Whichever way you host, a warm welcome at the door matters most.
records.zomi: Koi bangin mikhual na dawng zongin kongkhak-a muakna lum a thupi pen hi.

records.english: A small, cosy gathering suits my grandparents better than a big noisy party.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh pi adingin kipahna lian aw ngaih sangin kikhopna neu nuam khat a kilawm zaw hi.

records.english: Hiring a caterer costs more, but it means the host can enjoy the party too.
records.zomi: An bawl mi luah in a man tam zaw a, ahi zongin mikhual dawnpa in zong kipahna a nuam sa thei hi cihna hi.

records.english: Cooking everything yourself is impressive, but asking guests to bring a dish makes the evening more relaxed.
records.zomi: A khempeuh nangmah mah in huan a lamdang a, ahi zongin mikhualte an khat tawi dingin ngen in nitak a nuamsak zaw hi.

records.english: A guest who offers to help in the kitchen should usually be allowed to, at least a little.
records.zomi: An huanna inn ah huh dingin a kipia mikhual khat a tamzaw-in tawmno phal ding hi.

records.english: Inviting guests by phone takes longer, but it feels far warmer than a group message that half of them will never read.
records.zomi: Phone tawh mikhual sam in hun sawt zaw a la a, ahi zongin a langkhat in a sim ngei lo ding pawl thu sangin a lum zaw mahmah hi.

records.english: Should I put the children at their own table or mix them in with the adults?
records.zomi: Naupangte amau' dawhkan ah ka tutsak ding hiam, mi upate tawh ka kihel sak ding hiam?

records.english: My father had us move the big table into the living room so that everyone could sit together.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh khawm-a a tut theih nadingin ka pa in dawhkan lian tutna khan ah hong suansak hi.

records.english: Do you prefer guests who arrive early or exactly on time?
records.zomi: Hun ma-a tung mikhualte na deih zaw hiam, hun taktak-a tungte na deih zaw hiam?

records.english: Shall I serve the drinks, or will you?
records.zomi: Dawn ding ka pia ding hiam, nang in na pia ding hiam?

records.english: Some families host every holiday at the same house, while others move from house to house each year.
records.zomi: Innkuan pawl khat in tawlngakni khempeuh inn kibang ah a bawl uh a, a dangte in kum simin inn khat pan inn khat ah a suan uh hi.

records.english: Hosting at home is cheaper than booking a restaurant, though it means much more washing up.
records.zomi: Inn ah mikhual dawn in an zuakna inn lai sangin a man neem zaw a, ahi zongin sil ding a tam zaw mahmah hi.

records.english: A host should never make a guest feel that they've eaten too much or too little.
records.zomi: Mikhual dawnpa in mikhual khat a ne tam lua hiam a ne tawm lua hiam bangin a kisak sak ngei kei ding hi.

records.english: Do you two want to sleep in the spare room or on the sofa bed?
records.zomi: Na nih in khan awng ah na ihmu nuam uh hiam, sofa lupna tungah hiam?

records.english: A long lunch gives guests time to relax, while a quick dinner suits people who work the next day.
records.zomi: Sun an sau in mikhualte tawl nading hun a pia a, nitak an manlang in a zing nasep sem mite adingin a kilawm hi.

records.english: Our neighbours always host on Saturdays, while we prefer Sunday afternoons.
records.zomi: I innvengte Kiginni ah mikhual a dawng tawntung uh a, eite in Nipini nitak lam i deih zaw uh hi.

records.english: We let our guests choose between the guest room and a hotel nearby, and they chose to stay with us.
records.zomi: I mikhualte mikhual khan leh a kiang-a zinbuuk kikal-ah teel dingin i phal uh a, eite tawh om dingin a teel uh hi.

records.english: A host who is relaxed makes the guests relaxed too, which matters far more than whether the food turns out perfectly.
records.zomi: Lungnuam mikhual dawnpa in mikhualte zong a lungnuamsak a, tua in an a kicing-in a pian leh sangin a thupi zaw mahmah hi.

records.english: I'd rather invite fewer people and look after them properly.
records.zomi: Mi tawm zaw sam-in hoih takin kem ka deih zaw hi.

records.english: If the weather is good, we'll eat outside; if not, we'll squeeze round the kitchen table.
records.zomi: Huihkhua a hoih leh pua lam ah i ne ding a, a hoih kei leh an huanna inn-a dawhkan kiim ah kinek-in i tu ding hi.

records.english: Inviting the new neighbours for coffee was easier than waiting for them to introduce themselves.
records.zomi: Innveng thakte coffee adingin sam in amaute a kitheisak ding ngak sangin a baih zaw hi.

records.english: Inviting the neighbours as well as family turned a small dinner into a real celebration.
records.zomi: Innkuan bek hi lo-in innvengte zong sam in nitak an neu khat kipahna taktak ah a kheel hi.

records.english: A spare toothbrush and a clean towel can make an overnight guest feel very welcome.
records.zomi: Ha sitna behlap khat leh puan nawtna siangtho khat in zan giak mikhual khat a kimuak mahmah bangin a kisak sak thei hi.

records.english: Is it better to plan every detail or keep things simple when guests come?
records.zomi: Mikhualte a hong pai ciangin a khempeuh gel a hoih zaw hiam, a baih-in kem a hoih zaw hiam?

records.english: Keep it simple, because guests remember the welcome more than the menu.
records.zomi: A baih-in kem in, mikhualte in an min lai sangin muakna a phawk zaw uh ahih manin.

records.english: We chose a weekend lunch rather than a dinner, so that the children could join us.
records.zomi: Naupangte zong a kihel theih nadingun nitak an sangin kal tawp sun an i teel uh hi.

records.english: When you host people from different backgrounds, a mix of familiar and new dishes usually works best.
records.zomi: Mi tuamtuam pan hong pai mite na dawn ciangin an theih khin leh an thakte kihel in a hoih pen zel hi.

records.english: We chose a quiet Friday evening for the dinner, so that nobody would be rushing to another event.
records.zomi: Kuamah kikhopna dang ah a manlang loh nadingin nitak an adingin Laithai nitak dai khat i teel uh hi.

records.english: Shall we eat in the garden or inside?
records.zomi: Huan sungah i ne ding hiam, inn sungah hiam?

records.english: When guests have small children, a house with a garden is a better choice than a flat.
records.zomi: Mikhualte in naupang neu a neih uh ciangin huan nei inn khat in teelna hoih zaw ahi hi.

records.english: Would you rather host the party or help with the cooking at your sister's?
records.zomi: Kipahna na bawl nuam zaw hiam, na u numei' inn ah an huan na huh nuam zaw hiam?

records.english: Hiring extra chairs was cheaper than buying them for one party.
records.zomi: Kipahna khat adingin tutphah behlap luah in lei sangin a man neem zaw hi.

records.english: Hosting a family gathering at Grandma's means she doesn't have to travel, but it also tires her out.
records.zomi: Pi' inn ah innkuan kikhopna bawl in amah a khualzin kul kei a, ahi zongin a gimsak zong hi.

records.english: We let the children decide which games to play when their cousins visited.
records.zomi: A sanggamte a hong veh uh ciangin bang kimawlna kimawl ding hiam naupangte i khensatsak uh hi.

records.english: Hosting for one night is easy, but having guests for a whole week takes planning, patience and a very full fridge.
records.zomi: Zan khat mikhual dawn a baih a, ahi zongin kal bup mikhual neih in gelna, thuakzawhna leh an dim fridge khat a kisam hi.

records.english: A simple soup served warmly can feel more generous than an expensive meal served in a hurry.
records.zomi: Lum taka kipia an tui baih khat in manlang taka kipia an man tam sangin a deihsakhuai zaw thei hi.

records.english: Preparing the food the day before means less stress, although some dishes are better fresh.
records.zomi: A zan ma-in an bawl in lungkhamna a tawmsak a, ahi zongin an pawl khat a thak-in a hoih zaw hi.

records.english: Paper plates save time, but my mother insists on real ones for guests.
records.zomi: Lai kuang in hun a khol a, ahi zongin ka nu in mikhualte adingin kuang taktak a ngen den hi.

records.english: A buffet is easier for a big group, but a sit-down meal feels more special.
records.zomi: Buffet in mi tam adingin a baih zaw a, ahi zongin tu-a an nek in a tuam zaw hi.

records.english: A themed party is fun for children, but adults usually prefer good food and conversation.
records.zomi: Thupi khat tawh kibawl kipahna naupangte adingin a nuam a, ahi zongin mi upate in an hoih leh kihopihna a deih zaw zel uh hi.

records.english: Tea in the garden is lovely, but if it rains, we'll move everyone into the kitchen.
records.zomi: Huan sungah niangtui a nuam a, ahi zongin guah a zuk leh mi khempeuh an huanna inn ah i suan ding hi.

records.english: Fresh flowers or candles on the table?
records.zomi: Dawhkan tungah pak thak hiam khawimeivaak hiam?

records.english: Candles, but only if nobody knocks them over.
records.zomi: Khawimeivaak, kuamah in a pai kiaksak kei leh bek.

records.english: Should we put the board games out before the guests arrive?
records.zomi: Mikhualte a tun ma-un dawhkan kimawlnate i koih ding hiam?

records.english: Some hosts like to cook while the guests watch, whereas others prefer everything ready before anyone arrives.
records.zomi: Mikhual dawnpa pawl khat in mikhualte a et laitakin an huan a deih uh a, a dangte in kuamah a tun ma-in a khempeuh kigin khin a deih zaw uh hi.

records.english: I'd sooner have guests stay too long than leave too early.
records.zomi: Mikhualte hun ma-a a pai sangin a om sawt lua uh ka deih zaw hi.

records.english: Would your parents prefer to stay with us or in a hotel?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa eite tawh om a deih zaw ding uh hiam, zinbuuk ah hiam?

records.english: We switched from formal dinners to relaxed barbecues, and our friends seem much happier.
records.zomi: Nitak an kizahtak pan nuam taka sa halna kikhopna ah i kheel uh a, i lawmte a lungdam zaw mahmah uh hi.

records.english: Our guests really did enjoy the simple village food more than the restaurant meal.
records.zomi: I mikhualte in an zuakna inn an sangin khua an baih a nuam sa zaw taktak uh hi.

records.english: Choosing a date for a family gathering is harder than choosing the menu.
records.zomi: Innkuan kikhopna adingin ni teel in an min lai teel sangin a haksa zaw hi.

records.english: Background music is pleasant, but it shouldn't be so loud that guests have to shout.
records.zomi: Nung lam la a nuam a, ahi zongin mikhualte a kikou kul dong-in a ging lua kei ding hi.

records.english: Next time, let's invite fewer people and cook one thing really well.
records.zomi: A zom vei ciangin mi tawm zaw sam-in an khat hoih takin huan ni.

records.english: My aunt prefers to visit others rather than host, because her flat is so small.
records.zomi: Ka ni in a inn a neu lua ahih manin mikhual dawn sangin mi dangte veh a deih zaw hi.

records.english: Shall we buy dessert from the bakery or make it ourselves?
records.zomi: An khit-a ne ding moh bawlna dawl pan i lei ding hiam, eimau mah in i bawl ding hiam?

records.english: What do you think the disciples did after Jesus had gone?
records.zomi: Jesu a pai khit ciangin nungzuite in bang a bawl uh ding na ci hiam?

records.english: Different churches understand the return of Christ in quite different ways.
records.zomi: Pawlpi tuamtuamte in Khazih' hong kumsuk kikna tuamtuam-in a thei uh hi.

records.english: Hope in Christ's return has helped many persecuted believers endure suffering.
records.zomi: Khazih' hong kumsuk kikna lametna in bawlsiat thuak upmi tampi thuakna a thuakzawh nadingun a huh hi.

records.english: According to the book of Acts, the disciples watched as a cloud hid Jesus from their sight.
records.zomi: Sawltakte Thu laibu bangin meii khat in Jesu a muh lohna dingun a liah laitakin nungzuite in a en uh hi.

records.english: Many believers say that the return of Christ is a reason to care for others now, not to wait idly.
records.zomi: Upmi tampi in Khazih' hong kumsuk kikna pen daidai-a ngak ding hi lo-in tu-in mi dangte kem nading hang khat ahi hi, a ci uh hi.

records.english: The ascension and the return of Christ are linked in the creed that many churches recite.
records.zomi: Van ah kilatona leh Khazih' hong kumsuk kikna pawlpi tampi' sim upna thugen ah kizom hi.

records.english: The ascension reminds believers that Jesus is no longer limited to one place.
records.zomi: Van ah kilatona in Jesu mun khat bek ah kikhih nawn lo hi, ci-in upmite a phawksak hi.

records.english: Some Christians speak of the return of Christ with joy, while others feel more awe than comfort.
records.zomi: Khristian pawl khat in Khazih' hong kumsuk kikna lungdamna tawh a gen uh a, a dangte in hehnepna sangin launa a kisa zaw uh hi.

records.english: Can you tell me what Christians mean by the second coming?
records.zomi: Khristiante in a nihvei hong pai cih in bang a ci nopna uh hiam hong gen thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: They mean the return of Jesus at the end of time, which they believe will put all things right.
records.zomi: Hun tawpna-a Jesu' hong kumsuk kikna a ci nopna uh ahi a, tua in na khempeuh a dikin a bawl ding hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: Who saw Jesus go up into heaven?
records.zomi: Jesu van ah a kilato kua in a mu hiam?

records.english: Our youth group studied the ascension story with a map of Jerusalem and the Mount of Olives.
records.zomi: I khangno pawl in Jerusalem leh Oliv mual map tawh van ah kilatona tangthu a sin uh hi.

records.english: Every year, our village church walks up the hill behind the church on Ascension Day.
records.zomi: Kum simin i khua pawlpi in Ascension Day ni-in pawlpi nung-a mual tungah a kah uh hi.

records.english: Our pastor used a stained-glass window in the church to explain the ascension to the children.
records.zomi: I pastor in naupangte kiangah van ah kilatona genteh dingin pawlpi-a lim nei tukkhuak khat a zang hi.

records.english: We sang an old hymn about Christ's return at the end of the service.
records.zomi: Kikhopna tawpna ah Khazih' hong kumsuk kikna tungtang la lui khat i sa uh hi.

records.english: The children drew pictures of the disciples looking up at the sky.
records.zomi: Naupangte in van lam a en nungzuite lim a zeek uh hi.

records.english: Ten days after Ascension Day, many churches celebrate Pentecost.
records.zomi: Ascension Day khit ni sawm ciangin pawlpi tampi in Pentecost a lawp uh hi.

records.english: My grandmother says she prays every evening as if Christ might return tomorrow.
records.zomi: Ka pi in Khazih zingciang hong kumsuk kik kha ding bangin nitak simin thu a ngen hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Does your church hold a service on Ascension Day?
records.zomi: Na pawlpi in Ascension Day ni-in kikhopna a nei hiam?

records.english: Is it true that the disciples asked Jesus whether he would restore the kingdom to Israel?
records.zomi: Nungzuite in Jesu kiangah Israel' gam a uksak kik ding hiam a dong uh hi, cih a dik hiam?

records.english: When Grandpa was dying, he said he was ready to meet Christ.
records.zomi: Pu a sih dek ciangin Khazih a kimuh dingin a kiginkhol khin hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Christians in the early church expected Jesus to return very soon.
records.zomi: Pawlpi masa-a Khristiante in Jesu manlang mahmah-in a hong kumsuk kik ding a lamen uh hi.

records.english: Theologians have written a great deal about what the ascension means for the presence of Christ today.
records.zomi: Pasian thu siamte in van ah kilatona in tu-a Khazih' omna adingin bang ci nopna a nei hiam tampi a gelh uh hi.

records.english: We read the ascension story aloud in three languages at the service.
records.zomi: Kikhopna ah van ah kilatona tangthu pau thum tawh aw ngaih takin i sim uh hi.

records.english: The Sunday school children acted out the ascension with a white sheet for the cloud.
records.zomi: Nipini sang naupangte in meii adingin puan kang khat zang-in van ah kilatona a lak uh hi.

records.english: The pastor said, "We don't need to know the date; we need to live faithfully every day."
records.zomi: Pastor in, “Ni i theih kul kei a; ni simin muanhuai takin i nungta kul hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: The disciples went back to Jerusalem after the ascension, according to Luke.
records.zomi: Luka bangin van ah kilatona khit ciangin nungzuite Jerusalem ah a ciah kik uh hi.

records.english: Many Christians believe that Jesus now reigns with God the Father.
records.zomi: Khristian tampi in Jesu tu-in Pa Pasian tawh a uk hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: Christians believe that, forty days after the resurrection, Jesus was taken up into heaven.
records.zomi: Khristiante in thawhkikna khit ni sawmli ciangin Jesu van ah a kilato hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: The return of Christ is a theme in many of the hymns we sing during Advent.
records.zomi: Khazih' hong kumsuk kikna pen Advent sungin i sak la tampi-a thupi khat ahi hi.

records.english: Believers in our church greet each other warmly on Ascension Day.
records.zomi: I pawlpi-a upmite Ascension Day ni-in lum takin a kihopih uh hi.

records.english: Please don't frighten the children with stories about the end of the world.
records.zomi: Leitung bei ding tungtang tangthute tawh naupangte lausak kei un.

records.english: Some groups have tried to predict the date of Christ's return, and every prediction has been wrong.
records.zomi: Pawl pawl khat in Khazih' hong kumsuk kikna ni a gen khol sawm uh a, a gen khol khempeuh a khial hi.

records.english: Ascension Day is less widely celebrated than Christmas or Easter, even though it matters deeply in Christian belief.
records.zomi: Ascension Day pen Khristian upna ah thupi mahmah hangin Christmas hiam Easter sangin tawm zaw-in kilawp hi.

records.english: Shall we read the end of Luke's Gospel together tonight?
records.zomi: Tu zanin Luka' Lungdamna Thu' tawpna khawmin i sim ding hiam?

records.english: Many Christians believe that Jesus will one day return.
records.zomi: Khristian tampi in Jesu ni khat hong kumsuk kik ding hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: The church bells rang at noon on Ascension Day.
records.zomi: Ascension Day sun lai ciangin pawlpi khawngte a ging hi.

records.english: Some believers find comfort in the idea that Christ will return to judge the world fairly.
records.zomi: Upmi pawl khat in Khazih leitung dik taka thukhen dingin hong kumsuk kik ding hi, cih ngaihsutna ah hehnepna a mu uh hi.

records.english: Ascension Day always falls on a Thursday, forty days after Easter.
records.zomi: Ascension Day Easter khit ni sawmli ciangin Laizing ni ah a kia tawntung hi.

records.english: Mum, did Jesus take a plane to heaven?
records.zomi: Nu aw, Jesu vanleng tawh van ah a pai hiam?

records.english: Why did the disciples keep looking up at the sky?
records.zomi: Bang hangin nungzuite van lam a en den uh hiam?

records.english: Do you think the end of the world is something to fear?
records.zomi: Leitung bei ding pen lauhuai khat ahi ding na ci hiam?

records.english: In the book of Acts, two men in white tell the disciples that Jesus will come back in the same way.
records.zomi: Sawltakte Thu laibu ah puan kang silh mi nih in nungzuite kiangah Jesu tua bang mah-in hong kumsuk kik ding hi, a ci uh hi.

records.english: Is Ascension Day a public holiday in your country?
records.zomi: Na gam ah Ascension Day mipi tawlngakni ahi hiam?

records.english: Yes, and many families use the long weekend for trips.
records.zomi: Hi, innkuan tampi in kal tawp sau khualzinna adingin a zang uh hi.

records.english: Where in the Bible is the ascension described?
records.zomi: Laisiangtho ah koi lai ah van ah kilatona kigen hiam?

records.english: Did the disciples feel sad or hopeful when Jesus left them?
records.zomi: Jesu in a nusiat ciangin nungzuite a lungkham uh hiam, lametna a nei uh hiam?

records.english: For some believers, the return of Christ means the final healing of a broken world.
records.zomi: Upmi pawl khat adingin Khazih' hong kumsuk kikna in leitung kitan' a tawpna-a damna cihna hi.

records.english: Christians believe that the ascension was not the end of Jesus' work but a new beginning.
records.zomi: Khristiante in van ah kilatona pen Jesu' nasep tawpna hi lo-in kipatna thak ahi hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: Christians often pray, "Come, Lord Jesus," a prayer found at the end of the Bible.
records.zomi: Khristiante in Laisiangtho' tawpna-a om thungetna, “Topa Jesu aw, hong pai ta in,” ci-in thu a ngen zel uh hi.

records.english: What is Ascension Day?
records.zomi: Ascension Day bang hiam?

records.english: It's the day when many churches remember Jesus being taken up into heaven.
records.zomi: Pawlpi tampi in Jesu van ah a kilato a phawk uh ni ahi hi.

records.english: Christians often say the words "He will come again" when they recite their creed together.
records.zomi: Khristiante in a upna thugen khawm a sim uh ciangin “Hong pai kik ding hi” cih kammal a gen zel uh hi.

records.english: The return of Christ is described in the Bible with images such as clouds, trumpets and light.
records.zomi: Laisiangtho in Khazih' hong kumsuk kikna meii, peengkul leh vaak bang limte tawh a gen hi.

records.english: When will Jesus come back?
records.zomi: Jesu bang hun-in hong pai kik ding hiam?

records.english: The Gospels say that nobody knows the day or the hour.
records.zomi: Lungdamna Thu te in kuamah in tua ni leh nai a thei kei uh hi, a ci hi.

records.english: You mustn't laugh at people whose beliefs about the end times are different from yours.
records.zomi: Hun tawpna tungtang na upna tawh kibang lo mite na nuihsan kei ding hi.

records.english: According to Acts, the disciples were told to wait in Jerusalem for the Holy Spirit.
records.zomi: Sawltakte Thu bangin nungzuite Kha Siangtho ngak dingin Jerusalem ah om dingin kisawl hi.

records.english: For many believers, the hope of Christ's return gives them strength in difficult times.
records.zomi: Upmi tampi adingin Khazih' hong kumsuk kikna lametna in hun haksa ah thahatna a pia hi.

records.english: Children, today we're going to talk about why the disciples looked up at the sky.
records.zomi: Naupangte, tuni-in bang hangin nungzuite van lam a en uh hiam i kihopih ding hi.

records.english: Admitting to your children that you're unsure about something can teach them that uncertainty is normal.
records.zomi: Na tate kiangah thu khat na theih kician loh na pom in theih kician lohna pen a ngeina ahi hi, ci-in a hilh thei hi.

records.english: I'm not certain, but I think my great-grandparents came from a village in the north.
records.zomi: Ka thei kician kei a, ahi zongin ka pu leh pi' nu leh pate mal lam khua khat pan hong pai uh hi, ka sa hi.

records.english: My daughter still can't decide between medicine and music, and every time someone gives her advice, she changes her mind again.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in damdawi sinna leh la sinna kikal-ah a khensat zo lai kei a, mi khat in thuhilhna a piak vei khempeuh-in a ngaihsutna a kheel kik hi.

records.english: Is Grandma coming for Christmas this year?
records.zomi: Tu kum Christmas ciangin Pi hong pai ding hiam?

records.english: I'm not sure yet, because it depends on how her knee is.
records.zomi: Ka thei nai kei hi, a khuk dan tungah a kinga ahih manin.

records.english: My grandmother isn't sure whether she wants to move in with us or stay in her own flat.
records.zomi: Ka pi in eite tawh hong teeng ding hiam, amah' inn ah om ding hiam a theih kician kei hi.

records.english: Will you be moving back home after university?
records.zomi: Sangpi khit ciangin inn ah na ciah kik ding hiam?

records.english: I don't know yet; it depends on where I find work.
records.zomi: Ka thei nai kei hi; koi ah nasep ka ngah hiam tungah a kinga hi.

records.english: My son isn't sure whether he wants a big party or just a few friends.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in kipahna lian hiam lawm tawmno bek hiam a deih a thei kician kei hi.

records.english: Whether my son will pass his driving test this time is anyone's guess.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in tu vei-in mawtaw mawng sitna a zo ding hiam kuamah in a thei kei hi.

records.english: Was Grandpa really a sailor when he was young?
records.zomi: Pu a khangno lai-in tembaw mawngpa taktak ahi hiam?

records.english: So he says, but nobody in the family has ever seen proof.
records.zomi: Amah in tua bangin a ci a, ahi zongin innkuan sungah kuamah in lakna a mu ngei kei uh hi.

records.english: When a family member is seriously ill, living with uncertainty can be harder than hearing bad news.
records.zomi: Innkuan mi khat a nat gik ciangin theih kician lohna tawh nungta in thu hoih lo zak sangin a haksa zaw thei hi.

records.english: Parents often feel they should have every answer, but saying 'I don't know yet' can be more honest.
records.zomi: Nu leh pate in dotna khempeuh dawnna a nei ding uh bangin a kisa zel uh a, ahi zongin 'ka thei nai kei hi' ci in a dik zaw thei hi.

records.english: Children usually cope better with uncertainty when adults explain what they do and don't know.
records.zomi: Mi upate in a theih uh leh a theih loh uh a genteh uh ciangin naupangte in theih kician lohna a thuakzawh zaw zel uh hi.

records.english: Is Uncle Thomas bringing his new girlfriend to the wedding?
records.zomi: Pa neu Thomas in a numei it thak mopawi ah a paipih ding hiam?

records.english: Possibly, but nobody has met her yet, so we'll see.
records.zomi: Hi thei hi, ahi zongin kuamah in amah a mu nai kei uh ahih manin i en ding hi.

records.english: Who broke the vase in the hall?
records.zomi: Inn lutna-a pak bel kua in a khamsak hiam?

records.english: I'm not sure, but the cat was sitting next to it.
records.zomi: Ka thei kician kei a, ahi zongin zawhngeu a kiangah a tu hi.

records.english: The family is still unsure what to do with Grandpa's house now that he's gone.
records.zomi: Pu a om nawn loh ciangin a inn bang bawl ding hiam innkuan in a thei kician lai kei uh hi.

records.english: When my parents divorced, the hardest part was not knowing where we would live.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa a kikhen uh ciangin a haksa pen koi ah i teeng ding uh hiam theih lohna ahi hi.

records.english: When we moved to a new country, every day was full of small uncertainties.
records.zomi: Gam thak khat ah i suan uh ciangin ni khempeuh theih kician lohna neunote tawh a dim hi.

records.english: Nobody in the family is quite sure how old the house is, although Grandpa insists it was built before the railway came.
records.zomi: Innkuan sungah kuamah in inn kum bangzah a cing hiam a thei kician kei uh a, Pu in meileng a tun ma-in kilam hi, a ci den hi.

records.english: Perhaps my sister will come home for the summer, but she hasn't decided.
records.zomi: Ka u numei khal ciangin inn ah hong ciah kha ding a, ahi zongin a khensat nai kei hi.

records.english: Nobody knows exactly where my great-grandmother is buried.
records.zomi: Ka pi' nu koi ah kivui hiam kuamah in a kician-in a thei kei uh hi.

records.english: I can't remember whether I told my wife about the dinner on Friday.
records.zomi: Laithai-a nitak an thu ka zi kiangah ka gen hiam ka phawk kei hi.

records.english: Will Grandma be well enough to travel next month?
records.zomi: Kha zom ciangin Pi khualzin dingin a dam kicing ding hiam?
