records.english: Unable to choose between the red dress and the blue one, my sister wore one to the ceremony and the other to the party.
records.zomi: Puan san leh puan dum kikal-ah a teel zawh loh manin ka u numei in khat pawi ah, a dang kipahna ah a silh hi.

records.english: We couldn't decide between two puppies, so we took both home.
records.zomi: Ui-no nih kikal-ah i khensat zo kei uh ahih manin a nih inn ah i paipih uh hi.

records.english: My parents chose to rent a smaller house so that they could help my brother with his studies.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal' sinna a huh theih nadingun ka nu leh ka pa in inn neu zaw khat luah dingin a teel uh hi.

records.english: Is the bigger house worth the longer drive to work?
records.zomi: Inn lian zaw in nasep lam mawng sau zaw adingin a phu hiam?

records.english: For the children's sake, I think so, but ask me again in winter.
records.zomi: Naupangte hangin, a phu hi, ka sa hi, ahi zongin phalbi ciangin hong dong kik in.

records.english: Is it better to tell the children about the move now or after the exams?
records.zomi: Suan ding thu naupangte kiangah tu-in gen a hoih zaw hiam, sitna khit ciangin hiam?

records.english: After the exams, so that they can concentrate.
records.zomi: Sitna khit ciangin, a lungsim uh a koih theih nadingun.

records.english: Is your grandson more like his mother or his father?
records.zomi: Na tupa a nu tawh a kibang zaw hiam, a pa tawh hiam?

records.english: He looks like his father, but he behaves exactly like his mother.
records.zomi: A pa tawh kibang-in a kilang a, ahi zongin a nu bang taktak-in a om hi.

records.english: When two family members want different things, comparing the options openly can avoid hurt feelings.
records.zomi: Innkuan mi nih in nate tuamtuam a deih uh ciangin teelnate kilang taka kiteh in lungsim natna a dal thei hi.

records.english: Which of the two photos should we frame for Grandma's birthday?
records.zomi: Pi' pianni adingin lim nih lak ah koi i bawm sungah koih ding hiam?

records.english: My parents are trying to decide whether to retire to the village or stay in the city near us.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in a nasep tawp khit-in khua ah pai ding hiam, eite kiang-a khuapi ah om ding hiam khensat a sawm uh hi.

records.english: Comparing the two schools on paper was easy, but visiting them changed our minds completely.
records.zomi: Sang nih lai tungah kiteh a baih a, ahi zongin a nih veh in i ngaihsutna a kheel vekpi hi.

records.english: Which name do you like better for the baby, Lily or Grace?
records.zomi: Naungek adingin koi min na deih zaw hiam, Lily hiam Grace hiam?

records.english: Grace, because it was my grandmother's name.
records.zomi: Grace, ka pi' min ahih manin.

records.english: Do you think our son would be happier at the music school or the ordinary one?
records.zomi: I tapa la sang ah a lungdam zaw ding hiam, sang tavuan ah hiam na ci hiam?

records.english: The music school, but only if he still has time to see his friends.
records.zomi: La sang, a lawmte a muh theih nading hun a nei lai leh bek.

records.english: Whichever option you choose, we'll support you.
records.zomi: Koi na teel zongin kong huh ding uh hi.

records.english: My grandfather says that comparing two good options is a luxury his generation rarely had.
records.zomi: Ka pu in teelna hoih nih kiteh pen a khangthak in a neih ngei tawm nuamna khat ahi hi, a ci hi.

records.english: When we compared the two prams, the cheaper one was actually lighter and easier to fold.
records.zomi: Naungek leeng nih i kiteh uh ciangin a man neem zaw a zang zaw a, khup a baih zaw taktak hi.

records.english: Choosing between two jobs is harder when one pays more and the other leaves more time for the family.
records.zomi: Nasep nih kikal-ah teel in khat in man tam zaw a pia a, a dang in innkuan adingin hun tam zaw a nusiat ciangin a haksa zaw hi.

records.english: My husband prefers the beach for holidays, whereas I'd rather go to the mountains.
records.zomi: Ka pasal in tawlngakni adingin tuipi gei a deih zaw a, kei in mual lam pai ka deih zaw hi.

records.english: Do you think the old sofa or the new one looks better in the living room?
records.zomi: Tutna khan ah sofa lui in a kilawm zaw ding hiam, a thak in hiam na ci hiam?

records.english: Would it be better for Grandma to move in with us or into a flat nearby?
records.zomi: Pi eite tawh hong teeng a hoih zaw ding hiam, a kiang-a inn khat ah hiam?

records.english: A flat nearby, so that she keeps her independence but we can visit every day.
records.zomi: A kiang-a inn khat, amah kia-a om theihna a kem a, ni simin i veh theih nadingin.

records.english: Which would you rather have for your birthday, a party or a day out?
records.zomi: Na pianni adingin koi na deih zaw hiam, kipahna hiam, ni khat pua-a pai hiam?

records.english: A day out at the zoo, with just my cousins.
records.zomi: Ka sanggamte bek tawh zoo ah ni khat pai.

records.english: After comparing two holiday cottages for weeks, we chose the plainer one, simply because it was closer to my grandparents.
records.zomi: Kal tampi tawlngakni inn nih i kiteh khit ciangin ka pu leh pi tawh a nai zaw ahih man bek-in a baih zaw i teel uh hi.

records.english: My daughter compared the two universities by visiting both and talking to the students.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in sangpi nih a nih veh-in sangnaupangte tawh a kihopih tungtawnin a kiteh hi.

records.english: We weighed up the two nurseries and chose the one with the garden.
records.zomi: Naupang sang nih i kiteh uh a, huan nei pen i teel uh hi.

records.english: When we had to choose between two hospitals for the birth, we picked the one my sister recommended.
records.zomi: Nausuah nadingin damdawi inn nih kikal-ah i teel kul uh ciangin ka u numei' gen pen i teel uh hi.

records.english: The cheaper school uniform wore out so quickly that the dearer one would have saved us money.
records.zomi: Sang puan man neem zaw manlang lua-in a siat ahih manin a man tam zaw in sum hong khol ding hi.

records.english: Do you prefer Sunday lunch at your parents' or at mine?
records.zomi: Nipini sun an na nu leh na pa' inn ah na deih zaw hiam, kei-a ah hiam?

records.english: At yours, because your mother lets me help in the kitchen.
records.zomi: Nang-a ah, na nu in an huanna inn ah huh dingin hong phal ahih manin.

records.english: Should I study medicine like my mother or engineering like my father?
records.zomi: Ka nu bangin damdawi ka sin ding hiam, ka pa bangin engineering ka sin ding hiam?

records.english: Study whichever subject you'd be happy doing for the next forty years.
records.zomi: Kum sawmli zom sungin na sep ciangin na lungdam ding thu koi peuh sin in.

records.english: Would you rather live with your parents or share a flat with friends?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa tawh teeng na deih zaw hiam, lawmte tawh inn kihawm na deih zaw hiam?

records.english: With friends, although I'd miss my mother's cooking.
records.zomi: Lawmte tawh, ka nu' an ka ngai ding hangin.

records.english: Should we get a cat or a dog?
records.zomi: Zawhngeu i khawi ding hiam, ui i khawi ding hiam?

records.english: A cat, since nobody is home during the day to walk a dog.
records.zomi: Zawhngeu, sunlai-in ui paipih vialvial dingin kuamah inn ah om lo ahih manin.

records.english: Choosing between a cheap holiday every year and a big trip every three years divided our family for weeks.
records.zomi: Kum simin tawlngakni man neem leh kum thum simin khualzinna lianpi kikal teelna in kal tampi i innkuan a kikhensak hi.

records.english: Could you pick up some cough medicine for Grandma on your way home?
records.zomi: Inn na ciah lampi ah Pi adingin khu damdawi tawmno hong lei thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Our neighbour's son had measles, so the doctor checked that our children were vaccinated.
records.zomi: I innveng' tapa in measles a nei ahih manin siavuan in i naupangte natna hihna damdawi a kisut hiam a en hi.

records.english: Is Grandpa feeling any better today?
records.zomi: Tuni-in Pu a dam deuh hiam?

records.english: A little, but he's still coughing at night.
records.zomi: Tawmno, ahi zongin zan ciangin a khu lai hi.

records.english: My grandfather never complains when he's ill, so we have to watch him carefully.
records.zomi: Ka pu a nat ciangin a phun ngei lo ahih manin limtakin i en kul uh hi.

records.english: Our son is so used to his asthma inhaler that he carries it everywhere without being reminded.
records.zomi: I tapa in a asthma inhaler a zang khin mahmah ahih manin kuamah in a phawksak kei zongin koi ah zong a pua hi.

records.english: Who's going to stay home with the twins while they have the flu?
records.zomi: Apengte flu a neih laitakun kua in inn ah amaute tawh a om ding hiam?

records.english: Children often recover from a fever faster than their worried parents do.
records.zomi: Naupangte a pumpi lumna pan a lungkham nu leh pa uh sangin manlang zaw-in a dam kik zel uh hi.

records.english: When my mother had shingles, she said the pain was worse than childbirth.
records.zomi: Ka nu in shingles a neih ciangin a natna nausuah sangin a gik zaw hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Every winter, my grandmother gets a bad cough that lasts for weeks.
records.zomi: Phalbi simin ka pi in kal tampi a sawt khu gik khat a nei hi.

records.english: Should I keep my daughter at home if she has a runny nose?
records.zomi: Ka tanu' nak a luang leh inn ah ka om sak ding hiam?

records.english: Not usually, unless she also has a fever or feels really unwell.
records.zomi: A tamzaw-in hi lo hi, a pumpi a lum hiam a dam lo mahmah bangin a kisak kei leh.

records.english: When my wife caught a stomach bug, I took the children to my mother's for two days.
records.zomi: Ka zi gil natna a neih ciangin naupangte ka nu kiangah ni nih ka paipih hi.

records.english: Please stay in your room until your temperature goes down.
records.zomi: Na pumpi lumna a kiam dong na khan sungah om in.

records.english: The children were so bored after three days in bed that they started inventing games.
records.zomi: Naupangte ni thum lupna tungah a om khit uh ciangin a ning mahmah uh ahih manin kimawlna a phuak kipan uh hi.

records.english: I caught chickenpox from my little brother when I was twenty, and it was much worse for me than for him.
records.zomi: Kum sawmnih ka cin ciangin ka nau pasal pan chickenpox ka ngah a, amah sangin kei adingin a gik zaw mahmah hi.

records.english: Every member of our family reacts differently to the same cold.
records.zomi: I innkuan mi khempeuh huihvot natna kibang tungah a kibang lo-in a thuak uh hi.

records.english: Why do the children always get ill during the holidays?
records.zomi: Bang hangin naupangte tawlngakni sungin a na tawntung uh hiam?

records.english: Probably because they finally stop and rest, and they're mixing with lots of cousins.
records.zomi: A tawpna-ah a khawl-in a tawl uh a, sanggam tampi tawh a kihel uh ahih manin kha ding hi.

records.english: Our son's fever broke in the middle of the night, and by morning he wanted pancakes.
records.zomi: I tapa' pumpi lumna zan lai ah a kiam a, zingsang ciangin pancake a deih hi.

records.english: My parents still give each other the same advice for a cold: rest, soup and an early night.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in huihvot natna adingin thuhilhna kibang a kipia lai uh hi: tawl, an tui leh zan hun ma-a ihmu.

records.english: My parents still remember the winter when the whole street had whooping cough.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in lampi bup whooping cough a neih phalbi a phawk lai uh hi.

records.english: It might be just a cold, but let's ask the pharmacist to be sure.
records.zomi: Huihvot natna bek hi kha ding a, ahi zongin kician nadingin damdawi zuakpa i dong ni.

records.english: Washing hands carefully is one of the simplest ways to stop an illness spreading through a family.
records.zomi: Khut limtak-a sil pen innkuan khat sungah natna a kizel loh nadingin a dal nading baih pen khat ahi hi.

records.english: Did the doctor say how long the cough would last?
records.zomi: Khu bangzah sawt ding hiam siavuan in a gen hiam?

records.english: My little brother once pretended to be ill so convincingly that he missed both his maths test and a trip to the dentist.
records.zomi: Ka nau pasal khatvei a natpa bangin a kibawl kician mahmah ahih manin a maths sitna leh ha siavuan veh a nih a pelh hi.

records.english: When a child is ill, even a small improvement can feel like a huge relief.
records.zomi: Naupang khat a nat ciangin a hoih deuhna neu khat zong hehnepna lianpi bangin a kisa thei hi.

records.english: My husband takes to his bed with every cold, as if it were something far worse.
records.zomi: Ka pasal in huihvot natna khempeuh tawh a gik zaw mahmah bangin lupna ah a lum hi.

records.english: When my father gets a migraine, we close the curtains and keep the house quiet.
records.zomi: Ka pa migraine a neih ciangin tukkhuak puante i khak uh a, inn i daisak uh hi.

records.english: Shall I make you a hot drink and bring it to your room?
records.zomi: Dawn ding lum khat kong bawl sak a, na khan ah kong tawi ding hiam?

records.english: My sister's children get tonsillitis so often that the doctor has suggested an operation.
records.zomi: Ka u numei' tate tonsillitis a nei den uh ahih manin siavuan in zatui dingin a gen hi.

records.english: Please don't kiss the baby while you've got a cold sore.
records.zomi: Na muk ah natna a om laitakin naungek nam kei in.

records.english: Having a sick child at home and a job to go to is one of the hardest parts of being a parent.
records.zomi: Inn ah naupang na khat a om laitakin nasep ah pai kul pen nu leh pa hih' a haksa pen khat ahi hi.

records.english: Mum has a remedy for every illness, and most of them involve ginger.
records.zomi: Nu in natna khempeuh adingin damdawi a nei a, a tamzaw in siing a kihel hi.

records.english: My sister gets hay fever so badly that she keeps the windows closed all spring.
records.zomi: Ka u numei in hay fever a gik mahmah ahih manin spring sung bup tukkhuakte a khak den hi.

records.english: Do you get headaches when you don't drink enough water?
records.zomi: Tui kicing na dawn kei ciangin na lu a na zel hiam?

records.english: Looking after a sick parent can be exhausting, especially if you're also caring for children.
records.zomi: Nu hiam pa natpa kem a gimhuai thei mahmah a, a diak in naupangte zong na kem ciangin.

records.english: When everyone in the house is coughing, it's hard to know who started it.
records.zomi: Inn sung-a mi khempeuh a khu uh ciangin kua in a kipatsak hiam theih a haksa hi.

records.english: Whenever I was ill as a child, my father would sit by my bed and read to me for hours, even after I had fallen asleep.
records.zomi: Ka neu lai-a ka nat vei khempeuh-in ka pa in ka lupna kiangah a tu-in nai tampi hong sim sak a, ka ihmut khit ciangin zong.

records.english: Let's open the windows for a while to get some fresh air into the room.
records.zomi: Khan sungah huih thak a lut nadingin hun tawmno tukkhuakte i hon ni.

records.english: Did you catch your cold from me?
records.zomi: Na huihvot natna kei pan na ngah hiam?

records.english: Maybe, but half my office has one too.
records.zomi: Hi kha ding, ahi zongin ka office' a langkhat in zong a nei uh hi.

records.english: Why do sore throats go round our house every January?
records.zomi: Bang hangin January kha simin dawng natna i inn sungah a kizel hiam?

records.english: Grandma swears that honey and lemon cure everything.
records.zomi: Pi in khuaitui leh lemon in a khempeuh a damsak hi, ci-in a kiciam hi.

records.english: When one of the children gets a stomach bug, the rest of the family usually catches it within a week.
records.zomi: Naupang khat in gil natna a neih ciangin innkuan dangte in kal khat sungin a ngah zel uh hi.

records.english: The flu jab gave my father a sore arm for a day, but he didn't catch flu that winter.
records.zomi: Flu damdawi sutna in ka pa' ban ni khat a nasak a, ahi zongin tua phalbi in flu a ngah kei hi.

records.english: My grandmother's old home remedies don't always work, but they always make us feel loved.
records.zomi: Ka pi' inn damdawi luite a sem tawntung kei a, ahi zongin hong it uh hi, ci a kisak sak tawntung hi.

records.english: Is the rash contagious?
records.zomi: Vun san a kizel thei hiam?

records.english: The doctor said it isn't, so he can go back to school tomorrow.
records.zomi: Siavuan in a kizel kei hi, a ci ahih manin zingciang sang ah a pai kik thei hi.

records.english: You mustn't give the baby adult medicine, even in a small amount.
records.zomi: Naungek kiangah tawmno zong mi upa damdawi na pia kei ding hi.

records.english: I always feel guilty when I give my cold to the rest of the family.
records.zomi: Ka huihvot natna innkuan dangte ka ngahsak ciangin mawhna ka kisa tawntung hi.

records.english: A family that shares a bathroom also tends to share every cold.
records.zomi: Kisilna inn khat a kihawm innkuan khat in huihvot natna khempeuh zong a kihawm zel hi.

records.english: Our son had conjunctivitis, so we washed all the towels and pillowcases.
records.zomi: I tapa conjunctivitis a nei ahih manin puan nawtna leh lu-ah puan khempeuh i sawp uh hi.

records.english: When the baby caught her first cold, none of us slept properly for a week, and we jumped at every little cough.
records.zomi: Naungek in a huihvot natna masa a ngah ciangin kal khat sung kuamah hoih takin i ihmu kei uh a, khu neu khempeuh-in i khanglawh uh hi.

records.english: Can you check whether the baby has a temperature?
records.zomi: Naungek' pumpi a lum hiam na en thei ding hiam?

records.english: We keep a small first-aid box in the kitchen for cuts, burns and fevers.
records.zomi: Atna, kangna leh pumpi lumna adingin an huanna inn ah khatvei damna huh bawm neu khat i kem uh hi.

records.english: A cool cloth on the forehead made my little girl feel a lot better.
records.zomi: Maitang tungah puan vot khat in ka numei naupang neu a nuamsak mahmah hi.

records.english: My daughter had an ear infection, and she cried every time she lay down.
records.zomi: Ka tanu' bil natna a nei a, a lum vei khempeuh-in a kap hi.

records.english: Children with a stomach bug should drink small sips of water often.
records.zomi: Gil natna nei naupangte in tui tawmno tamvei a dawn ding uh hi.

records.english: A minor illness in an elderly relative can become serious quickly, so it's worth calling the doctor early.
records.zomi: Sanggam upa khat' natna neu manlang takin a gik thei ahih manin siavuan hun ma-in sam a phu hi.

records.english: Children, say goodbye to Mum at the door and then go and hang up your coats.
records.zomi: Naupangte, kongkhak ah Nu kiangah goodbye ci un a, tua khit ciangin na puan lian uh bulh un.

records.english: How was your first day?
records.zomi: Na ni masa bangci hiam?

records.english: Fine, but the bell is really loud.
records.zomi: A hoih, ahi zongin khawng aw a ging mahmah hi.

records.english: Our son came home from his first day and announced that he didn't need to go back, because he had already learned everything.
records.zomi: I tapa a ni masa pan inn ah hong ciah a, a khempeuh a sin khin ahih manin a pai kik kul kei hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Did the headteacher really shake every child's hand at the gate?
records.zomi: Sang makaipa in kongpi ah naupang khempeuh tawh khut a kilen taktak hiam?

records.english: Did you find your classroom on your own?
records.zomi: Na sangkhan nangmah kia-in na mu hiam?

records.english: By the end of the first week, my daughter was correcting my pronunciation of her teacher's name.
records.zomi: Kal masa a bei ciangin ka tanu in a saya' min ka gen dan a puah kipan hi.

records.english: Teachers know that the first few days can shape how a child feels about school for years.
records.zomi: Saya te in ni masa tawmno in naupang khat in sang a ngaihsut dan kum tampi a lawh thei hi, ci a thei uh hi.

records.english: Our eldest was disappointed that his first day didn't include any homework.
records.zomi: I upa pen a ni masa ah inn sinna om lo ahih manin a lungkia hi.

records.english: My grandfather walked five kilometres to school on his first day, and he still says it was worth it.
records.zomi: Ka pu in a ni masa ah sang ah kilometre nga a kal a, a phu hi, a ci lai hi.

records.english: My brother's first day was ruined before lunch, when he tripped in the playground and split his brand-new trousers.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal' ni masa sun an ma-in a siat a, kimawlna mun ah a puk-in a kekawm thak a kiphel hi.

records.english: My grandmother says that on her first day, she walked to school barefoot, carrying her shoes to keep them clean.
records.zomi: Ka pi in a ni masa ah a khedap a siangtho den nadingin a tawi-in khe awng tawh sang ah a kal hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Mum still has the drawing I brought home on my first day.
records.zomi: Nu in ka ni masa-a inn ah ka tawi lim a kem lai hi.

records.english: My sister insisted on wearing her new shoes to bed the night before her first day.
records.zomi: Ka u numei in a ni masa ma-a zan ah a khedap thak silh-in a ihmu dingin a ngen den hi.

records.english: Shall we buy a bigger school bag for the new books?
records.zomi: Laibu thakte adingin sang ip lian zaw khat i lei ding hiam?

records.english: I had to leave work early to collect my daughter after her first half-day at nursery.
records.zomi: Ka tanu naupang sang ah a ni langkhat masa khit ciangin la dingin nasep pan hun ma-in ka pusuak kul hi.

records.english: Please don't make a fuss at the gate, or she'll cry too.
records.zomi: Kongpi ah buaina bawl kei in, a kei leh amah zong a kap ding hi.

records.english: Our youngest was so tired after his first full day that he fell asleep at the dinner table.
records.zomi: I neu pen a ni bup masa khit ciangin a gim mahmah ahih manin nitak an dawhkan ah a ihmu hi.

records.english: What did you have for lunch on your first day?
records.zomi: Na ni masa ah sun an bang na ne hiam?

records.english: I was too nervous to eat anything except the apple Mum had packed.
records.zomi: Ka lau lua ahih manin Nu' hong koih apple bek ka ne hi.

records.english: Starting school in the middle of the year is often harder than starting with everyone else.
records.zomi: Kum laitak-a sang kipat pen mi khempeuh tawh kipat sangin a haksa zaw zel hi.

records.english: Who's going to take Mia to school on her first day?
records.zomi: Mia a ni masa ah sang ah kua in a paipih ding hiam?

records.english: When we dropped our eldest at university, it felt like her first day at school all over again.
records.zomi: I upa pen sangpi ah i nusiat ciangin a sang ni masa a kibang kik bangin a kisa hi.

records.english: Would you like to take your favourite toy to school tomorrow?
records.zomi: Zingciang na kimawlna van it pen sang ah na tawi nuam hiam?

records.english: My little sister was so excited about her first day that she was dressed, packed and waiting by the door at six in the morning.
records.zomi: Ka nau numei a ni masa tungtang a lungphamuan mahmah ahih manin zingsang nai guk ciangin a kisilh, a kigin-in kongkhak kiangah a ngak hi.

records.english: Grandpa walked my daughter to school on her first day, just as he had walked me thirty years earlier.
records.zomi: Kum sawmthum ma-in kei hong paipih bangin Pu in ka tanu a ni masa ah sang ah a paipih hi.

records.english: On the twins' first day, the teacher put them in different classes.
records.zomi: Apengte' ni masa ah saya in sangkhan tuam ah a koih hi.

records.english: They both cried at the door, holding each other's hands.
records.zomi: A nih kongkhak ah a khut uh kilen-in a kap uh hi.

records.english: By lunchtime, each of them had found a new best friend and forgotten all about it.
records.zomi: Sun an hun ciangin khatciat in lawm pen thak khat a mu uh a, tua thu a mangngilh khin uh hi.

records.english: Every year on the first day of school, my mother takes a photo of us by the front door, and the photos now fill a whole album.

records.english: Is it healthier to let yourself feel sad or to try to cheer yourself up quickly?

records.english: Whichever way you choose to grieve, there's no right or wrong way to feel.
records.zomi: Koi bangin kah dingin na teel zongin kisak dan dik hiam khial om lo hi.

records.english: Last winter, I had to choose between a party with colleagues and a quiet evening with an old friend who was grieving.
records.zomi: Phalbi nunung in nasep lawmte tawh kipahna khat leh a kah laitak lawm lui khat tawh nitak dai khat kikal-ah ka teel kul hi.

records.english: I went to see my friend, and we sat talking until midnight.
records.zomi: Ka lawm ka veh a, zan lai dong i tu-in i kihopih hi.

records.english: Months later, she told me it was the first evening she had laughed since her loss.
records.zomi: Kha tampi khit ciangin a mansuahna pan a nuih masa pen nitak ahi hi, hong ci hi.

records.english: When I'm sad, a hot bath helps more than any advice.
records.zomi: Ka lungkham ciangin kisilna lum khat in thuhilhna khatpeuh sangin hong huh zaw hi.

records.english: When you're sad, do you prefer to talk or to keep busy?
records.zomi: Na lungkham ciangin kihopih na deih zaw hiam, buai den na deih zaw hiam?

records.english: I keep busy first, and then I talk once I understand what I'm feeling.
records.zomi: A masa-in ka buai den a, tua khit ciangin bang ka kisa hiam ka theih ciangin ka kihopih hi.

records.english: Next time you're feeling low, call me instead of staying in your room.
records.zomi: A zom vei-in na lungsim a niam ciangin na khan ah om sangin hong sam in.

records.english: Some people feel better after a good cry, while others only feel more tired.
records.zomi: Mi pawl khat a kah khit uh ciangin a hoih zaw kisa uh a, a dangte a gim zaw bek uh hi.

records.english: Choosing to spend a sad evening with a friend rather than alone made all the difference.
records.zomi: Nitak lungkhamhuai khat amah kia sangin lawm khat tawh zat dingin teel in kibatlohna khempeuh a bawl hi.

records.english: Shall I tell the family the happy news now, or wait until everyone is together at dinner?
records.zomi: Lungdamna thu tu-in innkuan kiangah ka gen ding hiam, nitak an ah mi khempeuh a kikhop dong ka ngak ding hiam?

records.english: My father laughs when he's nervous, which people sometimes mistake for happiness.
records.zomi: Ka pa a lau ciangin a nuih a, mite in lungdamna bangin a thei khial zel uh hi.

records.english: A sad goodbye at the airport can turn into a happy reunion a year later.
records.zomi: Vanlengtual-a goodbye lungkhamhuai khat kum khat khit ciangin kimuh kikna lungdamhuai ah a kikheel thei hi.

records.english: Choosing gratitude over complaint doesn't remove sadness, but it can stop it from taking over.
records.zomi: Phunna sangin lungdamna teel in lungkhamna a bei sak kei a, ahi zongin a uk loh nadingin a dal thei hi.

records.english: A phone call from my grandmother can make a bad day feel much better.
records.zomi: Ka pi' phone sapna khat in ni hoih lo khat a hoih zaw mahmah sak thei hi.

records.english: Laughing with my sister makes me happier than any gift.
records.zomi: Ka u numei tawh nuih in letsong khatpeuh sangin hong lungdamsak zaw hi.

records.english: Do pets make people happier, or do happy people choose to have pets?
records.zomi: Ganhing khawi in mite a lungdamsak zaw hiam, mi lungdamte in ganhing khawi a teel uh hiam?

records.english: Helping someone else is often a better cure for sadness than thinking about your own problems.
records.zomi: Mi dang huh pen na buainate ngaihsut sangin lungkhamna damna hoih zaw a hi zel hi.

records.english: Happiness shared with family often feels bigger than happiness kept to yourself.
records.zomi: Innkuan tawh kihawm lungdamna nangmah adingin kem lungdamna sangin a lian zaw bangin a kisa zel hi.

records.english: Spending time in nature is one of the simplest ways to feel a little happier.
records.zomi: Leitung sungah hun zat pen tawmno lungdam zaw nading baih pen khat ahi hi.

records.english: My best friend knows whether I'd rather be hugged or left alone, without asking.
records.zomi: Ka lawm pen in dot lo-in hong pom ka deih hiam, hong nusia ka deih hiam a thei hi.

records.english: People who compare their lives with others online often feel less happy than those who don't.
records.zomi: Online-in a nuntakna uh mi dangte tawh a kiteh mite in a kiteh lo mite sangin a lungdam tawm zaw zel uh hi.

records.english: When do you feel happiest during the week?
records.zomi: Kal sungin bang hun ciangin na lungdam pen hiam?

records.english: My grandfather says that a happy home is not one without sadness but one where sadness is shared.
records.zomi: Ka pu in innkuan lungdam pen lungkhamna om lo hi lo-in lungkhamna kihawmna ahi hi, a ci hi.

records.english: The best way to teach a child about measuring is to let them help you build or cook something.
records.zomi: Naupang khat tehna sinsak nading hoih pen khat peuhpeuh lam hiam huan dingin hong huh sak ahi hi.

records.english: Dad always keeps a tape measure in his coat pocket, just in case.
records.zomi: Pa in a kisam kha ding hi, ci-in a puan lian ip sungah tehna khau a kem tawntung hi.

records.english: Children often measure distance in how long a journey takes rather than in kilometres.
records.zomi: Naupangte in gamlatna kilometre tawh hi lo-in khualzinna hun bangzah a la hiam tawh a teh zel uh hi.

records.english: My sister measures how much her tomato plants have grown every Sunday.
records.zomi: Ka u numei in Nipini simin a mehtuuk kungte bangzah a khang hiam a teh hi.

records.english: Every family I know has a different idea of what a cup of rice really means.
records.zomi: Ka theih innkuan khempeuh in buh haai khat a ci nopna tuamtuam-in a thei uh hi.

records.english: Last summer, my daughter decided to measure how far she walked in a day.
records.zomi: Khal nunung in ka tanu in ni khat-in bangzah gamla a kal hiam teh dingin a khensat hi.

records.english: She borrowed my phone and counted every step from breakfast until bedtime.
records.zomi: Ka phone a leitawi a, zingsang an pan a ihmut dong a khehlap khempeuh a sim hi.

records.english: By evening she had walked eleven kilometres and was too tired to eat dinner.
records.zomi: Nitak ciangin kilometre sawm leh khat a kal khin a, nitak an ne dingin a gim lua hi.

records.english: Will the bunk beds fit in the children's room?
records.zomi: Lupna kithuah te naupangte' khan sungah a lut ding hiam?

records.english: Only just, because the ceiling is 2.4 metres high and the beds are 1.6.
records.zomi: A lut thei mah hi, inn tungvum 2.4 metre a sang a, lupnate 1.6 ahih manin.

records.english: When my parents built the extension, they had the plans drawn up by a friend who is an architect.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in inn a behlap uh ciangin architect a hih lawm khat in a lim a ciamteh hi.

records.english: Which is longer, the hall or the kitchen, do you think?
records.zomi: Koi in a sau zaw na ci hiam, inn sung lampi hiam, an huanna inn hiam?

records.english: When we bought a new sofa, nobody thought to measure the front door, so it spent a whole night on the pavement before a neighbour helped us take the legs off.
records.zomi: Sofa thak khat i lei uh ciangin kuamah in mai kongkhak teh dingin a ngaihsun kei uh ahih manin innveng khat in a khe te i suah nadingin a huh ma-in lampi gei-ah zan bup a om hi.

records.english: Let's find out how much water the tank holds before we fill it.
records.zomi: I dimsak ma-in tank in tui bangzah a dim thei hiam en ni.

records.english: We marked the children's handprints on the garden wall every year to see how they'd grown.
records.zomi: Bangzah a khang uh hiam en dingin kum simin huan bang tungah naupangte' khut lim i ciamteh uh hi.

records.english: The children used a kitchen scale to weigh their pumpkins for the school competition.
records.zomi: Naupangte in sang kidemna adingin a mai te uh an huanna inn tehna tawh a teh uh hi.

records.english: When my sister sewed her wedding dress, she measured herself every week in case she changed size.
records.zomi: Ka u numei in a mopawi puan a khui ciangin a lianna a kikheel kha leh ci-in kal simin amah le amah a kiteh hi.

records.english: Our neighbour lent us a laser measure, which turned an afternoon of crawling around with a tape into ten minutes of pointing and clicking.
records.zomi: I innveng in laser tehna khat hong leitawi sak a, tehna khau tawh lei tungah kibawk-a nitak lam khat minit sawm sung liap-in nek bek ah a kheel hi.

records.english: When the baby had a fever, we checked her temperature every two hours through the night.
records.zomi: Naungek' pumpi a lum ciangin zan bup nai nih simin a pumpi lumna i en uh hi.

records.english: The nurse weighs the baby every month to check that she's growing well.
records.zomi: Nurse in naungek a khan hoih hiam en dingin kha simin a teh hi.

records.english: Children enjoy measuring things in their own units, such as how many shoes long the kitchen is.
records.zomi: Naupangte in an huanna inn khedap bangzah a sau hiam bang amau' tehna tawh nate teh a nuam sa uh hi.

records.english: Before the trip, we measured our car's roof to make sure the bicycle rack would fit.
records.zomi: Khualzin ma-in siiksakol koihna a lut ding hiam en dingin i mawtaw' tungvum i teh uh hi.

records.english: Weighing yourself every day can make you worry about small changes that mean nothing.
records.zomi: Ni simin na gikna teh in khiatna om lo kikheelna neunote tungah hong lungkhamsak thei hi.

records.english: How many footsteps long do you think the lake is?
records.zomi: Dil pen khehlap bangzah a sau ding na ci hiam?

records.english: My son measures the rain in the garden every morning with a plastic jar.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in zingsang simin huan sungah plastic bel khat tawh guahtui a teh hi.

records.english: Do you think a metre is taller or shorter than you?
records.zomi: Metre khat nang sangin a sang zaw ding hiam, a niam zaw ding hiam na ci hiam?

records.english: How tall are you now compared with your parents?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa tawh kiteh-in tu-in bangzah na sang hiam?

records.english: My aunt measures everything in her garden, from the height of the beans to the depth of the pond.
records.zomi: Ka ni in a huan sung-a na khempeuh, be' sanna pan dil neu' thukna dong a teh hi.

records.english: Shall we measure the garden to see whether there's room for a vegetable patch?
records.zomi: Anteh huan neu khat adingin mun a om hiam en dingin huan i teh ding hiam?

records.english: Can you check how many centimetres your feet have grown since the summer?
records.zomi: Khal pan na khe centimetre bangzah a khang hiam na en thei ding hiam?

records.english: How much did the baby weigh when she was born?
records.zomi: Naungek a suah ciangin kilo bangzah a gik hiam?

records.english: Just over 3 kilos, and she was 50 centimetres long.
records.zomi: Kilo 3 sang deuh, a sau centimetre 50 ahi hi.

records.english: Did you remember to measure the space for the new washing machine?
records.zomi: Puan sawpna seet thak adingin mun teh na phawk hiam?

records.english: My daughter measured her bedroom so that she could plan where to put her new desk.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in a dawhkan thak koi ah koih ding hiam a gel theih nadingin a lupna khan a teh hi.

records.english: Measuring medicine for a child must be done with the spoon that comes with the bottle, not a kitchen spoon.
records.zomi: Naupang adingin damdawi teh in an huanna inn kawm hi lo-in bel tawh hong pai kawm tawh teh ding hi.

records.english: Does Grandpa's old ruler have centimetres as well as inches?
records.zomi: Pu' tehna sing lui in inch bek hi lo-in centimetre zong a nei hiam?

records.english: Old measurements, such as a foot or a stone, still survive in some families' everyday speech.
records.zomi: Foot hiam stone bang tehna luite innkuan pawl khat' ni simin kammal ah a om lai hi.

records.english: A difference of a few millimetres can decide whether a new cupboard fits or not.
records.zomi: Millimetre tawmno kibatlohna in van koihna thak a lut ding hiam a khensat thei hi.

records.english: Mum still uses the old weighing scale her own mother used in the market.
records.zomi: Nu in amah' nu in zuakna mun ah a zat gikna tehna lui a zang lai hi.

records.english: Nobody in our family trusts the bathroom scale, because it shows a different weight every time.
records.zomi: Kisilna inn gikna tehna in vei khempeuh-in gikna tuam a lak ahih manin i innkuan ah kuamah in a muang kei uh hi.

records.english: How long is your hair now?
records.zomi: Tu-in na sam bangzah a sau hiam?

records.english: How far is Grandma's village from here?
records.zomi: Pi' khua hih pan bangzah gamla hiam?

records.english: About 90 kilometres, but the road is so bad that it takes three hours.
records.zomi: Kilometre 90 bang, ahi zongin lampi a hoih lo lua ahih manin nai thum a la hi.

records.english: My grandfather can judge a distance just by looking, and he's rarely wrong by more than a few metres.
records.zomi: Ka pu in en bek tawh gamlatna a teh thei a, metre tawmno sangin a khial ngei kei hi.

records.english: My father measured the land with a long rope before we built the house.
records.zomi: Inn i lam ma-un ka pa in khau sau khat tawh gam a teh hi.

records.english: Use the measuring jug, not a mug, when you make the baby's milk.
records.zomi: Naungek' nawitui na bawl ciangin haai hi lo-in tehna bel zang in.

records.english: Measuring ingredients carefully is especially important when you're baking bread.
records.zomi: Moh na hal ciangin an hel te limtakin teh a thupi diak hi.

records.english: Write down the measurements, or we'll have to do it all again tomorrow.
records.zomi: Tehnate gelh in, a kei leh zingciang a khempeuh i bawl kik kul ding hi.

records.english: We weighed the new puppy on the bathroom scale by holding him and then subtracting my weight.
records.zomi: Ui-no thak kisilna inn gikna tehna tungah ka len-in ka gikna i lak khia-in i teh uh hi.

records.english: The fish my uncle caught was 60 centimetres long, or so he says.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu' man ngasa centimetre 60 a sau hi, amah' gen bangin.

records.english: Grandma's recipes say things like a glass of flour and a spoon of salt.
records.zomi: Pi' an huan dante in mim haai khat leh cii kawm khat bang a ci hi.

records.english: My grandmother never measures anything when she cooks; she uses handfuls and pinches.
records.zomi: Ka pi in an a huan ciangin bangmah a teh ngei kei hi; khut tum leh tawmno a zang hi.

records.english: The thermometer in the hall shows that the house is only 16 degrees, so let's put the heating on.
records.zomi: Inn sung lampi-a thermometer in inn degree 16 bek ahi hi, a lak ahih manin inn lumna i hon ni.

records.english: Shoe sizes in our family range from a tiny 20 for the baby to a huge 46 for my brother.
records.zomi: I innkuan-a khedap lianna naungek adingin 20 neu pan ka sanggam pasal adingin 46 lian dong a om hi.

records.english: Our son grew 8 centimetres in one year, so none of his trousers fit any more.
records.zomi: I tapa kum khat sungin centimetre 8 a khang ahih manin a kekawm khempeuh a kilawm nawn kei hi.

records.english: How many litres of soup do you think we need for thirty people?
records.zomi: Mi sawmthum adingin an tui litre bangzah i kisam ding na ci hiam?

records.english: Thank you for helping me measure the room; I could never have held the tape on my own.
records.zomi: Khan teh dingin hong huh manin ka lungdam hi; keimah kia-in tehna khau ka len zo ngei kei ding hi.

records.english: We check the temperature of the bath water with our elbow before the baby goes in.
records.zomi: Naungek a lut ma-in i khut khiing tawh kisilna tui' lumna i en uh hi.

records.english: Mum can tell when the oil is hot enough just by watching it, without any thermometer.
records.zomi: Nu in thermometer om lo-in en bek tawh sathau a lum kicing hiam a thei thei hi.

records.english: The doctor measured my father's waist and told him to walk more.
records.zomi: Siavuan in ka pa' kawng a teh a, kal tam zaw dingin a hilh hi.

records.english: Can you recommend a doctor who speaks my parents' language?
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa' pau a gen siavuan khat hong gen thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: What would you advise my daughter, who wants to become a nurse?
records.zomi: Nurse a hih nop ka tanu kiangah bang thuhilhna na pia ding hiam?

records.english: Volunteer at a hospital first, so that she knows what the work is really like.
records.zomi: A masa-in damdawi inn ah deihsakna nasep sem in, nasep bang ahi taktak hiam a theih nadingin.

records.english: We followed our neighbour's recommendation and hired the same cleaner, who has been with us for years.

records.english: My grandmother recommended a tea for my cold, and it tasted awful but helped.

records.english: Who would you suggest as a godparent for our son?

records.english: What should I read to my son at bedtime?
records.zomi: Ihmut ma-in ka tapa kiangah bang ka sim sak ding hiam?

records.english: Anything with rhymes, because children his age love the sound of the words.
records.zomi: Kammal kituak nei khatpeuh, a kum bang naupangte in kammalte' ging a it uh ahih manin.

records.english: Can you recommend a good children's book for my nephew's birthday?
records.zomi: Ka tanau' pianni adingin naupang laibu hoih khat hong gen thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Try a book of animal stories, because he's mad about animals.
records.zomi: Ganhing tangthu laibu khat sin in, ganhingte a it mahmah ahih manin.

records.english: What would you recommend for a present for my grandmother's ninetieth birthday?
records.zomi: Ka pi' kum sawmkua pianni letsong adingin bang na gen ding hiam?

records.english: An album of family photos, with a note from each grandchild.

records.english: Whenever we need a recommendation, we ask the family group chat and get twelve different answers.

records.english: Is there a babysitter you'd recommend for Friday night?

records.english: Our neighbour's daughter is very reliable, and the children adore her.

records.english: Can you suggest something fun for the whole family to do this weekend?

records.english: Something with animals and songs, and nothing too frightening.
records.zomi: Ganhing leh la nei, a lauhuai lua lo khat.

records.english: I asked my aunt to recommend a dressmaker for my wedding dress.
records.zomi: Ka mopawi puan adingin puan khuipa khat gen dingin ka ni ka ngen hi.

records.english: Recommendations from other parents at the playground helped us find a nursery where our shy daughter finally felt at home.

records.english: The old garden behind the church, especially in the evening light.

records.english: Mum always asks her sister which recipe to use before trying something new.

records.english: Who would you call to repair a leaking gutter?
records.zomi: Tui luang inn tungvum tuiluang bawlphat dingin kua na sam ding hiam?

records.english: The builder who did my parents' house, because he's honest about prices.

records.english: When friends ask me to recommend a babysitter, I only suggest people I'd trust with my own children.

records.english: Which summer camp would you choose for a shy ten-year-old?

records.english: Do you know a good recipe for a birthday cake without eggs?

records.english: Can you recommend a shop that sells school uniforms at a fair price?

records.english: Asking several relatives for advice can leave you more confused than when you started.

records.english: My sister recommended a book about raising teenagers, which I wish I'd read years ago.

records.english: Which music teacher did your children have?

records.english: My parents recommended that we visit the village where they grew up, and it became the best part of our trip.

records.english: Do you know a good place to buy a second-hand bicycle for a child?

records.english: Mum recommended that I take a year to travel before I settled down.
records.zomi: Nu in ka kip ma-in kum khat khualzin dingin hong gen hi.

records.english: Which car seat would you recommend for a newborn?
records.zomi: Naungek thak adingin koi mawtaw tutna na gen ding hiam?

records.english: Do you know anyone who gives guitar lessons to adults?
records.zomi: Mi upate guitar a sinsak mi khat na thei hiam?

records.english: My brother recommends the same restaurant to everyone he meets, and in ten years nobody has come back disappointed.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in a kimuh mi khempeuh kiangah an zuakna inn kibang a gen a, kum sawm sungin kuamah lungkia-in a ciah kei uh hi.

records.english: My cousin recommended a holiday cottage by the sea, and it was perfect for the children.

records.english: When grandparents recommend old remedies, it's worth checking them with a doctor first.

records.english: Thank you for recommending that doctor; my father finally feels listened to.

records.english: Recommendations from family are useful, but they often say more about the person giving them than about the thing itself.

records.english: Would you recommend the swimming lessons at the leisure centre for a nervous child?

records.english: Within a week of our arrival, the neighbours had recommended everything from a plumber to a piano teacher, and we kept the list on the fridge for years.

records.english: Do you know a good paediatrician near here?

records.zomi: Kei-a te naupang laute tawh a hoih mahmah ahih manin a nambat kong khak ding hi.

records.english: What would you suggest for our anniversary dinner?

records.english: The little restaurant by the river, where we went on our first date.
records.zomi: I kimuh masa-a i pai lui kiang-a an zuakna inn neu.

records.english: Recommending a school to another family is a big responsibility, because every child is different.
records.zomi: Innkuan dang khat kiangah sang khat gen pen mawhpuakna lianpi ahi a, naupang khatciat a kibang lo uh ahih manin.

records.english: My father won't buy anything, not even a kettle, until he's asked at least three people what they think of it.
records.zomi: Ka pa in mi thum a tawm pen bang a ngaihsun uh hiam a dot ma-in kettle zong bangmah a lei kei hi.

records.english: Could you suggest a good game for children of different ages?
records.zomi: Kum tuamtuam naupangte adingin kimawlna hoih khat hong gen thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Do you think this offer is a scam?

records.english: Who can I ask if I'm not sure whether a message is real?

records.english: Investment offers that promise huge, quick profits are a common type of scam.
records.zomi: Manlang-a ngahna lianpi a kiciamsak sum koihna ngetnate zuauna kineih tamzaw khat ahi hi.

records.english: Scams change all the time, so it's worth talking about new ones with your family.
records.zomi: Zuaunate a kikheel den ahih manin na innkuan tawh a thakte tungtang kihopih a phu hi.

records.english: A friend in need online may not be a friend at all.
records.zomi: Online-a huhna kisam lawm khat lawm taktak hi lo kha thei hi.

records.english: How can I tell whether an online shop is genuine?
records.zomi: Online dawl khat a taktak hiam bangci ka thei thei ding hiam?

records.english: Look for a real address and phone number, read reviews on other sites, and be wary of prices far below everyone else's.
records.zomi: Teenna mun leh phone nambat taktak zong in, website dangte ah a gen dan sim inla, mi dang khempeuh sangin a man neem lua mahmah te lau in.

records.english: The bank was able to stop the payment because my father called them straight away.
records.zomi: Ka pa in a pah-in a sam ahih manin bank in man piakna a khawlsak thei hi.

records.english: A real company will usually give you time to check before you pay.
records.zomi: Company taktak khat in na piak ma-in en nading hun hong pia zel hi.

records.english: Many families now have a secret word that they use to check whether a call is really from a relative.
records.zomi: Tu-in innkuan tampi in sapna khat sanggam pan taktak hiam en nadingin kammal guk khat a zang uh hi.

records.english: The money was lost before anyone in the family realised what had happened.
records.zomi: Innkuan sungah kuamah in bang a piang hiam a theih ma-un sum a mang khin hi.

records.english: If you're unsure, wait a day; a real offer will still be there tomorrow.
records.zomi: Na theih kician kei leh ni khat ngak in; ngetna taktak zingciang ciangin a om lai ding hi.

records.english: Mum now reads every message twice before she clicks on anything.

records.english: I didn't click the link, but I was worried all evening that I had done something wrong.

records.english: Is this website safe for buying concert tickets?
records.zomi: Hih website la kikhopna lai lei nadingin a bit hiam?

records.english: An email told my father he had won a prize in a lottery he had never entered.
records.zomi: Email khat in ka pa a kihel ngei loh lottery khat ah letsong a zo hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Scammers often create a sense of urgency so that people act before they have time to think.
records.zomi: Zuauna bawlte in mite in a ngaihsun ma-un a bawl nadingun kinawhna a bawl zel uh hi.

records.english: Fake charity appeals often appear after a disaster, when people most want to help.
records.zomi: Charity zuau ngetnate tuahsiatna khit ciangin mite in huh a deih pen hun ah a kilang zel hi.

records.english: My neighbour lost a lot of money to a website that sold cheap phones that never arrived.
records.zomi: Ka innveng in a tung ngei lo phone man neem zuak website khat ah sum tampi a mansuah hi.

records.english: Hang up and call the company back on the number on their official website.
records.zomi: Khak inla company' kumpi website tung-a nambat tawh sam kik in.

records.english: When my aunt realised the website was fake, she called her bank and cancelled her card at once.
records.zomi: Website a zuau hi, ka ni in a theih ciangin a bank a sam a, a card a phiat pah hi.

records.english: The link in the email went to a page that looked like the bank's but had a strange address.
records.zomi: Email sung-a link in bank' bang a kilang ahi zongin teenna mun lamdang nei phek khat ah a pai hi.

records.english: Can you check this email for me before I reply?
records.zomi: Ka dawng ma-in hih email hong en sak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Never pay for something with a gift card just because someone on the phone tells you to.

records.english: Would a real employer ask for a fee before you start work?
records.zomi: Nasep piaktu taktak khat in na nasep na kipat ma-in man a ngen ding hiam?

records.english: When in doubt, don't click.
records.zomi: Na lungmang ciangin nek kei in.

records.english: Scam calls are so common now that my grandparents don't answer numbers they don't know.
records.zomi: Zuauna sapnate tu-in a tam mahmah ahih manin ka pu leh pi in a theih loh nambat a dawng kei uh hi.

records.english: I got a text saying a parcel was waiting for me, but I hadn't ordered anything.
records.zomi: Van bawm khat hong ngak hi, ci text khat ka ngah a, ahi zongin bangmah ka sap kei hi.

records.english: Shall I block this number?
records.zomi: Hih nambat ka khak ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, and report it so that others are warned too.
records.zomi: Khak in, mi dangte zong vaihilh a ngah nadingun gen in.

records.english: Teaching older relatives about scams works best with real examples rather than general warnings.
records.zomi: Sanggam upate kiangah zuauna tungtang sinsak in vaihilhna tavuan sangin entehna taktak tawh a hoih pen-in a sem hi.

records.english: Romance scams can go on for months before the victim is asked for money.
records.zomi: Itna zuauna in a thuakpa sum kingen ma-in kha tampi a sawt thei hi.

records.english: I almost paid a fake parking fine that arrived by text.
records.zomi: Text tawh hong tung mawtaw koih man zuau khat ka pia dek hi.

records.english: My sister ordered a dress online, and what arrived looked nothing like the photo.
records.zomi: Ka u numei in online-in puan khat a sap a, a tung pen lim tawh kibang khol lo hi.

records.english: Scammers sometimes use pictures of real people to make fake profiles look genuine.
records.zomi: Zuauna bawlte in mi taktakte' lim zang-in profile zuaute a taktak bangin a kilangsak zel uh hi.

records.english: If an offer seems too good to be true, it probably is.
records.zomi: Ngetna khat a dik lua bangin a kilang leh a taktak lo kha ding hi.

records.english: Some scammers pretend to be a relative in trouble and ask for money to be sent urgently.
records.zomi: Zuauna bawl pawl khat in buaina sung-a sanggam khat bangin kibawl-in sum manlang takin khak dingin a ngen uh hi.

records.english: My grandmother received a call from someone claiming to be her grandson, but the voice was wrong.
records.zomi: Ka pi in a tupa ka hi hi, ci mi khat pan sapna khat a ngah a, ahi zongin aw a khial hi.

records.english: Did you really win a holiday, or is it another scam?
records.zomi: Tawlngakni khat na zo taktak hiam, zuauna dang khat ahi hiam?

records.english: Talk to someone you trust before you send money to a stranger, however convincing the story sounds.
records.zomi: Mikhual khat kiangah sum na khak ma-in tangthu bangzah a muanhuai zongin na muan mi khat tawh kihopih in.

records.english: A message full of spelling mistakes and urgent warnings is often a scam.
records.zomi: Laimal khialh leh kinawh vaihilhna tawh a dim thu khat zuauna a hi zel hi.

records.english: My son showed his grandparents how to spot a fake message by checking the sender's address.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in a pu leh pi kiangah a khakpa' teenna mun en-in thu zuau bangci theih ding hiam a lak hi.

records.english: Our aunt was nearly tricked by a message that looked exactly like one from her mobile company.

records.english: The police told my grandfather that he was the fifth person in the street to get the same call.
records.zomi: Police in ka pu kiangah lampi sungah sapna kibang a ngah mi nganna ahi hi, a ci uh hi.

records.english: Last spring, my cousin found a flat to rent online at a very low price.
records.zomi: Spring nunung in ka sanggam in online-in man neem mahmah-a luah ding inn khat a mu hi.

records.english: The owner said he was abroad and asked for a deposit before she could see it.
records.zomi: A neipa in gamdang ah ka om hi, ci-in a muh ma-in sum koih masa dingin a ngen hi.

records.english: Luckily, she asked a friend in the town to knock on the door, and the real owner had never heard of the advert.
records.zomi: Kampha takin khuapi-a lawm khat kongkhak kiu dingin a ngen a, a neipa taktak in kizuakna thu a za ngei kei hi.

records.english: Please don't send money to anyone you've only met online.
records.zomi: Online bek-a na kimuh mi kiangah sum khak kei in.

records.english: When a stranger online asks you to keep your conversation secret, that's a warning sign.
records.zomi: Online-a mikhual khat in na kihopihna uh guk-in kem dingin a ngen ciangin vaihilhna khat ahi hi.

records.english: My uncle was so embarrassed about being scammed that he didn't tell anyone for weeks.

records.english: You all need to know that no bank will ever ask for your full password by text.

records.english: Thank you for warning me about that message; I nearly clicked on it.
records.zomi: Tua thu tungtang hong vaihilh manin ka lungdam hi; ka nek dek hi.

records.english: The scammer already knew my name and address, which made the message seem so real that I almost replied.
records.zomi: Zuauna bawlpa in ka min leh ka teenna mun a thei khin ahih manin thu a taktak lua bangin a kilang a, ka dawng dek hi.

records.english: Who should I report a scam to?
records.zomi: Zuauna kua kiangah ka gen ding hiam?

records.english: Have you ever received a scam message?
records.zomi: Zuauna thu khatpeuh na ngah ngei hiam?

records.english: Children should know that a friend request from a stranger isn't always what it seems.
records.zomi: Mikhual pan lawm ngetna in a kilan bang hi tawntung lo hi, ci naupangte in a theih ding uh hi.

records.english: Falling for a scam is not a sign of stupidity; scammers are skilled at persuading people.

records.english: Is this message from the bank real?

records.english: No, the bank never asks you to click a link to confirm your details.

records.english: When my mother had her tooth out, she couldn't eat anything but soup for three days.

records.english: Stretching before you start digging will save your back.

records.english: Toothache kept my brother awake all night, so he finally agreed to see the dentist.

records.english: Does it hurt when you walk, Grandpa?

records.english: Only on the stairs, and only first thing in the morning.

records.english: My wife gets migraines so badly that she has to lie in a dark room.

records.english: My daughter's braces made her teeth ache for the first few days.

records.english: Hours of driving give my father a dull ache in his lower back.
records.zomi: Nai tampi mawtaw mawng in ka pa' nung niam lam ah natna dai khat a pia hi.

records.english: A warm bath helped my husband's stiff neck more than any tablet.

records.english: When pain makes someone short-tempered, it helps to remember that the pain is talking, not the person.

records.english: A sore throat makes even swallowing water painful.

records.english: After a long day of gardening, my whole body aches, but in a satisfying way.

records.english: My grandfather's hip pain finally went after his operation, and he started dancing again.

records.english: Does your wrist still hurt when you write?
records.zomi: Na gelh ciangin na khut kizopna a na lai hiam?

records.english: Tell the nurse honestly how much it hurts; she can't help you if you pretend it's fine.

records.english: Pain is easier to bear when someone you trust is holding your hand.

records.english: Rest your eyes for a few minutes; you've been staring at the screen for hours.

records.english: Last winter, my mother slipped on the icy steps outside our house.

records.english: Three days later, an X-ray showed it was broken, and she has worn sensible boots ever since.

records.english: Who can tell me what helps a stomach ache?
records.zomi: Gil natna adingin bang in a huh hiam kua in hong gen thei ding hiam?

records.english: Children sometimes describe pain in surprising ways, such as saying their tummy feels angry.

records.english: Do your hands hurt when the weather turns cold?
records.zomi: Huihkhua a vot ciangin na khut a na zel hiam?

records.english: My little girl woke up crying because her ear hurt.

records.english: Sore feet after a long walk are a small price to pay for a beautiful day out.

records.zomi: Lupna puan nem zaw khat i lei uh a, kal khat sungin ka nung natna a dam deuh hi.

records.english: The doctor asked my son to point to the face on the chart that showed how much it hurt.
records.zomi: Siavuan in ka tapa bangzah a na hiam a lak chart tung-a maitang khat liap dingin a ngen hi.

records.english: My back has been aching since I carried the children's beds up the stairs.

records.zomi: Liamna luite kum tampi khit ciangin a nat kik kipan zel hi.

records.english: Growing pains in children's legs are common at night, though they usually disappear by morning.

records.english: My son twisted his ankle playing football and has been limping all week.

records.english: Do your ankles swell after standing at work all day?

records.english: Teenagers often play down their pain so that they don't miss a match or a party.

records.english: My grandfather says that his knees can tell him when it's going to rain.

records.english: Did the dentist give you anything for the pain?
records.zomi: Ha siavuan in natna adingin bangmah hong pia hiam?

records.english: My father would rather suffer in silence than admit that his shoulder is bothering him.
records.zomi: Ka pa in a liang a buaisak hi, ci a pom sangin dai takin a thuak a deih zaw hi.

records.english: Hold the ice on your knee for ten minutes, and keep your leg up.
records.zomi: Tuikhal na khuk tungah minit sawm len inla, na khe liap in.

records.english: Watching someone you love in pain can be harder than feeling the pain yourself.
records.zomi: Na it mi khat natna-a a om en in na natna mah thuak sangin a haksa zaw thei hi.

records.english: Could you rub my shoulders for a minute, because they're so stiff?
records.zomi: Ka liangte a khauh mahmah ahih manin minit khat hong nul sak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Is it the same pain as last time, or a different one?
records.zomi: A ma-a natna kibang ahi hiam, a tuam ahi hiam?

records.english: Let me know if the pain gets worse during the night.
records.zomi: Zan sungin natna a gik zaw leh hong gen in.

records.english: My father finally admitted that his knee was hurting after he had to stop halfway up the hill.
records.zomi: Mual tung lam a langkhat ah a khawl kul khit ciangin ka pa in a khuk a na hi, ci a tawpna-ah a pom hi.

records.english: Sometimes a child's pain is really worry, and a gentle conversation helps more than medicine.
records.zomi: A hun pawl ah naupang khat' natna lungkhamna ahi a, kihopihna nem khat in damdawi sangin a huh zaw hi.

records.english: When my father hurt his back, my brother and I did all his jobs on the farm for a month.

records.english: My little brother made a terrible fuss about a splinter, but it came out easily.

records.english: I've had a pain in my side since this morning.

records.english: My daughter bumped her head on the table and cried, but she was laughing again five minutes later.
records.zomi: Ka tanu' lu dawhkan ah a kidei a, a kap a, ahi zongin minit nga khit ciangin a nuih kik hi.

records.english: Is it better to face a fear quickly or to take it step by step?
records.zomi: Launa khat manlang taka maitang ngat a hoih zaw hiam, khat zawh khat-a pai a hoih zaw hiam?

records.english: Step by step usually works better, so that you don't feel overwhelmed.
records.zomi: Khat zawh khat a tamzaw-in a hoih zaw a, na lungsim a liap lua loh nadingin.

records.english: Children often fear things that adults think are silly, but the fear is very real to them.
records.zomi: Naupangte in mi upate in a hai a sak uh nate a lau zel uh a, ahi zongin launa amaute adingin a taktak mahmah hi.

records.english: Would you rather have a doctor who is honest or one who is gentle?
records.zomi: Thu dik gen siavuan hiam, nem siavuan hiam koi na deih zaw hiam?

records.english: Both, if possible, but honest first.
records.zomi: A nih, a theih leh, ahi zongin thu dik masa.

records.english: My daughter is less afraid of dogs since she started visiting our neighbour's puppy.
records.zomi: Ka tanu i innveng' ui-no a veh kipat pan ui a lau tawm zaw hi.

records.english: Small children often worry about losing a parent in a crowd more than about anything else.
records.zomi: Naupang neute in nate dang sangin mi tam lak-ah a nu hiam a pa a mansuah ding a lungkham zaw zel uh hi.

records.english: When I'm worried, my wife makes tea, and I find that it helps more than any words.
records.zomi: Ka lungkham ciangin ka zi in niangtui a bawl a, kammal khatpeuh sangin a huh zaw hi, ka thei hi.

records.english: Our youngest is more worried about his new teacher than about the new school.
records.zomi: I neu pen in sang thak sangin a saya thak a lungkham zaw hi.

records.english: What do you do when you can't stop worrying about something?
records.zomi: Khat peuhpeuh lungkham na khawl zo kei ciangin bang na bawl hiam?

records.english: Promise me you won't drive home if the roads are icy.
records.zomi: Lampi khal a om leh inn lam mawng kei dingin hong kiciamsak in.

records.english: Talking to someone who has faced the same fear is often more helpful than general advice.
records.zomi: Launa kibang a thuak khin mi khat tawh kihopih in thuhilhna tavuan sangin a huh zaw zel hi.

records.english: Is it braver to admit you're scared or to carry on despite your fear?
records.zomi: Ka lau hi, ci pom a hangsan zaw hiam, na lau hangin na pai den a hangsan zaw hiam?

records.english: Dad worries quietly, whereas my mother talks about every worry out loud.
records.zomi: Pa dai takin a lungkham a, ka nu in a lungkhamna khempeuh aw ngaih takin a gen hi.

records.english: Some fears fade with age, while new ones appear that we never expected.
records.zomi: Launa pawl khat kum tawh a mang a, i lamen ngei loh launa thakte a kilang hi.

records.english: A frightened animal and a frightened child both need calm voices and slow movements.
records.zomi: Ganhing lau khat leh naupang lau khat in aw dai leh kilawh nuamte a kisam uh hi.

records.english: Some people worry about big things like money, while others worry most about small daily problems.
records.zomi: Mi pawl khat in sum bang thu lianpite a lungkham uh a, a dangte in ni simin buaina neunote a lungkham pen uh hi.

records.english: Counting slowly to ten can calm a sudden wave of panic.
records.zomi: Sawm dong nuam takin sim in thakhat-a launa a daisak thei hi.

records.english: Choosing to face the fear of driving again after the accident took my aunt months.
records.zomi: Accident khit ciangin mawtaw mawng launa maitang kituak dingin teel in ka ni kha tampi a la hi.

records.english: Our son is braver about injections than he is about the dark.
records.zomi: I tapa in mial sangin damdawi sutna ah a hangsan zaw hi.

records.english: Before my operation, I had to choose between reading everything about it and reading nothing.
records.zomi: Ka zatui ma-in a tungtang khempeuh sim hiam bangmah sim lo hiam ka teel kul hi.

records.english: I decided to ask the surgeon three questions and leave the rest to the doctors.
records.zomi: Zatui siavuan kiangah dotna thum dong-in a dangte siavuante kiangah nusia dingin ka khensat hi.

records.english: It turned out to be the calmest I had felt in weeks.
records.zomi: Kal tampi sungah ka lungsim a dai pen hun a hi hi.

records.english: Some worries are worth sharing, while others disappear if you give them a day.
records.zomi: Lungkhamna pawl khat hawm a phu a, a dangte ni khat na piak leh a mang hi.

records.english: Do you think it's better to tell children about family worries or to protect them from them?
records.zomi: Innkuan lungkhamnate naupangte kiangah gen a hoih zaw hiam, amaute kem a hoih zaw hiam na ci hiam?

records.english: Some families talk openly about their fears, while others prefer to keep a brave face.
records.zomi: Innkuan pawl khat a launa uh kilang takin a kihopih uh a, a dangte hangsan maitang kem a deih zaw uh hi.

records.english: I worry less when I write a plan, even if I never follow it exactly.
records.zomi: Gelna khat ka gelh ciangin a taktak-in ka zui ngei kei zongin ka lungkham tawm zaw hi.

records.english: Is it more frightening to speak in public or to sing in front of people?
records.zomi: Mipi mai-ah thu gen a lauhuai zaw hiam, mite mai-ah la sa a lauhuai zaw hiam?

records.english: When I worry, I'd rather keep busy than sit still and think.
records.zomi: Ka lungkham ciangin daitak-a tu-a ngaihsun sangin buai den ka deih zaw hi.

records.english: My mother worried so much about the journey that she packed food for three days.
records.zomi: Ka nu in khualzinna tungtang a lungkham mahmah ahih manin ni thum adingin an a koih hi.

records.english: Fear of failure stops some students from even trying, which is worse than failing.
records.zomi: Zawh lohna launa in sangnaupang pawl khat sin zong a sinsak kei a, zawh lohna sangin a hoih lo zaw hi.

records.english: Worrying about money and worrying about health feel different, but they both keep you awake.
records.zomi: Sum lungkham leh damna lungkham a kibang lo a, ahi zongin a nih in hong ihmusak lo hi.

records.english: How can I help my son feel less frightened of thunderstorms?
records.zomi: Ka tapa van-ging a lau tawm zawk nadingin bangci ka huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Fear of the unknown is often worse than fear of something we can see.
records.zomi: Theih loh nate launa i muh theih na launa sangin a gik zaw zel hi.

records.english: I'm more afraid of heights than of the dark, but my sister is the opposite.
records.zomi: Mial sangin a sang mun ka lau zaw a, ahi zongin ka u numei in a kikheel hi.

records.english: Would you rather be told when something is wrong, even if it frightens you?
records.zomi: Na lausak zongin khat peuhpeuh a khial ciangin kigen na deih zaw ding hiam?

records.english: Worrying in advance rarely changes what actually happens, though it can help you prepare.
records.zomi: Hun ma-in lungkham in a taktak-a a piang a kheel tawm hi, kiginkholh nadingin a huh thei hangin.

records.english: A walk in the fresh air calms my worries better than watching television.
records.zomi: Huih thak sungah kalna khat in television en sangin ka lungkhamnate a daisak zaw hi.

records.english: Shall I stay with you during the appointment, or would you rather go in alone?
records.zomi: Kimuhna sungin nang tawh ka om ding hiam, nangmah kia-in na lut nuam zaw hiam?

records.english: Would you rather know bad news straight away or wait until you're ready?
records.zomi: Thu hoih lo a pah-in theih na deih zaw hiam, na kiginkholh dong ngak na deih zaw hiam?

records.english: Straight away, because waiting makes me imagine something even worse.
records.zomi: A pah-in, ngak in thu hoih lo zaw ka ngaihsutsak ahih manin.

records.english: Choosing to call a friend instead of lying awake worrying made the night much easier.
records.zomi: Lungkham-a khanglawh-in lum sangin lawm khat sam dingin teel in zan a baihsak mahmah hi.

records.english: Some fears are worth listening to, because they warn us of real danger.
records.zomi: Launa pawl khat ngaikhiat a phu hi, lauhuai taktak tungtang hong vaihilh uh ahih manin.

records.english: Shall we talk about it now, or would you rather sleep on it?
records.zomi: Tu-in i kihopih ding hiam, zan khat na ngaihsun nuam zaw hiam?

records.english: Does Grandpa fear loneliness more than illness?
records.zomi: Pu in natna sangin amah kia-a om a lau zaw hiam?

records.english: Are you more afraid of spiders or snakes?
records.zomi: Maimom na lau zaw hiam, gul na lau zaw hiam?

records.english: Do you get more nervous before an exam or before a job interview?
records.zomi: Sitna ma-in hiam nasep kidotna ma-in hiam na lau zaw hiam?

records.english: Before an interview, because I can't study for it.
records.zomi: Kidotna ma-in, a adingin ka sin thei kei ahih manin.

records.english: Flying frightens me more than driving, even though I know driving is more dangerous.
records.zomi: Mawtaw mawng in a lauhuai zaw hi, ka theih hangin vanleng tuang in mawtaw mawng sangin hong lausak zaw hi.

records.english: Do you two worry more about your children or about your parents?
records.zomi: Na nih in na tate na lungkham zaw uh hiam, na nu leh na pa uh hiam?

records.english: A small amount of worry before a test can actually help some students concentrate.
records.zomi: Sitna ma-a lungkhamna tawmno in sangnaupang pawl khat lungsim a koih nadingin a huh taktak thei hi.

records.english: Some people fear change, while others fear that nothing will ever change.
records.zomi: Mi pawl khat in kikheelna a lau uh a, a dangte in bangmah kikheel ngei lo ding a lau uh hi.

records.english: My brother would rather face a storm at sea than a room full of strangers.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in mikhual tawh a dim khan khat sangin tuipi tung-a huihpi khat a maitang ngat a deih zaw hi.

records.english: Next time you're worried, call me rather than keeping it to yourself.
records.zomi: A zom vei-in na lungkham ciangin na kem sangin hong sam in.

records.english: Hearing a calm voice on the phone helps me more than reading advice online.
records.zomi: Phone tungah aw dai khat zak in online-a thuhilhna sim sangin hong huh zaw hi.

records.english: Worries feel heavier at night than in the morning, so I try not to make decisions after midnight.
records.zomi: Lungkhamnate zingsang sangin zan ciangin a gik zaw ahih manin zan lai khit ciangin thukhenna bawl kei dingin ka hanciam hi.

records.english: Whichever way you face your fears, you don't have to face them alone.
records.zomi: Koi bangin na launate na maitang ngat zongin nangmah kia-in na maitang ngat kul kei hi.

records.english: I'd rather worry about being late than actually be late.
records.zomi: A taktak-a nung sangin nung ding lungkham ka deih zaw hi.

records.english: Choosing a familiar route to the hospital helped my mother feel less anxious.
records.zomi: Damdawi inn lam lampi theih khin teel in ka nu a lungkham tawm zawk nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: We let our daughter choose whether to watch the scary film or a cartoon, and she chose the cartoon.
records.zomi: Film lauhuai hiam cartoon hiam en dingin i tanu i teelsak uh a, cartoon a teel hi.

records.english: What does the eagle on the old shield stand for?
records.zomi: Phaw lui tung-a muvanlai in bang a lak hiam?

records.english: The patterns on our grandmother's blankets tell the story of the places she has lived.
records.zomi: I pi' puan tung-a limte in a teenna munte' tangthu a gen hi.

records.english: Symbols are a kind of language that families speak without words.
records.zomi: Ciamtehnate innkuante in kammal om lo-in a gen pau khat bang ahi hi.

records.english: Many families keep a special object that has been passed from parent to child for generations.
records.zomi: Innkuan tampi in khangthu tampi nu leh pa pan ta kiangah kipia khia van tuam khat a kem uh hi.

records.english: The children made paper birds as a symbol of hope for their sick classmate.
records.zomi: Naupangte in a sangkhan lawm natpa adingin lametna ciamtehna-in lai vasate a bawl uh hi.

records.english: Shaking hands with both hands shows extra respect in our family.
records.zomi: I innkuan ah khut nih tawh khut kilen in zahtakna behlap a lak hi.

records.english: A simple gesture, like bowing your head, can carry a deep meaning.
records.zomi: Lu kun bang kilakna baih khat in khiatna thuk khat a pua thei hi.

records.english: Shall we ask the elders what the old carvings on the church door mean?
records.zomi: Pawlpi kongkhak tung-a sing khen luite' khiatna mi upate i dong ding hiam?

records.english: In some families, a name is a symbol, chosen to carry a hope for the child's future.
records.zomi: Innkuan pawl khat ah min khat ciamtehna ahi a, naupang' hun zom adingin lametna khat pua dingin kiteel hi.

records.english: Telling children what family symbols mean helps them understand where they come from.
records.zomi: Naupangte kiangah innkuan ciamtehnate' khiatna gen in koi pan a hong pai uh hiam a theih nadingun a huh hi.

records.english: Thank you for explaining the meaning of the cloth; I'll treasure it even more now.
records.zomi: Puan' khiatna hong genteh manin ka lungdam hi; tu-in a manpha zaw-in ka kem ding hi.

records.english: Please don't sit on the elders' bench; it's kept for them as a sign of respect.
records.zomi: Mi upate' tutphah tungah tu kei un; zahtakna lahna-in amaute adingin kikem hi.

records.english: My mother taught us never to step over someone's food, because in our family it shows disrespect.
records.zomi: I innkuan ah zahtak lohna a lak ahih manin ka nu in mi khat' an kaan ngei lo dingin hong sinsak hi.

records.english: Dad keeps a small carved bird above the door, because he says it watches over the house.
records.zomi: Inn a kem hi, a ci ahih manin Pa in kongkhak tung lam ah sing tawh khen vasa neu khat a koih hi.

records.english: What does the pattern on this shawl mean?
records.zomi: Hih puan tung-a lim in bang a ci nopna hiam?

records.english: My grandmother says each line stands for a generation of our family.
records.zomi: Ka pi in zial khatciat in i innkuan' khangthak khat a lak hi, a ci hi.

records.english: The old tree in the middle of the village is where important decisions were once made.
records.zomi: Khua lailung-a sing lui pen a ma-in thukhenna thupite kibawlna mun ahi hi.

records.english: In our family, the eldest son receives his father's walking stick when the father dies.
records.zomi: I innkuan ah pa a sih ciangin ta pasal upa pen in a pa' ciangkhut a ngah hi.

records.english: Symbols often carry meanings that older people understand without needing to explain them.
records.zomi: Ciamtehnate in mi upate in genteh kul lo-in a theih khiatna a pua zel uh hi.

records.english: The flag over the community hall is raised only on important days.
records.zomi: Mipi inn tung-a flag ni thupite ciang bek-in kikai hi.

records.english: A gift of salt to a new neighbour is our family's way of wishing them a good life in their home.
records.zomi: Innveng thak kiangah cii letsong in amau' inn ah nuntakna hoih deihsakna i innkuan' lampi ahi hi.

records.english: When my brother left for the city, my mother gave him a small woven bag of seeds from our garden.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal khuapi ah a pai ciangin ka nu in i huan pan khaici ip neu tah khat a pia hi.

records.english: My grandfather taught me that the knife should always be passed handle first.
records.zomi: Ka pu in namsau a kaihna lam masa-in kipia ding hi, ci hong sinsak hi.

records.english: Children, please don't play with the old drum; it's used only for special ceremonies.
records.zomi: Naupangte, khuang lui tawh kimawl kei un; pawi tuam ciang bek-in kizang hi.

records.english: My aunt says that a sudden itchy palm means money is coming, but we've never seen any.
records.zomi: Ka ni in khut zang thakhatin a sik leh sum hong tung ding hi, a ci a, ahi zongin bangmah i mu ngei kei uh hi.

records.english: A candle by the window shows that someone in the house is waiting for a loved one to return.
records.zomi: Tukkhuak kiang-a khawimeivaak in inn sung-a mi khat in a it mi a ciah kik ding a ngak hi, ci a lak hi.

records.english: We hang green branches over the door at the new year to welcome fresh beginnings.
records.zomi: Kum thak ciangin kipatna thakte muak dingin kongkhak tung lam ah sing hiang eng i bulh uh hi.

records.english: When a child is born in our family, a tree is planted to grow alongside them.
records.zomi: I innkuan ah naupang khat a suah ciangin amah tawh khawm-a khang dingin sing khat kisuan hi.

records.english: Is a ring passed down through the family worth more than new jewellery?
records.zomi: Innkuan sungah kipia khia zungbuh khat kizeekna van thak sangin a manpha zaw hiam?

records.english: The colour white means something different in our family than it does in many other places.
records.zomi: Rong kang in mun dang tampi sangin i innkuan ah khiatna tuam a nei hi.

records.english: We light a lamp on the anniversary of my grandfather's death.
records.zomi: Ka pu' sihni kum cinna ciangin meivaak khat i tawisak uh hi.

records.english: Some symbols are shared by many cultures, while others belong to a single village.
records.zomi: Ciamtehna pawl khat ngeina tampi in a kihawm uh a, a dangte khua khat bek' ahi hi.

records.english: When young people leave the village, many take a handful of earth from home with them.
records.zomi: Khangnote in khua a nusiat uh ciangin tampi in inn pan leivui khut tum khat a tawi uh hi.

records.english: My grandfather wears a small stone on a string, which he says connects him to his birthplace.
records.zomi: Ka pu in a suahna mun tawh hong kizopsak hi, a cih suang neu khat khau tawh a bulh hi.

records.english: At the harvest festival, the first basket of grain is set aside as a thank-you.
records.zomi: Khuado pawi ah lungdamna-in buh bawm masa pen kikoih tuam hi.

records.english: In our family, a bowl of water left by the door welcomes guests after a long walk.
