records.zomi: I innkuan ah kongkhak kiang-a koih tui kuang khat in khualzin sau khit-a mikhualte a muak hi.

records.english: Every carving on the old house had a story, and my father knew all of them.
records.zomi: Inn lui tung-a sing khen khempeuh in tangthu a nei a, ka pa in a khempeuh a thei hi.

records.english: When the elders bless a new house, they sprinkle water in every room.
records.zomi: Mi upate in inn thak thupha a piak uh ciangin khan khempeuh ah tui a theh uh hi.

records.english: Who taught you the meaning of the patterns on the old baskets?
records.zomi: Bawm luite tung-a limte' khiatna kua in hong sinsak hiam?

records.english: Why do people in your family touch the doorframe before they leave on a journey?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na innkuan-a mite khualzin ding a pai ma-un kongkhak khuam a khoih uh hiam?

records.english: Do the colours on the festival clothes mean anything?
records.zomi: Pawi puan tung-a rongte in khiatna khat a nei hiam?

records.english: The old village gate was carved with animals that stood for strength, wisdom and patience.
records.zomi: Khua kongpi lui hatna, pilna leh thuakzawhna a lak ganhingte tawh kikhen hi.

records.english: Do your parents still follow any of these customs?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa in hih ngeinate khat peuhpeuh a zui lai uh hiam?

records.english: Can you explain what the knot on the gift means?
records.zomi: Letsong tung-a khau thuah in bang a ci nopna hiam hong genteh thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: In our family, it means that the friendship between the two families is tied for ever.
records.zomi: I innkuan ah innkuan nih kikal-a lawmtakna khantawn-in kikhih hi, cihna hi.

records.english: Why do you always leave one seat empty at the festival meal?
records.zomi: Bang hangin pawi an ah tutna khat awng-in na nusia tawntung hiam?

records.english: It's for the relatives who have died, so that they're remembered at the table.
records.zomi: A si khin sanggamte adingin ahi a, dawhkan ah kiphawk nadingun.

records.english: Some symbols are kept secret within a family and shared only with the next generation.
records.zomi: Ciamtehna pawl khat innkuan sungah guk-in kikem a, khangthak zom kiangah bek kihawm hi.

records.english: Giving someone a pair of something, like two cups, is our community's way of wishing them a happy marriage.
records.zomi: Haai nih bang khat nih ciat piak pen i mipi in kiteenna nuam deihsakna lampi ahi hi.

records.english: In your family, why does the bride's family give the groom a knife?
records.zomi: Na innkuan ah bang hangin moneu' innkuan in mopa kiangah namsau a pia uh hiam?

records.english: What symbols does your family use at weddings?
records.zomi: Na innkuan in mopawi ah bang ciamtehna a zang uh hiam?

records.english: Our village uses a particular call of the drum to announce that someone has died.
records.zomi: I khua in mi khat a sih thu zaksak dingin khuang tum dan tuam khat a zang hi.

records.english: Symbols can change their meaning over time, especially when young people use them in new ways.
records.zomi: Ciamtehnate' khiatna hun tawh a kikheel thei a, a diak in khangnote in lampi thak-in a zat uh ciangin.

records.english: Grandma says that a broken mirror should be thrown away carefully, not left in the house.
records.zomi: Pi in kitan mai en limtakin paikhiat ding a, inn sungah nusia lo ding hi, a ci hi.

records.english: I don't believe in lucky signs, but I still wear my grandmother's bracelet on important days.
records.zomi: Kampha ciamtehna ka um kei a, ahi zongin ni thupite ah ka pi' khut ziak ka bulh lai hi.

records.english: In our family, a red thread tied around a baby's wrist is a sign of protection and love.
records.zomi: I innkuan ah naungek' khut kizopna kiim-a kikhih khau san in kemna leh itna lahna ahi hi.

records.english: A symbol can comfort people in hard times, even when they can't explain why.
records.zomi: Ciamtehna khat in bang hang hiam a genteh zawh kei uh zongin hun haksa ah mite a hehnem thei hi.

records.english: Have you ever been given something that has been in your family for generations?
records.zomi: Na innkuan ah khangthu tampi a om khin na khat kipia na ngah ngei hiam?

records.english: My mother says that dropping a spoon means a visitor is coming soon.
records.zomi: Ka nu in kawm khat a kiak leh mikhual khat manlang takin hong pai ding hi, a ci hi.

records.english: At weddings in our village, rice is thrown to wish the couple plenty.
records.zomi: I khua-a mopawi te ah zi leh pasal thakte a tam nadingin buh kipaai hi.

records.english: Can you check whether my answer makes sense before I write it down?
records.zomi: Ka gelh ma-in ka dawnna a khiatna a nei hiam hong en thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Let's make up a word problem about our holiday, and you can solve it.
records.zomi: I tawlngakni tungtang kammal kisim dotna khat phuak ni, nang in na dawng ding hi.

records.english: Our daughter checks the shopping bill against her own calculation every time we go to the supermarket.
records.zomi: I tanu in supermarket i pai vei khempeuh-in van man lai amah' kisim tawh a teh hi.

records.english: The hardest part of a word problem is often deciding which numbers matter.
records.zomi: Kammal kisim dotna khat ah a haksa pen koi nambatte a thupi hiam khensat ahi zel hi.

records.english: If the train to Grandma's takes 3 hours and leaves at 9:15, when do we arrive?
records.zomi: Pi' inn lam meileng nai 3 a la a, nai 9:15 ciangin a pai leh bang hun-in i tung ding hiam?

records.english: At a quarter past twelve, just in time for lunch.
records.zomi: Nai 12 leh minit 15 ciangin, sun an hun tak-in.

records.english: Our son understands word problems much better when they're about his own family.
records.zomi: I tapa in kammal kisim dotnate amah' innkuan tungtang a hih ciangin a thei zaw mahmah hi.

records.english: Our youngest invented a word problem about how many sweets he would need to give one to every child in the school.
records.zomi: I neu pen in sang-a naupang khempeuh khat ciat a piak nadingin an tuithak bangzah a kisam hiam kammal kisim dotna khat a phuak hi.

records.english: Dad turns every car journey into a word problem about speed and distance.
records.zomi: Pa in mawtaw khualzinna khempeuh manlangna leh gamlatna tungtang kammal kisim dotna ah a kheel hi.

records.english: If a family of four eats 2 loaves of bread a week, how many loaves do they need for a month?
records.zomi: Mi li innkuan khat in kal khat ah moh tum 2 a ne uh leh kha khat adingin moh tum bangzah a kisam uh hiam?

records.english: About eight, or nine if the month has five weeks.
records.zomi: Giat bang, kha in kal nga a neih leh kua.

records.english: I set my children one word problem every morning on the walk to school, and the loser has to carry the other's bag.
records.zomi: Sang lam kalna ah zingsang simin ka tate kammal kisim dotna khat ka pia a, a zo lo pa in a dang' ip a pua kul hi.

records.english: My mother used to set us word problems at dinner, and nobody could leave until they'd solved one.
records.zomi: Ka nu in nitak an ah kammal kisim dotna hong pia zel a, khat a dawng zawh ma-un kuamah a pai thei kei uh hi.

records.english: My grandfather sets us word problems from his days as a shopkeeper, with prices from fifty years ago.
records.zomi: Ka pu in a dawl kem hun-a kum sawmnga ma-a man tawh kammal kisim dotna hong pia hi.

records.english: Mum drives 30 kilometres to work and back each day, so how far does she drive in a five-day week?
records.zomi: Nu nasep lam pai leh ciah ni simin kilometre 30 a mawng a, nasep ni nga kal khat ah bangzah gamla a mawng hiam?

records.english: Three hundred kilometres, because it's 60 a day.
records.zomi: Kilometre za thum, ni khat ah 60 ahih manin.

records.english: My sister and I still argue about a word problem our father set us twenty years ago.
records.zomi: Ka u numei leh kei kum sawmnih ma-a i pa' hong piak kammal kisim dotna khat tungtang i kinial lai hi.

records.english: Grandma says that every day of running a house is full of word problems.
records.zomi: Pi in inn kemna ni khempeuh kammal kisim dotna tawh a dim hi, a ci hi.

records.english: For her homework, my daughter wrote a word problem about how many kilometres the family dog walks in a year, and the answer astonished us all.
records.zomi: A inn sinna adingin ka tanu in innkuan ui kum khat ah kilometre bangzah a kal hiam kammal kisim dotna khat a gelh a, a dawnna in i khempeuh lamdang hong sak hi.

records.english: If we plant 4 rows of 6 tomato plants, how many plants do we need?
records.zomi: Mehtuuk kung 6 ciat tuat 4 i suan leh kung bangzah i kisam ding hiam?

records.english: Twenty-four, so we'll have to buy two more trays.
records.zomi: Sawmnih leh li, tua ahih manin bawm nih behlap i lei kul ding hi.

records.english: Can you help me understand what this word problem is actually asking?
records.zomi: Hih kammal kisim dotna in bang a dong taktak hiam theih dingin hong huh thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Word problems about money teach children skills they will use for the rest of their lives.
records.zomi: Sum tungtang kammal kisim dotnate in naupangte a nuntak sung bup a zat ding siamnate a sinsak hi.

records.english: If you get $5 pocket money a week and spend $2 of it, how much do you save in ten weeks?
records.zomi: Kal khat ah sum neu $5 na ngah a, $2 na zat leh kal sawm sungin bangzah na khol ding hiam?

records.english: Thirty dollars, if I don't buy any sweets.
records.zomi: Dollar sawmthum, an tuithak ka lei kei leh.

records.english: My brother writes word problems for his little sister using the names of her toys.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in a nau numei adingin a kimawlna van minte zang-in kammal kisim dotna a gelh hi.

records.english: If Dad's flight leaves at 7:40 and he must be at the airport two hours early, when does he need to arrive?
records.zomi: Pa' vanleng nai 7:40 ciangin a pai a, vanlengtual ah nai nih ma-in a tun kul leh bang hun-in a tun ding hiam?

records.english: By 5:40, so he'll have to leave home before five.
records.zomi: Nai 5:40 ma-in, tua ahih manin nai nga ma-in inn a nusia kul ding hi.

records.english: When my parents planned the wedding budget, it was like solving a giant word problem.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in mopawi sum zat ding a gel uh ciangin kammal kisim dotna lianpi khat dawng bang ahi hi.

records.english: Shall we see who can solve the next problem first?
records.zomi: Dotna zom kua in a masa-in a dawng zo ding hiam i en ding hiam?

records.english: Children often find the reading harder than the calculation in a word problem.
records.zomi: Naupangte in kammal kisim dotna khat ah kisim sangin sim a haksa zaw sa zel uh hi.

records.english: If Grandma is 72 and Grandpa is five years older, how old is Grandpa?
records.zomi: Pi kum 72 a cing a, Pu kum nga a upa zaw leh Pu kum bangzah a cing hiam?

records.english: He's 77.
records.zomi: Kum 77 a cing hi.

records.english: Who can make up a word problem using the ages of everyone at the table?
records.zomi: Dawhkan kiim-a mi khempeuh' kum zang-in kammal kisim dotna kua in a phuak thei ding hiam?

records.english: If the party starts at 4 and lasts two and a half hours, when does it finish?
records.zomi: Kipahna nai 4 ciangin a kipan a, nai nih leh a langkhat a sawt leh bang hun-in a bei ding hiam?

records.english: At half past six.
records.zomi: Nai guk leh a langkhat ciangin.

records.english: If the baby sleeps 14 hours a day, how many hours is she awake?
records.zomi: Naungek ni khat ah nai 14 a ihmut leh nai bangzah a khanglawh hiam?

records.english: Ten hours, though it feels like much more.
records.zomi: Nai sawm, a tam zaw mahmah bangin a kisa hangin.

records.english: It took the whole family an hour to solve my son's homework problem, and we got it wrong.
records.zomi: Ka tapa' inn sinna dotna dawng dingin innkuan bup in nai khat i zang uh a, i khial uh hi.

records.english: There are 25 eggs, and each cake needs 3, so how many cakes can we bake?
records.zomi: Aktui 25 a om a, cake khatciat in 3 a kisam leh cake bangzah i hal thei ding hiam?

records.english: Eight cakes, with one egg left over.
records.zomi: Cake giat, aktui khat a om lai ding hi.

records.english: When parents connect word problems to everyday life, children stop asking why they need maths.
records.zomi: Nu leh pate in kammal kisim dotnate ni simin nuntakna tawh a kizopsak uh ciangin naupangte in bang hangin maths a kisam uh hiam a dong nawn kei uh hi.

records.english: When my daughter got stuck on a word problem, we acted it out with buttons on the kitchen table.
records.zomi: Ka tanu kammal kisim dotna khat ah a ki-it ciangin an huanna inn dawhkan tungah thei-ang tawh i lak uh hi.

records.english: Acting a problem out with toys can make it much easier to understand.
records.zomi: Kimawlna van tawh dotna khat lak in a theih a baih zawsak mahmah thei hi.

records.english: Children who explain how they solved a problem usually understand it better.
records.zomi: Dotna khat bangci a dawng uh hiam a genteh naupangte in a tamzaw-in a thei zaw uh hi.

records.english: If a bag of rice lasts our family 10 days, how many bags do we need for a month?
records.zomi: Buh ip khat i innkuan adingin ni 10 a sawt leh kha khat adingin ip bangzah i kisam ding hiam?

records.english: Three bags, to be safe.
records.zomi: Ip thum, bit nadingin.

records.english: My niece hated word problems until her uncle started setting them about football scores.
records.zomi: Ka tunu in a pa neu in bawlung gah tungtang a piak kipat dong kammal kisim dotnate a huat hi.

records.english: Word problems about pocket money always seem to get my son's full attention.
records.zomi: Sum neu tungtang kammal kisim dotnate in ka tapa' lungsim a la khempeuh tawntung bang hi.

records.english: Working out how much paint we needed for the bedroom was the most useful word problem my son has ever solved.
records.zomi: Lupna khan adingin zeek bangzah i kisam hiam sim pen ka tapa' a dawn ngei kammal kisim dotna phatuam pen ahi hi.

records.english: My grandmother solves word problems in her head faster than anyone with a calculator.
records.zomi: Ka pi in calculator nei mi khatpeuh sangin a lu sungah kammal kisim dotnate manlang zaw-in a dawng hi.

records.english: We have 18 cousins and 3 cars, so how many cousins go in each car?
records.zomi: Sanggam 18 leh mawtaw 3 i nei uh a, mawtaw khatciat ah sanggam bangzah a tuang ding uh hiam?

records.english: Six in each car, though that's far too many for one car.
records.zomi: Mawtaw khatciat ah guk, mawtaw khat adingin a tam lua mahmah hangin.

records.english: A cake is cut into 12 slices and 5 people eat two each, so how many slices are left?
records.zomi: Cake khat tum 12 ah kiat a, mi 5 in nih ciat a nek uh leh tum bangzah a om lai hiam?

records.english: Two slices, and I'd like one of them.
records.zomi: Tum nih, a khat ka deih hi.

records.english: If the rent goes up from $600 to $650 a month, how much more do we pay in a year?
records.zomi: Inn man kha khat ah $600 pan $650 ah a khan leh kum khat ah bangzah behlap i pia ding hiam?

records.english: Six hundred dollars more, because it's $50 extra every month.
records.zomi: Dollar za guk behlap, kha simin $50 behlap ahih manin.

records.english: Thank you for helping my son with his word problems; he's much more confident now.
records.zomi: Ka tapa' kammal kisim dotnate ah na huh manin ka lungdam hi; tu-in a kimuang zaw mahmah hi.

records.english: Using real objects, such as coins or beans, helps young children picture a word problem.
records.zomi: Sum neu hiam be bang na taktak zat in naupang neute in kammal kisim dotna khat a lim a muh nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Word problems are easier when you underline the question first.
records.zomi: Dotna a masa-in a nuai ah na khang leh kammal kisim dotnate a baih zaw hi.

records.english: Shall we have a quiet Sunday at home or visit the cousins?
records.zomi: Inn ah Nipini dai khat i nei ding hiam, sanggamte i veh ding hiam?

records.english: Auntie prefers to give money as a present, because she says she never knows what young people like.
records.zomi: Ni in khangnote bang a deih uh hiam a theih ngei loh manin letsong-in sum piak a deih zaw hi.

records.english: If you'd rather not come to the family dinner, just tell me honestly.
records.zomi: Innkuan nitak an ah na pai nuam kei leh dik takin hong gen mah in.

records.english: What kind of present would you like for your retirement, Dad?
records.zomi: Pa aw, na nasep tawpna adingin bang letsong na deih hiam?

records.english: Nothing that needs batteries or instructions, please.
records.zomi: Battery hiam zatdan thuhilhna a kisam bangmah hi lo, maw.

records.english: When our tastes in music differ, we take it in turns to choose in the car.
records.zomi: I la deih dan a kibang loh ciangin mawtaw sungah a kizui-in i teel uh hi.

records.english: Shall I drive, or would you like to?
records.zomi: Kei in ka mawng ding hiam, nang na mawng nuam hiam?

records.english: What pet would you like to have when you're older?
records.zomi: Na upat ciangin bang ganhing na khawi nuam hiam?

records.english: A dog, because I want someone to go walking with.
records.zomi: Ui, ka paipih ding mi khat ka deih ahih manin.

records.english: Some people prefer a few close friends to a wide circle of acquaintances.
records.zomi: Mi pawl khat in lawm kinai tawmno a deih zaw uh a, kimuh khin mi tampi sangin.

records.english: Choosing a name for the baby showed us how differently the two of us think.
records.zomi: Naungek min teel in i nih bangzah tuamtuam-in i ngaihsun hiam hong lak hi.

records.english: Do you prefer to celebrate your birthday on the day or at the weekend?
records.zomi: Na pianni a ni taktak ah na lawp nuam zaw hiam, kal tawp ah hiam?

records.english: Asking children about their preferences, even for small things, helps them feel respected.
records.zomi: Naupangte kiangah a deihnate, nate neu adingin zong dot in amaute kizahtak bangin a kisak sak hi.

records.english: Do you prefer reading your children stories or making them up?
records.zomi: Na tate kiangah tangthu sim na deih zaw hiam, phuak na deih zaw hiam?

records.english: Making them up, because then I can include the dog.
records.zomi: Phuak, tua ahih leh ui ka kihel sak thei ahih manin.

records.english: Whatever you'd prefer is fine with me.
records.zomi: Na deih zaw khatpeuh kei adingin a hoih hi.

records.english: My partner prefers to plan everything, while I like to decide on the day.
records.zomi: Ka pasal hiam zi in a khempeuh gel a deih zaw a, kei in tua ni ah khensat ka deih hi.

records.english: Would you rather we cooked together tonight or ordered something?
records.zomi: Tu zanin khawmin an i huan ding hiam, khat peuhpeuh i sap ding hiam?

records.english: Let's cook together; it's more fun than waiting for a delivery.
records.zomi: Khawmin huan ni; tunsakna ngak sangin a nuam zaw hi.

records.english: Would you rather spend your birthday with friends or with the family?
records.zomi: Na pianni lawmte tawh na zang nuam zaw hiam, innkuan tawh hiam?

records.english: With the family in the afternoon and friends in the evening.
records.zomi: Nitak lam ah innkuan tawh, zan ah lawmte tawh.

records.english: Which room do you like best in the new house?
records.zomi: Inn thak ah koi khan na deih pen hiam?

records.english: The kitchen, because the morning sun comes straight in.
records.zomi: An huanna inn, zingsang ni a tang-in a lut ahih manin.

records.english: Dad's preference for the same holiday every year has become a family joke.
records.zomi: Kum simin tawlngakni kibang Pa' deihna innkuan nuihzakna khat a hi ta hi.

records.english: Preferences in a family can cause arguments, but they can also be a source of jokes for years.
records.zomi: Innkuan sung-a deihnate in kinialna a piangsak thei a, ahi zongin kum tampi nuihzakna kipatna zong a hi thei hi.

records.english: Would you move abroad for a better job, even if it meant leaving the family?
records.zomi: Innkuan nusia cihna hi zongin nasep hoih zaw adingin gamdang ah na suan ding hiam?

records.english: Only for a few years, and only if I could fly home often.
records.zomi: Kum tawmno bek, inn ah tamvei ka leng thei leh bek.

records.english: My grandfather has always preferred tea in a glass rather than in a cup.
records.zomi: Ka pu in niangtui haai sangin glass sungah a deih zaw tawntung hi.

records.english: Our son prefers baths, while my daughter insists on showers like a grown-up.
records.zomi: I tapa in kisilna bel a deih zaw a, ka tanu in mi upa bangin tui luang nuai-a kisil a ngen hi.

records.english: Do you like the bedroom warm or cool at night?
records.zomi: Zan ciangin lupna khan a lum na deih hiam, a vot na deih hiam?

records.english: Cool, even in winter, which drives my wife mad.
records.zomi: A vot, phalbi ciangin zong, tua in ka zi a hehsak hi.

records.english: I'd rather spend a quiet evening playing cards with my grandparents than go to a party where I hardly know anyone.
records.zomi: Ka theih tawm mite' kipahna khat ah pai sangin ka pu leh pi tawh card kimawl-in nitak dai khat zat ka deih zaw hi.

records.english: When it comes to holidays, my husband likes the mountains and I like the sea, so we alternate.
records.zomi: Tawlngakni thu ah ka pasal in mual a deih a, kei in tuipi ka deih ahih manin a kizui-in i pai uh hi.

records.english: My sister prefers a quiet holiday by a lake, whereas I need a busy city.
records.zomi: Ka u numei in dil gei-a tawlngakni dai khat a deih zaw a, kei in khuapi buai khat ka kisam hi.

records.english: My grandmother prefers to sit by the window, where she can watch the whole street and greet everyone by name.
records.zomi: Ka pi in lampi bup a en-a mi khempeuh a min tawh a hopih theih tukkhuak kiangah tu a deih zaw hi.

records.english: Our children prefer their grandmother's stories to any cartoon on television.
records.zomi: I tate in television-a cartoon khatpeuh sangin a pi uh' tangthute a deih zaw uh hi.

records.english: When everyone in the family wants something different for dinner, we each choose one dish.
records.zomi: Innkuan-a mi khempeuh in nitak an adingin a tuamtuam a deih uh ciangin an khat ciat i teel uh hi.

records.english: Teenagers often prefer to spend time with friends rather than family, which is perfectly normal.
records.zomi: Tangval-tangnute in innkuan sangin lawmte tawh hun zat a deih zaw zel uh a, tua pen a ngeina mah ahi hi.

records.english: Which do you prefer, Grandma's cooking or Mum's?
records.zomi: Koi na deih zaw hiam, Pi' an huan hiam, Nu' an huan hiam?

records.english: I'm not answering that question while they're both in the room.
records.zomi: A nih in khan sungah a om laitakun tua dotna ka dawng kei ding hi.

records.english: When two sets of grandparents prefer completely different ways of raising children, the parents can feel caught in the middle.
records.zomi: Pu leh pi nih pawlte in naupang khanglianna dan tuamtuam vekpi a deih uh ciangin nu leh pate in a lai-ah kikhih bangin a kisa thei uh hi.

records.english: Is it all right if I choose the film tonight?
records.zomi: Tu zanin film kei in ka teel leh a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: Some couples prefer to keep their money separate, while others share everything.
records.zomi: Zi leh pasal pawl khat in a sum uh a tuam-in kem a deih uh a, a dangte in a khempeuh a kihawm uh hi.

records.english: My mother prefers that we call before visiting, even though she always says we're welcome.
records.zomi: Ka nu in hong kimuak hi, a ci tawntung hangin a veh ma-un sam dingin a deih zaw hi.

records.english: In a big family, everyone's preferences can't be met every time, so we take it in order of birthdays.
records.zomi: Innkuan lian khat ah mi khempeuh' deihnate vei khempeuh-in kizopsak thei lo ahih manin pianni zui-in i bawl uh hi.

records.english: How many guests would you like at your wedding?
records.zomi: Na mopawi ah mikhual bangzah na deih hiam?

records.english: A small one, with just our families and closest friends.
records.zomi: A neu khat, i innkuante leh lawm kinai pente bek tawh.

records.english: Our son prefers to do his homework straight after school, while our daughter waits until after dinner.
records.zomi: I tapa in sang khit pah-in a inn sinna bawl a deih zaw a, i tanu in nitak an khit dong a ngak hi.

records.english: Do you prefer your grandparents' village or the city?
records.zomi: Na pu leh pi' khua na deih zaw hiam, khuapi hiam?

records.english: The village, because I can ride my cousin's horse there.
records.zomi: Khua, tua ah ka sanggam' sakol ka tuang thei ahih manin.

records.english: My little brother prefers the cardboard box to the toy that came in it.
records.zomi: Ka nau pasal in a sung-a hong pai kimawlna van sangin lai bawm a deih zaw hi.

records.english: My brother would rather fix an old bicycle than buy a new one.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in a thak lei sangin siiksakol lui bawlphat a deih zaw hi.

records.english: My grandfather prefers handwritten letters to video calls, even though the letters take a week.
records.zomi: Ka pu in laite kal khat a sawt hangin video sapna sangin khut tawh kigelh lai a deih zaw hi.

records.english: Shall we go to the beach or the park this afternoon?
records.zomi: Tu nitak lam tuipi gei ah i pai ding hiam, huan ah hiam?

records.english: My parents prefer to visit us rather than have us all visit them, because travelling with grandchildren is easier for them.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in tute tawh khualzin sangin amaute adingin a baih zaw ahih manin eite khempeuh in amaute i veh sangin eite veh a deih zaw uh hi.

records.english: Do your children prefer sweet or savoury snacks?
records.zomi: Na tate in an neu a tui hiam a al hiam a deih zaw uh hiam?

records.english: My daughter prefers dresses with pockets, so that she can carry her treasures.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in a manpha nate a pua theih nadingin ip nei puan a deih zaw hi.

records.english: Our family has always preferred simple celebrations to expensive ones, partly from habit and partly because nobody wants to be in debt.
records.zomi: I innkuan in a ngeina hangin leh kuamah leiba ah om nuam lo ahih manin man tam lawpna sangin lawpna baih a deih zaw tawntung hi.

records.english: Where should we have the reunion, at our house or at a restaurant?
records.zomi: Innkuan kikhopna koi ah i nei ding hiam, i inn ah hiam, an zuakna inn ah hiam?

records.english: At our house, because the children can play in the garden.
records.zomi: I inn ah, naupangte huan sungah a kimawl thei ding uh ahih manin.

records.english: What are we doing for Mum's birthday this year?
records.zomi: Tu kum Nu' pianni adingin bang i bawl ding hiam?

records.english: A picnic by the lake, with all her favourite food.
records.zomi: A an it pen khempeuh tawh dil gei-a an nekkhawmna.

records.english: Family celebrations can be stressful when relatives who don't get along are in the same room.
records.zomi: Kituak lo sanggamte khan khat sungah a om uh ciangin innkuan lawpnate a lungkhamhuai thei hi.

records.english: Even the smallest achievement can be a reason for a family celebration.
records.zomi: Zawhna neu pen zong innkuan lawpna hang khat a hi thei hi.

records.english: When the twins turned eighteen, we threw one party but baked two cakes.
records.zomi: Apengte kum sawm leh giat a cin uh ciangin kipahna khat i bawl uh a, ahi zongin cake nih i hal uh hi.

records.english: Could the cousins plan a treasure hunt for the children during the party?
records.zomi: Kipahna sungin sanggamte in naupangte adingin van zonna kimawlna a gel thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: The whole family came to the airport to welcome my cousin home after five years abroad.
records.zomi: Kum nga gamdang-a a om khit ciangin ka sanggam inn ah muak dingin innkuan bup vanlengtual ah a pai uh hi.

records.english: Every year on his birthday, my brother insists on the same chocolate cake our mother made when he was five.
records.zomi: Kum simin a pianni ciangin ka sanggam pasal in kum nga a cin lai-a i nu' bawl chocolate cake kibang mah a ngen den hi.

records.english: Family celebrations are a chance for children to hear stories from older relatives.
records.zomi: Innkuan lawpnate in naupangte in sanggam upate pan tangthu a zak nading hun ahi hi.

records.english: On the morning of my parents' fortieth anniversary, we filled their house with photos from every year of their marriage.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa' kiteenna kum sawmli cinna zingsang ciangin a inn uh a kiteenna kum khempeuh' lim tawh i dimsak uh hi.

records.english: My mother walked from room to room, laughing and crying at the same time.
records.zomi: Ka nu khan khat pan khan khat ah a kal a, hun kibang-in a nuih a, a kap hi.

records.english: Dad simply sat down and said he had never felt so lucky.
records.zomi: Pa a tu bek a, tu bangin kampha a kisa ngei kei hi, a ci hi.

records.english: The children made a banner that said "Welcome home" for their grandmother's return from hospital.
records.zomi: Naupangte in a pi uh damdawi inn pan a ciah kik nadingin “Inn ah hong kimuak hi” ci kammal puan khat a bawl uh hi.

records.english: We'll celebrate properly when your father is out of hospital.
records.zomi: Na pa damdawi inn pan a pusuak ciangin hoih takin i lawp ding hi.

records.english: My mother cried happy tears when all her children arrived home for her birthday.
records.zomi: A tate khempeuh a pianni adingin inn a tun uh ciangin ka nu in lungdamna kahna a kap hi.

records.english: We celebrated my parents' move into their new flat with a meal on the floor, because the table hadn't arrived.
records.zomi: Dawhkan a tun nai loh manin ka nu leh ka pa' inn thak suanna lei tungah an tawh i lawp uh hi.

records.english: We celebrated the news with a phone call to every relative before breakfast.
records.zomi: Zingsang an ma-in sanggam khempeuh phone tawh sam-in thu i lawp uh hi.

records.english: We had the old photographs restored and framed as a gift for my grandparents' anniversary.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh pi' kiteenna kum cinna letsong-in lim luite i bawlphat-in bawm sungah i koih uh hi.

records.english: We threw a party for my sister when she finally finished her nursing degree.
records.zomi: Ka u numei in a nurse degree a zawh ciangin kipahna khat i bawl sak uh hi.

records.english: At my niece's first birthday, she was more interested in the wrapping paper than the presents.
records.zomi: Ka tunu' pianni masa ah a letsongte sangin a tuamna lai a deih zaw hi.

records.english: Can you help me hang the balloons before the guests arrive?
records.zomi: Mikhualte a tun ma-un balloon te bulh dingin hong huh thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Shall we take a family photo before anyone leaves?
records.zomi: Kuamah a pai ma-un innkuan lim khat i la ding hiam?

records.english: We always light a candle for the relatives who can't be with us at family celebrations.
records.zomi: Innkuan lawpna ah om thei lo sanggamte adingin khawimeivaak khat i tawisak tawntung uh hi.

records.english: A simple family meal can feel like a celebration when everyone is finally together.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh a tawpna-ah a kikhawm uh ciangin innkuan an baih khat lawpna bangin a kisa thei hi.

records.english: My cousin organised a family reunion, and relatives came from four different countries.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam in innkuan kikhopna khat a bawl a, sanggamte gam li pan hong pai uh hi.

records.english: Celebrating together after a difficult year reminded us how much we had to be thankful for.
records.zomi: Kum haksa khat khit ciangin khawmin lawp in lungdam ding bangzah i nei hiam hong phawksak hi.

records.english: Who's making the speech at Grandpa's retirement party?
records.zomi: Pu' nasep tawpna kipahna ah kua in thu a gen ding hiam?

records.english: My uncle, because he's worked with him for thirty years.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu, amah tawh kum sawmthum nasep a sem khin ahih manin.

records.english: My brother flew home as a surprise for our mother's sixtieth birthday and hid behind the door.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal i nu' kum sawmguk pianni adingin lamdang sakna-in inn ah a leng a, kongkhak nung ah a bu hi.

records.english: A celebration doesn't need to be expensive to be memorable.
records.zomi: Lawpna khat phawk nop a hih nadingin man tam a kisam kei hi.

records.english: Shall we invite the neighbours to the baby's naming ceremony?
records.zomi: Naungek' min phuakna pawi ah innvengte i sam ding hiam?

records.english: Our son was so excited about his birthday that he woke the whole house at five in the morning to ask whether it was time for presents yet.
records.zomi: I tapa a pianni a lungphamuan mahmah ahih manin letsong hun a tung hiam dong dingin zingsang nai nga ciangin inn bup a phongkhia hi.

records.english: At the end of every family celebration, my father makes everyone stand together for one last photo.
records.zomi: Innkuan lawpna khempeuh' tawpna ah ka pa in lim nunung khat adingin mi khempeuh khawmin a dingsak hi.

records.english: Dad gave a short, funny speech at my brother's wedding that nobody will ever forget.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal' mopawi ah Pa in kuamah in a mangngilh ngei lo ding thugenna tom leh nuihhuai khat a gen hi.

records.english: When my sister passed her driving test, we celebrated by letting her drive us all to the beach.
records.zomi: Ka u numei mawtaw mawng sitna a zawh ciangin eite khempeuh tuipi gei dong a mawng dingin phal-in i lawp uh hi.

records.english: Our family celebrates every child's graduation, from nursery to university.
records.zomi: I innkuan in naupang sang pan sangpi dong naupang khempeuh' sang zawhna a lawp hi.

records.english: The party went on so late that the youngest guests fell asleep on the sofa.
records.zomi: Kipahna zan lai dong a sawt ahih manin mikhual neu pente sofa tungah a ihmu uh hi.

records.english: For the family photo, everyone wore the same shade of blue, which made the children giggle and the photographer despair.
records.zomi: Innkuan lim adingin mi khempeuh dum kibang a silh uh a, naupangte a nuihsak a, lim lakpa a lungkiasak hi.

records.english: How did you celebrate your engagement?
records.zomi: Na kiteen kiciamna bangci na lawp hiam?

records.english: We had a quiet dinner with both our families, and my father cried.
records.zomi: I innkuan nih tawh nitak an dai khat i nei uh a, ka pa a kap hi.

records.english: Our family's biggest celebration of the year is the harvest dinner at my uncle's farm.
records.zomi: I innkuan' kum sung-a lawpna lian pen ka pa neu' lo-a Khuado nitak an ahi hi.

records.english: Who will cut the cake, the birthday girl or her grandfather?
records.zomi: Cake kua in a at ding hiam, pianni numei naupang hiam, a pu hiam?

records.english: Family celebrations are often remembered for small surprises rather than for the food or the decorations.
records.zomi: Innkuan lawpnate an hiam kizeeknate hangin sangin lamdang sakna neunote hangin kiphawk zel hi.

records.english: Did you hear that my sister's baby was born last night?
records.zomi: Ka u numei' naungek zan in a suak hi, na za hiam?

records.english: Celebrating together helps families get through the hard times as well as enjoy the good ones.
records.zomi: Khawmin lawp in innkuante hun hoih a nuamsak uh bek hi lo-in hun haksa a kantan nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Shall I bake the cake, or would you rather buy one?
records.zomi: Cake ka hal ding hiam, khat na lei nuam zaw hiam?

records.english: Thank you all for coming; it means the world to us.
records.zomi: Hong pai na vekpi-un ka lungdam hi; eite adingin a thupi mahmah hi.

records.english: Who's bringing the music for the family party?
records.zomi: Innkuan kipahna adingin la kua in a tawi ding hiam?

records.english: Celebrations look different in every family, but they all say the same thing: you matter to us.
records.zomi: Lawpnate innkuan khatciat ah a kibang lo a, ahi zongin a khempeuh in thu kibang a gen hi: nang eite adingin na thupi hi.

records.english: The party was such a success that we've decided to make it a yearly event.
records.zomi: Kipahna a hoih mahmah ahih manin kum simin bawl dingin i khensat uh hi.

records.english: The best present at my grandfather's party was a song written by his great-grandchildren.
records.zomi: Ka pu' kipahna-a letsong hoih pen a tute' tate' phuak la khat ahi hi.

records.english: Does your family celebrate name days as well as birthdays?
records.zomi: Na innkuan in pianni bek hi lo-in min ni zong a lawp uh hiam?

records.english: Celebrating a grandparent's birthday in hospital taught us that the place matters less than the people.
records.zomi: Damdawi inn ah pu hiam pi khat' pianni lawp in mun sangin mite a thupi zaw hi, ci hong sinsak hi.

records.english: Please don't tell your father about the party; it's a surprise.
records.zomi: Na pa kiangah kipahna thu gen kei in; lamdang sakna ahi hi.

records.english: Our children still talk about the year Grandpa dressed up as a clown for their birthday.
records.zomi: I tate in Pu in a pianni uh adingin clown bangin a kisilh kum a gen lai uh hi.

records.english: When my grandfather turned a hundred, five generations of the family gathered in his garden.
records.zomi: Ka pu kum za a cin ciangin innkuan khangthak nga a huan sungah a kikhawm uh hi.

records.english: Who's going to look after the baby during the wedding?
records.zomi: Mopawi sungin naungek kua in a kem ding hiam?

records.english: My parents still celebrate the anniversary of the day they arrived in this country.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in hih gam a tun uh ni' kum cinna a lawp lai uh hi.

records.english: Let's each write a message for Grandma's birthday book.
records.zomi: Pi' pianni laibu adingin thu khat ciat i gelh ni.

records.english: Every Mother's Day, my children bring me breakfast in bed, and the kitchen is a disaster afterwards.
records.zomi: Mother's Day simin ka tate in lupna tungah zingsang an hong tawi uh a, a nung ciangin an huanna inn a buai mahmah hi.

records.english: Encouragement from an older sibling can sometimes mean more than encouragement from a parent.
records.zomi: U khat pan hanthawnna in nu hiam pa pan hanthawnna sangin a thupi zaw thei hi.

records.english: Shall I call her tonight, or would a letter give her more encouragement?
records.zomi: Tu zanin amah ka sam ding hiam, lai khat in hanthawnna tam zaw a pia ding hiam?

records.english: Can you encourage your cousin to apply for the job, even if she thinks she isn't good enough?
records.zomi: Na sanggam numei in a hoih kicing kei hi, a ci zongin nasep a nget nadingin na hanthawn thei ding hiam?

records.english: Encouragement given regularly in small doses does more good than rare grand gestures.
records.zomi: Tawmno-in a tawntung-a kipia hanthawnna in vei tawmno-a nate lianpi sangin a hoih zaw hi.

records.english: After failing his driving test twice, my brother had to decide whether to give up.
records.zomi: Mawtaw mawng sitna nihvei a zawh loh khit ciangin ka sanggam pasal in a khawl ding hiam a khensat kul hi.

records.english: Our father didn't lecture him; he just offered to take him out practising every Sunday.
records.zomi: I pa in amah thu a hilh kei a; Nipini simin kisin dingin a paipih ding hi, a ci bek hi.

records.english: Three months later, my brother passed, and he still says those Sundays mattered more than the lessons.
records.zomi: Kha thum khit ciangin ka sanggam pasal a zo a, sinnate sangin tua Nipini te a thupi zaw hi, a ci lai hi.

records.english: A simple thumbs-up from the coach meant more to my son than a medal.
records.zomi: Coach pan khut liapna baih khat in ka tapa adingin medal sangin a thupi zaw hi.

records.english: Children often need more encouragement after a small mistake than after a big success.
records.zomi: Naupangte in zawhna lian khat khit sangin khialhna neu khat khit ciangin hanthawnna tam zaw a kisam zel uh hi.

records.english: When hope runs low, a small, achievable goal works better than a big dream.
records.zomi: Lametna a niam ciangin tupna neu a tun theih khat in mang lianpi sangin a hoih zaw hi.

records.english: A friend who believes in you can change the way you see yourself.
records.zomi: Nangmah hong upna lawm khat in nangmah na kimuh dan a kheel thei hi.

records.english: Should I encourage my son to try again or let him rest for a while?
records.zomi: Ka tapa sin kik dingin ka hanthawn ding hiam, hun tawmno tawl dingin ka phal ding hiam?

records.english: Let him rest first, and then remind him how close he came.
records.zomi: A masa-in tawl sak inla, tua khit ciangin bangzah a nai hiam phawksak in.

records.english: A little hope is better than none, even when the road ahead is long.
records.zomi: Ma lam lampi a sau hangin lametna tawmno in om lo sangin a hoih zaw hi.

records.english: My teacher's encouragement made me choose science, even though I was afraid of it.
records.zomi: Ka saya' hanthawnna in ka lau hangin science hong teelsak hi.

records.english: Encouragement from someone who has failed and tried again carries a special weight.
records.zomi: A zo lo-a sin kik mi khat pan hanthawnna in gikna tuam khat a pua hi.

records.english: Shall we celebrate the small progress now instead of waiting for the final result?
records.zomi: A tawpna gah ngak sangin tu-in khanna neu i lawp ding hiam?

records.english: Do you think it's kinder to be honest about the risks or to focus only on hope?
records.zomi: Lauhuainate tungtang thu dik gen a hehpihna zaw hiam, lametna bek tungah koih a hehpihna zaw hiam na ci hiam?

records.english: Do you think encouragement or criticism helps people improve more?
records.zomi: Hanthawnna in hiam simmawhna in mite a hoihsak zaw hiam na ci hiam?

records.english: I'm so proud of how hard you've worked this year.
records.zomi: Tu kum hanciam takin na sep manin nang tungah ka kipak mahmah hi.

records.english: Would a quick message help him before his exam?
records.zomi: A sitna ma-in thu tomno khat in a huh ding hiam?

records.english: Thank you for not giving up on me.
records.zomi: Hong nusia lo manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: Some people need gentle encouragement, while others respond best to a friendly challenge.
records.zomi: Mi pawl khat in hanthawnna nem a kisam uh a, a dangte in lawm taka sitna tawh a hoih pen-in a dawng uh hi.

records.english: Which helps you more when you're down, a joke or a hug?
records.zomi: Na lungsim a niam ciangin koi in hong huh zaw hiam, nuihzakna hiam, pomna hiam?

records.english: Telling someone that you're proud of them can matter enormously, at any age.
records.zomi: Mi khat kiangah nang tungah ka kipak hi, ci pen kum khatpeuh ah a thupi mahmah thei hi.

records.english: Sometimes the most encouraging thing you can do is to listen without trying to fix anything.
records.zomi: A hun pawl ah hanthawnna lian pen khat peuhpeuh bawlphat sawm lo-in ngaikhia ahi hi.

records.english: Hope is easier to hold on to when you share it with others.
records.zomi: Lametna mi dangte tawh na hawm ciangin len den a baih zaw hi.

records.english: The best encouragement I ever received was a teacher writing "I believe in you" at the bottom of my essay.
records.zomi: Ka ngah ngei hanthawnna hoih pen saya khat in ka laigelh' a nuai lam ah “Kong um hi” a gelh ahi hi.

records.english: Shall I come to your interview with you for moral support?
records.zomi: Lungsim huhna adingin na kidotna ah kong zui ding hiam?

records.english: Telling children they're clever is less helpful than praising how hard they've worked.
records.zomi: Naupangte kiangah na pil hi, ci in bangzah hanciam takin a sep uh phat sangin a huh tawm zaw hi.

records.english: Our team encourages each other with a quick message before every big presentation.
records.zomi: I pawl in presentation lian khempeuh ma-in thu tomno khat tawh a kihanthawn uh hi.

records.english: Whose encouragement do you remember from your childhood?
records.zomi: Na naupan lai pan kua' hanthawnna na phawk hiam?

records.english: Hearing that others have overcome the same problem can give you more hope than any advice.
records.zomi: Mi dangte in buaina kibang a zo uh hi, ci zak in thuhilhna khatpeuh sangin lametna tam zaw hong pia thei hi.

records.english: My grandfather's favourite encouragement is to remind us how far we've already come.
records.zomi: Ka pu' hanthawnna it pen bangzah gamla i pai khin uh hiam hong phawksak ahi hi.

records.english: Do you two find encouragement more helpful from friends or from family?
records.zomi: Na nih in lawmte pan hiam innkuan pan hiam hanthawnna a phatuam zaw na sa uh hiam?

records.english: Hope spreads in a family when one person refuses to give up.
records.zomi: Innkuan khat ah mi khat in a khawl nuam loh ciangin lametna a kizel hi.

records.english: Choosing to see a setback as a lesson rather than a failure takes practice.
records.zomi: Dalna khat zawh lohna sangin sinna bangin muh dingin teel in kisinna a kisam hi.

records.english: You're nearly there, so don't stop now.
records.zomi: Na tun dek khin hi, tu-in khawl kei in.

records.english: Encouragement that focuses on the next step is easier to act on than general praise.
records.zomi: A zom khehlap tungah a kingat hanthawnna in phatna tavuan sangin bawl a baih zaw hi.

records.english: Encouraging someone to keep trying is different from pushing them when they need to stop.
records.zomi: Mi khat sin den dingin hanthawn pen a khawl kisam laitakun nawh tawh a kibang kei hi.

records.english: My grandmother encourages us with stories, whereas my grandfather simply says, "Keep going."
records.zomi: Ka pi in tangthute tawh hong hanthawn a, ka pu in, “Pai den un,” ci bek hi.

records.english: Is it more helpful to tell someone they can do it or to offer practical help?
records.zomi: Mi khat kiangah na zo hi, ci a phatuam zaw hiam, huhna taktak piak a phatuam zaw hiam?

records.english: Practical help usually, because kind words alone can feel empty when someone is struggling.
records.zomi: A tamzaw-in huhna taktak, mi khat a haksat ciangin kammal nem bek in a awng bangin a kisa thei ahih manin.

records.english: Mum's notes in our lunch boxes kept us going through exam season.
records.zomi: Nu in i an bawm sungah a koih lai neute in sitna hun sungin hong kalsuansak hi.

records.english: When everything seemed hopeless, my aunt reminded us of all the hard times we had already survived.
records.zomi: Na khempeuh lametna om lo bangin a kilan ciangin ka ni in i kantan khin hun haksa khempeuh hong phawksak hi.

records.english: Next time you feel like giving up, call me first.
records.zomi: A zom vei-in na khawl nop ciangin a masa-in hong sam in.

records.english: Some days, encouragement means saying nothing and just sitting beside someone.
records.zomi: Ni pawl khat ah hanthawnna in bangmah gen lo-in mi khat kiangah tu bek cihna hi.

records.english: When my neighbour lost his job, we helped him look for work instead of just telling him not to worry.
records.zomi: Ka innveng a nasep a mansuah ciangin lungkham kei in, ci bek sangin nasep a zon nadingin i huh uh hi.

records.english: Do you prefer someone to cheer you on loudly or to support you quietly?
records.zomi: Mi khat in aw ngaih takin hong hanthawn na deih zaw hiam, dai takin hong huh na deih zaw hiam?

records.english: Quietly, because loud cheering makes me more nervous.
records.zomi: Dai takin, kikou-a hanthawnna in hong lausak zaw ahih manin.

records.english: Some people find hope in faith, while others find it in the people around them.
records.zomi: Mi pawl khat in upna ah lametna a mu uh a, a dangte in a kiim-a mite ah a mu uh hi.

records.english: Hope can grow from a single good day, even after a long run of bad ones.
records.zomi: Ni hoih lo tampi khit ciangin zong ni hoih khat pan lametna a khang thei hi.

records.english: A card from a stranger gave my mother more hope than she expected during her treatment.
records.zomi: Ka nu' damdawi zatna sungin mikhual khat' card in a lamen sangin lametna tam zaw a pia hi.

records.english: My daughter encourages her little brother by letting him win at races, though he doesn't know it.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in a nau pasal a tai kidemna ah a zo sak-in a hanthawn a, ahi zongin amah in a thei kei hi.

records.english: A short message of hope at the right moment can mean more than a long speech.
records.zomi: Hun kilawm-a lametna thu tomno khat in thugenna sau khat sangin a thupi zaw thei hi.

records.english: A kind word from a nurse made my grandmother smile for the first time in days.
records.zomi: Nurse khat' kammal nem in ka pi ni tampi khit ciangin a masa pen-in a nuihsak hi.

records.english: My father keeps every encouraging letter he has ever received in a box under his bed.
records.zomi: Ka pa in a ngah ngei hanthawnna lai khempeuh a lupna nuai-a bawm khat sungah a kem hi.

records.english: My sister prefers encouragement in private, because public praise embarrasses her.
records.zomi: Ka u numei in mipi mai-a phatna in a zumsak ahih manin a guk-a hanthawnna a deih zaw hi.

records.english: Hope is sometimes a decision rather than a feeling.
records.zomi: Lametna pen a hun pawl ah kisakna hi lo-in khensatna ahi hi.

records.english: The doctor's calm words gave my father more hope than all the leaflets in the waiting room.
records.zomi: Siavuan' kammal dai in ngakna khan sung-a lai neu khempeuh sangin ka pa lametna tam zaw a pia hi.

records.english: Please don't treat the Holy Spirit as a mysterious idea; our church teaches that he is God present with us.
records.zomi: Kha Siangtho thu thuguk bangin ngaihsun kei un; i pawlpi in eite tawh a om Pasian ahi hi, ci-in a hilh hi.

records.english: According to Christian teaching, the Spirit lives in every believer.
records.zomi: Khristian hilhna bangin Kha Siangtho upmi khempeuh sungah a teeng hi.

records.english: The Holy Spirit is sometimes called the Comforter or the Advocate.
records.zomi: Kha Siangtho pen a hun pawl ah Huhpa kici hi.

records.english: Our pastor said, "The Spirit is closer to you than your own breath."
records.zomi: I pastor in, “Kha Siangtho na hu sangin nang tawh a nai zaw hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: My little sister asked whether the Holy Spirit was a ghost.
records.zomi: Ka nau numei in Kha Siangtho pen kha a hi hiam hong dong hi.

records.english: We light seven candles at Pentecost for the gifts of the Spirit.
records.zomi: Pentecost ciangin Kha Siangtho' letsongte adingin khawimeivaak sagih i tawisak uh hi.

records.english: Shall we make paper doves for the Pentecost service?
records.zomi: Pentecost kikhopna adingin lai vakhu i bawl ding hiam?

records.english: Christians believe that the Spirit helps them pray when they don't know what to say.
records.zomi: Khristiante in bang gen ding hiam a theih loh uh ciangin Kha Siangtho in thu a ngen nadingun a huh hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: Let's make a poster showing the fruit of the Spirit.
records.zomi: Kha Siangtho gah a lak poster khat i bawl ni.

records.english: Can the Holy Spirit help people change bad habits?
records.zomi: Kha Siangtho in mite ngeina hoih lote a kheel nadingun a huh thei hiam?

records.english: Some churches speak about the Holy Spirit much more often than others.
records.zomi: Pawlpi pawl khat in a dangte sangin Kha Siangtho thu tamvei zaw-in a gen uh hi.

records.english: For many believers, the Spirit is a source of courage in frightening times.
records.zomi: Upmi tampi adingin Kha Siangtho pen hun lauhuai ah hangsanna kipatna ahi hi.

records.english: Shall we read the story of Pentecost together this evening?
records.zomi: Tu nitakin Pentecost tangthu khawmin i sim ding hiam?

records.english: Who is the Holy Spirit?
records.zomi: Kha Siangtho kua ahi hiam?

records.english: At Pentecost, the disciples are said to have spoken in languages they had never learned.
records.zomi: Pentecost ciangin nungzuite in a sin ngei loh pau tawh thu a gen uh hi, kici hi.

records.english: Christians believe that the Holy Spirit is God, together with the Father and the Son.
records.zomi: Khristiante in Kha Siangtho pen Pa leh Tapa tawh khawm-a Pasian ahi hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: Many churches teach that the Spirit guided the writers of the Bible.
records.zomi: Pawlpi tampi in Kha Siangtho in Laisiangtho gelhte a makaih hi, ci-in a hilh uh hi.

records.english: Some Christians feel the presence of the Spirit most strongly in prayer, others in music or silence.
records.zomi: Khristian pawl khat in thungetna ah Kha Siangtho' omna a thei pen uh a, a dangte la hiam daina ah a thei uh hi.

records.english: Do you think of the Holy Spirit as a person?
records.zomi: Kha Siangtho mihing khat bangin na ngaihsun hiam?

records.english: Most Christian traditions teach that the Holy Spirit is a person, not just a power.
records.zomi: Khristian ngeina a tamzaw in Kha Siangtho pen vangliatna bek hi lo-in mihing khat ahi hi, ci-in a hilh uh hi.

records.english: Many Christians pray to the Holy Spirit for guidance before making important decisions.
records.zomi: Khristian tampi in thukhenna thupite a bawl ma-un makaihna adingin Kha Siangtho kiangah thu a ngen uh hi.

records.english: When Christians speak of being led by the Spirit, they usually mean following God's guidance in daily life.
records.zomi: Khristiante in Kha Siangtho' makaihna thu a gen uh ciangin ni simin nuntakna ah Pasian' makaihna zuih a ci nopna uh hi.

records.english: When we say the creed, we confess our belief in the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit.
records.zomi: Upna thugen i gen ciangin Pa, Tapa leh Kha Siangtho tungah i upna i pulak uh hi.

records.english: Does the Holy Spirit speak to people today?
records.zomi: Kha Siangtho in tu-in mite kiangah thu a gen hiam?

records.english: Many Christians believe so, though they often describe it as a quiet sense of guidance rather than a voice.
records.zomi: Khristian tampi in tua bangin a um uh a, ahi zongin aw sangin makaihna dai khat bangin a gen zel uh hi.

records.english: Do Christians pray to the Spirit as well as to the Father and the Son?
records.zomi: Khristiante in Pa leh Tapa bek hi lo-in Kha Siangtho kiangah zong thu a ngen uh hiam?

records.english: Is the Spirit with us even when we feel alone?
records.zomi: Eimau kia bangin i kisak uh ciangin zong Kha Siangtho eite tawh a om hiam?

records.english: Many churches pray for the Holy Spirit at baptisms and confirmations.
records.zomi: Pawlpi tampi in tuiphumna leh confirmation ah Kha Siangtho adingin thu a ngen uh hi.

records.english: My grandmother always begins her prayers by asking the Spirit to be with her.
records.zomi: Ka pi in amah tawh a om dingin Kha Siangtho ngen-in a thungetna a kipat tawntung hi.

records.english: In Paul's letters, believers are told not to grieve the Holy Spirit, which suggests the Spirit can be hurt.
records.zomi: Paul' laite ah upmite Kha Siangtho daksak kei dingin kigen a, tua in Kha Siangtho a dah thei hi, cihna hi.

records.english: Our pastor explained the Trinity using the example of water, ice and steam, though he admitted that every comparison falls short.
records.zomi: I pastor in tui, tuikhal leh meikhu entehna tawh Trinity a genteh a, ahi zongin entehna khempeuh a kicing lo hi, ci-in a pom hi.

records.english: In John's Gospel, Jesus promises his disciples a helper who will be with them for ever.
records.zomi: Johan' Lungdamna Thu ah Jesu in a nungzuite tawh khantawn-in a om ding Huhpa khat a kiciamsak hi.

records.english: Who gave the disciples the courage to preach after Jesus had gone?
records.zomi: Jesu a pai khit ciangin kua in nungzuite thu gen dingin hangsanna a pia hiam?

records.english: The Spirit is mentioned at the very beginning of the Bible, moving over the waters.
records.zomi: Kha Siangtho pen Laisiangtho' kipatna taktak ah tui tungah a kilawn bangin kigen hi.

records.english: The book of Acts describes the Spirit coming on the disciples at Pentecost like tongues of fire.
records.zomi: Sawltakte Thu laibu in Pentecost ciangin Kha Siangtho meikuang tawh kibang lei bangin nungzuite tungah a tun dan a gen hi.

records.english: Does the Spirit unite believers from every nation and language?
records.zomi: Kha Siangtho in gam leh pau khempeuh pan upmite a kipumkhatsak hiam?

records.english: In many churches, the Spirit is invoked when bread and wine are blessed.
records.zomi: Pawlpi tampi ah moh leh grape tui thupha kipiak ciangin Kha Siangtho kisam hi.

records.english: Our Bible study group spent a whole evening on the question of who the Holy Spirit is.
records.zomi: I Laisiangtho sinna pawl in Kha Siangtho kua ahi hiam dotna tungtang nitak bup a zang uh hi.

records.english: Why do Christians speak of the Holy Spirit as someone rather than something?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Khristiante in Kha Siangtho pen na khat bangin hi lo-in mi khat bangin a gen uh hiam?

records.english: Because they believe the Spirit is personal, someone who can teach, guide and comfort.
records.zomi: Kha Siangtho pen hilh, makaih leh hehnem thei mi khat ahi hi, ci-in a um uh ahih manin.

records.english: Some Christians say they first felt the Spirit's comfort at a time of great loss.
records.zomi: Khristian pawl khat in mansuahna lianpi hun ah Kha Siangtho' hehnepna a thei masa uh hi, a ci uh hi.

records.english: Teaching children about the Holy Spirit is harder than teaching them about Jesus, because the Spirit can't be pictured easily.
records.zomi: Kha Siangtho a lim baih takin kilak thei lo ahih manin naupangte kiangah Kha Siangtho thu sinsak in Jesu thu sinsak sangin a haksa zaw hi.

records.english: The Holy Spirit is described in the Bible as the one who gives life.
records.zomi: Laisiangtho ah Kha Siangtho pen nuntakna a pia pa bangin kigen hi.

records.english: Pentecost celebrates the coming of the Holy Spirit on the first followers of Jesus.
records.zomi: Pentecost in Jesu' zuite masa pente tungah Kha Siangtho' hong tunna a lawp hi.

records.english: Many people find it easier to understand the Spirit through his work than through definitions.
records.zomi: Mi tampi in a genteh nate sangin a nasep tungtawnin Kha Siangtho a theih baih zaw uh hi.

records.english: The deity of the Holy Spirit means that Christians worship the Spirit as fully God.
records.zomi: Kha Siangtho' Pasian hihna in Khristiante in Kha Siangtho Pasian kicing bangin a biak uh cihna hi.

records.english: Let's ask the Holy Spirit to guide our meeting tonight.
records.zomi: Tu zanin i kikhopna a makaih nadingin Kha Siangtho i ngen ni.

records.english: The Holy Spirit is often pictured as a dove, because of the story of Jesus' baptism.
records.zomi: Jesu' tuiphumna tangthu hangin Kha Siangtho vakhu bangin kilak zel hi.

records.english: In Paul's letter to the Galatians, love, joy and peace are listed among the fruit of the Spirit.
records.zomi: Galati-te kiang Paul' lai ah itna, lungdamna leh kilemna Kha Siangtho gah lak-ah kigelh hi.

records.english: May the Holy Spirit give you peace.
records.zomi: Kha Siangtho in kilemna hong pia ta hen.

records.english: Theologians have discussed the relationship between the Father, the Son and the Spirit for many centuries.
records.zomi: Pasian thu siamte in Pa, Tapa leh Kha Siangtho kikal kizopna kum za tampi a kinial uh hi.

records.english: When I feel lost, I ask the Holy Spirit to help me understand what to do.
records.zomi: Ka mang bangin ka kisak ciangin bang bawl ding hiam theih dingin Kha Siangtho in hong huh dingin ka ngen hi.

records.english: Every Sunday, our service ends with a blessing in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit.
records.zomi: Nipini simin i kikhopna Pa, Tapa leh Kha Siangtho' min tawh thupha piakna-in a bei hi.

records.english: The Nicene Creed calls the Holy Spirit "the Lord, the giver of life".
records.zomi: Nicene Creed in Kha Siangtho pen “Topa, nuntakna piakpa” a ci hi.

records.english: Could the choir sing the hymn about the Spirit at the end of the service?
records.zomi: Kikhopna tawpna ah la sa pawl in Kha Siangtho tungtang la a sa thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: The Spirit is described in the Bible as wind, breath, fire and water.
records.zomi: Laisiangtho ah Kha Siangtho huih, hu, mei leh tui bangin kigen hi.

records.english: The doctrine of the Trinity teaches that there is one God in three persons.
records.zomi: Trinity thuhilhna in Pasian khat mi thum ah a om hi, ci-in a hilh hi.

records.english: The Spirit is not a lesser part of God but equal with the Father and the Son, according to the creeds.
records.zomi: Upna thugente bangin Kha Siangtho pen Pasian' kenkhat niam zaw hi lo-in Pa leh Tapa tawh a kibang hi.

records.english: Can you explain the Trinity in simple words for my children?
records.zomi: Ka tate adingin Trinity kammal baih tawh hong genteh thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Christians understand the work of the Spirit in different ways, but most agree that he gives comfort and strength.
records.zomi: Khristiante in Kha Siangtho' nasep tuamtuam-in a thei uh a, ahi zongin a tamzaw in hehnepna leh thahatna a pia hi, ci-in a kituak uh hi.

records.english: The tax office's phone line was so busy that I waited forty minutes, only to be told that I needed a different department.
records.zomi: Siah office' phone a buai lua ahih manin minit sawmli ka ngak a, khen dang khat ka kisam hi, ci-in hong gen uh hi.

records.english: My husband does our tax return every year, and I check his arithmetic.
records.zomi: Ka pasal in kum simin i siah lai a bawl a, kei in a kisimte ka en hi.

records.english: If you're not sure whether something is taxable, it's better to ask than to guess.
records.zomi: Khat peuhpeuh siah piak kul hiam na theih kician kei leh ngaihsun sangin dot a hoih zaw hi.

records.english: Late tax returns can lead to a fine, even if no tax is owed.
records.zomi: Siah piak ding om kei zongin siah lai a nung leh man gawt a om thei hi.

records.english: Many people find tax forms confusing, even when their income is simple.
records.zomi: A sum ngah uh a baih hangin mi tampi in siah form a buaihuai sa uh hi.

records.english: I finally understood my tax return after my neighbour explained it line by line.
records.zomi: Ka innveng in tuat khat zawh khat a genteh khit ciangin a tawpna-ah ka siah lai ka thei hi.

records.english: Who should I call if I don't understand my tax bill?
records.zomi: Ka siah man ka theih kei leh kua ka sam ding hiam?

records.english: My cousin, who is an accountant, is very popular in our family every spring.
records.zomi: Accountant a hih ka sanggam spring simin i innkuan ah kideih mahmah hi.

records.english: We set aside a little money every month so that the tax bill doesn't come as a shock.
records.zomi: Siah man in lamdang hong sak loh nadingin kha simin sum tawmno i koih uh hi.

records.english: The tax office sent me a letter saying I had paid too much and would get a refund.
records.zomi: Siah office in tam lua ka pia a, a kik ka ngah ding hi, ci lai khat hong khak hi.

records.english: Many small businesses employ an accountant to deal with their taxes.
records.zomi: Sumbawlna neu tampi in a siah uh a kem dingin accountant a luah uh hi.

records.english: Please don't throw away any letters from the tax office, even old ones.
records.zomi: Siah office pan lai khatpeuh, a lui zong paikhia kei in.

records.english: My parents had an accountant check their tax return after my father started his own business.
records.zomi: Ka pa amah' sumbawlna a kipat khit ciangin ka nu leh ka pa in a siah lai uh accountant a en sak uh hi.

records.english: Children, taxes are the money people give the government so that everyone can share schools and hospitals.
records.zomi: Naupangte, siah pen mi khempeuh in sang leh damdawi inn a kihawm theih nadingun mite in kumpi a piak sum ahi hi.

records.english: My grandfather keeps every tax document he has received in a box under his bed.
records.zomi: Ka pu in a ngah siah lai khempeuh a lupna nuai-a bawm khat sungah a kem hi.

records.english: When my parents retired, they were surprised by how much their tax situation changed, and they needed help to understand the new forms.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa a nasep a tawp uh ciangin a siah dinmun uh bangzah a kikheel hiam lamdang a sa uh a, form thakte theih dingin huhna a kisam uh hi.

records.english: Shall we ask the volunteer adviser to look at our tax forms?
records.zomi: I siah form te en dingin deihsakna thuhilhpa i ngen ding hiam?

records.english: The government announced that it would raise taxes on cigarettes to discourage smoking.
records.zomi: Meizial dawn a kiamsak nadingin kumpi in meizial tung-a siah a khangsak ding hi, ci-in a gen hi.

records.english: If you work for an employer, tax is usually taken from your pay before you receive it.
records.zomi: Nasep piaktu khat adingin na sep leh na ngah ma-in na khasum pan siah kila zel hi.

records.english: The money from road taxes is supposed to be spent on repairing roads.
records.zomi: Lampi siah pan sum lampi bawlphatna ah kizang ding hi.

records.english: In some countries, families with children pay less tax than single people.
records.zomi: Gam pawl khat ah ta nei innkuante mi kia sangin siah tawm zaw a pia uh hi.

records.english: Last year, my mother received a tax bill that seemed far too high.
records.zomi: Kum nunung in ka nu in a sang lua bang siah man khat a ngah hi.

records.english: My brother sat with her for an evening, checking every number on the form.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in form tung-a nambat khempeuh en-in nitak khat amah tawh a tu hi.

records.english: They found a mistake, and the tax office corrected it within a month.
records.zomi: Khialhna khat a mu uh a, siah office in kha khat sungin a puah hi.

records.english: I got a small tax refund this year, which paid for a new pair of glasses.
records.zomi: Tu kum siah kik tawmno ka ngah a, tua in mitlimlang thak khat man a pia hi.

records.english: You must tell the tax office if your address changes.
records.zomi: Na teenna mun a kikheel leh siah office kiangah na gen kul hi.

records.english: Tax payments help to fund pensions for older people.
records.zomi: Siah piakte in mi upate' pension man a huh hi.

records.english: Some people use tax software, while others prefer to fill in the paper form by hand.
records.zomi: Mi pawl khat in siah software a zang uh a, a dangte in lai form khut tawh dim a deih zaw uh hi.

records.english: Sales tax is added to the price of many things you buy in the shops.
records.zomi: Van zuak siah dawl-a na lei van tampi' man tungah kibehlap hi.

records.english: Thank you for helping me with my tax form; I'd have been lost without you.
records.zomi: Ka siah form ah hong huh manin ka lungdam hi; nang om lo hi leh ka mang ding hi.

records.english: I've lost the form I need for my taxes; where can I get another copy?
records.zomi: Ka siah adingin ka kisam form ka mangsak hi; a dang khat koi ah ka ngah thei ding hiam?

records.english: Free tax advice is available at the community centre every Thursday evening.
records.zomi: Laizing ni nitak simin mipi inn ah man om lo siah thuhilhna a om hi.

records.english: Did you remember to declare the interest from your savings account?
records.zomi: Na sum khol account pan sum pung na gen hiam?

records.english: Next year, I'm going to keep my receipts in a folder instead of in a shoebox.
records.zomi: Kum zom ciangin ka man piakna laite khedap bawm sangin lai koihna khat sungah ka kem ding hi.

records.english: Taxes on property help to pay for local services like rubbish collection and street lights.
records.zomi: Inn leh gam tung-a siahte in eek kaikhopna leh lampi meivaak bang mun-a nasepte a huh hi.

records.english: Why do taxes always cause arguments at family dinners?
records.zomi: Bang hangin innkuan nitak an ah siah thu in kinialna a piangsak tawntung hiam?

records.english: Some charities can claim back tax on the donations they receive.
records.zomi: Charity pawl khat in a ngah piakna tung-a siah a ngen kik thei uh hi.

records.english: Self-employed people often have to set aside money every month to pay their tax bill.
records.zomi: Amau kia-a nasep sem mite in a siah man uh pia dingin kha simin sum a koih kul zel uh hi.

records.english: My uncle got into trouble with the tax office because he had never declared the rent from his second flat, which he thought didn't count.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in a inn nihna inn man a sim kei hi, a sa-in a gen ngei loh manin siah office tawh buaina ah a tuak hi.

records.english: Dad always files his tax return at the very last minute.
records.zomi: Pa in a siah lai hun nunung pen minit ah a pia tawntung hi.

records.english: When is the deadline for filing my tax return?
records.zomi: Ka siah lai piakna hun tawpna bang hun ahi hiam?

records.english: In our country, it's the end of April, but check the letter from the tax office to be sure.
records.zomi: I gam ah April kha tawp ahi a, ahi zongin kician nadingin siah office pan lai en in.

records.english: Honest tax records protect you if the tax office ever has questions.
records.zomi: Siah ciamtehna dikte in siah office in dotna a neih ciangin hong kem hi.

records.english: Taxes pay for public services such as schools, hospitals and roads.
records.zomi: Siah in sang, damdawi inn leh lampi bang mipi nasepte a huh hi.

records.english: Taxes on imported goods can make them much more expensive than local products.
records.zomi: Pua gam pan hong pai van tung-a siahte in mun-a van sangin a man tam zaw mahmah sak thei hi.

records.english: The tax office was able to correct the mistake once I sent them a copy of my payslip.
records.zomi: Ka khasum lai copy ka khak ciangin siah office in khialhna a puah thei hi.

records.english: Whether taxes are fair is one of the oldest questions in politics.
records.zomi: Siah a dik hiam cih pen politics-a dotna lui pen khat ahi hi.

records.english: Keep your receipts, because some expenses can be deducted from your taxable income.
records.zomi: Sum zat pawl khat siah piak ding sum ngah pan kiphiat thei ahih manin na man piakna laite kem in.

records.english: Do I have to pay tax on the money I earn from tutoring?
records.zomi: Naupang hilh pan ka ngah sum tungah siah ka pia kul ding hiam?

records.english: Usually, yes, so it's worth asking the tax office how to declare it.
records.zomi: A tamzaw-in, pia kul hi, tua ahih manin bangci gen ding hiam siah office dot a phu hi.

records.english: Is it quicker to file a tax return online or by post?
records.zomi: Siah lai online-in piak a manlang zaw hiam, lai khakna tawh hiam?

records.english: Tax rules change from year to year, so last year's advice may no longer apply.
records.zomi: Siah thukhamte kum simin a kikheel ahih manin kum nunung-a thuhilhna a kituak nawn kei kha thei hi.

records.english: Do you two file your taxes together or separately?
records.zomi: Na nih in na siah uh khawmin na pia uh hiam, a tuam-in hiam?

records.english: Fill in every section of the form, even if the answer is zero.
records.zomi: Dawnna bangmah lo hi zongin form' kenkhat khempeuh dim in.

records.english: Can someone help me fill in my tax return?
records.zomi: Ka siah lai dim dingin kuamah in hong huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Is there a reduced tax rate for basic foods in your country?
records.zomi: Na gam ah an tawmpi adingin siah niam zaw a om hiam?

records.english: Paying tax can feel painful, but most people value the services it pays for.
records.zomi: Siah piak a na bangin a kisa thei a, ahi zongin mi a tamzaw in a man piak nasepte a manpha sa uh hi.

records.english: My sister was surprised to learn that she had to pay tax on her first part-time job.
records.zomi: Ka u numei in a hun tawmno nasep masa pen tungah siah a pia kul hi, a theih ciangin lamdang a sa hi.

records.english: Do pensioners have to pay income tax?
records.zomi: Pension ngah mite sum ngah siah a pia kul uh hiam?

records.english: It depends on how much their pension is, and on the rules in their country.
records.zomi: A pension uh bangzah hiam leh a gam uh thukhamte tungah a kinga hi.

records.english: My grandfather always says that common sense is the most useful kind of logic.
records.zomi: Ka pu in ngaihsutna tavuan pen logic phatuam pen ahi hi, a ci tawntung hi.

records.english: If both your sisters say they didn't break the vase, and one of them is lying, how could you find out?
records.zomi: Na u leh nau numei nih in pak bel ka khamsak kei hi, a ci uh a, a khat in a zuau leh bangci na thei thei ding hiam?

records.english: Before buying a car, my father made a list of reasons for and against each one.
records.zomi: Mawtaw a lei ma-in ka pa in khatciat adingin a deihna leh a deih lohna hangte list khat a bawl hi.

records.english: If Mum is at work and Dad's car is outside, who's probably at home?
records.zomi: Nu nasep ah a om a, Pa' mawtaw pua ah a om leh kua inn ah a om kha ding hiam?

records.english: Dad, unless he went out on his bicycle.
records.zomi: Pa, a siiksakol tawh a pusuak kei leh.

records.english: If the train leaves every twenty minutes and we just missed one, how long do we wait?
records.zomi: Meileng minit sawmnih simin a pai a, khat i pelh pah leh bangzah sawt i ngak ding hiam?

records.english: Twenty minutes, or less if the next one is early.
records.zomi: Minit sawmnih, a zom pen hun ma-in a tun leh tawm zaw.

records.english: My aunt reasons so carefully that family arguments with her never last long.
records.zomi: Ka ni limtakin a ngaihsun ahih manin amah tawh innkuan kinialnate a sawt ngei kei hi.

records.english: A good argument at home should rely on reasons, not on who shouts the loudest.
records.zomi: Inn-a kinialna hoih khat kua in a kikou pen hiam tungah hi lo-in hangte tungah a kinga ding hi.

records.english: A careful reasoner looks for evidence before accusing anyone.
records.zomi: Limtak-a ngaihsun mi khat in kuamah a mawhsak ma-in lakna a zong hi.

records.english: Please don't jump to conclusions before you've heard both sides of the story.
records.zomi: Tangthu' lang nih na zak ma-in a manlang-in khensat kei in.

records.english: If it rains, the picnic is cancelled, and it's raining now, so what happens?
records.zomi: Guah a zuk leh an nekkhawmna kiphiat ding a, tu-in guah a zu hi, bang a piang ding hiam?

records.english: The picnic is cancelled, and we'll eat sandwiches on the living room floor.
records.zomi: An nekkhawmna kiphiat ding a, tutna khan lei tungah sandwich i ne ding uh hi.

records.english: If we leave at nine, we'll miss the traffic and arrive before lunch.
records.zomi: Nai kua ciangin i pai leh mawtaw buaina i pelh ding a, sun an ma-in i tung ding hi.

records.english: If you can explain your reasoning to a younger sibling, you probably understand it well yourself.
records.zomi: Na ngaihsutna nau neu khat kiangah na genteh thei leh nangmah zong in hoih takin na thei kha ding hi.

records.english: The children solved the treasure hunt clues faster than the adults who wrote them.
records.zomi: Naupangte in van zonna kimawlna' ciamtehnate a gelh mi upate sangin manlang zaw-in a dawng uh hi.

records.english: Can you work out which key opens the shed by trying the oldest ones first?
records.zomi: A lui pente masa-in sin-in koi tawh in van koihna inn a hong hiam na theih thei ding hiam?

records.english: Last week, my daughter's bicycle disappeared from the garden.
records.zomi: Kal nunung in ka tanu' siiksakol huan sung pan a mang hi.

records.english: She noticed muddy tyre marks leading to the neighbour's gate and fresh mud on their son's boots.
records.zomi: Innveng' kongpi lam a pai tyre lim nin leh a tapa' khedap tung-a nin thak a mu hi.

records.english: It turned out that he had only borrowed it, and he brought it back with an apology and a bag of sweets.
records.zomi: A leitawi bek ahi hi, ci a kilang a, maisakna ngetna leh an tuithak ip khat tawh a hong tawi kik hi.

records.english: Reasoning carefully as a family about big money decisions can save years of regret.
records.zomi: Sum thukhenna lianpite tungtang innkuan bangin limtakin ngaihsun in kum tampi sikhana pan hong hondoh thei hi.

records.english: My little brother thinks that if he can't see you, you can't see him.
records.zomi: Ka nau pasal in amah in na mu kei leh nang in amah na mu kei hi, a sa hi.

records.english: My grandfather can always tell what the weather will do by watching the clouds and the birds.
records.zomi: Ka pu in meii leh vasate en tawh huihkhua bang ci ding hiam a thei thei tawntung hi.

records.english: Grandpa and I do a logic puzzle together every Sunday morning.
records.zomi: Pu leh kei Nipini zingsang simin logic puzzle khat khawmin i bawl hi.

records.english: Sudoku taught my daughter patience as well as logic.
records.zomi: Sudoku in ka tanu logic bek hi lo-in thuakzawhna zong a sinsak hi.

records.english: Our eldest argued that if homework helps you learn, then no homework must mean he already knows everything.
records.zomi: I upa pen in inn sinna in sin dingin a huh leh inn sinna om loh in a khempeuh a thei khin hi, cihna ding hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Did you notice that the clock in the kitchen is ten minutes fast?
records.zomi: An huanna inn-a nai minit sawm a ma lam hi, na mu hiam?

records.english: That explains why we're always early for school.
records.zomi: Tua in bang hangin sang ah a hun ma-in i tung tawntung uh hiam a genteh hi.

records.english: Our youngest concluded that the moon follows our car, because it was always outside the window.
records.zomi: I neu pen in tukkhuak pua ah a om tawntung ahih manin kha in i mawtaw a zui hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Teaching children to check their assumptions can prevent many family quarrels.
records.zomi: Naupangte a ngaihsutnate en dingin sinsak in innkuan kinialna tampi a dal thei hi.

records.english: Mum uses logic to decide which shops to visit, so that she never walks the same street twice.
records.zomi: Nu in lampi kibang vei nih kal ngei lo dingin koi dawlte veh ding hiam khensat dingin logic a zang hi.

records.english: Shall we play a guessing game in the car to pass the time?
records.zomi: Hun zat nadingin mawtaw sungah ngaihsut kimawlna khat i kimawl ding hiam?

records.english: My daughter beat her uncle at a game of strategy, and he still hasn't recovered.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in a pa neu gelna kimawlna khat ah a zo a, a pa neu a lungkiat lai hi.

records.english: Can you think of a reason why the cat might be sitting by the door?
records.zomi: Zawhngeu bang hangin kongkhak kiangah a tu kha ding hiam a hang khat na ngaihsun thei ding hiam?

records.english: Board games on rainy days have taught our children more reasoning than any worksheet.
records.zomi: Guah zuk ni-a dawhkan kimawlnate in i naupangte sinna lai khatpeuh sangin ngaihsutna tam zaw a sinsak hi.

records.english: Children learn reasoning naturally when they're allowed to ask why and get a real answer.
records.zomi: Bang hangin ci-a dong-in dawnna taktak a ngah theih ciangun naupangte in ngaihsutna a ngeina-in a sin uh hi.

records.english: Thank you for helping my son with his logic puzzles; he talks about them all the time.
records.zomi: Ka tapa' logic puzzle te ah na huh manin ka lungdam hi; a tawntung-in a gen hi.
