records.english: Ask your grandparents to tell you one story each time you visit.
records.zomi: Na veh vei khempeuh-in na pu leh pi kiangah tangthu khat ciat gen dingin ngen in.

records.english: Some people share their experiences easily, while others need years before they can talk about them.
records.zomi: Mi pawl khat a tangthu uh baih takin a hawm uh a, a dangte a gen theih ma-un kum tampi a kisam uh hi.

records.english: My brother prefers to share his experiences through photographs, because he says he's no good with words.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in kammal ah a siam kei hi, a cih manin a tangthu lim tawh hawm a deih zaw hi.

records.english: Mum's stories about her village always end with a lesson.
records.zomi: Nu' khua tungtang tangthute sinna khat tawh a bei tawntung hi.

records.english: A story told by the person who lived it carries a different weight from one told about them.
records.zomi: A thuak mi mah in a gen tangthu in amah tungtang mi dang in a gen sangin gikna tuam a pua hi.

records.english: Can you tell me about the first time you went abroad?
records.zomi: Gamdang ah na pai masa pen tungtang hong gen thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Sharing an experience with someone who went through the same thing feels like being understood without explaining.
records.zomi: Thu kibang a thuak mi khat tawh tangthu hawm in genteh kul lo-in kitheisak bangin a kisa hi.

records.english: I like hearing travel stories from people who went slowly rather than people who saw everything quickly.
records.zomi: Na khempeuh manlang taka en mite sangin nuam taka pai mite pan khualzin tangthu zak ka deih zaw hi.

records.english: Thank you for trusting me with your story.
records.zomi: Na tangthu hong muan manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: My aunt laughs so much while telling her stories that she can hardly finish them.
records.zomi: Ka ni in a tangthu a gen laitakin a nuih lua ahih manin a zawh zo dek kei hi.

records.english: Shall I tell you about my first job, or have you heard it too many times?
records.zomi: Ka nasep masa tungtang kong gen ding hiam, tamvei na za khin hiam?

records.english: Some memories are easier to share in another language, especially painful ones.
records.zomi: Phawkna pawl khat pau dang tawh hawm a baih zaw a, a diak in a natna te.

records.english: I didn't believe my grandfather's stories until I saw the photographs.
records.zomi: Lim te ka muh ma-in ka pu' tangthute ka um kei hi.

records.english: When we share our experiences, we often discover that we weren't as alone as we thought.
records.zomi: I tangthute i hawm ciangin i kisak bangin eimau kia i hi kei uh hi, ci i mu zel uh hi.

records.english: Do you remember the summer we spent at the lake?
records.zomi: Dil ah i zat khal na phawk hiam?

records.english: I prefer writing letters about my travels to posting photos online.
records.zomi: Online-ah lim post sangin ka khualzinnate tungtang lai gelh ka deih zaw hi.

records.english: A shared experience can bring strangers closer faster than years of polite conversation.
records.zomi: Kihawm thupiang khat in kum tampi zahtakna kihopihna sangin mikhualte manlang zaw-in a kinaisak thei hi.

records.english: My sister tells the same story differently every time, and each version is better than the last.
records.zomi: Ka u numei in tangthu kibang vei khempeuh-in tuamtuam-in a gen a, khatciat a ma-a pen sangin a hoih zaw hi.

records.english: I'll finish the story after dinner, I promise.
records.zomi: Nitak an khit ciangin tangthu ka zo ding hi, ka kiciam hi.

records.english: Telling a story in person feels different from writing it down, even if the words are the same.
records.zomi: Kammal kibang hi zongin mai tang kituak-a tangthu gen pen gelh tawh a kibang lo hi.

records.english: My grandmother always asks, "Have I told you this before?" and we always say no.
records.zomi: Ka pi in, “Hih kong gen ngei hiam?” a ci tawntung a, i gen ngei kei hi, i ci tawntung uh hi.

records.english: Talking about the past is often easier with old friends than with one's own children.
records.zomi: Hun bei thu gen pen amah' tate sangin lawm luite tawh a baih zaw zel hi.

records.english: We recorded my grandmother's stories on a phone, so that the great-grandchildren can hear her voice.
records.zomi: Tu' tate in a aw a zak theih nadingun ka pi' tangthute phone tawh i la uh hi.

records.english: Shall we look at the old photos, or would you like me to tell you the story first?
records.zomi: Lim luite i en ding hiam, tangthu a masa-in kong gen na deih hiam?

records.english: Hearing about my parents' first years in the city made my own problems seem much smaller.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa' khuapi-a kum masate tungtang zak in ka buainate a neu zaw mahmah sak hi.

records.english: Old photographs often unlock stories that a person had forgotten they knew.
records.zomi: Lim luite in mi khat in a theih a mangngilh tangthute a hon zel hi.

records.english: Sometimes it's the small, ordinary memories that children ask to hear again and again.
records.zomi: A hun pawl ah naupangte in vei tampi a zak kik nop uh pen phawkna neu leh tavuante ahi hi.

records.english: How did your grandparents celebrate their wedding?
records.zomi: Na pu leh na pi in a mopawi uh bangci a lawp uh hiam?

records.english: Dad tells his war stories only to my son, never to us.
records.zomi: Pa in a gal tangthute ka tapa kiang bek ah a gen a, eite kiangah a gen ngei kei hi.

records.english: Some experiences are best shared over a meal, and others are better shared on a long walk.
records.zomi: Tangthu pawl khat an nek laitakin hawm a hoih pen a, a dangte kalna sau ah hawm a hoih zaw hi.

records.english: Talking about a shared experience years later can reveal how differently each person remembers it.
records.zomi: Kum tampi khit ciangin kihawm thupiang khat tungtang kihopih in mi khatciat in bangzah tuamtuam-in a phawk hiam a lak thei hi.

records.english: Our son loves one true story about my childhood more than any book.
records.zomi: I tapa in laibu khatpeuh sangin ka naupan lai tangthu taktak khat a it zaw hi.

records.english: My grandfather tells his stories slowly, whereas my grandmother rushes to the funny part.
records.zomi: Ka pu in a tangthute nuam takin a gen a, ka pi in a nuihhuai mun lam ah a manlang hi.

records.english: Should I tell my children about the hard years, or only the happy ones?
records.zomi: Ka tate kiangah kum haksate ka gen ding hiam, a nuam te bek hiam?

records.english: Tell them both, in a way that suits their age.
records.zomi: A nih gen in, a kum uh tawh a kilawm dan-in.

records.english: Do you think it's better to share an experience straight away or after some time has passed?
records.zomi: Tangthu khat a pah-in hawm a hoih zaw hiam, hun tawmno khit ciangin hiam na ci hiam?

records.english: Shall I tell the story of the night the car broke down in the mountains?
records.zomi: Mual sungah mawtaw a siat zan tangthu ka gen ding hiam?

records.english: Some families share stories at dinner, while in others the stories come out only at weddings and funerals.
records.zomi: Innkuan pawl khat nitak an ah tangthu a kihawm uh a, a dangte ah mopawi leh misi vuina ciang bek-in tangthute a pusuak hi.

records.english: Funny stories are easy to share, while painful ones need the right moment and the right listener.
records.zomi: Tangthu nuihhuaite hawm a baih a, a natna te hun kilawm leh ngaikhiat mi kilawm a kisam hi.

records.english: Do you two prefer listening to family stories or telling them?
records.zomi: Na nih in innkuan tangthu ngaikhia na deih zaw uh hiam, gen na deih zaw uh hiam?

records.english: When you share a difficult memory, the listener's silence can be a gift.
records.zomi: Phawkna haksa khat na hawm ciangin ngaikhiatpa' daina letsong khat a hi thei hi.

records.english: Children love stories about the times their parents got into trouble.
records.zomi: Naupangte in a nu leh a pa uh buaina-a a om hun tangthute a it mahmah uh hi.

records.english: Video calls let us share news with relatives abroad, but nothing replaces sitting together.
records.zomi: Video sapna in gamdang-a sanggamte tawh thuthak i hawm theisak a, ahi zongin khawm-a tu sangin bangmah in a kheel zo kei hi.

records.english: Experiences shared by colleagues can teach a new worker more than any training course.
records.zomi: Nasep lawmte' tangthute in nasem thak khat sinna khatpeuh sangin tam zaw a sinsak thei hi.

records.english: When my father finally told us about his childhood, we had to choose whether to record it or just listen.
records.zomi: Ka pa in a naupan lai thu a tawpna-ah hong gen ciangin la ding hiam, ngaikhia bek ding hiam i teel kul uh hi.

records.english: We decided to listen first and write it down afterwards.
records.zomi: A masa-in ngaikhia-in a nung ciangin gelh dingin i khensat uh hi.

records.english: Now my daughter reads those notes to her own children, and they laugh at the same places we did.
records.zomi: Tu-in ka tanu in tua lai neute a tate kiangah a sim a, eite i nuihna mun mah ah a nuih uh hi.

records.english: The best stories at family gatherings are usually the ones nobody planned to tell.
records.zomi: Innkuan kikhopna-a tangthu hoih pente kuamah in gen dingin a gel ngei loh te ahi zel hi.

records.english: Choosing which stories to pass on to the next generation is a kind of responsibility.
records.zomi: Koi tangthute khangthak zom kiangah pia khia ding hiam teel pen mawhpuakna khat ahi hi.

records.english: Listening to someone's experience is often more helpful than giving them advice.
records.zomi: Mi khat' tangthu ngaikhiat a tamzaw-in thuhilhna piak sangin a phatuam zaw hi.

records.english: Auntie chose a ground-floor flat because her knees can't manage the stairs any more.

records.english: Why are there flowers in the vegetable patch this year?
records.zomi: Bang hangin tu kum anteh huan ah pak a om hiam?

records.english: Giving the reason for a choice is a sign of respect for the person who has to live with it too.
records.zomi: Teelna khat' hang gen pen tua tawh nungta kul mi zong zahtakna lahna ahi hi.

records.english: Our son chose the cheaper bicycle and spent the difference on a good helmet, which made us proud.
records.zomi: I tapa in siiksakol man neem zaw a teel a, a kibatlohna lukhu hoih khat ah a zang a, tua in hong kipaksak hi.

records.english: Asking someone to explain their choice can sound like criticism, so it helps to ask kindly.
records.zomi: Mi khat kiangah a teelna genteh dingin ngen pen simmawhna bangin a kiza thei ahih manin hehpih takin dot a phatuam hi.

records.english: We explained to the children that we chose a smaller house so that we could travel more.
records.zomi: Khualzin tam zaw theih nadingin inn neu zaw i teel uh hi, ci-in naupangte i genteh uh hi.

records.english: Isn't that table rather big for such a small flat?
records.zomi: Tua dawhkan inn neu mahmah khat adingin a lian lua hi lo hiam?

records.english: Because my whole family comes for dinner every Sunday.
records.zomi: Ka innkuan bup Nipini simin nitak an adingin hong pai uh ahih manin.

records.english: Mum explained that she wears her hair the same way she did at twenty because my father likes it.

records.english: Our neighbours chose to keep their old car, explaining that they hardly ever drive.
records.zomi: I innvengte in a mawng tawm mahmah uh ahih manin a mawtaw lui uh kem dingin a teel uh hi, ci-in a genteh uh hi.

records.english: I chose this route because it passes my old school.
records.zomi: Ka sang lui a kantan ahih manin hih lampi ka teel hi.

records.english: My brother explains every choice he makes in such detail that we sometimes regret asking.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in a teelna khempeuh a kician lua-in a genteh ahih manin i dot uh a i sikha zel uh hi.

records.english: Why do you get up so early on Saturdays?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Kiginni simin zingsang tung mahmah-in na thou hiam?

records.english: It's the only quiet hour I have all week.
records.zomi: Kal bup sungah ka neih nai dai khat bek ahi hi.

records.english: Our son explained that he wanted short hair because the long hair made him too hot in football.
records.zomi: I tapa in sam sau in bawlung kimawl ciangin a sasak lua ahih manin sam tom a deih hi, ci-in a genteh hi.

records.english: Why do you keep all your grandmother's letters?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na pi' lai khempeuh na kem hiam?

records.english: Her handwriting is the closest thing I have to her voice.
records.zomi: A laigelh pen a aw tawh a kibang pen ka neih ahi hi.

records.english: Don't feel you have to explain every choice to your relatives.
records.zomi: Na teelna khempeuh na sanggamte kiangah na genteh kul hi, ci kisa kei in.

records.english: My grandfather chose to walk to the market every day, even when we offered to drive him, because he said it kept him young.
records.zomi: Ka pu in mawtaw tawh i paipih ding i ci zongin a khangno-in a kemsak hi, ci-in ni simin zuakna mun ah a kal dingin a teel hi.

records.english: My cousin's explanation for keeping three dogs was that each one had chosen her.

records.english: Of all the colours, why yellow for the new car?

records.english: So that I can find it in any car park, and so can my mother.
records.zomi: Mawtaw koihna mun khatpeuh ah ka muh theih nadingin, leh ka nu zong in a muh theih nadingin.

records.english: How come the sofa faces the window?
records.zomi: Bang hangin sofa tukkhuak lam a ngat hiam?

records.english: So that Grandma can watch the street while she knits.
records.zomi: Pi in puan a khui laitakin lampi a en theih nadingin.

records.english: What made you pick that name for the cat?
records.zomi: Bang in zawhngeu adingin tua min hong teelsak hiam?

records.english: She arrived on a Tuesday, so the children called her Tuesday.
records.zomi: Pithai ni-in a tung ahih manin naupangte in Pithai a ci uh hi.

records.english: Whose idea was it to paint the children's room green?
records.zomi: Naupangte' khan eng tawh zeek kua' ngaihsutna ahi hiam?

records.english: Mine; green is calming, and for once the children didn't argue.
records.zomi: Kei'; eng in lungsim a daisak a, vei khat ah naupangte a kinial kei uh hi.

records.english: Some choices need no explanation, but in a family, most of them deserve one.
records.zomi: Teelna pawl khat genteh kisam lo a, ahi zongin innkuan ah a tamzaw in genteh a kilawm hi.

records.english: Mum always explains her choices in the kitchen, so that we'll be able to cook her dishes one day.

records.english: My daughter's only explanation for choosing the purple shoes was that purple makes her happy, which seemed reason enough.

records.english: How come you take the long way home every evening?
records.zomi: Bang hangin nitak simin inn lam lampi sau zaw na zui hiam?

records.english: When my wife chose a smaller wedding ring, she said it was so that she could wear it while she worked.

records.english: Children usually accept a choice far more easily once someone has taken the time to explain the reason behind it.

records.english: Dad explained that he planted the apple tree where it would shade the house in summer.
records.zomi: Pa in apple kung khal ciangin inn a khuh theih nading mun ah a suan hi, ci-in a genteh hi.

records.english: When my father chose to work part-time, he explained that he wanted to be at home when we came back from school.

records.english: Talking through your choices with grandparents can bridge the gap between two very different generations.
records.zomi: Na teelnate pu leh pite tawh kihopih in khangthak nih kikal-a gamlatna a lei thei hi.

records.english: Telling someone why you chose a particular gift can make it mean much more to them.

records.english: Why have you stopped eating sweets?

records.english: The dentist frightened me, so I'm trying to give them up.

records.english: Why did you choose a school so far from home?
records.zomi: Bang hangin inn pan gamla mahmah sang khat na teel hiam?

records.english: How come you gave your brother a book instead of a gadget?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na sanggam pasal vanzat sangin laibu na pia hiam?

records.english: Why did you open your bakery in the old part of town?

records.english: Why did you choose the blue dress instead of the red one?

records.english: A small choice explained to a child, such as why we eat vegetables, often leads to a long and interesting conversation.

records.english: Why do you always cook on Sunday evenings?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Nipini nitak simin an na huan tawntung hiam?

records.english: Is that chair your favourite?
records.zomi: Tua tutphah na it pen ahi hiam?

records.english: It was my father's, and it's the most comfortable one in the house.
records.zomi: Ka pa' ahi a, inn sung-a nuam pen ahi hi.

records.english: Can you explain why you chose this film for the whole family?
records.zomi: Innkuan bup adingin bang hangin hih film na teel hiam na genteh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Shall I explain why I've chosen this restaurant before you complain about the menu?

records.english: Why have you started cycling to work?

records.english: Why do you always wear your grandfather's watch?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na pu' nai na bulh tawntung hiam?

records.english: It reminds me to be as patient as he was.
records.zomi: Amah bangin thuakzawhna nei dingin hong phawksak hi.

records.english: When I chose to study at night, my parents understood only after I explained that I needed to work during the day.

records.english: When people ask why I keep chickens in the city, I tell them it's for the eggs and for the children.

records.english: My daughter explained that she chose the violin because it was small enough to carry on the bus.

records.english: A budget has to balance the money that comes in with the money that goes out.

records.english: Some councils publish every payment above a certain amount, so that anyone can check them.
records.zomi: Khuapi office pawl khat in kuamah in a en theih nadingin a zah khat sang tam man piak khempeuh a tangko uh hi.

records.english: When the hospital budget was cut, the waiting lists grew longer.

records.english: Why was the road repair budget used up by June?

records.english: When the budget is tight, even small projects like new benches can be delayed for years.

records.english: Can the budget pay for a crossing outside the school?

records.english: Spending a little on prevention can save a lot on emergency services later.
records.zomi: Kidalna ah tawmno zat in a nung ciangin haksatna huhna ah tampi a khol thei hi.

records.english: Residents were invited to a meeting to discuss next year's budget.
records.zomi: Teeng mite kum zom sum zat ding kihopih dingin kikhopna khat ah kisam uh hi.

records.english: The town council publishes its budget every year, so that residents can see how their money is spent.

records.english: Shall we write to the council asking for more money for the library?
records.zomi: Laibu inn adingin sum tam zaw ngen dingin khuapi office kiangah lai i gelh ding hiam?

records.english: Do you think the council spends enough on young people?

records.english: A transparent budget helps residents trust the people who spend their taxes.
records.zomi: Kilang taka sum zat ding in teeng mite in a siah uh a zang mite a muan nadingun a huh hi.

records.english: Some people think the budget should spend more on parks, while others want more police.
records.zomi: Mi pawl khat in sum zat ding in huan tungah tam zaw a zang ding hi, a ci uh a, a dangte police tam zaw a deih uh hi.

records.english: Cutting a service is often easier than bringing it back later.
records.zomi: Nasep khat tan in a nung-a hong kik sak sangin a baih zaw zel hi.

records.english: Is there any money left in the budget for the summer festival?
records.zomi: Khal pawi adingin sum zat ding ah sum a om lai hiam?

records.english: When the council announced cuts, hundreds of people signed a petition to save the youth centre.
records.zomi: Khuapi office in sum tan ding a tangko ciangin khangno inn hondoh dingin mi za tampi in ngetna lai ah a min uh a khet uh hi.

records.english: Some councils let residents vote on how a small part of the budget should be spent.
records.zomi: Khuapi office pawl khat in sum zat ding' kenkhat neu bangci zat ding hiam teeng mite vote a piaksak hi.

records.english: Most of our council's money goes on schools, roads and care for older people.

records.english: Our community centre receives a small grant from the council each year.

records.english: Money was set aside to fix the roof of the old school before winter.

records.english: The swimming pool closed because the budget couldn't cover the cost of heating it.
records.zomi: Sum zat ding in lumsakna man a pia zo loh manin tuipeekna kikhak hi.

records.english: Thank you for explaining the budget so clearly at the meeting.
records.zomi: Kikhopna ah sum zat ding kician takin na genteh manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: Small habits, repeated every day, often matter more for health than occasional big efforts.

records.english: Good evening, Reverend; thank you for leading tonight's service.

records.english: Welcome aboard this flight to the capital.

records.english: Good morning, Professor; I hope I'm not disturbing you.

records.english: Good evening, ladies and gentlemen, and thank you for your patience while we resolve the technical problem.

records.english: In formal emails, many people begin with a simple greeting such as good morning, followed by the person's title.

records.english: Good afternoon, delegates, and welcome to the second day of the conference.

records.english: Good morning, Director; the visitors from the ministry have arrived.

records.english: Good evening; we're delighted that you could join us for the opening of the new library.

records.english: Asking for help with money is one of the hardest things for many families.

records.english: Many older people would rather struggle alone than ask their children for help.

records.english: Asking family for help can be harder than asking strangers, because we worry about being a burden.

records.english: My mother taught us to ask for help politely and to return the favour when we can.

records.english: Having asked for help once, my brother found it much easier the second time.

records.english: I finally asked my sister for help with the children, and I wish I'd done it months earlier.

records.english: When the baby arrived, we accepted every offer of help, from cooking to washing.

records.english: Shall I wake you if the sky is clear tonight?
records.zomi: Tu zanin van a siang leh kong khanglawhsak ding hiam?

records.english: Do you two want to stay up late to watch the meteor shower?
records.zomi: Na nih in aksi kiak en dingin zan lai dong na om nuam uh hiam?

records.english: My grandmother used to say that a ring around the moon means rain is coming.
records.zomi: Ka pi in kha kiim-a kual khat in guah hong zu ding hi, cihna hi, a ci zel hi.

records.english: Living near the coast, our children learned early how the moon affects the tides.
records.zomi: Tuipi gei ah i teen manin i tate in kha in tuipi tui khanna leh kiamna bangci a lawh hiam a sin masa uh hi.

records.english: We drove out of the city so that the children could see a sky full of stars for the first time.
records.zomi: Naupangte in a masa pen-in aksi tawh a dim van a muh theih nadingin khuapi pua ah i mawng uh hi.

records.english: My grandfather told us the old stories that his village used to tell about the stars.
records.zomi: Ka pu in a khua in aksite tungtang a gen ngei tangthu luite hong gen hi.

records.english: We used an app on my phone to name the constellations above our house.
records.zomi: I inn tung-a aksi pawlte' min theih dingin ka phone tung-a app khat i zang uh hi.

records.english: Is that bright star a planet?
records.zomi: Tua aksi taang pen planet khat ahi hiam?

records.english: It might be Venus, because it doesn't twinkle like the others.
records.zomi: Venus ahi kha ding, a dangte bangin a teekteek kei ahih manin.

records.english: A child who learns that the Earth is billions of years old begins to see time differently.
records.zomi: Leitung kum billion tampi a cing hi, ci a sin naupang khat in hun tuam-in a mu kipan hi.

records.english: Shall we visit the observatory again on your birthday?
records.zomi: Na pianni ciangin aksi enna inn i veh kik ding hiam?

records.english: We collect interesting stones on every walk, and my son keeps them in labelled boxes.
records.zomi: Kalna khempeuh ah suang lamdangte i kaikhawm a, ka tapa in min kigelh bawm sungah a kem hi.

records.english: Grandpa says that in his village, people could tell the time of year from the position of the stars.
records.zomi: Pu in a khua ah mite in aksite' omna pan kum hun a thei thei uh hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Children often ask questions about space that adults can't answer, which is a good reason to look things up together.
records.zomi: Naupangte in mi upate in a dawng zawh loh van tungtang dotna a dong zel uh a, tua in khawm-a zon nading hang hoih khat ahi hi.

records.english: Looking at the night sky together often leads to the biggest questions children ask.
records.zomi: Khawm-a zan van en in naupangte' dotna lian pente a tun zel hi.

records.english: Please put the telescope away carefully; the lens is fragile.
records.zomi: Telescope limtakin koih in; a mit glass a nem hi.

records.english: Looking up at the stars reminds my father of the nights he spent on his family's farm.
records.zomi: Aksite en in ka pa a innkuan' lo-a a zat zante a phawksak hi.

records.english: Counting the seconds between lightning and thunder has become a family game.
records.zomi: Van-ek leh van-ging kikal second sim innkuan kimawlna khat a hi ta hi.

records.english: Watching the stars with a parent can be a child's first lesson in wonder.
records.zomi: Nu hiam pa tawh aksi en pen naupang khat' lamdang sakna sinna masa a hi thei hi.

records.english: Our family found a fossil shell on the beach, millions of years old.
records.zomi: I innkuan in tuipi gei ah kum million tampi a cing fossil khamtang khat i mu uh hi.

records.english: When the earthquake shook our house, we sheltered under the kitchen table, as we had practised.
records.zomi: Leiling in i inn a lin ciangin i kisin bangin an huanna inn dawhkan nuai ah i bu uh hi.

records.english: Can we see the space station from our garden?
records.zomi: I huan pan space station i mu thei ding hiam?

records.english: What do you think is at the edge of the universe?
records.zomi: Van tawpna ah bang a om ding na ci hiam?

records.english: My daughter made a model of the solar system from old tennis balls and string.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in tennis bawl lui leh khau tawh ni leh aksite' model khat a bawl hi.

records.english: Who can find the North Star tonight?
records.zomi: Tu zanin North Star kua in a zong thei ding hiam?

records.english: Wherever we travel, the moon is the one thing my daughter always recognises.
records.zomi: Koi ah i khualzin zongin kha pen ka tanu' a theih tawntung na khat ahi hi.

records.english: Dad showed me how to find south using the sun and a stick.
records.zomi: Pa in ni leh sing khat zang-in sim lam zon dan hong lak hi.

records.english: Our youngest asked how hot the sun is, and we spent an evening reading about it together.
records.zomi: I neu pen in ni bangzah a sa hiam a dong a, nitak khat a tungtang khawmin i sim uh hi.

records.english: Can you see the moon during the day?
records.zomi: Sunlai-in kha na mu thei hiam?

records.english: The children cried when their sandcastle was washed away by the rising tide.
records.zomi: Tuipi tui khanna in a piaunel inn a sil mang ciangin naupangte a kap uh hi.

records.english: When my daughter learned that the stars she sees may no longer exist, she was amazed.
records.zomi: A muh aksite om nawn lo kha ding hi, a theih ciangin ka tanu lamdang a sa mahmah hi.

records.english: The full moon was so bright that we could walk home without a torch.
records.zomi: Kha bup a taang mahmah ahih manin meivak om lo-in inn ah i kal thei uh hi.

records.english: Why is the moon sometimes orange when it rises, Dad?
records.zomi: Pa aw, bang hangin kha a suah ciangin a hun pawl ah a san-eng hiam?

records.english: Its light passes through more of the air near the horizon, which makes it look orange.
records.zomi: A vaak in van leh lei kizopna kiang-a huih tam zaw a kantan ahih manin a san-eng bangin a kilang hi.

records.english: How many planets can we see without a telescope?
records.zomi: Telescope om lo-in aksi bangzah i mu thei hiam?

records.english: When we visited the volcano museum, my son finally understood why the ground sometimes shakes.
records.zomi: Meitang museum i veh ciangin ka tapa in bang hangin lei a hun pawl ah a lin hiam a theih kician hi.

records.english: Our neighbour has a meteorite on his shelf, and the children love holding it.
records.zomi: I innveng in a shelf tungah meteorite khat a nei a, naupangte in a len a nuam sa mahmah uh hi.

records.english: Shall we lie on the grass and count shooting stars?
records.zomi: Lopa tungah i lum-in aksi kiakte i sim ding hiam?

records.english: The children wanted to know why the sky turns red at sunset.
records.zomi: Naupangte in ni tum ciangin bang hangin van a san hiam a theih nuam uh hi.

records.english: Do you know why we have seasons?
records.zomi: Bang hangin hun tuamtuam i nei hiam na thei hiam?

records.english: During the eclipse last year, the whole family stood in the garden with special glasses.
records.zomi: Kum nunung-a ni kiliah laitakin innkuan bup mitlimlang tuam tawh huan sungah i ding uh hi.

records.english: As the sky grew darker, the birds went quiet and the air turned cold.
records.zomi: Van a mial semsem ciangin vasate a dai uh a, huih a vot hi.

records.english: Our son kept asking whether the sun would really come back, and he cheered when it did.
records.zomi: I tapa in ni a hong kik taktak ding hiam a dong den a, a hong kik ciangin a kikou hi.

records.english: Thank you for taking us to the planetarium; the children haven't stopped talking about it.
records.zomi: Planetarium ah hong paipih manin ka lungdam hi; naupangte in a gen khawl kei uh hi.

records.english: Our eldest wants to be an astronaut, so he reads everything about space that he can find.
records.zomi: I upa pen astronaut hi nuam ahih manin van tungtang a muh theih khempeuh a sim hi.

records.english: Every family holiday, we try to find somewhere dark enough to see the stars.
records.zomi: Innkuan tawlngakni khempeuh-in aksi a muh theih dong a mial mun khat i zong uh hi.

records.english: Children who learn about the Earth's history often become more interested in protecting it.
records.zomi: Leitung tangthu a sin naupangte in a kem nading tungah a deihna uh a khang zel hi.

records.english: My name is Peter Khai, and I will be your interpreter for today's hearing.
records.zomi: Ka min Peter Khai ahi a, tuni-a thukhenna-ah na pau lettu ka hi ding hi.

records.english: When the inspector introduced herself, the staff realised the visit was official.
records.zomi: Inspector a kitheisak ciangin nasemte in a vehna kumpi vehna ahi hi, ci a thei uh hi.

records.english: I am applying for the position of library assistant, and I have brought my references with me.
records.zomi: Laibu inn huhtu nasep ka ngen a, ka thuhilhna laite ka tawi hi.

records.english: At official events, name badges help everyone remember who they have already met.
records.zomi: Kumpi kikhopna te ah min ciamtehna in mi khempeuh in a kimuh khin mite a phawk nadingun a huh hi.

records.english: Dear Mr. Tuang, I would like to introduce myself as your daughter's new class teacher.
records.zomi: Pu Tuang, na tanu' sangkhan saya thak ka hih manin ka kitheisak nuam hi.

records.english: Before we begin, could each delegate please introduce themselves and the country they represent?
records.zomi: I kipat ma-in palai khatciat in amau leh a aipuseh gam uh a kitheisak thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: Introduce yourself at reception and show your identification.
records.zomi: Kimuakna dawhkan ah kitheisak inla na lakna lai lak in.

records.english: I'm the engineer responsible for the bridge repairs, and I'll answer any questions you have.
records.zomi: Kei lei bawlphatna adingin mawhpuakna nei engineer ka hi a, na dotna khatpeuh ka dawng ding hi.

records.english: May I take a moment to introduce myself and explain my role in this project?
records.zomi: Hun tawmno ka kitheisak-in hih nasep sung-a ka mawhpuakna ka genteh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Thank you for allowing me to introduce myself.
records.zomi: Ka kitheisak dingin hong phal manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: I am calling from the passport office regarding your application.
records.zomi: Passport office pan na ngetna tungtang kong sam hi.

records.english: Good afternoon, I'm the health visitor; may I come in?
records.zomi: Sunpha, kei damna vehpa ka hi hi; ka lut thei ding hiam?

records.english: Each candidate introduced themselves before answering the panel's questions.
records.zomi: Ngetmi khatciat in makaipawl' dotnate a dawng ma-un a kitheisak uh hi.

records.english: It is an honour to introduce myself to the members of the committee.
records.zomi: Makaipawl mite kiangah kitheisak pen zahtakna khat ahi hi.

records.english: Good morning, Your Honour; I am counsel for the defence.
records.zomi: Zingpha, Thukhenpa; kei kimawhsakpa' thukhen siam ka hi hi.

records.english: What should I say first when I walk into the interview room?
records.zomi: Kidotna khan ah ka lut ciangin a masa-in bang ka gen ding hiam?

records.english: Give your full name, say which position you've applied for, and thank them for seeing you.
records.zomi: Na min kicing gen inla, koi nasep na ngen hiam gen inla, hong muh manun lungdam gen in.

records.english: The new ambassador introduced herself to the president at the official reception.
records.zomi: Ambassador thak in kumpi kimuakna ah president kiangah a kitheisak hi.

records.english: My name is Esther, and I have been elected to represent this ward on the council.
records.zomi: Ka min Esther ahi a, hih gamkhen aipuseh dingin khuapi office ah kiteel ka hi hi.

records.english: In formal settings, it is customary to give your title and organisation when you introduce yourself.
records.zomi: Kizahtak mun te ah na kitheisak ciangin na min tuam leh na pawl gen pen ngeina ahi hi.

records.english: I am the lawyer representing your landlord, and I would like to explain why I am here.
records.zomi: Kei na inn neipa aipuseh thukhen siam ka hi a, bang hangin hih ah ka om hiam genteh ka deih hi.

records.english: I am writing to introduce myself as the new representative for your region.
records.zomi: Na gamkhen adingin aipuseh thak ka hih manin ka kitheisak dingin lai ka gelh hi.

records.english: In my letter of application, I introduced myself and explained my experience in teaching.
records.zomi: Ka ngetna lai ah ka kitheisak a, sinsakna-a ka theihnate ka genteh hi.

records.english: My name is Dr. Mung, and I'm the consultant who will perform your operation.
records.zomi: Ka min Dr. Mung ahi a, na zatui bawl ding siavuan ka hi hi.

records.english: Good morning, everyone; my name is Sarah Lian, and I have been appointed head of the finance department.
records.zomi: Zingpha, mi khempeuh; ka min Sarah Lian ahi a, sum khen makaipa dingin kiteel ka hi hi.

records.english: When you introduce yourself at a conference, mention your organisation and your area of work.
records.zomi: Kikhopna lian khat ah na kitheisak ciangin na pawl leh na nasep mun gen in.

records.english: I'm the new auditor, and I'll be reviewing the accounts this week.
records.zomi: Kei auditor thak ka hi a, hih kal sungin sum ciamtehnate ka en ding hi.

records.english: An official introduction usually includes your name, your position and the reason for your visit.
records.zomi: Kumpi kitheisakna in a tamzaw-in na min, na nasep leh na vehna hang a huam hi.

records.english: Hello, I'm the new head of security, and I'd like to go over the evacuation plan with you.
records.zomi: Hello, kei bitna makaipa thak ka hi a, nang tawh taikhiatna gelna en ka deih hi.

records.english: I am the official translator for this delegation.
records.zomi: Kei hih palai pawl' kumpi pau lettu ka hi hi.

records.english: Good morning; I'm from the tax office, and I have an appointment with the manager.
records.zomi: Zingpha; kei siah office pan ka hi a, manager tawh kimuhna ka nei hi.

records.english: When I introduced myself at the embassy, I gave my name exactly as it appears on my passport.
records.zomi: Embassy ah ka kitheisak ciangin ka passport tung-a a om bang taktak-in ka min ka gen hi.

records.english: Please wear your name badge so that visitors know who you are.
records.zomi: Mikhualte in kua na hi hiam a theih nadingun na min ciamtehna bulh in.

records.english: My name is Grace Ciin, and I am the nurse in charge of this ward tonight.
records.zomi: Ka min Grace Ciin ahi a, tu zanin hih damdawi inn khan' nurse makaipa ka hi hi.

records.english: Could you introduce yourself briefly for the minutes?
records.zomi: Kikhopna ciamtehna adingin tomno-in na kitheisak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Good afternoon; I'm a volunteer with the Red Cross, and I'm here to help with registration.
records.zomi: Sunpha; kei Red Cross-a deihsakna nasem ka hi a, min gelhna ah huh dingin hih ah ka om hi.

records.english: Are you the officer in charge of this investigation?
records.zomi: Hih sitna makaipa office nasempa nang na hi hiam?

records.english: If you are unsure how to introduce yourself formally, follow the example of the person who speaks first.
records.zomi: Kizahtak-a kitheisak dan na theih kician kei leh a masa-in a gen mi' entehna zui in.

records.english: My name is Joseph Pau, and I am the head of the village council.
records.zomi: Ka min Joseph Pau ahi a, khua makaipawl' makaipa ka hi hi.

records.english: I'd like to introduce myself as the school's new principal.
records.zomi: Sang' makaipa thak ka hih manin ka kitheisak nuam hi.

records.english: Please state your full name and occupation for the record.
records.zomi: Ciamtehna adingin na min kicing leh na nasep gen in.

records.english: Ladies and gentlemen, allow me to introduce myself before I begin the presentation.
records.zomi: Numeite leh pasalte, presentation ka kipat ma-in ka kitheisak dingin hong phal un.

records.english: Good afternoon; I am the inspector from the education office.
records.zomi: Sunpha; kei sinna office pan inspector ka hi hi.

records.english: My name is Ruth, and I'll be your guide for the official tour of the parliament building.
records.zomi: Ka min Ruth ahi a, parliament inn kumpi kalna-ah na lampi lakpa ka hi ding hi.

records.english: In formal emails, introduce yourself in the first sentence and state why you are writing.
records.zomi: Email kizahtak te ah kammal masa pen ah kitheisak inla, bang hangin na gelh hiam gen in.

records.english: Introducing yourself correctly to a senior official shows respect for their position.
records.zomi: Kumpi upa khat kiangah dik taka kitheisak in a dinmun zahtakna a lak hi.

records.english: Good evening, I'm the duty manager; how may I help you?
records.zomi: Nitakpha, kei tu-a nasep makaipa ka hi hi; bangci ka huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Hello, I'm the parent representative for Year Six.
records.zomi: Hello, kei Year Six-a nu leh pate' aipuseh ka hi hi.

records.english: A short, clear introduction makes a good first impression at an official meeting.
records.zomi: Kitheisakna tom leh kician khat in kumpi kikhopna khat ah muh masa hoih a bawl hi.

records.english: Excuse me, I'm the new tenant in flat four, and I'd like to introduce myself to the landlord.
records.zomi: Maisak in, kei inn nambat li-a teeng thak ka hi a, inn neipa kiangah ka kitheisak nuam hi.

records.english: I'm the social worker assigned to your family, and I'll visit you every two weeks.
records.zomi: Kei na innkuan adingin kikoih social worker ka hi a, kal nih simin kong veh ding hi.

records.english: Each new employee is asked to introduce themselves at the monthly staff meeting.
records.zomi: Nasem thak khatciat kha simin nasemte' kikhopna ah kitheisak dingin kingen hi.

records.english: I have been asked by the council to explain the new parking rules to residents.
records.zomi: Mawtaw koih thukham thakte teeng mite kiangah genteh dingin khuapi office in hong ngen hi.

records.english: Shall I introduce myself first, or would you like to begin?
records.zomi: Ka kitheisak masa ding hiam, nang na kipat nuam hiam?

records.english: Good morning; I'm the bank manager, and I've been asked to discuss your loan with you.
records.zomi: Zingpha; kei bank manager ka hi a, na leiba tungtang nang tawh kihopih dingin hong ngen uh hi.

records.english: At the start of the hearing, the judge asked both lawyers to introduce themselves.
records.zomi: Thukhenna kipatna ah thukhenpa in thukhen siam nih kitheisak dingin a ngen hi.

records.english: Please allow me to introduce myself and my two colleagues from the ministry.
records.zomi: Ministry pan ka nasep lawm nih leh keimah ka kitheisak dingin hong phal un.

records.english: Good afternoon, members of the board; I am the candidate for the position of treasurer.
records.zomi: Sunpha, makaipawl mite; kei sum kempa nasep ngetmi ka hi hi.

records.english: I represent the residents' association and would like to raise three concerns on their behalf.
records.zomi: Kei teeng mite' pawl aipuseh ka hi a, amaute aiah lungkhamna thum ka gen nuam hi.

records.english: Good evening; my name is David, and I chair the parents' committee.
records.zomi: Nitakpha; ka min David ahi a, nu leh pate' makaipawl ka makaih hi.

records.english: We had the old map of the village copied so that every family could keep one.
records.zomi: Innkuan khempeuh in khat ciat a kem theih nadingin khua' map lui i copy sak uh hi.

records.english: In my great-grandparents' time, the whole village moved when the soil in the old fields became tired.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh pi' nu leh pate' hun lai-in lo lui-a lei a gim ciangin khua bup a suan hi.

records.english: Stone walls from the old village still divide some of the fields.
records.zomi: Khua lui pan suang bangte in lo pawl khat a khen lai hi.

records.english: Shall we ask the oldest people in the village to tell us how it began?
records.zomi: Khua-a upa pente kiangah bangci a kipan hiam gen dingin i ngen ding hiam?

records.english: The old bridge was built by the villagers with wood they carried from the forest.
records.zomi: Lei lui pen khua mite in gammang pan a pua sing tawh a lam uh hi.

records.english: How long has our village stood in the same place?
records.zomi: I khua mun kibang ah bangzah sawt a om khin hiam?

records.english: Settlements were often built facing the morning sun, my grandmother says.
records.zomi: Khua te zingsang ni lam ngat-in kilam zel hi, ka pi in a ci hi.

records.english: The terraced fields on the hillside were made by hand by earlier generations.
records.zomi: Mual dawn-a lo kaalte khangthu masate in khut tawh a bawl uh hi.

records.english: Thank you for showing us the old village; the children will never forget it.
records.zomi: Khua lui hong lak manin ka lungdam hi; naupangte in a mangngilh ngei kei ding uh hi.

records.english: A visit to the old village site makes the stories of our grandparents feel real.
records.zomi: Khua lui mun veh in i pu leh pite' tangthu a taktak bangin a kisak sak hi.

records.english: Old settlements teach us how people lived closely with the land around them.
records.zomi: Khua luite in mite a kiim-a gam tawh bangci kinai takin a nungta uh hiam hong sinsak hi.

records.english: Were the first houses made of wood and bamboo, with roofs of grass?
records.zomi: Inn masate sing leh gua tawh kibawl a, lopa tawh kikhuh hiam?

records.english: The village moved twice before it settled in this valley, according to the elders.
records.zomi: Upate' gen bangin khua hih kuam ah a kip ma-in nihvei a suan hi.

records.english: Some old villages were abandoned because of sickness or war, the elders say.
records.zomi: Khua lui pawl khat natna hiam gal hangin kinusia hi, upate in a ci uh hi.

records.english: Dad says that in the past, houses were built close together so that neighbours could help each other.
records.zomi: Pa in a ma-in innvengte a kihuh theih nadingun inn kinai takin kilam hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Do you know where your family lived before they came to this village?
records.zomi: Na innkuan hih khua ah a hong pai ma-un koi ah a teeng uh hiam na thei hiam?

records.english: You need permission from the elders before you dig anywhere near the old site.
records.zomi: Khua lui mun kiang koi ah zong na tou ma-in upate' phalna na kisam hi.

records.english: The names of some hills and streams still remind us of the families who first lived near them.
records.zomi: Mual leh tuiluang pawl khat' minte in a kiang-a teeng masa innkuante hong phawksak lai hi.

records.english: When we found an old cooking pot in the ground, the elders told us it had belonged to an earlier settlement.
records.zomi: Lei sungah beel lui khat i muh uh ciangin upate in khua masa khat' a hi hi, hong ci uh hi.

records.english: The old village had no roads, only narrow footpaths between the houses.
records.zomi: Khua lui in lampi lian om lo a, inn kikal-ah kalna lampi kiat bek a om hi.

records.english: Each generation added something to the village, a path, a fence or a new well.
records.zomi: Khangthak khempeuh in khua ah lampi, huang hiam tuikhuk thak bang khat peuhpeuh a behlap uh hi.

records.english: Can you show me where the old village gate used to be?
records.zomi: Khua kongpi lui koi ah a om ngei hiam hong lak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: The elders say that our village was first built on the top of the hill, where it was easier to defend.
records.zomi: Upate in i khua a masa-in kidal a baih zawk nadingin mual tung ah kilam hi, a ci uh hi.

records.english: Does the village chief keep a list of all the families who have lived here?
records.zomi: Khuamang in hih ah a teeng ngei innkuan khempeuh' list a kem hiam?

records.english: Wear strong shoes, because the road to the old village site is steep.
records.zomi: Khua lui mun lam lampi a ding ahih manin khedap hat silh in.

records.english: The ruins of the old church are all that remain of the first village.
records.zomi: Pawlpi lui' a siat khinte bek khua masa pan a om lai hi.

records.english: Is the old village well still used today?
records.zomi: Khua tuikhuk lui tu dong kizang lai hiam?

records.english: Who knows how old the path to the next village is?
records.zomi: A kiang khua lam lampi bangzah a lui hiam kua in a thei hiam?

records.english: The elders still remember which family lived in each of the old houses.
records.zomi: Upate in inn lui khatciat ah koi innkuan a teeng hiam a phawk lai uh hi.

records.english: Many old settlements were built near rivers or springs, because water was the first thing people needed.
records.zomi: Mite' kisam masa pen tui ahih manin khua lui tampi lui hiam tui kiluanna kiang ah kilam hi.

records.english: Why did the village move down to the valley?
records.zomi: Bang hangin khua kuam ah a kum suk hiam?

records.english: According to my grandfather, the old spring dried up, so the families followed the water.
records.zomi: Ka pu' gen bangin tui kiluanna lui a keu ahih manin innkuante tui a zui uh hi.

records.english: Every family in our village has a story about how their ancestors arrived.
records.zomi: I khua-a innkuan khempeuh in a pu leh pa uh bangci a tung uh hiam tangthu a nei uh hi.

records.english: Is it true that the first families arrived here on foot over the mountains?
records.zomi: Innkuan masate mual tung kantan-in khe tawh hih ah a tung uh hi, cih a dik hiam?

records.english: Grandpa can point to the exact spot where the first school stood.
records.zomi: Pu in sang masa pen a dingna mun taktak a liap thei hi.

records.english: Did people in the old village keep animals inside their houses?
records.zomi: Khua lui-a mite in a inn sungah ganhing a khawi uh hiam?

records.english: My grandmother remembers when there were only twelve houses in the whole village.
records.zomi: Ka pi in khua bup ah inn sawm leh nih bek a om hun a phawk hi.

records.english: Grandma says the old village was so small that everyone ate together at festivals.
records.zomi: Pi in khua lui a neu lua ahih manin pawi ciangin mi khempeuh khawmin a ne uh hi, a ci hi.

records.english: When a new family arrived, the whole village helped them build their house.
records.zomi: Innkuan thak khat a tun ciangin khua bup in a inn uh a lam nadingin a huh uh hi.

records.english: Children, stay on the path when we visit the old village site.
records.zomi: Naupangte, khua lui mun i veh ciangin lampi tungah om un.

records.english: Please don't move the old stones on the hill; they mark where the first houses stood.
records.zomi: Mual tung-a suang luite suan kei un; inn masate' dingna a ciamteh hi.

records.english: Settlements grow and change, but the stories about their beginnings often stay the same.
records.zomi: Khuate a khang-in a kikheel a, ahi zongin a kipatna tungtang tangthute a kibang den zel hi.

records.english: Shall we show the elders the pieces of old pottery we found behind the school?
records.zomi: Sang nung-a i muh leibel lui kenkhatte upate i lak ding hiam?

records.english: The young people are helping to record the history of the village before the oldest members pass away.
records.zomi: Upa pente a si ma-un khangnote in khua' tangthu a ciamteh nadingin a huh uh hi.

records.english: How did people choose where to build a village in the past?
records.zomi: A ma-in mite in khua lam nading mun bangci a teel uh hiam?

records.english: They looked for water, good soil and a place that was safe from storms and enemies.
records.zomi: Tui, lei hoih leh huihpi leh galte pan a bit mun a zong uh hi.

records.english: When I was a boy, my grandfather took me up to the old village site.
records.zomi: Naupang ka hih lai-in ka pu in khua lui mun ah hong paipih hi.

records.english: He showed me where his own grandfather's house had stood, using a stick to trace the outline in the earth.
records.zomi: Amah' pu' inn a dingna mun hong lak a, sing khat tawh lei tungah a gei a khang hi.

records.english: Ever since then, the empty hilltop has felt like part of our family.
records.zomi: Tua pan mual tung awng in i innkuan' kenkhat bangin a kisa hi.

records.english: The village has grown so much that the old centre is now surrounded by new houses.
records.zomi: Khua a khang mahmah ahih manin lailung lui inn thakte in a kim hi.

records.english: Knowing where your family came from can give you a strong sense of belonging.
records.zomi: Na innkuan koi pan hong pai hiam theih in kihelna kisakna hat khat hong pia thei hi.

records.english: The village graveyard on the hill tells us how long people have lived here.
records.zomi: Mual tung-a khua' hanmual in mite hih ah bangzah sawt a teeng khin uh hiam hong gen hi.

records.english: Some settlements disappeared completely when the young people moved to the towns.
records.zomi: Khangnote khuapi ah a suan uh ciangin khua pawl khat a mang vekpi hi.

records.english: Stories about how a village was founded are often passed down by word of mouth.
records.zomi: Khua khat bangci kiphut hiam tangthute kam tawh kipia khia zel hi.

records.english: Old settlements often grew around a meeting place, such as a large tree or an open square.
records.zomi: Khua luite sing lianpi hiam mun awng bang kikhopna mun khat kiim ah a khang zel hi.

records.english: Our teacher took the class to see the old village site and asked us to draw what we imagined it looked like.
records.zomi: I saya in sangkhan khua lui mun en dingin a paipih a, bangci a kilang ding hiam i ngaihsut a zeek dingin hong ngen hi.

records.english: The history of a settlement is written not only in books but in its paths, walls and fields.
records.zomi: Khua khat' tangthu laibu sung bek hi lo-in a lampi, a bang leh a lote ah kigelh hi.

records.english: Some families can name every place their ancestors lived before they settled here.
records.zomi: Innkuan pawl khat in hih ah a kip ma-un a pu leh pate' teenna mun khempeuh a min a gen thei uh hi.

records.english: My family still owns a field near the place where our ancestors first lived.
records.zomi: Ka innkuan in i pu leh pate' teenna masa mun kiang-a lo khat a nei lai hi.

records.english: You can still see the stone foundations of the old houses among the trees.
records.zomi: Sing kikal-ah inn luite' suang inn khuam kipna na mu thei lai hi.

records.english: My daughter asked me to repeat her phone number three times before she wrote it down.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in a gelh ma-in a phone nambat vei thum gen kik dingin hong ngen hi.

records.english: Can you say that again, but in our language?
records.zomi: I pau tawh gen kik thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Sorry, I wasn't listening; what did you say?
records.zomi: Hong maisak in, ka ngaikhia kei hi; bang na ci hiam?

records.english: When we speak to our grandparents on video calls, we often have to repeat things because of the delay.
records.zomi: Video sapna tungah i pu leh pi tawh i kihopih ciangin a nungdaih hangin thu i gen kik kul zel uh hi.

records.english: My son mumbles so much that I have to ask him to repeat almost everything.
records.zomi: Ka tapa a kam sung-a a gen mahmah ahih manin a gen khempeuh dek gen kik dingin ka ngen kul hi.

records.english: Please don't sigh when Grandma asks you to repeat something.
records.zomi: Pi in khat peuhpeuh gen kik dingin a nget ciangin hu hal kei in.

records.english: What was the name of that restaurant you mentioned yesterday?
records.zomi: Zan in na gen an zuakna inn' min bang hiam?

records.english: The Blue Lantern, near the river.
records.zomi: The Blue Lantern, lui kiangah.

records.english: Our youngest loves hearing the story of the day he was born again and again.
records.zomi: I neu pen in a suah ni tangthu vei tampi zak a it hi.

records.english: I had to ask my uncle to repeat his story, because I couldn't believe what I'd heard.
records.zomi: Ka zak ka um zo kei ahih manin ka pa neu a tangthu gen kik dingin ka ngen kul hi.

records.english: Speak a little louder, please; Grandpa can't hear you from over there.
records.zomi: Aw ngaih zaw-in gen in, maw; Pu in tua mun pan a za thei kei hi.

records.english: When my grandparents first got a mobile phone, every call began with three requests to repeat ourselves.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh pi in mobile phone a neih masa ciangin sapna khempeuh gen kik dingin ngenna thum tawh a kipan hi.

records.english: Grandpa tells the same jokes so often that the children can finish them for him.
records.zomi: Pu in nuihzakna kibang a gen tamvei mahmah ahih manin naupangte in amah adingin a zo thei uh hi.

records.english: Repeating instructions back is a good way for children to show they've understood.
records.zomi: Thuhilhnate gen kik pen naupangte in a theih uh lak nading hoih khat ahi hi.

records.english: When you're tired, it's easy to miss what people say and ask them to repeat it.
records.zomi: Na gim ciangin mite' gen pelh-in gen kik dingin ngen a baih hi.

records.english: Nodding along without understanding has led to more than one family argument in our house.
records.zomi: Theih lo-in lu nong bek in i inn ah innkuan kinialna khat sang a tam a piangsak hi.

records.english: Hearing aids made it possible for my grandfather to follow the conversation without constant repetition.
records.zomi: Bil zak huhnate in ka pu gen kik den kul lo-in kihopihna a zui thei hi.

records.english: Could you tell me again how to get to your new flat?
records.zomi: Na inn thak lam pai dan hong gen kik thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Take the number six bus and get off at the hospital; I'm right opposite.
records.zomi: Bus nambat guk tuang inla damdawi inn ah kiak in; kei a langkhat ah ka om hi.

records.english: My grandmother repeats her advice every time we visit, just in case we've forgotten.
records.zomi: Ka pi in i mangngilh kha leh ci-in i veh vei khempeuh-in a thuhilhna a gen kik hi.

records.english: Can you play that voice message again?
records.zomi: Tua aw thu na sim kik thei ding hiam?

records.english: Sorry, could you start from the beginning?
records.zomi: Hong maisak in, a kipatna pan na kipan kik thei ding hiam?

records.english: My son asked me to say the instructions again, because he had been watching the cat.
records.zomi: Ka tapa zawhngeu a en ahih manin thuhilhnate gen kik dingin hong ngen hi.

records.english: Did you get all that, or shall I go through it again?
records.zomi: A khempeuh na thei hiam, kong gen kik ding hiam?

records.english: Patience is the first thing you learn when you live with someone who is losing their hearing.
records.zomi: Thuakzawhna pen a bil zak a kiam mi khat tawh na teen ciangin na sin masa pen ahi hi.

records.english: Dad is hard of hearing, so we always face him when we speak.
records.zomi: Pa' bil a za hoih lo ahih manin i gen ciangin amah i ngat tawntung uh hi.

records.english: Could you write the recipe down instead of telling me again?
records.zomi: Hong gen kik sangin an huan dan na gelh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Asking a relative to repeat something on a bad phone line is better than guessing.
records.zomi: Phone hoih lo ah sanggam khat kiangah gen kik dingin ngen in ngaihsut sangin a hoih zaw hi.

records.english: Could you possibly repeat the doctor's instructions, because I was too worried to take them in?
records.zomi: Ka lungkham lua ahih manin ka za zo kei hi; siavuan' thuhilhnate na gen kik thei ding hiam?

records.english: In our house, if anyone has to ask for something to be repeated more than twice, we turn the music off.
records.zomi: I inn ah kuamah in nihvei sang khat peuhpeuh gen kik dingin a ngen kul leh la i phel hi.

records.english: Thank you for repeating it; I understand now.
records.zomi: Gen kik manin ka lungdam hi; tu-in ka thei hi.

records.english: Repeating something patiently for an elderly relative is a small act of love.
records.zomi: Sanggam upa khat adingin thuakzawh taka gen kik pen itna lahna neu khat ahi hi.

records.english: Did you say you'd be home at six or at seven?
records.zomi: Nai guk ciangin hiam nai sagih ciangin hiam inn ah na om ding hi, na ci hiam?

records.english: Seven, because I have to stop at the shop.
records.zomi: Sagih, dawl ah ka khawl kul ahih manin.

records.english: Children often ask you to read the same story again and again, even when they know every word.
records.zomi: Naupangte in kammal khempeuh a theih uh hangin tangthu kibang vei tampi sim dingin a ngen zel uh hi.

records.english: Would it help if I wrote the times down for you as well?
records.zomi: Nang adingin hun te ka gelh sak leh a huh ding hiam?

records.english: Sorry, I missed that; the television was too loud.
records.zomi: Hong maisak in, ka pelh hi; television a ging lua hi.

records.english: At family dinners, everyone talks at once, so we're always asking each other to repeat things.
records.zomi: Innkuan nitak an ah mi khempeuh khatvei-in a gen uh ahih manin khat leh khat gen kik dingin i kingen tawntung uh hi.

records.english: Will you explain the rules of the game once more?
records.zomi: Kimawlna' thukhamte vei khat na genteh kik ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, but this time please listen until the end.
records.zomi: Ka genteh ding hi, ahi zongin tu vei-in a tawpna dong ngaikhia in.

records.english: What did your sister say just before she hung up?
records.zomi: Na u numei in a khak ma-in bang a ci hiam?

records.english: Something about the baby, but the line was breaking up.
records.zomi: Naungek tungtang khat peuhpeuh, ahi zongin phone a kitan zel hi.

records.english: Can you repeat the name of your new teacher?
records.zomi: Na saya thak' min na gen kik thei ding hiam?

records.english: Mrs. Hau, and she teaches maths as well.
records.zomi: Nu Hau, maths zong a hilh hi.

records.english: Sorry, Grandpa, could you say that again a bit more slowly?
records.zomi: Hong maisak in, Pu aw, nuam deuh-in na gen kik thei ding hiam?

records.english: I said I'd like you to fetch my glasses from the bedroom.
records.zomi: Lupna khan pan ka mitlimlang hong la sak dingin ka deih hi, ka ci hi.

records.english: Sorry, how many people did you say were coming for lunch?
records.zomi: Hong maisak in, sun an adingin mi bangzah hong pai ding hi, na ci hiam?

records.english: Twelve, if your brother brings his friends.
records.zomi: Sawm leh nih, na sanggam pasal in a lawmte a paipih leh.

records.english: What did the baby just say?
records.zomi: Naungek in tu-in bang a ci hiam?

records.english: I think she was asking for more milk, but it's hard to tell.
records.zomi: Nawitui behlap a ngen hi, ka sa a, ahi zongin theih a haksa hi.

records.english: When my mother's hearing got worse, the whole family learned to speak more clearly.
records.zomi: Ka nu' bil zak a kiam semsem ciangin innkuan bup in kician zaw-in gen a sin uh hi.

records.english: My niece repeats new words over and over until she can say them perfectly.
records.zomi: Ka tunu in kammal thakte a kician-in a gen theih dong a gen kik den hi.

records.english: Would you mind repeating the date of the wedding?
records.zomi: Mopawi ni na gen kik thei ding hiam?

records.english: My little sister repeats everything I say just to annoy me.
records.zomi: Ka nau numei in hong lungkimsak lo dingin ka gen khempeuh a gen kik hi.

records.english: Please repeat what I've just told you, so I know you've understood.
records.zomi: Na theih ka theih nadingin tu-a kong gen gen kik in.

records.english: When a child keeps asking you to repeat something, they may simply be confused by the way you've explained it.
records.zomi: Naupang khat in khat peuhpeuh gen kik dingin a ngen den ciangin na genteh dan in a buaisak bek kha ding hi.

records.english: When my grandmother talks on the phone, she asks me to repeat everything the other person says.
records.zomi: Ka pi phone tungah a kihopih ciangin a dang mi' gen khempeuh gen kik dingin hong ngen hi.

records.english: Could you say the address again, so I can type it into the map?
records.zomi: Map tungah ka gelh theih nadingin teenna mun na gen kik thei ding hiam?

records.english: My husband has to hear something three times before he remembers it.
records.zomi: Ka pasal in a phawk ma-in thu khat vei thum a za kul hi.

records.english: In a busy family kitchen, it's normal to ask someone to repeat what they said.
records.zomi: Innkuan an huanna inn buai khat ah mi khat' gen gen kik dingin ngen pen ngeina ahi hi.

records.english: Grandpa's appointment lasted only ten minutes, but the journey took two hours.
records.zomi: Pu' kimuhna minit sawm bek a sawt a, ahi zongin khualzinna in nai nih a la hi.

records.english: Missing an appointment without telling the clinic means someone else loses that slot.
records.zomi: Clinic gen lo-in kimuhna khat na pelh leh mi dang khat in tua hun a mansuah hi.

records.english: Write the appointment card number on the calendar so you can find it quickly.
records.zomi: Manlang taka na muh theih nadingin kimuhna card nambat calendar tungah gelh in.

records.english: Juggling appointments for three children and two grandparents is almost a full-time job.
records.zomi: Naupang thum leh pu leh pi nih adingin kimuhnate kem pen nasep bup bang dek ahi hi.

records.english: Booking the next appointment before you leave the clinic saves a phone call later.
records.zomi: Clinic na nusiat ma-in a zom kimuhna na lai leh a nung-a phone sapna khat a khol hi.

records.english: My aunt couldn't get an appointment for three weeks, so she went to the walk-in clinic instead.
records.zomi: Ka ni kal thum sung kimuhna a ngah zo lo ahih manin lai lo-a pai theih clinic ah a pai hi.

records.english: Could the doctor see my son on Saturday morning instead?
records.zomi: Siavuan in ka tapa Kiginni zingsang ah a en thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, the clinic is open until noon on Saturdays.
records.zomi: Thei hi, clinic Kiginni ciangin sun lai dong a kihong hi.

records.english: Mum never misses an appointment, even when she feels perfectly well.
records.zomi: Nu a dam kicing zongin kimuhna khat zong a pelh ngei kei hi.

records.english: Our family doctor knows us so well that the appointments feel like visits to a friend.
records.zomi: I innkuan siavuan in eite hong thei mahmah ahih manin kimuhnate lawm veh bangin kisa hi.

records.english: Every January, I sit down with the calendar and book the whole family's check-ups for the year, before everyone's diary fills up.
records.zomi: January simin mi khempeuh' hun ciamteh laibu a dim ma-in calendar tawh ka tu a, innkuan bup' kum sung damna sitnate ka lai hi.

records.english: Booking appointments online has made life much easier for my parents, once they learned how.
records.zomi: Online-in kimuhna lai in ka nu leh ka pa' nuntakna a baihsak mahmah a, a zat dan a sin khit uh ciangin.

records.english: Next time, let's book the appointments for the same day.
records.zomi: A zom vei-in kimuhnate ni kibang-in i lai ni.

records.english: My sister books her appointments early in the morning, so that she can still go to work.
records.zomi: Ka u numei in nasep ah a pai thei lai nadingin a kimuhnate zingsang tung-in a lai hi.

records.english: Some clinics let families book several appointments together, which saves a great deal of time.
records.zomi: Clinic pawl khat in innkuante kimuhna tampi khawmin a lai theisak uh a, tua in hun tampi a khol hi.

records.english: Who's going to stay with the children while I'm at the hospital on Friday?
records.zomi: Laithai ni-in damdawi inn ah ka om laitakin naupangte tawh kua a om ding hiam?

records.english: Keeping a list of questions for each appointment helps my father remember what to ask.
records.zomi: Kimuhna khatciat adingin dotna list kem in ka pa bang dong ding hiam a phawk nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Last month, I booked appointments for my mother and my son at the same clinic.
records.zomi: Kha nunung in ka nu leh ka tapa adingin clinic kibang ah kimuhna ka lai hi.

records.english: Unfortunately, I mixed up the times and brought my son on the wrong day.
records.zomi: Lungkham huai takin hun te ka khial a, ka tapa ni khial ah ka paipih hi.

records.english: The receptionist laughed kindly and managed to fit him in between two other patients.
records.zomi: Kimuakna nasempa in hehpih takin a nuih a, natpa dang nih kikal-ah amah a koih thei hi.

records.english: Thank you for driving me to all my appointments while I couldn't drive.
records.zomi: Mawtaw ka mawng zawh loh laitakin ka kimuhna khempeuh ah hong paipih manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: My children are less nervous about the dentist when they have appointments together.
records.zomi: Ka tate kimuhna khawmin a neih uh ciangin ha siavuan a lau tawm zaw uh hi.

records.english: The waiting list for the specialist was so long that we booked a private appointment for my father.
records.zomi: A tuam siavuan ngakna list a sau lua ahih manin ka pa adingin a guk-a kimuhna khat i lai uh hi.

records.english: When my wife was pregnant, we planned our weekends around her hospital appointments.
records.zomi: Ka zi nau a pai lai-in a damdawi inn kimuhnate kiim ah i kal tawpte i gel uh hi.

records.english: Can you check whether the children's eye tests are due this year?
records.zomi: Naupangte' mit sitna tu kum ah a tung hiam na en thei ding hiam?

records.english: The clinic phoned to ask whether we could come in an hour earlier.
records.zomi: Clinic in nai khat ma-in hong pai thei ding i hi hiam dong dingin hong sam hi.

records.english: Did you remember to book your father's blood test?
records.zomi: Na pa' sisan sitna lai na phawk hiam?

records.english: Yes, it's on Monday morning, before breakfast.
records.zomi: Phawk hi, Pizing ni zingsang, zingsang an ma-in ahi hi.

records.english: Grandpa insists on arriving an hour early for every appointment.
records.zomi: Pu in kimuhna khempeuh ah nai khat ma-in tun a ngen den hi.

records.english: My brother forgot his appointment twice, so the clinic now calls him the day before.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in a kimuhna nihvei a mangngilh ahih manin clinic in a zan ma-in a sam hi.

records.english: Please write down the date and time of the vaccination so that we don't forget.
records.zomi: I mangngilh loh nadingin natna hihna damdawi sutna ni leh hun gelh in.

records.english: We've booked a video appointment, because Grandpa finds the journey too tiring.
records.zomi: Pu in khualzinna a gimhuai sa ahih manin video kimuhna khat i lai uh hi.

records.english: The dentist's receptionist remembered all our names after just two visits.
records.zomi: Ha siavuan' kimuakna nasempa in vehna nih khit ciangin i min khempeuh a phawk hi.

records.english: When both parents work full-time, finding a time for a child's appointment can be a real challenge.
records.zomi: Nu leh pa a nih in hun bup nasep a sep uh ciangin naupang khat' kimuhna adingin hun zon a haksa taktak thei hi.

records.english: Can you take Grandma to her eye appointment on Thursday?
records.zomi: Laizing ni-in Pi a mit kimuhna ah na paipih thei ding hiam?

records.english: Only if it's after three, because I'm working until then.
records.zomi: Nai thum khit ciang bek, tua hun dong nasep ka sem ding ahih manin.

records.english: Making a doctor's appointment for a teenager can be tricky when they want privacy.
records.zomi: Tangval-tangnu khat adingin siavuan kimuhna bawl in a guk-a om a deih ciangun a haksa thei hi.

records.english: Can I bring my daughter to my appointment, or should I find a babysitter?
records.zomi: Ka kimuhna ah ka tanu ka paipih thei ding hiam, naupang kem mi khat ka zong ding hiam?

records.english: My son's school asked us to make medical appointments outside school hours when possible.
records.zomi: Ka tapa' sang in a theih ciangin sang hun pua ah damdawi kimuhnate bawl dingin hong ngen hi.

records.english: I booked the whole family in for dental check-ups on the same afternoon, which saved us three trips.
records.zomi: Innkuan bup ha sitna nitak lam kibang ah ka lai a, tua in khualzinna thum hong khol hi.

records.english: We moved my father's appointment so that he wouldn't have to travel in the rush hour.
records.zomi: Mi tam hun ah ka pa a khualzin kul loh nadingin a kimuhna i suan uh hi.

records.english: When is the next free appointment for a child's vaccination?
records.zomi: Naupang' natna hihna damdawi sutna adingin a zom kimuhna awng bang hun ahi hiam?

records.english: Shall we go for lunch after your appointment?
records.zomi: Na kimuhna khit ciangin sun an ne dingin i pai ding hiam?

records.english: We asked for a longer appointment, because my mother has several things to discuss with the doctor.
records.zomi: Ka nu in siavuan tawh a kihopih nop thu tampi a neih manin kimuhna sau zaw khat i ngen uh hi.

records.english: Mum keeps every family appointment on the calendar by the fridge.
records.zomi: Nu in innkuan kimuhna khempeuh fridge kiang-a calendar tungah a kem hi.

records.english: Setting a reminder on my phone is the only way I remember the children's appointments.
records.zomi: Ka phone tungah phawksakna koih bek tawh naupangte' kimuhnate ka phawk thei hi.

records.english: Is it possible to book an evening appointment for my husband?
records.zomi: Ka pasal adingin nitak kimuhna khat lai theih ding hiam?

records.english: A little planning can turn a stressful round of appointments into a manageable week.
records.zomi: Gelna tawmno in kimuhna lungkhamhuai tampi kal khat zawh theih ah a kheel thei hi.

records.english: The appointment was moved to the afternoon, which suited everyone better.
records.zomi: Kimuhna nitak lam ah kisuan a, tua in mi khempeuh adingin a kilawm zaw hi.

records.english: Do you prefer morning or afternoon appointments?
records.zomi: Zingsang kimuhna na deih zaw hiam, nitak lam hiam?

records.english: I'm sorry, but I need to cancel my mother's appointment, because she's in hospital.
records.zomi: Hong maisak in, ka nu damdawi inn ah a om ahih manin a kimuhna ka phiat kul hi.

records.english: Could you remind me about my appointment on Tuesday?
records.zomi: Pithai ni-a ka kimuhna hong phawksak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: I always book the first appointment of the day, because the doctor is never late then.
records.zomi: Tua hun ciangin siavuan a nung ngei lo ahih manin ni sung-a kimuhna masa pen ka lai tawntung hi.

records.english: My parents have so many appointments that I made them a colour-coded calendar.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa' kimuhna a tam mahmah ahih manin rong tawh kikhen calendar khat ka bawl sak hi.

records.english: We always schedule the children's check-ups during the school holidays, so that nobody has to miss lessons or work.
records.zomi: Kuamah in sinna hiam nasep a pelh loh nadingin sang tawlngakni sungin naupangte' damna sitna i bawl tawntung uh hi.

records.english: Could you call the dentist and move my appointment to next week?
records.zomi: Ha siavuan sam inla ka kimuhna kal zom ah na suan thei ding hiam?

records.english: We had to cancel the baby's check-up because she had a fever.
records.zomi: Naungek' pumpi a lum ahih manin a damna sitna i phiat kul uh hi.

records.english: Rescheduling an appointment is better than missing it without a word.
records.zomi: Kimuhna khat suan in gen lo-a pelh sangin a hoih zaw hi.

records.english: Shall I book your check-up at the same time as mine?
records.zomi: Na damna sitna kei' tawh hun kibang-in ka lai ding hiam?

records.english: Coordinating hospital appointments for an elderly parent often means taking days off work.
records.zomi: Nu hiam pa upa khat adingin damdawi inn kimuhnate kem in nasep pan ni tampi tawl cihna a hi zel hi.

records.english: We made a list of who was bringing what, so that we wouldn't end up with five desserts and no rice.
records.zomi: An khit-a ne ding nga leh an om lo-in i bei loh nadingin kua in bang a tawi ding hiam list khat i bawl uh hi.

records.english: Is anyone bringing a guitar this year?
records.zomi: Tu kum kuamah in guitar a tawi ding hiam?

records.english: Every gathering ends with the same argument about whose turn it is to wash up.
records.zomi: Kikhopna khempeuh kua' kuang sil ding ahi hiam kinialna kibang tawh a bei hi.

records.english: Shall we video-call our cousins abroad so they can join the gathering?
records.zomi: Gamdang-a i sanggamte kikhopna ah a kihel theih nadingun video tawh i sam ding hiam?

records.english: A family gathering is a chance to remember the people who are no longer with us.
records.zomi: Innkuan kikhopna pen i kiang-a om nawn lo mite phawk nading hun khat ahi hi.

records.english: Shall the children put on a little concert after dinner?
records.zomi: Nitak an khit ciangin naupangte in la lakna neu khat a bawl ding uh hiam?

records.english: Dad always makes a short speech at the start of the meal.
records.zomi: Pa in an kipatna ah thugenna tom khat a gen tawntung hi.

records.english: Do you think we should invite the neighbours to the family gathering this year?
records.zomi: Tu kum innkuan kikhopna ah innvengte i sam ding na ci hiam?

records.english: Our uncle drives four hours each way to be at every gathering, and he hasn't missed one in twenty years.
records.zomi: I pa neu kikhopna khempeuh ah om dingin pai lam leh ciah lam nai li ciat a mawng a, kum sawmnih sungin khat zong a pelh kei hi.

records.english: Last summer, forty relatives arrived for my grandparents' sixtieth wedding anniversary.
records.zomi: Khal nunung in ka pu leh pi' kiteenna kum sawmguk cinna adingin sanggam sawmli hong tung uh hi.

records.english: We borrowed chairs from the church and tables from the school, and the garden looked like a festival.
records.zomi: Pawlpi pan tutphah leh sang pan dawhkan i leitawi uh a, huan pawi bangin a kilang hi.

records.english: Late at night, when the youngest had gone to bed, my grandfather stood up and thanked everyone by name.
records.zomi: Zan lai ciangin a neu pente a ihmut khit uh ciangin ka pu a ding-in mi khempeuh a min tawh lungdam a gen hi.

records.english: For a week after the gathering, the house was so full of leftovers that we didn't need to cook once.
records.zomi: Kikhopna khit kal khat sung an om lai-in inn a dim ahih manin vei khat zong an i huan kul kei uh hi.

records.english: At big gatherings, the oldest relatives are always served first in our family.
records.zomi: Kikhopna lianpite ah i innkuan in sanggam upa pente a masa-in an a pia tawntung hi.

records.english: The quiet cousin turned out to be the best storyteller at the whole gathering.
records.zomi: Sanggam dai pen kikhopna bup-a tangthu gen siam pen ahi hi, ci a kilang hi.

records.english: My brother's new girlfriend was nervous about meeting the whole family at once.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal' numei it thak innkuan bup khatvei-in a kimuh ding a lau hi.

records.english: Shall I bring extra chairs from our house?
records.zomi: I inn pan tutphah behlap ka tawi ding hiam?

records.english: Can you set up the long table in the garden before the guests arrive?
records.zomi: Mikhualte a tun ma-un huan sungah dawhkan sau koih na thei ding hiam?

records.english: Please don't bring up politics at the dinner table this year.
records.zomi: Tu kum an ne dawhkan ah politics thu kipan kei un.

records.english: Each family brings one dish, so nobody has to cook for thirty people alone.
records.zomi: Innkuan khatciat in an khat a tawi uh ahih manin kuamah in mi sawmthum adingin amah kia-in a huan kul kei hi.

records.english: The best part of a family gathering is often the quiet conversation late at night.
records.zomi: Innkuan kikhopna' a hoih pen a tamzaw-in zan lai-a kihopihna dai ahi hi.

records.english: Some family gatherings happen every year, while others take place only for weddings and funerals.
records.zomi: Innkuan kikhopna pawl khat kum simin a om a, a dangte mopawi leh misi vuina ciang bek-in a om hi.

records.english: Who's going to look after the little ones while we cook?
records.zomi: An i huan laitakin a neute kua in a kem ding hiam?

records.english: Gatherings are where family news is shared, from new jobs to new babies.
records.zomi: Kikhopnate nasep thak pan naungek thak dong innkuan thuthakte kihawmna mun ahi hi.

records.english: Long-distance relatives often plan their holidays around the yearly family gathering.
records.zomi: Gamla-a teeng sanggamte in kum simin innkuan kikhopna kiim ah a tawlngakni uh a gel zel uh hi.

records.english: Grandpa always slips money into the children's pockets when he thinks nobody is looking.
records.zomi: Pu in kuamah in en kei hi, a sak ciangin naupangte' ip sungah sum a sel tawntung hi.

records.english: Our family gatherings have got smaller as the older generation has passed away.
records.zomi: Khangthak upate a sih khit uh ciangin i innkuan kikhopnate a neu zaw hi.

records.english: The children made name cards for every place at the table.
records.zomi: Naupangte in dawhkan-a mun khempeuh adingin min card a bawl uh hi.

records.english: After the meal, the old men played cards while the children played football in the yard.
records.zomi: An khit ciangin pasal upate card a kimawl uh a, naupangte inn mai huang ah bawlung a kimawl uh hi.
