records.english: Do you two want to sit with the cousins or with the grown-ups?
records.zomi: Na nih in sanggamte tawh na tu nuam uh hiam, mi upate tawh hiam?

records.english: We hired a minibus so that the older relatives could travel together.
records.zomi: Sanggam upate khawmin a khualzin theih nadingun bus neu khat i luah uh hi.

records.english: Gatherings give cousins who live far apart a chance to become friends.
records.zomi: Kikhopnate in gamla-a teeng sanggamte lawm a suah nadingun hun a pia hi.

records.english: My little sister cried when the cousins had to leave.
records.zomi: Sanggamte a pai kul uh ciangin ka nau numei a kap hi.

records.english: Large family gatherings need planning, or the same two people end up doing all the work.
records.zomi: Innkuan kikhopna lianpite gelna a kisam a, a kei leh mi nih kibang mah in nasep khempeuh a sem tawntung uh hi.

records.english: Who's going to pick up Great-Grandma from the care home?
records.zomi: Mi upa kemna inn pan Pi' nu kua in a la ding hiam?

records.english: You two can be in charge of welcoming guests at the door.
records.zomi: Na nih kongkhak ah mikhual muak nading makaite na hi ding uh hi.

records.english: Let's hold the next gathering at the lake, where there's room for everyone.
records.zomi: A zom kikhopna mi khempeuh adingin mun a om dil gei ah i bawl ni.

records.english: Everyone went home tired, full and already looking forward to next year.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh a gim, a vah-in kum zom a lamen khin-in inn ah a ciah uh hi.

records.english: A family gathering can be exhausting for the hosts, even when everyone helps.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh in a huh uh zongin innkuan kikhopna khat in mikhual dawnte a gimsak thei hi.

records.english: Thank you all for making the journey from so far away.
records.zomi: Gamla mahmah pan hong pai na vekpi-un ka lungdam hi.

records.english: Who's in charge of the games for the children?
records.zomi: Naupangte' kimawlna kua in a makaih ding hiam?

records.english: My brother, because he's the only one with enough energy.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal, thahatna kicing a nei bek ahih manin.

records.english: When a family gathering goes badly, it can take months for everyone to forgive each other.
records.zomi: Innkuan kikhopna khat a hoih loh ciangin mi khempeuh a kimaisak nadingin kha tampi a la thei hi.

records.english: Mum counts heads every hour at family gatherings, just to make sure no child has wandered off.
records.zomi: Naupang khat zong a mang loh nadingin innkuan kikhopna ah Nu in nai simin mite a sim hi.

records.english: The teenagers usually disappear upstairs as soon as the meal is over.
records.zomi: An a bei pah ciangin tangval-tangnute inn tung khan ah a mang zel uh hi.

records.english: When the whole family stays at Grandma's, the children sleep on mattresses in the living room.
records.zomi: Innkuan bup Pi' inn ah a om uh ciangin naupangte tutna khan ah lupna puan tungah a ihmu uh hi.

records.english: Gatherings sometimes reveal how much the youngest children have grown since the last time.
records.zomi: Kikhopnate in a neu pen naupangte a ma-a hun pan bangzah a khang uh hiam a lak zel hi.

records.english: When there are three generations at the table, conversations range from school to retirement.
records.zomi: Dawhkan ah khangthak thum a om ciangin kihopihnate sang pan nasep tawp dong a tung hi.

records.english: We bought paper plates this year, so that nobody would spend the whole party washing up.
records.zomi: Kipahna bup kuamah in kuang sil-in a zat loh nadingin tu kum lai kuang i lei uh hi.

records.english: Auntie and my mother cooked together all morning, laughing like they did as girls.
records.zomi: Ni leh ka nu numei naupang a hih lai uh bangin nuih-in zingsang bup khawmin an a huan uh hi.

records.english: Family gatherings feel different now that our grandparents are gone, but we still meet every year.
records.zomi: I pu leh pi a om nawn loh uh pan innkuan kikhopnate tuam-in a kisa a, ahi zongin kum simin i kikhawm lai uh hi.

records.english: When relatives who rarely meet sit together, old misunderstandings can surface quickly.
records.zomi: Kimu tawm sanggamte khawmin a tut uh ciangin kituak lohna luite manlang takin a pusuak thei hi.

records.english: Where is everyone going to sleep this weekend?
records.zomi: Hih kal tawp mi khempeuh koi ah a ihmu ding uh hiam?

records.english: The adults in the bedrooms, and the cousins in tents in the garden.
records.zomi: Mi upate lupna khan ah, sanggamte huan sung-a puan inn ah.

records.english: Please greet your great-uncle properly; he's come all the way from the city.
records.zomi: Na pu' sanggam pasal hoih takin hopih in; khuapi pan a hong pai hi.

records.english: Has anyone started a group chat to plan next year's gathering?
records.zomi: Kum zom kikhopna gel dingin kuamah in group chat a kipatsak khin hiam?

records.english: A family gathering is the only time my parents see all their grandchildren together.
records.zomi: Innkuan kikhopna pen ka nu leh ka pa in a tute khempeuh khawmin a muh theih hun bek ahi hi.

records.english: Hosting the family gathering has become the job of a different household each year.
records.zomi: Innkuan kikhopna dawn kum simin innkuan tuam khat' nasep a hi ta hi.

records.english: Our family gatherings always start with a long, noisy lunch and end with everyone asleep on the sofa.
records.zomi: I innkuan kikhopnate sun an sau leh aw ngaih tawh a kipan a, mi khempeuh sofa tungah a ihmut tawh a bei tawntung hi.

records.english: At the end of the gathering, everyone wrote a message in the family guest book.
records.zomi: Kikhopna tawpna ah mi khempeuh in innkuan mikhual laibu ah thu khat a gelh uh hi.

records.english: My letter of introduction for my cousin helped him find a place at the training college.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam adingin ka kitheisakna lai in sinsakna college ah mun a ngah nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: My mother was introduced to the governor at the opening of the new hospital.
records.zomi: Ka nu damdawi inn thak kihonna ah governor kiangah kitheisak hi.

records.english: The ceremony began with the chairman introducing the families of the new graduates.
records.zomi: Pawi makaipa in sang zo thakte' innkuante a kitheisak tawh a kipan hi.

records.english: How should I introduce my partner at the embassy reception?
records.zomi: Embassy kimuakna ah ka zi hiam pasal bangci ka kitheisak ding hiam?

records.english: By full name and, if it's relevant, their profession.
records.zomi: A min kicing tawh, a kisam leh a nasep tawh.

records.english: It is customary to stand when you are being introduced to an elder at a formal gathering.
records.zomi: Kikhopna kizahtak khat ah upa khat kiangah na kitheisak ciangin ding pen ngeina ahi hi.

records.english: Ladies and gentlemen, it is my pleasure to introduce my colleague and friend, Dr. Lal.
records.zomi: Numeite leh pasalte, ka nasep lawm leh ka lawm Dr. Lal kong kitheisak ding hi.

records.english: At the funeral, the eldest son introduced the relatives who had travelled from far away.
records.zomi: Misi vuina ah ta pasal upa pen in gamla pan hong khualzin sanggamte a kitheisak hi.

records.english: Mr. Pau, this is my oldest friend; we went to school together.
records.zomi: Pu Pau, hih pen ka lawm lui pen ahi a, sang ah khawmin i kah uh hi.

records.english: The ambassador introduced her husband and children at the start of the national day reception.
records.zomi: Gam ni kimuakna kipatna ah ambassador in a pasal leh a tate a kitheisak hi.

records.english: When the president visited our school, the principal introduced each teacher by name.
records.zomi: President in i sang a veh ciangin sang makaipa in saya khatciat a min tawh a kitheisak hi.

records.english: I am writing to introduce a close friend of mine, who is moving to your city and hopes to find work as a nurse.
records.zomi: Na khuapi ah suan ding a, nurse nasep zong nuam ka lawm kinai khat kong kitheisak nadingin lai ka gelh hi.

records.english: Madam Chair, may I introduce our newest committee member, my colleague Ruth?
records.zomi: Makaipa Nu, i makaipawl mi thak pen, ka nasep lawm Ruth kong kitheisak thei ding hiam?

records.english: I would be grateful if you could introduce my nephew to someone in your department.
records.zomi: Ka tanau na office-a mi khat kiangah na kitheisak thei leh ka lungdam mahmah ding hi.

records.english: Ladies and gentlemen, my wife and I thank you for coming.
records.zomi: Numeite leh pasalte, ka zi leh kei hong pai manun ka lungdam uh hi.

records.english: Mr. Mayor, this is my daughter, who is studying law at the university.
records.zomi: Khuapi makaipa, hih pen ka tanu ahi a, sangpi ah thukham a sin hi.

records.english: Councillor, may I introduce my neighbour, who has been organising the street clean-up?
records.zomi: Councillor, lampi siangsakna a makaih ka innveng kong kitheisak thei ding hiam?

records.english: The head teacher introduced the visiting parents to the school governors.
records.zomi: Sang makaipa in hong veh nu leh pate sang makaipawl kiangah a kitheisak hi.

records.english: Professor, I believe you've already met my brother at the conference.
records.zomi: Professor, kikhopna lian ah ka sanggam pasal na mu khin hi, ka sa hi.

records.english: At the awards ceremony, each winner introduced their family to the audience.
records.zomi: Letsong piakna pawi ah a zo mi khatciat in a innkuan uh mipi kiangah a kitheisak uh hi.

records.english: Judge, this is my sister, who will be acting as my witness today.
records.zomi: Thukhenpa, hih pen ka u numei ahi a, tuni-in ka teci a pang ding hi.

records.english: During the ceremony, the new citizens were invited to introduce the family members who had come to support them.
records.zomi: Pawi sungin gam mi thakte amaute huh dingin hong pai innkuan mite kitheisak dingin kisam uh hi.

records.english: Officer, this is my uncle; he witnessed the accident.
records.zomi: Office nasempa, hih pen ka pa neu ahi a, accident a mu hi.

records.english: A careful introduction can open doors for a friend that they could never open alone.
records.zomi: Limtak-a kitheisakna khat in lawm khat adingin amah kia-in a hon zawh ngei loh kongkhakte a hon thei hi.

records.english: Would it be appropriate to introduce my children to the minister?
records.zomi: Ka tate minister kiangah ka kitheisak a kilawm ding hiam?

records.english: Thank you for introducing me to your family; it was an honour to meet them.
records.zomi: Na innkuan hong kitheisak manin ka lungdam hi; amaute kimuh zahtakna khat ahi hi.

records.english: Please allow me to introduce my cousin's husband, who is visiting from abroad.
records.zomi: Gamdang pan hong veh ka sanggam' pasal kong kitheisak dingin hong phal un.

records.english: In a formal introduction, mention the senior person's title first.
records.zomi: Kizahtak kitheisakna ah upa zaw mi' min tuam a masa-in gen in.

records.english: Formal introductions usually include the person's full name and their relationship to you.
records.zomi: Kizahtak kitheisaknate in a tamzaw-in mi' min kicing leh nang tawh a kizopna a huam hi.

records.english: Director, this is my colleague's son, who is doing work experience with us this week.
records.zomi: Director, hih pen ka nasep lawm' tapa ahi a, hih kal sungin eite tawh nasep a sin hi.

records.english: I have the honour of introducing my grandmother, the oldest member of our community.
records.zomi: I mipi-a upa pen ka pi kong kitheisak pen zahtakna khat ahi hi.

records.english: Doctor, this is my mother; she prefers to be addressed as Mrs. Ciin.
records.zomi: Siavuan, hih pen ka nu ahi a, Nu Ciin ci-in sam a deih zaw hi.

records.english: Sir, this is my friend Paul, who has kindly agreed to interpret for us today.
records.zomi: Pu, hih pen ka lawm Paul ahi a, tuni-in eite adingin pau let dingin hehpih takin a pom hi.

records.english: At official events, it is polite to introduce your companion to anyone you speak with.
records.zomi: Kumpi kikhopna ah na kihopih mi khempeuh kiangah na lawm kitheisak pen zahtakna ahi hi.

records.english: In formal settings, avoid nicknames when you introduce friends or relatives.
records.zomi: Kizahtak mun te ah lawmte hiam sanggamte na kitheisak ciangin min neu zang kei in.

records.english: Reverend, this is my mother, who has come to help us plan the service.
records.zomi: Rev., hih pen ka nu ahi a, kikhopna gel dingin hong huh dingin a hong pai hi.

records.english: The village chief introduced the visiting officials to every family in the square.
records.zomi: Khuamang in hong veh kumpi nasemte mun-a innkuan khempeuh kiangah a kitheisak hi.

records.english: Good evening, Ambassador; may I introduce my husband, Samuel?
records.zomi: Nitakpha, Ambassador; ka pasal Samuel kong kitheisak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Before the meeting starts, make sure every guest has been introduced to the chair.
records.zomi: Kikhopna a kipat ma-in mikhual khempeuh makaipa kiangah kitheisak khin hiam en in.

records.english: After the ceremony, I'd like you to meet everyone in my family.
records.zomi: Pawi khit ciangin ka innkuan khempeuh na kimuh ka deih hi.

records.english: May I present my brother, Thomas, who represents our village on the regional council?
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal, gamkhen makaipawl ah i khua aipuseh Thomas, kong kitheisak thei ding hiam?

records.english: May I present my colleague, who led the project that we are celebrating tonight?
records.zomi: Tu zanin i lawp nasep a makaih ka nasep lawm kong kitheisak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Could you introduce me to the director's wife, since I've never met her?
records.zomi: Director' zi ka mu ngei lo ahih manin amah kiangah hong kitheisak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Allow me to present the members of my delegation.
records.zomi: Ka palai pawl mite kong kitheisak dingin hong phal un.

records.english: When introducing a friend in a formal letter, explain how long you have known them and why you recommend them.
records.zomi: Kizahtak lai khat ah lawm khat na kitheisak ciangin bangzah sawt na thei hiam, bang hangin na gen hiam genteh in.

records.english: Minister, may I introduce my wife, Esther, who teaches at the primary school?
records.zomi: Minister, primary sang ah a hilh ka zi Esther kong kitheisak thei ding hiam?

records.english: The host introduced every guest at the dinner, so that nobody felt like a stranger.
records.zomi: Kuamah mikhual bangin a kisak loh nadingin mikhual dawnpa in nitak an ah mikhual khempeuh a kitheisak hi.

records.english: Who should be introduced first at a formal dinner?
records.zomi: Nitak an kizahtak khat ah kua kitheisak masa ding hiam?

records.english: Our protocol office prefers guests to be introduced in order of rank, starting with the most senior.
records.zomi: I ngeina office in mikhualte a dinmun uh zui-in, a upa pen pan kipan-in kitheisak a deih zaw hi.

records.english: Allow me to introduce my business partner, with whom I have worked for fifteen years.
records.zomi: Kum sawm leh nga nasep khawm ka sumbawlna lawm kong kitheisak dingin hong phal un.

records.english: When you introduce two people formally, add a detail that will help them start a conversation.
records.zomi: Mi nih kizahtak taka na kitheisak ciangin kihopihna a kipat theih nadingun huhna thu khat behlap in.

records.english: Can you introduce yourself and your family to the panel?
records.zomi: Makaipawl kiangah nangmah leh na innkuan na kitheisak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Your Excellency, allow me to present my parents, who have travelled from the village for this ceremony.
records.zomi: Excellency, hih pawi adingin khua pan hong khualzin ka nu leh ka pa kong kitheisak dingin hong phal in.

records.english: Doctor, may I introduce my husband, who will be helping to look after me at home?
records.zomi: Siavuan, inn ah hong kem dingin hong huh ding ka pasal kong kitheisak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Ladies and gentlemen, please welcome my daughter, who will present tonight's award.
records.zomi: Numeite leh pasalte, tu zan letsong a pia ding ka tanu muak un.

records.english: Inspector, let me introduce the parents' representative, Mrs. Mung.
records.zomi: Inspector, nu leh pate' aipuseh Nu Mung kong kitheisak ning.

records.english: I would like to introduce my son, who will be joining the company as an apprentice next month.
records.zomi: Kha zom ciangin nasep sin mi bangin company ah a lut ding ka tapa kong kitheisak nuam hi.

records.english: Professor, I'd like you to meet my cousin, who is thinking of applying to your department.
records.zomi: Professor, na khen ah ngen dingin a ngaihsun ka sanggam na kimuh ka deih hi.

records.english: I'm proud to introduce my father, who served as a nurse in this hospital for thirty years.
records.zomi: Hih damdawi inn ah kum sawmthum nurse bangin nasep a sem ka pa kipak takin kong kitheisak hi.

records.english: The bride's father introduced each member of his family to the guests of honour.
records.zomi: Moneu' pa in a innkuan mi khatciat zahtakna mikhualte kiangah a kitheisak hi.

records.english: Our pastor often reminds us that the Spirit never gives up on anyone.
records.zomi: I pastor in Kha Siangtho in kuamah a nusia ngei kei hi, ci-in hong phawksak zel hi.

records.english: Thank you for praying for me; I felt strengthened all week.
records.zomi: Kei adingin thu hong ngen manin ka lungdam hi; kal bup hatna ka kisa hi.

records.english: Can people from very different backgrounds really become one church?
records.zomi: Mi tuamtuam pan hong pai mite pawlpi khat taktak a suak thei uh hiam?

records.english: Is it possible to feel joy even in hard times?
records.zomi: Hun haksa ah zong lungdamna kisa thei hiam?

records.english: The work of the Spirit is described in the Bible as making people more like Christ.
records.zomi: Kha Siangtho' nasep pen mite Khazih tawh a kibang zawk nadingin bawl ahi hi, ci-in Laisiangtho in a gen hi.

records.english: Many people say that they understood the Spirit's work in their lives only when they looked back.
records.zomi: Mi tampi in a nuntakna uh-a Kha Siangtho' nasep nung lam a en kik uh ciang bek-in a thei uh hi, a ci uh hi.

records.english: Missionaries often speak of the Spirit leading them to unexpected places.
records.zomi: Tangthu genna mite in Kha Siangtho in lamen loh munte ah a makaih uh hi, ci-in a gen zel uh hi.

records.english: Because the Spirit gives different gifts to different people, church members need one another, many teachers say.
records.zomi: Kha Siangtho in mi tuamtuam hehpihna tuamtuam a piak ahih manin pawlpi mite khat leh khat a kisam uh hi, ci-in hilhpa tampi in a gen uh hi.

records.english: Believers often pray, "Come, Holy Spirit," at the beginning of worship.
records.zomi: Upmite in biakna kipatna ah, “Kha Siangtho aw, hong pai in,” ci-in thu a ngen zel uh hi.

records.english: Some Christians feel the Spirit's work most clearly in times of worship and singing.
records.zomi: Khristian pawl khat in biakna leh la sak hun ah Kha Siangtho' nasep a thei kician pen uh hi.

records.english: Has your faith ever given you the courage to speak when you were afraid?
records.zomi: Na lau laitakin na upna in thu gen dingin hangsanna hong pia ngei hiam?

records.english: In Acts, the early believers are sent by the Spirit to new places.
records.zomi: Sawltakte Thu ah upmi masate Kha Siangtho in mun thakte ah a sawl hi.

records.english: Our church celebrates the work of the Spirit at Pentecost with a special service.
records.zomi: I pawlpi in Pentecost ciangin kikhopna tuam khat tawh Kha Siangtho' nasep a lawp hi.

records.english: Using our gifts to serve others is one way, Christians believe, of following the Spirit.
records.zomi: Mi dangte nasem sak dingin i hehpihna zat pen Kha Siangtho zuih dan khat ahi hi, ci-in Khristiante in a um uh hi.

records.english: Can a person have more than one gift of the Spirit?
records.zomi: Mi khat in Kha Siangtho' hehpihna khat sang tam a nei thei hiam?

records.english: How does the Holy Spirit help Christians in daily life?
records.zomi: Kha Siangtho in Khristiante ni simin nuntakna ah bangci a huh hiam?

records.english: Many say the Spirit gives them strength, patience and a sense of God's presence.
records.zomi: Tampi in Kha Siangtho in thahatna, thuakzawhna leh Pasian' omna kisakna a pia hi, a ci uh hi.

records.english: Our Bible study is reading Paul's letter about the gifts of the Spirit this month.
records.zomi: I Laisiangtho sinna in hih kha sungin Kha Siangtho' hehpihna tungtang Paul' lai a sim hi.

records.english: My grandmother believes that the Spirit gave her peace when my grandfather died.
records.zomi: Ka pi in ka pu a sih ciangin Kha Siangtho in kilemna hong pia hi, ci-in a um hi.

records.english: A member of our church says the Spirit gave her the patience to care for her sick mother.
records.zomi: I pawlpi mi khat in a nu natpa a kem nadingin Kha Siangtho in thuakzawhna hong pia hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Growing in love is the work of a whole lifetime, according to many Christian teachers.
records.zomi: Khristian hilhpa tampi' gen bangin itna ah khang pen nuntak sung bup' nasep ahi hi.

records.english: Christians speak of the Spirit as the one who makes them new from the inside.
records.zomi: Khristiante in Kha Siangtho pen sung lam pan amaute a thaksak pa bangin a gen uh hi.

records.english: Christians often pray for the Spirit's help before they read the Bible.
records.zomi: Khristiante in Laisiangtho a sim ma-un Kha Siangtho' huhna a ngen zel uh hi.

records.english: Our youth leader said, "The Spirit gives each of you something that the church needs."
records.zomi: I khangno makaipa in, “Kha Siangtho in pawlpi' kisam khat peuhpeuh note khatciat hong pia hi,” a ci hi.

records.english: Many Christians believe that the Spirit convicts people of sin so that they turn back to God.
records.zomi: Khristian tampi in mite Pasian lam a kihei kik nadingun Kha Siangtho in mawhna a pulak hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: Shall we pray together for the Spirit's help before the meeting?
records.zomi: Kikhopna ma-in Kha Siangtho' huhna adingin khawmin thu i ngen ding hiam?

records.english: Do you think the Holy Spirit still works miracles today?
records.zomi: Kha Siangtho in tu-in lamdang nasepte a sem lai hi, na ci hiam?

records.english: Christian views on that question differ, so our church encourages people to read and pray about it.
records.zomi: Tua dotna tungtang Khristian ngaihsutnate a kibang kei ahih manin i pawlpi in mite sim-in thu ngen dingin a hanthawn hi.

records.english: Our choir prays for the Spirit to bless every song they sing.
records.zomi: I la sa pawl in a sak la khempeuh Kha Siangtho in thupha a piak nadingin thu a ngen uh hi.

records.english: The Spirit is believed to help Christians speak the truth with love.
records.zomi: Kha Siangtho in Khristiante itna tawh thudik a gen nadingin a huh hi, ci-in kium hi.

records.english: Our pastor says that the Spirit helps people see their mistakes and want to change.
records.zomi: I pastor in Kha Siangtho in mite a khialhnate a muh nadingin leh a kheel nop nadingin a huh hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Some churches believe that the Spirit still gives special gifts, such as speaking in tongues, while others are more cautious.
records.zomi: Pawlpi pawl khat in Kha Siangtho in pau tuam gen bang hehpihna tuamte a pia lai hi, ci-in a um uh a, a dangte a kidawm zaw uh hi.

records.english: The Spirit is described as giving life, both at creation and in the lives of believers.
records.zomi: Kha Siangtho pen piansakna hun ah leh upmite' nuntakna ah nuntakna piakpa bangin kigen hi.

records.english: Please don't argue about the gifts of the Spirit in a way that divides the church.
records.zomi: Pawlpi a khen dan-in Kha Siangtho' hehpihna tungtang kinial kei un.

records.english: When our church was divided, many prayed that the Spirit would bring us together again.
records.zomi: I pawlpi a kikhen ciangin mi tampi in Kha Siangtho in eite hong kipumkhatsak kik nadingin thu a ngen uh hi.

records.english: Believers often say that the Spirit gives them strength in situations they could never face alone.
records.zomi: Upmite in amau kia-in a maitang ngat zawh ngei loh dinmunte ah Kha Siangtho in hatna a pia hi, a ci zel uh hi.

records.english: My father says that the Spirit helped him stop drinking after many years.
records.zomi: Ka pa in kum tampi khit ciangin zu dawn khawl nadingin Kha Siangtho in a huh hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Loving difficult people is easier, believers say, with the Spirit's help.
records.zomi: Mi haksa it pen Kha Siangtho' huhna tawh a baih zaw hi, ci-in upmite in a gen uh hi.

records.english: May the Spirit guide you in all that you do.
records.zomi: Kha Siangtho in na bawl khempeuh ah hong makaih ta hen.

records.english: The Spirit's work is often seen in small acts of kindness rather than in great events.
records.zomi: Kha Siangtho' nasep thupiang lianpi sangin hehpihna neunote ah kimu zel hi.

records.english: Who in our church has the gift of teaching children?
records.zomi: I pawlpi ah kua in naupangte hilh nading hehpihna a nei hiam?

records.english: According to Paul's letters, the gifts of the Spirit are given for the good of the whole church, not for personal pride.
records.zomi: Paul' laite bangin Kha Siangtho' hehpihnate amah le amah kiliansak nadingin hi lo-in pawlpi bup' hoihna adingin kipia hi.

records.english: Forgiving those who have hurt them is something many believers say the Spirit makes possible.
records.zomi: Amaute a liamsak mite maisak pen Kha Siangtho in a theisak hi, ci-in upmi tampi in a gen uh hi.

records.english: Christians believe the Spirit is at work even when they cannot feel it.
records.zomi: Khristiante in a theih zawh kei uh ciangin zong Kha Siangtho nasep a sem hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: The children learned that the Spirit helps them be kind even when it's hard.
records.zomi: Naupangte in a haksa ciangin zong Kha Siangtho in hehpih dingin a huh hi, ci a sin uh hi.

records.english: Christians in different traditions emphasise different aspects of the Spirit's work.
records.zomi: Ngeina tuamtuam-a Khristiante in Kha Siangtho' nasep kenkhat tuamtuam a thupi sak uh hi.

records.english: Some people discover their gifts by trying different kinds of service in the church.
records.zomi: Mi pawl khat in pawlpi-a nasep tuamtuam sin-in a hehpihna uh a mu uh hi.

records.english: The work of the Spirit, many believers say, is to point people towards Jesus.
records.zomi: Upmi tampi' gen bangin Kha Siangtho' nasep pen mite Jesu lam a liapsak ahi hi.

records.english: Paul compares the church to a body, in which each part has its own gift and purpose.
records.zomi: Paul in pawlpi pumpi khat tawh a teh a, a kenkhat khatciat in amau' hehpihna leh tupna a nei hi.

records.english: Do you believe the Spirit guides people through their conscience?
records.zomi: Kha Siangtho in mite a lungsim tungtawnin a makaih hi, na um hiam?

records.english: Does your church pray for guidance before choosing new leaders?
records.zomi: Na pawlpi in makai thakte a teel ma-in makaihna adingin thu a ngen hiam?

records.english: My aunt says that her gift is hospitality, and nobody who has eaten at her table would disagree.
records.zomi: Ka ni in a hehpihna pen zindo ahi hi, a ci a, a dawhkan ah an a ne ngei mi kuamah in a nial kei uh hi.

records.english: Many Christians believe that the Holy Spirit gives each believer gifts to serve others.
records.zomi: Khristian tampi in Kha Siangtho in upmi khatciat mi dangte nasem sak nadingin hehpihna a pia hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: What gift do you think the Spirit has given you?
records.zomi: Kha Siangtho in bang hehpihna hong pia ding na ci hiam?

records.english: Our pastor encourages us to use our gifts in the community, not only inside the church building.
records.zomi: I pastor in i hehpihnate pawlpi inn sung bek hi lo-in mipi lak ah zong zang dingin hong hanthawn hi.

records.english: Shall I lead the prayer for the Holy Spirit at the start of the service?
records.zomi: Kikhopna kipatna ah Kha Siangtho adingin thungetna ka makaih ding hiam?

records.english: Many believers describe the Spirit's work as slow and quiet rather than dramatic.
records.zomi: Upmi tampi in Kha Siangtho' nasep lamdang sangin nuam leh dai bangin a gen uh hi.

records.english: What are the gifts of the Spirit?
records.zomi: Kha Siangtho' hehpihnate bang hiam?

records.english: Paul lists several, such as teaching, healing, wisdom and encouragement.
records.zomi: Paul in hilhna, damsakna, pilna leh hanthawnna bang tampi a gen hi.

records.english: Let's ask the Spirit to give us wisdom as we make this decision.
records.zomi: Hih thukhenna i bawl laitakin Kha Siangtho in pilna hong piak nadingin i ngen ni.

records.english: Are free school meals paid for by the government?
records.zomi: Sang an man om lote kumpi in a man a pia hiam?

records.english: Good government spending is planned for the long term, not just for the next election.
records.zomi: Kumpi sum zat hoih in teelna zom bek adingin hi lo-in hun sawt adingin kigel hi.

records.english: Our town finally got a new bridge after years of waiting for government funding.
records.zomi: Kumpi sum kum tampi i ngak khit ciangin i khuapi in lei thak khat a ngah hi.

records.english: Some citizens join groups that track how government money is spent in their area.
records.zomi: Gam mi pawl khat in a mun-a kumpi sum bangci kizang hiam a en pawlte ah a kihel uh hi.

records.english: Shall we look at the government's website to see where the money goes?
records.zomi: Sum koi ah a pai hiam en dingin kumpi' website i en ding hiam?

records.english: When a project costs far more than planned, the public often demands an explanation.
records.zomi: Nasep khat in a kigel sangin a man tam mahmah ciangin mipi in genteh a ngen zel uh hi.

records.english: Why does the government borrow money when it already collects taxes?
records.zomi: Bang hangin siah a kaikhawm khin hangin kumpi in sum a ba hiam?

records.english: Because spending is often higher than tax income, especially during a crisis.
records.zomi: A diak in haksatna hun ah sum zat siah ngah sangin a tam zaw zel ahih manin.

records.english: The government promised to spend more on rural roads, and our road was repaired last year.
records.zomi: Kumpi in khua lam lampite tungah tam zaw zang dingin a kiciam a, kum nunung in i lampi kibawlphat hi.

records.english: Building a new road can create jobs as well as improve travel.
records.zomi: Lampi thak lam in khualzinna a hoihsak bek hi lo-in nasep zong a piangsak thei hi.

records.english: Does the government pay for children's vaccinations here?
records.zomi: Hih ah naupangte' natna hihna damdawi sutna kumpi in a man a pia hiam?

records.english: Thank you for explaining the budget so simply; now I understand where our taxes go.
records.zomi: Sum zat ding baih takin na genteh manin ka lungdam hi; tu-in i siah koi ah a pai hiam ka thei hi.

records.english: Government spending pays for hospitals, schools, roads, pensions and many other public services.
records.zomi: Kumpi sum zat in damdawi inn, sang, lampi, pension leh mipi nasep dang tampi a man a pia hi.

records.english: Is the clinic funded by the national government or by the region?
records.zomi: Clinic pen gam kumpi in hiam gamkhen in hiam a sum a pia hiam?

records.english: Every road, school and clinic in our town was paid for, at least in part, by public money.
records.zomi: I khuapi-a lampi, sang leh clinic khempeuh a tawm pen a kenkhat mipi sum tawh kibawl hi.

records.english: Public money spent on clean water has transformed life in many villages.
records.zomi: Tui siangtho tungah kizang mipi sum in khua tampi' nuntakna a kheel vekpi hi.

records.english: Transparent spending makes it harder for public money to be stolen or wasted.
records.zomi: Kilang taka sum zat in mipi sum kiguk hiam kizang mawk a haksa zawsak hi.

records.english: Money is set aside every year for emergencies such as storms and earthquakes.
records.zomi: Huihpi leh leiling bang haksatna hun adingin kum simin sum kikoih hi.

records.english: A new school was opened in our village thanks to a government programme for rural areas.
records.zomi: Khua lam gamte adingin kumpi nasep khat hangin i khua ah sang thak khat kihong hi.

records.english: Many people don't realise how much government money goes into keeping the streets lit and clean.
records.zomi: Mi tampi in lampite meivaak leh siangtho a om nadingin kumpi sum bangzah kizang hiam a thei kei uh hi.

records.english: How is the money for pensions raised?
records.zomi: Pension adingin sum bangci kikaikhawm hiam?

records.english: A new clinic was built, but there was no money left to pay the nurses.
records.zomi: Clinic thak khat kilam a, ahi zongin nurse te khasum piak nading sum om nawn lo hi.

records.english: Should the government spend more on young people or on the elderly?
records.zomi: Kumpi in khangnote tungah hiam mi upate tungah hiam tam zaw a zang ding hiam?

records.english: Spending on parks and libraries improves the quality of life in a community.
records.zomi: Huan leh laibu inn tungah sum zat in mipi khat' nuntakna hoihna a khangsak hi.

records.english: My father reads the newspaper every year to see how the new budget will affect our family.
records.zomi: Ka pa in kum simin sum zat ding thak in i innkuan bangci a lawh ding hiam en dingin thuthak lai a sim hi.

records.english: Spending on public health can save money later by preventing illness.
records.zomi: Mipi damna tungah sum zat in natna dal-in a nung ciangin sum a khol thei hi.

records.english: When the economy slows down, governments sometimes spend more to create jobs.
records.zomi: Sumbawlna a nuam ciangin kumpite in nasep piangsak dingin sum tam zaw a zang zel uh hi.

records.english: Why is spending on defence such a sensitive topic in many countries?
records.zomi: Bang hangin gam tampi ah galkap sum zat thu a buaihuai hiam?

records.english: Pensions are one of the largest areas of government spending in many countries.
records.zomi: Gam tampi ah pension te kumpi sum zat lian pen khat ahi hi.

records.english: Wasting public money is a common complaint against governments everywhere.
records.zomi: Mipi sum zat mawk pen koi ah zong kumpite tungah phunna kineih tam khat ahi hi.

records.english: Many citizens want to know exactly how their taxes are being spent.
records.zomi: Gam mi tampi in a siah uh bangci kizang hiam a theih kician nuam uh hi.

records.english: Too little spending on maintenance can make roads and bridges dangerous.
records.zomi: Kemna tungah sum zat tawm lua in lampi leh leite a lauhuai sak thei hi.

records.english: Spending wisely is harder than spending a lot.
records.zomi: Pil taka zat pen tampi zat sangin a haksa zaw hi.

records.english: Every year, the finance minister presents the government's spending plans to parliament.
records.zomi: Kum simin sum minister in parliament kiangah kumpi' sum zat gelnate a lak hi.

records.english: The new hospital in our region was built with government money.
records.zomi: I gamkhen-a damdawi inn thak kumpi sum tawh kilam hi.

records.english: Have you ever asked your representative how public money is being spent?
records.zomi: Mipi sum bangci kizang hiam na aipuseh na dong ngei hiam?

records.english: Students, please find one example of government spending in your town for tomorrow's lesson.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte, zingciang sinna adingin na khuapi-a kumpi sum zat entehna khat zong un.

records.english: Government grants helped my cousin start a small business.
records.zomi: Kumpi huhna sum in ka sanggam sumbawlna neu khat a kipatsak nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Government spending on research can lead to discoveries that benefit everyone.
records.zomi: Sinna-a kumpi sum zat in mi khempeuh a phatuam theih thak muhnate a tun thei hi.

records.english: My grandmother's pension is paid by the government every month.
records.zomi: Ka pi' pension kha simin kumpi in a pia hi.

records.english: Government money helped farmers in our district buy new equipment after the drought.
records.zomi: Khuakeu sawtna khit ciangin kumpi sum in i gamkhen-a lo neite vanzat thak a lei nadingun a huh hi.

records.english: Can you find out how much the government spends on public transport?
records.zomi: Kumpi in mipi khualzinna tungah bangzah a zang hiam na zong thei ding hiam?

records.english: The government had independent experts review the cost of the new railway.
records.zomi: Kumpi in meileng lampi thak man amah kia-a siamte a en sak hi.

records.english: The more people understand government spending, the better they can judge their leaders.
records.zomi: Mite in kumpi sum zat a theih tam semsem leh a makaite uh hoih zaw-in a thukhen thei uh hi.

records.english: When the factory closed, the government paid for training courses for the workers.
records.zomi: Factory a kikhak ciangin kumpi in nasemte adingin sinna man a pia hi.

records.english: Some government money is given as aid to other countries during emergencies.
records.zomi: Kumpi sum pawl khat haksatna hun ah gam dangte kiangah huhna bangin kipia hi.

records.english: Who decides how the national budget is spent?
records.zomi: Gam sum zat ding bangci kizang ding hiam kua in a khensat hiam?

records.english: The government proposes a budget, and in many countries parliament must approve it.
records.zomi: Kumpi in sum zat ding khat a gen a, gam tampi ah parliament in a pom kul hi.

records.english: When the government spends more on one service, it often has to spend less on another.
records.zomi: Kumpi in nasep khat tungah tam zaw a zat ciangin a dang khat tungah tawm zaw a zang kul zel hi.

records.english: Spending that is announced with great fanfare is not always spent as quickly as promised.
records.zomi: Aw ngaih taka kitangko sum zatte kiciam bangin manlang takin a kizang tawntung kei hi.

records.english: Did you know that the government pays part of the cost of every university place?
records.zomi: Kumpi in sangpi mun khempeuh' man a kenkhat a pia hi, na thei hiam?

records.english: Independent auditors check whether government money has been spent properly.
records.zomi: Amau kia-a sum ciamtehna enpate in kumpi sum hoih takin kizang hiam a en uh hi.

records.english: Is it fair to borrow money now that future generations will have to repay?
records.zomi: Hun zom khangthakte in a pia kik kul ding sum tu-in leitawi a dik hiam?

records.english: After reports that many classrooms were overcrowded, spending on schools was increased.
records.zomi: Sangkhan tampi a dim lua hi, ci thu khit ciangin sang tungah sum zat kibehlap hi.

records.english: Spending cuts often affect the poorest families first.
records.zomi: Sum zat kiamsakna in innkuan zawng pente a masa-in a lawh zel hi.

records.english: Government spending is, in the end, the citizens' own money.
records.zomi: Kumpi sum zat pen a tawpna-ah gam mite' amau' sum ahi hi.

records.english: Do you think the government spends enough on healthcare?
records.zomi: Kumpi in damna tungah a kicing-in a zang hi, na ci hiam?

records.english: Spending on education is often seen as an investment in the country's future.
records.zomi: Sinna tungah sum zat gam' hun zom adingin sum koihna bangin kimu zel hi.

records.english: How much a government should spend, and on what, is one of the main questions in every election.
records.zomi: Kumpi khat in bangzah, bang tungah a zang ding hiam pen teelna khempeuh-a dotna lian pen khat ahi hi.

records.english: Some people believe the government spends too much, while others think it spends too little on the poor.
records.zomi: Mi pawl khat in kumpi in a zang tam lua hi, a ci uh a, a dangte in mi zawngte tungah a zang tawm lua hi, a ci uh hi.

records.english: Children learn about melting and freezing every time they make ice lollies.
records.zomi: Naupangte in tuikhal lolly a bawl vei khempeuh-in tui kizai leh khal tungtang a sin uh hi.

records.english: A timer on the porch light turns it off at midnight.
records.zomi: Inn mai-a meivaak tungah hun tehna khat in zan lai ciangin a phel hi.

records.english: Our youngest asked why a battery goes flat, so we looked it up together.
records.zomi: I neu pen in bang hangin battery a bei hiam a dong a, khawmin i zong uh hi.

records.english: Heating only the rooms we use has made a big difference to our winter bills.
records.zomi: I zat khan bek lumsak in i phalbi man tungah kibatlohna lianpi a bawl hi.

records.english: Small changes in how a family uses energy can add up to a big difference over a year.
records.zomi: Innkuan khat in meivaak a zat dan-a kikheelna neunote in kum khat sungin kibatlohna lianpi a tun thei hi.

records.english: Please don't touch the iron; it stays hot for a long time after you switch it off.
records.zomi: Meisek khoih kei in; na phel khit zongin hun sawtpi a lum den hi.

records.english: A tight-fitting door keeps the warm air in and the cold air out.
records.zomi: Kician taka kikhak kongkhak khat in huih lum a kem a, huih vot a dal hi.

records.english: My father explained that the bicycle lamp gets its power from the turning wheel.
records.zomi: Ka pa in siiksakol meivaak in a kikual ke pan thahatna a ngah hi, ci-in a genteh hi.

records.english: A family that understands where its energy comes from usually wastes less of it.
records.zomi: A meivaak koi pan hong pai hiam a thei innkuan khat in a tamzaw-in tawm zaw a zang mawk hi.

records.english: Shall we walk to school today and save the bus fare?
records.zomi: Tuni-in sang ah i kal-in bus man i khol ding hiam?

records.english: Wrapping the hot water tank in a thick jacket keeps the water warm for longer.
records.zomi: Tui lum tank puan khauh khat tawh tuam in tui hun sawt zaw a lum den hi.

records.english: My daughter's science homework was to find five ways our family wastes energy.
records.zomi: Ka tanu' science inn sinna pen i innkuan in meivaak a zat mawk dan nga zong ahi hi.

records.english: When my son put a balloon in the freezer, he was surprised that it shrank.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in balloon khat freezer sungah a koih ciangin a neu sak hiam lamdang a sa hi.

records.english: Solar lamps in our garden store energy during the day and light up at night.
records.zomi: I huan sung-a ni meivaakte in sunlai-in thahatna a kem a, zan ciangin a taang hi.

records.english: Using energy wisely at home is one of the simplest ways a family can help the environment.
records.zomi: Inn ah meivaak pil taka zat pen innkuan khat in leitung a huh theih dan baih pen khat ahi hi.

records.english: Do you two want to try an experiment with salt and ice?
records.zomi: Na nih in cii leh tuikhal tawh sitna khat na sin nuam uh hiam?

records.english: When the power goes off, we use a torch with batteries we keep in the kitchen drawer.
records.zomi: Meivaak a mit ciangin an huanna inn bawm sungah i kem battery tawh meivak i zang uh hi.

records.english: The bread rises because yeast produces gas inside the dough.
records.zomi: Yeast in mim sungah huih a piangsak ahih manin moh a khang hi.

records.english: Who left the television on all night?
records.zomi: Television zan bup kua in a hon nusia hiam?

records.english: The family car uses fuel, while our neighbour's electric car is charged at night.
records.zomi: Innkuan mawtaw in dat a zang a, i innveng' meivaak mawtaw zan ciangin kicharge hi.

records.english: When the electricity was cut for a whole day, we realised how much we depend on it.
records.zomi: Ni bup meivaak a kiphel ciangin bangzah i kinga hiam i thei uh hi.

records.english: Energy from food is what keeps our bodies warm and moving all day.
records.zomi: An pan thahatna in i pumpi ni bup a lum leh a kilawh sak hi.

records.english: Our son was amazed to see water turn into steam when the kettle boiled.
records.zomi: Kettle a so ciangin tui meikhu ah a kikheel a muh ciangin ka tapa lamdang a sa mahmah hi.

records.english: Teaching children to save energy at home builds habits that last a lifetime.
records.zomi: Naupangte inn ah meivaak khol dingin sinsak in nuntak sung bup a om ngeinate a bawl hi.

records.english: Do you leave your computer on standby or switch it off completely?
records.zomi: Na computer standby ah na nusia hiam, a kicing-in na phel hiam?

records.english: Cooking with a lid on the pot uses less energy, because less heat escapes.
records.zomi: Beel tungah khuhna tawh an huan in a lumna tawm zaw a pusuak ahih manin meivaak tawm zaw a zang hi.

records.english: We made a simple solar oven from a cardboard box and some foil, and it melted chocolate.
records.zomi: Lai bawm leh foil tawh ni oven baih khat i bawl uh a, chocolate a zaisak hi.

records.english: Can you unplug the phone charger when you're not using it?
records.zomi: Na zat loh ciangin phone charger na suah thei ding hiam?

records.english: The kettle switches itself off when the water boils.
records.zomi: Tui a so ciangin kettle amah mah in a kiphel hi.

records.english: Why does the window steam up when we cook?
records.zomi: Bang hangin an i huan ciangin tukkhuak a dum hiam?

records.english: Warm, wet air from the pan meets the cold glass and turns back into tiny drops of water.
records.zomi: Beel pan huih lum leh diak in glass vot a tuah a, tui tang neunote ah a kikheel kik hi.

records.english: My little brother thought the sun went out at night.
records.zomi: Ka nau pasal in zan ciangin ni a mit hi, a sa hi.

records.english: We hang the washing outside, where the sun and wind dry it for free.
records.zomi: Ni leh huih in man om lo-in a keusak theih nadingin puan sawpte pua lam ah i vui uh hi.

records.english: Switch off the heater before you go to bed.
records.zomi: Na lup ma-in heater phel in.

records.english: Thank you for helping the children with their energy project; they learned a lot.
records.zomi: Naupangte' meivaak nasep ah na huh manin ka lungdam hi; tampi a sin uh hi.

records.english: Why does the ice in my drink melt so quickly?
records.zomi: Bang hangin ka dawn sung-a tuikhal manlang mahmah-in a zai hiam?

records.english: Because the warm air and the drink pass their heat to the ice.
records.zomi: Huih lum leh dawn ding in a lumna tuikhal kiangah a pia uh ahih manin.

records.english: My grandmother keeps her drinking water cool in a clay pot, which works without electricity.
records.zomi: Ka pi in meivaak om lo-in a sem leibel khat sungah a dawn tui a vot sak den hi.

records.english: My daughter keeps a chart of how much water and electricity our family uses each week.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in kal simin i innkuan in tui leh meivaak bangzah a zang hiam chart khat a kem hi.

records.english: Shall we check the meter to see how much electricity we used this month?
records.zomi: Hih kha sungin meivaak bangzah i zang hiam en dingin meter i en ding hiam?

records.english: My mother never wastes the heat left in the oven after baking; she uses it to warm the plates and dry the herbs.
records.zomi: Ka nu in moh hal khit-a oven sung-a lumna om lai a zang mawk ngei lo a; kuangte lumsak leh an hel keusak nadingin a zang hi.

records.english: Why does bread go hard when it's left out?
records.zomi: Bang hangin moh pua lam ah kinusia ciangin a khauh hiam?

records.english: When we lived in the village, we cooked on wood, and my job was to collect it every morning.
records.zomi: Khua ah i teen lai-in sing tawh an i huan uh a, zingsang simin a kaikhop pen ka nasep ahi hi.

records.english: Please close the fridge door, or all the cold air will escape.
records.zomi: Fridge kongkhak khak in, a kei leh huih vot khempeuh a pusuak ding hi.

records.english: Can we make our own wind turbine for the science fair?
records.zomi: Science kipahna adingin i mah-in huih seet i bawl thei ding hiam?

records.english: Last winter, our electricity bill was so high that we decided to make some changes.
records.zomi: Phalbi nunung in i meivaak man a sang lua ahih manin kikheelna pawl khat bawl dingin i khensat uh hi.

records.english: We put thick curtains on the windows and stopped leaving the heater on all night.
records.zomi: Tukkhuakte ah puan khauh i bulh uh a, zan bup heater hon i khawl uh hi.

records.english: By spring, the bill had fallen by almost a third, and the house felt just as warm.
records.zomi: Spring ciangin man a thum-a khat dek a kiam a, inn a lum kibang mah hi.

records.english: Ice on the windscreen melted quickly once the sun rose.
records.zomi: Ni a suah ciangin mawtaw mai-a glass tung-a tuikhal manlang takin a zai hi.

records.english: Are energy-saving bulbs really worth the extra money?
records.zomi: Meivaak khol bulb te man behlap adingin a phu taktak hiam?

records.english: Grandpa taught us that a fire needs air, fuel and heat to keep burning.
records.zomi: Pu in mei khat a kang den nadingin huih, sing leh lumna a kisam hi, ci hong sinsak hi.

records.english: Always switch off the power before anyone touches the wiring, my father says.
records.zomi: Kuamah in meivaak khau a khoih ma-in meivaak phel masa in, ka pa in a ci hi.

records.english: The rice cooker turns itself to warm when the rice is ready.
records.zomi: An a min ciangin buh huanna seet amah mah in lumsakna ah a kikheel hi.

records.english: We bought a pressure cooker, which cooks beans in a fraction of the time and saves gas.
records.zomi: Pressure cooker khat i lei uh a, be te hun tawmno sungin a min sak a, gas a khol hi.

records.english: Children love watching snow turn to water in their warm hands.
records.zomi: Naupangte in a khut lum sungah vuk tui ah a kikheel en a nuam sa mahmah uh hi.

records.english: When we finally measured it, the old fridge turned out to be using far more electricity than the new one we had been afraid to buy.
records.zomi: A tawpna-ah i teh ciangin fridge lui in i lei dingin i lau a thak sangin meivaak tam zaw mahmah a zang hi, ci a kilang hi.

records.english: Why does the pan get hot while its handle stays cool?
records.zomi: Bang hangin beel a lum a, a kaihna a vot den hiam?

records.english: The handle is made of plastic, which doesn't carry heat well.
records.zomi: Kaihna plastic tawh kibawl a, plastic in lumna hoih takin a pua kei hi.

records.english: Old newspapers make good fuel for starting a fire, but they burn very quickly.
records.zomi: Thuthak lai luite mei kipatsak nadingin hoih a, ahi zongin manlang mahmah-in a kang hi.

records.english: Why does butter go hard in the fridge?
records.zomi: Bang hangin butter fridge sungah a khauh hiam?

records.english: When my parents say we'll see, they usually mean they haven't decided yet.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in i en ding hi, a cih uh ciangin a khensat nai kei uh hi, a ci nopna uh a hi zel hi.

records.english: Whenever Auntie says she'll think about it, she usually means no.
records.zomi: Ni in ka ngaihsun ding hi, a cih ciangin a tamzaw-in nial a ci nopna ahi hi.

records.english: Saying clearly what you mean is a kindness to the people who love you.
records.zomi: Na ci nopna kician taka gen pen nang hong it mite tungah hehpihna khat ahi hi.

records.english: Our grandparents' idea of a short phone call and ours are very different.
records.zomi: I pu leh pi' phone sapna tom ngaihsutna leh eite' ngaihsutna a kibang mahmah kei hi.

records.english: My cousin's 'small wedding' had three hundred guests.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam' 'mopawi neu' in mikhual za thum a nei hi.

records.english: My husband says 'later' when he means 'never', and we both know it.
records.zomi: Ka pasal in 'a nung ciangin' a cih ciangin 'ngei kei ding' a ci nopna ahi a, i nih in i thei hi.

records.english: Do you mean the blue bag or the black one?
records.zomi: Ip dum na ci nopna hiam, a nak hiam?

records.english: The blue one by the door.
records.zomi: Kongkhak kiang-a a dum.

records.english: Saying what you really meant after an argument can repair a lot of damage.
records.zomi: Kinialna khit ciangin na ci nopna taktak gen in siatna tampi a bawlphat thei hi.

records.english: When you say the children are welcome, do you mean the baby too?
records.zomi: Naupangte kimuak hi, na cih ciangin naungek zong na ci nopna hiam?

records.english: Yes, the baby is very welcome too.
records.zomi: Hi hi, naungek zong kimuak mahmah hi.

records.english: Please tell me exactly what you need, so that I can help properly instead of guessing.
records.zomi: Ngaihsut sangin hoih takin ka huh theih nadingin bang na kisam hiam kician takin hong gen in.

records.english: Did you mean this weekend or next weekend?
records.zomi: Hih kal tawp na ci nopna hiam, kal tawp zom hiam?

records.english: I didn't understand what my uncle meant by his remark at dinner, so I quietly asked my sister to explain it afterwards.
records.zomi: Nitak an ah ka pa neu' gen bang a ci nopna hiam ka thei kei ahih manin a nung ciangin ka u numei kiangah dai takin genteh dingin ka ngen hi.

records.english: What did your teacher mean by 'more effort'?
records.zomi: Na saya in 'hanciamna tam zaw' bang a ci nopna hiam?

records.english: She wants me to check my work before I hand it in.
records.zomi: Ka pia ma-in ka nasep ka en dingin a deih hi.

records.english: Grandma uses old expressions that my children need me to translate.
records.zomi: Pi in ka tate in let dingin hong ngetsak kammal luite a zang hi.

records.english: Is 'cheap' good or bad in this review?
records.zomi: Hih gen dan sungah 'man neem' a hoih hiam, a hoih lo hiam?

records.english: Good, because it means the meals cost less than elsewhere.
records.zomi: A hoih, ante mun dang sangin a man neem zaw cihna ahih manin.

records.english: If I've understood correctly, you'd like the whole family to share the cost?
records.zomi: Ka theih a dik leh innkuan bup in man kihawm na deih hiam?

records.english: What do you mean by a quiet weekend, exactly?
records.zomi: Kal tawp dai na cih in bang na ci nopna taktak hiam?

records.english: Could you explain what you mean by a small party?
records.zomi: Kipahna neu na cih in bang na ci nopna hiam hong genteh thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Do you want me to call Grandma tonight or just send her a message?
records.zomi: Tu zanin Pi ka sam ding na deih hiam, thu bek ka khak ding hiam?

records.english: Call her, because she can't read small writing on her phone.
records.zomi: Sam in, a phone tung-a laimal neute a sim thei kei ahih manin.

records.english: Let me make sure I've understood: you want us at seven, not eight?
records.zomi: Ka theih kician nadingin: nai giat hi lo-in nai sagih ciangin eite hong om dingin na deih hiam?

records.english: My mother's idea of a quick visit is three hours and a meal.
records.zomi: Ka nu' veh manlang ngaihsutna nai thum leh an khat ahi hi.

records.english: Clarifying expectations before a family holiday prevents many arguments.
records.zomi: Innkuan tawlngakni ma-in lamenna kician sak in kinialna tampi a dal hi.

records.english: Thank you for explaining; I'd completely misunderstood you.
records.zomi: Na genteh manin ka lungdam hi; ka thei khial vekpi hi.

records.english: When you say you'll be home soon, do you mean in ten minutes or in an hour?
records.zomi: Manlang takin inn ah ka tung ding hi, na cih ciangin minit sawm hiam nai khat hiam na ci nopna hiam?

records.english: About half an hour, unless the bus is late.
records.zomi: Nai langkhat bang, bus a nung kei leh.

records.english: When my daughter said she was busy, she really meant that she wanted to be left alone.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in ka buai hi, a cih ciangin amah kia-a om a deih hi, a ci nopna taktak ahi hi.

records.english: Can you show me what you mean instead of explaining it?
records.zomi: Genteh sangin na ci nopna hong lak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Asking someone what they mean is not rude; it shows that you want to understand.
records.zomi: Mi khat kiangah bang na ci nopna hiam dot pen zahtak lohna hi lo a; theih na deih lahna ahi hi.

records.english: My grandmother's 'a little sugar' is enough to sweeten a whole cake.
records.zomi: Ka pi' 'til tawmno' in cake bup a tuisak dingin a kicing hi.

records.english: Our son asked what I meant by 'be home by dark', since it gets dark at different times in winter and summer.
records.zomi: Phalbi leh khal ah hun tuamtuam-in a mial ahih manin 'a mial ma-in inn ah tung in' ka cih bang ka ci nopna hiam i tapa in a dong hi.

records.english: Misunderstandings in families often come from words that seem perfectly clear to the person who says them.
records.zomi: Innkuan-a kituak lohnate a tamzaw-in a gen mi adingin a kician mahmah bang kammalte pan hong pai hi.

records.english: Can you tell me again what you meant about selling the house?
records.zomi: Inn zuak tungtang bang na ci nopna hiam hong gen kik thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: My father's 'just round the corner' turned out to be a two-hour walk.
records.zomi: Ka pa' 'kil kiang bek' in nai nih kalna ahi hi, ci a kilang hi.

records.english: Are you saying you don't want to come, or that you can't?
records.zomi: Na hong pai nuam kei hi, na ci hiam, na hong pai thei kei hi, na ci hiam?

records.english: I'd love to come, but I'm working that evening.
records.zomi: Hong pai ka nuam mahmah a, ahi zongin tua nitak in nasep ka sem hi.

records.english: When you say 'everyone', do you mean the whole family or just us?
records.zomi: 'Mi khempeuh' na cih in innkuan bup na ci nopna hiam, eite bek hiam?

records.english: I'm not sure whether my brother was joking or serious.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal a nuihzak hiam, a taktak hiam ka thei kician kei hi.

records.english: In families, the same words can mean very different things to different generations.
records.zomi: Innkuan-ah kammal kibang in khangthak tuamtuam adingin khiatna tuam vekpi a nei thei hi.

records.english: Could you be a little more specific about when you'll arrive, since we're cooking for twelve?
records.zomi: Mi sawm leh nih adingin an i huan ding ahih manin bang hun ciangin na tung ding hiam kician zaw-in na gen thei ding hiam?

records.english: When my mother says 'we'll talk about it later', we know we're in trouble.
records.zomi: Ka nu in 'a nung ciangin i kihopih ding hi' a cih ciangin buaina ah i om hi, ci i thei uh hi.

records.english: By 'a few friends', how many do you mean?
records.zomi: 'Lawm tawmno' na cih in bangzah na ci nopna hiam?

records.english: Five or six, and they'll all bring food.
records.zomi: Nga hiam guk, a khempeuh in an a tawi ding uh hi.

records.english: Do you mean you'll pay for everyone, or just for the children?
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh adingin na pia ding hiam, naupangte adingin bek hiam na ci nopna hiam?

records.english: When you said you were tired of the arrangement, did you mean the job itself or all the travelling?
records.zomi: Kituakna na ning hi, na cih ciangin nasep mah hiam, khualzinna khempeuh hiam na ci nopna hiam?

records.english: When you said 'family dinner', did you include the cousins?
records.zomi: 'Innkuan nitak an' na cih ciangin sanggamte na kihel sak hiam?

records.english: Just the six of us this time.
records.zomi: Tu vei-in eite guk bek.

records.english: What did Grandpa mean when he said the soup needed something?
records.zomi: Pu in an tui khat peuhpeuh a kisam hi, a cih ciangin bang a ci nopna hiam?

records.english: I think he meant more salt, but he was too polite to say so.
records.zomi: Cii behlap a ci nopna hi, ka sa a, ahi zongin a zahtak lua ahih manin a gen kei hi.

records.english: What exactly do you mean by helping with the wedding?
records.zomi: Mopawi huh na cih in bang na ci nopna taktak hiam?

records.english: Mostly cooking, and a little decorating if you have time.
records.zomi: A tamzaw an huan, hun na neih leh kizeekna tawmno.

records.english: Sorry, do you mean my sister's son or my brother's?
records.zomi: Hong maisak in, ka u numei' tapa na ci hiam, ka sanggam pasal' tapa hiam?

records.english: Clarifying what you mean early can save a family from a week of hurt feelings.
records.zomi: Na ci nopna hun ma-in kician sak in innkuan khat kal khat lungsim natna pan a hondoh thei hi.

records.english: Does 'tidy your room' include under the bed?
records.zomi: 'Na khan siangsak in' cih in lupna nuai zong a huam hiam?

records.english: Yes, especially under the bed.
records.zomi: Huam hi, a diak in lupna nuai.

records.english: When my father says he's fine, we've learned that he often means the opposite.
records.zomi: Ka pa in ka hoih hi, a cih ciangin a tamzaw-in a kikalh a ci nopna ahi hi, ci i sin uh hi.

records.english: Visitors to the parliament can watch debates from the public gallery.
records.zomi: Parliament veh mite in mipi tutna mun pan kinialnate a en thei uh hi.

records.english: The welcome dinner was held in the old town hall, which had been decorated with flowers.
records.zomi: Muakna nitak an pak tawh kizeek khuapi inn lui ah kibawl hi.

records.english: Please greet our visitors politely, children, and then return to your desks.
records.zomi: Naupangte, i mikhualte zahtak takin hopih unla, tua khit ciangin na dawhkan uh ah ciah kik un.

records.english: Welcome to our hospital; if you need help finding a ward, please ask at the information desk.
records.zomi: I damdawi inn ah hong kimuak hi; damdawi inn khan zon dingin huhna na kisam leh thuhilhna dawhkan ah dong in.

records.english: We are honoured to welcome the mayor and the members of the council to this evening's concert.
records.zomi: Tu nitak la kikhopna ah khuapi makaipa leh khuapi office mite muak pen eite adingin zahtakna ahi hi.

records.english: Welcome, and thank you for travelling so far to be with us today.
records.zomi: Hong kimuak hi, tuni-in eite tawh om dingin gamla mahmah pan hong khualzin manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: The delegation's rooms were prepared with care the day before they arrived.
records.zomi: Palai pawl' khante a tun ma-un a zan in limtakin kigin hi.

records.english: We welcome visitors to the community garden every Saturday morning.
records.zomi: Kiginni zingsang simin mipi huan ah vehte i muak hi.

records.english: Visitors to the prison must leave their phones in the lockers at the entrance.
records.zomi: Thong inn veh mite in lutna-a koihna bawm ah a phone uh a nusia ding uh hi.

records.english: We hope the visit has been useful, and we would be glad to host you again.
records.zomi: Vehna a phatuam hi, ci-in i lamen uh a, nang kik muak ding i lungdam ding uh hi.

records.english: The delegation was welcomed at the airport by the deputy mayor and a group of schoolchildren.
records.zomi: Palai pawl vanlengtual ah deputy khuapi makaipa leh sangnaupang pawl khat in a muak uh hi.

records.english: Our school has welcomed visitors from more than twenty countries.
records.zomi: I sang in gam sawmnih sang tam pan hong veh mite a muak khin hi.

records.english: On arrival, each guest received a folder with the programme for the day.
records.zomi: A tun uh ciangin mikhual khatciat in ni' kalsuan dan nei lai koihna khat a ngah uh hi.

records.english: Official visitors are often given a programme that includes time to meet local people.
records.zomi: Kumpi vehte in mun-a mite kimuh nading hun nei kalsuan dan khat a ngah zel uh hi.

records.english: Can you arrange a room where the visitors can rest after their journey?
records.zomi: Vehte in a khualzinna uh khit ciangin a tawl theih nadingun khan khat na bawl thei ding hiam?

records.english: Welcoming visitors properly reflects well on the whole organisation.
records.zomi: Vehte hoih taka muak in pawl bup' min hoih a piangsak hi.

records.english: Our team welcomed the visiting engineers and showed them the new equipment.
records.zomi: I pawl in hong veh engineer te a muak uh a, vanzat thakte a lak uh hi.

records.english: The ambassador welcomed the guests in three languages at the national day reception.
records.zomi: Gam ni kimuakna ah ambassador in pau thum tawh mikhualte a muak hi.

records.english: All visitors must sign in at reception and wear a visitor's badge at all times.
records.zomi: Vehte khempeuh in kimuakna ah min gelh-in mikhual ciamtehna tawntung-in a bulh ding uh hi.

records.english: When we host international visitors, we try to explain our customs as well as our work.
records.zomi: Gam tuamtuam vehte i muak ciangin i nasep bek hi lo-in i ngeinate zong i genteh uh hi.

records.english: The company had a welcome lunch prepared for the visitors from abroad.
records.zomi: Company in gamdang pan vehte adingin muakna sun an khat a kiginsak hi.

records.english: We welcome visitors with disabilities, and ramps are available at every entrance.
records.zomi: Pumpi haksatna nei vehte i muak a, lutna khempeuh ah ramp a om hi.

records.english: How should we welcome the delegation when it arrives?
records.zomi: Palai pawl a tun ciangin bangci i muak ding hiam?

records.english: Meet them at the entrance, introduce the senior staff and offer them tea before the tour.
records.zomi: Lutna ah muak unla, nasem upate kitheisak unla, kalna ma-in niangtui pia un.

records.english: Please make our guests feel at home during their visit.
records.zomi: I mikhualte a vehna sungin inn ah bangin a kisak nadingun bawl un.

records.english: Please don't leave visitors waiting in the corridor; bring them straight to the office.
records.zomi: Vehte inn sung lampi ah ngak sak kei un; office ah a tang-in paipih un.

records.english: A warm welcome sets the tone for an official visit, even before any business is discussed.
records.zomi: Muakna lum khat in thu khatpeuh kihopih ma-in kumpi vehna adingin dinmun a bawl hi.

records.english: On behalf of the hospital board, we welcome the visiting health officials.
records.zomi: Damdawi inn makaipawl aiah hong veh damna kumpi nasemte i muak hi.

records.english: When the president visited the hospital, the staff welcomed him with flowers and songs.
records.zomi: President in damdawi inn a veh ciangin nasemte in pak leh la tawh a muak uh hi.

records.english: Shall we show the visitors the short video about the company?
records.zomi: Vehte company tungtang video tomno i lak ding hiam?

records.english: Please make sure the visitors' parking spaces are kept free tomorrow.
records.zomi: Zingciang vehte' mawtaw koihna munte a awng den hiam en in.

records.english: Is there anything our visitors need before the tour begins?
records.zomi: Kalna a kipat ma-in i vehte in bangmah a kisam uh hiam?

records.english: Children copy the screen habits of the adults around them.

records.english: Turn the volume down when you wear headphones, or you could damage your hearing.

records.english: Using technology safely is less about fear and more about good habits.

records.english: Taking a short break every hour helps your eyes rest when you work at a screen.
