records.english: May I take this opportunity to thank the organisers for an excellent conference?
records.zomi: Hih hun zang-in kikhopna lian hoih mahmah a bawl makaite kiangah lungdam ka gen thei ding hiam?

records.english: With your permission, I'll take my leave now.
records.zomi: Na phalna tawh tu-in ka pai ding hi.

records.english: Thank you for receiving us, and we hope to continue our cooperation.
records.zomi: Hong muak manun ka lungdam uh a, i kithuahna i zom den ding i lamen uh hi.

records.english: Would the visiting team like a group photograph before they depart?
records.zomi: Hong veh pawl in a pai ma-un pawl lim khat a la nuam uh hiam?

records.english: At the end of her final assembly, the head teacher stood quietly for a moment.
records.zomi: A kikhopna nunung pen' tawpna ah sang makaipa dai takin hun tawmno a ding hi.

records.english: Then she thanked the staff, the parents and every pupil by year group.
records.zomi: Tua khit ciangin nasemte, nu leh pate leh sangnaupang khempeuh kum pawl zui-in lungdam a gen hi.

records.english: She left the stage to a standing ovation that lasted several minutes.
records.zomi: Minit tawmno sung a sawt mite' ding-a khut beng tawh lamna mun a nusia hi.

records.english: The farewell address was brief, dignified and warmly applauded.
records.zomi: Goodbye thugenna a tom a, a zahtakhuai a, lum takin khut kibeng hi.

records.english: I'm afraid I must excuse myself, as I have another engagement this evening.
records.zomi: Hong maisak in, tu nitakin kikhopna dang khat ka nei ahih manin ka pai kul hi.

records.english: Kind regards, and I hope to hear from you soon.
records.zomi: Deihsakna tawh, manlang takin na thu ka zak ding ka lamen hi.

records.english: I'll leave my contact details with your secretary.
records.zomi: Ka kizopna thute na secretary kiangah ka nusia ding hi.

records.english: Before we close, please join me in wishing Mrs. Cing every success in her new post.
records.zomi: I khak ma-in, Nu Cing a nasep thak ah a lawhcin nadingin kei tawh deihsak un.

records.english: Do you think it would be appropriate to send the chairman a farewell card?
records.zomi: Makaipa kiangah goodbye card khat khak a kilawm ding na ci hiam?

records.english: At the end of the official visit, both leaders issued a short joint statement.
records.zomi: Kumpi vehna tawpna ah makai nih in khawm-a thugenna tomno khat a pia uh hi.

records.english: On behalf of the board, I would like to thank our departing director for twelve years of service.
records.zomi: Makaipawl aiah kum sawm leh nih nasep a sem i pai ding director kiangah lungdam ka gen nuam hi.

records.english: Should the company send an announcement to all staff when a senior colleague leaves?
records.zomi: Nasep lawm upa khat a pai ciangin company in nasem khempeuh kiangah thuzaksak a khak ding hiam?

records.english: The judge thanked the jury for their service and dismissed them.
records.zomi: Thukhenpa in jury te a nasep uh adingin lungdam a gen a, a pai sak hi.

records.english: The Embassy hosted a reception to mark the end of the consul's term.
records.zomi: Embassy in consul' nasep hun tawpna ciamteh dingin kimuakna khat a bawl hi.

records.english: Thank you all for coming, and have a safe journey home.
records.zomi: Hong pai na vekpi-un ka lungdam hi, bit takin inn ah ciah un.

records.english: We look forward to welcoming you back next year.
records.zomi: Kum zom ciangin nang kik muak dingin i ngak uh hi.

records.english: It has been a privilege to serve this community.
records.zomi: Hih mipi nasem sak pen zahtakna khat ahi hi.

records.english: Our staff lined the entrance to say goodbye to the departing general manager.
records.zomi: I nasemte in pai ding general manager goodbye ci dingin lutna ah a ding uh hi.

records.english: Please accept my sincere thanks and best wishes for your retirement.
records.zomi: Ka lungtang taka lungdamna leh na nasep tawpna adingin deihsakna hoih pen pom in.

records.english: We wish you a pleasant stay for the rest of your visit.
records.zomi: Na vehna a dang sungin nuam takin om in.

records.english: How should I end a formal letter when I don't know the reader's name?
records.zomi: Simmi' min ka theih kei ciangin lai kizahtak khat bangci ka khak ding hiam?

records.english: In British English, you would normally write Yours faithfully.
records.zomi: British English ah a tamzaw-in Yours faithfully na gelh ding hi.

records.english: Will the minister be staying for the reception after the ceremony?
records.zomi: Pawi khit-a kimuakna ah minister a om lai ding hiam?

records.english: Unfortunately not; she must leave for the airport at four o'clock.
records.zomi: Lungkham huai takin a om kei ding; nai li ciangin vanlengtual ah a pai kul hi.

records.english: A short, sincere speech is more fitting at a formal farewell than a long list of achievements.
records.zomi: Zahtakna goodbye ah zawhna list sau sangin thugenna tom leh lungtang tawh kigen a kilawm zaw hi.

records.english: The ambassador took her formal leave of the president before returning home.
records.zomi: Ambassador in a gam ah a ciah kik ma-in president kiangah zahtak takin goodbye a ci hi.

records.english: Allow me to walk you to the lift.
records.zomi: Lift dong kong paipih dingin hong phal in.

records.english: A formal resignation letter should thank the employer and state your last working day.
records.zomi: Kizahtak nasep nusiatna lai in nasep piaktu kiangah lungdam a gen-in nasep ni nunung a gen ding hi.

records.english: A formal goodbye at work should be gracious, even if you are leaving for unhappy reasons.
records.zomi: Lungkham hang tawh na pai zongin nasep-a goodbye zahtak a hehpih ding hi.

records.english: The retiring officer saluted the flag one last time.
records.zomi: Nasep tawp office nasempa in a nunung pen-in flag zahtak lahna a bawl hi.

records.english: Goodbye, everyone, and congratulations once again to our graduates.
records.zomi: Goodbye, mi khempeuh, i sang zo thakte kiangah lungdam kik ka gen hi.

records.english: The ceremony ended with the national anthem, after which the guests left in silence.
records.zomi: Pawi gam la tawh a bei a, tua khit ciangin mikhualte dai takin a pai uh hi.

records.english: I'm sorry to leave early, but my flight is at six.
records.zomi: Hun ma-in ka pai ding hangin maisak in, ka vanleng nai guk ciangin ahi hi.

records.english: Thank you for your hospitality during our visit.
records.zomi: I vehna sungin na zindo manin ka lungdam uh hi.

records.english: The board accepted his resignation with regret.
records.zomi: Makaipawl in a nasep nusiatna lungkham takin a pom hi.

records.english: At official dinners, guests should not leave before the guest of honour.
records.zomi: Kumpi nitak an ah mikhualte zahtakna mikhual ma-in a pai kei ding uh hi.

records.english: The president bade farewell to the visiting prime minister at the airport.
records.zomi: President in hong veh prime minister vanlengtual ah goodbye a ci hi.

records.english: It was a pleasure meeting you, Dr. Thawng.
records.zomi: Nang kimuh a nuam hi, Dr. Thawng.

records.english: It has been an honour to work alongside such dedicated colleagues.
records.zomi: Tua bang mawhpuakna nei nasep lawmte tawh nasep pen zahtakna khat ahi hi.

records.english: Should I shake hands with each member of the panel before I leave the interview?
records.zomi: Kidotna ka nusiat ma-in makaipawl mi khatciat tawh khut ka kilen ding hiam?

records.english: A polite nod and a thank-you to the whole panel is usually enough.
records.zomi: Lu nong zahtak khat leh makaipawl bup kiangah lungdamna in a tamzaw-in a kicing hi.

records.english: Please don't hesitate to contact us if you need anything further.
records.zomi: Bangmah na kisam leh hong sam dingin lungmang kei in.

records.english: We thank you for your many years of faithful service.
records.zomi: Kum tampi muanhuai taka na nasep adingin ka lungdam uh hi.

records.english: In formal settings, it is polite to thank the host before saying goodbye to the other guests.
records.zomi: Kizahtak mun te ah mikhual dangte kiangah goodbye na cih ma-in mikhual dawnpa kiangah lungdam gen pen zahtakna ahi hi.

records.english: Will the head of the school see our guests off at the main gate?
records.zomi: Sang makaipa in i mikhualte kongpi lian ah a paipih ding hiam?

records.english: Your Honour, may I step down now?
records.zomi: Thukhenpa, tu-in ka kum suk thei ding hiam?

records.english: Safe travels, and please convey our thanks to your government.
records.zomi: Bit takin khualzin in, na kumpi kiangah i lungdamna hong gen sak in.

records.english: It is customary for the outgoing chairperson to say a few words at the final meeting.
records.zomi: Pai ding makaipa in kikhopna nunung ah kammal tawmno gen pen ngeina ahi hi.

records.english: Visitors are requested to sign out at the security desk before leaving the building.
records.zomi: Vehte inn a nusiat ma-un bitna dawhkan ah min gelh-in a pusuak ding uh hi.

records.english: The outgoing mayor handed the chain of office to her successor at a short ceremony.
records.zomi: Pai ding khuapi makaipa in pawi tomno khat ah a zom ding mi kiangah nasep khainiang a pia hi.

records.english: The delegation was escorted to the airport by an officer from the foreign ministry.
records.zomi: Palai pawl gamdang ministry pan office nasem khat in vanlengtual dong a paipih hi.

records.english: Goodbye, sir, and thank you for your time.
records.zomi: Goodbye, Pu, na hun hong piak manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: We regret that Professor Lal is unable to stay for the closing session.
records.zomi: Professor Lal kikhopna khakna ah a om thei kei ding hangin i lungkham uh hi.

records.english: When we were short of money, the family next door never let us feel ashamed.
records.zomi: Sum i tasam ciangin i kiang inn innkuan in hong zumsak ngei kei uh hi.

records.english: When our baby was born, the neighbours took our older children to school for a whole month.
records.zomi: I naungek a suah ciangin inn vengte in kha khat bup i ta upate sang ah a paipih uh hi.

records.english: My father always says that the neighbours who helped him are the reason he finished school.
records.zomi: Ka pa in amah hong huh inn vengte hangin sang a zo hi, a ci tawntung hi.

records.english: Do you remember the neighbour who taught you to swim?
records.zomi: Tuipeek hong sinsak inn veng na phawk hiam?

records.english: The summer I turned twelve, our neighbour's barn caught fire.
records.zomi: Kum sawm leh nih ka cin khal in i inn veng' van koihna inn mei a kang hi.

records.english: My parents woke us, and we joined the line of people passing buckets of water.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in hong phongsak a, tui bawm a kipia-a kipia mi tampi tawh i kithuah uh hi.

records.english: We couldn't save the barn, but the animals all got out safely.
records.zomi: Van koihna inn i hum zo kei uh hi, ahi zongin ganhingte khempeuh bit takin a pusuak uh hi.

records.english: The neighbours' kindness during my father's illness is something our family will never forget.
records.zomi: Ka pa a nat lai-a inn vengte' hehpihna i innkuan in i mangngilh ngei kei ding hi.

records.english: Grandma used to say that you should never let a neighbour go to bed hungry.
records.zomi: Pi in inn veng khat gilkial-in a lupsak ngei kei in, a ci zel hi.

records.english: Dad repaired the neighbour's car for free, and they gave us a basket of mangoes.
records.zomi: Pa in inn veng' mawtaw a man la lo-in a bawl hoih a, amaute in theihai bawm khat hong pia uh hi.

records.english: Who showed you how to mend a puncture?
records.zomi: Mawtaw kawng puak bangci bawl hoih ding hiam kua in hong lak hiam?

records.english: The old man next door, when I was about nine.
records.zomi: Ka kum kua bang ka kim lai-in i kiang inn pu upa in.

records.english: After the widower's wife died, each family on our lane cooked for him one evening a week.
records.zomi: Meigong pasal' zi a sih khit ciangin i lampi tung innkuan khatciat in kal khat-in nitak khat amah adingin an a huan uh hi.

records.english: My wife taught the young mother next door how to bathe her newborn.
records.zomi: Ka zi in kiang inn nu khangno kiangah a naungek bangci kisil ding hiam a lak hi.

records.english: Our neighbour drove my wife to the hospital at three in the morning when our car wouldn't start.
records.zomi: I mawtaw a kipan loh ciangin zingkal nai thum-in i inn veng in ka zi damdawi inn ah a paipih hi.

records.english: Shall I take the neighbours' bins in while they're on holiday?
records.zomi: Inn vengte tawlngakni a zat lai-un a bin uh ka lut sak ding hiam?

records.english: Because our parents worked late, the woman across the road gave my sister and me supper twice a week.
records.zomi: I nu leh i pa nitak lam dong na a sep uh ahih manin lampi khat lam-a om numei in ka u numei leh kei kal khat-in nihvei nitak an hong pia hi.

records.english: Did you thank Mrs. Ngaih for looking after your little brother?
records.zomi: Na nau pasal a cingcing manin Nu Ngaih kiangah lungdam na gen hiam?

records.english: Whenever someone on our street is sick, my aunt arrives with a pot of chicken soup.
records.zomi: I lampi tung-a mi khat a nat ciangin ka ni in ar an tui beel khat tawh a tung zel hi.

records.english: Our daughter walks the neighbour's dog when his knees are bad.
records.zomi: Inn veng' khuk a nat ciangin i tanu in a ui a paipih zel hi.

records.english: Thank you for helping my mum with her shopping when I couldn't come.
records.zomi: Ka pai theih loh lai-in ka nu' van leina na huh manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: Our neighbour helped me fill in my citizenship forms, line by line.
records.zomi: I inn veng in ka gam mi suah lai-te kigelh khat zawh khat hong huh hi.

records.english: My brother helped our neighbour's son with his maths every week until he passed his exams.
records.zomi: Ka nau pasal in i inn veng' tapa a sitna a zawh dong kal simin a maths a huh hi.

records.english: My cousin moved in with an elderly neighbour to keep her company after her stroke.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam in inn veng upa khat a lutang natna khit ciangin a om khawm dingin a inn ah a teng khawm hi.

records.english: The family downstairs lent us their cot when our cousins came to stay with their baby.
records.zomi: I sanggamte a naungek tawh hong om uh ciangin a nuai lam-a innkuan in a naungek lupna hong leitawi uh hi.

records.english: I'm going to help Mrs. Dim paint her fence this afternoon.
records.zomi: Tu sunin Nu Dim' huang ka khuh sak ding hi.

records.english: The day we moved out, the neighbours cooked us a farewell meal.
records.zomi: I pem ni-in inn vengte in goodbye an hong huan sak uh hi.

records.english: Why do you always check on Mrs. Hau in the mornings?
records.zomi: Bang hangin zingsang simin Nu Hau na en tawntung hiam?

records.english: Because she lives alone, and she once fell and couldn't reach the phone.
records.zomi: Amah kia-in a om a, khatvei a kia a, phone a tun zo kei ahih manin.

records.english: My grandparents' house was always open to any neighbour who needed a bed for the night.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh pi' inn zan khat lupna a kisam inn veng khempeuh adingin a kihong tawntung hi.

records.english: We all chipped in to buy a wheelchair ramp for the family at the end of the street.
records.zomi: Lampi tawp-a innkuan adingin wheelchair lampi khiahna lei dingin i khempeuh in sum i kikhawm uh hi.

records.english: Mum always cooks a little extra in case a neighbour needs a meal.
records.zomi: Inn veng khat in an a kisam kha ding hi, ci-in nu in an tawmno a behlap-in a huan tawntung hi.

records.english: My children learned to share by watching their grandparents share everything with the neighbours.
records.zomi: Ka tate in a pu leh a pi uh in inn vengte tawh na khempeuh a hawm uh a muh uh pan hawm a sin uh hi.

records.english: Helping the people next door was simply part of how my family lived.
records.zomi: Kiang inn mite huh pen ka innkuan' nuntakzia bek ahi hi.

records.english: Could you hold the ladder while I fix Mr. Kham's gutter?
records.zomi: Pu Kham' innkhum tui luanna ka bawl hoih laitakin kahlei na len sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: We help the neighbours, and they help us; that's how it has always been in our family.
records.zomi: Inn vengte i huh a, amaute in hong huh uh hi; tua bangin i innkuan ah a om tawntung hi.

records.english: Grandpa still talks about the night the whole village helped him rebuild his roof before the rains.
records.zomi: Guah ma-in a innkhum a lam kik nadingin khua bup in a huh zan thu Pu in tu dong a gen lai hi.

records.english: When my uncle's shop was robbed, the neighbours raised enough money to restock his shelves.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu' sumbuk a kiguk ciangin inn vengte in a dawhkan tungah van a koih kik theih ding sum a kaikhawm uh hi.

records.english: When the river rose, our neighbours on higher ground let us keep our goats in their yard.
records.zomi: Gun a kan ciangin mun sang-a om i inn vengte in a inn mai uh ah i keelte hong koih sak uh hi.

records.english: Helping a neighbour with small jobs often turns into a friendship that lasts for decades.
records.zomi: Inn veng khat na neu tawmno huh in kum sawm tampi sung om lawmta khat ah a kikhel thei hi.

records.english: Is it all right if I go and help Mr. Tuang carry his firewood?
records.zomi: Pu Tuang' singphuai puak a huh dingin ka pai le a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, but come back before it gets dark.
records.zomi: Hoih hi, ahi zongin a mial ma-in ciah kik in.

records.english: Shall we invite the new family to lunch on Sunday?
records.zomi: Innkuan thak Nipini sun an ne dingin i sam ding hiam?

records.english: I learned kindness from watching my grandmother look after the whole street.
records.zomi: Ka pi in lampi bup a kem a muh ka muh pan hehpihna ka sin hi.

records.english: Our grandparents still write to the family who sheltered them during the war.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh pi in gal hun lai-a amaute a hu innkuan kiangah tu dong lai a khak lai uh hi.

records.english: My little brother shovelled snow for the neighbours and refused to take any money.
records.zomi: Ka nau pasal neu in inn vengte adingin vuuk a phiat a, sum a la nuam kei hi.

records.english: Please help me carry these chairs over to Mrs. Zam's for her party.
records.zomi: Nu Zam' pawi adingin hih tutphahte a inn ah puak dingin hong huh in.

records.english: Our son mows the lawn for the elderly couple next door every other Saturday.
records.zomi: I tapa in Kiginni nih zawh khat ciangin kiang inn zi leh pasal upa' inn mai lopa a at sak hi.

records.english: Can we bring the neighbours some of the cake we made?
records.zomi: I bawl cake tawmno inn vengte i paipih thei ding hiam?

records.english: When I came home from hospital, I found that my neighbours had cleaned the whole house.
records.zomi: Damdawi inn pan inn ka tun ciangin ka inn vengte in inn bup a siangsak uh ka mu hi.

records.english: Every Christmas, my parents invited the lonely bachelor next door to eat with us.
records.zomi: Christmas simin ka nu leh ka pa in kiang inn tangval kia-a om lungkham pa kei tawh an ne dingin a sam uh hi.

records.english: Can you take this bowl of soup to the lady next door?
records.zomi: Hih an tui kuang khat kiang inn numei kiangah na paipih thei ding hiam?

records.english: What did the neighbours do when Grandma was in hospital?
records.zomi: Pi damdawi inn ah a om lai-in inn vengte in bang a hih uh hiam?

records.english: They fed her chickens and watered her garden every day.
records.zomi: Ni simin a arte uh an a pia uh a, a huan ah tui a buak uh hi.

records.english: Do you remember how Grandpa lent his tools to anyone on the street who asked?
records.zomi: Pu in a vanzatte lampi tung-a a ngen peuhmah kiangah a leitawi zel na phawk hiam?

records.english: Let's ask the new neighbours if they need help unpacking.
records.zomi: Inn veng thakte a van uh phelkhiat ding huh a kisam hiam i dong ding.

records.english: My sister and I used to read stories to the blind lady across the street.
records.zomi: Ka u numei leh kei in lampi khat lam-a om numei mittaw kiangah tangthute i sim sak zel uh hi.

records.english: When Dad lost his job, our neighbours quietly left bags of rice and vegetables on our doorstep.
records.zomi: Pa a nasep a man ciangin i inn vengte in dai takin i lutna kong mai ah buh leh anteh ip hong koih uh hi.

records.english: Mum sent me next door with a hot water bottle when the old lady's heating stopped working.
records.zomi: Numei upa' inn lumsakna a sem nawn loh ciangin nu in tui lum bawm khat tawh kiang inn ah hong sawl hi.

records.english: Our children grew up thinking that every adult on the street was a kind of uncle or aunt.
records.zomi: I tate in lampi tung-a mi upa khempeuh pa neu hiam ni hi, ci-in a khangkhia uh hi.

records.english: Please report any damaged street signs to the council.
records.zomi: Lampi min lim a siate khuapi office kiangah gen un.

records.english: There's a big hole in the road outside our school.
records.zomi: I sang mai-a lampi ah kua lian khat a om hi.

records.english: Many rural schools still lack basic infrastructure such as toilets and running water.
records.zomi: Khuaneu sang tampi in tu dong eek inn leh tui pipe bang a kisam pen mipi zat dingte a nei nai kei uh hi.

records.english: How much did the new stadium cost the taxpayers?
records.zomi: Stadium thak in siah pia mite bangzah a beisak hiam?

records.english: The old bridge was closed after engineers found cracks in its supports.
records.zomi: Engineer te in a khaukhing ah a kiphel na a muh uh khit ciangin lei lui kikhak hi.

records.english: Has the council said when it will repair the broken pavement?
records.zomi: Lampi pang kia-a siate bang hun-in a bawl hoih ding hiam khuapi office in a gen ta hiam?

records.english: Did you hear that they're finally fixing the potholes on our road?
records.zomi: I lampi tung-a kuate a tawpna-ah a bawl hoih uh ding thu na za hiam?

records.english: Rather than building a new road, the council decided to improve the bus service.
records.zomi: Lampi thak lam sangin khuapi office in bus nasep hoih zaw sak dingin a khensat hi.

records.english: Do you know who is responsible for fixing the traffic lights?
records.zomi: Mawtaw meivakte bawl hoih kua in mawhpuak hiam na thei hiam?

records.english: Without regular maintenance, even a new road can fall apart within a few years.
records.zomi: Ciangtan-a kem lo-in lampi thak zong kum tawmno sungin a sia thei hi.

records.english: Our town finally got a proper sewage system last year.
records.zomi: I khua in kum bei-in eek tui luanna hoih khat a nei ta hi.

records.english: Every year, part of the national budget is set aside for repairing roads.
records.zomi: Kum simin gam sum zat ding pawl khat lampi bawl hoih nadingin a kikoih hi.

records.english: The ferry is the only link between the island and the mainland.
records.zomi: Tembaw pen tuikulh leh gam lian kikal-a kizopna khat bek ahi hi.

records.english: Why is the main road being dug up again?
records.zomi: Bang hangin lampi lian a kitou kik hiam?

records.english: They're laying new pipes for clean water.
records.zomi: Tui siang adingin tui pipe thakte a koih uh hi.

records.english: When infrastructure fails, poor families are often the first and worst affected.
records.zomi: Mipi zat dingte a sia ciangin innkuan zawngte a tamzaw-in a masa pen leh a gimna thupi pen-in a thuak uh hi.

records.english: Our neighbourhood finally has street lights, so walking home at night feels safer.
records.zomi: I lampi ah lampi meivak a om ta ahih manin zanin inn ah ciah a bit zaw hi.

records.english: Public transport works best when buses, trains and footpaths are planned together.
records.zomi: Bus, meileng leh peel lampite khawm-a ki-ngaihsut ciangin mipi khualzinna a hoih pen hi.

records.english: The underground station near my office has a new lift for wheelchair users.
records.zomi: Ka office kiang-a leinuai meileng mun ah wheelchair zangte adingin lift thak a om hi.

records.english: The new bridge has cut my journey to work by twenty minutes.
records.zomi: Lei thak in nasep mun ka paina minit sawmnih a tomsak hi.

records.english: The council publishes a list of planned road repairs on its website.
records.zomi: Khuapi office in bawl hoih ding lampite list a website ah a koih hi.

records.english: The government is asking private companies to help pay for the new highway.
records.zomi: Kumpi in lampi lian thak a man piak nadingin company te huh dingin a ngen hi.

records.english: The new market hall was paid for by the town and opened last spring.
records.zomi: Sumbuk inn thak khua in a man a pia a, spring bei-in a kihong hi.

records.english: Taxes from fuel help pay for new roads and bridges.

records.english: I wrote to the council to ask when our street lights would be fixed.

records.english: The new tunnel goes under the river and connects the two halves of the city.

records.english: Good drainage is one of the cheapest ways to protect a city from damage.

records.english: Investing in infrastructure today can save a government far more money in the future.

records.english: Can you show me where the nearest bus stop is?
records.zomi: A kiang pen bus khawlna koi ah a om hiam hong lak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Is the airport really being expanded to handle more flights?
records.zomi: Vanleng tam zaw a khawl theih nadingin vanlengtual taktak-in a kibawl lian hiam?

records.english: Good public infrastructure helps businesses move goods quickly and cheaply.
records.zomi: Mipi zat dingte hoih in sumbawlte van manlang leh man neu takin a puak theih nadingun a huh hi.

records.english: The train line was electrified, so the journey is quieter and faster now.
records.zomi: Meileng lampi ah meivak tha a kikoih ahih manin tu-in khualzinna a daih zaw a, a manlang zaw hi.

records.english: Public toilets in the park are cleaned twice a day.
records.zomi: Huan lian sung-a mipi eek innte ni khat-in nihvei kisiangsak hi.

records.zomi: Lampi meivakte man kua in a pia hiam?

records.english: The local council pays for them with money from taxes.
records.zomi: Khua khuapi office in siah sum tawh a man a pia hi.

records.english: Clean water from a public tap has changed daily life in our village.
records.zomi: Mipi tui kongpi pan tui siang in i khua ah ni simin nuntakna a khel hi.

records.english: Which districts get their electricity from the new power station?
records.zomi: Bang khua pawlte in meivak tha inn thak pan meivak a ngah uh hiam?

records.english: The government has promised to connect every village to the electricity grid within ten years.
records.zomi: Kum sawm sungin khua khempeuh meivak tha tawh kizopsak dingin kumpi in a kiciam hi.

records.english: Is the water from the public fountain safe to drink?
records.zomi: Mipi tui kongpi pan tui dawn ding a bit hiam?

records.english: A new road can bring jobs to a remote area, but it can also bring heavy traffic.
records.zomi: Lampi thak in khua gamla khat ah nasep a tun thei a, ahi zongin mawtaw tampi zong a tun thei hi.

records.english: The government is building a new railway line between the two cities.
records.zomi: Kumpi in khuapi nih kikal ah meileng lampi thak a lam hi.

records.english: Roads, bridges, water pipes and power lines are all part of a country's public infrastructure.
records.zomi: Lampi, lei, tui pipe leh meivak khaute khempeuh gam khat' mipi zat dingte ahi hi.

records.english: Building a road through the mountains took the engineers almost ten years.
records.zomi: Mualte kal ah lampi khat lam in engineer te kum sawm dekin a zang hi.

records.english: Large infrastructure projects often cost more and take longer than originally planned.
records.zomi: Mipi zat ding nasep lian tampi in a kigelh masak sangin sum tam zaw a zang a, hun sawt zaw a la hi.

records.english: The road to the village is closed for repairs until Friday.
records.zomi: Khua paina lampi Laithai ni dong bawl hoih nadingin kikhak hi.

records.english: Our street fills with water every rainy season because the drains are too small.
records.zomi: Tui luanna lampite a neu lua ahih manin guahkhua simin i lampi tui-in a dim hi.

records.english: Why are there traffic cones on the bridge?
records.zomi: Bang hangin lei tungah mawtaw dalna van a om hiam?

records.english: Workers are repainting the railings this week.
records.zomi: Hih kal sungin nasemte in a khutden te a khuh kik uh hi.

records.english: The bus station was rebuilt with money from the national government.
records.zomi: Bus khawlna mun gam kumpi sum tawh kilam kik hi.

records.english: Our mayor wants to turn the old railway into a walking path.
records.zomi: I khuapi makaipa in meileng lampi lui peel lampi ah a khel nuam hi.

records.english: The village well was replaced by a pipe system that brings water to every house.
records.zomi: Khua tuikhuk inn khempeuh ah tui a tun pipe tawh kikhel hi.

records.english: The city plans to build more bicycle lanes over the next five years.
records.zomi: Kum nga sungin siiksakol lampi tam zaw lam dingin khuapi in a ngaihsun hi.

records.english: Please use the footbridge to cross the motorway.
records.zomi: Lampi lian kantan nadingin peel lei zang un.

records.english: The new hospital needs a reliable electricity supply, so it has its own generator as well.
records.zomi: Damdawi inn thak in meivak muanhuai a kisam ahih manin amah mah generator zong a nei hi.

records.english: Building a dam can provide electricity and water, but it may also force families to leave their land.
records.zomi: Tui khakna lam in meivak leh tui a pia thei a, ahi zongin innkuante a gam uh nusia dingin a sawl thei hi.

records.english: Old water pipes can leak a large share of the water before it reaches people's homes.
records.zomi: Tui pipe luite in mite inn a tun ma-in tui tampi a zui thei hi.

records.english: My grandmother was a nurse during the epidemic, and she still talks about the long nights.
records.zomi: Ka pi natna lianpi hun lai-in nurse ahi a, zan sau thu tu dong a gen lai hi.

records.english: Our family's history changed completely the year my grandparents left their village.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh ka pi a khua uh a nusiat kum in i innkuan tangthu a kikhel bup hi.

records.english: Understanding what our grandparents went through helps us appreciate the peace we have now.
records.zomi: I pu leh pi' thuakna i theih ciangin tu-a i neih lungmuanna lungdam zaw dingin hong huh hi.

records.english: We visited the town where my great-grandparents lived before they emigrated.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh pi' nu leh pa gamdang a pem ma-un a tenna khua i veh uh hi.

records.english: Our family album has a picture of the first car that came to the village.
records.zomi: I innkuan lim bu ah khua ah a tung masa mawtaw' lim a om hi.

records.english: When my parents talk about the year of the revolution, they always disagree about the details.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in gam kiheina kum thu a gen uh ciangin a thu neu deuhte ah a kituak ngei kei uh hi.

records.english: My grandparents queued for hours to vote in the first election after independence.
records.zomi: Gam suahtakna khit-a teelna masa pen ah vote khiat dingin ka pu leh ka pi nai tampi sung a kizom-in a ngak uh hi.

records.english: Could you help me find out where my grandfather was born?
records.zomi: Ka pu koi ah a suak hiam ka theih nadingin hong huh thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Let's record Grandpa telling his story before he forgets the details.
records.zomi: Pu in a thu neu deuhte a mangngilh ma-in a tangthu a gen i ciamteh ding.

records.english: When I was a girl, my mother told me about the night soldiers came to her village.
records.zomi: Ka nungak lai-in ka nu in galkapte a khua uh ah a tun zan thu hong gen hi.

records.english: Her family hid in the forest for three days with almost nothing to eat.
records.zomi: A innkuan uh an ne ding om dek lo-in ni thum sung gammang ah a bu uh hi.

records.english: She never spoke about it again, but I wrote her story down so that my children would know it.
records.zomi: Tua thu a gen kik ngei nawn kei hi, ahi zongin ka tate in a theih nadingun a tangthu ka gelh hi.

records.english: My aunt saw the old king's funeral procession when she was a little girl.
records.zomi: Ka ni in a naupan lai-in kumpipa lui' vuina ah a mi paite a mu hi.

records.english: My parents met at a protest march in the city when they were students.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa sangnaupang a hih lai-un khuapi-a langpanna lampi pai ah a kimu uh hi.

records.english: Talking to older relatives can reveal how national events shaped ordinary lives.
records.zomi: Sanggam upate tawh kihopihna in gam thupiangte in mi nuntakna bangci a kheel hiam a lak thei hi.

records.english: Can you tell me again how Great-Grandma escaped across the border?
records.zomi: Pi upa gam gi bangci a tai kan hiam hong gen kik thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Ask your grandfather what school was like before the new government came.
records.zomi: Kumpi thak a tun ma-in sang bangci om hiam na pu dong in.

records.english: I wish I had asked my grandfather more about his years in the army.
records.zomi: Ka pu' galkap kumte thu ka dong tam zaw le ka cih hi.

records.english: The great storm of 1974 is still the event my family uses to measure time.
records.zomi: 1974 kum-a huihpi lian pen ka innkuan in hun a tehna thupiang ahi lai hi.

records.english: History becomes personal when you realise your own family lived through it.
records.zomi: Na innkuan mah in a thuak uh hi, ci na theih ciangin tangthu pen nangmah thu a suak hi.

records.english: Grandpa has kept a coin from every new government since he was a boy.
records.zomi: Pu in a naupan lai pan kumpi thak khatciat sum kuang khat a kem hi.

records.english: I didn't understand the history of our country until I heard my father's stories.
records.zomi: Ka pa' tangthu ka zak ma-in i gam tangthu ka thei kei hi.

records.english: Was Grandma alive when the war started?
records.zomi: Gal a kipat lai-in Pi a nungta ta hiam?

records.english: Grandpa still remembers listening to the news of independence on a neighbour's radio.
records.zomi: Pu in inn veng' radio tungah gam suahtakna thu a ngaihkhiat tu dong a phawk lai hi.

records.english: Our son was surprised that his grandparents had lived without the internet.
records.zomi: A pu leh a pi uh internet om lo-in a nungta uh hi, ci-in i tapa lamdang a sa hi.

records.english: My great-grandmother kept the ration book she used during the war in a tin box.
records.zomi: Pi upa in gal hun lai-a a zat an hawmna bu sik bawm khat sungah a kem hi.

records.english: My grandmother still has the medal her father received for his service.
records.zomi: Ka pi in a pa' nasepna adingin a ngah medal tu dong a nei lai hi.

records.english: Our son's history project was based on his great-grandfather's journey to the capital.
records.zomi: I tapa' tangthu nasep pen a pu upa' gam khuapi lian a paina tungah kinga hi.

records.english: Do you have any old photos from the time Grandma was at school?
records.zomi: Pi sang a kah lai hun pan lim lui na nei hiam?

records.english: Mum, can you remember the day the first school opened in your village?
records.zomi: Nu, na khua ah sang masa a kihon ni na phawk thei hiam?

records.english: Mum, what do you remember about the year the wall came down?
records.zomi: Nu, kulh a kiphet kum tungtang bang na phawk hiam?

records.english: Big historical events often appear in family stories as small, everyday details.
records.zomi: Tangthu thupiang lianpite in innkuan tangthu ah ni sim-a thu neu deuhte bangin a lang zel uh hi.

records.english: We keep my great-grandmother's travel papers in a frame on the wall.
records.zomi: Pi upa' khualzinna laite bang tungah lim kuang khat sungah i kem uh hi.

records.english: Listening to family memories teaches children that history happened to real people.
records.zomi: Innkuan phawkna ngaihkhiat in tangthu pen mi taktakte tungah a piang hi, ci-in naupangte a lak hi.

records.english: Why does Grandpa get quiet whenever we talk about that year?
records.zomi: Tua kum thu i gen ciangin bang hangin Pu a dai zel hiam?

records.english: Because he lost two of his brothers then, and it still hurts him.
records.zomi: Tua hun-in a sanggam pasal nih a sih manin tu dong a lungtang a na lai hi.

records.english: We still celebrate the day our family arrived safely in the new country.
records.zomi: I innkuan gam thak ah bit taka a tun ni tu dong i lawm lai uh hi.

records.english: Did anyone in our family fight in the war?
records.zomi: I innkuan sung pan kuamah in gal a do ngei hiam?

records.english: Hearing my grandfather describe the famine made the history lesson feel very real.
records.zomi: Ka pu in kialpi a gen ka zak ciangin tangthu sinna a taktak mahmah hi.

records.english: Every family has its own way of remembering the big events of the past.
records.zomi: Innkuan khatciat in a beisa-a thupiang lianpite a phawkzia uh tuam a nei ciat uh hi.

records.english: My daughter interviewed her grandmother for a school project on the 1990s.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in 1990 kumte tungtang sang nasep adingin a pi a dong hi.

records.english: We found my great-grandfather's name on the list of soldiers at the memorial.
records.zomi: Phawkna suang ah galkapte' min list sungah ka pu upa' min i mu hi.

records.english: Dad, did your school close during the civil war?
records.zomi: Pa, gam sung gal hun lai-in na sang a kikhak hiam?

records.english: When the earthquake struck, my parents were newly married and living in a small rented room.
records.zomi: Lei a lin ciangin ka nu leh ka pa a kiteng thak uh a, khan neu khat a hawh uh ah a teng uh hi.

records.english: Grandpa's diary from the 1960s gives a very personal view of a turbulent time.
records.zomi: Pu' 1960 kumte-a nitum ciamtehna bu in buaina hun khat a muhna tuam taktak a lak hi.

records.english: Mum's family moved three times during the war, each time with fewer belongings.
records.zomi: Gal hun sungin nu' innkuan thumvei a pem uh a, khatvei simin a van uh a tawm semsem hi.

records.english: Our children were amazed to learn that their grandmother had never seen a telephone until she was twenty.
records.zomi: A pi uh kum sawmnih a phak dong telephone a mu ngei lo hi, ci a theih uh ciangin i tate lamdang a sa mahmah uh hi.

records.english: Grandpa, what was it like to vote in the first free election?
records.zomi: Pu, teelna zalen masa pen ah vote khiat bang ci-in a om hiam?

records.english: Do you know why our family name changed?
records.zomi: Bang hangin i innkuan min a kikheel hiam na thei hiam?

records.english: Did Great-Grandpa ever write down what he saw during the war?
records.zomi: Gal hun sungin a muhte Pu upa in a gelh ngei hiam?

records.english: My family still tells the story of the day the railway reached our town.
records.zomi: Meileng lampi i khua a tun ni tangthu ka innkuan in tu dong a gen lai uh hi.

records.english: Grandma, what was happening in the country the year you got married?
records.zomi: Pi, na kiten kum in gam sungah bang a piang hiam?

records.english: My family's history is a small part of the history of our whole nation.
records.zomi: Ka innkuan tangthu pen i gam bup' tangthu sung-a a neu khat ahi hi.

records.english: Every year on Independence Day, my grandfather tells us what that first celebration was like.
records.zomi: Kum simin Gam Suahtakna Ni ciangin ka pu in a lawm masakpen bangci om hiam hong gen hi.

records.english: Some events are too painful for my grandparents to talk about, and we respect that.
records.zomi: Thupiang pawl khat ka pu leh pi in gen dingin a na lua a, tua i zahtak uh hi.

records.english: Because my grandparents lived through hard times, they never waste food.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh pi in hun haksa a thuak uh ahih manin an a paikhia ngei kei uh hi.

records.english: Dad cried when he found his old school in a photograph taken after the bombing.
records.zomi: Bomb puak khit-a kila lim khat ah a sang lui a muh ciangin Pa a kap hi.

records.english: My mother still keeps the letter her brother sent from the front line.
records.zomi: Ka nu in a sanggam pasal in galdona mun pan a khak lai tu dong a kem lai hi.

records.english: Our grandfather says the arrival of electricity was the biggest event of his childhood.
records.zomi: Meivak a tun pen a naupan lai-a thupiang lian pen ahi hi, ci-in i pu in a gen hi.

records.english: The more I learn about my family's past, the better I understand my parents.
records.zomi: Ka innkuan' a beisa thu ka sin tam semsem ciangin ka nu leh ka pa ka thei zaw semsem hi.

records.english: When you said Auntie was upset, did you find out why?
records.zomi: Ni a lungkham hi, na cih ciangin bang hang hiam na thei hiam?

records.english: I think it's about the wedding plans.
records.zomi: Mopawi bawl ding thu hi ding hi, ka ci hi.

records.english: Grandma loves it when we ask more questions about her childhood stories.
records.zomi: A naupan lai tangthu tungtang dotna tam zaw i dot ciangin Pi a nuam mahmah hi.

records.english: Mum, you said we might visit Grandpa this weekend; have you decided yet?
records.zomi: Nu, hih kal tawp ciangin Pu i veh kha ding hi, na ci a; na khensat ta hiam?

records.english: Yes, we'll go on Saturday after lunch.
records.zomi: Khensat ing, Kiginni sun an khit ciangin i pai ding hi.

records.english: Did you ask your sister what she meant by that comment?
records.zomi: Tua thu a gen bang a ci nuam hiam na u numei na dong hiam?

records.english: What did Grandma mean when she said the house would need to be sold?
records.zomi: Inn kizuak kul ding hi, Pi a cih ciangin bang a ci nuam hiam?

records.english: She means it's too big for her now, and she wants something smaller.
records.zomi: Tu-in amah adingin a lian lua a, a neu zaw khat a deih hi, a ci nuam hi.

records.english: Did your cousin say why she didn't come to the party?
records.zomi: Pawi ah bang hangin a hong pai kei hiam na sanggam in a gen hiam?

records.english: She said her son had a fever.
records.zomi: A tapa a lum hi, a ci hi.

records.english: I followed up on my son's vague answer and discovered that he had lost his coat.
records.zomi: Ka tapa' dawnna kician lo ka dot behlap ciangin a puansilh lian a mansuah hi, ka thei hi.

records.english: When Dad says he'll see, it usually means he wants us to ask again later.
records.zomi: Pa in ka en ding hi, a cih ciangin a nung ciangin i dong kik ding a deih hi, a ci nuam zel hi.

records.english: You mentioned money worries; is there anything we can do to help?
records.zomi: Sum lungkhamna na gen hi; i huh theih ding bangmah a om hiam?

records.english: Thank you, but I think we'll manage if we're careful.
records.zomi: Ka lungdam hi, ahi zongin i kidawm leh i zo ding hi, ka ci hi.

records.english: When my wife says nothing is wrong, I give her time and then ask again later.
records.zomi: Ka zi in bangmah a om kei hi, a cih ciangin hun ka pia a, a nung ciangin ka dong kik hi.

records.english: Asking a follow-up question at dinner can turn a quiet meal into a real conversation.
records.zomi: Nitak an ne laitakin dotna behlap khat in an nekna dai khat kihopihna taktak ah a khel thei hi.

records.english: When Grandpa gives a short answer, it's worth asking a gentle second question.
records.zomi: Pu in a tom takin a dawn ciangin dotna nihna nem takin dot a kilawm hi.

records.english: You mentioned a problem at school last week; is it any better?
records.zomi: Kal bei-in sang ah buaina khat na gen hi; a hoih zaw ta hiam?

records.english: A bit, because the teacher moved me to a different table.
records.zomi: Tawmno, saya in dawhkan dang khat ah hong koih ahih manin.

records.english: Asking a second question shows my teenager that I was really listening the first time.
records.zomi: Dotna nihna dot in a masa pen-in ka ngaikhia taktak hi, ci-in ka tangval-tangnu kiangah a lak hi.

records.english: What did you mean when you said you were thinking of leaving?
records.zomi: Pai ding ka ngaihsun hi, na cih ciangin bang na ci nuam hiam?

records.english: Only that I'd like to try living in the city for a year.
records.zomi: Kum khat sung khuapi ah teng sak ka nuam hi, ci bek ka ci nuam hi.

records.english: Following up on a relative's answer can reveal a worry they were too shy to mention.
records.zomi: Sanggam khat' dawnna dot behlap in gen dingin a zak lua lungkhamna khat a lak thei hi.

records.english: My mother always remembers what I told her the week before and asks how it ended.
records.zomi: Ka nu in kal bei-a ka gen a phawk tawntung a, bangci a bei hiam a dong hi.

records.english: And what did your teacher say about the drawing?
records.zomi: Tua ciangin lim gelh tungtang na saya in bang a ci hiam?

records.english: She said it was the best in the class.
records.zomi: Khan sung-a a hoih pen ahi hi, a ci hi.

records.english: You said the dinner went well, but did your parents like him?
records.zomi: Nitak an a hoih hi, na ci a, ahi zongin na nu leh na pa in amah a uk uh hiam?

records.english: They did, especially when he offered to wash the dishes.
records.zomi: A uk uh hi, a hoih pen-in kuang a sil sak ding a cih ciangin.

records.english: Mum, you never told me what the doctor said about your knee.
records.zomi: Nu, na khuk tungtang siavuan in bang a gen hiam hong gen ngei kei hi.

records.english: So in the end, who is going to look after Grandma's garden?
records.zomi: Tua ahih leh a tawpna-ah Pi' huan kua in a kem ding hiam?

records.english: When my parents answer a question with a story, I often ask how the story ends.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in dotna khat tangthu tawh a dawn uh ciangin a tangthu bangci a bei hiam ka dong zel hi.

records.english: What happened after you told your boss you wanted a day off?
records.zomi: Ni khat tawlngak ka deih hi, ci-in na makaipa na gen khit ciangin bang a piang hiam?

records.english: Earlier you said you might change schools; are you serious?
records.zomi: A ma-in sang na kheel kha ding hi, na ci hi; na ngaihsut taktak hiam?

records.english: Yes, because the other school offers the science course I want.
records.zomi: Ngaihsun taktak ing, sang dang in ka deih science sinna a pia ahih manin.

records.english: You said you'd met someone at work; what's he like?
records.zomi: Nasep mun ah mi khat na mu hi, na ci a; bangci mi hiam?

records.english: His name is Thang, and he works in the accounts department.
records.zomi: A min Thang hi a, accounts department ah na a sem hi.

records.english: My husband always asks me a follow-up question when I tell him about my day.
records.zomi: Ka ni sung thu ka gen ciangin ka pasal in dotna behlap khat hong dong tawntung hi.

records.english: Following up on a child's answer shows them that what they say really matters to you.
records.zomi: Naupang khat' dawnna dot behlap in a gen uh na adingin a thupi taktak hi, ci-in a lak hi.

records.english: So when you said fine, did you mean good or just okay?
records.zomi: Tua ahih leh a hoih hi, na cih ciangin a hoih mahmah, a ci nuam hiam, a pha deuh bek a ci nuam hiam?

records.english: Earlier you said the doctor was pleased; what exactly did she tell you?
records.zomi: A ma-in siavuan a lungdam hi, na ci a; bang taktak hong gen hiam?

records.english: That my blood pressure is lower and I can reduce the tablets.
records.zomi: Ka sisan nek a niam zaw a, damdawi ka kiamsak thei hi, a ci hi.

records.english: You told me you were fine yesterday; why are you crying now?
records.zomi: Zanni-in ka hoih hi, hong ci hi; bang hangin tu-in na kap hiam?

records.english: Because I've just heard that my friend is moving away.
records.zomi: Ka lawm khat a pem ding thu tu-in ka zak manin.

records.english: Dad, have you decided about the bike yet?
records.zomi: Pa, siiksakol tungtang na khensat ta hiam?

records.english: I asked my father to explain his answer, because I didn't understand why he'd said no.
records.zomi: Bang hangin hi lo, a cih hiam ka theih loh manin ka pa a dawnna genteh dingin ka ngen hi.

records.english: Did the bank give you the loan in the end?
records.zomi: A tawpna-ah bank in leiba hong pia hiam?

records.english: Not yet, because they need more documents.
records.zomi: Hong pia nai kei, lai behlap a kisam uh ahih manin.

records.english: My grandmother often answers one question with another, so I've learned to be patient.
records.zomi: Ka pi in dotna khat dotna dang tawh a dawn zel ahih manin thuakzawh ka sin hi.

records.english: When my son answers with one word, I ask him to tell me one thing that happened.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in kammal khat tawh a dawn ciangin a piang na khat hong gen dingin ka ngen hi.

records.english: Following up gently, rather than pressing, helps children open up about difficult things.
records.zomi: Nawh lo-in nem takin dot behlap in naupangte haksa thute tungtang a gen theih nadingun a huh hi.

records.english: I should have asked my grandfather more questions when he first started talking about the war.
records.zomi: Ka pu in gal thu a gen masak ciangin dotna tam zaw ka dong le ka cih hi.

records.english: I followed up on my daughter's answer because I could tell she wasn't telling me everything.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in na khempeuh hong gen kei hi, ka theih manin a dawnna ka dot behlap hi.

records.english: You said the baby slept badly; what time did she finally settle?
records.zomi: Naungek a ihmut a hoih kei hi, na ci a; bang hun-in a tawpna-ah a ip hiam?

records.english: Around three in the morning, after a bottle.
records.zomi: Zingkal nai thum kiim, nawi bel khat khit ciangin.

records.english: You told me you'd found a flat; when can you move in?
records.zomi: Inn khat na mu hi, hong ci a; bang hun-in na lut thei ding hiam?

records.english: At the start of next month.
records.zomi: A zom kha kipat ciangin.

records.english: A teenager's short answer is not always a closed door; sometimes it is an invitation to ask more.
records.zomi: Tangval-tangnu khat' dawnna tom pen kongkhak kikhak hi tawntung kei a; a hun deuh ciangin dot behlap dingin sapna ahi hi.

records.english: Asking a follow-up question at the right moment can stop a small misunderstanding from becoming a family quarrel.
records.zomi: Hun kilawm ah dotna behlap khat dot in kithei kholhna neu khat innkuan kiselna ah a kikheel loh nadingin a dal thei hi.

records.english: You told the children you'd think about a puppy; what have you decided?
records.zomi: Ui no tungtang ka ngaihsun ding hi, ci-in naupangte na gen hi; bang na khensat hiam?

records.english: We'll wait until the youngest is a little older.
records.zomi: A naupang pen a lian deuh dong i ngak ding hi.

records.english: Do you have the original document or only a photocopy?
records.zomi: A bul lai na nei hiam, photocopy bek na nei hiam?

records.english: Please state your relationship to the patient in the space provided.
records.zomi: Natpa tawh na kizopna a kipiak mun ah gelh in.

records.english: When my parents married, their union was registered at the district office.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa a kiteng uh ciangin a kitenna uh district office ah kigelh hi.

records.english: Please list your siblings in order of age.
records.zomi: Na sanggamte a kum zui-in gelh in.

records.english: I am writing to confirm that Mr. Lian is my nephew and lives at the same address.
records.zomi: Pu Lian ka tanau ahi a, inn kibang mah ah a teng hi, ci-in ka gelh hi.

records.english: Please attach a certified copy of your child's birth certificate.
records.zomi: Na naupang' suahna lai copy kipsak khat behlap in.

records.english: The lawyer read the will aloud to the whole family.
records.zomi: Lawyer in innkuan bup kiangah gamluah lai aw ngaih takin a sim hi.

records.english: Please sign here to confirm that you are the child's mother.
records.zomi: Naupang' nu na hihna kipsak nadingin hih mun ah na min gelh in.

records.english: My uncle signed as a witness at my sister's wedding.
records.zomi: Ka u numei' mopawi ah ka pa neu in theihpihtu-in a min a gelh hi.

records.english: Are you the parent or the guardian of this student?
records.zomi: Hih sangnaupang' nu hiam pa na hi hiam, a kemtu na hi hiam?

records.english: Applicants must list all members of their household, including dependent children.
records.zomi: Ngetnate in a innkuan sung mi khempeuh, amaute tungah kinga naupangte tel in, a gelh ding uh hi.

records.english: Our family's land is registered in my mother's name.
records.zomi: I innkuan' gam ka nu' min tawh kigelh hi.

records.english: A family register records every birth, marriage and death in a household.
records.zomi: Innkuan min bu in inn khat sung-a suahna, kitenna leh sihna khempeuh a ciamteh hi.

records.english: I would be grateful if you could confirm my mother's date of birth from your records.
records.zomi: Na ciamtehna pan ka nu' suahni na kipsak thei le ka lungdam ding hi.

records.english: Is your mother's maiden name required on this application?
records.zomi: Hih ngetna ah na nu' a kiten ma-a innkuan min a kisam hiam?

records.english: The family court will decide which parent the children will live with.
records.zomi: Innkuan thukhenna in naupangte nu hiam pa kua tawh a teng ding uh hiam a khensat ding hi.

records.english: Some families still expect a formal letter when a young man asks permission to marry.
records.zomi: Tangval khangno khat in nupi neih ding phalna a nget ciangin innkuan pawl khat in lai kizahtak khat tu dong a lamen lai uh hi.

records.english: I hereby confirm that the information about my family is true and complete.
records.zomi: Ka innkuan tungtang thute a dik a, a kicing hi, ci-in hih tawh ka kipsak hi.

records.english: The family tree was submitted as supporting evidence for the inheritance claim.
records.zomi: Gamluah ngetna a kip nadingin innkuan khangthu lim kipia hi.

records.english: My grandmother's will divides the house equally between her three children.
records.zomi: Ka pi' gamluah lai in inn a tate thum kiangah kibang takin a hawm hi.

records.english: The registrar recorded the names of the bride's and groom's parents in the marriage register.
records.zomi: Min gelhtu in mopawi min bu ah mo leh mopa' nu leh pate min a gelh hi.

records.english: My grandparents' marriage was never officially registered, which caused problems later.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh pi' kitenna kumpi ah kigelh ngei lo ahih manin a nung ciangin buaina a piang hi.

records.english: My cousin is sponsoring her elderly parents for a family visa.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam in a nu leh a pa upate innkuan visa adingin a huh hi.

records.english: Our solicitor advised us to update our wills after the birth of our second child.
records.zomi: I tate nihna a suah khit ciangin i gamluah laite bawl thak dingin i lawyer in hong gen hi.

records.english: The bank asked me to bring a death certificate before closing my father's account.
records.zomi: Ka pa' bank account ka khak ma-in sihna lai tawi dingin bank in hong ngen hi.

records.english: Who is the registered owner of the family home?
records.zomi: Innkuan inn a neitu-in kigelh kua hiam?

records.english: May I ask what your relationship is to the deceased?
records.zomi: A si mi tawh na kizopna bang hiam ka dong thei ding hiam?

records.english: The census asks how each person in the household is related to the head of the household.
records.zomi: Mi simna in inn sung-a mi khatciat innkuan lu tawh bangci kizom hiam a dong hi.

records.english: Please write your father's full name, not his nickname.
records.zomi: Na pa' min kicing gelh in, a min neu hi lo.

records.english: Do I need my parents' marriage certificate for the passport application?
records.zomi: Passport ngetna adingin ka nu leh ka pa' kitenna lai ka kisam hiam?

records.english: Only if your surname differs from the one on your birth certificate.
records.zomi: Na innkuan min na suahna lai tung-a min tawh a kibat loh leh bek.

records.english: We changed our daughter's surname by deed poll after the adoption.
records.zomi: Ta-a i laak khit ciangin lai kizahtak tawh i tanu' innkuan min i kheel hi.

records.english: Can a grandparent apply for custody?
records.zomi: Pu hiam pi khat in naupang kemna nget thei hiam?

records.english: Please notify the office of any change in your marital status.
records.zomi: Na kitenna dinmun a kikheel leh office kiangah gen in.

records.english: I am writing on behalf of my late husband's family.
records.zomi: Ka pasal si' innkuan aiah ka gelh hi.

records.english: Next of kin: Mrs. Ciin Mang, sister.
records.zomi: A naih pen sanggam: Nu Ciin Mang, u numei.

records.english: Twins must each have their own passport.
records.zomi: Apengte in passport amau tuam ciat a nei ding uh hi.

records.english: My parents' names are printed on the back of my identity card.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa' min ka identity card nung lam ah kikhen hi.

records.english: Proof of family relationship is required for all visa applications in this category.
records.zomi: Hih pawl sung-a visa ngetna khempeuh adingin innkuan kizopna kipsakna a kisam hi.

records.english: The court appointed my aunt as the children's legal guardian.
records.zomi: Thukhenna in ka ni naupangte' kemtu-in a seh hi.

records.english: Please bring both of your parents to sign the enrolment form.
records.zomi: Sang lutna lai min gelh dingin na nu leh na pa a nih in paipih in.

records.english: Children under sixteen must be accompanied by a parent or legal guardian.
records.zomi: Kum sawm leh guk nuai naupangte in nu hiam pa hiam kemtu khat a zui ding uh hi.

records.english: Who is authorised to collect the child from school?
records.zomi: Sang pan naupang la dingin kua phalna a nei hiam?

records.english: The adoption became final when the judge signed the order.
records.zomi: Thukhenpa in thupiak lai tungah a min a gelh ciangin ta-a laakna a kicing hi.

records.english: In official documents, my grandfather is listed as the head of the household.
records.zomi: Kumpi laite ah ka pu innkuan lu-in kigelh hi.

records.english: Married couples may submit a joint application.
records.zomi: Kiteng zi leh pasalte in ngetna khat khawm-in a pia thei uh hi.

records.english: The school requires written permission from a parent or guardian for all overnight trips.
records.zomi: Zan lum khualzinna khempeuh adingin nu hiam pa hiam kemtu' phalna lai sang in a ngen hi.

records.english: Please indicate whether you are single, married, divorced or widowed.
records.zomi: Kiteng nai lo, kiteng, kikhen hiam meigong na hi hiam lak in.

records.english: Can my brother sign the consent form on my behalf?
records.zomi: Ka nau pasal in phalna lai tungah ka aiah min a gelh thei hiam?

records.english: Only if he holds a legal power of attorney for you.
records.zomi: Na aiah thu khensat theihna lai kizahtak a neih leh bek.

records.english: Under the law of some countries, a spouse automatically inherits part of the estate.
records.zomi: Gam pawl khat' thukham bangin kiteng pa hiam nu in gou pawl khat amah mah-in a luah hi.

records.english: A guardian may make medical decisions for a child when the parents are unavailable.
records.zomi: Nu leh pa a om theih loh ciangin kemtu khat in naupang khat adingin damdawi thu a khensat thei hi.

records.english: Each dependant listed on the application must have a valid identity document.
records.zomi: Ngetna ah kigelh tungah kinga mi khatciat in identity lai zat theih khat a nei ding hi.

records.english: Do stepchildren count as dependants for tax purposes?
records.zomi: Siah thu-ah pakik hiam nukik' tate in tungah kinga mi bangin kisim uh hiam?

records.english: A sworn statement from a family member may be accepted in place of a missing birth certificate.
records.zomi: Suahna lai a man ciangin innkuan mi khat' kiciamna tawh thu gen khat a mun ah kipom thei hi.

records.english: I attach copies of our children's birth certificates for your records.
records.zomi: Na ciamtehna adingin i tate' suahna lai copy ka behlap hi.

records.english: Full name of father, as it appears on official documents.
records.zomi: Pa' min kicing, kumpi laite tunga a kigelh bangin.

records.english: The embassy requested proof that my wife and I are legally married.
records.zomi: Ka zi leh kei thukham bangin i kiteng uh hi, cih kipsakna embassy in a ngen hi.

records.english: The judge asked the child, in private, which parent she wished to live with.
records.zomi: Thukhenpa in naupang, amah kia-in, nu hiam pa kua tawh teng a deih hiam a dong hi.

records.english: After the divorce, the court gave both parents equal responsibility for the children.
records.zomi: Kikhen khit ciangin thukhenna in nu leh pa a nih in naupangte tungah mawhpuakna kibang a pia hi.

records.english: Dad and I sat in the waiting room while my sister had her examination.
records.zomi: Ka u numei a kisit laitakin Pa leh kei ngakna khan ah i tu uh hi.

records.english: My parents still keep the card from my very first baby examination.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in ka naungek lai-a sitna masa pen card tu dong a kem lai uh hi.

records.english: I held my daughter's hand while the doctor looked in her ears.
records.zomi: Siavuan in ka tanu' bilte a en laitakin a khut ka len hi.

records.english: Where do we keep the folder with the children's examination results?
records.zomi: Naupangte' sitna gahte koihna folder koi ah i koih uh hiam?

records.english: Will Grandpa have to take his shirt off for the check-up?
records.zomi: Damna sitna adingin Pu in a puan a suah kul ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, so the doctor can listen to his chest properly.
records.zomi: Kul ding hi, siavuan in a awm hoih takin a ngaihkhiat theih nadingin.

records.english: Do you want me to tell the doctor about your headaches, or will you?
records.zomi: Na lu natna siavuan kiangah kei in ka gen ding na deih hiam, nangmah in na gen ding hiam?

records.english: Please don't let go of my hand while they take the blood.
records.zomi: Sisan a lak laitakun ka khut hong khah kei in.

records.english: Mum insisted that I go for a full examination after my fortieth birthday.
records.zomi: Ka kum sawmli suahni khit ciangin sitna kicing khat ah pai dingin nu in hong nawh hi.

records.english: Our son was proud to tell his grandmother that he'd been examined like a grown-up.
records.zomi: Mi lian bangin kisit hi, ci-in a pi kiangah gen dingin i tapa a kisaktheih hi.

records.english: The doctor examined both of our twins at the same time, one on each knee.
records.zomi: Siavuan in i apengte a nih hun kibang-in a sit a, khat khuk khatciat tungah a tu uh hi.

records.english: Auntie Niang cried with relief when the scan showed nothing wrong.
records.zomi: Scan in bangmah a sia om lo a lak ciangin Ni Niang a lungdam mahmah ahih manin a kap hi.

records.english: Shall I come with you for the scan tomorrow?
records.zomi: Zingciang scan adingin kong zui ding hiam?

records.english: Our family doctor examines the children quickly because she knows them so well.
records.zomi: I innkuan siavuan in naupangte a thei mahmah ahih manin manlang takin a sit hi.

records.english: Can I stay in the room while they examine my son?
records.zomi: Ka tapa a sit laitakun khan sungah ka om thei ding hiam?

records.english: A family medical history helps the doctor decide which examinations each of us needs.
records.zomi: Innkuan damna tangthu in i khatciat bang sitna i kisam hiam siavuan in a khensat theih nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Why does Grandpa always want to know every number the doctor writes down?
records.zomi: Bang hangin siavuan' gelh nambat khempeuh Pu in a theih nop tawntung hiam?

records.english: After the examination, Grandpa said he felt ten years younger.
records.zomi: Sitna khit ciangin kum sawm in ka khangno zaw hi, ka ci a sa hi, ci-in Pu in a gen hi.

records.english: I was relieved when the nurse said my son's height and weight were normal for his age.
records.zomi: Ka tapa' a sanna leh a gikna a kum adingin a pha hi, ci-in nurse in a gen ciangin ka lungmuang hi.

records.english: Grandma, the doctor just needs to press gently on your tummy.
records.zomi: Pi, siavuan in na gil nem takin a nen bek ding hi.

records.english: When our baby was six weeks old, we took her for her first proper examination.
records.zomi: I naungek kal guk a phak ciangin a sitna taktak masa pen adingin i paipih uh hi.

records.english: The doctor checked her hips, her heartbeat and the way she followed a toy with her eyes.
records.zomi: Siavuan in a khuh guh, a lungtang tawk leh a mit tawh a lawhna van a zui na a en hi.

records.english: We both relaxed when he smiled and said she was doing beautifully.
records.zomi: A nuih a, a hoih mahmah hi, a cih ciangin i nih in i lungmuang uh hi.

records.english: My brother finally agreed to have his heart checked after our father's illness.
records.zomi: I pa' natna khit ciangin ka nau pasal in a lungtang sit dingin a tawpna-ah a pom hi.

records.english: Mum, will the doctor look in my throat again?
records.zomi: Nu, siavuan in ka ngawng sung a en kik ding hiam?

records.english: My husband was embarrassed when the doctor asked him to undress, so I waited outside.
records.zomi: Siavuan in puan suah dingin a nget ciangin ka pasal a zum ahih manin pualam ah ka ngak hi.

records.english: After his examination, my father finally agreed to stop smoking.
records.zomi: A sitna khit ciangin ka pa in a tawpna-ah meizial dawn nusia dingin a pom hi.

records.english: My grandmother refuses to have any examination unless my aunt is there with her.
records.zomi: Ka ni amah tawh a om kei leh ka pi in sitna bangmah a pom kei hi.

records.english: I always tell the children exactly what the doctor will do, so there are no surprises.
records.zomi: Lamdang sakna a om loh nadingin siavuan in bang a bawl ding hiam naupangte kiangah kician takin ka gen tawntung hi.

records.english: Because heart problems run in our family, my doctor examines me every year.
records.zomi: I innkuan ah lungtang natna a om ahih manin ka siavuan in kum simin hong sit hi.

records.english: The doctor weighed my little sister on a scale shaped like a big plastic boat.
records.zomi: Siavuan in ka nau numei tembaw lian plastic lim gikna tehna tungah a gikna a teh hi.

records.english: Dad pretends he isn't nervous before an examination, but he always taps his foot.
records.zomi: Sitna ma-in Pa a lau kei hi, ci-in a kibawl a, ahi zongin a khe a bengbeng tawntung hi.

records.english: My daughter's hearing test was a game where she dropped a block every time she heard a beep.
records.zomi: Ka tanu' bil za sitna pen beep a zak simin bawm neu khat a khiat ding lawhna khat ahi hi.

records.english: The doctor let my daughter listen to her own heartbeat.
records.zomi: Siavuan in ka tanu amah mah' lungtang tawk a ngaikhia sak hi.

records.english: Why did the doctor tap my knee with a little hammer?
records.zomi: Bang hangin siavuan in sekdeng neu khat tawh ka khuk a bengbeng hiam?

records.english: To check that your nerves and muscles are working properly.
records.zomi: Na guizangte leh na tha te a sem hoih hiam en nadingin.

records.english: Since my mother's examination showed high cholesterol, the whole family has been eating less fried food.
records.zomi: Ka nu' sitna in cholesterol a sang hi, a lak khit pan innkuan bup in an kikang tawm zaw i ne uh hi.

records.english: I bribed my brother with ice cream to get him to the dentist's check-up.
records.zomi: Ka nau pasal ha siavuan' damna sitna ah a pai nadingin ice cream tawh ka khem hi.

records.english: Taking a relative to a medical examination is a small way of showing that you care.
records.zomi: Sanggam khat damdawi sitna ah paipih pen na deihsakna lahna neu khat ahi hi.

records.english: My grandfather joked with the nurse the whole time she was measuring his blood pressure.
records.zomi: Nurse in a sisan nek a teh sung bup ka pu in amah tawh a kipaih hi.

records.english: Could you explain to my father why the examination is necessary?
records.zomi: Bang hangin sitna a kisam hiam ka pa kiangah na genteh thei ding hiam?

records.english: My parents encourage each other to go for regular check-ups.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in ciangtan-a damna sitna ah pai dingin a kihanthawn uh hi.

records.english: Our son was so brave during his first eye test that the optician gave him a sticker.
records.zomi: I tapa a mit sitna masa pen ah a hangsan mahmah ahih manin mit siavuan in sticker khat a pia hi.

records.english: Children often behave better at examinations when they have practised with a toy doctor's kit at home.
records.zomi: Inn ah siavuan van lawhna tawh a kisin uh ciangin naupangte sitna ah a om hoih zaw uh hi.

records.english: Is it normal for a toddler to cry through the whole examination?
records.zomi: Naupang neu khat sitna sung bup a kap a pha hiam?

records.english: Very normal, and it doesn't stop us checking what we need to.
records.zomi: A pha mahmah hi, a kisam i sit dal kei hi.

records.english: When parents stay calm during an examination, their children usually stay calm too.
records.zomi: Sitna sungin nu leh pa a lungnem uh ciangin a tate uh zong a lungnem zel uh hi.

records.english: Can we book the children's check-ups for the same afternoon?
records.zomi: Naupangte' damna sitna sun kibang ah i bawl thei ding hiam?

records.english: Our son's eyes were tested twice because he kept guessing the letters.
records.zomi: I tapa in laimal a ngaihsun-in a gen zel ahih manin a mit nihvei kisit hi.

records.english: Seeing my mother so small on the examination table made me realise how much she had aged.
records.zomi: Sitna dawhkan tungah ka nu a neu mahmah ka muh ciangin bangzah a kumpi hiam ka thei hi.

records.english: My wife's pregnancy examinations were the first time I'd seen inside a maternity clinic.
records.zomi: Ka zi' nau pai sitnate pen nau suahna clinic sung ka muh masak pen ahi hi.

records.english: We bring Grandma's glasses and hearing aid to every examination so she can follow what's happening.
records.zomi: Bang a piang hiam Pi in a zui theih nadingin sitna khempeuh ah a mitlimlang leh a bil za van i paipih uh hi.

records.english: Thank you for being so patient with my nervous father.
records.zomi: Ka pa lau thei tungah thuakzawhna na neih manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: We're taking our son for his school medical next Tuesday.
records.zomi: A zom Pithai ni ciangin i tapa sang damna sitna ah i paipih ding uh hi.

records.english: Did they check your blood sugar as well?
records.zomi: Na sisan sungah sugar zong a en uh hiam?

records.english: Having my teenage daughter examined without me in the room was hard, but I knew it was right.
records.zomi: Ka tanu tangnu kei om lo-in khan sungah kisit pen a haksa a, ahi zongin a dik hi, ka thei hi.

records.english: It's your turn now, darling; the doctor will be very gentle.
records.zomi: Tu-in nang' hun hi, ka it; siavuan in nem mahmah takin hong bawl ding hi.

records.english: Did the doctor find anything during Mum's check-up?
records.zomi: Nu' damna sitna ah siavuan in bangmah a mu hiam?

records.english: Nothing serious, just a slightly low iron level.
records.zomi: A gik bangmah om lo, sisan sung sik tawmno a niam bek.

records.english: Our whole family went for health checks on the same day, so we could support each other.
records.zomi: I khat leh khat i kihuh theih nadingin innkuan bup ni kibang ah damna sitna ah i pai uh hi.

records.english: Grandma still talks about the year she won first prize for her pickles.
records.zomi: A anteh khawi tawh nambat khat a ngah kum thu Pi in tu dong a gen lai hi.

records.english: Shall we take the children to the book festival again this autumn?
records.zomi: Hih kumphal ciangin naupangte laibu pawi ah i paipih kik ding hiam?

records.english: My brothers and I used to sell lemonade to the crowds at the town fair.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasalte leh kei in khua pawi lian ah mipite kiangah lemonade i zuak zel uh hi.

records.english: Do you remember the year it rained on the whole parade?
records.zomi: Lampi pai pawi bup tungah guah a zuk kum na phawk hiam?

records.english: My parents still hold hands during the fireworks every New Year.
records.zomi: Kum Thak simin meipiak puakte laitakin ka nu leh ka pa a khut uh a kilen lai uh hi.

records.english: My wife made a quilt for the craft show with patches from the children's old clothes.
records.zomi: Ka zi in khutsiam lahna adingin naupangte' puan lui ponte tawh puanzal khat a bawl hi.

records.english: What do you want to dress up as for the costume parade?
records.zomi: Puan tuam silh lampi pai pawi ah bang bangin silh na deih hiam?

records.english: When my uncle came home after many years abroad, the whole village held a celebration for him.

records.english: Our grandparents met at a summer dance in the village hall more than fifty years ago.

records.english: My grandparents still enter the dancing competition, although they never win.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh ka pi in a zo ngei kei uh hangin lamna kidemna ah a lut lai uh hi.

records.english: Is there a family discount for the summer festival tickets?
