records.english: Why does Grandpa always cry at the remembrance service?
records.zomi: Bang hangin phawkna pawi ah Pu a kap tawntung hiam?

records.english: Because he lost his best friend in the war, and he thinks of him every year.
records.zomi: Gal sungah a lawm hoih pen a sih manin kum simin amah a ngaihsun hi.

records.english: Watching my daughter perform at the festival made me remember my own first performance.
records.zomi: Pawi ah ka tanu a lam a muh ciangin keimah' lamna masa pen ka phawk hi.

records.english: This year we were asked to light the candles at the opening of the festival.
records.zomi: Hih kum in pawi kihonna ah khawimeivaak te tak dingin hong ngen uh hi.

records.english: The village fete was where my daughter learned to ride a pony.
records.zomi: Khua pawi pen ka tanu in sakol neu tuang a sinna mun ahi hi.

records.english: Our family has marched in the independence parade every year since I was born.
records.zomi: Ka suah pan kipan kum simin i innkuan in gam suahtakna lampi pai pawi ah a pai uh hi.

records.english: My mother has kept every programme from every concert I've played in.
records.zomi: Ka nu in ka tumna la sakna khempeuh-a programme khempeuh a kem hi.

records.english: My brother organised the first football tournament our street had ever had.
records.zomi: Ka nau pasal in i lampi in a neih ngeih loh football kidemna masa pen a bawl hi.

records.english: The village festival is a good chance to introduce the children to relatives they rarely see.
records.zomi: Khua pawi in naupangte a muh tawm sanggamte tawh kitheisak ding hun hoih khat ahi hi.

records.english: We missed the carnival this year because my mother was in hospital.
records.zomi: Ka nu damdawi inn ah a om ahih manin hih kum carnival ah i pai kei uh hi.

records.english: Our family has had a stall at the harvest fair for three generations.
records.zomi: I innkuan in khang thum sung buh lak pawi lian ah van zuakna mun khat a nei uh hi.

records.english: Grandpa taught all of us the traditional dance for the harvest festival.
records.zomi: Buh lak pawi adingin Pu in i khempeuh kiangah ngeina lamna hong sinsak hi.

records.english: Can I go to the youth concert with my cousins on Friday?
records.zomi: Laithai ni ciangin ka sanggamte tawh khangnote la sakna ah ka pai thei ding hiam?

records.english: Who's looking after the baby while we're at the fair?
records.zomi: Pawi lian ah i om laitakin naungek kua in a cing ding hiam?

records.english: Your aunt offered, so we can stay as long as we like.
records.zomi: Na ni in a cing ding a ci ahih manin i deih sung i om thei uh hi.

records.english: Auntie Dim has run the cake stall at the church fair for as long as anyone can remember.
records.zomi: Ni Dim in kuamah' phawk theih sung pan pawlpi pawi lian ah cake zuakna mun a kem hi.

records.english: Thank you for taking the children to the fair while I was working.
records.zomi: Na ka sep laitakin naupangte pawi lian ah na paipih manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: Let's take Grandpa to the music festival this year; he'd love it.
records.zomi: Hih kum Pu la pawi ah i paipih ni; a nuam sa mahmah ding hi.

records.english: We always walk to the New Year celebrations as a family, even when it's cold.
records.zomi: A vot zongin innkuan bup in Kum Thak pawi ah peel-in i pai tawntung uh hi.

records.english: Mum makes us new clothes every year for the community dance.
records.zomi: Mipi lamna adingin kum simin Nu in puan thak hong bawl sak hi.

records.english: My husband and I first danced together at a charity ball.
records.zomi: Ka pasal leh kei mi huhna pawi lamna ah a masa pen-in i kilam khawm uh hi.

records.english: Our youngest was so excited about the lantern parade that he made his lantern a week early.
records.zomi: I tate a neu pen in khawimeivaak lampi pai pawi a lunggulh lua ahih manin a khawimeivaak kal khat ma-in a bawl hi.

records.english: My parents met many of their closest friends through the community choir.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in a lawm naihpente uh mipi la sa pawl tungtawn-in a kimu uh hi.

records.english: Dad, what was the festival like when you were a boy?
records.zomi: Pa, na naupan lai-in pawi bangci om hiam?

records.english: Going to the same community events every year gives our family a sense of belonging.
records.zomi: Kum simin mipi pawi kibang ah pai in i innkuan in kua i hi hiam theihna hong pia hi.

records.english: Did you see Dad dancing at the wedding party in the square?
records.zomi: Mun lian-a mopawi ah Pa a lam na mu hiam?

records.english: I lost my little brother in the crowd at the carnival, and we found him at the ice-cream van.
records.zomi: Carnival-a mipi lak ah ka nau pasal neu ka mansuah a, ice cream mawtaw kiang ah i mu uh hi.

records.english: My sister and I sang together in the town choir at the spring concert.
records.zomi: Spring la sakna ah ka u numei leh kei khua la sa pawl ah i sa khawm uh hi.

records.english: Community events are where my children learned to talk confidently to adults.
records.zomi: Mipi pawite pen ka tate in mi upate tawh hangsan taka kihopih a sinna mun ahi hi.

records.english: Our teenagers pretend to be bored at village events, but they always stay late.
records.zomi: I tangval-tangnute in khua pawi ah a lungkhamsak kibawl uh a, ahi zongin a nung dong a om tawntung uh hi.

records.english: We stayed until the very last song, and the children fell asleep in the car.
records.zomi: La nunung pen dong i om uh a, naupangte mawtaw sungah a ihmu uh hi.

records.english: My little sister's first time on stage was at the village talent show.
records.zomi: Ka nau numei' lamna mun tung a kah masak pen khua thiamna lahna pawi ahi hi.

records.english: Are we going to the village sports day this year, Dad?
records.zomi: Pa, hih kum khua tai kidemna ni ah i pai ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, and I've entered us both in the father-and-son race.
records.zomi: Pai ding hi, pa leh tapa tai kidemna ah i nih in kong gelh khin hi.

records.english: Every family in our village brings one dish to the end-of-year feast.
records.zomi: I khua-a innkuan khatciat in kum tawp ankuang ah an khat ciat a paipih uh hi.

records.english: At last year's village festival, Dad volunteered to cook for everyone.
records.zomi: Kum bei-a khua pawi ah Pa in mi khempeuh adingin an huan dingin amah mah a kipia hi.

records.english: He made three huge pots of rice and curry, and we children served the queue.
records.zomi: Beel lian thum ah an leh hin a huan a, naupangte in a kizom-a ngak mite an i hawm uh hi.

records.english: By the end of the evening he was exhausted, but he said it was the best day of his year.
records.zomi: Nitak tawp ciangin a gim mahmah hi, ahi zongin ka kum sungah ni hoih pen ahi hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Each year, my grandmother tells the same story about the festival before electricity came to the village.
records.zomi: Kum simin ka pi in meivak khua a tun ma-a pawi thu kibang mah a gen hi.

records.english: Our children have performed in every school and village show since they were tiny.
records.zomi: I tate a neu lai pan sang leh khua lahna pawi khempeuh ah a lam uh hi.

records.english: The community picnic is the only day of the year when all my relatives are in one place.
records.zomi: Mipi gam pai an nekna pen ka sanggamte khempeuh mun khat ah a om khawm kum sung ni khat bek ahi hi.

records.english: Our photo albums are full of pictures from local festivals.
records.zomi: I lim bute khua pawi pan limte tawh a dim hi.

records.english: When my grandmother was too weak to go to the fair, we brought the fair to her in photos and videos.
records.zomi: Ka pi pawi lian ah pai dingin a thaneem lua ciangin pawi lian lim leh video tawh amah kiangah i paipih uh hi.

records.english: Community events have helped our immigrant family feel at home in a new country.
records.zomi: Mipi pawite in gamdang pan hong pem i innkuan gam thak ah inn bangin a om dingin hong huh hi.

records.english: Shall we invite our new neighbours to come with us to the street party?
records.zomi: I inn veng thakte lampi pawi ah hong zui dingin i sam ding hiam?

records.english: My nephew won the egg-and-spoon race and wouldn't stop talking about it.
records.zomi: Ka tanau in aktui leh keu tai kidemna a zo a, a gen tawp thei kei hi.

records.english: Shall we make a family team for the quiz night?
records.zomi: Quiz zan adingin innkuan pawl khat i bawl ding hiam?

records.english: Are the cousins from the city coming for the boat race again this summer?
records.zomi: Hih khal tembaw kidemna adingin khuapi-a om sanggamte hong pai kik ding uh hiam?

records.english: I remember sitting on my father's shoulders to watch the parade.
records.zomi: Lampi pai pawi en dingin ka pa' liangko tungah ka tut ka phawk hi.

records.english: A spreadsheet is useful for keeping track of household spending.
records.zomi: Inn sung sum zat ciamteh nadingin spreadsheet in a phatuam hi.

records.english: Please put the dates in the first column and the amounts in the second.
records.zomi: Column masa pen ah ni leh kha te koih in, a nihna ah sum zahte koih in.

records.english: The total at the bottom of the column is wrong, so let's check the numbers.
records.zomi: Column nuai-a total a dik kei ahih manin nambatte i en kik ding.

records.english: My grandfather learned to type documents at seventy, and now he writes his own letters.
records.zomi: Ka pu in kum sawmsagih a phak ciangin document type a sin a, tu-in amah mah in a laite a gelh hi.

records.english: Highlight the rows where the payment is late.
records.zomi: Sum piak a nunung row te highlight in.

records.english: I printed the spreadsheet on one page so that it would be easier to read.
records.zomi: Sim a baih zawk nadingin spreadsheet page khat tungah ka print hi.

records.english: Let's put all the contact details into one spreadsheet.
records.zomi: Kizopna thu khempeuh spreadsheet khat sungah i koih ding.

records.english: Comments in the margin let colleagues suggest changes without editing the text itself.
records.zomi: Margin-a comment te in nasep lawmte in a gelh mah bawl lo-in kheelna a gen theih nadingun a huh hi.

records.english: Saving a document as a PDF keeps its layout the same on any computer.
records.zomi: Document PDF-in na save ciangin computer kua ah zong a layout kibang mah-in a om hi.

records.english: I accidentally deleted a whole column, but I pressed undo straight away.
records.zomi: Ka theih kei-in column bup ka delete a, ahi zongin undo ka nen pah hi.

records.english: Please check the document for spelling mistakes before you send it.
records.zomi: Na khak ma-in document ah laimal khialhna en in.

records.english: Can you make the table fit on the screen?
records.zomi: Table screen tungah a kilan nadingin na bawl thei ding hiam?

records.english: I typed my letter in a word processor and printed two copies.
records.zomi: Ka lai word processor ah ka type a, copy nih ka print hi.

records.english: Learning a few keyboard shortcuts can make working with documents much faster.
records.zomi: Keyboard shortcut tawmno sin in document tawh nasep a manlang zaw mahmah sak thei hi.

records.english: Shared documents let several people edit the same file at the same time.
records.zomi: Share document te in mi tampi in file kibang mah hun kibang-in a edit theih nadingun a huh hi.

records.english: Did you remember to share the folder with the whole team?
records.zomi: Folder pawl bup tawh share ding na phawk hiam?

records.english: Typing a small error into a formula can make every total in the spreadsheet wrong.
records.zomi: Formula sungah khialhna neu khat na type leh spreadsheet sung-a total khempeuh a khial thei hi.

records.english: I set the spreadsheet to calculate the average score for each student.
records.zomi: Sangnaupang khatciat' score average a tuat nadingin spreadsheet ka bawl hi.

records.english: If several people edit the same spreadsheet, agree who is responsible for each section.
records.zomi: Mi tampi in spreadsheet kibang mah a edit uh leh section khatciat kua in mawhpuak ding hiam kituak un.

records.english: Do you know how to insert a picture into the document?
records.zomi: Document sungah lim bangci koih ding hiam na thei hiam?

records.english: Spreadsheets are most useful when the data is entered in the same way every time.
records.zomi: Data a kikoih zia kibang den ciangin spreadsheet te a phatuam pen hi.

records.english: I copied the table from the email and pasted it into my report.
records.zomi: Email pan table ka copy a, ka report sungah ka paste hi.

records.english: The chart shows our sales for the last six months.
records.zomi: Chart in kha guk sung-a i van zuak te a lak hi.

records.english: My budget spreadsheet has a column for each month of the year.
records.zomi: Ka sum zat spreadsheet in kum sung kha khatciat adingin column khat ciat a nei hi.

records.english: Click on the cell and type the number.
records.zomi: Cell tungah click in a, nambat type in.

records.english: Save the document before you close it.
records.zomi: Na khak ma-in document save in.

records.english: How do I make the title bigger?
records.zomi: Title bangci a lian zaw sak ding hiam?

records.english: Select the text and choose a larger font size.
records.zomi: Laimalte select in a, font size lian zaw khat teel in.

records.english: Use bold for the headings so that they stand out.
records.zomi: Lutang te a lan nadingin bold zang in.

records.english: A well-organised spreadsheet can save hours of work every week.
records.zomi: Kician taka kibawl spreadsheet in kal simin nai tampi nasep a keng thei hi.

records.english: Oh no, I closed the document without saving my changes.
records.zomi: Ai, ka kheelnate save lo-in document ka khak hi.

records.english: Shall I make the headings a different colour?
records.zomi: Lutangte a rong tuam-in ka bawl ding hiam?

records.english: Printing a draft helps me notice mistakes that I miss on the screen.
records.zomi: Draft khat print in screen tungah ka muh loh khialhnate a mu sak hi.

records.english: This document has too many fonts, which makes it hard to read.
records.zomi: Hih document in font tam lua a nei ahih manin sim a haksa hi.

records.english: A simple template can make every letter you write look neat and consistent.
records.zomi: Template baih khat in na gelh lai khempeuh a siangthou-in a kibang sak thei hi.

records.english: My daughter uses a spreadsheet to plan her revision timetable.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in a sinkik hun ciamteh bawl nadingin spreadsheet a zang hi.

records.english: A clear layout with short paragraphs makes a document much easier to read.
records.zomi: Layout kician leh paragraph tomte in document sim a baih zaw mahmah sak hi.

records.english: Before deleting old files, make sure nobody else still needs them.
records.zomi: File luite na delete ma-in kuamah in a kisam nawn kei hiam en masa in.

records.english: Is there a way to get back an older version of this document?
records.zomi: Hih document' version lui zaw khat ngah kik theihna a om hiam?

records.english: Yes, open the version history and choose the one you want.
records.zomi: Om hi, version history hong a, na deih teel in.

records.english: Why does the cell show a row of hash symbols?
records.zomi: Bang hangin cell in hash limte a lak hiam?

records.english: The column is too narrow, so just make it wider.
records.zomi: Column a zawl lua ahih manin a zai zaw sak bek in.

records.english: When you've finished editing, please send me the final version.
records.zomi: Edit na zawh ciangin final version hong khak in.

records.zomi: File in email dingin a lian lua ahih manin link kong khak ding hi.

records.english: Turn on the tracking feature so that we can see who changed what.
records.zomi: Kua in bang a kheel hiam i muh theih nadingin tracking feature on in.

records.english: Keep a backup copy of important files on another device.
records.zomi: File thupi te backup copy device dang khat ah kem in.

records.english: Could you add page numbers to the document?
records.zomi: Document ah page number na behlap thei ding hiam?

records.english: Freezing the top row keeps the column headings visible while you scroll down.
records.zomi: Row tung pen freeze in scroll na suk laitakin column lutangte a lang den hi.

records.english: Many small businesses still keep all their accounts in a single spreadsheet.
records.zomi: Sumbawlna neu tampi in a sum ciamtehna khempeuh spreadsheet khat sungah a kem lai uh hi.

records.english: The spell checker underlines words it doesn't recognise in red.
records.zomi: Spell checker in a theih loh kammalte a sansan tawh a nuai ah a khang hi.

records.english: You can find the file in the shared folder called Monthly Reports.
records.zomi: File Monthly Reports a kici share folder sungah na mu thei hi.

records.english: Can you send me the file as an attachment?
records.zomi: File attachment-in hong khak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Spreadsheets can sort a long list of names into alphabetical order in seconds.
records.zomi: Spreadsheet in min list sau khat second tawmno sungin laimal zui-in a koih thei hi.

records.zomi: Mi dang in software kibang a neih kei leh file format bang ka zat ding hiam?

records.english: The document is too long, so I'll split it into two parts.
records.zomi: Document a sau lua ahih manin a tuam nih-in ka khen ding hi.

records.english: The spreadsheet adds up the totals automatically.
records.zomi: Spreadsheet in total te amah mah in a kikhawm sak hi.

records.english: I made a simple table to compare the prices of three washing machines.
records.zomi: Puan silna machine thum' man kitehkak nadingin table baih khat ka bawl hi.

records.english: Please don't change the formulas in the yellow cells.
records.zomi: Cell a gialte sung-a formula te kheel kei un.

records.english: We use a shared spreadsheet to plan who brings what to the family picnic.
records.zomi: Innkuan gam pai an nekna ah kua in bang a paipih ding hiam i gelh nadingin share spreadsheet khat i zang uh hi.

records.english: Can you show me how to add a new row in the middle of the table?
records.zomi: Table laizang ah row thak bangci behlap ding hiam hong lak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: How many years passed between Grandpa leaving the village and coming back?
records.zomi: Pu in khua a nusiat leh a ciah kik kikal ah kum bangzah a beisa hiam?

records.english: Do you remember which year we went to the beach for the first time?
records.zomi: Tuipi geiah i pai masak pen kum bang hiam na phawk hiam?

records.english: Can you help me work out how old Great-Grandpa would be today?
records.zomi: Pu upa tu-in a nungta le kum bangzah a phak ding hiam tuat dingin hong huh thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Mum says she got her first phone in the same month she started university.
records.zomi: Sangpi a kah kipat kha mah-in a phone masa pen a ngah hi, Nu in a ci hi.

records.english: Were there mobile phones when you were a child, Mum?
records.zomi: Nu, na naupan lai-in mobile phone a om hiam?

records.english: Which happened first, Uncle Pau's wedding or the big fire in the market?
records.zomi: Pa neu Pau' mopawi leh sumbuk mun-a mei lian kua a piang masa hiam?

records.english: Our son put photos of each family member on a timeline in the order they were born.
records.zomi: I tapa in innkuan mi khatciat' lim a suah zui-in hun kizui lim tungah a koih hi.

records.english: My mother started her shop the same year my youngest brother started school.
records.zomi: Ka nau pasal neu pen sang a kah kipat kum mah-in ka nu in a sumbuk a kipat hi.

records.english: My mother finished her teacher training just before I was born.
records.zomi: Ka suah ma tawmno-in ka nu in saya sinna a zo hi.

records.english: Did Grandpa live in the city before or after he met Grandma?
records.zomi: Pu in Pi a muh ma hiam a muh khit hiam khuapi ah a teng hiam?

records.english: How old was Grandma when the country became independent?
records.zomi: Gam a suahtak ciangin Pi kum bangzah ahi hiam?

records.english: She was about twelve, so she remembers the celebrations clearly.
records.zomi: Kum sawm leh nih bang ahi a, tua ahih manin pawite a phawk kician hi.

records.english: My brother is exactly twenty years younger than our oldest sister.
records.zomi: Ka nau pasal pen i u numei upa pen sangin kum sawmnih taktak a neu zaw hi.

records.english: My grandmother's diary helped us put the family events of the 1970s in the right order.
records.zomi: Ka pi' nitum ciamtehna bu in 1970 kumte-a innkuan thupiangte a kizui dik-in koih dingin hong huh hi.

records.english: My parents can date almost any old photo by the clothes people are wearing.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in mite' puan silh tawh lim lui kimteng a kum a thei uh hi.

records.english: My parents celebrated their silver wedding anniversary the year I finished school.
records.zomi: Ka sang ka zawh kum in ka nu leh ka pa in a kitenna kum sawmnih leh nga a lawm uh hi.

records.english: Dad started school the year the first television arrived in the village.
records.zomi: Khua ah television masa pen a tun kum in Pa sang a kah kipan hi.

records.english: By the time my father was born, his parents had already lived in three different countries.
records.zomi: Ka pa a suah ma-in a nu leh a pa gam tuam thum ah a teng khin uh hi.

records.english: We all laughed when we realised Grandpa was older than the bridge he crosses every day.
records.zomi: Ni simin a kantan lei sangin Pu a upa zaw hi, ci i theih ciangin i khempeuh i nuih uh hi.

records.english: Which of your grandparents is the oldest?
records.zomi: Na pu leh na pite lak ah kua a upa pen hiam?

records.english: When we lined up the old family photos by date, we could see the village changing behind us.
records.zomi: Innkuan lim luite a ni zui-in i koih ciangin i nung-a khua a kikheelzia i mu thei hi.

records.english: Grandma counts the years by her grandchildren's ages.
records.zomi: Pi in a tute' kum tawh kumte a sim hi.

records.english: Were you born before or after Grandpa built the house?
records.zomi: Pu in inn a lam ma-in hiam a lam khit-in hiam na suak hiam?

records.english: Two years after, so I've lived there all my life.
records.zomi: Kum nih khit-in, tua ahih manin ka nuntak sung bup tua ah ka teng hi.

records.english: Each new baby in our family is added to the timeline on the kitchen wall.
records.zomi: I innkuan-a naungek thak khatciat anbuk bang tung-a hun kizui lim ah kibehlap hi.

records.english: My sister and I were both born in the rainy season, two years apart.

records.english: Each generation in our family has left the village a little earlier in life than the one before.

records.english: Working out the order of events in my family's history helped me understand why we moved so often.
records.zomi: Ka innkuan tangthu-a thupiangte a kizui dik-in ka koih ciangin bang hangin i pem zel uh hiam ka thei hi.

records.english: When I put my grandparents' stories in order, some of the dates didn't match.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh pi' tangthute a kizui dik-in ka koih ciangin ni leh kum pawl khat a kituak kei hi.

records.english: Our son was amazed that his grandmother had lived through six different governments.
records.zomi: A pi in kumpi tuam guk nuai ah a nungta hi, ci-in i tapa lamdang a sa mahmah hi.

records.english: Our family left the hills gradually, one household at a time, over about twenty years.
records.zomi: I innkuan kum sawmnih kiim sungin inn khat zawh khat-in mualte a nusia uh hi.

records.english: Our family Bible lists every birth and marriage in order, going back five generations.
records.zomi: I innkuan Laisiangtho in khang nga dong suahna leh kitenna khempeuh a kizui-in a gelh hi.

records.english: We realised that Grandpa had started work at fourteen, the same age my son is now.

records.english: Mum, was I walking yet when we moved into this house?
records.zomi: Nu, hih inn ah i pem ciangin ka pai thei ta hiam?

records.english: Was Grandma really alive before there were cars in the village?
records.zomi: Khua ah mawtaw a om ma-in Pi a nungta taktak hiam?

records.english: I was born in the year of the big snowstorm, so my parents never forget my age.
records.zomi: Vuuk huihpi lian kum in ka suak ahih manin ka nu leh ka pa in ka kum a mangngilh ngei kei uh hi.

records.english: How old was Grandma when she got married, and how old were you, Mum?
records.zomi: Pi a kiten ciangin kum bangzah ahi hiam, nang Nu, kum bangzah na hi hiam?

records.english: My grandparents waited a long time for children, and my father arrived in their twelfth year of marriage.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh ka pi naupang dingin hun sawtpi a ngak uh a, a kitenna kum sawm leh nihna-in ka pa a suak hi.

records.english: My grandfather measures time by the big events of his life, like the war and the year of the great drought.
records.zomi: Ka pu in gal leh khuakhal lianpi kum bangin a nuntakna sung-a thupiang lianpite tawh hun a teh hi.

records.english: Let's write everyone's birth year on the family tree.
records.zomi: Innkuan khangthu lim tungah mi khempeuh' suah kum i gelh ding.

records.english: Putting family events beside national events showed us how history touched our own lives.
records.zomi: Innkuan thupiangte gam thupiangte kiangah i koih ciangin tangthu in i nuntakna bangci a khoih hiam hong lak hi.

records.english: We worked out that my great-grandfather was born more than a hundred years ago.
records.zomi: Ka pu upa kum za val paisa-in a suak hi, ci i tuat uh hi.

records.english: In our family, the year of the earthquake divides everything into before and after.
records.zomi: I innkuan ah lei ling kum in na khempeuh a ma leh a nung ah a khen hi.

records.english: Grandma was born the same year the first bus came to her village.
records.zomi: Pi' khua ah bus masa pen a tun kum mah-in Pi a suak hi.

records.english: My cousin and I worked out that our grandmothers were at school at the same time.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam leh kei in i pite uh hun kibang-in sang a kah uh hi, ci i tuat uh hi.

records.english: We made a family timeline that starts with my great-grandparents' wedding and ends with my baby brother's birth.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh pi' nu leh pa' mopawi pan kipan ka nau pasal neu' suahna dong-a innkuan hun kizui lim khat i bawl uh hi.

records.english: When I asked Grandpa to tell me his life in order, he laughed.
records.zomi: A nuntakna a kizui dik-in hong gen dingin Pu ka nget ciangin a nuih hi.

records.english: He said memories don't come in a neat line; they come when something reminds you.
records.zomi: Phawknate kizui kician-in a hong pai kei a; na khat in hong phawk sak ciangin a hong pai hi, a ci hi.

records.english: So we spent a whole afternoon moving his stories around until they made sense.
records.zomi: Tua ahih manin a tangthute a kituak dong sun bup i lehhei uh hi.

records.english: Dad, which came first, your first job or your first car?
records.zomi: Pa, na nasep masa pen hiam na mawtaw masa pen hiam kua a masa hiam?

records.english: My parents left the farm for the city when my oldest brother was still a baby.
records.zomi: Ka u pasal upa pen naungek a hih lai-in ka nu leh ka pa in lou a nusia-in khuapi ah a pem uh hi.

records.english: Our family has lived in this house since 1962.
records.zomi: I innkuan 1962 pan kipan hih inn ah a teng uh hi.

records.english: Ordering family stories by date sometimes reveals that two famous family legends cannot both be true.
records.zomi: Innkuan tangthute ni leh kum zui-in koih in innkuan tangthu minthang nih a dik khawm thei kei hi, ci a lak zel hi.

records.english: My father was the first person in our family to finish university, in 1985.
records.zomi: I innkuan ah sangpi a zo masa pen ka pa ahi a, 1985 kum in ahi hi.

records.english: Our family moved house four times before I turned ten.
records.zomi: Kum sawm ka phak ma-in i innkuan in inn livei a pem uh hi.

records.english: I drew a timeline of my life for school, starting with the day I was born.
records.zomi: Sang adingin ka suah ni pan kipan ka nuntakna hun kizui lim khat ka gelh hi.

records.english: Talking about when things happened helps children understand how long ago their grandparents were young.
records.zomi: Bang hun-in na piang hiam kihopih in a pu leh a pite uh a khangno lai hun bangzah a sawt khin hiam naupangte a theih nadingun a huh hi.

records.english: Was Dad born before or after the family moved to the coast?
records.zomi: Innkuan tuipi gei a pem ma-in hiam a pem khit-in hiam Pa a suak hiam?

records.english: My great-aunt is the only person in the family who remembers life before the railway.
records.zomi: Ka pu upa' u numei pen meileng lampi om ma-a nuntakna a phawk innkuan sung-a mi khat bek ahi hi.

records.english: My aunt keeps a calendar where she marks the birthday of every relative.
records.zomi: Ka ni in sanggam khempeuh' suahni a ciamtehna calendar khat a kem hi.

records.english: Please inform the school in writing if anyone other than a parent will collect your child.
records.zomi: Nu leh pa simloh mi dang in na naupang a hong lak ding leh sang kiangah lai tawh gen in.

records.english: Thank you for your letter regarding our son's behaviour in class.
records.zomi: Khan sung-a i tapa' omzia tungtang na lai adingin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: Do both parents have to be present at the citizenship ceremony?
records.zomi: Gam mi suahna pawi ah nu leh pa a nih in a om kul uh hiam?

records.english: Please complete this form to apply for child benefit.
records.zomi: Naupang huhna sum ngetna adingin hih lai gelh in.

records.english: Kindly confirm your attendance at the parents' evening by Friday.
records.zomi: Nu leh pate kikhopna nitak ah na hong pai ding hiam Laithai ni ma-in kipsak in.

records.english: The marriage register is kept at the district office.
records.zomi: Kitenna min bu district office ah kikem hi.

records.english: The ceremony will begin at two o'clock, and guests are asked to be seated by a quarter to two.
records.zomi: Pawi nai nih ciangin kipan ding a, mikhualte nai nih kimlo minit sawm leh nga ciangin tu dingin kingen hi.

records.english: What documents do we need to register our marriage?
records.zomi: I kitenna gelh nadingin bang laite i kisam uh hiam?

records.english: Your passports, birth certificates and proof of address.
records.zomi: Na passport, na suahna lai leh na tenna mun kipsakna.

records.english: A prenuptial agreement sets out how property will be divided if the marriage ends.
records.zomi: Kiten ma-a kituakna in kitenna a bei leh neihsate bangci kihawm ding hiam a gen hi.

records.english: The marriage certificate must be signed by two witnesses.
records.zomi: Kitenna lai theihpihtu nih in a min a gelh ding uh hi.

records.english: Is there a fee for the parenting course run by the local health service?
records.zomi: Khua damna nasep in a bawl nu leh pa sinna adingin a man a om hiam?

records.english: The couple exchanged rings and signed the register in front of their families.
records.zomi: Zi leh pasal ding in a innkuan uh mai ah zungbuh a kipia-in min bu ah a min uh a gelh uh hi.

records.english: Couples who marry abroad may need to register their marriage when they return home.
records.zomi: Gamdang-a kiteng zi leh pasalte in inn a ciah kik uh ciangin a kitenna uh a gelh kul thei uh hi.

records.english: Shared parental leave allows both parents to divide the time off between them.
records.zomi: Nu leh pa tawlngak hun kihawm in nu leh pa a nih in tawlngak hun a kihawm thei uh hi.

records.english: Our employer offers two weeks of paid leave to new fathers.
records.zomi: I nasep piaktu in pa thakte adingin kal nih sung khasum tawh tawlngak hun a pia hi.

records.english: The family support worker will visit on Tuesday to discuss your concerns.
records.zomi: Innkuan huhna nasem in na lungkhamnate kihopih dingin Pithai ni ciangin hong veh ding hi.

records.english: I am writing to inform the school that our son will be absent next week for a family wedding.
records.zomi: Innkuan mopawi hangin i tapa a zom kal sang ah a om kei ding hi, ci-in sang kiangah ka gelh hi.

records.english: We hereby give permission for our daughter to take part in the school trip.
records.zomi: I tanu sang khualzinna ah a tel nadingin hih tawh phalna ka pia uh hi.

records.english: The adoption agency requires every applicant to attend a preparation course.
records.zomi: Ta-a laakna office in ngetna khempeuh kiginna sinna khat ah a pai dingin a ngen hi.

records.english: New mothers in our company are entitled to six months of maternity leave.
records.zomi: I company-a nu thakte in kha guk sung nau suah tawlngak hun a ngah thei uh hi.

records.english: Foster parents receive an allowance to cover the cost of caring for a child.
records.zomi: Naupang kemtu nu leh pate in naupang khat kemna man adingin huhna sum a ngah uh hi.

records.english: Each parent must sign the passport application for a child under sixteen.
records.zomi: Kum sawm leh guk nuai naupang khat' passport ngetna ah nu leh pa khatciat in a min a gelh ding uh hi.

records.english: Can parents choose which school their child attends?
records.zomi: Nu leh pate in a tate uh a kah ding sang a teel thei uh hiam?

records.english: You can list three preferences, but places are offered according to the admissions rules.
records.zomi: Deih nate thum na gelh thei hi, ahi zongin sang lutna thukham bangin mun kipia hi.

records.english: The school sent an official letter asking parents to sign the permission form.
records.zomi: Phalna lai tungah min gelh dingin nu leh pate ngetna lai kizahtak khat sang in a khak hi.

records.english: The officiant asked whether anyone knew of a reason why the couple could not lawfully marry.
records.zomi: Kitenna pawi makaipa in zi leh pasal ding thukham bangin a kiten theih loh nading a hang kuamah in a thei hiam a dong hi.

records.english: The health visitor will call at your home within two weeks of the birth.
records.zomi: Nau suah khit kal nih sungin damna vehtu in na inn ah hong veh ding hi.

records.english: We regret to inform you that your application to adopt has been delayed.
records.zomi: Ta-a laakna na ngetna a hun a kiphawng hi, ci-in lungkham takin kong gen hi.

records.english: Who is legally allowed to perform a wedding ceremony in this country?
records.zomi: Hih gam ah kitenna pawi thukham bangin kua in a bawl thei hiam?

records.english: We are delighted to announce the marriage of our daughter Mary to Mr. David Kim.
records.zomi: I tanu Mary leh Pu David Kim' kitenna nuam takin kong gen uh hi.

records.english: The bride's father signed the register as a witness.
records.zomi: Mo' pa in theihpihtu-in min bu ah a min a gelh hi.

records.english: Couples must give notice of their intention to marry at least one month before the ceremony.
records.zomi: Zi leh pasal dingte in kitenna pawi a om ma kha khat pan kiteng ding uh hi, ci-in a gen ding uh hi.

records.english: May I take a day's leave for my daughter's graduation ceremony?
records.zomi: Ka tanu' sang zawhna pawi adingin ni khat tawlngak ka la thei ding hiam?

records.english: I'd like to make an appointment to discuss my son's progress with the head teacher.
records.zomi: Ka tapa' sinna kalsuan sang makaipa tawh kihopih dingin kimuhna khat ka bawl nuam hi.

records.english: The judge granted the divorce and approved the agreement on the children's care.
records.zomi: Thukhenpa in kikhenna a phal a, naupangte kemna kituakna a pom hi.

records.english: Parents are legally responsible for making sure their children attend school.
records.zomi: Nu leh pate in a tate uh sang a kah nadingin thukham bangin mawhpuakna a nei uh hi.

records.english: Married couples may be eligible for a tax allowance.
records.zomi: Kiteng zi leh pasalte in siah kiamsakna a ngah thei uh hi.

records.english: Do we need to bring the baby when we register the birth?
records.zomi: Suahna i gelh ciangin naungek i paipih kul hiam?

records.english: Parents must give written consent before their child can receive the vaccination at school.
records.zomi: Sang ah naupang khat in kidawnna damdawi a ngah ma-in nu leh pate in lai tawh phalna a pia ding uh hi.

records.english: Grandparents may apply to the court for the right to see their grandchildren.
records.zomi: Pu leh pite in a tute uh muh theihna adingin thukhenna ah a ngen thei uh hi.

records.english: The court will always put the welfare of the child first.
records.zomi: Thukhenna in naupang' hoihna masa pen-in a koih tawntung ding hi.

records.english: Ladies and gentlemen, please rise for the bride.
records.zomi: Numeite leh pasalte, mo adingin ding un.

records.english: Parents who are separated are both welcome to attend school meetings.
records.zomi: Kikhen nu leh pate a nih in sang kikhopnate ah hong pai thei uh hi.

records.english: I would like to apply for flexible working hours to care for my newborn child.
records.zomi: Ka naungek thak kem nadingin nasep hun kikheel thei ka ngen nuam hi.

records.english: We would like to request a copy of our marriage certificate.
records.zomi: I kitenna lai copy khat i ngen nuam uh hi.

records.english: Is there an official form for changing a child's surname?
records.zomi: Naupang khat' innkuan min kheelna adingin kumpi lai khat a om hiam?

records.english: The marriage was solemnised in the presence of the bride's and groom's families.
records.zomi: Mo leh mopa' innkuante mai ah kitenna kibawl hi.

records.english: Employees are entitled to up to twelve weeks of parental leave after the birth of a child.
records.zomi: Naupang khat a suah khit ciangin nasemte in kal sawm leh nih dong nu leh pa tawlngak hun a ngah thei uh hi.

records.english: Please state the full names of both parents.
records.zomi: Nu leh pa a nih' min kicing gelh in.

records.english: Every parent has the right to see their child's school records.
records.zomi: Nu leh pa khatciat in a ta' sang ciamtehna en theihna a nei uh hi.

records.english: Can a father be named on the birth certificate if the parents are not married?
records.zomi: Nu leh pa a kiteng kei uh leh pa' min suahna lai tungah kigelh thei hiam?

records.english: Please submit your child's immunisation record with the enrolment form.
records.zomi: Sang lutna lai tawh na naupang' kidawnna damdawi ciamtehna pia in.

records.english: Childcare costs may be partly refunded through the government scheme.
records.zomi: Naupang kemna man kumpi nasep tungtawn-in a kim lang kikhel kik thei hi.

records.english: The couple were declared husband and wife at exactly noon.
records.zomi: Sun tawh taktak-in zi leh pasal-in kiphuang uh hi.

records.english: Social services may become involved if there are serious concerns about a child's safety.
records.zomi: Naupang khat' bitna tungtang lungkhamna gik a om leh mipi huhna office in a kihel thei hi.

records.english: Please bring your marriage certificate when you apply for the family visa.
records.zomi: Innkuan visa na nget ciangin na kitenna lai tawi in.

records.english: By law, a birth must be registered within six weeks.
records.zomi: Thukham bangin suahna kal guk sungin kigelh ding hi.

records.english: The court ordered that the children should spend alternate weekends with each parent.
records.zomi: Thukhenna in naupangte kal tawp khat zawh khat-in nu leh pa khatciat tawh a om ding uh hi, ci-in a thupiak hi.

records.english: A copy of the birth certificate will be posted to you within ten working days.
records.zomi: Nasep ni sawm sungin suahna lai copy khat nang kiangah kikhak ding hi.

records.english: Grandpa walked for many days to reach the town where he found work.
records.zomi: Pu in nasep a muhna khua a tun nadingin ni tampi a pai hi.

records.english: Our family has lived in three countries in the last twenty years.
records.zomi: Kum sawmnih sungin i innkuan gam thum ah a teng uh hi.

records.english: How many of your cousins still live in the home village?
records.zomi: Na sanggamte bangzah in khua bul ah a teng lai uh hiam?

records.english: Why did your family leave the hills?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na innkuan in mualte a nusia uh hiam?

records.english: My parents wanted us to go to a better school.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in sang hoih zaw ah kah dingin a deih uh hi.

records.english: My cousin lives in Tulsa, where many families from our community have settled.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam Tulsa ah a teng a, tua ah i mipi pan innkuan tampi a teng uh hi.

records.english: My uncle helped five young men from our village find work in the city.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in i khua pan tangval nga khuapi ah nasep a muh nadingun a huh hi.

records.english: My sister married a man from our community who lives in Norway.
records.zomi: Ka u numei in Norway ah a teng i mipi pan pasal khat a kiteng hi.

records.english: Moving to a new country was hard for my parents because they didn't speak the language.
records.zomi: Pau a theih loh uh ahih manin gam thak ah pem pen ka nu leh ka pa adingin a haksa hi.

records.english: Our children were born here, but they still call the village home.
records.zomi: I tate hih gam ah a suak uh hi, ahi zongin khua inn bangin a sam lai uh hi.

records.english: Every Christmas, people who moved away try to come back to the village.
records.zomi: Christmas simin a pem mite in khua ah ciah kik dingin a hanciam uh hi.

records.english: Migration has spread our people across many countries.
records.zomi: Pemna in i mite gam tampi ah a zeksak hi.

records.english: Auntie Hau is the only one of her brothers and sisters who stayed in the village.
records.zomi: Ni Hau pen a sanggamte lak ah khua ah a om lai mi khat bek ahi hi.

records.english: Families who moved to the same city often settled in the same neighbourhood.
records.zomi: Khuapi kibang ah a pem innkuante tamzaw in khua sung mun kibang ah a teng uh hi.

records.english: How long did your parents save to pay for the journey?
records.zomi: Khualzinna man piak nadingin na nu leh na pa in hun bangzah sung sum a kem uh hiam?

records.english: The first families who moved to the city lived together in one small house.
records.zomi: Khuapi ah a pem masa innkuante inn neu khat sungah a teng khawm uh hi.

records.english: The roads are better now, so it's easier for people to visit the village.
records.zomi: Tu-in lampite a hoih zaw ahih manin mite in khua veh a baih zaw hi.

records.english: Grandma cried for a week when her youngest son moved overseas.
records.zomi: A tapa neu pen gamdang ah a pem ciangin Pi kal khat sung a kap hi.

records.english: When we first arrived, a family from our own village gave us a place to stay.
records.zomi: I tun masak ciangin i khua mah pan innkuan khat in teenna mun hong pia hi.

records.english: Is it true that your whole family moved to the town in one year?
records.zomi: Na innkuan bup kum khat sungin khuapi ah a pem uh cih a dik hiam?

records.english: Even after thirty years abroad, my uncle still speaks of the village as home.
records.zomi: Gamdang ah kum sawmthum a om khit zongin ka pa neu in khua inn bangin a gen lai hi.

records.english: My father worked in a factory for ten years before he could bring us to join him.
records.zomi: Hong sam theih ma-in ka pa in kum sawm sung factory ah na a sem hi.

records.english: Many young people from our village go away to study and never come back to live.
records.zomi: I khua pan khangno tampi sang kah dingin a pai uh a, teng dingin a ciah kik ngei kei uh hi.

records.english: Do you know anyone from our community in Australia?
records.zomi: Australia ah i mipi pan kuamah na thei hiam?

records.english: People who move abroad often keep strong ties with their home villages.
records.zomi: Gamdang ah a pem mite in a khua bul uh tawh kizopna hat a kem zel uh hi.

records.english: Our community association helps newcomers find homes and jobs.
records.zomi: I mipi pawlpi in a tung thakte inn leh nasep a muh nadingun a huh hi.

records.english: How old were you when your family moved from the village to the city?
records.zomi: Na innkuan khua pan khuapi ah a pem uh ciangin kum bangzah na hi hiam?

records.english: Children who grow up abroad sometimes understand their parents' language but answer in another.
records.zomi: Gamdang ah a khangkhia naupangte in a nu leh a pa' pau a thei uh a, ahi zongin pau dang tawh a dawng zel uh hi.

records.english: Moving away taught my father how much he loved his home.
records.zomi: Pemna in ka pa a inn bangzah a it hiam a lak hi.

records.english: What do you miss most about home?
records.zomi: Inn tungtang bang na lunggulh pen hiam?

records.english: When my brother left for work abroad, our mother packed his favourite dried meat.
records.zomi: Ka u pasal gamdang ah na sem dingin a pai ciangin i nu in a it pen sa gawh a tawi sak hi.

records.english: Many of our elders worry that the young people who move away will forget their culture.
records.zomi: I upa tampi in a pem khangnote in a ngeina uh a mangngilh kha ding hi, ci-in a lungkham uh hi.

records.english: Do your parents still talk about the day they left home?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa in inn a nusiat ni uh tu dong a gen lai uh hiam?

records.english: Please write down the address of our relatives in the city.
records.zomi: Khuapi-a i sanggamte' tenna mun gelh in.

records.english: Many people from our community first went to work in Malaysia before moving on to other countries.
records.zomi: I mipi pan mi tampi gam dangte ah a pem ma-un Malaysia ah na sem dingin a pai masa uh hi.

records.english: Migration changed our village, because fewer young people stayed to farm the fields.
records.zomi: Lou-a nasem dingin khangno tawm zaw a om ahih manin pemna in i khua a kheel hi.

records.english: People often move to follow relatives who have already settled somewhere.
records.zomi: Mite in mun khat ah a teng khin sanggamte zui dingin a pem zel uh hi.

records.english: Our community in the city meets every Sunday after church to share news from home.
records.zomi: Khuapi-a i mipi in Nipini simin pawlpi khit ciangin inn lam thu a kihawm dingin a kikhawm uh hi.

records.english: We still keep the house in the village for when the family comes back.
records.zomi: Innkuan a ciah kik ciang adingin khua-a inn i kem lai uh hi.

records.english: My little sister was born after we arrived in the new country.
records.zomi: Gam thak ah i tun khit ciangin ka nau numei a suak hi.

records.english: When my aunt left for India, she took a bag of rice and a few photographs.
records.zomi: Ka ni India ah a pai ciangin buh ip khat leh lim tawmno a tawi hi.

records.english: My grandparents never left the village, but all their children did.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh ka pi in khua a nusia ngei kei uh a, ahi zongin a tate khempeuh in a nusia uh hi.

records.english: Shall we call our relatives abroad this weekend?
records.zomi: Hih kal tawp ciangin gamdang-a i sanggamte i sam ding hiam?

records.english: Shall we send some photos to Grandma in the village?
records.zomi: Khua-a Pi kiangah lim pawl khat i khak ding hiam?

records.english: Many families from our village moved to the town to find work.
records.zomi: I khua pan innkuan tampi nasep zong dingin khuapi ah a pem uh hi.

records.english: Does our community in the city still celebrate the traditional festivals?
records.zomi: Khuapi-a i mipi in ngeina pawite a lawm lai uh hiam?

records.english: Sending photos and videos helps the relatives at home feel close to us.
records.zomi: Lim leh video khak in inn-a sanggamte i kiang uh ah a om bangin a phawk sak hi.

records.english: When people move far away, our language and songs travel with them.
records.zomi: Mite gamla ah a pem ciangin i pau leh i la te amaute tawh a pai khawm hi.

records.english: Leaving home is never easy, even when it brings a better life.
records.zomi: Nuntakna hoih zaw a tun zongin inn nusiat pen a baih ngei kei hi.

records.english: Doesn't the village feel quiet now that so many families have moved away?
records.zomi: Innkuan tampi a pem khit ciangin khua a dai mahmah kei hiam?

records.english: Do you still have relatives in the old village?
records.zomi: Khua lui ah sanggam na nei lai hiam?

records.english: Yes, my grandmother and two of my aunts.
records.zomi: Nei lai ing, ka pi leh ka ni nih.

records.english: Our church in the city was started by families who came from the same villages.
records.zomi: Khuapi-a i pawlpi khua kibang pan hong pai innkuante in a kipat uh hi.

records.english: When a family moves away, the whole village gathers to pray for them.
records.zomi: Innkuan khat a pem ciangin khua bup amaute adingin thungen dingin a kikhawm uh hi.

records.english: Can you tell me how your family came to live here?

records.english: Do your parents hope to return to the village when they are old?

records.english: New families in our community are usually helped by people who arrived before them.
records.zomi: I mipi-a innkuan thakte a tamzaw-in amaute ma-a tung mite in a huh uh hi.

records.zomi: Pemna tangthute i mipi' tangthu sung-a a thupi khat ahi hi.

records.english: Each new generation adds another chapter to our family's story of moving and settling.
records.zomi: Khang thak khatciat in i innkuan' pemna leh tenna tangthu ah a dawh thak khat a behlap hi.

records.zomi: Naungek ka hih lai-in ka pa neu Malaysia ah a pem hi.

records.zomi: Innkuan khat' sum buaina pen a tamzaw-in a thupi a ngaihsut uh kibang lo buaina ahi hi.

records.english: Why do you think your daughter is struggling to sleep?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na tanu a ihmut haksa sa hi, na ci hiam?

records.english: Dad noticed that the plants were dying because the window was always shut.

records.english: Has something happened at work that's making you so tense?

records.zomi: Pu in ka hoih hi, a ci den a, ahi zongin zingsang an a ne nawn kei hi, ci i phawk uh hi.

records.english: Why is there always a queue for the bathroom in the morning?
records.zomi: Bang hangin zingsang simin kisilna inn adingin mi a kizom-a ngak den uh hiam?

records.english: Because everyone gets up at exactly the same time.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh hun kibang taktak-in a thou uh ahih manin.

records.english: Our son's teacher helped us see that his bad behaviour was really a problem with his eyesight.
records.zomi: I tapa' saya in a omzia hoih lo pen a mit buaina ahi hi, ci i theih nadingin hong huh hi.

records.zomi: Buaina pen inn nasep hi lo-in naupang a kipat ciangin bangzah a gim hiam ahi zel hi.

records.english: What is it about the new school that you don't like?

records.english: I think he hears the neighbour's motorbike coming home.

records.english: Is something wrong between you and your sister?

records.english: Do you think the problem is the new teacher or the new subject?

records.english: Before we argue about the chores, let's work out what the real problem is.

records.english: Why are you so quiet at dinner lately?

records.english: When the family keeps quarrelling about the same thing, it's worth finding out what's behind it.

records.english: Mum finally told us that the stairs had become too hard for her.
records.zomi: Kahlei pen amah adingin a haksa ta hi, ci-in Nu in a tawpna-ah hong gen hi.

records.english: Shall we write down everything that goes wrong this week and look at it together?
records.zomi: Hih kal sungin a khial na khempeuh gelh-in khawm-in i en ding hiam?

records.english: Is anything worrying you that you haven't told me?
records.zomi: Hong gen nai lo na lungkhamna bangmah a om hiam?

records.english: Mum always asks one simple question when something is wrong: what changed?
records.zomi: Na khat a sia ciangin Nu in dotna baih khat a dong tawntung hi: bang a kikheel hiam?

records.english: Are you upset about the trip being cancelled or about something else?
records.zomi: Khualzinna kikhak hangin na lungkham hiam, thu dang hangin hiam?

records.zomi: Thu dang, nang leh Pa na kiel na ka zak manin.

records.english: Why does the kitchen always smell of gas in the evening?
records.zomi: Bang hangin nitak simin anbuk gas gim nam den hiam?

records.english: Mum, why does the baby keep crying after her bath?

records.zomi: Amah adingin tui a vot deuh hi ding hi, ka ci hi.

records.english: What is it that makes mornings so stressful in our house?
records.zomi: I inn ah bang in zingsangte lungkhamhuai a sak hiam?

records.english: Understanding why a teenager is angry matters more than winning the argument.
records.zomi: Tangval-tangnu khat bang hangin a heh hiam theih pen kielna zawh sangin a thupi zaw hi.

records.english: We realised the real problem was that nobody had agreed who would pick up the children.
records.zomi: Buaina taktak pen naupangte kua in a la ding hiam kuamah in a kituak kei uh hi, ci i thei uh hi.

records.english: Could the problem be that your shoes are too small?
records.zomi: Buaina pen na khedap a neu lua hi thei hiam?

records.english: What's the biggest problem with living so far from your parents?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa tawh gamla taka teng ah buaina lian pen bang hiam?

records.english: Not being there when they need help at short notice.
records.zomi: Manlang taka huhna a kisam uh ciangin a kiang uh ah om theih loh.

records.english: Identifying what upsets a toddler can take a lot of patience.
records.zomi: Naupang neu khat bang in a lungkhamsak hiam theih in thuakzawhna tampi a kisam thei hi.

records.english: Can you tell me exactly when your tummy starts to hurt?
records.zomi: Na gil bang hun taktak-in a na kipan hiam hong gen thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: My husband and I made a list of the problems in our week and found that most of them were about time.
records.zomi: Ka pasal leh kei i kal sung-a buainate list khat i bawl uh a, a tamzaw hun tungtang ahi hi, ci i thei uh hi.

records.english: Every economic policy has winners and losers, even when the overall effect is positive.

records.english: Cutting spending can reduce government debt, but it may also mean fewer public services.

records.english: The price of petrol is controlled by the government in some countries.

records.english: Will the plan to reduce electricity costs really help households?
records.zomi: Meivak man kiamsakna lampi in innkuante a huh taktak ding hiam?

records.english: A good economic policy should help both businesses and ordinary families.
records.zomi: Sum leh neihsa thu kumpi lampi hoih khat in sumbawlte leh innkuan nautangte a huh ding hi.

records.zomi: Sum zat ding thak in damdawi inn leh sangte adingin sum tam zaw a nei hi.

records.zomi: Bang hangin van man manlang takin a khang hiam?

records.english: Partly because fuel and imported goods have become more expensive.

records.english: A new trade agreement has made it easier to export fruit to neighbouring countries.
records.zomi: Sumbawlna kituakna thak in kiang gamte ah theigah zuak a baih zaw sak hi.

records.english: Economic policy affects everything from the price of bread to the number of jobs available.
records.zomi: Sum leh neihsa thu kumpi lampi in moh man pan nasep zah dong na khempeuh a khoih hi.

records.english: Who decides how much tax we pay?
records.zomi: Siah bangzah i piak ding kua in a khensat hiam?

records.english: Subsidies for fertiliser helped farmers grow more food last season.

records.english: Policies that protect local industries can also make goods more expensive for consumers.

records.english: Raising the minimum wage helps workers, but some employers say it makes hiring harder.

records.english: What does the government do when unemployment is high?

records.english: It may spend more on public projects to create jobs.
records.zomi: Nasep a om nadingin mipi nasep lian ah sum tam zaw a zang thei hi.

records.english: Free healthcare for children is paid for by the national budget.
records.zomi: Naupangte adingin man om lo damdawi bawlna gam sum zat ding pan kipia hi.

records.english: Farmers can get government loans at a low interest rate.
records.zomi: Loubawlte in kumpi pan ki-ap man niam taka leiba a ngah thei uh hi.

records.english: Higher taxes on cigarettes are meant to encourage people to smoke less.

records.english: Some policies take years before their effects can be seen.

records.english: Our town received money from the government to build a new market.

records.english: The new law makes employers pay workers for overtime.

records.english: A new training scheme helps young people find their first jobs.

records.zomi: Khum mahmah dawn ding siah in mite' damna a kem nadingin ahi hi.

records.english: Only if your yearly sales are over the limit.

records.english: Why does the price of bread keep changing?
records.zomi: Bang hangin moh man a kikheel den hiam?

records.english: Have you noticed that prices in the shops have gone up again?
records.zomi: Sumbuk-a van man a khang kik na phawk hiam?

records.english: What exactly is inflation, and why does it matter to families?
records.zomi: Inflation pen bang taktak hiam, innkuante adingin bang hangin a thupi hiam?

records.english: Free school meals are one way the government supports poorer families.

records.english: The central bank raised interest rates to slow down rising prices.
records.zomi: Van man khan a dal nadingin central bank in ki-ap man a khangsak hi.

records.zomi: Kumpi in an siah a kiamsak ding thu na za hiam?

records.zomi: Lampi thak lam pen kumpite in sum leh neihsa a khan nadingin a hanciamna lampi khat ahi hi.

records.zomi: Sum leh neihsa a kalsuan a nem ciangin mite in sum tawm zaw a zang-in tam zaw a kem zel uh hi.

records.english: Is the government doing anything to help people who have lost their jobs?

records.english: My brother's wife comes from a region where they speak a different language from ours.

records.english: My uncle has worked in so many countries that he can say thank you in ten languages.

records.english: Living in two countries has given my children two sets of friends and two favourite foods.

records.english: Can you show me on the globe where Grandpa worked when he was young?

records.english: Visiting my mother's home region showed me where many of her habits came from.
records.zomi: Ka nu' gam lam ka veh ciangin a ngeina tampi koi pan hong pai hiam ka mu hi.

records.english: Auntie Cing said the hardest thing about moving abroad was the cold winters.
records.zomi: Gamdang ah pemna-ah a haksa pen phalbi vot ahi hi, Ni Cing in a ci hi.

records.english: Dad was born in the north of the country, and Mum grew up near the coast.

records.english: My parents taught us the names of all the regions they had lived in before we were born.
records.zomi: I suah ma-un ka nu leh ka pa in a tenna gam lam khempeuh uh min hong sinsak uh hi.

records.english: Studying the geography of a relative's country makes their letters easier to understand.
records.zomi: Sanggam khat' gam' leitung zia sin in a laite theih a baih zaw sak hi.

records.english: We went to the border with my father to see the river where he used to fish.
records.zomi: Ka pa nga a manna gun en dingin gam gi ah amah tawh i pai uh hi.

records.english: Talking to relatives in other countries has taught my children that people live in very different ways.
records.zomi: Gamdang-a sanggamte tawh kihopih in mite nuntakzia tuam mahmah hi, ci-in ka tate a sinsak hi.

records.english: My cousin moved to a region where nobody had heard of our hometown.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam i khua min kuamah in a zak ngei loh gam lam khat ah a pem hi.

records.english: When my cousins visit from America, they ask so many questions about our region.
records.zomi: America pan ka sanggamte hong veh uh ciangin i gam lam tungtang dotna tampi a dong uh hi.

records.english: Which part of the country are your parents from?
records.zomi: Na nu leh na pa gam bang lam pan ahi uh hiam?

records.english: Shall we watch the programme about Peru together on Sunday?
