records.english: Shall we ask the children for their ideas before we decide?
records.zomi: I khensat ma-in naupangte' ngaihsutna i dong ding hiam?

records.english: Would it help if I picked the children up on Wednesdays?
records.zomi: Nilai ni simin naupangte ka lak leh a huh ding hiam?

records.english: It would, because that's my late day at work.
records.zomi: Huh ding hi, tua ni nasep ah ka om sauna ni ahih manin.

records.english: Could we save money by cooking at home more often?
records.zomi: Inn ah an huan tam zaw tawh sum i kem thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, and the children could help plan the meals.
records.zomi: Thei hi, naupangte in an ding gelh a huh thei uh hi.

records.english: Sometimes the best solution for a family is the one everyone is willing to try.
records.zomi: Khatvei khat innkuan khat adingin lampi hoih pen mi khempeuh in a zat nop pen ahi zel hi.

records.english: My husband and I agreed to try the new budget for one month and then review it.
records.zomi: Ka pasal leh kei in sum zat ding thak kha khat sung i zang a, tua khit ciangin en kik dingin i kituak uh hi.

records.english: Auntie Ngun helped our family apply for a state grant to repair our roof.
records.zomi: Ni Ngun in i innkhum bawl hoih nadingin state huhna sum ngen dingin i innkuan a huh hi.

records.english: Grandma wrote to the president once, and she still has the reply.
records.zomi: Pi in khatvei president kiangah lai a gelh a, a dawnna a nei lai hi.

records.english: My father took me to the state parliament building when I was ten.
records.zomi: Kum sawm ka hih lai-in ka pa in state parliament building ah hong paipih hi.

records.english: Our family's land documents are kept at the state records office.
records.zomi: I innkuan' gam laite state ciamtehna office ah kikem hi.

records.english: Because Dad is a national civil servant, we moved to a new state every few years.
records.zomi: Pa gam kumpi nasem ahih manin kum tawmno zawh khat-in state thak ah i pem uh hi.

records.english: When Grandma needed a carer, the state paid for part of it.
records.zomi: Pi kemtu a kisam ciangin state in a man a lang a pia hi.

records.english: Who in our family has ever worked for the government?
records.zomi: I innkuan sung pan kua in kumpi nasep a sem ngei hiam?

records.english: My uncle is a member of the state assembly, so the whole family watched his first speech.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu state assembly mi khat ahih manin a thugen masa pen innkuan bup in i en uh hi.

records.english: My sister works as a teacher in a state school, so her salary comes from the state budget.
records.zomi: Ka u numei state sang khat ah saya ahih manin a khasum state sum zat ding pan kipia hi.

records.english: My brother joined the national army, and my sister works for the state police.
records.zomi: Ka u pasal gam galkap ah a lut a, ka u numei state police ah na a sem hi.

records.english: My grandfather's medal was presented by the national government.
records.zomi: Ka pu' medal gam kumpi in a pia hi.

records.english: We celebrate both National Day and our State Day with the family.
records.zomi: Innkuan tawh National Day leh i State Day a nih i lawm uh hi.

records.english: My father keeps his national identity card and his state voter card in the same wallet.
records.zomi: Ka pa in a gam identity card leh a state vote card wallet kibang sungah a koih hi.

records.english: My grandparents are proud that they helped vote in the first national government after independence.
records.zomi: Gam suahtakna khit-a gam kumpi masa pen teel dingin vote a khiat uh hangin ka pu leh ka pi a kisaktheih uh hi.

records.english: My parents still remember when our region became a separate state.
records.zomi: I gam lam state tuam khat a suah lai ka nu leh ka pa in a phawk lai uh hi.

records.english: Ask your grandfather what life was like before the state had its own government.
records.zomi: State in amah kumpi a neih ma-in nuntakna bangci om hiam na pu dong in.

records.english: We drove to the state capital to register our new business.
records.zomi: I sumbawlna thak gelh dingin state khuapi lian ah mawtaw tawh i pai uh hi.

records.english: Dad, does the state or the national government pay your pension?
records.zomi: Pa, na pension state in a pia hiam, gam kumpi in a pia hiam?

records.english: The national government, because I worked for the post office.
records.zomi: Gam kumpi in, post office ah na ka sep manin.

records.english: Is our town's hospital run by the state or by the national health service?
records.zomi: I khua damdawi inn state in a kem hiam, gam damna nasep in a kem hiam?

records.english: My cousin's family received help from the state after their house burned down.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam' innkuan in a inn uh mei a kan khit ciangin state pan huhna a ngah uh hi.

records.english: Shall we ask our representative's office to look into Grandpa's pension problem?
records.zomi: Pu' pension buaina en dingin i aiawhpa' office i ngen ding hiam?

records.english: Our son's homework was to find out the names of our governor and our president.
records.zomi: I tapa' inn nasep pen i governor leh i president min zong ahi hi.

records.english: Our son wrote a letter to the governor about the broken playground.
records.zomi: I tapa in naupang kimawlna mun sia tungtang governor kiangah lai a gelh hi.

records.english: Our family got a letter from the national tax office asking for more documents.
records.zomi: I innkuan in gam siah office pan lai behlap ngetna lai khat a ngah hi.

records.english: My cousin's family had to deal with both the state and the national office to get their visas sorted.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam' innkuan in a visa uh kician nadingin state office leh gam office a nih tawh a kithuah kul uh hi.

records.english: Why are there two flags outside the government building, Dad?
records.zomi: Pa, bang hangin kumpi building pualam ah flag nih a om hiam?

records.english: My father taught me that national laws apply everywhere in the country, even where state laws differ.
records.zomi: State thukhamte a kibat loh mun ah zong gam thukhamte gam bup ah kizang hi, ci-in ka pa in hong sinsak hi.

records.english: Who's going to help Grandma with her state pension application?
records.zomi: Pi' state pension ngetna ah kua in a huh ding hiam?

records.english: When our state elected its first woman governor, my grandmother cried with joy.
records.zomi: I state in numei governor masa pen a teel uh ciangin ka pi a lungdam mahmah ahih manin a kap hi.

records.english: Our children's school trip to the national parliament made them very interested in politics.
records.zomi: Gam parliament ah i tate' sang khualzinna in kumpi thu ah a kisapsak mahmah uh hi.

records.english: Each state has its own rules about when children must start school, so my cousins started a year earlier than me.
records.zomi: State khatciat in naupangte sang a kah kipat ding hun thukham tuam a nei ahih manin ka sanggamte kei sangin kum khat ma-in a kipan uh hi.

records.english: My grandfather worked for the state roads department for forty years.
records.zomi: Ka pu in state lampi department ah kum sawmli sung na a sem hi.

records.english: The governor's speech at my school graduation was the first time I heard a politician in person.
records.zomi: Ka sang zawhna pawi-a governor' thugenna pen kumpi thu mi khat ka zak masak pen ahi hi.

records.english: The national government's new child benefit made a real difference to our family's budget.
records.zomi: Gam kumpi' naupang huhna sum thak in i innkuan sum zat ding ah a khelna taktak a bawl hi.

records.english: Our family watched the governor's announcement about the school holidays with great interest.
records.zomi: Sang tawlngak hun tungtang governor' thuzaksak i innkuan in lungsim tak-in i en uh hi.

records.english: Did you know that Grandpa once shook hands with the prime minister?
records.zomi: Pu in prime minister tawh khatvei khut a kilen hi, ci na thei hiam?

records.english: We watched the national election results as a family until midnight.
records.zomi: Zan laizang dong innkuan bup in gam teelna gah i en uh hi.

records.english: Would you really like to be governor when you grow up?
records.zomi: Na lian ciangin governor hih na deih taktak hiam?

records.english: Growing up with a mother in state government and a father in national government made politics part of everyday dinner.
records.zomi: Nu state kumpi ah, pa gam kumpi ah a om lai-a khanglian in kumpi thu ni sim nitak an kihopihna ah a suaksak hi.

records.english: Which office should my parents contact about their land tax?
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in a gam siah tungtang bang office a sam ding uh hiam?

records.english: Our neighbour helped us understand which forms go to the state and which to the national office.
records.zomi: I inn veng in bang lai state ah, bang lai gam office ah a pai ding hiam i theih nadingin hong huh hi.

records.english: Is it the state or the nation that decides the school holidays?
records.zomi: Sang tawlngak hun state in a khensat hiam, gam in a khensat hiam?

records.english: Talking about politics at home helped my children understand the difference between state and national government.
records.zomi: Inn ah kumpi thu kihopih in ka tate in state kumpi leh gam kumpi kikal kibat lohna a thei uh hi.

records.english: Mum, why did you have to go to the capital for your passport?
records.zomi: Nu, bang hangin na passport adingin gam khuapi lian ah na pai kul hiam?

records.english: Because passports are issued by the national government.
records.zomi: Passport te gam kumpi in a pia ahih manin.

records.english: My aunt says the state offices are friendlier than the national ones.
records.zomi: State office te gam office te sangin a nem zaw uh hi, ka ni in a ci hi.

records.english: Thank you for explaining the state housing rules to my parents.
records.zomi: State inn thukhamte ka nu leh ka pa kiangah na genteh manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: My parents argued about the national election for weeks, but they always voted together.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa gam teelna tungtang kal tampi a kiel uh a, ahi zongin vote a khia khawm tawntung uh hi.

records.english: When we visit relatives in another state, Dad always comments on how different their roads are.
records.zomi: State dang-a sanggamte i veh ciangin a lampite uh bangzah a kibang lo hiam Pa in a gen tawntung hi.

records.english: When my parents disagreed about the new law, Dad wanted the state to decide and Mum wanted national rules.
records.zomi: Thukham thak tungtang ka nu leh ka pa a kituak loh uh ciangin Pa in state in a khensat ding a deih a, Nu in gam thukham a deih hi.

records.english: Grandma voted in every national election for sixty years.
records.zomi: Pi in kum sawmguk sung gam teelna khempeuh ah vote a khia hi.

records.english: Grandpa still talks about the day the president visited his village.
records.zomi: President in a khua a veh ni thu Pu in tu dong a gen lai hi.

records.english: When we moved, our state health card wasn't accepted, so we had to apply for a new one.
records.zomi: I pem ciangin i state damna card kipom lo ahih manin a thak i ngen kul uh hi.

records.english: My mother complained to the state transport office about the bus service in our village.
records.zomi: Ka nu in i khua-a bus nasep tungtang state khualzinna office kiangah a phun hi.

records.english: Did your parents vote in the state election last month?
records.zomi: Kha bei-a state teelna ah na nu leh na pa vote a khia uh hiam?

records.english: My mother works for the state education department, and my father for a national ministry.
records.zomi: Ka nu state sinna department ah na a sem a, ka pa gam ministry khat ah na a sem hi.

records.english: My parents met while working in the same national ministry.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa gam ministry kibang ah na a sep lai-un a kimu uh hi.

records.english: Mum, who is in charge of the whole country, the president or the governor?
records.zomi: Nu, gam bup kua in a uk hiam, president hiam governor hiam?

records.english: When my parents moved to another state, they had to apply for new driving licences.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa state dang ah a pem uh ciangin mawtaw mawngna lai thak a ngen kul uh hi.

records.english: Thank you for completing the registration forms for your son.
records.zomi: Na tapa' min gelhna laite na gelh manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: The welfare of the child is the first consideration in all our decisions.
records.zomi: I khensatna khempeuh ah naupang' hoihna a masa pen-in ngaihsut ahi hi.

records.english: Staff are trained in first aid and in the safe handling of medicines.
records.zomi: Nasemte in khut-a damsakna masa leh damdawi bit taka kemzia a kisin uh hi.

records.english: The day centre provides transport for elderly residents who cannot travel alone.
records.zomi: Ni sung kemna mun in amau kia-a pai thei lo upate adingin mawtaw a pia hi.

records.english: Please label all of your child's clothing with their name.
records.zomi: Na naupang' puan khempeuh ah a min gelh in.

records.english: Each care worker must record every visit in the client's daily log.
records.zomi: Kemtu khatciat in a vehna khempeuh a kem mi' ni sim ciamtehna ah a gelh ding hi.

records.english: Who is the named contact for safeguarding at the school?
records.zomi: Sang ah naupang bitna adingin a kisam ding mi kua hiam?

records.english: I am writing to request a review of my father's care package.
records.zomi: Ka pa' kemna kalsuan en kik dingin ka ngen hi.

records.english: Please tell us about any religious or dietary needs your relative may have.
records.zomi: Na sanggam in biakna hiam an nekzia tungtang kisapna a neih leh hong gen in.

records.english: Medication will only be given to children with written permission from a parent.
records.zomi: Nu hiam pa' lai tawh phalna a nei naupangte bek damdawi kipia ding hi.

records.english: What evidence is needed to apply for a disabled parking badge for Grandma?
records.zomi: Pi adingin ki-sial mawtaw koihna lai ngen nadingin bang kipsakna a kisam hiam?

records.english: The home care agency will send a replacement carer if the regular one is ill.
records.zomi: Kemtu a nat leh inn kemna agency in kemtu dang a sawl ding hi.

records.english: Family members may visit the care home at any time between nine and eight.
records.zomi: Innkuan mite zingsang nai kua pan nitak nai giat kikal hun bangkim ah upa kemna inn veh thei uh hi.

records.english: A lasting power of attorney allows a trusted person to make decisions about an elderly relative's care.
records.zomi: Thu khensat theihna lai kizahtak in mi muanhuai khat in sanggam upa khat' kemna tungtang thu a khensat theih nadingin a phal hi.

records.english: The council provides a free assessment for anyone who may need help at home.
records.zomi: Khuapi office in inn ah huhna a kisam thei mi khempeuh adingin man om lo enna a bawl hi.

records.english: Can I see the latest inspection report for the care home?
records.zomi: Upa kemna inn' enna lai thak pen ka en thei ding hiam?

records.english: Certainly, it's on the notice board and on our website.
records.zomi: Thei hi, thuzakna bang tungah leh i website ah a om hi.

records.english: What qualifications does a nanny need?
records.zomi: Naupang kemnu khat in bang sinna a kisam hiam?

records.english: The nursery's safeguarding policy explains what staff must do if they are worried about a child.
records.zomi: Naupang neu sang' naupang bitna thukham in nasemte naupang khat tungtang a lungkham uh leh bang a bawl ding uh hiam a genteh hi.

records.english: Carers who look after someone for more than thirty-five hours a week may be entitled to an allowance in some countries.
records.zomi: Gam pawl khat ah kal khat-in nai sawmthum leh nga val mi khat a kem kemtute in huhna sum a ngah thei uh hi.

records.english: The law requires a minimum number of staff for every group of young children.
records.zomi: Naupang neu pawl khatciat adingin nasem zah niam pen thukham in a ngen hi.

records.english: The care home holds a meeting for families every three months.
records.zomi: Upa kemna inn in kha thum simin innkuante adingin kikhopna a bawl hi.

records.english: The care plan sets out what help your father will receive each day.
records.zomi: Kemna kalsuan in na pa ni simin bang huhna a ngah ding hiam a gen hi.

records.english: Please allow us forty-eight hours to process your application.
records.zomi: Na ngetna en nadingin nai sawmli leh giat hong pia un.

records.english: The nursery is inspected regularly by the national education authority.
records.zomi: Naupang neu sang gam sinna makaipawl in ciangtan-in a en hi.

records.english: If you are unable to collect your child, please telephone the nursery as soon as possible.
records.zomi: Na naupang na lak theih kei leh naupang neu sang manlang thei pen-in phone tawh sam in.

records.english: Residents and their families are invited to the quarterly care review meeting.
records.zomi: Tenna mite leh a innkuante uh kha thum sim kemna enkikna kikhopna ah kisam uh hi.

records.english: We regret to inform you that there is currently a waiting list for day centre places.
records.zomi: Tu laitakin ni sung kemna mun ah mun ngakna list a om hi, ci-in lungkham takin kong gen hi.

records.english: Under our policy, no adult is ever left alone with a child behind a closed door.
records.zomi: I thukham bangin kongkhak kikhak nung ah mi upa khat naupang khat tawh a kia-in om ngei lo ding hi.

records.english: All childminders must be registered with the local authority.
records.zomi: Naupang kemtu khempeuh khua makaipawl ah kigelh ding hi.

records.english: Do care workers need to wear a uniform during home visits?
records.zomi: Kemtute inn vehna ah puan kibang a silh kul uh hiam?

records.english: Kindly inform the nursery in writing if your child has any allergies.
records.zomi: Na naupang in natna ciat a neih leh naupang neu sang kiangah lai tawh gen in.

records.english: Please let the office know if your relative's needs change.
records.zomi: Na sanggam' kisapnate a kikheel leh office kiangah gen in.

records.english: The care home contract sets out the fees and the notice period.
records.zomi: Upa kemna inn contract in a man leh khak ma-a gen ding hun a gen hi.

records.english: Foster carers receive training before a child is placed with them.
records.zomi: Naupang kemtu nu leh pate in naupang khat a kiangah a kikoih ma-in sinna a ngah uh hi.

records.english: Can the council help us adapt the bathroom for my mother's wheelchair?
records.zomi: Ka nu' wheelchair adingin kisilna inn kheel nadingin khuapi office in hong huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Your mother's care needs will be reviewed again in six months.
records.zomi: Na nu' kemna kisapnate kha guk sungin en kik ding hi.

records.english: Any concerns about an elderly person's safety can be reported to adult social services.
records.zomi: Mi upa khat' bitna tungtang lungkhamna khempeuh mi upa huhna office kiangah kigen thei hi.

records.english: Children must be collected by six o'clock, or a late fee will be charged.
records.zomi: Naupangte nai guk ma-in kila ding a, a hih kei leh a nunung man kila ding hi.

records.english: The council has approved funding for three home visits a week.
records.zomi: Khuapi office in kal khat-in inn vehna thum adingin sum a pom hi.

records.english: Does the nursery close on public holidays?
records.zomi: Mipi tawlngak nite-in naupang neu sang a kikhak hiam?

records.english: Please provide your child's immunisation record when you register.
records.zomi: Na min gelh ciangin na naupang' kidawnna damdawi ciamtehna pia in.

records.english: Every member of staff at the nursery has had a background check.
records.zomi: Naupang neu sang-a nasem khempeuh a tangthu kisit khin hi.

records.english: Young carers can get support through their school and the local council.
records.zomi: Kemtu khangnote in a sang leh khua khuapi office tungtawn-in huhna a ngah thei uh hi.

records.english: Please sign the consent form so that the nursery can give your child sunscreen.
records.zomi: Naupang neu sang in na naupang ni khuhna cream a piak theih nadingin phalna lai tungah min gelh in.

records.english: All new residents receive a welcome pack explaining the home's routines.
records.zomi: Tenna thak khempeuh in inn' ni sim ngeinate a genteh kimuakna bawm a ngah uh hi.

records.english: Who should I contact to request a carer's assessment?
records.zomi: Kemtu enna ngen dingin kua ka sam ding hiam?

records.english: Parents will be informed immediately if their child becomes unwell.
records.zomi: Naupang a nat leh nu leh pate manlang takin kigen ding hi.

records.english: Accidents involving children must be recorded and reported to parents on the same day.
records.zomi: Naupangte tunga thupiang lauhuaite ni kibang-in kigelh-a nu leh pate kiangah kigen ding hi.

records.english: Childcare vouchers can be used to pay for registered childminders.
records.zomi: Naupang kemna voucher te kigelh naupang kemtute man piak nadingin kizang thei hi.

records.english: The care agency must give at least two weeks' notice before ending the contract.
records.zomi: Kemna agency in contract a khak ma-in kal nih pan a gen masa ding hi.

records.english: Every resident has the right to privacy and to be treated with dignity.
records.zomi: Tenna mi khatciat in a mimal hun nei theihna leh zahtak taka kibawl theihna a nei hi.

records.english: Is my mother eligible for financial help with the cost of her care?
records.zomi: Ka nu in a kemna man adingin sum huhna a ngah thei ding hiam?

records.english: That depends on her income and savings, which we will assess.
records.zomi: Tua pen a sum ngah leh a sum kemsa tungah kinga a, tua i en ding hi.

records.english: May I bring my grandmother's own furniture to her room?
records.zomi: Ka pi' khan ah amah mah innsung vante ka paipih thei ding hiam?

records.english: A social worker will carry out a needs assessment before any care services are arranged.
records.zomi: Kemna nasep bangmah a kibawl ma-in mipi huhna nasem in kisapna enna khat a bawl ding hi.

records.english: Children may be collected from the after-school club only by named adults.
records.zomi: Sang khit-a naupang kemna pan min kigelh mi upate bek in naupangte a la thei uh hi.

records.english: A respite care place may be offered to give family carers a short break.
records.zomi: Innkuan kemtute tawlngak tomno a ngah nadingin hun tom kemna mun kipia thei hi.

records.english: The occupational therapist assessed the house and recommended several changes to the bathroom.
records.zomi: Nasep damsakna siavuan in inn a en a, kisilna inn ah kikheelna tampi a gen hi.

records.english: Complaints about care services should first be raised with the manager.
records.zomi: Kemna nasep tungtang phunnate makaipa kiangah gen masa ding hi.

records.english: When my father went back to see the surgeon, he was very nervous.
records.zomi: Ka pa zatui siavuan mu dingin a pai kik ciangin a lau mahmah hi.

records.english: The surgeon looked at the scan, smiled, and said the operation had been a complete success.
records.zomi: Zatui siavuan in scan a en a, a nuih a, zatui a lawhcing bup hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Dad called every one of his children from the car park to share the news.
records.zomi: Pa in mawtaw koihna mun pan a tate khempeuh thu thak gen dingin a sam hi.

records.english: Supporting a relative through months of follow-up visits can be tiring for the whole family.
records.zomi: Kha tampi sung a zom vehnate ah sanggam khat huh pen innkuan bup adingin a gimhuai thei hi.

records.english: I take notes during Dad's follow-ups, because he only remembers the good news.
records.zomi: Pa' zom vehnate ah ka ciamteh hi, thu hoih bek a phawk ahih manin.

records.english: Thank you for always remembering our daughter's name at her visits.
records.zomi: A vehna khempeuh ah i tanu' min na phawk tawntung manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: Our son's stitches were checked at the follow-up, and the doctor said he could play football again.
records.zomi: Zom vehna ah i tapa' liamna khui khaute kien a, football a kimawl kik thei hi, ci-in siavuan in a gen hi.

records.english: How was Grandpa's appointment this morning?
records.zomi: Tu zingsang Pu' kimuhna bangci om hiam?

records.english: Mum and I go together to all of Dad's follow-up visits since his heart attack.
records.zomi: Pa' lungtang natna khit pan kipan a zom vehna khempeuh ah Nu leh kei khawm-in i pai uh hi.

records.english: Each follow-up visit reminds us how far Mum has come since her stroke.
records.zomi: Zom vehna khatciat in a lutang natna khit pan Nu bangzah a hoih zaw hiam hong phawk sak hi.

records.english: My son was disappointed when the doctor said his cast had to stay on for two more weeks.
records.zomi: A cast kal nih behlap a om kul hi, ci-in siavuan a cih ciangin ka tapa a lungkia hi.

records.english: Was the doctor happy with your knee this time?
records.zomi: Hih vei-in na khuk tungtang siavuan a lungdam hiam?

records.english: Mum likes to see the same doctor each time, so she always books with Dr. Lian.
records.zomi: Nu in khatvei simin siavuan kibang a muh a deih ahih manin Dr. Lian tawh kimuhna a bawl tawntung hi.

records.english: Let's ask whether the next check-up can be done by phone, because Grandma hates travelling.
records.zomi: Pi in khualzin a uk loh manin a zom damna sitna phone tawh a kibawl thei hiam i dong ding.

records.english: I put a reminder in the family calendar for my son's next ear check.
records.zomi: Ka tapa' bil sitna zom adingin innkuan calendar ah phawksakna ka koih hi.

records.english: Grandpa always takes his best hat to the hospital, even for a short check-up.
records.zomi: Damna sitna tom adingin zong Pu in damdawi inn ah a lukhu hoih pen a paipih tawntung hi.

records.english: The doctor asked my mother whether the family had noticed any changes in her memory.
records.zomi: A phawkna ah kikheelna innkuan in a muh uh hiam siavuan in ka nu a dong hi.

records.english: Seeing my father walk without a stick at his follow-up made the whole family proud.
records.zomi: A zom vehna ah ka pa ciangkhut om lo-in a pai ka muh ciangin innkuan bup a kipak hi.

records.english: Our daughter's asthma check-ups have become easier as she has grown older.
records.zomi: I tanu' huihsan natna damna sitnate a lian semsem ciangin a baih zaw hi.

records.english: Will Grandma need to go back to the hospital after this?
records.zomi: Hih khit ciangin Pi damdawi inn ah a pai kik kul ding hiam?

records.english: Only once more, in three months, so they can check her new hip.
records.zomi: Khatvei bek, kha thum khit ciangin, a khuh guh thak a en theih nadingun.

records.english: My daughter has grown so much that the doctor joked about needing a taller scale.
records.zomi: Ka tanu a sang lua ahih manin gikna tehna sang zaw a kisam hi, ci-in siavuan a kipaih hi.

records.english: After each visit, Grandpa tells us exactly what the doctor said, word for word.
records.zomi: Vehna khatciat khit ciangin siavuan' gen kammal khatciat Pu in hong gen kik hi.

records.english: Do you want me to wait in the car or come in with you?
records.zomi: Mawtaw sungah kong ngak ding na deih hiam, nang tawh ka lut ding hiam?

records.english: The specialist said my father could stop coming every month and come once a year instead.
records.zomi: Ka pa kha simin a pai nawn kul kei a, kum khat-in khatvei hong pai thei hi, ci-in siavuan thupi in a gen hi.

records.english: Next month is Mum's last follow-up visit, and we're planning a small party.
records.zomi: A zom kha pen Nu' zom vehna nunung pen ahi a, pawi neu khat i gelh uh hi.

records.english: We write down every change we notice in Grandpa between appointments.
records.zomi: Kimuhna kikal ah Pu tungah kikheelna i muh khempeuh i gelh uh hi.

records.english: Following up on a child's treatment is easier when both parents know the plan.
records.zomi: Nu leh pa a nih in a kalsuan a theih uh ciangin naupang khat' damdawi zatna zui a baih zaw hi.

records.english: Please remind me to ask about Grandma's sleep at the next appointment.
records.zomi: A zom kimuhna ah Pi' ihmut tungtang dong dingin hong phawk sak in.

records.english: When follow-up visits become routine, it's easy to forget how worried we were at the start.
records.zomi: Zom vehnate ngeina a suah ciangin a kipat lai-in bangzah i lungkham hiam mangngilh a baih hi.

records.english: I'm so glad your results are still good, Dad.
records.zomi: Pa, na sitna gahte a hoih lai ahih manin ka lungdam mahmah hi.

records.english: My sister and I share the job of driving our mother to her follow-up appointments.
records.zomi: Ka u numei leh kei in ka nu a zom kimuhna ah mawtaw tawh paipih nasep i kihawm uh hi.

records.english: Our family doctor sees our son every month until his medicine is right.
records.zomi: A damdawi a kituak dong i innkuan siavuan in kha simin i tapa a mu hi.

records.english: What did the doctor say about your blood sugar, Dad?
records.zomi: Pa, na sisan sung sugar tungtang siavuan in bang a ci hiam?

records.english: It's much better, but she wants me to keep walking every day.
records.zomi: A hoih zaw mahmah hi, ahi zongin ni simin ka peel den ding a deih hi.

records.english: Who's free to drive Grandma to the eye clinic next week?
records.zomi: A zom kal ciangin Pi mit clinic ah mawtaw tawh paipih dingin kua a awng hiam?

records.english: When the results stayed the same at three follow-ups, my parents finally relaxed.
records.zomi: Zom vehna thum ah sitna gahte a kibang den ciangin ka nu leh ka pa a lungmuang tawp uh hi.

records.english: We celebrated when the doctor said our son no longer needed any follow-up visits.
records.zomi: I tapa in zom vehna bangmah a kisam nawn kei hi, ci-in siavuan a cih ciangin i lawm uh hi.

records.english: After the check-up, we always treat the children to an ice cream.
records.zomi: Damna sitna khit ciangin naupangte ice cream i nek sak tawntung uh hi.

records.english: Shall I drive you to the clinic to get your results?
records.zomi: Na sitna gahte la dingin clinic ah mawtaw tawh kong paipih ding hiam?

records.english: My brother lives far away, so he joins Mum's follow-up calls on video.
records.zomi: Ka u pasal gamla ah a teng ahih manin Nu' zom vehna call te video tawh a kihel hi.

records.english: Going to follow-up visits with my parents showed me how much they rely on each other.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa tawh zom vehnate ah pai in bangzah a kingak uh hiam a lak hi.

records.english: Our grandmother insists on cooking for the whole family after every good check-up.
records.zomi: Damna sitna hoih khatciat khit ciangin i pi in innkuan bup adingin an huan dingin a nawh hi.

records.english: At each check-up, the nurse lets our son weigh himself on the big scale.
records.zomi: Damna sitna khatciat ah nurse in i tapa gikna tehna lian tungah amah mah a kiteh sak hi.

records.english: My husband forgets his follow-up visits unless I remind him the night before.
records.zomi: Zan ma-in ka phawk sak kei leh ka pasal in a zom vehnate a mangngilh hi.

records.english: Does the doctor want to see the baby again next month?
records.zomi: Siavuan in a zom kha ciangin naungek a mu kik nuam hiam?

records.english: Auntie Ciin was relieved when the follow-up scan showed that the lump had gone.
records.zomi: A zom scan in a vawk a mang hi, ci a lak ciangin Ni Ciin a lungmuang hi.

records.english: When Dad missed his follow-up visit, the clinic called our house to rebook it.
records.zomi: Pa in a zom vehna a mansuah ciangin clinic in a thak bawl dingin i inn a sam hi.

records.english: Are you nervous about tomorrow's check-up, love?
records.zomi: Ka it, zingciang damna sitna na lau hiam?

records.english: A little, but I'm glad you're coming with me.
records.zomi: Tawmno, ahi zongin nang hong zui ahih manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: My daughter drew a picture for the nurse who had looked after her at every visit.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in vehna khempeuh ah amah a kem nurse adingin lim khat a gelh hi.

records.english: My uncle refuses to go to follow-ups, so his daughter makes the appointments for him.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in zom vehnate ah pai a nial ahih manin a tanu in a kimuhnate a bawl sak hi.

records.english: Did the doctor say the baby's weight is better now?
records.zomi: Naungek' gikna tu-in a hoih zaw hi, siavuan in a ci hiam?

records.english: Yes, she's put on half a kilo in a month.
records.zomi: Ci hi, kha khat sungin kilo a lang a behlap hi.

records.english: The doctor was pleased that my grandmother had kept doing her exercises at home.
records.zomi: Ka pi in inn ah a thadah kisinsaknate a bawl den ahih manin siavuan a lungdam hi.

records.english: My wife and I take a day off together whenever our daughter has a hospital follow-up.
records.zomi: I tanu in damdawi inn zom vehna a neih simin ka zi leh kei khawm-in ni khat tawlngak i la uh hi.

records.english: My brother keeps a folder with copies of all of Dad's test results.
records.zomi: Ka u pasal in Pa' sitna gah khempeuh copy tawh folder khat a kem hi.

records.english: Mum brings her blood pressure notebook to every follow-up.
records.zomi: Nu in zom vehna khempeuh ah a sisan nek ciamtehna lai neu a paipih hi.

records.english: Did anyone write down when Grandma has to go back?
records.zomi: Pi bang hun-in a pai kik ding hiam kuamah in a gelh hiam?

records.english: Could you check if Mum's next appointment is in the morning or the afternoon?
records.zomi: Nu' a zom kimuhna zingsang hiam nitak lam hiam na en thei ding hiam?

records.english: Dad walked to the pharmacy in the rain at midnight to get my sister's medicine.
records.zomi: Ka u numei' damdawi la dingin Pa zan laizang guah tungah damdawi zuakna ah a pai hi.

records.english: Why does Dad always give up the best seat for Grandma?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pa in tutna hoih pen Pi a pia den hiam?

records.english: Our grandmother sewed a quilt for every new baby in the family.
records.zomi: I pi in innkuan-a naungek thak khatciat adingin puanzal khat a khui hi.

records.english: Shall we visit Auntie, who has been feeling lonely since Uncle died?
records.zomi: Pa neu a sih pan a kia-in a om sa Ni i veh ding hiam?

records.english: When my grandmother lost her sight, my cousin started visiting her every Sunday afternoon.
records.zomi: Ka pi a mit a khuaimuh nawn loh ciangin ka sanggam in Nipini sun simin a veh kipan hi.

records.english: She read the newspaper aloud, then the letters from the family abroad.
records.zomi: Thuthak lai aw ngaih takin a sim a, tua khit ciangin gamdang-a innkuante' laite a sim hi.

records.english: Grandma said those afternoons were the brightest part of her week.
records.zomi: Tua sunte pen a kal sungah a vak pen hun ahi hi, Pi in a ci hi.

records.english: My brother remembered my favourite flowers and brought them to my graduation.
records.zomi: Ka u pasal in ka it pen paakte a phawk a, ka sang zawhna pawi ah a paipih hi.

records.english: Can you help your sister with her homework tonight?
records.zomi: Tu zanin na u numei' inn nasep na huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: My son left a thank-you note for the bin collectors on our gate.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in i kongpi ah nawi latute adingin lungdamna lai khat a nusia hi.

records.english: Mum always saves the last piece of cake for whoever had the hardest day.
records.zomi: Nu in cake tawp pen ni haksa pen a nei mi adingin a kem tawntung hi.

records.english: Who gave you that lovely scarf?
records.zomi: Tua ngawngkhih hoih kua in hong pia hiam?

records.english: I'll never forget how my brother sat with me all night when I was frightened.
records.zomi: Ka lauh lai-in ka u pasal in zan bup kei tawh a tut ka mangngilh ngei kei ding hi.

records.english: Small kindnesses at home teach children more than any lecture about kindness.
records.zomi: Inn sung-a hehpihna neute in hehpihna tungtang thugen khatpeuh sangin naupangte a sinsak zaw hi.

records.english: Who cleaned the kitchen while I was asleep?
records.zomi: Ka ihmut laitakin anbuk kua in a siangsak hiam?

records.english: Your brother did, because he knew you were exhausted.
records.zomi: Na u pasal in, na gim mahmah hi, ci a theih manin.

records.english: Did you thank Grandpa for fixing your bicycle?
records.zomi: Na siiksakol a bawl hoih manin Pu lungdam na gen hiam?

records.english: Every night, my father checks that each of us has a blanket.
records.zomi: Zan simin ka pa in i khatciat puan lum a nei hiam a en hi.

records.english: When Mum was ill, my brothers did all the cooking and cleaning without being asked.
records.zomi: Nu a nat ciangin ka u pasalte in kingen lo-in an huan leh siangsak khempeuh a bawl uh hi.

records.english: When I moved to the city, my grandmother sewed some money into the lining of my coat.
records.zomi: Khuapi ah ka pem ciangin ka pi in ka puansilh lian sung lam ah sum tawmno a khui hi.

records.english: Our daughter carried Grandma's shopping up the hill every Saturday.
records.zomi: Kiginni simin i tanu in Pi' van leite mual tungah a puak hi.

records.english: My husband repaired my grandmother's radio without telling anyone.
records.zomi: Ka pasal in kuamah gen lo-in ka pi' radio a bawl hoih hi.

records.english: When I failed my exam, my sister quietly left a note in my bag saying she believed in me.
records.zomi: Ka sitna ka zawh loh ciangin ka u numei in kong um hi, ci lai khat dai takin ka ip sungah a nusia hi.

records.english: My daughter shared her pocket money with her cousin, who had lost his.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in a khut sum a sanggam a mansuah pa tawh a kihawm hi.

records.english: Grandpa's kindest habit was listening without interrupting.
records.zomi: Pu' ngeina hoih pen pen mi gen tatsat lo-in a ngaihkhiatna ahi hi.

records.english: Thank you for always thinking of others first, Mum.
records.zomi: Nu, midangte a masa pen-in na ngaihsun tawntung manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: Dad gets up early every winter morning to warm the car for Mum.
records.zomi: Phalbi zingsang simin Nu adingin mawtaw lumsak dingin Pa a thou ma hi.

records.english: I want to be as generous as my grandmother was.
records.zomi: Ka pi bangin pia nuam ka hih nop hi.

records.english: When our baby was born, my husband's mother cooked for us for a month.
records.zomi: I naungek a suah ciangin ka pasal' nu in kha khat sung an hong huan sak hi.

records.english: Which of your grandparents was the kindest to you?
records.zomi: Na pu leh na pite lak ah kua in hong hehpih pen hiam?

records.english: The kindest thing my father ever did was forgive his brother after years of silence.
records.zomi: Ka pa' bawl hehpihna lian pen pen kum tampi kihopih lo khit ciangin a sanggam pasal a maisak ahi hi.

records.english: Our teenage son taught his grandfather to use the phone, patiently, for weeks.
records.zomi: I tapa tangval no in kal tampi sung thuakzawh takin a pu phone zat a sinsak hi.

records.english: When my parents couldn't afford a wedding cake, the neighbours baked one together.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in mopawi cake a lei zawh loh uh ciangin inn vengte in khat a khawm-in a bawl uh hi.

records.english: Could I borrow your best dress for my job interview?
records.zomi: Ka nasep kidotna adingin na puan hoih pen ka leitawi thei ding hiam?

records.english: My brother gave up his room for a whole year so that Grandma could live with us.
records.zomi: Pi i kiang ah a om theih nadingin ka u pasal in kum khat bup a khan a nusia hi.

records.english: My uncle drove six hours to bring me home when my car broke down.
records.zomi: Ka mawtaw a sia ciangin inn ah hong paipih dingin ka pa neu nai guk sung mawtaw a mawng hi.

records.english: When our house burned down, my uncle's family took us in for six months.
records.zomi: I inn mei a kan ciangin ka pa neu' innkuan in kha guk sung hong teng sak uh hi.

records.english: How can we thank Auntie for looking after us all summer?
records.zomi: Khal bup hong kem manin Ni bangci lungdam i gen thei ding hiam?

records.english: Let's make her a photo album of everything we did.
records.zomi: I bawl khempeuh lim bu khat amah adingin i bawl ding.

records.english: Children learn kindness by watching how their parents treat each other.
records.zomi: Naupangte in a nu leh a pa' kibawlzia en-in hehpihna a sin uh hi.

records.english: Kindness in our family was rarely spoken about, but it was everywhere.
records.zomi: I innkuan ah hehpihna kigen ngei lo deuh a, ahi zongin koi-ah zong a om hi.

records.english: Did our son really spend his birthday money on a present for his little sister?
records.zomi: I tapa in a suahni sum a nau numei adingin letsong lei dingin a zang taktak hiam?

records.english: My wife wrote letters to my mother every week when she was in hospital.
records.zomi: Ka nu damdawi inn ah a om lai-in ka zi in kal simin lai a khak hi.

records.english: Auntie Zam gave her wedding ring to my mother to wear until Dad could buy one.
records.zomi: Pa in khat a lei theih dong a bulh dingin Ni Zam in a zungbuh ka nu a pia hi.

records.english: Shall we make breakfast in bed for Mum on her birthday?
records.zomi: A suahni ciangin Nu adingin lupna tungah zingsang an i bawl ding hiam?

records.english: Looking after each other has kept our family together through very hard times.
records.zomi: Kikem in hun haksa mahmahte sungah i innkuan a kikhawm den sak hi.

records.english: My little brother gave his favourite toy to a child at the hospital.
records.zomi: Ka nau pasal neu in a lawhna van it pen damdawi inn-a naupang khat a pia hi.

records.english: My husband takes our neighbour's son fishing with our boys every Saturday.
records.zomi: Ka pasal in Kiginni simin i inn veng' tapa i tapate tawh nga man dingin a paipih hi.

records.english: My cousin donated blood for my mother's operation.
records.zomi: Ka nu' zatui adingin ka sanggam in a sisan a pia hi.

records.english: My grandparents paid for my school uniform every year without ever mentioning it.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh ka pi in gen ngei lo-in kum simin ka sang puan man a pia uh hi.

records.english: Grandpa taught all of his grandchildren to ride a bike, one by one.
records.zomi: Pu in a tute khempeuh khat zawh khat siiksakol tuang a sinsak hi.

records.english: Grandma always slipped a few coins into our pockets when we said goodbye.
records.zomi: Goodbye i ci ciangin Pi in i puan ip sungah sum kuang tawmno a koih tawntung hi.

records.english: My cousin travelled across the country just to be at my wedding.
records.zomi: Ka mopawi ah a om theih nadingin ka sanggam gam bup a kantan hi.

records.english: Why did you leave flowers on Mum's pillow?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Nu' lukhung tungah paak na koih hiam?

records.english: Because she's been working so hard, and I wanted to surprise her.
records.zomi: Na tampi a sep ahih manin lamdang a sak nadingin ka deih hi.

records.english: My parents still help the poorest family in our village, even though they have little themselves.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in a neih uh a tawm zongin i khua-a innkuan zawng pen a huh lai uh hi.

records.english: Let's leave a cup of tea for Dad on the table before he comes home.
records.zomi: Pa inn a tun ma-in dawhkan tungah niangtui haai khat i koih ding.

records.english: Auntie Hoih sent my parents money every month when Dad was out of work.
records.zomi: Pa nasep a neih loh lai-in Ni Hoih in kha simin ka nu leh ka pa kiangah sum a khak hi.

records.english: Every act of kindness in our family seemed to inspire another.
records.zomi: I innkuan-a hehpihna khatciat in a dang khat a hanthawn bangin a om hi.

records.english: My little sister made a card for every member of the family when Grandpa died.
records.zomi: Pu a sih ciangin ka nau numei in innkuan mi khatciat adingin card khat ciat a bawl hi.

records.english: Because the clinic opened, my grandmother lived to see all her great-grandchildren.
records.zomi: Clinic a kihon ahih manin ka pi in a tu' tate khempeuh a muh dong a nungta hi.

records.english: How old was Grandpa when he finally came home after the war?
records.zomi: Gal khit-a inn a ciah kik tawpna ciangin Pu kum bangzah ahi hiam?

records.english: Our family's recipes changed when new spices became available at the market.
records.zomi: Sumbuk mun ah anlim thakte a om ciangin i innkuan an huanziate a kikheel hi.

records.english: Did Grandma stop grinding maize by hand once the new mill opened?
records.zomi: Buh suatna thak a kihon khit ciangin Pi in khut tawh vaimim a suat nawn kei hiam?

records.english: Do you know why Grandpa speaks three languages?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pu pau thum a gen thei hiam na thei hiam?

records.english: My grandparents moved to the coast because the fishing was good.
records.zomi: Nga man a hoih ahih manin ka pu leh ka pi tuipi gei ah a pem uh hi.

records.english: Did the new school change anything for your family?
records.zomi: Sang thak in na innkuan adingin bangmah a kheel hiam?

records.english: Ask Grandma why she never learned to ride a bicycle.
records.zomi: Bang hangin siiksakol tuang a sin ngei kei hiam Pi dong in.

records.english: Mum became a nurse after watching the doctors who came to the village during an epidemic.
records.zomi: Natna lianpi hun lai-in khua ah hong pai siavuante a muh khit ciangin Nu nurse a suak hi.

records.english: Because my uncle got a scholarship, his younger brothers all believed they could study too.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in sinna sum a ngah ahih manin a nau pasalte khempeuh in amaute zong sin thei hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: When the mine closed, my grandfather lost his job overnight.
records.zomi: Lei kua tou nasepna a kikhak ciangin ka pu zan khat sungin a nasep a mansuah hi.

records.english: He started selling tea at the bus station to feed his six children.
records.zomi: A tate guk a vak theih nadingin bus khawlna mun ah niangtui a zuak kipan hi.

records.english: That small tea stall later became the shop my father runs today.
records.zomi: Tua niangtui zuakna neu pen a nung ciangin tu-in ka pa' kem sumbuk ah a suak hi.

records.english: What was the effect of the new factory on your family, Grandpa?
records.zomi: Pu, factory thak in na innkuan tungah bang a piangsak hiam?

records.english: Grandpa believes that one good harvest changed the fortunes of his whole family.
records.zomi: Buh lak hoih khat in a innkuan bup' nuntakna a kheel hi, ci-in Pu in a um hi.

records.english: Every change in my family's history seems to have started with someone moving.
records.zomi: Ka innkuan tangthu-a kikheelna khempeuh mi khat' pemna tawh a kipan bangin a om hi.

records.english: Because Grandpa's village got a school, he was the first in his family to read.
records.zomi: Pu' khua in sang a ngah ahih manin a innkuan sung ah laisim thei masa pen ahi hi.

records.english: My parents met because the railway brought my father to my mother's town.
records.zomi: Meileng lampi in ka pa ka nu' khua ah a tun sak ahih manin ka nu leh ka pa a kimu uh hi.

records.english: Our village grew quickly after the bus route reached it.
records.zomi: Bus lampi a tun khit ciangin i khua manlang takin a khang hi.

records.english: Looking at our family's history helps me see how big events affected ordinary people.
records.zomi: I innkuan tangthu en in thupiang lianpite in mi nautangte bangci a khoih hiam ka theih nadingin hong huh hi.

records.english: My grandmother's decision to send her daughters to school changed our family for generations.
records.zomi: A tanute sang ah sawl ding ka pi' khensatna in i innkuan khang tampi sung a kheel hi.

records.english: A single decision by my grandfather changed where all of his grandchildren grew up.
records.zomi: Ka pu' khensatna khat bek in a tute khempeuh koi ah a khangkhia ding uh hiam a kheel hi.

records.english: Because my parents lived through hard times, they taught us to save every coin.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa hun haksa a thuak uh ahih manin sum kuang khatciat kem dingin hong sinsak uh hi.

records.english: My aunt became a teacher because the government opened a college in her district.
records.zomi: Kumpi in a district ah college khat a hon ahih manin ka ni saya a suak hi.

records.english: When the school started teaching girls, my grandmother's life changed completely.
records.zomi: Sang in nungakte a sinsak kipat ciangin ka pi' nuntakna a kikheel bup hi.

records.english: What happened to Grandpa's farm when the dam was built?
records.zomi: Tui khakna a kilam ciangin Pu' lou bang a piang hiam?

records.english: The water covered his fields, and the family had to move up the hill.
records.zomi: Tui in a lou te a khuh a, innkuan mual tung lam ah a pem kul uh hi.

records.english: Why did our family move to the city?
records.zomi: Bang hangin i innkuan khuapi ah a pem hiam?

records.english: The factory where Grandpa worked closed, so he had to find new work.
records.zomi: Pu' nasepna factory a kikhak ahih manin nasep thak a zong kul hi.

records.english: Dad's first job came about because a neighbour recommended him.
records.zomi: Inn veng khat in a gen sak ahih manin Pa' nasep masa pen a ngah hi.

records.english: Grandpa got his first bicycle because he won a prize at school.
records.zomi: Sang ah letsong a ngah ahih manin Pu in a siiksakol masa pen a ngah hi.

records.english: Many families in our town have relatives abroad because of the hard years after the war.
records.zomi: Gal khit-a kum haksate hangin i khua-a innkuan tampi in gamdang ah sanggam a nei uh hi.

records.english: The cheap flights that started in the 1990s meant our relatives abroad could visit every year.
records.zomi: 1990 kumte-a kipan man niam vanleng hangin gamdang-a i sanggamte kum simin hong veh thei uh hi.

records.english: Our family business grew because the market moved closer to our street.

records.english: Was it the new law that allowed Grandma to own land?
records.zomi: Pi in gam a neih theih nadingin a phal pen thukham thak ahi hiam?

records.english: Dad, why did you leave school so early?

records.english: Why did Great-Grandpa change his name when he arrived in the new country?
records.zomi: Bang hangin gam thak a tun ciangin Pu upa in a min a kheel hiam?

records.english: Ask your parents what changed in their lives when the internet arrived.
records.zomi: Internet a tun ciangin a nuntakna uh ah bang a kikheel hiam na nu leh na pa dong in.

records.english: My great-grandmother's illness led the whole family to move closer to the hospital.
records.zomi: Ka pi upa' natna hangin innkuan bup damdawi inn kiang zaw ah a pem uh hi.

records.english: Because Dad's company sent him abroad, I grew up speaking two languages.
records.zomi: Pa' company in gamdang ah a sawl ahih manin pau nih gen-in ka khangkhia hi.

records.english: We live in this house because my great-grandfather bought the land a hundred years ago.

records.english: Mum says that television changed how her family spent their evenings.
records.zomi: Television in a innkuan' nitak zatzia a kheel hi, Nu in a ci hi.

records.english: The new bridge meant my father could visit his parents every weekend.
records.zomi: Lei thak hangin ka pa in kal tawp simin a nu leh a pa a veh thei hi.

records.english: When the government built the road, my father's village was finally connected to the city.
records.zomi: Kumpi in lampi a lam ciangin ka pa' khua khuapi tawh a kizom tawp hi.

records.english: The mobile phone meant Mum could call her sister abroad every week instead of writing letters.
records.zomi: Mobile phone hangin Nu in lai gelh sangin kal simin gamdang-a a u numei a sam thei hi.

records.english: The family moved twice because of my father's job with the railway.
records.zomi: Ka pa' meileng nasep hangin innkuan nihvei a pem uh hi.

records.english: Why did your family keep the old house in the village?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na innkuan in khua-a inn lui a kem uh hiam?

records.english: The family stopped farming when my uncle went to university and never came back.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu sangpi ah a pai a, a ciah kik ngei loh ciangin innkuan in lou bawl a tawp uh hi.

records.english: The drought of my grandfather's childhood is the reason he never wastes water.

records.english: Did you and Mum choose this town because of the secondary school?
records.zomi: High school hangin nang leh Nu in hih khua na teel uh hiam?

records.english: What made Grandpa decide to leave the army?
records.zomi: Bang in Pu galkap nusia dingin a khensat sak hiam?

records.english: The earthquake destroyed my grandparents' home, so they rebuilt it with stronger walls.
records.zomi: Lei ling in ka pu leh ka pi' inn a siatsak ahih manin kulh hat zaw tawh a lam kik uh hi.

records.english: Mum learned English because foreign companies started opening offices in her city.
records.zomi: Gamdang company te in a khuapi ah office a hon kipat uh ahih manin Nu in English a sin hi.

records.english: A good teacher in my father's village is the reason he became a doctor.
records.zomi: Ka pa' khua-a saya hoih khat hangin ka pa siavuan a suak hi.

records.english: Because of the new hospital, my little brother was born safely in town instead of at home.
records.zomi: Damdawi inn thak hangin ka nau pasal neu inn ah hi lo-in khuapi ah bit takin a suak hi.

records.english: The new road meant my grandmother could finally sell her vegetables in town.
records.zomi: Lampi thak hangin ka pi in a anteh khuapi ah a zuak thei tawp hi.

records.english: Our relatives on the island visited less often after the old ferry stopped running.
records.zomi: Tembaw lui a tawp khit ciangin tuikulh-a i sanggamte tawm zaw-in hong veh uh hi.

records.english: If electricity hadn't come to the village, my mother would have stayed at home instead of training as a nurse.
records.zomi: Khua ah meivak a tun kei le ka nu nurse sinna ah pai lo-in inn ah a om ding hi.

records.english: My great-grandparents had to leave everything behind at the start of the war.

records.english: Because the train came to our town, my mother's family opened a small hotel.
records.zomi: Meileng i khua a tun ahih manin ka nu' innkuan in zinbuuk neu khat a hon uh hi.

records.english: My brother didn't think about the consequences when he bought a motorbike, and now he can't pay for it.

records.english: What happens if I don't finish my homework tonight?

records.english: You'll have to explain to your teacher and do it at break.
records.zomi: Na saya kiangah na genteh ding a, tawlngak hun-in na bawl ding hi.

records.english: What could happen if you lend your brother that much money?
records.zomi: Na u pasal tua zah sum na leitawi leh bang a piang thei ding hiam?

records.english: He might not pay it back for years, and that could hurt your marriage.
records.zomi: Kum tampi sung a piak kik kei kha ding a, tua in na innkuan a khoih thei hi.

records.english: Would it hurt your brother's feelings if we invited only you?
records.zomi: Nangmah bek i sam leh na u pasal' lungsim a na ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, so please invite both of us.
records.zomi: Na ding hi, tua ahih manin i nih in hong sam un.

records.english: Weighing up the effects on everyone in the family takes time, but it prevents regret.

records.english: We decided against the cheaper flat because the children would have had to change schools.

records.english: If Grandpa moves in with us, where will he sleep?

records.english: In the study, if we move the desk to our bedroom.
records.zomi: Sinna khan ah, dawhkan i lupna khan ah i suan leh.

records.english: Before we bought the puppy, we talked about who would walk it every day.
records.zomi: Ui no i lei ma-in ni simin kua in a paipih ding hiam i kihopih uh hi.

records.english: If I stop piano lessons now, can I start again later?
records.zomi: Tu-in piano sinna ka tawp leh a nung ciangin ka kipan kik thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, but you'll have forgotten a lot.
records.zomi: Thei hi, ahi zongin tampi na mangngilh khin ding hi.

records.english: My grandparents taught us to ask who else might be affected before making a choice.
records.zomi: Khensatna khat i bawl ma-in kua dang tungah a gah ding hiam dot dingin ka pu leh ka pi in hong sinsak uh hi.

records.english: Every choice a parent makes about work affects the children in some way.
records.zomi: Nu hiam pa khat' nasep tungtang teelna khempeuh in naupangte bangci peuhmah-in a khoih hi.

records.english: If we all go to the wedding abroad, who will feed the animals?

records.english: Have you thought about how moving schools will affect your little sister?
records.zomi: Sang kheel in na nau numei bangci a khoih ding hiam na ngaihsun hiam?

records.english: Do you really want to give up your holiday to babysit for your cousin?

records.english: Before agreeing to host the wedding, my parents counted how many people the house could hold.
records.zomi: Mopawi bawl ding a pom ma-un ka nu leh ka pa in inn in mi bangzah a koih zo hiam a sim uh hi.

records.english: What happens if the twins share a room?
records.zomi: Apengte khan khat a kihawm uh leh bang a piang ding hiam?

records.english: They'll fight at first, but they may become closer.
records.zomi: A kipat ciangin a kisual ding uh a, ahi zongin a kinaih zaw thei uh hi.

records.english: When my sister wanted to leave university, Dad asked her to imagine her life five years later.
records.zomi: Ka u numei sangpi nusia a deih ciangin kum nga khit-a a nuntakna ngaihsun dingin Pa in a ngen hi.

records.english: Our family made a list of what we would gain and lose by moving to the coast.

records.english: What would happen to the shop if Dad retired next year?
records.zomi: Pa kum zom ciangin nasep a tawp leh sumbuk bang a piang ding hiam?

records.english: I'd have to run it, or we'd have to sell it.
records.zomi: Kei in ka kem kul ding a, a hih kei leh i zuak kul ding hi.

records.english: My uncle regretted selling the family land, because his sons later wanted to farm it.
records.zomi: A tapate in a nung ciangin lou bawl a deih uh ahih manin innkuan gam zuak ka pa neu a lungkham hi.

records.english: If I move to the city for work, will Grandma manage without me?

records.english: Your brother and I can help her, but we'll need you at weekends.
records.zomi: Na u pasal leh kei in i huh thei a, ahi zongin kal tawp ciangin nang i kisam ding hi.

records.english: What will happen if we let the children stay up late every night?

records.english: They'll be tired and grumpy at school.

records.english: What if Grandma can't manage the stairs in the new house?
records.zomi: Inn thak ah Pi in kahlei a kah zo kei leh bangci ding hiam?

records.english: Then we'll make the room downstairs into her bedroom.
records.zomi: Tua ciangin nuai lam khan a lupna khan-in i bawl ding hi.

records.english: What would happen if we let the children choose their own bedtime for a week?

records.english: What will the neighbours say if we cut down the old tree?

records.english: They might be sad, because the children have always played under it.
records.zomi: Naupangte a nuai ah a kimawl tawntung uh ahih manin a lungkham kha ding uh hi.

records.english: When my husband wanted to work abroad, we asked what it would mean for the children.
records.zomi: Ka pasal gamdang ah na sem a deih ciangin naupangte adingin bang cihna hi ding hiam i kidong uh hi.

records.english: How would you feel if your best friend told everyone your secret?
records.zomi: Na lawm hoih pen in na thuguk mi khempeuh kiangah a gen leh bangci na sa ding hiam?

records.english: Terrible, so I won't tell anyone hers.
records.zomi: A hoih lo mahmah ding, tua ahih manin amah' thuguk kuamah kiangah ka gen kei ding hi.

records.english: What happens to the baby's routine if we travel during the holidays?

records.english: It will be upset for a few days, but she'll settle again.
records.zomi: Ni tawmno sung a buai ding a, ahi zongin a nem kik ding hi.

records.english: Will Dad be angry if I tell him about the broken window?
records.zomi: Tohkhawng kitam thu Pa ka gen leh a heh ding hiam?

records.english: Less angry than if he finds out himself.
records.zomi: Amah mah in a theih sangin a heh tawm zaw ding hi.

records.english: If we spend the savings on a car, what will we do if the roof leaks again?
records.zomi: Sum kemsa mawtaw lei dingin i zat leh innkhum a zui kik ciangin bang i bawl ding hiam?

records.english: Mum always says that a decision made in a hurry is paid for slowly.
records.zomi: Kinawh taka khensatna khat dahdah-in man kipia hi, Nu in a ci tawntung hi.

records.english: Thinking about the consequences together helped our family make a calmer decision.
records.zomi: A gah ding khawm-in ngaihsut in i innkuan lungnem zaw takin thu a khensat theih nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: How will your mother feel if we don't visit her this Christmas?
records.zomi: Hih Christmas ciangin i veh kei leh na nu bangci a sa ding hiam?

records.english: Is it worth getting a dog if nobody is home during the day?
records.zomi: Sun sungin kuamah inn ah a om kei leh ui khat neih a phatuam ding hiam?

records.english: If you stay out late, how will we know you're safe?
records.zomi: Zan nung dong na om leh na bit hiam bangci i thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: I'll send you a message when I get to the party and when I leave.
records.zomi: Pawi ah ka tun ciangin leh ka pai ciangin message kong khak ding hi.

records.english: What will the children lose if we move abroad?
records.zomi: Gamdang ah i pem leh naupangte in bang a mansuah ding uh hiam?

records.english: Their friends and their grandparents nearby, at least for a while.
records.zomi: A lawmte uh leh a kiang-a a pu leh a pite uh, hun tawmno sung bek zong.

records.english: Considering how a decision will affect elderly relatives is part of being a responsible adult.
records.zomi: Khensatna khat in sanggam upate bangci a khoih ding hiam ngaihsut pen mawhpuakna nei mi upa hihna sung-a khat ahi hi.

records.english: My parents worried about what would happen to the farm if none of us stayed.
records.zomi: Kuamah a om kei leh lou bang a piang ding hiam ka nu leh ka pa a lungkham uh hi.

records.english: Shall we give it a month and then see how the new routine is working?
records.zomi: Kha khat sung i zang a, tua khit ciangin ni sim ngeina thak bangci a sem hiam i en ding hiam?

records.english: Choosing a school far away meant our son would spend two hours a day on the bus.
records.zomi: Sang gamla khat teel in i tapa ni simin nai nih bus sungah a om ding cihna ahi hi.

records.english: Will it upset Auntie if we don't go to her party?
records.zomi: A pawi ah i pai kei leh Ni a lungkham ding hiam?

records.english: Probably, so let's at least call and explain.
records.zomi: Lungkham ding hi, tua ahih manin i sam-in i genteh ding.

records.english: Would buying a bigger house mean we couldn't afford holidays?
records.zomi: Inn lian zaw lei in tawlngak hun adingin sum i nei nawn lo ding cihna ahi ding hiam?

records.english: For a few years, yes, but the children would have their own rooms.
records.zomi: Kum tawmno sung ahi ding, ahi zongin naupangte in khan tuam a nei ding uh hi.

records.english: On the morning of the ceremony, the graduates must collect their gowns by eight.
records.zomi: Pawi zingsang ciangin sang zo thakte in nai giat ma-in a puan sau uh a la ding uh hi.

records.english: Staff working with food must remove all jewellery before starting their shift.

records.english: The national anthem is played every morning before work begins at the ministry.

records.english: Is there an extra charge for breakfast in the dining room?

records.english: Personal protective equipment must be put on before entering the construction site.

records.english: The school bell rings at eight, and registration begins five minutes later.
records.zomi: Sang khuang nai giat ciangin a ging a, minit nga khit ciangin min sapna kipan hi.

records.english: Please return all keys and towels to reception by eleven o'clock on the day of departure.

records.english: The ceremony will start at ten sharp, so guests are asked to be seated by a quarter to ten.
records.zomi: Pawi nai sawm taktak ciangin kipan ding ahih manin mikhualte nai sawm kimlo minit sawm leh nga ciangin tu dingin kingen hi.

records.english: Candidates must bring photo identification to the examination hall.

records.english: Pupils must arrive in full school uniform, including the school tie.

records.english: Each soldier is responsible for keeping his or her uniform clean and pressed.

records.english: What is the dress code for the embassy reception?

records.english: Dark suits for men and formal dresses or national dress for women.
records.zomi: Pasalte adingin suit dum, numeite adingin puan kizahtak hiam gam puan.

records.english: The bride's family began getting ready at dawn on the morning of the official wedding.

records.english: Please make sure that your passport is in your hand luggage, not in your suitcase.

records.english: Officers are expected to be clean-shaven and in full uniform at the morning inspection.

records.english: Do I need to bring my own towel to the hostel?

records.english: Could I have a wake-up call at half past five, please?

records.zomi: Thei hi, Pu; nai nga leh minit sawmthum ciangin na khan kong sam ding hi.

records.english: A shower and fresh clothes will be provided for each patient after the procedure.
records.zomi: Damdawi bawlna khit ciangin natpa khatciat kisilna leh puan thak kipia ding hi.

records.english: Recruits are woken at six and must be dressed and on parade by six thirty.

records.english: Can the hotel arrange a taxi to the airport for six o'clock?

records.english: Clean clothes and a tidy appearance are expected of all staff who meet the public.

records.english: Morning assembly is held in the main hall every Monday.

records.english: Kindly leave your room key at reception when you go out.

records.english: Students who arrive late must sign the late book at the office.

records.english: Breakfast is served in the dining room from seven until half past nine.
records.zomi: An nekna khan ah zingsang an nai sagih pan nai kua leh a lang dong kipia hi.

records.english: All athletes must report to the call room forty minutes before their event.

records.english: Witnesses should dress respectfully when they appear in court.

records.english: Patients having surgery should not eat anything after midnight on the night before the operation.

records.english: Before the state visit, the palace staff prepared the guest rooms down to the last detail.

records.english: Members of parliament are expected to dress formally in the chamber.
records.zomi: Parliament mite in kikhopna khan ah puan kizahtak a silh ding uh hi.

records.english: Are visitors allowed to wear shorts in the government building?
records.zomi: Kumpi building ah vehte in kekawm tom a silh thei uh hiam?

records.english: The ward lights are switched on at seven, and the doctors begin their rounds at eight.
records.zomi: Natpa khan meivakte nai sagih ciangin kihong a, nai giat ciangin siavuante in a vak kipan uh hi.

records.english: Guests who require a wake-up call should inform reception before ten o'clock at night.

records.english: Please remove all make-up and nail polish before the operation.

records.english: The school's policy on hair states that long hair must be tied back.

records.english: The morning briefing for all staff begins promptly at eight fifteen.

records.english: The visiting delegation will be collected from their hotel at eight thirty.

records.english: Did you give the dog his worm tablet this month?
records.zomi: Hih kha ui a gil-a lungno damdawi na pia hiam?

records.english: My wife and I agreed that only one of us would give the baby her medicine, to avoid giving it twice.
records.zomi: Nihvei a kipiak loh nadingin naungek' damdawi i lak ah khat bek in a pia ding hi, ci-in ka zi leh kei i kituak uh hi.

records.english: My son doesn't like the taste of his medicine, so we mix it with a little yogurt.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in a damdawi limna a uk loh manin yogurt tawmno tawh i kiat uh hi.

records.english: Mum keeps a small notebook in her bag with the names of everything Dad takes.
records.zomi: Nu in a ip sung-a lai neu khat ah Pa' nek khempeuh min a gelh hi.

records.english: My little sister thinks vitamins are sweets, so we hide them.
records.zomi: Ka nau numei in vitamin pen an khum ahi hi, a ci ahih manin i sel uh hi.

records.english: Thank you for showing my father how to use his new inhaler.
records.zomi: Ka pa kiangah a inhaler thak zatzia na lak manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: Please don't let the children help themselves to vitamins, because too many can be harmful.
records.zomi: A tam lua in a siatna a om thei ahih manin naupangte amau mah-in vitamin la kei sak un.

records.english: Grandpa's new tablets must not be taken with grapefruit juice.
records.zomi: Pu' damdawi thakte grapefruit tui tawh kine lo ding hi.

records.english: My brother forgot his medicine on holiday, so we had to find a doctor abroad.
records.zomi: Ka u pasal in tawlngak hun ah a damdawi a mangngilh ahih manin gamdang ah siavuan i zong kul uh hi.

records.english: Is this cream for your face or for your hands, Grandma?
records.zomi: Pi, hih cream na mai adingin hiam, na khut adingin hiam?

records.english: Never give a child medicine meant for adults.
records.zomi: Mi upate adinga damdawi naupang khat pia ngei kei in.

records.english: Our children know that medicine is never a treat.
records.zomi: Damdawi pen an khum ngei lo hi, ci i tate in a thei uh hi.

records.english: We always carry Grandpa's spray for chest pain when we go out.
records.zomi: I pusuak ciangin Pu' awm natna adinga spray i paipih tawntung uh hi.

records.english: My son's school keeps a spare inhaler for him in the office.
records.zomi: Ka tapa' sang in office ah amah adingin inhaler behlap khat a kem hi.

records.english: My daughter learned to measure her own medicine with the little syringe.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in syringe neu tawh amah' damdawi teh a sin hi.

records.english: My mother writes the date she opened each bottle on the label.
records.zomi: Ka nu in bel khatciat a hon ni a min gelhna tungah a gelh hi.

records.english: Shall I check the expiry date on the medicine before we give it to the baby?
records.zomi: Naungek i piak ma-in damdawi' a hun beina ni ka en ding hiam?

records.english: My mother never stops a medicine without asking her doctor first.
records.zomi: Ka nu in a siavuan dot masa lo-in damdawi khat a ne tawp ngei kei hi.

records.english: Do you know where Mum keeps the thermometer?
records.zomi: Nu in lumna tehna koi ah a koih hiam na thei hiam?

records.english: My father takes his heart tablets at the same time as his morning tea.
records.zomi: Ka pa in a lungtang damdawi a zingsang niangtui tawh hun kibang-in a ne hi.

records.english: Should Grandma keep her eye drops in the fridge?
records.zomi: Pi in a mit damdawi fridge sungah a kem ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, once the bottle has been opened.
records.zomi: Kem ding hi, bel a kihon khit ciangin.

records.english: A shared family list of everyone's medicines helped the doctors when Grandma was rushed to hospital.
records.zomi: Pi damdawi inn ah manlang taka a kipaipih ciangin mi khempeuh' damdawi innkuan list khat in siavuante a huh hi.

records.english: Can I give my daughter the same cough syrup as her older brother?
records.zomi: Ka tanu a u pasal' khuk damdawi tui kibang ka pia thei hiam?

records.english: Only if the label says it's suitable for her age.
records.zomi: A min gelhna in a kum adingin a kilawm hi, a cih leh bek.

records.english: My parents label their tablets with big letters so they don't mix them up.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in a damdawite a kizawh loh nadingun laimal lian tawh min a gelh uh hi.

records.english: My wife reads the leaflet for every new medicine before anyone in the family takes it.
records.zomi: Innkuan sung kuamah in a nek ma-in ka zi in damdawi thak khatciat' lai neu a sim hi.

records.english: Last winter, my son had an ear infection and was given antibiotics for a week.
records.zomi: Phalbi bei-in ka tapa in bil natna a nei a, kal khat sung antibiotics a kipia hi.

records.english: After three days he felt fine and begged us to stop the medicine.
records.zomi: Ni thum khit ciangin a hoih ta a, damdawi tawp dingin hong ngen den hi.

records.english: We kept giving it until the bottle was empty, as the doctor had told us.
records.zomi: Siavuan in hong gen bangin bel a bei dong i pia den uh hi.

records.english: My husband sets the oven clock to remind him when his next dose is due.
records.zomi: Ka pasal in a zom damdawi nek hun a phawk nadingin oven nai a koih hi.

records.english: Giving medicine to a sick toddler often takes two adults.
records.zomi: Naupang neu khat a nat ciangin damdawi piak in mi upa nih a kisam zel hi.

records.english: If the baby is sick within an hour of taking her medicine, should we give it again?
records.zomi: Naungek in a damdawi a nek khit nai khat sungin a lok leh a pia kik ding i hi hiam?

records.english: When Mum started a new medicine, we asked the pharmacist whether it would affect her other tablets.
records.zomi: Nu in damdawi thak a nek kipat ciangin a damdawi dangte a khoih ding hiam damdawi zuakpa i dong uh hi.

records.english: Our son's dose of fever medicine depends on his weight, so the nurse weighed him first.
records.zomi: I tapa' lumna damdawi zah a gikna tungah kinga ahih manin nurse in a masa-in a gikna a teh hi.

records.english: When our son needed injections every day, a nurse taught us how to give them at home.
records.zomi: I tapa in ni simin damdawi sutna a kisam ciangin nurse khat in inn ah bangci pia ding hiam hong sinsak hi.

records.english: How many hours should we wait between doses of the children's painkiller?
records.zomi: Naupangte' na-dalna damdawi nek kikal ah nai bangzah i ngak ding hiam?

records.english: When Dad's prescription changed, we made sure the old tablets were taken back to the pharmacy.
records.zomi: Pa' damdawi lai a kikheel ciangin damdawi luite damdawi zuakna ah kiap kik hiam i en uh hi.

records.english: Auntie Lun once took her husband's tablets by mistake because the boxes looked the same.
