records.zomi: Pu a puk ciangin lauhuai nambat i sam uh a, tua khit ciangin naupangte adingin i dai uh hi.

records.english: Our son's teacher called us when she saw how upset he was at school.
records.zomi: Sang ah i tapa bangzah a lungkham hiam cih a muh ciangin a saya in hong sam hi.

records.english: Our daughter wrote her grandmother a letter of comfort after Grandpa died.
records.zomi: Pu a sih khit ciangin i tanu in a pi adingin hehnemna laikhak khat a gelh hi.

records.english: Supporting a frightened child begins with staying calm yourself.
records.zomi: Lau naupang khat huh pen nangmah na daih pan a kipan hi.

records.english: My husband called the doctor when he saw how distressed I was.
records.zomi: Ka lungkham mahmah lam a muh ciangin ka pasal in siavuan a sam hi.

records.english: When Dad had a panic attack, we called the doctor and stayed with him.
records.zomi: Pa lau ngal natna a neih ciangin siavuan i sam uh a, a kiangah i om uh hi.

records.english: When my sister lost her baby, we cooked and cleaned so that she could rest.
records.zomi: Ka u numei in a naungek a mansuah ciangin a tawl theih nadingin an i huan uh a, i siangsak uh hi.

records.english: Can I sit with Grandpa for a while?
records.zomi: Hun tawmno Pu kiangah ka tu thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, he'd like that, because he's feeling very low today.
records.zomi: Thei hi, a deih ding hi, bang hang hiam cih leh tuni-in a lungkia mahmah hi.

records.english: How does Mum always know when one of us is upset?
records.zomi: Kote lak-a khat i lungkham ciangin Nu in bangci-in a thei den hiam?

records.english: Do the children know they can wake us if they're frightened?
records.zomi: A lauh uh leh kote hong kaithou thei uh hi, ci naupangte in a thei uh hiam?

records.english: Shall I sleep on the sofa tonight, so that you're not alone?
records.zomi: Na kia-in na om loh nadingin tuzan sofa tungah ka lum ding hiam?

records.english: My brother asked me not to tell our parents, but I knew they needed to know.
records.zomi: Ka u pasal in i nu leh pa gen lo dingin hong ngen a, ahi zongin amaute in a theih a kisam hi, ci ka thei hi.

records.english: When our teenager stopped talking to us, we didn't force her but kept the door open.
records.zomi: I tangnu in kote hong kihopih nawn loh ciangin i hanthawn kei uh a, ahi zongin kongkhak i hong den uh hi.

records.english: Families often find the right words only after they have sat together in silence.
records.zomi: Innkuante in dai takin a kiang khawm-a a tut khit uh ciangin bek kammal kilawm a mu zel uh hi.

records.english: My husband sat with our son in the car until he stopped shaking.
records.zomi: Ka pasal in i tapa a lin tawp mateng mawtaw sungah a kiangah a tu hi.

records.english: Our teenager told us about her friend's problems, and we helped her find support.
records.zomi: I tangnu in a lawm' haksatnate hong gen a, huhna a muh nadingin i huh uh hi.

records.english: When Mum heard that her brother was ill, we took her to see him the next day.
records.zomi: A u pasal a cina hi, ci Nu in a zak ciangin a zingciang-in amah veh dingin i paipih uh hi.

records.english: When our son was bullied, we listened first and asked questions later.
records.zomi: I tapa a kibawlsiat ciangin a masa-in i ngai uh a, a nungin i dong uh hi.

records.english: It's all right to cry; we're here with you.
records.zomi: Kap thei hi; na kiangah kong om uh hi.

records.english: Grandma held my hand for an hour when I heard the bad news.
records.zomi: Thu hoih lo ka zak ciangin Pi in nai khat sung ka khut a len hi.

records.english: Is there somewhere safe you can stay tonight?
records.zomi: Tuzan na om theih ding mun bit khat a om hiam?

records.english: My brother stayed on the phone with me until I felt calm enough to sleep.
records.zomi: Ka lup theih dong ka dai mateng ka u pasal in phone ah hong kihopih hi.

records.english: Mum still remembers the neighbour who sat with her after her father died.
records.zomi: A pa a sih khit ciangin a kiangah a tu inn veng numei Nu in a phawk lai hi.

records.english: Grandpa cried for the first time when his best friend died, and we just held him.
records.zomi: A lawm pen a sih ciangin Pu a masa pen-in a kap a, kote in a pawm bek uh hi.

records.english: You're not alone; we'll get through this together.
records.zomi: Na kia hi lo hi; khawm-in hih i pal khin ding uh hi.

records.english: We made sure Mum ate something, even though she said she wasn't hungry.
records.zomi: Gilkial lo ka hi a ci zongin Nu in an tawmno a nek nadingin i kem uh hi.

records.english: Our family doctor helped us understand how to support Dad after his breakdown.
records.zomi: Pa' lungsim a buai mahmah khit ciangin bangci-in amah huh ding cih i innkuan siavuan in hong theisiamsak hi.

records.english: Supporting a relative in distress often means staying quiet and present.
records.zomi: Lungkham sanggam khat huh pen dai taka a kiangah om cihna ahi zel hi.

records.english: What should I do when my sister has a panic attack?
records.zomi: Ka u numei lau ngal natna a neih ciangin bang ka hih ding hiam?

records.english: Stay calm, breathe slowly with her, and remind her that it will pass.
records.zomi: Dai in, amah tawh zawi takin hu la in, a bei ding hi, ci-in phawksak in.

records.english: Calling a relative every day can make a frightened person feel less alone.
records.zomi: Ni simin sanggam khat sam in lau mi khat a kia bang a kisa nawn lo thei hi.

records.english: When everything feels too much, just take one step at a time.
records.zomi: Na kisa khempeuh a tam luat ciangin, a pai khat ciat-in pai bek in.

records.english: When Grandma became confused and frightened, we spoke softly and held her hands.
records.zomi: Pi a lungsim a buai a, a lauh ciangin nem takin i kihopih uh a, a khutte i len uh hi.

records.english: Our daughter was frightened after the accident, so we let her sleep in our room.
records.zomi: Lampi siatna khit ciangin i tanu a lau a, tua ahih manin i lupna dan ah a lum dingin i phal uh hi.

records.english: I drove to my sister's house in the middle of the night when she called me crying.
records.zomi: Ka u numei in a kap kawm-in hong sam ciangin zanlai-in a inn ah mawtaw ka tawl hi.

records.english: Can I call your mum for you?
records.zomi: Na nu kong sam sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Supporting a family member in crisis can be exhausting, so carers need support too.
records.zomi: Haksatna sung-a innkuan sung mi khat huh pen a gimhuai thei a, tua ahih manin kemtute zong huhna a kisam uh hi.

records.english: When Dad cried at the hospital, my sister and I held his hands.
records.zomi: Damdawi inn ah Pa a kap ciangin ka u numei leh kei in a khutte i len uh hi.

records.english: Shall I make you some tea, or would you rather be alone?
records.zomi: Niangtui kong bawl sak ding hiam, na kia-in om na deih zaw hiam?

records.english: Just stay with me for a little while.
records.zomi: Hun tawmno ka kiangah om bek in.

records.english: Christians often see the Fall as the beginning of sin and suffering in the world.
records.zomi: Khristiante in Adam' mawhna pen leitung-a mawhna leh thuakna kipatna-in a mu zel uh hi.

records.english: The children asked why God put the tree in the garden at all.
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pasian in huan sungah sing a koih hiam ci-in naupangte in a dong uh hi.

records.english: Paul writes that sin entered the world through one man.
records.zomi: Mi khat hangin leitung ah mawhna a lut hi, ci-in Paul in a gelh hi.

records.english: In Genesis, the ground is cursed, and work becomes hard after the Fall.
records.zomi: Piancilna ah Adam' mawhna khit ciangin lei hamsiatna a tuak a, nasep a haksa suak hi.

records.english: Our Bible study group discussed how temptation often starts with a small doubt.
records.zomi: I Laisiangtho kisinna pawl in sitna pen ngaihsun kiamna neuno khat pan a kipan zel hi, cih a kikum uh hi.

records.english: Is the story of the Fall read in your church before Easter?
records.zomi: Na pawlpi ah Easter ma-in Adam' mawhna tangthu a kisim hiam?

records.english: Christians pray that God will heal what was broken by the Fall.
records.zomi: Khristiante in Adam' mawhna in a susiat te Pasian in a dam sak nadingin a thungen uh hi.

records.english: Christians see the story of the Fall as showing how quickly people make excuses.
records.zomi: Khristiante in Adam' mawhna tangthu pen mite in bangzah a hun-in a mawhna midang tungah a koih uh hiam cih a lak tangthu-in a mu uh hi.

records.english: Christian traditions differ in how they describe the effects of the Fall on human nature.
records.zomi: Khristian ngeina tuamtuam te in Adam' mawhna in mihing pianzia tungah a hih te gen zia ah a kibang kei uh hi.

records.english: Christians believe that what was lost in the Fall is restored through Christ.
records.zomi: Khristiante in Adam' mawhna-a mangthang te Khazih tungtawnin a kipia kik hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: Where is the story of Adam and Eve found?
records.zomi: Adam leh Eve tangthu koi-ah a om hiam?

records.english: In the first chapters of the book of Genesis.
records.zomi: Piancilna laibu' tangthu masa te ah.

records.english: The story says that God told them not to eat from one particular tree.
records.zomi: Pasian in sing khat pan ne kei un, ci-in amaute a gen hi, ci tangthu in a ci hi.

records.english: In the story, Adam and Eve were sent out of the garden.
records.zomi: Tangthu ah Adam leh Eve huan sung pan a kihawl khia uh hi.

records.english: Some theologians describe Jesus as a new Adam who obeyed where the first Adam failed.
records.zomi: Pasian thu siam khenkhat in Jesu pen Adam masa pen in a zawh loh mun ah thu a man Adam thak khat-in a gen uh hi.

records.english: Was the fruit really an apple?
records.zomi: A gah pen theigah taktak ahi hiam?

records.english: Genesis doesn't say what kind of fruit it was, although artists often paint an apple.
records.zomi: Piancilna in gah bang ahi hiam cih a gen kei a, ahi zongin lim lai siamte in theigah a lai zel uh hi.

records.english: Did God stop loving Adam and Eve after they disobeyed?
records.zomi: Adam leh Eve thu a man loh khit uh ciangin Pasian in amaute a it nawn lo hiam?

records.english: Christian teaching says that God continued to care for them and promised a future rescue.
records.zomi: Khristian thuhilhna in Pasian in amaute a kem zel a, hun hong tung ding-a hotkhiatna khat a kiciam hi, a ci hi.

records.english: The story of Eden reminds Christians that God made the world good.
records.zomi: Eden tangthu in Pasian in leitung hoih takin a bawl hi, ci-in Khristiante a phawksak hi.

records.english: In Genesis, God placed the first humans in a garden called Eden.
records.zomi: Piancilna ah Pasian in mihing masa te Eden kici huan khat ah a koih hi.

records.english: Why did Adam and Eve eat the fruit?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Adam leh Eve in gah a ne uh hiam?

records.english: According to Genesis, the serpent persuaded Eve that it would make them wise like God.
records.zomi: Piancilna bangin gulpi in Pasian bangin a pil sak ding hi, ci-in Eve a khem hi.

records.english: The Fall is not mentioned often in the Old Testament after Genesis, but it became central in Christian thought.
records.zomi: Adam' mawhna pen Piancilna khit ciangin Thukham Lui ah a kigen tam kei a, ahi zongin Khristian ngaihsutna ah a thupi suak hi.

records.english: Why did Eve listen to the serpent?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Eve in gulpi a ngai hiam?

records.english: In the story, God asks Adam where he is, and Christians see this as God seeking people.
records.zomi: Tangthu ah Pasian in Adam koi-ah na om hiam ci-in a dong a, Khristiante in hih pen Pasian in mite a zon lam-in a mu uh hi.

records.english: Shall we read the story of the garden together tonight?
records.zomi: Tuzan huan tangthu khawm-in i sim ding hiam?

records.english: What happened after they ate the fruit?
records.zomi: Gah a nek khit uh ciangin bang a piang hiam?

records.english: They felt ashamed and hid from God among the trees, the story says.
records.zomi: A maizum uh a, singte lak ah Pasian a kiselsan uh hi, ci tangthu in a ci hi.

records.english: Children learn from the story that disobedience has consequences.
records.zomi: Naupangte in thu man lohna in a gah a nei hi, cih tangthu pan a sin uh hi.

records.english: Christians often see God making clothes for them as a sign of care even after disobedience.
records.zomi: Khristiante in thu man lohna khit ciangin zong Pasian in amaute adingin puan a bawl sak pen kemna lim khat-in a mu zel uh hi.

records.english: Our pastor said that the story shows the danger of wanting to be like God.
records.zomi: I pastor in tangthu in Pasian bang hih deihna lauhuaina a lak hi, a ci hi.

records.english: The serpent in Genesis is often linked with the devil in later Christian teaching.
records.zomi: Piancilna-a gulpi pen a nunung Khristian thuhilhna ah Dawimangpa tawh a kizom zel hi.

records.english: According to many Christians, the Fall affected the whole of creation.
records.zomi: Khristian tampi' ngaihsutna bangin Adam' mawhna in piansakna khempeuh a tuak hi.

records.english: Children's Bibles often tell the story of the Fall with simple pictures.
records.zomi: Naupang Laisiangtho te in Adam' mawhna tangthu lim baih te tawh a gen zel uh hi.

records.english: Do all Christians read the story of the Fall literally?
records.zomi: Khristian khempeuh in Adam' mawhna tangthu a kammal bangin a sim uh hiam?

records.english: No, some read it as history, while others read it as a story that teaches deep truths.
records.zomi: Hi lo hi, khenkhat in tangthu taktak-in a sim uh a, khenkhat in thuman thuk sinsakna tangthu-in a sim uh hi.

records.english: What is meant by the Fall in Christian teaching?
records.zomi: Khristian thuhilhna ah Adam' mawhna in bang cihna hiam?

records.english: It refers to the story in Genesis in which the first humans disobeyed God and lost their closeness to him.
records.zomi: Piancilna-a mihing masa te in Pasian thu a man loh uh a, amah tawh a kinaihna uh a mansuah uh tangthu a genna ahi hi.

records.english: Does the Fall explain why the world is not as God intended?
records.zomi: Adam' mawhna in leitung Pasian' deihna bang a hih loh hang a gen hiam?

records.english: According to the story, the tree gave knowledge of good and evil.
records.zomi: Tangthu bangin tua sing in hoih leh hoih lo theihna a pia hi.

records.english: Thank you for explaining the story of Eden so clearly.
records.zomi: Eden tangthu kician takin hong genna manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: Many hymns speak of Christ as the one who undoes the damage of the first sin.
records.zomi: La tampi in Khazih pen mawhna masa pen' susiatna a bawlphat kikpa-in a gen uh hi.

records.english: Christians believe that the effects of the Fall can be seen in broken relationships.
records.zomi: Khristiante in Adam' mawhna gah te kizopna kisia te ah a kimu thei hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: The Fall is a central idea in Christian teaching about sin and salvation.
records.zomi: Adam' mawhna pen mawhna leh hotkhiatna tawh kisai Khristian thuhilhna ah ngaihsutna thupi khat ahi hi.

records.english: The story of the Fall raises questions that Christians have discussed for centuries.
records.zomi: Adam' mawhna tangthu in Khristiante in kum za tampi sung a kikum uh dotnate a piangsak hi.

records.english: Our Sunday school class acted out the story of the garden of Eden.
records.zomi: I Nipini sang class in Eden huan tangthu a lim-in a lak uh hi.

records.english: What does the story of the Fall teach us about ourselves?
records.zomi: Adam' mawhna tangthu in eimah tawh kisai bang hong sinsak hiam?

records.english: Many believers say that the story of the Fall helps them understand their own temptations.
records.zomi: Um mi tampi in Adam' mawhna tangthu in amau sitnate a theisiam nadingin a huh hi, a ci uh hi.

records.english: Our pastor reminded us that the story of Eden is also a story about freedom and choice.
records.zomi: Eden tangthu pen zalenna leh teelna tawh kisai tangthu zong ahi hi, ci-in i pastor in hong phawksak hi.

records.english: Paintings of Adam and Eve leaving the garden are found in many old churches.
records.zomi: Adam leh Eve in huan a paisan lim te pawlpi lui tampi ah a om hi.

records.english: Did Adam and Eve have children after they left the garden?
records.zomi: Huan a paisan khit uh ciangin Adam leh Eve in ta a nei uh hiam?

records.english: Yes, Genesis tells of their sons Cain and Abel, and later Seth.
records.zomi: Nei uh hi, Piancilna in a tapa uh Kain leh Abel, a nungin Seth tawh kisai a gen hi.

records.english: Christian teaching links the Fall with the need for salvation through Jesus.
records.zomi: Khristian thuhilhna in Adam' mawhna pen Jesu tungtawn-a hotkhiatna kisapna tawh a zom hi.

records.english: After the Fall, according to Genesis, God made clothes for Adam and Eve.
records.zomi: Piancilna bangin Adam' mawhna khit ciangin Pasian in Adam leh Eve adingin puan a bawl sak hi.

records.english: Can you tell me the story of Adam and Eve, Grandma?
records.zomi: Pi, Adam leh Eve tangthu hong gen thei ding hiam?

records.english: Children often find the story of the talking serpent strange and exciting.
records.zomi: Naupangte in a pau gulpi tangthu lamdang leh lungdemhuai-in a mu zel uh hi.

records.english: In the story, Adam blamed Eve, and Eve blamed the serpent.
records.zomi: Tangthu ah Adam in Eve a mawhsak a, Eve in gulpi a mawhsak hi.

records.english: Some Christians see the Fall as the moment when trust between humans and God was broken.
records.zomi: Khristian khenkhat in Adam' mawhna pen mihing leh Pasian kikal-a kiumna a kisiat hun-in a mu uh hi.

records.english: The story of the Fall ends with hope, because God does not abandon the first humans.
records.zomi: Adam' mawhna tangthu pen lametna tawh a tawp hi, bang hang hiam cih leh Pasian in mihing masa te a nusia kei hi.

records.english: Will the results be good enough for a scholarship?
records.zomi: Sitna gah te scholarship ngah nadingin a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: There's a chance the factory will close for a week in August.
records.zomi: August kha sung-in factory kal khat sung a khak thei ding hi.

records.english: Good leaders explain what they know and what they don't know.
records.zomi: Makai hoih te in a theih leh a theih loh te a gen uh hi.

records.english: Will the bus be on time, do you think?
records.zomi: Bus hun-in a tung ding hi na ci hiam?

records.english: The forecast is uncertain, so the outdoor training may be cancelled.
records.zomi: Khuahun ngaihsutna a kician kei a, tua ahih manin pualam-a training a kiphiat kha ding hi.

records.english: I wouldn't be surprised if the exam were harder this year.
records.zomi: Tu kum-in sitna a haksa zaw leh lamdang ka sa kei ding hi.

records.english: Is the client likely to sign the contract this week?
records.zomi: Hih kal sung-in client in contract ah min a gelh kha ding hiam?

records.english: I'm not sure, because they're still comparing offers.
records.zomi: Ka thei kei hi, bang hang hiam cih leh ngetna te a kiteh lai uh hi.

records.english: Students who say when they are unsure learn more than those who pretend to know.
records.zomi: A theih loh ciangun a gen sangnaupangte in a theih bang-a kibawl te sangin a sin tam zaw uh hi.

records.english: Experts disagree, so the safest answer is that we don't know yet.
records.zomi: Siamte a kilem kei uh a, tua ahih manin a bit pen dawnna pen tu-in i thei nai kei hi, cih ahi hi.

records.english: Is it true that the canteen is changing its menu, or is that just a rumour?
records.zomi: An nekna inn in an ciamtehna a khek ding cih a dik hiam, thugen bek ahi hiam?

records.english: Did my application arrive in time, I wonder?
records.zomi: Ka ngetna lai hun-in a tung hiam?

records.english: It looks as if the printer is broken again.
records.zomi: Printer a sia kik bang hi.

records.english: Do you know if the staff party is still happening?
records.zomi: Nasemte poai a om lai hiam cih na thei hiam?

records.english: I'm afraid I don't know the answer, but I'll find out.
records.zomi: Dawnna ka thei kei hi, ahi zongin ka zong ding hi.

records.english: Honest uncertainty is more useful to a manager than false confidence.
records.zomi: Manager adingin thuman taka ka thei kei cih pen lepkhem kiciamna sangin a phattuam zaw hi.

records.english: I'd say the odds are about fifty-fifty.
records.zomi: A kikim-in a kikhen hi ka ci ding hi.

records.english: I'm not sure I understood the instructions correctly.
records.zomi: Thuhilhna te dik takin ka theisiam hiam cih ka thei kei hi.

records.english: Are we getting a pay rise this year?
records.zomi: Tu kum-in khasum khanna i ngah ding uh hiam?

records.english: Nobody knows yet, because the budget hasn't been approved.
records.zomi: Kuamah in a thei nai kei uh hi, bang hang hiam cih leh budget a kiphal nai kei hi.

records.english: Could you check, because I'm not sure the figures are up to date?
records.zomi: Nambat te a thak ahi hiam cih ka thei kei ahih manin na en thei ding hiam?

records.english: Do you think I passed the interview?
records.zomi: Interview ka zo hi na ci hiam?

records.english: It's hard to tell, but they seemed impressed by your answers.
records.zomi: Gen a haksa hi, ahi zongin na dawnnate a lungdam bang uh hi.

records.english: I'm not sure whether the lecture is recorded.
records.zomi: Thuhilhna a kikhum hiam cih ka thei kei hi.

records.english: Is it likely that we'll need to work overtime?
records.zomi: Hun beh-in na i sep kul kha ding hiam?

records.english: Is this the correct formula for the calculation?
records.zomi: Hih pen kisimna adingin formula dik ahi hiam?

records.english: I think so, but let's check it against the textbook.
records.zomi: Ka ci hi, ahi zongin textbook tawh i kiteh ni.

records.english: Could the deadline be extended, do you think?
records.zomi: Hun bei sawt zaw thei hi na ci hiam?

records.english: Will there be enough time for questions at the end?
records.zomi: A tawp ciangin dotnate adingin hun a cing ding hiam?

records.english: Admitting uncertainty at work is better than giving wrong information confidently.
records.zomi: Nasepna ah ka thei kei cih pulak pen thu khial kiciam takin gen sangin a hoih zaw hi.

records.english: Is the head teacher going to be at the assembly?
records.zomi: Sangpi saya assembly ah a om ding hiam?

records.english: It's too early to say whether the new method works better.
records.zomi: Lam thak in a hoih zaw hiam cih gen dingin a hun nai lua hi.

records.english: Do you think the teacher will accept late homework?
records.zomi: Saya in a phawng inn-a sin ding a sang ding hi na ci hiam?

records.english: I think the deadline is the twentieth, but please check the email.
records.zomi: Hun bei pen ni sawmnih ni hi ka sa hi, ahi zongin email na en ding hi.

records.english: I'll let you know once the director has decided.
records.zomi: Director in a khensat khit ciangin kong theisak ding hi.

records.english: I can't say for certain whether the course will run next year.
records.zomi: Kum hong tung ding ah sinna a om ding hiam cih ka gen kip thei kei hi.

records.english: I might be wrong, but I believe the answer is twelve.
records.zomi: Ka khial kha thei a, ahi zongin dawnna pen sawmlenih hi ka sa hi.

records.english: We're still waiting for confirmation, so nothing is certain.
records.zomi: Kiciamna i ngak lai uh a, tua ahih manin bangmah a kip nai kei hi.

records.english: Is the answer in the textbook, or do we have to work it out?
records.zomi: Dawnna textbook sungah a om hiam, i sim khiat kul hiam?

records.english: Uncertainty about exam results can make the summer feel very long.
records.zomi: Sitna gah tawh kisai a thei lohna in khal hun a sausak mahmah thei hi.

records.english: Will the new software be ready before the deadline?
records.zomi: Software thak hun bei ma-in a kicing ding hiam?

records.english: Maybe, if there are no more problems with testing.
records.zomi: Kicing kha ding hi, testing ah haksatna dang a om nawn kei leh.

records.english: I have a feeling that the client isn't happy with our proposal.

records.zomi: Ka pi in a sam ding hiam cih a thei kip kei a, tua ahih manin kei hong sam masa hi.

records.english: Keep your phone charged when someone in the family is ill.
records.zomi: Innkuan sung-ah mi khat a cina ciangin na phone charge-in koih den in.

records.english: Every member of our family has the doctor's number saved in their phone.
records.zomi: I innkuan sung mi khempeuh in a phone sungah siavuan' nambat a kem uh hi.

records.english: Do the children know our address?
records.zomi: Naupangte in i inn mun a thei uh hiam?

records.english: Yes, we practise it with them every week.
records.zomi: Thei uh hi, kal simin amaute tawh i kisin uh hi.

records.english: Is the emergency number different when we're abroad?
records.zomi: Gamdang ah i om ciangin lauhuai nambat a tuam hiam?

records.english: Our teenager called an ambulance for a stranger who collapsed on the bus.
records.zomi: I tangnu in bus sungah a puk mi theih ngeih lo khat adingin ambulance a sam hi.

records.english: When the river rose, our family called the rescue service and waited on the roof.
records.zomi: Lui a lian ciangin i innkuan in hotkhiatna nasemte a sam uh a, inn tung ah a ngak uh hi.

records.english: The operator asked me to count Grandpa's breaths while we waited.
records.zomi: I ngak lai-in a dawngpa in Pu' hu lak a sim dingin hong ngen hi.

records.english: What should I do if Grandpa falls and can't get up?
records.zomi: Pu a puk a, a thou thei kei leh bang ka hih ding hiam?

records.english: Call for an ambulance, keep him warm, and don't try to lift him alone.
records.zomi: Ambulance sam inla, amah lum takin kem in, na kia-in domto sawm kei in.

records.english: Our family's village has changed more in ten years than in the previous fifty.
records.zomi: I innkuan' khua kum sawm sung-in a ma-a kum sawmnga sung sangin a kikhel tam zaw hi.

records.english: My grandmother says the village was much busier before the new road took people away.
records.zomi: Lampi thak in mite a paipih ma-in khua a nuam zaw mahmah hi, ci-in ka pi in a gen hi.

records.english: The road to our village winds through tea gardens and pine forests.
records.zomi: I khua paina lampi pen lakphak huan leh mangkhawng gam te lak ah a kikawi hi.

records.english: Our village is famous in the region for its oranges.
records.zomi: I khua pen a sangtam hangin a gam sung-ah a kithei hi.

records.english: Children in our village swim in the river during the summer holidays.
records.zomi: Khal tawlngakni sung-in i khua-a naupangte lui ah tuipeek a kisin uh hi.

records.english: What was the first thing you noticed when you went back?
records.zomi: Na ciah kik ciangin bang na mu masa pen hiam?

records.english: How small the school looked, although it seemed huge when I was a child.
records.zomi: Naupang ka hih lai-in a lian mahmah bang hi napi, sang a neu bang mahmah hi.

records.english: Dad's village has only one shop, run by the same family for three generations.
records.zomi: Pa' khua ah sumbuk khat bek a om a, khangthu thum sung innkuan khat in a kem hi.

records.english: My wife fell in love with the village on her first visit.
records.zomi: Ka zi in khua a veh masa pen-in khua a it pah hi.

records.english: Which house belongs to Uncle Pau?
records.zomi: Pa neu Pau' inn bang ahi hiam?

records.english: The children collected stones from the village stream to take home.
records.zomi: Naupangte in inn-a paipih dingin khua guh pan suangte a kaikhawm uh hi.

records.english: Our cousins in the village keep goats, chickens and two very noisy geese.
records.zomi: Khua-a i sanggamte in kel, ak leh ngang ging mahmah nih a vulh uh hi.

records.english: In the rainy season, the path to Grandpa's house turns to thick mud.
records.zomi: Guahzu hun-in Pu' inn paina lampi a nin thuk mahmah suak hi.

records.english: Dad can name every family who lived along the main path when he was young.
records.zomi: A neu lai-in lampi lian dung-a teng innkuan khempeuh' min Pa in a gen thei hi.

records.english: Thank you for taking us to see the house where you were born, Grandpa.
records.zomi: Pu, na suahna inn hong lak manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: How long does it take to walk from one end of the village to the other?
records.zomi: Khua tawp khat pan tawp khat ah kal-in bangzah sawt hiam?

records.english: At night, the only lights in the village come from the houses and the stars.
records.zomi: Zan-in khua-a meivak te pen inn te leh aksite pan bek ahi hi.

records.english: Our family's village sits between two rivers at the foot of a mountain.
records.zomi: I innkuan' khua pen mual bul-a lui nih kikal ah a om hi.

records.english: In the dry season, the fields around the village turn brown.
records.zomi: Khuavot hun-in khua kim-a lou te a kang suak hi.

records.english: Grandpa's village feels like home, even though I have never lived there.
records.zomi: Pu' khua pen ka teng ngei kei napi inn bang-in ka kisa hi.

records.english: My cousin built a new house in the village, but he kept the old one for his parents.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam in khua ah inn thak khat a lam a, ahi zongin a lui pen a nu leh pa adingin a kem hi.

records.english: We always leave the village with bags full of fruit from our relatives.
records.zomi: I sanggamte' theigah ip dim tawh khua pan i pai den uh hi.

records.english: The village square is where weddings, markets and festivals all take place.
records.zomi: Khua lai pen mopawi, sumbuk leh pawi khempeuh a kibawlna mun ahi hi.

records.english: In the evenings, old men sit on benches by the church and talk about the harvest.
records.zomi: Nitak simin pasal upate pawlpi kiang-a tutphah tungah a tu uh a, lou lakna tawh kisai a kihopih uh hi.

records.english: When my grandparents were young, the village had no electricity at all.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh pi te a khangno lai-un khua ah meivak bangmah om lo hi.

records.english: Next summer, let's stay in the village for the whole holiday.
records.zomi: Khal hong tung ding-in tawlngakni bup khua ah om ni.

records.english: Shall we walk to the top of the hill to see the whole village?
records.zomi: Khua bup i muh nadingin mual tung dong i kal ding hiam?

records.english: The village bakery opens before dawn, and the whole street smells of bread.
records.zomi: Khua-a moh huanna in khuavak ma-in a hong a, lampi bup moh gim a nam hi.

records.english: Is Grandma's house still the one by the well?
records.zomi: Pi' inn pen tuikhuk kiang-a inn mah ahi lai hiam?

records.english: Yes, the green one with the big mango tree in front.
records.zomi: Hi lai hi, a maiah haigah kung lian khat a om eng inn.

records.english: My grandparents' house has a wooden veranda where the family sits in the evening.

records.english: Walking through the village with Grandpa takes hours because he stops to talk to everyone.
records.zomi: Pu in mi khempeuh tawh a kihopih dingin a khawl den ahih manin amah tawh khua sung kal pen nai tampi a sawt hi.

records.english: Do you think the village will still be here when our children are grown?
records.zomi: I tate a lian khit uh ciangin khua a om lai ding hi na ci hiam?

records.english: Every morning, smoke rises from the kitchens as families cook breakfast.
records.zomi: Zingsang simin innkuante zingsang an a huan uh ciangin an huanna pan meikhu a kah hi.

records.english: Did everyone in the village really come out to greet us?
records.zomi: Khua sung mi khempeuh hong dawn dingin a pawt taktak uh hiam?

records.english: Coming down the hill, you can see the whole village spread out below you.
records.zomi: Mual tung pan na hong kum ciangin khua bup a nuai-ah a kizal na mu thei hi.

records.english: When we visit the village, the children run barefoot all day.
records.zomi: Khua i veh ciangin naupangte ni bup khe-sawl-in a tai uh hi.

records.english: Our cousins' school in the village has only two classrooms, but the children love it.
records.zomi: Khua-a i sanggamte' sang ah sangdan nih bek a om a, ahi zongin naupangte in a it uh hi.

records.english: The old bridge in Grandpa's village was built by the villagers themselves.
records.zomi: Pu' khua-a lei lui pen khua mite amau mah in a lam uh ahi hi.

records.english: Which part of the village do you miss most?
records.zomi: Khua sung-ah koi mun na ngaih pen hiam?

records.english: The hill behind the church, where we watched the sunset every evening.
records.zomi: Pawlpi nunglam-a mual, nitak simin ni tum i en uh na mun.

records.english: Grandpa, what was the village like when you were a boy?
records.zomi: Pu, na naupan lai-in khua bang ci hiam?

records.english: There was no road, only a footpath, and every house had a thatched roof.
records.zomi: Lampi lian om lo-in kal lampi bek a om a, inn khempeuh in lumbeek inntung a nei uh hi.

records.english: The terraced fields around the village were built by hand over many generations.
records.zomi: Khua kim-a lou kaihkawi te khangthu tampi sung khut tawh a kilam ahi hi.

records.english: Which path leads down to the river, Grandpa?
records.zomi: Pu, koi lampi in lui ah a kum hiam?

records.english: Water from Grandma's well is the coldest I've ever tasted.
records.zomi: Pi' tuikhuk tui pen ka dawn ngei pen lak-ah a vot pen ahi hi.

records.english: Our children were surprised that the village has no traffic lights.
records.zomi: Khua ah mawtaw meivak khawlna a om loh manin i tate lamdang a sa uh hi.

records.english: A village holds the memories of every family that has lived there.
records.zomi: Khua khat in tua-a teng ngei innkuan khempeuh' phawkna a kem hi.

records.english: Dad gets emotional every time we drive past the sign with his village's name.
records.zomi: A khua min kigelhna ciamtehna i pal ciangin Pa a lungsim a ki-ok den hi.

records.english: Can you show me the house where you grew up, Mum?
records.zomi: Nu, na khanna inn hong lak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Shall we take Grandma back to her village for her birthday?
records.zomi: A suahni dingin Pi a khua ah i paipih kik ding hiam?

records.english: In my mother's village, the church bell wakes everyone at six.
records.zomi: Ka nu' khua ah pawlpi khawng in nai guk-in mi khempeuh a phongsak hi.

records.english: Auntie Lun still lives in the house where my mother was born.
records.zomi: Ni Lun ka nu' suahna inn ah a teng lai hi.

records.english: Grandma feels safer now that the village has a new clinic.
records.zomi: Khua in damdawi inn neu thak khat a neih manin Pi a bit zaw-in a kisa hi.

records.english: Every house in Grandma's village has a small garden full of beans and pumpkins.
records.zomi: Pi' khua-a inn khempeuh in bete leh mai a dim huan neuno khat a nei uh hi.

records.english: Does the village still have a market?
records.zomi: Khua ah sumbuk a om lai hiam?

records.english: Only once a week now, on Saturdays.
records.zomi: Tu-in kal khat ah khatvei bek, Kiginni-in.

records.english: Dad describes his village so often that I could draw a map of it.
records.zomi: Pa in a khua tawh kisai a gen tam mahmah ahih manin a map ka lai thei ding hi.

records.english: Describing my family's village to my friends made me realise how much I love it.
records.zomi: Ka lawmte kiangah ka innkuan' khua ka gen ciangin bangzah ka it hiam cih ka thei hi.

records.english: Is the church really the oldest building for miles around?
records.zomi: Pawlpi pen a kim-a mun khempeuh ah inn lui pen taktak ahi hiam?

records.english: My cousin was fined because he didn't know he needed a permit to sell food at the market.
records.zomi: Sumbuk ah an zuak dingin phalna lai a kisam cih a theih loh manin ka sanggam dan a kitai hi.

records.english: The new rules on recycling mean we now sort our rubbish into four bins.
records.zomi: Recycling tawh kisai thukhun thakte hangin tu-in i eek te bawm li-ah i khen uh hi.

records.english: Dad, why does the car beep until everyone has a seat belt on?
records.zomi: Pa, bang hangin mi khempeuh seat belt a bulh mateng mawtaw a ging hiam?

records.english: Because the law says so, and because they save lives in accidents.
records.zomi: Thukham in a gen ahih manin, tua banah lampi siatna ah nuntakna a hotkhiat manin.

records.english: My wife checked the law on maternity leave before talking to her employer.
records.zomi: Ka zi in a nasep neipa tawh a kihopih ma-in nau suah tawlna tawh kisai thukham a en hi.

records.english: Do we need to register the baby's birth within a certain time?
records.zomi: Naungek suahna hun khat sung-in i ciamteh kul hiam?

records.english: Understanding the law helped my parents protect their land.
records.zomi: Thukham theisiam in ka nu leh ka pa' gam a kem nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: My uncle was shocked to learn that his old car was no longer legal to drive.
records.zomi: A mawtaw lui pen thukham tawh kituakin tawl theih nawn lo hi, cih a theih ciangin ka pa neu lamdang a sa mahmah hi.

records.english: Do children have to wear helmets when they ride bicycles here?
records.zomi: Hih mun ah naupangte in siiksakol a tawl ciangin lukhu a khuh kul uh hiam?

records.english: Is it true that you can be fined for not clearing snow from the pavement?
records.zomi: Lampi gei pan vuuk na hawlkhiat loh leh dan na kitai thei hi, cih a dik hiam?

records.english: Do we need a licence to keep bees in the garden?
records.zomi: Huan sungah khuai vulh dingin licence i kisam hiam?

records.english: In our town you only need to register them with the council.
records.zomi: I khuapi ah council kiangah ciamteh bek na kisam hi.

records.english: What does the new law about school attendance mean for us?
records.zomi: Sang pai tawh kisai thukham thak in kote adingin bang cihna hiam?

records.english: It means we must tell the school if the children will be absent.
records.zomi: Naupangte sang a pai loh ding uh leh sang i theisak kul hi, cihna ahi hi.

records.english: Our family discusses the news when an important new law is passed.
records.zomi: Thukham thak thupi khat a kipiak ciangin i innkuan in thuthak a kikum uh hi.

records.english: Can the landlord raise the rent whenever he wants?
records.zomi: Inn neipa in a deih hun-in inn man a khangsak thei hiam?

records.english: Not here; he has to give notice and follow the rules in the tenancy law.
records.zomi: Hih mun ah thei lo hi; a theisak masa-in inn luah thukham-a thukhunte a zui kul hi.

records.english: In our country, children must go to school until they are sixteen.
records.zomi: I gam ah naupangte kum sawmlenguk dong sang a pai ngei ding uh hi.

records.english: Is it legal for me to work at fourteen?
records.zomi: Kum sawmleli-in na ka sem thei ding cih thukham tawh kituak hiam?

records.english: In our country, you can do light work for a few hours, but there are strict limits.
records.zomi: I gam ah nai tawmno sung na zangkhai na sem thei a, ahi zongin a kip mahmah gamgi te a om hi.

records.english: Thank you for helping us understand the new housing law.
records.zomi: Inn tawh kisai thukham thak hong theisiamsak manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: My brother's lawyer explained the law in simple words, which helped us all.
records.zomi: Ka u pasal' thukham siam in thukham kammal baih tawh a gen a, tua in kote khempeuh hong huh hi.

records.english: In our country, is it against the law to leave a young child alone at home?
records.zomi: I gam ah naupang neu khat inn ah a kia-in nusiat pen thukham tawh kituak lo hiam?

records.english: Who explained the inheritance laws to Grandma after Grandpa died?
records.zomi: Pu a sih khit ciangin gamluah thukhamte Pi kiangah kua in a gen hiam?

records.english: Our neighbour lent us a booklet about the local rules when we arrived.
records.zomi: I tun ciangin i inn veng in a mun thukhunte tawh kisai laibu neu khat hong pia hi.

records.english: Knowing the law gives families confidence when they deal with officials.
records.zomi: Thukham theih in innkuante in kumpi nasemte tawh a kituak ciangin kiciamna a pia hi.

records.english: Shall we ask a lawyer before we sign the contract for the house?
records.zomi: Inn contract ah min i gelh ma-in thukham siam khat i dong ding hiam?

records.english: My brother studies law and explains new rules to the family at dinner.
records.zomi: Ka u pasal in thukham a sin a, nitak an ciangin innkuan kiangah thukhun thakte a gen hi.

records.english: Is it legal to take photos of people in the street without asking?
records.zomi: Lampi tungah mite dong lo-in a photo lak pen thukham tawh kituak hiam?

records.english: Laws can feel distant until one of them affects your own family.
records.zomi: Thukhamte pen khat in na innkuan a tuak mateng a gamla bang-in a kisa thei hi.

records.english: When the law on smoking changed, Grandpa finally gave up his pipe.
records.zomi: Meizial dawn tawh kisai thukham a kikhel ciangin Pu in a tuibuuk a nusia khin hi.

records.english: Our family learned the hard way that fishing in the river requires a licence.
records.zomi: Lui ah nga man pen licence a kisam hi, cih i innkuan in haksa takin a sin uh hi.

records.english: Our children learned at school why it's illegal to drive without insurance.
records.zomi: Insurance om lo-in mawtaw tawl pen bang hangin thukham tawh kituak lo hiam cih i tate in sang ah a sin uh hi.

records.english: Grandpa explained that the laws of his village were never written down.
records.zomi: A khua' thukhamte a kigelh ngei kei hi, ci-in Pu in a gen hi.

records.english: Mum checked whether the babysitter needed to be a certain age by law.
records.zomi: Naupang kemtu pen thukham bangin kum bangzah a cin kul hiam cih Nu in a en hi.

records.english: In our town, it's against the law to play loud music after eleven at night.
records.zomi: I khuapi ah zan nai sawmlekhat khit ciangin la ging hat tum pen thukham tawh kituak lo hi.

records.english: Auntie Hoih learned about her rights as a widow from a free legal advice service.
records.zomi: Ni Hoih in man om lo thukham thuhilhna nasep pan meigong-a a thuneihnate a sin hi.

records.english: Our teenager found the new rules about online privacy confusing.
records.zomi: I tangnu in online kiselna tawh kisai thukhun thakte a buaihuai sa hi.

records.english: Mum always reminds us to check the rules before we do anything new.
records.zomi: Bangmah thak i bawl ma-in thukhunte en dingin Nu in hong phawksak den hi.

records.english: When we moved to this country, we had to learn many new rules about driving.
records.zomi: Hih gam ah i pai ciangin mawtaw tawl tawh kisai thukhun thak tampi i sin kul uh hi.

records.english: Dad taught us that laws can be changed, but only through fair processes.
records.zomi: Thukhamte kikhel thei a, ahi zongin a dik kalsuanna tungtawn bek-in, ci-in Pa in hong sinsak hi.

records.english: Helping elderly relatives understand new laws can take a lot of patience.
records.zomi: Sanggam upate thukham thakte a theisiam nadingin huh pen thuakzawhna tampi a kisam thei hi.

records.english: Children learn about laws when they see their parents following them.
records.zomi: Naupangte in a nu leh pate thukhamte a zui a muh uh ciangin thukham tawh kisai a sin uh hi.

records.english: We had to get a permit before we could hold the street party.
records.zomi: Lampi poai i bawl ma-in phalna lai khat i ngah kul hi.

records.english: We explained to the children that laws are rules made to keep everyone safe.
records.zomi: Thukhamte pen mi khempeuh a bit nadingin kibawl thukhunte ahi hi, ci-in naupangte kiangah i gen uh hi.

records.english: We read the new rules on pets together before getting a dog.
records.zomi: Ui khat i neih ma-in ganhing vulh tawh kisai thukhun thakte khawm-in i sim uh hi.

records.english: The children were surprised to learn that cycling without lights at night is against the law here.
records.zomi: Hih mun ah zan-in meivak om lo-in siiksakol tawl pen thukham tawh kituak lo hi, cih naupangte in a theih ciangin lamdang a sa uh hi.

records.english: Our son asked why it's against the law to buy fireworks before a certain age.
records.zomi: Kum a cin ma-in meipuak lei pen bang hangin thukham tawh kituak lo hiam ci-in i tapa in a dong hi.

records.english: Dad reads the new laws in the newspaper and explains them to Grandma.
records.zomi: Pa in thuthak laipi sung-a thukham thakte a sim a, Pi kiangah a gen hi.

records.english: Let's read the leaflet about the new rules together.
records.zomi: Thukhun thakte tawh kisai laikhak neu khawm-in sim ni.

records.english: Our family keeps important legal documents in a safe place.
records.zomi: I innkuan in thukham tawh kisai lai thupi te mun bit khat ah a kem hi.

records.english: Grandma remembers when our country made it illegal for children to work in factories.
records.zomi: I gam in naupangte factory ah na sem lo dingin thukham a bawl hun Pi in a phawk hi.

records.english: Do you know whether we need permission to build a wall in the garden?
records.zomi: Huan sungah bang khat lam dingin phalna i kisam hiam cih na thei hiam?

records.english: We learned that our neighbour's tree is our responsibility if it falls on our side.
records.zomi: I inn veng' sing kung i lam ah a puk leh kote' mawhpuakna ahi hi, cih i sin uh hi.

records.english: Our children know that it's against the law to steal, even something small.
records.zomi: Bangmah neuno khat zong guk pen thukham tawh kituak lo hi, cih i tate in a thei uh hi.

records.english: Our son's school invited a police officer to talk about the law and young people.
records.zomi: I tapa' sang in thukham leh khangnote tawh kisai gen dingin police khat a sam hi.

records.english: Grandpa says the law should protect the weak, not only the strong.
records.zomi: Thukham in a hat te bek hi lo-in a hat lo te zong a kem ding hi, Pu in a ci hi.

records.english: My parents helped us understand the rules about renting our first flat.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in i inn masa pen luah tawh kisai thukhunte i theisiam nadingin hong huh uh hi.

records.english: My parents always obey the law, even when nobody is watching.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in kuamah a en loh hangin thukham a zui den uh hi.

records.english: Can you explain the new tax rules to me, Dad?
records.zomi: Pa, siah tawh kisai thukhun thakte hong gen thei ding hiam?

records.english: Is it better to specialise early or to keep your options open?

records.english: Is this year's intake larger than last year's?

records.english: Is the new timetable better than the old one?

records.english: Would the students prefer a trip to the museum or to the factory?

records.english: Which internship offers better experience for a young engineer?

records.english: Grandpa was embarrassed to report his fall, but the doctor said it was important.

records.english: When our son crashed his bicycle into a parked car, he left a note with our phone number.

records.english: Our neighbour helped us fill in the accident form in the right language.
records.zomi: I inn veng in pau dik tawh siatna form a dimsak nadingin hong huh hi.

records.english: My uncle reported a dangerous bend in the road after a family friend crashed there.

records.english: Have you told the school nurse about the bump on your head?

records.zomi: Siatna thu gelh nadingin i innkuan in mawtaw sungah ciamtehna laibu neu khat a kem hi.

records.english: Dad keeps a copy of every accident report in a folder.
records.zomi: Pa in siatna report khempeuh' kopi folder khat sungah a kem hi.

records.english: Mum wrote a careful description of her fall for the hospital.
records.zomi: Nu in damdawi inn adingin a puk zia kidawm takin a gelh hi.

records.english: My sister reported the dog that bit her son, so that it wouldn't hurt anyone else.
records.zomi: Ka u numei in a tapa a kek ui a theisak a, midang a liamsak nawn loh nadingin.

records.english: Shall I call the police, or can we sort it out between us?

records.english: Did the school tell you how the accident happened?

records.english: When our son fell off his bike, we reported the broken drain cover to the council.
records.zomi: I tapa a siiksakol tung pan a kiak ciangin tuikuang khuhna kisia council kiangah i theisak uh hi.

records.english: How much detail should I give about my fall at school?
records.zomi: Sang-a ka puk tawh kisai bangzah ka gen ding hiam?

records.english: Describe it step by step, in plain words, as you saw it.
records.zomi: Na muh bangin, kammal baih tawh, a kalsuan khatciat-in gen in.

records.english: Is it too late to report an accident that happened last week?
records.zomi: Kal sung-a piang siatna khat gen dingin a phawng khin hiam?

records.english: My cousin forgot to report a small accident, and later the insurance refused to pay.

records.english: Children may not report accidents if they think they will be blamed.

records.english: Can you help Grandma explain the accident to the officer?
records.zomi: Pi in officer kiangah siatna a gen nadingin na huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: My husband called the insurance company from the side of the road.
records.zomi: Ka pasal in lampi gei pan insurance company a sam hi.

records.english: Our teenager was shaking after the minor crash, so I made the phone calls.
records.zomi: Siatna neuno khit ciangin i tangnu a lin ahih manin phone ka sam hi.

records.english: The police officer was kind to Grandma when she reported the accident.
records.zomi: Pi in siatna a gen ciangin police in a hehpih hi.

records.english: Our daughter learned to describe events clearly after her small accident at school.
records.zomi: Sang-a a siatna neuno khit ciangin i tanu in thupiangte kician takin gen a sin hi.

records.english: We reported the broken streetlight after Grandpa walked into a post in the dark.
records.zomi: Khuamial ah Pu in khuam khat a tawng khit ciangin lampi meivak kisia i theisak uh hi.

records.english: Did you tell your boss about the accident on the way to work?

records.english: We photographed the wet floor where my father slipped in the hospital corridor.

records.english: Our children know to tell a teacher immediately if anyone gets hurt.

records.english: Did you remember to tell the landlord about the leak that made me slip?
records.zomi: Hong kizuatsak tui luang tawh kisai inn neipa kiangah na gen hiam?

records.english: Did you report the broken step at the shop where Grandma fell?
records.zomi: Pi a puk na sumbuk-a kahlei kisia na theisak hiam?

records.english: Yes, and the manager wrote it in their accident book.
records.zomi: Ka theisak hi, manager in amau siatna laibu ah a gelh hi.

records.english: Who should we tell about the hole in the playground fence?

records.english: Not the police, but we should tell the insurance company.
records.zomi: Police hi lo-in, ahi zongin insurance company i gen ding hi.

records.english: My wife called the school to report that our son had been hurt on the bus.
records.zomi: I tapa bus tungah a liam hi, ci-in ka zi in sang a sam hi.

records.english: A calm report after an accident makes everything easier later.

records.english: My brother and I used to catch tadpoles in the stream behind our house.

records.english: Who told you that story about the giant bird?

records.english: In the exam, we had to summarise a long article in a hundred words.

records.english: Summarising helps students remember what they have studied.

records.english: A short summary of the minutes was sent to everyone who was absent.

records.english: A summary should be accurate, even if it is short.

records.english: Summarising customer feedback helped us see which problems were most common.

records.english: When summarising, leave out examples and keep the main ideas.

records.english: Our supervisor asked us to summarise each chapter of the safety manual.

records.english: I summarised the meeting in five bullet points for the team.

records.english: A good summary tells the reader what happened, to whom, and why it matters.

records.english: Can you summarise the client's email in two sentences?
records.zomi: Client' email kammal tang nih tawh na tomkim thei ding hiam?

records.english: They're happy with the design but want the delivery date moved forward.
records.zomi: Design ah a lungdam uh a, ahi zongin van tunna ni a ma lam ah sawn a deih uh hi.

records.english: Summarising a discussion is harder than summarising a written text.

records.english: The best summaries are written after you understand the whole text.
records.zomi: Tomkimna hoih pen te laigelh bup na theisiam khit ciangin a kigelh hi.

records.english: A summary that changes the meaning of the original is worse than no summary at all.

records.english: The lecturer asked us to write a summary of the case study before the seminar.

records.english: Can you summarise what the customer wanted on the phone?

records.english: Summaries in plain language make reports accessible to everyone.
records.zomi: Kammal baih-a tomkimna te in report te mi khempeuh adingin a theisiam baih sak hi.

records.english: Each department sends a monthly summary to the head office.

records.english: My summary of the project was presented to the board.
records.zomi: Project tawh kisai ka tomkimna board kiangah a kilak hi.

records.english: I'll send you a summary of the conference by the end of the week.
records.zomi: Kal tawp ma-in conference tomkimna khat kong khak ding hi.

records.english: My wife sends me a message when she's leaving work.

records.zomi: Pu in a ngah thugen khempeuh a forward ahih manin a en masa dingin i sinsak uh hi.

records.english: Mum, can I join the cousins' group chat?

records.english: My little brother sends funny stickers instead of writing words.

records.english: Let's agree to keep the family chat for important news only.

records.english: Should we make a separate group for planning Grandpa's surprise party?
records.zomi: Pu' lamdang poai ciamteh nadingin group tuam khat i bawl ding hiam?

records.zomi: Bawl ni, innkuan group sung-a message te a muh loh nadingin.

records.english: Dad replies to every message with a thumbs-up.
records.zomi: Pa in message khempeuh thumbs-up tawh a dawng hi.

records.english: I sent my brother a voice message because I was driving.
records.zomi: Mawtaw ka tawl lai ahih manin ka u pasal kiangah voice message khat ka khak hi.

records.english: Our family group chat is full of photos of the children.

records.zomi: Nitak an tawh kisai Pa' message na mu hiam?

records.english: Yes, he'll be home late, so we should eat without him.
records.zomi: Mu hi, inn a phawng-in a tung ding ahih manin amah om lo-in an i ne ding hi.

records.english: When Grandpa's phone broke, he missed a whole week of family news.
records.zomi: Pu' phone a sia ciangin innkuan thuthak kal khat bup a mangngilh kha hi.

records.english: Family groups work best when everyone respects each other's time.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh in a kihun zahtak tuah ciangin innkuan group te a hoih pen hi.

records.english: When the baby was born, the family group filled with congratulations in minutes.
records.zomi: Naungek a suah ciangin innkuan group minit tawmno sung-in lungdampihna tawh a dim hi.

records.english: My wife saves every message from her late mother.
records.zomi: Ka zi in a sihsa nu pan message khempeuh a kem hi.

records.english: Messaging makes it easy to say sorry, but it's still better to say it in person.
records.zomi: Message in maisak ngen a baihsak a, ahi zongin kimaituah-a gen a hoih zaw lai hi.

records.english: Can you send the photos to me privately instead of to the group?
records.zomi: Group kiang sangin kei kiangah bek photo te na khak thei ding hiam?

records.zomi: Bang hangin group sungah ciamtehna kikhekna kuamah in hong gen kei uh hiam?

records.english: Mum reads our messages aloud to Grandpa, who can't see well.
records.zomi: Nu in i message te a mit a muh hoih loh Pu adingin aw tawh a sim hi.

records.english: Our daughter's school sends messages when classes are cancelled.
records.zomi: Class a kiphiat ciangin i tanu' sang in message a khak hi.

records.zomi: I tapa a mang ciangin innkuan group kiang-a message hun khat in amah i muh nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: The family chat helped us organise care for Grandma when she was ill.
records.zomi: Pi a cina lai-in amah kem nading ciamteh dingin innkuan chat in hong huh hi.

records.english: Our children message us when they arrive at school.
records.zomi: I tate in sang a tun ciangun message hong khak uh hi.

records.english: Messages can sometimes sound colder than we mean them to.
records.zomi: Message te in i deih sangin a vot zaw bang-in a kiza thei hi.

records.english: We use a messaging app to share our location when we travel.
records.zomi: I khualzin ciangin i omna mun hawm nadingin messaging app khat i zang uh hi.

records.english: My sister and I message each other every night, even though we live in different countries.
records.zomi: Gam tuam ah i teng hangin ka u numei leh kei zan simin message i kikhak tuah uh hi.

records.english: My parents still prefer phone calls to messages.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in message sangin phone sapna a deih zaw lai uh hi.

records.english: We muted the family group during exam week.
records.zomi: Sitna kal sung-in innkuan group i mute uh hi.

records.english: Auntie Lun sends good-morning messages to the whole family every day.
records.zomi: Ni Lun in ni simin innkuan bup kiangah zingsang hoih message a khak hi.

records.english: Our teenager hides her phone whenever a message arrives.
records.zomi: Message a hong tun ciangin i tangnu in a phone a sel hi.

records.english: Can you message Grandma to say we'll be late?
records.zomi: I phawng ding uh hi, ci-in Pi kiangah message na khak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Why is Grandma sending us so many voice messages?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pi in voice message tampi hong khak hiam?

records.english: She finds typing too hard, so she talks instead.
records.zomi: Laimal nek a haksa sa ahih manin a gen zaw hi.

records.english: Can you send me the address by message?
records.zomi: Inn mun message tawh hong khak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Our son taught his grandmother how to delete messages she sent by mistake.
records.zomi: I tapa in a pi kiangah a khial-a a khak message te bangci-in phiat ding cih a sinsak hi.

records.english: Our family uses messaging to share prayers when someone is ill.
records.zomi: Mi khat a cina ciangin i innkuan in thungetna kihawm nadingin message a zang hi.

records.english: Who added the neighbours to our family group?
records.zomi: I innkuan group ah inn vengte kua in a beh hiam?

records.english: Did you reply to Auntie's message about the wedding?
records.zomi: Mopawi tawh kisai Ni' message na dawng hiam?

records.english: Did you get my message, or is your phone off again?
records.zomi: Ka message na ngah hiam, na phone a mit kik hiam?

records.english: A long message from my father on my birthday made me cry.
records.zomi: Ka suahni-in ka pa' message sau khat in hong kapsak hi.

records.english: Dad finally learned to use emojis, and now he uses them in every message.
records.zomi: A tawp-in Pa in emoji zat a sin a, tu-in message khempeuh ah a zang hi.

records.english: Our son's class has a parents' group where the teacher shares news.
records.zomi: I tapa' class in saya in thuthak a hawmna nu leh pate' group khat a nei hi.

records.english: Your message made Grandpa's whole day.
records.zomi: Na message in Pu' ni bup a nuamsak hi.

records.english: Voice messages help my grandmother hear her grandchildren's voices every day.
records.zomi: Voice message te in ka pi in ni simin a tute' aw a za thei hi.

records.english: Auntie Hoih sent a scam message to the whole family without realising.
records.zomi: Ni Hoih in a theih loh-in khemna message khat innkuan bup kiangah a khak hi.

records.english: Did anyone send a message to Uncle about his operation?
records.zomi: Pa neu' zaina tawh kisai kuamah in message a khak hiam?

records.english: Shall I create a group for the family holiday?
records.zomi: Innkuan tawlngakni adingin group khat ka bawl ding hiam?

records.english: My grandmother learned to make video calls through the messaging app.
records.zomi: Ka pi in messaging app tungtawnin video call bawl a sin hi.

records.english: My cousin sent a message to the wrong group, and everyone laughed.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam in group khial khat ah message a khak a, mi khempeuh a nui uh hi.

records.english: Messages from home help students abroad feel less lonely.
records.zomi: Inn pan message te in gamdang-a sangnaupangte kia-a om a kisak tawmsak hi.

records.english: My uncle sends long messages that nobody has time to read.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in kuamah in sim hun a neih loh message sau te a khak hi.

records.english: Our family group has a rule: no politics and no forwarded videos.
records.zomi: I innkuan group in thukhun khat a nei hi: politics om lo, forward video om lo.

records.english: Messaging apps help our family stay close despite living far apart.
records.zomi: Gamla-a i teng hangin messaging app te in i innkuan a kinai-in a om nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: The nurse asked us to stay calm and answer her questions one at a time.
records.zomi: Nurse in dai-in i om a, a dotnate khat ciat-in dawng dingin hong ngen hi.

records.english: I'm not sure what she ate, but she started coughing right after lunch.
records.zomi: Bang a ne hiam cih ka thei kei a, ahi zongin sun an khit pah-in a khuk kipan hi.

records.english: When my husband collapsed, I could tell the doctors exactly what he had eaten.
records.zomi: Ka pasal a puk ciangin bang a ne hiam cih siavuante kiangah kician takin ka gen thei hi.

records.english: Did Grandpa hit his head when he fell?
records.zomi: Pu a puk ciangin a lu a kitawng hiam?

records.english: Is your mother diabetic?
records.zomi: Na nu in diabetes a nei hiam?

records.english: We showed the paramedics the empty tablet packet we found by Grandpa's bed.
records.zomi: Pu' lupna kiangah i muh damdawi tang ip awng damdawi huhtute i lak uh hi.

records.english: Please call me as soon as you have any news about my mother.
records.zomi: Ka nu tawh kisai thuthak na neih pah ciangin hong sam in.

records.english: When communication is clear, emergency treatment is faster and safer.
records.zomi: Kihopihna a kician ciangin lauhuai hun-a damdawi piakna a hun zaw a, a bit zaw hi.

records.english: Please tell the doctor that my wife is pregnant.
records.zomi: Ka zi nau a pai hi, ci-in siavuan kiangah gen in.

records.english: Thank you for explaining everything so clearly to my parents.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa kiangah khempeuh kician takin na gen manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: Our children know to tell the doctor about their peanut allergy.
records.zomi: I tate in bekang allergy a neih uh siavuan kiangah gen ding cih a thei uh hi.

records.english: Grandma's heart condition is written on a card in her purse.
records.zomi: Pi' lungtang natna a sum ip sung-a card khat tungah a kigelh hi.

records.english: The ambulance crew kept us informed about what they were doing.
records.zomi: Ambulance nasemte in a sep te hong theisak den uh hi.

records.english: Is anyone here a family member?

records.english: Who's the best person to talk to about Grandma's medicines?
records.zomi: Pi' damdawi te tawh kisai kua tawh kihopih a hoih pen ding hiam?

records.english: Auntie Mang's medical history was in a folder by the front door, ready for emergencies.
records.zomi: Ni Mang' damdawi tangthu lauhuai hun adingin a kiging-in mai kongkhak kiang-a folder khat sungah a om hi.

records.english: We explained to the paramedic that Grandma had fallen twice this week.

records.english: Do you know your grandfather's date of birth?
records.zomi: Na pu' suahni na thei hiam?

records.english: The paramedic asked the children to tell her what had happened, and they did it calmly.
records.zomi: Damdawi huhtu in naupangte bang a piang hiam cih gen dingin a ngen a, dai takin a gen uh hi.

records.english: Our family doctor's number is saved in all our phones.

records.english: Our neighbour helped explain Grandma's condition because she speaks the local language better.

records.english: My brother forgot to mention his asthma, which delayed his treatment.
records.zomi: Ka u pasal in a asthma gen a mangngilh a, tua in a damdawi piakna a phawngsak hi.

records.english: When did your husband start feeling unwell?
records.zomi: Na pasal bang ciang pan a dam lo kipan hiam?

records.english: About an hour ago, after dinner.
records.zomi: Nai khat bang ma-in, nitak an khit ciangin.

records.english: We keep a list of everyone's medicines in the family emergency folder.

records.english: Shall we put a medical information sheet on the fridge for the babysitter?
records.zomi: Naupang kemtu adingin fridge tungah damdawi thu lai-ek khat i koih ding hiam?

records.english: I'll stay with Dad and answer any questions the doctors have.

records.zomi: Na tanu in allergy khatpeuh a nei hiam?

records.english: My wife's phone has an emergency card with her medical information.

records.zomi: A lungtang natna gen inla, a damdawi ciamtehna lak in.

records.english: We practised telling the emergency operator our address and Grandma's condition.

records.english: Can you tell us what medicines your mother takes?

records.english: When my son was injured, I gave the doctors his date of birth and blood type.

records.english: I chose to work in a restaurant during the holidays to learn how a business runs.
