records.zomi: Kha bei-a team in nai bangzah na a sem uh hiam cih hong gen thei ding hiam?

records.english: The nurse calculated the dose carefully, using the child's weight in kilograms.
records.zomi: Nurse in naupang' gikna kilogram tawh zang-in damdawi zah kidawm takin a sim hi.

records.english: How much is 3 metres of fabric at $6 a metre?
records.zomi: Meter khat $6 man puan meter 3 bangzah hiam?

records.english: If the shop sells 40 loaves a day, how many does it sell in a week?
records.zomi: Sumbuk in ni khat ah moh 40 a zuak leh kal khat ah bangzah a zuak ding hiam?

records.english: The new trainee divided the stock by the number of shelves and filled each one evenly.
records.zomi: Trainee thak in van te dawh zah tawh a khen a, khatciat kikim-in a dimsak hi.

records.english: I worked out the area of the classroom so that we could order new carpet.
records.zomi: Puan-phah thak i order theih nadingin sangdan' zatzah ka sim hi.

records.english: Our manager asked us to estimate how many customers we would serve during the holiday.
records.zomi: Tawlngakni sung-in customer bangzah i nasem sak ding hiam cih ngaihsun dingin i manager in hong ngen hi.

records.english: A mistake with a decimal point can make a price ten times too high.
records.zomi: Decimal point tawh khialhna khat in man khat sawmvei a sangsak thei hi.

records.english: Calculating the cost per unit helped the factory decide which product to stop making.
records.zomi: Khat ciat' man sim in factory in bang van bawl khawl ding hiam cih a khensat nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Double the numbers in the second column, then add them to the first.
records.zomi: Kigual nihna sung-a nambat te nihvei-in bawl inla, a masa pen tawh beh in.

records.english: Can you work out the percentage of students who passed?
records.zomi: Sitna a zo sangnaupangte' percentage na sim thei ding hiam?

records.english: Thank you for checking my figures before the meeting.
records.zomi: Kikhopna ma-in ka nambat te hong en manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: The farmer calculated how many sacks of seed he needed for each field.
records.zomi: Loubawlpa in lou khatciat adingin chi ip bangzah a kisam hiam cih a sim hi.

records.english: I keep a small notebook for adding up my travel expenses.
records.zomi: Ka khualzinna sum zat te beh nadingin ciamtehna laibu neu khat ka kem hi.

records.english: How many hours did you work this week?
records.zomi: Hih kal sung-in nai bangzah na sem hiam?

records.english: 38, including two hours of overtime on Thursday.
records.zomi: 38, Laizing ni-a hun beh nai nih zong kihel-in.

records.english: Write the sum on the board, and show each step clearly.
records.zomi: Board tungah kisimna gelh inla, a kalsuan khatciat kician takin lak in.

records.english: The accountant spotted an error of $1,000 in last year's figures.
records.zomi: Accountant in nidang kum nambat te ah $1,000 khialhna khat a mu hi.

records.english: Can you check whether the invoice adds up?
records.zomi: Invoice a dik hiam cih na en thei ding hiam?

records.english: The items come to $460, but the total says $490.
records.zomi: Van te $460 a suak a, ahi zongin a vekpi in $490 a ci hi.

records.english: The architect's calculations showed that the roof could carry the weight of the snow.
records.zomi: Architect' kisimna in inn tung in vuuk gikna a pua thei hi, cih a lak hi.

records.english: Our company pays 40 cents a kilometre for car travel, so I keep a record of every trip.
records.zomi: I company in mawtaw khualzinna adingin kilometre khat ah cent 40 a pia ahih manin khualzinna khempeuh ka ciamteh hi.

records.english: Our maths teacher let us use calculators only for the final question.
records.zomi: I maths saya in a tawp pen dotna adingin bek calculator zat a phal hi.

records.english: What's 15% of 200?
records.zomi: 200 a za-a 15 bangzah hiam?

records.english: It's 30.
records.zomi: 30 ahi hi.

records.english: The cashier counts the money in the till at the end of every shift.
records.zomi: Sum lakpa in nasep hun khatciat a tawp ciangin sum bawm sung-a sum a sim hi.

records.english: Our science teacher showed us how to calculate speed from distance and time.
records.zomi: I science saya in gamla zah leh hun pan manlanna bangci-in sim ding cih hong lak hi.

records.english: How many boxes of tiles do we need for a floor of 24 square metres?
records.zomi: Square metre 24 lei adingin tile bawm bangzah i kisam hiam?

records.english: Each box covers 2 square metres, so we need 12, plus one spare.
records.zomi: Bawm khatciat in square metre 2 a khuh ahih manin 12 i kisam a, a beh khat zong.

records.english: Spreadsheets do the calculations, but someone still has to check that the formulas are right.
records.zomi: Spreadsheet te in a sim hi, ahi zongin formula te a dik hiam cih kuamah in a en lai kul hi.

records.english: If prices rise by 10% and then fall by 10%, you don't end up where you started.
records.zomi: Man za-a 10 a khang a, tua khit ciangin za-a 10 a kiam leh na kipatna mun ah na tung kik kei hi.

records.english: I add up my tips at the end of every evening.
records.zomi: Nitak simin ka letsong sum te ka beh khawm hi.

records.english: Please sign at the bottom of each page.
records.zomi: Lai-ek khatciat nuai lam ah min gelh in.

records.english: Do Mum and Dad have a will?
records.zomi: Nu leh Pa in gamluah lai a nei uh hiam?

records.english: Yes, they made one with a lawyer after our youngest sister was born.
records.zomi: Nei uh hi, i nau numei neu pen a suah khit ciangin thukham siam khat tawh a bawl uh hi.

records.english: Our son's school asked for a copy of the court order about custody.
records.zomi: I tapa' sang in naupang kemna tawh kisai thukhenna thupiak kopi a ngen hi.

records.english: We registered our daughter's birth the week after she was born.
records.zomi: I tanu a suah khit kal khat ciangin a suahna i ciamteh uh hi.

records.english: My parents hired an interpreter so that Grandma could follow the hearing.
records.zomi: Pi in thukhenna kikhop a zui theih nadingin ka nu leh ka pa in pau letpa khat a zang uh hi.

records.english: Our neighbour helped my parents fill in the forms for their citizenship application.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa a gam mi hihna ngetna form a dimsak nadingin i inn veng in a huh hi.

records.english: When my cousin changed her surname after marriage, she had to update every document.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam a kiteen khit ciangin a min tawp a khek a, lai khempeuh a khek kul hi.

records.english: Hearing the judge read out the decision, my mother burst into tears.
records.zomi: Thukhenpa in thukhensatna a sim a zak ciangin ka nu a kap pah hi.

records.english: Dad was called for jury service and had to take a week off work.
records.zomi: Pa jury nasep dingin kisam a, nasep pan kal khat a tawl kul hi.

records.english: Who will be the children's guardian if something happens to us?
records.zomi: Kote tungah bangkhat a piang leh naupangte' kemtu kua ding hiam?

records.english: Legal steps that seem cold to a family are often there to protect its weakest members.
records.zomi: Innkuan khat adingin a vot bang-a kilang thukham kalsuanna te a hat lo pen mite kem nadingin a om zel hi.

records.english: Mum keeps every legal document in a locked box under the bed.
records.zomi: Nu in thukham lai khempeuh lupna nuai-a khak bawm khat sungah a kem hi.

records.english: Did you remember to sign the form in black ink?
records.zomi: Form ah ink vom tawh min gelh na phawk hiam?

records.english: How much does it cost to get a document certified?
records.zomi: Lai khat kipsakna nadingin bangzah a man hiam?

records.english: Can we write a simple will ourselves, or should we pay a lawyer?
records.zomi: Gamluah lai baih khat eimah in i gelh thei ding hiam, thukham siam khat i pia ding hiam?

records.english: My aunt became my grandmother's legal guardian after Grandma's memory began to fail.
records.zomi: Pi' phawkna a kiam kipat khit ciangin ka ni Pi' thukham kemtu-in a suak hi.

records.english: Dad had to swear an oath before he gave evidence.
records.zomi: Pa in tecipanna a piak ma-in kiciamna a bawl kul hi.

records.english: My parents had their signatures on the will witnessed by two neighbours.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in gamluah lai tunga a min gelhnate inn veng nih in a teci uh hi.

records.english: The police came to our house to take Mum's statement about the stolen bicycle.
records.zomi: Siiksakol kiguk tawh kisai Nu' thugen la dingin police i inn ah a hong uh hi.

records.english: Why does the notary need to see both of you?
records.zomi: Bang hangin notary in note nih a muh kul hiam?

records.english: Because the house is in both our names, so we both have to sign in person.
records.zomi: Bang hang hiam cih leh inn pen kote nih' min tawh a om ahih manin kimaituah-in kote nih min i gelh kul hi.

records.english: How long did the adoption take?
records.zomi: Ta kiteh bangzah sawt hiam?

records.english: Almost two years, with home visits, interviews and a final court hearing.
records.zomi: Kum nih dek, inn vehna, interview leh a tawp-a thukhenna kikhop tawh.

records.english: Our family went to court together to support my uncle at his hearing.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu a thukhenna kikhop ah amah panpih dingin i innkuan khawm-in thukhenna ah i pai uh hi.

records.english: Have you got the letter from the court?
records.zomi: Thukhenna pan laikhak na ngah hiam?

records.english: We had to wait six weeks before the court approved the change to our son's name.
records.zomi: I tapa' min kikhekna thukhenna in a phal ma-in kal guk i ngak kul uh hi.

records.english: Will Dad have to go to court because of the speeding fine?
records.zomi: Manlang taka mawtaw tawl dan hangin Pa thukhenna ah a pai kul ding hiam?

records.english: Only if he decides to challenge it, according to the letter.
records.zomi: Laikhak bangin, a nial nop leh bek.

records.english: Let's photocopy everything before we hand in the originals.
records.zomi: A bulpi te i piak ma-un khempeuh photocopy i bawl ni.

records.english: In our country, a marriage is official only after it has been registered at the town hall.
records.zomi: I gam ah kiteenna pen khuapi office ah a kiciamteh khit ciang bek-in a kipsak hi.

records.english: The judge spoke kindly to my little brother when he gave evidence.
records.zomi: Ka nau pasal in tecipanna a piak ciangin thukhenpa in nem takin a kihopih hi.

records.english: Dividing an inheritance fairly takes patience as well as paperwork.
records.zomi: Gamluah dik taka khen pen lai nasep bek hi lo-in thuakzawhna zong a kisam hi.

records.english: Did the court accept the guardianship application?
records.zomi: Thukhenna in kemtu ngetna a sang hiam?

records.english: We kept a diary of every noise complaint, as the council's lawyer had advised.
records.zomi: Council' thukham siam in a hilh bangin ging tawh kisai phunna khempeuh ciamtehna laibu khat ah i kem uh hi.

records.english: Mum was relieved when the judge agreed that the debt wasn't hers.
records.zomi: Leiba pen a leiba hi lo hi, ci-in thukhenpa in a kilem ciangin Nu a lungdam hi.

records.english: My grandparents' marriage was never registered, which caused problems when Grandpa died.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh pi te' kiteenna a kiciamteh ngei kei a, Pu a sih ciangin haksatna a piangsak hi.

records.english: Uncle Thang paid a lawyer to check the contract before he bought the field.
records.zomi: Lou a lei ma-in Pa neu Thang in contract en nadingin thukham siam khat a pia hi.

records.english: Grandma gave Dad power of attorney so that he could manage her bank account.
records.zomi: Pi in a bank account a kem theih nadingin Pa thuneihna a pia hi.

records.english: Where do we register Grandpa's death?
records.zomi: Pu' sihna koi-ah i ciamteh ding hiam?

records.english: At the town hall, and we have to take the doctor's certificate with us.
records.zomi: Khuapi office ah, siavuan' lai-ciam zong i paipih kul hi.

records.english: The court letter was so formal that my father asked me to explain it in simple words.
records.zomi: Thukhenna laikhak a khauh mahmah ahih manin ka pa in kammal baih tawh gen dingin hong ngen hi.

records.english: The registry office sent us the marriage certificate by post.
records.zomi: Ciamtehna office in kiteenna lai-ciam post-in hong khak hi.

records.english: When my parents divorced, a mediator helped them agree on where we would live.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa a kikhen ciangin kilemsaktu khat in koi-ah i teng ding hiam cih ah a kilem nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Our family's dispute over the shared well was settled without going to court.
records.zomi: Kihawm tuikhuk tawh kisai i innkuan kitelna thukhenna pai lo-in a kilemsak hi.

records.english: The lawyer asked us to find the old papers that prove the land belonged to Grandpa.
records.zomi: Gam pen Pu' a hihna a kipsak lai lui te zong dingin thukham siam in hong ngen hi.

records.english: Our family lawyer explained each step of selling Grandma's house.
records.zomi: I innkuan thukham siam in Pi' inn zuakna kalsuanna khatciat a gen hi.

records.english: After months of paperwork, the adoption hearing took only twenty minutes.
records.zomi: Kha tampi lai nasep khit ciangin ta kiteh thukhenna kikhop minit sawmnih bek a sau hi.

records.english: Thank you for coming to the hearing with me.
records.zomi: Thukhenna kikhop ah kei tawh na hong manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: Is it true that we need two witnesses for the marriage registration?
records.zomi: Kiteenna ciamteh nadingin teci nih i kisam hi, cih a dik hiam?

records.english: Bring your birth certificate and two photos to the passport appointment.
records.zomi: Passport kimuhna ah na pianna lai leh photo nih paipih in.

records.english: Who's going to read Grandpa's will to the family?
records.zomi: Pu' gamluah lai innkuan kiangah kua in a sim ding hiam?

records.english: When the landlord refused to return our deposit, my parents wrote him a formal letter before going any further.
records.zomi: Inn neipa in i dawng sum a ap kik nuam loh ciangin ka nu leh ka pa in a ma-a kalsuan ma-un khauh taka laikhak khat a gelh uh hi.

records.english: Where should we send the copies of the death certificate?
records.zomi: Sihna lai-ciam kopi te koi-ah i khak ding hiam?

records.english: Does the court send the decision to both families?
records.zomi: Thukhenna in thukhensatna innkuan nih kiangah a khak hiam?

records.english: Can you come with me to the notary on Friday?
records.zomi: Laithai ni-in notary kiangah kei tawh na hong thei ding hiam?

records.english: My wife and I updated our wills when we bought the house.
records.zomi: Inn i lei ciangin ka zi leh kei i gamluah lai i khek kik uh hi.

records.english: My sister was nervous before her first court appearance as a witness.
records.zomi: Ka u numei teci-in a masa pen-a thukhenna ah a pai ma-in a lau hi.

records.english: Families who keep their papers in order face far fewer problems in court.
records.zomi: A lai te kician taka a kem innkuante thukhenna ah haksatna a tawm zaw mahmah uh hi.

records.english: Shall we ask the lawyer to explain the will in plain language?
records.zomi: Thukham siam in gamluah lai kammal baih tawh a gen dingin i ngen ding hiam?

records.english: Always walk the children to the bus stop until they're old enough to go alone.
records.zomi: Naupangte a kia-in a pai theih dong bus khawlna mun ah paipih den in.

records.english: Our son learned to swim before we let him play near the river.
records.zomi: Lui kiangah a kimawl dingin i phal ma-in i tapa tuipeek a sin hi.

records.english: We fitted a gate at the top of the stairs when our son started crawling.
records.zomi: I tapa a kibawh kipat ciangin kahlei tung ah kongkhak khat i koih uh hi.

records.english: We keep a first-aid kit in the car and another in the kitchen.
records.zomi: Mawtaw sungah first-aid kit khat, an huanna ah khat i kem uh hi.

records.english: After our neighbour's toddler pulled a television onto himself, we fixed all our heavy furniture to the wall.
records.zomi: I inn veng' naupang neu in TV a tungah a khaisuk khit ciangin i van gik khempeuh bang tawh i khih uh hi.

records.english: Before we go hiking, we always tell a neighbour our route and when we'll be back.
records.zomi: Mual ah i kal ma-un i paina lampi leh i ciah kik hun inn veng khat i theisak den uh hi.

records.english: Auntie Lun taught her grandchildren to stop, drop and roll if their clothes ever catch fire.
records.zomi: A puan uh a kan leh khawl un, lum un, kiheel un, ci-in Ni Lun in a tute a sinsak hi.

records.english: Don't share your address or school name with people you meet online.
records.zomi: Online-a na kimuh mite kiangah na inn mun ahi zongin na sang min gen kei in.

records.english: Shall we practise what to do if the smoke alarm goes off at night?
records.zomi: Zan-in meikhu vaihilhna a ging leh bang hih ding cih i kisin ding hiam?

records.english: Teach your grandparents to hang up on callers who ask for bank details.
records.zomi: Bank thu a ngen sam mite' phone khak dingin na pu leh pi te sinsak in.

records.english: Why do you lock the garden shed every evening?
records.zomi: Bang hangin nitak simin huan inn neu na khak hiam?

records.english: A family that talks about safety calmly is less likely to panic in a real emergency.
records.zomi: Bitna tawh kisai dai taka a kikup innkuan khat lauhuai hun taktak-in a lau baih kei hi.

records.english: Teach your children which berries in the garden are poisonous.
records.zomi: Huan sung-a theigah neu bang te in gu a nei hiam cih na tate sinsak in.

records.english: Don't answer the door to strangers when we're out.
records.zomi: Kote i om loh ciangin mi theih ngeih lo te adingin kongkhak hong kei un.

records.english: Our children know our home address and Mum's phone number by heart.
records.zomi: I tate in i inn mun leh Nu' phone nambat a lungsim-in a thei uh hi.

records.english: Empty the paddling pool every evening so that nobody falls in at night.
records.zomi: Zan-in kuamah a kiak loh nadingin nitak simin naupang tuipeek kuang a tui sung khia un.

records.english: Can I go on the trampoline with my cousins?
records.zomi: Ka sanggamte tawh trampoline tungah ka kah thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, but only one at a time, and nobody does flips.
records.zomi: Thei hi, ahi zongin khat ciat-in bek, kuamah kiheel lo-in.

records.english: My uncle installed a carbon monoxide alarm after hearing about a family who fell ill from their heater.
records.zomi: A meisa hangin a cina innkuan khat tawh kisai a zak khit ciangin ka pa neu in carbon monoxide vaihilhna khat a koih hi.

records.english: Can you make sure the fireguard is in front of the fire before the children come in?
records.zomi: Naupangte a lut ma-un mei kemna mei maiah a om hiam cih na en thei ding hiam?

records.english: Mum, why can't I sleep with my phone charging under my pillow?
records.zomi: Nu, bang hangin ka lukhung nuai-ah ka phone charge kawm-in ka ihmu thei kei hiam?

records.english: Because it can overheat and start a fire.
records.zomi: Bang hang hiam cih leh a sa luat thei a, mei a piangsak thei hi.

records.english: Store matches and lighters where small children can't reach them.
records.zomi: Meitawh leh meikhet te naupang neute' tun theih loh mun ah koih in.

records.english: Make sure the babysitter knows where the fire extinguisher is kept.
records.zomi: Mei mitna koi-ah a kikem hiam cih naupang kemtu in a theih nadingin kem in.

records.english: When my sister's baby started walking, she covered every sharp corner with soft pads.
records.zomi: Ka u numei' naungek a pai kipat ciangin a zum mun khempeuh nem tawh a khuh hi.

records.english: Mum taught us to turn off the heater before we leave the room.
records.zomi: Inndan i paisan ma-in meisa phiat dingin Nu in hong sinsak hi.

records.english: Grandpa tests the smoke alarms on the first day of every month.
records.zomi: Pu in kha khatciat' ni masa pen-in meikhu vaihilhna te a sit hi.

records.english: Why do we need life jackets if we can all swim?
records.zomi: I khempeuh in tuipeek i thei leh bang hangin nuntakna puan i kisam hiam?

records.english: Because even strong swimmers can get tired or cold in a lake.
records.zomi: Bang hang hiam cih leh tuipeek siam mahmah te zong dil sungah a gim thei a, a vot thei uh hi.

records.english: Is it safe to leave the candles burning while we eat in the garden?
records.zomi: Huan sungah an i nek lai-in khawimeivaak a kang lai-in nusia a bit hiam?

records.english: No, blow them out first; it only takes a moment.
records.zomi: Bit lo hi, a masa-in mut mit in; hun tomno bek a la hi.

records.english: Wear gloves when you use the hedge trimmer, and keep the cable behind you.
records.zomi: Huang kiatna seh na zat ciangin khut-ip bulh inla, cable na nunglam ah koih in.

records.english: My parents wrote their emergency numbers on a card inside each child's school bag.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in naupang khatciat' sang ip sung-a card khat ah lauhuai nambat te a gelh uh hi.

records.english: Grandma removed the loose rugs from her hallway after the doctor's advice.
records.zomi: Siavuan' thuhilhna khit ciangin Pi in a inn paina lam pan puan-phah kikhai lo te a la khia hi.

records.english: Hold the railing on the boat, and don't lean over the side.
records.zomi: Long tunga khutden len inla, a gei lam ah kun kei in.

records.english: Our family agreed on a meeting point outside in case we ever have to leave the house quickly.
records.zomi: Inn pan a hun-in i pawt kul kha leh cih-in pualam ah kimuhna mun khat i innkuan in i kilem uh hi.

records.english: Keep the barbecue lighter fluid tightly closed and store it in the shed.
records.zomi: Barbecue mei kuanna tui a khauh-in khak inla, huan inn neu ah koih in.

records.english: Our children are allowed to cycle to the park only if they ride together.
records.zomi: I tate in khawm-in a tawl uh leh bek huan lian ah siiksakol a tawl thei uh hi.

records.english: Leaving young children in a parked car, even for a few minutes, can be extremely dangerous.
records.zomi: Minit tawmno sung zong a kikoih mawtaw sungah naupang neute nusiat pen a lauhuai mahmah thei hi.

records.english: Children should learn to say no to an adult who asks them to keep a secret from their parents.
records.zomi: A nu leh pate kiang-a kisel ding thu khat kem dingin a ngen upa khat naupangte in nial dingin a sin ding uh hi.

records.english: Remind Grandma to turn on the light before she gets up at night.
records.zomi: Zan-in a thoh ma-in meivak hal dingin Pi phawksak in.

records.english: Dad taught us never to fly kites near power lines.
records.zomi: Meivak khau kiangah kite lengsak ngei lo dingin Pa in hong sinsak hi.

records.english: Our teenager rolled her eyes when we asked her to share her location on the night out, but she still did it.
records.zomi: Nitak pai-in a omna mun hawm dingin i ngen ciangin i tangnu in a mit a heisak a, ahi zongin a hawm lai hi.

records.english: Never put water on a pan of burning oil; cover it with a lid instead.
records.zomi: A kang sathau beel tungah tui buak ngei kei in; a khuhna tawh khuh zaw in.

records.english: Mum checks the car seat straps every time she puts the baby in.
records.zomi: Nu in naungek a koih ciangin mawtaw tutna khau te a en den hi.

records.english: Why do you always unplug the iron before you leave the house?
records.zomi: Bang hangin inn na paisan ma-in iron na pai khia den hiam?

records.english: Keep hot drinks away from the edge of the table when the baby is around.
records.zomi: Naungek a om ciangin dawn sa te taupi gei pan gamla-ah koih in.

records.english: Can you check that the gas is off before we go to bed?
records.zomi: I lup ma-un gas a phiat hiam cih na en thei ding hiam?

records.english: Please don't let the dog sleep on the stairs; someone will trip over him.
records.zomi: Ui kahlei tungah lum sak kei in; kuamah a tungah a kikhaih kha ding hi.

records.english: When we stay at Grandpa's farm, the children must keep away from the machines.
records.zomi: Pu' lou ah i om ciangin naupangte in seh te pan a gamla-in a om ding uh hi.

records.english: Dad's rule is simple: nobody touches the lawnmower unless he's there.
records.zomi: Pa' thukhun a baih hi: amah a om loh leh kuamah in lopa satna seh a khoih kei ding hi.

records.english: Did you remind the children to wear their helmets?
records.zomi: Naupangte a lukhu uh khuh dingin na phawksak hiam?

records.english: What should we do if Grandpa falls and can't get up?
records.zomi: Pu a puk a, a thou thei kei leh bang i hih ding hiam?

records.english: Our family made a fire escape plan and stuck it on the fridge.
records.zomi: I innkuan in meikang taikhiatna ciamtehna khat a bawl a, fridge tungah i kaap uh hi.

records.english: When fireworks are lit, children must stand behind the rope with an adult.
records.zomi: Meipuak a kihal ciangin naupangte upa khat tawh khau nunglam ah a ding ding uh hi.

records.english: Where should we keep Grandma's tablets when the children visit?
records.zomi: Naupangte a hong veh ciangin Pi' damdawi tang te koi-ah i kem ding hiam?

records.english: In the top cupboard, in a box with a lock.
records.zomi: Tunglam dawh-a khak theih bawm khat sungah.

records.english: Grandpa wears slippers with rubber soles so that he doesn't slip on the tiles.
records.zomi: Tile tungah a kizuat loh nadingin Pu in rubber khe-nuai nei khedap neu a silh hi.

records.english: Grandma keeps a whistle by her bed in case she falls and nobody hears her.
records.zomi: A puk a, kuamah in a zak loh leh cih-in Pi in a lupna kiangah phit khat a kem hi.

records.english: Put your phone away while you're driving, even at traffic lights.
records.zomi: Mawtaw na tawl lai-in, mawtaw meivak khawlna ah zong, na phone koih khol in.

records.english: Which song do you want us to sing at the wedding?
records.zomi: Mopawi ah bang la sa dingin hong deih hiam?

records.english: Last winter, my grandfather sang an old harvest song at the family gathering.
records.zomi: Phalbi nunung-in ka pu in innkuan kikhopna ah lou lakna la lui khat a sa hi.

records.english: Halfway through, his voice shook, and my aunt quietly joined in.
records.zomi: A kim ciangin a aw a lin a, ka ni in dai takin a kihel hi.

records.english: By the last verse, everyone in the room was singing with them.
records.zomi: A tawp pen-a la khen ciangin dan sung-a mi khempeuh amaute tawh la a sa uh hi.

records.english: Everyone, please stand when the elders begin the song.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, upate in la a kipat ciangun ding un.

records.english: In our family, the old songs are sung at every wedding.
records.zomi: I innkuan ah mopawi khempeuh ah la lui te kisa hi.

records.english: I do want to learn the songs my grandfather knows.
records.zomi: Ka pu' theih la te sin ka deih taktak hi.

records.english: Do you remember the song we sang at Grandpa's birthday?
records.zomi: Pu' suahni-a i sak la na phawk hiam?

records.english: Have you noticed that young people in our town are starting to sing the old songs again?
records.zomi: I khuapi-a khangnote in la lui te a sa kik kipan uh hi, cih na mu hiam?

records.english: Is it all right to record the singing at the ceremony?
records.zomi: Kikhopna-a la sakna khum a hoih hiam?

records.english: If nobody learns these songs, they might be forgotten within a generation.
records.zomi: Kuamah in hih la te a sin kei uh leh khangthu khat sung-in mangngilh kha thei hi.

records.english: When does your family sing the old songs?
records.zomi: Na innkuan in la lui te bang ciangin a sa uh hiam?

records.english: Mostly at weddings, at Christmas and when relatives visit from far away.
records.zomi: A tamzaw mopawi ah, Christmas ah, leh gamla pan sanggamte a hong veh ciangun.

records.english: Do you know any traditional songs from your village?
records.zomi: Na khua pan ngeina la khatpeuh na thei hiam?

records.english: Only a few, but my uncle knows dozens.
records.zomi: Tawmno bek, ahi zongin ka pa neu in tampi a thei hi.

records.english: My grandmother sings old songs while she cooks.
records.zomi: Ka pi in an a huan kawm-in la lui te a sa hi.

records.english: My grandmother made me sing the song again until I had learned every word.
records.zomi: Kammal khempeuh ka sin mateng ka pi in la kik dingin hong sasak hi.

records.english: Grandpa had the old cassette of family songs copied onto a CD before it broke.
records.zomi: Innkuan la te' cassette lui a sia ma-in Pu in CD ah a kopi sak hi.

records.english: Shall we sing the welcome song when the visitors arrive?
records.zomi: Khualte a tun ciangun dawnna la i sa ding hiam?

records.english: Nobody in our family knows who first made up the harvest song we sing.
records.zomi: I sak lou lakna la kua in a phuak masa hiam cih i innkuan sung kuamah in a thei kei uh hi.

records.english: Our family sings a thanksgiving song after the harvest is brought in.
records.zomi: Lou lakna a kizawh khit ciangin i innkuan in lungdamna la khat a sa hi.

records.english: Grandpa says that some of the old songs are so long that singing them takes most of the night.
records.zomi: La lui khenkhat a sau mahmah ahih manin a sak in zan a tamzaw a la hi, Pu in a ci hi.

records.english: We sang a farewell song for my brother before he left for university.
records.zomi: University a pai ma-in ka u pasal adingin nusiatna la khat i sa uh hi.

records.english: Why do the elders sing so slowly?
records.zomi: Bang hangin upate in zawi takin la a sa uh hiam?

records.english: They say the slow songs give everyone time to think about the words.
records.zomi: Zawi la te in mi khempeuh kammal te ngaihsun nadingin hun a pia hi, a ci uh hi.

records.english: My uncle recorded the old songs on his phone so that they would not be lost.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in a mangthan loh nadingin a phone tungah la lui te a khum hi.

records.english: Can you sing me the song Grandma used to sing?
records.zomi: Pi' sak zel la hong sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: I'll try, but I only remember the first verse.
records.zomi: Ka sawm ding a, ahi zongin a la khen masa pen bek ka phawk hi.

records.english: Dad's favourite song is about a man who leaves home to find work.
records.zomi: Pa' it pen la pen nasep zong dingin inn a paisan pasal khat tawh kisai ahi hi.

records.english: Who taught you the old songs?
records.zomi: La lui te kua in hong sinsak hiam?

records.english: My grandmother, while she was weaving in the evenings.
records.zomi: Ka pi in, nitak-in puan a tah kawm-in.

records.english: Mum sings a slow traditional song to put the baby to sleep.
records.zomi: Naungek ihmut nadingin Nu in ngeina la zawi khat a sa hi.

records.english: The old women clapped slowly while the young people danced to the song.
records.zomi: Khangnote in la tawh a lam lai-un numei upate in zawi takin khut a beng uh hi.

records.english: Dad hums the same old tune when he works in the field.
records.zomi: Pa in lou ah na a sep ciangin la lui kibang a ngawng hi.

records.english: Learning the old songs is hard, because some of the words are no longer used.
records.zomi: La lui sin a haksa hi, bang hang hiam cih leh a kammal khenkhat a kizang nawn kei hi.

records.english: Some traditional songs in our village are only sung at funerals.
records.zomi: I khua-a ngeina la khenkhat mithi vuina ah bek kisa hi.

records.english: Our teacher invited an elder to sing traditional songs to the class.
records.zomi: I saya in class kiangah ngeina la sa dingin upa khat a sam hi.

records.english: Please write down the words so that the children can practise them at home.
records.zomi: Naupangte in inn ah a kisin theih nadingun kammal te gelh un.

records.english: Singing the old songs together makes us feel close to the people who came before us.
records.zomi: La lui khawm-a sak in ei ma-a hong om mite tawh hong kinaisak hi.

records.english: My cousin plays the guitar while the family sings old songs.
records.zomi: Innkuan in la lui a sak lai-un ka sanggam in guitar a tum hi.

records.english: Visitors are always surprised by how many songs our elders can remember.
records.zomi: I upate in la bangzah tam a phawk uh hiam cih khualte in lamdang a sa den uh hi.

records.english: Our pastor asked the elders to sing a traditional song at the church anniversary.
records.zomi: I pastor in pawlpi kum phawkna ah upate ngeina la khat sa dingin a ngen hi.

records.english: Many of the old songs my grandmother sings tell stories about the land and the people who lived on it.
records.zomi: Ka pi' sak la lui tampi in gam leh tua-a teng mite tawh kisai tangthu a gen uh hi.

records.english: Our youth group is collecting traditional songs from the elders in the community.
records.zomi: I khangno pawl in khuasung-a upate pan ngeina la te a kaikhawm uh hi.

records.english: Grandpa taught me that a traditional song should be sung with respect.
records.zomi: Ngeina la khat zahtakna tawh kisa ding hi, ci-in Pu in hong sinsak hi.

records.english: Mum cried when the choir sang the song from her childhood.
records.zomi: La sa pawl in a naupan lai la a sak uh ciangin Nu a kap hi.

records.english: I can't sing well, but I love listening to the old songs.
records.zomi: La ka sa siam kei a, ahi zongin la lui ngaih ka it hi.

records.english: Could you teach us the song you sang last night?
records.zomi: Zan-a na sak la hong sinsak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Do you also think of Grandma's kitchen when you hear that song?
records.zomi: Tua la na zak ciangin nang zong Pi' an huanna na phawk hiam?

records.english: Songs that have been passed down by memory change a little with every singer.
records.zomi: Phawkna tawh a kipia la te a sa mi khatciat tawh tawmno a kikhel hi.

records.english: Having grown up hearing these songs, I feel at home whenever I hear them.
records.zomi: Hih la te za kawm-in ka khan ahih manin ka zak ciangin inn bang-in ka kisa den hi.

records.english: Recording the elders' songs is one way to keep our oral heritage alive for our children.
records.zomi: Upate' la khum pen i tate adingin i kammal tawh kisan gamh nungta-a kem nading lam khat ahi hi.

records.english: Children, listen carefully to the words, because each verse tells part of a story.
records.zomi: Naupangte, kammal te kidawm takin ngai un, bang hang hiam cih leh la khen khatciat in tangthu khenkhat a gen hi.

records.english: My aunt says that every family in her village had its own songs.
records.zomi: A khua-a innkuan khatciat in a la ciat a nei uh hi, ci-in ka ni in a gen hi.

records.english: Hearing the old songs in a foreign city made me feel homesick.
records.zomi: Gamdang khuapi khat ah la lui ka zak ciangin inn ka ngai hi.

records.english: According to my father, traditional songs were once the way our grandparents remembered important events.
records.zomi: Ka pa' gen bangin ngeina la te pen nidang-in i pu leh pi te in thu thupi te a phawkna lam ahi hi.

records.english: You can sing along if you know the words.
records.zomi: Kammal na theih leh i tawh na sa thei hi.

records.english: Is this song about love or about war?
records.zomi: Hih la pen itna tawh kisai hiam, gal tawh kisai hiam?

records.english: I didn't understand the old words until my grandmother explained them to me.
records.zomi: Ka pi in hong gen mateng kammal lui te ka theisiam kei hi.

records.english: Our community choir sings traditional songs at Christmas.
records.zomi: I khuasung la sa pawl in Christmas-in ngeina la te a sa hi.

records.english: Could you possibly stay late tonight to help us finish the order?
records.zomi: Order i zawh nadingin tuzan nunung zaw-in om-in hong huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: In our company, new staff are paired with a buddy they can ask for help.
records.zomi: I company ah nasem thakte in huhna a ngen theih ding lawm khat tawh kizopsak uh hi.

records.english: Good managers make it easy for their staff to ask for help.
records.zomi: Manager hoih te in a nasemte in huhna a ngen baih nadingin a bawl uh hi.

records.english: The team leader asked for volunteers to help with the stocktake.
records.zomi: Team makaipa in van sim nadingin thalawp te a ngen hi.

records.english: Who should I talk to if I'm having trouble with my course?
records.zomi: Ka sinna ah haksatna ka neih leh kua tawh ka kihopih ding hiam?

records.english: Sorry to interrupt, but could you help me with the printer jam?
records.zomi: Maisak in, ahi zongin printer a kituap pen hong huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Not every problem at work needs a manager, because sometimes a colleague can help more quickly.
records.zomi: Nasepna-a haksatna khempeuh in manager a kisam kei hi, bang hang hiam cih leh nasem pih khat in a hun zaw-in a huh thei hi.

records.english: Rather than struggling alone, I asked two colleagues to divide the work with me.
records.zomi: Ka kia-in hanciam sangin nasem pih nih kei tawh nasep kikhen dingin ka ngen hi.

records.english: Would you be willing to read the first chapter of my thesis?
records.zomi: Ka thesis' tangthu khen masa pen na sim nuam ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, if you send it to me by Wednesday.
records.zomi: Nilai ni ma-in hong khak leh sim ding hi.

records.english: Could you help me prepare for the interview by asking me some practice questions?
records.zomi: Kisinna dotna khenkhat hong dot-in interview adingin ka kiginkholh nadingin hong huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Can you help me understand what the teacher wants in this task?
records.zomi: Hih nasep ah saya in bang a deih hiam cih ka theisiam nadingin hong huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: The nurse asked a colleague to help her move the patient.
records.zomi: Nurse in natpa a sawn nadingin nasem pih khat a ngen hi.

records.english: Your help with the spreadsheet saved me hours.
records.zomi: Spreadsheet ah na huhna in nai tampi hong hehpih hi.

records.english: Don't be embarrassed to ask for help in your first week.
records.zomi: Na kal masa sung-in huhna ngen na zum kei ding hi.

records.english: Could you show me how to submit the assignment online?
records.zomi: Online-in assignment bangci-in pia ding cih hong lak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Sure, it takes two minutes, and I'll walk you through it.
records.zomi: Thei hi, minit nih bek a la a, khat ciat kong lak ding hi.

records.english: Can somebody help the new receptionist with the phones?
records.zomi: Receptionist thak phone te-ah kuamah in a huh thei hiam?

records.english: Would you mind checking my calculations before I send them to the client?
records.zomi: Client kiangah ka khak ma-in ka kisimna na en sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: I asked the librarian to help me find articles for my research project.
records.zomi: Ka research project adingin article te zong dingin laibu inn kemtu ka ngen hi.

records.english: Our tutor holds office hours every Tuesday for students who need help.
records.zomi: I tutor in Pithai ni simin huhna a kisam sangnaupangte adingin office hun a nei hi.

records.english: I wish I had asked for help with my thesis much earlier.
records.zomi: Ka thesis adingin a hun zaw-in huhna ka ngen leh ka hoih ding hi.

records.english: My classmate helped me catch up after I'd been ill for two weeks.
records.zomi: Kal nih ka cina khit ciangin ka class lawm in a phawng ka man nadingin hong huh hi.

records.english: I asked my tutor for help with the essay structure.
records.zomi: Essay lamzia adingin ka tutor kiangah huhna ka ngen hi.

records.english: I needed help translating the instructions, so I asked a colleague who speaks Arabic.
records.zomi: Thuhilhnate let dingin huhna ka kisam a, Arabic pau thei nasem pih khat ka ngen hi.

records.english: My manager encouraged me to ask questions during my first month.
records.zomi: Ka kha masa sung-in dotnate dong dingin ka manager in hong lungkhauhsak hi.

records.english: Where can students get help with their university applications?
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte in a university ngetna adingin koi-ah huhna a ngah thei uh hiam?

records.english: When I asked for help with my timetable, the office found a solution in minutes.
records.zomi: Ka sinna hun lai adingin huhna ka ngen ciangin office in minit tawmno sung-in a bawlphatna a mu hi.

records.english: Can I ask you for help with my presentation slides?
records.zomi: Ka presentation slide te adingin huhna kong ngen thei ding hiam?

records.english: Happily, but let's look at them after the lunch break.
records.zomi: Lungdam takin, ahi zongin sun an tawlna khit ciangin i en ni.

records.english: I'd appreciate some help organising the conference next month.
records.zomi: Kha hong tung ding-a conference bawl nadingin huhna ka ngah leh ka lungdam ding hi.

records.english: When students are afraid of looking foolish, they often don't ask for the help they need.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte in mawl bang-a kilang a lau uh ciangin a kisap huhna a ngen kei zel uh hi.

records.english: The head teacher asked the parents for help painting the classrooms.
records.zomi: Sangpi saya in sangdan te sai nuh nadingin nu leh pate kiangah huhna a ngen hi.

records.english: If you're stuck, raise your hand and I'll come round.
records.zomi: Na tawp kha leh na khut dom inla, kong pai ding hi.

records.english: Our school has a study centre where older students help younger ones.
records.zomi: I sang in sangnaupang upa zawte in a neu zawte a huhna kisinna mun khat a nei hi.

records.english: Who can help me with the new accounting software?
records.zomi: Accounting software thak ah kua in hong huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Ask Thomas in finance, because he trained everyone last month.
records.zomi: Finance-a Thomas dong in, bang hang hiam cih leh kha nunung-in mi khempeuh a sinsak hi.

records.english: I emailed the IT department because I couldn't log in to the system.
records.zomi: System ah ka lut zo loh manin IT department kiangah email ka khak hi.

records.english: Students who ask for help early in the term usually do better in exams.
records.zomi: Term kipat ciangin huhna a ngen sangnaupangte sitna ah a hoih zaw zel uh hi.

records.english: Could you explain this formula again, please?
records.zomi: Hih formula hong gen kik thei ding hiam?

records.english: I'm not sure how to fill in this expense form, so could you help?
records.zomi: Hih sum zat form bangci-in dimsak ding cih ka thei kei ahih manin hong huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Could I borrow you for five minutes?
records.zomi: Minit nga sung nangmah ka zang thei ding hiam?

records.english: Can you spare a moment to look at this report?
records.zomi: Hih report en dingin hun tomno na nei hiam?

records.english: Help me carry these books to the staffroom, please.
records.zomi: Hih laibu te sayate tawlna dan ah hong puak sak in.

records.english: I asked my mentor for advice before applying for the promotion.
records.zomi: Nasep sang zaw ka ngen ma-in ka makaipa kiangah thuhilhna ka ngen hi.

records.english: Asking a colleague for help is quicker than searching the manual for an hour.
records.zomi: Nasem pih khat kiangah huhna ngen pen nai khat sung manual zon sangin a hun zaw hi.

records.english: Admitting that I didn't understand the task was difficult, but my teacher was very kind.
records.zomi: Nasep ka theisiam kei hi, ci-in pulak a haksa a, ahi zongin ka saya a hehpih mahmah hi.

records.english: Would it be possible to get an extension on the deadline?
records.zomi: Hun bei a sawt zaw thei ding hiam?

records.english: Is there a teacher who could help me after school?
records.zomi: Sang khit ciangin hong huh thei ding saya khat a om hiam?

records.english: Please let me know if you need help with the new system.
records.zomi: System thak ah huhna na kisam leh hong theisak in.

records.english: Could someone help me set up the projector before the lesson?
records.zomi: Sinna kipat ma-in projector koih nadingin kuamah in hong huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: When the machine broke down, I called the technician immediately instead of trying to fix it myself.
records.zomi: Seh a sia ciangin keimah in bawlphat sawm sangin technician ka sam pah hi.

records.english: Is there someone who can help me lift these boxes into the van?
records.zomi: Hih bawm te van mawtaw sungah domto dingin hong huh thei ding kuamah a om hiam?

records.english: Wait for Ali, because you shouldn't lift them on your own.
records.zomi: Ali ngak in, bang hang hiam cih leh na kia-in na domto kei ding hi.

records.english: Is anyone good at writing cover letters?
records.zomi: Cover letter gelh siam kuamah a om hiam?

records.english: Excuse me, could you help me find the library?
records.zomi: Maisak in, laibu inn zong dingin hong huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: My supervisor prefers questions to guesses, especially with safety equipment.
records.zomi: Ka makaipa in a tuamin bitna vanzat tawh kisai ngaihsun sangin dotna a deih zaw hi.

records.english: I asked a colleague to come with me to the difficult meeting with the client.
records.zomi: Client tawh kikhopna haksa ah kei tawh hong dingin nasem pih khat ka ngen hi.

records.english: The new apprentice was too shy to ask for help, so he made the same mistake twice.
records.zomi: Na kisin mi thak huhna ngen a zum luat manin khialhna kibang nihvei a bawl hi.

records.english: Asking for help in a new job shows that you care about getting things right.
records.zomi: Nasep thak khat ah huhna ngen in thu a dik taka bawl na deih hi, cih a lak hi.

records.english: The project is about 60% complete, so we should finish on time.
records.zomi: Project a za-a 60 bang a zo khin ahih manin hun-in i zo ding hi.

records.english: Our class raised 80% of the money for the trip by selling cakes.
records.zomi: I class in changkhuai zuak-in khualzinna sum za-a 80 a kaikhawm uh hi.

records.english: Half the students handed in their projects late, so the teacher extended the deadline.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte a kim in a project uh a phawng-in a pia uh ahih manin saya in hun bei a sawtsak hi.

records.english: When the price of fuel went up by 30%, the delivery company raised its charges.
records.zomi: Datsi man za-a 30 a khan ciangin van tunsakna company in a man a khangsak hi.

records.english: Our company gives every employee a 10% discount in its shops.
records.zomi: I company in a sumbuk te ah nasem khatciat za-a 10 man kiamna a pia hi.

records.english: Our bank charges 3% for every international transfer.
records.zomi: I bank in gamdang sum khakna khatciat-ah za-a 3 a la hi.

records.english: The cost of materials has risen by a fifth since last spring.
records.zomi: Nidang spring pan vanzat man nga-a khat a khang hi.

records.english: Having compared the two offers, I realised that a 15% discount was worth more than free delivery.
records.zomi: Ngetna nih ka kiteh khit ciangin za-a 15 man kiamna pen man om lo van tunsakna sangin a manpha zaw hi, cih ka thei hi.

records.english: Only a small fraction of the applicants were invited to an interview.
records.zomi: Ngente lak-ah a tawm khat bek interview ah kisam hi.

records.english: The examiner gave partial marks for answers that were half right.
records.zomi: Sitna entupa in a kim dik dawnna te adingin mark khenkhat a pia hi.

records.english: Did you include tax in the price?
records.zomi: Man sungah siah na kihel sak hiam?

records.english: What fraction of your working week do you spend in meetings?
records.zomi: Na kal sung nasep hun ah kikhopna ah bang fraction na zang hiam?

records.english: A quarter of our customers now pay by phone.
records.zomi: I customer te li-a khat in tu-in phone tawh sum a pia uh hi.

records.english: Can you give me the answer as a fraction in its simplest form?
records.zomi: Dawnna a baih pen fraction-in hong pia thei ding hiam?

records.english: Shall I put the results in a pie chart so that the fractions are easier to see?
records.zomi: Fraction te muh baih nadingin gah te pie chart sungah ka koih ding hiam?

records.english: How do I turn this fraction into a percentage?
records.zomi: Hih fraction percentage-in bangci-in ka khek ding hiam?

records.english: Divide the top number by the bottom one and multiply by 100.
records.zomi: A tung nambat a nuai nambat tawh khen inla, 100 tawh multiply in.

records.english: Our electrician measures cable in fractions of a metre.
records.zomi: I electrician in cable pen meter fraction-in a teh hi.

records.english: The builder added 10% to the materials to allow for waste.
records.zomi: Inn lampa in a mang ding adingin vanzat ah za-a 10 a beh hi.

records.english: The new machine cut our electricity use by almost half.
records.zomi: Seh thak in i meivak zat a kim dek a niamsak hi.

records.english: Our shop takes 5% off for students who show their cards.
records.zomi: I sumbuk in a card a lak sangnaupangte adingin za-a 5 a kiamsak hi.

records.english: The nurse gave the patient half the usual dose because of his age.
records.zomi: A kum hangin nurse in natpa damdawi zah a ngeina zah kim a pia hi.

records.english: The chef cut the recipe to a third because only ten guests were coming.
records.zomi: Khual sawm bek a hong ding ahih manin an huanpa in an huanzia thum-a khat-in a niamsak hi.

records.english: What percentage of the class passed the exam?
records.zomi: Class' za-a bangzah in sitna a zo hiam?

records.english: About 80%, which is better than last year.
records.zomi: Za-a 80 bang, nidang kum sangin a hoih zaw hi.

records.english: Two thirds of the class chose science for next year.
records.zomi: Class thum-a nih in kum hong tung ding adingin science a teel uh hi.

records.english: In the lab, we diluted the solution to one tenth of its original strength.
records.zomi: Lab ah solution pen a bul hatna sawm-a khat dong i niamsak uh hi.

records.english: If you answer 45 out of 50 questions correctly, you get 90%.
records.zomi: Dotna 50 lak-ah 45 dik takin na dawn leh za-a 90 na ngah hi.

records.english: What fraction of the team works from home?
records.zomi: Team' bang fraction in inn pan na a sem uh hiam?

records.english: About a third, mostly on Mondays and Fridays.
records.zomi: Thum-a khat bang, a tamzaw Pizing ni leh Laithai ni-in.

records.english: The waiter's tips make up nearly a third of his income.
records.zomi: An piakpa' letsong sum te a sum ngah thum-a khat dek a suak hi.

records.english: Please round each percentage to the nearest whole number.
records.zomi: Percentage khatciat a nai pen nambat bup-in kimkhai in.

records.english: A pass mark of 50% means you need half the points to pass.
records.zomi: Za-a 50 zawhna mark cih in zawh nadingin mark a kim na kisam hi, cihna ahi hi.

records.english: Profits rose by 12% after we changed suppliers.
records.zomi: Van zuakpa i khek khit ciangin mehna za-a 12 a khang hi.

records.english: Our department had spent 90% of its budget by October.
records.zomi: October kha-in i department in a budget za-a 90 a zang khin hi.

records.english: Which is larger, 0.6 or two thirds?
records.zomi: Bang a lian zaw hiam, 0.6 hiam, thum-a nih hiam?

records.english: Can you show the figures as percentages in the report?
records.zomi: Report sungah nambat te percentage-in na lak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Our school expects students to attend at least 90% of their lessons.
records.zomi: I sang in sangnaupangte in a sinna za-a 90 a tawm pen-in a kihel ding uh hi, ci-in a lamen hi.

records.english: The factory reduced its waste by a quarter in one year.
records.zomi: Factory in kum khat sung-in a eek li-a khat a niamsak hi.

records.english: If a quarter of the staff are on holiday, the rest of us will have to cover their work.
records.zomi: Nasemte li-a khat tawlngakni a om uh leh a dang kote in a nasep uh i sep sak kul ding hi.

records.english: Our sales team earns a commission of 2% on each sale.
records.zomi: I zuakna team in zuakna khatciat ah za-a 2 commission a ngah uh hi.

records.english: Understanding percentages helps employees read their payslips correctly.
records.zomi: Percentage theisiam in nasemte in a khasum lai dik takin a sim thei uh hi.

records.english: Write two fifths as a percentage.
records.zomi: Nga-a nih percentage-in gelh in.

records.english: How much is 15% off a $40 shirt?
records.zomi: $40 puansilh khat za-a 15 a kiam leh bangzah hiam?

records.english: Our teacher showed us that 33% is a little less than one third.
records.zomi: Za-a 33 pen thum-a khat sangin tawmno a tawm zaw hi, ci-in i saya in hong lak hi.

records.english: Did sales really drop by 20% last month?
records.zomi: Kha nunung-in zuakna za-a 20 a kiam taktak hiam?

records.english: Yes, but only because one big customer delayed an order.
records.zomi: Kiam hi, ahi zongin customer lian khat in order khat a sawn manin bek ahi hi.

records.english: The survey showed that one in five employees wanted more training.
records.zomi: Nasem nga lak-ah khat in training tam zaw a deih uh hi, ci-in survey in a lak hi.

records.english: The engineer calculated that the bridge could carry a load 25% heavier than expected.
records.zomi: Lei in a lamen sangin za-a 25 a gik zaw pua thei hi, ci-in engineer in a sim hi.

records.english: Our tutor asked us to explain why one half is bigger than three sevenths.
records.zomi: Bang hangin nih-a khat pen sagih-a thum sangin a lian zaw hiam cih gen dingin i tutor in hong ngen hi.

records.english: Most of my marks came from the coursework, which counted for 60%.
records.zomi: Ka mark tamzaw pen za-a 60 a hih coursework pan a hong hi.

records.english: Three quarters of the staff have finished the safety training.
records.zomi: Nasemte li-a thum in bitna training a zo khin uh hi.

records.english: Only one fifth of the students finished the last question.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte nga-a khat bek in a tawp pen dotna a zo uh hi.

records.english: The test was worth 40% of our final grade.
records.zomi: Sitna pen i grade tawp pen za-a 40 a manpha hi.

records.english: The manager was pleased that only 2% of the orders were returned.
records.zomi: Order te za-a 2 bek a kiap kik manin manager a lungdam hi.

records.english: When you use percentages in a presentation, always say what they are a percentage of.
records.zomi: Presentation ah percentage na zat ciangin bang pan percentage ahi hiam cih gen den in.

records.english: How much is a 5% pay rise on a salary of $30,000?
records.zomi: Khasum $30,000 tungah za-a 5 khasum khanna bangzah hiam?

records.english: It's $1,500 a year, before tax.
records.zomi: Siah ma-in kum khat ah $1,500 ahi hi.

records.english: Who can tell me what 1% of 500 is?
records.zomi: 500 a za-a 1 bangzah hiam cih kua in hong gen thei ding hiam?

records.english: Three out of ten workers said they cycle to work.
records.zomi: Nasem sawm lak-ah thum in siiksakol tawh nasepna ah a pai uh hi, a ci uh hi.

records.english: Not a single thing went wrong on the day of my parents' anniversary party.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa' kiteen kum phawkna poai ni-in bangmah a khial kei hi.

records.english: The day Dad came home after three years of working abroad, we all waited at the bus station.
records.zomi: Gamdang ah kum thum na a sep khit-a Pa inn a ciah ni-in i khempeuh bus khawlna mun ah i ngak uh hi.

records.english: When he finally stepped off the bus, my little sister didn't recognise him and hid behind Mum.
records.zomi: A tawp-in bus pan a kum ciangin ka nau numei in amah a thei kei a, Nu nunglam ah a kisel hi.

records.english: By the evening, she was sitting on his lap and refusing to let him go.
records.zomi: Nitak ciangin a pheng tungah a tu a, a khah nuam nawn kei hi.

records.english: Auntie Lun's wedding was the first day I saw my grandfather cry.
records.zomi: Ni Lun' mopawi pen ka pu a kap ka muh masak pen ni ahi hi.

records.english: When my parents paid off the house, we had a party in the garden.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa' inn leiba a bei ciangin huan ah poai i bawl uh hi.

records.english: Shall we make an album of photos from that day?
records.zomi: Tua ni-a photo te album khat i bawl ding hiam?

records.english: Our first family trip to the mountains ended with a picnic above the clouds.
records.zomi: I innkuan mual khualzinna masa pen meii tung-ah an nekna tawh a tawp hi.

records.english: How did you feel when you first saw your father's village?
records.zomi: Na pa' khua na muh masak pen-in bangci-in na kisa hiam?

records.english: Strangely at home, as if I'd been there before.
records.zomi: Lamdang takin inn bang-in, tua-ah ka om ngei bangin.

records.english: We took Grandma to see the house where she was born, and she cried with joy.
records.zomi: Pi a suahna inn en dingin i paipih uh a, a lungdam mahmah ahih manin a kap hi.

records.english: That summer day by the river is the clearest memory I have of my mother.
records.zomi: Lui gei-a tua khal ni pen ka nu tawh kisai ka phawkna kician pen ahi hi.

records.english: What's the best day you've ever spent with Grandpa?
records.zomi: Pu tawh na zat ni hoih pen bang hiam?

records.english: The day he taught me to ride his old motorbike in the field behind the house.
records.zomi: Inn nunglam-a lou ah a motorbike lui tawl zia hong sinsak ni.

records.english: That was the day I learned that my grandfather could sing.
records.zomi: Tua ni pen ka pu la a sa thei hi, cih ka theih ni ahi hi.

records.english: Remember the day we all went fishing and Dad slipped into the river?
records.zomi: I khempeuh nga man dingin i pai a, Pa lui sungah a kizuat ni na phawk hiam?

records.english: It was the day I met my half-sister for the first time, and we talked until midnight.
records.zomi: Pa kibang lo ka u numei ka muh masak pen ni ahi a, zanlai dong i kihopih uh hi.

records.english: The day we scattered Grandpa's ashes on the hill was sad but strangely peaceful.
records.zomi: Pu' vuk mual tungah i theh ni a lungkham huai a, ahi zongin lamdang takin a nuam hi.

records.english: The day the whole family climbed the mountain together, Grandma reached the top before anyone else.
records.zomi: Innkuan bup mual tung i kah khawm ni-in mi khempeuh ma-in Pi a tung masa hi.

records.english: On the afternoon our family planted the mango tree, Grandpa made each of us dig a little.
records.zomi: I innkuan in haigah kung i suan nitak lam-in Pu in eite khatciat tawmno tou dingin hong sawl hi.

records.english: I'll never forget the morning Grandma read her first book aloud to us.
records.zomi: Pi in a laibu masa pen aw tawh hong sim zingsang ka mangngilh ngei kei ding hi.

records.english: The day my brother proposed, he was so nervous that he dropped the ring.
records.zomi: Ka u pasal in kiteen ngetna a bawl ni-in a lau mahmah ahih manin khutzung a khiat hi.

records.english: It was an ordinary Sunday until my cousin arrived with news of her baby.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam a naungek thuthak tawh a tun mateng Nipini ngeina ahi hi.

records.english: We celebrated the day Grandpa came home from hospital with his favourite soup.
records.zomi: Damdawi inn pan Pu inn a ciah ni a it pen an tui tawh i lungdampih uh hi.

records.english: Do you remember the day we brought the puppy home?
records.zomi: Ui neu inn i paipih ni na phawk hiam?

records.english: Yes, she cried all night, and so did you.
records.zomi: Phawk hi, zan bup a kap a, nang zong na kap hi.

records.english: Which day of last year was the best for you?
records.zomi: Nidang kum-a bang ni na adingin a hoih pen hiam?

records.english: Our family calls it the day of the broken boat, and we tell the story every year.
records.zomi: I innkuan in long kisia ni ci-in a sam a, kum simin tangthu i gen uh hi.

records.english: Days spent with the whole family together are rare, so we try to remember every detail.
records.zomi: Innkuan bup khawm-a i zat ni te a tawm ahih manin thu neuno khempeuh phawk dingin i sawm uh hi.

records.english: On the day I left home, Mum packed my bag with enough food for a week.
records.zomi: Inn ka paisan ni-in Nu in kal khat adingin a tham an ka ip sungah a thun sak hi.

records.english: Who took the photos on the day of the family picnic?
records.zomi: Innkuan an nekna ni-in kua in photo a lak hiam?

records.english: The day my grandmother turned a hundred, she danced with every one of her great-grandchildren.
records.zomi: Ka pi kum za a cin ni-in a tu' tate khempeuh tawh a lam hi.

records.english: What did you do on the day the exams finished?
records.zomi: Sitna a zawh ni-in bang na bawl hiam?

records.english: The day after the storm, the neighbours came to help us mend the roof, and it felt like a festival.
records.zomi: Huihpi khit zingciang-in inn vengte i inn tung bawlphat dingin a hong uh a, pawi bang a kisa hi.

records.english: On my tenth birthday, Dad woke me before dawn to watch the sunrise from the hill.
records.zomi: Ka kum sawm suahni-in Pa in mual tung pan ni suah en dingin khuavak ma-in hong kaithou hi.

records.english: Our son's first day at nursery was harder for me than for him.
records.zomi: I tapa' naupang sang ni masa pen amah sangin kei adingin a haksa zaw hi.

records.english: Finding our lost cat was one of the happiest moments of my childhood.
records.zomi: I zawhngeu mangsa mu kik pen ka naupan lai-a hun nuam pen te lak-ah khat ahi hi.

records.english: My daughter wrote about our trip to the waterfall for her school project.
records.zomi: I tanu in a sang project adingin tui kiat mun-a i khualzinna a gelh hi.

records.english: Why did we drive around the village so many times on the day we got our first car?
records.zomi: I mawtaw masa pen i ngah ni-in bang hangin khua kim tampi vei mawtaw tawh i kawi hiam?

records.english: Even the dog seemed to understand that it was a special day.
records.zomi: Ui zong ni tuam ahi hi, cih a thei bang hi.

records.english: When we visited my mother's old school, she showed us the desk where she used to sit.
records.zomi: Ka nu' sang lui i veh ciangin a tutna taupi hong lak hi.

records.english: We spent the whole day at the beach, and nobody looked at a phone.
records.zomi: Tuipi gei ah ni bup i om uh a, kuamah in phone a en kei uh hi.

records.english: Can you describe the day you became a grandmother?
records.zomi: Pi na suah ni na gen thei hiam?

records.english: Do you remember how excited the children were by their first snowfall here?
records.zomi: Hih mun-a vuuk masa pen a kiak ciangin naupangte bangzah a lungdam uh hiam cih na phawk hiam?

records.english: Our son talked about our day at the zoo for weeks afterwards.
records.zomi: I tapa in zoo-a i ni tawh kisai kal tampi sung a gen hi.

records.english: What made that holiday so memorable?
records.zomi: Bang in tua tawlngakni a phawk huai sak hiam?

records.english: It was the first time all four generations of our family were together.
records.zomi: I innkuan' khangthu li khempeuh a kikhop masak pen hun ahi hi.

records.english: Grandpa's last day at the farm was quiet, but he walked every field once more.
records.zomi: Lou-a Pu' ni nunung pen a dai a, ahi zongin lou khempeuh a kal kik hi.

records.english: Why do you always smile when you talk about that day?
records.zomi: Bang hangin tua ni na gen ciangin na nui den hiam?

records.english: The day my parents renewed their wedding vows, my father forgot his words.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa a kiteen kiciamna a thak kik ni-in ka pa in a kammal te a mangngilh hi.

records.english: Our son's wedding day began with rain and ended with the brightest sunset I've ever seen.
records.zomi: I tapa' mopawi ni guah tawh a kipan a, ka muh ngeih lak-a ni tum vak pen tawh a tawp hi.

records.english: I do want to remember how quiet the house was on Grandpa's last morning with us.
records.zomi: Kote tawh Pu' zingsang nunung pen-in inn bangzah a dai hiam cih phawk ka deih taktak hi.

records.english: That day, for the first time, my father told me he was proud of me.
records.zomi: Tua ni-in a masa pen-in ka pa in kei tungah a kipak hi, hong ci hi.

records.english: Who remembers the day the whole family got stuck in the lift?
records.zomi: Innkuan bup lift sungah i kitawm ni kua in a phawk hiam?

records.english: When my grandparents flew on a plane for the first time, they held hands the whole way.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh pi te a masa pen-in vanleng a tuan ciangin a lampi bup-ah a khut a kilen uh hi.

records.english: My little brother still remembers the day the circus came to our town.
records.zomi: I khuapi ah circus a hong ni ka nau pasal in a phawk lai hi.

records.english: The day my brother came back from the army, Mum cooked all his favourite dishes.
records.zomi: Ka u pasal galkap pan a ciah kik ni-in Nu in a it an khempeuh a huan hi.

records.english: The first time my son saw the sea, he ran straight into the waves with his shoes on.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in tuipi a muh masak pen-in a khedap tawh tuiphual lam-ah a tai pah hi.

records.english: Why was your mother's citizenship ceremony so special?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na nu' gam mi hihna kikhop a tuam mahmah hiam?

records.english: She had waited many years for it, and the whole family came to watch.
records.zomi: Kum tampi a ngak a, innkuan bup en dingin a hong uh hi.

records.english: The connection in my parents' village is so weak that we often switch to voice only.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa' khua-a connection a hat lo mahmah ahih manin aw bek ah i khek zel uh hi.

records.english: My father-in-law insists on wearing a shirt and tie for every family video call.

records.english: Our family reunion was held online because nobody could afford to travel.
records.zomi: Kuamah in khualzin man a neih loh manin i innkuan kikhopna online-in a kibawl hi.

records.english: Thank you for setting up the call so that Grandpa could join the party.
records.zomi: Pu in poai ah a kihel theih nadingin call na bawl manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: My parents learned to use video calls during the long lockdown, and now they call us every day.
records.zomi: Kikhakna sawt lai-in ka nu leh ka pa in video call zat a sin uh a, tu-in ni simin hong sam uh hi.

records.english: The dog barks every time he hears my mother's voice coming from the laptop.
records.zomi: Laptop pan ka nu' aw a zak simin i ui a hau hi.

records.english: Shall we sing happy birthday to Grandma over video?
records.zomi: Video tungtawnin Pi adingin suahni la i sa ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, but let's wait until everyone has joined the call.
records.zomi: Sa ni, ahi zongin mi khempeuh call ah a kihel mateng i ngak ni.

records.english: We watched my cousin open her exam results live on a video call.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam in a sitna gah a hon video call tungah i en uh hi.

records.english: Video calls can never fully replace a hug, but they help.
records.zomi: Video call in kipawmna a laih bup thei ngei kei a, ahi zongin a huh hi.

records.english: Our son accidentally ended the call by pressing the red button.
records.zomi: I tapa in a theih loh-in mehthol san a nek-in call a khak hi.

records.english: What time should we call your parents on Sunday?
records.zomi: Nipini-in na nu leh pa bang hun-in i sam ding hiam?

records.english: After church, which is late evening for them.
records.zomi: Pawlpi khit ciangin, amaute adingin nitak nunung ahi hi.

records.english: Grandma keeps asking us to speak up, even with the volume at maximum.
records.zomi: Aw a sang pen-a a om hangin Pi in kiko zaw dingin hong ngen den hi.

records.english: Who wants to say hello to Grandma before she goes?
records.zomi: Pi a pai ma-in kua in chibai a ci nuam hiam?

records.english: Having moved so far away, I rely on video calls to feel part of family life.
records.zomi: Gamla mahmah ah ka tai khit ciangin innkuan nuntakna sung-a kihel ka kisak nadingin video call tungah ka kinga hi.

records.english: On my birthday, five relatives in three countries joined the same video call.
records.zomi: Ka suahni-in gam thum-a om sanggam nga in video call kibang ah a kihel uh hi.

records.english: Did Dad get the link for tonight's family call?
records.zomi: Tuzan innkuan call adingin Pa in link a ngah hiam?

records.english: When the call started, Grandma was holding the phone upside down.
records.zomi: Call a kipat ciangin Pi in phone a kilehheh-in a len hi.

records.english: Let's call Uncle before the children go to bed.
records.zomi: Naupangte a lup ma-un Pa neu i sam ni.

records.english: Why does Grandpa always hold the phone so close to his face?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pu in phone a mai kiangah a nai mahmah-in a len den hiam?

records.english: He says he wants to see us properly, not just the tops of our heads.
records.zomi: I lu tung bek hi lo-in kote dik takin a muh nop hi, a ci hi.

records.zomi: Ka tanau in a ha kiak camera kiang nai-in a lak hi.

records.english: Because of the time difference, someone in our family is always yawning during the call.
records.zomi: Hun kibat lohna hangin call lai-in i innkuan sung-ah mi khat a hamkhawng den hi.

records.english: Can you hear the baby laughing?
records.zomi: Naungek a nui na za hiam?

records.english: Grandma waves at the screen long after the call has ended.
records.zomi: Call a tawp khit sawt zong Pi in screen tungah khut a vai lai hi.

records.english: Don't walk around with the phone, because it makes Grandpa feel dizzy.
records.zomi: Phone tawh vak kei in, bang hang hiam cih leh Pu a lu a mang hi.

records.english: Mum cooks along with Grandma on video so that she can learn her recipes.
records.zomi: Pi' an huanzia te a sin theih nadingin Nu in video tungah Pi tawh khawm-in an a huan hi.

records.english: Can you show Auntie the new kitchen on the video?
records.zomi: Video tungah Ni kiangah an huanna thak na lak thei ding hiam?

records.english: My mother-in-law can hear us perfectly but can never find the camera button.
records.zomi: Ka sungnu in kote hoih takin a za a, ahi zongin camera mehthol a mu ngei kei hi.

records.english: Turn the light on, love, or we'll only see your silhouette.
records.zomi: Ka it, meivak hal in, tua hi lo leh na lim mial bek i mu ding uh hi.

records.english: Shall we leave the call open while we eat, so that it feels like dinner together?
records.zomi: Nitak an khawm-a ne bang-in a kisak nadingin an i nek lai-in call i hong ding hiam?

records.english: Our cousins abroad joined Grandpa's funeral by video, and it meant a lot to them.
