records.zomi: Kidawm taka ngaihsun sangnaupangte in online-a thugen te a um baih kei uh hi.

records.english: Logic lessons taught me to separate facts from opinions.
records.zomi: Ngaihsutna kalsuanzia sinna in thutak leh ngaihsutna kikhen dingin hong sinsak hi.

records.english: Is this a cause or just a coincidence?
records.zomi: Hih pen a hang ahi hiam, a kituak bek hiam?

records.english: The detective game in our class taught us to question every clue.
records.zomi: I class-a thuzong kimawlna in ciamtehna khempeuh dong dingin hong sinsak hi.

records.english: Our supervisor rejected the idea because it solved one problem and created two more.
records.zomi: Haksatna khat a bawlphat a, nih a piangsak ahih manin i makaipa in tua ngaihsutna a nial hi.

records.english: What's wrong with this argument?
records.zomi: Hih ngaihsutna ah bang a khial hiam?

records.english: It assumes that because sales rose after the advert, the advert caused the rise.
records.zomi: Advert khit ciangin zuakna a khan manin advert in a khangsak hi, ci-in a ngaihsun hi.

records.english: Our maths teacher sets a reasoning question every Friday.
records.zomi: I maths saya in Laithai ni simin ngaihsutna dotna khat a pia hi.

records.english: The accountant found the error by checking which figures didn't match the receipts.
records.zomi: Accountant in receipt te tawh a kituak lo nambat te en-in khialhna a mu hi.

records.english: How did you work out which supplier made the error?
records.zomi: Bang van zuakpa in khialhna a bawl hiam cih bangci-in na thei hiam?

records.english: Only one of them delivered on both days when the parts were faulty.
records.zomi: Kikhen te a sia ni nih khempeuh ah amaute lak-ah khat bek in van a tunsak hi.

records.english: Our debate coach taught us to attack the reasoning, not the person.
records.zomi: I kikupna sinsakpa in mi hi lo-in ngaihsutzia do dingin hong sinsak hi.

records.english: Who can find the mistake in my reasoning on the board?
records.zomi: Board tung-a ka ngaihsutzia sung-a khialhna kua in a mu thei hiam?

records.english: The engineers ruled out the simplest causes first.
records.zomi: Engineer te in a baih pen hang te a masa-in a phiat uh hi.

records.english: Puzzles like this one help pupils learn to think in an orderly way.
records.zomi: Hih bang ngaihsutna dotna te in sangnaupangte a kalsuan kilawm-in ngaihsun dingin a huh hi.

records.english: Our teacher gave us a logic puzzle to solve before the lesson started.
records.zomi: Sinna a kipat ma-in i saya in ngaihsutna dotna khat hong pia hi.

records.english: The new rule sounds sensible, but it creates a problem for part-time staff.
records.zomi: Thukhun thak a kilawm bang a, ahi zongin hun khenkhat nasemte adingin haksatna a piangsak hi.

records.english: Dad showed us where his childhood home stood before the road was widened.
records.zomi: Lampi a kizai sak ma-in a naupan lai inn a omna mun Pa in hong lak hi.

records.english: Our family's shop was the first in town to sell bicycles.
records.zomi: I innkuan sumbuk pen khuapi ah siiksakol zuak masa pen ahi hi.

records.english: I do want my children to know who built the house they're growing up in.
records.zomi: Ka tate in a khanna inn kua in a lam hiam cih a theih ka deih taktak hi.

records.english: Mum still uses the old names for streets that were renamed years ago.
records.zomi: Kum tampi ma-a min kikhek lampi te adingin Nu in min lui te a zang lai hi.

records.english: My parents were married in the first wedding held in the new church.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa pawlpi thak-a mopawi masa pen ah a kiteen uh hi.

records.english: My great-uncle was one of the men who built the bridge across the river.
records.zomi: Ka pu' u pasal ahi zongin nau pasal pen lui tung-a lei a lam mite lak-a khat ahi hi.

records.english: Grandpa, what was our street like when you were young?
records.zomi: Pu, na khangno lai-in i lampi bang ci hiam?

records.english: There were only four houses, and cows grazed where the school is now.
records.zomi: Inn li bek a om a, tu-a sang omna mun ah bawng te an a ne uh hi.

records.english: My aunt collects old photos of the village and labels them with the names of everyone in them.
records.zomi: Ka ni in khua' photo lui te a kaikhawm a, a sung-a mi khempeuh' min a gelh hi.

records.english: My uncle found an old coin while digging in our garden and gave it to the museum.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in i huan a tou lai-in sum-ek lui khat a mu a, museum ah a pia hi.

records.english: Grandma's stories about the market make me wish I could have seen it.
records.zomi: Pi' sumbuk tangthu te in ka muh theih leh hoih ding hi ka sak sak hi.

records.english: Not until I read my grandfather's diary did I understand how hard life in the village had been.
records.zomi: Ka pu' ciamtehna laibu ka sim mateng khua-a nuntakna bangzah a haksa hiam cih ka theisiam kei hi.

records.english: In our house, the history of the town is told through the history of our family.
records.zomi: I inn ah khuapi tangthu pen i innkuan tangthu tungtawnin kigen hi.

records.english: My parents met at the harvest supper that the village held every autumn.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa khua in teh kiakna hun simin a bawl lou lak nitak an ah a kimu uh hi.

records.english: When my mother was a girl, the only shop in our village was run by her uncle.
records.zomi: Ka nu a nungak neu lai-in i khua-a sumbuk khat bek pen a pa neu in a kem hi.

records.english: People came from three villages to buy salt, cloth and paraffin there.
records.zomi: Khua thum pan mite cii, puan leh mei-ek tui lei dingin tua-ah a hong uh hi.

records.english: Today the building is a house, but the old shop sign still hangs above the door.
records.zomi: Tu-in tua inn pen teen inn ahi a, ahi zongin sumbuk ciamtehna lui kongkhak tungah a kikhai lai hi.

records.english: Our family still owns the plough that my great-grandfather used on the hill fields.
records.zomi: Ka pu' pa in mual lou te ah a zat leilet i innkuan in a nei lai hi.

records.english: Shall we ask Grandma to label the people in these old photos?
records.zomi: Hih photo lui te sung-a mite' min gelh dingin Pi i ngen ding hiam?

records.english: Who in our family remembers the old railway?
records.zomi: I innkuan sung-ah kua in meileng lampi lui a phawk hiam?

records.english: Do you know why our neighbourhood is called the Upper Field?
records.zomi: Bang hangin i mun pen Upper Field kici hiam cih na thei hiam?

records.english: Children, ask your grandparents what the town looked like when they were your age.
records.zomi: Naupangte, na pu leh pi te na kum bang a hih lai-un khuapi bang ci hiam cih dong un.

records.english: The town museum displays the sewing machine my grandmother used in her shop.
records.zomi: Khuapi museum in ka pi in a sumbuk-a a zat puan khui seh a lak hi.

records.english: Our children made a family history book for a school project about the town.
records.zomi: I tate in khuapi tawh kisai sang project adingin innkuan tangthu laibu khat a bawl uh hi.

records.english: Was Grandma really the first woman in our village to drive a tractor?
records.zomi: Pi pen i khua-a tractor a tawl numei masa pen ahi taktak hiam?

records.english: Grandma remembers carrying water from the river before the village had taps.
records.zomi: Khua in tuikhau a neih ma-in lui pan tui a puak hun Pi in a phawk hi.

records.english: Grandpa helped dig the first water pipes in our village.
records.zomi: I khua-a tuikhau masa pen tou dingin Pu in a huh hi.

records.english: The oldest photo in our album shows the village before the first road was built.
records.zomi: I album sung-a photo lui pen in lampi masa pen a kilam ma-a khua a lak hi.

records.english: Whose idea was it to start the family history album?
records.zomi: Innkuan tangthu album kipatsak pen kua' ngaihsutna ahi hiam?

records.english: Our family recorded Grandpa's memories of the village before he died.
records.zomi: Pu a sih ma-in i innkuan in khua tawh kisai a phawkna te a khum uh hi.

records.english: My cousins and I mapped where each of our relatives lived in the old village.
records.zomi: Ka sanggamte leh kei in khua lui ah i sanggam khatciat a tenna mun i ciamteh uh hi.

records.english: Why is the old well covered with a stone?
records.zomi: Bang hangin tuikhuk lui suang tawh a kikhuh hiam?

records.english: A child fell in once, long ago, so the elders sealed it.
records.zomi: Nidang sawt-in naupang khat a kiak khatvei ahih manin upate in a khuh uh hi.

records.english: Can you tell us how the village celebrated when the road was finished?
records.zomi: Lampi a zawh ciangin khua in bangci-in a lungdampih hiam cih hong gen thei ding hiam?

records.english: When the old cinema was knocked down, my parents kept a seat from it as a souvenir.
records.zomi: Cinema lui a kisiat ciangin ka nu leh ka pa in phawkna dingin a tutna khat a kem uh hi.

records.english: Dad can name every family that has lived on our street since 1960.
records.zomi: 1960 kum pan i lampi-a teng innkuan khempeuh' min Pa in a gen thei hi.

records.english: My grandmother remembers when the road to the town was only a footpath.
records.zomi: Khuapi paina lampi pen kal lampi bek a hih lai Pi in a phawk hi.

records.english: Did you know that Grandpa keeps a box of old newspapers about the town's history?
records.zomi: Pu in khuapi tangthu tawh kisai thuthak laipi lui bawm khat a kem hi, cih na thei hiam?

records.english: Our street party this year celebrated a hundred years since the first houses were built.
records.zomi: Tu kum-a i lampi poai in inn masa te a kilam pan kum za khat a cin a lungdampih hi.

records.english: Learning our community's history made me proud of the ordinary people in my family.
records.zomi: I khuasung tangthu sin in ka innkuan sung-a mi ngeina te tungah hong kipaksak hi.

records.english: The house we live in was once the village post office.
records.zomi: I tenna inn pen nidang-in khua post office ahi hi.

records.english: The tree in our garden was planted by my grandparents on their wedding day.
records.zomi: I huan sung-a sing kung pen ka pu leh pi te in a kiteen ni-in a suan uh ahi hi.

records.english: Thank you for sharing your memories of the village, Grandpa.
records.zomi: Pu, khua tawh kisai na phawkna te hong hawm manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: Our family has lived on this street for four generations.
records.zomi: I innkuan khangthu li sung hih lampi ah a teng hi.

records.english: Our family helped plant the trees that line the main road today.
records.zomi: Tu-a lampi lian gei-a sing kung te suan dingin i innkuan a huh hi.

records.english: Every Christmas, my grandfather tells us how the village celebrated before there was electricity.
records.zomi: Christmas simin meivak a om ma-in khua in bangci-in a lungdampih hiam cih ka pu in hong gen hi.

records.english: Dad's old school report is now part of the town archive.
records.zomi: Pa' sang report lui tu-in khuapi tangthu kemna ah a kihel hi.

records.english: Grandpa says that the whole village helped rebuild our house after the storm.
records.zomi: Huihpi khit ciangin khua bup in i inn a lam kik nadingin a huh uh hi, Pu in a ci hi.

records.english: Who started the market in our village?
records.zomi: I khua-a sumbuk kua in a kipatsak hiam?

records.english: My great-grandmother and three other women, according to the family story.
records.zomi: Innkuan tangthu bangin ka pu' nu leh numei dang thum in.

records.english: The children were amazed to learn that their school had once had only one room.
records.zomi: A sang uh nidang-in inndan khat bek a nei hi, cih a theih ciangin naupangte lamdang a sa mahmah uh hi.

records.english: Mum still has the photo of the day the village school opened.
records.zomi: Khua sang a kihon ni-a photo Nu in a nei lai hi.

records.english: Is our great-grandparents' wooden chest really the oldest object in the house?
records.zomi: I pu' pu leh pi' pi te' sing sanduk pen inn sung-a van lui pen taktak ahi hiam?

records.english: When the mine closed, my grandparents moved to the town and opened a tea shop.
records.zomi: Lei kua tou nasepna a khak ciangin ka pu leh pi te khuapi ah a tai uh a, niangtui sumbuk khat a hong uh hi.

records.english: Is it true that our school used to be a hospital?
records.zomi: I sang pen nidang-in damdawi inn ahi hi, cih a dik hiam?

records.english: How do you know so much about the town's history?
records.zomi: Khuapi tangthu bangci-in tampi na thei hiam?

records.english: My grandmother told me stories every night, and I've never forgotten them.
records.zomi: Ka pi in zan simin tangthu hong gen a, ka mangngilh ngei kei hi.

records.english: Every summer, my family visits the graves of the people who founded our village.
records.zomi: Khal simin ka innkuan in i khua a kipatsak mite' han te a veh hi.

records.english: Did our family help build the church?
records.zomi: I innkuan in pawlpi lam dingin a huh hiam?

records.english: Yes, your great-grandfather carried stones for it every Sunday for two years.
records.zomi: Huh hi, na pu' pa in kum nih sung Nipini simin suang a puak hi.

records.english: My wife reads every question twice before she writes anything down.
records.zomi: Ka zi in bangmah a gelh ma-in dotna khempeuh nihvei a sim hi.

records.english: Our daughter wrote her name in capital letters for the first time on her school form.
records.zomi: I tanu in a sang form ah a masa pen-in a min laimal lian tawh a gelh hi.

records.english: A single wrong date on the form delayed my sister's pension by two months.
records.zomi: Form tung-a ni khial khat in ka u numei' pension kha nih a phawngsak hi.

records.english: Our family doctor had to sign part of Grandma's disability form.
records.zomi: I innkuan siavuan in Pi' pumpi kicing lo huhna form' khenkhat ah min a gelh kul hi.

records.english: Government forms are less frightening when the whole family sits down to do them together.
records.zomi: Innkuan bup khawm-in a tut uh ciangin kumpi form te a lauhuai tawm zaw hi.

records.english: Filling in forms for my grandparents means I know their whole life history.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh pi te adingin form dimsak in a nuntakna tangthu bup ka thei hi.

records.english: The form asked for my mother's maiden name, which I had to ask her for.
records.zomi: Form in ka nu' kiteen ma-a min tawp a ngen a, amah kiangah ka dong kul hi.

records.english: Our family spent a whole evening filling in the census form.
records.zomi: I innkuan in census form dimsak dingin nitak bup a zang hi.

records.english: Auntie Lun keeps a list of every form she has sent and when she sent it.
records.zomi: Ni Lun in a khak form khempeuh leh a khak hun ciamtehna khat a kem hi.

records.english: My daughter helped her grandmother apply for a bus pass online.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in a pi online-in bus pass a ngen nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Helping my parents with government forms taught me more than any school lesson.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa kumpi form te tawh huh in sang sinna khatpeuh sangin hong sinsak tam zaw hi.

records.english: Do you have to fill in the form again every year?
records.zomi: Kum simin form na dimsak kik kul hiam?

records.english: We filled in the travel form at the airport while the children slept on the chairs.
records.zomi: Naupangte tutphah tungah a ihmut lai-un vanlengtual ah khualzinna form i dimsak uh hi.

records.english: Who's going to fill in Grandpa's pension form?
records.zomi: Pu' pension form kua in a dimsak ding hiam?

records.english: I will, but he has to sign it himself.
records.zomi: Kei in, ahi zongin amah mahin min a gelh kul hi.

records.english: I photographed every page of the form before we posted it.
records.zomi: Post-in i khak ma-un form' lai-ek khempeuh photo ka lak hi.

records.english: Do the dates on these forms look right to you?
records.zomi: Hih form tunga ni te a dik bang na sa hiam?

records.english: My brother filled in the wrong form and had to wait another month.
records.zomi: Ka u pasal in form khial a dimsak a, kha khat beh a ngak kul hi.

records.english: Our son filled in his first official form when he applied for a student card.
records.zomi: Student card a ngen ciangin i tapa in a kumpi form masa pen a dimsak hi.

records.english: My parents still argue about who forgot to send the voter registration form.
records.zomi: Vote piak ciamtehna form khak kua in a mangngilh hiam cih ka nu leh ka pa a kinial lai uh hi.

records.english: My uncle's application was returned because he had written outside the boxes.
records.zomi: Bawm pualam ah a gelh manin ka pa neu' ngetna a kiap kik hi.

records.english: Please don't fold the form, because the machine won't read it.
records.zomi: Seh in a sim theih loh ding ahih manin form khep kei in.

records.english: The council sent us the same form twice, so we called to check.
records.zomi: Council in form kibang nihvei hong khak ahih manin en dingin i sam uh hi.

records.english: Did you remember to put a stamp on the envelope?
records.zomi: Laikhak ip tungah stamp koih na phawk hiam?

records.english: Without our neighbour's help, my parents would never have finished the citizenship application.
records.zomi: I inn veng' huhna om lo hileh ka nu leh ka pa in gam mi hihna ngetna a zo ngei lo ding uh hi.

records.english: Is this the form for the child benefit or for the housing allowance?
records.zomi: Hih pen naupang huhna sum form ahi hiam, inn huhna sum form ahi hiam?

records.english: Thank you for explaining the form to my grandmother so patiently.
records.zomi: Ka pi kiangah thuakzawh takin form na gen manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: Shall we do the forms together after dinner?
records.zomi: Nitak an khit ciangin form te khawm-in i bawl ding hiam?

records.english: Where should I write the baby's name if we haven't chosen it yet?
records.zomi: Naungek' min i teel nai loh leh koi-ah ka gelh ding hiam?

records.english: The form for free school meals was only two pages, which surprised us.
records.zomi: Sang an man om lo form lai-ek nih bek ahih manin lamdang i sa uh hi.

records.english: Have you finished the school admission form yet?
records.zomi: Sang lutna form na zo khin hiam?

records.english: Almost, but I need our son's vaccination record.
records.zomi: Zo dek hi, ahi zongin i tapa' kidawnna damdawi ciamtehna ka kisam hi.

records.english: Let's write our questions in the margin and ask at the office tomorrow.
records.zomi: I dotna te a gei ah gelh unla, zingciang office ah dong ni.

records.english: Dad always fills in forms in pencil first, then copies them in pen.
records.zomi: Pa in form te a masa-in pencil tawh a dimsak a, tua khit ciangin pen tawh a gelh kik hi.

records.english: The form for the children's travel documents asked for both our places of birth.
records.zomi: Naupangte' khualzinna lai form in kote nih' suahna mun a ngen hi.

records.english: Which of you knows our passport numbers by heart?
records.zomi: Note lak-ah kua in i passport nambat te a lungsim-in a thei hiam?

records.english: Do we need both parents' signatures on the passport form for the baby?
records.zomi: Naungek' passport form ah nu leh pa nih' min gelhna i kisam hiam?

records.english: Yes, and a photo of the baby with her eyes open.
records.zomi: Kisam hi, a mit a hong naungek photo khat zong.

records.english: My cousin had to fill in a form in three languages when she moved abroad.
records.zomi: Gamdang ah a tai ciangin ka sanggam in pau thum tawh form khat a dimsak kul hi.

records.english: My brother is so afraid of making mistakes on forms that he puts them off for weeks.
records.zomi: Ka u pasal form tungah khialh a lau mahmah ahih manin kal tampi a sawnsawn hi.

records.english: Mum couldn't read the form, so a neighbour translated it for her.
records.zomi: Nu in form a sim thei kei ahih manin inn veng khat in a let sak hi.

records.english: The tax form was so complicated that my parents asked an accountant to help.
records.zomi: Siah form a buaihuai mahmah ahih manin ka nu leh ka pa in accountant khat a huh dingin a ngen uh hi.

records.english: We had to fill in a form to register our new car.
records.zomi: I mawtaw thak ciamteh nadingin form khat i dimsak kul hi.

records.english: The new online form saves our answers, so we can finish it later.
records.zomi: Online form thak in i dawnnate a kem ahih manin a nungin i zo thei hi.

records.english: The children love helping us tick the boxes on easy forms.
records.zomi: Form baih te-a bawm te ciamteh dingin naupangte in hong huh a it uh hi.

records.english: The application for the death certificate was the hardest form I've ever filled in.
records.zomi: Sihna lai-ciam ngetna pen ka dimsak ngeih form lak-ah a haksa pen ahi hi.

records.english: Our family's change of address took five different forms to complete.
records.zomi: I innkuan inn mun kikhekna zawh nadingin form tuam nga a kisam hi.

records.english: Dad writes the reference number on the back of every form he sends.
records.zomi: Pa in a khak form khempeuh nunglam ah reference nambat a gelh hi.

records.english: Which documents do we need to attach to this form?
records.zomi: Hih form tawh bang lai te i kizopsak kul hiam?

records.english: Our neighbour brings her forms to us because our son is good with computers.
records.zomi: I tapa in computer a siam manin i inn veng in a form te kote kiangah a paipih hi.

records.english: Grandpa's form was rejected because the photo was too old.
records.zomi: Photo a lui luat manin Pu' form a kinial hi.

records.english: Grandpa's old forms show how his handwriting changed over fifty years.
records.zomi: Pu' form lui te in kum sawmnga sung a laigelhzia bangzah a kikhel hiam cih a lak hi.

records.english: The marriage registration form asked for two witnesses, so we chose our best friends.
records.zomi: Kiteenna ciamtehna form in teci nih a ngen ahih manin i lawm hoih pen te i teel uh hi.

records.english: Mum, which box do I tick for my nationality?
records.zomi: Nu, ka gam mi hihna adingin bang bawm ka ciamteh ding hiam?

records.english: The second one, and then write the country underneath.
records.zomi: A nihna, tua khit ciangin a nuai-ah gam min gelh in.

records.english: When my husband died, I had to fill in more forms than I could count.
records.zomi: Ka pasal a sih ciangin ka sim zawh loh form tampi ka dimsak kul hi.

records.english: Why is the census form asking how many rooms we have?
records.zomi: Bang hangin census form in inndan bangzah i nei hiam ci-in a dong hiam?

records.english: The government uses the answers to plan housing, as far as I know.
records.zomi: Ka theih tawh kituakin kumpi in inn ciamteh nadingin dawnnate a zang hi.

records.english: Grandma signs her name slowly and carefully on every form.
records.zomi: Pi in form khempeuh tungah zawi takin kidawm takin a min a gelh hi.

records.english: Filling in the adoption forms took us almost a year.
records.zomi: Ta kiteh form te dimsak in kum khat dek kote' hun a la hi.

records.english: Did you remember the children's bus passes?
records.zomi: Naupangte' bus pass te na phawk hiam?

records.english: Yes, they're in the side pocket of my bag.
records.zomi: Phawk hi, ka ip gei lam ip neu sungah a om hi.

records.english: The children love sitting upstairs at the front of the double-decker.
records.zomi: Naupangte in double-decker tunglam maiang lam ah tut a it uh hi.

records.english: We missed the ferry by two minutes and had to wait three hours for the next one.
records.zomi: Minit nih tawh tembaw i pal uh a, a zom ding nai thum i ngak kul uh hi.

records.english: When the train broke down, the passengers shared snacks with our hungry children.
records.zomi: Meileng a sia ciangin khualte in i gilkial tate tawh an neuno a kihawm uh hi.

records.english: Let's take the train to the zoo instead of driving.
records.zomi: Mawtaw tawl sangin zoo ah meileng tawh i pai ni.

records.english: Is there a family ticket for the ferry?
records.zomi: Tembaw adingin innkuan lakkhak a om hiam?

records.english: Which bus goes to Grandma's house?
records.zomi: Pi' inn ah bang bus in a pai hiam?

records.english: The number 12, and it stops right outside her gate.
records.zomi: Nambat 12, a kongpi mai ngei-ah a khawl hi.

records.english: My grandmother still keeps her very first bus ticket in a drawer.
records.zomi: Ka pi in a bus lakkhak masa pen dawh sungah a kem lai hi.

records.english: Our family's Sunday outing is a ride to the end of the tram line and back.
records.zomi: I innkuan Nipini vakna pen tram lampi tawp dong tuang-a ciah kik ahi hi.

records.english: Can you meet Grandma off the coach on Thursday?
records.zomi: Laizing ni-in coach pan Pi na dawn thei ding hiam?

records.english: Since my mother stopped driving, the bus has given her back her freedom.
records.zomi: Ka nu mawtaw a tawl nawn loh khit pan bus in a zalenna a pia kik hi.

records.english: Without the village bus, my grandparents would be completely cut off.
records.zomi: Khua bus om lo hileh ka pu leh pi te a kikhen vek ding uh hi.

records.english: Public transport is one reason we chose to live in this part of town.
records.zomi: Mipi mawtaw pen khuapi khen hih mun ah teng dingin i teelna hang khat ahi hi.

records.english: We play counting games on the long bus ride to my aunt's village.
records.zomi: Ka ni' khua paina bus sau ah sim kimawlna i kimawl uh hi.

records.english: Grandma calls the bus her second living room, because she knows everyone on it.
records.zomi: Pi in a sung-a mi khempeuh a theih manin bus pen a tutna inndan nihna ci-in a sam hi.

records.english: The bus company's app tells me exactly when the children's bus will arrive.
records.zomi: Bus company' app in naupangte' bus bang hun-in a tung ding hiam cih kician takin hong gen hi.

records.english: The new tram line means my parents can visit us without changing buses.
records.zomi: Tram lampi thak hangin ka nu leh ka pa bus khek lo-in kote hong veh thei uh hi.

records.english: Does Mum get a free bus pass now that she's retired?
records.zomi: Nu nasep a tawp khit ciangin man om lo bus pass a ngah hiam?

records.english: When the last bus was cancelled, my cousin drove forty minutes to pick us up.
records.zomi: Bus nunung pen a kiphiat ciangin ka sanggam in kote la dingin minit sawmli mawtaw a tawl hi.

records.english: When Grandpa got lost on the underground, a kind passenger helped him find his line.
records.zomi: Pu leinuai meileng ah a mang ciangin hehpih khualpa khat in a lampi a muh nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Travelling by bus with my grandmother taught me patience and a lot of local gossip.
records.zomi: Ka pi tawh bus tawh khualzin in thuakzawhna leh a mun thugen tampi hong sinsak hi.

records.english: Shall we take the train to the coast again this summer?
records.zomi: Tu khal-in tuipi gei ah meileng tawh i pai kik ding hiam?

records.english: My daughter phones me when she gets off the bus after school.
records.zomi: Sang khit ciangin bus pan a kum ciangin ka tanu in hong sam hi.

records.english: When the bus driver saw my father's walking stick, he waited until Dad had sat down.
records.zomi: Bus tawlpa in ka pa' ciang a muh ciangin Pa a tut mateng a ngak hi.

records.english: Shall we buy weekly tickets for the whole family?
records.zomi: Innkuan bup adingin kal khat lakkhak i lei ding hiam?

records.english: Our daughter's first journey alone on the train was a big step for the whole family.
records.zomi: I tanu' meileng tunga a kia-a khualzinna masa pen innkuan bup adingin khekhap lian khat ahi hi.

records.english: Our son is obsessed with trains and knows every station on the line.
records.zomi: I tapa in meileng a it mahmah a, lampi-a khawlna mun khempeuh a thei hi.

records.english: Hold my hand when we get on the escalator.
records.zomi: Escalator tungah i kah ciangin ka khut len in.

records.english: Mum gets nervous on crowded trains, so we travel after the rush hour.
records.zomi: Mi a tam meileng tungah Nu a lau ahih manin mi tamna hun khit ciangin i pai uh hi.

records.english: The cost of train tickets for a family of five can be more than the cost of petrol.
records.zomi: Mi nga innkuan adingin meileng lakkhak man in datsi man sangin a tam thei hi.

records.english: The bus strike meant that I had to walk the children to school for a week.
records.zomi: Bus nasemte' na sem nawn lohna hangin kal khat sung naupangte sang ah ka kal pih kul hi.

records.english: We sold our car because the buses in our town are so reliable.
records.zomi: I khuapi-a bus te a muanhuai mahmah ahih manin i mawtaw i zuak uh hi.

records.english: My parents taught us to give up our seats to older passengers.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in khual upa te adingin i tutna nusia dingin hong sinsak uh hi.

records.english: Moving closer to the station has made family visits much easier.
records.zomi: Khawlna mun kiang zaw-ah i tai khit ciangin innkuan vehna a baih zaw mahmah hi.

records.english: Our grandparents travel free on local buses, which helps their small pension.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh pi te in a mun bus ah man om lo-in a tuang uh a, tua in a pension neuno a huh hi.

records.english: My brother uses a wheelchair, so we always check that the station has a lift.
records.zomi: Ka u pasal in wheelchair a zang ahih manin khawlna mun in lift a nei hiam cih i en den uh hi.

records.english: My wife and I met on the morning train to the city.
records.zomi: Ka zi leh kei khuapi paina zingsang meileng tungah i kimu uh hi.

records.english: Our son learned to read the bus timetable when he was 8.
records.zomi: I tapa kum 8 a cin ciangin bus hun lai sim a sin hi.

records.english: The children wave at the driver every morning when the school bus arrives.
records.zomi: Zingsang simin sang bus a tun ciangin naupangte in mawtaw tawlpa khut a vai uh hi.

records.english: Taking the bus with a baby and a pushchair is still hard work.
records.zomi: Naungek leh naungek tolhna tawh bus tuang pen nasep haksa ahi lai hi.

records.english: Our son left his school bag on the bus, but the driver handed it in.
records.zomi: I tapa in a sang ip bus tungah a nusia a, ahi zongin mawtaw tawlpa in a ap kik hi.

records.english: The driver let my little sister press the bell for our stop.
records.zomi: I khawlna mun adingin mawtaw tawlpa in ka nau numei bell a nek dingin a phal hi.

records.english: How did your parents get around before they had a car?
records.zomi: Mawtaw a neih ma-un na nu leh pa bangci-in a vak uh hiam?

records.english: On the old village bus, which came twice a day if it came at all.
records.zomi: Khua bus lui tungah, a hong leh ni khat ah nihvei a hong hi.

records.english: Children, feet off the seats, please.
records.zomi: Naupangte, tutna tung pan khe la khia un.

records.english: Our teenager uses the night bus to get home from his job at the cinema.
records.zomi: I tangval in cinema-a a nasep pan inn a ciah nadingin zan bus a zang hi.

records.english: Thank you for giving my mother your seat.
records.zomi: Ka nu na tutna na piak manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: Dad drove a city bus for thirty years and still waves at every driver he sees.
records.zomi: Pa in kum sawmthum khuapi bus a tawl a, a muh mawtaw tawlpa khempeuh khut a vai lai hi.

records.english: Grandpa takes the tram to the market every Saturday.
records.zomi: Pu in Kiginni simin sumbuk ah tram tawh a pai hi.

records.english: Why do you always sit at the front of the bus, Grandpa?
records.zomi: Pu, bang hangin bus maiang lam ah na tu den hiam?

records.english: So that I can see the stops and ask the driver if I'm lost.
records.zomi: Khawlna mun te ka muh a, ka mang leh mawtaw tawlpa ka dot theih nadingin.

records.english: Do you think the children are old enough to take the bus to the cinema alone?
records.zomi: Naupangte a kia-un cinema ah bus tawh a pai thei dingin a kum a cing hi na ci hiam?

records.english: Can the children travel on the train by themselves?
records.zomi: Naupangte amau bek-in meileng tungah a khualzin thei uh hiam?

records.english: Only the older two, and only in the daytime.
records.zomi: A upa zaw nih bek, sun lai bek-in.

records.english: Can you help Grandma with her bags when she gets off the train?
records.zomi: Pi meileng pan a kum ciangin a ip te-ah na huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Our children know which stop to get off at by the big yellow church.
records.zomi: I tate in pawlpi gial lian kiang ah kum ding cih a thei uh hi.

records.english: Teaching children to use public transport gives them independence.
records.zomi: Naupangte mipi mawtaw zat sinsak in amau mah-a kipan theihna a pia hi.

records.english: My niece was so excited about her first train journey that she didn't sleep the night before.
records.zomi: Ka tunu a meileng khualzinna masa pen ah a lungdam mahmah ahih manin a ma zan-in a ihmu zo kei hi.

records.english: My aunt grows herbs that our family uses for cooking and for simple home remedies.
records.zomi: Ka ni in i innkuan in an huan nadingin leh damdawi baih adingin a zat an-lim-nah te a suan hi.

records.english: Shall we share some of our vegetables with the neighbours again this year?
records.zomi: Tu kum-in i anteh te inn vengte tawh i kihawm kik ding hiam?

records.english: We pick the beans early in the morning, while it's still cool.
records.zomi: A vot lai-in zingsang tung-in be te i lo uh hi.

records.english: Who taught you how to read the soil?
records.zomi: Lei sim zia kua in hong sinsak hiam?

records.english: My grandfather, by making me smell it and feel it in my hands.
records.zomi: Ka pu in, a gim nam sak-in, ka khut-in tawng sak-in.

records.english: According to my grandfather, families in his time moved their fields every few years to let the forest grow back.
records.zomi: Ka pu' gen bangin a hun-a innkuante in gammang a khan kik nadingin kum tawmno simin a lou uh a khek uh hi.

records.english: We had the old terrace walls repaired before the rainy season.
records.zomi: Guahzu hun ma-in lou kaihkawi bang lui te i bawlphat uh hi.

records.english: Dad made us pick up every stone in the new field.
records.zomi: Pa in lou thak sung-a suang khempeuh hong lo sak hi.

records.english: Can you show me how to plant the seeds in a straight line?
records.zomi: Chi te a kigual dik-in bangci-in suan ding cih hong lak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Could you help me carry the seed bags up the hill?
records.zomi: Chi ip te mual tung ah puak dingin hong huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: If the harvest is good, we hold a small thanksgiving at church.
records.zomi: Lou lakna a hoih leh pawlpi ah lungdamna kikhop neuno khat i nei uh hi.

records.english: Grandpa mixes ash into the soil before he plants the vegetables.
records.zomi: Anteh a suan ma-in Pu in lei sungah vut a hel hi.

records.english: In our village, people help each other at harvest time.
records.zomi: I khua ah lou lak hun-in mite a kihuh tuah uh hi.

records.english: I do want to learn how my grandparents farmed without machines.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh pi te seh om lo-in bangci-in lou a bawl uh hiam cih sin ka deih taktak hi.

records.english: My little brother scares the birds away from the rice with a tin can.
records.zomi: Ka nau pasal in buh pan vasa te sik-ek tawh a lausak hi.

records.english: Have you kept the best seeds from this harvest for next year?
records.zomi: Kum hong tung ding adingin hih lou lakna pan chi hoih pen te na kem hiam?

records.english: Grandpa plants trees at the edge of the field to stop the soil from washing away.
records.zomi: Lei a luang mang loh nadingin Pu in lou gei ah sing kung a suan hi.

records.english: Why are you leaving that field empty this year?
records.zomi: Bang hangin tu kum-in tua lou na nusia hiam?

records.english: My father says the land needs a rest, or the harvest will be poor.
records.zomi: Gam in tawlna a kisam a, tua hi lo leh lou lakna a hoih lo ding hi, ci-in ka pa in a gen hi.

records.english: We store the rice in large baskets to keep it dry.
records.zomi: A ciin loh nadingin buh pen bawm lian te sungah i kem uh hi.

records.english: You can plant the pumpkins near the fence, where there's more space.
records.zomi: Huang kiangah mai na suan thei hi, tua-ah mun a tam zaw hi.

records.english: Our grandparents' farming knowledge was passed down by talking and working together, not by books.
records.zomi: I pu leh pi te' lou nasep theihna pen laibu hi lo-in kihopihna leh khawm-a nasep tawh a kipia hi.

records.english: Do you still use the old ways of farming?
records.zomi: Lou nasep lam lui te na zang lai hiam?

records.english: Some of them, alongside a few new ideas from the agricultural office.
records.zomi: Khenkhat zang lai hi, lou nasep office pan ngaihsutna thak tawmno tawh.

records.english: Our family plants beans between the maize so that they can climb the stalks.
records.zomi: I innkuan in a kung uh tungah a kah theih nadingin vaimim kikal ah be a suan hi.

records.english: We let the chickens into the garden after the harvest to eat the insects.
records.zomi: Lou lak khit ciangin lungzu te a nek nadingin ak te huan ah i khah uh hi.

records.english: Children, please stay on the path so that you don't step on the young plants.
records.zomi: Naupangte, suan thakte na suh loh nadingin lampi tung bek ah om un.

records.english: In our village, the elders decide together when the harvest should begin.
records.zomi: I khua ah upate in bang ciangin lou lakna kipan ding cih khawm-in a khensat uh hi.

records.english: Dad keeps a notebook of when he planted each crop and how well it grew.
records.zomi: Pa in a suan chi khatciat bang ciangin a suan a, bangzah a hoih-in a khang hiam cih ciamtehna laibu khat a kem hi.

records.english: Some young people in our village are learning to farm again from their grandparents.
records.zomi: I khua-a khangno khenkhat a pu leh pi te pan lou nasep a sin kik uh hi.

records.english: Who will look after the animals while we're working in the field?
records.zomi: Lou ah na i sep lai-un ganhing te kua in a kem ding hiam?

records.english: When does your family plant the rice?
records.zomi: Na innkuan in bang ciangin buh a suan uh hiam?

records.english: When the first heavy rains come, usually in early summer.
records.zomi: Guah hat masa a zuk ciangin, khal kipat ciangin a tamzaw.

records.english: The first rice of the year is always cooked for the whole family.
records.zomi: Kum khat-a buh masa pen innkuan bup adingin kihuan den hi.

records.english: Do you know which month is best for planting potatoes?
records.zomi: Alu suan nadingin bang kha a hoih pen hiam cih na thei hiam?

records.english: My grandparents grew rice, maize and beans on the hillside.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh pi te in mual ah buh, vaimim leh be a suan uh hi.

records.english: Did you water the seedlings this morning?
records.zomi: Tu zingsang-in suan thakte tui na buak hiam?

records.english: Is it true that ash from the fire makes the soil better?
records.zomi: Mei pan vut in lei a hoihsak hi, cih a dik hiam?

records.english: The old farmers in our village can tell the weather from the wind.
records.zomi: I khua-a lou bawl upate in huih pan khuahun a thei thei uh hi.

records.english: Mum taught me to plant onions on a cloudy day.
records.zomi: Meii a om ni-in lothaang suan dingin Nu in hong sinsak hi.

records.english: My grandmother can tell whether a seed is good by dropping it in water.
records.zomi: Ka pi in chi khat tui sungah a khiat-in a hoih hiam cih a thei thei hi.

records.english: Dad checks the sky every morning before he goes to the field.
records.zomi: Pa in lou ah a pai ma-in zingsang simin vantung a en hi.

records.english: Every spring, my whole family went up to the hill field to clear the weeds.
records.zomi: Spring simin ka innkuan bup lopa te phiat dingin mual lou ah a kah uh hi.

records.english: Grandpa walked ahead with a long knife, and we children gathered the cut grass behind him.
records.zomi: Pu in namsau tawh a maiah a pai a, kote naupangte in a nunglam ah a kisat lopa i kaikhawm uh hi.

records.english: By evening, we were tired and dirty, but the field was ready for planting.
records.zomi: Nitak ciangin i gim uh a, i niin uh hi, ahi zongin lou suan dingin a kiging khin hi.

records.english: Grandpa taught me never to plant the same crop in the same place two years in a row.
records.zomi: Kum nih kizom-in mun kibang ah suan chi kibang suan ngei lo dingin Pu in hong sinsak hi.

records.english: Watching my grandparents work the land taught me to respect food.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh pi te lou a bawl a ka muh in an zahtak dingin hong sinsak hi.

records.english: Knowing when to plant and when to wait is the most important skill on a farm, my grandfather says.
records.zomi: Bang ciangin suan ding a bang ciangin ngak ding cih theih pen lou nasep-a siamna thupi pen ahi hi, ci-in ka pu in a gen hi.

records.english: Grandpa says that a farmer must listen to the land.
records.zomi: Lou bawlpa in gam a ngai ding hi, Pu in a ci hi.

records.english: My uncle uses a simple wooden tool to make holes for the seeds.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in chi suanna kua bawl nadingin sing vanzat baih khat a zang hi.

records.english: Grandma knows which plants keep insects away from the vegetables.
records.zomi: Pi in bang kung te in anteh pan lungzu te a hawlkhia hiam cih a thei hi.

records.english: Please bring the baskets down to the field after lunch.
records.zomi: Sun an khit ciangin bawm te lou ah hong paipih in.

records.english: Mum never wastes anything from the harvest, and even the stalks feed the animals.
records.zomi: Nu in lou lakna pan bangmah a paai ngei kei a, a kung te zong ganhing te' an a suak hi.

records.english: My cousin studies agriculture at college so that she can help our village farm better.
records.zomi: I khua in lou hoih zaw-in a bawl nadingin a huh theih nadingin ka sanggam in college ah lou nasep a sin hi.

records.english: When the maize was harvested, the whole family sat together to remove the husks.
records.zomi: Vaimim a kilak ciangin innkuan bup in a hawng phel dingin a kikhawm uh hi.

records.english: Why does Grandma always dry the chillies on the roof in autumn?
records.zomi: Bang hangin teh kiakna hun-in Pi in malcha inn tung-ah a sak den hiam?

records.english: Our neighbours lend us their buffalo to plough the low field.
records.zomi: I inn vengte in lou niam lei khoh nadingin a bawngtal hong leibatsak uh hi.

records.english: When the rains are late, the whole village worries about the harvest.
records.zomi: Guah a phawng ciangin khua bup in lou lakna a lungkham uh hi.

records.english: How do you know when the maize is ready?
records.zomi: Vaimim a min hiam cih bangci-in na thei hiam?

records.english: The silk turns brown and the kernels feel firm.
records.zomi: A sam a sanngo a, a tang te a khauh hi.

records.english: Did the manager say when the new rota would start?
records.zomi: Nasep hun ciamtehna thak bang ciangin a kipan ding hiam cih manager in a gen hiam?

records.english: What did the customer say when you offered the refund?
records.zomi: Sum ap kik ding na gen ciangin customer in bang a ci hiam?

records.english: Following up on a colleague's answer shows that you value their experience.
records.zomi: Nasem pih khat' dawnna dong zawh in a theihna na zahtak hi, cih a lak hi.

records.english: When my student said she didn't like maths, I asked which part she found hardest.
records.zomi: Ka sangnaupang in maths a deih kei hi a cih ciangin bang a haksa sak pen hiam ci-in ka dong hi.

records.english: I followed up with the candidate to ask about a gap in her CV.
records.zomi: A CV sung-a hun awng khat tawh kisai dong dingin ngetnu ka sam kik hi.

records.english: Sorry, could you say more about why the budget was cut?
records.zomi: Maisak in, bang hangin budget a kiam hiam cih na gen beh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Follow-up questions in class give quieter students a second chance to speak.
records.zomi: Class-a dong zawh dotna te in a dai sangnaupangte gen nading hun nihna a pia hi.

records.english: What did the inspector write in the report?
records.zomi: Entupa in report sungah bang a gelh hiam?

records.english: When our team leader asks how we feel about a plan, she always waits for a real answer.
records.zomi: I team makaipa in ciamtehna khat tawh kisai bangci-in i kisa uh hiam ci-in a dot ciangin dawnna taktak a ngak den hi.

records.english: You said the exam was easy, so why did you look so worried afterwards?
records.zomi: Sitna a baih hi na ci a, bang hangin a khit ciangin na lungkham mahmah bang hiam?

records.english: Who else did you speak to about the complaint?
records.zomi: Phunna tawh kisai kua dang tawh na kihopih hiam?

records.english: Have you heard back from the university yet?
records.zomi: University pan dawnna na ngah khin hiam?

records.english: Asking how a new employee's first week went can make them feel welcome.
records.zomi: Nasem thak khat' kal masa bangci-in a kalsuan hiam cih dong in a kisang bang-in a kisasak thei hi.

records.english: Rather than accepting my first answer, the examiner asked me to give an example.
records.zomi: Ka dawnna masa sang lo-in sitna entupa in entehna khat gen dingin hong ngen hi.

records.english: I asked the apprentice why he had chosen that tool, and his answer surprised me.
records.zomi: Bang hangin tua vanzat a teel hiam ci-in na kisin mi ka dong a, a dawnna in hong lamdangsak hi.

records.english: You told me the customer was angry, but was it about the price or the delay?
records.zomi: Customer a heh hi hong ci a, man hang hiam, phawngna hang hiam?

records.english: A good teacher follows a correct answer by asking how the student knows it is correct.
records.zomi: Saya hoih khat in dawnna dik khat a zawh ciangin sangnaupang in a dik hi, bangci-in a thei hiam ci-in a dong hi.

records.english: What's the next step after the trial period?
records.zomi: Sitna hun khit ciangin a zom kalsuan bang hiam?

records.english: You said you'd applied for promotion, so when will you hear?
records.zomi: Nasep sang zaw na ngen hi na ci a, bang ciangin dawnna na ngah ding hiam?

records.english: When I asked the nurse what the results meant, she explained them in detail.
records.zomi: Gah te bang cihna hiam ci-in nurse ka dot ciangin kician takin a gen hi.

records.english: You mentioned some problems with the new software, so which ones are they?
records.zomi: Software thak tawh haksatna khenkhat na gen a, bang te ahi hiam?

records.english: It crashes when two people edit the same file.
records.zomi: Mi nih in file kibang a khek ciangin a khawl hi.

records.english: Was the problem fixed the first time, or did they have to come back?
records.zomi: Haksatna a masa pen-in a kibawlphat hiam, a hong kik kul uh hiam?

records.english: When you say the interview went well, what did they actually ask you?
records.zomi: Interview a hoih hi na cih ciangin bang hong dong taktak uh hiam?

records.english: Mostly about my experience with customers and why I want to move.
records.zomi: A tamzaw customer tawh ka theihna leh bang hangin ka tai nop hiam cih.

records.english: Did you ever find out why the order was cancelled?
records.zomi: Bang hangin order a kiphiat hiam cih na thei khin hiam?

records.zomi: Thei hi, customer in van zuakpa man neu zaw khat a mu hi.

records.english: And what did the teacher say when you handed it in late?
records.zomi: Tua ahih leh a phawng-in na piak ciangin saya in bang a ci hiam?

records.english: She took ten marks off but said the work was good.
records.zomi: Mark sawm a phiat a, ahi zongin nasep a hoih hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Was the problem hard to fix in the end?
records.zomi: A tawp-in haksatna bawlphat a haksa hiam?

records.english: Could you tell me more about the results you mentioned?
records.zomi: Na gen gah te tawh kisai hong gen beh thei ding hiam?

records.english: You said you'd talked to the supplier, so what did they say?
records.zomi: Van zuakpa tawh na kihopih hi na ci a, bang a ci uh hiam?

records.english: My manager remembered my answer from the last review and asked how things had changed.
records.zomi: Ka manager in nidang enna-a ka dawnna a phawk a, bangci-in a kikhel hiam ci-in a dong hi.

records.english: Did anyone ask the cleaners what they thought of the new rules?
records.zomi: Thukhun thakte tawh kisai siangsakna nasemte kuamah in a dong hiam?

records.english: Did the head teacher explain why the trip was cancelled?

records.english: The forecaster on the radio warned drivers about fog on the motorway.

records.english: In geography, we learned why some countries have a rainy season.

records.english: Weather affects many jobs, from fishing to building to selling ice cream.

records.english: Our lecturer explained why coastal cities are worried about rising sea levels.
records.zomi: Bang hangin tuipi gei-a khuapi te tuipi a sanna tawh kisai a lungkham uh hiam cih i sinsakpa in a gen hi.

records.english: Outdoor workers must drink plenty of water during a heatwave.

records.english: Wind farms produce more electricity on stormy days.

records.english: Insurance companies study climate data before they set the price of storm cover.

records.english: Our class compared the average temperatures of three cities on different continents.
records.zomi: I class in gam tuamtuam-a khuapi thum' lum-vot average a kiteh uh hi.

records.english: Do the fishermen check the forecast before they leave the harbour?
records.zomi: Nga mantute in tuipi kongpi a paisan ma-un khuahun ngaihsutna a en uh hiam?

records.english: The ferry was delayed by high winds, so the workers arrived late.
records.zomi: Huih hat in tembaw a phawngsak ahih manin nasemte a phawng-in a tung uh hi.

records.english: Ski resorts depend on reliable snow, so warmer winters are a serious problem for them.
records.zomi: Ski mun te vuuk muanhuai tungah a kinga ahih manin phalbi lum zaw te amaute adingin haksatna lian ahi hi.

records.english: The heat made the railway lines expand, so the trains had to slow down.

records.english: The climate scientist explained how ocean currents affect the weather on land.

records.english: Our office closes when the government issues a red weather warning.

records.english: The airline cancelled several flights because of the thunderstorms.
records.zomi: Khuaphia leh huihpi hangin vanleng company in vanleng khualzinna tampi a phiat hi.

records.english: Hurricane warnings give people time to leave the coast before the storm arrives.

records.english: Can you find out the forecast for the day of the school trip?

records.english: The road crews put salt on the roads when ice is forecast.

records.english: Auntie Lun applied for citizenship after living here for twelve years.

records.english: My brother's university application needed a letter from his headteacher.

records.english: Our family's application for a hardship grant was approved within days.

records.english: Have you sent the application for the summer camp yet?
records.zomi: Khal camp adingin ngetna na khak khin hiam?

records.english: We waited anxiously for the letter about our son's school place.
records.zomi: I tapa' sang mun tawh kisai laikhak lungkham takin i ngak uh hi.

records.english: My sister applied for a grant to start her own bakery.

records.english: Families with low incomes in our town can apply for help with school trips.

records.english: Shall we apply for the family railcard before the holiday?

records.zomi: I tapa' min kikhekna ngetna in nu leh pa nih' min gelhna a kisam hi.
