records.english: Scientists use satellites to measure how fast the ice at the poles is melting.
records.zomi: Science siamte in leitung tawp lam-a tuikhal bangzah hun-in a tui hiam cih teh nadingin satellite te a zang uh hi.

records.english: What does a geologist look for in a rock sample?
records.zomi: Geologist khat in suang enton khat sungah bang a zong hiam?

records.english: Minerals, layers and fossils that show how and when the rock formed.
records.zomi: Suang bangci-in le bang ciangin a piang hiam cih a lak mineral, a tuang leh fossil te.

records.english: What do you call a scientist who studies the stars?
records.zomi: Aksi te a sin science siampa bang na ci hiam?

records.english: The radio telescope listens for signals from distant galaxies.
records.zomi: Radio telescope in gamla mahmah-a aksi pawl lian te pan ciamtehna a ngai hi.

records.english: The geology students spent a week mapping the rock layers in the valley.
records.zomi: Geology sangnaupangte in kal khat sung guam sung-a suang tuang te a ciamteh uh hi.

records.english: The quarry workers found a fossil fish in a block of limestone.
records.zomi: Suang tou nasemte in limestone suang tang khat sungah nga fossil khat a mu uh hi.

records.english: Our class watched a live video of a rocket launch during the lesson.
records.zomi: I class in sinna lai-in rocket khahna video khat a om lai-in a en uh hi.

records.english: Which rocks are formed from cooled lava?
records.zomi: Bang suang te mei-mual tui a vot pan a piang hiam?

records.english: Airlines plan long flights along curved routes because the Earth is round.
records.zomi: Leitung a bem ahih manin vanleng company te in khualzinna sau te lampi kawi tungah a ciamteh uh hi.

records.english: Draw the moon's phases in your notebook for the next two weeks.
records.zomi: Kal nih hong tung ding sung-a kha' pianzia te na ciamtehna laibu ah lai in.

records.english: The navigator checked the position of the ship using the sun at noon.
records.zomi: Lampi zonpa in sun-a ni zang-in long' omna mun a en hi.

records.english: The space agency is looking for engineers who can design lighter rockets.
records.zomi: Space agency in rocket zang zaw a ciamteh thei engineer te a zong hi.

records.english: Can you explain why we always see the same side of the moon?
records.zomi: Bang hangin kha' lam kibang i mu den hiam cih na gen thei ding hiam?

records.english: Weather satellites take photos of the Earth every few minutes.
records.zomi: Khuahun satellite te in minit tawmno simin leitung photo a lak uh hi.

records.english: Mining engineers study the rock carefully before they dig a tunnel.
records.zomi: Lei kua tou engineer te in kua a tou ma-un suang kidawm takin a sin uh hi.

records.english: Building a model of the solar system to scale showed us how empty space really is.
records.zomi: A zah tawh kilem ni leh aksi kalsuanna lim khat i bawl in vantung bangzah a awng hiam cih hong lak hi.

records.english: Why do astronauts have to exercise every day in space?
records.zomi: Bang hangin astronaut te in vantung ah ni simin pumpi kisinna a bawl kul uh hiam?

records.english: Because their muscles and bones become weaker without gravity.
records.zomi: Bang hang hiam cih leh gravity om lo-in a sa te leh a guh te a hat lo suak hi.

records.english: How long does it take the Earth to turn once?
records.zomi: Leitung khatvei a kiheina bangzah sawt hiam?

records.english: Our class collected rocks from the beach and sorted them by type.
records.zomi: I class in tuipi gei pan suang te a kaikhawm uh a, a chi zui-in a khen uh hi.

records.english: Farmers once planted crops by the phases of the moon, and some still do.
records.zomi: Nidang-in lou bawlte in kha pianzia zui-in a suan uh a, khenkhat in tu-in zong a bawl lai uh hi.

records.english: The physics teacher used a lamp and a globe to show why we have time zones.
records.zomi: Physics saya in bang hangin time zone i nei hiam cih lak nadingin meivak leh leitung bem khat a zang hi.

records.english: How do astronauts sleep on the space station?
records.zomi: Space station tungah astronaut te bangci-in a ihmu uh hiam?

records.english: In sleeping bags tied to the wall, so that they don't float around.
records.zomi: Bang tawh kikhih lupna ip sungah, a leng lo nadingin.

records.english: Is the sun a planet or a star?
records.zomi: Ni pen aksi lian hiam, aksi hiam?

records.english: The museum guide explained how the Earth's crust is made of moving plates.
records.zomi: Museum makaipa in leitung' khuh pen a tawn lei-ek lian te tawh a kibawl hi, ci-in a gen hi.

records.english: A pilot must understand the Earth's magnetic field to use a compass properly.
records.zomi: Vanleng tawlpa in compass dik taka a zat theih nadingin leitung' magnet hatna a theisiam ding hi.

records.english: Our school's telescope was paid for by a parents' fundraising evening.
records.zomi: I sang' telescope pen nu leh pate' sum kaikhawmna nitak in a pia hi.

records.english: Will we be able to see the eclipse from the school?
records.zomi: Sang pan ni-man i mu thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, but only through the special glasses the science department bought.
records.zomi: Mu thei ding hi, ahi zongin science department' lei mitlimlang tuam tawh bek.

records.english: Which planet has the most moons?
records.zomi: Bang aksi lian in kha tam pen a nei hiam?

records.english: The astronomer at the observatory let each student look through the big telescope.
records.zomi: Aksi enna inn-a aksi siampa in sangnaupang khatciat telescope lian sung pan a ensak hi.

records.english: Is it true that astronauts grow a little taller in space?
records.zomi: Astronaut te vantung ah tawmno a sang zaw uh hi, cih a dik hiam?

records.english: Satellite photos help firefighters see where a wildfire is spreading.
records.zomi: Satellite photo te in mei mitna nasemte gammang mei koi-ah a zel hiam cih a muh nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: What's the job of a seismologist?
records.zomi: Seismologist khat' nasep bang hiam?

records.english: To study earthquakes and the waves they send through the ground.
records.zomi: Lei ling leh tua te in lei sungah a khak lingna te sin.

records.english: Mum's favourite historical figure is a woman who started schools for girls in her region.
records.zomi: Nu' it pen tangthu mi pen a gam sungah numei naupangte adingin sang a kipatsak numei khat ahi hi.

records.english: Grandpa's diary mentions meeting a famous traveller on the road to the market.
records.zomi: Pu' ciamtehna laibu in sumbuk paina lampi-a khualzin min thang khat a kimuhna a gen hi.

records.english: Which person from history would you invite to dinner?
records.zomi: Tangthu pan kua nitak an ah na sam ding hiam?

records.english: Florence Nightingale, because I'd love to ask her about nursing in wartime.
records.zomi: Florence Nightingale, bang hang hiam cih leh gal hun-a nurse nasep tawh kisai dong ka deih hi.

records.english: Mum told us the story of a woman from her village who saved many children during a famine.
records.zomi: Gilkialna hun-in naupang tampi a hotkhia a khua-a numei khat tangthu Nu in hong gen hi.

records.english: Who is the man in the old photo with Great-grandpa?
records.zomi: Pu' pa tawh photo lui sung-a pasal kua hiam?

records.english: The first pastor of our church, who baptised half the village.
records.zomi: I pawlpi' pastor masa pen, khua kim a baptaiz pa.

records.english: Shall we take the children to the museum about the famous doctor?
records.zomi: Siavuan min thang tawh kisai museum ah naupangte i paipih ding hiam?

records.english: Did your uncle really name his son after a famous scientist?
records.zomi: Na pa neu in a tapa science siampa min thang khat' min a phuak taktak hiam?

records.english: Our son's school project was about Rosa Parks and her courage on the bus.
records.zomi: I tapa' sang project pen Rosa Parks leh bus tunga a hangsanna tawh kisai ahi hi.

records.english: Mum's book club is reading a biography of a famous nurse.
records.zomi: Nu' laibu sim pawl in nurse min thang khat' nuntakna tangthu a sim uh hi.

records.english: Who is your favourite person from history?
records.zomi: Tangthu pan na it pen mi kua hiam?

records.english: Dad tells us stories about the founder of our town every time we pass his statue.
records.zomi: A lim i pal simin Pa in i khuapi kipatsakpa tawh kisai tangthu hong gen hi.

records.english: Do you think Great-grandpa would be proud of the village today?
records.zomi: Pu' pa in tu-a khua tungah a kipak ding hi na ci hiam?

records.english: Grandma still keeps a letter that a famous writer sent to her father.
records.zomi: Laigelh siam min thang khat in a pa kiangah a khak laikhak Pi in a kem lai hi.

records.english: When we watched the film about Gandhi, Grandpa told us how people in his town had followed the news.
records.zomi: Gandhi tawh kisai film i en ciangin Pu in a khuapi-a mite thuthak bangci-in a zui uh hiam cih hong gen hi.

records.english: The children made a family tree that included a famous painter on their grandmother's side.
records.zomi: Naupangte in a pi lam ah lim lai siam min thang khat a kihel innkuan suahna lam khat a bawl uh hi.

records.english: Did Grandma really meet a famous singer?
records.zomi: Pi in la sa min thang khat a mu taktak hiam?

records.english: Yes, she sold him a cup of tea at the station when she was 16.
records.zomi: Mu hi, kum 16 a cin lai-in meileng khawlna mun ah niangtui haai khat a zuak hi.

records.english: Did your parents ever tell you about the leaders they admired as young people?
records.zomi: Na nu leh pa in a khangno lai-un a phat makaite tawh kisai hong gen ngei uh hiam?

records.english: Our neighbour's grandfather was a soldier who knew the general personally.
records.zomi: I inn veng' pu pen galkap pi khat a theih galkap khat ahi hi.

records.english: My daughter chose Marie Curie for her school presentation because she wants to be a scientist.
records.zomi: Ka tanu science siampa suah a deih manin a sang presentation adingin Marie Curie a teel hi.

records.english: The children were amazed that their great-grandmother had once sung for a queen.
records.zomi: A pi' pi in nidang-in kumpinu khat adingin la a sa ngei hi, cih naupangte in lamdang a sa mahmah uh hi.

records.english: My grandmother cried when she heard that the leader she admired had died.
records.zomi: A phat makaipa a sih hi, cih a zak ciangin ka pi a kap hi.

records.english: Our son was surprised to learn that his hero had failed many times before he succeeded.
records.zomi: A phat mi in a lawhcing ma-in vei tampi a sun ngei hi, cih a theih ciangin i tapa lamdang a sa hi.

records.english: Why did we name our dog after a famous explorer?
records.zomi: Bang hangin i ui gam zong min thang khat' min i phuak hiam?

records.english: Who in our family is named after someone famous?
records.zomi: I innkuan sung-ah kua in min thang khat' min a nei hiam?

records.english: Has your brother read every biography he can find about explorers?
records.zomi: Na u pasal in gam zongte tawh kisai nuntakna tangthu a muh theih khempeuh a sim hiam?

records.english: Our son's favourite bedtime stories are about explorers who crossed the oceans.
records.zomi: I tapa' it pen lup ma tangthu te tuipi a pal gam zongte tawh kisai ahi hi.

records.english: Every year, our family visits the grave of a relative who died helping others during the war.
records.zomi: Kum simin i innkuan in gal lai-in midangte a huh kawm-a si sanggam khat' han a veh hi.

records.english: My great-grandfather once carried messages across the mountains for the village chief.
records.zomi: Ka pu' pa in khua makaipa adingin mual te tungah thuthak a puak ngei hi.

records.english: He walked for three days each way, sleeping in caves and farmers' huts.
records.zomi: Lam khat ah ni thum a kal a, suang kua te leh lou bawlte' buk te ah a ihmu hi.

records.english: The family still keeps the walking stick he used on those journeys.
records.zomi: Tua khualzinna te-a a zat ciang innkuan in a kem lai hi.

records.english: My grandparents' wedding photo includes a man who later became a minister.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh pi te' mopawi photo ah a nungin minister a suak pasal khat a kihel hi.

records.english: Dad taught us that heroes are often ordinary people who made one brave choice.
records.zomi: Hangsan mite pen hangsan teelna khat a bawl mi ngeina te ahi zel uh hi, ci-in Pa in hong sinsak hi.

records.english: Our family is proud that a distant relative fought for independence.
records.zomi: Sanggam gamla khat in gam suahtakna adingin a do hi, cih i innkuan in a kipak hi.

records.english: Is it true that our great-great-grandfather knew the town's first doctor?
records.zomi: I pu' pu' pa in khuapi' siavuan masa pen a thei hi, cih a dik hiam?

records.english: When we visited the capital, my father showed us the house where a great poet had lived.
records.zomi: Khuapi lian i veh ciangin ka pa in la phuak siam lian khat' tenna inn hong lak hi.

records.english: Mum's great-uncle was a well-known preacher in the hill villages.
records.zomi: Nu' pu' u pasal ahi zongin nau pasal pen mual khua te-a a kithei thugenpa khat ahi hi.

records.english: According to Grandpa, our family name comes from a village headman who lived three hundred years ago.
records.zomi: Pu' gen bangin i innkuan min pen kum za thum ma-a teng khua makaipa khat pan a hong hi.

records.english: Dad's teacher was later remembered as one of the great thinkers of the region.
records.zomi: Pa' saya pen a nungin gam sung-a ngaihsut siam lian te lak-a khat-in kiphawk hi.

records.english: Why does Dad keep a picture of that old teacher on the wall?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pa in tua saya lui' lim bang tungah a kem hiam?

records.english: She taught his whole village to read, and he was one of her first pupils.
records.zomi: Amah in a khua bup sim a sinsak a, Pa a sangnaupang masa te lak-a khat ahi hi.

records.english: Dad admires the leaders who chose peace when war seemed easier.
records.zomi: Gal a baih zaw bang hun-in kilemna a teel makaite Pa in a phat hi.

records.english: My aunt is writing a book about our great-grandmother, who ran the village school.
records.zomi: Ka ni in khua sang a makaih i pu' nu tawh kisai laibu khat a gelh hi.

records.english: Tell us about the most famous person you've ever met, Grandma.
records.zomi: Pi, na muh ngeih lak-ah min thang pen kua hiam cih hong gen in.

records.english: My daughter dressed up as a famous inventor for book day.
records.zomi: Laibu ni adingin ka tanu in bawlsiam min thang khat bangin a kizem hi.

records.english: Grandpa shook hands with a famous boxer once and still shows us the hand he used.
records.zomi: Pu in khatvei boxer min thang khat tawh khut a kilen a, a zat khut hong lak lai hi.

records.english: Thank you for telling the children about the leaders you remember, Grandpa.
records.zomi: Pu, na phawk makaite tawh kisai naupangte kiangah na gen manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: My grandmother has a signed photo of a famous footballer from her youth.
records.zomi: Ka pi in a khangno lai-a football kimawlpa min thang khat' min gelhna nei photo khat a nei hi.

records.english: Grandpa, who was your hero when you were a boy?
records.zomi: Pu, na naupan lai-in na phat mi kua hiam?

records.english: A local doctor who walked from village to village to treat the sick.
records.zomi: Natte damsak dingin khua khat pan khat ah a kal a mun siavuan khat.

records.english: Grandpa keeps newspaper cuttings about the famous people he has met.
records.zomi: Pu in a muh ngeih mi min thang te tawh kisai thuthak laipi tan te a kem hi.

records.english: Our family visits the birthplace of a national hero every time we go to the coast.
records.zomi: Tuipi gei i pai simin i innkuan in gam hangsan khat' suahna mun a veh hi.

records.english: The children asked Grandma what life was like when the old king ruled.
records.zomi: Kumpipa lui a uk lai-in nuntakna bang ci hiam ci-in naupangte in Pi a dong uh hi.

records.english: Which famous person from history would you like to have as a teacher?
records.zomi: Tangthu pan bang min thang mi saya-in na neih nop hiam?

records.english: Our son hung a poster of Albert Einstein above his desk.
records.zomi: I tapa in a taupi tungah Albert Einstein poster khat a khai hi.

records.english: My grandparents still talk about the day the president visited their village.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh pi te in president a khua uh a veh ni a gen lai uh hi.

records.english: Learning about famous people from our own region makes history feel close to home.
records.zomi: I gam sung pan min thang mite tawh kisai sin in tangthu inn kiang-ah a om bang-in a kisasak hi.

records.english: My cousin wrote her university essay about a woman scientist from our country.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam in a university essay i gam pan numei science siam khat tawh kisai a gelh hi.

records.english: My brother deleted his post when his wife said it shared too much about their argument.
records.zomi: A zi in a kitelna uh tawh kisai a tam luat a hawm hi a cih ciangin ka u pasal in a post a phiat hi.

records.english: Can I post a photo of our new puppy?
records.zomi: I ui neu thak photo khat ka post thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, but don't show the house number in the background.
records.zomi: Thei hi, ahi zongin a nunglam ah inn nambat lak kei in.

records.english: When my daughter won the race, I had to stop myself from posting about it at once.
records.zomi: Ka tanu tai kidemna a zawh ciangin a pah-in post kei dingin ka kikham kul hi.

records.english: My teenager says my posts are embarrassing, but she still reads them.
records.zomi: Ka post te a maizumhuai hi, ci-in ka tangnu in a gen a, ahi zongin a sim lai hi.

records.english: Why does Auntie Hoih add twenty hashtags to every post?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Ni Hoih in post khempeuh ah hashtag sawmnih a beh hiam?

records.english: Dad's posts are full of proverbs that only his generation understands.
records.zomi: Pa' post te a khangthu bek in a theisiam paunak te tawh a dim hi.

records.english: Posting about family news is easier than phoning thirty relatives one by one.
records.zomi: Innkuan thuthak post pen sanggam sawmthum khat ciat sam sangin a baih zaw hi.

records.english: Our family posts a new photo of the children on the first day of each school year.
records.zomi: I innkuan in sang kum khatciat' ni masa pen-in naupangte' photo thak khat a post hi.

records.english: Our cousin posts a photo of her garden every morning.
records.zomi: I sanggam in zingsang simin a huan photo khat a post hi.

records.english: Please ask me first before you post any pictures of the twins.
records.zomi: Apeng te' lim khatpeuh na post ma-in hong dong masa in.

records.english: Mum posted a photo of the cake she made for my birthday.
records.zomi: Ka suahni adingin a bawl changkhuai photo khat Nu in a post hi.

records.english: Grandma's post asking for her old classmates was shared all over her home town.
records.zomi: A sang lawm luite a zonna Pi' post a suahna khuapi bup ah a kihawm hi.

records.english: My sister posted a video of her son's first steps, and the whole family watched it ten times.
records.zomi: Ka u numei in a tapa' khekhap masa video khat a post a, innkuan bup in sawmvei a en uh hi.

records.english: My sister writes a long post every year on our parents' anniversary.
records.zomi: Ka u numei in kum simin i nu leh pa' kiteen kum phawkna ni-in post sau khat a gelh hi.

records.english: My cousin's post about our grandmother's recipes started a long family conversation.
records.zomi: I pi' an huanzia te tawh kisai ka sanggam' post in innkuan kihopihna sau khat a kipatsak hi.

records.english: I wrote a post to thank everyone who came to Grandpa's funeral.
records.zomi: Pu' mithi vuina-a hong mi khempeuh lungdam ka gen nadingin post khat ka gelh hi.

records.english: A post from a relative abroad can make a whole family feel close for a moment.
records.zomi: Gamdang-a sanggam khat' post in hun tawmno innkuan bup a kinai bang-in a kisasak thei hi.

records.english: My husband posted the photo of my new haircut before I was ready.
records.zomi: Ka kiging ma-in ka pasal in ka sam metna thak photo a post hi.

records.english: Grandma asked me to post the news of her eightieth birthday party so that old friends could come.
records.zomi: Lawm luite a hong theih nadingin Pi in a kum sawmgiat suahni poai thuthak post dingin hong ngen hi.

records.english: My mother-in-law comments on every post within minutes.
records.zomi: Ka sungnu in post khempeuh minit tawmno sung-in comment a bawl hi.

records.english: Writing a post about my father's illness helped me accept what was happening.
records.zomi: Ka pa' natna tawh kisai post khat gelh in bang a piang hiam cih ka sang nadingin hong huh hi.

records.english: The reunion photos you posted made Grandpa so happy.
records.zomi: Na post innkuan kikhopna photo te in Pu a lungdamsak mahmah hi.

records.english: Our son's first post was a blurry photo of his own foot.
records.zomi: I tapa' post masa pen amah' khe photo kician lo khat ahi hi.

records.english: My daughter spends ages choosing a filter before she posts anything.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in bangmah a post ma-in filter teel dingin hun sawt a zang hi.

records.english: Did you see the post Uncle Thang wrote about his first grandchild?
records.zomi: Pa neu Thang in a tu masa pen tawh kisai a gelh post na mu hiam?

records.english: Our son posted a video of his grandfather playing the guitar.
records.zomi: I tapa in a pu guitar a tum video khat a post hi.

records.english: My wife edits her photos so carefully that a single post can take an hour.
records.zomi: Ka zi in a photo te kidawm mahmah-in a bawlphat ahih manin post khat nai khat a la thei hi.

records.english: Grandma types her posts in capital letters because she says they're easier to read.
records.zomi: Pi in a post te laimal lian tawh a gelh hi, bang hang hiam cih leh sim a baih zaw hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Let's take one more photo for the post, because Dad had his eyes closed.
records.zomi: Pa' mit a kikhuh ahih manin post adingin photo khat beh i lak ni.

records.english: My niece makes short videos of her baking and posts them for the family.
records.zomi: Ka tunu in a moh huan video tomno te a bawl a, innkuan adingin a post hi.

records.english: Why did you delete the post about the holiday?
records.zomi: Bang hangin tawlngakni tawh kisai post na phiat hiam?

records.english: Auntie said it showed that our house would be empty for two weeks.
records.zomi: Kal nih sung i inn a hawm ding hi, cih a lak hi, ci-in Ni in a gen hi.

records.english: Shall we post a photo of the new house for the relatives back home?
records.zomi: Inn lam-a sanggamte adingin inn thak photo khat i post ding hiam?

records.english: Dad always forgets to add a caption to his photos.
records.zomi: Pa in a photo te ah caption beh a mangngilh den hi.

records.english: Should I post about the baby before the whole family knows?
records.zomi: Innkuan bup in a theih ma-un naungek tawh kisai ka post ding hiam?

records.english: No, wait until we've told the grandparents ourselves.
records.zomi: Hi lo hi, eimah in pu leh pi te i gen mateng ngak in.

records.english: My husband writes his posts in two languages so that both our families can read them.
records.zomi: I innkuan nih in a sim theih nadingin ka pasal in a post te pau nih tawh a gelh hi.

records.english: Our family has a rule that nobody posts photos of the youngest children's faces.
records.zomi: I innkuan in naupang neu pen te' mai photo kuamah in post lo ding cih thukhun khat a nei hi.

records.english: When my brother graduated, Mum wrote the proudest post I've ever read.
records.zomi: Ka u pasal sang a zawh ciangin Nu in ka sim ngeih lak-a a kipak pen post a gelh hi.

records.english: Who taught Grandpa to make his own posts?
records.zomi: Pu amah post bawl kua in a sinsak hiam?

records.english: His granddaughter, during a long afternoon with a lot of patience.
records.zomi: A tu numei in, thuakzawhna tampi tawh nitak lam sau khat sung.

records.english: When Grandpa posted his first photo, it was upside down.
records.zomi: Pu in a photo masa pen a post ciangin a kilehheh hi.

records.english: We save our favourite family posts in an album so that we can look at them later.
records.zomi: A nungin i en theih nadingin i it pen innkuan post te album khat sungah i kem uh hi.

records.english: My uncle posts every photo twice because he forgets he has already shared it.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in a hawm khin cih a mangngilh ahih manin photo khempeuh nihvei a post hi.

records.english: My parents' first joint post was a picture of their fortieth anniversary dinner.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa' khawm-a post masa pen a kum sawmli kiteen kum phawkna nitak an lim ahi hi.

records.english: Before posting a photo of the cousins, I asked each of their parents for permission.
records.zomi: Sanggamte' photo khat ka post ma-in a nu leh pa khatciat kiangah phalna ka ngen hi.

records.english: Who took the photo that Mum posted this morning?
records.zomi: Tu zingsang-in Nu' post photo kua in a lak hiam?

records.english: Our children write captions for the family album before we post it.
records.zomi: I post ma-un i tate in innkuan album adingin caption te a gelh uh hi.

records.english: Auntie Lun writes a poem in every birthday post.
records.zomi: Ni Lun in suahni post khempeuh ah la phuak khat a gelh hi.

records.english: We agreed not to post anything about the children's schools.
records.zomi: Naupangte' sang tawh kisai bangmah post lo dingin i kilem uh hi.

records.english: Before I post anything about the family, I imagine how Grandma would feel reading it.
records.zomi: Innkuan tawh kisai bangmah ka post ma-in Pi in a sim leh bangci-in a kisa ding hiam cih ka ngaihsun hi.

records.english: Should I post the video of the wedding speech, or would your brother mind?
records.zomi: Mopawi thugen video ka post ding hiam, na u pasal in a lungkim lo ding hiam?

records.english: My daughter writes the captions, and I choose the photos.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in caption te a gelh a, kei in photo te ka teel hi.

records.english: Is it rude to post a photo of the family dinner without asking everyone?
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh dong lo-in innkuan nitak an photo post pen zahtakna om lo ahi hiam?

records.english: Can you help me write a post for my mother's retirement?
records.zomi: Ka nu' nasep tawpna adingin post khat gelh dingin hong huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Our son made a funny video of the cat and asked permission before posting it.
records.zomi: I tapa in zawhngeu' nuihhuai video khat a bawl a, a post ma-in phalna a ngen hi.

records.english: Dad's post about his new fishing boat got more likes than any of mine.
records.zomi: Pa' nga manna long thak tawh kisai post in kei' post khempeuh sangin like a tam zaw hi.

records.english: What should I write under the photo of Grandma's birthday?
records.zomi: Pi' suahni photo nuai-ah bang ka gelh ding hiam?

records.english: Something simple, like how lucky we are to have her.
records.zomi: Baih khat, amah i neih manin bangzah i vangphat hiam cih bang.

records.english: My son passed his driving test, and his licence arrived within a week.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in a mawtaw tawl sitna a zo a, a licence kal khat sung-in a tung hi.

records.english: Our family's oldest document is my great-grandfather's land paper from the village.
records.zomi: I innkuan' lai lui pen ka pu' pa' khua-a gam lai ahi hi.

records.english: Our son needed his birth certificate to register for football.
records.zomi: Football ah a min gelh nadingin i tapa in a pianna lai a kisam hi.

records.english: My brother's identity card still shows his old address in the village.
records.zomi: Ka u pasal' mi hihna card in khua-a a inn mun lui a lak lai hi.

records.english: My uncle waited a year for his pension because nobody could find his birth certificate.
records.zomi: Kuamah in a pianna lai a muh loh manin ka pa neu in a pension kum khat a ngak hi.

records.english: The officer at the border asked my son to take off his hat for the photo check.
records.zomi: Gamgi-a officer in photo enna adingin ka tapa a lukhu la khia dingin a ngen hi.

records.english: My parents had to prove their identity before they could collect Grandpa's pension.
records.zomi: Pu' pension a la theih ma-un ka nu leh ka pa in a mi hihna a kipsak kul uh hi.

records.english: Mum took photos of all our documents and saved them in a safe place online.
records.zomi: Nu in i lai khempeuh photo a lak a, online ah mun bit khat ah a kem hi.

records.english: Dad lost his wallet with his identity card in it, so he had to report it to the police.
records.zomi: Pa in a mi hihna card om sum ip a mansuah ahih manin police kiangah a theisak kul hi.

records.english: We laughed at the baby's passport photo for weeks.
records.zomi: Naungek' passport photo kal tampi i nui uh hi.

records.english: My grandparents' marriage certificate is handwritten and almost too faded to read.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh pi te' kiteenna lai-ciam khut tawh kigelh a, sim theih loh dong a kang hi.

records.english: Do I need to bring the children's documents to the doctor's appointment?
records.zomi: Siavuan kimuhna ah naupangte' lai te ka paipih kul hiam?

records.english: When my parents became citizens, they framed their certificates and hung them in the hall.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa gam mi a suah ciangin a lai-ciam te uh bawm tawh a kikoih uh a, inn paina lam ah a khai uh hi.

records.english: Who has Grandma's passport now that she's moved in with us?
records.zomi: Pi kote tawh a teng khit ciangin a passport kua in a kem hiam?

records.english: Grandpa's identity card photo was taken thirty years ago, and he insists it still looks like him.
records.zomi: Pu' mi hihna card photo kum sawmthum ma-in kilak a, amah bang lai hi, ci-in a ngetsak hi.

records.english: Our daughter's name was spelled wrongly on her birth certificate, so we had it corrected.
records.zomi: I tanu' min a pianna lai tungah a khial-in kigelh ahih manin i bawlphat sak uh hi.

records.english: Have you checked whether the children's passports are still valid?
records.zomi: Naupangte' passport te hun bei nai lo hiam cih na en hiam?

records.english: Grandma still carries her late husband's identity card in her purse.
records.zomi: Pi in a pasal sihsa' mi hihna card a sum ip sungah a pua lai hi.

records.english: When does your identity card expire, Dad?
records.zomi: Pa, na mi hihna card bang ciangin a hun a bei ding hiam?

records.english: Next spring, so I'll renew it before our summer holiday.
records.zomi: Spring hong tung ding-in, tua ahih manin i khal tawlngakni ma-in ka thak ding hi.

records.english: Why is Grandma's name spelled differently on her new card?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pi' card thak tungah a min tuam-in a kigelh hiam?

records.english: The clerk copied it from an old document that had a mistake in it.
records.zomi: Nasempa in khialhna nei lai lui khat pan a kaih hi.

records.english: Mum keeps all our passports in a locked drawer.
records.zomi: Nu in i passport khempeuh khak theih dawh khat sungah a kem hi.

records.english: My sister collected her new passport on the morning of her flight.
records.zomi: Ka u numei in a vanleng khualzinna zingsang-in a passport thak a la hi.

records.english: The children's new identity cards arrived in the post today.
records.zomi: Tuni-in naupangte' mi hihna card thak te post tawh a tung hi.

records.english: Does the baby need her own passport for the trip?
records.zomi: Khualzinna adingin naungek in amah passport a kisam hiam?

records.english: Yes, every child needs a passport to travel abroad from here.
records.zomi: Kisam hi, hih mun pan gamdang ah khualzin dingin naupang khatciat in passport a kisam hi.

records.english: Let's put all the documents back in the folder before the children get to them.
records.zomi: Naupangte in a tun ma-un lai khempeuh folder sungah i koih kik ni.

records.english: Can I use my student card as identification at the bank?
records.zomi: Bank ah ka student card mi hihna-in ka zang thei hiam?

records.english: Probably not, so bring your passport just in case.
records.zomi: Thei kha lo ding hi, tua ahih manin na passport paipih den in.

records.english: Grandma's old passport is full of stamps from her travels as a young woman.
records.zomi: Pi' passport lui pen a nungak lai-a khualzinna stamp te tawh a dim hi.

records.english: Our son was so proud when he got his first identity card.
records.zomi: A mi hihna card masa pen a ngah ciangin i tapa a kipak mahmah hi.

records.english: My cousin needed a translation of her birth certificate when she married abroad.
records.zomi: Gamdang ah a kiteen ciangin ka sanggam in a pianna lai' lettna a kisam hi.

records.english: Thank you for finding my identity card, because I'd been looking everywhere.
records.zomi: Ka mun khempeuh ah ka zon ahih manin ka mi hihna card hong muh sak manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: Why does your brother keep his passport in the same drawer as his football medals?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na u pasal in a passport a football medal te tawh dawh kibang sungah a kem hiam?

records.english: Shall we get passport photos taken for the whole family on Saturday?
records.zomi: Kiginni-in innkuan bup adingin passport photo i lak ding hiam?

records.english: Our family keeps copies of everyone's documents at my aunt's house too.
records.zomi: I innkuan in mi khempeuh' lai kopi te ka ni' inn ah zong a kem hi.

records.english: Grandpa doesn't know his exact date of birth, so his card shows only the year.
records.zomi: Pu in a suahni kician a thei kei ahih manin a card in kum bek a lak hi.

records.english: Our son forgot his identity card and couldn't sit the exam.
records.zomi: I tapa in a mi hihna card a mangngilh a, sitna a sit thei kei hi.

records.english: Our son's identity card says he's taller than he really is.
records.zomi: I tapa' mi hihna card in a taktak sangin a sang zaw hi, a ci hi.

records.english: My daughter's passport photo was taken five times because she kept smiling.
records.zomi: Ka tanu a nui den ahih manin a passport photo nga vei kilak hi.

records.english: Identity documents tell a family's story through names, dates, places and changes.
records.zomi: Mi hihna lai te in min, ni, mun leh kikhekna tungtawnin innkuan khat' tangthu a gen hi.

records.english: Dad's first passport photo shows him with a moustache none of us has ever seen.
records.zomi: Pa' passport photo masa pen in kuamah in i muh ngeih loh a khamul tawh hong lak hi.

records.english: When my grandfather applied for his first identity card, he was already 60.
records.zomi: Ka pu in a mi hihna card masa pen a ngen ciangin kum 60 a cing khin hi.

records.english: When we moved here, the whole family had to register for new identity cards.
records.zomi: Hih mun ah i tai ciangin innkuan bup in mi hihna card thak adingin min i gelh kul uh hi.

records.english: Please don't let the baby chew Daddy's passport.
records.zomi: Naungek in Pa' passport a ngawh kei ding hi, hong kem in.

records.english: Is it safe to send a copy of my passport by email?
records.zomi: Ka passport kopi email tawh khak a bit hiam?

records.english: We had to renew all five passports before the family wedding abroad.
records.zomi: Gamdang-a innkuan mopawi ma-in passport nga khempeuh i thak kul uh hi.

records.english: My wife renewed her identity card online, which saved her a morning off work.
records.zomi: Ka zi in a mi hihna card online-in a thak a, nasep pan zingsang khat tawl kul lo hi.

records.english: My sister's passport was stolen on holiday, so she spent a day at the embassy.
records.zomi: Ka u numei' passport tawlngakni-in kiguk ahih manin embassy ah ni khat a zang hi.

records.english: I need my passport to open a bank account for my daughter.
records.zomi: Ka tanu adingin bank account khat hon nadingin ka passport ka kisam hi.

records.english: Was your birth certificate issued in this country or abroad?
records.zomi: Na pianna lai hih gam ah kipia hiam, gamdang ah hiam?

records.english: My uncle's identity card was destroyed in the fire, along with all his papers.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu' mi hihna card a lai khempeuh tawh meikang ah a kang khin hi.

records.english: Before the trip, Dad checked every passport twice.
records.zomi: Khualzinna ma-in Pa in passport khempeuh nihvei a en hi.

records.english: My mother-in-law has three documents with three different spellings of her name.
records.zomi: Ka sungnu in a min gelhzia tuam thum nei lai thum a nei hi.

records.english: My daughter keeps a photocopy of her passport in her school bag when we travel.
records.zomi: I khualzin ciangin ka tanu in a sang ip sungah a passport photocopy khat a kem hi.

records.english: Where did you put the children's birth certificates?
records.zomi: Naupangte' pianna lai te koi-ah na koih hiam?

records.english: In the blue folder, behind the insurance papers.
records.zomi: Folder dum sungah, insurance lai te nunglam ah.

records.english: My wife decided to keep her own surname on her documents after our wedding.
records.zomi: I mopawi khit ciangin ka zi in a lai te tungah amah min tawp kem dingin a khensat hi.

records.english: My brother's passport ran out the week before his holiday, so he paid for a fast renewal.
records.zomi: Ka u pasal' passport a tawlngakni ma kal-in a hun a bei ahih manin a hun-a thak nadingin a pia hi.

records.english: Rather than hiring more staff, the company changed the shift pattern.
records.zomi: Nasem tam zaw zat sangin company in nasep hun kikhekna a khek hi.

records.english: The head teacher asked the pupils to design a fairer system for the canteen queue.
records.zomi: Sangpi saya in sangnaupangte an nekna inn-a mi kigual adingin a dik zaw kalsuanna khat ciamteh dingin a ngen hi.

records.english: Thanks for your idea, because it saved us a lot of time.
records.zomi: Na ngaihsutna in hun tampi hong hehpih manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: The apprentice found a way to cut the wood with less waste.
records.zomi: Na kisin mi in mang tawm zaw-in sing sat zia khat a mu hi.

records.english: The engineer suggested a simpler part that would be easier to replace.
records.zomi: Engineer in laih baih zaw kikhen baih zaw khat a gen hi.

records.english: A solution that nobody understands will not last long in a busy office.
records.zomi: Kuamah in a theisiam loh bawlphatna khat hun neilo office ah a sawt kei ding hi.

records.english: Could we move the class to the morning, when everyone is less tired?
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh a gim tawm zaw zingsang lam ah class i sawn thei ding hiam?

records.english: Can you think of a way to make the instructions clearer?
records.zomi: Thuhilhnate kician zaw-a bawl nading lam khat na ngaihsun thei hiam?

records.english: The team chose the second option because it could be tried quickly and cheaply.
records.zomi: A hun-in leh man neu-in sit theih ahih manin team in teelna nihna a teel hi.

records.english: The class came up with five different ways to solve the problem.
records.zomi: Class in haksatna bawlphat nading lam tuam nga a ngaihsun uh hi.

records.english: How about splitting the class into two groups for the practical work?
records.zomi: Khut tawh nasep adingin class pawl nih-in i khen leh bang ci ding hiam?

records.english: The best idea came from the youngest apprentice, who had a fresh view of the process.
records.zomi: Ngaihsutna hoih pen pen kalsuanna tungah muhna thak nei na kisin mi neu pen pan a hong hi.

records.english: We fixed the slow computers by deleting old files and adding more memory.
records.zomi: File lui te phiat-in memory beh-in computer zawi te i bawlphat uh hi.

records.english: Combining two average ideas sometimes produces a very good one.
records.zomi: Ngaihsutna ngeina nih kizopsak in ngaihsutna hoih mahmah khat a piangsak zel hi.

records.english: Instead of one long meeting, the manager tried two short ones each week.
records.zomi: Kikhopna sau khat sangin manager in kal simin kikhopna tom nih a sawm hi.

records.english: How can we cut the time customers spend waiting at the counter?
records.zomi: Customer te' sum lakna mun-a ngak hun bangci-in i tomsak thei ding hiam?

records.english: We could open a second till during the lunchtime rush.
records.zomi: Sun an hun buai lai-in sum bawm nihna khat i hon thei hi.

records.english: Good solutions often come from people who actually do the job every day.
records.zomi: Bawlphatna hoih te ni simin nasep a sem taktak mite pan a hong zel hi.

records.english: We trialled the new system in one branch before using it everywhere.
records.zomi: Mun khempeuh ah i zat ma-un branch khat ah system thak i sit uh hi.

records.english: Shall we ask the cleaners how they would improve the system?
records.zomi: Siangsakna nasemte system bangci-in a hoihsak ding uh hiam cih i dong ding hiam?

records.english: Let's brainstorm a few ideas before the meeting ends.
records.zomi: Kikhopna a tawp ma-in ngaihsutna tawmno i kigen ni.

records.english: Do you have any other suggestions before we vote?
records.zomi: Vote i piak ma-un ngaihsutna dang na nei lai hiam?

records.english: Our company solved its delivery delays by opening a small warehouse closer to the city.
records.zomi: I company in khuapi kiang zaw-ah warehouse neu khat a hon-in van tunsakna phawngna a bawlphat hi.

records.english: Our tutor encouraged us to suggest solutions, not just complain about problems.
records.zomi: I tutor in haksatna tawh kisai phun bek hi lo-in bawlphatna gen dingin hong lungkhauhsak hi.

records.english: Could we try the new layout for a week and see how it works?
records.zomi: Koihzia thak kal khat sung i sit a, bangci-in a kalsuan hiam cih i en thei ding hiam?

records.english: Could we share the printer with the office next door?
records.zomi: A kiang-a office tawh printer i kihawm thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, if we agree on who pays for the paper and ink.
records.zomi: Thei hi, lai-ek leh ink man kua in a pia ding hiam cih ah i kilem leh.

records.english: If the room is too small, why don't we hold the training online?
records.zomi: Inndan a neu luat leh bang hangin training online-in i bawl lo ding hiam?

records.english: Could we put a suggestion box in the staff room?
records.zomi: Nasemte tawlna dan ah ngaihsutna bawm khat i koih thei ding hiam?

records.english: Shall we try your plan on Monday and meet again on Friday to see how it went?
records.zomi: Pizing ni-in na ciamtehna i sit a, Laithai ni-in bangci-in a kalsuan hiam cih en dingin i kimu kik ding hiam?

records.english: Our supervisor suggested that we rotate the boring tasks between everyone.
records.zomi: I makaipa in nasep nuam lo te mi khempeuh kikal ah kikhek tuah dingin a gen hi.

records.english: We solved the parking problem by encouraging staff to share cars.
records.zomi: Nasemte mawtaw kihawm dingin i lungkhauhsak uh-in mawtaw khawl haksatna i bawlphat uh hi.

records.english: Which solution would be quickest to put in place?
records.zomi: Bang bawlphatna in koih a hun pen ding hiam?

records.english: Would it help to send the agenda out the day before?
records.zomi: Kikhopna thuciamtehna a ma ni-in khak leh a huh ding hiam?

records.english: When nothing else worked, we asked an expert to look at the problem with fresh eyes.
records.zomi: Bangmah a nasem kei ciangin muhna thak tawh haksatna en dingin siampa khat i ngen uh hi.

records.english: Our manager asked every department for one idea to save energy.
records.zomi: I manager in thahatna kem nadingin department khempeuh ngaihsutna khat a ngen hi.

records.english: What if we moved the deadline to the end of the month?
records.zomi: Hun bei kha tawp ah i sawn leh bang ci ding hiam?

records.english: Then the team would have time to test everything properly.
records.zomi: Tua hileh team in khempeuh dik takin a sit theih nadingin hun a nei ding hi.

records.english: Why don't we ask the customers what they would like us to change?
records.zomi: Bang hangin customer te in bang i khek ding a deih uh hiam ci-in i dong lo ding hiam?

records.english: Could the night staff leave notes for the morning team?
records.zomi: Zan nasemte in zingsang team adingin ciamtehna a nusia thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: A simple sign on the door solved weeks of confusion about the new entrance.
records.zomi: Kongkhak tunga ciamtehna baih khat in lutna thak tawh kisai kal tampi buaina a bawlphat hi.

records.english: Would a shared online calendar stop people from booking the same room?
records.zomi: Kihawm online calendar khat in mite inndan kibang a koih khol tuah loh nadingin a khawlsak ding hiam?

records.english: Before choosing a solution, our manager asks who will be affected by it.
records.zomi: Bawlphatna khat a teel ma-in i manager in kua tungah a tuak ding hiam ci-in a dong hi.

records.english: The students solved the noise problem by putting felt pads under the chairs.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte in tutphah nuai-ah puan-phah neu koih-in ging haksatna a bawlphat uh hi.

records.english: Is there a cheaper supplier who could deliver on time?
records.zomi: Hun-in a tunsak thei van zuakpa man neu zaw khat a om hiam?

records.english: A short checklist solved most of the mistakes in our orders.
records.zomi: Checklist tomno khat in i order te-a khialhna tamzaw a bawlphat hi.

records.english: Every solution has a cost, so we need to compare them carefully.
records.zomi: Bawlphatna khatciat in a man a nei ahih manin kidawm takin i kiteh kul hi.

records.english: The students suggested a quiet room for anyone who needed to study at lunchtime.
records.zomi: Sun an hun-in kisin kisap mi khatpeuh adingin dan dai khat sangnaupangte in a gen uh hi.

records.english: Our team tested two designs with real customers before choosing one.
records.zomi: I team in khat a teel ma-un customer taktak te tawh design nih a sit uh hi.

records.english: What would it cost to fix the problem properly, rather than patching it again?
records.zomi: Bawlphat kik zel sangin haksatna dik taka bawlphat in bangzah a man ding hiam?

records.english: Is there a way to help the students who keep falling behind?
records.zomi: Nung ah a om den sangnaupangte huh nading lam khat a om hiam?

records.english: We could run a short catch-up session every Thursday after school.
records.zomi: Laizing ni simin sang khit ciangin a phawng mante kisinna tomno khat i bawl thei hi.

records.english: What's the worst that could happen if we try your idea?
records.zomi: Na ngaihsutna i sit leh a hoih lo pen bang a piang thei hiam?

records.english: Who will check whether the new solution is actually working?
records.zomi: Bawlphatna thak a nasem taktak hiam cih kua in a en ding hiam?

records.english: How else could we reduce the waste from the kitchen?
records.zomi: An huanna pan eek bangci-in i tawmsak thei lai ding hiam?

records.english: Smaller portions, and a deal with a farm that takes food scraps for its animals.
records.zomi: An zah neu zaw, leh a ganhing te adingin an kitam a la lou khat tawh kilemna.

records.english: The workshop taught us to look for solutions that tackle the cause, not just the symptoms.
records.zomi: Workshop in natna lim bek hi lo-in a hang a do bawlphatna zon dingin hong sinsak hi.

records.english: Can we find a way to finish the job without working at the weekend?
records.zomi: Kal tawp-in na sem lo-in nasep zawh nading lam khat i mu thei ding hiam?

records.english: Let's write each idea on a card and put them in order of cost.
records.zomi: Ngaihsutna khatciat card khat tungah i gelh a, a man zui-in i koih ni.

records.english: Let's ask the students what would help them most.
records.zomi: Bang in amaute huh pen ding hiam ci-in sangnaupangte i dong ni.

records.english: Leave the beaker to cool before you pick it up.
records.zomi: Beaker na len ma-in a vot dingin nusia in.

records.english: Solar engineers install panels on roofs to catch as much sunlight as possible.
records.zomi: Ni thahatna engineer te in ni vak tam thei pen a mat nadingin inn tung ah panel te a koih uh hi.

records.english: What gas do plants take in from the air?
records.zomi: Kung te in huih pan bang gas a la uh hiam?

records.english: Why do electricians wear rubber gloves?
records.zomi: Bang hangin electrician te in rubber khut-ip a bulh uh hiam?

records.english: Rubber doesn't conduct electricity, so it protects their hands.
records.zomi: Rubber in meivak a pai sak kei ahih manin a khutte uh a kem hi.

records.english: In chemistry, we heated copper and watched it change colour.
records.zomi: Chemistry ah sumpi i sasak uh a, a pianzia a kikhel i en uh hi.

records.english: Our teacher showed us that sound needs a material, such as air, to travel through.
records.zomi: Ging pen huih bang vanzat khat tungtawn bek-in a pai thei hi, ci-in i saya in hong lak hi.

records.english: Which materials in this box are conductors, and which are insulators?
records.zomi: Hih bawm sung-a vanzat te-ah bang te conductor ahi a, bang te insulator ahi hiam?

records.english: Our lab report described how salt changed the freezing point of water.
records.zomi: I lab report in cii in tui' khal mun bangci-in a khek hiam cih a gen hi.

records.english: A refrigerator moves heat from the inside to the outside.
records.zomi: Fridge in a sung pan a pualam ah lumna a sawn hi.

records.english: Engineers at the factory are trying to reduce the energy their machines waste.

records.english: Which material should we use to insulate the pipes?

records.english: The new heating system in our school uses heat pumps instead of a boiler.

records.english: Our class compared how quickly different cups kept tea warm.
records.zomi: I class in haai tuamtuam in niangtui bangzah sawt a lum sak hiam cih a kiteh uh hi.

records.english: Why did the ice melt faster in the metal tray?

records.english: Recycling aluminium uses much less energy than making it from raw materials.

records.zomi: Bang hangin mei mitna nasemte in puan tuam a silh uh hiam?

records.english: Write down what you observe when the sugar is heated.

records.english: Who can explain why a hot-air balloon rises?

records.english: The battery factory recycles old cells to recover the metals inside them.
records.zomi: Battery factory in battery lui te sung-a sik te a ngah kik nadingin a recycle hi.

records.english: The cook added salt to the water, which made it boil at a slightly higher temperature.
records.zomi: An huanpa in tui sungah cii a koih a, tua in degree tawmno sang zaw-in a lum sak hi.

records.english: The baker explained how heat makes bread rise in the oven.
records.zomi: Moh huanpa in an huanna meikhuk sungah lumna in moh bangci-in a khangsak hiam cih a gen hi.

records.zomi: Mawtaw' engine in chemical thahatna kitawnna-in a khek hi, ci-in mawtaw bawlphatpa in a gen hi.

records.english: Chefs know that copper pans heat up faster than steel ones.
records.zomi: An huanpa te in sumpi beel te steel beel sangin a hun zaw-in a lum hi, cih a thei uh hi.

records.english: Our science teacher used a pendulum to show energy changing from one form to another.
records.zomi: I science saya in thahatna lam khat pan lam dang ah a kikhel zia lak nadingin pendulum khat a zang hi.

records.english: Engineers designing spacecraft must protect them from extreme heat on their return to Earth.

records.english: Can we test which material makes the best insulation for a lunch box?
records.zomi: Sun an bawm adingin bang vanzat in lumna a kem pen hiam cih i sit thei ding hiam?

records.english: Shall we repeat the experiment to check our results?
records.zomi: I gah te en nadingin experiment i bawl kik ding hiam?

records.english: How does the factory reuse the heat from its ovens?
records.zomi: Factory in a an huanna meikhuk te pan lumna bangci-in a zang kik hiam?

records.english: Pipes carry the hot air to warm the offices in winter.
records.zomi: Phalbi-in office te lumsak nadingin tuikhau te in huih lum a pua hi.

records.english: The quality inspector checks that the steel can handle very high temperatures.
records.zomi: Hoihna entupa in steel in lum-vot sang mahmah a thuak zo hiam cih a en hi.

records.english: A vacuum flask keeps drinks hot by stopping heat from escaping.
records.zomi: Vacuum flask in lumna a pawt loh nadingin a khawlsak-in dawn te a lum sak hi.

records.english: The workers in the foundry pour molten iron into moulds.
records.zomi: Sik tuisakna mun-a nasemte in a tui sik pen bawmna te sungah a sung uh hi.

records.english: The students recorded how long each ice cube took to melt in different places.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte in mun tuamtuam ah tuikhal tang khatciat a tui dingin bangzah a sawt hiam cih a ciamteh uh hi.

records.english: Our school saved energy by fitting sensors that switch off the lights in empty rooms.
records.zomi: I sang in mi om lo inndan te-a meivak a phiat sensor te koih-in thahatna a kem hi.

records.english: The power station burns gas to heat water and make steam.
records.zomi: Meivak bawlna mun in tui sasak-in tui huih bawl nadingin gas a hal hi.

records.english: What happens to the metal when the welder heats it?
records.zomi: Sik zompa in a sasak ciangin sik bang a suak hiam?

records.english: It melts at the joint and then hardens as it cools, joining the two pieces.
records.zomi: A kizopna ah a tui a, a vot ciangin a khauh kik a, kikhen nih a kizom hi.

records.english: Thank you for helping me set up the experiment.
records.zomi: Experiment koih nadingin hong huh manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: Students, put on your safety glasses before you light the burner.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte, burner na hal ma-un bitna mitlimlang bulh un.

records.english: Is steam a liquid or a gas?
records.zomi: Tui huih pen tui hiam, gas hiam?

records.english: How did you find a free tutor for your son?
records.zomi: Na tapa adingin man om lo tutor bangci-in na mu hiam?

records.english: The library keeps a list of volunteers who help with homework.
records.zomi: Laibu inn in inn-a sin ding huh thalawpte' ciamtehna khat a kem hi.

records.english: Please tell your grandmother about the free hearing tests at the health centre.
records.zomi: Damna inn ah man om lo bil za enna tawh kisai na pi kiangah gen in.

records.english: The council gave our family a free compost bin when we moved in.
records.zomi: I tai ciangin council in i innkuan man om lo leinin bawm khat hong pia hi.

records.english: The school told us about a charity that pays for children's music lessons.
records.zomi: Sang in naupangte' la sinna man a pia charity khat tawh kisai hong gen hi.

records.english: Our cousin volunteers at the toy library, so she knows all the best games.
records.zomi: I sanggam in lawhna van laibu inn ah thalawp a sem ahih manin kimawlna hoih pen khempeuh a thei hi.

records.english: Let's look at the council website to see what's on for families this half-term.
records.zomi: Hih tawlngakni tomno sung-in innkuante adingin bang a om hiam cih council website ah i en ni.

records.english: Is there free parking near the clinic for parents with prams?
records.zomi: Naungek tolhna nei nu leh pate adingin damdawi inn neu kiangah man om lo mawtaw khawlna a om hiam?

records.english: My parents learned about online banking at a free workshop run by the bank.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in bank in a bawl man om lo workshop khat ah online banking a sin uh hi.

records.english: Shall we ask the library about the free coding club for the kids?
records.zomi: Naupangte adingin man om lo coding club tawh kisai laibu inn i dong ding hiam?

records.english: Can we take the old bicycles to the repair workshop?
records.zomi: Siiksakol lui te bawlphatna inn ah i paipih thei ding hiam?

records.english: My uncle gets help with his gas bill from an energy charity.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in thahatna charity khat pan a gas sum piak ding adingin huhna a ngah hi.

records.english: Local services helped us more than we expected when Dad came home from hospital.
records.zomi: Pa damdawi inn pan inn a ciah ciangin a mun huhna te in i lamen sangin hong huh tam zaw hi.

records.english: Does the council collect old furniture?
records.zomi: Council in van lui te a kaikhawm hiam?

records.english: Yes, but you have to book a collection online and pay a small fee.
records.zomi: Kaikhawm hi, ahi zongin online-in kaikhawm hun na koih khol a, man neuno na pia kul hi.

records.english: Thanks to the free legal advice, we finally understood our rights as tenants.
records.zomi: Man om lo thukham thuhilhna hangin a tawp-in inn luah mite' thuneihna i theisiam uh hi.

records.english: Grandpa learned about the free bus pass only after his friend mentioned it.
records.zomi: A lawm in a gen khit ciang bek-in Pu in man om lo bus pass tawh kisai a thei hi.

records.english: When my husband lost his job, the job centre helped him find a training course.
records.zomi: Ka pasal in a nasep a mansuah ciangin nasep office in training sinna khat a muh nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Do you know where the nearest bottle bank is?
records.zomi: A nai pen um koihna bawm koi-ah a om hiam cih na thei hiam?

records.english: My brother found a free counselling service after his divorce.
records.zomi: Ka u pasal in a kikhen khit ciangin man om lo thuhilhtu nasep khat a mu hi.

records.english: My sister joined a free walking group for new mothers.
records.zomi: Ka u numei in nu thakte adingin man om lo kalna pawl khat ah a kihel hi.

records.english: The library's free museum passes let our family visit places we could never have afforded.
records.zomi: Laibu inn' man om lo museum lakkhak te in i innkuan i man piak zawh loh ding mun te veh dingin hong phal hi.

records.english: We never knew the park had free cooking classes until our neighbour invited us.
records.zomi: I inn veng in hong sam mateng huan lian in man om lo an huan class a nei hi, cih i thei kei uh hi.

records.english: When the baby was born, the health visitor told us about every local group for parents.
records.zomi: Naungek a suah ciangin damna vehpa in nu leh pate adingin a mun pawl khempeuh hong gen hi.

records.english: My aunt picks up free wood chips from the council depot for her garden.
records.zomi: Ka ni in a huan adingin council khawlna inn pan man om lo sing tan neuno te a la hi.

records.english: We asked the council whether there was any help with insulating our old house.
records.zomi: I inn lui lum-a kem nadingin huhna a om hiam ci-in council i dong uh hi.

records.english: We found a second-hand school uniform shop through the parents' group.
records.zomi: Nu leh pate' pawl tungtawnin sang uniform luina sumbuk khat i mu uh hi.

records.english: Who should we ask about a free car seat check?
records.zomi: Man om lo mawtaw naupang tutna enna tawh kisai kua i dong ding hiam?

records.english: My parents use the free English conversation café at the library.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in laibu inn-a man om lo English kihopihna cafe a zang uh hi.

records.english: Grandma goes to a free singing group for people with breathing problems.
records.zomi: Pi in hu lak haksatna nei mite adingin man om lo la sa pawl khat ah a pai hi.

records.english: We learned about the free fireworks display from the town's newsletter.
records.zomi: Khuapi' newsletter pan man om lo meipuak lakna tawh kisai i thei uh hi.

records.english: We spent a rainy Saturday at the free science centre with the children.
records.zomi: Guah zuk Kiginni khat naupangte tawh man om lo science inn lian ah i zang uh hi.

records.english: The children's centre runs free baby massage classes on Wednesdays.
records.zomi: Naupang inn lian in Nilai ni simin man om lo naungek ziau class a bawl hi.

records.english: Our family takes our extra garden fruit to the community fridge.
records.zomi: I innkuan in i huan-a theigah beh te khuasung fridge ah i paipih uh hi.

records.english: Shall we keep a list of useful local phone numbers on the fridge, as Mum does?
records.zomi: Nu bangin fridge tungah a mun phone nambat phattuam te ciamtehna khat i kem ding hiam?

records.english: The local radio station announces free events for families every Friday.
records.zomi: A mun radio in Laithai ni simin innkuante adingin man om lo kikhopna te a theisak hi.

records.english: Since we moved here, the neighbours have shown us every useful service in town.
records.zomi: Hih mun ah i tai khit pan inn vengte in khuapi-a huhna phattuam khempeuh hong lak uh hi.

records.english: Mum found out about the free health check from a leaflet at the pharmacy.
records.zomi: Damdawi zuakna mun-a laikhak neu khat pan Nu in man om lo damna enna tawh kisai a thei hi.

records.english: My daughter borrowed a violin from the music service instead of buying one.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in lei sangin la nasep pan violin khat a leiba hi.

records.english: When our son needed glasses, the school nurse told us where to get them cheaply.
records.zomi: I tapa in mitlimlang a kisap ciangin sang nurse in koi-ah man neu-in i ngah thei hiam cih hong gen hi.

records.english: Can Grandpa get his flu jab at the local pharmacy?
records.zomi: Pu in a mun damdawi zuakna mun ah flu kidawnna damdawi a ngah thei hiam?
