records.zomi: Thei hi, tua-ah kimuhna hun zong a kisam kei hi.

records.english: Our son uses the free gym at the youth centre after school.
records.zomi: I tapa in sang khit ciangin khangno inn lian-a man om lo gym a zang hi.

records.english: Mum never used local services until a neighbour took her along to the over-sixties club.
records.zomi: Inn veng khat in kum 60 val pawl ah a paipih mateng Nu in a mun huhna a zang ngei kei hi.

records.english: Who told you about the free swimming lessons?
records.zomi: Man om lo tuipeek sinna tawh kisai kua in hong gen hiam?

records.english: Another mum at the school gate, while we were waiting for the children.
records.zomi: Sang kongpi ah naupangte i ngak lai-un nu dang khat in.

records.english: We took Grandpa's old wheelchair to a charity that repairs and lends them.
records.zomi: Pu' wheelchair lui pen a bawlphat a, a leibatsak charity khat ah i paipih uh hi.

records.english: Is there anywhere we can borrow a high chair for the cousins' visit?
records.zomi: Sanggamte' vehna adingin naupang tutphah sang khat i leiba theihna mun khat a om hiam?

records.english: The baby bank at the children's centre lends them for free.
records.zomi: Naupang inn lian-a naungek van kemna in man om lo-in a leibatsak hi.

records.english: My wife takes our son to the free speech therapy group at the clinic.
records.zomi: Ka zi in damdawi inn neu-a man om lo pau gen kisinna pawl ah i tapa a paipih hi.

records.english: Is there a free place nearby where the children can play football?
records.zomi: Naupangte in football a kimawl theih ding kiang-a man om lo mun khat a om hiam?

records.english: We borrowed a pressure washer from the tool library to clean the patio.
records.zomi: Inn-a lei siangsak nadingin vanzat laibu inn pan huih-tui hat seh khat i leiba uh hi.

records.english: My grandmother collects her free prescriptions from the pharmacy on the corner.
records.zomi: Ka pi in lampi kikawm-a damdawi zuakna mun pan a man om lo damdawi te a la hi.

records.english: We found a free summer camp for the children through the council's website.
records.zomi: Council website tungtawnin naupangte adingin man om lo khal camp khat i mu uh hi.

records.english: Our neighbour told us about a dentist who treats children for free.
records.zomi: I inn veng in naupangte man om lo-in a damsak ha siavuan khat tawh kisai hong gen hi.

records.english: Our family has grown vegetables on a rented allotment for ten years.
records.zomi: I innkuan in kum sawm sung luah huan khat ah anteh a suan hi.

records.english: Using local resources has helped our family save money and meet new people.
records.zomi: A mun vanzat te zang in i innkuan sum kem leh mi thak kimuh dingin a huh hi.

records.english: A volunteer from the church drives my mother to her eye appointments.
records.zomi: Pawlpi pan thalawp khat in ka nu a mit kimuhna ah mawtaw tawh a paipih hi.

records.english: Without the local food co-op, our weekly shopping would cost much more.
records.zomi: A mun an kihawm sumbuk om lo hileh i kal sung van lei a man tam zaw mahmah ding hi.

records.english: Our family uses the free tennis courts in the park every Sunday.
records.zomi: I innkuan in Nipini simin huan lian-a man om lo tennis mun te a zang hi.

records.english: How was your wedding different from your parents' wedding?
records.zomi: Na mopawi na nu leh pa' mopawi tawh bangci-in a kibang lo hiam?

records.english: Theirs lasted three days in the village, while ours was one evening in a hall.
records.zomi: Amaute' mopawi khua ah ni thum a sau a, kote' mopawi inn lian khat ah nitak khat ahi hi.

records.english: Children in our family used to start working at 12, but now they study until 20 or more.
records.zomi: I innkuan-a naupangte kum 12-in na a sem kipan zel uh a, tu-in kum 20 ahi zongin a val dong a kisin uh hi.

records.english: Our son's first phone cost less than my father's first radio, in today's money.
records.zomi: Tu-a sum tawh i tapa' phone masa pen ka pa' radio masa pen sangin a man a neu zaw hi.

records.english: Grandma learned to cook from her mother, while my daughter learns from online videos.
records.zomi: Pi in a nu pan an huan a sin a, ka tanu in online video te pan a sin hi.

records.english: My daughter shares the housework with her husband, which my grandfather finds very strange.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in a pasal tawh inn nasep a kihawm a, tua pen ka pu in lamdang a sa mahmah hi.

records.english: Grandpa says that children used to respect their teachers more, but I'm not so sure.
records.zomi: Nidang-in naupangte in a sayate a zahtak zaw uh hi, ci-in Pu in a gen a, ahi zongin ka thei kip kei hi.

records.english: Doesn't Grandpa's advice about money still make sense today?
records.zomi: Sum tawh kisai Pu' thuhilhna tu-in zong a kilawm lai hi lo hiam?

records.english: Did Grandpa ever learn to use a computer?
records.zomi: Pu in computer zat a sin ngei hiam?

records.english: Yes, at 70, and now he sends us emails every morning.
records.zomi: Sin hi, kum 70-in, tu-in zingsang simin email hong khak hi.

records.english: Did the whole family really sleep in one room in Mum's village?
records.zomi: Nu' khua ah innkuan bup inndan khat ah a ihmu taktak uh hiam?

records.english: My grandmother had her first child at 19, in the same room where she had been born.
records.zomi: Ka pi in kum 19-in a ta masa pen amah a suahna inndan kibang ah a nei hi.

records.english: My mother had me at 30, in a hospital in the city.
records.zomi: Ka nu in kum 30-in khuapi-a damdawi inn ah kei hong nei hi.

records.english: I'm 35 and still not sure whether I want children at all.
records.zomi: Kum 35 ka cing a, ta neih ka deih hiam cih ka thei kip nai kei hi.

records.english: Living longer has given my grandparents time with their great-grandchildren.
records.zomi: Sawt zaw-a nuntak in ka pu leh pi te a tu' tate tawh hun a pia hi.

records.english: My parents grew up with very little, which is why they never waste food.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa tawmno tawh a khang uh ahih manin an a paai ngei kei uh hi.

records.english: Each generation in our family has moved a little further from the village.
records.zomi: I innkuan-a khangthu khatciat khua pan tawmno-in a gamla zaw-in a tai uh hi.

records.english: Grandma used to make all our clothes, but now we buy them online.
records.zomi: Nidang-in Pi in i puan khempeuh a khui a, tu-in online-in i lei uh hi.

records.english: Why did people in Grandpa's time marry so young?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pu' hun-in mite a khangno lai-un a kiteen uh hiam?

records.english: Our children call their grandparents every day, something my parents could never do with theirs.
records.zomi: I tate in ni simin a pu leh pi te a sam uh a, tua pen ka nu leh ka pa in a pu leh pi te tawh a bawl thei ngei lo ahi hi.

records.english: Why does Grandma still save every plastic bag?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pi in plastic ip khempeuh a kem lai hiam?

records.english: She grew up when nothing was ever thrown away.
records.zomi: Bangmah kipaai lo hun-in a khang hi.

records.english: My grandparents walked to church every Sunday, while we drive five minutes.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh pi te in Nipini simin pawlpi ah a kal uh a, kote in minit nga mawtaw i tawl uh hi.

records.english: Shall we ask Grandpa how he learned to fix everything himself?
records.zomi: Bangkhempeuh amah mahin bangci-in bawlphat a sin hiam ci-in Pu i dong ding hiam?

records.english: When did your parents buy their first fridge?
records.zomi: Na nu leh pa in a fridge masa pen bang ciangin a lei uh hiam?

records.english: When I tell my children about my childhood, they think I'm describing another planet.
records.zomi: Ka naupan lai tawh kisai ka tate kiangah ka gen ciangin leitung dang khat ka gen bang-in a sa uh hi.

records.english: Is it true that you had to share one pair of shoes with your brother, Grandpa?
records.zomi: Pu, na u pasal ahi zongin nau pasal tawh khedap kibang na kihawm kul hi, cih a dik hiam?

records.english: My grandparents had eight children, but my parents had only two.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh pi te in ta giat a nei uh a, ahi zongin ka nu leh ka pa in nih bek a nei uh hi.

records.english: The way we celebrate birthdays has changed completely since my parents were children.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa a naupan lai-un pan i suahni lungdampih zia a kikhel vek hi.

records.english: When my father was young, a doctor visited the village only once a month.
records.zomi: Ka pa a khangno lai-in siavuan khat kha khat ah khatvei bek khua ah a hong hi.

records.english: My daughter wants to learn the old songs that my mother knows.
records.zomi: Ka nu' theih la lui te ka tanu in sin a deih hi.

records.english: Dad walked an hour to school each way, and my children complain about a ten-minute bus ride.
records.zomi: Pa sang ah lam khat ah nai khat a kal a, ka tate in minit sawm bus tuang a phun uh hi.

records.english: Dad writes with a fountain pen, I type, and my son talks to his phone.
records.zomi: Pa in fountain pen tawh a gelh a, kei in ka type a, ka tapa in a phone kiangah a gen hi.

records.english: Grandpa's generation worked with their hands, while mine works mostly with screens.
records.zomi: Pu' khangthu in a khut tawh na a sem uh a, kei' khangthu in a tamzaw screen tawh na a sem uh hi.

records.english: Dad worked for the same company for forty years, but I've had five jobs already.
records.zomi: Pa in company kibang ah kum sawmli na a sem a, ahi zongin kei in nasep nga ka nei khin hi.

records.english: Will our grandchildren laugh at our phones the way we laugh at Grandpa's radio?
records.zomi: I tute in Pu' radio i nuihsan bangin i phone te a nuihsan ding uh hiam?

records.english: Do your children know what a typewriter is?
records.zomi: Na tate in typewriter bang ahi hiam cih a thei uh hiam?

records.english: Could you live without the internet, like Grandma did?
records.zomi: Pi bangin internet om lo-in na nungta thei ding hiam?

records.english: Fewer young people in our family farm the land now.
records.zomi: Tu-in i innkuan-a khangno tawm zaw in lou a bawl uh hi.

records.english: What job did your father do when he was young?
records.zomi: Na pa a khangno lai-in bang nasep a sem hiam?

records.english: He drove a bullock cart to the market, long before there were lorries in the village.
records.zomi: Khua ah mawtaw lian te a om ma sawt-in sumbuk ah bawngtal leeng a tawl hi.

records.english: In Grandma's day, girls in her village rarely went to secondary school.
records.zomi: Pi' hun-in a khua-a nungakte sang lian ah a pai tawm mahmah uh hi.

records.english: Our family used to eat together every night, but now everyone's schedules are different.
records.zomi: I innkuan in zan simin khawm-in an i ne zel uh a, ahi zongin tu-in mi khempeuh' hun ciamtehna a kibang kei hi.

records.english: Thank you for telling us how things were when you were young, Grandma.
records.zomi: Pi, na khangno lai-in thu te bang ci hiam cih hong gen manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: Our children speak English better than our own language, which worries their grandparents.
records.zomi: I tate in i pau sangin English a gen siam zaw uh a, tua in a pu leh pi te a lungkhamsak hi.

records.english: Mum washed clothes by hand when she was young, but now the machine does it.
records.zomi: Nu a khangno lai-in puan khut tawh a sawp a, tu-in seh in a sawp hi.

records.english: Auntie Lun was the first woman in our family to have her own bank account.
records.zomi: Ni Lun pen i innkuan-a amah bank account nei numei masa pen ahi hi.

records.english: Mum had to ask her father's permission to get married.
records.zomi: Nu in kiteen dingin a pa' phalna a ngen kul hi.

records.english: Mum says that we have more things but less time than her generation had.
records.zomi: A khangthu sangin van tam zaw i nei uh a, hun tawm zaw i nei uh hi, ci-in Nu in a gen hi.

records.english: Our son laughed when Grandpa showed him how to dial a number on the old phone.
records.zomi: Pu in phone lui tungah nambat bangci-in nek ding cih a lak ciangin i tapa a nui hi.

records.english: Grandpa paid for everything in cash, while my son pays with his phone.
records.zomi: Pu in bangkhempeuh sum lai tawh a pia a, ka tapa in a phone tawh a pia hi.

records.english: My grandmother never travelled abroad, but my daughter has studied in two countries.
records.zomi: Ka pi gamdang ah a khualzin ngei kei a, ahi zongin ka tanu gam nih ah a kisin khin hi.

records.english: Dad remembers when the village got its first television, and everyone came to watch it.
records.zomi: Khua in a television masa pen a ngah a, mi khempeuh en dingin a hong uh hun Pa in a phawk hi.

records.english: Today my children choose their own friends, their own careers and their own partners.
records.zomi: Tu-in ka tate in amau lawm, amau nasepna leh amau kiteen pih te amau mahin a teel uh hi.

records.english: My grandparents wrote letters to each other for two years before they married.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh pi te a kiteen ma-un kum nih laikhak a kigelh tuah uh hi.

records.english: Why does Grandpa still prefer a paper newspaper to the news on his phone?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pu in a phone tunga thuthak sangin lai-ek thuthak laipi a deih zaw lai hiam?

records.english: Did families in Dad's time really save for years to buy a bicycle?
records.zomi: Pa' hun-a innkuante in siiksakol lei nadingin kum tampi sum a kem taktak uh hiam?

records.english: Grandma, what did you do for fun when you were my age?
records.zomi: Pi, ka kum bang na hih lai-in nuam nadingin bang na bawl hiam?

records.english: We made dolls from corn husks and held races along the river bank.
records.zomi: Vaimim hawng tawh dawl lim i bawl uh a, lui gei dung ah tai kidemna i nei uh hi.

records.english: Grandma's recipes have changed slightly with every cook who has made them.
records.zomi: Pi' an huanzia te a huan an huanpa khatciat tawh tawmno a kikhel hi.

records.english: The old marriage register showed that my grandparents' witnesses were their best friends.
records.zomi: Kiteenna ciamtehna lui in ka pu leh pi te' teci te a lawm hoih pen te ahi hi, cih a lak hi.

records.english: The church records show that my grandparents were married on a rainy Tuesday.
records.zomi: Pawlpi ciamtehna te in ka pu leh pi te guah zuk Pithai ni khat-in a kiteen uh hi, cih a lak hi.

records.english: Auntie Hoih traced our family to a village we had never heard of, using old public records.
records.zomi: Ni Hoih in mipi ciamtehna lui te zang-in i zak ngeih loh khua khat ah i innkuan a zui hi.

records.english: Our son's school asked for his birth record before he could start.
records.zomi: I tapa a kipat ma-in a sang in a suahna ciamtehna a ngen hi.

records.english: The registry office sent us my grandmother's birth record within a week.
records.zomi: Ciamtehna office in kal khat sung-in ka pi' suahna ciamtehna hong khak hi.

records.english: Can we look at the old photographs in the archive?
records.zomi: Tangthu kemna mun-a photo lui te i en thei ding hiam?

records.english: Where does Mum keep her parents' registration papers?
records.zomi: Nu in a nu leh pa' ciamtehna lai te koi-ah a kem hiam?

records.english: Please bring Grandpa's identity card when we go to the record office.
records.zomi: Ciamtehna office ah i pai ciangin Pu' mi hihna card paipih in.

records.english: The clerk said that my great-grandfather's records were in a different district.
records.zomi: Nasempa in ka pu' pa' ciamtehna te district dang ah a om hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Shall we visit the archive to look for Great-grandpa's army records?
records.zomi: Pu' pa' galkap ciamtehna te zong dingin tangthu kemna mun i veh ding hiam?

records.english: Grandma cried when she saw her mother's signature in the old register.
records.zomi: Ciamtehna lui sungah a nu' min gelhna a muh ciangin Pi a kap hi.

records.english: Some records about our family are kept in the capital, so we'll visit them in the summer.
records.zomi: I innkuan tawh kisai ciamtehna khenkhat khuapi lian ah a kikem ahih manin khal-in i veh ding hi.

records.english: Grandpa can't believe that anyone can now see the village records online.
records.zomi: Tu-in kuapeuh in online-in khua ciamtehna te a mu thei uh hi, cih Pu in a um zo kei hi.

records.english: Mum needed three certified copies of Grandpa's will for the bank, the council and the lawyer.
records.zomi: Bank, council leh thukham siam adingin Nu in Pu' gamluah lai kipsakna kopi thum a kisam hi.

records.english: We discovered from the records that two of my great-uncles had emigrated.
records.zomi: Ka pu' u pasal ahi zongin nau pasal nih gamdang ah a tai uh hi, cih ciamtehna te pan i thei uh hi.

records.english: Our family's records were lost when the old town hall burned down.
records.zomi: Khuapi office lui a kan ciangin i innkuan' ciamtehna te a mang hi.

records.english: Do you know when Grandpa's birth was registered?
records.zomi: Pu' suahna bang ciangin a kiciamteh hiam cih na thei hiam?

records.english: Mum found her own baptism in the church book, signed by a priest she still remembers.
records.zomi: Nu in pawlpi laibu sungah amah baptaizna, a phawk lai siampi khat' min gelhna tawh a mu hi.

records.english: We looked up the history of our street in the town archive.
records.zomi: Khuapi tangthu kemna ah i lampi tangthu i en uh hi.

records.english: According to the court records, my grandfather won the case about the boundary.
records.zomi: Thukhenna ciamtehna te bangin ka pu in gamgi tawh kisai thu a zo hi.

records.english: How did you find out who built our house?
records.zomi: I inn kua in a lam hiam cih bangci-in na thei hiam?

records.english: The council archive had the original building plans with the builder's name on them.
records.zomi: Council tangthu kemna in inn lampa' min tawh inn lamna ciamtehna bulpi te a nei hi.

records.english: Dad keeps a copy of every public record that mentions our family.
records.zomi: Pa in i innkuan a gen mipi ciamtehna khempeuh' kopi a kem hi.

records.english: When we sold Grandma's house, the lawyer checked every record of who had owned it.
records.zomi: Pi' inn i zuak ciangin thukham siam in kua in a nei ngei hiam cih ciamtehna khempeuh a en hi.

records.english: Dad requested his medical records when he moved to a new doctor.
records.zomi: Pa in siavuan thak kiangah a tai ciangin a damdawi ciamtehna te a ngen hi.

records.english: The archive clerk helped my son find his grandfather's school reports.
records.zomi: Tangthu kemna nasempa in ka tapa a pu' sang report te a muh nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Can anyone see our family's records at the registry office?
records.zomi: Ciamtehna office ah i innkuan' ciamtehna te kuapeuh in a mu thei uh hiam?

records.english: Only some of them, and the rest need proof that you're a relative.
records.zomi: A khenkhat bek, a dang te adingin sanggam na hihna kipsakna na kisam hi.

records.english: Who in the family knows how to search the online archive?
records.zomi: Innkuan sung-ah online tangthu kemna bangci-in zong ding cih kua in a thei hiam?

records.english: Grandma's name appears in the council minutes from 1965, when she asked for a new well.
records.zomi: Tuikhuk thak a ngetna 1965 kum-a council kikhopna ciamtehna sungah Pi' min a om hi.

records.english: Old records proved that the path through our field had always been public.
records.zomi: Ciamtehna lui te in i lou kal lampi pen tawntung-in mipi lampi ahi hi, cih a kipsak hi.

records.english: Dad keeps asking the archive whether they have found his brother's records yet.
records.zomi: A u pasal ahi zongin nau pasal' ciamtehna te a mu khin uh hiam ci-in Pa in tangthu kemna mun a dong den hi.

records.english: Our son was amazed to see his great-grandfather's handwriting in the register.
records.zomi: Ciamtehna laibu sungah a pu' pa' laigelhzia a muh ciangin i tapa lamdang a sa mahmah hi.

records.english: Is our land properly registered?
records.zomi: I gam dik takin a kiciamteh hiam?

records.english: Yes, Grandpa registered it after the family argument in 1998.
records.zomi: Kiciamteh hi, 1998 kum-a innkuan kitelna khit ciangin Pu in a ciamteh hi.

records.english: Our village's baptism records go back over a hundred years.
records.zomi: I khua' baptaizna ciamtehna te kum za val a sawt khin hi.

records.english: My cousin found our great-grandmother's name in an old school register.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam in sang ciamtehna lui khat sungah i pu' nu' min a mu hi.

records.english: Our family discovered a great-aunt we had never known about in the census.
records.zomi: Census sungah i theih ngeih loh i pu' nu ahi zongin pi' u numei khat i innkuan in a mu hi.

records.english: My sister spent a whole afternoon searching the land records for our grandfather's field.
records.zomi: Ka u numei in i pu' lou zong dingin gam ciamtehna te sungah nitak lam bup a zang hi.

records.english: Let's keep a notebook of every archive we've visited and what we found.
records.zomi: I veh ngeih tangthu kemna mun khempeuh leh i muh te ciamtehna laibu khat i kem ni.

records.english: My wife was relieved to find her father's citizenship record after years of searching.
records.zomi: Kum tampi zon khit ciangin a pa' gam mi hihna ciamtehna a muh ciangin ka zi a lungdam hi.

records.english: Why do you need a copy of your parents' marriage certificate?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na nu leh pa' kiteenna lai-ciam kopi na kisam hiam?

records.english: The bank wants it before they'll transfer the house into Mum's name.
records.zomi: Inn Nu' min ah a khek ma-un bank in tua a deih hi.

records.english: My daughter used old newspapers in the library for her family history project.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in a innkuan tangthu project adingin laibu inn-a thuthak laipi lui te a zang hi.

records.english: Uncle Thang asked the archive to send copies of the village land map.
records.zomi: Pa neu Thang in khua gam map kopi te khak dingin tangthu kemna mun a ngen hi.

records.english: Did you know that our house was once owned by the village doctor?
records.zomi: I inn nidang-in khua siavuan' inn ahi hi, cih na thei hiam?

records.english: Where can we find Great-grandpa's birth record?
records.zomi: Pu' pa' suahna ciamtehna koi-ah i mu thei ding hiam?

records.english: Probably in the church register in his home village.
records.zomi: A khua bul-a pawlpi ciamtehna laibu sungah a om kha ding hi.

records.english: Our family tree has a gap where the records were lost during the war.
records.zomi: Gal lai-in ciamtehna te a mang manin i innkuan suahna lam ah mun awng khat a om hi.

records.english: Our family name is written three different ways in the old records.
records.zomi: Ciamtehna lui te ah i innkuan min lam tuam thum-in a kigelh hi.

records.english: We printed the old record and framed it for Grandma's birthday.
records.zomi: Ciamtehna lui i print uh a, Pi' suahni adingin bawm tawh i koih uh hi.

records.english: Dad was surprised to find his own birth registered under a different name.
records.zomi: Amah suahna min dang tawh a kiciamteh a muh ciangin Pa lamdang a sa hi.

records.english: What did you find in the old records, Mum?
records.zomi: Nu, ciamtehna lui te sungah bang na mu hiam?

records.english: Records from my grandparents' village were handwritten in beautiful, faded ink.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh pi te' khua pan ciamtehna te ink hoih leh kang khin tawh khut-in a kigelh hi.

records.english: The records showed that our school was built on land donated by a local family.
records.zomi: I sang pen a mun innkuan khat in a piak gam tungah a kilam hi, ci-in ciamtehna te in a lak hi.

records.english: The records gave us the date, but only Grandma's stories gave us the rest.
records.zomi: Ciamtehna te in ni hong pia a, ahi zongin a dang te Pi' tangthu te bek in hong pia hi.

records.english: My brother asked for a copy of his school records before applying to university.
records.zomi: University a ngen ma-in ka u pasal in a sang ciamtehna kopi khat a ngen hi.

records.english: Public records helped our family prove that we had lived in the town for decades.
records.zomi: Mipi ciamtehna te in i innkuan kum sawm tampi khuapi ah a teng hi, cih kipsak nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: How much does it cost to get a copy of a birth record?
records.zomi: Suahna ciamtehna kopi khat ngah nadingin bangzah a man hiam?

records.english: My cousin is putting all our family's records into one online file.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam in i innkuan ciamtehna khempeuh online file khat sungah a koih hi.

records.english: Grandpa forgets what he ate for breakfast, but he never forgets a story from his childhood.
records.zomi: Pu in zingsang an a nek a mangngilh a, ahi zongin a naupan lai tangthu khat zong a mangngilh ngei kei hi.

records.english: Why do the elders tell the same stories every year?
records.zomi: Bang hangin upate in kum simin tangthu kibang a gen uh hiam?

records.english: They say that a story told only once is easily lost.
records.zomi: Khatvei bek-a kigen tangthu khat a mang baih hi, a ci uh hi.

records.english: The best storytellers in our family can make everyone laugh and cry in the same evening.
records.zomi: I innkuan-a tangthu gen siam pen te in nitak khat sung-in mi khempeuh a nuisak a, a kapsak thei uh hi.

records.english: When an old person dies, many stories die with them, my father says.
records.zomi: Mi upa khat a sih ciangin tangthu tampi amah tawh a si hi, ka pa in a ci hi.

records.english: My aunt writes down the stories in our own language, word for word.
records.zomi: Ka ni in i pau tawh tangthu te kammal khat ciat-in a gelh hi.

records.english: The village elders meet every month to share stories with the young people.
records.zomi: Khua upate in khangnote tawh tangthu kihawm dingin kha simin a kikhop uh hi.

records.english: We keep the recordings on a memory stick in Dad's locked drawer.
records.zomi: Khumna te Pa' khak theih dawh sung-a memory stick khat ah i kem uh hi.

records.english: Write the date and the storyteller's name on every recording.
records.zomi: Khumna khempeuh ah ni leh tangthu genpa' min gelh in.

records.english: Each storyteller adds small details, so no two versions of a story are exactly the same.
records.zomi: Tangthu gen mi khatciat in thu neuno te a beh uh ahih manin tangthu khat' kigen zia nih a kibang dik ngei kei hi.

records.english: My little brother asks Grandpa for the same story every night.
records.zomi: Ka nau pasal in zan simin tangthu kibang Pu a ngen hi.

records.english: Who told you this story when you were young?
records.zomi: Na neu lai-in hih tangthu kua in hong gen hiam?

records.english: Let's record the stories in our own language first and translate them later.
records.zomi: Tangthu te i pau tawh a masa-in i khum ni, a nungin i let ding hi.

records.english: Some stories are only told at special times of the year in our village.
records.zomi: I khua ah tangthu khenkhat kum khat-a hun tuam te-in bek kigen hi.

records.english: Can you tell the story again so that I can write it down?
records.zomi: Ka gelh theih nadingin tangthu na gen kik thei ding hiam?

records.english: Our family keeps a notebook of the stories the elders tell at weddings.
records.zomi: I innkuan in mopawi te-ah upate' gen tangthu te' ciamtehna laibu khat a kem hi.

records.english: We listen to the old recordings together at Christmas.
records.zomi: Christmas-in khumna lui te khawm-in i ngai uh hi.

records.english: Can you help me set up the recorder for Grandma?
records.zomi: Pi adingin khumna seh koih dingin hong huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Last summer, my cousin and I visited every old person in our village with a small recorder.
records.zomi: Khal nunung-in ka sanggam leh kei khumna seh neu khat tawh i khua-a mi upa khempeuh i veh uh hi.

records.english: Each of them told us one story they had heard as a child.
records.zomi: Amaute khatciat in naupang a hih lai-un a zak tangthu khat hong gen uh hi.

records.english: By the end of the summer, we had more than forty stories saved for the whole community.
records.zomi: Khal a tawp ciangin khuasung bup adingin tangthu sawmli val i kem uh hi.

records.english: Grandpa laughs when he hears his own voice on the recording.
records.zomi: Khumna sungah amah aw a zak ciangin Pu a nui hi.

records.english: Having heard these stories all my life, I now feel responsible for passing them on.
records.zomi: Ka nuntak sung bup hih tangthu te ka zak khit ciangin tu-in a ma ah ka paipih ding mawhpuakna ka nei hi, ka kisa hi.

records.english: Every family has stories worth saving, even if they seem ordinary.
records.zomi: Innkuan khempeuh in a ngeina bang a kilang zongin kem tham tangthu a nei uh hi.

records.english: Thank you for sharing your memories with us, Grandpa.
records.zomi: Pu, na phawknate kote tawh na hawm manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: Shall we ask Grandma about the year the family moved to the hills?
records.zomi: Innkuan mual ah a tai kum tawh kisai Pi i dong ding hiam?

records.english: If nobody listens to the elders now, their knowledge could be lost forever.
records.zomi: Tu-in kuamah in upate a ngai kei uh leh a theihna uh khangtawn-in a mang thei hi.

records.english: Is it all right if we share your story with the school?
records.zomi: Na tangthu sang tawh i hawm leh a hoih hiam?

records.english: Our pastor asked the oldest members to tell how the church in our village began.
records.zomi: I pastor in a upa pen mite i khua-a pawlpi bangci-in a kipan hiam cih gen dingin a ngen hi.

records.english: Grandpa's stories are the only history of our village that we have.
records.zomi: Pu' tangthu te i khua' i neih tangthu khat bek ahi hi.

records.english: Why are you recording Grandpa's stories?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pu' tangthu te na khum hiam?

records.english: So that our children can hear his voice and his memories one day.
records.zomi: I tate in ni khat ni-in a aw leh a phawknate a zak theih nadingin.

records.english: How do you keep the stories safe?
records.zomi: Tangthu te bangci-in bit takin na kem uh hiam?

records.english: We write them down, record them on a phone and keep copies in two places.
records.zomi: I gelh uh a, phone tungah i khum uh a, mun nih ah kopi te i kem uh hi.

records.english: In our community, some stories belong to a particular family and are not told by others.
records.zomi: I khuasung ah tangthu khenkhat innkuan tuam khat' ahi a, midangte in a gen kei uh hi.

records.english: Old photographs help my grandmother remember stories she had almost forgotten.
records.zomi: Photo lui te in ka pi a mangngilh dek tangthu te a phawk nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Who knows the most about our village's history?
records.zomi: I khua' tangthu kua in a thei tam pen hiam?

records.english: The oldest women, because they remember what their own grandmothers told them.
records.zomi: Numei upa pen te, bang hang hiam cih leh amau pi te in a gen te a phawk uh hi.

records.english: Grandpa remembers the names of seven generations of our family.
records.zomi: Pu in i innkuan' khangthu sagih min a phawk hi.

records.english: My cousin had the old cassette recordings copied onto a computer before they were damaged.
records.zomi: Cassette khumna lui te a sia ma-un ka sanggam in computer tungah a kopi sak hi.

records.english: The young people in our church are collecting stories from the oldest members.
records.zomi: I pawlpi-a khangnote in a upa pen mite pan tangthu a kaikhawm uh hi.

records.english: Our youth group made a short film of the elders telling stories in front of the old church.
records.zomi: I khangno pawl in pawlpi lui maiah upate tangthu a gen film tomno khat a bawl uh hi.

records.english: Mum wrote a small book of Grandpa's stories for his eightieth birthday.
records.zomi: Pu' kum sawmgiat suahni adingin Nu in a tangthu te laibu neu khat a gelh hi.

records.english: Please speak a little louder, Grandma, so that the phone can record you.
records.zomi: Pi, phone in a khum theih nadingin tawmno kiko zaw-in gen in.

records.english: The story of how our village got its name changes a little depending on who tells it.
records.zomi: I khua' a min ngah zia tangthu pen kua in a gen hiam cih tungah tawmno a kikhel hi.

records.english: Can I record you telling the story of how our family came to this valley?
records.zomi: I innkuan hih guam ah bangci-in a hong hiam cih tangthu na gen kong khum thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, but let me tell it slowly, so that I don't forget anything.
records.zomi: Thei hi, ahi zongin bangmah ka mangngilh loh nadingin zawi takin kong gen ding hi.

records.english: Listening to the old stories helps me understand why my parents think the way they do.
records.zomi: Tangthu lui ngaih in bang hangin ka nu leh ka pa tua bangin a ngaihsun uh hiam cih ka theisiam nadingin hong huh hi.

records.english: Grandma says that stories are a way of keeping the dead close to the living.
records.zomi: Tangthu te pen misite nungtate kiangah a kinai sak nading lam khat ahi hi, Pi in a ci hi.

records.english: Children, listen carefully, because one day you will tell these stories to your own children.

records.english: How would a four-day week affect our customers?

records.zomi: Zan nasep hun ah ka tai khit pan ka gil a na den hi.

records.english: The school nurse asked me whether the pain was on the left or the right.
records.zomi: Sang nurse in natna a veilam ah hiam taklam ah hiam ci-in hong dong hi.

records.english: I've been sneezing all week since we moved to the dusty storeroom.
records.zomi: Leivui tam van kemna dan ah i tai khit pan kal bup ka hacip hi.

records.english: I've been feeling anxious and short of breath before every presentation.
records.zomi: Presentation khempeuh ma-in ka lungkham a, ka hu a tom hi.

records.english: Can you tell me exactly where the pain is?
records.zomi: Koi-ah a na hiam cih kician takin hong gen thei ding hiam?

records.english: Do you also get a headache when the office gets too warm?
records.zomi: Office a sat luat ciangin nang zong na lu a na hiam?

records.english: The apprentice said he felt dizzy after working on the roof in the sun.
records.zomi: Ni sat nuai-ah inn tung ah na a sep khit ciangin a lu a mang hi, ci-in na kisin mi in a gen hi.

records.english: Since the new shift pattern started, I've had trouble sleeping.
records.zomi: Nasep hun kikhekna thak a kipat pan hoih takin ka ihmu zo kei hi.

records.english: My hands go numb when I use the drill for too long.
records.zomi: Drill sawt luat ka zat ciangin ka khut a si hi.

records.english: My shoulder hurts every time I lift my arm above my head.
records.zomi: Ka lu tung ah ka ban ka dom simin ka liang a na hi.

records.english: I haven't been able to sleep properly since the accident at the warehouse.
records.zomi: Warehouse-a siatna khit pan hoih takin ka ihmu thei kei hi.

records.english: Please tell your manager if you feel unwell during your shift.
records.zomi: Na nasep hun sung-in na dam kei leh na manager kiangah gen in.

records.english: When did the headaches start?
records.zomi: Lu natna bang ciangin a kipan hiam?

records.english: About two weeks ago, when I started working on the new computer screen.
records.zomi: Kal nih bang ma-in, computer screen thak tungah na ka sep kipat ciangin.

records.english: The student said her stomach hurt, but she didn't have a fever.
records.zomi: Sangnaupang in a gil a na hi a ci a, ahi zongin a cisa kei hi.

records.english: My voice has gone, so I can't take the phone calls today.
records.zomi: Ka aw a mang ahih manin tuni-in phone sapna te ka la thei kei hi.

records.english: I've had a sore throat since I started teaching the big class.
records.zomi: Class lian ka sinsak kipat pan ka kawlok a na hi.

records.english: I can't concentrate in class because my tooth has been hurting since Monday.
records.zomi: Pizing ni pan ka ha a na ahih manin class ah ngaihsut ka kip zo kei hi.

records.english: I felt faint in the meeting, so a colleague brought me some water.
records.zomi: Kikhopna ah ka lu a mang ahih manin nasem pih khat in tui hong paipih hi.

records.english: My throat feels raw after a day of shouting instructions on the building site.
records.zomi: Inn lamna mun ah ni bup thuhilhna kiko khit ciangin ka kawlok a dawi hi.

records.english: The cleaner said the strong chemicals made her eyes water and her throat sore.
records.zomi: Chemical hat te in a mit tui a luangsak a, a kawlok a natsak hi, ci-in siangsakna nasem numei in a gen hi.

records.english: I started coughing a lot after we began working with the new paint.
records.zomi: Sai thak tawh na i sep kipat khit ciangin ka khuk tam mahmah kipan hi.

records.english: Is the itching worse at work or at home?
records.zomi: A thak pen nasepna ah a hat zaw hiam, inn ah hiam?

records.english: The bus driver told the doctor that his back pain was worse in the mornings.
records.zomi: Bus tawlpa in a nungzang natna zingsang-in a hat zaw hi, ci-in siavuan kiangah a gen hi.

records.english: My legs feel heavy after a twelve-hour shift on my feet.
records.zomi: Nai 12 a ding nasep hun khit ciangin ka khe te a gik hi.

records.english: Honesty about symptoms at work can stop a small problem from becoming serious.
records.zomi: Nasepna-a natna lim tawh kisai thuman in haksatna neuno khat a thupi suak lo dingin a khawlsak thei hi.

records.english: My ears were ringing for hours after the noisy machine was switched off.
records.zomi: Ging hat seh a kiphiat khit nai tampi sung ka bil a ging-ging hi.

records.english: My wrist clicks and hurts whenever I use the computer mouse.
records.zomi: Computer mouse ka zat simin ka khut-zang a ging a, a na hi.

records.english: My colleague described the pain in his chest as a heavy weight pressing down.
records.zomi: Ka nasem pih in a awm natna pen gikna gik khat in a ngiat bang hi, ci-in a gen hi.

records.english: The teacher noticed that the boy was rubbing his eyes and squinting at the board.
records.zomi: Tangval neu in a mit a sik a, board a mit tang-tang-in a en hi, cih saya in a mu hi.

records.english: My neck has been stiff ever since we got the new desks.
records.zomi: Taupi thak te i ngah khit pan ka ngawng a khauh den hi.

records.english: The chef burned his hand and said it was throbbing badly.
records.zomi: An huanpa lian in a khut a kang a, a phu-phu-in a na hi, a ci hi.

records.english: I didn't want to make a fuss, but the cut on my finger kept bleeding.
records.zomi: Buaina bawl ka deih kei a, ahi zongin ka khutzung tunga liamna in sisan a luang den hi.

records.english: What does the pain in your wrist feel like?
records.zomi: Na khut-zang natna bang bang hiam?

records.english: It's a dull ache that gets worse after I've been typing for an hour.
records.zomi: Nai khat laimal ka nek khit ciangin a hat zaw natna nem khat ahi hi.

records.english: I'm sorry, but I need to go home, because I have a high temperature.
records.zomi: Maisak in, ka cisa mahmah ahih manin inn ka ciah kul hi.

records.english: Have you had these symptoms before?
records.zomi: Hih natna lim te na nei ngei hiam?

records.english: Only once, during last summer's heatwave, when I was working outside.
records.zomi: Khatvei bek, khal nunung-a ni sa mahmah hun-in pualam ah na ka sep lai-in.

records.english: Do you feel any pain when you bend down to pick things up?
records.zomi: Van domto dingin na kun ciangin natna na nei hiam?

records.english: The nurse asked whether the rash on my hands appeared after I used the cleaning products.
records.zomi: Siangsakna van te ka zat khit ciangin ka khut tunga a phiat a kilang hiam ci-in nurse in hong dong hi.

records.english: The doctor asked whether my symptoms improved when I was on holiday.
records.zomi: Tawlngakni ka om lai-in ka natna lim te a hoih zaw hiam ci-in siavuan in hong dong hi.

records.english: How's your back this morning?
records.zomi: Tu zingsang-in na nungzang bang ci hiam?

records.english: Still stiff from lifting those boxes yesterday.
records.zomi: Zana tua bawm te ka domto manin a khauh lai hi.

records.english: Why did you leave the lesson early?
records.zomi: Bang hangin sinna na paisan hun hiam?

records.english: I felt sick and dizzy, so the teacher sent me to the school nurse.
records.zomi: Ka cina a, ka lu a mang ahih manin saya in sang nurse kiangah hong sawl hi.

records.english: Should I see the nurse about my sore wrist?
records.zomi: Ka khut-zang na tawh kisai nurse ka mu ding hiam?

records.english: The teacher wrote down when the student's breathing problems started and stopped.
records.zomi: Sangnaupang' hu lak haksatna bang ciangin a kipan a, a khawl hiam cih saya in a gelh hi.

records.english: Describe your symptoms in the order they appeared, starting with the first.
records.zomi: Na natna lim te a kilat dan bangin gen inla, a masa pen pan kipan in.

records.english: The farmer described a burning feeling in his eyes after spraying the crops.
records.zomi: Lou bawlpa in suante damdawi a buak khit ciangin a mit a kang bang hi, ci-in a gen hi.

records.english: We walked an hour to school every morning, carrying our lunch in a tin.
records.zomi: Zingsang simin sang ah nai khat i kal uh a, i sun an sik bawm sungah i pua uh hi.

records.english: Why did the whole school sing a song before lessons every morning?
records.zomi: Bang hangin sang bup in zingsang simin sinna ma-in la khat a sa uh hiam?

records.english: Our village teacher taught every subject, from history to football.
records.zomi: I khua saya in tangthu pan football dong laigil khempeuh a sinsak hi.

records.english: Our headmaster knew the name of every child in the school.
records.zomi: I sangpi saya in sang sung-a naupang khempeuh' min a thei hi.

records.english: What do you remember about your first school?
records.zomi: Na sang masa pen tawh kisai bang na phawk hiam?

records.english: It had only two rooms, and we sat on benches made from old planks.
records.zomi: Inndan nih bek a nei a, sing-ek lui pan kibawl tutphah sau tungah i tu uh hi.

records.english: I used to pretend to be a teacher and line up my younger cousins as pupils.
records.zomi: Saya bang-a kibawl-in ka sanggam neu zawte sangnaupang bangin ka kigual sak zel hi.

records.english: I used to help my father in his shop after school, counting the change.
records.zomi: Sang khit ciangin ka pa' sumbuk ah sum ap kik sim-in ka huh zel hi.

records.english: I still remember the smell of chalk in our old classroom.
records.zomi: I sangdan lui-a cak gim ka phawk lai hi.

records.english: My teacher's kind words when I failed a test made me want to try harder.
records.zomi: Test ah ka sun ciangin ka saya' kammal hoih te in a hanciam zaw-in sawm dingin hong deihsak hi.

records.english: Every Friday afternoon, our teacher read us a chapter from an adventure story.
records.zomi: Laithai ni nitak lam simin i saya in hamphatna tangthu khat pan tangthu khen khat hong sim sak hi.

records.english: I was the smallest boy in the class, so I always sat in the front row.
records.zomi: Class sung-a tangval neu a neu pen ka hih manin maiang kigual ah ka tu den hi.

records.english: Our school had no electricity, so we went home before it got dark.
records.zomi: I sang in meivak a nei kei ahih manin a mial ma-in inn i ciah uh hi.

records.english: We used to write on small slates because paper was too expensive.
records.zomi: Lai-ek a man tam luat manin suang-ek neute tungah i gelh zel uh hi.

records.english: My first job was delivering newspapers on my bicycle before school.
records.zomi: Ka nasep masa pen sang ka pai ma-in ka siiksakol tawh thuthak laipi tunsak ahi hi.

records.english: My parents could not read, so I read their letters to them when I was only nine.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa a sim thei kei uh ahih manin kum kua ka hih lai-in a laikhak te uh ka sim sak hi.

records.english: Dad's workshop was where I first learned how things were made.
records.zomi: Pa' nasepna inn pen bang te bangci-in a kibawl hiam cih ka sin masak na mun ahi hi.

records.english: Looking back, I can see how much my first teacher shaped the person I became.
records.zomi: Nunglam ka et kik ciangin ka saya masa pen in ka suah zia bangzah a bawl hiam cih ka mu hi.

records.english: Why did you decide to become a nurse?
records.zomi: Bang hangin nurse suah dingin na khensat hiam?

records.english: When I was eight, a nurse looked after my brother so kindly that I never forgot her.
records.zomi: Kum giat ka hih lai-in nurse khat in ka u pasal hehpih takin a kem ahih manin ka mangngilh ngei kei hi.

records.english: My older sister walked me to school and checked my homework every evening.
records.zomi: Ka u numei in sang ah hong paipih a, nitak simin ka inn-a sin ding a en hi.

records.english: Helping in my grandparents' shop taught me to talk to adults without fear.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh pi te' sumbuk-a huh in upate tawh lau lo-in kihopih dingin hong sinsak hi.

records.english: Did Mum really test you on your spelling while she cooked dinner?
records.zomi: Nu in nitak an a huan kawm-in na laimal gelhzia a sit taktak hiam?

records.english: The smell of the school kitchen still reminds me of my childhood.
records.zomi: Sang an huanna gim in ka naupan lai hong phawksak lai hi.

records.english: My first pay, for helping at the harvest, was a single coin that I kept for years.
records.zomi: Lou lakna ah huh manin ka khasum masa pen sum-ek khat bek ahi a, kum tampi ka kem hi.

records.english: We had to carry wood to school in winter to heat the classroom.
records.zomi: Phalbi-in sangdan lumsak nadingin sang ah sing i puak kul uh hi.

records.english: Was your school far from your home?
records.zomi: Na sang na inn pan a gamla hiam?

records.english: Did your school have a uniform when you were young?
records.zomi: Na khangno lai-in na sang in uniform a nei hiam?

records.english: Do you remember the name of your first teacher?
records.zomi: Na saya masa pen' min na phawk hiam?

records.english: The teacher who taught me to read lives in our village still, and I visit her every year.
records.zomi: Sim hong sinsak saya i khua ah a teng lai a, kum simin ka veh hi.

records.english: I'll never forget the day the teacher read my story aloud to the whole school.
records.zomi: Saya in ka tangthu sang bup kiangah aw tawh a sim ni ka mangngilh ngei kei ding hi.

records.english: The day the school got its first computer, the whole class crowded around it.
records.zomi: Sang in a computer masa pen a ngah ni-in class bup in a kim ah a kikhawm uh hi.

records.english: My best friend and I sat at the same desk for six years.
records.zomi: Ka lawm pen leh kei kum guk sung taupi kibang ah i tu uh hi.

records.english: When I was ten, I won a prize for the best handwriting in the class.
records.zomi: Kum sawm ka hih lai-in class sung-ah laigelhzia hoih pen adingin thaman khat ka ngah hi.

records.english: My childhood dream of becoming a teacher came true after many years of study.
records.zomi: Saya suah ding ka naupan lai deihna kum tampi kisin khit ciangin a tangtung hi.

records.english: Did you really learn your times tables by singing them every morning?
records.zomi: Zingsang simin la sa-in multiplication te na sin taktak hiam?

records.english: Our class grew vegetables in the school garden and sold them to parents.
records.zomi: I class in sang huan ah anteh a suan uh a, nu leh pate kiangah a zuak uh hi.

records.english: On my first day at school, I hid behind my mother and refused to go in.
records.zomi: Sang ka pai ni masa pen-in ka nu nunglam ah ka kisel a, lut ka nial hi.

records.english: Were you ever sent to the head teacher's office?
records.zomi: Sangpi saya' office ah na kisawl ngei hiam?

records.english: Thank you for helping me with my homework all those years ago, Grandpa.
records.zomi: Pu, kum tampi ma-in ka inn-a sin ding hong huh manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: The school trip to the city was the first time I had seen a tall building.
records.zomi: Khuapi-a sang khualzinna pen inn sang ka muh masak pen hun ahi hi.

records.english: When I was twelve, I spent the summer helping my uncle in his workshop.
records.zomi: Kum sawmlenih ka hih lai-in ka pa neu' nasepna inn ah khal bup ka huh hi.

records.english: I still have the notebook in which I wrote my first stories.
records.zomi: Ka tangthu masa te ka gelhna ciamtehna laibu ka nei lai hi.

records.english: I remember feeling proud the first time I could read a whole page without help.
records.zomi: Huhna om lo-in lai-ek bup ka sim thei masak pen-in ka kipak ka phawk hi.

records.english: My grandmother paid for my school books by selling eggs at the market.
records.zomi: Ka pi in sumbuk ah aktui zuak-in ka sang laibu te man a pia hi.

records.english: What games did you play at break time?
records.zomi: Tawlna hun-in bang kimawlna na kimawl uh hiam?

records.english: Did you have to work when you were a child?
records.zomi: Na naupan lai-in na na sep kul hiam?

records.english: Yes, I helped my parents in the rice fields every school holiday.
records.zomi: Kul hi, sang tawlngakni simin ka nu leh ka pa buh lou ah ka huh hi.

records.english: Watching my mother work long hours at the factory taught me the value of hard work.
records.zomi: Ka nu factory ah nai tampi na a sep a ka muh in nasep kipna' manphatna hong sinsak hi.

records.english: Did your teacher ring a bell when the break was over?
records.zomi: Tawlna hun a bei ciangin na saya in bell a tum hiam?

records.english: What was the hardest subject for you at school?
records.zomi: Sang ah bang laigil in na adingin a haksa pen hiam?

records.english: Maths, until a new teacher showed me how to use beans to count.
records.zomi: Maths, saya thak khat in sim nadingin be bangci-in zang ding cih hong lak mateng.

records.english: I was so nervous before my first exam that I couldn't eat breakfast.
records.zomi: Ka sitna masa pen ma-in ka lau mahmah ahih manin zingsang an ka ne zo kei hi.

records.english: When the school flooded one year, lessons were held in the church instead.
records.zomi: Kum khat sang tuilian a tuak ciangin sinna te pawlpi ah a kibawl hi.

records.english: I remember helping my mother sell vegetables before the school bell rang.
records.zomi: Sang bell a ging ma-in ka nu anteh zuak ka huh ka phawk hi.

records.english: Not until I started working did I appreciate how patient my teachers had been.
records.zomi: Na ka sep kipat mateng ka sayate bangzah thuakzawhna a nei uh hiam cih ka theisiam kei hi.

records.english: When I was small, I wanted to be a pilot because of a book in the school library.
records.zomi: Ka neu lai-in sang laibu inn-a laibu khat hangin vanleng tawlpa suah ka deih hi.

records.english: Who was your favourite teacher when you were small?
records.zomi: Na neu lai-in na it pen saya kua hiam?

records.english: Mr Pau, who let us read under the tree when it was too hot inside.
records.zomi: Saya Pau, inn sung a sat luat ciangin sing kung nuai-ah hong sim sak pa.

records.english: I loved the end of the school year, when we had a picnic by the river.
records.zomi: Lui gei-ah an i nek sang kum tawp ka it mahmah hi.

records.english: Different churches worship in different ways, but many share the same core beliefs.
records.zomi: Pawlpi tuamtuam in lam tuamtuam-in Pasian a bia uh a, ahi zongin tampi in upna bulpi kibang a nei uh hi.

records.english: Many churches in our area work together during the Easter celebrations.
records.zomi: I mun-a pawlpi tampi in Easter lungdampihna lai-in khawm-in na a sem uh hi.

records.english: Our church family celebrated with us when our baby was born.
records.zomi: I naungek a suah ciangin i pawlpi innkuan in kote tawh a lungdampih uh hi.

records.english: Some Christians call the church the bride of Christ, a picture taken from the Bible.
records.zomi: Khristian khenkhat in pawlpi pen Khazih' mo ci-in a sam uh a, Laisiangtho pan lak lim khat ahi hi.

records.english: Our church is like a big family.
records.zomi: I pawlpi pen innkuan lian khat bang ahi hi.

records.english: Let's pray for the churches in other parts of the world.
records.zomi: Leitung mun dang-a pawlpi te adingin i thungen ni.

records.english: The church is a place where young and old can learn from each other.
records.zomi: Pawlpi pen khangno leh upa te khat leh khat a kisinna mun ahi hi.

records.english: Is it possible to be a Christian without belonging to a church?
records.zomi: Pawlpi khat ah kihel lo-in Khristian khat hih thei hiam?

records.english: Many Christians describe the church as the family of God.
records.zomi: Khristian tampi in pawlpi pen Pasian' innkuan-in a gen uh hi.

records.english: Our pastor reminds us that the church is not a club for perfect people.
records.zomi: Pawlpi pen a kicing mite' club hi lo hi, ci-in i pastor in hong phawksak hi.

records.english: The Lord's Supper is shared in many churches as a sign of unity.
records.zomi: Pawlpi tampi in kipumkhatna lim-in Topa' Nitak An a kihawm uh hi.

records.english: Shall we take the visitors to church with us on Sunday?
records.zomi: Nipini-in khualte kote tawh pawlpi ah i paipih ding hiam?

records.english: The church is not perfect, but our pastor says it is a place where people can change.
records.zomi: Pawlpi a kicing kei a, ahi zongin mite a kikhek theihna mun ahi hi, ci-in i pastor in a gen hi.

records.english: Everyone is welcome at our church, whatever their age.
records.zomi: Kum bangzah hi taleh mi khempeuh i pawlpi ah kisang hi.

records.english: I do want to be more involved in the life of our church.
records.zomi: I pawlpi nuntakna sungah ka kihel zaw ka deih taktak hi.

records.english: Children, you are an important part of our church too.
records.zomi: Naupangte, note zong i pawlpi' thupi khen khat na hi uh hi.

records.english: Our pastor says that the church is strongest when every member uses their gifts.
records.zomi: Pawlpi pen a member khatciat in a letsongte a zat uh ciangin a hat pen hi, ci-in i pastor in a gen hi.

records.english: Who started the first church in our village?
records.zomi: I khua-a pawlpi masa pen kua in a kipatsak hiam?

records.english: Many Christians believe that the church should serve the whole community, not only its members.
records.zomi: Khristian tampi in pawlpi in a member te bek hi lo-in khuasung bup a nasem sak ding hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: Can we help the church collect food for families in need this month?
records.zomi: Hih kha-in kisapna nei innkuante adingin an kaikhawm nadingin pawlpi i huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Can I belong to the church if I'm still young?
records.zomi: Ka neu lai hangin pawlpi ah ka kihel thei hiam?

records.english: Yes, children are part of the church family too.
records.zomi: Thei hi, naupangte zong pawlpi innkuan khen khat ahi uh hi.

records.english: When our village had no church building, the believers met under a big tree.
records.zomi: I khua in pawlpi inn a neih loh lai-in um mite sing kung lian khat nuai-ah a kikhop uh hi.

records.english: Every Sunday, families brought mats and sat together in the shade to pray and sing.
records.zomi: Nipini simin innkuante in phah a paipih uh a, thungen leh la sa dingin a limliam ah khawm-in a tu uh hi.

records.english: Years later, they built a small church on the same spot, and the tree still stands beside it.
records.zomi: Kum tampi khit ciangin mun kibang ah pawlpi inn neu khat a lam uh a, sing kung a kiangah a ding lai hi.

records.english: Having grown up in the church, I now help to teach the younger children.
records.zomi: Pawlpi sungah ka khan ahih manin tu-in naupang neu zawte sinsak dingin ka huh hi.

records.english: Our youth group helps to clean the church every Saturday.
records.zomi: I khangno pawl in Kiginni simin pawlpi siangsak dingin a huh uh hi.

records.english: Thank you for making us feel so welcome at your church.
records.zomi: Na pawlpi ah hong san manin ka lungdam uh hi.

records.english: When the church building burned down, the members kept meeting in a tent.
records.zomi: Pawlpi inn a kan ciangin member te puan inn sungah a kikhop lai uh hi.

records.english: According to the book of Acts, the first Christians shared their meals and their possessions.
records.zomi: Sawltak Thuhilhna laibu bangin Khristian masa te in a an uh leh a neihsa uh a kihawm uh hi.

records.english: Does the church still meet in the school hall on Sunday mornings?
records.zomi: Nipini zingsang-in pawlpi sang inn lian ah a kikhop lai hiam?

records.english: The church bell rings every Sunday morning to call people to worship.
records.zomi: Nipini zingsang simin mite Pasian biak dingin sam nadingin pawlpi khawng a ging hi.

records.english: The elders of our church meet every month to pray and make decisions.
records.zomi: I pawlpi upate in thungen leh thukhensatna bawl dingin kha simin a kikhop uh hi.

records.english: My uncle helps the church by fixing the roof and painting the walls.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in inn tung bawlphat leh bang sai nuh-in pawlpi a huh hi.

records.english: When someone in our church is ill, other members bring them meals.
records.zomi: I pawlpi sung-ah mi khat a cina ciangin member dangte in an a paipih uh hi.

records.english: What does it mean to be a member of a church?
records.zomi: Pawlpi khat' member hihna in bang cihna hiam?

records.english: The early church grew quickly, even though its members were often in danger.
records.zomi: A member te lauhuaina sungah a om zel hangin pawlpi masa a hun-in a khang hi.

records.english: Our pastor says that the church is people, not bricks.
records.zomi: Pawlpi pen tual-ek hi lo-in mite ahi hi, ci-in i pastor in a gen hi.

records.english: What is the church?
records.zomi: Pawlpi pen bang hiam?

records.english: Christians believe the church is the people who follow Jesus, not just a building.
