records.zomi: Ka zi in naupangte' sang lakna te inn lian nunglam pan a video hi.

records.english: Did anyone record the speeches at the wedding?
records.zomi: Mopawi-a thugen te kuamah in a khum hiam?

records.english: My brother did, but his phone ran out of battery halfway through.
records.zomi: Ka u pasal in a khum a, ahi zongin a kim ah a phone battery a bei hi.

records.english: Watching old videos of my children makes me realise how quickly they grow up.
records.zomi: Ka tate' video lui te en in bangzah hun-in a khang uh hiam cih hong theisak hi.

records.english: Can you film the baby's first birthday party?
records.zomi: Naungek' suahni masa pen poai na video thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, and I'll make sure Grandma is in every shot.
records.zomi: Thei hi, lim khempeuh ah Pi a om nadingin ka en ding hi.

records.english: We filmed the children's interviews with their grandparents for a family history project.
records.zomi: Innkuan tangthu project adingin naupangte in a pu leh pi te tawh interview a bawl uh i video uh hi.

records.english: When Grandpa saw himself on video, he said he looked older than he felt.
records.zomi: Pu in video sungah amah a muh ciangin a kisak sangin a upa zaw-in a kilang hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Who filmed this, and why is it upside down?
records.zomi: Hih kua in a video a, bang hangin a kilehheh hiam?

records.english: My sister made a video of the whole family singing for our parents' anniversary.
records.zomi: Ka u numei in i nu leh pa' kiteen kum phawkna adingin innkuan bup la a sak video khat a bawl hi.

records.english: Thank you for filming the wedding, because it's the only record we have.
records.zomi: I neih ciamtehna khat bek ahih manin mopawi na video manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: Should we record a message for Grandma's ninetieth birthday?
records.zomi: Pi' kum sawmkua suahni adingin thuthak khat i khum ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, and each grandchild can say one thing they love about her.
records.zomi: Khum ni, tu khatciat in amah tawh kisai a it bangkhat ciat a gen thei uh hi.

records.english: The old video of my parents' wedding is so faded that we can hardly see their faces.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa' mopawi video lui a kang luat manin a mai uh i mu zo kei uh hi.

records.english: Our family video archive now fills three hard drives.
records.zomi: I innkuan video kemna tu-in hard drive thum a dimsak hi.

records.english: We record a short video of the children every birthday.
records.zomi: Suahni simin naupangte' video tomno khat i khum uh hi.

records.english: Our son recorded his grandmother telling the story of her wedding.
records.zomi: I tapa in a pi a mopawi tangthu a gen a khum hi.

records.english: My brother films every family meal for his cooking channel, which annoys Mum.
records.zomi: Ka u pasal in a an huan channel adingin innkuan an nek khempeuh a video a, tua in Nu a hehsak hi.

records.english: Our family's first video camera was so heavy that Dad needed both hands to hold it.
records.zomi: I innkuan' video camera masa pen a gik mahmah ahih manin Pa in a len nadingin a khut nih a kisam hi.

records.english: Let's record a short video for Auntie Lun's birthday.
records.zomi: Ni Lun' suahni adingin video tomno khat i khum ni.

records.english: Shall we film Grandpa teaching the children his favourite card game?
records.zomi: Pu in a it pen card kimawlna naupangte a sinsak i video ding hiam?

records.english: How do I stop the video from shaking when I film the children running?
records.zomi: Naupangte a tai lai-un ka video ciangin video a lin loh nadingin bangci-in ka bawl ding hiam?

records.english: Hold the phone with both hands and keep your elbows close to your body.
records.zomi: Phone khut nih tawh len inla, na ban-khuk te na pumpi kiangah koih in.

records.english: Turn off the sound of the TV before you start recording.
records.zomi: Na khum ma-in TV ging phiat in.

records.english: My nephew made a funny video of the family dog doing tricks.
records.zomi: Ka tanau in innkuan ui' kimawlna te tawh kisai nuihhuai video khat a bawl hi.

records.english: We used the old family videos to make a film for my parents' fortieth anniversary.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa' kum sawmli kiteen kum phawkna adingin innkuan video lui te zang-in film khat i bawl uh hi.

records.english: My cousin recorded his first speech as best man and played it back to practise.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam in mopawi-a pasal huhpa-a a thugen masa pen a khum a, kisin nadingin a ngai kik hi.

records.english: Dad filmed my first steps on his old camera.
records.zomi: Pa in a camera lui tungah ka khekhap masa te a video hi.

records.english: The recording of my late grandmother's voice is one of our family's treasures.
records.zomi: Ka pi sihsa' aw khumna pen i innkuan' van manpha te lak-ah khat ahi hi.

records.english: Mum refuses to be filmed unless she has done her hair.
records.zomi: A sam a bawl ma-in Nu in video-a kilak a nial hi.

records.english: Our children love watching videos of themselves as babies.
records.zomi: I tate in naungek a hih lai-uh video te en a it uh hi.

records.english: Grandpa now records a short video diary every evening.
records.zomi: Pu in tu-in nitak simin video ciamtehna laibu tomno khat a khum hi.

records.english: We always ask the children before we share their videos.
records.zomi: A video te i hawm ma-un naupangte i dong den uh hi.

records.english: Did you remember to press record this time?
records.zomi: Hih vei-in record nek na phawk hiam?

records.english: Why are you filming Grandpa while he cooks?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pu an a huan lai-in na video hiam?

records.english: So that we have his recipes in his own words, with every step.
records.zomi: A an huanzia te amah kammal tawh, kalsuan khempeuh tawh i neih nadingin.

records.english: Recording family moments is easy, but finding time to watch them is harder.
records.zomi: Innkuan hun te khum a baih a, ahi zongin en nading hun zon a haksa zaw hi.

records.english: My daughter edits our family videos and adds music to them.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in i innkuan video te a bawlphat a, la a beh hi.

records.english: Our son filmed a tour of our new house for the relatives back home.
records.zomi: I tapa in inn lam-a sanggamte adingin i inn thak sung vakna video khat a bawl hi.

records.english: My uncle recorded the whole football match, including his own shouting.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in football kimawlna bup, amah' kikona zong kihel-in, a khum hi.

records.english: Our son recorded our goodbye at the airport, and I still can't watch it without crying.
records.zomi: I tapa in vanlengtual-a i nusiatna a khum a, ka kap lo-in ka en thei lai kei hi.

records.english: The camera picked up every word the children whispered during the ceremony.
records.zomi: Kikhop lai-in naupangte' a kihopih neu kammal khempeuh camera in a la hi.

records.english: Please put the phone down and enjoy the party instead of filming it.
records.zomi: Video sangin phone koih inla, poai nuam takin om in.

records.english: When we lost the phone, we also lost a year of family videos.
records.zomi: Phone i mansuah ciangin innkuan video kum khat zong i mansuah uh hi.

records.english: We send short videos to Grandma because she can't read long messages.
records.zomi: Pi in message sau a sim zo kei ahih manin video tomno te i khak uh hi.

records.english: We filmed the children opening their presents on Christmas morning.
records.zomi: Christmas zingsang-in naupangte in a letsong a hon uh i video uh hi.

records.english: The video of our holiday is mostly the back of my husband's head.
records.zomi: I tawlngakni video pen a tamzaw ka pasal' lu nunglam ahi hi.

records.english: Can you send me the video of the twins dancing?
records.zomi: Apeng te' lam video hong khak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Can you hold the phone sideways when you film the school concert?
records.zomi: Sang concert na video ciangin phone kikawi-in na len thei ding hiam?

records.english: Is the battery charged enough to film the whole play?
records.zomi: Lam-en bup video nadingin battery a cing hiam?

records.english: What should kitchen staff do if they have a stomach bug?
records.zomi: An huanna nasemte in gil natna a neih uh leh bang a hih ding uh hiam?

records.english: In our kitchen, they stay away until they've been free of symptoms for two days.
records.zomi: I an huanna ah natna lim om lo-in ni nih a cin mateng a om kei uh hi.

records.english: Can I work from home until my cough gets better?
records.zomi: Ka khuk a hoih mateng inn pan na ka sem thei ding hiam?

records.english: I took a day off because my migraine made it impossible to look at a screen.
records.zomi: Ka lu natna hat in screen en a theih loh manin ni khat ka tawl hi.

records.english: Wash your hands before lunch, everyone.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh, sun an ma-in na khut sil un.

records.english: Why is the office so empty this week?
records.zomi: Bang hangin hih kal sung-in office a hawm mahmah hiam?

records.english: Half the team has the flu, so people are working from home where they can.
records.zomi: Team kim in flu a nei uh ahih manin a theih teng-in inn pan na a sem uh hi.

records.english: The students made posters explaining how to avoid catching colds.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte in khuavot natna pial zia a genna poster te a bawl uh hi.

records.english: The head teacher closed the school for a day so that it could be cleaned.
records.zomi: A siangsak theih nadingin sangpi saya in ni khat sang a khak hi.

records.english: Do you have a sick note from your doctor?
records.zomi: Na siavuan pan cina laikhak na nei hiam?

records.english: The meeting room is so stuffy that half of us have headaches.
records.zomi: Kikhopna dan huih hoih lo mahmah ahih manin kote a kim in i lu a na hi.

records.english: Please let the school know if your child has measles.
records.zomi: Na ta in measles a neih leh sang theisak un.

records.english: Regular breaks and enough sleep help nurses avoid catching every bug on the ward.
records.zomi: Tawlna hun kip leh ihmut a cing in nurse te in damdawi inn dan-a natna khempeuh a kai loh nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: The school asked parents to keep children at home for two days after a stomach bug.
records.zomi: Gil natna khit ciangin ni nih sung naupangte inn ah koih dingin sang in nu leh pate a ngen hi.

records.english: Our office offers free flu jabs every autumn.
records.zomi: I office in teh kiakna hun simin man om lo flu kidawnna damdawi a pia hi.

records.english: Half the football team missed the match because of a stomach bug.
records.zomi: Gil natna hangin football team kim in kimawlna a pai zo kei uh hi.

records.english: Our class had a lesson on how germs spread from hand to hand.
records.zomi: I class in natna lung khut pan khut ah bangci-in a kizel hiam cih sinna khat a nei uh hi.

records.english: Many new teachers say they catch more colds in their first year than ever before.
records.zomi: Saya thak tampi in a kum masa sung-in nidang sangin khuavot natna a kai tam zaw uh hi, a ci uh hi.

records.english: The cook was sent home because he had a bad stomach upset.
records.zomi: An huanpa in gil natna hat a neih manin inn ah kisawl hi.

records.english: Working while ill often spreads the illness to the whole team.
records.zomi: Na cina kawm-a nasep in team bup ah natna a zelsak zel hi.

records.english: In our café, staff who handle food must report any illness to their supervisor.
records.zomi: I cafe ah an a khoih nasemte in natna khatpeuh a makaipa uh kiangah a gen ding uh hi.

records.english: The hotel staff were trained to spot the signs of food poisoning among guests.
records.zomi: Zinbuuk nasemte in khualte lak-a an gu lim te thei dingin kisinsak uh hi.

records.english: My colleague's sinus infection kept him off work for a week.
records.zomi: Ka nasem pih' nak natna in kal khat sung nasep pan a khawlsak hi.

records.english: When a sickness bug went round the cruise ship, the crew cleaned every surface twice a day.
records.zomi: Tuipi tunga long lian ah natna khat a kizel ciangin nasemte in ni khat ah nihvei mun khempeuh a siangsak uh hi.

records.english: Hand gel was placed by every door when the winter bugs started.
records.zomi: Phalbi natna te a kipat ciangin kongkhak khempeuh kiangah khut sil gel a kikoih hi.

records.english: The supply teacher covered three classes because so many staff were ill.
records.zomi: Nasem tampi a cina uh ahih manin a laih saya in class thum a sinsak hi.

records.english: The sales team took fewer sick days after the company started paying for flu jabs.
records.zomi: Company in flu kidawnna damdawi man a piak kipat khit ciangin zuakna team in cina ni a tawm zaw uh hi.

records.english: Our boss sends anyone with a cold home, which keeps the rest of us healthy.
records.zomi: I boss in khuavot natna nei kuapeuh inn ah a sawl a, tua in kote dangte i dam nadingin a kem hi.

records.english: Should I tell my boss about my asthma?
records.zomi: Ka boss kiangah ka asthma ka gen ding hiam?

records.english: My eyes stream every spring, so I keep tissues on my desk.
records.zomi: Spring simin ka mit tui a luang ahih manin ka taupi tungah tissue ka kem hi.

records.english: Thank you for covering my shift while I was ill.
records.zomi: Ka cina lai-in ka nasep hun na sem sak manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: When can a child with chickenpox come back to school?
records.zomi: Chickenpox nei naupang bang ciangin sang ah a ciah thei ding hiam?

records.english: Once all the spots have dried and crusted over.
records.zomi: A ma te khempeuh a keu a, a hawng a khauh khit ciangin.

records.english: Office workers who share keyboards may also share their germs.
records.zomi: Keyboard kihawm office nasemte in natna lung zong a kihawm thei uh hi.

records.english: My hay fever makes it hard to concentrate in exams in June.
records.zomi: Ka hay fever in June-a sitna te ah ngaihsut kip a haksak hi.

records.english: After a week of colds in the office, someone brought in a box of oranges for everyone.
records.zomi: Office ah kal khat khuavot natna khit ciangin mi khat in mi khempeuh adingin sangtam bawm khat a paipih hi.

records.english: The factory installed better air filters after many workers complained of coughs.
records.zomi: Nasem tampi in khuk tawh kisai a phun khit uh ciangin factory in huih siangsakna hoih zaw a koih hi.

records.english: Please stay at home if you have a fever.
records.zomi: Na cisa leh inn ah om in.

records.english: Three teachers are off with the flu this week.
records.zomi: Hih kal sung-in saya thum flu hangin a om kei uh hi.

records.english: I caught a cold from someone in the office.
records.zomi: Office-a mi khat pan khuavot natna ka kai hi.

records.english: How many pupils are off sick today?
records.zomi: Tuni-in sangnaupang bangzah a cina-in a om lo uh hiam?

records.english: Seven, most of them with the stomach bug that's going round.
records.zomi: Sagih, a tamzaw a kizel gil natna tawh.

records.english: My cold was so bad that I couldn't hear the customers on the phone.
records.zomi: Ka khuavot natna a hat mahmah ahih manin phone tungah customer te ka za zo kei hi.

records.english: My manager told me to go home when she saw how pale I looked.
records.zomi: Ka mai bangzah a vom-ngo hiam cih a muh ciangin ka manager in inn ciah dingin hong gen hi.

records.english: Do you get ear infections when you go swimming?
records.zomi: Tuipeek na pai ciangin na bil a na hiam?

records.english: I've had this cough since I started working in the dusty warehouse.
records.zomi: Leivui tam warehouse ah na ka sep kipat pan hih khuk ka nei hi.

records.english: The nursery warned parents that a stomach bug was going round the toddler room.
records.zomi: Naupang sang in naupang neu dan ah gil natna a kizel hi, ci-in nu leh pate a vaihilh hi.

records.english: The nurse at work checked my temperature and sent me home.
records.zomi: Nasepna-a nurse in ka lum-vot a teh a, inn ah hong sawl hi.

records.english: Who's covering for Mr Thang while he's off sick?
records.zomi: Saya Thang a cina-in a om loh lai-in kua in a laih hiam?

records.english: Is conjunctivitis contagious enough to keep a child off school?
records.zomi: Conjunctivitis pen naupang sang ah pai lo dingin a kizel tham hiam?

records.english: The pharmacist at the shop near work recommended something for my sore throat.
records.zomi: Nasepna kiang-a sumbuk-a damdawi zuakpa in ka kawlok natna adingin bangkhat a gen hi.

records.english: Can I come into work with a cold?
records.zomi: Khuavot natna nei kawm-in nasepna ah ka hong thei hiam?

records.english: Only if you feel well enough, and please wash your hands often.
records.zomi: Na dam tham leh bek, leh na khut tam vei sil in.

records.english: Our team leader came back too early from the flu and ended up ill for another week.
records.zomi: I team makaipa flu pan a hun luat-a nasepna ah a ciah kik a, kal khat beh a cina kik hi.

records.english: My throat infection meant I couldn't teach for three days.
records.zomi: Ka kawlok natna hangin ni thum sung ka sinsak thei kei hi.

records.english: The nursery closes a room for cleaning whenever there's a stomach bug.
records.zomi: Gil natna a om ciangin naupang sang in siangsak nadingin inndan khat a khak hi.

records.english: Coughing into your elbow helps protect your colleagues.
records.zomi: Na ban-khuk sungah khuk in na nasem pihte a kem hi.

records.english: I lost my voice the day before my presentation.
records.zomi: Ka presentation ma ni-in ka aw a mang hi.

records.english: I'm sorry I missed the meeting, but I had a terrible migraine.
records.zomi: Maisak in, kikhopna ka mawh hi, ahi zongin lu natna hat mahmah ka nei hi.

records.english: The children were checked for fever at the school gate during the outbreak.
records.zomi: Natna a kizel lai-in sang kongpi ah naupangte cisa a kien uh hi.

records.english: Who keeps the spare key to the church hall?
records.zomi: Pawlpi inn lian' tawh beh kua in a kem hiam?

records.english: It's still not clear who will run the youth club after the leader retires.
records.zomi: Makaipa a nasep a tawp khit ciangin khangno pawl kua in a makaih ding hiam cih a kician nai kei hi.

records.english: Who should residents contact if the lift in their building breaks down?
records.zomi: A inn uh-a lift a sia leh teng mite in kua a sam ding uh hiam?

records.english: Who can I complain to about the rubbish that wasn't collected?
records.zomi: A kikaikhawm lo eek tawh kisai kua kiangah ka phun thei hiam?

records.english: Who's in charge of the community garden?
records.zomi: Khuasung huan kua in a makaih hiam?

records.english: Mrs Lun, who has looked after it for nearly ten years.
records.zomi: Nu Lun, kum sawm dek sung a kem nu.

records.english: Who's the new receptionist at the community centre?
records.zomi: Khuasung inn lian-a receptionist thak kua hiam?

records.english: Who will look after the community garden while Mrs Lun is away?
records.zomi: Nu Lun a om loh lai-in khuasung huan kua in a kem ding hiam?

records.english: Do you know who cleans the bus shelter on our corner?
records.zomi: I lampi kikawm-a bus ngakna mun kua in a siangsak hiam cih na thei hiam?

records.english: Who took over the bakery when the old baker retired?
records.zomi: Moh huanpa lui a nasep a tawp ciangin moh huanna kua in a la hiam?

records.english: Who among the councillors actually lives in our neighbourhood?
records.zomi: Councillor te lak-ah kua in i mun ah a teng taktak hiam?

records.english: Who would be the best person to ask about local history?
records.zomi: A mun tangthu tawh kisai dot dingin kua a hoih pen ding hiam?

records.english: Who do I talk to about a parking permit?
records.zomi: Mawtaw khawl phalna lai tawh kisai kua tawh ka kihopih ding hiam?

records.english: Who's going to deliver the leaflets about the clean-up day?
records.zomi: Siangsakna ni tawh kisai laikhak neu te kua in a tunsak ding hiam?

records.english: Who answers the phone at the police station at night?
records.zomi: Zan-in police inn ah phone kua in a dawng hiam?

records.english: Who has volunteered to cook at the lunch club this month?
records.zomi: Hih kha-in sun an pawl ah an huan dingin kua in thalawp a sem hiam?

records.english: Who should I ask about joining the library?
records.zomi: Laibu inn ah kihel nadingin kua ka dong ding hiam?

records.english: Who is on duty at the health centre this weekend?
records.zomi: Hih kal tawp-in damna inn ah kua in nasep a nei hiam?

records.english: Find out who is selling tickets for the charity concert.
records.zomi: Charity concert lakkhak kua in a zuak hiam cih zong in.

records.english: Whoever reaches the hall first should switch on the heating before the meeting.
records.zomi: Kuapeuh inn lian ah a tung masa in kikhopna ma-in meisa a hal ding hi.

records.english: Who will collect the old furniture if I book it online?
records.zomi: Online-in ka koih khol leh van lui te kua in a la ding hiam?

records.english: Who can explain how the council spends the money we pay in local taxes?
records.zomi: I piak a mun siah sum council in bangci-in a zang hiam cih kua in a gen thei hiam?

records.english: Who paid for the new playground in the square?
records.zomi: Khua lai-a naupang kimawlna mun thak man kua in a pia hiam?

records.english: Who decided to move the market to Thursdays?
records.zomi: Sumbuk Laizing ni ah sawn dingin kua in a khensat hiam?

records.english: Who can help my mother fill in her pension form?
records.zomi: Ka nu in a pension form a dimsak nadingin kua in a huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: The advice centre has a volunteer who speaks her language on Wednesdays.
records.zomi: Thuhilhna mun in Nilai ni simin a pau gen thei thalawp khat a nei hi.

records.english: Who should we speak to about the noise from the new bar?
records.zomi: Zu zuakna inn thak pan ging tawh kisai kua tawh i kihopih ding hiam?

records.english: The council's environmental health team deals with noise complaints.
records.zomi: Council' khuasung damna team in ging phunna te a bawl hi.

records.english: Who collects the recycling in our street?
records.zomi: I lampi ah recycling kua in a kaikhawm hiam?

records.english: A private company that works for the council, every second Tuesday.
records.zomi: Council adingin na a sem company khat, Pithai ni nih khat simin.

records.english: Who represents our street on the residents' committee?
records.zomi: Teng mite' committee ah i lampi kua in a aiawh hiam?

records.english: The person who runs the repair café can fix almost anything.
records.zomi: Bawlphatna cafe a makaihpa in bangkhempeuh dek a bawlphat thei hi.

records.english: Who should be told first if a child goes missing at the festival?
records.zomi: Pawi ah naupang khat a mang leh kua theisak masa ding hiam?

records.english: Who drives the mobile library to the villages?
records.zomi: Khua te ah vak laibu inn kua in a tawl hiam?

records.english: Who's teaching the first-aid course at the community centre?
records.zomi: Khuasung inn lian ah first-aid sinna kua in a sinsak hiam?

records.english: Who runs the food bank on Saturdays?
records.zomi: Kiginni-in an huhna mun kua in a makaih hiam?

records.english: A group of volunteers from the local church and the mosque.
records.zomi: A mun pawlpi leh mosque pan thalawp pawl khat in.

records.english: Who voted to close the swimming pool?
records.zomi: Tuipeek mun khak dingin kua in vote a pia hiam?

records.english: Who do you think should pay for repairing the old bridge?
records.zomi: Lei lui bawlphat man kua in a pia ding hi na ci hiam?

records.english: Who checks the fire alarms in the block of flats?
records.zomi: Inn lian sung-a mei vaihilhna te kua in a en hiam?

records.english: Who decides where the new bus stops will go?
records.zomi: Bus khawlna mun thak te koi-ah koih ding cih kua in a khensat hiam?

records.english: The transport office, after it has asked residents for their views.
records.zomi: Mawtaw office in, teng mite' ngaihsutna a dot khit ciangin.

records.english: Who's in the queue before me?
records.zomi: Kigual sungah ka ma-ah kua a om hiam?

records.english: Who are the people in green jackets at the station?

records.english: My brother and I shared the waiting with Grandma, one of us in the morning and one in the afternoon.

records.english: Grandpa's appointment was in a building with no lift, so the officer came down to meet him.

records.english: Who has the reference number for the appointment?

records.english: Our neighbour drove us to the appointment when our car broke down.

records.english: Grandpa wrote the appointment date on the calendar in big red letters.

records.english: My sister booked appointments for the whole family on the same day, which saved us a lot of travel.

records.english: Why does Dad always arrive at appointments half an hour early?

records.english: My brother forgot about his appointment and had to wait another month.

records.english: Thank you for coming with me to the appointment, because I was very nervous.
records.zomi: Ka lau mahmah ahih manin kimuhna ah kei tawh na hong manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: Every time Mum goes to the town hall, she brings a book because she knows she will wait.

records.english: Why did they cancel our appointment at the housing office?

records.english: Mum always phones the office the day before to check that the appointment is still on.

records.english: The officer explained everything slowly, because she could see that my grandmother was worried.

records.english: We were the last family to be seen before the office closed for the weekend.

records.english: Do we all need to go to the passport appointment?

records.english: I took the morning off work to go with my mother to the council office.

records.english: Who's going to take Dad to his appointment at the tax office?

records.english: When we got home, we realised we had left the baby's birth certificate on the counter.

records.english: The children came with us to the appointment, so we brought snacks and books.
records.zomi: Naupangte kote tawh kimuhna ah a hong uh ahih manin an neuno leh laibu te i paipih uh hi.

records.english: When we finally reached the counter, the office was about to close.
records.zomi: A tawp-in taupi i tun ciangin office a khak dek hi.

records.zomi: Pension office-a kimuhna ah Pi in a puan hoih pen silh dingin a ngetsak hi.

records.english: How long did you wait at the registry office?
records.zomi: Ciamtehna office ah bangzah sawt na ngak uh hiam?

records.english: Almost two hours, with a baby who wouldn't stop crying.

records.english: When the officer asked for a document we didn't have, Mum calmly showed her the photocopy.

records.english: Our family keeps all the appointment letters in one folder on the shelf.

records.english: Why was our appointment at the visa office moved twice?

records.english: We have to be at the immigration office at 9 a.m. tomorrow.

records.english: The officer apologised for the delay and offered us a glass of water.

records.english: My husband translated for his parents at their appointment with the tax officer.

records.english: Our appointment was confirmed by text, so I saved the message on my phone.

records.english: Can you remind me about Grandma's appointment on Thursday?

records.english: Is there a waiting room where the children can play?

records.english: My aunt's appointment to renew her residence permit took a whole day.

records.english: We arrived late because the car wouldn't start, but the officer still saw us.

records.english: Mum booked an appointment to register the baby's birth.
records.zomi: Naungek' suahna ciamteh nadingin Nu in kimuhna khat a koih khol hi.

records.english: My cousin travelled three hours for a ten-minute appointment.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam in minit sawm kimuhna adingin nai thum a khualzin hi.

records.zomi: Office-a laigelhna te a nasem ngei loh manin Pa in laigelhna khat a paipih den hi.

records.english: Let's leave early so that we're not rushing when we get there.
records.zomi: Tua-ah i tun ciangin i hanciam loh nadingin a hun-in i pai ni.

records.english: The children were so quiet during the appointment that the officer gave them each a sticker.
records.zomi: Kimuhna lai-in naupangte a dai mahmah uh ahih manin nasempa in khatciat sticker a pia hi.

records.english: The appointment took five minutes, but finding a parking space took forty.
records.zomi: Kimuhna minit nga a la a, ahi zongin mawtaw khawlna mun zon minit sawmli a la hi.

records.english: Grandpa asks the grandchildren to explain every emoji that people send him.

records.english: Are most of Grandma's followers her former students?
records.zomi: Pi' follower tamzaw a sangnaupang luite ahi uh hiam?

records.english: Can you help me reply to all these messages about the lost dog?
records.zomi: Ui mangthang tawh kisai hih message khempeuh dawn dingin hong huh thei ding hiam?

records.zomi: Gamdang-a i sanggam in amah hun-a zingsang nai thum-in zong post khempeuh ah comment a bawl hi.

records.english: The more personal my father's posts are, the more people respond to them.

records.english: Do you answer the comments on your videos yourself?

records.english: Who wrote that lovely comment under Grandpa's photo?
records.zomi: Pu' photo nuai-ah comment hoih tua kua in a gelh hiam?

records.english: Mum's followers sent her get-well messages when she was in hospital.

records.english: Having seen how happy the comments made her, my mother now posts every day.
records.zomi: Comment te in a lungdamsak mahmah cih a muh khit ciangin tu-in ka nu in ni simin post a bawl hi.

records.english: When nobody replied to my post, my brother kindly left the first comment.

records.english: Asking the cousins to share their favourite childhood memory got fifty replies in one evening.

records.english: Please don't argue with Uncle in the comments, and call him instead.
records.zomi: Comment sungah pa neu tawh kiniamkhiat kei inla, ama sam zaw in.

records.english: Encouraging the older relatives to comment took patience, but now they never stop.
records.zomi: Innkuan upate comment bawl dingin a lungnop sakna in thuakzawhna a ngai a, ahi zongin tu-in a khawl ngei kei uh hi.

records.english: Shall we ask the family to choose the date of the reunion in a poll?

records.english: Our family's online cookbook started when Auntie Hoih asked everyone to share one recipe.
records.zomi: Ni Hoih in mi khempeuh an huan dan khat hawm dingin a ngetna pan i innkuan' online an huan laibu a kipan hi.

records.english: Our son asks his viewers which game he should play next.
records.zomi: I tapa in a ngaktu te kiangah bang game a sun ding hiam cih a dong hi.

records.english: Our son's school asked parents to comment on the photos of the sports day.
records.zomi: I tapa' sang in nu leh pate kiangah kimawlna ni photo te tungah comment bawl dingin a ngen hi.

records.english: Grandpa was delighted when a stranger thanked him for his fishing tips.
records.zomi: A theih loh mi khat in a ngasi lak thu hilhna adingin lungdam a gen ciangin Pu a lungdam mahmah hi.

records.english: Grandma once spent a whole evening replying to every birthday message.

records.english: Should I delete the rude comment on our wedding photos?

records.english: My brother holds a live chat every Friday for the fans of his model trains.

records.english: Our family's group chat was quiet until Dad started a weekly photo challenge.

records.zomi: I innkuan thuthak lai tawp lamah puzzle khat a om a, a zo in cake a ngah hi.

records.english: My little sister's first follower was our grandmother.

records.english: My daughter's art page grew when she started showing how she makes each picture.

records.english: Why does Dad ask a question at the end of every post?

records.english: He says it gets the relatives talking to each other.
records.zomi: Tua in sanggamte a kihoupih sak hi, ci-in a gen hi.

records.english: Who replies to the messages on Auntie Lun's craft page?

records.english: Thank you for sharing my post with your friends.

records.english: Our family blog has a comment section where the cousins leave messages for each other.

records.english: Thank everyone who wished you a happy birthday.

records.english: What's the best time of day to visit the council office without queuing?

records.zomi: Inn-ah sanggam a kem mite adingin bang huhna a om hiam?

records.english: What do the different coloured bins mean?
records.zomi: Pianzia tuamtuam eek bawm te in bang a lak hiam?

records.english: What should we do with old paint and batteries?
records.zomi: Paint lui leh battery te bang i bawl ding uh hiam?

records.english: Take them to the recycling centre, because they can't go in the normal bins.
records.zomi: Recycling centre ah paipih in, bang hang hiam cih leh eek bawm tavuan sungah koih theih hi lo hi.

records.english: Which number should I ring if I smell gas?
records.zomi: Gas namtui ka nam leh bang nambat ka sam ding hiam?

records.zomi: Ka theih nop pen bang hangin zanlai-in lampi meivak te a mit hiam cih ahi hi.

records.zomi: Bus pass nih' kibang lohna bang hiam?

records.zomi: Sang lampi kantanna thak a kihon ma-in nu leh pate in bang a theih kul uh hiam?

records.english: What did the council decide about the new car park?
records.zomi: Mawtaw khawlna mun thak tawh kisai-in council in bang a khensat hiam?

records.english: Geography lessons help students understand news from other countries.
records.zomi: Geography sinna in sangnaupangte gamdang thuthak a theisiam sak hi.

records.english: My colleague from Nepal showed us photos of the mountains near his home.
records.zomi: Nepal pan ka nasem pih in a inn kiang-a mualte' photo hong lak hi.

records.english: The report compares the cost of living in five regions.
records.zomi: Report in gamkhen nga-a nuntakna man a kiteh hi.

records.english: Our class wrote to a school in Ghana and learned about life there.
records.zomi: I class in Ghana-a sang khat kiangah lai a gelh a, tua-a nuntakna tawh kisai a sin uh hi.

records.english: Trade between neighbouring countries often depends on good roads and bridges.
records.zomi: Kiang-a gamte' kikal sumbawlna in lampi hoih leh lei hoih tungah kinga zel hi.

records.english: The journalist has reported from more than thirty countries.
records.zomi: Thuthak gelhpa in gam sawmthum tung pan thu a gen khin hi.

records.english: The tourism board promotes the coastal regions in summer and the mountains in winter.
records.zomi: Khualzin board in khal-in tuipi gei gamkhen te leh phalbi-in mualte a lakkhia hi.

records.english: Working with colleagues from different regions taught me to be patient with accents.
records.zomi: Gamkhen tuamtuam pan nasem pihte tawh na ka sep in pau ngaihzia tuamtuam tungah thuakzawh dingin hong sinsak hi.

records.english: The economist explained why some regions grew richer than others.
records.zomi: Economist in bang hangin gamkhen khenkhat a dang sangin a hau zaw hiam cih a gen hi.

records.zomi: Khualzin lampi lakpa in bang hangin gamkhen nih in an kibang lo mahmah a nei uh hiam cih a gen hi.

records.english: What time is it in our Tokyo office now?
records.zomi: Tu-in i Tokyo office ah bang hun hiam?

records.english: It's already evening there, so they've probably gone home.
records.zomi: Tua-ah nitak lam a hi khin ahih manin inn ah a ciah khin kha ding uh hi.

records.english: The teacher pointed to Mongolia and asked whether it has a coastline.
records.zomi: Saya in Mongolia a lak a, tuipi gei a nei hiam cih a dong hi.

records.english: Countries that share a river must agree on how its water is used.
records.zomi: Lui khat a kihawm gamte in a tui bangci-in a zat ding uh hiam cih a kilem kul uh hi.

records.zomi: Huhna nasemte leiling in a siatsak pen gamkhen ah kisawl uh hi.

records.english: Which countries does your company export to?

records.english: Mainly Thailand, Vietnam and Japan, with a few orders from Europe.
records.zomi: A tamzaw Thailand, Vietnam leh Japan ah, Europe pan order tawm khat tawh.

records.english: When planning a meeting across countries, we always check the public holidays first.
records.zomi: Gam tuamtuam kikal kikhopna i ciamteh ciangin gam tawlngakni te i en masa den hi.

records.english: Our class learned that some countries have more than one capital city.
records.zomi: Gam khenkhat in khuapi lian pen nih sang a tam a nei uh hi, cih i class in a sin hi.

records.english: Which countries border the Mediterranean Sea?
records.zomi: Mediterranean Tuipi gei ah bang gamte a om hiam?

records.english: Is Singapore a city or a country?
records.zomi: Singapore pen khuapi hiam, gam hiam?

records.english: The truck drivers cross two borders on their weekly route.
records.zomi: Truck tawlpate in kal sim a pai lampi tungah gamgi nih a kantan uh hi.

records.english: Studying other countries teaches students that there is more than one way to live.
records.zomi: Gamdang tawh kisai sinna in sangnaupangte nuntak dan khat bek om lo hi, cih a sinsak hi.

records.english: In our country, the regions near the border trade more with the neighbouring country than with the capital.
records.zomi: I gam sungah gamgi kiang gamkhen te in khuapi lian pen sangin kiang gam tawh sumbawlna a tam zaw uh hi.

records.english: The airline flies to twenty countries across Asia and Europe.
records.zomi: Vanleng company in Asia leh Europe-a gam sawmnih ah a leng hi.

records.english: My first job abroad was teaching English in a small town in South Korea.
records.zomi: Gamdang-a ka nasep masa pen South Korea-a khuapi neuno khat ah English sinsakna ahi hi.

records.english: Did our company really open a new office in the north last year?
records.zomi: Kum bei-in i company in a mal lamah office thak khat a hong taktak hiam?

records.english: Our teacher asked us why most of the country's cities are near the coast.
records.zomi: Bang hangin gam' khuapi tamzaw tuipi gei ah a om hiam cih i saya in hong dong hi.

records.english: Our sales team is divided into regions, and each one has its own manager.
records.zomi: I zuakna team gamkhen tawh kikhen a, khatciat in amah manager a nei hi.

records.english: Is Peru on the Atlantic or the Pacific side of South America?

records.english: The Pacific side, with the Andes running behind its coast.
records.zomi: Pacific lam ah, a tuipi gei nung ah Andes mualte a tual hi.

records.english: Our school's international day celebrates every country our pupils come from.
records.zomi: I sang' gamdang ni in i sangnaupangte' hong paina gam khempeuh a lungdampih hi.

records.english: The exchange students taught us greetings from each of their countries.
records.zomi: Kikhek sangnaupangte in a gam uh khatciat pan kikhamna pau hong sinsak uh hi.

records.english: Each region of the country has its own traditional dress, which we studied in class.
records.zomi: Gam' gamkhen khatciat in amah ngeina puan a nei a, tua i class sungah i sin uh hi.

records.english: The new map shows the borders that were agreed after the war.

records.english: Which country is the largest in South America?

records.english: My manager has worked in every region of the country, so she knows the customers well.

records.english: Thank you for explaining the regions so clearly in today's lesson.
records.zomi: Tuni sinna sungah gamkhen te tak takin na gen manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: My job at the embassy involves helping citizens who are travelling in the region.
records.zomi: Embassy-a ka nasep in gamkhen sungah khualzin gammite huhna a kihel hi.

records.english: The engineers chose a region with plenty of wind for the new wind farm.
records.zomi: Engineer te in huih tha thak adingin huih tam gamkhen khat a teel uh hi.

records.english: Which country hosts the conference next year?
records.zomi: Kum thak-in bang gam in conference a bawl ding hiam?

records.english: Our textbook describes the five main regions of the country and their industries.
records.zomi: I sinna laibu in gam' gamkhen pi nga leh a nasepna te a gen hi.

records.english: The students compared the population of each region using a bar chart.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte in bar chart zang-in gamkhen khatciat' mihing tamna a kiteh uh hi.

records.english: Which region produces most of the country's electricity?
records.zomi: Bang gamkhen in gam' electricity tamzaw a bawl hiam?

records.english: Students who study abroad often learn as much about their own country as about the new one.
records.zomi: Gamdang-a sinna kai sangnaupangte in gam thak tawh kisai a sin bang-in amah gam tawh kisai zong a sin zel uh hi.

records.english: The farmers' cooperative sells coffee from three different regions.
records.zomi: Lo neite' kipawlna in gamkhen tuamtuam thum pan coffee a zuak hi.

records.english: Can the shipping company deliver to most countries within a week?
records.zomi: Van khakna company in kal khat sungin gam tamzaw ah a khak thei hiam?

records.english: Our geography class studied the regions of our country one by one.
records.zomi: I geography class in i gam' gamkhen te khat khit khat a sin hi.

records.english: Which region of the country has the highest mountains?
records.zomi: Gam' bang gamkhen in mual sang pen a nei hiam?

records.english: Do I need a visa to work in that country?
records.zomi: Tua gam ah na sep nadingin visa ka kul hiam?

records.english: Yes, and your employer has to apply for a work permit first.
records.zomi: Kul hi, na nasepsakpa in work permit a ngen masa kul hi.

records.english: Students, find Indonesia on the map and count how many large islands you can see.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte, map tungah Indonesia zong unla, tuikulh lian bangzah na muh thei uh hiam cih sim un.

records.english: Our research project compared schools in a rich region and a poor one.
records.zomi: I sut kankanna project in gamkhen hau khat leh zawng khat-a sang te a kiteh hi.

records.english: The engineers travelled to three countries to inspect the company's factories.
records.zomi: Engineer te in company' factory te en dingin gam thum ah a khualzin uh hi.

records.english: The company's training is translated into the languages of every region where it works.
records.zomi: Company' kisinsakna te a nasepna gamkhen khempeuh' pau-in kiletkhia hi.

records.english: Which region of the country grows most of the rice?

records.english: The central plains, where the rivers bring water to the fields every year.
records.zomi: Lui te in kum simin lo te ah tui a tun sakna laizang phaizang ah.

records.zomi: Geography sayate in sangnaupangte gam thak khat tawh kimel thei sak dingin an zang zel uh hi.

records.zomi: Sangnaupang khatciat in gam khat a teel a, a khuahun leh a mite tawh kisai poster khat a bawl hi.

records.english: The airline's map shows its routes as red lines between the countries.
records.zomi: Vanleng company' map in a lampi te gamte kikal-ah khau san tawh a lak hi.

records.english: Please tell the supervisor if the new gloves rub your hands.

records.zomi: Lo-a gah lakna ni masa pen-in lo neipa' khut a vun a puam hi.

records.english: The football coach checked the player's ankle before letting him back on the pitch.

records.english: When the pain in my knee got worse, I asked to move to a desk job for a while.

records.zomi: Minit khat ka tu thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, and put your foot up on this chair.
records.zomi: Thei hi, na khe hih tutphah tungah koih in.

records.english: The builder's knees are sore from kneeling on the concrete floor.
records.zomi: Inn lampa' khuk te concrete tungah a kuun manin a na hi.

records.english: Tell me if the new boots are rubbing your heels.

records.zomi: Nasepna-a kipan natna, a neu bang zongin, theisak ding hi.

records.zomi: Lamte in liamna a nialna dingin kisinna khatciat ma-in minit sawmnih sung a tha a kizang uh hi.

records.english: The surgeon said that long operations leave her with a painful neck.

records.zomi: PE saya in class kiangah bangpeuh a nat leh khawl un, ci hi.

records.zomi: I mit tawlngak nadingin hun tawntung tawlngak dingin i manager in a ngen kip hi.

records.zomi: Ka nungzang a nat lai-in hong tawlngak sak manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: The physiotherapist at work showed us how to sit properly at our desks.
records.zomi: Nasepna-a physiotherapist in i taupi ah bangci-in a dik takin tut ding hiam cih hong lak hi.

records.zomi: Sangdan sung-a tutphah thak te a khauh mahmah ahih manin sun an hun ciangin i nungzang uh a na hi.

records.english: Our school nurse keeps ice packs for students who get hurt in the playground.
records.zomi: I sang nurse in naupang kimawlna mun-a liam sangnaupangte adingin tuikhal ip a kem hi.

records.english: Ignoring discomfort at work can turn a small problem into a long injury.
records.zomi: Nasepna-a kisa lohna limsak lo pen in buaina neuno khat liamna sau khat ah a suaksak thei hi.

records.english: My shoulders ache from carrying the children's books between classrooms.
records.zomi: Sangdan kikal-ah naupangte' laibu ka puak manin ka liang te a na hi.

records.english: Which part of your hand hurts most?
records.zomi: Na khut' bang mun in a na pen hiam?

records.english: At the base of my thumb, especially when I use scissors.
records.zomi: Ka khutpi' bul ah, a tuamtuam-in nam-et ka zat ciangin.

records.english: The chef burned his arm on the oven door and kept working.
records.zomi: An huanpa in oven kongkhak tungah a ban a kang a, na a sem suak lai hi.

records.english: Do your fingers ache in the cold when you work outside?
records.zomi: Pualam-ah na na sep ciangin vot-in na khutzung te a na hiam?

records.english: The musician has a sore jaw from playing the trumpet every evening.
records.zomi: Sumtum siampa in nitak simin trumpet a mut manin a khaang a na hi.

records.english: My neck is stiff from looking down at the laptop all day.
records.zomi: Ni bup laptop ka en suk manin ka ngawng a khauh hi.

records.english: Students who carry heavy bags often complain of shoulder pain.
records.zomi: Ip gik a puak sangnaupangte in liang natna a phun zel uh hi.

records.english: I pulled a muscle in my back lifting the delivery on my own.
records.zomi: Van hong tung keimah bek-in ka dawn manin ka nungzang tha khat ka kihel hi.

records.english: Can you adjust the height of my chair?
records.zomi: Ka tutphah' a sanna na bawl thei ding hiam?

records.english: My wrists hurt from carrying heavy trays in the restaurant.
records.zomi: Restaurant ah an kuang gik ka puak manin ka khut ngawng te a na hi.

records.english: Does your back hurt after a full shift?
records.zomi: Shift khat bup khit ciangin na nungzang a na hiam?

records.english: Only when I've been bending over the patients all day.
records.zomi: Ni bup cinate tungah ka kun ciang bek.

records.english: My headache disappeared once I started drinking more water at work.
records.zomi: Nasepna ah tui tam zaw ka dawn kipat ciangin ka lu natna a bei hi.

records.english: The warehouse introduced lifting equipment after several workers hurt their backs.
records.zomi: Nasem tampi in a nungzang a liam khit ciangin van koihna inn in van dawnna khawl a kipat sak hi.

records.english: Is the pain worse in the morning or at the end of the day?

records.english: Do your feet ache after a whole day standing at the till?
records.zomi: Sum lakna mun ah ni bup na din khit ciangin na khe te a na hiam?

records.english: Sitting in the same position for hours can cause pain in the lower back.
records.zomi: Nai tampi sung mun khat-a tut in nungzang nuai lam ah natna a piangsak thei hi.

records.english: The gardener wears knee pads so that the ground doesn't hurt her knees.
records.zomi: Huan kempa in lei in a khuk a natsak loh nadingin khuk hum a silh hi.

records.english: The piano teacher reminded us to relax our shoulders so that they wouldn't ache.
records.zomi: Piano saya in i liang a nat loh nadingin a nem sak dingin hong phawksak hi.

records.english: The delivery driver's knee hurts every time he climbs into the van.
records.zomi: Van khakpa' khuk van khak mawtaw sungah a kah simin a na hi.

records.english: Is there a first-aid kit in the staff room?
records.zomi: Nasemte' inndan ah first-aid kit khat a om hiam?

records.english: Using a footrest reduced the pain in my back within a week.
records.zomi: Khe koihna khat ka zat in kal khat sungin ka nungzang natna a kiamsak hi.

records.english: After a week of carrying the camera, my shoulder started to ache.
records.zomi: Camera kal khat sung ka puak khit ciangin ka liang a na kipan hi.

records.english: The trainee nurse's feet were covered in blisters by the end of her first week.
records.zomi: A kal masa pen a bei ciangin kisin nurse' khe tungah vun puamna dim hi.

records.english: The long flight left the cabin crew with swollen ankles.
records.zomi: Vanleng khualzinna sau in vanleng sung nasemte' khe ngawng a vulsak hi.

records.english: The cleaner's hands are sore and cracked from the strong chemicals.
records.zomi: Siangsakna nasempa' khut te zatui hat te hangin a na a, a kek hi.

records.english: The singer cancelled the concert because her throat was too painful.
records.zomi: Lasa numei in a dang a na lua ahih manin concert a phiat hi.

records.english: Why are you rubbing your shoulder?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na liang na nuaih hiam?

records.english: It's been aching since I moved the filing cabinets on Friday.
records.zomi: Laithai ni-a lai koihna bawm te ka sawn pan a na hi.

records.english: How do you cope with the pain during long exams?
records.zomi: Sitna sau sungin natna bangci-in na thuak hiam?

records.zomi: Dotna kikal-ah ka khutzung te ka zan a, huih ka dawn thuk hi.

records.english: The new uniform is so tight that it's uncomfortable to sit in.
records.zomi: Uniform thak a cip mahmah ahih manin a sungah tut a nuam lo hi.

records.english: Repetitive work can cause discomfort that builds up slowly over months.

records.english: The mechanic's back hurts from lying under cars all day.
records.zomi: Mawtaw bawlpa ni bup mawtaw nuai-ah a lum manin a nungzang a na hi.

records.english: The student fainted in the heat and hit her head on the desk.
records.zomi: Sangnaupang numei khat sat-in a kipuk a, a lu taupi tungah a kisu hi.

records.english: Not until my brother finished university did my parents finally take a holiday.

records.english: Our family celebrates the first day of every new job with a special breakfast.
records.zomi: I innkuan in nasep thak khatciat ni masa pen zingsang an tuamtak tawh a lungdampih hi.

records.english: My grandmother still talks about the day all her grandchildren finished school.
