records.english: We vote on the holiday destination with a poll in the family chat.
records.zomi: Innkuan chat sungah vote tawh tawlngakna khualzin mun i teel uh hi.

records.english: Too many notifications from the family chat drove Dad to leave it.
records.zomi: Innkuan chat pan notification tam lua in Pa a pai khiasak hi.

records.english: We share the job of checking on Grandma through a simple rota in the chat.
records.zomi: Chat sung-a hun kizom baih khat tungtawn-in Pi en nasep i hawm uh hi.

records.english: We planned Mum's surprise party in a secret group that she didn't know about.
records.zomi: Nu' lamdang sak poai a theih loh group kuku khat-ah i ngimna bawl uh hi.

records.english: How are you planning the reunion with relatives in five countries?
records.zomi: Gam nga-a sanggamte tawh innkuan kikhopna bangci-in na ngimna bawl hiam?

records.english: We use a shared document for ideas and a poll to choose the dates.
records.zomi: Ngaihsutna adingin kihawm document khat leh ni teel nadingin vote khat i zang uh hi.

records.english: Grandma learned to react to messages with emojis, and now she uses them all the time.
records.zomi: Pi in thukhak te emoji tawh a dawn dan a sin a, tu-in a zang den hi.

records.english: Is the link for Sunday's call the same as last week's?
records.zomi: Nipini' call adingin link pen kal bei khin pen tawh a kibang hiam?

records.english: My children write birthday messages together in a shared card online.
records.zomi: Ka tate in online card kihawm khat-ah suahni thukhak te khawm-in a gelh uh hi.

records.english: Can Grandma join our video call from her tablet?
records.zomi: Pi in a tablet pan i video call ah a kihel thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, I'll send her the link and stay on the phone until she's in.
records.zomi: Thei hi, link ka khak ding a, a lut dong phone tungah ka om ding hi.

records.english: Greet your aunt, and then you can go and play.
records.zomi: Na ni dawnsawn in, tua khit ciangin na pai thei a, na kimawl thei hi.

records.english: Our cousins from the city greet the village elders more formally than we do.
records.zomi: Khuapi lian pan i sanggamte in eite sangin khua upate a zahtak zaw-in a dawnsawn uh hi.

records.english: Have you said good night to everyone in the room?
records.zomi: Inndan sung-a mi khempeuh kiangah zan hoih na gen khin hiam?

records.english: Greetings in our family are never rushed, even when we're late for church.
records.zomi: Pawlpi ah i phawng zongin i innkuan-a dawnsawnna te a manlang ngei kei hi.

records.english: Grandma was offended when a young cousin waved at her instead of greeting her properly.
records.zomi: Sanggam neu khat in hoih takin a dawnsawn sangin khut a lap ciangin Pi a lungkham hi.

records.english: My niece practises the greetings in front of the mirror before family visits.
records.zomi: Ka tunu in innkuan vehna ma-in mitlimlang mai-ah dawnsawnna te a kisin hi.

records.english: Grandpa greets each grandchild by name, even though there are twenty of us.
records.zomi: Ei sawmnih i om zongin Pu in tu khatciat a min-in a dawnsawn hi.

records.english: When I forgot to greet my great-aunt, Mum quietly sent me back across the room.
records.zomi: Ka pi lian ka dawnsawn ding ka mangngilh ciangin Nu in dai takin inndan langkhat ah hong ciahsak kik hi.

records.english: My brother's children greet our parents in two languages, which makes everyone laugh.
records.zomi: Ka sanggampa' tate in ka nu leh ka pa pau nih tawh a dawnsawn uh a, tua in mi khempeuh a nuihsak hi.

records.english: Welcome guests warmly at the door, even if you're busy.
records.zomi: Na buai zongin kongkhak-ah khualte lungdam takin dawnsawn in.

records.english: Why does Grandma kiss the children on both cheeks?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pi in naupangte' biang nihvei a tawp hiam?

records.english: That's how her own grandmother greeted her, and she keeps the habit alive.
records.zomi: Tua pen a pi mah in amah a dawnsawn dan ahi a, ngeina a om den nadingin a kem hi.

records.english: Keeping our greetings alive is one way of keeping our families close across many countries.
records.zomi: I dawnsawnna te a om den nadingin kem pen gam tampi-ah i innkuan te kinai den sak nading lampi khat ahi hi.

records.english: Greeting elders properly is the first thing we teach our children when they visit the village.
records.zomi: Upate hoih takin dawnsawn pen i tate khua a veh ciangun i sinsak masa pen ahi hi.

records.english: Please greet Auntie properly; she came a long way to see you.
records.zomi: Ni hoih takin dawnsawn in; nang hong mu dingin gamla mahmah pan a hong hi.

records.english: When my son brought his fiancée home for the first time, she had practised our greetings for weeks.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in a zi ding a masa pen-in inn ah a paipih ciangin kal tampi sung i dawnsawnna te a kisin khin hi.

records.english: She stood when Grandma came in and greeted her with both hands, just as he had taught her.
records.zomi: Pi a lut ciangin a ding a, ka tapa' sinsak bang-in khut nih tawh a dawnsawn hi.

records.english: Grandma was so delighted that she told the whole church about it the following Sunday.
records.zomi: Pi a lungdam lua ahih manin a zom Nipini-in pawlpi bup kiangah a gen hi.

records.english: In our house, the youngest child greets the guests first.
records.zomi: I inn ah naupang neupen in khualte a masa-in a dawnsawn hi.

records.english: Our family greets the grandparents before anyone else at the table.
records.zomi: I innkuan in dawhkan kiang-ah kuapeuh ma-in pu leh pite a dawnsawn uh hi.

records.english: Dad taught me never to greet an elder while chewing or eating.
records.zomi: Pa in an ka nek lai hiam, ka ngawh lai hiam upa khat dawnsawn ngei lo dingin hong sinsak hi.

records.english: The traditional greeting at weddings takes so long that the food often goes cold.
records.zomi: Mopawi-a ngeina dawnsawnna a sau lua ahih manin an a vot zel hi.

records.english: Do you shake hands with your grandparents or hug them?
records.zomi: Na pu leh pite na khut na kilen hiam, na kawi hiam?

records.english: At funerals, our family greets mourners with a quiet handshake and few words.
records.zomi: Misi vuina ah i innkuan in dah mite dai taka khut kilenna leh kammal tawm tawh a dawnsawn uh hi.

records.english: Dad lowers his eyes slightly when he greets an elder.
records.zomi: Upa khat a dawnsawn ciangin Pa in a mit tawm khat a niamsak hi.

records.english: Go and greet your grandmother before you unpack your bag.
records.zomi: Na ip na hon ma-in na pi va dawnsawn in.

records.english: When my parents greet each other's families, they use the most respectful words they know.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in khat leh khat' innkuan a dawnsawn uh ciangin a theih uh kammal zahtak huai pen te a zang uh hi.

records.english: How should the children greet Grandpa when he arrives?
records.zomi: Pu a tun ciangin naupangte in bangci-in a dawnsawn ding uh hiam?

records.english: They should stand up, go to him and wait for him to take their hands.
records.zomi: A ding ding uh a, a kiang-ah a pai ding uh a, a khut uh a len dong a ngak ding uh hi.

records.english: We teach the youngest children to greet guests by bringing them a glass of water.
records.zomi: Naupang neupen te tui haai khat paipih-in khualte dawnsawn dingin i sinsak uh hi.

records.english: Shall I greet your parents in the traditional way when I visit?
records.zomi: Ka veh ciangin na nu leh na pa ngeina dan-in ka dawnsawn ding hiam?

records.english: My cousin's children, who grew up abroad, learned the greetings from their grandmother during her visit.
records.zomi: Gamdang-a a khang ka sanggam' tate in a pi a hong veh lai-in dawnsawnna te a pi pan a sin uh hi.

records.english: The children found the long greetings at the reunion tiring but funny.
records.zomi: Innkuan kikhopna-a dawnsawnna sau te naupangte in a gim sa uh a, ahi zongin a nuihza sa uh hi.

records.english: Don't forget to greet the neighbours on the way out.
records.zomi: Na pai khiat ciangin inn vengte dawnsawn ding mangngilh kei in.

records.english: Our teenagers sometimes forget the greetings, but the grandparents gently remind them.
records.zomi: I tangvalnote in khatveivei dawnsawnna te a mangngilh uh a, ahi zongin pu leh pite in nem takin a phawksak uh hi.

records.english: Greeting relatives in the old way makes our children feel connected to the village.
records.zomi: Sanggamte ngeina lui dan-in dawnsawn in i tate khua tawh a kizom bang-in a kisaksak hi.

records.english: My little brother bows so seriously to the elders that everyone smiles.
records.zomi: Ka nau neu in upate kiangah thupi takin a kun ahih manin mi khempeuh a nuihmai uh hi.

records.english: A greeting from the eldest at a family gathering is treated like a blessing.
records.zomi: Innkuan kikhopna-ah a upa pen' dawnsawnna pen thupha bang-in kingaihsun hi.

records.english: In our family, children greet visitors at the door and take their bags.
records.zomi: I innkuan ah naupangte in kongkhak-ah khualte a dawnsawn uh a, a ip uh a la uh hi.

records.english: My grandmother still greets the postman as if he were a member of the family.
records.zomi: Ka pi in laikhak khakpa innkuan mi khat bang-in a dawnsawn lai hi.

records.english: Grandma taught me to greet every guest with a smile and a question about their health.
records.zomi: Pi in khual khempeuh nuihmai leh a cidamna tawh kisai dotna khat tawh dawnsawn dingin hong sinsak hi.

records.english: My daughter's friends were surprised when she stood up to greet my mother.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in ka nu dawnsawn dingin a ding ciangin a lawmte a lamdang sa uh hi.

records.english: Is it polite to greet elders while you're sitting down?
records.zomi: Na tut lai-in upate dawnsawn pen zahtak huai hiam?

records.english: Not in our family, so stand up first, even if it's only for a moment.
records.zomi: I innkuan ah hi lo hi, tua ahih manin tawm khat bek ding zongin a masa-in ding in.

records.english: Some greetings are used only on special days, such as weddings or the start of the harvest.
records.zomi: Dawnsawnna khenkhat pen mopawi hiam, an lak kipatna hiam bang ni tuam te-in bek kizang hi.

records.english: We greet my grandparents first thing every morning when we stay with them.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh pite tawh i om ciangin zingsang simin a masa pen-in amaute i dawnsawn uh hi.

records.english: Grandpa always holds a greeting for a long moment, looking you in the eye.
records.zomi: Pu in dawnsawnna khat a sawt takin a len den a, na mit sungah a en hi.

records.english: Grandma says a proper greeting costs nothing and means everything.
records.zomi: Dawnsawnna hoih khat in bangmah a man kei a, ahi zongin bangkim a hi hi, ci-in Pi in a gen hi.

records.english: Why did Uncle bow so low to the old pastor?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pa neu in pastor upa kiangah niam takin a kun hiam?

records.english: Because the pastor baptised him, and he wanted to show special respect.
records.zomi: Bang hang hiam cih leh pastor in amah a baptaiz a, zahtakna tuam a lak nop hi.

records.english: How do we greet relatives at a wedding?
records.zomi: Mopawi-ah sanggamte bangci-in i dawnsawn ding hiam?

records.english: Go to the eldest relatives first, and let them ask about your family before you say much.
records.zomi: Sanggam upa pen te kiangah a masa-in pai inla, tam na gen ma-in na innkuan tawh kisai amaute dong sak in.

records.english: Children learn our greetings by copying their parents at every gathering.
records.zomi: Naupangte in kikhopna khempeuh-ah a nu leh pa uh zui-in i dawnsawnna te a sin uh hi.

records.english: Did your husband find our family greetings hard to learn?
records.zomi: Na pasal in i innkuan dawnsawnna te sin a haksa sa hiam?

records.english: When the pastor visits, the whole family stands to greet him.
records.zomi: Pastor a hong veh ciangin innkuan bup amah dawnsawn dingin a ding uh hi.

records.english: The way we greet each other changes when an elder is present.
records.zomi: Upa khat a om ciangin khat leh khat i kidawnsawn dan a kikhek hi.

records.english: Have you greeted everyone yet?
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh na dawnsawn khin hiam?

records.english: Our family greets newborn babies with a short prayer before anyone holds them.
records.zomi: I innkuan in kuamah in a pom ma-in naungek thakte thungetna tomno khat tawh a dawnsawn uh hi.

records.english: Why does Grandpa always ask about the crops when he greets his brothers?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pu in a sanggampate a dawnsawn ciangin lo te tawh kisai a dong den hiam?

records.english: At New Year, every family member greets the eldest with a blessing for good health.
records.zomi: Kum thak ciangin innkuan mi khempeuh in a upa pen cidamna thupha tawh a dawnsawn uh hi.

records.english: Who, if anyone, should be told before we make the announcement?
records.zomi: Theisakna i bawl ma-in kua kiangah gen ding hiam, kuamah kiangah gen kul leh?

records.english: Who cooked for you when you were ill?
records.zomi: Na dam loh lai-in kua in an hong huan sak hiam?

records.english: Who ate all the biscuits?
records.zomi: Biscuit khempeuh kua in a ne hiam?

records.english: Who was the woman you were chatting with at the bus stop?
records.zomi: Bus khawlna-ah na kihoupih numei kua hiam?

records.english: The detective wanted to know not who had taken the money, but who had known where it was kept.
records.zomi: Thu zong mi in sum kua in a la hiam cih hi lo-in, koi-ah kikem hiam cih kua in a thei hiam cih a theih nop hi.

records.english: Who did the police arrest after the robbery?
records.zomi: Sum gukna khit ciangin police in kua a man hiam?

records.english: At the school quiz night, the final question asked who had written the school song.
records.zomi: Sang' dotna kidemna zan-in dotna nunung in sang la kua in a phuak hiam cih a dong hi.

records.english: None of the teams knew, and even the head teacher had to admit that he wasn't sure.
records.zomi: Team kuamah in a thei kei uh a, sang makaipa zong in a kip kei hi, ci-in a pulak kul hi.

records.english: In the end, the elderly caretaker raised his hand and said that his own father had written it.
records.zomi: A tawp-ah inn kemtupa upa in a khut a khang a, a pa mah in a phuak hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Who painted the portrait in the hall?
records.zomi: Inn lian-a mi lim kua in a zep hiam?

records.english: A local artist whose name nobody remembers anymore.
records.zomi: Kuamah in a min a phawk nawn loh mun-a lim zepmi khat.

records.english: Who did you sit next to on the plane?
records.zomi: Vanleng tungah kua kiangah na tu hiam?

records.english: Whoever left this anonymous note clearly knows a great deal about the club's finances.
records.zomi: Min om lo lai tomno hih a nusia kua peuhmah in club' sum tawh kisai tampi a thei hi, cih a kician hi.

records.english: Who are you writing to?
records.zomi: Kua kiangah na gelh hiam?

records.english: Who knows the answer to question five?
records.zomi: Dotna nga-na' dawnna kua in a thei hiam?

records.english: Who does this jacket belong to?
records.zomi: Hih puan-ak kua' ahi hiam?

records.english: Who else is coming to dinner?
records.zomi: Nitak an-ah kua dang a hong ding hiam?

records.english: Who has been using my toothbrush?
records.zomi: Ka ha sitna kua in a zang hiam?

records.english: The quiz master refused to say who had written the hardest questions.
records.zomi: Dotna kidemna makaipa in dotna haksa pen kua in a gelh hiam cih a gen nop kei hi.

records.english: Who would be willing to read at the funeral?
records.zomi: Misi vuina-ah sim nop kua a om hiam?

records.english: Ask the guide who built the castle.
records.zomi: Kulhpi kua in a lam hiam cih lampi lakpa dong in.

records.english: It was never discovered who had sent the flowers to the hospital every week.
records.zomi: Kal simin damlo inn ah pak te kua in a khak hiam cih kithei ngei kei hi.

records.english: Who first showed that germs cause disease?
records.zomi: Natna lawngsiat neu te in natna a tunsak hi, cih kua in a masa pen-in a lak hiam?

records.english: Several scientists, though Louis Pasteur and Robert Koch are the best known.
records.zomi: Pilna mi tampi, Louis Pasteur leh Robert Koch a minthang pen uh hi napi.

records.english: Who's playing in goal today?
records.zomi: Tuni-in goal kua in a kem hiam?

records.english: Do you know the man waving at us from across the street?
records.zomi: Lampi langkhat pan khut hong lap pasal na thei hiam?

records.english: Who sang the song at the end of the film?
records.zomi: Film tawp-a la kua in a sa hiam?

records.english: Who's winning?
records.zomi: Kua in a zo hiam?

records.english: In an interview, asking who your manager will be can tell you a lot about the job.
records.zomi: Interview khat-ah na manager kua ding hiam cih dot in nasep tawh kisai tampi a gen thei hi.

records.english: Who needs a break?
records.zomi: Kua in tawlngak a kisam hiam?

records.english: Who are you hoping to meet at the conference?
records.zomi: Kikhopna lian-ah kua na muh nop hiam?

records.english: Who gets to decide what counts as good manners?
records.zomi: Bang pen om dan hoih-in kisim hiam cih kua in a khensat hiam?

records.english: Who is your favourite singer at the moment?
records.zomi: Tu hun-in na deih pen la sa kua hiam?

records.english: Who lives next door to you on the left?
records.zomi: Na veilam-a na kiang-ah kua a teng hiam?

records.english: Who said they'd bring the tent?
records.zomi: Puan inn ka paipih ding hi, kua in a ci hiam?

records.english: Who was the first person to swim across the lake?
records.zomi: Dil a kantan-a a tuipeek masa pen mi kua hiam?

records.english: Who would you invite to dinner if you could choose anyone in history?
records.zomi: Tangthu sung-a kuapeuh na teel thei leh nitak an-ah kua na sam ding hiam?

records.english: Who should I put down as my referee?
records.zomi: Ka thu pang dingin kua ka gelh ding hiam?

records.english: Your last manager, if you left on good terms.
records.zomi: Na manager nunung, hoih takin na kikhen leh.

records.english: Who gave you the idea for the business?
records.zomi: Sumbuk nasep adingin ngaihsutna kua in hong pia hiam?

records.english: Who's in the photo with you at the top of the mountain?
records.zomi: Mual tung-a photo sungah nang tawh kua a om hiam?

records.english: Who scored the winning goal?
records.zomi: Goal zawhna kua in a lut sak hiam?

records.english: Who's the quiz master at the pub tonight?
records.zomi: Tuni zan-in zu zuakna inn-a dotna kidemna makaipa kua hiam?

records.english: The landlord's son, and his questions are always about football.
records.zomi: Inn neipa' tapa, leh a dotna te football tawh kisai den hi.

records.english: Who gives the first speech at the wedding?
records.zomi: Mopawi-ah thugenna masa pen kua in a pia hiam?

records.english: Who, apart from you, has a key to the flat?
records.zomi: Nang simloh, kua in flat' tawh a nei hiam?

records.english: Who's the actor who plays the detective in that series?
records.zomi: Tua series sungah thu zong mi a lak lai mi kua hiam?

records.english: Asking who benefits is often the quickest way to understand a strange decision.

records.english: Who drew this lovely picture?
records.zomi: Hih lim hoih kua in a suai hiam?

records.english: Who are those children in the garden?
records.zomi: Huan sung-a naupangte kua te hiam?

records.english: I can't remember who lent me this book.
records.zomi: Hih laibu kua in hong pukip hiam cih ka phawk zo kei hi.

records.english: Who sent you this parcel?
records.zomi: Hih bawm kua in hong khak hiam?

records.english: Who will walk the dog while you're in hospital?
records.zomi: Damlo inn-a na om sung kua in ui a vak sak ding hiam?

records.english: Who could possibly have predicted that a tiny café would outlast the big supermarket?
records.zomi: Cafe neu khat in supermarket lian sangin a sawt zaw-in a om ding cih kua in a genkholh thei ding hiam?

records.zomi: Club vote kidemna-ah kua na huh ding hiam?

records.english: I haven't decided yet, but I'll listen to both speeches first.

records.english: Who among us has never said something we later regretted?
records.zomi: I lak-ah kua in a nung-a a kisik thu khat gen ngei lo hiam?

records.zomi: A tung lam-a flat-ah kua a hong teng ding hiam cih na thei hiam?

records.english: Who wants the last slice of pizza?
records.zomi: Pizza a nunung pen kua in a deih hiam?

records.english: The man who repaired our roof also fixed the gate for free.
records.zomi: I inn tung a bawl kik pasal in man om lo-in kongkhak zong a bawl kik hi.

records.english: Should Christians be afraid of hard questions?
records.zomi: Khristiante in dotna haksa te a lau ding uh hiam?

records.english: No, because honest questions often lead to a deeper faith.
records.zomi: Hi lo, bang hang hiam cih leh thuman taka dotna te in upna thuk zaw ah a tun zel hi.

records.english: The children asked who made the world.
records.zomi: Naupangte in leitung kua in a bawl hiam cih a dong uh hi.

records.english: Faith and reason are often presented as enemies, but many thinkers have seen them as partners.
records.zomi: Upna leh ngaihsutna pen galte bang-in kigen zel hi, ahi zongin ngaihsun siam mi tampi in lawm bang-in a mu uh hi.

records.english: Why do people believe different things?
records.zomi: Bang hangin mite in a tuamtuam-in a um uh hiam?

records.english: Faith is trusting God when you can't see everything.
records.zomi: Upna pen bangkim na muh zawh loh ciangin Pasian um ahi hi.

records.english: Is there a book you'd recommend on faith and reason?
records.zomi: Upna leh ngaihsutna tawh kisai na hilh theih laibu khat a om hiam?

records.english: It takes humility to admit that neither faith nor science has answered every question.
records.zomi: Upna in hiam, pilna in hiam dotna khempeuh a dawng khin kei hi, cih pulak dingin kiniamkhiatna a kisam hi.

records.english: Faith involves trust, but that doesn't mean it ignores reasons.
records.zomi: Upna in kium a kihel hi, ahi zongin a hang te a nusia hi, cihna hi lo hi.

records.english: Is it normal to have questions about God?
records.zomi: Pasian tawh kisai dotna neih pen a pianzia hiam?

records.english: Do you pray before an important decision?
records.zomi: Thukhensatna thupi khat ma-in thu na ngen hiam?

records.english: I find it helpful to write down my questions and bring them to the Bible study.
records.zomi: Ka dotna te gelh-a Laisiangtho sinna-ah paipih pen hong huh hi, ka ci hi.

records.english: Do you think God made the stars?
records.zomi: Pasian in aksi te a bawl hi, na ci hiam?

records.english: My brother lost his faith at university, but we still talk about it kindly.
records.zomi: Ka sanggampa in university-ah a upna a mansuah a, ahi zongin hehpihna tawh i kikup lai hi.

records.english: Some of the greatest scientists in history were also people of deep faith.
records.zomi: Tangthu sung-a pilna mi lian pen khenkhat upna thuk nei mite zong ahi uh hi.

records.english: Our Bible study group looks at the historical evidence for the life of Jesus.
records.zomi: I Laisiangtho sinna pawl in Jesu' nuntakna tawh kisai tangthu kipsakna te a en uh hi.

records.english: Why did the early Christians write so carefully about what they had seen?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Khristian masate in a muh uh te tawh kisai cian mahmah-in a gelh uh hiam?

records.english: Discussing faith respectfully means listening as carefully as you speak.

records.english: The repair café showed residents how to replace the heating element in a kettle.

records.english: When the electricity failed across the town, the community centre's battery kept the lights on for the evening.

records.english: The library lends out energy meters for free.

records.english: Our community centre turned the heating down by one degree.

records.english: After a year, three families had sold their own cars, and the street was noticeably quieter.

records.english: How does the new heating system at the swimming pool work?

records.english: The town's free bike scheme has reduced the amount of fuel burned by short car journeys.

records.english: The museum keeps its old manuscripts in rooms with carefully controlled humidity.

records.english: The ice rink uses a lot of energy to keep the ice frozen.

records.english: The school has a wind turbine on its field.

records.english: Our church hall's old boiler used more gas than all our houses put together.

records.english: Community energy projects let residents invest in renewable power and share the savings.

records.english: Are your tutor's comments usually helpful?

records.english: My lab partner is careful and very tidy.

records.english: Which of your teachers had the biggest influence on you?

records.english: The reference described him as reliable, punctual and good with customers.

records.english: A good job reference describes both your skills and your character.

records.english: What was the best teacher you ever had like?

records.english: Strict in lessons, but she always had time to listen afterwards.
records.zomi: Sinna sungah a khauh hi, ahi zongin a nung-ah ngaikhia dingin hun a nei den hi.

records.english: The caretaker is a kind old man with a white beard.

records.english: Our science teacher has a loud laugh.

records.english: At my cousin's wedding, three generations of women danced together.

records.english: Why is Grandpa so happy about my sister's engagement?

records.english: Because he knew the groom's grandfather when they were boys.
records.zomi: Bang hang hiam cih leh a naupan lai uh-in kiteeng ding pasal' pu a thei hi.

records.english: My grandfather's advice to every new couple is to settle disagreements before going to sleep.
records.zomi: Ka pu in kiteeng thak khatciat tungah a piak thuhilhna pen ihmut ma-in kinialna te a kituaksak ding ahi hi.

records.english: My husband's family welcomed me with a meal on my first evening in their home.
records.zomi: Ka pasal' innkuan in a inn uh-a ka nitak masa pen-in an tawh hong dawn uh hi.

records.english: Can I help my aunt with the wedding flowers?
records.zomi: Mopawi pak te ah ka ni ka huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: My brother and his wife live with my parents.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal leh a zi in ka nu leh ka pa tawh a teeng khawm uh hi.

records.english: Shall we start making the decorations for the wedding hall this weekend?
records.zomi: Hih kal tawp-in mopawi inn lian adingin kizepna te i bawl pan ding hiam?

records.english: Our families argued gently about the date, but in the end the elders agreed on June.
records.zomi: I innkuan te ni thu-ah nem takin a kinial uh hi, ahi zongin a tawp-ah upate in June kha a kipsak uh hi.

records.english: My grandparents believed a couple should never argue in front of their parents during the first year of marriage.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh ka pi in kiteeng nih in a kiteen kum masa sungin a nu leh a pa uh mai-ah a kinial ngei lo ding hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: How did your families decide where you would live after the wedding?
records.zomi: Mopawi khit ciangin koi-ah na teen ding uh hiam cih na innkuan te in bangci-in a khensat uh hiam?

records.english: My husband's parents offered us two rooms in their house until we could afford our own.
records.zomi: Ka pasal' nu leh pa in amau inn ah i inn i lei zawh dong inndan nih hong pia uh hi.

records.english: My mother-in-law gave me her own wedding ring when my husband and I married.
records.zomi: Ka pasal leh kei ka kiteen ciangin ka sungnu in amah' mopawi zungbuh hong pia hi.

records.english: The whole family waited outside the church for the bride.
records.zomi: Innkuan bup in biakinn pualam-ah kiteeng nu a ngak uh hi.

records.english: Has your cousin chosen a date for the wedding yet?
records.zomi: Na sanggam in mopawi ni a teel khin hiam?

records.english: Combining two family traditions in one wedding took months of patient negotiation between our mothers.
records.zomi: Mopawi khat sungah innkuan ngeina nih kigawm pen i nu te kikal-ah kha tampi sung thuakzawh taka kihoupihna a ngai hi.

records.english: The wedding gifts were laid out so that every relative could see who had given what.
records.zomi: Mopawi letsong te sanggam khatciat in kua in bang a pia hiam cih a muh theih nadingin kikoih hi.

records.english: The children sang at their aunt's wedding.
records.zomi: Naupangte in a ni uh' mopawi ah la a sa uh hi.

records.english: Are you nervous about meeting her family?
records.zomi: A innkuan kimuh ding na lau hiam?

records.english: Before the wedding, my father took my fiancé aside for a long, serious talk.
records.zomi: Mopawi ma-in ka pa in ka kiteen ding pa mun tuamah a paipih a, a sawt mahmah-in thupi takin a kihou uh hi.

records.english: Our eldest aunt reminded the couple that a marriage needs the support of both families.
records.zomi: I ni upa pen in kiteenna in innkuan nih' huhna a ngai hi, ci-in kiteeng nih a phawksak hi.

records.english: When my brother got engaged, my mother opened the old wooden chest that had come from her own wedding.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal a kiciam ciangin ka nu in amah mopawi pan a hong pai sing kuang lui a hong hi.

records.english: Inside were the blanket, the shawl and the cooking pot that her parents had given her forty years earlier.
records.zomi: A sungah kum sawmli ma-a a nu leh a pa in a piak puannap, puan-ak leh beel a om hi.

records.english: She gave them to his bride, saying that they should be used, not kept for best.
records.zomi: A kiteen ding nu a pia a, a kizang ding hi, kikem lel lo ding hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Why does Auntie keep giving me advice about marriage?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Ni in kiteenna thu-ah thuhilhna hong pia den hiam?

records.english: She's the eldest woman in the family, so she sees it as her duty.
records.zomi: Innkuan sungah numei upa pen ahih manin a tavuan bangin a ngaihsun hi.

records.english: What should I wear when we visit my fiancée's parents for the first time?
records.zomi: A masa pen-in ka kiteen ding nu' nu leh pa kiangah i pai ciangin bang ka silh ding hiam?

records.english: Something simple and respectful, and bring a small gift for her mother.
records.zomi: A baih leh zahtak huai khat, a nu adingin letsong neu khat zong paipih in.

records.english: Should we follow the old customs or do something simpler for our wedding?
records.zomi: I mopawi adingin ngeina lui te zui ding hiam, a baih zaw khat bawl ding hiam?

records.english: My grandparents' marriage was arranged by their families, but they say they grew to love each other deeply.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh ka pi' kiteenna pen a innkuan te in a kipsak uh hi, ahi zongin a kikal uh-ah itna thuk mahmah a khang hi, a ci uh hi.

records.english: Mum made a new dress for my sister's engagement.
records.zomi: Ka nu in ka sanggam numei' kiciamna adingin puan thak khat a bawl hi.

records.english: My brother asked our grandfather's advice before choosing a date for the wedding.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in mopawi ni a teel ma-in i pu' thuhilhna a ngen hi.

records.english: Living with my husband's parents after the wedding taught me patience, but it also gave me a second family.
records.zomi: Mopawi khit ciangin ka pasal' nu leh pa tawh teen khawmna in thuakzawhna hong sinsak a, innkuan nihna zong hong pia hi.

records.english: My cousin is getting married in the village.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam khua-ah a kiteeng ding hi.

records.english: When my brother's engagement was announced, relatives we hadn't heard from in years phoned to congratulate him.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal' kiciamna thu a kitheisak ciangin kum tampi sung i thu zak nai loh sanggamte in lungdam a ko nadingin phone a sam uh hi.

records.english: Our family visited the bride's family twice before the engagement.
records.zomi: Kiciamna ma-in i innkuan in kiteeng nu' innkuan nihvei a va kan uh hi.

records.english: My parents asked the pastor to visit both families before the engagement.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in kiciamna ma-in innkuan nih kiangah pastor a pai dingin a ngen uh hi.

records.english: My parents worry that families abroad are forgetting the customs that once shaped our marriages.
records.zomi: Gamdang-a om innkuan te in i kiteenna te a bawl ngeina te a mangngilh ding hi, ci-in ka nu leh ka pa a lungkham uh hi.

records.english: My uncle carried the gifts to the bride's house.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in kiteeng nu' inn ah letsong te a tawi hi.

records.english: My sister's wedding is in two months.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam numei' mopawi kha nih ciangin ahi hi.

records.english: Our family expects the groom's relatives to visit first, and we prepare a big meal for them.
records.zomi: I innkuan in kiteeng ding pasal' sanggamte a hong pai masa dingin a lamen a, amaute adingin an lian khat i bawl hi.

records.english: Did Dad give a speech at your sister's wedding?
records.zomi: Na sanggam numei' mopawi ah Paa in thu a gen hiam?

records.english: Our family keeps a notebook recording every wedding gift, so that we can show the same respect in return.
records.zomi: I innkuan in mopawi letsong khatciat a ciamtehna lai khat a kem a, zahtakna kibang a kik piak theih nading ahi hi.

records.english: My aunt is helping to choose the wedding songs.
records.zomi: Ka ni in mopawi la te teel nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: My son once asked me who made God, if God made everything.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in Pasian in na khempeuh a bawl leh, Pasian kua in a bawl hiam, ci-in hong dong ngei hi.

records.english: I told him that many believers think of God as the one being who was never made at all.
records.zomi: Upmi tampi in Pasian pen kuamah in a bawl ngei loh khat bek ahi hi, ci-in a ngaihsun uh hi, ci-in ka gen hi.

records.english: He thought about it for a minute and then asked whether he could have a biscuit.
records.zomi: Minit khat sung a ngaihsun a, tua khit ciangin biscuit khat a ne thei hiam, ci-in a dong hi.

records.english: Is beauty a good reason to believe in a Creator?
records.zomi: Hoihna pen Piangsakpa um nading a hang hoih khat ahi hiam?

records.english: We read a short book about reasons for faith.
records.zomi: Upna adinga a hang te tawh kisai laibu tom khat i sim hi.

records.english: The order in nature makes me wonder.
records.zomi: Leitung' kizopna in hong lamdangsak hi.

records.english: Our study group compared the arguments of believers and sceptics side by side.
records.zomi: I sinna pawl in upmite leh a um lote' tetteh nading thu te a kikiang-in a teh uh hi.

records.english: C. S. Lewis argued that our longing for something beyond this world points to something real that could satisfy it.
records.zomi: C. S. Lewis in hih leitung pualam-a khat i deihna pen tua deihna a lungkimsak thei taktak khat a om hi, cih a lak hi, ci-in a gen hi.

records.english: Even if an argument doesn't prove God exists, it may show that belief isn't unreasonable.
records.zomi: Tetteh nading thu khat in Pasian a om hi, ci-in a tettehsak kei zongin, upna pen a kilawm lo hi lo hi, cih a lak thei hi.

records.english: Can anyone prove that God exists?
records.zomi: Pasian a om hi, ci-in kuapeuh in a tettehsak thei hiam?

records.english: Not like a maths problem, but many people find the arguments convincing.
records.zomi: Maths dotna bangin hi lo hi, ahi zongin mi tampi in tetteh nading thu te a um huai sa uh hi.

records.english: Some people see God's hand in every sunrise.
records.zomi: Mi khenkhat in ni suah khatciat-ah Pasian' khut a mu uh hi.

records.english: The problem of evil is often raised as the strongest challenge to arguments for a good God.
records.zomi: Gitlohna dotna pen Pasian hoih a om hi, cih tetteh nading thu te tungah a haksa pen dotna bangin kilangsak zel hi.

records.english: Our class discussed reasons people give for believing in God.
records.zomi: I class in mite in Pasian a um nading uh-a a piak hang te a kihoupih uh hi.

records.english: Why is there something instead of nothing?
records.zomi: Bang hangin bangmah om lo sangin khat a om hiam?

records.english: My daughter asked me how we know God is real.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in Pasian a om taktak hi, cih bangci-in i thei hiam, ci-in hong dong hi.

records.english: Is it reasonable to believe in God?
records.zomi: Pasian um pen a kilawm hiam?

records.english: Some arguments convince me, and some don't.
records.zomi: Tetteh nading thu khenkhat in hong lungkimsak a, khenkhat in hong lungkimsak kei hi.

records.english: Do you think the universe had a beginning?
records.zomi: Leitung bup a kipatna a nei hi, na ci hiam?

records.english: The argument from design was popular long before modern science.
records.zomi: Bawlpa om hi, cih tetteh nading thu pen tu laitak science a om ma sawtpi-in mi tampi in a deih uh hi.

records.english: The cosmological argument says that the universe must have a cause outside itself.
records.zomi: Cosmological tetteh nading thu in leitung bup in amah pualam-ah a hang khat a nei ding hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Can we talk about why you believe?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na um hiam cih i kihoupih thei ding hiam?

records.english: Taking an argument seriously means facing its weaknesses as honestly as its strengths.
records.zomi: Tetteh nading thu khat thupi takin lak pen a hatna te bang mahin a hatlohna te zong thuman takin maitang ahi hi.

records.english: Did many great thinkers believe in God?
records.zomi: Ngaihsutna siam mi lian tampi in Pasian a um uh hiam?

records.english: The ontological argument tries to prove God's existence from the idea of a perfect being.
records.zomi: Ontological tetteh nading thu in a kicing Pasian' ngaihsutna pan Pasian a om hi cih a tettehsak dingin a hanciam hi.

records.english: The moral argument asks where our deep sense of right and wrong comes from.
records.zomi: Gamtat hoih leh gamtat hoih lo tetteh nading thu in thu hoih leh thu hoih lo i theihna thuk pen koi pan a hong pai hiam, ci-in a dong hi.

records.english: Some believers point to the fine balance of the laws of physics that makes life possible.
records.zomi: Upmi khenkhat in nuntakna om theihna a bawl physics thukham te' kikimna nem pen a lak uh hi.

records.english: Does everything need a cause?
records.zomi: Na khempeuh in a hang khat a ngai hiam?

records.english: Most things we know do, and some thinkers argue that the universe needs one too.
records.zomi: I theih na tamzaw in a ngai hi, ngaihsutna siam mi khenkhat in leitung bup in zong khat a ngai hi, ci-in a gen uh hi.

records.english: Many people believe in God because of the world around them.
records.zomi: Mi tampi in a kiim-a leitung hangin Pasian a um uh hi.

records.english: Critics of the design argument point out that natural processes can produce order without a designer.
records.zomi: Bawlpa om hi cih tetteh nading thu a phawkte in leitung-a kibawl tawh ngeina te in bawlpa om lo-in kizopna a bawl thei hi, ci-in a lak uh hi.

records.english: A watch needs a watchmaker, my uncle always says.
records.zomi: Nai khawl in nai khawl bawlpa a ngai hi, ci-in ka pa neu in a gen den hi.

records.english: Does the world look designed to you?
records.zomi: Leitung pen kibawl khat bang na sa hiam?

records.english: Thomas Aquinas set out five ways in which he believed God's existence could be shown.
records.zomi: Thomas Aquinas in Pasian a om hi cih a kilak thei hi, ci-in a um lam nga a gen hi.

records.english: Where did the first life come from?
records.zomi: Nuntakna masa pen koi pan a hong pai hiam?

records.english: Some people come to believe in God after asking where human consciousness comes from.
records.zomi: Mi khenkhat in mihing' theihna lungsim koi pan a hong pai hiam cih a dot khit uh ciangin Pasian a um pan uh hi.

records.english: Many people say their personal experience of God matters more to them than any argument.
records.zomi: Mi tampi in Pasian a theihna uh pen tetteh nading thu khat peuh sangin a thupi zaw hi, ci-in a gen uh hi.

records.english: Why do some scientists find the beginning of the universe so significant for belief in God?
records.zomi: Bang hangin science mi khenkhat in leitung bup' kipatna pen Pasian upna adingin thupi mahmah-in a ngaihsun uh hiam?

records.english: My philosophy teacher presented each argument and then the strongest objections to it.
records.zomi: Ka lungpil saya in tetteh nading thu khatciat a lak a, tua khit ciangin a tung-a a kidona hat pen te a lak hi.

records.english: For many Christians, the life and resurrection of Jesus are the heart of the case for God, more than abstract arguments.
records.zomi: Khristian tampi adingin Jesu' nuntakna leh a thawhkikna pen ngaihsutna bek-a tetteh nading thu sangin Pasian adinga thu' lungtang ahi hi.

records.english: My grandfather says the mountains show God's power.
records.zomi: Ka pu in mualte in Pasian' vangliatna a lak hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Believers often say their faith rests on several reasons together rather than on any single argument.
records.zomi: Upmite in a upna uh pen tetteh nading thu khat bek tungah hi lo-in hang tampi a kigawm tungah a kinga hi, ci-in a gen zel uh hi.

records.english: Philosophers have debated the classical arguments for God's existence for centuries without reaching agreement.
records.zomi: Lungpilte in Pasian a om hi cih tetteh nading thu lui te kum zalom tampi sung a kinial uh a, a kilemna ngah nai lo uh hi.

records.english: Discussing these arguments respectfully helps believers and non-believers understand each other better.
records.zomi: Hih tetteh nading thu te zahtak takin kihoupih in upmite leh a um lote a kitheisiam zaw nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: What's the argument from design?
records.zomi: Bawlpa om hi cih tetteh nading thu bang ahi hiam?

records.english: It says that the order in the universe points to a mind that designed it.
records.zomi: Leitung bup-a kizopna in amah a bawl lungsim khat a lak hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Arguments for God's existence rarely persuade someone who has already made up their mind.
records.zomi: Pasian om hi cih tetteh nading thu te in a lungsim khensat khin mi khat a lungkimsak zel kei hi.

records.english: How do you answer a friend who says there's no evidence for God?
records.zomi: Pasian adingin tettehna om lo hi, a ci lawm khat bangci-in na dawng ding hiam?

records.english: I tell them what convinces me and ask what kind of evidence they'd accept.
records.zomi: Bang in hong lungkimsak hiam cih ka gen a, bang tettehna a san ding uh hiam cih ka dong hi.

records.english: Sceptics respond that we would only be here to notice the fine-tuning if the universe allowed life in the first place.
records.zomi: A um lote in leitung bup in nuntakna a phal masak leh bek kizopna nem i muh theih nadingin hih munah i om ding hi, ci-in a dawng uh hi.

records.english: My neighbour asks me hard questions about God, and I enjoy answering them.
records.zomi: Ka inn kiang mi in Pasian tawh kisai dotna haksa te hong dong a, ka dawn nuam hi.

records.english: I find the moral argument more convincing than the scientific ones.
records.zomi: Gamtat hoih leh hoih lo tetteh nading thu pen science lam pan tetteh nading thu te sangin ka um huai sa zaw hi.

records.english: Pascal suggested that, when reason cannot decide, it is wiser to wager on God than against him.
records.zomi: Pascal in ngaihsutna in a khensat zawh loh ciangin Pasian a kalh-in hi lo-in Pasian tungah ki-ap pen a pil zaw hi, ci-in a gen hi.

records.english: The fine-tuning argument claims that the constants of nature fall within a remarkably narrow range that permits life.
records.zomi: Kizopna nem tetteh nading thu in leitung' ngeina kikhek lo te nuntakna a phal zawh nadingin a cing mahmah mun zau lo khat sungah a om hi, a ci hi.

records.english: A strong argument for God still leaves open the question of what God is like.
records.zomi: Pasian adingin tetteh nading thu hat khat in zong Pasian bangci om hiam cih dotna a hong den lai hi.

records.english: Look at the stars and ask yourself where they came from.
records.zomi: Aksite en inla, koi pan a hong pai uh hiam ci-in nangmah kidong in.

records.english: Why does the beauty of nature make you think of God?
records.zomi: Bang hangin leitung hoihna in Pasian hong ngaihsunsak hiam?

records.english: It seems too wonderful to be an accident, though I know others see it differently.
records.zomi: Kibawl lo lel ding in a lamdang lua hi, ka ci hi, ahi zongin midangte in tuamtuam-in a mu uh hi, cih ka thei hi.

records.english: Our pastor says that a world with no Creator would be hard to explain.
records.zomi: I pastor in Piangsakpa om lo leitung khat pen gen siam ding haksa ding hi, a ci hi.

records.english: I believe because of how my prayers were answered.
records.zomi: Ka thungetna a kidawn dan hangin ka um hi.

records.english: Where would you recommend for a weekend away?
records.zomi: Kal tawp khualzin adingin koi-ah na hilh ding hiam?

records.english: The question of where to spend Christmas causes more arguments in our family than anything else.
records.zomi: Christmas koi-ah zat ding cih dotna in i innkuan-ah na dang khempeuh sangin kinialna a tam zaw a piangsak hi.

records.english: The lost tourists asked so many people where the hotel was that they heard four different answers.
records.zomi: Lampi a mangthang khualzin mite in zinbuuk koi-ah a om hiam cih mi tampi a dot uh ciangin dawnna tuamtuam li a za uh hi.

records.english: Where exactly did you see the fox?
records.zomi: Ngalhia koi taktak-ah na mu hiam?

records.english: Where has the dog hidden my slipper this time?
records.zomi: Hih vei-in ui in ka khedap koi-ah a sel hiam?

records.english: Under the sofa, as usual, with the other one.
records.zomi: Sofa nuai-ah, a ngeina bangin, a dang khat tawh.

records.english: Where does your best friend live?
records.zomi: Na lawm hoih pen koi-ah a teeng hiam?

records.english: The detective asked the witness where she had been standing.
records.zomi: Detective in teci kiangah koi-ah na ding hiam, ci-in a dong hi.

records.english: Where is your new flat?
records.zomi: Na flat thak koi-ah a om hiam?

records.english: Wherever she travels, my aunt sends a postcard to every grandchild.
records.zomi: Ka ni in koi-ah khualzin zongin tu khatciat kiangah postcard khat a khak hi.

records.english: Where are you staying while the house is being repaired?
records.zomi: Inn a kibawl kik sungin koi-ah na om hiam?

records.english: Where's the best place for pizza around here?
records.zomi: Hih kiangah pizza adingin mun hoih pen koi ahi hiam?

records.english: Where did you put the shopping list?
records.zomi: Van leina lai koi-ah na koih hiam?

records.english: Where do the swallows go in the winter?
records.zomi: Khuaphal-in vahte koi-ah a pai uh hiam?

records.english: Where are we meeting the others?
records.zomi: A dang te koi-ah i kimuh ding uh hiam?

records.english: Where's the ticket office?
records.zomi: Lai man zuakna mun koi-ah a om hiam?

records.english: Where a question is asked can change the answer, so interviews are often held somewhere neutral.
records.zomi: Dotna khat a kidotna mun in dawnna a khek thei ahih manin interview te a lam lam lo mun khat-ah kibawl zel hi.

records.english: Which shop sells boots like yours?
records.zomi: Van zuakna inn bang in na khedap bang khedap sau a zuak hiam?

records.english: Where the money came from was never explained, which made people suspicious.
records.zomi: Sum koi pan a hong pai hiam cih kigen ngei lo ahih manin mite in a lungmang uh hi.

records.english: Where did you learn to speak such good French?
records.zomi: French pau a hoih mahmah-in pau dingin koi-ah na sin hiam?

records.english: At night school, and then two summers working in a hotel in Lyon.
records.zomi: Zan sang ah, tua khit ciangin Lyon khuapi-a zinbuuk khat ah khal nih sung ka sem hi.

records.english: Where did the road use to go before they built the motorway?
records.zomi: Lampi lian a bawl ma uh-in lampi koi-ah a pai zel hiam?

records.english: Where you grow up shapes your accent long before you notice it.
records.zomi: Na khanlianna mun in na phawk ma sawtpi-in na pau ging a bawl hi.

records.english: Where is the light switch in here?
records.zomi: Hih sungah meivak phiatna koi-ah a om hiam?

records.english: Where on the map is your grandmother's island?
records.zomi: Na pi' tuikulh map tungah koi-ah a om hiam?

records.english: That tiny dot just south of the big bay.
records.zomi: Tuipi lui lian' simlam ah a om tawm neu mahmah khat.

records.english: Where can we sit in the shade?
records.zomi: Limliam-ah koi-ah i tu thei ding hiam?

records.english: Please tell us where you'd like the furniture before the removal van arrives.
records.zomi: Inn suangna mawtaw a tun ma-in inn sung van te koi-ah na koih nop hiam cih hong gen in.

records.english: Knowing where to find information matters more these days than memorising it.
records.zomi: Tu hun-in thu theihna koi-ah zon ding hiam cih theih pen a ciamteh sangin a thupi zaw hi.

records.english: Has anyone seen where the cat went?
records.zomi: Zawhngeu koi-ah a pai hiam cih kuapeuh in a mu hiam?

records.english: Where were you when the lights went out?
records.zomi: Meivak a mit ciangin koi-ah na om hiam?

records.english: On my first day in the city, I asked a stranger where the cathedral was.
records.zomi: Khuapi-a ka ni masa pen-in mi theih lo khat kiangah biakinn lian koi-ah a om hiam, ci-in ka dong hi.

records.english: She didn't just point; she walked me there herself, talking about the best cafés on the way.
records.zomi: A lak lel kei a, amah mah in hong paipih a, lampi-ah cafe hoih pen te thu a gen hi.

records.english: We still meet for coffee every month, twenty years later.
records.zomi: Kum sawmnih khit ciangin zong kha simin coffee ne-in i kimu lai hi.

records.english: Cloud storage has replaced the shoebox of photos that every family once kept under the bed.

records.english: We share a folder for the children's school reports.

records.english: Teaching older relatives about cloud storage takes patience, because files that aren't anywhere physical can be a confusing idea.

records.english: My children will inherit thousands of digital photos, but I wonder whether anyone will ever look at them.

records.english: When my mother's memory began to fade, the shared photo stream helped her recognise new grandchildren.

records.english: That evening, we sat on the floor of the empty study and looked through ten years of pictures on my phone.

records.english: Should we keep copies of the children's birth certificates in the cloud?

records.english: My daughter sorted twenty years of family photos into folders by year.

records.english: Can you share the holiday videos with Grandma?

records.english: Have you saved the photos from the party?

records.english: Keeping both a cloud copy and a hard drive at home means our memories aren't in one company's hands.

records.english: My son filled up the family storage with games.

records.english: The best family backup plan is the one that runs automatically, without anyone needing to remember it.

records.english: My mum's tablet keeps asking her to buy more space.

records.english: Who uploaded three hundred photos of the cat?

records.english: My daughter's school photos are in the cloud.

records.english: Is the shared album private?

records.english: Scanning our grandparents' letters gave the whole family a way to read them without damaging the originals.

records.english: The shared folder has every bill, contract and warranty for the house.

records.english: Our first-aid instructor said that the most common mistake is assuming someone else has already called for help.

records.english: After the accident, the site manager gave the hospital a clear account of what had happened.

records.english: Her teacher stayed beside her while another student ran to the office with a note saying where she was and that she was having an asthma attack.

records.english: Teachers on school trips carry a list of each child's medical needs and emergency contacts.

records.english: The police asked witnesses to describe the evening step by step, starting from the moment the shop closed.
records.zomi: Palik te in teci te kiangah van zuakna inn a kikhak hun pan kipan-in nitak thu a kalsuan in gen dingin a ngen uh hi.

records.english: The museum arranges its rooms in order, so visitors walk forward through time.
records.zomi: Tangthu van kemna inn in a inndan te a kizom in a koih ahih manin mikhualte hun sung-ah mai lam ah a pai uh hi.

records.zomi: Bang hun-in khuapi in misi vuina mun lui zat a khawl hiam?

records.english: Comparing the census returns decade by decade shows how quickly the population grew after the factory opened.

records.english: The health centre published a timeline for moving all its services to the new building.

records.english: Can you help me put these old photos of the high street in order?
records.zomi: Lampi lian' photo lui te a kizom in koih nadingin hong huh thei ding na hiam?

records.english: Yes, look at the cars and the shop signs; they'll tell you roughly when each was taken.
records.zomi: Thei hi, mawtaw te leh van zuakna inn ciamtehna te en in; bang hun-in kila hiam cih a kinai deuh-in hong gen ding hi.

records.english: The local paper ran a series showing the town in 1900, 1950 and today.
records.zomi: Mun thuthak lai in 1900, 1950 leh tu ni-a khuapi a lak thu kizom khat a suah hi.

records.english: The heritage trail places each building in the town's history, from medieval inn to modern library.
records.zomi: Ngeina tangthu pai lampi in inn khatciat khuapi' tangthu sungah a koih hi, tangthu lai hun-a zinbuuk pan tu hun-a laibu inn dong.

records.english: The council's timeline for the new sea wall was published so that residents could see when each section would be finished.
records.zomi: Council' tuipi kiang bang thak adinga hun kizom lak in teng mite in khen khatciat bang hun-in zo ding hiam cih a muh theih nadingin kisuah hi.

records.zomi: Damlo inn' tangthu in a nasep tampi pen thalawpte in a bawl huhna pawl neu te-in a kipan uh hi, cih a lak hi.

records.english: Which came first in this town, the railway or the canal?

records.english: The canal, by about fifty years, and the railway later followed it along the valley.
records.zomi: Tuiluang laam, kum sawmnga bang-in, tua khit ciangin meileng lampi in guam kawm-ah a zui hi.

records.english: How long has the post office been on this street?

records.english: Which is older, the church or the castle?

records.zomi: Ka sinsak kum masa sung-a ni sim ciamtehna ka kem ahih manin tua ni gim mahmah, lamdang mahmah te ka phawk kik thei lai hi.

records.english: The day I was trusted to run the shop alone, I realised how much my manager believed in me.
records.zomi: Van zuakna inn keimah bek-in a kem dingin hong muan ni-in ka makaipa in bangzah hong um hiam cih ka thei hi.

records.english: On the morning of my first job interview, it was pouring with rain, and I missed the bus.
records.zomi: Ka nasep interview masa pen zingsang-in guah a zu mahmah a, bus ka mansuah hi.

records.english: I ran the whole way and arrived soaked, with my notes stuck together.
records.zomi: Lampi bup ka tai a, ka diah bup-in ka tung a, ka ciamtehna lai te a kibelh khawm hi.

records.english: The interviewer laughed, lent me a towel and offered me the job before the end of the afternoon.
records.zomi: Interview la a nui a, puan-ip khat hong puksak a, sun nung lam a bei ma-in nasep hong pia hi.

records.english: Have you still got the photo from your first day at work?
records.zomi: Nasep mun-a na ni masa pen pan photo na nei lai hiam?

records.english: Looking back, my first day as a teacher was chaotic, but I learned more on that first day than in a year of training.
records.zomi: A nung lam ka et ciangin saya-a ka ni masa pen a buai mahmah hi, ahi zongin kum khat sinna sangin tua ni masa pen-in tam zaw ka sin hi.

records.english: Everyone wore their best uniform when the new head teacher arrived.
records.zomi: Sang makaipa thak a tun ciangin mi khempeuh in a puan kibang hoih pen uh a silh uh hi.

records.english: The day the inspectors came, the whole school was unusually quiet and polite.
records.zomi: Enkipa te a hong ni-in sang bup a dai mahmah a, zahtakna a nei lamdang uh hi.

records.english: Do you remember the day the school closed for snow?
records.zomi: Vuk hangin sang a kikhak ni na phawk hiam?

records.english: The office closed early because of the heat.
records.zomi: Khuasa hangin office a kikhak masa hi.

records.english: I'll never forget the morning I walked into the hospital as a qualified doctor.
records.zomi: Siavuan cian-in damlo inn ah ka lut zingsang ka mangngilh ngei kei ding hi.

records.english: Was the school's centenary the busiest day the building had ever seen?
records.zomi: Sang' kum za kikimna pen inn in a muh ngei buai pen ni ahi hiam?

records.english: How did your first pay cheque make you feel?
records.zomi: Na nasep man masa pen in bangci-in hong kisaksak hiam?

records.english: When the strike ended and we went back to work, the factory felt different, as if something had been won.
records.zomi: Nasep khawlna a bei a, nasep ah i ciah kik ciangin van bawlna inn a tuam bang kilang a, na khat i zo bang hi.

records.english: Do you remember your first day as a teacher?
records.zomi: Saya-a na ni masa pen na phawk hiam?

records.english: Vividly, because a pupil was sick on my shoes before nine o'clock.
records.zomi: Cian takin ka phawk hi, bang hang hiam cih leh nai kua ma-in sangnaupang khat in ka khedap tungah a lua hi.

records.english: Was your first day at university scary?
records.zomi: University-a na ni masa pen a lauhuai hiam?

records.english: My grandfather's first day at the mine, when he was only fourteen, is a story our family still tells.
records.zomi: Kum sawm leh li bek a hih lai-in leikhuk-ah ka pu' ni masa pen pen i innkuan in a gen lai tangthu khat ahi hi.

records.english: Our class went to the beach on the last day of school.
records.zomi: Sang' ni nunung pen-in i class tuipi kiang ah a pai uh hi.

records.english: When I finally got the job offer, I called my mother from the car park.
records.zomi: A tawp-ah nasep pia dingin hong sam ciangin mawtaw khawlna mun pan ka nu phone ka sam hi.

records.english: A memorable school day for a child might be one that adults have completely forgotten.
records.zomi: Naupang khat adinga phawk huai sang ni pen upate in a mangngilh bup ni khat ahi thei hi.

records.english: Do you remember what you wore to your first interview?
records.zomi: Na interview masa pen ah bang na silh hiam cih na phawk hiam?

records.english: The school's last day before the summer always ended with a water fight on the field.
records.zomi: Khal ma-a sang' ni nunung pen mual tungah tui kikapna tawh a bei den hi.

records.english: Which moment in your training stands out for you?
records.zomi: Na sinna sungah hun bang in nangma adingin a kilang pen hiam?

records.english: I forgot my lines halfway through the school play.
records.zomi: Sang lam lakna lai-ah ka kammal te ka mangngilh hi.

records.english: Our teacher cried on her last day before retiring.
records.zomi: I saya in nasep a nusiat ma-a a ni nunung pen-in a kap hi.

records.english: Who showed you around on your first morning?
records.zomi: Na zingsang masa pen-in kua in hong kiimah paipih hiam?

records.english: Did your boss really buy cakes for everyone on your birthday?
records.zomi: Na pianni-in na makaipa in mi khempeuh adingin cake a lei taktak hiam?

records.english: During my first presentation, my hands shook so much that I could barely hold my notes.
records.zomi: Ka lakna masa pen sungin ka khut a ling mahmah ahih manin ka ciamtehna lai te ka len zo dek kei hi.

records.english: At the end of my apprenticeship, my mentor gave me his own set of tools.
records.zomi: Ka nasep sinna a bei ciangin hong makaipa in amah' van te hong pia hi.

records.english: On my last day at the bank, my colleagues decorated my desk with balloons.
records.zomi: Bank-a ka ni nunung pen-in ka nasem pihte in ka dawhkan balloon te tawh a zep uh hi.

records.english: On the day the new hospital wing opened, staff who had campaigned for it for years stood at the door to greet patients.
records.zomi: Damlo inn khen thak a kihon ni-in kum tampi sung a ngen nasemte damlote dawn dingin kongkhak-ah a ding uh hi.

records.english: Our trip to the science museum was the first time many of the children had been on a train.
records.zomi: Science tangthu van kemna inn ah i khualzinna pen naupang tampi in meileng a tuan masa pen uh ahi hi.

records.english: Our retirement book collects colleagues' memories of their best and worst days in the office.
records.zomi: I nasep nusiat laibu in nasem pihte' office-a a ni hoih pen leh a hoih lo pen te' phawkna a kaikhawm hi.

records.english: Our children feel more connected to the old country after a celebration than at any other time of year.
records.zomi: I tate in kum sung hun dang khat peuh sangin pawi khit ciangin gam lui tawh a kizopna uh a lian zaw hi, a kisa uh hi.

records.english: My husband, who grew up in a different culture, now looks forward to our celebrations more than I do.
records.zomi: Ngeina tuam khat sungah a khanglian ka pasal in tu-in kei sangin i pawi te a lamen zaw hi.

records.english: Who will look after the baby during the dance?
records.zomi: Lam laitak-in naungek kua in a kem ding hiam?

records.english: The money our family saves all year for the celebration is spent gladly, because it brings everyone together.
records.zomi: I innkuan in pawi adingin kum bup a kemsak sum pen lungdam takin kizang hi, bang hang hiam cih leh mi khempeuh a kikaikhawmsak hi.

records.english: Is Auntie bringing her famous soup?
records.zomi: Ni in a an tui minthang a paipih ding hiam?

records.english: Our family gave money to help pay for the hall.
records.zomi: I innkuan in inn lian man piak nadingin sum a pia hi.

records.english: My parents met at a community celebration, so the day is special for our family.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa mipi pawi khat ah a kimu uh ahih manin tua ni pen i innkuan adingin a tuam hi.

records.english: Did the children stay up very late?
records.zomi: Naupangte zan nung mahmah dong a ihmu kei uh hiam?

records.english: Why does Mum cook so much before the Christmas gathering?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Christmas kikhopna ma-in ka nu in an tampi a huan hiam?

records.english: Every family brings food to share, and she never wants ours to run out.
records.zomi: Innkuan khatciat in hawm ding an a paipih a, i an a bei ding a deih ngei kei hi.

records.english: My daughter was nervous about her first traditional dance, but her grandmother practised with her for weeks.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in a ngeina lam masa pen a lau hi, ahi zongin a pi in kal tampi sung amah tawh a kisin hi.

records.english: Last December, my family hosted the community's Christmas dinner for the first time.
records.zomi: December beisa-in ka innkuan in a masa pen-in mipi' Christmas nitak an a bawl hi.

records.english: My father cooked for two days, my sisters decorated the hall, and the children wrapped small gifts for every guest.
records.zomi: Ka pa in ni nih sung an a huan a, ka sanggam numeite in inn lian a zep uh a, naupangte in mikhual khatciat adingin letsong neu te a tuam uh hi.

records.english: When the last guest left, we sat on the floor among the empty pots, too tired to talk but very happy.
records.zomi: Mikhual nunung pen a ciah ciangin beel a om nawn lo te lak-ah zang tungah i tu a, kihoupih ding gim lua napi lungdam mahmah hi.

records.english: In my family, missing the annual celebration without a good reason is quietly noticed by everyone.
records.zomi: Ka innkuan sungah kum simin pawi a hang hoih om lo-in nusia pen mi khempeuh in dai takin a phawk hi.

records.english: Watching my son lead the dance this year, I remembered my own father doing the same thing.
records.zomi: Hih kum-in ka tapa in lam a makaih ka en ciangin ka pa in tua mah a bawl ngei hun ka phawk hi.

records.english: My mother wore her mother's traditional dress.
records.zomi: Ka nu in a nu' ngeina puan a silh hi.

records.english: Did we take enough photos of the whole family?
records.zomi: Innkuan bup' photo i la tawk hiam?

records.english: My little brother carried the flag this year.
records.zomi: Hih kum-in ka nau pasal in puanzal a tawi hi.

records.english: Shall we bring the drum from Grandpa's house?
records.zomi: Pu' inn pan khuang i la ding hiam?

records.english: My parents say that preparing for a celebration teaches children more about their culture than any book.
records.zomi: Pawi adinga kiginna in naupangte a ngeina uh thu laibu khat peuh sangin tam zaw a sinsak hi, ci-in ka nu leh ka pa in a gen uh hi.

records.english: Should we teach our children the old dances, or let them choose for themselves?
records.zomi: I tate lam lui te i sinsak ding hiam, amau mah in a teel dingin i nusia ding hiam?

records.english: Our family recorded Grandma singing the old songs so that the children could learn them.
records.zomi: Naupangte in a sin theih nadingin i innkuan in Pi in la lui te a sak a la uh hi.

records.english: Everyone in our family joined in the last song.
records.zomi: I innkuan-a mi khempeuh la nunung pen ah a kihel uh hi.

records.english: My cousins came from far away for the celebration.
records.zomi: Ka sanggamte pawi adingin gamla pan a hong pai uh hi.

records.english: We keep the dance costumes in a box under my parents' bed.
records.zomi: Lam puan te ka nu leh ka pa' lupna nuai-a bawm khat sungah i kem hi.

records.english: Grandma makes the best rice cakes for the celebration.
records.zomi: Pi in pawi adingin buh moh hoih pen a bawl hi.

records.english: When my aunt could not travel, we joined the celebration by video call from her hospital room.
records.zomi: Ka ni a khualzin zawh loh ciangin a damlo inndan pan video call tawh pawi ah i kihel hi.

records.english: We practised the dance at home every evening.
records.zomi: Nitak simin inn ah lam i kisin hi.

records.english: Every celebration ends with my father thanking each family that helped.
records.zomi: Pawi khatciat ka pa in a huh innkuan khatciat lungdam a kohna tawh a bei hi.

records.english: My family always goes to the harvest festival together.
records.zomi: Ka innkuan buh lak pawi ah a kikhawm-in a pai den uh hi.

records.english: Our children learn the traditional songs by singing them in the car on the way to the hall.
records.zomi: I tate in inn lian pai lampi-ah mawtaw sungah a sak tawh ngeina la te a sin uh hi.

records.english: Why does Grandpa always sit with the other elders instead of with us?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pu in ei tawh hi lo-in upa dangte tawh a tu den hiam?

records.english: My grandparents' stories about celebrations in the village make our modern ones feel part of a long tradition.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh ka pi' khua-a pawi tawh kisai tangthu te in tu hun-a i pawi te ngeina sau khat' khen khat bangin hong kisaksak hi.

records.english: Grandma insists that every grandchild greets the elders before joining the games.
records.zomi: Pi in tu khatciat in kimawlna ah a kihel ma-in upate a dawnsawn dingin a ngen den hi.

records.english: Are we taking Grandma to the harvest celebration?
records.zomi: Buh lak pawi ah Pi i paipih ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, and your uncle will drive her so that she doesn't have to take the bus.
records.zomi: Paipih ding hi, bus a tuan lohna dingin na pa neu in a tawi ding hi.

records.english: For our family, the community celebrations are the only times when four generations are together in one room.
records.zomi: I innkuan adingin mipi pawi te bek in suan li inndan khat sungah a kikhawm hun ahi hi.

records.english: When my grandmother could no longer cook, the younger women of the family took over her famous dishes.
records.zomi: Ka pi in an a huan zawh nawn loh ciangin innkuan-a numei khangno te in a an minthang te a la zom uh hi.

records.english: After the celebration, my parents always drive the oldest relatives home.
records.zomi: Pawi khit ciangin ka nu leh ka pa in sanggam upa pen te inn ah a tawi den uh hi.

records.english: My cousin's baby was blessed in front of the whole community at the harvest service.
records.zomi: Buh lak pawlpi kikhopna ah ka sanggam' naungek mipi bup mai-ah thupha kipia hi.

records.english: Did you see Grandpa dancing?
records.zomi: Pu a lam na mu hiam?

records.english: Dad helped to set up the chairs in the hall.
records.zomi: Paa in inn lian sungah tutphah te a koih huh hi.

records.english: Some of my relatives worry that our celebrations are becoming shorter and less traditional.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam khenkhat in i pawi te a tom semsem a, ngeina tawh a kituak semsem lo hi, ci-in a lungkham uh hi.

records.english: My sister read a poem at the celebration.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam numei in pawi ah la phuak khat a sim hi.

records.english: My brother and I always help to wash the huge cooking pots after the celebration.
records.zomi: Pawi khit ciangin ka sanggam pasal leh kei beel lian mahmah te sil dingin i huh den hi.

records.english: Mixed families in our community often combine customs from both sides at the celebration.
records.zomi: I mipi sung-a innkuan kigawm te in pawi ah lam nih pan ngeina te a gawm zel uh hi.

records.english: Can I wear Grandpa's old shirt to the cultural evening?
records.zomi: Ngeina nitak ah Pu' puan-ak lui ka silh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, he'd be proud, but ask Grandma first.
records.zomi: Thei hi, a kisa ding hi, ahi zongin Pi dong masa in.

records.english: The celebration was the first time my children saw so many of their relatives in one place.
records.zomi: Pawi pen ka tate in a sanggam tampi mun khat-ah a muh masa pen uh ahi hi.

records.english: Can we invite our neighbours to the cultural evening?
records.zomi: Ngeina nitak ah i inn kiang mite i sam thei ding hiam?

records.english: Is our family making the tea for everyone in the hall again?
records.zomi: Inn lian sungah mi khempeuh adingin i innkuan in lahpek a bawl kik ding hiam?

records.english: Grandpa told the story of the first celebration abroad.
records.zomi: Pu in gamdang-a pawi masa pen tangthu a gen hi.

records.english: Why do you always cry at the community's New Year service?
records.zomi: Bang hangin mipi' Kum Thak pawlpi kikhopna ah na kap den hiam?

records.english: It reminds me of my parents, who used to sit in the front row every year.
records.zomi: Kum simin mai lam tut dan masa pen-ah a tu ngei ka nu leh ka pa hong phawksak hi.

records.english: Who in our family is singing at the celebration this year?
records.zomi: Hih kum-in pawi ah i innkuan-a kua in la a sa ding hiam?

records.english: Your cousins, and your aunt is leading the choir.
records.zomi: Na sanggamte, na ni in la sa pawl a makaih ding hi.

records.english: Mum sewed new clothes for us for the festival.
records.zomi: Ka nu in pawi adingin puan thak te hong khui hi.

records.english: Every year, my grandfather gives a short blessing before the meal begins.
records.zomi: Kum simin an kipat ma-in ka pu in thupha ngetna tomno khat a gen hi.

records.english: Our family sat together at the long table.
records.zomi: I innkuan dawhkan sau tungah a kikhawm-in a tu uh hi.

records.english: Natural disasters raise a different challenge, because no human choice seems to cause them.
records.zomi: Leitung buaina lian te in dotna tuam khat a piangsak hi, bang hang hiam cih leh mihing teelna khat in a piangsak bang a kilang kei hi.

records.english: Why does God allow earthquakes?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pasian in leiling a phal hiam?

records.english: The free will defence suggests that love requires the freedom to choose, and freedom brings the risk of evil.
records.zomi: Suahtakna-a teelna dawnna in itna in teelna suahtakna a ngai a, suahtakna in gitlohna lauhuai a paipih hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Some suffering is caused by human choices, while some comes from disease or natural disasters.
records.zomi: Thuakna khenkhat mihing teelna in a piangsak a, khenkhat natna ahih kei leh leitung buaina lian pan a hong pai hi.

records.english: Honest believers admit that the problem of evil remains one of the strongest objections to their faith.
records.zomi: Thuman upmite in gitlohna dotna pen a upna uh tunga kidona hat pen te lak-a khat ahi lai hi, ci-in a pom uh hi.

records.english: Some believers say that a world with real freedom must include the possibility of evil.
records.zomi: Upmi khenkhat in suahtakna taktak nei leitung khat in gitlohna om theihna a huam ding hi, ci-in a gen uh hi.

records.english: How would you comfort a friend who says God has abandoned them?
records.zomi: Pasian in hong nusia hi, a ci lawm khat bangci-in na lungmuansak ding hiam?

records.english: The church brought food to the family after the fire.
records.zomi: Mei kat khit ciangin pawlpi in innkuan adingin an a paipih hi.

records.english: Theologians have warned against answers to suffering that make God sound cruel or make victims feel blamed.
records.zomi: Pasian thu siam mite in Pasian a gilo bang a kilangsak ahih kei leh a thuak mite a mawh bang a kisaksak thuakna dawnna te a vaukholh uh hi.

records.english: Christian tradition holds that the cross shows God entering suffering rather than standing apart from it.
records.zomi: Khristian ngeina in singlamteh in Pasian thuakna pan a kikhen lo-in thuakna sungah a lut hi, cih a lak hi, ci-in a pom hi.

records.english: Can we pray for the people in the war?
records.zomi: Galdona sung-a mite adingin thu i ngen thei ding hiam?

records.english: Many believers find that sitting with someone in their grief is more faithful than trying to explain it.
records.zomi: Upmi tampi in mi khat a dahna sungah a kiangah tu pen a gen siam dinga hanciam sangin upna nei zaw ahi hi, cih a mu uh hi.

records.english: My grandmother trusted God through very hard years.
records.zomi: Ka pi in kum haksa mahmah te sungin Pasian a muang hi.

records.english: Philosophers distinguish between showing that evil and God are logically compatible and explaining why God permits particular evils.
records.zomi: Lungpilte in gitlohna leh Pasian a kituak thei hi, cih lak leh bang hangin Pasian in gitlohna khenkhat a phal hiam cih gen a khen uh hi.

records.english: Many of the Psalms are honest cries of pain and confusion addressed to God.
records.zomi: Late tampi pen natna leh lungbuaina tawh Pasian kiangah thuman taka kikou-na ahi hi.

records.english: My pastor admitted that he doesn't have a neat answer to the problem of evil.
records.zomi: Ka pastor in gitlohna dotna adingin dawnna cian khat ka nei kei hi, ci-in a pom hi.

records.english: The book of Job ends without explaining Job's suffering, yet he meets God in a new way.
records.zomi: Job laibu in Job' thuakna a gen siam lo-in a bei hi, ahi zongin lam thak khat-in Pasian a kimuh hi.

records.english: Some Christians find hope in the promise that God will one day wipe away every tear.
records.zomi: Khristian khenkhat in Pasian in ni khat ciangin khitui khempeuh a nul siang ding hi, cih kamciamna sungah lametna a mu uh hi.

records.english: The Bible tells many stories of people who suffered.
records.zomi: Laisiangtho in a thuak mi tampi' tangthu a gen hi.

records.english: Can suffering ever lead to something good?
records.zomi: Thuakna in na hoih khat ah a paipih thei ngei hiam?

records.english: Sometimes it does, though that never makes the suffering itself good.
records.zomi: Khatvei khat ciangin a paipih hi, ahi zongin tua in thuakna mah a hoihsak ngei kei hi.

records.english: Hold on to hope, even in the dark.
records.zomi: Khuamial sungah zong lametna len den in.

records.english: When my grandmother was dying, a young nurse asked her how she could still smile.
records.zomi: Ka pi a sih kuan ciangin nurse khangno khat in bangci-in na nuih thei lai hiam, ci-in a dong hi.

records.english: Grandma said she didn't understand why she was suffering, but she trusted that she wasn't suffering alone.
records.zomi: Pi in bang hangin ka thuak hiam cih ka theisiam kei hi, ahi zongin keimah bek ka thuak kei hi, cih ka muang hi, a ci hi.

records.english: The nurse came back the next day to ask more, and they talked until visiting hours ended.
records.zomi: Nurse in a ni zom-in dong behlap dingin a hong kik a, mi kan hun a bei dong a kihoupih uh hi.

records.english: My friend lost his faith after his mother died.
records.zomi: Ka lawm in a nu a sih khit ciangin a upna a mansuah hi.

records.english: Why doesn't God stop wars?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pasian in galdona te a khawlsak kei hiam?

records.english: Many Christians believe God gives people real freedom, even when they use it to hurt each other.
records.zomi: Khristian tampi in mite in a kisusia nadingin a zat uh hun-in zong Pasian in suahtakna taktak a pia hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: Sometimes I feel that God is far away.
records.zomi: Khatvei khat ciangin Pasian a gamla bang ka kisa hi.

records.english: Do you think it's possible to trust God without understanding why something happened?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na khat a piang hiam cih theisiam lo-in Pasian muan theih ahi hi, na ci hiam?

records.english: I don't understand why there is so much pain.
records.zomi: Bang hangin natna tampi a om hiam cih ka theisiam kei hi.

records.english: My son asked why his dog had to die.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in bang hangin a ui a si ding hiam, ci-in a dong hi.

records.english: Our pastor said it's all right to have questions.
records.zomi: I pastor in dotna neih pen a hoih hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Is it wrong to be angry with God?
records.zomi: Pasian tungah heh pen a khial hiam?

records.english: Many people in the Bible were, and they still kept talking to him.
records.zomi: Laisiangtho sung-a mi tampi a heh uh a, ahi zongin amah tawh a kihoupih lai uh hi.

records.english: After the accident, our neighbours' kindness helped us more than any explanation.
records.zomi: Lamdang tunna khit ciangin i inn kiang mite' hehpihna in genna khat peuh sangin hong huh zaw hi.

records.english: For some people, the problem of evil is an intellectual puzzle; for others, it is a wound.
records.zomi: Mi khenkhat adingin gitlohna dotna pen ngaihsutna buaina khat ahi a, midangte adingin liamna khat ahi hi.

records.english: Job lost everything, but he kept talking to God.
records.zomi: Job in na khempeuh a mansuah a, ahi zongin Pasian tawh a kihoupih den hi.

records.english: Why did God let the storm destroy our church?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pasian in huihpi in i biakinn a susia dingin a phal hiam?

records.english: Hope in the face of suffering does not deny the pain; it refuses to let the pain have the final word.
records.zomi: Thuakna mai-a lametna in natna a nial kei a; natna in thu nunung a gen dingin a phal kei hi.

records.english: We prayed for her, but she still died.
records.zomi: Amah adingin thu i ngen hi, ahi zongin a si lai hi.

records.english: Christians believe that Jesus himself suffered, so God is not distant from human pain.
records.zomi: Khristiante in Jesu amah mah a thuak hi, ci-in a um uh ahih manin Pasian pen mihing natna pan a gamla kei hi.

records.zomi: Gam tuamtuam-a khuapi te kikal-a kizopna te galdona khit ciangin kilemna lam nading lam khat-in a kipan hi.

records.zomi: Thukham office in nasep sinna mite in ni simin a zat uh thukhenna lui te' laibu inn khat a kem hi.
