records.english: What happened to the high street when the supermarket opened?
records.zomi: Supermarket a kihon ciangin lampi lian bang a suak hiam?

records.english: Several small shops closed within two years, and the street became much quieter.
records.zomi: Kum nih sungin van zuakna inn neu tampi a kikhak a, lampi a dai zaw mahmah hi.

records.english: Gas lamps on the main streets made people feel safer walking home after dark.
records.zomi: Lampi lian te tunga gas meivak te in mite zan-in inn ah pai ciah ding a bit zaw kisaksak hi.

records.english: After the road was built, the village shop closed.
records.zomi: Lampi a kibawl khit ciangin khua van zuakna inn a kikhak hi.

records.english: The new health centre reduced the queues at the hospital's emergency department.
records.zomi: Cidamna office thak in damlo inn' hun haksa damsakna mun-a kituanna te a niamsak hi.

records.english: The market closed because the rents went up.
records.zomi: Inn man a khan manin sumbuk mun a kikhak hi.

records.english: The canal brought coal and jobs to the valley.
records.zomi: Tuiluang laam in guam ah suangtual leh nasep te a hong paipih hi.

records.english: Why did the population double in the 1960s?
records.zomi: Bang hangin 1960 kum te-ah mi zah a nihvei a khang hiam?

records.english: When the ferry service ended, the island's population began to shrink.
records.zomi: Tembaw kantanna nasep a bei ciangin tuikulh' mi zah a kiam pan hi.

records.english: After a fire destroyed the wooden houses, the council required all new buildings to be made of brick.
records.zomi: Mei in sing inn te a susiat khit ciangin council in inn thak khempeuh inn suang tawh kilam dingin a ngen hi.

records.english: Older people now travel to the next town since the bank closed.
records.zomi: Bank a kikhak pan kipan mi upate khuapi zom ah a khualzin uh hi.

records.english: The fire led to new building rules.
records.zomi: Mei in inn lamna thukham thak te a piangsak hi.

records.english: Why are there so many Victorian schools in this part of the city?
records.zomi: Bang hangin khuapi lian' hih khen-ah Victoria hun-a sang tampi a om hiam?

records.english: A law in the 1870s required every area to provide schools for young children.
records.zomi: 1870 kum te-a thukham khat in mun khatciat in naupang neute adingin sang a piak dingin a ngen hi.

records.english: Public health measures introduced after past epidemics still protect the town today.
records.zomi: Natna kizelna lui te khit ciangin kikoih mipi cidamna bawl dan te in tu ni dong khuapi a kem lai hi.

records.english: Understanding why the town changed helps residents argue more convincingly about what should happen next.
records.zomi: Bang hangin khuapi a kikhek hiam cih theisiam in teng mite in a zom-a bang a piang ding hiam cih tawh kisai lungkimhuai zaw-in a gen thei nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: The decision to close the youth club was followed by complaints about teenagers in the park.
records.zomi: Khangno pawl inn khak dinga thukhensatna khit ciangin park-a khangnote tawh kisai phunna te a hong om hi.

records.english: The first public library in the town was paid for by a wealthy mill owner.
records.zomi: Khuapi-a mipi laibu inn masa pen pen puan khotna inn nei hau mi khat in a man a pia hi.

records.english: Why are the houses on the seafront raised above the pavement?
records.zomi: Bang hangin tuipi kiang-a inn te lampi suang sangin a sang zaw-in kilam uh hiam?

records.english: A great storm had destroyed dozens of houses along the front, and the council never wanted it to happen again.
records.zomi: Huihpi lian khat in tuipi kiang-a inn sawm tampi a susia a, council in tua bang piang kik ding a deih ngei kei hi.

records.english: Why did the council plant trees on the hillside?
records.zomi: Bang hangin council in mual pang-ah singkung te a suan hiam?

records.english: Because the town's population grew so quickly, a second secondary school had to be built.
records.zomi: Khuapi' mi zah a manlang mahmah-in a khan manin sang lian nihna khat a kilam ding a ngai hi.

records.english: Why is the hospital so far from the town centre?
records.zomi: Bang hangin damlo inn khuapi lai pan a gamla mahmah hiam?

records.english: It was built there during an epidemic, when patients were kept away from crowded streets.
records.zomi: Natna kizelna hun-in tua munah a kilam a, tua hun-in damlote mi tam lampi te pan a gamla-in a kikem uh hi.

records.english: Rising house prices have pushed many young families out of the old town.
records.zomi: Inn man khanna in innkuan khangno tampi khuapi lui pan a hawlkhia hi.

records.english: Some changes that seemed small at the time, such as moving the market day, reshaped the whole town.
records.zomi: Tua hun-in a neu bang kilang kikhekna khenkhat, sumbuk ni suan bang, in khuapi bup a khek hi.

records.english: The great storm of the 1950s still affects where the council allows new houses to be built.
records.zomi: 1950 kum te-a huihpi lian in council in inn thak te koi-ah a kilam dingin a phal hiam cih a khoih lai hi.

records.english: The opening of the motorway turned the quiet market town into a busy commuter town.
records.zomi: Lampi lian a kihon in khuapi neu dai khat nasep mun ah pai kik mite' khuapi buai khat-in a khek hi.

records.english: What effect did the new ring road have on the shops in the centre?
records.zomi: Khuapi kiim-a lampi thak in khuapi lai-a van zuakna inn te tungah bang gah a nei hiam?

records.english: The museum shows how the town's first hospital was founded after a smallpox outbreak killed dozens of children.
records.zomi: Tangthu van kemna inn in nasuah natna kizelna in naupang sawm tampi a sih khit ciangin khuapi' damlo inn masa pen bangci-in kiphut hiam cih a lak hi.

records.english: Free parking brought shoppers back to the high street.
records.zomi: Man om lo mawtaw khawlna in van leite lampi lian ah a hong ciah kiksak hi.

records.english: The café lost customers after the bus route changed.
records.zomi: Bus lampi a kikhek khit ciangin cafe in van lei mite a mansuah hi.

records.english: Who took these old photos of the harbour?
records.zomi: Tembaw tual' photo lui te kua in a la hiam?

records.english: A fisherman who worked here in the 1950s, and his daughter gave them to the school.
records.zomi: 1950 kum te-a hih munah a sem ngabeng mi khat in a la a, a tanu in sang a pia hi.

records.english: The closure of the mill was a turning point that older residents still describe as the end of an era.
records.zomi: Puan khotna inn a kikhak pen teng mi upate in hun khat' tawpna ci-in a gen lai uh kikheina khat ahi hi.

records.english: The school's first pupils wrote on slates.
records.zomi: Sang' sangnaupang masa te in suang pek tungah lai a gelh uh hi.

records.english: Community history projects at school help pupils see that ordinary jobs shaped the place they live.
records.zomi: Sang-a mipi tangthu nasep te in sangnaupangte nasep ngeina te in a teen na mun uh a bawl hi, cih a muh nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Our project compared the jobs people did in the town in 1900 with the jobs they do today.
records.zomi: I nasep in 1900 kum-a khuapi-ah mite' sep nasep te tu hun-a a sep uh nasep te tawh a teh hi.

records.english: Local businesses that have lasted for generations often hold records that tell the story of the whole town.
records.zomi: Suan tampi sung a dai mun-a sumbuk te in khuapi bup' tangthu a gen ciamtehna te a kem zel uh hi.

records.english: How long has the factory been in the town?
records.zomi: Van bawlna inn khuapi-ah bangzah sawt a om khin hiam?

records.english: Since 1921, and some families have worked there for four generations.
records.zomi: 1921 kum pan, innkuan khenkhat suan li sung tua munah a sem uh hi.

records.english: Learning that our school had survived two wars and a fire made the students prouder of its old buildings.
records.zomi: I sang galdona nih leh mei khat a pelh hi, cih theih in sangnaupangte a inn lui uh tungah a kisa zaw uh hi.

records.english: Why did the town's first school open in a church?
records.zomi: Bang hangin khuapi' sang masa pen biakinn khat sungah a kihong hiam?

records.english: There was no other building big enough, and the vicar offered it for free.
records.zomi: A lian tawk inn dang a om kei a, biakinn makaipa in man om lo-in a pia hi.

records.english: Our class visited the old printing works.
records.zomi: I class in laibu khetna mun lui a va kan uh hi.

records.english: When the factory celebrated its anniversary, former workers came from all over the country.
records.zomi: Van bawlna inn in a kum kikimna pawi a bawl ciangin nasem lui te gam bup pan a hong pai uh hi.

records.english: Former workers at the shipyard told the class what a launch day had been like.
records.zomi: Tembaw bawlna mun-a nasem lui te in class kiangah tembaw kipiak ni bangci om hiam cih a gen uh hi.

records.english: Our school is a hundred years old.
records.zomi: I sang kum za khat a upa hi.

records.english: The school archive contains every register since the first day the doors opened.
records.zomi: Sang' lai kemna mun in kongkhak a kihon ni masa pen pan min lai khempeuh a nei hi.

records.english: Company archives can reveal how working conditions improved, sometimes only after strikes or accidents.
records.zomi: Company lai kemna mun te in nasep mun om dan bangci-in a hoih zaw hiam, khatvei khat ciangin nasep khawlna ahih kei leh lamdang tunna khit ciangin bek, cih a lak thei hi.

records.english: Recording the memories of retired workers before they are lost has become an urgent task for the history society.
records.zomi: Nasep nusia nasemte' phawkna te a mang ma-in ciamteh pen tangthu pawl adingin manlang taka sep ding nasep khat a suak hi.

records.english: Our teacher showed us photographs of the classroom as it looked in the 1920s.
records.zomi: I saya in 1920 kum te-a sinna inndan om dan photo te hong lak hi.

records.english: The students found the names of former pupils carved into the old desks.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte in sangnaupang lui te' min dawhkan lui te-ah a kikhui a mu uh hi.

records.english: The students discovered that their school had once housed families who had lost their homes in the war.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte in a sang uh in galdona-ah a inn mansuah innkuan te a teen ngei sak hi, cih a mukhia uh hi.

records.english: For our history project, our class interviewed the oldest staff at the town's bus depot.
records.zomi: I tangthu nasep adingin i class in khuapi' bus koihna mun-a nasem upa pen te a dong uh hi.

records.english: One driver had started work at sixteen, when the buses still had conductors who collected the fares.
records.zomi: Mawtaw tawipa khat kum sawm leh guk-in nasep a kipan a, tua hun-in bus te in man a kaikhawm conductor a nei lai uh hi.

records.english: His stories became the centre of an exhibition at the town museum, which ran for the whole summer.
records.zomi: A tangthu te khuapi tangthu van kemna inn-a lakna khat' lai a suak a, khal bup sung a kibawl hi.

records.english: The exhibition showed how women ran the factories during the war and then lost their jobs when the men returned.
records.zomi: Lakna in galdona sungin numeite in van bawlna inn te a kem uh a, tua khit ciangin pasalte a ciah kik ciangin a nasep uh a mansuah uh hi, cih a lak hi.

records.english: My first job was at the town's bakery.
records.zomi: Ka nasep masa pen khuapi' moh bawlna inn-ah ahi hi.

records.english: When the students presented their findings, former workers in the audience corrected several dates and added stories of their own.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte in a mukhiat uh a lak ciangin a ngai mite lak-a nasem lui te in ni tampi a puahsak uh a, amau tangthu zong a behlap uh hi.

records.english: Is it true that the old factory is now a college?
records.zomi: Van bawlna inn lui tu-in college ahi hi, cih a dik hiam?

records.english: Did the town really have six cinemas once?
records.zomi: Khuapi in cinema inn guk a nei taktak ngei hiam?

records.english: The company published a book about its history to celebrate its hundredth year.
records.zomi: Company in a kum za khatna pawi bawl nadingin a tangthu tawh kisai laibu khat a suah hi.

records.english: Before the library was built, books were lent from the back room of the chemist's.
records.zomi: Laibu inn a kilam ma-in damdawi zuakna inn' nung lam inndan pan laibu te kipukip hi.

records.english: Has the shop really kept the same sign since 1930?
records.zomi: Van zuakna inn in 1930 kum pan ciamtehna kibang a kem taktak hiam?

records.english: The market traders have been here for generations.
records.zomi: Sumbuk mun-a van zuakte suan tampi sung hih munah a om uh hi.

records.english: A single photograph of the dockers' strike sparked a project that filled a whole wing of the museum.
records.zomi: Tembaw tual nasemte' nasep khawlna photo khat bek in tangthu van kemna inn' khen bup a dimsak nasep khat a kipansak hi.

records.english: My mum worked at the old sweet factory.
records.zomi: Ka nu a khum neu bawlna inn lui-ah a sem hi.

records.english: Our history project traced how the town's main employers changed over a century.
records.zomi: I tangthu nasep in khuapi' nasepsakpa lian te kum za khat sungin bangci-in a kikhek hiam cih a zui hi.

records.english: The town's industrial past is still visible in the chimneys, canals and rows of workers' cottages.
records.zomi: Khuapi' van bawlna hun lui pen meikhu khuam te, tuiluang laam te leh nasemte' inn neu kizom te-ah a kimu lai hi.

records.english: Why is our school named after a local nurse?
records.zomi: Bang hangin i sang mun-a nurse khat' min tawh kiphuak hiam?

records.english: She ran the town's first clinic and trained many of the women who worked there.
records.zomi: Khuapi' damdawi inn neu masa pen a kem a, tua munah a sem numei tampi a sinsak hi.

records.english: What's the oldest business still running on the high street?
records.zomi: Lampi lian tungah a kalsuan lai sumbuk upa pen bang ahi hiam?

records.english: The ironmonger's, which has been run by the same family since before the war.
records.zomi: Galdona ma pan innkuan kibang in a kem sik van zuakna inn.

records.english: Has anyone recorded the memories of the people who worked at the old brewery?
records.zomi: Zu bawlna inn lui-ah a sem mite' phawkna te kuapeuh in a ciamteh khin hiam?

records.english: Our office building used to be a bank.
records.zomi: I office inn bank ahi ngei hi.

records.english: The students interviewed the oldest teacher in the school.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte in sang sung-a saya upa pen a dong uh hi.

records.english: How long has the local newspaper been printed in the same building?
records.zomi: Mun thuthak lai inn kibang sungah bangzah sawt kikhen khin hiam?

records.english: Who started the school's football team?
records.zomi: Sang' football pawl kua in a kipan hiam?

records.english: Did your grandfather work at the old mill?
records.zomi: Na pu buh-gawhna inn lui-ah a sem hiam?

records.english: Our school's centenary book includes memories from pupils of every decade.
records.zomi: I sang' kum za kikimna laibu in kum sawm khatciat-a sangnaupangte' phawkna te a huam hi.

records.english: The engineering firm's first workshop was a garden shed behind the founder's house.
records.zomi: Engineering company' nasep inn masa pen a phutpa' inn nung-a huan inn neu khat ahi hi.

records.english: Our teacher brought in an old school bell.
records.zomi: I saya in sang khau lui khat a paipih hi.

records.english: Why did the town's lace-making industry disappear?
records.zomi: Bang hangin khuapi' puan zeng bawlna nasep a mang hiam?

records.english: The fire station was built in 1910.
records.zomi: Mei-sih nasemte' inn 1910 kum-in kilam hi.

records.english: Our teacher reminded us that the history of a workplace includes the cleaners and porters as well as the owners.
records.zomi: I saya in nasep mun khat' tangthu in a neite bang mahin inn siang bawlte leh van tawite zong a huam hi, ci-in hong phawksak hi.

records.english: This hospital was built by local workers.
records.zomi: Hih damlo inn mun-a nasemte in a lam uh hi.

records.english: Many of the town's streets are named after the trades that were once carried out there.
records.zomi: Khuapi' lampi tampi tua munah a kisem ngei nasep te' min tawh kiphuak hi.

records.english: Is the old school register in the museum?
records.zomi: Sang min lai lui tangthu van kemna inn sungah a om hiam?

records.english: Who was the first head teacher here?
records.zomi: Hih munah sang makaipa masa pen kua ahi hiam?

records.english: The miners' club still meets every Friday.
records.zomi: Leikhuk nasemte' pawl Laithai ni simin a kikhop lai hi.

records.english: The bakery's owner keeps her great-grandmother's recipe book behind the counter.
records.zomi: Moh bawlna inn neinu in a pi' nu' an huan dan laibu zuakna dawhkan nung-ah a kem hi.

records.english: Did you offer our guest something to drink?
records.zomi: I mikhual dawn ding khat na pia hiam?

records.english: Do we have to give our room to the visitors again?
records.zomi: I inndan mikhualte i pia kik ding ngei hiam?

records.english: Only for three nights, and you can sleep in the living room with your cousins.
records.zomi: Zan thum bek, na sanggamte tawh inn sung lian-ah na ihmu thei hi.

records.english: My mother believes that the way you treat a guest shows the kind of family you really are.
records.zomi: Ka nu in mikhual khat na lim dan in innkuan bangci om taktak hiam cih a lak hi, ci-in a um hi.

records.english: My father makes coffee for every visitor.
records.zomi: Ka pa in mikhual khatciat adingin coffee a bawl hi.

records.english: We cooked a big meal for our cousins.
records.zomi: Ka sanggamte adingin an lian khat i huan hi.

records.english: Hosting relatives for weeks at a time can be tiring, but my parents never let the guests see it.
records.zomi: Sanggamte kal tampi sung dawn pen a gimhuai thei hi, ahi zongin ka nu leh ka pa in mikhualte a muh dingin a phal ngei kei uh hi.

records.english: Shall I make up the spare bed for Uncle?
records.zomi: Pa neu adingin lupna a tam lai ka bawlsak ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, and put the good blanket on it, because he feels the cold.
records.zomi: Bawlsak in, puannap hoih zong a tungah koih in, bang hang hiam cih leh a vot zawk hi.

records.english: My children complain about sharing their room, but they love it when their cousins stay.
records.zomi: Ka tate in a inndan uh hawm pen a phun uh hi, ahi zongin a sanggamte uh a om ciangin a nuam sa mahmah uh hi.

records.english: Is the guest towel in the bathroom?
records.zomi: Mikhual puan-ip kisilna inn sungah a om hiam?

records.english: Grandpa always asks visitors about their families first.
records.zomi: Pu in mikhualte a innkuan uh thu a dong masa den hi.

records.english: The children helped to carry the guests' bags upstairs.
records.zomi: Naupangte in mikhualte' ip te tung lam ah a tawi tou nadingin a huh uh hi.

records.english: Our children learn hospitality not from being told but from watching how their grandparents welcome everyone.
records.zomi: I tate in mikhual dawn dan kigen tawh hi lo-in a pu leh a pi uh in mi khempeuh a dawn dan et tawh a sin uh hi.

records.english: My aunt says that a house without visitors is a house without blessings.
records.zomi: Ka ni in mikhual om lo inn pen thupha om lo inn ahi hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Mum ironed the best tablecloth for the visitors.
records.zomi: Ka nu in mikhualte adingin dawhkan puan hoih pen a tek hi.

records.english: Do you welcome your brother's friends like family?
records.zomi: Na sanggam pasal' lawmte innkuan bangin na dawn hiam?

records.english: Can our friends stay the night after the party?
records.zomi: Poai khit ciangin i lawmte zan khat a om thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: Dad gave his chair to the old man.
records.zomi: Paa in a tutphah pasal upa a pia hi.

records.english: When my husband's colleague came to stay for a weekend, my husband's mother took over the whole kitchen.
records.zomi: Ka pasal' nasem pih kal tawp khat a hong om ciangin ka pasal' nu in an huanna inn bup a la hi.

records.english: She cooked for two days, set aside the best room and insisted that our guest eat before anyone else.
records.zomi: Ni nih sung an a huan a, inndan hoih pen a koih tuam a, i mikhual mi dang khempeuh ma-in an ne dingin a ngen den hi.

records.english: Our guest still sends her a card every Christmas, ten years later.
records.zomi: Kum sawm khit ciangin zong i mikhual in Christmas simin amah kiangah card khat a khak lai hi.

records.english: My wife's family welcomed me so warmly that I felt at home on my first visit.
records.zomi: Ka zi' innkuan in lungdam mahmah-in hong dawn uh ahih manin ka va kanna masa pen-in ka inn-ah bang ka kisa hi.

records.english: Our flat is small, but my parents still invite everyone from church for lunch at Easter.
records.zomi: I flat a neu hi, ahi zongin ka nu leh ka pa in Easter-in pawlpi pan mi khempeuh sun an ne dingin a sam lai uh hi.

records.english: When my cousin's family arrived late at night, my mother cooked a full meal anyway.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam' innkuan zanlai-in a tun uh ciangin ka nu in an kicing khat a huan lai hi.

records.english: How did your family make my parents feel so welcome?
records.zomi: Na innkuan in ka nu leh ka pa bangci-in a lungdam mahmah-in a dawn uh hiam?

records.english: My mother simply treated them as if they had always been part of the family.
records.zomi: Ka nu in innkuan khen khat ahi den bangin a lim lel hi.

records.english: Should we let our guests help with the washing-up, or would that embarrass them?
records.zomi: I mikhualte kuang sil-ah a huh dingin i phal ding hiam, ahih kei leh a zumsak ding hiam?

records.english: My sister gave up her bed for our grandmother.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam numei in i pi adingin a lupna a pia hi.

records.english: We were taught to stand up whenever an older visitor entered the room.
records.zomi: Mikhual upa khat inndan sungah a lut ciangin ding dingin hong sinsak uh hi.

records.english: Our guests can sleep in my brother's room.
records.zomi: I mikhualte ka sanggam pasal' inndan-ah a ihmu thei uh hi.

records.english: We borrowed chairs from the neighbours for the visit.
records.zomi: Mikhual hong pai nadingin inn kiang mite pan tutphah te i puk hi.

records.english: My parents never let a visitor leave hungry.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in mikhual khat ngilkial-in a ciah dingin a phal ngei kei uh hi.

records.english: In my family, the youngest children serve tea to the guests before they sit down.
records.zomi: Ka innkuan sungah naupang neu pen te in a tut ma-un mikhualte lahpek a pia uh hi.

records.english: Shall I bring the guests some fruit?
records.zomi: Mikhualte gah khenkhat ka paipih ding hiam?

records.english: Our tiny flat in the city is crowded with visitors every weekend, just like my grandparents' house was.
records.zomi: Khuapi lian-a i flat neu mahmah kal tawp simin mikhualte tawh a dim hi, ka pu leh ka pi' inn bang mahin.

records.english: Why did your father refuse to let me pay for dinner?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na pa in nitak an man hong piak sak nuam lo hiam?

records.english: In our family, a guest never pays, even when the meal is in a restaurant.
records.zomi: I innkuan-ah an inn-a an ne zongin mikhual in man a pia ngei kei hi.

records.english: Why does Grandma always cook for more people than are coming?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pi in a hong pai ding mi zah sangin mi tam zaw adingin an a huan den hiam?

records.english: Because her own mother did the same, and the habit has never left her.
records.zomi: Bang hang hiam cih leh amah' nu in tua bang mah a bawl a, tua ngeina in amah a nusia ngei kei hi.

records.english: My husband's family, who come from a different culture, were amazed at how many people my parents fed.
records.zomi: Ngeina tuam pan hong pai ka pasal' innkuan in ka nu leh ka pa in mi bangzah an a pia hiam cih a lamdang sa mahmah uh hi.

records.english: Please take your shoes off and come in.
records.zomi: Kong ngen hi, na khedap suah inla, hong lut in.

records.english: My grandmother still apologises that the meal is too simple, even when the table is full.
records.zomi: Ka pi in dawhkan a dim zongin an a baih lua hi, ci-in maisak a ngen lai hi.

records.english: Who will meet our guests at the station?
records.zomi: Station-ah i mikhualte kua in a dawn ding hiam?

records.english: When my parents visited my wife's family, both mothers tried so hard to be generous that neither would let the other pay.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in ka zi' innkuan a va kan uh ciangin nu nih in pia hat dingin hanciam mahmah-in kuamah in a dang man a piak dingin a phal kei uh hi.

records.english: When my friend from school visited, my mother treated her like a member of the family.
records.zomi: Sang-a ka lawm a hong pai ciangin ka nu in innkuan mi khat bangin a lim hi.

records.english: Some young people in our family find the old rules of hospitality exhausting, yet they follow them when guests arrive.
records.zomi: I innkuan-a khangno khenkhat in mikhual dawn ngeina lui te a gimhuai sa uh hi, ahi zongin mikhualte a tun ciangin a zui uh hi.

records.english: My husband learned that refusing a second helping can upset my mother.
records.zomi: Ka pasal in an behlap nialna in ka nu a lungkhamsak thei hi, cih a sin hi.

records.english: Did your aunt really stay with you for a whole month?
records.zomi: Na ni na kiangah kha bup sung a om taktak hiam?

records.english: A family's reputation in our community still depends partly on how generously it treats its guests.
records.zomi: I mipi lak-ah innkuan khat' minthanna in a mikhualte bangzah pia hat takin a lim hiam cih tungah a kinga lai hi.

records.english: Grandma remembers what every visitor likes to eat and cooks it for them next time.
records.zomi: Pi in mikhual khatciat in bang an ne nuam hiam cih a phawk a, a vei zom-in amaute adingin a huan hi.

records.english: My mother always keeps tea ready for visitors.
records.zomi: Ka nu in mikhualte adingin lahpek a kiging den hi.

records.english: Why does Dad always walk visitors all the way to their car?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Paa in mikhualte a mawtaw uh dong a paipih den hiam?

records.english: My parents kept the visitors' room ready all year, just in case.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in a hong pai leh cih-in kum bup mikhual inndan a kigingsak den uh hi.

records.english: We moved the children into one room so that our relatives had space to sleep.
records.zomi: I sanggamte in ihmut nading mun a neih theih nadingin naupangte inndan khat ah i suan hi.

records.english: Even in the hardest years, my father made sure visitors ate before the family did.
records.zomi: Kum haksa pen te sungin zong ka pa in innkuan ma-in mikhualte an a ne dingin a en den hi.

records.english: Grandma always cooks her best dish for new visitors.
records.zomi: Pi in mikhual thakte adingin a an hoih pen a huan den hi.

records.english: Our neighbours are always invited to share the food when relatives arrive.
records.zomi: Sanggamte a tun ciangin i inn kiang mite an hawm dingin i sam den hi.

records.english: My grandparents' house was so famous for its welcome that travellers would ask for it by name.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh ka pi' inn mikhual dawnna-ah a minthang mahmah ahih manin khualzin mite in a min tawh a dong uh hi.

records.english: Our house is always full of guests at Christmas.
records.zomi: Christmas-in i inn mikhualte tawh a dim den hi.

records.english: Did people write about Jesus soon after he died?
records.zomi: Jesu a sih khit nai-in mite in amah tawh kisai a gelh uh hiam?

records.english: Who wrote the Gospels?
records.zomi: Lungdamna Thu te kua in a gelh hiam?

records.english: Pontius Pilate was the Roman governor of Judea.
records.zomi: Pontius Pilat pen Judah gam-a Rom mangpa ahi hi.

records.english: Thousands of ancient manuscripts of the New Testament have survived.
records.zomi: Thuciam Thak' laigelh lui tulsang tampi a om lai hi.

records.english: Christians believe that their faith rests on events that really happened in history.
records.zomi: Khristiante in a upna uh tangthu sungah a piang taktak thupiang te tungah a kinga hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: Did Jesus really exist?
records.zomi: Jesu a om taktak hiam?

records.english: Almost all historians, including those who aren't Christians, agree that he did.
records.zomi: Khristian hi lo te zong huam-in tangthu siam mi khempeuh dek in a om hi, ci-in a kithukim uh hi.

records.english: Is Nazareth a real place?
records.zomi: Nazareth pen mun taktak khat ahi hiam?

records.english: How old are the oldest copies of the Gospels?
records.zomi: Lungdamna Thu' copy lui pen te kum bangzah a upa uh hiam?

records.english: Some fragments date from the second century, not long after the originals were written.
records.zomi: A khen neu khenkhat kum za nihna pan ahi a, a bulpi te a kigelh khit nai-in ahi hi.

records.english: My son asked how we know Jesus was real.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in Jesu a om taktak hi, cih bangci-in i thei hiam, ci-in a dong hi.

records.english: Can we trust the Gospels?
records.zomi: Lungdamna Thu te i muang thei hiam?

records.english: Our pastor talked about the evidence for the resurrection.
records.zomi: I pastor in thawhkikna adinga tettehna te thu a gen hi.

records.english: Our teacher encouraged us to read what both Christian and non-Christian historians say.
records.zomi: I saya in Khristian leh Khristian hi lo tangthu siam mite in bang a gen uh hiam cih sim dingin hong hanthawn hi.

records.english: The early Christians were willing to suffer rather than deny what they believed they had seen.
records.zomi: Khristian masa te in a muh uh a cih uh a nial sangin thuak nopna a nei uh hi.

records.english: For many Christians, the historical evidence supports faith rather than replacing it.
records.zomi: Khristian tampi adingin tangthu tettehna te in upna a laih lo-in a dingpih hi.

records.english: Our class learned about the time when Jesus lived.
records.zomi: I class in Jesu a nuntak hun tawh kisai a sin uh hi.

records.english: How quickly did the early church grow?
records.zomi: Pawlpi masa bangzah manlang-in a khang hiam?

records.english: Why do some historians think the empty tomb story is early?
records.zomi: Bang hangin tangthu siam mi khenkhat in han awng tangthu pen a masa lam pan ahi hi, a ci uh hiam?

records.english: We saw old copies of the Bible at the museum.
records.zomi: Tangthu van kemna inn ah Laisiangtho' copy lui te i mu hi.

records.english: Our Bible study looked at how the Gospels describe real places and rulers.
records.zomi: I Laisiangtho sinna in Lungdamna Thu te in mun taktak te leh uk mi taktak te bangci-in a gen hiam cih a en hi.

records.english: History matters to Christian faith.
records.zomi: Tangthu in Khristian upna adingin a thupi hi.

records.english: Archaeology can confirm that places and rulers existed, but it cannot prove what people believed about them.
records.zomi: Leitang lai tou siamna in mun te leh uk mi te a om ngei hi, cih a tettehsak thei a, ahi zongin mite in amaute tawh kisai bang a um uh hiam cih a tettehsak thei kei hi.

records.english: The four Gospels tell the same story in different ways, which historians find useful.
records.zomi: Lungdamna Thu li in tangthu kibang lam tuamtuam-in a gen uh a, tua pen tangthu siam mite in a manpha sa uh hi.

records.english: Our youth group visited a museum of Bible history.
records.zomi: I khangno pawl in Laisiangtho tangthu van kemna inn khat a va kan uh hi.

records.english: The Romans ruled the land where Jesus lived.
records.zomi: Jesu a nuntakna gam pen Rom mite in a uk uh hi.

records.english: Historians generally agree that Jesus was a Jewish teacher who was crucified under Pontius Pilate.
records.zomi: Tangthu siam mite in Jesu pen Pontius Pilat uk lai-in singlamteh tungah kikhai Judah saya khat ahi hi, ci-in a kithukim zel uh hi.

records.english: Many places in the Bible can still be visited today.
records.zomi: Laisiangtho sung-a mun tampi tu-in zong va kan theih lai hi.

records.english: Faith doesn't depend only on historical evidence, but many Christians find it important.
records.zomi: Upna pen tangthu tettehna tungah bek a kinga kei hi, ahi zongin Khristian tampi in a thupi sa uh hi.

records.english: On a church trip to Israel, our group visited the caves where the Dead Sea Scrolls were found.
records.zomi: Isael gam ah pawlpi khualzinna-ah i pawl in Si Tuipi Laizial te a kimuhna kua te a va kan uh hi.

records.english: Our guide explained that the scrolls, discovered in 1947, include some of the oldest known copies of the Hebrew Bible.
records.zomi: I lampi lakpa in 1947 kum-in a kimu laizial te in Hebru Laisiangtho' copy lui pen theih te khenkhat a huam hi, ci-in a gen hi.

records.english: My teenage son, who had been bored all week, asked questions for the rest of the afternoon.
records.zomi: Kal bup a lungmang ka tapa khangno in sun nung lam a om lai bup dotna a dong hi.

records.english: The apostle Paul wrote that if Christ has not been raised, the faith of Christians is in vain.
records.zomi: Sawltak Paul in Khazih a thokik kei leh Khristiante' upna a mawkna ahi hi, ci-in a gelh hi.

records.english: Studying the historical background of the Bible helps readers understand what its first audiences heard.
records.zomi: Laisiangtho' tangthu bulpi sin in simmite in a ngai masa mite in bang a zak uh hiam cih a theisiam nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Did the first Christians write in Greek or in Hebrew?
records.zomi: Khristian masa te Greek pau tawh a gelh uh hiam, Hebru pau tawh a gelh uh hiam?

records.english: The Roman governor Pliny wrote to the emperor asking how to treat Christians.
records.zomi: Rom mangpa Pliny in Khristiante bangci-in lim ding hiam, ci-in Kaisar kumpipa kiangah lai a gelh hi.

records.english: Some scholars question parts of Josephus's account because later copyists may have added words.
records.zomi: Siam mi khenkhat in Josephus' genna khenkhat a dong uh hi, bang hang hiam cih leh a nung-a copy bawlte in kammal a behlap thei uh hi.

records.english: Archaeologists have uncovered a pool in Jerusalem that matches a description in John's Gospel.
records.zomi: Leitang lai a tou mite in Jerusalem khua-ah Johan Lungdamna Thu sung-a genna tawh a kituak dil khat a mukhia uh hi.

records.english: Archaeologists have found the remains of ancient Jerusalem.
records.zomi: Leitang lai a tou mite in Jerusalem lui' a om lai te a mu uh hi.

records.english: How do historians decide whether an ancient document is reliable?
records.zomi: Tangthu siam mite in laigelh lui khat a um huai hiam cih bangci-in a khensat uh hiam?

records.english: The first Christians met in people's homes.
records.zomi: Khristian masa te mite' inn te-ah a kikhop uh hi.

records.english: The apostles travelled far to tell others about Jesus.
records.zomi: Sawltak te midangte kiangah Jesu thu gen dingin gamla-ah a khualzin uh hi.

records.english: The Jewish historian Josephus mentioned Jesus in his writings.
records.zomi: Judah tangthu siam mi Josephus in a laigelh te-ah Jesu thu a gen hi.

records.english: A stone found in Caesarea in 1961 carries the name of Pontius Pilate.
records.zomi: 1961 kum-in Kaisaria khua-ah kimu suang khat in Pontius Pilat' min a nei hi.

records.english: Is the Bible a history book?
records.zomi: Laisiangtho pen tangthu laibu ahi hiam?

records.english: It contains history, but also poetry, law, letters and prayers.
records.zomi: Tangthu a huam hi, ahi zongin la phuak, thukham, laikhak leh thungetna te zong a huam hi.

records.english: Honest study of the evidence means admitting where the sources are uncertain as well as where they are strong.
records.zomi: Tettehna thuman taka sin pen thu bulpi te a cian loh mun leh a hat mun te pom ahi hi.

records.english: Was the Bible first written by hand?
records.zomi: Laisiangtho a masa pen-in khut tawh kigelh hiam?

records.english: The rapid spread of Christianity across the Roman Empire is a historical fact that needs some explanation.
records.zomi: Rom gam lian bup-ah Khristian upna a manlang taka kizel pen gen siam ding a ngai tangthu thutak khat ahi hi.

records.english: Do any Roman writers mention Jesus?
records.zomi: Rom laigelhpa khatpeuh in Jesu thu a gen hiam?

records.english: Yes, the historian Tacitus wrote that he was executed under Pontius Pilate.
records.zomi: Gen hi, tangthu siam mi Tacitus in Pontius Pilat uk lai-in kithat hi, ci-in a gelh hi.

records.english: Christians have studied history for centuries.
records.zomi: Khristiante in kum zalom tampi sung tangthu a sin uh hi.

records.english: Were the disciples real people?
records.zomi: Nungzui te mi taktak ahi uh hiam?

records.english: Believers and sceptics disagree about the resurrection, though both must explain why the early church began so quickly.
records.zomi: Upmite leh a um lote thawhkikna thu-ah a kithukim kei uh hi, ahi zongin a nih in bang hangin pawlpi masa a manlang mahmah-in a kipan hiam cih a gen siam ding uh hi.

records.english: Historians of the ancient world rarely have as many early copies of a text as scholars have of the New Testament.
records.zomi: Tangthu lui hun-a tangthu siam mite in Thuciam Thak adingin siam mite' neih zah bang laigelh khat' copy masa a nei zel kei uh hi.

records.english: Why do historians care about Paul's letters?
records.zomi: Bang hangin tangthu siam mite in Paul' laikhak te a ngaihsak uh hiam?

records.english: They were written within a few decades of Jesus' death, so they are among our earliest sources.
records.zomi: Jesu' sih khit kum sawm tawm khat sungin kigelh ahih manin i thu bulpi masa pen te lak-ah a om uh hi.

records.english: Paul lists people who said they had seen Jesus alive after his death.
records.zomi: Paul in Jesu a sih khit ciangin a nungta-in ka mu hi, a ci mite min a gen hi.

records.english: Historians compare the Gospels with other ancient writings from the same period.
records.zomi: Tangthu siam mite in Lungdamna Thu te hun kibang-a laigelh lui dangte tawh a teh uh hi.

records.english: Some historians accept the basic facts of Jesus' life while rejecting the Gospels' accounts of miracles.
records.zomi: Tangthu siam mi khenkhat in Jesu' nuntakna thu bulpi te a san uh a, ahi zongin Lungdamna Thu te' nalamdang genna te a nial uh hi.

records.english: How do we know the charity actually spends the money on the children?
records.zomi: Huhna pawl in sum naupangte tungah a zang taktak hiam cih bangci-in i thei hiam?

records.english: The insurance company asked for photos taken on the day of the accident.
records.zomi: Insurance company in lamdang tunna ni-a kila photo te a ngen hi.

records.english: Has the station announced a delay?
records.zomi: Station in hun nunna khat a theisak khin hiam?

records.english: Can you send me a picture of the leak?
records.zomi: Tui luanna lim khat hong khak thei ding na hiam?

records.english: Even honest witnesses can be mistaken, which is why investigators look for physical evidence too.
records.zomi: Thuman teci te zong a khial thei ahih manin enkite in pumpi tettehna zong a zong uh hi.

records.english: How do you know the restaurant has reopened?
records.zomi: An inn a kihong kik hi, cih bangci-in na thei hiam?

records.english: I walked past last night, and every table was full.
records.zomi: Zan-in ka kan a, dawhkan khempeuh a dim hi.

records.english: Show me the photo you took of the car.
records.zomi: Mawtaw' photo na lak hong lak in.

records.english: How can we be sure the bridge is safe?
records.zomi: Lei a bit hi, cih bangci-in i thei cian thei ding hiam?

records.english: A screenshot can be useful evidence, though it is easy to fake and should be checked.
records.zomi: Screenshot khat tettehna manpha khat ahi thei a, ahi zongin a khem theih baih ahih manin kien ding ahi hi.

records.english: Do you have the ticket for your coat?
records.zomi: Na puan-ak adinga lai man na nei hiam?

records.english: Can you show me where you read that coffee is bad for you?
records.zomi: Coffee na adingin a hoih lo hi, cih koi-ah na sim hiam cih hong lak thei ding na hiam?

records.english: My friend didn't believe I had met the actor until I showed her the photo.
records.zomi: Ka lawm in photo ka lak dong lam lakpa ka kimu hi, cih a um kei hi.

records.english: What makes you so sure the parcel was delivered?
records.zomi: Van bawm kipia khin hi, cih bang in hong thei cian sak hiam?

records.english: The tracking page has a photo of it on our doorstep.
records.zomi: Zuihna lai-ek in i kongkhak mai-a a om photo khat a nei hi.

records.english: Did anyone see the accident happen?
records.zomi: Lamdang tunna a piang kuapeuh in a mu hiam?

records.english: How do you know it's going to rain?
records.zomi: Guah a zu ding hi, cih bangci-in na thei hiam?

records.english: Is the price on the shelf correct?
records.zomi: Laibu koihna tunga man a dik hiam?

records.english: I'd like to see the inspection report before I buy the house.
records.zomi: Inn ka lei ma-in enkikna report en ka nop hi.

records.english: Is there a video of the goal?
records.zomi: Goal' video khat a om hiam?

records.english: Which website did that story come from?
records.zomi: Tua tangthu website bang pan a hong pai hiam?

records.english: Online reviews are weak evidence, because you rarely know who wrote them or why.
records.zomi: Online genna te tettehna hat lo ahi hi, bang hang hiam cih leh kua in bang hangin a gelh hiam cih na thei zel kei hi.

records.english: The doctor admitted that the evidence for the treatment was mixed, which made me trust her more.
records.zomi: Siavuan in damsakna adinga tettehna a kigawm hi, ci-in a pom a, tua in amah ka muan zawk nadingin a bawl hi.

records.english: When I asked the salesman for evidence of his claims, he suddenly remembered another appointment.
records.zomi: Van zuakpa kiangah a genna te adingin tettehna ka nget ciangin kimuhna dang khat a phawk lamdang hi.

records.english: Is there a photo of the dent in the van?
records.zomi: Van tawi mawtaw-a kiluap photo khat a om hiam?

records.english: Who told you the cinema was closing?
records.zomi: Cinema inn a kikhak ding hi, cih kua in hong gen hiam?

records.english: Have you got the warranty card for the washing machine?
records.zomi: Puan silna khawl' kamciamna card na nei hiam?

records.english: It's in the folder with the other appliance papers, in the kitchen drawer.
records.zomi: An huanna inn' dawhkan bawm sung-a van dang lai te tawh folder sungah a om hi.

records.english: Is that really his bike by the gate?
records.zomi: Kongpi kiang-a siiksakol tua pen amah' siiksakol taktak hiam?

records.english: The judge dismissed the complaint because there was no evidence beyond one person's memory.
records.zomi: Mi khat' phawkna bek tua pualam-ah tettehna om lo ahih manin thukhennu in phunna a paikhia hi.

records.english: How can you be certain the ring is real gold?
records.zomi: Zungbuh pen kham taktak ahi hi, cih bangci-in na thei cian thei hiam?

records.english: A careful buyer asks to see the documents before the money changes hands.
records.zomi: Cian taka van lei mi khat in sum a kikhek ma-in lai te en dingin a ngen hi.

records.english: My neighbour insisted that a fox had been stealing her shoes from the garden.
records.zomi: Ka inn kiang mi in ngalhia khat in huan pan a khedap te a guk hi, ci-in a gen den hi.

records.english: Nobody believed her until she set up a small camera by the back door.
records.zomi: Kongkhak nung lam kiangah camera neu khat a koih dong kuamah in a um kei uh hi.

records.english: The next morning, the video showed a fox trotting off with a slipper in its mouth.
records.zomi: A zingsang ciangin video in ngalhia khat a kam-ah khedap khat tawh a tai a lak hi.

records.english: Have you got anything in writing from the landlord about the rent?
records.zomi: Inn man tawh kisai inn neipa pan lai tawh na nei hiam?

records.english: Can I see the menu with the prices?
records.zomi: Man te tawh an lista ka en thei ding hiam?

records.english: Are you sure she likes dark chocolate?
records.zomi: Chocolate a vom pen a deih hi, cih na thei cian hiam?

records.english: How do you know the bread was baked this morning?
records.zomi: Moh tu zingsang-in kihuan hi, cih bangci-in na thei hiam?

records.english: What makes you think the flat upstairs is empty?
records.zomi: Bang in tung lam-a flat a awng hi, ci-in hong ngaihsunsak hiam?

records.english: Has the face cream been tested by anyone other than the company that sells it?
records.zomi: Mai nuh sathau a zuak company sangin mi dang khat in a sit khin hiam?

records.english: Where does it say that we can't have a barbecue in the garden?
records.zomi: Huan sungah barbecue i bawl thei kei hi, cih koi-ah a kigelh hiam?

records.english: The landlord could not prove the damage had been caused by the tenants, so he returned the full deposit.
records.zomi: Inn neipa in siatna pen inn lut mite in a piangsak hi, cih a tettehsak zo lo ahih manin a sum koih khempeuh a pia kik hi.

records.english: Before I pay, could you show me that the car's service history is complete?
records.zomi: Ka sum ka piak ma-in mawtaw' kibawl kikna tangthu a kicing hi, cih hong lak thei ding na hiam?

records.english: Did the shop give you a receipt?
records.zomi: Van zuakna inn in van lei lai hong pia hiam?

records.english: When someone makes an extraordinary claim, it's reasonable to ask for more than their word.
records.zomi: Mi khat in lamdang mahmah thu khat a gen ciangin a kammal bek sangin a tam zaw ngen pen a kilawm hi.

records.english: Who saw the cat climb onto the roof?
records.zomi: Zawhngeu inn tung-ah a kah a kua in a mu hiam?

records.english: Can I see the label on that jar?
records.zomi: Tua um tunga ciamtehna lai ka en thei ding hiam?

records.english: Can you prove the painting is really a hundred years old?
records.zomi: Lim suai pen kum za khat a upa taktak hi, cih na tettehsak thei hiam?

records.english: The museum tested the paint and found that it was made before 1920.
records.zomi: Tangthu van kemna inn in zum a sit a, 1920 ma-in kibawl hi, cih a mu hi.

records.english: The headline claimed that the town was the happiest in the country, but the survey had only twelve replies.
records.zomi: Thulu in khuapi pen gam sung-a lungdam pen ahi hi, ci-in a gen hi, ahi zongin enkikna in dawnna sawm leh nih bek a nei hi.

records.english: Show me where the water is coming in.
records.zomi: Tui koi pan a lut hiam cih hong lak in.

records.english: How can you tell the eggs are fresh?
records.zomi: Aktui te a thak hi, cih bangci-in na thei thei hiam?

records.english: Do you have any proof that the dog next door is the one barking at night?
records.zomi: Zan-in a hawng ui pen inn kiang-a ui ahi hi, cih tettehna khatpeuh na nei hiam?

records.english: Could you show me the reviews from people who have actually stayed there?
records.zomi: Tua munah a om taktak mite' genna te hong lak thei ding na hiam?

records.english: Can I see your boarding pass, please?
records.zomi: Kong ngen hi, na vanleng tuanna lai ka en thei ding hiam?

records.english: Has anyone actually tested the diet that's in all the magazines?
records.zomi: Magazine khempeuh sung-a an ne dan pen kuapeuh in a sit taktak khin hiam?

records.english: Honestly, there isn't much, apart from a few reviews on the company's own website.
records.zomi: Thuman takin, a tam kei hi, company' amah website tunga genna tawm khat bek.

records.english: Asking where a story came from before sharing it can stop a rumour spreading through a whole town.
records.zomi: Tangthu khat na hawm ma-in koi pan a hong pai hiam cih dot in kamsang thu khat khuapi bup-ah a zel lohna dingin a kham thei hi.

records.english: The mechanic showed me the worn brake pads as proof that they needed replacing.
records.zomi: Mawtaw bawlpa in a kikhek ding a ngaihna tettehna-in brake pad a kiam te hong lak hi.

records.english: Students can volunteer at the library on Saturdays.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte in Kiginni-in laibu inn-ah thalawp-in a sem thei uh hi.

records.english: The students' survey of local shops was published in the community newsletter.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte' mun-a van zuakna inn enkikna khuasung thuthak lai-ah kisuah hi.

records.english: Our office adopted a small park near the station that nobody seemed to look after.
records.zomi: I office in station kiang-a kuamah in a kem bang a kilang lo park neu khat a kem hi.

records.english: Every month, a team of volunteers spent a lunchtime clearing litter and planting bulbs.

records.english: Why did Marie Curie move from Poland to France?

records.english: Who was the first person to fly across the Atlantic alone?
records.zomi: Atlantic tuipi a kumpi-a vanleng tawh a kan masa pen mi kua ahi hiam?

records.english: Biographies of famous scientists often leave out the colleagues and assistants who made their work possible.
records.zomi: Science mi minthang te' nuntakna gelhna te in a nasep uh a bawl theisak nasem pih leh huhpa te a nusia zel uh hi.

records.english: Which scientist do you admire most?
records.zomi: Science mi kua na zahtak pen hiam?

records.english: Rosalind Franklin, whose X-ray images helped reveal the structure of DNA.
records.zomi: Rosalind Franklin, a X-ray lim te in DNA' kibawl dan a lak nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Which explorer is your project about?
records.zomi: Na nasep pen gam zong mi bang tawh kisai ahi hiam?

records.english: Who are you writing your history project about?
records.zomi: Na tangthu nasep kua tawh kisai na gelh hiam?

records.english: Louis Braille, who invented a reading system for blind people when he was only a teenager.
records.zomi: Louis Braille, khangno bek a hih lai-in mit tang lo mite adingin laisim lam khat a bawl hi.

records.english: Does our library have books about famous scientists?
records.zomi: I laibu inn in science mi minthang te tawh kisai laibu te a nei hiam?

records.english: The hospital ward is named after a famous doctor.
records.zomi: Damlo inndan siavuan minthang khat' min tawh kiphuak hi.

records.english: The local library ran a reading challenge based on the lives of famous women.
records.zomi: Mun-a laibu inn in numei minthang te' nuntakna tungah kinga laibu sim kidemna khat a bawl hi.

records.english: Our class debated whether Napoleon was a great leader or a dangerous one.
records.zomi: I class in Napoleon pen makaipa lian khat ahi hiam, lauhuai khat ahi hiam cih a kinial uh hi.

records.english: For our school's history week, each class adopted a famous person from the past.
records.zomi: I sang' tangthu kal adingin class khatciat in a beisa hun pan mi minthang khat a teel uh hi.

records.english: Our class chose Mary Seacole, a nurse who cared for soldiers in the Crimean War.
records.zomi: I class in Crimea galdona-ah galkapte a kem nurse Mary Seacole a teel uh hi.

records.english: By the end of the week, the classroom walls were covered with maps, letters and drawings of her journeys.
records.zomi: Kal a bei ciangin sinna inndan bang te map, lai leh a khualzinna lim suai te tawh a kikhuh hi.

records.english: Historians now pay more attention to women whose achievements were credited to men in their lifetimes.
records.zomi: Tangthu siam mite in tu-in a nuntak lai-uh-in a zawhna uh pasalte tungah a kiko numeite a ngaihsak zaw uh hi.

records.english: Why is the engineering building named after a woman?
records.zomi: Bang hangin engineering inn numei khat' min tawh kiphuak hiam?

records.english: She was the first female engineer to graduate from this university, back in the 1920s.
records.zomi: Hih university pan a zo engineer numei masa pen ahi a, 1920 kum te-ah ahi hi.

records.english: Students at the nursing school learn how Florence Nightingale used statistics to improve hospitals.
records.zomi: Nurse sinna sang-a sangnaupangte in Florence Nightingale in damlo inn te hoihsak nadingin nambat tehna a zat dan a sin uh hi.

records.english: The teacher asked us to compare two leaders who faced the same crisis in different ways.
records.zomi: Saya in buaina kibang a tuak, lam tuamtuam-in a dawng makaipa nih teh dingin hong ngen hi.

records.english: Has anyone in the class read the diary of Samuel Pepys?
records.zomi: Class sungah kuapeuh in Samuel Pepys' ni sim ciamtehna a sim khin hiam?

records.english: The class discovered that Alexander Fleming's discovery of penicillin began with a mouldy dish left out by accident.
records.zomi: Class in Alexander Fleming' penicillin a muhna pen lamdang taka kinusia kuang mau khat pan a kipan hi, cih a mukhia uh hi.

records.english: A visiting historian explained how the town's first librarian had collected books door to door.
records.zomi: Hong kan tangthu siam mi khat in khuapi' laibu inn kemtupa masa pen in inn khatciat-ah laibu te bangci-in a kaikhawm hiam cih a gen hi.

records.english: Marie Curie studied in Paris.
records.zomi: Marie Curie Paris khuapi-ah a sin hi.

records.english: The medical school's oldest building is named after the surgeon who founded it.
records.zomi: Damdawi sang' inn lui pen a phut zatui satpa' min tawh kiphuak hi.

records.english: Our science teacher told us that Marie Curie's notebooks are still too radioactive to handle without protection.
records.zomi: I science saya in Marie Curie' ciamtehna laibu te kepna om lo-in khoih ding a lauhuai lai hi, ci-in hong gen hi.

records.english: Who invented the telephone?
records.zomi: Telephone kua in a bawl masa hiam?

records.english: The younger cousins always clear the table so that the elders can rest after the meal.
records.zomi: An khit ciangin upate a tawlngak theih nadingin sanggam neu zaw te in dawhkan a siangsak den uh hi.

records.english: Every New Year, the younger members of our family visit each elder's home in turn.
records.zomi: Kum Thak simin i innkuan-a neu zaw te in upa khatciat' inn ah a kalsuan in a va kan uh hi.

records.english: In our family, it would be unthinkable to move a grandparent into a care home while any relative could look after them.
records.zomi: I innkuan-ah sanggam khatpeuh in a kem thei lai-in pu ahih kei leh pi khat upate' kemna inn ah suan pen ngaihsut ding zong hi lo hi.

records.english: The way my parents speak to their own parents has shaped how I hope my children will speak to me.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in amau nu leh pa tawh a kihopih dan in ka tate in kei tawh a kihopih ding dan ka lamen na a bawl hi.

records.english: My parents gave up their bedroom so that my grandmother would have the room nearest the bathroom.
records.zomi: Ka pi kisilna inn tawh a nai pen inndan a neih theih nadingin ka nu leh ka pa in a lupna inndan uh a pia uh hi.

records.english: Some young people in our community feel torn between the respect they owe their elders and the freedom they have abroad.
records.zomi: I mipi sung-a khangno khenkhat in a upate uh tungah a zahtak ding uh leh gamdang-ah a neih uh suahtakna kikal-ah a kikhen bang a kisa uh hi.

records.english: We always kiss Grandma's hand when we arrive.
records.zomi: I tun ciangin Pi' khut i tawp den hi.

records.english: Our children write letters to their great-grandmother because she doesn't use a phone.
records.zomi: I tate in a pu uh' nu adingin lai a gelh uh hi, bang hang hiam cih leh phone a zang kei hi.

records.english: Should I talk to Grandpa before I accept the job abroad?
records.zomi: Gamdang-a nasep ka san ma-in Pu tawh ka kihoupih ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, even if you've already decided, because he'll appreciate being asked.
records.zomi: Kihoupih in, na khensat khin zongin, bang hang hiam cih leh kidot a lungdam pih ding hi.

records.english: Why does Grandpa get upset when we use our phones at the table?
records.zomi: Bang hangin dawhkan kiangah i phone i zat ciangin Pu a heh hiam?

records.english: My father phones his mother every evening.
records.zomi: Ka pa in nitak simin a nu phone a sam hi.

records.english: My cousin postponed her wedding until our great-uncle had recovered and could attend.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam in i pu lian a dam kik a, a hong pai thei dong a mopawi a nunsak hi.

records.english: My grandmother's blessing before my first job interview meant more to me than any advice from my teachers.
records.zomi: Ka nasep interview masa ma-in ka pi' thupha in ka saya te' thuhilhna khatpeuh sangin a thupi zaw hi.

records.english: Ask Grandma whether she wants more rice before you take some.
records.zomi: Na lak ma-in Pi kiangah an behlap a deih hiam cih dong in.

records.english: How do you stay close to your grandparents now that you've moved abroad?
records.zomi: Gamdang-ah na suan khit ciangin na pu leh na pi tawh bangci-in na kinai den hiam?

records.english: I call every Sunday, send photos of the children and visit every summer.
records.zomi: Nipini simin phone ka sam a, naupangte' photo ka khak a, khal simin ka va kan hi.

records.english: Can you help Grandma with her coat?
records.zomi: Pi a puan-ak silh nadingin na huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Please speak politely to your uncle.
records.zomi: Kong ngen hi, na pa neu tawh zahtak takin kihopih in.

records.english: My children love listening to their grandfather's stories.
records.zomi: Ka tate in a pu uh' tangthu ngaihkhiat a nuam sa mahmah uh hi.

records.english: Shall we take Grandpa to church on Sunday?
records.zomi: Nipini-in Pu biakinn ah i paipih ding hiam?

records.english: Did you call your grandmother on her birthday?
records.zomi: Na pi' pianni-in phone na sam hiam?

records.english: Our family takes Grandpa's advice seriously, even when we don't follow it.
records.zomi: I innkuan in i zui kei zongin Pu' thuhilhna thupi takin a la hi.

records.english: My aunt always gives the elders the first cup of tea.
records.zomi: Ka ni in upate lahpek haai masa pen a pia den hi.

records.english: My grandfather says that respect is earned by elders who listen as well as by young people who obey.
records.zomi: Ka pu in zahtakna pen thu ngaikhia upate leh thu mang khangnote in a ngah ahi hi, a ci hi.

records.english: My son helps his grandmother in the garden.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in a pi huan sungah a huh hi.

records.english: Should I call my grandmother more often, or would visiting once a month be better?
records.zomi: Ka pi tamvei zaw phone ka sam ding hiam, ahih kei leh kha khat-in khatvei va kan a hoih zaw ding hiam?

records.english: Our teenagers sometimes find the rules of respect old-fashioned, but they still follow them at home.
records.zomi: I khangnote in zahtakna thukham te a lui bang a kisa uh hi, ahi zongin inn-ah a zui lai uh hi.

records.english: Is Grandpa coming to the wedding?
records.zomi: Pu mopawi ah a hong pai ding hiam?

records.english: Caring for my grandmother at home has been hard work, but my parents see it as an honour, not a burden.
records.zomi: Inn-ah ka pi kem pen nasep haksa ahi hi, ahi zongin ka nu leh ka pa in puak gik hi lo-in zahtakna khat bangin a mu uh hi.

records.english: Grandma has her own room at our house.
records.zomi: Pi in i inn-ah amah' inndan a nei hi.

records.english: Let Grandpa finish his story.
records.zomi: Pu in a tangthu a zawh dingin nusia in.

records.english: My husband's family were surprised at how carefully our children greet their elders.
records.zomi: Ka pasal' innkuan in i tate in a upate uh bangzah cian takin a dawnsawn uh hiam cih a lamdang sa uh hi.

records.english: My parents look after my grandmother at home.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in ka pi inn-ah a kem uh hi.

records.english: Why do we always visit Grandpa before anyone else?
records.zomi: Bang hangin mi dang khempeuh ma-in Pu i va kan den hiam?

records.english: Because he's the eldest in the family, and he'd be hurt if we went somewhere else first.
records.zomi: Bang hang hiam cih leh innkuan sungah upa pen ahi a, mun dang ah i pai masa leh a lungkham ding hi.

records.english: Don't raise your voice in front of the elders.
records.zomi: Upate mai-ah na aw khang kei in.

records.english: Even the youngest children go quiet when Grandpa speaks at family gatherings.
records.zomi: Innkuan kikhopna-ah Pu a pau ciangin naupang neu pen te zong a dai uh hi.

records.english: When my grandfather turned ninety, all fourteen grandchildren came home to kneel and receive his blessing.
records.zomi: Ka pu kum sawmkua a cin ciangin a tu sawm leh li khempeuh khukdin-a a thupha la dingin inn ah a ciah uh hi.

records.english: He placed his hand on each head in turn and said a few words that he had chosen for each of us.
records.zomi: Lu khatciat tungah a kalsuan in a khut a koih a, eite khatciat adingin a teel kammal tawm khat a gen hi.

records.english: My cousin, who lives abroad and rarely visits, cried more than anyone.
records.zomi: Gamdang-a teeng a, hong kan zel lo ka sanggam in mi khempeuh sangin a kap zaw hi.

records.english: My mother taught me never to walk between an elder and the person they are talking to.
records.zomi: Ka nu in upa khat leh a kihopih mi kikal-ah pai ngei lo dingin hong sinsak hi.

records.english: When my teenage son disagreed with his grandfather, he waited until they were alone to say so gently.
records.zomi: Ka tapa khangno in a pu tawh a kithukim loh ciangin a nih bek a om dong a ngak a, nem takin a gen hi.

records.english: Grandpa sits at the head of the table.
records.zomi: Pu dawhkan' lu lam ah a tu hi.

records.english: As our family has spread across countries, video calls have become a new way to show respect to the elders.
records.zomi: I innkuan gam tuamtuam-ah a kizel ciangin video call te upate zahtakna lak nading lam thak khat a suak hi.

records.english: Have you thanked Grandma for the meal?
records.zomi: An adingin Pi lungdam na ko khin hiam?

records.english: Why did your father stand up when your grandmother came in?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na pi a lut ciangin na pa a ding hiam?

records.english: In our family, everyone stands when the eldest woman arrives, even my father at sixty.
records.zomi: I innkuan-ah numei upa pen a tun ciangin mi khempeuh a ding uh hi, kum sawmguk a cing ka pa zong.

records.english: We save the best fruit for our grandparents.
records.zomi: I pu leh i pi adingin gah hoih pen te i kem hi.

records.english: Respect for elders in our family means listening to their advice, even when we choose a different path.
records.zomi: I innkuan-ah upate zahtakna pen lampi tuam i teel zongin a thuhilhna uh ngaihkhiat ahi hi.

records.english: When my father became an elder himself, he finally understood why his parents had expected so much of him.
records.zomi: Ka pa amah mah upa a suak ciangin bang hangin a nu leh a pa in amah tungah tampi a lamen uh hiam cih a tawp-ah a theisiam hi.

records.english: Grandma insists on serving the guests herself, so we have to be quick to help her.
records.zomi: Pi in mikhualte amah mah in an pia dingin a ngen den ahih manin a huh nadingin i manlang ding hi.

records.english: Once Grandma could no longer climb the stairs, my brothers carried her up to see the new baby.
records.zomi: Pi kahlei a kah zawh nawn loh ciangin ka sanggam pasal te in naungek thak a muh nadingin tung lam ah a pomtou uh hi.

records.english: Respect for elders is easy to keep in a village, but in the city it takes deliberate effort and planning.
records.zomi: Upate zahtakna pen khua-ah kem a baih a, ahi zongin khuapi lian-ah ngim taka hanciam ngai hi.

records.english: Nothing important is decided in our family until Grandma has given her view.
records.zomi: Pi in a ngaihsutna a gen ma-in i innkuan-ah thu thupi khatpeuh kikhensat ngei lo hi.

records.english: My sister takes flowers to our great-aunt every Friday.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam numei in Laithai ni simin i pi lian kiangah pak a paipih hi.

records.english: My brother carries Grandpa's bag to the car.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in Pu' ip mawtaw dong a tawi hi.

records.english: Our family bought Grandpa a comfortable chair.
records.zomi: I innkuan in Pu adingin tutphah nuam khat a lei hi.

records.english: Can I call Auntie by her first name now that I'm grown up?
records.zomi: Tu-in ka khanglian khin ahih manin Ni a min tawh ka sam thei ding hiam?

records.english: Not in our family; she'll always be Auntie to you.
records.zomi: I innkuan-ah thei lo hi; nang adingin Ni den ahi ding hi.

records.english: Our pastor encourages us to bring our faith into the office, not leave it at the church door.
records.zomi: I pastor in i upna biakinn kongkhak-ah nusia lo-in office ah paipih dingin hong hanthawn hi.

records.english: Our family's faith affects which films we watch and which jokes we laugh at.
records.zomi: I innkuan' upna in film bang i en ding, nuihza bang i nui ding hiam cih a khoih hi.

records.english: Living out a Christian worldview at work can mean refusing a profitable deal that would harm others.
records.zomi: Nasep mun-ah Khristian leitung muhna tawh nuntak in midangte a susia ding mu tam thukimna khat nial a cihna ahi thei hi.

records.english: Many believers see history as heading somewhere, not just going round in circles.
records.zomi: Upmi tampi in tangthu pen kual-in a hei lel hi lo-in mun khat ah a pai hi, ci-in a mu uh hi.

records.english: Respecting people with different worldviews is itself part of how many Christians understand love.
records.zomi: Leitung muhna tuamtuam nei mite zahtak pen Khristian tampi in itna a theisiam dan khen khat ahi hi.

records.english: My friend's faith makes her slow to judge people and quick to help them.
records.zomi: Ka lawm' upna in mite thukhen ding a zawisak a, huh ding a manlangsak hi.

records.english: Christians try to be kind to strangers.
records.zomi: Khristiante in mi theih lo te tungah hehpihna nei dingin a hanciam uh hi.

records.english: When my grandfather ran his small shop, he refused to sell anything that was faulty, even at a discount.
records.zomi: Ka pu in a van zuakna inn neu a kem lai-in man niamsak zongin a siat van khatpeuh a zuak nuam kei hi.

records.english: He said that his faith would not let him take money for something he knew was broken.
records.zomi: A siat hi, a theih na khat adingin sum a lak dingin a upna in a phal kei hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Years later, customers still told me that they had trusted him more than any other shopkeeper in town.
records.zomi: Kum tampi khit ciangin van lei mite in khuapi-a van zuakpa dang khempeuh sangin amah a muan zaw uh hi, ci-in hong gen lai uh hi.

records.english: My grandfather taught me that a promise made before God must always be kept.
records.zomi: Ka pu in Pasian mai-a kiciamna khat a kitangtungsak den ding hi, ci-in hong sinsak hi.

records.english: Our church collects food for the food bank.
records.zomi: I pawlpi in an piakna mun adingin an a kaikhawm hi.

records.english: Our youth group talks about faith and everyday life.
records.zomi: I khangno pawl in upna leh ni sim nuntakna thu a kihoupih uh hi.

records.english: How should a Christian respond when a colleague is treated unfairly?
records.zomi: Nasem pih khat dik lo taka a kilim ciangin Khristian khat in bangci-in a dawng ding hiam?

records.english: Christians believe that Jesus is the Son of God.
records.zomi: Khristiante in Jesu pen Pasian Tapa ahi hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: Why do Christians care for the environment?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Khristiante in leitung a kem uh hiam?

records.english: Many believe that the world belongs to God and that people are meant to look after it.
records.zomi: Mi tampi in leitung pen Pasian' a hi a, mite in a kem dingin a kibawl uh hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: Christians are called to love their enemies, which is perhaps the hardest part of their faith to practise.
records.zomi: Khristiante a galte uh it dingin kisam uh a, tua pen a upna uh-a a zat a haksa pen khen ahi kha ding hi.

records.english: Does God want us to look after animals?
records.zomi: Pasian in ganhing te i kem dingin a deih hiam?

records.english: Is work part of serving God?
records.zomi: Nasep pen Pasian na sepna khen khat ahi hiam?

records.english: The belief that every person bears God's image is why many Christians campaign against injustice.
records.zomi: Mi khatciat in Pasian lim a pua hi, cih upna hangin Khristian tampi in dik lohna kalh-in a kipan uh hi.

records.english: A Christian view of time sees each life as part of a story that God is still writing.
records.zomi: Khristian' hun muhna in nuntakna khatciat Pasian in a gelh lai tangthu khat' khen khat bangin a mu hi.

records.english: Do you believe that God cares about everything?
records.zomi: Pasian in na khempeuh a lim hi, na um hiam?

records.english: Is Sunday a day of rest in your family?
records.zomi: Na innkuan-ah Nipini tawlngak ni ahi hiam?

records.english: God made the world, according to the first chapter of the Bible.
records.zomi: Laisiangtho' khen masa pen bangin Pasian in leitung a bawl hi.

records.english: We thank God before every meal, even in restaurants.
records.zomi: An inn-ah zongin an kipat ma simin Pasian lungdam i ko hi.

records.english: Many Christians believe that work is a way of serving God and other people.
records.zomi: Khristian tampi in nasep pen Pasian leh midangte na sepna lam khat ahi hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: How does your faith affect the way you spend money?
records.zomi: Na upna in sum na zat dan bangci-in a khoih hiam?

records.english: We try to give some away first, and we think twice before buying things we don't need.
records.zomi: A masa-in khenkhat pia dingin i hanciam a, i kisam lo na te i lei ma-in nihvei i ngaihsun hi.

records.english: The Christian worldview teaches that suffering and evil are real but not the final word.
records.zomi: Khristian leitung muhna in thuakna leh gitlohna a om taktak hi, ahi zongin thu nunung hi lo hi, ci-in a sinsak hi.

records.english: Love your neighbour as yourself.
records.zomi: Na pumpi na it bangin na lawmte na it in.

records.english: My faith gives me hope for the future.
records.zomi: Ka upna in a hun ding adingin lametna hong pia hi.

records.english: Is it always possible to forgive someone who has hurt you?
records.zomi: Hong natsak mi khat maisak pen hun khempeuh-in a theih hiam?

records.english: Why do some Christians choose not to work on Sundays?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Khristian khenkhat in Nipini-in a sem lo dingin a teel uh hiam?

records.english: Some Christians choose simpler lifestyles so that they can give more to people in need.
records.zomi: Khristian khenkhat in kisamte tungah tam zaw a piak theih nadingin nuntakna baih zaw a teel uh hi.

records.english: Does being a Christian change how you do your job?
records.zomi: Khristian ahih na in na nasep dan a khek hiam?

records.english: It should, because I try to work honestly and treat people fairly, even when nobody is watching.
records.zomi: A khek ding hi, bang hang hiam cih leh kuamah in a en kei zongin thuman takin ka sem a, mite dik takin ka lim dingin ka hanciam hi.

records.english: We try to tell the truth, even when it's hard.
records.zomi: A haksat ciangin zong thutak gen dingin i hanciam hi.

records.english: A Christian worldview shapes how believers think about work, money, family and the world.
records.zomi: Khristian leitung muhna in upmite' nasep, sum, innkuan leh leitung tawh kisai ngaihsutna a bawl hi.

records.english: Believers often find that their faith raises as many questions as it answers, especially about justice.
records.zomi: Upmite in a upna uh in a dawn sangin dotna a piangsak zaw hi, cih a mu zel uh hi, a thupi pen in dikna tawh kisai.

records.english: Christians believe that people are both deeply valuable and deeply in need of forgiveness.
records.zomi: Khristiante in mite pen a manpha mahmah a, maisakna a kisam mahmah zong ahi uh hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: For many believers, faith is less a list of rules than a relationship that shapes every decision.
records.zomi: Upmi tampi adingin upna pen thukham lista sangin thukhensatna khempeuh a bawl kizopna khat ahi zaw hi.

records.english: Why do Christians say that every person is valuable?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Khristiante in mi khatciat a manpha hi, a ci uh hiam?

records.english: That every person is made in the image of God, so nobody is worthless.
records.zomi: Mi khatciat Pasian lim-in kibawl ahih manin kuamah a manpha lo om lo hi, cih ahi hi.

records.english: My father prays in the car before he goes into the office.
records.zomi: Ka pa in office ah a lut ma-in mawtaw sungah thu a ngen hi.

records.english: Our church helps people who are poor.
records.zomi: I pawlpi in mi zawng te a huh hi.

records.english: My mother says every person is precious to God.
records.zomi: Ka nu in mi khatciat Pasian adingin a manpha hi, a ci hi.

records.english: In Christian teaching, the world is good because God made it, but it is also broken by sin.
records.zomi: Khristian thuhilhna-ah Pasian in a bawl ahih manin leitung a hoih hi, ahi zongin mawhna in a susia zong hi.

records.english: Christian ideas about human dignity influenced the founding of many early hospitals and schools.

records.english: What does it mean to have a Christian worldview?

records.english: Teachers who know the town's museums, libraries and parks can bring lessons to life at very little cost.

records.english: When the job centre began working with the library, far more people used both services.

records.english: The council's education office keeps a list of museums and farms that welcome school groups at no cost.

records.english: The enterprise centre's free advice has helped dozens of new businesses survive their difficult first year.

records.english: Schools that build links with local businesses can offer pupils work experience that would otherwise be hard to find.

records.english: Many free resources go unused simply because the people who need them have never heard of them.

records.english: Is the careers office open every afternoon?

records.english: Employers who point staff towards local support often see lower absence and better morale.

records.english: Ask the student office about travel grants.
records.zomi: Khualzinna sum huhna tawh kisai sangnaupang office dong in.

records.english: Can I use the college gym for free?

records.english: Admitting uncertainty is often more helpful than a confident answer that turns out to be wrong.

records.english: Will the paint be dry by tonight?

records.english: Probably, although the label says it can take longer when it's damp.

records.english: It's anyone's guess how long the queue at the post office will be.

records.english: The cat might be hiding under the bed.
records.zomi: Zawhngeu lupna nuai-ah a kisel kha ding hi.

records.english: Is the milk still fresh, do you think?
records.zomi: Nawi a thak lai hiam, na ci hiam?

records.english: Phrases like 'as far as I know' let listeners judge how much weight to give an answer.
records.zomi: 'Ka theih bangin' cih kammal te in a ngai mite dawnna khat bangzah a gik hiam cih a khen theih nadingin a phal hi.

records.english: My grandmother used to say that the only thing certain about the weather is that it will change.
records.zomi: Ka pi in khuamun tawh kisai a kician na khat bek pen a kikhek ding ahi hi, a ci zel hi.

records.english: It could be a cold, or it could just be hay fever.

records.english: Uncertainty about the date of the move made it impossible to give notice at work.
records.zomi: Inn suanna ni a kician loh manin nasep mun-ah thu theisak theih lo hi.

records.english: I couldn't say for certain, but I think the bakery has changed owners.
records.zomi: Ka thei cian kei hi, ahi zongin moh bawlna inn in a neipa a khek hi, ka ci hi.

records.english: I think the café is on the left, but I'm not sure.

records.english: I have a feeling that the meeting will be moved again.

records.english: Is that mushroom safe to eat?

records.english: I honestly couldn't tell you, so let's leave it where it is.

records.english: The more I learn about cooking, the less certain I am that there is one right way to do anything.

records.english: I'm not sure if I turned off the lights.
records.zomi: Meivak te ka phiat hiam cih ka thei cian kei hi.

records.english: Your guess is as good as mine about what the boss will decide.
records.zomi: Makaipa in bang a khensat ding hiam cih kei bang mahin nang zong na thei kei hi.

records.english: Maybe we should take an umbrella.
records.zomi: Guahtuk i paipih kha ding hi.

records.english: I'm fairly sure the concert starts at eight, but check the tickets to be safe.
records.zomi: La sakna nai giat-in a kipan hi, ka thei cian deuh hi, ahi zongin a bit nadingin lai man te en in.

records.english: I'm in two minds about whether to take the job abroad.
records.zomi: Gamdang-a nasep ka la ding hiam cih-ah ka lungsim a nih hi.

records.english: Do you happen to know if the museum opens on Mondays?
records.zomi: Tangthu van kemna inn Pizing ni-in a kihong hiam cih na thei kha hiam?

records.english: I don't know whether he's coming tonight.
records.zomi: Tu zan a hong ding hiam cih ka thei kei hi.

records.english: I can't remember the name of that film.
records.zomi: Tua film' min ka phawk thei kei hi.

records.english: I wouldn't bet on the train being on time today.
records.zomi: Tu ni-in meileng hun dik-in a tung ding hi, ci-in ka ap kei ding hi.

records.english: The doctor was careful to say that the results were encouraging rather than conclusive.
records.zomi: Siavuan in gah te lametna hoih a lak hi, ahi zongin a kicing nai kei hi, ci-in a cian takin a gen hi.

records.english: I might be late, so don't wait for me.
records.zomi: Ka nung kha ding ahih manin hong ngak kei in.

records.english: Is this jacket warm enough, do you think?

records.english: Is this the right key for the shed?
records.zomi: Hih van koihna inn neu adingin tawh dik ahi hiam?

records.english: When the guide admitted she didn't know the answer, the tourists seemed to trust everything else she said.

records.english: The vet couldn't tell whether the dog had eaten something or was just tired.
records.zomi: Ganhing siavuan in ui in na khat a ne hiam, a gim lel hiam cih a gen thei kei hi.

records.english: Which bus goes to the zoo, do you know?

records.english: We're not sure yet whether we'll be able to afford a holiday this year.
records.zomi: Hih kum-in tawlngakna khualzin man i pia zo ding hiam cih i thei cian nai kei hi.

records.english: Nobody seems to know exactly when the road will reopen.

records.zomi: Kizuak kha ding hi, ahi zongin lei ding mite in kum thak dong a ngak zel uh ahih manin ka lamen kei ding hi.

records.english: I might have left my wallet in the car.
records.zomi: Ka sum ip mawtaw sungah ka nusia kha ding hi.

records.english: Experienced travellers build extra time into every journey, because something uncertain always happens.

records.english: I'm not certain the oven is hot enough.
records.zomi: Meikhuk a sa tawk hiam cih ka thei cian kei hi.

records.english: It's hard to know whether the new neighbours have moved in yet.
records.zomi: Inn kiang mi thakte a lut khin uh hiam cih theih a haksa hi.

records.english: Planning a wedding during such uncertain times meant booking a venue that offered full refunds.
records.zomi: Thei cian loh hun-in mopawi ngim in sum bup piak kik theih mun khat laih a ngai hi.

records.english: When my phone died on a mountain walk, I wasn't sure which path led back to the car park.
