records.zomi: I innkuan-a khangno khenkhat in ngeina bawl dan te a gimhuai sa uh a, ahi zongin a pu leh pi uh adingin an a huan ciangin tua bawl dan te a ciptak uh hi.

records.english: Teaching children to prepare food safely, from washing their hands to using a knife, is part of growing up in our family.
records.zomi: Naupangte khut sil pan namsau zat dong an bit taka bawl dan sinsak pen i innkuan-a khanlet' a kiang khat ahi hi.

records.english: Learning to prepare traditional food from my father has helped me feel connected to a village I have never visited.
records.zomi: Ka pa pan ngeina an bawl dan sin in ka kan ngei loh khua khat tawh kizopna nei bangin hong kisaksak hi.

records.english: Can I taste the soup?
records.zomi: An tui ka ne en thei ding hiam?

records.english: Every autumn, my grandparents spent a whole weekend drying vegetables for the winter.
records.zomi: Phal lam simin ka pu leh ka pi in khuaphal adingin anlah keusak dingin kal tawp bup a zang uh hi.

records.english: My grandfather sliced the beans and pumpkins, while my grandmother laid them out on bamboo trays in the sun.
records.zomi: Ka pu in be leh mai te a at a, ka pi in ni tungah ma pheek-ah a phah hi.

records.english: By the end of the month, the shelves were full of jars, and we ate those vegetables until the spring.
records.zomi: Kha bei ciangin van koihna te bel tawh a dim a, spring dong tua anlah te i ne hi.

records.english: My aunt says you can tell how much a family respects its guests by how carefully the food is prepared.
records.zomi: Innkuan khat in a mikhualte bangzah in a zahtak hiam cih pen an bangzah kician taka a bawl hiam cih tawh na thei thei hi, ka ni in a ci hi.

records.english: My aunt makes the chilli paste every week.
records.zomi: Ka ni in kal simin malcha gawi a bawl hi.

records.english: We let the soup cook slowly on a low fire for most of the afternoon.
records.zomi: Sun nung lam a tamzaw sung an tui mei neu tungah zawl takin a min i khawl hi.

records.english: Drying and smoking food was once essential for surviving the winter, but now my family does it mainly to keep the tradition alive.
records.zomi: An keusak leh hal pen khatvei lai-in khuaphal pelh nadingin a kisam mahmah a, ahi zongin tu-in i innkuan in ngeina a nungta lai nadingin bek a bawl hi.

records.english: Who taught Grandpa to cook?
records.zomi: Pu an huan dan kua in a sinsak hiam?

records.english: How did your family prepare food for the wedding?
records.zomi: Na innkuan in mopawi adingin an bangci-in a bawl uh hiam?

records.english: Everyone came the day before, and the aunts chopped vegetables while the men built the cooking fires.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh a ni ma-in a hong uh a, nite in anlah a at uh laitakin pasalte in an huanna mei a bawl uh hi.

records.english: When my grandmother prepares bamboo shoots, she boils them twice to remove the bitterness.
records.zomi: Ka pi in ma a bawl ciangin a khahna beisak nadingin nihvei a lawh hi.

records.english: Does hope for the future change how you live?
records.zomi: Hong tung ding hun adinga lametna in na nuntak dan a khek hiam?

records.english: Believers across many traditions say together in their creeds that they look for the life of the world to come.
records.zomi: Ngeina tuamtuam-a um mite in a upna gen uh-ah hong piang ding hun-a nuntakna a lamen uh hi, ci-in a gen khawm uh hi.

records.english: Do you think about the future often?
records.zomi: Hong tung ding hun tawh kisai na ngaihsun zel hiam?

records.english: What do Christians mean when they say Jesus will come again?
records.zomi: Jesu hong paikik ding hi, a cih uh ciangin Khazih mite in bang a cihna uh hiam?

records.english: They believe he will return one day to bring God's kingdom in full and to set the world right.
records.zomi: Ni khat ni-in Pasian Gam a kicing-in hong piang sak a, leitung a dik sak dingin hong ciahkik ding hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: Jesus said to keep watch.
records.zomi: Jesu in na ngak un, a ci hi.

records.english: Does your church pray for justice in the world?
records.zomi: Na pawlpi in leitung-a thumanna adingin thu a ngen hiam?

records.english: My grandmother kept her best dress in the wardrobe and said she was saving it for the day Jesus came back.
records.zomi: Ka pi in a puan hoih pen puan bawm sungah a kem a, Jesu a hong paikik ni adingin ka kem hi, a ci hi.

records.english: When we laughed, she smiled and said that she simply wanted to be ready, whenever that day might be.
records.zomi: I nuih ciangin a nuih a, tua ni bang hun-in hong tung zongin a kisakcip-in om nuam lel ka hi hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Years later, at her funeral, the pastor told that story, and everyone understood what she had meant.
records.zomi: Kum tampi khit ciangin a misi vuina-ah pastor in tua tangthu a gen a, mi khempeuh in a cihna a theisiam uh hi.

records.english: Advent sermons often speak of the first coming of Jesus and his promised second coming together.
records.zomi: Advent thuhilhna te in Jesu' a hong pai masakna leh a kiciamsa a hong paikikna a gen khawm zel hi.

records.english: The expectation of Christ's return encouraged early Christians to care for the poor and to share their possessions.
records.zomi: Khazih' hong paikik ding lamenna in Khazih mite masate a zawngte kem dingin leh a neihsa uh a zang khawm dingin a hanthawn hi.

records.english: What do Christians hope for in the future?
records.zomi: Hong tung ding hun-ah Khazih mite in bang a lamen uh hiam?

records.english: Our church sings about Jesus' return.
records.zomi: I pawlpi in Jesu' hong paikikna tawh kisai la a sa hi.

records.english: Some Christians fear that too much focus on the end times can distract believers from loving their neighbours today.
records.zomi: Khazih mite khenkhat in tawpna hun tungah lungsim tam lua koih in um mite tuni-a a inn kiang mite it pan a lamang thei hi, ci-in a lau uh hi.

records.english: The hope of Christ's return has inspired Christians to work for justice, believing that God's kingdom is already breaking in.
records.zomi: Khazih' hong paikikna lametna in Pasian Gam a hong lut khin hi, ci-in um-in Khazih mite thumanna adingin a sep dingin a hanthawn hi.

records.english: Is the second coming in the Bible?
records.zomi: A nihvei hong paikikna pen Laisiangtho sungah a om hiam?

records.english: Believers disagree about many details, but most agree that the future is in God's hands.
records.zomi: Um mite in a neu tampi tawh kisai-in a kitup kei uh a, ahi zongin a tamzaw in hong tung ding hun Pasian' khut sungah a om hi, ci-in a kitup uh hi.

records.english: Is it frightening to think about the end of the world?
records.zomi: Leitung tawpna ngaihsut pen a lauhuai hiam?

records.english: For many believers it's a hope rather than a fear, because they trust God to make things new.
records.zomi: Um mi tampi adingin launa sangin lametna ahi hi, bang hang hiam cih leh Pasian in na te a thakin a bawl ding hi, ci-in a muang uh hi.

records.english: My grandmother talks about heaven a lot.
records.zomi: Ka pi in vantung thu a gen tam mahmah hi.

records.english: Christians believe Jesus will come back.
records.zomi: Khazih mite in Jesu hong paikik ding hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: Why do some churches sing about Christ's return at Christmas?
records.zomi: Bang hangin pawlpi khenkhat in Christmas-in Khazih' hong paikikna tawh kisai la a sa uh hiam?

records.english: Because Advent looks forward both to his birth and to his coming again.
records.zomi: Bang hang hiam cih leh Advent in a pianna leh a hong paikikna a nih a en lawh hi.

records.english: Christians believe God will judge fairly.
records.zomi: Khazih mite in Pasian in thumanna tawh thu a khen ding hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: My pastor warned us to be careful of anyone who claims to know exactly when the world will end.
records.zomi: Ka pastor in leitung bang hun-in a bei ding hiam cih a thei cian hi, a ci kuapeuh tawh kisai-in kidawm dingin hong vaihawm hi.

records.english: How should a Christian live if Jesus might return at any time?
records.zomi: Jesu bang hun-in hong paikik ding hiam cih a kitheih loh leh Khazih mi khat bangci-in a nungta ding hiam?

records.english: Do all Christians agree about how Christ's return will happen?
records.zomi: Khazih' hong paikikna bangci-in a piang ding hiam cih tawh kisai-in Khazih mite khempeuh a kitup uh hiam?

records.english: No, they agree that he will return, but they interpret the details of the Bible's prophecies differently.
records.zomi: Kitup kei uh hi, a hong paikik ding hi, cih ah a kitup uh a, ahi zongin Laisiangtho' kamsangte thugen' a neu te a tuamtuam-in a khiatna a gen uh hi.

records.english: Interpretations of the book of Revelation range from symbolic readings to detailed predictions of future events.
records.zomi: Mangmuhna Lai' khiatna te in lim khiatna pan hong tung ding thupiang te' kician taka genkholhna dong a tuamtuam hi.

records.english: Advent is a time of waiting.
records.zomi: Advent pen ngakna hun ahi hi.

records.english: Christian hope looks forward to a time when God will wipe away every tear.
records.zomi: Khazih mite' lametna in Pasian in khitui khempeuh a nul siang ding hun a lamen hi.

records.english: Theologians describe the Christian view of history as moving towards a goal rather than repeating endless cycles.
records.zomi: Pasian thu siamte in Khazih mite' tangthu ngaihsutna pen tawp om lo kikheel kik zel sangin ngim khat lam-ah a pai hi, ci-in a gen uh hi.

records.english: Belief in Christ's return gives many believers hope when the world seems full of injustice.
records.zomi: Leitung in dik lohna tawh a dim bang a kilat ciangin Khazih' hong paikikna upna in um mi tampi lametna a pia hi.

records.english: The pastor preached about being ready.
records.zomi: Pastor in kisakcip-in om ding thu a hilh hi.

records.english: Christian teaching about the return of Christ is less about predicting the future than about trusting God with it.
records.zomi: Khazih' hong paikikna tawh kisai Khazih mite' thuhilhna pen hong tung ding hun genkholh sangin tua hun Pasian tungah muan thu ahi zaw hi.

records.english: The early Christians prayed 'Come, Lord Jesus', expressing their longing for his return.
records.zomi: Khazih mite masate in 'Topa Jesu aw, hong pai ta in' ci-in thu a ngen uh a, a hong paikikna a lunggulh uh a lak uh hi.

records.english: Throughout history, groups that set dates for the end of the world have been proved wrong, which many churches see as a warning.
records.zomi: Tangthu sung khempeuh-in leitung tawpna ni a koih pawl te a khial uh hi, cih a kilang a, tua pen pawlpi tampi in vaihawmna khat ahi hi, ci-in a mu uh hi.

records.english: Jesus told stories about waiting servants.
records.zomi: Jesu in a ngak nasemte tawh kisai tangthu te a gen hi.

records.english: Christian funerals often express the hope of resurrection at Christ's return, giving mourners comfort in their grief.
records.zomi: Khazih mite' misi vuina te in Khazih' hong paikik ciang-a thawhkikna lametna a gen zel a, dah mite a dahna uh-ah hehnepna a pia hi.

records.english: My friend asked me what the second coming means.
records.zomi: Ka lawm in a nihvei hong paikikna in bang a cihna hiam, ci-in hong dong hi.

records.english: Why do you light a candle each week in Advent?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Advent sungin kal simin khawimeivaak khat na tang hiam?

records.english: The Apostles' Creed says that Christ will come again to judge the living and the dead.
records.zomi: Sawltakte' Upna Gen in Khazih mi nungta leh mi site thu khen dingin hong paikik ding hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Living in hope of Christ's return means taking both the present world and the world to come seriously.
records.zomi: Khazih' hong paikikna lametna tawh nuntak pen tu hun-a leitung leh hong piang ding hun-a leitung a nih a thupi sa-in kep ahi hi.

records.english: Some churches emphasise the return of Christ in their preaching more than others do.
records.zomi: Pawlpi khenkhat in a thuhilhna uh-ah Khazih' hong paikikna a dangte sangin a gen tam zaw uh hi.

records.english: Why do some people try to predict the date of Christ's return, when the Bible says nobody knows it?
records.zomi: Laisiangtho in kuamah in a thei kei hi, a cih laitakin bang hangin mi khenkhat in Khazih' hong paikik ding ni a genkholh tum uh hiam?

records.english: Some Christians find the idea of final judgement troubling, while others find comfort in the promise of justice.
records.zomi: Khazih mite khenkhat in thukhenna nunung ngaihsutna in a lungkhamsak a, a dangte in thumanna kamciamna-ah hehnepna a mu uh hi.

records.english: For many believers, the return of Christ is the moment when evil will finally be defeated and creation restored.
records.zomi: Um mi tampi adingin Khazih' hong paikikna pen gilote a tawp-ah kizo ding a, a kibawlsa na khempeuh a kicing kik ding hun ahi hi.

records.english: Nobody knows when it will happen.
records.zomi: Bang hun-in a piang ding hiam cih kuamah in a thei kei hi.

records.english: Will there be peace when Jesus returns?
records.zomi: Jesu a hong paikik ciangin lungnopna a om ding hiam?

records.english: Jesus told a parable about ten young women waiting with lamps for a wedding to begin.
records.zomi: Jesu in mopawi kipat ding ngak in meivak tawi nungak sawm tawh kisai thugentehna khat a gen hi.

records.english: The parables of waiting suggest that faithfulness in ordinary tasks matters more than knowing the exact time.
records.zomi: Ngakna thugentehna te in nasep ngeina te-a muanhuaina pen hun cian theih sangin a thupi zaw hi, cih a lak hi.

records.english: Many Christians believe that waiting for Christ's return means living faithfully now, not just watching the sky.
records.zomi: Khazih mite tampi in Khazih' hong paikikna ngak pen van lam en bek hi lo-in tu-in muanhuai takin nungta ahi hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: Do you know when Jesus will return?
records.zomi: Jesu bang hun-in hong paikik ding hiam cih na thei hiam?

records.english: No, and Jesus himself said that nobody knows the day or the hour.
records.zomi: Ka thei kei hi, Jesu mah in zong tua ni leh nai kuamah in a thei kei hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Why does the Bible tell us to be ready?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Laisiangtho in kisakcip-in om dingin hong hilh hiam?

records.english: My father reads about it in the Gospels.
records.zomi: Ka pa in Lungdamna Thu te-ah tua thu a sim hi.

records.english: We pray for God's kingdom to come.
records.zomi: Pasian Gam hong piang dingin thu i ngen hi.

records.english: The book of Revelation uses vivid images that Christians have interpreted in many different ways.
records.zomi: Mangmuhna Lai in Khazih mite in tuamtuam-in a khiatna uh lim kician mahmah te a zang hi.

records.english: Hope helps us live well today.
records.zomi: Lametna in tuni-in hoih takin i nuntak nadingin hong huh hi.

records.english: Shall we eat now or later?
records.zomi: Tu-in i ne ding hiam, a nung ciangin i ne ding hiam?

records.english: We decided to have a small wedding and spend the money on a longer honeymoon.
records.zomi: Mopawi neu khat bawl-in sum pen kiteen khit tawlngakna sau zaw-ah zang dingin i khensat hi.

records.english: Should I call him or send a message?
records.zomi: Phone tawh ka sam ding hiam, thukhak ka khak ding hiam?

records.english: We made the decision to adopt a dog after the children promised to walk him every day.
records.zomi: Naupangte in ni simin a pi-in a kalsak ding uh a ciam uh khit ciangin ui khat kem dingin i khensat hi.

records.english: We've decided to paint the bedroom yellow.
records.zomi: Lupna inndan gial-in sat dingin i khensat hi.

records.english: Would you rather make the decision tonight or talk it over with your family first?
records.zomi: Tu zan na khensat ding hiam, ahih kei leh na innkuan tawh a masa-in na kihoupih ding hiam, bang na deih zaw hiam?

records.english: I've decided to cut my hair short.
records.zomi: Ka sam tom-in at dingin ka khensat hi.

records.english: Regret often comes not from the decisions we make but from the ones we keep putting off.
records.zomi: Kisikna pen i khensatna te pan sangin i nawlsak zel te pan a hong pai zaw zel hi.

records.english: When a decision affects the whole family, everyone deserves to be heard, even the youngest.
records.zomi: Khensatna khat in innkuan bup a sukha ciangin mi khempeuh, a neu pen zong, a thu uh kingai ding a kilawm hi.

records.english: My cousin made a list of reasons on each side, but she still followed her heart.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam in a lang khatciat-ah hangsan lista khat a bawl a, ahi zongin a lungsim deihna a zui lai hi.

records.english: Is it too late to change my mind about the course?
records.zomi: Sinna tawh kisai ka ngaihsutna khek dingin a nung khin hiam?

records.english: Not until the end of next week, so you still have time to think.
records.zomi: Kal zom tawp dong a nung nai kei a, tua ahih manin ngaihsut nading hun na nei lai hi.

records.english: A decision that seems selfish may be the only way someone can look after their own health.
records.zomi: Kimai deihna bang a kilang khensatna khat pen mi khat in amah' cidamna a kem theihna lampi khat bek a suak thei hi.

records.english: Once you've made the decision, try not to keep asking yourself whether it was right.
records.zomi: Na khensat khit ciangin a dik hiam cih na kidot zel lohna dingin hanciam in.

records.english: Let's flip a coin.
records.zomi: Dangka khat i khiat ni.

records.english: How did the family decide who would look after Grandpa's dog?
records.zomi: Pu' ui kua in a kem ding hiam cih innkuan in bangci-in a khensat uh hiam?

records.english: We asked the dog, in a way: he followed my youngest cousin home and refused to leave.
records.zomi: Ui i dong bang hi: ka sanggam neu pen' inn dong a zui a, a pai khiat nuam kei hi.

records.english: I finally decided to sell my old guitar, though I'll miss it.
records.zomi: Ka guitar lui zuak dingin a tawp-ah ka khensat hi, ka lunggulh ding hangin.

records.english: Once my parents had decided to move, they never once looked back or complained.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in suan dingin a khensat khit ciangin nung lam a et kik ngei kei uh a, a phun ngei kei uh hi.

records.english: We decided to stay at home this weekend.
records.zomi: Hih kal tawp inn-ah om dingin i khensat hi.

records.english: The hardest part of choosing a flat was deciding what we could live without.
records.zomi: Flat teelna-a a haksa pen pen bang om lo-in i nungta thei ding hiam cih khensat ahi hi.

records.english: Who decides where the family goes for Christmas this year?
records.zomi: Tu kum Christmas adingin innkuan koi-ah a pai ding hiam cih kua in a khensat hiam?

records.english: Some decisions feel enormous at the time but turn out to matter very little, while small ones can change everything.
records.zomi: Khensatna khenkhat tua hun-in a lian mahmah bangin a kisa a, ahi zongin a thupi lo mahmah suak a, a neu te in na khempeuh a khek thei hi.

records.english: Have you chosen a name for the puppy?
records.zomi: Ui no adingin min khat na teel khin hiam?

records.english: I need more time to think about it.
records.zomi: Tua tawh kisai ngaihsut nadingin hun behlap ka kisam hi.

records.english: Making a decision is often easier than living with the uncertainty of not making one.
records.zomi: Khensat pen a khensat lohna' kician lohna tawh nuntak sangin a baih zaw zel hi.

records.english: My uncle changed his mind three times before he booked the flights.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in vanleng lai a ciamteh ma-in a ngaihsutna thumvei a khek hi.

records.english: Shall we go with the tiles for the bathroom or the cheaper paint?
records.zomi: Kisilna inndan adingin tile i zang ding hiam, ahih kei leh man neem zaw paint i zang ding hiam?

records.english: Choosing between two good options is a luxury, but it can still keep people awake at night.
records.zomi: Teel ding hoih nih kikal-ah teel pen hauhna khat ahi a, ahi zongin mite zan-in a ihmut loh nadingin a om sak thei lai hi.

records.english: My sister decided to learn the piano.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam numei in piano sin dingin a khensat hi.

records.english: Should I accept the first offer for my old car?
records.zomi: Ka mawtaw lui adingin a hong ngen masa pen man ka san ding hiam?

records.english: Wait a week, because two more people have said they want to see it.
records.zomi: Kal khat ngak in, bang hang hiam cih leh mi nih in a en nop uh hi, ci-in a gen uh hi.

records.english: Writing down the reasons for a choice helps when you later need to explain it to others.
records.zomi: Teelna khat' hangsan te gelh pen a nung ciangin mi dangte kiangah na gen ding a kisam ciangin a huh hi.

records.english: Do you trust your first instinct, or do you prefer to think everything through?
records.zomi: Na lungsim ngaihsut masak na muang hiam, ahih kei leh na khempeuh kician taka ngaihsun na deih zaw hiam?

records.english: I can never decide what to order, so I usually ask the waiter to choose for me.
records.zomi: Bang ka ngen ding hiam cih ka khensat thei ngei kei ahih manin an pia nasem kiangah hong teelsak dingin ka ngen zel hi.

records.english: Which seat do you want?
records.zomi: Bang tutna na deih hiam?

records.english: I can't decide what to wear.
records.zomi: Bang ka silh ding hiam cih ka khensat thei kei hi.

records.english: My father's rule is that any decision made while angry must be checked again the next morning.
records.zomi: Ka pa' thukham pen hehna tawh kibawl khensatna khatpeuh a zingciang zingsang-in en kik ding hi, cih ahi hi.

records.english: Have you decided where to go for the summer?
records.zomi: Khal hun adingin koi-ah pai ding na khensat khin hiam?

records.english: We're choosing between the coast and my sister's farm, and the children want the farm.
records.zomi: Tuipi kiang leh ka sanggam numei' lo inn kikal-ah i teel laitak hi, naupangte in lo inn a deih uh hi.

records.english: My friend decided to give up her car and cycle everywhere instead.
records.zomi: Ka lawm in a mawtaw nusia-in koi-ah zong siiksakol tawh pai dingin a khensat hi.

records.english: Should we spend the money on a holiday or save it for a new kitchen?
records.zomi: Sum pen tawlngakni-ah i zang ding hiam, ahih kei leh an huanna inndan thak adingin i kem ding hiam?

records.english: Did you choose the cake or the ice cream?
records.zomi: Cake na teel hiam, ice cream na teel hiam?

records.english: Good decisions usually balance what we want now with what we will need later.
records.zomi: Khensatna hoih te in tu-a i deih leh a nung ciangin i kisam ding te a kizopsak zel hi.

records.english: We decided to take the early train.
records.zomi: Zingsang meileng masa pen la dingin i khensat hi.

records.english: I'll decide after lunch.
records.zomi: Sun an khit ciangin ka khensat ding hi.

records.english: Which way should we go?
records.zomi: Bang lampi i zui ding hiam?

records.english: When my brother was offered a place at two universities, he couldn't choose between them.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal university nih-ah mun a ngah ciangin a nih kikal-ah a teel thei kei hi.

records.english: He visited both on the same weekend and wrote down how he felt walking around each one.
records.zomi: Kal tawp khat mah-in a nih a va kan a, khatciat a vak ciangin bangci-in a kisa hiam cih a gelh hi.

records.english: In the end, he chose the smaller one, because it was the only place where he could imagine being happy for four years.
records.zomi: A tawp-ah a neu zaw a teel hi, bang hang hiam cih leh kum li sung a lungdam ding hi, ci-in a ngaihsut theih mun khat bek ahi hi.

records.english: I'm going to buy the cheaper one.
records.zomi: A man neem zaw ka lei ding hi.

records.english: Which film shall we see?
records.zomi: Bang film i en ding hiam?

records.english: Asking too many people for advice can make a decision harder rather than easier.
records.zomi: Mi tam lua kiangah thuhilhna ngen in khensatna a baih zaw sangin a haksa zaw sak thei hi.

records.english: After years of indecision, my aunt finally left her job and opened the café she had always dreamed of.

records.english: My parents decided to retire to the coast after visiting the town's health centre and library.

records.english: The decision to foster changed our family's life, but it was the training from the council that gave us the confidence.

records.english: My grandmother decided to stop driving.

records.english: A decision made with good advice may still be difficult, but it is rarely one that people regret.

records.english: The town's decision to keep its library open was made after hundreds of residents wrote to the council.
records.zomi: Khuapi' laibu inn kihong zom dingin khensatna pen khua mi za tampi in council kiangah lai a gelh khit ciangin a kibawl hi.

records.english: Advice services help people make decisions calmly, instead of in panic when a crisis arrives.
records.zomi: Thuhilhna nasep te in mite haksatna a tun ciangin lauthawng-in khensat sangin lungmuang takin a khensat nadingin a huh uh hi.

records.english: Deciding to move a parent into care is often harder for the children than for the parent.

records.english: Why do so many families find it hard to decide whether a relative should go into a care home?

records.english: The firefighter told us to check our smoke alarms.
records.zomi: Meikang mitsuakpa in i meikhu theihna khawl te en dingin hong gen hi.

records.english: What's the most important thing you learned as a nurse?
records.zomi: Nurse na hih lai-in na sin thupi pen bang hiam?

records.english: To listen to patients, because they often know what's wrong before the tests do.
records.zomi: Damlote ngai ding, bang hang hiam cih leh sitna te ma-in bang a siat hiam cih a thei zel uh hi.

records.english: Volunteering teaches humility, because those we set out to help often end up helping us.
records.zomi: Thalawp sep in kiniamkhiatna a sinsak hi, bang hang hiam cih leh i huh ding a ci mite in a tamzaw-in eite hong huh zaw uh hi.

records.english: The old postman on our street knew everyone, and he taught me that small conversations matter.
records.zomi: I lampi-a lai paipih upa pa in mi khempeuh a thei a, kiho neute a thupi hi, cih hong sinsak hi.

records.english: Did working in a shop teach you to be polite?
records.zomi: Van zuakna inn-a nasep in zahtak taka gamta dingin hong sinsak hiam?

records.english: Driving an ambulance showed me how much difference a calm voice can make.
records.zomi: Ambulance tawi in aw nem khat in bangzah kikhekna a piang sak thei hiam cih hong lak hi.

records.english: I learned to be kind from my teacher.
records.zomi: Ka saya pan lungsim hoih ding ka sin hi.

records.english: My first year as a social worker taught me to listen before trying to fix anything.
records.zomi: Mi huhna nasem ka hih kum masa pen in bangmah bawl kik ka tum ma-in ngai dingin hong sinsak hi.

records.english: Did working at the library change you?
records.zomi: Laibu inn-a nasep in hong khek hiam?

records.english: Yes, it taught me that people come for help with far more than books.
records.zomi: Khek hi, mite in laibu sangin na tam zaw mahmah adingin huhna ngen dingin a hong uh hi, cih hong sinsak hi.

records.english: What did you learn from your years as a police officer?
records.zomi: Palik pa na hih kum te pan bang na sin hiam?

records.english: Helping at the soup kitchen made me realise how lonely some people are.
records.zomi: An tui piakna mun-ah ka huh in mi khenkhat bangzah in a kia uh hiam cih hong theisiam sak hi.

records.english: Helping others made me happier.
records.zomi: Midangte huh in hong lungdam zaw sak hi.

records.english: The lessons learned from helping others are usually about patience, gratitude and the value of ordinary days.
records.zomi: Midangte huhna pan sinna te a tamzaw-in thuakzawhna, lungdamna leh ni ngeina te' manphatna tawh kisai ahi hi.

records.english: What has the fire service taught you about life?
records.zomi: Meikang mitsuakna pawl in nuntakna tawh kisai bang hong sinsak hiam?

records.english: That small precautions, like checking a smoke alarm, can save a whole family.
records.zomi: Kidawmna neute, meikhu theihna khawl en bang, in innkuan bup a huhdam thei hi, cih.

records.english: Coaching the youth football team taught me that every child wants to be noticed.
records.zomi: Khangno football pawl sinsak in naupang khempeuh in kiphawk a deih uh hi, cih hong sinsak hi.

records.english: Has volunteering taught you anything you didn't expect?
records.zomi: Thalawp sep in na lamen loh na khatpeuh hong sinsak hiam?

records.english: Working with families in crisis taught the counsellor that every person has a story worth hearing.
records.zomi: Haksatna-a om innkuante tawh nasep in lungsim thuhilhpa mi khempeuh in zak kilawm tangthu khat a nei hi, cih a sinsak hi.

records.english: My neighbour taught me to share what I have.
records.zomi: Ka inn kiang mi in ka neih te hawm dingin hong sinsak hi.

records.english: Small kindnesses make a big difference.
records.zomi: Lungsim hoihna neute in kikhekna lian a piang sak hi.

records.english: My old headteacher used to say that patience is a kind of respect, and I've never forgotten it.
records.zomi: Ka sang makaipa lui in thuakzawhna pen zahtakna khat ahi hi, a ci den a, ka mangngilh ngei kei hi.

records.english: Some of the most valuable lessons in life are learned while serving others, not while studying.
records.zomi: Nuntakna-a sinna manpha pen khenkhat sin laitak hi lo-in midangte na a sep laitakin kisin hi.

records.english: Years of answering emergency calls taught the operator that panic spreads, but so does calm.
records.zomi: Kum tampi sung manlang ding sapna te a dawng nasem in lauthawnna a kizel hi, ahi zongin lungmuanna zong a kizel hi, cih a sin hi.

records.english: The library taught me to love reading.
records.zomi: Laibu inn in laibu sim it dingin hong sinsak hi.

records.english: When you see a community from behind the counter of a post office, you learn how much people rely on one another.
records.zomi: Post office' dohkan nung pan khuasung khat na et ciangin mite in bangzah a kingak uh hiam cih na sin hi.

records.english: The town's oldest volunteer says that giving time has taught her more than any job she was paid for.
records.zomi: Khuapi' thalawp upa pen in hun piak in man a ngah nasep khatpeuh sangin a sin tam zaw sak hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Retired teachers who help adults learn to read often say it is the most rewarding work they have ever done.
records.zomi: Upate lai sim sinsak-a a huh nasep pan tawlngak sayate in a sep ngei nasep a lungdam huai pen ahi hi, a ci zel uh hi.

records.english: What did volunteering at the food bank teach you?
records.zomi: An piakna mun-a thalawp sep in bang hong sinsak hiam?

records.english: That almost anyone can fall on hard times, and that asking for help takes courage.
records.zomi: Kuapeuh in hun haksa a tuak thei a, huhna ngen in hangsanna a kisam hi, cih.

records.english: My first job taught me the value of money.
records.zomi: Ka nasep masa pen in sum' manphatna hong sinsak hi.

records.english: I learned to save money at the bank.
records.zomi: Bank-ah sum kem ding ka sin hi.

records.english: Why do you still drive the community bus at seventy-five?
records.zomi: Bang hangin kum sawmsagih le nga na hih zongin khuasung bus na tawi lai hiam?

records.english: Because the passengers taught me that a lift to the shops can be the only conversation someone has all week.
records.zomi: Bang hang hiam cih leh khualzin mite in van zuakna inn-a mawtaw tuan khat pen mi khat in kal bup sungah a kihona khat bek a suak thei hi, cih hong sinsak uh hi.

records.english: Hospital porters often say that the job taught them to treat every patient as if they were family.
records.zomi: Damlo inn-a damlo paipih nasemte in nasep in damlo khempeuh innkuan bangin bawl dingin a sinsak hi, a ci zel uh hi.

records.english: Working at the advice centre taught me that most problems are easier to solve when caught early.
records.zomi: Thuhilhna mun-a nasep in buaina a tamzaw pen manlang taka a kimuh ciangin bawlkik a baih zaw hi, cih hong sinsak hi.

records.english: Listening is more important than talking.
records.zomi: Ngaihna pen genna sangin a thupi zaw hi.

records.english: Our family photo album shows four generations wearing the same patterned cloth.
records.zomi: I innkuan photo laibu in suan li in puan lim kibang a silh uh a lak hi.

records.english: My cousins wore matching skirts at the wedding.
records.zomi: Ka sanggamte in mopawi-ah numei puan kibang a silh uh hi.

records.english: My daughter wears her traditional skirt with trainers, which makes her grandmother laugh.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in a ngeina numei puan tai khedap tawh a silh a, tua in a pi a nuihsak hi.

records.english: My cousin borrowed my skirt for the dance.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam in lam dingin ka numei puan a puk hi.

records.english: Do the children have traditional clothes for the festival?
records.zomi: Naupangte in pawi adingin ngeina puan a nei uh hiam?

records.english: The girls do, and Grandma is sewing a jacket for the little one this week.
records.zomi: Numei naupangte in a nei uh a, Pi in hih kal sungin a neu pen adingin puan khak khat a khui hi.

records.english: My brother wore a traditional shirt at his wedding.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal in a mopawi-ah ngeina puan khak a silh hi.

records.english: Can I try on your shawl?
records.zomi: Na puan khuh ka silh en thei ding hiam?

records.english: The bride's beads belonged to her great-aunt.
records.zomi: Mo' khi te a pi neu' ahi hi.

records.english: Why do the older women in our family wear darker colours than the younger ones?
records.zomi: Bang hangin i innkuan-a numei upate in a neu zawte sangin dawng vom zaw a silh uh hiam?

records.english: My aunt worries that weaving will disappear when her generation is gone, so she teaches anyone who asks.
records.zomi: Ka ni in a suan a bei ciangin puan tah a mang ding hi, ci-in a lungkham ahih manin a dong kuapeuh a sinsak hi.

records.english: Who made your beautiful wrap skirt?
records.zomi: Na numei puan hoih kua in a bawl hiam?

records.english: My aunt wove it for me when I finished university.
records.zomi: University ka zawh ciangin ka ni in hong tah sak hi.

records.english: The patterns on my grandmother's shawl tell a story that only the oldest women in our family can fully read.
records.zomi: Ka pi' puan khuh tunga lim te in i innkuan-a numei upa pen te bek in a sim kim thei tangthu khat a gen hi.

records.english: My grandmother still weaves every evening.
records.zomi: Ka pi in nitak simin puan a tah lai hi.

records.english: My aunt is learning to weave.
records.zomi: Ka ni in puan tah a sin hi.

records.english: Grandma taught me to fold the skirt properly.
records.zomi: Pi in numei puan hoih taka kawi dan hong sinsak hi.

records.english: My uncle bought a new traditional jacket.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in ngeina puan khak thak khat a lei hi.

records.english: Traditional clothing connects my children to their grandparents' village, even though they have never lived there.
records.zomi: Ngeina puan in ka tate a teen ngei kei uh hangin a pu leh pi uh' khua tawh a kizopsak hi.

records.english: My grandfather wears a traditional hat on Sundays.
records.zomi: Ka pu in Nipini simin ngeina lukhu a khu hi.

records.english: Grandma made this bag on her loom.
records.zomi: Pi in hih ip a puan tahna tungah a bawl hi.

records.english: Mum washes the shawls by hand.
records.zomi: Nu in puan khuh te khut tawh a sil hi.

records.english: Is the old shawl too fragile to wear?
records.zomi: Puan khuh lui pen silh dingin a nem lua hiam?

records.english: My grandmother's wedding skirt took her mother almost a year to weave.
records.zomi: Ka pi' mopawi numei puan a nu in a tah ding kum khat dek a la hi.

records.english: Can you help me tie this skirt?
records.zomi: Hih numei puan khih dingin hong huh thei ding na hiam?

records.english: How did your family keep the old clothes in such good condition?
records.zomi: Na innkuan in puan lui te bangci-in a hoih taka a kem uh hiam?

records.english: My grandmother folded them in cloth and packed dried leaves between them to keep the insects away.
records.zomi: Ka pi in puan tawh a kawi a, ganhing neute a hong lut lohna dingin a kikal-ah lah keu a koih hi.

records.english: My mother keeps a skirt for each of her daughters to wear on their wedding days.
records.zomi: Ka nu in a tanu khatciat a mopawi ni-a a silh ding numei puan khat ciat a kem hi.

records.english: My uncle asked to be married in the jacket his father had worn as a young man.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in a pa a khangno lai-a a silh puan khak tawh a kiteen nopna a ngen hi.

records.english: My grandmother taught me which patterns are worn for celebrations and which are worn for mourning.
records.zomi: Ka pi in bang lim te lawmna-ah kisilh a, bang lim te dahna-ah kisilh hiam cih hong sinsak hi.

records.english: Before my sister's wedding, the women of our family spent a whole evening dressing her in traditional clothes.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam numei' mopawi ma-in i innkuan-a numeite in nitak bup ngeina puan a silhsak uh hi.

records.english: My grandmother tied the skirt, my mother arranged the shawl, and my aunt fixed the beads in her hair.
records.zomi: Ka pi in numei puan a khih a, ka nu in puan khuh a koih a, ka ni in a sam-ah khi te a koih hi.

records.english: When she stepped outside, the guests went quiet, and my father had tears in his eyes.
records.zomi: Pualam-ah a pai khiat ciangin mikhualte a dai uh a, ka pa' mit-ah khitui a om hi.

records.english: Hand-woven cloth is so valuable to my family that it is passed down like jewellery.
records.zomi: Khut tawh kitah puan i innkuan adingin a manpha mahmah ahih manin van manpha bangin a kipia zom hi.

records.english: When we moved abroad, my mother packed her best shawls before anything else.
records.zomi: Gamdang-ah i suan ciangin ka nu in na dang khempeuh ma-in a puan khuh hoih pen te a guan hi.

records.english: Should we buy machine-made cloth for the children, since they grow so quickly?
records.zomi: Naupangte a khang manlang mahmah ahih manin amaute adingin khawl tawh kibawl puan i lei ding hiam?

records.english: My grandmother repairs every tear in her shawls with tiny, careful stitches.
records.zomi: Ka pi in a puan khuh te tunga kitat khatciat khuina neu leh kician tawh a khui kik hi.

records.english: The children complain that the traditional clothes are heavy, but they look proud in the photos.
records.zomi: Naupangte in ngeina puan te a gik hi, ci-in a phun uh a, ahi zongin photo te-ah a kisaktheih uh hi.

records.english: Can I wear Grandma's shawl to the wedding?
records.zomi: Pi' puan khuh mopawi-ah ka silh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, but ask her first, because it's the one she wore to her own wedding.
records.zomi: Thei hi, ahi zongin a masa-in dong in, bang hang hiam cih leh amah' mopawi-ah a silh ahi hi.

records.english: My little sister loves wearing Grandma's beads.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam numei neu in Pi' khi te silh a deih mahmah hi.

records.english: Grandma keeps her best clothes in a chest.
records.zomi: Pi in a puan hoih pen te bawm lian khat sungah a kem hi.

records.english: Do you like the colours of this cloth?
records.zomi: Hih puan' dawng te na deih hiam?

records.english: My children feel a mixture of pride and embarrassment when they wear traditional clothes at school events.
records.zomi: Ka tate in sang thupiang te-ah ngeina puan a silh ciangin kisaktheihna leh maizumna a gawm in a kisa uh hi.

records.english: Dad ironed his shirt for the festival.
records.zomi: Paa in pawi adingin a puan khak a meiluk hi.

records.english: When my grandmother weaves, she is not only making cloth but also keeping our family's history alive.
records.zomi: Ka pi puan a tah ciangin puan bawl bek hi lo-in i innkuan' tangthu zong a nungta sak hi.

records.english: We took family photos in our traditional clothes.
records.zomi: I ngeina puan tawh innkuan photo te i la hi.

records.english: Why does Dad keep his old jacket in the wardrobe?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Paa in a puan khak lui puan bawm sungah a kem hiam?

records.english: His father gave it to him when he left the village, and he wears it only on special days.
records.zomi: Khua a nusiat ciangin a pa in a piak ahi a, ni tuam te-ah bek a silh hi.

records.english: My grandmother can tell which village a cloth comes from by looking at its pattern.
records.zomi: Ka pi in puan khat' lim en-in bang khua pan a hong pai hiam cih a thei thei hi.

records.english: Abroad, our traditional clothes have become a way of showing pride in where our family comes from.
records.zomi: Gamdang-ah i ngeina puan te i innkuan koi pan a hong pai hiam cih tawh kisai kisaktheihna lakna lampi khat a suak khin hi.

records.english: My mother believes that wearing traditional clothes at a wedding shows respect for both families.
records.zomi: Mopawi-ah ngeina puan silh in innkuan nih a zahtakna a lak hi, ci-in ka nu in a um hi.

records.english: Some young people in our family wear traditional clothes only for photos, which saddens the older relatives.
records.zomi: I innkuan-a khangno khenkhat in photo adingin bek ngeina puan a silh uh a, tua in sanggam upate a dahsak hi.

records.english: My mother wears her shawl to church.
records.zomi: Ka nu in pawlpi-ah a puan khuh a silh hi.

records.english: Choosing what to wear to a family celebration can cause arguments between the generations.
records.zomi: Innkuan lawmna khat-ah bang silh ding hiam cih teelna in suan te kikal-ah kinialna a piangsak thei hi.

records.english: My father wears his traditional shirt to every funeral as a sign of respect.
records.zomi: Ka pa in misi vuina khatciat-ah zahtakna lim dingin a ngeina puan khak a silh hi.

records.english: My sister added modern buttons to her traditional jacket, and the whole family argued about it.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam numei in a ngeina puan khak-ah tu hun-a kawl te a behlap a, innkuan bup in tua tawh kisai a kinial uh hi.

records.english: The children wear their festival clothes once a year.
records.zomi: Naupangte in kum khat-in khatvei a pawi puan uh a silh uh hi.

records.english: My aunt is teaching me to weave, but my first piece of cloth was full of mistakes.
records.zomi: Ka ni in puan tah hong sinsak a, ahi zongin ka puan masa pen khialhna tawh a dim hi.

records.english: My husband's family were delighted when I wore our traditional clothes to their celebration.
records.zomi: Ka pasal' innkuan in amau lawmna-ah i ngeina puan ka silh ciangin a lungdam mahmah uh hi.

records.english: Belief in a final judgement can motivate believers to work for justice, rather than leaving everything to the future.
records.zomi: Thukhenna nunung upna in um mite na khempeuh hong tung ding hun-ah nusia sangin thumanna adingin a sep nadingin a hanthawn thei hi.

records.english: My grandfather says he will leave the judging of his old enemies to God.
records.zomi: Ka pu in a galte lui thukhenna Pasian tungah ka nusia ding hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Christians are taught to forgive others, while trusting God to deal with justice.
records.zomi: Khazih mite midangte maisak dingin kisinsak a, thumanna tawh kisai-in Pasian a muang uh hi.

records.english: Will God judge people fairly?
records.zomi: Pasian in mite thumanna tawh thu a khen ding hiam?

records.english: Christians believe that God sees everything, including what people could not explain or hide.
records.zomi: Pasian in na khempeuh a mu a, mite in a gen thei loh uh leh a selsel thei loh uh te zong a mu hi, ci-in Khazih mite in a um uh hi.

records.english: Is God's mercy greater than his judgement?
records.zomi: Pasian' hehpihna in a thukhenna sangin a lian zaw hiam?

records.english: Christians pray for those who have done wrong.
records.zomi: Khazih mite in khialhna a bawl mite adingin thu a ngen uh hi.

records.english: My friend asked me if I'm afraid of judgement day.
records.zomi: Thukhenna ni ka lau hiam, ci-in ka lawm in hong dong hi.

records.english: Believers disagree about whether the final judgement leads to eternal punishment or to some other outcome.
records.zomi: Um mite in thukhenna nunung in tawntung gawtna-ah a tun ding hiam, ahih kei leh a dang khat-ah a tun ding hiam cih tawh kisai-in a kitup kei uh hi.

records.english: The idea of a final judgement raises hard questions, which many Christians admit they cannot fully answer.
records.zomi: Thukhenna nunung ngaihsutna in dotna haksa te a piangsak a, Khazih mite tampi in a kicing-in a dawng thei kei uh hi, ci-in a pulak uh hi.

records.english: For many believers, the final judgement is the moment when every hidden kindness will finally be seen.
records.zomi: Um mi tampi adingin thukhenna nunung pen kiselsel lungsim hoihna khempeuh a tawp-ah a kimuh ding hun ahi hi.

records.english: Will God remember everything we do?
records.zomi: Pasian in i sep khempeuh a phawk ding hiam?

records.english: Our pastor preached about judgement and mercy.
records.zomi: I pastor in thukhenna leh hehpihna tawh kisai thu a hilh hi.

records.english: Thinking about the final judgement encourages many Christians to live honestly now.
records.zomi: Thukhenna nunung ngaihsut in Khazih mite tampi tu-in thuman taka nungta dingin a hanthawn hi.

records.english: Theologians have long debated how God's perfect justice can be combined with his love for every person.
records.zomi: Pasian thu siamte in Pasian' thumanna kicing pen mi khatciat a itna tawh bangci-in a kigawm thei hiam cih hun sawt mahmah a kinial uh hi.

records.english: Some Christians emphasise that judgement is about setting the world right, not merely about punishment.
records.zomi: Khazih mite khenkhat in thukhenna pen gawtna bek hi lo-in leitung a dik sak thu ahi hi, ci-in a gen tam uh hi.

records.english: Does the Bible say that people will be judged by their actions?
records.zomi: Laisiangtho in mite a gamtatna uh bangin thukhenna a thuak ding uh hi, a ci hiam?

records.english: Is it wrong to judge other people?
records.zomi: Mi dangte thu khen pen a khial hiam?

records.english: Some people find the idea of judgement frightening because they remember things they are ashamed of.
records.zomi: Mi khenkhat in a maizumna uh na te a phawk uh manin thukhenna ngaihsutna a lauhuai sa uh hi.

records.english: Some Christians believe that every person will be given a final chance to respond to God.
records.zomi: Khazih mite khenkhat in mi khempeuh Pasian a dawng nadingin hun nunung khat kipia ding hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: God is a fair judge.
records.zomi: Pasian pen thukhenpa dik ahi hi.

records.english: Christian teaching holds together God's justice and his mercy, insisting that neither cancels the other.
records.zomi: Khazih mite' thuhilhna in Pasian' thumanna leh a hehpihna a len khawm a, khat in a dang a phiat kei hi, ci-in a ciptak hi.

records.english: God's judgement is different from human judgement.
records.zomi: Pasian' thukhenna in mihing' thukhenna tawh a kibang kei hi.

records.english: Why do some Christians find the idea of judgement comforting?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Khazih mite khenkhat in thukhenna ngaihsutna in a hehnep hiam?

records.english: Because it means that injustice and cruelty will not have the last word.
records.zomi: Bang hang hiam cih leh dik lohna leh hehna khualna in kammal nunung a nei kei ding hi, cih a cihna ahi hi.

records.english: Christians believe that judgement belongs to God, so they should be careful about condemning others.
records.zomi: Thukhenna pen Pasian' a hi hi, ci-in Khazih mite in a um uh ahih manin midangte mawhsak-ah a kidawm ding uh hi.

records.english: My pastor says that the cross shows both how seriously God takes sin and how far he goes to forgive.
records.zomi: Singlamteh in Pasian in mawhna bangzah thupi sa-in a ngaihsun hiam leh maisak dingin bangzah gamla a pai hiam cih a nih a lak hi, ci-in ka pastor in a gen hi.

records.english: Christians believe Jesus will judge the world.
records.zomi: Khazih mite in Jesu in leitung thu a khen ding hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: The Bible talks about the book of life.
records.zomi: Laisiangtho in nuntakna laibu tawh kisai thu a gen hi.

records.english: Jesus talked about the final judgement.
records.zomi: Jesu in thukhenna nunung tawh kisai thu a gen hi.

records.english: What do Christians mean by the final judgement?
records.zomi: Khazih mite in thukhenna nunung a cih uh ciangin bang a cihna uh hiam?

records.english: They believe that God will one day judge every person with perfect justice and truth.
records.zomi: Pasian in ni khat ni-in mi khempeuh thumanna kicing leh thuman tawh thu a khen ding hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: How can a God of love also be a judge?
records.zomi: Itna Pasian khat in bangci-in thukhenpa zong a hi thei ding hiam?

records.english: Does God forgive people who are sorry?
records.zomi: Pasian in a kisik mite a maisak hiam?

records.english: In one of his parables, Jesus described people being judged by how they treated the hungry and the sick.
records.zomi: A thugentehna khat sungah Jesu in mite a gilkial te leh a cina te a bawl dan uh bangin thukhenna a thuak uh hi, ci-in a gen hi.

records.english: Many churches teach that Christ himself, not any human authority, will be the final judge.
records.zomi: Pawlpi tampi in mihing ulian khatpeuh hi lo-in Khazih amah mah thukhenpa nunung ahi ding hi, ci-in a hilh uh hi.

records.english: Do all Christians agree about what happens at the final judgement?

records.zomi: Bang hangin nangma mah in na zum sangin van zuakna inn pan khau na lei kei hiam?

records.english: Because the colours we make from leaves and bark are the ones my mother used, and they last much longer.
records.zomi: Bang hang hiam cih leh lah leh sing hawng pan i bawl dawng te ka nu' zat te ahi a, sawt zaw mahmah-in a om hi.

records.english: My father's job is to wind the thread onto the wooden bobbins for my mother.
records.zomi: Ka pa' nasep pen ka nu adingin sing bawknang te-ah khau a kheel ahi hi.

records.english: My aunt weaves bags for the whole family.
records.zomi: Ka ni in innkuan bup adingin ip te a tah hi.

records.english: Is this pattern from your village, Grandma?
records.zomi: Pi, hih lim na khua pan ahi hiam?

records.english: When my mother weaves, she tells stories about the relatives who first wove the same patterns.
records.zomi: Ka nu puan a tah ciangin lim kibang te a tah masa sanggam te tawh kisai tangthu a gen hi.

records.english: Mum weaves every evening after dinner.
records.zomi: Nu in nitak an khit simin puan a tah hi.

records.english: Dad made a new frame for Mum's loom.
records.zomi: Paa in Nu' puan tahna adingin bawm thak khat a bawl hi.

records.english: My mother wove a blanket for each of her grandchildren before they were born.
records.zomi: Ka nu in a tu khatciat a pian ma-un puan sial khat ciat a tah hi.

records.english: The first cloth I wove is full of mistakes, but my mother still keeps it in her cupboard.
records.zomi: Ka tah masak puan khialhna tawh a dim a, ahi zongin ka nu in a puan bawm sungah a kem lai hi.

records.english: Can I help you set up the loom, Grandma?
records.zomi: Pi, puan tahna koih dingin kong huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, hold the threads straight while I tie them to the bar.
records.zomi: Thei hi, sing-ah ka khih laitakin khau te a tang-in len in.

records.english: My sister is weaving her first scarf.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam numei in a ngawng khih puan masa pen a tah hi.

records.english: My grandmother can weave without looking, because her hands remember every movement.
records.zomi: Ka pi in en lo-in puan a tah thei hi, bang hang hiam cih leh a khut te in sawlna khatciat a phawk hi.

records.english: The loom in our house has been repaired so many times that hardly any of the original wood remains.
records.zomi: I inn-a puan tahna vei tampi a kibawl kik ahih manin a lui sing a om nawn dek kei hi.

records.english: When the loom broke, my father carved a new piece from an old door frame.
records.zomi: Puan tahna a siat ciangin ka pa in kongkhak bawm lui khat pan a thak khat a ek hi.

records.english: Weaving connects the women in our family across four generations, even though we now live in different countries.
records.zomi: Tu-in gam tuamtuam-ah i teen hangin puan tah in suan li sung-a i innkuan-a numeite a kizopsak hi.

records.english: My grandmother counts the threads very carefully.
records.zomi: Ka pi in khau te kician mahmah-in a sim hi.

records.english: My aunt worries that her daughters will stop weaving once they have busy jobs in the city.
records.zomi: Ka ni in a tanute in khuapi-ah nasep buai a neih uh ciangin puan tah a khawl ding uh hi, ci-in a lungkham hi.

records.english: My grandmother's hands are slow now, but she still checks every piece of cloth that her granddaughters make.
records.zomi: Ka pi' khut te tu-in a zawl khin a, ahi zongin a tu numeite' bawl puan khatciat a en lai hi.

records.english: My grandmother weaves on the veranda.
records.zomi: Ka pi in inn mai tual-ah puan a tah hi.

records.english: Grandma's loom is older than my father.
records.zomi: Pi' puan tahna in ka pa sangin a upa zaw hi.

records.english: My aunt sells her cloth at the market.
records.zomi: Ka ni in a puan te sumbuk mun-ah a zuak hi.

records.english: How long does it take you to weave a shawl?
records.zomi: Puan khuh khat tah dingin hun bangzah na la hiam?

records.english: About three weeks, if I weave for a few hours every evening.
records.zomi: Kal thum bang, nitak simin nai tawm khat ka tah leh.

records.english: Keeping the family's weaving tradition alive means teaching both sons and daughters, my mother says.
records.zomi: Innkuan' puan tah ngeina a nungta lai nadingin tapa leh tanu a nih sinsak ding hi, ka nu in a ci hi.

records.english: Is it true that Great-Grandma wove the cloth for her own wedding?
records.zomi: Pi upa in amah' mopawi adinga puan amah mah in a tah hi, cih a man hiam?

records.english: My mother started teaching me to weave the summer I turned twelve.
records.zomi: Ka kum sawm le nih cin khal hun-in ka nu in puan tah hong sinsak pan hi.

records.english: Our family's loom stays in the back room.
records.zomi: I innkuan' puan tahna nung lam inndan-ah a om hi.

records.english: My little brother wants to learn to weave too.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam pasal neu in zong puan tah a sin nop hi.

records.english: When my mother was ill one winter, she couldn't finish the shawl she was weaving for my sister's wedding.
records.zomi: Khuaphal khat-in ka nu a cina ciangin ka sanggam numei' mopawi adingin a tah laitak puan khuh a zo thei kei hi.

records.english: My aunt and I sat at the loom every night for two weeks, trying to copy her pattern exactly.
records.zomi: Ka ni leh kei kal nih sung zan simin puan tahna-ah i tu a, a lim a kician taka pal dingin i hanciam hi.

records.english: On the wedding day, my mother looked at the shawl and said she couldn't tell where her work ended and ours began.
records.zomi: Mopawi ni-in ka nu in puan khuh a en a, a nasep koi-ah a bei a, ei' nasep koi-ah a kipan hiam cih a thei thei kei hi, a ci hi.

records.english: We dyed the thread together in big pots in the yard, and our hands were blue for a week.
records.zomi: Inn tual-ah beel lian te sungah khau te i kikhawm-in i zum a, kal khat sung i khut te a dum hi.

records.english: The children like watching Grandma weave.
records.zomi: Naupangte in Pi' puan tah a en a deih uh hi.

records.english: My grandmother unpicked a whole row of my weaving because one thread was too loose.
records.zomi: Khau khat a khau lua ahih manin ka pi in ka puan tah tang bup a phel kik hi.

records.english: My mother wove the cloth for my school bag.
records.zomi: Ka nu in ka sang ip adinga puan a tah hi.

records.english: Why does your cloth have a red stripe in the middle?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na puan in a lai-ah tang san khat a nei hiam?

records.english: Every woman in our family puts that stripe in her first piece, so that we remember who taught us.
records.zomi: I innkuan-a numei khatciat in a puan masa pen-ah tua tang a koih uh hi, kua in hong sinsak hiam cih i phawk nadingin.

records.english: Please don't touch the threads on the loom.
records.zomi: Kong ngen hi, puan tahna tunga khau te khoih kei in.

records.english: Who taught Mum how to weave?
records.zomi: Nu puan tah dan kua in a sinsak hiam?

records.english: Her grandmother taught her when she was about ten years old.
records.zomi: A kum sawm bang a hih lai-in a pi in a sinsak hi.

records.english: My cousin dyed the thread dark blue.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam in khau te dum vom-in a zum hi.

records.english: Learning to weave from my grandmother taught me patience as well as a craft.
records.zomi: Ka pi pan puan tah sin in siamna khat bang mahin thuakzawhna zong hong sinsak hi.

records.english: Grandma says my rows are getting straighter.
records.zomi: Ka tang te a tang semsem hi, Pi in a ci hi.

records.english: Can I keep the leftover thread?
records.zomi: Khau tam lai te ka kem thei ding hiam?

records.english: Christians at funerals often speak about the hope of meeting their loved ones again.
records.zomi: Misi vuina-ah Khazih mite in a it mite uh a kimuh kik ding lametna thu a gen zel uh hi.

records.english: Will there be sadness in heaven?
records.zomi: Vantung-ah dahna a om ding hiam?

records.english: For many believers, the joys of heaven will include the restoration of everything good in this life.
records.zomi: Um mi tampi adingin vantung' lungdamna in hih nuntakna sung-a na hoih khempeuh a kicing kikna zong a huam ding hi.

records.english: Belief in a new creation encourages many Christians to work for justice and to care for the earth now.
records.zomi: Bawlsa thak upna in Khazih mite tampi tu-in thumanna adingin sem dingin leh leitung kem dingin a hanthawn hi.

records.english: My aunt finds comfort in the hope of heaven.
records.zomi: Ka ni in vantung lametna-ah hehnepna a mu hi.

records.english: Some theologians argue that popular pictures of heaven owe more to art than to the Bible.
records.zomi: Pasian thu siam khenkhat in vantung tawh kisai mite' ngaihsutna lim te Laisiangtho sangin lim gelhna pan a hong pai zaw hi, ci-in a gen uh hi.

records.english: Christians believe that in the new creation there will be no more hunger, injustice or war.
records.zomi: Bawlsa thak sungah gilkialna, dik lohna leh galdona a om nawn kei ding hi, ci-in Khazih mite in a um uh hi.

records.english: At our house group, someone asked whether we will recognise each other in heaven.
records.zomi: I inn pawl kikhopna-ah mi khat in vantung-ah i kithei kik ding hiam, ci-in a dong hi.

records.english: Christians believe heaven is a place of peace.
records.zomi: Vantung pen lungnopna mun ahi hi, ci-in Khazih mite in a um uh hi.

records.english: Is heaven up in the sky?
records.zomi: Vantung pen van tung lam-ah a om hiam?

records.english: Most Christians don't think of it as a place in the sky, but as being in God's presence.
records.zomi: Khazih mite a tamzaw in van tung-a mun khat bangin ngaihsun lo-in Pasian' ma-a om bangin a ngaihsun uh hi.

records.english: What do Christians believe about heaven?
records.zomi: Vantung tawh kisai-in Khazih mite in bang a um uh hiam?

records.english: They believe it is being with God, where there is no more pain, sorrow or death.
records.zomi: Natna, dahna leh sihna a om nawn lohna mun Pasian tawh om ahi hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: The image of God wiping away every tear has comforted grieving Christians for centuries.
records.zomi: Pasian in khitui khempeuh a nul siang lim in kum zalom tampi sung a dah Khazih mite a hehnep hi.

records.english: Why do some Christians say that heaven is not the end of the story?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Khazih mite khenkhat in vantung pen tangthu tawpna hi lo hi, a ci uh hiam?

records.english: Because they believe God's final plan is a renewed heaven and earth, where people live with resurrected bodies.
records.zomi: Bang hang hiam cih leh Pasian' ngimna nunung pen mite thokik pumpi tawh a teenna van thak leh lei thak ahi hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: How can Christians talk about heaven with children without making it sound frightening?
records.zomi: Khazih mite in naupangte tawh vantung thu lauhuai bang a kilang lo-in bangci-in a kihoupih thei uh hiam?

records.english: What will people do in heaven?
records.zomi: Vantung-ah mite in bang a bawl ding uh hiam?

records.english: My grandfather was not afraid of dying.
records.zomi: Ka pu in sih a lau kei hi.

records.english: Christians hope for a world without pain.
records.zomi: Khazih mite in natna om lo leitung khat a lamen uh hi.

records.english: Christians believe God will live with his people.
records.zomi: Pasian in a mite tawh a om khawm ding hi, ci-in Khazih mite in a um uh hi.

records.english: For many believers, heaven is above all a relationship with God rather than a place with clouds and harps.
records.zomi: Um mi tampi adingin vantung pen meii leh khuang tum mun khat sangin Pasian tawh kizopna ahi zaw hi.

records.english: We sang a song about heaven in church.
records.zomi: Pawlpi-ah vantung tawh kisai la khat i sa hi.

records.english: The prophet Isaiah described a time when the wolf and the lamb would live together in peace.
records.zomi: Kamsangpa Isaia in ngalhia leh tuuno lungnopna tawh a om khawm ding hun khat a gen hi.

records.english: Is it wrong to feel afraid of death if you believe in heaven?
records.zomi: Vantung na um leh sihna na lau pen a khial hiam?

records.english: Christians believe death is not the end.
records.zomi: Sihna pen tawpna hi lo hi, ci-in Khazih mite in a um uh hi.

records.english: Our Sunday school drew pictures of the new creation.
records.zomi: I Nipini sang in bawlsa thak lim te a gelh uh hi.

records.english: Christians pray, "Your kingdom come."
records.zomi: Khazih mite in, "Na Gam hong piang ta hen" ci-in thu a ngen uh hi.

records.english: Will heaven ever feel boring?
records.zomi: Vantung in a lung neksak ngei ding hiam?

records.english: When my grandfather was dying, he asked us to read the passage about God wiping away every tear.
records.zomi: Ka pu a sih kuan ciangin Pasian in khitui khempeuh a nul siang thu a gen mun sim dingin hong ngen hi.

records.english: He said that he wasn't afraid, because he believed he was going home to God.
records.zomi: Pasian kiangah inn-ah ka ciah ding hi, ci-in a um manin a lau kei hi, a ci hi.

records.english: At his funeral, the pastor read the same passage, and my grandmother held my hand very tightly.
records.zomi: A misi vuina-ah pastor in tua mun mah a sim a, ka pi in ka khut a len khauh mahmah hi.

records.english: The promise of a new creation gives believers a reason to hope even when the present world seems broken.
records.zomi: Bawlsa thak kamciamna in tu-a leitung a kitam bang a kilat ciangin zong um mite lametna nading hangsan a pia hi.

records.english: When Christians talk about the new creation, what are they hoping for?
records.zomi: Khazih mite in bawlsa thak thu a gen uh ciangin bang a lamen uh hiam?

records.english: They believe that God will one day renew the whole world and set everything right.
records.zomi: Pasian in ni khat ni-in leitung bup a thaksak a, na khempeuh a dik sak ding hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: My little sister asked me what heaven looks like.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam numei neu in vantung bangci-in a kilang hiam, ci-in hong dong hi.

records.english: Some believers think of heaven as rest, while others imagine it full of joyful work and worship.
records.zomi: Um mi khenkhat in vantung pen tawlngakna bangin a ngaihsun uh a, a dangte in lungdam huai nasep leh biakna tawh a dim bangin a ngaihsun uh hi.

records.english: The Bible says there will be no more tears.
records.zomi: Laisiangtho in khitui a om nawn kei ding hi, a ci hi.

records.english: When Christians pray for God's kingdom to come, they are expressing hope for a world made new.
records.zomi: Khazih mite in Pasian Gam hong piang dingin thu a ngen uh ciangin a thakin kibawl leitung khat adingin lametna a gen uh hi.

records.english: Near the end of the Bible, John sees a holy city where God lives among his people.
records.zomi: Laisiangtho' tawp lam-ah Johan in Pasian a mite lak-ah a teenna khuapi siangtho khat a mu hi.

records.english: Do Christians believe animals go to heaven?
records.zomi: Ganhing te vantung-ah a pai uh hi, ci-in Khazih mite in a um uh hiam?

records.english: Can children understand what heaven means?
records.zomi: Naupangte in vantung in bang a cihna hiam cih a theisiam thei uh hiam?

records.english: In the view of many Christians, the new creation will be this world healed, not replaced by something else.
records.zomi: Khazih mite tampi' ngaihsutna-ah bawlsa thak pen na dang khat tawh khek hi lo-in hih leitung a dam kik ahi ding hi.

records.english: Jesus promised to prepare a place for his followers.
records.zomi: Jesu in a nungzuite adingin mun khat bawlkhol dingin a ciam hi.

records.english: Paul wrote that the whole of creation is waiting to be set free from decay.
records.zomi: Paul in a kibawlsa na khempeuh kisiatna pan kikhah-khia dingin a ngak hi, ci-in a gelh hi.

records.english: Will we see Grandma again in heaven?
records.zomi: Vantung-ah Pi i mu kik ding hiam?

records.english: Many Christians hope so, because they believe that God brings his people together again.
records.zomi: Khazih mite tampi in tua bangin a lamen uh hi, bang hang hiam cih leh Pasian in a mite a kikhawmsak kik hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: Why do some hymns describe heaven as a city with streets of gold?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pasian phatna la khenkhat in vantung pen kham lampi nei khuapi khat bangin a gen hiam?

records.english: Christian hope looks forward not only to life after death but to the renewal of the whole creation.
records.zomi: Khazih mite' lametna in sih khit nung nuntakna bek hi lo-in kibawlsa na khempeuh' thakna zong a lamen hi.

records.english: Our pastor preached about the new creation.
records.zomi: I pastor in bawlsa thak tawh kisai thu a hilh hi.

records.english: The hope of heaven helped my grandmother face her illness with calm and courage.
records.zomi: Vantung lametna in ka pi a natna lungmuanna leh hangsanna tawh a maituah nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: The Bible describes a new heaven and a new earth.
records.zomi: Laisiangtho in van thak leh lei thak a gen hi.

records.english: Many Christians believe that heaven is a gift from God, not a reward that people earn.
records.zomi: Khazih mite tampi in vantung pen mite in a sem-in a ngah letsong hi lo-in Pasian pan letsong ahi hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: Christians disagree about many details of heaven, but most share the hope that death does not have the final word.
records.zomi: Khazih mite vantung' a neu tampi tawh kisai-in a kitup kei uh a, ahi zongin a tamzaw in sihna in kammal nunung a nei kei hi, cih lametna a kikhen pih uh hi.

records.english: My pastor says that hope for the new creation should make us care more for this world, not less.
records.zomi: Bawlsa thak lametna in hih leitung i kem tawm zaw lo-in i kem tam zaw ding hi, ci-in ka pastor in a gen hi.

records.english: Christians believe God will make all things new.
records.zomi: Pasian in na khempeuh a thakin a bawl ding hi, ci-in Khazih mite in a um uh hi.

records.english: Christians believe that Jesus' resurrection is the first sign of the new creation.
records.zomi: Jesu' thawhkikna pen bawlsa thak' lim masa pen ahi hi, ci-in Khazih mite in a um uh hi.

records.english: Speaking honestly about heaven at a funeral requires both confidence in God's promises and humility about the details.
records.zomi: Misi vuina-ah vantung tawh kisai thuman taka gen in Pasian' kamciamna te tungah muanna leh a neu te tawh kisai kiniamkhiatna a nih a kisam hi.

records.english: Some Christians admit that they don't know what heaven will be like, but they trust God's promises.
records.zomi: Khazih mite khenkhat in vantung bangci-in a om ding hiam cih ka thei kei hi, ci-in a pulak uh a, ahi zongin Pasian' kamciamna te a muang uh hi.

records.english: My friend believes her father is with God now.
records.zomi: Ka lawm in a pa tu-in Pasian tawh a om hi, ci-in a um hi.

records.english: So how long did the drive take?
records.zomi: Tua ahih leh mawtaw tawi in hun bangzah a la hiam?

records.english: You finished the marathon, but how did your knees feel the next day?
records.zomi: Marathon na zo hi, ahi zongin a zingciang-in na khuk te bangci-in a kisa hiam?

records.english: Stiff for two days, but nothing a few slow walks didn't fix.
records.zomi: Ni nih sung a khauh hi, ahi zongin zawl taka pai-in kal tawm khat in a dam sak lo bangmah om lo hi.

records.english: You said the new recipe was a disaster, so what would you change next time?
records.zomi: Huan dan thak buaina khat ahi hi, na ci a, tua ahih leh a zom vei-in bang na khek ding hiam?

records.english: You mentioned you're learning the guitar, so which songs can you play now?
records.zomi: Guitar na sin hi, na ci a, tua ahih leh tu-in bang la te na tum thei hiam?

records.english: Did the shop agree to exchange the jacket after you showed them the receipt?
records.zomi: Man lai na lak khit ciangin van zuakna inn in puan khak a khek dingin a kipsak hiam?

records.english: So after your first fishing trip, did you catch anything at all?
records.zomi: Tua ahih leh na nga mat masa pen khit ciangin na mat ngei hiam?

records.english: Did you find your lost ring?
records.zomi: Na zungbuh mangthang na mu hiam?

records.english: So after all that training, would you enter the race again next year?
records.zomi: Tua ahih leh tua kisinna khempeuh khit ciangin kum zom-in lehdona-ah na kihel kik ding hiam?

records.english: Did the new shoes stop hurting?
records.zomi: Khedap thak te in hong natsak nawn kei hiam?

records.english: And did the cake rise in the end?
records.zomi: A tawp-ah cake a kho hiam?

records.english: Did your tomatoes ever turn red?
records.zomi: Na mehtuuk te a san ngei hiam?

records.english: So what time did you get home?
records.zomi: Tua ahih leh bang hun-in inn-ah na tung hiam?

records.english: And what did the mechanic find?
records.zomi: Mawtaw bawlpa in bang a mu hiam?

records.english: When a story ends too quickly, a gentle follow-up often brings out the most interesting details.
records.zomi: Tangthu khat a manlang lua-in a bei ciangin dotna zom nem khat in a neu lungdam huai pen te a gen khiasak zel hi.

records.english: Did your sister like the present?
records.zomi: Na sanggam numei in letsong a deih hiam?

records.english: You mentioned your grandmother's garden; what does she grow there now?
records.zomi: Na pi' huan thu na gen hi; tu-in tua mun-ah bang a suan hiam?

records.english: Asking about the outcome of someone's adventure makes them feel that the adventure mattered.
records.zomi: Mi khat' khualzinna lamdang a tawpna dot in tua khualzinna a thupi hi, cih a kisaksak hi.

records.english: So did your team finish the race?
records.zomi: Tua ahih leh na pawl in lehdona a zo hiam?

records.english: A friend who asks how your new hobby is going can give you the encouragement to keep at it.
records.zomi: Na lungnopna thak bangci-in a pai hiam cih a dot lawm khat in na sep zom nadingin hanthawnna hong pia thei hi.

records.english: When you say the beach was crowded, do you mean you couldn't find a space?
records.zomi: Tuipi kiang-ah mi a tam hi, na cih ciangin mun khat na mu zo kei hi, na cihna hiam?

records.english: Did the plant survive the winter?
records.zomi: Kung in khuaphal a pelh zo hiam?

records.english: And did the rain stop in the end?
records.zomi: A tawp-ah vuah a khawl hiam?

records.english: You told me you'd bought a second-hand car, so has it been reliable?
records.zomi: Mawtaw lui khat na lei hi, na ci a, tua ahih leh a muan huai hiam?

records.english: So far, yes, apart from a flat battery on the first cold morning.
records.zomi: Tu dong a muan huai hi, khua vot zingsang masa pen-a battery a bei loh buang.

records.english: People enjoy talking about their hobbies, especially when a listener asks for more detail.
records.zomi: Mite in a lungnopna uh tawh kisai thu gen a deih uh a, a diakin a ngai mi in a neu behlap a dot ciangin.

records.english: So did you pass your driving test?
records.zomi: Tua ahih leh na mawtaw tawi sitna na zo hiam?

records.english: Did you enjoy the second half of the book?
records.zomi: Laibu' a nunung langkhat na deih hiam?

records.english: Good listeners ask what happened next, rather than rushing to tell their own story.
records.zomi: Ngai siam mite in amau tangthu gen dingin a manlang sangin a zom bang a piang hiam cih a dong uh hi.

records.english: And did the cat come home?
records.zomi: Zawhngeu inn-ah a hong ciah hiam?

records.english: You mentioned that the campsite was noisy, so did you move to another one?
records.zomi: Puanin kipna mun a ging tam hi, na ci a, tua ahih leh mun dang khat-ah na suan hiam?

records.english: A follow-up question at the right moment can turn small talk into a real conversation.
records.zomi: Hun kilawm-a dotna zom khat in kiho lel pen kihoupihna taktak khat-ah a khek thei hi.

records.english: You said the flight was delayed, so did you miss your connection?
