records.zomi: Nipini-in gamdang-a i innkuanpihte phone tawh i sam ding hiam?

records.english: Why did your parents move here?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na nu leh na pa hih mun-ah a pem uh hiam?

records.english: My parents sent part of every pay packet back home to help my grandparents build a new roof.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in ka pu leh ka pi te in inntung thak a lam nadingin a khasum ngah khatciat a khen khat inn-ah a khak uh hi.

records.english: My father sends money home every month.
records.zomi: Ka pa in kha simin inn-ah sum a khak hi.

records.english: Does our church help new arrivals?
records.zomi: I pawlpi in mi thak hong tung te a huh hiam?

records.english: In my family, those who moved first always felt responsible for helping those who came after them.
records.zomi: Ka innkuan sungah a masa-a pem mite in a nung-a hong pai te huh ding mawhpuakna a nei uh hi, ci-in a kizak den uh hi.

records.english: My mother cried when she saw snow for the first time in our new country.
records.zomi: I gam thak-ah vuk a muh masak pen ciangin ka nu a kap hi.

records.english: Migration has spread my family across the world, yet our shared stories keep us connected.
records.zomi: Gam pemna in ka innkuan leitung bup-ah a zeel sak hi, ahi zongin i kikhawm tangthu te in i kizom den hi.

records.english: Grandpa still talks about the day he left home.
records.zomi: Pu in inn a nusiat ni tawh kisai a gen lai hi.

records.english: Children who grow up far from their grandparents' village often feel both proud of it and distant from it.
records.zomi: A pu leh a pi te' khua pan gamla takah a khang naupangte in tua khua a kisapphatna leh a gamla bangin a kizak khawm uh hi.

records.english: My grandfather says that each family that moved away took a piece of the village with them.
records.zomi: A pem innkuan khatciat in khua' a khenkhat a paipih uh hi, ci-in ka pu in a gen hi.

records.english: Will we ever live in Grandpa's village?
records.zomi: Pu' khua-ah i teng ngei ding hiam?

records.english: Maybe one day, but for now our home and our jobs are here in the city.
records.zomi: Ni khat-ah a hi thei hi, ahi zongin tu-in i inn leh i nasep te khuapi sungah a om hi.

records.english: My grandmother worries that her great-grandchildren will forget where the family came from.
records.zomi: A tu' tate in innkuan a hong pai panna mun a mangngilh ding uh hi, ci-in ka pi in a lungkham hi.

records.english: Our children speak our language at home but use another language with their friends.
records.zomi: I tate in inn-ah i pau a zang uh a, a lawmte uh tawh pau dang a zang uh hi.

records.english: When my uncle moved abroad, the whole family gathered to pray for him before he left.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu gamdang-ah a pem ciangin a pai ma-in innkuan bup a kikhawm-in amah adingin thu a ngen uh hi.

records.english: My little brother was born after we moved.
records.zomi: Ka sanggampa neu pen i pem khit ciangin a suak hi.

records.english: Did your cousin find a job in the city?
records.zomi: Na sanggam in khuapi-ah nasep a mu hiam?

records.english: Did Grandma travel here by plane?
records.zomi: Pi in vanleng tawh hih mun-ah a hong hiam?

records.english: My grandparents stayed in the village, while all six of their children moved to different towns.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh ka pi te khua-ah a om uh a, a tate guk khempeuh khuapi tuamtuam-ah a pem uh hi.

records.english: My father worked nights in a restaurant for years so that we could join him here.
records.zomi: Hih mun-ah amah tawh i om khawm thei nadingin ka pa in kum tampi sung an ne inn khat-ah zan-in a sem hi.

records.english: Every family gathering abroad includes a moment when someone speaks about the relatives who stayed behind.
records.zomi: Gamdang-a innkuan kikhopna khempeuh-ah mi khat in a om lai innkuanpihte tawh kisai a genna hun khat a om zel hi.

records.english: When my father finally got his residence papers, he flew home to show his parents.
records.zomi: A tawp-ah ka pa in a tenna phalna laigelh te a ngah ciangin a nu leh a pa lak dingin inn-ah vanleng tawh a ciah hi.

records.english: Do you ever regret leaving the village, Grandma?
records.zomi: Pi aw, khua na nusiat na kisik ngei hiam?

records.english: Sometimes I miss the hills, but I'm grateful that my children and grandchildren have had chances I never had.
records.zomi: Pawlkhat vei-in mual te ka ngaih hi, ahi zongin ka tate leh ka tu te in ka ngah ngei loh theihna te a ngah uh ahih manin ka lungdam hi.

records.english: For my family, home is no longer a single place but a network of people in many countries.
records.zomi: Ka innkuan adingin inn pen mun khat bek hi nawn lo-in gam tampi-a mite' kizopna khat ahi hi.

records.english: My aunt keeps a list of every relative who has moved away, with their addresses and birthdays.
records.zomi: Ka ni in a pem innkuanpih khempeuh' lista, a tenna mun leh a piancilni te tawh, a kem hi.

records.english: We send photos to our cousins overseas.
records.zomi: Gamdang-a i sanggam te kiangah lim te i khak hi.

records.english: Why do my parents still call the village home after living in the city for twenty years?
records.zomi: Bang hangin ka nu leh ka pa khuapi-ah kum sawmnih sung a om khit hangin khua pen a inn uh a ci lai uh hiam?

records.english: How did your family manage when you first arrived in this country?
records.zomi: Hih gam-ah na tun masak lai-in na innkuan uh bangci a om uh hiam?

records.english: My cousins let us stay in their flat until my father found work.
records.zomi: Ka pa in nasep a muh mateng ka sanggam te in a inn uh-ah hong om sak uh hi.

records.english: My brother returned to the village after ten years abroad and opened a small shop.
records.zomi: Ka sanggampa gamdang-ah kum sawm a om khit ciangin khua-ah a ciah kik a, van zuakna inn neu khat a hong hi.

records.english: My parents keep photos of the old house.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in inn lui' lim te a kem uh hi.

records.english: My uncle helped us find our first flat.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in i inn masa pen i muh nadingin hong huh hi.

records.english: The money sent home by relatives abroad has changed my grandparents' village in ways they never expected.
records.zomi: Gamdang-a innkuanpihte in a khak sum in ka pu leh ka pi te' khua a lamen ngei loh dan-in a khek hi.

records.english: We still speak our language at home.
records.zomi: Inn-ah i pau i zang lai hi.

records.english: Was Grandpa sad when his sons left?
records.zomi: A tapa te a pai ciangin Pu a dah hiam?

records.english: My cousin helped two young men from our village find jobs and rooms when they arrived.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam in i khua pan pasal khangno nih a tun ciangin nasep leh inndan a muh nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: When my grandmother visited us abroad, she couldn't believe how different our lives had become.
records.zomi: Ka pi in gamdang-ah hong kan ciangin i nuntakna a kikhek dan a um thei kei hi.

records.english: Our family moved twice before I was ten.
records.zomi: Kum sawm ka phak ma-in i innkuan nihvei a pem hi.

records.english: My cousins abroad learned to cook our traditional dishes from videos my mother sent them.
records.zomi: Gamdang-a ka sanggam te in ka nu' a khak video te pan i ngeina an huan dan a sin uh hi.

records.english: My mother learned a new language at forty.
records.zomi: Ka nu in kum sawmli-in pau thak khat a sin hi.

records.english: My father says that migration taught him to value his community more than he ever did at home.
records.zomi: Gam pemna in inn-a a om lai sangin a khuasung a manpha sak zaw dingin a hilh hi, ci-in ka pa in a gen hi.

records.english: My cousins and I want to record our parents' stories of migration before the details are lost.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam te leh kei in a neuneu te a mang ma-in i nu leh i pa te' gam pemna tangthu te ciamteh i nuam hi.

records.english: Does Mum miss her sisters in the village?
records.zomi: Nu in khua-a a sanggamnu te a ngaih hiam?

records.english: Why did Uncle Mang move so far away?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pa Neu Mang a gamla mahmah-ah a pem hiam?

records.english: He found a job at a factory there, and he sends money home every month.
records.zomi: Tua mun-ah sepna inn khat-ah nasep a mu a, kha simin inn-ah sum a khak hi.

records.english: Grandma sends us dried fish from home.
records.zomi: Pi in inn pan nga keu hong khak hi.

records.english: Our family has relatives on three continents, but we still meet online for every festival.
records.zomi: I innkuan in gam lian thum-ah innkuanpihte a nei a, ahi zongin pawi khempeuh-ah online-ah i kimu lai hi.

records.english: Our community in the city welcomes every new family with a meal and a list of useful contacts.
records.zomi: Khuapi-a i khuasung in innkuan thak khempeuh an khat leh a huh huai mite' phone nambat lista tawh a muak hi.

records.english: My parents believe that leaving home was the hardest and the best decision they ever made.
records.zomi: Inn nusiat pen a thukhensatna uh lakah a haksa pen leh a hoih pen ahi hi, ci-in ka nu leh ka pa in a um uh hi.

records.english: Is Auntie happy living so far away?
records.zomi: Ni in gamla mahmah-ah a om in a lungdam hiam?

records.english: My cousin married a girl from our community abroad.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam in gamdang-a i khuasung pan numei khat a ten hi.

records.english: When will we visit the village again?
records.zomi: Khua ciang-in i kan kik ding hiam?

records.english: Why do so many of our relatives live in the same part of the city?
records.zomi: Bang hangin i innkuanpih tampi khuapi' mun kibang-ah a teng uh hiam?

records.english: The first families helped the ones who came later, so everyone settled close together.
records.zomi: Innkuan masa te in a nung-a hong pai te a huh uh ahih manin mi khempeuh a kinai takin a teng uh hi.

records.english: My aunt came back to the village to retire.
records.zomi: Ka ni in nasep tawp ciangin om dingin khua-ah a ciah kik hi.

records.english: When my father left for work abroad, I was only six, and I didn't understand why he had to go.
records.zomi: Ka pa gamdang-ah nasep dingin a pai ciangin kum guk bek ka pha a, bang hangin a pai ding a kisam hiam cih ka theisiam kei hi.

records.english: Every month, a letter came with a little money and a drawing he had made for me on the back.
records.zomi: Kha simin sum tawmno leh a nung lam-ah kei adingin a gelh lim khat tawh lai khat a hong tung hi.

records.english: Years later, when our whole family joined him, I found every one of those letters kept safely in a box under his bed.
records.zomi: Kum tampi khit ciangin i innkuan bup amah tawh i om khawm ciangin tua lai khempeuh a lupna nuai-a bawm khat sungah bit takin a kikem hi, cih ka mu hi.

records.english: Christians pray because they believe God hears them.
records.zomi: Khazih mite in Pasian in a za hi, ci-in a um uh ahih manin thu a ngen uh hi.

records.english: God's ways often seem mysterious, yet many believers trust that his purposes are good.
records.zomi: Pasian' lampi te a thuk bangin a kilang zel hi, ahi zongin upmi tampi in a ngimna te a hoih hi, ci-in a muang uh hi.

records.english: In our family, the hope that God holds the future has turned many anxious evenings into times of prayer.
records.zomi: I innkuan sungah Pasian in hun hong tung ding a len hi, cih lamenna in lungkham nitak tampi thungetna hun-ah a khek hi.

records.english: My mother finds it comforting that God sees the whole of our lives at once, from beginning to end.
records.zomi: Pasian in i nuntakna bup, a kipatna pan a tawp dong, khat vei-in a mu hi, cih in ka nu a hehnep hi.

records.english: Mum, is God in charge of everything?
records.zomi: Nu aw, Pasian in na khempeuh a uk hiam?

records.english: Christians believe God rules over all things, even when the world seems out of control.
records.zomi: Khazih mite in leitung a ukzawh lo bangin a kilang ciangin zong Pasian in na khempeuh a uk hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: Why does Grandma say our times are in God's hands?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pi in i hun te Pasian' khut sungah a om hi, a ci hiam?

records.english: She means that she trusts God with every part of her life, including the future.
records.zomi: Hun hong tung ding kihel-in a nuntakna khen khempeuh Pasian a muang hi, cihna ahi hi.

records.english: Theologians have long discussed how an eternal God relates to a world that moves through time.
records.zomi: Pasian thu siamte in Pasian tawntung in hun sung-a pai leitung tawh bangci a kizom hiam cih sawt tak a kikup uh hi.

records.english: Does God control the weather?
records.zomi: Pasian in khuamun a uk hiam?

records.english: Christian teaching holds that God's sovereignty is always joined to his goodness, so his rule can be trusted.
records.zomi: Khazih thuhilhna in Pasian' thuneihna pen a hoihna tawh a kigawm den a, tua ahih manin a ukna a kimuang thei hi, ci-in a gen hi.

records.english: When our family's business failed, my father sat us all down at the kitchen table.
records.zomi: I innkuan' sumbawlna a puk ciangin ka pa in an ne dohkan kiangah kote khempeuh hong tusak hi.

records.english: He told us honestly that money would be tight, but that he trusted God was still in charge of our lives.
records.zomi: Sum a haksa ding hi, ci-in thuman takin hong gen a, ahi zongin Pasian in i nuntakna a uk lai hi, ci-in a muang hi.

records.english: Looking back, I believe his calm faith during that year taught us more than any lesson about money could have.
records.zomi: Ka en kik ciangin tua kum sungah a upna dai in sum tawh kisai sinna khempeuh sangin tam zaw hong hilh hi, ci-in ka um hi.

records.english: My little brother asked whether God gets bored, since he has lived forever.
records.zomi: Ka sanggampa neu in Pasian a tawntungin a nungta ahih manin a lungkia ngei hiam, ci-in a dong hi.

records.english: Why do some believers feel peaceful about death because they believe God is eternal?
records.zomi: Bang hangin upmi khenkhat in Pasian a tawntung hi, ci-in a um uh ahih manin sihna tawh kisai a lungmuang uh hiam?

records.english: Our Bible study discussed how Joseph saw God's purpose even in his brothers' cruelty.
records.zomi: I Laisiangtho sinna in Josef in a sanggampa te' hehpih lohna sungah zong Pasian' ngimna a muh dan a kikup hi.

records.english: My father taught us that God's eternity means his love for us will never run out.
records.zomi: Pasian' tawntung hihna in eite hong itna a bei ngei lo ding cihna ahi hi, ci-in ka pa in hong hilh hi.

records.english: How can believing that God is eternal help our family when Grandpa is so ill?
records.zomi: Pu a cina mahmah laitakin Pasian a tawntung hi, cih upna in i innkuan bangci a huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Many Christians find comfort in knowing that God, who has no beginning or end, holds Grandpa's life beyond this world too.
records.zomi: Khazih mite tampi in kipatna leh tawpna nei lo Pasian in hih leitung pua-ah zong Pu' nuntakna a len hi, cih theih in hehnepna a ngah uh hi.

records.english: Christians believe God rules the whole world.
records.zomi: Khazih mite in Pasian in leitung bup a uk hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: For my family, believing that God is eternal gives a sense of security when everything around us changes.
records.zomi: Ka innkuan adingin Pasian a tawntung hi, cih upna in i kiim-a na khempeuh a kikhek ciangin bitna a pia hi.

records.english: Our pastor preached about God's sovereignty.
records.zomi: I pastor in Pasian' thuneihna tawh kisai thu a gen hi.

records.english: My grandmother says that trusting God's sovereignty has freed her from trying to control everything herself.
records.zomi: Pasian' thuneihna muan in amah mahmah in na khempeuh uk sawm pan a suaktasak hi, ci-in ka pi in a gen hi.

records.english: Our family prays for God's will to be done.
records.zomi: I innkuan in Pasian' deihna a kicin nadingin thu a ngen hi.

records.english: My aunt says God has a plan for her life.
records.zomi: Pasian in a nuntakna adingin ngimna khat a nei hi, ci-in ka ni in a gen hi.

records.english: Grandpa reads Psalm 90 every New Year.
records.zomi: Pu in Kum Thak simin Late 90 a sim hi.

records.english: If God is in control, why did Dad lose his job?
records.zomi: Pasian in na khempeuh a uk leh bang hangin Pa in a nasep a mansuah hiam?

records.english: Christians believe God is sovereign, but they also admit that they don't always understand why hard things happen.
records.zomi: Khazih mite in Pasian in thuneihna a nei hi, ci-in a um uh a, ahi zongin bang hangin na haksa te a piang hiam cih a theisiam den kei uh hi, ci-in zong a san uh hi.

records.english: My brother asked if God knows the future.
records.zomi: Ka sanggampa in Pasian in hun hong tung ding a thei hiam, ci-in a dong hi.

records.english: Grandma says a thousand years are like one day to God.
records.zomi: Pasian adingin kumtul khat pen ni khat bangin ahi hi, ci-in Pi in a gen hi.

records.english: Why does Dad call God the King of everything?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pa in Pasian pen na khempeuh' Kumpipa a ci hiam?

records.english: We sing a hymn about God's eternal love.
records.zomi: Pasian' itna tawntung tawh kisai Pasian phatna la khat i sa hi.

records.english: My sister asked who made God.
records.zomi: Ka sanggamnu in Pasian kua in a bawl hiam, ci-in a dong hi.

records.english: Christians believe God has no beginning.
records.zomi: Khazih mite in Pasian in kipatna a nei kei hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: My father says that God's sovereignty is a comfort, not an excuse for doing nothing.
records.zomi: Pasian' thuneihna pen hehnepna khat ahi a, bangmah bawl lo nading kipiakna hi lo hi, ci-in ka pa in a gen hi.

records.english: Christians often find that the idea of God's eternity puts their own short lives into perspective.
records.zomi: Khazih mite in Pasian' tawntung hihna ngaihsutna in amau nuntakna tomno a kician zaw-in a lak hi, cih a mu zel uh hi.

records.english: Is God bigger than time?
records.zomi: Pasian pen hun sangin a lian zaw hiam?

records.english: My father says that trusting God's control doesn't mean we stop working hard or making plans.
records.zomi: Pasian' ukna muan in nasep hat taka sep leh ngimna bawl i khawl cihna hi lo hi, ci-in ka pa in a gen hi.

records.english: Grandpa, was God alive before the world began?
records.zomi: Pu aw, leitung a kipat ma-in Pasian a nungta khin hiam?

records.english: Christians believe God has always existed, long before the world and everything in it.
records.zomi: Khazih mite in Pasian pen leitung leh a sung-a na khempeuh ma-in a om den hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: Why do some Christians say that God is outside time, while others say he acts within it?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Khazih mite khenkhat in Pasian pen hun pua-ah a om hi, a ci uh a, a dangte in hun sungah a gamtat hi, a ci uh hiam?

records.english: When my sister was waiting for her exam results, Grandma told her that the future was safe in God's hands.
records.zomi: Ka sanggamnu in a kisinna suak ngak laitakin hun hong tung ding pen Pasian' khut sungah a bit hi, ci-in Pi in a gen hi.

records.english: Dad thanks God for every new day.
records.zomi: Pa in ni thak khatciat adingin Pasian tungah lungdam a ci hi.

records.english: Christians disagree about how God's sovereignty fits with human freedom, but most believe both are real.
records.zomi: Khazih mite in Pasian' thuneihna leh mihing' suahtakna bangci a kituak hiam cih a ngaihsutna uh a kibang kei a, ahi zongin a tam zaw in a nih tuak a om taktak hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: My grandmother often quotes the verse that says God is from everlasting to everlasting.
records.zomi: Ka pi in Pasian pen tawntung pan tawntung dong ahi hi, a ci Laisiangtho kammal tang a gen zel hi.

records.english: Is God ever in a hurry, Mum?
records.zomi: Nu aw, Pasian a manlang ngei hiam?

records.english: Does Grandma trust God with her future?
records.zomi: Pi in a hun hong tung ding Pasian a muang hiam?

records.english: My uncle says that knowing God is eternal makes his own worries seem much smaller.
records.zomi: Pasian a tawntung hi, cih theih in amah' lungkhamna te a neu zaw mahmah bangin a kilang sak hi, ci-in ka pa neu in a gen hi.

records.english: My grandmother prays every morning, saying that she hands the day over to God.
records.zomi: Ka pi in zingsang simin thu a ngen a, ni pen Pasian kiangah ka ap hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Will God be here forever?
records.zomi: Pasian tawntungin a om ding hiam?

records.english: In Christian belief, God's sovereignty means he rules with wisdom and love, not with cruelty.
records.zomi: Khazih upna-ah Pasian' thuneihna in pilna leh itna tawh a uk a, hehpih lohna tawh a uk kei hi, cihna ahi hi.

records.english: God's promises can be trusted, Christians say, because he never changes.
records.zomi: Pasian' kamciamna te a kimuang thei hi, bang hang hiam cih leh amah a kikhel ngei kei hi, ci-in Khazih mite in a gen uh hi.

records.english: Believing that God is sovereign does not stop Christians from grieving, but it shapes how they grieve.
records.zomi: Pasian in thuneihna a nei hi, cih upna in Khazih mite a dah khawlsak kei a, ahi zongin a dah dan uh a bawl hi.

records.english: When my parents faced uncertainty, their belief in God's eternal care helped them make decisions calmly.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in kician lohna a tuak uh ciangin Pasian' kemna tawntung a upna uh in dai takin thukhensatna a bawl nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Can anything happen without God knowing?
records.zomi: Pasian in a theih lo-in na khat a piang thei hiam?

records.english: Our family trusts God in hard times.
records.zomi: I innkuan in hun haksa-in Pasian a muang hi.

records.english: Our family's favourite hymn speaks of God as our help in ages past and our hope for years to come.
records.zomi: I innkuan' deih pen Pasian phatna la in Pasian pen hun bei-a i huhna leh kum hong tung ding-a i lamenna ahi hi, ci-in a gen hi.

records.english: When our house was damaged in the storm, my father reminded us that God was still on his throne.
records.zomi: Huihpi in i inn a susiat ciangin Pasian a tokhom tungah a tu lai hi, ci-in ka pa in hong phawk sak hi.

records.english: Does God ever get old?
records.zomi: Pasian a upa ngei hiam?

records.english: Where should we put the extra chairs?
records.zomi: Tutphah behlap te koi-ah i koih ding hiam?

records.english: Where can the dog sleep while we paint the kitchen?
records.zomi: An huan i zum laitakin ui koi-ah a ihmu thei ding hiam?

records.english: Many practical problems are solved simply by finding out where to go for the right kind of help.
records.zomi: Buaina taktak tampi pen huhna chi dik adingin koi-ah pai ding hiam cih theih bek tawh a kiphel hi.

records.english: Where can I get this lamp repaired?
records.zomi: Hih meivak koi-ah ka bawlphat sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Knowing where important documents are kept saves a great deal of stress in an emergency.
records.zomi: Laigelh thupi te koi-ah a kikem hiam cih theih in lauhuai hun-in lungkhamna tampi a kem sak hi.

records.english: Where should I start looking if the internet keeps cutting out in one room?
records.zomi: Inndan khat-ah internet a tat zel leh koi-ah ka zong pan ding hiam?

records.english: Where can I find a mechanic who will look at the car on a Sunday?
records.zomi: Nipini-in mawtaw a en ding mawtaw bawlpa koi-ah ka mu thei ding hiam?

records.english: Where should we hide the spare key?
records.zomi: Tawh behlap koi-ah i sel ding hiam?

records.english: Where should we put the new baby's cot when the flat has only one bedroom?
records.zomi: Inn-ah lupna inndan khat bek a om leh nausen thak' lupna koi-ah i koih ding hiam?

records.english: Put it in your room for the first months, and move it to the corner of the living room once she sleeps through the night.
records.zomi: A kha masa te sungin na inndan-ah koih inla, zan bup a ihmut theih ciangin inn sung inndan lian' a kil-ah koih in.

records.english: Where would be a better spot for the bins so they don't block the path?

records.english: Did Dad's house have a tin roof?
records.zomi: Pa' inn in kangtek inntung a nei hiam?

records.english: Our family's village is high in the hills.
records.zomi: I innkuan' khua pen mual sang mahmah tungah a om hi.

records.english: Did Dad play football on the hillside?
records.zomi: Pa in mual kawm-ah football a lawh hiam?

records.english: I want my children to visit the village one day, so that our family's stories become real places for them.
records.zomi: I innkuan tangthu te amau adingin mun taktak a suak nadingin ka tate ni khat-ah khua a kan ding ka deih hi.

records.english: My grandmother believes that the habits she learned in the village, such as wasting nothing, still matter today.
records.zomi: Ka pi in bangmah zang siat lo bang khua-ah a sin ngeina te tuni-in zong a thupi lai hi, ci-in a um hi.

records.english: How did your family keep in touch with relatives who moved across the border?
records.zomi: Gamgi kantan-a pem innkuanpihte tawh na innkuan uh bangci a kizom uh hiam?

records.english: We sent letters with anyone who was travelling, and sometimes it took months for a reply to reach us.
records.zomi: Khualzin mi kua peuh tawh lai i khak a, pawlkhat vei-in dawnna khat i tun nadingin kha tampi a la hi.

records.english: We send photos to our relatives across the border.
records.zomi: Gamgi kantan-a i innkuanpihte kiangah lim te i khak hi.

records.english: Grandma remembers the first bus to the village.
records.zomi: Khua-a hong tung bus masa pen Pi in a phawk hi.

records.english: Our family's stories of life in the region connect relatives who now live in many different countries.
records.zomi: Gam' tangthu-a i innkuan' nuntakna tangthu te in tu-in gam tuamtuam-ah a teng innkuanpihte a kizom sak hi.

records.english: Listening to my grandparents describe their village helps me understand the values they passed on to us.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh ka pi te in a khua uh a gen uh ngai in eite hong pia uh ngeina hoih te ka theisiam nadingin hong huh hi.

records.english: My aunt told us that the whole village gathered in the church whenever there was important news.
records.zomi: Thu thupi a om simin khua bup biakinn-ah a kikhawm uh hi, ci-in ka ni in hong gen hi.

records.english: My grandmother still speaks her village language.
records.zomi: Ka pi in a khua pau a zang lai hi.

records.english: Grandma remembers when the first mobile phone arrived and everyone queued to make a call.
records.zomi: Mobile phone masa pen a hong tun lai-in mi khempeuh phone sam dingin a kizui-in a ngak uh lai Pi in a phawk hi.

records.english: My cousins who grew up in the city were amazed by how dark the nights were in our grandparents' village.
records.zomi: Khuapi-a a khang ka sanggam te in ka pu leh ka pi te' khua-a zan te a mial mahmah dan a lamdang sa uh hi.

records.english: Did you have to walk to school every day, Dad?
records.zomi: Pa aw, ni simin sang-ah na pai ding a kisam hiam?

records.english: Yes, an hour each way, and in the rainy season I carried my shoes so they wouldn't get muddy.
records.zomi: Kisam hi, a pai leh a ciah nai khat ciat, vuah hun-in ka khedap a nawk lo nadingin ka pua hi.

records.english: Why did so many young people from Dad's village go to work in neighbouring countries?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pa' khua pan khangno tampi kiang gam te-ah nasep dingin a pai uh hiam?

records.english: My grandparents still travel to their village for church festivals, even though the journey takes two days.
records.zomi: Khualzinna in ni nih a la hangin ka pu leh ka pi te pawlpi pawi te adingin a khua uh-ah a khualzin lai uh hi.

records.english: Growing up far from my family's village, I rely on my relatives' stories to picture where we came from.
records.zomi: Ka innkuan' khua pan gamla takah ka khan ahih manin i hong pai panna mun lim ka ngaihsut nadingin ka innkuanpihte' tangthu te tungah ka kinga hi.

records.english: Does Grandpa still remember the old market?
records.zomi: Pu in sumbuk lui a phawk lai hiam?

records.english: Why does Grandpa still wake up before sunrise?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pu ni a suak ma-in a khanglawh lai hiam?

records.english: In his village, everyone started work in the fields before it got too hot.
records.zomi: A khua-ah mi khempeuh in a sa lua ma-in lo-ah nasep a kipan uh hi.

records.english: Did Mum walk to church every Sunday?
records.zomi: Nu in Nipini simin biakinn-ah a pai hiam?

records.english: My mother prays before every meal.
records.zomi: Ka nu in an a nek simin thu a ngen hi.

records.english: Why is the Bible called the Holy Bible?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Laisiangtho pen Lai Siangtho kici hiam?

records.english: Why do we stand when we read the Bible in church?
records.zomi: Bang hangin biakinn-ah Laisiangtho i sim ciangin i ding hiam?

records.english: Why do we bow our heads when we pray?
records.zomi: Bang hangin thu i ngen ciangin i lu i kun hiam?

records.english: In our home, the idea of God's holiness has taught the children to respect the Bible, prayer and one another.
records.zomi: I inn-ah Pasian' siangthona ngaihsutna in naupangte Laisiangtho, thungetna leh khat leh khat zahtak dingin a hilh hi.

records.english: We sang a song about God's goodness.
records.zomi: Pasian' hoihna tawh kisai la khat i sa hi.

records.english: We say sorry to God when we do wrong.
records.zomi: Na khial i bawl ciangin Pasian kiangah maisak i ngen hi.

records.english: Can people become holy?
records.zomi: Mite a siangtho thei uh hiam?

records.english: My cousin asked why the Bible calls God a consuming fire, and Grandpa explained it gently.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam in bang hangin Laisiangtho in Pasian pen a kang tum thei mei a ci hiam, ci-in a dong a, Pu in nem takin a gen hi.

records.english: My grandfather believes that a holy God calls his people to be different, not by looking down on others but by loving them.
records.zomi: A siangtho Pasian in a mite midangte nuamsa lo-in hi lo-in it-in a tuam dingin a sam hi, ci-in ka pu in a um hi.

records.english: Our family Bible study talked about how Moses took off his sandals at the burning bush.
records.zomi: I innkuan Laisiangtho sinna in Moses in a kang lopa-ah a khedap a suah dan tawh kisai a kikup hi.

records.english: Is it normal for a believer to feel small when thinking about God's holiness?
records.zomi: Upmi khat in Pasian' siangthona a ngaihsun ciangin amah a neu bangin a kizak pen a ngeina ahi hiam?

records.english: My grandmother believes that God's justice gives hope to people who have been treated badly.
records.zomi: Pasian' dikna in a hoih lo taka kibawl mite lamenna a pia hi, ci-in ka pi in a um hi.

records.english: My father taught us the Ten Commandments.
records.zomi: Ka pa in Thupiak Sawm hong hilh hi.

records.english: My brother asked why God made rules.
records.zomi: Ka sanggampa in bang hangin Pasian in thukham te a bawl hiam, ci-in a dong hi.

records.english: My aunt reads Isaiah to her children.
records.zomi: Ka ni in a tate kiangah Isaiah a sim hi.

records.english: God's righteousness, Christians believe, is shown in his promise to put the world right one day.
records.zomi: Pasian' diksakna pen ni khat-ah leitung a dik sak ding kamciamna-ah a kilang hi, ci-in Khazih mite in a um uh hi.

records.english: In Christian teaching, God's holiness reveals human failings, but his love invites people to change.
records.zomi: Khazih thuhilhna-ah Pasian' siangthona in mihing' khialhna te a lak a, ahi zongin a itna in mite kikhek dingin a sam hi.

records.english: Is it wrong to joke about God?
records.zomi: Pasian tawh kisai nuihzak thu gen pen a khial hiam?

records.english: My parents taught us that saying sorry to God and to others is part of living a holy life.
records.zomi: Pasian leh mi dangte kiangah maisak ngen pen nuntakna siangtho nuntak' a khen khat ahi hi, ci-in ka nu leh ka pa in hong hilh uh hi.

records.english: My father often reminds us that God's concern for justice should shape how our family spends its money and time.
records.zomi: Pasian' dikna tawh kisai a ngaihsutna in i innkuan in sum leh hun bangci a zat ding hiam cih a bawl ding hi, ci-in ka pa in hong phawk sak zel hi.

records.english: For my family, God's holiness is not a cold idea but a reason to treat everyday life with reverence.
records.zomi: Ka innkuan adingin Pasian' siangthona pen ngaihsutna dai lel khat hi lo-in ni sim nuntakna zahtakna tawh nuntak nading hangsan khat ahi hi.

records.english: When I was ten, I took some money from my father's coat and spent it on sweets.
records.zomi: Kum sawm ka phak lai-in ka pa' puan-ak pan sum khenkhat ka la a, a lim na te-ah ka zang hi.

records.english: That evening, he read us a psalm about God's holiness, and I felt so guilty that I confessed everything.
records.zomi: Tua nitak-in Pasian' siangthona tawh kisai Late khat hong sim a, ka mawh ka kizak mahmah ahih manin khempeuh ka pulak hi.

records.english: Instead of shouting, he prayed with me and told me that God forgives people who are truly sorry.
records.zomi: A kiko sangin keimah tawh thu a ngen a, Pasian in a kisik taktak mite a maisak hi, ci-in hong gen hi.

records.english: Grandpa says holy means set apart.
records.zomi: Siangtho cih in tuam-a kikoih cihna ahi hi, ci-in Pu in a gen hi.

records.english: Shall we read a psalm together tonight?
records.zomi: Tu zan Late khat i sim khawm ding hiam?

records.english: My little sister asked if God has ever told a lie.
records.zomi: Ka sanggamnu neu in Pasian in zuau a gen ngei hiam, ci-in a dong hi.

records.english: Our family's habit of confessing faults in prayer has made it easier for us to forgive one another.
records.zomi: Thungetna-ah khialhna pulak i innkuan ngeina in khat leh khat i kimaisak nadingin a baih zaw sak hi.

records.english: Why does Grandma say that God's righteousness should make us care about the poor?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pi in Pasian' diksakna in mi zawngte i ngaihsun nadingin a bawl ding hi, a ci hiam?

records.english: Because she believes a righteous God cares about justice, so his people should treat others fairly too.
records.zomi: Bang hang hiam cih leh dik Pasian in dikna a ngaihsun hi, ci-in a um ahih manin a mite in zong mi dangte dik takin a bawl ding uh hi.

records.english: Our family prays for people who are treated unfairly.
records.zomi: I innkuan in dik lo taka kibawl mite adingin thu a ngen hi.

records.english: Is God always fair, Grandma?
records.zomi: Pi aw, Pasian a dik den hiam?

records.english: Dad says God sees what we do in secret.
records.zomi: Pasian in a guk-a i bawl te a mu hi, ci-in Pa in a gen hi.

records.english: God's holiness makes my grandmother want to live more carefully, not more fearfully.
records.zomi: Pasian' siangthona in ka pi lau zaw-in hi lo-in cian zaw-in nuntak dingin a deihsak hi.

records.english: Whenever my parents explain God's righteousness, they talk about the prophets who defended the poor.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in Pasian' diksakna a gen simin mi zawngte a kem kamsangte tawh kisai a gen uh hi.

records.english: Mum says God wants us to be kind and honest.
records.zomi: Pasian in eite hehpihna nei-in thuman dingin hong deih hi, ci-in Nu in a gen hi.

records.english: Does God like it when we tell the truth?
records.zomi: Thu tak i gen ciangin Pasian in a deih hiam?

records.english: Grandpa, what does righteous mean?
records.zomi: Pu aw, dik cih in bang a cihna hiam?

records.english: It means doing what is right and fair, and Christians believe God is always righteous.
records.zomi: A dik leh a kilawm bawl cihna ahi a, Khazih mite in Pasian a dik den hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: Why do Christians believe that Jesus makes it possible for people to stand before a holy God?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Khazih mite in Jesu in mite a siangtho Pasian mai-ah a ding thei dingin a bawl hi, ci-in a um uh hiam?

records.english: Christians believe God hates injustice.
records.zomi: Khazih mite in Pasian in dik lohna a hua hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: Many Christians find that reflecting on God's holiness leads them to humility rather than pride.
records.zomi: Khazih mite tampi in Pasian' siangthona ngaihsun in kiletsakna sangin kiniamkhiatna-ah a paipih hi, cih a mu uh hi.

records.english: My father gave back the extra money a shop had given him, saying that God cares about honesty in small things.
records.zomi: Ka pa in van zuakna inn in a piak sum behlap a pia kik a, Pasian in na neute-ah zong thumanna a ngaihsun hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Grandma keeps her Bible on a special shelf.
records.zomi: Pi in a Laisiangtho van koihna tuam khat tungah a koih hi.

records.english: My mother teaches us that being righteous means treating others fairly, even when nobody is watching.
records.zomi: Dik cih pen kuamah in a en kei hangin mi dangte dik taka bawl cihna ahi hi, ci-in ka nu in hong hilh hi.

records.english: My aunt reminds her children that God's holiness is a reason to respect his name and his people.
records.zomi: Pasian' siangthona pen a min leh a mite zahtak nading hangsan khat ahi hi, ci-in ka ni in a tate a phawk sak hi.

records.english: Christians often say that God's righteousness is both a standard they cannot meet and a gift they receive by faith.
records.zomi: Pasian' diksakna pen amau in a phak zo lo ding tehna khat leh upna tawh a ngah letsong khat ahi hi, ci-in Khazih mite in a gen zel uh hi.

records.english: Mum, why do we close our eyes when we pray?
records.zomi: Nu aw, bang hangin thu i ngen ciangin i mit i khuh hiam?

records.english: It helps us stop looking around and remember that we are speaking to a holy God.
records.zomi: A kiim en khawl-in a siangtho Pasian tawh i kiho hi, cih i phawk nadingin hong huh hi.

records.english: When our family prays, we often ask God to make us more honest and fair in our daily lives.
records.zomi: I innkuan in thu a ngen ciangin i ni sim nuntakna-ah thuman zaw leh dik zaw dingin Pasian kiangah i ngen zel hi.

records.english: When my parents talk about righteousness, they mean right relationships with God and with other people.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh ka pa in diksakna a gen uh ciangin Pasian leh mi dangte tawh kizopna dik a cihna uh ahi hi.

records.english: What makes Dad say grace before every meal?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pa in an nek simin lungdam thu a ngen hiam?

records.english: He wants to thank God for the food and remember that everything good comes from him.
records.zomi: An adingin Pasian tungah lungdam ci-in, na hoih khempeuh amah pan a hong pai hi, cih phawk a nuam hi.

records.english: My father believes that a righteous God cares about how we treat people who cannot defend themselves.
records.zomi: Dik Pasian in amau le amau a kikem zo lo mite i bawl dan a ngaihsun hi, ci-in ka pa in a um hi.

records.english: Our family discussed how Isaiah felt unworthy when he saw a vision of God in the temple.
records.zomi: Isaiah in biakinn-ah Pasian' mangmuhna a muh ciangin amah a kilawm lo bangin a kizak dan i innkuan in a kikup hi.

records.english: My grandfather says that the more he understands God's goodness, the more he notices his own faults.
records.zomi: Pasian' hoihna a theisiam tam semsem ciangin amah' khialhna te a phawk tam semsem hi, ci-in ka pu in a gen hi.

records.english: If God is holy, will he still love me when I do something wrong?
records.zomi: Pasian a siangtho leh na khial khat ka bawl ciangin hong it lai ding hiam?

records.english: Christians believe God's holiness and love go together, so he is ready to forgive you when you say sorry.
records.zomi: Khazih mite in Pasian' siangthona leh itna a kikhawm hi, ci-in a um uh a, tua ahih manin maisak na ngen ciangin hong maisak dingin a kiging hi.

records.english: According to my grandmother, God's righteousness and his mercy meet in Jesus, which is why she is not afraid of him.
records.zomi: Ka pi' genna bangin Pasian' diksakna leh a hehpihna Jesu-ah a kituak a, tua ahih manin amah a lau kei hi.

records.english: Shops and services can often suggest solutions that customers never knew existed.
records.zomi: Van zuakna inn te leh nasep te in lei mite in a theih ngei loh phelna te a gen thei zel uh hi.

records.english: How do I fix a squeaky door?
records.zomi: Ging kongkhak khat bangci ka bawlphat ding hiam?

records.english: How can I save money on my weekly shopping without eating badly?
records.zomi: Hoih lo-in ne lo-in ka kal sim van lei-ah sum bangci ka kem thei ding hiam?

records.english: Plan your meals before you go, buy fruit and vegetables in season, and cook big batches to freeze.
records.zomi: Na pai ma-in na an te ngimna bawl inla, a hun-a gah leh anteh te lei inla, tuikhal khawl-ah koih dingin tam takin huan in.

records.english: A good how question includes enough detail for the other person to give useful advice.
records.zomi: 'Bangci' dotna hoih khat in mi dang khat in thuhilhna huh huai a pia thei nadingin thu kicing a nei hi.

records.english: Asking how a problem started is often the first step towards stopping it from happening again.
records.zomi: Buaina khat bangci a kipan hiam cih dot pen a piang kik lo nadingin kham nading kalsuan masa pen ahi zel hi.

records.english: How can I fix a wobbly table?
records.zomi: A kihot dohkan khat bangci ka bawlphat thei ding hiam?

records.english: When my grandmother's hearing got worse, she stopped answering the phone and missed calls from the whole family.
records.zomi: Ka pi' a zak a hoih lo semsem ciangin phone a dawng nawn kei a, innkuan bup' sapna te a mansuah hi.

records.english: My cousin asked the phone company how they could help, and they sent a phone with a flashing light and a very loud ring.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam in phone company bangci a huh thei hiam, ci-in a dong a, meivak kiliak leh ging mahmah nei phone khat a khak uh hi.

records.english: Now Grandma answers every call, and she says she feels part of the family's news again.
records.zomi: Tu-in Pi in sapna khempeuh a dawng a, innkuan thu thak sungah a kihel kik bangin a kizak hi, a ci hi.

records.english: When people share how they solved a problem, they turn their own frustration into help for others.
records.zomi: Mite in buaina khat bangci a phel uh hiam cih a gen uh ciangin amau' lungkiatna mi dangte adingin huhna-ah a khek uh hi.

records.english: Many household problems can be solved with cheap materials and a little patience.
records.zomi: Inn sung buaina tampi pen man neem van te leh thuakzawhna tawmno tawh a kiphel thei hi.

records.english: How can I dry my shoes quickly?
records.zomi: Ka khedap manlang takin bangci ka keu sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: How can we share one bathroom fairly between five people in the morning?
records.zomi: Zingsang-in mi nga kikal-ah kisilna inndan khat dik takin bangci i kihawm thei ding hiam?

records.english: Online videos show how to fix many things, but some repairs are safer left to professionals.
records.zomi: Online video te in na tampi bawlphat dan a lak hi, ahi zongin bawlphatna khenkhat siam mite kiangah nusia a bit zaw hi.

records.english: How can I get the smell out of the fridge?
records.zomi: Dahkhawl sung pan gim bangci ka paikhia thei ding hiam?

records.english: How should we split the cost of a shared car between three families?
records.zomi: Innkuan thum kikal-ah kizang khawm mawtaw khat' man bangci i khen ding hiam?

records.english: Small changes in habits, such as opening a window or switching off a plug, solve many everyday problems.
records.zomi: Tawlet hon ahih kei leh plug khak bang ngeina-a kikhekna neute in ni sim buaina tampi a phel hi.

records.english: How do I get chewing gum off my shoe?
records.zomi: Ka khedap pan cingam bangci ka la khia ding hiam?

records.english: How should we prepare the house before a big storm arrives?
records.zomi: Huihpi lian khat a tun ma-in inn bangci i kiginsak ding hiam?

records.english: How do I stop my laptop from overheating when I work in bed?
records.zomi: Lupna tungah ka sep ciangin ka laptop a sa lua lo nadingin bangci ka kham ding hiam?

records.english: When a solution is explained step by step, people feel confident enough to try it themselves.
records.zomi: Phelna khat kalsuan khatciat-in a kigen ciangin mite in amau mahmah-in a sit nadingin a kihuai uh hi.

records.english: How can I make my bicycle safer for riding home in the dark?
records.zomi: Mial-in inn-ah ka ciah nadingin ka siiksakol bangci a bit zaw-in ka bawl thei ding hiam?

records.english: How do I hang a picture without a drill?
records.zomi: Tha tawh kua om lo-in lim khat bangci ka khai thei ding hiam?

records.english: How should I tell my landlord about the damp without sounding rude?
records.zomi: Zahtak lo bangin kizak lo-in ka inn neipa kiangah tui hual tawh kisai bangci ka gen ding hiam?

records.english: How can we keep the mosquitoes out?
records.zomi: Thosi te bangci i kham thei ding hiam?

records.english: How do I clean the oven without using strong chemicals?
records.zomi: Chemical hat zang lo-in oven bangci ka siangsak ding hiam?

records.english: Families who ask how they can share tasks fairly often find that arguments disappear.
records.zomi: Nasep te dik takin bangci i kihawm thei ding hiam cih a dong innkuan te in kinialna te a mang hi, cih a mu zel uh hi.

records.english: How can we make the long drive to Grandma's easier for the children?
records.zomi: Pi' inn-ah mawtaw tawh khualzinna sau naupangte adingin bangci a baih zaw-in i bawl thei ding hiam?

records.english: How can I get my teenage son to help more around the house?
records.zomi: Ka tapa khangno inn sung nasep-ah a huh tam zaw nadingin bangci ka bawl thei ding hiam?

records.english: How can I stop my glasses from slipping?
records.zomi: Ka mitlimlang a kiliam lo nadingin bangci ka kham thei ding hiam?

records.english: How do I get a stuck ring off my finger?
records.zomi: Ka khut zung-a kitang khutzungbuh bangci ka suakkhia ding hiam?

records.english: Hold your hand up for a minute, then use a little soap and twist the ring gently.
records.zomi: Minit khat sung na khut khai tou inla, tua khit ciangin saapho tawmno zang-in khutzungbuh nem takin heih in.

records.english: How do I remove a splinter safely?
records.zomi: Sing gulh khat bit takin bangci ka la khia ding hiam?

records.english: How can we keep the cat off the kitchen table?
records.zomi: An huan dohkan tung pan zawhngeu bangci i kham thei ding hiam?

records.english: Give her a high shelf of her own near the window, and put her down every time she jumps up.
records.zomi: Tawlet kiangah amah adingin van koihna sang khat pia inla, a diah tou simin a nuai-ah koih in.

records.english: How do I unblock the shower drain?
records.zomi: Kisilna mun tuilam bangci ka hon ding hiam?

records.english: How can I keep the bread fresh longer?
records.zomi: Moh sawt zaw a thak den nadingin bangci ka kem thei ding hiam?

records.english: How should we handle a neighbour who keeps parking across our driveway?
records.zomi: I mawtaw lampi a tan zel inn kiang mi khat bangci i bawl ding hiam?

records.english: Speak to them politely first, and if it continues, write a short note and keep a record of the dates.
records.zomi: A masa-in zahtak takin gen in, a zom zel leh lai tomno khat gelh inla, a ni te ciamteh in.

records.english: How can I stop worrying that I've left the cooker on every time I go out?
records.zomi: Ka pai khiat simin an huanna khawl ka nusia hiam cih ka lungkham nawn lo nadingin bangci ka bawl thei ding hiam?

records.english: How do I clean a burnt pan?
records.zomi: Beel kang khat bangci ka siangsak ding hiam?

records.english: How can I stop the window from steaming up?
records.zomi: Tawlet a meikhu khuh lo nadingin bangci ka kham thei ding hiam?

records.english: How can I stop the bathroom tiles from going mouldy?
records.zomi: Kisilna inndan suang te a mu lo nadingin bangci ka kham thei ding hiam?

records.english: Open the window after every shower, and wipe the corners with a dry cloth once a week.
records.zomi: Na kisil khit simin tawlet hong inla, kal simin puan keu tawh a kil te nul in.

records.english: Asking how to solve a problem, rather than complaining about it, usually leads to practical help.

records.english: By the end of the week, we had drawn and named twelve different living things from a single spoonful of water.
