records.english: May we store our bikes in the shed?
records.zomi: I siiksakol te van koihna inn neu sungah i koih thei ding hiam?

records.english: Would the school let parents use the playground for a weekend clean-up?
records.zomi: Kal tawp-in sianghsakna adingin sang in nu leh pa te naupang kimawlna mun a zat sak ding hiam?

records.english: Getting permission is usually quicker than dealing with the consequences of not asking.
records.zomi: Phalna ngah pen a dot lohna suakna te tawh kituah sangin a manlang zaw zel hi.

records.english: Can we move the meeting to the bigger room, since twenty people are coming?
records.zomi: Mi sawmnih a hong ding uh ahih manin kikhopna inndan lian zaw-ah i khek thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, I'll ask the caretaker to unlock it and set out the chairs.
records.zomi: Thei hi, a kemmi kiangah hong dingin leh tutphah te koih dingin ka ngen ding hi.

records.english: Can we paint the wall in the hallway?
records.zomi: Inn sung lampi-a kul i hal thei ding hiam?

records.english: Would the hotel allow us to bring our own birthday cake to the restaurant?
records.zomi: Zinbuuk in an ne inn-ah eimau' suahni cake paipih dingin hong phal ding hiam?

records.english: Community projects often succeed because someone took the trouble to ask the right questions first.
records.zomi: Khuasung nasep te pen mi khat in dotna dik te a dong masa ahih manin a zawh zel hi.

records.english: Can we use the hall kitchen?
records.zomi: Inn lian an huanna inn i zang thei ding hiam?

records.english: Can I hang a shelf in the rented flat?
records.zomi: Ka hal inn sungah dawhkan khai khat ka khai thei ding hiam?

records.english: Would it be all right if the volunteers stored the food parcels in your garage for a week?
records.zomi: Thalawp te in kal khat sung an ip te na garage sungah a koih leh a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: May we put a bench outside the shop?
records.zomi: Van zuakna inn pua-ah tutphah sau khat i koih thei ding hiam?

records.english: Could I ask the farmer whether we can cross his field to reach the river?
records.zomi: Lui i tun nadingin a lo i kan thei ding hiam cih lo neipa kiangah ka dong thei ding hiam?

records.english: Written permission protects both sides if there is a disagreement about what was agreed.
records.zomi: Laigelh-a phalna in bang a kilungkim hiam cih tawh kisai kinialna a om leh lam nih tuak a kem hi.

records.english: May I cut back the hedge on your side?
records.zomi: Na lam-a huang sing te ka at thei ding hiam?

records.english: Many practical problems can be solved simply by asking the right person for permission.
records.zomi: Buaina tampi pen mi dik khat kiangah phalna ngen bek tawh a kiphel thei hi.

records.english: May I fix the fence myself?
records.zomi: Huang kei mahmah-in ka bawlphat thei ding hiam?

records.english: Could I ask the school whether my son can leave early on Fridays for his hospital appointments?
records.zomi: Ka tapa in damlo inn kihona hun te adingin Laithai ni simin a ma-in a pai thei ding hiam cih sang kiangah ka dong thei ding hiam?

records.english: Do we need the other tenants' agreement before we change the lock on the shared door?
records.zomi: Kongkhak kihawm' khawlh i khek ma-in inn hal dangte' lungkimna i kisam hiam?

records.english: Knowing who has the authority to give permission saves a great deal of time and frustration.
records.zomi: Phalna pia thei thuneihna kua in a nei hiam cih theih in hun leh lungsim buaina tampi a kem hi.

records.english: When our street wanted to hold a summer party, nobody knew whose permission we needed to close the road.
records.zomi: I lampi in khal pawi khat bawl a deih ciangin lampi khak nadingin kua' phalna i kisam hiam cih kuamah in a thei kei hi.

records.english: A neighbour rang the council, filled in the form and gathered signatures from every household.
records.zomi: Inn kiang mi khat in council a sam a, lai a gelh a, innkuan khatciat pan min gelhna te a kaikhawm hi.

records.english: Three weeks later the road was closed for the day, and the children played football where the cars usually park.
records.zomi: Kal thum khit-in ni khat sung lampi a kikhak a, naupangte in mawtaw te a koih ngeina mun-ah football a mawl uh hi.

records.english: Would the landlord let us put up a satellite dish if we pay for any damage?
records.zomi: Siatna khatpeuh adingin i pia leh inn neipa in satellite dish khat koih dingin hong phal ding hiam?

records.english: Asking permission early often turns a possible argument into a friendly agreement.
records.zomi: A ma-in phalna ngen in kinialna piang thei khat lawmta kilungkimna-ah a khek zel hi.

records.english: What should we do if the landlord refuses permission to fix the broken window ourselves?
records.zomi: Inn neipa in tawhkhuak siat eimau' mahmah-in bawlphat dingin phalna a nial leh bang i bawl ding hiam?

records.english: Ask him to put his refusal in writing, and then contact the housing advice service about who must pay for the repair.
records.zomi: A nialna laigelh-in gelh dingin ngen in, tua khit-in bawlphatna man kua in a pia ding hiam cih tawh kisai inn thuhilhna nasep tawh kizom in.

records.english: Could we ask the park keeper whether the children's club can use the pavilion when it rains?
records.zomi: Guah a zuk ciangin naupangte' pawl in park inn neu a zang thei ding hiam cih park kemmi kiangah i dong thei ding hiam?

records.english: May I use the printer for my tickets?
records.zomi: Ka ticket te adingin printer ka zang thei ding hiam?

records.english: May I charge my phone at your desk?
records.zomi: Na dawhkan-ah ka phone charge ka bawl thei ding hiam?

records.english: May I move my desk nearer the heater?
records.zomi: Ka dawhkan lumsakna khawl kiang nai zaw-ah ka khek thei ding hiam?

records.english: Do we need the council's permission to build a small shed in the back garden?
records.zomi: Inn nung huan-ah van koihna inn neu khat lam nadingin council' phalna i kisam hiam?

records.english: When several people are affected, asking everyone's permission prevents resentment later.
records.zomi: Mi tampi a kituak ciangin mi khempeuh' phalna ngen in a nunung-a lungkimlohna a kham hi.

records.english: When permission is refused, asking for the reason can reveal another way to solve the problem.
records.zomi: Phalna a kinial ciangin hangsan dot in buaina phel nading lampi dang khat a lak thei hi.

records.english: Is it possible to get permission to keep a cat in a flat where pets aren't usually allowed?
records.zomi: Ganhing kem phalna om lo inn khat-ah zawhngeu khat kem nadingin phalna ngah thei ahi hiam?

records.english: Would it be all right if I worked from the library while my flat is being repaired?
records.zomi: Ka inn a kibawlphat laitakin laibu inn pan nasep ka sem leh a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, as long as you're reachable by phone and can come in for Thursday's meeting.
records.zomi: Hoih hi, phone tawh hong sam theih na hih a, Laizing ni kikhopna-ah na hong thei leh.

records.english: May I borrow your ladder for the gutters?
records.zomi: Inn tui luanna adingin na kahlei ka puk thei ding hiam?

records.english: Offering to pay for any damage makes it easier for a landlord or neighbour to say yes.
records.zomi: Siatna khatpeuh adingin pia dingin kiciam in inn neipa ahih kei leh inn kiang mi in a phal a baih zaw sak hi.

records.english: Could I ask the library whether our language group can use the meeting room every Monday?
records.zomi: I pau pawl in Pizing ni simin kikhopna inndan a zang thei ding hiam cih laibu inn kiangah ka dong thei ding hiam?

records.english: Can the children play in the yard?
records.zomi: Naupangte inn mai-ah a kimawl thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: May I use the car park after six?
records.zomi: Nai guk khit-in mawtaw koihna mun ka zang thei ding hiam?

records.english: Can I swap seats with my friend?
records.zomi: Ka lawm tawh tutna ka kikhek thei ding hiam?

records.english: Councils and landlords are often more willing to give permission when the request is clear and specific.
records.zomi: Ngetna a kician leh a cian ciangin council te leh inn neipa te in phalna pia dingin a ut zaw zel uh hi.

records.english: Can I park in your space while you're away?
records.zomi: Na om lohna sungin na mun-ah ka mawtaw ka koih thei ding hiam?

records.english: Can I bring my dog to the office tomorrow?
records.zomi: Zing-in ka ui office-ah ka paipih thei ding hiam?

records.english: Do I need my manager's permission to change my lunch break so I can collect my daughter?
records.zomi: Ka tanu ka la theih nadingin ka sun an tawlngak hun ka khek nadingin ka manager' phalna ka kisam hiam?

records.english: May we use your driveway while our builders fix the wall?
records.zomi: I inn lam te in kul a bawlphat laitak-un na mawtaw lampi i zang thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, for a week, but please keep the gate clear on Wednesday for the bin lorry.
records.zomi: Thei hi, kal khat sung, ahi zongin nawi mawtaw adingin Nilai ni-in kongpi kilawn sak in.

records.english: Can I take the old chairs home?
records.zomi: Tutphah lui te inn-ah ka paipih thei ding hiam?

records.english: Can I leave the bins in the alley?
records.zomi: Nawi koihna te lampi neu-ah ka nusia thei ding hiam?

records.english: Is it all right if we leave the car on the road overnight while the drive is being resurfaced?
records.zomi: Mawtaw lampi a kithak bawl laitakin zan khat sung lampi tungah mawtaw i nusia leh a hoih ding hiam?

records.english: Can we have the party in the garden?
records.zomi: Huan sungah pawi i bawl thei ding hiam?

records.english: Could I put a ramp at the shop entrance for my wheelchair?
records.zomi: Ka tawlek tutphah adingin van zuakna inn kongkhak-ah kahtohna nem khat ka koih thei ding hiam?

records.english: You'll need the landlord's permission, but I'll ask him for you today.
records.zomi: Inn neipa' phalna na kisam ding a, ahi zongin tuni-in nang adingin ka dong ding hi.

records.english: Classmates who share stories from their home regions bring geography lessons to life.
records.zomi: A gam lam uh pan tangthu a hawm sinna pihte in leitung sinna te a nungta sak uh hi.

records.english: How do borders sometimes split people who share the same language?
records.zomi: Gamgi te in pau kibang a ham mite bangci a khen zel hiam?

records.english: Can I find this country on the globe?
records.zomi: Hih gam leitung lim bawl tungah ka mu thei ding hiam?

records.english: What language do people speak there?
records.zomi: Tua mun-ah mite in bang pau a ham uh hiam?

records.english: Understanding the regions of one's own country is a good first step towards understanding the wider world.
records.zomi: Mi khat' amah gam sung-a mun tuamtuam theisiam pen leitung lian zaw theisiam nading lamkal masa hoih khat ahi hi.

records.english: Why do some countries have their capital in a smaller city?
records.zomi: Bang hangin gam khenkhat in a khuapi lian pen khuapi neu zaw khat-ah a koih uh hiam?

records.english: Which region has the most people?
records.zomi: Bang gam khen in mi a tam pen hiam?

records.english: What money do they use in that country?
records.zomi: Tua gam-ah bang sum a zang uh hiam?

records.english: What is the capital of this region?
records.zomi: Hih gam khen' khuapi lian pen bang ahi hiam?

records.english: How do mountains affect where people choose to live?
records.zomi: Mual te in mite' tenna ding mun teelna bangci a khawng hiam?

records.english: Why do some countries have time zones while others don't?
records.zomi: Bang hangin gam khenkhat in hun khen tuamtuam a nei a, a dangte in a nei kei uh hiam?

records.english: Which country is closest to ours?
records.zomi: Bang gam in i gam tawh a kinai pen hiam?

records.english: How many regions does our country have?
records.zomi: I gam in gam khen bangzah a nei hiam?

records.english: How can learning about a neighbouring country help us understand our own?
records.zomi: I gam kiang-a gam khat tawh kisai sin in i gam bangci a theisiam sak thei hiam?

records.english: Teachers often answer questions about countries by comparing them with places pupils already know.
records.zomi: Saya te in gam te tawh kisai dotna te sangnaupangte in a theih khin mun te tawh khaikhin in a dawng zel uh hi.

records.english: How can a country be rich in natural resources but still have poor regions?
records.zomi: Gam khat in leitung pan van manpha tampi a nei hangin gam khen zawng te bangci a nei thei hiam?

records.english: Which continent is this country in?
records.zomi: Hih gam pen bang leitung lian sungah a om hiam?

records.english: How can I find out what the climate is like in another country?
records.zomi: Gam dang khat' khuamun ngeina bangci a om hiam cih bangci ka thei thei ding hiam?

records.english: Look at a climate graph, which shows the average temperature and rainfall for each month.
records.zomi: Kha khatciat' lumna tehna lai leh guah zuk zah a lak khuamun ngeina lim khat en in.

records.english: How can we learn about a country fairly, without relying on stereotypes?
records.zomi: Mite' ngaihsutna kibawl te tungah kinga lo-in gam khat tawh kisai dik takin bangci i sin thei ding hiam?

records.english: Use several sources, including people who live there, and look at its history, culture and daily life, not just its problems.
records.zomi: Tua mun-a teng mite tel-in thu pianna tampi zang in, a buaina te bek hi lo-in a tangthu, a ngeina leh ni sim nuntakna en in.

records.english: When a new pupil joined our class, our teacher asked her to tell us about the region she came from.
records.zomi: Sangnaupang thak khat i sinna-ah a hong lut ciangin i saya in a hong pai na gam khen tawh kisai hong gen dingin a ngen hi.

records.english: She brought photos of rice fields, a busy market and her grandmother's kitchen.
records.zomi: Buh lo te, mi tam kawlpi khat leh a pi' an huanna inn' photo te a paipih hi.

records.english: By the end of the lesson, the region we had only seen on maps felt like a real place full of real people.
records.zomi: Sinna a bei ciangin map tungah bek i muh gam khen pen mi taktak tawh a dim mun taktak khat bangin a kizak hi.

records.english: A curious question about a faraway country can lead to a lifelong interest in travel and other cultures.
records.zomi: Gamla-a gam khat tawh kisai theih nopna dotna khat in khualzinna leh ngeina dangte tungah nuntak sung deihna-ah a pi thei hi.

records.english: What do people grow in this region?
records.zomi: Hih gam khen-ah mite in bang a suan uh hiam?

records.english: Stereotypes about countries often fade when students meet people who actually live there.
records.zomi: Sangnaupangte in tua mun-a teng taktak mite a muh uh ciangin gam te tawh kisai ngaihsutna kibawl te a mang zel hi.

records.english: Is the north of the country colder?
records.zomi: Gam' a mal lam a vot zaw hiam?

records.english: What makes a region good for farming?
records.zomi: Bang in gam khen khat lo bawl nadingin a hoih sak hiam?

records.english: Why do people in coastal regions often eat more fish?
records.zomi: Bang hangin tuipi gei gam khen-a mite in nga a ne tam zaw zel uh hiam?

records.english: Is this country in Asia or Europe?
records.zomi: Hih gam pen Asia-ah a om hiam, Europe-ah a om hiam?

records.english: How far is this country from ours?
records.zomi: Hih gam i gam pan bangzah a gamla hiam?

records.english: Why do maps sometimes make countries near the poles look bigger than they really are?
records.zomi: Bang hangin map te in leitung tawpna kiang-a gam te a lianna taktak sangin a lian zaw bangin a lak zel hiam?

records.english: Questions about why cities grew where they did reveal how much people have always depended on water.
records.zomi: Bang hangin khuapi te a khanna mun-ah a khang hiam cih dotna te in mite tui tungah bangzah a kinga den uh hiam cih a lak hi.

records.english: Climate graphs help students turn numbers into a clear picture of life in another region.
records.zomi: Khuamun ngeina lim te in sangnaupangte in nambat te gam khen dang khat-a nuntakna lim kician khat-ah a khek nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Why are some countries divided into states while others have provinces?
records.zomi: Bang hangin gam khenkhat in state te-ah a kikhen a, a dangte in province te a nei uh hiam?

records.english: Why do some regions of the same country have very different weather?
records.zomi: Bang hangin gam kibang-a gam khen khenkhat in khuamun kibang lo mahmah a nei uh hiam?

records.english: Is it hot all year in this region?
records.zomi: Hih gam khen-ah kum bup a sa hiam?

records.english: Questions about languages and borders help students see that maps do not always match how people live.
records.zomi: Pau leh gamgi te tawh kisai dotna te in sangnaupangte in map te mite' nuntak dan tawh a kituak den kei hi, cih a mu nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: What is this country's flag like?
records.zomi: Hih gam' puanzar bang ahi hiam?

records.english: Do they drive on the left there?
records.zomi: Tua gam-ah veilam-ah mawtaw a mawng uh hiam?

records.english: Is this country north of the equator?
records.zomi: Hih gam pen leitung kikal lam' mal lam-ah a om hiam?

records.english: Does this country have a coastline?
records.zomi: Hih gam in tuipi gei a nei hiam?

records.english: Why do some countries have more than one official language?
records.zomi: Bang hangin gam khenkhat in pau tak khat sanga tam a nei hiam?

records.english: Because different groups of people have lived there for centuries, and the country wants to respect them all.
records.zomi: Bang hang hiam cih leh mi pawl tuamtuam kum zatampi sung tua mun-ah a teng uh a, gam in amaute khempeuh a zahtak nuam hi.

records.english: Why do many people move from rural regions to cities?
records.zomi: Bang hangin mi tampi khuaneu gam khen te pan khuapi te-ah a pem uh hiam?

records.english: How do rivers that cross several countries affect relations between them?
records.zomi: Gam tampi a kan lui te in amaute kikal-a kizopna bangci a khawng hiam?

records.english: Maps are useful tools, but students should know that every map simplifies the world in some way.
records.zomi: Map te pen nasep van manpha ahi a, ahi zongin sangnaupangte in map khatciat in leitung lampi khat-in a baih sak hi, cih a theih ding uh hi.

records.english: How do geographers decide where one region ends and another begins?
records.zomi: Leitung pilmite in gam khen khat koi-ah a tawp a, a dang khat koi-ah a kipan hiam cih bangci a thukhen uh hiam?

records.english: Why are most big cities built near rivers or the sea?
records.zomi: Bang hangin khuapi lian tampi lui ahih kei leh tuipi kiangah a kilam hiam?

records.english: Water was needed for drinking, farming and trade, so people settled where it was easy to reach.
records.zomi: Tui pen dawn ding, lo bawl ding leh sumbawl ding a kisam ahih manin mite in a tun baih mun-ah a teng uh hi.

records.english: Pupils who ask why regions differ are beginning to connect geography with history and economics.
records.zomi: Bang hangin gam khen te a kibang lo hiam cih a dong sangnaupangte in leitung sinna tangthu leh sum leh van sinna tawh a kizom sak pan uh hi.

records.english: Questions about rural and urban regions help pupils think about where they might live and work in future.
records.zomi: Khuaneu leh khuapi gam khen te tawh kisai dotna te in sangnaupangte hun zom-ah koi-ah a teng ding uh a, koi-ah nasep a sem ding uh hiam cih a ngaihsun nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Is a region the same as a country?
records.zomi: Gam khen khat pen gam khat tawh a kibang hiam?

records.english: No, a region is a part of a country, or sometimes an area that covers parts of several countries.
records.zomi: Kibang kei hi, gam khen khat pen gam khat' a khen ahi a, ahih kei leh gam tampi' a khen te a huap mun khat ahi zel hi.

records.english: Which ocean is near this country?
records.zomi: Bang tuipi lian in hih gam a nai hiam?

records.english: Which mountains are in the north?
records.zomi: Mal lam-ah bang mual te a om hiam?

records.english: How does a region's history affect the languages people speak there today?
records.zomi: Gam khen khat' tangthu in tuni-in tua mun-a mite' ham pau te bangci a khawng hiam?

records.english: Learning about a country through its people, not only its statistics, gives students a fairer picture.
records.zomi: Gam khat a nambat te bek hi lo-in a mite tungtawn-in sin in sangnaupangte lim dik zaw khat a pia hi.

records.english: How big is this country?
records.zomi: Hih gam bangzah a lian hiam?

records.english: The physiotherapist at the community clinic helped my uncle walk without a stick after his stroke.
records.zomi: Khuasung damdawi inn neu-a pumpi sawlna siampa in ka pa neu a natna lian khit-in ciangkhut om lo-in a pai theih nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Asking for help early is a sign of strength, not weakness, and it often makes recovery faster.
records.zomi: A ma-in huhna ngen pen hatna lahna ahi a, hatlohna hi lo a, damkikna a manlang sak zel hi.

records.english: The food bank's advice desk helped us claim the support we hadn't known we were entitled to.
records.zomi: An piakna mun' thuhilhna dawhkan in i ngah thei a i theih loh huhna te i ngen nadingin hong huh hi.

records.english: What helped you most when you arrived in the country with almost nothing?
records.zomi: Bangmah nei lo-in gam-ah na hong tun ciangin bang in hong huh pen hiam?

records.english: A volunteer at the refugee centre helped me with forms, found English classes and introduced me to people who became friends.
records.zomi: Galtai inn-a thalawp khat in lai te-ah hong huh a, English sinna hong zong sak a, lawm a suak mite tawh hong theisak hi.

records.english: The nurse helped my mother walk again.
records.zomi: Nurse in ka nu a pai kik nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: My English class gave me confidence.
records.zomi: Ka English sinna in hanna hong pia hi.

records.english: After the factory closed, the council set up a retraining scheme that helped hundreds of workers find new jobs.
records.zomi: Sepna inn a kikhak khit-in council in nasem zatampi in nasep thak a muh nadingin a huh kisin kikna ngimna khat a bawl hi.

records.english: The refugee centre helped my cousin have her qualifications recognised so that she could work as a nurse again.
records.zomi: Galtai inn in ka sanggam nurse-in a sem kik theih nadingin a lai sinna te a kipom nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: The school's family support worker helped us through the months after my father's death.
records.zomi: Sang' innkuan huhna nasempa in ka pa' sihna khit-a kha te sungin hong huh hi.

records.english: A social worker helped us find a nursery.
records.zomi: Mipi huhna nasempa khat in naupang kemna inn khat i muh nadingin hong huh hi.

records.english: The job centre paid for my training course.
records.zomi: Nasep zonna office in ka kisinna man a pia hi.

records.english: Our neighbours raised money for the hospital trip.
records.zomi: I inn kiang mite in damlo inn khualzinna adingin sum a kaikhawm uh hi.

records.english: When my father lost his job at sixty, he was sure nobody would ever employ him again.
records.zomi: Ka pa kum sawmguk-in a nasep a mansuah ciangin kuamah in amah nasep a pia nawn kei ding hi, ci-in a ngaihsun cian hi.

records.english: A careers adviser at the library helped him update his CV and practise for interviews.
records.zomi: Laibu inn-a nasep lamlak thuhilhpa in a CV a thak bawl nadingin leh kikupna adingin a kisin nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Six months later, he was training younger workers at a local garage and enjoying it more than his old job.
records.zomi: Kha guk khit-in khuasung garage khat-ah nasem naupang zaw te a hilh a, a nasep lui sangin a nuam sa zaw hi.

records.english: My neighbour's addiction recovery group meets in the church hall every Wednesday evening.
records.zomi: Ka inn kiang mi' zu-zat lehna pan damkikna pawl pen Nilai ni nitak simin biakinn inn lian-ah a kikhawm uh hi.

records.english: Did the food bank help you through the winter?
records.zomi: An piakna mun in khuaphal sungin hong huh hiam?

records.english: Many people do not know which services are available until a neighbour or friend tells them.
records.zomi: Mi tampi in inn kiang mi ahih kei leh lawm khat in a gen ma-un bang nasep te a om hiam cih a thei kei uh hi.

records.english: How did the council find you a new flat so quickly?
records.zomi: Council in inn thak khat manlang takin bangci hong zong sak hiam?

records.english: The youth club kept my son out of trouble.
records.zomi: Tangvalte pawl in ka tapa buaina pan a kem hi.

records.english: With help from the disability service, my son now travels to college on his own.
records.zomi: Pumpi kicinglohna huhna nasep' huhna tawh ka tapa in tu-in amah bek-in college-ah a pai thei hi.

records.english: The clinic helped my brother stop drinking.
records.zomi: Damdawi inn neu in ka sanggampa zu dawn a khawl nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Advice centres help people solve problems that seem impossible when faced alone.
records.zomi: Thuhilhna mun te in mite in a khat bek-a a thuak uh ciangin a theih loh bangin a kilang buaina te a phel nadingin a huh uh hi.

records.english: Who helped you get back to work after your injury?
records.zomi: Na liamna khit-in nasep-ah na ciah kik nadingin kua in hong huh hiam?

records.english: An adviser at the job centre arranged a course and found me an employer willing to adapt my hours.
records.zomi: Nasep zonna office-a thuhilhpa khat in sinna khat a bawl a, ka nasep hun a khek sak nuam nasep nei khat hong zong sak hi.

records.english: Communities that work together with public services recover more quickly from hard times.
records.zomi: Mipi nasep te tawh a kithuah khuasung te in hun haksa te pan manlang zaw-in a dam kik uh hi.

records.english: The school gave my children free meals.
records.zomi: Sang in ka tate an man om lo a pia hi.

records.english: Which charity paid for your new glasses?
records.zomi: Bang huhna pawl in na mitlimlang thak man a pia hiam?

records.english: Who helped you with the housing application?
records.zomi: Inn ngetna lai-ah kua in hong huh hiam?

records.english: The youth worker helped my brother find an apprenticeship after he left school without qualifications.
records.zomi: Tangvalte nasempa in ka sanggampa lai sinna nei lo-in sang a nusiat khit-in nasep sinna khat a muh nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Did the church give you furniture after the fire?
records.zomi: Mei kang khit-in biakinn in innsung van te hong pia hiam?

records.english: The community centre runs a debt advice session.
records.zomi: Khuasung inn lian in leiba thuhilhna kikhopna khat a bawl hi.

records.english: A volunteer helped me fill in the forms.
records.zomi: Thalawp khat in lai te gelh dingin hong huh hi.

records.english: Recognising qualifications from abroad allows newcomers to rebuild their careers and contribute fully.
records.zomi: Gamdang pan lai sinna te kipom in a hong tung thak te in a nasep uh a bawl kik theih nadingin leh a bup-in a huh theih nadingin a pia hi.

records.english: Where did your family go when the fire destroyed your house?
records.zomi: Mei in na inn a susiat ciangin na innkuan koi-ah a pai uh hiam?

records.english: The council put us in a hotel for a month, and the church collected clothes and furniture for us.
records.zomi: Council in kha khat sung zinbuuk khat-ah hong koih a, biakinn in puan leh innsung van te hong kaikhawm sak hi.

records.english: Support for families after a death or illness can help children stay in school and keep their hopes alive.
records.zomi: Sihna ahih kei leh natna khit-in innkuan te huh in naupangte sang-ah a om den nadingin leh a lametna uh nungta den nadingin a huh thei hi.

records.english: Retraining schemes give workers a second chance when industries close.
records.zomi: Kisin kikna ngimna te in sepna nasep te a kikhak ciangin nasemte theihna nihna a pia hi.

records.english: Volunteers at the debt advice service helped my parents agree a payment plan with the bank.
records.zomi: Leiba thuhilhna nasep-a thalawp te in ka nu leh pa bank tawh sum pia dan ngimna khat a kilungkim nadingin a huh uh hi.

records.english: How did you manage when your benefits were delayed for weeks?
records.zomi: Na huhna sum kal tampi sung a nunung ciangin bangci na om hiam?

records.english: The food bank helped us through, and an advice worker sorted out the problem with the office.
records.zomi: An piakna mun in hong huh a, thuhilhna nasempa khat in office tawh buaina a bawlphat hi.

records.english: Help that arrives quickly after a disaster can prevent a temporary crisis from becoming a permanent one.
records.zomi: Siatna lian khit-a manlang taka hong tung huhna in hun tomkhat buaina khat a tawntung-a suah lohna a kham thei hi.

records.english: Why do some people wait so long before asking public services for help?
records.zomi: Bang hangin mi khenkhat in mipi nasep te kiangah huhna a ngen ma-un sawt mahmah a ngak uh hiam?

records.english: Could the advice centre help me write to the council about the delay in my housing repair?
records.zomi: Ka inn bawlphatna a nunung tawh kisai council kiangah lai ka gelh nadingin thuhilhna mun in hong huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Overcoming hardship is easier when services treat people with respect rather than suspicion.
records.zomi: Nasep te in mite lungmuanlohna sangin zahtakna tawh a kem ciangin haksatna zawh a baih zaw hi.

records.english: How did you find somewhere to live after the eviction?
records.zomi: Inn pan na kihawlkhiat khit-in tenna mun bangci na mu hiam?

records.english: The housing advice centre found us a temporary flat, and they helped us apply for something permanent.
records.zomi: Inn thuhilhna mun in hun tomkhat inn khat hong zong sak a, a tawntung adingin ngetna hong huh hi.

records.english: Can the library really help me find a job?
records.zomi: Laibu inn in nasep ka muh nadingin hong huh thei taktak ding hiam?

records.english: The advice centre sorted out our debts.
records.zomi: Thuhilhna mun in i leiba te a bawlphat sak hi.

records.english: The domestic abuse service found my friend a safe place to live and helped her start again.
records.zomi: Inn sung-a gimbawlna huhna nasep in ka lawm tenna mun bit khat a zong sak a, a kipan kik nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Public services and charities often make the difference between a family sinking and recovering.
records.zomi: Mipi nasep te leh huhna pawl te in innkuan khat a kiak leh a dam kik kikal-ah a khenna a bawl zel uh hi.

records.english: The volunteers cleared our flooded kitchen.
records.zomi: Thalawp te in i an huanna inn tui a lut a sianghsak uh hi.

records.english: Stories of people who have overcome difficulties with community support can encourage others to seek help.
records.zomi: Khuasung huhna tawh haksatna a zo mite' tangthu te in midangte huhna a zon nadingin a hanthawn thei hi.

records.english: Can the advice centre help with my rent?
records.zomi: Thuhilhna mun in ka inn man adingin hong huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Volunteers who have faced difficulties themselves are often the most understanding helpers.
records.zomi: Amau' mahmah-in haksatna a thuak ngei thalawp te pen huhmite lak-ah a theisiam pen zel uh hi.

records.english: A charity paid for my daughter's school uniform when we couldn't afford it.
records.zomi: I pia zawh loh ciangin huhna pawl khat in ka tanu' sang puan man a pia hi.

records.english: The police helped me get my documents back.
records.zomi: Palik in ka laigelh te ka ngah kik nadingin hong huh hi.

records.english: After the storm damaged our roof, the council's emergency team covered it with a tarpaulin within hours.
records.zomi: Huihpi in i inntung a susiat khit-in council' lauhuai hun pawl in hun tawmno sungin plastic puan tawh a khuh hi.

records.english: My grandmother learned to apply for her pension online at a free class in the library.
records.zomi: Ka pi in laibu inn-a sinna man om lo khat-ah online tawh a pension ngen dan a sin hi.

records.english: We still use the carved wooden spoon that has been passed down through four generations.
records.zomi: Suan li sung a kikhah suk sing tawh kibawl keu kizem pen i zang lai hi.

records.english: When do we sing the harvest song?
records.zomi: Buh lak la ciang-in i sa hiam?

records.english: Grandma, will you teach me the song you sing at harvest time?
records.zomi: Pi aw, buh lak hun-in na sak la hong hilh ding na hiam?

records.english: Yes, and when you know it, you can teach it to your own children one day.
records.zomi: Ka hilh ding hi, na theih khit-in ni khat-in na tate kiangah na hilh thei ding hi.

records.english: How did your family keep our traditions alive after moving to the city?
records.zomi: Khuapi-ah na pem khit uh-in na innkuan in i ngeina te bangci a nungta sak den uh hiam?

records.english: We spoke our language at home, kept our festivals and visited the village every year.
records.zomi: Inn-ah i pau i ham a, i pawi te i kem a, kum simin khua i kan hi.

records.english: My mother still cooks with the old pots.
records.zomi: Ka nu in beel lui te tawh an a huan lai hi.

records.english: Teaching children why a tradition matters helps them keep it even when no adult is watching.
records.zomi: Naupangte bang hangin ngeina khat a thupi hiam cih hilh in upa kuamah a en kei hangin a kem den nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Our family keeps a list of our ancestors.
records.zomi: I innkuan in i pu leh pa te' lista khat a kem hi.

records.english: For my family, cultural continuity means passing on not only customs but the values behind them.
records.zomi: Ka innkuan adingin ngeina zom den pen ngeina te bek hi lo-in a nung-a manphatna te zong khah suk cihna ahi hi.

records.english: My cousin is learning the old weaving patterns.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam in puan khui dan lui te a sin hi.

records.english: My father taught me to greet elders in the traditional way, and I've taught my son the same.
records.zomi: Ka pa in upa te ngeina lui-in cibai dingin hong hilh a, ka tapa zong tua bangin ka hilh hi.

records.english: My cousins abroad video-call us during the festival so that they can sing the old songs with us.
records.zomi: Gamdang-a ka sanggam te in la lui te i tawh a sak khawm theih nadingin pawi laitakin video tawh hong sam uh hi.

records.english: Our children learn the proverbs at Sunday school.
records.zomi: I tate in Nipini sang-ah paunak te a sin uh hi.

records.english: Our family has adapted some customs to city life, but we still keep their meaning.
records.zomi: I innkuan in ngeina khenkhat khuapi nuntakna tawh a kituak dingin a khek a, ahi zongin a cihna i kem lai hi.

records.english: We greet our elders with a bow.
records.zomi: I upa te kun-in cibai i bawl hi.

records.english: We wear our traditional clothes at weddings.
records.zomi: Mopawi te-ah i ngeina puan i silh hi.

records.english: Mum, why do you still make rice cakes the old way?
records.zomi: Nu aw, bang hangin buh moh ngeina lui-in na bawl lai hiam?

records.english: Your grandmother taught me, and I want you to taste what she made.
records.zomi: Na pi in hong hilh a, a bawl bangin na ne nadingin ka deih hi.

records.english: Are we visiting the village at New Year?
records.zomi: Kum thak-in khua i kan ding hiam?

records.english: Where does Grandma keep the family recipe book?
records.zomi: Pi in innkuan an huan dan laibu koi-ah a kem hiam?

records.english: Will Dad teach us the old songs this weekend?
records.zomi: Hih kal tawp-in Pa in la lui te hong hilh ding hiam?

records.english: My mother says that our traditions survive because each generation chooses to keep them, not because they must.
records.zomi: I ngeina te pen a kisam ahih manin hi lo-in suan khatciat in kem dingin a teel uh ahih manin a nungta lai hi, ci-in ka nu in a gen hi.

records.english: Why do you want our children to learn the old proverbs when they hardly use them?
records.zomi: I tate in a zang kei hamtang uh hangin bang hangin paunak lui te sin dingin na deih hiam?

records.english: Because the proverbs carry the wisdom of our grandparents, and one day the children will understand them.
records.zomi: Bang hang hiam cih leh paunak te in i pu leh pi te' pilna a pua a, ni khat-in naupangte in a theisiam ding uh hi.

records.english: My brother recorded Grandpa's stories on his phone.
records.zomi: Ka sanggampa in Pu' tangthu te a phone tawh a ciamteh hi.

records.english: Why do we take off our shoes at Grandpa's house?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pu' inn-ah i khedap i suah hiam?

records.english: My grandmother says that a family which forgets its stories forgets who it is.
records.zomi: A tangthu te a mangngilh innkuan khat in amah a kua hiam cih a mangngilh hi, ci-in ka pi in a gen hi.

records.english: Grandma taught me to fold the festival cloth.
records.zomi: Pi in pawi puan zial dan hong hilh hi.

records.english: When the youngest members of my family learn the old songs, the elders feel that their lives have been worth it.
records.zomi: Ka innkuan-a a naupang pen te in la lui te a sin uh ciangin upa te in a nuntakna uh a manpha hi, ci-in a kizak uh hi.

records.english: My grandparents believe that our language is the thread that ties every generation together.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh pi te in i pau pen suan khempeuh a gawm khawm khau ahi hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: In my family, festivals are the moments when old and young remember together where we come from.
records.zomi: Ka innkuan-ah pawi te pen upa leh naupang in koi pan i hong pai hiam cih a phawk khawm uh hun te ahi hi.

records.english: Do we still have to speak our language at dinner?
records.zomi: Nitak an ne laitakin i pau i ham lai ding a kisam hiam?

records.english: Grandpa tells us stories about our clan.
records.zomi: Pu in i phung tawh kisai tangthu hong gen hi.

records.english: We share our food with the neighbours at festivals.
records.zomi: Pawi te-ah i an inn kiang mite tawh i hawm hi.

records.english: We pray in our own language at home.
records.zomi: Inn-ah eimau' pau tawh thu i ngen hi.

records.english: My mother worries that busy modern lives leave little time for the old ways, so she makes time for them deliberately.
records.zomi: Tu hun-a nuntakna buai te in ngeina lui te adingin hun tawmno bek a nusia ding hi, ci-in ka nu in a lungkham a, tua ahih manin amaute adingin a ngim takin hun a koih hi.

records.english: My parents insist that we speak our language at home, even though we use another at school.
records.zomi: Sang-ah pau dang i zat hangin inn-ah i pau i ham dingin ka nu leh pa in a ngen den uh hi.

records.english: Every time a baby is born in our family, Grandma blesses it with the same words her mother used.
records.zomi: I innkuan-ah naupang khat a suah simin Pi in a nu in a zat kammal kibang tawh thupha a pia hi.

records.english: Is it possible to keep our traditions alive if our grandchildren grow up speaking another language?
records.zomi: I tu te pau dang ham-in a khang uh leh i ngeina te nungta sak den thei ahi hiam?

records.english: My son was proud when he could finally tell our family's story in our own language.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in eimau' pau tawh i innkuan tangthu a gen thei ciangin a kipak hi.

records.english: My grandfather wrote down the names of every ancestor he could remember, so that we would never forget them.
records.zomi: Ka pu in i mangngilh ngei loh nadingin a phawk theih pu leh pa khempeuh' min a gelh hi.

records.english: My father says that each generation must decide which customs to keep and how to keep them alive.
records.zomi: Suan khatciat in bang ngeina te kem ding a, bangci nungta sak ding hiam cih a thukhen ding uh hi, ci-in ka pa in a gen hi.

records.english: When my grandfather died, we followed the customs he had taught us, and it comforted the whole family.
records.zomi: Ka pu a sih ciangin hong hilh ngeina te i zui a, tua in innkuan buppi a lungmuang sak hi.

records.english: Every year before our family festival, my grandmother gathers the girls to prepare the traditional dishes.
records.zomi: Kum simin i innkuan pawi ma-in ka pi in ngeina an te bawl dingin nungak te a kaikhawm hi.

records.english: She tells the same stories while we cook, about the village where she learned each recipe from her own mother.
records.zomi: An i huan laitakin a nu pan an huan dan khatciat a sinna khua tawh kisai tangthu kibang te a gen hi.

records.english: This year, my little cousin repeated one of the stories word for word, and my grandmother's eyes filled with tears.
records.zomi: Hih kum-in ka sanggam neu in tangthu khat kammal khatciat a gen kik a, ka pi' mit-ah mittui a dim hi.

records.english: Can Uncle play the traditional drum at the wedding?
records.zomi: Mopawi-ah Pa neu in ngeina khuang a tum thei ding hiam?

records.english: Keeping our culture alive abroad has made my family more aware of how precious it is.
records.zomi: Gamdang-ah i ngeina nungta sak in ka innkuan in bangzah a manpha hiam cih a phawk zaw sak hi.

records.english: Why does Grandma wear her beads every day?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pi in ni simin a khi a bulh hiam?

records.english: Some of our traditions have changed shape over the years, yet my family still recognises them as our own.
records.zomi: I ngeina khenkhat kum tampi sung a lim a kikhek hangin ka innkuan in eimau' ta hi-in a thei lai hi.

records.english: My aunt runs a small class where children learn the songs our grandparents sang in the fields.
records.zomi: Ka ni in naupangte in i pu leh pi te in lo-ah a sak la te a sin nadingin sinna neu khat a bawl hi.

records.english: The stories my grandmother tells while we cook have become as important to me as the recipes themselves.
records.zomi: An i huan laitakin ka pi' gen tangthu te in an huan dan te bangin keimah adingin a thupi hi.

records.english: We name our babies after grandparents.
records.zomi: I naupang neu te pu leh pi te' min tawh i phuak hi.

records.english: Who teaches the children the old dances now?
records.zomi: Tu-in naupangte lamna lui te kua in a hilh hiam?

records.english: Our family festival brings relatives from three countries to the same table every year.
records.zomi: I innkuan pawi in kum simin gam thum pan sanggam te an dawhkan kibang-ah a kaikhawm hi.

records.english: Why does Grandma insist that the youngest child serves the eldest guest first?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pi in a naupang pen in khualmi a upa pen a masa-in a ne sak ding hi, ci-in a ngen den hiam?

records.english: Why do we always eat together on Sunday evenings?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Nipini nitak simin an i ne khawm den hiam?

records.english: Because my parents did it, and their parents before them, and it keeps the family close.
records.zomi: Bang hang hiam cih leh ka nu leh pa in a bawl uh a, amaute ma-in a nu leh pa uh in a bawl uh a, tua in innkuan a kinai sak hi.

records.english: When my sister married, she wore our grandmother's shawl to keep a link with the family's past.
records.zomi: Ka sanggamnu a kiten ciangin innkuan' hun bei tawh kizopna a kem nadingin ka pi' ngeina puan a silh hi.

records.english: When my daughter asked how God could be three and one, my husband poured water into a glass, froze some into ice and boiled some into steam.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in Pasian thum leh khat bangci a hi thei hiam, ci-in a dot ciangin ka pasal in haai khat sungah tui a sung a, a khenkhat tuikhal-ah a khal sak a, a khenkhat tui huih-ah a tuang sak hi.

records.english: Then he admitted that the picture wasn't perfect, because God isn't one thing changing shape.
records.zomi: Tua khit-in Pasian pen a lim kikhek na khat hi lo ahih manin tua lim a kicing kei hi, ci-in a pom hi.

records.english: My daughter thought for a moment and said that maybe some things about God are too big for pictures.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in tomkhat a ngaihsun a, Pasian tawh kisai na khenkhat lim adingin a lian lua thei hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Explaining the Trinity to children requires simple words that do not pretend the mystery is easy.
records.zomi: Naupangte kiangah Trinity gen in thuguk pen a baih hi, ci-in a kikhem lo kammal baih te a kisam hi.

records.english: My grandmother prays to Jesus by name.
records.zomi: Ka pi in Jesu' min lo-in thu a ngen hi.

records.english: Why does our pastor say the Trinity is a mystery?
records.zomi: Bang hangin i pastor in Trinity pen thuguk khat ahi hi, a ci hiam?

records.english: Because Christians believe it is true, but they admit that human minds can't fully explain it.
records.zomi: Bang hang hiam cih leh Khazih mite in a dik hi, ci-in a um uh a, ahi zongin mihing' lungsim in a bup-in a gen thei kei hi, ci-in a pom uh hi.

records.english: My grandmother says that she prays to the Father, thanks the Son and asks the Spirit to guide her.
records.zomi: Pa kiangah thu ka ngen a, Tapa kiangah lungdam ka ko a, Kha in hong pi dingin ka ngen hi, ci-in ka pi in a gen hi.

records.english: Is the Holy Spirit really God, Grandma?
records.zomi: Pi aw, Kha Siangtho pen Pasian ahi taktak hiam?

records.english: My grandfather says that the Trinity shows that God is not lonely but lives in perfect love.
records.zomi: Trinity in Pasian pen a khat bek-a om hi lo-in itna kicing sungah a nungta hi, cih a lak hi, ci-in ka pu in a gen hi.

records.english: Mum says the Spirit is like the wind.
records.zomi: Kha pen huih bang ahi hi, ci-in ka nu in a gen hi.

records.english: My father admits that he doesn't fully understand the Trinity, but he says his faith doesn't depend on that.
records.zomi: Ka pa in Trinity a bup-in a theisiam kei hi, ci-in a pom a, ahi zongin a upna tua tungah a kinga kei hi, a ci hi.

records.english: We read about Pentecost at breakfast this morning.
records.zomi: Tu zingsang an ne laitakin Pentecost tawh kisai i sim hi.

records.english: For my family, the Trinity is less a puzzle to solve than a reason to worship God with wonder.
records.zomi: Ka innkuan adingin Trinity pen phel ding lungsim sitna khat sangin lamdang sakna tawh Pasian biak nading hangsan khat ahi zaw hi.

records.english: Our church sings a hymn about the Trinity.
records.zomi: I pawlpi in Trinity tawh kisai Pasian phatna la khat a sa hi.

records.english: Is the Holy Spirit a person?
records.zomi: Kha Siangtho pen mi khat ahi hiam?

records.english: Mum, why do we say the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit when we pray?
records.zomi: Nu aw, bang hangin thu i ngen ciangin Pa, Tapa leh Kha Siangtho i ci hiam?

records.english: Because Christians believe God is one God in three persons, and we name all three.
records.zomi: Bang hang hiam cih leh Khazih mite in Pasian pen mi thum-a Pasian khat ahi hi, ci-in a um uh a, a thum khempeuh i min lo hi.

records.english: My father reminds us that Christians believe in one God, even though they speak of three persons.
records.zomi: Khazih mite in mi thum thu a gen uh hangin Pasian khat a um uh hi, ci-in ka pa in hong phawk sak hi.

records.english: My aunt hums the same Pentecost hymn while she cooks.
records.zomi: Ka ni in an a huan laitakin Pentecost Pasian phatna la kibang a hum hi.

records.english: My little brother asked whether Jesus prayed to himself, which led to a long conversation at dinner.
records.zomi: Ka nau pasal neu in Jesu in amah leh amah kiangah thu a ngen hiam, ci-in a dong a, tua in nitak an ne laitakin kikupna sau khat-ah a pi hi.

records.english: My son asked if the Holy Spirit is a ghost.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in Kha Siangtho pen kha-mang ahi hiam, ci-in a dong hi.

records.english: When my son was baptised, the pastor used the names of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit.
records.zomi: Ka tapa a kibaptaiz ciangin pastor in Pa, Tapa leh Kha Siangtho' min a zang hi.

records.english: My father explains the Trinity with a triangle.
records.zomi: Ka pa in Trinity pen lim gil thum tawh a gen hi.

records.english: Our family Bible has a picture of three linked rings on its cover, which my children love to trace.
records.zomi: I innkuan Lai Siangtho' a tung khuh-ah kual thum kizom lim khat a om a, ka tate in a zui-in suai a nuam sa uh hi.

records.english: My cousin's friend, who is Muslim, asked her about the Trinity, and they had a respectful conversation.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam' lawm Muslim khat in Trinity tawh kisai a dong a, zahtak takin a kikum uh hi.

records.english: My grandmother believes that God's love within the Trinity is the pattern for love within families.
records.zomi: Trinity sung-a Pasian' itna pen innkuan sung-a itna' a ettehna ahi hi, ci-in ka pi in a um hi.

records.english: Do we pray to the Father or to Jesus?
records.zomi: Pa kiangah thu i ngen ding hiam, Jesu kiangah thu i ngen ding hiam?

records.english: At Christmas, my mother reminded us that Christians believe the Son existed before he was born as a baby.
records.zomi: Christmas-in ka nu in Khazih mite in Tapa pen naupang neu-in a suah ma-in a om khin hi, ci-in a um uh hi, ci-in hong phawk sak hi.

records.english: Many Christians say that they experience the Trinity in prayer before they can explain it in words.
records.zomi: Khazih mite tampi in kammal tawh a gen theih ma-un thu ngetna sungah Trinity a thei uh hi, ci-in a gen uh hi.

records.english: The early church spent many years finding words for the Trinity, and believers still find those words helpful today.
records.zomi: Pawlpi masa in Trinity adingin kammal zong-in kum tampi a zang a, tu-in upmite in tua kammal te a phattuam sa lai uh hi.

records.english: Grandma makes the sign of the cross.
records.zomi: Pi in singlamteh limtak a bawl hi.

records.english: Can a child understand the Trinity?
records.zomi: Naupang khat in Trinity a theisiam thei hiam?

records.english: Our pastor preached on Trinity Sunday.
records.zomi: I pastor in Trinity Nipini-in thu a gen hi.

records.english: Why do Christians call Jesus the Son of God?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Khazih mite in Jesu Pasian Tapa a ci uh hiam?

records.english: My mother finds it comforting that the Spirit, as Christians believe, lives within every believer.
records.zomi: Khazih mite' upna bangin Kha in upmi khempeuh sungah a teng hi, cih ka nu in a lungmuan huai sa hi.

records.english: Is Jesus God or God's son?
records.zomi: Jesu pen Pasian ahi hiam, Pasian' Tapa ahi hiam?

records.english: Christians believe he is both, the Son of God and fully God himself.
records.zomi: Khazih mite in a nih tuak ahi hi, Pasian Tapa leh a bup-in Pasian mahmah ahi hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: Grandpa, are there three gods?
records.zomi: Pu aw, Pasian thum a om hiam?

records.english: No, Christians believe in one God, who exists as Father, Son and Holy Spirit.
records.zomi: Om kei hi, Khazih mite in Pa, Tapa leh Kha Siangtho-in a om Pasian khat a um uh hi.

records.english: My father says that the Trinity reminds him that God is both beyond us and close to us.
records.zomi: Trinity in Pasian pen eite tungah a sang a, eite kiangah zong a nai hi, cih hong phawk sak hi, ci-in ka pa in a gen hi.

records.english: Our family discussed why many teachers warn that every picture of the Trinity falls short.
records.zomi: Bang hangin saya tampi in Trinity' lim khatpeuh a kicing kei hi, ci-in a vaukhak uh hiam cih i innkuan in i kikum hi.

records.english: We learned about the Trinity at Sunday school.
records.zomi: Nipini sang-ah Trinity tawh kisai i sin hi.

records.english: Is Jesus older than his mother?
records.zomi: Jesu pen a nu sangin a upa zaw hiam?

records.english: Why do some Christians compare the Trinity to a family bound together by love?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Khazih mite khenkhat in Trinity itna tawh a kigawm innkuan khat tawh a khaikhin uh hiam?

records.english: Christians often admit that the Trinity stretches human understanding, while still believing it to be true.
records.zomi: Khazih mite in Trinity in mihing' theisiamna a sau sak hi, ci-in a pom zel uh a, a dik hi, ci-in a um lai uh hi.

records.english: Did Jesus pray to the Father when he was on earth?
records.zomi: Leitung-ah a om laitakin Jesu in Pa kiangah thu a ngen hiam?

records.english: We say a blessing before every meal.
records.zomi: An ne khatciat ma-in thupha ngetna i bawl hi.

records.english: Our Bible study read the story of Jesus' baptism, where the Father speaks and the Spirit comes like a dove.
records.zomi: I Lai Siangtho sinna in Jesu' kibaptaizna tangthu, Pa' aw a ging a, Kha vakhu bangin hong kum suk tangthu a sim uh hi.

records.english: In our home, the blessing in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit marks the end of every family prayer.
records.zomi: I inn-ah Pa, Tapa leh Kha Siangtho' min tawh thupha ngetna in innkuan thu ngetna khatciat' a tawpna a lak hi.

records.english: My parents taught us that respectful conversations about the Trinity are possible with people of other faiths.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh pa in upna dang nei mite tawh Trinity tawh kisai zahtak taka kikupna a om thei hi, ci-in hong hilh uh hi.

records.english: Christian teaching insists that the Father, the Son and the Spirit are distinct, yet they are one God.
records.zomi: Khazih mite' hilhna in Pa, Tapa leh Kha a kibang lo hangin Pasian khat ahi uh hi, ci-in a ngen den hi.

records.english: Does the Holy Spirit help us pray?
records.zomi: Kha Siangtho in thu i ngen nadingin hong huh hiam?
