records.zomi: Map tampi in mal lam a tung lam-ah a koih uh a, ahi zongin a cian nadingin a genna en in ahih kei leh a lam te en in.

records.english: Giving clear directions to others requires both map skills and the ability to describe landmarks.
records.zomi: Midangte kiangah lampi kician taka gen in map siamna leh theihna mun te gen theihna tuak a kisam hi.

records.english: How can I tell how steep a hill is from the map?
records.zomi: Map pan mual khat bangzah a ding hiam cih bangci ka thei thei ding hiam?

records.english: Look at the contour lines, because the closer together they are, the steeper the slope.
records.zomi: Sanna lam te en in, bang hang hiam cih leh a kinai semsem ciangin a ding semsem hi.

records.english: Where are we on the map now?
records.zomi: Tu-in map tungah koi-ah i om hiam?

records.english: Is the river north of the town?
records.zomi: Lui pen khuapi' mal lam-ah a om hiam?

records.english: What does a dotted line on the map usually mean?
records.zomi: Map tunga a kikhak lam in bang a cihna zel hiam?

records.english: It's often a footpath or a boundary, so look at the key to see which.
records.zomi: Kalsuan lampi ahih kei leh gamgi khat ahi zel a, tua ahih manin bang ahi hiam cih en nadingin a genna en in.

records.english: How can I find my way if my phone loses its signal in the countryside?
records.zomi: Khuaneu-ah ka phone in signal a mansuah leh ka lampi bangci ka mu thei ding hiam?

records.english: What does this blue line mean?
records.zomi: Hih lam dum in bang a cihna hiam?

records.english: Where is the key on this map?
records.zomi: Hih map tunga a genna koi-ah a om hiam?

records.english: Why do maps of the whole world always look a little wrong?
records.zomi: Bang hangin leitung buppi' map te a khial deuh bangin a kilang den hiam?

records.english: Because a round Earth has to be stretched to fit on flat paper, so some areas look bigger or smaller than they really are.
records.zomi: Bang hang hiam cih leh a kual leitung pen lai phiat tungah a kituak nadingin a kidawh ding a kisam a, tua ahih manin mun khenkhat a lianna taktak sangin a lian zaw ahih kei leh a neu zaw bangin a kilang hi.

records.english: How many centimetres is the park from the school on the map?
records.zomi: Map tungah park pen sang pan centimetre bangzah a gamla hiam?

records.english: How do mapmakers decide which places are important enough to show?
records.zomi: Map bawlmite in bang mun te lak ding dingin a thupi hiam cih bangci a thukhen uh hiam?

records.english: How many kilometres is it to the lake?
records.zomi: Dil kiang dong kilometre bangzah a gamla hiam?

records.english: What does a green patch show?
records.zomi: Mun eng khat in bang a lak hiam?

records.english: Can I fold the map like this?
records.zomi: Hih bangin map ka zial thei ding hiam?

records.english: Why are there different kinds of maps for walkers and for drivers?
records.zomi: Bang hangin kalsuan mite leh mawtaw mawngmite adingin map tuamtuam a om hiam?

records.english: Why do maps of the same area sometimes use different names for places?
records.zomi: Bang hangin mun kibang' map te in mun te adingin min tuam a zang zel hiam?

records.english: Teachers often answer questions about directions by sending pupils outside with a map and a compass.
records.zomi: Saya te in lampi tawh kisai dotna te sangnaupangte map leh compass tawh pua-ah sawl in a dawng zel uh hi.

records.english: How do I turn the map so that it matches the land around me?
records.zomi: Ka kiim-a leitang tawh a kituak nadingin map bangci ka hei ding hiam?

records.english: Is the sea to the east of the village on this map?
records.zomi: Hih map tungah tuipi pen khua' ni suahna lam-ah a om hiam?

records.english: Why do some maps show the height of the land with colours instead of contour lines?
records.zomi: Bang hangin map khenkhat in sanna lam te sangin pianzia tawh leitang sanna a lak hiam?

records.english: How can I give directions to someone who can't read a map?
records.zomi: Map sim thei lo mi khat kiangah lampi bangci ka gen thei ding hiam?

records.english: Why do some cities use a grid of streets while others have winding roads?
records.zomi: Bang hangin khuapi khenkhat in lampi zang kikhen a zang a, a dangte in lampi kawikawi a nei uh hiam?

records.english: What does the little tent symbol mean?
records.zomi: Puanbuuk lim tangna neu in bang a cihna hiam?

records.english: How can I estimate how long a walk will take from the map?
records.zomi: Kalsuanna khat in hun bangzah a la ding hiam cih map pan bangci ka tuat thei ding hiam?

records.english: Every world map distorts something, which is a useful lesson in how information is presented.
records.zomi: Leitung map khatciat in na khat a khial sak zel a, tua pen thu te bangci a kilak hiam cih sinna manpha khat ahi hi.

records.english: Why might an old map show roads that no longer exist?
records.zomi: Bang hangin map lui khat in om nawn lo lampi te a lak thei hiam?

records.english: Can I use a ruler to measure the route?
records.zomi: Lampi teh nadingin tehna sau ka zang thei ding hiam?

records.english: Which road goes to the station?
records.zomi: Bang lampi in station-ah a pai hiam?

records.english: On our school orienteering day, my partner and I were sure we had found the third checkpoint.
records.zomi: I sang' orienteering ni-in ka pih leh kei in a thumna khawlna mun i mu khin hi, ci-in i um cian hi.

records.english: When we checked the map again, we realised we had followed the wrong stream for almost a kilometre.
records.zomi: Map i en kik ciangin kilometre khat bang tuikuang khial khat i zui hi, cih i theisiam hi.

records.english: We worked our way back using the contour lines and still finished, though we were the last team in.
records.zomi: Sanna lam te zang-in i ciah kik a, i zo lai hi, ahi zongin pawl nunung pen i hi hi.

records.english: What's the difference between a map and a plan of a building?
records.zomi: Map leh inn khat' lim kikal-ah bang a kibang lo hiam?

records.english: Questions about contour lines help students imagine the shape of the land from a flat piece of paper.
records.zomi: Sanna lam te tawh kisai dotna te in sangnaupangte lai phiat pan leitang' lim a ngaihsut theih nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Can I draw my own map of the garden?
records.zomi: Huan' map ka mah-in ka suai thei ding hiam?

records.english: How do I use grid references to describe exactly where something is?
records.zomi: Na khat a om mun kician takin gen nadingin grid reference te bangci ka zang ding hiam?

records.english: Why are satellite photos sometimes easier to understand than maps?
records.zomi: Bang hangin satellite photo te map te sangin theisiam a baih zaw zel hiam?

records.english: Do I hold the compass flat?
records.zomi: Compass ka len phiat ding hiam?

records.english: Is this map up to date?
records.zomi: Hih map a thak lai hiam?

records.english: Which direction does the sun set?
records.zomi: Ni bang lam-ah a tum hiam?

records.english: Questions about why certain places appear on maps lead to discussions about who decides what is important.
records.zomi: Bang hangin mun khenkhat map tungah a kilang hiam cih dotna te in kua in bang a thupi hiam cih a thukhen hiam cih kikupna-ah a pi hi.

records.english: How can I work out the real distance if the map has a scale of one to fifty thousand?
records.zomi: Map in sang nga sawm-a khat tehna a neih leh gamlatna taktak bangci ka tuat thei ding hiam?

records.english: Can I use my phone instead of a paper map on the field trip?
records.zomi: Pua-a sinna khualzinna-ah lai map sangin ka phone ka zang thei ding hiam?

records.english: Bring both, because there may be no signal in the hills.
records.zomi: A nih tuak paipih in, bang hang hiam cih leh mual te-ah signal a om kei thei hi.

records.english: What does the letter P mean on the map?
records.zomi: Map tungah P laimal in bang a cihna hiam?

records.english: A pupil who can read a map well is less likely to become lost and more likely to explore with curiosity.
records.zomi: Map hoih taka a sim thei sangnaupang khat in lampi a mansuah kha tawm a, theih nopna tawh a kan zaw hi.

records.english: Pupils who ask how maps represent the real world are learning an important skill for travel and everyday life.
records.zomi: Map te in leitung taktak bangci a lak hiam cih a dong sangnaupangte in khualzinna leh ni sim nuntakna adingin siamna thupi khat a sin uh hi.

records.english: Is the school marked on the map?
records.zomi: Sang pen map tungah a kiciamteh hiam?

records.english: Comparing old and new maps shows pupils how towns and landscapes change over time.
records.zomi: Map lui leh thak te khaikhin in sangnaupangte khuapi leh gam te hun sungin bangci a kikhek hiam cih a lak hi.

records.english: The government pays for our school books.
records.zomi: Ukpi in i sang laibu te man a pia hi.

records.english: When our town's main employer closed, the government funded a training centre in the old factory office.
records.zomi: I khuapi' nasep pia lian pen a kikhak ciangin ukpi in sepna inn lui' office-ah kisinna inn khat a bawl sak hi.

records.english: My uncle, who had worked there for twenty years, learned to repair solar panels on a six-month course.
records.zomi: Tua mun-ah kum sawmnih sung nasep a sem ka pa neu in kha guk sinna khat-ah solar panel bawlphat dan a sin hi.

records.english: Now he runs a small team that installs panels on schools and homes across the region.
records.zomi: Tu-in gam khen buppi-a sang te leh inn te tungah panel a koih nasem pawl neu khat a makai hi.

records.english: Understanding how governments spend money helps students take part in debates about public policy.
records.zomi: Ukpi te in sum bangci a zang uh hiam cih theisiam in sangnaupangte mipi ngimna tawh kisai kinialna te-ah a kihel nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: The teachers' union argued that spending on schools had not kept up with rising prices.
records.zomi: Saya te' pawl in sang te-a sum zat pen man khan te tawh a kizui kei hi, ci-in a gen hi.

records.english: Is it fair that some regions receive more government spending per person than others?
records.zomi: Gam khen khenkhat in a dangte sangin mi khat simin ukpi sum zat tam zaw a ngah uh pen a dik hiam?

records.english: Research paid for with public money can benefit society in ways that private companies might not pursue.
records.zomi: Mipi sum tawh kibawl sui-sinna in company tuam te in a zon loh ding lampi te-ah khuasung mite a phattuam sak thei hi.

records.english: Public spending on transport made it possible for me to commute to the college in town.
records.zomi: Lampi pai nading mipi sum zat in khuapi-a college-ah ni simin ka pai theih nadingin a bawl hi.

records.english: How can students find out whether government spending on education has really increased?
records.zomi: Ukpi' sinna tunga sum zat a khang taktak hiam cih sangnaupangte in bangci a thei thei uh hiam?

records.english: Compare the official figures over several years and take rising prices into account, not just the headline numbers.
records.zomi: Kum tampi sung-a nambat tak te khaikhin in, nambat lian bek hi lo-in man khan te zong ngaihsun in.

records.english: Grants for new businesses can help create jobs in areas where traditional industries have closed.
records.zomi: Sumbawlna thak adingin huhna sum te in ngeina sepna nasep a kikhak mun te-ah nasep a bawl thei hi.

records.english: Is university free in your country?
records.zomi: Na gam-ah university pen a man om lo hiam?

records.english: Training schemes funded by the government can help workers adapt when the economy changes.
records.zomi: Ukpi' sum piak kisinna ngimna te in sum leh van a kikhek ciangin nasemte a kituak theih nadingin a huh thei hi.

records.english: The government spends a lot on roads.
records.zomi: Ukpi in lampi te-ah sum tampi a zang hi.

records.english: Public money built our new college.
records.zomi: Mipi sum in i college thak a lam hi.

records.english: The government supports small businesses.
records.zomi: Ukpi in sumbawlna neu te a huh hi.

records.english: My apprenticeship is partly paid by the state.
records.zomi: Ka nasep sinna khenkhat pen gam ukpi in a pia hi.

records.english: Who pays for free school lunches?
records.zomi: Sang-a sun an man om lo te kua in a pia hiam?

records.english: Why did our company receive a government grant for new machines?
records.zomi: Bang hangin i company in khawl thak te adingin ukpi huhna sum khat a ngah hiam?

records.english: The government wanted factories to use less energy, so it paid part of the cost of greener equipment.
records.zomi: Ukpi in sepna inn te in tha tawm zaw zat a deih ahih manin leitung kem zaw van te' man khenkhat a pia hi.

records.english: Workers at the job centre explained which government schemes could pay for my driving lessons.
records.zomi: Nasep zonna office-a nasemte in ukpi' ngimna bang in ka mawtaw mawng sinna man a pia thei hiam cih a gen uh hi.

records.english: Our hospital got new money this year.
records.zomi: I damlo inn in hih kum-in sum thak a ngah hi.

records.english: Did the class discover that every spending decision means choosing what not to fund?
records.zomi: Sum zat thukhensatna khatciat in bang piak lo ding hiam cih teelna ahi hi, cih sinna in a mu hiam?

records.english: Our economics class compared how much different countries spend on education and health.
records.zomi: I sum leh van sinna in gam tuamtuam in sinna leh cidamna-ah bangzah a zang uh hiam cih a khaikhin uh hi.

records.english: Why do governments sometimes spend more during a recession instead of saving money?
records.zomi: Bang hangin ukpi te in sum kem sangin sum leh van a niam hun-in sum tam zaw a zang zel uh hiam?

records.english: Are teachers paid by the government?
records.zomi: Saya te pen ukpi in khasum a pia hiam?

records.english: At state schools, yes, their salaries come from public spending on education.
records.zomi: Ukpi sang te-ah pia hi, a khasum uh sinna tunga mipi sum zat pan a hong pai hi.

records.english: Our school got a grant for new computers.
records.zomi: I sang in computer thak te adingin huhna sum khat a ngah hi.

records.english: Who pays for the police?
records.zomi: Palik te kua in a pia hiam?

records.english: Our tutor explained that government spending on research often leads to new jobs years later.
records.zomi: I saya in sui-sinna tunga ukpi' sum zat in kum tampi khit-in nasep thak te a piangsak zel hi, ci-in a gen hi.

records.english: Public funding for apprenticeships helps young people gain skills while earning a wage.
records.zomi: Nasep sinna adingin mipi sum piakna in tangvalte khasum a ngah laitak-un siamna a ngah nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: The government's grant for new businesses helped my cousin open a small bakery.
records.zomi: Sumbawlna thak adingin ukpi' huhna sum in ka sanggam moh bawlna inn neu khat a hong nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: The government pays for job training.
records.zomi: Ukpi in nasep kisinna man a pia hi.

records.english: Was your training course free?
records.zomi: Na kisinna pen a man om lo hiam?

records.english: The library is paid for by taxes.
records.zomi: Laibu inn pen siah tawh a kipia hi.

records.english: When government spending is cut, services for young people and students are often among the first to suffer.
records.zomi: Ukpi sum zat a kiat ciangin tangvalte leh sangnaupangte adingin nasep te pen a masa-in a thuak te lak-ah a kihel zel hi.

records.english: Spending on public transport makes it easier for students and workers to reach schools and jobs.
records.zomi: Mipi pai nading van tunga sum zat in sangnaupangte leh nasemte sang leh nasep a tun nadingin a baih sak hi.

records.english: Money spent on schools and colleges today shapes the skills of the workforce for decades.
records.zomi: Tuni-in sang leh college te tunga sum kizang in kum sawm tampi sung nasem pawl' siamna a bawl hi.

records.english: Does the council pay for the bus to the technical college?
records.zomi: Council in khut siamna college-ah pai nading bus man a pia hiam?

records.english: When spending on youth services was cut, our college lost its careers adviser.
records.zomi: Tangvalte nasep tunga sum zat a kiat ciangin i college in a nasep lamlak thuhilhpa a mansuah hi.

records.english: The hospital's new scanner was bought with money from the government's health budget.
records.zomi: Damlo inn' scanner thak pen ukpi' cidamna sum zat ngimna pan sum tawh a kilei hi.

records.english: Why does the government give money to universities?
records.zomi: Bang hangin ukpi in university te sum a pia hiam?

records.english: Because educated workers help the whole economy, so public money supports teaching and research.
records.zomi: Bang hang hiam cih leh pilna nei nasemte in sum leh van buppi a huh uh ahih manin mipi sum in hilhna leh sui-sinna a huh hi.

records.english: Students who study government spending learn that every budget reflects a set of priorities.
records.zomi: Ukpi sum zat a sin sangnaupangte in sum zat ngimna khatciat in a masa ding te a lak hi, cih a sin uh hi.

records.english: Teachers, nurses and police officers are among the many workers whose salaries depend on government budgets.
records.zomi: Saya te, nurse te leh palik te pen a khasum uh ukpi' sum zat ngimna tungah a kinga nasem tampi lak-ah a kihel uh hi.

records.english: The government funds my research project.
records.zomi: Ukpi in ka sui-sinna nasep man a pia hi.

records.english: Who pays for the training on my apprenticeship?
records.zomi: Ka nasep sinna-a kisinna man kua in a pia hiam?

records.english: In many countries, the government pays part of the cost and your employer pays the rest.
records.zomi: Gam tampi-ah ukpi in man khenkhat a pia a, na nasep nei in a dang a pia hi.

records.english: Why does the government spend so much on pensions compared with schools?
records.zomi: Bang hangin ukpi in sang te sangin pension-ah sum tampi a zang hiam?

records.english: The new science laboratories at our school were paid for by a national investment programme.
records.zomi: I sang-a pilna laboratory thak te pen gam buppi sum koihna ngimna khat in a pia hi.

records.english: Clear information about government spending helps citizens judge whether their taxes are being used well.
records.zomi: Ukpi sum zat tawh kisai thu cian in gam mite in a siah uh hoih takin a kizang hiam cih a khen theih nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Our factory got help to buy new machines.
records.zomi: I sepna inn in khawl thak te lei nadingin huhna a ngah hi.

records.english: My manager said that the company would hire more apprentices if the government increased its funding.
records.zomi: Ukpi in a sum piakna a behlap leh company in nasep sinmi tam zaw a la ding hi, ci-in ka manager in a gen hi.

records.english: Comparing spending figures over time requires care, because rising prices can make increases look larger than they are.
records.zomi: Hun sung-a sum zat nambat te khaikhin pen a kiphawk ding a kisam hi, bang hang hiam cih leh man khan te in khanna te a taktak sangin a lian zaw bangin a kilang sak thei hi.

records.english: My course is free for students under nineteen.
records.zomi: Ka sinna pen kum sawm leh kua nuai sangnaupangte adingin a man om lo hi.

records.english: Do nurses get paid by the government?
records.zomi: Nurse te ukpi in khasum a pia hiam?

records.english: Are museums free for students here?
records.zomi: Hih mun-ah sangnaupangte adingin museum te a man om lo hiam?

records.english: The government offers grants to students from low-income families to cover travel and books.
records.zomi: Ukpi in sum ngah tawm innkuan pan sangnaupangte adingin khualzinna leh laibu man adingin huhna sum a pia hi.

records.english: My scholarship comes from public funds.
records.zomi: Ka sangkah huhna sum pen mipi sum pan a hong pai hi.

records.english: Public services often meet people in distress first, so trained staff can make a vital difference.
records.zomi: Mipi nasep te in lungsim gimna a nei mite a masa-in a kimu zel ahih manin kisinna nei nasemte in na thupi mahmah a bawl thei uh hi.

records.english: Support in a crisis should continue afterwards, with follow-up from the right services.
records.zomi: Buaina lian khat sung-a huhna pen tua khit-in nasep dik te pan a zom en tawh a pai zom ding hi.

records.english: Outreach teams help people who might never walk into a clinic or an office by themselves.
records.zomi: Pua lam-a nasem pawl te in amau' mah-in damdawi inn neu ahih kei leh office-ah a lut ngei lo ding mite a huh uh hi.

records.english: Why do so many people feel unsure about how to help a stranger in distress?
records.zomi: Bang hangin mi tampi in lungsim gimna nei mi theih loh khat bangci huh ding hiam cih a kician kei uh hiam?

records.english: The shop assistant called an ambulance.
records.zomi: Van zuakna inn nasem in damlo mawtaw a sam hi.

records.english: Quiet rooms in public buildings give people in crisis a safe space away from crowds.
records.zomi: Mipi inn te-a inndan dai te in buaina lian-a om mite mipi pan gamla mun bit khat a pia hi.

records.english: The college's welfare team responded within minutes when a student was found crying in the library.
records.zomi: Laibu inn-ah sangnaupang khat a kap a kimuh ciangin college' kemna pawl in minute tawmno sungin a dawng uh hi.

records.english: The council's leaflet explains what to say and do if you find someone in crisis in a public place.
records.zomi: Council' laipek in mipi mun khat-ah buaina lian-a om mi khat na muh leh bang gen ding leh bang bawl ding hiam cih a gen hi.

records.english: Could the community centre display the crisis line number in every room?
records.zomi: Khuasung inn lian in inndan khempeuh-ah buaina lian phone nambat a koih thei ding hiam?

records.english: The pharmacist noticed the man was upset.
records.zomi: Damdawi zuakpa in mipa a lungsim a buai hi, cih a phawk hi.

records.english: The crisis team asked the family to stay calm and keep talking gently until they arrived.
records.zomi: Buaina lian pawl in a tun mateng uh innkuan te a dai den ding uh leh nem takin a kiho den ding uh a ngen uh hi.

records.english: Calling for professional help is not abandoning someone; it is often the most caring thing to do.
records.zomi: Siam mite' huhna sam pen mi khat nusiat hi lo a, kemna lungsim lak pen ahi zel hi.

records.english: The police officer stayed with the frightened teenager until a social worker arrived.
records.zomi: Palik in mipi huhna nasempa a tun mateng a lau naupang lianno tawh a om khawm hi.

records.english: The paramedic stayed calm and kind.
records.zomi: Damdawi nasempa a dai a, a hehpih hi.

records.english: A calm presence and simple, practical help can reduce a person's distress more than many words.
records.zomi: Lungdai taka om leh huhna baih taktak in mi khat' lungsim gimna kammal tampi sangin a kiam sak thei zaw hi.

records.english: The nurse spoke calmly to the patient.
records.zomi: Nurse in damlo kiangah dai takin a kiho hi.

records.english: Ring for an ambulance straight away if someone has collapsed.
records.zomi: Mi khat a puk leh pahtakin damlo mawtaw sam in.

records.english: Is there a quiet room at the clinic?
records.zomi: Damdawi inn neu-ah inndan dai khat a om hiam?

records.english: Supporting someone in distress usually begins with listening, not with solving their problems.
records.zomi: Lungsim gimna nei mi khat huh pen a buaina uh phel tawh hi lo-in ngaihngai tawh a kipan zel hi.

records.english: The security guard walked her to a safe place.
records.zomi: Bitna kemmi in amah mun bit khat-ah a paipih hi.

records.english: Is there a drop-in centre for people in crisis?
records.zomi: Buaina lian-a om mite adingin kiko-lut inn khat a om hiam?

records.english: A taxi driver noticed that his passenger was in distress and drove her to the hospital instead of home.
records.zomi: Taxi mawngpa khat in a tuangmi lungsim gimna a nei hi, cih a phawk a, inn sangin damlo inn-ah a paipih hi.

records.english: The pharmacy has a private room where staff can talk to customers who are upset.
records.zomi: Damdawi zuakna inn in nasemte in a lungsim buai lei mite tawh a kiho theih nadingin inndan tuam khat a nei hi.

records.english: Knowing local crisis numbers in advance helps people act quickly when someone is struggling.
records.zomi: Khuasung buaina lian phone nambat te a ma-in theih in mi khat a haksat ciangin mite manlang takin a bawl theih nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: The helpline volunteer listened for an hour.
records.zomi: Helpline thalawp in hun khat sung a ngai hi.

records.english: The outreach team visits people sleeping rough to check that they are safe and to offer support.
records.zomi: Pua lam-a nasem pawl in lampi tunga a ihmu mite a bit uh hiam cih en nadingin leh huhna pia nadingin a kan uh hi.

records.english: What should I do if someone at the bus stop seems very distressed?
records.zomi: Bus khawlna-a mi khat lungsim gimna mahmah a nei bangin a kilang leh bang ka bawl ding hiam?

records.english: Ask gently if they're all right, stay calm, and call the emergency number if they're in danger.
records.zomi: Hoih na hiam, ci-in nem takin dong in, dai den in, lauhuai sungah a om leh lauhuai hun nambat sam in.

records.english: At the station one evening, I noticed a young woman sitting alone on the floor, shaking and unable to speak.
records.zomi: Nitak khat station-ah numei naupang khat a khat bek-in leitang-ah a tu a, a ling a, a ham thei lo a mu hi.

records.english: A member of staff knelt beside her, spoke slowly and asked whether she would like to sit in the warm office.
records.zomi: Nasem khat in a kiangah a khukdin a, zawlzawl-in a gen a, office lum-ah tu nuam hiam, ci-in a dong hi.

records.english: They stayed with her until her brother arrived, and she later wrote to thank the station for their kindness.
records.zomi: A sanggampa a tun mateng a kiangah a om uh a, a nunung-in a hehpihna uh adingin station kiangah lungdamna lai a gelh hi.

records.english: The teacher called the school counsellor.
records.zomi: Saya in sang thuhilhmi a sam hi.

records.english: Can the church help someone who is struggling?
records.zomi: Pawlpi in a haksa mi khat a huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: When workers in shops, stations and libraries know how to respond, public spaces become safer for everyone.
records.zomi: Van zuakna inn, station leh laibu inn-a nasemte in bangci dawng ding hiam cih a theih uh ciangin mipi mun te mi khempeuh adingin a bit zaw hi.

records.english: The crisis line is open all night.
records.zomi: Buaina lian phone pen zan buppi a kihong hi.

records.english: Can the police help someone in distress?
records.zomi: Palik in lungsim gimna nei mi khat a huh thei hiam?

records.english: How should volunteers at the food bank respond if a visitor starts crying?
records.zomi: Khualmi khat a kap pan leh an piakna mun-a thalawp te in bangci a dawng ding uh hiam?

records.english: Offer them a quiet seat and a drink, listen without rushing, and tell the coordinator if they need more help.
records.zomi: Tutna dai khat leh dawn ding khat pia in, kinawh lo-in ngai in, huhna tam zaw a kisam leh a makaipa kiangah gen in.

records.english: Can the library staff help someone who is upset and has nowhere to go?
records.zomi: Laibu inn nasemte in a lungsim buai a, pai ding mun nei lo mi khat a huh thei uh hiam?

records.english: Yes, they can call the outreach team, who will come and talk to the person.
records.zomi: Thei uh hi, pua lam-a nasem pawl a sam thei uh a, amaute hong pai in tua mi tawh a kiho ding uh hi.

records.english: Staff at the job centre are trained to notice when someone is in serious distress.
records.zomi: Nasep zonna office-a nasemte in mi khat lungsim gimna lian a nei ciangin a phawk nadingin kisin uh hi.

records.english: Who can I call if my neighbour is in crisis?
records.zomi: Ka inn kiang mi buaina lian-ah a om leh kua ka sam thei ding hiam?

records.english: Volunteers at the night shelter learn how to calm people who arrive in crisis.
records.zomi: Zan giahna inn-a thalawp te in buaina lian-a hong tung mite lungdai sak dan a sin uh hi.

records.english: The volunteer gave her a cup of tea.
records.zomi: Thalawp in lapha haai khat a pia hi.

records.english: Is there a number I can give to a friend who is in crisis at night?
records.zomi: Zan-in buaina lian-a om ka lawm khat kiangah ka piak theih nambat khat a om hiam?

records.english: Yes, the local crisis line is open all night, and the number is on the back of this card.
records.zomi: Om hi, khuasung buaina lian phone pen zan buppi a kihong a, a nambat hih card nung lam-ah a om hi.

records.english: Is it all right to sit with someone who is upset, even if you don't know what to say?
records.zomi: Bang gen ding hiam cih na theih kei hangin a lungsim buai mi khat kiangah tut a hoih hiam?

records.english: The church opened its doors after the accident so that witnesses had somewhere quiet to sit.
records.zomi: Kisiatna khit-in a mu mite in a tutna mun dai a neih nadingin pawlpi in a kongkhak a hong hi.

records.english: The community centre has trained first-aiders.
records.zomi: Khuasung inn lian in huhna masa pia dingin a kisin mite a nei hi.

records.english: Our neighbourhood group shares the numbers of local support services in its newsletter every month.
records.zomi: I inn kiang pawl in kha simin a thuthak lai-ah khuasung huhna nasep te' nambat a hawm hi.

records.english: Communities that share information about support services make it easier for everyone to help.
records.zomi: Huhna nasep te tawh kisai thu a hawm khuasung te in mi khempeuh adingin huh a baih sak hi.

records.english: Our neighbour checked on the old lady after the storm.
records.zomi: Huihpi khit-in i inn kiang mi in numei upa a en hi.

records.english: Volunteers who support people in distress need support themselves after difficult encounters.
records.zomi: Lungsim gimna nei mite a huh thalawp te in kimuhna haksa khit-in amau' adingin zong huhna a kisam uh hi.

records.english: A volunteer sat with the frightened man.
records.zomi: Thalawp khat a lau mipa kiangah a tu hi.

records.english: Mental health first aid training gives ordinary workers the confidence to respond calmly.
records.zomi: Lungsim cidamna huhna masa kisinna in nasem ngeina te dai taka a dawn theih nadingin hanna a pia hi.

records.english: The bus driver waited until help arrived.
records.zomi: Bus mawngpa in huhna a tun mateng a ngak hi.

records.english: When the man collapsed in tears at the counter, the post office worker closed her window and sat with him.
records.zomi: Mipa dawhkan-ah a kap a puk ciangin post office nasemnu in a tawhkhuak a khak a, a kiangah a tu hi.

records.english: The librarian called the outreach team.
records.zomi: Laibu inn nasem in pua lam-a nasem pawl a sam hi.

records.english: Why did the community centre train its staff in mental health first aid?
records.zomi: Bang hangin khuasung inn lian in a nasemte lungsim cidamna huhna masa a hilh hiam?

records.english: Because staff often meet people at their lowest point, and knowing how to respond calmly can make a real difference.
records.zomi: Bang hang hiam cih leh nasemte in mite a niam pen hun uh-in a mu zel uh a, dai taka dawn dan theih in na thupi a bawl thei hi.

records.english: I'm not sure the table will fit in the car.
records.zomi: Dawhkan mawtaw sungah a lut zo ding hiam cih ka thei cian kei hi.

records.english: A cautious plan that turns out to be unnecessary is usually better than no plan at all.
records.zomi: Kisam lo hi, cih a kimuh ngimna kiphawk khat pen ngimna om lo sangin a hoih zaw zel hi.

records.english: Uncertainty is less frightening when people share what they know and what they still need to discover.
records.zomi: Mite in a theih uh leh a theih nop lai uh a hawm uh ciangin kician lohna a lauhuai tawm zaw hi.

records.english: Maybe we need a bigger tent.
records.zomi: Puanbuuk lian zaw khat i kisam thei hi.

records.english: I'm not sure the paint will cover the stain.
records.zomi: Sawmhal in a nin a khuh zo ding hiam cih ka thei cian kei hi.

records.english: I can't be certain the medicine is safe with your other tablets, so ask the pharmacist.
records.zomi: Damdawi pen na damdawi tang dangte tawh a bit hiam cih ka thei cian thei kei a, tua ahih manin damdawi zuakpa dong in.

records.english: Since we're not sure the bridge will be open, let's plan a route that avoids it.
records.zomi: Lei a kihong ding hiam cih i thei cian kei ahih manin tua a pelh lampi khat i ngim ding hi.

records.english: Perhaps the noise is just the pipes cooling down, but I'll call the engineer if it continues.
records.zomi: Aw ging pen tuikuang a dai kik bek hi thei a, ahi zongin a om den leh engineer ka sam ding hi.

records.english: Planning for more than one outcome reduces stress when the future is uncertain.
records.zomi: Suakna khat sanga tam adingin ngim in hun zom a kician lo ciangin lungsim gimna a kiam sak hi.

records.english: When our car broke down far from home, nobody was sure whether it was the battery or something worse.
records.zomi: Inn pan gamla-ah i mawtaw a siat ciangin battery ahi hiam, a siatna lian zaw ahi hiam cih kuamah in a thei cian kei hi.

records.english: Rather than guessing, my husband rang the breakdown service and described every sound the engine had made.
records.zomi: Ngaihsut sangin ka pasal in mawtaw siat huhna nasep a sam a, mawtaw khawl in a bawl aw ging khempeuh a gen hi.

records.english: The mechanic arrived with the right part, and we were on the road again within an hour.
records.zomi: Mawtaw bawlmi van dik tawh a hong a, hun khat sungin lampi tungah i om kik hi.

records.english: Pretending to be certain can make a problem worse, especially when safety is involved.
records.zomi: Thei cian bangin kibawl in buaina a hoih lo zaw sak thei a, bitna a kihel ciangin a thupi zaw hi.

records.english: Since nobody knows if the train will run, we'd better book a taxi as a backup.
records.zomi: Meileng a pai ding hiam cih kuamah in a thei kei ahih manin a kem nadingin taxi khat ciamteh leng a hoih zaw ding hi.

records.english: It might rain during the picnic.
records.zomi: An ne khawmna-ah guah a zuk thei hi.

records.english: Good problem solvers treat uncertainty as a reason to ask questions, not as a reason to give up.
records.zomi: Buaina phel siam te in kician lohna pen nusiat nading hangsan hi lo-in dotna dong nading hangsan bangin a mu uh hi.

records.english: I can't promise the cake will rise properly in this old oven, but it's worth trying.
records.zomi: Hih tuhvang lui sungah cake hoih takin a kah ding hiam cih ka kiciam thei kei hi, ahi zongin sit huai hi.

records.english: Admitting uncertainty early gives everyone time to prepare a backup plan.
records.zomi: A ma-in kician lohna pom in mi khempeuh a kem ding ngimna bawl nading hun a pia hi.

records.english: Does the router need restarting?
records.zomi: Router a phiat kik ding kisam hiam?

records.english: I'm not sure whether the damp is coming from the roof or the gutter, so let's check both.
records.zomi: Tui hual pen inntung pan ahi hiam, inn tui luanna pan ahi hiam cih ka thei cian kei a, tua ahih manin a nih tuak i en ding hi.

records.english: Saying I'm not sure, but here's how we can find out, keeps a problem moving towards a solution.
records.zomi: Ka thei cian kei hi, ahi zongin hih bangin i thei thei ding hi, ci-in gen in buaina khat phelna lam-ah a pai den sak hi.

records.english: Is the tap broken, or just loose?
records.zomi: Tuikuang kaihna a siat hiam, a kilonh bek hiam?

records.english: When nobody is sure what is causing a problem, testing one possibility at a time is the safest approach.
records.zomi: Bang in buaina khat a piangsak hiam cih kuamah in a thei cian kei ciangin hun khat-ah lampi khat bek sit pen lampi bit pen ahi hi.

records.english: Will the builders finish the roof before the rain comes?
records.zomi: Guah a zuk ma-in inn lam te in inntung a zo ding uh hiam?

records.english: Probably not, so I've asked them to cover the open part with a tarpaulin tonight.
records.zomi: Zo lo thei uh hi, tua ahih manin tu zan-in a hong lai mun plastic puan tawh khuh dingin ka ngen hi.

records.english: The stain might come out with soap, but test it on a small corner first.
records.zomi: Nin pen saupo tawh a pai thei a, ahi zongin a ma-in a ciang neu khat-ah sit masa in.

records.english: Could the dog have eaten something bad?
records.zomi: Ui in na hoih lo khat a ne kha thei ding hiam?

records.english: I'm not sure the neighbours know about the leak, so let's knock on their door now.
records.zomi: Inn kiang mite in tui luang thu a thei uh hiam cih ka thei cian kei a, tua ahih manin tu-in a kongkhak i khu ding hi.

records.english: I'm not sure who has the spare key.
records.zomi: Tawh behlap kua in a nei hiam cih ka thei cian kei hi.

records.english: Is the internet problem on our side or the company's?
records.zomi: Internet buaina pen i lam ahi hiam, company lam ahi hiam?

records.english: I can't tell yet, so let's restart the router and see whether the neighbours have the same problem.
records.zomi: Tu-in ka thei thei nai kei a, tua ahih manin router phiat kik in, inn kiang mite in buaina kibang a nei uh hiam cih i en ding hi.

records.english: It's possible the delivery went to our old address, so I'll ring the company to check.
records.zomi: Van paipihna i tenna mun lui-ah a pai thei a, tua ahih manin en dingin company ka sam ding hi.

records.english: Will the plumber be able to fix the leak today?
records.zomi: Tuikuang bawlmi in tuni-in tui luang a bawlphat thei ding hiam?

records.english: I'm not sure, because he hasn't seen how bad it is yet, so let's put a bucket under it for now.
records.zomi: Ka thei cian kei hi, bang hang hiam cih leh bangzah a hoih lo hiam cih a mu nai kei hi, tua ahih manin tu-in a nuai-ah bel khat i koih ding hi.

records.english: Could the cat have got out through the window?
records.zomi: Zawhngeu in tawhkhuak tungtawn-in a pai khia thei ding hiam?

records.english: It could take a week to arrive.
records.zomi: A tun nadingin kal khat a la thei hi.

records.english: I don't know why the light keeps flickering.
records.zomi: Bang hangin meivak a kilau-kiliap den hiam cih ka thei kei hi.

records.english: The landlord may not agree, so let's ask in writing.
records.zomi: Inn neipa in a lungkim lo thei a, tua ahih manin laigelh tawh i ngen ding hi.

records.english: I'm not certain the shop will take the return without the box, but let's ask.
records.zomi: Box om lo-in van zuakna inn in a pia kik van a sang ding hiam cih ka thei cian kei hi, ahi zongin i dong ding hi.

records.english: Could the battery be flat?
records.zomi: Battery a bei thei ding hiam?

records.english: Has the fuse blown, do you think?
records.zomi: Fuse a kang hiam, na ci hiam?

records.english: It's hard to know whether the plants are dying from too much water or too little.
records.zomi: Kung te tui tam lua hangin ahih kei leh tawm lua hangin a si hiam cih theih a haksa hi.

records.english: Is the post late today, or has it already come?
records.zomi: Tuni-in lai a nunung hiam, a tung khin hiam?

records.english: It might be cheaper to repair the washing machine, but I'd like a second opinion first.
records.zomi: Puan sawpna khawl bawlphat pen a man niam zaw thei a, ahi zongin mi dang khat' ngaihsutna ka deih masa hi.

records.english: How should we plan the party if we don't know how many guests will come?
records.zomi: Khualmi bangzah a hong ding hiam cih i theih kei leh pawi bangci i ngim ding hiam?

records.english: Prepare food that keeps well, ask people to reply by Friday, and have a backup plan for a smaller room.
records.zomi: Sawt kem theih an te bawl in, Laithai ni ma-in dawng dingin mite ngen in, inndan neu zaw adingin a kem ding ngimna khat nei in.

records.english: Do you think the old car will pass its test?
records.zomi: Mawtaw lui in a sitna a zo ding hi, na ci hiam?

records.english: It might, but the brakes are worn, so we should ask the garage for a price just in case.
records.zomi: A zo thei hi, ahi zongin a khawlna te a siat deuh ahih manin a om kha leh ci-in garage kiangah man i dong ding hi.

records.english: Many household problems become clear only after someone takes the time to check the simplest causes.

records.english: Are you sure this key fits?
records.zomi: Hih tawh a kituak hi, cih na thei cian hiam?

records.english: Is this the wrong charger, perhaps?

records.english: A temporary solution can protect a home while people find out exactly what has gone wrong.

records.english: We're not sure how long the power cut will last, so let's keep the fridge closed.

records.english: It's unclear whether the warranty covers the screen, so keep the receipt safe.
records.zomi: Kamciamna lai in screen a huap hiam cih a kician kei ahih manin sum pia lai bit takin kem in.

records.english: Asking an expert is wiser than guessing when a mistake could be expensive or dangerous.

records.english: Keeping receipts and records helps when it is unclear who is responsible for fixing something.
records.zomi: Sum pia lai leh ciamtehna te kem in na khat bawlphat dingin kua in mawhpuakna a nei hiam cih a kician loh ciangin a huh hi.

records.english: I can't tell if the milk is off.
records.zomi: Bawngnawi a siat hiam cih ka thei thei kei hi.

records.english: Could it be a blocked pipe?
records.zomi: Tuikuang kitan khat ahi thei ding hiam?

records.english: Has the bus broken down, I wonder?
records.zomi: Bus a siat ahi hiam?

records.english: I'm not sure the shop is still open.
records.zomi: Van zuakna inn a kihong lai hiam cih ka thei cian kei hi.

records.english: Could the council help us find a school place for our son, who has been studying abroad?
records.zomi: Gamdang-ah a kisin ka tapa adingin council in sang mun khat i muh nadingin hong huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: The job centre ran a workshop for people returning to work after caring for relatives.
records.zomi: Nasep zonna office in sanggam te a kem khit-a nasep-ah a ciah kik mite adingin sinna khat a bawl hi.

records.english: The volunteer drove Grandma home.
records.zomi: Thalawp in Pi inn-ah a paipih hi.

records.english: Community volunteers can turn a lonely return into a welcoming one.
records.zomi: Khuasung thalawp te in a khat bek-a ciah kikna khat kidawn nuamna khat-ah a khek thei uh hi.

records.english: When my uncle came home after ten years working abroad, he didn't know how to register for anything.

records.english: Within a month, he felt at home again, and he now helps other returning workers with the same forms.
records.zomi: Kha khat sungin inn-ah a om kik bangin a kizak a, tu-in a ciah kik nasem dangte lai kibang te-ah a huh hi.

records.english: The community centre's language class helped our children catch up after years abroad.
records.zomi: Khuasung inn lian' pau sinna in i tate gamdang-a kum tampi khit-in a zui kik nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Did the council give you a temporary flat?

records.english: Because they wanted to make sure the right support, such as a carer and equipment, was ready before he arrived.

records.english: Why do some people find returning home harder than moving abroad in the first place?
records.zomi: Bang hangin mi khenkhat in a masa-a gamdang-a pem sangin inn-a ciah kik a haksa sa zaw uh hiam?

records.english: Public services that keep clear records make it easier for people to pick up where they left off.

records.english: Adapting a home for a returning patient can make the difference between independence and a long stay in care.

records.english: The nurse visits Dad at home every day.
records.zomi: Nurse in ni simin Pa inn-ah a kan hi.

records.english: Can the bank reopen my old account?
records.zomi: Bank in ka account lui a hong kik thei ding hiam?

records.english: A well-planned homecoming supports both the person returning and the family who welcome them.
records.zomi: Hoih taka kingim inn ciahna in a ciah kik mi leh amah a dawn innkuan tuak a huh hi.

records.english: When we moved back, the health centre needed our old medical records from the other country.
records.zomi: I pem kik ciangin cidamna inn in gam dang pan i damdawi ciamtehna lui te a kisam hi.

records.english: Can I get my old phone number back?
records.zomi: Ka phone nambat lui ka ngah kik thei ding hiam?

records.english: Can the council help us find a flat now that we've returned from abroad?
records.zomi: Gamdang pan i ciah kik khit-in council in inn khat i muh nadingin hong huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, the housing office can put you on the list and explain what support is available.

records.english: How often does the carer come now?

records.english: The housing association adapted our flat so that my brother could come home in his wheelchair.
records.zomi: Inn kemna pawl in ka sanggampa a tawlek tutphah tawh inn-ah a hong theih nadingin i inn a bawlphat hi.

records.english: Volunteers from the befriending scheme visited my grandmother every week after she left hospital.

records.english: The bank asked for proof of address before it would reopen my account.
records.zomi: Bank in ka account a hong kik ma-in tenna mun tettehna a ngen hi.

records.english: The school found a place for my daughter.
records.zomi: Sang in ka tanu adingin mun khat a mu hi.

records.english: The social worker visited after the operation.
records.zomi: Zatna khit-in mipi huhna nasempa a hong kan hi.

records.english: The veterans' charity helped my cousin find work after he left the army.
records.zomi: Galkap lui huhna pawl in ka sanggam galkap a nusiat khit-in nasep a muh nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: The council's welcome pack explained how to restart our bin collection and council tax.
records.zomi: Council' dawnna ip in i nawi lakna leh council siah bangci a kipan kik ding hiam cih a gen hi.

records.english: The advice centre explained the forms.
records.zomi: Thuhilhna mun in lai te a gen hi.

records.english: Do I need to register with the doctor again now that I've moved back?

records.english: Who helps people coming home from hospital?

records.english: Advice centres save returning residents many hours of confusion over forms and documents.
records.zomi: Thuhilhna mun te in a ciah kik a teng mite lai leh laigelh tawh kisai lungbuaina hun tampi a kem sak hi.

records.english: The district nurse showed my father how to change his own dressing once he was home.

records.zomi: A manlang leh a baih genna dan te in a sung-a teng mite kuamah a liam ma-in buaina te gen dingin a hanthawn hi.

records.english: Why does the library record even small accidents involving visitors?
records.zomi: Bang hangin laibu inn in khualmite tawh kisai kisiatna neu te zong a ciamteh hiam?

records.english: Because a pattern of small falls or bumps can reveal a hazard before someone is seriously hurt.
records.zomi: Bang hang hiam cih leh puk neu ahih kei leh kisatna neu te' a kibangzia in mi khat a liam mahmah ma-in lauhuai khat a lak thei hi.

records.english: My son hurt his hand at the playground.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in naupang kimawlna mun-ah a khut a liam hi.

records.english: Can I report an accident at the pool if I'm only a visitor?
records.zomi: Khualmi bek ka hih hangin tuipeek mun-ah kisiatna khat ka gen thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, any of the lifeguards can fill in the form with you before you leave.
records.zomi: Thei hi, tuipeek kemmi khatpeuh in na pai khiat ma-in nang tawh lai a gelh thei hi.

records.english: The museum guard wrote down the names of two visitors who saw the child fall.
records.zomi: Museum kemmi in naupang a puk a mu khualmi nih' min a gelh hi.

records.english: Where do I report an accident on the train?
records.zomi: Meileng tunga kisiatna khat koi-ah ka gen ding hiam?

records.english: The shop called an ambulance for my mother.
records.zomi: Van zuakna inn in ka nu adingin damlo mawtaw a sam hi.

records.english: The train company's staff filled in a report after a passenger tripped on the gap by the platform.
records.zomi: Tuangmi khat platform kiang-a kua tungah a kibah puk khit-in meileng company' nasemte in report khat a gelh uh hi.

records.english: Why did the bus company ask for the time and route number of the accident?
records.zomi: Bang hangin bus company in kisiatna' hun leh lampi nambat a dong hiam?

records.english: Did anyone call the ambulance?
records.zomi: Kuamah in damlo mawtaw a sam hiam?

records.english: The road safety team installed a speed camera after a series of accident reports from the school.
records.zomi: Sang pan kisiatna report tampi khit-in lampi bitna pawl in mawtaw manlang tehna camera khat a koih uh hi.

records.english: Could the leisure centre send me a copy of the accident report for my insurance?
records.zomi: Kimawlna inn in ka insurance adingin kisiatna report copy khat hong khak thei ding hiam?

records.english: The pharmacist reported a fall in the shop to the head office the same day.
records.zomi: Damdawi zuakpa in van zuakna inn-a puk khat ni kibang-in a makai office kiangah a gen hi.

records.english: Is the hill path suitable for wheelchairs?
records.zomi: Mual lampi pen tawlek tutphah adingin a kituak hiam?

records.english: Why does the visitor centre describe the forest in several languages?
records.zomi: Bang hangin khualmite inn in gammang pen pau tampi tawh a gen hiam?

records.english: Because many visitors come from abroad, and the staff want everyone to understand what makes the forest special.
records.zomi: Bang hang hiam cih leh khualmi tampi gamdang pan a hong uh a, nasemte in gammang a tuam sak bang hiam cih mi khempeuh in a theisiam nadingin a deih uh hi.

records.english: Well-written signs in nature reserves help visitors see details they would otherwise walk past.
records.zomi: Gam kemna mun te-a hoih taka kigelh lim tangna te in khualmite a dang-in a pai khak ding thu neu te a mu nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Rangers who describe a landscape with care can turn a simple walk into a lesson in observation.
records.zomi: Gam khat cian takin a gen gam kemmi te in kalsuanna baih khat et-ciamtehna sinna khat-ah a khek thei uh hi.

records.english: Why is part of the park left wild?
records.zomi: Bang hangin park' a khenkhat gam bangin a kinusia hiam?

records.english: The council lets the grass grow long there so that flowers, insects and birds have a place to live.
records.zomi: Pak te, lungkhai te leh vasa te in a tenna mun a neih nadingin council in tua mun-ah lopa sau-in a khan sak hi.

records.english: The volunteers planted wild flowers by the road.
records.zomi: Thalawp te in lampi kiangah gam pak te a suan uh hi.

records.english: The botanical garden has a glass house full of palms.
records.zomi: Kung huan lian in phaisan kung tawh a dim mitlim inn khat a nei hi.

records.english: Our local radio station broadcasts a short report on what is flowering in the parks each week.
records.zomi: I khuasung radio in kal simin park te-ah bang pak a vul hiam cih report tom khat a suah hi.

records.english: Where can we see the waterfall from?
records.zomi: Tuikhawh koi pan i mu thei ding hiam?

records.english: The tourist office recommends the coastal path for its views of cliffs and seabirds.
records.zomi: Khualzinmite thuhilhna office in suangpang leh tuipi vasa te' muhna dingin tuipi gei lampi a gen hi.

records.english: Our neighbourhood turned an empty plot behind the library into a community garden.
records.zomi: I inn kiang mite in laibu inn nung-a mun lawn khat khuasung huan khat-ah a khek uh hi.

records.english: In the first summer, sunflowers stood taller than the fence, and the air was full of bees moving between the beans and the marigolds.
records.zomi: Khal masa pen-in ni pak te huang sangin a sang zaw a, khaukhap te leh pak dangte kikal-ah a kizuan khuai te in huih a dim hi.

records.english: Now the library holds its storytelling sessions there on warm afternoons.
records.zomi: Tu-in laibu inn in nitak lam lum te-in tua mun-ah tangthu genna kikhopna te a bawl hi.

records.english: Public parks give city residents a daily chance to notice the changing seasons.
records.zomi: Mipi park te in khuapi-a teng mite ni simin kum hun kikhekna te a phawk theih nading hun a pia hi.

records.english: Community gardens show that nature can return even to the most neglected corners of a town.
records.zomi: Khuasung huan te in khuapi khat' a kinusia pen mun te-ah zong gam nuntakna a hong kik thei hi, cih a lak hi.

records.english: Is the path by the river open again?
records.zomi: Lui kiang-a lampi a kihong kik hiam?

records.english: The visitor centre has a map of the forest.
records.zomi: Khualmite inn in gammang' map khat a nei hi.

records.english: The council planted trees along our street.
records.zomi: Council in i lampi kiangah singkung te a suan hi.

records.english: Is the lake in the park safe for swimming?
records.zomi: Park sung-a dil pen tuipeek adingin a bit hiam?

records.english: A river that has been cleaned and protected can become the pride of a whole community.
records.zomi: Kisianghsak a kikem lui khat khuasung buppi' kipahna a suak thei hi.

records.english: Local volunteers often know a stretch of river or woodland better than any official map.
records.zomi: Khuasung thalawp te in lui ahih kei leh gammang mun khat map tak khatpeuh sangin a thei zaw zel uh hi.

records.english: The ranger told us the names of the trees.
records.zomi: Gam kemmi in singkung te' min hong gen hi.

records.english: Descriptions of nature in council plans tend to be practical, while those in visitor guides aim to inspire.
records.zomi: Council ngimna te-a gam genna te a taktak lam-ah a om zel a, khualmite lamlakna-a genna te in lungsim a hanthawn dingin a ngim uh hi.

records.english: The park's roses are at their best in June.
records.zomi: Park' pak te June kha-in a hoih pen uh hi.

records.english: Volunteers count the butterflies in the meadow every summer and send the results to a national survey.
records.zomi: Thalawp te in khal simin lopa mun-a mailip te a sim uh a, a suakna te gam buppi dotna khat-ah a khak uh hi.

records.english: The school's nature garden has a small pond.
records.zomi: Sang' gam huan in dil neu khat a nei hi.

records.english: The park is full of flowers in May.
records.zomi: May kha-in park pak tawh a dim hi.

records.english: Is it true that the council wants to build on the meadow behind the station?
records.zomi: Council in station nung-a lopa mun tungah inn lam a deih hi, cih a tak hiam?

records.english: Could the park put up signs naming the trees along the main path?
records.zomi: Park in lampi lian kiang-a singkung te' min lak lim tangna te a koih thei ding hiam?

records.english: Nature walks led by local experts help residents value the wildlife on their own doorstep.
records.zomi: Khuasung siam mite' makaih gam kalsuanna te in a sung-a teng mite a inn kiang-a gam ganhing te a manpha sa theih nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Why has the council stopped cutting the grass along the roadside in summer?
records.zomi: Bang hangin council in khal-in lampi kiang-a lopa a at nawn kei hiam?

records.english: How did the river look after the volunteers cleaned it?
records.zomi: Thalawp te in a sianghsak khit-in lui bangci a kilang hiam?

records.english: The water was clear again, and within a month we saw ducks nesting where the rubbish had been.
records.zomi: Tui a kician kik a, kha khat sungin nawi a omna mun-ah vatui te buk a bawl i mu hi.

records.english: When a meadow is threatened by development, residents' descriptions of its beauty can become part of a public debate.
records.zomi: Lopa mun khat inn lamna in a lauhuai sak ciangin a sung-a teng mite in a hoihna tawh kisai a gen te mipi kinialna khat' khen khat a suak thei hi.

records.english: Access to green spaces should not depend on whether a family can afford to travel.
records.zomi: Gam hing mun te-a pai theihna pen innkuan khat in khualzinna man a pia zo hiam cih tungah a kinga lo ding hi.

records.english: The beach was cleaned by local volunteers.
records.zomi: Tuipi gei pen khuasung thalawp te in a sianghsak uh hi.

records.english: Is the nature reserve open in winter?
records.zomi: Gam kemna mun pen khuaphal-in a kihong hiam?

records.english: Yes, and the frozen marsh is beautiful at sunrise, though the paths can be slippery.
records.zomi: Kihong hi, ni suah-in a khal tui mun a hoih mahmah a, ahi zongin lampi te a zuat thei hi.

records.english: The old oak in the square is protected.
records.zomi: Khua lai-a singkung lian lui pen a kikem hi.

records.english: Can we walk our dog in the nature reserve?
records.zomi: Gam kemna mun sungah i ui i paipih thei ding hiam?

records.english: Which trail has the best view of the valley?
records.zomi: Bang lampi in guam a muh theih hoih pen hiam?

records.english: From the wooden shelter by the marsh, we watched a line of wading birds feeding at low tide.
records.zomi: Tui mun kiang-a sing tawh kibawl khuhna pan tuipi a kiam hun-in a an a ne tui sung pai vasa lam khat i en hi.

records.english: Children from the estate helped plant the hedge that now shelters the playground from the wind.
records.zomi: Inn kikhawmna mun pan naupangte in tu-in naupang kimawlna mun huih pan a khuh huang sing a suan nadingin a huh uh hi.

records.english: The park's night walk introduced us to bats, owls and the glow of tiny insects.
records.zomi: Park' zan kalsuanna in bak, zing leh lungkhai neu te' tang hong theisak hi.

records.english: The pond in the park is green and full of frogs.
records.zomi: Park sung-a dil a eng a, ukeng tawh a dim hi.

records.english: Are there guided walks on Sundays?
records.zomi: Nipini-in lamlak kalsuanna te a om hiam?

records.english: The community orchard is open to everyone, and residents can pick the apples in autumn.
records.zomi: Khuasung gah huan pen mi khempeuh adingin a kihong a, a sung-a teng mite in autumn hun-in apple te a lo thei uh hi.

records.english: The ranger described the marsh as a giant sponge that soaks up rain and slowly releases it.
records.zomi: Gam kemmi in tui mun pen guah a dawn a, zawlzawl-in a khah sawn guah puanphah lian khat bang ahi hi, ci-in a gen hi.

records.english: How do the gardeners keep the botanical garden so green during the dry season?
records.zomi: Khuakhal hun sungin huan kemmite in kung huan lian a eng den nadingin bangci a kem uh hiam?

records.english: The ranger showed us a bird's nest.
records.zomi: Gam kemmi in vasa buk khat hong lak hi.

records.english: After the volunteers cleared the rubbish, the stream ran clear over the stones again.
records.zomi: Thalawp te in nawi a sianghsak khit-in tuikuang suang te tungah a kician kik-in a luang hi.

records.english: The community garden smells of mint and tomatoes.
records.zomi: Khuasung huan pen pak namtui leh mehtuuk namtui a nam hi.

records.english: What can we see on the ranger's guided walk?
records.zomi: Gam kemmi' lamlak kalsuanna-ah bang i mu thei ding hiam?

records.english: In spring, you'll see bluebells under the beech trees and maybe a heron by the pond.
records.zomi: Spring-in singkung nuai-ah pak dum te na mu ding a, dil kiangah va sau khat zong na mu thei ding hi.

records.english: The new boardwalk lets visitors cross the wetland without trampling the reeds.
records.zomi: Sing lampi thak in khualmite lopa sau te sik lo-in tui mun a kan theih sak hi.

records.english: The council's leaflet describes the woodland walk as gentle, shaded and suitable for families.
records.zomi: Council' laipek in gammang kalsuanna pen a nem, a limliam nei leh innkuan te adingin a kituak ahi hi, ci-in a gen hi.

records.english: Leaving some areas of a park unmowed can make it far richer in flowers and insects.
records.zomi: Park khat' mun khenkhat a lopa at lo-in nusia in pak leh lungkhai te tawh a dim zaw mahmah sak thei hi.

records.english: Public botanical gardens preserve rare plants while giving visitors a glimpse of landscapes from around the world.
records.zomi: Mipi kung huan lian te in kung khawng te a kem a, khualmite leitung buppi-a gam te' lim tawmno a mu sak hi.

records.english: We say grace together before dinner.
records.zomi: Nitak an ne ma-in an ne ma thu ngetna khawm takin i bawl hi.

records.english: Grandma calls the mountains God's handwriting.
records.zomi: Pi in mual te Pasian' laigelh a ci hi.

records.english: Why do you think God made so many different kinds of birds?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pasian in vasa tuamtuam tampi a piangsak hi, na ci hiam?

records.english: Grandma believes that caring for her garden is a way of caring for God's creation.
records.zomi: Pi in a huan kem pen Pasian' piansak nate kemna lampi khat ahi hi, ci-in a um hi.

records.english: Why does Grandma thank God when she sees the sunrise?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pi in ni suah a muh ciangin Pasian kiangah lungdam a ko hiam?

records.english: Because she believes that each new day is a gift from the God who created the world.
records.zomi: Bang hang hiam cih leh ni thak khatciat pen leitung a piangsak Pasian pan letsong khat ahi hi, ci-in a um hi.

records.english: Our family walks in the hills to enjoy God's world.
records.zomi: Pasian' leitung nuam sa dingin i innkuan mual te-ah a kalsuan hi.

records.english: Why did God give us such a beautiful world?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pasian in hoih mahmah leitung khat hong pia hiam?

records.english: My mother says she feels closest to God at the edge of the sea.
records.zomi: Tuipi gei-ah Pasian tawh a kinai pen bangin a kizak hi, ci-in ka nu in a gen hi.

records.english: Our family thanks God for the rain.
records.zomi: I innkuan in guah adingin Pasian kiangah lungdam a ko hi.

records.english: Mum reads Genesis to us on Sundays.
records.zomi: Nu in Nipini simin Piancilna laibu hong sim sak hi.

records.english: Our family's evening prayer always includes thanks for the beauty of the day.
records.zomi: I innkuan' nitak thu ngetna in ni' hoihna adingin lungdamna a huap den hi.

records.english: Do your children ask difficult questions about how the world began?
records.zomi: Na tate in leitung bangci a kipan hiam cih dotna haksa te a dong uh hiam?

records.english: My husband and I disagree about how literally to read Genesis, but we both believe God created the world.
records.zomi: Ka pasal leh kei Piancilna laibu bangzah tak-in sim ding hiam cih-ah i kibang kei a, ahi zongin i nih in Pasian in leitung a piangsak hi, ci-in i um hi.

records.english: Our children collect leaves and stones to put on the table at the harvest service.
records.zomi: I tate in buh lak Pasian biakna dawhkan tungah koih dingin teh leh suang te a kaikhawm uh hi.

records.english: Grandma's garden makes her think of Eden.
records.zomi: Pi' huan in Eden a phawk sak hi.

records.english: How did your parents explain the creation story to you?
records.zomi: Na nu leh pa in piansakna tangthu bangci hong gen uh hiam?

records.english: They read it slowly with us and said the most important thing was that God made the world with care.
records.zomi: Zawlzawl-in hong sim sak uh a, a thupi pen Pasian in leitung kem lungsim tawh a bawl hi, cih ahi hi, a ci uh hi.

records.english: My son wants to know how big the sky is.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in van bangzah a lian hiam cih a theih nuam hi.

records.english: Who made the animals, Mum?
records.zomi: Nu aw, ganhing te kua in a bawl hiam?

records.english: When my son asked who made God, I told him that Christians believe God has always existed.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in Pasian kua in a bawl hiam, ci-in a dot ciangin Khazih mite in Pasian a om den hi, ci-in a um uh hi, ka ci hi.

records.english: My daughter drew the seven days of creation.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in piansakna ni sagih a suai hi.

records.english: My little brother loves the story of the animals.
records.zomi: Ka nau pasal neu in ganhing te' tangthu a deih mahmah hi.

records.english: We pray together under the stars on holiday.
records.zomi: Tawlngakni-in aksi nuai-ah khawm takin thu i ngen hi.

records.english: Did God make the sea too?
records.zomi: Pasian in tuipi zong a bawl hiam?

records.english: Is the world very old, Dad?
records.zomi: Pa aw, leitung a lui mahmah hiam?

records.english: How do you explain the seventh day of rest to young children?
records.zomi: Ni sagihna tawlngakna naupang neu te kiangah bangci na gen hiam?

records.english: Within a single Christian family, people may read the creation story differently while sharing the same basic faith.
records.zomi: Khazih innkuan khat sungah mite in upna bulpi kibang a neih kawm-un piansakna tangthu a kibang lo-in a sim thei uh hi.

records.english: The teaching that people are made in God's image has given many Christian families a strong sense of human dignity.
records.zomi: Mite Pasian lim bangin kibawl ahi hi, cih hilhna in Khazih innkuan tampi mihing' manphatna lungsim khauh a pia hi.

records.english: Family traditions such as giving thanks for the harvest keep the idea of creation present in everyday life.
records.zomi: Buh lak adingin lungdam ko bang innkuan ngeina te in piansakna ngaihsutna ni sim nuntakna sungah a om den sak hi.

records.english: We started recycling at home after our pastor preached about looking after creation.
records.zomi: I pastor in piansakna kem tawh kisai thu a gen khit-in inn-ah van zat kik i kipan hi.

records.english: On the night my daughter was born, my father stood by the hospital window and said that every new life reminded him of the first chapter of Genesis.
records.zomi: Ka tanu a suah zan-in ka pa in damlo inn tawhkhuak kiangah a ding a, nuntakna thak khatciat in Piancilna laibu' a khen masa pen a phawk sak hi, a ci hi.

records.english: I didn't understand him then, but years later, holding my daughter's hand under a sky full of stars, I felt the same wonder he had described.
records.zomi: Tua hun-in ka theisiam kei a, ahi zongin kum tampi khit-in aksi dim van nuai-ah ka tanu' khut ka len laitakin a gen lamdang sakna kibang ka kizak hi.

records.english: Now we read the creation story together on her birthday every year.
records.zomi: Tu-in kum simin a suahni-in piansakna tangthu khawm takin i sim hi.

records.english: Grandparents who share their faith in the creator often pass on a love of nature at the same time.
records.zomi: A piangsakpa tungah a upna uh a hawm pu leh pi te in tua hun mahmah-in gam it lungsim zong a khah suk zel uh hi.

records.english: Did God make the dinosaurs?
records.zomi: Pasian in dinosaur te a bawl hiam?

records.english: Reading Genesis together can help families talk about responsibility for the earth in a way that children understand.
records.zomi: Piancilna laibu khawm taka sim in innkuan te in leitung tunga mawhpuakna tawh kisai naupangte' theisiam theih dan-in a kikum thei uh hi.

records.english: Grandpa's favourite psalm praises God for the moon and stars he has made.
records.zomi: Pu' deih pen Late in Pasian a bawl kha leh aksi te adingin a phat hi.

records.english: Can we read the creation story before bed?
records.zomi: Ihmut ma-in piansakna tangthu i sim thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, and afterwards we can look out of the window and find the moon together.
records.zomi: Thei hi, tua khit-in tawhkhuak pan en-in kha khawm takin i zong thei ding hi.

records.english: My teenage son says that learning about the size of the universe has made his faith stronger.
records.zomi: Ka tapa naupang lianno in leitung buppi' lianna sin in a upna a khauh sak zaw hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Grandpa says God painted the sky.
records.zomi: Pasian in van a zuh hi, ci-in Pu in a gen hi.

records.english: Dad woke us early to watch the sun rise.
records.zomi: Ni suah en dingin Pa in zingsang ma lam-in hong khanghsak hi.

records.english: My sister sings a song about creation.
records.zomi: Ka sanggamnu in piansakna tawh kisai la khat a sa hi.

records.english: Every summer, our family camps far from the city lights to see the stars clearly.
records.zomi: Khal simin i innkuan in aksi te kician takin a muh theih nadingin khuapi meivak pan gamla-ah puanbuuk-in a om hi.

records.english: For many believers, wonder at the size of the universe deepens rather than weakens their sense of God's greatness.
records.zomi: Upmi tampi adingin leitung buppi' lianna tungah lamdang sakna in Pasian' thupina lungsim a nem sak sangin a thuk zaw sak hi.

records.english: When a child is born, many Christian families speak of new life as part of God's ongoing care for creation.
records.zomi: Naupang khat a suah ciangin Khazih innkuan tampi in nuntakna thak pen Pasian in a piansak nate a kem den sungah ahi hi, ci-in a gen uh hi.

records.english: Mum, who made the stars?
records.zomi: Nu aw, aksi te kua in a bawl hiam?

records.english: Christians believe that God made them, along with everything else in the universe.
records.zomi: Khazih mite in leitung buppi-a na khempeuh tawh Pasian in a bawl hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: We thank God for the new baby.
records.zomi: Naupang neu thak adingin Pasian kiangah lungdam i ko hi.

records.english: Grandpa planted a tree for each grandchild.
records.zomi: Pu in a tu khatciat adingin singkung khat a suan hi.

records.english: Could we visit the planetarium as a family to see how vast the universe is?
records.zomi: Leitung buppi bangzah a lian hiam cih en dingin innkuan khawm takin aksi inn i kan thei ding hiam?

records.english: My parents taught us that every person is made in God's image, so nobody is worthless.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh Pasian lim bangin kibawl ahi a, tua ahih manin kuamah a manpha lo kei hi, ci-in ka nu leh pa in hong hilh uh hi.

records.english: Children's questions about how the world began often lead families into deep conversations about meaning and purpose.
records.zomi: Leitung bangci a kipan hiam cih naupangte' dotna te in innkuan te cihna leh ngimna tawh kisai kikupna thuk te-ah a pi zel hi.

records.english: Can God see every star?
records.zomi: Pasian in aksi khempeuh a mu thei hiam?

records.english: Believing that the world is a gift can shape how a family cares for land, animals and each other.
records.zomi: Leitung pen letsong khat ahi hi, cih um in innkuan khat in leitang, ganhing leh khat leh khat a kem dan a bawl thei hi.

records.english: When we lost our dog, my daughter asked whether God had made animals to live forever.
records.zomi: I ui i mansuah ciangin ka tanu in Pasian in ganhing te tawntung-a nungta dingin a bawl hiam, ci-in a dong hi.

records.english: Many Christian parents use the beauty of nature to begin conversations with their children about God as creator.
records.zomi: Khazih nu leh pa tampi in a tate tawh piangsakpa Pasian tawh kisai kikupna kipat nadingin gam' hoihna a zang uh hi.

records.english: Do you think the creation story and science can both be true?
records.zomi: Piansakna tangthu leh pilna a nih in a dik thei uh hi, na ci hiam?

records.english: Volunteer fire crews provide vital protection in rural areas far from a full-time station.

records.english: Can the fire service check my home for risks?

records.english: The fire service asked residents to keep the access road clear of parked cars.

records.english: The fire service's leaflet explains how to escape from a high-rise building.

records.english: The council can arrange emergency housing, and charities often help with clothes, food and furniture.

records.english: After a serious fire, neighbours, charities and public services often work together to support those affected.

records.english: Firefighters checked the smoke alarms in our flats.

records.english: I prefer the stairs when the lift is busy.

records.english: When the restaurant ran out of fish, I chose the chicken rather than wait for something else.

records.english: I'd rather have the money back.

records.english: Flexible services that adapt to people's preferences can reduce complaints without costing much.

records.english: A preference expressed politely is far more likely to be accommodated than one expressed as a demand.
