records.zomi: Kua in tettehna tam zaw a nei hiam?

records.english: A strong answer to a question about arguments explains why one is more convincing, not just which.
records.zomi: Genna te tawh kisai dotna khat' dawnna khauh in bang in a muanhuai zaw hiam cih bek hi lo-in bang hangin a muanhuai zaw hiam cih a gen hi.

records.english: Let's compare the two answers.
records.zomi: Dawnna nih i khaikhin ni.

records.english: What is your main point?
records.zomi: Na thu thupi pen bang ahi hiam?

records.english: When the class compared the two speeches, most of us preferred the one that admitted its weaknesses.
records.zomi: Sinna in thugenna nih a khaikhin ciangin ei tampi in a hatlohna te a pom khat i deih zaw hi.

records.english: In our debating club, the coach once made us argue both sides of the same question in a single evening.
records.zomi: I kinialna pawl-ah hilhpa in nitak khat sungin dotna kibang' lam nih tuak a kinial dingin hong ngen ngei hi.

records.english: After defending school uniforms for ten minutes, I had to attack them, and I found that some of my own points were weaker than I had thought.
records.zomi: Minute sawm sung sang puan ka dinpih khit-in ka simmawh ding a kisam a, ka genna khenkhat ka ngaihsut sangin a nem zaw hi, cih ka mu hi.

records.english: Since then, I always try to state the other side's best argument before I make my own.
records.zomi: Tua pan ka mah' genna ka gen ma-in a dang lam' genna hoih pen gen dingin ka hanciam den hi.

records.english: Why did the teacher say my argument was one-sided?
records.zomi: Bang hangin saya in ka genna lam khat bek ahi hi, a ci hiam?

records.english: How can I tell whether an argument is using emotion instead of evidence?
records.zomi: Genna khat in tettehna sangin lungsim kizakna a zang hiam cih bangci ka thei thei ding hiam?

records.english: Debates become more useful when participants agree on the facts before arguing about what they mean.
records.zomi: Kinialna te a cihna tawh kisai a kinial ma-un a kihel mite in thu tak te-ah a kilungkim uh ciangin a phattuam zaw hi.

records.english: When two arguments rest on different values, evidence alone may not settle which is better.
records.zomi: Genna nih in manphatna tuam tungah a kinga uh ciangin tettehna bek in bang a hoih zaw hiam cih a phel thei kei hi.

records.english: Is that a good reason?
records.zomi: Tua pen hangsan hoih khat ahi hiam?

records.english: Can you explain the other side?
records.zomi: A dang lam na gen thei ding hiam?

records.english: Each side made a good point.
records.zomi: Lam khatciat in thu hoih khat a gen uh hi.

records.english: Why do some debates never end, even when everyone has heard all the arguments?
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh in genna khempeuh a zak khin uh hangin bang hangin kinialna khenkhat a bei ngei kei hiam?

records.english: Readers who compare arguments carefully are less likely to be misled by clever wording.
records.zomi: Genna te cian taka a khaikhin simmite in kammal pil te in a khem kha tawm zaw uh hi.

records.english: Is this reason fair to everyone?
records.zomi: Hih hangsan pen mi khempeuh adingin a dik hiam?

records.english: Which speaker was clearer?
records.zomi: Bang thugenpa a kician zaw hiam?

records.english: An argument that admits its limits can be more persuasive than one that claims to explain everything.
records.zomi: A ciang a pom genna khat pen na khempeuh a gen thei hi a ci genna khat sangin a muanhuai zaw thei hi.

records.english: His reason is about money.
records.zomi: A hangsan pen sum tawh kisai ahi hi.

records.english: The crossing guard outside the school always smiles.
records.zomi: Sang pua-a lampi kanna kemmi a nuisuak den hi.

records.english: How would you describe the police officer who spoke at the meeting?
records.zomi: Kikhopna-ah thu a gen palik bangci na gen ding hiam?

records.english: Direct but friendly, and she listened to every complaint before answering.
records.zomi: A kician a, ahi zongin a nuam a, a dawn ma-in phunna khempeuh a ngai hi.

records.english: The vicar is a tall, gentle man who visits every patient in the local hospital each week.
records.zomi: Pastor pen a sang a, a nem pa khat ahi a, kal simin khuasung damlo inn-a damlo khempeuh a kan hi.

records.english: The mayor is shorter than I expected.
records.zomi: Khuapi ukpa pen ka lamen sangin a niam zaw hi.

records.english: The interpreter at the clinic was quiet, precise and careful never to add her own opinions.
records.zomi: Damdawi inn neu-a pau letmi pen a dai, a kician a, a mah' ngaihsutna behlap lo dingin a kiphawk hi.

records.english: What's the new community nurse like?
records.zomi: Khuasung nurse thak bangci ahi hiam?

records.english: She's calm and practical, and she always explains things twice without making you feel slow.
records.zomi: A dai a, a taktak a, nangmah a nawl hi, ci-in kizak sak lo-in thu te nihvei a gen den hi.

records.english: Our refuse collector is a cheerful young man who sings while he works.
records.zomi: I nawi lami pen nasep a sep laitakin la a sa nuam tangval neu khat ahi hi.

records.english: The volunteer at the desk speaks three languages.
records.zomi: Dawhkan-a thalawp in pau thum a ham thei hi.

records.english: The woman who runs the charity shop is generous with her time and strict about the prices.
records.zomi: Huhna pawl van zuakna inn makaipa numei pen a hun-ah a pia hoih a, man-ah a khauh hi.

records.english: Describing a community worker fairly means mentioning both their skills and the pressures they work under.
records.zomi: Khuasung nasem khat dik taka gen in a siamna te leh a nasep sungah a thuak puakgik te tuak a gen ding hi.

records.english: Our librarian knows every book in the library.
records.zomi: I laibu inn nasem in laibu inn-a laibu khempeuh a thei hi.

records.english: Public servants who listen patiently are often described as kind, even when they cannot give people what they want.
records.zomi: Thuakzawh taka a ngai mipi nasemte pen mite' deih a pia thei kei uh hangin hehpih mi bangin a kigen zel uh hi.

records.english: The new doctor is young and very patient.
records.zomi: Siavuan thak pen a naupang a, a thuakzawh mahmah hi.

records.english: The health visitor is a calm, experienced woman who never seems to be in a hurry.
records.zomi: Inn kankan cidamna nasem pen kinawh ngei lo bangin a kilang a dai, thuakna nei numei khat ahi hi.

records.english: The lifeguard at the pool is strict but fair.
records.zomi: Tuipeek mun-a tuipeek kemmi pen a khauh a, ahi zongin a dik hi.

records.english: Volunteers who give their time every week often become familiar faces that a neighbourhood depends on.
records.zomi: Kal simin a hun a pia thalawp te pen inn kiang mite' a kinga mai theih te a suak zel uh hi.

records.english: The rubbish collectors wave to the children every week.
records.zomi: Nawi lami te in kal simin naupangte a khut a sing uh hi.

records.english: People who work in public services are often remembered for small kindnesses rather than for their official roles.
records.zomi: Mipi nasep-a nasem mite pen a nasep tak uh sangin hehpihna neu te tawh a kiphawk zel uh hi.

records.english: Could you describe the officer who took your statement, so that I can ask for her?
records.zomi: Na thu a la palik nu na gen thei ding hiam, amah ka ngen theih nadingin?

records.english: The man at the advice centre was so well organised that he sorted out my forms in ten minutes.
records.zomi: Thuhilhna mun-a pa in a nasep a cian mahmah ahih manin minute sawm sungin ka lai te a bawlphat hi.

records.english: The receptionist at the clinic is always polite.
records.zomi: Damdawi inn neu-a dawnmi in zahtakna a nei den hi.

records.english: Who is the man in the yellow jacket?
records.zomi: Jacket gial a silh pa kua hi hiam?

records.english: The character of a local doctor can matter as much to patients as their medical knowledge.
records.zomi: Khuasung siavuan khat' omzia in damlo te adingin a damdawi theihna bangin a thupi thei hi.

records.english: Long-serving postal workers often notice changes in a neighbourhood before anyone else does.
records.zomi: Sawt mahmah nasep a sem lai paipih te in inn kiang mite kikhekna te kuamah ma-in a phawk zel uh hi.

records.english: When residents describe a trusted police officer, they usually mention fairness before anything else.
records.zomi: A sung-a teng mite in a muan palik khat a gen uh ciangin na dang khempeuh ma-in a dikna a gen zel uh hi.

records.english: The paramedics were young, but they worked so calmly that my father stopped panicking.
records.zomi: Damdawi nasemte a naupang uh hangin dai mahmah-in a sem uh ahih manin ka pa a lau nawn kei hi.

records.english: Job references for care workers usually describe patience, reliability and respect for the people they support.
records.zomi: Kemtute adingin nasep gen lai te in thuakzawhna, muanhuaina leh a huh mite zahtakna a gen zel uh hi.

records.english: The caretaker at the hall is quiet but helpful.
records.zomi: Inn lian-a kemmi a dai a, ahi zongin a huh siam hi.

records.english: Why do people in the village trust the old postman so much?
records.zomi: Bang hangin khua-a mite in lai paipih upa a muang mahmah uh hiam?

records.english: For thirty years he has noticed who hasn't collected their milk or opened their curtains, and he always checks that they're all right.
records.zomi: Kum sawmthum sung kua in a bawngnawi a la kei a, a puan khai a hong kei hiam cih a phawk a, a hoih uh hiam cih a en den hi.

records.english: The guard at the bus station knows all the timetables.
records.zomi: Bus station kemmi in hun lista khempeuh a thei hi.

records.english: The woman who runs our community café is small, quick and always wearing a flowery apron.
records.zomi: I khuasung cafe makaipa numei pen a neu, a manlang a, pak lim nei puan khuh a bulh den hi.

records.english: She remembers how every regular takes their tea, and she notices at once when someone looks lonely or worried.
records.zomi: A hong den mi khatciat in lapha bangci a dawn uh hiam cih a phawk a, mi khat a khat bek ahih kei leh a lungkham bangin a kilang ciangin pahtakin a phawk hi.

records.english: When she retired last spring, half the neighbourhood came to the café to thank her.
records.zomi: Spring bei-in a nasep a tawp ciangin inn kiang mite' a kim lam in lungdam ko dingin cafe-ah a hong uh hi.

records.english: The firefighter who visited us was very funny.
records.zomi: Hong kan mei sihmi in a nuihuai mahmah hi.

records.english: Is the new head of the community centre as friendly as the old one?
records.zomi: Khuasung inn lian makai thak pen a lui bangin a nuam hiam?

records.english: The councillor who chairs our meetings is patient, but she stops anyone who speaks for too long.
records.zomi: I kikhopna a makai council nu pen a thuakzawh a, ahi zongin sawt lua a gen mi khatpeuh a khawl sak hi.

records.english: Is the social worker easy to talk to?
records.zomi: Mipi huhna nasempa tawh kiho a baih hiam?

records.english: Can you describe the man who runs the food bank?
records.zomi: An piakna mun a makai pa na gen thei ding hiam?

records.english: He's in his sixties, with a grey beard and a loud laugh, and he knows every volunteer by name.
records.zomi: Kum sawmguk kiim a pha a, khamul kang leh nui ging khauh a nei a, thalawp khempeuh' min a thei hi.

records.english: Is the new nurse friendly?
records.zomi: Nurse thak a nuam hiam?

records.english: Our pharmacist is the sort of person who remembers your children's names and asks how they're getting on.
records.zomi: I damdawi zuakpa pen na tate' min a phawk a, bangci om uh hiam cih a dong mi khat ahi hi.

records.english: The woman at the post office is very kind.
records.zomi: Post office-a numei a hehpih mahmah hi.

records.english: Our dentist talks the whole time.
records.zomi: I ha siavuan in hun khempeuh a gen hi.

records.english: Our postman is tall and very cheerful.
records.zomi: I lai paipih a sang a, a lungdam mahmah hi.

records.english: Which librarian helped you with the forms?
records.zomi: Bang laibu inn nasem in lai te-ah hong huh hiam?

records.english: The young one with glasses, who sits by the computers on Tuesdays.
records.zomi: Pithai ni simin computer kiangah a tu mitlimlang nei a naupang zaw nu.

records.english: A good receptionist can shape how patients feel about a whole clinic.
records.zomi: Dawnmi hoih khat in damlo te in damdawi inn neu buppi tungah bangci a kizak uh hiam cih a bawl thei hi.

records.english: Why does everyone describe the old caretaker as the heart of the school?
records.zomi: Bang hangin mi khempeuh in kemmi upa pen sang' lungtang a ci uh hiam?

records.english: How would you describe the new manager at the leisure centre?
records.zomi: Kimawlna inn-a manager thak bangci na gen ding hiam?

records.english: The volunteer driver who takes Grandma to hospital is a retired teacher with endless stories.
records.zomi: Pi damlo inn-ah a paipih thalawp mawngpa pen tangthu a bei lo a nei saya nasep tawp khat ahi hi.

records.english: Communities often realise how much a familiar worker meant to them only after that person has retired.
records.zomi: Khuasung te in a theih den nasem khat a nasep a tawp khit ciangin bek bangzah a manpha hiam cih a theisiam zel uh hi.

records.english: The pharmacist has a soft, kind voice.
records.zomi: Damdawi zuakpa in aw nem leh hehpih a nei hi.

records.english: The midwife who delivered both my children was calm, funny and completely unshockable.
records.zomi: Ka tate nih a suah sak naupang suahsakmi pen a dai, a nuihuai a, bangmah in a lau sak ngei lo hi.

records.english: What does the new police officer look like?
records.zomi: Palik thak bangci a kilang hiam?

records.english: The man who runs the youth club is very energetic.
records.zomi: Tangvalte pawl makaipa a thahat mahmah hi.

records.english: A description of a community leader should rely on what they have done, not on how they look.
records.zomi: Khuasung makaipa khat genna in a kilatzia sangin a nasep te tungah a kinga ding hi.

records.english: People tend to describe service workers by one memorable habit, such as humming or a particular greeting.
records.zomi: Mite in nasem te a ngeina phawk theih khat, hum ahih kei leh cibai tuam bang tawh a gen zel uh hi.

records.english: Why do the stories always happen long ago?
records.zomi: Bang hangin tangthu te hun sawtpi ma-in a piang den hiam?

records.english: Because it lets the storyteller teach a lesson without pointing at anyone in the room.
records.zomi: Bang hang hiam cih leh tangthu genpa in inndan sung-a kuamah a zawn lo-in sinna khat a hilh thei hi.

records.english: Grandpa tells a story every night.
records.zomi: Pu in zan simin tangthu khat a gen hi.

records.english: Dad still remembers his grandfather's stories.
records.zomi: Pa in a pu' tangthu te a phawk lai hi.

records.english: My favourite folktale is about a lazy giant.
records.zomi: Ka deih pen pianpih tangthu pen mi lian thadah khat tawh kisai ahi hi.

records.english: My brother falls asleep halfway through every story.
records.zomi: Ka sanggampa in tangthu khatciat a kim lam-ah a ihmu hi.

records.english: When the family gathers at New Year, the oldest uncle always tells the same story about a stolen harvest.
records.zomi: Kum thak-in innkuan a kikhawm ciangin pa neu a upa pen in buh kiguk tawh kisai tangthu kibang a gen den hi.

records.english: After Grandma died, we found that each grandchild remembered her stories slightly differently.
records.zomi: Pi a sih khit-in tu khatciat in a tangthu te a kibang lo deuh-in a phawk uh hi, cih i mu hi.

records.english: Every time my uncle tells the story of the clever servant, he gives it a new joke.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in sal pil tangthu a gen simin kihahkhuatna thak khat a behlap hi.

records.english: When parents retell the folktales of their own childhood, they often discover lessons they missed as children.
records.zomi: Nu leh pa te in amau' naupan lai-a pianpih tangthu te a gen kik uh ciangin naupan lai-a a mansuah sinna te a mu zel uh hi.

records.english: My husband's family tells a different version of the same story, which causes friendly arguments.
records.zomi: Ka pasal' innkuan in tangthu kibang' a dang khat a gen uh a, tua in lawmta kinialna a piangsak hi.

records.english: Which story did Grandma tell at the wedding?
records.zomi: Mopawi-ah Pi in bang tangthu a gen hiam?

records.english: Mum's stories always have a clever girl in them.
records.zomi: Nu' tangthu te in nungak pil khat a nei den hi.

records.english: Tell the one about the singing frog, please.
records.zomi: Kong ngen hi, la sa ukeng tangthu gen in.

records.english: Why should we record Grandma telling her folktales?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pi in a pianpih tangthu a gen laitak i ciamteh ding hiam?

records.english: Because her voice, her pauses and her jokes are part of the story, and a written copy would lose them.
records.zomi: Bang hang hiam cih leh a aw, a tawlngakna leh a kihahkhuatna te tangthu' a khen ahi a, laigelh copy khat in a mansuah ding hi.

records.english: Did your father tell the same stories in the same way every time?
records.zomi: Na pa in tangthu kibang te hun khempeuh-in a kibang dan-in a gen hiam?

records.english: No, he added new details whenever he saw that we were getting bored.
records.zomi: Hi kei hi, i lungzing ding bangin a mu simin thu thak te a behlap hi.

records.english: Families separated by distance can keep their folktales alive through recordings and video calls.
records.zomi: Gamla-a kikhen innkuan te in ciamtehna leh video sam tawh a pianpih tangthu uh a nungta sak den thei uh hi.

records.english: Children who hear folktales from their grandparents often feel a deeper connection to their family's past.
records.zomi: A pu leh pi uh pan pianpih tangthu a za naupangte in a innkuan' hun bei tawh kizopna thuk zaw a kizak zel uh hi.

records.english: Grandma's stories always end with a lesson.
records.zomi: Pi' tangthu te in sinna khat tawh a tawp den hi.

records.english: Dad makes funny voices for the animals.
records.zomi: Pa in ganhing te adingin aw nuihuai te a bawl hi.

records.english: Grandparents who tell folktales give children a sense of belonging that books alone cannot provide.
records.zomi: Pianpih tangthu a gen pu leh pi te in naupangte laibu bek in a pia thei lo kizopna lungsim a pia uh hi.

records.english: Grandma never tells a story the same way twice.
records.zomi: Pi in tangthu khat nihvei a kibang dan-in a gen ngei kei hi.

records.english: Who taught you all these old stories, Mum?
records.zomi: Nu aw, hih tangthu lui te kua in hong hilh hiam?

records.english: My grandmother did, when we sat together shelling beans in the evenings.
records.zomi: Ka pi in hong hilh hi, nitak simin khawm takin khaukhap i hak laitak.

records.english: My aunt knows the longest folktales.
records.zomi: Ka ni in pianpih tangthu a sau pen te a thei hi.

records.english: The grandchildren recorded Grandpa telling his favourite story on their phones.
records.zomi: Tu te in Pu in a deih pen tangthu a gen laitak a phone uh tawh a ciamteh uh hi.

records.english: We heard a new folktale at Uncle's house.
records.zomi: Pa neu' inn-ah pianpih tangthu thak khat i za hi.

records.english: Grandpa, can you tell the story about the clever monkey again?
records.zomi: Pu aw, zong pil tangthu na gen kik thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, but tonight you can tell me what happens at the end.
records.zomi: Thei hi, ahi zongin tu zan-in a tawpna-ah bang a piang hiam cih na gen ding hi.

records.english: When my daughter was small, she refused to sleep unless I told her the folktale about the girl who talked to the moon.
records.zomi: Ka tanu a neu lai-in kha tawh a kiho nungak pianpih tangthu ka gen kei leh a ihmu nuam kei hi.

records.english: One night I was too tired and tried to shorten it, but she corrected every detail I had left out.
records.zomi: Zan khat-in ka gim lua a, a tom sak ka sawm a, ahi zongin ka nusiat thu khempeuh a bawlphat hi.

records.english: Now she tells the same story to her own little brother, and I notice that she has added a dog.
records.zomi: Tu-in a nau pasal neu kiangah tangthu kibang a gen a, ui khat a behlap hi, cih ka phawk hi.

records.english: The children want the tiger story again.
records.zomi: Naupangte in humpi tangthu a deih kik uh hi.

records.english: Does the poor boy win in the end?
records.zomi: A tawpna-ah tangval zawng a zo hiam?

records.english: Do your children prefer the old folktales or the stories in their picture books?
records.zomi: Na tate in pianpih tangthu lui te a deih zaw uh hiam, lim laibu te-a tangthu te a deih zaw uh hiam?

records.english: In many families, the right to tell a particular story passes quietly from one generation to the next.
records.zomi: Innkuan tampi-ah tangthu khat gen theihna pen suan khat pan suan dang khat-ah a dai takin a pai hi.

records.english: A folktale can give a family a shared way of talking about honesty, greed or courage.
records.zomi: Pianpih tangthu khat in innkuan khat dikna, duhaina ahih kei leh hanna tawh kisai a kiho khawm dan khat a pia thei hi.

records.english: I didn't realise how frightening some of the old stories were until I told them to my own children.
records.zomi: Ka tate kiangah ka gen ma-in tangthu lui khenkhat bangzah a lauhuai hiam cih ka theisiam kei hi.

records.english: Which folktale did your parents tell you when you were afraid of the dark?
records.zomi: Mial na lau lai-in na nu leh pa in bang pianpih tangthu hong gen uh hiam?

records.english: We tell old stories when the lights go out.
records.zomi: Meivak a mit ciangin tangthu lui te i gen hi.

records.english: Folktales told at bedtime often become some of a child's earliest and most lasting memories.
records.zomi: Ihmut hun-a kigen pianpih tangthu te in naupang khat' phawkna masa leh sawt pen te lak-ah a suak zel hi.

records.english: The children acted out Grandpa's story.
records.zomi: Naupangte in Pu' tangthu a lak uh hi.

records.english: Why do Grandpa's stories always have an orphan as the hero?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pu' tangthu te in tagah khat a hanna mi-in a nei den hiam?

records.english: Why does the fox always win?
records.zomi: Bang hangin ngia in a zo den hiam?

records.english: Is that story from your village, Grandpa?
records.zomi: Pu aw, tua tangthu pen na khua pan ahi hiam?

records.english: Folktales told within a family carry the voices of the people who first shared them.
records.zomi: Innkuan sung-a kigen pianpih tangthu te in a masa-a a hawm mite' aw a pua uh hi.

records.english: My father used to stop at the most exciting moment and make us wait until the next night.
records.zomi: Ka pa in a lamdang pen hun-ah a khawl a, a zom zan dong hong ngak sak hi.

records.english: Different branches of a family may keep different versions of the same folktale, each one equally precious.
records.zomi: Innkuan khat' khen tuamtuam in pianpih tangthu kibang' a lim tuamtuam a kem thei uh a, a khatciat a kibang-in a manpha hi.

records.english: My grandmother's folktales were her way of teaching us manners without lecturing.
records.zomi: Ka pi' pianpih tangthu te pen thu hilh lo-in zahtakna ngeina hong hilh dan ahi hi.

records.english: Our children laugh at the foolish king in Grandma's story, but they also learn from his mistakes.
records.zomi: I tate Pi' tangthu-a kumpipa haai a nui uh a, ahi zongin a khialhna pan a sin uh hi.

records.english: Writing down a family's folktales preserves the words, but telling them aloud keeps their spirit alive.
records.zomi: Innkuan khat' pianpih tangthu gelh in kammal te a kem a, ahi zongin aw tawh gen in a lungsim a nungta sak hi.

records.english: When my son was ill, I told him folktales for hours to take his mind off the pain.
records.zomi: Ka tapa a cina laitakin a natna a mangngilh nadingin hun tampi pianpih tangthu ka gen hi.

records.english: I told my son the story my father told me.
records.zomi: Ka pa in hong gen tangthu ka tapa kiangah ka gen hi.

records.english: My cousin wrote down our grandmother's stories.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam in i pi' tangthu te a gelh hi.

records.english: Could you tell the children the story about the two sisters before they go to bed?
records.zomi: A ihmut ma-un naupangte kiangah sanggamnu nih tangthu na gen thei ding hiam?

records.english: Have you ever changed the ending of a folktale to make it kinder for your children?
records.zomi: Na tate adingin a hehpih zaw nadingin pianpih tangthu khat' a tawpna na khek ngei hiam?

records.english: Can you tell us a story, Grandma?
records.zomi: Pi aw, tangthu khat hong gen thei ding na hiam?

records.english: My mother keeps a notebook of the folktales her parents told her.
records.zomi: Ka nu in a nu leh pa in a gen pianpih tangthu te' laibu neu khat a kem hi.

records.english: My husband and I want our children to treat everyone as someone God has made.
records.zomi: Ka pasal leh kei in i tate in mi khempeuh Pasian' bawl mi bangin a kem ding uh i deih hi.

records.english: The belief that God created humanity can shape how a family treats elderly and disabled relatives.
records.zomi: Pasian in mihing a piangsak hi, cih upna in innkuan khat in sanggam upa leh pumpi kicinglohna nei te bangci a kem hiam cih a bawl thei hi.

records.english: Does God love people who look different from us?
records.zomi: Pasian in eite tawh a kibang lo-in a kilang mite a it hiam?

records.english: Yes, Christians believe that every person is made in God's image, whatever they look like.
records.zomi: It hi, Khazih mite in mi khempeuh bangci kilang zongin Pasian lim bangin kibawl ahi hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: Who made the first people?
records.zomi: Mihing masa te kua in a bawl hiam?

records.english: Christian teaching about creation reminds families that their worth does not depend on wealth, beauty or success.
records.zomi: Piansakna tawh kisai Khazih hilhna in innkuan te a manphatna uh pen hauhna, hoihna ahih kei leh zawhna tungah a kinga kei hi, cih a phawk sak hi.

records.english: God made every person special, Grandma says.
records.zomi: Pasian in mi khempeuh a tuam takin a bawl hi, ci-in Pi in a gen hi.

records.english: Our grandmother says that every new grandchild reminds her of God breathing life into Adam.
records.zomi: I pi in tu thak khatciat in Pasian in Adam sungah nuntakna a mut lut hi, cih a phawk sak hi, a ci hi.

records.english: For many believers, the creation of humanity explains why family relationships are seen as sacred.
records.zomi: Upmi tampi adingin mihing piansakna in bang hangin innkuan kizopna te siangtho bangin a kimu hiam cih a gen hi.

records.english: Grandpa prays for every grandchild by name.
records.zomi: Pu in tu khatciat' min lo-in thu a ngen hi.

records.english: We pray for our family every night.
records.zomi: Zan simin i innkuan adingin thu i ngen hi.

records.english: We read about Adam and Eve at home.
records.zomi: Inn-ah Adam leh Eve tawh kisai i sim hi.

records.english: In our family, birthdays begin with a short prayer of thanks for the gift of life.
records.zomi: I innkuan-ah suahni te nuntakna letsong adingin lungdamna thu ngetna tom khat tawh a kipan hi.

records.english: Why do you think God made the first person from the dust of the ground?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pasian in mihing masa pen leitang' leivui pan a bawl hi, na ci hiam?

records.english: Grandma, why does the Bible say we are made from dust?
records.zomi: Pi aw, bang hangin Lai Siangtho in leivui pan kibawl i hi hi, a ci hiam?

records.english: Christians often take it as a reminder that we are humble creatures who depend on God for life.
records.zomi: Khazih mite in nuntakna adingin Pasian tungah a kinga kiniamkhiat ganhing i hih uh phawk sakna khat bangin a la zel uh hi.

records.english: When my daughter asked why God made people, I told her that Christians believe he made us to know and love him.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in bang hangin Pasian in mihing a bawl hiam, ci-in a dot ciangin Khazih mite in amah a theih uh leh a it uh nadingin hong bawl hi, ci-in a um uh hi, ka ci hi.

records.english: Why did God make us different?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pasian in i kibang lo dingin hong bawl hiam?

records.english: My son decided that God must enjoy variety, because he made so many different noses.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in Pasian in a tuamtuam a deih ding hi, bang hang hiam cih leh nak tuamtuam tampi a bawl hi, ci-in a thukhen hi.

records.english: Are all people part of one family?
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh innkuan khat' a khen i hi hiam?

records.english: My brother thinks Adam was very lonely.
records.zomi: Ka sanggampa in Adam a khat bek-in a om mahmah ding hi, ci-in a ngaihsun hi.

records.english: Why does our family pray for people we have never met?
records.zomi: Bang hangin i muh ngei loh mite adingin i innkuan in thu a ngen hiam?

records.english: We believe that every human being is created and loved by God, so their lives matter to us as well.
records.zomi: Mihing khempeuh Pasian in a piangsak a, a it hi, ci-in i um a, tua ahih manin a nuntakna uh eite adingin zong a thupi hi.

records.english: Our family talks about Adam and Eve whenever the children ask where people came from.
records.zomi: Naupangte in mite koi pan a hong pai uh hiam, ci-in a dot uh simin i innkuan in Adam leh Eve tawh kisai a kikum hi.

records.english: My son loves the story of Eden.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in Eden tangthu a deih mahmah hi.

records.english: Why do you say that every baby is a gift from God?
records.zomi: Bang hangin naupang neu khatciat Pasian pan letsong ahi hi, na ci hiam?

records.english: Because I believe that God gives each person life and loves them before they are even born.
records.zomi: Bang hang hiam cih leh Pasian in mi khatciat nuntakna a pia a, a suah ma-un a it hi, ci-in ka um hi.

records.english: My grandmother taught us that every face in the family, wrinkled or new, shows God's handiwork.
records.zomi: Ka pi in innkuan-a mai khempeuh, a kiawn ahih kei leh a thak, Pasian' khut nasep a lak hi, ci-in hong hilh hi.

records.english: Could you explain to the children what it means to be made in God's image?
records.zomi: Pasian lim bangin kibawl cih in bang a cihna hiam cih naupangte kiangah na gen thei ding hiam?

records.english: Mum says God made us to love each other.
records.zomi: Pasian in khat leh khat i kiit nadingin hong bawl hi, ci-in Nu in a gen hi.

records.english: Grandpa reminds us that God gave people the job of looking after the animals on the farm.
records.zomi: Pasian in mite lo-a ganhing te kem nasep a pia hi, ci-in Pu in hong phawk sak hi.

records.english: Mum read Genesis to my baby brother.
records.zomi: Nu in ka nau pasal neu kiangah Piancilna laibu a sim sak hi.

records.english: Dad says nobody is unimportant to God.
records.zomi: Pasian adingin kuamah a thupi lo kei hi, ci-in Pa in a gen hi.

records.english: My sister asked why God made boys and girls.
records.zomi: Ka sanggamnu in bang hangin Pasian in tangval leh nungak a bawl hiam, ci-in a dong hi.

records.english: Grandparents who speak of life as God's gift often help grandchildren face illness and death with hope.
records.zomi: Nuntakna pen Pasian' letsong ahi hi, ci-in a gen pu leh pi te in a tu te natna leh sihna lametna tawh a dawn nadingin a huh zel uh hi.

records.english: Did God make people like him?
records.zomi: Pasian in mite amah bangin a bawl hiam?

records.english: My parents taught me that caring for my elderly grandparents was a way of honouring the life God gave them.
records.zomi: Ka pu leh pi upa te kem pen Pasian in amaute a piak nuntakna zahtakna lampi khat ahi hi, ci-in ka nu leh pa in hong hilh uh hi.

records.english: My daughter asked who the first mother was.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in nu masa pen kua hi hiam, ci-in a dong hi.

records.english: Within one family, Christians may interpret the details of Genesis differently while agreeing on the value of every person.
records.zomi: Innkuan khat sungah Khazih mite in mi khatciat' manphatna-ah a kilungkim uh hangin Piancilna laibu' thu neu te a kibang lo-in a gen thei uh hi.

records.english: The teaching that all people share one origin encourages many Christian families to welcome strangers.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh in kipatna khat a hawm uh hi, cih hilhna in Khazih innkuan tampi khualmite dawn dingin a hanthawn hi.

records.english: Why did God give people a garden?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pasian in mite huan khat a pia hiam?

records.english: After the baby's birth, our church family brought meals and prayed for her every day.
records.zomi: Naupang neu a suah khit-in i pawlpi innkuan in an hong paipih uh a, ni simin amah adingin thu a ngen uh hi.

records.english: Grandma calls each grandchild a blessing.
records.zomi: Pi in tu khatciat thupha khat a ci hi.

records.english: When my son was born, my grandmother held him and said that God had made him with great care.
records.zomi: Ka tapa a suah ciangin ka pi in a pom a, Pasian in amah kem lungsim tampi tawh a bawl hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Years later, when he came home upset because other children had laughed at his ears, I reminded him of her words.
records.zomi: Kum tampi khit-in naupang dangte in a bil a nui uh ahih manin a lungkham-in inn-ah a hong ciah ciangin a kammal te ka phawk sak hi.

records.english: He smiled and said that God must have liked his ears, even if the other children didn't.
records.zomi: Naupang dangte in a deih kei uh hangin Pasian in a bil a deih ding hi, ci-in a nuisuak hi.

records.english: Did God know me before I was born?
records.zomi: Ka suah ma-in Pasian in hong thei hiam?

records.english: Do your children ever ask why God made people in so many colours?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pasian in mite pianzia tuamtuam-in a bawl hiam, ci-in na tate in a dong ngei uh hiam?

records.english: How do you explain to a teenager that their worth comes from God and not from their looks?
records.zomi: Naupang lianno khat kiangah a manphatna pen a kilatzia pan hi lo-in Pasian pan a hong pai hi, cih bangci na gen hiam?

records.english: Many Christian families teach children that every person has dignity because each one is made in God's image.
records.zomi: Khazih innkuan tampi in mi khatciat Pasian lim bangin kibawl ahih manin zahtakna a nei hi, ci-in naupangte a hilh uh hi.

records.english: Did God make Grandpa too?
records.zomi: Pasian in Pu zong a bawl hiam?

records.english: When my father was dying, he told us he was going back to the God who had made him.
records.zomi: Ka pa a sih ding laitakin amah a bawl Pasian kiangah a ciah kik ding hi, ci-in hong gen hi.

records.english: God gave us hands to help others, Dad says.
records.zomi: Pasian in midangte i huh nadingin khut hong pia hi, ci-in Pa in a gen hi.

records.english: How did your parents teach you that people are made in God's image?
records.zomi: Na nu leh pa in mite Pasian lim bangin kibawl ahi hi, cih bangci hong hilh uh hiam?

records.english: They treated every visitor with the same respect, whether the person was rich or poor.
records.zomi: Khualmi khempeuh a hau hiam, a zawng hiam cih nawlkhin lo-in zahtakna kibang tawh a kem uh hi.

records.english: My teenage daughter says that believing she is made in God's image helps her resist pressure from social media.
records.zomi: Ka tanu naupang lianno in Pasian lim bangin kibawl hi, cih um in social media pan nawhna a dal nadingin a huh hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Christian parents often answer questions about where people came from by reading Genesis together with their children.
records.zomi: Khazih nu leh pa te in mite koi pan a hong pai uh hiam cih dotna te a tate tawh Piancilna laibu khawm taka sim-in a dawng zel uh hi.

records.english: God made us to care for the earth, Grandpa says.
records.zomi: Pasian in leitung i kem nadingin hong bawl hi, ci-in Pu in a gen hi.

records.english: Believing that humans were made to care for the earth gives many families a reason to live more simply.
records.zomi: Mihing te leitung kem dingin kibawl ahi hi, cih um in innkuan tampi baih zaw-in a nuntak nading hangsan a pia hi.

records.english: Children who hear that they were made with care may develop a secure sense of their own worth.
records.zomi: Kem lungsim tawh kibawl ahi hi, cih a za naupangte in amau' manphatna tungah lungmuanna a nei thei uh hi.

records.english: Let's take the safer option.
records.zomi: Teelna bit zaw i la ni.

records.english: I decided to ask for help.
records.zomi: Huhna ngen dingin ka thukhen hi.

records.english: I need to decide by Friday.
records.zomi: Laithai ni ma-in ka thukhen ding a kisam hi.

records.english: We'll decide together tomorrow.
records.zomi: Zing-in khawm takin i thukhen ding hi.

records.english: Should I return the shoes or keep them?
records.zomi: Khedap ka pia kik ding hiam, ka kem ding hiam?

records.english: Decisions based on money alone can create new problems that cost more in the end.
records.zomi: Sum bek tungah kinga thukhensatna te in a tawpna-ah a man tam zaw buaina thak te a piangsak thei hi.

records.english: Deciding what the real problem is often matters more than choosing a solution quickly.
records.zomi: Buaina taktak bang ahi hiam cih thukhen pen phelna khat manlang taka teel sangin a thupi zaw zel hi.

records.english: I'll decide when I know the price.
records.zomi: A man ka theih ciangin ka thukhen ding hi.

records.english: Should we cancel the trip or go later?
records.zomi: Khualzinna i nusia ding hiam, a nunung-in i pai ding hiam?

records.english: We decided to sell the old car.
records.zomi: Mawtaw lui zuak dingin i thukhen hi.

records.english: What should we do if the group can't agree on a solution?
records.zomi: Pawl in phelna khat-ah a kilungkim zo kei leh bang i bawl ding hiam?

records.english: Agree first on how you'll decide, such as a vote or letting the person most affected choose.
records.zomi: Vote ahih kei leh a khawng pen mi teel sak bang bangci thukhen ding hiam cih tungah a masa-in kilungkim un.

records.english: In an emergency, a reasonable decision made quickly is often better than a perfect one made too late.
records.zomi: Lauhuai hun-in manlang taka kibawl thukhensatna kituak khat pen nunung lua-a kibawl a kicing khat sangin a hoih zaw zel hi.

records.english: The team decided to test both solutions for a week before choosing one.
records.zomi: Pawl in khat a teel ma-un phelna nih tuak kal khat sung sit dingin a thukhen uh hi.

records.english: Should we wait for the bus or walk?
records.zomi: Bus i ngak ding hiam, kalsuan-in i pai ding hiam?

records.english: Let's make a list before we decide.
records.zomi: I thukhen ma-in lista khat i bawl ni.

records.english: My parents decided to rent out a room to help with the rising bills.
records.zomi: Man lai khang te huh nadingin ka nu leh pa in inndan khat hal sak dingin a thukhen uh hi.

records.english: Should I tell my manager about the mistake now or wait until Monday?
records.zomi: Ka khialhna tawh kisai ka manager kiangah tu-in ka gen ding hiam, Pizing ni dong ka ngak ding hiam?

records.english: Tell your manager today, because problems are easier to fix before anyone else finds them.
records.zomi: Tuni-in na manager kiangah gen in, bang hang hiam cih leh buaina te mi dang in a muh ma-un bawlphat a baih zaw hi.

records.english: After many complaints, the shop decided to change its return policy.
records.zomi: Phunna tampi khit-in van zuakna inn in a pia kik thukham a khek dingin a thukhen hi.

records.english: We chose the cheaper repair.
records.zomi: Bawlphatna man niam zaw i teel hi.

records.english: I made the wrong choice, so I'll fix it.
records.zomi: Teelna khial ka bawl a, tua ahih manin ka bawlphat ding hi.

records.english: When a decision is difficult to reverse, it is worth gathering more information first.
records.zomi: Thukhensatna khat a khek kik haksat ciangin thu tam zaw kaikhawm masa a manpha hi.

records.english: How did your family decide what to do when Grandpa could no longer live alone?
records.zomi: Pu a khat bek-in a teng thei nawn kei ciangin na innkuan in bang bawl ding hiam cih bangci a thukhen uh hiam?

records.english: We listed every option, visited two care homes, and then let Grandpa choose, since it was his life that would change most.
records.zomi: Teelna khempeuh i gelh a, kemna inn nih i kan a, tua khit-in Pu a teel sak hi, bang hang hiam cih leh a kikhek pen ding pen amah' nuntakna ahi hi.

records.english: Good decisions in a crisis usually come from calm, simple questions about what matters most.
records.zomi: Buaina lian khat sung-a thukhensatna hoih te pen bang in a thupi pen hiam cih tawh kisai lungdai leh baih dotna te pan a hong pai zel hi.

records.english: We decided to fix the roof first.
records.zomi: Inntung a masa-in bawlphat dingin i thukhen hi.

records.english: Once we'd decided who was responsible for each task, the problem was solved within a day.
records.zomi: Nasep khatciat adingin kua in mawhpuakna a nei hiam cih i thukhen khit-in ni khat sungin buaina a kiphel hi.

records.english: Is it too late to change our plan?
records.zomi: I ngimna khek dingin a nunung lua khin hiam?

records.english: Can we decide tonight what to do about the broken car?
records.zomi: Mawtaw siat tawh kisai bang bawl ding hiam cih tu zan-in i thukhen thei ding hiam?

records.english: Let's wait until the garage gives us a price, so that we're not guessing.
records.zomi: I ngaihsut lohna dingin garage in man hong gen mateng i ngak ni.

records.english: Admitting that a decision was wrong and changing it is a sign of good judgement, not weakness.
records.zomi: Thukhensatna khat a khial hi, ci-in pom a khek pen pilna hoih lahna ahi a, hatlohna hi lo hi.

records.english: A small decision made today can prevent a much harder one later.
records.zomi: Tuni-a kibawl thukhensatna neu khat in a nunung-a thukhensatna haksa zaw mahmah khat a kham thei hi.

records.english: We decided to move the meeting online when half the team was ill.
records.zomi: Pawl' a kim lam a cina ciangin kikhopna online-ah khek dingin i thukhen hi.

records.english: We decided against borrowing money and cut our spending instead.
records.zomi: Sum leipuk lo dingin i thukhen a, tua sangin i sum zat i kiam sak hi.

records.english: If we can't afford both repairs this month, which one should we do first?
records.zomi: Hih kha-in bawlphatna nih tuak i pia zo kei leh bang a masa-in i bawl ding hiam?

records.english: Let's decide after we've asked the landlord.
records.zomi: Inn neipa i dot khit-in i thukhen ni.

records.english: The committee decided to delay the festival rather than hold it in the rain.
records.zomi: Pawl neu in guah sungah bawl sangin pawi nunung sak dingin a thukhen hi.

records.english: Decisions about shared problems are easier to accept when everyone affected has been heard.
records.zomi: Buaina kihawm tawh kisai thukhensatna te pen a khawng mi khempeuh' thu a kizak ciangin san a baih zaw hi.

records.english: I've decided to call the plumber.
records.zomi: Tuikuang bawlmi sam dingin ka thukhen hi.

records.english: People often avoid deciding because they fear being blamed if the choice goes wrong.
records.zomi: Teelna a khial leh mawhsak a kilau uh ahih manin mite in thukhen a pelh zel uh hi.

records.english: Who should decide about the broken fence?
records.zomi: Huang siat tawh kisai kua in a thukhen ding hiam?

records.english: Is it better to decide quickly when a pipe bursts, or to wait for a second opinion?
records.zomi: Tuikuang a keh ciangin manlang takin thukhen a hoih zaw hiam, mi dang ngaihsutna ngak a hoih zaw hiam?

records.english: When our shop's rent doubled, my sister and I had a month to decide whether to move, close or try to stay.
records.zomi: I van zuakna inn' inn man a nihvei khan ciangin ka sanggamnu leh kei in pem ding, khak ding ahih kei leh om den ding cih thukhen dingin kha khat i nei hi.

records.english: We sat down every evening with the accounts, and slowly it became clear that staying would ruin us within a year.
records.zomi: Nitak simin sum ciamtehna te tawh i tu a, om den in kum khat sungin hong susia ding hi, cih zawlzawl-in a kician hi.

records.english: We moved to a smaller unit across the road, and most of our regular customers followed us.
records.zomi: Lampi galkhat-a mun neu zaw khat-ah i pem a, i lei mi ngeina tampi in hong zui uh hi.

records.english: We decided to sleep on the problem, and by morning the answer seemed obvious.
records.zomi: Buaina tungah ihmu masa dingin i thukhen a, zingsang-in dawnna a kilang mahmah hi.

records.english: Could you look at both quotes with me before I choose?
records.zomi: Ka teel ma-in man genna nih tuak kei tawh na en thei ding hiam?

records.english: When the school bus was cancelled, the parents decided to share the driving.
records.zomi: Sang bus a kinusia ciangin nu leh pa te in mawtaw mawngna a hawm dingin a thukhen uh hi.

records.english: Reviewing a decision after the problem is solved helps people choose better next time.
records.zomi: Buaina a kiphel khit-in thukhensatna khat en kik in mite a zom vei-in a teel hoih zaw nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: How do you decide whether a problem needs a professional or can be fixed at home?
records.zomi: Buaina khat siam mi a kisam hiam, inn-ah bawlphat theih hiam cih bangci na thukhen hiam?

records.english: Should I accept the cheaper offer, even though the seller seems unreliable?
records.zomi: Zuakmi a muanhuai lo bangin a kilang hangin man niam zaw piakna ka sang ding hiam?

records.english: Breaking a large problem into smaller decisions can make it feel far more manageable.
records.zomi: Buaina lian khat thukhensatna neu te-ah khen in a bawl baih zaw mahmah bangin a kizak sak thei hi.

records.english: Setting a deadline for a decision can stop a problem from growing while people keep hesitating.
records.zomi: Thukhensatna khat adingin hun ciang koih in mite a lau laitak-un buaina khat a khan lohna a kham thei hi.

records.english: How did you decide which bill to pay first?
records.zomi: Bang man lai a masa-in pia ding hiam cih bangci na thukhen hiam?

records.english: We paid the rent and the electricity first, because missing those would cause the biggest problems.
records.zomi: Inn man leh meivak tha man i pia masa hi, bang hang hiam cih leh tua te mansuah in buaina lian pen a piangsak ding hi.

records.english: Before deciding to quit, I spoke to my manager about reducing my hours.
records.zomi: Nusiat dingin ka thukhen ma-in ka nasep hun kiam sak nading ka manager tawh ka kikum hi.

records.english: What's the safest choice here?
records.zomi: Hih mun-ah teelna bit pen bang ahi hiam?

records.english: What helped you decide to change schools when your son was unhappy?
records.zomi: Na tapa a lungkim lo ciangin sang khek dingin bang in hong huh hiam?

records.english: Should I call the doctor tonight?
records.zomi: Tu zan-in siavuan ka sam ding hiam?

records.english: The test isn't finished yet.
records.zomi: Sitna a zo nai kei hi.

records.english: Why did the jury take so long to reach a verdict?
records.zomi: Bang hangin thukhenmi pawl in thukhensatna a tun nadingin hun sawt mahmah a la uh hiam?

records.english: Did the test prove anything?
records.zomi: Sitna in bangmah a lak cian hiam?

records.english: Why did you decide that?
records.zomi: Bang hangin tua na thukhen hiam?

records.english: Why do you think the shop has closed for good?
records.zomi: Bang hangin van zuakna inn a tawntung-in a kikhak hi, na ci hiam?

records.english: The windows are empty and there's a sign from an estate agent on the door.
records.zomi: Tawhkhuak te a lawn a, kongkhak tungah inn zuakna company' lim tangna khat a om hi.

records.english: Should we trust a conclusion that the researchers themselves call uncertain?
records.zomi: Sui-sinmite mahmah in a kician lo hi, a cih tawpna ngaihsutna khat i muang ding hiam?

records.english: What would make you change your conclusion?
records.zomi: Bang in na tawpna ngaihsutna a khek sak ding hiam?

records.english: Can a conclusion be reasonable even if it later turns out to be wrong?

records.english: Goals set by others may be useful, but goals people choose for themselves usually last longer.

records.english: The national post office is in the capital.

records.english: In federal countries, states can try different policies, and others can learn from the results.

records.english: Can I renew my licence online?

records.english: Who checks the safety of our food?

records.english: Why does the state take so long to approve permits for new businesses?
records.zomi: Bang hangin gam khen ukpi in sumbawlna thak te adingin phalna lai te a pia nadingin hun sawt mahmah a la hiam?

records.english: Cooperation between state and national agencies is essential during large emergencies.
records.zomi: Lauhuai hun lian te sungin gam khen leh gam pawl te kikal-a kithuahna a kisam mahmah hi.

records.english: The national park is open to everyone.
records.zomi: Gam park pen mi khempeuh adingin a kihong hi.

records.english: Who runs the hospitals here?
records.zomi: Hih mun-ah damlo inn te kua in a makai hiam?

records.english: The state health department runs most of them, using money from both the state and national budgets.

records.english: Can the state help farmers after a drought?
records.zomi: Khuakhal khit-in gam khen ukpi in lo neite a huh thei hiam?

records.english: Yes, the state agriculture office offers emergency grants and cheap loans.
records.zomi: Thei hi, gam khen lo nasep office in lauhuai hun huhna sum leh leiba man niam te a pia hi.

records.english: When responsibilities overlap, problems can fall between the gaps and remain unsolved.
records.zomi: Mawhpuakna te a kikhum ciangin buaina te kikal kua-ah a kia thei a, a phel lo-in a om thei hi.

records.english: How does national funding reach services in our town?

records.english: The national government gives money to the state, and the state passes part of it to local councils for schools, clinics and roads.
records.zomi: Gam ukpi in gam khen kiangah sum a pia a, gam khen in a khenkhat sang, damdawi inn neu leh lampi te adingin khuasung council te kiangah a pia hi.

records.english: The national government pays for the army.
records.zomi: Gam ukpi in galkap te a pia hi.

records.english: The national health service pays for vaccines, but the state organises the clinics where they're given.
records.zomi: Gam cidamna nasep in natna kham nading tun man a pia a, ahi zongin gam khen in a kipiakna damdawi inn neu te a bawl hi.

records.english: National funding allows poorer regions to provide services that their own taxes could not pay for.
records.zomi: Gam sum piakna in gam khen zawng te in amau' siah in a pia zo lo nasep te a pia theih nadingin a bawl hi.

records.english: Representatives who listen to their constituents can bring local problems to the attention of national leaders.
records.zomi: A aiawh mite a ngai aiawhmite in khuasung buaina te gam makaite' theih nadingin a paipih thei uh hi.

records.english: Is the job centre run by the state?

records.english: Why does the state office ask for documents the national office already has?
records.zomi: Bang hangin gam khen office in gam office in a nei khin laigelh te a ngen hiam?

records.english: The two systems aren't fully connected yet, so each one keeps its own records.
records.zomi: A zatna dan nih a bup-in a kizom nai kei ahih manin a khatciat in amau' ciamtehna a kem uh hi.

records.english: Who should I contact if my state pension payment hasn't arrived?
records.zomi: Ka gam khen pension sum a tung kei leh kua kiangah ka kizom ding hiam?

records.english: The national government's new website lets citizens apply for many documents without visiting an office.
records.zomi: Gam ukpi' website thak in gam mite office kan lo-in laigelh tampi a ngen theih nadingin a phal hi.

records.english: The state's employment office runs free training courses for people who have lost their jobs.
records.zomi: Gam khen' nasep office in a nasep a mansuah mite adingin kisinna man om lo te a bawl hi.

records.english: The national library has a reading room.
records.zomi: Gam laibu inn in laisimna inndan khat a nei hi.

records.english: The state paid for the new bridge.
records.zomi: Gam khen ukpi in lei thak man a pia hi.

records.english: State health inspectors visit every restaurant at least once a year.
records.zomi: Gam khen cidamna enmi te in kum khat-ah an ne inn khempeuh a tawm pen-in vei khat a kan uh hi.

records.english: In our country, national laws protect workers' basic rights, but each state can add further protections.
records.zomi: I gam-ah gam thukham te in nasemte' thuneihna bulpi te a kem a, ahi zongin gam khen khatciat in kemna behlap a koih thei hi.

records.english: Clear information about which government provides a service helps people get help more quickly.
records.zomi: Bang ukpi in nasep khat a pia hiam cih thu cian in mite huhna a manlang zaw-in a ngah nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Who pays for the new school?
records.zomi: Sang thak man kua in a pia hiam?

records.english: How can citizens tell which level of government is responsible for a particular service?
records.zomi: Gam mite in nasep khat adingin bang ukpi ciang in mawhpuakna a nei hiam cih bangci a thei thei uh hiam?

records.english: Our governor opened the new hospital.
records.zomi: I gam khen ukpa in damlo inn thak a hong hi.

records.english: Online services have made it easier for citizens to deal with government offices without travelling.
records.zomi: Online nasep te in gam mite khualzin lo-in ukpi office te tawh a kizop baih zaw nadingin a bawl hi.

records.english: Is it the state or the national government that decides how much teachers are paid?
records.zomi: Saya te khasum bangzah pia ding hiam cih gam khen ukpi in a thukhen hiam, gam ukpi in a thukhen hiam?

records.english: The national parliament debated whether to give states more control over their own taxes.
records.zomi: Gam kikhopna lian in gam khen te a siah uh tungah thuneihna tam zaw pia ding hiam cih a kinial uh hi.

records.english: The national weather service warned us about the storm.

records.english: Good public services depend on governments at different levels working together rather than blaming each other.
records.zomi: Mipi nasep hoih te pen ukpi ciang tuamtuam te khat leh khat kimawhsak sangin a kithuah uh tungah a kinga hi.

records.english: When our state's only children's hospital was threatened with closure, parents from every district travelled to the state capital.

records.english: They stood outside the parliament building with photographs of their children, while the health minister met a small group inside.
records.zomi: A tate uh' photo te tawh kikhopna lian inn pua-ah a ding uh a, cidamna makaipa in a sung-ah pawl neu khat a kimupih hi.

records.english: A week later, the state announced that the hospital would stay open, with extra money from the national government.
records.zomi: Kal khat khit-in gam khen in gam ukpi pan sum behlap tawh damlo inn a kihong den ding hi, ci-in a tangko hi.

records.english: Public trust grows when governments at every level explain their decisions openly.
records.zomi: Ukpi ciang khempeuh in a thukhensatna uh a kilang takin a gen uh ciangin mipi muanna a khang hi.

records.english: Strong state services can respond to local needs that national planners may not notice.
records.zomi: Gam khen nasep khauh te in gam ngimmite in a phawk loh khuasung kisapna te a dawng thei uh hi.

records.english: Our state introduced free school meals, while neighbouring states chose not to.
records.zomi: I gam khen in sang-a an man om lo a koih a, a kiang-a gam khen te in a koih lo dingin a teel uh hi.

records.english: Could our representative ask the state to build a clinic in our district?
records.zomi: I aiawhpa in gam khen kiangah i khen-ah damdawi inn neu khat lam dingin a ngen thei ding hiam?

records.english: The state built a new road to our town.
records.zomi: Gam khen ukpi in i khuapi dong lampi thak khat a bawl hi.

records.english: The national statistics office uses the census to plan where new schools and hospitals are needed.
records.zomi: Gam nambat office in sang thak leh damlo inn thak te koi-ah a kisam hiam cih ngim nadingin gam mi simna a zang hi.

records.english: The national tax office sent me a letter.
records.zomi: Gam siah inn in lai khat hong khak hi.

records.english: Citizens often find it confusing that different levels of government share responsibility for the same service.
records.zomi: Ukpi ciang tuamtuam in nasep kibang adingin mawhpuakna a hawm uh pen gam mite in a lungbuai huai sa zel uh hi.

records.english: The state transport department added more trains after commuters complained about overcrowding.
records.zomi: Ni sim nasep-a pai mite in mi dim lua thu a phun khit-in gam khen lampi pai khen in meileng tam zaw a behlap hi.

records.english: The minister visited our clinic today.
records.zomi: Tuni-in ukpi makaipa in i damdawi inn neu a kan hi.

records.english: The state runs our public hospitals.
records.zomi: Gam khen ukpi in i mipi damlo inn te a makai hi.

records.english: Which office handles national pensions?
records.zomi: Bang office in gam pension te a bawl hiam?

records.english: Our state gives free bus passes to students.
records.zomi: I gam khen in sangnaupangte bus pass man om lo a pia hi.

records.english: Debates about how much power states should have are common in many countries with federal systems.
records.zomi: Gam khen te in thuneihna bangzah a nei ding uh hiam cih tawh kisai kinialna te gam khen kigawm gam tampi-ah a om zel hi.

records.english: Does the state help families with childcare?
records.zomi: Gam khen ukpi in naupang kemna-ah innkuan te a huh hiam?

records.english: Which government pays for the motorway repairs?
records.zomi: Bang ukpi in lampi lian bawlphatna man a pia hiam?

records.english: In our country, the national roads agency pays for motorways, while the state looks after smaller main roads.
records.zomi: I gam-ah gam lampi kemna pawl in lampi lian te man a pia a, gam khen in lampi lian neu zaw te a kem hi.

records.english: Our state has its own police force.
records.zomi: I gam khen in amah' palik pawl a nei hi.

records.english: The state office opens at nine.
records.zomi: Gam khen office pen nai kua-in a kihong hi.

records.english: After the storm, state workers repaired power lines while the national army cleared the roads.
records.zomi: Huihpi khit-in gam khen nasemte in meivak khau te a bawlphat uh a, gam galkap te in lampi te a sianghsak uh hi.

records.english: The bus company asks passengers to hold on while standing, especially on sharp bends.
records.zomi: Bus company in a ding tuangmite in a kikawi mahmah lampi te-ah a len ding uh hi, ci-in a ngen hi.

records.english: Don't lean over the bridge railing.
records.zomi: Lei len theihna tungah kun kei in.

records.english: Lifeguards and park staff often explain the reasons behind rules, because people follow rules they understand.
records.zomi: Tuipeek kemmite leh park nasemte in thukham te' hangsan a gen zel uh hi, bang hang hiam cih leh mite in a theisiam uh thukham te a zui uh hi.

records.english: How often does the council check that the safety signs in the parks are still clear?
records.zomi: Council in park te-a bitna lim tangna te a kician lai hiam cih bangzah vei a en hiam?

records.english: Are the safety instructions at the swimming pool available in large print?
records.zomi: Tuipeek mun-a bitna thuhilhna te lai lian tawh a om hiam?

records.english: Keep dogs on a lead in the park.
records.zomi: Park sungah ui te khau tawh len den in.

records.english: Don't climb on the statues.
records.zomi: Lim kibawl te tungah kah kei un.

records.english: Public services review their safety instructions after accidents so that the same mistakes are not repeated.
records.zomi: Mipi nasep te in khialhna kibang a kibawl kik lohna dingin kisiatna khit-in a bitna thuhilhna uh a en kik uh hi.

records.english: Please wear a helmet on the ice rink.
records.zomi: Kong ngen hi, tuikhal tunga kimawlna mun-ah lukhu khauh khu un.

records.english: Stand behind the yellow line on the platform.

records.english: Testing safety notices with real users helps councils discover which instructions are confusing.
records.zomi: Zangmi taktak te tawh bitna thu tangna te sit in council te in bang thuhilhna te a lungbuai huai hiam cih a mu uh hi.

records.english: The beach patrol explains the meaning of each flag to visitors at the start of the day.
records.zomi: Tuipi gei kemmite in ni' kipatna-ah khualmite kiangah puanzar khatciat' cihna a gen uh hi.

records.english: Can my child use the slide alone?

records.english: Is it safe to drink the water from the fountain?

records.english: Visitors to the farm park are asked to wash their hands before eating, because animals can carry germs.

records.english: Keep away from the building site.

records.english: Don't swim when the red flag is up.

records.english: Why does the library ask parents to stay with young children?

records.english: Because staff can't supervise every child, and the stairs and lifts can be dangerous for little ones on their own.
records.zomi: Bang hang hiam cih leh nasemte in naupang khempeuh a kem zo kei uh a, kahlei te leh lift te in a khat bek-a om naupang neu te adingin a lauhuai thei hi.

records.english: Why does the pool have so many rules on the wall?
records.zomi: Bang hangin tuipeek mun kul tungah thukham tampi a om hiam?

records.english: Each one is there because of an accident that happened somewhere, so they really matter.
records.zomi: A khatciat pen mun khat-ah a piang kisiatna khat hangin a om ahih manin a thupi taktak hi.

records.english: Safety instructions in public places are most effective when they are short, clear and placed where people need them.
records.zomi: Mipi mun te-a bitna thuhilhna te pen a tom a, a kician a, mite in a kisam mun-ah a kikoih ciangin a hoih pen-in a sem hi.

records.english: Use the crossing by the school.

records.english: A safety inspection before a public event can prevent accidents that would be difficult to deal with on the day.
records.zomi: Mipi pawi khat ma-in bitna enna in tua ni-in bawl a haksa ding kisiatna te a kham thei hi.

records.english: Before the summer festival, the council's safety officer walked around the park with the organisers.

records.english: She pointed out a loose cable, a gap in the fence by the pond and a stall placed too close to the fire exit.

records.english: By the morning of the festival, every problem had been fixed, and the day passed without a single injury.

records.english: Instructions that tell people what to do, rather than only what not to do, are usually easier to follow.

records.english: The museum asks visitors not to touch the old machines, because some parts are still sharp.

records.english: Please don't run near the pool.

records.english: Volunteers at the community garden must read the safety rules before using the power tools.
records.zomi: Khuasung huan-a thalawp te in meivak tha nasep van te a zat ma-un bitna thukham te a sim ding uh hi.

records.english: The library's new safety notice tells parents where to meet staff if the alarm sounds.
records.zomi: Laibu inn' bitna thu tangna thak in vaukhakna a ging leh koi-ah nasemte kimu ding hiam cih nu leh pa te a gen hi.

records.english: Wash your hands after touching the animals.
records.zomi: Ganhing te na tawk khit-in na khut sil in.

records.english: Where should I wait during the fire drill?
records.zomi: Mei kang kisinna laitakin koi-ah ka ngak ding hiam?

records.english: The community centre added pictures to its fire instructions so that young children could follow them.
records.zomi: Khuasung inn lian in naupang neu te in a zuih theih nadingin a mei thuhilhna te-ah lim te a behlap hi.

records.english: Read the sign before you enter the lake.
records.zomi: Dil sungah na lut ma-in lim tangna sim in.

records.english: Don't feed the animals at the farm park.
records.zomi: Lo park-ah ganhing te an pia kei un.

records.english: Large-print and audio versions of safety instructions make public spaces safer for people with poor eyesight.
records.zomi: Lai lian leh aw tawh bitna thuhilhna te in mit hoih lo mite adingin mipi mun te a bit zaw sak hi.

records.english: How does the council make sure everyone understands its safety warnings?
records.zomi: Council in mi khempeuh in a bitna vaukhakna te a theisiam uh hiam cih bangci a en cian hiam?

records.english: It uses simple words, pictures and several languages, and it tests new signs with residents before printing them.
records.zomi: Kammal baih te, lim te leh pau tampi a zang a, a kheh ma-in a sung-a teng mite tawh lim tangna thak te a sit hi.

records.english: Switch off your engine while you wait.
records.zomi: Na ngak laitakin na mawtaw khawl phiat in.

records.english: Could the council put up signs warning drivers about children crossing near the park?
records.zomi: Council in park kiang-a lampi a kan naupangte tawh kisai mawtaw mawngmite vaukhakna lim tangna te a koih thei ding hiam?

records.english: Pictures and symbols allow public safety signs to reach people who cannot read the local language.
records.zomi: Lim te leh lim tangna te in mipi bitna lim tangna te khuasung pau sim thei lo mite a tun theih nadingin a bawl hi.

records.english: Public safety campaigns are more successful when they involve schools, families and local groups.
records.zomi: Mipi bitna nasep te sang te, innkuan te leh khuasung pawl te a hel ciangin a zawh zaw zel hi.

records.english: Clear safety instructions at community events protect both visitors and the volunteers who organise them.
records.zomi: Khuasung pawi te-a bitna thuhilhna cian te in khualmite leh a bawl thalawp te tuak a kem hi.

records.english: Keep the gate closed at the playground.
records.zomi: Naupang kimawlna mun-ah kongpi khak den in.

records.english: Please follow the arrows to the exit.
records.zomi: Kong ngen hi, khiatna dong zang lim te zui in.

records.english: Safety rules in shared spaces work only when most people follow them, so friendly reminders matter.
records.zomi: Mun kihawm te-a bitna thukham te mi tampi in a zui uh ciangin bek a sem a, tua ahih manin lawmta phawk sakna te a thupi hi.

records.english: What should I do if I smell gas in the street?
records.zomi: Lampi-ah gas gim ka zak leh bang ka bawl ding hiam?

records.english: Move away, don't use your phone near the smell, and call the gas emergency line from a safe distance.

records.english: When my laptop died the night before my thesis deadline, I posted a message in the class group asking whether anyone could lend me a computer.

records.english: Within ten minutes, three classmates had replied, and one of them drove across town with a spare laptop and a hard drive to recover my files.

records.english: I handed in the thesis on time, and I still owe that friend several dinners.

records.english: Could you lend me a charger?

records.english: I asked my neighbour for help when the pipe burst, and he knew exactly where the water valve was.

records.english: Asking for help with money problems is difficult, but free advice services can prevent serious debt.
