records.english: The day the bridge opened, we walked across it.
records.zomi: Lei a kihon ni-in i kan uh hi.

records.english: The memorial day for the miners began with a silence that even the youngest children respected.
records.zomi: Suangtum laihmite' phawkna ni pen naupang neu pen te zong in a zahtak daina tawh a kipan hi.

records.english: How would you describe the day the town welcomed the refugee families?
records.zomi: Khuapi in galtai innkuan te a dawn ni bangci na gen ding hiam?

records.english: The church hall was full of food and flowers, and the children were playing football together before the speeches had ended.
records.zomi: Biakinn inn lian an leh pak te tawh a dim a, thugenna te a bei ma-in naupangte khawm takin football a mawl uh hi.

records.english: When a public service opens or reopens, residents often remember the day for years.
records.zomi: Mipi nasep khat a kihon ahih kei leh a kihon kik ciangin a sung-a teng mite in kum tampi sung tua ni a phawk zel uh hi.

records.english: I'll always remember the morning the whole street helped my grandmother move into her new flat.
records.zomi: Lampi buppi in ka pi a inn thak-ah a pem nadingin a huh zingsang ka phawk den ding hi.

records.english: When the river path finally reopened, families walked its whole length on the first Sunday.
records.zomi: Lui lampi a tawpna-ah a kihon kik ciangin innkuan te Nipini masa pen-in a sau buppi a kalsuan uh hi.

records.english: The day our neighbourhood finally got its own bus route, the first bus left the stop at seven in the morning.
records.zomi: I inn kiang mite in amau' bus lampi a ngah ni-in bus masa pen zingsang nai sagih-in khawlna pan a pai khia hi.

records.english: Older residents who had walked to the main road for years climbed on board in their best clothes, and the driver sounded the horn as the bus pulled away.
records.zomi: Kum tampi sung lampi lian dong a pai a sung-a teng upa te in a puan hoih pen uh silh-in a tuang uh a, bus a pai khiat ciangin mawngpa in a mut ging a suah hi.

records.english: That evening, someone tied a ribbon to the new bus stop sign, and it stayed there all summer.
records.zomi: Tua nitak-in mi khat in bus khawlna lim tangna thak tungah puan khau khat a kaih a, khal buppi tua mun-ah a om hi.

records.english: Do you remember the day the ambulance came to our street?
records.zomi: Damlo mawtaw i lampi-ah a hong ni na phawk hiam?

records.english: Yes, the whole street waited outside until we heard that Mr Lal was all right.
records.zomi: Phawk hi, Pu Lal a hoih hi, cih i zak mateng lampi buppi pua-ah a ngak uh hi.

records.english: The day the food bank opened its new building, volunteers formed a chain to carry boxes from the old one.
records.zomi: An piakna mun in a inn thak a hon ni-in thalawp te in a lui pan box te pua nadingin a kizui-in a ding uh hi.

records.english: The festival day ended with fireworks.
records.zomi: Pawi ni pen mei vak tumna tawh a tawp hi.

records.english: A memorable day for one family may be a routine working day for the staff who made it possible.
records.zomi: Innkuan khat adingin ni phawk huai khat pen a theih theih sak nasemte adingin nasep ni ngeina khat ahi thei hi.

records.english: Shared public events can turn an ordinary day into a memory that a whole neighbourhood keeps.
records.zomi: Mipi pawi kihawm te in ni ngeina khat inn kiang mite buppi in a kem phawkna khat-ah a khek thei hi.

records.english: What do you remember about the day the new library opened?
records.zomi: Laibu inn thak a kihon ni tawh kisai bang na phawk hiam?

records.english: The queue went round the block, and the children ran straight to the picture books.
records.zomi: Kizui ngakna in inn kim a vel a, naupangte lim laibu te kiangah a tai pah uh hi.

records.english: The day the youth club won its grant, the teenagers painted a giant thank-you banner for the council.
records.zomi: Tangvalte pawl in a huhna sum a ngah ni-in naupang lianno te in council adingin lungdamna puan lian khat a zuh uh hi.

records.english: Why do so many people remember the day the clinic reopened after the fire?
records.zomi: Bang hangin mi tampi in mei kang khit-a damdawi inn neu a kihon kik ni a phawk uh hiam?

records.english: Because the staff had worked for months in temporary rooms, and when the doors opened, patients clapped as the nurses walked in.
records.zomi: Bang hang hiam cih leh nasemte kha tampi sung hun tomkhat inndan te-ah a sem uh a, kongkhak a kihon ciangin nurse te a lut uh laitakin damlo te in khut a beng uh hi.

records.english: Our school concert in the town hall was unforgettable.
records.zomi: Khuapi heutu inn-a i sang la pawi pen mangngilh theih loh ahi hi.

records.english: Do you remember the day the snow closed the roads?
records.zomi: Vuk in lampi te a khak ni na phawk hiam?

records.english: Can we record you singing, Grandpa?
records.zomi: Pu aw, la na sak laitak i ciamteh thei ding hiam?

records.english: We sing together on long car journeys.
records.zomi: Mawtaw tunga khualzinna sau te-ah khawm takin la i sa hi.

records.english: Family songs can comfort people in illness and grief when ordinary words fail.
records.zomi: Kammal ngeina te in a zawh loh ciangin innkuan la te in natna leh dahna sungah mite a lungmuang sak thei hi.

records.english: Recording elderly relatives singing preserves both the songs and the voices that gave them meaning.
records.zomi: Sanggam upa te la a sak laitak ciamteh in la te leh tua la te' cihna a pia aw te tuak a kem hi.

records.english: When families scattered across countries sing the same songs, they keep a shared identity alive.
records.zomi: Gam tuamtuam-ah a kithe innkuan te in la kibang a sak uh ciangin a kua uh hiam cih kihawm a nungta sak den uh hi.

records.english: Our family has a song that we sing only when someone leaves home for a long time.
records.zomi: I innkuan in mi khat hun sawt sung inn a nusiat ciangin bek i sak la khat a nei hi.

records.english: Which song did Grandpa sing to you as a baby?
records.zomi: Naupang neu na hih lai-in Pu in bang la hong sak sak hiam?

records.english: After Grandpa died, we found a notebook where he had written the words of all his favourite songs.
records.zomi: Pu a sih khit-in a deih pen la khempeuh' kammal a gelhna laibu neu khat i mu hi.

records.english: Mum sang the old song at my wedding.
records.zomi: Nu in ka mopawi-ah la lui a sa hi.

records.english: Is that song very old, Grandma?
records.zomi: Pi aw, tua la a lui mahmah hiam?

records.english: Grandma taught my daughter a lullaby.
records.zomi: Pi in ka tanu ihmut la khat a hilh hi.

records.english: My little brother invented his own verse for the family song, and now everyone sings it.
records.zomi: Ka nau pasal neu in innkuan la adingin a mah' la tang khat a phuak a, tu-in mi khempeuh in a sa uh hi.

records.english: When I'm homesick, I play the recording of my grandmother singing at my brother's wedding.
records.zomi: Inn ka phawk ciangin ka pi in ka sanggampa' mopawi-a la a sak laitak ciamtehna ka tum hi.

records.english: A song passed down through several generations becomes part of a family's story.
records.zomi: Suan tampi tungtawn-in a kikhah suk la khat innkuan khat' tangthu' a khen a suak hi.

records.english: Can you teach me Grandma's favourite song?
records.zomi: Pi' deih pen la hong hilh thei ding na hiam?

records.english: Mum and her sisters still argue about the right words to one of their mother's songs.
records.zomi: Nu leh a sanggamnu te in a nu uh' la khat' kammal dik tawh kisai a kinial lai uh hi.

records.english: Who knows the second verse?
records.zomi: La tang nihna kua in a thei hiam?

records.english: We always sing before the Christmas meal.
records.zomi: Christmas an ma-in la i sa den hi.

records.english: Grandpa sings while he works in the garden.
records.zomi: Pu in huan-ah nasep a sep laitakin la a sa hi.

records.english: Singing together gives young and old relatives a way to share an experience without needing many words.
records.zomi: Khawm taka la sak in sanggam naupang leh upa te kammal tampi kisam lo-in thuakna khat a kihawm nadingin lampi khat a pia hi.

records.english: Why does Dad always sing that song when he drives?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pa in mawtaw a mawng ciangin tua la a sa den hiam?

records.english: It reminds him of his father, who sang it on the way to market.
records.zomi: Kawlpi a pai uh lampi-ah tua la a sa a pa a phawk sak hi.

records.english: The songs Grandma taught us are the first thing I want to pass on to my daughter.
records.zomi: Pi in hong hilh la te pen ka tanu kiangah ka khah suk masa nop pen ahi hi.

records.english: Who taught you the wedding songs, Auntie?
records.zomi: Ni aw, mopawi la te kua in hong hilh hiam?

records.english: My mother did, while we sewed the bride's clothes together.
records.zomi: Ka nu in hong hilh hi, mo' puan khawm taka i khui laitak.

records.english: Traditional songs sung within a family carry memories that photographs alone cannot preserve.
records.zomi: Innkuan sungah kisa ngeina la te in photo bek in a kem thei lo phawkna te a pua hi.

records.english: The children love the song about the bird.
records.zomi: Naupangte in vasa tawh kisai la a deih mahmah uh hi.

records.english: Dad's voice is deep and strong.
records.zomi: Pa' aw a thuk a, a khauh hi.

records.english: Families that sing together at celebrations often find it easier to gather in difficult times too.
records.zomi: Pawi te-ah khawm taka la a sa innkuan te in hun haksa te-ah zong kikhawm a baih zaw zel uh hi.

records.english: Why does that song make Mum cry?
records.zomi: Bang hangin tua la in Nu a kap sak hiam?

records.english: The first time my son sang a traditional song in front of the family, Grandpa wiped away tears.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in innkuan mai-ah ngeina la khat a sak masa pen ciangin Pu in a mittui a nul hi.

records.english: I sing Dad's song to my own children.
records.zomi: Pa' la ka tate kiangah ka sa hi.

records.english: Why do the old songs sound so different when Grandpa sings them?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pu in a sak ciangin la lui te a kibang lo mahmah hiam?

records.english: My uncle plays the drum while we sing.
records.zomi: I la sak laitakin ka pa neu in khuang a tum hi.

records.english: Children who sing with their grandparents often absorb a sense of belonging without realising it.
records.zomi: A pu leh pi uh tawh la a sa naupangte in a theih kha loh-in kizopna lungsim a ngah zel uh hi.

records.english: Could you write down the words of the song before the wedding, so that the children can practise?
records.zomi: Naupangte in a kisin theih nadingin mopawi ma-in la' kammal te na gelh thei ding hiam?

records.english: The whole family sang at the reunion.
records.zomi: Kikhopna kik-ah innkuan buppi in la a sa uh hi.

records.english: Grandma, will you sing the song about the river again?
records.zomi: Pi aw, lui tawh kisai la na sa kik thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, if you sing the chorus with me this time.
records.zomi: Thei hi, tu vei-in kei tawh la tang kikiik na sak leh.

records.english: My sister knows every song in the family.
records.zomi: Ka sanggamnu in innkuan sung-a la khempeuh a thei hi.

records.english: Each family may sing a traditional song slightly differently, and every version has its own value.
records.zomi: Innkuan khatciat in ngeina la khat a kibang lo deuh-in a sa thei uh a, a khatciat in amah' manphatna a nei hi.

records.english: When my grandmother sings, she closes her eyes as if she can see her old village.
records.zomi: Ka pi in la a sak ciangin a khua lui a mu thei bangin a mit a sing hi.

records.english: Have your children ever asked you to sing the songs you heard as a child?
records.zomi: Na tate in naupan lai-in na zak la te sa dingin hong ngen ngei uh hiam?

records.english: My son sings the old songs better than I do.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in kei sangin la lui te a sa hoih zaw hi.

records.english: My cousin, who grew up abroad, learned our family songs from recordings on her phone.
records.zomi: Gamdang-a a khang ka sanggam in a phone tunga ciamtehna te pan i innkuan la te a sin hi.

records.english: My father sings the same harvest song every year, even though we no longer farm.
records.zomi: Lo i bawl nawn kei hangin ka pa in kum simin buh lak la kibang a sa hi.

records.english: Do your parents sing the same songs at every family celebration?
records.zomi: Na nu leh pa in innkuan pawi khatciat-ah la kibang a sa uh hiam?

records.english: Learning a grandparent's songs can open conversations about the life and places they remember.
records.zomi: Pu ahih kei leh pi khat' la te sin in a nuntakna leh a phawk mun te tawh kisai kikupna a hong thei hi.

records.english: My husband didn't know any of our songs when we married, but now he sings them louder than anyone.
records.zomi: I kiten ciangin ka pasal in i la khat zong a thei kei a, ahi zongin tu-in kuamah sangin a khauh zaw-in a sa hi.

records.english: We sang Grandma's song at her funeral.
records.zomi: Pi' misi vuina-ah a la i sa hi.

records.english: Why did Grandpa ask for that song at his ninetieth birthday?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pu in a kum sawmkua pawi-ah tua la a ngen hiam?

records.english: It was the song his mother sang when he left home as a young man, so it carries his whole life story for him.
records.zomi: Tangval a hih lai-in inn a nusiat ciangin a nu in a sak la ahih manin amah adingin a nuntakna tangthu buppi a pua hi.

records.english: When my grandmother was in hospital, she could no longer speak clearly, but she still hummed the songs of her childhood.
records.zomi: Ka pi damlo inn-ah a om laitakin kician takin a gen thei nawn kei a, ahi zongin a naupan lai-a la te a hum lai hi.

records.english: One evening, my mother started to sing one of them softly, and Grandma's eyes opened and her lips began to move with the words.
records.zomi: Nitak khat-in ka nu in tua lak-a khat nem takin a sa pan a, Pi' mit a ki-hong a, a muk te kammal tawh a kitawl pan hi.

records.english: The nurse stood quietly in the doorway until the song had finished.
records.zomi: La a bei mateng nurse kongkhak-ah dai takin a ding hi.

records.english: Grandma's songs are slow and beautiful.
records.zomi: Pi' la te a nawl a, a hoih hi.

records.english: Mum hums when she's happy.
records.zomi: Nu a lungdam ciangin a hum hi.

records.english: Our family sings a blessing song over every new baby, holding hands in a circle.
records.zomi: I innkuan in naupang neu thak khatciat tungah kual-in khut kilen-in thupha la khat a sa hi.

records.english: Do you think the children will remember the old songs when they're grown up?
records.zomi: Naupangte a khan ciangin la lui te a phawk ding uh hi, na ci hiam?

records.english: They will if we sing them together often, not just at weddings and funerals.
records.zomi: Mopawi leh misi vuina te-ah bek hi lo-in khawm taka a zawhthawh-in i sak leh a phawk ding uh hi.

records.english: Does God love people who do bad things?
records.zomi: Pasian in thu hoih lo bawl mite a it hiam?

records.english: Christians believe God still loves them and that they never lose the image of God.
records.zomi: Khazih mite in Pasian in amaute a it lai a, Pasian lim a mansuah ngei kei uh hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: Why do you think God made people able to love and to create beautiful things?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pasian in mite kiit thei leh na hoih bawl thei dingin a bawl hi, na ci hiam?

records.english: Believing that a child reflects God's image can strengthen that child's sense of worth.
records.zomi: Naupang khat in Pasian lim a lak hi, cih um in tua naupang' manphatna lungsim a khauh sak thei hi.

records.english: My parents believed that being made in God's image meant that girls deserved the same education as boys.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh pa in Pasian lim bangin kibawl cih in nungak te in tangval te bangin sinna kibang a ngah ding uh hi, cihna ahi hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: My grandmother taught us to greet the street sweeper as warmly as the pastor.
records.zomi: Ka pi in lampi sianghsakmi pastor bangin lungsim lum takin cibai dingin hong hilh hi.

records.english: In our family, we try to remember God's image in each other even when we argue.
records.zomi: I innkuan-ah i kinial ciangin zong khat leh khat sung-a Pasian lim phawk dingin i hanciam hi.

records.english: Why does our family visit Uncle in the care home every week, even though he no longer recognises us?
records.zomi: Pa neu in hong thei nawn kei hangin bang hangin i innkuan in kal simin kemna inn-ah amah a kan hiam?

records.english: We believe he still bears the image of God and is precious, whatever his memory or abilities.
records.zomi: A phawkna ahih kei leh a siamna bangci om zongin Pasian lim a pua lai a, a manpha hi, ci-in i um hi.

records.english: Our family helps at the shelter on Sundays.
records.zomi: I innkuan in Nipini simin om nading mun-ah a huh hi.

records.english: Is my friend made in God's image too?
records.zomi: Ka lawm zong Pasian lim bangin kibawl ahi hiam?

records.english: Is God's image inside us?
records.zomi: Pasian lim i sungah a om hiam?

records.english: We pray for people who are different from us.
records.zomi: Eite tawh a kibang lo mite adingin thu i ngen hi.

records.english: Grandma says every face shows God's love.
records.zomi: Mai khempeuh in Pasian' itna a lak hi, ci-in Pi in a gen hi.

records.english: Why does the Bible say both men and women were made in God's image?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Lai Siangtho in pasal leh numei tuak Pasian lim bangin kibawl hi, a ci hiam?

records.english: Dad thanks God for each of us at dinner.
records.zomi: Pa in nitak an-ah ei khatciat adingin Pasian kiangah lungdam a ko hi.

records.english: Our family visits an elderly neighbour every Sunday because she has no relatives nearby.
records.zomi: Inn kiang mi upa nu khat a kiangah sanggam a nei kei ahih manin i innkuan in Nipini simin a kan hi.

records.english: The teaching that all people bear God's image has inspired many Christian families to work for justice.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh in Pasian lim a pua uh hi, cih hilhna in Khazih innkuan tampi dikna adingin a sem dingin a hanthawn hi.

records.english: We were taught to respect every person.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh zahtak dingin hong hilh uh hi.

records.english: When my son made fun of a disabled boy, we talked about why every person bears God's image.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in pumpi kicinglohna nei tangval neu khat a simmawh ciangin bang hangin mi khempeuh in Pasian lim a pua uh hiam cih i kikum hi.

records.english: Grandpa never laughs at anyone.
records.zomi: Pu in kuamah a nui ngei kei hi.

records.english: My brother asked if dogs are made in God's image.
records.zomi: Ka sanggampa in ui te Pasian lim bangin kibawl ahi uh hiam, ci-in a dong hi.

records.english: We pray for the people in prison.
records.zomi: Thong-a om mite adingin thu i ngen hi.

records.english: Many Christian families teach children to see the image of God in every person they meet.
records.zomi: Khazih innkuan tampi in naupangte a kimuh mi khempeuh-ah Pasian lim mu dingin a hilh uh hi.

records.english: Grandparents who treat every guest with honour often pass on a lived understanding of human dignity.
records.zomi: Khualmi khempeuh zahtakna tawh a kem pu leh pi te in mihing manphatna theihna taktak a khah suk zel uh hi.

records.english: Is my baby sister made in God's image too?
records.zomi: Ka sanggamnu neu naupang neu zong Pasian lim bangin kibawl ahi hiam?

records.english: Yes, Christians believe that every person, even the smallest baby, bears God's image.
records.zomi: Hi hi, Khazih mite in mi khempeuh, naupang neu pen zong, Pasian lim a pua uh hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: Christian parents often link the image of God with practical acts such as visiting the sick and feeding the hungry.
records.zomi: Khazih nu leh pa te in Pasian lim pen a cina mite kan leh a gilkial mite an pia bang nasep taktak te tawh a kizop sak zel uh hi.

records.english: Does God see the good in everyone?
records.zomi: Pasian in mi khempeuh sung-a hoihna a mu hiam?

records.english: When my daughter was teased about her skin colour, I reminded her that she reflects God's image.
records.zomi: Ka tanu a vun pianzia hangin a kisimmawh ciangin Pasian lim a lak hi, ci-in ka phawk sak hi.

records.english: Grandpa used to say that every baby is a new picture of God's goodness.
records.zomi: Naupang neu khatciat pen Pasian' hoihna lim thak khat ahi hi, ci-in Pu in a gen ngei hi.

records.english: Remembering that relatives also bear God's image can help families forgive one another.
records.zomi: Sanggam te zong in Pasian lim a pua uh hi, cih phawk in innkuan te khat leh khat a kimaisak nadingin a huh thei hi.

records.english: Dad says nobody is worthless in God's eyes.
records.zomi: Pasian' mit-ah kuamah a manpha lo kei hi, ci-in Pa in a gen hi.

records.english: Why do we visit sick people?
records.zomi: Bang hangin a cina mite i kan hiam?

records.english: God made Grandpa special, Mum says.
records.zomi: Pasian in Pu a tuam takin a bawl hi, ci-in Nu in a gen hi.

records.english: My sister painted a picture of God's family.
records.zomi: Ka sanggamnu in Pasian' innkuan lim khat a zuh hi.

records.english: Why does Grandma say we must be kind to everyone?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pi in mi khempeuh tungah i hehpih ding hi, a ci hiam?

records.english: She believes that every person is made in the image of God, so everyone deserves respect.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh Pasian lim bangin kibawl ahih manin mi khempeuh in zahtakna a ngah ding hi, ci-in a um hi.

records.english: Did God make me in his image?
records.zomi: Pasian in amah' lim bangin hong bawl hiam?

records.english: How did your parents show you that every person bears God's image?
records.zomi: Na nu leh pa in mi khempeuh in Pasian lim a pua uh hi, cih bangci hong lak uh hiam?

records.english: They welcomed beggars and visitors to our table and spoke to them as kindly as to our own relatives.
records.zomi: Ngetmi leh khualmite i an dawhkan-ah a dawn uh a, eimau' sanggam te bangin nuam takin a kiho pih uh hi.

records.english: My husband reminds the children that even people we disagree with are made in God's image.
records.zomi: Ka pasal in i kilungkim loh mite zong Pasian lim bangin kibawl ahi uh hi, ci-in naupangte a phawk sak hi.

records.english: For many Christians, the image of God gives disabled and elderly relatives the same dignity as everyone else.
records.zomi: Khazih mite tampi adingin Pasian lim in pumpi kicinglohna nei leh upa sanggam te mi dang khempeuh bangin zahtakna kibang a pia hi.

records.english: Mum says God loves every child the same.
records.zomi: Pasian in naupang khempeuh kibang-in a it hi, ci-in Nu in a gen hi.

records.english: Do your children understand why we treat the people who clean our streets with respect?
records.zomi: Bang hangin i lampi sianghsakmi te zahtakna tawh i kem hiam cih na tate in a theisiam uh hiam?

records.english: Could you explain to the children why our family helps at the refugee centre?
records.zomi: Bang hangin i innkuan in galtai inn-ah a huh hiam cih naupangte kiangah na gen thei ding hiam?

records.english: My teenage son says that believing in God's image makes it harder for him to join in with cruel jokes.
records.zomi: Ka tapa naupang lianno in Pasian lim um in nuamsa lo kihahkhuatna te-ah kihel a haksa sak hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Why should we respect old people?
records.zomi: Bang hangin upa te i zahtak ding hiam?

records.english: How do you explain to a child that a person who hurt them is still made in God's image?
records.zomi: Amah a susia mi khat Pasian lim bangin kibawl lai hi, cih naupang khat kiangah bangci na gen hiam?

records.english: Teaching children about the image of God can help them resist prejudice and cruelty.
records.zomi: Naupangte Pasian lim tawh kisai hilh in mi kisimmawhna leh nuamsa lohna te a dal nadingin a huh thei hi.

records.english: My mother cared for my disabled brother all his life, saying that his worth came from God.

records.english: Who made the error, the machine or me?

records.english: We learned a lot from that failure.

records.english: Because finding the error yourself helps you remember it far better than being told.

records.english: Learning from mistakes requires curiosity about what happened, not just regret.

records.english: I forgot to check my answers.
records.zomi: Ka dawnna te en ding ka mangngilh hi.

records.zomi: Bang hangin lista te in nasep siam mite khialhna baih te a pelh nadingin a huh hiam?

records.english: In my first piano exam, I forgot the middle of a piece and had to stop completely.
records.zomi: Ka piano sitna masa pen-ah late khat' a laizang ka mangngilh a, a bup-in ka khawl hi.

records.english: My teacher didn't scold me; she asked me to play the piece slowly every day for a month, starting from a different place each time.
records.zomi: Ka saya in hong phun lo a, kha khat sung ni simin late zawi zawi-in tum dingin, vei khat ciat mun tuamtuam pan kipan dingin hong ngen hi.

records.english: At the next exam, I made a small slip but carried on, and the examiner praised my calm recovery.

records.english: Why do pilots report their own small mistakes?
records.zomi: Bang hangin vanleng tawlpa te in amau' khialhna neu te a gen uh hiam?

records.english: Sharing even minor errors helps the whole industry spot dangerous patterns before they cause an accident.
records.zomi: Khialhna neu te zong hawm in nasep bup in a hong piang ma-in lauhuai a kibang kik dan te a mu thei nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Is it bad to make mistakes when learning to drive?
records.zomi: Mawtaw mawng kisin lai-in khialhna bawl a hoih lo hiam?

records.zomi: Hi kei hi, khat ciat pan na sin a, na hilhpa in hong kem dingin a om leh hoih hi.

records.english: How can I admit a mistake without feeling embarrassed?
records.zomi: Ka zum lo-in khialhna khat bangci ka pom thei ding hiam?

records.english: Feedback that explains why something went wrong helps people improve far more than a simple correction.
records.zomi: Bang hangin a khial hiam cih a gen ngaihsutna in khialhna bawlphatna baih sangin mite a khantoh zaw mahmah sak hi.

records.english: My mistake taught me to slow down.
records.zomi: Ka khialhna in zawi zawi-in bawl dingin hong hilh hi.

records.zomi: Saya te in sangnaupang te khialh ding a lau tawm zaw nadingin bangci a bawl thei uh hiam?

records.zomi: Hong tung ding-in ka kidawm zaw ding hi.

records.english: Admitting a mistake honestly usually earns more trust than pretending it never happened.

records.english: How should I respond when a friend points out my mistake?
records.zomi: Lawm khat in ka khialhna a lak ciangin bangci ka dawng ding hiam?

records.english: Why do I keep making the same mistake?
records.zomi: Bang hangin khialhna kibang ka bawl den hiam?

records.english: Is this mistake easy to fix?
records.zomi: Hih khialhna bawlphat a baih hiam?

records.english: What did you learn from the mistake?
records.zomi: Khialhna pan bang na sin hiam?

records.english: Why do some people repeat the same mistakes again and again?
records.zomi: Bang hangin mi pawlkhat in khialhna kibang a bawl kik zel uh hiam?

records.english: A mistake that is analysed carefully can prevent many similar errors in the future.

records.english: Who can help me fix this?
records.zomi: Hih bawlphat dingin kua in hong huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Good answers to questions about failure often include practical changes rather than general advice.
records.zomi: Lawhsamna tawh kisai dotna te' dawnna hoih te in thuhilhna tangpi sangin nasep kikhekna te a koih zel hi.

records.english: Did the mistake cost a lot?
records.zomi: Khialhna in sum tampi a bei sak hiam?

records.english: Can a mistake ever lead to a better result than the original plan?
records.zomi: Khialhna khat in ngimna masa sangin a hoih zaw khat a piangsak thei ngei hiam?

records.english: Some mistakes reveal weaknesses in a system rather than in the person who made them.
records.zomi: Khialhna pawlkhat in a bawlmi sangin nasep dan sung-a hatlohna te a lak hi.

records.english: Reviewing a mistake soon after it happens makes the lesson clearer and easier to remember.
records.zomi: Khialhna khat a piang khit manlang takin a et kik in sinna a kician zaw sak a, a phawk a baih zaw sak hi.

records.english: Where did the error start?
records.zomi: Khialhna koi-ah a kipan hiam?

records.english: People learn more from mistakes when they feel safe enough to admit them.
records.zomi: Mite in a pom thei dingin a bit kizak ciangin khialhna pan a sin tam zaw uh hi.

records.english: A plaque marks the old post office.

records.english: Is it true that the council plans to name the new streets after local nurses?
records.zomi: Council in lampi thak te khuasung nurse te' min a phuah ding hi, cih a tak hiam?

records.english: Why is the old fire station now a café?
records.zomi: Bang hangin mei sihna inn lui pen tu-in cafe ahi hiam?

records.zomi: Khuapi' map lui te ka en thei ding hiam?

records.english: How can our community group record the history of the closed hospital?

records.english: Ask former nurses and patients for interviews, and contact the archives for its old records and plans.
records.zomi: Nurse lui te leh damlo lui te kikupna dingin ngen in la, a ciamtehna lui leh ngimna lui te adingin lai kemna mun kiangah thu khak in.

records.english: The council's archive holds records of every building permit since the town was founded.
records.zomi: Council' lai kemna mun in khuapi a kiphut pan inn lam phalna khempeuh' ciamtehna a kem hi.

records.english: The war memorial was cleaned last week.
records.zomi: Galte phawkna suang pen kal nunung in kisiangsak hi.

records.english: Our library keeps old copies of the local paper.
records.zomi: I laibu inn in khuasung thusuah lai lui te' copy te a kem hi.

records.english: Volunteers are often the people who keep local history alive when budgets are tight.
records.zomi: Sum a tawm ciangin khuasung tangthu a kem den mite pen thalawp te ahi zel uh hi.

records.english: Schools that use local history make the past feel relevant to pupils' own lives.
records.zomi: Khuasung tangthu a zang sang te in nidang hun te sangnaupang te' nuntakna tawh a kizom sak hi.

records.english: Restoring historic buildings can give a town a stronger sense of identity.
records.zomi: Tangthu inn lui te bawlphat kik in khuapi khat a hihna a kician zaw sak thei hi.

records.english: Our school had a history fair.
records.zomi: I sang in tangthu pawi khat a nei hi.

records.english: Public archives and libraries keep a community's history available to everyone, not only experts.
records.zomi: Mipi lai kemna mun te leh laibu inn te in khuasung tangthu siam mite bek hi lo-in mi khempeuh adingin a kem uh hi.

records.english: Museums that involve local people in their exhibitions tell richer and more accurate stories.
records.zomi: A lak van te-ah khuasung mite a kihelsak museum te in tangthu a hau zaw leh a dik zaw te a gen uh hi.

records.english: The heritage open days let residents see inside buildings that are usually closed.
records.zomi: Tangthu kihonna ni te in a sung-a teng mite in a ngeina-in a kikhak inn te a sung a en thei nadingin a phal hi.

records.english: Was the market hall once a church?
records.zomi: Kizuakna inn lian pen nidang-in biakinn ahi ngei hiam?

records.english: Volunteers at the museum are transcribing handwritten records from the old workhouse.
records.zomi: Museum-a thalawp te in sum nei lo mite' nasep inn lui pan khut tawh kigelh ciamtehna te a gelh kik uh hi.

records.english: The town celebrated its five hundredth birthday.
records.zomi: Khuapi in a kum za nga ni pawi a bawl hi.

records.english: The history society's guided walks attract both newcomers and families who have lived here for generations.
records.zomi: Tangthu pawl' lamlakna vak te in hong tung thak te leh hih mun-ah khang tampi sung a teng innkuan te a pai sak hi.

records.english: Could the library put the old newspapers online so that people abroad can read them?

records.english: Community history helps newcomers understand the places where they now live.
records.zomi: Khuasung tangthu in hong tung thak te a tu-a a tenna mun uh a theisiam nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Local schools use the archive's old photographs to show pupils how their neighbourhood has changed.
records.zomi: Khuasung sang te in sangnaupang te a khuasung uh bangci a kikhek hiam cih lak nadingin lai kemna mun' photo lui te a zang uh hi.

records.english: Where can I find old photos of our street?
records.zomi: I lampi' photo lui te koi-ah ka mu thei ding hiam?

records.english: The library's local history room has boxes of them, arranged by street name.
records.zomi: Laibu inn' khuasung tangthu inndan in lampi min bangin kikoih ip tampi a nei hi.

records.english: Memorials and plaques remind residents of events and people that shaped their community.
records.zomi: Phawkna suang te leh ciamtehna suang te in a sung-a teng mite a khuasung uh a bawl thu te leh mite a phawk sak hi.

records.english: Preserving community history is easier when public services, schools and residents work together.
records.zomi: Mipi nasep te, sang te leh a sung-a teng mite khawm-in a sep ciangin khuasung tangthu kemna a baih zaw hi.

records.english: Maps of the history trail are free at the library.
records.zomi: Tangthu lampi map te laibu inn-ah man om lo hi.

records.english: Is the town archive open to visitors?
records.zomi: Khuapi lai kemna mun pen khualmite adingin a kihong hiam?

records.english: The old station is now a museum.
records.zomi: Station lui pen tu-in museum ahi hi.

records.english: When the old cottage hospital closed, a group of former nurses asked the library to help them record its history.
records.zomi: Khuaneu damlo inn lui a kikhak ciangin nurse lui pawl khat in a tangthu ciamteh nadingin laibu inn a ngen uh hi.

records.english: Over one winter, they collected photographs, ward diaries and memories from patients who had been born there.
records.zomi: Khuaphal khat sungin photo te, damlo inndan nitum lai te leh tua mun-ah a piang damlo te' phawkna te a kaikhawm uh hi.

records.english: The exhibition they created now hangs in the new health centre's waiting room.
records.zomi: A bawl uh lak van te pen tu-in cidamna inn thak' ngakna inndan-ah a kikhai hi.

records.english: The town clock works again after fifty years.

records.english: The library has a box of old postcards.
records.zomi: Laibu inn in postcard lui ip khat a nei hi.

records.english: Could the council add signs explaining the history of the old mill?

records.english: Digitising old records allows people far away to connect with the history of their family's town.

records.english: How did the community raise money to restore the bandstand in the park?
records.zomi: Huan lian sung-a late tumna mun bawlphat kik nadingin khuasung mite in sum bangci a kaikhawm uh hiam?

records.english: The community radio station broadcasts a weekly programme about forgotten local events.
records.zomi: Khuasung radio in a kimangngilh khuasung thu te tawh kisai kal sim program khat a suah hi.

records.english: Who looks after the war memorial?
records.zomi: Galte phawkna suang kua in a kem hiam?

records.english: The council cleans it every spring, and volunteers plant flowers around it before the remembrance service.
records.zomi: Council in spring simin a siangsak a, phawkna kikhopna ma-in thalawp te in a kim-a pak te a suan uh hi.

records.english: A town's history includes difficult chapters, and good public services present them honestly.
records.zomi: Khuapi khat' tangthu in a haksa khen te a huap a, mipi nasep hoih te in a dik takin a gen uh hi.

records.english: The old pump still stands in the square.
records.zomi: Tui khaina khawl lui pen mun lai-ah a ding lai hi.

records.english: Can I donate old photos to the museum?
records.zomi: Museum-ah photo lui te ka pia thei ding hiam?

records.english: Why did the council put plaques on some of the town's buildings?
records.zomi: Bang hangin council in khuapi' inn pawlkhat tungah ciamtehna suang te a koih hiam?

records.english: To mark places where important local people lived or worked, so that residents and visitors can learn their stories.
records.zomi: Khuasung mi thupi te a tenna ahih kei leh a nasepna mun te ciamteh nadingin, a sung-a teng mite leh khualmite in a tangthu uh a sin thei nadingin.

records.english: Oral history projects capture voices that official records often leave out.

records.english: The history society meets on Mondays.

records.english: Who built the town hall?

records.english: The museum's exhibition about the railway was designed with help from retired railway workers.

records.english: The town's oral history project gives copies of each recording to the families who took part.
records.zomi: Khuapi' kam tawh tangthu ciamtehna nasep in kihel innkuan te tungah ciamtehna khat ciat' copy a pia hi.

records.english: The library's memory café invites older residents to share stories about the town.
records.zomi: Laibu inn' phawkna cafe in a sung-a teng upa te khuapi tawh kisai tangthu hawm dingin a sam hi.

records.english: Volunteers repaired the old bridge.
records.zomi: Thalawp te in lei lui a bawlphat uh hi.

records.english: Heritage projects often bring together residents who might otherwise never meet.
records.zomi: Tangthu nasep te in a dang-in kimu ngei lo ding a sung-a teng mite a kaikhawm zel hi.

records.english: Why did the council decide to keep the old factory chimney when the rest was demolished?
records.zomi: A dang khempeuh a kiphiat ciangin bang hangin council in sepna inn lui' meikhu khuk a kem ding a thukhen hiam?

records.english: Why does our family still farm the old way on the hillside field?

records.english: Because those methods kept the soil healthy for generations, and Grandpa wants us to understand them before we try anything new.

records.english: My cousins come to help us harvest.

records.english: Dad writes down the date of the first rain every year in an old notebook.

records.english: When my grandfather could no longer climb the hill, he taught me everything about his field from the porch.
records.zomi: Ka pu in mual a kah zo nawn loh ciangin inn mai-a tutna pan a lo tawh kisai khempeuh hong hilh hi.

records.english: My father learned from his uncle how to graft a branch from one orange tree onto another.

records.english: Mum saves the vegetable peels for the compost.
records.zomi: Nu in anteh hawng te eek paikawng adingin a kem hi.

records.zomi: Ka sanggampa in zingsang simin ak te an a pia hi.

records.zomi: Nu in ni in a nah te a kang loh nadingin zingsang tuak-in anlim te tui buak dingin hong hilh hi.

records.english: Children who work beside their grandparents in the fields learn skills that books rarely teach.
records.zomi: Lo-ah a pu leh pi te kiang-a nasem naupang te in laibu te in a hilh ngei loh siamna te a sin uh hi.

records.english: My grandmother taught me to plant onions and garlic at the edge of the garden to keep pests away.

records.english: Grandma keeps seeds in old jars.
records.zomi: Pi in khaici te um lui te sungah a kem hi.

records.english: Mum grows vegetables behind the house.
records.zomi: Nu in inn nung-ah anteh a suan hi.

records.english: After a poor harvest, Grandpa told us about the hungry years when he was a boy.

records.english: When elderly relatives explain their farming practices, they also pass on values such as patience and thrift.
records.zomi: Innkuan upa te in a lo nasep dan uh a gen ciangin thuakzawhna leh sum kem siamna bang ngeina hoih te zong a khah suk uh hi.

records.english: Grandma's garden has herbs for every meal.
records.zomi: Pi' huan-ah an khat ciat adingin an hel te a om hi.

records.english: My uncle combines his father's methods with advice from the farming college.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in a pa' dan te lo nasep sanginn pan thuhilhna tawh a hel khawm hi.

records.english: The children planted their own beans.
records.zomi: Naupang te in amau' be te a suan uh hi.

records.english: Our family's best farming advice is written on the back of an old calendar in the kitchen.
records.zomi: I innkuan' lo nasep thuhilhna hoih pen te an huanna-a calendar lui khat' nung lam-ah kigelh hi.

records.english: Why do we save the biggest seeds, Dad?
records.zomi: Pa, bang hangin khaici lian pen te i kem uh hiam?

records.english: Because strong seeds usually grow into strong plants for next year's harvest.
records.zomi: Bang hang hiam cih leh khaici hat te in kum hong tung ding buh lak adingin anlim hat te-ah a khang zel hi.

records.english: Why does Grandma plant marigolds between the tomatoes?

records.english: What did your father teach you about looking after the soil?
records.zomi: Na pa in lei kem dan tawh kisai bang hong hilh hiam?

records.english: He taught me to leave some fields to rest and to feed the soil with manure and leaves.

records.english: Saving seeds from year to year links each harvest to the family's past.

records.english: Can I water the young plants?

records.english: Every harvest, my grandmother chose the best ears of maize and hung them above the kitchen fire to dry.

records.english: When I asked why, she explained that the smoke kept insects away and that those seeds would feed the family the following year.

records.english: Now my mother hangs maize in the same place, and I have started helping her choose.

records.english: Grandma, how do you know when it's time to plant?

records.english: When the first rains have soaked the ground and the soil crumbles softly in my hand.
records.zomi: Guah kia masa pen in lei a ciin a, lei ka khut sungah a nem ciangin.

records.english: When will the mangoes be ready?
records.zomi: Theihai te bang ciangin a min ding hiam?

records.english: Dad knows when the rain will come.
records.zomi: Pa in guah bang ciangin a kia ding hiam cih a thei hi.

records.english: Our family keeps a small field of the old rice variety, even though it grows more slowly.
records.zomi: I innkuan in a khan nawl zaw hangin buh lui khat' lo neu khat a kem uh hi.

records.english: Do your children know how to tell when the fruit is ripe?
records.zomi: Na ta te in theigah a min hun bangci theih ding hiam cih a thei uh hiam?

records.english: Is the soil too dry to plant today?
records.zomi: Tuni suan dingin lei a keu lua hiam?

records.english: Farming knowledge passed down through families often reflects generations of careful observation.
records.zomi: Innkuan te sung pan a kikhah suk lo nasep theihna in khang tampi sung-a kidawm taka et-na a lak zel hi.

records.english: Dad mends the fence before the goats get in.

records.english: When our cousins visit from the city, Grandpa takes them to the fields to show them how rice grows.

records.english: Every autumn, Grandma and I collect the dry bean pods and shell them together in the evenings.

records.english: Grandpa shows us how to dig a straight row.

records.english: The idea of leaving the earth better for future generations is central to many Christian families' understanding of stewardship.

records.english: Because we believe God has given us the earth to look after, and wasting energy is careless.

records.zomi: Ka zahtak lo bang ka kilan lo-in sinna te a manlang lua hi, cih ka saya bangci ka gen thei ding hiam?

records.english: Say which part you lost track of and ask whether there's extra practice you could do.
records.zomi: Koi khen-ah na mang hiam cih gen in la, na bawl thei kisinna behlap a om hiam cih dong in.

records.english: Our teacher uses an anonymous question box so that nobody feels embarrassed.
records.zomi: I saya in kuamah a zum lo nadingin min om lo dotna ip khat a zang hi.

records.english: I got lost halfway through your explanation.
records.zomi: Na gennop a laizang-ah ka mang hi.

records.english: What should I do if I'm too shy to ask questions in class?
records.zomi: Class-ah dotna dot dingin ka zum lua leh bang ka bawl ding hiam?

records.english: Write your question on a card and leave it on my desk, and I'll answer it privately.
records.zomi: Na dotna card khat tungah gelh in la, ka dawhkan tungah koih in, tua ciangin a kiseel-in ka dawng ding hi.

records.english: Is it fair for a teacher to discuss my marks in front of the class?
records.zomi: Saya khat in class mai-ah ka mark te a kikup pen a dik hiam?

records.english: A justice system that listens to users' complaints can improve the experience of everyone who comes to court.
records.zomi: A zatmite' phunna a ngai thukhenna nasep dan khat in thukhenna inn-ah a hong pai mi khempeuh' theihna a hoih zaw sak thei hi.

records.english: Why did the town open a community mediation service next to the court?
records.zomi: Bang hangin khuapi in thukhenna inn kiangah khuasung kilemna bawlna nasep khat a hong hiam?

records.english: Many neighbour disputes can be settled faster and more cheaply through mediation, which leaves the court free for serious cases.
records.zomi: Inn kiang mite' kinialna tampi kilemna bawlna tawh a manlang zaw-in leh man niam zaw-in kiphel thei a, tua in thukhenna inn thu gik te adingin a awng sak hi.

records.english: Our community centre hosts a monthly session where a lawyer answers questions about tenancy disputes.
records.zomi: I khuasung inn lian in kha simin thukham siam mi khat in inn hal kinialna tawh kisai dotna te a dawnna hun khat a bawl hi.

records.english: Where can I get free legal advice before my hearing?
records.zomi: Ka thukhenna ma-in man om lo thukham thuhilhna koi-ah ka ngah thei ding hiam?

records.english: The law centre near the court gives free advice on Monday and Thursday mornings.
records.zomi: Thukhenna inn kiang-a thukham thuhilhna mun in Pizing ni leh Laizing ni zingsang-in man om lo thuhilhna a pia hi.

records.english: Witness support services make it easier for frightened people to give clear evidence.
records.zomi: Theihpihtu huhna nasep te in a lau mite tettehna kician a pia thei nadingin a baih sak hi.

records.english: Can I bring my daughter into the courtroom?
records.zomi: Ka tanu thukhenna inndan-ah ka paipih thei ding hiam?

records.english: Only if the judge agrees, so ask the usher before the hearing starts.
records.zomi: Thukhenpa in a phal leh bek, tua ahih manin thukhenna a kipat ma-in kongkhak kemmi dong in.

records.english: Who pays for the interpreter?
records.zomi: Pau letmi' man kua in a pia hiam?

records.english: Why do some cases take months to reach the court?
records.zomi: Bang hangin thu pawlkhat thukhenna inn a tun nadingin kha tampi a la hiam?

records.english: The small claims court is upstairs.
records.zomi: Thu neu thukhenna inn pen inn tung lam-ah a om hi.

records.english: The interpreter arrived before the hearing.
records.zomi: Pau letmi thukhenna ma-in a tung hi.

records.english: Where do witnesses wait?
records.zomi: Theihpihtu te koi-ah a ngak uh hiam?

records.english: The law school runs a free clinic where students, supervised by lawyers, advise local residents.
records.zomi: Thukham sanginn in thukham siam mite' en-na nuai-ah sangnaupang te in khuasung mite thu a hilh man om lo thuhilhna mun khat a bawl hi.

records.english: Can I park near the court?
records.zomi: Thukhenna inn kiangah mawtaw ka koih thei ding hiam?

records.english: The council funds a mediation service for neighbours who disagree about noise or boundaries.
records.zomi: Council in ging ahih kei leh gam gi tawh kisai a kituak lo inn kiang mite adingin kilemna bawlna nasep khat sum a pia hi.

records.english: The security guard checked my bag.
records.zomi: Kemna nasempa in ka ip a en hi.

records.english: Accessible court buildings allow everyone to take part in the justice system.
records.zomi: Zat baih thukhenna inn te in mi khempeuh thukhenna nasep dan-ah a kihel thei nadingin a phal hi.

records.english: Who can come with me to court?
records.zomi: Thukhenna inn-ah kua in hong paipih thei ding hiam?

records.english: Why are some hearings held in private?
records.zomi: Bang hangin thukhenna pawlkhat a kiseel-in kibawl hiam?

records.english: Could the court send letters in simpler language, so that people understand what they must do?
records.zomi: Mite in bang a bawl ding uh hiam cih a theisiam nadingin thukhenna inn in pau baih zaw tawh lai a khak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Interpreters protect the fairness of trials for people who do not speak the court's language.
records.zomi: Pau letmi te in thukhenna inn' pau a ham thei lo mite adingin thukhenna a dik nadingin a kem uh hi.

records.english: The law centre gives free advice.
records.zomi: Thukham thuhilhna mun in man om lo thuhilhna a pia hi.

records.english: Is it possible to give evidence by video if I'm too frightened to face the defendant?
records.zomi: Kimawhsakpa ka maitang dingin ka lau lua leh video tawh tettehna ka pia thei ding hiam?

records.english: Can I get a copy of the judgment?
records.zomi: Thukhensatna' copy khat ka ngah thei ding hiam?

records.english: The usher showed us where to sit.
records.zomi: Kongkhak kemmi in koi-ah i tut ding hiam cih hong lak hi.

records.english: When my elderly neighbour was called as a witness, she was terrified of going to court alone.
records.zomi: Ka inn kiang upa nu theihpihtu-in a kisam ciangin a khat bek-in thukhenna inn-ah pai ding a lau mahmah hi.

records.english: A volunteer from the witness service met her at the entrance, showed her the empty courtroom and explained who would sit where.
records.zomi: Theihpihtu huhna pawl pan thalawp khat in lutna-ah a dawn a, thukhenna inndan awng a lak a, kua koi-ah tu ding hiam cih a gen hi.

records.english: By the time she gave her evidence, she felt calm enough to speak clearly, and she thanked the volunteer for weeks afterwards.
records.zomi: A tettehna a piak hun ciangin kician taka gen thei dingin a lungsim a nuam zo a, a nung-ah kal tampi sung thalawp tungah a lungdam hi.

records.english: After the court introduced online forms, fewer people had to travel to the building.
records.zomi: Thukhenna inn in online lai te a koih khit-in inn-ah a pai kisam mi a tawm zaw hi.

records.english: The court has a help desk on the ground floor.
records.zomi: Thukhenna inn in inn nuai lam-ah huhna dawhkan khat a nei hi.

records.english: Law clinics give students practical experience while serving residents in need.
records.zomi: Thukham thuhilhna mun te in sangnaupang te nasep theihna a pia a, a kisam khuasung mite a huh hi.

records.english: The judge explained the decision in plain words so that everyone in the room could understand.
records.zomi: Inndan sung-a mi khempeuh in a theisiam thei nadingin thukhenpa in thukhensatna pau baih tawh a gen hi.

records.english: Free legal advice helps ensure that people are not denied justice because they cannot afford a lawyer.
records.zomi: Man om lo thukham thuhilhna in thukham siam mi man a pia zo loh hangin mite thukhenna dik a ngah loh nadingin a kem hi.

records.zomi: Mipi tawlngakni te-in thukhenna inn kikhak hi.

records.zomi: Thukhenna inn in ni tawh lai khat hong khak hi.

records.zomi: Thukhenna inndan-ah lift khat a om hiam?

records.english: The hearing was moved to Friday.
records.zomi: Thukhenna pen Laithai ni-ah kikhek hi.

records.english: How does the court help people who don't speak the local language?
records.zomi: Thukhenna inn in khuasung pau a ham thei lo mite bangci a huh hiam?

records.english: It provides a trained interpreter free of charge, so you should tell the court when you receive your letter.
records.zomi: A kisin pau letmi khat man om lo-in a pia hi, tua ahih manin na lai na ngah ciangin thukhenna inn gen in.

records.english: Is the court café open to the public?

records.english: The family court has a children's room with toys and books for young witnesses.
records.zomi: Innkuan thukhenna inn in theihpihtu naupang te adingin kawm leh laibu te tawh naupang inndan khat a nei hi.

records.english: Video evidence can protect vulnerable witnesses while still allowing a fair trial.
records.zomi: Video tettehna in thukhenna dik a phal lai-in a kem kisam theihpihtu te a kem thei hi.

records.english: How can I find out whether I'm entitled to free legal help?
records.zomi: Man om lo thukham huhna ka ngah thei hiam cih bangci ka theih thei ding hiam?

records.english: Mediation can resolve many disputes more quickly and cheaply than a court case.
records.zomi: Kilemna bawlna in kinialna tampi thukhenna inn thu sangin a manlang zaw-in leh man niam zaw-in a phel thei hi.

records.english: Long delays in the court system can cause real hardship for families waiting for decisions.
records.zomi: Thukhenna nasep dan-a sawtna lian te in thukhensatna a ngak innkuan te adingin haksatna taktak a piangsak thei hi.

records.english: The volunteer explained the court rules.
records.zomi: Thalawp in thukhenna inn thukham te a gen hi.

records.english: Is there somewhere quiet to wait before I give evidence?
records.zomi: Tettehna ka piak ma-in ngak nading mun dai khat a om hiam?

records.english: Yes, the witness service has a private room on the first floor.
records.zomi: Om hi, theihpihtu huhna pawl in inn tung lam-ah a kiseel inndan khat a nei hi.

records.english: The courthouse added ramps and a hearing loop after complaints from disabled visitors.
records.zomi: Liamna nei khualmite' phunna khit-in thukhenna inn in kahlei-zai te leh za theihna khawl khat a behlap hi.

records.english: The witness service offers visits to the courtroom before a trial so that witnesses know what to expect.
records.zomi: Theihpihtu huhna pawl in theihpihtu te in bang a ngak ding uh hiam cih a theih nadingin thukhenna ma-in thukhenna inndan kanna a pia hi.

records.english: Clear letters from the court reduce the number of people who miss hearings by mistake.
records.zomi: Thukhenna inn pan lai kician te in phawk lo-a thukhenna a mansuah mi tam zah a kiam sak hi.

records.english: Volunteers at the advice desk help people fill in court forms correctly.
records.zomi: Thuhilhna dawhkan-a thalawp te in mite thukhenna inn lai te a dik takin a gelh nadingin a huh uh hi.

records.english: Public trust in the courts depends on decisions being explained openly.
records.zomi: Mipi in thukhenna inn te a um nading pen thukhensatna te kihong taka kigen-ah a kinga hi.

records.english: Can I watch a trial today?
records.zomi: Tuni-in thukhenna khat ka en thei ding hiam?

records.english: I need a lawyer for my case.
records.zomi: Ka thu adingin thukham siam mi khat ka kisam hi.

records.english: Courts serve the community best when people can understand their procedures.
records.zomi: Mite in a nasep dan uh a theisiam thei ciangin thukhenna inn te in khuasung a huh hoih pen uh hi.

records.english: The court allowed my mother to sit beside me while I gave evidence.
records.zomi: Tettehna ka piak lai-in thukhenna inn in ka nu ka kiangah a tu thei dingin a phal hi.

records.english: Can I book the small meeting room?
records.zomi: Kikhopna inndan neu ka ngetsak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Centres that offer advice on money and housing can prevent problems from becoming crises.
records.zomi: Sum leh inn tawh kisai thuhilhna a pia inn lian te in buaina te buaina lian a suah loh nadingin a kem thei uh hi.

records.english: After the storm, the centre collected donations of clothes and furniture for families who had lost everything.
records.zomi: Huihpi khit-in inn lian in a neih khempeuh mansuah innkuan te adingin puan leh innsung van piakna te a kaikhawm hi.

records.english: Community centres often provide services that have disappeared from the high street, such as banking advice.
records.zomi: Khuasung inn lian te in bank thuhilhna bang khuapi lampi lian pan a mang khin nasep te a pia zel uh hi.

records.english: The community centre's language café pairs newcomers with local volunteers for informal conversation.
records.zomi: Khuasung inn lian' pau cafe in hong tung thak te khuasung thalawp te tawh kikupna baih adingin a kizop sak hi.

records.english: Food clubs at community centres help families stretch their budgets with dignity.
records.zomi: Khuasung inn lian te-a an pawl te in innkuan te a sum uh zahtakna tawh a zat sawt thei nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Shared spaces like community centres help neighbours from different backgrounds get to know each other.
records.zomi: Khuasung inn lian bang khawm-a zat mun te in nidang tuamtuam pan inn kiang mite a kitheih nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: The centre has a new lift.
records.zomi: Inn lian in lift thak khat a nei hi.

records.english: The centre's bike workshop fixed my brakes.
records.zomi: Inn lian' siiksakol bawlna mun in ka break te a bawlphat hi.

records.english: The yoga class starts at ten.
records.zomi: Yoga sinna nai sawm-in a kipan hi.

records.english: The centre's garden has a pond.
records.zomi: Inn lian' huan-ah tuili khat a om hi.

records.english: Accessible facilities ensure that disabled residents can take part fully in community life.
records.zomi: Zat baih mun te in liamna nei a sung-a teng mite khuasung nuntakna-ah a bup-in a kihel thei nadingin a kem hi.

records.english: The centre's noticeboard lists jobs.
records.zomi: Inn lian' thuzakna phah in nasep te a gen hi.

records.english: Can I use the centre's hall for a charity sale?
records.zomi: Huhna pawl adingin van zuakna khat-ah inn lian' inndan lian ka zang thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, charities pay half the usual price, but you'll need to book at least a month ahead.
records.zomi: Thei hi, huhna pawl te in a ngeina man' a khen khat a pia uh a, ahi zongin a tawm pen-in kha khat a ma-in na ngetsak ding kisam hi.

records.english: In emergencies, community centres can quickly become places of shelter and support.
records.zomi: Lauhuai hun te-in khuasung inn lian te manlang takin kihumbitna leh huhna mun te a suak thei uh hi.

records.english: Free coffee is served every morning.
records.zomi: Zingsang simin man om lo coffee kipia hi.

records.english: Why do so many groups compete for the main hall on Saturday mornings?
records.zomi: Bang hangin pawl tampi in Kiginni zingsang te-in inndan lian a kidaal uh hiam?

records.english: The bike workshop teaches teenagers to repair bicycles, which they can then keep.
records.zomi: Siiksakol bawlna mun in khangno te siiksakol bawlphat dan a hilh a, tua siiksakol te a nei thei uh hi.

records.english: Is the centre used as a polling station?
records.zomi: Inn lian pen vote lakna mun-in kizang hiam?

records.english: Yes, on election days the main hall closes for classes and opens for voting.
records.zomi: Kizang hi, vote lak ni te-in inndan lian in sinna te adingin a kikhak a, vote lak nadingin a kihong hi.

records.english: The kitchen can be hired for cooking classes.
records.zomi: An huanna pen an huan sinna adingin kihal thei hi.

records.english: How can a small group book the centre's minibus for a day trip?
records.zomi: Pawl neu khat in ni khat khualzinna adingin inn lian' minibus bangci a ngetsak thei hiam?

records.english: A well-run community centre depends on the work of volunteers as much as paid staff.
records.zomi: Hoih taka kivaihawm khuasung inn lian khat pen man piak nasemte' nasep bangin thalawp te' nasep-ah a kinga hi.

records.english: The centre's food club lets members buy groceries at a fraction of supermarket prices.
records.zomi: Inn lian' an pawl in a mite van zuakna lian' man' khen neu khat tawh an te a lei sak hi.

records.english: Can I hold a meeting there in the evening?
records.zomi: Nitak-in tua mun-ah kikhopna khat ka bawl thei ding hiam?

records.english: The centre hosts a blood donation day.
records.zomi: Inn lian in sisan piakna ni khat a bawl hi.

records.english: Giving young people real influence over a centre's activities helps keep them involved.
records.zomi: Khangno te inn lian' nasep te tungah thuneihna taktak piak in a kihel den nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: The youth council chose to spend this year's grant on a recording studio.
records.zomi: Khangno council in tu kum-a a ngah sum aw ciamtehna inndan khat-ah zang dingin a teel hi.

records.english: When residents help to run a centre, they develop a stronger sense of ownership and pride.
records.zomi: A sung-a teng mite in inn lian khat a vaihawm khawm ciangin amau' neih bangin a ngaihsut leh a kiphatsakna a hat zaw hi.

records.english: When the bank in our town closed, many older residents had no way to manage their money.
records.zomi: I khuapi-a bank a kikhak ciangin a sung-a teng upa tampi in a sum uh a kem thei nading lampi a nei kei uh hi.

records.english: The community centre arranged for a banking adviser to visit every Wednesday and set up a small room for private appointments.
records.zomi: Khuasung inn lian in Nilai ni simin bank thuhilhmi khat hong pai dingin a bawl sak a, kiseel kihona hun te adingin inndan neu khat a bawl hi.

records.english: Now the queue on Wednesday mornings is a chance to catch up with neighbours as well as to pay bills.
records.zomi: Tu-in Nilai ni zingsang-a mi tang pen man ngetna lai te pia bangin inn kiang mite tawh kiho kik nading hun khat zong ahi hi.

records.english: The centre is open late on Thursdays.
records.zomi: Inn lian pen Laizing ni simin a nunung dong a kihong hi.

records.english: During the elections, the centre's staff move all the furniture to make room for the voting booths.
records.zomi: Vote lak hun sungin inn lian' nasemte in vote lakna inn neu te adingin mun a om nadingin innsung van khempeuh a khek uh hi.

records.english: Why did the centre set up a youth council?
records.zomi: Bang hangin inn lian in khangno council khat a bawl hiam?

records.english: Because young people kept leaving, and the staff realised they needed a real say in how the centre was run.
records.zomi: Bang hang hiam cih leh khangno te a paikhia den uh a, inn lian bangci kivaihawm ding hiam cih tungah a thu gen theihna taktak a kisam uh hi, cih nasemte in a thei uh hi.

records.english: The council installed a new heating system at the centre after volunteers raised half the cost.
records.zomi: Thalawp te in a man' a khen khat a kaikhawm khit-un council in inn lian-ah inn lumsakna khawl thak khat a koih hi.

records.english: Does the centre have help with energy bills?
records.zomi: Inn lian in mei-et man tawh huhna a nei hiam?

records.english: An adviser comes every Thursday to check whether you're on the cheapest tariff.
records.zomi: Thuhilhmi khat Laizing ni simin a hong pai a, man niam pen tawh na zang hiam cih a en hi.

records.english: Is the hall big enough for a wedding?
records.zomi: Inndan lian in mopawi adingin a lian zo hiam?

records.english: Could the centre stay open on Sunday afternoons for people who work during the week?
records.zomi: Kal sungin nasep a sem mite adingin Nipini nitak lam-in inn lian a kihong den thei ding hiam?

records.english: The centre added a sensory room for children with autism after parents asked for one.
records.zomi: Nu leh pa te in a nget khit-un inn lian in autism nei naupang te adingin lungsim nuamsakna inndan khat a behlap hi.

records.english: Who runs the knitting circle?
records.zomi: Puan siam pawl kua in a makai hiam?

records.english: The centre lends books and toys.
records.zomi: Inn lian in laibu leh kawm te a puk sak hi.

records.english: How did the centre become a rest centre during the storm?
records.zomi: Huihpi lai-in inn lian bangci tawlngakna mun a suak hiam?

records.english: The council asked us to open overnight, and volunteers brought camp beds, blankets and hot food for families who had lost power.
records.zomi: Council in zan bup kihong dingin hong ngen a, thalawp te in mei-et a mansuah innkuan te adingin lupna neu te, puannak te leh an lum te a paipih uh hi.

records.english: Is the centre closed in August?
records.zomi: August kha-in inn lian a kikhak hiam?

records.english: Could the centre put on a session about staying safe online for older residents?
records.zomi: Inn lian in a sung-a teng upa te adingin online-ah bit taka om dan tawh kisai sinna khat a bawl thei ding hiam?

records.english: The centre's language café is on Fridays.
records.zomi: Inn lian' pau cafe pen Laithai ni-in ahi hi.

records.english: Is there a café at the centre?
records.zomi: Inn lian-ah cafe khat a om hiam?

records.english: Affordable room hire allows small charities and groups to meet without high costs.
records.zomi: Man niam inndan halna in huhna pawl neu te leh pawl te man tam lo-in a kikhawm thei nadingin a phal hi.

records.english: The voting booths are in the main hall.
records.zomi: Vote lakna inn neu te inndan lian-ah a om uh hi.

records.english: A podiatrist visits the centre once a month to check older residents' feet.
records.zomi: Khe siavuan khat kha khat-ah vei khat inn lian-ah a hong pai a, a sung-a teng upa te' khe a en hi.

records.english: Is there someone at the centre who can help me apply for a council flat?
records.zomi: Council inn khat ka nget nadingin hong huh thei inn lian-ah mi khat a om hiam?

records.english: The centre's board includes residents of every age, from a sixteen-year-old to a retired head teacher.
records.zomi: Inn lian' makaite pawl in kum sawm leh guk naupang khat pan pension ngah sang makaipa khat dong, kum tuamtuam-a a sung-a teng mite a huap hi.

records.english: Can teenagers use the music room?
records.zomi: Khangno te in late inndan a zang thei uh hiam?

records.english: Language cafés help newcomers practise everyday conversation in a relaxed setting.
records.zomi: Pau cafe te in hong tung thak te nuam taka mun-ah ni sim kikupna a kisin nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Community centres adapt to local needs, from election days to emergency shelters.
records.zomi: Khuasung inn lian te in vote lak ni pan lauhuai hun kihumbitna mun dong khuasung kisapna te tawh a kituak dingin a kikhek uh hi.

records.english: The centre offers free internet.
records.zomi: Inn lian in man om lo internet a pia hi.

records.english: What made the paint bubble?
records.zomi: Bang in ciatna a pokpok sak hiam?

records.english: Why are the lights flickering?
records.zomi: Bang hangin meivak te a mitmal hiam?

records.english: What's making that smell in the fridge?
records.zomi: Tuikhal sianna khawl sung-a tua namna bang in a bawl hiam?

records.english: Why did the bulb blow?
records.zomi: Bang hangin meivak bawk a kang hiam?

records.english: Why is the tap water cloudy?
records.zomi: Bang hangin tuikuang tui a nin hiam?

records.english: Why is the car so noisy?
records.zomi: Bang hangin mawtaw a ging mahmah hiam?

records.english: We realised the high heating bill was caused by a window that wouldn't close properly.
records.zomi: Inn lumsakna man tam pen hoih taka kikhak thei lo tawlet khat hangin ahi hi, cih i thei uh hi.

records.english: My manager asked what had caused the mistake before deciding how to fix it.

records.zomi: Sinna thak in amah pen kinot nasep pan sum a ngah hi, cih a lak ahih manin tu-in museum in a zawhna te leh tua susiatna te a gen tuak hi.

records.english: The school is named after a famous nurse.

records.english: Teaching children about local figures can inspire them to contribute to their own community.

records.english: The museum invited descendants of the town's first teacher to an exhibition about her life.

records.english: Public debate about statues and names can help a town understand its own history more honestly.

records.english: My daughter used Grandpa's stories for a school project about how life has changed.

records.english: Can you write down Grandma's story?

records.english: Dad keeps the old tapes in a box.

records.english: I keep a copy of every recording.

records.english: When Grandma's memory began to fade, we were glad we had recorded her stories years earlier.

records.english: Who is in this old photo, Grandma?

records.english: Families that ask questions early save stories that might otherwise be lost forever.
records.zomi: A ma-in dotna a dong innkuan te in a dang-in a mang khin ding tangthu te a kem uh hi.

records.english: Can I ask you about your childhood?
records.zomi: Na naupan lai tawh kisai kong dong thei ding hiam?

records.english: Grandma laughs at her old stories.

records.english: Translating family recordings helps relatives who grew up in other countries feel connected to their roots.
records.zomi: Innkuan ciamtehna te let in gamdang-ah a khang sanggam te a bul uh tawh a kizom bangin a kizak nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: We sent the stories to our cousins abroad.

records.english: My grandmother asked us to record her voice saying a blessing for each grandchild.
records.zomi: Ka pi in tu khat ciat adingin thupha a gen aw ciamteh dingin hong ngen hi.

records.english: My brother made a family tree that links each story to the person who told it.
records.zomi: Ka sanggampa in tangthu khat ciat a gen mi tawh a kizop sak innkuan kung khat a bawl hi.

records.english: My uncle knows the oldest family stories.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in innkuan tangthu lui pen te a thei hi.

records.english: Do your children ask you about the places your family lived before?

records.zomi: Gamdang-ah a khang sanggam te in a theisiam thei nadingin ka ni in ciamtehna lui te a let hi.

records.english: Old photographs often unlock memories that elderly people find hard to recall on their own.
records.zomi: Photo lui te in upa te in amau mah-in a phawk haksa sa phawkna te a hong zel hi.

records.english: Listening to the voices of relatives who have died can bring comfort to grieving families.
records.zomi: A si khin sanggam te' aw ngai in a lungkham innkuan te lungmuanna a pia thei hi.

records.english: Some families decide that certain stories are private, and respecting that choice matters.
records.zomi: Innkuan pawlkhat in tangthu pawlkhat kisel ding hi, ci-in a thukhen uh a, tua teelna zahtak pen a thupi hi.

records.english: Grandpa corrected my notes when I mixed up the names of two of his brothers.

records.english: Stories told within a family change slightly over time, and each version has its own value.

records.english: Why do the old people in our family remember stories better than they remember last week?

records.english: When my grandmother turned ninety, my cousins and I sat with her for three afternoons and recorded everything she remembered.

records.english: She described her wedding, the year the village moved to the valley and the names of every relative in an old photograph.

records.english: After she died, we played the recordings at the family gathering, and even the youngest children sat in silence to listen.

records.english: My cousin films Grandma's stories.

records.zomi: Ka pa in Nipini simin Pu dotna khat a dong a, a dawnna innkuan laibu neu khat-ah a gelh hi.

records.english: I recorded Grandpa on my phone.
records.zomi: Ka phone-ah Pu ka ciamteh hi.

records.english: We made a family book of stories.
records.zomi: Tangthu innkuan laibu khat i bawl uh hi.

records.english: Oral histories help younger family members understand the hardships and choices of earlier generations.
records.zomi: Kam tawh tangthu te in innkuan-a khangno te in khang masa te' haksatna te leh teelna te a theisiam nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: When my uncle visited from abroad, he added stories that nobody else in the family knew.

records.english: Did your mother tell you this story?

records.english: We listen to Grandpa's voice at Christmas.
records.zomi: Christmas-in Pu' aw i ngai uh hi.

records.english: Listening to the recordings, I noticed that Grandma changed small details every time she told a story.
records.zomi: Ciamtehna te ka ngaih lai-in Pi in tangthu khat a gen vei khempeuh-in thu neu te a khek hi, cih ka mu hi.

records.english: Why does our family meet every year to listen to the old recordings?

records.english: Hearing the voices of relatives who have died reminds us where we come from and keeps their memory alive for the children.
records.zomi: A si khin sanggam te' aw za in koi pan i hong pai hiam cih hong phawk sak a, naupang te adingin a phawkna uh a kem den hi.

records.english: Our family keeps the recordings on a computer and on two memory sticks in different houses.

records.english: The children love hearing about the old days.
records.zomi: Naupang te in nidang hun tawh kisai za a nuam sa mahmah uh hi.

records.english: Grandpa's memory is still very sharp.
records.zomi: Pu' phawkna a hat mahmah lai hi.

records.english: Mum labels every recording with a date.

records.english: Recording elderly relatives preserves voices and memories that writing alone cannot capture.
records.zomi: Innkuan upa te ciamteh in laigelh bek in a ciamteh zo loh aw te leh phawkna te a kem hi.

records.english: Grandma tells a story every Sunday.
records.zomi: Pi in Nipini simin tangthu khat a gen hi.

records.english: My sister types up the stories.

records.english: What did you learn when you interviewed your great-aunt?
records.zomi: Na pi nu' sanggamnu na dot ciangin bang na sin hiam?

records.english: She told me how the family survived a hungry winter by sharing one cow's milk among three houses.

records.english: Christian teaching on providence does not promise an easy life, but it does promise God's presence.

records.zomi: Kum Thak simin i innkuan in Josef' tangthu i sim uh a, Pasian in haksatna sung pan thu hoih bangci a piangsak hiam cih i phawk uh hi.

records.english: My parents believe that God guided them to each other when they met in a crowded bus station.

records.english: Did God send the rain for the farmers?
records.zomi: Pasian in lo nasem te adingin guah a zuak sak hiam?

records.english: When our house was damaged in a storm, my parents had no money to repair the roof.

records.english: Within a week, neighbours from our church arrived with ladders and tiles, and a builder they knew offered to work for free.

records.english: Could we write down the things we're thankful for this year and read them at Christmas?

records.english: My husband and I disagree about how much God plans our lives, but we both trust that he cares for us.

records.english: Does God know when I'm sad?

records.english: Can God help Grandpa get better?

records.english: After the operation went well, my father wrote a letter of thanks to the hospital and said a prayer of thanks to God.

records.english: Families who share their struggles in prayer often find strength in one another as well as in God.

records.english: Christians differ in how they understand providence, but many share a trust that God is with them.

records.english: Why do Christians in our family say that God provides even when things go badly?

records.english: Many Christians believe that God's care is not the same as an easy life, and that he stays with them through suffering.

records.english: For many believers, the kindness of neighbours and strangers is one way God's care is shown.

records.english: Why do some prayers seem to go unanswered, Grandma?
records.zomi: Pi, bang hangin thu ngetna pawlkhat a kidawng lo bang hiam?

records.english: We prayed when the baby was sick.
records.zomi: Nauneu a cina ciangin thu i ngen uh hi.

records.english: Dad says God gave us our home.
records.zomi: Pasian in i inn hong pia hi, ci-in Pa in a gen hi.

records.english: God helped us find a new house, Mum says.
records.zomi: Pasian in inn thak khat i muh nadingin hong huh hi, ci-in Nu in a gen hi.

records.english: Mum prays for us every morning.
records.zomi: Nu in zingsang simin eite adingin thu a ngen hi.

records.english: We pray for our family far away.

records.english: My teenage son struggles to believe in God's care since his friend died, and we talk about it often.

records.english: Why does Grandma thank God when things go wrong?

records.english: She believes God cares for us even in hard times and can bring good out of them.

records.english: Many Christian families see God's providence most clearly when they look back on difficult years.

records.english: Giving thanks together for daily provision is a simple way many families express their faith.

records.english: Keeping a record of answered prayers helps some families remember God's faithfulness in hard times.

records.english: My aunt keeps a jar of notes about small blessings and opens it whenever she feels discouraged.

records.english: How did your family trust God during the year Grandpa was ill?
records.zomi: Pu a cina kum sungin na innkuan in Pasian bangci a um uh hiam?

records.english: We prayed together every evening, accepted help from neighbours and believed that God would not leave us alone.
records.zomi: Nitak simin khawm-in thu i ngen uh a, inn kiang mite' huhna i la uh a, Pasian in hong nusia ngei kei ding hi, ci-in i um uh hi.
