records.zomi: Innkuan pawi te tawh kituak dingin ka tawlngakni te ka ngaihsun a, kikhopna lian khat a om ding ciangin ka manager a ma-in ka gen hi.

records.english: At the office, I keep a calendar of family events so that I can book leave early.
records.zomi: Office-ah tawlngak ni a ma-in ka ngen theih nadingin innkuan pawi te' calendar khat ka kem hi.

records.english: Why did your manager allow you to work from home while your father was ill?
records.zomi: Na pa a cina lai-in bang hangin na manager in inn pan nasep sem dingin hong phal hiam?

records.english: I explained that in our family the eldest child cares for sick parents, and my manager understood how important that was.
records.zomi: I innkuan-ah ta upa pen in a nu leh pa cina te a kem hi, ci-in ka gen a, tua bangzah a thupi hiam cih ka manager in a theisiam hi.

records.english: Schools that ask pupils about their families help them feel their backgrounds are valued.
records.zomi: A innkuan uh tawh kisai sangnaupang te a dong sang te in a nidang uh a manpha bangin a kizak nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Explaining family customs to colleagues can reduce misunderstandings at work.
records.zomi: Nasem pih te kiangah innkuan ngeina te gen in nasep mun-ah kitheisiam lohna te a kiam sak thei hi.

records.english: When my colleagues asked why so many relatives came to my wedding, I explained how close our family is.
records.zomi: Ka mopawi-ah bang hangin sanggam tampi a hong pai uh hiam cih ka nasem pih te in a dot ciangin i innkuan bangzah a kinai hiam cih ka gen hi.

records.english: My aunt runs a small shop with her sons.
records.zomi: Ka ni in a tapa te tawh zuakna inn neu khat a makai hi.

records.english: My nephew starts school this year.
records.zomi: Ka tu in tu kum-in sang a kipan hi.

records.english: I'm the eldest grandchild in my family.
records.zomi: Ka innkuan-ah tu upa pen ka hi hi.

records.english: My manager was impressed when twenty of my relatives came to cheer at my graduation.
records.zomi: Ka sang zawhna pawi-ah ka sanggam sawm nih in hong hanthawn dingin a hong pai uh ciangin ka manager a lamdang sa hi.

records.english: Can I miss school for my grandmother's funeral?
records.zomi: Ka pi' vuina adingin sang ka nusia thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, and the school will give you time to catch up afterwards.
records.zomi: Thei hi, leh a nung-ah na zui kik nadingin sang in hun hong pia ding hi.

records.english: I call my grandparents every Sunday.
records.zomi: Nipini simin ka pu leh pi ka sam hi.

records.english: Extended families can share the costs of education, care and celebrations.
records.zomi: Sanggam tampi a nei innkuan te in sinna, kemna leh pawi te' man a hawm thei uh hi.

records.english: My aunt, who is a nurse, encouraged me to apply for nursing college.
records.zomi: Nurse ahi ka ni in nurse sanginn-ah ngen dingin hong hanthawn hi.

records.english: My father's brother is my teacher.
records.zomi: Ka pa' sanggampa pen ka saya ahi hi.

records.english: Can I leave early to meet my relatives at the airport?
records.zomi: Vanlengtual-ah ka sanggam te dawn dingin a ma-in ka paikhia thei ding hiam?

records.english: My younger sister lives with my family during the week so that she can attend a better school.
records.zomi: Sang hoih zaw khat-ah a kah theih nadingin ka sanggamnu neu kal sungin ka innkuan tawh a teng hi.

records.english: My boss met my whole family at the wedding.
records.zomi: Ka makaipa in mopawi-ah ka innkuan bup a mu hi.

records.english: Does your cousin study at the same college as you?
records.zomi: Na sanggam nangma tawh college kibang-ah a kisin hiam?

records.english: Why did you take a day off work last week?
records.zomi: Bang hangin kal nunung in nasep pan ni khat na tawlngak hiam?

records.english: My cousin was getting married, and in our family everyone helps prepare the wedding.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam a kiteng ding a, i innkuan-ah mi khempeuh in mopawi kiginna-ah a huh uh hi.

records.english: Do your colleagues know how many relatives depend on your income?
records.zomi: Na sum ngahna tungah sanggam bangzah in a kinga uh hiam cih na nasem pih te in a thei uh hiam?

records.english: Why do some employers find it hard to understand how much family events matter to us?
records.zomi: Bang hangin nasep nei pawlkhat in innkuan pawi te eite adingin bangzah a thupi hiam cih a theisiam haksa sa uh hiam?

records.english: Do you send money to your parents every month?
records.zomi: Kha simin na nu leh pa kiangah sum na khak hiam?

records.english: Employers who understand employees' family responsibilities can build more loyal teams.
records.zomi: Nasemte' innkuan mawhpuakna te a theisiam nasep nei te in a muanhuai zaw pawl te a bawl thei uh hi.

records.english: Who helped you find your first job?
records.zomi: Na nasep masa pen muh nadingin kua in hong huh hiam?

records.english: My uncle, who knew the manager of the factory where he worked.
records.zomi: A nasepna sepna inn' makaipa a thei ka pa neu.

records.english: When my teacher asked our class to draw a family tree, mine needed three sheets of paper.
records.zomi: Ka saya in i class innkuan kung khat zuk dingin a ngen ciangin keimah' a ciin thum a kisam hi.

records.english: My grandmother helped me remember every uncle, aunt and cousin, and she explained who had married into which clan.
records.zomi: Ka pi in pa neu, ni leh sanggam khempeuh ka phawk nadingin hong huh a, kua in koi phung-ah a kiteng hiam cih hong gen hi.

records.english: The teacher pinned it on the wall and asked me to explain to the class how our relatives look after one another.
records.zomi: Saya in pal-ah a kap a, i sanggam te in a khat le khat bangci a kem uh hiam cih class tungah gen dingin hong ngen hi.

records.english: Family support can make the difference between giving up and finishing a course.
records.zomi: Innkuan huhna in sinna khat lungkiat leh zawh kikal-ah kibang lohna a bawl thei hi.

records.english: Workplaces benefit when they recognise that family obligations differ between cultures.
records.zomi: Innkuan mawhpuakna te ngeina tuamtuam kikal-ah a kibang lo hi, cih a theisiam ciangin nasep mun te phattuamna a ngah uh hi.

records.english: Balancing work with family duties requires planning and honest conversations.
records.zomi: Nasep leh innkuan mawhpuakna te kibang taka kem in ngaihsutna leh kikupna tak te a kisam hi.

records.english: I told my teacher about my big family.
records.zomi: Ka innkuan lian tawh kisai ka saya kiangah ka gen hi.

records.english: Respect learned within the family often shapes how people treat others at school and work.
records.zomi: Innkuan sungah a kisin zahtakna in sang leh nasep mun-ah mite in midangte bangci a bawl uh hiam cih a bawl zel hi.

records.english: My brother found me this job.
records.zomi: Ka sanggampa in hih nasep hong zong sak hi.

records.english: Young people who move away for work often stay closely connected to their relatives.
records.zomi: Nasep adingin a pem khangno te in a sanggam uh tawh a kinai taka a kizom den zel uh hi.

records.english: The Bible is on the table by the window.
records.zomi: Lai Siangtho pen tawlet kiang-a dawhkan tungah a om hi.

records.english: Why do Christians say that Jesus shows us what God is like?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Khazih mite in Jesu in Pasian bangci a om hiam cih hong lak hi, a ci uh hiam?

records.english: They believe that in his life, teaching, death and resurrection God has revealed himself more fully than anywhere else.
records.zomi: A nuntakna, a thuhilhna, a sihna leh a thawhkikna-ah Pasian in mun dang khempeuh sangin amah a kicing zaw-in a kilaksak hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: My sister is learning a psalm.
records.zomi: Ka sanggamnu in Late khat a sin hi.

records.english: Parents who answer children's questions honestly help them think carefully about faith.
records.zomi: Naupang te' dotna te a dik takin a dawng nu leh pa te in upna tawh kisai kidawm taka a ngaihsun nadingin a huh uh hi.

records.english: Grandpa underlines verses he loves.
records.zomi: Pu in a deih Lai Siangtho cang te nuai-ah tang a khai hi.

records.english: We listen to the Bible on the radio.
records.zomi: Radio tungah Lai Siangtho i ngai uh hi.

records.english: Our family often reads a Bible passage together before making a big decision.
records.zomi: I innkuan in thukhensatna lian khat i bawl ma-un Lai Siangtho khen khat khawm-in i sim zel uh hi.

records.english: Every Christmas, the youngest child in our family reads the story of Jesus' birth.
records.zomi: Christmas simin i innkuan-a naupang neu pen in Jesu' pianna tangthu a sim hi.

records.english: How do you explain difficult Bible stories to young children?
records.zomi: Lai Siangtho tangthu haksa te naupang neu te kiangah bangci na gen hiam?

records.english: Translations into everyday languages have allowed many families to read the Bible for themselves.
records.zomi: Ni sim pau te-a kilet Lai Siangtho te in innkuan tampi amau mah-in Lai Siangtho a sim thei nadingin a phal hi.

records.english: Old family Bibles often hold handwritten notes that connect generations.
records.zomi: Innkuan Lai Siangtho lui te in khang tuamtuam a kizom sak khut tawh kigelh ciamtehna te a nei zel uh hi.

records.english: Why do Christians in our family read the Gospels more often than other books?
records.zomi: Bang hangin i innkuan-a Khazih mite in laibu dang te sangin Lungdamna Thu laibu te a sim zel zaw uh hiam?

records.english: Mum reads us a Bible story every night.
records.zomi: Nu in zan simin Lai Siangtho tangthu khat hong sim sak hi.

records.english: My teenage daughter has started reading the Bible on her own, and she asks me hard questions.
records.zomi: Kum sawm leh tawm ka tanu in amah mah-in Lai Siangtho a sim kipan a, dotna haksa te hong dong hi.

records.english: Why do we read the Bible after dinner?
records.zomi: Bang hangin nitak an khit-in Lai Siangtho i sim uh hiam?

records.english: Because we believe God speaks to us through it, and we want to listen together as a family.
records.zomi: Bang hang hiam cih leh Pasian in tua tungtawn-in hong gen hi, ci-in i um a, innkuan khat bangin khawm-in i ngai nuam uh hi.

records.english: My brother has a children's Bible.
records.zomi: Ka sanggampa in naupang Lai Siangtho khat a nei hi.

records.english: Within one family, Christians may interpret some passages differently while sharing the same faith.
records.zomi: Innkuan khat sungah Khazih mite in upna kibang a hawm lai-un cang pawlkhat a theisiam dan uh kibang lo thei hi.

records.english: Many Christians believe that the Holy Spirit helps readers understand what they read in the Bible.
records.zomi: Khazih mi tampi in Kha Siangtho in simmite Lai Siangtho-ah a sim te a theisiam nadingin a huh hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: Dad bought a Bible in our language.
records.zomi: Pa in i pau tawh Lai Siangtho khat a lei hi.

records.english: Who wrote the Bible, Grandpa?
records.zomi: Pu, Lai Siangtho kua in a gelh hiam?

records.english: Many different people over many centuries, and Christians believe God guided what they wrote.
records.zomi: Kum za tampi sungin mi tuamtuam tampi in, leh a gelh uh pen Pasian in a lamlak hi, ci-in Khazih mite in a um uh hi.

records.english: Grandpa says that the Bible became much clearer to him when it was translated into his own language.
records.zomi: Lai Siangtho a pau mah-in a kilet ciangin a kician zaw mahmah hi, ci-in Pu in a gen hi.

records.english: On Sunday evenings, my husband reads a chapter aloud to the children before bed.
records.zomi: Nipini nitak te-in ka pasal in naupang te a ihmut ma-un khen khat aw sang tawh a sim sak hi.

records.english: Can I have my own Bible for my birthday?
records.zomi: Ka piancil ni adingin keimah' Lai Siangtho khat ka ngah thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, and we'll choose one with pictures and a big map at the back.
records.zomi: Thei hi, a nung lam-ah lim te leh map lian khat a nei khat i teel ding hi.

records.english: Do your children understand that Christians see Jesus as God's clearest word to people?
records.zomi: Khazih mite in Jesu pen Pasian in mite tungah a gen kician pen thu ahi hi, a ci uh cih na ta te in a theisiam uh hiam?

records.english: Our family keeps the old Bible that my great-grandparents brought from their village.
records.zomi: I innkuan in ka pi nu' nu leh pa te in a khuaneu uh pan a paipih Lai Siangtho lui a kem hi.

records.english: My mother copied her favourite verses into a notebook, which we now read at family gatherings.
records.zomi: Ka nu in a deih cang te laibu neu khat-ah a gelh kik a, tu-in innkuan kikhopna te-ah i sim uh hi.

records.english: Mum writes verses on cards for us.
records.zomi: Nu in eite adingin cang te card tungah a gelh hi.

records.english: For many Christians, the life of Jesus is the clearest way God has made himself known.
records.zomi: Khazih mi tampi adingin Jesu' nuntakna pen Pasian in amah a kitheisak kician pen lampi ahi hi.

records.english: Why are there so many books in the Bible?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Lai Siangtho sungah laibu tampi a om hiam?

records.english: Can you read me the story of Noah?
records.zomi: Noah' tangthu hong sim sak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: When my father was dying, he asked me to read the Gospel of John to him every evening.
records.zomi: Ka pa a sih kuan ciangin nitak simin Johan' Lungdamna Thu sim sak dingin hong ngen hi.

records.english: Some nights he fell asleep after a few verses, but on others he asked me to read the same chapter again and again.
records.zomi: Zan pawlkhat-in cang bangzah khit-in a ihmu a, a dang te-in khen kibang vei tampi sim kik dingin hong ngen hi.

records.english: After he died, I found his old Bible with those chapters underlined in pencil from his own youth.
records.zomi: A sih khit-in a khangno lai pan pencil tawh nuai-ah tang a khaisa tua khen te tawh a Lai Siangtho lui ka mu hi.

records.english: Children who hear Bible stories at home often carry them into adulthood.
records.zomi: Inn-ah Lai Siangtho tangthu a za naupang te in a upa ciang-un a paipih zel uh hi.

records.english: Which Bible story do you like best?
records.zomi: Koi Lai Siangtho tangthu na deih pen hiam?

records.english: Does God still speak today?
records.zomi: Pasian in tuni dong thu a gen lai hiam?

records.english: After the funeral, we found comfort in the passages Grandma had marked in her Bible.
records.zomi: Vuina khit-in Pi in a Lai Siangtho sungah a ciamteh khen te-ah lungmuanna i mu uh hi.

records.english: Grandpa knows many verses by heart.
records.zomi: Pu in cang tampi a lungsim sungah a thei hi.

records.english: Many Christian families read the Bible together because they believe God speaks through it.
records.zomi: Khazih mite innkuan tampi in Pasian in Lai Siangtho tungtawn-in thu a gen hi, ci-in a um uh ahih manin khawm-in a sim uh hi.

records.english: Could we read a psalm together before we visit Grandpa in hospital?
records.zomi: Pu damlo inn-ah i kan ma-un Late khat khawm-in i sim thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: Who was Moses, Mum?
records.zomi: Nu, Moses kua ahi hiam?

records.english: My parents chose a verse for each of their children when we were baptised.
records.zomi: Kote baptaiz i kiciang uh ciangin ka nu leh pa in a ta khat ciat adingin cang khat a teel uh hi.

records.english: Grandma reads her Bible every morning.
records.zomi: Pi in zingsang simin a Lai Siangtho a sim hi.

records.english: Reading Scripture together can help families face illness and grief with hope.
records.zomi: Lai Siangtho khawm-in sim in innkuan te natna leh lungkhamna lametna tawh a maitang nadingin a huh thei hi.

records.english: We learned a new verse this week.
records.zomi: Hih kal-in cang thak khat i sin uh hi.

records.english: When my daughter asked whether the Bible stories were true, we talked about how Christians understand them.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in Lai Siangtho tangthu te a tak hiam cih a dot ciangin Khazih mite in bangci a theisiam uh hiam cih i kikum uh hi.

records.english: My grandmother taught me to read using her Bible and a lamp at the kitchen table.
records.zomi: Ka pi in an huanna dawhkan-ah a Lai Siangtho leh meivak khat zang-in laisim hong hilh hi.

records.english: We pray before we read the Bible.
records.zomi: Lai Siangtho i sim ma-un thu i ngen uh hi.

records.english: Grandma's Bible is very old.
records.zomi: Pi' Lai Siangtho a lui mahmah hi.

records.english: When my son left home for university, I gave him a small Bible with a note inside.
records.zomi: Ka tapa sanglian-a kah dingin inn a nusiat ciangin a sung-ah lai neu khat tawh Lai Siangtho neu khat ka pia hi.

records.english: My son asked who Jesus was.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in Jesu kua ahi hiam cih a dong hi.

records.english: How did your parents teach you to read the Bible?
records.zomi: Na nu leh pa in Lai Siangtho sim dingin bangci hong hilh uh hiam?

records.english: They read a short passage with us every morning and asked what it told us about God.
records.zomi: Zingsang simin kote tawh khen tom khat a sim uh a, Pasian tawh kisai bang hong gen hiam cih a dong uh hi.

records.english: We read the Christmas story every year.
records.zomi: Kum simin Christmas tangthu i sim uh hi.

records.english: Can I read the next chapter?
records.zomi: Khen hong tung ding ka sim thei ding hiam?

records.english: A verse chosen at a child's baptism can become a lifelong source of encouragement.
records.zomi: Naupang khat' baptaiz kiciang ni-a kiteel cang khat in a nuntak sung hanthotna a suak thei hi.

records.english: Visiting the place where a family story happened can make it feel real for younger generations.
records.zomi: Innkuan tangthu khat a pianna mun kan in khang neu zaw te adingin a tak bangin a kizak sak thei hi.

records.english: Where did you and Grandpa go dancing?
records.zomi: Nangma leh Pu koi-ah laam dingin na pai uh hiam?

records.english: When places change beyond recognition, the memories of where things used to be become part of local heritage.
records.zomi: Mun te a theih theih nawn loh dong a kikhek ciangin nidang-a thu te koi-ah a om hiam cih phawkna te khuasung ngeina-a khen khat a suak hi.

records.english: Where did you find this photograph?
records.zomi: Hih photo koi-ah na mu hiam?

records.english: Where did your mother find the courage to start a business on her own?
records.zomi: Na nu in a khat bek-in sumbawlna khat kipan nading hanna koi pan a ngah hiam?

records.english: Nobody in our family knew where Great-Grandfather had worked before he married.
records.zomi: Pu' pa a kiten ma-in koi-ah nasep a sem hiam cih i innkuan-ah kuamah in a thei kei hi.

records.english: Last spring, my aunt found an old photograph of him standing outside a railway station in a uniform.
records.zomi: Spring nunung in ka ni in meileng station khat pua-ah puan tak silh-in a ding photo lui khat a mu hi.

records.english: We visited the station together, and an old porter remembered hearing his name from his own father.
records.zomi: Station i kan khawm uh a, van puamite upa khat in a min a pa pan a zak ngei a phawk hi.

records.english: Where was your first school?
records.zomi: Na sang masa pen koi-ah a om hiam?

records.english: Where did the old road go?
records.zomi: Lampi lui koi-ah a pai hiam?

records.english: Where did the children go to school before the village had a classroom?
records.zomi: Khuaneu in sinna inn a neih ma-in naupang te koi-ah sang a kah uh hiam?

records.english: Where did Grandpa keep his old army medals?
records.zomi: Pu in a galkap ciamtehna lui te koi-ah a kem hiam?

records.english: In a tin box under the bed, wrapped in a handkerchief.
records.zomi: Lupna nuai-a sik ip khat sungah, puan neu khat tawh kituam-in.

records.english: Where did your mother learn to sew?
records.zomi: Na nu in puan khui koi-ah a sin hiam?

records.english: Where did you spend your first night in the city?
records.zomi: Khuapi lian-ah na zan masa pen koi-ah na zang hiam?

records.english: Where was the wedding party held?
records.zomi: Mopawi koi-ah a kibawl hiam?

records.english: Where did you sleep during the long journey north?
records.zomi: Mal lam-a khualzinna sau sungin koi-ah na lum hiam?

records.english: On the floors of churches and schools, wherever the villagers let us stay.
records.zomi: Biakinn te leh sang te' inn leitang tungah, khuaneu mite in hong teng sak mun peuhmah-ah.

records.english: Where a story took place often explains why it was told in a particular way.
records.zomi: Tangthu khat a pianna mun in bang hangin tua bangin a kigen hiam cih a gen zel hi.

records.english: Where did people get married before the church was built?
records.zomi: Biakinn a kilam ma-in mite koi-ah a kiteng uh hiam?

records.english: Older people often remember places more clearly than dates, so questions about where things happened are easier to answer.
records.zomi: Upa te in ni te sangin mun te a phawk kician zaw zel uh ahih manin thu te koi-ah a piang hiam cih dotna te dawng a baih zaw hi.

records.english: Maps drawn from memory by grandparents can show where streets and buildings stood long ago.
records.zomi: Pu leh pi te in a phawkna pan a zuk map te in nidang sawt-a lampi te leh inn te koi-ah a ding hiam cih a lak thei hi.

records.english: Where did you grow up, Grandma?
records.zomi: Pi, koi-ah na khang hiam?

records.english: Where did you hide during the storm?
records.zomi: Huihpi lai-in koi-ah na bu hiam?

records.english: Where were the old village boundaries before the new road divided the fields?
records.zomi: Lampi thak in lo te a khen ma-in khuaneu' gam gi lui te koi-ah a om hiam?

records.english: Asking where a relative once lived can open a door to a whole forgotten chapter of family history.
records.zomi: Sanggam khat nidang-in koi-ah a teng hiam cih dotna in innkuan tangthu-a kimangngilh khen bup khat' kongkhak a hong thei hi.

records.english: Where did people in the town go for news before anyone had a radio?
records.zomi: Kuamah in radio a neih ma-in khuapi-a mite in thu koi-ah a ngah uh hiam?

records.english: To the market square, where a man read the newspaper aloud every Saturday morning.
records.zomi: Kizuakna mun lai-ah, Kiginni zingsang simin pasal khat in thusuah lai aw sang tawh a simna mun-ah.

records.english: Questions about where people sheltered in difficult times can bring back painful memories, so they should be asked gently.
records.zomi: Hun haksa te-in mite koi-ah a kihumbit uh hiam cih dotna te in lungkham huai phawkna te a hong paipih kik thei ahih manin nem takin kidong ding hi.

records.english: Where did your father go when he left home to look for work?
records.zomi: Na pa in nasep zong dingin inn a nusiat ciangin koi-ah a pai hiam?

records.english: Where did you play as a child?
records.zomi: Na naupan lai-in koi-ah na kawm hiam?

records.english: Where did the villagers fetch water before the pipes were laid?
records.zomi: Tuikuang a kikoih ma-in khuaneu mite koi-ah tui a khai uh hiam?

records.english: Where did you keep your savings?
records.zomi: Na sum kemsa koi-ah na kem hiam?

records.english: Where did your grandparents bury the family's valuables during the fighting?
records.zomi: Kidona lai-in na pu leh pi in innkuan' van manpha te koi-ah a phum uh hiam?

records.english: Where were you standing when you first saw the ocean?
records.zomi: Tuipi na muh masa pen ciangin koi-ah na ding hiam?

records.english: Where did your brother sleep when he first arrived abroad?
records.zomi: Na sanggampa gamdang-ah a tun masa ciangin koi-ah a lum hiam?

records.english: Knowing where a family came from helps children understand customs that might otherwise seem strange.
records.zomi: Innkuan khat koi pan a hong pai hiam cih theih in naupang te a dang-in lamdang bang a kilang ngeina te a theisiam nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Where did the travelling doctor see patients when he came through the valley?
records.zomi: Guam sungah a hong paikhiat ciangin kivei siavuan in damlo te koi-ah a en hiam?

records.english: Where did you live after the war?
records.zomi: Gal khit-in koi-ah na teng hiam?

records.english: Where was the old cinema that everyone in town talks about?
records.zomi: Khuapi-a mi khempeuh in a gen cinema lui koi-ah a om hiam?

records.english: Where were the horses kept?
records.zomi: Sakol te koi-ah a kikem hiam?

records.english: Where exactly was the house you were born in, and is it still standing?
records.zomi: Na pianna inn a dik takin koi-ah a om a, a ding lai hiam?

records.english: Where did you buy your first car?
records.zomi: Na mawtaw masa pen koi-ah na lei hiam?

records.english: Where did the old bakery stand?
records.zomi: Moh bawlna inn lui koi-ah a ding hiam?

records.english: Where did you first hear that song?

records.english: Where did Grandpa work before he retired?
records.zomi: Pu in a nasep a khawl ma-in koi-ah a sem hiam?

records.english: Many families have no records of where their ancestors lived, so spoken memories become precious.
records.zomi: Innkuan tampi in a pu leh pa te koi-ah a teng uh hiam cih ciamtehna a nei kei uh ahih manin kam tawh phawkna te a manpha mahmah hi.

records.english: Where did your uncle learn the trade that he practised all his life?
records.zomi: Na pa neu in a nuntak sung a sep siamna koi-ah a sin hiam?

records.english: Old photographs often raise the question of where they were taken, and the answer can surprise everyone.
records.zomi: Photo lui te in koi-ah kila hiam cih dotna a piangsak zel a, a dawnna in mi khempeuh a lamdang sak thei hi.

records.english: Where were you and Grandpa living when Mum was born?
records.zomi: Nu a pian ciangin nangma leh Pu koi-ah na teng uh hiam?

records.english: In a tiny room above a bakery, so the whole place smelled of bread.
records.zomi: Moh bawlna inn tung-a inndan neu mahmah khat-ah, tua ahih manin mun bup in moh namna a nam hi.

records.english: Recording where each family story happened makes an oral history far more useful to future readers.
records.zomi: Innkuan tangthu khat ciat koi-ah a piang hiam cih ciamteh in kam tawh tangthu khat hong tung ding simmite adingin a manpha zaw mahmah sak hi.

records.english: Where did the family hide the rice when soldiers came through the village?
records.zomi: Galkap te khuaneu sungah a hong paikhiat ciangin innkuan in buh koi-ah a sel uh hiam?

records.english: Under the floorboards of the kitchen, beneath a heavy wooden chest.
records.zomi: An huanna inn leitang sing nuai-ah, sing van ip gik khat nuai-ah.

records.english: Where was Dad born?
records.zomi: Pa koi-ah a piang hiam?

records.english: Where did the family go every summer?
records.zomi: Khal simin innkuan koi-ah a pai hiam?

records.english: Historians compare memories with old maps to work out where vanished buildings once stood.
records.zomi: Tangthu siam mite in a mang khin inn te nidang-in koi-ah a ding hiam cih a theih nadingin phawkna te map lui te tawh a teh khawm uh hi.

records.english: Where did the family stay while the new house was being built?
records.zomi: Inn thak a kilam lai-in innkuan koi-ah a om hiam?

records.english: Where did you and your friends meet when you were teenagers?
records.zomi: Kum sawm leh tawm na hih lai-un nangma leh na lawm te koi-ah na kimu uh hiam?

records.english: Where did you learn to swim?
records.zomi: Tuipeek koi-ah na sin hiam?

records.english: The local newspaper published a map showing where each polling station was.
records.zomi: Khuasung thusuah lai in vote lakna mun khat ciat koi-ah a om hiam cih a lak map khat a suah hi.

records.english: When polling stations move, clear notices prevent voters from turning up at the wrong place.
records.zomi: Vote lakna mun te a kikhek ciangin thuzakna kician te in vote lakmite mun khial-ah a tun loh nadingin a kem hi.

records.english: After complaints about long queues, the council opened two extra polling stations for the next election.
records.zomi: Mi tang sau te tawh kisai phunna te khit-in council in vote lakna hong tung ding adingin vote lakna mun behlap nih a hong hi.

records.english: Local services such as libraries and community centres play a quiet but important role in elections.
records.zomi: Laibu inn te leh khuasung inn lian te bang khuasung nasep te in vote lakna te-ah dai takin ahi zongin thupi takin a sem uh hi.

records.english: The library has a list of all the candidates.
records.zomi: Laibu inn in vote dingin ding mi khempeuh' lista khat a nei hi.

records.english: Is the voting information available in other languages?
records.zomi: Vote tawh kisai thu te pau dang te-in a om hiam?

records.english: The election office trained library staff to answer basic questions about registration.
records.zomi: Vote lakna office in laibu inn nasemte min gelhna tawh kisai dotna baih te a dawn nadingin a hilh hi.

records.english: Why did the community centre hold a meeting before the election?
records.zomi: Bang hangin vote lakna ma-in khuasung inn lian in kikhopna khat a bawl hiam?

records.english: So that residents could hear every candidate answer questions about local services in the same room.
records.zomi: A sung-a teng mite in vote dingin ding mi khempeuh in khuasung nasep te tawh kisai dotna te inndan kibang-ah a dawn uh a zak theih nadingin.

records.english: Clear information in several languages helps newer residents take part in local democracy.
records.zomi: Pau tampi-a thu kician in a sung-a teng thak zaw te khuasung mipi vaihawmna-ah a kihel nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: How does the council check that the polling stations are accessible to wheelchair users?
records.zomi: Vote lakna mun te wheelchair zangmite adingin a zat baih hiam cih council in bangci a en hiam?

records.english: Free transport to polling stations can make a real difference to turnout in rural areas.
records.zomi: Vote lakna mun te-ah man om lo khualzinna in khuaneu mun te-ah vote la mi tam zah tungah kikhekna taktak a bawl thei hi.

records.english: Why did the council close the library for a day during the election?
records.zomi: Bang hangin vote lak lai-in council in laibu inn ni khat a khak hiam?

records.english: Accessible polling stations allow disabled voters to take part without depending on others.
records.zomi: Zat baih vote lakna mun te in liamna nei vote lakmite midangte a kinga lo-in a kihel thei nadingin a phal hi.

records.english: Where can I register to vote?
records.zomi: Vote dingin koi-ah min ka gelh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Councils that publish easy-to-read election guides make it easier for first-time voters to take part.
records.zomi: Sim baih vote lakna lamlakna te a suah council te in vote masa pen a la mite a kihel nadingin a baih zaw sak uh hi.

records.english: The candidates will visit the market on Saturday.
records.zomi: Vote dingin ding mi te Kiginni-in kizuakna mun-ah a hong kan ding uh hi.

records.english: The town hall is open late for registration.
records.zomi: Khuapi office inn pen min gelhna adingin a nunung dong a kihong hi.

records.english: Local elections matter because they decide who manages many of the services people use every day.
records.zomi: Khuasung vote lakna te pen mite in ni simin a zat nasep tampi kua in a vaihawm ding hiam cih a thukhen ahih manin a thupi hi.

records.english: Can I vote at the community centre?
records.zomi: Khuasung inn lian-ah vote ka la thei ding hiam?

records.english: The council sent us a leaflet about the election.
records.zomi: Council in vote lakna tawh kisai laipek khat hong khak hi.

records.english: Bring your polling card and some identification.
records.zomi: Na vote card leh na hihna lak lai khat paipih in.

records.english: The youth centre held a session explaining how local elections affect services like buses and parks.
records.zomi: Khangno inn lian in khuasung vote lakna te in bus leh huan lian bang nasep te bangci a khoih hiam cih a gen hun khat a bawl hi.

records.english: Before the local election, our library offered free sessions to help residents register to vote.
records.zomi: Khuasung vote lakna ma-in i laibu inn in a sung-a teng mite vote dingin min a gelh nadingin a huh man om lo hun te a pia hi.

records.english: Volunteers sat with each person at a computer and explained every question on the form in plain language.
records.zomi: Thalawp te computer khat-ah mi khat ciat tawh a tu uh a, lai tung-a dotna khempeuh pau baih-in a gen uh hi.

records.english: By the end of the month, more than two hundred people had registered, many of them for the first time.
records.zomi: Kha a tawp ciangin mi za nih sanga tam in min a gelh uh a, a tam zaw te a masa pen vei-in ahi hi.

records.english: The council printed the voting guide in four languages so that every resident could understand it.
records.zomi: A sung-a teng khempeuh in a theisiam thei nadingin council in vote lakna lamlakna pau li-in a kheh hi.

records.english: In our town, the council sends a reminder by text to anyone who has registered for one.
records.zomi: I khuapi-ah council in a ngen kuapeuh tungah text tawh phawk sakna khat a khak hi.

records.english: Election staff who are trained to help voters with disabilities protect both access and secrecy.
records.zomi: Liamna nei vote lakmite huh dingin a kisin vote lakna nasemte in lutna leh kiseelna tuak a kem uh hi.

records.english: The council office can answer your questions about voting.
records.zomi: Council office in vote lakna tawh kisai na dotna te a dawng thei hi.

records.english: Our residents' association invited all the candidates to answer questions about the local clinic.
records.zomi: I a sung-a teng mite' pawl in vote dingin ding mi khempeuh khuasung damdawi inn neu tawh kisai dotna dawng dingin a sam hi.

records.english: Candidates' meetings held in community spaces allow residents to compare promises directly.
records.zomi: Khuasung mun te-a kibawl vote dingin ding mite' kikhopna te in a sung-a teng mite kiciamna te a diktak-in a teh khawm thei nadingin a phal hi.

records.english: Where can I get the election information in large print?
records.zomi: Vote lakna thu laimal lian-in koi-ah ka ngah thei ding hiam?

records.english: At the library or the council office, and you can also ask for an audio version.
records.zomi: Laibu inn ahih kei leh council office-ah, leh aw-a om khat zong na ngen thei hi.

records.english: The election results will be posted outside the town hall.
records.zomi: Vote lakna a piang te khuapi office inn pua-ah kikhai ding hi.

records.english: Who runs the polling stations?
records.zomi: Vote lakna mun te kua in a makai hiam?

records.english: When the polling station moved, the council put signs on every street corner to direct voters.
records.zomi: Vote lakna mun a kikhek ciangin vote lakmite a lamlak nadingin council in lampi kil khempeuh-ah thuzakna te a koih hi.

records.english: Postal voting helps people who are ill, disabled or working away from home to have their say.
records.zomi: Laikhak tawh vote in a cina, liamna nei ahih kei leh inn pan gamla-ah nasep sem mite a thu uh a gen thei nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Is there a phone number I can call if I have a problem on election day?
records.zomi: Vote lak ni-in buaina khat ka neih leh ka sam thei phone number khat a om hiam?

records.english: Do I need an appointment to register?
records.zomi: Min gelh nadingin kihona hun ka kisam hiam?

records.english: Is there a bus to the polling station from the care home?
records.zomi: Kemna inn pan vote lakna mun-ah bus khat a om hiam?

records.english: Yes, the council runs a free minibus every hour on election day.
records.zomi: Om hi, vote lak ni-in council in nai khat simin man om lo minibus khat a makai hi.

records.english: Is there parking near the polling station?
records.zomi: Vote lakna mun kiangah mawtaw koihna mun a om hiam?

records.english: Is there a ramp at the polling station?
records.zomi: Vote lakna mun-ah kahlei-zai khat a om hiam?

records.english: Our street's polling station has moved to the school.
records.zomi: I lampi' vote lakna mun sang-ah a kikhek hi.

records.english: The community centre is hosting a candidates' meeting.
records.zomi: Khuasung inn lian in vote dingin ding mite' kikhopna khat a bawl hi.

records.english: The polling station is in the library this year.
records.zomi: Tu kum-in vote lakna mun pen laibu inn-ah ahi hi.

records.english: Registration drives run by trusted local organisations often reach people that official campaigns miss.
records.zomi: Um huai khuasung pawl te in a bawl min gelhna hanciamna te in lai tak hanciamna te in a tun loh mite a tung zel uh hi.

records.english: The care home staff helped every resident who wanted to vote apply for a postal ballot.
records.zomi: Kemna inn nasemte in vote la nuam a sung-a teng mi khempeuh laikhak tawh vote ngen dingin a huh uh hi.

records.english: Could the community centre arrange a sign language interpreter for the candidates' debate?
records.zomi: Khuasung inn lian in vote dingin ding mite' kikupna adingin khut lahna pau letmi khat a bawl sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Can I bring my children to the polling station?
records.zomi: Vote lakna mun-ah ka ta te ka paipih thei ding hiam?

records.english: Can I get help filling in the postal vote form?
records.zomi: Laikhak tawh vote lai dim nadingin huhna ka ngah thei ding hiam?

records.english: Can someone help me read the ballot paper?
records.zomi: Vote lai sim nadingin kuamah in hong huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, the staff can help you, or you can bring a trusted friend or relative.
records.zomi: Thei hi, nasemte in hong huh thei uh a, ahih kei leh na um lawm ahih kei leh sanggam khat na paipih thei hi.

records.english: Volunteers at the advice centre help people who have lost their identity documents to register in time.
records.zomi: Thuhilhna mun-a thalawp te in a hihna lak lai uh a mansuah mite a hun ciangin min a gelh nadingin a huh uh hi.

records.english: Volunteers will drive older voters to the polls.
records.zomi: Thalawp te in vote lakmi upa te vote lakna mun-ah a paipih ding uh hi.

records.english: Could you tell me whether the polling station has a quiet room for people who feel anxious in crowds?
records.zomi: Vote lakna mun in mi tampi lak-ah a lau mite adingin inndan dai khat a nei hiam cih hong gen thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: How does the council make sure people in remote villages can vote?
records.zomi: Gamla khuaneu-a mite in vote a la thei nadingin council in bangci a en cian hiam?

records.english: It sets up polling stations in village halls and sends postal ballots to anyone who asks for one.
records.zomi: Khuaneu office inn te-ah vote lakna mun te a koih a, a ngen kuapeuh tungah laikhak tawh vote lai a khak hi.

records.english: Public trust in elections grows when residents can see that the process is open and fair.
records.zomi: Nasep dan a kihong leh a dik hi, cih a sung-a teng mite in a muh thei ciangin vote lakna tungah mipi' upna a khang hi.

records.english: Start with the main idea.
records.zomi: Ngaihsutna bulpi tawh kipan in.

records.english: Cross out the small details.
records.zomi: Thu neu te phiat in.

records.english: Practising with feedback is the most reliable way to improve at summarising.
records.zomi: Ngaihsutna tawh kisin pen thu tomno bawl siam nading lampi um huai pen ahi hi.

records.english: My notes are too messy.
records.zomi: Ka ciamtehna te a buai lua hi.

records.english: Many problems with summaries come from trying to include everything instead of choosing what matters.
records.zomi: Thu tomno tawh kisai buaina tampi pen bang a thupi hiam cih teel sangin khempeuh koih dingin hanciam pan a hong pai hi.

records.english: Short written summaries can help people remember advice they would otherwise forget.
records.zomi: Laigelh-a thu tomno tom te in mite in a dang-in a mangngilh ding thuhilhna te a phawk nadingin a huh thei hi.

records.english: After I left out the writer's warning, my summary gave the wrong impression of the article.
records.zomi: Laigelhmi' vaukhakna ka nusiat khit-in ka thu tomno in laigelh tawh kisai ngaihsutna khial a pia hi.

records.english: I ran out of time again.
records.zomi: Ka hun a bei kik hi.

records.english: Ask a friend to read your summary.
records.zomi: Na thu tomno sim dingin na lawm khat ngen in.

records.english: Summaries of meetings work best when they record decisions, deadlines and who is responsible.
records.zomi: Kikhopna thu tomno te in thukhensatna te, hun ciang te leh kua in mawhpuakna a nei hiam cih a ciamteh ciangin a hoih pen hi.

records.english: Read the text again before you start.
records.zomi: Na kipat ma-in laigelh sim kik in.

records.english: Why can't I finish my summary on time?
records.zomi: Bang hangin ka thu tomno a hun ciangin ka zo thei lo hiam?

records.english: Because you're trying to read and write at once, so read the whole text first.
records.zomi: Bang hang hiam cih leh khatvei-in sim leh gelh dingin na hanciam ahih manin laigelh bup a masa-in sim in.

records.english: I forgot the most important fact.
records.zomi: Thu thupi pen ka mangngilh hi.

records.english: My summary missed the ending.
records.zomi: Ka thu tomno in a tawpna a nusia hi.

records.english: The nurse found that patients forgot long explanations, so she began giving them short written summaries.
records.zomi: Damlo te in gennop sau te a mangngilh uh hi, cih nurse in a mu a, laigelh-a thu tomno tom te a pia kipan hi.

records.english: When my father received a long letter about his pension, he was too worried to read past the first page.
records.zomi: Ka pa in a pension tawh kisai lai sau khat a ngah ciangin lai mai masa pen khit-in a sim zo lo dong a lungkham hi.

records.english: I underlined the key dates and amounts and wrote them on a single card in large letters.
records.zomi: Ni thupi te leh sum zah te nuai-ah tang ka khai a, card khat bek tungah laimal lian tawh ka gelh hi.

records.english: Once he could see the whole message at a glance, he calmed down and phoned the office himself.
records.zomi: Thuzakna bup a et khatvei-in a muh theih ciangin a lungsim a nuam a, amah mah-in office a sam hi.

records.english: Why does my summary always miss the point that the teacher thinks is most important?
records.zomi: Bang hangin ka thu tomno in saya in a thupi pen a ci thu a nusia den hiam?

records.english: Why did the manager reject the summary of the customer survey?
records.zomi: Bang hangin manager in leimi dotna lai' thu tomno a nial hiam?

records.english: It reported only the positive comments, so the team would have missed the most serious complaints.
records.zomi: Ngaihsutna hoih te bek a gen ahih manin pawl in phunna gik pen te a mansuah ding hi.

records.english: I copied too much from the text.
records.zomi: Laigelh pan tam lua ka gelh kik hi.

records.english: Writing from memory helps summarisers use their own expressions instead of copying the original.
records.zomi: Phawkna pan gelh in thu tomno bawlmite in a bulpi gelh kik sangin amau' genna te a zat nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: When my summary kept growing, my teacher told me to choose just three main points.
records.zomi: Ka thu tomno a sau semsem ciangin ka saya in thu bulpi thum bek teel dingin hong gen hi.

records.english: Let's make a list of the key points.
records.zomi: Thu thupi te' lista khat bawl ni.

records.english: I used to summarise every chapter in detail, but now I write only the main argument of each.
records.zomi: Nidang-in khen khempeuh a kicing takin thu tomno ka bawl a, ahi zongin tu-in khen khat ciat' genna bulpi bek ka gelh hi.

records.english: When the report was too technical, I asked an engineer to check that my summary was accurate.
records.zomi: Report in nasep kammal tam lua a nei ciangin ka thu tomno a dik hiam cih en dingin engineer khat ka ngen hi.

records.english: What should I do if I don't understand part of the text?
records.zomi: Laigelh khen khat ka theisiam kei leh bang ka bawl ding hiam?

records.english: Ask someone or look it up before you summarise, or your summary may be wrong.
records.zomi: Thu tomno na bawl ma-in mi khat dong in ahih kei leh zong in, a hih kei leh na thu tomno a khial kha thei hi.

records.english: How can I stop my summaries from sounding like the original?
records.zomi: Ka thu tomno te a bulpi bangin a kilang lo nadingin bangci ka bawl thei ding hiam?

records.english: Close the text, write the main points from memory, and then check them against the original.
records.zomi: Laigelh khak in, thu bulpi te phawkna pan gelh in, tua khit-in a bulpi tawh en kik in.

records.english: How can I summarise a meeting when everyone talked at the same time?
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh hun kibang-in a gen ciangin kikhopna khat' thu tomno bangci ka bawl thei ding hiam?

records.english: Keep it short and clear.
records.zomi: Tom takin leh kician takin bawl in.

records.english: Cut this part in half.
records.zomi: Hih khen khen nih-in khen in.

records.english: Summaries that leave out important warnings can mislead readers as much as false information.
records.zomi: Vaukhakna thupi te a nusia thu tomno te in thu zuau bangin simmite a khem thei hi.

records.english: The volunteers' summaries were so different that we agreed on a simple checklist for everyone.
records.zomi: Thalawp te' thu tomno te a kibang lo mahmah ahih manin mi khempeuh adingin lista baih khat tungah i kituak uh hi.

records.english: Summarising technical material accurately sometimes requires help from an expert.
records.zomi: Nasep thu te a dik taka thu tomno bawl in a hun khenkhat-in siam mi khat' huhna a kisam hi.

records.english: My son's summaries improved once he started asking himself what a stranger would need to know.
records.zomi: Thei lo mi khat in bang a theih ding kisam hiam cih amah le amah a kidot kipat khit-in ka tapa' thu tomno te a hoih zaw hi.

records.english: I solved the problem of copying by explaining the text aloud before I wrote anything.
records.zomi: Bangmah ka gelh ma-in laigelh aw sang tawh gen-in gelh kikna buaina ka phel hi.

records.english: Could you help me shorten this summary without losing the most important facts?
records.zomi: Thu thupi pen te mansuah lo-in hih thu tomno tom sak dingin hong huh thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Is my summary fair to the writer?
records.zomi: Ka thu tomno in laigelhmi tungah a dik hiam?

records.english: I don't know what to leave out.
records.zomi: Bang ka nusia ding hiam cih ka thei kei hi.

records.english: How do I avoid leaving out an important exception when I summarise a set of rules?
records.zomi: Thukham te' thu tomno ka bawl ciangin a dang-a thu thupi khat ka nusiat loh nadingin bangci ka bawl ding hiam?

records.english: Could you tell me which parts of my summary are inaccurate?
records.zomi: Ka thu tomno-a koi khen te a dik lo hiam cih hong gen thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Underline the main ideas first.
records.zomi: Ngaihsutna bulpi te nuai-ah tang a masa-in khai in.

records.english: Is it better to summarise each section separately or the whole text at once?
records.zomi: Khen khat ciat a tuam-in thu tomno bawl in a hoih zaw hiam, laigelh bup khatvei-in?

records.english: My summary has too many numbers.
records.zomi: Ka thu tomno in nambat tam lua a nei hi.

records.english: Reading the whole text before writing prevents summaries that miss the main point.
records.zomi: Gelh ma-in laigelh bup sim in thu bulpi a mansuah thu tomno te a kem hi.

records.english: Count the main points first.
records.zomi: Thu bulpi te a masa-in sim in.

records.english: My summary doesn't fit on one page.
records.zomi: Ka thu tomno lai mai khat tungah a kiling kei hi.

records.english: My summary is longer than the article, so what went wrong?
records.zomi: Ka thu tomno laigelh sangin a sau zaw hi, tua ahih leh bang a khial hiam?

records.english: You kept the examples, so cut those and keep only the main points.
records.zomi: Ettehna te na kem ahih manin tua te phiat in la, thu bulpi te bek kem in.

records.english: Checking a summary against the original is the simplest way to catch mistakes.
records.zomi: Thu tomno khat a bulpi tawh en kik pen khialhna te mat nading lampi baih pen ahi hi.

records.english: I added my own opinion by mistake.
records.zomi: Phawk lo-in keimah' ngaihsutna ka behlap hi.

records.english: Good summarisers ask what their readers need to know rather than what they found interesting.

records.zomi: Zawi zawi-in, a tam lam-in hehna ka kem in amau' sangin keimah a hong na zaw sak hi, cih ka theih manin.

records.english: When I was a teenager, I asked my grandfather how he stayed so calm when things went wrong.
records.zomi: Kum sawm leh tawm ka hih lai-in, thu te a khial ciangin bangci a lungnuam den hiam cih ka pu ka dong hi.

records.english: He took me to his vegetable garden and showed me a plant that had been broken by a storm but was growing again.
records.zomi: Amah in a anteh huan-ah hong paipih a, huihpi in a kitam sak a, ahi zongin a khang kik singkung neu khat hong lak hi.

records.english: He said nothing more, but I have thought of that plant every time my own life has fallen apart.
records.zomi: Amah in bang zong gen nawn lo a, ahi zongin ka nuntakna a kisiat ciang khempeuh-in tua singkung neu ka ngaihsun hi.

records.english: What would you tell your younger self about worrying?
records.zomi: Lunghimawhna tawh kisai na naupan lai-a nangmah kiangah bang na gen ding hiam?

records.english: Have you learned to be patient?
records.zomi: Thuakzawh na sin khin hiam?

records.english: Answers about life lessons often reveal the values a person has lived by.
records.zomi: Nuntakna sinna tawh kisai dawnna te in mi khat in a zuih manphatna te a lak zel hi.

records.english: Sharing what we have learned is one way of making our mistakes useful to others.
records.zomi: I sin te hawm pen i khialhna te mi dang te adingin a phattuam nading lampi khat ahi hi.

records.english: Did you ever ignore good advice and later wish you hadn't?
records.zomi: Thuhilhna hoih na limsak lo ngei a, a nung-in na limsak ding hi ka ci, na ci ngei hiam?

records.english: Did travelling change you?
records.zomi: Khualzinna in hong khek hiam?

records.english: What keeps you hopeful?
records.zomi: Bang in hong lametna neisak den hiam?

records.english: Asking older people about their life lessons often brings out stories they have never shared.
records.zomi: Upa te kiangah a nuntakna sinna uh dot in a hawm ngei loh tangthu te a hong pusak zel hi.

records.english: What did living in another country teach you about your own home?
records.zomi: Gam dang khat-ah na om in na inn tawh kisai bang hong sinsak hiam?

records.english: Many of the most important lessons in life are learned through loss and recovery.
records.zomi: Nuntakna-a sinna thupi pen tampi pen mansuahna leh damkikna tungtawn-in kisin ahi hi.

records.english: Life lessons are often easier to accept when they come through a story rather than a rule.
records.zomi: Nuntakna sinna te pen thukham khat sangin tangthu khat tungtawn-in a hong pai ciangin a san baih zaw zel hi.

records.english: Did you learn anything from your first failure?
records.zomi: Na lawhsamna masa pen pan khat peuhpeuh na sin hiam?

records.english: Yes, that preparing well matters more than being confident.
records.zomi: Sin hi, a hoih takin kithukim pen hangsanna sangin a thupi zaw hi, cih.

records.english: Do you still follow your mother's advice?
records.zomi: Na nu' thuhilhna na zui lai hiam?

records.english: Did an illness ever change the way you saw your life?
records.zomi: Natna khat in na nuntakna na et dan a khek ngei hiam?

records.english: What lesson do you think young people today most need to hear?
records.zomi: Tu-a khangno te in a zak a kisam pen sinna bang ahi hi, na ci hiam?

records.english: That a life is built from small, steady choices, not from one big moment of luck.
records.zomi: Nuntakna pen teelna neu, kip te pan kilam ahi a, vannuam hun lian khat pan hi lo hi, cih.

records.english: Which of your grandparents' habits have you kept?
records.zomi: Na pu leh pi te' ngeina koi te na kem hiam?

records.english: Questions about what someone has learned invite reflection rather than boasting.
records.zomi: Mi khat in bang a sin hiam cih tawh kisai dotna te in kiphatsakna sangin ngaihsut kikna a sam hi.

records.english: How did your parents teach you right from wrong without lecturing you?
records.zomi: Na nu leh pa in hong thuhilh sau lo-in a hoih leh a hoih lo bangci hong sinsak uh hiam?

records.english: Is there anything about your past you would change?
records.zomi: Na nidang tawh kisai na khek nuam khat peuhpeuh a om hiam?

records.english: Did your parents teach you to save?
records.zomi: Na nu leh pa in sum kem dingin hong sinsak uh hiam?

records.english: What was your biggest mistake?
records.zomi: Na khialhna lian pen bang ahi hiam?

records.english: A simple question about advice can open a conversation that changes someone's direction.
records.zomi: Thuhilhna tawh kisai dotna baih khat in mi khat' a pai nading lam khek kikumna khat a hong thei hi.

records.english: Who do you admire most?
records.zomi: Kua na lamdang sa pen hiam?

records.english: What did school teach you about life?
records.zomi: Sang in nuntakna tawh kisai bang hong sinsak hiam?

records.english: How did you learn to accept the things you couldn't change?
records.zomi: Na khek theih loh thu te san bangci na sin hiam?

records.english: Who gave you the best advice?
records.zomi: Kua in thuhilhna hoih pen hong pia hiam?

records.english: Would you give the same advice to your children?
records.zomi: Na ta te kiangah thuhilhna kibang na pia ding hiam?

records.english: Our class cleans the school together.
records.zomi: I tanglai in sang khawm takin i siangsak uh hi.

records.english: Community values may need to be explained to colleagues from different backgrounds.
records.zomi: Khuasung manphatna te pen a kipatna kibang lo nasep lawm te kiangah hilhcian kisam thei hi.

records.english: We stay late when a colleague needs help.
records.zomi: Nasep lawm khat in huhna a kisam ciangin a nunung dong i om uh hi.

records.english: Who taught you to respect older colleagues?
records.zomi: Nasep lawm upa te zahtak dingin kua in hong sinsak hiam?

records.english: My grandmother, who said that people with experience deserve to be heard first.
records.zomi: Ka pi, theihna nei mite' thu a masa-in kingai ding hi, a ci nu.

records.english: Do you greet your boss every morning?
records.zomi: Zingsang simin na makaipa na cibai buk hiam?

records.english: Can I lend you my notes from yesterday's class?
records.zomi: Zan-a sang tanglai-a ka gelh te kong leitawi thei ding hiam?

records.english: Why do you think young people find it harder to keep these values in a city office?
records.zomi: Bang hangin khangno te in khuapi office khat-ah hih manphatna te a kem haksa zaw uh hi, na ci hiam?

records.english: How do your community's values help you at work?
records.zomi: Na khuasung' manphatna te in nasep-ah bangci hong huh hiam?

records.english: They taught me to keep my promises and to help others without being asked, and my manager notices that.
records.zomi: Ka kamciam te kem dingin leh kingen lo-in mi dang huh dingin hong sinsak uh a, ka manager in tua a mu hi.

records.english: Sharing and mutual help can turn a group of workers into a supportive team.
records.zomi: Hawm leh khat leh khat kihuh in nasemte pawl khat kithuahpih pawl khat-ah a khek thei hi.

records.english: My teacher says I'm very polite.
records.zomi: Ka sangsia in na zahtak mahmah hi, hong ci hi.

records.english: Workplaces benefit when employees help each other without waiting to be asked.
records.zomi: Nasemte in kingen ngak lo-in khat leh khat a kihuh ciangin nasepna mun te in phattuamna a ngah hi.

records.english: My manager asked me why I always arrive early, and I explained that my father did the same all his life.
records.zomi: Ka manager in bang hangin a ma-in hong tung den hiam cih hong dong a, ka pa in a nuntak sung khempeuh tua bangin a bawl hi, ci-in ka hilhcian hi.

records.english: Keeping community values alive in a new setting requires both pride and flexibility.
records.zomi: Mun thak khat-ah khuasung manphatna te a nungta-in kem in kiliansakna leh kikhek theihna a nih a kisam hi.

records.english: I help my classmates with their homework.
records.zomi: Ka sang lawm te a inn nasep uh-ah ka huh hi.

records.english: My boss trusts me because I'm honest.
records.zomi: Ka thuman ahih manin ka makaipa in hong um hi.

records.english: Why do you always help the new workers at the factory?
records.zomi: Bang hangin factory-a nasem thak te na huh den hiam?

records.english: My parents taught me that nobody should feel alone in a strange place.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh pa in mun theih ngei loh khat-ah kuamah a khat bek-in a kizak ding hi lo hi, ci-in hong sinsak uh hi.

records.english: The teachers at our school noticed that the older pupils looked after the younger ones without being told.
records.zomi: I sang-a sangsia te in sangnaupang upa zaw te in kigen lo-in a neu zaw te a kem uh hi, cih a mu uh hi.

records.english: When a classmate's father died, our whole class collected money for the family.
records.zomi: Sang lawm khat' pa a sih ciangin, i tanglai khempeuh in innkuan adingin sum i kaikhawm uh hi.

records.english: Can I help you carry those books?
records.zomi: Tua laibu te kong puak sak thei ding hiam?

records.english: I thank the cleaner every evening.
records.zomi: Zan simin innsiangsakmi tungah lungdam ka ko hi.

records.english: My teacher taught us to be kind.
records.zomi: Ka sangsia in mi tungah hoih dingin hong sinsak hi.

records.english: My father told me to work for an employer as carefully as if the business were my own.
records.zomi: Ka pa in nasep nei khat adingin nasep pen ka sumbawlna hi bangin kidawm takin sem dingin hong gen hi.

records.english: Our team shares the hard jobs fairly.
records.zomi: I pawl in nasep haksa te a dik takin i hawm uh hi.

records.english: Our youth group helps younger pupils with reading every Saturday morning.
records.zomi: I khangno pawl in Kiginni zingsang simin sangnaupang neu zaw te laisim-ah a huh hi.

records.english: I offer my seat to older teachers.
records.zomi: Sangsia upa zaw te kiangah ka tutna ka pia hi.

records.english: My father works hard and never complains.
records.zomi: Ka pa in hanciam takin nasep a sem a, a phun ngei kei hi.

records.english: Young people who carry their community's values into new workplaces can influence others.
records.zomi: A khuasung' manphatna te nasepna mun thak te-ah a paipih khangno te in mi dang te a khek thei uh hi.

records.english: I was raised never to speak badly about colleagues behind their backs.
records.zomi: Nasep lawm te' nungah a hoih lo-in gen ngei lo dingin hong khankhia uh hi.

records.english: Honesty at work builds trust that is difficult to win back once it is lost.
records.zomi: Nasep-a thumanna in a mansuah khit-in ngah kik haksa upna a lam hi.

records.english: Does your team celebrate birthdays at work?
records.zomi: Na pawl in nasepna mun-ah suahni pawi a bawl uh hiam?

records.english: We collect money for sick classmates.
records.zomi: Sang lawm cidam lo te adingin sum i kaikhawm uh hi.

records.english: At university, I joined other students from our community to help newcomers find housing.
records.zomi: University-ah, hong tung thak te in tenna inn a muh nadingin huh dingin i khuasung pan sangnaupang dang te tawh ka kihel hi.

records.english: My boss said that my habit of sharing information made the whole team stronger.
records.zomi: Thu theih te ka hawm zel ngeina in pawl khempeuh a hat zaw sak hi, ci-in ka makaipa in a gen hi.

records.english: Shall we visit our teacher while she is ill?
records.zomi: I sangsia nu a cidam loh lai-in i va kan ding hiam?

records.english: Loyalty to a team is valued in many cultures, though it is expressed in different ways.
records.zomi: Pawl tungah muanhuaina pen ngeina tampi-ah manpha-in kisim a, ahi zongin lampi kibang lo te-in a kilak hi.

records.english: I keep my promises at work.
records.zomi: Nasep-ah ka kamciam te ka kem hi.

records.english: When the factory cut hours, the workers agreed to share the remaining shifts so that nobody lost everything.
records.zomi: Factory in nasep hun a tan ciangin, kuamah in a khempeuh a mansuah loh nadingin nasemte in a om lai nasep hun te hawm dingin a kituak uh hi.

records.english: Values learned at home often shape how people behave at school and work.
records.zomi: Inn-a kisin manphatna te in mite sang leh nasep-ah bangci a gamtat uh hiam cih a bawl zel hi.

records.english: Respect for elders can help young employees learn from experienced colleagues.
records.zomi: Upa te zahtakna in nasem khangno te theihna nei nasep lawm te pan a sin nadingin a huh thei hi.

records.english: Schools that recognise pupils' home values can help them feel proud of where they come from.
records.zomi: Sangnaupang te' inn-a manphatna te a pahtawi sang te in amau' a kipatna mun tungah a kiliansak nadingin a huh thei hi.

records.english: I never take credit for other people's work.
records.zomi: Mi dang te' nasep tawh kipahtawi ngei ka hi kei hi.

records.english: At my first job in the city, I noticed that colleagues ate lunch alone at their desks.
records.zomi: Khuapi-a ka nasep masa pen-ah, nasep lawm te in a dawhkan uh-ah a khat bek-in sun an a ne uh hi, cih ka mu hi.

records.english: Remembering how meals were shared in my village, I started bringing extra food and inviting others to join me.
records.zomi: Ka khua-ah an bangci a kihawm hiam cih ka phawk ciangin, an behlap paipih in mi dang te hong kihel dingin ka sam kipan hi.

records.english: Within a few months, half the office was eating together every Friday.
records.zomi: Kha bangzah khat sung-in, office mi a lang zah in Laithai ni simin an khawm takin a ne uh hi.

records.english: When our team missed a deadline, I admitted my part in the mistake before anyone asked.
records.zomi: I pawl in hun ciang a mansuah ciangin, kuamah a dot ma-in khialhna-a ka khen ka pulak hi.

records.english: My colleague helped me on my first day.
records.zomi: Ka ni masa pen-in ka nasep lawm in hong huh hi.

records.english: My colleagues were surprised when I refused to accept a gift from a customer.
records.zomi: Van leitu khat pan letsong la ding ka nial ciangin ka nasep lawm te a lamdang sa uh hi.

records.english: Do you help new students at your school?
records.zomi: Na sang-ah sangnaupang thak te na huh hiam?

records.english: How do you explain your community's idea of sharing to colleagues who grew up differently?
records.zomi: Na khuasung' hawmna ngaihsutna pen tuam takin a khanglian nasep lawm te kiangah bangci na hilhcian hiam?

records.english: Why did you share your lunch with the new pupil?
records.zomi: Bang hangin sangnaupang thak tawh na sun an na hawm hiam?

records.english: He had forgotten his, and at home we always share food with anyone who is hungry.
records.zomi: Amah in a sun an a mangngilh a, inn-ah gilkial kuapeuh tawh an i hawm den uh hi.

records.english: Why did you turn down the promotion that would have meant leaving your team behind?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na pawl na nusiat ding a hih dinmun kahsakna na nial hiam?

records.english: In my family, we were raised to believe that success means little if it costs the people who supported you.
records.zomi: Ka innkuan-ah, lawhcinna in hong huh mite a mansuah sak leh a manpha kei hi, ci-in hong khankhia uh hi.

records.english: Do you share your food at school?
records.zomi: Sang-ah na an na hawm hiam?

records.english: At school, I was taught to listen to the oldest person in the room before giving my own opinion.
records.zomi: Sang-ah, keimah ngaihsutna ka gen ma-in inndan sung-a upa pen' thu ngai dingin hong sinsak uh hi.

records.english: My teacher encouraged me to write about the values I learned at home for the school magazine.
records.zomi: Ka sangsia in sang magazine adingin inn-a ka sin manphatna te tawh kisai gelh dingin hong hanthawn hi.

records.english: Could we organise a rota so that someone visits our sick colleague every week?
records.zomi: I nasep lawm cidam lo kal simin mi khat in a kan nadingin a kiheisa-a kanna ngimna khat i bawl thei ding hiam?

records.english: Many Christian parents describe inspiration to children as God working through human writers.
records.zomi: Khazih nu leh pa tampi in Pasian a humopna pen Pasian in mihing gelhmi te tungtawn-in a sepna ahi hi, ci-in naupang te kiangah a gen uh hi.

records.english: Is the Bible true, Dad?
records.zomi: Lai Siangtho a tak hiam, Pa?

records.english: Some Christians believe inspiration covers every word, while others stress the message and purpose of each book.
records.zomi: Khazih mi pawlkhat in Pasian a humopna in kammal khempeuh a huam hi, ci-in a um uh a, a dang te in laibu khat ciat' thu leh a ngimna a thupisak zaw uh hi.

records.english: Why does my father say that the letters of Paul are God's word as well as Paul's?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Paul' laikhak te pen Paul' thu bek hi lo-in Pasian thu zong ahi hi, ci-in ka pa in a gen hiam?

records.english: Why do Christians in our family disagree about how the Bible was inspired?
records.zomi: Bang hangin i innkuan-a Khazih mite in Lai Siangtho Pasian in bangci a humop hiam cih-ah a kituak kei uh hiam?

records.english: They all believe God guided Scripture, but they differ on whether that guidance extended to every detail or mainly to its message.
records.zomi: Amau khempeuh in Pasian in Lai Siangtho a makaih hi, ci-in a um uh a, ahi zongin tua makaihna in a neu khempeuh dong a tung hiam, a thu bek-ah a tung zaw hiam cih-ah a kibang kei uh hi.

records.english: Did the people who wrote the Bible know they were writing for us?
records.zomi: Lai Siangtho a gelh mite in eite adingin a gelh uh hi, cih a thei uh hiam?

records.english: Some probably didn't, but Christians believe God knew their words would reach people like us.
records.zomi: Pawlkhat in a thei kei kha ding uh a, ahi zongin Khazih mite in Pasian in a kammal uh eite bang mite kiang a tung ding hi, cih a thei hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: When my teenage son told me he no longer believed the Bible was inspired, I didn't know what to say.
records.zomi: Kum sawm leh tawm ka tapa in Lai Siangtho Pasian a humop hi, cih a um nawn kei hi, hong ci ciangin bang gen ding ka thei kei hi.

records.english: Instead of arguing, I asked him to read one Gospel with me and tell me honestly what he thought.
records.zomi: Kinial sangin, Lungdamna Thu khat keimah tawh sim dingin leh a ngaihsutna a tak takin hong gen dingin ka ngen hi.

records.english: We still don't agree on everything, but those evenings of reading together brought us closer.
records.zomi: Thu khempeuh-ah i kituak nai kei uh a, ahi zongin khawm taka laisimna tua nitak te in hong kinaisak zaw hi.

records.english: My mum explained what inspired means.
records.zomi: Ka nu in Pasian a humop cih' a khiatna hong hilhcian hi.

records.english: Could you explain to the children how Christians believe God guided the writers?
records.zomi: Pasian in gelhmi te bangci a makaih hiam cih Khazih mite' upna naupang te kiangah hilhcian thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Can I read the Bible by myself?
records.zomi: Lai Siangtho keimah bek-in ka sim thei ding hiam?

records.english: Children's questions about who wrote the Bible can lead to rich discussions about faith and history.
records.zomi: Lai Siangtho kua in a gelh hiam cih tawh kisai naupang te' dotna te in upna leh tangthu tawh kisai kikumna hau te-ah a tun thei hi.

records.english: My daughter wants to understand the Bible.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in Lai Siangtho theisiam a deih hi.

records.english: Christians hold a range of views on inspiration while sharing a belief that God speaks through Scripture.
records.zomi: Khazih mite in Pasian humopna tawh kisai ngaihsutna tuamtuam a nei uh a, ahi zongin Pasian in Lai Siangtho tungtawn-in thu a gen hi, cih upna a kibang uh hi.

records.english: Why do some Christians in our family believe every detail is guided while others focus on the message?
records.zomi: Bang hangin i innkuan-a Khazih mi pawlkhat in a neu khempeuh Pasian in a makaih hi, ci-in a um uh a, a dang te in a thu-ah a ngaihsut zaw uh hiam?

records.english: My uncle, who is a pastor, says that inspiration doesn't mean the writers stopped thinking for themselves.
records.zomi: Pastor ahi ka pa neu in Pasian a humopna in gelhmi te amau' ngaihsutna tawh a ngaihsut nawn lo uh hi, cih a hi kei hi, a ci hi.

records.english: We talk about the Bible at dinner.
records.zomi: Nitak an ne kawm-in Lai Siangtho tawh kisai i kikum uh hi.

records.english: For many believers, the Bible's inspiration explains why old texts still speak to new situations.
records.zomi: Um mi tampi adingin, Lai Siangtho Pasian a humopna in bang hangin lai lui te in thu thak te-ah thu a gen lai hiam cih a hilhcian hi.

records.english: Within one family, different views on inspiration can be held with respect and love.
records.zomi: Innkuan khat sungah, Pasian humopna tawh kisai ngaihsutna tuamtuam te zahtakna leh itna tawh kikem thei hi.

records.english: Many Christians believe the Holy Spirit who inspired Scripture also helps readers understand it.
records.zomi: Lai Siangtho a humop Kha Siangtho in a simmi te a theisiam nadingin zong a huh hi, ci-in Khazih mi tampi in a um uh hi.

records.english: My brother asked who chose the books.
records.zomi: Ka unau pa in laibu te kua in a teel hiam, ci-in a dong hi.

records.english: How can the Bible be inspired if it was written by ordinary people?
records.zomi: Mihing tangpi te in a gelh ahih leh Lai Siangtho Pasian in bangci a humop thei ding hiam?

records.english: Many Christians believe God worked through the writers' own personalities, memories and language rather than replacing them.
records.zomi: Pasian in gelhmi te' mimal omzia, phawkna leh pau te a laih sangin tua te tungtawn-in a sem hi, ci-in Khazih mi tampi in a um uh hi.

records.english: Did Paul know he was writing the Bible?
records.zomi: Paul in Lai Siangtho a gelh hi, cih a thei hiam?

records.english: Mum, did God write the Bible himself?
records.zomi: Nu, Pasian amah mahmah in Lai Siangtho a gelh hiam?

records.english: Christians believe God guided people to write it, so it is both God's word and their words.
records.zomi: Pasian in mite a gelh nadingin a makaih hi, ci-in Khazih mite in a um uh hi, tua ahih manin Pasian thu leh amau' kammal a nih in ahi hi.

records.english: Grandma's Bible has notes in the margins.
records.zomi: Pi' Lai Siangtho-ah a gei-ah ciamtehna te a om hi.

records.english: Was Moses one of the writers?
records.zomi: Moses pen gelhmi khat ahi hiam?

records.english: Why is the Bible special?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Lai Siangtho a tuam hiam?

records.english: How do you answer a child who asks why the Bible has different accounts of the same event?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Lai Siangtho-ah thu piang kibang tawh kisai genna tuamtuam a om hiam, ci-in a dong naupang khat bangci na dawng hiam?

records.english: Our family discussed whether a translation can carry the same authority as the original texts.
records.zomi: Lai let khat in a kipatna lai te' thuneihna kibang a nei thei hiam cih i innkuan in i kikum uh hi.

records.english: My grandmother told me that the Bible feels alive to her because she believes God still speaks through it.
records.zomi: Pasian in tua tungtawn-in thu a gen lai hi, ci-in a um ahih manin Lai Siangtho amah adingin a nungta bang a kizak hi, ci-in ka pi in hong gen hi.

records.english: Why does Grandpa say the Bible is different from other books?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pu in Lai Siangtho pen laibu dang te tawh a kibang kei hi, a ci hiam?

records.english: Because he believes God speaks through it in a way that he doesn't through other books.
records.zomi: Bang hang hiam cih leh Pasian in laibu dang te tungtawn-in a gen loh dan khat-in tua tungtawn-in thu a gen hi, ci-in a um hi.

records.english: Why are there four Gospels?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Lungdamna Thu li a om hiam?

records.english: My daughter was surprised to learn that some parts of the Bible were sung long before they were written down.
records.zomi: Lai Siangtho' khenkhat te a kigelh ma sawt-in a kisa ngei hi, cih a theih ciangin ka tanu a lamdang sa hi.

records.english: Is the Bible God's word?
records.zomi: Lai Siangtho pen Pasian thu ahi hiam?

records.english: Believing in inspiration does not prevent Christians from studying the history behind each book.
