records.zomi: Lai Siangtho in i maisak ding hi, a ci hiam?

records.english: Is it in the Bible, Mum?
records.zomi: Lai Siangtho-ah a om hiam, Nu?

records.english: Testing teachers against Scripture is a long tradition in many Christian churches.
records.zomi: Sinsakmi te Lai Siangtho tawh sin pen Khazih biakinn tampi-ah ngeina sau khat ahi hi.

records.english: How do Christian families decide what to do when the Bible doesn't speak directly about a situation?
records.zomi: Lai Siangtho in omzia khat tawh kisai a kingaih-in a gen kei ciangin Khazih innkuan te in bang bawl ding hiam cih bangci a khensat uh hiam?

records.english: Many look for principles in Scripture, pray together and ask advice from wise believers in their church.
records.zomi: Tampi in Lai Siangtho-ah thu kipna te a zong uh a, khawm takin thu a ngen uh a, a biakinn uh-a um mi pil te kiangah thuhilhna a ngen uh hi.

records.english: My parents say the Bible guides our home.
records.zomi: Lai Siangtho in i inn a makaih hi, ci-in ka nu leh pa in a gen uh hi.

records.english: Why do Christians say that a church leader's teaching must be tested against the Bible?
records.zomi: Bang hangin biakinn makai khat' sinsakna pen Lai Siangtho tawh kisin ding hi, ci-in Khazih mite in a gen uh hiam?

records.english: When my brother wanted to marry outside the church, my parents went to the Bible before they responded.
records.zomi: Ka unau pa in biakinn pua-a mi tawh kiten a deih ciangin, ka nu leh pa in a dawn ma-in Lai Siangtho a en uh hi.

records.english: Grandma trusts the Bible more than anything.
records.zomi: Pi in Lai Siangtho bangkim sangin a muang zaw hi.

records.english: We try to live the way the Bible teaches.
records.zomi: Lai Siangtho' sinsak bangin nungta dingin i hanciam uh hi.

records.english: What should I do if my friends say the Bible is just an old book?
records.zomi: Ka lawm te in Lai Siangtho pen laibu lui khat bek ahi hi, a ci uh leh bang ka bawl ding hiam?

records.english: Listen respectfully, explain why you trust it, and remember that faith isn't proved by winning arguments.
records.zomi: Zahtak takin ngai in la, bang hangin na muan hiam cih hilhcian in la, upna pen kinialna zawhna tawh a kilak hi lo hi, cih phawk in.

records.english: Grandma reads the Bible before breakfast.
records.zomi: Pi in zingsang an ma-in Lai Siangtho a sim hi.

records.english: Does the Bible tell us how to treat our grandparents?
records.zomi: Lai Siangtho in i pu leh pi te bangci i bawl ding hiam cih hong gen hiam?

records.english: Yes, it says to honour your father and mother, and many Christians apply that to grandparents too.
records.zomi: Gen hi, na nu leh pa zahtak in, a ci a, Khazih mi tampi in pu leh pi te tungah zong tua a zang uh hi.

records.english: My brother asked if the Bible is always right.
records.zomi: Lai Siangtho a dik den hiam, ci-in ka unau pa in a dong hi.

records.english: For many Christian families, Scripture is the final authority for faith and daily life.
records.zomi: Khazih innkuan tampi adingin, Lai Siangtho pen upna leh ni sim nuntakna adingin a tawp-a thuneihna ahi hi.

records.english: My grandmother taught me that when people disagree, Christians should go back to what Scripture says.
records.zomi: Mite a kituak kei ciangin, Khazih mite in Lai Siangtho in a gen bang-ah a ciah kik ding uh hi, ci-in ka pi in hong sinsak hi.

records.english: Our family Bible has a page where each generation wrote a verse that guided their lives.
records.zomi: I innkuan Lai Siangtho-ah khang khat ciat in a nuntakna uh a makaih cang khat a gelhna lai khat a om hi.

records.english: We read a verse before family meetings.
records.zomi: Innkuan kikhopna ma-in cang khat i sim uh hi.

records.english: Families who read the Bible together often find shared language for making decisions.
records.zomi: Lai Siangtho khawm taka a sim innkuan te in thukhensatna bawl nadingin kammal kibang a mu zel uh hi.

records.english: My parents always explained which of their rules came from the Bible and which were just family habits.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh pa in a thukham te-ah koi te Lai Siangtho pan a hong pai a, koi te innkuan ngeina bek ahi hiam cih a hilhcian den uh hi.

records.english: How do you explain to children that the Bible is authoritative but still needs careful reading?
records.zomi: Lai Siangtho in thuneihna a nei a, ahi zongin kidawm taka sim ding a kisam lai hi, cih naupang te kiangah bangci na hilhcian hiam?

records.english: When my son asked why we follow rules from such an old book, we talked about why Christians trust it.
records.zomi: Bang hangin tua bang laibu lui pan thukham te i zui hiam, ci-in ka tapa in a dot ciangin, bang hangin Khazih mite in a muang uh hiam cih i kikum uh hi.

records.english: Christians in the same family may apply biblical teaching differently while respecting its authority.
records.zomi: Innkuan kibang-a Khazih mite in a thuneihna zahtak kawm-in Lai Siangtho sinsakna te a kibang lo-in a zang thei uh hi.

records.english: Our parents pray and read the Bible together.
records.zomi: I nu leh pa in khawm takin thu a ngen uh a, Lai Siangtho a sim uh hi.

records.english: Our family learns a verse every week.
records.zomi: I innkuan in kal simin cang khat i sin uh hi.

records.english: When my parents disagreed about whether to move abroad, they decided to read the Bible together every evening for a month.
records.zomi: Gamdang-ah suan ding hiam cih-ah ka nu leh pa a kituak kei ciangin, kha khat sung nitak simin Lai Siangtho khawm taka sim dingin a khensat uh hi.

records.english: They didn't find a verse telling them what to do, but they found passages about trusting God and caring for strangers.
records.zomi: Bang bawl ding hiam cih a gen cang khat a mu kei uh a, ahi zongin Pasian muan leh zin mi te kem tawh kisai lai tang te a mu uh hi.

records.english: In the end, they moved, and my father still says those evenings gave them peace about the decision.
records.zomi: A tawp-in, a suan uh a, tua nitak te in thukhensatna tawh kisai nopna a pia hi, ci-in ka pa in a gen lai hi.

records.english: My children know that in our house the Bible matters more than anyone's opinion, including mine.
records.zomi: I inn-ah Lai Siangtho pen keimah' kihel-in kuapeuh' ngaihsutna sangin a thupi zaw hi, cih ka ta te in a thei uh hi.

records.english: For believers, the Bible's authority is felt most strongly when its teaching is hard to follow.
records.zomi: Um mite adingin, Lai Siangtho' thuneihna pen a sinsakna a zuih haksat ciangin a hat pen-in a kizak hi.

records.english: Accepting the Bible's authority does not remove the need for careful and humble interpretation.
records.zomi: Lai Siangtho' thuneihna san in kidawm leh kiniamkhiat taka a khiatna theisiam ding kisapna a la khia kei hi.

records.english: Many Christian parents try to show that their rules flow from Scripture rather than personal preference.
records.zomi: Khazih nu leh pa tampi in a thukham te uh mimal deihna pan hi lo-in Lai Siangtho pan a hong pai hi, cih lak dingin a hanciam uh hi.

records.english: Could we read what the Bible says about honesty before we talk to your teacher?
records.zomi: Na sangsia tawh i kikup ma-in thuman tawh kisai Lai Siangtho in bang a gen hiam cih i sim thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: Our family follows what the Bible teaches.
records.zomi: I innkuan in Lai Siangtho' sinsak bang a zui hi.

records.english: Why does Grandpa always say, "Let's see what the Bible says"?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pu in, Lai Siangtho in bang a gen hiam i en ding uh, ci-in a gen den hiam?

records.english: He believes the Bible has the final word on how Christians should live.
records.zomi: Khazih mite bangci a nuntak ding uh hiam cih tungah Lai Siangtho in a tawp-a thu a nei hi, ci-in a um hi.

records.english: The Bible helps our family decide things.
records.zomi: Lai Siangtho in i innkuan thu te i khensat nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Our family argued about the passage until my father suggested we ask our pastor what it meant.
records.zomi: Ka pa in i pastor kiangah a khiatna dot dingin a gen dong i innkuan in lai tang tawh kisai i kinial uh hi.

records.english: My sister wants to read the whole Bible.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu in Lai Siangtho a bup-in a sim nuam hi.

records.english: Children who see their parents submit to Scripture often take its authority more seriously.
records.zomi: A nu leh pa uh Lai Siangtho nuai-ah a kiniamkhiat a mu naupang te in a thuneihna a thupisak zaw zel uh hi.

records.english: Why do we obey the Bible?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Lai Siangtho i zui uh hiam?

records.english: Why do some Christian families read the same passage very differently?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Khazih innkuan pawlkhat in lai tang kibang a kibang lo mahmah-in a sim uh hiam?

records.english: Dad reads the Bible to us on Sundays.
records.zomi: Nipini-in Pa in Lai Siangtho hong sim sak hi.

records.english: Grandpa knows what the Bible says about money.
records.zomi: Pu in sum tawh kisai Lai Siangtho in bang a gen hiam cih a thei hi.

records.english: Can we look it up in the Bible?
records.zomi: Lai Siangtho-ah i zong thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: My wife and I decided how to raise our children by studying what the Bible says about families.
records.zomi: Kei leh ka zi in innkuan te tawh kisai Lai Siangtho in bang a gen hiam cih sin-in i ta te bangci i khawi ding uh hiam cih i khensat uh hi.

records.english: My grandfather refused to do business with anyone who cheated, because he said the Bible forbids it.
records.zomi: Lai Siangtho in a khak hi, a ci ahih manin, ka pu in a khem mi kuapeuh tawh sumbawl a nial hi.

records.english: Why do we check the Bible before making big decisions?
records.zomi: Bang hangin thukhensatna lian te i bawl ma-in Lai Siangtho i en uh hiam?

records.english: Because our family believes God guides us through it, so we want to listen first.
records.zomi: Bang hang hiam cih leh Pasian in tua tungtawn-in hong makaih hi, ci-in i innkuan in a um ahih manin, a masa-in ngai i deih uh hi.

records.english: We keep our family Bible on the shelf.
records.zomi: I innkuan Lai Siangtho shelf tung-ah i koih uh hi.

records.english: Dad says the Bible is God's word.
records.zomi: Lai Siangtho pen Pasian thu ahi hi, ci-in Pa in a gen hi.

records.english: Can the Bible help me with my friends?
records.zomi: Lai Siangtho in ka lawm te tawh kisai hong huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Are you sure it was that year?
records.zomi: Tua kum ahi hi, cih na thei kician hiam?

records.english: Was there a witness who saw the bridge collapse?
records.zomi: Lei a puk a mu theihpihtu khat a om hiam?

records.english: Can we check the church records?
records.zomi: Biakinn ciamtehna te i en thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: Historians compare several kinds of evidence before accepting a claim about the past.
records.zomi: Tangthu siam mite in nidang tawh kisai thu khat a san ma-in lahna tuamtuam a kikteh uh hi.

records.english: How can we tell whether this old coin is genuine or a copy?
records.zomi: Hih dangka lui a tak hiam, a kisuaktawm hiam cih bangci i thei thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: Why do you trust your aunt's memory more than the official records?
records.zomi: Bang hangin kumpi ciamtehna te sangin na ni' phawkna na muang zaw hiam?

records.english: When records and memories disagree, both may hold part of the truth.
records.zomi: Ciamtehna te leh phawkna te a kituak kei ciangin, a nih in thutak khen khat a nei kha thei hi.

records.english: How do you know Grandpa really met the president?
records.zomi: Pu in president a mu taktak hi, cih bangci na thei hiam?

records.english: There's a photograph of them shaking hands, and it's signed on the back.
records.zomi: Amau khut a kilen lim khat a om a, a nung lam-ah min a kigelh hi.

records.english: How do you know it was your grandfather?
records.zomi: Tua pen na pu ahi hi, cih bangci na thei hiam?

records.english: Old photographs, letters and records often provide the proof that memories cannot.
records.zomi: Lim lui te, laikhak te leh ciamtehna te in phawkna te in a piak theih loh lahna a pia zel uh hi.

records.english: How did historians prove that the village had been settled earlier than people thought?
records.zomi: Mite' ngaihsut sangin a ma zaw-in khua a kisat hi, cih tangthu siam mite in bangci a lak uh hiam?

records.english: They found pottery and tools buried under the old church that were several centuries older than its foundations.
records.zomi: Biakinn lui nuai-ah a kivui, a khuam kipatna sangin kum za tampi a lui zaw beel leh nasep van te a mu uh hi.

records.english: Could the old newspaper archive confirm the date of the fire?
records.zomi: Thuthak lai lui kemna in mei kanna ni a lak thei ding hiam?

records.english: What evidence did you find that your grandmother had been a teacher?
records.zomi: Na pi sangsia ahi ngei hi, cih lahna bang na mu hiam?

records.english: A class photograph from 1952 with her standing at the back, and a letter from a former pupil.
records.zomi: Kum 1952-a tanglai lim khat-ah a nung lam-ah a ding, leh a sangnaupang ngei khat' laikhak khat.

records.english: Is there a letter or a diary that shows what your father did during the war?
records.zomi: Galkapna lai-in na pa bang a bawl hiam cih a lak laikhak ahih kei leh ni sim ciamtehna lai khat a om hiam?

records.english: Physical objects such as tools and pottery can reveal how long people have lived in a place.
records.zomi: Nasep van leh beel bang van taktak te in mite mun khat-ah hun bangzah a teeng uh hiam cih a lak thei hi.

records.english: Can anyone else remember it?
records.zomi: Mi dang khat peuhpeuh in a phawk thei hiam?

records.english: Could the shipping company's records confirm Grandpa's account of the shipwreck?
records.zomi: Tuipi long kipukna tawh kisai Pu' genna pen long company' ciamtehna te in a lak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Can you show me the letter?
records.zomi: Laikhak hong lak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Is there proof he was a soldier?
records.zomi: Galkap ahi hi, cih lahna a om hiam?

records.english: Asking for evidence about family stories can confirm some memories and correct others.
records.zomi: Innkuan tangthu te tawh kisai lahna ngen in phawkna pawlkhat a lak a, a dang te a bawlphat thei hi.

records.english: Evidence from the past is often incomplete, so conclusions should be held with some caution.
records.zomi: Nidang pan lahna te a kicing lo zel ahih manin, a tawp-a thu te kidawm neu takin kem ding hi.

records.english: Many family legends grow larger with each telling, so evidence helps keep them honest.
records.zomi: Innkuan tangthu minthang tampi a kigen kik ciang khempeuh-in a lian semsem ahih manin, lahna in a taktak-in a kemcing hi.

records.english: What would convince you that the famous painter really stayed in our town?
records.zomi: Lim suai siam minthang in i khuapi-ah a om taktak hi, cih bang in hong umsak ding hiam?

records.english: Did you read that story somewhere, or did a relative tell you?
records.zomi: Tua tangthu mun khat-ah na sim hiam, sanggam khat in hong gen hiam?

records.english: Who told you about it?
records.zomi: Tua tawh kisai kua in hong gen hiam?

records.english: Can you prove it was your house?
records.zomi: Tua pen na inn ahi hi, cih na lak thei hiam?

records.english: Archives, registers and newspapers can answer questions that families have argued about for years.
records.zomi: Ciamtehna kemna, min gelhna laibu leh thuthak lai te in innkuan te in kum tampi sung a kinialna dotna te a dawng thei hi.

records.english: Finding proof of a relative's story can bring great joy to the whole family.
records.zomi: Sanggam khat' tangthu' lahna muh in innkuan khempeuh adingin lungdamna lian a pia thei hi.

records.english: Was it in the newspaper?
records.zomi: Thuthak lai-ah a om hiam?

records.english: Preserving documents and photographs today provides evidence for the questions of future generations.
records.zomi: Tuni-in lai te leh lim te kem in khang hong tung ding te' dotna te adingin lahna a pia hi.

records.english: How do you know your great-grandmother came from the mountains and not the coast?
records.zomi: Na pi upa pen mual tung pan hong pai a, tuipi gei pan hi lo hi, cih bangci na thei hiam?

records.english: How did the museum know which family the old wedding dress belonged to?
records.zomi: Mopawi puan lui pen koi innkuan' ahi hiam cih museum in bangci a thei hiam?

records.english: Is that the original photo?
records.zomi: Tua pen a kipatna photo ahi hiam?

records.english: Did anyone write it down?
records.zomi: Kuamah in a gelh hiam?

records.english: Learning to ask how we know something about the past is an important part of thinking clearly.
records.zomi: Nidang tawh kisai thu khat bangci i thei hiam cih dot sin pen kician taka ngaihsutna-a khen thupi khat ahi hi.

records.english: Could we compare the photo with the old map to see where the house stood?
records.zomi: Inn a dinna mun muh nadingin photo leh gam lim lui i kikteh thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: Did Grandma keep any letters?
records.zomi: Pi in laikhak khat peuhpeuh a kem hiam?

records.english: How do you know the date?
records.zomi: Ni bangci na thei hiam?

records.english: How did you discover that the old house was once a school?
records.zomi: Inn lui pen nidang-in sang ahi ngei hi, cih bangci na thei khia hiam?

records.english: Did the church register the wedding?
records.zomi: Biakinn in mopawi a ciamteh hiam?

records.english: Where is the old certificate?
records.zomi: Lai lui pen koi-ah a om hiam?

records.english: Did anyone take photographs of the school on the day it opened?
records.zomi: Sang a kihon ni-in kuamah in sang' lim a la hiam?

records.english: Is there any record of our family in the old village register?
records.zomi: Khua lui min gelhna laibu-ah i innkuan' ciamtehna khat peuhpeuh a om hiam?

records.english: Did you keep the ticket?
records.zomi: Ticket na kem hiam?

records.english: Is that really what happened?
records.zomi: Tua pen a taktak-in a piang bang ahi hiam?

records.english: Did your parents keep anything that proves they lived in the capital before you were born?
records.zomi: Nang na suah ma-in gam khuapi lian-ah a teeng uh hi, cih a lak khat peuhpeuh na nu leh pa in a kem uh hiam?

records.english: Do you have a photo of it?
records.zomi: Tua' lim na nei hiam?

records.english: My uncle always claimed that he had once won a national cycling race as a teenager.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in kum sawm leh tawm a hih lai-in gam sung siiksakol tai kidemna khat a zo ngei hi, ci-in a gen den hi.

records.english: Nobody believed him until my cousin found a yellowed newspaper cutting in the attic with his photo on the front page.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam in inn tung lam-ah a ma lam-ah a lim a om thuthak lai tan lui mahmah khat a muh dong kuamah in amah a um kei uh hi.

records.english: Now the cutting hangs in a frame in the hall, and he points to it whenever anyone doubts his stories.
records.zomi: Tu-in thuthak lai tan pen inn kongpi kiang-ah bawm tawh a kikhai a, kuapeuh in a tangthu te a lungmuan loh ciangin amah in a lak hi.

records.english: Was anyone else with you that day?
records.zomi: Tua ni-in mi dang khat peuhpeuh nang tawh a om hiam?

records.english: Is there any proof that our family once owned the mill?
records.zomi: I innkuan in nidang-in tui khawl a nei ngei hi, cih lahna khat peuhpeuh a om hiam?

records.english: Yes, the old deed is kept in the town archive with your great-grandfather's name on it.
records.zomi: Om hi, na pu upa pen' min a om lei lai lui pen khuapi ciamtehna kemna-ah a kikem hi.

records.english: How can you be sure the old bridge was built in 1890?
records.zomi: Lei lui pen kum 1890-in a kilam hi, cih bangci na thei kician hiam?

records.english: The date is carved into the stone at the end, and the council records agree.
records.zomi: A tawp-a suang tung-ah kum a kigelh a, council ciamtehna te zong a kituak hi.

records.english: What evidence is there that the market has been held in the same square for centuries?
records.zomi: Zuakna mun pen kum za tampi sung mun kibang-ah a kibawl hi, cih lahna bang a om hiam?

records.english: Asking politely for proof shows interest in a story rather than doubt about the teller.
records.zomi: Zahtak taka lahna ngen in genmi tungah lungmuanlohna hi lo-in tangthu tungah deihna a lak hi.

records.english: Free advice services help people use rights that would otherwise remain on paper.
records.zomi: Man om lo thuhilhna nasep te in lai tung-ah bek a om ding thuneihna te mite a zat nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Can I appeal the decision?
records.zomi: Thukhensatna ka dot kik thei ding hiam?

records.english: The advice centre explained that I had the right to see the notes the social worker had written.
records.zomi: Mipi kemna nasem in a gelh te en dingin thuneihna ka nei hi, ci-in thuhilhna mun in a hilhcian hi.

records.english: Ombudsmen and review panels give people a route when ordinary complaints fail.
records.zomi: Ngaihsutna gen mite leh enkikna pawl te in phunna tangpi a lawhsap ciangin mite adingin lampi a pia uh hi.

records.english: Who checks the council's decisions?
records.zomi: Council' thukhensatna te kua in a en hiam?

records.english: Can they stop my benefits?
records.zomi: Ka kumpi huhna te a tan thei uh hiam?

records.english: Can I see my file?
records.zomi: Ka file ka en thei ding hiam?

records.english: The citizens' advice volunteers helped my grandfather claim the pension he had been missing for years.
records.zomi: Gam mi thuhilhna thalawp te in ka pu kum tampi sung a mansuah pension a nget nadingin a huh uh hi.

records.english: When the council cut my mother's home care without explanation, she thought nothing could be done.
records.zomi: Council in hilhcianna om lo-in ka nu' inn-a kemna a tan ciangin, bangmah bawl theih a om kei hi, ci-in a ngaihsun hi.

records.english: An adviser at the community centre explained that she had the right to a review and helped her request one in writing.
records.zomi: Khuasung inn lian-a thuhilhmi khat in en kik ding a ngen thei thuneihna a nei hi, ci-in a hilhcian a, lai tawh a nget nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Within a month, the care was restored, and she now tells other neighbours about the service.
records.zomi: Kha khat sung-in, kemna a kipia kik a, tu-in a inn kiang mi dang te kiangah tua nasep tawh kisai a gen hi.

records.english: Do tenants in council flats have the same rights as those who rent privately?
records.zomi: Council inn-a teng mite in mimal inn luak mite' thuneihna kibang a nei uh hiam?

records.english: Why didn't anyone tell me that I was entitled to help with my heating bills?
records.zomi: Ka inn lumsakna man adingin huhna ngah thei ka hi hi, cih bang hangin kuamah in hong gen kei hiam?

records.english: How can I find out which public services I have a right to as a new resident?
records.zomi: Teng thak khat ka hih manin ka ngah thei mipi nasep te koi te ahi hiam cih bangci ka thei khia thei ding hiam?

records.english: Can they share my information?
records.zomi: Ka thu te a hawm thei uh hiam?

records.english: Knowing one's rights makes it easier to deal with public services confidently.
records.zomi: Mimal thuneihna theih in mipi nasep te tawh hang takin kisai nading a baih zaw sak hi.

records.english: Can the library ask for my identity card before I join?
records.zomi: Ka kihel ma-in laibu inn in ka mimal lai a ngen thei hiam?

records.english: It can ask for proof of address, but in our town you don't need an identity card.
records.zomi: Na tenna lahna a ngen thei hi, ahi zongin i khuapi-ah mimal lai na kisam kei hi.

records.english: After the hospital lost my test results, the patient advice service helped me make a formal complaint.
records.zomi: Damlo inn in ka sittelna gah te a mansuah khit-in, damlo thuhilhna nasep in phunna kician khat ka bawl nadingin hong huh hi.

records.english: People are more likely to claim their rights when information is simple and easy to find.

records.zomi: I biakinn in sangnaupang te nasep a muh nadingin a huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Does your cousin study in another country?
records.zomi: Na sanggam gam dang khat-ah sang a kah hiam?

records.english: My uncle, who works as an engineer abroad, sends us books for our studies.
records.zomi: Gamdang-ah engineer-in nasep a sem ka pa neu in i sinna adingin laibu te hong khak hi.

records.english: Is there a Zomi student club at your college?
records.zomi: Na college-ah Zomi sangnaupang pawl khat a om hiam?

records.english: We study together after church.
records.zomi: Biakinn khit-in i sin khawm uh hi.

records.english: Weekend schools help children abroad keep their language while succeeding in local schools.
records.zomi: Kal tawp sang te in gamdang-a naupang te khuasung sang te-ah a lawhcin kawm-in a pau uh a kem nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: The community helps newcomers with forms.
records.zomi: Khuasung in hong tung thak te lai lak-ah a huh hi.

records.english: Professionals from the community can inspire young people to aim for new careers.
records.zomi: Khuasung pan siam mi te in khangno te nasep thak te ngim dingin a hanthawn thei uh hi.

records.english: Do your children's teachers know about our culture?
records.zomi: Na ta te' sangsia te in i ngeina tawh kisai a thei uh hiam?

records.english: A little, and the school asked us to talk to the class about our festivals.
records.zomi: Neu khat, sang in i pawi te tawh kisai tanglai kiangah gen dingin hong ngen uh hi.

records.english: My brother pays for our sister's school fees from abroad.
records.zomi: Ka unau pa in gamdang pan i sanggam nu' sangkah man a pia hi.

records.english: How do Zomi students abroad balance their studies with helping their families back home?
records.zomi: Gamdang-a Zomi sangnaupang te in a sinna uh leh inn lam-a a innkuan uh huhna bangci a kibang-in a kem uh hiam?

records.english: Balancing studies abroad with responsibilities at home can be a heavy burden for young people.
records.zomi: Gamdang-a sinna leh inn lam-a mawhpuakna te kibang-in kem pen khangno te adingin puak gik khat a suak thei hi.

records.english: My sister met other Zomi nurses at a conference and now they share advice online.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu in kikhopna lian khat-ah Zomi nurse dang te a mu a, tu-in online-ah thuhilhna a kihawm uh hi.

records.english: Students who share their culture at school help classmates understand their background.
records.zomi: Sang-ah a ngeina uh a hawm sangnaupang te in a sang lawm te in a kipatna uh a theisiam nadingin a huh uh hi.

records.english: How do Zomi students abroad help each other with their studies?
records.zomi: Gamdang-a Zomi sangnaupang te in a sinna uh-ah khat leh khat bangci a kihuh uh hiam?

records.english: The older students share notes, explain how the university works and help newcomers find part-time jobs.
records.zomi: Sangnaupang upa zaw te in a gelh te uh a hawm uh a, university bangci a sem hiam cih a hilhcian uh a, hong tung thak te nasep neu a muh nadingin a huh uh hi.

records.english: The Zomi teachers in our city organise extra lessons for children who are new to the country.
records.zomi: I khuapi-a Zomi sangsia te in gam-ah a thak naupang te adingin sinna belap te a bawl uh hi.

records.english: How did you find your job abroad?
records.zomi: Gamdang-ah na nasep bangci na mu hiam?

records.english: My cousin worked at the same company and told me when they needed new staff.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam company kibang-ah nasep a sem a, nasem thak a kisap uh ciangin hong gen hi.

records.english: My sister teaches our language at weekends.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu in kal tawp-in i pau a hilh hi.

records.english: Can the community help me find work?
records.zomi: Khuasung in nasep ka muh nadingin hong huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Why did the Zomi workers in your city start their own association?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na khuapi-a Zomi nasemte in amau' pawl a kipatsak uh hiam?

records.english: Many of them were new to the country and needed help understanding contracts, rights and services in a language they knew well.
records.zomi: Amau tampi in gam-ah a thak uh a, a theih hoih uh pau-in kithukimna lai, thuneihna leh nasep te theisiam dingin huhna a kisam uh hi.

records.english: Community associations can explain workplace rights to people who are new to a country.
records.zomi: Khuasung pawl te in gam khat-ah a thak mite kiangah nasepna mun-a thuneihna te a hilhcian thei uh hi.

records.english: Did you meet other Zomi students at university?
records.zomi: University-ah Zomi sangnaupang dang te na mu hiam?

records.english: The association has a job notice board.
records.zomi: Pawl in nasep thugenna laimal khaina khat a nei hi.

records.english: Many families abroad combine hard work with a strong commitment to their children's education.
records.zomi: Gamdang-a innkuan tampi in hanciam taka nasep leh a ta te uh sinna tungah lungsim kip a gawm uh hi.

records.english: My friend works at a Zomi restaurant.
records.zomi: Ka lawm Zomi an zuakna inn khat-ah nasep a sem hi.

records.english: At work, my colleagues were curious when I explained why I take a day off for our national festival.
records.zomi: Nasep-ah, i gam pawi adingin bang hangin ni khat tawlngak ka la hiam cih ka hilhcian ciangin ka nasep lawm te in a theih a deih uh hi.

records.english: Our teacher asked about our festivals.
records.zomi: I sangsia in i pawi te tawh kisai a dong hi.

records.english: Our church abroad invites professionals to talk to young people about different careers.
records.zomi: Gamdang-a i biakinn in khangno te kiangah nasep tuamtuam tawh kisai gen dingin siam mi te a sam hi.

records.english: Is there anyone from our community at your new university?
records.zomi: Na university thak-ah i khuasung pan kuamah a om hiam?

records.english: Yes, a small group of Zomi students meets every Friday in the student café.
records.zomi: Om hi, Zomi sangnaupang pawl neu khat sangnaupang cafe-ah Laithai ni simin a kimu uh hi.

records.english: When I arrived at university abroad, the Zomi student group met me at the airport.
records.zomi: Gamdang-a university-ah ka tun ciangin, Zomi sangnaupang pawl in vanlengtual-ah hong dawn uh hi.

records.english: Helping newcomers with applications and interviews strengthens the whole community.
records.zomi: Hong tung thak te ngetna lai leh kidotna te-ah huh in khuasung khempeuh a hat sak hi.

records.english: My mother taught me to read the hard passages slowly and to admit when I don't understand them.
records.zomi: Ka nu in lai tang haksa te zawi takin sim dingin leh ka theisiam loh ciangin pulak dingin hong sinsak hi.

records.english: Dad uses a study Bible with notes.
records.zomi: Pa in ciamtehna nei sinna Lai Siangtho khat a zang hi.

records.english: How do you decide what a difficult passage means?
records.zomi: Lai tang haksa khat' khiatna bangci na khensat hiam?

records.english: I ask what it meant to the first readers, compare it with other passages and pray for understanding.
records.zomi: A masa simmi te adingin bang a gen hiam cih ka dong a, lai tang dang te tawh ka kikteh a, theisiamna adingin thu ka ngen hi.

records.english: Humility in interpretation allows family members to disagree without losing respect for each other.
records.zomi: Khiatna theisiam-ah kiniamkhiatna in innkuan mite khat leh khat zahtakna mansuah lo-in a kituak lo thei nadingin a phal hi.

records.english: Is the story of Jonah and the big fish true?
records.zomi: Jonah leh nga lian tangthu a tak hiam?

records.english: Christians read it in different ways, but they all agree it teaches that God's mercy reaches everyone.
records.zomi: Khazih mite in lam tuamtuam-in a sim uh a, ahi zongin Pasian' hehpihna in mi khempeuh a tung hi, cih a sinsak hi, ci-in a khempeuh in a kituak uh hi.

records.english: Can a story teach us without being history?
records.zomi: Tangthu khat tangthu taktak hi lo-in hong sinsak thei hiam?

records.english: Children's questions about Bible stories often lead families into deeper study.
records.zomi: Lai Siangtho tangthu te tawh kisai naupang te' dotna te in innkuan te sinna thuk zaw-ah a paipih zel hi.

records.english: Many Christians believe that Scripture is best interpreted in the light of Jesus' life and teaching.
records.zomi: Lai Siangtho pen Jesu' nuntakna leh a sinsakna vak tawh a khiatna theisiam a hoih pen hi, ci-in Khazih mi tampi in a um uh hi.

records.english: We look up hard words together.
records.zomi: Kammal haksa te i zong khawm uh hi.

records.english: Why do people read the same verse differently?
records.zomi: Bang hangin mite in cang kibang a kibang lo-in a sim uh hiam?

records.english: My teenage daughter challenged me when I quoted a single verse without explaining its context.
records.zomi: A kiim-a thu hilhcian lo-in cang khat bek ka gen ciangin kum sawm leh tawm ka tanu in hong langdo hi.

records.english: We pray before we try to understand a passage.
records.zomi: Lai tang khat theisiam dingin i hanciam ma-in thu i ngen uh hi.

records.english: Why are some parts of the Bible poems?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Lai Siangtho' khenkhat te pen late ahi hiam?

records.english: My grandfather always reminded us that the Old Testament laws were given to a particular people at a particular time.
records.zomi: Thuciamna Lui thukham te pen hun khat-ah mi pawl khat kiangah a kipia ahi hi, ci-in ka pu in hong phawksak den hi.

records.english: Our family keeps a list of questions about difficult passages to discuss with older believers.
records.zomi: I innkuan in um mi upa zaw te tawh kikum dingin lai tang haksa te tawh kisai dotna lista khat a kem hi.

records.english: When my son asked why the Bible has two creation accounts, we read them side by side.
records.zomi: Bang hangin Lai Siangtho-ah piansakna genna nih a om hiam, ci-in ka tapa in a dot ciangin, a kiang leh kiang-in i sim uh hi.

records.english: Dad, why does the Bible say God is a shepherd?
records.zomi: Pa, bang hangin Lai Siangtho in Pasian pen tuucing ahi hi, a ci hiam?

records.english: It's a picture to show that God cares for people the way a shepherd cares for his sheep.
records.zomi: Tuucing khat in a tuu te a kep bangin Pasian in mite a kem hi, cih lak nading lim khat ahi hi.

records.english: Commentaries and study Bibles help families understand the historical background of a passage.
records.zomi: Hilhcianna laibu te leh sinna Lai Siangtho te in innkuan te lai tang khat' nuai-a tangthu a theisiam nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Why does Grandma read the verses before and after the one we're talking about?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pi in i kikup cang' a ma leh a nung-a cang te a sim hiam?

records.english: She says a verse can only be understood properly when you know what surrounds it.
records.zomi: Cang khat pen a kiim-a om bang na theih ciang bek-in a dik takin kitheisiam thei hi, a ci hi.

records.english: My brother wants to understand the prophets.
records.zomi: Ka unau pa in Pasian kamsangte theisiam a deih hi.

records.english: Our family Bible study compares the same story in two Gospels to see what each writer emphasises.
records.zomi: I innkuan Lai Siangtho sinna in gelhmi khat ciat in bang a thupisak hiam cih muh nadingin Lungdamna Thu nih-a tangthu kibang a kikteh hi.

records.english: Grandpa says the Bible explains itself.
records.zomi: Lai Siangtho in amah le amah a kihilhcian hi, ci-in Pu in a gen hi.

records.english: How do you explain to children that some Bible stories are meant to be read as pictures?
records.zomi: Lai Siangtho tangthu pawlkhat pen lim bangin sim ding ahi hi, cih naupang te kiangah bangci na hilhcian hiam?

records.english: My wife reads the Bible with a map so that the children can see where each story happened.
records.zomi: Tangthu khat ciat koi-ah a piang hiam cih naupang te in a muh theih nadingin ka zi in gam lim tawh Lai Siangtho a sim hi.

records.english: Grandpa explains the hard verses to us.
records.zomi: Pu in cang haksa te hong hilhcian hi.

records.english: Paying attention to context helps believers avoid misusing single verses.
records.zomi: A kiim-a thu tungah lim kep in um mite cang khat bek a zat khial loh nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Different traditions within Christianity may interpret the same passage in different ways.
records.zomi: Khazih upna sung-a ngeina tuamtuam te in lai tang kibang lam tuamtuam-in a khiatna a theisiam thei uh hi.

records.english: Why do many Christians say that Jesus is the key to understanding the whole Bible?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Khazih mi tampi in Jesu pen Lai Siangtho bup theisiam nading-a a thupi pen ahi hi, a ci uh hiam?

records.english: Is this story a parable, Mum?
records.zomi: Hih tangthu pen thugentehna ahi hiam, Nu?

records.english: Does this rule still apply today?
records.zomi: Hih thukham tu-in a kizang lai hiam?

records.english: Do your children know the difference between a parable, a psalm and a letter in the Bible?
records.zomi: Na ta te in Lai Siangtho-a thugentehna, Late leh laikhak te kikal-a kibatlohna a thei uh hiam?

records.english: My father taught us to ask who wrote each book and why before deciding what it means for us.
records.zomi: Ka pa in eite adingin bang a gen hiam cih i khensat ma-in laibu khat ciat kua in a gelh a, bang hangin a gelh hiam cih dong dingin hong sinsak hi.

records.english: When my daughter asked whether the parable of the lost son was a true story, I wasn't sure how to answer.
records.zomi: Tapa mang thugentehna pen tangthu taktak ahi hiam, ci-in ka tanu in a dot ciangin, bangci dawng ding hiam cih ka thei kician kei hi.

records.english: My mother explained that Jesus told it as a parable, a story meant to teach something deeper about God's love.
records.zomi: Jesu in Pasian' itna tawh kisai thuk zaw khat sinsak nading tangthu, thugentehna khat bangin a gen hi, ci-in ka nu in a hilhcian hi.

records.english: Now my daughter asks whether every new story she reads in the Bible is a parable or a history.
records.zomi: Tu-in ka tanu in Lai Siangtho-ah a sim tangthu thak khempeuh thugentehna ahi hiam, tangthu taktak ahi hiam, ci-in a dong hi.

records.english: Mum says to read the verses around it.
records.zomi: A kiim-a cang te sim in, ci-in Nu in a gen hi.

records.english: After reading the letters of Paul together, my son understood that they were written to real churches with real problems.
records.zomi: Paul' laikhak te i sim khawm khit-in, buaina taktak nei biakinn taktak te kiangah a kigelh ahi hi, cih ka tapa in a theisiam hi.

records.english: Recognising different kinds of writing in the Bible shapes how Christians interpret them.
records.zomi: Lai Siangtho-a gelhna tuamtuam te theih in Khazih mite in a khiatna bangci a theisiam uh hiam cih a bawl hi.

records.english: For many believers, interpreting Scripture is a shared journey rather than a solitary task.
records.zomi: Um mi tampi adingin, Lai Siangtho khiatna theisiam pen nasep khat bek-in sem ding sangin khawm taka khualzinna khat ahi hi.

records.english: Our family asks what the passage meant then.
records.zomi: I innkuan in tua hun lai-in lai tang in bang a gen hiam cih a dong hi.

records.english: Could we look at what the commentary says about this passage before we argue about it?
records.zomi: I kinial ma-in hih lai tang tawh kisai hilhcianna laibu in bang a gen hiam cih i en thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: Which church received this letter first?
records.zomi: Hih laikhak a masa-in koi biakinn in a ngah hiam?

records.english: Mum keeps a notebook of our questions.
records.zomi: Nu in i dotna te' ciamtehna laibu khat a kem hi.

records.english: Our family reads the whole chapter together.
records.zomi: I innkuan in a khen bup i sim khawm uh hi.

records.english: What did Jesus mean by that?
records.zomi: Tua tawh Jesu in bang a gen nopna hiam?

records.english: My sister asks lots of questions about the Bible.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu in Lai Siangtho tawh kisai dotna tampi a dong hi.

records.english: We talk about the Bible after church.
records.zomi: Biakinn khit-in Lai Siangtho tawh kisai i kikum uh hi.

records.english: Christian families often learn interpretation by reading passages together and asking questions.
records.zomi: Khazih innkuan te in lai tang te khawm taka sim-in leh dotna dong-in khiatna theisiam dan a sin zel uh hi.

records.english: Grandma compares different translations.
records.zomi: Pi in lai let tuamtuam te a kikteh hi.

records.english: Why do Christians in our own family sometimes interpret the same passage differently?
records.zomi: Bang hangin i innkuan sung-a Khazih mite in hun khenkhat-in lai tang kibang a kibang lo-in a khiatna a theisiam uh hiam?

records.english: They bring different experiences and traditions to their reading, though they share the same trust in Scripture.
records.zomi: A simna uh-ah omzia leh ngeina kibang lo te a paipih uh a, ahi zongin Lai Siangtho tungah muanna kibang a nei uh hi.

records.english: Why do some Christians in our family read Revelation as symbols and others as predictions?
records.zomi: Bang hangin i innkuan-a Khazih mi pawlkhat in Mangmuhna Lai pen lim bangin a sim uh a, a dang te in a piang ding thu bangin a sim uh hiam?

records.english: My grandmother says that poetry in the Bible should be read with the heart as well as the mind.
records.zomi: Lai Siangtho-a late te pen ngaihsutna bek tawh hi lo-in lungsim tawh zong sim ding hi, ci-in ka pi in a gen hi.

records.english: Asking what a passage meant to its first readers is an important step in interpreting it today.
records.zomi: Lai tang khat in a masa simmi te adingin bang a gen hiam cih dot pen tu-in a khiatna theisiam nading-ah khebai thupi khat ahi hi.

records.english: Is this verse about us too?
records.zomi: Hih cang in eite tawh kisai zong a gen hiam?

records.english: When my husband and I disagreed about a passage, we asked our pastor for help understanding it.
records.zomi: Kei leh ka pasal lai tang khat tawh kisai i kituak kei ciangin, a theisiam nadingin huh dingin i pastor i ngen uh hi.

records.english: When nothing was available, families often relied on neighbours and relatives instead of services.
records.zomi: Bangmah a om kei ciangin, innkuan te in nasep te sangin inn kiang mite leh sanggam te a kinga zel uh hi.

records.english: Was the village hall free for your sister's engagement party?
records.zomi: Na sanggam nu' kiteng ding kipahna pawi adingin khua inndan lian a awng hiam?

records.english: Recording such memories preserves an understanding of how ordinary life used to work.
records.zomi: Tua bang phawkna te ciamteh in nidang-in nuntakna tangpi bangci a om hiam cih theisiamna a kemcing hi.

records.english: Were there teachers available for the new school when it first opened?
records.zomi: Sang thak a kihon masak lai-in sangsia te a om uh hiam?

records.english: Was the old doctor still seeing patients when you were a child?
records.zomi: Na naupan lai-in siavuan lui in damlo te a en lai hiam?

records.english: Did the factory have any jobs left when you arrived from the countryside?
records.zomi: Khuaneu pan na tun ciangin factory-ah nasep a om lai hiam?

records.english: Was the bus full that morning?
records.zomi: Tua zingsang-in bus a dim hiam?

records.english: Stories about waiting for a place or a seat often show how patient earlier generations had to be.
records.zomi: Mun ahih kei leh tutna khat ngakna tawh kisai tangthu te in khang masa te bangzah thuakzawh ding a kisam hiam cih a lak zel hi.

records.english: Was the church free on the day you wanted to get married?
records.zomi: Na kiten nuam ni-in biakinn a awng hiam?

records.english: No, it was booked, so we married on a Tuesday instead.
records.zomi: Awng kei hi, kingetsak khin ahih manin Pithai ni-in i kiten uh hi.

records.english: Were there places on the evening course when you decided to study again?
records.zomi: Sin kik dingin na khensat ciangin nitak sinna-ah mun a om hiam?

records.english: Was anyone at home to help?
records.zomi: Huh dingin inn-ah kuamah a om hiam?

records.english: Were your cousins free to visit?
records.zomi: Na sanggam te a hong kan thei uh hiam?

records.english: Did the church have a spare room where the travellers could sleep?
records.zomi: Khualzin mite a ihmut nadingin biakinn in inndan awng khat a nei hiam?

records.english: Was there room on the boat when your family left the island?
records.zomi: Na innkuan in tuikulh a nusiat uh ciangin long tung-ah mun a om hiam?

records.english: Only just, and my father had to stand for the whole journey.
records.zomi: A kicing dek tak hi, ka pa in khualzinna khempeuh sung a din ding a kisam hi.

records.english: Was the hall booked that weekend?
records.zomi: Tua kal tawp-in inndan lian a kingetsak khin hiam?

records.english: Was the ferry running that week?
records.zomi: Tua kal-in luipi tan long a pai hiam?

records.english: Did the shop have any shoes in your size?
records.zomi: Zuakna inn-ah na lianzah khedap a om hiam?

records.english: Comparing past and present availability helps communities see what still needs to improve.
records.zomi: Nidang leh tu-a ngah theihna kikteh in khuasung te in bang hoih zaw sak ding a kisam lai hiam cih a muh nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Answers about availability in the past can reveal inequalities between towns and villages.
records.zomi: Nidang-a ngah theihna tawh kisai dawnna te in khuapi te leh khuaneu te kikal-a kibatlohna te a lak thei hi.

records.english: Were any of your relatives free to look after you while your parents worked?
records.zomi: Na nu leh pa nasep a sep lai-un nang hong kem dingin na sanggam te lak-ah kuamah a awng hiam?

records.english: When my parents wanted to rent their first flat, every landlord in town told them nothing was available.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh pa in a inn masa pen uh luak a deih uh ciangin, khuapi-a inn neipa khempeuh in bangmah a om kei hi, a ci uh hi.

records.english: My grandmother heard that an old teacher was moving in with her daughter and went to ask whether her rooms would be free.
records.zomi: Sangsia lui nu khat a tanu tawh om dingin a suan hi, cih ka pi in a za a, a inndan te a awng ding hiam cih dot dingin a pai hi.

records.english: My parents moved in a week later and stayed in that flat for twenty years.
records.zomi: Kal khat khit-in ka nu leh pa a lut uh a, tua inn-ah kum sawm nih sung a teeng uh hi.

records.english: Were there tickets left for the concert?
records.zomi: La sakna adingin ticket a om lai hiam?

records.english: Did any of the shops still have flour during the hard winter?
records.zomi: Khuaphal haksa lai-in zuakna inn khatpeuh-ah flour a om lai hiam?

records.english: Older people often remember the kindness of those who made room for them when nothing seemed free.
records.zomi: Bangmah a awng bang a kilat loh lai-in amau adingin mun a bawl mite' hehpihna upa te in a phawk zel uh hi.

records.english: Were there any seats on the train?
records.zomi: Meileng tung-ah tutna a om hiam?

records.english: Questions about whether help was available invite elders to talk about community support.
records.zomi: Huhna a om hiam cih tawh kisai dotna te in upa te khuasung huhna tawh kisai a gen dingin a sam hi.

records.english: Did the hotel have a room for you?
records.zomi: Zinbuuk in nang adingin inndan a nei hiam?

records.english: Was the doctor free that day?
records.zomi: Tua ni-in siavuan a awng hiam?

records.english: Asking whether things were available in the past reveals how scarce many services once were.
records.zomi: Nidang-in thu te a om hiam cih dot in nasep tampi bangzah a tawm hiam cih a lak hi.

records.english: Did the railway have any seats left when the soldiers came home?
records.zomi: Galkap te a ciah uh ciangin meileng in tutna a om lai hiam?

records.english: Was there still space in the cemetery for Grandpa next to his parents?
records.zomi: Han mun-ah Pu adingin a nu leh pa kiang-ah mun a om lai hiam?

records.english: Were there any places left at the school when you moved to the city?
records.zomi: Khuapi-ah na suan ciangin sang-ah mun a om lai hiam?

records.english: Not at first, so I waited a whole term before a place became free.

records.zomi: Ka min gelhna kua in a theihpih thei ding hiam?

records.english: The advice centre explained each step of the small claims process before I filled in the form.
records.zomi: Lai lak ka dim ma-in thuhilhna mun in sum neu ngetna nasep dan khebai khat ciat a hilhcian hi.

records.english: The registrar explained that a marriage must be registered before the couple can change their names.
records.zomi: Zi leh pasal te in a min uh a khek theih ma-in kitenna a kiciamteh ding hi, ci-in min gelhmi in a hilhcian hi.

records.english: Can I send the form online?
records.zomi: Lai lak online-ah ka khak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Simple, well-designed forms make legal procedures easier for everyone.
records.zomi: A baih, a hoih taka kibawl lai lak te in mi khempeuh adingin thukham nasep dan te a baih zaw sak hi.

records.english: How long will it take to register my father's death?
records.zomi: Ka pa' sihna ciamteh dingin hun bangzah a la ding hiam?

records.english: About half an hour, if you bring the doctor's certificate and his identity card.
records.zomi: Siavuan' lai leh a mimal lai na paipih leh nai lang bang.

records.english: Write the case number on every letter you send.
records.zomi: Na khak laikhak khempeuh tung-ah thu nambat gelh in.

records.english: Can I just turn up at the court office?
records.zomi: Thukhenna inn office-ah ka pai bek thei ding hiam?

records.english: Our residents' association invited a lawyer to explain how to challenge a planning decision.
records.zomi: I a sung-a teng mite' pawl in inn lamna thukhensatna khat bangci langdo ding hiam cih hilhcian dingin thukham siam mi khat a sam hi.

records.english: The court sent a letter explaining what to bring and where to wait on the day of the hearing.
records.zomi: Thukhenna hun ni-in bang paipih ding a, koi-ah ngak ding hiam cih a hilhcian lai khat thukhenna inn in a khak hi.

records.english: After the hearing was postponed, the clerk sent a new date by text and by post.
records.zomi: Thukhenna hun a kinunsak khit-in, lai gelhmi in text leh lai tawh ni thak a khak hi.

records.english: Why do some people miss their court dates even when they want to attend?
records.zomi: Bang hangin mi pawlkhat in a kihel nuam hang a thukhenna ni uh a mansuah uh hiam?

records.english: The volunteer helped my grandfather understand the letter from the court about his pension.
records.zomi: Thalawp in ka pu a pension tawh kisai thukhenna inn pan lai a theisiam nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Free advice services guide residents through forms and deadlines.
records.zomi: Man om lo thuhilhna nasep te in a sung-a teng mite lai lak leh hun ciang te-ah a lamlak uh hi.

records.english: Fair procedures depend on people knowing their rights and the steps they must take.
records.zomi: Nasep dan dik te pen mite in a thuneihna uh leh a bawl ding uh khebai te a theih tungah a kinga hi.

records.english: The hearing is next Monday.
records.zomi: Thukhenna hun pen kal hong tung Pizing ni-in ahi hi.

records.english: What happens after I report a stolen bike to the police?
records.zomi: Siiksakol kiguk tawh kisai palik te kiangah ka gen khit-in bang a piang ding hiam?

records.english: They give you a crime number for your insurance and will contact you if the bike is found.
records.zomi: Na kemcingna adingin thu nambat khat hong pia uh a, siiksakol a kimuh leh hong gen ding uh hi.

records.english: Can someone from the advice centre come to the hearing with me?
records.zomi: Thuhilhna mun pan mi khat thukhenna hun-ah hong zui thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, a volunteer can sit with you, though they can't speak for you.
records.zomi: Thei hi, thalawp khat na kiangah a tu thei hi, ahi zongin nangma' aiawh-in a gen thei kei hi.

records.english: Missing a deadline can end a case, so procedures should be explained early.
records.zomi: Hun ciang mansuah in thu khat a tawp sak thei ahih manin, nasep dan te a ma-in kihilhcian ding hi.

records.english: Ask at the front desk.
records.zomi: A ma lam dawhkan-ah dong in.

records.english: When our landlord refused to return our deposit, we had no idea how to take the matter further.
records.zomi: I inn neipa in i a ma-a piak sum a pia kik nuam loh ciangin, a ma lam-ah bangci pai ding hiam cih i thei kei uh hi.

records.english: A volunteer at the community law centre showed us how to send a formal letter and, when that failed, how to fill in the court form.
records.zomi: Khuasung thukham huhna mun-a thalawp khat in lai kician khat bangci khak ding hiam cih hong lak a, tua a lawhsap ciangin thukhenna inn lai lak bangci dim ding hiam cih hong lak hi.

records.english: The landlord paid the deposit back the week before the hearing was due.
records.zomi: Thukhenna hun a tun ma kal-in inn neipa in a ma-a piak sum a pia kik hi.

records.english: Mediation can resolve many disputes without the stress of a court hearing.
records.zomi: Kilemsakna in thukhenna hun' lungkhamna om lo-in kinialna tampi a phel thei hi.

records.english: Do I need to bring my passport?
records.zomi: Ka passport ka paipih ding kisam hiam?

records.english: Keeping copies and reference numbers protects people when procedures become complicated.
records.zomi: A kisuaktawm leh nambat te kem in nasep dan te a buai ciangin mite a kemcing hi.

records.english: Public services that explain their complaint procedures earn more trust from residents.
records.zomi: A phunna nasep dan uh a hilhcian mipi nasep te in a sung-a teng mite pan upna tam zaw a ngah uh hi.

records.english: Could you tell me how long the council has to respond to my appeal?
records.zomi: Ka dotkikna dawng dingin council in hun bangzah a nei hiam cih hong gen thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Volunteers who accompany people to hearings can reduce anxiety a great deal.
records.zomi: Thukhenna hun-ah mite a zui thalawp te in lungkhamna a kiam sak mahmah thei uh hi.

records.english: The office closes at four.
records.zomi: Office pen nai li-in a kikhak hi.

records.english: Please sign each page.
records.zomi: Lai khat ciat-ah na min gelh in, kong ngen hi.

records.english: Why does the registry office need the original certificate rather than a photocopy?
records.zomi: Bang hangin min gelhna office in photocopy sangin a kipatna lai a kisam hiam?

records.english: Where do I report a crime?
records.zomi: Gilo bawlna koi-ah ka gen ding hiam?

records.english: The law centre runs a phone line for residents who can't travel to its office.
records.zomi: Thukham huhna mun in a office-ah a pai thei lo a sung-a teng mite adingin phone sapna khat a nei hi.

records.english: Is it possible to have a mediation session at the community centre instead of going to court?
records.zomi: Thukhenna inn-ah pai sangin khuasung inn lian-ah kilemsakna hun khat neih theih ding a om hiam?

records.english: Clear explanations of legal procedures help people take part fairly.
records.zomi: Thukham nasep dan te' hilhcianna kician te in mite a dik takin a kihel nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Is there a waiting room?
records.zomi: Ngakna inndan a om hiam?

records.english: Bring two copies of each form.
records.zomi: Lai lak khat ciat' a kisuaktawm nih paipih in.

records.english: Interpreters ensure that people understand what happens at each step.
records.zomi: Pau lettu te in mite in khebai khat ciat-ah bang a piang hiam cih a theisiam nadingin a huh uh hi.

records.english: Could the council send me a copy of the procedure for making a formal complaint?
records.zomi: Phunna kician bawl nading nasep dan' a kisuaktawm khat council in hong khak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Do I have to pay a fee?
records.zomi: Man ka pia ding kisam hiam?

records.english: Can I change the date of the hearing?
records.zomi: Thukhenna hun' ni ka khek thei ding hiam?

records.english: I need a certified copy.
records.zomi: Kipsak kisuaktawm khat ka kisam hi.

records.english: In our town, the library offers free help with filling in legal forms every Wednesday.
records.zomi: I khuapi-ah, laibu inn in Nilai ni simin thukham lai lak dim-ah man om lo huhna a pia hi.

records.english: Can I bring an interpreter?
records.zomi: Pau lettu khat ka paipih thei ding hiam?

records.english: Where do I hand in the forms for the small claims court?
records.zomi: Sum neu ngetna thukhenna inn adingin lai lak te koi-ah ka ap ding hiam?

records.english: At the court office on the ground floor, or you can send them by post.
records.zomi: Inn nuai lam-a thukhenna inn office-ah, ahih kei leh lai tawh na khak thei hi.

records.english: Registering births, marriages and deaths correctly prevents problems later in life.
records.zomi: Suahna, kitenna leh sihna te a dik takin ciamteh in nuntakna-a a nung-a buaina te a kham hi.

records.english: Why does the law centre ask clients to bring all their letters to the first meeting?
records.zomi: Bang hangin thukham huhna mun in kikhopna masa pen-ah a lai khempeuh paipih dingin a mite a ngen hiam?

records.english: The adviser needs to see every deadline and decision, because missing one could end the case before it starts.
records.zomi: Thuhilhmi in hun ciang leh thukhensatna khempeuh a muh ding a kisam hi, bang hang hiam cih leh khat a mansuah leh thu a kipat ma-in a tawp thei hi.

records.english: The clerk checked my papers.
records.zomi: Lai gelhmi in ka lai te a en hi.

records.english: What will you be checking for at my next follow-up visit?
records.zomi: Ka a zom enna-ah bang na en ding hiam?

records.english: How long will I need follow-up visits after this treatment ends?
records.zomi: Hih zatui-enna a bei khit-in a zom enna te hun bangzah sung ka kisam ding hiam?

records.english: What happens if I miss a follow-up appointment because I'm ill?
records.zomi: Ka cidam loh manin a zom kihona hun ka mansuah leh bang a piang ding hiam?

records.english: Will I see the same doctor next time?
records.zomi: A zom vei-in siavuan kibang ka mu ding hiam?

records.english: I'll try to book you with me, but if I'm away, a colleague will have all your notes.
records.zomi: Keimah tawh kong ngetsak dingin ka hanciam ding hi, ahi zongin ka om kei leh nasep lawm khat in na ciamtehna khempeuh a nei ding hi.

records.english: Can I go back to work?
records.zomi: Nasep-ah ka ciah kik thei ding hiam?

records.english: When should I come back?
records.zomi: Bang hun-in ka hong pai kik ding hiam?

records.english: Is there anything I should do differently before my next appointment?
records.zomi: Ka kihona hun a zom ma-in a kibang lo-in ka bawl ding khat peuhpeuh a om hiam?

records.english: Do I still need to come back if I feel completely fine?
records.zomi: Ka kizak hoih mahmah leh ka hong pai kik ding kisam lai hiam?

records.english: Yes, because some problems don't cause symptoms, and we need to check your blood pressure again.
records.zomi: Kisam lai hi, bang hang hiam cih leh buaina pawlkhat in natna lahna a piangsak kei a, na sisan nawhna kien kik ding i kisam hi.

records.english: Can I have the results sent to me in writing as well as to my doctor?
records.zomi: Gah te ka siavuan kiangah bek hi lo-in kei kiangah zong lai tawh hong khak thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: Can my follow-up be at the clinic nearer my home instead of the hospital?
records.zomi: Ka a zom enna pen damlo inn sangin ka inn kiang zaw damdawi inn neu-ah a om thei ding hiam?

records.english: At my first follow-up after the operation, I was too nervous to ask the surgeon anything.
records.zomi: Zatui-at khit-in ka a zom enna masa pen-ah, at siavuan khat peuhpeuh dot dingin ka lungkham lua hi.

records.english: Before the second visit, my daughter helped me write a short list, and I read each question aloud.
records.zomi: A nihna kan ma-in, ka tanu in lista tom khat ka gelh nadingin hong huh a, dotna khat ciat aw ngaih takin ka sim hi.

records.english: The surgeon answered every one and thanked me for being so well prepared.
records.zomi: At siavuan in a khempeuh a dawng a, kithukim takin ka om ahih manin lungdam hong ko hi.

records.english: Phone follow-ups can save time when no physical examination is needed.
records.zomi: Pumpi enna kisam lo ciangin phone tawh a zom enna te in hun a kem sak thei hi.

records.english: Telling the doctor about new medicines or supplements prevents dangerous combinations.
records.zomi: Damdawi thak ahih kei leh a behlap an te tawh kisai siavuan gen in kihel lauhuai te a kham hi.

records.english: Comparing results over time helps doctors spot gradual changes.
records.zomi: Hun zui-in gah te kikteh in siavuan te kikhekna zawi te a muh nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Can the nurse see me instead?
records.zomi: A sangin nurse in hong mu thei ding hiam?

records.english: Patients who prepare questions get more out of short follow-up appointments.
records.zomi: Dotna a kithukimsak damlo te in kihona hun tom a zom te pan tam zaw a ngah uh hi.

records.english: Should I keep doing the exercises?
records.zomi: Pumpi sawizawi te ka bawl den ding hiam?

records.english: Is the swelling normal?
records.zomi: A vung pen a tangpi ahi hiam?

records.english: Feeling well does not always mean that follow-up checks are unnecessary.
records.zomi: Kizak hoih in a zom enna te kisam lo hi, cih a gen den kei hi.

records.english: Will the clinic send me the date for the next visit?
records.zomi: Damdawi inn neu in a zom kan ding ni hong khak ding hiam?

records.english: Why does the doctor want to compare this year's results with last year's?
records.zomi: Bang hangin siavuan in tu kum-a gah te leh kum nunung-a gah te a kikteh nuam hiam?

records.english: Should I call if it gets worse?
records.zomi: A hoih lo semsem leh ka sam ding hiam?

records.english: Good follow-up care turns a single treatment into a long-term plan for health.
records.zomi: A zom kemna hoih in zatui-enna khat bek pen sawt pi cidamna ngimna khat-ah a khek hi.

records.english: Is this my last follow-up?
records.zomi: Hih pen ka a zom enna nunung pen ahi hiam?

records.english: Will you check my blood pressure again?
records.zomi: Ka sisan nawhna na en kik ding hiam?

records.english: Will the stitches come out today?
records.zomi: Tuni-in stitch te a kila khia ding hiam?

records.english: Missing a follow-up can delay the discovery of problems that need attention.
records.zomi: A zom enna mansuah in limsak ding a kisam buaina te' muhna a nun sak thei hi.

records.english: Should I bring my notebook?
records.zomi: Ka ciamtehna laibu ka paipih ding hiam?

records.english: Is the wound healing well?
records.zomi: Liamna a dam hoih hiam?

records.english: Can my husband come with me next time?
records.zomi: A zom vei-in ka pasal in hong zui thei ding hiam?

records.english: Family members can help patients remember information from follow-up visits.
records.zomi: Innkuan mite in damlo te a zom enna-a thu te a phawk nadingin a huh thei uh hi.

records.english: Will I need another scan?
records.zomi: Scan dang khat ka kisam ding hiam?

records.english: Is it normal for recovery to be slower than you predicted at the first appointment?
records.zomi: Kihona hun masa pen-ah na gen sangin damna a zawi zaw pen a tangpi ahi hiam?

records.english: Why do some patients need follow-up visits for years after an operation?
records.zomi: Bang hangin damlo pawlkhat in zatui-at khit-in kum tampi sung a zom enna a kisam uh hiam?

records.english: Can my follow-up be done by phone?
records.zomi: Ka a zom enna phone tawh a kibawl thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, as long as you don't need any tests, the nurse can call you.
records.zomi: Thei hi, sittelna khatpeuh na kisam kei leh, nurse in hong sam thei hi.

records.english: Why do I need to keep coming back if the treatment seems to be working?
records.zomi: Zatui-enna a sem bang a kilang hang, bang hangin ka hong pai den ding a kisam hiam?

records.english: Clear explanations of why a follow-up is needed encourage patients to attend.
records.zomi: A zom enna bang hangin a kisam hiam cih hilhcianna kician te in damlo te a hong pai nadingin a hanthawn hi.

records.english: How long will this appointment take?
records.zomi: Hih kihona hun in hun bangzah a la ding hiam?

records.english: Could we talk about the side effects before deciding whether to change the dose?
records.zomi: Damdawi dawn zah khek ding hiam cih i khensat ma-in a dang gahna te tawh kisai i kikum thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: Are my results better?
records.zomi: Ka gah te a hoih zaw hiam?

records.english: Can I change the date?
records.zomi: Ni ka khek thei ding hiam?

records.english: Do I need another blood test?
records.zomi: Sisan enna dang khat ka kisam hiam?

records.english: Can I stop the tablets now?
records.zomi: Tu-in damdawi mum ka khawl thei ding hiam?

records.english: Follow-up visits allow doctors to see whether treatment is working as planned.
records.zomi: A zom enna te in siavuan te zatui-enna a kingim bangin a sem hiam cih a muh nadingin a phal hi.

records.english: How will I know whether the results of today's tests are good or bad?
records.zomi: Tuni sittelna gah te a hoih hiam, a hoih lo hiam cih bangci ka thei ding hiam?

records.english: Will the next follow-up include a physical examination, or just a conversation?
records.zomi: A zom enna-ah pumpi enna a kihel ding hiam, kikumna bek ahi ding hiam?

records.english: Honest reports about side effects help doctors adjust treatment safely.
records.zomi: A dang gahna te tawh kisai genna tak te in siavuan te zatui-enna bit takin a bawl kituak nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Would it help if my son came with me to the next appointment to take notes?
records.zomi: Ciamteh dingin kihona hun a zom-ah ka tapa hong zui leh a huh ding hiam?

records.english: Why does the doctor want to see me again after only two weeks?
records.zomi: Bang hangin siavuan in kal nih khit-in bek hong mu kik nuam hiam?

records.english: The new medicine can affect your kidneys, so the doctor wants to check your blood before the dose is increased.
records.zomi: Damdawi thak in na kal a khoih thei ahih manin, damdawi dawn zah a kah sak ma-in siavuan in na sisan a en nuam hi.

records.english: Seeing the same doctor regularly helps build trust and continuity of care.
records.zomi: Siavuan kibang vei tam-in mu in upna leh kemna kizom den a lam hi.

records.english: What should I bring to my follow-up appointment?
records.zomi: Ka a zom kihona hun-ah bang ka paipih ding hiam?

records.english: Bring your medicines, a note of any side effects and the questions you've thought of since your last visit.
records.zomi: Na damdawi te, a dang gahna khatpeuh' ciamtehna leh na kan nunung khit-a na ngaihsut dotna te paipih in.

records.english: Should I mention that I've started taking vitamins since my last visit?
records.zomi: Ka kan nunung khit-in vitamin ka dawn kipan hi, cih ka gen ding hiam?

records.english: Can I eat breakfast before the blood test?
records.zomi: Sisan enna ma-in zingsang an ka ne thei ding hiam?

records.english: Uncertainty about family history can inspire young people to search for records.
records.zomi: Innkuan tangthu tawh kisai thei kician lohna in khangno te ciamtehna te a zong dingin a hanthawn thei hi.

records.english: Was it raining on your wedding day?
records.zomi: Na mopawi ni-in guah a zuk hiam?

records.english: Living with uncertainty about the past is part of understanding any family's history.
records.zomi: Nidang tawh kisai thei kician lohna tawh nungta pen innkuan khatpeuh' tangthu theisiamna' khen khat ahi hi.

records.english: Did your father build this wall?
records.zomi: Na pa in hih bang a lam hiam?

records.english: Was the old mill still working when you were a child, or had it already closed?
records.zomi: Na naupan lai-in tui khawl lui a sem lai hiam, a kikhak khin hiam?

records.english: Did my great-grandmother live to see me born?
records.zomi: Ka pi upa pen in ka suahna a mu hiam?

records.english: Did your parents meet at the market?
records.zomi: Na nu leh pa zuakna mun-ah a kimu uh hiam?

records.english: I think so, but my aunt says it was at a wedding.
records.zomi: Ka ngaihsutin tua bang hi, ahi zongin ka ni in mopawi-ah ahi hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Was the church always this big?
records.zomi: Biakinn hih bangin a lian den hiam?

records.english: Did you really walk all that way?
records.zomi: Tua bang gamla na pai taktak hiam?

records.english: Did we live here when I was a baby?
records.zomi: Ka nau lai-in hih mun-ah i teeng uh hiam?

records.english: Do you think the family story about the hidden gold could be true?
records.zomi: Kisel kham tawh kisai innkuan tangthu a tak thei hi, na ci hiam?

records.english: When nobody is certain about the past, comparing several accounts can help.
records.zomi: Kuamah in nidang tawh kisai a thei kician kei ciangin, genna tuamtuam kikteh in a huh thei hi.

records.english: Was your first car red or blue?
records.zomi: Na mawtaw masa pen san hiam, dum hiam?

records.english: Could your grandparents have come here by boat rather than by train?
records.zomi: Na pu leh pi te meileng sangin long tawh a hong pai kha thei uh hiam?

records.english: Different relatives may be equally confident about very different versions of an event.
records.zomi: Sanggam tuamtuam te in thu piang khat' genna kibang lo mahmah te tungah a kibang-in a kician sa thei uh hi.

records.english: Was the market on Fridays?
records.zomi: Zuakna mun pen Laithai ni-in ahi hiam?

records.english: Was that before I was born?
records.zomi: Tua pen ka suah ma-in ahi hiam?

records.english: Did Grandma ever say whether she regretted leaving the island?
records.zomi: Tuikulh a nusiat a kisik hiam cih Pi in a gen ngei hiam?

records.english: Recording both the story and the doubts gives future generations a fuller picture.
records.zomi: Tangthu leh lungmuanlohna te a nih ciamteh in khang hong tung ding te kician zaw lim khat a pia hi.

records.english: Was the shop on this corner?
records.zomi: Zuakna inn pen hih ka-ah a om hiam?

records.english: Asking whether someone is sure about a story invites them to reflect rather than defend it.
records.zomi: Mi khat tangthu khat a thei kician hiam cih dot in a kidal sangin a ngaihsun kik nadingin a sam hi.

records.english: Did the village really have no electricity until the sixties?
records.zomi: Kum 1960 dong khua in mei-et a nei taktak kei hiam?

records.english: Was your teacher very strict?
records.zomi: Na sangsia a khauh mahmah hiam?

records.english: Older relatives often express uncertainty about events that happened long ago.
records.zomi: Sanggam upa te in sawt mahmah-a piang thu te tawh kisai thei kician lohna a gen zel uh hi.

records.english: Was the war over by then?
records.zomi: Tua hun-in galkapna a bei khin hiam?

records.english: For years, my grandmother wasn't sure whether her brother had survived the long journey across the mountains.
records.zomi: Kum tampi sung, mual te tan khualzinna sau-ah a unau pa a nungta hiam cih ka pi in a thei kician kei hi.

records.english: Then, when she was eighty, a letter arrived from a stranger who said he was that brother's grandson.
records.zomi: Tua khit-in, kum sawm giat a phak ciangin, tua unau pa' tu ka hi hi, a ci zin mi khat pan laikhak khat a hong tung hi.

records.english: She read it ten times before she believed it, and they met in person the following spring.
records.zomi: A um ma-in vei sawm a sim a, a zom spring-in a kimu taktak uh hi.

records.english: Did the family really lose the farm because of a bet, or is that just a story?
records.zomi: Kilawnna khat hangin innkuan in lo a mansuah taktak uh hiam, tangthu bek ahi hiam?

records.english: Did you go to school with Uncle?
records.zomi: Pa neu tawh sang na kah khawm uh hiam?

records.english: Is it possible that our family came from a different village altogether?

records.english: It's quite possible, because the records were lost, and the older relatives often disagreed about where the family began.

records.english: Carrying a list of medicines helps doctors treat patients safely in emergencies.

records.english: Can I travel abroad with this medicine in my hand luggage?

records.english: What if I miss a dose?

records.english: Patients who ask about medicine instructions avoid many common mistakes.

records.english: Clear answers about side effects help patients decide when to seek advice.
records.zomi: A dang gahna te tawh kisai dawnna kician te in damlo te bang hun-in thuhilhna a zong ding uh hiam cih a khensat nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Asking questions about medication is a sign of responsibility, not of ignorance.
records.zomi: Damdawi tawh kisai dotna dot pen mawhpuakna lahna ahi a, theih lohna lahna hi lo hi.

records.english: The bus company asked passengers to report drivers who didn't let wheelchair users board.

records.english: I reported the noisy party last night.

records.english: Public services should tell residents what happened after they report a problem.

records.english: Translating reporting forms ensures that everyone can use them.

records.english: How do I report a broken swing in the park?

records.english: Use the council's online form, or call the number on the sign by the gate.

records.english: Following up a report politely often speeds up a response.
records.zomi: Genna khat zahtak takin dot kik in dawnna a manlang zaw sak zel hi.

records.english: Could the council translate its reporting forms into the main community languages?

records.english: Could the community centre help older residents report problems without using the internet?

records.english: The council sent me a reference number.

records.english: Reports with dates, photos and locations help officials act quickly.
records.zomi: Ni, photo leh mun te nei genna te in kumpi nasemte a manlang takin a sep nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Can I report a problem by phone?
records.zomi: Phone tawh buaina khat ka gen thei ding hiam?

records.english: Did anyone report the broken fence?

records.english: The council's app lets residents report problems with a photo and a map location.

records.english: The water company sent an engineer within hours of a resident reporting a burst pipe.

records.english: Who should I tell if a restaurant looks dirty?

records.english: In our town, the food safety team at the council deals with that.
records.zomi: I khuapi-ah, council-a an bitna pawl in tua a en hi.

records.english: Does the council have a website for reports?
records.zomi: Council in genna adingin website khat a nei hiam?

records.english: The police station is open all night.

records.english: Trust grows when councils treat every report seriously and respond clearly.
records.zomi: Council te in genna khempeuh a thupisak a, a kician takin a dawn ciangin upna a khang hi.

records.english: Save the email the council sends back.

records.english: After several reports about speeding, the council installed a camera outside the school.

records.english: Residents who report problems help protect their neighbours as well as themselves.

records.english: The residents' association collected reports from every household before contacting the council.

records.english: Where is the reporting form?

records.english: For months, a shop on our high street sold cigarettes to schoolchildren, and everyone knew about it.

records.english: After an inspection, the shop lost its licence to sell tobacco, and the parents' group was thanked at a public meeting.

records.english: Community organisations can help vulnerable residents report violations safely.

records.english: Who checks the food at the market?

records.english: I reported the fly-tipping yesterday.

records.english: In our town, the library staff will help you fill in a report form if you ask.

records.english: The community police officer visits the market every week so that traders can report problems in person.

records.english: Is the report really anonymous?

records.english: Write down the time and place.
records.zomi: Hun leh mun gelh in.

records.english: Clear reporting systems encourage residents to speak up about problems.
records.zomi: Genna nasep dan kician te in a sung-a teng mite buaina te tawh kisai a gen nadingin a hanthawn hi.

records.english: The inspector will visit next week.
records.zomi: Enmi in kal hong tung-ah a kan ding hi.

records.english: Is there a fee for reporting a problem?
records.zomi: Buaina khat gen nadingin man piak ding a om hiam?

records.english: Reporting procedures vary between towns, so it helps to check the local rules.
records.zomi: Genna nasep dan te khuapi tuamtuam-ah a kibang kei ahih manin, khuasung thukham te en in a huh hi.

records.zomi: Buaina' photo khat la in, kong ngen hi.

records.english: Is it possible to report a problem at the hospital without affecting my mother's care?

records.zomi: Ka gen ciangin ka min ka gen ding kisam hiam?

records.english: Why didn't anyone tell me what happened after I reported the dangerous building?

records.english: Anonymous reporting protects people who fear retaliation.
records.zomi: Min om lo genna in thuk lehna lau mite a kemcing hi.

records.english: Repeated reports about the same problem can reveal wider failures.

records.english: Did the town really refuse to let the railway pass through it?
records.zomi: Khuapi in meileng lampi a sung tawn-in a pai dingin a phal taktak kei hiam?

records.english: Some landowners objected, but the real reason was that the hills made building the line here too expensive.
records.zomi: Lei neitu pawlkhat in a langdo uh hi, ahi zongin bang hang taktak pen mual te in hih mun-ah lampi lam a man tam lua sak hi.

records.english: Did Grandpa really carry his mother across the river on his back?
records.zomi: Pu in a nu a nungzang-ah pua-in luipi a tan taktak hiam?

records.english: Hadn't the fighting stopped by then?

records.english: Didn't the shop belong to Grandma?

records.english: A family legend may not need correcting, although knowing the truth adds depth to the story.

records.english: Was the famous visitor actually the prime minister, or just someone who looked like him?

records.english: Is it true that the house was once a school for the whole valley?
records.zomi: Inn pen nidang-in guam khempeuh adingin sang ahi ngei hi, cih a tak hiam?

records.english: Didn't the old market move to the square only after the river damaged its banks?

records.english: Was the village really empty during the war, or did some families stay behind?
records.zomi: Galkapna lai-in khua a awng taktak hiam, innkuan pawlkhat a om lai uh hiam?

records.english: Was it Grandma who planted the tree?
records.zomi: Sing a suan pen Pi ahi hiam?

records.english: Wasn't the old school burned down by soldiers?

records.english: No, it burned because a stove was left on during the winter holiday.

records.english: Did Mum have a twin?
records.zomi: Nu in apeng a nei hiam?

records.english: Didn't you grow up in the city?
records.zomi: Khuapi-ah na khanglian hi lo hiam?

records.english: Was the town really founded by fishermen, or is that just what the sign says?
records.zomi: Khuapi pen nga manmi te in a kipatsak taktak hiam, laimal in a gen bang bek ahi hiam?

records.english: For years, I believed that my grandmother had been a famous singer before she married.
