records.english: When I finally asked her about it, she laughed and said she had sung once on local radio, as part of a school choir.

records.english: I was a little disappointed, but her real story about that day turned out to be much funnier.

records.english: Did Dad really break his leg skiing?

records.english: Did you really hide in the attic, or was it the cellar?

records.english: Recording corrected stories helps future generations avoid repeating the same errors.
records.zomi: Kibawlphat tangthu te ciamteh in khang hong tung ding te khialhna kibang a bawl kik loh nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Did the fire start in the bakery?
records.zomi: Moh zuakna inn-ah mei a kipan hiam?

records.english: Was the river cleaner when you were young?
records.zomi: Na neu lai-in luipi a siang zaw hiam?

records.english: Did you really live in a tent?

records.english: Correcting family stories gently helps keep history accurate without hurting anyone's feelings.
records.zomi: Innkuan tangthu te nem takin bawlphat in kuamah' lungsim a na sak lo-in tangthu a dik den sak hi.

records.english: Did your parents really marry in secret, or did the whole village know?
records.zomi: Na nu leh pa a kisel-in a kiten taktak uh hiam, khua khempeuh in a thei uh hiam?

records.english: Did Uncle really win a prize?
records.zomi: Pa neu in letsong a ngah taktak hiam?

records.english: Did the old teacher really punish you for laughing in church?

records.english: Did your parents prefer to save money or to spend it on travelling?
records.zomi: Na nu leh pa in sum kem a deih zaw uh hiam, khualzinna-ah zang?

records.english: Did people in your youth prefer to marry someone from their own village or from outside?
records.zomi: Na khangno lai-in mite in amau' khua-a mi tawh kiten a deih zaw uh hiam, a pua-a mi tawh?

records.english: Most preferred their own village, because families knew each other, but more young people married outsiders once they began working in town.
records.zomi: A tam zaw in amau' khua a deih zaw uh hi, bang hang hiam cih leh innkuan te in khat leh khat a kithei uh a, ahi zongin khuapi-ah nasep a sep kipat uh ciangin khangno tam zaw in a pua-a mi tawh a kiten uh hi.

records.english: Older people may value things from the past that younger generations overlook.
records.zomi: Upa te in khang neu zaw te in a limsak loh nidang-a thu te a manpha sa thei uh hi.

records.english: Comparing the past with the present helps families decide which traditions to keep.
records.zomi: Nidang leh tu kikteh in innkuan te in koi ngeina te a kem ding uh hiam cih a khensat nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Did you choose the train or the boat?
records.zomi: Meileng na teel hiam, long?

records.english: Was your wedding day more exciting than the day your first child was born?
records.zomi: Na mopawi ni in na ta masa pen a suah ni sangin a lungdam huai zaw hiam?

records.english: Was the old house bigger than this one?
records.zomi: Inn lui pen hih sangin a lian zaw hiam?

records.english: Smaller, but it had a huge garden where we grew all our vegetables.
records.zomi: A neu zaw hi, ahi zongin i anteh khempeuh i suanna huan lian mahmah khat a nei hi.

records.english: Was the market busier on Saturdays?
records.zomi: Kiginni-in zuakna mun a buai zaw hiam?

records.english: Questions about which option someone preferred can bring out unexpected memories.
records.zomi: Mi khat in koi teelna a deih zaw hiam cih tawh kisai dotna te in lamen loh phawkna te a hong pusak thei hi.

records.english: Was it easier to find work then?
records.zomi: Tua hun-in nasep muh a baih zaw hiam?

records.english: Some choices that seemed obvious at the time are seen differently decades later.
records.zomi: Tua hun lai-in a kilang bang a kilang teelna pawlkhat pen kum sawm tampi khit-in a kibang lo-in kien hi.

records.english: Did your family prefer the old market or the new supermarket when it first opened?
records.zomi: Supermarket thak a kihon masak lai-in na innkuan in zuakna mun lui a deih zaw uh hiam, supermarket thak?

records.english: Was the winter colder in those days?
records.zomi: Tua hun lai-in khuaphal a hat zaw hiam?

records.english: Hearing how elders weighed difficult choices can guide younger people facing their own.
records.zomi: Upa te in teelna haksa te bangci a khaisak uh hiam cih zak in amau' teelna tuak khangno te a lamlak thei hi.

records.english: Was your brother taller than you?
records.zomi: Na unau pa nang sangin a sang zaw hiam?

records.english: Was the old road shorter than the new one?
records.zomi: Lampi lui pen a thak sangin a tom zaw hiam?

records.english: Why did Grandpa choose the factory job instead of staying on the farm?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pu in lo-ah om den sangin factory nasep a teel hiam?

records.english: The factory paid every week, while the farm only paid when the harvest was good.
records.zomi: Factory in kal simin a pia a, lo in buh lak a hoih ciang bek-in a pia hi.

records.english: Was school stricter then or now?
records.zomi: Sang tua hun-in a khauh zaw hiam, tu-in?

records.english: Did you like the old church better?
records.zomi: Biakinn lui na deih zaw hiam?

records.english: Was life harder in the village or in the city when you were young?
records.zomi: Na neu lai-in khua-ah nuntakna a haksa zaw hiam, khuapi-ah?

records.english: The village was harder work, but the city was lonelier.
records.zomi: Khua-ah nasep a haksa zaw a, ahi zongin khuapi-ah a khat bek-in kizak a tam zaw hi.

records.english: Which was more frightening, the storm of 1974 or the earthquake years later?
records.zomi: Koi in a lauhuai zaw hiam, kum 1974-a huihpi hiam, kum tampi khit-a lei ling hiam?

records.english: Did Grandma prefer tea or coffee?
records.zomi: Pi in lakphak a deih zaw hiam, coffee?

records.english: Did you prefer your mother's cooking or your grandmother's?
records.zomi: Na nu' an huan na deih zaw hiam, na pi'?

records.english: Family stories often turn on a moment when someone chose one path instead of another.
records.zomi: Innkuan tangthu te in mi khat in lampi khat sangin lampi dang khat a teel hun khat-ah a kinga zel hi.

records.english: Did you live closer to the river or the market?
records.zomi: Luipi kiang-ah na teeng zaw hiam, zuakna mun kiang-ah?

records.english: Was the bus faster than walking?
records.zomi: Bus in khe tawh pai sangin a manlang zaw hiam?

records.english: Comparing old and new ways of living helps young people understand both.
records.zomi: Nidang leh tu-a nuntak dan kikteh in khangno te in a nih a theisiam nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Was the city cleaner then than now?
records.zomi: Tua hun-in khuapi tu-a sangin a siang zaw hiam?

records.english: Many older people compare the hardships of the past with its sense of community.
records.zomi: Upa tampi in nidang-a haksatna te a khuasung kipawlna uh tawh a kikteh uh hi.

records.english: Asking older relatives to compare two periods of their lives reveals how much the world has changed.
records.zomi: Sanggam upa te a nuntakna uh hun nih kikteh dingin ngen in leitung bangzah a kikhek hiam cih a lak hi.

records.english: Which was harder to learn, riding a bicycle or driving a car?
records.zomi: Koi in sin a haksa zaw hiam, siiksakol tuan hiam, mawtaw mawng hiam?

records.english: When my parents married, they had to choose between a bigger wedding and a small plot of land.
records.zomi: Ka nu leh pa a kiten uh ciangin, mopawi lian zaw leh lei neu khat kikal-ah a teel ding uh a kisam hi.

records.english: They chose the land, held the ceremony in my grandmother's garden and served only rice and tea.
records.zomi: Lei a teel uh a, ka pi' huan-ah mopawi a bawl uh a, an leh lakphak bek a pia uh hi.

records.english: Forty years later, the house they built on that land is where the whole family gathers every New Year.
records.zomi: Kum sawm li khit-in, tua lei tung-ah a lam inn pen Kum Thak simin innkuan khempeuh a kikhawmna mun ahi hi.

records.english: Did you prefer football or swimming?
records.zomi: Football na deih zaw hiam, tuipeek?

records.english: Was the old wooden bridge safer than the stone one that replaced it?
records.zomi: Sing lei lui in a laih suang lei sangin a bit zaw hiam?

records.english: Was it cheaper to live in the village?
records.zomi: Khua-ah nuntak a man neu zaw hiam?

records.english: Did people in your youth prefer radio or newspapers for the news?
records.zomi: Na khangno lai-in mite in thuthak adingin radio a deih zaw uh hiam, thuthak lai?

records.english: Questions about past choices can lead to conversations about regret and gratitude.
records.zomi: Nidang teelna te tawh kisai dotna te in kisikna leh lungdamna tawh kisai kikumna te-ah a tun thei hi.

records.english: Comparisons between past choices often show what people valued most at the time.
records.zomi: Nidang teelna te kikteh in tua hun lai-in mite in bang a manpha sa pen uh hiam cih a lak zel hi.

records.english: Did you prefer reading or playing outside?
records.zomi: Laisim na deih zaw hiam, a pua-ah kawm?

records.english: My son asked if Jesus ever cried.
records.zomi: Jesu a kap ngei hiam, ci-in ka tapa in a dong hi.

records.english: Many Christian parents teach that Jesus was not partly God and partly human but completely both.
records.zomi: Khazih nu leh pa tampi in Jesu pen a khenkhat Pasian, a khenkhat mihing hi lo-in a bup-in a nih ahi hi, ci-in a sinsak uh hi.

records.english: For believers, the humble birth of Jesus shows that God values the poor and the weak.
records.zomi: Um mite adingin, Jesu' niamkhiat taka suahna in Pasian in mi zawng leh mi hatlo te a manpha sa hi, cih a lak hi.

records.english: Why do we put the baby in the nativity scene only on Christmas morning?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Christmas zingsang-in bek Jesu suahna lim-ah naungek i koih uh hiam?

records.english: It's our family's way of waiting for the day we celebrate his birth.
records.zomi: Tua pen a suahna i pawi bawl ni i ngakna innkuan dan ahi hi.

records.english: How can Jesus be both God and a human being at the same time?
records.zomi: Jesu hun kibang-in Pasian leh mihing a nih bangci a hi thei hiam?

records.english: Christians believe it is a mystery, but they hold that he was fully divine and fully human without either side being lessened.
records.zomi: Khazih mite in thuthuk khat ahi hi, ci-in a um uh a, ahi zongin a lam khat zong a kiam lo-in a bup-in Pasian leh a bup-in mihing ahi hi, ci-in a lenkip uh hi.

records.english: We read a verse every day in Advent.
records.zomi: Advent sung ni simin cang khat i sim uh hi.

records.english: For many Christian families, Christmas is a time to reflect on God becoming human.
records.zomi: Khazih innkuan tampi adingin, Christmas pen Pasian mihing a suahna ngaihsun kik hun ahi hi.

records.english: How do you explain to a young child that God became a human being?
records.zomi: Pasian mihing hong suak hi, cih naupang neu khat kiangah bangci na hilhcian hiam?

records.english: Dad says God became a person.
records.zomi: Pasian mi khat hong suak hi, ci-in Pa in a gen hi.

records.english: We give gifts to remember God's gift.
records.zomi: Pasian' letsong phawk dingin letsong i kipia uh hi.

records.english: Our family gives money to a children's hospital at Christmas, because Jesus came as a child.
records.zomi: Jesu naupang-in a hong pai ahih manin i innkuan in Christmas-in naupang damlo inn khat kiangah sum a pia hi.

records.english: Christians often describe the Incarnation as one of the most distinctive teachings of their faith.
records.zomi: Khazih mite in Pasian mi bangin hong suakna pen a upna uh-a sinsakna tuam pen khat ahi hi, ci-in a gen zel uh hi.

records.english: We go to church on Christmas morning.
records.zomi: Christmas zingsang-in biakinn-ah i pai uh hi.

records.english: Why was Jesus born in a stable?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Jesu bawng inn-ah a piang hiam?

records.english: Why do some Christian families wait until Christmas Eve to put up their nativity scene?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Khazih innkuan pawlkhat in Christmas zan dong Jesu suahna lim a koih ngak uh hiam?

records.english: My grandmother says that God coming as a helpless baby shows how much he trusts us.
records.zomi: Pasian naungek huhna nei lo-in a hong pai in eite bangzah a hong muang hiam cih a lak hi, ci-in ka pi in a gen hi.

records.english: Could we read the first chapter of John's Gospel together on Christmas Eve this year?
records.zomi: Hih kum Christmas zan-in Johan' Lungdamna Thu' a khen masa pen i sim khawm thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: Why do Christians say that Jesus was God even while he was a baby in a manger?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Khazih mite in bawng ankuang-a naungek a hih lai-in zong Jesu pen Pasian ahi hi, a ci uh hiam?

records.english: Do your children understand why Christians call Jesus Emmanuel, God with us?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Khazih mite in Jesu pen Emmanuel, Eite tawh Pasian hong om khawm hi, a ci uh hiam cih na ta te in a theisiam uh hiam?

records.english: When my daughter asked whether Jesus got sick, we talked about how he shared ordinary human life.
records.zomi: Jesu a cidam lo ngei hiam, ci-in ka tanu in a dot ciangin, mihing nuntakna tangpi a hawm dan tawh kisai i kikum uh hi.

records.english: Was Jesus a real baby?
records.zomi: Jesu pen naungek taktak ahi hiam?

records.english: Many Christian parents use nativity scenes to help children picture the Christmas story.
records.zomi: Khazih nu leh pa tampi in naupang te in Christmas tangthu a lim a muh nadingin Jesu suahna lim te a zang uh hi.

records.english: Did Jesus have to learn to walk and talk?
records.zomi: Jesu in pai leh pau gen a sin ding a kisam hiam?

records.english: Christians believe he did, because he grew up as a real human child.
records.zomi: Khazih mite in sin hi, ci-in a um uh hi, bang hang hiam cih leh mihing naupang taktak-in a khanglian hi.

records.english: My little brother loves the angels in the story.
records.zomi: Ka nau pa in tangthu-a vantungmi te a deih mahmah hi.

records.english: Christmas is my grandmother's favourite festival.
records.zomi: Christmas pen ka pi' pawi it pen ahi hi.

records.english: Why does our family's faith say the Incarnation matters so much?
records.zomi: Bang hangin i innkuan' upna in Pasian mi bangin hong suakna a thupi mahmah hi, a ci hiam?

records.english: Christians believe that by becoming human, God shared our life from the inside and showed his love in a way we could see and touch.
records.zomi: Mihing a hong suah in Pasian in i nuntakna a sung lam pan a hawm a, i muh leh i khoih theih dan khat-in a itna a lak hi, ci-in Khazih mite in a um uh hi.

records.english: Christians often find comfort in believing that God has shared human pain and joy.
records.zomi: Khazih mite in Pasian in mihing natna leh lungdamna a hawm khin hi, cih um-in lungmuanna a ngah zel uh hi.

records.english: Grandpa tells us about the shepherds.
records.zomi: Pu in tuucing te tawh kisai hong gen hi.

records.english: Did Jesus help Joseph in the workshop?
records.zomi: Jesu in nasep inn-ah Josef a huh hiam?

records.english: Did Mary know who Jesus was?
records.zomi: Jesu kua ahi hiam cih Mari in a thei hiam?

records.english: The children act out the nativity at home.
records.zomi: Naupang te in inn-ah Jesu suahna tangthu lim a bawl uh hi.

records.english: Our family keeps an old nativity set that my great-grandfather carved from wood.
records.zomi: I innkuan in ka pu upa pen in sing tawh a thuk Jesu suahna lim lui khat a kem hi.

records.english: When my mother was dying, she said it comforted her that God had known human suffering.
records.zomi: Ka nu a sih dek ciangin, Pasian in mihing thuakna a thei khin hi, cih in amah a lungmuan sak hi, a ci hi.

records.english: The Christmas after our son was born, my wife held him during the carol service while the choir sang about the child in the manger.
records.zomi: I tapa a suah khit-a Christmas-in, la sa pawl in bawng ankuang-a naungek tawh kisai a sak lai-in Christmas la hun-ah ka zi in amah a pom hi.

records.english: She told me later that she had never understood until that night how fragile God had chosen to become.
records.zomi: Pasian bangzah hatlo dingin a teel hiam cih tua zan dong a theisiam ngei kei hi, ci-in a nung-in hong gen hi.

records.english: Every Christmas since, she has held our youngest child during that same carol.
records.zomi: Tua pan kipan Christmas simin, tua la kibang lai-in i ta neu pen a pom den hi.

records.english: My daughter is playing Mary this year.
records.zomi: Hih kum-in ka tanu Mari lim a bawl ding hi.

records.english: Mum, was Jesus a baby like my little sister?
records.zomi: Nu, Jesu pen ka nau nu bang naungek ahi hiam?

records.english: Yes, Christians believe he was a real baby who needed his mother just like she does.
records.zomi: Hi hi, Khazih mite in a nu a kisam naungek taktak ahi a, na nau nu bangmah ahi hi, ci-in a um uh hi.

records.english: Grandma reads the Christmas story to us.
records.zomi: Pi in Christmas tangthu hong sim sak hi.

records.english: My parents taught me that the Incarnation means God understands every human sorrow.
records.zomi: Pasian mi bangin hong suakna in Pasian in mihing lungkhamna khempeuh a theisiam hi, cih a lak hi, ci-in ka nu leh pa in hong sinsak uh hi.

records.english: My teenage son asked why it matters whether Jesus was really human, and we talked for hours.
records.zomi: Jesu mihing taktak a hih leh hih kei bang hangin a thupi hiam, ci-in kum sawm leh tawm ka tapa in a dong a, nai tampi sung i kikum uh hi.

records.english: After her baby was born, my sister said she understood Christmas in a completely new way.
records.zomi: A nau a suah khit-in, Christmas lam thak mahmah khat-in ka theisiam hi, ci-in ka sanggam nu in a gen hi.

records.english: We light a candle on Christmas Eve.
records.zomi: Christmas zan-in khawimeivaak khat i tak uh hi.

records.english: Why did God come as a baby?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pasian naungek-in a hong pai hiam?

records.english: My son was surprised to learn that Jesus worked as a carpenter before he began to teach.
records.zomi: Jesu in a sinsak ma-in khutsiampa-in nasep a sem hi, cih a theih ciangin ka tapa a lamdang sa hi.

records.english: Family traditions at Christmas help children connect the Incarnation with everyday life.
records.zomi: Christmas-a innkuan ngeina te in naupang te Pasian mi bangin hong suakna ni sim nuntakna tawh a kizop nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: We pray for poor families at Christmas.
records.zomi: Christmas-in innkuan zawng te adingin thu i ngen uh hi.

records.english: Christian families often return each year to the same readings to remember the Incarnation.
records.zomi: Khazih innkuan te in Pasian mi bangin hong suakna phawk dingin kum simin simna kibang te-ah a ciah kik zel uh hi.

records.english: The Incarnation is often described by believers as a mystery to be wondered at rather than fully explained.
records.zomi: Pasian mi bangin hong suakna pen um mite in a bup-in hilhcian ding sangin lamdang sak ding thuthuk khat bangin a gen zel uh hi.

records.english: Many Christians see in the Incarnation a reason to care for every human body and life.
records.zomi: Khazih mi tampi in Pasian mi bangin hong suakna-ah mihing pumpi leh nuntakna khempeuh kem nading bang hang khat a mu uh hi.

records.english: My husband reads the story of the shepherds to our children every Christmas night.
records.zomi: Ka pasal in Christmas zan simin i ta te kiangah tuucing te' tangthu a sim sak hi.

records.english: We set up the nativity scene every December.
records.zomi: December simin Jesu suahna lim i koih uh hi.

records.english: Our family sings carols together.
records.zomi: I innkuan in Christmas la te i sa khawm uh hi.

records.english: My grandfather always wept a little when the choir sang about God coming to live among us.
records.zomi: La sa pawl in Pasian eite lak-ah teeng dingin a hong pai tawh kisai a sak ciangin ka pu a kap neu den hi.

records.english: My sister made a star for the tree.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu in sing adingin aksi khat a bawl hi.

records.english: My timeline is too crowded.
records.zomi: Ka hun kizui lim a kikhap lua hi.

records.english: When our class made a timeline of our town, two groups gave different dates for the opening of the railway.
records.zomi: I tanglai in i khuapi' hun kizui lim a bawl uh ciangin, pawl nih in meileng lampi a kihon ni kibang lo a gen uh hi.

records.english: We visited the library together and found an old newspaper report announcing the first train.
records.zomi: Laibu inn-ah i pai khawm uh a, meileng masa pen' tun thu a tangko thuthak lai lui khat i mu uh hi.

records.english: Both groups had been wrong by a year, and we fixed the timeline before the parents' evening.
records.zomi: Pawl nih in kum khat a khial uh a, nu leh pa nitak kikhopna ma-in hun kizui lim i bawlphat uh hi.

records.english: Why did the museum change the order of its displays after the new research was published?
records.zomi: Zonna thak a kitangko khit-in bang hangin museum in a lakna te a kizui dan a khek hiam?

records.english: Historians discovered that the old tools were older than everyone had thought, so the timeline had to be corrected.
records.zomi: Nasep van lui te mi khempeuh' ngaihsut sangin a lui zaw hi, cih tangthu siam mite in a mu uh a, ahih manin hun kizui lim bawlphat ding a kisam hi.

records.english: When the timeline on the classroom wall fell down, we rebuilt it with the events we had missed.
records.zomi: Tanglai bang-a hun kizui lim a puk ciangin, i mansuah thu piang te tawh i lam kik uh hi.

records.english: After comparing two textbooks, we realised that one had confused the start and end of the reign.
records.zomi: Sinna laibu nih i kikteh khit-in, khat in kumpipa' ukna a kipatna leh a tawpna a kilamdang khial hi, cih i phawk uh hi.

records.english: How can I show that the industrial changes happened slowly rather than all at once?
records.zomi: Khawl nasep kikhekna te a khempeuh khatvei-in hi lo-in zawi zawi-in a piang hi, cih bangci ka lak thei ding hiam?

records.english: What should I do if I don't know the exact year of an event?
records.zomi: Thu piang khat' kum taktak ka theih kei leh bang ka bawl ding hiam?

records.english: Write the decade, or put a question mark next to your best guess.
records.zomi: Kum sawm khen gelh in, ahih kei leh na ngaihsut hoih pen kiangah dotna lim khat koih in.

records.english: Personal timelines connect pupils' own lives with wider history.
records.zomi: Mimal hun kizui lim te in sangnaupang te' nuntakna leh tangthu lian zaw a kizop sak hi.

records.english: Use a ruler for the line.
records.zomi: Tang adingin tehna sing zang in.

records.english: Family memories are valuable, but dates should be checked against records.
records.zomi: Innkuan phawkna te a manpha a, ahi zongin ni te ciamtehna te tawh kien ding hi.

records.english: How can two calendars disagree about which year it is?
records.zomi: Calendar nih in koi kum ahi hiam cih-ah bangci a kituak lo thei hiam?

records.english: How can we compare what was happening in our village and in the capital in the same decade?
records.zomi: Kum sawm kibang sung-in i khua leh gam khuapi lian-ah bang a piang hiam cih bangci i kikteh thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: Draw two parallel lines with the same scale, one for each place, so you can compare them year by year.
records.zomi: Tehna kibang nei tang nih kikiang-in suai in, mun khat ciat adingin khat ciat, kum khat ciat-in na kikteh theih nadingin.

records.english: Count the years between them.
records.zomi: A kikal-a kum te sim in.

records.english: After we found an old diary, we moved three family events to earlier dates.
records.zomi: Ni sim ciamtehna lai lui khat i muh khit-in, innkuan thu piang thum ni ma zaw te-ah i suan uh hi.

records.english: Let's check the dates again.
records.zomi: Ni te i en kik ding uh.

records.english: The teacher showed us how to check a date by comparing a letter with a newspaper from the same week.
records.zomi: Kal kibang-a thuthak lai khat tawh laikhak khat kikteh-in ni bangci en ding hiam cih sangsia in hong lak hi.

records.english: Building and correcting timelines teaches patience and careful reasoning.
records.zomi: Hun kizui lim bawl leh bawlphat in thuakzawhna leh kidawm taka ngaihsutna a sinsak hi.

records.english: Put the oldest event first.
records.zomi: A lui pen thu piang a masa-in koih in.

records.english: The dates in the book are different.
records.zomi: Laibu-a ni te a kibang kei hi.

records.english: Start with the year you were born.
records.zomi: Na suah kum tawh kipan in.

records.english: Add pictures to the timeline.
records.zomi: Hun kizui lim-ah lim te behlap in.

records.english: Different calendar systems can make the same date look very different.
records.zomi: Calendar dan tuamtuam te in ni kibang a kibang lo mahmah-in a kilang sak thei hi.

records.english: Put a question mark if you're not sure.
records.zomi: Na thei kician kei leh dotna lim khat koih in.

records.english: Could we add our own birthdays to the town timeline so that it feels more personal?
records.zomi: Mimal bang a kizak nadingin khuapi hun kizui lim-ah i suahni te i behlap thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: Parallel timelines help learners compare events in different places.
records.zomi: Kikiang hun kizui lim te in sinmi te mun tuamtuam-a thu piang te a kikteh nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Checking dates against more than one source prevents common errors.

records.english: Is it better to use the same scale for the whole timeline or to stretch the recent years?

records.english: When my family timeline became too long, I divided it into one sheet for each generation.
records.zomi: Ka innkuan hun kizui lim a sau lua ciangin, khang khat ciat adingin lai khat ciat-in ka khen hi.

records.english: Could you help me work out how many years passed between the two wars?
records.zomi: Galkapna nih kikal-ah kum bangzah a pai hiam cih tuat dingin hong huh thei ding na hi hiam?

records.english: This event is in the wrong place.

records.english: I mixed up the two kings.

records.english: Ask your grandparents for the dates.

records.english: Why do the dates on the old church sign differ from those in the town records?

records.english: Uncertain dates should be marked clearly rather than guessed with false confidence.
records.zomi: Kician lo ni te pen kician lo lungmuanna tawh ngaihsun bang sangin a kician takin kiciamteh ding hi.

records.english: Why do my dates go the wrong way on the timeline?

records.english: Breaking long timelines into sections makes them easier to read.
records.zomi: Hun kizui lim sau te khen neu te-ah khen in a sim baih zaw sak hi.

records.zomi: Kum za tuamtuam adingin pianzia tuamtuam zang in.

records.english: My timeline doesn't fit on the page.

records.english: Write the year above each event.
records.zomi: Thu piang khat ciat tung-ah kum gelh in.

records.english: Draw a longer line.
records.zomi: A sau zaw tang khat suai in.

records.english: Our class fixed the problem of overlapping events by drawing them above and below the line.
records.zomi: I tanglai in kituak thu piang te tang' a tung leh a nuai-ah suai-in buaina a phel uh hi.

records.english: Many problems with timelines come from using an uneven scale.
records.zomi: Hun kizui lim tawh kisai buaina tampi pen kibang lo tehna zang pan a hong pai hi.

records.english: Pharmacists can adapt labels for people with poor eyesight or limited reading skills.

records.zomi: Kammal tom te tawh kisai dawnna kician te in damlo te lamlakna te a dik takin a zuih nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Does it say to keep it in the fridge?
records.zomi: Fridge sung-ah koih dingin a gen hiam?

records.zomi: Bang hangin ka laimal in damdawi thakhat-in khawl lo dingin hong pulak hiam?

records.zomi: A kibang bang kilang bawm te pen damlo upa te adingin lungbuaina ngahna mun tangpi khat ahi hi.

records.english: Who prescribed this medicine?

records.english: Asking about a changed dose prevents patients from following outdated instructions.

records.english: Does the label say how many to take?
records.zomi: Laimal in bangzah dawn ding hiam cih a gen hiam?

records.english: Could you explain what the warning about drowsiness on my label means for my job?
records.zomi: Ka laimal tung-a ihmut lua tawh kisai pulakna in ka nasep adingin bang a gen hiam cih na hilhcian thei ding hiam?

records.english: Questions about labels give pharmacists a chance to check for other problems.
records.zomi: Laimal te tawh kisai dotna te in damdawi zuakmi te buaina dang te en nading hun a pia hi.

records.english: Labels in a patient's own language help families give medicines safely.
records.zomi: Damlo khat' mimal pau-a laimal te in innkuan te damdawi bit takin a piak nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Can the pharmacy add a picture to the label so that my grandmother can recognise it?
records.zomi: Ka pi in a theih kik theih nadingin damdawi zuakna inn in laimal tung-ah lim khat a behlap thei ding hiam?

records.english: A misspelled name on a label should always be corrected before the medicine is used.
records.zomi: Laimal tung-a min khial khat pen damdawi a kizat ma-in a kibawlphat den ding hi.

records.english: Where is the dose written?
records.zomi: Damdawi dawn zah koi-ah a kigelh hiam?

records.english: Expiry dates on labels protect patients from medicines that may have lost their effect.
records.zomi: Laimal tung-a hun bei ni te in a hatna a mansuah kha thei damdawi te pan damlo te a kemcing hi.

records.english: What does "as needed" mean on my label?

records.english: It means you take the medicine only when you need it, not on a regular schedule.

records.english: What should I do if the name on the label is spelled wrongly?
records.zomi: Laimal tung-a min a kigelh khial leh bang ka bawl ding hiam?

records.english: What made you go back?
records.zomi: Bang in hong ciah kik sak hiam?

records.english: What helped you overcome your fear of hospitals after the accident?
records.zomi: Thu piang khit-in damlo inn lauhna na zawh nadingin bang in hong huh hiam?

records.english: Who taught you to be brave?

records.english: What gave you the courage to start your own business after losing your job?

records.english: My children were watching how I would cope, and I wanted to show them that you can begin again.
records.zomi: Ka ta te in bangci ka thuak zo ding hiam cih a en uh a, kipan kik thei hi, cih ka lak nuam hi.

records.english: Stories of courage from older relatives connect families with their history.
records.zomi: Sanggam upa te' hangsanna tangthu te in innkuan te a tangthu uh tawh a kizop sak hi.

records.english: What advice would you give to someone who is afraid to ask for help?

records.english: How long did it take to feel better?

records.english: How did you feel afterwards?
records.zomi: A nung-in bangci na kizak hiam?

records.english: Why do some people find it easier to be brave for others than for themselves?

records.english: When someone they love is in danger, their fear seems less important than the need to help.

records.english: Many people say that thinking of others gave them the strength to act.
records.zomi: Mi tampi in mi dang te ngaihsut in sep nading hatna hong pia hi, a ci uh hi.

records.zomi: Natna gik khat tawh a nungta mi khat adingin hangsanna in bang a gen hiam?

records.english: People who are asked about their courage often insist that anyone would have done the same.
records.zomi: A hangsanna uh tawh kisai kidong mite in kuapeuh in tua bangin a bawl ding hi, ci-in a gen den zel uh hi.

records.english: Did your parents know what you did?
records.zomi: Na bawl na nu leh pa in a thei uh hiam?

records.english: Who helped you?

records.english: How did you find the courage to tell your parents that you wanted to study music?
records.zomi: La sinna sin na deih hi, cih na nu leh pa gen nadingin hangsanna bangci na ngah hiam?

records.english: Was it hard to speak up?

records.english: Answers about overcoming fear often describe small steps rather than sudden change.
records.zomi: Lauhna zawhna tawh kisai dawnna te in thakhat-a kikhekna sangin khebai neu te a gen zel uh hi.

records.english: Were you hurt?
records.zomi: Na liam hiam?

records.english: Questions about regret show that courage sometimes comes at a personal cost.

records.english: Were you scared when you jumped into the river to save the boy?

records.english: How did you stay calm?
records.zomi: Bangci na lungnuam den hiam?

records.english: Would you take the same risk again?

records.zomi: Galkap a nusiat thukhensatna na pa in bangci a hilhcian hiam?

records.english: Were you afraid?

records.english: Moral courage at work can be harder to explain than physical bravery.

records.english: Did you get a medal?

records.english: What did you say to yourself just before you walked onto the stage?

records.english: Then I remembered the day I told my boss that I wouldn't sign a report I knew was false.

records.english: My son listened carefully and said that sounded braver than anything in his comic books.

records.english: How did you find the courage to stand up to the bully?
records.zomi: Mi hiamgam langdo nadingin hangsanna bangci na ngah hiam?

records.english: Children who hear honest answers about fear learn that bravery is possible for everyone.

records.english: How did you learn to swim after being so frightened of water?

records.english: How did your grandmother keep the family going during the war?

records.english: Talking about courage encourages communities to support those who speak up.
records.zomi: Hangsanna tawh kisai kikum in khuasung te a gen mite a huh dingin a hanthawn hi.

records.english: Questions about courage often reveal that brave people felt deeply afraid.
records.zomi: Hangsanna tawh kisai dotna te in hangsan mite in a thuk mahmah-in a lau uh hi, cih a lak zel hi.

records.english: Whose recommendation brought you to this town in the first place?

records.english: Hearing how elders weighed different advice can help young people make careful choices.
records.zomi: Upa te in thuhilhna tuamtuam bangci a khaisak uh hiam cih zak in khangno te kidawm taka teelna a bawl nadingin a huh thei hi.

records.english: Who told you about this job?
records.zomi: Hih nasep tawh kisai kua in hong gen hiam?

records.english: A recommendation that changed one person's life can echo through several generations.
records.zomi: Mi khat' nuntakna a khek thuhilhna khat in khang tampi-ah a ging kik thei hi.

records.english: Some of the best advice older people received came from people outside their families.
records.zomi: Upa te' ngah thuhilhna hoih pen pawlkhat pen a innkuan uh pua-a mite pan a hong pai hi.

records.english: Which relative persuaded you to take the job abroad?
records.zomi: Gamdang-a nasep na lak dingin koi sanggam in hong thuhilh zo hiam?

records.english: Who recommended this house to you?
records.zomi: Hih inn kua in hong gen hiam?

records.english: Did the village elders recommend the land where the new school was built?
records.zomi: Sang thak kilam lei pen khua upa te in a gen uh hiam?

records.english: When my father was young, he asked the village blacksmith what trade he should learn.
records.zomi: Ka pa a khangno lai-in, khua sik sekmi kiangah bang siamna ka sin ding hiam, ci-in a dong hi.

records.english: The blacksmith told him that people would always need their bicycles mended, and he lent him tools to practise with.
records.zomi: Sik sekmi in mite in a siiksakol uh bawlphat ding a kisam den ding uh hi, ci-in a gen a, kisin dingin nasep van te a leitawi hi.

records.english: My father opened a bicycle shop ten years later, and it still bears the blacksmith's name over the door.
records.zomi: Kum sawm khit-in ka pa in siiksakol zuakna inn khat a hong a, tu dong kongpi tung-ah sik sekmi' min a om lai hi.

records.english: Older people often remember the advice that shaped their lives more clearly than the details.
records.zomi: Upa te in thu neu te sangin a nuntakna uh a bawl thuhilhna te a kician zaw-in a phawk zel uh hi.

records.english: Did you ever regret taking your brother's advice about the house?
records.zomi: Inn tawh kisai na unau pa' thuhilhna na zuih manin na kisik ngei hiam?

records.english: Did your aunt advise you to go back to school after the children were born?
records.zomi: Na ta te a suah khit-in na ni in sang-ah ciah kik dingin hong thuhilh hiam?

records.english: Recommendations passed down through generations can become part of a family's identity.
records.zomi: Khang tampi tungtawn-a kilak thuhilhna te in innkuan khat' mimal omzia khen khat a suak thei hi.

records.english: Why did your parents follow the priest's advice to send you to the city school?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na nu leh pa in khuapi sang-ah hong khak dingin siampi' thuhilhna a zui uh hiam?

records.english: He told them I was clever enough to win a scholarship, and they trusted him more than anyone.
records.zomi: Sangkah sum huhna ngah zo dingin ka pil hi, ci-in a gen a, mi khempeuh sangin amah a muang zaw uh hi.

records.english: Who told you to buy that field?
records.zomi: Tua lo lei dingin kua in hong gen hiam?

records.english: Remembering who gave good advice keeps gratitude alive within families and communities.
records.zomi: Kua in thuhilhna hoih a pia hiam cih phawk in innkuan leh khuasung te sungah lungdamna a nungta-in a kem hi.

records.english: Did anyone warn you about the winter?
records.zomi: Khuaphal tawh kisai kuamah in hong pulak hiam?

records.english: Did anyone advise you not to leave?
records.zomi: Pai lo dingin kuamah in hong thuhilh hiam?

records.english: Questions about past recommendations show how communities shared knowledge before the internet.
records.zomi: Nidang thuhilhna te tawh kisai dotna te in internet om ma-in khuasung te in theihna bangci a kihawm uh hiam cih a lak hi.

records.english: Why did you ignore your father's advice about the business?
records.zomi: Bang hangin sumbawlna tawh kisai na pa' thuhilhna na limsak kei hiam?

records.english: Did your teacher advise you to go to college?
records.zomi: Na sangsia in college kah dingin hong thuhilh hiam?

records.english: Who told you about the scholarship?
records.zomi: Sangkah sum huhna tawh kisai kua in hong gen hiam?

records.english: Who recommended the midwife who delivered all of your children?
records.zomi: Na ta khempeuh a pusak nau pusak mi kua in hong gen hiam?

records.english: Did the old shopkeeper really recommend that you start your own stall?
records.zomi: Zuakna inn lui neipa in nangmah' zuakna dawhkan kipatsak dingin hong thuhilh taktak hiam?

records.english: Did your teacher really recommend that you become a writer?
records.zomi: Na sangsia in laigelhmi suak dingin hong thuhilh taktak hiam?

records.english: Who suggested you move to the city?
records.zomi: Khuapi-ah suan dingin kua in hong gen hiam?

records.english: Did the teacher recommend any books?
records.zomi: Sangsia in laibu khat peuhpeuh a gen hiam?

records.english: Did the neighbours recommend a builder?
records.zomi: Inn kiang mite in inn lam mi khat a gen uh hiam?

records.english: Asking who recommended a past decision often reveals a hidden mentor in a family's story.
records.zomi: Nidang thukhensatna khat kua in a thuhilh hiam cih dot in innkuan tangthu-ah kisel lamlakmi khat a lak zel hi.

records.english: Who recommended the boat for the journey?
records.zomi: Khualzinna adingin long kua in a gen hiam?

records.english: Many life-changing choices began with a single recommendation from a trusted neighbour.
records.zomi: Nuntakna khek teelna tampi pen inn kiang mi muanhuai khat' thuhilhna khat bek pan a kipan hi.

records.english: Did your father advise you to marry young?
records.zomi: Na pa in na neu lai-in kiten dingin hong thuhilh hiam?

records.english: Recommendations from village elders once carried as much weight as official information.
records.zomi: Nidang-in khua upa te' thuhilhna te in kumpi thu te bangin gikna a nei uh hi.

records.english: Who told your family which crops would grow best on the hillside?
records.zomi: Mual ka-ah koi lo gah te a khang hoih pen ding hiam cih na innkuan kua in a gen hiam?

records.english: Did your parents follow the doctor's advice about where to raise the children?
records.zomi: Ta te koi-ah khawi ding hiam cih tawh kisai siavuan' thuhilhna na nu leh pa in a zui uh hiam?

records.english: Did anyone suggest a different route before you set off across the mountains?
records.zomi: Mual te na tan dingin na kipat ma-in kuamah in lampi dang khat a gen hiam?

records.english: Family stories about good advice often include tales of advice that was ignored.
records.zomi: Thuhilhna hoih tawh kisai innkuan tangthu te in kilimsak lo thuhilhna tangthu te zong a kihel zel hi.

records.english: Which doctor did the village recommend when you were ill as a child?
records.zomi: Na neu lai-in na cidam loh ciangin khua in koi siavuan a gen uh hiam?

records.english: An old man in the next valley who made medicines from plants.
records.zomi: A kiang guam-a singkung te pan damdawi a bawl pasal upa khat.

records.english: Who recommended the doctor you went to?
records.zomi: Na kan siavuan kua in a gen hiam?

records.english: Did anyone advise your grandparents against moving to the coast?
records.zomi: Tuipi gei-ah suan lo dingin kuamah in na pu leh pi te a thuhilh hiam?

records.english: Whose recommendation finally persuaded the family to leave the island?
records.zomi: Kua' thuhilhna in a tawp-in innkuan tuikulh a nusiat dingin a thuhilh zo hiam?

records.english: A cousin who had already settled on the mainland wrote that there was work, schools and a doctor within walking distance.
records.zomi: Gam lian-ah a teng khin sanggam khat in nasep, sang leh khe tawh pai theih dong-ah siavuan khat a om hi, ci-in lai a gelh hi.

records.english: Did Grandma suggest that name for me?
records.zomi: Pi in hih min kei adingin a gen hiam?

records.english: Who suggested this church for the wedding?
records.zomi: Mopawi adingin hih biakinn kua in a gen hiam?

records.english: Did anyone advise you to study nursing?
records.zomi: Nurse sinna sin dingin kuamah in hong thuhilh hiam?

records.english: My aunt did, after she saw how calmly I looked after my little brother when he broke his arm.
records.zomi: Ka ni in, ka nau pa' ban a tan ciangin lungnuam takin amah ka kem a muh khit-in.

records.english: Did your friends recommend the factory?
records.zomi: Na lawm te in factory a gen uh hiam?

records.english: Whose advice did you follow when you chose your first car?
records.zomi: Na mawtaw masa pen na teel ciangin kua' thuhilhna na zui hiam?

records.english: Who told Grandpa to apply for the job at the railway?
records.zomi: Meileng lampi-ah nasep ngen dingin Pu kua in a gen hiam?

records.english: His uncle, who said the railway would still be there long after the farms had gone.
records.zomi: A pa neu, lo te a bei khit sawt-in zong meileng lampi a om lai ding hi, a ci pa.

records.english: Who suggested you open a shop?
records.zomi: Zuakna inn hong dingin kua in hong gen hiam?

records.english: Who suggested that the family keep its savings in the bank rather than under the bed?
records.zomi: Innkuan in a kem sum uh lupna nuai sangin bank-ah koih dingin kua in a gen hiam?

records.english: Who told you to plant the apple trees?
records.zomi: Apple kung te suan dingin kua in hong gen hiam?

records.english: Did Grandpa ever give you advice about money?
records.zomi: Pu in sum tawh kisai thuhilhna khat peuhpeuh hong pia ngei hiam?

records.english: Did your mother suggest you learn to sew?
records.zomi: Na nu in puan khui sin dingin hong gen hiam?

records.english: Asking whose advice a relative followed helps younger people understand their choices.
records.zomi: Sanggam khat in kua' thuhilhna a zui hiam cih dot in khangno te in a teelna uh a theisiam nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Offering paper forms alongside online versions protects people without internet access.
records.zomi: Online lai lak te tawh lai tung-a lai lak te zong pia in internet nei lo mite a kemcing hi.

records.english: In our town, the library will print and scan forms for free.
records.zomi: I khuapi-ah, laibu inn in lai lak te man om lo-in a print a, a scan sak hi.

records.english: The library has copies of the form.
records.zomi: Laibu inn in lai lak' a kisuaktawm te a nei hi.

records.english: Simple, clear forms reduce mistakes and save time for both residents and officials.
records.zomi: A baih, a kician lai lak te in khialhna te a kiam sak a, a sung-a teng mite leh kumpi nasemte a nih' hun a kem sak hi.

records.english: Translated forms help newcomers deal with public services more confidently.
records.zomi: Kilet lai lak te in hong tung thak te mipi nasep te tawh hang zaw-in a kisai nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: After the council simplified its housing form, far fewer applications were returned.
records.zomi: Council in a inn ngetna lai lak a baih zaw sak khit-in, ngetna tawm mahmah zaw a kikhak kik hi.

records.english: Where can I get a paper copy of the parking permit form?
records.zomi: Mawtaw khawlna phalna lai lak' lai tung-a khat koi-ah ka ngah thei ding hiam?

records.english: At the council office reception, or the library can print one for you.
records.zomi: Council office dawnna mun-ah, ahih kei leh laibu inn in khat hong print sak thei hi.

records.english: Large-print and accessible forms allow more residents to complete them independently.
records.zomi: Laimal lian leh zat baih lai lak te in a sung-a teng mite tam zaw in amau mahmah-in a dim thei nadingin a phal hi.

records.english: What happens if I make a mistake on the benefits form?
records.zomi: Kumpi huhna lai lak-ah khialhna khat ka bawl leh bang a piang ding hiam?

records.english: Ring the office as soon as you notice, because they can usually correct it before your payment is affected.
records.zomi: Na phawk pakin office sam in, bang hang hiam cih leh na sum ngah a kikhoih ma-in a bawlphat thei zel uh hi.

records.english: Should I book a time with the adviser?
records.zomi: Thuhilhmi tawh hun khat ka ngetsak ding hiam?

records.english: The council now sends a text message to confirm that it has received each form.
records.zomi: Tu-in council in lai lak khat ciat a ngah hi, cih kician sak dingin text khat a khak hi.

records.english: Is there a form for reporting a change of address?
records.zomi: Tenna mun kikhekna gen nading lai lak khat a om hiam?

records.english: Yes, you can fill it in online or pick one up at the town hall.
records.zomi: Om hi, online-ah na dim thei a, ahih kei leh khuapi office lian-ah khat na la thei hi.

records.english: Community help with forms ensures that residents receive the services they are entitled to.
records.zomi: Lai lak tawh khuasung huhna in a sung-a teng mite in a ngah thei nasep te a ngah nadingin a kician sak hi.

records.english: I've lost my reference number.
records.zomi: Ka nambat ka mansuah hi.

records.english: Why does the council need proof of address when I've lived here for twenty years?
records.zomi: Hih mun-ah kum sawm nih ka teeng khin hang bang hangin council in tenna lahna a kisam hiam?

records.english: Can I take a photo of the form?
records.zomi: Lai lak' photo khat ka la thei ding hiam?

records.english: Explaining which documents are needed in advance prevents many delays.
records.zomi: Koi lai te kisam hiam cih a ma-in hilhcian in hun nunna tampi a kham hi.

records.english: The town hall offers a quiet room where residents can fill in forms with an adviser.
records.zomi: Khuapi office lian in a sung-a teng mite thuhilhmi tawh lai lak a dim theih nadingin inndan dai khat a pia hi.

records.english: Can I post the form instead?
records.zomi: A sangin lai lak lai tawh ka khak thei ding hiam?

records.english: The form needs two signatures.
records.zomi: Lai lak in min gelhna nih a kisam hi.

records.english: Can my son fill it in for me?
records.zomi: Ka tapa in kei adingin a dim thei ding hiam?

records.english: The community centre runs a weekly session to help residents complete government forms.
records.zomi: Khuasung inn lian in a sung-a teng mite kumpi lai lak te a dim nadingin kal simin huhna hun khat a bawl hi.

records.english: Is it possible to get help with the form over the phone if I can't come in?
records.zomi: Ka hong pai theih kei leh phone tawh lai lak-ah huhna ngah theih ding a om hiam?

records.english: Confirmation messages reassure residents that their forms have been received.
records.zomi: Kician sakna thukhakna te in a sung-a teng mite a lai lak uh a kingah hi, cih a lungmuan sak hi.

records.english: Do you have a pen I can use?
records.zomi: Ka zat theih khedawi khat na nei hiam?

records.english: The volunteer translated each question for my father and wrote down his answers on the form.
records.zomi: Thalawp in ka pa adingin dotna khat ciat a let a, a dawnna te lai lak tung-ah a gelh hi.

records.english: Is there anyone who helps with council forms at the library?
records.zomi: Laibu inn-ah council lai lak te-ah a huh mi khat a om hiam?

records.english: Yes, a volunteer is there every Tuesday morning to help with council forms.
records.zomi: Om hi, council lai lak te-ah huh dingin Pithai ni zingsang simin thalawp khat a om hi.

records.english: The adviser leaves at half past four.
records.zomi: Thuhilhmi pen nai li leh a lang-in a pai hi.

records.english: Is there a large-print version?
records.zomi: Laimal lian-a kigelh khat a om hiam?

records.english: Mistakes on forms are common, so offices should make corrections easy.
records.zomi: Lai lak-a khialhna te a tangpi ahih manin, office te in bawlphatna te a baih sak ding uh hi.

records.english: Could the council send the form in my mother's language?
records.zomi: Council in ka nu' pau-in lai lak a khak thei ding hiam?

records.english: Libraries and community centres have become important places for help with official paperwork.
records.zomi: Laibu inn te leh khuasung inn lian te pen kumpi lai te-ah huhna ngahna mun thupi te a suak khin uh hi.

records.english: When will I hear back?
records.zomi: Bang hun-in dawnna ka ngah ding hiam?

records.english: The reception desk has the forms.
records.zomi: Dawnna dawhkan-ah lai lak te a om hi.

records.english: Consulting residents when designing forms makes them easier to understand.
records.zomi: Lai lak te a bawl ciangin a sung-a teng mite dot in a theisiam baih zaw sak hi.

records.english: Our residents' association made a simple guide to the forms most people need.
records.zomi: I a sung-a teng mite' pawl in mi tampi in a kisam lai lak te tawh kisai lamlakna baih khat a bawl hi.

records.english: The form is in three languages.
records.zomi: Lai lak pen pau thum-in a kigelh hi.

records.english: The form asks for my bank details.
records.zomi: Lai lak in ka bank thu te a ngen hi.

records.english: Can I complete the form at home?
records.zomi: Inn-ah lai lak ka dim thei ding hiam?

records.english: The job centre helped me complete the online form when the website kept crashing.
records.zomi: Website a sia den ciangin nasep zonna mun in online lai lak ka dim nadingin hong huh hi.

records.english: Is there a desk where I can write?
records.zomi: Ka gelh theih nading dawhkan khat a om hiam?

records.english: The advice worker explained which documents I needed to attach before I sent the form.
records.zomi: Lai lak ka khak ma-in koi lai te ka belap ding a kisam hiam cih thuhilhna nasem in a hilhcian hi.

records.english: Volunteers who help with forms often notice when residents are missing out on support.
records.zomi: Lai lak te-ah a huh thalawp te in a sung-a teng mite in huhna a mansuah ciangin a phawk zel uh hi.

records.english: Why did the council redesign its forms after consulting residents?
records.zomi: A sung-a teng mite a dot khit-in bang hangin council in a lai lak te a bawlthak hiam?

records.english: Many people found the old forms confusing, so the council used simpler questions and added examples of how to answer.
records.zomi: Mi tampi in lai lak lui te a lungbuai sa uh ahih manin, council in dotna baih zaw te a zang a, bangci dawng ding hiam cih ettehna te a belap hi.

records.english: The volunteer helped me with my form.
records.zomi: Thalawp in ka lai lak-ah hong huh hi.

records.english: How long should I wait before contacting the office if I haven't received a reply?
records.zomi: Dawnna ka ngah kei leh office ka sam ma-in hun bangzah ka ngak ding hiam?

records.english: Could someone check my form before I post it, so that it isn't sent back?
records.zomi: A kikhak kik loh nadingin ka khak ma-in mi khat in ka lai lak a en thei ding hiam?

records.english: Question seven on the form confuses me.
records.zomi: Lai lak tung-a dotna sagihna in hong lungbuai sak hi.

records.english: Good public services judge forms by how easily ordinary people can complete them.
records.zomi: Mipi nasep hoih te in mi tangpi te in bangzah a baih-in a dim thei uh hiam cih tawh lai lak te a khensat uh hi.

records.english: Why do so many forms ask for the same information on different pages?
records.zomi: Bang hangin lai lak tampi in lai tuamtuam-ah thu kibang a ngen hiam?

records.english: Where do I hand in the form?
records.zomi: Lai lak koi-ah ka ap ding hiam?

records.english: When my neighbour received a twelve-page form about her pension, she put it in a drawer and tried to forget it.
records.zomi: Ka inn kiang nu in a pension tawh kisai lai sawm leh nih lai lak khat a ngah ciangin, dawhkan ip sungah a koih a, a mangngilh dingin a hanciam hi.

records.english: A volunteer at the community centre went through it with her, one page at a time, over two afternoons.
records.zomi: Khuasung inn lian-a thalawp khat in nitak nih sung lai khat ciat-in amah tawh a en khawm uh hi.

records.english: A month later, she received the extra payment she had been entitled to for years.
records.zomi: Kha khat khit-in, kum tampi sung a ngah thei sum behlap a ngah hi.

records.english: The advice centre checks forms for free.
records.zomi: Thuhilhna mun in man om lo-in lai lak te a en hi.

records.english: Regions that lose a major employer often need new ideas to recover.
records.zomi: Nasep nei lian khat a mansuah gam mun te in a hoih kik nadingin ngaihsutna thak te a kisam zel uh hi.

records.english: Find the capital city first.
records.zomi: A masa-in gam khuapi lian zong in.

records.english: How did the coastal region protect its towns from rising sea levels?
records.zomi: Tuipi gei gam mun in tuipi kah semsem pan a khuapi te bangci a kemcing hiam?

records.english: Let's use the globe instead.
records.zomi: A sangin globe i zang ding uh.

records.english: When our class couldn't agree on the size of two countries, we compared them on a globe instead of a flat map.
records.zomi: I tanglai in gam nih' lianzah-ah a kituak theih kei uh ciangin, gam lim pheh sangin globe tung-ah i kikteh uh hi.

records.english: After visiting the region, the students understood why its farmers grow tea instead of rice.
records.zomi: Gam mun a kan khit-in, bang hangin a lo neimi te in buh sangin lakphak a suan uh hiam cih sangnaupang te in a theisiam uh hi.

records.english: This border has changed.
records.zomi: Hih gam ciang a kikhek khin hi.

records.english: Our teacher showed us that old maps can make some countries look much bigger than they really are.
records.zomi: Gam lim lui te in gam pawlkhat a taktak sangin a lian zaw mahmah bang a kilang sak thei hi, ci-in i sangsia in hong lak hi.

records.english: My cousin's village solved its water shortage by building tanks to collect rain from the roofs.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam' khua in inn tung pan guahtui kaikhawm nadingin tui bawm lian te lam-in a tui kisapna a phel hi.

records.english: Coastal regions face growing challenges from storms and rising seas.
records.zomi: Tuipi gei gam mun te in huihpi leh tuipi kah te pan haksatna a khang semsem a tuak uh hi.

records.english: How can farmers in a dry region grow enough food?
records.zomi: Gam mun keu khat-a lo neimi te in an kicing bangci a suan thei uh hiam?

records.english: They can collect rainwater, choose crops that need little water and use drip irrigation.
records.zomi: Guahtui a kaikhawm thei uh a, tui tawm kisam lo gah te a teel thei uh a, tui zuk neu-in tui buakna a zang thei uh hi.

records.english: How can a mountain region with few roads attract more visitors?
records.zomi: Lampi tawm nei mual gam mun khat in kanmi tam zaw bangci a la thei ding hiam?

records.english: Solving regional problems requires understanding both geography and the people who live there.
records.zomi: Gam mun buaina te phel in gam omzia leh a sung-a teng mite a nih theisiamna a kisam hi.

records.english: Is that country in Asia or in Africa?
records.zomi: Tua gam Asia-ah a om hiam, Africa-ah?

records.english: Remote regions need good transport and schools to keep young people from leaving.
records.zomi: Gamla gam mun te in khangno te a pai khiat loh nadingin khualzinna hoih leh sang te a kisam uh hi.

records.english: Many difficulties in learning geography come from relying on a single map.
records.zomi: Gam omzia sinna-a haksatna tampi pen gam lim khat bek a kinga pan a hong pai hi.

records.english: Learning one distinctive fact about each country helps learners avoid confusing them.
records.zomi: Gam khat ciat tawh kisai thu tuam khat sin in sinmi te a kilamdang khial loh nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Count the countries in Africa.
records.zomi: Africa-a gam te sim in.

records.english: Classmates from different regions can bring geography lessons to life.
records.zomi: Gam mun tuamtuam pan sang lawm te in gam omzia sinna te a nungta sak thei uh hi.

records.english: The map is too small.
records.zomi: Gam lim a neu lua hi.

records.english: Shared rivers require agreements between the countries that depend on them.
records.zomi: Kihawm luipi te in a kinga gam te kikal-ah kithukimna te a kisam hi.

records.english: Let's colour each country.
