records.zomi: A gamtatna uh adingin mawhpuakna a la mite in zahtakna kip a ngah zel uh hi.

records.english: Why did you offer to look after the shop when the owner was ill?
records.zomi: Neitu a cidam loh ciangin bang hangin zuakna inn kem dingin na gen hiam?

records.english: Did you return the library book?
records.zomi: Laibu inn laibu na ap kik hiam?

records.english: Who left the tap running?
records.zomi: Tuikhau kua in a hong-in a nusia hiam?

records.english: Is it fair to make the eldest child responsible for the younger ones?
records.zomi: Ta upa pen a neu zaw te tungah mawhpuakna a la dingin bawl a dik hiam?

records.english: Did you lock the gate?
records.zomi: Kongpi na khak hiam?

records.english: Questions about responsibility often reveal how people were raised.
records.zomi: Mawhpuakna tawh kisai dotna te in mite bangci a kikhawi uh hiam cih a lak zel hi.

records.english: How can a teacher help pupils take responsibility for their own learning?
records.zomi: Sangsia khat in sangnaupang te a sinna uh tungah mawhpuakna a lak nadingin bangci a huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: What would you do if you damaged something you had borrowed?
records.zomi: Na leitawi khat peuhpeuh na susiat leh bang na bawl ding hiam?

records.english: What did you learn when you were left in charge for the first time?
records.zomi: A masa pen vei-in mawhpuakna kipia na hih ciangin bang na sin hiam?

records.english: Answers about community duties remind people that public spaces belong to everyone.
records.zomi: Khuasung mawhpuakna te tawh kisai dawnna te in mipi mun te pen mi khempeuh a neih ahi hi, cih mite a phawksak hi.

records.english: Should children be given chores from an early age?
records.zomi: Naupang te a neu lai-in inn nasep kipia ding hiam?

records.english: Who's in charge today?
records.zomi: Tuni-in kua in a makai hiam?

records.english: Why did you pay for the window you broke?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na khiat tawlet man na pia hiam?

records.english: It was my ball that broke it, so it was my job to put it right.
records.zomi: Tua a khiat pen ka ball ahih manin, a bawlphat ding pen ka nasep ahi hi.

records.english: Did you water the plants?
records.zomi: Singkung neu te tui na buak hiam?

records.english: Questions about mistakes can teach that responsibility includes putting things right.
records.zomi: Khialhna te tawh kisai dotna te in mawhpuakna in thu te a bawlphat zong a huam hi, cih a sinsak thei hi.

records.english: Who promised to buy the bread?
records.zomi: Moh lei dingin kua in a ciam hiam?

records.english: Can I trust you with the key?
records.zomi: Tawh kong muang thei ding hiam?

records.english: Answers about caring for younger siblings show how early some people take on responsibility.
records.zomi: Unau neu zaw kemna tawh kisai dawnna te in mi pawlkhat bangzah a ma-in mawhpuakna a la uh hiam cih a lak hi.

records.english: Can you walk the dog tonight?
records.zomi: Tuni zan-in ui na paipih thei ding hiam?

records.english: Who cared for your little brothers while your parents were in the fields?
records.zomi: Na nu leh pa lo-ah a om lai-un na unau pa neu te kua in a kem hiam?

records.english: I did, because I was the eldest, even though I was only ten.
records.zomi: Kei in, ka upa pen ahih manin, kum sawm bek ka hih hang.

records.english: How can neighbours share responsibility for keeping the street clean?
records.zomi: Inn kiang mite in lampi siang taka kem nading mawhpuakna bangci a hawm thei uh hiam?

records.english: How did it feel when your parents finally trusted you with the car?
records.zomi: A tawp-in na nu leh pa in mawtaw tawh hong muan ciangin bangci na kizak hiam?

records.english: Did you finish your chores?
records.zomi: Na inn nasep te na zo hiam?

records.english: What made you decide to admit the mistake before anyone noticed it?
records.zomi: Kuamah in a phawk ma-in khialhna pulak dingin bang in hong khensat sak hiam?

records.english: What should happen if a volunteer forgets an important task?
records.zomi: Thalawp khat in nasep thupi khat a mangngilh leh bang a piang ding hiam?

records.english: Did you remember to feed the neighbour's cat?
records.zomi: Inn kiang mi' zawhngeu an vak ding na phawk hiam?

records.english: Yes, twice a day, and I wrote down when I did it.
records.zomi: Phawk hi, ni khat-ah vei nih, ka bawl ciang khempeuh ka gelh hi.

records.english: Answers about accepting blame show that honesty strengthens trust.
records.zomi: Mawhna sanna tawh kisai dawnna te in thumanna in upna a hat sak hi, cih a lak hi.

records.english: Asking children about their chores helps them see their part in the family.
records.zomi: Naupang te a inn nasep uh tawh kisai dot in innkuan sung-a a khen uh a muh nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Will you remember to call Grandma?
records.zomi: Pi sam ding na phawk ding hiam?

records.english: When I was fourteen, my mother went into hospital for a month, and I was left in charge of my two little brothers.
records.zomi: Kum sawm leh li ka phak ciangin, ka nu kha khat sung damlo inn-ah a om a, ka unau pa neu nih kem dingin keimah ka kinusia hi.

records.english: I cooked their meals, checked their homework and walked them to school every morning before my own lessons.
records.zomi: A an uh ka huan a, a inn nasep uh ka en a, keimah' sinna ma-in zingsang simin sang-ah ka paipih hi.

records.english: When my mother came home, she said nothing, but she hugged me for a long time in the doorway.
records.zomi: Ka nu inn-ah a ciah ciangin, bangmah a gen kei hi, ahi zongin kongpi-ah sawt mahmah hong pom hi.

records.english: Why did your grandfather insist that every promise must be kept?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na pu in kamciam khempeuh kem ding hi, ci-in a gen den hiam?

records.english: Whose turn is it to wash up?
records.zomi: An kuang sil ding kua' a hun ahi hiam?

records.english: Will you look after your sister?
records.zomi: Na sanggam nu na kem ding hiam?

records.english: Asking why someone took responsibility can reveal deep personal values.
records.zomi: Bang hangin mi khat in mawhpuakna a la hiam cih dot in mimal ngeina hoih thuk te a lak thei hi.

records.english: Did you put the tools away?
records.zomi: Nasep van te na koih kik hiam?

records.english: Who in your family taught you the most about responsibility?
records.zomi: Na innkuan sungah kua in mawhpuakna tawh kisai tam pen hong sinsak hiam?

records.english: How did your parents teach you to be responsible with money?
records.zomi: Na nu leh pa in sum tawh mawhpuakna nei dingin bangci hong sinsak uh hiam?

records.english: Can the children use our language in their school projects?
records.zomi: Naupang te in a sang project uh-ah i pau a zang thei uh hiam?

records.english: Yes, the teacher said they can include it as long as they explain it to the class.
records.zomi: Thei hi, tanglai kiangah a hilhcian leh a kihel thei hi, ci-in sangsia in a gen hi.

records.english: Universities can help by offering courses and resources for minority languages.
records.zomi: University te in mi tawm pau te adingin sinna leh van te pia-in a huh thei uh hi.

records.english: At the factory, the Zomi workers started a notice board with news in our language.
records.zomi: Factory-ah, Zomi nasemte in i pau-a thuthak a koih laimal khaina khat a kipatsak uh hi.

records.english: Our teacher has a Zomi dictionary.
records.zomi: I sangsia in Zomi kammal laibu khat a nei hi.

records.english: Language clubs give children a place to use their language with friends.
records.zomi: Pau pawl te in naupang te a lawm te uh tawh a pau uh a zat nading mun khat a pia hi.

records.english: My boss asked me to translate a notice.
records.zomi: Ka makaipa in thugenna khat let dingin hong ngen hi.

records.english: Teachers who learn a few phrases of pupils' languages build trust with families.
records.zomi: Sangnaupang te' pau-a genna tawm khat a sin sangsia te in innkuan te tawh upna a lam uh hi.

records.english: Why do you record the elders at work during your lunch break?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na sun an hun-in nasep-ah upa te na ciamteh hiam?

records.english: Several of them know old stories that nobody else remembers, and I want to save them.
records.zomi: Amau tampi in kuamah in a phawk nawn loh tangthu lui te a thei uh a, kem ka deih hi.

records.english: Shall we speak our language at lunch today?
records.zomi: Tuni sun an-ah i pau i gen ding uh hiam?

records.english: Why do so many young people stop using our language once they start working?
records.zomi: Bang hangin khangno tampi in nasep a sep kipat uh ciangin i pau a zang nawn kei uh hiam?

records.english: Do you speak our language at work?
records.zomi: Nasep-ah i pau na gen hiam?

records.english: My manager asked how to greet our visitors.
records.zomi: Ka manager in i kanmi te bangci cibai buk ding hiam cih a dong hi.

records.english: We sing in our language at assemblies.
records.zomi: Kikhopna te-ah i pau-in la i sa uh hi.

records.english: Can the club meet in the classroom?
records.zomi: Pawl in tanglai inndan-ah a kikhawm thei ding hiam?

records.english: I practise reading on the bus to work.
records.zomi: Nasep-ah paina bus tung-ah laisim ka kisin hi.

records.english: How does your company help Zomi staff keep their language?
records.zomi: Na company in Zomi nasemte a pau uh a kem nadingin bangci a huh hiam?

records.english: It lets us form a lunchtime language circle and print some notices in our language for the newer workers.
records.zomi: Sun an hun-a pau kikhawmna pawl khat bawl dingin hong phal a, nasem thak zaw te adingin i pau-in thugenna pawlkhat a print hi.

records.english: When the clinic needed an interpreter, they asked me to help a Zomi patient.
records.zomi: Damdawi inn neu in pau lettu khat a kisap ciangin, Zomi damlo khat huh dingin hong ngen uh hi.

records.english: My colleague and I practise our language during our coffee break.
records.zomi: Ka nasep lawm leh kei coffee dawn hun-in i pau i kisin uh hi.

records.english: My colleague is learning our language too.
records.zomi: Ka nasep lawm in zong i pau a sin hi.

records.english: The students made a video in our language.
records.zomi: Sangnaupang te in i pau-in video khat a bawl uh hi.

records.english: My manager was surprised that I could speak three languages fluently.
records.zomi: Pau thum ka gen siam mahmah ahih manin ka manager a lamdang sa hi.

records.english: When my daughter's school asked pupils to bring something from home for a culture day, she chose her grandmother's songbook.
records.zomi: Ka tanu' sang in ngeina ni adingin sangnaupang te inn pan khat peuhpeuh paipih dingin a ngen ciangin, a pi' la laibu a teel hi.

records.english: She practised one song in our language for a week and sang it in front of the whole school.
records.zomi: Kal khat sung i pau-in la khat a kisin a, sang khempeuh ma-ah a sa hi.

records.english: Afterwards, three other Zomi children asked the teacher whether they could start a singing group.
records.zomi: A nung-in, Zomi naupang dang thum in la sa pawl khat a kipatsak thei ding uh hiam, ci-in sangsia a dong uh hi.

records.english: My teacher asked me to teach the class a song.
records.zomi: Ka sangsia in tanglai kiangah la khat sinsak dingin hong ngen hi.

records.english: Bilingual workers are valuable to employers and to their communities.
records.zomi: Pau nih gen thei nasemte pen nasep nei te leh a khuasung uh adingin a manpha uh hi.

records.english: The children wrote a play in our language.
records.zomi: Naupang te in i pau-in lim bawl tangthu khat a gelh uh hi.

records.english: Could the school let our language club use the library on Friday afternoons?
records.zomi: Sang in Laithai ni nitak lam-in i pau pawl in laibu inn a zang dingin a phal thei ding hiam?

records.english: Can we record the elders this Sunday?
records.zomi: Hih Nipini-in upa te i ciamteh thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: Preserving a language requires support from homes, schools and workplaces together.
records.zomi: Pau khat kemcing in inn, sang leh nasepna mun te khawm taka huhna a kisam hi.

records.english: My cousin teaches our language online.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam in online-ah i pau a hilh hi.

records.english: At work, I help newer colleagues from our community fill in forms in the local language.
records.zomi: Nasep-ah, i khuasung pan nasep lawm thak zaw te khuasung pau-in lai lak a dim nadingin ka huh hi.

records.english: My friend wants to learn our songs.
records.zomi: Ka lawm in i la te sin a deih hi.

records.english: The students recorded their grandparents explaining old farming words.
records.zomi: Sangnaupang te in a pu leh pi te uh lo nasep kammal lui te a hilhcian a ciamteh uh hi.

records.english: Why did the university agree to host a course on the Zomi language?
records.zomi: Bang hangin university in Zomi pau sinna khat a bawl dingin a phal hiam?

records.english: Zomi students and teachers showed that there were enough learners and offered to help prepare the materials themselves.
records.zomi: Zomi sangnaupang leh sangsia te in sinmi a kicing a om hi, cih a lak uh a, sinna van te amau mahmah in bawl dingin a gen uh hi.

records.english: Does your school teach our language?
records.zomi: Na sang in i pau a hilh hiam?

records.english: Not during lessons, but there's a club on Wednesday afternoons run by a parent.
records.zomi: Sinna lai-in hi lo hi, ahi zongin Nilai ni nitak lam-in nu ahih kei leh pa khat in a makai pawl khat a om hi.

records.english: My son reads Zomi stories to his class.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in a tanglai kiangah Zomi tangthu te a sim sak hi.

records.english: Schools that welcome home languages help children feel proud of their heritage.
records.zomi: Inn pau te a dawn sang te in naupang te a ngeina uh tungah a kipak nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Workplaces can support language preservation by allowing informal language groups.
records.zomi: Nasepna mun te in pau pawl tangpi te phal-in pau kemcing nading a huh thei uh hi.

records.english: The school invited a Zomi storyteller.
records.zomi: Sang in Zomi tangthu genmi khat a sam hi.

records.english: Our church asked young professionals to teach weekend classes for the children.
records.zomi: I biakinn in khangno siam mi te naupang te adingin kal tawp sinna te hilh dingin a ngen hi.

records.english: My son was proud when his teacher learned to say good morning in our language.
records.zomi: A sangsia in i pau-in zingsang hoih cih gen a sin ciangin ka tapa a kipak hi.

records.english: The language club made a short dictionary of school words for younger pupils.
records.zomi: Pau pawl in sangnaupang neu zaw te adingin sang kammal te' kammal laibu tom khat a bawl hi.

records.english: My teacher encouraged me to write about our language for the school magazine.
records.zomi: Ka sangsia in sang magazine adingin i pau tawh kisai gelh dingin hong hanthawn hi.

records.english: Using a language in everyday settings keeps it alive more than occasional lessons.
records.zomi: Ni sim mun te-ah pau khat zang in hun khenkhat-a sinna te sangin a nungta zaw sak hi.

records.english: Recording elders' knowledge is urgent, because each generation loses some memories.
records.zomi: Upa te' theihna ciamteh pen a manlang ding a kisam hi, bang hang hiam cih leh khang khat ciat in phawkna pawlkhat a mansuah hi.

records.english: The town library now lends Zomi storybooks.
records.zomi: Tu-in khuapi laibu inn in Zomi tangthu laibu te a leitawi hi.

records.english: Our language class needs more teachers.
records.zomi: I pau sinna in sangsia tam zaw a kisam hi.

records.english: Does the club meet after school?
records.zomi: Pawl sang khit-in a kikhawm hiam?

records.english: Young people who teach their language to others often strengthen their own skills.
records.zomi: A pau uh mi dang te a sinsak khangno te in amau' siamna zong a hat zaw sak zel uh hi.

records.english: Could our community work with the local college to train language teachers?
records.zomi: I khuasung in pau sangsia te hilh nadingin khuasung college tawh a kithuahpih thei ding hiam?

records.english: The university's Zomi students meet every month to read stories together.
records.zomi: University-a Zomi sangnaupang te tangthu sim khawm dingin kha simin a kikhawm uh hi.

records.english: The headteacher agreed to display a welcome sign in our language at the entrance.
records.zomi: Sangpi heutu in lutna-ah i pau-a dawnna laimal khat koih dingin a phal hi.

records.english: How can working parents find time to teach their children the language?
records.zomi: Nasep sem nu leh pa te in a ta te uh pau a sinsak nading hun bangci a mu thei uh hiam?

records.english: Can I write my project in our language?
records.zomi: Ka project i pau-in ka gelh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Jesus wept when his friend died.
records.zomi: A lawm a sih ciangin Jesu a kap hi.

records.english: Mum says Jesus knows how we feel.
records.zomi: Jesu in i kizak dan a thei hi, ci-in Nu in a gen hi.

records.english: How do you explain to a child that Jesus was a baby but also God?
records.zomi: Jesu pen naungek ahi a, ahi zongin Pasian zong ahi hi, cih naupang khat kiangah bangci na hilhcian hiam?

records.english: Our family believes Jesus is God.
records.zomi: I innkuan in Jesu pen Pasian ahi hi, ci-in a um hi.

records.english: Did Jesus get hungry?
records.zomi: Jesu a gil a kial ngei hiam?

records.english: My daughter was surprised to learn that Jesus once fell asleep while his friends were afraid.
records.zomi: A lawm te a lau lai-un Jesu a ihmu ngei hi, cih a theih ciangin ka tanu a lamdang sa hi.

records.english: Christians believe that Jesus' humanity allows him to understand human weakness and pain.
records.zomi: Jesu' mihing hihna in mihing hatlohna leh natna a theisiam thei hi, ci-in Khazih mite in a um uh hi.

records.english: Did Jesus have feelings like us?
records.zomi: Jesu in eite bangin lungsim kizakna a nei hiam?

records.english: Christians believe he did, because the Bible says he wept when his friend died.
records.zomi: Khazih mite in a nei hi, ci-in a um uh hi, bang hang hiam cih leh Lai Siangtho in a lawm a sih ciangin a kap hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Dad reads us stories about Jesus' life.
records.zomi: Pa in Jesu' nuntakna tawh kisai tangthu te hong sim sak hi.

records.english: We call Jesus our Lord.
records.zomi: Jesu pen i Topa i ci uh hi.

records.english: Did Jesus play games as a boy?
records.zomi: Jesu a tangval neu lai-in a kawm ngei hiam?

records.english: When my father was dying, he said he was not afraid because Jesus had walked through death before him.
records.zomi: Ka pa a sih dek ciangin, Jesu in amah ma-in sihna a tan khin ahih manin a lau kei hi, a ci hi.

records.english: My parents taught me that Jesus is fully God and fully human, not half of each.
records.zomi: Jesu pen a lang Pasian, a lang mihing hi lo-in, a bup-in Pasian leh a bup-in mihing ahi hi, ci-in ka nu leh pa in hong sinsak uh hi.

records.english: In many Christian homes, Jesus is spoken of both as Lord and as a close friend.
records.zomi: Khazih inn tampi-ah, Jesu pen Topa leh lawm kinai khat a nih bangin a kigen hi.

records.english: My son wondered whether Jesus told jokes.
records.zomi: Jesu in nuihzaak a gen ngei hiam, ci-in ka tapa in a lamdang sa hi.

records.english: Children's questions about Jesus often lead families into discussions of deep theological ideas.
records.zomi: Jesu tawh kisai naupang te' dotna te in innkuan te Pasian thu ngaihsutna thuk te tawh kisai kikumna te-ah a paipih zel hi.

records.english: Why do we pray to Jesus if he was a man?
records.zomi: Mihing a hih leh bang hangin Jesu kiangah thu i ngen uh hiam?

records.english: Christians believe he was also God, so they pray to him as their Lord.
records.zomi: Khazih mite in Pasian zong ahi hi, ci-in a um uh ahih manin, a Topa uh bangin a kiangah thu a ngen uh hi.

records.english: My grandmother keeps a picture of Jesus as a carpenter to remind her that he worked with his hands.
records.zomi: Ka pi in a khut tawh nasep a sem hi, cih a phawksak nadingin khutsiampa-a Jesu' lim khat a kem hi.

records.english: Christian teaching on Christ's two natures was shaped by long debates in the early church.
records.zomi: Khazih' omzia nih tawh kisai Khazih sinsakna pen biakinn masa-a kinialna sau te in a bawl hi.

records.english: Why does our church insist that Jesus was both fully God and fully human?
records.zomi: Bang hangin i biakinn in Jesu pen a bup-in Pasian leh a bup-in mihing ahi hi, ci-in a lenkip hiam?

records.english: Christians believe that only someone who was truly both could bring God and humanity together.
records.zomi: A nih taktak ahi mi khat bek in Pasian leh mihing a kikhawm sak thei hi, ci-in Khazih mite in a um uh hi.

records.english: Jesus had a mother like us.
records.zomi: Jesu in eite bangin nu khat a nei hi.

records.english: My husband finds comfort in the story of Jesus' tiredness after a long day of teaching.
records.zomi: Ka pasal in ni sau sinsakna khit-a Jesu' gimna tangthu-ah lungmuanna a ngah hi.

records.english: Christians often describe Jesus as one person with two complete natures.
records.zomi: Khazih mite in Jesu pen omzia kicing nih nei mi khat ahi hi, ci-in a gen zel uh hi.

records.english: Did Jesus live in a real town, Mum?
records.zomi: Nu aw, Jesu khuapi taktak khat-ah a om hiam?

records.english: My daughter loves the stories about Jesus.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in Jesu tawh kisai tangthu te a deih mahmah hi.

records.english: My grandmother says she finds it easier to pray because Jesus knows what human sorrow feels like.
records.zomi: Jesu in mihing dahna bangci kizak hiam cih a theih manin thu ngen a baihlam zaw hi, ci-in ka pi in a gen hi.

records.english: Dad, did Jesus ever get tired?
records.zomi: Pa aw, Jesu a gim ngei hiam?

records.english: Yes, the Gospels say he once fell asleep in a boat during a storm.
records.zomi: Gim ngei hi, huihpi a nun lai-in gunkuang sungah a ihmu ngei hi, ci-in Lungdamna Thu in a gen hi.

records.english: Grandpa prays to Jesus every morning.
records.zomi: Pu in zingsang simin Jesu kiangah thu a ngen hi.

records.english: Our family talks about Jesus' friendship with Martha and Mary when we discuss what it means to be a friend.
records.zomi: Lawm hihna bang ahi hiam cih i kikup ciangin, i innkuan in Jesu leh Martha leh Mari' kilawmta na tawh kisai a kikup uh hi.

records.english: For believers, Jesus' divine nature is why they worship him rather than only admire him.
records.zomi: Ummite adingin, Jesu' Pasian hihna hangin amah a lamdang sak bek hi lo-in a bia uh hi.

records.english: Why do Christians say that Jesus was tempted but never sinned?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Khazih mite in Jesu pen sitna a tuak hi, ahi zongin mawhna a bawl ngei kei hi, ci-in a gen uh hiam?

records.english: My teenage son asked whether Jesus ever doubted, and we talked about his prayer in the garden.
records.zomi: Ka tapa tangval khangno in Jesu a lunglai ngei hiam ci-in a dong a, huan sungah a thungetna tawh kisai i kikum uh hi.

records.english: Could we read the story of Jesus weeping for his friend together this evening?
records.zomi: Tuni nitak-in a lawm adinga Jesu' kahna tangthu khawm-in i sim thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: Did Jesus have friends?
records.zomi: Jesu in lawm a nei hiam?

records.english: Our family Bible study looked at the moments when Jesus showed both human weakness and divine power.
records.zomi: I innkuan Lai Siangtho sinna in Jesu in mihing hatlohna leh Pasian thuneihna a nih a lak hun te a en hi.

records.english: Believers often turn to Jesus in suffering because they believe he suffered too.
records.zomi: Ummite in Jesu zong a thuak hi, ci-in a um uh ahih manin thuakna sungah Jesu lam a nga zel uh hi.

records.english: Do your children understand why Christians worship Jesus as well as follow his teaching?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Khazih mite in Jesu a sinsakna a zui bek hi lo-in a bia zong uh hiam cih na ta te in a theisiam uh hiam?

records.english: Christian parents often use stories of Jesus' tiredness and tears to show his humanity.
records.zomi: Khazih nu leh pa te in Jesu' mihing hihna a lak nadingin a gimna leh a kahna tangthu te a zang zel uh hi.

records.english: Can Jesus hear our prayers?
records.zomi: Jesu in i thungetna te a za thei hiam?

records.english: We sing songs about Jesus at home.
records.zomi: Inn-ah Jesu tawh kisai la i sa uh hi.

records.english: How can Jesus understand my problems if he is God?
records.zomi: Pasian a hih leh, Jesu in ka buaina te bangci a theisiam thei ding hiam?

records.english: Christians believe he lived a real human life, so he knows what it is like to be tired, sad and tempted.
records.zomi: Mihing nuntakna taktak a nuntak hi, ci-in Khazih mite in a um uh ahih manin, gim, dah leh sitna tuak bang ahi hiam cih a thei hi.

records.english: We pray to Jesus before bed.
records.zomi: I ihmut ma-in Jesu kiangah thu i ngen uh hi.

records.english: When my grandmother was very ill, she told me that she prayed to Jesus because he had suffered too.
records.zomi: Ka pi a na mahmah ciangin, Jesu zong a thuak ngei ahih manin a kiangah thu a ngen hi, ci-in hong gen hi.

records.english: She said it comforted her to think that the one she prayed to had known pain in his own body.
records.zomi: A thungetpih pa in amah' pumpi tungah natna a thei ngei hi, cih a ngaihsut ciangin lungmuanna a ngah hi, ci-in a gen hi.

records.english: I have remembered her words every time I have sat beside someone who is suffering.
records.zomi: A thuak mi khat kiangah ka tut ciangin a kammal te ka phawk zel hi.

records.english: Jesus had a job as a carpenter.
records.zomi: Jesu in khutsiampa nasep a nei hi.

records.english: My son was fascinated that Jesus forgave sins, which his critics said only God could do.
records.zomi: Pasian bek in a bawl thei hi, ci-in a langpang te in a gen mawhna maisakna Jesu in a bawl ciangin ka tapa a lamdang sa mahmah hi.

records.english: Why did my grandfather always bow his head when he said the name of Jesus?
records.zomi: Bang hangin ka pu in Jesu' min a gen ciangin a lu a kun den hiam?

records.english: Grandma says Jesus understands us.

records.english: Many Christians see in Jesus' prayers a model of how humans can relate to God.
records.zomi: Khazih mi tampi in Jesu' thungetna te-ah mihing te in Pasian tawh bangci a kizop thei uh hiam cih ettehna a mu uh hi.

records.zomi: Bang hangin Jesu pen Pasian' Tapa i ci uh hiam?

records.english: When my son asked how Jesus could be God and a man, we read about the time he calmed the storm.

records.english: Many Christian families find comfort in believing that Jesus shared ordinary human life.

records.english: Did Jesus eat with his friends?

records.zomi: Jesu a lau ngei hiam ci-in ka unau pa in a dong hi.

records.english: Older relatives sometimes explain decisions differently as they look back over the years.

records.english: Was medicine your first choice?

records.english: Why did you buy the bakery?

records.english: What would you decide differently if you could live that year again?
records.zomi: Tua kum na nuntak kik thei leh, bang tuam takin na khensat ding hiam?

records.english: Who decided to move the market?
records.zomi: Kua in sum-kuan mun a suan dingin a khensat hiam?

records.zomi: Bang hangin na nu in a ta te a khanlet khit uh ciangin nasep sem kipat dingin a khensat hiam?

records.english: Did you ever regret your decision to become a teacher?
records.zomi: Sangsia hih dingin na khensatna na kisik ngei hiam?

records.english: When my grandmother was offered a place at a nursing college far from home, her father said no.

records.english: Did you choose your own job?
records.zomi: Na nasep amah mahmah in na teel hiam?

records.english: Who decided that the children would learn both languages at home?
records.zomi: Ta te in inn-ah pau nih a sin ding uh hi, ci-in kua in a khensat hiam?

records.english: Why did you change schools?
records.zomi: Bang hangin sang na lai hiam?

records.english: How long did it take Grandpa to decide whether to accept the job in the mine?
records.zomi: Khuam sung nasep a la ding hiam cih khensat dingin Pu in hun bangzah a la hiam?

records.english: Why did the family decide to stop farming after so many generations?
records.zomi: Bang hangin innkuan in khang tampi khit-in lo nasep khawl dingin a khensat uh hiam?

records.english: Why did you go abroad?
records.zomi: Bang hangin gamdang-ah na pai hiam?

records.english: Hearing about difficult decisions helps young people prepare for their own choices.

records.zomi: Ka khat ciat bang i deih uh hiam ci-in a dong uh a, ka unau pa neu pen bek in a deih taktak hi.

records.english: Who decided that the family would move to the city?
records.zomi: Innkuan in khuapi-ah a tai ding uh hi, ci-in kua in a khensat hiam?

records.english: When did you decide to retire?
records.zomi: Bang hun-in nasep khawl dingin na khensat hiam?

records.english: Decisions made under pressure in the past can be hard for younger generations to understand.
records.zomi: Nidang-a nawhsawhna nuai-a thukhensatna te pen khangno te adingin theisiam haksa thei hi.

records.zomi: Khuasung te in thukhensatna thupi te upa te' tangthu khang khat pan khang khat-ah a kigen te tawh a phawk zel uh hi.

records.english: How did Grandpa decide to buy the land by the river?

records.zomi: A khensat ma-in kha khat sung zingsang simin tua gam-ah a pai hi.

records.zomi: Bang hangin khuasung upa te in tuikhuk thak a tou nading mun khensat dingin hun sau a la uh hiam?

records.english: Every family wanted it near their own house, so the elders walked the whole village twice before choosing the centre.
records.zomi: Innkuan khempeuh in amau' inn kiangah a deih uh ahih manin, khuasung upa te in laizang a teel ma-un khuasung bup vei nih a pai uh hi.

records.english: Did you decide to emigrate on your own, or did your whole family decide together?
records.zomi: Gamdang-ah tai dingin nangmah bek na khensat hiam, ahih kei leh na innkuan bup khawm-in a khensat uh hiam?

records.english: Why did you choose to study at night instead of stopping work?
records.zomi: Bang hangin nasep khawl lo-in zan-in sinna na teel hiam?

records.english: Asking how a past decision was made often reveals the values of the person who made it.

records.english: Many family stories turn on a single decision that changed the direction of several lives.

records.english: How long did you think before saying yes?

records.english: Why did you leave the farm?
records.zomi: Bang hangin lo na nusia hiam?

records.zomi: Bang hangin galkap nasep nusia dingin a khensat hiam cih na pa in hong hilhcian ngei hiam?

records.english: Questions about who made a decision can show how authority worked in a family or community.
records.zomi: Kua in thukhensatna a bawl hiam cih tawh kisai dotna te in innkuan ahih kei leh khuasung khat-ah thuneihna bangci a kizang hiam cih a lak thei hi.

records.english: Did you ever change your mind?

records.english: Why did you come back home?

records.english: Did you choose this house yourself?
records.zomi: Hih inn nangmah mahmah in na teel hiam?

records.english: Who decided that the wedding would take place in the village church?

records.english: When our residents' group applied for a grant to repair the playground, we didn't know where to start.

records.english: Three months later, the grant was approved, and the new swings were installed before the summer holidays.

records.english: The library staff helped me scan my documents so that I could apply online.

records.english: Can I apply for a bus pass here?
records.zomi: Hi-ah bus lai ka ngen thei ding hiam?

records.english: The community centre runs a weekly session to help residents apply for council services.
records.zomi: Khuasung inn in khuasung mite council nasep te a ngen nading huh dingin kal simin hun khat a bawl hi.

records.english: Where can I get an application form?

records.english: Applications for community grants often bring neighbours together around a shared goal.
records.zomi: Khuasung grant ngetna te in inn kiang mite a ut khawm uh ngimna khat tungah a kikhawm sak zel hi.

records.english: Community advisers often notice when residents qualify for more than one service.

records.english: Which office deals with parking permits?

records.english: How long does the council take to decide on a housing application?

records.english: Can my daughter apply on my behalf?

records.zomi: Huhna pawl te in lampi-ah sum kai nading phalna kum simin a ngen ding uh hiam?

records.zomi: Khuasung mite' pawl in July kha-in lampi-ah pawi khat bawl nadingin phalna a ngen uh hi.

records.english: Why does the council ask applicants for a community grant to describe who will benefit?

records.english: The grant has to help as many residents as possible, so the panel compares how each project would serve the community.

records.english: Ask for the reason in writing, and the advice centre can help you appeal within the time limit.
records.zomi: A hang lai tawh gelh dingin ngen in, huan thuhilhna inn in hun ciang sungah nial kik dingin hong huh thei hi.

records.english: The library helps people with applications.
records.zomi: Laibu inn in mite a ngetna uh-ah a huh hi.

records.english: Can the advice centre help me apply for a disabled parking badge?
records.zomi: Thuhilhna inn in pumpi a kim lo mi' mawtaw koihna lai ngen dingin hong huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, a volunteer can fill in the application with you and check your documents.
records.zomi: Thei hi, thalawp khat in nang tawh ngetna a dim a, na lai te a en thei hi.

records.english: Grant applications encourage community groups to plan their projects carefully.
records.zomi: Grant ngetna te in khuasung pawl te a project uh kilawm taka ciamteh dingin a hanthawn hi.

records.english: Many residents miss out on help simply because they never apply.
records.zomi: Khuasung mi tampi in a ngen ngei lo uh hang bek-in huhna a ngah kei uh hi.

records.english: The deadline is next Friday.
records.zomi: Hun ciang pen a zom Laithai ni ahi hi.

records.english: Do I need to apply in person?
records.zomi: Ka mah ka pai in ka ngen ding kisam hiam?

records.english: Our youth club applied for a grant to buy sports equipment for local teenagers.
records.zomi: I khangno pawl in khuasung khangno te adingin kawmna van lei nadingin grant a ngen uh hi.

records.english: Written reasons for refusals allow applicants to appeal fairly.
records.zomi: Nialna a hang lai-a kigelh te in ngenmi te dik takin a nial kik thei dingin a phal hi.

records.english: Help with applications ensures that residents receive the support they are entitled to.
records.zomi: Ngetna-a huhna in khuasung mite in a ngah ding uh huhna a ngah nadingin a kem hi.

records.english: Understanding past causes and effects helps communities plan for the future.
records.zomi: Nidang-a a hang leh a gah te theisiam in khuasung te in hun ding adingin a ciamteh nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Our class couldn't understand why our town had grown so quickly in the 1960s.

records.english: Every Lent, our family reads one Gospel from beginning to end.
records.zomi: Lent hun khempeuh-in, i innkuan in Lungdamna Thu khat a kipatna pan a tawp dong i sim uh hi.

records.english: My grandfather taught us that the parables are meant to make us think, not just to entertain us.
records.zomi: Thugentehna te pen nuamsak nading bek hi lo-in i ngaihsun nadingin ahi hi, ci-in ka pu in hong sinsak hi.

records.english: Mum explains the parables to us.
records.zomi: Nu in thugentehna te hong hilhcian hi.

records.english: How does the story of the Good Samaritan apply to our family?
records.zomi: Samaria mi hoih tangthu pen i innkuan tungah bangci a kizang hiam?

records.english: It reminds us that our neighbour is anyone who needs help, even someone very different from us.
records.zomi: Eite tawh a kibang lo mahmah mi khat zong hi leh, i inn kiang mi pen huhna a kisam mi khempeuh ahi hi, cih hong phawksak hi.

records.english: Christian parents often use Jesus' example to teach children kindness and service.
records.zomi: Khazih nu leh pa te in naupang te hehpihna leh nasep sakna a sinsak nadingin Jesu' ettehna a zang zel uh hi.

records.english: My son likes the story of the lost sheep.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in tuu mang tangthu a deih hi.

records.english: Family traditions based on Gospel stories help children remember Jesus' teaching.
records.zomi: Lungdamna Thu tangthu tungah a kinga innkuan ngeina te in naupang te Jesu' sinsakna a phawk nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Our family Bible study compared how Matthew and Luke tell the story of Jesus' birth.
records.zomi: I innkuan Lai Siangtho sinna in Matthai leh Luka in Jesu' piancilna tangthu bangci a gen uh hiam cih a kiteh hi.

records.english: My wife reads the Beatitudes aloud whenever our family faces a difficult time.
records.zomi: I innkuan in hun haksa a tuak ciang khempeuh-in ka zi in Thupha Ngahna Thu te ging taka a sim hi.

records.english: Did Jesus walk everywhere?
records.zomi: Jesu in mun khempeuh-ah a peel hiam?

records.english: Could we read the story of the prodigal son together before you visit your father?
records.zomi: Na pa na ve ma-in tapa mangthang tangthu khawm-in i sim thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: Do your children know that Jesus spent most of his ministry in small towns and villages?
records.zomi: Jesu in a nasep hun tamzaw khuapi neu leh khuano te-ah a zang hi, cih na ta te in a thei uh hiam?

records.english: We visited a church with paintings of Jesus' life.
records.zomi: Jesu' nuntakna lim zial te a nei biakinn khat i ve uh hi.

records.english: My son was surprised that Jesus got angry with the traders in the temple.
records.zomi: Biakinnpi sung-a sumzuakte tungah Jesu a heh hi, cih ka tapa in a lamdang sa hi.

records.english: Grandma tells us how Jesus healed the blind man.
records.zomi: Jesu in mittaw pa bangci a damsak hiam cih Pi in hong gen hi.

records.english: Every Easter, my grandmother tells us the story of Jesus washing his disciples' feet.
records.zomi: Easter khempeuh-in, Jesu in a nungzuite' khe a silsak tangthu ka pi in hong gen hi.

records.english: Last year, she asked each of us to wash the feet of the person sitting next to us at the table.
records.zomi: Kum nunung-in, dokhan-ah eite kiang-a tu mi' khe sil dingin ka khat ciat hong ngen hi.

records.english: My little brother laughed at first, but then he went quiet when Grandma knelt down to wash his.
records.zomi: Ka unau pa neu a masa-in a nuih hi, ahi zongin a khe sil dingin Pi a khukdin ciangin a dai hi.

records.english: Which Gospel story would you choose for bedtime?
records.zomi: Ihmut hun adingin Lungdamna Thu tangthu koi na teel ding hiam?

records.english: Grandma knows all the parables by heart.
records.zomi: Pi in thugentehna khempeuh a lungsim-ah a thei hi.

records.english: Did Jesus really feed thousands of people with a few loaves?
records.zomi: Jesu in khomun tawm khat tawh mi tulte a vak taktak hiam?

records.english: The Gospels say so, and Christians believe it showed God's care for hungry people.
records.zomi: Lungdamna Thu in tua bangin a gen a, tua in a gil kial mite tungah Pasian' kemna a lak hi, ci-in Khazih mite in a um uh hi.

records.english: For many believers, the ministry of Jesus shows what the kingdom of God is like.
records.zomi: Ummi tampi adingin, Jesu' nasep in Pasian Gam bang ahi hiam cih a lak hi.

records.english: We read a story about Jesus every night.
records.zomi: Zan simin Jesu tawh kisai tangthu khat i sim uh hi.

records.english: Why did Jesus go to weddings?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Jesu mopawi te-ah a pai hiam?

records.english: When my mother was ill, she found comfort in the stories of Jesus healing the sick.
records.zomi: Ka nu a na ciangin, Jesu in damlo te a damsakna tangthu te-ah lungmuanna a ngah hi.

records.english: Our family helps the poor because Jesus did.
records.zomi: Jesu in a bawl ahih manin i innkuan in mi zawng te i huh uh hi.

records.english: Many Christians see Jesus' habit of prayer as a model for their own lives.
records.zomi: Khazih mi tampi in Jesu' thungetna ngeina amau' nuntakna adingin ettehna khat bangin a mu uh hi.

records.english: We pray the Lord's Prayer together.
records.zomi: Topa' Thungetna khawm-in i ngen uh hi.

records.english: After hearing the story of the widow's coins, my son gave his pocket money to the church.
records.zomi: Meigong' dangka tangthu a zak khit ciangin, ka tapa in a sum neu biakinn-ah a pia hi.

records.english: Why did Jesus tell so many stories?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Jesu in tangthu tampi mahmah a gen hiam?

records.english: Did Jesus have a boat?
records.zomi: Jesu in gunkuang a nei hiam?

records.english: Where did Jesus sleep when he travelled?
records.zomi: Jesu a khualzin ciangin koi-ah a ihmu hiam?

records.english: Why did Jesus spend time with people that others avoided?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Jesu in mi dang te in a pumpelh mite tawh hun a zang hiam?

records.english: Christians believe he wanted everyone to know they were welcome in God's family.
records.zomi: Mi khempeuh in Pasian' innkuan-ah a kidawn uh hi, cih a theih nadingin a deih hi, ci-in Khazih mite in a um uh hi.

records.english: We read the Gospel of Luke this year.
records.zomi: Tu kum-in Luka' Lungdamna Thu i sim uh hi.

records.english: Why did Jesus choose fishermen and tax collectors as his closest followers?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Jesu in nga beng mi te leh siahdongte a nungzui kinai pen te-in a teel hiam?

records.english: Why does our family return to the Gospels whenever life is difficult?
records.zomi: Bang hangin nuntakna a haksat ciang khempeuh-in i innkuan in Lungdamna Thu-ah i ciah kik uh hiam?

records.english: Christians believe the life and teaching of Jesus show most clearly what God is like and how believers should live.
records.zomi: Jesu' nuntakna leh sinsakna in Pasian bang ahi hiam leh ummite bangci nungta ding uh hiam cih kician pen-in a lak hi, ci-in Khazih mite in a um uh hi.

records.english: For believers, Jesus' healing miracles reveal both his compassion and his authority.
records.zomi: Ummite adingin, Jesu' damsakna nalamdang te in a hehpihna leh a thuneihna a nih a lak hi.

records.english: Christians believe that Jesus' care for outsiders shows God's love for every person.
records.zomi: Jesu' pua mite kemna in mi khempeuh tungah Pasian' itna a lak hi, ci-in Khazih mite in a um uh hi.

records.english: Why did Jesus wash his friends' feet, Mum?
records.zomi: Nu aw, bang hangin Jesu in a lawm te' khe a silsak hiam?

records.english: The Gospel says he wanted to show them that loving people means serving them.
records.zomi: Mite it pen amau nasep sak cihna ahi hi, cih amaute a lak nuam hi, ci-in Lungdamna Thu in a gen hi.

records.english: When my daughter asked why Jesus ate with tax collectors, we talked about welcoming people others reject.
records.zomi: Bang hangin Jesu in siahdongte tawh an a ne hiam ci-in ka tanu in a dot ciangin, mi dang te' nial mite dawn tawh kisai i kikup uh hi.

records.english: Many Christian families learn about Jesus' ministry through stories read aloud at home.
records.zomi: Khazih innkuan tampi in inn-ah ging taka kisim tangthu te tawh Jesu' nasep a sin uh hi.

records.english: My parents taught us to share our food because Jesus fed the hungry crowds.
records.zomi: Jesu in gil kial mihonpi te a vak ahih manin i an uh hawm dingin ka nu leh pa in hong sinsak uh hi.

records.english: Our family acts out the parables at Christmas.
records.zomi: Christmas-in i innkuan in thugentehna te lim i bawl uh hi.

records.english: Recording family stories means listeners can replay them instead of asking again and again.
records.zomi: Innkuan tangthu ciamteh in ngaimi te in dong kik den lo-in a ngai kik thei uh hi.

records.english: Some elders enjoy retelling their stories, while others find it painful to repeat them.
records.zomi: Upa pawlkhat in a tangthu uh gen kik a nuam sa uh a, a dang te in gen kik a na sa uh hi.

records.english: Would you tell the story of your first day at school once more for my children?
records.zomi: Na sang kah ni masa pen tangthu ka ta te adingin vei khat gen kik ding na hi hiam?

records.english: What year did you say you married?
records.zomi: Bang kum-in na kiteen hi na ci hiam?

records.english: What was the name of the boat again?
records.zomi: Gunkuang min bang a hi kik hiam?

records.english: How do you write the name of your village?
records.zomi: Na khua min bangci na gelh hiam?

records.english: Can you tell the joke about the goat again?
records.zomi: Kel tawh kisai nuihzaak na gen kik thei ding hiam?

records.english: Which side of the river was the farm on?
records.zomi: Lo pen tuipi' lang koi-ah a om hiam?

records.english: Sorry, could you say again which year the factory closed and which year you left?
records.zomi: Hong maisak in, bang kum-in factory a kikhak a, bang kum-in na pawt hiam cih na gen kik thei ding hiam?

records.english: How far did you say you walked?
records.zomi: Bangzah gamla na pai hi na ci hiam?

records.english: Which war did you say Grandpa fought in?
records.zomi: Pu in koi gal-ah a kidou hi na ci hiam?

records.english: Could you repeat the name of the ship your parents travelled on?
records.zomi: Na nu leh pa' tuanna tembaw min na gen kik thei ding hiam?

records.english: It was called the Morning Star, and it carried about two hundred passengers.
records.zomi: Morning Star a kici a, khualzin mi za nih bang a puak hi.

records.english: Asking an elder to repeat a story often brings out details that were missed the first time.
records.zomi: Upa khat kiangah tangthu gen kik dingin ngen in a masa vei-in a kipelh thu te a lak khia zel hi.

records.english: Could you say that more loudly for Grandpa?
records.zomi: Pu adingin a ging zaw-in na gen thei ding hiam?

records.english: Could you repeat what your mother said?
records.zomi: Na nu' gen na gen kik thei ding hiam?

records.english: Repeating a story for younger generations can help an older person feel valued.
records.zomi: Khangno te adingin tangthu gen kik in mi upa khat a manpha bang a kizak nadingin a huh thei hi.

records.english: Grandpa, could you tell the story about the tiger again?
records.zomi: Pu aw, humpi tawh kisai tangthu na gen kik thei ding hiam?

records.english: Only if you sit still this time and don't interrupt halfway through.
records.zomi: Tu-in dai takin na tut a, a lai-ah na kihel loh leh bek.

records.english: Asking for a name or date to be repeated helps families record their history accurately.
records.zomi: Min ahih kei leh ni khat gen kik dingin ngen in innkuan te in a tangthu uh dik takin a ciamteh nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Listening carefully the first time is a gift, but asking again is better than forgetting.
records.zomi: A masa vei-in kilawm taka ngai pen letsong khat ahi hi, ahi zongin dong kik pen mangngilh sangin a hoih zaw hi.

records.english: Could you start again from where the bus broke down?
records.zomi: Bus a sia mun pan na kipan kik thei ding hiam?

records.english: Writing down a story as it is repeated slowly preserves it for future readers.
records.zomi: Tangthu khat zawi takin a kigen kik lai-in gelh in hun ding-a simmi te adingin a kem hi.

records.english: Could you go back to the bit where the soldiers arrived in the village?
records.zomi: Galkap te khuasung-ah a tun mun-ah na ciah kik thei ding hiam?

records.english: When my grandmother told her life story to the youth group, she spoke so softly that we kept asking her to repeat things.
records.zomi: Ka pi in a nuntakna tangthu khangno pawl kiangah a gen ciangin, nem mahmah-in a gen ahih manin thu te gen kik dingin i ngen den uh hi.

records.english: In the end, my cousin recorded her on his phone so that we could play each part again later.
records.zomi: A tawp-in, a nung-in khen khat ciat i ngai kik thei nadingin ka sanggam in a phone tawh a ciamteh hi.

records.english: That recording is now the only copy of her voice we have, and we listen to it every year on her birthday.
records.zomi: Tua ciamteh pen i neih a aw' lak khat bek ahi a, a pianni kum simin i ngai uh hi.

records.english: What did your father call his horse?
records.zomi: Na pa in a sakol bang a ci hiam?

records.english: Could you repeat the old saying your grandmother used whenever it rained?
records.zomi: Guah a zuk ciang khempeuh-in na pi' gen zel genkhia lui na gen kik thei ding hiam?

records.english: Sorry, I didn't catch whether your father was a carpenter or a blacksmith.
records.zomi: Hong maisak in, na pa pen khutsiampa hi hiam, sik-sek mi hi hiam cih ka za kha kei hi.

records.english: Children who ask to hear the same story repeatedly help keep it alive.
records.zomi: Tangthu kibang vei tampi za nuam naupang te in a nungta lai nadingin a huh uh hi.

records.english: Could you say again why the village moved its market to the hilltop?
records.zomi: Bang hangin khuasung in a sum-kuan mun mual tung-ah a suan hiam cih na gen kik thei ding hiam?

records.english: After the bridge collapsed, traders from the other side could no longer reach the old square, so the elders chose a place both sides could walk to.
records.zomi: Lei a kiat khit ciangin, a lang dang pan sumbawlmi te in mun lui a tung thei nawn kei uh ahih manin, upa te in a lang nih in a pai thei mun khat a teel uh hi.

records.english: What was the name of your first teacher?
records.zomi: Na sangsia masa pen' min bang hiam?

records.english: Sorry, was it the church or the school that burned?
records.zomi: Hong maisak in, a kang pen biakinn hi hiam, sang hi hiam?

records.english: Sorry, did you say your family came from the north or the south?
records.zomi: Hong maisak in, na innkuan pen sang lam pan hi hiam, nitum lam pan hi hiam, na ci hiam?

records.english: The north, from a village near the border with the mountains.
records.zomi: Sang lam pan, mual te' gamgi kiang-a khua khat pan.

records.english: Older storytellers sometimes tell a story differently each time it is repeated.
records.zomi: Tangthu gen upa pawlkhat in tangthu khat a gen kik ciang khempeuh-in tuam takin a gen zel uh hi.

records.english: Did you say the wedding lasted three days or a whole week?
records.zomi: Mopawi pen ni thum sung hi hiam, kal khat bup hi hiam, na ci hiam?

records.english: Could you tell me again how Great-Grandpa found his way across the mountains?
records.zomi: Pu-pi in mual te bangci a kantan hiam cih hong gen kik thei ding hiam?

records.english: Sorry, I missed the part about why the family left the island, so could you repeat it?
records.zomi: Hong maisak in, bang hangin innkuan in tuilai gam a nusia uh hiam cih ka za kha kei ahih manin, na gen kik thei ding hiam?

records.english: Could you tell the story about the lost goat again, because the children loved it?
records.zomi: Naupang te in a deih mahmah uh ahih manin, kel mang tangthu na gen kik thei ding hiam?

records.english: Could you describe the old house again, room by room, so I can draw it?
records.zomi: Ka lim bawl thei nadingin, inn lui pen inndan khat ciat-in hong gen kik thei ding hiam?

records.english: Sorry, did your parents meet before or after the war?
records.zomi: Hong maisak in, na nu leh pa gal ma-in a kimu uh hiam, gal khit-in a kimu uh hiam?

records.english: Would you mind explaining again how the family managed during the long winter?
records.zomi: Khuaphal sau lai-in innkuan in bangci a pal uh hiam cih hong hilhcian kik ding na lungkim hiam?

records.english: Sorry, how old were you then?
records.zomi: Hong maisak in, tua hun-in kum bangzah na hi hiam?

records.english: Would you mind going over the part about the year of the great rains again, more slowly?
records.zomi: Guah lianpi zuk kum tawh kisai thu zawi zaw takin hong gen kik ding na lungkim hiam?

records.english: Of the three bad harvests, the second was the worst, because the river rose and covered every field for a month.
records.zomi: Gah lakna hoih lo thum sungah a nihna pen a siat pen hi, bang hang hiam cih leh tuipi a liat a, kha khat sung lo khempeuh a khuh hi.

records.english: Can you say the date once more?
records.zomi: Ni pen vei khat na gen kik thei ding hiam?

records.english: Asking for repetition can reveal contradictions that lead to new questions about the past.
records.zomi: Gen kik dingin ngen in kinaih lohna te a lak thei a, tua te in nidang tawh kisai dotna thak te-ah a paipih hi.

records.english: Could you repeat the end of the story?
records.zomi: Tangthu' a tawp na gen kik thei ding hiam?

records.english: Patient requests for repetition show respect for the person telling the story.
records.zomi: Thuakzawhna taka gen kik dingin ngetna te in tangthu genmi zahtakna a lak hi.

records.english: Sorry, which village was that?
records.zomi: Hong maisak in, tua pen koi khua hi hiam?

records.english: Would you mind repeating the names of all your brothers and sisters in order?
records.zomi: Na unau pa leh nu khempeuh' min a kizui-in hong gen kik ding na lungkim hiam?

records.english: Did you say your mother walked to the market or rode on a cart?
records.zomi: Na nu sum-kuan mun-ah a peel hiam, leeng tungah a tuang hiam, na ci hiam?

records.english: Stories retold at every family gathering often become part of a family's identity.
records.zomi: Innkuan kikhopna khempeuh-a kigen kik tangthu te in innkuan khat' hihna sung-a khen khat a suak zel hi.

records.english: Did you say six brothers or seven?
records.zomi: Unau pa guk hi hiam, sagih hi hiam, na ci hiam?

records.english: Could you say Grandma's maiden name again?
records.zomi: Pi' a nungak lai-a min na gen kik thei ding hiam?

records.english: Sorry, did you say spring or autumn?
records.zomi: Hong maisak in, spring na ci hiam, autumn hun na ci hiam?

records.english: Would you repeat that last part slowly so that I can write it in the family book?
records.zomi: Innkuan laibu-ah ka gelh thei nadingin a tawp khen zawi takin na gen kik ding hiam?

records.english: The library printer is jammed.
records.zomi: Laibu inn printer a kikhap hi.

records.english: Would the volunteers know whether a ten-year-old laptop can still be saved?
records.zomi: Kum sawm a pha laptop khat a kihoihsak thei lai hiam cih thalawp te in a thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: Is it safe to let a volunteer look at my phone if it has my bank details on it?
records.zomi: Ka phone in ka bank thu a nei leh, thalawp khat in en dingin ka phal pen a bit hiam?

records.english: Simple guides to common problems save time for both staff and visitors.
records.zomi: Buaina tangpi te adingin lamlakna baihlam te in nasem te leh kanmi te' hun a nih a kem sak hi.

records.english: My headphones don't work with this computer.
records.zomi: Ka headphone in hih computer tawh a sem kei hi.

records.english: Can someone check my laptop?
records.zomi: Kua hiam khat in ka laptop a en thei ding hiam?

records.english: Why do the community centre's computers take so long to start in the morning?
records.zomi: Bang hangin khuasung inn' computer te in zingsang-in a kipat nadingin hun sau mahmah a la uh hiam?

records.english: When the library's printer broke, staff printed my boarding pass in the office instead.
records.zomi: Laibu inn' printer a sia ciangin, nasem te in office sungah ka vanlengtual tuanna lai hong print sak uh hi.

records.english: Offering free charging during emergencies keeps residents in touch with their families.
records.zomi: Thu manlang hun-in man om lo-in charge sak in khuasung mite a innkuan uh tawh a kizop lai nadingin a kem hi.

records.english: Older residents often gain confidence when they learn to solve small problems themselves.
records.zomi: Khuasung mi upa zaw te in buaina neu te amau mahmah in a bawlphat dan a sin uh ciangin muanna a ngah zel uh hi.

records.english: Could the library run a session on what to do when an app stops working?
records.zomi: App khat a sep nawn loh ciangin bang bawl ding hiam cih tawh kisai laibu inn in sinna hun khat a bawl thei ding hiam?

records.english: Ask the volunteer for help.
records.zomi: Thalawp kiangah huhna ngen in.

records.english: The library volunteers keep a list of the most common problems and how to fix them.
records.zomi: Laibu inn thalawp te in buaina tangpi pen te leh bangci bawlphat ding hiam cih lista khat a kem uh hi.

records.english: Our residents' group invited a technician to show members how to keep their devices running smoothly.
records.zomi: I khuasung mite' pawl in a mi te uh van te hoih taka a sep lai nadingin bangci kem ding hiam cih lak dingin technician khat a sam uh hi.

records.english: Libraries have become important places for help with everyday technology.
records.zomi: Laibu inn te pen ni sim technology huhna adingin mun thupi te a suak khin hi.

records.english: The keyboard is not working.
records.zomi: Keyboard a sem kei hi.

records.english: The council's helpline explained how to restart my router when the internet stopped working.
records.zomi: Internet a sep nawn loh ciangin council' huhna phone in ka router bangci kipat kik sak ding hiam cih a hilhcian hi.

records.english: What should I do if my phone stops working while I'm filling in an online council form?
records.zomi: Online council lai lak ka dim lai-in ka phone a sep nawn kei leh bang ka bawl ding hiam?

records.english: Ask at the library, where a volunteer can help you finish the form on one of their computers.
records.zomi: Laibu inn-ah dong in, tua-ah thalawp khat in a computer te sung-a khat-ah lai lak na zo nadingin hong huh thei hi.

records.english: The printer says there's no ink.
records.zomi: Printer in ink om lo hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Can I borrow a charger?
records.zomi: Charger khat ka leitawi thei ding hiam?

records.english: The computer screen is frozen.
records.zomi: Computer screen a khawl khin hi.

records.english: Why did the library start running sessions on fixing common phone problems?
records.zomi: Bang hangin laibu inn in phone buaina tangpi bawlphat dan sinna hun te a bawl kipan hiam?

records.english: Staff noticed that many visitors came in only because their devices had stopped working and they had nobody else to ask.
records.zomi: Kanmi tampi in a van uh a sep nawn loh ahih manin bek a hong lut uh a, a dot ding kuamah a nei kei uh hi, cih nasem te in a phawk uh hi.

records.english: The job centre's computer kept freezing, so the advisor helped me finish my application on paper.
records.zomi: Nasep zonna office' computer a khawl den ahih manin, thuhilhmi in ka ngetna laimai tungah zo dingin hong huh hi.

records.english: The computer won't turn on.
records.zomi: Computer a kihong thei kei hi.

records.english: The sound isn't working.
records.zomi: Aw a sem kei hi.

records.english: Volunteers who explain solutions patiently help residents become more independent.
records.zomi: Thuakzawhna taka bawlphat dan a hilhcian thalawp te in khuasung mite amau mahmah-a ding thei zaw dingin a huh uh hi.

records.english: Residents should be careful about sharing devices that contain private information.
records.zomi: Khuasung mite in mimal thu a nei van te hawm-ah a kidawm ding uh hi.

records.english: Many device problems can be solved by restarting, updating or checking cables.
records.zomi: Van buaina tampi pen kipat kik sak, update bawl, ahih kei leh cable en tawh a kibawlphat thei hi.

records.english: The library has a help desk.
records.zomi: Laibu inn in huhna dokhan khat a nei hi.
