records.english: Can stress really cause headaches?
records.zomi: Lungsim nawhsawhna in lu natna a tun sak taktak thei hiam?

records.english: Yes, tense muscles in the neck and shoulders often lead to headaches.
records.zomi: Thei hi, ngawng leh liang-a tha khauh te in lu natna a tun sak zel hi.

records.english: Should I talk to a doctor?
records.zomi: Damdawi siam tawh ka kikum ding hiam?

records.english: Feeling lonely in a new place is common, even for experienced travellers.
records.zomi: Mun thak khat-ah kikhamna kizak pen khualzin siam mi te adingin zong a tangpi ahi hi.

records.english: Where is the best place to eat here?
records.zomi: Hi-ah an nekna mun hoih pen koi ahi hiam?

records.english: Is the market open today?
records.zomi: Tuni-in sum-kuan mun a kihong hiam?

records.english: Can you recommend a good guide?
records.zomi: Lampi lakmi hoih khat hong gen thei ding hiam?

records.english: What was the strangest custom you noticed in the town you visited?
records.zomi: Na ve khuapi-ah na phawk ngeina lamdang pen bang ahi hiam?

records.english: Why do some travellers feel lonely in a new place even when it is beautiful?
records.zomi: Bang hangin khualzin mi pawlkhat in mun thak khat a hoih mahmah hang kikhamna a kizak uh hiam?

records.english: Without familiar faces or routines, even small tasks feel difficult, and the beauty can make the loneliness feel sharper.
records.zomi: A theih mite leh ni sim ngeina te a om kei uh leh, nasep neu te zong a haksa bang a kizak a, a hoihna in kikhamna a thuk zaw sak thei hi.

records.english: When we arrived in the mountain village after dark, every guesthouse was full.
records.zomi: Khua a mial khit ciangin mual khua-ah i tun ciangin, zinbuuk khempeuh a dim khin hi.

records.english: An old woman saw us standing in the square with our bags and invited us to sleep in her spare room.
records.zomi: Nu upa khat in i ip te uh tawh laizang-ah i ding uh a mu a, a inndan ki-awng-ah i ihmut nadingin hong sam hi.

records.english: We stayed with her for three nights, and she cried when we left.
records.zomi: Amah tawh zan thum i om uh a, i pai ciangin a kap hi.

records.english: What time does the museum open?
records.zomi: Museum bang hun-in a kihong hiam?

records.english: Answers about getting lost frequently include stories of kindness from strangers.
records.zomi: Lampi mangthang tawh kisai dawnna te in zin mi te' hehpihna tangthu te a huam zel hi.

records.english: What should a newcomer to the city avoid doing in the first week?
records.zomi: Khuapi-a hong tung thak mi khat in kal masa pen sungin bang a bawl loh ding kisam hiam?

records.english: Learning a few local phrases often changes how visitors are received.
records.zomi: Khuasung genna tawm khat sin in kanmi te bangci a kidawn uh hiam cih a khek zel hi.

records.english: Where do the locals go at weekends?
records.zomi: Kal tawp-in khuasung mite koi-ah a pai uh hiam?

records.english: Which place on your trip would you most like to visit again?
records.zomi: Na khualzinna-ah koi mun na ve kik nuam pen hiam?

records.english: Where can we buy a map?
records.zomi: Gam lim koi-ah i lei thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: Visiting a new place can change how people see their own home.
records.zomi: Mun thak khat ve in mite in amau' inn bangci a mu uh hiam cih a khek thei hi.

records.english: Answers about homesickness show that travel can be both exciting and difficult.
records.zomi: Inn lunggulhna tawh kisai dawnna te in khualzin pen a nuam a, a haksa zong ahi hi, cih a lak hi.

records.english: Questions about a new place help travellers plan their visits more wisely.
records.zomi: Mun thak tawh kisai dotna te in khualzin mi te in a ve nading uh pilna zaw-in a ciamteh nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Which local dish did you try first, and did you like it?
records.zomi: Koi khuasung an na ne masa a, na deih hiam?

records.english: What did you learn about your own home by visiting somewhere so different?
records.zomi: Mun tuam mahmah khat na ve in na inn tawh kisai bang na sin hiam?

records.english: What should we see first?
records.zomi: Bang i en masa ding uh hiam?

records.english: How much is a taxi to the station?
records.zomi: Station-ah taxi man bangzah hiam?

records.english: Did you feel homesick during your first month abroad?
records.zomi: Gamdang-ah na om kha masa pen sungin inn na lunggulh hiam?

records.english: Are the people here friendly?
records.zomi: Hi-a mite a lawm thei uh hiam?

records.english: Is this the way to the old town?
records.zomi: Hih pen khuapi lui-ah paina lampi ahi hiam?

records.english: Can we swim in the lake?
records.zomi: Dil-ah tuipeek i pai thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: Travellers who ask locals for advice often discover places no guidebook mentions.
records.zomi: Khuasung mite kiangah thuhilhna a ngen khualzin mi te in lampi lakna laibu khatmah in a gen lo mun te a mu zel uh hi.

records.english: Is it safe to walk at night?
records.zomi: Zan-in peel pen a bit hiam?

records.english: Why do some places feel welcoming as soon as you arrive?
records.zomi: Bang hangin mun pawlkhat in na tun phet ciangin hong dawn bang a kizak hiam?

records.english: Why did you decide to stay an extra week in the little fishing town?
records.zomi: Bang hangin ngasa man khuapi neu-ah kal khat beh om dingin na khensat hiam?

records.english: Is the castle worth visiting?
records.zomi: Kulhpi pen ve man a phu hiam?

records.english: Did you get lost on your first day in the new town?
records.zomi: Khuapi thak-a na ni masa pen-in lampi na mang hiam?

records.english: Twice, but both times a shopkeeper drew me a little map on a paper bag.
records.zomi: Vei nih, ahi zongin a vei nih in dawr neipa khat in laimai ip tungah gam lim neu khat hong suai sak hi.

records.english: How far is the waterfall?
records.zomi: Tuikhawng bangzah gamla hiam?

records.english: Sharing stories of visits helps others feel curious about the wider world.
records.zomi: Mun vehna tangthu hawm in mi dang te leitung zai zaw tawh kisai theih nuamna a nei sak hi.

records.english: How do we get to the beach?
records.zomi: Tuipi gei-ah bangci i tung ding uh hiam?

records.english: How did the local families welcome you when you arrived in their village?
records.zomi: A khua uh-ah na tun ciangin khuasung innkuan te in bangci hong dawn uh hiam?

records.english: What surprised you most about the food when you first visited the north?
records.zomi: Sang lam na ve masak pen ciangin an tawh kisai bang in hong lamdang sak pen hiam?

records.english: Stories of being welcomed by strangers encourage others to show hospitality.
records.zomi: Zin mi te' dawnna tangthu te in mi dang te zinmi dawn dingin a hanthawn hi.

records.english: How did your children cope with the long journey to the coast?
records.zomi: Tuipi gei-a khualzinna sau-ah na ta te in bangci a thuak zo uh hiam?

records.english: Where can we watch the sunset?
records.zomi: Ni tum koi-ah i en thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: Questions about a first visit often bring back vivid memories of sights, sounds and smells.
records.zomi: Ve masakna tawh kisai dotna te in muhna, zakna leh namna te' phawkna kician te a ciahpih kik zel hi.

records.english: Many travellers find that local advice leads them to the most memorable places.
records.zomi: Khualzin mi tampi in khuasung thuhilhna in phawk thupi pen mun te-ah a paipih hi, cih a mu uh hi.

records.english: Asking what surprised a traveller can reveal differences between cultures.
records.zomi: Khualzin mi khat bang in a lamdang sak hiam cih dot in ngeina tuam te' kibatloh a lak thei hi.

records.english: What was your first room in the capital like?
records.zomi: Gam khuapi lian pen-a na inndan masa pen bang bang ahi hiam?

records.english: A tiny space above a noodle shop, where the smell of soup came through the floor.
records.zomi: Noodle dawr tung-a mun neu mahmah khat, tua-ah inn nuai pan an-tui namna a hong lut hi.

records.english: Is there a pharmacy near here?
records.zomi: Hih kiangah damdawi zuakna mun khat a om hiam?

records.english: How did you find a place to stay when the hotels were all full?
records.zomi: Zinbuuk khempeuh a dim khin ciangin om nading mun bangci na mu hiam?

records.english: Do the buses run on Sundays?
records.zomi: Nipini-in bus te a pai uh hiam?

records.english: How did you find your way around the island without a map?
records.zomi: Gam lim om lo-in tuilai gam bangci na vak kim hiam?

records.english: I asked the fishermen every morning, and they always pointed me towards the best beaches.
records.zomi: Zingsang simin nga beng mi te ka dong a, tuipi gei hoih pen te lam-ah hong lak den uh hi.

records.english: How long did it take before the new city stopped feeling strange?
records.zomi: Khuapi thak in lamdang a kizak nawn loh nadingin hun bangzah a la hiam?

records.english: Will we need warm clothes?
records.zomi: Puan lum i kisam ding uh hiam?

records.english: How did you find out about the hidden valley that isn't in any guidebook?
records.zomi: Lampi lakna laibu khatmah-ah a om lo guam sel tawh kisai bangci na thei hiam?

records.english: How did you manage to buy train tickets without speaking the language?
records.zomi: Pau gen thei lo-in meileng lai bangci na lei thei hiam?

records.english: Is there a festival this week?
records.zomi: Hih kal-in pawi khat a om hiam?

records.english: What was the first thing you noticed when you arrived in the city?
records.zomi: Khuapi-ah na tun ciangin bang na phawk masa pen hiam?

records.english: The noise, because even at midnight the streets were full of cars and music.
records.zomi: Ging, bang hang hiam cih leh zanlai-in zong lampi te mawtaw leh la tawh a dim hi.

records.english: By the old road, do you mean the one through the forest or the one along the river?
records.zomi: Lampi lui na cih ciangin, gammang sung pai lampi na cihna hiam, tuipi gei pai lampi na cihna hiam?

records.english: The one along the river, which was washed away long before you were born.
records.zomi: Tuipi gei pai lampi, nang na pian ma sawt mahmah-in tui in a luang khin hi.

records.english: Do you mean before or after the war?
records.zomi: Gal ma-in na cihna hiam, gal khit-in na cihna hiam?

records.english: Explaining old expressions to children helps keep a family's way of speaking alive.
records.zomi: Gen dan lui te naupang te kiangah hilhcian in innkuan khat' gen dan a nungta lai nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Do you mean the market or the shop?
records.zomi: Sum-kuan mun na cihna hiam, dawr na cihna hiam?

records.english: Was that the boat or the bridge?
records.zomi: Tua pen gunkuang hi hiam, lei hi hiam?

records.english: By your first job, do you mean the one on the farm or the one in the shop?
records.zomi: Na nasep masa pen na cih ciangin, lo-a nasep na cihna hiam, dawr-a nasep na cihna hiam?

records.english: When you say Grandpa was a soldier, do you mean in the army or the police?
records.zomi: Pu galkap ahi hi na cih ciangin, galkap pawl-ah na cihna hiam, palik-ah na cihna hiam?

records.english: In the army, though he worked as a village guard after the war.
records.zomi: Galkap pawl-ah, ahi zongin gal khit-in khuasung ngaksuimi-in a sem hi.

records.english: When you say long ago, how long?
records.zomi: Nidang sawt mahmah na cih ciangin, bangzah sau hiam?

records.english: When you say the harvest failed, do you mean there was no food at all?
records.zomi: Gah lakna a sia hi na cih ciangin, an bangmah a om kei hi na cihna hiam?

records.english: When you say rich, how rich?
records.zomi: Hau hi na cih ciangin, bangzah hau hiam?

records.english: Asking politely what someone means shows that their story is being taken seriously.
records.zomi: Mi khat bang a cihna hiam cih zahtak taka dot in a tangthu a kingaihsut thupi hi, cih a lak hi.

records.english: Asking what an older relative means by a phrase often reveals a whole hidden story.
records.zomi: Upa khat in genna khat tawh bang a cihna hiam cih dot in a kisel tangthu bup khat a lak zel hi.

records.english: When you say the family was poor, do you mean you went hungry?
records.zomi: Innkuan a zawng hi na cih ciangin, gil kial-in na om uh hi na cihna hiam?

records.english: Some winters we did, but most of the time we simply had very few clothes and no money for school.
records.zomi: Khuaphal pawlkhat-in kial hi, ahi zongin a tamzaw-in puan tawm mahmah bek i nei uh a, sang adingin sum i nei kei uh hi.

records.english: What did your teacher mean when she called you a natural storyteller?
records.zomi: Na sangsia in a pianpih tangthu genmi hong ci ciangin bang a cihna hiam?

records.english: When you say the family moved to the city, do you mean everyone or just your father?
records.zomi: Innkuan khuapi-ah a tai uh hi na cih ciangin, mi khempeuh na cihna hiam, na pa bek na cihna hiam?

records.english: Did you mean the road or the path?
records.zomi: Lampi na cihna hiam, lampi neu na cihna hiam?

records.english: By the city, do you mean the capital?
records.zomi: Khuapi na cih ciangin, gam khuapi lian pen na cihna hiam?

records.english: When you say a big family, how many children?
records.zomi: Innkuan lian na cih ciangin, ta bangzah hiam?

records.english: Which school are you talking about?
records.zomi: Koi sang tawh kisai na gen hiam?

records.english: Clarifying vague memories helps families record their history more accurately.
records.zomi: Phawkna kician lo te hilhcian in innkuan te in a tangthu uh dik zaw-in a ciamteh nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: What did Great-Grandma mean when she called the hill the sleeping giant?
records.zomi: Pi-pu nu in mual pen a ihmu mi lianpi a ci ciangin bang a cihna hiam?

records.english: She meant its shape, because from the village it looks like a man lying on his back.
records.zomi: A lim a cihna ahi hi, bang hang hiam cih leh khuasung pan en leh mi khat a nungzang-a lum bang a kilang hi.

records.english: Some expressions used by grandparents only make sense once their background is explained.
records.zomi: Pu leh pi te' zat genna pawlkhat pen a nunglam thu kihilhcian khit ciangin bek a kitheisiam hi.

records.english: Did you mean the winter of the big snow?
records.zomi: Vuk tam khuaphal na cihna hiam?

records.english: Did you mean the old church or the new one?
records.zomi: Biakinn lui na cihna hiam, a thak na cihna hiam?

records.english: Clarifying a story can turn a vague memory into a precise piece of family history.
records.zomi: Tangthu khat hilhcian in phawkna kician lo khat innkuan tangthu kician khat-ah a khek thei hi.

records.english: What did your mother mean when she said the soldiers took everything?
records.zomi: Galkap te in bangkim a la uh hi, na nu in a cih ciangin bang a cihna hiam?

records.english: Do you mean Grandpa's father or his uncle?
records.zomi: Pu' pa na cihna hiam, a pa neu na cihna hiam?

records.english: Was the field yours or your uncle's?
records.zomi: Lo pen na lo hi hiam, na pa neu' lo hi hiam?

records.english: Do you mean your grandparents arrived here with nothing, or just with very little?
records.zomi: Na pu leh pi hi-ah bangmah nei lo-in a hong tung uh hi na cihna hiam, ahih kei leh tawm mahmah bek tawh na cihna hiam?

records.english: Old place names can confuse listeners until someone explains where they actually were.
records.zomi: Mun min lui te in kua hiam khat in a taktak-a a omna mun a hilhcian dong ngaimi te a lungmang sak thei hi.

records.english: When relatives remember the same event differently, asking what each one means can resolve the confusion.
records.zomi: Pi le pu te in thupiang khat mah tuam takin a phawk uh ciangin, a khat ciat bang a cihna uh hiam cih dot in lungmanna a bawlphat thei hi.

records.english: Which brother do you mean?
records.zomi: Koi unau pa na cihna hiam?

records.english: What did Grandma mean when she said the city changed your father?
records.zomi: Khuapi in na pa a khek hi, Pi in a cih ciangin bang a cihna hiam?

records.english: When you say the village was cut off, do you mean for days or for the whole winter?
records.zomi: Khuasung a kikhen hi na cih ciangin, ni tampi sung na cihna hiam, khuaphal bup na cihna hiam?

records.english: Questions that clarify meaning make family stories easier to pass on to future generations.
records.zomi: A cihna hilhcian dotna te in innkuan tangthu te khang hong tung ding te-ah a pia nading a baihlam zaw sak hi.

records.english: What did people in those days mean by a good marriage?
records.zomi: Tua hun lai-a mite in kiteenna hoih na ci ciangin bang a cihna uh hiam?

records.english: When you say you walked a long way, do you mean hours or days?
records.zomi: Gamla mahmah ka pai hi na cih ciangin, nai tampi na cihna hiam, ni tampi na cihna hiam?

records.english: Was that the first house or the second?
records.zomi: Tua pen inn masa pen hi hiam, a nihna hi hiam?

records.english: Which wedding do you mean?
records.zomi: Koi mopawi na cihna hiam?

records.english: When you say the factory was dangerous, what kind of accidents happened?
records.zomi: Factory a lauhuai hi na cih ciangin, bang accident te a piang hiam?

records.english: What did the elders mean when they said the river had a temper?
records.zomi: Tuipi in lungsim ngong a nei hi, upa te in a cih ciangin bang a cihna uh hiam?

records.english: Many family misunderstandings last for years because nobody asked what was really meant.
records.zomi: Innkuan theihkhialhna tampi pen bang a cihna taktak hiam cih kuamah in a dot loh manin kum tampi sung a om hi.

records.english: Which village was that, exactly?
records.zomi: Tua pen koi khua taktak hi hiam?

records.english: By the war, do you mean the first one your family lived through or the later one?
records.zomi: Gal na cih ciangin, na innkuan in a tuak masa pen gal na cihna hiam, a nung-a gal na cihna hiam?

records.english: Do you mean the house burned down completely, or only the roof?
records.zomi: Inn bup a kang khin hi na cihna hiam, inn tung bek na cihna hiam?

records.english: When you say the old days, what year?
records.zomi: Nidang hun na cih ciangin, bang kum hiam?

records.english: When my grandmother wrote that she had walked 'to the end of the world' to find work, we thought she was exaggerating.
records.zomi: Nasep zong dingin 'leitung tawp dong' ka pai hi, ci-in ka pi in a gelh ciangin, a lian lua sak hi, ci-in i ngaihsun uh hi.

records.english: Years later, we learned that the end of the world was what her village called the last bus stop before the mountains.
records.zomi: Kum tampi khit-in, leitung tawp pen a khua mite in mual te ma-a bus dinna nunung pen a ci uh ahi hi, cih i thei uh hi.

records.english: We drove there together on her ninetieth birthday, and she laughed when she saw the old sign still standing.
records.zomi: A pianni kum sawm kua ciangin khawm-in tua-ah mawtaw tawh i pai uh a, laimal lui a ding lai a muh ciangin a nuih hi.

records.english: Elders sometimes use understatement, so asking for details can reveal great hardship.
records.zomi: Upa te in hun khenkhat thu a niam sak-in a gen uh ahih manin, a kician zaw dot in haksatna lian te a lak thei hi.

records.english: When you say hard work, what did you do?
records.zomi: Nasep haksa na cih ciangin, bang na bawl hiam?

records.english: What did your father mean when he said the village had lost its heart after the school closed?
records.zomi: Sang a kikhak khit-in khuasung in a lungsim a mangsuah hi, na pa in a cih ciangin bang a cihna hiam?

records.english: He meant that without children walking through the square every morning, people stopped meeting and talking as they used to.
records.zomi: Zingsang simin laizang-ah naupang te a pai nawn kei uh ciangin, mite nidang bangin a kimu a kiho nawn kei uh hi, cih a cihna ahi hi.

records.english: Do you mean your mother or your aunt?
records.zomi: Na nu na cihna hiam, na ni na cihna hiam?

records.english: Words like poor, rich and far meant different things to earlier generations.
records.zomi: Zawng, hau leh gamla cih kammal te in khang masa te adingin cihna tuam a nei uh hi.

records.english: When Grandpa says he was the best student, does he mean in the class or in the whole school?
records.zomi: Sangnaupang hoih pen ka hi hi, Pu in a cih ciangin, tanglai sungah a cihna hiam, sang bup sungah a cihna hiam?

records.english: The library runs a monthly workshop on using public records to trace family history.
records.zomi: Laibu inn in innkuan tangthu zon nadingin mipi lai kemte zat dan tawh kisai kha simin sinna hun khat a bawl hi.

records.english: The records are kept in boxes.
records.zomi: Lai kemte bawm te sungah a kikem hi.

records.english: The volunteers helped my mother find her school records from sixty years ago.
records.zomi: Thalawp te in kum sawm guk a ma-a ka nu' sang lai kemte a muh nadingin a huh uh hi.

records.english: The council kept the records of the old market, which showed how prices changed over a century.
records.zomi: Council in sum-kuan mun lui' lai kemte a kem a, kum za khat sung man te bangci a kikhek hiam cih a lak hi.

records.english: How long does it usually take to get a certified copy of a marriage record?
records.zomi: Kiteenna lai kemte' a kiciaptehsa copy khat ngah nadingin a tamzaw-in hun bangzah a la hiam?

records.english: I found my grandmother's name.
records.zomi: Ka pi' min ka mu hi.

records.english: After the archive put its maps online, local schools began using them in history lessons.
records.zomi: Lai lui kemna inn in a gam lim te online-ah a koih khit ciangin, khuasung sang te in tangthu sinna-ah a zang kipan uh hi.

records.english: The old register is very fragile.
records.zomi: Min gelhna laibu lui a nem mahmah hi.

records.english: Does the archive hold records from the old village school?
records.zomi: Lai lui kemna inn in khuasung sang lui' lai kemte a kem hiam?

records.english: The archive has old photos of the town.
records.zomi: Lai lui kemna inn in khuapi' lim lui te a nei hi.

records.english: How can I find out whether my house was ever used as a shop?
records.zomi: Ka inn pen dawr-in a kizang ngei hiam cih bangci ka thei thei ding hiam?

records.english: Can I see the old maps?
records.zomi: Gam lim lui te ka en thei ding hiam?

records.english: When our residents' group wanted to save the old footpath, the landowner claimed it had never been public.
records.zomi: I khuasung mite' pawl in lampi neu lui kem a ut uh ciangin, gam neipa in mipi lampi a hi ngei kei hi, ci-in a gen hi.

records.english: A volunteer spent three days in the town archive and found a map from 1910 showing the path as a public right of way.
records.zomi: Thalawp khat in khuapi lai lui kemna inn-ah ni thum a zang a, tua lampi pen mipi paina lampi ahi hi, cih a lak kum 1910-a gam lim khat a mu hi.

records.english: The council accepted the evidence, and the path was reopened the following spring.
records.zomi: Council in ettehna a san a, a zom spring-in lampi a kihong kik hi.

records.english: I need a copy of my birth record.
records.zomi: Ka pianna lai kemte' copy khat ka kisam hi.

records.english: Schools that use local archives help pupils connect history with their own streets.
records.zomi: Khuasung lai lui kemna inn a zang sang te in sangnaupang te tangthu leh amau' lampi te a kizop sak nadingin a huh uh hi.

records.english: Archives preserve evidence that can settle local disputes fairly.
records.zomi: Lai lui kemna inn te in khuasung kinialna te dik taka a bawlphat thei ettehna te a kem uh hi.

records.english: The local history group published a booklet using records from the town archive.

records.zomi: Kammal lista pen sang website-ah a om hi.

records.english: Why did the clinic ask our community to agree on medical terms?
records.zomi: Bang hangin damdawi inn neu in i khuasung kiangah damdawi kammal te kisaipih dingin a ngen hiam?

records.english: Patients were confused because each interpreter used a different word for the same illness.
records.zomi: Pau lettu khat ciat in natna khat mah adingin kammal tuam a zat uh ahih manin damlo te a lungmang uh hi.

records.english: The Zomi teachers' group agreed on terms for mathematics so that pupils in different cities use the same words.
records.zomi: Zomi sangsia pawl in khuapi tuam-a sangnaupang te in kammal kibang a zat nadingin mathematics adingin kammal te a kisaipih uh hi.

records.english: Which term should I use for the hospital notice?
records.zomi: Damlo inn thugenna adingin koi kammal ka zang ding hiam?

records.english: Use the one in the health glossary, so that every clinic says the same thing.
records.zomi: Damna kammal lista-a om pen zang in, damdawi inn neu khempeuh in a kibang a gen nadingin.

records.english: My boss asked for the agreed term.
records.zomi: Ka makaipa in kammal kisaipih a ngen hi.

records.english: When I began translating safety notices at the factory, I found three different words for the same machine.
records.zomi: Factory-ah bitna thugenna te ka let kipat ciangin, seh khat mah adingin kammal tuam thum ka mu hi.

records.english: I asked the community's terminology group for advice, and they told me which word had been agreed for official documents.
records.zomi: Khuasung kammal pawl kiangah thuhilhna ka ngen a, official lai te adingin koi kammal a kisaipih hiam cih hong gen uh hi.

records.english: Now every notice in the factory uses that word, and new workers understand the warnings straight away.
records.zomi: Tu-in factory-a thugenna khempeuh in tua kammal a zang a, nasem thak te in vaihawmna te a manlang-in a theisiam uh hi.

records.english: The children learn the agreed terms.
records.zomi: Naupang te in kammal kisaipih te a sin uh hi.

records.english: The clinic uses the standard words.
records.zomi: Damdawi inn neu in kammal kisaipih te a zang hi.

records.english: Please use the agreed term.
records.zomi: Kammal kisaipih zang in, kong ngen hi.

records.english: Shared online lists allow communities in different countries to work together.
records.zomi: Online-a kihawm lista te in gam tuam-a khuasung te a sem khawm thei sak hi.

records.english: Could the terminology group suggest a word for the new machines at the factory?
records.zomi: Kammal pawl in factory-a seh thak te adingin kammal khat a gen thei ding hiam?

records.english: My colleague suggested a new term.
records.zomi: Ka nasep lawm in kammal thak khat a gen hi.

records.english: We have a new list of science terms.
records.zomi: Science kammal lista thak khat i nei uh hi.

records.english: The translators meet every month.
records.zomi: Pau lettu te kha simin a kikhawm uh hi.

records.english: Testing new terms with real users helps make them easier to accept.
records.zomi: Kammal thak te zangmi taktak te tawh sin in a san baihlam zaw nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: My cousin, who works as a translator, sends suggestions to the committee whenever she meets a new term.
records.zomi: Pau lettu-a a sem ka sanggam nu in kammal thak khat a tuak ciang khempeuh-in committee kiangah a ngaihsutna a khak hi.

records.english: My manager was pleased that every Zomi notice in the office now uses the same vocabulary.
records.zomi: Office-a Zomi thugenna khempeuh in tu-in kammal kibang a zat uh ahih manin ka manager a lungdam hi.

records.english: Which word do the teachers use?
records.zomi: Sangsia te in koi kammal a zang uh hiam?

records.english: Workplaces benefit when translated notices use consistent vocabulary.
records.zomi: Kilet thugenna te in kammal kibang a zat uh ciangin nasepna mun te in phattuamna a ngah uh hi.

records.english: Regional words remain valuable even when a standard term is agreed.
records.zomi: Kammal kisaipih khat a om hang gam khen khat kammal te a manpha lai hi.

records.english: The hospital interpreters met with community elders to agree on words for common illnesses.
records.zomi: Damlo inn pau lettu te in natna tangpi te adinga kammal kisaipih nadingin khuasung upa te tawh a kimu uh hi.

records.english: How does the committee decide between two words that are both widely used?
records.zomi: Mi tampi in a zat kammal nih kikal-ah committee in bangci a khensat hiam?

records.english: The Saturday school asked parents to use the standard terms when helping with homework.
records.zomi: Kiginni sang in inn nasep-ah a huh ciangin kammal kisaipih te zang dingin nu leh pa te a ngen hi.

records.english: Why is Good Friday called good if Jesus died that day?
records.zomi: Tua ni-in Jesu a sih leh bang hangin Good Friday a hoih ci-in a kisam hiam?

records.english: Christians believe his death brought forgiveness, so they see something good even in that sad day.
records.zomi: A sihna in maisakna a tun sak hi, ci-in Khazih mite in a um uh ahih manin, tua dah ni sungah zong hoihna khat a mu uh hi.

records.english: Many Christians see the cross as a symbol of both suffering and victory.
records.zomi: Khazih mi tampi in singlamteh pen thuakna leh zawhna a nih' lim khat bangin a mu uh hi.

records.english: How can we explain the crucifixion to young children without frightening them?
records.zomi: Naupang neu te lau sak lo-in singlamteh tunga kikhaina bangci i hilhcian thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: Tell them simply that Jesus was hurt and died, and then focus on the joy of Easter morning.
records.zomi: Jesu a kisual a, a si hi, ci-in baihlam takin gen in, tua khit-in Easter zingsang' lungdamna ngaihsun in.

records.english: Could we read the story of the women at the empty tomb together on Easter morning?
records.zomi: Easter zingsang-in han a ki-awng-a om numei te' tangthu khawm-in i sim thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: Family traditions at Easter help children connect the story with their own lives.
records.zomi: Easter hun-a innkuan ngeina te in naupang te tangthu leh amau' nuntakna a kizop nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Dad says Easter is a day of hope.
records.zomi: Easter pen lametna ni ahi hi, ci-in Pa in a gen hi.

records.english: We sing a special hymn on Easter morning.
records.zomi: Easter zingsang-in Labu-a la tuam khat i sa uh hi.

records.english: Did Jesus really come back to life, Dad?
records.zomi: Pa aw, Jesu a thokik taktak hiam?

records.english: Christians believe he did, and that's why Easter is our happiest celebration.
records.zomi: A thokik hi, ci-in Khazih mite in a um uh a, tua ahih manin Easter pen i pawi nuam pen ahi hi.

records.english: Why do some Christian families fast before Easter and others do not?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Khazih innkuan pawlkhat in Easter ma-in an a ngawl uh a, a dang te in a ngawl kei uh hiam?

records.english: Why was Jesus put on a cross?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Jesu singlamteh tungah a kikhai hiam?

records.english: Our family walks to the hill behind the village before dawn every Easter Sunday.
records.zomi: Easter Nipini khempeuh-in i innkuan in khua a vak ma-in khuasung nunglam mual tungah i peel uh hi.

records.english: My daughter was surprised that the disciples didn't recognise Jesus at first after he rose.
records.zomi: A thawhkik khit-in nungzuite in a masa-in Jesu a thei kei uh hi, cih ka tanu in a lamdang sa hi.

records.english: Christians believe that Jesus' death and resurrection open the way to forgiveness and new life.
records.zomi: Jesu' sihna leh thawhkikna in maisakna leh nuntakna thak lampi a hong hi, ci-in Khazih mite in a um uh hi.

records.english: My parents taught us that Good Friday is a day for quiet and Easter Sunday is a day for joy.
records.zomi: Good Friday pen dai taka om ni ahi a, Easter Nipini pen lungdam ni ahi hi, ci-in ka nu leh pa in hong sinsak uh hi.

records.english: Christian parents often explain Good Friday gently before celebrating Easter Sunday.
records.zomi: Khazih nu leh pa te in Easter Nipini a pawi uh ma-in Good Friday nem takin a hilhcian zel uh hi.

records.english: For many Christian families, Easter is the most joyful celebration of the year.
records.zomi: Khazih innkuan tampi adingin, Easter pen kum khat sung-a pawi lungdam pen ahi hi.

records.english: Many grieving Christians find hope in the belief that death is not the end.
records.zomi: Dah Khazih mi tampi in sihna pen a tawpna hi lo hi, cih upna-ah lametna a mu uh hi.

records.english: After the funeral, our family found comfort in the Easter promise of new life.
records.zomi: Vuina khit-in, i innkuan in Easter-a nuntakna thak kamciam-ah lungmuanna i ngah uh hi.

records.english: Why do we have a cross at home?
records.zomi: Bang hangin inn-ah singlamteh i nei uh hiam?

records.english: Every Good Friday, my father tells us how his own father kept the day in silence.
records.zomi: Good Friday khempeuh-in, ka pa in a pa in tua ni dai taka a kem dan hong gen hi.

records.english: Do your children know why Christians call Easter the most important festival?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Khazih mite in Easter pen pawi thupi pen a ci uh hiam cih na ta te in a thei uh hiam?

records.english: For many believers, the resurrection changes how they face their own fears.
records.zomi: Ummi tampi adingin, thawhkikna in amau' lauhna te bangci a tuak uh hiam cih a khek hi.

records.english: We light a candle on Easter Eve.
records.zomi: Easter nitak-in khawimeivaak khat i tan uh hi.

records.english: Our family goes to church on Good Friday.
records.zomi: I innkuan in Good Friday-in biakinn-ah a pai hi.

records.english: My son asked why Jesus died.
records.zomi: Bang hangin Jesu a si hiam ci-in ka tapa in a dong hi.

records.english: Grandma keeps a small cross by her bed.
records.zomi: Pi in a lupna kiangah singlamteh neu khat a kem hi.

records.english: When my son asked why Jesus didn't run away, we read about his prayer in the garden.
records.zomi: Bang hangin Jesu a tai kei hiam ci-in ka tapa in a dot ciangin, huan sung-a a thungetna i sim uh hi.

records.english: My grandmother lights a candle on Easter Eve for every family member who has died.
records.zomi: Ka pi in Easter nitak-in a si khin innkuan mi khat ciat adingin khawimeivaak a tan hi.

records.english: Our family fasts on Good Friday.
records.zomi: I innkuan in Good Friday-in an i ngawl uh hi.

records.english: Easter is my favourite celebration.
records.zomi: Easter pen ka deih pen pawi ahi hi.

records.english: Why does Grandma cry during the Easter service?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Easter biakna-ah Pi a kap hiam?

records.english: She says she cries with joy, because Easter reminds her that death is not the end.
records.zomi: Easter in sihna pen a tawpna hi lo hi, cih a phawksak ahih manin, lungdamna tawh ka kap hi, a ci hi.

records.english: We take spring flowers to the cemetery on Easter Monday.
records.zomi: Easter Pizing ni-in han mun-ah spring pak te i paipih uh hi.

records.english: For believers, the empty tomb is a sign that God's love is stronger than death.
records.zomi: Ummite adingin, han ki-awng pen Pasian' itna sihna sangin a hat zaw hi, cih lim khat ahi hi.

records.english: Why do Christians believe that Jesus' death can bring forgiveness?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Khazih mite in Jesu' sihna in maisakna a tun thei hi, ci-in a um uh hiam?

records.english: How do you explain to a teenager why the resurrection matters to Christians?
records.zomi: Bang hangin thawhkikna Khazih mite adingin a thupi hiam cih tangval khangno khat kiangah bangci na hilhcian hiam?

records.english: Why are there flowers on the cross at Easter?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Easter-in singlamteh tungah pak te a om hiam?

records.english: My daughter made a cross from sticks.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in singzang tawh singlamteh khat a bawl hi.

records.english: Mum says Easter is about new life.
records.zomi: Easter pen nuntakna thak tawh kisai ahi hi, ci-in Nu in a gen hi.

records.english: Our children decorate the cross with flowers on Easter morning to show that death has been defeated.
records.zomi: I ta te in Easter zingsang-in sihna a kizo khin hi, cih a lak nadingin singlamteh pak tawh a zem uh hi.

records.english: Who found the empty tomb?
records.zomi: Han ki-awng kua in a mu hiam?

records.english: My grandmother says that the cross reminds her how much God loves her family.
records.zomi: Singlamteh in Pasian in a innkuan bangzah a it hiam cih a phawksak hi, ci-in ka pi in a gen hi.

records.english: We greet each other with joy on Easter Sunday.
records.zomi: Easter Nipini-in lungdamna tawh cibai i kibuk uh hi.

records.english: Did Jesus' friends see him again?
records.zomi: Jesu' lawm te in amah a mu kik uh hiam?

records.english: Christian families often remember loved ones who have died during Easter services.
records.zomi: Khazih innkuan te in Easter biakna te-ah a si khin it mite a phawk zel uh hi.

records.english: Grandma reads about the empty tomb after breakfast on Easter Sunday.
records.zomi: Easter Nipini-in zingsang an khit-in Pi in han ki-awng tawh kisai a sim hi.

records.english: Christians from different traditions mark Holy Week in different ways.
records.zomi: Ngeina tuam-a Khazih mite in Holy Week lampi tuamtuam-in a kem uh hi.

records.english: Why do we eat fish on Good Friday?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Good Friday-in ngasa i ne uh hiam?

records.english: My husband reads the story of Thomas every Easter, because he says it gives doubters hope.
records.zomi: Ka pasal in lunglai mite lametna a pia hi, a cih ahih manin, Easter khempeuh-in Thomas tangthu a sim hi.

records.english: Why does our family find hope in the resurrection when someone we love dies?
records.zomi: Bang hangin i it mi khat a sih ciangin i innkuan in thawhkikna-ah lametna a mu hiam?

records.english: Christians believe that because Jesus rose from the dead, those who trust in him will also share in new life.
records.zomi: Jesu sihna pan a thokik ahih manin, amah a muang mite zong nuntakna thak-ah a kihel ding uh hi, ci-in Khazih mite in a um uh hi.

records.english: We paint eggs every Easter.
records.zomi: Easter khempeuh-in aktui i zial uh hi.

records.english: Why is the tomb empty?
records.zomi: Bang hangin han a ki-awng hiam?

records.english: When my mother was dying, she said the resurrection gave her courage to face death.
records.zomi: Ka nu a sih dek ciangin, thawhkikna in sihna a tuak nadingin hangsanna a pia hi, a ci hi.

records.english: The Easter after my father died, I didn't want to go to church at all.
records.zomi: Ka pa a sih khit-a Easter-in, biakinn-ah ka pai nuam mawk kei hi.

records.english: My daughter took my hand and said that Grandpa would want us to sing the Easter hymns he loved.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in ka khut a len a, Pu in a it Easter la te i sak dingin a deih ding hi, a ci hi.

records.english: I sang through my tears that morning, and for the first time since his death, I felt a little hope.
records.zomi: Tua zingsang-in ka kap kawm-in ka sa a, a sih khit-a a masa pen vei-in lametna tawm khat ka kizak hi.

records.english: When Grandma says those were hungry years, what did you eat?
records.zomi: Tua te pen kial kum te ahi hi, Pi in a cih ciangin, bang na ne uh hiam?

records.english: What was the teacher's name?
records.zomi: Sangsia' min bang hiam?

records.english: You said your uncle came home a different man; in what way?
records.zomi: Na pa neu mi tuam khat suak-in inn-ah a ciah hi na ci hi; bangci-in hiam?

records.english: When my grandmother mentioned that she had once missed a boat, I almost changed the subject.
records.zomi: Ka pi in gunkuang khat a tai sak ngei hi, a cih ciangin, kikumna ka khek tawp hi.

records.english: Instead I asked which boat, and she told me it had sunk that night with forty passengers on board.
records.zomi: Ahi zongin koi gunkuang hiam ci-in ka dong a, tua zan-in khualzin mi sawm li tawh a kiat hi, ci-in hong gen hi.

records.english: That single follow-up question gave me the story she had never told anyone in the family.
records.zomi: Tua dotna zom khat bek in innkuan sungah kuamah kiangah a gen ngei loh tangthu hong pia hi.

records.english: Did your mother find out?
records.zomi: Na nu in a thei kha hiam?

records.english: A careful listener notices the names and places that a storyteller mentions in passing.
records.zomi: Kilawm taka ngaimi in tangthu genmi in a gen kha min leh mun te a phawk hi.

records.english: And after you left home, how often did you write to your parents?
records.zomi: Huan inn na pawt khit-in, na nu leh pa kiangah bangzah vei lai na gelh hiam?

records.english: And what happened to the old mill after the river changed course?
records.zomi: Huan tuipi in a luanna a khek khit-in buhsuk inn lui bang a suak hiam?

records.english: It stood empty for years, and then a family turned it into a small bakery.
records.zomi: Kum tampi sung a ki-awng a, tua khit-in innkuan khat in moh suatna inn neu khat-ah a bawl hi.

records.english: Did the soldiers stay long?
records.zomi: Galkap te sawt a om uh hiam?

records.english: You mentioned the year the harvest failed; how did the family survive the winter?
records.zomi: Gah lakna a sia kum na gen hi; tua khuaphal innkuan in bangci a pal uh hiam?

records.english: We sold the cow, ate wild roots from the forest and borrowed rice from relatives in the next valley.
records.zomi: Bawng i zuak uh a, gammang pan zungbul te i ne uh a, a kiang guam-a pi le pu te pan buh i leitawi uh hi.

records.english: You mentioned a quarrel over the land; was it ever settled?
records.zomi: Gam tawh kisai kinialna na gen hi; a kibawlphat ngei hiam?

records.english: Children who learn to ask follow-up questions become the keepers of a family's memories.
records.zomi: Dotna zom dot a sin naupang te in innkuan' phawkna te a kem mi te a suak uh hi.

records.english: Following up a story on another day often brings out details that were forgotten the first time.
records.zomi: Ni dang khat-in tangthu khat zom kik in a masa vei-in a kimangngilh thu te a lak khia zel hi.

records.english: And what did the doctor do?
records.zomi: Huan damdawi siam in bang a bawl hiam?

records.english: Asking where, when and who helps turn a family anecdote into a reliable record.
records.zomi: Koi-ah, bang hun-in leh kua cih dot in innkuan tangthu tom khat muan huai lai kemte khat-ah a khek thei hi.

records.english: And after the fire, did anyone find out how it started?
records.zomi: Huan meikang khit-in, bangci a kipan hiam cih kua hiam in a thei kha hiam?

records.english: And how did the wedding end?
records.zomi: Huan mopawi bangci a bei hiam?

records.english: When you say the winter of the big snow, which year was that?
records.zomi: Vuk tam khuaphal na cih ciangin, tua pen bang kum hiam?

records.english: So who won the bet?
records.zomi: Huan sum kikoih kinialna kua in a zo hiam?

records.english: Did they ever find the stolen horse?
records.zomi: Kiguk sakol a mu kik uh hiam?

records.english: Did the dog find its way home after the storm?
records.zomi: Huihpi khit-in ui in inn-ah a ciahna lampi a mu hiam?

records.english: Many family histories are incomplete because nobody asked a second question while there was still time.
records.zomi: Innkuan tangthu tampi pen hun a om lai-in kuamah in dotna a nihna a dot loh manin a kicing kei hi.

records.english: You told me the family photo was lost; do you remember who was in it?
records.zomi: Innkuan lim a mang hi, hong ci hi; a sungah kua te a om uh hiam cih na phawk hiam?

records.english: Did you ever see her again?
records.zomi: Amah na mu kik ngei hiam?

records.english: When you talk about the long walk to the city, how many days did it take?
records.zomi: Khuapi-a khualzinna sau tawh kisai na gen ciangin, ni bangzah a la hiam?

records.english: Older relatives often stop at the edge of a painful memory unless someone gently asks what happened next.
records.zomi: Kua hiam khat in nem takin a zom-ah bang a piang hiam ci-in a dot kei leh, upa te in phawkna natna' gei-ah a khawl zel uh hi.

records.english: You said Grandpa kept a diary; does anyone still have it?
records.zomi: Pu in ni sim lai a gelh hi na ci hi; kua hiam in a nei lai hiam?

records.english: What did the house look like?
records.zomi: Inn pen bang bang ahi hiam?

records.english: You said Grandpa walked to school; how far was it?
records.zomi: Pu sang-ah a peel hi na ci hi; bangzah gamla hiam?

records.english: Seven kilometres each way, and he did it barefoot until he was ten.
records.zomi: Pai leh ciah kilometer sagih ciat, huan kum sawm a phak dong khedap lo-in a pai hi.

records.english: Who gave you the watch?
records.zomi: Khut-nai kua in hong pia hiam?

records.english: Earlier you said the letter arrived too late; what had it been trying to tell you?
records.zomi: A ma-in lai a nunung lua-in a tung hi na ci hi; bang hong hilh nuam hiam?

records.english: It was from my uncle, inviting me to join him abroad, but by the time it came he had already given my place to someone else.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu pan ahi a, gamdang-ah amah tawh kihel dingin hong sam hi, ahi zongin a tun ciangin ka mun mi dang khat kiangah a pia khin hi.

records.english: The best interviewers of older people ask short questions and leave long silences.
records.zomi: Mi upa te a dong hoih pen mi te in dotna tom te a dong a, dai hun sau te a nusia uh hi.

records.english: Did you keep the letter?
records.zomi: Lai pen na kem hiam?

records.english: So did the two brothers ever speak to each other again?
records.zomi: Huan unau pa nih a kiho kik ngei uh hiam?

records.english: Yes, at their mother's funeral, after twenty years of silence.
records.zomi: Kiho kik uh hi, kum sawm nih sung kiho lo khit-in a nu uh' vuina-ah.

records.english: And where did you sleep that night?
records.zomi: Huan tua zan-in koi-ah na ihmu hiam?

records.english: You said the village moved after the earthquake; where did everyone go?
records.zomi: Leiling khit-in khuasung a tai hi na ci hi; mi khempeuh koi-ah a pai uh hiam?

records.english: Following up on an old story can reveal links between relatives who never knew each other.
records.zomi: Tangthu lui khat zom kik in kithei ngei lo pi le pu te' kizopna a lak thei hi.

records.english: Was the driver hurt in the crash?
records.zomi: Mawtaw kisual-ah mawngpa a liam hiam?

records.english: A follow-up question about a single detail can bring a whole forgotten story to life.
records.zomi: Thu khat tawh kisai dotna zom khat in a kimangngilh tangthu bup khat a nungta kik sak thei hi.

records.english: And did you find the key?
records.zomi: Huan, kongkhak tawh na mu hiam?

records.english: So what did Grandma say?
records.zomi: Huan Pi in bang a gen hiam?

records.english: So when the new road arrived, did the village shop survive?
records.zomi: Huan lampi thak a tun ciangin, khuasung dawr a om lai hiam?

records.english: Were you still at school then?
records.zomi: Tua hun-in sang na kah lai hiam?

records.english: So when the stranger knocked at the door that night, did your mother let him in?
records.zomi: Huan tua zan-in zin mi in kongpi a kiu ciangin, na nu in a lut sak hiam?

records.english: Was the bridge ever rebuilt?
records.zomi: Lei a kilam kik ngei hiam?

records.english: Who told you the story first?
records.zomi: Kua in tangthu hong gen masa hiam?

records.english: Follow-up questions show storytellers that their memories are worth hearing in full.
records.zomi: Dotna zom te in tangthu genmi te a phawkna uh a bup-in zak man a phu hi, cih a lak hi.

records.english: So after the factory closed, how did your father find work?
records.zomi: Huan factory a kikhak khit-in, na pa in nasep bangci a mu hiam?

records.english: Local historians record follow-up answers as carefully as the original account.
records.zomi: Khuasung tangthu siam te in dotna zom dawnna te pen a bulpi genna bangmah-in kilawm takin a ciamteh uh hi.

records.english: You mentioned the first radio in the village; who owned it?
records.zomi: Khuasung-a radio masa pen na gen hi; kua' a hi hiam?

records.english: Earlier you said you nearly became a priest; what changed your mind?
records.zomi: A ma-in siampi na suak dek hi na ci hi; bang in na lungsim a khek sak hiam?

records.english: She asked me why I thought that, and I realised I had been told so by others for years.
records.zomi: Bang hangin tua bangin na ngaihsun hiam ci-in hong dong a, mi dang te in kum tampi sung tua bangin hong gen uh hi, cih ka phawk hi.

records.english: By the end of the hour, I had stopped apologising for needing help.

records.english: How will I know whether therapy is actually working for me?

records.english: You might notice small changes first, such as sleeping better, arguing less or coping more calmly with a difficult day.
records.zomi: A masa-in khekna neu te na phawk kha thei hi, ihmut hoih zaw, kinial tawm zaw ahih kei leh ni haksa khat lungnem zaw-in pal bang.

records.english: Can I bring my notes to the session?

records.english: Will you write down what I say?

records.english: Will I get medicine?

records.english: What's the difference between a counsellor and a psychiatrist?

records.english: A counsellor helps you talk through problems, while a psychiatrist is a doctor who can diagnose illness and prescribe medicine.
records.zomi: Thuhilhmi in na buaina te gen-in hong huh a, lungsim natna damdawi siam pen natna a thei thei a, damdawi a pia thei damdawi siam ahi hi.

records.english: Feeling worse briefly can be part of facing difficult memories in therapy.
records.zomi: Hun tom sung siat zaw kizak pen lungsim damdawi enna-ah phawkna haksa te tuak' khen khat ahi thei hi.

records.english: Why does my counsellor ask me to rate my mood every week?

records.english: Many people start with six to eight sessions, and then we decide together whether to continue.
records.zomi: Mi tampi in hun guk pan giat tawh a kipan uh a, tua khit-in zom ding hiam cih khawm-in i khensat ding uh hi.

records.english: Knowing what to do in a crisis between sessions is an important part of any plan.

records.english: Is it all right to feel nervous?

records.english: Why do some therapists set a fixed number of sessions from the start?

records.english: Can we meet online next time?

records.english: Do I have to lie on a couch during therapy?
records.zomi: Lungsim damdawi enna lai-in lupna tungah ka lum ding kisam hiam?

records.english: No, you'll sit in an ordinary chair, facing the therapist, and talk.
records.zomi: Kisam kei hi, lungsim damdawi siam ma-ah tutphah tangpi khat tungah na tu ding a, na gen ding hi.

records.english: Is it normal to cry in therapy?
records.zomi: Lungsim damdawi enna-ah kap pen a tangpi ahi hiam?

records.zomi: Lungsim damdawi siam khat keimah tawh a kituak hiam cih bangci ka thei thei ding hiam?

records.english: Could you explain what cognitive behavioural therapy involves?

records.english: What happens if I miss a session?

records.english: Asking practical questions at the start of therapy can ease much of the anxiety.
records.zomi: Lungsim damdawi enna' kipatna-ah dotna tangpi te dot in lunghimawhna tampi a nem sak thei hi.

records.english: Is it possible to get free therapy if I can't afford private fees?
records.zomi: Mimal man ka piak zawh kei leh man om lo lungsim damdawi enna ka ngah thei ding hiam?

records.english: Can I stop therapy whenever I want?

records.english: Yes, although it helps to have one last session to talk about how you're doing.

records.english: What should I do if I feel unsafe between appointments?

records.english: Honest feedback from clients helps therapists adjust their approach.
records.zomi: Thu ngenmi te' thuman ngaihsutna in lungsim damdawi siam te in a sep dan uh a kibawlphat thei nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Stories of chance meetings can encourage others to talk to people they meet on the road.
records.zomi: Kituahkhakna kimuhna tangthu te in mi dang te lampi tungah a kimu mite tawh kikum dingin a hanthawn thei hi.

records.english: What did the stranger on the train tell you about the city that the guidebook didn't?

records.english: How did you discover that the waiter came from your parents' village?

records.english: What did you talk about with the musician you met at the station?
records.zomi: Station-ah na kimuh la siam mi tawh bang na kikup uh hiam?

records.english: Many travellers remember the people they met more clearly than the sights they saw.
records.zomi: Khualzin mi tampi in a muh mun te sangin a kimuh mite kician zaw-in a phawk uh hi.

records.english: Asking how an encounter ended often reveals whether a friendship lasted.

records.english: Why do you think strangers are so willing to help travellers?

records.english: How did you end up spending the night with a family you'd only just met?
records.zomi: Na kimuh thak bek innkuan khat tawh zan khat bangci na om khak hiam?

records.english: Did they offer you tea?
records.zomi: Tea hong pia uh hiam?

records.english: Did you take a photo with the singer?
records.zomi: La sa mi tawh lim na kila hiam?

records.english: Why were you so surprised to see the man at the border crossing?
records.zomi: Bang hangin gamgi kantanna mun-ah tua pa na muh ciangin na lamdang sa mahmah hiam?

records.english: He had sold me a fake watch in another country two years earlier, and he recognised me at once.

records.english: Strangers met on journeys sometimes become lifelong friends.

records.english: Questions about unexpected encounters often lead to the best travel stories.

records.english: Answers about wildlife encounters often include useful lessons about safety.
records.zomi: Gam sa kimuhna tawh kisai dawnna te in bitna tawh kisai sinsakna phatuam te a huam zel hi.

records.english: How did you meet the family you stayed with in the mountains?
records.zomi: Mual te-ah na om pih innkuan bangci na kimu uh hiam?

records.english: Their son found us sheltering from the rain and invited us home for soup.
records.zomi: A tapa in guah pan i kiselna-ah hong mu a, an-tui ne dingin inn-ah hong sam hi.

records.english: Why did the monk invite you to stay for the evening prayers?

records.english: How did you react when you saw your old teacher on the beach so far from home?

records.english: What made you trust the stranger who offered to guide you through the market?

records.english: Where did you see the eagle?

records.english: Was the man really your cousin?

records.english: What did you do when the monkey grabbed your bag?

records.english: I stood still, and a market seller threw it a banana until it dropped the bag.
records.zomi: Dai takin ka ding a, sum-kuan mun-a zuakmi khat in a ip a puk sak dong banana a paih sak hi.

records.english: Was the dolphin close to the boat?

records.english: Did you keep in touch with them?
records.zomi: Amaute tawh na kizom lai uh hiam?

records.english: Chance meetings abroad can reveal surprising links between distant places.
records.zomi: Gamdang-a kituahkhakna kimuhna te in gamla mun te' kizopna lamdang te a lak thei hi.

records.english: How did the group of students on the mountain help you when you were lost?
records.zomi: Lampi na mang ciangin mual tunga sangnaupang pawl in bangci hong huh uh hiam?

records.english: Did the elephant in the road block your car for long?
records.zomi: Lampi tunga sai in na mawtaw sawt a khap hiam?

records.english: Unexpected encounters can change the course of a whole journey.
records.zomi: Lamen lo kimuhna te in khualzinna bup' lampi a khek thei hi.

records.english: Did meeting that couple on the cruise change where you travelled next?
records.zomi: Tembaw tunga na kimuh kiteen nih in na zom-a khualzinna mun a khek hiam?

records.english: Travellers who ask locals questions are more likely to experience unexpected kindness.
records.zomi: Khuasung mite a dong khualzin mi te in lamen lo hehpihna a tuak zaw uh hi.

records.english: Did you ever find out why the old woman left flowers on your doorstep?

records.english: Meeting someone from home in a faraway place can feel strangely comforting.
records.zomi: Gamla mun khat-ah inn pan mi khat kimuh in a lamdang takin lungmuanna a pia thei hi.

records.english: Did the camel really follow you?
records.zomi: Camel in hong zui taktak hiam?

records.english: Hospitality from strangers is one of the most common themes in travel stories.
records.zomi: Zin mi te' zinmi dawnna pen khualzin tangthu te-a thu tangpi pen te sung-a khat ahi hi.

records.english: Did the stranger tell you his name?
records.zomi: Zin mi in a min hong gen hiam?

records.english: Did you chat with anyone on the ferry?
records.zomi: Tuipi kantan gunkuang tungah kua hiam tawh na kiho hiam?

records.english: Did the woman speak your language?
records.zomi: Tua nu in na pau a gen thei hiam?

records.english: How did the shepherd find you?

records.english: Who invited you to the wedding?

records.english: Did the dog walk with you all day?

records.english: How long did you talk to her?

records.english: On a night bus across the desert, a passenger offered me some dates and asked where I was from.

records.zomi: Ka khuapi neu min ka gen ciangin, khualzin mi in a nuih a, a pu in tua khua' sang a lam hi, a ci hi.

records.english: We spent the rest of the journey comparing family stories until the sun rose over the dunes.

records.english: What happened after you met the retired pilot in the airport café?

records.english: We talked for an hour about his flights in the 1970s, and he later sent me a book of photographs from his career.

records.english: Were you scared of the bear?

records.english: Where did you meet the old fisherman?

records.english: Was the monkey friendly?

records.english: Unexpected encounters remind travellers that the world is smaller than it seems.

records.english: Who paid for dinner in the end?

records.english: Did the guide know your uncle?

records.english: Who was the woman who hugged you at the ferry terminal?

records.english: My old neighbour from the city, who moved to the islands ten years ago.

records.english: Why did the hotel owner refuse to let you pay for your room?

records.english: How did the children in the village react when they saw you arrive?

records.english: Did you share a taxi with them?
records.zomi: Amaute tawh taxi khat na tuang khawm uh hiam?

records.english: Why did the fisherman take you out to the island for free?

records.english: Who spotted the rot in the barn door?

records.english: Why did the cows stop giving milk?

records.english: Who found the hole in the boat?
records.zomi: Gunkuang-a kua kua in a mu hiam?

records.english: Why did the two villages argue about the water for so many years?

records.english: Why did the family quarrel about the house go on for a decade?

records.english: Older people often recall the moment a problem was finally understood more clearly than the problem itself.
records.zomi: Mi upa te in buaina mahmah sangin a tawp-a buaina a kitheisiam hun kician zaw-in a phawk zel uh hi.

records.english: How did you realise that the problem was the landlord and not the neighbours?

records.english: Did anyone know why the lights failed?

records.english: What did the engineers find when they finally opened up the dam?

records.english: What made the school realise that the children's poor marks came from hunger?

records.english: Why did the roof leak every winter?

records.english: Stories about old problems often show that the obvious cause was not the real one.

records.english: How did the doctor discover what was really making your brother so tired?

records.english: A careful account of a past problem is more useful than blaming the people involved.

records.english: Many family stories turn on the day someone finally named what everyone had been avoiding.

records.english: For three winters, our school's pipes burst during the first frost, and the caretaker repaired them each time.

records.english: In the fourth year, a new teacher traced the pipes outside and found that one stretch ran through an unheated shed.

records.english: Who realised the map was wrong?

records.english: Identifying the real cause of an old failure can prevent the same mistake in the next generation.

records.english: Why did the old bridge keep cracking every spring?
