records.english: Teenage helpers can make younger pupils more eager to learn their heritage language.
records.zomi: Khangno huhmi te in sangnaupang neu zaw te a pu leh pa pau sin a nuam zaw sak thei uh hi.

records.english: Our teacher gives us Zomi homework.
records.zomi: I sangsia in Zomi inn nasep hong pia hi.

records.english: At the end of term, the older pupils read their own Zomi poems to the whole community.
records.zomi: Sinna hun a bei ciangin, sangnaupang upa zaw te in amau' Zomi la-gelh te khuasung bup kiangah a sim uh hi.

records.english: Volunteer teachers are often the backbone of community language classes.
records.zomi: Thalawp sangsia te pen khuasung pau sinna te' nungzang ahi zel uh hi.

records.english: How do you keep the teenagers interested in Zomi class?
records.zomi: Khangno te Zomi sinna-ah bangci na deih sak den hiam?

records.english: We let them write short Zomi captions for videos about their own lives.
records.zomi: Amau' nuntakna tawh kisai video te adingin Zomi kammal tom te gelh dingin i phal uh hi.

records.english: How many pupils are in your class?
records.zomi: Na tanglai-ah sangnaupang bangzah a om uh hiam?

records.english: Our class sings at the end of term.
records.zomi: Sinna hun a bei ciangin i tanglai in la a sa hi.

records.english: Why did the Saturday school start training older pupils as helpers?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Kiginni sang in sangnaupang upa zaw te huhmi-in a hilh kipan hiam?

records.english: There weren't enough adult teachers, and the younger children listen closely to teenagers they admire.
records.zomi: Mi upa sangsia a kicing kei a, naupang neu te in a phat khangno te a ngai hoih mahmah uh hi.

records.english: How do you teach Zomi to a class where some children speak it at home and others don't?
records.zomi: Naupang pawlkhat in inn-ah a gen uh a, a dang te in a gen kei uh tanglai khat-ah Zomi pau bangci na sinsak hiam?

records.english: Do you teach Zomi at the Saturday school?
records.zomi: Kiginni sang-ah Zomi pau na sinsak hiam?

records.english: Yes, I teach the eight-year-olds, and we start every lesson with a song.
records.zomi: Sinsak hi, kum giat a pha te ka sinsak a, sinna khempeuh la tawh i kipan uh hi.

records.english: The class put on a play for parents.
records.zomi: Tanglai in nu leh pa te adingin lim bawl tangthu khat a lak uh hi.

records.english: Did the pupils enjoy today's story?
records.zomi: Tuni-a tangthu sangnaupang te in a nuam sa uh hiam?

records.english: Children learn a language faster when lessons connect to their own interests.
records.zomi: Sinna te amau' deihna te tawh a kizom ciangin naupang te in pau khat a manlang zaw-in a sin uh hi.

records.english: Our church sponsors the printing of Zomi worksheets for every class in the city.
records.zomi: I biakinn in khuapi-a tanglai khempeuh adingin Zomi nasep lai-ek te' print man a pia hi.

records.english: The teenagers in our class created a Zomi quiz app for their younger brothers and sisters.
records.zomi: I tanglai-a khangno te in a unau neu zaw te adingin Zomi dotna app khat a bawl uh hi.

records.english: Is there a training course for people who want to teach Zomi to children?
records.zomi: Naupang te Zomi pau sinsak nuam mite adingin sinna khat a om hiam?

records.english: The children learn a Zomi song each week.
records.zomi: Naupang te in kal simin Zomi la khat a sin uh hi.

records.english: Why does our Zomi teacher bring work documents to the advanced class?
records.zomi: Bang hangin i Zomi sangsia in sinna sang tanglai-ah nasep lai te a paipih hiam?

records.english: The teacher wants the older students to see how Zomi is used in real letters, notices and reports, not only in stories and songs.
records.zomi: Sangsia in sangnaupang upa zaw te in Zomi pau tangthu leh la te-ah bek hi lo-in, lai taktak, thugenna leh report te-ah bangci a kizang hiam cih a muh nadingin a deih hi.

records.english: My manager was surprised to learn that I spend my weekends teaching Zomi to children.
records.zomi: Ka kal tawp te naupang te Zomi pau sinsak-in ka zang hi, cih a theih ciangin ka manager a lamdang sa hi.

records.english: My daughter helps with the class now.
records.zomi: Tu-in ka tanu in tanglai-ah a huh hi.

records.english: Do you meet in the church hall?
records.zomi: Biakinn inn lian-ah na kikhawm uh hiam?

records.english: Workplaces that support community classes help languages thrive beyond the home.
records.zomi: Khuasung sinna te a huh nasepna mun te in pau te inn pua-ah zong a khang sak uh hi.

records.english: I prepare the lessons on Friday nights.
records.zomi: Laithai ni zan-in sinna te ka kiginsak hi.

records.english: Shared teaching materials save volunteers many hours of preparation.
records.zomi: Kihawm sinna van te in thalawp te' kiginsakna hun tampi a kem sak hi.

records.english: Our Zomi teachers meet once a term to share lesson ideas and teaching materials.
records.zomi: I Zomi sangsia te sinna hun khat-ah vei khat sinna ngaihsutna leh sinna van te hawm dingin a kikhawm uh hi.

records.english: The teenagers help the little ones.
records.zomi: Khangno te in a neu te a huh uh hi.

records.english: The pupils interviewed their grandparents in Zomi and presented the stories to the class.
records.zomi: Sangnaupang te in a pu leh pi te uh Zomi pau-in a dong uh a, a tangthu te tanglai kiangah a lak uh hi.

records.english: Mixed-ability classes require teachers to plan activities for very different levels.
records.zomi: Siamna tuamtuam nei tanglai te in sangsia te a ciang tuam mahmah te adingin sepna ciamteh dingin a kisam hi.

records.english: The school has a new Zomi reading book.
records.zomi: Sang in Zomi sim laibu thak khat a nei hi.

records.english: Can my workplace help with our community's Zomi lessons?
records.zomi: Ka nasepna mun in i khuasung' Zomi sinna-ah a huh thei ding hiam?

records.english: Yes, the company lets us use its meeting room on Saturday mornings for free.
records.zomi: Thei hi, company in Kiginni zingsang-in a kikhopna inndan man om lo-in zang dingin hong phal hi.

records.english: My colleague teaches Zomi too.
records.zomi: Ka nasep lawm in zong Zomi pau a sinsak hi.

records.english: Which volunteer runs the reading corner?
records.zomi: Koi thalawp in laisimna mun a makaih hiam?

records.english: My boss lent us a room for the lessons.
records.zomi: Ka makaipa in sinna adingin inndan khat hong leitawi hi.

records.english: The youngest pupils learn the Zomi names of colours by sorting coloured blocks.
records.zomi: Sangnaupang neu pen te in a pianzia tuam bawm neu te a khen-in pianzia' Zomi min te a sin uh hi.

records.english: Who prints the worksheets?
records.zomi: Nasep lai-ek te kua in a print hiam?

records.english: Presenting work to the community gives pupils a reason to practise carefully.
records.zomi: Nasep te khuasung kiangah lak in sangnaupang te kilawm taka kisin nading a hang khat a pia hi.

records.english: The pupils wrote letters in Zomi.
records.zomi: Sangnaupang te in Zomi pau-in lai a gelh uh hi.

records.english: When I started teaching the Zomi class at our community centre, only five children came.
records.zomi: I khuasung inn-ah Zomi sinna ka sinsak kipat ciangin, naupang nga bek a hong pai uh hi.

records.english: I asked their parents what the children enjoyed, and I began each lesson with a game based on their favourite cartoons.
records.zomi: Naupang te in bang a nuam sa uh hiam ci-in a nu leh pa te uh ka dong a, a deih pen cartoon te tungah a kinga kawmna khat tawh sinna khempeuh ka kipat sak hi.

records.english: By the end of the year, twenty-three children were coming every week, and some of them brought their cousins.
records.zomi: Kum a bei ciangin, kal simin naupang sawm nih leh thum a hong pai uh a, pawlkhat in a sanggam te uh a paipih uh hi.

records.english: Exam pressure at school can make it hard for families to keep up weekend classes.
records.zomi: Sang-a sinna kisinna nawhsawhna in innkuan te kal tawp sinna te a zom lai nadingin a haksa sak thei hi.

records.english: My colleague who teaches primary school showed us how to plan a lesson with clear aims.
records.zomi: Naupang sang-a sinsak ka nasep lawm in ngimna kician tawh sinna khat bangci ciamteh ding hiam cih hong lak hi.

records.english: My son loves his Zomi teacher.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in a Zomi sangsia a it mahmah hi.

records.english: The Saturday school gives each pupil a certificate when they can read a Zomi story aloud.
records.zomi: Kiginni sang in Zomi tangthu khat ging taka a sim thei ciangin sangnaupang khat ciat certificate khat a pia hi.

records.english: Does the lesson start before ten?
records.zomi: Sinna nai sawm ma-in a kipan hiam?

records.english: When my daughter became a classroom helper, her own Zomi improved more than ever.
records.zomi: Ka tanu tanglai huhmi a suak ciangin, amah' Zomi pau nidang sangin a hoih zaw mahmah hi.

records.english: Training for volunteer teachers improves the quality and consistency of lessons.
records.zomi: Thalawp sangsia te adinga sinna in sinna te' hoihna leh kibatna a hoih zaw sak hi.

records.english: After work on Fridays, I plan the Zomi lesson for the next morning with two other volunteers.
records.zomi: Laithai ni nasep khit-in, thalawp dang nih tawh a zom zingsang-a Zomi sinna ka ciamteh hi.

records.english: We use picture cards in class.
records.zomi: Tanglai-ah lim card te i zang uh hi.

records.english: My work schedule changed, so another volunteer now teaches my Saturday group.
records.zomi: Ka nasep hun a kikhek ahih manin, tu-in thalawp dang khat in ka Kiginni pawl a sinsak hi.

records.english: Could the university students help us make Zomi teaching videos for the Saturday school?
records.zomi: University sangnaupang te in Kiginni sang adingin Zomi sinsakna video bawl dingin hong huh thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: Why did the disciples look up?
records.zomi: Bang hangin nungzuite van lam a et uh hiam?

records.english: On Ascension Day, my grandfather always took us up the hill behind our house before breakfast.
records.zomi: Ascension Day-in, ka pu in zingsang an ma-in i inn nunglam mual tungah hong paipih den hi.

records.english: He read the story of the disciples watching Jesus rise into the sky, and then he asked each of us to say one prayer.
records.zomi: Nungzuite in Jesu van-ah a kilato a et uh tangthu a sim a, tua khit-in ka khat ciat thungetna khat ngen dingin hong ngen hi.

records.english: Now that he has died, my children and I still climb the same hill every year to remember him.
records.zomi: Tu-in a si khin hang, ka ta te leh kei amah phawk dingin kum simin mual khat mah tungah i kahto lai uh hi.

records.english: Dad says Jesus will come again.
records.zomi: Jesu hong kumsuk kik ding hi, ci-in Pa in a gen hi.

records.english: Will Grandpa see Jesus in heaven?
records.zomi: Pu in vantung-ah Jesu a mu ding hiam?

records.english: Mum, where did Jesus go when he left his friends?
records.zomi: Nu aw, Jesu in a lawm te a nusiat ciangin koi-ah a pai hiam?

records.english: Christians believe he went up to be with God in heaven, and that he still cares for us.
records.zomi: Vantung-ah Pasian tawh om dingin a kahto hi, huan tu dong hong kem lai hi, ci-in Khazih mite in a um uh hi.

records.english: Christian families often connect the hope of Christ's return with comfort in grief.
records.zomi: Khazih innkuan te in Khazih' hong kumsuk kikna lametna leh dahna-a lungmuanna a kizop sak zel uh hi.

records.english: Our family prays together every night.
records.zomi: I innkuan in zan simin khawm-in thu i ngen uh hi.

records.english: Grandpa says we should always be ready.
records.zomi: Kiging den ding i hi uh hi, ci-in Pu in a gen hi.

records.english: My father taught us that waiting for Christ's return means caring for others in the meantime.
records.zomi: Khazih' hong kumsuk kikna ngak pen tua sungin mi dang kem cihna ahi hi, ci-in ka pa in hong sinsak hi.

records.english: We read from Acts at dinner tonight.
records.zomi: Tuni zan-in nitak an lai-in Sawltakte Thuhilhna pan i sim uh hi.

records.english: We light candles on Ascension Eve and pray for relatives who live far away.
records.zomi: Ascension Day ma nitak-in khawimeivaak i tan uh a, gamla-a om pi le pu te adingin thu i ngen uh hi.

records.english: For many Christian families, Ascension Day is a time to remember that Jesus reigns with God.
records.zomi: Khazih innkuan tampi adingin, Ascension Day pen Jesu Pasian tawh a uk hi, cih phawk hun ahi hi.

records.english: Will Jesus really come back one day?
records.zomi: Jesu ni khat-in a hong kumsuk kik taktak ding hiam?

records.english: Christians believe he will, and Grandpa says we should live kindly every day while we wait.
records.zomi: Hong kumsuk kik ding hi, ci-in Khazih mite in a um uh a, i ngak lai-in ni simin hehpihna tawh i nungta ding uh hi, ci-in Pu in a gen hi.

records.english: Christian parents often explain the second coming as a promise of joy rather than fear.
records.zomi: Khazih nu leh pa te in a nihna-a hong pai kikna pen lauhna sangin lungdamna kamciam khat bangin a hilhcian zel uh hi.

records.english: My son asked if Jesus can see us.
records.zomi: Jesu in hong mu thei hiam ci-in ka tapa in a dong hi.

records.english: Our family walks to church that morning.
records.zomi: Tua zingsang-in i innkuan in biakinn-ah i peel uh hi.

records.english: Grandma waves at the sky and smiles.
records.zomi: Pi in van lam-ah a khut a ham a, a nuih hi.

records.english: Why did Jesus go to heaven?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Jesu vantung-ah a pai hiam?

records.english: My son made a card for Ascension Day.
records.zomi: Ka tapa in Ascension Day adingin card khat a bawl hi.

records.english: We sing a hymn about Christ's return.
records.zomi: Khazih' hong kumsuk kikna tawh kisai la khat i sa uh hi.

records.english: After my father's funeral, my mother found comfort in the belief that Christ will one day return.
records.zomi: Ka pa' vuina khit-in, ka nu in Khazih ni khat-in hong kumsuk kik ding hi, cih upna-ah lungmuanna a ngah hi.

records.english: Every Ascension Day, my aunt invites the whole family for a meal after the church service.
records.zomi: Ascension Day khempeuh-in, biakna khit-in ka ni in innkuan bup nitak an ne dingin a sam hi.

records.english: My grandfather kept a note in his Bible with the words "He will come again" in his own handwriting.
records.zomi: Ka pu in a Lai Siangtho sungah amah' khut tawh "Hong kumsuk kik ding hi" cih kammal a kigelh lai neu khat a kem hi.

records.english: We go to church on Ascension Day.
records.zomi: Ascension Day-in biakinn-ah i pai uh hi.

records.english: Mum lights a candle on Ascension Day.
records.zomi: Ascension Day-in Nu in khawimeivaak a tan hi.

records.english: My wife reminds the children that Jesus promised to send the Holy Spirit after he left.
records.zomi: Jesu in a pawt khit-in Kha Siangtho hong sawl ding hi, ci-in a ciam hi, cih ka zi in ta te a phawksak hi.

records.english: Our children asked their grandfather why the disciples went back to Jerusalem so happily.
records.zomi: I ta te in bang hangin nungzuite lungdam mahmah-in Jerusalem-ah a ciah kik uh hiam ci-in a pu uh a dong uh hi.

records.english: Why do some Christian families celebrate Ascension Day while others hardly notice it?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Khazih innkuan pawlkhat in Ascension Day a pawi uh a, a dang te in a phawk mawk kei uh hiam?

records.english: Why does Grandma say "Come, Lord Jesus" before she sleeps?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pi in a ihmut ma-in "Topa Jesu aw, hong pai ta in" a ci hiam?

records.english: She says it's a prayer of hope that Jesus will return and make everything right.
records.zomi: Jesu hong kumsuk kik a, bangkim a dik sak ding hi, cih lametna thungetna khat ahi hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Grandma reads the ascension story to us.
records.zomi: Pi in van-ah kilato tangthu hong sim sak hi.

records.english: Many Christians see the ascension as a reminder that Jesus is not limited to one place.
records.zomi: Khazih mi tampi in Jesu' van-ah kilatona pen Jesu mun khat bek-ah a kikhak kei hi, cih phawksakna khat bangin a mu uh hi.

records.english: When my mother was very ill, she said that the hope of Christ's return gave her peace.
records.zomi: Ka nu a na mahmah ciangin, Khazih' hong kumsuk kikna lametna in nopna a pia hi, a ci hi.

records.english: My daughter drew a cloud and a cross.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in meii khat leh singlamteh khat a suai hi.

records.english: Our church has a picnic after the service.
records.zomi: Biakna khit-in i biakinn in gam pua-ah an ne khawmna a bawl hi.

records.english: For believers, the promise that Jesus will come again shapes how they face the future.
records.zomi: Ummite adingin, Jesu hong kumsuk kik ding hi, cih kamciam in hun ding a tuak dan uh a bawl hi.

records.english: Could we read the last chapter of Luke together as a family on Ascension Day?
records.zomi: Ascension Day-in innkuan khawm-in Luka' a tawpna khen i sim thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: Christians believe that the ascension marked the beginning of a new kind of presence among believers.
records.zomi: Jesu' van-ah kilatona in ummite lakah a omna thak khat' kipatna a lak hi, ci-in Khazih mite in a um uh hi.

records.english: Our family pastor told us that nobody, not even the angels, knows when Christ will return.
records.zomi: Khazih bang hun-in hong kumsuk kik ding hiam cih kuamah in a thei kei hi, vantung mite zong in a thei kei uh hi, ci-in i innkuan pastor in hong gen hi.

records.english: My daughter was worried about the end of the world until her teacher explained the Christian hope of joy.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in a sangsia in Khazih lungdamna lametna a hilhcian ma-in leitung tawpna tawh kisai a lunghimawh hi.

records.english: Family traditions on Ascension Day help children remember the story year after year.
records.zomi: Ascension Day-a innkuan ngeina te in naupang te kum simin tangthu a phawk nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: My grandmother says she feels close to God whenever she remembers that Jesus went to heaven.
records.zomi: Jesu vantung-ah a pai hi, cih a phawk ciang khempeuh-in Pasian a nai bang a kizak hi, ci-in ka pi in a gen hi.

records.english: When my son asked whether Jesus was lonely in heaven, my husband smiled and said he was with God.
records.zomi: Jesu vantung-ah a kikham hiam ci-in ka tapa in a dot ciangin, ka pasal a nuih a, Pasian tawh a om hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Many Christians find hope in the belief that Christ will return to make all things new.
records.zomi: Khazih mi tampi in Khazih in bangkim thak sak dingin hong kumsuk kik ding hi, cih upna-ah lametna a mu uh hi.

records.english: Why does our church read about the ascension forty days after Easter?
records.zomi: Bang hangin i biakinn in Easter khit ni sawm li ciangin van-ah kilato tawh kisai a sim hiam?

records.english: Christian traditions hold a range of views about how and when Christ will return.
records.zomi: Khazih ngeina te in Khazih bangci leh bang hun-in hong kumsuk kik ding hiam cih tawh kisai ngaihdan tuamtuam a nei uh hi.

records.english: How should we talk to the children about Christ's return without scaring them?
records.zomi: Khazih' hong kumsuk kikna tawh kisai naupang te lau sak lo-in bangci i gen ding uh hiam?

records.english: Tell them Christians see it as a day of joy, when God will wipe away every tear.
records.zomi: Khazih mite in Pasian in khitui khempeuh a nul siang sak ding ni, lungdamna ni khat bangin a mu uh hi, ci-in hilh in.

records.english: Is Ascension Day a holiday here?
records.zomi: Hi-ah Ascension Day pen tawlngakni ahi hiam?

records.english: Grandpa painted a picture of the ascension.
records.zomi: Pu in van-ah kilato lim khat a zial hi.

records.english: Mum keeps a small Bible by the door.
records.zomi: Nu in kongpi kiangah Lai Siangtho neu khat a kem hi.

records.english: Does anyone know the day Jesus will return?
records.zomi: Jesu hong kumsuk kik ding ni kua hiam in a thei hiam?

records.english: For many believers, waiting for Christ's return means living faithfully in everyday life.
records.zomi: Ummi tampi adingin, Khazih' hong kumsuk kikna ngak pen ni sim nuntakna-ah ummanna tawh nungta cihna ahi hi.

records.english: Why did your father keep his best clothes ready when he was very old?
records.zomi: Na pa a upa mahmah ciangin bang hangin a puan hoih pen te a kiging-in a kem hiam?

records.english: He believed that Christ could return at any time, and he liked to say he wanted to be ready to welcome him.
records.zomi: Khazih hun khempeuh-in hong kumsuk kik thei hi, ci-in a um a, amah dawn dingin kiging ka deih hi, ci-in a gen nuam hi.

records.english: How do you explain to a teenager what Christians mean by the second coming?
records.zomi: Khazih mite in a nihna-a hong pai kikna a cih uh bang a cihna hiam cih tangval khangno khat kiangah bangci na hilhcian hiam?

records.english: When the doctor's visits stopped, how did the village find another way to get medicine?
records.zomi: Damdawi siam' hong ve a khawl ciangin, khuasung in damdawi ngah nading lampi dang bangci a mu hiam?

records.english: Many communities solved past crises by combining several modest ideas.
records.zomi: Khuasung tampi in nidang buaina lian te ngaihsutna neu tampi gawm-in a bawlphat uh hi.

records.english: Older relatives often remember the person whose suggestion finally solved a problem.
records.zomi: Upa te in a tawp-in buaina khat a bawlphat genna a gen mi a phawk zel uh hi.

records.english: How did they keep the seeds dry?
records.zomi: Khaici te bangci-in a keu takin a kem uh hiam?

records.english: How did the two families finally agree on where to put the boundary fence?
records.zomi: Gamgi huang koi-ah koih ding hiam cih innkuan nih in a tawp-in bangci a kisaipih uh hiam?

records.english: When the river changed course, how did the farmers get water to their fields?
records.zomi: Tuipi in a luanna a khek ciangin, lo neite in a lo uh-ah tui bangci a tun sak uh hiam?

records.english: Did anyone try a different way?
records.zomi: Kua hiam in lampi tuam khat a sin hiam?

records.english: Whose idea was the bamboo bridge?
records.zomi: Ma lei pen kua' ngaihsutna ahi hiam?

records.english: How long did the repair take?
records.zomi: Bawlphatna in hun bangzah a la hiam?

records.english: Who lent them the money?
records.zomi: Kua in sum a leitawi uh hiam?

records.english: How did Grandma keep the family fed when the harvest failed?
records.zomi: Gah lakna a sia ciangin Pi in innkuan an bangci a vak hiam?

records.english: She swapped her silver bracelets for sacks of rice and grew beans on every bit of spare ground.
records.zomi: A ngun khutbuh te buh ip tawh a khek a, mun awng khempeuh-ah be a suan hi.

records.english: What did the family decide in the end?
records.zomi: A tawp-in innkuan in bang a khensat uh hiam?

records.english: Hearing how elders solved problems helps young people feel less helpless about their own.
records.zomi: Upa te in buaina bangci a bawlphat uh hiam cih zak in khangno te amau' buaina tungah a thuneihna nei lo bang a kizak lo nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Did the plan work in the end?
records.zomi: A tawp-in ciamteh a sem hiam?

records.english: A story about a failed plan can teach as much as a story about a successful one.
records.zomi: Ciamteh sia khat tangthu in ciamteh lawhcing khat tangthu bangmah-in a sinsak thei hi.

records.english: How did they pay for the new roof?
records.zomi: Inn tung thak man bangci a pia uh hiam?

records.english: How did your grandmother manage to keep the business going after Grandpa died?
records.zomi: Pu a sih khit-in na pi in sumbawlna bangci a zom thei hiam?

records.english: Asking how a village survived a crisis can reveal forgotten skills and customs.
records.zomi: Khuasung khat in buaina lian khat bangci a pal hiam cih dot in a kimangngilh siamna leh ngeina te a lak thei hi.

records.english: How did the farmers solve the problem of wild pigs eating the maize?
records.zomi: Gam vok te in vainim a nek buaina lo neite in bangci a bawlphat uh hiam?

records.english: Did the first plan fail?

records.zomi: Sangpi heutu a lut ciangin i ding uh hi.

records.english: Why do some Zomi teenagers feel shy about greeting elders traditionally at school events?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Zomi khangno pawlkhat in sang thupiang te-ah upa te ngeina bangin cibai buk a zum uh hiam?

records.english: Our class invited an elder to explain why greetings matter so much in Zomi families.
records.zomi: I tanglai in bang hangin Zomi innkuan te-ah cibai bukna a thupi mahmah hiam cih hilhcian dingin upa khat a sam uh hi.

records.english: Were the elders pleased with the pupils?
records.zomi: Upa te in sangnaupang te tungah a lungdam uh hiam?

records.english: My manager asked about our greetings.
records.zomi: Ka manager in i cibai bukna tawh kisai a dong hi.

records.english: Should I greet my Zomi manager the traditional way at work?
records.zomi: Nasep-ah ka Zomi manager ngeina bangin cibai ka buk ding hiam?

records.english: A handshake is fine at the office, but a slight bow shows extra respect.
records.zomi: Office-ah khut kilen a hoih hi, ahi zongin neu taka kun in zahtakna belh a lak hi.

records.english: The new teacher greeted us in Zomi.
records.zomi: Sangsia thak in Zomi pau-in hong cibai buk hi.

records.english: My colleague from another country learned our greeting by watching how I greeted my uncle at the office.
records.zomi: Gam dang pan ka nasep lawm in office-ah ka pa neu cibai ka buk dan a en-in i cibai bukna a sin hi.

records.english: The head teacher greeted the Zomi parents at the door during the open evening.
records.zomi: Kihon nitak-in sangpi heutu in kongpi-ah Zomi nu leh pa te cibai a buk hi.

records.english: Shall our class make a poster about greetings?
records.zomi: I tanglai in cibai bukna tawh kisai lim-lai khat i bawl ding uh hiam?

records.english: How should a young Zomi doctor greet older patients at the clinic?
records.zomi: Zomi damdawi siam khangno khat in damdawi inn neu-ah damlo upa zaw te bangci cibai a buk ding hiam?

records.english: A greeting can show respect even when people do not share a language.
records.zomi: Mite in pau kibang a nei kei uh hang cibai bukna khat in zahtakna a lak thei hi.

records.english: Could the youth group teach the new teachers how Zomi families greet each other?
records.zomi: Khangno pawl in sangsia thak te Zomi innkuan te bangci a kicibai buk uh hiam cih a sinsak thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: The school asked Zomi parents to record short videos showing how they greet elders.
records.zomi: Sang in Zomi nu leh pa te upa te bangci cibai a buk uh hiam cih a lak video tom te ciamteh dingin a ngen hi.

records.english: Why did your company ask you to explain Zomi greetings to new staff?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na company in nasem thak te kiangah Zomi cibai bukna hilhcian dingin hong ngen hiam?

records.english: Many of our customers are older Zomi people, and the manager wanted the staff to greet them in a way that feels respectful.
records.zomi: I leilei mi tampi pen Zomi mi upa te ahi uh a, manager in nasem te in zahtak huai bang a kizak lampi-in cibai a buk nadingin a deih hi.

records.english: The interpreter greeted each elder first before starting her work at the meeting.
records.zomi: Kikhopna-ah a nasep a kipat ma-in pau lettu in upa khat ciat a masa-in cibai a buk hi.

records.english: Who will look after Grandma at Christmas?
records.zomi: Christmas-in kua in Pi a kem ding hiam?

records.english: Who will be our new neighbour?
records.zomi: Kua in i inn kiang mi thak a suak ding hiam?

records.english: Who would you choose as a mentor if you started a new career?
records.zomi: Nasep thak khat na kipat leh kua na makaih dingin na teel ding hiam?

records.english: Who's going to be your bridesmaid?
records.zomi: Kua in na mopawi nungak huhmi a hi ding hiam?

records.english: My best friend from school, if my friend can get time off work in June.
records.zomi: Sang-a ka lawm kinai pen, June kha-in a nasep pan tawlngak a ngah thei leh.

records.english: Who's going to help Dad move the furniture when we change houses?
records.zomi: Inn i tai ciangin kua in Pa inn van te a suan dingin a huh ding hiam?

records.english: Who do you plan to invite to your fortieth birthday?
records.zomi: Na pianni kum sawm li-ah kua te sam dingin na ciamteh hiam?

records.english: Who's organising the reunion?
records.zomi: Kikhawm kikna kua in a ciamteh hiam?

records.english: Who's likely to be chosen as captain for next season?
records.zomi: A zom hun adingin kua makai dingin a kiteel kha ding hiam?

records.english: Who will look after the farm when Grandpa retires next year?
records.zomi: A zom kum-in Pu nasep a khawl ciangin kua in lo a kem ding hiam?

records.english: My uncle has agreed to run it, and my cousin will help him at weekends.
records.zomi: Ka pa neu in a makaih dingin a lungkim a, ka sanggam in kal tawp te-ah a huh ding hi.

records.english: Who will teach the class next term?
records.zomi: A zom sinna hun-in kua in tanglai a sinsak ding hiam?

records.english: Who's filming the christening?
records.zomi: Naungek tuiphumna kua in video-in a lak hiam?

records.english: Who will walk the dog during our holiday?
records.zomi: I tawlngak hun lai-in kua in ui a paipih ding hiam?

records.english: Who would you trust to manage the family savings if you went abroad?
records.zomi: Gamdang-ah na pai leh innkuan sum kikhol makaih dingin kua na muang ding hiam?

records.english: Who will take care of the church garden after the old gardener retires?
records.zomi: Huan kemmi lui nasep a khawl khit-in kua in biakinn huan a kem ding hiam?

records.english: Asking who might help with a future project can reveal hidden talents in a group.
records.zomi: Hun ding project khat-ah kua in a huh thei ding hiam cih dot in pawl khat sung-a kisel siamna te a lak thei hi.

records.english: Succession plans answer the question of who will lead when a leader leaves.
records.zomi: Zom ciamteh te in makai khat a pawt ciangin kua in a makaih ding hiam cih dotna a dawng hi.

records.english: Who will run the youth club if the leader takes the job in the city?
records.zomi: Makaipa in khuapi-a nasep a la leh kua in khangno pawl a makaih ding hiam?

records.english: Communities often worry about who will continue the work of long-serving volunteers.
records.zomi: Khuasung te in sawt mahmah a sem thalawp te' nasep kua in a zom ding hiam cih tawh kisai a lunghimawh zel uh hi.

records.english: Who's going to replace the doctor when she retires in the autumn?
records.zomi: Autumn hun-in damdawi siam nu nasep a khawl ciangin kua in a laih ding hiam?

records.english: Choosing guardians for children is one of the most important decisions parents can make.
records.zomi: Naupang te adingin kemcingmi teel pen nu leh pa te in a bawl thei thukhensatna thupi pen te sung-a khat ahi hi.

records.english: Who will be responsible for the new community garden once it opens?
records.zomi: Khuasung huan thak a kihon khit-in kua in a mawhpuakna a la ding hiam?

records.english: Who will drive us to the airport?
records.zomi: Kua in vanlengtual-ah hong paipih ding hiam?

records.english: Who do you hope will win the election in the spring?
records.zomi: Spring hun-a teelna-ah kua a zo dingin na lamen hiam?

records.english: I'd like the candidate who promised to reopen the clinic in our town.
records.zomi: I khuapi-ah damdawi inn neu kik hong dingin a ciam mi ka deih hi.

records.english: Who's moving into the house next door?
records.zomi: Kua in a kiang inn-ah a tai hiam?

records.english: Who will inherit the old family house in the village?
records.zomi: Khuasung-a innkuan inn lui kua in a luah ding hiam?

records.english: Who's playing the lead in the school play?
records.zomi: Sang lim bawl tangthu-ah kua in a makai mi a lak hiam?

records.english: Who will water the garden in August?
records.zomi: August kha-in kua in huan tui a buak ding hiam?

records.english: Asking who will be affected by a future decision helps planners consider everyone.
records.zomi: Hun ding thukhensatna khat in kua a khak ding hiam cih dot in ciamtehmi te mi khempeuh a ngaihsut nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Who will be living in the flat after your brother moves out?
records.zomi: Na unau pa a pawt khit-in flat-ah kua a om ding hiam?

records.english: Asking who will be responsible prevents tasks from falling between people.
records.zomi: Kua in mawhpuakna a la ding hiam cih dot in nasep te mi kikal-ah a kia loh nadingin a dal hi.

records.english: Who's going to share your flat?
records.zomi: Kua in na flat a om khawm ding hiam?

records.english: Who's going to open the new café?
records.zomi: Kua in cafe thak a hong ding hiam?

records.english: Who will lead the trip next summer?
records.zomi: A zom khal hun-in kua in khualzinna a makaih ding hiam?

records.english: Who do you think will be the first in our class to start a business?
records.zomi: I tanglai sungah kua in sumbawlna a kipatsak masa pen ding hi, na ci hiam?

records.english: Questions about who will take on future roles help families and teams plan ahead.
records.zomi: Hun ding mun te kua in a la ding hiam cih tawh kisai dotna te in innkuan leh pawl te a ma-in a ciamteh nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Who would you like to travel with when you finally visit South America?
records.zomi: A tawp-in South America na ve ciangin kua tawh khualzin na deih ding hiam?

records.english: Who will be the new coach?
records.zomi: Kua in sinsakmi thak a hi ding hiam?

records.english: Young people's hopes about who they will become shape their choices at school.
records.zomi: Khangno te in kua a suak ding uh hiam cih a lametna uh in sang-a a teelna uh a bawl hi.

records.english: Who's hosting the meeting next month?
records.zomi: A zom kha-in kua in kikhopna a bawl ding hiam?

records.english: When our team leader announced that she would retire in the summer, everyone wondered who would replace her.
records.zomi: I pawl makai nu in khal hun-in nasep ka khawl ding hi, a cih ciangin, kua in a laih ding hiam ci-in mi khempeuh in a lamdang sa uh hi.

records.english: She invited each of us to say whether we would like the role and what we would change if we got it.
records.zomi: Tua mun na deih hiam, na ngah leh bang na khek ding hiam cih gen dingin ka khat ciat hong sam hi.

records.english: Two months later, the quietest member of the team was chosen, and she has already started planning the handover.
records.zomi: Kha nih khit-in, pawl sung-a a dai pen mi a kiteel a, nasep ap nading a ciamteh kipan khin hi.

records.english: Planning who will care for elderly relatives is a conversation many families delay too long.
records.zomi: Pi le pu upa te kua in a kem ding hiam cih ciamteh pen innkuan tampi in sawt lua a nawh kikumna khat ahi hi.

records.english: Who will decide where the new school is built?
records.zomi: Sang thak koi-ah a kilam ding hiam cih kua in a khensat ding hiam?

records.english: Who's coming to the party next week?
records.zomi: A zom kal-in pawi-ah kua te a hong pai ding uh hiam?

records.english: Who would you ask to be the baby's guardian if anything happened to you?
records.zomi: Nang tungah khat peuhpeuh a piang leh naungek' kemcingmi dingin kua na ngen ding hiam?

records.english: We've talked about it, and we'd ask my sister, because she already knows the baby's routine.
records.zomi: I kikum khin uh a, ka sanggam nu i ngen ding uh hi, bang hang hiam cih leh naungek' ni sim ngeina a thei khin hi.

records.english: Questions about who will be invited show what kind of event people are planning.
records.zomi: Kua te a kisam ding hiam cih tawh kisai dotna te in mite in bang pawi a ciamteh uh hiam cih a lak hi.

records.english: Who will cook for the wedding?
records.zomi: Mopawi adingin kua in an a huan ding hiam?

records.english: Who might take over the shop when the owner moves abroad next year?
records.zomi: A zom kum-in a neipa gamdang-ah a tai ciangin kua in dawr a la thei ding hiam?

records.english: Two of the staff are thinking about running it together, but they need to find a loan first.
records.zomi: Nasem nih in khawm-in a makaih dingin a ngaihsun uh a, ahi zongin a masa-in sum leitawi a zong ding uh a kisam hi.

records.english: Deciding who will inherit property early can prevent family disputes later.
records.zomi: Kua in van a luah ding hiam cih a ma-in khensat in a nung-in innkuan kinialna te a dal thei hi.

records.english: Who's joining the team in March?
records.zomi: March kha-in pawl-ah kua a kihel ding hiam?

records.english: Who should we ask to give the speech at Grandma's ninetieth birthday?
records.zomi: Pi' pianni kum sawm kua-ah thugen dingin kua i ngen ding uh hiam?

records.english: Who's speaking at the graduation?
records.zomi: Sinna zo pawi-ah kua in thu a gen ding hiam?

records.english: Who will collect the children tomorrow?
records.zomi: Zingciang kua in naupang te a la ding hiam?

records.english: Clear answers about who will cover a role give everyone confidence during changes.
records.zomi: Kua in mun khat a laih ding hiam cih tawh kisai dawnna kician te in khekna hun-in mi khempeuh muanna a pia hi.

records.english: My grandmother says that the Holy Spirit is as much God as the Father and the Son.
records.zomi: Kha Siangtho pen Pa leh Tapa bangmah-in Pasian ahi hi, ci-in ka pi in a gen hi.

records.english: Grandma sings a hymn to the Spirit.
records.zomi: Pi in Kha Siangtho kiangah la khat a sa hi.

records.english: Mum says the Spirit gives us comfort.
records.zomi: Kha Siangtho in lungmuanna hong pia hi, ci-in Nu in a gen hi.

records.english: Why do some Christian families pray directly to the Holy Spirit?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Khazih innkuan pawlkhat in Kha Siangtho kiangah a ngal-in thu a ngen uh hiam?

records.english: My wife believes that the Holy Spirit comforted her during the year her mother was ill.
records.zomi: A nu a na kum sungin Kha Siangtho in amah lungmuanna a pia hi, ci-in ka zi in a um hi.

records.english: How can we explain to our children that the Holy Spirit is God?
records.zomi: Kha Siangtho pen Pasian ahi hi, cih i ta te kiangah bangci i hilhcian thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: You could say that Christians believe in one God who is Father, Son and Spirit, all equally God.
records.zomi: Pa, Tapa leh Kha Siangtho a hi, khempeuh a kibang-in Pasian a hi Pasian khat Khazih mite in a um uh hi, na ci thei hi.

records.english: When my son was six, he asked me whether the Holy Spirit had a face.
records.zomi: Ka tapa kum guk a phak ciangin, Kha Siangtho in mai a nei hiam ci-in hong dong hi.

records.english: I told him that Christians believe the Spirit is a person who loves and comforts us, even though we can't see him.
records.zomi: I mu thei kei hang, Kha Siangtho pen hong it a, lungmuanna hong pia mi khat ahi hi, ci-in Khazih mite in a um uh hi, ci-in ka hilh hi.

records.english: He thought for a moment and said that the Spirit must be like the wind that he feels but never sees.
records.zomi: Hun tom khat a ngaihsun a, Kha Siangtho pen a kizak a, a muh ngei loh huih bang a hi ding hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Our family prays to the Spirit for wisdom before the children's exams.
records.zomi: Naupang te' sinna kisinna ma-in i innkuan in pilna adingin Kha Siangtho kiangah thu i ngen uh hi.

records.english: Why do we say Father, Son and Spirit?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Pa, Tapa leh Kha Siangtho i ci uh hiam?

records.english: Does the Spirit help us before school, Mum?
records.zomi: Nu aw, sang ma-in Kha Siangtho in hong huh hiam?

records.english: My little sister thinks the Spirit is a bird.
records.zomi: Ka sanggam nu neu in Kha Siangtho pen vasa khat ahi hi, a ci hi.

records.english: Can the Holy Spirit hear me when I pray at night?
records.zomi: Zan-in thu ka ngen ciangin Kha Siangtho in hong za thei hiam?

records.english: Christians believe the Spirit hears every prayer, even the ones whispered under the blanket.
records.zomi: Kha Siangtho in thungetna khempeuh a za hi, puan nuai-a nem taka kingen te zong, ci-in Khazih mite in a um uh hi.

records.english: After her husband died, my neighbour said that the Holy Spirit was her daily comfort.
records.zomi: A pasal a sih khit-in, Kha Siangtho pen a ni sim lungmuanna ahi hi, ci-in ka inn kiang mi nu in a gen hi.

records.english: Our children asked their grandmother why the creed says the Spirit is worshipped with the Father and the Son.
records.zomi: I ta te in bang hangin upna genna in Kha Siangtho pen Pa leh Tapa tawh kibia hi, a ci hiam ci-in a pi uh a dong uh hi.

records.english: My grandfather always ended family prayers with a blessing in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit.
records.zomi: Ka pu in innkuan thungetna te Pa' min, Tapa' min leh Kha Siangtho' min tawh thupha pia-in a khak den hi.

records.english: Could we read the passage where Jesus promises the Spirit as a helper?
records.zomi: Jesu in Huhpa bangin Kha Siangtho a ciamna thu i sim thei ding uh hiam?

records.english: The creeds teach that the Spirit is worshipped and glorified with the Father and the Son.
records.zomi: Upna genna te in Kha Siangtho pen Pa leh Tapa tawh kibia a, kiphat ahi hi, ci-in a sinsak uh hi.

records.english: Where does the Holy Spirit live, Dad?
records.zomi: Pa aw, Kha Siangtho koi-ah a om hiam?

records.english: How do you explain to a teenager why Christians see the Spirit as a person rather than a force?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Khazih mite in Kha Siangtho pen hatna khat hi lo-in mi khat bangin a mu uh hiam cih tangval khangno khat kiangah bangci na hilhcian hiam?

records.english: Many Christians say that the Spirit helps them pray when words fail.
records.zomi: Kammal a bei ciangin Kha Siangtho in thu ngen dingin hong huh hi, ci-in Khazih mi tampi in a gen uh hi.

records.english: My daughter made a paper flame.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in laimai meikuang khat a bawl hi.

records.english: Why do Christians pray to the Spirit?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Khazih mite in Kha Siangtho kiangah thu a ngen uh hiam?

records.english: Our family lights a candle at Pentecost.
records.zomi: Pentecost-in i innkuan in khawimeivaak khat i tan uh hi.

records.english: Christians believe that the Holy Spirit is a person who can comfort, teach and guide.
records.zomi: Kha Siangtho pen lungmuanna a pia, a sinsak a, a makaih thei mi khat ahi hi, ci-in Khazih mite in a um uh hi.

records.english: For many believers, speaking of the Spirit as a person makes their faith more personal.
records.zomi: Ummi tampi adingin, Kha Siangtho mi khat bangin gen in a upna uh a mimal zaw sak hi.

records.english: Grandpa prays for the Spirit's help.
records.zomi: Pu in Kha Siangtho' huhna adingin thu a ngen hi.

records.english: When my son asked how the Spirit could be everywhere, my husband said that only God can do that.
records.zomi: Kha Siangtho in mun khempeuh-ah bangci a om thei hiam ci-in ka tapa in a dot ciangin, Pasian bek in tua bang a bawl thei hi, ci-in ka pasal in a gen hi.

records.english: For many believers, the Spirit's personal presence brings comfort in times of grief.
records.zomi: Ummi tampi adingin, Kha Siangtho' mimal omna in dahna hun-in lungmuanna a pia hi.

records.english: Many Christian families teach their children that the Holy Spirit is fully God.
records.zomi: Khazih innkuan tampi in a ta te uh Kha Siangtho pen a bup-in Pasian ahi hi, ci-in a sinsak uh hi.

records.english: My daughter drew a dove for Pentecost.
records.zomi: Ka tanu in Pentecost adingin vakhu khat a suai hi.

records.english: Christian parents often use simple pictures to explain the Trinity to young children.
records.zomi: Khazih nu leh pa te in naupang neu te kiangah Trinity hilhcian nadingin lim baihlam te a zang zel uh hi.

records.english: My father taught us to speak of the Spirit as a person, because he believed the Spirit can be grieved.
records.zomi: Kha Siangtho a kidaksak thei hi, ci-in ka pa in a um ahih manin, Kha Siangtho mi khat bangin gen dingin hong sinsak hi.

records.english: Christian teaching that the Spirit can be grieved shows belief in the Spirit's personhood.
records.zomi: Kha Siangtho a kidaksak thei hi, cih Khazih sinsakna in Kha Siangtho mi khat ahi hi, cih upna a lak hi.

records.english: My son wore red to church at Pentecost.
records.zomi: Pentecost-in ka tapa in biakinn-ah puan san a silh hi.

records.english: Is the Holy Spirit with us now?
records.zomi: Tu-in Kha Siangtho eite tawh a om hiam?

records.english: My son was surprised to learn that Christians believe the Spirit has feelings and can be sad.
records.zomi: Kha Siangtho in lungsim kizakna a nei a, a dah thei hi, ci-in Khazih mite in a um uh hi, cih a theih ciangin ka tapa a lamdang sa hi.

records.english: Family traditions at Pentecost remind children of the Spirit's coming.
records.zomi: Pentecost-a innkuan ngeina te in naupang te Kha Siangtho' hong tunna a phawksak hi.

records.english: Is the Spirit God too?
records.zomi: Kha Siangtho zong Pasian ahi hiam?

records.english: Dad blesses us in the name of the Spirit.
records.zomi: Pa in Kha Siangtho' min tawh thupha hong pia hi.

records.english: When I was a child, my mother explained the Trinity using water, ice and steam.
records.zomi: Ka naupan lai-in, ka nu in tui, tuikhal leh tui-meikhu zang-in Trinity a hilhcian hi.

records.english: Mum, is the Holy Spirit a ghost?
records.zomi: Nu aw, Kha Siangtho pen kha-sia ahi hiam?

records.english: No, love, Christians believe the Holy Spirit is God, who is with us and helps us.
records.zomi: Hi kei hi, ka it aw, Kha Siangtho pen eite tawh a om a, hong huh Pasian ahi hi, ci-in Khazih mite in a um uh hi.

records.english: We sing about the Spirit at bedtime.
records.zomi: Ihmut hun-in Kha Siangtho tawh kisai la i sa uh hi.

records.english: Family prayers often help children understand the role of the Spirit in Christian faith.
records.zomi: Innkuan thungetna te in naupang te Khazih upna sung-a Kha Siangtho' mun a theisiam nadingin a huh zel hi.

records.english: Do your children understand why Christians call the Holy Spirit the Lord and giver of life?
records.zomi: Bang hangin Khazih mite in Kha Siangtho pen Topa leh nuntakna pia ahi hi, a ci uh hiam cih na ta te in a theisiam uh hiam?

records.english: We pray to the Holy Spirit at dinner.
records.zomi: Nitak an-ah Kha Siangtho kiangah thu i ngen uh hi.

records.english: My aunt says she first felt the Spirit's presence at her baptism as a teenager.
records.zomi: Khangno a hih lai-a a tuiphumna-ah Kha Siangtho' omna a kizak masa hi, ci-in ka ni in a gen hi.

records.english: Can the Spirit help me be kind?
records.zomi: Hehpihna ka neih nadingin Kha Siangtho in hong huh thei hiam?

records.english: Grandma calls the Spirit her Comforter.
records.zomi: Pi in Kha Siangtho pen a Huhpa a ci hi.

records.english: Why did your father always ask the Holy Spirit for guidance before family decisions?
records.zomi: Bang hangin na pa in innkuan thukhensatna ma-in Kha Siangtho kiangah makaihna a ngen den hiam?

records.english: He believed the Spirit was a personal guide who cared about our family, not a distant force, so he prayed before every big choice.
records.zomi: Kha Siangtho pen gamla hatna khat hi lo-in i innkuan a ngaihsut mimal makaipa khat ahi hi, ci-in a um ahih manin, teelna lian khempeuh ma-in thu a ngen hi.

records.english: Our family celebrates Pentecost with a special meal to remember the coming of the Spirit.
records.zomi: I innkuan in Kha Siangtho' hong tunna phawk dingin an tuam khat tawh Pentecost i pawi uh hi.

records.english: We read about Pentecost on Sunday.
records.zomi: Nipini-in Pentecost tawh kisai i sim uh hi.

records.english: My son asked if the Spirit can see him.
records.zomi: Kha Siangtho in amah a mu thei hiam ci-in ka tapa in a dong hi.

records.english: Why does Grandma talk about the Holy Spirit as "he"?

records.english: Many Christians believe the Spirit is a person, not just a power, so they say "he" instead of "it".

records.english: Did your teacher write comments in red ink?
records.zomi: Na sangsia in ink san tawh ngaihsutna te a gelh hiam?

records.english: Thanking a former teacher years later can mean a great deal to both people.
records.zomi: Kum tampi khit-in sangsia lui khat lungdam in mi nih adingin a thupi mahmah thei hi.

records.english: Do you remember the teacher who wrote a personal letter to every pupil at the end of the year?
records.zomi: Kum tawp-in sangnaupang khempeuh kiangah mimal lai khat a gelh sangsia na phawk hiam?

records.english: A teacher's written comment can be remembered for a lifetime.
records.zomi: Sangsia khat' gelh ngaihsutna khat nuntak sung a kiphawk thei hi.

records.english: We wrote our questions on slips of paper.
records.zomi: Laimai neu te tungah i dotna te i gelh uh hi.

records.english: Did your teacher call you by your full name?
records.zomi: Na sangsia in na min bup tawh hong sam hiam?

records.english: Do you still see your old teacher?
records.zomi: Na sangsia lui na mu lai hiam?

records.english: The first time a teacher asked for my opinion, I was so surprised that I couldn't answer.
records.zomi: A masa pen vei-in sangsia khat in ka ngaihdan a dot ciangin, ka lamdang sa mahmah ahih manin ka dawng thei kei hi.

records.english: Our science teacher used to answer every question with another question, which annoyed us at the time.
records.zomi: I science sangsia in dotna khempeuh dotna dang khat tawh a dawng zel a, tua hun lai-in i lungkham sak hi.

records.english: Our teacher listened to every excuse.
records.zomi: I sangsia in kipelhna a hang khempeuh a ngai hi.

records.english: Stories of teachers' kindness are often passed down in families.
records.zomi: Sangsia te' hehpihna tangthu te innkuan te-ah khang khat pan khang khat-ah a kigen zel hi.

records.english: In my last year at school, I was too embarrassed to tell my teacher that I couldn't afford the exam fee.
records.zomi: Sang-a ka kum nunung pen-in, sinna kisinna man ka pia zo kei hi, cih ka sangsia kiangah gen dingin ka zum lua hi.

records.english: She noticed that I hadn't handed in the form and quietly asked me to stay behind after class.
records.zomi: Lai lak ka ap kei hi, cih a phawk a, tanglai khit-in om lai dingin dai takin hong ngen hi.

records.english: The next week, the fee had been paid by a school fund, and I never found out who had arranged it.
records.zomi: A zom kal-in, sang sum-bawm in man a pia khin a, kua in a ciamteh hiam cih ka thei ngei kei hi.

records.english: My literature teacher encouraged me to write.
records.zomi: Ka laibu sinna sangsia in gelh dingin hong hanthawn hi.

records.english: The head teacher spoke to us every Monday.
records.zomi: Sangpi heutu in Pizing ni khempeuh-in hong gen hi.

records.english: Teachers who listened carefully often had the greatest influence on their pupils' futures.
records.zomi: Kilawm taka a ngai sangsia te in a sangnaupang te' hun ding tungah a khakna lian pen a nei zel uh hi.

records.english: Our teacher praised me in front of everyone.
records.zomi: I sangsia in mi khempeuh ma-ah hong phat hi.

records.english: Were you afraid to ask questions in class?
records.zomi: Tanglai-ah dotna dot dingin na lau hiam?

records.english: In my first job as a teacher, an older colleague showed me how to talk to nervous pupils.
records.zomi: Sangsia-a ka nasep masa pen-ah, nasep lawm upa zaw khat in a lau sangnaupang te tawh bangci kiho ding hiam cih hong lak hi.

records.english: I cried when my teacher left the school.
records.zomi: Ka sangsia in sang a nusiat ciangin ka kap hi.

records.english: Recalling their own school days helps parents understand how their children communicate with teachers.
records.zomi: Amau' sang kah ni te phawk in nu leh pa te in a ta te uh sangsia te tawh bangci a kiho uh hiam cih a theisiam nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: What did your favourite teacher write on your last report?
records.zomi: Na deih pen sangsia in na report nunung-ah bang a gelh hiam?

records.english: "Keep asking questions," and I still have the report in a drawer.
records.zomi: "Dong den in," a ci a, report pen tu dong bawm neu khat sungah ka kem lai hi.

records.english: Our music teacher took the time to learn every pupil's name in the first week.
records.zomi: I la sangsia in kal masa pen sungin sangnaupang khempeuh' min sin dingin hun a zang hi.

records.english: Changes in how teachers talk to pupils reflect wider changes in society.
records.zomi: Sangsia te in sangnaupang te tawh bangci a kiho uh hiam cih khekna te in mipi' khekna zai zaw te a lak hi.

records.english: Pupils who were afraid to speak in class sometimes found other ways to ask for help.
records.zomi: Tanglai-ah gen dingin a lau sangnaupang te in hun khenkhat huhna ngen nading lampi dang te a mu uh hi.

records.english: Did you have to stand when you spoke to a teacher?
records.zomi: Sangsia khat tawh na kiho ciangin na ding ding a kisam hiam?

records.english: My uncle says his teacher only praised the top pupil and ignored everyone else.
records.zomi: A sangsia in a tung pen sangnaupang bek a phat a, a dang khempeuh a nusia hi, ci-in ka pa neu in a gen hi.

records.english: Communication between teachers and pupils was once far more formal than it is today.
records.zomi: Sangsia leh sangnaupang te' kikhopna pen nidang-in tu hun sangin a khauh zaw mahmah hi.

records.english: Were you too shy to greet your teacher?
records.zomi: Na sangsia cibai buk dingin na zum lua hiam?

records.english: Many older people remember teachers who noticed problems that pupils were too shy to mention.
records.zomi: Mi upa tampi in sangnaupang te' gen dingin a zum uh buaina te a phawk sangsia te a phawk uh hi.

records.english: Former pupils often realise only as adults how much their teachers noticed.
records.zomi: Nidang sangnaupang te in a sangsia te uh bangzah a phawk uh hiam cih mi upa a suak uh ciangin bek a thei zel uh hi.

records.english: Did you ever talk to your teachers about problems at home?
records.zomi: Inn-a buaina te tawh kisai na sangsia te tawh na kikum ngei hiam?

records.english: Hardly ever, because in my day you only spoke to a teacher when you were spoken to.
records.zomi: Kikum ngei mawk kei hi, bang hang hiam cih leh ka hun lai-in sangsia hong gen ciangin bek na gen thei hi.

records.english: My grandmother remembers being punished for speaking her home language to a classmate.
records.zomi: Tanglai lawm khat kiangah a inn pau a gen hangin gawtna a ngah hi, cih ka pi in a phawk hi.

records.english: Did you ever argue with a teacher?
records.zomi: Sangsia khat tawh na kinial ngei hiam?

records.english: How did communication between teachers and pupils change during your forty years in the classroom?
records.zomi: Tanglai-a na kum sawm li sungin sangsia leh sangnaupang te' kiho dan bangci a kikhek hiam?

records.english: At first pupils barely spoke to me, but by the end they emailed questions at midnight and expected a reply by breakfast.

records.english: Pupils whose home language was discouraged at school sometimes felt unable to speak freely.
records.zomi: Sang-ah a inn pau uh a kikham sangnaupang te in hun khenkhat suakta takin a gen thei kei bang a kizak uh hi.

records.english: When I was bullied, the teacher I trusted most was the one who always asked how I was.
records.zomi: Hong bawlsia uh ciangin, ka muan pen sangsia pen na dam hiam ci-in hong dong den mi ahi hi.

records.english: My teacher once apologised to the class.
records.zomi: Ka sangsia in vei khat tanglai kiangah maisakna a ngen hi.

records.english: Have you ever written to an old teacher?
records.zomi: Sangsia lui khat kiangah lai na gelh ngei hiam?

records.english: My teacher's comment that I had a talent for drawing led me to become an architect.
records.zomi: Lim suai siamna ka nei hi, cih ka sangsia' genna in architect hong suak sak hi.

records.english: The teacher sent a note home to my parents.
records.zomi: Sangsia in ka nu leh pa kiangah lai neu khat a khak hi.

records.english: Our class wrote anonymous notes to the teacher about what we found difficult.
records.zomi: I tanglai in i haksa sa te tawh kisai min om lo lai neu te sangsia kiangah i gelh uh hi.

records.english: My teacher remembered my birthday once.
records.zomi: Ka sangsia in vei khat ka pianni a phawk hi.

records.english: What did you tell the teacher when you lost your homework?
records.zomi: Na inn nasep na mangsuah ciangin sangsia kiangah bang na gen hiam?

records.english: How did your teachers tell your parents about your marks?
records.zomi: Na sangsia te in na nu leh pa kiangah na sinna gah bangci a gen uh hiam?

records.english: They sent a handwritten report home twice a year, and my father signed it at the kitchen table.
records.zomi: Kum khat-ah vei nih khut tawh kigelh report khat inn-ah a khak uh a, ka pa in an huanna inn dokhan-ah a min a khen hi.

records.english: Years later, I met my old teacher and finally thanked her for believing in me.
records.zomi: Kum tampi khit-in, ka sangsia lui ka mu a, hong muan hangin a tawp-in ka lungdam hi.

records.english: When my mother was at school, pupils had to write to the head teacher to ask for anything.
records.zomi: Ka nu sang a kah lai-in, sangnaupang te in bangkim ngen dingin sangpi heutu kiangah lai a gelh ding uh a kisam hi.

records.english: Could you call teachers by their first names?
records.zomi: Sangsia te a min masa tawh na sam thei uh hiam?

records.english: When I finally told my teacher that I couldn't see the board, she moved me to the front row.
records.zomi: Laimal suaina ka mu thei kei hi, ci-in a tawp-in ka sangsia kiangah ka gen ciangin, a ma pen tutna kizui-ah hong suan hi.

records.english: My father says his teacher never spoke to him directly, only to the class as a whole.
records.zomi: A sangsia in amah tawh a ngal-in a kiho ngei kei a, tanglai bup kiangah bek a gen hi, ci-in ka pa in a gen hi.

records.english: Memories of teachers often focus on a single conversation that made a difference.
records.zomi: Sangsia te' phawkna te pen kikhekna a tun sak kikumna khat bek tungah a kinga zel hi.

records.english: When I misunderstood the essay question, my teacher let me explain and rewrite it.
records.zomi: Essay dotna ka theikhialh ciangin, ka sangsia in hilhcian dingin hong phal a, ka gelh kik hi.

records.english: My teacher noticed when I was sad.
records.zomi: Ka lungkham ciangin ka sangsia in a phawk hi.

records.english: Do you remember a conversation with a teacher that changed your life?
records.zomi: Na nuntakna a khek sangsia khat tawh kikumna khat na phawk hiam?

records.english: When I said I wanted to leave school, my history teacher talked me into staying for one more year, and I went on to university.
records.zomi: Sang ka nusia nuam hi, ka cih ciangin, ka tangthu sangsia in kum khat beh om dingin hong hanthawn a, university-ah ka pai hi.

records.english: What should I do if I slipped in a supermarket but didn't report it at the time?
records.zomi: Dawr lianpi khat-ah ka dalh a, tua hun-in ka gen kei leh bang ka bawl ding hiam?

records.english: People are more likely to report accidents when the process is simple and blame-free.
records.zomi: Kalsuan a baihlam a, mawhsakna a om kei ciangin mite in accident a gen zaw uh hi.

records.english: Is there an accident form here?
records.zomi: Hi-ah accident lai lak khat a om hiam?

records.english: Asking questions about accident reports helps people act correctly after a shock.
records.zomi: Accident genna tawh kisai dotna te dot in mite lamdang sakna khit-in dik takin a bawl nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: When a cyclist was knocked down outside my shop, I was the only person who saw the van that drove away.

records.english: I wrote down the colour, the first part of the number plate and the time before I could forget them.
records.zomi: Ka mangngilh ma-in a pianzia, a nambat lai' a masa khen leh hun ka gelh hi.

records.english: Two days later, the police phoned to say that my notes had helped them find the driver.

records.english: Accurate details recorded soon after an accident are far more reliable than later memories.

records.english: Is it important to report a near miss at work if nobody was hurt?

records.english: Should I take photos?

records.english: Recording small accidents allows organisations to spot dangerous patterns.
records.zomi: Accident neu te ciamteh in pawl te in lauhuai kalsuan te a phawk thei uh hi.

records.english: Interpreters can help people report accidents when they don't speak the local language well.
records.zomi: Khuasung pau a gen siam kei uh ciangin pau lettu te in mite accident a gen nadingin a huh thei uh hi.

records.english: Can I stay anonymous as a witness?

records.english: How soon after an accident do I have to tell my insurance company?
records.zomi: Accident khit-in ka insurance company kiangah bangzah manlang-in ka gen ding kisam hiam?

records.english: Should I keep the damaged item?

records.zomi: A copy khat hong khak ding uh hiam?

records.english: What time did it happen?

records.english: Don't argue at the scene; write down what you saw, take photos and give the details to your insurance company and the police.

records.english: Photographs give insurers and investigators clear evidence of what happened.
records.zomi: Lim te in insurance mi leh ensuimi te kiangah bang a piang hiam cih ettehna kician a pia hi.

records.english: Rules about reporting accidents vary between countries and between workplaces.
records.zomi: Accident gen tawh kisai thukham te gam khat le khat leh nasepna mun khat le khat kikal-ah a kibang kei hi.

records.english: How do I report an accident involving a bus or a train?

records.english: Delayed injuries should still be reported, along with a doctor's assessment.

records.english: Admitting partial responsibility honestly usually makes a report more credible.

records.english: How should I describe an accident if I'm still in shock?

records.zomi: Accident koi-ah leh bangci gen ding hiam cih theih in hun haksa khat-ah lungsim nawhsawhna a niam sak hi.

records.english: Can I report a dangerous pavement after I tripped on it last month?

records.english: Do I need to report a minor car accident if nobody was hurt?
records.zomi: Kuamah a liam kei leh mawtaw accident neu khat ka gen ding kisam hiam?

records.english: In many places you must report it if the other driver won't give details, so check the local rules.
records.zomi: Mun tampi-ah mawtaw mawng dang in a thu te a pia nuam kei leh na gen ding a kisam ahih manin, khuasung thukham te en in.

records.english: Why do insurance companies ask for photos of both vehicles?
records.zomi: Bang hangin insurance company te in mawtaw nih' lim a ngen uh hiam?

records.english: Did anyone see the crash?

records.english: Reports of near misses help prevent serious accidents in the future.
records.zomi: A tung dek accident te' genna in hun ding-a accident lian te a dal hi.

records.english: What if the injury only becomes painful a few days after the accident?
records.zomi: Accident khit ni tawm khat ciangin bek liamna a na kipan leh bangci ahi ding hiam?

records.english: Should I mention in the report that I was partly to blame?
records.zomi: Genna-ah khen khat-ah keimah zong ka mawh hi, ci-in ka gen ding hiam?

records.english: Why does the school record every small accident in the playground?
records.zomi: Bang hangin sang in kawmna mun-a accident neu khempeuh a ciamteh hiam?

records.english: How can I report an accident if I don't speak the local language well?
records.zomi: Khuasung pau ka gen siam kei leh accident khat bangci ka gen thei ding hiam?

records.english: Witness descriptions can be crucial when the people involved disagree.
records.zomi: A kihel mite a kituak kei uh ciangin theihpihmi te' genna a thupi mahmah thei hi.

records.english: Who signs the accident book?
records.zomi: Accident laibu-ah kua in a min a khen hiam?

records.english: Can a child report an accident?
records.zomi: Naupang khat in accident a gen thei hiam?

records.english: Do I need a police reference number?
records.zomi: Palik reference nambat ka kisam hiam?

records.english: Should I report an accident to the council if it happened on a public road?
records.zomi: Mipi lampi tungah a piang leh accident pen council kiangah ka gen ding hiam?

records.english: Where do I report the accident?
records.zomi: Accident koi-ah ka gen ding hiam?

records.english: Will the report be kept private?
records.zomi: Genna a kisel-in a kikem ding hiam?

records.english: Is it too late to report it?
records.zomi: Gen dingin a nunung lua khin hiam?

records.english: Should I call my insurance company?

records.english: Who do I tell at work?
records.zomi: Nasep-ah kua kiangah ka gen ding hiam?

records.english: Is there a website for reporting crashes?
records.zomi: Mawtaw kisual gen nading website khat a om hiam?

records.english: Can I report an accident I only saw from my window?

records.english: Yes, and your description could help the police understand what happened.

records.english: Descriptions of wildlife bring a natural scene to life for listeners.

records.english: How do the hills look when the morning mist lifts?

records.zomi: A mu thei lo mi khat kiangah gam omdan gen in ging leh kituk a ngaihsut nadingin a hanthawn hi.

records.english: What does the valley smell like?

records.zomi: Gamkeu a mu ngei lo mi khat kiangah bangci na gen ding hiam?

records.english: Imagine an ocean of orange sand under a huge sky, silent in the day and freezing cold at night.

records.english: Good descriptions of weather help readers feel the atmosphere of a place.

records.english: How would you describe the silence on top of a mountain?
records.zomi: Mual tung-a daina bangci na gen ding hiam?

records.english: What animals do you hear in the forest at night?
records.zomi: Zan-in gammang sungah bang ganhing te' ging na za hiam?

records.zomi: Gam omdan-ah bang a kikhek hiam cih dot in mi khat bangzah kilawm takin a en hiam cih a lak hi.

records.english: Is there fog in the mornings?
records.zomi: Zingsang te-in meikhu a om hiam?

records.english: What makes the sunrise over the valley so special?
records.zomi: Guam tung-a ni suahna bang in a tuam sak hiam?

records.english: What changes in the hills when the dry season begins?
records.zomi: Keu hun a kipat ciangin mual te-ah bang a kikhek hiam?

records.english: The grass turns gold, the streams shrink to thin trickles, and dust hangs in the air every afternoon until the first rains return.
records.zomi: Lopa kham bangin a kilang a, tuilui te a neu-in a khawi a, guah masa a tun dong nitak lam khempeuh-in huih-ah leivui a liang hi.

records.zomi: Gam omdan a gen gelhtu te in a kician-a et leh lungsim kizakna a gawm zel uh hi.

records.english: Is the river fast?

records.english: What does the coast look like after a big storm?
records.zomi: Huihpi lian khat khit-in tuipi gei bang bang a kilang hiam?

records.english: What does the forest look like after a heavy rain?
records.zomi: Guah lianpi khit-in gammang bang bang a kilang hiam?

records.zomi: Bangkim a tang a, a kizul te a eng mahmah a, a nah khempeuh pan tui a tak hi.

records.english: How would you describe a waterfall to someone who is blind?
records.zomi: Mittaw mi khat kiangah tuikhawng bangci na gen ding hiam?

records.english: What does a field of wild flowers look like in early summer?
records.zomi: Khal kipat lai-in gam pak a dimna mun khat bang bang a kilang hiam?

records.english: Which season is the most beautiful there?
records.zomi: Tua-ah koi hun a hoih pen hiam?

records.english: Is the water warm in summer?
records.zomi: Khal hun-in tui a lum hiam?

records.english: How high is the waterfall?
records.zomi: Tuikhawng bangzah a sang hiam?

records.english: People who grew up close to nature often describe it with deep affection.
records.zomi: Gam omdan kiangah a khanlet mite in itna thuk tawh a gen zel uh hi.

records.english: Comparisons, such as an ocean of sand, help listeners imagine unfamiliar places.
records.zomi: Ngazilh tuipi bang kiteh genna te in ngaimi te mun theih lo te a ngaihsun thei nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: Can you hear the waterfall from far away?
records.zomi: Gamla pan tuikhawng na za thei hiam?

records.english: What's the view like from the top of the hill?
records.zomi: Mual tung pan et ciangin bang bang ahi hiam?

records.english: You can see three valleys, a silver river and, on clear days, the snow on the far mountains.
records.zomi: Guam thum, ngun bang a tang tuipi khat leh, khua siang ni te-in, gamla mual tunga vuk na mu thei hi.

records.english: What do the rice fields look like just before the harvest?
records.zomi: Gah lakna ma-in buh lo te bang bang a kilang uh hiam?

records.english: Is the lake deep?
records.zomi: Dil a thuk hiam?

records.english: What does the river look like when the snow melts in spring?
records.zomi: Spring hun-in vuk a tuisuak ciangin tuipi bang bang a kilang hiam?

records.english: When my niece asked me to describe the mountains where I grew up, I didn't know where to start.
records.zomi: Ka khanletna mual te gen dingin ka tunu in hong ngen ciangin, bang pan kipan ding hiam cih ka thei kei hi.

records.english: In the end I described the morning mist in the valleys, the smell of pine and the cold, clear water of the streams.

records.english: She said it sounded like a painting, so we spent the afternoon trying to draw it together.

records.english: Are there wild animals in the woods?
records.zomi: Gammang sungah gam sa te a om hiam?

records.english: Can you describe the colours of the sky at sunset over the sea?
records.zomi: Tuipi tungah ni tum ciangin van' pianzia te na gen thei ding hiam?

records.english: Are the stars bright out there?
records.zomi: Tua-ah aksi te a tang uh hiam?

records.english: What birds live near the lake?
records.zomi: Dil kiangah bang vasa te a om uh hiam?

records.english: What colour is the sea there?
records.zomi: Tua-ah tuipi in bang pianzia a nei hiam?

records.english: What are you planning to do with the money from the harvest?
records.zomi: Gah lakna pan sum tawh bang na bawl dingin na ciamteh hiam?

records.english: What a family decides to do with an inheritance can shape relationships for years.
records.zomi: Innkuan khat in gamluah tawh bang a bawl ding hiam cih a khensat in kum tampi sung kizopna te a bawl thei hi.

records.english: What will you miss most when you move to the city next month?
records.zomi: A zom kha-in khuapi-ah na tai ciangin bang na lunggulh pen ding hiam?

records.english: What time will you leave tomorrow?
records.zomi: Zingciang bang hun-in na pawt ding hiam?

records.english: What people imagine for the next generation often reflects their own past.
records.zomi: Mite in khang zom adingin a ngaihsut te uh in amau' nidang a lak zel hi.

records.english: What do you think the children will remember about this summer?
records.zomi: Hih khal hun tawh kisai naupang te in bang a phawk ding uh hi, na ci hiam?

records.english: What are you going to tell your parents about the new job?
records.zomi: Nasep thak tawh kisai na nu leh pa kiangah bang na gen ding hiam?

records.english: What are you going to study?
records.zomi: Bang na sin ding hiam?

records.english: What could the youth club offer next year to attract more teenagers?
records.zomi: Khangno tam zaw a sawl nadingin a zom kum-in khangno pawl in bang a pia thei ding hiam?

records.english: What are you going to paint next?
records.zomi: A zom-ah bang na zial ding hiam?

records.english: What will happen to the church if the young people keep leaving?
records.zomi: Khangno te a pawt den uh leh biakinn bang a suak ding hiam?

records.english: What are you hoping to find at the market?
records.zomi: Sum-kuan mun-ah bang na mu dingin na lamen hiam?

records.english: What will you bring to the picnic?
records.zomi: Gam pua-a an ne khawmna-ah bang na paipih ding hiam?

records.english: What are you saving up for?
records.zomi: Bang adingin sum na kikhol hiam?

records.english: Plans for the future often depend on money, health and family responsibilities.
records.zomi: Hun ding ciamteh te sum, damna leh innkuan mawhpuakna te tungah a kinga zel hi.

records.english: What will you call the new puppy?
records.zomi: Ui neu thak bang na ci ding hiam?

records.english: What kind of business would you start if you had the chance?
records.zomi: Hun na neih leh bang sumbawlna na kipatsak ding hiam?

records.english: What would you do differently if you had another year to prepare?
records.zomi: Kiginkhol nading kum khat na nei beh leh bang tuam takin na bawl ding hiam?

records.english: Communities that discuss what they want in the future can plan more fairly.
records.zomi: Hun ding-ah bang a deih uh hiam cih a kikum khuasung te in dik zaw takin a ciamteh thei uh hi.

records.english: When my daughter asked what we would do when she left for university, my husband and I had no answer.
records.zomi: University-ah a pai ciangin bang na bawl ding uh hiam ci-in ka tanu in a dot ciangin, ka pasal leh kei dawnna i nei kei uh hi.

records.english: After talking for a whole evening, we decided to learn to dance, visit my sister abroad and finally paint the house.
records.zomi: Nitak khat bup i kikum khit-in, lam sin dingin, gamdang-a ka sanggam nu ve dingin leh a tawp-in inn zial dingin i khensat uh hi.

records.english: She laughed and said that our plans sounded more exciting than hers.
records.zomi: A nuih a, i ciamteh te amah' ciamteh sangin a lamdang zaw hi, a ci hi.

records.english: What job would you like one day?
records.zomi: Ni khat-in bang nasep na deih hiam?

records.english: What will you do after you finish school next year?
records.zomi: A zom kum-in sang na zo khit-in bang na bawl ding hiam?

records.english: I'm hoping to train as an electrician, if I can find an apprenticeship near home.
records.zomi: Inn kiangah nasep sinna khat ka muh leh electric siam-in kisin dingin ka lamen hi.

records.english: What do you think the town will look like in twenty years?
records.zomi: Kum sawm nih sungin khuapi bang bang a suak ding hi, na ci hiam?

records.english: Probably bigger and busier, with a new bridge and more young families moving in from the villages.
records.zomi: A lian zaw a, a buai zaw ding a, lei thak khat leh khuasung te pan a hong tai innkuan khangno tam zaw tawh.

records.english: What changes will the new road bring to the market?
records.zomi: Lampi thak in sum-kuan mun-ah bang khekna a tun ding hiam?

records.english: Sharing plans with friends can bring both encouragement and useful advice.
records.zomi: Lawm te tawh ciamteh hawm in hanthawnna leh thuhilhna phatuam te a nih a tun thei hi.

records.english: What will the new shop sell?
records.zomi: Dawr thak in bang a zuak ding hiam?

records.english: What are the council's plans for the empty field behind the school?
records.zomi: Sang nunglam-a lo awng adingin council' ciamteh te bang ahi hiam?

records.english: Future plans become more realistic when people say them aloud to others.
records.zomi: Mite in mi dang te kiangah ging taka a gen uh ciangin hun ding ciamteh te a kituak zaw hi.

records.english: What are you planning for your parents' golden wedding anniversary?
records.zomi: Na nu leh pa' kiteenna kum sawm nga pawi adingin bang na ciamteh hiam?

records.english: Which dish will you bring to the harvest festival?
records.zomi: Gah lakna pawi-ah bang an na paipih ding hiam?

records.english: What will you do on your birthday?
records.zomi: Na pianni-in bang na bawl ding hiam?

records.english: What do you hope your son will be doing in ten years?
records.zomi: Kum sawm sungin na tapa in bang a bawl ding dingin na lamen hiam?

records.english: What would you buy first if you won the village raffle?
records.zomi: Khuasung aisan-ah na zo leh bang na lei masa ding hiam?

records.english: What are your plans for the holidays?

records.english: What will the weather be like on Saturday?

records.english: What will happen to the old school?
records.zomi: Sang lui bang a suak ding hiam?

records.english: What languages do you want to learn?
records.zomi: Bang pau te sin na deih hiam?

records.english: What are you going to plant in the new garden this spring?
records.zomi: Hih spring hun-in huan thak-ah bang na suan ding hiam?

records.english: Beans, chillies and a row of sunflowers for the children.
records.zomi: Be, malta leh naupang te adingin ni pak gual khat.

records.english: What will you wear to the wedding?
records.zomi: Mopawi-ah bang na silh ding hiam?

records.english: What are they building by the river?
records.zomi: Tuipi gei-ah bang a lam uh hiam?

records.english: Asking what might change helps people prepare for possibilities rather than be surprised by them.
records.zomi: Bang a kikhek thei hiam cih dot in mite lamen lo-a a lamdang sak sangin a piang thei te adingin a kiginkhol nadingin a huh hi.

records.english: What would you change about your job if you could start again next year?

records.english: I'd ask for one day a week working from home, so that I could spend more time with my children after school.

records.english: What will you name your shop?
